          What’s Different About the Premier League This Season? Five Trends We’ve Spotted in 2026-27
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re just five matchdays into the 2026-27 Premier League season, but some interesting patterns are already beginning to emerge. Here are five league-wide trends we’ve spotted.
OK, ‘gone’ might be an oversimplification. ‘Evaporating’ could be more accurate.

However you put it, the home win percentage in the Premier League is just 36.0% this season, the lowest rate in the competition’s history. It’s even lower than in the COVID-affected 2020-21 campaign, when the majority of matches were played without fans in stadiums.

The fading importance of home advantage is part of a wider trend. As you can see above, four of the six lowest home win rates in Premier League history have come this decade. Of course, teams would still much prefer to play at home than away, but the extent to which doing so provides an advantage appears to be falling.

The answer is that they're broadly becoming draws rather than away wins. There have been 16 draws in the first 50 matches this season, meaning 32.0% of games have finished level. That’s the highest draw percentage of any Premier League season.
Away wins are also fairly prevalent – 32.0% (16/50) is still the seventh-highest on record – but it’s not as notable as the increase in draws.

Matchday 4 of the Premier League was a good demonstration of this pattern. Across the 10 matches, there was just one home win (Leeds’ 4-1 win against Newcastle), while four of the other nine games finished level.
Had Leeds drawn or lost against Newcastle, MD4 would have become just the fourth matchday in Premier League history not to feature a single home win, and the first since September 2000.
One reason why draws are at an all-time high could be because sides are struggling to hold onto leads this season.

A team has scored first in 45 of the 50 Premier League games played so far, but only 29 of those sides have gone on to win. That gives teams scoring first a win rate of just 64.4%, the second-lowest percentage across the last 14 years, and the fourth-lowest in the campaign’s history.

Bournemouth have been the biggest culprits. They’ve dropped seven points in games that they've scored in first already, with Brentford next on six. Overall, the Cherries have dropped nine points from winning positions having taken the lead in four of their five matches but have failed to win any of them.
When Pep Guardiola joined Manchester City in 2016-17, his arrival led to a revolution in how Premier League sides wanted to play.
Goalkeepers increasingly played shorter, teams became more committed to building from the back, and it felt like monopolising possession became an objective in itself.
Many teams, to varying degrees, tried to replicate Guardiola’s tactics.

But as that style became dominant, opponents increasingly adapted to counter it. Winning the ball back and attacking quickly and vertically in transition has become more popular in recent seasons. And it is becoming increasingly effective, too.
There have been 22 matches this season in which a team has enjoyed at least 60% possession. On only eight occasions has that side gone on to win.
That equates to a win rate of just 36.4%, the third lowest in a Premier League season since we have detailed possession data available (from 2005-06).
It follows last season’s record-low rate of 34.1%. Teams are now set up to be more and more successful without the ball.
Another way to measure that shift is through the rise of counter-attacking football.
Fast breaks – defined as a quick counter-attack beginning in the defensive half against an opposition defence that is at least partially unsorted – are an excellent proxy for measuring counters.

          Roma 3-4 Real Madrid Stats: Rüdiger Completes Seven-Minute Comeback in Champions League Thriller
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Joel Sritharan / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Roma seemed to be heading for a famous victory over Real Madrid in the Champions League, but José Mourinho's men had other ideas.
Antonio Rüdiger and José Mourinho came back to haunt Roma as Real Madrid scored three goals in seven minutes late on to claim a thrilling 4-3 Champions League win.
Los Blancos were trailing 3-1 before Carlos Espí struck in the 83rd minute.
From there, Endrick and former Roma defender Rüdiger completely flipped the script at Stadio Olimpico as Mourinho got one over on his old club.

Roma, encouraged by a roaring home crowd, made a fast start as Matías Soulé curled narrowly wide after just 48 seconds before Mario Hermoso's curling effort was tipped away by Thibaut Courtois at full stretch.

Paulo Dybala poked wide from Nahuel Molina's cutback, and though Roma received a blow when Manu Koné was forced off with an injury, they took a deserved lead when Marten de Roon‘s first-time strike from outside the box was deflected past Courtois in the 20th minute.

However, Madrid equalised against the run of play as Kylian Mbappé, on his 100th Champions League appearance, capitalised on an error from Hermoso before lashing past Pierluigi Gollini, bringing up his 500th goal involvement in club football in the process (378 goals, 122 assists).

Jude Bellingham missed a huge opportunity before half-time, sweeping past the right post, and it looked to be costly when Donyell Malen scored twice in six second-half minutes; he first beat Courtois at the near post after a brilliant pass from Rodrigo Mora, while his second was a routine finish following a clever pass from Soule.
Mbappé had a goal disallowed after the hour-mark, but substitutes Espi and Endrick swung the tide.
Endrick's initial header from a corner was kept out by Gollini, but Espí was on hand to tap in the rebound.
Roma were undone again two minutes later when Endrick headed in unchallenged from Arda Güler's corner, and Rüdiger had the final say as he volleyed past Gollini in the 90th minute.
Mourinho was asked about Endrick's lack of minutes in his pre-match press conference and the Portuguese insisted the youngster has a bright future at the club, which was perhaps proven by this cameo.
The Brazilian's two shots proved crucial, with the first leading to Espí's goal and the quickfire second giving Madrid hope of snatching all three points rather than settling for just a point.

While Endrick, Espí and Rüdiger will take most of the headlines, it was another substitute in Güler who was the unsung hero. His two assists were crucial as his pinpoint crossing proved to be the difference in the end.

Only Lamine Yamal (40), Michael Olise (36) and Florian Thauvin (33) have created more chances in Europe's top five leagues this season than Güler (31), who will surely regain his starting position in Mourinho's team now.
Endrick, though, will likely have to still settle for a role as a super-sub, given he is behind Mbappé in the pecking order.

Mbappé became the youngest player to reach a century of European Cup/Champions League games, aged 27 years and 298 days, surpassing the record previously held by Lionel Messi (28 years, 84 days in 2015).

The France superstar became the eighth player to mark their 100th appearance in the competition with a goal, and the third to do so while playing for Madrid, after Cristiano Ronaldo in 2014 and Toni Kroos in 2019.

          One Stat to Sum Up 2026-27 So Far for Every Premier League Team
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Is it possible to summarise the 2026-27 Premier League season so far through just one statistic for each of the 20 teams? We’ve given it a go.

Five matchdays into the 2026-27 season, the Premier League table is looking rather better for some teams (Manchester City, Brighton, Brentford, Hull) than it is for others (Spurs, Fulham, Bournemouth).
But while the actual table is all that really matters, a look into the numbers shows there is more to the Premier League than meets the eye.

With that in mind, we’ve found one statistic that summarises each team’s campaign. From mitigating factors and reasons to be positive to concerning issues and damning truths, in order of current league position, this is the season so far in one stat for each team.
Just five games into the Enzo Maresca era, Manchester City sit top of the pile with the only remaining 100% record in the top four tiers of English football.

They have done it not by leaning on a solid defence but instead through an extremely talented and ruthlessly efficient attack. They are averaging higher-quality chances than any other team in the Premier League this season, with the average expected goals value of their non-penalty shots the best of the lot (0.15). That has helped them maintain the best non-penalty conversion rate, too (19.1%).

This is the 15th instance of a team winning their first five games of a Premier League season but, perhaps surprisingly, only four of the previous 14 have gone on to win the title. City’s lethal attack gives them as good a chance as any of joining the title-winning group.
Arsenal have the talent to beat anyone – yes, the Brighton defeat was an off day – but they also know how important it is to better your opponents when it comes to physical effort.
Across their first five games, Mikel Arteta’s men have run 22.7 kilometres more than their opponents, the biggest positive difference of any team so far.

The fact that they have more of the ball – often significantly so, averaging 59.5% possession – makes this statistic even more stark: Arsenal’s players work incredibly hard both in and out of possession. Sometimes, hard work trumps talent.
Speaking of physical effort, no other team has embodied the importance of hard work, specifically when out of possession, more than Brighton, whose high press has functioned brilliantly so far.

Fabian Hürzeler’s impressive side have enforced a suffocating high press to devastating effect, with the lowest PPDA (opposition passes per defensive action) rate (7.4) of every team in the Premier League, which shows how little time they give their opponents without putting pressure on them.
That has resulted in Brighton forcing more high turnovers (56) than any other team in the Premier League this season.
It helps when you’re trying not to lose matches if you never go behind, and Brentford have very nearly done just that so far this season.

Over their five Premier League matches, they have been trailing for just three minutes and 10 seconds, all of which came when they briefly went 2-1 down away to Bournemouth before equalising shortly afterwards.

That accounts for just 0.6% of their entire season so far which is, unsurprisingly, the lowest of all top-flight teams. They therefore remain one of just five undefeated sides and, flying high in fourth, will clearly take some beating.
Leeds have become a very good multi-faceted team under Daniel Farke, and while they are by no means reliant on set-pieces, they do use them more than most.

They are top of the Premier League this season for the proportion of their shots (46.7%) and xG (41.0%) which have been generated at non-penalty set-pieces. They have scored three of their seven goals from dead-ball situations, too.

Set-pieces aren’t the reason that Leeds are fifth in the table and one of the five remaining unbeaten sides, but they are clearly a significant part of the reason. Leeds are using dead balls better than most, and that’s nothing to be ashamed of.

With draws rescued late on against both Newcastle and Nottingham Forest, more dropped points at home to struggling Fulham, and two wins that weren’t exactly the most convincing against Ipswich and Bournemouth, it hasn’t been the strongest start to life at Anfield for Andoni Iraola.

          Manchester United’s WSL Turnaround: Is the Eva Olid Effect Taking Shape?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 28, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After a difficult start, Manchester United are beginning to show what Eva Olid wants them to be. Now fourth in the WSL table, the signs of progress are encouraging, but are United really turning a corner?
Criticism can fall quickly on new managers, and the football industry has a habit of judging a seed before it has had time to take root.
Cast your mind back four matchdays and you might recall a forlorn figure on the touchline, seemingly wrestling with the task of turning her vision into reality.
Eva Olid has faced her share of scrutiny since taking charge at Manchester United, including from us just last month.

Questions centred on the defensive frailties exposed in United’s opening two games against London City Lionesses and Chelsea, especially the 5-0 thrashing against the Blues, while Olid’s vision for a possession-based, attack-minded side was difficult to discern.
Their opening two defeats made it just the second time in WSL history that United had started a season with back-to-back losses, following their debut campaign in 2019-20.
Fast-forward to now and the picture could not look more different.

United are unbeaten in their last six games in all competitions, with their 1-1 draw against Manchester City last time out offering the clearest sign yet that Olid’s ideas are taking hold against the league’s best.

They are also outperforming their expected points tally by 4.3 points, the largest margin in the league. But is this just down to good fortune, or do the underlying numbers point to genuine improvement?
The draw against City was not simply a case of the Red Devils hanging on for a point against their neighbours, but it was a performance backed by belief that three points were there for the taking.
Andrée Jeglertz’s side completed a WSL double over United last season, winning both games 3-0. This time, the contest was far more evenly matched.

As you can see from the respective zones of control below, in this fixture last season, City controlled the majority of zones on the pitch. However, United had more control in their own half this time around, and imposed themselves on the game far more.
Though United started on the front foot, City grew into the contest and the hosts were forced to absorb pressure. Unlike in their heavy defeat to Chelsea, though, they found ways to push back.

United’s 45.6% field tilt – a metric that measures territorial dominance by looking at the share of possession each side has in their attacking third compared to their opponent – was their highest against one of the WSL’s traditional top three since recording 50% against Chelsea in April 2025. Against City, it was their best figure since May 2023, when they registered 56.4%.
They also recorded 13 high turnovers, their third-most against the traditional top three in WSL history.
Their average of 3.62 passes per sequence against City was also their third-highest against any traditional top three opponent in the WSL.

Add those all together and the figures suggest a side no longer content to sit back. United were competing for the ball higher up the pitch, sustaining possession and looking to exploit City’s defensive weaknesses.
Their best passages came when they moved the ball quickly. One- and two-touch combinations offered a glimpse of Olid’s philosophy at its most effective, even against the reigning champions.
The clearest example came when Ella Toone backheeled the ball into Andrea Medina’s path, helping to create an opening for Julia Zigiotti Olme.
After the game, Olid said: “If we play like this, nothing can stop us.”

          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 2 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 30, 2026
          
                      Emily Clogg / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions across Matchday 2 in 2026-27.

It was goals galore for Lyon and Barcelona on Matchday 1 against Servette and Paris FC, respectively, whilst over in London, both Arsenal and Chelsea squeezed past their opponents with narrow 1-0 victories.
Meanwhile, reigning WSL champions Manchester City, came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 against Bayern Munich City becoming the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.
The next round of fixtures promises even more entertainment.

The blockbuster match of the week sees Chelsea travel to eight-time winners Lyon; Sonia Bompastor is set to make a return to her old stomping ground hoping to take all three points back to the English capital.
Matches elsewhere include Benfica hosting Bayern Munich, Arsenal travelling to Paris FC, and Roma facing the tough test of welcoming a formidable Barcelona to Stadio Tre Fontane.
Opta Analyst presents data-driven predictions for each game from MD2, powered by the Opta supercomputer’s pre-match simulations.
There are three 5:45pm kick-offs to start the matchday on Wednesday as BK Häcken, Paris FC and Roma host the first set of matches.
For inaugural 2025-26 UEFA Women’s Europa Cup winners Häcken, the supercomputer backs them to get the Italian job done this week after a tight 1-0 defeat at the hands of Inter Milan last time out.

This week’s opponents are six-time Serie A champions Juventus. The Bianconere won their opening league match of the season 2-0 against Napoli at the weekend, but tasted defeat in the UWCL at the hands of Portuguese outfit Benfica.
Häcken have lost each of their last three UWCL matches, equalling their longest-ever losing streak in the competition, previously set between 17 November 2021 and 15 December 2021.

The supercomputer predicts a similar fate for Juve this time around; Häcken came out victorious in 64.5% of pre-match simulations. In fact, the simulations saw more draws (19.0%) than wins for Juventus (16.5%).

Elsewhere, two-time UWCL winners Arsenal travel to the French capital to play Paris FC as they look to improve on their 1-0 win against HB Køge. The Gunners netted a stoppage-time penalty to sugarcoat what was otherwise a limp performance against the Danish side.
The big headscratcher for Renée Slegers is quite simply how to get the ball in the back of the net.

A disappointing 1-0 defeat against rivals Chelsea at the weekend leaves Arsenal seventh in the WSL table, having failed to score in two of their four games. In fact, only newly-promoted Charlton Athletic (3) have failed to score more often in league this season.

It will be the first meeting between Paris FC and Arsenal in the UWCL, with the French side having lost each of their previous three matches against English opponents in the competition, all against Chelsea (1-4, 0-4 and 0-4 between 2023 and 2025).

The Gunners came out victorious 1-0 in a pre-season friendly against their opponents this summer, and the supercomputer backs Slegers' side to start the UWCL campaign with back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022-23, coming out on top in 63.5% of the computer's 10,000 pre-match simulations.
The third and final early kick-off Wednesday has to offer comes in the form of Roma against competition giants, and favourites Barcelona.

Barça, perhaps unsurprisingly, are flying high once again this season boasting a perfect record in Liga F after five games, having scored 21 times and conceded just twice. Their quest for a fifth UWCL crown got off to a great start too as Barça dominated Servette in an 8-0 win last week.
Before the start of this year’s edition, the Opta supercomputer heavily favoured Barcelona ending the tournament as winners once again; the Blaugrana won the trophy in 41.2% of simulations.

          Late Goals, Struggles Versus 10 Men, Unable to Hold a Lead: Do Man Utd Have a Mentality Problem?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 13, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester United once again failed to make the most of their opposition having a man sent off on Saturday, but that's not the only reason some critics might question their mentality.

It hadn’t been pretty, but Manchester United were practically there; just their second win of the Premier League season was within touching distance as they entered the final 10 minutes of regulation time against Tottenham 1-0 up and with a man advantage at Old Trafford.

Rodrigo Bentancur nudging his forehead into Luke Shaw’s face in response to the United full-back shoving him to the floor yielded a red card for the Uruguayan with 78 minutes on the clock. It capped a bad few moments for Spurs, who’d gone behind to Bryan Mbeumo’s well-placed finished just five minutes earlier.

Bentancur’s dismissal was, obviously, greeted with jubilation among the majority of those at Old Trafford. For Michael Carrick on the touchline, thoughts must have turned to how his team were going to react to the situation.

He won’t have needed any reminding about what occurred the last time United played against a team with 10 men, when they seemed to wilt under the added expectation that accompanied Phil Foden’s red card in last month’s 1-0 Manchester derby defeat, highly controversial though Manchester City's win was.
At least on this occasion United already had the lead and only needed to hold on for 12 minutes plus added time.

Of course, they didn’t manage to. Sandro Tonali’s cross in the second minute of stoppage time was glanced in by Dominic Solanke during his intimate embrace/wrestling bout with Lisandro Martínez, and Tottenham – deservedly, it should be emphasised – equalised to ultimately earn a 1-1 draw.

Tottenham were comfortably the better team over the course of the 90 minutes, to the point where even a win for United wouldn’t have earned them or Carrick that much credit. Spurs went into the game bottom of the table but played their hosts off the park at times, especially during the first 30 minutes.
The outcome produced two especially damning facts for United.

Firstly, it was the third successive occasion on which they’d failed to beat a team who started the day bottom of the table, having also drawn 1-1 with Fulham prior to the international break and with Wolves in December 2025.

Then, it was also the third time in a row that they’d failed to defeat opposition who’d been reduced to 10 men, the other occasions being at home to City last month (1-0 loss) and at Newcastle in March (2-1 loss).

Considering those facts, it’s perfectly understandable that United’s mentality might be called into question. All are instances where they would be favourites to win, even accounting for City being a very, very good team who benefited from a goal that shouldn't have stood.
Aside from the aforementioned controversy surrounding Erling Haaland's goal, there aren’t really any redeeming factors from the six games noted.

In December’s 1-1 draw with rock-bottom Wolves at Old Trafford, United were desperately poor, generating just 0.84 xG to their visitors’ 1.16. And this was a Wolves side who finished 2025 with the worst points-per-game ratio (0.76) over a full year of Premier League football since 2018 (Huddersfield Town – 0.62).

In the loss to 10-man Newcastle, the Red Devils had the whole second half with an extra man. But even then, the two best chances of the second period fell to Newcastle, and neither of them even resulted in a goal.
And the draw with Fulham last month; sure, United were unfortunate to trail to Martínez’s own goal, but they were also very lucky to earn a point via Matheus Cunha’s late deflected shot.

Many United fans will also remember November’s dismal 1-0 home defeat to Everton, when the visitors had Idrissa Gueye sent off in the 13th minute for tussling with his own teammate. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall netted 16 minutes later and that proved decisive.
It could all be a massive coincidence. After all, there have been other occasions since the start of last season when United have overcome 10-man opposition or other teams they’d be expected to beat.
But situations like Saturday have become all too familiar; and it is increasingly difficult to argue it’s just a coincidence.
Since the start of last season in all competitions, United have played seven matches in which their opponents have been reduced to 10 men; they’ve won just three of them, losing as many.

          Arsenal's Struggles, Sonia Bompastor Makes WSL History, and More: Five WSL Talking Points From Matchday 6
        
      
                          
                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Matchday 6 delivered another dramatic weekend of WSL action, with Arsenal's struggles continuing, Chelsea and Manchester City maintaining their strong starts, and London City Lionesses continuing to make headlines.
The WSL returned for Matchday 6 after the international break and, as ever, there was no shortage of talking points.

Arsenal's struggles deepened with another frustrating result, Chelsea and Manchester City maintained their perfect starts at the top, while London City Lionesses continued to prove they belong among the division's frontrunners.
Elsewhere, Aston Villa produced one of the comebacks of the weekend to inflict a surprise defeat on Liverpool.
Here are our biggest takeaways from the latest round of action.
Arsenal's difficult start to the season showed little sign of improving as they were held 1-1 by Birmingham City, with familiar issues at both ends of the pitch again coming to the fore.
While the Gunners dominated stretches of possession, they lacked the cutting edge to turn pressure into goals and were exposed defensively.

The result extended Arsenal's winless run to five WSL matches, the longest such streak in the club's history. They are now also without a win in their last two league meetings with promoted opposition; their longest such run against promoted teams in the competition.

There was a sense of inevitability about Arsenal's attacking struggles. They have scored just five goals in six league matches this season, with no WSL side finding themselves in a more frustrating position in front of goal.

Arsenal are the only team that have hit the woodwork (5) as many times as they've scored goals (also 5). They've now gone four consecutive home league games without scoring in the first half for the first time since a five-match run between April and October 2023.

When Arsenal did finally find the net, it came through Olivia Smith's excellent finish from distance, a goal met almost with relief among the home support. It was Smith's first WSL goal since March and ended the longest league scoring drought of her career, at 12 matches.

Birmingham City's disciplined back line repeatedly withstood Arsenal pressure, with all four members of the visitors' defence recording 11 or more clearances (Millie Turner – 12, Shannon Cooke – 12, Rebecca McKenna – 11, Neve Herron – 11). It is the first time in WSL history that four players from the same team have each made at least 11 clearances in a single match, which just highlights Arsenal's inability to break down teams in a low block.

With just six points from their opening six matches, this is Arsenal's second-worst start to a WSL campaign, better only than their four-point return in 2014. No side has gone on to win the WSL title after collecting as few as six points from their first six matches.

If there were any doubts about Sonia Bompastor's ability to sustain Chelsea's dominance, they are fading fast. Chelsea's 6-2 win over Tottenham was a statement performance, and it moved Bompastor onto 125 points from her first 50 WSL matches, the most by any manager at that stage of their career in the competition, overtaking Joe Montemurro (123).

The Blues scored six times from just eight shots on target. That's the highest shots-on-target conversion rate (75%) Chelsea have ever recorded in a WSL match in which they've scored five or more goals, showing just how clinical they were against Spurs.
It was also the first time the Blues had scored six goals in a WSL game since their 6-0 victory over Crystal Palace in September 2024.
The defeat compounded a miserable afternoon for Tottenham, who've now lost consecutive WSL matches by four or more goals for the first time in their history.

Chelsea's attacking fluidity was on show throughout the contest. Four players recorded at least two goal involvements in the same WSL match for the first time since May 2023, with Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter scoring twice each, while Keira Walsh and Alyssa Thompson each registered two assists.
James continues to add greater end product to her game. Her average of 1.2 goals per 90 minutes this season is the highest scoring rate of her WSL career.
Carpenter became the first Chelsea defender to score multiple goals in a WSL match since Maren Mjelde against West Ham in February 2020, underlining her growing influence in attacking areas.

067CE17E8D98F8BF229076DD4D02C482.title: Preview: PSG face Barça in Champions League blockbuster
067CE17E8D98F8BF229076DD4D02C482.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: PSG face Barça in Champions League blockbusterShareTuesday sees a high-octane meeting in the Champions League between the competition’s two highest-scoring teams.

The Champions League holders are back in stellar form after a poor start to the Ligue 1 season and Luis Enrique‘s star-studded squad come in to the game on an impressive six-match winning streak across all competitions, including a couple of high-scoring victories on the continent. Paris Saint-Germain put six past Slovan Bratislava and four past Manchester City, respectively, to set a new competition record for goals scored after two rounds of the league phase. The Parisians are averaging 3.1 goals on their current run and are undefeated against Barcelona in the previous two meetings between the sides.

Remarkably, the reigning LaLiga champions are in even more impressive form than PSG, as Barça are on an 11-match winning streak, or more precisely, celebrating a victory in each and every match this campaign. Furthermore, the in-form Raphinha & co. have scored an incredible 48 goals in total, averaging 4.3 per match, which is by some distance the highest across Europe's top 5 leagues. In the Champions League, no club is enjoying more time on the ball (71.3% possession) or completing more accurate passes per match (686.5) than the Blaugrana.

Ousmane Dembélé is waiting to find out whether he will keep hold of the prestigious Ballon d'Or award for another year, but the 29-year-old is already strengthening his case to be a strong contender at next year's ceremony. The French international is averaging a FotMob rating of 9.04 in the Champions League and no player is boasting more goals and assists (six) in the competition. Lamine Yamal is one behind on five. Further confirmation of his exceptional form came in the form of his cameo off the bench against Strasbourg on Saturday, when the lethal forward scored a goal and recorded an assist in just 27 minutes spent on the pitch.

Frenkie de Jong returned to the Barcelona squad over the weekend, for the first time since May, and the comeback of the 29-year-old will provide a timely boost for Hansi Flick amid the mounting injuries and the busy schedule. With only Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín being available at centre-back, it will be no surprise if the Netherlands international or Rodri fill in at the heart of the defence given their qualities and rich experience. Last, but definitely not least, the former Ajax prodigy (297 apps) is closing in on a landmark 300th appearance in the Blaugrana shirt and the midfielder is set to play a vital role once again this season.

Eric García and Jules Koundé did not make the trip to Paris after getting injured against Real Betis, giving Flick a headache with Andreas Christensen also sidelined. On a positive note, Frenkie de Jong is back and ready to play.For PSG, Nuno Mendes will miss Tuesday's clash due to a thigh injury and the same goes for Senny Mayulu, but Maghnes Akliouche is fit after an injury scare on Sunday and everyone else should be available.

With both PSG and Barça in free-scoring form and most of their past meetings being goal fests, I expect more of the same at the Parc des Princes. But given Barcelona's injury troubles in defence, I would not be surprised if their perfect start to the season ends in the City of Light.

The Parisians are averaging 3.1 goals on their current run and are undefeated against Barcelona in the previous two meetings between the sides.

Remarkably, the reigning LaLiga champions are in even more impressive form than PSG, as Barça are on an 11-match winning streak, or more precisely, celebrating a victory in each and every match this campaign. Furthermore, the in-form Raphinha & co. have scored an incredible 48 goals in total, averaging 4.3 per match, which is by some distance the highest across Europe's top 5 leagues. In the Champions League, no club is enjoying more time on the ball (71.3% possession) or completing more accurate passes per match (686.5) than the Blaugrana.

Ousmane Dembélé is waiting to find out whether he will keep hold of the prestigious Ballon d'Or award for another year, but the 29-year-old is already strengthening his case to be a strong contender at next year's ceremony. The French international is averaging a FotMob rating of 9.04 in the Champions League and no player is boasting more goals and assists (six) in the competition. Lamine Yamal is one behind on five. Further confirmation of his exceptional form came in the form of his cameo off the bench against Strasbourg on Saturday, when the lethal forward scored a goal and recorded an assist in just 27 minutes spent on the pitch.

Frenkie de Jong returned to the Barcelona squad over the weekend, for the first time since May, and the comeback of the 29-year-old will provide a timely boost for Hansi Flick amid the mounting injuries and the busy schedule. With only Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín being available at centre-back, it will be no surprise if the Netherlands international or Rodri fill in at the heart of the defence given their qualities and rich experience. Last, but definitely not least, the former Ajax prodigy (297 apps) is closing in on a landmark 300th appearance in the Blaugrana shirt and the midfielder is set to play a vital role once again this season.

Eric García and Jules Koundé did not make the trip to Paris after getting injured against Real Betis, giving Flick a headache with Andreas Christensen also sidelined. On a positive note, Frenkie de Jong is back and ready to play.For PSG, Nuno Mendes will miss Tuesday's clash due to a thigh injury and the same goes for Senny Mayulu, but Maghnes Akliouche is fit after an injury scare on Sunday and everyone else should be available.

With both PSG and Barça in free-scoring form and most of their past meetings being goal fests, I expect more of the same at the Parc des Princes. But given Barcelona's injury troubles in defence, I would not be surprised if their perfect start to the season ends in the City of Light.

          Vertical, Relentless, Effective: The Tottenham Transformation Under Martin Ho
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Martin Ho has overseen a remarkable turnaround at Tottenham. From an 11th-place finish two seasons ago to one of the WSL's most exciting and progressive teams, and just one of four unbeaten sides this season after three games. How close are Spurs to closing the gap on the division's elite?

Tottenham Hotspur's 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace may have been the performance that turned heads in the Women's Super League this weekend, but the foundations for such a display have been building for some time.

Just over a year ago, Spurs were coming off an 11th-place finish and searching for a new direction. While there had been flashes of progress in earlier seasons, including fifth- and sixth place finishes in 2021-22 and 2023-24 respectively, their slide towards the bottom end of the table in 2024-25 underlined the gap that still existed to the league's leading clubs.
Since Martin Ho's arrival in July 2025, however, that trajectory has changed dramatically.

Tottenham collected a club-record 36 WSL points in Ho's first season in charge, winning 11 matches and returning to fifth place. Indeed, that points tally was the most ever by an English manager in their debut season in the competition.
Since taking the reins, Ho has overseen 13 WSL victories in just 25 matches, with only Manchester City (21), Chelsea (17) and Arsenal (16) winning more games in that period.
And their start to the 2026-27 campaign suggests that progress has continued.
Spurs are one of only four unbeaten teams remaining in the division, and sit second in the table after three matches, just behind Man City.

Tottenham are currently enjoying a six-match unbeaten run in the competition, equalling the longest in the club's WSL history, and the first since such a six-game streak between October-November 2023. The challenge now is sustaining that momentum.
They face the third-toughest fixture run in the division over their next five WSL games according to the Opta Power Rankings, coming up against London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal.
That makes their start even more intriguing.

Spurs won four of their opening five WSL games last season, before winning just seven of their remaining 17. This time around, Ho will be hoping his side can bridge that gap to the league’s elite, and, crucially, sustain their strong start across the entirety of the campaign.
The meetings with the ‘big four' will provide a significant test, but there is growing evidence that Spurs are closer to that level than they have been before.
Ho's emphasis on brave, front-foot football combined with defensive discipline is already evident in Tottenham's early-season performances, none more so than their 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace.

While the visitors were helped by Palace being reduced to 10 players after just seven minutes, scoring seven goals at WSL level is no simple task. After all, this was a Palace side that had drawn 0-0 against Arsenal at Emirates Stadium just a week earlier despite facing 30 shots.
The manner of Tottenham's dominance was particularly striking. Spurs registered 42 shots, the third-highest total in WSL history, and the most ever recorded by an away side in the competition.

They also amassed 82 touches in the opposition box, the most by Tottenham in a WSL match and the joint fourth-highest total ever recorded in the league. No team had reached that figure since Chelsea managed 82 against Leicester City in December 2024.
On top of that, the game was goalless at the break, with all seven goals coming in a ruthless second half.

There were standout individual performances.Olivia Holdt became just the second Tottenham player to score a WSL hat-trick, after Martha Thomas against Aston Villa in October 2023, while Amanda Nildén‘s late goal perfectly captured the collective nature of Spurs' attacking play.
Nildén's 86th-minute strike came at the end of a 37-second move involving nine different Tottenham players, the most players involved in a single WSL goal this season.

08308F6B7325AA01555C6E23B19AA180.title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?
08308F6B7325AA01555C6E23B19AA180.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsSport AfricaWhy has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?Image source, ReutersImage caption, Sadio Mane's Senegal won Afcon 2025 but the result was later overturned in favour of Morocco, and the Court of Arbitration for Sport will determine the ultimate destination of the title
After a shock announcement 10 months ago that the Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) would be held every four years, the governing body of football on the continent has reversed course.

The Confederation of African Football (Caf) will instead retain the tournament's traditional biennial staging, with its president Patrice Motsepe saying the U-turn was based on "advancing, protecting and promoting" the interests of the African game.
The first indication that the frequency of Afcon was being reconsidered came at Caf's strategy conference in Cape Verde earlier this month.
Questions are now being asked about the decision-making process and what this means for the future of African football.
Afcon has predominantly been held every two years since its first edition in 1957, barring two three-year gaps in the 1960s and one year between the 2012 and 2013 tournaments.
On the eve of the 2025 finals in Morocco, Motsepe announced all that would change from 2028.
The South African said the shift to a four-year cycle was, in part, to help the global calendar "be significantly more synchronised and harmonised".
In recent years Afcon has been staged midway through the European club season, leading to recurring disputes over the release of African players.

Fifa general secretary Mattias Grafstrom was sitting aside Motsepe when the plan was announced, and critics highlighted that the scheduling change favoured football's world governing body more than the African game.
"I think the general sentiment around the continent has been that the two-year cycle has served the continent very well," Football Association of Zambia (Faz) official Sydney Mungala told the BBC.
"The idea of pushing it to a four-year cycle was a bit of a surprise, maybe a concern, to the bulk of the African federations."
Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn
Published11 hours agoAfcon to be held every four years from 2028

Published20 December 2025What were the benefits of the switch?Afcon has developed into Caf's biggest revenue generator, with a profit of $114m (£85m) forecast for Afcon 2025, up from $75m (£56m) for the previous finals in Ivory Coast.
In its stead, an annual Africa Nations League involving all 54 countries on the continent was proposed. Motsepe described the ambition as creating a "world-class competition every year".
The idea was to move beyond Caf's heavy reliance on Afcon and develop a more sustainable commercial model which could support football development.
Yet the last time an ambitious alternative competition took place in Africa, it failed to deliver on its financial promise and was quickly ditched.
The Africa Super League, announced by Caf in 2022 to revolutionise continental club competition, and with projected annual revenues of $200m (£149m), was discontinued after just one edition.
Motsepe later acknowledged that commercial deals fell short of expectations.

084418D3C7670A753DF35CB4FE0A3B8A.title: Preview: Chelsea welcome the winless Cherries to the Bridge
084418D3C7670A753DF35CB4FE0A3B8A.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Chelsea welcome the winless Cherries to the BridgeShareThe Premier League (finally) returns this week following the conclusion of the three-week international break.
Chelsea welcome Bournemouth to Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon in what could be a crucial match, especially with the league struggles of both teams of late.
Alonso led his new side to four wins from their opening five matches in all competitions this season, with their only defeat coming against reigning Premier League champions Arsenal.
Even then, Chelsea took an early lead and showed plenty of promise during the game and it looked as though Alonso might just be the man to lead the club into a new era.

In the two most recent games before the international break, Chelsea drew 2-2 with Hull before suffering a truly dismal 3-0 defeat to Brentford. In truth, the Bees could have had more than their three goals, registering 13 shots in total.
Alonso’s side may have the joint-third best attacking record in the top flight, yet the Blues have conceded 12 times in just five matches – the worst defensive record.
There has been some positives, but until there are improvements defensively, Chelsea wont be a factor this term.
Bournemouth were always going to take time to adapt to Andoni Iraola’s departure at the end of last season, especially given how successful he was on the south coast.
Marco Rose was appointed, but the Cherries are still awaiting their first Premier League win of the campaign.
Against Manchester City on matchday one, Bournemouth were leading until the 84th minute, but then conceded twice to lose 2-1. It was a solid display, however, and the club have only lost once since.

Those defeats were sandwiched by three successive draws, leaving Rose’s men 17th in the table. Plenty of encouragement should be taken from the 2-1 Europa league win over Real Sociedad, yet questions will be asked until they finally claim a maiden league win of the season.
Despite losing four of their previous eight encounters against Chelsea, given how poor the Blues have been defensively this term, Bournemouth might not have a better chance to end that drought.

Chelsea came through the recent international break unscathed, with none of their nine-strong contingent reporting back injured. Cole Palmer did withdraw from the England squad, but he it looks like he will be fit to play on Saturday.
Alonso’s only absentee will be Jamie Gittens, who suffered an ankle injury playing for England U21s recently.

Rose hasn’t quite been so lucky. Alex Scott is now out for between 6-8 weeks after representing England during the break, while the likes of Eli Junior Kroupi, Julián Araujo and Justin Kluivert are also missing for this clash.
David Brooks is a doubt and it remains to be seen whether he features.
Given the form of both teams prior to the international break, either side could secure all three points in this match.
Chelsea will be determined to return to winning ways, while Bournemouth are aiming to win their first Premier League game since May 9.
Goals are inevitable and I can see this tie ending in a high-scoring draw: Chelsea 2-2 Bournemouth.

          Do Premier League Teams Really Need to Run More to Win?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Ruben Diaz / Design, Peter McKeever / Data Viz, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
These days, running stats are regularly wheeled out and portrayed as key identifiers of underperforming teams, but there's little evidence to suggest covering more ground means you're a better team in the long run.
Manchester United dropped points again in Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical stats to make certain points.

Former Tottenham midfielder Jamie Redknapp, working as a pundit on Sky Sports, said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. [On Saturday] Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Man Utd.”

Physical metrics such as distance run and number of sprints are increasingly accessible in modern football, and given they’re hardly complex to understand in essence, it stands to reason that they might fall into common use.
And they have. Man Utd fans may be more acutely aware of this than supporters of any other club in recent weeks.

It’s become a common theme that when United fail to meet expectations, pundits, commentators, social media personalities et cetera will look to their running metrics in search of one catch-all explanation.

This obviously isn’t only used for United, in fairness. Liverpool and Chelsea were also the targets of similar judgement last season, so we aren’t trying to suggest there’s some kind of conspiracy here. It just feels particularly pertinent given the discourse often surrounding Michael Carrick’s team.
But is it fair? How much of a correlation actually is there between a team running lots and that team being successful?

While the numbers may not be complex at face value, answering this question is, which probably highlights that such metrics are so nuanced in a team sport that it likely isn’t best practice to tie too much significance to the topline figures.
Either way, it’s a question worth digging into.

The first way we can assess it is by comparing the Premier League table to the rankings of distance run and high-intensity distance – yes, this is pretty simple and rudimentary, but it’s a place to start.

As you can see below, last season’s Premier League table hardly mirrors the rankings for distance covered or high-intensity distance per game. Sure, Arsenal and Manchester City were high for overall distance, but the teams who came third to eighth had middling – at best – outputs in this respect.

The teams who finished in the top 10 averaged 4,363km over the course of the season; those who finished in the bottom 10 averaged 4,332km. In the grand scheme of things, a difference of 31km between those averages is rather small.
Again, there’s a slight difference between the average high-intensity distance for top-10 teams (338.7km) and those in the bottom 10 (328.4km), but we’re talking about an increase of just 3.0%.
Similarly when perusing data from this season, it's difficult to see much of a link.

Looking at it in relation to the table does ignore that success is relative, however. Of course Burnley weren’t going to finish seventh in the table just because they came seventh in the distance rankings.

Instead, we can use the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions to give us an idea of what a successful campaign (or at least in line with expectations) may have looked like for all clubs and whether there was a trend of overachieving teams also running more than others.

There were 10 teams in the Premier League last season who finished at least one place higher than their likeliest final place according to the Opta supercomputer in pre-season, and they averaged 4,369km over the season; the nine clubs who finished at least a place below their likeliest final position averaged 4,308km. So again, there is a difference, it’s just very small at a 1.4% increase from the latter to the former.

However, Sunderland (+13 places) and Man Utd (+9 places) weren’t in the top 10 for distance covered but exceeded the supercomputer’s expectations to a greater degree than any other team; Crystal Palace (-8 places) and Newcastle (-6 places) were in the top 10 for ground covered but were among the most disappointing teams relative to pre-season expectations.

We can also look at expected points, a model that simulates the goals scored by each side in each match based on the xG value of all shots and then simulates every game 10,000 times to determine the proportion that the fixtures end with a win, draw or defeat. It isn’t perfect as it's limited by the natural pitfalls of xG, but it does give a decent barometer of performance over a season.

092C8F239593CAA8FA023AE0C0DAFF02.title: Wrexham fined for fielding ineligible players
092C8F239593CAA8FA023AE0C0DAFF02.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsWrexhamScores & FixturesTableTop ScorersWrexham fined for fielding ineligible playersImage source, Getty Images/ShutterstockImage caption, Callum O'Hare (left) and Issa Kabore (right) joined Wrexham on permanent deals during the 2026 summer transfer window
Wrexham have been fined £75,000 - of which £25,000 is suspended - by the English Football League after two incidents of fielding ineligible players this season.
The EFL ruled that Issa Kabore and Callum O'Hare were ineligible to feature in Wrexham's games against Birmingham and Millwall, respectively.
Kabore came off the bench in Wrexham's 2-1 defeat by Birmingham City on 28 August, despite his Home Office 'right to work' documents not being correctly uploaded.
O'Hare, having joined from Sheffield United the day before, was an unused substitute in Wrexham's 3-0 win at Millwall on 2 September, though his documentation was not uploaded in time.
A club statement read: "We can confirm that Wrexham AFC has reached an agreed decision with the EFL concerning two breaches relating to player eligibility."
Unlucky seven? Wrexham aim to buck bizarre trend
Published1 day agoThe EFL's investigation states that Wrexham ignored an official warning via the system which hosts team sheets that Kabore was ineligible.
Kabore was highlighted by a red bar, and the disciplinary commission rejected the suggestion that the warning disappeared upon closing and reopening the app.
O'Hare had been successfully registered before Wrexham's defeat at Millwall, though not in time to be eligible to play at the Den.

The findings state that Wrexham had three applications rejected before the 25-year-old's registration was confirmed at 11:15 am on Wednesday, 2 September - nearly 24 hours after the eligibility deadline.
Wrexham were also noted to have initially submitted "substantially incomplete documents" which the Football Association rejected.
The Red Dragons are said to have had a full understanding of the rules, but the fact O'Hare did not feature from the bench was also noted by the disciplinary committee.
Wrexham - currently 17th in the Championship - admitted the second breach and have committed to a combination of recruitment and training to avoid a repeat of such matters.
They are thought to be hiring a club secretary in addition to improving administrative training.

A club official told BBC Sport Wales that the incidents involving Kabore and O'Hare were not the fault of boss Phil Parkinson, the club's coaching staff or new sporting director Steve Nickson - who was not officially appointed to his role until 7 September.
The Wrexham statement added: "The club is taking the appropriate steps to prevent such issues occurring in the future."

0A9A41300B4CB29B865CFBF90CE84AE9.title: Preview: Vinícius-less Real await stern Sevilla test in Madrid
0A9A41300B4CB29B865CFBF90CE84AE9.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Vinícius-less Real await stern Sevilla test in MadridShareSevilla’s last win at the Bernabéu dates back to 2008 and Real Madrid have been perfect at home so far this season.

Real Madrid produced a late eight-minute blitzkrieg to complete a dramatic comeback and silence the jubilant Stadio Olimpico upon José Mourinho‘s emotional return to Rome, with Los Blancos making it two wins from two in the Champions League. However, the Special One voiced his concerns about his defence afterwards, which has kept only a couple of clean sheets across all competitions this season.

With El Clásico next up in the league after this test against Sevilla, Thibaut Courtois must be worried about stopping Barcelona's lethal attack. Equally, Kylian Mbappé & co. (19 goals) are not too shabby either with only Barça scoring more goals after eight rounds in LaLiga.

Sevilla's six-goal thriller with Levante extended the Andalusia club's two-match winless run (1D, 1L) in LaLiga after Los Blanquirrojos were just minutes away from celebrating a hard-fought victory at Estadio Ciudad de Valencia.

On a brighter note, Luis García‘s squad enjoyed a decent start to the season and have surpassed expectations, sitting fifth in the standings and only four points behind Real. Furthermore, Los Nervionenses are destined to provide a stern physical test for Los Blancos, with no club averaging more (19.5) tackles per match or possession won in the final third per match (5.9) across the league.

Yan Diomande is still settling in a star-studded Madrid dressing room, but the lightning-quick winger is set for an extended run and more prominent role in the starting XI following Vinícius Júnior‘s reckless sending off last weekend. Also, the 19-year-old's debut goal in a white shirt proved to be the winner against Villarreal and the most expensive signing in the club's history is beginning to impress despite his restricted playing time in LaLiga so far. The Ivory Coast international has started only three of the eight matches played, but no player in the squad is averaging more successful dribbles per 90 (4.9).

Robbie Ure continues his rise to prominence and after making his Scotland debut over the past international break, the 22-year-old scored his first LaLiga goal against Levante. Subsequently, the skillful forward earned a FotMob rating of 8.5 and recorded an assist as well, his second of the campaign. Additionally, the Rangers academy product is leading the ranks in terms of goals + assists (3) and big chances created (2) among his teammates, and the No. 9 is expected to lead Sevilla's prolific attack at the Bernabéu.

Vinícius Júnior is set to miss Sunday's clash and the Brazil international will miss El Clásico as well due to his four-match suspension. Éder Militao and Ferland Mendy are back in first-team training, making Raúl Asencio and Rodrygo the only injured absentees.Similarly, Isaac Romero received a red card for offensive celebration following his stoppage-time goal at Levante and the striker will be absent from Luis García's squad, while Marcão and Miguel Sierra are injured.

The limelight will be on the officials at the Bernabéu following Real's constant complaints about the standard of refereeing in the league, but José Mourinho can't afford for his squad to slip up ahead of next week's Clásico.
I fully expect Los Blancos to find a way to secure an important win, although I do not think Sevilla will make it easy for them, especially given their relentlessly aggressive approach.

0CA986F4B63FF4ACDE9622D780659B0E.title: Preview: Monday night football see Spurs host Lampard’s Coventry City
0CA986F4B63FF4ACDE9622D780659B0E.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Monday night football see Spurs host Lampard’s Coventry CityShareTottenham Hotspur host Coventry City in a match that could prove pivotal to both teams’ hopes of climbing the table.
Sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table, it’s fair to say Tottenham Hotspur haven’t enjoyed the start to the season that Roberto De Zerbi and his players had hoped for.

However, the 1-1 draw against Manchester United offered Spurs hope that De Zerbi’s ideas and methods are finally taking root with the North London side unfortunate not to leave Old Trafford with all three points.
Coventry City are also hanging around the wrong end of the table having won just two of their opening six league fixtures since promotion from the Championship.
Of course, Frank Lampard’s newly promoted team were widely expected to be involved in the relegation scrap in some form and so their early-season form is less surprising than Tottenham’s.

Like Spurs, they are aiming to build on recent results after beating Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United in back-to-back games. If Coventry can replicate the form of their last outing against Newcastle, three wins on the bounce could be on the cards.
Coventry’s last top flight winning streak of three victories in a row came all the way back in 1998 under Gordon Strachan. Lampard and his players can make some history on Monday.

Dominic Solanke’s stoppage time equaliser gave Tottenham a share of the spoils against United with the 29-year-old expected to lead the line once again on Monday. No player had more shots than Solanke in last weekend’s match at Old Trafford.

Sandro Tonali had arguably his best game as a Spurs player last time out. The Italian midfielder will be a key figure for the home side in the centre of the pitch, offering energy on both sides of the ball.
Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke have shown signs of a burgeoning partnership in central defence recently, combining for 14 defensive contributions in the 1-1 draw against Manchester United.

Sidiki Cherif is expected to keep his place as Coventry’s starting centre forward after finding the back of the net in the rampant 4-1 win over Newcastle. The Frenchman’s movement will make him a threat on Monday.
Jack Rudoni also notched a goal against Newcastle and will be a supporting figure behind Cherif in the number 10 role. The 25-year-old has started the season strongly for Lampard’s team.

Matt Grimes and Caleb Yirenkyi are likely to retain their places as Lampard’s starting double pivot in the centre of the pitch with goalkeeper Carl Rushworth required to be in top form between the posts to keep Spurs out.
De Zerbi revealed in his pre-match press conference that Lucas Bergvall and Sávio will miss Monday’s match with Pedro Porro also likely to be unavailable for the hosts.
Mykhaylo Mudryk, Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons are similarly on the sidelines for Tottenham while Rodrigo Bentancur is suspended following his red card against Manchester United.
Taiwo Awoniyi has completed a three-game ban and will be back for Coventry against Spurs. However, Luke Woolfenden, Aurèle Amenda, Josh Eccles and Haji Wright are all expected to miss out.
We're thinking this will be a nervous but narrow, and much needed home win: Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 Coventry City.

          England vs Greece Prediction: Women's World Cup Play-Off Second Leg Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 12, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Following a slightly unconvincing 3-1 victory on Friday, England will look to seal their place in Round 2 of the qualification play-offs for the 2027 Women's World Cup. We preview the second leg with our England vs Greece prediction.
England take a two-goal advantage into Tuesday's second leg against Greece after a 3-1 victory in Crete put them firmly in control of their FIFA Women's World Cup 2027 play-off tie.

The Lionesses extended their unbeaten run against first-time European opposition in competitive matches to 16 games (W14 D2) with Friday's win. Yet, against a side sitting 54 places below them in the FIFA rankings, it was far from the straightforward evening many had anticipated.

Greece arrived in the tie full of confidence after topping Group C4, winning three and drawing one of their four qualifying matches. Although they ultimately fell to their first defeat of the campaign, they demonstrated exactly why England had been warned against complacency.

For Sarina Wiegman's side, however, the result continued an impressive record in World Cup qualifying. England have now won 20 of their last 21 such matches (L1), scoring 110 goals and conceding just three times across those 20 victories.

Should England complete the job at the King Power Stadium, they will progress to a Round 2 play-off against either Slovakia or Ukraine. The latter hold a commanding 3-1 advantage after the first leg of their tie.
Against Greece on Friday, England's breakthrough came from Georgia Stanway, whose goal just before half-time once again underlined her importance to this side.

The Arsenal midfielder is now England's joint-leading scorer under Wiegman with 32 goals, level with Beth Mead, while her 34 senior international goals place her outright seventh in the Lionesses' all-time scoring charts.
Indeed, she is one contribution away from becoming the second player to reach 50+ goal involvements (also 17 assists) under the Dutch manager after Mead (58).
Her partnership with Keira Walsh remains central to England's success.

The Lionesses have won 40 of the 60 matches the pair have started together (D9 L11), while Walsh could make yet more history after starting each of England's last 24 matches in all competitions. This century, only Rachel Unitt (35), Steph Houghton (26) and Alex Scott (25) have enjoyed longer consecutive starting streaks.

Interestingly, Lucy Bronze’s absence means she has now missed back-to-back competitive England fixtures for the first time since Wiegman's opening six matches in charge between September and November 2021.
History suggests England should have little trouble seeing the tie through on home soil.

The Lionesses have won each of their last seven home matches against fellow UEFA nations by an aggregate score of 19-0 and have lost just one of their last 48 competitive home fixtures (W41 D6), a 2-1 defeat to France in May 2024.
Wiegman's side are also unbeaten across 26 home qualifiers (W24 D2), scoring 120 goals while remarkably keeping a clean sheet in every one of those matches.
The first leg brought some individual milestones.

Erica Meg Parkinson (18 years, 174 days) came off the bench to become England's youngest debutant since Lianne Sanderson in 2006, while Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier netted her first senior international goal on her 15th appearance. England remain unbeaten in matches in which a United player has scored, winning 29 and drawing one of those 30 games.

Alessia Russo continued her impressive England form, as she both scored and assisted in a competitive match for England for the third time. The Arsenal forward has now registered 11 goal involvements in 11 World Cup qualifying appearances (nine goals, two assists).

Russo's strike in the 67th minute was her 23rd goal in 50 international starts. Among England players this century, only Mead (30) has scored more goals in her first 50 starts, while Kelly Smith also managed 23.

For Greece, Veatriki Sarri will return to familiar surroundings at the King Power. The midfielder has made four WSL appearances at the venue for three different clubs, winning just once, while one of her nine WSL goals came against England goalkeeper Hannah Hampton when Birmingham City faced Aston Villa in May 2022.

0D97A8DB20B69AEB2D3185A442A8B1DE.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsPremier LeagueScores & FixturesTableFollow Your TeamTransfersTop ScorersGossipBritain's first £100m man facing defining momentImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jack Grealish was excluded from Everton's squad to face Newcastle United in the Carabao Cup for "a breach of club" discipline

Chief football writerPublished1 hour agoWhen Jack Grealish breezed back into Everton in his white Lamborghini one hour before the end of this summer's transfer deadline, the excitement among supporters and the player himself was clearly evident.

Grealish's previous spell on loan from Manchester City had been cut short by a serious foot injury, but the 31-year-old had produced enough moments of excitement to make his return to the Finch Farm training base a rare moment of joy amid a miserable summer in the transfer market.

When Grealish finally left in the early hours - with the deal done, every autograph signed and every selfie posed for - it was a sort of homecoming for an everyman personality Everton fans had come to regard as one of their own.

This was a move with a lot riding on it - for Everton manager David Moyes, who had been left with only 18 senior players after a botched transfer window, and especially for Grealish, whose exile from City at the start of the final year of his contract confirmed his banishment.
Now, Grealish's future and Everton's faith in him, has reached a defining moment.
Grealish's exclusion from Everton's squad before the Carabao Cup tie at home to Newcastle was publicly described as "a breach of club discipline".

Specifically, it was a failure to turn up for training on Monday, leaving the talented maverick - who was Britain's first £100m footballer when he signed for City from Aston Villa in summer 2021 - facing another rebuild in his career.
Everton's decision to go public before the game with the reasons for Grealish's absence emphasised the seriousness of his transgression.
The fall-out means this now looks increasingly like Grealish's 'now or never' moment, because failure at Everton will surely mark a downward spiral from the top echelons of the Premier League.

Everton do not regard this week's misdemeanour as marking the proverbial 'Last Chance Saloon' for Grealish. Moyes does not have enough players at his disposal to make rapid outcasts of potential game-changers.
But it increases the pressure on the former England forward to win back the faith of fans who love his obvious enjoyment of life and the magic he has shown he can produce.
Moyes will hope it is a harsh lesson learned, because Everton now have even more to play for, given Wembley has suddenly come into view in the Carabao Cup.

BBC Sport believes there have been occasional time-keeping issues with Grealish in the past, but nothing on this scale from a personality regarded as a hard trainer who, in general, keeps himself in good condition.

Grealish has held talks with those in authority at Everton, where it is sure to have been made crystal clear there must be no repeat, certainly not under a strict disciplinarian such as Moyes, and he must now attempt to be rehabilitated back into the squad.
The inevitable decision to punish Grealish, taken at a high level within the club but with input and full support from Moyes, leaves him at the crossroads.

That is especially the case because Everton gave arguably their best performance of the season to beat Newcastle United 3-1 and set up a quarter-final at League Two Fleetwood Town, conquerors of Premier League champions Arsenal in the last round.
And it was done with the more dynamic style of 20-year-old Tyrique George playing on the left flank, which Grealish might have been expected to occupy.

          Greece vs England Prediction: Women's World Cup Play-Off First Leg Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The reigning European champions find themselves on an unlikely path to the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup. We look ahead to England's play-off first leg against Greece as Sarina Wiegman's side begin their bid to secure qualification for the tournament.

England find themselves in the unfamiliar position of having to navigate the FIFA Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs, kicking off against Greece on Friday at the Pankritio Stadium, a side they have never faced in their history across all international competitions.
It is the first time since September 2010 the Lionesses have found themselves in such a position.

England finished runners-up to Spain in their League A UEFA Women's World Cup qualifying group after a damaging 4-0 defeat to the world champions on Matchday 5. Although the reigning European champions won the reverse fixture 1-0, Spain claimed automatic qualification on a head-to-head basis.

What perhaps is most remarkable is that England's overall numbers were still among the best in qualifying. Only Germany (16) collected more points than the Lionesses (15), while only Spain (21) and Germany (18) scored more goals than England (13).

It does raise an interesting question about the qualification format. Despite ranking among the competition's strongest teams by some of the most important metrics, England have been forced into the play-offs. That's a debate for another day, however.

That heavy defeat in Spain was significant beyond its impact on qualification. At 4-0, it was England's biggest loss in any competition since a 6-2 defeat to Germany in the final of the 2009 UEFA Women's Euros under Hope Powell.
As a result, Sarina Wiegman's side must now navigate the play-off route to secure their place at the tournament, having qualified for the last six editions.

Should the Lionesses progress past Greece across two legs, they will meet the winners of Slovakia's tie with Ukraine in the second round of play-offs to secure their place at the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup.
And all the data, as one would expect, points in the European champions' favour.
While England may not have expected to be here, they are no strangers to play-off football.

The Lionesses have contested six major tournament play-off ties previously, advancing from four, including routes to the 1999 and 2011 FIFA Women's World Cup finals and the 2001 UEFA Women's European Championship.

Greece, meanwhile, are still chasing a historic first appearance at either a Women's World Cup or Euros. This is only their second play-off tie for a major tournament, having lost 5-0 on aggregate to Belgium in qualifying for Euro 2025. There were encouraging signs within that tie, however, with Greece holding Belgium to a goalless draw in the first leg on home soil.
Recent form suggests this may not be as straightforward a task for England as the respective pedigrees of the two nations imply.

They have won just two of their last seven competitive away matches (D2 L3), having won 23 of their previous 25 such games (L2). Greece, by contrast, have lost only three of their last 10 home internationals (W4 D3).

For England, scoring first could prove crucial. Under Wiegman, they have won 51 of their 58 matches when opening the scoring (D5 L2), with their only defeats in such games coming against France in May 2024 and Spain in June 2025 (both 2-1).

Although there is no previous head-to-head history between the sides, England have plenty of experience when it comes to facing new European opposition. They are unbeaten in their last 15 competitive matches against a European nation they had never previously faced (W13 D2), scoring 87 goals and conceding just three. Their last defeat in such a fixture came against France in a World Cup qualifying play-off in October 2002.
England will also look to some of their key attacking talents to make the difference.

Georgia Stanway has scored against 22 different nations for the Lionesses, with only Ellen White (24), Kelly Smith (24) and Fara Williams (23) netting against more countries. The Arsenal midfielder is also England's leading scorer in 2027 World Cup qualifying with four goals.

Meanwhile, Lauren Hemp has been England's primary creative outlet in the qualifying campaign, creating more chances (13) and attempting more dribbles (28) than any other player, while also registering a joint-high two assists.
