          Everton 0-2 Chelsea: Neto Double Ends Toffees' Unbeaten Start
        
      
                          
                      Oct 17, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Pedro Neto scored his first ever Premier League brace to secure three points for Chelsea on the road. Re-live this clash with our Everton vs Chelsea stats page.
Pedro Neto‘s second-half brace secured Chelsea a 2-0 win over Everton, whose unbeaten start to the Premier League season came to an end.
An entertaining first half did not result in any goals, though Moisés Caicedo hit the woodwork with a stunning volley, and Neto was the star in a dominant Chelsea showing after the break.
The Portuguese scored within the first minute of the second half, and then secured all three points in the 90th minute, profiting from some poor Everton defending.
The hosts started well, with Emiliano Martínez holding onto Merlin Röhl‘s drilled effort, before getting fully behind Thierno Barry‘s glancing header on the set-piece.
Jack Grealish‘s bouncing volley then needed to be tipped over the bar before Vitalii Mykolenko skilfully opened up space to tee up Barry, who could only poke at Martínez on the turn.
After a couple of flashpoints, Chelsea finished the first half on top, with Caicedo smacking a powerful strike against the crossbar while unmarked from a corner.
And Maxence Lacroix got in front of his marker on another set-piece just before half-time, but his flicked header was cleared off the line by Harrison Armstrong.
Chelsea made a trademark fast start after the break, though, with Morgan Rogers linking up well with Jorrel Hato on the left, but the deflected cross was turned home by Neto.
Rogers continued to cause problems, with his first-time effort blocked by Rohl before Palmer attempted to catch Pickford out from the edge of the box, but the ball ended up in the stands.

Martinez was stretchered off in the 75th minute with a head injury following a clash with Jarrad Branthwaite, and though Everton tried to apply late pressure to substitute Mike Penders, they were instead almost caught out at the other end as Pickford had to make himself big to deny João Pedro following a Palmer-led counter-attack.

Chelsea eventually breached Everton's defence again ahead of a lengthy 11 minutes of stoppage time. Jordan Henderson‘s free-kick hit the wall, but the Toffees did not clear their lines, and Neto reacted quickest to slot into the bottom-left corner.

Chelsea have not had a lot of joy on their recent travels to Everton, winning just one of their previous nine such Premier League games (D2 L6) prior to this one, and they lost their first match at Hill Dickinson Stadium 3-0 last season.

However, Xabi Alonso's side made it back-to-back league wins, scoring as many goals on Saturday as they did in their last nine visits, though they had to ride their luck at times, especially in the first half.

Having netted twice in the opening three minutes against Bournemouth last time out, it was a slow start by Chelsea's standards, with this being the second-longest they have had to wait for a goal in the Premier League this season.

Tensions were high in the first half, with five yellow cards, though things settled down after the break, helped by Neto's goal. He has now scored more Premier League goals (12) for Chelsea (76 appearances) than he did for Wolves (111 apps).
This also marked the first time Neto has scored twice in a Premier League game in his 187th appearance in the competition.

But while the goals – and ultimately the win – will please Alonso, it is their defensive work that will bring him the most joy as they kept their first Premier League clean sheet since January. They had conceded in each of their 22 Premier League matches beforehand, but finally got their first shutout since a 2-0 home win over Brentford.
Our Opta match centre delivers you all the Everton vs Chelsea stats from their Premier League meeting at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday 17 October.
The match centre below includes team and player stats, expected goals data, passing networks, an Opta chalkboard and more. It gives you everything you need to do your own match analysis.

          Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham Stats: Palmer Sees Red as Penders Error Helps Gift Spurs Victory
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Mike Penders' calamitous own goal and a late strike from Mathys Tel saw Tottenham beat 10-man Chelsea 2-0 in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening.
Cole Palmer saw red as Tottenham Hotspur claimed a deserved 2-0 victory over a dismal Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.
Spurs had only won one of their last 36 league visits to Chelsea prior to Saturday's contest, with that triumph coming in 2017-18.
But Roberto De Zerbi's team ended that run, and claimed their second Premier League win of the campaign, thanks to a calamitous own goal from Mike Penders and Mathys Tel‘s sumptuous late strike.
Palmer's dismissal, which came between Spurs' goals, compounded a miserable day for Xabi Alonso, who suffered his first home defeat as Chelsea boss.
Spurs were dominant from the off, though it was not until the 29th minute that they created a clear opening, with Omar Marmoush firing at Penders from Andy Robertson's cutback.
Penders had to smother Tel's attempt soon after, but Jordan Henderson forced Antonin Kinsky into a save at the other end.
Pedro Neto forced Kinsky into action before the break, and Spurs were dealt a blow early in the second half as James Maddison was forced off injured.
Former Chelsea man Conor Gallagher came on in his place, and would go on to play a pivotal role, though only after Neto had drawn another stop out of Kinsky following Mateus Fernandes' error.
But Spurs' deserved goal arrived in the 77th minute.

Penders, who featured in the absence of Emiliano Martinez, came out to punch Fernandes' corner, but got it all wrong and instead flapped his attempted clearance back over his own line, with Maxence Lacroix unable to hook it clear.
Chelsea's misery was compounded when Palmer, nine minutes after he was booked for lashing out at Fernandes, received his second yellow card following a stamp on Gallagher.
Tel then capped off a superb Spurs win, charging through midfield and sending a low, crisp strike into the bottom-left corner from range.

While De Zerbi will feel it is finally clicking for his Spurs team, this was a bad, bad day for Alonso, and it showed the work he has to do to get this Chelsea side back to where the club's fans feel they should be.

Chelsea had just seven attempts, their fewest in a Premier League game this season and their fewest at home in the competition since January against Brentford (six). Spurs had 15 shots and created chances worth 0.74 expected goals to the Blues' 0.43.
They failed to score at home in a Premier League London derby for just the second time in their last 17 such games, after a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace on MD1 last season.
This also marks the first time Chelsea have been beaten by Spurs while also failing to score at Stamford Bridge since December 1986 (2-0).
Their performance was summed up by Palmer's petulance. The playmaker led Chelsea for chances created (two) but was far from his best, and his loss of temper proved costly.

Palmer's dismissal was the 100th red card Chelsea have been shown in the Premier League (excluding rescinded cards), with the Blues becoming the third team to reach this milestone after Everton (113) and Arsenal (110).

Penders, meanwhile, had a full Premier League debut to forget, as he became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to score an own goal in the competition, after Petr Cech against Everton in December 2009.

          UEFA Women's Champions League Predictions 2026-27: The Opta Supercomputer Projections
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Yash Thakur / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Who will win the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2026-27? Will Barcelona retain their crown? Here, we detail how the Opta supercomputer sees this season playing out.
The UEFA Women’s Champions League is back with its 18-team league-phase format for the 2026-27 season, and Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday.

Each team will play six games in the league phase, with the top four teams at the end securing direct qualification to the quarter-finals, while the teams ranked 5th to 12th will compete in a knockout play-off to book their place in the last eight.

Barcelona were crowned champions for the fourth time in their history after thrashing OL Lyonnes 4-0 in the final last season. Ewa Pajor and Salma Paralluelo both scored twice in the second half to secure the title.

In a summer of major moves, two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas departed Barcelona for the WSL, while Salma Paralluelo made the switch to Lyon. Arsenal and Lyon have both strengthened their already potent attacks, Real Madrid continue to build around an exciting young core, and Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Manchester City will all be firmly in the hunt for silverware this season.
So, which side has got the Opta supercomputer's backing for European glory?

Barcelona come into another season as the favourites to win the competition and equal their men’s team’s tally of five European titles. The Spanish champions have featured in all the UWCL finals this decade, being crowned champions four times.

Despite losing some long serving members of the squad this summer, Pere Romeu’s side came out winners in 41.2% of the supercomputer's simulations. The Blaugranas are the side to beat in Europe and have lost just three out of 38 games in the UWCL since the start of 2023, with all three losses coming against English sides (1-0 vs Arsenal on 24 May 2025, 2-0 vs Man City on 10 October 2024 and 1-0 vs Chelsea on 20 April 2024).

After losing out to eventual champions Barcelona in the semi-finals of the last edition, Bayern Munich are the second most likely side to win the competition this season with Opta’s supercomputer. José Barcala’s winning machine reached the final in 34.8% of the simulations and were crowned champions in 17.3% of them.

In fact, Bayern’s only two losses in all competitions last season came at the hands of Barcelona (7-1 in October and 4-2 in May). Although Georgia Stanway switched the Bavarians for Arsenal this summer, Barcala should feel confident in their attack of Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder, Edna Imade and others.
Bayern and Barça are set to face each other again in the final match of the league phase this season. Bayern will hope to do better this time.
According to the supercomputer, all English teams and OL Lyonnes are expected to secure a place in the quarter-finals of the UWCL this year, alongside the title contenders of course.

Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea (94.0%) have been given the second highest chance of reaching the last eight of the competition, behind Barcelona. This is largely down to their favourable draw as the Blues have the lowest average fixture difficulty rating of all teams in the league phase this year.

Surprisingly, the Opta supercomputer is not too bullish on the prospects of eight-time champions and last year’s runners-up OL Lyonnes, or the 2024-25 champions Arsenal. Those two teams came out on top in only 8.7% and 7.0% of the simulations, respectively.Jonatan Giráldez's side reached the final in 20.6% of simulations, behind Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Man City. Despite adding more attacking firepower to the side with the signings of Caroline Weir and Paralluelo, Lyon lack balance in the midfield following Lindsey Heaps’ departure this summer to Denver Summit FC.
The side struggled to maintain the intensity and compactness throughout the 90 minutes in last season’s final against Barcelona and could yet fall short in that regard this season.

Renee Slegers’ Arsenal have had their own issues in front of goal, unable to maximise their goalscoring opportunities, a glimpse of what has continuously haunted the Gunners when it comes to the fine margins.

Their recent goalless draw against Crystal Palace was another in a long list of games where they failed to convert their chances. According to the Opta supercomputer, Arsenal reached the final on just 17.8% of the simulations.

English champions Manchester City reached the semi-final stage in 50.1% of the simulations on their return to the competition. Andree Jeglertz’s side haven’t featured in the final four since the 2017-18 season, when they were beaten by the eventual champions Lyon thanks to a goal by Lucy Bronze.

Spearheaded by Khadija Shaw, City will hope to add a European star to their domestic triumphs, building on their momentum. The side has talented players across all positions but potentially lacks the depth needed to compete three times a week.

Outside the top six, Real Madrid have the highest probability of making the quarter-finals of the UWCL this season (49.6%). Las Blancas have lost their leading goalscorer and assist provider in the club’s history, Caroline Weir, but have brought in the prodigious talent of Felicia Schroder to lead the attack alongside Linda Caicedo.

105ep4aayvb5d1xa03fknol4to.title: Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth: Pressure builds on Carrick after another thumping loss
105ep4aayvb5d1xa03fknol4to.subtitle: Bournemouth ran riot at Old Trafford, piling more misery on Michael Carrick and Manchester United amid their winless streak.
paragraphs: Evanilson's stunning second-half strike capped a memorable 3-0 Premier League win for Bournemouth at Manchester United to pile even more pressure on Michael Carrick.

Rayan and Marcus Tavernier scored in five first-half minutes to put United – who left captain Bruno Fernandes on the bench – on the back foot, leading to boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time.

Evanilson then had a goal disallowed from the restart, but he got his goal later on, rounding Senne Lammens to finish into an unguarded net and extend United's winless run to eight games in all competitions.
Bournemouth started on the front foot without testing Lammens, as Rayan and Evanilson both sent headers wide either side of Diogo Dalot blazing over the bar at the other end.
Ayden Heaven threw himself into a dangerous tackle – luckily without making contact on Evanilson – to give away a free-kick, which led to Bournemouth's 38th-minute opener.

Justin Kluivert whipped his right-sided set-piece into the far post, and Rayan was completely unmarked to drill it past Lammens into the bottom-right corner to end his nine-game goal drought in the league.

Bryan Mbeumo was denied by Djordje Petrovic as United sought an equaliser, and Bournemouth doubled their lead in the 43rd minute. Adrien Truffert profited from an untimely Leny Yoro slip to tee up Tavernier to tap into an empty net.
Things almost got even worse 21 seconds after the break when a loose Harry Maguire pass was cut out by Tavernier on the edge of the box, but Evanilson was offside when he slotted in.
United tried to make their possession count in the second half, but Mbeumo fired just over on the turn before Lisandro Martinez's low fizzer was comfortably held by Petrovic.

But Bournemouth still remained a threat on the break, as they proved in the 71st minute. Lewis Cook went long, and Lammens was not quick enough to get there before Evanilson, who curled a stunning effort into the far side of the gaping goal from the right wing.
Andrey Santos saw a header blocked on the line, while Mason Mount had a tame shot saved in stoppage time as Bournemouth easily held out for a clean sheet.
Bournemouth pick up more momentum against stumbling United
After Fernandes seemingly criticised Carrick's tactics in midweek, he was named on the bench for a Premier League game for only the sixth time, and the first since May 2025 against Brentford.
In fact, it is the first time Carrick has not named the club captain in his starting line-up in the top-flight since he got the caretaker job in January (this is his 27th such game in charge).

It was a must-win game for United, who remain with just one league victory to their name this term (D4 L3), and they have triumphed in just one of their last 11 outings without Fernandes in the starting line-up (D3 L7).

Nothing should take away from Bournemouth's performance, though, as they became just the third side to score 2+ goals in four consecutive Premier League away games against United, after Manchester City (2011-12 - 2014-15) and Brighton (2022-23 - 2025-26).
Rayan's first top-flight goal of the season opened the scoring, and he led the team throughout, having five of Bournemouth's 10 shots, and it paid off as he got his first league goal of the season.
Bournemouth look to be hitting their stride after three straight wins, while United cannot escape the spotlight, having failed to take any of their 17 chances.
105ep4aayvb5d1xa03fknol4to.html:
Evanilson's stunning second-half strike capped a memorable 3-0 Premier League win for Bournemouth at Manchester United to pile even more pressure on Michael Carrick.

Rayan and Marcus Tavernier scored in five first-half minutes to put United – who left captain Bruno Fernandes on the bench – on the back foot, leading to boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time.

Evanilson then had a goal disallowed from the restart, but he got his goal later on, rounding Senne Lammens to finish into an unguarded net and extend United's winless run to eight games in all competitions.

Bournemouth started on the front foot without testing Lammens, as Rayan and Evanilson both sent headers wide either side of Diogo Dalot blazing over the bar at the other end.

Ayden Heaven threw himself into a dangerous tackle – luckily without making contact on Evanilson – to give away a free-kick, which led to Bournemouth's 38th-minute opener.

Justin Kluivert whipped his right-sided set-piece into the far post, and Rayan was completely unmarked to drill it past Lammens into the bottom-right corner to end his nine-game goal drought in the league.

Bryan Mbeumo was denied by Djordje Petrovic as United sought an equaliser, and Bournemouth doubled their lead in the 43rd minute. Adrien Truffert profited from an untimely Leny Yoro slip to tee up Tavernier to tap into an empty net.

Things almost got even worse 21 seconds after the break when a loose Harry Maguire pass was cut out by Tavernier on the edge of the box, but Evanilson was offside when he slotted in.

United tried to make their possession count in the second half, but Mbeumo fired just over on the turn before Lisandro Martinez's low fizzer was comfortably held by Petrovic.

But Bournemouth still remained a threat on the break, as they proved in the 71st minute. Lewis Cook went long, and Lammens was not quick enough to get there before Evanilson, who curled a stunning effort into the far side of the gaping goal from the right wing.

Andrey Santos saw a header blocked on the line, while Mason Mount had a tame shot saved in stoppage time as Bournemouth easily held out for a clean sheet.

Bournemouth pick up more momentum against stumbling United

After Fernandes seemingly criticised Carrick's tactics in midweek, he was named on the bench for a Premier League game for only the sixth time, and the first since May 2025 against Brentford.

In fact, it is the first time Carrick has not named the club captain in his starting line-up in the top-flight since he got the caretaker job in January (this is his 27th such game in charge).

It was a must-win game for United, who remain with just one league victory to their name this term (D4 L3), and they have triumphed in just one of their last 11 outings without Fernandes in the starting line-up (D3 L7).

Nothing should take away from Bournemouth's performance, though, as they became just the third side to score 2+ goals in four consecutive Premier League away games against United, after Manchester City (2011-12 - 2014-15) and Brighton (2022-23 - 2025-26).

Rayan's first top-flight goal of the season opened the scoring, and he led the team throughout, having five of Bournemouth's 10 shots, and it paid off as he got his first league goal of the season.

108w6stzxj8zc1ujzo1taheqe5.title: Spain have 'no intention of stopping winning', says De la Fuente
108w6stzxj8zc1ujzo1taheqe5.subtitle: Spain's stellar unbeaten streak looked like it was under pressure at Wembley, but they came from behind to beat England in the second half.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente insists Spain have "no intention of stopping winning" after securing a 3-2 comeback win over England to start their Nations League campaign.
Lamine Yamal put the world champions ahead after just 105 seconds, capitalising on a Marc Guehi mistake, but they found themselves behind at the break after goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane.
A slow start to the second half saw Rodri give away a penalty, but Spain were given a reprieve when Kane sent his spot-kick crashing against the bar.
Two substitutes then flipped the script, with Alex Baena equalising before setting up Mikel Oyarzabal for the winner.
Spain are now unbeaten in their last 39 matches (across 90 minutes), extending the record run among all European nations in all competitions (W30 D9).
La Roja, who dominated for long periods, have won each of their last eight competitive matches, and De la Fuente was particularly impressed with the resilience his side showed.
"We are very happy with the result, with the performance, and for having shown the world that we have a lot of ambition and a strong desire to win," he told Teledeporte.
"It is true that there were moments when we had to suffer. But this is England.
"We talked at half-time. We had the game under control; we had three clear chances. We continue to show that this team never gives up, that we have no intention of stopping winning.
"I'm lucky to have these players. Anyone can step onto the pitch and be ready. It's about trying to make changes. They have exceptional talent."

Spain could have been out of sight in the first 30 minutes against England, with Ferran Torres having a goal disallowed for offside before he saw two golden one-on-one chances against James Trafford go begging.

Dani Olmo and Yamal also wasted opportunities before the Three Lions scored, and they went into half-time knowing they had conceded more goals in those 45 minutes (two) than they did in their World Cup-winning campaign (one).
"We conceded both of England's goals; it was a moment of disconnection," De la Fuente said in his press conference.
"They could hurt us, and we weren't able to fight them back. Generally speaking, the game was under control against a superpower.
"We all played our part, and I think we had the game under control against such a powerful opponent."
And when asked about the current unbeaten streak, he added: "What this generation of footballers is doing is truly remarkable.
"They never stop striving to improve. The statistics speak for themselves. It's incredibly difficult to replicate what Spain is achieving.
"We'll approach the match against Croatia as if it were our last. These players are always eager to keep developing."

10afbmzk5gc7e129jab1kjypud.title: Italy 3-1 Turkiye: Mancini's men grind it out
10afbmzk5gc7e129jab1kjypud.subtitle: Italy moved into second place in Nations League Group A1, with Riccardo Calafiori and Francesco Pio Esposito sealing a win over Turkiye.
paragraphs: Italy continued their strong start under Roberto Mancini with a hard-fought 3-1 win over Turkiye in the Nations League.
Mancini's second spell as Italy coach started with a loss to Belgium, but the Azzurri have now taken seven points from their next three outings to sit second in Group A1.
They had to do it the hard way at Stadio Renato Dall'Ara, where Turkiye – under the tutelage of Italian coach Vincenzo Montella – kept them in a tussle until the end.

A first half of few clear chances was punctuated by a real moment of quality from Gianluca Scamacca, who instinctively fired in a snapshot off the underside of the crossbar to break the deadlock in the 26th minute.
Yet a decent response from Italy early in the second half told when Aral Simsir turned into an empty net after the ball broke kindly for him at the back post.
Parity, however, lasted just three minutes, as substitute Riccardo Calafiori leapt highest to meet Nicolo Barella's delivery and thumped in a header to restore Italy's advantage.
The contest was settled in the 87th minute, as another of Mancini's substitutes, Francesco Pio Esposito, flicked in from Alessandro Romano's centre.
Esposito into the history books
It was a grind, but Italy got over the line in Bologna, and Mancini can reflect on a decent points haul from his first four matches back at the helm.
This was an even game, as evidenced by the match stats.
Italy had 15 shots to Turkiye's 14, while the Azzurri had six attempts on target to their visitors' five.
The hosts also had 28 touches in the opponent's box, whereas Turkiye had 27 going the other way, while Italy generated chances worth 1.9 expected goals to Turkiye's 1.31 xG.
Ultimately, Esposito settled matters with a smart finish.

He has become only the second player in the history of the Italian national team to score his seventh international goal before turning 22, after Giuseppe Meazza (20 years and 155 days on January 25, 1931).
Esposito will hope to be at the spearhead of Mancini's second spell, as the coach looks to repeat his success from the first time around.

10do9su6yhosq1ifgenic1r6mb.title: Bastoni 'in debt to the Italian people' following World Cup qualification failures
10do9su6yhosq1ifgenic1r6mb.subtitle: After Italy won for the first time since Roberto Mancini's return, Alessandro Bastoni admitted he must work to get their fans back on-side.
paragraphs: Alessandro Bastoni admits he is 'in debt to the Italian people' following the Azzurri's World Cup shortcomings, though he has urged patience as Roberto Mancini's team look to get things right.
Italy failed to qualify for a third straight edition of the World Cup this year, losing on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina following a 1-1 draw in a play-off in March.
Their task was made more difficult in that match by Bastoni being sent off late in the first half, having hacked Amar Memic down when he was racing clear on goal.

Italy are the first former champions to ever miss three straight World Cups, with their latest humiliating failure leading to the dismissal of Gennaro Gattuso and the return of Euro 2020-winning coach Mancini, following a lengthy and frustrating recruitment process.

Mancini's men started their Nations League campaign with a 2-0 defeat to France last week, but they bounced back with a 4-1 rout of Turkiye on Monday, with Bastoni scoring the opening goal as they roared into a 3-0 lead within 27 minutes.
After that victory, Bastoni reflected on the Bosnia-Herzegovina defeat and admitted he has plenty of work to do to atone for his red card.
"It was inevitable that my mind would go back to Zenica," Bastoni told RAI Sport. "I will be in debt to the Italian people for the next four years.
"When faced with difficult situations, I have always chosen to emerge with my head held high and take my responsibility.
"We hit rock bottom in recent years, but we want to get back on our feet.
"All we ask for is some balance and patience in judging this side, as there are many young players who want to learn."
Italy's win over Turkiye was their first by three or more goals away from home since November 2019, when they beat Bosnia-Herzogovina 3-0.

It was also their first win under Mancini in 1,198 days, having overcome the Netherlands 3-2 under him in the Nations League third-place play-off in June 2023, before he called time on his first stint in charge to join Saudi Arabia.
"We are still a young team overall, we have quality and we want to prove what we can do," Bastoni added, with a trip to France up next on Friday.
"We mustn't get too over-excited now, we had some peaks last year too, and then saw what happened. It is at least good to feel happy every now and then."

10lnkrsdrtedk1nyr6banwha9w.title: Koumas backs 'unbelievable' Barcola to build on Champions League hat-trick
10lnkrsdrtedk1nyr6banwha9w.subtitle: Bradley Barcola announced himself as a Liverpool player with a hat-trick against LASK, much to the delight of Lewis Koumas.
paragraphs: Lewis Koumas has no doubts Bradley Barcola will be a success at Liverpool after the former Paris Saint-Germain forward starred in their Champions League win on Wednesday.
Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool's 6-3 win over LASK, becoming the first Reds player since Mohamed Salah in 2022 to net three in an away Champions League match.
Ronald Araujo and Jeremie Frimpong were also on target in Austria, with Koumas eventually getting himself on the scoresheet after seeing two goals disallowed for offside.
Koumas's impressive display saw him become the youngest player to score and assist in a Champions League match for Liverpool (21y 25d), breaking Steven Gerrard's record.
However, the Wales international was full of praise for Barcola, with Koumas saying the Frenchman still has plenty more to give in a Liverpool shirt this season.
"I think it's been really hard for him," Koumas said. "Not in terms of on the pitch, because we all know how good he is, but, moving country and trying to settle in fast is tough.
"I found it tough on loan, so changing countries must be something else, so I'm just really happy that he showed how good he is, and I just hope he carries on doing it now.
"He's unbelievable. He's an unbelievable talent, and I'm sure he'll be unbelievable for Liverpool."
Barcola will be hoping to impress in the Premier League this Saturday when Liverpool travel to face a Brentford side that have made yet another strong start to the campaign.
The Bees are fourth in the table after playing out a 2-2 draw against Aston Villa last time out, with Kristoffer Ajer proving to be the unlikely hero with a 79th-minute equaliser.

Since their promotion to the top-flight in 2021, Brentford have dropped more points from winning positions than any other side in the Premier League (102). They have already lost eight points from ahead this season, with only Bournemouth dropping more (nine).
Nevertheless, Keith Andrews said his team have taken confidence from their encouraging start to the season, with eight points separating them and leaders Manchester City.
"We do. We've started well, and we're content with a lot of aspects of what we're doing and how," Andrews said after Brentford's stalemate at Villa Park.

"We want to keep pushing hard, and we are disappointed we could've played a bit better and maybe the result was there for us if we'd tidied up a few aspects of our game. Then it would have been a really good start to the season."
Brentford could be without Kevin Schade to face Liverpool, with the German sustaining an issue before being replaced by Mamadou Sangare in the 52nd minute against Villa.
"He probably wasn't right at half-time, he wanted to give it a go," Andrews said of Schade. "He's picked up a shoulder injury so we'll see how he is in the next few days."
Brentford – Igor Thiago
It's been a difficult start to the season for Thiago, who is underperforming his expected goals more than any other player in the Premier League, scoring once from an xG of 3.2.
The Brazilian did, however, score a penalty in Brentford's win over Liverpool at the Gtech Community Stadium last term, and how he would love another goal against them here.
Liverpool – Bradley Barcola
After failing to score in his first six Liverpool games in all competitions, Barcola announced himself in a Reds shirt with a hat-trick in the Champions League in midweek.
On what was the 238th game of his senior career (for club and country combined), Barcola netted his first treble, which he will hope can kickstart his Premier League career.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Brentford were unbeaten in their two Premier League games against Liverpool last season (W1 D1), last going more without defeat against the Reds in the league between April 1936 and November 1937 (four).

Andrews' side are also unbeaten in their six Premier League games this season (W2 D4), their best run from the start of a league campaign since 2006-07 in League One (first seven). Overall, the Bees are unbeaten in eight top-flight games, the longest current run of any side (W2 D6).
The Bees (fourth) are facing Liverpool (ninth) while above them in the league table for the first time since March 1938, with the 20th-placed Reds beating the Bees in 6th 3-1 at Griffin Park.

Liverpool have, however, won their last two away Premier League games, keeping a clean sheet in both. The Reds last had a longer away winning run between August and October 2024 (four), while they haven't kept three away clean sheets in a row since March 2022.
But they suffered their first Premier League defeat of the season last time out against Manchester City, while the 3-0 loss also ended manager Andoni Iraola's 23-game unbeaten run in the competition.

And you can expect plenty of action between the two teams. The five Premier League meetings between Brentford and Liverpool at the Gtech have seen 22 goals scored at an average of 4.4 per game, with both sides scoring in four of those five games.

10nyiozd0a42n1mxlmxnedd14s.title: Mancini sets his sights on France after dominant victory over Turkiye
10nyiozd0a42n1mxlmxnedd14s.subtitle: Roberto Mancini claimed his first win since returning to manage Italy against Turkiye, but he is already thinking of the next match.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini immediately switched his focus to Italy's trip to France after he claimed his first win in his second stint with the Azzurri against Turkiye in the Nations League.
Mancini watched on as his Italy team emerged 4-1 victors in Bursaspor, with three goals inside the opening 27 minutes doing the damage against Vincenzo Montella's side.
Alessandro Bastoni handed the visitors a ninth-minute lead before Davide Frattesi rounded off an excellent passing move to double Italy's advantage in the 22nd minute.

Michael Kayode, on his international debut, put the Azzurri out of sight, as Italy scored three goals inside the first 30 minutes of play for the first time since a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania in September 2021.
Baris Alper Yilmaz threatened a comeback early in the second half, but Francesco Pio Esposito restored Italy's three-goal advantage in the 50th minute to seal an impressive win.
The result saw Italy win an away match by a 3+ goal margin for the first time since November 2019, when they beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-0.
More importantly, the Azzurri claimed their first win under Mancini, 1,198 days since his last win in charge of Italy, which came in a 3-2 triumph over the Netherlands in June 2023.

However, Mancini was already thinking about Italy's next game, which takes them to the Stade de France to face Zinedine Zidane's side, who sit top of Group A1 following their late win against Belgium on Monday.
"Now we have to focus on the next match, try to recover our strength, we've got fresh legs at home and will try to have our say in Paris," Mancini told RAI Sport.
The victory marked a huge improvement to the one Mancini oversaw on his second debut, with Italy outclassed during their 2-0 defeat against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico.
Italy only registered an expected goals (xG) total of 1.7 from their 21 shots against Belgium, but they improved that to 2.4 from 14 attempts in a clinical display against Turkiye.

Mancini did, however, confirm that Giacomo Raspadori's substitution at half-time was because of an injury, and he was unable to add whether he would be available to face France and then Turkiye at home.
"We were on a pitch where it had been raining for a whole day, and it was only natural to expect a response from Turkiye," Mancini added.
"Everyone played a great game. Raspadori went off with a problem.
"We were worried that we might have to take him off after five minutes in the second half, so we substituted him at the break.
"The team pushed up, kept the ball, moved it around well. Raspadori did what we asked; he had a good game."

Roberto Mancini immediately switched his focus to Italy's trip to France after he claimed his first win in his second stint with the Azzurri against Turkiye in the Nations League.

Mancini watched on as his Italy team emerged 4-1 victors in Bursaspor, with three goals inside the opening 27 minutes doing the damage against Vincenzo Montella's side. 

Alessandro Bastoni handed the visitors a ninth-minute lead before Davide Frattesi rounded off an excellent passing move to double Italy's advantage in the 22nd minute. 

Michael Kayode, on his international debut, put the Azzurri out of sight, as Italy scored three goals inside the first 30 minutes of play for the first time since a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania in September 2021. 

Baris Alper Yilmaz threatened a comeback early in the second half, but Francesco Pio Esposito restored Italy's three-goal advantage in the 50th minute to seal an impressive win. 

The result saw Italy win an away match by a 3+ goal margin for the first time since November 2019, when they beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-0. 

More importantly, the Azzurri claimed their first win under Mancini, 1,198 days since his last win in charge of Italy, which came in a 3-2 triumph over the Netherlands in June 2023.

However, Mancini was already thinking about Italy's next game, which takes them to the Stade de France to face Zinedine Zidane's side, who sit top of Group A1 following their late win against Belgium on Monday.

"Now we have to focus on the next match, try to recover our strength, we've got fresh legs at home and will try to have our say in Paris," Mancini told RAI Sport.

The victory marked a huge improvement to the one Mancini oversaw on his second debut, with Italy outclassed during their 2-0 defeat against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico. 

Italy only registered an expected goals (xG) total of 1.7 from their 21 shots against Belgium, but they improved that to 2.4 from 14 attempts in a clinical display against Turkiye.

Mancini did, however, confirm that Giacomo Raspadori's substitution at half-time was because of an injury, and he was unable to add whether he would be available to face France and then Turkiye at home. 

"We were on a pitch where it had been raining for a whole day, and it was only natural to expect a response from Turkiye," Mancini added. 

"Everyone played a great game. Raspadori went off with a problem.

"We were worried that we might have to take him off after five minutes in the second half, so we substituted him at the break.

"The team pushed up, kept the ball, moved it around well. Raspadori did what we asked; he had a good game."

10o4xwc5fnrw019pi0i38tsodg.title: AC Milan 3-2 Atalanta: Amorim's side hold on to extend unbeaten start
10o4xwc5fnrw019pi0i38tsodg.subtitle: AC Milan just about preserved their unbeaten start to the season on Sunday, with Atalanta almost coming from two goals down to take a point.
paragraphs: AC Milan extended their unbeaten start to the Serie A season to seven matches, though they were forced to hold on for a nervy 3-2 victory over Atalanta at San Siro.
Goncalo Ramos and Adrien Rabiot put Milan in control before the break, with Mario Gila pulling the hosts further clear in the second half, but Atalanta threatened a comeback.
Gianluca Gaetano's 66th-minute strike was followed up with a Nikola Krstovic goal nine minutes from time, but Ruben Amorim's side were able to hold on for all three points.
Christian Pulisic thought he had broken the deadlock after 14 minutes, powering a shot past Marco Carnesecchi, but the goal was disallowed for offside following a VAR review.
Krstovic then squandered a chance to put Atalanta ahead five minutes later as the visitors countered at pace, rounding Mike Maignan before sliding his effort into the side netting.
Milan's breakthrough finally came 24 minutes in when Relja Obric was penalised for handball inside the box, with Ramos making no mistake from the resulting spot-kick.

Rabiot doubled the Rossoneri's lead minutes before half-time, continuing his good form with a superb finish as he cushioned Diego Moreira's pass before chopping past Orbic and guiding a tidy finish into the bottom-left corner.

An eventful second half began with Omari Hutchinson crashing an effort against the post before Atalanta conceded another penalty when Thomas Kristensen handled inside the area, but Ramos saw his shot from 12 yards kept out by Carnesecchi.
Milan, though, swiftly added to their lead off the resulting corner as Rabiot flicked on Luka Modric's teasing corner for Gila, who nodded home untroubled from close range.

But Amorim's side took their foot off the gas and allowed Gaetano to pull one back, with Krstovic reducing the deficit even further in the 81st minute, drilling home Raoul Bellanova's cutback to leave Milan sweating.
Maignan was called into action moments later to preserve the hosts' slender advantage, parrying Davide Zappacosta's effort as the Rossoneri held firm and saw out the win.
Milan hold firm to end winless run against Atalanta

Amorim would have expected a fairly straightforward second half after his side went into the break with a 2-0 lead, but it proved to be anything but. Nonetheless, his side held on to extend their unbeaten start, and also bring an end to a winless run against La Dea.
The Rossoneri secured their first Serie A victory over Atalanta since February 2023, ending a six-match winless streak against their rivals.
Milan are now unbeaten in their opening seven league matches, their longest such run since going 24 games without defeat between August 2025 and February 2026.
Rabiot has been instrumental in their impressive form, scoring in each of his last three Serie A appearances (three goals) – his longest scoring streak in the competition.
The Frenchman has also registered a goal involvement in each of his last four league matches, contributing three goals and two assists.

Milan's attacking superiority was reflected in their 2.41 expected goals (xG), compared to Atalanta's 1.65, though Amorim will be concerned by his side's late collapse, which could easily have proved costly on another day.

10rvhkuzcdvy01rmqfu7xmjk73.title: 'We have to keep going' – Mourinho's sights higher than one Clasico win
10rvhkuzcdvy01rmqfu7xmjk73.subtitle: Real Madrid claimed a 2-1 win over LaLiga leaders Barcelona on Sunday, but Jose Mourinho is far from satisfied.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho is not content with just beating Barcelona as he demanded his Real Madrid team target a title tilt in LaLiga.
Kylian Mbappe's double at Camp Nou propelled Madrid to a  2-1 victory in El Clasico.
Mourinho has now won six Clasicos across his two spells in charge of Los Blancos, with only two Madrid coaches – Miguel Munoz (16) and Carlo Ancelotti (nine) – winning more.
But Mourinho is not satisfied, as he insisted Madrid must now follow up this win.
"This is a great win, but when we get back to work, I'm not going to let anyone have their head in the clouds," Mourinho said.
"Real Madrid don't play to win at Camp Nou, but rather to win the league. We have to keep going.
"I think it was a great game. A game at a high level, a game which the world that loves football stopped to see, and they weren't let down.
"In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage.
"For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent. The boys deserve it."
Madrid had to do without goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who was absent due to illness.
Courtois' replacement Andriy Lunin, though, made five saves.
"The only thing I said to Lunin before the game was: you train to play, not to be on the bench," Mourinho added.
"We have the best keeper in the world, but today we weren't crying before the game because Thibaut couldn't play. The group is strong."

10tvummvu04th1i6on49egp0eh.title: Wicky excited to see Sporting KC's confidence build
10tvummvu04th1i6on49egp0eh.subtitle: Sporting Kansas City and the Seattle Sounders both head into Thursday's clash on the back of morale-boosting wins in MLS.
paragraphs: Raphael Wicky is hopeful that Sporting Kansas City's recent wins will continue to help build their confidence ahead of a visit to the Seattle Sounders in MLS.
Sporting have won two of their last three league games (L1), including a 2-0 victory over high-flying Houston Dynamo last time out.

That was their first clean sheet of the 2026 season, though they remain bottom of the Western Conference with 21 points, 14 behind the ninth-place Sounders, who occupy the final playoff spot with eight games left to play.
While Wicky had hoped for more goals against the Dynamo, he was thrilled to see another battling display, which he wants to carry forward.
"We had a chance to make it 3-0, and I think then it would be even harder for Houston to stay in the game," Wicky said after that result.
"We didn't, and 2-0 is always a tough result. I'm very pleased with what I saw, and I hope this gives the team confidence.
"I think over the last weeks, or even since the World Cup break, besides maybe two games, we've shown that we're competitive with most teams, so I'm happy with that."
Seattle were on a torrid run just a few weeks ago, having gone 13 games without a victory in MLS, but they have now won their last two games.

After beating Real Salt Lake, they followed it up with a 3-1 win over Minnesota United to move into the playoff places for the first time in months, but Brian Schmetzer believes the Sounders still have work to do to keep their revival going.
"Our structure, where we have a little bit of rotation between positions, is okay," he said, as quoted by Sounder at Heart.
"But the player who rotates into a different position has to understand the rules and responsibilities of where he's playing.
"You need to still be exciting, entertain the fans, do all that sort of stuff. I'm not trying to stifle any sort of creative moments.
"But we have to win games and make sure that we make a 2-0 lead, a 3-0 lead, and then we can kind of spitball and do what they want and have a little more joy."
Seattle Sounders – Albert Rusnak
Albert Rusnak assisted two of Seattle's three goals against Minnesota United, taking him to 12 assists on the season.
He has 38 assists over the last three seasons, the third-most in MLS in that time behind only Lionel Messi (49) and Evander (46).
Sporting Kansas City – Andre Luiz
Andre Luiz was directly involved in both goals in Sporting KC's win at Houston, scoring once and assisting once.
He is the first player to record a goal and an assist in a regular-season away match for Sporting since current Sounders player Dejan Joveljic against the LA Galaxy on March 14.
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
Seattle are unbeaten in four straight matches against Sporting KC (W3 D1), including a 1-1 draw in Kansas City on May 2.
The Sounders managed to avoid defeat only three times in their previous 10 against Sporting (W3 L7) dating back to 2019.

After a 13-match regular-season winless run, Seattle have recorded back-to-back victories with wins over Real Salt Lake and Minnesota. The Sounders, who drew the final five matches of that winless run, are now unbeaten in seven straight matches, the fourth-longest active streak in MLS.
As for Sporting KC, they won their third away match of the season on Saturday, a 2-0 victory at Houston.
Sporting last won two straight away from home in league play over five years ago, a three-match winning streak in July and August 2021 that included a victory in Seattle.
Seattle Sounders – 62.7%
Sporting Kansas City – 17.5%

10u20asbr2uef17lke3udn2gyv.title: Netherlands and Dumfries target first clean sheet of the year
10u20asbr2uef17lke3udn2gyv.subtitle: The Netherlands are yet to keep a clean sheet in 2026, but they are hoping to change that when they host Serbia in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Denzel Dumfries insists the Netherlands are working to improve their defensive performances as they target their first clean sheet of the year.
The Netherlands face Serbia in the Nations League on Sunday, having conceded in each of their 11 matches in 2026.
They most recently conceded twice in a draw with Greece, though they did come from two goals down to salvage a point.
The Netherlands are unbeaten in their three games under Xavi (W1 D2), leaving them second in their Nations League group.
Despite their solid start, Dumfries acknowledged the Oranje still need to improve at the back.
"That is a nice challenge for the team. We want to change things and concede fewer goals," said Dumfries.
"It is not a problem, but it is, of course, an issue. When you look at the defenders we have, you shouldn't be conceding so many goals.
"That is a point of attention we are working on to improve."
It could be a special occasion at Philips Stadion for Netherlands captain Virgil van Dijk, who is in line to win his 100th cap for his country.

Van Dijk, who has scored 18 goals for the Netherlands, helped his country reach the semi-finals at Euro 2024, the quarter-finals at the 2022 World Cup and the final of the inaugural Nations League in 2019.
"It could be an emotional day for Virgil," Xavi said. "I am very happy to work with him and he is a true leader."
"He fits in well. One hundred caps is incredible. Whether he plays? We'll see on Sunday."

1108t1oiygwmm12mk678wpl61h.title: Pocognoli not concerned about Scotland's goal drought
1108t1oiygwmm12mk678wpl61h.subtitle: Scotland have not scored in any of their last three matches, but Sebastien Pocognoli believes their fortunes could change very quickly.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli insisted he is not concerned about Scotland's lack of goals ahead of their Nations League clash with Switzerland on Tuesday.
Scotland drew 0-0 with Slovenia in their first game under Pocognoli, despite accumulating 2.2 expected goals (xG) from 17 shots, four of which were Opta-defined 'big' chances.
Oliver McBurnie has failed to score in all 17 of his appearances for Scotland in all competitions, with the goalless draw at Slovenia his first game for the national side in 2,005 days.
Scotland have failed to score in their last three internationals after also blanking twice at the World Cup. They last failed to score in four consecutive matches between February and May 1971.
Nevertheless, ahead of his first home game in charge, Pocognoli is confident his Scotland side can change their fortunes in front of goal.
"It was one game. Some games you score. Some games you are unlucky," said the Belgian.
"I don't think there's any concerns from my side to score goals because we have good strikers. It's not only the strikers, but we are creating chances from many positions.
"Let's say we score [against Switzerland], I hope, and we can open another topic. I really hope we can start strong in the game.

"It will be a special moment, first time at home. I'm really looking forward for that moment since I've been appointed. As a new gaffer, that was really the date that was in my schedule that I want to experience."
Scotland have won just one of their last six meetings with Switzerland in all competitions (D3 L2), with this their first meeting since a 1-1 draw at Euro 2024.
Switzerland have won just one of their eight away games against Scotland in all competitions (D2 L5), though it was on their last visit in a March 2006 friendly (3-1).

Francesco Farioli has impressed since taking over at Portuguese giants FC Porto in July 2025. Opta Analyst had the chance to sit down with the Italian coach for an exclusive interview to pick his brains over the rise of the Dragões.

Defending champions FC Porto, fresh off the back of winning their first league title since 2021-22 last season, have kicked off their campaign in scintillating fashion. They've won each of their first seven league matches, netting 18 goals and conceding just three.

Under the tutelage of Italian coach Francesco Farioli, the man who has brought the Dragões back to the summit of Portuguese football, Porto, not content to celebrate the glories of the previous campaign, look hungrier and more determined than we’ve seen in a long, long time.
Their flawless start to the campaign has served as a message to the rest of the league that under this bright, enthusiastic coach, Porto are just getting started.

Opta Analyst spoke with Farioli in an exclusive interview to discuss how he has managed to completely rejuvenate Porto, who are gunning to win back-to-back Primeira Liga titles for the first time since a run of three between 2010-11 and 2012-13, the importance of hard work and discipline, dealing with adversity, and aims for the future.

Let’s rewind to the end of the 2024-25 campaign. Porto had just finished third for the second consecutive season, making it the first time they had finished outside the top two of the Primeira Liga in back-to-back campaigns since the mid-1970s, while their points tally of 71 was their lowest in a 34-game season since 2004-05 (62 points).
Three different managers took charge during the season in the form of two permanent coaches; Vítor Bruno and Martín Anselmi, as well as interim boss José Tavares.
This was a club in serious need of rejuvenation, and so they turned to former Nice and Ajax boss, Farioli.

“Since the first moment I spoke with the president [André Villas-Boas], for me, the decision to join the club was clear and now, I can say of course that it was the right decision,” Farioli tells Opta Analyst.

“I believe that we met in a very good moment for both of us. Both myself and the club, we felt the same level of desire, the same level of commitment in changing things and adapting ourselves in order to click, in order to work properly, to rebuild and to revamp the squad and this is what we tried to do.
“Last summer was a really important market, we had to bring in players with a certain mentality that could help us to bring the Porto DNA to the centre of everything that we were doing.”

The club brought in the likes of Victor Froholdt from Copenhagen, Gabri Veiga from Al-Ahli, and Borja Sainz from Norwich City to bolster the midfield and attack, players with an appetite who wanted to prove they could excel at the next level in a high-pressure environment and play for supporters that were desperate to taste glory once again.

At the back, Jan Bednarek came in from Southampton, Alberto Costa from Juventus and Jakub Kiwior from Arsenal, three players who contributed enormously to the team’s fantastic defensive numbers, with Porto’s 18 goals conceded the fewest of any team across Europe’s top 10 leagues last season, while their 21 clean sheets were also the most.
For Farioli though, those statistics are a testament to the whole team, not just the result of the brilliance of goalkeeper Diogo Costa and the back four in front of him.

“Of course, the defenders played a key role. If you look at individuals, having a goalkeeper like Diogo Costa is definitely an advantage, but I truly believe that these numbers come from a collective effort.
“Recently, I saw that William Gomes, one of our wingers, ranks as one of the best in terms of his defensive effort and this says a lot about the contribution of everybody.”
Gomes has won possession in the final third in the Primeira Liga nine times this season, the most of any Porto player.

“I believe that the game is an accumulation of moments and momentum within the game, and that's why the competitive capacity of the team is the key,” Farioli adds. “We have a group of players starting from the striker all the way to the goalkeeper where everybody is absolutely committed in helping the team and in those moments where we lose the ball, the players are prepared to react to that moment.”

Throughout the history of the club, some of the greatest Porto sides have mixed flair with aggression, finely striking the balance between supreme talent on the ball with an incredible tenacity off it. The supporters demand it; they expect their players to battle for every ball and then be capable of creating magic when they win it. It’s a formula that has served the club well throughout history and it’s something Farioli is conscious of.

“I believe there are certain behaviours that are quite contagious. Running those extra meters, putting in the extra effort, the desire to run for my team-mate when it’s close to the end of the match is something that is a positive virus and this is what our team has,” he says.

113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.title: De Bruyne: I did not try to leave Napoli
113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.subtitle: Kevin De Bruyne previously seemed to suggest he could leave Napoli, but the Belgian has insisted he did not try to do so this summer.
paragraphs: Kevin De Bruyne has claimed he did not attempt to push through an exit from Napoli in the summer transfer window.
De Bruyne previously suggested he was unhappy at Napoli, and there was speculation linking him with a move away from the Serie A club.
The Manchester City great did not see eye to eye with coach Antonio Conte, who has since been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri.
De Bruyne, however, has now insisted he was not interested in leaving Napoli.
He told reporters: "No, I haven't really spoken to anyone about it.
"I just enjoyed my holidays and went straight back to Naples."
Napoli have made their worst start to a Serie A season in a decade, having taken seven points from their opening five matches.
De Bruyne, though, is not overly concerned.
He said: "We've had a rough start to the season, we've played a lot of strong teams already.
"We even had the chance to win it in the final minute against Inter, but we still lost. Those details are the difference between our seven points and the 10 or 11 we might've deserved.
"We're not doing so well in terms of points, but I think we're doing fine."
Injury restricted De Bruyne to 21 games last term. He scored five goals, assisted four more and created 40 chances.
De Bruyne has made six appearances this season, scoring once and providing one assist.

115tkn4u990fd1t4ot5v1ugy6b.title: Tuchel does not have 'anymore words' for Kane ahead of landmark England appearance
115tkn4u990fd1t4ot5v1ugy6b.subtitle: Harry Kane could become England's joint all-time leading appearance maker against Czechia, with Thomas Tuchel hailing his influence.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel says he has run out of words to describe Harry Kane, with the England captain in line to earn his 125th cap against Czechia on Tuesday.
Should he play at Wembley, Kane would equal Peter Shilton as the all-time record appearance maker for the England men's national team in this match.
Kane has 21 goals in his last 22 appearances for the Three Lions and has scored three goals in four games against Czechia.

Following a disappointing 3-2 loss to Spain in their opening Nations League match, England have since beaten Czechia and Croatia – who they thumped 7-0 – with Tuchel ready to rotate his squad ahead of the final match of the break.
While Tuchel did not give away too many hints about his squad selection, he was full of praise for the 33-year-old.
"I'm not sure I have anymore words," Tuchel said about Kane.
"He's on the shortlist for the Ballon d'Or. We've spoken so often about him, and I try to find new words which then make no sense!
"Everything he does, he does it on the highest level; he does it consecutively, and I am very sure he will be the one leading the team out onto the training pitch.
"He will lead the team in the warm-up and not do one step less or one step slower. That is the level he has.
"Since he took this major role for Bayern Munich, he found a new level. It's the highest level, on and off the pitch.
"All these number nines in world football, no matter in which league, they are built a bit different.
"They don't only do it so their team wins; they also do it for themselves and for the records: 'How many can I score? How many can I assist? Where is the next record?'
"That's what drives them, and it's good that drives them. You will not find a striker of this calibre who does not have these individual goals."
One of the players Tuchel will definitely be without is Alex Scott, who withdrew from the squad with a thigh injury on Monday.
Reports suggest Bournemouth are unhappy with how England have managed the 23-year-old's issue, given he could be out for up to eight weeks during a busy period for the club.
But Tuchel insists England took no risks with Scott's fitness when they chose to start him against Croatia.
"On a human level, I feel bad that he does not get his next cap [against Czechia]," says Tuchel. "In my mind, he started [the game].

"I would not have taken any risk, even if it was a big opportunity for him. We wanted him to start, but if we had the slightest idea it was a risk [to play him], we would not have taken it. We never do this.
"We – the medical and physical departments – are always in communication with all the players who are with us.
"We share information; this is a totally open process. I can understand that Bournemouth are not happy because they lose a key player.
"But I can just say that from the moment we took the decision, there was absolutely not risk apparent to me or our physical staff. It's a one-off."
England are unbeaten in all eight of their games against Czechia at Wembley Stadium (W6 D2), the most recent of which saw the Three Lions finish their Euro 2020 group stage campaign with a 1-0 win.
However, they were beaten by Spain at the national stadium earlier in this international window.
England last lost back-to-back competitive home matches between November 1999 (v Scotland) and October 2000 (v Germany) under Kevin Keegan.

11732ehf1u7qu10dyizu8w44kn.title: Luis Enrique: Hakimi is the best right-back in the world
11732ehf1u7qu10dyizu8w44kn.subtitle: Achraf Hakimi stole the show with a hat-trick in Paris Saint-Germain's win over Le Havre, which earned him praise from Luis Enrique.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique labelled Paris Saint-Germain's hat-trick hero Achraf Hakimi "the best right-back in the world" after his stunning individual display against Le Havre on Friday.
Hakimi had a hand in all five of PSG's goals during their 5-1 win at Stade CMA CGM Oceane, with their triumph moving them two points clear at the top of Ligue 1.
Mika Godts quickly cancelled out Josh Maja's 18th-minute opener before Senny Mayulu carved open the Le Havre defence to tee up Hakimi to complete the turnaround.
PSG flexed their muscles after the break, with Hakimi's second-half goals coming either side of Mayulu's strike, which the Morocco international also got the assist for.

Hakimi's fine display saw him become only the second player to be involved in five goals (three goals, two assists) in a single Ligue 1 match since Opta began analysing the competition (2006-07), joining the likes of Neymar, Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Edinson Cavani, Kylian Mbappe and Carlos Eduardo in doing so.
He is the first defender to achieve the feat over that period, having never been involved in more than two goals in a Ligue 1 game in 135 appearances before facing Le Havre.

In fact, ahead of Friday's triumph, Hakimi had failed to register a single goal involvement in his first seven appearances in Ligue 1 this season. However, he now has the joint-most goal contributions in PSG ranks in the league in 2026-27, level with Ferran Torres.
"Hakimi is the captain. We know his qualities perfectly. He's more of a striker. He plays higher, he has this ability to make calls and deliver assists," Luis Enrique said of Hakimi.
"He's clearly a striker when we have the ball. And when we don't have it, everyone is a defender. He's the best right-back in the world.
"But I'm not particularly excited to see him score three goals. What I like is seeing him constantly at the highest level, always ready. It means a lot to our team."
PSG have now won each of their last nine matches in all competitions, their second-longest winning run under Luis Enrique after a run of ten between January and March 2025.
With Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia both out injured, the PSG boss elected to rest the in-form Desire Doue, with Mayulu and Godts taking their chance.
Godts has been involved in three goals in his last two games for PSG in all competitions (two goals, one assist), after only managing one of his first seven (one assist v Lille).

Mayulu, meanwhile, scored and assisted in a Ligue 1 match for just the second time in 57 appearances, after December 2025 (one goal, one assist v Rennes). The PSG forward has also found the net in two consecutive top-flight games for the first time.

But it was also a special occasion for Luis Enrique. The Spaniard claimed his 127th win in charge of PSG in all competitions, becoming the coach with the most victories with the French giants and surpassing Laurent Blanc (126).
"I never thought about that. The only thing I've said since I arrived is that I want to make history at PSG," Luis Enrique said of his achievement. "I want to continue to make history.
"I'm lucky to be in the best club in the world, with a sporting direction and a president. It's an incredible city. I want to enjoy it and continue to try to improve our level."

117743oleoy0u12rq4xj2od7mt.title: Politano shoulders blame for Napoli's defeat at Villarreal
117743oleoy0u12rq4xj2od7mt.subtitle: Villarreal came from behind to beat Napoli in the Champions League, leading to an honest apology from Matteo Politano on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Matteo Politano took responsibility for Napoli's defeat after his error helped Villarreal to a 3-1 win in Tuesday's Champions League clash.
Amir Rrahmani gave Napoli an early lead at El Madrigal, heading home eight minutes in after Billy Gilmour's floated cross towards the back post.
However, Villarreal levelled 15 minutes later when Politano's poor pass backwards was intercepted by Georges Mikautadze, who converted from a tight angle after drawing out Vanja Milinkovic-Savic.
A stunning strike from Santiago Mourino sent Inigo Perez's side ahead just three minutes after their equaliser before Tani Oluwaseyi's late strike sealed all three points.
Having played such a key role in Villarreal's response, Politano shouldered the blame immediately after the full-time whistle.
"I am sorry for the error, I take responsibility, and I know that I made a challenging match more difficult," Politano told Sky Sport Italia.
"I already apologised to my team-mates and now to the fans. We had chances to get back into it, but then we got a bit too stretched out in the second half."
Massimiliano Allegri's side had chances to extend their early lead, with Rasmus Hojlund denied by the woodwork from Politano's cross moments before the Napoli winger's mistake.

Hojlund then wasted another opportunity on the volley to level in the second half, while Kevin De Bruyne's delivery narrowly evaded both Lorenzo Lucca and Giovanni Di Lorenzo before Villarreal's third goal.
"Aside from the two goals conceded, we did well in the first half and created lots of chances," Politano added.
"After the break, we made a lot of mistakes, and Villarreal were far more of a team unit.
"I feel what we need to rediscover now is to learn how to defend together and then attack together, because we don’t have that unity."
The defeat may raise pressure on Allegri, given Napoli have lost three consecutive Champions League games for just the second time, previously doing so between February and September 2017.
By contrast, Villarreal's victory ended a 12-game winless streak, and a run of seven defeats in a row, in this competition.

1187i99ks00ua1ofbwlkojq45y.title: Van Bommel '100% happy and satisfied' after winning start to Belgium reign
1187i99ks00ua1ofbwlkojq45y.subtitle: Mark van Bommel began his tenure as Belgium boss with an impressive 2-0 victory over Italy at Stadio Olimpico in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel said he was "100% happy and satisfied" after marking his first match as Belgium boss with a 2-0 victory over Italy.
Mika Godts opened the scoring at Stadio Olimpico after 20 minutes, while Dodi Lukebakio secured all three points in their Nations League opener with a stunning curler after the hour mark.
It marked Italy's second defeat on home soil while conceding at least two goals and scoring none in the last 40 years, following their 2-0 loss to Croatia in August 2006.
Belgium particularly dominated in the first half, where they accumulated 2.39 expected goals (xG) from 14 attempts while restricting Italy to 0.32 from five shots.

Gianluigi Donnarumma pulled off impressive saves to deny Godts, Charles De Ketelaere and Nicolas Raskin from adding a second before the break, though his efforts proved in vain after Lukebakio's strike.
Subsequently, Belgium defeated Italy for the first time in a competitive match since May 1972.
"I am 100% happy and satisfied, although of course one can always improve too," said Van Bommel in his press conference.
"We started work on Monday with the right hunger and intensity that we also saw on the field.
"We worked on this 4-3-3 system for three days, it wasn't a top performance, but we controlled the first half very well.

"Italy pressed us better after the break and Senne Lammens made an incredible save. With the changes, we regained control of the match and Lukebakio’s wonderful goal sealed it, just like he did at San Siro against Milan.
"We don’t just have 11 starters, everyone can make the difference. Some players didn’t have 90 minutes in their legs.
"Godts had an extraordinary performance, I told him to always try to run at players and make something happen.
"It is difficult to keep up this tempo for 90 minutes, especially at international level, but we hope to keep it going for as long as possible."

11c3zjuchv9j21mkjmel5prnf8.title: Haaland '100% available' for Man City after midweek rest
11c3zjuchv9j21mkjmel5prnf8.subtitle: Enzo Maresca will be able to call upon Erling Haaland this weekend as Manchester City look to extend their 100% start against Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca has confirmed Erling Haaland is "100% available" for Manchester City's trip to Aston Villa in the Premier League.
Haaland was an unused substitute as City brushed aside AEK Athens 5-1 in midweek, with Phil Foden the biggest threat in his absence as he netted a hat-trick.
But the Norwegian will be back to help City try to continue their perfect start in the Premier League, having won all seven of their games so far after a 3-2 victory over Ipswich Town last time out.
Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes, and Nico O'Reilly are the other injury doubts, and Maresca was less sure if the trio would be available for Saturday.
"Erling is the only one 100% available. And the other three, we need to wait for [Thursday's] training session," Maresca said.
Despite having a maximum of 21 points and sitting three points clear at the top of the table at this stage, Maresca still believes there is room for improvement.
"We can attack and defend better," he said.
"In the past three games, we had the best defence in the league before our game started, but then we conceded goals. I am always looking for how we can improve.
"Sometimes we forget it has been just three or four months since we started. I was here before, but it is a completely new project.
"We only started months ago, but that's why I'm sure we can improve."

11cgsfvvpnv481f2pwk1l9n6dz.title: Everton 3-1 Newcastle United: No Grealish, no problem in comfortable EFL Cup win
11cgsfvvpnv481f2pwk1l9n6dz.subtitle: James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry scored as Everton beat Newcastle United 3-1 in Thursday's EFL Cup fourth-round tie.
paragraphs: Everton cruised into the EFL Cup quarter-finals by dispatching Newcastle United 3-1 at Hill Dickinson Stadium, with James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry scoring.

David Moyes' men were without Jack Grealish after he was disciplined for "a breach of club discipline", but they made light of his absence to tee up a last-eight clash with Fleetwood Town, who stunned Arsenal in the fourth round earlier this week.

Harvey Barnes was heavily involved for Newcastle throughout the first half, seeing an early header kept out by Jordan Pickford, dragging a half-volley past the post and having a penalty appeal waved away following Kiernan Dewsbury Hall's challenge.

But it was Everton who went into the interval with a commanding lead. Their opener arrived in the 34th minute, with Garner curling a lovely finish into the far corner from just inside the area, after Hackney pounced on some loose play from Amar Dedic.

And the Toffees' second goal, on the stroke of half-time, saw them go from back to front quickly as Pickford found Dewsbury-Hall with a quick punt forward. Jacob Ramsey appeared to bring him down in full flight, but referee Farai Hallam played advantage and Barry's left-wing cross was volleyed home by Hackney.
Matthias Jaissle's Magpies pushed for a route back into the tie at the start of the second half, with Yoane Wissa and Dan Burn unable to take headed chances.

But Everton put the result beyond all doubt in the 69th minute, with Garner and Dewsbury-Hall involved again. The former slid the latter into the left-hand channel with a lovely pass, and after Dewsbury-Hall centred for Barry, the striker made no mistake.

Newcastle got a goal back two minutes from time, with Burn nodding Joe Willock's deep cross beyond Pickford, but that proved a mere consolation as a tetchy final few minutes passed without any further chances at either end.
Moyes ends fourth-round hoodoo
Thursday's victory had been a long time coming for Moyes, who had only won one of his previous seven EFL Cup fourth-round ties in charge of Everton, versus Luton Town in 2007-08.

Newcastle, by contrast, had reached the quarter-finals of this competition in four straight seasons, but after the 2025 winners were dumped out in meek fashion, the murmurs of discontent surrounding Jaissle's early leadership will only grow louder.
But judging by the underlying metrics, the Magpies were unfortunate not to progress, having fired off 28 shots (nine of which hit the target) to Everton's 11 (five on target).
Newcastle also narrowly edged the expected goals (xG) battle by 2.09 to 1.84 and created four big chances compared to three for their hosts, but their finishing touch deserted them.

11cvsiddsjq6h1w1e5c3ztq5yy.title: Arsenal 'lack stardust' but are still Premier League title favourites, says Carragher
11cvsiddsjq6h1w1e5c3ztq5yy.subtitle: Arsenal are three points behind Manchester City at the top of the Premier League, but Jamie Carragher still views them as title favourites.
paragraphs: Although Arsenal lack "stardust" in attack, they are still favourites to retain their Premier League title this season.
That is the view of former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher, who feels Manchester City are once again the only team capable of rivalling Mikel Arteta's men.
Noni Madueke came off the bench to score an 80th-minute winner for the Gunners on Sunday, as they ground out a 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.
Since Arteta became Arsenal manager in December 2019, they have had the joint-most 1-0 wins in the Premier League of any side (32, level with Everton).
They are three points below City in the Premier League table, with Enzo Maresca becoming the first manager in the competition's history to win his first seven games in charge of a club.
But the Opta supercomputer still makes the Gunners favourites, with 46.9% of season simulations seeing them top the pile, compared to City's 40.4% chance.

There is also the possibility of City's chances being affected by any punishment levied against the club after they were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules, but even without those off-the-pitch issues, Carragher still feels Arsenal are the team to beat.
"We've said before that Arsenal are not the most exciting champions we've ever seen," Carragher told Sky Sports' Monday Night Football.
"They still lack stardust in the final third and didn't get that superstar over the line that they wanted in the summer.

"There was talk of Vinicius Junior coming in, obviously, and Julian Alvarez, but they didn't get those deals done. They do lack star power in the final third and we saw more evidence of that on Sunday.
"Some people will also say Mikel Arteta has still got the reins on and is stopping them from showing their absolute best going forward, because they value the defence so much.
"But they've got the best squad in the country and the best starting lineup. I don't think anyone can go up against that really, except maybe Man City.
"We said all of this last year as well. They didn't have a game-changer, but what they had were two top-quality players in every position.

"I still see Arsenal as the team to stop. If they dropped more points on Sunday, they could have been five behind Man City. We obviously don't know what’s going to happen with City, we have to take it as it is right now.
"Arsenal would have been a bit worried about being five points behind someone like Man City and dropping points in quick succession, but they got the win."

Arsenal visit Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday before welcoming Everton to the Emirates Stadium on Saturday. City's next Premier League game, meanwhile, is a tricky trip to Aston Villa.
