11hj61xa6ebsj1fz2bbor0kbrv.title: Man City players are 'more together than ever', says Anderson after Anfield triumph
11hj61xa6ebsj1fz2bbor0kbrv.subtitle: Elliot Anderson believes forging a siege mentality can help Manchester City after they were found guilty of breaching Premier League rules.
paragraphs: Elliot Anderson declared Manchester City's players are "more together than ever" in the wake of their guilty Premier League verdict, following Saturday's 3-0 win at Liverpool.

During the international break, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of the competition's financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, and the majority of charges relating to their failure to co-operate with the League's investigation.

City continue to argue their innocence and have appealed against the verdict, although that has not stopped talk of potential punishments – ranging from fines to point deductions, relegations and the stripping of historic titles – from dominating the headlines.
But Enzo Maresca's players did not let the external noise affect their performance against Liverpool on Sunday, as they earned a dominant 3-0 victory at Anfield.
City are the only team to win all six of their games in the Premier League this campaign, as Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki struck after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.

Cherki's goal capped a superb team performance from City, who completed 41 passes in the build-up, the longest for any Premier League goal since Phil Foden netted for them against Nottingham Forest in September 2023 (46 passes).
City were given a frosty reception on Merseyside, and Anderson admits the way others have spoken about their guilty verdict has given them additional motivation.
"We're all so together, more together than ever and I think we have to be like that," Anderson said, as quoted by ESPN.
"We've got to stick together. I think it really brings us together. It gives you that determination to come out here, everyone is against you, and turn them over, which we did.
"We have got some outstanding players and an outstanding coach, so we're only going to get better, and I look forward to that."
Having won at Anfield with Nottingham Forest in 2024-25 (1-0) and 2025-26 (3-0), Anderson is the seventh player to win on his first three away starts against Liverpool in the Premier League.
He controlled Sunday's game, racking up more touches (100), accurate passes (71/78) and successful duels (11/17) than any other player on the pitch.
City put up 1.21 expected goals in the second half of the match, having only registered 0.07 xG in the first half, and Anderson hailed their improvement after the interval.
"In the second half we showed a lot more quality than in the first half," he added.
"It was very noisy in the first half, but we really managed to quieten them in the second half, carried out the plan better and scored three really good goals."
City have another huge game to look forward to on Wednesday, as they welcome two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain to the Etihad Stadium in the Champions League.

11mr2nqtq6zi31tdf6fgikc35d.title: Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: Mac Allister and Ngumoha star in another Anfield comeback
11mr2nqtq6zi31tdf6fgikc35d.subtitle: Liverpool found themselves two goals down in their Champions League tie with Villarreal, but Anfield experienced another European comeback.
paragraphs: Liverpool came from two goals down to produce another memorable Champions League comeback at Anfield as they beat Villarreal 4-3 to keep their perfect record intact.
Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona had put Villarreal in a strong position by the 29th minute, but Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo levelled things up before the break.
Mac Allister scored his second after being teed up by the impressive Rio Ngumoha, with Florian Wirtz netting a confidence-boosting goal before Tani Oluwaseyi's late consolation.

Andoni Iraola made six changes to the side that beat nine-man Brentford, though it was one of the players who remained that gifted Villarreal a shock fourth-minute lead, with Virgil van Dijk's wayward header back to Alisson pinched by Mikautadze, who tucked home from a tight angle.

Ngumoha led Liverpool's fightback by causing havoc down the right-hand side, but it was Villarreal who doubled their lead with relative ease just before the half-hour mark when Nathan Saliba's pass carved open the hosts' defence, allowing Cardona to race through and slot into the bottom-left corner.
However, Liverpool hit back quickly through Mac Allister, who glanced Kostas Tsimikas' in-swinging corner home, with the Argentine then firing inches wide moments later.

And on the stroke of half-time, Liverpool were level. Ngumoha whipped a teasing ball into the penalty area that Cardona attempted to shield, but Araujo steamed in at the back post to nod past former Reds goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi.
Liverpool maintained their momentum early in the second half with Cody Gakpo and Wirtz testing Gulacsi before Trey Nyoni's arrowed drive whistled past the right post.

The comeback was complete just after the hour when Ngumoha once again terrorised the Villarreal defence. This time he provided a pinpoint cross for Mac Allister to sweep home his second – and Liverpool's third – off the crossbar.

Wirtz, who had yet to score for Liverpool this season, continued his good recent form with a left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner in the 68th minute, but Villarreal threatened a nervy finish when Oluwaseyi tucked in from Ayoze Perez's delivery, though the Reds held on to make it three wins from three in Europe this season.
Iraola experiences Anfield magic in the Champions League

Ahead of kick-off, Iraola expressed the importance of building a winning feeling at Anfield, having failed to win at home in the Premier League since taking charge of the Reds, and he would have been fearing the worst when his side found themselves two goals down early on.

Indeed, Cardona's goal, timed at 28:08, was the earliest Liverpool have been two goals down in a game in major European competition since April 2016 against Borussia Dortmund in the Europa League (08:20). However, this is Anfield in the Champions League.

Every time Liverpool have gone 2-0 down this early in a major home European match, they have come back to win – April 1976 vs Club Brugge (12th minute, won 3-2), October 1996 vs Sion (23rd minute, won 6-3) and April 2016 vs Dortmund (ninth minute, won 4-3) – with that trend continuing here.

Two players, in Mac Allister and Ngumoha, took the game by the scruff of the neck, with the latter, at 18 years and 52 days old, becoming the third-youngest player to provide multiple assists in a Champions League game behind Warren Zaire-Emery against AC Milan (17y 231d) and Theo Walcott against Hamburg (17y 250d).

Ngumoha also completed seven of his eight dribbles, but Mac Allister popped up with two big goals. All eight of his strikes in the Champions League have come at Anfield, including one already this season against Atletico Madrid on MD1.

Iraola will, however, feel there is plenty to work on ahead of this weekend's clash with in-form Brighton in the Premier League, but his team were worthy winners here, having finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.37 from their 22 shots to Villarreal's tally of 1.58 from 14 attempts.

11n3subfoazqo11u9nmee8uj2o.title: Jones does not see 'huge change' from Premier League to Serie A
11n3subfoazqo11u9nmee8uj2o.subtitle: Inter's Serie A title defence continues on Saturday as they host strugglers Fiorentina following a midweek win in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Inter midfielder Curtis Jones does not believe "there's a huge change" between the Premier League and Serie A.
Jones, who has missed Inter's last four matches with a thigh injury, joined the Nerazzurri this summer from Liverpool, where he rose through the ranks.
The 25-year-old has featured just five times for Cristian Chivu's side this season, with two of those appearances coming as a starter, and he is yet to score or assist.

Although Inter have 19 points on the board after seven games, 10 of those have come from losing positions. No side has gained more such points in their first seven matches of a season in Serie A's three-points-for-a-win era, level with Juventus in 2013-14 and Inter themselves in 2021-22.
They had to fight back to beat Bologna 3-1 last week, before overcoming Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 in the Champions League in midweek.
And speaking ahead of Sunday's home clash with Fiorentina, Jones explained why he disagreed with some of the stereotypes about the quality of Serie A.
"I don't think there's a huge change [between Serie A and the Premier League]," Jones told DAZN.
"I feel the perspective of the league is that it's a slower league and that the standard is not as high.
"I can agree to an extent in terms of, the games are slower in a way, because of the way teams will play against us, but at Liverpool it was exactly the same.
"[We are] one of the best teams in the league, so I don't think other teams are going to come and try press us, they're going to sit in a low block and make it difficult for us."
Fiorentina have struggled so far in 2026-27, winning just four points from their opening seven Serie A games.
Inter – Hakan Calhanoglu
Calhanoglu has scored more goals against Fiorentina in Serie A than any other side (seven).

In the three-points-for-a-win era, only four midfielders have scored more goals against a single opponent in the competition: Cristiano Doni against Inter (eight), Andrea Pirlo against Parma (eight), Clarence Seedorf against Juventus (eight) and Marek Hamsik against Palermo (eight) and Bologna (nine).
Fiorentina – Cher Ndour

Ndour, who scored in his last game against Inter, is one of five players born in 2004 or later to have registered at least 30 line-breaking passes (41) and at least 30 ball recoveries (32) in Serie A this season, alongside Darryl Bakola, Reda Belahyane, Oumar Ngom and Alessandro Romano.
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER WIN
Inter have won each of their four home games in Serie A this season, scoring 15 goals.

In the last 50 years, only three teams have won each of their first five home matches in a Serie A season while scoring more goals: Roma in 1990-91 (16 goals) and 2016-17 (17), Juventus in 2014-15 (17) and Sampdoria in 2017-18 (16).
Inter are also unbeaten in 16 of their last 18 Serie A matches against Fiorentina (W10 D6), winning four of the most recent six (D1 L1).
Fiorentina have lost all of their last three away Serie A games against Inter, after remaining unbeaten in three of the previous four (W1 D2).
The last time the Viola were defeated in more consecutive away league matches against Inter in Serie A was between 2001 and 2013 (12 straight defeats on that occasion).

Fiorentina have conceded the most goals in Serie A this season (17) and will face the league's best attack in Inter (21 goals); the Viola have conceded a goal every five shots on average, the worst ratio in the current Serie A campaign.

11noa022ig8rh1cetrnma34w5y.title: Wales boss Bellamy 'hurting' after Nations League defeat to Denmark
11noa022ig8rh1cetrnma34w5y.subtitle: Wales' poor run of form continued after they were beaten by Denmark in the Nations League, a result that left Craig Bellamy disappointed.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy admitted he was "hurting" after Wales' defeat to Denmark in the Nations League, conceding his team were second-best at Parken on Sunday.
Wales slumped to back-to-back defeats to begin their Group A4 campaign, with Ben Davies' own goal and Gustav Isaksen's second-half finish sealing a 2-0 win for Denmark.
Rasmus Hojlund had seen a goal ruled out for offside before Denmark took the lead in the 53rd minute when Mikkel Damsgaard's free-kick was turned into the net by Davies.
And it was another Damsgaard free-kick that led to Denmark's second, with Isaksen's deflected volley looping over Danny Ward, and it could have got even worse for Wales.

Hojlund saw another goal chalked off after straying into an offside position, though Neco Williams was denied a late consolation for the visitors after the referee blew his whistle early for a foul by Ethan Ampadu in the build-up.

Wales have now failed to win any of their last six matches across all competitions (D3 L3), losing each of their last three. This is their longest run without a victory since a run of nine between June 2022 and March 2023.
Despite the loss, Bellamy remains confident his side will improve by playing against Europe's elite on a consistent basis, with Norway their next match this Thursday.
"I'm really hurting. When you see an athletic team run over you a little bit, but then, will we improve? I think we will," said Bellamy.
"This team will get better, these players will keep improving. There are young ones coming in well after I'm gone.
"For me now it's just focus, two more games to go. How can I help you improve for the next two games, but also how can I improve?
"I'm probably more loving when I'm losing, I'm probably more of a pain in the backside when I'm winning."

Denmark's dominance was backed up by the metrics. They fired off 20 shots, only managing more in the Nations League on two occasions, coming against the Republic of Ireland in November 2019 (26) and Portugal in March last year (23).
Brian Riemer's side are also now unbeaten in their last eight home matches across all competitions, winning six of those contests (D2).
Wales were only able to muster an expected goals (xG) total of 0.65 from their 10 attempts, but Sorba Thomas acknowledged there was still plenty of room for improvement.
"We are down as a team. We felt we were in the game. They had the proper chances, and they took them," Thomas said.
"We need to be more clinical, we need to start punishing teams when we're on top, that's what they did.
"I would have loved for my shot to go in, maybe the game could have been different. But we had more chances after that and didn't score. We've got to learn from that.
"Thankfully, we've got two games at home still to come. We'll have home advantage, so we need to show a reaction.
"We are just going to get better. We are a small nation, but we've got big hearts and beliefs and, for us, it's about showing that more on the pitch."
Bellamy's main frustration was the way in which his side conceded both goals, with Damsgaard's set-pieces causing the Wales defence all kinds of problems.
"I said to the players before the game, 'this is going to be tougher than Portugal'," Bellamy added.
"It was a different challenge but a very difficult one. The best team won overall.
"As disappointed as I am with that, the result I probably think was fair."

11obk5recdrfk1qntnmb3qyrvm.title: Mancini unfazed by Italy's lack of fluidity in win over Turkiye
11obk5recdrfk1qntnmb3qyrvm.subtitle: Italy were not at their free-flowing best against Turkiye in the Nations League, but Roberto Mancini's side managed to grind out a victory.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini admitted Italy's lack of fluidity against Turkiye in the Nations League was to be expected, given the number of changes he made.
Italy rounded off the international break with a 3-1 win over Turkiye, meaning they have now taken seven points across the first four games of Mancini's second stint in charge.
Aral Simsir cancelled out Gianluca Scamacca's first-half goal on the hour, but two substitutes secured the victory for Italy.
Riccardo Calafiori soon restored the hosts' lead, and Francesco Pio Esposito scored the clinching goal with three minutes of the 90 remaining.
Esposito became only the second player in the history of Italy's national team to score his seventh goal before turning 22, after Giuseppe Meazza (20 years and 155 days on January 25, 1931).

And though Italy did not look their best during the victory, Mancini, who made nine changes to his starting line-up from the draw with France last time out, was not too concerned about the performance.
"Despite the changes, naturally there was also fatigue," Mancini told RAI Sport.
"We suffered at the start, but the lads did well to get it back on track, score again after the 1-1, so it was a good game as the fourth in such a short spell of time.

"The only certainty was that we would lose some of that fluidity; it was fully expected and predicted. We also had two players on yellow cards and the referee seemed inclined to book them again, so I took them off."
Italy sit three points behind leaders France in Group A1, having improved following a 2-0 defeat to Belgium that began their Nations League campaign.
Their final two matches of the group in November will see them host France before travelling to Belgium, with the hopes of reaching the quarter-finals.
"We've got to continue like this; we'll probably have to play for our spot in Belgium," Mancini added.

11preowifnix91u70qxeqaxohq.title: Nashville boss Callaghan demands focus during Supporters' Shield chase
11preowifnix91u70qxeqaxohq.subtitle: Nashville SC could clinch the Supporters' Shield when they face Eastern Conference bottom side CF Montreal on Saturday.
paragraphs: Nashville SC head coach BJ Callaghan has urged his side to remain focused in their hunt for the Supporters' Shield this weekend.
After a 1-1 draw with the San Jose Earthquakes last time out, Nashville will clinch the MLS Supporters' Shield if they win or draw against CF Montreal on Saturday.

Nashville have already topped the Eastern Conference for the first time in their history, and they could set a new MLS single-season points record if they win eight points from their final four matches.
Despite Nashville being on course to record a historic MLS campaign, Callaghan wants focus from his players in Montreal.
"We don't daydream. We don't think about there; we know where we want to go," said Callaghan.
"That's the image of ourselves that we're chasing. But how we go about it is by turning the page each day, and that's where we remain focused on.
"There'll be plenty of time for other people to decide how chapter seven stacks up in the history books of Nashville, but that's not for us.
"Our vision is to take steps each and every day to work, to compete and to execute at an elite standard on this vision of trying to become elite."
Nashville midfielder Cristian Espinoza added: "We have the next opportunity in Montreal.
"Whether it's at home or away, we go with a mindset to take the three points, and that's what we are going to do in Montreal."
Montreal are bottom of the East following a 1-1 draw with the Seattle Sounders last time out, while they also lost the Canadian Championship final against Forge during the week.
To have any chance of pulling off a miraculous recovery and reach the postseason, Montreal must pick up three points against Nashville.
CF Montreal – Prince Owusu
After missing Montreal's draw with Seattle, Owusu will make a return to face conference leaders Nashville.
Owusu leads Montreal in goals (15) and assists (six) this season, and he will need to be at his best if they are to beat Nashville.
Nashville SC – Hany Mukhtar
Mukhtar scored for Nashville in their draw with San Jose, netting his 16th league goal of the season, and his 10th since the World Cup break.
He has also netted in each of his last five MLS games (six goals), his joint-best scoring streak in the competition.
MATCH PREDICTION: NASHVILLE SC WIN
Nashville are unbeaten in their last six MLS matches (W4 L2) and have lost just twice in their last 24 league games (W16 D6).
Only Inter Miami (30) have won more points on the road this season than Nashville (24) among all teams in the East.
When Nashville hosted Montreal back in July, Sam Surridge's penalty secured a 1-0 victory for the conference leaders.
Nashville are unbeaten in their last five meetings with Montreal (W3 D2), but have failed to win in their last three away trips (D2 L1).

11qpxv0jhm1lp1ftnp7ovlhhft.title: Sullivan laments 'terrible' display but MLS record falls to teenager as Union beat Fire
11qpxv0jhm1lp1ftnp7ovlhhft.subtitle: Despite being unhappy with his own performance, Cavan Sullivan broke an MLS record as the Philadelphia Union's winning run continued.
paragraphs: Cavan Sullivan felt his own performance in the Philadelphia Union's win over the Chicago Fire was "terrible", but the teenage sensation still made a piece of MLS history on Wednesday.
By assisting the first of two goals for Bruno Damiani in the Union's 3-1 win at Soldier Field, the 17-year-old broke the MLS single-season goal involvements record by a teenager.

Having tied Diego Fagundez's 2013 mark of 20 goal involvements for the New England Revolution in Philadelphia's previous match, Sullivan now has 21 (seven goals and 14 assists) in 2026, the outright most by any teenager in a campaign.
But the United States' breakout star felt he could have done better on a personal level, having failed to score from four shots and only managed a 75% passing accuracy (28/47).
"I was sort of terrible tonight, so I'm not really focused on any records or stats like that, to be honest," Sullivan said.
"I'm happy with the win, but I've got to look in the mirror and watch some film and see what I have to do better. I'm not really happy with my performance, but it's a great win."
But the Union's interim coach, Ryan Richter, was far more positive in his outlook, saying: "It seems like every week, something else is popping up for him. I'm so happy for him.
"A big emphasis for him is to continue to be decisive in games, and when he's chipping in with goals and assists the way that he has over this last stretch, he's making the difference.
"His work rate has been great, his creativity has been great, but now he's being really decisive. He has been for a long stretch now, so he deserves that, and we're proud of him."
Having won eight straight games, the Union are sixth in the Eastern Conference and boast a nine-point cushion to the teams outside the automatic playoff places.
With just five regular-season games to go, they need a maximum of seven points to clinch a round-one berth, while even four points would guarantee them a wild-card spot.
In the Western Conference, St. Louis City guaranteed their playoff place by rewriting league history.

Though they were held to a goalless draw by the Vancouver Whitecaps, St. Louis have now gone 19 regular-season games without defeat since May 3, equalling the all-time record, which is now held jointly by four teams.
The Columbus Crew in 2004 and 2005, FC Dallas in 2010, and Inter Miami in 2024 and 2025, all previously enjoyed 19-match unbeaten streaks in the regular season.
St Louis' 21-match unbeaten streak in all competitions, meanwhile, is the longest ever managed by an MLS team, surpassing the New York Red Bulls' 20-game run in 2016.
Head coach Yoann Damet said: "It's more than a number. It's the pride in working so hard to create that momentum and to sustain it and to show consistency.
"I think this is one of the hardest things to do in sport at the professional level. There is a reason why it's never been done before."

11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.title: Koge relishing Women's Champions League adventure after Arsenal edge out minnows
11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.subtitle: Arsenal had 19 shots but hit the target just twice as they edged out minnows Koge in their opening Women's Champions League games.
paragraphs: Nadia Nadim says minnows Koge are simply relishing their Women's Champions League adventure following a narrow defeat to Arsenal.
The Gunners, European champions in 2025, clinched a 1-0 win over the Danish team, who are featuring in just their second Champions League campaign.
Mariona Caldentey's last-gasp penalty claimed the points for Arsenal, who were wasteful in front of goal.
Arsenal had 19 shots, but got just two of them on target, while they also hit the woodwork.
While Koge suffered late heartbreak, Nadim, who led the visitors' line, was thrilled with her team-mates.
"So proud of the team and the way we conducted ourselves, especially in the first half," she told ESPN on Disney+.

"We have a young team, a lot of them have no experience playing at this level, good for them to experience what it's like at this level. Good learning, disappointed they got the goal and penalty in the last minute. That's a part of the game, could've done better, but it's our first Champions League game and there's a lot of games left.
"We wanted to be compact and keep the ball, we had people who were comfortable with the ball. We changed in the last 30 minutes, and it didn't do us well because we couldn't get out of the pressure.
"Credit to Arsenal, great team, they find each other well. It's okay, happy for the young players to experience this.
"I enjoy the game. Physically, it's tough because you're so low, it becomes hard to be dangerous, takes a toll to try and get in the box the whole time.
"I love football, I love this game. It's nice to be back here. I always love the Champions League. Now we're a new team, let's see where this adventure will take us."
English sides are now unbeaten in their last 11 Champions League games against clubs from Denmark (W8 D3), since Arsenal’s 1-5 defeat to Fortuna Hjorring in the 2002-03 semi-final.
This win did see Arsenal snap a run of losing their opening Champions League fixtures in each of the past two seasons.
"We left it late," said Arsenal defender Steph Catley.
"It's tough at the moment and in the Champions League there are no easy games. They defended great, we didn't score early and it didn't come until the end.

"In the Champions League, you never think it's an easy day. I was expecting a tough game and it became really difficult but credit to the girls, they did everything and Mariona was very calm in that moment.

"It's hard to put your finger on it [what is going wrong], it is a bit of a slog and the goals are not coming as freely as they have in the past. It's not a lack of trying, we're doing everything we can to put the ball into the back of the net.

"We have great history in this competition and it's important we are in it every year and challenging to win. We have a real belief that we can go on and win it. It's a long season and we're working really hard so to get the wins early on is very important."
Elsewhere on Tuesday, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain drew 1-1.
Felicia Schroder opened the scoring for Madrid after just two minutes, but Sakina Karchaoui equalised from the penalty spot in the second half.

121o6p2cwjskf1rbog3fy9ebfc.title: Luis Enrique dedicates PSG win to injured Kvaratskhelia
121o6p2cwjskf1rbog3fy9ebfc.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain won their first game since Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's injury, but he was not far from the team's thoughts.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique dedicated Paris Saint-Germain's 2-0 win over Lyon to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia following his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.
Kvaratskhelia was taken off during PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona in the Champions League last week and has been ruled out for the remainder of the season.
It is a huge blow for PSG, with Kvaratskhelia proving a key player for them, helping them to back-to-back Champions League and Ligue 1 triumphs in the last two seasons.
On Monday, Luis Enrique's side moved top of the Ligue 1 table, with substitutes Senny Mayulu and Mika Godts netting the goals against their title rivals.
And the Spaniard says the team did it for Kvaratskhelia.
"It's a very important win, and we dedicate it to Kvara," he said. "We are a team that looks to win everything.
"That's our mentality. To do that, you always need to be ready, and the players that came on showed the level they have and that they deserve to play more.
"It's hard for me as a coach, but I love this character and this mentality."
PSG, who were named the men's Club of the Year at Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony, have now won their last eight matches in all competitions, their longest run since January to March 2025 (10).
The victory over Lyon was Luis Enrique's 126th win in all competitions with the club, equalling Laurent Blanc as the manager with the most victories on the PSG bench.
It was the substitutes who ultimately proved the difference against Lyon, with PSG benefiting from eight goals from the bench this term, including each of the last four.
In just 33 minutes of play, Godts was involved in more goals (one goal, one assist) than in his first seven appearances for the club in all competitions (one goal in 203 minutes).
And Luis Enrique was impressed with what he saw from the players who have not had as many minutes recently.
"Obviously, it was a very difficult match – coming after the Champions League – against a very good Lyon side with lots of individual quality and a very good coach," he added.

"It was very tough. I think we made a good start to the game, but it was hard because they defended very well. In the second half, I think we improved a little, and they found it tougher because they had been doing a lot of running.
"We got our goals from players that haven't played as much recently, and I'm very happy for Senny Mayulu, Quentin Ndjantou, Mika Godts, Beraldo and Lucas Hernandez, all the substitutes."

122615eewvk8t12yq2nkzdv9p2.title: Calheira frustrated Sporting KC's performances have not been rewarded
122615eewvk8t12yq2nkzdv9p2.subtitle: Sporting Kansas City and Austin FC are the bottom two teams in the Western Conference, and both are in need of a win on Saturday.
paragraphs: Sporting Kansas City forward Taylor Calheira conceded that it is frustrating for the club when they give their all and do not get results, with Austin FC next up.
Sporting KC have no chance of finishing in the playoffs as they sit bottom of the Western Conference on 22 points, having failed to win any of their last four games (D1 L3).
They have lost their last two outings, including a 3-1 defeat to Real Salt Lake in their most recent match.
And Calheira is disappointed that they have not been able to pick up more points during a frustrating campaign.
"We're all trying. That's the frustrating part," he said. "I feel like we're all giving our 100% no matter what.
"We're trying to get out of last place. We know how big of a club the club is and how much it means to wear the Sporting badge.
"We're all trying. We're all giving our 100%, and I think that's the frustrating part, when things aren't going our way."
Austin's playoff hopes are slipping away after failing to win any of their last five MLS matches (D2 L3), falling to three straight defeats, including a 2-1 loss to the Vancouver Whitecaps.
They sit eight points behind the ninth-place Colorado Rapids with four games remaining, and interim head coach Davy Arnaud lamented their slow starts in recent performances.
"They're good teams," Arnaud said.
"They're very good teams, and against these very good teams, you have to be performing at a top level from the start of the game, which we haven't been."
Sporting Kansas City – Andre Luiz
Luiz had an assist on Kansas City's goal against Salt Lake and now has nine goal contributions (seven goals, two assists) in his nine career MLS matches.
Despite not making his debut until August 29, Luiz's nine goal contributions are the third-most by an SKC player this season (Dejan Joveljic – 11, Calvin Harris – 10).
Austin FC – Myrto Uzuni
Uzuni scored his seventh goal of the season and his third with his left foot against Vancouver.
Uzuni has six career left-footed goals for Austin in the regular season, the second most by any player in club history, trailing only Jon Gallagher (seven).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Sporting KC earned their first road win against Austin in May, but the club have never won consecutive matches in the series.
The only time Kansas City have earned at least a point in consecutive matches against Austin was a win and a draw in the first two meetings in the series in 2021.

And Sporting KC have conceded at least three goals in 15 different MLS matches this season following their 3-1 loss to RSL. No other team in MLS history has had more than 13 matches with three or more goals allowed in a single regular season.

Meanwhile, since joining MLS in 2021, Austin have scored exactly 100 goals on the road in the regular season. That is the second-fewest road goals among teams who have been in the league every season during that time, besting only Toronto FC's 86 goals.
Sporting Kansas City – 37.2%

123bva2gru2vv1veovpnm7iy0d.title: Arteta lauds Gabriel's 'unique' quality for Arsenal
123bva2gru2vv1veovpnm7iy0d.subtitle: Gabriel Magalhaes scored on his 200th Premier League appearance as Arsenal overcame Everton 2-0 at Emirates Stadium.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta believes Gabriel Magalhaes offers a "unique" quality to his Arsenal side after the defender scored on his 200th Premier League appearance.
The Gunners defeated Everton 2-0 at Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Ezri Konsa opening the scoring with his first goal for the club before Gabriel netted after the break.

Gabriel's goal was his 14th headed goal in the Premier League, with only Olivier Giroud (27) scoring more headers for Arsenal in the competition (Ian Wright also 14), but this was the Brazilian's first goal in the competition to not come from a set-piece situation.
In Gabriel and Konsa, Arsenal had two centre-backs score in a Premier League match for the first time since February 2024 (Gabriel and William Saliba against David Moyes’ West Ham, in a 6-0 win).
Arteta was full of praise for his centre-back, who also avoided an injury after an awkward lunge to intercept a cross early in the second half.
"I think he's one of the best centre-backs in the world, no question, with the impact he has in both boxes," Arteta told Sky Sports about Gabriel.
"His leadership, his presence, what he offers to the rest of the boys is unique and we're very happy to have him."
And on the win itself, Arteta added: "Really happy. We made five changes. We've had three games in less than six days, so we knew how tough it was going to be.
"But I thought the team performed really well. I thought it was really active from the beginning, put a lot of pressure on the opposition.
"Players are in good moments and they need minutes. They all did really well."
Having been unbeaten in their first six Premier League games this season (W2 D4), Everton have now lost their last two without scoring.
It was Everton boss Moyes' 400th defeat across all competitions in his managerial career. He has suffered 31 of those against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent.
The Toffees found themselves 1-0 down after just seven minutes, and Moyes felt the early goal made things too difficult for his side.
"[Going 1-0 down early] made it hard and we couldn't really get ourselves back into the game after that," Moyes told BBC Match of the Day.
"Huffed and puffed a little bit, stuck at it for long parts of the game, which was good. We never gave them anything easy but, in the end, we didn't have enough.
"We didn't do enough in an attacking sense, but we certainly did a really good job defensively, trying to make it difficult."

12e1h3o4k68t13armg9omhdek.title: Mac Allister admits 'something wasn't right' under Slot at Liverpool
12e1h3o4k68t13armg9omhdek.subtitle: Alexis Mac Allister was one of the Liverpool players to struggle last season, and he has claimed something was wrong under Arne Slot.
paragraphs: Alexis Mac Allister has admitted "something wasn't right" for Liverpool under Arne Slot last season.
Slot became the seventh boss to win the Premier League in their first season in the competition when he led Liverpool to the title in 2024-25.
Yet the Reds dropped off last term, finishing fifth and failing to make significant progress in the cups.
Slot was dismissed at the end of the campaign, with Andoni Iraola coming in to replace him.
Iraola has made a strong start, with Liverpool losing only one game under the Spaniard so far. On Tuesday, the Reds recovered from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League.
Mac Allister netted Liverpool's first goal at Anfield, and he conceded that it just did not click for the Reds in Slot's second season, as he credited Iraola for the turnaround.
"Last year was a really difficult year for all of us," he told Amazon Prime.
"It was clear that I was not at the level. I am the first one to say, I have no problem.
"Something wasn't right in the group. This manager changed it, and that's really important.
"The way we play is quite different. I don't like to compare. I feel good, that's what I want and that's what I enjoy.

"Now, it's more man-to-man. You have to communicate less because you have to follow [the opponent]. Last year it was more of a zonal thing. With the national team we do more of a zonal thing and it works. Now, we do a one v one and it works.
"In the end, it's about us taking the responsibility."

Liverpool have avoided defeat in five of their six games in all competitions this season in which they have conceded the opening goal (W3 D2 L1), already more than across the entirety of 2025-26 (W2 D2 L18).

12fytptholf7i1erdgqmlacsmi.title: Australia friendlies the beginning of 'new generation' for Brazil, says Ancelotti
12fytptholf7i1erdgqmlacsmi.subtitle: Brazil face Australia in their first matches since exiting the World Cup, with Carlo Ancelotti making a string of changes to his squad.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti says Brazil's friendlies during this international break should serve as the beginning for a "new generation", following their disappointing World Cup campaign.
Brazil were dumped out of the last 16 at this summer's World Cup by Norway, which was the earliest they had been eliminated from FIFA's flagship tournament since 1990.
Ancelotti has responded by making a raft of changes to his 26-man squad to face Australia (twice) and India, with Casemiro and Fabinho among the big names to miss out.
In fact, only Gabriel Magalhaes, Marquinhos, Bruno Guimaraes, Danilo Santos, Vinicius Junior, Raphinha, Endrick and Rayan remain from Brazil's World Cup contingent.
Ancelotti's selection is partly built around players who are also eligible for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, hoping he can use them as the spine of his squad for the 2030 World Cup.
The Brazil boss is expecting a tough test in Brazil's two friendlies against Australia, and he hopes they mark the start of the new era for the Selecao.
"It's difficult to say it's a friendly. For Brazil, it will never be a friendly game," Ancelotti said. "It will be an important game.
"A new season, we have a goal to find new players, to find a new generation of players for the World Cup and the Copa America. And we start the game tomorrow.
"I know that soccer in Australia is not the biggest sport. But they did really well [at the World Cup], and Tony [Popovic, Australia's coach] did a fantastic job.
"He organised a fantastic team, really compact, strong defensively, with a fantastic counter-attack. They won a fantastic game against Turkiye, then lost on penalties against Egypt.
"I think that in modern football, there are no easy games. You have to prepare well for the game; you have to respect the rival and do your best."
Australia come into the game fresh from reaching the World Cup knockout stages for the third time in their history, having lost on penalties to Egypt in the round of 32.
Tony Popovic is preparing Australia for the Asian Cup next January, at which point his contract is set to conclude.
It will be the first time that Ancelotti has managed a match in Australia, and he is looking forward to reuniting with Popovic, with whom he has a friendship with off the pitch.
"We are good friends," Ancelotti said of his relationship with Popovic. "Sometimes we have the possibility to meet to talk about football.
"We spent time together when I was in Milan; we spent time together in Brisbane. It's a pleasure to talk about football with him. He's doing a fantastic job here.
"A really passionate manager. I hope the best for him. I think the World Cup he had was a really good World Cup. The team showed strong quality, a compact team.
"We've had a fantastic reception, not only from the Brazilian community, but from all the people.
"The national team of Brazil is really respected everywhere in the world. [It's] my first time in Australia, so I'm trying my best to enjoy this beautiful country."

12h2ekjm7e45g1pdui5i36ofst.title: Spalletti says Juventus have learned plenty since Sassuolo defeat
12h2ekjm7e45g1pdui5i36ofst.subtitle: Juventus have only lost once in all competitions this season, and Luciano Spalletti feels his side have clearly improved since that defeat.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti believes his Juventus players have already shown they are quick learners this season, as they prepare to resume their Serie A campaign away to Cagliari.
The Bianconeri emerge from the international break seventh in the Italian top flight, with 10 points on the board after five matches.
And Spalletti was impressed with the response the Bianconeri showed after their unbeaten start was halted by Sassuolo, who inflicted a 3-2 defeat on his team on September 13.
In the week after that loss – which was the result of a 94th-minute strike by Vasilije Adzic – Juventus thumped NEC 5-0 in the Europa League, then beat Atalanta 2-0 in Serie A.
"We always want to improve and keep growing," Spalletti told reporters at Saturday's pre-match press conference.
"We always want to learn, because whoever stops learning often ends up repeating themselves, and those who go out and learn new things usually grow.
"I don't see anything negative stopping us from reaching the level you mentioned. What did you call it, hunger? That's always important in football.
"Your love for the game has to show on the pitch, by passing on to those around you a serious approach and a constant drive for high standards. That's something we're doing.
"There's always time and room to grow a bit more. You think you've reached a certain level, and then the following year you say: 'How much more is there?'
"But our attitude is right. After the defeat at Sassuolo, we won two games that were far from straightforward. We're on the path we need to be on."
On Sunday at the Unipol Domus, Juve will be facing a team above them in the table, as Cagliari have made a wonderful start to the campaign under Fabio Pisacane.
They have won four of their opening five matches to occupy a place in the top four throughout the international break, with their only defeat coming by a 1-0 scoreline at home to Inter.
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Cagliari – Daniel Maldini
Maldini has scored in each of his last three Serie A appearances.
The last Cagliari player to score in more consecutive games in the competition was Joao Pedro, who netted in five in a row between October and November 2020.
Juventus – Randal Kolo Muani
Among forwards who have made five Serie A starts this season, Kolo Muani is one of just five players yet to score (alongside Paulo Dybala, El Bilal Toure, Armand Lauriente and Nicolo Cambiaghi).
Additionally, among players with at least 25 touches in the opposition box, only Assane Diao (10) has attempted fewer shots than Kolo Muani (11) – will he find his shooting boots this week?
MATCH PREDICTION – JUVENTUS WIN
Cagliari won their last Serie A match against Juventus, 1-0 on January 17, following a run of nine consecutive games without a win against the Bianconeri (D2 L7).
The last time the Sardinians recorded two consecutive victories against the Bianconeri in the competition was in 2009, when Massimiliano Allegri was Cagliari's head coach.

Despite Juventus winning 47 Serie A matches against Cagliari (only Inter and AC Milan, both with 48, have beaten them more often), the Bianconeri have only won two of their last five league games against the Rossoblu (D2 L1).
Juventus have earned 10 points in Serie A so far this season (W3 D1 L1); only recording more wins in their opening six league games once in the previous six seasons: in 2023-24 (four).

Spalletti's side are favourites, but they may not have things all their own way, with Cagliari starting a Serie A season with four wins in their opening five games for just the second time in their history, previously doing so in 1969-70 – when they drew their sixth match.

12l4gbdxgx10a1o1qiz5owt8ug.title: Chivu: Inter cannot feel sorry for themselves after Champions League horror show against Brugge
12l4gbdxgx10a1o1qiz5owt8ug.subtitle: Cristian Chivu wants Inter to swiftly get back on track after their shock defeat to Club Brugge in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Inter lost 4-3 to Club Brugge in midweek, but Cristian Chivu wants his team to put that defeat swiftly behind them.
Chivu's team fought back to trail 3-2 in the 81st minute of Tuesday's Champions League clash with Brugge at San Siro.
Yet they conceded the decisive blow just six minutes later, with Ange-Yoan Bonny's stoppage-time effort not enough.
Now, Chivu has urged Inter to get back on track when they take on Bologna in Serie A.
"We accept our responsibilities," he said.
"Something didn't work in the final 30 minutes against Brugge, but we mustn't lose sight of what we did well in the first hour.
"We created a lot and entered the second half with the right attitude, producing two major chances.
"Then everything collapsed. We have to analyse it as two matches within one. We need to react and find new energy as quickly as possible. We mustn't feel sorry for ourselves; we need to respond."
Serie A leaders Inter have already shipped 14 goals in all competitions this season, and Chivu acknowledged he needs to find a solution defensively.

"It has to begin with me. I'm the one primarily responsible," Chivu said. "We need to develop a shared mindset and take responsibility. This is a group of fantastic players; we just need to find unity and reconnect with the different moments of a match without allowing adversity to bring us down.
"We must not turn it [the defeat against Brugge] into a drama, even if it hurts, because expectations were high.

"It was a win we could have taken, and I say it with the utmost respect for the opponent. They were well organised and caused us problems when we declined mentally. We lost our confidence and became confused. We reacted emotionally instead of staying organised."
Inter have been dealt a blow, however, with Chivu confirming talisman Lautaro Martinez is set to miss up to a month due to injury.
Bologna - Federico Bernardeschi
Bernardeschi has been involved in six goals (four goals, two assists) in Serie A in 2026, more than any other Bologna player.
Bologna's five goals in Serie A this season have been scored by five different players, with Bernardeschi among those to find the net.
Inter - Marcus Thuram
Martinez has scored five goals against Bologna in Serie A, so Inter will have to do without their top scorer.
The pressure, then, will be on Marcus Thuram, who has three league goals to his name this term, to deliver in Martinez's absence.
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER WIN

There has been a perfect balance in the last nine Serie A matches between Bologna and Inter, with three wins for each side and three draws – including a 3-3 draw in their most recent encounter in May at the Dall'Ara.
Bologna and Inter could draw consecutive league matches for the first time since November 2013 and April 2014.
And Bologna are unbeaten in four of their last five home Serie A matches against Inter (W3 D1), having lost 12 of their previous 15 home league games against them (D3).

However, since last December, Bologna have conceded more goals in home Serie A games than any other side (26); in the same period, excluding promoted and relegated teams, Bologna (W2 D5 L10) have gained the fewest points in home league matches (11 in 17 games, at least five fewer than any other side).

Bologna have drawn four of their last five home Serie A matches (L1), including their two most recent; they could record at least three consecutive home draws in the competition for the first time since between April and October 2024 (seven in that run).

Inter have already taken 16 points in Serie A this season. The Nerazzurri could reach at least 19 points after their first seven league games for only the fourth time in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95), after 2017-18 under Luciano Spalletti (19), 2002-03 under Hector Cuper (19) and 1997-98 under Luigi Simoni (19).

12n7mluytdhay182b4hp43ce2x.title: 'Fear doesn't exist' – Zidane relishing home debut as France boss
12n7mluytdhay182b4hp43ce2x.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane's first home match as France head coach comes against Italy in the Nations League, in a repeat of the 2006 World Cup final.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane is relishing what he believes will be a "very emotional" return to the Stade de France as he prepares for his first home match as France boss.
Les Bleus take on Italy in the Nations League on Friday, aiming to continue their perfect start in the competition.
After Kylian Mbappe helped secure a 1-0 win over Turkiye in their opener, Michael Olise's late stunner against Belgium clinched another 1-0 victory in the competition.
France completed 92.8% of their passes in the opponent's half against Belgium, their highest pass completion rate during a match over the last 20 years.
Zidane insists there is no fear ahead of his home debut, which he hopes to mark with an important win.
"It is very emotional being back here, and will be even more so when the stands are packed with fans," said Zidane in his press conference.
"Fear doesn't exist, otherwise I wouldn't be here. I've never thought about failure in my career. On the contrary, I see only opportunities.
"I have an incredible team, I'm ready to make the dream come true, and I'm going to give it my all."
France and Italy also met in the 2024-25 Nations League group stage, with the away side winning 3-1 on both occasions.
Zidane has a history with Italy; he infamously headbutted Marco Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 World Cup final, which the Azzurri won after Zidane was sent off.
"The images are being replayed everywhere on a loop, I've seen them," added Zidane.
"I haven't spoken to Materazzi since that day. I'm not proud of what I did. I've always said that, but at the same time, I have no regrets. It is part of my career.
"Fortunately, that is not all that I did in my career. There are positive and enjoyable moments, and I prefer to remember those. You can't just have a career of all great moments."

12ne9f6jindxa1ajvhjmzh4fgv.title: Flick urges Barcelona to 'analyse and react' after back-to-back defeats
12ne9f6jindxa1ajvhjmzh4fgv.subtitle: Barcelona's winning start to their LaLiga campaign came to an end on Sunday as they lost 2-1 to Real Madrid in El Clasico.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick wants a swift response from Barcelona after back-to-back defeats.
Barca went down 2-1 to rivals Real Madrid in El Clasico on Sunday.

The Blaugrana had started their LaLiga campaign with nine straight wins. Had Barca won, they would have become the first team on record to win 10 successive matches at the start of a season in Europe's top five leagues.
Flick, meanwhile, is waiting on his 100th Barca win, with the defeat to Madrid coming after a Champions League loss to Paris Saint-Germain.
And the German now wants to see a strong reaction from his team.
"Of course, we have to improve. After this defeat, we have neither arguments nor excuses," Flick said.
"We will talk in every training session. I'm not worried. Two defeats are too many for me and for the fans; we don't want to lose.
"Now it is important to analyse and react. For me, it is clear that we have faced an opponent with great quality, who have been perhaps better than in previous Clasicos, and we were not fresh enough.
"We have to recover well, train very well and respond to this defeat. It's not all bad when you lose, and the road is very long until the end of the season; these things happen.
"We lacked a bit of luck; they also did well. We lacked freshness, but it's [our] first defeat in LaLiga; we won nine in a row, and that also has to be taken into account.
"Now it's important to analyse and react."
Barca take on Alaves in their next LaLiga outing on Saturday.

12vnvv8cqbur219mipd8ekmxq9.title: De la Fuente guarantees 'no complacency' from world champions Spain
12vnvv8cqbur219mipd8ekmxq9.subtitle: Spain face England in their first match since becoming world champions, and Luis De la Fuente remains as motivated as ever.
paragraphs: Luis De la Fuente has guaranteed "there will be no complacency" from his Spain side after becoming world champions.
Spain won their second World Cup after defeating Argentina in this summer's showpiece, with Ferran Torres scoring the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

La Roja are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation, ahead of their Nations League opener against England at Wembley Stadium.
De la Fuente, who signed a new contract in recent weeks, insists his side can still improve as they chase more glory on the international stage.
"I guarantee there will be no complacency," said the Spain boss.
"I know these players; they want to keep winning and making history. It's the only way to achieve our goals.
"The drive to improve must be constant, and this team has it. This match will demand our absolute best.
"What we've done so far isn't enough, but this team has enormous room for improvement."
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
Their last away game vs the Three Lions also ended 2-1, at Wembley in the Nations League in September 2018.
When asked why England seem to falter in big matches, unlike Spain, De la Fuente chose to speak about the threat posed by Thomas Tuchel's side instead.
"I can only speak about what's happening to us; I don't know the inner workings of England," added De la Fuente.
"They're a great team, finalists in the last two European Championships and the World Cup. They're third in the FIFA rankings. A footballing superpower.
"Spain always tries to rise to the occasion in important matches. The game at Wembley will be against a very difficult opponent.
"We're currently in a moment of confidence and security, but any team can beat you, especially one like England."

12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.title: Chelsea's Estevao to 'seize every opportunity' after falling behind Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro
12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.subtitle: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have shone as a front three for Chelsea this season, with Estevao playing a backup role.
paragraphs: Estevao is determined to "seize every opportunity" he gets at Chelsea, having found himself behind Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro in Xabi Alonso's pecking order.
The Brazilian arrived at Stamford Bridge from Palmeiras in 2025 and appeared 36 times across all competitions for the Blues in his debut season at Stamford Bridge.

Across those outings, 20 of which were starts, he scored eight goals and laid on three assists, while ranking second for dribbles attempted (133) and third for dribbles completed (58) among all players in Chelsea's squad, despite his relative lack of gametime.

The 19-year-old would have been hoping to kick on at the start of 2026-27, following Xabi Alonso's appointment as head coach, but he is yet to provide a goal involvement in six outings and has only started twice.
While Pedro Neto has found a new role at wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-3 system, the attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro have been highly impressive.
Of the Blues' 10 Premier League goals this season, only one – Romeo Lavia's opening goal in a 4-3 win over Brighton – has not involved at least one of that trio as the scorer or the assister.
Estevao understands the form of Chelsea's other attackers has limited his opportunities, but he hopes to make a big impression when he gets a chance.
"I think every coach has their own way of playing. Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day, and that's what I do," Estevao said at a press conference while on international duty.
"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training. When I get an opportunity, I try to give my best, day after day.
"I try to seize every opportunity I have, control everything I can, and I leave it in God's hands, and I trust myself a lot, too."
Estevao has only played 148 minutes in all competitions for Chelsea this term, compared to 578 for Palmer and 552 for Rogers, with those figures making them the Blues' two most-used players.
Joao Pedro has played 377 minutes, having missed last Friday's 3-0 defeat to Brentford due to a knee issue.
That injury caused the striker to withdraw from Brazil's squad, but Estevao will hope to rack up some minutes when the Selecao face Australia (twice) and India in friendlies.

"I try to seize every opportunity I have, control everything I can, and I leave it in God's hands, and I trust myself a lot, too."

Estevao has only played 148 minutes in all competitions for Chelsea this term, compared to 578 for Palmer and 552 for Rogers, with those figures making them the Blues' two most-used players. 

Joao Pedro has played 377 minutes, having missed last Friday's 3-0 defeat to Brentford due to a knee issue.

That injury caused the striker to withdraw from Brazil's squad, but Estevao will hope to rack up some minutes when the Selecao face Australia (twice) and India in friendlies.

12y7zx83b0zse1om07hb8dqvc3.title: Carragher: Alexander-Arnold made mistake by joining Real Madrid
12y7zx83b0zse1om07hb8dqvc3.subtitle: Trent Alexander-Arnold is struggling for game time at Real Madrid, and Jamie Carragher would love to see him back in a Liverpool shirt.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Trent Alexander-Arnold "made a mistake" going to Real Madrid, and would like to see him back at Liverpool.
Alexander-Arnold went through the Liverpool academy, making his senior team breakthrough in 2016-17 before ultimately joining Madrid in May 2025.
The right-back made 354 appearances for the Reds in all competitions, winning two Premier League titles, an FA Cup, two EFL Cups, the Champions League, the Super Cup and the Club World Cup.
No defender in Premier League history has provided as many assists in the competition as Alexander-Arnold (64), with ex-team-mate Andy Robertson (62) still remaining behind him.
He has also recorded 82 goal contributions in the Premier League, trailing only Leighton Baines (85) among defenders.
Liverpool fans were not happy when Alexander-Arnold opted to let his contract run down in order to join Madrid, but Carragher thinks a move back to his boyhood club is the right solution.
"I would bring him back," Carragher said of Alexander-Arnold, as quoted by AS.
"He would get a lot of criticism, because I think he made a mistake. I think he made a big mistake going to Madrid. We [Liverpool] have certainly missed his creativity.

"At the moment, he is the third option at right-back [for Madrid]. They are playing a midfielder, [Federico] Valverde, in that position; even in the Clasico, Denzel Dumfries, the starting right-back, came on ahead of him.
"When you are the third option at a club, obviously they want you to leave."
Alexander-Arnold has made seven appearances (four starts) for Madrid in all competitions this term, though he has only tallied 345 minutes. He has one assist to his name.

1319htp1md8ld19sexvna3psgu.title: Man City 'deserved more' against PSG, claims Maresca
1319htp1md8ld19sexvna3psgu.subtitle: Manchester City had 27 shots against Paris Saint-Germain and created some huge chances in the second half, but went down 4-2 in a thriller.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca felt Manchester City's display against Paris Saint-Germain merited a better result.
City found themselves 3-0 down inside 32 minutes at Etihad Stadium, where former boss Pep Guardiola took in his first game since leaving the club.

Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha were on target as the Champions League holders laid down a marker, with City conceding three goals in the first half of a home game for the first time since November 2015 against Liverpool in the Premier League.

Maresca made three changes at half-time, and one of those substitutes, Iliman Ndiaye, curled in a cross for Erling Haaland to score in the 53rd minute. In the process, the striker surpassed Sergio Aguero as City's all-time leading Champions League goalscorer.

City had the impetus, yet a blunder from Gianluigi Donnarumma gifted Maghnes Akliouche a goal. Haaland pulled another one back, only to then squander a golden chance to make it 4-3. Ferran Torres missed a late penalty, but the hosts' comeback hopes fell flat.
Maresca's team ended with 2.57 expected goals to PSG's 1.83 xG, and the Italian felt City's performance was worthy of more.
"We started quite well, until the first goal, and then we concede the second one after one minute," he told TNT Sports.
"That created some bad feelings. Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more.
"Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky today.
"You have to be clinical but not lose the balance."
City have lost four of their last seven Champions League home games (W3) – more than their previous 50 beforehand (three).
PSG, though, are now unbeaten in 10 Champions League matches against English opponents (W8 D2), scoring 26 goals while conceding just 10 in this run.

1353A34F9263AA99BB5F6F85641E5DE8.title: Jurgen Klopp’s new-look Germany yet to find their feet
1353A34F9263AA99BB5F6F85641E5DE8.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesJurgen Klopp’s new-look Germany yet to find their feetShareGermany are still reeling from their painful exit to Paraguay at the World Cup, and a third successive failure to reach the last 16.

In the immediate aftermath, it was clear change was imminent. Julian Nagelsmann resigned on July 3 and it wasn’t long before the German Football Association (DFB) intended to hold talks with former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund manager Jürgen Klopp regarding the vacant role.

Why would Klopp, who held a cushy position as Head of Global Soccer for Red Bull, wish to swap that life by returning to the stress of management? Was it a chance to restore national pride that made him take the job? Or was the itch to get back into the dugout simply proving too strong to resist?

Whatever the reason, the charismatic 59-year-old is back. His first target will be to lead Germany to Nations League glory next summer in what is a perfect warm up for the 2028 European Championships.
It hasn’t quite gone to plan thus far, though.
Euro 2028 may well be less than two years away, but there was plenty of optimism surrounding Klopp’s appointment that the Germans could pose a threat at the tournament – if he got things right.

Several nations changed managers following the World Cup, including Portugal, France, Netherlands, and Belgium. There are always likely to be a period of experimentation whenever a new man is at the helm, especially with a national side, but Klopp has gone one step further.
Indeed, the German opted to select 44 players for the four Nations League games, splitting them into two squads, each due to participate in two of their four Nations League fixtures.
“I want to get to know as many players as possible,” said Klopp during a press conference ahead of the matches.
“There is no A or B team. The squads are put together in a way that makes sense on the pitch and in terms of character and experience.”

The first set of players, which included the likes Nico Schlotterbeck, Jonathan Tah, Joshua Kimmich, Lennart Karl and Kai Havertz, were chosen to feature in the first two matches, while Florian Wirtz, Nick Woltemade and Aleksandar Pavlović were among those selected for the final two games.
Denis Undav and Leroy Sané – who both featured at the World Cup – missed out, with Klopp mixing experience with youth as 16 uncapped players were called up.

It looked as though Klopp was going to get off to a winning start against neighbours Netherlands in match one of the Nations League. A first half goal by Felix Nmecha had Germany well on their way to three points, before Cody Gakpo netted a late equaliser.
Still, a point away from home against arguably their biggest rivals for top spot was certainly encouraging.

Klopp’s first home tie in charge of Die Mannschaft came three days later – against Greece – and while his side dominated proceedings, recording 16 shots to Greece’s eight and finishing the game with 76% possession, the Greeks came away from the WWK Arena with a stunning 1-0 triumph.
Wirtz and Karim Adeyemi were drafted in early to the first squad due to injuries to Havertz and Jamal Musiala, yet neither could make the difference in the end.
Germany now occupy third place in Group 2, with matches against Serbia (home) and Greece (away) coming up over the next few days.
The key question now is, can Klopp’s B squad deliver a maiden victory?
Much will depend on the results against Serbia and Greece, but anything less than six points will surely be seen as a failure – both by Klopp himself, and those higher up in the DFB.
Germany were by far the more dominate team against the Greeks last time out, but failing to take chances is going to prove costly, no matter who it is against.

1361b2vs1au6317ghp0j1wznf9.title: Maresca expecting another difficult test for Man City against Brighton
1361b2vs1au6317ghp0j1wznf9.subtitle: Manchester City got the better of Brighton in the EFL Cup in midweek, with the two teams squaring off once again in the Premier League next.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca has warned his Manchester City team to expect another difficult day at the office when they face Brighton at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.
City and Brighton lock horns once again just three days after their fourth-round clash in the EFL Cup, with the defending champions going through following a penalty shoot-out.
The Citizens had to come from behind twice to force spot-kicks on Wednesday, with Mateo Kovacic and Vitor Reis scoring the equalisers to send the tie the distance.
Geronimo Rulli came up trumps for Maresca's side, saving Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk's efforts from 12 yards out, with Bradford City their opponents in the quarter-finals.
But City now turn their attention to the Premier League, and they will be hoping to return to winning ways after suffering their first league defeat of the season to Aston Villa.
They come up against a Brighton side who lost 2-0 to Liverpool last time out, but this promises to be an entertaining clash, with just five points separating the two teams.

Brighton have scored more goals than any other side in the Premier League this season (23), while City (16.7) and the Seagulls (16.2) are the two highest ranked teams for expected goals (xG) so far in the top-flight in 2026-27.
"What I can say is what I see from there. They are a bit different in terms of style," Maresca told reporters of the challenges Brighton may pose his team.
"They are much more man-to-man oriented. The reason it is so difficult to play against them, it is always on the front foot. They score three, four, five goals.
"That is why you need the right balance. We knew it was a difficult test for us. Again, this is what he said [City were lucky].
"Every manager can say something different. We try to prepare for the game knowing what they will do.
"It's going to be a tough game for anyone who comes against them. No matter if they play in a different competition or in the Premier League."
Brighton have never won in 16 away league games against City (D4 L12), though have avoided defeat in their last two.
It's the most Brighton have played away without winning against an opponent and the most Man City have faced an opponent at home without losing.
The Citizens won 12 of their first 14 Premier League matches against Brighton (D1 L1) but they are without a victory in four since then (D2 L2).
Fabian Hurzeler's side have already produced some impressive results so far this season, most notably beating Premier League champions Arsenal 3-0 last month.
Brighton have been tipped to challenge for a spot in the top four after their electric start, with Maresca saying: "It's early for all the clubs to make predictions. They are very good.
"It's a team that, in any game, they score many goals and creates many chances. It's going to be tough. Where they will be at the end of the season, I don't know."

13939o9dkwowy10yi5x2980z6t.title: Allegri highlights 'important game' for Napoli against Roma
13939o9dkwowy10yi5x2980z6t.subtitle: After a shock defeat to Venezia last time out in Serie A, Napoli host in-form Roma as they look to close the gap on the top four.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri believes Napoli's upcoming Serie A clash with Roma is "an important game" and is "worth a lot".
Napoli have struggled in the league this season, with a 1-0 defeat to Venezia last time out leaving the Partenopei ninth after seven games.

They have lost three of their first seven Serie A matches this season (W3 D1 L3); the last time they recorded at least three defeats in their opening seven league games was in the 2009-10 campaign (four in that instance).
Roma, meanwhile, have announced themselves as title contenders following a strong start under Gian Piero Gasperini.
They have gained 17 points in Serie A this season (W5 D2), their best start after seven games since 2014-15 (18 points).
Should Roma beat Napoli, they would reach 20 points, their joint third-best tally after eight Serie A matches, behind only 21 points in 2000-01 and 24 in 2013-14.
Although Allegri acknowledged the importance of the match, he insisted it would determine how the final league table pans out.
"It's worth a lot, it's an important game, it's Napoli-Roma," said Allegri.

"Roma have been doing well since last year, they qualified for the Champions League, they're near first place. Gasperini is doing a great job. They're a team that's playing with enthusiasm, good technique.

"So it will be a difficult game, but it would be nice to pick things back up after two wins and a draw before slipping against Venezia, while being aware of the fact that it is an important game, but not our last one, nor will it decide Champions League qualification.
"But, we are in ninth place, and we have to improve in certain areas on the pitch.
"Gasperini's teams make plays because they take you man for man, they create a lot of spaces. These can be beautiful and entertaining games, if you get the result. If not, it's a problem.
"We can talk about having good games, but in the end, as we always say, we make our judgements on results."
Napoli – Rasmus Hojlund
Roma are the opponent against whom Hojlund has played the most minutes (223) in Serie A without scoring.
However, they are the only side against whom the Danish forward has provided more than one assist in the competition (two).
Roma – Emanuele Lulli
Emanuele Lulli has made five starts in Serie A this season at 19 years and 61 days old and could make his sixth at 19 years and 68 days.
Among debutants in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95), only Marquinhos (18 years and 181 days) has surpassed this threshold for Roma at a younger age in the top-flight.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Napoli have drawn 55 Serie A matches against Roma (W50 D53 L55); only against Torino (56) have they recorded more draws in their top-flight history.

Napoli are unbeaten in their last eight Serie A home games against Roma (W4 D4); they have not registered a longer unbeaten run at home against the Giallorossi in the competition since the period between 1971 and 1982, when they went 11 games without defeat (W10 D1).
However, in the three-points-for-a-win era, only Atalanta (eight) have won more Serie A away games against Napoli than Roma (seven, level with Fiorentina, Juventus and Lazio).

Napoli have kept a clean sheet in their last two Serie A home matches; they have not recorded three consecutive clean sheets at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in the league since September-October 2021.

Roma have kept a clean sheet in all three of their away games in Serie A this season; in their Serie A history, the Giallorossi have only managed to keep a clean sheet in their first four away games of a season once before, in 2017-18.

13c6f7yf69uql18zec436suubg.title: Viking 3-3 Bayern Munich: Haugen levels late to claim memorable draw after Olise red
13c6f7yf69uql18zec436suubg.subtitle: Viking claimed a memorable draw with Bayern Munich after Michael Olise's red card turned a thrilling Champions League contest on its head.
paragraphs: Michael Olise's avoidable red card proved costly as Herman Haugen's late leveller claimed a memorable 3-3 draw for Viking against Bayern Munich in Tuesday's Champions League classic.
Olise was sent off for two bookings in the space of one second-half minute, and Viking made that advantage count when substitute Herman Haugen steered home from Zlatko Tripic's 90th-minute cross.

Harry Kane's double had earlier dragged Bayern level, cancelling out first-half goals from Gianni Stensness and Peter Christiansen, before Luis Diaz's 71st-minute finish was overshadowed by Olise's petulance soon after in a mistake that ultimately proved decisive.
Viking stunned the Bundesliga giants just 71 seconds in when Stensness nodded past Jonas Urbig from Tripic's right-sided corner.
Lennart Karl whipped wide in response before Olise, Diaz and Kane all tested Arild Ostbo without success, while Tom Bischof fired narrowly wide.
The Norwegian hosts doubled their lead seven minutes before half-time when Christiansen burst onto Erik Botheim's throughball, brushing off Nathaniel Brown before firing into the bottom-right corner.
Henrik Bjordal had a nervy moment soon into the second half, with his challenge from behind on Joshua Kimmich surviving a VAR review for a potential Bayern penalty.
Bayern did get their spot-kick shortly after, with Kane tucking into the bottom-right corner after a VAR review penalised Kristoffer Haugen for his challenge on Konrad Laimer.
Kane levelled with his second strike on the hour, heading home from Kimmich’s clipped cross, before Diaz saw a cute finish that would have made it 3-2 ruled out for offside.
However, Diaz would not be denied for much longer as he stroked into the roof of the net after Laimer selflessly squared with a volley across goal from Kane's delicate clip in behind.

Olise's moment of madness brought more jeopardy just two minutes later when the France winger was first cautioned for a foul on Henrik Heggheim, before a second yellow followed for throwing the ball at Tripic.

Viking capitalised in the dying minutes as Tripic lofted in a left-sided cross, with Herman Haugen rising the highest at the back post and writing his name into the history of a massive European scalp.
Kane form continues as Bayern slip up

Before this clash, only Malta's Valletta (90% – nine defeats in 10) had a higher loss percentage than Viking's 84.6% (11 losses in 13) among all teams to play 10+ European Cup/Champions League matches.
The Eliteserien leaders put a halt to a poor run in Europe, however, claiming a point that will live long in the memory of Norwegian football supporters.

For large parts of Tuesday, it looked like the game would again belong to Kane, who has 36 goals in 40 Champions League games since turning 30. That tally is one more than the great Lionel Messi scored in his 30s in this competition (35 goals in 48 appearances).
Only Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2018 (11) has enjoyed a longer run of successive games with a goal in the European Cup/Champions League than Kane's ongoing streak of nine.
His free-scoring form means Bayern have scored 65 goals across 23 games since a team last kept a clean sheet against them in Europe (3-0 loss to Feyenoord in January 2025).

But Olise's needless sending-off turned a thrilling contest on its head once again, and Vincent Kompany will now be without his star man for Bayern's next game against last season's finalists Arsenal.

Kompany will feel his side did more than enough for all three points, though. Bayern accumulated a massive 3.51 expected goals (xG) to Viking's meagre 0.56, but that should not take away from a momentous outing for the hosts.
