Olise's moment of madness brought more jeopardy just two minutes later when the France winger was first cautioned for a foul on Henrik Heggheim, before a second yellow followed for throwing the ball at Tripic.

Viking capitalised in the dying minutes as Tripic lofted in a left-sided cross, with Herman Haugen rising the highest at the back post and writing his name into the history of a massive European scalp.

Kane form continues as Bayern slip up

Before this clash, only Malta's Valletta (90% – nine defeats in 10) had a higher loss percentage than Viking's 84.6% (11 losses in 13) among all teams to play 10+ European Cup/Champions League matches.

The Eliteserien leaders put a halt to a poor run in Europe, however, claiming a point that will live long in the memory of Norwegian football supporters.

For large parts of Tuesday, it looked like the game would again belong to Kane, who has 36 goals in 40 Champions League games since turning 30. That tally is one more than the great Lionel Messi scored in his 30s in this competition (35 goals in 48 appearances).

Only Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2018 (11) has enjoyed a longer run of successive games with a goal in the European Cup/Champions League than Kane's ongoing streak of nine.

His free-scoring form means Bayern have scored 65 goals across 23 games since a team last kept a clean sheet against them in Europe (3-0 loss to Feyenoord in January 2025).

But Olise's needless sending-off turned a thrilling contest on its head once again, and Vincent Kompany will now be without his star man for Bayern's next game against last season's finalists Arsenal.

Kompany will feel his side did more than enough for all three points, though. Bayern accumulated a massive 3.51 expected goals (xG) to Viking's meagre 0.56, but that should not take away from a momentous outing for the hosts.

13c9j25pgjfo71dk8o2sr3s92l.title: Jakirovic acknowledges Hull must help McBurnie in attack
13c9j25pgjfo71dk8o2sr3s92l.subtitle: Hull City will look to get back to winning ways in the Premier League when they welcome Ipswich Town to MKM Stadium on Saturday.
paragraphs: Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic acknowledged striker Oliver McBurnie needs more support in the final third.
McBurnie scored his first goal of the season on Sunday, converting from the penalty spot as Hull drew 1-1 with Brentford.
On what was his 50th appearance for Hull, McBurnie netted his 20th goal for the club – the most of any player for the Tigers in that timeframe.

McBurnie has applied more high-intensity pressures than any other player in the Premier League this season (554), while only three players have applied more final third pressures than the Hull forward (275).
While Jakirovic was delighted to see McBurnie on the scoresheet, he admitted his striker needs help in attack as the Tigers prepare to take on Ipswich Town.
"It's great for us to see Oli score," said Jakirovic.
"It has not been easy for him to play this role because sometimes he is very alone in the box, and often he is one against two, especially when the ball goes wide.
"We must work on getting more numbers in the box in those situations because it will make us more dangerous and make our opponents drop back more as well.

"However, Oli certainly doesn't suffer any confidence problems. I'd said to him that a goal will come, but more so, it is about performing all over the pitch – to win the ball and play it as we see him do so much.
"He takes pressure off us by doing this and winning free kicks."
Ipswich also drew 1-1 last time out, coming back from a goal down to share the points with Nottingham Forest.
The Tractor Boys took a more defensive approach to the second half, recording just one shot, which came in the 92nd minute, after the restart.
Gary O'Neil praised his Ipswich side's determination and resilience to hold out for a draw against Forest.
"We were never quite able to get our style to get on top of theirs, really. Maybe a little spell in the first half where we got some control," said O'Neil.
"But yeah, one where we had to show a different side to make sure we got something from the game.
"We could have still won it, of course. We had some good moments; [Jack] Clarkey came on and had a big chance again.

"But one where togetherness and shutting up a little bit – going a little bit safer – managed to get us through to the finish line, and I'm proud of the players because it's not easy to do that, so a good point for us."
Hull City – Mohamed Belloumi

Mohamed Belloumi has completed more dribbles than any other player in the Premier League this season (19), while his success rate of 61% (19/31) is the highest of any player to have attempted at least 15.
Ipswich Town – Julio Enciso
Julio Enciso has had more shots from outside the box than any other player in the Premier League this season (17), with his opener against Forest last time out coming from range.
MATCH PREDICTION: HULL CITY WIN

This is the first-ever top-flight meeting between Hull and Ipswich, the 1,456th fixture to have been played in England's top division (946th in the Premier League). The Tigers are winless in five league games against the Tractor Boys (D1 L4).
Both Hull and Ipswich have 10 points in the league this season, the first time two promoted sides have double figures after eight games since 2010-11 (West Brom 12, Blackpool 10).
It is also the joint-earliest two promoted sides have faced each other with 10+ points, along with West Brom (10) v Hull (17) on MD9 in 2008-09.

Having won their first two Premier League games this season, Hull are now winless in six (D4 L2), with no side currently on a longer run without victory than the Tigers (Manchester United and Sunderland also six).

However, Ipswich have conceded in each of their last 27 Premier League games (eight this season, final 19 in 2024-25). The last team to have a longer run without a clean sheet were Watford (30 between March 2020 and January 2022).

13fm7c75kvm261e7vls7qfuvd6.title: 'It's an unbelievable moment for Bournemouth' – Tavernier relishing Milan clash
13fm7c75kvm261e7vls7qfuvd6.subtitle: Bournemouth continue their maiden Europa League campaign with a huge test against European giants AC Milan at Vitality Stadium.
paragraphs: Bournemouth winger Marcus Tavernier believes their Europa League clash with AC Milan is "an unbelievable moment" for the club.
The Cherries have enjoyed a strong start to their maiden European campaign, following up a 2-1 away win at Real Sociedad with a 3-0 home victory against Sturm Graz.
Bournemouth are now looking to become the first English side to win their first three matches in major European competition since Sunderland in the 1973-74 Cup Winners' Cup.
Standing in the way of a third consecutive European win for Marco Rose's side are Milan, who have won the Champions League seven times – the second-most of any team after Real Madrid (15).
Tavernier, who scored in Bournemouth's win over Sunderland last weekend, is relishing the chance to play against a European heavyweight such as Milan.

"For us, it's our job but at the same time, when we got the draw, we wanted to play these massive clubs who have had so much success in their own leagues and European competitions," said the 27-year-old.
"If you told us last season that, this season, we would be playing against Milan at home in the Europa League, I think we would have snapped your hand off for it.
"It's an unbelievable moment for Bournemouth in the way we want to proceed, to carry on going to be involved in these types of games and make Bournemouth a bigger club in the world."
Bournemouth will be the 12th different English team that Milan have faced in major European competition.

Milan's first game against each of the last six English clubs they have faced ended in draws, though one of those was the 3-3 draw with Liverpool in the 2005 Champions League final, which they lost on penalties.
Rossoneri head coach Ruben Amorim failed to beat Bournemouth in all three games as Manchester United boss (D2 L1), most recently a 4-4 draw in December 2025.

13hpl4v63z5h21ktg7afrw550z.title: Austin are 'up for any challenge' ahead of facing Nashville, says Arnaud
13hpl4v63z5h21ktg7afrw550z.subtitle: Austin FC are still aiming to clinch an MLS Cup Playoff spot, but they must next face Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC at Q2 Stadium.
paragraphs: Austin FC's interim head coach Davy Arnaud is confident his side are up to the challenge of facing Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC in MLS.
Austin still have outside hopes of trying to clinch a playoff spot in the Western Conference, sitting 13th on 31 points, just five off LA Galaxy in the final wildcard place.
They are unbeaten in their last eight games (W3 D5), though all of their wins have come on the road in that time.
However, last time out at home, they trailed 3-0 to San Diego FC before coming from behind to earn a draw.
Austin come back from the international break knowing they face a tough test versus Nashville, but Arnaud has no doubt his players will give it their all.
"Nashville is very good, and we understand that. Listen, there is not an easy game in this league," Arnaud said.
"We say the most important thing is for us to be tough to beat.
"I think you've seen these guys; they're up for any challenge. I think they've shown that."
Nashville are top of the East on 60 points, with a 14-point cushion over the New England Revolution and Inter Miami in second and third, respectively.
With seven games left to play, BJ Callaghan's side need 15 points to break the all-time points record for a regular-season campaign.
They have lost just one of their last 10 league games and went into the international break on the back of two straight wins in which they did not concede, against the Chicago Fire and Toronto FC.
Austin FC – Christian Ramirez
Ramirez scored in the 82nd and 86th minutes in Austin's draw with San Diego, and he has now scored five goals in the 80th minute or later this season.
That is tied for the most such goals by any MLS player this year and is the most in a single season ever by an Austin player.
Nashville SC – Hany Mukhtar
Mukhtar scored his 100th MLS goal (95 regular season, five playoffs) for Nashville, the first player to hit the mark for the club and the seventh in MLS history to do so with any single team.
The next five highest-scoring German players in league history have a combined 97 goals (regular season and playoffs).
MATCH PREDICTION: NASHVILLE SC WIN
Nashville have won three of their five all-time meetings (D1 L1) with Austin, with the last being Nashville's 2-1 triumph in last year's U.S. Open Cup Final.
That was one of Austin's two times hosting Nashville, as the teams also played out a 1-1 league draw in Texas in 2022.
Nashville need 15 points over the final seven regular-season matches to surpass Inter Miami (74 in 2024) for the most points in a season in MLS history.
Austin, meanwhile, extended their unbeaten streak in league play to eight games (W3 D5) with a 3-3 draw with San Diego, coming from 3-0 down.
It was Austin's first time earning a result in an MLS match (regular season or playoffs) in which they trailed by 3+ goals (L23 prior to the draw).

13lly3g9au5g119mkhxti1u0gy.title: St. Louis City's Navarro wants to be 'among the greats'
13lly3g9au5g119mkhxti1u0gy.subtitle: St. Louis City SC are on a 17-game unbeaten streak, with the LA Galaxy coming to town this weekend.
paragraphs: Rafael Navarro is out to be one of the greats in MLS, having made a superb start to life at St. Louis City SC.
Navarro has netted 15 goals in MLS this term, with five of those coming in as many games for St. Louis.
He joined the club in a $12m deal from the Colorado Rapids at the end of MLS' summer transfer window.
And Navarro has lofty ambitions as he aims to live up to a record-setting price tag.
"It means a lot to me, because I like to be among the greats. I work hard for that, you know?" Navarro told MLSsoccer.com.
"So I like having that price tag.
"I know it happened because I’m doing my job well, so I enjoy it. I know that I can improve more.
"For sure, it's an honour. I know what my responsibilities are, what my job is, what my game is. I think there’s pressure, but I'm used to playing with pressure. I played in Brazil."
Navarro has come into a team that are flying high, with St. Louis City on a 17-game unbeaten run.
St. Louis City are also riding high towards the top of the Western Conference. Next up is a clash with the LA Galaxy.
"It's been a very good experience for me," Navarro said.

"I enjoy the league, which is getting better and better, and all the big-name players who have come here, like [Lionel] Messi, Robert Lewandowski, Antoine Griezmann, Thomas Muller. So MLS is a very good league.
"The culture, the pitches, the competition, they're a little different. But I've been treated very well. I also like the city a lot. I like living here. I enjoy the life I live."
St. Louis City SC - Rafael Navarro

Navarro is only the second player in MLS history to have scored at least 10 goals with one team and five with another in the same regular season, joining Mike Magee in his 2013 MVP season (15 with the Chicago Fire, six with the LA Galaxy).
LA Galaxy - Justin Haak
Haak scored his first goal of the season for the Galaxy in their win over the Rapids last time out.
The goal came from a header, and two of the Galaxy's last four goals have been headers after not having a header among any of their previous 23 regular-season goals prior to that.
MATCH PREDICTION: ST. LOUIS CITY WIN
St. Louis City have never lost to the Galaxy, winning three matches and drawing the other four.
They have scored multiple goals in each of the last six matches in the fixture and tallied three goals in each of the last three meetings.
The Galaxy defeated Colorado 3-2 before the international break, their second straight win by that scoreline after they also beat Minnesota United.
They had scored three goals just once in their first 26 regular-season matches of 2026 entering their current run.
St. Louis City, though, are on the third-longest single-season point streak in MLS history (after FC Dallas – 19 games in 2010, and the Columbus Crew – 18 games in 2004).

13o601wucv8ge1ud4klyge60ol.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended by Portugal amid investigation into explosive statement
13o601wucv8ge1ud4klyge60ol.subtitle: The Portuguese Football Federation has opened disciplinary proceedings against Cristiano Ronaldo, after his sudden exit from their camp.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by Portugal while the country's football federation investigates the explosive statement he issued regarding his departure from their squad.
During the recent international break, Ronaldo made headlines by storming out of the Selecao's camp after Jorge Jesus failed to bring him off the bench during a 2-1 Nations League win in Norway.
Jesus subsequently said he would never allow any player to influence his tactical decisions, and Ronaldo issued a statement addressing his choice to turn his back on the team.
Ronaldo said he will continue to make himself available for selection by his country but accused Jesus of "breaking his word" regarding his involvement in the Norway game.

In his 1,700-word statement, Ronaldo also said his camp had prepared eight points for Jesus to read at a press conference, one of which read: "I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game."
Jesus refused to read those points to the media, which Ronaldo said led directly to his decision to leave the camp.

Now, despite Ronaldo saying he would like to play "one or more farewell matches", the future of the all-time leading scorer in men's internationals (with 146 goals in 234 caps) is in major doubt, with the Portuguese Football Federation opening disciplinary proceedings against him.

A statement from the FPF confirmed the initiation of "disciplinary proceedings against Cristiano Ronaldo, with the purpose of the investigation of any disciplinary relevance of the facts revealed on October 7.
"The preventive suspension of the player was determined, and an urgent nature was attributed to the process."
Ronaldo and Jesus had seemingly enjoyed a strong relationship prior to the row, with the 72-year-old leading Al-Nassr to the Saudi Pro League title last season.
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 appearances under Jesus at club level in 2025-26, averaging one every 99 minutes.

But in his only Portugal outing under Jesus, in a 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, Ronaldo had seven shots with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.03 without scoring – his most attempts without netting in any game since a World Cup qualifier against the Republic of Ireland in October 2025 (also seven).
Since the start of 2025, Portugal have won five of their six games (D1, 83.3% win rate) when Ronaldo has not appeared, compared to 10 of 17 with the forward (D4 L3, 59% win rate).

13q51g1bke3d3111iiywrd7opz.title: 'Ronaldo will never be forgotten' – Hojlund dedicates goal to 'idol' Cristiano
13q51g1bke3d3111iiywrd7opz.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal future is unclear, but Denmark's Rasmus Hojlund paid tribute to international football's record goalscorer.
paragraphs: Rasmus Hojlund paid tribute to his "idol" Cristiano Ronaldo in the best way he knew how.
Hojlund netted for Denmark against Portugal in the Nations League on Thursday.
Portugal went on to win 4-2, doing so in the absence of their iconic forward Ronaldo.
The 41-year-old sensationally left Portugal's squad earlier this week, reportedly due to a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus over his game time.
Ronaldo's Portugal future is unclear, but former Manchester United striker Hojlund dedicated his goal to the five-time Ballon d'Or winner.
Hojlund mimicked Ronaldo's iconic 'siuuu' celebration, and explained he wanted to pay homage to his favourite player.
"I just wanted to dedicate my goal to my idol," Hojlund said.
"For everything Cristiano is going through at this point in his career, he will never be forgotten."
Ronaldo is the highest-scoring player in the history of international football, with 146 goals to his name.
He has netted 979 career goals in total.

13rfsg9b6p3sq19vkq2rgtc78d.title: Heavy workload led to Haaland substitution, says Solbakken
13rfsg9b6p3sq19vkq2rgtc78d.subtitle: Erling Haaland asked to be taken off against Portugal on Sunday, with Stale Solbakken revealing that fatigue played a big part in it.
paragraphs: Norway head coach Stale Solbakken revealed Erling Haaland's heavy workload led to him asking to be substituted against Portugal in the Nations League.
Haaland signalled to Norway's bench that he needed to be replaced in the 2-1 loss to the Group A4 leaders and was taken off in the 67th minute.
The striker started all four of the team's Nations League matches during the extended break, scoring three goals, though they all came in the first two games.
Haaland has also started all seven of Manchester City's games so far in all competitions, coming off the back of a summer in which he helped take Norway to the World Cup quarter-finals.
He was not moving freely before his substitution against Portugal, though Solbakken tried to allay injury worries ahead of Haaland's return to Manchester.
"He was tired against Wales," Solbakken said when asked about Haaland.
"That's why we had a heart-to-heart conversation [on Saturday]. We went through the possible options.
"He might have played the last 45 minutes against Portugal. That was a discussion. But he has very bad vibes and feelings about it. I am very pleased that he managed to pull out 60 good minutes.
"He's in the group that carries the heaviest workload — precisely because his team [City] plays in every tournament and he's the main man.
"It's tough. But we can't do anything about it. We just have to play the games we are called up for. It's tough.

"For those who play in the Champions League and have had little vacation, it's more brutal than for the others. Especially for the players who didn't get a vacation this summer because of the World Cup and that they came far. We did that."
Norway currently sit at the bottom of their Nations League group with only two games left to go: a home game against Wales before a trip to Denmark in November.
"The points haul is too poor," Solbakken added. "But there is no nut to crack.
"It's just a matter of continuing as we have done for a while, and which we have had great success with. We will get even more of that in the future if we have our best players with us."

13s5q7hl0vjfe15te3d0ajszsy.title: Paris Saint-Germain 3-1 Le Mans: Luis Enrique's side cruise to third straight win
13s5q7hl0vjfe15te3d0ajszsy.subtitle: Despite being pegged back early in the second half, Paris Saint-Germain rallied to continue their Ligue 1 winning streak.
paragraphs: Paris Saint-Germain earned a third straight win in Ligue 1, beating Le Mans 3-1 to move up to fifth in the table.
Louis Mafouta cancelled out Beraldo's first-half penalty before quickfire goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Maghes Akliouche secured all three points.
PSG started on the front foot and got their reward in the 19th minute as Harold Voyer was penalised for a handball in the box following a lengthy VAR check.
Beraldo drilled his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner, just squeezing it past Nicolas Kocik, who had dived the right way.
Matvey Safonov rushed off his line to smother Mafouta's one-on-one chance 29 minutes in, while Akliouche also saw a header saved at the other end just before half-time.
Just moments after Achraf Hakimi was denied one-on-one by Kocik, Le Mans moved quickly up the field in a sweeping counter-attack, and Mafouta was on hand to finish it off in the 54th minute.

But PSG restored their lead in the 61st minute as Kocik failed to properly clear a corner. His punch was fired back at goal by Fabian Ruiz, and though the goalkeeper parried it, Kvaratskhelia was on hand to turn in the rebound.
And Akliouche got his first PSG goal just seven minutes later; he was allowed to advance down the right by Le Mans before picking out a near-post finish.
Dame Gueye clipped the crossbar after a mazy run into the PSG box shortly after, but there was still time for late drama.

Lucas Hernandez was tugged back in the box by Rayan Bamba, and Desire Doue's 93rd-minute penalty was well saved by Kocik. Vitinha was caught in the process of trying to reach the rebound, with the referee awarding another spot-kick, though that was overturned by VAR.
It was an uncharacteristic start to the season for PSG as they failed to win any of their first three matches, but they have been in fine form since then.
Three straight wins mark their best run of victories since a sequence of seven consecutive victories between December 2025 and February 2026.

It was another dominant display in the final third for Luis Enrique's side, too. They had 22 shots against Le Mans, taking their tally for the season up to 128, while they had seven Opta-defined 'big' chances overall.
Top-scorer Ferran Torres was kept fairly quiet, with Hakimi leading the way for shots (five) and touches in the opposition box (nine) among PSG players.

Warren Zaire-Emery certainly made his mark after coming off the bench, creating a joint-team-high three chances (three, level with Lucas Digne), and getting one assist, proving Luis Enrique has the strength in depth, even in Ousmane Dembele's absence.

13x92vs7xzx8b1hp7iojyveic9.title: Messi delivers emotional farewell ahead of final Argentina appearance
13x92vs7xzx8b1hp7iojyveic9.subtitle: Lionel Messi will make his final appearance for Argentina against Benin, and he has taken the time to thank the Albiceleste's supporters.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi penned an emotional tribute to the people of Argentina as he prepares to represent the national team for one final time in Buenos Aires.
Messi confirmed in August that he would draw the curtain on his stellar international career, following Argentina's 1-0 defeat to Spain in this summer's World Cup final.
The 39-year-old will make his 208th cap in a friendly against Benin. No player in Argentina's history has represented their country more times than Messi.
During his international career, which started in 2005, Messi has gone on to score 125 goals for Argentina, at least 69 more than second-placed Gabriel Batistuta.
He led Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022, while he has also won two Copa Americas and the Finalissima in that time.

Messi was included in a 28-man squad list published by the Argentine Football Association (AFA) for home friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin during this international break, with it later confirmed Messi would only be present for the clash with Benin at Estadio Monumental.
And ahead of his goodbye, Messi paid tribute to the Argentina supporters.
"The moment has arrived. I leave in peace. I gave it my all. This shirt was my dream, my pride, and my life for years," Messi said.
"Thank you for loving me so much, thank you for your support. I will always carry you with me."

No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34) and most editions (six, level with Cristiano Ronaldo).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, while only Kylian Mbappe (22) has netted more often, though the Inter Miami star was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 this summer.
But the post-Messi era has begun strongly, with Argentina beating Bolivia 4-0 and Burkina Faso 7-0 across their two friendlies so far.

13zqowgjve3a41r1rsy5yjstjb.title: Nashville still have 'more work to do' after clinching Supporters' Shield, says Callaghan
13zqowgjve3a41r1rsy5yjstjb.subtitle: Nashville SC got their hands on the trophy at the weekend, but with history in their sights, BJ Callaghan is chasing a win in midweek.
paragraphs: BJ Callaghan insists Nashville SC still have "more work to do" after clinching up the MLS Supporters' Shield last time out.
Nashville won only the second title in the club's history thanks to their 2-0 win over CF Montreal last time out, following their 2025 U.S. Open Cup triumph.
Callaghan's side are now chasing history, with only five points needed from their final five games to record the highest-ever single-season points tally, and they have the Philadelphia Union next.
Despite achieving their goal, Callaghan is not ready to take his foot off the gas, wanting to take momentum into the playoffs.
"It's a huge step forward for the club and for the city," said Callaghan.
"We know that the consistency and the body of work all year is what we want, but it also validates that the work that we're doing is good work.

"We're constantly reflecting, refining what we're doing. It shows that body of work has occurred throughout the season. That's what that Supporters' Shield recognizes, the long-term season's body of work.
"And we know that we've got more work to do."
Philadelphia, meanwhile, lost for the first time since before the World Cup break last time out, suffering a 2-1 defeat to the New England Revolution.

They have all but confirmed their playoff place thanks to that 15-game unbeaten streak, which leaves them sixth in the Eastern Conference, but they will be without top goalscorer Milan Iloski for the clash with Nashville after he suffered a hamstring injury last time out.

"It doesn't seem like it's something that's a long-term thing, but he has a minor hamstring strain that he picked up at the end of the game," interim manager Ryan Richter said of Iloski, who has 19 league goals this term.
"He'll be out for sure for Nashville, and he'll be out for [FC Cincinnati]. And then we have to see how he progresses in the next few days to give the timeline of when he actually will be fully fit."
Nashville SC – Sam Surridge
Sam Surridge scored the winning goal in Nashville's Supporters' Shield-clinching win on Saturday, just his fourth goal on the road this season.
His 14 goals at home this season are the most in MLS, one ahead of Petar Musa and team-mate Hany Mukhtar's 13.
Philadelphia Union – Cavan Sullivan
Cavan Sullivan has recorded a goal contribution in eight straight regular-season away matches (six goals, five assists) dating back to May.
Only eight players in MLS history have contributed to a goal in nine or more consecutive road matches.
MATCH PREDICTION: NASHVILLE SC WIN
There have been just 17 total goals in 10 all-time regular-season meetings between Nashville and Philadelphia, with the last match ending in a scoreless draw.
There have been fewer than two goals scored in five of the 10 meetings, including a pair of scoreless draws.

But Nashville will want to win on the celebration of their Supporters' Shield win. They need just five points from their last three matches to set a new MLS single-season points record (Inter Miami – 74 in 2024).

The Union's 15-match regular-season unbeaten streak came to an end with a 2-1 loss at New England, Richter's first regular-season loss as Union head coach. It was the Union's first defeat since May 24 at Miami.
Philadelphia Union – 25.3%

1429plvnrr9a91g86ly7cguppv.title: Saka: Seven-goal demolition of Croatia 'everything England were looking for'
1429plvnrr9a91g86ly7cguppv.subtitle: England crushed Croatia 7-0 in their third Nations League fixture on Saturday, with a performance Bukayo Saka felt was close to perfection.
paragraphs: Bukayo Saka said England's performance against Croatia was "everything we were looking for", after they made history with a staggering 7-0 win in Rijeka.
Saka joined Kane in scoring twice, while Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers were also on target on a memorable night for Thomas Tuchel's side.
England's win was their biggest over a team in the top 50 of the FIFA World Rankings since they were first published in 1992, while it was also the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history.

Croatia's previous worst result was a 6-0 Nations League defeat in Spain in 2018, while they had never previously lost a home game by more than a three-goal margin or conceded more than four goals in a match on their own turf, losing 4-1 to England in September 2008.

Kane, Gordon, Bellingham and Saka all scored in the first half, marking the first instance of four different England players netting before half-time in a single game since March 2013, when Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain did so in an 8-0 win over San Marino.
England now have six points on the board after three Nations League games, and a victory over Czechia on Tuesday would put them on the brink of qualifying for March's quarter-finals.
Speaking to ITV Sport after full-time, Saka praised the Three Lions for their relentless approach and their refusal to take their foot off the gas after half-time.
"It was an amazing night. We came out from the start and we were on top," he said. "We played with high energy, high spirit and we punished them.
"We enjoyed that performance. It was special and it was really fun to play in. We played with energy and we were really clinical today, which made the difference.
"Scoring two goals for England is always a nice feeling, so I'm really happy with that.
"I think we showed the hunger, passion and quality that we have. It was a mixture of everything. It's everything we were looking for, so we're really proud and we want to finish strongly on Tuesday.
"There's still three games left, but that will definitely give us a massive boost in confidence and momentum."
While Saka scored two right-footed goals in a game for the very first time in his senior career, on his 378th outing for club and country, it was Bellingham who truly stole the show.
He had three assists to go with his goal, becoming the first England midfielder to record four goal involvements in a game since David Platt scored four against San Marino in February 1993.
Bellingham, who was crowned England's Player of the Year for 2026 last month, created eight chances for team-mates.
No player has ever created more in a single top-tier game in the Nations League.
"He was amazing tonight, to be fair. He deserved to be our Player of the Year and he probably deserves Man of the Match tonight as well," Saka said of Bellingham.
"He was special. I'm so happy to play with him and to have him in the England team."

And Saka also heaped praise upon Gordon, who has been directly involved in a goal on each of his last five England appearances (four goals, two assists in total) – in the last 10 years, Kane is the only other player to achieve that feat for the Three Lions.
"He's another player who's also on fire in an England shirt," Saka said. "It's nice to have players like that around you, putting in performances like tonight."

1479ub0ho48g51ayzoznx5paae.title: Christie: 'Special' win over Milan can give Bournemouth momentum
1479ub0ho48g51ayzoznx5paae.subtitle: Bournemouth's fine start in the Europa League continued against AC Milan, but Ryan Christie turned his attention to their league form.
paragraphs: Ryan Christie was thrilled to deliver on a "special" occasion for the Bournemouth supporters as their perfect start in the Europa League continued with a 3-0 win over AC Milan.
Bournemouth became the first English side to win their first three games in major European competition since Sunderland back in October 1973 with a fine display on Thursday.
Justin Kluivert's early penalty got the Cherries off to the perfect start, with their task made even easier when Mike Maignan was sent off for shoving Tyler Adams in the face.
The incident saw referee Vassilios Fotias point to the penalty spot again, with Lorenzo Torriani's first touch of the ball was to pick Marcus Tavernier's spot-kick out of the Milan net.
Bournemouth's dominance continued after the break, and it was rewarded in the 84th minute when substitute Amine Adli bent a brilliant left-footed free-kick past Torriani's dive.
Marco Rose's side netted twice from the penalty spot in the first half of a game (any competition) for the first time since November 2024 against Wolves in the Premier League.

And just 16 years after competing in the fourth tier, Bournemouth earned a seismic win over seven-time European champions Milan, with Christie describing the Cherries' rise up until this point as "incredible".
"What a game. The boys spoke about it before the game. Listen, it's a special game for the club, but it becomes a lot more special if you go and win the game," Christie said.

147gcfxedqe5t1i80q483px4mx.title: Spalletti: Juventus cannot afford weak moments against Celta Vigo
147gcfxedqe5t1i80q483px4mx.subtitle: Juventus started their Europa League campaign with a big win over NEC, and they face Celta Vigo next on Thursday.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti believes his Juventus side "cannot afford moments where we seem weak" in their Europa League clash against Celta Vigo.
Juve won 5-0 on matchday one against NEC, converting five goals from just 11 shots to top the league phase.
The Bianconeri have also kept a clean sheet in each of their last four group stage games across the Europa League and Champions League.
Celta Vigo, meanwhile, have now lost their last three Europa League games, their worst ever losing run in major European competitions, and won just once in LaLiga this term (D5 L2).

However, Juventus are winless in their last six major European matches against Spanish teams (D3 L3) since a 3-0 win over Barcelona in December 2020, and Spalletti is wary of the threat posed by Celta.
"This competition gives us the possibility of expanding our knowledge of the group, because we need to play some new faces and allow others to recuperate for the next match," said Spalletti.
"We go into this competition the same way we do any tournament, as we must always battle to get as far as possible.
"There are teams in this competition that could easily have been in the Champions League and narrowly missed out, but are built for that level.
"Claudio Giraldez is a very good coach and he sets his team out in an interesting way, so we need to be at the right level that is fitting for our club.
"There is no fear, nor pressure upon us. Giraldez has shown he can field a team with quality and experience, so we cannot afford moments where we seem weak."
Celta and Juve met in the UEFA Cup in the last 16 stage in 1999-00 – after losing 1-0 away in the first leg, Celta won 4-0 at home in the second leg to progress.

          Arsenal 3-0 Lille Stats: Subs Inspire Second-Half Blitz to Secure Comfortable Champions League Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 13, 2026
          
                      Oliver King / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Check out the best facts, stats and Opta data from this Champions League match with our Arsenal vs Lille stats page
Arsenal's perfect start to their Champions League campaign continued as Bukayo Saka starred off the bench in the Gunners' 3-0 win over Lille at the Emirates Stadium.
Jurriën Timber scored the first of Arsenal's three goals in seven second-half minutes, with Saka then teeing up Eberechi Eze two minutes after replacing Noni Madueke.
Saka got in on the act in the 71st minute after combining with fellow substitute Kai Havertz, as Arsenal followed up their win over Napoli with a more convincing display here.

Arsenal did, however, struggle to find their groove early on but carved out two chances in quick succession, with Bruno Guimarães turning Timber's cross wide from inside the box, before another delivery from the Dutchman was headed straight at Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer by Mikel Merino.

The visitors then had a goal ruled out for an offside against Ayase Ueda, who finished calmly past David Raya, but the Spaniard's clean sheet was preserved on the day he went level with David Seaman for most European Cup/Champions League games played among Arsenal goalkeepers (38).

Eze then had a shot saved before Guimarães' swerving strike in first-half stoppage time almost caught out Özer, who jumped quickly to his feet to swat the ball behind with Viktor Gyökeres waiting to pounce on the rebound.

Lille continued to frustrate Arsenal in the second half and just as Mikel Arteta was preparing to bring on his rested first-team players in Saka, Havertz and Martin Ødegaard, the Gunners took the lead when, in the 64th minute, when Timber collected Madueke's pass before lofting the ball over Özer.
Saka wasted little time in making his mark on proceedings as he pulled the ball back for Eze to brilliantly stroke home a bouncing effort that nestled into the bottom-right corner.
And the result was sealed four minutes later by Saka, who curled into the back of the net to round off a flowing Arsenal move that saw Havertz and Ødegaard heavily involved.
Guimarães almost capitalised on a mistake by Benjamin André, but his shot was saved, but Arsenal's blistering seven-minute spell was enough to seal all three points.

Despite leaving the likes of Saka, Havertz and Ødegaard on the bench, Arteta was still able to field a front line that consisted of Merino, Gyökeres and Madueke, but the Arsenal boss was forced to turn to his first-team regulars to click his side into gear.

Arsenal have now failed to score a first-half goal in any of their last five games in the Premier League or Champions League. Their last goal before the break was against Chelsea on 6 September, and Arteta sought to change things with a triple substitution just after the hour.

Timber got the Gunners ahead before Saka came to the party, but the England international was key to Arsenal taking the game away from their opponents. After his goal, Saka has now scored 19 goals in major European competition for Arsenal, the outright second most of any player at the club after Thierry Henry (42).

In addition, only Henry (16) and Cesc Fàbregas (14) have more Champions League assists for Arsenal than Saka (nine, level with Alexis Sánchez and Theo Walcott), while he is the fifth Arsenal player to both score and assist a goal as a substitute in a Champions League match.

14f9ez1hoyyz21cti11qjbid9m.title: United States 3-0 Mexico: Sullivan overhauls Albert record in big win for Pochettino's men
14f9ez1hoyyz21cti11qjbid9m.subtitle: Mathis Albert was not the United States' youngest-ever goalscorer for long, as Cavan Sullivan overhauled him in a 3-0 win over Mexico.
paragraphs: Cavan Sullivan surpassed Mathis Albert as the United States' youngest-ever goalscorer – only four days after that record was set – in an eye-catching 3-0 win over 10-man Mexico.
Albert scored in Tuesday's 4-2 win over Chile at the age of 17 years and 131 days, but Philadelphia Union sensation Sullivan netted at 17 years and five days old on Saturday.
He was not the only young player to impress for Mauricio Pochettino's hosts in Glendale, either, with 18-year-old forward Julian Hall netting their 28th-minute opener.

After Santiago Gimenez passed up a huge early chance for Mexico, Hall was on hand to finish following some suspect goalkeeping from Raul Rangel, who found Malik Tillman's right-wing cross too hot to handle, following a lovely, disguised pass from Sebastian Berhalter.

Gimenez somehow steered wide with the goal gaping at the end of the first half, while his team-mate Roberto Alvarado was only denied by a reflex Diego Kochen stop early in the second, having thumped a volley goalwards on the swivel.

But the USA doubled their lead just beyond the hour mark, with a more glaring mistake from Rangel gifting Sullivan his first international goal. Under little pressure, he passed straight to the teenage midfielder, who immediately lobbed the goalkeeper from 35 yards out.
Things went from bad to worse for the visitors when Mateo Chavez was sent off for slapping Berhalter across the face, amid a melee prompted by his own late challenge on Yunus Musah.
And there was more self-inflicted pain for Mexico in the 84th minute as Tillman intercepted Alvaro Fidalgo's pass and lashed into the top-left corner.
Young Stars and Stripes shine again
Coming off the back of a traumatic World Cup elimination at the hands of Belgium in Seattle, this international break has proven very therapeutic for the USA.
Several new players have made the most of the opportunities handed to them by Pochettino, with Sullivan the latest – and the youngest – to do so.

The USA's youngest goalscorer record stood for just over 10 years between Christian Pulisic netting against Bolivia at 17 years and 253 days old in May 2016, and Albert overhauling him earlier this week.

But Albert's name was only in the record books for four days, with Sullivan capping a lively performance with a moment to remember. No USA player completed more dribbles than his three (from four attempted), while he won eight of his 11 duels in total.
The USA had lost each of their previous two games against Mexico, including the 2025 Gold Cup final, but they have now won six of the teams' last 10 meetings overall (D2 L2).

14j64o8rsdufo13bthdmqvi447.title: Mourinho not thinking about El Clasico as Madrid take things one game at a time
14j64o8rsdufo13bthdmqvi447.subtitle: Real Madrid will take on Barcelona in a huge clash at the end of this week, but for the next few days, Jose Mourinho's focus is elsewhere.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho "won't spend a minute" thinking about this weekend's Clasico showdown with Barcelona until Real Madrid have navigated their midweek Champions League assignment.
Madrid thrashed Sevilla 4-1 in LaLiga on Sunday, with Kylian Mbappe helping himself to a brace and being joined on the scoresheet by Arda Guler and Yan Diomande.
Los Blancos are now six points behind league leaders Barca, who they will face at Camp Nou on Sunday.
In his first stint with Madrid between 2010 and 2013, Mourinho won five of the 17 matches he oversaw against Barca (D6 L6), with three of those victories coming in nine away games (D3 L3).
But with a Champions League clash with RB Leipzig to come on Wednesday, Mourinho is not looking too far ahead.

"There is the Champions League to play first, and that's the only game we are thinking about. I won't spend even a minute thinking about our opponent for next Sunday until Wednesday at 11pm," he said when asked about El Clasico.
"There's no way to quantify which 11 players deserve to play the most. Many people deserve to play, and today some came on, and others didn't leave the bench at all.

"For example, the player who scored the winning goal against Roma [Antonio Rudiger] didn't even play. We had more possession, more control of the game, created a lot, and got the ball to our wide players a lot. It was a very good game."
After Madrid's 4-1 win, Sevilla boss Luis Garcia was furious that Guler was not sent off for an apparent elbow on Peque Fernandez, but Mourinho was bemused by that reaction.
"I don't comment on that. No one has managed to show me what they say happened. I haven't seen a single image," he said.
"I've asked my analysts and the TV people for images, and I haven't been able to see any image of the things they are talking about that upset Luis.
"If one day something happens that I believe benefited us, I'll have no problem coming out and saying it, but I think the opposite is more likely to happen because it's the natural trend of things."

Asked if he had any brief concern about Guler getting suspended for the Barcelona game, which Vinicius Junior is already banned for, Mourinho reiterated: "I haven't thought for a minute about El Clasico, only about winning this game.
"For a coach who loses by four goals and is given the opportunity to answer four or five questions about that... it's fantastic because it allows him to talk about other things.
"When the situation happened, I looked at the tablet and I didn't see anything. Have any of you seen it? That's why I don't understand the obsession with so many questions about this story."

14l41t79dlzs51qd7b9ocax7m9.title: Manchester City 3-2 Ipswich Town: Maresca makes history with seventh straight win
14l41t79dlzs51qd7b9ocax7m9.subtitle: Manchester City made it seven wins from seven to start the Premier League, with Erling Haaland's brace helping them past Ipswich Town.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland scored in a sixth consecutive Premier League game to keep Manchester City's 100% start intact with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town.

Daizen Maeda immediately cancelled out Phil Foden's opener, but Haaland scored in either half to make Enzo Maresca the first manager in the league's history to win his first seven games in charge of a club.
City started brightly, with Ruben Dias sending a header wide before his arrowed effort needed to be punched off the line by Christian Walton.
But the hosts found the breakthrough in the 19th minute as Mateo Kovacic set Jeremy Doku away down the left, and Foden got in front of his defender to poke the Belgian's cross in.

Ipswich hit back quickly after the restart, though, with Abdoul Ouattara's throughball causing havoc for Marc Guehi, who was left on the floor by Maeda, who coolly beat Gianluigi Donnarumma at the near post while one-on-one.
Emersonn then sliced wide, but City heeded that warning in the 34th minute. Kovacic was again heavily involved, and his lovely dinked cross was met by Haaland, who beat Walton with a powerful header.
City remained in control after the break, with Haaland getting his second 69 minutes in. He latched onto Iliman Ndiaye's stunning pass and outmuscled Ouattara to fire in.

Haaland did have the ball in the back of the net a third time in the 85th minute. Enzo Fernandez – on for the injured Kovacic – forced a smart stop out of Walton before Ndiaye hit the crossbar, but the Argentinian was offside when he recycled it to Haaland, and the goal was disallowed.

Ipswich set up a slightly nervy ending, with Guehi penalised for kicking Abdul Fatawu during an attempted clearance in the box. The penalty was awarded following a VAR review, with substitute Zian Flemming emphatically finishing from 12 yards.
Despite late pressure from both sides, neither could find another goal, and City moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League.
Maresca writes his name into the history books
City are just the third team to begin their season with seven straight wins after Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight), but Maresca has his own slice of history.
Never before has a manager won each of his first seven Premier League outings with a club, and it was a much-needed victory after the disappointing Champions League loss to Paris Saint-Germain.

As can be expected, Haaland was at the centre of the victory; he has now netted 100 non-penalty goals in the competition, reaching this milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139). The previous fewest was 150 appearances by Alan Shearer.
He has also scored at least two goals in 29 different Premier League matches – already the ninth most in the competition's history.

Despite only getting six of their 19 shots on target, City were utterly dominant, accumulating 3.53 expected goals (xG) to Ipswich's 1.66, but the visitors still caused City some issues, and Gary O'Neil will have positives to take from the result.
They once again finished strongly with another 90th-minute goal; 10 of Flemming's 13 Premier League goals have come away from home (77%).
14l41t79dlzs51qd7b9ocax7m9.html:
Erling Haaland scored in a sixth consecutive Premier League game to keep Manchester City's 100% start intact with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town.

Daizen Maeda immediately cancelled out Phil Foden's opener, but Haaland scored in either half to make Enzo Maresca the first manager in the league's history to win his first seven games in charge of a club.

City started brightly, with Ruben Dias sending a header wide before his arrowed effort needed to be punched off the line by Christian Walton.

But the hosts found the breakthrough in the 19th minute as Mateo Kovacic set Jeremy Doku away down the left, and Foden got in front of his defender to poke the Belgian's cross in.

Ipswich hit back quickly after the restart, though, with Abdoul Ouattara's throughball causing havoc for Marc Guehi, who was left on the floor by Maeda, who coolly beat Gianluigi Donnarumma at the near post while one-on-one.

Emersonn then sliced wide, but City heeded that warning in the 34th minute. Kovacic was again heavily involved, and his lovely dinked cross was met by Haaland, who beat Walton with a powerful header. 

City remained in control after the break, with Haaland getting his second 69 minutes in. He latched onto Iliman Ndiaye's stunning pass and outmuscled Ouattara to fire in.

Haaland did have the ball in the back of the net a third time in the 85th minute. Enzo Fernandez – on for the injured Kovacic – forced a smart stop out of Walton before Ndiaye hit the crossbar, but the Argentinian was offside when he recycled it to Haaland, and the goal was disallowed.

Ipswich set up a slightly nervy ending, with Guehi penalised for kicking Abdul Fatawu during an attempted clearance in the box. The penalty was awarded following a VAR review, with substitute Zian Flemming emphatically finishing from 12 yards.

Despite late pressure from both sides, neither could find another goal, and City moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League.

Maresca writes his name into the history books

City are just the third team to begin their season with seven straight wins after Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight), but Maresca has his own slice of history.

Never before has a manager won each of his first seven Premier League outings with a club, and it was a much-needed victory after the disappointing Champions League loss to Paris Saint-Germain.

As can be expected, Haaland was at the centre of the victory; he has now netted 100 non-penalty goals in the competition, reaching this milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139). The previous fewest was 150 appearances by Alan Shearer.

He has also scored at least two goals in 29 different Premier League matches – already the ninth most in the competition's history.

Despite only getting six of their 19 shots on target, City were utterly dominant, accumulating 3.53 expected goals (xG) to Ipswich's 1.66, but the visitors still caused City some issues, and Gary O'Neil will have positives to take from the result.

They once again finished strongly with another 90th-minute goal; 10 of Flemming's 13 Premier League goals have come away from home (77%).

14mdmqibp5hj51w1wr7jwmkgt2.title: Arteta warns Arsenal squad must earn opportunities after Lille win
14mdmqibp5hj51w1wr7jwmkgt2.subtitle: Arsenal comfortably eased past Lille on Tuesday in the Champions League, despite Mikel Arteta making five changes to his starting XI.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal's squad must earn their opportunities to play after they swept aside Lille 3-0 in the Champions League.
Arsenal were frustrated for large parts of the first half on Tuesday at the Emirates Stadium, but produced a dominant second period to ease to victory.
Jurrien Timber scored the first of Arsenal's three goals in seven second-half minutes, with substitute Bukayo Saka then setting up Eberechi Eze before scoring a goal of his own soon after.
Arteta made five changes for this European encounter after the 2-1 win over Leeds United in the Premier League, reminding his players to take their opportunities when they come.
"The minutes are given because they deserve them. Everyone has to earn it because we can see competition and options and that will only benefit our performances," he told TNT Sports.
This was the third time Arsenal won a Champions League match by 3+ goals, having been goalless at half-time, with all three coming under Arteta.
Clear chances were hard to come by for Arsenal in the first half, while Lille's Ayase Ueda also had a goal ruled out for offside in a brief scare for David Raya.
"We had to increase the technical level, teams are really well-organised at this level," Arteta said of the first-half performance.
"We gave simple things away; bad touches, mistimed things, when we sent balls into the box, it was into the wrong areas, and we got caught.
"Once we did that better, we started to play in the opposition box, and with the quality we have, they made a difference."
Arsenal have now won their last 14 Champions League group stage/league phase games, keeping nine clean sheets in this run.
Their next clash in the competition sees them travel to Bayern Munich, who will be without Michael Olise after his sending-off in their unexpected 3-3 draw with Viking.
First, Arteta will turn his attention to Sunday's trip to Nottingham Forest as Arsenal look to make ground on early Premier League leaders Manchester City.
"It's difficult in the Champions League, Lille are a brilliant team," Arteta concluded. "But winning helps; the energy will be good when we start to prepare for the Sunday game."

14qi2wh9aop4w1iaia6yqd00d6.title: Portugal 1-0 Wales: Joao Felix goal enough to give Jesus winning start
14qi2wh9aop4w1iaia6yqd00d6.subtitle: Portugal's first match under Jorge Jesus saw them beat Wales in the Nations League, but they were made to work for Thursday's victory.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus got his Portugal tenure up and running with a win as the defending Nations League champions began their 2026-27 campaign with a 1-0 victory against Wales.
Joao Felix struck the decisive blow in the first half at Estadio Jose Alvalade, though Wales had more than enough chances to at least claim a point away from home.
Portugal started brightly as Cristiano Ronaldo's first sight of goal saw him drag a shot wide, before Vitinha and Joao Felix had their efforts blocked by Wales' retreating defence.

The hosts had to wait until the 22nd minute for their first shot on target, and it resulted in a goal. Nuno Mendes skipped beyond Ethan Ampadu before laying the ball off to Joao Felix, who took a touch before seeing his attempt nestle into the bottom-left corner from the edge of the penalty area.
Ronaldo, in his quest to reach 1,000 career goals, then volleyed just wide before his tame effort after being found by Joao Felix was comfortably held by Danny Ward.

Portugal should have doubled their lead four minutes into the second half, but Ronaldo somehow turned Ruben Neves' cross over the bar, and he thought he had got his goal when he raced onto Bruno Fernandes' defence-splitting pass, only for it to be ruled out following a VAR check for offside.

But Wales spurned a glorious chance to draw level when Brennan Johnson ghosted in behind the Portugal backline and lofted an effort onto the crossbar, with Lewis Koumas' attempt on the rebound blocked off the line by Ruben Dias.

Daniel James and Mendes then fired wide at either end before substitute Goncalo Ramos stung the palms of Ward, with Portugal able to weather the Wales storm in the minutes that remained, getting themselves up and running in the Nations League.
Portugal fail to build on Joao Felix strike

With Wales missing several key players including Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon, many expected a comfortable outing for Portugal, and it looked as though it would be following Joao Felix's goal, which was his fifth in his last 10 starts for the Selecao.

He was teed up by the marauding Mendes, who registered his seventh assist for Portugal since the start of 2024. Overall, he's third for goal involvements in that time for his nation, behind Ronaldo (20) and Fernandes (17).

Portugal's 13 shots in the first half were also their most in the opening 45 minutes of a game since November 2025 against Armenia (17), but after the break, Wales looked the more likely to alter the scoreline.

Wales do, however, remain winless in their last five matches (D3 L2), their worst run under manager Craig Bellamy, but there will plenty of positives he can take from their performance ahead of facing Denmark in three days' time.

Jesus' side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.36 from their 23 shots, only five of which were on target, compared to Wales' tally of 0.84 from their five attempts, with Portugal's next test seeing them take on Erling Haaland and Norway.

152j5eqdlkk2f16ewh7gutl3pl.title: Putellas' Ballon d'Or chances will improve after WSL move, says London City boss
152j5eqdlkk2f16ewh7gutl3pl.subtitle: Alexia Putellas' move to London City Lionesses was the marquee transfer of the summer, following a trophy-laden career with Barcelona.
paragraphs: London City Lionesses boss Eder Maestre believes Alexia Putellas' move to the Women's Super League will only help her chances of winning more Ballon d'Or awards.
After spending her entire career with Barcelona, Putellas joined London City as a free agent in the summer.

Putellas has four goal involvements in WSL games this term (three goals, one assist); across the last five seasons, she has only registered more goal contributions in her opening five league appearances once: six for Barca in 2024-25 (four goals, two assists).
She won the Ballon d'Or twice during her time with Barca, claiming the award in both 2021 and 2022.
And Maestre is confident Putellas can do so again in the future.
"I think it represents how powerful the competition is," Maestre said.
"It’s not just Alexia being in the WSL. It’s Alexia, through her performances in the WSL, having more opportunities to win the Ballon d’Or.
"It makes the competition better, but also it makes Alexia better due to the challenges she will face in this tough competition.
"Alexia is a very talented and experienced player. We understand her abilities.

"I think this competition is the most difficult and tough from a physical perspective, so I think we need to create something to empower the strengths of Alexia and create an environment where she can show her best."
After the international break, London City are back in WSL action when they host Everton on Sunday.
London City have won each of their last three WSL matches, their longest winning run in the competition.
They could win four consecutive league games for the first time since doing so between March and April 2025 in the WSL2.

157g5rock11h0105mejgyfjhs1.title: Patience pays off for Fofana after scoring Sunderland's winner against Brentford
157g5rock11h0105mejgyfjhs1.subtitle: Sunderland's first-half performance was enough to defeat Brentford and secure their place in the EFL Cup quarter-finals.
paragraphs: Malick Fofana was delighted his hard work and patience finally paid off after celebrating his first Sunderland goal.
Sunderland progressed into the quarter-finals with a 3-2 victory at the Stadium of Light, with all three of their goals coming in a 13-minute first-half spell.

Chemsdine Talbi opened the scoring after Jocelin Ta Bi saw an effort cleared off the line, though the latter went on to assist both Tymur Tutierov and Fofana, whose maiden Sunderland goal turned out to be the winner.
Callum Wilson pulled a goal back for the Bees before half-time, while Igor Thiago scored in second-half stoppage time, but it was too late for Brentford.
Sunderland lost the expected goals (xG) battle 2.37 to 2.75, with Brentford creating four Opta-defined big chances from their 16 shots.
Nevertheless, the Black Cats made the most of their opportunities.
"I'm very happy. Finally, you can say," said Fofana, who joined Sunderland from Lyon at the end of the summer transfer window.
"It was very hard, so I've been patient and I'm very happy with my goal.
"It's always a good feeling to score at home with the fans. They support us every day, every time, so I'm very happy to give them something back.
"Since day one, I've felt a warm welcome, so I already feel at home. I'm very happy here and just enjoying the moment. I work hard every day, so I hope I can continue like this.
"The win was also very important for the team, so I hope we can continue on Saturday."
Bi had a big influence. He created more chances than any other player (three), while completing two of his three dribbles, winning eight of his 15 duels and regaining possession five times.
"Jocelin comes from another country, another culture, we can't teach him how to dribble because he's gifted," said Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris.
"He worked hard to gain those qualities, but we can help him to learn to defend. He was brave, running much more than expected, but he was still able to deliver those two assists.

"He's a young player, and we want to give opportunities to young players. It's always easier with experienced players. In our mind, we can combine both. They can't learn until they are exposed to the problems."
Sunderland's reward for their win is a trip to Crystal Palace in the quarter-finals.

159b8hezyf6ze11g85cyffy3vo.title: 'I'm making the most of every moment' – Giroud admits retirement is close
159b8hezyf6ze11g85cyffy3vo.subtitle: Ahead of his 40th birthday, Olivier Giroud conceded his retirement is closer than ever, with the 2026-27 campaign likely to be his last.
paragraphs: Olivier Giroud has said this season will "very probably" be his last.
Giroud, now playing for Lille, will turn 40 on Wednesday and is seemingly set to call time on his career that began in 2005.
He has played for the likes of Arsenal, Chelsea, AC Milan and Los Angeles FC.
Giroud was also France's record goalscorer with 57 goals, earning the record at the 2022 World Cup, though it was beaten by Kylian Mbappe earlier this year.
"As a player, I think it is very probably my last season," he told L'Equipe. "That's why I'm making the most of every moment.
"I am at peace with myself and everything I have accomplished in my career. I feel more relaxed than ever.
"The goal is to enjoy every moment, to continue to find pleasure in what I do, what I love every day.
"Returning to France, making this choice after this long career as an expatriate abroad, has been one of the best decisions I've ever made."
Giroud won the 2018 World Cup with France and was also part of the squad that finished as runners-up at the 2022 edition, as well as the 2016 European Championships.
He made 137 appearances in total for Les Bleus with his last cap coming back in 2024.
At club level, the Frenchman has made 806 appearances across his career, scoring 303 goals, with 105 of those coming at Arsenal (253 games) – the most he has scored at any single club.
He also won league titles with Montpellier and AC Milan, as well as the Champions League and Europa League with Chelsea.

15layo80q7mke170ye3jt997li.title: Lampard thrilled with Coventry's 'complete performance' against Newcastle
15layo80q7mke170ye3jt997li.subtitle: Coventry City recorded a statement victory in the Premier League on Monday, thrashing Newcastle United 4-1 at home.
paragraphs: Frank Lampard labelled Coventry City's stunning victory over Newcastle United as a "complete performance".
The Sky Blues climbed out of the relegation zone after a 4-1 win at the Coventry Building Society Arena, securing their first home win in the Premier League since promotion.
Jack Rudoni opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the sixth minute, while Sidiki Cherif, Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni also got on the scoresheet in what was a clinical performance.

Coventry have enjoyed back-to-back Premier League wins for the first time since March and April 2001, while they netted 4+ goals in a top-flight game for the first time since May 2000 (versus Sheffield Wednesday, also 4-1).
While Lampard insisted his side must stay humble, he was still delighted with an impressive performance in front of their home fans.
"Very, very satisfying. It's so hard to win. We played like the team that we want to be here," Lampard told Sky Sports.

"There is so much spirit and energy in the group and we know we are going to have to suffer a lot this season. The work ethic of the boys and the belief... you get what you deserve, which was great finishes.
"We haven't quite had that rub of the green this season that would help us nick more points. It was a complete performance.
"We have to keep our feet on the ground. It's a great feeling for the players to feel that."

Courtesy of Cherif (19 years, 301 days) and Mfuni (18 years, 242 days), Coventry saw two teenagers score in the same Premier League game for the first time, with Mfuni the youngest-ever scorer for the club in a competition.
Cherif became the first Coventry player to both score a goal and win a penalty in a Premier League game since Lee Carsley against Everton in January 2001.
"It's very exciting because he's so young," Lampard said about Cherif, who made his first start in the competition.
"He's got a really good manner, a really good way about him, he wants to train, he wants to learn.
"He's quite quiet, but he showed a lot of personality and didn't stop running. There is a lot to come."

15o4gti9ewrtv1p6zumibudnnx.title: Arena: San Jose not a team positioned to be MLS Cup favourites
15o4gti9ewrtv1p6zumibudnnx.subtitle: Despite booking their spot in the playoffs, Bruce Arena believes there is plenty of room for improvement for the San Jose Earthquakes.
paragraphs: Bruce Arena believes improvements have been made across the board at the San Jose Earthquakes, though he does not think they are capable of challenging for trophies yet.
San Jose have already sealed their spot in the postseason, and they could finish as high as second in the Western Conference should results around them go their way.
The Earthquakes were held to a 2-2 draw with the Colorado Rapids in midweek, with Jack Jasinski scoring a late equaliser despite Arena's side seeing Timo Werner sent off.
Arena took charge of the Earthquakes in November 2024 and, after failing to qualify for the postseason in 2025, has got his team back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023.
San Jose's penultimate game of the regular season sees them welcome Real Salt Lake to PayPal Park, and Arena believes the club is heading in the right direction.
"We made progress from 2024 to 2025, and we've made progress this year. We're not a team positioned to be MLS Cup favourites now, but we're getting better," Arena said.
"There are a lot of things we need to improve on, both on and off the field, but we're making progress. The guys did a great job. I'm really proud of them.
"I don't think it's about me. The entire organisation has improved, from the players and coaching staff to sports medicine, sports performance, and everyone behind the scenes.
"We were behind in a lot of areas, so ownership stepped up and supported us by investing in our facilities. That said, we still have a long way to go."
RSL, meanwhile, are yet to confirm their place in the playoffs, but have done their chances no harm after putting together a three-game winning run at a crucial part of the season.

15theaobt91mw1snlkcemydewv.title: Sydney FC 0-0 Western Sydney Wanderers: Drab derby draw kicks-off A-League season
15theaobt91mw1snlkcemydewv.subtitle: The 2026-27 A-League season did not get off with a bang, as Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers drew 0-0 at Allianz Stadium.
paragraphs: Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers opened the 2026-27 A-League season with a 0-0 derby draw.
A derby between last season's grand final runners-up and their city rivals was an enthralling prospect to start the new campaign.
Yet both Sydney and the Wanderers, who finished bottom of the ladder last season, failed to deliver in a game devoid of attacking quality.
Western Sydney suffered a blow early on when Awan Lual limped off injured, but the only other notable moment in the first half came when Miguel Di Pizio's booking resulted in a bit of a flashpoint.
Di Pizio could have put the Wanderers ahead in the 53rd minute, only to skew over from the game's first clear opening.
Atiya Waraga sliced wide for the visitors late on, but Sydney did not manage a shot on target until the 91st minute, as the season got going in underwhelming fashion.
No derby delight
There were 18 shots between the teams on Friday, with Sydney having nine and the Wanderers 13, though they only combined for three attempts on target.
The lack of guile in the final third was summed up by the expected goals figures: Sydney finished with 0.57 and the Wanderers with 0.94.
Western Sydney have now failed to win their last eight A-League matches, marking their longest such run in the competition since 2019 (10 games).
Sydney, meanwhile, have now kept 13 clean sheets since the start of last season, which is the most of any team in the competition.
However, the Sky Blues have drawn their last three league fixtures at Allianz Stadium, and are now winless in seven games at the venue (D5 L2).
Sydney did, though, maintain their strong record against their local rivals at Allianz Stadium, where they have not lost to Western Sydney in five league games.

15ty00tdqd02k15mauaxn9tdde.title: Mourinho: No Real Madrid player is untouchable
15ty00tdqd02k15mauaxn9tdde.subtitle: Vinicius Junior's performances have been underwhelming this season, and Real Madrid youngster Yan Diomande is pushing to start.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho insisted no Real Madrid player is "untouchable" amid calls for Yan Diomande to start over Vinicius Junior.
Vinicius has struggled to make his mark this season, scoring just once and providing three assists in 10 appearances for Los Blancos.
The 26-year-old also received a four-match ban in LaLiga for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba, meaning the Brazilian will miss the first Clasico of the season on October 25.
Diomande, meanwhile, has impressed since returning after the international break, directly contributing to four goals in three games (two goals, two assists).
Mourinho claimed no player is a guaranteed starter in his side and revealed Vinicius will start in their Champions League match against RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
"The only thing untouchable is the badge. I don't like this concept of an untouchable player," said Mourinho.
"What makes a player untouchable is their performance on the field.
"Vinicius is going to play on the left wing [against Leipzig]. Yan doesn't know if he's going to play or not."
Madrid and Leipzig will meet for a fifth time in the Champions League, with the German side only winning one of the previous four (D1 L2): 3-2 in a home match in October 2022.
Los Blancos lost both of their games against German opponents in last season's Champions League, both against Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals.
They last lost three consecutive European games against German opposition between May 2001 and April 2002 (three).
Ahead of the match, Mourinho explained Madrid's immediate goals in the Champions League.
"It's very early. Our goal now is to qualify, and then the next objective will be to avoid the play-offs," added the Portuguese.

"I have a feeling that we're going to need a lot of points to do that. First, we need to reach the 11 or 12 points that qualify us, and then we need to get the points that allow us to finish in the top eight."

15wlyz4pmpwu21m8ok6rnansou.title: 'Everybody knows what needs to be done' – Sands focused on NYCFC's playoff push
15wlyz4pmpwu21m8ok6rnansou.subtitle: New York City FC are hoping to end their winless streak and continue their playoff push against Orlando City SC, who are in fine form.
paragraphs: New York City FC midfielder James Sands says the club are well aware of what is at stake in the playoff race as they travel to Orlando City SC in need of an MLS win.
NYCFC have failed to win any of their last five league games, meaning they have slipped down to 12th in the Eastern Conference.

They snapped a two-game losing streak to draw 1-1 with Los Angeles FC last time out, but they remain two points behind their rivals New York Red Bulls, who occupy the last wildcard spot, with four games left to play.
It is the worst time of the season to hit a downslide in form, and Sands believes his team-mates are well-equipped to deal with the pressure of the playoff race.
"Everybody at this point is a professional," he said. "Everybody's dealt with their highs and their lows.
"I don't think guys on this team need their hands held in these tough moments. Everybody's a grown-up; everybody knows what needs to be done. When things are not going our way, nobody sugarcoats it.
"So, I think it's just about being professional, trying to manage the games a little bit better than we have.
"I don't think we're so far off from getting the results we need, but obviously, we do need to take a couple of steps forward now."
Orlando, by contrast, are seven points better off, sitting in the final automatic playoff spot in seventh.
They are unbeaten in their last three MLS matches (W2 D1) and come into this match with a confidence-boosting 4-1 win over D.C. United last time out.
"I think they are giving everything on the field, and [D.C.] was a tough game," interim head coach Martin Perelman said.
"We had to battle, to fight and to play when we could. Fortunately, we won, which is very important at home.
"But now, it's time to prepare for the next one, which will be very important, like every game."
Orlando City SC – Martin Ojeda
Martin Ojeda tallied his 15th goal of the season in the win over D.C., netting a sublime scorpion kick, marking his second consecutive season with at least 15 goals for Orlando.
Only one other player in Orlando's history has even one MLS season with 15+ goals (Cyle Larin – 17 in 2015).
New York City FC – Nicolas Fernandez Mercau
Nicolas Fernandez Mercau delivered an assist on Saturday for his ninth of 2026, with only team-mate Agustin Ojeda having more this season (11).
With another Fernandez Mercau assist, the pair would join Santiago Rodriguez and Talles Magno in 2022 as the only pair in team history with 10+ assists in the same regular season.
MATCH PREDICTION: ORLANDO CITY SC
NYCFC's 5-0 win over Orlando in March was their second five-goal win in the regular-season series (also doing so in July 2021).
NYCFC has recorded five-goal wins in MLS play against D.C. United, FC Cincinnati and Real Salt Lake, but Orlando is the only opponent they have beaten twice by that margin.

However, they have registered 10 draws in MLS this season after their 1-1 draw with LAFC last weekend. It is their 23rd stalemate since the start of 2023, two more than San Jose Earthquakes' 21 in that same time.
Orlando are expected to make their home advantage count on Saturday. Their 4-1 win over D.C. marked their 10th league game this season with at least three goals scored.
Orlando's 32 regular-season games with at least three goals since the start of the 2024 season are tied with the Vancouver Whitecaps for second most, trailing only Inter Miami’s 41 matches.
Orlando City SC – 46.6%
New York City FC – 26.9%

15y38a957qpth1g9zuwm4dvk3j.title: Kane backed for Ballon d'Or over Olise by Bayern president
15y38a957qpth1g9zuwm4dvk3j.subtitle: Harry Kane is among the frontrunners for the Ballon d'Or this term, after an incredibly free-scoring 2025-26 campaign with Bayern Munich.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer has backed Harry Kane to win the Ballon d'Or over team-mate Michael Olise.
The Ballon d'Or will be awarded later this month, with Kane among the frontrunners to lift it, along with Kylian Mbappe and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.
Kane plundered 64 goals across all competitions (including the Club World Cup) for Bayern last term, before then scoring six more to help Thomas Tuchel's side finish third at the World Cup.
No other player from Europe's top five leagues scored more than 50 goals in all competitions last term, with Mbappe his closest challenger with a half-century for Real Madrid.

Olise is an outside contender for the Ballon d'Or after a stellar campaign with Bayern in 2025-26; he had 34 goal involvements (15 goals, 19 assists), a new record for a winger since Opta data collection began in the German top-flight in 2004-05.
Only Kane (41) directly contributed to more Bundesliga goals than the Frenchman, who also scored five goals and provided seven assists in 13 Champions League games.
He also carried his form into the World Cup, becoming the first player on record (since 1966) to register seven assists in a single edition.
But Hainer believes Kane is the deserving recipient this time around.
"Both Michael and Harry deserve it [the Ballon d'Or]," Hainer told BILD.
"But I would give it to Harry Kane.
"Michael Olise has many more years ahead of him to win the Ballon d'Or."
Kane has also reportedly agreed to a new deal with Bayern, which would take him through to the end of the 2028-29 campaign.
He has scored 154 goals in 156 matches with Bayern since joining from Tottenham in August 2023, winning two Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal in that time.

He has also written his name into the Bundesliga history books this term, having reached the 100-goal landmark in his 98th appearance, making him the quickest player to hit that tally, smashing Dieter Muller's previous record of 129 games.
