162d59wsc9rzk15jhloqqpj6u6.title: Vinicius apologises for red card as Mourinho skips Real Madrid press conference
162d59wsc9rzk15jhloqqpj6u6.subtitle: Real Madrid earned a 1-0 win over Villarreal despite finishing with 10 men, after Vinicius Junior was sent off for a hair pull.
paragraphs: Vinicius Junior apologised to Real Madrid after being sent off for a hair pull in their 1-0 win over Villarreal.
Madrid got back to winning ways in LaLiga, edging past Villarreal thanks to Yan Diomande's first goal for the club in the second half.

However, the win was marred by Vinicius' sending-off. The Brazilian thought he had added a second goal for Jose Mourinho's side, but it was ruled out, and he was instead shown a red card for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in the build-up.
Vinicius had started the match on the bench – having been replaced in the starting XI by Diomande – with his cameo lasting just 20 minutes after he was introduced shortly after half-time.
The red card was classed as violent conduct, meaning he could miss El Clasico on October 25.
"The joy continues. My apologies to my team and the fans," Vinicius posted on social media.

Vinicius' Madrid team-mate Aurelien Tchouameni was in disbelief at the referee's decision following the game, telling Real Madrid TV: "I don't understand what's happening with the referees, with the red card. I don't understand it."
Following the incident, Mourinho also opted to skip his post-match press conference.
Despite finishing the match with 10 men, Madrid saw out a win that moved them up to third in LaLiga, with Diomande opening his account for Los Blancos.

Along with his match-winner, Diomande also had the joint-most touches in the box of any Madrid player (seven), created the joint-most chances (three), won the joint-most duels (six) and attempted the second-most dribbles (five).
"It was a good match; we always play to win, and we did that. I'm very happy with the victory," he said.
"It's always great to play at the Bernabeu—the most beautiful stadium in the world and the biggest club.
"Of course, I'm happy; I'd been waiting for that first goal for a long time. In that position, I think the only option was to control, turn, and shoot. That's what I did.
"I'm really excited to play in the Champions League; it's every kid's dream, and I'm very grateful to be doing it with Madrid."

Kane is one of three players being tipped to contend for football's most prestigious individual award next month, alongside Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal.

But speaking in the build-up to England's 2026-27 Nations League opener against Spain on Saturday, Tuchel said Kane's game is about much more than his goals, highlighting his out-of-possession work.
Asked if Kane was his pick to be crowned the world's best player, Tuchel told ITV Sport: "Yeah. After this season, yeah.
"Seventy-plus goals [for club and country], three titles with Bayern Munich, the semi-finals at the World Cup and in the Champions League...
"He's getting better and better. I think he added a level of physicality to his match. He's just so committed to the high press and being involved in every part of the match.
"Be it in deep build-up, be it in finishing, be it in build-up play in the middle block, be it in defending. He's just the full package."

Last season, Kane recovered possession 124 times for Bayern, with 34 of those regains being in the final third. Those figures put him below Yamal (176 recoveries, 42 in final third) but ahead of Mbappe (65 recoveries, 30 in final third).
Kane also won 222 duels, less than Yamal's 381 but more than Mbappe's 162, and won 20 of his 28 tackles.
Yamal won 32 of 58 for Barcelona, while Mbappe – somewhat remarkably – only won two of six attempted tackles for Madrid, in 44 games.

He will turn 37 shortly after the conclusion of the 2030 edition, which will be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, but Tuchel feels he has every chance of featuring.
"Yeah, there's no problem," Tuchel said when asked about Kane's longevity. "Age is age. It doesn't matter. It's only about quality, and he has a long way to go."

After hosting Spain on Saturday, England continue their Nations League campaign away to Czechia next Tuesday, before visiting Croatia and welcoming Czechia back to Wembley Stadium for a swift return fixture.
England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine of those matches (D2).
However, one of those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0), with the other being away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

163cofk4nwnn1inyyvjk7hvei.title: Ipswich Town 2-1 Fulham: Ouattara and O'Shea complete stunning comeback
163cofk4nwnn1inyyvjk7hvei.subtitle: Ipswich Town completed a stunning comeback to defeat Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road in the Premier League.
paragraphs: Ipswich Town completed a stunning comeback as late goals from Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea sealed a memorable 2-1 win over Fulham at Portman Road.

The result means Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa is still winless in his first six Premier League games in charge, with the pressure mounting on the Spaniard, while Ipswich have secured their third league win of the campaign.
After a tepid start to the contest, Julio Enciso had the first opening of the game, whistling an attempt past the right-hand post.
David Affengruber headed wide from Alex Iwobi’s left-wing centre, before Christian Walton repelled Sander Berge’s rasping drive at the near post.
Gonzalo Garcia thought he had put his side ahead early in the second half, but Issa Diop did enough to make a crucial goal-line block, after some good work from Oscar Bobb down the byline.

Arbeloa’s men eventually found the back of the net in the 55th minute as Diop’s headed clearance kindly fell to Ryan Sessegnon 25 yards from goal, with the left-back fizzing a low strike into the bottom-right corner.
The hosts almost responded with an equaliser, but Emersonn crashed a header against the upright following Enciso’s exquisite cross, with Bobb then lashing a shot over at the other end.

However, in a remarkable ending, the Tractor Boys levelled in the 88th minute with Ouattara picking out the bottom-left corner from outside the box, before O’Shea glanced a header in at the near post following Jack Clarke’s free-kick.
Kevin looked to add a further twist to this enthralling contest, but the Brazilian was brilliantly denied by the outstretched leg of Walton at the near post.
Tractor Boys show fight as Arbeloa's winless run continues
After seeing his side concede a late equaliser to Manchester United prior to the international break, Arbeloa would have hoped his team had learned their lesson.
However, after taking a deserved lead 10 minutes after the interval, the visitors, who opted to sit back in the closing stages, found themselves pegged back again.
The away side registered an expected goals (xG) figure of 1.81 from 13 shots in this contest, compared to Ipswich tallying 1.15 from 11 attempts.
But regardless of the underlying stats, the result keeps Fulham winless and ensures they have already lost eight points from winning positions this season, Only Bournemouth (nine) have lost more.

As for the home side, they have now won three of their first six Premier League games in a season for only the second time, while also remaining undefeated against Fulham overall in the competition (W2 D3).

1641z9xizoi411ds3hzbrwz5hz.title: Minoungou hails Colorado's 'tough mentality' as playoff race heats up
1641z9xizoi411ds3hzbrwz5hz.subtitle: Colorado Rapids and Portland Timbers are both enduring winless streaks in MLS, and they need a win to boost their playoff hopes.
paragraphs: Colorado Rapids winger Georgi Minoungou believes the team's "tough mentality" will be their key to reaching the playoffs, with the Portland Timbers next up in MLS.
The Rapids are winless in their last four matches (D1 L3), and they slipped down to ninth – the last wildcard spot – in the Western Conference in midweek after a 2-2 draw with Minnesota United.
Having had a man sent off midway through the second half, Loic Williams then scored a late own goal to gift the Loons a point, and it leaves Colorado three points off the automatic playoff spots.
But Minoungou is confident Colorado can rally and get back to winning ways with only five games of the regular season remaining.
"We have a tough mentality," he said after the draw with Minnesota. "We always want to give high energy in everything.
"But there's some moments that there will be ups and downs, and that's why we have a great coach [Matt Wells].

"He's always on the side, pushing us to keep going forward when we're down and injecting some urgency into players so we can raise the level. We're good, we're focused on the playoffs; we want to get there."
Portland are one place behind Colorado in the table, sitting 10th, but have a five-point gap to make up to the playoff places.
They are one of three teams on 33 points – though they sit above Real Salt Lake on goals scored – and have failed to win any of their last six matches (D2 L4).
They were beaten 2-0 by the LA Galaxy last time out, and head coach Marti Cifuentes acknowledged recent results and performances have not been good enough.
"There are a lot of things that we need to improve, that's for sure," he said.
"You can be unlucky in one game, you can be unlucky in two games if you want, but it's difficult when we have this trend that means we've not done well enough in certain areas.

"One of them is that we're conceding in every game, and we have been speaking with the guys that we cannot put ourselves in a situation where we need to score three, four goals every game to get something from them."
Portland Timbers – Antony
Antony has scored five goals in six regular-season matches against Colorado, while the only other team he has scored more than once against is the Houston Dynamo (two).
He has scored in all three of his home matches against the Rapids, netting four goals over the three games.
Colorado Rapids – Darren Yapi
Darren Yapi scored his first goal since April in Colorado's 2-2 draw with Minnesota United.
He had gone 20 consecutive regular-season matches without a goal contribution prior to scoring against the Loons.
MATCH PREDICTION: PORTLAND TIMBERS WIN
Colorado recorded a 2-0 win over Portland on February 28 after the Timbers won both meetings during the 2025 season.
Colorado's only set of consecutive wins over Portland in all competitions came in the first three all-time meetings between the teams in 2011-12 (W3).

However, the Rapids have lost 20 of their last 28 regular-season away matches (W3 D5) dating back to April 2025, including five of the last six. Over this 28-match stretch, Colorado have been outscored 60-29, managing to keep just two clean sheets.
The Timbers, meanwhile, lost their last home match 1-0 against Atlanta United on September 19.
They have not lost two straight regular-season home matches since September 2019, avoiding defeat in the match following each of their previous 29 regular-season home losses.
Portland Timbers – 46.7%
Colorado Rapids – 26.9%

          Why Aren’t Arsenal Scoring Any Corners?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal broke the Premier League record for goals from corners last season, but seven games into their title defence, they haven’t scored from a single one yet in 2026-27. What’s going wrong for the set-piece specialists?
By now, we all know the story of Arsenal’s first Premier League title in 22 years.

It was a success built not on a fierce, free-flowing attack, but on an exceptional defence, the deepest squad in the division, and an ability to master the fine margins of football better than anyone else.
Nowhere was that more evident than at set-pieces.

Arsenal exploited corners to devastating effect in 2025-26. They broke the record for the number of goals scored from corners in a single Premier League season with 19, and their 26.8% of goals coming from corners was comfortably the highest share of any Premier League champion.

Even with referees paying closer attention to grappling and blocking at corners this season, the expectation was that Arsenal would continue to lean heavily into their set-piece strength. Why wouldn’t they?

But that hasn’t transpired. We’re seven league games into the new campaign, and Arsenal haven’t scored a single goal from a corner. In fact, across all competitions, they haven’t scored from any non-penalty set-piece at all.
At the same stage of last season, they’d already scored six goals from corners in the league alone.
So, what’s going on? Are ‘Set-Piece FC’ suddenly… bad at set-pieces? Or is there another explanation?

Let’s just check the premise. Given we’re only seven games into the season, goals alone don't necessarily tell us the full story as to how effective Arsenal’s corners have been. For a better look under the hood, we can turn to our old friend expected goals (xG).
Last season, Arsenal led the Premier League for total xG generated from corners, with 13.8. That worked out at 0.36 xG per game, at an average of 0.064 xG per corner.

Put another way, when Arsenal took a corner, there was a 6.4% chance that it would result in a goal, the second-best value of any team. Arsenal slightly overperformed in reality, scoring from 8.8% of all their corners – the highest rate of any team.
This season, though, things have changed.
Arsenal are generating just 0.22 xG per game from corners, at an average of 0.047 xG per corner. They've fallen from the second-most dangerous team per corner to the ninth.
A drop from 0.064 to 0.047 might not sound particularly dramatic, but it represents a 26.6% reduction in the average quality of chances they’re generating per corner.

And it’s not just the quality of chances that has declined. Arsenal are also generating fewer shots from corners, down from 2.8 per game last season, the second-highest figure in the league, to 2.1 this season, the ninth highest.

Before we get into trying to work out why, it’s worth saying that Arsenal have still generated 1.55 xG from corners this season. That's the seventh-highest total in the Premier League and suggests they could reasonably have expected to score at least once. In fact, only Liverpool (-2.05) have underperformed their corner xG by a greater margin than Arsenal (-1.55).
So, what’s with the drop-off? Has Arsenal’s approach changed?
In 2025-26, Arsenal crossed the ball into the penalty area from 86.6% of their corners, opting to go short on 13.0% of occasions.
This season, those shares haven’t changed much. They're crossing from 84.9% of corners and playing short from the remaining 15.1%.

165ymzry9p0s41imwzyixi63jx.title: Flick admits surprise over Jesus impact at Barcelona
165ymzry9p0s41imwzyixi63jx.subtitle: Gabriel Jesus has made a strong start to life in Barcelona, which has caught head coach Hansi Flick by surprise.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick admits he has been surprised by Gabriel Jesus' impact since the striker joined Barcelona.
After four seasons with Arsenal, which ended with a Premier League triumph, Jesus completed a reported €15m (£12.8m) move to the reigning LaLiga champions this summer.
Despite starting on just one of his five appearances for Barca across all competitions, the 29-year-old has scored three goals for the Blaugrana.
He netted on his only start, which came last time out against Getafe, with Raphinha sidelined due to a muscle problem.
Raphinha, who has scored 21 goals in 34 Champions League games for Barca, is also expected to miss their trip to Galatasaray on Tuesday, with Jesus in line for another start.
"He's ready. Whether he plays, which we don't know yet, we'll decide after training," said Flick about Jesus.
"We're very happy with him. He's a bit of a surprise, we have to admit. His behaviour is fantastic and he's a great player."
Galatasaray and Barca have faced each other on 10 occasions to date, with the Turkish side winning just one of those (D3 L6): 2-1 in a Champions League home game in November 1994.

Barca have won their last four away games against Turkish teams in European competition, the last three of which have all been at Galatasaray (1-0 in March 2002, 2-0 in September 2002 and 2-1 in March 2022).
"They have very good attackers and we have to adapt," Flick said about Galatasaray.
"We always have to adapt to the opponent and to what we need. And that's what we'll do.
"Many of these [Barca] players are world champions, and we've seen that they're still hungry.
"It's difficult, but they're hungry. We have to work for our fans, for our families. It's difficult, and the road is long."

          Croatia vs England Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Saturday's UEFA Nations League matchup with our Croatia vs England prediction and preview, as Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions look to make it back-to-back wins.
It's fair to say Croatia are familiar foes for England at this point.

A blistering second-half performance saw Thomas Tuchel's side overcome Croatia 4-2 in their opening game at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and they also beat the same opponents in their first match at Euro 2020 under Gareth Southgate.
Of course, the biggest meeting between the teams in recent years – in the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup – went the way of Luka Modric and co.
With both teams on three points after two games in Group A3 of the UEFA Nations League, Saturday's clash at Stadion HNK Rijeka could be pivotal in the fight to make the last eight.
England needed a response after finishing on the wrong side of a five-goal thriller against Spain, and they got one against Czechia on Tuesday, helped by Pavel Sulc's first-half red card.

Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane were on target in a 2-0 win for the Three Lions, which was their sixth in their last eight Nations League matches (L2) across the top two tiers, scoring 20 goals in that span. That is more victories and goals than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition overall (W5 D6 L7, 18 goals).
It was also England's eighth straight away win in all competitions, giving them an opportunity to match a team record this weekend.
Only once have they ever won nine away games in a row, doing so under World Cup-winning manager Sir Alf Ramsey between December 1965 and October 1967.
And Kane – who smacked a penalty off the crossbar against Spain after losing his footing – has also enjoyed playing on the road lately, netting in each of his last five away games for England.

He could become just the fourth player to score in six consecutive away games for the Three Lions, after James Windridge (six from March to June 1908), Tom Finney (seven from September 1946 to May 1948) and Stan Mortensen (six from May 1947 to October 1948).

While Kane is almost a guaranteed starter, Tuchel has plenty of decisions to make elsewhere. Against Czechia, he handed Trent Alexander-Arnold his first England start since October 2024 (versus Finland), having made the more conservative choice to deploy Jarell Quansah at right-back against Spain.
Alexander-Arnold teed up Gordon's opener with a trademark delivery to the far post, which was also his first assist for his country since that Finland game under Lee Carsley.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has deputised capably for his Arsenal club-mate Declan Rice in midfield, but with Alex Scott winning his first senior cap off the bench in midweek and Morgan Gibbs-White also looking lively, Tuchel has plenty of options.
Slaven Bilic made a winning return to the Croatia dugout against Czechia last weekend, but a crushing 4-1 defeat to Spain brought them back to earth on Tuesday.

Croatia have now lost five of their 10 matches overall in 2026 (W5), just the third time they have suffered that many defeats in a single calendar year (also 2018 and 2020), though they have never previously lost six in one year.

Despite briefly getting back on level terms in the first half through Dion Beljo‘s first international goal, Croatia were well beaten by the world champions. They only attempted five shots to Spain's 16 and put up 0.47 expected goals (xG) to their opponents' 1.81.
They have only registered a lower xG figure in three previous Nations League fixtures – versus France in March 2025 (0.18), Sweden in November 2020 (0.3) and England in October 2018 (0.42).

Modric could return to the starting lineup after getting 10 minutes off the bench in Seville, while England's old nemesis Ivan Perisic has started both games in this international window. Perisic – who registered a goal and an assist against the Three Lions in that 2018 semi-final – has 15 goal involvements in his last 18 starts for Croatia (six goals, nine assists).

Eight years ago, Kieran Trippier‘s memorable fifth-minute free-kick in Moscow was cancelled out by Perisic's instinctive finish, before Mario Mandzukic sent Croatia through to the World Cup final with an extra-time winner, though they lost the final 4-2 to France.

168m42i6rkuzx1r16w8tz9fu3u.title: 'What do you want us to do?' – Maresca defends Man City's Anfield celebrations
168m42i6rkuzx1r16w8tz9fu3u.subtitle: Manchester City's squad have come in for some criticism for their celebrations against Liverpool, leaving Enzo Maresca baffled.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca is puzzled as to what people expect from his Manchester City players after they received criticism for their celebrations at Anfield.
City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 on Sunday, with their players and fans celebrating jubilantly.
The victory came in the wake of City having been found guilty of breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

City have started a league season with six straight wins for the second time since 2020-21. However, critics have directed their ire at Maresca's squad, claiming the celebrations were over the top, and even tasteless, but the former Chelsea boss bit back.

"Criticised for what? We won 0-3 at Anfield, what do you want us to do?" the Italian asked reporters in his pre-match press conference ahead of City's Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain.
"And even if it was 0-1 it would be exactly the same. We work every day to win games.
"We can be focused. The rest is things from outside we need to deal with. We were so, so happy inside the pitch and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.
"After we were very happy on the pitch, sharing time with our fans. Probably it has been tougher for our fans than for the players or for me.

"It is more complicated because if I was an Arsenal fan or Manchester United fan and you are a City fan, I can say 'my friend, you are a cheat' or these kinds of things. So probably, it has been more tough for them.
"But again, we were happy at the end of the game. Inside the changing room, we were very happy, celebrating because we know how difficult it is Anfield away, so that is why we were very happy."
And Ruben Dias said it was a case of shutting out the noise.
"Personally and I really feel like I speak for the whole group, we trust the club," Dias said.
"We're very calm and were very focused on enjoying football. We know the team we've got, we want to make the most out of it, we want to win, and that's the only thing in our mind.
"If there's more or less noise or whatever the reason the noise is, at the end of the day it's all the same, same as before, because people don't love us winning and we love to win.
"I very much stand by the manager's words as well. To win at Anfield in whatever circumstance, whether it's earlier in the season or later in the season, we will enjoy it just as much.
"We will celebrate however it feels in the moment and it will obviously be a show of how much it means to us."
City have lodged an appeal against the guilty verdict.

16ac6wacdy0y61a9za2aphbcxf.title: 'We are not in Disneyland' – Arteta defends reaction to Dowman red card
16ac6wacdy0y61a9za2aphbcxf.subtitle: Max Dowman will be unavailable for Arsenal's trip to Anfield after his red card against Fleetwood, which frustrated Mikel Arteta.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta has defended his reaction to Max Dowman's sending off in Arsenal's shock defeat to Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup, insisting "we are not in Disneyland".
Dowman was shown a straight red card after lashing out at a strong challenge from a Fleetwood player, with the Gunners going on to lose on penalties against the League Two side.
The teenager also received a red card while representing England's Under-19s during the last international break for the same action.
Dowman will miss Arsenal's next three domestic games, including their Premier League trip to Anfield on Sunday.
Arteta did not hide his frustration with Dowman on the sidelines at Fleetwood, and the Spaniard stood by his reaction.
"If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say 'I don't like the reaction'. For me it was the best reaction to be who I am," said Arteta.
"Whether it is right or wrong, that is the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [expletive] off big time.
"So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this is the level.

"We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him like everybody else because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to say to me? You need to be fair."
Arsenal are winless in their last 13 away Premier League games against Liverpool (D5 L8), since winning 2-0 in 2012-13.

They have never gone 14 winless away at Anfield in their league history, also going 13 between 1975-76 and 1987-88, a run which was broken by their famous 2-0 final-day victory in 1988-89, which secured the title.

"It's an opportunity. I came here and in many places we were 20, 22 years, 18 years without winning, and we've been doing all these things, so on Sunday, that's the opportunity that we have," added Arteta.
"We expect a big game on Sunday; we're looking forward to it for sure. It's 14 years that we haven't won there, so it's time to do it."

16d97oet5l83c16w5c1p484jjt.title: Tuchel: Kane a one-off for England
16d97oet5l83c16w5c1p484jjt.subtitle: Harry Kane is just two appearances away from becoming England's joint-most-capped player, but Thomas Tuchel says the striker is a one-off.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel feels England are unlikely to see another striker of Harry Kane's level.
Kane is two games away from equalling Peter Shilton as England's all-time record appearance maker, on 125 caps.
The Bayern Munich forward is already England's record scorer, with 87 goals in 123 appearances for the Three Lions.
Kane has scored twice in England's last two games, although he did miss a penalty in last Saturday's 3-2 loss to world champions Spain.
The 33-year-old plundered 73 goals for club and country last season and Tuchel does not think there will be another forward of his ilk that comes along anytime soon.
"The highest level of goalscorer, of finishing," Tuchel said of Kane.
"He is the first one to push everyone and that is his mindset and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills. He is a complete package."
Asked who could replace Kane once he retires, Tuchel said: "You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all.
"We look for different options and solutions. We finished the game with Jude [Bellingham] up front as a number nine.
"There will be someone else, but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years."
One possibility could be Jude Bellingham, who netted eight goals for England at the World Cup.
"I like him as a nine," Tuchel said of Bellingham. "Then he can contribute to both sides and overload the sides and doesn't affect so much of the balance.

"We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides. We are working on that.
"Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and should always be able to end up in the box.
"He is a natural goalscorer and he has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to be there and have the decisive action, so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a nine or a 10."

16ddte0k3n8vg1eorxrmyrc39r.title: Maresca can create 'siege mentality' at Man City, claims Mills
16ddte0k3n8vg1eorxrmyrc39r.subtitle: Danny Mills believes Enzo Maresca can use Manchester City's guilty verdict to his advantage by creating a "siege mentality" in the squad.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca can create a "siege mentality" off the back of Manchester City's guilty verdict, so says Danny Mills.
Earlier this week, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of breaching the competition's financial rules across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.
City still insist they are innocent and have pledged to fight the ruling and have until Friday to appeal it, while a sanctions hearing will take place separately.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said City had "systematically broken Premier League Rules for nearly a decade" and described the decision as the "most significant" in the competition's history.
Former City defender Mills, however, feels Maresca can use the situation to his advantage.

Mills told Stats Perform: "For Maresca, I think you can create that siege mentality and just go, 'Look, all we can do is do what we do now and get as many points as possible and just play football. You're all getting paid, lads. You're still getting paid. It's not a problem.'
"This is not going into administration and the club's going to go bust, and next week you might not have a contract, or you might not have a job.

"This is not like League Two when it was happening with Bury and things like that. Completely different scenario. So, ultimately, if the Manchester City owners weren't allowed to remain in charge, somebody would take them over.

"Wouldn't be a big problem for them. We've seen what's happened at Chelsea and everywhere else. So, yeah, I think you just have to say, look, 'Let's dig in, lads. It's the world against us. Let's just keep winning football matches and whatever stick we get, we're going to get and it's not our fault. It's not of our doing, but we're going to have to take it'."
Pep Guardiola has come out in support of City, while Rodri said last week that the players would not look back on their success at the club in a different light following this verdict.
In the years they have been found to have breached the rules, City won three Premier League titles, while they then went on to enjoy a period of dominance after 2018.
Mills, though, does not think any of the players who won titles at the club will be rushing to give away their medals.

He added: "[The Manchester City players] would not have been aware that there was effectively cheating going on or sports doping, whatever you want to call it. I'm not sure many of the managers did either.

"When you talk about Roberto Mancini going, 'Well, it wasn't my fault. Nothing to do with me.' Pep Guardiola has come out and been slightly, well, a lot more backing of the club, and he's got behind the club at this point.

"Obviously, there's an appeal process we expect that will happen in the near future. But it's hard as a player. I've seen some pundits say, 'They'll all be wanting to give their medals back.' No they won't. If they give their medals back, are they going to give back their bonuses, their contracts, their investments? No, it's not going to happen.

"The problem that you've now got is it's so far on from when it happened. It's going to be so difficult to punish those that were there at the time. Retrospective punishment is very, very difficult. You can only really punish now and going forward. And of course, that's a lot of the players who are at the football club who had nothing to do with this at all."
City sit top of the Premier League with a perfect record so far in 2026-27. They travel to Liverpool in their first game back after the international break.

16gkw85f0u1e31893e2snsolex.title: Flick says Barca struggled to match Madrid's physicality in Clasico defeat
16gkw85f0u1e31893e2snsolex.subtitle: Barcelona saw their perfect start to the season in LaLiga halted by their arch-rivals Real Madrid, with Kylian Mbappe doing the damage.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick felt a lack of physical freshness cost Barcelona in a game he thought they controlled, after they slumped to a 2-1 defeat against rivals Real Madrid.

Kylian Mbappe's brace decided the first edition of El Clasico this season, with the France captain slotting in an 87th-minute winner following a wonderful counter involving Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler and Eduardo Camavinga.
The result saw Barca miss the chance to become the first team on record to start a season in one of Europe's top five leagues with 10 straight victories.
Their run of nine wins to open 2026-27 puts them level with the record starts made by Chelsea in the Premier League (in 2005-06) and Madrid in LaLiga (in 1968-69).

Madrid have now won on four of their last seven trips to Barca in LaLiga (L3), more victories than they managed in their previous 16 such visits (W3 D6 L7), with the result moving them within three points of the LaLiga leaders.
And though Flick was content with aspects of his team's performance, he noted that Madrid had the physical edge throughout the contest.
"I'm not satisfied. We weren't 100% fresh, that's the reality," Flick said, as quoted by Sport ES.
"Real Madrid had chances and scored two goals, we had control of the game, but we lacked fluidity in the first half.
"In the second we were doing damage, but that late goal made it 1-2. It's difficult, but we have to accept it.
"We lacked freshness to circulate the ball, and we have to disconnect a little bit now, to regain our best condition and come back fresher."
Barca had 18 shots to Madrid's 10, with 11 of their attempts coming from inside the area, but they lost the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.19 to 1.95.
"There's not much to say. From my point of view, we were superior, but this is Madrid, they can have few chances and still score against you," defender Joao Cancelo said.
"We are going to look at the mistakes we made – we have to react. We always want to press high and there are times when we need to have more control of the ball, we lacked that today.
"We are a humble team that likes to work hard, and now, with all the boys, we have to think about Alaves [on Saturday]."
While Barca welcome Alaves to Camp Nou for their next LaLiga game on Saturday, Madrid are away to Racing Santander the following day.

Having gone down 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday, the Blaugrana have now suffered back-to-back defeats in all competitions, having won their first 11 games of the campaign.

"Real Madrid had chances and scored two goals, we had control of the game, but we lacked fluidity in the first half. 

"In the second we were doing damage, but that late goal made it 1-2. It's difficult, but we have to accept it.

"We lacked freshness to circulate the ball, and we have to disconnect a little bit now, to regain our best condition and come back fresher."

Barca had 18 shots to Madrid's 10, with 11 of their attempts coming from inside the area, but they lost the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.19 to 1.95.

"There's not much to say. From my point of view, we were superior, but this is Madrid, they can have few chances and still score against you," defender Joao Cancelo said. 

"We are going to look at the mistakes we made – we have to react. We always want to press high and there are times when we need to have more control of the ball, we lacked that today.

"We are a humble team that likes to work hard, and now, with all the boys, we have to think about Alaves [on Saturday]."

While Barca welcome Alaves to Camp Nou for their next LaLiga game on Saturday, Madrid are away to Racing Santander the following day.

Having gone down 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday, the Blaugrana have now suffered back-to-back defeats in all competitions, having won their first 11 games of the campaign.

16ll62s97o9mc104mlfr1clzw3.title: Bayern Munich 6-1 Magdeburg: Olise leads holders into last 16
16ll62s97o9mc104mlfr1clzw3.subtitle: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane remained on the bench for Bayern Munich, but Michael Olise led their charge in the DFB-Pokal without him.
paragraphs: Michael Olise starred in Bayern Munich's commanding 6-1 victory over Magdeburg to help the reigning DFB-Pokal holders into the round of 16.
Olise got two goals and an assist – teeing up Ismael Saibari – in the first 50 minutes, before Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and David Santos Daiber finished off the big win at Allianz Arena.

Bayern had already seen two chances go begging before they got their 10th-minute opener. Josip Stanisic carved open Magdeburg's defence with his throughball to Saibari, who drew Dominik Reimann off his line before teeing up Olise for a tap-in into the empty net.

Just five minutes later, though, Magdeburg were level with a piece of quality from Felipe Chavez. He stood up Jonathan Tah on the left before cutting inside and whipping a wonderful finish into the top-right corner.
Bayern restored their lead six minutes later, with Olise turning provider by sliding it forward for Saibari, who dinked a lovely shot over Reimann.
Magdeburg caused more problems down the left on the stroke of half-time, with Baris Atik cutting inside to hit the near post before Jonas Urbig smothered Chavez's follow-up.

Bayern were on top from the start of the second half; Davies' first involvement was winning a penalty after being tripped by Pierre Nadjombe, and Olise chipped the spot-kick into the net 50 minutes in.
Reimann was called into action to deny Lennart Karl, but Bayern got their fourth in the 70th minute, with Davies bundling over from Karl's tight-angled shot.

Davies then cut inside from the left, wrong-footing his defender along the way, to tee up Brown for a stretching finish four minutes later, but debutant Daiber added late gloss with the last kick of the game, as he arrowed a low finish into the bottom-right corner.
Olise takes up the mantle
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane remained on the bench throughout the match, but he was not needed, as Olise stepped up to help Bayern into a comfortable lead.
He has now scored 12 competitive goals for Bayern in all competitions this season – more than any other Bundesliga player.
Olise had the third-most shots in the game (three), and the third-most touches in the opposition box (eight), while only Tom Bischof (50) made more passes in the final third than him (49).

As expected, Bayern blew their second-tier opponents away, having 19 shots worth 3.98 expected goals (xG), with eight of those shots on target, while Magdeburg's nine attempts amounted to just 0.86 xG.

Things could have been so different if Atik had buried his chance on the stroke of half-time instead of hitting the woodwork, but instead, it is Bayern who will progress to the next round as they keep their title defence alive.

171qq6pujuxo31h0w7pwphf3ly.title: PSG are better than Barcelona, claims Flick
171qq6pujuxo31h0w7pwphf3ly.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 in a Champions League thriller on Tuesday, but Hansi Flick feels his team learned valuable lessons.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick claimed Paris Saint-Germain are simply a better team than Barcelona, who will take lessons from their Champions League defeat.
Tuesday's contest between two of Europe's best teams served up a thriller at the Parc des Princes, where PSG won 4-2.
Barca twice dragged themselves level, through Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal, but Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz clinched the points for PSG late on.
PSG had 22 shots, with Barca having 18. Blaugrana goalkeeper Joan Garcia made 10 saves, while the hosts recorded 3.7 expected goals to the visitors' 2.23 xG.
And Flick felt, ultimately, two-time reigning European champions PSG are just a better side than his Barca team, though he is sure the Blaugrana will have learned plenty.
"It was a fantastic match, from both teams. PSG showed they are a better team than us," said Flick, who is one win shy of picking up his 100th for Barca.
"We lost, but we learned. Mistakes happen. But what we've done in recent weeks is fantastic.
"Today wasn't easy; the players ran a lot and tried to play. What happened after Sevilla, with the recovery, wasn't the best. It's not an excuse.
"We have to learn. It's October, and you don't win titles in October; the Champions League is won in June."
Barcelona have scored 50 goals in just 12 games in all competitions this season.
However, PSG had 15 shots on target, the most Barca faced on record (since 2003-04) in a Champions League match.
Flick, though, believes that was down to PSG's attacking quality, and not necessarily because Barca defended poorly.
"I think PSG also scored a lot of goals against City. In the end, in the last 10 minutes, the team dropped off, and we conceded the fourth," Flick added.
"But I saw some very good things. We have potential. I'm not negative. It was a good experience. We have to do better."
Barca will now turn their focus back to LaLiga, and Sunday's upcoming Clasico.
Should the Blaugrana beat Real Madrid, they will become the first team to win their opening 10 LaLiga games of a season.

176994dtvglxv169fdvjsxnrku.title: Croatia 1-2 Spain: Super-sub Merino inspires second-half comeback
176994dtvglxv169fdvjsxnrku.subtitle: Spain reached the quarter-finals of the Nations League after substitute Mikel Merino scored twice in their victory over Croatia.
paragraphs: Mikel Merino was Spain's hero from the bench as his double clinched a 2-1 win over 10-man Croatia in the Nations League.
Luis de la Fuente's side looked on course to see their long unbeaten run come to an end after Ivan Perisic's early goal, but Merino helped turn things around after the break.
Merino's two goals came either side of Perisic's red card, with his winning strike in the 88th minute ensuring Spain remained perfect from their four Group A3 matches.
Spain needed Unai Simon to come to their rescue in the 13th minute with a point-blank save to deny Josip Stanisic's towering header.
Croatia's pressure told in the 17th minute when Igor Matanovic's stinging shot was parried by Simon, with Perisic the quickest to react as he nodded in the rebound.

The hosts should have doubled their tally six minutes later when Simon's loose pass was picked off by Nikola Vlasic. He laid it off for Matanovic, but Spain's goalkeeper atoned for his error with a fine stop.

Spain's first attempt on target did not come until the stroke of half-time, but Mikel Oyarzabal's header was comfortably held by Dominik Livakovic, with Lamine Yamal then firing into the side-netting after he was picked out by Pedri's sensational pass.
De la Fuente brought on Merino at the break, and the Arsenal midfielder hauled Spain level just after the hour with a calm finish into the bottom-left corner.

From there, La Roja dominated proceedings as Yamal's deflected effort narrowly evaded the far post, but they were almost caught out at the other end when Martin Zubimendi's poor pass teed up Perisic, but his shot was straight at Simon.
But Croatia were forced to see out the final stages with 10 men when Perisic received his second yellow card after tripping Marc Cucurella, with the decision upheld by VAR.

And Spain made their advantage count when Merino brilliantly took down Zubimendi's ball into the area before hammering a left-footed strike into the top-left corner, sealing La Roja's progression to the quarter-finals.
Super-sub Merino proves his worth

With Spain struggling to create many chances in the final third during the first half, highlighted by their expected goals (xG) total of 0.57 from their five attempts, De la Fuente made the decision to replace Alex Baena for Merino, who turned the game on its head.

Merino has made a name for being a key player off the bench for Spain, and he has now scored six goals in 16 matches for La Roja as a substitute since the start of 2025. No player has netted more as a substitute for a European national team in that time.

The result also sees Spain's unbeaten run extend to 42 matches in all competitions (W32 D10), though there were some concerns for De la Fuente. The world champions have now conceded at least one goal in each of their last four official matches (five goals in total), their worst run of conceding since June 2025 (six matches).

It was also a mixed match for Perisic, who has been involved in five goals (two goals, three assists) in five matches against Spain, the most of any player against the nation over the last 20 years (level with Kylian Mbappe), before he was sent for an early bath for a needless coming together.
And though it was an improved performance from Slaven Bilic's side after their 7-0 thrashing by England, they came away empty-handed.
Croatia edged the xG battle with a total of 1.17 from their 10 shots, compared to Spain's tally of 1.08 from the same number of attempts.

176mwh9ppzb461d508p2ihc5h0.title: Shaw disappointed by Man City's slow start in draw with Madrid
176mwh9ppzb461d508p2ihc5h0.subtitle: Manchester City are still winless after two Champions League games, and Khadija Shaw felt a slow start cost them versus Real Madrid.
paragraphs: Khadija Shaw said Manchester City were disappointed with the way they started against Real Madrid and felt they should have won the game, even if the Spanish giants were denied a late winner by referee Silvia Gasperotti.
Having drawn 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their 2026-27 Champions League opener last week, City were again forced to settle for a point on Thursday, drawing 1-1 on home soil.

Linda Caicedo fired into the far corner to put Madrid in front in the 29th minute, and City could have few complaints at being behind at half-time, having only attempted five shots to their visitors' 11.
However, City came out stronger following the interval, drawing level when Shaw finished on the turn, having been fed by Yui Hasegawa in the 51st minute.

City ended the game with 1.69 expected goals (xG) to Madrid's 0.89, with both teams having 16 shots apiece, although visiting head coach Pau Quesada was furious to see Silvia Cristobal's late strike disallowed, with Gasperotti having already blown the whistle after the official inadvertently blocked Beth Mead on the edge of the City area.
And Shaw felt City would have won the match if they had produced their second-half level throughout the full 90 minutes.
"I think when you look at the game, we tried in the second half much better than we started the first, and I think that's one thing we're going to look at as a team," Shaw told Disney+.
"We're disappointed that we didn't win the game, but we definitely fought until the end and that's good.
"I think with our pressing, we gave them a lot more time in the first half. In the second half, we stuck in and pressed them higher up the pitch and that caused a lot of errors from them.
"I think if we had done that in the first half, it would've been a different game."
Reflecting on her goal, Shaw added: "When I'm in the box, I try to stay calm, with the players I have around me, that's something we try to build in training.
"Sometimes it doesn't come, but more often than not, they look for me. I try to stay calm, stay level-headed and focus on where the goal is.
"With the centre-backs I'm up against, it depends on what they give me. If they give me time and space, I know I can turn and get a shot off."
Thursday's draw ended City's seven-match winning run on home soil in the Champions League, which was the longest ever recorded by an English team in the competition.
Madrid have still won just one of their 10 Champions League games against English sides in the competition, though (D3 L6), beating Arsenal 2-0 in the 2024-25 quarter-finals.
Their win rate against WSL teams stands at 10%, making it their worst against teams from a specific country in the competition (minimum three games played).

177n9256d2ntd1bu3dy00iyp3p.title: Al-Qadsiah 2-3 Al-Hilal: Martinelli and Neves on target as visitors go top
177n9256d2ntd1bu3dy00iyp3p.subtitle: Despite a late goal from Mateo Retegui, Al-Hilal were able to hold on for all three points against Al-Qadsiah to go top of the league.
paragraphs: Al-Hilal moved to the top of the Saudi Pro League with a 3-2 victory over Al-Qadsiah at Prince Mohammed Bin Fahd Stadium.
Gabriel Martinelli, Ruben Neves and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic were on the scoresheet for the visitors, who had to hold on during a nervy finish after Mateo Retegui halved Al-Qadsiah's deficit late on.
Al-Hilal were ahead after 21 minutes as Ollie Watkins raced onto a long ball from midfield and squared to Martinelli, who saw his shot with the outside of his right boot deflect past Koen Casteels.

However, the hosts restored parity just after the half-hour mark through Julian Quinones after he headed Musab Al Juwayr's lofted pass into the bottom-left corner, leaving Yassine Bounou with no chance of saving it.

Watkins and Crysencio Summerville both tested Casteels after the break, but it was Neves who scored the go-ahead goal in the 77th minute as Milinkovic-Savic teed the Portuguese midfielder up for a curling finish from outside the box.

Milinkovic-Savic then went from provider to scorer seven minutes later as he fired in from Sultan Mandash's cut-back, rendering Retegui's glancing header from Tijjani Reijnders' free-kick a consolation.
Al-Hilal's stars shine bright

Al-Nassr placed pressure on both Al-Hilal and Al-Qadsiah earlier on Friday after defeating Al-Faysaly, but the visitors took their opportunity to go top of the pack, and did so with more dominance than the scoreline suggests.

Al-Hilal accumulated 2.84 expected goals (xG) from 19 shots to Al-Qadsiah's 0.68 from 14 attempts, with Martinelli and Theo Hernandez (both four) leading the way in shots, while Watkins recorded the most xG (1.09).

Milinkovic-Savic created the most chances for Al-Hilal (five), Watkins completed 100% of passes (19/19) while creating three chances, and Summerville won eight of his 12 duels as Al-Hilal worked hard for their win.

Al-Qadsiah forward duo of Quinones and Retegui both got on the scoresheet, with the latter scoring the second-most goals in the league this season (seven), but Brendan Rodgers will know his side must perform better against their title competitors if they are to win the league.

178xvzue5708h1k4tw5ffr5hau.title: 'I don't feel fear' – Arbeloa not worried about Fulham future
178xvzue5708h1k4tw5ffr5hau.subtitle: Fulham are still seeking their first Premier League win under Alvaro Arbeloa, who shrugged off the rising pressure on his shoulders.
paragraphs: Alvaro Arbeloa says he is not worried about losing his job as Fulham head coach, despite a difficult start to life at Craven Cottage.
Ahead of matchday seven, Fulham sit bottom of the table with just two points to their name, while they are one of three teams – along with Tottenham and Bournemouth – yet to win this term.
Having drawn two and lost four of their six games so far, it is their worst start to a Premier League campaign since 2020-21, when they drew once and lost five of their opening fixtures.
Only once have they had a longer run from the start of a top-flight campaign, failing to win any of their first seven in 1951-52.

And Fulham have failed to win any of their first three home Premier League matches this season (D1 L2). They have only had a longer winless home start in one top-flight season, failing to win their first five at Craven Cottage in 1966-67.
The Cottagers have also lost eight points from winning positions already in the Premier League this season, with only Bournemouth (nine) dropping more.
But when asked whether he was concerned about his future, Arbeloa said he was still optimistic, despite results not going Fulham's way.
"I am focused on my players, on my team," he said. "That is the most important thing.
"It is not about me; it is about the club, the players and the supporters.  We are waiting for the game when the performance turns into the result.
"I never worry about my position. I don't feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it. You have to work, take the decision, and you need to show confidence to your players.
"For me, I am so happy with many things that they are doing. I know it is not easy for them.
"It's not about my position; it is about Fulham's position. That is the most important thing. Obviously, it is just six games, but it is true we need points."
Fulham host Hull City in their next Premier League match, with the Opta supercomputer predicting they will earn their first top-flight victory as they are given a 55.8% win probability.

Alvaro Arbeloa says he is not worried about losing his job as Fulham head coach, despite a difficult start to life at Craven Cottage.

Ahead of matchday seven, Fulham sit bottom of the table with just two points to their name, while they are one of three teams – along with Tottenham and Bournemouth – yet to win this term.

Having drawn two and lost four of their six games so far, it is their worst start to a Premier League campaign since 2020-21, when they drew once and lost five of their opening fixtures.

Only once have they had a longer run from the start of a top-flight campaign, failing to win any of their first seven in 1951-52.

And Fulham have failed to win any of their first three home Premier League matches this season (D1 L2). They have only had a longer winless home start in one top-flight season, failing to win their first five at Craven Cottage in 1966-67.

The Cottagers have also lost eight points from winning positions already in the Premier League this season, with only Bournemouth (nine) dropping more.

But when asked whether he was concerned about his future, Arbeloa said he was still optimistic, despite results not going Fulham's way.

"I am focused on my players, on my team," he said. "That is the most important thing.

"It is not about me; it is about the club, the players and the supporters.  We are waiting for the game when the performance turns into the result.

"I never worry about my position. I don't feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it. You have to work, take the decision, and you need to show confidence to your players.

"For me, I am so happy with many things that they are doing. I know it is not easy for them. 

"It's not about my position; it is about Fulham's position. That is the most important thing. Obviously, it is just six games, but it is true we need points."

1791vuyah6dek1rgi6yqe2mjsk.title: Napoli 3-0 Frosinone: De Bruyne and Lang on target in routine win
1791vuyah6dek1rgi6yqe2mjsk.subtitle: Napoli marked their return from the international break with three points as they cruised to victory against Frosinone in Serie A.
paragraphs: Napoli returned to winning ways in Serie A with a 3-0 victory over Frosinone at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
Kevin De Bruyne netted a brace, scoring either side of Noa Lang's strike, as Massimiliano Allegri's side picked up their third league victory of the season.

Napoli started on the front foot as Rasmus Hojlund struck the right post from Giovanni Di Lorenzo's drilled cross in the third minute, while Leonardo Spinazzola sent a strike from distance over the bar.

The hosts then won a penalty before the half-hour mark as Giorgio Cittadini brought down Hojlund, who initially missed the spot-kick before it was retaken due to encroachment and dispatched by De Bruyne.

And their lead was doubled in the 32nd minute. Di Lorenzo saw a poked effort smothered by Lorenzo Palmisani, but the rebound fell to Lang, who took a touch past Cittadani to convert into an unguarded net.
David Neres sent two promising shots wide of the target either side of half-time, while Scott McTominay made his return following his spell on the sidelines due to heart surgery.

Frosinone showed some threat late on through Giorgi Kvernadze and Tomas Bobcek, but Napoli went on to score a third as De Bruyne tapped in from Giovane's low centre in the fourth minute of stoppage time.
Napoli bounce back with team performance

There was certainly some early pressure mounting on Allegri after Napoli's slow start to the season, but the Partenopei have relieved their head coach with an impressive team display at home after the extended international break.

De Bruyne, Di Lorenzo, Lang, Neres, Hojlund and Giovane all created two chances each as Napoli played on the front foot against their high-flying opponents, while Lang led the way in shots (five) and Neres in attempted dribbles (five).
Napoli also won the expected goals (xG) battle 2.76 to 1.01, albeit with their total boosted by De Bruyne's penalty – the Belgian midfielder was responsible for 1.33 of their total xG.

De Bruyne has carried his form from the international break, during which he directly contributed to three goals (two goals, one assist) in three games, back to Napoli, who face Villarreal next in the Champions League.

17a93nv5v0pw1hjocx7gd3tbn.title: Klopp says Germany can do better after ill-tempered Netherlands draw
17a93nv5v0pw1hjocx7gd3tbn.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's first match in charge of Germany, a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands, was marred by injuries to Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp was satisfied with a point on his debut as Germany's head coach, although he knows his side have plenty more gears to go through after their 1-1 draw with the Netherlands.
Felix Nmecha's 32nd-minute strike put Germany on course for victory against their old rivals on Thursday, on Klopp's eagerly anticipated international debut in the Nations League.

However, two minutes into second-half stoppage time, Cody Gakpo – who played 79 games under Klopp for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – met Ruben van Bommel's outside-of-the-foot cross with a sumptuous volley to snatch a point for the Netherlands.
The Oranje, who were playing their first game under Barcelona great Xavi, utterly dominated the second half, racking up 2.61 expected goals to Germany's 0.24 xG after half-time.
Overall, the Netherlands posted an xG figure of 3.12 from 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 from 10 attempts, while they also had four Opta-defined 'big chances', with Klopp's men having two.

It was the first time the Oranje had created 3.0 xG or greater in a match against a team inside the top 30 of FIFA's world rankings since June 2019, when they had 3.1 in a Nations League semi-final win over England.
Speaking to RTL after full-time, Klopp acknowledged there was plenty for his team to work on ahead of Sunday's matchup with Greece, but his initial assessment was still positive.
"There were lots of things that worked. I'm very satisfied with many individual performances, with the passion as well," he said.
"But we can play better football, for sure. I would have loved to win, but I can live with the point."
Asked if he was nervous ahead of the game, Klopp replied: "I stood there over 1,000 times, so it was quite natural."

A high-octane and at times bad-tempered affair saw the Netherlands have two goals disallowed, with the first – a Virgil van Dijk header that was chalked off for Brian Brobbey backing into Marc-Andre ter Stegen – proving contentious.

And Germany's goal also came with a hint of controversy as Klopp's side played on while Brobbey was down injured, with the Netherlands' players reacting furiously after Nmecha swept into the top-left corner.

Brobbey had to be substituted when the game restarted, and his exit came after Germany striker Kai Havertz also hobbled off, having been on the receiving end of a high tackle from Quinten Timber – the twin brother of his Arsenal team-mate Jurrien.
Germany also lost Jamal Musiala to a thigh issue during the warm-ups, and Klopp is now waiting for updates on both players.
"Unfortunately, this happened to Jamal before the game, then Kai also said he felt it. They are both having an MRI at the moment. I hope we get the diagnosis tonight," he said.
"Of course, it's not great now. I hope it's just nothing bad. The boys are probably out of our next game, but hopefully they'll be ready to play again quite quickly."

17eqhgeq4fs6m1ogej8u1qk6xf.title: Hurzeler thrilled by Brighton's response to Struijk red card
17eqhgeq4fs6m1ogej8u1qk6xf.subtitle: Fabian Hurzeler commended his Brighton side after they overcame Pascal Struijk's second-half red card before defeating Sunderland 2-0.
paragraphs: Fabian Hurzeler was full of praise for his Brighton team after they overcame Pascal Struijk's second-half sending off to beat Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light.
Having brushed aside Arsenal before the international break, Brighton took the lead in the 53rd minute when Maxim De Cuyper was on hand to finish past Robin Roefs.
But just four minutes after going in front, the Seagulls were reduced to 10 men when Struijk was penalised for a last-man foul on Wilson Isidor, following a VAR review.

With over half-an-hour to play with a player down, Brighton showed a steely determination to shut out Sunderland before substitute Jaouen Hadjam scored in the third minute of second-half stoppage time to seal all three points.
Brighton have now won their last three games in the Premier League, while also keeping a clean sheet in four of their six games.
Hurzeler's side remain third in the league table, two points behind leaders Manchester City, who play on Sunday.
On his team's performance, Hurzeler said, "It was a different performance [to the win over Arsenal] because we had difficult circumstances and faced different adversities.
"It was key for us today to have a really good defensive mindset. I feel it was a deserved win and I have to praise my players.
"They really stuck together, faced adversity no matter how hard it was. They did the basics really well and that is so crucial in a game like this, especially when you are one man down."
For Sunderland, they have now suffered their fourth defeat of the league campaign.
In this fixture, the Black Cats mustered an expected goals (xG) of 0.64 from 12 attempts, and will surely feel they should have done better after Brighton were reduced to 10 men.

The result means Sunderland have now lost back-to-back Premier League home games without scoring for the first time since April/May 2017, with this the first time they have lost two of their opening three home matches of a league season since 2017-18 (also L2).

On his side’s defeat, Regis Le Bris said, "It was a disappointing result, to be fair. Think we had several chances in the game. The first half was balanced. It was intense, really tight. We created a few chances, but we lacked quality in the final third."
"We missed composure. Our ideas were good. Our energy, we tried until the end. But we lacked composure at the end."

17ev07xbbdyub1evjo3ro2o0jx.title: Juventus 0-3 Lazio: Gattuso's side deliver statement away victory
17ev07xbbdyub1evjo3ro2o0jx.subtitle: Lazio continued to keep pace with Inter at the top of Serie A, with Gennaro Gattuso's side breezing past a lacklustre Juventus on Sunday.
paragraphs: Lazio's unbeaten start to the Serie A season continued at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday as they delivered a statement performance in their 3-0 win against Juventus.
Having seen Inter pull ahead following their 3-1 win over Bologna on Saturday, Gennaro Gattuso's side joined them on 19 points at the top of the table after a dominant display.
Kerim Alajbegovic, the only change to Juventus' team, fired off the game's first shot in the fifth minute, but his swerving attempt was watched and well held by Christos Mandas.

Juventus then had the ball in the net when Randal Kolo Muani volleyed home, but his joy was short-lived after the offside flag on the far side was raised, with the Frenchman just behind the Lazio defence when Douglas Luiz's deflected effort fell kindly to him.

Lazio had failed to trouble Guglielmo Vicario in the first half, but it was the visitors who took the lead eight minutes before the break. Mattia Zaccagni whipped a dangerous delivery into the box, with Provstgaard glancing his header into the bottom-right corner.
The visitors nearly doubled their advantage in the 44th minute, but Nuno Tavares' shot with his right foot deflected off Juventus captain Bremer and onto the top of the crossbar.

Marco Domenichini, who replaced the suspended Luciano Spalletti in the Juventus dugout, turned to his bench at the break and introduced Nick Woltemade, and the on-loan Newcastle United striker almost made an immediate impact, but he could not force Mandas into action after being picked out by Kolo Muani.

And Juventus were made to pay for that missed chance just after the hour by Isaksen, who, after taking down Nuno Tavares' cross field switch, cut inside Zeki Celik and curled into the bottom-left corner.

The hosts struggled to get themselves back in contention, with Kolo Muani heading over from six yards out, and their misery was compounded in the 89th minute when Fisayo Dele-Bashiru's driving run from inside his own half ended with an arrowed strike into the bottom corner to seal the win.
Danish duo do the damage and pile more misery on Juventus

Lazio have not won the Scudetto since 1999-00 when Sven-Goran Eriksson was at the helm, but their supporters may be daring to dream this season after producing arguably their most complete performance of the campaign so far.

And with their triumph, Gattuso (W6 D1) became the first manager in Serie A history to win six of his first seven games in charge of Lazio in the competition, with Igor Tudor, Tommaso Maestrelli and Vladimir Petkovic only managing to win five of their first seven.

Lazio have also now avoided defeat in each of their first seven matches of a Serie A campaign for the seventh time in their history, though this is the first time they have managed to accumulate six victories at this stage.

They were helped by Provstgaard and Isaksen. Before today, Juventus had only once conceded two goals from two different Danish players in a Serie A match, which came back in October 1949, when Jorgen Leschly Sorensen and Karl Aage Hansen netted for Atalanta.

For Spalletti, there will be plenty to ponder, with Juventus already eight points off leaders Inter. They did, however, win the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 0.78 from their nine attempts, compared to Lazio's 0.53 from the same number of shots.

17krq7bj4h1kr121kdkw5s68ve.title: Seattle Sounders 2-0 Real Salt Lake: Musovski and Rusnak end long winless streak
17krq7bj4h1kr121kdkw5s68ve.subtitle: Seattle Sounders had not tasted victory since mid-May, but they got three points on the board against a struggling Real Salt Lake side.
paragraphs: Seattle Sounders ended their long wait for a win in MLS as they beat Real Salt Lake 2-0 at Lumen Field.
The Sounders had not won a league game since May, but Paul Arriola got two assists to set up Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnak to secure all three points.
Arriola flashed an early shot just wide of the near post and into the side netting after the Sounders cut through RSL's defense.
Cristian Roldan also failed to hit the target, while RSL's only effort of the first half saw Sergi Solans bend a long-range shot well wide of the far post on the stroke of half-time.

But Seattle made a strong start after the break, taking just over two minutes to break the deadlock. Arriola laid it off to Musovski, whose low fizzer trickled past Rafael Cabral into the back of the net.

Solans forced a fine stop out of Andrew Thomas moments later from a tight angle, but Seattle continued to push, with Jordan Morris' effort – which could have been a cross – from the right of the box pushed away by Cabral.
A loose touch from Philip Quinton almost gifted Arriola a goal; the striker rushed onto the ball in the box, but Cabral rushed back to get his foot behind it.
Rusnak made sure of the points with 17 minutes remaining, though, as he was allowed to run through RSL's half before slotting it past Cabral.
Seattle taste victory again
After a strong start to the season, Seattle have slowly been sliding down the Western Conference table after failing to taste victory since a 3-2 win over the San Jose Earthquakes on May 13.

But on Wednesday, they ended a winless run of 13 straight MLS matches (D5 L8). They had lost eight straight before drawing each of their last five – including coming from 3-1 down to earn a point against the Colorado Rapids last time out.

The clear-cut chances were few and far between in the match, with the Sounders accumulating 0.91 expected goals (xG) from their 11 attempts, though four were on target. While RSL had 12 shots (0.43 xG), only two tested Thomas.
Arriola was the driving force, having a joint-game-high three shots and the only 'big' chance of the match, while he also got an assist from both of the chances he created.
While Seattle moved up to 10th in the West, level on points with the Portland Timbers, RSL sit 13th after extending their own winless run to 13 games, having lost each of the last four.

17m3llo12rkmq1obwgma87yxeo.title: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami: Messi free-kick not enough to halt winless run
17m3llo12rkmq1obwgma87yxeo.subtitle: Inter Miami are now winless in five MLS games after falling to a late 2-1 defeat against the Columbus Crew on Sunday.
paragraphs: Jamal Thiare scored a 98th-minute winner for the Columbus Crew in a 2-1 victory over Inter Miami at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.
Lionel Messi cancelled out Josef Martinez's penalty with a brilliant free-kick in the first half, but Thiare snatched a last-gasp winner shortly after Santiago Morales saw red for Miami.
Columbus started on the front foot as Anass Zaroury saw a strike from the edge of the box cannon off the woodwork 10 minutes in, though the Crew would take the lead just before the half-hour mark.
Yannick Bright wrestled with Martinez during a corner, with the latter winning the penalty and dispatching it for his first MLS goal for Columbus.
However, Miami were level just five minutes later as Messi scored a stunning free-kick from the right wing, curling the ball over Patrick Schulte and into the far corner.

17sz9pe33kr6z1gvr1wj1fbhrh.title: Australia 2-4 Brazil: Raphinha and Vinicius score penalties in absorbing Brisbane friendly
17sz9pe33kr6z1gvr1wj1fbhrh.subtitle: Following a 1-1 draw between the teams last Friday, Brazil got the better of Australia in a six-goal thriller to cap their tour Down Under.
paragraphs: Raphinha and Vinicius Junior were both on target from the penalty spot as Brazil beat Australia 4-2 in a thrilling friendly encounter in Brisbane.

Carlo Ancelotti made seven changes to the Selecao lineup that drew 1-1 with the same opponents in Townsville four days prior, but three of those who kept their places – Raphinha, Vinicius and Bruno Guimaraes – got on the scoresheet in an entertaining win.

Brazil had to wait until the 95th minute for Rayan's equaliser on Friday, but they made the breakthrough far quicker this time around as Vanderson's touch sat up perfectly for the full-back to thump a volley across Patrick Beach and in with three minutes gone, after Gabriel Bontempo laid the ball back into his path.
Beach then repelled two efforts from Raphinha as Brazil's furious start threatened to overwhelm Australia, but the hosts grew into the encounter and equalised in the 28th minute.

Connor Metcalfe's inswinging corner somehow travelled all the way through to Alessandro Circati, who hooked his right foot behind him and sent an instinctive flick looping into the far corner. Referee Yusuke Araki initially awarded a foul on Brazil goalkeeper Otavio, but a VAR review led to that decision being overturned.
And the Socceroos were ahead only five minutes later, as a flowing move resulted in Metcalfe exchanging passes with Circati and sending a glorious, 20-yard strike dipping into the top-right corner.
However, Brazil got back on level terms just before half-time, with Raphinha planting his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner after Danilo Santos was tripped by Harry Soutter.

And, after Gabriel Magalhaes' header was kept out by Beach, Guimaraes put Brazil back in front in the 69th minute, sweeping into a gaping net after Vinicius linked up with his Real Madrid team-mate Endrick in the left-hand channel.

Another driving run from Vinicius led to him being felled by Nestory Irankunda, and with Raphinha having been substituted at half-time, the Madrid superstar became the second Brazilian to convert from the spot 10 minutes from time, finally putting the game out of Australia's reach.
Vinicius leads the way, but defensive issues remain for Brazil
Ancelotti's side were far from their free-flowing best at this summer's World Cup, as they were beaten by Norway in the round of 16.
And after Australia came within seconds of upsetting them in the first of two friendly matches between the sides, the Italian came in for more criticism from the Brazilian media.
However, his side looked much brighter in attack on Tuesday, putting up 3.62 expected goals from 18 shots, compared to Australia's 1.65 xG from eight attempts.

Vinicius was at the heart of everything positive about Brazil's play, tallying game-high figures for dribbles attempted (four), touches in the opposition area (seven) and chances created (two, joint with Bontempo).

Brazil still have defensive issues to solve ahead of Saturday's meeting with India, though. This was the first instance of Australia both scoring and conceding multiple goals before half-time in any game since a 2-2 draw with Saudi Arabia in June 2017.
The Socceroos also become just the second team from the AFC confederation to score twice against Brazil in a game in the last 21 years, after Japan beat the Selecao 3-2 last October.

17v4mcaxi0wx41uwfesbmrnwdc.title: Wells urges Colorado to keep showing strength and maturity
17v4mcaxi0wx41uwfesbmrnwdc.subtitle: Colorado Rapids need to get back to winning ways in their playoff push, but Western Conference leaders Vancouver Whitecaps are next up.
paragraphs: Matt Wells was thrilled with the maturity he saw from the Colorado Rapids last time out and is hoping to see more of that when they host the Vancouver Whitecaps in MLS.
The Colorado Rapids sit in the final wildcard spot in the Western Conference but are currently on a five-game winless streak in the league (D4 L1).
They have drawn each of their last three matches, shutting up shop to play out a goalless draw with the Portland Timbers last time out.

It was the Rapids' first clean sheet since their last win, which came against CF Montreal on September 12 (1-0), and Wells is hoping they can rally to another big result to keep their playoff hopes alive.

"There's still too many times in games recently where I've realised we're a little way away from where I want us to get to as a team, just in terms of the stuff I keep alluding to about the strength and the stability of the team in key moments," Wells said.
"We've been too soft, and we've also done a couple of naive things that you guys and other guys could rightfully say was a little bit immature at key moments of the game.
"We were keen to eradicate that [against Portland]. I thought we did that to really good effect. I loved how mature we looked as a group. We looked together. We looked committed."
Vancouver remain top of the West, having returned to winning ways last time out when they edged past Austin FC 2-1.
They were winless in four prior to that match (D3 L1), but Jesper Sorensen is continuing to use these final four games as a chance to fine-tune elements of his team before the playoffs.
"The players look good, and it's now the final time of year," he said. "We have to be ready physically, and we also have to be ready mentally.
"We're a good team, so now we just have to also see if we need to do something before the playoffs in regards to changing it up a little bit or maybe trying some new stuff we haven't done yet."
Colorado Rapids – Paxten Aaronson
Paxten Aaronson has tallied seven goals and nine assists this regular season.
The only other Rapids player to reach those marks in a single season since 2010 is Djordje Mihailovic in 2024 (11 goals, 12 assists).
Vancouver Whitecaps – Brian White
Brian White scored a brace in Vancouver's last meeting with Colorado in April, his fifth and sixth career regular-season goals against the Rapids.
The only teams White has scored more regular-season goals against in his career are St. Louis City SC and Portland Timbers (eight goals).
MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN
Each of the last three meetings between Colorado and Vancouver has resulted in a multi-goal victory for one team, including a 3-1 win by the Whitecaps in April.
Neither team in the series has ever won consecutive matches by multiple goals.
The Rapids' last three matches have been draws after having just three draws in their previous 20 regular-season matches.
It is the first time Colorado have drawn three straight MLS games since April 2023, while the club have not had four straight since doing so in September 2021.
Colorado Rapids – 32.3%
Vancouver Whitecaps – 42.3%
