17wh48u3h3xx2z5rkewiybzp9.title: Yildiz compared to Kvaratskhelia by Juventus boss Spalletti
17wh48u3h3xx2z5rkewiybzp9.subtitle: Luciano Spalletti has compared Juventus youngster Kenan Yildiz to another big-name attacker he coached while at Napoli.
paragraphs: Kenan Yildiz has the unpredictability and "madness of invention" that makes him comparable to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, says Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti.
Juventus went into the international break seventh in a congested Serie A table, having beaten Atalanta 2-0 to bounce back from a 3-2 defeat to Sassuolo.
Yildiz has only made one appearance, totalling 69 minutes, across all competitions this season, after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured metatarsal in August.
The Turkiye international, who is unlikely to return until next month, scored 14 goals and supplied 10 assists last season, leading all Bianconeri players in both categories.
He also created the most chances (100) and both attempted (220) and completed (105) the most dribbles for the Turin giants, leading Spalletti to compare him to another tricky attacker he has managed.

Spalletti worked with Kvaratskhelia – now a two-time Champions League winner with Paris Saint-Germain – in 2022-23 after the Georgian first joined Napoli, and he provided 14 goals and 14 assists that season as the Partenopei won the Scudetto.
"Yildiz makes football shine," Spalletti told Tuttosport. "His every move is ingenious and breaks the system.
"When he starts, even he doesn't necessarily have a plan of what he'll do next. Sometimes, in training, I see the defenders predict his movement, and they still can't stop him.
"He has the madness of invention. For me, he is comparable to Kvaratskhelia.
"He needs to play a bit more, but I see similarities in the unpredictability, the way he stays outside of the rules and timing you expect in football.
"He's a lovely guy, the boy next door type, but also a leader – one that doesn't need to talk much."
Juventus return to action following the extended international break next Sunday, as they visit a Cagliari side that currently sit one point above them in the table.

17y7t7f444xak1dh65qfruca6b.title: LAFC sack Dos Santos amid MLS struggles
17y7t7f444xak1dh65qfruca6b.subtitle: After just one win across their last 10 MLS games, Los Angeles FC have sacked head coach Marc Dos Santos ahead of an important run.
paragraphs: Los Angeles FC have sacked head coach Marc Dos Santos after a poor run of form in MLS.

Dos Santos was appointed to the role in December 2025 after serving as an assistant under previous boss Steve Cherundolo, but has been relieved of his duties after just 38 games in charge across all competitions.
The 49-year-old won 17 of his 38 games at the helm (D11 L10), with his 44.7% win rate the lowest of any LAFC head coach since their first match in 2018 (Cherundolo – 53.9%, Bob Bradley – 47.2%).
LAFC made a strong start to the 2026 season, but have fallen to sixth in the Western Conference after just one win across their last 10 games in the league (D5 L4).

The Black and Gold are now closer to eighth-place rivals LA Galaxy (five points) than they are to conference leader Vancouver Whitecaps (nine points), and they are very much at risk of missing out on home-field advantage for the play-offs.
With just six games to go before the postseason, LAFC have decided to part ways with Dos Santos.

“Marc has given a great deal to this club over the years, and we are grateful for his commitment, care and contributions to LAFC. We wish Marc and his family all the best moving forward," said John Thorrington, LAFC's president of soccer operations.
After the international break, LAFC host Vancouver and Austin FC before a trip to New York City FC.
The club are yet to name an interim boss, despite the play-offs now looming on the horizon.

18217lohamyel1k5rtcqbrvn2x.title: Hallgrimsson says rotation has kept Ireland fresh for Israel rematch
18217lohamyel1k5rtcqbrvn2x.subtitle: Ireland end their extended international break with a rematch against Israel, and Heimir Hallgrimsson believes his players are ready to go.
paragraphs: Heimir Hallgrimsson hopes his policy of shuffling Ireland's pack will ensure his players are raring to go when they face Israel in their final game of the international break on Sunday.

Ireland sit third in Nations League Group B3 with four points from their opening three games, having lost 1-0 to Kosovo, beaten Israel 3-0, then squandered a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 with Austria on Thursday.
Troy Parrott scored twice for the Boys in Green last time out, with the first of his goals being an exceptional solo effort.

Parrott's four braces for Ireland are the most by any player aged under 25 for the country, surpassing Robbie Keane's three, and the Real Betis forward has nine goals in his last six competitive internationals overall.

He was one of several big names to be withdrawn by Hallgrimsson in the latter stages of Thursday's game, allowing Austria to play their way into the contest, but the 59-year-old insists those changes were necessary in order to keep everyone fresh for their next match.
"We need to think about this as a four-game window. Like we said in the beginning, we will rotate and we have been using our squad really well in these games," he said.
"We were always thinking about more than just that [Austria] game, but not on purpose – we didn't want to lose two goals in the end.
"But obviously, we had to think about the fact we are playing another game, both for players to avoid injuries and to be fit and fresh."

Ireland's draw with Austria was interrupted by protests relating to the staging of this Sunday's fixture – which will take place on neutral ground in Backa Topola, Serbia – and Hallgrimsson admits the extra scrutiny his team have faced during recent days has taken its toll.
But he hopes the experience of coming through a tough period will benefit Ireland in the long run.
"Surviving this camp, coming out of it together as one would be a massive win for me. That is coming from my heart," he said.
"After everything this team has gone through, the criticism, surviving as a group after this game would be a big win for me.
"As a coach, obviously having another three points would probably be more than I could have asked for before the camp, knowing what was to come.
"The most pleasing thing has been the togetherness and what they have done for each other. This bond of brothers will be stronger than others. All the obstacles we face in the future will be less."

1895zg3p13emw1j2px21t4kn7r.title: Venezia 1-0 Napoli: Hosts earn first Serie A win after De Bruyne penalty miss
1895zg3p13emw1j2px21t4kn7r.subtitle: The pressure continues to mount on Massimiliano Allegri after his Napoli side suffered a shock defeat to bottom-of-the-table Venezia.
paragraphs: Napoli's stuttering start to their Serie A campaign continued on Saturday as Kevin De Bruyne's penalty miss proved costly in a 1-0 defeat to Venezia at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.
Venezia came into the game as the only team in the division yet to register a point, but they took the lead in the 49th minute when Akor Adams found a way past Alex Meret.
De Bruyne then saw his penalty saved by Filip Stankovic in the second half, and despite dominating the closing stages, they could not find a way past the Venezia goalkeeper.

Massimiliano Allegri made five changes to the team that beat Frosinone last time out, and those alterations made for a disjointed opening as Adams' bouncing shot was saved by Meret before John Yeboah saw his attempt go well wide.
But Venezia needed Ridgeciano Haps to be in the right place at the right time to clear Amir Rrahmani's effort off the line, with Scott McTominay's deflected shot then looping over.

However, the hosts took the lead four minutes after the restart through Adams, who saw his strike deflect off Rrahmani and past Meret after the Napoli defender failed to deal with Simon Sohm's hopeful ball over the top.

Allegri responded by making a triple substitution, with De Bruyne, Alisson Santos and Rasmus Hojlund thrown on, and the latter almost made an immediate impact, but Juan Jesus brilliantly cleared Santos' cross off the line with the Dane lurking in the box.
Napoli were then handed a glorious chance to draw level in the 66th minute when Matias Moreno chopped down Hojlund in the area, but De Bruyne's spot-kick was superbly kept out by Stankovic.

Stankovic provided more heroics to ensure Venezia's first league win since returning to Serie A. He first clawed Stanislav Lobotka's shot from distance behind before he got down low to repel Matteo Politano, with Santos also seeing an effort cleared off the line by Haps as the hosts held on for a memorable win.
Venezia get up and running to pile pressure on Allegri

Coming into Saturday's clash, Venezia had lost all of their first six Serie A matches of the season for only the second time, after 1949-50 while also failing to win their last four top-flight matches at home, but they delivered a battling display to get their first points on the board.

Adams' strike saw Venezia score against Napoli in Serie A for the first time in eight attempts, and it was their first win over the Partenopei since a 4-1 victory at the Stadio Pier  Luigi Penzo all the way back in March 1942.

Napoli, meanwhile, suffered their first defeat against a newly-promoted side in their eighth such match. They have now just taken one point from their last three away league games, last having a longer run between February and April 2025 (D4 L1).

18clvcnhr77r1xk4i28xsje2p.title: Napoli 'need to find solutions to the problems', says Allegri
18clvcnhr77r1xk4i28xsje2p.subtitle: Napoli have struggled under Massimiliano Allegri so far this season, but face bottom side Venezia next in Serie A.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri believes Napoli "need to find solutions" to their early-season woes ahead of their trip to Venezia.
Napoli are eighth in Serie A after winning just 10 points from their opening six games, already seeing them six points adrift of leaders Inter.
The Partenopei have also lost their two Champions League matches this season, most recently losing 3-1 against Villarreal on Tuesday.

Napoli have picked up just one point in their last two away league games (a defeat against Inter and a draw against Fiorentina); the last time they went on a run of at least three away Serie A matches without a win was between February and April 2025 (D4 L1).
While Allegri insisted he is not overly concerned about their struggles, the Napoli boss acknowledged solutions are needed.
"I'm not concerned; we need to find solutions to the problems," Allegri insisted.
"We need to manage the ball better at certain points in the match and then deal better with unexpected incidents which can happen.
"When a team is strong, even during difficult moments, and there are opponents to consider too, your world cannot fall apart. Once that moment has passed, we still have plenty of time to improve.
"We just need to work, get all the players back and available, and manage playing every three days. We need everyone.

"Unfortunately, we have lost [David] Neres again, as he has been struggling with these injuries, but [Antonio] Vergara and [Constantino] Favasuli are progressing well. They are not close to returning yet, but they are making progress.
"We also have [Scott] McTominay and others who need to regain fitness by playing, because a match is completely different."
Venezia are bottom of Serie A heading into this fixture, having lost all six of their league matches this season.
Venezia – Antoine Hainaut
No defender has been involved in more goals than Antoine Hainaut (two goals, one assist) in Serie A this season (three), level with Hassane Kamara, Nuno Tavares and Ricardo Mangas.
The 24-year-old has also delivered the most open-play crosses (35) in the current campaign, at least 11 more than any other player.
Napoli – Kevin De Bruyne

After his brace against Frosinone, Kevin De Bruyne could score in two consecutive league appearances for the first time in four years, since October 2022 (in the Premier League for Manchester City against Brighton and Leicester City).
The Belgian has been involved in seven goals in 10 appearances (five goals, two assists) since the start of August for club and country in all competitions.
MATCH PREDICTION: NAPOLI WIN

Napoli are unbeaten in 14 of their 16 Serie A matches against Venezia (W7 D7 L2), avoiding defeat in all of the last 10 (W6 D4); Venezia's last top-flight victory against Napoli was on 8th March 1942 (4-1 at the Penzo).

Napoli have won all of their last seven Serie A matches against newly promoted sides, with a combined score of 18-2. They have also kept eight clean sheets in their last nine such games, including in each of their last five.

However, there has been great balance in the eight Serie A matches played at the Penzo between Venezia and Napoli, with two wins apiece and four draws – including the most recent encounter (0-0 in March 2025).
Nevertheless, Venezia have lost all of their first six Serie A matches of the season for only the second time, after 1949-50.

So far, only three teams have lost all of their first seven matches in a single top-flight campaign in the competition's history: Benevento in 2017-18, Legnano in 1951-52 and Venezia in 1949-50 – Venezia could become the first team to record this negative record twice.

18ekcxxline8m1lwvvl94uc6bd.title: Former Man Utd players could 'help more' instead of criticising, says Ten Hag
18ekcxxline8m1lwvvl94uc6bd.subtitle: Manchester United have faced heavy criticism from their former players, and Erik ten Hag thinks a more positive approach could work.
paragraphs: Former Manchester United boss Erik ten Hag believes former players turned pundits could find ways to help the club more instead of giving heavy criticism.
Ten Hag led United between May 2022 and October 2024, winning the EFL Cup and FA Cup during his tenure.
He took charge of 128 games in all competitions, winning 70 of those (D23 L35), leaving the club with a 54.7% win rate.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag has spoken about how he felt Cristiano Ronaldo "let the team down" after their public fallout, and how he felt the club broke promises to him surrounding the transfer market.
And the Dutchman has now highlighted that he feels the club's former players, who were part of United's rich history, speak out without having a full understanding.
"It's everywhere the same; they always want to protect their legacies," Ten Hag told The Athletic.
"It's no different than Bayern Munich or Ajax; they do the same. But they are [part of United's] history, and they do not always know what's going on. Football evolves.
"For United, it's clear: they had great contributions; they achieved massive results, trophies for the club and for themselves, so I respect them."

The former United players who regularly pass comment on the club are Gary Neville, Roy Keane, Rio Ferdinand, Paul Scholes and Wayne Rooney – all players who were hugely successful during the Alex Ferguson era.

Keane and Neville have passed judgement this term, with the former labelling United a "circus" following Lisandro Martinez's outburst after the loss to Atletico Madrid, while the latter was heavily critical of their second-half performance against Fulham.
While Ten Hag noted the players can get frustrated by the pundits' comments, he himself enjoyed a good relationship with them while he was at Old Trafford.
"I have to say, I had a very good relationship with them all, with Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand," Ten Hag added.

"I did nice interviews with them both, so it didn't hurt me. Of course, they have podcasts; they have their models. Sometimes it's difficult for players. Some of them get affected by it, get annoyed by it.

"They achieved massive successes. But also, they can help the club more, help the players more. There should be two ways that they support it. But I think always the thing you most love, you most criticise."

18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.title: Ter Stegen says Klopp call-up was extra special following injury woes
18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.subtitle: Marc-Andre ter Stegen has already been named as Jurgen Klopp's Germany number one, after more than a year in the international wilderness.
paragraphs: Marc-Andre ter Stegen says being named as Jurgen Klopp's first-choice goalkeeper for Germany was extra special, following his well-documented injury issues.

Germany will face the Netherlands in their first match under Klopp on Thursday, in the Nations League, with further games against Greece (home and away) and Serbia to come during this international break.
And, with Manuel Neuer retiring from international football in the aftermath of Germany's shock round-of-32 World Cup defeat to Paraguay, the former Liverpool boss had to name a new number one.
Despite calling up Besiktas' Alexander Nubel, Bayern Munich's Jonas Urbig, Eintracht Frankfurt's Noah Atubolu and Augsburg's Finn Dahmen, he has gone with the experience of Ter Stegen.
The most recent of Ter Stegen's 44 caps came against France in the previous edition of the Nations League in June 2025, with injuries restricting his gametime in recent years.
He only made 10 appearances across all competitions combined in 2024-25 and 2025-26, for parent club Barcelona and Girona, who he joined on loan for the second half of last season.
But, after starting eight straight games for his latest loan club, Ajax, Ter Stegen is excited to be back on the international stage.

"It's always something special for me, to be here again now," he told Sky Sport DE. "Especially if you had a time when things didn't go the way you imagined, when your body wasn't by your side, then of course, you appreciate it all the more.

"I believe that I have worked a lot to make this happen again. I'm also looking forward to meeting many new faces, some old friends who are here, and just to start again and give our best for the team.
"There's a smile on my face. I'm just happy to be 100% back, to be able to be with the national team and hopefully play successful football. That is the wish of all of us."

Klopp takes charge of his country after overseeing 674 games in the Bundesliga and the Premier League, across wildly successful spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool. That is more games in Europe's top five leagues than any previous Germany head coach had tallied before taking the job.
Ter Stegen said of Klopp: "He's one of one, as you know, with the joy he conveys and his interest in football, the enthusiasm he has for his own football.
"I don't think you need to say anything. I think everyone knows him and everyone knows how much he lives and feels football."

Klopp is one of only three bosses – alongside Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti – to have won the Bundesliga and Premier League titles, and he became famed for his "heavy metal" style of play with both Dortmund and Liverpool.

But Ter Stegen knows adopting that way of playing will be a learning curve for Germany, adding: "There are issues he would like to tackle, because he has his way of seeing football and understanding football. We have to try to internalise that as quickly as possible.

"For the time being, there are smaller levers that can and must be pulled, to then get into his philosophy. We want to play great football from the start, to defend not through individual actions, but really through the collective.
"We have very few training sessions to talk a lot about gameplan and so on, so we will keep it relatively simple now. We have to be attentive and implement that as quickly as possible."

18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.title: Branthwaite hopes injury issues are behind him following England recall
18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.subtitle: Injuries have restricted Jarrad Branthwaite to just one senior cap for England, but he will hope to add to that tally in the next two weeks.
paragraphs: Jarrad Branthwaite hopes he is back in the England setup for good after missing Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, having earned a recall to the Three Lions' squad.
Branthwaite has been named in Thomas Tuchel's group for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (who they face both home and away) and Croatia.

He has been an ever-present for Everton so far this season, helping the Toffees keep three clean sheets in five games and concede the joint-fewest goals in the Premier League (three, alongside Leeds United).

Branthwaite won his only senior England cap to date in June 2024, when he was named in Gareth Southgate's preliminary Euro 2024 squad and appeared in a friendly against Bosnia-Herzegovina, only to miss out on the final party.
The 24-year-old also missed this summer's World Cup after an injury-hit 2025-26 season, in which he was restricted to just 10 Premier League appearances and seven starts.

But, having visited a specialist in Germany in a bid to combat his persistent hamstring issues during the off-season, Branthwaite hopes he can now challenge Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa for an England starting spot.
"Being out for such a long time with injury didn't help, missing three or four of the camps and missing a lot of football," Branthwaite said of his England struggles.
"My aim is to stay injury-free and play as many games as I can and keep giving myself the best possible chance to be in the squad.
"I've not spoken to him [Tuchel] recently. When we get there, we'll have a chat. I can't wait to join up with the squad and enjoy the couple of weeks.

"It is a proud moment. In the last season or so, it has been a target of mine when I've been out to get back playing and give myself the best possible chance of being in and around the England squad after missing a length of time.
"The season has started well individually and as a team and that has definitely helped. I believe I am good enough to be in the England squad, so hopefully I can show that."

Branthwaite, Guehi, Konsa, Jarell Quansah and Trevoh Chalobah are the centre-backs in England's group for this international break, with their Nations League opener against world champions Spain taking place at Wembley on Saturday.
England have won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their last five without conceding.
Only once before have the Three Lions won six competitive home fixtures to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
However, Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation.

18n2lw269uf0h1udau4n91ijqo.title: 'Inferior' Juventus beginning to worry Spalletti after defeat to Lazio
18n2lw269uf0h1udau4n91ijqo.subtitle: Juventus' indifferent start to their Serie A campaign continued on Sunday against Lazio, and Luciano Spalletti expressed his concern.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti said he saw an "inferior" Juventus team during Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Lazio, adding that he was surprised with the performance his side produced.
Spalletti was not in the dugout at the Allianz Stadium because of a touchline ban, with Marco Domenichini overseeing the match, but he was unable to inspire Juventus to victory.
Oliver Provstgaard headed Lazio in front with 37 minutes on the clock before Gustav Isaksen doubled the visitors' advantage with a fine finish in the 66th minute.
The win was sealed by an excellent run and finish from Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, with the result seeing Gennaro Gattuso's side go back level on points with league leaders Inter.

Juventus, however, find themselves eight points off the pace after just seven matches, while also losing by at least three goals against Lazio in Serie A for the first time since a 4-1 defeat at the Olimpico on March 18, 2001.
The Bianconeri have also lost two of their last five home league games (W2 D1), as many defeats as they recorded in their previous 44 such matches (W24 D18).

Spalletti's side have accumulated just 11 points from their first seven Serie A games, failing to surpass that mark after the first seven games for the third time in the last 11 seasons, after 2021-22 (11 points) and 2022-23 (10).
"It was certainly an inferior Juventus, a team that did not control the game, nor have ideas on where to take the game," Spalletti confessed to DAZN Italia.
"It's hard to explain it even to ourselves, because we returned at 4am on Friday from Vigo, then let the players recover with the physical performance staff.
"We tried to change a few things. There were six new players, but we were slow both in legs and mind.
"In football, you can see the opponents, you can see the ball, and if you are too slow to react, show no heart or rhythm, tactics and systems become irrelevant."

Following the full-time whistle, the Juventus players were jeered off by their supporters, with Lazio beating the Bianconeri by at least three goals away from home in Serie A for only the third time in their history, after a 3-0 win in May 1995 and a 3-0 win in March 1964.
Juventus created very little in the final third, accumulating an expected goals (xG) total of just 0.74 from their nine shots, and only two of those tested Christos Mandas.

"Without tempo, without ideas, without running, without the desire to work hard, and when there is fragility in duels, letting heads drop when things aren't working, those are all things I did not like," Spalletti added.
"The important thing is to show a reaction, not abandon yourself to events. Our careers aren't just down to luck, we've got to fight for those opportunities.
"We are forced to learn that lesson. There are youngsters today who fight and others who let themselves fall down at the first stumble, but every person has a different character."
Juventus' 11 points are one fewer than they had at this stage of last season under Igor Tudor, while Thiago Motta had amassed 13 after seven games in his brief stint in charge.

18n5oxcxc50j91x41apfd1dfdf.title: Nuno laments West Ham's wasted chances after late penalty miss against QPR
18n5oxcxc50j91x41apfd1dfdf.subtitle: West Ham missed the chance to leapfrog Swansea City to the top of the Championship after being held to a 1-1 draw by QPR.
paragraphs: Nuno Espirito Santo rued West Ham's missed chances as a late penalty save denied them the chance to go top of the Championship.
West Ham came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw with QPR at London Stadium on Friday.

A slow West Ham start was punished in the 18th minute as QPR were awarded a controversial penalty; Tomas Soucek – making his first appearance of the season – gave the ball away and recovered possession just outside the box, but the referee awarded a spot-kick.
Nicolas Madsen coolly guided his penalty into the bottom-right corner, sending Mads Hermansen the wrong way.
West Ham got their equaliser in the 70th minute, with Jarrod Bowen scoring on the rebound after his initial shot was blocked.

And he had the chance to snatch all three points at the death after Amadou Mbengue tugged back Pablo, but Charles got down sharply to push Bowen's penalty away before hopping up to tip Arne Engels' follow-up header against the post.
West Ham would have leapfrogged Swansea City to the top of the Championship with a win but will now be looking over their shoulders during the rest of the weekend's action.
"We started well, but the first half was not good; the second half was better. We had chances to win the game," Nuno told Sky Sports.
"We expect much more; we have the quality to do much better.
"QPR are a good side, well-organised, good players, but everyone who saw the game will think there was one team who deserved to win the game.
"Two points got away; let's try to perform better and get a better result."
On Bowen's penalty miss, he added: "Credit to the keeper; it was two incredible saves."
Soucek, playing for the first time since recovering from an ankle injury sustained at the World Cup, was seen with a look of disbelief on his face after the QPR penalty was awarded.
And in his post-match interview, he revealed the referee admitted he had made the wrong decision.
"It's tough to take; I am disappointed," Soucek told Sky Sports. "I was so happy I won the challenge; from my perspective, it's a massive mistake.
"I saw it [afterwards] inside, and it's even worse than I thought, but I can't change that.
"I asked to speak to [the referee], but he wouldn't speak – after the game, he told me he was wrong."
Charles impressed for QPR, having the second-most touches (55) and making four saves, helping the team earn a point that moved them up to fifth in the table.
"It's just a blur," he said. "I work on it every day, and it paid off at the end of the day, and I'm just happy to get the point.
"I'm on a bit of a roll at the minute, but it can change at any point, so I have to stay focused."

18peoe8y2r0xd1je13e4vmvraa.title: Kompany relishing derby test after Augsburg's 'flying start'
18peoe8y2r0xd1je13e4vmvraa.subtitle: Augsburg and Bayern Munich are both currently in the Bundesliga's top four as they look to build on strong starts at WWK Arena.
paragraphs: Vincent Kompany is excited for Bayern Munich's derby against Augsburg and expects a tough test after their opponents' "flying start" to the Bundesliga season.
Augsburg currently sit fourth in the table with seven points, having seen their unbeaten start (W2 D1) ended by a 3-2 loss to Werder Bremen before the international break.
They are just three points behind Bayern, who are still unbeaten after three wins and a draw, though the champions are not top of the pile after four games.
Borussia Dortmund have a 100% record and play on Friday, meaning they could have a five-point lead over Kompany's side by the time they kick off on Saturday.

This is the first of nine fixtures in all competitions between the two international breaks for Bayern, but Kompany is relishing the challenges ahead of his side in the coming weeks, starting with Augsburg.
"It's a very important match; we lost one Bundesliga game last year, and that was against Augsburg," Kompany said.
"It's still a derby, and it's an away fixture. What sets Augsburg apart is that they're very compact and can be very dangerous on the ball.
"They've got a lot of individual qualities – more than people sometimes realise. They've made a flying start to the season. It's a derby; the fans are looking forward to it, and so are we.
"We've got the squad for it [the busy schedule]. We want to go into every match with 100% conviction.

"I'd rather play every three days than have a long break. The players want to play anyway. We have to beat Magdeburg in the cup – it's like a final. But we also want to put in convincing performances in all the other competitions."
Bayern will be without Jamal Musiala for the trip to Augsburg as he continues to recover from a small muscle tear.
It is another setback for Musiala in a season that has already been stop-start, but Kompany is confident he will come back even stronger than before.
"I can relate to his story of setbacks; I've experienced that often in my own career," Kompany said of Musiala.
"Coming back from that is a great strength. I hope he can happily go on playing over the next few years. But when you make a strong comeback, it's something that stays with you for life.
"The team is always delighted when he scores goals. He'll keep doing that, no doubt about it."
Augsburg – Fabian Rieder

Rieder is one of only three players to have recorded a goal involvement in each of the first four Bundesliga matchdays of the 2026-27 season; with three assists, he has already equalled his total from the previous Bundesliga campaign.
Only one Augsburg player has managed a goal involvement in five consecutive Bundesliga games in the last 10 years – Florian Niederlechner in autumn 2019.
Bayern Munich – Harry Kane
In his 98th Bundesliga appearance, Harry Kane scored his 100th and 101st goals in the German top-flight – a new record, as no other player has reached their first 100 Bundesliga goals in fewer games.
With his next Bundesliga goal, he will equal Dieter Hoeness in sixth place on Bayern's all-time Bundesliga goalscoring list (102 goals).
MATCH PREDICTION: BAYERN MUNICH WIN
Bayern lost their last Bundesliga home game against Augsburg 1-2 in January this year.

However, Bayern have won 11 of their 15 away Bundesliga matches against Augsburg (D1 L3) – it is their highest away win percentage against any side they have faced at least 10 times in the top flight (73%).

Augsburg have lost only one of their last 14 Bundesliga home games (W7 D6), a 5-2 defeat against Stuttgart in March. Excluding promoted and relegated teams, only Bayern have lost as few home games as Augsburg (one) since the beginning of November 2025 in the competition.

Bayern, meanwhile, have lost just one of their last 47 league games (against Augsburg in January). On the road, they are unbeaten in 28 matches (W21 D7) – only once have they had a longer unbeaten away streak (33 games between 2012 and 2014).
Only Eintracht Frankfurt have spent more time in a winning position in the Bundesliga this season (257 minutes) than Augsburg (227). Bayern, though, have not trailed for a single minute.
Bayern Munich – 74.8%

18petm1hkar6b1rbksshdq85kg.title: Atletico Madrid 1-0 Deportivo: Alvarez ends LaLiga goal drought
18petm1hkar6b1rbksshdq85kg.subtitle: Atletico Madrid extended their winning run in LaLiga to six games after Julian Alvarez secured all three points against Deportivo.
paragraphs: Julian Alvarez ended his goal drought in LaLiga as Atletico Madrid defeated Deportivo A Coruna 1-0 at Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

The Argentina international's strike early in the second half was enough for Diego Simeone's side to secure a sixth consecutive victory in the competition, moving them two points behind leaders Barcelona ahead of Sunday's Clasico.

Deportivo put Jan Oblak under some early pressure, with the Atleti goalkeeper keeping out Miguel Loureiro's header in the sixth minute, while Alvarez and Pablo Barrios failed to trouble Leo Roman at the other end with their shots.

The best chance in the first half was created by Deportivo, but after Oblak spilt Yeremay Hernandez's initial effort, the shot-stopper reacted quickly to deny Lorenzo Amatucci on the rebound with his feet.

Atleti made the most of that reprieve as they took the lead in the 48th minute. Alejandro Grimaldo burst into the left side of the box and drilled a low cross into the six-yard box, with Alvarez able to finish on the stretch.

Giuliano Simeone could not get enough power behind his header to beat Roman, but Deportivo saw a huge chance go begging as Kevin Sanchez shot straight at Oblak from four yards out with the final kick of the game.
Alvarez back to his best?
After assisting Atleti's winner against Espanyol last time out in LaLiga, Alvarez also scored their only goal in a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in the Champions League during the week.
His strike against Stuttgart was his first for the club this season, while his goal against Deportivo was his first in LaLiga since February 28, when he netted the winner against Real Oviedo.

It is also the first time he has scored in back-to-back games since finding the back of the net in the Copa del Rey final against Real Sociedad and in the Champions League semi-final first leg against Arsenal in the Champions League last season.

The forward is still getting back to his best after a turbulent summer, during which he publically pushed for a move to LaLiga rivals Barcelona, but he is slowly working his way back into the good books of the Atleti faithful.
In this match, he recorded more shots than any Atleti player (three), while also creating the most chances (five) and completing three of his five dribbles - a tally only bettered by Lee Kang-in.
Simeone would have hoped for a stronger team performance, with Atleti losing the expected goals (xG) battle 1.36 to 1.95, but he cannot complain with six league wins on the bounce.

18pkmhpejjmj1m9x31elqf7dv.title: Dortmund will live up to their own standards in Der Klassiker, says Kovac
18pkmhpejjmj1m9x31elqf7dv.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich's clash on Saturday sees the top two in the Bundesliga face off in an enthralling Klassiker.
paragraphs: Niko Kovac knows Borussia Dortmund must play at an extremely high level if they are to beat Bayern Munich, but he was adamant his team have their own standards to live up to.
Dortmund sit second in the Bundesliga, behind Bayern on goal difference, ahead of Saturday's Klassiker at Allianz Arena.
This will be the 141st competitive meeting between the rivals since the formation of the Bundesliga, the most-played fixture in German professional football.

Bayern have suffered more defeats against Dortmund than any other opponent in professional football (33); however, they have lost only one of their last 17 meetings (W13 D3 L1), a 0-2 home defeat in March 2024.
And Kovac, whose team sealed a last-gasp DFB-Pokal win over Werder Bremen on Tuesday, knows the scale of the challenge facing Dortmund.
"This certainly makes things a lot more exciting than in recent years," said former Bayern boss Kovac.
"But that doesn’t make it any easier, because Bayern is undoubtedly the best of the best. Not just in Germany, but also in Europe.
"We have to play at the very highest level. But we're BVB, we have our own standards, and we intend to live up to them."
Bayern and Dortmund are the only two teams remaining unbeaten in the 2026-27 Bundesliga season (W5 D2 each).

In two of the last three Bundesliga seasons, Bayern have handed BVB their first defeat of the campaign, winning 2-1 in Munich on matchday seven last season and 4-0 in Dortmund on matchday 10 in 2023-24.
Bayern's Michael Olise has recorded at least one goal and one assist in three of his last four Bundesliga appearances, as many as in his previous 23 league games combined.
Olise's nine goal involvements (six goals, three assists) in the 2026-27 Bundesliga are the joint-most in the league, level with team-mate Harry Kane, who on Monday won the Ballon d'Or.
"There's no need to say a word about him," replied Kovac when quizzed on Kane.
"The mere fact that he received [the Ballon d'Or] says everything about him. He was already a top player in England. To take another leap forward now is sensational."

18rnum92f8coc1wvv0ng62ge4b.title: Milan goalkeeper Maignan defends himself after red card
18rnum92f8coc1wvv0ng62ge4b.subtitle: After a humbling defeat to Bournemouth in the Europa League, AC Milan are looking to bounce back in Serie A against Udinese.
paragraphs: Mike Maignan defended his actions after receiving a red card in AC Milan's Europa League defeat to Bournemouth.
The goalkeeper was shown a red card in the first half after pushing Tyler Adams in the face, with the Rossoneri going 3-0 down at Vitality Stadium.
Milan's Serie A form, on the other hand, has been better as they remain unbeaten after seven games, with a trip to Udinese up next.

Ruben Amorim is the third manager to remain unbeaten in each of his first seven Serie A games with Milan, after Hector Puricelli in 1955 (unbeaten in his first eight) and Luis Carniglia in 1963 (unbeaten in his first 13).

Milan could go unbeaten in their first eight league games of a season for the third time in the last 20 Serie A seasons, after 2020-21 and 2021-22, though Maignan felt the need to explain his actions after being sent off in Europe.
"My action was not intentional. Like every goalkeeper in every match, I wanted to make space for myself in my area," Maignan explained on Instagram.
"Unfortunately, this gave off a bad image, especially in front of the young supporters who watch us.
"The club, the staff and my team-mates know what sort of person I am. They know my intentions and abandoning them is never part of the plan.
"As for the rest, we are accustomed to the interpretations given by certain people and certain media outlets."
Udinese, meanwhile, are 16th in Serie A after winning just four points from their seven games.

Udinese have lost five of their seven Serie A games this season (W1 D1); only three times in their history in the competition have they registered more defeats in their first eight league games: in 1960-61 (six), in 1961-62 (seven) and in 2017-18 (six).
Udinese – Jurgen Ekkelenkamp
Ekkelenkamp has only scored and assisted in the same Serie A match once, which was back in April against Milan.
The Udinese player, who is yet to score at home in the current Serie A season, is the midfielder with the second-most shots attempted in the competition (20), fewer only than Nico Paz (35).
AC Milan – Adrien Rabiot
Rabiot has scored or assisted in each of his last four Serie A appearances (three goals, two assists).

18t5sflp7wkw1042382wl9t50.title: Klopp not anticipating more titles following Man City verdict
18t5sflp7wkw1042382wl9t50.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool were one of the teams that ran Manchester City close in several Premier League title races.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp is not readying himself to receive more titles retrospectively in the wake of Manchester City's guilty verdict.
It was confirmed on Tuesday that an independent commission had found Man City guilty on the vast majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.
The charges, which were made in 2023, relate to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.
It has been found that City's breach amounted to around £900m.
During the period in question, City won three Premier League titles. However, it also paved the way for what was to come under Pep Guardiola.
In 2018-19, City won their fourth Premier League crown, and their second under Guardiola, by finishing one point ahead of Klopp's Liverpool.
That sparked a thrilling rivalry between City and the Reds, with Liverpool winning the title in 2020 and pushing Guardiola's juggernaut close again in 2022.

With a plethora of punishments open to the commission at an upcoming sanctions hearing, there has been a suggestion City could have titles stripped, but Klopp is not expecting to receive a retrospective winners' medal.
"I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course," said the Germany boss.

"Should any sanctions be imposed, I naturally have nothing to do with it anyway, and that's why I'm waiting to see how things pan out. But when you're talking about legal proceedings that have been going on for so long now, I assume there will be an appeal or something like that? That will take ages again of course.
"So I'm a long way from preparing myself for it in any way and I don't have any feelings about it."
City insist they are innocent and are expected to appeal the verdict.
Their next Premier League outing is against Liverpool at Anfield on October 11.

18wa22x9ciuea1k1fgkud5wunp.title: Muller extends Vancouver stay through 2027 MLS Sprint Season
18wa22x9ciuea1k1fgkud5wunp.subtitle: After helping the Vancouver Whitecaps reach their first MLS Cup final last season, Thomas Muller has extended his stay in Canada.
paragraphs: Thomas Muller has extended his contract with the Vancouver Whitecaps through to the end of the 2027 MLS Sprint Season.
The 37-year-old's previous deal was set to expire this December, but he will now remain with the 2026 MLS Cup runners-up until June 2027.
Muller has scored 19 goals and provided 12 assists in 45 appearances for the Whitecaps since joining as a free agent in the summer of 2025.
Since his arrival, Muller leads Vancouver players in direct goal contributions (27 – 16 goals, 11 assists) in MLS.
During his first campaign, Vancouver reached the MLS Cup showpiece for the first time, though they lost to Lionel Messi's Inter Miami, while they won the Canadian Championship.
The Whitecaps are leading the Western Conference this season, with Muller named an MLS All-Star earlier in the year.
"I've really enjoyed my time here from the beginning," Muller told the club website.
"Vancouver has been very open and welcoming to me, and I've felt that same spirit throughout the club.

"We have an offensive, possession-based style that is fun to play and fun to watch, and you can really feel the excitement around the team and the city right now. The fans are enjoying it, and I think everyone wants to be part of what we are building.
"For me, it's still so much fun to be out on the pitch every week, and I feel good physically.
"I'm very happy to continue this journey with the 'Caps, and I'm looking forward to what we can achieve together this year and next year in the Sprint Season."

18wegcewub9z31dk43zs2dzanu.title: Inter Miami 2-0 New York City FC: Messi and company book playoff spot
18wegcewub9z31dk43zs2dzanu.subtitle: German Berterame and Rodrigo De Paul were on target as Inter Miami beat New York City FC to confirm their place in the postseason.
paragraphs: Inter Miami rubber-stamped their place in the MLS Cup Playoffs with a 2-0 victory over New York City FC at Nu Stadium.
First-half goals from German Berterame and Rodrigo De Paul were enough for the Herons to get the job done on Wednesday, with Dayne St. Clair making a late penalty save to preserve their clean sheet.

Lionel Messi was involved in Miami's first real opening as his superb reverse pass released Gonzalo Lujan, but from the right-back's cross, Matt Freese got down to repel a bullet header from Sergio Reguilon.

Miami made their superiority count in the 20th minute, though. Messi and De Paul linked up on the edge of the area, with the latter lofting a pass towards the far post for Luis Suarez, who beautifully slid it across the face of goal to give Berterame a tap-in.

Another well-worked move resulted in Messi clipping a shot over the crossbar, but he played the final pass for Miami's second goal in first-half stoppage time, picking out De Paul for a powerful finish at the end of a rapid counter-attack.
The second half was more of an evenly matched affair, but Miami had several good chances to extend their lead.

Freese made a smart one-v-one save to thwart Messi, then saw the frame of the goal come to his aid twice late on. He pushed De Paul's effort against his right post then saw Riquelme Fillipi strike the foot of the same upright.

NYCFC had a huge chance to at least grab a consolation goal when Ian Fray tripped Talles Magno inside the area in the sixth minute of stoppage time, but Nicolas Fernandez Mercau saw his spot-kick brilliantly turned around the post by St. Clair.
Messi continues goal involvement streak
Miami's victory confirmed their place in the postseason for a third consecutive year, having never failed to make the playoffs since Lionel Messi's first full campaign in 2024.
There was no goal for the Argentinian maestro here, but his assist for De Paul's strike did at least extend his streak of regular-season games with a direct goal involvement to 11.
Both teams had 14 shots apiece, but Miami's victory was deserved as they won the expected goals (xG) battle by 2.23 to 1.47, even with NYCFC's figures being boosted by their late penalty.
NYCFC, who are three points outside the playoff picture, have only won one of their last 13 matches in all competitions (D4 L8) in a run dating back to early August.
Since returning from the Leagues Cup group-stage break, only Real Salt Lake (six) have collected fewer points in MLS than NYCFC's seven (W1 D4 L5).

18y30s30bjxli1ihmjnj13x9ck.title: Amorim not worried about Ramos' Milan performances
18y30s30bjxli1ihmjnj13x9ck.subtitle: Goncalo Ramos has scored in his last three games for Portugal, but he has only found the net once for AC Milan since his big-money move.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim is not concerned about Goncalo Ramos' failure to replicate his Portugal displays with AC Milan as he is prioritising team performances rather than his striker's goal record.
Milan resume their Serie A campaign against Sassuolo on Sunday, having won three and drawn two of their first five games to start the Amorim era.

The Rossoneri's major acquisition in the summer transfer window was Ramos, who scored 45 goals in 131 appearances for Paris Saint-Germain and won 12 major trophies, including back-to-back Champions League crowns.

He only has one goal in five league outings for his new club, striking in a 2-0 win over Venezia in August, though he did find the net in three straight matches for Portugal during the international break, following Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt exit from their camp.

But when asked if he had a plan to get more out of his new recruit on Saturday, Amorim said: "My job as a manager is getting the team to play better, it is not about putting one player in a position to score more goals individually.
"We need to create more chances for our strikers, all our strikers, to put the ball in the box more often. I have my own ideas, I know what we want to do."
Amorim is hoping to mastermind an immediate return to the Champions League for Milan, who missed out under Massimiliano Allegri on the final day of last season.
But looking beyond that, his aim is to bring major silverware back to the red and black side of Milan – and to do so relatively quickly.
"The idea is always to win titles, I don't know how long it is going to take, but we are taking those steps to win," Amorim said.
"In this club you cannot think we are going to win in two or three years, we are a top club, we have to think we're going to win now.

"It is step by step to reach this goal, as there are a lot of good teams in the league. Serie A is becoming a little bit different, the new rules about not wasting time are getting more minutes and speed into the game.
"People don't give Serie A the value it deserves. I am having fun preparing the games, I often have a lot of issues to deal with, as there are so many different styles."

Sassuolo could provide Amorim's men with a difficult test at Mapei Stadium, having taken seven points from their first five matches – including a dramatic 3-2 victory over Juventus last time out at home.
Sassuolo – Domenico Berardi
Berardi has scored 12 goals in 20 Serie A matches against Milan.
In the league's history, only Silvio Piola (22) and Enrico Chiesa (14) have scored more goals against the Rossoneri (Antonio Di Natale, Carlo Reguzzoni and Stefano Nyers also have 12).
AC Milan – Diego Moreira
Moreira has scored three goals for Milan in Serie A, despite only totalling 127 minutes across three appearances.
Only two players have netted four goals in their first four games for the Rossoneri in the competition in the 2000s – Mario Balotelli in 2013 and Krzysztof Piatek in 2019.
MATCH PREDICTION – AC MILAN WIN
Sassuolo have avoided defeat in seven of their last nine Serie A matches against Milan (W4 D3), including their last three (W1 D2).
It is their longest-ever run without defeat against the Rossoneri in the competition.

However, the Neroverdi have only won one of their last 10 Serie A fixtures against Milan to take place in the first half of the season (D3 L6): a 3-1 comeback victory in November 2021 with goals from Gianluca Scamacca and Berardi, and an own goal from Simon Kjaer.
But Milan are looking to go unbeaten in their first six Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23, and Opta's predictive model fancies their chances of doing so.
There could be plenty of entertainment in store, though, as Sassuolo – along with Monza – were one of two teams to both score and concede in each of their first five Serie A games this season.
The only previous instances of the Neroverdi finding the net in each of their first six top-flight matches of a season were in 2015-16, 2018-19 and 2020-21.

194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.title: Bompastor will not risk James in Champions League as Arsenal clash looms
194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.subtitle: Chelsea open their Women's Champions League campaign against Austria Wien, but with Arsenal next up in the WSL, squad rotation is likely.
paragraphs: Chelsea will not take any risks with Lauren James against Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League, as Sonia Bompastor looks to get her ready to face Arsenal on Sunday.

The Blues are overwhelming favourites to open their European league-phase campaign with three points on Wednesday, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 93.3% chance of victory over the tournament debutants.
Chelsea's only previous meeting with an Austrian side in the Champions League came last season, as they thumped St. Polten 6-0 in the league phase.
Having gone out at the quarter-final stage last term following three straight semi-final defeats, the Blues are hoping to go further in Europe this term, but rotation is likely this week.
With a huge London derby against Arsenal on the horizon in the Women's Super League, Bompastor has already confirmed James – who picked up a minor injury in training – will be rested.
"She should be available for the game on the weekend, but we don't want to take any risks for the game tomorrow," Bompastor said of James. "She's a bit short."
Bompastor also confirmed Erin Cuthbert, Manaka Matsukubo and Aggie Beever-Jones are all back in training, with the latter being the only one of that trio to appear in a WSL match this season.
"They are training again with the team, so a lot of players and it's good news. Manaka is back in training, not fully fit yet, but it's good to have her back," Bompastor said.
"It's really good to see Erin back. I'm always happy when I have most of my players on the pitch. It brings positivity around the team and the quality on the pitch progresses.
"It's always good to have that competition in the squad, with everyone happy to be on the pitch together."
Chelsea lost just one of their eight games in the Champions League last season (W5 D2), conceding the fewest goals of any side in the competition (six).

Austria Wien will become the fourth different side from Austria to participate in the Champions League, but those teams are winless in 21 games in the competition (D3 L18) since St. Polten beat Slavia Prague 1-0 in November 2022.
English sides have won all five of their meetings with Austrian opponents in the competition by an aggregate score of 17-2.

          Mass Overhaul or Squad Continuity: What is the Recipe for Premier League Success?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
In an age when fans wants limitless spending on shiny new signings, we ask whether less change can sometimes be more beneficial.
If a cautionary tale was needed for a football club assuming the grass is always greener on the other side, Tottenham Hotspur’s experience so far in 2026-27 may well do the job.

After a dismal 2025-26, in which Spurs escaped relegation by the skin of their teeth, the club dived head first into their hopes for a shiny new era on the back of Roberto De Zerbi’s insistence the squad needed immediate, severe and costly surgery. After De Zerbi saved the club from the drop, he was handed the keys to a weighty war chest, and he spent big.

Upwards of £300 million was dished out and more or less an entire new team was brought in. Spurs signed 10 new players who have all gone into the first team; just five league games into the new season and all nine of the outfield signings have made at least one appearance in the Premier League, while many of them are already key players.
You don’t need a deep data dive to see it hasn’t worked yet. Spurs are bottom of the table without a win five games into 2026-27. It’s their worst start to a Premier League season.

It might all work out in the end. Spurs might become world beaters with this squad. Or even if it doesn’t go quite that well, they could feasibly become a half-decent team very soon indeed. This season obviously isn’t a complete write-off already.

But even if they do turn things around, by making such a poor start, they have given everyone else a head start. Spurs are playing catch-up with every other team, and now face a 33-game run in which they have to make up a deficit if they are to retain their Premier League status. They need to improve drastically to make the season anything like a success.

In fairness to De Zerbi, the evidence of the last two seasons was pretty strong. Spurs had finished 17th twice consecutively, last season playing some utterly miserable football while suffering a string of serious and debilitating injuries, and the squad clearly needed new additions. But has too much been changed too suddenly?

Spurs have become only the 12th team in Premier League history (excluding promoted teams) to hand more than 25 starts in the space of the first five games of a season to players who didn’t play for the club the previous year.

The concern for Spurs is, historically, doing that doesn’t go well. Six of the previous 11 have ended up finishing 17th or lower in the first season after the summer overhaul. Only one has finished higher than ninth.
Many of those teams were arguably always destined to be in a relegation battle and had attempted to avoid as much by making a lot of summer signings, such as QPR in 2012-13 or Portsmouth in 2005-06.

Spurs finished fifth as recently as 2023-24 and would have been hoping to get back into the elite quickly, but they are, whether they like it or not, a relegation-battling side. And the early evidence of this season along with the history of other clubs who have made this much change doesn’t bode well for them.
So, are these numbers and Spurs’ troubles the sign of a wider problem with significant player turnover? Were they wrong to approach the summer with this aggressive approach to the transfer market?

First up, it’s worth noting that there are examples of teams signing lots of players and things working out, if not always immediately, then in the long term. Nottingham Forest broke the record for the most players signed by a Premier League club after winning promotion in the summer of 2022 and have since established themselves as top-flight regulars (although they were later deducted four points for breaching the Premier League’s Profitability and Sustainability Rules). Chelsea transformed their squad and fortunes after Roman Abramovich arrived at the club. Sunderland qualified for Europe last season after a summer of overhaul following their promotion.

But there are many more examples of teams struggling after making a lot of signings, as is the case with many of the sides in the above table who gave lots of starts to new signings early on in the new season.
And this term, too, the teams who have started well are generally those who have not overhauled their squad.

Of the eight teams to give 10 or fewer starts to players who didn’t play for them last season, five are better off than the position in which the Opta supercomputer predicted they would finish before the start of the campaign. In other words, when comparing season-to-season changes in the starting XI with performance relative to (the supercomputer’s) expectations, teams who didn’t make many alterations are doing well.

And it’s the opposite at the other end of the spectrum. Of the eight teams who have given at least 13 starts this season to new players, all but one are currently in a lower position than they were in the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions.

Whether by complete coincidence or not, there appears to be a correlation between the two. A greater number of new players this season has led to underperformance compared to what the supercomputer foresaw for that team.

There are a few obvious outliers. Bournemouth have given fewer starts to new players (five) than any other team in the Premier League this season (though they do have a new manager), but they are currently seven places lower than their predicted position from pre-season.

197rqdcsi8fzl10wb5mtwhz3tt.title: Romania 0-1 Sweden: Gyokeres continues hot streak
197rqdcsi8fzl10wb5mtwhz3tt.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres scored his fourth goal in as many games for Sweden as Graham Potter's team edged out Romania in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Sweden are in prime position to earn promotion back to the top table in the Nations League after they beat Romania 1-0 on Monday.
Graham Potter's team rounded off the first international break of the season with a slender victory at Arena Nationala, with Viktor Gyokeres' goal proving decisive.
Sweden remain unbeaten in Group B4, which they top on 10 points, two ahead of Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Gyokeres' goal came just 12 minutes in, with the Arsenal forward pouncing on the rebound from Sebastian Nanasi's shot, which had struck the woodwork.
He should have doubled up later in the first half, but failed to direct a header goalwards after meeting Eric Smith's cross.
Viktor Johansson was called into action in Sweden's goal in the second half, as he denied Nicolae Stanciu and Florin Tanase, but that was all Romania could really manage in response.
Sweden close in on promotion as Gyokeres delivers
Three wins and one draw from their opening four fixtures is a fantastic start for Sweden, who are now on the brink of sealing a return to the top section of the Nations League.
That is where Sweden will feel they belong, given some of the quality they have at their disposal, albeit Gyokeres was their only real star name in action this time out.
He has now scored 25 goals for Sweden, and he led the way for Potter's team with four attempts here.
Gyokeres only managed to hit the target once, but he was in the right place, at the right time, to get the goal that mattered in the end.
His goal came from a chance worth a whopping 0.95 expected goals, so it would have been difficult for him to miss.
But in Alexander Isak's absence, Gyokeres is the main man, and he duly delivered for Sweden.

          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 3 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 28, 2026
          
                      Emily Clogg / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions for Matchday 3.
Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 UEFA Women’s Champions League is upon us and after what has been an almost month-long wait, the anticipation has built ahead of another week of fixtures.

With two wins from their opening two matches, Barcelona are the only side to have maintained a perfect start to the competition. Pere Romeu’s side put six past Roma last time out as Caroline Graham Hansen, Clàudia Pina and Ewa Pajor all found the net.

For all three English sides in the competitions, things weren’t quite so straightforward. Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal all drew their clashes with OL Lyonnes, Real Madrid and Paris FC respectively.
For the latter, it was a moment of sheer madness from Leah Williamson that turned three valuable points to just one in the French capital; elsewhere in the city, PSG thrashed OH Leuven 5-0.

This week’s set of fixtures features a number of delectable matchups. The two standouts see Bayern Munich host Real Madrid on Wednesday, before Manchester City face PSG at the Joie Stadium the next day.
Elsewhere, Chelsea host Roma, Arsenal welcome Benfica, and Barcelona head to Denmark to take on HB Køge.
Here, we look out the Opta supercomputer's data-led predictions for each game on MD3.
There are three 17:45 (GMT) kick-offs to choose from on Wednesday, one of which is guaranteed to be an entertaining affair as Real Madrid make the trip to Germany to take on Bayern Munich.

In this early stage of the UWCL, there are few trickier tasks than beating Bayern in front of their own fans. In fact, José Barcala’s side haven’t lost a single round-one match at home (W12 D4); only Barcelona and Chelsea have played as many such matches without defeat.

As for Real Madrid, they’ve lost just one of their last eight league-phase matches (2-1 defeat to Arsenal last term), with their last three all ending in a draw, the longest such streak in the competition alongside PSG.
This is the first UWCL meeting between the two sides, and the supercomputer expects a one-way encounter with Bayern winning 60.6% % of pre-match simulations.

Meanwhile, Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea welcome Roma to the English capital, with the Blues boasting an enviable record against Italian sides in the competition; they are unbeaten across their previous five (W4 D1).
The Blues enter this one with a spring in their step, having leapfrogged City to the summit of the Women’s Super League table at the weekend following a 3-1 win against promoted side Crystal Palace.
Roma are also top of their respective domestic table, the Serie A Femminile, but have been struggling in Europe, and enter this fixture looking for their first win of the new campaign.

Yet to score a goal, Roma are the only team to have underperformed by 2+ goals based on the xG they’ve generated in this season’s UWCL (-2.53). However, Chelsea are also just  one of four others to have underperformed by at least one goal (-1.17).
The Blues are strong favourites going into this match-up, and the pre-match sims saw them take all three points 81.2% of the time.
Wednesday's other early kick-off is a crucial clash as Servette host OH Leuven, with both teams looking to kick-start their Champions League campaigns. Neither side has scored a goal yet.
The supercomputer leans slightly towards a first win in the competition for Servette, who came out on top in 47.3% of simulations.
Wednesday's 20:00 (GMT) matches feature two European heavyweights, with Lyon and Arsenal both in action hosting Inter and Benfica, respectively.

19dmmstrz51ed1s46e1dfr4xkx.title: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami: Messi doubles up again
19dmmstrz51ed1s46e1dfr4xkx.subtitle: Inter Miami surged to a 3-1 win over Atlanta United on Saturday, with Lionel Messi once again scoring twice.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi doubled up once more to lead Inter Miami to a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United.
Messi scored twice in Miami's 4-0 win over D.C. United last weekend, though he did not find the net in a 2-0 defeat of New York City FC in midweek.
However, Messi was back on target twice on Saturday as Miami eased to a triumph at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Messi had seen a free-kick kept out by Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos before German Berterame put Miami up on the stroke of half-time, turning in from Luis Suarez's cross.
Miami's captain then put the contest to bed with two goals in the space of four second-half minutes.
First, Messi combined with Berterame before slotting home at the end of a brilliant run.
Then, the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner latched onto Suarez's pass, turned his marker inside out and duly finished.
Messi looked set to get the chance to score a hat-trick when Paulo Diaz was pinned for handball, though VAR intervened, deeming that Suarez had committed a foul first.
Matt Edwards struck the woodwork for Atlanta, though the hosts did get a consolation late on when Maximiliano Falcon felled Fafa Picault, who dispatched the resulting spot-kick.
More MLS history for magnificent Messi
Messi has now gone 12 straight regular-season matches with a goal involvement.
The only longer single-season streak in MLS history is 15, set by Josef Martinez in 2019, with Messi now matching Sebastian Giovinco's run of 12 games in 2018.
Messi has now scored 23 goals and set up 15 this season, making him the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three straight campaigns.
"I can't believe this guy does what he does at 39 years of age," Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said of Messi.
"And what makes me happiest is that he's happy. So if he's happy, he performs the way he performs, he enjoys... Every day that I see him, I smile.
"He's a player who never stops surprising you.
"To me, he's an alien. He's a player who amazes me in every action, during every training session that I watch. And God willing, he'll keep on amazing us until the day he decides to retire."

19gt2steqgabb1br5wpgtpx0mx.title: Sage encourages Palace 'to turn the page quickly' after Europa League loss
19gt2steqgabb1br5wpgtpx0mx.subtitle: Crystal Palace lost 3-2 against Lyon in the Europa League, but Pierre Sage has called on the Eagles to keep looking forward.
paragraphs: Pierre Sage has urged his Crystal Palace side "to turn the page quickly" after their Europa League defeat to his former club Lyon.
Palace lost 3-2 at Groupama Stadium after a poor first-half showing, which saw Corentin Tolisso and Ernest Nuamah give Lyon a 2-0 lead.
Yeremy Pino pulled a goal back for Palace before Pavel Sulc's instinctive finish restored Lyon's two-goal lead, rendering Daichi Kamada's 81st-minute strike a consolation.
Tolisso opened the scoring after Palace failed to clear their lines from a corner, something which has become a persistent problem for the Eagles.
Palace have shipped 35 set-piece goals in all competitions since the start of last season, a figure only two Premier League sides have exceeded (Chelsea on 37 and Newcastle United on 36).
However, with a clash against rivals Brighton in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage does not want Palace to dwell on the defeat.
"It was a game of two different halves," said Sage.
"We were absent in the first half. The second half is more like what we’re used to seeing.
"We can be frustrated with the result, but we can be frustrated with the first half. Going two goals down meant this was too difficult to turn around.
"We didn't fight enough, we didn't manage some of the tactical problems and we were not proactive with the ball. If we want to be competitive, we need to be better in these areas.
"We have to turn the page quickly and take the lesson. Now the most important game is the game in Brighton."
Brighton were also in action on Thursday, kicking off their Conference League campaign with a 4-0 win over Kauno Zalgiris.

19kkdsviy67021tkqixv1gwnkt.title: Palmer eyes major trophies after penning new Chelsea contract until 2034
19kkdsviy67021tkqixv1gwnkt.subtitle: Cole Palmer, who is closing in on 50 Premier League goals, has signed a new contract with Chelsea to run for the next eight years.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer wants to challenge for more major trophies after committing his long-term future to Chelsea, signing a new contract to run until 2034.
The Blues confirmed their star forward had penned an eight-year deal on Saturday, ahead of their home Premier League game against Bournemouth.
Palmer has become the face of Chelsea's attack since joining from Manchester City in August 2023, scoring 58 goals and supplying 33 assists in all competitions – both team-high figures.
He helped the Blues win the Conference League and the Club World Cup under Enzo Maresca in 2025, while he has also been a losing finalist in the FA Cup (in 2025-26) and the EFL Cup (2023-24).

In the Premier League, Palmer's 71 combined goal involvements for Chelsea are more than double the amount any other player has registered for the club since the start of 2023-24 (Nicolas Jackson managed 34), and are the fourth-most of any player overall.
Only Erling Haaland (97), Mohamed Salah (89) and Ollie Watkins (75) have managed more direct goal contributions in the competition during that time.

However, Palmer is yet to enjoy sustained success in the league, with Chelsea managing finishes of sixth, fourth and 10th in his three campaigns at Stamford Bridge, and the England international wants that to change going forward.
"Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I'm delighted to sign, and I'm obviously very happy," Palmer told the club's website.
"Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and, obviously, the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence, so it was only right to sign.
"Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too."
Palmer has enjoyed a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign under Xabi Alonso, though Chelsea went into the international break on a three-game winless streak (D1 L2).

His four goal involvements in the Premier League this season (two goals, two assists) have only been bettered by team-mate Joao Pedro, Brighton's Pascal Gross (both six), Manchester City trio Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo and Liverpool's Cody Gakpo (all five).

"Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too."

Palmer has enjoyed a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign under Xabi Alonso, though Chelsea went into the international break on a three-game winless streak (D1 L2).

His four goal involvements in the Premier League this season (two goals, two assists) have only been bettered by team-mate Joao Pedro, Brighton's Pascal Gross (both six), Manchester City trio Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo and Liverpool's Cody Gakpo (all five).

19nrwtk28rdcb1xk59b9sk7a4t.title: Under-pressure Sage 'frustrated' by Palace's draw with Besiktas
19nrwtk28rdcb1xk59b9sk7a4t.subtitle: Crystal Palace could not find a way past Besiktas in the Europa League, with Pierre Sage saying his side deserved more than just a point.
paragraphs: Pierre Sage believed his Crystal Palace team "deserved better" from their 2-2 draw with Besiktas as the pressure continued to mount on the Frenchman on Thursday.
Palace claimed a point at Tupras Stadyumu in the Europa League, despite playing the final 13 minutes with a man extra after Umit Akdag was sent off for a second yellow card.
Besiktas had taken the lead at the end of the first half through Wilfred Ndidi, but two goals in four minutes from Yeremy Pino and Jean-Philippe Mateta turned things around.
However, Junior Olaitan came off the bench to salvage a point for Besiktas in the 73rd minute, with the hosts scoring with their only two shots on target of the game.
The heat was on Sage after last weekend's 5-0 defeat to rivals Brighton in the Premier League, with reports suggesting the Palace boss had just two matches to save his job.

It was a match with little quality in the final third, with Palace's expected goals (xG) total of 0.44 just bettered by Besiktas' tally of 0.69, Sage believed his team should have earned all three points, telling TNT Sports:"I am satisfied with the performance.
"A little bit frustrated for the lads, because they gave a lot this evening and I think they deserved better.
"We lacked concentration in the final minute of the first half and at the end. It was the same when we were 2-1 up. In this kind of situation, you pay if you make a little mistake.
"The performance was worse on Sunday. We made a good step and now to go forward and win against Newcastle on Sunday."

Palace's problems have been centred around conceding goals, particularly away from home. They have kept just one clean sheet in their last 16 games on the road in all competitions, shipping a total of 33 goals in that time.

In the Premier League, the Eagles have conceded more goals (17), faced more shots (125), faced more shots on target (43), and have a higher xG against (14.8) than any other side in the top flight this season.
But ahead of welcoming Newcastle United to Selhurst Park this Sunday, Sage was given a boost at the other end by Mateta, who marked his return from injury with a goal.
Since his debut for Palace in February 2021, Mateta has scored 63 goals in all competitions for the club, 26 more than any other player (Eberechi Eze next on 37).
"I am really happy for him," Sage said of Mateta's display. "It's a good moment for him. Just before coming out, he was not really ready to play.
"You could then see he was tired, but when you have this mindset and give your life on the pitch it is good for you.
"We have a lot of satisfaction in individual performances and I have to underline the team performance, too.
"At the end, we had a good game without the result we deserved."

19p7xhsygyxob1j9e3g5vytwk4.title: Charlton Athletic 0-1 Manchester City: Greenwood free-kick keeps champions perfect
19p7xhsygyxob1j9e3g5vytwk4.subtitle: Manchester City made it four wins from four to begin their Women's Super League campaign, but they were made to work by Charlton Athletic.
paragraphs: Manchester City's perfect start to their Women's Super League title defence continued as Alex Greenwood's first-half free-kick sealed a 1-0 win over Charlton Athletic.
Greenwood curled in the only goal in the 36th minute at The Valley, moving Andree Jeglertz's side, at least now, five points clear at the top of the standings.
Jeglertz elected to make six changes to the side that came from behind to beat Liverpool last time out, with Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw starting on the City bench.
Charlton started brightly, but it was the visitors who registered the first shot on target, though Sophie Whitehouse had no problem collecting Mary Fowler's 19th-minute attempt.
Jodie Hutton's cross into the area almost caught out Eartha Cumings soon after, with Beth Mead then forcing a save out of Whitehouse at the other end moments later.
However, City took the lead nine minutes before half-time through captain Greenwood, who curled an effort over the Charlton wall that nestled into the bottom-right corner from 25 yards.
City should have pulled further clear shortly after the restart, but Whitehouse produced two instinctive saves to keep out Gracie Prior and Grace Clinton in quick succession.
Cassandra Korhonen should have done better when she was picked out by Hutton's cross, with Jeglertz introducing Shaw into the action in the 60th minute.

And she should have made it more comfortable for City, but she could only head wide of the left post from Carlotta Wamser's delivery. It mattered little, though, as they held on for a fourth league win.
Can anyone stop champions City?

City arrived into the contest having scored 3+ goals in each of their opening three games of a WSL campaign, becoming the first side to do so since Arsenal in 2021-22, and though they were unable to continue that stretch, they showed they can win in different ways.

The Citizens have now won each of their opening four games this season, equalling their longest 100% winning start across their eight most recent top-flight campaigns, having also won four in a row back in 2019-20.

In addition, they have also emerged victorious in 29 of their 30 WSL games against newly promoted teams, winning eight straight since a 2-1 loss at Liverpool in 2022-23, though it was a moment of magic from Greenwood that got them over the line.

Greenwood netted for the first time in the WSL since April 2024 against Bristol City, though Mead also impressed for the Citizens. She finished with game-high totals for chances created (four), touches (98) and passes in the final third (47).

City were deserving of their win too, finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.98 from their 19 shots to Charlton's 0.63 from their five attempts, with Jeglertz now turning his attention to the Women's Champions League, with a tie against Real Madrid up next.
