19w7m2lz4gt141q5b1vzbn3eje.title: Tuchel: England harnessed the pain of World Cup exit in Croatia rout
19w7m2lz4gt141q5b1vzbn3eje.subtitle: After England produced one of their all-time greatest displays to rout Croatia 7-0, Thomas Tuchel said his players were playing with pain.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel felt England's players harnessed the pain of their World Cup failure in a positive way against Croatia, after they trounced their old rivals 7-0 in the Nations League.

Less than four months on from the Three Lions' semi-final collapse against Argentina, when Tuchel was fiercely criticised for reining in his attacking players, his team showed a completely different side in Rijeka.

Harry Kane, Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka all scored in the first half to put the result beyond all reasonable doubt, with Kane and Saka both clinching their braces and Morgan Rogers adding the final goal off the bench in the second period.
It was the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history and England's biggest-ever Nations League win, as well as their biggest victory over any top 50 team in the FIFA World Rankings.

The Three Lions had four different players score in the first half of a game for the first time since March 2013 against San Marino (Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain), while their nine-match winning streak away from home is their joint-longest ever, having managed an identical run between December 1965 and October 1967 either side of their World Cup triumph.
And while Tuchel admits the pain of July's defeat to Argentina still weighs heavily on everyone connected to the England team, he was pleased to see them take out their anger on a top-tier opponent.
"This is the only way to move forward, even if you still feel pain," Tuchel said.
"You have to play with the pain if you still feel the disappointment, you have to play with it. That is the nature of sport.

"It was not an easy camp in the beginning, after this long tournament, for multiple reasons. But straight away, from the first training session... we had an excellent performance against Spain but not the result, then the reaction to that result in Czechia, and now the build-up here.
"The focus in the meetings, the translation of the meetings onto the pitch and to bring it in these circumstances in Croatia, to win with this dominant performance, that is the way to move on."
Although all of England's attackers impressed, Bellingham was the real star of the show, as he capped a 27-pass move for his goal and also added three assists.

The Real Madrid superstar – who recently won England's Player of the Year award for 2026 after scoring seven goals at the World Cup – teed up Kane and Saka in the first half, then supplied the defence-splitting pass for Rogers to add the seventh goal.
When asked if Bellingham had gone up a level in 2026, Tuchel said: "At the moment it seems like it, and you always need to. You can never stand still.
"It's like on these electric escalators, if you stand still, if you walk against the escalator, you have to walk to even maintain your level.
"You have to develop and you have to push for the next level, otherwise other teams will catch up."

England have six points on the board after three Nations League games, putting them three behind Group A3 leaders Spain and three above third-placed Croatia, ahead of Tuesday's clash with Czechia at Wembley.

19wtxvpva5y5y1bv9bj02xb1vv.title: Andrews says Hull belong at Premier League level and expects major test for Brentford
19wtxvpva5y5y1bv9bj02xb1vv.subtitle: Brentford travel to Hull City on Sunday, after seeing their unbeaten start to the Premier League season halted by Liverpool last weekend.
paragraphs: Brentford boss Keith Andrews expects his side to face a real test when they go up against Hull City on Sunday, saying the Tigers have already shown they belong at Premier League level.
Andrews' side were beaten 2-1 by Liverpool last Saturday, having led 1-0 before ultimately being pegged back and finishing the game with nine men.
Both Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were sent off and will now be suspended for the trip to Hull, with Brentford currently sat sixth in the Premier League table with 10 points.
Hull are only a point worse off in ninth place, having silenced many of their doubters since winning promotion via the Championship play-offs.

And Andrews has been impressed with how Sergej Jakirovic's side have adapted to top-flight football, telling reporters on Thursday: "I expect a proper test; they have a way of playing that can be very testing.
"They have a belief that they can absolutely compete at this level. They've shown that they can, week in, week out.
"They've produced some really, really good performances, and they've been in every single game they've played in."
However, after starting the season with back-to-back wins, Hull have failed to taste victory in their last five league games (D3 L2), most recently going down 1-0 to Fulham last week.
They are the first team to win their first two games of the season, then none of their next five, since both Huddersfield Town and West Brom in 2017-18.
And centre-back Semi Ajayi says they need to treat last week's defeat at Craven Cottage as a learning opportunity and move on quickly.
"It's a learning curve for us," Ajayi told the club's website. "We were well below the standards we have shown previously, and we all know that.
"In this league, even if you're only 5% down on your level, you're going to get punished, as we saw against Fulham.
"We need to put that right quickly and be much better against Brentford next weekend."
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Hull City – Mohamed Belloumi
Only four players have had more shots from outside the box in the Premier League this season than Belloumi (10).
As a team, the Tigers rank third for their percentage of attempts coming from outside the box (44%, 33/75), so it may be up to him to provide a moment of magic.
Brentford – Igor Thiago
Thiago has six goals in his last six Premier League appearances against newly promoted clubs.
And, in the last two seasons, only four players have more goals and assists combined in the Premier League than the Brazilian (23 goals, two assists).
MATCH PREDICTION – DRAW
This will be the first-ever top-flight meeting between Hull and Brentford, with the sides facing in each of the second, third and fourth tiers previously.
It will also be their first league meeting since February 2020, a 5-1 win for the Bees in the Championship at MKM Stadium.
Indeed, each of Brentford's last three away league wins against Hull have been in different divisions – the third tier in 1995-96, the fourth tier in 1998-99 and the second in 2019-20.
Brentford have also never won an away Premier League match in Yorkshire in five attempts (D4 L1); their last away top-flight win there was back in May 1947, 2-1 at Leeds United.

Hull, meanwhile, are unbeaten at home this season (W1 D2). Across the last 11 seasons, only two newly promoted teams have remained unbeaten in their first four home games: Wolves in 2018-19 (four) and Sunderland in 2025-26 (first 12), both of whom finished seventh.

And though Brentford are slight favourites with the Opta supercomputer, it struggles to split the teams overall, and the Bees have already dropped 11 points from winning positions in the Premier League this season – the joint-second most after seven games of a season.

19xzitax7mapxz8jzdq1fk6o2.title: 'Ipswich deserved the win' – O’Neil delighted with late victory against Fulham
19xzitax7mapxz8jzdq1fk6o2.subtitle: Gary O'Neil felt Ipswich Town "deserved the win" after scoring two late goals to defeat winless Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road.
paragraphs: Gary O'Neil was full of praise for his Ipswich Town side as they completed a stunning 2-1 comeback over Fulham in the Premier League.
After Ryan Sessegnon picked out the bottom-right corner with a long-range strike, Ipswich were heading for defeat at Portman Road.
However, the Tractor Boys, who registered an expected goals (xG) of 1.15, levelled the scoreline in the 88th minute thanks to Abdoul Ouattara’s curling left-footed effort.
And the action did not end there as captain Dara O'Shea netted a stoppage-time winner, heading in Jack Clarke’s free-kick at the near post.

The result means Ipswich have now won three of their first six Premier League games in a season for only the second time, while also winning six points from losing positions with no team having recovered more.
After seeing his side seal a late win against Fulham, O’Neil said, “We deserved the win today, to perform the way we did.
“We were the better side, we were in control. We conceded a goal from 30 yards, which was tough to take when you are the team that has the momentum.
"But we are a fit side, they can run [the group]. So, we were able to make five changes from the bench which had a positive impact.
"We get the win that we deserve, which is important. A lot of work went into it, the players were excellent, they deserve a lot of credit.”
On Ouattara’s performance, O’Neil added, “He’s a good player, Abdoul. Still has a lot to do. Still working hard. I’ve had him for a while now, obviously [at Strasbourg].
"He can play in a number of different positions, he has some stuff we still need to improve, but his left foot shooting from 30 yards does not seem to be one of them."
Meanwhile, Alvaro Arbeloa continues his search for a first Premier League win as Fulham boss.
In a contest which saw the Cottagers muster a superior xG of 1.81 from 13 attempts, Arbeloa’s side were made to pay for sitting too deep in the final few minutes of the game.
Fulham have now failed to win in their last six games in the Premier League, while also losing eight points from winning positions, with only Bournemouth (nine) having lost more.
More worryingly, Fulham sit 20th in the Premier League table, with pressure mounting on the former Real Madrid boss.
"It is painful to lose three points in the way that we did. It is something we need to accept and prepare the same for the next game," said Arbeloa.
“We need to keep improving. We did many things well, we played well for 60–70 minutes, but in the end we conceded two late goals and lost the game.
“If you don't take your chances, your opponent will. We are creating so many chances during games, if we want to win games we need to start taking chances.”

“We need to keep improving. We did many things well, we played well for 60–70 minutes, but in the end we conceded two late goals and lost the game.

“If you don't take your chances, your opponent will. We are creating so many chances during games, if we want to win games we need to start taking chances.”

19y5fzrchycuf195qqraf71b79.title: Martinez clarifies criticism of Man Utd hierarchy, outlines need for unity
19y5fzrchycuf195qqraf71b79.subtitle: Having made headlines for his criticism of Manchester United's recruitment on Tuesday, Lisandro Martinez has attempted to explain himself.
paragraphs: Lisandro Martinez has moved to clarify his recent criticism of Manchester United's hierarchy, saying he believes in everyone at the club and that unity will be key if they are to turn their season around.

Following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, which extended United's winless run to five games in all competitions, Martinez gave an explosive post-match interview to Amazon Prime.

The Argentina centre-back suggested there had not been sufficient investment in the playing squad ahead of the season, singling out director of football Jason Wilcox and saying, "We expect more from the top."
Reports subsequently suggested Martinez's contract may not be renewed when it expires at the end of the season, while head coach Michael Carrick opted against responding to the defender's comments.
But Martinez has now taken to Instagram to clarify his words, saying the responsibility for United's poor results starts with the playing squad.
"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club," Martinez wrote.
"To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.
"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.
"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."
Having only beaten Ipswich Town and Sabah in nine matches across all competitions this season, the Red Devils visit Elland Road to face old rivals Leeds United on Sunday.
It will be the teams' first Premier League meeting with Leeds above Man Utd in the table (excluding matchday one) since September 2002, when the Whites earned a 1-0 win at Elland Road.

A win for Leeds put them six points clear of their rivals in the table as late as the seventh matchday of a Premier League campaign for just the second time – they were seven points ahead in December 2001 after playing 15 games.

19yjyzvj9qy4315f9qzwb51j9d.title: Maza hails Leverkusen record-breaker Schick as fruitful partnership continues
19yjyzvj9qy4315f9qzwb51j9d.subtitle: Patrik Schick and Ibrahim Maza combined for Bayer Leverkusen's goals against Freiburg, as they claimed their third Bundesliga win in a row.
paragraphs: Ibrahim Maza is enjoying playing alongside Patrik Schick, who made a piece of club history for Bayer Leverkusen during Sunday's 2-1 success against Freiburg.
A third straight victory for Carles Martinez's side lifted them to fourth in the Bundesliga table, with Maza and Schick getting the goals.

Schick's 76th-minute winner continued his run of scoring in every Bundesliga match this season, with his streak of six games with a goal from the beginning of a campaign being the longest by any Leverkusen player.

Dimitar Berbatov (in 2005-06) and Stefan Kiessling (in 2009-10) had both previously scored in the opening five games of a Bundesliga campaign for Leverkusen, and the latter's outright club record of seven straight Bundesliga matches on the scoresheet is now within Schick's reach.
Maza and Schick both assisted each other's goals, with the Czechia international recording two goal involvements in a single Bundesliga game for the second time this season.
When he previously did so, against Union Berlin in September, another of team-mates – Miguel Gutierrez – also had a pair of goal involvements in the same match.
"It was a lot of fun, especially against such a strong opponent. Huge respect to Freiburg but we showed what we can do," Maza told DAZN afterwards.
"We played some great football today, but a lot of credit to Freiburg as well. They put in a great performance.
"Schicki and I are building some pretty good chemistry. The more time we spend playing together, the better it gets. It's going pretty well right now."
While Schick was pleased to write his name into the record books, his main source of happiness was the victory, with Leverkusen just one point off Bayern Munich at the summit.
"I've already heard that I've broken the record, which obviously makes me very happy," he said.
"Our result is really important for the table. Freiburg are one of the best teams in the league, so it was a tough game. I'm happy with the result.
"You can see our development. We're not making the same simple mistakes we were making at the start of the season. A game like this could easily have ended in a draw, so we're happy today."
Leverkusen visit OFI Crete in the Europa League on Thursday, before travelling to Hoffenheim for their next Bundesliga fixture on Sunday.

19yxdy6kwkwjm1cs6l5xryon4c.title: Tottenham 3-1 Coventry City: Maddison, Marmoush and Davies snap winless run
19yxdy6kwkwjm1cs6l5xryon4c.subtitle: Tottenham finally ended their wait for a Premier League win this season, as they beat Coventry City 3-1 on Monday.
paragraphs: Omar Marmoush scored his first goal for Tottenham as Roberto De Zerbi's men battled to a 3-1 win over Coventry City.

Spurs had gone winless in their first six Premier League matches this term, and another failure to take all three points on Monday would have seen them draw to within one game of matching their longest winless start to a season in the competition.
Yet Marmoush's superb finish and Ben Davies' stoppage-time effort saw Spurs get over the line at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
James Maddison, making his first competitive start for Spurs since May 2025, opened the scoring in the 14th minute.
The former Coventry playmaker met Mohammed Kudus' cutback on the cusp of the visitors' area and bent a sensational strike into the top-left corner.

Yet Spurs failed to build on their lead, with Dominic Solanke having a goal disallowed for offside before he arrowed over, and Coventry were level early in the second half when the in-form Jack Rudoni hammered in from close range.

Sandro Tonali blazed over as Spurs got straight onto the front foot, though, and that pressure paid off as Marmoush spun Milan van Ewijk, who took an elbow to the face for his troubles, and curled beyond Carl Rushworth, who might have done better.
Rushworth should definitely have kept out the decisive third in the 96th minute, but Coventry's goalkeeper allowed Davies' tame shot to sneak in and settle the contest.
Long-awaited victory comes with long-awaited Kulusevski return
It was a big night for two Tottenham stars who have had a torrid time of it over the past year or so.

Maddison made his first start in a meaningful game for Spurs since a Europa League semi-final tie against Bodo/Glimt at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, with the midfielder having missed the majority of last season due to a serious knee injury.
He had at least returned towards the end of the campaign, but the same could not be said for Dejan Kulusevski, who was back in a Premier League matchday squad for the first time in 526 days.

Kulusevski came on to huge applause in the 87th minute, and though he was clearly rusty, every touch and pass the Swede made was cheered by the home crowd, who will be thrilled to have him back and will now be praying he is over his injury issues.

Spurs only created chances worth a combined 0.87 expected goals, but they became the first team to score three goals from outside the box in a Premier League game since Fulham against Leicester City in May 2023.

Since the start of 2024-25, Tottenham have dropped more points from winning positions in Premier League home games than any other side (30), so the nerves will certainly have crept in, especially given Spurs' dismal home record.
Yet they got the job done in the end, and De Zerbi will now be hoping Spurs, who moved above Coventry and into 16th place, can kick on. Next up for them is a trip to Chelsea on Saturday.

19z4npnxn4rpj1oc4bi6y47yuc.title: Real Madrid's Asencio to have surgery on leg fracture
19z4npnxn4rpj1oc4bi6y47yuc.subtitle: Raul Asencio has failed to play a single minute for Real Madrid this season, and is now having surgery on the injury that has kept him out.
paragraphs: Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio is set to have surgery on a stress fracture in his right tibia.
Asencio has been struggling with the injury since the start of the season and was not included in any of Madrid's first five matchday squads this term.
Even following his return, he has not played a single minute for Madrid so far and seemingly aggravated the issue in training on Wednesday.
As such, he will undergo surgery on Thursday, with Spanish media reports suggesting he is set for two to four months on the sidelines.
Asencio made 34 appearances for Madrid in all competitions last term but lost his starting place in the latter stages of the season.
Jose Mourinho has been using Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen as his regular centre-back pairing since his arrival.
However, the Portuguese head coach could soon be able to call on Eder Militao, who has returned to training following hamstring surgery that has kept him out since April.
Madrid return to action at home to Villarreal on October 10 after the international break.

19z6vpoopafug1b3qn9bjt61ce.title: Allegri challenges Napoli to 'change the trend' after Venezia defeat
19z6vpoopafug1b3qn9bjt61ce.subtitle: Napoli's poor start to the season continued with a loss to Venezia, but Massimiliano Allegri has called for calm.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri has challenged his Napoli side to "change that trend" of things not going their way after losing to Venezia.
Napoli fell to a 1-0 defeat against Serie A's bottom side, with Akor Adams scoring the only goal before Kevin De Bruyne missed a penalty.

De Bruyne has missed just three of the 14 penalties he has taken in his career across Europe's top five leagues in all competitions – his previous unsuccessful kick was in November 2020 for Manchester City.
Napoli have now lost five of their last nine matches in all competitions (W3 D1 L5), as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 29 games (W16 D8 L5).
They have lost five of their first nine matches in all competitions (W3 D1) in a season for the first time since the 2001-02 campaign (W2 D2 L5 under Gigi De Canio, when the club was in Serie B).
However, despite failing to score against Venezia, Napoli did create 2.44 expected goals (xG) from their 29 shots, 10 of which hit the target.
Allegri believes his side are doing a lot of things right, but he knows they must find a way to change their recent results.
"We created a great deal, but continue to be penalised for costly errors," Allegri told DAZN Italia.
"Considering how many chances we created, it's a concern that we were unable to score a goal. We've got to analyse this moment with clear heads, there is time to recover.
"Venezia defended very well, and we didn't stretch them out to create space between the lines. It was a different match after the break, the spaces opened up, but we didn't make the most of them.
"There's no point being worried now, we need to do what we're doing, but do it better.
"At this moment, incidents just aren't going our way, and we conceded at the first opportunity. It is up to us to change that trend."

19zxgpff4u1ss1aaoctm9kxr2e.title: Former Inter defender Darmian joins Bologna on free transfer
19zxgpff4u1ss1aaoctm9kxr2e.subtitle: Matteo Darmian has finally landed himself a new club following his summer exit from Inter, joining fellow Serie A side Bologna on Thursday.
paragraphs: Bologna have announced the arrival of experienced defender Matteo Darmian following his exit from Serie A champions Inter at the end of last season.
Darmian has put pen to paper on a contract with Bologna until the end of the 2026-27 campaign, and he could make his debut for his new club against Lecce on Sunday.
The 36-year-old arrives after five successful years with Inter, where he won nine major honours, which include three Scudettos and three Copa Italia crowns.
During his time with the Nerazzurri, Darmian made 218 appearances across all competitions, scoring 13 goals and providing 13 assists.
His arrival comes after Emil Holm sustained a serious injury while away on international duty with Sweden, with the Bologna full-back expected to be sidelined for up to six months.
Bologna will be hopeful Darmian's arrival can have a positive impact on the team, with Raffaele Palladino's 18th in Serie A and winless after their opening five league matches.
Darmian joins a Bologna side that have only conceded six goals so far in Serie A, though they have only scored three times at the other end, the joint-lowest tally in the division.
Bologna have gained five points fewer than at this stage last season in Serie A (two vs seven), with no side having a worse difference in the top flight.
They have collected two points so far (D2 L3). During the three-points-for-a-win era, they have never had fewer than three points after their first six Serie A games in a season.

          Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé Strikes Twice as José Mourinho Claims Clásico Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 25, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Kylian Mbappé was the hero as Real Madrid cut the gap at the top of La Liga with a deserved win at Barcelona. Check out all the best Clásico numbers with our stats page.
Kylian Mbappé scored twice, including an 87th-minute winner, as Real Madrid claimed a huge 2-1 victory over their Clásico rivals Barcelona at Camp Nou.

Barça were hoping to become the first team to ever start a season in one of Europe's top five leagues with 10 straight victories, having already built a six-point buffer to Madrid ahead of Sunday's clash.

Hansi Flick's hosts were up against it when Gerard Martín's attempted clearance ricocheted in off Mbappé in the 41st minute, although Raphinha's 13th league goal of the season drew them level shortly after the hour mark.
However, Mbappé was on hand to slot into an empty net following a lightning quick Madrid break late on, prompting wild celebrations from manager José Mourinho on the sidelines.
Madrid quickly got on the front foot as they looked to quiet a raucous Catalan crowd, but no white shirts were lurking for a tap-in when Joan García could only parry Arda Güler's drive.

Raphinha had three efforts at the other end, the second of which was the most threatening as his first-time strike whistled over the crossbar following some industrious work from Pedri, while Andrii Lunin – standing in for the ill Thibaut Courtois – denied Anthony Gordon at his near post.

Yan Diomande was one of Madrid's brightest sparks in attack, and their opening goal came from him being slipped into the area by Marc Cucurella. The Ivorian's centre was far from his best, but Martín blasted it straight off Mbappé and into the net.
Barça should have had a quickfire equaliser when Lamine Yamal scuffed an uncharacteristically poor finish wide, but Flick's team were cut open on two more occasions before the interval.
Mbappé rifled against the inside of the post, only for the offside flag to go up against him, but Diomande was onside when he broke in behind and hit the side netting moments later.
Madrid spurned another excellent counter-attacking chance early in the second half, with Jude Bellingham failing to get his pass off when Mbappé was supporting him against an isolated Martín.
And Barça made those reprieves count when Raphinha's shot proved too hot for Lunin to handle, after the Brazilian was cleverly found by Pedri on the right side of the area.
Lunin made a terrific, one-handed save to keep out Martín's header shortly afterwards, though he was lucky to see one Yamal effort drift narrowly wide and another smack Dean Huijsen in the face.

However, there was a cruel twist to come at the other end as, after some superb work from the outstanding Bellingham, substitute Eduardo Camavinga burst down the right flank and centred for Mbappé, who simply could not miss.
Just 24 hours before the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony takes place in London, Sunday's Clasico saw two of the main contenders for the prize – Yamal and Mbappé – go head-to-head.
And though the voting has long since been finalised, it was Mbappé who provided one final reminder of his credentials to be crowned the best player in the world.

There may have been a huge slice of fortune about Mbappé's opener, but his brace took him to five goals in two visits to Barça as a Madrid player. That is the most by any Blancos player since the start of 2013-14, surpassing Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema (four each).

Yamal, meanwhile, missed a glaring chance to equalise in the first half and was unable to hit the net with any of his five shots, which were worth a team-high 0.51 expected goals (xG). He also failed to create a single chance and only completed 76.6% of his passes (47/76)
And, on a night where Barça could have opened up a huge nine-point gap to Madrid and made La Liga history in the process, it was Mourinho who earned the bragging rights.

His unbeaten run in Clásico matches – which dates back to his previous spell in charge of Madrid – now stands at six games (W4 D2). He is just the third Blancos coach to enjoy such a run, after Miguel Muñoz (1962 to 1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001 to 2003) both had seven-match streaks.

1E4E085EEFDD68B70368E7DE0495A7B9.title: Preview: The lunchtime kick off sees Everton entertain Chelsea
1E4E085EEFDD68B70368E7DE0495A7B9.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: The lunchtime kick off sees Everton entertain ChelseaShareThe Toffess look to continue their unbeaten run with Chelsea the visitors to the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday.
They face a Chelsea side that have struggled on the road against Everton in recent years, winning just once since 2017.

Xabi Alonso’s men have been one of the most exciting teams to watch so far this season, conceding and scoring goals for fun. No side has conceded more goals than Chelsea so far this season, but only Brighton and Manchester City have scored more.
Everton are at the opposite end of the spectrum, scoring few but conceding even less.

David Moyes confirmed in his press conference that Vitalii Mykolenko has a chance of being available for this game. The left-back missed Everton’s draw against Hull City last time out, but he could be back for this one.
Jarrad Branthwaite has also been dealing with a problem, but it’s unclear if he’ll be ruled out.
Chelsea confirmed this week that Reece James is set for an extended period on the sidelines. The England international has undergone knee surgery and could be out for a few months.
Jamie Gittens and Emmanuel Emegha remain sidelined.

Everton’s draw with Hull City was a disappointing one for Moyes, mainly due to the number of chances they failed to convert. Although Thierno Barry did find the back of the net, he could have undoubtedly scored more, and missed chances have been the tale of Everton’s season so far.

In fact, only Nottingham Forest have missed more big chances in the Premier League so far this season. The Toffees have found the back of the net on just eight occasions, but there’s no doubt they could have scored more.
Chelsea’s attacking prowess is no secret. Alonso is getting a real tune out of Chelsea trio Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, and João Pedro, but they are being somewhat let down by their leaky defence.

The London club have conceded 10.2 xG so far this season, which isn’t at the level they’d expect if they want to be pushing for the Champions League places. They were much improved last time out against Bournemouth, so Alonso will be hoping that they’ve turned a corner.

The performances of Brazilian striker João Pedro have gone to another level this season. The help of Rogers and Palmer behind him have undoubtedly aided his performance levels, but he’s looking like more of a complete striker this campaign.

Everton will have to get a hold of him if they want to pick up a result against Chelsea this weekend. Even if the former Brighton man isn’t firing, Alonso has Rogers and Palmer, who are a constant threat, sitting behind him.
It feels like a game where there’s going to be plenty of goals. We’re going for a 3-2 victory to Chelsea.

          Has the WSL Become More Competitive Than Ever?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 13, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Five matchdays into the 2026-27 WSL season, the established hierarchy is under pressure as Arsenal struggle and Tottenham and London City Lionesses mount a push for Europe. But is the WSL genuinely more competitive than ever?
The 2026-27 Women’s Super League season is already challenging our pre-season expectations.
Arsenal are languishing in the bottom half, London City Lionesses and Tottenham are pushing for European qualification, and the traditional ‘big four' are facing competition from the chasing pack.

Results have been very unpredictable as well. Teams outside the usual elite are taking points off their more decorated opponents at a record rate, while the gap between the league's traditional powers and new challengers looks like it's shrinking. The three promoted sides are also showing signs of both promise and vulnerability in equal measure.
The only stable element seems to be reigning champions Manchester City, who have made a perfect start to their title defence.
So, with five matchdays played, is the WSL really becoming more competitive? We examine five key trends in the data to find out.

If there has been one recurring theme among WSL fans this season, it is that the league feels harder to call. There are fewer games that look straightforward on paper, particularly in the middle of the table where the gap between teams is becoming increasingly difficult to see.

Arsenal sitting 10th with five points after five games is the most obvious example. Manchester United, meanwhile, are three places above them in seventh. We're only five matchdays in, but the Red Devils have only finished above Arsenal once in WSL history, in 2022-23, when they finished second and Arsenal third.

Results to date have given us a lot of contrasting conclusions. London City opened their campaign by beating Man Utd, before losing to West Ham. United then beat West Ham, while Tottenham subsequently defeated the Hammers before being thumped 6-1 by London City. It definitely feels like anyone can beat anyone.

The data supports that theory as well.  Non-big four sides are averaging a record 0.42 points per game against the big four, the highest on record across a season since 2015 (0.43), while it is up from 0.30 last season.

There's something in the data that should give us pause here, though. At the moment, teams with a higher expected goals (xG) total have won just 62.9% of those matches, the lowest rate since Opta’s updated model was introduced in 2021-22. So there is a chance that the big four teams have just been on the receiving end of some unusual results in the opening stages of the campaign.

Underperformance against expected goals is something that's afflicting the league as a whole this season. The league-wide difference between goals scored and xG stands at -3.88, the first time it's been a negative figure in a WSL season since Opta's xG model was recently updated.
What’s even more interesting is that sides outside the traditional big four have been responsible for some of the biggest wins in the WSL season so far.

London City (6-1 vs Tottenham), Brighton (5-1 vs Charlton), Liverpool (4-0 vs Charlton) and Tottenham (7-0 vs Crystal Palace; 4-0 vs Aston Villa) have already produced five wins by a margin of four or more goals.

It is only the second time in WSL history that teams outside the traditional top four have recorded at least five such victories in a season. The only previous occasion was 2020-21, when there were eight; last season, there were just two.
By comparison, Chelsea are the only traditional big four side to have won by four or more goals this season, beating Man Utd 5-0 on MD2.

The established hierarchy is becoming less reliable, with more teams capable of producing convincing results against stronger opposition. That is perhaps the clearest evidence yet that the WSL is becoming more competitive.

The battle to break into the UWCL looks considerably more possible than it did for the chasing pack at the start of the season, as both London City Lionesses and Tottenham have made impressive starts.

Spurs have scored 16 goals, the joint-most in the WSL alongside Man City, with London City side just behind on 15. Tottenham’s attacking threat was particularly clear in their 7-0 win over Crystal Palace, when all seven goals came in the second half – the first time in WSL history a team had scored seven goals after half-time.
While London City’s aggressive squad overhaul initially sparked debate over whether a group of superstars could fit together immediately, the team is quickly proving they can.

1a1r7zsvh6jjk1lqbinvvlsw6a.title: Gasperini had no doubt Roma would bounce back from 'devastating' loss to Real Madrid
1a1r7zsvh6jjk1lqbinvvlsw6a.subtitle: Roma beat Genoa 2-0 on Saturday, with Gian Piero Gasperini picking up his 300th Serie A win as a coach in the process.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini harboured no doubts over whether Roma would be able to bounce back from their Champions League defeat to Real Madrid.
Roma went down 4-3 to Madrid in dramatic fashion on Wednesday, with Los Blancos scoring three late goals.
Yet Roma, despite the absence of Donyell Malen through suspension, eased to a 2-0 victory over Genoa to keep within touching distance of Serie A leaders Inter.
It marked Gasperini's 300th win in Serie A, as he became just the fifth coach to hit this milestone.
And he had no doubt Roma had the ability to put their defeat to Madrid behind them.
He told Sky Sport Italia: "Losing that way was devastating, because the performance had been so good, and thoroughly deserved.
"We ruined it for ourselves with three corner kicks in about seven minutes, but before that Real Madrid were not hurting us at all, in fact we were creating the chances.

"That's what irritated us, so I had no doubt that we would react well this evening. Many of the players had to experience it from the bench, so I knew they'd have that determination and energy in them today to let it all out on the pitch.
"Genoa might not have the champions of Real Madrid, but they are tactically very well-drilled, and it took us a while to get to grips with them."
Santiago Castro and youth product Emanuele Lulli grabbed the goals for Roma, who have taken 17 points from their first seven league matches for the first time since 2014-15 (18).
Roma are unbeaten in 40 of their last 41 home Serie A matches against Genoa (W33 D6), including all of their last 24 (W20 D4).

1a3ihy38uq4rl1xp8ps33154bl.title: ​Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City: Jackson double ends Maresca's winning start
1a3ihy38uq4rl1xp8ps33154bl.subtitle: Manchester City's winning Premier League start under Enzo Maresca ended on Saturday, as they slumped to a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Nicolas Jackson punished two sloppy errors as Manchester City's winning start to the Premier League season was halted in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa.
Jackson scored in either half at Villa Park, aided by a dismal touch from Marc Guehi for his sixth-minute opener and some weak goalkeeping from Gianluigi Donnarumma for his second goal on the hour.

Erling Haaland briefly got City level at the start of the second half, but Enzo Maresca's side were unable to respond after falling behind for a second time, as they failed to become only the third team to start a Premier League campaign with eight straight victories.
It did not take long for the suspect defending that has plagued City this season to rear its head, as a dreadful individual error from Guehi led to Villa's breakthrough.
Guehi was under no pressure as he looked to bring down a chipped pass from Ruben Dias, but he knocked the ball off his standing leg and into the path of John McGinn, who immediately released Jackson.
The Senegal international still had plenty to do, but he skipped inside Elliot Anderson then lashed into the roof of the net from close range.

Jackson dragged another effort wide, but it was City who spent much of the first half pushing for a goal. Zion Suzuki did brilliantly to tip Iliman Ndiaye's curler around the post and was later fortunate to see a near-identical effort from the same player strike the upright.
Between those close calls, Suzuki held Rayan Cherki's shot under pressure from Haaland, while Abdukodir Khusanov also called Villa's goalkeeper into action.

City's 29 touches in the Villa area during the first half were the most by any team in the first 45 minutes of a Premier League game this season, and their pressure finally told in the 52nd minute, as Ndiaye's hanging cross from the right was nodded home by Haaland.
The visitors had a glorious chance to go 2-1 up when Josko Gvardiol's shot was pushed onto the crossbar by Suzuki, but Villa then struck at the other end, with another error costing City.

Jackson's clever pass released Ibrahim Mbaye down the right flank, and when the substitute supplied a return ball into the middle, the shot from Villa's striker was straight at Donnarumma. However, the Italian went down awkwardly and let it squirm beneath him.

City were restricted to half-chances from then on, with Suzuki smothering the ball at Gvardiol's feet and Ian Maatsen clearing a Haaland header off his line, as Unai Emery's men clung on for another statement win.
Villa rise to the occasion again
Villa always seem to relish these fixtures at Villa Park, and they are now unbeaten in their last four home games against teams starting the day top of the Premier League table.
Prior to Saturday's victory, they also beat Arsenal 1-0 in December 2023 and 2-1 in December 2025, either side of a 2-2 draw with Liverpool in February 2025.
And City only had themselves to blame, with both goals being the direct result of lapses in concentration at the back.

Since the start of last season, Jan Paul van Hecke (four) is the only outfielder to make more errors leading to goals in the Premier League than Guehi (three), and the centre-back was hooked at half-time by Maresca, who sent on Rico Lewis in his place.

Donnarumma's error, meanwhile, was his third leading directly to a goal in the Premier League since he joined City last season. The only goalkeepers to commit more in that time are Bart Verbruggen (five) and Robin Roefs (four).
And it was Jackson who profited, becoming the first Villa player to score a Premier League brace against the league leaders since Andreas Weimann against Manchester United in November 2012.
Jackson has seven goals in all competitions this term, with Haaland (13) the only Premier League player to outscore him.

1a5q4mtlb29ld1to3ec75ja391.title: 'We had very few performers today' – Moyes frustrated by Everton after Hull draw
1a5q4mtlb29ld1to3ec75ja391.subtitle: Everton failed to hold onto their lead against Hull City on Sunday, eventually settling for a draw that left David Moyes disappointed.
paragraphs: David Moyes cut a frustrated figure after Everton's 2-2 draw with Hull City, claiming his team had "very few performers" who met the required level at the MKM Stadium.
Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring three minutes into the second half, though Everton soon restored parity through Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's header.

Dewsbury-Hall then turned provider for Thierno Barry to put the Toffees ahead in the 68th minute, only for substitute Mohamed Belloumi to rescue a point for Hull with a left-footed finish six minutes later.
The draw nevertheless extended the Toffees' unbeaten start to six Premier League matches, a feat they had previously achieved in 2006-07 (seven games) and 2013-14 (six).
Moyes, though, was not overly impressed.
"A really frustrating day. We get a draw and it's a decent point away from home," Moyes told Sky Sports.
"Hull have done really well here, but we should have won the game. We had very few performing today. I'm frustrated with it a little bit.
"There were not many performing at the level I think they have been or can perform at. I could hardly pick a player out who I could give a pass mark.
"When we went 2-1 up, I didn't think they could come back. We were so comfortable and didn't look like we should be conceding. A couple of defensive lapses were really poor.
"Everybody here needs to step up their game."
Hull, meanwhile, preserved their unbeaten home record this season thanks to another decisive contribution from Belloumi.
The winger has now scored three goals and assisted two more, contributing to five of Hull's eight Premier League goals this term (63%).
"I'm very happy with the boys because we showed a great mentality and we equalised," Hull head coach Sergej Jakirovic told Sky Sports. "It's a good point for us.

"Everton are still unbeaten after six games. It's difficult to beat them. They have high tactical discipline and are strong in challenges, especially the centre-backs. It was not easy but we scored two nice goals."

1a9hd2soo27qg1onzg8kakvn2l.title: Real Madrid 1-0 Villarreal: Diomande opens Bernabeu account as Vinicius sees red
1a9hd2soo27qg1onzg8kakvn2l.subtitle: Despite seeing Vinicius Junior sent off for a hair pull, Real Madrid held on for all three points against Villarreal in LaLiga.
paragraphs: Real Madrid held on for a 1-0 victory against Villarreal after Vinicius Junior was shown a straight red card for Jose Mourinho's side.
Yan Diomande scored his first goal for Los Blancos, and his strike was enough to secure all three points at the Estadio Bernabeu as Madrid got back in the win column in LaLiga.
After Pape Gueye dragged wide early on, Kylian Mbappe struck the woodwork in the seventh minute as he could not divert his left-footed attempt from Alvaro Carreras' cross on target.

Mbappe went close again before the break, shooting straight at Peter Gulacsi after a brilliant lofted pass from Trent Alexander-Arnold, while Arda Guler failed to test the Villarreal goalkeeper from a tight angle.

Madrid finally broke the deadlock in the 62nd minute as Diomande took in a pass from Federico Valverde and arrowed a strike into the bottom-left corner, though the hosts were dealt a blow 10 minutes later.

Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid's lead after converting from Jude Bellingham's cut-back, but the goal was ruled out and the Brazilian was instead shown a red card as he had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up to the goal.

1abufti19tkb7185h371q2pybp.title: Ronaldo statement 'beyond anything I've ever seen' – Rooney slams former team-mate
1abufti19tkb7185h371q2pybp.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's explosive exit from the Portugal squad has prompted strong criticism, including from his former team-mate Wayne Rooney.
paragraphs: Wayne Rooney believes Cristiano Ronaldo's explosive statement regarding his exit from the Portugal camp went "beyond anything" he has seen in football and was "so wrong".
During the recent international break, Ronaldo made headlines by storming out of Portugal's camp after Jorge Jesus left him on the bench throughout a 2-1 Nations League win in Norway.
Ronaldo subsequently released a statement in which he accused Jesus – who was his head coach at Al-Nassr last season – of a "breach of trust".

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner revealed his decision to leave Portugal's camp came after Jesus refused to read a series of pre-agreed statements at a press conference, which amounted to an apology to Ronaldo, compared him to Pele and Diego Maradona, and praised his interactions with fans.
While Ronaldo insists he remains available for selection by his country, the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has suspended the forward pending an investigation.
And Rooney, who made 140 Premier League appearances alongside Ronaldo for Manchester United between 2004 and 2009, felt he was out of line.

"My thoughts on Ronaldo are just: 'Why?' It was the same day [Lionel] Messi was retiring from Argentina and for him to come out of the Portugal squad in that way, then put that statement out... It's just wrong in every sense," Rooney said on The United Stand.
"To undermine your manager and undermine your team-mates the way he has – it was just so wrong. To undermine the Portuguese FA, everything about it was just wrong.
"From a football point of view, from being a team-mate of his and a manager, it wasn't nice to see.
"It comes down to every player. You have to stop playing international football eventually and, unfortunately, he's not dealing with it well. It's uncomfortable to see.
"You can't tell a manager what he's got to say. That just goes beyond anything I've ever seen."
Ronaldo and Jesus had seemingly enjoyed a strong relationship prior to the row, with the 72-year-old leading Al-Nassr to the Saudi Pro League title last season.
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 appearances under Jesus at club level in 2025-26, averaging one every 99 minutes.

But in his only Portugal outing under Jesus, in a 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, Ronaldo had seven shots with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.03 without scoring – his most attempts without netting in any game since a World Cup qualifier against the Republic of Ireland in October 2025 (also seven).
Since the start of 2025, Portugal have won five of their six games (D1, 83.3% win rate) when Ronaldo has not appeared, compared to 10 of 17 with him (D4 L3, 59% win rate).

1ad3x11g6jmbs1kgn0xqkvz17w.title: Mourinho defends Vinicius from growing criticism
1ad3x11g6jmbs1kgn0xqkvz17w.subtitle: Vinicius Junior was far from his best again for Real Madrid, but Jose Mourinho refused to pile more pressure on the Brazilian winger.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho insisted he was "happy" with Vinicius Junior's performance in Real Madrid's Champions League win over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
Los Blancos cruised to a 4-1 victory at home, with Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande getting on the scoresheet.

Mbappe has scored in each of his last five Champions League appearances for Madrid, now the second-longest scoring streak of his career in the competition (after a six-game run for Paris Saint-Germain – November 2021 to September 2022).

At 19 years and 341 days, Diomande, who replaced Vinicius, became the youngest Madrid substitute to score and assist in a Champions League match, and the fourth-youngest player to achieve this with any team in the history of the competition.
And Diomande's recent success has coincided with Vinicius' dip in form since Mourinho's arrival.

Vinicius has not attempted a single dribble in his last two matches across all competitions, the first time he has strung together two consecutive starts without attempting a dribble in his Los Blancos career.
It is just one fewer time than in the rest of his starts with Madrid (three in 309).
Nevertheless, Mourinho came to Vinicius' defence, claiming his substitution was due to Madrid's strong squad depth.
"If he is sad, that is a very personal matter. You may have a perception, but I think only he can openly tell you how he feels or doesn't feel," Mourinho said on Vinicius.
"As a coach, I am happy with the match he played. From Vinicius, more is always expected, and that he is individually decisive, but he played a match that I liked.

"Of the three attackers, he had the greatest responsibility from the defensive balance standpoint. Leipzig's right-back was a player who moved between the lines, and Vinicius closed him down very well. The ball entered the central area only once.
"Then, offensively, he wasn’t overwhelming, but he was balanced. He didn’t lose possession and had an action where the goalkeeper made a great save.

"The substitution isn't the decision of a coach who isn't happy; it's the decision of a coach who has a rich bench. With the substitution, I knew I could bring a different speed to the game with players like Yan (Diomande) or Endrick.
"As a coach, I am happy with what he has done."

1auf8cupqwdpn1rj3rx3mblv1a.title: Hallgrimsson says physical and mental fatigue saw Ireland 'run out of gas' against Austria
1auf8cupqwdpn1rj3rx3mblv1a.subtitle: The Republic of Ireland squandered a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 with Austria, which Heimir Hallgrimsson blamed on physical and mental tiredness.
paragraphs: Heimir Hallgrimsson always expected the Republic of Ireland to "run out of gas" against Austria, as he put their 2-2 Nations League draw down to physical and mental fatigue.
Ireland stormed into a 2-0 lead in their third match in Nations League Group B3, as they attempted to build on last Sunday's 3-0 victory over Israel.
Troy Parrott scored both of Ireland's goals in Dublin, with his first being an incredible solo effort in which he skipped past two defenders before slotting past Florian Wiegele.
Parrot's second was a penalty late in the first half, which came after the game had twice been halted due to protests related to Ireland's upcoming reverse fixture against Israel.
And Hallgrimsson felt the mental toll of the debate surrounding that game – which will take place on Sunday on neutral ground in Belgrade – played a part in Ireland's second-half collapse.

Liam Kitching's error allowed Alexander Prass to pull a goal back for Austria in the 71st minute, and shortly afterwards, fellow substitute Michael Gregoritsch curled a free-kick past Caoimhin Kelleher to equalise, with Austria remaining top of the group on seven points from three games.
"Obviously we were happy to be 2-0 up at half-time," Hallgrimsson told RTE Sport afterwards.
"We knew, and I told you before the game, that this team is high energy; and we knew that we needed to do some rotation and make changes.
"I felt like we just lost organisation, probably due to tiredness, and then you start to make mistakes.
"That was something that we were obviously not happy with, but the first half was good, the organisation was good, we know we can do this.
"I expected us to run out of gas at some point, but maybe not so quickly. This week has not only been physically difficult, but it's been mentally difficult and that takes a lot of energy as well."

Parrott's brace took him to nine goals in his last six competitive outings for Ireland, while his four braces for his country are the most any player has ever scored for them while aged under 25, surpassing Robbie Keane's three.

Prass scored Austria's first goal just 208 seconds after coming off the bench, opening his international account on his 23rd senior cap, while Gregoritsch has now netted 25 times for Thursday's visitors, becoming the 11th Austrian to hit that figure.
Ireland have four points on the board ahead of their return fixture against Israel, who are bottom after earning their first point in a goalless draw with Kosovo on Thursday.

1awckzecix70419z8th9divu1y.title: Maresca passes credit to Man City players after record-breaking Premier League start
1awckzecix70419z8th9divu1y.subtitle: Enzo Maresca's start with Manchester City has officially been the best in Premier League history, following their win over Ipswich Town.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca insisted all the credit must go to his Manchester City players after recording the best start by any manager in charge of a Premier League club.

Saturday's 3-2 victory over Ipswich Town at the Etihad Stadium maintained City's perfect start to the campaign and made Maresca the first manager to ever win their first seven matches in charge of a club in the competition.
Only Chelsea under Jose Mourinho in 2005-06 (first nine games) and Liverpool under Jurgen Klopp in 2019-20 (first eight) have ever enjoyed longer winning starts to a Premier League campaign.
Both of those sides went on to win the title in those respective seasons, and Maresca could not have been more pleased with the way his players have adapted to his methods.

With so much off-the-pitch uncertainty surrounding City, who were recently found guilty of "systematically" breaching the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period, the Italian knows it would have been easy for them to lose their focus.
Asked if he was proud of his personal record, Maresca said: "Absolutely, but I also understand we give credit to the players.

"They only need to be worried about people inside the club, and I give the credit to them. They are not worried about people who judge from outside, because those are people working to create problems.
"Inside, I promise the players are happy, they're getting credit and I give the credit to them. It's a matter of winning games in this business.
"We were able to win seven in a row and what made me very happy was working day-by-day with the players, the way I can see them improving.
"Today, I thought we controlled the game, created chances and were good off the ball. We are doing well, and I think that's the most important thing."

Though it was Erling Haaland's brace that ultimately secured the points for City, Phil Foden opened the scoring, ending his longest-ever run without a Premier League goal, having endured a 23-match drought since netting against Crystal Palace in December 2025.
And Maresca is determined for Foden to reclaim his place as one of the Premier League's best players, having won the competition's Player of the Season award as recently as 2023-24.
"With Phil, I have said it many times, I knew him from years ago, and for me, he's one of the best Premier League players," Maresca said.
"And since day one, it's been my duty to help him to be one of the best players again.
"I'm very happy about his goal, and hopefully it can be just the beginning of many goals and good performances."

Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil, meanwhile, was generally positive about a performance in which the Tractor Boys generated 1.66 expected goals but gave up plenty of big chances at the other end, allowing City to rack up 3.53 xG.
"We did have a go. There are a few things we need to do better, then it's fine margins in a game like that," O'Neil said.
"I'm proud of the group. It's not what we came for, and we thought we could take points, so we're disappointed we haven't.
"But the players gave everything. The second goal I'm not happy with, and then there were a few bits that were just fine margins."

1ay7lniq06mzw1m1807f3fdoe9.title: 'It gave me goosebumps' – Pochettino impressed by USA's youngsters
1ay7lniq06mzw1m1807f3fdoe9.subtitle: Mauricio Pochettino fielded a new-look United States team against Peru, and he is thrilled by what he saw from the younger players.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino says the United States' 4-1 victory over Peru "gave me goosebumps" after he fielded a lot of new faces at Inter.co Stadium.
The Argentine head coach, who signed a new four-year deal following the World Cup, handed out 11 senior team debuts on Saturday, with many of his new stars shining.
Justin Ellis and Julian Hall were both on the scoresheet during their first international cap, with Malik Tillman and Sebastian Berhalter also hitting the back of the net.
Mathis Albert also impressed off the bench, with one of his first involvements seeing him win the penalty from which Tillman scored.
Of the 11 debutants, eight of them were teenagers, and Pochettino was full of praise for how quickly they settled into the team.
"I am so proud of the performance," Pochettino said.
"To see these young players come in, embrace the moment, and play with this kind of freedom and courage – it gave me goosebumps at times.
"It is about opportunity: giving the opportunity, and then they have to take it. What we saw is that the future is here, but soccer is about now. They showed they can compete right now."
All eyes were on 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan – who turns 17 on Monday – as he became the youngest player to earn a senior cap for the USA since Freddy Adu in 2006.
He was one of three debutants in the starting line-up, and Pochettino made it clear that he is determined to open the door to as many players as he can during the new World Cup cycle.
"Nobody can think their place belongs to them because of what they did in the past," he added.
"It's a fresh start, a new cycle. Everyone has the door open, but you must earn it every single day."

1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.title: Real Madrid 'living in another galaxy' over referee claims, says LaLiga chief Tebas
1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.subtitle: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has slammed Real Madrid for their treatment of referee Ortiz Arias following Sunday's loss to Atletico Madrid.
paragraphs: Real Madrid are "living in another galaxy" if they believe LaLiga's officials are biased against them, the competition's president Javier Tebas said amid a fierce debate over refereeing standards.
Madrid were beaten 2-1 by Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby at the Estadio Metropolitano, but the controversial nature of their loss sparked a furious reaction from Los Blancos.

Jose Mourinho's team had Dean Huijsen sent off for a last-man foul early in the second half, but Madrid felt Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, saying they were the "story of the game" and describing referee Ortiz Arias as weak and inexperienced.
Atleti hit back on their social media channels on Monday, posting an image taken during Mourinho's press conference alongside the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Madrid used the title "a terrible refereeing performance decides the derby" for their official club-produced match report, accompanied by images of the Lee and Romero challenges.
And Tebas – who has criticised Madrid's treatment of referees and desire to set up a breakaway European Super League in the past – has now slammed the club's behaviour.

"Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime's television, building the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy," Tebas wrote on X, responding to a Spanish media article that alleged referees routinely favour Madrid's opponents.
"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.
"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.
"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.
"GET THE BLINDERS OFF! It's September, and they're already claiming the League is tainted. Nobody with common sense believes that old excuse anymore."

Madrid previously sent a formal letter of complaint about LaLiga's referees to the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) in 2025, prompting Tebas to accuse Madrid of harming the competition and "building a story of victimhood."

Madrid were beaten 2-1 by Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby at the Estadio Metropolitano, but the controversial nature of their loss sparked a furious reaction from Los Blancos.

Jose Mourinho's team had Dean Huijsen sent off for a last-man foul early in the second half, but Madrid felt Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.

Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, saying they were the "story of the game" and describing referee Ortiz Arias as weak and inexperienced. 

Atleti hit back on their social media channels on Monday, posting an image taken during Mourinho's press conference alongside the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."

Madrid used the title "a terrible refereeing performance decides the derby" for their official club-produced match report, accompanied by images of the Lee and Romero challenges.

And Tebas – who has criticised Madrid's treatment of referees and desire to set up a breakaway European Super League in the past – has now slammed the club's behaviour.

"Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime's television, building the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy," Tebas wrote on X, responding to a Spanish media article that alleged referees routinely favour Madrid's opponents. 

"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.

"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.

"GET THE BLINDERS OFF! It's September, and they're already claiming the League is tainted. Nobody with common sense believes that old excuse anymore."

Madrid previously sent a formal letter of complaint about LaLiga's referees to the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) in 2025, prompting Tebas to accuse Madrid of harming the competition and "building a story of victimhood."

1b69u0q1qpg61114oxvae5thsv.title: Bastoni confident Italy can take on anyone after France draw
1b69u0q1qpg61114oxvae5thsv.subtitle: Italy fought from a goal down to draw 1-1 with France in the Nations League, giving Roberto Mancini's side a huge confidence boost.
paragraphs: Alessandro Bastoni believes Italy "can do it against anyone" after holding France to a draw in the Nations League.
Italy drew 1-1 with Zinedine Zidane's side at the Stade de France on Friday, with Bastoni cancelling out Michael Olise's stunning opener.

After also netting against Turkiye, Bastoni is only the third centre-back to score in two consecutive appearances for Italy in the last 10 years, after Gianluca Mancini (October-November 2025) and Alessio Romagnoli (October-November 2019).
Gianluigi Donnarumma also played a huge role in the draw, making seven saves, including an impressive double save to keep out Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele in quick succession.
Only twice has Donnarumma made more saves in a single game for the Azzurri: 10 against Bosnia-Herzegovina in March 2026 and eight against Spain in June 2024.
"It was a tough game, we knew it would be, it's hardly news, but I am so happy with the team performance," Bastoni told RAI Sport.

"We fought hard, we suffered, we even ruined some of France's objectives for tonight, as they were prepared for a big celebration. We knew we weren't coming here for a walk in the park, and that's how it was.

"It's certainly pleasing to score again, but the moment it was done, I thought we had to make sure we didn't concede another, otherwise it was all points. This is a good result that boosts our confidence going forward.
"It's a strong signal, because if we can put in a performance like this against France in Paris, then we can do it against anyone."
Italy won the expected goals (xG) 1.46 to 1.21, with both Moise Kean and Davide Frattesi squandering good opportunities in the first half.

Nevertheless, head coach Roberto Mancini agreed with Bastoni's sentiment, as he told RAI Sport: "We knew it would be a very difficult match, especially at the start, but we did well to allow them very little in terms of chances, even if they had more possession.
"We played as a team, attacking and defending together, and so it is certainly a very positive evening for us.
"I wanted this to be another step forward in our journey. I liked that we tried to play football, despite being against an extraordinary France side full of champions."

1bfm53a7z5fhg1vz088ehy5x16.title: Mastroeni backs Real Salt Lake 'to put their best foot forward against anyone'
1bfm53a7z5fhg1vz088ehy5x16.subtitle: Real Salt Lake's playoff push continues with an away clash against Austin FC, who are unlikely to qualify for the postseason.
paragraphs: Pablo Mastroeni believes his Real Salt Lake side can "put their best foot forward against anyone" as they look to surge into the playoff places.
RSL are 10th in the Western Conference ahead of a trip to Austin FC, just two points behind the Los Angeles Galaxy, who have played one game more.
Mastroeni's side are in good form heading into the final three games of the regular season, winning three of their last five matches, including their last two.
After a 3-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City, RSL defeated in-form St. Louis City 3-0 at home after a brace from Sergi Solans and a strike from Dominik Marczuk.
RSL were handed a further boost as club captain Justen Glad made his first appearance since May after suffering a groin injury.
Amid their recent form and with key players returning to fitness, Mastroeni is optimistic his side can take on anyone in the league.
"I'll back this group to be able to put their best foot forward against anyone," Mastroeni said. "Given the way we're playing and the mentality that the group has."
"I think in all phases, we played fantastic [against St. Louis City]. But we have got no time to celebrate.
"We have got to win out. That was a good performance to build upon."
Austin are not yet out of playoff contention, but despite a 2-1 win over Sporting KC, their chances are slim.
With three games to go, Austin are seven points off the final playoff spot in 14th, with a win in this fixture necessary if they are to keep their hopes alive.
Austin FC – Myrto Uzuni
Uzuni scored both goals in Austin's win at Sporting KC on Saturday, the second player to score multiple goals in a match for Austin since the start of last season.
Austin's three multi-goal performances since the start of last season are the fewest in MLS in that time.
Real Salt Lake – Sergi Solans
Solans scored twice for Real Salt Lake on Saturday, his third multi-goal game of the season.

Only four RSL players have had more than three multi-goal games in a single season: Jeff Cunningham (four) in 2006, Alvaro Saborio (five) in 2012, Cristian Arango (five) in 2024 and Andres Gomez (four) in 2024.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Austin snapped a five-match winless run (D2 L3) with a 2-1 victory at Sporting KC, but they remain winless in seven straight home matches (D3 L4), the longest such streak in club history.
Real Salt Lake is unbeaten in six straight matches against Austin (W4 D2), including winning the last two. Neither team has managed three consecutive wins over the other before.
After winning one of their previous 16 regular-season matches (D5 L10), Real Salt Lake have back-to-back wins.
RSL have a record of W7 D0 L1 when scoring three or more goals this season, while they have won just four of 23 matches when scoring fewer than three.
Real Salt Lake – 39.2%

1bkwqpeac33wa10g1f977ixjbp.title: Baleba can make 'a big difference' for Man Utd, says Stam
1bkwqpeac33wa10g1f977ixjbp.subtitle: Manchester United have struggled so far in 2026-27, but Jaap Stam has backed Carlos Baleba to help turn things around.
paragraphs: Former Manchester United defender Jaap Stam believes Carlos Baleba can make "a big difference" for the Red Devils after a poor start to the season.
United are 13th in the Premier League after their draw with 10-man Tottenham last weekend, while they were also eliminated from the EFL Cup in the third round by Brighton.

The pressure on head coach Michael Carrick then increased on Tuesday after their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, while Lisandro Martinez's attack on United's leadership did not help matters.
United have lost three of their last five games in all competitions (D2), as many as in their previous 21 games under Carrick (W14 D4).
It is also their longest winless run since a streak of six games without a victory in January 2025 (D2 L4).
However, after missing the start of the season through injury, £70m summer signing Baleba has featured in their last two games.
He came off the bench against Spurs for his debut before starting against Atleti; he won six of his eight duels against Diego Simeone's side before being replaced in the 66th minute.
After encouraging signs from Baleba in his first two appearances, Stam has backed the 22-year-old to make an impact in United's midfield.
"You can see the promise of Baleba, the quality that he has," Stam told Flashscore.
"He made a difference straight away, which is very promising of course. Hopefully he can start and keep that up for a long time during a game, for 95 minutes.

"I think that's very important, because Carrick is still looking for the ideal partnership of midfield players in the middle of the field, who can work together, who can bring that fresh spark together with Bruno and be dominant against the opposition, but also defensively not give away too much.
"It's a combination of both that he's looking for, and with Baleba in there, I think that makes a big difference."
Baleba will be hoping to make his first Premier League start for United on Sunday when they face rivals Leeds United at Elland Road.

1bn2p0w777kst101usdlqatwxe.title: Pochettino thanks United States players for 'massive effort' after extending winning streak
1bn2p0w777kst101usdlqatwxe.subtitle: The United States made it four wins from four post-World Cup, much to the delight of head coach Mauricio Pochettino.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino praised his United States players for their "massive effort" in beating Canada to make it four wins in a row.
Justin Ellis' 29th-minute goal – his second in three games this window – earned the USA a 1-0 win over their neighbours in Minnesota.
Tuesday's friendly at Allianz Field lacked any real quality, with Luc De Fougerolles firing against the bar from the best chance Canada had to equalise.
However, Pochettino says the effort put in by his players on the back of wins over Peru, Chile and Mexico is what pleased him most.
"It was a massive effort," he told reporters. "We played four games in two weeks.
"To play with the same intensity, the same commitment, the same passion is not easy.
"I'm not happy because we won. I'm happy because of the performance and the commitment that the players showed."
Pochettino made six changes from the 3-0 win over Mexico, with rising star Cavan Sullivan dropping out and not featuring from the bench.
Mathis Albert and Brian Schwake were handed full debuts as Pochettino again used this first post-World Cup window as a chance to experiment.
"We need to give credit to the players," he said. It was really tough to play in Orlando, St Louis, Arizona because of the time zones.
"To be honest, as a coach it has been really tough and for the players they have needed to perform.
"Nobody has said anything negative and that is why we have performed."
Canada, who like fellow co-hosts USA were eliminated from the World Cup at the last-16 stage, edged the shot count in Minnesota.
However, a lack of cutting edge proved costly as Jesse Marsch's side saw their two-game winning run come to an end.
"We just weren't decisive enough and aggressive enough to get first contacts and finish off a bunch of the plays," Marsch told reporters.
"There were a lot of 'almost' actions, but we were not effective enough in the final third.
"Some of it is decisiveness and some of it is understanding different roles. But I don't want to be overly critical.
"There's a lot of good stuff going on, but you want to see a team on the pitch that's more decisive and ready to take moments. We're not quite there yet."

1bupib0u5cuyb1i5jz7jfjrjwe.title: Quill lauds Dallas' resilience after securing playoff berth
1bupib0u5cuyb1i5jz7jfjrjwe.subtitle: FC Dallas will definitely feature in the playoffs and are looking to keep up their momentum against the Houston Dynamo on Saturday.
paragraphs: FC Dallas head coach Eric Quill hailed his team's resilience against the Seattle Sounders as they secured their playoff berth in MLS ahead of travelling to Houston Dynamo.
Last weekend, Dallas lost 3-2 to Charlotte FC, but they bounced back with a 1-0 win over the Seattle Sounders in midweek to move up to third in the Western Conference.
They had to wait for their playoff berth to be confirmed, with results later on Wednesday meaning they will be featuring in the postseason for the second straight year.
The loss to Charlotte is their only defeat in their last eight league games, and Quill was impressed by how Dallas responded to that setback.
"I told the guys that the last 20 minutes were what I was most proud of," Quill said after beating Seattle.
"You could see that when their legs were gone and their minds were exhausted, they were still giving everything they had.
"They were diving around, putting their bodies on the line, blocking shots and dealing with more corners than we wanted to face.

"Seattle is a tough team to beat any night you play them, but after what happened in Charlotte the other night, getting a response like this is exactly what we needed heading into Houston on Saturday."
As for the Dynamo, they have slipped down the West after a run of five games without a victory (D3 L2), though they remain fifth in the table.
They drew 3-3 with San Diego FC in midweek, giving up a lead late on, but Guilherme once again played a vital role, including his 16th league goal of 2026.
The Brazilian also has nine assists on top of that, and Houston head coach Ben Olsen is thrilled to have him in the squad.
"He's carried a big load for us – it's too much. So we as a team have to continue to work on whether we can take some of that pressure off of him," said Olsen.
"It's not healthy to live on one guy scoring and providing that much.
"But when you need something [or] you need a play, it's nice to have that type of player on the field for us."
Houston Dynamo – Guilherme
Guilherme had two goals and an assist in Houston's draw against San Diego on Wednesday.
He is the first Dynamo player to record two goals and an assist in a regular-season match since Nelson Quinones in October 2023.
Kaick scored the lone goal in Dallas' victory over Seattle Sounders, his third goal in his last seven matches.
He had managed just three goals in his first 49 regular-season MLS appearances before matching that total over his last seven games.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Dallas snapped an 11-match winless run at Houston with a 2-1 victory at Shell Energy Stadium in February 2025, the club's first win at Houston since 2016.
The Dynamo have won only three of the last 13 meetings between the sides in Houston, with eight of those ending in draws.

Dallas have won seven of their last 11 regular-season matches (D2 L2) following a 1-0 victory over Seattle, which was their third clean sheet in four matches after they managed just four clean sheets in their first 25 matches of the 2026 regular season.

The Dynamo have won only one of their last nine matches (D5 L3), including going five straight without a win (D3 L2), after a five-match winning streak in July-August, leaving this one too close to call for the Opta supercomputer.
