1bw4b4j8qe5t618na967le382d.title: Alaba joins Udinese as free agent following Real Madrid exit
1bw4b4j8qe5t618na967le382d.subtitle: Following five successful years with Real Madrid, David Alaba will now ply his trade in Serie A after joining Udinese on Thursday.
paragraphs: David Alaba has laid out his ambitions to "win again" after the former Real Madrid defender completed his move to Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.
Alaba has joined Udinese as a free agent on a contract that will run until the end of the 2026-27 season, following five successful years in the Spanish capital.
The 34-year-old brings with him a wealth of European experience, having also spent 13 years with Bayern Munich before making the move to Madrid in 2021.

He won 25 trophies with the Bundesliga giants, before going on to win two LaLiga crowns and two Champions League titles, in addition to a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana, a UEFA Super Cup, a Club World Cup and an Intercontinental Cup with Los Blancos.
Alaba was a regular in his first few seasons with Madrid and started their 2022 Champions League final win against Liverpool, but injuries have hampered him in recent seasons.
The Austria international missed 13 months of action after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in December 2023, and failed to rediscover his impressive form.
He was restricted to 17 appearances in 2023-24, across all competitions, then made 14 in 2024-25 and 16 in 2025-26.

He only played 600 minutes in 2024-25 and was limited to 575 last season, with both of those campaigns ending without silverware, something he intends to change having now sealed his switch to Udinese.
"I've had a lot of different experiences, and I've won a lot during my career, but one thing hasn't changed. I want to compete and win again," Alaba said.
"I still want to achieve something special and that is the mentality I will bring to Udinese."
Alaba joins an Udinese side that sit 13th in Serie A this season, having taken four points from their opening five league games of 2026-27.
Only Venzia (13), Fiorentina and Monza (both 12) have conceded more league goals than Udinese (11) this term, something Alaba will be aiming to improve.
"The signing of David Alaba is a source of enormous pride for the whole club," said Udinese general manager Franco Collavino.
"We're welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival demonstrates Udinese's desire to grow and compete at the highest levels."
Udinese return to action after the extended international break on October 12, with a trip to Torino up next.

He won 25 trophies with the Bundesliga giants, before going on to win two LaLiga crowns and two Champions League titles, in addition to a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana, a UEFA Super Cup, a Club World Cup and an Intercontinental Cup with Los Blancos. 

Alaba was a regular in his first few seasons with Madrid and started their 2022 Champions League final win against Liverpool, but injuries have hampered him in recent seasons. 

The Austria international missed 13 months of action after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in December 2023, and failed to rediscover his impressive form. 

He was restricted to 17 appearances in 2023-24, across all competitions, then made 14 in 2024-25 and 16 in 2025-26.

He only played 600 minutes in 2024-25 and was limited to 575 last season, with both of those campaigns ending without silverware, something he intends to change having now sealed his switch to Udinese. 

"I've had a lot of different experiences, and I've won a lot during my career, but one thing hasn't changed. I want to compete and win again," Alaba said.

"I still want to achieve something special and that is the mentality I will bring to Udinese."

Alaba joins an Udinese side that sit 13th in Serie A this season, having taken four points from their opening five league games of 2026-27. 

Only Venzia (13), Fiorentina and Monza (both 12) have conceded more league goals than Udinese (11) this term, something Alaba will be aiming to improve. 

"The signing of David Alaba is a source of enormous pride for the whole club," said Udinese general manager Franco Collavino.

"We're welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival demonstrates Udinese's desire to grow and compete at the highest levels."

Udinese return to action after the extended international break on October 12, with a trip to Torino up next.

1c0qv932xf7y61j04brselmuro.title: Yamal 'on his way to being a legendary player', says Spain boss De la Fuente
1c0qv932xf7y61j04brselmuro.subtitle: Lamine Yamal's exceptional goalscoring form continued as Spain beat Czechia in the Nations League, drawing lofty praise from his head coach.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal is already on the path to becoming a legend of the game and "never ceases to amaze", Luis de la Fuente declared after Spain's win over Czechia on Saturday.
La Roja remain top of Nations League Group A3 with maximum points after three games, having held off a second-half fightback from Czechia to win 3-1 in Oviedo.

First-half goals from Barcelona duo Yamal and Rodri put Spain in a commanding position, though Czechia later had them on the ropes following Jiri Slama's goal, only for Ladislav Krejci's red card and a late strike from Mikel Merino to end their comeback hopes.
Yamal's opening goal was a trademark left-footed curler from the right corner of the area, after he exchanged passes with club-mate Dani Olmo.

He now has 12 goals in his last nine games for club and country combined (four for Spain in the Nations League, eight for Barcelona in all competitions), with a 3-1 LaLiga win over Sevilla being the only game in which he has failed to find the net in that period.
Asked if he was ever surprised by Yamal's production in his post-match press conference, De la Fuente said: "He never ceases to amaze us all.
"He is so talented, there is much more to see of the best version of Lamine.
"He is growing by leaps and bounds. He is a reference for the national team, a player with great weight, and we have to celebrate him."

Asked about Yamal's Ballon d'Or prospects, with just over three weeks left before the award ceremony in London, De la Fuente added: "If he were the only Spaniard among the nominees, I would tell him that he is the best in the world.
"He does everything well. If he is not the best because of competition with other Spaniards, he is one of the best. But he is on the way to being a legendary player."
Yamal was one of two players to be substituted at half-time, alongside Alex Baena, with De la Fuente looking to keep his attackers fresh ahead of Tuesday's trip to Croatia.
La Roja's performance levels dipped sharply after the interval, as they only registered five shots and 0.75 expected goals, compared to 13 attempts and 1.35 xG in the first period.
But De la Fuente insists it was necessary to manage the winger's load, saying: "We take care of Lamine exactly the same as the other players.
"We do not make a distinction. We take care of everyone equally.
"We thought that the game would go in a different direction, but we wanted to take away some minutes from his load, so that he could stay in the best condition."

1c2qypi0yn8gu186216fgvd6tv.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day ban from Portugal action
1c2qypi0yn8gu186216fgvd6tv.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended from Portugal duty for 30 days and handed a small fine for his explosive comments last month.
paragraphs: Portugal's Football Federation has handed Cristiano Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for his comments over coach Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo left the Portugal squad last month, and subsequently claimed Jesus had "broken his word".
The 41-year-old then released a long statement in which he explained why he felt wronged, though he admitted he had made a mistake and should receive a punishment.
Jesus left the door open for Ronaldo to return to action for Portugal in next month's Nations League games.
The Portuguese Football Federation did not confirm when Ronaldo's ban starts.
Portugal host Denmark on November 14 before facing Wales three days later.
Ronaldo has also been handed a fine of just €255.
He has scored 981 career goals, and is the highest-scoring player in the history of international football.

1c3tv7581tc0j1cd9f7k4de8g9.title: Diomande will have every chance to succeed at Madrid, says former coach Demichelis
1c3tv7581tc0j1cd9f7k4de8g9.subtitle: Martin Demichelis only worked with Yan Diomande for a short time in pre-season, but he expects the winger to thrive at Real Madrid.
paragraphs: Yan Diomande has all the necessary attributes to be a long-term success at Real Madrid, Martin Demichelis declared ahead of the winger's reunion with RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
Madrid and Leipzig will face off at the Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on matchday three of the 2026-27 Champions League, with Diomande going up against some familiar faces.

He only left the Bundesliga club for Madrid in August, with the Spanish giants shelling out €140m including add-ons after seeing off competition for his signature from Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain.
The Ivory Coast international has been in excellent form since the international break, scoring his first two LaLiga goals in victories over Villarreal and Sevilla.

He has five goal involvements for Madrid this season across all competitions (two goals, three assists), with only Kylian Mbappe (13), Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler (six each) boasting more for Jose Mourinho's men.

And ahead of Diomande facing his old club on Wednesday, Demichelis said he only wished he was able to work with the jet-heeled winger properly, having taken charge just a few weeks before his departure.

"I couldn't enjoy him much! I had been named Leipzig coach in July and he was at the World Cup, so I know Yan more from watching him on television than from being able to enjoy him on the pitch," Demichelis told AS.
"He is one of those players today who can make a difference both on the left and on the right, thanks to his great control of the ball with both feet.
"At a great club like Madrid, I have no doubt that he is going to have great coaches and great team-mates, but it will depend a bit more on him, on his desire for self-improvement."

But it remains to be seen whether Diomande will start against Leipzig, as Mourinho confirmed in his pre-match press conference that Vinicius Junior – who is currently serving a four-match ban in LaLiga – will return to his lineup on the left flank.
Mourinho said: "Vinicius is going to play on the left wing. Yan doesn't know if he's going to play or not."
This will be the fifth Champions League meeting between Madrid and Leipzig, with the German side only winning one of the previous four (D1 L2) – 3-2 at home in October 2022.

Madrid lost both of their games against German opponents in last season's Champions League, home and away against Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals. They last lost three consecutive European games against German teams between May and April 2002.

And Madrid are looking to make history by scoring in a 45th consecutive home game in the Champions League, with their current 44-match streak being the joint-longest in the competition, alongside another identical run by Los Blancos that ended in 2018.

1c73r2ub9a41j1n70plhn44939.title: 'USA is not a football country', says Giroud
1c73r2ub9a41j1n70plhn44939.subtitle: Olivier Giroud spent some time with Los Angeles FC in 2024 and 2025, but the striker was not convinced by MLS.
paragraphs: Olivier Giroud believes "the United States is not a football country" after his time with Los Angeles FC.
The 40-year-old made his LAFC debut in September 2024, but left the MLS club less than a year later in June 2025.
Across 38 appearances in all competitions for LAFC, Giroud scored five goals and provided three assists.
He won the US Open Cup with the club in 2024, also finishing runner-up in the Leagues Cup in the same season.
Now playing for Lille in his native France, Giroud reflected on his decision to leave LAFC earlier than expected.
"On the football front, it wasn't really for me," Giroud told Ligue 1+.
"I missed this passion, this fervour, these boiling stadiums of Europe and the competition.
"For me, the United States is not a football country."
LAFC are sixth in the Western Conference this season, with Son Heung-min and Denis Bouanga now leading the line.

1cb3wuza3mwsn1jxkpy0gmnpok.title: Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal: Madueke makes the difference
1cb3wuza3mwsn1jxkpy0gmnpok.subtitle: Arsenal were far from their best at the City Ground, but Noni Madueke's deflected effort saw them beat Nottingham Forest 1-0.
paragraphs: Noni Madueke came off the bench to make the difference for Arsenal as his deflected effort clinched a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.
The reigning Premier League champions were largely flat at the City Ground on Sunday, yet they had the quality to get the job done in the end.
A low-key first half saw Kai Havertz head over from Declan Rice's free-kick, but little else of note occurred at either end.
Forest, shorn of the injured Morgan Gibbs-White, were quick out of the blocks after the interval, with Liam Delap almost setting up Neco Williams.
Gabriel Magalhaes headed over from a corner, before Rice blasted over the crossbar from inside the Forest box.

Yet the deadlock was finally broken in the 80th minute as Madueke, who replaced Eberechi Eze at half-time, skipped in from the left, took on Daniel Munoz and found the far corner courtesy of a huge deflection off Jair Cunha.
Oliver Glasner's team came on strong in the closing stages, with Rice denying Chris Wood a free shot before Murillo, on his 100th appearance for Forest, fired just over at the end of a brilliant run.
But their fate was sealed when Ezri Konsa made a fine recovery challenge on Delap, condemning Forest to a third straight defeat.
Arsenal's away-day specialist strikes again
Madueke has scored 13 of his 17 Premier League goals away from home (76%), including all four for Arsenal.
This is the highest away ratio of any player with 15+ goals in Premier League history.
The England winger is also coming up big in the key moments, too. Three of his last five goals in the top flight have been the first of the game.

It was far from a classic, as evidenced by both teams managing just one attempt on target between them. Forest had two of those, but Arsenal made theirs count, even if they did get lucky with Cunha's deflection.
Arsenal generated the slightly better chances, recording 1.07 expected goals (xG) to Forest's 0.75, but Mikel Arteta will know his team can reach much greater heights.

That said, this is a familiar scoreline for the Gunners. Since Arteta took charge in December 2019, Arsenal have registered 32 1-0 wins in the Premier League, the joint-most of any team, along with Everton.
Forest, meanwhile, find themselves in the relegation zone with just five points from their seven games, having won just one of their last 15 Premier League games at the City Ground (D8 L6).

1cbbipodk6i3n1mzwx2erc2npt.title: Kvaratskhelia vows to come back stronger as Ronaldo leads tributes to PSG star
1cbbipodk6i3n1mzwx2erc2npt.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament against Barcelona.
paragraphs: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia vowed to come back stronger for Paris Saint-Germain after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury against Barcelona on Tuesday.
It was confirmed by PSG that Kvaratskhelia would undergo surgery to repair the issue, which he suffered in their 4-2 victory over the LaLiga giants in the Champions League.
Kvaratskhelia had to be helped off the field when he was withdrawn in the 59th minute following a challenge with Xavi Espart, with the Georgia international not expected to play again this season.

The 25-year-old's injury comes as a huge blow for PSG, who are expected to be without Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos after the pair also suffered injuries against Barcelona. Nuno Mendes was another notable absentee from their midweek win at the Parc des Princes.
In a social media post on Wednesday, Kvaratskhelia thanked the PSG fans for their support and said he would not "waste a second" during his lengthy recovery journey.
"Many people asked me about this stand; many said that if all the footballers in the world prayed, the game would end in a draw," Kvaratskhelia said.
"This could be true, but before every game I play, I ask God to leave the field healthy, but in vain. It hasn't been a long time, but it's still on my mind – why me anyway?

"I have never missed anything; probably I prepared for this game, the best I have ever prepared for. I thought I was prepared for everything, but not, and I realise that God chose me and if I protected the players on another field, I'm ready to go through these months in labour, pain, tears.
"I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always have my back. I won't let you down. I promise I won't waste a second. Thank you all for your support. See you soon."
Since joining PSG from Napoli in January 2025, Kvaratskhelia has become one of the most prolific wingers in Europe and has been crucial in PSG's recent success.
In his 91 appearances across all competitions for the Parisiens, Kvaratskhelia has recorded 47 goal involvements (29 goals, 18 assists).
He has won nine major honours in the French capital, including two Champions League crowns, scoring in their 5-0 thrashing of Inter in the 2024-25 showpiece match.
Cristiano Ronaldo was one of several players to send words of support to Kvaratskhelia.
"The hardest battles in football are often the ones nobody sees. I know that feeling, Kvara," Ronaldo's comment on Kvaratskhelia's post began.
"But never forget what brought you this far, and don't let a difficult moment make you doubt how far you can go. Keep that fire on. Your best is still to come."

1cdw583e5nv7r17qculki419s3.title: Getafe president Torres confirms 'final offer' made to Sancho
1cdw583e5nv7r17qculki419s3.subtitle: Jadon Sancho is yet to find a new club after leaving Manchester United, but he could be playing his football in LaLiga with Getafe soon.
paragraphs: Getafe president Angel Torres has confirmed the club have been working on a deal for the last four months to bring free agent Jadon Sancho to Spain.
Sancho is without a club after Manchester United chose not to trigger the one-year option in his contract at the end of last season.
The 26-year-old endured a difficult five-year stint at Old Trafford, scoring just 12 goals and providing six assists in 83 appearances across all competitions for the Red Devils.
He also spent time on loan with former club Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa, with the latter stint resulting in Europa League glory under Unai Emery.
But after his exit from United, Sancho has failed to find a new club, though reports suggested a move back to Dortmund was close, but never materialised.
And it has now emerged that Getafe are keen to sign Sancho, with Torres confirming a final offer has been made to the former England international.
"That's absolutely true; I've been working on this for four months. He's now a free agent. We've made him a final offer," Torres told Cadena Cope radio.
Getafe sit 14th in LaLiga after their opening eight games of the season, with Rayo Vallecano their next opponents at Estadio Coliseum on Monday.
They have won just one of their last six LaLiga games (D2 L3), a 1-0 victory against Malaga, but that did not stop them from bringing Dani Carvajal to the club.
Carvajal, like Sancho, was also without a team after bringing the curtain down on a trophy-laden 13-year stint with Real Madrid, but has since arrived at Getafe.
Torres, however, said a deal to sign Sancho was a little more difficult than the one for Carvajal, saying: "He's 26 years old, he's very good, so this [signing] is a bit trickier.
"He's previously played for Manchester [United] and Aston Villa, so it's not as if he's coming from anywhere. I know he's got offers from Qatar and from a number of other places.
"We need to be patient, not put pressure on him, and let him decide for himself."

Torres, however, said a deal to sign Sancho was a little more difficult than the one for Carvajal, saying: "He's 26 years old, he's very good, so this [signing] is a bit trickier. 

"He's previously played for Manchester [United] and Aston Villa, so it's not as if he's coming from anywhere. I know he's got offers from Qatar and from a number of other places.

"We need to be patient, not put pressure on him, and let him decide for himself."

1ce6alpps6tdd1axrl90uhd203.title: Buendia 'should have scored more' for Villa in Champions League win
1ce6alpps6tdd1axrl90uhd203.subtitle: Emiliano Buendia was once again on target in the Champions League as Aston Villa eased past Viking on Wednesday.
paragraphs: Emiliano Buendia believes he "should have scored more" in Aston Villa's "important win" over Viking in the Champions League.
Unai Emery's side maintained their perfect start in the competition with a 3-1 win at Villa Park on Wednesday.
Villa are the first Europa League holders to win their first three games of a Champions League campaign since Manchester United in 2017-18.
They are also the second-quickest team to record 20 wins in the European Cup/Champions League (30 matches), behind only Real Madrid (29 matches).
Ross Barkley opened the scoring before Buendia scored a penalty before half-time, while an own goal from Henrik Heggheim secured the win before Peter Christiansen's consolation for Viking.

Buendia is the first Villa player to score in four consecutive appearances in major European competition, and the first Argentinian to do so for a Premier League team since Manchester City's Sergio Aguero in 2018-19.
However, Buendia recorded seven shots in the win, four of which were Opta-defined 'big' chances.
"I should have scored more; I had chances," Buendia told TNT Sports. "I'm happy to score with the penalty [though].
"It was an important win, and we have to keep going.
"Obviously, these kinds of teams come here with all their energy, and they try and show their character.
"We respect them a lot; we worked, and we prepared the match really well. Then we showed that in the match."

Alysson (20 years and 169 days) became the youngest Brazilian to take 3+ shots (three), create 3+ chances (three) and complete 4+ dribbles (four) in a Champions League match since Shakhtar Donetsk's Willian (20y 109d) vs Basel in November 2008 (five, three and four).

And after assisting Barkley, Ibrahim Mbaye became the joint-youngest player to assist in consecutive Champions League appearances for a Premier League team, alongside Arsenal's Jack Wilshere in September 2010 (18y 270d).
"He [Alysson] was incredible; he showed his potential, his ability on the wing," added Buendia.
"Mbaye as well; their speed and qualities will help the team a lot.
"It's very important to have them and try to improve, because they are young talents and can improve a lot."

1clg92hc14s1810uei3b7bnwrn.title: Kulusevski 'a different man' after 526-day Tottenham absence
1clg92hc14s1810uei3b7bnwrn.subtitle: Tottenham's Premier League win over Coventry City on Monday saw Dejan Kulusevski make his long-awaited return, after 17 months out.
paragraphs: Dejan Kulusevski feels like "a different man" after making his first Tottenham appearance in 526 days during Monday's 3-1 win over Coventry City.
Kulusevski missed Spurs' entire 2025-26 campaign after suffering a serious right patella injury during a 2-0 Premier League defeat to Crystal Palace in May 2025.

The Sweden international underwent surgery and endured multiple setbacks during his rehabilitation, and Spurs parted ways with three head coaches – Ange Postecoglou, Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor – while he was on the sidelines.
But Kulusevski received a standing ovation when he was brought off the bench by Roberto De Zerbi against Coventry, replacing Mohammed Kudus in the 87th minute.
During that brief cameo, Kulusevski completed all four of his passes and contested six duels, winning two of those, including one successful dribble out of two attempted.
And after his long road back to first-team football, Kulusevski is determined to enjoy every appearance he makes for Spurs.
"I will tell everyone about the journey. It has been an amazing journey, even if it has been hard sometimes – hard is beautiful," he told Sky Sports.
"I am so grateful that I had to experience it. Now, I am ready to play football.
"I see myself as different now. I think that I am a different man. I'm the same guy that wants to play football, but a little bit smarter, so I am happy."
Spurs' victory was their first in the Premier League this season, at the seventh attempt, and once Kulusevski entered the fray with De Zerbi's men leading 2-1, it was all business.
"I was locked in, I was ready to play those 10 minutes and make a good impact," he said. "It's amazing.
"It was more emotional this morning. It's a beautiful day and I am so happy that we won."

James Maddison also made his long-awaited first Premier League start since April 2025 after recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament tear, and he opened the scoring with a glorious finish from outside the box.

1clrgb6ichllh1tvuhpbqvdajn.title: Havertz and Musiala withdraw from Germany squad in double injury blow
1clrgb6ichllh1tvuhpbqvdajn.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp suffered two withdrawals from his Germany squad, but had replacements to call upon from his second party of players.
paragraphs: Germany have been dealt a double injury blow as Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala have both withdrawn from the squad.
Musiala suffered a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh during the warm-up for their Nations League opener against the Netherlands.
Havertz started the match, which finished as a 1-1 draw, but was then withdrawn in the 30th minute due to a muscle strain – as announced by the German Football Association (DFB).
No timeline has been set for Havertz's return, but German media reports that Musiala will be out for three to four weeks for Bayern Munich.
Jurgen Klopp has named two squads for this extended international break, including 44 players, so Florian Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt have now been called up one game earlier than originally planned.
Wirtz has come under criticism for his Liverpool performances so far this season, particularly after their 1-0 victory over Bournemouth.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool in all competitions this term, registering just one assist, despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
Burkardt, meanwhile, has made a stellar start to the campaign for Eintracht Frankfurt, netting six goals in his five outings.
He is currently averaging a goal every 64.7 minutes and a 42.9% shot conversion rate.
Germany's second Nations League match sees them host Greece on Sunday.

1cm0oscojseck1v29y1up5akkc.title: Sweden 2-1 Romania: Isak and Gyokeres on target in Nations League win
1cm0oscojseck1v29y1up5akkc.subtitle: Sweden returned to League B with a victory in the Nations League, with their star strikers both hitting the back of the net in Stockholm.
paragraphs: Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres were both on target as Sweden made a winning start to the Nations League with a 2-1 victory over Romania.
Having been promoted to League B during the last Nations League campaign, Sweden made a winning return to the competition.
They started fast, with Sebastian Nanasi seeing a curling effort pushed away by Ionut Radu with just 32 seconds on the clock.

And Isak found a way through in the 20th minute; he peeled off the back of Virgil Ghita to latch onto Yasin Ayari's throughball and his powerful effort nestled into the net, despite Radu getting a hand to the shot.

Just nine minutes later, though, Romania were back on level terms. A pacy counter-attack finished with Dennis Man flicking the ball over Victor Lindelof before volleying past a helpless Viktor Johansson.
Romania attempted to push for a second, but their momentum was halted two minutes before half-time when Gyokeres fired in the rebound of Lucas Bergvall's saved shot.

Elliot Stroud thought he had added a third for Sweden when his lovely looping shot flew into the top-right corner 53 minutes in, but his celebrations were cut short after the goal was ruled out following a VAR review for a handball by Isak in the build-up.
Both teams had further chances to add to their tallies, but neither could find another goal, with Sweden moving top of their group with the victory.
Sweden's superstars get the ball rolling
Isak and Gyokeres have endured very different starts to their respective seasons, but both of them will be thrilled to get on the scoresheet for their nation.

Isak has put last season's struggles behind him at Liverpool, already netting four goals in his seven games for them in all competitions, and he was a shining light for Sweden with a game-high three shots and seven touches in the opposition box.
Meanwhile, Gyokeres has stumbled so far in 2026-27, failing to hit the back of the net for Arsenal after making just five appearances and only as a starter, without scoring in them.
He may have netted the winner for Sweden, but he had a hard time imposing himself in the game, with only one shot in total, while he only managed 31 touches, just over half of what Isak did (60).

1cmcdzvbcahj01cqvdgmm7kxin.title: Roma must put things right after Champions League collapse, urges Gasperini
1cmcdzvbcahj01cqvdgmm7kxin.subtitle: Roma fell to a dramatic defeat in the Champions League midweek, with Gian Piero Gasperini eager to bounce back against Genoa.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini has called on his Roma side to put things right after their Champions League loss to Real Madrid.
Roma were leading 3-1 in the 82nd minute, but Madrid scored three goals from corners in a seven-minute spell to take all three points at Stadio Olimpico.
Excluding games that went to extra time, this was the latest that an away side had been behind by at least two goals in a Champions League match and gone on to win.
It marked Roma's first defeat of the season across all competitions, while they have drawn their last two Serie A matches.
Gasperini is seeking a big response from his side when they host Genoa in the league on Saturday.
"The psychological blow came when the score became 3-2. We need to work on that and put it right," said Gasperini.
"This team must not feel that it necessarily has to win the Champions League, the league title, or who knows what else.
"This team needs to express itself. If you concede a goal, you cannot let your morale drop. In my opinion, performance always matters.
"We know that matches are often decided in the closing minutes, but we decided them ourselves against Parma and Atalanta. We probably suffered the opposite against Inter, Juventus and Real Madrid.

"[On Saturday] we need strength, belief and energy. We are returning to the league as one of the leading teams. We will have the spirit, mentality and energy to try to win, because winning validates the players."
Roma slipped from first to third in the table last weekend, while at the other end, Genoa are 17th in Serie A, though they won 2-1 against Fiorentina last time out.
Genoa boss Daniele De Rossi managed Roma in 30 matches between January and September 2024 (W13 D10 L7), while also making 616 appearances as a player, scoring 63 goals for the Giallorossi.
He ranks second for most official appearances for Roma in history, behind only Francesco Totti (786).
With top scorer Donyell Malen suspended and Paulo Dybala sidelined with injury, Matias Soule has the chance to prove his worth for Roma.
The 23-year-old impressed against Madrid, recording two assists before being replaced in the 63rd minute while Roma were 3-1 up.
Genoa – Milutin Osmajic
Milutin Osmajic has scored three goals in five Serie A appearances for Genoa.

Only three players have netted at least four goals in their first six games for the Grifone in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95): Krzysztof Piatek (eight), Diego Milito (five) and Marco Borriello (five).
MATCH PREDICTION: ROMA WIN

Roma have won 14 points in Serie A this season, one fewer than they had after their first six matches last term (15); they could collect at least 17 points after their first seven league games for the first time since 2014-15 (18 in that season).
Roma are unbeaten in their last 15 home Serie A matches (W11 D4), with their last home defeat in the competition dating back to 30th November 2025 against Napoli.
The Giallorossi are also unbeaten in 39 of their last 40 home Serie A matches against Genoa (W33 D6), including all of their last 23 home games (W19 D4).
Genoa's last top-flight away victory against Roma dates back to January 1990 (1-0, with a goal from Carlos Aguilera at the Stadio Flaminio).

After a run of ten consecutive Serie A matches without a win (D3 L7), Genoa won their most recent game against Fiorentina; the Grifone could secure back-to-back victories in the competition for the first time since last April (against Sassuolo and Pisa).

1covehf8wlgfd186xyhyxsoe4c.title: Germany 2-0 Serbia: Klopp earns first win after stunning Wirtz display
1covehf8wlgfd186xyhyxsoe4c.subtitle: After falling short in his first two games with Germany, Jurgen Klopp finally got into the win column with a dominant victory over Serbia.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp picked up his first win as Germany boss with a 2-0 victory over Serbia in the Nations League.

Florian Wirtz was the star of the show in a relentless display from the home side at the Allianz Arena, with the Liverpool midfielder scoring the second goal after Tom Bischof got a deserved opener late in the first half.

Germany started on the front foot as Aleksandar Pavlovic curled narrowly wide before Nick Woltemade sent a header off target, while Gnabry dragged an effort wide of the left post in the 18th minute, following a brilliant pass from Wirtz.

Djordje Petrovic was then on hand to deny both Gnabry and Wirtz with two brilliant saves, but he could do nothing when Bischof fired into the roof of the net after Wirtz's initial effort bounced back off the post, six minutes before half-time.

Germany continued to push either side of the break, with Petrovic tipping a fierce attempt from Bischof over the bar before Said El Mala's deflected strike landed just wide of the right post after the restart.

Woltemade inexplicably fired over from mere yards out from Philipp Treu's cross, but Germany doubled their lead just past the hour as Wirtz showed brilliant skill to take in a pass from Maximilian Mittelstadt and dribble past Srdjan Babic before scoring.

Serbia's first, and only, shot came in the 78th minute as Jonas Urbig easily dealt with a long-range attempt from Filip Kostic, as Germany's dominance on the ball was too much for the visitors to handle.
Wirtz inspires Germany to three points

The only criticism Klopp could possibly give his side will relate to their wastefulness in front of goal, as they scored just twice despite accumulating 3.82 expected goals (xG) from 32 shots, six of which were Opta-defined big chances.
Germany had as many shots on goal in the first half as they managed in their entire previous match against Greece (16).

But the former Liverpool boss will take great joy from the performance of current Reds player Wirtz; aside from the two goals, Klopp's biggest smile on the touchline came when Wirtz regained possession in the final third.

Despite his struggles at club level this term, Wirtz was at his best for Germany against Serbia. He created a match-high six chances, recorded the most touches in the opposition box (eight) and completed two of his three dribbles, while also playing a key role in Bischof's opener.

Wirtz scored his 12th goal for Germany at the age of 21 years and 37 days; only Edmund Conen in 1935 (20 years, 281 days) and Lukas Podolski in 2006 (20 years, 357 days) reached this milestone for the German national team at a younger age.

1cv3gtqp58r6x1ni44gqdh6k84.title: Milan owner praises Amorim for navigating injury crisis
1cv3gtqp58r6x1ni44gqdh6k84.subtitle: AC Milan have sustained several injury issues ahead of their meeting with Bologna, leaving them shorthanded in midfield.
paragraphs: AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale has been impressed by the resilience shown by Ruben Amorim's squad this season, with injuries hitting them ahead of Wednesday's meeting with Bologna.
The Rossoneri are still unbeaten after eight Serie A games under the former Manchester United boss, amassing 18 points.
Having been thrashed 3-0 by Bournemouth in the Europa League last Thursday, Milan responded with a 2-0 league win at Udinese on Sunday.
After their wins against Atalanta (3-2) and Udinese (2-0), Milan could win three Serie A matches in a row for the first time in 2026.
Milan last did so between November and December 2025 (against Inter, Lazio and Torino on that occasion).
They have a big week ahead of them, as their midweek clash with Bologna comes three days before the first Derby della Madonnina of the season, against Inter at San Siro.
Adrien Rabiot, Mario Gila and Diego Moreira will all reportedly miss the Bologna game, while Ruben Loftus-Cheek will reportedly miss around a month after sustaining a knee issue.
But Cardinale says Amorim has done an excellent job of managing his undermanned group.
"The team continues to improve and has shown great resilience after the disappointing match in Europe," the managing partner of RedBird Capital told Sky Sport Italia.
"Ruben has managed rotations and substitutions well. All of this puts us in a good condition ahead of Wednesday's home game."

1cwqtizb896b213retchwo4t7z.title: England and Tuchel not to blame for Scott's injury, says Rose
1cwqtizb896b213retchwo4t7z.subtitle: Bournemouth could be without the injured Alex Scott for up to a month, but Marco Rose said England were not to blame for his absence.
paragraphs: Marco Rose said Alex Scott would be a "big loss" for Bournemouth after being injured on international duty, but he said the blame did not lie with Thomas Tuchel and England.
Scott became just the second Bournemouth player to start a match for England after Callum Wilson in 2018 during the Three Lions' 7-0 win over Croatia in the Nations League.
The 23-year-old impressed before he was replaced in the 70th minute at Stadion HNK Rijeka, though it has since been confirmed he was struggling with a thigh injury.
It has now been revealed Scott could be out for up to a month with the issue, which is a huge blow for Bournemouth and Rose ahead of their return to Premier League action.
Bournemouth have been reported as being unhappy with Scott's involvement against Croatia, though Rose said the only thing that mattered was he played well for England.
"It's an injury to a muscle, and we'll do pictures [scans] in some days again," Rose told reporters.
"But we're going to miss him, for sure, for four or five weeks. I'm very disappointed and it's a big loss.
"Did he have an injury before? No, I think not. I think the club have already said everything about it.
"For me, it's disappointing. We miss a very important player, but I don't want to blame anyone. We are very happy that he made his debut for the English national team.
"He did well, and we just hope that he gets fit again quite soon."

Only Kobbie Mainoo (40) and Lewis Hall (38) have won possession more times in the Premier League this season than Scott (36), who has also won the most ground duels (30) and covered the fifth-most distance (57.7km) in the competition in 2026-27.
Bournemouth make the trip to Stamford Bridge this Saturday to face Chelsea, with the Cherries one of only three Premier League sides yet to win this season.

Rose's side have gone winless in five to start a Premier League campaign for only the second time, after 2023-24 (D3 L2 in both). The German is the second manager to fail to win their first five top-flight matches with the Cherries, alongside his predecessor Andoni Iraola (first nine).
However, three of Bournemouth's four Premier League wins against Chelsea have come away from home, with those three victories their only clean sheets at Stamford Bridge.

1cyu77rxj09ez1r1xrs29g5as7.title: Martinez keen to improve Leverkusen's away record
1cyu77rxj09ez1r1xrs29g5as7.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen are yet to win away in the Bundesliga in 2026-27, while Mainz have not picked up a victory at home so far.
paragraphs: Carles Martinez is eyeing a first Bundesliga away win of the season for Bayer Leverkusen when they travel to Mainz on Saturday.
Leverkusen lost their league opener 3-2 away to newly promoted Elversberg but have gone unbeaten since then, with two wins and a draw.
That stalemate also came on the road against Augsburg, with both of their wins – and clean sheets – coming at the BayArena.
And despite sitting fifth in the early standings, Martinez knows it is important to get their first road win on the board sooner rather than later.
"Mainz are a good team; we're a good team," Martinez said.
"We're determined to improve our away record and come away with three points.
"[Saturday's] match is an important one. I want to see my team put in the same performance they did against RB Leipzig [a 2-0 home win]."
Martinez has a few injury worries to contend with after the extended international break, with Ibrahim Maza, Kennet Eichhorn and Guela Doue all set to miss the Mainz game.
"He's [Maza] better. We have to check in training and then decide whether he's ready," Martinez said about Maza before addressing the other injury concerns.
"Guela is working on his comeback; it's still taking some time. However, the process is going well, as planned.
"We're in touch with Kennet; we speak regularly, including about football in general. Despite his absence, he wants to feel part of the team, and that's what we're aiming for as well."
Mainz are level on points with Leverkusen, only sitting behind their opponents on goal difference.
Unlike Martinez's side, Mainz have had a lot of joy on the road in 2026-27, but they are yet to win at home, after a draw with Paderborn and a 3-1 loss to Eintracht Frankfurt.
Mainz – Philipp Tietz
Tietz has scored in three consecutive Bundesliga matches, a feat he previously only achieved for Augsburg in October and November 2023.
He is the first Mainz player to score four goals in the first four Bundesliga matchdays since Shinji Okazaki in 2014-15 (also four).
Bayer Leverkusen – Patrik Schick
Schick has scored in each of the first four matchdays of a Bundesliga season for the first time (four goals).
He could now become the third player to do so in the first five matchdays for Leverkusen, following Stefan Kiessling in 2009-10 and Dimitar Berbatov in 2005-06 (five goals each).
Scoring in five consecutive Bundesliga matches would also be a first for the Czechia international.
MATCH PREDICTION: BAYER LEVERKUSEN WIN
Mainz have won only two of their last 17 Bundesliga matches against Leverkusen (D3 L12) and are winless against them in the top flight since a 3-2 away victory in February 2023.
Indeed, Mainz have picked up fewer points against Leverkusen (two) than against any other current Bundesliga side across their last six league meetings.
They are enjoying their best Bundesliga start in seven years, though, having collected seven points from four matches – they have matched their haul from 2022-23.

Leverkusen have won their last two matches in all competitions and could now secure three consecutive victories for the first time since January and February (four). They have also scored at least twice in all six matches under Martinez in all competitions.
And Mainz have failed to win any of their last five Bundesliga home games, losing four (D1); among current top-flight sides, only Eintracht (six) are currently on a longer winless run at home.
Bayer Leverkusen – 42.6%

1d278ewvzy6121v58olswbrifd.title: Xavi sees 'superior' Netherlands in second half against Germany
1d278ewvzy6121v58olswbrifd.subtitle: Xavi was forced to settle for a draw on his Netherlands debut against Germany, but he felt his team should have taken all three points.
paragraphs: Xavi believed his Netherlands team deserved more than a point in their Nations League opener against Germany following a "superior" performance in the second half.
The former Barcelona boss made his Netherlands bow at Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday, with his team playing out a 1-1 draw against Jurgen Klopp's Germany.
Felix Nmecha had given Germany a 32nd-minute lead when he finished past Bart Verbruggen, though the hosts felt that Brian Brobbey had been fouled in the build-up.
But the Netherlands dominated after the break, with Denzel Dumfries denied by Marc-Andre ter Stegen before Mexx Meerdink's goal was disallowed for a foul by Virgil van Dijk.
However, Xavi's side were able to get the goal their performance merited in second-half stoppage time when Cody Gakpo brilliantly volleyed Ruben van Bommel's cross home.

The Netherlands improved their expected goals (xG) total from 0.57 to 2.61 in the second half, while also having more shots (14 to five), more big chances (five to none) and touches in the opposition box (26 to 11) than their opponents.

In fact, the Oranje recorded an overall expected goals (xG) total of 3.18 to Germany's 1.45 xG. It was the first time they had registered above 3.0 in that metric against a nation ranked inside the top 30 of the FIFA rankings since June 2019.
"We were a bit nervous in the first half," Xavi said. "So at half-time, I said that we had to show more personality. I asked for more ambition.
"I saw that in the second half. I'm glad that the players realised after the break that we were superior.
"We deserved more than this. We created a lot of chances, put on good pressure and took a lot of initiative.
"I'm less happy with the number of lost duels, I'm not happy about that. But I have a good feeling about it.
"The debutants also did a great job. Mexx Meerdink was easy to play and fought continuously, and Ruben van Bommel filled in excellently with his ball conquest and assist."
But there was concern for Xavi following the stalemate, with Brobbey replaced in the 35th minute by Meerdink because of what appeared to be an injury to his hamstring.
The Sunderland striker arrived into the international break fresh from scoring a hat-trick against Manchester City, but it remains to be seen how severe the injury is.
Xavi confirmed that Brobbey would take no further part in the rest of the Netherlands' fixtures, and he revealed another striker would be called up to fill that gap in the final third.
"Brian is indeed injured, unfortunately, so we will call up another striker. We haven't decided who yet. I haven't had time for that yet," Xavi said of Brobbey's issue.
Brobbey's injury led to Germany's opening goal, with the Netherlands frustrated by their opponents, who appeared as though they were going to kick the ball out of play.
However, Nadiem Amiri and Joshua Kimmich instead kept the attack going, and Nmecha swept home after Nathaniel Brown's cross into the penalty area was flicked into his path.
"I think it's normal to stop when a player is injured on the ground, although there are no rules for it. They didn't do that, that's not sporting," Gakpo said of Germany's goal.
"We were pushing and we had opportunities. And that we still managed to score an equaliser, is nice."

1d34ciyz49gik1niyzma8x19as.title: Fulham 1-0 Hull City: Arbeloa records first Premier League win
1d34ciyz49gik1niyzma8x19as.subtitle: Fulham delighted the Craven Cottage faithful on Saturday, picking up their first Premier League win of the season.
paragraphs: Fulham earned their first Premier League win of the season as they defeated Hull City 1-0 on Saturday, courtesy of a first-half goal from Alex Iwobi.
Alvaro Arbeloa's side produced a dominant display to end their six-match winless start to the campaign, though their long-awaited victory was soured by Ryan Sessegnon's late dismissal.
Fulham dominated possession from the outset, as Iwobi went close to an early opener with a powerful strike that took a sharp deflection off John Egan before sailing narrowly over the crossbar.

Alvaro Arbeloa’s side continued to probe for a breakthrough as Sander Berge and Timothy Castagne combined neatly – the latter firing into the side netting – before Oscar Bobb stung Konstantinos Tzolakis’ palms with a low free-kick.

The hosts’ dominance finally bore fruit just past the half-hour mark as Brooke Norton-Cuffy was caught in possession, allowing Berge to tee up Iwobi for a superb curling strike into the bottom corner.

Tzolakis was called into action just before the break to deny Fulham a deserved second, keeping out Josh King’s effort across goal with an outstretched leg after the midfielder was slipped through by Bobb.

King threatened again shortly after the restart, with Bobb smartly cutting out Semi Ajayi’s loose pass and playing a fantastic one-two with the midfielder, who was once more thwarted by Tzolakis’ outstretched leg.
Though the Tigers posed minimal threat at the other end, Fulham continued to squander chances.
Tzolakis produced another superb stop just before the hour mark, brilliantly denying Iwobi’s close-range effort after Garcia cushioned King’s looping cross into the Nigerian’s path.
Garcia then went close himself in the 74th minute but could only guide Iwobi’s floated back-post cross straight onto the crossbar, leaving the Craven Cottage faithful on edge.

A frenetic end to the match saw Mohamed Belloumi twice fire wide of the net before Sessegnon was given his marching orders for an unblushing late challenge on Robinio Vaz in the fourth minute of stoppage time.
Fulham finally play to their potential
Fulham had endured a difficult start to the season, failing to win any of their opening six matches despite performances that arguably deserved more.
But Arbeloa’s side were full value for the victory on this occasion, producing 1.44 expected goals (xG) to Hull’s modest 0.16 xG.
Indeed, they registered 10 first-half shots – their second-most across the opening 45 minutes in a Premier League match this season, behind only their 13 against Crystal Palace in September.

Iwobi accounted for three of those attempts, with his winner taking him to 36 Premier League goals, drawing him level with Peter Odemwingie as the joint-sixth highest-scoring Nigerian in league history.

His standout performance saw him become the first Fulham player since Bryan Ruiz against Swansea City in December 2012 to register at least five shots (five), create three chances (three), and complete 50 passes (57) in a Premier League match.

Hull, meanwhile, may have feared the worst as soon as Iwobi broke the deadlock, with the Tigers now winless in their last seven Premier League matches when conceding first, dating back to a victory over Middlesbrough in April 2017.
Indeed, Sergej Jakirovic’s side have seen their bright start to the season fade slightly, having now gone five league matches without a win.
Against Fulham, they also failed to register a single shot on target in a Premier League match for the first time since facing Crystal Palace in May 2017.

Against Fulham, they also failed to register a single shot on target in a Premier League match for the first time since facing Crystal Palace in May 2017.

1d3e92w39rmdbzegnorg26sel.title: NYCFC midfielder Shore ready for 'three finals' in playoff push
1d3e92w39rmdbzegnorg26sel.subtitle: New York City FC have three more games to try and break into the Eastern Conference playoff spots, starting at home to Atlanta United.
paragraphs: New York City FC midfielder Jonathan Shore believes they have "three finals" as they look to make a late playoff push in the Eastern Conference.
NYCFC are 12th in the East, four points off rivals New York Red Bulls in ninth heading into the last three regular-season matches.
They kept their slim postseason hopes alive with a 2-2 draw at Orlando City at the weekend, with Shore scoring a last-gasp equaliser for Pascal Jansen's side.
With a home clash against Atlanta United kicking off a key run, Shore has called on his team-mates to already have a playoff mentality.
"I mean, we know it's three finals for us," said Shore.
"It's almost like the playoffs start early because we need to win all three. We need to just leave everything on the field no matter what.
"We need to outwork the opponent, bring the energy, and yeah, we're going to give it our all. Just being focused and being ready to go all in as a team."
Nineteen-year-old Shore has made 51 MLS appearances over the last two seasons, scoring twice.
He believes his experience at this level has prepared him for NYCFC's upcoming crunch fixtures.
"Obviously, with the experience I've gotten at first-team level, you build confidence," said Shore.
"You get better. I think I've also physically matured over the last two years.
"So yeah, I think all the minutes I have been getting have been helping me, and it's just the start for and there's so much more to do.
"But yeah, the experience builds confidence for me, definitely."
Atlanta's playoff hopes are all but over, with the Five Stripes nine points off the Red Bulls after a 3-2 loss against the Chicago Fire last time out.
New York City FC – Jonathan Shore
Shore scored the equalising goal in NYCFC's draw with Orlando on Saturday in the ninth minute of stoppage time. It was the latest tying or go-ahead goal ever scored by a teenager in MLS history.
Atlanta United – Miguel Almiron

Miguel Almiron created three chances against Chicago, including setting up the fourth-minute goal for Tomas Jacob, taking his total to 43 chances created since the World Cup break, tied for fifth-most in MLS.
It was Almiron's 15th game since the World Cup break with multiple chances created, tied with Carles Gil for most in MLS in that time.
MATCH PREDICTION: NEW YORK CITY FC WIN
While home advantage could play a role, NYCFC have won only one of their last 14 regular-season matches (D7 L6), though they have managed draws in each of their last two matches.
NYCFC have not won a regular-season home match since July 25, going six straight without a home win (D3 L3), equalling the longest streak in club history.
Atlanta are unbeaten in five consecutive regular-season away matches (W3 D2), their longest road unbeaten run since a six-game stretch in March-June 2018.
The Five Stripes have lost only one of their last seven meetings with NYCFC (W1 D5), including earning a 2–2 home draw on September 26.
Atlanta are one of two Eastern Conference teams (Inter Miami) that NYCFC have not defeated multiple times in league play since the start of the 2023 season.

1d4dg254v4svl1xj5g9c21hxab.title: Amorim calms expectations around Milan youngster Cisse
1d4dg254v4svl1xj5g9c21hxab.subtitle: The hype is increasing around AC Milan teenager Alphadjo Cisse, but Ruben Amorim believes the forward still has a long way to go.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim has urged the media not to put pressure on AC Milan teenager Alphadjo Cisse.
The 19-year-old has made a name for himself in the Milan first team this season, highlighted by his display against Salzburg last time out in the Europa League.
Cisse scored a hat-trick for the Rossoneri in a 4-0 win over their Austrian counterparts, securing their first win in the competition this season.
With his treble, Cisse became the youngest Italian player in the history of major European competition to score a hat-trick.
Ahead of their trip to Bournemouth in the Europa League, Amorim has eased expectations around the youngster.
"I think we shouldn't blow the situation out of proportion and put pressure on the youngsters," said Amorim.
"We need to help them understand that football is a rollercoaster, everything can change in an instant.
"We're just getting started with Cisse, he's at 50% of his potential, he's still missing some top-level things.
"Let's give him time, he's doing well, we need to understand that football changes quickly."
Amorim has won six of his last seven Europa League group stage matches (L1), and has never lost an away game in the group stage (W4 D2).
However, he failed to beat Bournemouth in all three games as Manchester United manager (D2 L1), most recently a 4-4 draw in December 2025.
Milan have won just two of their 22 away major European matches in England (D7 L13), beating United in February 2005 and Newcastle United in December 2023 on their most recent visit.
When asked if he's seen any difference in Bournemouth since Marco Rose took over, Amorim said: "I feel the same rhythm and the same pressure, Rose is like that.
"They have quality, they're doing well in scouting, I don't see big differences in identity despite the changes in players. We have the responsibility to fight for the win."

1d9qvv4bsdhx01ptrel20b6jyr.title: O'Reilly withdraws from England squad with injury
1d9qvv4bsdhx01ptrel20b6jyr.subtitle: Nico O'Reilly will be unavailable for England's Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Czechia after leaving the squad due to injury.
paragraphs: England have confirmed Nico O'Reilly has withdrawn from their squad due to injury.
The Manchester City defender started in last Saturday's Nations League defeat to Spain at Wembley Stadium, but he was then absent for their win over Czechia on Tuesday.
O'Reilly assisted Harry Kane in a thrilling game against the world champions, but then made a mistake in the lead-up to Alex Baena's goal to make it 2-2.
The 21-year-old will now miss the Three Lions' trip to Croatia and home fixture against Czechia, with Thomas Tuchel opting against calling up a replacement for the left-back.
"Nico O'Reilly has returned to Manchester City and will play no part in the forthcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures," a statement read.
"No further replacements are planned as the Three Lions prepare to face Croatia in Rijeka on Saturday before returning to Wembley to take on Czechia on Tuesday."
England have won six of their last eight Nations League matches (L2), scoring 20 goals in the process.
That is more wins (W5 D6 L7) and goals (18) than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition.

The Three Lions have also won their last eight away matches in all competitions – a win against Croatia would see them equal their record of nine away wins in a row, set between December 1965 and October 1967 under Sir Alf Ramsey.
O'Reilly may now face a battle to be fit for Manchester City's next Premier League game, away to Liverpool on October 11.

1dia4psctbp2p1j3erm5n34hdq.title: Bournemouth 2-0 Sunderland: Tavernier and Evanilson seal first Premier League win
1dia4psctbp2p1j3erm5n34hdq.subtitle: Marco Rose recorded his first Premier League victory as his Bournemouth side dispatched 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality Stadium.
paragraphs: Marco Rose's wait for a first Premier League win finally came to an end on Sunday as goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson sealed a 2-0 win over 10-man Sunderland.
Tavernier had given Bournemouth a sixth-minute lead, with Sunderland's hopes of a comeback dented when Kevin Danso was sent off for a last-man foul on Evanilson.
Robin Roefs was in inspired form, but he could do nothing to stop Evanilson from doubling Bournemouth's lead early in the second half, which clinched the victory.

After Evanilson saw an early deflected attempt fly wide, the Cherries got themselves in front after the Brazilian shrugged off the challenges of Danso and Omar Alderete before squaring for Tavernier to head into an empty net.

Danso could only divert Granit Xhaka's free-kick past the right post, and that proved to be his final action after he got himself in all sorts of trouble before bringing down Evanilson, leaving referee Craig Pawson with no option but to brandish a red card.
Rayan aimed to make Bournemouth's numerical advantage count, but he was met by a strong save from Roefs, with Adam Smith blazing the rebound over the crossbar.
The Sunderland goalkeeper again came to his team's rescue twice in quick succession, first saving Rayan's header before palming away a long-range strike by the Bournemouth number 37.

However, some more slack defending from Regis Le Bris' side gifted Bournemouth their second in the 48th minute. Alderete's under hit back pass was intercepted by Evanilson, who rounded Roefs and slotted into the net.

Tavernier thought he had scored his second of the contest, but the midfielder saw his close-range effort snuffed out by the onrushing Roefs before Evanilson's scorpion kick flew inches past the upright, with Bournemouth holding on for a morale-boosting league win.
Cherries delight for Rose

Coming into this game, Rose knew the pressure was on him to notch a first league win, and his players did not disappoint. Bournemouth came racing out of the blocks instantly with Evanilson being at the forefront of an impressive display.
The Brazilian, who scored his second goal in three Premier League appearances against Sunderland, registered six shots with an expected goals (xG) of 1.12.

Moreover, Evanilson leads the Premier League assists chart with four and has now been involved in a goal in each of his last three appearances for Bournemouth across all competitions (three goals, one assist), his joint-longest run for the Cherries.
The Cherries were so dominant that they generated an xG total of 4.46 in this match – their highest total on record (from 2021-22) during a Premier League contest.
For Sunderland, they have now lost each of their last four Premier League games, their longest losing run in the competition since a five-match stint in December 2015 under Sam Allardyce.

The Black Cats faced a tough task after Danso received his marching orders, timed at 16:29, which is Sunderland's third-earliest Premier League red card after George McCartney vs Manchester City in March 2009 (14:14) and Wes Brown vs Hull City in February 2014 (3:08).
Interestingly, it was Danso who had Sunderland's best chance, with Le Bris' side mustering a measly xG tally of 0.07 from three attempts.

1dj8oh7o6p4gt17bsshytl7bwe.title: Greece 0-0 Germany: Klopp's men frustrated in Nations League draw
1dj8oh7o6p4gt17bsshytl7bwe.subtitle: Greece once again frustrated Germany, as they held Jurgen Klopp's team to a 0-0 draw in Sunday's Nations League contest.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp's first international window in charge of Germany ended in underwhelming fashion as his team were held to a 0-0 draw by Greece.
Klopp has won just one of his first four games in charge of Germany, who sit third in Nations League Group A2, three points behind Greece and the Netherlands.
Indeed, Greece got the better of Germany in Klopp's second game in charge, winning 2-1, and there was to be no revenge for Klopp's team on Sunday.
Germany did think they had taken the lead midway through the first half at Stadio Toumbas, but Jonathan Burkardt saw his goal disallowed for handball.
The lively Derry Scherhant also went close before half-time, but some changes from Greece boss Ivan Jovanovic helped the hosts tighten matters up after the break.
Giorgos Masouras could well have won it for Greece, but he headed wide from a free header.
Philipp Treu, however, had the best chance to settle the contest, only to slice over late on.
Germany dominate, but lack clinical touch
If it was an all-round, dominant display Klopp was looking for, then it was certainly served up by his team.
Germany had 45 touches in the opponent's box, took on 21 shots and had 70.1% possession.
Yet they only translated that to one big chance, four shots on target and chances worth a combined 1.05 expected goals.
Greece, on the other hand, had just five attempts, but they were worth a combined 0.72 xG.

Klopp must, then, have his concerns about Germany's strength in both boxes, and five points from the 12 on offer across his first four games in charge of the national team is not the return he would have been hoping for.

1djgy4hen1pkwzpi713u52jtf.title: England are lucky to have Ballon d'Or winner Kane, says Tuchel
1djgy4hen1pkwzpi713u52jtf.subtitle: After Harry Kane became the first English Ballon d'Or winner in a quarter of a century, Thomas Tuchel was among those to congratulate him.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel said England are lucky to have Harry Kane as their captain after the striker became the Three Lions' first Ballon d'Or winner since 2001.
Kane followed in the footsteps of Michael Owen (2001), Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Stanley Matthews (1956) by claiming football's most prestigious individual award.
Only France (six) have produced more different Ballon d'Or winners than England's five, and at the age of 33 years and 90 days, Kane is the fourth-oldest first-time winner of the prize.
Only Matthews (41 years, 321 days), Karim Benzema (34 years, 302 days) and Lev Yashin (34 years, 56 days) have claimed their first Ballon d'Or at an older age.
Eight of the last 10 Ballon d'Or winners, including Kane, have been 30 or older, after only seven of the first 60 recipients between 1956 and 2015 were aged above 30.
Kane plundered 73 goals for club and country in 2025-26, including six at the World Cup as England finished third – their best-ever finish on foreign soil.

And Tuchel believes Kane's triumph was long in the making, saying: "I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.
"To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special, and we are lucky to have you as our leader.
"I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches."
Tuchel was among the coaches Kane paid tribute to in his acceptance speech, saying: "All of you played a big role in my development at different stages of my life.
"Without every single one of you I wouldn't be standing here today. I have learnt lots.
"When you surround yourself with the best people, it only improves you as a person and as a player."
Kane has scored in four straight games for England since the World Cup, finding the net six times in total to help England put nine points on the board in the Nations League.

1dm7ia4wlktkb1jtipym78jkf5.title: Luis Enrique relishes PSG's fearlessness on the road
1dm7ia4wlktkb1jtipym78jkf5.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain have hit their stride in 2026-27 after a wobbly start, and they want a fourth straight league win against Strasbourg.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique is impressed by Paris Saint-Germain's fearless approach to games as they look to extend their winning streak against Strasbourg in Ligue 1.
PSG began the season with a three-game winless run in the French top-flight (D2 L1), but they have since won their last three, including a 3-1 victory over Le Mans last time out.
It moved them up to sixth in Ligue 1, and they boosted their confidence further in midweek with a resounding 4-2 win over Manchester City in the Champions League.
And Luis Enrique has been impressed by how his team react within games to turn things in their favour.
"If I have to confirm one thing in this match or over the past three years, it is the players' ability to be aggressive and brave at all times, especially away from home," Luis Enrique said.
"The key characteristic of this team is that they are never afraid.
"We prepare for every match in the same way because we want to win them all. This is a clear goal for us and for the players.
"We strive to play good football and create chances, and we know that the three points are essential for us."
Strasbourg sit 11th in the table after going winless in their last three outings (D1 L2), following back-to-back wins.
They have lost to both Paris FC and Nice in their last two matches, both by a 2-1 scoreline, though both defeats came on the road.
Ousmane Dembele will be aiming to have an impact, similar to the one he had against Man City, where he scored and assisted.
He joked after the match that he would ask for another break, having been given an extended holiday following the international break, and Luis Enrique responded in kind.
"He's the boss!" Luis Enrique said in response to Dembele's comments. "If he wants a holiday and asks for it, he'll get it!
"He's joking all the time, and I love his approach to football and his passion for it."
Strasbourg – Gessime Yassine
Gessime Yassine has attempted 42 take-ons in Ligue 1 this season, 15 more than any other player.
He has completed 20 of them, already doubling his total from last season (10).
Paris Saint-Germain – Matvey Safonov
Matvey Safonov is the only PSG player to have started all six of their Ligue 1 matches in the 2026-27 season; only Le Mans have as few players in this situation (one).
Among goalkeepers with a minimum of five top-flight appearances this season, only Patrick Beach (55.2%) has a lower save percentage than the Russian (57.9%).

1dma1ftqe1t3m1399ggv10zolc.title: 'A history that will last forever' – Ronaldo honours Messi after Argentina send-off
1dma1ftqe1t3m1399ggv10zolc.subtitle: After Lionel Messi brought the curtain down on his glittering international career, Cristiano Ronaldo was among those to praise his legacy.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo has taken to social media to pay tribute to his great rival Lionel Messi following his final Argentina game, saying he created "a history that will last forever."
Messi won his 208th and final cap for the Albiceleste on Tuesday, scoring and providing two assists in a 3-0 win over Benin, on an emotional occasion in Buenos Aires.
Messi's glittering international career ended with 126 goals, one World Cup win and two Copa America triumphs, as well as two further runner-up finishes at FIFA's flagship tournament.
A visibly moved Messi addressed the crowd in the aftermath of Tuesday's game, with many of his team-mates past and present hailing his achievements on social media.
So, too, did his great rival Ronaldo, who commented below a post on Messi's Instagram account to pay his own respects.
"Leo, so many years defending your country and a history that will last forever," Ronaldo wrote.
"All my respect for what you have achieved with Argentina."
While Messi received a fitting farewell from Argentina during the international break, Ronaldo has been in the headlines for his unceremonious departure from the Portugal camp.

He accused head coach Jorge Jesus of "breaching his word" by leaving him on the bench during a Nations League win over Norway, also saying the Portugal boss went back on a deal to read a set of pre-agreed statements at a subsequent press conference.
Ronaldo, who says he remains available for selection by the Selecao, has scored 146 goals in 234 appearances for his country – both all-time records in men's international football.

1dofuka5qfm801nd72hkzwpc8t.title: Pickford welcomes England competition from Trafford
1dofuka5qfm801nd72hkzwpc8t.subtitle: James Trafford has started in both of England's Nations League games so far, but Jordan Pickford is ready to fight for the number one spot.
paragraphs: Jordan Pickford has welcomed the competition from James Trafford in the fight to be England's starting goalkeeper.
Pickford has been England's first-choice goalkeeper since the 2018 World Cup, but Trafford has started in each of their Nations League matches during this international break.

Trafford became the first England goalkeeper other than Pickford to start consecutive games since Nick Pope in September 2022, though the Everton shot-stopper could be back between the sticks when the Three Lions face Croatia on Saturday.
Pickford believes the competition will only help him grow as a goalkeeper, while insisting he has no immediate plans to retire.
"I feel for me personally it's always good to have good competition, I've always said in interviews I've always wanted that competition.
"We have a good crop of goalkeepers coming through and it's a credit to England to have that and may it continue for longer.
"I'll always push myself at the club to be the best version of me and keep getting those caps. You can't let your foot off the gas at any time you want to push yourself to be who you want to be.
"I'm 32 now, you see keepers playing still at 40, still playing at the highest level. It's about me focusing on myself; I set myself my own goals."

England have won their last eight away matches in all competitions – a win against Croatia would see them equal their record of nine away wins in a row between December 1965 and October 1967 under Sir Alf Ramsey.
Since beating England in the 2018 World Cup semi-final, Croatia are winless in all four games against the Three Lions (D1 L3).
Pickford played in the World Cup defeat in 2018, though he believes England cannot rely on their recent success over Croatia.
"I think it's always a good competitive match, we know we lost in the 2018 World Cup against them," added Pickford.

"But we are looking past recent history and we have always played well against them. You're always going to be against good competition at pot one in the Nations League; it's about being the best version of us."

1dpq5fzah0yjb1ulfpojg4v0ri.title: Netherlands 2-1 Serbia: Zirkzee's winner continues Xavi's unbeaten run
1dpq5fzah0yjb1ulfpojg4v0ri.subtitle: Joshua Zirkzee's 72nd-minute winner ensured the Netherlands continued their unbeaten run under Xavi, as they beat Serbia 2-1.
paragraphs: Joshua Zirkzee's 72nd-minute strike ensured the Netherlands continued their unbeaten Nations League run after overcoming a stubborn Serbia 2-1 in Group A2.
After Teun Koopmeiners fired in a free-kick, Serbia instantly levelled thanks to Mihajlo Cvetkovic's header at Philips Stadion.
But, with both sides missing a host of chances, it was Zirkzee's close-range strike which settled the contest.

The Netherlands almost made Vanja Milinkovic-Savic pay for his sloppiness inside the opening three minutes, but Mexx Meerdink was unable to keep his shot down before Noa Lang dragged an attempt wide of the post.
However, the Oranje took the lead in the 31st minute, with Koopmeiners fizzing a free-kick into the bottom-right corner.
But the Netherlands' lead lasted only four minutes as Serbia grabbed a shock equaliser thanks to Cvetkovic’s header.

It all came from Aleksa Terzic's left-wing delivery, with Cvetkovic guiding a finish into the far corner. That was the third goal the Netherlands have conceded in the last 15 minutes of the first half, with no team conceding more such goals so far in the 2026-27 Nations League.
The visitors should have taken the lead within 48 seconds of the second half, but Cvetkovic steered an effort wide of the upright after being played through on goal by Dusan Tadic.

After grabbing an equaliser against Greece in the Netherlands' previous Nations League encounter, Tijjani Reijnders should have scored after being slipped in by Joey Veerman, but the midfielder lashed a bouncing shot wide of the far post.
However, Reijnders was involved in the decisive goal, as Zirkzee swept home a 72nd-minute finish, ensuring Xavi's side sit top of Group A2.
Zirkzee the hero in Eindhoven
With the Netherlands struggling to break down a stubborn Serbia defence, it was looking like more dropped points for the Oranje.
However, Xavi decided to bring on Zirkzee for the second half, and his change paid off.
The Manchester United striker showed great instinct to be in the box at the right time to sweep home a six-yard finish.

That was Zirkzee's only attempt on target. Virgil van Dijk, on his 100th appearance for the Oranje, also made a vital contribution in the heart of defence, making nine clearances, while having four shots.
The Netherlands are undefeated in their last eight games in the Nations League, while having scored in four of their four games, with no team having done so more often in the competition.
Xavi's team registered 22 shots, with seven on target, and they created chances worth a combined 2.75 expected goals (xG).
Meanwhile, Serbia, who almost equalised in stoppage time through Nemanja Gudelj's long-range strike, mustered an xG of 1.66 from 14 shots.
