1dvvqf75e2vx113tv6klzilt7r.title: Simeone insists Atletico can compete with Barcelona for title
1dvvqf75e2vx113tv6klzilt7r.subtitle: Atletico Madrid host Deportivo this weekend, with a clash against LaLiga leaders Barcelona also on the horizon for Diego Simeone's side.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone believes his Atletico Madrid side are capable of challenging reigning LaLiga champions Barcelona for the league title.
Barca are currently top of the table after winning all nine league games this season, giving them a five-point lead over second-place Atleti.
Atletico are in fine form themselves, having won each of their last five LaLiga games, with the last three being by a one-goal margin.
Atleti face Barca at home on November 8, but not before LaLiga matches with Deportivo A Coruna and Levante, as well as a Champions League clash with Bayern Munich.
Despite the upcoming test, Simeone insisted that his full focus is on Deportivo this weekend.
When asked if Atleti can challenge Barca this season, Simeone responded: "Yes, of course, you can always compete. That's perfectly clear. It's obvious.
"That doesn't change the fact that they [Barca] have a fantastic team.
"Before that [Barcelona match], there's Levante, Bayern... There's a long way to go.
"We're focused on Saturday's match, on where we can hurt them. Deportivo has been competing very well in every game; they've won, they've drawn, they've lost, but they always compete well.
"They're a brave team. We already faced them in the last Copa del Rey, and it was a tough match. All our energy is focused on doing well in this game."
Deportivo made a strong start to the campaign, going unbeaten in their first five games (W2 D3), but they have since gone winless in four league games (D2 L2).
Their struggles have coincided with the injury of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, who scored five goals and provided two assists in their opening five games this season.
Atletico Madrid – Alex Baena
Alex Baena has scored three goals from outside the box in LaLiga in the 2026-27 season, the most by a midfielder after his team's first eight games since Santi Cazorla for Malaga in 2011-12 (four).
Deportivo A Coruna – Bil Nsongo
At 22 years and 25 days old, Deportivo's Bil Nsongo became the youngest player to score for the club in LaLiga since Ivan Cavaleiro in February 2015 (21y 111d) in their last match against Levante.
MATCH PREDICTION: ATLETICO MADRID WIN

Atleti have not lost any of their last 13 matches against Deportivo in LaLiga (W10 D3), since a 2-1 defeat in November 2009, their longest historical unbeaten run against the Galicians in the competition.

At home, Atleti have not lost any of their last 14 matches against Deportivo in LaLiga (W13 D1), winning the last 12 and keeping a clean sheet in the last seven, Atleti's current longest winning run and clean sheet streak at home against the same opponent in the competition.
Simeone has only overseen more home LaLiga games with a 100% win rate against Real Valladolid (seven out of seven) than against Deportivo (five out of five, level with Las Palmas).
Deportivo are also the team Simeone has faced joint most at home without conceding a single goal in the competition (five, level with Las Palmas).

Deportivo have not won any of their last 11 away games against teams from the Community of Madrid in LaLiga (D3 L8), but they have drawn the last two and could pick up points in three consecutive away games against these sides in the competition for the first time in their history.
Atletico Madrid – 71%
Deportivo A Coruna – 12.1%

1dxjj4luxe2zq1sl81f7lr37he.title: Hull City 1-1 Brentford: Ouattara nets equaliser but Jakirovic's men still unbeaten at home
1dxjj4luxe2zq1sl81f7lr37he.subtitle: Dango Ouattara's strike denied Hull City three points against Brentford, but the Tigers are still unbeaten at home since their promotion.
paragraphs: Hull City maintained their unbeaten Premier League home record for 2026-27 despite being pegged back in a 1-1 draw with Brentford on Saturday.
Dango Ouattara netted the equaliser midway through the second half for the Bees, cancelling out Oliver McBurnie’s 24th-minute penalty.
Brentford almost raced into a lead inside 54 seconds, but Sepp van den Berg’s close-range header was denied by Konstantinos Tzolakis.
Minutes later, Van den Berg almost converted into his own net but was thankful to see the ball fly over his own crossbar.

It was the Tigers who took the lead in the 24th minute with McBurnie converting a penalty into the bottom-right corner, after Aaron Hickey brought down Tim Iroegbunam inside the box, following a poor pass from Caoimhin Kelleher.
Brentford should have got themselves level before the break, but Kevin Schade’s strike was inadvertently blocked by his team-mate Igor Thiago six yards out.

The visitors were thwarted by Tzolakis once again after the break with the Hull goalkeeper blocking Van den Berg’s latest header, but there was nothing he could do about Brentford’s 63rd minute leveller.
Moments after coming on, Jaidon Anthony floated a left-wing centre into the box with Ryan Giles failing to clear the danger. That allowed Thiago to set up Ouattara, who duly slotted home.
Anthony almost put his side ahead minutes later, but the winger fizzed an effort wide of the upright before Joe Gelhardt failed to connect with Mohamed-Ali Cho’s low cross from six yards.
Tigers' den a tough place to go
Coming into the game, Brentford boss Keith Andrews stressed that Hull deserved to belong in the Premier League, and that assessment was proven correct.
The Tigers started the contest brightly and deservedly went ahead thanks to McBurnie’s penalty.

Brentford were fortunate not to concede a further two spot-kicks with Regan Slater and Mohamed Belloumi going down inside the box after challenges from Van den Berg and Mamadou Sangare, but referee Robert Jones waved those appeals away.

Hull registered an expected goals (xG) figure of 1.84 from 12 shots, but they have now failed to win their last six games in the Premier League, with their last longer such streak coming between November 2016 and January 2017, a run of nine games. However, Hull have lost just one of their six home league games against Brentford (W4 D1) this century, after losing four of their prior five.
Meanwhile, after a poor first half, Brentford improved after the break, finishing the contest with a slightly lower xG total of 1.81, from 14 attempts.

The Bees have now failed to win their last three Premier League games, and their winless record in Yorkshire continues. Brentford have now failed to win in six attempts in the county, with their last away top-flight win registered in May 1947, a 2-1 triumph over Leeds United.
This was also the first time this season Brentford conceded first in a Premier League game, becoming the 20th and final team to suffer that fate.

1dxlw1dvi69hl16fjrlm2qr67b.title: Kane: On another day England could have beaten Spain
1dxlw1dvi69hl16fjrlm2qr67b.subtitle: England were 2-1 up against Spain when Harry Kane missed a penalty, with the world champions going on to turn things around and win 3-2.
paragraphs: Harry Kane conceded England could have beaten Spain "on another day" after starting their Nations League campaign with a 3-2 defeat to the world champions.
England came from behind to lead after a Marc Guehi error gifted Lamine Yamal a second-minute goal, with Anthony Gordon and Kane netting in the space of four first-half minutes.
However, Kane then struck the crossbar after his standing foot slipped when he took a penalty, and Spain flipped the script, with Alex Baena equalising shortly after.
Mikel Oyarzabal then secured all three points for Spain, coming back to haunt England, having also netted the winner in the Euro 2024 final.

England lost a match in which they led at half-time for the first time since June 2019 (versus the Netherlands in the Nations League). They had won 41 of their previous 42 games when ahead at the break since then (D1).

Kane has scored 17 goals in 19 appearances for England under Thomas Tuchel, but having scored 39 of his 40 penalties for club and country in 2023, 2024 and 2025, he has now missed three of his 16 spot-kicks in all competitions so far in 2026.
"I spoke before that we reached good levels at the World Cup but didn't quite put a full 90 minutes together," Kane told ITV Sport.
"Probably similar again. We had a couple of good moments though; that period was as good as we've played in a long, long time, and that's the standard we know we can reach.
"We're playing against the world champions, the European champions, and we went toe-to-toe. On another day, for sure, we'd have won that game.
"We have to take the positives from it. We have to dust ourselves down and go again in a few days."
England have conceded 3+ goals in consecutive matches for the first time since June 1995, having beaten France 6-4 in their third-place play-off at the World Cup.
Overall, they have conceded 13 goals in their last six matches in all competitions, almost double the amount they had shipped in their first 17 under Tuchel (seven).
But the Three Lions were disappointed, as this was also the first time they made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive match since June 2019 against the Netherlands in the Nations League.
"I think it was a bit of a missed chance," Gordon told ITV Sport.
"I thought it was a great game to watch and to play in; some of the attacking play was at the highest level. But I think in a game like that, mistakes cost you.

"You always feel like it's you're giving it away rather than them winning it. But, of course, you could argue both teams because they were as good as us and we were as good as them. I'm just gutted about the mistakes."
Gordon's goal came at the end of a pacy counter-attack, just days after he said England needed to rely on their own strengths instead of trying to match other teams' styles.

Asked if his goal was the epitome of how England should play, he added: "Kind of, if you want to phrase it that way, in terms of what I said in the week about being direct and playing to an English style, being quick, really putting teams on the back foot.
"It kind of summed up what I said, which was quite nice, but ultimately it didn't lead to a victory.
"Like I said a couple of days ago, I don't think there is a gap [to Spain]; I feel like we're right there. We can win that game so easily.

"I don't think there is a gap, and I think if we played them in the final, I would've felt confident. Being confident doesn't always translate into a win, but I think you've seen here tonight that we're a top team."

1dyaxzir9us711mcyvmfgngaip.title: Philadelphia have earned unbeaten MLS run, says Richter
1dyaxzir9us711mcyvmfgngaip.subtitle: The Philadelphia Union will look to extend their unbeaten run in MLS to 15 games when they host Charlotte FC on Saturday.
paragraphs: Philadelphia Union interim boss Ryan Richter believes his side have earned their unbeaten run as they prepare to take on Charlotte FC.
The Union are unbeaten across their last 14 MLS games (W12 D2), a club-record run, after defeating the Chicago Fire on Wednesday.
Milan Iloski and Bruno Damiani both scored in a 3-1 win over the Fire, who were reduced to 10 men in first-half stoppage time.
Philadelphia's impressive run has seen them climb to sixth in the Eastern Conference, just one point and one place behind upcoming opponents Charlotte.
"It's a great run, something that we’re proud of," Richter said.

"It's something that the guys have earned because of the way that they work every single day, the way that they’re focused, the way that they approach games, the dirty work that they're willing to commit to during the games."
Teenager Cavan Sullivan picked up an assist in the Union's win over Chicago, and he is relishing the chance to prove the doubters wrong.
"People doubt the Philadelphia Union," Sullivan said. "They want to say that we're only beating bottom-of-the-table teams.
"But we were once at the bottom of the table. So we're just proving it week in and week out and hoping to keep this thing rolling."
Charlotte failed to pick up three points during the week, falling to a 3-1 defeat to the Columbus Crew on the road.
Dean Smith's side took the lead through Idan Toklomati, but failed to keep out an in-form Columbus side, with the head coach describing the performance "as bad as I've seen in a long time."
Philadelphia Union – Cavan Sullivan
Sullivan's assist against Chicago marked his 21st direct goal contribution of the season (seven goals, 14 assists), the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS campaign.
The 17-year-old has also registered a direct goal involvement in each of his last eight MLS matches either side of the international break.
Charlotte FC – Idan Toklomati
Toklomati is Charlotte's joint-top scorer in MLS this season with 12 goals, level with Pep Biel.
The 22-year-old has already equalled his goal tally from the 2025 campaign, despite playing in five fewer matches.
MATCH PREDICTION – PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN
Not only are Philadelphia unbeaten in their last 14 MLS games, but they have also won their last eight on the bounce.
The Union have scored 28 goals across their last eight league matches, including 5-0 wins over San Diego FC and FC Cincinnati.
However, Charlotte won the previous meeting against Philadelphia this season, when Wilfried Zaha scored the winner in a 2-1 victory back in April.
Nevertheless, the Union have won both of their last two home meetings with Charlotte, once in MLS (2-1) and the other in the Leagues Cup.
Philadelphia Union – 54.3%

1ee6tjvvdxqk41tf22b476zqnt.title: Yamal is the best player in the world, claims Flick
1ee6tjvvdxqk41tf22b476zqnt.subtitle: Lamine Yamal spearheaded Barcelona in their 5-2 defeat of Real Betis, and Hansi Flick feels the winger is the world's best player.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick has hailed Lamine Yamal as the world's best player after another star turn from Barcelona's teenage sensation.
Yamal scored twice and provided an assist as Barca made it six wins in LaLiga this season by beating Real Betis 5-2.
The winger has been directly involved in a goal in nine consecutive games in all competitions (nine goals, ten assists), which is his best run at club level in his career (162 games).
Yamal is the first player from Europe's five major leagues to reach 10 assists this season across all competitions, and Flick feels he is the best player on the planet as it stands.
"When you see the first goal he scored, it's incredible; right now he is the best player in the world," Flick said of Yamal.
"I am very happy with his performance and that is what I want to say.

"Of course, he is under pressure; he is 19 years old and has played every game, but he is 100% focused and committed, and he is very good. His performances have been incredible and his attitude, and that is how great players are.
"I told him that I was very proud because he had played a fantastic game."
Barca have become the second LaLiga team to win their first nine matches of a season in all competitions, after Real Madrid in 1968-69.
But Flick's focus was on swiftly turning attention to Tuesday's Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain.
He added: "For the moment the most important thing is to recover. Recovery is very important and seeing how we manage the minutes on Tuesday.
"We'll see, we'll look for 11 players. We don't know what will happen with Eric [Garcia], and [Jules] Kounde has small problems. We'll have to see."

1eh3r0jsdgu56106oid28tgrxj.title: 'No drama, no panic' for Sunderland and Le Bris
1eh3r0jsdgu56106oid28tgrxj.subtitle: Sunderland remain bottom of the Premier League after drawing with Leeds United, but Regis Le Bris is not worried about their position.
paragraphs: Regis Le Bris insisted there was "no drama, no panic" in the Sunderland dressing room despite a goalless draw with Leeds United leaving them bottom of the Premier League.
Sunderland remain rooted to the bottom of the top-flight table following a tepid affair at the Stadium of Light on Sunday, with the weather conditions not helping either side.
Brian Brobbey, making his return from a hamstring injury, had Sunderland's best chances in the first half, but he was denied both times by Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.
Nilson Angulo twice tested Trafford in the second half, but Leeds almost won it in stoppage time, with former Newcastle United man Sean Longstaff twice going close.

Sunderland have nine points fewer than they did at the same stage of last season's Premier League (five in 2026-27, 14 in 2025-26), the biggest drop-off after eight games of any team, though they are also competing in Europe this term.
The Black Cats drew with Lech Poznan in the Europa League on Thursday, making it seven points from their opening three games.
"This is what we want to be," Le Bris told Sky Sports when asked about the difficulty of managing in different competitions.
"We want to play in Europe as regularly as possible, so facing this challenge is new for us, and you need to learn, you need to create something new and it takes time.
"No drama, no panic and we are in the situation we expected ourselves to be. Obviously, it's still difficult to lose games, but we think we are in the right direction.
"It's a positive [point]. The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness. It's still a long journey.
"We know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it's a new challenge for us and we need to embrace it.
"I think we showed that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves, and we probably deserved a bit more today."
The conditions made for an underwhelming contest, with Sunderland registering an expected goals (xG) total of 0.91 from their 15 attempts to Leeds' 0.57 from their 11 shots.
Storm Boelo has battered much of the United Kingdom over the weekend, and neither team could really gain a foothold as the high winds made it difficult.
Leeds have now played out the joint-most draws of any team in the Premier League in 2026 (14 – level with Brentford), while their five nil-nil draws are the outright most this year.
Daniel Farke's side are seventh in the Premier League and four points behind Liverpool in fourth, with the Leeds boss highlighting how difficult the conditions were to play in.
"The conditions played a big part. It is fair to say that it wasn't a nice piece of football, but it's difficult in these conditions when you don't know the curve of the ball," Farke said.
"It is easy to play proper football on a nice Sunday, when the sun is shining, but these types of games are important, and you have to adapt and accept the conditions.
"You have to adapt to the fight, there are lots of fights for second ball and long balls, and you have to show lots of skill and we did this today.
"A clean sheet is always a good outcome for us. In possession, you could see a bit that we had a difficult training week when key players in offence were absent.
"I need to give praise to my lads, we have a different game. We have created a very honest team and we have to adapt. I like another clean sheet and how we looked defensively.
"It is never easy for a team, but we handled this occasion really well. On a good day we can be better."

1ej1gkk4a5ujg10bv4hm5rln54.title: Wales 2-1 Norway: Williams hits free-kick winner after Heggem red card
1ej1gkk4a5ujg10bv4hm5rln54.subtitle: Wales claimed the first victory of their 2026-27 Nations League campaign, fighting back for a statement win over Norway in Cardiff.
paragraphs: Wales got their Nations League campaign up and running at the third attempt, with Neco Williams' free-kick proving decisive as they fought back to beat 10-man Norway 2-1.

Craig Bellamy's side were rooted to the bottom of Group A4 after defeats to Portugal and Denmark, and though Oscar Bobb gave them a mountain to climb in Cardiff on Thursday, Torbjorn Heggem's red card in the first minute of the second half gave them the impetus to fight back.

Norway received a boost ahead of kick-off as Arsenal playmaker Martin Odegaard was passed fit to start after falling victim to a rough challenge from Bernardo Silva against Portugal on Sunday, and it did not take long for him to get involved.
Eleven minutes in, Bobb played a quick give-and-go with Odegaard near the right corner of the box, then wriggled beyond Ben Davies and finished past Danny Ward.

Norway lost Julian Ryerson to injury soon afterwards, and Wales' Sorba Thomas got some joy against his replacement Marcus Pedersen, though only a lucky bounce off Ben Cabango – which took the ball into Ward's arms – denied Norway a second goal in the 36th minute.
And Wales made the most of that reprieve two minutes later, with the ever-dangerous Thomas sliding a great ball into the six-yard box to hand Dan James an easy finish.

A dream start to the second half then put Wales in complete control. Just 21 seconds after kick-off, James darted in front of the hesitant Heggem and was pushed to the ground, with the Norway centre-back sent off for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.
And from the resulting free-kick, Williams whipped an inch-perfect effort beyond Orjan Nyland's reach and into the bottom corner, sparking wild celebrations among the home fans.
Only a good save from Nyland prevented Lewis Koumas from stretching Wales' lead, though the uncharacteristically quiet Erling Haaland then failed to direct a header on target at the other end.

Cabango was arguably fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty for handball and Jorgen Strand Larsen went close from distance as Norway pushed hard for an equaliser late on, but they could not avoid a second straight Nations League defeat.
Williams and James give Bellamy statement result
Wales went into Thursday's game off the back of three straight defeats – the last two of them to nil – and already looking bound for relegation back to League B.

They had failed to win their first six matches of 2026, across all competitions (D3 L3), but a memorable fightback against the surprise package from this summer's World Cup should do wonders for their confidence.

Williams' goal was Wales' first from a direct free-kick since Harry Wilson netted against North Macedonia in a 7-1 World Cup qualifying win last November. It was only Wales' second such goal in the Nations League, with Wilson previously scoring directly from a free-kick in a 1-0 win over the Republic of Ireland in October 2018.

Although Williams stole the headlines with his set-piece strike, James' role in Thursday's turnaround cannot be overstated, having scored Wales' equaliser, forced Heggem's red card and, in the process, forced the free-kick from which the hosts went ahead.
Ten of James' 11 goals for Wales have now been scored at the Cardiff City Stadium, including each of his last six.

And defensively, Wales restricted Haaland to two shots (one on target) and 0.35 expected goals. As a team, they finished with a lower xG tally than Stale Solbakken's visitors, 1.05 to 1.3, but Bellamy will not care after masterminding his first win over a side ranked above Wales in the FIFA World Rankings.

1em4fvjjaoarz1a64apn2otj3d.title: Bodo/Glimt 1-0 Borussia Dortmund: Sjovold strike stuns Kovac's side
1em4fvjjaoarz1a64apn2otj3d.subtitle: The Aspmyra Stadion once again proved to be a difficult place for European giants, with Borussia Dortmund losing out to Bodo/Glimt.
paragraphs: Bodo/Glimt registered yet another famous Champions League win as Fredrik Sjovold's 52nd-minute goal was enough to beat Borussia Dortmund 1-0 at Aspmyra Stadion.
The Norwegian minnows beat the likes of Manchester City and Inter in their giant-killing run last season, and they added another European powerhouse to that list on Wednesday.
Sondre Fet fired over after 21 seconds as Bodo looked to make a lightning start, with Ramy Bensebaini then sending a speculative effort wide of Nikita Haikin's at the other end.
The only shot on target in the first half came in the 10th minute, but Jens Petter Hauge's volley from just inside the Dortmund penalty area was comfortably held by Gregor Kobel.

But Bodo came closest to taking the lead when Fet's curling attempt narrowly evaded the right post, with Hauge then firing over as the opening 45 minutes petered out with nothing to split the two sides going into the break.

Andreas Helmersen forced Kobel into action 23 seconds after the restart, and Bodo's lightning start to the second half was rewarded when Sjovold smashed Sondre Auklend's cross in at the Dortmund goalkeeper's near post.
Kovac responded by making four changes on the hour, with Felix Nmecha, Serhou Guirassy, Julian Ryerson and Ethan Nwaneri all thrown on to try and change the game.

Nmecha came close to making an instant impact, but his curling effort from distance was brilliantly tipped behind by Haikin, with Nwaneri then seeing a glancing header land in the grateful arms of the Bodo shot-stopper soon after.
More heroics from Haikin smothered another Nwaneri attempt from close range before Nmecha once again saw his shot repelled, with Bodo holding on for their first Champions League win of the season.
There was, however, a better result for Dortmund's Bundesliga counterparts Stuttgart, who made light work of Slovan Bratislava and eased to a comfortable 3-0 win.

Lovro Majer's opener was cancelled out by Pedrinho's 34th-minute penalty, but two goals in six minutes from Vinicius Tobias and Gleiker Mendoza turned the game around.

Ahead of kick-off, Kovac urged his Dortmund players to be wary of the threat Bodo possessed after their Champions League exploits from last season, but the Bundesliga giants failed to take on that early warning as they failed to win on their travels in Europe again.

Bodo were forced to weather a late storm from Dortmund, but they were able to hold on for all three points. They edged the expected goals (xG) battle with a total of 1.13 from their 11 attempts to BVB's 0.78 from their nine attempts.

1enrx2qrova71bn7aa50eg9tw.title: India 0-4 Brazil: Estevao, Pedro and Lino shine in Kolkata friendly
1enrx2qrova71bn7aa50eg9tw.subtitle: Brazil thrashed India 4-0 in their final friendly of this international break, with Estevao, Pedro and Samuel Lino getting the goals.
paragraphs: Estevao and Pedro registered a goal and an assist apiece and Samuel Lino scored twice off the bench, as Brazil beat India 4-0 in an eagerly anticipated friendly in Kolkata.

Saturday's result meant Carlo Ancelotti's Selecao ended the international break with an unbeaten record and no other injury concerns to speak of, following Raphinha's midweek withdrawal from their squad.

India started positively with Apuia trying his luck from distance, but the midfielder could not test Brazil's debutant goalkeeper Pedro Morisco, while Vinicius Junior drew a solid near-post save from Gurpreet Singh Sandhu at the other end.

The Selecao slowly grew more dominant as the first half wore on, though, and they went in front after 28 minutes, with Sandhu unable to keep out Estevao's rasping 20-yard drive despite getting a touch on the ball down to his left.

The Chelsea man continued to threaten as his cross was headed against the right-hand post by Pedro, but that same duo combined for Brazil's second goal in the 42nd minute as Estevao's clever reverse pass put the Flamengo striker clean through, and he powered his finish past Sandhu.

Apuia reacted quicker than any yellow shirts when Sandhu blocked Vinicius' drive, and the Real Madrid superstar was one of several players to be withdrawn at half-time as both coaches rang the changes.
Vinicius' replacement, Lino, did not need long to make an impact, as he curled a lovely finish into the far corner just before the hour mark, having been found by Pedro's instinctive flick.

Though India looked a beaten team from that moment on, Ryan Williams had two chances to give the home fans something to cheer, forcing Mauro Junior into a desperate goal-line clearance, then firing narrowly wide from the right side of the area shortly afterwards.
There was another goal to come for the visitors, though, as Lino menacingly cut inside from the left flank before drilling past substitute shot-stopper Prabhsukhan Gill in stoppage time.
Young forwards show promise for Brazil

Brazil approached their first-ever meeting with India off the back of a 1-1 draw and a 4-2 win in back-to-back games against Australia, but the chaotic nature of their performances Down Under had led to criticism from some fans and pundits.

A thigh injury suffered by Raphinha further dampened the mood, and while Ancelotti acknowledged the Selecao were enduring a difficult period ahead of kick-off at the Salt Lake Stadium, he urged his players to "play with joy".

Though Brazil's tally of 1.2 expected goals (from 20 shots) was somewhat underwhelming against India, who are ranked 138th in the world and amassed 0.29 xG from nine attempts, there were several individual moments to savour.

Estevao's performance was a notable positive as Brazil enter the post-Neymar era, with the Chelsea winger now boasting six goals in just 14 appearances for his country, only seven of which have been starts.
Pedro marked his first Brazil start with a pair of goal involvements, while Lino's two goals were his first in senior international football, on his fourth cap.

Brazil will be back in Asia during the November international break, with friendlies against Japan and Singapore in the diary, and those young attackers will surely get more opportunities to impress next month.

1eswgwrq6anfc17owyjhnig5bo.title: The Numbers Game: Man City take perfect record to Anfield following tumultuous break
1eswgwrq6anfc17owyjhnig5bo.subtitle: Manchester City have the Premier League's only perfect record this season, but they are in for a chilly reception at Anfield this Sunday.
paragraphs: It is fair to say Manchester City had an eventful international break.

The Premier League was thrown into turmoil following confirmation that City had been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the competition's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and the majority of charges in relation to their failure to co-operate with the league's investigation.
City deny all the allegations and have appealed against the verdict.

As difficult as it may be amid all the talk of hefty punishments, Enzo Maresca and his players must turn their attention back to on-pitch matters this weekend, when they are sure to receive a vociferous welcome from Liverpool's fans at Anfield.

While City boast the only 100% record remaining in the Premier League this term, winning their first five games, Liverpool have two wins and three draws following their first five matches under Andoni Iraola.
But who will come out on top when these two rivals face off on Sunday? Here, we use Opta insights to preview the standout fixture of the weekend.
What's expected?
The Opta supercomputer makes City narrow favourites to keep their winning start going, as they triumphed in 40.7% of our pre-match simulations.

Liverpool took all three points in 34.6%, while the remaining 24.7% finished level – none of the last five meetings between the teams in all competitions have been drawn, since they shared the points in both Premier League matches in 2023-24.
Liverpool lost home and away to City in the Premier League last season, which was the first time they had lost back-to-back league games against the Citizens since March 1937 (four in a row).
And, following their 2-1 victory on Merseyside in February, City are looking to win on successive league visits to Liverpool for the first time since 1953.
The away side has won two of the last three Premier League games between Liverpool and City, as many as in the previous 32 beforehand.
The only time there have been back-to-back away wins in this Premier League fixture was back in 2002-03.

Sunday's game will be the first between these sides in the Premier League to not feature Jurgen Klopp or Pep Guardiola in the dugouts since March 2015, when Brendan Rodgers' Reds beat Manuel Pellegrini's Citizens 2-1 at Anfield.
Can grudge-match atmosphere help Liverpool to first home win?
Liverpool are six points off the pace being set by City, having earned nine points from their first five matches under Iraola, though they did beat Bournemouth 1-0 last time out.
Iraola could become only the third permanent Liverpool manager to avoid defeat in each of his first six top-flight matches in charge, after Bob Paisley in 1974 and Joe Fagan in 1983.
But the Spaniard is still seeking his first home Premier League victory in his new job, having overseen draws with Nottingham Forest and Fulham.
There have only been seven previous instances of Liverpool failing to win any of their first three home games in a league campaign, and just two since the First World War – in 1963-64 and 2012-13.

The Reds have certainly shown signs of adapting to the high-octane style Iraola instilled at Bournemouth, having applied high-intensity pressures to 48.9% of their opponent's touches in the opposition's half in the Premier League this season – the highest rate of any side.
Backed by a vocal home crowd, Iraola's side will likely look to press high and throw City off their game, though Liverpool will be without two of their key attackers due to injury.

Iraola revealed on Friday that both Alexander Isak – whose four Premier League goals have only been bettered by Erling Haaland this season – and Cody Gakpo – who has six goal involvements in all competitions this term – are out after withdrawing from their national squads.
In their absence, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha will be Iraola's forward options.
Maresca looks to create siege mentality
City's last game – a topsy-turvy 5-3 win over Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium – must feel like a lifetime ago for their supporters.
But Maresca cannot allow the fallout from the Premier League's verdict to affect his players, as he looks to accomplish a rare feat among managers in the English top flight.

The Italian could become only the fourth manager to open a spell in charge of any club with six straight Premier League wins, after Carlo Ancelotti with Chelsea, Guardiola with City, and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer with Manchester United.
Having served as part of Guardiola's backroom staff, he will be acutely aware of the reception City are likely to receive on Merseyside.
And in that atmosphere, cool heads will be key.
As a team, City are completing 83% of their passes attempted while under high-intensity pressure in the competition this term, the best accuracy of any side.
After starring for England in Declan Rice's absence during the international break, Elliot Anderson will look to dictate proceedings in midfield.
Anderson leads all midfielders in the Premier League this season for line-breaking passes (105), progressive carries (64), and duel success rate (60.7%, minimum 50 contested).

Having won at Anfield with Nottingham Forest in 2024-25 (1-0) and 2025-26 (3-0), Anderson could become the seventh player to win on his first three away starts against Liverpool in the Premier League, and the first since Martin Kelly with Crystal Palace between 2015 and 2017.

City will have to tighten up defensively, as their figure of 7.25 expected goals against (xGA) in the Premier League this season has been bettered by eight other clubs, including a winless Bournemouth side and Forest, both of whom are in the bottom half.

But going forward, they have been devastatingly clinical. In Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo, City boast the top two players for xG overperformance in the Premier League this term – Cherki has scored three goals from 0.72 xG (+2.28), while Semenyo has struck twice from 0.34 xG (+1.66).
Liverpool – Florian Wirtz

Wirtz made three appearances for Klopp's Germany side during the international break, scoring in their 2-0 win over Serbia, after Jamie Carragher said the attacking midfielder's performance against Bournemouth was "his poorest in a Liverpool shirt".
In 403 minutes of Premier League action this season, Wirtz has tallied just 0.39 expected assists (xA) from nine chances created.
He needs a breakout performance, preferably on a big stage, and there would be no better fixture than this one.
Manchester City – Erling Haaland
Haaland already leads this season's Premier League Golden Boot race, having five goals to his name after finding the net against Sunderland.
That strike meant he has scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the English top flight.

And, having failed to score on his first three Premier League trips to Anfield, the Norwegian finally found the net on the fourth attempt in February, hitting City's stoppage-time winner as they earned a 2-1 victory.

1ex9mz1u93mlf1b37rwx3j1t42.title: Gordon urges England to focus on their strengths, not replicate Spain
1ex9mz1u93mlf1b37rwx3j1t42.subtitle: England's tactics in their World Cup semi-final loss were questioned, but Anthony Gordon believes they need to focus on their strengths.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon agreed with Thomas Tuchel's comments about England's inability to control games and believes playing to their own strengths will help them win major tournaments.
England lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina 2-1, before going on to beat France in the third-place play-off and record their best finish at the tournament since winning it in 1966.

However, England were levelled with a lot of criticism for how they played in the semi-final, having gone to a back five after taking the lead in the match, through Gordon, to try and see out a victory.
The tactical tweak saw the Three Lions sit back and defend deeper, with Enzo Fernandez equalising before Lautaro Martinez finished the turnaround in stoppage time.
Tuchel claimed it was "not in England's DNA" to control matches like Spain – their Nations League opponents on Saturday – or Argentina and Brazil, and Gordon backed up that view.
"England, as a nation, we don't have that strength, like the Spanish, where we control games like they do," said Gordon in a press conference. "It's not in us.
"[The] scar [of losing to Argentina] doesn't have to be a negative one, because it might lead us to victory in the next tournaments.

"We can't keep looking at other countries and trying to be like them, because we're not them – we're English, and we have our own strengths which they don't have, so maybe we start playing the way we're good at."
Gordon secured a move to Barcelona from Newcastle United before the start of the World Cup and has made an impressive start to life in Spain.
He acknowledged that the way they approach play is very different to how England do, though it is not a bad thing.
"I'm not sure it's something that can be [taught]," he added.
"Playing in Spain, I can speak with an educated view on the way they keep the ball is different. It's much different than I've ever experienced playing in this country.

"I'm not sure we can ever get that, but we can definitely get better or maybe go the other way and really play to our strengths, which is play physical, play direct football, and on the counter-attack."
England are looking to begin their Nations League campaign with a win when they host Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

However, they have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2); those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
England have, though, won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of the most recent five without conceding.

England have, though, won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of the most recent five without conceding.

1ez0r7iepcvi61b5kdt9w6jbpw.title: Kolarov: Inter have nothing to prove to anyone
1ez0r7iepcvi61b5kdt9w6jbpw.subtitle: Inter came from behind to beat Bologna 3-1 on Saturday, with Aleksandar Kolarov knowing there is more to come from the Serie A champions.
paragraphs: Aleksandar Kolarov says Inter have nothing to prove to anybody but themselves.
Inter were disjointed against Bologna on Saturday, though the reigning Serie A champions nevertheless claimed a 3-1 win to bounce back from their Champions League defeat to Club Brugge.
Tommaso Pobega put Bologna ahead after 10 minutes, but Marcus Thuram equalised before half-time, with substitutes Carlos Augusto and Ange-Yoan Bonny on target in the second half.
Inter sit top of Serie A, two points clear of Roma, but Kolarov feels Cristian Chivu's team must remember they do not need to prove their credentials.
"We don't have anything to prove to anyone, other than to ourselves," Kolarov told DAZN, as he stood in for Chivu.
"We want to be more intense, both on and off the ball. In the second half today, in Madrid, and in the first 50 minutes against Club Brugge, we were intense with the ball at our feet.
"That is not to be taken for granted, we've got to set the tempo starting from the defenders.
"It is true that we are having a few problems, but we are also aware of our capabilities and have the time to make up for those dropped points.
"We've had a few setbacks, but we know how strong we are. Our strength is the group and the quality we have in the squad."

Inter have conceded the opening goal of the match more times than any other team in Serie A and the  Champions League combined this season (six); they are followed by Parma, Torino, Fiorentina and Venezia (five each).
They take on Shakhtar Donetsk in their next Champions League fixtures.

1ezq15nemdsbq14exua507zk2c.title: Arsenal have not reached 'highest mountain', says Arteta
1ezq15nemdsbq14exua507zk2c.subtitle: Arsenal are looking to continue their perfect Champions League start against Bayern Munich, but Mikel Arteta has eyes on bigger success.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta says Arsenal have not reached the highest mountain so far in terms of their success as they prepare for their Champions League tie against Bayern Munich.
Last season, Arsenal ended their long wait for a Premier League title – having finished as runners-up in each of the previous three campaigns, they topped the pile for the first time since 2003-04.
For much of 2025-26, they were on course to win a quadruple, before losing the EFL Cup final to Manchester City and being shocked in the FA Cup quarter-finals by Southampton.
They also reached the Champions League final as they remained in search of their first-ever crown in the competition but lost 4-3 on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain after a 1-1 draw.
Arsenal are once again targeting silverware this time around and have already made a strong start to the Champions League, winning both matches so far.
And Arteta is excited to keep pushing the team to see what they can achieve.
"I think we have reached a mountain [with their Premier League triumph], but not the highest one or the one that I certainly visualise," Arteta said on Inside the Game for HBO Max.
"We have achieved an objective, which was part of a chapter, and then we have to go to the next one.
"We talk about being able to win again, and especially how we are going to approach that mentality and that journey. It is very, very important, and I am super excited about it.
"The consistency is probably the hardest thing to do.
"To keep all the things that have taken you to reach that objective, but actually being able again to inspire and to lead those guys, that they can still reach another level and the same ambition."

Arsenal have won each of their last 14 Champions League group-stage matches, and since they returned to the competition in 2023, only PSG and Real Madrid (both 28) have won more games overall in the competition than the Gunners (27, level with Bayern).

They have lost 53% of their games against Bayern (8/15) – of the sides they have faced at least five times in major European competition, only against Barcelona (67% – 6/9) do they have a higher loss percentage.
Having beaten Vincent Kompany's side 3-1 at home in the last term, this is another big test for Arsenal, who are looking to replicate their perfect record, having won all eight league-phase games.
Arteta has full confidence in his team for the 2026-27 campaign and is relishing the chance to protect the winning culture he has honed.
"Well, first of all, [we need to] maintain a lot of the foundations and the powerful thing that we have within the club and within the team, the habits and the behaviours that we have," Arteta said.
"To be able from there to evolve and be very curious to evolve, very willing to go again and find the best version of yourself.
"I have to be someone that is able to ignite and lead that mentality every single day, so that we are always better and we are always improving.
"There will be setbacks, and there will be learning moments for us, and they are going to make us better.
"I think you can ignite that competitiveness within people, but I think you have to have it already.
"You need an edge to be able to do that, because when you are a winner, you are a winner when you are training, when you are playing padel or table tennis or chess or whatever.

"You actually love winning, and it is something that you strive for. If it is not there and it is not natural, maybe you can do it for a period of time, but long-term, I think it is difficult to achieve."

1f861q9batb1d12ijxftjbyv18.title: Odegaard: Silva 'completely lost his head' with late tackle
1f861q9batb1d12ijxftjbyv18.subtitle: Martin Odegaard was on the end of a late challenge from Portugal's Bernardo Silva, something the Norway captain said was unacceptable.
paragraphs: Martin Odegaard said Bernardo Silva's tackle on him during Norway's Nations League defeat to Portugal "does not belong on a football pitch".
The incident occurred during Sunday's 2-1 loss to Portugal, with Goncalo Ramos punishing an error from Norway goalkeeper Orjan Nyland to seal the win.
Joao Felix had given Portugal a first-half lead before Erling Haaland's scoring streak continued as he tucked home from close range six minutes after the restart.
In Norway's attempts to find an equaliser, Odegaard picked up possession in his own half before Silva came in late and swiped at the Arsenal midfielder after the ball was played.
Odegaard was clearly angered by the nature of the challenge as, shortly after, he shouted at Silva when he was on the ball before the pair came together later on.

Silva and Odegaard have faced off several times during battles between Manchester City and Arsenal, though the Norway captain said the nature of the tackle came from a player who had "completely lost his head".
"It does not belong on a football pitch," Odegaard told TV2 about the challenge from Silva.
"It's a shame that people behave like that. He completely lost his head. He just kicks me down long after I've played the ball. I don't understand what he's doing."
Odegaard appeared to be in pain at the end of the game as he refrained from taking a corner, with his side chasing an equaliser, and crouched down with his head in his hands.
The Arsenal star revealed that Silva did not apologise for the tackle, and instead chose to downplay the incident.
When he was leaving the Ullevaal Stadion, a reporter asked Silva about the challenge, to which he replied: "It's football, my friend."
Norway boss Stale Solbakken described the incident as "completely unnecessary", while defender Leo Ostigard believed Silva should have been sent off.
"The challenge from Bernardo Silva came very late," Ostigard said. "From the video replay, the tackle was extremely ugly. I think a red card would have been fully justified.
"It's a really nasty one. It's just absolutely awful to do. That's the kind of thing we don't want to see happen to our captain.
"When it comes that long after the ball has gone, it looks pretty deliberate."
Norway have two more fixtures during this international break, with a clash against Wales this Thursday followed up by a trip to Porto to face Portugal three days later.
Asked whether he would miss upcoming games, Odegaard said: "I hope not. I got a knock on my ankle there, so it probably won't be good [short term]."

1f94bl98l1jza1u97dnu7rt5zs.title: De Zerbi describes Spurs as 'complete team' after Chelsea victory
1f94bl98l1jza1u97dnu7rt5zs.subtitle: Tottenham earned a 2-0 win over London rivals Chelsea on Saturday, aided by Mike Penders' bizarre own goal and Cole Palmer's red card.
paragraphs: Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham have shown they are now a "complete team", after their revival continued with a 2-0 win over Chelsea.

Spurs, who have a dismal historic record at Stamford Bridge, only winning there once in 34 attempts in the Premier League prior to Saturday (D11 L22), built on Monday's 3-1 success over Coventry City with a morale-boosting derby win.
A calamitous own goal from Mike Penders and a glorious solo effort from Mathys Tel clinched back-to-back victories for Spurs, while Chelsea had Cole Palmer sent off.
It was the first instance of Spurs winning to nil at Stamford Bridge in any competition since December 1986 (2-0), and their first win there by any scoreline since April 2018 (3-1).

And the result did not flatter De Zerbi's men, either, as they restricted Chelsea to just seven shots – the Blues' fewest in a Premier League game this season and their lowest tally in a home match since January (six versus Brentford).
Though Spurs got a helping hand when Penders' attempted punch sailed over his own goal-line, they racked up 15 shots and 0.74 expected goals, with Chelsea tallying 0.43 xG.
"It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also. They deserved this win, they prepared very well," De Zerbi told Sky Sports afterwards.
"We are improving a lot, we are improving in our mentality and the relationships with the players, and then we are improving on the pitch.
"Against Aston Villa, and Everton for 30 minutes, we were playing very well. Maybe with no goals, with finishing that was not good enough, and then in the first bad moment we changed mentality.

"Now it is a complete team. The players are playing better, we improved in our style. When we stay for dinner and stay together in the dressing room I see a different group, a different relationship and a different atmosphere among the players."
And the Italian puts that improved harmony down to a bonding and warm weather training trip Spurs made to Marbella ahead of the victory over Coventry.

"The character was great today, but we have many, many new players," he added. "The players who were here last season, two or three seasons ago, they suffered those results, finishing 17th two times – we are working to change the last part of the history of the club.
"We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room, many great players. I think if we work hard, we can do something important.
"I have to believe in this group, for sure. I never lost confidence in my players.
"The week in Marbella, to speak better face to face, to open ourselves up and remove the mask, that was important.
"The atmosphere in the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics."
Spurs are now up to 12th in the Premier League table with nine points, only four adrift of fourth-placed Chelsea.

1fdvrwbghkk7b1e96aiqvx1cof.title: Hurzeler: Brighton did not play to highest level against Jablonec
1fdvrwbghkk7b1e96aiqvx1cof.subtitle: Brighton's impressive winning streak came to a halt in the Conference League as they were held to a draw by Jablonec.
paragraphs: Fabian Hurzeler admitted Brighton "did not play on our highest level" as they were held to a 0-0 draw by Jablonec in the Conference League.
Brighton have been flying high this season and came into this match on the back of a six-game winning streak in all competitions, having netted 22 goals during that run.
However, they were unable to mark Hurzeler's 100th game in charge of the club with another win as they were held in an uneventful goalless stalemate.

Georginio Rutter – who scored a brace in their last Conference League match – missed two good chances before the break, while Malick Yalcouye thought he had broken the deadlock 50 minutes in, only to be caught offside.
Jablonec could have snatched a win late on, though, with Bart Verbruggen called into action to deny Jiri Slama and Vakhtang Tchanturishvili, earning a fifth straight clean sheet in all competitions.
Hurzeler named a heavily changed side from the one that beat Crystal Palace 5-0 in the Premier League last time out, and he highlighted a need to improve the basics going forward.

"We did not play on our highest level; Jablonec defended well and defended the box well, good movement in transition. Overall, not the result we wanted, but we have to keep going," he told TNT Sports.
"If you play 0-0, then you didn't create enough; that's definitely something we have to get better at.
"We have to understand what it needs to play in this Cup. Understand we have to be brilliant at the basics. We weren't good at the basics; that's something we have to improve."
Brighton certainly had their chances, tallying 26 shots in total, though only four of those were on target as they mustered just 1.42 expected goals (xG).
They also had 56 touches in the opposition box, 63 final-third entries and finished with 72.1% possession, but Jablonec kept their discipline to shut Brighton out.

Asked why Brighton struggled to find a way through, Hurzeler added: "Good defending and crosses not where we wanted to have them. The precision in the last action was missing; that's something we have to improve.

"The longer the game got, the more space they had to make transitions. We tried to push hard for scoring the goal, and of course they had the space to make countermovements. In certain moments, we were lucky.
"We always learn. I think it's important to take things away from this game and improve in the next game. There is no time for a lot of disappointment; we have to focus on the next game."

1fj7l2uktcgls146f1x6r2xsfx.title: Manzambi will go all the way to the top, says Jackson after more Villa heroics
1fj7l2uktcgls146f1x6r2xsfx.subtitle: Johan Manzambi continued his excellent start to Premier League life on Saturday, and Nicolas Jackson feels there is still more to come.
paragraphs: Nicolas Jackson predicted his Aston Villa team-mate Johan Manzambi will go right to the top of the game after he continued his impressive form with the winning goal against Newcastle United.
Manzambi – who had looked set to join Newcastle in the summer before Villa hijacked the move to sign him from Freiburg – scored the only goal at St James' Park on Saturday.
Having been left totally unmarked, he powered Joao Gomes' right-wing cross past Lukas Hornicek in the 36th minute, and Villa held on for three deserved points.
Unai Emery's team had one fewer shot than Newcastle (15 to 16), but they won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.5 to 1.06 and generated three Opta-defined big chances while not conceding any.

Manzambi now has five goal involvements (three goals, two assists) in all competitions for Villa, and since his debut against Tottenham on September 19, Manchester City star Erling Haaland is the only Premier League player to tally more (six).

The Switzerland international is also just the fourth player to either score or assist on each of their first three Premier League starts for Villa, after Dalian Atkinson in August 1992, Dion Dublin in November 1998 and Danny Ings in August 2021.
Asked about Manzambi's impact in his post-match interview with Sky Sports, Jackson said: "He's an amazing player. He's still growing.
"Hopefully he can be better and better every game, score goals and assist me sometimes as well! Hopefully we work together and achieve many things together.
"He will go a long way and hopefully he gets no injuries. For sure, if he is okay and he is training hard, he will go a long way and get many more goals and assists."

Jackson was involved in a controversial incident midway through the first half, when Sven Botman's challenge on the Villa striker was checked for a possible red card but cleared by the VAR, despite the centre-back appearing to jump into the tackle recklessly.
Asked if he felt any effects from that challenge, Jackson said: "I'm good. I know the referee said yellow card, but it was so high and hopefully next time it will be a red card.
"I nearly broke my leg, but anyway, it's part of football. The most important thing is that we won and I'm okay."
Newcastle are now without a home clean sheet in 16 consecutive games in all competitions, which is the longest run in their history.
They have only failed to score in two of their 23 home Premier League games since the start of last season, though, but both have been in defeats to Villa (also 0-2 in January).
And head coach Matthias Jaissle knows his team need to be better in the final third, even if he was pleased with aspects of their performance.
"It was a game we were dominating, where we saw a team giving a response," Jaissle said. "We created many situations where you felt like we were going to win that game, until we conceded the goal.
"We need to be honest – we were shaking a bit until half-time, but again, we showed a good response. In the second 45 minutes, it was really aggressive from our lads.

"We won the duels, unfortunately we were not smart enough in the final decision-making in the opposition box, so that is something we need to work on. We need to threaten the opposition much more – the lucky punch was missing.
"We need to learn to find the reset straight away and consistently believe in the things we were doing before. I cannot say anything against the attitude, but the goal was missing."

Asked about Manzambi's impact in his post-match interview with Sky Sports, Jackson said: "He's an amazing player. He's still growing. 

"Hopefully he can be better and better every game, score goals and assist me sometimes as well! Hopefully we work together and achieve many things together.

"He will go a long way and hopefully he gets no injuries. For sure, if he is okay and he is training hard, he will go a long way and get many more goals and assists."

Jackson was involved in a controversial incident midway through the first half, when Sven Botman's challenge on the Villa striker was checked for a possible red card but cleared by the VAR, despite the centre-back appearing to jump into the tackle recklessly.

Asked if he felt any effects from that challenge, Jackson said: "I'm good. I know the referee said yellow card, but it was so high and hopefully next time it will be a red card. 

"I nearly broke my leg, but anyway, it's part of football. The most important thing is that we won and I'm okay."

Newcastle are now without a home clean sheet in 16 consecutive games in all competitions, which is the longest run in their history.

They have only failed to score in two of their 23 home Premier League games since the start of last season, though, but both have been in defeats to Villa (also 0-2 in January).

And head coach Matthias Jaissle knows his team need to be better in the final third, even if he was pleased with aspects of their performance. 

"It was a game we were dominating, where we saw a team giving a response," Jaissle said. "We created many situations where you felt like we were going to win that game, until we conceded the goal.

"We need to be honest – we were shaking a bit until half-time, but again, we showed a good response. In the second 45 minutes, it was really aggressive from our lads. 

"We won the duels, unfortunately we were not smart enough in the final decision-making in the opposition box, so that is something we need to work on. We need to threaten the opposition much more – the lucky punch was missing.

"We need to learn to find the reset straight away and consistently believe in the things we were doing before. I cannot say anything against the attitude, but the goal was missing."

1fn9kq3e2y81114yor61luqjf2.title: Former Man Utd midfielder Fred slams 'piece of crap' Ten Hag
1fn9kq3e2y81114yor61luqjf2.subtitle: Fred left Manchester United during Erik ten Hag's tenure, and the Brazilian midfielder was highly critical of the Dutch coach.
paragraphs: Fred has called former Manchester United boss Erik ten Hag "a piece of crap" for the way he managed the squad.
Ten Hag was appointed United boss in June 2022 and went on to win the FA Cup and EFL Cup before being sacked in October 2024.
The 56-year-old won 70 of his 128 matches in charge (D23 L35), while also losing the FA Cup final in 2022-23.
Since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, only Jose Mourinho (58.3%) and Michael Carrick (58.3%) have had a better win percentage than Ten Hag (54.7%) among permanent Manchester United managers.
Although he praised Ten Hag's tactical knowledge, Fred slammed the Dutch coach's man-management skills.
"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," Fred said on the Charla Podcast.
"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.
"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.
"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."
Fred was brought to Manchester by Mourinho in 2018, and the pair worked together again at Fenerbahce last season, with the midfielder far more fond of the current Real Madrid boss.
"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahce; he brought me to United," said Fred.
"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].
"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

1fnbwwn4ubtl41vw8zxh70z5hp.title: Nashville 'ready for more' after winning Supporters' Shield, says Mukhtar
1fnbwwn4ubtl41vw8zxh70z5hp.subtitle: Nashville SC have secured top spot in MLS and clinched the Supporters' Shield with a 2-0 win over CF Montreal, with history now in sight.
paragraphs: Hany Mukhtar says Nashville SC are "ready for more" after they clinched the MLS Supporters' Shield with their 2-0 win over CF Montreal on Saturday.
Nashville have secured top spot in MLS with three games to spare after their victory at Stade Saputo took them to 70 points.
They initially struggled to open up Montreal, having just two shots in the first half while their hosts managed five.

However, Sam Surridge opened the scoring in the 51st minute with his 18th MLS goal of the season, with a Samsy Keita own goal securing all three points – the goalkeeper helped it over his own line, taking the goal off Mukhtar.
Nashville have won just the second trophy in their history, following their 2025 U.S. Open Cup triumph, while they are now targeting MLS history.
Inter Miami hold the all-time points record in the competition, tallying 74 in 2024, and Nashville have three games left to surpass that total.
BJ Callaghan's side are unbeaten in their last seven league matches (W6 D1), and Mukhtar is confident they will achieve even more by the end of the campaign.
"It's our second trophy in two years, and I think we have done a really good job all together," Mukhtar told Apple TV.
"And yeah, we are ready for more.
"At the beginning of the season, we made plans that we want to compete for the trophy. We want to make the next step for the club and for us as players, and I think we did a good job."
Elsewhere in the Eastern Conference, the New England Revolution moved up to second – albeit 15 points behind Nashville – with a 2-1 win over the Philadelphia Union.
Dor Turgeman and Carles Gil scored in stoppage time in either half for the Revs, who conceded a 102nd-minute consolation from Neil Pierre.
The Chicago Fire also moved up to fourth, after edging Atlanta United 3-2.
In the West, FC Dallas have turned up the pressure on leaders Vancouver Whitecaps after a thumping 3-0 win over the San Jose Earthquakes, with a Petar Musa brace leading the way.
They now sit just one point behind the Whitecaps, who suffered a 1-0 loss to the Colorado Rapids.
Dallas also opened up a gap over third-place St. Louis City SC, who lost a second consecutive match after going down 3-0 to Real Salt Lake.

1foo1wdxt4dfq1vtcnnxwj7gvu.title: Noonan: Cincinnati not good enough to overlook anybody in playoff hunt
1foo1wdxt4dfq1vtcnnxwj7gvu.subtitle: FC Cincinnati are in desperate need of a win to keep their playoff hopes alive, and they make the trip to Atlanta United next.
paragraphs: Pat Noonan hinted at a growing concern about the engagement and energy within his FC Cincinnati team as their regular season draws closer to its conclusion.
Cincinnati's winless league run extended to five matches going into the international break, losing 3-1 away to Eastern Conference strugglers CF Montreal.
Tom Barlow had cancelled out Daniel Rios' early goal, but two strikes in the space of three second-half minutes from Prince Owusu was enough for the victory at Stade Saputo.
It's a run of results that have seen Cincinnati's playoff hopes put at risk. They are 10th in the East, sitting outside the postseason spots but level on points with New York City FC.
Cincinnati last failed to make the playoffs in 2021, and Noonan believes if the attitude does not change in his squad, then they will miss out on reaching the postseason.
"We're not good enough to overlook anybody," he said. "Missing players or not, they were in a more dire situation, and that's why it's confusing to not have more energy to play.
"There are guys that we could probably make changes with. That's something to look at to see how you bring life and shake things up to see how we get out of that funk.

"Some guys looked tired. Some guys look uncertain of themselves on the field, and it doesn't matter where you are in the standings, it doesn't matter talent level, you have to care, and you have to bring the energy and the confidence in your play."
Cincinnati's next clash sees them make the trip to Mercedes-Benz Stadium to face an Atlanta United side that are also in with an outside chance of reaching the playoffs.
Atlanta are 14th in the East but only six points adrift of the postseason places, having come from behind twice to draw 2-2 with NYCFC in their last league match.
Elias Baez has enjoyed a strong first season since joining the Five Stripes from San Lorenzo in February, and he remains confident his team can reach the playoffs.
"We're going to fight to make the playoffs," Baez said.
"We want all the people to come for these matches, that it's going to be a great help for us to have a crowd at home that makes us stronger."
When asked about making a new start in the United States, Baez added: "It's about adapting to the country, the club, how things are here.
"I think gradually adapting [to a new country] will help you grow personally as a player."
Atlanta United – Giuliano Galoppo
Galoppo scored just 10 minutes into his first career regular-season home game for Atlanta, netting in their draw with NYCFC last month.
He is one of 10 players to score in his first regular-season home match for the Five Stripes, something no player has done in their first two.
Evander has 26 goal contributions this season (13 goals, 13 assists), second in MLS behind only Inter Miami's Lionel Messi (34).
This is the third straight season Evander has recorded at least 13 goals and 13 assists, one of two players to do so in three straight seasons in MLS history (Messi 2024-26).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Atlanta have lost two of eight all-time home games against Cincinnati (W4 D2). The two defeats, 2-1 losses in 2023 and 2024, were the only two home matches in which Atlanta has trailed at all against them, going behind for a total of 46 minutes, 16 seconds over the eight matches.

The Five Stripes also avoided defeat for the fourth time in five matches with a 2–2 draw against NYCFC on September 26 (W1 D3). Atlanta have scored multiple goals in eight of their last 12 regular-season matches (18 goals) after finding the net more than once in just four of their first 15 league games this year (14 goals).

Cincinnati, meanwhile, have won only one of their 14 regular-season away matches (D6 L7) in 2026, including going winless in eight straight on the road (D4 L4). From 2023 to 2025, they had 29 regular-season away wins, six more than any other team over that time (Orlando City – 23).
Atlanta United – 35.7%

1fovopk176myj14sm66idi1vin.title: Mendez predicts 'big things' for Columbus ahead of trip to Inter Miami
1fovopk176myj14sm66idi1vin.subtitle: The Columbus Crew still have hope of reaching the playoffs this season, and those ambitions will be tested once again by Inter Miami.
paragraphs: Brais Mendez believes things will only get better for the Columbus Crew this season as they prepare to welcome Inter Miami to the ScottsMiracle-Gro Field this weekend.
The Crew kept their playoff hopes alive with a 2-0 win over CF Montreal last time out, with second-half goals from Mohamed Farsi and Mendez sealing the win for Columbus.
Laurent Courtois' side are 13th in the Eastern Conference and six points adrift of FC Cincinnati in ninth, while their win against Montreal ended a two-game losing stretch.
Columbus also have the US Open Cup final to look forward to on October 21, with Western Conference high-flyers St. Louis City SC their opponents in the showpiece match.
Since signing a three-year deal with Columbus in July, Mendez has scored three times in nine MLS appearances, including a brilliant free-kick against Montreal.
Mendez revealed he was still adjusting to his new surroundings, but he believes Columbus are in for an exciting end to the season if they can maintain their winning momentum.
"Everything is a process, and everything needs its time, especially for me to adapt to my team-mates, the club, the culture, the hot weather of Columbus," Mendez said.
"The humidity is different to Spain's. I feel better now and more connected to my team-mates. I am very happy to help the team and be here. Big things will come. I am sure of it."
"I knew that the goalkeeper thought that I was going to cross the ball, I knew I could catch him by surprise.
"That's why I tried to place it as far as possible from him so he would not be able to reach it at the far post. I hit it well and I scored."
Columbus come up against a Miami team that are third in the East following a 2-2 draw with San Diego FC last weekend, with Anders Dreyer netting an 82nd-minute equaliser.
Lionel Messi had cancelled out Dreyer's opener, with Luis Suarez then turning the contest in Miami's favour in the 74th minute, only for the Herons to concede shortly afterwards.
Cristian Gonzalez will, however, be without several of his starting players, including Messi, who is preparing for his final match for Argentina against Benin on October 6.

German Berterame, Fricio Caicedo, Rodrigo De Paul, Lovend's Delinois, Matias Galarza, Daniel Pinter, Alex Shaw and Dayne St. Clair are also on international duty with their respective nations, something Gonzalez said Miami must simply deal with.
"Yes, obviously in this kind of situation. Being in such an important team, we have national team players, and we have to adapt," Gonzalez said.
"I always say the same thing, when you have a squad that is not so prolonged in terms of players, we have to find a way and try to put together the best team to go there and win the game."
Columbus Crew – Brais Mendez
Mendez scored his second direct free-kick goal, and the Crew's third of the year, after Columbus had scored one regular-season direct free-kick goal from 2023 to 2025.
He is the second Crew player in the last decade with multiple direct free-kick goals in a season, after Lucas Zelarayan in 2021 and 2022.
Inter Miami – Luis Suarez
Miami will have to make do without Messi, who has four goals in four career matches against Columbus, recording braces in both October 2024 and May 2025.
But they have a capable deputy in Suarez, who has 13 goals in 22 MLS appearances this season. He also has four goal involvements (three goals, one assist) in four league matches against the Crew.
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER MIAMI WIN

Miami are unbeaten in eight straight regular-season matches against Columbus (W6 D2), last losing to the Crew in August 2022. This is the Herons' longest unbeaten run against a single opponent in league play in club history.

Since returning from the World Cup break, Miami have won just one of the eight regular-season matches in which Messi has contributed to a goal (D5 L2). Prior to this, they had failed to win just 11 times in 46 league matches in which Messi had a goal involvement (W35 D8 L3).

Columbus, meanwhile, won for just the second time in nine regular-season matches last time out. The Crew have just one set of consecutive league wins since July 2025, defeating the Los Angeles Galaxy and Philadelphia Union in April.
Columbus Crew – 33.7%

1fr5599lsvglq1r2h77jygquek.title: Malen says Roma can 'do something special' ahead of crunch meeting with Como
1fr5599lsvglq1r2h77jygquek.subtitle: Roma have marked themselves out as the foremost challengers for Inter's Serie A crown early on this season, ahead of their trip to Como.
paragraphs: Donyell Malen believes Roma can achieve special things this season and says Giallorossi coach Gian Piero Gasperini has finally helped him fulfil his potential.
Roma have taken 13 points from their opening five games to set the pace at the top of Serie A, alongside Inter, ahead of Sunday's showdown with Scudetto outsiders Como.
And Malen has been a key part of the Giallorossi's flying start, plundering six goals already to lead the Golden Boot race.
Malen had to withdraw from the Netherlands' squad during the recent international break, having reportedly experienced discomfort in his knee, though the issue is not thought to be significant.

In fact, Italian media reports suggest Malen will be available to face Como at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia this weekend, and ahead of that fixture, the forward discussed how he has rediscovered his love for the game since leaving Aston Villa in January.
"It was my decision," Malen told Corriere dello Sport, when asked about his move from Villa to the Italian capital.
"I wanted to play and be part of a team where I could take to the field every weekend and play an important role.
"At that stage, I didn't feel important, so I think I made the best choice. Today, I feel I'm in the right place with the right people.
"The coach and my team-mates show a lot of confidence in me, and together, all of this is helping me become the player I dreamed of being."

Gasperini has overseen 299 wins in Serie A overall, and his next victory will make him just the fifth manager to win 300 or more matches in the competition's history, after Giovanni Trapattoni (352), Massimiliano Allegri (324), Luciano Spalletti (306) and Nereo Rocco (302).

Malen has been hugely impressed with the way the 68-year-old has Roma playing this term – only Inter scored more goals (15 to 14) or generated more expected goals (14.5 xG to 12.8) across the first five matchdays than the Giallorossi, who drew 2-2 with the champions in their most recent game.
"As a team, you know, we were strong and connected, and I immediately had a very good feeling," Malen added. "We can build on moments like these and do something special."
Como have also started strongly, earning 10 points from their first five games, though they were beaten 2-0 by surprise package Frosinone going into the international break.

Nevertheless, Fabregas' work with the club has earned him plenty of admirers, and president Mirwan Suwarso says that when the time comes for the former midfielder to move on, he will not stand in his way.
"He doesn't need a clause to go anywhere he wants," Suwarso said. "In a business like this, he's a friend more than anything else. He can go wherever he wants, whenever he wants.
"If tomorrow he calls me and says, 'Hey, I want to go to Leverkusen'. I would say if that's something you want to do, then go. I don't need any compensation."
Como – Tasos Douvikas
With 12 goals in 2026, Douvikas has already set the record for the most goals scored by a Como player in a single calendar year in Serie A.
However, each of the Greek forward's last five league goals have come away from home, and he is seeking his first Serie A strike at the Sinigaglia since March 22, when he netted against Pisa.
Roma – Donyell Malen
Since making his Serie A debut for Roma on January 18, 2026, Malen has been the leading scorer across Europe's big five leagues, netting 20 times in 23 appearances.

Roma have taken 13 points from their opening five games to set the pace at the top of Serie A, alongside Inter, ahead of Sunday's showdown with Scudetto outsiders Como.

And Malen has been a key part of the Giallorossi's flying start, plundering six goals already to lead the Golden Boot race.

Malen had to withdraw from the Netherlands' squad during the recent international break, having reportedly experienced discomfort in his knee, though the issue is not thought to be significant.

In fact, Italian media reports suggest Malen will be available to face Como at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia this weekend, and ahead of that fixture, the forward discussed how he has rediscovered his love for the game since leaving Aston Villa in January.

"It was my decision," Malen told Corriere dello Sport, when asked about his move from Villa to the Italian capital.

"I wanted to play and be part of a team where I could take to the field every weekend and play an important role.

"At that stage, I didn't feel important, so I think I made the best choice. Today, I feel I'm in the right place with the right people.

"The coach and my team-mates show a lot of confidence in me, and together, all of this is helping me become the player I dreamed of being."
