1frt5j1auot131241p6kvlwwc5.title: 'It's not tennis' – Barella unconcerned by Italy rotation role
1frt5j1auot131241p6kvlwwc5.subtitle: Italy star Nicolo Barella believes he needs to step up when it comes to goalscoring, as he hailed Roberto Mancini's impact.
paragraphs: Italy midfielder Nicolo Barella has no issue with having to fight for his place in the starting XI.

It has been a mixed start to their Nations League campaign for Italy, with Roberto Mancini's side having lost 2-0 to Belgium before crushing Turkiye 4-1 in Bursa, and salvaging a 1-1 draw with France.
Barella missed out on the matchday squad for the Turkiye trip, and was only used as a substitute in Paris. He has featured for only 108 minutes across the three games so far.
During that time, Barella failed to register a goal or an assist.
However, he is expected to line up for the Azzurri in Bologna on Monday.
Speaking to reporters before the game, Barella said: "I am not old, but I do have a lot of games in my legs and have had to learn how to listen to my body.
"Playing 70 games a year, you don't have the same sharpness you did at age 23, but looking at the statistics, I am still one of those who covers the most ground.
"The only thing I'm lacking for the Nazionale is a few goals. That is where I'm lagging behind."
When asked about his response to not starting against France, Barella simply replied: "This is a team sport, it's not tennis."
Barella also spoke glowingly of Mancini, who he won the European Championship under in 2021.

"One of the best things about the coach is that he allows us players to feel a sense of peace. We had some very difficult and not positive experiences in recent years, especially when it comes to me, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Alessandro Bastoni," Barella said.
"The coach asked us to rediscover our enthusiasm, and I think we are doing that, because otherwise we wouldn't have got back on track in France and then nearly won it at the end."

1fx6014g8ajgl1xs79ntj1rz27.title: 'It's very hard to say no' to Napoli, says Gilmour
1fx6014g8ajgl1xs79ntj1rz27.subtitle: Billy Gilmour is playing his third season for Napoli, after getting an offer he could not refuse from them back in the summer of 2024.
paragraphs: Billy Gilmour admitted it was "very hard to say no" when Napoli approached him while at Brighton.
Gilmour spent two years with the Seagulls before making the move from the Amex Stadium to Napoli in August 2024, signing a five-year contract in Italy.
He has made 52 appearances for the Partenopei in all competitions and won the Scudetto in his first season at the club, under Antonio Conte.
The midfielder scored the first goal of his club career last term, netting in a 3-2 win over Pisa, and he has also hit the back of the net in 2026-27, in a 1-1 draw with Fiorentina.
"It's an exciting league,” Gilmour told Premier Sports TV.
"When you have these big clubs from Italy who approach and say they want to sign you, it's very hard to say no.
"I wanted to come here; I wanted to challenge for trophies and be at such a great club."
Gilmour signed for Napoli on the same day as Scotland team-mate Scott McTominay, who has taken Napoli by storm since his debut.
McTominay was named the Serie A Player of the Year in 2025 for his part in Napoli's Scudetto success, while he has been named in the league's Team of the Year in both of his seasons so far.
The 29-year-old has made 82 appearances, scoring 27 goals, though he is currently sidelined following heart surgery to correct a mild cardiac arrhythmia.
He is expected to return after the international break.
"Since he's been here, Scott's confidence has grown massively," Gilmour said.
"You can see how much he means to the fans and to us as players; we can rely on him whenever we need a goal and need help. The same goes for Scotland.
"We're missing Scott now, and hopefully things went well; we can't wait to have him back."

1fxfhwmm4r3j91g49fvpiehwoh.title: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United: Messi and Suarez double up to snap winless streak
1fxfhwmm4r3j91g49fvpiehwoh.subtitle: Inter Miami's winless streak came to an end in emphatic fashion, with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez starring in a 4-0 win over D.C United.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez both scored twice each to propel Inter Miami to a 4-0 victory over D.C. United.
Miami went into Saturday's contest at Nu Stadium without a win in five MLS games.
But their streak ended in style as Messi, fresh from his final appearance for Argentina, and Suarez did the damage.
Just three minutes had passed when Suarez opened the scoring with a delicate, lofted finish.

Messi played his part in Miami's second goal in the 39th minute, with his shot parried out by D.C. goalkeeper Sean Johnson. German Berterame got onto the rebound and cushioned a header back for Suarez to double up.
Determined not to be outdone, Messi got in on the act two minutes after half-time, with Suarez crossing it in for the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner to nudge home.
Messi then hit the post, but the 39-year-old doubled his tally soon after as he finished at the end of a trademark, mazy run into the area.
A hat-trick goal just evaded Messi when he fired wide late on, as Miami consolidated their place in second in the Eastern Conference.
Superstar strikers get Miami back on track
It has been a tough start for Miami coach Cristian Gonzalez, and the Herons needed a win in this fashion to really get themselves back on course ahead of the regular season run-in, and the playoffs.
They had their superstar attackers to thank, with Messi and Suarez delivering in the key moments.
Messi is now on 23 goals, four clear of any other rivals for MLS' Golden Boot, and a third successive MVP award is in the offing.
He has been directly involved in at least one goal in 11 straight matches in all competitions for Miami (12 goals, five assists).
This is after Messi went five straight league matches without a win for the first time in his career.
Suarez, meanwhile, is now on 24 MLS goal involvements for the season (15 goals, nine assists).
"Luis is one of the most important players on the squad," said Gonzalez. "He's totally committed, not only to us but to the club.
"Anybody who didn't understand before should understand now that he's a fundamental player for this team."

1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.title: Mbappe: Working under Zidane 'like something from a movie'
1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.subtitle: Current Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe will link up with former Blancos hero Zinedine Zidane for the first time this week, with France.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has likened being coached by Zinedine Zidane to "something from a movie", as France prepare to play their first game under the legendary former midfielder.
Zidane succeeded Didier Deschamps in the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup, which saw France reach the semi-finals before losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain.

Deschamps led Les Bleus for 14 years and 187 matches in total (also 103 as a player), overseeing their second World Cup triumph in 2018 in addition to runner-up finishes at the 2022 edition and at Euro 2016, with the latter tournament being on home soil.
And France's new era begins with a Nations League trip to Turkiye on Friday, with matches against Belgium – both home and away – and Italy to follow in the next two weeks.
Zidane made 108 appearances for France during his illustrious playing career, scoring 31 goals including a brace in their win over Brazil in the 1998 World Cup final.
He also scored a Panenka penalty in the 2006 final before receiving a red card for an infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi, as Italy went on to defeat Les Bleus on spot-kicks.
And Mbappe – who will keep hold of the captain's armband under the new regime – has a chance to pass Zidane in the all-time France appearance charts during the extended international break.
Mbappe's next cap will be his 107th, so he could potentially equal Zidane against Belgium next Monday and surpass him versus Italy on October 2, should he appear in all of those matches.

In an interview with AS, Mbappe recalled his first meeting with Zidane, which came when he was a youth player attracting interest from Europe's top clubs, while the former midfield icon was working in Real Madrid's academy.
"Years ago, he was the first to pick me up ‌and ⁠take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex. I was 13 or 14; it was ages ago," Mbappe said.
"And now he's my national team coach. It's like something from a movie, but he's top-level.
"It's real, we're in a new process in France, we have two years to prepare for the European Championships and we're working towards it now."

Zidane is the only manager to win three successive Champions League crowns, doing so with Real Madrid between 2015-16 and 2017-18, but he neglected to take another job in club football after leaving the Santiago Bernabeu for the second time in 2021.
He repeatedly outlined his interest in the France job during the latter years of Deschamps' tenure, and Mbappe is excited to see what changes he makes.
"It's a new phase with a new coach. It's going ⁠to be a new experience for everyone, since we've only ever had Deschamps," Mbappe said.
"It will be a change for us, but I think ⁠everything will turn out very well."

1g4fpyqghpmdg1bofbm17rsokk.title: Fleetwood to face more Premier League opposition as Man City draw Bradford in EFL Cup
1g4fpyqghpmdg1bofbm17rsokk.subtitle: The draw for the EFL Cup quarter-finals was made on Wednesday, with Fleetwood Town and Bradford City both getting glamour ties.
paragraphs: Manchester City will face Bradford City in the EFL Cup quarter-finals, while Fleetwood Town's reward for stunning Arsenal is another home game against top-flight opponents.
Man City edged out Brighton 4-3 in a penalty shoot-out in the fourth round on Wednesday, having come from behind on two occasions to draw 2-2 in 90 minutes.
Geronimo Rulli thwarted Lewis Dunk from the decisive spot-kick in that fourth-round tie, and Enzo Maresca's men will be at home again in the last eight.

League One promotion contenders Bradford will visit the Etihad Stadium following their 2-0 success over Peterborough, while the only other lower-league side still in the competition were also handed an eye-catching tie.
Fleetwood, who became just the seventh League Two team to beat a top-six team from the top flight when they overcame Arsenal on spot-kicks on Tuesday, will host either Everton or Newcastle United.
The Toffees and the Magpies – who won the EFL Cup in 2024-25 to end a domestic trophy drought spanning 70 years – will face off on Thursday, in the final tie of the fourth round.
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will face another reunion with his former club Bournemouth in the last eight, after masterminding a 1-0 success at the Vitality Stadium in September.

The Reds overcame Chelsea 6-5 in a shoot-out on Wednesday, having drawn 1-1 with their rivals in regulation time, while Bournemouth thrashed Aston Villa 3-0 to extend their winning run to five games in all competitions.
The final quarter-final tie will pit Crystal Palace against Sunderland, after they eliminated Fulham and Brentford, respectively, in the fourth round.
EFL Cup quarter-final tie in full

Manchester City v Bradford City
Fleetwood Town v Everton/Newcastle United
Liverpool v Bournemouth
Crystal Palace v Sunderland

1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.title: Slegers: Big Arsenal squad is a 'luxury problem'
1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.subtitle: Renee Slegers is prepared to rotate her Arsenal squad ahead of their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers believes having a large squad is a "luxury problem" as Arsenal prepare for their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
Arsenal won the Champions League in 2024-25 but fell at the semi-final hurdle last season, as Lyon came from behind to beat them on aggregate and reach the showpiece.
The Gunners, who also finished as runners-up to Manchester City in the Women's Super League last term, bolstered their squad over the summer as they aim to fight for silverware once again.

They brought in eight new signings, including Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodriguez, but so far, it has not had the desired effect, with Arsenal winning just one of their three WSL games (D2).
Slegers' side have a big week ahead of them, with a WSL clash with Chelsea to come after their Champions League outing.
But Slegers pointed out that Arsenal were prepared for their packed schedule.
"It's a luxury problem, of course," Slegers said when asked if a big squad was a nice problem to have.
"We have so many different options. The balance becomes, or the challenge becomes, how do you then choose certain things for certain games?
"We're still keeping the main ideas and consistency within the team. You don't chop and change everything.
"At the same time, if I look at where the players are at and where we are, from a game model understanding and players playing their roles, it's on a really high level throughout the squad.
"That also makes me really confident to say, 'I can make changes. These partnerships are working. This is working. This player knows her role on the pitch'.
"It's in a really good place, and that's where we wanted it to be. For the length of the season and all the games that we're going to play, we are able to do these things.

"The reason why we have the size of the squad with basically only senior national team players, so much quality doubled up in every position, is that we can use the whole squad. Especially when it's short turnarounds and we need freshness."
Arsenal are heavy favourites to beat Koge, with an 81.1% win probability according to the Opta supercomputer.
They have won both of their previous meetings with Koge in the Champions League, beating them twice in the 2021-22 group stage (3-0 home, 5-1 away).
However, Arsenal have lost their opening game in each of the last two Champions League seasons: 2-5 to Bayern Munich in 2024-25 and 1-2 to Lyon in 2025-26.
Slegers is also familiar with Koge herself, having faced them while in charge of Rosengard, and she is expecting a tough challenge.
"They're, of course, top of the league in Denmark," Slegers said. "They're a good team.

1gh6km6ztujfn1mybx1zd8jx6l.title: Pocognoli wants first Scotland win for the players' sake
1gh6km6ztujfn1mybx1zd8jx6l.subtitle: Sebastien Pocognoli is still waiting for his first win as Scotland boss, and he knows his players need more confidence.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli is eager to win his first game as Scotland boss so his players can grow in confidence.
Pocognoli's reign as Scotland boss began with a goalless draw with Slovenia, though his first home match ended in a 3-0 defeat against Switzerland after Jack Hendry was sent off early on.
Scotland have failed to score in each of their last four internationals for only the second time in their history, after May 1971; they have never gone five straight games without a goal.

Pocognoli (D1 L1) could become only the fourth Scotland manager to fail to win any of their first three games in charge of the national team after John Prentice, Berti Vogts and George Burley, with the trio all failing to win any of their first four matches.
While Pocognoli denied suggestions Scotland must beat North Macedonia on Saturday, he knows they need a win sooner rather than later.
"No, because the challenge is longer than this camp, you know, we have to do piece by piece," Pocognoli told BBC Scotland when asked about feeling pressure for the win.
"For sure, we want to have a first really positive [win] on the pitch.

"In terms of ranking, we want this, but I think it's important for the players to have a first win, that everything makes sense because the win makes the joy and the joy gives the freedom on the pitch to make decisions and to accelerate the process.
"If we have the three points in Slovenia, which I think we deserve, we talk maybe a little bit differently, but it's like this."
Scotland have lost only one of their previous seven away matches in all competitions (W4 D2), keeping a clean sheet in five of those matches.
After losing their first ever encounter with North Macedonia in September 2008 (0-1), Scotland are unbeaten in their three meetings since (W2 D1), winning 2-1 most recently in September 2013.

1gpk2w4i99ndh1glrfkpp13zyb.title: Cifuentes urges Portland to find clinical edge ahead of trip to San Jose
1gpk2w4i99ndh1glrfkpp13zyb.subtitle: The Portland Timbers will be looking to keep their playoff hopes alive when they make the trip to the San Jose Earthquakes this weekend.
paragraphs: Marti Cifuentes believes the only thing missing from his Portland Timbers team is the final product in attack after their disappointing defeat to Atlanta United last time out.
Portland were beaten 1-0 by the Five Stripes at Providence Park, with Aleksey Miranchuk's 28th-minute strike enough to compound the Timbers to a 12th defeat of the season.
That is despite Portland registering an expected goals (xG) total of 2.3 from their 21 shots at Lucas Hoyos' net to Atlanta's tally of 0.85 from their 10 attempts.

It was a result that left the Timbers in a precarious position in the Western Conference, with Cifuentes' side ninth in the division, but the Seattle Sounders, San Diego FC and Austin FC are all within striking distance.

Portland's struggles against teams below them in the standings has been a recurring theme in 2026, and ahead of a trip to PayPal Park to face the San Jose Earthquakes, Cifuentes wants his team to take their chances when they arrive.
"We created more shots, we regained the ball higher up the pitch and there was a lot of positives, but that does not explain the whole history," Cifuentes said.
"The whole history is that we need to be better in front of goal and we need to be more clinical. We need to be better in how we break down low blocks and so on.
"It's going to be a good challenge against San Jose because of the situations we are talking about. There are a lot of situations, but I do not want to spend my time there.
"I want to be focused, be positive and have a lot of energy to go to San Jose that are having a good season, and try to leave there with a good feeling."
San Jose, meanwhile, kept their playoff push going with a 2-2 draw against 10-man Los Angeles FC, with Reid Roberts scoring a 98th-minute equaliser for Bruce Arena's side.
Son Heung-min had given LAFC the lead before Aaron Long was sent off, but Denis Bouanga doubled the visitors' lead eight minutes into the second half at Levi's Stadium.
However, substitute Preston Judd halved the deficit, before Roberts' drive from distance nestled into the bottom-right corner to seal a share of the spoils.
The Earthquakes are fifth in the West and just two points off fourth-place FC Dallas, and Arena believes their draw with LAFC was a true test of his team's character against a difficult opposition.
"The fact that we went down two goals and came back and got a point out of the game is a tremendous test of character and competitiveness on our part," Arena said.
"I thought LAFC did an outstanding job in trying to close out the game. So give both teams credit. This was a really good MLS game today. A lot of quality out there.
"I think that was a very entertaining game for the people here, and to see players like Son [Heung-min] and [Denis] Bouanga and [Hugo] Lloris, he was fantastic.
"And to see quality like [Timo] Werner and have those kinds of players on the field, that was enjoyable and a great setting. The fan base was great. So a good day for MLS."
SJ Earthquakes – Reid Roberts
Roberts scored at 97:32 to secure a deserved point against LAFC last time out.

It was the latest result-changing goal by an Earthquakes player in an MLS match since Shea Salinas (97:34) scored a match-winning goal on July 15, 2020, in the MLS is Back Group Stage against the Vancouver Whitecaps.
Portland Timbers – Kristoffer Velde
Among players currently on the Timbers roster, Velde leads Portland in both goals (eight) and assists (nine).

With another assist, Velde would become the fifth player in club history have 10+ assists in a single MLS regular season, joining Diego Valeri (five), Sebastian Blanco (twice), Evander and Santiago Moreno.
MATCH PREDICTION: SJ EARTHQUAKES WIN

San Jose are unbeaten in their last four games with Portland (W3 D1) across all competitions, including a 3-1 win away from home in May. The Earthquakes have never swept the season series, while the four-match unbeaten run is their longest in the fixture since the Timbers joined MLS in 2011.

The Earthquakes' 12 victories this season are their most wins in a single season since the team's 13-win campaign in 2019. After having 11 wins in 2025, it marks the first time San Jose have recorded double-digit wins in back-to-back seasons since 2012 and 2013.

Portland, meanwhile, have failed to record a clean sheet on the road this regular season, one of four MLS teams without one. The Timbers have never gone a full MLS regular season without a road clean sheet after equalling their club record with five during the 2025 season.
Portland Timbers – 27.3%

1gr2oxy674iy1c3f2w4kk8fiv.title: Women's Super League predictions: Man City backed to record historic derby win over Man Utd
1gr2oxy674iy1c3f2w4kk8fiv.subtitle: Manchester City have won all six of their Women's Super League matches this season ahead of facing rivals Manchester United on Sunday.
paragraphs: Manchester City could extend their perfect start to the Women's Super League season when they face rivals Manchester United in the blockbuster clash of MD7.
Another derby, this time in north London, starts the weekend's action as Tottenham look to get back to winning ways against fellow strugglers Arsenal on Saturday.
Brighton host West Ham in the other match that day, before unbeaten Chelsea travel to Crystal Palace in Sunday's early kick-off.
Birmingham City and Charlton Athletic go head-to-head as they both look to escape the relegation zone, while Everton welcome Aston Villa to Goodison Park.
Alexia Putellas and the London City Lionesses face Liverpool before the Manchester derby rounds off the weekend.
Here's how the Opta supercomputer predicts MD7 of the WSL will unfold in what promises to be an exciting round of fixtures.
Tottenham have lost only two of their last five WSL home games against Arsenal (W1 D1), drawing 0-0 in this fixture last season, but Spurs' recent record in the competition has let them down.
After going unbeaten in their first four league games this season (W3 D1), Spurs have lost 6-1 to London City and 6-2 to Chelsea in their last two games.
Indeed, Spurs are only the second team in WSL history to concede six or more goals in back-to-back games, after Doncaster Rovers Belles in 2013.
And the supercomputer has backed them to falter again, as they won just 21.6% of the pre-match simulations and clinched a draw in a further 21.8%.
Arsenal are winless in their last four games across all competitions (D2 L2), but have been given a 56.6% win probability.
Arsenal have won 10 of their 13 north London derbies in the WSL (D2 L1), scoring five goals in their last two wins: 5-0 in February 2025, 5-2 in March 2026.
The Gunners will be keen to see Alessia Russo return to her best; she has scored more WSL goals against Spurs (eight) than any other opponent.
Just one point separates ninth-place West Ham and 12th-place Brighton, and the supercomputer is backing the Seagulls to win their second league game of the season.
Brighton have a 50.4% chance of victory to the Hammers' 24.5%, with the probability of a draw coming in at 25.1%.

Brighton have scored seven goals across their last two league games, more than across their previous seven (six) – they could score at least two goals in three consecutive WSL matches in the same season for the first time.
And after losing their first two WSL home games against West Ham, Brighton have since won five of six home meetings with the Hammers in the top-flight (L1).
However, West Ham have won four of their nine WSL away games in 2026 (L5), as many away victories as they managed across 2023 (two), 2024 (one) and 2025 (one) combined.
CRYSTAL PALACE V CHELSEA
This is the fourth successive WSL season Chelsea have started with an unbeaten run of at least six, and the third in a row that they have conceded exactly three times after six matches.
The Blues are unbeaten in each of their last 38 WSL games across September, October and November (W33 D5), since a 2-1 loss away to Liverpool in September 2022.
The supercomputer has given Chelsea a 75.4% likelihood of victory, the most of any team on MD7.
Palace have a 10.7% chance of causing a major upset and a 13.9% probability of clinching a draw, but their WSL record against the Blues does not bode well.
In the WSL era, Chelsea have won all seven of their matches against Palace in all competitions by an aggregate score of 25-0.

Palace have also lost 10 of their 11 London derbies in the WSL (D1), conceding 47 goals and scoring just five times. Chelsea meanwhile are unbeaten in their last 11 away derbies (W9 D2) in the competition and could break the record for the longest streak without defeat on the road in such matches.
BIRMINGHAM CITY V CHARLTON ATHLETIC
Birmingham and Charlton occupy the bottom two spots in the WSL, with neither side recording a win following their respective promotions.

Charlton (L6) remain one of two teams without a point across the WSL and WSL2 this season (also Durham – L5); the only sides to lose their first seven matches in the WSL are Yeovil Town (first seven in 2017) and Leicester City (first nine in 2021).
Last time out against Arsenal, Birmingham took a point from a WSL away game against a 'big four' opponent for the first time in 14 attempts.

Birmingham are the supercomputer's favourites for this basement battle, winning 53.3% of the pre-match simulations, though Charlton, who won 22.8% of the simulations and secured a draw in 23.9%, have a strong record in this fixture.
They have kept a clean sheet in each of their last three away league games against Birmingham, taking seven points from those matches (two 1-0 wins and a 0-0 draw).
EVERTON V ASTON VILLA

Everton have won five of their last seven WSL home games (L2), having lost a club-record six in a row before that. The Toffees could now win four in a row on home turf for the very first time, and they have the backing of the supercomputer.
Everton have a 50.8% chance of victory at Goodison Park, while Villa have a 24.2% probability of winning, and a 25% chance of snatching a draw.
Villa have only won one of their last five WSL away games against Everton (W3 D1), scoring first on each of those five visits.
They picked up their first victory of the season last time out against Liverpool, though they have not won back-to-back WSL games since winning their final five matches of the 2024-25 campaign.
It will be a special occasion for Villa's interim boss Brian Sorensen, who has taken charge of more WSL games with Everton (80) than any other manager.
LIVERPOOL V LONDON CITY LIONESSES
London City are on a four-game winning streak in the WSL, which is as many victories as they had achieved through their first 13 games in the competition under Eder Maestre (W4 D3 L6).

They could become just the fourth team to win three consecutive WSL away games by at least three goals, after Arsenal (longest run is five), Man City (four) and Chelsea (three), but they are set for a stern test at St Helens Stadium.

London City have a 41.6% likelihood of victory according to the supercomputer, which has also given Liverpool a 32.8% chance of winning and a 25.6% probability of holding their opponents to a draw at home.
Liverpool are winless in each of their last five league games against London City (D3 L2), since a 1-0 away win in December 2020 in the WSL2.
However, 67% of Liverpool's points won in the WSL in 2026 have come in home matches (14/21), the highest percentage by any side with at least games played this year.
MANCHESTER UNITED V MANCHESTER CITY

Victory for league leaders Manchester City would prove to be historic; they won 3-0 at home and 3-0 away to Manchester United last season and could be the first team on either side of the Manchester derby to win three in a row in the WSL.

City have maintained a perfect record in the WSL so far this season (6/6) and could equal their best start to a campaign in the competition alongside 2017-18 (7/7), when they were also reigning champions.
The supercomputer has given Andree Jeglertz's side a 48.5% chance of victory against the Red Devils, who have a 27.5% probability of winning and a 24% likelihood of clinching a draw.

United have won their last three WSL games, having gone winless in the seven prior (D3 L4); however, the Red Devils have won the fewest points in games between the 'big four' since the start of last season (four – D4 L4) while City have won the most (15 – W5 L2).
If United are to cause an upset on Sunday, they will need to find a way to keep Khadija Shaw quiet.

Shaw could make her 100th WSL appearance – with 90 goals in 99 games, she has already scored 12 more goals than any other player managed in their first 100 outings. Shaw could also become the first player to score in their first six starts of a WSL season.

However, 67% of Liverpool's points won in the WSL in 2026 have come in home matches (14/21), the highest percentage by any side with at least games played this year.

MANCHESTER UNITED V MANCHESTER CITY

Victory for league leaders Manchester City would prove to be historic; they won 3-0 at home and 3-0 away to Manchester United last season and could be the first team on either side of the Manchester derby to win three in a row in the WSL.

City have maintained a perfect record in the WSL so far this season (6/6) and could equal their best start to a campaign in the competition alongside 2017-18 (7/7), when they were also reigning champions.

The supercomputer has given Andree Jeglertz's side a 48.5% chance of victory against the Red Devils, who have a 27.5% probability of winning and a 24% likelihood of clinching a draw.

United have won their last three WSL games, having gone winless in the seven prior (D3 L4); however, the Red Devils have won the fewest points in games between the 'big four' since the start of last season (four – D4 L4) while City have won the most (15 – W5 L2).

If United are to cause an upset on Sunday, they will need to find a way to keep Khadija Shaw quiet.

Shaw could make her 100th WSL appearance – with 90 goals in 99 games, she has already scored 12 more goals than any other player managed in their first 100 outings. Shaw could also become the first player to score in their first six starts of a WSL season.

1gsplow0f3z7q14o77x67kjbzw.title: Real Madrid 4-1 Sevilla: Mbappe at the double for Mourinho's men
1gsplow0f3z7q14o77x67kjbzw.subtitle: Real Madrid put together back-to-back LaLiga wins on Sunday as Kylian Mbappe continued his fine form with two goals against Sevilla.
paragraphs: Real Madrid followed up their dramatic Champions League win over Roma by scoring four goals once again as Kylian Mbappe netted twice in a 4-1 victory over Sevilla.
With the suspended Vinicius Junior unavailable, Mbappe led from the front, while summer signing Yan Diomande also impressed by grabbing a goal and an assist on Sunday.
But Sevilla started brightly at Estadio Bernabeu, with Robbie Ure's glancing header saved by Thibaut Courtois before Ruben Vargas fired just wide of the left post on the swivel.

Federico Valverde's shot from distance was then inadvertently cleared by Mbappe, but Madrid opened the scoring in the 30th minute in some style. Diomande drove down the left before laying the ball back to Arda Guler, who curled a sensational strike over Odysseas Vlachodimos.

And Jose Mourinho's side doubled their advantage seven minutes later through Mbappe, with the Frenchman collecting Jude Bellingham's neat flick on the turn before rounding Vlachodimos and rolling the ball home.
Chidera Ejuke, a half-time replacement for Sevilla, almost made an instant impact but could only fire over before Diomande pulled his shot wide at the other end moments later.

But the hosts pulled further clear just after the hour when Mbappe was tripped inside the penalty area by Andres Castrin, with the Madrid number 10 stepping up and confidently dinking the resulting spot-kick down the middle.

Sevilla did not let their heads drop and got themselves on the scoresheet in the 80th minute when Manu Bueno dispossessed Mbappe before playing a neat one-two with Lucas Stassin and curling into the bottom-left corner.

However, any hopes of an unlikely Sevilla comeback were ruthlessly ended by Diomande, who capped a fine individual performance with a stunning strike that rifled into the top corner and sealed an emphatic victory.
Mbappe haunts Sevilla again as Diomande breaks Bellingham's record

The attacking emphasis was largely resting on the shoulders of Mbappe with Vinicius serving the first of his four-match suspension following his red card against Villarreal for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair, and he delivered against one of his favourite opponents.

Mbappe has now been involved in six goals in five LaLiga games against Sevilla (five goals, one assist), scoring in four different matches against them, and he did all the work for his second goal after being fouled inside the Sevilla box.

It is the ninth penalty he has won since joining Madrid from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024. In that time, only Ante Budimir (12) and Serhou Guirassy (10) have won more penalties among players from the top five European leagues.

But there was also a standout display from Diomande, who became the first player under the age of 20 (19 years and 338 days) to both score and assist in the same LaLiga match with Madrid in the 21st century, surpassing Bellingham's previous record (20y and 51d).

Diomande also provided an assist in two consecutive matches in all competitions for the first time in his career in the top five European leagues, and his performance was key in helping Madrid accumulate an expected goals (xG) total of 2.24 from their 15 shots to Sevilla's 0.75 from their 11 attempts.

1gtkotpxbi2551iem6y7kcf3oh.title: Hat-trick hero Barcola showed his level against LASK, says Iraola
1gtkotpxbi2551iem6y7kcf3oh.subtitle: Liverpool made it two wins from two to begin their Champions League campaign, with Bradley Barcola hitting a hat-trick against LASK.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola said Bradley Barcola was "in the zone" during Liverpool's thumping 6-3 win over LASK in the Champions League, a match that saw him score a hat-trick.
Liverpool registered a confidence-boosting win at Raiffeisen Arena on Wednesday having come into the game on the back of a defeat to Manchester City in the Premier League.
Barcola had failed to register a goal contribution in his first six games in all competitions for the Reds, but he produced a fine display to get his Liverpool career up and running.
Ronald Araujo had headed Liverpool in front before Barcola opened his account with a sweeping 24-minute finish, going on to double his goal tally just before half-time.
Jeremie Frimpong pulled Liverpool further clear, only for Robert Ljubicic to pull one back, but Barcola completed his hat-trick in the 66th minute to all but secure the victory.

Barcola's hat-trick was just the fifth scored by a Liverpool player in an away match in the European Cup/Champions League and the first since Mohamed Salah against Rangers in 2022, while it was the Frenchman's first-ever treble in the 238th appearance of his senior career (for club and country combined).

Ahead of kick-off, Iraola leapt to the defence of Barcola and Florian Wirtz, insisting he had "100% trust" in the pair amid Liverpool's injury issues, and the Spaniard believed the big-money duo more than proved their worth.
"I think he played so well today and not just the goals. He had more chances to score, he was always a threat attacking the spaces in behind," Iraola said of Barcola.
"In training, sometimes you feel when a player is in the zone, and fortunately, tonight for us, he has shown the level that he has."
On Wirtz, who notched his second assist of the season in all competitions, Iraola added: "I think he was amazing in possession.
"I think he had lively passes, good assists, he helped us to control the game. Especially in the first half where he was roaming around and finding good spots."

Liverpool had 19 shots by half-time against LASK – the most on record (since 2003-04) by any team in the first half of a Champions League away match. Furthermore, their 26 shots overall were the Reds' joint-most in an away game in the competition on record.

The Reds also scored 6+ goals in a European Cup/Champions League away game for just the third time, previously doing so in 2017 (7-0 v Maribor) and 2022 (7-1 v Rangers), though there was some concern at the opposite end of the pitch.
Jeremy Jacquet and Araujo were replaced by Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez just after the hour, with all three of LASK's goals coming when the substitutes were on the pitch.
After Lewis Koumas had put Liverpool 5-1 up, two goals in three minutes from Florian Flecker threatened a nervy finish, but the damage had already been done by the visitors.
"Probably the reason why the manager shouldn't change both centre-backs," Iraola said of his team's defensive woes.
"But we were already winning 4-0, and you have to think about the next game and saving the legs of the players. We didn't defend properly at the end of the game."

1gx0lwmkxy6021ggesfypovjdc.title: Pochettino names 'perfect role model' Adams as new USA captain
1gx0lwmkxy6021ggesfypovjdc.subtitle: Following Tim Ream's retirement from international football, Tyler Adams will once again wear the armband for the United States.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino has named "perfect role model" Tyler Adams as the United States' new captain.
The decision comes after previous captain Tim Ream announced his retirement from international football, with Adams taking on the role for the second time.
The Bournemouth midfielder led the USA at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, where they were knocked out in the last 16 by the Netherlands.
Pochettino's side reached the same stage this summer when they hosted the tournament, and he believes Adams is the right person to lead the team through the next World Cup cycle.
"I think [we're] so happy to announce and for everyone to know that he's going to be our leader and our captain," Pochettino said about Adams.

"I think we've been [in] a very good relationship in the last two years. I think we were talking a lot, and I think he knows what I expect, and he's a perfect role model for everyone in the way that the philosophy, the future, representing that amazing country.
"I think he's the player and the person that can lead that period that we have ahead. And I [say] congratulations."
The USA have impressed during this international break, following up a 4-1 win over Peru with a 4-2 victory over Chile.
Next up for Pochettino's side is a clash with rivals Mexico, and the former Tottenham boss feels a tough atmosphere at State Farm Stadium will help his team grow.
"I think this type of adversity is a good example," added Pochettino.
"I celebrate to have this type of game, to play in a difficult atmosphere, and I think that for sure is going to help for the future."

1gy00wq8798me1htwues36m1rf.title: Arsenal teenager Dowman set for minutes amid Saka injury
1gy00wq8798me1htwues36m1rf.subtitle: With Bukayo Saka reportedly sidelined for up to eight weeks, Max Dowman is set for more minutes at Arsenal.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta revealed teenager Max Dowman will get minutes for Arsenal in the upcoming games following an injury to Bukayo Saka.
Saka was substituted off in the first 10 minutes of their Champions League showdown against Bayern Munich after suffering a quad injury.

No Arsenal player has directly contributed to more goals than Saka this season (five – level with Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice), and the winger has also created the fourth-most chances for the Gunners (12).
Reports suggest Saka could be out for up to eight weeks, though Arteta explained the severity of the injury is not yet known.
"He's got quite a lot of fluid in the area, so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury, but we will probably know more [on Saturday]," said Arteta.

"We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. Obviously, when a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, his movement is restricted; they are not good signs.
"So, again, let's be a little bit patient so we can get a definitive assessment, and I will let you know."
With Christos Tzolis also out with injury, Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke and Dowman are Arsenal's remaining options on the wing.
The Gunners have a busy schedule coming up, with five fixtures still to play before the international break starts on November 9.
Up first for Arsenal is Everton at home, the same fixture in which Dowman scored last season to become the youngest scorer in Premier League history.
"There is something inevitable to go back to that memory and the feeling of the moment," said Arteta. "That's with us, and that's going to stay in that stadium for a long, long time.
"He's [Dowman] training, and every time he's got a moment to play, he is showing that he is a player who is going to impact the game, so for sure he is going to have minutes.
"It would be a great story if we win the game, especially."

1h0myvt5xzcp01iwot46hhqt3d.title: 'This is what we love' – Zidane revels in France's comeback win
1h0myvt5xzcp01iwot46hhqt3d.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane remains unbeaten in charge of France after his first international break, with his substitutions securing three more points.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane hailed France's "complete team performance" after they came from behind to beat Belgium in the Nations League.

France triumphed 4-1 at the Stade de France, but Zidane's unbeaten start with Les Bleus looked under real threat when they still trailed through Dodi Lukebakio's 35th-minute goal heading into the final 13 minutes.
However, Zidane's substitutions more than paid off, with Desire Doue drawing France level before Rayan Cherki put them ahead four minutes later.
And a three-minute brace from Michael Olise, who also set up Cherki's goal, then rounded off the scoring to give France a stunning win that puts them within touching distance of the quarter-finals.
France were completely dominant, with the scoreline eventually reflecting that, and Zidane revelled in the stunning comeback victory.
"This is soccer, this is what we love," Zidane said.
"We faced some difficulties in the first half, but that's part of the game; it's the kind of match you get from time to time.
"It's good to set things right – which is what we did – and we managed to play an extraordinary second half.
"We knew the substitutes could change the game because they are high-quality players.

"But, once again, it was a complete team performance; while the substitutes might have made the difference when they came on, everyone has been good over these past two weeks – everyone played their part, and that's what stands out to me."
Doue, Cherki and Olise were all spellbinding. Each of them crafted two chances, while Olise ended up having four shots, a total bettered only by Ousmane Dembele (five).
Olise has scored in his last three games in the Nations League (four goals), with no France player netting more than him in this international break.
"It's a collective effort, too," Olise said.
"He [Zidane] brings in ideas; we follow them – we've done that well over the last four matches, we're going to continue like this."

1h1zcv7vrdlxw197nxu5nyy9yj.title: 'Amazing' PSG stand between Flick and 100th Barcelona win
1h1zcv7vrdlxw197nxu5nyy9yj.subtitle: Hansi Flick could earn his 100th win in charge of Barcelona on Tuesday, but the opposition are Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick reflected on a "great journey" with Barcelona as his 100th win in charge of the club could come in a mouth-watering Champions League tie with Paris Saint-Germain.
In one of the standout games in the league phase of this year's competition, the Spanish champions make the trip to the Parc des Princes to face the holders on Tuesday.
Barca have made an electric start to their LaLiga title defence, winning all nine of their opening games to sit five points clear of Atletico Madrid in the standings.

They are the first team to achieve the feat since Real Madrid in 1968-69, while their 39 goals are the second-most by a team after their first nine matches in LaLiga, after the Sevilla team of 1940-41 plundered 42 goals.
And Barca have also begun their quest for a first Champions League title since 2014-15 with thumping back-to-back wins over Feyenoord (5-1) and Galatasaray (4-1).
Flick saw his side beat Real Betis 5-2 in LaLiga on Saturday, taking the Barcelona boss to 99 wins from his 128 matches (D10 L19) in charge across all competitions.
"When we started here we already said we were ready. It has been a great journey. I appreciate the respect and affection of the Catalans, it's incredible," Flick told reporters.
"When you win, everyone is happy. And I think the team is doing very well. I'm very proud.
"The players came back from a long World Cup, people thought that they might not be 100% and they are. It's amazing to see them and the atmosphere in the dressing room."

This will be the 17th time that PSG have faced Barca (W6 D4 L6), which is the joint most games they have played against an opponent in major European competition (also 17 against Bayern Munich – W7 D1 L9).
PSG have won their last two games against Barca, while only Bayern have won three consecutive matches against them in the European Cup/Champions League (a run of six – May 2015 to October 2022).
And of fixtures played 10+ times in European Cup/Champions League history, only Ajax versus Bayern (3.9) has a higher goals-per-game ratio than PSG versus Barcelona (3.8 – 57 goals in 15 meetings).

Luis Enrique's side are unbeaten in their last 12 games in this competition (W8 D4), and can equal their longest ever unbeaten run in the European Cup/Champions League (13 games between October 2012 and November 2013).
"His team plays fantastic football, and he is one of the best coaches in the world," Flick said of Luis Enrique.
"I love their intensity, the pressure of their team, how they swap positions, the flexibility of their system. At this level, they're amazing. It's a fantastic job."
Since 2024-25, the two teams whose games have seen the most Champions League goals have been Barcelona (130) and PSG (134).
Flick has both the best goals per game ratio (three) and worst goals conceded per game ratio (1.6) of any Barca coach to take charge of 5+ games in the competition.
These two are among the favourites to reach the Champions League final in Madrid next June, though Flick is not looking that far ahead.
"I think tomorrow is a good test for us. I would like our team to play with confidence, as a team that has won the last eleven games," Flick added.
"We played against the best team in the world in the last two years. For us, it's an opportunity."

This will be the 17th time that PSG have faced Barca (W6 D4 L6), which is the joint most games they have played against an opponent in major European competition (also 17 against Bayern Munich – W7 D1 L9).

PSG have won their last two games against Barca, while only Bayern have won three consecutive matches against them in the European Cup/Champions League (a run of six – May 2015 to October 2022).

And of fixtures played 10+ times in European Cup/Champions League history, only Ajax versus Bayern (3.9) has a higher goals-per-game ratio than PSG versus Barcelona (3.8 – 57 goals in 15 meetings).

Luis Enrique's side are unbeaten in their last 12 games in this competition (W8 D4), and can equal their longest ever unbeaten run in the European Cup/Champions League (13 games between October 2012 and November 2013).

"His team plays fantastic football, and he is one of the best coaches in the world," Flick said of Luis Enrique.

"I love their intensity, the pressure of their team, how they swap positions, the flexibility of their system. At this level, they're amazing. It's a fantastic job."

Since 2024-25, the two teams whose games have seen the most Champions League goals have been Barcelona (130) and PSG (134).

Flick has both the best goals per game ratio (three) and worst goals conceded per game ratio (1.6) of any Barca coach to take charge of 5+ games in the competition.

These two are among the favourites to reach the Champions League final in Madrid next June, though Flick is not looking that far ahead. 

"I think tomorrow is a good test for us. I would like our team to play with confidence, as a team that has won the last eleven games," Flick added.

"We played against the best team in the world in the last two years. For us, it's an opportunity."

1h64s2rd5exkn16klbwyxxlsns.title: 'We're winning for Kompany,' says Brown after Bayern's emphatic DFB-Pokal win
1h64s2rd5exkn16klbwyxxlsns.subtitle: Bayern Munich stormed into the last 16 of the DFB-Pokal on Wednesday, with Nathaniel Brown praising the squad's unity in difficult times.
paragraphs: Nathaniel Brown says Bayern Munich are winning for head coach Vincent Kompany, who was recently discharged from hospital, following their 6-1 thrashing of Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal on Wednesday.
Bayern cruised to victory at Allianz Arena, with Michael Olise starring with a brace, while Brown, Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies and David Santos Daiber also got on the scoresheet.
Mateusz Zukowski cancelled out Olise's opener in the 15th minute, but the defending champions quickly regained control, restoring their lead before the break and running riot in the second half.
Olise converted from the penalty spot in the 50th minute before Davies, Brown and debutant Daiber added gloss to the scoreline late on.
"We want to win every game, regardless of the opponent," Brown said.
"We wanted to get through this Pokal tie. We had a good performance and deserved the win. Now we're focusing on Saturday [Der Klassiker]."
With Kompany continuing his recovery from home, Brown also made it clear that the team wants to deliver results for their head coach.
"We're also winning for [Kompany], of course," he added. "It's really good that he's back home now. He should get some rest, but I hope we'll see him again soon."
Wednesday's victory extended Bayern's winning run in the DFB-Pokal to eight matches – their second-longest streak after winning 13 on the trot between August 2018 and October 2020.
They are also now the only team from Europe's top five leagues still yet to taste defeat in 2026-27 (W9 D4).

Bayern have already scored 146 competitive goals in the calendar year 2026 (3.4 per game), which is at least 18 more than any other team from Europe's top five leagues (Barcelona – 128), and Jonathan Tah echoed Brown's sentiments, praising the squad's togetherness amid Kompany's absence.
"It's never easy, even though it looks like it from outside," Tah said.

"Regardless of who's on the pitch, when I look at the players who came on towards the end, Daiber scoring the goal and Binder coming on, it shows that we stick together as a team and that everyone is ready to deliver when called upon.

"That's something you have to work for in training. It makes me happy to see that, despite having players missing and the coach being absent at the moment, we're still able to produce performances like this on the pitch.
"I'd be lying if I said [Kompany's hospitalisation] didn't affect us in some way, because we're all human.  Of course, you feel for those affected.

"But ultimately, I think it's about being professional. When you consider what we can do right now to give those who aren't here some positive energy, the answer is to go out on the pitch and show what we showed. I'm pleased that we've managed to do that in each of our last two games."

1h66l6lcnvz121dhpm5e0rvqc2.title: Kane scoops first Ballon d'Or after pipping Yamal, Mbappe
1h66l6lcnvz121dhpm5e0rvqc2.subtitle: Harry Kane lifted the Ballon d'Or for the first time, on home soil in London, while Alexia Putellas took home her record-equalling third.
paragraphs: Harry Kane edged out Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to claim the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or, with Alexia Putellas claiming her third award.
Kane was one of the front-runners to be named for the trophy, and he became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to lift the prestigious award.

Confusion had swirled earlier on Monday when an article on the award's website claiming Kane had won the award went live ahead of the delayed ceremony, with similar pieces on Mbappe and Yamal also being published inadvertently before being taken down.

But at the star-studded event in London, it was Kane who took home the trophy after he scored 61 goals in all competitions in the 2025-26 season, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues.

It was the most by a player in a single season since Cristiano Ronaldo also scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15, while for club and country, Kane netted a superb 73 goals last season, having also helped England to a third-place finish at the World Cup.
Kane also took home the men's Gerd Muller Trophy after his astonishing goalscoring run.
Barcelona and Spain largely dominated the awards across both the men's and women's categories, with Lamine Yamal picking up the Kopa Award for the third straight year.

Yamal was involved in 41 goals in all competitions in 2025-26 (24 goals, 17 assists), 19 more than any other teenager in Europe's big five leagues as he helped Barcelona to win LaLiga and the Supercopa de Espana.

He also became the first player to play in both a European Championship and World Cup final as a teenager, having won Euro 2024 with La Roja two years ago before adding the world title to his collection.
He beat team-mate Pau Cubarsi, who was named Young Player of the Tournament at the World Cup, and upon receiving the award, Yamal said it should have been given to the defender.
"It is an honour to be here and receive this prize," Yamal said.
"I would have liked to see my team-mate Cubarsi here because I think this prize should have been for him. He has been playing at an excellent level for some time.
"This is my third year up here for this prize. I would like to thank my club and my national team. Speaking about this one specifically, this one should have been for Cubarsi."

The teenager finished third in the voting for the main award, also finishing behind Madrid's Kylian Mbappe. Lionel Messi finished in fifth, with World Cup-winning captain Rodri just above him in fourth.
Luis de la Fuente, meanwhile, won the Johan Cruyff Trophy as he was named men's coach of the year after leading Spain to the World Cup title.
He helped La Roja lift the trophy for the second time and has led Spain to a 42-match unbeaten streak in all competitions, the longest ever run by any European or South American team in history.
And their excellent defensive record at the tournament also meant Unai Simon was awarded the men's Yashin Trophy.
He conceded just one goal in Spain's eight World Cup games, the fewest goals conceded by any team in a World Cup-winning campaign.

Quadruple winners Barcelona swept the women's awards, with former captain Putellas, who now plays for the London City Lionesses, winning the women's Ballon d'Or for a record-equalling third time, becoming the second woman to do so after Aitana Bonmati last year.

Vicky Lopez won the women's Kopa Trophy for the second straight year after scoring the most goals (10) and registering the most assists (nine) of any teenager across the big-five women's leagues in Europe in 2025-26.
And their head coach, Pere Romeu, took the women's Johan Cruyff Trophy, having led the team to the 2025-26 Liga F trophy with 29 wins from 30 games, while registering a goal difference of +121.
Barcelona goalkeeper Cata Coll took home the women's Yashin Trophy for her part in the quadruple triumph, having conceded just six goals in 17 league games, while keeping 11 clean sheets.
So, it was no surprise when Barcelona were also named the women's Club of the Year.
Paris Saint-Germain took home the award for the men, pipping Arsenal – who they beat in the Champions League final for their second consecutive trophy.
Mexico and Pachuca striker Charlyn Corral clinched the women's Gerd Muller Trophy, becoming the first Mexican player to win an award at the Ballon d'Or ceremony.
Full List of Ballon d'Or Winners 2026
Men's Ballon d'Or – Harry Kane (Bayern Munich/England)
Women's Ballon d'Or – Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/Spain)
Men's Johan Cruyff Trophy – Luis de la Fuente (Spain)
Women's Johan Cruyff Trophy – Pere Romeu (Barcelona)
Men's Kopa Trophy – Lamine Yamal (Barcelona/Spain)
Women's Kopa Trophy – Vicky Lopez (Barcelona/Spain)
Men's Yashin Trophy – Unai Simon (Athletic Club/Spain)
Women's Yashin Trophy – Cata Coll (Barcelona/Spain)
Men's Gerd Muller Trophy – Harry Kane (Bayern Munich/England)
Women's Gerd Muller Trophy – Charlyn Corral (Pachuca/Mexico)

1h6vjht0mf6kj1pzmwkg69khzk.title: Bayern have a score to settle with Arsenal, says Gnabry
1h6vjht0mf6kj1pzmwkg69khzk.subtitle: Bayern Munich were beaten 3-1 by Arsenal in the Champions League last November, and they want to put that right in Wednesday's rematch.
paragraphs: Serge Gnabry admits Bayern Munich have a score to settle with Arsenal ahead of their Champions League clash on Wednesday, after losing at the Emirates Stadium last year.
Bayern and Arsenal will go head-to-head on matchday three of the 2026-27 league phase, with both sides having the chance to send an early statement against a potential rival for the trophy.
They also faced off at the same stage last season, with Jurrien Timber, Noni Madueke and Gabriel Martinelli scoring in a 3-1 home win for Arsenal, who went on to finish as runners-up.

In that match last November, Bayern had just eight shots, 14 touches in the opposition box and an expected goals (xG) total of 0.65, all three of which remain their worst figures in a Champions League match under Vincent Kompany.

But their historical record against Arsenal is positive. The Gunners have lost 53% of their meetings with Bayern in major European competitions (8/15), only posting a higher loss ratio against Barcelona (67%, 6/9) among teams they have faced at least five times.
And for Gnabry, who joined Arsenal as a 16-year-old in 2011 and was with the club for five years, revenge is definitely a motivating factor.
"We were the two best teams at the time; unfortunately, we conceded one goal too many towards the end," Gnabry told reporters, recalling last year's game in North London.
"In a game like this, when two top teams face each other, it always comes down to who is on top form on the day.
"It's all about us being in better form. We do still have a bit of a score to settle from last season."

Wednesday's game will also put Gnabry in the curious position of going up against a manager who he played alongside, with Arteta spending the final few years of his playing career at Arsenal when the Germany international was there.
And Gnabry says Arteta's leadership skills always stood out, noting: "He was a leader in the team back then, and our captain too.
"He spoke a lot with me and with Hector Bellerin as well, and he was always willing to listen – that shows what sort of person he is.
"He led the team to that great success last season, and he's doing a very good job.
"It's always a special match against a former club. I grew up there and I'm really looking forward to it.
"It's a bit strange to play against a coach you used to play alongside yourself! But we want to win – that’s what it's all about. I'm looking forward to the match."

1haews0ljchld1qld4jz6yz6d6.title: Roma 'paralysed with fear' in dramatic defeat to Madrid, laments Gasperini
1haews0ljchld1qld4jz6yz6d6.subtitle: Roma conceded from three corners in a seven-minute spell late on in their heartbreaking Champions League defeat to Real Madrid.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini admitted "there is huge regret" after Roma's dramatic defeat to Real Madrid in the Champions League.
Roma looked certain to win all three points at Stadio Olimpico after Donyell Malen's brace gave them a 3-1 lead, but Los Blancos pulled off a stunning turnaround.
Carlos Espi, Endrick and Antonio Rudiger all scored from corners in a seven-minute spell, with the final goal from the German defender coming in the 90th minute.

With Roma 3-1 ahead as late as the 82nd minute, excluding games that went to extra time, this was the latest that an away side had been behind by 2+ goals in a Champions League match and gone on to win.
This was also just the second time Roma have lost a European Cup/Champions League match in which they had led by 2+ goals – both of them have been against Madrid (4-2 in 2004).
Roma dropped deeper as the minutes ticked on, and Gasperini felt his players were "paralysed with fear" when defending Arda Guler's corners late in the game.

"They had taken corners in the first half too, but in the final minutes it was as if we were paralysed with fear on those corners, they scored too easily," Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia and Amazon Prime Video Italia.
"There is huge regret, because a game played like that should not have ended with that epilogue.
"We have to build on the positives, so even if this defeat weighs heavily, we need to shake it off quickly, otherwise we risk cancelling out all the good things we saw in this match.
"It is so hard to accept, but Roma certainly did some very good things, which we ruined at the end. Quite beyond Real Madrid's capabilities on set plays, we were far too passive, and that is a pity."
There certainly were positives as Malen scored two goals and Matias Soule recorded two assists.

Since Malen's debut for Roma on January 18th, only Harry Kane (37) and Raphinha (24) have scored more goals for a big-five European league side than the Dutchman (23 across all competitions), while Soule is just the second Roma player to assist 2+ goals in a Champions League match.
Nevertheless, Roma now have just one point from their opening two Champions League games this season.

1hc8dkvib3ad41xv2ng566hnav.title: Chelsea captain James could miss three months after knee surgery
1hc8dkvib3ad41xv2ng566hnav.subtitle: Reece James' Chelsea career has been plagued by injuries, and the England international is set for another spell on the sidelines.
paragraphs: Chelsea have confirmed captain Reece James has undergone successful minor knee surgery.
James missed Chelsea's last two games, a 3-0 defeat at Brentford and 5-1 win against Bournemouth, after suffering an injury in training.
The club confirmed the 26-year-old has already started his recovery, with reports suggesting he could be sidelined for three months.
James has made six appearances for the Blues this season, with Xabi Alonso's side sitting sixth in the Premier League ahead of Saturday's trip to Everton.
The right-back has struggled with injuries since breaking into the Chelsea first-team; he has suffered various hamstring injuries in each of the last four seasons.
In fact, the 2025-26 campaign (44) was the first time James played over 40 games for Chelsea in a single season since 2020-21 (47).
Alonso could start Pedro Neto in the right-wingback role as he did against Bournemouth, while summer signing Marco Palestra made his return from injury against the Cherries.
Though they are the third-highest goalscorers in the Premier League this season (15), no side has conceded more so far this term than Chelsea (13).
The Blues have conceded in each of their last 22 league games, only once having a longer run without a clean sheet (31 games between November 1960 and August 1961).

1hf1sdfq82mqb1wssmhgbuw72o.title: Sabitzer's 'stroke of genius' earned Dortmund's DFB-Pokal win, says Schlotterbeck
1hf1sdfq82mqb1wssmhgbuw72o.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund let a two-goal lead slip against Werder Bremen, but Marcel Sabitzer stepped up late on with a sensational free-kick.
paragraphs: Nico Schlotterbeck said only a "stroke of genius" from Marcel Sabitzer was the difference in Borussia Dortmund's narrow victory against Werder Bremen in the DFB-Pokal.
Dortmund booked their place in the third round of the competition with a 3-2 win at Signal Iduna Park on Tuesday, despite surrendering a two-goal lead in the second half.
Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka had put Niko Kovac's side in control after 17 minutes, with Maximilian Beier also seeing a goal ruled out for Dortmund.
But Werder substitute Niclas Fullkrug flipped the script in three second-half minutes, first scoring a 65th-minute penalty before levelling things up with a stunning run and finish.

1hhoqh1tt8no01t64v596jxdkx.title: Genoa 2-0 Juventus: Spalletti's men downed by De Rossi's fast starters
1hhoqh1tt8no01t64v596jxdkx.subtitle: Juventus were defeated 2-0 by Genoa on Wednesday, with Kingsley Ehizibue and Tommaso Baldanzi getting on the scoresheet.
paragraphs: Juventus dropped way off the pace set by Serie A's leading teams as they went down 2-0 to Genoa at Stadio Comunale Luigi Ferraris.
First-half goals from Kingsley Ehizibue and Tommaso Baldanzi proved enough for Daniele De Rossi's side, who condemned Juve to their third league defeat of the season.

Ehizibue put Genoa ahead after just 12 minutes, darting in unmarked to meet Baldanzi's cutback before drilling a powerful effort that flew into the top corner via a heavy deflection off a desperate Andrea Cambiaso.
Guglielmo Vicario had to be alert to deny the hosts a second eight minutes later, reaching his near post to smother a teasing delivery from Milutin Osmajic.

After Kerim Alajbegovic saw a low effort denied, Genoa nearly doubled their lead off the ensuing counter-attack. Justin Bijlow picked out Osmajic's run perfectly, but the striker could only fire into the side netting after some heavy pressure from Pierre Kalulu.
Matters worsened for the Bianconeri in the 28th minute as Baldanzi turned from provider to scorer to double Genoa's lead, capping off a ruthless counter with a simple tap-in.
An array of midfield turnovers continued to cost Juventus as Genoa again threatened on the break, with Morten Frendrup's low centre narrowly evading Osmajic's outstretched boot.

Kalulu then spurned the Bianconeri's best chance to halve the deficit on the stroke of half-time, failing to find the target from 12 yards out after being found in space by a smart Weston McKennie pass.
Genoa continued to push after the break, with Leo Ostigard heading narrowly over off a corner before Vitinha followed suit shortly after, sending a swerving effort over Vicario's head from range.
Juventus struggled to create in excess until the dying minutes, when Bremer could not make the most of one of their biggest openings, glancing a header over the bar.

Edon Zhegrova then unleashed a shot from the edge of the area that forced Bijlow into an awkward save before Teun Koopmeiners fired a stinging effort that deflected off Johan Vasquez and onto the underside of the bar as Genoa saw out a hard-fought win.
Genoa's fast start comes good
Genoa ended a six-match winless run against Juventus in Serie A, claiming their first victory over the Bianconeri since May 6, 2022.
The Rossoblu also recorded three consecutive home league wins for the first time since January-February 2025, when they did so under Patrick Vieira.

De Rossi's side have developed a habit of doing their damage early. Indeed, Genoa are one of just three Serie A teams, alongside Cagliari and Udinese, who have not scored a single second-half goal since the start of October.
Juventus may feel unfortunate to have left empty-handed, having generated 1.28 expected goals (xG) compared to Genoa's 0.97, but the hosts proved far more clinical in front of goal.

Both goalscorers made the most of relatively low-value opportunities, with Ehizibue scoring from an individual xG of just 0.08, albeit with the help of a deflection, while Baldanzi did so from 0.23 xG.
The defeat leaves Juve in eighth in Serie A, 11 points back from Inter and Lazio, who lead the way.

1hj9pel3lacaf11rtm4dinnkkt.title: Sabah 1-2 Borussia Dortmund: Guirassy double sees off Champions League minnows
1hj9pel3lacaf11rtm4dinnkkt.subtitle: Serhou Guirassy was on point as Borussia Dortmund navigated a tricky test against Sabah in Baku on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Borussia Dortmund claimed a 2-1 win over Champions League minnows Sabah thanks to Serhou Guirassy's double.
Aden McCarthy gave Sabah hope of causing a huge upset in Baku, but BVB got the job done.
Niko Kovac demanded a response after last week's defeat to Bodo/Glimt, and Dortmund started well at Baki Olimpiya Stadionu.
The visitors went ahead in the 10th minute, with Guirassy on hand to tap home from close range after Stas Pokatilov parried Felix Nmecha's strike.
Pokatilov made a fine double save to deny Joey Veerman and Carney Chukwuemeka, and Sabah made their goalkeeper's work count.
Joy-Lance Mickels saw a goal disallowed for the tightest of offsides, but McCarthy restored parity when he headed in from Tymoteusz Puchacz's free-kick.
Veljko Simic forced Gregor Kobel into action, with Kaheem Parris also drawing a save out of the Dortmund shot-stopper before half-time.
Yet Dortmund restored their lead eight minutes into the second half. Veerman delivered a teasing cross, and Guirassy was on the spot to turn it in.
McCarthy made a fantastic block to deny Guirassy a hat-trick strike, but Sabah did not have it in them to fight back for a second time.
In Tuesday's other early kick-off, Slavia Prague recovered from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 at Fenerbahce, with Pavel Kacor netting late on.
Guirassy closes in on Reus' record
Guirassy has now netted 21 goals in the Champions League for Dortmund.
He is the second player to net 20+ goals in the competition for BVB, after Marco Reus (24).

Guirassy has played 27 times in the Champions League for the club, meaning he has reached 20 goals in the second-fewest appearances for any German team, behind only Harry Kane for Bayern Munich (20 goals in 26 games).

In fact, Guirassy has scored 62% of all Champions League goals by Guinean players (23/37). Of nations with 5+ scorers, only Son Heung-min (66% of South Korea's goals, 19/29) and Robert Lewandowski (64% of Poland's goals, 109/171) have scored a higher share.
Dortmund have ended a run of four consecutive away Champions League defeats, with this their first away win in 364 days, since beating FC Copenhagen 4-2 in October 2025.

Sabah gave it their all, creating chances worth a respectable 1.46 expected goals, but BVB dominated in terms of opportunities, with their 22 shots (nine of which were on target) worth a combined 3.72 xG.

1hjc8dhnqf9xj1c459eh09hbde.title: Tottenham chief Venkatesham backs De Zerbi to turn things around
1hjc8dhnqf9xj1c459eh09hbde.subtitle: Manchester United and Tottenham are both in desperate need of wins in the Premier League, and they square off at Old Trafford this weekend.
paragraphs: Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham has backed Roberto De Zerbi to turn things round after a poor start to their Premier League campaign in 2026-27.
Spurs signed off for the extended international break with a 3-2 defeat at home to Aston Villa, a result that sees them bottom of the standings after five games of the season.
It is the club's worst start to a Premier League season after five games, with two points and a goal difference of -6, eclipsing their 2008-09 start (2 points, -3 goal difference).
De Zerbi has, however, navigated a busy summer off the pitch, with the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke all part of a major squad overhaul.
Spurs make the trip to Old Trafford to take on Manchester United on Saturday, with Michael Carrick also under pressure after an underwhelming start for the Red Devils.

De Zerbi won his only previous Premier League away game against United, beating them 3-1 in September 2023 with Brighton. Only Sam Allardyce, Ronald Koeman, Pep Guardiola and Andoni Iraola have won their first two away visits to Old Trafford in the competition.
But speaking at a Fan Advisory Board meeting at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Venkatesham retained his confidence that De Zerbi was the right man for the job.
"The club had made significant changes over the summer, both on and off the pitch, and we recognised that these might take time to take full effect," Venkatesham's minutes read.
"[Venkatesham] expressed confidence in Roberto De Zerbi, in the players brought in and in the changes made, noting the considerable work under way behind the scenes."
United, meanwhile, needed a last-gasp equaliser from Matheus Cunha to earn a 1-1 draw with Fulham last time out, a result that leaves them 12th in the Premier League.
The Red Devils are averaging just one point per game under Carrick in the Premier League this season – across his 17 league games last season, they averaged 2.3 points per game under the Englishman.

Despite picking up a late point at Craven Cottage, United have won just five points from five league games this season – their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign (also five in 2014-15).

Carrick will also be without several key players against Spurs, with the likes of Benjamin Sesko, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Karl Darlow all withdrawing from international duty with their respective nations through injury.

"I have always played for Slovenia and will always play with heart and pride. The most important thing now is to fully dedicate myself to recovery," Sesko posted on Instagram following his withdrawal.
"I am already working on getting back on the field as soon as possible and helping the national team and the club again."
Manchester United – Bryan Mbeumo
Mbeumo has enjoyed a strong start to the Premier League campaign, scoring two goals in five appearances, and he comes up against one of his favourite opponents next.
He has been involved in seven goals in his last six Premier League appearances against Spurs (six goals, one assist), netting home and away against them last season.
Tottenham – Mohammed Kudus
In what has been a dismal start to Spurs' league campaign, the timely return of Kudus has given their supporters something to cheer after their opening five matches.

Despite playing just 123 minutes in the Premier League so far this season, Kudus ranks fourth for take-on success rate (58.8% - 10/17 – min. 10 take-ons), while he is second for goal involvements per 90 for Spurs since the start of last term (0.43 – min. 900 mins).
MATCH PREDICTION: MANCHESTER UNITED WIN
United won this exact fixture 2-0 in February, ending a six-game winless run against Spurs in the Premier League (D3 L3).
However, the Red Devils are winless across their last three Premier League games (D2 L1). They last went four games without a win in the competition in May 2025 during an eight-game stretch (D2 L6).

And despite ranking first for shots (113) and fourth for expected goals (9.89) in the Premier League this term, United's xG per shot (0.088) is the fourth-worst ratio in the division, better only than Hull City, Nottingham Forest, and Spurs.
Spurs, meanwhile, have lost 25 Premier League away games against United. Only Everton (26 at Arsenal) have lost more on the road against an opponent in the competition.

They have also failed to win any of their last 37 Premier League games in which they have conceded the opening goal (D8 L29). Only between September 1996 and August 1998 have they endured a longer run in the competition’s history (38 games – D7 L31).

In addition, only in 1912-13 (first 12 games), 2008-09 (first eight), and 1955-56 (first six) have Spurs failed to win any of their opening six games of a league campaign, while among ever-present sides in the Premier League in 2026, they have accumulated the fewest points (18).
Manchester United – 54.1%
Tottenham – 22.3%
