1hl3p5ixlxojd1ew6k0ry9rlrj.title: Crystal Palace 3-1 Nottingham Forest: Superb comeback seals Sage's first home league win
1hl3p5ixlxojd1ew6k0ry9rlrj.subtitle: Crystal Palace came from behind to pick up their maiden Premier League victory over Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
paragraphs: Goals from Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma, and Yeremy Pino helped Crystal Palace to their first Premier League home win over Pierre Sage after beating Nottingham Forest 3-1.
They went behind early on to Dan Ndoye, but Palace weathered the pressure and eventually came out on top to earn their first-ever win over Forest in the competition.
Forest needed only three minutes to break the deadlock as Ndoye capitalised on a careless backpass from Anan Khalaili before driving a fine strike beyond Walter Benitez to stun Selhurst Park.
Palace nearly found an immediate response, though, as Jorgen Strand Larsen twice threatened to restore parity, only to be denied by a sharp Matz Sels save and a timely block from Murillo.
But Forest regained control and enjoyed a host of chances. Ndoye headed straight at Benitez before Daniel Munoz failed to get one over his old side, swiping a dipping effort inches wide.

The Tricky Trees should have doubled their lead when Morgan Gibbs-White's long-range clip crashed against the crossbar, with the rebound falling invitingly to Liam Delap, whose close-range volley was superbly kept out by Benitez.

Forest's wastefulness eventually came back to haunt them as Palace staged a remarkable first-half fightback, with Kamada capping off a fine team move to level the score with his first Premier League goal.

And there was still time for the Eagles to turn the contest completely on its head on the stroke of half-time, as Sels parried Tyrick Mitchell's wicked volley, and Lerma bundled the resulting corner through Sels' legs.

Forest emerged from the break seeking a response, but their wastefulness persisted as Xaver Schlager and Gibbs-White squandered promising openings. Palace remained dangerous, though, with Sels denying Lerma a second header with a timely save.

Palace made their next opportunity count and extended their lead just before the hour mark as Pino capitalised on slack defending, slotting home after Sels parried Strand Larsen's effort into the Spaniard’s path.
Sage's side continued to push for a fourth, but Strand Larsen failed to trouble Sels before Benitez once again denied Forest, parrying Chris Wood's header late on.
Forest made to pay as Palace celebrate
Forest will rue their wastefulness after squandering numerous chances to extend their lead, denying Oliver Glasner a happy return to Selhurst Park.
They registered 16 first-half shots – their joint-most before the break in a Premier League match since their latest promotion – reaching 10 attempts inside just 22 minutes.
Indeed, fans were treated to a highly entertaining first half as the two sides combined for 3.8 expected goals (xG) before the break – the highest first-half total in a Premier League match in 2026.
Forest's profligacy ultimately proved costly, though, ending their nine-match unbeaten away league run against Palace (W3 D6), dating back to December 2003.

Glasner's side scored just once despite generating 2.97 xG, while Palace netted three times, doing full justice to their 2.38 xG. The match also featured 12 big chances, with only Manchester United against Ipswich Town in August producing more this season (13).

For Sage, the victory marked his first home league win in charge and Palace's maiden Premier League triumph over Forest in 13 attempts (previously D8 L4). The Eagles have now beaten all 35 teams they have faced at least five times in the competition.
1hl3p5ixlxojd1ew6k0ry9rlrj.html:
Goals from Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma, and Yeremy Pino helped Crystal Palace to their first Premier League home win over Pierre Sage after beating Nottingham Forest 3-1.

They went behind early on to Dan Ndoye, but Palace weathered the pressure and eventually came out on top to earn their first-ever win over Forest in the competition. 

Forest needed only three minutes to break the deadlock as Ndoye capitalised on a careless backpass from Anan Khalaili before driving a fine strike beyond Walter Benitez to stun Selhurst Park. 

Palace nearly found an immediate response, though, as Jorgen Strand Larsen twice threatened to restore parity, only to be denied by a sharp Matz Sels save and a timely block from Murillo. 

But Forest regained control and enjoyed a host of chances. Ndoye headed straight at Benitez before Daniel Munoz failed to get one over his old side, swiping a dipping effort inches wide. 

The Tricky Trees should have doubled their lead when Morgan Gibbs-White's long-range clip crashed against the crossbar, with the rebound falling invitingly to Liam Delap, whose close-range volley was superbly kept out by Benitez. 

Forest's wastefulness eventually came back to haunt them as Palace staged a remarkable first-half fightback, with Kamada capping off a fine team move to level the score with his first Premier League goal. 

And there was still time for the Eagles to turn the contest completely on its head on the stroke of half-time, as Sels parried Tyrick Mitchell's wicked volley, and Lerma bundled the resulting corner through Sels' legs.

Forest emerged from the break seeking a response, but their wastefulness persisted as Xaver Schlager and Gibbs-White squandered promising openings. Palace remained dangerous, though, with Sels denying Lerma a second header with a timely save. 

Palace made their next opportunity count and extended their lead just before the hour mark as Pino capitalised on slack defending, slotting home after Sels parried Strand Larsen's effort into the Spaniard’s path. 

Sage's side continued to push for a fourth, but Strand Larsen failed to trouble Sels before Benitez once again denied Forest, parrying Chris Wood's header late on. 

Forest made to pay as Palace celebrate 

Forest will rue their wastefulness after squandering numerous chances to extend their lead, denying Oliver Glasner a happy return to Selhurst Park. 

They registered 16 first-half shots – their joint-most before the break in a Premier League match since their latest promotion – reaching 10 attempts inside just 22 minutes. 

Indeed, fans were treated to a highly entertaining first half as the two sides combined for 3.8 expected goals (xG) before the break – the highest first-half total in a Premier League match in 2026. 

Forest's profligacy ultimately proved costly, though, ending their nine-match unbeaten away league run against Palace (W3 D6), dating back to December 2003. 

Glasner's side scored just once despite generating 2.97 xG, while Palace netted three times, doing full justice to their 2.38 xG. The match also featured 12 big chances, with only Manchester United against Ipswich Town in August producing more this season (13). 

For Sage, the victory marked his first home league win in charge and Palace's maiden Premier League triumph over Forest in 13 attempts (previously D8 L4). The Eagles have now beaten all 35 teams they have faced at least five times in the competition.

1hlutev1pz0em18epuso8urhza.title: Sarri thrilled with Atalanta progress ahead of Milan clash
1hlutev1pz0em18epuso8urhza.subtitle: Atalanta are looking to earn a third straight win this week when they travel to AC Milan, who are unbeaten in Serie A this season.
paragraphs: Maurizio Sarri is impressed with the progress he has seen from Atalanta in recent games, and he hopes to carry that on against AC Milan in Serie A.
After a run of three straight losses in the Italian top flight, Atalanta halted their slump with a 3-1 win over Venezia last weekend, though they remain in mid-table.
They then followed that up with a 3-1 win over Pafos in the Conference League in midweek – a victory built on Eljif Elmas’ first-minute goal.
Atalanta are now chasing back-to-back league wins for the second time this season, following their first two matches of the campaign, and Sarri is confident in their ability.

"We started well [against Pafos], and unlike the game with Venezia where we had lots of chances and got disorganised, we made better choices on when to be direct, when to keep possession, and allowed practically nothing until that late goal," Sarri told Sky Sport Italia.
"We have found a way to be more dangerous in attack; now we need to seek greater balance and solidity too.
"The club is a model for anyone; I had never encountered a situation like this.
"Naturally, it came from many years with a completely different style of football, but the players are working hard. I hope they have a significant margin for improvement.
"I honestly don't know what we can achieve in the first year, but we have set a target for the medium-to-long term."
They face a Milan side who remain unbeaten in Serie A so far in 2026-27, winning three and drawing three of their matches to earn 12 points.

The Rossoneri were pegged back in a 1-1 draw with Sassuolo last time out in the league, but like Atalanta, they come into this match on the back of a European win after beating Salzburg 4-0 last time out.

Ruben Amorim will be aiming to get back to winning ways in Serie A, but if he avoids defeat, he will become only the third Milan manager in the league’s history to remain unbeaten in each of his first seven games in charge, and the first since Luis Carniglia (W4 D3) in 1963.
AC Milan – Adrien Rabiot

After an assist against Lazio and goals against Lecce and Sassuolo, Rabiot could be involved in at least one goal in four consecutive matches for the first time in his career across Europe's big five leagues.
The last midfielder to achieve this for Milan in Serie A was Hakan Calhanoglu in December 2020 (one assist per game against Parma, Genoa and Sassuolo, one goal and two assists against Lazio).
Atalanta – Nikola Krstovic

Nikola Krstovic was involved in all three of Atalanta's goals in their last league match against Venezia, scoring two goals and providing one assist; this is the same number of goal involvements he had in his previous 11 appearances in the competition.
The 26-year-old has only been involved in more than one goal in two consecutive Serie A matches once before: in September 2025 against Lecce (two assists) and Torino (two goals).
MATCH PREDICTION: AC MILAN WIN

AC Milan are winless in their last six Serie A matches against Atalanta (D2 L4); only once in their history have the Rossoneri endured a longer winless run against them in the top flight (seven games between November 2015 and September 2018 – D5 L2).

And Atalanta have won their last two away games against Milan in Serie A; only once have they recorded three consecutive away wins against the Rossoneri in the competition, between March 1941 and March 1943.

However, Milan are the favourites to win as they are unbeaten in their first six league matches this season (W3 D3); the last time they avoided defeat in each of their first seven league games was in the 2021-22 campaign (W6 D1).
Milan could also win three consecutive home matches in Serie A for the first time in 2026.

As for Atalanta, they have lost their last two away games in Serie A (1-2 against Roma, 0-2 against Juventus) and could lose three consecutive away matches in the competition under the same manager for the first time since October and November 2017, with Gian Piero Gasperini.

1hnz40ler5mb114h0wtlanlxld.title: Olise 'a pure talent' but Zidane lauds team effort from France
1hnz40ler5mb114h0wtlanlxld.subtitle: While reserving praise for France match-winner Michael Olise, Zinedine Zidane was pleased to see everyone contribute against Belgium.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane hailed the "pure talent" of Michael Olise after France's win over Belgium on Monday, but he was also glad to see other players contribute after making sweeping changes.
Zidane made nine alterations to the team that beat Turkiye 1-0 in his first game in charge last Friday, as Les Bleus made the short trip across the border to face Belgium in the Nations League.
Captain Kylian Mbappe was absent due to a minor left knee injury, but fellow star Olise came off the bench to provide the decisive moment in the 88th minute.

The Bayern Munich man travelled from inside his own half before slotting a neat finish into the bottom-left corner from the edge of the area, taking him to 13 goal involvements in his last 14 appearances for France (four goals, nine assists).
Zidane said of Olise afterwards, as quoted by L'Equipe: "He's a pure talent – I like this type of player. He wants to please people when he plays, but not only that.
"He feels football, he knows when to go and when to slow things down. I'm happy to be by his side, to see him play like this."
But Zidane was also impressed by many of those players that came into his lineup.

Paris Saint-Germain's Maghnes Akliouche created three chances and played a game-high 35 passes into the final third, while his club-made Desire Doue created four chances, attempted five shots and completed five dribbles.

It was just the fifth instance of a France player creating four or more chances, attempting five or more shots and completing at least five dribbles in a single game on record, after Nicolas Anelka (vs Faroe Islands in 2009), Franck Ribery (vs Belarus in 2012), and Mbappe twice (vs South Africa in 2022 and Azerbaijan in 2025).
Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was another impressive performer at the back, completing 91.8% of his passes (67/73) and winning six of his nine duels.
"I'm very satisfied with what the team did, and not only with the ball. Like the match in Turkiye, but on a much better pitch, we were very good everywhere," Zidane added.
"We put things in place against a good Belgium team who also made us suffer, but we held on, we were brave, we weren't afraid to go into the opponents' half.
"That's what I like, that's what we want. We may have dropped a little bit in the second half, when we had some small difficulties, but that's logical.
"We made nine changes, but what I like about this team is that everyone feels involved."
France are back in action on Friday, with Italy visiting the Stade de France, before they round out the international break with another home game against Turkiye next week.

1hsmy01ozeeam1bvkl88xk2s2q.title: Man City must 'make our own noise' by winning games, says Maresca
1hsmy01ozeeam1bvkl88xk2s2q.subtitle: Manchester City beat Liverpool comfortably at Anfield on Sunday, and Enzo Maresca wants his team to continue silencing away grounds.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca insisted his Manchester City players brought their own noise to Anfield as they thrashed 10-man Liverpool to maintain their perfect start in the Premier League.
City were playing in their first game since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations, and they delivered a statement performance on Sunday.
The Citizens managed to quieten a vociferous home crowd during the first half, and the game turned in the 62nd minute when Ryan Gravenberch received a second yellow card.
Gravenberch was penalised for a careless foul on Jeremy Doku, having already been booked earlier in the second half for a questionable tackle on Elliot Anderson in midfield.
But City made their dominance immediately count when Erling Haaland fired home in the 65th minute before Doku curled a sensational effort beyond Alisson Becker's grasp.
Rayan Cherki rounded off a fine individual move that saw 41 passes and every City player touch the ball in the 78th minute, making it six wins from six games for City.
A team have started with six straight wins in just two of the last seven Premier League seasons (since 2020-21), with City being both of those sides in 2023-24 and 2026-27.
Maresca was thrilled to overcome a difficult trip to Merseyside, but he challenged his players to continue silencing opposition crowds by maintaining their winning momentum.
"Very difficult circumstances, difficult environment. We struggled in the first half, we were on the ball but not so much off the ball," Maresca told Sky Sports.
"In the second half, we made some adjustments and we were much better. In the build-up, we were not doing the right things. The second half we were better.
"We need to learn how to deal with the noise because the noise will be with us at all of our away games – there will be noise. We need to deal with that and make our own noise.
"Our noise is to win games. The feeling at the end of the game with our fans and our noise, that's a nice feeling and a different noise."

Haaland's opener was a clinical finish after Doku's cross deflected off Alexis Mac Allister and into his path, with the Norwegian netting his eighth goal in his eighth appearance against Liverpool across all competitions.

Doku, meanwhile, scored his 12th Premier League goal, but only his second as a substitute (also October 2024 vs Fulham) – he is the third sub to score at Anfield for City in the competition after George Weah in September 2000 and Bernardo Silva in January 2018.

And despite only coming on in the 56th minute, he also recorded the most dribbles (five) and was directly involved in the joint-second most shots (two shots, two chances created) of any visiting player for Maresca's side.
The quality of City's goals pleased Maresca, while he also hailed Doku for the impact he had after replacing Iliman Ndiaye with the game still awaiting its first goal.
"Outstanding – Jeremy [Doku] was very good we need to take care of him. He is important but only just back from injury. Performance from everyone was brilliant," he added.
"With one more player, it was easier to keep the ball, but I am very happy with three points.
"I can not control things outside football, so why stress? I stress about the gameplan, day by day training sessions, but the rest is not in my hands."

1i1sr8r1omutk154g1rmdpvz1g.title: Saka: Scars still remain from England's World Cup defeat to Argentina
1i1sr8r1omutk154g1rmdpvz1g.subtitle: England are preparing to begin their Nations League campaign, but Bukayo Saka said their World Cup exit was still fresh in the memory.
paragraphs: Bukayo Saka believes England's players are still scarred from their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals of this summer's World Cup.
England were on the brink of reaching the World Cup final for the first time since winning the tournament in 1966, after Anthony Gordon's 55th-minute strike gave them the lead.
However, a Lionel Messi-orchestrated comeback saw Argentina score two goals in seven minutes late on to end the Three Lions' dreams of lifting the trophy.
Argentina were trailing until the 85th minute against England, the latest a team has been behind but gone on to win in normal time in a World Cup semi-final.
The Three Lions did, however, achieve their second-best finish at the World Cup after beating France in a thrilling third-place match, with Saka scoring a hat-trick in a 6-4 win.
But Saka, who was an unused substitute in England's defeat to Argentina, said there were still feelings of regret within the squad about their shortcomings at the World Cup.
"Obviously, there is still a scar on us when you believed and everyone was so united and so confident we could do it," Saka said.
"Not just us, but the whole country felt it. You try to move on as soon as possible, but you know, a scar is a scar, it decides to heal when it heals itself."
Argentina would go on to lose the final to Spain at MetLife Stadium, and Luis de la Fuente's side are up next for England in the first match of their Nations League campaign.

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
Spain have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of Euro 2024.

Thomas Tuchel's side welcome Spain to Wembley Stadium in the first of four matches during the extended international break, with further matches against Croatia and Czechia (both home and away) to come.
It will be the first time England have stepped out onto the pitch since their third-place finish, and Saka insists their full focus is on making a good start in the Nations League.
"We are trying to draw a line under [the World Cup] now and focus on the new international season that we have coming up," Saka added.
"We have got four massive, difficult group games to try and qualify us for the Nations League [knockouts] that we are really focused on."

1ipyu2d1qzq1m1o208cjvigsew.subtitle: Ibrahima Konate has suffered a minor injury which has ruled him out of France's first four Nations League matches/
paragraphs: Ibrahima Konate has withdrawn from France's Nations League squad through injury, with Leny Yoro receiving his first call-up to the senior squad.
Konate felt pain in his right knee during Wednesday's training session and underwent an MRI.
He has been diagnosed with a minor sprain and released back to Real Madrid, for whom he has made seven appearances in all competitions since moving from Liverpool.
Following his withdrawal, Zidane has called on Manchester United's Yoro, who had initially been called up to the Under-21s squad.
Yoro is the seventh uncapped player in Zidane's France squad and will link up with the team to fly to Turkiye on Thursday.
The 20-year-old has had a mixed start to the season with United, making just two starts in all competitions – neither of which came in the Premier League.
He started their Champions League thrashing of Sabah and the EFL Cup loss to Brighton, but has played just 22 minutes in the top-flight, with both of his appearances coming from the bench.
Yoro could make his France debut against Turkiye on Friday, with Les Bleus also set to take on Belgium twice, on either side of their clash with Italy.

1iryy0270qvkj1q3yn5h5ximio.title: Damet relishing MLS playoffs with St. Louis
1iryy0270qvkj1q3yn5h5ximio.subtitle: St. Louis City SC have already qualified for the playoffs, but could still boost their seeding as they prepare to host San Diego FC.
paragraphs: Yoann Damet is embracing the end of the regular season as St. Louis City SC begin to turn their attention to the playoffs in MLS.
St. Louis are third in the Western Conference following their impressive form, which started just before the World Cup break.
They host San Diego FC in their final home match of the campaign on Saturday, while they travel to the Houston Dynamo on Decision Day.
St. Louis could still finish second in the West, currently three points behind FC Dallas, and Damet is enjoying the run-in.
"It's a crazy feeling, to be honest," said Damet. "It's gone by just like that.

"It's a good time of the year. It's a time I've always enjoyed. I think if you take it the right way, and you understand that this group and what we've done and what we've built since January is coming to an end – the end of a chapter and the beginning of a new one.
"And if you embrace it and if you embrace sharing those moments with the people around you, I think it can be quite special.
"I think it's a little bit the feeling we have wanted to create, to be in the position we're in. We're approaching the end of the regular season and starting to think and focus on the playoffs."
San Diego are out of playoff contention after losing 4-1 to the Vancouver Whitecaps last time out.
They last won in MLS at the end of August, defeating the LA Galaxy 3-1.
St. Louis City SC – Daniel Edelman
Daniel Edelman scored for St. Louis in Wednesday's 3-2 loss to the Portland Timbers, giving him five regular-season goals in his first season with the club.
Edelman scored a total of three goals across his 96 career regular-season matches prior to 2026 (all with the New York Red Bulls).
San Diego FC – Jeppe Tverskov

With 65 completed passes against Vancouver, San Diego's Jeppe Tverskov became the first player since Opta began detailed data collection of MLS in 2010 to complete 3,000 passes in a single season (3,046).
MATCH PREDICTION: ST. LOUIS CITY SC WIN

San Diego are winless in 10 consecutive matches (D5 L5) following their defeat to Vancouver. After opening the season with three straight wins, they have managed just five wins in their last 29 regular-season matches (D11 L13).

However, St. Louis have lost three straight MLS matches, allowing three goals in each defeat. It is the second time they have allowed three or more goals in three straight regular-season games (also August 2025).
San Diego are unbeaten in three all-time meetings with St. Louis (W2 D1), including winning each of the last two meetings.
St. Louis's only point against San Diego came in the first all-time meeting, a scoreless draw in San Diego.
St. Louis City SC – 51.4%

1iyf7aju7687szj7i373ue45u.title: Joao Felix confident goals will come under new Portugal boss Jesus
1iyf7aju7687szj7i373ue45u.subtitle: Jorge Jesus began his Portugal tenure with a win over Wales in the Nations League, and Joao Felix is excited about what the future holds.
paragraphs: Joao Felix believes it is only a matter of time before Portugal find their shooting boots under new boss Jorge Jesus after they beat Wales 1-0 in the Nations League on Thursday.
Jesus was taking charge of Portugal for the first time following Roberto Martinez's departure, and his team made a blistering start to the match at Estadio Jose Alvalade.
Portugal eventually took the lead in the 22nd minute through Joao Felix, who picked out the bottom-left corner from outside the box after good work from full-back Nuno Mendes.
Cristiano Ronaldo spurned two chances at the end of a dominant first half that saw Portugal register 13 shots, their most in the opening 45 minutes of a game since November 2025 against Armenia (17).

Ronaldo should have doubled Portugal's lead early in the second half, but he could only turn Ruben Neves' delivery over the crossbar, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner then seeing a goal ruled out for offside soon after.

But the Selecao were made to work for their win, with Wales coming on strong as the match progressed. Brennan Johnson lifted an effort onto the crossbar, with Ruben Dias on hand to clear Lewis Koumas' rebound off the line.

Portugal are now unbeaten in their last 10 home matches in all competitions (W9 D1), while in competitive games it’s 13 unbeaten since a 1-0 defeat to Spain in September 2022 (W12 D1), and Joao Felix is confident things will only get better under Jesus.
"We knew it wasn't going to be an easy game. Wales are a good team," Joao Felix told Sport TV. "The first game under a new coach is always difficult.
"We had very little time to work on the coach's game patterns, but I think that, overall, we played a great game and we deserve to be commended.
"I think we could see our dynamic, very attacking football, high pressing, without giving the opponent any space to breathe.
"We had 13 shots before half-time, which is a lot for the first half. I don't remember a single clear chance for them, when we had several.
"That's what people can expect. Attacking football, pressing, not letting opponents breathe and creating chances.
"We only scored one today, but in the next few games, if we continue like this, we will surely score more."

Joao Felix has now scored five goals across his last 10 starts for Portugal, while each of his last two goals have come from outside the box, as many as his first 11 for the national team, and he looks set to play a big role under Jesus.
The 26-year-old has worked with Jesus before at Al-Nassr, scoring 20 goals in 33 appearances on their way to the Saudi Pro League title in 2025-26.
Jesus made the decision to deploy Joao Felix in the second striker position, just behind Ronaldo and with Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Pedro Neto around him.
"I've always been myself; I always tried to do my best for the team, no matter what position I was playing," Joao Felix added.
"As I've always said, my position is right here, as a second striker. If this is the case, there is a much higher chance that things will go well.
"This is what happened last year. Today, the whole team delivered a good performance, and that's where I can help them the most."
It proved to be a frustrating match for Ronaldo, whose seven shots without scoring is his most in a game since a World Cup qualifier against Republic of Ireland in October 2025 (also seven).
Ronaldo was replaced by Goncalo Ramos in the 67th minute, and Jesus said the decision to substitute the Portugal captain was pre-planned.

"I took him out 25 minutes before the end of the game because I thought it was important to have a fresh player on the pitch who was able to defend with pressure and not let the central defenders of Wales build the game," Jesus said.
"I wanted to have a player at the first line with speed, and I knew that Goncalo Ramos could do that.
"I knew that Cris could stay a little longer, five to 10 minutes. But I would have taken him out anyway. I planned it."

1j4e7qmvax9xm1mxtwuohnveam.title: LAFC interim boss Tamarit lauds Bouanga's impact in new role
1j4e7qmvax9xm1mxtwuohnveam.subtitle: Los Angeles FC have ended their winless run in MLS ahead of their trip to an out-of-form New York City FC side.
paragraphs: Los Angeles FC interim boss Xavier Tamarit has praised Denis Bouanga's impact in his new role for the side.
Bouanga scored twice against Austin FC in a 3-1 win for LAFC on Wednesday, with Son Heung-min netting the other goal.
The 31-year-old also scored for LAFC in their 1-1 draw with the Vancouver Whitecaps in Tamarit's first game in charge, thriving in his new role as their lone striker.
Bouanga has now scored 17 goals in MLS this season, and he has recorded 17 regular-season multi-goal games in his MLS career, the fourth-most among active players in the competition.
Ahead of their trip to New York City FC on Saturday, Tamarit lauded Bouanga's impact in his new role.
"I say if you feel you have to do it, you can do it," said Tamarit.
"I'm very happy with Denis. I think he's helping the team a lot. He's putting all his help and effort.
"He's going out from his natural position and he's, I think, giving us something that we didn't have before.
"But I said to the players congratulations, because they are doing a big effort to work in the new way and trying what we are asking."
Bouanga added: "It's so good for the confidence. For me. For Sonny. For all the team.
"We need goals. We need passing. We have to be decisive, too. We need points."
NYCFC, meanwhile, remain outside the play-off places in the Eastern Conference after a 2-0 defeat to Inter Miami during the week.
This will be their first home match since September 18, when they lost to rivals New York Red Bulls, after a three-game road trip.
New York City FC – Nicolas Mercau

Nicolas Mercau hit five of his six shot attempts on Wednesday on target, taking his total to 42 shots on target for the season, tied for fourth most in MLS behind only Lionel Messi (67), Bouanga (44) and Brian White (43).
Los Angeles FC – Son Heung-min
Son had a goal and two assists against Austin on Wednesday, taking his totals to 18 goals and 16 assists in MLS.
He is one of three players, along with Messi and Anders Dreyer, with at least 16 goals and 16 assists since he made his MLS debut in September 2025.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
After the first two meetings between NYCFC and LAFC ended in draws, each team recorded one win in the last two meetings, both in Los Angeles.
LAFC have managed just one win in their 12 away matches in all competitions since the beginning of May (D5 L6), including going winless in seven straight (D4 L3).
LAFC's only road win in that time came at LA Galaxy as the Black and Gold last won outside of southern California on April 25 at Minnesota.
However, NYCFC have won only one of their last 13 matches in all competitions dating back to early August (D4 L8), including losing three of the last four (D1).
New York City FC – 36.9%
Los Angeles FC – 36.8%

1j6jd7x6pch8m152v3ixmnd3hg.title: Schmetzer urges Seattle to build on 'statement win'
1j6jd7x6pch8m152v3ixmnd3hg.subtitle: The Seattle Sounders' excellent run of form continued at the weekend, but a stern test against FC Dallas comes next for Brian Schmetzer.
paragraphs: The Seattle Sounders delivered a "statement win" against the New England Revolution, but now they must build on that until the end of the season, so says Brian Schmetzer.
Schmetzer's Sounders recorded their fourth straight victory at Gillette Stadium last weekend, with two late goals clinching a 3-0 win against New England.
It has been a remarkable upturn in form for Seattle, who endured an 11-game winless run in MLS following the return to action after this summer's World Cup.
They have now boosted their chances of reaching the postseason, with the Sounders sitting seventh in the Western Conference and eight points clear of 10th-place Portland Timbers.
But Seattle's playoff credentials will be once again put to the test with a trip to high-flying FC Dallas up next as the end of the campaign draws ever closer.
Schmetzer said his team outplayed New England last time out, but he wants his team to continue their winning momentum to further aid their potential postseason preparations.
"This was a statement win," Schmetzer said. "New England is a really good team. They were second in the East.
"We went into their building. It wasn't just a smash-and-grab. We outplayed them. In past years, the team has come together at the end of the year, and we've made a strong run.
"Some of that experience helps me through the challenging period that we had when we were losing games.

"That group has a lot of experienced players that understand that sometimes you go through those moments where you're not doing so well, but what really matters is when it comes to the playoffs, you have to be playing at a very high level."
Dallas, meanwhile, come into this match off the back of a 3-2 defeat away to Charlotte FC, their first league defeat in six league matches (W4 D2).
Logan Farrington and Petar Musa had put Dallas in control by the 64th minute, but two goals in four minutes from Idan Toklomati and Harry Toffolo turned the game on its head.
Charlotte made their momentum count in the second minute of second-half stoppage time, with Toklomati tucking in Pep Biel's cross from close range to complete the comeback.
The result keeps Dallas in third in the West, but they are now only one point ahead of the San Jose Earthquakes, with the Houston Dynamo also within striking distance.
Musa scored his 53rd regular-season MLS goal in Dallas' defeat to Charlotte FC on Saturday as the race for the Golden Boot heats up.
Only Josef Martinez (77), David Villa (63), Raul Diaz Arce (56), Sebastian Giovinco (55) and Roy Lassiter (55) have scored more goals in their first three MLS seasons.
Seattle Sounders – Paul Arriola
Arriola has been involved in five goals in his last four appearances (two goals, three assists), including scoring and assisting once against New England at the weekend.
He had contributed to just four goals (two goals, two assists) in his previous 24 regular-season games dating back to September 2024.
MATCH PREDICTION: DALLAS WIN
Dallas have lost only two of their last 18 regular-season home matches dating back to August 2025 (W10 D6), including going unbeaten in four straight (W3 D1).
They have also not conceded a goal in their last two home matches, though they have not kept three straight home clean sheets in league play since between May and July 2015.

But despite being the underdogs according to the Opta supercomputer, Seattle have won four straight matches against Dallas, including a 2-1 home win on April 25, the longest winning streak by either team in the 49 all-time meetings between the sides in all competitions.
The Sounders are also unbeaten in nine straight regular-season matches (W4 D5), including winning four straight, after an eight-match losing streak.
They last went 10 or more games unbeaten in a single season in 2021, when they started with 13 straight games without a loss.
Seattle Sounders – 27%

1j830tjitz6px14nbj03ycncb9.title: Neville hits out at Man Utd players as pressure mounts on Carrick
1j830tjitz6px14nbj03ycncb9.subtitle: The pressure is growing on Michael Carrick after Manchester United's dismal form continued with a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth.
paragraphs: Gary Neville feels Manchester United's squad are letting Michael Carrick down as the pressure grows on his former team-mate.
United's season hit a new low on Sunday, as the Red Devils went down 3-0 at home to Bournemouth.
They have won just seven points from eight Premier League games this season (W1 D4 L3), their lowest at this stage of a league season since 1986-87 (four).
That followed on from Wednesday's 4-1 Champions League defeat to Cesc Fabregas' Como.
The United fans sang Carrick's name as he made his way from the pitch at full-time, but the supporters jeered the players.
And Neville feels United's squad deserve the criticism.

"Nothing against Tottenham here, nothing against Como, nothing against Atletico Madrid. A little bit against Leeds [United], it was a bit of a fight, but nothing against Fulham. That was a waste of time," Neville said on the Gary Neville Podcast.
"So, this is a pattern of nothings, of players switching off and downing tools.
"Michael Carrick is a brilliant man.
"He's a man of integrity, of credibility, of decency, of professionalism, of high-quality football and consistency and reliability. Everything the group of players in that dressing room aren't.
"And he's going to suffer for it because he's not been able to deliver. It's been too much for him in these last few months.
"He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him."
Bruno Fernandes sat on the bench against Bournemouth, having been dropped following his comments in the wake of the defeat at Como.
7 - Since the 2023-24 season, no Premier League side has lost more home games by a margin of three or more goals in all competitions than Man Utd (7).
Neville added: "If Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.
"If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.
"A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

"There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be and as professionals should.
"Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players."
United are eight games without a win in all competitions (D3 L5) for the first time since November/December 2015.
They have lost consecutive games twice in this run, having not suffered back-to-back defeats at all in the 2025-26 season.
Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann have been mooted as potential candidates to replace Carrick.

1jdlty23ofll61aneb4fxs4e83.title: Schmetzer senses positive momentum after end to Seattle's winless run
1jdlty23ofll61aneb4fxs4e83.subtitle: The Seattle Sounders finally ended their 13-game winless run in MLS this week, and they have a home match against Minnesota United next up.
paragraphs: Brian Schmetzer already believed the Seattle Sounders were building some momentum even before they ended their four-month wait for a victory on Wednesday, as they look to go back-to-back against Minnesota United.
The Sounders went 13 games without victory after beating the San Jose Earthquakes on May 13, prior to the World Cup break.

They lost eight straight matches before turning the corner somewhat by drawing five in a row, prior to overcoming Real Salt Lake – who are also on a long winless streak of their own – by a 2-0 scoreline in midweek.
Now only outside the playoff spots on games won in the Western Conference, Seattle will look to inject some more impetus at home to Minnesota on Saturday.
But Schmetzer believes they were already on an upward trajectory of sorts, saying: "Well, I think we've already been starting to build – the five draws have been something.
"It's been a long time – May 13, for the guys that are publishing the facts. I think all the people in this room are good reporters. There's no fake news in here!
"I told those guys in there to enjoy the moment. And on a personal note, there were fans behind the bench saying, 'Congratulations Brian, enjoy this moment'.

"So I listened to those fans, and I told the same thing to the guys in there. I think we've been building some momentum, but this really gives them a lot of belief and that’s what we discussed before the game."
Minnesota are second from bottom in the West, albeit only three points behind the Sounders, after losing four straight games.

Their most recent defeat came by a 3-2 scoreline against the LA Galaxy last weekend, and if the Loons are to make a late push for the postseason, head coach Cameron Knowles knows it will take a collective effort.
"We're going to need everyone. We need everyone to push, whether it's in training during the week or whether it's coming into a game," he said.
"We need guys to step up and everyone to give exactly what they're capable of. Everyone in that locker room has shown they're capable of contributing."
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Seattle Sounders – Paul Arriola
Arriola assisted both Seattle goals against RSL on Wednesday, while he also had a joint-game-high three shots and the only Opta-defined 'big' chance of the match.
He also scored his first MLS goal for the Sounders earlier this month, to salvage a point against the Galaxy in a 1-1 draw on September 12.
Minnesota United – Kelvin Yeboah
Only Lionel Messi (20), Petar Musa (18), Brian White and Sam Surridge (16 each) have scored more goals in MLS this year than Yeboah's 14.
The Minnesota forward – who was on target against the Galaxy last weekend – also ranks third in the league for expected goals (14.6 xG), only behind Messi (17.2) and White (16.1).
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
When these two sides last met in MLS action, they played out a 0-0 draw at Allianz Field in March.
All of a sudden, Seattle's club-record winless streak has turned into a six-game unbeaten run, even if they did play out five draws in that time.
And they are the Opta supercomputer's favourites for this one, with Minnesota only managing one win in their last six MLS games (D1 L4).

Away from home, the Loons have lost their last two matches while conceding a total of nine goals (5-4 at Portland Timbers, 4-2 at St. Louis City SC), so without a big defensive improvement, they could be up against it.

1jg3gmmr4mhqn10zc3m0m08oxc.title: Danks reveals congratulatory message from Kompany after Bayern beat Freiburg
1jg3gmmr4mhqn10zc3m0m08oxc.subtitle: Vincent Kompany was not in the Bayern Munich dugout after his health scare, but he did offer his thoughts on their win at Freiburg.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich's assistant coach Aaron Danks revealed he received a congratulatory message from the absent Vincent Kompany after Sunday's 3-1 victory over Freiburg.
Dayot Upamecano, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were on target as the reigning Bundesliga champions went back above Borussia Dortmund on goal difference, returning to the top of the table.
Bayern's win came without Kompany on the touchline after he collapsed at the club's training ground on Friday, with the club subsequently confirming he was stable and undergoing tests in hospital.
Sporting director Max Eberl said Kompany could miss several weeks, but the former Manchester City centre-back watched Sunday's win and passed on a post-match message to Danks.
"I just opened my phone to a WhatsApp from Vince straight away, saying 'well done', and he was happy," Danks told reporters afterwards.
"I just replied saying, 'Brilliant, now rest', and sent him a kissing emoji. So hopefully, he rests up."
Bayern only had one shot more than their opponents, tallying 17 to Freiburg's 16, yet their opportunities were of a higher quality as they dominated the expected goals (xG) battle by 2.99 to 0.9.
"We're really pleased with the performance," he said. "We always knew it was going to be such a difficult place to come. They're a top team; they're in really good form.
"And even for the last 10 minutes there, where they have that momentum and the crowd is up, and they're trying to chase an equaliser, it's good for us.
"We had to show a bit of resilience, a bit of character, and I thought we defended those moments quite well."
Kompany was not the only Bayern absentee at Europa-Park Stadion, with first-choice goalkeeper Manuel Neuer ruled out with a foot injury.

Although Danks is uncertain whether Neuer will return in time to face Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal on Wednesday – or Dortmund in the upcoming Klassiker – he does not expect the 40-year-old to be out for the long term.
"I'm not too sure. He had a small aggravation in his foot. It depends on how much time that takes to settle," he said.
"It could be a little bit uncomfortable for him at the moment, but I don't think it will take too long."

1jgme7xwo0l71vbfphceoiqfo.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal: Rice salvages late draw to deny Kane winner
1jgme7xwo0l71vbfphceoiqfo.subtitle: Harry Kane got a goal and an assist to turn the scoreline in Bayern Munich's favour, but Declan Rice stepped up late to deny them a win.
paragraphs: Declan Rice struck late to snatch a point for Arsenal, who came from behind to earn a thrilling 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich at Allianz Arena.
It looked like the game would belong to Harry Kane, who orchestrated the comeback after Eberechi Eze – an early replacement for the injured Bukayo Saka – opened the scoring.
Kane set up Alphonso Davies' equaliser before netting from the penalty spot, but Rice finished off a pacy move down Arsenal's right to take a share of the spoils.
Serge Gnabry had the first clear opening, with Kane launching a goal-kick over the top to Davies, who squared it into the middle. Ismael Saibari helped it onto Gnabry, who tamely shot at David Raya.
But it was Arsenal who broke the deadlock 25 minutes in, as Eze latched onto Martin Odegaard's wonderful pass to slot under Manuel Neuer into the bottom-right corner.
Their lead lasted just 10 minutes, though, with Kane once again showing his range with a lovely throughball for Davies to chase, and he coolly curled past Raya while one-on-one.

It was a frenetic start to the second half, with Neuer making a point-blank save on his line to tip Bruno Guimaraes' header onto the crossbar, before Raya pushed away Dayot Upamecano's effort at the other end following a blistering counter-attack.
Eze almost got a second goal when he skipped through the left of the box before trying his luck from near the byline, but Neuer was once again equal to it.

Kane was then at the heart of Bayern's second goal in the 61st minute. His shot was blocked by Jurrien Timber's arm, and the former Tottenham man stepped up from 12 yards to emphatically finish past Raya.

Kai Havertz saw a poked effort blocked on the line before Luis Diaz's curler was well-saved by Raya, and that set Arsenal up to find their 82nd-minute equaliser as Rice raced onto Viktor Gyokeres' lay-off to drill into the bottom-left corner.
Timber, looking to make up for conceding the earlier penalty, could have won the game in the 91st minute, but Neuer got a strong hand behind the bending shot to keep it level.
Kane denied three points after haunting his familiar foe
Kane has always enjoyed playing against Arsenal, but could not prove the difference despite scoring his 16th goal against them – only versus Leicester City (20) has he scored more.
This is the ninth Champions League match in which he has both scored and assisted, two more than any other Englishman has managed.
Kane is also just the second player to score in 10 consecutive Champions League appearances, along with Cristiano Ronaldo from June 2017 to April 2018 (11).

The 33-year-old was showing off all of his attributes with some incredible passes opening Arsenal up. Only Barcelona's Lamine Yamal (10) has set up more goals in Europe's big five leagues in all competitions than Kane (seven) this term.

Arsenal started well, though, especially considering Saka's early exit, with Eze getting a much-needed goal. He scored the earliest goal by a substitute in a Champions League game since Junior Adamu in February 2022 for Salzburg – also against Bayern (21st minute).
And they finished strong after riding the pressure. No Premier League side has had more goal contributions from substitutes in all competitions this season than Arsenal (five goals, four assists).
Rice scored his sixth Champions League goal, but his first-ever away from home, and in the end, it was a fair result with both sides preserving their unbeaten starts to the competition.

1jgp0v4sjcfm117ra12teh8jg3.title: Barcelona defender Garcia leaves Spain squad after knee injury
1jgp0v4sjcfm117ra12teh8jg3.subtitle: Robin Le Normand has been called up to the Spain squad by Luis De la Fuente after Barcelona's Eric Garcia picked up a knee injury.
paragraphs: Robin Le Normand has replaced Eric Garcia in the Spain squad after the Barcelona defender picked up a knee injury.
Garcia did not feature in Spain's thrilling win over England in their Nations League opener, with Aymeric Laporte and Pau Cubarsi starting at centre-back for Luis De la Fuente's side.
The 25-year-old has featured in six of Barca's eight games this season, with the Blaugrana making the perfect start to the 2026-27 campaign.
Garcia leads Barca defenders in tackles won this season (10), while he has won the third-most duels (21), completed the third-most passes (393) and recorded the fourth-most clearances (16).
Spain released a statement which read: "Atletico Madrid player Robin Le Normand replaces Eric Garcia in the Spanish national team camp, which is playing in the UEFA Nations League group stage.

"The Barcelona centre-back felt some discomfort in his left knee and after the tests carried out, it has been decided to withdraw him from the squad due to the proximity of the upcoming international matches, thus avoiding any risk and preserving the player's health."
Following their win at Wembley Stadium, Spain host Croatia and Czechia before a return fixture against the former in the remainder of this international break.
Spain are unbeaten in their last 39 matches, the longest such run among all European nations in all competitions (W30 D9).

1jktcu5ii7vd51my45m8v8l098.title: Paris Saint-Germain 4-2 Barcelona: Vitinha and Fabian strike late to settle Champions League thriller
1jktcu5ii7vd51my45m8v8l098.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain were wasteful early on, but they found their shooting boots late on in a dramatic clash with Barcelona.
paragraphs: Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz struck in the last 10 minutes to clinch Paris Saint-Germain a 4-2 win over Barcelona in an enthralling Champions League tie.
Both sides were guilty of wasting chances, but Desire Doue gave PSG a half-time lead that Xavi Espart cancelled out early in the second half.
Lamine Yamal then levelled after Lucas Hernandez had put the reigning champions back in front, Vitinha and Fabian both scored late on to end Barcelona's perfect start to the season.

PSG almost got off to a dream start as Pedri was caught in possession and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Ousmane Dembele latched onto the rebound and blazed wide of the empty net, but the offside flag spared his blushes.
Ferran Torres – an early replacement after Dembele pulled up holding his hamstring – was played in behind Barcelona's defence, but Joan Garcia was equal to the scuffed volley.
And Garcia's inspired form continued as he again denied Ferran from point-blank range before getting back to his feet to push away Fabian's bouncing volley.
The breakthrough came in the 38th minute, as Joao Neves cut out Yamal's dinked pass from defence, and Doue skipped away from his marker to curl past Garcia.
Fermin Lopez – who came on for the injured Dani Olmo – should have equalised moments later, but Matvey Safonov stood his ground to block the chip one-on-one.
PSG started the second half on top as well, with Doue picking out the unmarked Achraf Hakimi, who could only aim his first-time effort at Garcia.
Barcelona punished their hosts for their profligacy in the 55th minute as a lovely, flowing team move resulted in Fermin sliding in Espart to drill past Safonov.

Gavi then forced a sharp stop out of Safonov, but PSG soon swung momentum back in their favour. Ferran struck the post from close range, and from the next corner, Doue picked out Hernandez to thump past the helpless Garcia.

Barcelona were not done yet, with Yamal dragging them level with a piece of individual brilliance. Warren Zaire-Emery could not clear a long ball forward, and the teenager readjusted brilliantly to bring it in his stride and rifle a stunning tight-angled strike into the roof of the net with 11 minutes to go.

But Vitinha restored PSG’s advantage two minutes later; Hakimi's cross was only half-cleared by Gerard Martin and the Portugal international put his laces through a volley on the edge of the box to give Garcia no chance.

With four minutes of the 90 remaining, Fabian made sure of all three points. Hakimi's low cross took a slight deflection, but it still made it through to the unmarked Spaniard, who tapped in at the far post.
Flick's side come unstuck for the first time this season

If this fixture promised one thing, it was goals. The previous 15 European/Cup Champions League meetings between these sides saw a combined 57 goals scored, and this one arguably should have had even more.
PSG dominated the first half and got 10 of their 12 shots on target, the highest number of attempts on target Barcelona have faced before the break in the competition since at least 2003-04.
Despite being on the losing side, Garcia proved to be the key part of Flick's side as he made 10 saves in total.
Flick's side have been the ones to beat in 2026-27, but their perfect record across all competitions has now ended – they had won all of their previous 11 games while scoring 48 goals.
The two teams combined for 40 shots (22 for PSG, 18 for Barca) and had 11 Opta-defined 'big' chances between them (six for PSG, five for Barcelona).

This was always going to be Barcelona's toughest test of the season, and PSG made sure they knew they were in a contest. Luis Enrique, facing his former side, has now overseen a 13-game unbeaten streak in the Champions League (W9 D4).
They have equalled their longest-ever run without defeat in the European Cup/Champions League (13 games between October 2012 and November 2013).

1jnuwjy0wm41s191l5w5d11b1n.title: Bellamy insists Wales 'performance was more important' than win over Norway
1jnuwjy0wm41s191l5w5d11b1n.subtitle: Wales came from behind to defeat 10-man Norway at Cardiff City Stadium, but Craig Bellamy took more pleasure in their display than the win.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy insisted Wales' "performance was more important" than their win over Norway on Thursday.
Wales came from behind to defeat 10-man Norway 2-1 in the Nations League, ending a seven-match winless run across all competitions.
Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb's opener before Torbjorn Heggem was shown a straight red card early in the second half, with Neco Williams scoring the winner from the resulting free-kick.

Heggem was sent off just 21 seconds following the restart, making it the quickest-ever second-half red card in a Nations League match, while this was Wales' first win after falling behind since November 2024 against Iceland (4-1).
While Bellamy was pleased with the three points, he took more pride in Wales' display at Cardiff City Stadium.
"Really pleasing. The performance was more important, to look like us," Bellamy told BBC Match of the Day Wales.
"We've worked hard to get to Nations League A and we know the teams are littered and loaded with good players.
"I know we've got a lot of players out, but we still have to be us. So that was nice and was pleasing.
"The last few days in training, we had an identity meeting. I have to give credit to the players, they've been brilliant.
"What do we want to do? Do we want to sit deep and play on counter-attacks or do we want to be aggressive and be on the front foot and keep the ball when we have it?
"That's really it. I think that's us. We do have to punch above our weight, but let's give it a right go. That's always been brought to me as a Welsh person growing up."
Norway struggled after going a man down, though Erling Haaland uncharacteristically missed a great chance at 2-1.
The visitors would have been optimistic after Martin Odegaard, who has assisted 14 goals in his last 15 matches for Norway, was declared fit, but Heggem's dismissal proved too much to come back from.
Stale Solbakken told TV 2 Play: "I think we were too careful in the first half. Far too much back-and-forth football."

1jug4eefmlrcr1sgin96xbi3ii.title: 'Every game is a new story', says Perelman as Orlando bid to halt losing run
1jug4eefmlrcr1sgin96xbi3ii.subtitle: Orlando City and the Columbus Crew are both involved in the playoff battle in the Eastern Conference, ahead of their head-to-head matchup.
paragraphs: Orlando City SC went into the international break on a three-game losing run, but interim head coach Martin Perelman says they are ready to write a new chapter against the Columbus Crew.
After losing 2-1 to the Crew in the U.S. Open Cup semi-finals on September 16, the Lions were on the wrong end of two six-goal thrillers in MLS play.
They were beaten 4-2 by the New England Revolution and the Philadelphia Union, sending them into the hiatus seventh in the Eastern Conference.

While they currently occupy the final automatic spot for the MLS Cup Playoffs, there are three teams – the New York Red Bulls, New York City and FC Cincinnati – within a single point of them, while three more – D.C. United, the Crew and Toronto FC – are within five.
But Perelman is ready to draw a line under Orlando's recent results, saying: "We always analyse the opponents and their previous games.
"Every game is a new chapter. Every game is a new story, a different context, sometimes a different competition.
"We focus on us. We focus on our team. Everybody will be ready to compete."
The Crew, meanwhile, approach Saturday's game off the back of two straight wins – 2-0 over CF Montreal and 2-1 over Inter Miami.
It is just the second time this season the Crew have managed to win two straight games, and the first since beating the LA Galaxy and Philadelphia back-to-back in April.
Their dramatic victory over Lionel Messi and company last time out bolstered their own postseason hopes, but interim boss Laurent Courtois was equally enthused by their performance.
"It was important, especially before a mini-break, to have not only the performance but the key moments and also the three points," Courtois said.
"And of course, that's going to give the guys confidence."
Orlando City – Ivan Angulo
Angulo scored and provided an assist for Orlando in their loss to Philadelphia last time out.

He has played more minutes than any other Orlando player this year (2,358) and has 12 goal involvements (five goals, seven assists), tied for second on the team behind leading goalscorer Martin Ojeda (13 goals, two assists).
Columbus Crew – Jamal Thiare
Thiare's winning goal against Miami was timed at 97:47, the sixth-latest goal in MLS this season and the fourth-latest game-winner.
It was the latest goal for Columbus since Jacen Russell-Rowe scored in the 99th minute against the Chicago Fire in September 2024.
MATCH PREDICTION – ORLANDO CITY WIN
Orlando City have a narrow lead over Columbus Crew in the all-time regular-season series between the two teams, with 10 wins and eight losses (D6).
The Lions are currently on a three-game unbeaten streak against Columbus in MLS play (W1 D2) after suffering three straight losses against them in 2023 and 2024 (including playoffs).
Orlando's back-to-back 4-2 defeats moved them into a tie for the second-most goals conceded in MLS this season, alongside Cincinnati (64), with only Sporting Kansas City (65) allowing more.
But even with their leaky backline, Orlando are the Opta supercomputer's favourites on home soil, where they have won each of their last three games in MLS.
Columbus Crew – 29.1%

1jzc4exup849u1pj73g1jmzxz2.title: Carrick admits Man Utd regrets after 10-man Tottenham salvage a point
1jzc4exup849u1pj73g1jmzxz2.subtitle: Manchester United failed to kill off the 10 men of Tottenham on Saturday, as two under-pressure teams drew 1-1 at Old Trafford.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick admitted there were huge regrets in Manchester United's camp for failing to kill off another team with 10 men, after they drew 1-1 with Tottenham.
United spent long periods under pressure in front of a disgruntled Old Trafford crowd on Saturday, with Spurs passing up multiple chances to go in front.

But when Bryan Mbeumo turned and slotted into the bottom-right corner with 73 minutes gone, and Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for a headbutt on Luke Shaw soon afterwards, the Red Devils' second Premier League win of the season appeared to be within reach.
However, in the second of eight minutes of second-half stoppage time, Dominic Solanke took advantage of Lisandro Martinez's poor marking to nod Sandro Tonali's cross home.
The result leaves United 12th in the Premier League table with just six points on the board after five matches, with boos greeting the full-time whistle.

United have now failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against the team starting the day bottom of the table, drawing 1-1 on all three occasions, against Wolves in December 2025, Fulham last month, and Spurs on Saturday.
Just as damningly, they are winless in their last three league games against teams who have received a red card, also losing to Manchester City last month and against Newcastle United in March.
"A really mixed game. We found it tough in the first half. It was a challenging opening period," Carrick told Sky Sports afterwards.
"It just wasn't quite there, with the little bits of play, and we kept getting caught on the ball.
"We weren't finding the pass, we were a little bit late with the press, leaving spaces, there were a number of things.
"We warmed to the game and were much better in the second half in so many different ways. We got ourselves in a really good position to show that bit of spirit and fight to put ourselves 1-0 up.
"It's a game we then should kill off and we didn't find a way. We turned the ball over too easily at times and it leaves the game open.
"It's obviously a bad goal and it sums things up. We're very disappointed to be in a position like that and not come away with the game."

Things do not get much better for Carrick's under-fire team, either, as they visit Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday, before facing old rivals Leeds United – who have only lost once all season – in the Premier League next weekend.

1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.title: Carrick understands jeers from Man Utd fans after Mainoo substitution
1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.subtitle: Manchester United's travelling fans made their feelings known when Kobbie Mainoo was substituted with 10 minutes to play against Fulham.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick understands the "emotional" reactions to Manchester United's recent struggles, after his decision to withdraw Kobbie Mainoo against Fulham was booed by their travelling fans.
With just five points on the board after five games, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign, having also taken five at this stage of 2014-15.

Things could have been worse for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage on Sunday, too, as Matheus Cunha's deflected strike snatched a point in the 89th minute, after Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal had put them on the back foot.
With United 1-0 down and chasing the game, Carrick's choice to replace Mainoo with Mason Mount in the 80th minute was loudly jeered by the away end.
Mainoo had completed 64 of his 68 passes, 27 of which were in the final third, with only Bryan Mbeumo (100%) and Harry Maguire (95.8%) bettering his 94.1% pass accuracy among United's starters.
But Carrick feels that reaction came from a place of frustration and understands the disgruntled feeling among the fanbase.
"There are always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," Carrick said. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.
"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are – as they should be – desperate for us to do the right thing.
"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.
"The supporters were unbelievable, I have to say, all the way through. They stuck with the boys and supported them.
"At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

With United 12th in the Premier League table going into the extended international break, the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 17% chance of qualifying for the Champions League, but Carrick is sure there are plenty of twists and turns ahead.
"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick said. "It's a long season, and you're going to have these spells through a season. That's part of the journey. It's not a sprint; it's a long effort.
"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better, and we wanted to do other things.
"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch, and that's what will carry us through the season, without a doubt."
United face Tottenham, who are still winless and prop up the table, in their next Premier League game on October 10.

1k0dmga5l6mey1l0my4y5azs2b.title: Merino insists Arsenal can win the quadruple this season
1k0dmga5l6mey1l0my4y5azs2b.subtitle: Arsenal have already won the Community Shield in 2026-27, and Mikel Merino believes the Gunners can win all four trophies available to them.
paragraphs: Mikel Merino has outlined his and Arsenal's desire "to win everything" this season after the Gunners' strong start to their 2026-27 campaign continued on Tuesday.
Arsenal beat Lille 3-0 to make it two wins from two in the Champions League, with Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka all on target at the Emirates Stadium.
The Gunners have now won their last 14 Champions League group stage/league phase games, while also keeping nine clean sheets during their incredible stretch.
Arteta's side also responded to their thumping 3-0 defeat to Brighton before the international break with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Leeds United in the Premier League.
They have won 14 of their last 17 Premier League games (L3), with nine of those wins coming via a one-goal margin, and are just three points behind leaders Manchester City.
League Two side Fleetwood Town are Arsenal's opponents in the last 16 of the EFL Cup, while their FA Cup journey will begin in January next year.

Merino was a part of the side that won the Premier League but also lost the Champions League and EFL Cup finals, while a quarter-final exit to Southampton in the FA Cup saw Arsenal lift just one piece of silverware in 2025-26.
But the Spaniard believes Arsenal are capable of winning the quadruple this year, telling Sky Sports after Arsenal's win over Lille: "It's an unbelievable run.
"We know we're making history in the competition. At the same time, we know how difficult it is to win games. We keep a lot of value and credit in the team for what we're doing.
"The goal is to win the Champions League, the Premier League, to win everything. That's what the manager wants.
"That's what the fans want. That's what we as players want as well."
The last time Arsenal won more than one trophy in the same season (excluding the Community Shield) was in 2001-02, when they lifted the Premier League and the FA Cup.
When asked if winning all four trophies was possible, Merino said: "Absolutely. This is the mentality. This is the aim.
"We were so, so close last season and that proved to us, we are ready for it. Now it's about details, being present and ready at the right moments. And we believe that."

1k1h354oppgun1hlr87f1bthvq.title: Monza 1-4 Napoli: Hojlund ends goal drought in Serie A thrashing
1k1h354oppgun1hlr87f1bthvq.subtitle: Napoli got back to winning ways in Serie A with a routine victory over Monza at U-Power Stadium, where Rasmus Hojlund got on the scoresheet.
paragraphs: Rasmus Hojlund scored for the first time since September 5 for Napoli as they thrashed Monza 4-1 in Serie A.
Matteo Politano, Rafa Marin and Kevin De Bruyne also got on the scoresheet as Massimiliano Allegri watched on from the stands at U-Power Stadium, serving the first match of his two-game ban.
Napoli needed just 10 minutes to break the deadlock as Giovanni Di Lorenzo played Hojlund in behind the Monza defence, and the Dane made no mistake with his sliding finish at the near post.

Politano pounced on a poor pass from Ricardo Mangas but saw his shot blocked by Saba Goglichidze, while Vanja Milinkovic-Savic bailed out Di Lorenzo at the other end after the Napoli captain was dispossessed by Gustavo Varela.

Monza were level two minutes before the break through Varela, who glanced a header into the far corner from Jay Robinson's cross, but Napoli restored their lead in the 48th minute after Politano capitalised on a heavy touch from Mangas before curling into the bottom-left corner.

Milinkovic-Savic was called into action again, this time getting low to his right to keep out Manga Foe Ondoa's volley, and Napoli made the most of that reprieve as Marin flicked Politano's corner past Noel Tornqvist in the 62nd minute.

De Bruyne then came off the bench to add further gloss to the scoreline five minutes later, finishing through the legs of the Monza goalkeeper following a brilliant throughball from Noa Lang, while Scott McTominay flashed a potential fifth past the left post.
Hojlund helps ease pressure on Allegri

The pressure was growing on Allegri ahead of this fixture after they squandered the lead twice against Roma off the back of a defeat against Venezia, but Hojlund, another who has been heavily criticised, opened the scoring in an important win.

Hojlund scored for the first time since MD3 against Inter, while he also led Napoli in shots on target (two), touches in the box (four) and aerial duels won (3/4), and his goal comes at an important time.

Napoli face Juventus and Lazio in Serie A either side of a Champions League encounter with Porto, and the Partenopei will need their striker firing on all cylinders if they are to continue turning their season around.

Despite the four goals and three points, with Napoli also winning the expected goals (xG) battle 1.37 to 0.73, there will be some concern for Allegri after Stanislav Lobotka was stretchered off in the 17th minute with a suspected ankle injury.

Varela, meanwhile, became the second-youngest player (21 years and 271 days) to score at least eight goals in his first eight appearances in the history of Serie A, after Otello Torri (eight in eight games with Novara between 1936 and 1937 at 19y 364d).

Varela, meanwhile, became the second-youngest player (21 years and 271 days) to score at least eight goals in his first eight appearances in the history of Serie A, after Otello Torri (eight in eight games with Novara between 1936 and 1937 at 19y 364d).

1k36x0k0emsqb12pwrssuggwq0.title: England 2-3 Spain: Oyarzabal completes comeback to seal world champions victory
1k36x0k0emsqb12pwrssuggwq0.subtitle: England mounted a first-half comeback to lead at the break, but Spain refused to give up and completed their own turnaround to earn the win.
paragraphs: Mikel Oyarzabal scored the winner against England once again as Spain came from behind to win 3-2 in their Nations League opener.
Lamine Yamal gave the world champions an early lead before Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane flipped the script before the break.

But after Kane missed a penalty, Spain rallied to earn three points in their first match since the World Cup final, with Alex Baena equalising before Oyarzabal securing the victory, just as he did in the Euro 2024 final.

Spain made the perfect start at Wembley, with Marc Guehi dispossessed as he turned back towards his own goal. Yamal picked his pocket and ruthlessly punished the mistake, turning his shot in off the inside of the far post just two minutes in.
Ferran Torres then saw a goal disallowed shortly after; Fabian Ruiz bent a lovely cross into the box, but the striker's diving header was ruled out for offside.
Ferran then saw two golden opportunities go begging, with James Trafford making himself big to smother a one-on-one shot, before firing wide from a similar position.
An exquisite Yamal backheel slipped in Dani Olmo, who fired wide from a tight angle, before Kane bent one wide at the other end in England's first clear-cut opener.

But England needed just four minutes to flip the game on its head. Nico Williams' slip opened the door for a pacy counter-attack, and Gordon played a one-two with Jude Bellingham before slotting it past Unai Simon from the edge of the box 36 minutes in.
And with Spain on the ropes, Kane met Nico O'Reilly's chipped cross after getting in front of Aymeric Laporte, and Marc Cucurella could only help it in off his thigh.

England started brightly after the break, with Bellingham winning a penalty after going down under Rodri's challenge. But Kane could not take advantage, smashing it against the crossbar after his standing foot slipped.
Spain made that reprieve count on the hour, with another helping hand from England. O'Reilly's loose pass went straight to Olmo, who picked out Baena to fire past Trafford.
And his fellow substitute secured the victory in the 74th minute; Baena cut open England's defence with his throughball and Oyarzabal lifted a lovely dink over Trafford when he rushed off his line.
Spain find another gear after England put on some pressure

It was not all smooth sailing for Spain, with their lengthy unbeaten streak also coming under some pressure, but La Roja are now unbeaten in their last 39 matches in all competitions (W30 D9, in 90 minutes), extending the longest-ever such run by a European nation.
But they conceded two goals in the first half of an official match for the first time since October 2018, when they let in three at the Benito Villamarin against England, also in the Nations League.
Spain also conceded more goals in the first 45 minutes (two) than they did in the entirety of their World Cup-winning campaign (one).

While they had their wobbles, they made a stunning start, with Yamal scoring the third-quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley, while he is the youngest player to score against the Three Lions in a competitive match at the stadium in the last 20 years (19 years, 75 days).
It is a disappointing loss for England, but they made sure Spain knew they were in a fight.
The hosts had 12 shots, with four of those on target, though they only accumulated 1.51 expected goals (xG). Spain, by contrast, had 15 attempts worth 1.99 xG, with five on target.
England also caused their own problems, though, making two errors leading to goal in a competitive match for the first time since June 2019 against the Netherlands, also in the Nations League.

1k97az1e32wuy15jn6xdw82rel.title: 'We will get through this' – Guardiola addresses Man City fans after Premier League verdict
1k97az1e32wuy15jn6xdw82rel.subtitle: Pep Guardiola has responded after Manchester City were found guilty of "systematically" breaking the Premier League's rules.
paragraphs: Pep Guardiola has addressed Manchester City's fans after the club were found guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, saying: "We will get through this together."
In February 2023, the Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 breaches of the competition's rules across a nine-year period.

And in a statement released on Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of all charges that related to serious breaches of financial rules and the majority of charges which were "in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league's investigation".

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said City had "systematically broken Premier League Rules for nearly a decade" and described the decision as the "most significant" in the competition's history.

City have pledged to fight the ruling and have until October 2 to exercise their right to appeal, with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak saying last Friday he remained confident of proving the club's innocence.
Former City defender Micah Richards – who won a Premier League title and an FA Cup during his time at the Etihad Stadium – said the verdict left him feeling "absolutely devastated".
But former head coach Guardiola issued a more defiant response via his social media channels on Wednesday, outlining his continued support for the club's hierarchy.
"I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever," Guardiola wrote, alongside an image of himself and Al Mubarak.

"I am, always have been, and always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano, chief executive of the City Football Group], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters.
"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."
Guardiola won 20 major trophies during his decade-long stint with City, including six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five EFL Cups and the Champions League in 2022-23.
