1kbibnjz7g5ic1kxli2k7122we.title: Foden 'going in the right direction' after Champions League hat-trick
1kbibnjz7g5ic1kxli2k7122we.subtitle: Manchester City returned to winning ways in the Champions League by thumping AEK Athens, with Phil Foden starring with a hat-trick.
paragraphs: Phil Foden believes he is "going in the right direction" but is far from being back to his best despite scoring a hat-trick in Manchester City's 5-1 win over AEK Athens.

Foden starred in Tuesday's victory at Etihad Stadium, becoming the third Englishman to score a hat-trick and assist a goal in a Champions League match, along with Wayne Rooney (September 2004 against Fenerbahce, for Manchester United) and Raheem Sterling (October 2019 against Atalanta, for City).
Elliot Anderson got things going in the 12th minute before Foden combined with Rico Lewis to double the Citizens' lead just before Willy Delajod blew the whistle for half-time.
AEK reduced the deficit through Stavros Pilios seven minutes after the restart, but a moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki quickly restored the hosts' two-goal lead.

Foden sealed the win with two goals 11 minutes, the latter seeing him combine with Lewis once again to complete his hat-trick, and score in back-to-back appearances for the club, having gone 35 outings without finding the back of the net.

Before lining up against AEK, Foden had managed just three goal involvements (one goal, two assists) in seven appearances across all competitions this season, but he starred in the absence of Erling Haaland, who watched on from the bench.
In fact, it was City's first Champions League hat-trick since March 2023 when Haaland scored five against RB Leipzig, though Foden was just thrilled to help his team to victory.
"Slowly, but surely," Foden told TNT Sports when asked if he was getting back to his best. "Still got a long way to go, but I'm going in the right direction.
"Scoring along the way definitely helps. I just want to keep working hard and trying to be the best I can for the manager and the team.
"I enjoyed that a lot. The lads were great again. We showed determination again. It wasn't pretty at times.
"I thought we stuck at the gameplan, we kept going and in the end we broke them down."
Foden's indifferent run of form over the last two seasons saw him miss out on a spot in Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad this summer, with England going on to finish third.
But Maresca, who led City to their 10th win in 12 matches in all competitions this season, said he never doubted Foden's talent since replacing Pep Guardiola this summer.
"I've said since day one, I consider him one of the best English players," Maresca told a news conference.
"For different reasons in the last three years he was not good enough, but I know how good he is so I'm trying to help him because we are sure he is going to help us this season."

Maresca is now one of six managers in the Premier League era (since 1992-93) with 10 wins in as few as 12 games with a club, along with Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea (12), Guardiola at Man City (10), Unai Emery at Arsenal (12), Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Man Utd (11) and Arne Slot at Liverpool (11).
But more importantly, City returned to winning ways in the Champions League having lost 4-2 to defending champions Paris Saint-Germain on home soil.

And aged 24 years and 63 days, Maresca named City's youngest ever line-up for a Champions League game, and he praised his talented youngsters for playing their part in delivering a "complete" performance.
"For the academy, I think there are three players from the academy that made their debut tonight, so it is nice news for the academy and for the club," Maresca said.
"I think it was a complete performance. It was not easy, especially after the PSG game.

"So we had two games, Ipswich and today that we needed to win and, yes, we did our job. I think again, we concede the goal in transition, but probably could have made something better in that situation.
"Again, we scored five. We could have probably scored more, but happy because some of the players were not playing many minutes. They were ready and this is important.
"To be honest, it is the best feeling for any manager when you make many changes, but at the end the performance is good, so happy for especially them."

1kc5fgn8wc18z1dtbg7z1ltu4i.title: 'It's going to be a war' – LAFC ready for crucial derby clash
1kc5fgn8wc18z1dtbg7z1ltu4i.subtitle: Los Angeles FC need just a point in Sunday's derby clash with the LA Galaxy to secure their place in the playoffs.
paragraphs: Sergi Palencia is ready to do battle as Los Angeles FC aim to secure their place in the playoffs when they take on the LA Galaxy.
Sunday's Trafico clash has plenty riding on it.
LAFC know a win or draw will see them clinch their playoff spot.
The Galaxy, meanwhile, are six points behind their city rivals, and are well in the playoff picture themselves.
And LAFC defender Palencia is prepared for a fiercely contested derby.
"It adds a little bit more pressure and tension," he told reporters.
"But in the end, it's 11 against 11, a derby, and we know each other really well. So, it's going to be a war."
Galaxy defender Harbor Miller echoed Palencia's sentiments.
He said: "It's always going to be one of the biggest games of the season, if not the biggest. The biggest thing is it's going to be a battle."
The record between these rivals is fairly split. Both teams have won 10 games, with the other seven derbies finishing level.
LAFC recorded a 3-0 win in July, but Palencia knows that result means little now.
"This situation is different. But for sure, they're going to use that to motivate themselves and to come with more intensity than ever," said Palencia.
"And we have to be ready for that. We have to know what’s at stake, and we are ready. We just want to beat these guys again."
LAFC - Denis Bouanga
Bouanga has scored in seven consecutive regular-season matches against the Galaxy.
That ties Bouanga with Raul Ruidiaz (2019-22) for the longest streak of consecutive regular-season games with a goal against the Galaxy.
LA Galaxy - Joao Klauss
Klauss scored his 34th regular-season goal against San Diego FC, but it was just his fourth goal from outside the box.
The three other outside-the-box goals for Klauss came in February against Charlotte FC this season and twice in a six-minute span on March 25, 2023, for St. Louis City SC against Real Salt Lake.
MATCH PREDICTION: LAFC WIN
The Galaxy have scored multiple goals in five straight games, the team's longest such streak in league play since a five-game run in September-October 2024.
The club's last longer such streak in the regular season was a six-game run in July-August 2023.
LAFC, meanwhile, have scored 12 goals from outside the box this season. Only two other MLS teams have double-digit such goals this term: Inter Miami (14) and the Houston Dynamo (10).
LAFC's 3-0 win over the Galaxy in July marked the fourth clean sheet by either team across their all-time regular-season meetings.
All three previous shutouts came in 2020.

1kdoumq01kfm11icbyy3tdteh5.title: Tarkowski urges Everton to respond to Chelsea setback against Arsenal
1kdoumq01kfm11icbyy3tdteh5.subtitle: Everton's unbeaten Premier League start ended last weekend, and they are looking to bounce back against the reigning champions, Arsenal.
paragraphs: James Tarkowski has called on Everton to make a good response against Arsenal, following their loss to Chelsea last time out in the Premier League.
Everton had been unbeaten in the top-flight heading into MD7 (W2 D4), but were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea, who scored at the start and the end of the second half.

The result leaves them eighth in the table, but a win over the reigning champions would get them back on the right track and would move them at least up to fifth – taking them above rivals Liverpool in the process.
Tarkowski believes Everton's attitude heading into the clash at Emirates Stadium is key, pointing to last season as an example of what they can do if they take the right approach.
"I always felt last year that anytime we suffered a defeat, we responded pretty well. So, hopefully that happens [this weekend]," Tarkowski told evertontv.
"Hopefully, the team can keep picking up points. [Chelsea] was a tough day, a setback.
"We dealt with them pretty well last year, so we're looking forward to [the next match]."
Arsenal, meanwhile, sit second in the table, three points behind Manchester City heading into the weekend's action, having bounced back from their loss to Brighton with two consecutive wins.
They edged past Nottingham Forest last time out in the top-flight and followed that up by coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Bayern Munich in the Champions League.
Arsenal lost Bukayo Saka to injury early in that match, but Mikel Arteta was pleased with their reaction and will hope to carry those positives into Saturday's match.

"The character, personality and quality we showed to understand what the game required, because the game changed, and they pressed in two different ways, what the team understood and executed was really, really good," Arteta said about the performance against Bayern.
"Execution-wise, we had some great moments – we could have been even better and more clinical in certain aspects with our final shot – but overall, it's a game we can take a lot of positives from."
Arsenal – Gabriel Magalhaes
Gabriel Magalhaes could make his 200th Premier League appearance in this match, the 11th Brazilian to reach this milestone.

Arsenal have won 65% of their games when he plays (44% when he does not since 2020-21) – among players to have played 150+ Premier League games for the Gunners, only Lauren has a higher win rate (66%).
Everton – Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall
No player has made more line-breaking passes into the opposition box than Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in the Premier League this season (16, level with Granit Xhaka).
He has scored 13 goals in the competition in total, including one in Everton's last away game against Hull City. All four of his away goals in the top-flight in 2026 have been equalisers.
MATCH PREDICTION: ARSENAL WIN
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last seven Premier League matches against Everton (W5 D2), their best run against the Toffees since going 13 without defeat between December 2007 and December 2013.
And Everton have won one of their last 30 away league matches against Arsenal (D5 L24), a 1-0 victory in 2020-21 under Carlo Ancelotti.
Under David Moyes, the Toffees have never won away at the Gunners in 13 attempts in the league (D3 L10).

Everton's recent away form does not help, given they are winless in their last eight Premier League games on the road (D5 L3), with all three this season ending level. The last time a team drew each of their first four away games in a season of the competition was 2010-11, with both Fulham and Manchester United doing so.
Arsenal, meanwhile, have won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games (L1), winning all six at the Emirates Stadium in that run.

Arsenal have won 65% of their games when he plays (44% when he does not since 2020-21) – among players to have played 150+ Premier League games for the Gunners, only Lauren has a higher win rate (66%).

Everton – Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall

No player has made more line-breaking passes into the opposition box than Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in the Premier League this season (16, level with Granit Xhaka).

He has scored 13 goals in the competition in total, including one in Everton's last away game against Hull City. All four of his away goals in the top-flight in 2026 have been equalisers.

MATCH PREDICTION: ARSENAL WIN

Arsenal are unbeaten in their last seven Premier League matches against Everton (W5 D2), their best run against the Toffees since going 13 without defeat between December 2007 and December 2013.

And Everton have won one of their last 30 away league matches against Arsenal (D5 L24), a 1-0 victory in 2020-21 under Carlo Ancelotti.

Under David Moyes, the Toffees have never won away at the Gunners in 13 attempts in the league (D3 L10).

Everton's recent away form does not help, given they are winless in their last eight Premier League games on the road (D5 L3), with all three this season ending level. The last time a team drew each of their first four away games in a season of the competition was 2010-11, with both Fulham and Manchester United doing so.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games (L1), winning all six at the Emirates Stadium in that run.

1ki29umyxbp731295rnh0ee04w.title: Carrick disagrees with Ten Hag's 'toxic' Man Utd claims
1ki29umyxbp731295rnh0ee04w.subtitle: Erik ten Hag claimed the environment at Manchester United was toxic, but current boss Michael Carrick feels differently than the Dutchman.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick "couldn't be happier with the togetherness" at Manchester United amid claims from former boss Erik ten Hag about a "toxic culture" at the club.
Ten Hag was sacked as United head coach in 2024 after winning the FA Cup and EFL Cup during his time at Old Trafford, and he has heavily criticised the club in an interview with The Athletic.
The Dutchman believes Cristiano Ronaldo let the team down, while also blaming the board for not sticking to their word in the transfer market.

The Red Devils have struggled in 2026-27 so far under Carrick; United have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4 L2), their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87 – also one victory after seven games.
Nevertheless, Carrick praised his side's unity ahead of their Champions League clash with Como on Wednesday.
"I haven't [experienced the toxicity]," said Carrick when asked about Ten Hag's comments. "The players and staff has given everything they can.
"The type of performance the group put in on the weekend – there's a lot of togetherness, will and determination to do better. I couldn't be happier with the togetherness.
"That's Erik's opinion on the board. Wrong for me to comment and get involved. Results dictate a lot of the feeling at a football club.
"Within our walls as a group, we are pretty composed but driven. We've got to think calmly, with emotions directed in the right way. The conversations we have, we are quite clear.
"It's important we are all pulling in the right direction."

This will be the first meeting between Como and United – since the start of last season, the six matches between Italian and English sides in the Champions League have been won by the Premier League outfit on five occasions (L1 – Atalanta 2-1 Chelsea the exception).

United are unbeaten in their last six away games against Italian sides in the Champions League (W3 D3), last losing there in the competition in May 2007 against AC Milan (3-0 in the semi-final second leg).
"Our concentration and focus has to be 100%, and I know it will," added Carrick.
"I have a huge amount of respect for what Cesc [Fabregas] has done here and for the football club. It's clear he has good ideas. Huge amount of respect.
"He's one of the best I've played against. That doesn't necessarily mean he'll turn that into a good coaching career, but he's doing that."

1kiwo1dyygy3b1ji8pf10tf9z3.title: Paz: Como must play every game like it's our last
1kiwo1dyygy3b1ji8pf10tf9z3.subtitle: Nico Paz ran the show for Como against Manchester United, helping them run out with a 4-1 victory against Michael Carrick's side.
paragraphs: Nico Paz has urged Como to play "every game as if it's our last" after they hammered Manchester United 4-1 in the Champions League.
Paz scored twice and set up Tasos Douvikas in a stunning display, with Jacobo Ramon rounding off the brilliant performance by Cesc Fabregas' side.

Though they conceded a late consolation from Joshua Zirkzee, Como never looked in doubt about taking all three points as they became the first Italian team to win both of their first two home games in major European competition since Udinese in 1997-98.

Since the start of September, Paz has been directly involved in more goals in all competitions than any other Serie A player, recording nine contributions in eight appearances (four goals, five assists).

He was the heartbeat of their performance and, at 22 years and 43 days, became the second-youngest player to be involved in three goals in a Champions League game against an English side, behind Porto's Andre Silva in December 2016 (21y 31d against Leicester City).
Paz was also the youngest Argentinian to be involved in three goals in a Champions League game since Lionel Messi in April 2009 against Bayern Munich (21y 288d).
"That was one of the most beautiful games of my career; I'll never forget it," Paz told Sky Sport Italia, as quoted by Football Italia.
"It's more than what I had dreamed of; we played an incredible game. We have to continue like this, but this was an historic night for everyone from Como.
"We have to carry on like this, not thinking about where we can go, but to take on every game as if it's our last."
Como completed 594 passes, the most by a team in a Champions League game against United since Barcelona in April 2019 (725).
They are also only the second Italian team to beat United by at least three goals in the history of the European Cup/Champions League, after AC Milan (twice).
"It's a special night, but we are still at the beginning for everything we have in our minds," Fabregas told Sky Sport Italia.
"The team played well, but we need to keep our feet on the ground and remember there is another match coming up on Saturday."
When asked if Como could replicate their dominant approach against anyone in Europe, Fabregas added: "I don't know about that; it's a bold statement. We must try to remain humble.

"We will always prepare and try to play our game, whether it's against Inter in the Coppa Italia semi-final, or with Napoli and Roma in Serie A. Preparation is fundamental, but so is the belief of these lads. It is all more difficult if they don't have that.

"This was Manchester United we were up against; it doesn't matter if they are struggling at the moment, we must never forget that some of our players were having the third Champions League game of their entire careers.

"This is why the belief of these lads and their way of doing things gives me life. Winning this way is very satisfying, but this is where it gets difficult: playing the same way on Saturday in Serie A."

1klct1hycjsl71341j9jox0ukg.title: Nuno hails West Ham's professional win over nine-man Lincoln
1klct1hycjsl71341j9jox0ukg.subtitle: West Ham cruised to a big win over nine-man Lincoln City, with Championship leaders Swansea City up next for the Hammers.
paragraphs: Nuno Espirito Santo credited West Ham's professionalism after a resounding victory over nine-man Lincoln City on Wednesday.
The Hammers moved up to third in the Championship with a 6-0 win at ProAmpac Stadium, with all the goals coming after Lincoln duo Tom Hamer and Conor McGrandles were shown straight red cards.
Konstantinos Mavropanos scored the opener on the stroke of half-time before Edvin Austbo netted a stunning strike three minutes after the restart.
Jarrod Bowen and Pablo then got on the scoresheet, while Tomas Soucek came off the bench to seal the win with a brace.
West Ham dominated proceedings, accumulating 3.2 expected goals (xG) from 32 shots, 12 of which were on target, and retaining 82.8% of possession.

With this their second 6-0 win of the league this season (also against Wrexham), West Ham are now the top scorers in the top four divisions of English football (29), while they equalled their club-record away win (6-0 v Leicester City in 1923).
Next up for the Hammers is a trip to Championship leaders Swansea City, and Nuno acknowledged the size of the task ahead.
"We have a big game on the weekend now," Nuno told Sky Sports.
"This is what we didn't expect to happen but it's not up to us, I think we did our job, but we know it's going to be very tough at Swansea.
"We are trying to build momentum, trying to keep improving and the table is not vital, not important to look at but to just keep the lads focused and keep improving.
"What matters is the end and our objective is clear, we have to go back and we work very hard to achieve it. We know it's going to be tough and a very long season."
Southampton, meanwhile, moved into the play-off places after Kuryu Matsuki's strike secured a 1-0 win over Norwich City at Carrow Road.

1kni7tv2pzuto1fhc0ypmkm4i4.title: Gonzalez calls on Miami 'to keep improving' after securing playoff berth
1kni7tv2pzuto1fhc0ypmkm4i4.subtitle: Inter Miami have qualified for the play-offs and will now look to tighten their grip on second place when they face Atlanta United.
paragraphs: Cristian Gonzalez has called on his Inter Miami side "to keep improving" after they booked their place in the MLS play-offs.
The Herons qualified for the postseason after defeating New York City FC 2-0 on Wednesday, courtesy of goals from German Berterame and Rodrigo De Paul, with the latter assisted by Lionel Messi.
Miami are second in the Eastern Conference after back-to-back wins in the league, but they remain 14 points behind leaders Nashville SC, who have all-but-secured the Supporters' Shield.
Nevertheless, Gonzalez has urged his Miami side to keep fixing their mistakes ahead of their clash with Atlanta United on Saturday.
"Well, [qualifying for the playoffs] was one of the club's initial goals for the season, and we're there, but we still need to keep improving as a team," said Gonzalez.
"When you have players who are willing to buy into the vision you're trying to implement, everything becomes easier.
"We recognise the mistakes we've been making, or are still making, and we address them during training. And really, that willingness makes it much easier to convey clear concepts."
Gonzalez also spoke about star player Messi, who has had a busy and emotional year both on and off the pitch.
After Argentina reached a second consecutive World Cup final, this time losing to Spain, Messi's father passed away, leading to his retirement from international football.
"This is a club that looks after him and protects him," Gonzalez said about Messi.
"His teammates show him constant affection. They go all out for him and give everything they have. He pushes us to be better every single day and challenges us."
Atlanta, meanwhile, returned to winning ways in MLS with a 3-0 victory over CF Montreal during the week.
The Five Stripes are still 14th in the East, but now just six points off the play-off spots with five regular-season games to go.
Atlanta United – Miguel Almiron
Miguel Almiron has scored in back-to-back matches, including netting the first goal in Wednesday's win at Montreal.
The goal was Almiron's seventh match-winner for Atlanta in all competitions, the third-most in club history (Josef Martinez - 31, Thiago Almada - eight).
Inter Miami – Lionel Messi
Messi had an assist in Miami's win over NYCFC, his 11th consecutive regular-season match with a goal contribution.
The only longer single-season streaks in MLS history are Martinez's 15 straight in 2019 and Sebastian Giovinco's 12 straight in 2018.
MATCH PREDICTION – INTER MIAMI WIN
After winning only two of their previous 12 matches in all competitions (D5 L5), keeping just one clean sheet, Miami have recorded back-to-back shutout wins, both at home.
Miami have not won an away match in nearly three months, since a 1-0 triumph at Montreal on July 25.
Atlanta have scored multiple goals in eight of their last 12 regular-season matches, including equalling a season-high win at Montreal, for a total of 19 goals in those games.

The Five Stripes have recorded four wins over Miami in all competitions since Messi made his debut for the club in July 2023, the most wins by any MLS team over Miami in all competitions since Messi joined the Herons.
Atlanta United – 28.5%

1krsbncizt2sz1vrqelj0p9i2y.title: Norway 3-2 Denmark: Haaland brace decides Scandinavian scuffle in Nations League
1krsbncizt2sz1vrqelj0p9i2y.subtitle: Erling Haaland carried his World Cup and Premier League form into the 2026-27 Nations League, as Norway downed rivals Denmark 3-2.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland scored twice as Norway opened their Nations League campaign with an entertaining 3-2 win over Denmark, despite finishing the game with 10 men.

Having trailed 2-0 after just 18 minutes, Denmark fought back valiantly to level Thursday's matchup between Scandinavian rivals, but Haaland's second goal proved to be the winner, with the hosts surviving a late red card for David Moller Wolfe.

Two of Norway's other Premier League stars combined to give them the advantage in the 14th minute, as Oscar Bobb took in Martin Odegaard's cute pass, then shaped a curling finish around Denmark defender Oliver Provstgaard and into the far corner.

And Norway did not have to wait long for their second goal, as Antonio Nusa skipped infield and played a clever reverse pass in behind for Haaland, whose driven finish went straight through Filip Jorgensen.

Denmark found a route back into the contest in the 25th minute, with Mikkel Damsgaard's free-kick dipping over the Norway wall and beating Orjan Nyland, though only a superb reflex stop from Jorgensen prevented Patrick Berg from making it 3-1 late in the first half.
And the visitors drew level on the hour mark, with Rasmus Hojlund reacting quickest to nod home when Nyland blocked Morten Hjulmand's downward header from a corner.

But Haaland re-established Norway's lead when he lashed inside the near post following a well-worked corner routine that saw Odegaard receive a short pass from Nusa, reach the byline, and cut the ball back for the Manchester City talisman.
Moller Wolfe received his second yellow card three minutes into stoppage time, having blocked Gustav Isaksen's run down the right as Denmark chased another equaliser, but Norway held on.
New Nations League campaign, same old Haaland
Haaland's staggering form was one of the stories of this summer's World Cup, as he almost single-handedly powered Norway into the quarter-finals with seven goals in five games.

And he picked up where he left off at the start of their Nations League Group A4 campaign, scoring twice from a game-high five shots (four of which were on target), although his goals were hardly put on a plate, with all those efforts adding up to 0.35 expected goals (xG).
Haaland has now scored in 10 of his last 13 competitive games for Norway and Man City combined (16 goals in total), and in each of his last six (nine goals).

He last enjoyed a longer run between August and October 2025, going 12 straight matches with a goal. With two meetings against Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal to come during this international break, either side of a trip to Wales, Stale Solbakken will be desperate to see that streak continue.

1kunyghi1kc3w1ob361llq135v.title: Milan teenager Cisse has 'only shown 70% of my capabilities so far'
1kunyghi1kc3w1ob361llq135v.subtitle: Alphadjo Cisse has made an impressive start to the season with AC Milan, though he feels he can still offer more for the Rossoneri.
paragraphs: AC Milan teenager Alphadjo Cisse believes he has "only shown 70% of my capabilities so far" this season.
Cisse joined Milan in February, but spent the remainder of the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Catanzaro before breaking into the Rossoneri's first team this summer.
The 19-year-old impressed in pre-season under Ruben Amorim, scoring in their victory over Manchester United before also netting in Milan's Serie A opener over Torino.
Cisse became the youngest Italian player (19 years, 305 days) to score for Milan in Serie A since Patrick Cutrone (19 years, 236 days) did so against Cagliari on August 27, 2017.

And after also scoring in a 1-1 draw with Juventus, Cisse (19 years and 319 days old) became the youngest player to score in his first two away appearances for Milan in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95).
He took that form into the international break, scoring the only goal in Italy Under-21s' European qualifier victory over Armenia Under-21s.
"This year has brought me a lot of joy," Cisse said in an interview with Rai Sport.
"I’ve only shown 70% of my capabilities so far, I know I can do much better.
"The goal [against Armenia] brings me a lot of happiness, and from now on I hope to be able to show lots of other characteristics."
Milan face Sassuolo in their first match after the international break, before taking on Salzburg in the Europa League.

1kwmnjrbyd9kx1gutn5xedfgxe.title: Chelsea 1-0 Arsenal: Thompson seals derby bragging rights
1kwmnjrbyd9kx1gutn5xedfgxe.subtitle: Chelsea held on to continue their unbeaten start, edging to a narrow victory over Arsenal thanks to Alyssa Thompson's strike.
paragraphs: Alyssa Thompson's first-half strike downed wasteful Arsenal as Chelsea secured a 1-0 win that moved them third in the Women's Super League.

Chelsea took advantage of a sloppy piece of defending from Arsenal six minutes before the break, and Renee Slegers' side could not find an equaliser as they tasted defeat for the first time this season.
Arsenal started fairly well, with Kyra Cooney-Cross causing problems, though she saw an early shot blocked by her own team-mate.
Kim Little – making her 184th WSL appearance for Arsenal – almost caught Chelsea out with a cross that deflected towards goal and had Hannah Hampton worried, but it struck the crossbar.

Mariona Caldentey also struck the woodwork; Alessia Russo started a fast break, picking out Little on the right, and her switch found the Spaniard, who drilled her low shot against the foot of the near post.

But Arsenal created their own problems in the 39th minute, with Steph Catley's loose clearance pounced upon. Kiera Walsh's powerful strike was pushed away by Anneke Borbe, but only as far as Thompson, who emphatically fired into the roof of the net from close range.
Melvine Malard then broke forward on the counter-attack four minutes later, racing down the right with nobody closing her down, but Borbe made herself big to smother the angled attempt.
It was a much-improved Arsenal who emerged after the break, with Lisa Baum and Caldentey both forcing Hampton into action.

Malard then ghosted between two Arsenal defenders only to flick a close-range effort wide, while Stina Blackstenius raced in behind only to chip over under pressure from Hampton, though the offside flag would have denied her anyway.
Arsenal's scoring woes go on as Chelsea stay unbeaten
It was a fairly cagey London derby between two sides who desperately needed a win so they did not lose sight of leaders Manchester City.

Chelsea are now unbeaten across their opening four games of a WSL campaign for the fourth successive season, while Arsenal only have five points to their name at this stage for the second time in the last three seasons (also 2024-25).

Arsenal's attacking troubles have drawn the eye this season as they have netted just two goals this campaign, and despite piling the pressure on Chelsea, especially in the closing stages, they never looked likely to get a goal.
They had 18 shots overall, but only two of those were on target, and their 1.04 expected goals (xG) tells the story of their lack of spark in the box as they dawdled over their chances.

This loss ends Arsenal's 20-game unbeaten league streak, but they will feel they could have had a late equaliser from the spot after a handball by Ellie Carpenter in the box, but nothing was given, with her arm tight to her body when the ball hit her.

Slegers had already beaten Sonia Bompastor twice this calendar year, but the Frenchwoman ensured she came out on top this time, even if she thinks Chelsea could have had more goals after getting seven of their 13 shots on target.

1l3mrj35d8d2k1txjhzoj792u8.title: Raphinha to miss Barcelona's next two games as Flick adopts cautious approach
1l3mrj35d8d2k1txjhzoj792u8.subtitle: Barcelona will look to maintain their winning start to the LaLiga season against Getafe this weekend, but they will be without Raphinha.
paragraphs: Raphinha will miss Barcelona's next two games, against Getafe and Galatasaray, with Hansi Flick adopting a cautious approach to the thigh injury he suffered on Brazil duty.
Raphinha withdrew from the Selecao's squad during the international break, having been substituted at half-time in a 4-2 win over Australia.

The Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) said the winger had sustained "a small muscle edema in the posterior region of the right thigh", which represented a potential blow to Barca after he scored a remarkable 14 goals in their opening eight matches of 2026-27, across all competitions.

The Blaugrana, who have won their first seven games to set the pace at the top of LaLiga, welcome Getafe to Camp Nou on Saturday before travelling to Istanbul for their second Champions League game of 2026-27, and they will let their captain sit out those matches as he recovers.
"It is not a major injury, but it is something that must be taken into account because he had many injuries," Flick said of Raphinha.
"We have to take care of him. He will not be available [against Getafe] or against Galatasaray."
Flick was then asked if he had any complaints about the way Brazil managed Raphinha's fitness, but he said it was not worth worrying about factors Barca cannot control.
"It's the national team, and everyone wants to play for their national team. It's their mentality, and we can't change the calendar," he said.

"He always gives 100%. You question whether it was necessary to play in Australia, 30,000 kilometres away... but then you would have to choose friendlies in Europe, and with the Nations League, it is not possible.
"There is a lot of pressure on the players. You have to accept the situation as it is; it's not the best, it's not ideal, but I can't change it. I have to manage the load of minutes.
"I like it when I see the Spanish national team in performance, the distribution of minutes... The relationship is very good. Spain is the best team in the world; I like to see them play."
On Thursday, Barca handed teenage left-back Xavi Espart a new contract to run until 2030, and Flick was delighted to see another graduate of La Masia rewarded.
"For each position we have many players. Everyone must be at the best level, or we will make substitutions. They know it. I like this situation," the Barca boss added.
"It's fantastic to have this kind of player coming from La Masia. It's incredible."
Getafe are 11th in the table going into Saturday's game with eight points on the board, having beaten Malaga 1-0 in their final match before the international break.
Barcelona – Lamine Yamal
With Raphinha absent, it will be up to Yamal to provide the attacking spark for the hosts.

He has tallied a remarkable 14 goal involvements in eight appearances across all competitions this season (eight goals, six assists), while he also scored four goals in four outings for Spain during the international break.
Getafe – Djene Dakonam
Djene Dakonam, who has made the most appearances for Getafe in the top flight (311), could be the first player to reach 100 wins for the club in the competition's history (99).
MATCH PREDICTION: BARCELONA WIN

Barcelona are unbeaten in their 21 home games against Getafe in LaLiga (W17 D4). Only against Elche (25 games – W18 D7) have they played more home matches without suffering a single defeat in the competition's history.

The Blaugrana have also won their opening seven LaLiga games in the 2026-27 season and can equal their best ever start in the competition, achieved under Gerardo Martino in 2013-14, when they won their first eight matches of the campaign.
Flick's side have scored 31 goals in LaLiga 2026-27, the second-best goalscoring start by a team after their first seven games of a season in the competition's history, after Sevilla in 1940-41 (40).

Getafe, meanwhile, have lost their last eight away LaLiga games against Barcelona, failing to score in the last four. This is their worst run of consecutive defeats at the Blaugrana in the top-flight.

They have also lost all three of their away games in LaLiga 2026-27, failing to score in any of them. This is the first time they have lost their opening three away matches of a season in the competition and failed to score in any of them.

1lcd5udt7pv3314nikbdd0zwhj.title: Croatia 'not afraid' of Spain, says Kovacic
1lcd5udt7pv3314nikbdd0zwhj.subtitle: Croatia are looking to make it two wins from two in the 2026-27 Nations League, but next up for them is a trip to world champions Spain.
paragraphs: Mateo Kovacic insists Croatia are "not afraid of anyone" as they prepare to face world champions Spain in the Nations League.
Spain are the dominant figure in world football at the moment, having clinched their second World Cup over the summer with a 1-0 win over Argentina in the final.
They are currently on a 39-match unbeaten streak (across 90 minutes (W30 D9), the longest such run by a European nation in history.
Croatia won their opening Nations League match 2-1 against Czechia, and sit level on points with Spain, who enjoyed a 3-2 comeback win over England.
But as perhaps expected, Spain are heavy favourites in this clash, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 78.3% win probability to Croatia's 8.4%.
Kovacic, however, is not shying away from the challenge ahead of the team.
"Of course. Spain, right now, is the best team in the world," he said. "There's nothing better than playing against the best.

"It will be a difficult match against the best team in the world. But it will be difficult for them too. We have played against them several times, and sometimes we have done very well. Hopefully, we can repeat that.
"We're not afraid of anyone. We respect everyone. Spain is a very strong team. They're very united. They're a top team, but we'll focus on our own game."
Asked if getting a win on Tuesday would be impossible, Kovacic said: "No.
"We know about the 39 games without losing, but I don't want to dwell on that; I want to focus on our game and take the ball away from them."
Spain are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Croatia, winning two and drawing the other – though they eventually won that match on penalties in the Nations League.
Croatia's last win against Spain did come in this competition, winning 3-2 back in November 2018.
And Slaven Bilic is confident Spain are not unbeatable if Croatia can get their game plan right.
"Spain has some strengths that can be exploited, as England showed," Bilic said.
"We don't need a miracle; we need faith. We've played great matches against them. Matches are long.
"Against the Czechs, there were moments when we didn't know how to suffer. We can't repeat that. We know they'll have possession, but it can't always be theirs.
"We must have confidence in what we do, in ourselves."

1lfheoj9g7zqo1aqnm34c53qdf.title: Nico: Newcastle move the best decision I could have ever made
1lfheoj9g7zqo1aqnm34c53qdf.subtitle: Nico Gonzalez has made a strong start to life at Newcastle United, a move he said was the right call in order to progress his career.
paragraphs: Nico Gonzalez believes his move to Newcastle United this summer was the best decision he could have ever made after enjoying a strong start to life at St. James' Park.
Nico put pen to paper on a long-term contract in August for a reported £52m after spending just 18 months with fellow Premier League side Manchester City.
The 24-year-old made 59 appearances for City in all competitions, with 40 of those being starts, scoring four goals before being found surplus to requirements.
Newcastle signed the Spaniard after both Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes departed for big-money fees to Tottenham and Arsenal, respectively.
And Nico has wasted little time in getting used to his new surroundings, ranking sixth in Newcastle's squad for successful passes (155) despite only playing four matches.

He has played a crucial role in Newcastle's Premier League campaign under new boss Matthias Jaissle so far this season, and Nico revealed the atmosphere he experienced as an away player at St. James' was a part of his decision.
"Those moments [the unveiling] were in the middle of so many different emotions," Gonzalez said in an interview with Sky Sports.
"Leaving City, coming here and feeling that, was the best decision I could have ever made."
Jaissle's eight points are the most by a manager in his first five Premier League games in charge of Newcastle since Alan Pardew in January 2011 (nine).
A win against Coventry City next Monday would give him the most points in his first six in charge of the club in the competition (11) since Sam Allardyce in September 2007 (11).
During his time under Pep Guardiola, Nico ranked fourth in City's squad for tackles won (56), successful passes (2,908) and duels won (212).

However, he failed to nail down a starting spot, and with the additions of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi this summer, Nico acknowledged it was time to move on and pursue another challenge away from the Etihad Stadium.
"It was a huge opportunity for me," Gonzalez added.
"I was obviously at a top, top club in Manchester City, but I think Newcastle have been amazing the last few years and have even more potential, so I think we are a top team.
"The best thing is not about being in the best club; it's about enjoying football and being the best that you can, and helping the team.
"I was looking at my options and Newcastle was the best one."

1lhhkqjeaiov718lgf8gkvoahl.title: Horvath urges Red Bulls to carry momentum into D.C. United clash
1lhhkqjeaiov718lgf8gkvoahl.subtitle: The New York Red Bulls will look to make it four wins from five MLS games when they travel to D.C. United on Wednesday.
paragraphs: New York Red Bulls goalkeeper Ethan Horvath believes his side are hitting form at the right time, but he has urged them to take their momentum into Wednesday's clash with D.C. United.
The Red Bulls are now just one point off seventh-place Orlando City in the Eastern Conference after thrashing San Diego FC 4-1 at the weekend.
Julian Hall, Devin Padelford, Jorge Ruvalcaba and Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting all scored for Michael Bradley's side, while Horvath also saved a penalty in the first half.
While Horvath praised the performance of his team-mates during that win, he acknowledged they cannot slow down now, with six regular-season games to go.
"We're coming into form at the right time, and before the game we said we had seven finals, one down," Horvath said, reflecting on the win against San Diego.
"It was a great performance from the team."
"We'll come back in and already be prepared for D.C.
"We'll probably look back on the stuff we did well, but I think the message is we need to continue the momentum forward, and going into D.C. We have nothing to be afraid of.
"It's all in our hands and all in our control."
D.C., on the other hand, were thrashed 4-0 by Inter Miami last time out, after braces from both Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez.
They are 12th in the East, but only six points off the playoff places ahead of the run-in.
D.C. United – Kimito Nono
D.C. defender Nono scored twice in a 3-3 draw with the Vancouver Whitecaps last time out, and he impressed in their heavy defeat against Miami.
He recorded a team-high four shots while also creating two chances and winning six of his eight duels.
New York Red Bulls – Julian Hall
Hall is NYRB's top scorer in the league this season, with 11 goals, and he also netted against San Diego in his first game back after representing the United States during the international break.
He recorded a match-high seven shots against San Diego, hitting the target six times, and also created two chances for his team-mates.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
The Red Bulls have won three of their previous five MLS games (L2); only the Philadelphia Union (15), Nashville SC (10) and Charlotte FC (10) have won more points over that run.
D.C., meanwhile, are winless in their last four MLS outings (D2 L2) since defeating the Columbus Crew in early September.
However, the last three meetings between D.C. and the Red Bulls have been split evenly, with one win each and one draw.
The draw came earlier in this season, when the points were shared after an eight-goal thriller at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
New York Red Bulls – 31.8%

1lpj2mnveie9d1et5ep4f97pyt.title: McTominay returns to Napoli training following heart procedure
1lpj2mnveie9d1et5ep4f97pyt.subtitle: Scott McTominay underwent a procedure to correct an issue with his heartbeat last month, but he is now available again for Napoli.
paragraphs: Napoli have confirmed Scott McTominay is back in team training and available for selection after undergoing a minor heart procedure.
At the end of August, the Partenopei announced McTominay had been diagnosed with a "mild benign arrhythmia" that would require surgery and sideline him until the international break.

He subsequently missed four games for his club – three in Serie A and a 1-0 defeat to Arsenal in the Champions League – and was left out of Scotland's squad for their opening four Nations League fixtures.
Scotland earned four points in his absence, with their only victory thus far under Sebastien Pocognoli coming away to North Macedonia (2-0).

McTominay's club face a packed schedule before the next international break in November, with Saturday's meeting with Frosinone kickstarting a run of nine matches in just over four weeks, both domestically and in Europe.
But the midfielder will be available for selection, after Napoli released a positive update on his condition on Wednesday.
They said: "Today, Scott McTominay underwent further diagnostic tests, which confirm his fitness for competitive activity.
"Therefore, the Azzurri player has resumed training with the group after a period of personalised work on the pitch."

Scotland earned four points in his absence, with their only victory thus far under Sebastien Pocognoli coming away to North Macedonia (2-0).

1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.title: Amorim vows not to repeat Man Utd errors with Milan
1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.subtitle: AC Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A under Ruben Amorim rolled on, and he intends to continue allowing his team to play with freedom.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insists he will not be pushed into making the same tactical mistakes he made during his stint with Manchester United, now he is in charge of AC Milan.
Amorim's unbeaten start in Serie A continued on Sunday with a comfortable 3-0 win against Lecce at San Siro, with the result moving Milan up to fifth in the standings.
Christian Pulisic's sensational touch and finish put Milan ahead early on, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira sealed the win for the Rossoneri during a dominant second half.
Milan's victory saw them remain unbeaten in their opening five Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23 (W3 D2).

Amorim (W3 D2) has become only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to not taste defeat in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.

Speaking after the game, Amorim revealed he allowed his side to play with "freedom", and when asked about the reasoning behind that decision, he highlighted his turbulent tenure at Old Trafford, where he was reluctant to adapt his style of play.
"It's an observation of the games and the characteristics," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, I listen to the players, but a manager, especially in a big team, is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every player wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.
"It's always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.
"Sometimes we don't have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don't have them, we have to adapt. I think today worked.
"In another game, we can return to the build-up with three [at the back]. The important thing is to have different ways of playing.

"That's especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lose the reference to what we want to do, it's harder for them to understand their mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams."

Milan have now won their first two home Serie A matches of a season while keeping a clean sheet in both for the first time since 2020-21, when they beat Bologna 2-0 and Spezia 3-0 under Stefano Pioli.

Their dominance was backed up by the underlying metrics, too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.93 from their 10 attempts, while also restricting Lecce to a measly xG total of 0.17 from six shots.
It was a much-needed victory heading into the international break, with Milan coming into the clash with Lecce without a win in three matches in all competitions (D2 L1).
Roma, Inter and Lazio are the early pace setters in the division, all sitting two points clear of Milan, and Amorim feels his team are on the right track.
"If you look at the way we play, Roma and Inter had more time as a team, you can see the patterns are there," Amorim added.
"We didn't lose so many points, we dropped two to Lazio and Juventus away, so not everything is bad.

"Sometimes it looks like that, especially after recent results, but we have to see the balance. We won today against a good team that is doing well, but it is a different team, and sometimes we will have issues.
"It's a process, I think we should have more points, as against Juventus we weren't playing so well, but we were 30 seconds off getting three points.
"Even against Lazio, if you look at the balance of the game, I feel we deserved a little bit more."

1lu3j4v1qrslc1gaorn93bvper.title: Aston Villa 6-0 Fenerbahce: Jackson and Barkley at the double in record win
1lu3j4v1qrslc1gaorn93bvper.subtitle: Aston Villa registered their first victory on home soil in 2026-27 after they brushed aside Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.
paragraphs: Aston Villa recorded their biggest-ever win in European competition as Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley scored twice in a 6-0 rout of Fenerbahce in the Champions League.
Johan Manzambi marked his Champions League debut with a goal before two goals in eight minutes from Jackson had Unai Emery's side cruising heading into the break.
Barkley followed up his 68th-minute penalty with another goal moments later, with substitute Tammy Abraham adding further gloss to the scoreline in the 90th minute.
The hosts started brightly as Barkley headed over following a clever corner routine before Ibrahim Mbaye cut inside and forced Ederson into making a comfortable save.

But Villa had their goal in the 12th minute. Another short corner saw John McGinn's cross headed only as far as Manzambi, who took a touch before seeing his shot towards goal deflect off Milan Skriniar and wrong-foot Ederson.

Fenerbahce did, however, respond well to going behind, but were met with two fine stops by Zion Suzuki. Vedat Muriqi was denied in quick succession by the Villa goalkeeper, first seeing his header saved at the near post before seeing his effort on the slide repelled.

And Emery's team doubled their advantage through Jackson, who moments after seeing his deflected shot saved by Ederson, picked out the bottom-right corner with a brilliant finish just after the half-hour mark.
Oguz Aydin then thundered against the crossbar, but Villa pulled further clear six minutes before half-time, with Jackson doubling up with an arrowed strike into the same corner.
The hosts continued where they left off in the second half, with McGinn and Mbaye calling Ederson into action before Matty Cash's deflected drive rippled the side-netting.

Mbaye was denied again by Ederson, but Villa were awarded a penalty when Manzambi was chopped down inside the area by Ismail Yuksek, with Barkley stepping up and sending the Fenerbahce goalkeeper the wrong way.
And it got even better for Emery's side four minutes later as Barkley swept home his second, with his shot deflecting off Bartug Elmaz and nestling into the bottom-right corner.

Suzuki preserved his clean sheet late on when he tipped over Aydin's attempt from a tight angle, with Villa scoring their sixth late on when Abraham tucked home after good work from Alysson to conclude a record-breaking encounter.
Jackson hitting his stride as birthday boy Manzambi impresses

After a summer of change at Villa Park, the loss of Ollie Watkins looked like the biggest miss in Emery's ranks at the start of the season, but Jackson proved once again he is more than a capable replacement with another fine individual performance.

Jackson became the first player to score in as many as four of his first five Champions League starts since Sebastien Haller in December 2021 (all five), while he now has five goals and two assists across just five starts in the competition.

He now has five goals in eight appearances across all competitions for Villa, but another summer arrival in Manzambi has also made a strong start. The Switzerland international has two goals and two assists in three starts for the Villans.

Not many will remember what they did when they turned 21, but Manzambi's special day will certainly live long in the memory. He is just the second player to score on their Champions League debut on his birthday, alongside Spartak Moscow's Romulo against Barcelona in September 2012 (22).

Barkley also scored twice in a game for the first time since January 2023 for Nice against Montpellier in Ligue 1, though he was forced off in the 83rd minute with an injury, with Leon Goretzka coming on to make his Villa debut.

The result also marked Villa's first home win in all competitions this season, and they thoroughly deserved their victory. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 3.07 from their 20 shots to Fenerbahce's tally of 1.9 from their 15 attempts.

1lwu8z1y7q941lefppyop1gx6.title: Van Dijk: Gravenberch red card changed the game against Man City
1lwu8z1y7q941lefppyop1gx6.subtitle: Liverpool were brushed aside 3-0 by Manchester City, with all three goals coming after Ryan Gravenberch's 62nd-minute dismissal.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk conceded Liverpool's 3-0 loss to Manchester City turned on Ryan Gravenberch's second-half red card.
Gravenberch was sent off for a second-bookable offence in the 62nd minute, having been penalised for a clumsy challenge on the back of Jeremy Doku.
City, playing for the first time since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations, scored twice in the following six minutes, through Erling Haaland and Doku.
A stunning Rayan Cherki goal then finished off a flowing team move to cap the victory and deal Liverpool their first loss under Andoni Iraola.

This was the Reds' joint-biggest defeat at Anfield in the Premier League after 4-1 losses to Chelsea (October 2005) and City (February 2021), and 3-0 defeats to West Ham (August 2015) and Nottingham Forest (November 2025).
Liverpool have also now gone winless in five successive home games in the competition (D4 L1) for the fourth time, and the first since March 2021 (eight).
And Van Dijk said that the momentum of the game shifted when Liverpool went down to 10 men, as they had been strong up until that point.
"The first half was good from us," Van Dijk told Sky Sports. "We showed our intensity; could've done better on occasions where we got on the break.
"They weren't massive chances, but we showed we wanted to win, and we had intensity, which is the bare minimum.

"Second half, the red card changed the game, especially when you concede quickly afterwards. We end up with 10 men is the fact, and we concede quickly after, and it becomes a difficult game against them again.

"I think the atmosphere is always good here; I've been fortunate to play in a lot of big games here. For other players, maybe it was different, but for me, I was ready to compete, and I think we showed that, especially in the first half."
Iraola suffered his first Premier League defeat in 24 games (W10 D13) since losing 3-2 against Arsenal when he was in charge of Bournemouth back in January.
He has lost five times to City in the competition, his joint-most defeats to a single club (also five against Liverpool).
The Reds are also winless in eight Premier League games when facing the team starting the day top of the league (D6 L2), their second-worst run behind nine matches (2002 to 2008).
"I think it's obvious. We've played two games," Iraola told Sky Sports.
"One game until the 60th minute, and then another game after the red card. We were the best team in the first game, and then they were better.

"The first one [Gravenberch booking] is not a yellow. [Elliot] Anderson carries on a couple of steps; he wasn't even going to give a foul. I've no idea why he gives a yellow card. We have like nine players behind the ball.

"It's already difficult to press them when it's 11 v 11, but with one less, it becomes a different game, and then we concede straight away before making a substitution. You have to play differently when you're 1-0 down."
Liverpool were without three key players in Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai ahead of a busy run of fixtures in all competitions.
However, Iraola played down worries that they would be sidelined for a lengthy spell.
"They are not too big injuries, but we travel to Austria in two days [to face LASK in the Champions League]," Iraola added.
"It will be difficult; they are ready for the next one."

1lx18c2cvb8nj115lnfxwv3im8.title: Sage prepared to become a 'better coach' after difficult spell with Palace
1lx18c2cvb8nj115lnfxwv3im8.subtitle: Crystal Palace won in the EFL Cup in midweek, but they want to carry that momentum into the Premier League against a resurgent Tottenham.
paragraphs: Pierre Sage believes the adversity he is currently facing at Crystal Palace could make him a better coach, as they look to get back to winning ways in the Premier League against Tottenham.
Sage is under a lot of pressure after a poor start to the season, which sees Palace sitting 17th in the league table with only seven points to their name.

They have lost their last two matches in the competition without scoring – 5-0 v Brighton and 2-0 v Newcastle United – but they earned a reprieve in midweek, with a 1-0 victory over Fulham to reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals.

Sage is now hoping to build some momentum in the Premier League, likening this game against Spurs to a “final” after that win over Fulham, and he believes they will come out stronger after their tough run.
"Maybe you will think my answer is crazy, but I think it's an opportunity for me to become a better coach," he told Sky Sports.
"Faced with the difficulty, the problem, you have to find a solution I didn't anticipate. It's an opportunity to challenge my ideas, my way of doing [things], some adaptation...

"I know the most important thing is the results. We need to change things to become the team we're able to be. I have to take the good decisions at the good moment in this period because the player needs [me to].
"This situation is maybe a positive opportunity for me. Every day I want to improve and become a better coach and help the players and team to become better too."
Spurs, meanwhile, are on a different trajectory. After failing to win their first six games of the season, they have since beaten Coventry City and Chelsea to move up to 14th.
They are boosted by the news that James Maddison, who went down unchallenged against Chelsea, will be fit to play against Palace.

But Spurs' recent upturn in form has also coincided with the return of Dejan Kulusevski, who spent over a year on the sidelines – 526 days – with a knee injury that he suffered against Palace in 2024-25.
"I know I can compete, and I know that because I put in the work," Kulusevski told SpursPlay about managing the injury.
"I am not afraid because I put in the work for one year, so I know I will be ready to play, and the knee is strong.

"Roberto, I know from before because he is a very special manager, so when he came here, it feels also like it is special. I am so happy to have him and the staff because they are different, and I like to work with different people."
Tottenham – Mathys Tel
Six of Spurs' eight Premier League goals this season have been scored in the final 15 minutes of games, the joint most of any side, with Mathys Tel the latest to net a late goal.
Against Chelsea, he scored in the 87th minute, having had just two shots overall, though he led the team for touches in the opposition box (11) and chances created (two).
Crystal Palace – Jorgen Strand Larsen
Jorgen Strand Larsen has scored three goals in four Premier League appearances against Tottenham.
With those three goals, he has netted the equaliser (once) or the winning goal (twice) for his teams.
MATCH PREDICTION: TOTTENHAM WIN
Tottenham have lost their last two home Premier League matches against Palace, having won nine on the spin beforehand between 2015-16 and 2023-24.
And Palace have three wins in their last four Premier League games against Spurs (L1), only one fewer than in their first 30 against them in the competition (W4 D7 L19).

But recent form means momentum is behind Spurs at the moment, as they have won their last two Premier League matches, only one fewer than they had won in their previous 26 (W3 D10 L13). They last won three in a row back in February 2025.

Spurs' last two Premier League games have been wins against Coventry and Chelsea. The last side to win three in a row against sides all beginning with the same letter was Burnley in March/April 2018 against West Ham, West Brom and Watford.
Palace have shipped 19 Premier League goals this season, more than any other side and their most at this stage of a league season since 1980-81 in the top-flight (22).
Crystal Palace – 22.6%

1lyznjcm6iqlr11syu5k2369w9.title: Leverkusen striker Schick eases injury concerns after Europa League win
1lyznjcm6iqlr11syu5k2369w9.subtitle: Patrik Schick was substituted on, scored two penalties and was then taken off in Bayer Leverkusen's Europa League win over Lech Poznan.
paragraphs: Patrik Schick has eased any worries about a potential injury after an eventful display in Bayer Leverkusen's Europa League win over Lech Poznan.
Leverkusen won 4-0 at Enea Stadion, moving them up to second in the league phase standings after matchday two, behind Juventus only on goals scored.
It was a bizarre outing for Schick, who was introduced in the 18th minute after an injury to Martin Terrier, and then scored two penalties before being substituted off in the 76th minute.

Schick is only the second player in UEFA's main competitions since the 1992-93 season who entered the match as a substitute and converted two penalties – the first being David McMillan in the Rapid Wien v Dundalk match in November 2020.
Overall, it was a comfortable victory for Carles Martinez's side, who also saw Ibrahim Maza and Malik Tillman get on the scoresheet.
Leverkusen accumulated 5.34 expected goals (xG) from their 22 attempts, eight of which were Opta-defined big chances, while restricting their opponents to 0.46 xG.
There were worries Schick had also been taken off through injury, but the Czech striker confirmed that was not the case.
"I told him [Martinez] at halftime that I felt good and that he didn't need to worry," said Schick, who has scored eight goals in as many games this season.
"But he didn't want to take any risks. I wanted to score the third goal, but everything's fine."
Leverkusen have won 16 of their last 18 Europa League group stage matches (D1 L1), winning the last eight in a row since a 1-0 defeat to Ferencvaros in December 2021.
However, they could now be without Terrier for the foreseeable future, much to the regret of Martinez.
"We are sad, we sympathise with Martin. Everyone loves him because he is a wonderful guy. We have to wait and see what happened," said the Leverkusen boss.

1m5k3wp04gc0812b2kci0ogg83.title: 'The football-loving world always stops to watch' – Mourinho on global impact of El Clasico
1m5k3wp04gc0812b2kci0ogg83.subtitle: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has hailed the global reach of El Clasico, believing it to be the most unique derby in world football.
paragraphs: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has hailed the global appeal of El Clasico, insisting that "the football-loving world always stops to watch" when his side face Barcelona.
Mourinho's side travel to Camp Nou on Sunday for a crucial clash at the top of LaLiga, with leaders Barcelona currently holding a six-point advantage over their rivals.
Los Blancos head into the contest on the back of consecutive league victories, having also secured an emphatic 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig last Wednesday.
Mourinho, meanwhile, is unbeaten in his last five meetings with Barcelona across all competitions as Madrid manager (W3 D2).
Only two Real Madrid managers have previously gone unbeaten in six or more consecutive Clasicos: Miguel Munoz between 1962 and 1965 (seven wins) and Vicente del Bosque between 2001 and 2003 (W2 D5).
"Real Madrid-Barcelona means at least two Clasicos per season, sometimes more," Mourinho told reporters.
"It doesn't matter much who the coaches are; the most important thing is the global dimension of a Clasico, which is unique.
"There are other important derbies in the world of football, but this one is unique, and usually, the football-loving world stops to watch it. Let it be a great match and may we win."
While Mourinho expectedly remains confident of a Madrid victory, it is actually Barcelona who have gotten the better of their rivals of late.

Hansi Flick's side have won their last two home league meetings with Madrid, though they have only managed three consecutive victories in this fixture once in the 21st century, under Pep Guardiola between 2008 and 2010.
When asked whether Sunday's Clasico would be a test to see if his side can win titles, Mourinho was characteristically candid, adding: "No. Madrid with Mourinho wins titles.
"I feel that Real Madrid is like that. But I only seek to give credit to my players when they do well and accept criticism as a coach when we do less well.
"That's the history, not only of Real Madrid but of practically all coaches in the world. Players win matches, and coaches lose them; that's a bit of our life."

1m6hibefmoqwp1de6sqjxg9vq1.title: 'It means everything' – Robertson marks 100th Scotland cap with victory
1m6hibefmoqwp1de6sqjxg9vq1.subtitle: Andy Robertson was beaming after winning his 100th Scotland cap, though he was disappointed not to mark the occasion with a goal.
paragraphs: Andy Robertson was proud to mark his 100th Scotland appearance with a victory, as Saturday's 2-0 win over North Macedonia got the Sebastien Pocognoli era up and running.

Following a goalless draw with Slovenia and a chastening 3-0 loss at home to Switzerland, Scotland finally got their first victory in the 2026-27 Nations League, with Kieron Bowie and John McGinn on target in Skopje.
Bowie's first international goal was a brilliant effort in the seventh minute, as he spun Mario Mladenovski then found the bottom-right corner from outside the area.

McGinn made it 2-0 from the penalty spot in the 69th minute, with Bojan Miovski deemed to have committed handball during a goalmouth scramble in which Scott McKenna – who was later sent off – headed against the post.
While it was an occasion to remember for Pocognoli, Robertson also celebrated a landmark moment, becoming only the second player to win 100 caps for Scotland, after Kenny Dalglish (102).

Dalglish's 30 international goals remain the joint-most by any Scotland player, alongside Denis Law, and Robertson – who only has four goals for his country – joked he had a chance of matching that figure after being heavily involved as an attacking outlet.
Having never previously had four shots in a game for Scotland, Robertson managed that figure in the opening 13 minutes, with Stole Dimitrievski making one wonderful save to keep the left-back out.
"It means everything to me, and it means everything to my family," Robertson told BBC Scotland afterwards.
"I've been away now 100 times; I've got to feel sorry for my wife! It's been an unbelievable journey. I remember my first game, and it's been a process since then.
"It's emotional for me. I love this country, there's only one person before me in the men's game to do that, so it's a pretty special achievement.
"I thought Kenny Dalglish was going to be worried about his goalscoring record in the first few minutes! I had about six shots!
"They did a nice presentation for me; I told them I wanted the win. The lads did so well to get the win, it'll be a special one for me and my family."
McGinn, meanwhile, said Scotland could not afford to rest on their laurels ahead of hosting Slovenia on Tuesday, as he praised Pocognoli's efforts to build a new identity.
"The most important thing tonight was a win and a clean sheet," McGinn said. "When results go against you, things are said about you both personally and as a team, it's part of football.
"We deserve the praise that comes tonight. It was not an easy game, but we handled it well.
"The manager has brought a lot of ideas, a lot of identity, and it's up to us to buy into it. It's up to us to keep believing in what he wants to do and bring our qualities to the pitch.
"Tuesday's going to be a difficult game, but we've got to back this up with another win."

1m6x2tv7cuzb8124782eqrhq29.title: 'Business as usual' for PSG despite Kvaratskhelia injury
1m6x2tv7cuzb8124782eqrhq29.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain overcame Barcelona 4-2 in the Champions League, but they suffered several injury blows.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique says it is "business as usual" for Paris Saint-Germain, despite Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's serious injury.
Kvaratskhelia faces a long spell out after he suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona in the Champions League.
Ousmane Dembele was also a casualty in that win, with last year's Ballon d'Or winner now expected to miss several weeks. Marquinhos also sustained an issue against Barca.
PSG host Lyon in a top-of-the-table clash on Monday, with the clash pushed back a day due to ongoing protests in the French capital.
However, Luis Enrique insisted PSG will not be altering how they approach games due to their absences.
"It will be business as usual. I don't want to change anything I've done, but I also want to change," Luis Enrique told reporters.
"That's what you have to do to remain unpredictable. It depends on the team and the time of year.
"It's true that losing three players in the same game is strange. It's a motivation for us as a team. We're moving on to improve."
Asked about Kvaratskhelia's state of mind, Luis Enrique said: "It's a tough injury. You think about the player, what he's going to go through. It's difficult, but you have to stay positive.

"When you're a professional player and you want to have a 10-15 year career, you have to have injuries. You have to try to find positive things, and there will be some. He is and will be very important for us.

"It's a risk to be a professional player. You have to accept the positive and negative things, that's life. You have to overcome this to show what kind of player he is. We'll see after the operation. He'll come back stronger, I have no doubt."
Lyon, the current league leaders, have 14 points from seven Ligue 1 matches this season.
This is the joint-fewest points total for a leader at this stage in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95), level with Lyon and Paris SG in 1999-00, Nice in 2002-03, and Monaco in 2023-24.
With Kvaratskhelia and Doue absent, there will be more onus on Desire Doue to lead PSG's attack, though the youngster is certainly capable of that.
Doue scored against Barca in midweek, and has now been involved in 16 goals in his last 16 Champions League games.
Morton leads Ligue 1 this season for throughballs (eight), ahead of Doue (five).
He has created four chances, too, though the former Liverpool man is yet to provide an assist or score this term.
MATCH PREDICTION: PSG WIN

PSG are the favourites according to Opta's model, but they have lost three of their last six home games against Lyon in Ligue 1 (W3), as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 30 such encounters (W18 D9).
The two-time European champions have conceded at least one goal in their last seven Ligue 1 matches against Lyon (10 conceded), their longest current run against a single opponent.
Lyon are top of Ligue 1 at such an advanced stage of the season for the first time since the end of MD19 in 2020-21. PSG were also second behind Lyon at that point.
PSG have scored in their last 52 home Ligue 1 matches (132 goals), since a 0-0 draw against Lorient in Luis Enrique's first game in charge in August 2023.
They could equal the longest such run in the last 50 years, set by Monaco between September 2015 and April 2018 (53).

1m7u2ylj8dna310vc5ci3kpfis.title: Vanney hopes St. Louis defeat 'lights a fire' in LA Galaxy players
1m7u2ylj8dna310vc5ci3kpfis.subtitle: The LA Galaxy are aiming to return to winning ways in the MLS when they face the Portland Timbers at Dignity Health Sports Park.
paragraphs: Greg Vanney said there was "anger and disappointment" in his LA Galaxy players after being thumped by St. Louis City SC, and he wants his team to respond quickly.
The Galaxy were beaten 6-2 at Energizer Park, with Carlo Holse's 21-minute hat-trick proving too much for the visitors to bounce back from.
St. Louis' extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to 20 matches, while the Galaxy's hopes of reaching the playoffs remain in the balance.
Vanney's side are ninth in the Western Conference and three points ahead of 10th-place Portland Timbers, who are their next opponents in the MLS in midweek.
And while Vanney said the defeat was not the end of the world because of other results, he was determined to see his team bounce back to get their season back on track.
"I feel like [this game] lights a fire under some people and under the group. That was the emotion that I went into in the locker room," Vanney said.
"There was certainly anger and disappointment, but I also felt a recognition that there's a big week still ahead of us.
"Those games are going to be at home, and they are what our focus is on. I feel like there will be a good bounce back. It’s important that everybody bounces back.
"I just have to keep an eye on maybe a couple of guys, but in general, I think the group is going to be resilient and excited to be back at home in front of the crowd.

"We didn't make up ground on the teams in front of us, and we didn't separate ourselves from the teams behind us. In not doing so, we didn't lose a lot of ground on what's behind us, but we know the importance of what’s in front of us now, games wise."
Portland, meanwhile, come into their latest clash off the back of a 3-3 draw with struggling Sporting Kansas City SC, with the Timbers failing to capitalise twice on a two-goal lead.
David da Costa and Vincent Janssen had put Portland two goals up by the 49th minute, but Andre Luiz ensured Sporting KC only went in one goal behind at the break.
Ariel Lassiter restored the Timbers' two-goal advantage just after the hour, but two quickfire goals from Justin Reynolds and Luiz ensured a share of the spoils at Sporting Park.
Portland are now without a win in their last five league matches, and Marti Cifuentes urged his team to be more creative in the final third moving forward.
"There was a sense of frustration, but obviously we need to move on quickly and learn from it, but we definitely lost an opportunity to take all three points," Cifuentes conceded.
"I think there are positives we can take from the game, particularly in the first half until the moment we conceded the penalty. It was a good first half in many areas of the game.
"But we definitely need to create more chances with the possession we had. With everything considered, it was a good away performance."
LA Galaxy – Joao Klauss
Klauss has scored in three straight matches, equalling the longest run of his career, a mark he set at the start of this season.
He is the third player in the last 10 seasons with multiple three-match scoring streaks in a single season for LA Galaxy along with Riqui Puig (2024) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic (2019).
Portland Timbers – David da Costa
Da Costa scored his ninth goal for Portland last time out to go along with 15 assists. His 24 goal contributions are more than any other player since joining the club at the start of last season.
Of Da Costa's nine goals, six have come in sets of back-to-back games, including his last two, and he will be hoping to continue that run here.
MATCH PREDICTION: LA GALAXY WIN

Portland snapped a five-match road winless run against LA Galaxy (D2 L3) with a 4-2 victory in April 2025. It was the Timbers' fourth win in 19 all-time visits to Dignity Health Sports Park and the first since 2020. Portland have never won two in a row at the Galaxy.

The Timbers have, however, won only two of their last 22 away matches in all competitions dating back to August 2025 (D6 L14). They have also conceded at least one goal in 20 straight games away from home, allowing two or more goals in 13 of their last 16 on the road.
The Galaxy, meanwhile, are unbeaten in five straight home matches (W3 D2).
They have not had a longer single-season unbeaten run at home in league play since finishing the 2024 season with six straight wins on their way to winning the MLS Cup.
Portland Timbers – 29.7%
