1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.title: Man Utd striker Sesko withdraws from Slovenia squad due to shin issue
1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.subtitle: A shin injury troubled Benjamin Sesko at the end of last season, and a flare-up of the issue has ruled him out of Slovenia's upcoming games.
paragraphs: Manchester United have confirmed striker Benjamin Sesko must undergo tests after withdrawing from the Slovenia squad with a shin injury.
Sesko was a notable absentee as United drew 1-1 with Fulham on Sunday, with Matheus Cunha's deflected strike salvaging a point for the Red Devils following Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal.
Having joined from RB Leipzig in a £74m deal last August, Sesko scored 12 goals in 32 appearances across all competitions last term.
That tally was only matched by Bryan Mbeumo among his Red Devils team-mates, despite 13 of Sesko's outings coming from the bench.
The 23-year-old missed the final few games of 2025-26, however, as well as United's entire pre-season campaign, with a shin problem.
Sesko has played six times for Michael Carrick's side this season, scoring twice, though he has only started twice – against Sabah in the Champions League and Brighton in the EFL Cup.
In the aftermath of last week's cup defeat to Brighton, Carrick revealed that the same issue was bothering Sesko again, and he has now withdrawn from Slovenia's squad.
Sesko was initially named in Bostjan Cesar's party for Nations League fixtures against Scotland – who they will face home and away – plus North Macedonia and Switzerland.
In a medical update released on Monday, United said: "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."
Sesko has almost three weeks of recovery time if he is to feature in United's next Premier League game, against bottom club Tottenham on October 10.
They also face Leeds United, Bournemouth and Chelsea in the league next month, having made their joint-worst start to a Premier League season through five matchdays (also five points in 2014-15).

1me87rszgt47j132u6ble521dv.title: Ballon d'Or will convince Kane to stay at Bayern, says Matthaus
1me87rszgt47j132u6ble521dv.subtitle: Harry Kane is reportedly close to agreeing a new Bayern Munich deal, which will be off the back of his first-time Ballon d'Or win.
paragraphs: Former World Cup winner Lothar Matthaus believes winning the Ballon d'Or will convince Harry Kane he must extend his current deal with Bayern Munich.
Kane became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the prestigious award on Monday, pipping Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal in the voting.
The striker has also been locked in contract negotiations with Bayern, and reports suggest they are close to agreeing a new deal.
And Matthaus is confident that Kane's latest accolade will only further convince him that he is in the right place at Bayern.
"We are ​very happy to have Harry Kane in the Bundesliga," Matthaus, the Ballon d'Or winner in 1990, said in an online media roundtable.
"He is an international ​ambassador of football.
"Maybe he was dreaming ​to win the Ballon d'Or, but you have to play in a ​big club like Bayern. He found his peace in Munich and the right club ‌with the ⁠right team-mates."
Last season, Kane helped Bayern to the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double before then leading England to third place in the World Cup – their best finish since winning the tournament in 1996.

He plundered a remarkable 73 goals for club and country in 2025-26, with the only other instance of a player from Europe's top five leagues scoring 70+ goals in a single campaign coming in 2011-12, when Lionel Messi netted 82 en route to one of his eight Ballon d'Or triumphs.

For Bayern, Kane scored 61 goals in all competitions in the 2025-26 season, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues. It was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15.
"I think he ​gets a bonus [for ⁠winning the Ballon d'Or]; 36 years ago, I got nothing," Matthaus added.
"But it is about more than money. It ​is a good moment to sign [a new deal] for Bayern. ​Bayern ⁠helped him get this Ballon d'Or.

"The relationship between Harry Kane and Bayern Munich is perfect, and with everything that has happened in the last three years, ⁠I think ​Harry will sign his contract for the ​next two, three years."

1mec37kyn0o9715yn7pvc661gg.title: Sorensen: Vancouver cannot 'flip a coin' against Chicago
1mec37kyn0o9715yn7pvc661gg.subtitle: Jesper Sorensen felt his Vancouver Whitecaps team played with too much risk in their 3-3 draw with D.C. United last time out in MLS.
paragraphs: The Vancouver Whitecaps must get away from "flipping a coin" after the "Wild West" nature of their recent fixtures, so says head coach Jesper Sorensen.
Vancouver sit top of the Western Conference in MLS, but drew 3-3 with D.C. United in their last outing.
The Whitecaps came from behind to lead, but then were pegged back before going ahead again through Thomas Muller.
However, Sorensen's team conceded another equaliser in the 80th minute, meaning they have now won just two of their last five league games.
And Sorensen wants his team to get back to a more composed, solid approach when they take on the Chicago Fire on Tuesday.
"We'll have some players out, they'll have some players out," he said.
"Let's see how it's going to play out. Normally, we'd have the same approach as to how we'd like to play.
"Hopefully we can play a much better connected and much less wild game. We have to be more in control and not be as open, and not have it be quite as like the Wild West.
"It was how we were playing the game and how we have played as of late.
"We conceded 10 corners, which is not usual for us. It's very unusual. We flipped a coin last time, and we usually don't do that. We have to get away from that again."
Chicago Fire - Johan Gomez
Gomez scored the only goal in Chicago’s win over Charlotte FC on September 26.

It marked the first regular-season goal scored by a Fire player other than Robert Lewandowski or Maren Haile-Selassie since August 19, after the pair had netted Chicago's previous nine league goals between them (excluding own goals).
Vancouver Whitecaps - Brian White
White has scored seven goals in his last seven MLS appearances, including scoring in each of his last four games.
This is the fifth time White has scored in at least four straight league games for the Whitecaps, including a club record-tying five-match run in 2025 (also Camilo Sanvezzo in 2013).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
The Whitecaps have won their last three regular-season away matches without conceding, the first time Vancouver have recorded three straight shutout wins on the road.
The only teams in MLS history to record four straight road shutout wins in a single season are LA Galaxy in 2010 and D.C. in 2007.
Chicago snapped a seven-match winless run in all competitions (D4 L3) with a 1-0 road victory over Charlotte FC last time out.
The Fire have gone three straight without a win at home (D1 L2) after failing to win only three of their previous 12 home matches (W9 D0 L3).
Chicago and Vancouver have alternated wins over the four meetings since 2020 with the Fire winning the last match, 3-1, on the road in March 2025.
The only time either team won consecutive meetings with the other was a pair of Whitecaps wins over the Fire in 2015 and 2016.
Vancouver Whitecaps - 37.7%

1mh1ibaer440p1qjfnhz9janks.title: Ronaldo's importance to Portugal should not be underestimated, insists Riemer
1mh1ibaer440p1qjfnhz9janks.subtitle: Brian Riemer's Denmark side host Portugal on Thursday in the Nations League, and he is wary of the threat posed by Cristiano Ronaldo.
paragraphs: Denmark boss Brian Riemer believes "it's a bit absurd" to suggest Portugal are better off without Cristiano Ronaldo.
Portugal lead their Nations League group ahead of their trip to Denmark on Thursday, having won against Wales and Norway to begin their title defence.
Ronaldo featured against Wales, seeing a goal chalked off, but was an unused substitute in Portugal's 2-1 victory over Norway last time out.
In his absence, starting strikers Goncalo Ramos and Joao Felix both scored for Jorge Jesus' side, with the head coach also insisting Ronaldo was left on the bench for tactical reasons.

Reports claimed Ronaldo's relationship with Jesus is now fractured, while some fans suggested Portugal are better off without their all-time leading scorer, but Riemer came to the 41-year-old's defence.
"I think it's a bit absurd to be discussing this in relation to Cristiano Ronaldo," Riemer told TV2 Sport.
"I believe that many people underestimate the importance he has in the Portuguese team. I even think that, the day he retires, Portugal will have a problem.
"There's something called hierarchy. There are many strong personalities in a team like Portugal. Who will make decisions and set the terms? It can be a big challenge.
"Definitely, you shouldn't underestimate Ronaldo's importance when he plays. Portugal's best team is with Ronaldo playing."
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 games under the command of Jesus for Al-Nassr in the 2025-26 campaign, at an average of one goal every 99 minutes.
Jesus revealed Ronaldo could be in for some minutes against Denmark, while Portugal also host Norway before the end of the extended international break.

1mmrog5woqf0y1nu0imp1vp39w.title: Bastoni: Inter 'need to deliver a significant response' in Champions League
1mmrog5woqf0y1nu0imp1vp39w.subtitle: Inter have lost both of their Champions League games this season, and Alessandro Bastoni believes they must now beat Shakhtar Donetsk.
paragraphs: Alessandro Bastoni has urged his Inter team-mates to "deliver a significant response" in their Champions League clash with Shakhtar Donetsk.
Inter have lost both of their league phase matches so far this season, going down 2-1 to Real Madrid and 4-3 to Club Brugge.

Cristian Chivu's side were beaten on home soil last time out in the Champions League, despite scoring three goals (v Brugge). That was the 86th time they had scored 3+ goals in a major European match, yet the first time they had gone on to lose.
Inter are currently on their longest-ever losing streak in the European Cup/Champions League (four matches).
They have lost seven of their last eight (W1), which is more than they did in their previous 41 in the competition combined (six), and Bastoni is desperate to provide a strong showing.
"We're forced to get a result, or it becomes impossible to get into the top eight," Bastoni said.
"We need to look more at reality. The finals and the journeys we've had in the Champions League in recent years are a thing of the past.
"The schedule and recent matches must bring us back down to earth. Starting against Shakhtar, we need to deliver a significant response.
"Intellectual honesty is needed from each of us. Looking at individual incidents, you see many individual errors."
Including qualifiers, Inter are unbeaten in their seven games against Shakhtar (W3 D4), while keeping six clean sheets (only one goal conceded).

Of fixtures played at least three times in the European Cup/Champions League, none have a lower goals-per-game ratio than matches played between Inter and Shakhtar (0.5 – two goals in four games, both scored by Inter).

The last win by a Ukrainian side against an Italian opponent in the Champions League was in October 2019 (Atalanta 1-2 Shakhtar) – since then, Ukrainian sides are winless in nine games (D4 L5) and failed to score a single goal.

1mpcxk69szwjt1pm8nhi5n4com.title: Manchester City 4-2 Arsenal: Hemp scores twice as comeback win keeps champions perfect
1mpcxk69szwjt1pm8nhi5n4com.subtitle: Manchester City twice fell behind to struggling Arsenal, but the Women's Super League champions recovered to win a six-goal thriller.
paragraphs: Manchester City twice came from behind to clinch a thrilling 4-2 victory over Arsenal and maintain their 100% record in the Women's Super League this season.

Lauren Hemp struck twice for the hosts at the Etihad Stadium, while Kerstin Casparij scored a brilliant goal with her first touch off the bench and Khadija Shaw added a late clincher, with Andree Jeglertz's team earning their fifth win in as many games.
Following a cagey start, Arsenal enjoyed a spell of pressure without truly testing Ayaka Yamashita, as Lotte Wubben-Moy headed wide.

City's first real opportunity saw Shaw shoot straight at Anneke Borbe, and though the Jamaica striker had the ball in the net in the 36th minute, her header was chalked out for a foul after she clattered the Arsenal goalkeeper in mid-air.

And, after Yamashita pulled off a fine save to thwart Emily Fox, Arsenal hit the front in the 43rd minute. Wubben-Moy nodded Alessia Russo's cross back into the danger zone, and following a touch from Yamashita, the ball deflected in off Lisa Baum's knee.
City were not even behind for four minutes, though, as in first-half stoppage time, Hemp saw her left-footed drive take a wicked deflection off Fox and spin past Borbe.

An injury to Mariona Caldentey represented another blow for Arsenal right before the interval, but they restored their advantage five minutes into the second half. City had already got away with one giveaway in a dangerous area before Yui Hasegawa lost possession to Russo, who curled a pinpoint finish into the far corner.
But once again, City came storming back as Casparij came off the bench in the 62nd minute and, just 65 seconds later, bent a beautiful first-time effort beyond Borbe.
All the momentum was with the hosts at that point, and after a big intervention from Leah Williamson kept Shaw out, Hemp showed great composure to collect Hasegawa's far-post delivery and slot home.
And City made the points safe with six minutes of the 90 left, as Aoba Fujino slipped a neat pass into Shaw, who wrong-footed Williamson with her first touch, then stroked home.
Perfect five for City as pressure mounts on Slegers

City have started a WSL campaign with five straight wins for the third time, having previously done so in their 2016 title-winning season (won first six) and repeated the trick in 2017-18 (won first seven).

Jeglertz's team have also won 15 straight home matches in the WSL dating back to last season, with only Chelsea ever enjoying a longer winning run on their own turf in the competition – a 22-game run from March 2022 to February 2024.
City's clinical finishing was the difference, as they hugely outperformed their tally of 0.92 expected goals (xG), which came from nine shots (five on target).
Renee Slegers' visitors had 16 shots and hit the target nine times, generating 1.59 xG, but seven saves from Yamashita – many of which were routine – helped City keep them at bay.

While City go into the WSL's international break two points clear of Chelsea at the summit, Arsenal – last season's runners-up – are already 10 points off the pace in 10th, only making a worse start to a WSL campaign in 2014 (four).

1mugrndf4tj9311xpaha3as3qv.title: Kane says England 'sent a message' with thumping win over Croatia
1mugrndf4tj9311xpaha3as3qv.subtitle: Harry Kane said England had set the standard for future tournament performances with their historic 7-0 thrashing of Croatia.
paragraphs: Harry Kane said England had sent out a resounding message to the rest of Europe by routing Croatia 7-0 on Saturday, also acknowledging the Three Lions need to adopt the same mentality at future tournaments.
Kane scored twice as the Three Lions ran riot in Rijeka, making it back-to-back Nations League victories following their opening 3-2 defeat to Spain.
Thomas Tuchel's side were utterly dominant as they put up an expected goals (xG) figure of 6.43 – the largest ever recorded in any Nations League game, in any tier.
Bukayo Saka also helped himself to a brace, with Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers getting England's other goals.

It was England's biggest ever win against a team in the top 50 of the FIFA World Rankings and the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history, and Kane said the scale of their accomplishment should not be underestimated.
"Even when we were 1-0 up, we went for two, went for three, went for four, and that's got to be our mentality," Kane said, as quoted by ESPN.
"When you have a certain style of playing, you can't just pick and choose when you want to do it. It's just relentless. It's non-stop.
"You get four, you want five. You go and have a hungry mentality. That's needed to change, especially in the bigger games, in the bigger tournaments, and these games will only help us.
"We were playing against a really good side. We can't take this type of win for granted because it could have been a really tricky game for us.
"And it's always about sending messages, not just to yourself, but to the other teams around Europe. I think we've done that again.

"We're hungry. We're a young team. We have players in amazing form right now, and I think everyone's just excited to be out there on the pitch. Performances like this will only make us more motivated."
Kane now has 11 goals for England in 2026, becoming the first player to ever reach double figures in three separate calendar years for the Three Lions (also 12 in 2019 and 16 in 2021).
Both he and Gordon have scored in three straight games for England, becoming the first pair of players to do so for them since Kane and Marcus Rashford in 2019.
England, whose last seven-goal victory came against North Macedonia in a Euro 2024 qualifier three years ago, welcome Czechia to Wembley for their final game of this international break on Tuesday.
Should Kane feature in that match, he will match legendary former goalkeeper Peter Shilton at the top of England's all-time appearance charts, with 125 caps.

"Even when we were 1-0 up, we went for two, went for three, went for four, and that's got to be our mentality," Kane said, as quoted by ESPN.

"When you have a certain style of playing, you can't just pick and choose when you want to do it. It's just relentless. It's non-stop.

"You get four, you want five. You go and have a hungry mentality. That's needed to change, especially in the bigger games, in the bigger tournaments, and these games will only help us.

"We were playing against a really good side. We can't take this type of win for granted because it could have been a really tricky game for us.

"And it's always about sending messages, not just to yourself, but to the other teams around Europe. I think we've done that again.

"We're hungry. We're a young team. We have players in amazing form right now, and I think everyone's just excited to be out there on the pitch. Performances like this will only make us more motivated."

Kane now has 11 goals for England in 2026, becoming the first player to ever reach double figures in three separate calendar years for the Three Lions (also 12 in 2019 and 16 in 2021).

Both he and Gordon have scored in three straight games for England, becoming the first pair of players to do so for them since Kane and Marcus Rashford in 2019.

England, whose last seven-goal victory came against North Macedonia in a Euro 2024 qualifier three years ago, welcome Czechia to Wembley for their final game of this international break on Tuesday.

Should Kane feature in that match, he will match legendary former goalkeeper Peter Shilton at the top of England's all-time appearance charts, with 125 caps.

1muk7ea3o972z15gjzre3t9mhj.title: Kane and Bayern 'fairly close' to agreeing new contract
1muk7ea3o972z15gjzre3t9mhj.subtitle: Harry Kane is keen to extend his stay at Bayern Munich and is in talks over a reported two-year extension with the Bundesliga giants.
paragraphs: Harry Kane hinted his Bayern Munich contract renewal is "fairly close" and could be announced soon.
Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham in August 2023 and has gone from strength to strength with the Bundesliga giants, winning two straight titles and a DFB-Pokal trophy.
He has also written his name into the Bundesliga history books this term, having netted his 100th and 101st goals in the competition last time out in a 7-0 hammering of Union Berlin.
Kane reached the 100-goal landmark in his 98th appearance, making him the quickest player to hit that tally, smashing Dieter Muller's previous record of 129 games.
Overall, the England captain has netted 152 goals in 154 appearances, and in 2025-26 alone, he scored a whopping 64 times in all competitions (including the Club World Cup).
Kane's current contract is due to run out at the end of this season, but a new deal – reportedly through to June 2029 – is in the works.
"We're in good talks. We're fairly close," Kane told The Independent.
"There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement."
Bayern are chasing a third straight Bundesliga title this term and are also among the favourites to clinch the Champions League.
They went into the international break second in the German top-flight, behind Borussia Dortmund, but Kane is excited to see what the team can achieve.
"I feel really comfortable in the team, with the coach, the environment," Kane added. "I want to just be at this level and push this level for as long as possible.
"Especially as you're getting a bit older, if you don't have a great season somewhere, or you don't play as well, the drop-off is maybe more than what it would have been when you're younger.
"So, it's just about extracting as much as I can, with the boss there, with the players I have in the team, I think they're getting the best out of me. I'm helping them as well."

1mvfxhn5xgc2r1o8n1vqojg0ul.title: Premier League predictions: Villa to test Man City and Maresca's perfect run
1mvfxhn5xgc2r1o8n1vqojg0ul.subtitle: Nobody has been able to take a Premier League point off Manchester City this season, with Aston Villa next to try their luck.
paragraphs: The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season.
With seven wins from seven, Manchester City sit top of the Premier League table and are the only team left in the competition yet to lose a game this term after their 3-2 win over Ipswich Town.

Everton were beaten by Chelsea, and Brentford suffered a late loss to Liverpool as their unbeaten starts came to an end, while there were also first wins of the campaign for Fulham, Bournemouth and Tottenham.

Reigning champions Arsenal edged past Nottingham Forest to stay three points behind City, and Brighton continue to impress after their 5-0 thrashing of Crystal Palace, but Michael Carrick and Manchester United are coming under increasing pressure.
But who can make moves up the table this weekend? Matchday 8 sees fixtures take place across Friday, Saturday and Sunday in another bumper weekend.
Ahead of what should be another exciting group of Premier League fixtures, let us check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.
IPSWICH TOWN V NOTTINGHAM FOREST
The action begins at Portman Road on Friday, as Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest look to get back to winning ways.

Forest have lost their last three Premier League games, more than they had in their previous 14 (W5 D7 L2), and have drawn a blank in four different matches this season, including last time out against Arsenal.

Ipswich won their first two Premier League games against Forest in the 1992-93 season, but they have since lost all four against them, though our predictive model suggests they will end that run, with a 43.2% win probability.
Forest, who have a 30.1% chance of victory, won 4-2 on their last visit to Ipswich in 2024-25, but have not won on consecutive league visits since 2010-11 and 2011-12 in the Championship.
At 26.7%, this is one of the most likely draws of the weekend, though, so a stalemate could be on the cards.
ASTON VILLA V MANCHESTER CITY

Onto Saturday, Aston Villa will be the next team to try to end Manchester City's perfect start, after Enzo Maresca made history last weekend by becoming the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a club.

City could become the eighth side to win each of their first eight games of an English top-flight season, after Everton in 1894-95 (first eight), Sheffield United in 1903-04 (eight), Tottenham in 1960-61 (11), Manchester United in 1985-86 (10), Liverpool in 1990-91 (eight), Chelsea in 2005-06 (nine), and Liverpool in 2019-20 (eight).
And with a 43.2% win probability, they are the most likely away winners of the weekend.

However, City – who thrashed AEK Athens 5-1 in the UEFA Champions League in midweek – have lost their last two league games against Villa, last losing three straight between August 1962 and September 1966.

Villa, whose win probability sits at 31.6%, are unbeaten in their last three home league games against sides starting top of the table (W2 D1), while they are in good form, having won two of their last three league games (D1) and beaten Viking 3-1 in the Champions League.
Arsenal will be waiting to pounce on any potential Man City slip-up, so they will be determined to walk away with three points against Everton.

Arsenal, who battled back to draw 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their European outing, won 69.6% of the supercomputer's simulations, making them the most likely winners of the weekend, and they are also unbeaten in their last seven league matches against Everton (W5 D2).

The Gunners have won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games (L1), winning all six at Emirates Stadium in that run, while their defensive record continues to impress; no side has conceded fewer league goals than them (five), while they have also faced fewer shots on target (21) and have a lower expected goals against figure (5.6 xGA) than any other side.
Everton were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea last time out to end their unbeaten start and are winless in their last eight away league games (D5 L3), with all three on the road this season ending level.

They have a 17.1% chance of claiming a point and a further 13.3% likelihood of winning, but have won one of their last 30 away Premier League matches against Arsenal (D5 L24), a 1-0 victory in 2020-21 under Carlo Ancelotti.
COVENTRY CITY V FULHAM
Alvaro Arbeloa's long wait for a league win is now over after Fulham (29.9%) beat Hull City last time out, with Coventry City (43.4%) next up for them.
This is just the third-ever top-flight meeting between the sides – they met in the 1967-68 season, with the Cottagers unbeaten in both fixtures (W1 D1).

The Cottagers are winless in their last eight away league games, alternating between a draw (four) and defeat (four) each time. They lost their last such match 2-1 to Ipswich, and at 26.7%, this is the other most likely stalemate of the weekend.

Coventry have lost five of their seven Premier League games this term (L2), their most defeats at this stage of a campaign since 1996-97 (also five). They avoided relegation on the final day of that season.
Saturday rounds off with Tottenham looking to build on their win over Coventry against Chelsea, who recorded their first clean sheet of the season against Everton.

The Blues are heavy favourites at 53.6% and have won each of their last six league matches against Spurs, their joint-longest winning league run against them (also six between January 2000 and March 2002).

Chelsea have only lost one of their last 16 London derbies in the league at Stamford Bridge, while Spurs have lost each of their last six derbies in the competition – they have never lost seven straight before.
Monday's victory was huge for Spurs, and it was just their fourth of 2026 in the Premier League. Since the start of last season, only twice have they won consecutive league matches.
They are given a 22.6% chance of victory against Chelsea (and a further 23.8% hope of clinching a draw), and have won on just one of their last 36 league visits to Stamford Bridge (D11 L24).
That was a 3-1 victory in 2017-18 under Mauricio Pochettino, and they have only picked up two points in eight visits since then (D2 L6).
CRYSTAL PALACE V NEWCASTLE UNITED
Both Crystal Palace and Newcastle United are looking to get back to winning ways at Selhurst Park, with Pierre Sage, in particular, feeling the pressure.
Palace were thumped 5-0 by Brighton last weekend, though they are favoured to pick up three points on Sunday, with a 40.5% win probability to Newcastle's 32.8%.

The Eagles are looking for consecutive league wins over Newcastle for the first time since a run of three between August 1971 and September 1972, and the Magpies have won on just one of their last 11 top-flight trips to Selhurst Park (D6 L4).
Palace have not had much home joy recently, but they are looking for back-to-back Premier League wins on home soil for the first time since April 2025 (three straight).

And that is coupled with Newcastle's away-day blues; they have lost 4-1 at both Leeds United and Coventry in their last two away Premier League games. Only between January and March 2008 have they lost more consecutive away games by at least three goals in the competition (four).
HULL CITY V BRENTFORD
Last weekend was disappointing for Brentford (38.1%), who suffered their first league defeat of the campaign and finished with nine men, but they will want to bounce back against Hull City (35.8%).
This is the first-ever top-flight meeting between Hull and Brentford, with the Bees seeking their first Premier League win in Yorkshire (D4 L1).
Hull are winless in their last five games (D3 L2) after starting the season with back-to-back wins, but they are also unbeaten at home in the league this term (W1 D2).

They will have hope of finding their next win even if they go behind, though, as Brentford have dropped 11 points from winning positions, the joint-second-most from a side's first seven matches of a campaign in the Premier League.
Keith Andrews' side will be looking to Igor Thiago to provide the attacking spark; he has six goals in his last six Premier League appearances against newly promoted clubs.

It has been a good week so far for Liverpool, who followed up that win over Brentford with a stunning comeback triumph over Villarreal in the Champions League, but they face another tough test against Brighton.

The Seagulls head into the weekend sitting third, having won each of their last four matches by an aggregate score of 15-0, and they have also won two of their last three Premier League matches against Liverpool (L1).
Despite that run, they are given a 26.8% win probability on Sunday – only marginally higher than the 26.4% chance of a draw – with Liverpool the outright favourites at 46.8%.

However, the Reds are winless in their last five home Premier League matches (D4 L1), only twice having worse runs at Anfield (seven – November 2002 to February 2003, and eight – December 2020 to March 2021).

Brighton's attack is sure to cause problems – they are the highest scorers with 23 goals – but Alexander Isak will be keen to test their defence, too. He has scored five goals in his last five Premier League appearances, as many as he scored in his previous 20 combined for Newcastle and Liverpool.
MANCHESTER UNITED V BOURNEMOUTH

Carrick is feeling the heat at Manchester United, and they are in desperate need of a Premier League victory when they host Bournemouth, who won for the first time in the league under Marco Rose last time out.

United have seven points from seven games this season (W1 D4 L2), their worst start to a league campaign since 1989-90 (also seven in seven). And things got even worse on Wednesday as they were thumped 4-1 by Como in the Champions League, extending their winless run across all competitions to seven games (D3 L4).
Things may not get any easier here; they are winless in six against the Cherries, who are unbeaten on their last three league visits to Old Trafford (W2 D1).
United are still backed to come out on top by the supercomputer (48.5%), with Bournemouth given a 25.7% chance of another away victory against the Red Devils.
Carrick's side have drawn their last three league games, their longest such run since five straight stalemates between September and October 1992 – there is a 25.8% chance of a draw on Sunday.
SUNDERLAND V LEEDS UNITED
The weekend finishes at the Stadium of Light as Sunderland and Leeds United both look to end their respective winless streaks.

Sunderland sit bottom of the table and have lost their last four Premier League games, last enduring a longer such run in December 2015 (four), and they are narrow favourites, winning 38.8% of the pre-match simulations.
In fact, they have won just four points in seven league games this season (W1 D1 L5), their lowest at this stage of a league season since 2016-17, when they were relegated.

As for Leeds, they have only lost on one of their last eight top-flight visits to Sunderland (W6 D1), going down 2-0 in November 2001, but they have never won a Premier League game in the 16:30 kick-off in eight attempts (D3 L5).

They are given a 34.7% chance of ending that run against Sunderland, but there is also a 26.5% chance of a draw – a result Leeds are increasingly familiar with, given they have drawn more Premier League games in 2026 than any other side (13), including a 1-1 stalemate with Man Utd last weekend.

1n3oglsinppb91dpewml0rdbez.title: The Numbers Game: Shaw and Hemp eye centuries as City favoured in Manchester derby
1n3oglsinppb91dpewml0rdbez.subtitle: Manchester United and Manchester City go head-to-head in the Women's Super League this weekend, with the visitors still perfect in 2026-27.
paragraphs: This weekend's action in the Women's Super League is headlined by the first Manchester derby of the season at the Progress with Unity Stadium on Sunday.
The recent international break did little to slow City's momentum as, after last week's 3-2 victory over Brighton, Andree Jeglertz's defending champions retain a 100% record.

They are two points clear of Chelsea at the top of the WSL, and though United are down in fifth, they have some wind in their sails after recovering from a slow start to Eva Olid's first campaign at the helm.
But who will claim the bragging rights? Here, we consult Opta insights to provide a data-powered preview for the standout clash of matchday seven.
What's expected?
The Opta supercomputer makes City favourites for Sunday's game, even with home advantage favouring United.
The champions are assigned a 47% chance of taking all three points, compared to United's 28.6% win probability. The remaining 24.4% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations finished level.
City won 3-0 both home and away against United in the WSL last season, so they could become the first team to win three straight Manchester derbies in the competition.
And United have only won one of their six home games against City in the competition overall (D3 L2), by a 2-1 scoreline in May 2023 with Lucia Garcia netting a 91st-minute winner.
Furthermore, across all games played between WSL's 'big four' since the start of last season, United have earned the fewest points (four – D4 L4).
City, meanwhile, have taken the most points from such matches, winning 15 (W5 D2) versus United, Arsenal and Chelsea in that time.
United showing signs of progress

A few short weeks ago, keeping City quiet would certainly have looked to be beyond United, who opened the campaign with one point from their first three games, as part of a seven-match winless run dating back to last season (D3 L4).
But Olid's side have turned things around with three straight victories in the competition, while they also earned a thrilling 5-3 success against Liverpool in the League Cup on Wednesday.
Ella Toone, Andrea Medina and Julia Zigiotti all scored in the first 31 minutes of their most recent WSL game, a 3-1 triumph over rock bottom Charlton.
And though the strength of the opposition should be taken into account, United have certainly shown signs of adapting to Olid's methods.
Against Charlton, United completed a whopping 700 passes with a pass accuracy of 88.7%, also boasting a 76.2% possession share.
Those were all record highs for them in a WSL game, while it was the most passes completed by any side in the competition since January 2025, when Arsenal tallied 707 against Crystal Palace.
Sunday's game should be an intriguing measure of how far United have come, as they go head-to-head with another team that looks to dominate possession whenever possible.

And Olid is unlikely to change a winning formula, as only Tottenham (four) have made fewer alterations to their starting line-ups in the WSL this season than the Red Devils (five) – City have made the most, with 18.
United could also name the same starting XI for four consecutive league games for the first time since 2021-22, when they did so for the first five matches of the campaign.
Deadly duo Shaw and Hemp in line for centuries
Although City came out on the right side of a five-goal thriller against Brighton last time out, that victory was far less straightforward than it might have been.

1n597582ko2a31k68ulkm4b2dd.title: Gakpo determined to enjoy life at Liverpool after 'difficult' transfer saga
1n597582ko2a31k68ulkm4b2dd.subtitle: It looked like Cody Gakpo's time at Liverpool was over this summer, but he never made his high-profile move to Manchester City.
paragraphs: Cody Gakpo revealed it was a "difficult summer" after his potential move to Manchester City from Liverpool fell through.
Gakpo had a turbulent summer after the World Cup, with his future at Anfield remaining up in the air for the majority of the transfer window.
He was initially linked with a move to Tottenham before it emerged in the final days of the window that City were interested in bringing him to the Etihad Stadium.
However, the deal fell through in the final hours of deadline day, with Gakpo ultimately staying at Liverpool.
"I don't know if you want to go into detail about that, but there's no point in talking about it," Gakpo told The Telegraph.
"It was a difficult summer for me, my family and everything to do with football and life. So yeah, I just let it happen, and it ended the way it ended.
"It's a very long story. The summer was very tough, on all fronts. I just let it all sink in and saw how it would go, and it went this way.
"Now it is what it is. I just want to enjoy my life with my family and friends. And from playing football with my team-mates here and at the club."
Gakpo has made a strong start to the 2026-27 season for Liverpool, making six appearances under Andoni Iraola so far.
He has already racked up six goal involvements in all competitions – two goals and four assists – more than any other player for the club.
His 13 chances created, meanwhile, are second only to Dominik Szoboszlai.
"When you play for a big club like Liverpool, you have to perform," Gakpo, who also scored for the Netherlands in their 1-1 draw with Germany on Thursday, added.
"I don't want to talk about others or other players, but I know I could have done much better myself than last year.
"I don't know if the criticism was unfair. Maybe it was, but in a way, I understand it.
"At Liverpool, you have to win, perform and show that you are one of the best clubs in the world. We didn't do that last year, including myself. That's just the way it goes."

1n5p1b2ytadf71qmyd7fy0h20a.title: Joao Felix wants to assist Ronaldo's 1,000th goal
1n5p1b2ytadf71qmyd7fy0h20a.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo is close to reaching the 1,000-goal mark, and Joao Felix wants to be the player to assist the historic goal.
paragraphs: Joao Felix revealed he has thought about being the player to assist Cristiano Ronaldo's 1,000th goal, claiming "the goal will go down in soccer history".
Ronaldo scored in Al-Nassr's win over Abha earlier this month, taking his career total to 979 goals for club and country.
While the 41-year-old hinted his international career could be over by the end of the season, it also remains to be seen whether his club career goes beyond 2026-27.
Joao Felix plays alongside Ronaldo for both Al-Nassr and Portugal, and the former Chelsea forward would be honoured to assist his team-mates' milestone goal.
"I've thought about that," Joao Felix told Diario AS when asked about assisting Ronaldo's 1,000th goal.
"When he's one goal away, every time I get the ball I'll look for him to see if I can give him the pass.
"That goal will go down in soccer history, and being part of it would be a great moment."
Joao Felix impressed in his debut season with Al-Nassr, scoring 20 goals and providing 13 assists to help his team end a seven-year wait to win the Saudi Pro League title.
The 26-year-old was named the league's player of the season, and he was delighted to see Ronaldo finally get his hands on the trophy.
"It's something few people in soccer can say they've done," added Joao Felix. "I got to do it with the national team, and now at Al Nassr.
"It's an honour, honestly. We grew up watching Cristiano. He was our idol, someone we looked up to, and now I get to share these moments with him.
"Winning the league last year was especially meaningful. Being able to help Cristiano win the title he had been chasing since he arrived.
"We have to enjoy it as much as we can because we know it won't last forever. But while he's here, we'll be here too."

1n7ltzyjftusn16tpxd8zfwyoo.title: Giroud: Leaving Arsenal was necessary for my career
1n7ltzyjftusn16tpxd8zfwyoo.subtitle: Olivier Giroud swapped Arsenal for Chelsea in 2018, with the Frenchman detailing why he had to leave Emirates Stadium.
paragraphs: Olivier Giroud explained it was necessary for him to leave Arsenal in order to boost his chances of making France's 2018 World Cup squad.
Giroud joined Arsenal on the back of propelling Montpellier to the Ligue 1 title in 2012.
He scored 105 goals in 253 games for the Gunners, but left in January 2018 to join Chelsea.
And Giroud, who is set for a reunion with Arsenal with Lille in the Champions League on Tuesday, said he ultimately had to make a ruthless call for the good of his career.
"It was part of my career and my time," he said.
"I had to leave the club in order to play the 2018 World Cup and we know the end of the story.
"I was really sad to leave the club but I had to make that choice and that was a tough one in my career but it was necessary and important for the rest of my career."
Giroud went on to play a key role in France's World Cup triumph in Russia.
He played 119 times for Chelsea, and scored 39 goals for the Blues, before spells at AC Milan, Los Angeles FC and now Lille.
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta played alongside Giroud, and he was effusive in his praise of the 40-year-old.
"Every time you had him on the pitch, you had a massive threat inside the box," Arteta said of Giroud.
"He was very smart. He was so good at connecting with other players as well and his work rate was phenomenal, so certainly not [underrated] by us."

1n8dk1du0hfgw1c1up4xns7nt3.title: Arteta: Arsenal's basics have to be through the roof to beat Fleetwood
1n8dk1du0hfgw1c1up4xns7nt3.subtitle: Mikel Arteta and Arsenal head to League Two Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup fourth round, aiming to avoid a major upset.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta says Arsenal's basics "must be through the roof" when they face Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup fourth round on Tuesday.
Arsenal and Fleetwood have never met before in any competition, with the League Two side winless in all five of their matches against top-flight opponents in their history (D1 L4).
The Gunners, who lost last season's final to Manchester City, beat Ipswich Town 4-2 in the third round to continue their run in the competition.

And they come into this game in fine form, extending their unbeaten streak to five games (W4 D1) in all competitions thanks to their 2-0 win over Everton, which took them level on points with Premier League leaders City.
But Arteta noted how important it is for Arsenal not to get complacent against lower-league opposition.
"Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play," Arteta said.

"So, every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve to do that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.
"We all have one [upset] at some stage.

"We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that's why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game."
This will be Arsenal's 10th tie in the EFL Cup against a side from the fourth tier of English football – they have progressed from eight of their previous nine.
The only exception was when they were knocked out by Bradford City in 2012-13 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in their most recent such game.

Fleetwood, meanwhile, are through to the fourth round of the competition for the first time, and while manager Matt Lawlor is expecting a tough test, he urged his players not to fear the Premier League champions.
"It is an amazing night for the club and an amazing night for the fans, the town and the area," he told BBC Radio Lancashire.
"We have sold out for the first time in 11 or 12 years, which is unbelievable, and it is an amazing thing to be a part of.
"We are glad that it is here, and we are glad that we are welcoming the best team in the country and the champions of last year – to Highbury.

"The champions are coming to town on our patch, and it's on telly, so if you can't get up for this game you can't get up for any game. The players need to be excited for it, but while respect is through the roof, the fear can't be."

1n951rauw9tjp1tda4hqne710p.title: Carvajal backs Vinicius to be 'unstoppable again very soon'
1n951rauw9tjp1tda4hqne710p.subtitle: Vinicius Junior has struggled for form at Real Madrid this season, but former team-mate Dani Carvajal still has high hopes for the winger.
paragraphs: Dani Carvajal has backed Vinicius Junior to be "unstoppable again very soon" after a poor start to the season with Real Madrid.
After signing a new six-year deal in the summer, Vinicius has scored just once and provided three assists in 11 appearances this season.
The 26-year-old is also currently halfway through serving a four-match ban in LaLiga after pulling Nathan Saliba's hair during Madrid's 1-0 win over Villarreal.
He missed their Clasico victory over Barcelona on Sunday, with Yan Diomande also emerging as a potential starter for Jose Mourinho's side.
Vinicius has been starting in Madrid's Champions League games during his league suspension, but many have called for the Brazilian to be dropped for Diomande.
Despite the criticism, Carvajal believes Vinicius will return to his best at some point this season.
"He's a fantastic person. He brings immense joy to the locker room," Carvajal told AS about Vinicius.
"And he's never hesitated to carry the team on his shoulders, to ask for the ball when matches were at their toughest, and that's something to be valued. A player who never hides.

"I think that objectively, right now, with the sending-off the other day, with the doubts about whether he should play or not... well, it's not a pleasant situation for absolutely anyone. But Vini has bounced back from more complex situations.
"He needs to stay calm; he just renewed his contract, he has years ahead of him, he's a spectacular player, and we're going to see that unstoppable Vini again very soon."
Madrid are third in LaLiga, three points behind leaders Barca following their 2-1 victory at Camp Nou at the weekend.
Los Blancos face three more away fixtures before the international break, travelling to Racing Santander and Valencia either side of a trip to Athens to face AEK in the Champions League.

1nb5y78qo6m7q11ywp0h3rq0hm.title: 'My time will come' – Yamal confident of future Ballon d'Or success
1nb5y78qo6m7q11ywp0h3rq0hm.subtitle: After missing out on the 2026 Ballon d'Or, Lamine Yamal is already looking forward to what he can achieve in the future.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal is confident he will get his hands on the Ballon d'Or one day, after placing third in the 2026 standings.
Yamal enjoyed a trophy-laden 2025-26 season, winning the LaLiga title with Barcelona before carrying his form into the World Cup and helping Spain lift the trophy.
However, he finished behind Bayern Munich's Harry Kane – the first Englishman to win the award since 2001 – and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe in the voting.
Yamal tallied 41 goal involvements across all competitions in 2025-26 (24 goals, 17 assists), with only five players from Europe's top five leagues managing more.

The teenager also attempted (429) and completed (225) more dribbles than any other player in that group, as well as ranking joint-sixth for chances created (118), with 59 of those coming after a carry – only Vinicius Junior (60) had more.

Yamal, who had talked up his chances of winning the Ballon d'Or, did not walk away from the ceremony empty-handed, winning the under-21 Kopa Trophy for the third straight year, but he remains focused on the top prize.
"It will come; good things take time. I trust in the path I'm building," Yamal wrote in a social media post.
"No rush, just excitement and the calm assurance that one day my time will come.
"Congratulations to the winners. My focus is back on what matters most: making FC Barcelona win again."
Yamal has hit the ground running in 2026-27 for Barcelona, with no LaLiga player bettering his 20 goal involvements (10 goals, 10 assists) across all competitions.
He tops the charts for assists (10) and chances created (45), while only Raphinha (15) and Mbappe (14) have netted more goals than him so far.

The teenager also attempted (429) and completed (225) more dribbles than any other player in that group, as well as ranking joint-sixth for chances created (118), with 59 of those coming after a carry – only Vinicius Junior (60) had more. 

Yamal, who had talked up his chances of winning the Ballon d'Or, did not walk away from the ceremony empty-handed, winning the under-21 Kopa Trophy for the third straight year, but he remains focused on the top prize.

"It will come; good things take time. I trust in the path I'm building," Yamal wrote in a social media post.

"No rush, just excitement and the calm assurance that one day my time will come.

"Congratulations to the winners. My focus is back on what matters most: making FC Barcelona win again."

Yamal has hit the ground running in 2026-27 for Barcelona, with no LaLiga player bettering his 20 goal involvements (10 goals, 10 assists) across all competitions.

He tops the charts for assists (10) and chances created (45), while only Raphinha (15) and Mbappe (14) have netted more goals than him so far.

1nfjc9v699vwq1hzjdoev5k7cb.title: 'We need to win' – Noonan wants no excuses against D.C. United
1nfjc9v699vwq1hzjdoev5k7cb.subtitle: FC Cincinnati are embroiled in a tight tussle for the wildcard slots in the Eastern Conference, as Decision Day approaches.
paragraphs: Pat Noonan labelled FC Cincinnati's clash with D.C. United as a must-win after their loss to the Columbus Crew.
Columbus clinched a 2-0 derby victory last time out, leaving Cincinnati in ninth place in MLS' Eastern Conference.
Cincinnati are one of seven teams separated by just six points, with D.C. also not out of the run-in for qualifying for the playoffs.
And Noonan is not looking for any excuses from his team ahead of Wednesday's contest.
"We have D.C. next, and that's the focus," he said after the loss to the Crew.
"How do we position ourselves for a better result?
"Right now, we can talk about stats all we want. We need to win. That's it. We need to win, however that looks, however that feels, we need to win games."
Cincinnati have won just one of their last nine league games.
D.C., on the other hand, have won only one in six.

"We don't need new ideas and strategies," Noonan added. "But if you look at how the games are being played right now structurally, chance creation, we still concede in almost every big moment that we concede or give up.
"I wouldn't say a lot drastically needs to change, other than winning the boxes. That's something that we haven't done.

"You still want to play the game the way we're playing it, but have a little bit more, I would say, game understanding of when you're playing with the league, when you're trailing, when I say urgency of how do we make the most out of specific moments in the game to change an outcome?

"Because there were enough there to finish off some plays, but as a game progresses and you're down, or you've been losing games and things aren't going your way, how do you approach that mentally to either cave or keep pushing."
FC Cincinnati – Evander
Evander has 13 goals and 10 assists in MLS this term.
The Brazilian playmaker ranks joint-sixth for MLS goal involvements in 2026, while his 78 chances created rank second in the competition, behind Carles Gil (81).
D.C. United – Tai Baribo
Baribo, who scored D.C.'s lone goal in their defeat to Orlando City SC on Saturday, has scored in 13 different matches this season, including each of the last two.
The only D.C. players to score in more matches in a single season since 2010 are Christian Benteke (15) in 2024 and Ola Kamara (14) in 2021.
MATCH PREDICTION: FC CINCINNATI WIN
Cincinnati are the favourites to take the three points, according to Opta's predictive model.

However, they have conceded 70 goals in MLS this term. It is the third time they have done so (75 in 2019, 74 in 2021), making them the only team in MLS history to have three seasons in which they have shipped at least 70 goals.
D.C. are winless in seven straight away matches (D4 L3). United have won just five of 32 away matches in all competitions since the start of the 2025 season, including two of 15 this year.
United recorded a 2-1 win last May in their last road match against Cincinnati.
In fact, they have just one loss in eight visits to Cincinnati (W4 D3). D.C.'s 1.88 points per match at Cincinnati is their highest points-per-match average on the road against any MLS opponent.
Cincinnati – 57.3%

1nslo4uxy8um91leizu2bmeb57.title: Gattuso confident Lazio can continue surprising people
1nslo4uxy8um91leizu2bmeb57.subtitle: Lazio are only behind Serie A leaders Inter on goal difference after their huge win over Juventus, and they could go top outright this week.
paragraphs: Gennaro Gattuso believes Lazio can sustain their surprise push at the top of Serie A if they take things one game at a time, following Sunday's eye-catching win over Juventus.

Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru were on target as the Biancocelesti claimed a statement 3-0 victory at the Allianz Stadium, a result that moved them back level with Inter at the top of Serie A.
It was just the third time in Lazio's Serie A history that they had beaten Juventus by at least three goals away from home, after 3-0 victories in March 1964 and May 1995.

With 19 points from seven matches in 2026-27, Lazio have made their best-ever start to a Serie A campaign at this stage, while Gattuso is the first coach in their history to win six of his first seven games in charge in the competition.
While the former Italy boss is not getting carried away with his team's flying start, he believes anything is possible if they stay focused.
"We must not look at the table right now. We'll enjoy this marvellous victory, but then it's heads down and back to work ahead of Parma," Gattuso told DAZN Italia.
"We're not accustomed to being up there, and maybe we're not ready to be there either, but if we take it one game at a time, we can surprise people.

"The mentality and hunger were important, as we went into half-time 1-0 up, and we ran risks in the games against Milan and Venezia, but this time, I think we took another step forward in terms of controlling the match.
"This is why I feel this is progress, because we are all or nothing; we don't yet have the maturity to control a lead.
"That is why we've always got to push with intensity, as that is what got us this win."

Lazio only had a modest €16m spend in their first transfer window under Gattuso, but the likes of Davide Frattesi and Josip Sutalo have become immediate contributors, and he feels the Biancocelesti did a good job of seeking out strong characters.
"It is the first time I've won here since I started this profession. My staff and I propose ideas, but it's the lads who put them into practice, so they deserve the credit," he said.
"We push hard in training, but we've created a real family unit here.

"The club also deserves compliments, as we had little money for the transfer market, but we went looking for good people who were determined, who wanted to come here at all costs. It took a while, we didn't have a lot of money, but it's easy for me to coach them."
Lazio are at home to Parma on Saturday, and with Inter not facing Fiorentina until the following day, a victory in that game would take Gattuso's men top of the table outright.

1o2557slkcbvs1hnp5z6fpwxsm.title: Neto completes Juventus return as Grabara replacement
1o2557slkcbvs1hnp5z6fpwxsm.subtitle: After Kamil Grabara was ruled out for the rest of the season through injury, Juventus have signed free agent Neto for the second time.
paragraphs: Juventus have announced the return of goalkeeper Neto on a free transfer following a season-ending injury to on-loan shot-stopper Kamil Grabara.
Neto has signed a contract until the end of the 2026-27 campaign and returns to Turin nine years after leaving for Valencia.
The 37-year-old's arrival comes after Grabara, who was on loan from Wolfsburg, sustained an anterior cruciate (ACL) injury just two days after making his debut for Juventus.
Grabara assisted Nico Gonzalez's opener during a 5-0 win over NEC in the Europa League, and he has since had successful surgery to repair the issue.
But having allowed Michele Di Gregorio and Mattia Perin to leave the club, Juventus have acted quickly to strengthen their goalkeeper options during the international break.
Neto played 22 times across all competitions during his previous stint from 2015 to 2017 with Juventus, keeping 12 clean sheets and winning five major honours.
Since his exit from Juventus nine years ago, he has gone on to represent Valencia, Barcelona, Bournemouth, Arsenal and most recently, Botafogo.
Juventus are seventh in Serie A after their first five games of the season, and they return to action after the international break against Cagliari on October 11.

1o4jczhxk81pz1bn475og0sugu.title: 'Selfishness isn’t part of his vocabulary' – Chivu lauds in-form Esposito
1o4jczhxk81pz1bn475og0sugu.subtitle: Inter cruised to a 3-0 victory over Parma in Serie A, with Francesco Pio Esposito the unsung hero for the reigning champions.
paragraphs: Inter head coach Cristian Chivu was full of praise for Francesco Pio Esposito after their Serie A victory over Parma on Saturday.
Petar Sucic, Hakan Calhanoglu and Marcus Thuram were all on target in a 3-0 win at San Siro, seeing Inter go top ahead of Roma's meeting with Como on Sunday.

Inter have won their first four home Serie A matches of a season for the third time in the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95), following 2005-06 (under Roberto Mancini) and 2017-18 (under Luciano Spalletti).
The Nerazzurri have also reached 16 points after their first six matches of a season for the fourth time in the 2000s, following 2002-03 (16), 2017-18 (16) and 2019-20 (18).
Esposito won the penalty, which was converted by Calhanoglu, and played a key role in the build-up to Thuram's goal.
He created a joint-team-high two chances while winning 100% of his duels (3/3), and Chivu lauded the Italian's unselfishness.
"His main characteristic is generosity. Selfishness isn't part of his vocabulary," Chivu told DAZN about Esposito.
"He works for the team, he works well, he counter-presses too, he reacted, and he was able to do certain things.
"When you lose the ball and go and win it back, you've also done excellent mental work.
"He has room to improve. He's a lad who works hard and puts himself at the group's disposal, and the group sees him as someone who will give us an important hand, as he has so far."
Chivu also expressed his delight over Inter's performance after the three-week international break.
"It was an unknown after three weeks off. That had never happened before, and we didn't know how it would go. But over these weeks the lads worked well," added Chivu.
"They had enthusiasm and were keen to do certain training sessions, and those who stayed here made their contribution.
"I’m happy with the energy, the quality we showed and how quickly we adapted to the opponent, because we didn’t have much information on how they might play.
"I gave minutes to those who were behind, and I'm happy to have rested those who gave a lot for their national teams."

1o7sh0fbei5sp1d7y32550j3qh.title: Gonzalez lauds Casemiro's impact on Miami defence
1o7sh0fbei5sp1d7y32550j3qh.subtitle: Inter Miami host New York City at Nu Stadium as they look to strengthen their grip on second place in MLS' Eastern Conference.
paragraphs: Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez lauded the impact of Casemiro after moving the Brazilian into the heart of Inter Miami's defence.
While Casemiro made a name for himself as one of Europe's best midfielders during his time with Real Madrid, he has been playing as a centre-back in recent games for Miami.
The Herons won 4-0 against D.C. United last time out after both Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez scored braces, but Casemiro controlled the match from his deeper position.
He recorded the most touches of any Miami player (101) and completed the most passes (80), while also winning both of his duels as they conceded just two shots on target.
The victory saw Miami end a five-game winless run in MLS (D4 L1), which had seen them drop out of contention for the Supporters' Shield.
Nevertheless, Gonzalez admires the way Casemiro has taken to his new role, praising the veteran for his confidence on the ball as the Herons prepare to host New York City.
"I have a lot of dialogue with them and the first thing I focus on is really believing in what they can become in these positions," said Gonzalez.
"They are not used to playing in these positions, but they are very well-prepared.
"For me, Casemiro is a player who gives me a lot of security defensively in ball distribution, in managing lines of cover and in communicating well with the rest of the midfielders.
"I see that he's getting more and more established, and he's one of my leaders in the locker room. He's very committed to us."
New York City lost 2-1 to the Chicago Fire last time out, despite taking the lead and seeing their opponents reduced to 10 men in the first half.
Since returning from the Leagues Cup group stage, only Minnesota United (six) and Real Salt Lake (five) have collected fewer points than NYCFC (seven – W1 D4 L5).
Inter Miami – Lionel Messi
Messi netted a brace on Saturday to extend his streak of regular-season games with a goal contribution to 10.
Since the beginning of May, Messi has been directly involved in 27 goals (16 goals, 11 assists) in 16 matches, more than 13 MLS teams have scored in that time.
New York City FC – Agustin Ojeda
Ojeda set up Hannes Wolf for New York City's only goal at Chicago on Saturday.
Ojeda has now assisted (primary or secondary) on six of the last eight goals scored by NYCFC players (excluding own goals) dating back to August 19.
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER MIAMI WIN

The Herons' win over D.C. was their ninth victory by four or more goals in regular-season play since the start of the 2024 season, two more than any other team in MLS in that time, though it was just the second such win for Miami this year (also 7-1 over CF Montreal).
After winning only one of their first 12 meetings in all competitions with NYCFC (D4 L7), Miami have won three straight in the series, including a 3-2 victory on March 22.
Miami have scored 12 goals over the last three games against NYCFC after scoring just 11 times in the first 12.
NYCFC have won only one of their last 12 matches in all competitions (D4 L7) dating back to early August, following a 2–1 defeat at Chicago on Saturday.
New York City FC – 21.1%

1okm5ph8gbk811jzul4cxsaeud.title: Portland great Chara confirms impending retirement
1okm5ph8gbk811jzul4cxsaeud.subtitle: Diego Chara has been with the Portland Timbers for over 15 years, but he will bring the curtain down on his career in 2027.
paragraphs: Portland Timbers stalwart Diego Chara has confirmed he will retire after the 2027 MLS Sprint Season.
With MLS' schedule set to change next year, there will be a shortened, 14-round regular season between February and April in 2027.
The playoffs will then take place in May, before the 2027-28 campaign starts later in the year.
However, Chara will bow out after Portland's Sprint Season is over.
Chara joined Portland ahead of their inaugural MLS campaign in 2011. He has played the most MLS games for the Timbers (450).
He has scored 13 goals and provided 38 assists for the Timbers in all competitions.

"The performances I had during the season give me that confidence as well [as] the support of my team-mates, coaching staff, by the club. That gives me the strength to continue," Chara said as he prepares for the run-in of what will now be his penultimate MLS campaign.
"It's going to be really good and I'm really happy to have the opportunity to be back for next year.
"Being for this long with the team, being one of the 'original Timbers,' I think is the best way to finish this career with the Timbers."
Chara's first game post-announcement comes on Wednesday, as the Timbers face St. Louis City SC.
After tying the longest regular-season unbeaten run in MLS history at 19 games, St. Louis City have lost two straight matches.
With three regular-season games remaining, the Timbers are still in playoff contention, while St. Louis City sit pretty in third place in the Western Conference.
St. Louis City - Rafael Navarro
Navarro has netted 18 MLS goals this season, and though St. Louis City's place in the playoffs is ensured, he will be eager to end the regular campaign on a high note.
Portland Timbers - Eric Izoita
Izoita assisted two of the Timbers' three goals in their win over Charlotte FC on Saturday.
At 19 years, 46 days old, Izoita became the youngest player in Timbers history to record multiple assists in a match, surpassing Cristhian Paredes' two assists at 19 years, 331 days in April 2018.
MATCH PREDICTION: ST. LOUIS CITY WIN
The seven regular-season meetings between St. Louis City and the Timbers have been split evenly, with each team winning twice (D3) and scoring 12 goals.
Both teams have recorded a home win and a road win over the other in league play.
The Timbers have won just two of their last 23 away matches in all competitions dating back to August 2025, with both wins coming on the west coast (at San Diego FC and the Seattle Sounders).
Portland have not won outside of the Pacific time zone since a 4–2 win at Sporting Kansas City on April 13, 2025.
St. Louis City - 53.1%
Portland Timbers - 25.3%

He has scored 13 goals and provided 38 assists for the Timbers in all competitions.

"The performances I had during the season give me that confidence as well [as] the support of my team-mates, coaching staff, by the club. That gives me the strength to continue," Chara said as he prepares for the run-in of what will now be his penultimate MLS campaign.

"It's going to be really good and I'm really happy to have the opportunity to be back for next year.

"Being for this long with the team, being one of the 'original Timbers,' I think is the best way to finish this career with the Timbers."

Chara's first game post-announcement comes on Wednesday, as the Timbers face St. Louis City SC.

After tying the longest regular-season unbeaten run in MLS history at 19 games, St. Louis City have lost two straight matches.

With three regular-season games remaining, the Timbers are still in playoff contention, while St. Louis City sit pretty in third place in the Western Conference.

PLAYERS TO WATCH

St. Louis City - Rafael Navarro

Navarro has netted 18 MLS goals this season, and though St. Louis City's place in the playoffs is ensured, he will be eager to end the regular campaign on a high note.

Portland Timbers - Eric Izoita 

Izoita assisted two of the Timbers' three goals in their win over Charlotte FC on Saturday.

At 19 years, 46 days old, Izoita became the youngest player in Timbers history to record multiple assists in a match, surpassing Cristhian Paredes' two assists at 19 years, 331 days in April 2018.

MATCH PREDICTION: ST. LOUIS CITY WIN

The seven regular-season meetings between St. Louis City and the Timbers have been split evenly, with each team winning twice (D3) and scoring 12 goals.

Both teams have recorded a home win and a road win over the other in league play.

The Timbers have won just two of their last 23 away matches in all competitions dating back to August 2025, with both wins coming on the west coast (at San Diego FC and the Seattle Sounders).

Portland have not won outside of the Pacific time zone since a 4–2 win at Sporting Kansas City on April 13, 2025.

OPTA WIN PROBABILITY

St. Louis City - 53.1%

Draw - 21.6%

Portland Timbers - 25.3%

1onnyw3xcm8ib1b1yektcapuix.title: Atletico Madrid 2-0 Manchester United: Simeone's side pile more misery on Carrick
1onnyw3xcm8ib1b1yektcapuix.subtitle: Atletico Madrid are up and running in the Champions League after Pablo Barrios and Ademola Lookman helped them beat Manchester United.
paragraphs: Atletico Madrid earned their first win in the Champions League this season after they brushed aside 10-man Manchester United 2-0.
The Metropolitano had something to cheer about in the first minute as Pablo Barrios broke the deadlock within 47 seconds, while Johnny Cardoso had a second goal disallowed before the break.
Though United tried to push for an equaliser, Leny Yoro's sending-off made it an uphill battle, and Ademola Lookman duly punished Michael Carrick's struggling side.

Atletico made a dream start as they cut open United's defence with minimum fuss and Alex Baena squared it to Barrios. His low shot sneaked in after a deflection off Ayden Heaven, with Senne Lammens unable to scramble back and keep it out.
Bryan Mbeumo had United's two best chances of the first half. His low drive was blocked, while Jan Oblak covered his near post well to smother his next tight-angled effort.
Atletico soon turned up the pressure again, though, as Alejandro Grimaldo curled a free-kick from 20 yards out against the corner of the goal frame.

And on the stroke of half-time, Cardoso thought he had doubled Atletico's lead by sweeping in Barrios' lay-off, but the goal was ruled out following a VAR review as Marcos Llorente handled the ball as he bundled it past Heaven in the build-up.

The woodwork denied Atletico again in the 54th minute as Julian Alvarez volleyed past a helpless Lammens against the post, while Bruno Fernandes fired wide and curled a looping effort off the top of the crossbar at the other end.

But United were given a mountain to climb in the 74th minute; Jonathan David was originally penalised for handling the ball before teeing up Lookman for a saved one-on-one shot, but Yoro was sent off following a VAR review for denying the Canadian a goalscoring opportunity moments before.
And it took Atletico just five minutes to use their numerical advantage. Grimaldo surged forward and picked out David, who was denied by Lammens, but Lookman reacted quickest to turn in the rebound.
United almost got a late consolation through Matheus Cunha after a poor clearance, but after Joshua Zirkzee teed him up, Oblak denied the former Atletico man with an outstretched leg.
Atletico make quick impacts as United's defence wobbles again
A disappointing draw with 10-man Tottenham at the weekend piled extra pressure on Carrick, who knew how important a morale-boosting victory would have been here.

But Atleti ensured the Red Devils made the worst possible start; United have now conceded in the opening minute of a Champions League game for the fourth time, while it was the hosts' second-earliest goal in the competition after Conor Gallagher against Real Madrid in March 2025 (27 seconds).
When Lookman came on, it took him just eight minutes to find an opening. In his six Champions League appearances as a substitute, he has been involved in four goals (three goals, one assist).
United are a favourite opponent for Atletico, however, as they have never lost to the Red Devils, with this being their fifth meeting (W3 D2).

It was a fairly even game, at least until Yoro became the third-youngest United player to be sent off in a Champions League game. Atleti had 11 shots worth 1.42 expected goals (xG), with five of those on target, while United racked up nine attempts worth 0.98 xG and tested Oblak four times.
They could not find a breakthrough, though, meaning Atletico have a precious clean sheet – just their second in their last 16 home Champions League games.

1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.title: Colwill expects Chelsea to be better after international break
1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.subtitle: Chelsea's strong start to the season fizzled out before the international break, but Levi Colwill is confident they can improve after it.
paragraphs: Levi Colwill has backed Chelsea to come out on the other side of the international break "flying".
Chelsea made a strong start to life under Xabi Alonso, winning four of their first five matches across all competitions (L1).

However, having had to come from behind to draw 2-2 with high-flying Hull City, the Blues were then thrashed 3-0 by Brentford in their final match before the extended international break to leave them winless in three league games.
Chelsea have already lost more Premier League matches in 2026 (11) than they did in the entirety of 2025 (10).

Alonso became only the sixth Premier League boss to see his side concede at least two goals in each of his first five games, after Mick McCarthy, Sammy Lee, Terry Connor, Slavisa Jokanovic, and Scott Parker.

And Chelsea's defensive woes have been highlighted on multiple occasions, even before Alonso's appointment; since the start of last season, they have conceded 23 Premier League goals from non-penalty set-pieces, now the joint-most of any side, along with Bournemouth.
Colwill admitted the start of the season was not what Chelsea expected, but he wants to use the extended international break to get back on track.
"[There have been] some good bits, some other not so good bits," he said, as quoted by Chelsea's website.
"Luckily, we've got a while now to try and improve.
"Hopefully, we will come out the other side flying, pick up our play, and become a better team."
Chelsea return to action at home to Bournemouth on October 10.

1ooo5sawiqft91hpmfscpu5ncb.title: 'We are not a low-block team' – Norway to take the game to Portugal
1ooo5sawiqft91hpmfscpu5ncb.subtitle: Norway suffered a 2-1 defeat against Portugal in the Nations League last week, with the two sides facing off again on Sunday.
paragraphs: Stale Solbakken insisted his Norway side "are not a low-block team" as they plan to play on the front foot against Portugal.
Norway have won just one of their three Nations League games during this break (L2), most recently losing 2-1 to Wales after Torbjorn Heggem was sent off early in the second half.
Their other defeat came against Portugal in the reverse fixture, with Jorge Jesus' side picking up a 2-1 win in Norway.
In that match, Norway won the expected goals (xG) battle 2.52 to 1.04, creating six Opta-defined big chances and retaining 62% of possession.
Solbakken acknowledged it could be harder to dominate away from home against Portugal, but he insists his players will not sit back at the Estadio Do Dragao.
"We are not a low-block team. Always with our heads up, looking for the goal. I think the players also feel that we can take the game to Portugal's goal," said Solbakken.
"I have great respect for Portugal. The team is in the top two or top three in Europe at the moment.

"Portugal presses very well, with high intensity, and we have to think differently. In the first game, we managed to play through the central corridor, but now I think they will have a different plan. We have to be able to adapt to the circumstances.
"It was probably one of the best games we've ever played, in the first 60 minutes against Portugal. Hopefully, we can repeat that.
"Now it might be different, because Portugal are playing at home, but we'll give our best and see how far we can go."

Norway have lost nine of their 12 matches against Portugal (75% – W1 D2), their third-highest loss percentage against all opponents they faced more than five times (83% against the USSR, 77% against Yugoslavia).
They have conceded at least twice in each of their last four games; the last time they saw their opponents score at least two times in five consecutive games was in 1975-1976 (six).

1or6s2qt4lt221k4i5blb8icwe.title: Olmo rejected Bayern twice, reveals Barcelona star's agent
1or6s2qt4lt221k4i5blb8icwe.subtitle: Dani Olmo has become an important player for both Barcelona and Spain over recent years, after twice rejecting Bayern Munich.
paragraphs: Dani Olmo twice rejected Bayern Munich before joining Barcelona, his agent has revealed.
Olmo joined Barca ahead of the 2024-25 campaign and has since scored 20 goals and provided 18 assists in 96 matches for the Blaugrana.
The Spain international has won two LaLiga titles, two Supercopas de Espana and one Copa del Rey since leaving RB Leipzig, while also winning the World Cup with La Roja this summer.
Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Olmo has directly contributed to the sixth-most goals among Barca players (38), while also creating the fourth-most chances (116).
Hansi Flick's side have made a perfect start to 2026-27, with Olmo providing three assists across their eight wins in all competitions.
Bayern tried to sign Olmo twice in the past, once before he joined Barca and the other while he was still at Dinamo Zagreb, though his agent believes it all worked out in the end.
"He rejected Bayern on my initiative when he was at Dinamo. I told him: you need to take another step, and that's what happened," Marc Bara told the Inkubator podcast.
"Later, he received another offer from Bayern as a Leipzig player, and Barcelona and other clubs were also interested.
"We chose Barcelona, which perhaps wasn't the best choice, but everything worked out for him afterwards.
"He won the European Championship, the Nations League, the World Cup, and is one of the ten best players in the national team.
"His story is like a movie, and I'm happy to have been part of it."

Barca will look to continue their perfect start when they host Getafe after the international break, while they will also face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga this month.
