1orntv1it6kfw1pms6c57qpqju.title: Bournemouth 3-0 Aston Villa: In-form visitors sink on the south coast
1orntv1it6kfw1pms6c57qpqju.subtitle: Amine Adli, Lewis Cook and Alvaro Rodriguez were on target as Bournemouth sealed their spot in the quarter-finals of the EFL Cup.
paragraphs: Bournemouth cruised into the quarter-finals of the EFL Cup following a commanding 3-0 victory over Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium.

Villa went into Wednesday's contest unbeaten in seven games, having won six of those, but they were no match for Marco Rose's in-form team, with goals from Amine Adli, Lewis Cook, and Alvaro Rodriguez doing the damage.

Bournemouth made a dream start through Adli, who capped off a superb team move involving a lovely combination between Marcus Tavernier and Julio Soler with a close-range finish into the roof of the net.
Ben Gannon-Doak came close to doubling the Cherries' lead 16 minutes in, taking a delightful touch before whipping a powerful shot on target that Marco Bizot tipped over the bar.
Bournemouth continued to threaten as Tavernier saw a bending effort bounce just wide of the left-hand post, before Adli rifled a half-volley high into the stands.
Villa returned from the break with plenty of intent, nearly levelling the scores through Ibrahim Mbaye, who caught Michele Di Gregorio wrong-footed but could not find the target.
But Bournemouth doubled their lead in fortuitous fashion in the 51st minute. Cook sent a cross into the box that Bizot completely misjudged, allowing the ball to beat him at his near post.

Unai Emery shuffled his cards on the hour mark with a slew of substitutions, though the damage had already been done, and Rodriguez put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute, latching onto Tyler Adams' pass before drilling a tidy left-footed finish into the bottom corner.
Alysson spurned a late chance to grab a consolation goal, sending his header wide off Alejandro Garnacho's bending cross.
Five on the spin as Cherries revel in sweet victory
Bournemouth not only have a place in the last eight to celebrate. They have also ended a frustrating run against fellow Premier League opposition in the EFL Cup.

They had previously been eliminated in each of their last four EFL matches against fellow Premier League sides, but they have now defeated a fellow Premier League side in the EFL Cup for the first time since a 4-1 home win over Everton in the third round in 2022-23.
And they did so in style, with Adli setting the tone by breaking the deadlock after just six minutes and 17 seconds.

They just had too much attacking quality for a much-changed Villa, generating 2.71 expected goals (xG) from 19 shots (seven on target), compared to the visitors' 1.65 xG from 17 attempts (five on target).
Bournemouth's winning streak now stands at five matches across all competitions, a run that includes successive 3-0 victories over AC Milan, Manchester United, and now Villa.

1owavihkg7f0z1vcvc08jmhq4e.title: 'They are the present and future' – Arbeloa hails Fulham's young core after Coventry win
1owavihkg7f0z1vcvc08jmhq4e.subtitle: Oscar Bobb scored his first Premier League goal of the season to inspire Fulham to a 1-0 win over Coventry City on Saturday.
paragraphs: Alvaro Arbeloa praised Fulham's young core following Saturday's victory over Coventry City, describing them as "the present and future of the club."
Fulham sealed a 1-0 victory at CBS Arena courtesy of Oscar Bobb's maiden Premier League goal of the season and for Fulham – a lovely 80th-minute, curling strike.
Clear-cut chances had been scarce before Bobb's breakthrough, though Josh King came closest when his powerful first-half strike crashed off the post.
The result marked Fulham's second victory of the season, following their 1-0 triumph over Hull City last time out.

It also signalled the first time they had won consecutive Premier League matches since March, when they beat Sunderland and Tottenham, while they last recorded back-to-back wins without conceding in December 2025.
"I'm so happy. Again, a very good game for us in a difficult stadium against a tough team," Arbeloa told Sky Sports.
"This is what we want: run, press, play our football and win games.
"We need goals from Oscar Bobb, Josh King and Gonzalo [Garcia]. They are young players and, obviously, as a coach, it could be easier to sign players with experience.
"Last season, Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez were there – players with 300 or 500 games in their legs and in their heads. Everything is easier when you have that experience.
"But these players are young and have the talent. I trust them because I think they are the present and the future of Fulham. I'm so happy and pleased with this young talent.
"We are working so hard every day. We are a team that need to give our best every day.
"We started preparing for this game at the beginning of the week, and I'm so happy with everybody. This is the way we have to play."
Following Saturday's win, Fulham ended a run of eight away games without a win, having alternated between a draw (four) and a loss (four) each time.
Moreover, Bobb ended a run of 29 Premier League appearances without a goal contribution, having last registered an assist in the league for Manchester City against Wolves in August 2025.
It also marked the Norwegian's second-ever goal in the league, with his first coming for City against Newcastle United in January 2024.
Coventry boss Frank Lampard, meanwhile, saw his losing run extended, as he has now won just three of his last 25 Premier League matches (D4 L18).
"They are a good team and there was not much in it with limited chances," Lampard told Sky Sports.
"That is the story of this league. The gap is what it is. Games like this come along. We want to win but if you can't, don't lose them.
"We were off our usual selves. We have to try and turn that."

1ozwcpqd6jbfw1jzlxdbbxe577.title: Chelsea 1-0 Austria Wien: Bompastor's side survive scare in Women's Champions League opener
1ozwcpqd6jbfw1jzlxdbbxe577.subtitle: Wieke Kaptein's early goal was enough for Chelsea to see off Austria Wien, but it was from a convincing display from Sonia Bompastor's side.
paragraphs: Chelsea began their Women's Champions League campaign with a nervy win as Wieke Kaptein's first-half stunner sealed a 1-0 victory over tournament debutants Austria Wien.
The Blues looked far from the team that reached the quarter-finals of the competition in 2025-26, but a moment of individual quality was enough to get them over the line.

Chelsea needed just 11 minutes to take the lead through Kaptein. Katharina Schiechtl's tackle on Melvine Malard saw the ball drop kindly to the midfielder, who took a touch before crashing her shot in off the crossbar from the edge of the box.
Sonia Bompastor was forced into making an early change as Keira Walsh left the field with an injury, but the Blues continued where they left off in their search for a second.
The lively Alyssa Thompson drilled a shot just wide of the left post following a driving run down the right, but Wien had their chances to level things up going into the break.
Virginia Kirchberger could only turn over after Modesta Uka's wicked delivery was spilled by Livia Peng before Louise Schoffel's effort whistled past the bottom-left corner.

Wien grew in confidence as the second half wore on as Uka's shot on the swivel was repelled by Peng, with the Chelsea goalkeeper then on hand to thwart Valentina Potzl after Veerle Buurman had played herself into trouble.

The visitors continued to get closer and closer to levelling things up, with Uka chopping inside before curling her attempt onto the post, but Wien were unable to find the equaliser their performance merited in the closing stages.
Chelsea ride their luck

Ahead of kick-off, Bompastor stressed the need for her Chelsea team to be more clinical, having stumbled to a 2-0 victory against Birmingham City in the Women's Super League last weekend, and once again her team looked vulnerable at both ends of the pitch.

In what was a historic match for Wien, becoming the fourth Austrian side to participate in the competition after Neulengbach, St. Polten and Sturm Graz, they announced their arrival on the European stage in some style, and were extremely unlucky not to leave with at least a point.

Uka was the particular standout for the visitors. She finished with team-high totals for shots (five), touches in the opposition box (seven), crosses (six) and attempted dribbles (three), while also coming within inches of scoring an equaliser in the second half.

The Blues were, however, able to hold on to begin their campaign with a win. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.43 from their 13 attempts compared to Wien's 0.87 from two more shots at Peng's net.
Bompastor will be hoping for improvements in the WSL this weekend, but things do not get any easier, with London rivals and two-time Champions League winners Arsenal their next opponents this Sunday.
Elsewhere, there was no such trouble for last year's runners-up Lyon, who thumped Servette 8-0, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring a hat-trick at Stade de Geneve.

Defending champions Barcelona also got their campaign up and running with a win. They came from a goal down to beat Paris FC 5-2, with Caroline Graham Hansen and Ewa Pajor starring in the turnaround. Roma, meanwhile, played out a 0-0 draw with OH Leuven.

1p2e8jc8dbwr3128fwj3b7kba5.title: 'I don't read papers or watch TV' – Amorim not fazed by Milan pressure
1p2e8jc8dbwr3128fwj3b7kba5.subtitle: Ruben Amorim is already feeling the heat seven games into his AC Milan tenure, but he was only focused about matters on the pitch.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insisted he was not feeling the pressure during his AC Milan tenure, but he acknowledged it was "impossible to have a lot of time" at a football club.
Amorim has had a mixed start to life in charge of Milan. They are unbeaten in their first six Serie A matches, though they have drawn three of their last four league outings.
The Rossoneri began their Europa League campaign with a 2-0 defeat at home to Benfica, with their next European clash seeing them make the trip to Salzburg on Thursday.
Milan have won nine of their 13 major European games against Austrian sides, with this their first since a 4-0 win against Salzburg in the Champions League in November 2022.
Amorim, however, has now lost each of his last two Europa League matches, as many as in his previous 21 games combined in the competition (W12 D7).
There is already growing pressure on the former Manchester United boss, but ahead of taking on Salzburg, Amorim remained focused on matters on the pitch.
"I don't read papers or watch TV, so that I can focus on my work," Amorim told Sky Italia as quoted by Football Italia.
"We are at the start of something. Obviously, we want to win more games and have more points. In regard to the rest, it's normal at a big club.
"Every project needs time, but nowadays with football media it is impossible to have a lot of time, so it is necessary to win games.
"I am not worried about that, I am focused on winning games, everything else that happens around that is not a concern."
Salzburg have never beaten Milan in four previous major European encounters, all in the Champions League (D1 L3).
It's the joint most they have faced a side without winning, along with Bayern Munich (D1 L3) and Inter (L4), but they did start their Europa League campaign with a win.
Danny Rohl's side won 1-0 against Levski Sofia on MD1, but they have not won consecutive major European games since October 2021, while they last did so with a clean sheet each time in October 2017.
And though they are competing in the Europa League after missing out on the Champions League last season, Amorim urged his players to treat the game as if it is the latter.
"It is always the Champions League, everything is important, every detail, every match is important and difficult," Amorim added.
"Salzburg are good technically, so we need to be strong on the runs, physically prepared and play our game."

1pb3eym1hal1u1kk8ido1epgg2.title: Arteta concedes Saka's injury 'doesn't look good at all'
1pb3eym1hal1u1kk8ido1epgg2.subtitle: Bukayo Saka went off injured early on in Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich, and he could face a spell on the sidelines.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta admitted Bukayo Saka's injury "doesn't look good", pointing to the packed calendar as a potential reason.
Arsenal came from behind to earn a late 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich, with Declan Rice scoring an 82nd-minute equaliser.
Eberechi Eze, Saka's replacement, had given the Gunners the lead before Harry Kane set up Alphonso Davies to level the score and then put Bayern in front from the penalty spot.
This was only the second time Arsenal have scored first, fallen behind, but then avoided defeat in a European Cup/Champions League match, and the other was also a 2-2 draw with Bayern in April 2024.
Despite the positive result, it was marred by Saka's exit in the 10th minute after he pulled up while trying to play a routine pass, and Arteta sounded pessimistic about the injury.
"They [the medical team] are a bit concerned," Arteta told TNT Sports.
"A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news, but we have to wait and see."

Asked in his press conference if the hectic schedule played its part, Arteta added: "Against Lille, he didn't start the game. Then he started the game at the weekend. And then it's very early in this game.

"The level of intensity these games require is something incredible. You could see what happened in the PSG-Barcelona game [on Tuesday]. This is man-to-man for 96 minutes. Every action. There's no breathing.
"The strength, the quality, the attention, the level that you need is unbelievable because it's the highest level.
"Those things happen, unfortunately. It doesn't look good at all, but we have to wait and see."

No Premier League side has had more goal contributions from substitutes in all competitions this season than Arsenal (five goals, four assists), with Eze scoring and Viktor Gyokeres assisting off the bench against Bayern.
But it was one of their starters, Rice, who had the decisive say as he netted his sixth Champions League goal, though this was his first away from home.
He has also been involved in five goals in his last eight games in all competitions (one goal, four assists).
"When you play against teams who are man-to-man all over the pitch, you have to apply certain principles," Rice told TNT Sports.

"They follow you all over the pitch, but I lost my man, and I just kept running and lost my runner, and then I was in on the goal. So happy. Gyokeres has been making such a good impact coming off the bench. He made some great runs and set me up for the goal.

"It is what the manager has drilled into us. We aren't just going to come here and sit. At home, they are probably one of the best teams in Europe, so to come here and give that account of ourselves was really good. We have to keep going."

1pciepkv6nb591bfa90trf5n6q.title: Mancini and Bastoni say Italy will not play like underdogs against France
1pciepkv6nb591bfa90trf5n6q.subtitle: Italy go to France for their third Nations League fixture on Friday, with Roberto Mancini pledging the Azzurri will push for three points.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini insists Italy will play to win against France, with defender Alessandro Bastoni revealing that boosting the Azzurri's confidence and self-esteem has been a key focus of their returning head coach.
Italy have registered one win and one defeat so far in the Nations League, losing 2-0 at home to Belgium in Mancini's first game at the helm since 2023, before winning 4-1 in Turkiye.
Their next assignment is a daunting one, though, as they head to the Stade de France to take on Zinedine Zidane's France side.

Les Bleus have maximum points on the board in Group A1, and Italy have only won three of their last 15 head-to-head meetings with France dating back to 1982 (two draws, 10 defeats), albeit they did overcome them on penalties in the 2006 World Cup final.
While 12 places now separate Italy (15th) and France (third) in the FIFA World Rankings, Mancini is refusing to adopt an underdog mentality.
"It will certainly be a great game against a top team, full of extraordinary players, but we always want to make a good impression and will do our best," Mancini said, as quoted by Football Italia.
"When you are up against such strong teams, you never play not to win, so naturally we must always play looking for the victory. After that, anything can happen."

Defender Bastoni scored Italy's opening goal against Turkiye, exorcising some of his demons from March's World Cup qualification play-off defeat to Bosnia-Herzegovina, when he was sent off shortly before half-time.

Given the negativity of the last few years, with Italy becoming the first former World Cup winners to miss three straight editions of the tournament, Bastoni says building self-belief must be a priority for Mancini and his staff.
"We are capable of having our say in a one-off match against anyone, but we also want to be consistent and make sure that Italy have an identity on the pitch," Bastoni said.
"Our standard has to be the one we saw in the most recent match.

"Everyone hopes to get results as soon as possible, but we must also recognise we're at the start of this process. After the game against with Turkiye, we need patience, as more tough moments will come.
"The coach is working on our self-esteem. In Italy, we're very good at moaning, feeling sorry for ourselves and focusing on all the negatives.
"But in my view, we should also learn to say when we have done something good. too. The more we say it, the more we'll start to believe it, so we've got to work on that.
"I've seen strong characters in the squad, they aren't afraid to try something new, and that touch is probably what we needed."

1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.title: Xavi promises 'intensity and passion' in new-look Netherlands approach
1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.subtitle: Xavi will take charge of the Netherlands for the first time this international break, and he is preparing his team for a new approach.
paragraphs: Xavi has promised to bring "intensity, passion and a good rhythm" to the Netherlands' play as he prepares to take charge for the first time.
The Spaniard was named as the Oranje's head coach on a four-year deal after Ronald Koeman left in the wake of a disappointing World Cup campaign over the summer.
While the Netherlands enjoyed an unbeaten group stage, they fell at the first hurdle in the knockouts, losing on penalties to Morocco.
Xavi, a former World Cup winner with Spain, will face Germany in his first game in charge in Amsterdam on Thursday, as the Netherlands kick off their Nations League campaign.

Koeman was criticised at times for taking a defensive approach with his tactics, and while Xavi did not give away too many hints about his approach, he outlined what he expects from his players on Monday.
"Everything is new ​for me and for the staff, so it will first be to get to know each other, ​know all the players, insist or convince them about our way to play," Xavi told reporters.
"We don't have too much time. But no excuses; every coach is in the same situation.

"I want to explain the values that ​we want from the squad. I want to show them that I'm open to them; I want ​to help them. I want to enjoy the process with them. We want to create a family; we want ‌to ⁠create a big group.
"The players must come to the national team with happiness, but at the end, the main goal is to win.

"You cannot promise results, but ​we will work ⁠for results. I can promise that we will play with intensity, with passion, with a good rhythm, trying to be competitive and trying to ​take the initiative in the game. This is for sure.
"There's going ​to be ⁠a different way of playing. I don't want to compare, and I don't want to talk about the past. I respect Ronald a lot. But I'm focused on the present."
Virgil van Dijk will remain the Netherlands' captain, having revealed on Sunday that he plans to keep representing his national team until Euro 2028.
"It ​was a really good meeting," Xavi said of meeting Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his Netherlands future.
"He was very honest. He has the capacity to continue. He's a good leader. He's positive, ​he's motivated. He's ready to be the leader."

1pdzulsuttus71jp3xska0i74k.title: 'It means everything' – Southampton boss Eckert revels in South Coast derby delight
1pdzulsuttus71jp3xska0i74k.subtitle: Tonda Eckert and Southampton were thrilled to put their off-field distractions to one side and claim bragging rights against Portsmouth.
paragraphs: Tonda Eckert says Southampton's victory over Portsmouth "means everything" after the Saints put their off-field distractions behind them to claim local bragging rights.
James Bree scored the only goal at St. Mary's Stadium, tucking away from Finn Azaz's cross in the 20th minute as the hosts came out on top in the South Coast derby.
That was despite Southampton playing the entire second half with 10 men, following Cameron Bragg's red card for a second bookable offence in the 44th minute.
Victory came at the end of a week in which Eckert received a suspended six-week ban from all football activity for his role in last season's 'Spygate' scandal.
"It means everything," the Saints boss told Sky Sports. "We had to dig deep, probably a lot deeper than we thought before the game. Credit to the boys because they deserve that.
"[The red card] did change the game, to be fair. Not on the scoreline, but the game changes then, and they needed to find different qualities.
"From there, we knew we had to defend, and I think we did that excellently. You probably look back at the end of the season and say this is the game that gave us a big push."
Meanwhile, Bree and Flynn Downes highlighted the importance of the victory, in spite of Eckert's punishment weighing "large on everyone".
"The news about the gaffer was positive for us," Bree said. "It just pushed us on this week, and we knew it was going to be a big game.
"It made it harder going down to 10 men, but we spoke all week about getting a clean sheet and digging in. The boys did that unbelievably."
"We've been desperate for a clean sheet and a win, and we've got both, so it's a good day at the office," Downes added.
"Everyone knows what it means to win a derby. Playing in these games is what you dream of as a kid, so to come out on the right side is always good.
"[Eckert's punishment] weighed large on everyone at the club. It's a clean slate now. We've got a fresh block of games, and hopefully we can carry on winning."
Southampton moved up to 11th in the Championship, having got back to winning ways after losing 2-1 to Wrexham before the international break.
Portsmouth, meanwhile, stay 19th after stretching their winless streak to three matches (D2 L1).

"It made it harder going down to 10 men, but we spoke all week about getting a clean sheet and digging in. The boys did that unbelievably."

"We've been desperate for a clean sheet and a win, and we've got both, so it's a good day at the office," Downes added.

"Everyone knows what it means to win a derby. Playing in these games is what you dream of as a kid, so to come out on the right side is always good.

"[Eckert's punishment] weighed large on everyone at the club. It's a clean slate now. We've got a fresh block of games, and hopefully we can carry on winning."

Southampton moved up to 11th in the Championship, having got back to winning ways after losing 2-1 to Wrexham before the international break.

Portsmouth, meanwhile, stay 19th after stretching their winless streak to three matches (D2 L1).

1pferb0aavbmk1p668syxtx3dj.title: Doue: Zidane told us we're on the right track
1pferb0aavbmk1p668syxtx3dj.subtitle: France were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy in the Nations League on Friday, though Zinedine Zidane took away plenty of positives.
paragraphs: Desire Doue agreed with Zinedine Zidane in believing France are "on the right track" despite dropping points in the Nations League against Italy.
In Zidane's first home match as France boss, Les Bleus were held to a 1-1 draw by Italy at the Stade de France.
Michael Olise opened the scoring with a stunning free-kick 10 minutes into the second half, but Alessandro Bastoni equalised after a costly mistake from Adrien Rabiot.
France failed to win a match after having opened the scoring for the first time since September 2024, when they lost 3-1 at home to Italy in the Nations League.
Dayot Upamecano also received a late red card after being shown a second yellow for dragging down Moise Kean.
He is the first player in the history of the France national team to receive two red cards in the same calendar year, after also being sent off against Brazil back in March.
Nevertheless, Doue took positives from the result, and so did Zidane.
"We're disappointed with the result; we would have liked to win in front of our fans," said the Paris Saint-Germain forward.
"We're not going to dwell on the negatives; we applied the coach's instructions in many aspects. We're on the right track, as he told us in the locker room.
"We're capable of creating a lot of danger; in the first half, they were very solid. We need to be more clinical; we came up against a great goalkeeper. But we stuck together."
Zidane added: "I'm very disappointed, we deserved better, but that's football. We should have killed the game off, but I'm proud of my players.
"The performance was very good, my players were exemplary. I'm frustrated for my players because they gave everything.
"We had possession in the first half but it was sterile, that's what we tried to correct at half-time. To hurt the opponent, you have to exploit the spaces.
"In terms of our play, we put things in place, they played their game, defensive, 'Italian style'. We weren't in too much danger."

1pfnsccuhtmfh1i3obd7wmxz2r.title: Bayern Munich 6-1 RB Leipzig: Diaz and Kane star to send Kompany's men top
1pfnsccuhtmfh1i3obd7wmxz2r.subtitle: Bayern Munich recorded another big win on home soil in the Bundesliga, brushing aside RB Leipzig with a six-goal showing.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich were back to their rampant best as Luis Diaz's hat-trick helped them to a 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig, which took them top of the Bundesliga.
Diaz also got an assist, while Harry Kane – on his 100th Bundesliga appearance – got a goal and set up two more, with Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise on the scoresheet as well.
Kane fired straight at Maarten Vandevoordt inside the first two minutes, and though Leipzig showed some threat immediately after, Bayern soon took charge.
Diaz got his first goal in the 12th minute, racing in behind to meet Joshua Kimmich's throughball and emphatically lashed home the opener.
Kimmich and Dayot Upamecano then tested Vandevoort as Bayern chased a second, which arrived in the 26th minute as Diaz picked out Pavlovic for a tight-angled drive.
Olise saw a shot tipped onto the post shortly after but got on the scoresheet 34 minutes in, with a low curler from the edge of the box after being picked out by Kane.

Diaz forced a smart stop out of Vandevoort before the break but got the better of the Belgian again 95 seconds into the second half, cutting inside from the left to curl a lovely strike into the bottom-right corner.
Kane kept pushing and finally got a goal to mark his landmark appearance in the 52nd minute, turning in from close range after it was put on a plate by Nathaniel Brown.
Leipzig struggled to deal with the pressure, and Diaz got Bayern's sixth in the 69th minute, whipping a stunning curler through the crowded box following a short corner.
The visitors had the final say, though, with their late surge turning into a 91st-minute goal when Andrija Maksimovic cannoned in off the underside of the crossbar.
Bayern shake off the cobwebs
It has been a mixed start to the 2026-27 campaign for Bayern, who have had big wins - 5-1 v Stuttgart and 7-0 v Union Berlin - as well as some questionable draws.
In the last week, they drew 2-2 with Augsburg and followed it up with a last-gasp draw against Viking in the Champions League, but they were back to their free-scoring best on Saturday.
Bayern registered 17 shots on target against Leipzig (29 attempts overall), their highest tally in a Bundesliga match since August 2022, when they managed 20 against Borussia Monchengladbach.
They are also the first team in Bundesliga history to score 18 goals in their opening three home games of a season, surpassing their own previous record of 17, set in the 2020-21 campaign.
Diaz was the star of the show, netting his second Bundesliga hat-trick and was directly involved in four goals in a single match in the competition for the first time.

As for Kane, he scored his 102nd Bundesliga goal, more than any other player has managed in their first 100 games in the competition, while his two assists also mean he has nine goal involvements this term (four goals, five assists).
But it was a demoralising result for Martin Demichelis' side, even with Vandevoort making 11 saves (a new record for a Leipzig goalkeeper in a single Bundesliga match).

1phhi2yl0vtbh1lt4r8oi37eie.title: Gasperini labels Slovan clash a must-win for Roma
1phhi2yl0vtbh1lt4r8oi37eie.subtitle: Roma are without a win in the Champions League this season, and their next match in the competition sees them face Slovan Bratislava.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini labelled Roma's Champions League tie with Slovan Bratislava as a must-win game if his team stand any chance of advancing from the league phase.
Roma welcome Slovan to the Stadio Olimpico on Tuesday in search of their first win in Europe this season, having taken just one point from their opening two fixtures.
After drawing with Fenerbahce on MD1, Roma endured a late collapse against Real Madrid, who came from three goals down to win 4-3 late on.

Gasperini's side have led in both of their Champions League games this season, but won neither (D1 L1), and they could be the first team to score first in each of their opening three matches of a campaign but go winless since Montpellier in 2012-13.

However, they are going up against a Slovan side that have conceded the most goals (nine), faced the most shots on target (22) and faced the joint-most shots (51) in the 2026-27 Champions League, currently finding themselves bottom of the 36-team standings.
For the last two seasons, 16 points have been enough to finish inside the top eight of the league phase, meaning Roma need to win five of their last six games to reach that total.
And while Roma are the favourites going into their latest European clash, Gasperini warned his players they must not underestimate their opponents.
"They're a dynamic team, well-prepared athletically, and they have some excellent players," Gasperini told reporters.
"They might not be 'top-tier' compared to some of the other teams in the Champions League, but like all games in this competition, it will be tough.
"We will not underestimate our opponents because we need to win. For the last few years, the points target has always been around 10 or 11.
"We have to win our games at home, it's always difficult in away games. That's our goal."
Roma beat Genoa 2-0 on Saturday, with Santiago Castro and Emanuele Lulli on target.
Donyell Malen missed that win through suspension, but the Dutchman will be back to face Slovan and hoping to continue his goal-scoring exploits in the Champions League.
Malen assisted against Fenerbahce before scoring twice against Madrid. However, no player has ever scored or assisted in each of Roma's opening three matches of a Champions League campaign.
And after Castro impressed during Malen's absence, Gasperini believes the pair could play together, but hinted he will choose one or the other to start against Slovan.
"[Castro] scored a great goal. He and Malen can play together with their characteristics, but I don’t know if I'll start him or bring him on during the game," the Roma boss said.
"I don't want to interrupt a team that is doing well in attack just so that we can see them together. I don't need to look for other solutions at the moment, but he could be one."
But one player who remains unavailable to Roma is Paulo Dybala, who continues his recovery from an injury sustained against Madrid last week.
Dybala has four assists in eight appearances across all competitions so far this season for Roma, but Gasperini confirmed he will remain sidelined for a few more weeks.
"I hoped Dybala would have recovered quicker. The tests he had yesterday showed a small injury, it will take a few more weeks," Gasperini conceded.

1pjypktw8wuvq13fli1eah6ssy.title: ​Brentford 1-2 Liverpool: Yarmoliuk and Janelt sent off as Isak scores winner
1pjypktw8wuvq13fli1eah6ssy.subtitle: Liverpool got back to winning ways in the Premier League on Saturday, as they took advantage of two Brentford red cards to win 2-1.
paragraphs: Yehor Yarmoliuk and Vitaly Janelt were both sent off for Brentford as Liverpool came from behind to win 2-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday.
Yarmoliuk saw red for thrusting his head into Jeremy Jacquet eight minutes into first-half stoppage time, shortly after Keane Lewis-Potter's thumping header had given the Bees the lead.

And that moment proved costly as Brentford suffered their first defeat of the Premier League season, with Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak – the latter on his return from injury – scoring to flip the game on its head.
The hosts caused Liverpool a few nervy moments even with 10 men, but Vitaly Janelt's second yellow card killed their hopes of an equaliser as the Reds leapfrogged them to go fifth in the table.

Jacquet made a strong block to thwart Michael Kayode from Brentford's first chance, but Liverpool should have scored on the counter from the resulting corner, with Bradley Barcola's lob drifting wide after Janelt's poor header gifted him possession.

Another excellent recovery challenge from Jacquet put Igor Thiago off after Dango Ouattara unselfishly attempted to square the ball for his team-mate, before Liverpool had a penalty overturned following a VAR review.
John Brooks pointed to the spot when Ouattara slid in on Alexis Mac Allister, but replays showed the Brentford man flicked the ball away with his heel and the spot-kick was overturned.

Brentford then hit the front in the 44th minute, with Liverpool's defence standing off Thiago and allowing him to cross completely unopposed for Lewis-Potter, whose header sailed into the top-right corner.
But the Bees would have to play the entire second half with 10 men due to a petulant act from Yarmoliuk, who headbutted Jacquet while the players were jostling in preparation for a Liverpool corner.

Liverpool did not truly threaten Caoimhin Kelleher's goal until Mac Allister had a long-range attempt beaten away just before the hour mark, but their next attack resulted in the equaliser as Munoz raced onto Florian Wirtz's pass, cut back onto his left foot, then steered his finish into the bottom-left corner.
It was 2-1 soon afterwards, with Isak drilling home from the left side of the area after Barcola nodded Mac Allister's deep delivery down to him.

Barcola almost put the game beyond Brentford when his curling attempt bounced off the crossbar, but when an enterprising run from substitute Rio Ngumoha ended with a cynical foul from Janelt, who received his marching orders, Liverpool could finally breathe easily.
Isak back with a bang against favourite opponents

Having suffered a minor thigh injury while representing Sweden during the international break, Isak was forced to sit out Liverpool's 3-0 Premier League loss to Manchester City, in addition to their thrilling 6-3 Champions League victory over LASK.
But the striker will have been relishing his return to action this weekend, as Brentford are among his favourite teams to face in the Premier League.
He has now scored in all five of his appearances against the Bees in the competition (four for Newcastle United), only netting in as many matches against Nottingham Forest and Tottenham.
Andoni Iraola, meanwhile, had never beaten Brentford in six attempts in charge of Bournemouth (D2 L4), so Saturday's win should be a cathartic one for the Liverpool boss.

And another assist for Wirtz – who has been fiercely criticised in the early weeks of the campaign – will give Iraola another reason to smile. This is the first time he has assisted in back-to-back games for Liverpool across all competitions.
The major negatives for the Reds were injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong, the latter of whom only lasted seven minutes as a half-time substitute.

Brentford, meanwhile, will have a pair of suspensions to deal with when they visit Hull City next week, having received two red cards in the same league game for the first time since April 2013, against Sheffield United in League One.

1plzoan08kp9r1evutqluolifh.title: Jaissle apologises to Newcastle fans but says Coventry loss 'not the worst game'
1plzoan08kp9r1evutqluolifh.subtitle: Newcastle suffered a surprise 4-1 defeat at Coventry City on Monday, having also lost their previous away league game by the same scoreline.
paragraphs: Matthias Jaissle apologised to Newcastle United's fans after his team suffered a second straight 4-1 away defeat, though he insists they did not play "the worst game" against Coventry City on Monday.
Having been routed by Leeds United on their previous road trip before the international break, Newcastle again had four goals put past them by Frank Lampard's men.
It is the first time they have conceded four or more goals in back-to-back Premier League away games since December 2012, when they lost 4-3 at Manchester United and 7-3 at Arsenal.

Jack Rudoni's penalty and Sidiki Cherif's lovely finish on the turn gave Newcastle a mountain to climb, and though Sven Botman's 70th-minute stunner inspired some hope, Coventry substitutes Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni struck to put the game to bed.
Newcastle's defensive record is now the joint-worst in the Premier League this season, with Chelsea and Bournemouth the only other teams to match their 13 goals conceded.
The Magpies have also given up the joint-third worst expected goals against (xGA) tally, at 10.48, while only Crystal Palace (108) have faced more shots on target than them (106).
And despite his team controlling 66.7% of the possession and having 19 shots to Coventry's nine, Jaissle acknowledges that will count for nothing if they do not improve in both boxes.
"It's hard. That's the punishment in this league," Jaissle told BBC Sport.
"We controlled many phases but it's not enough. The games are decided in the boxes – and we were not clean in both boxes.
"It's something we need to learn fast. The momentum was there. We have a young squad but that shouldn't be an excuse. It was a tough game in general.
"The injured players are hopefully getting more gametime, more minutes.
"Today, if you see the whole picture, it was not the worst game. But I apologise to the fans because they deserved a different result."

Newcastle host Aston Villa in their next Premier League game on Saturday, having taken eight points from six matches so far this campaign, before visiting Crystal Palace and facing Everton twice in five days – once in the league and once in the EFL Cup.

1pnrn2gfgmlef1rvhmj39ofd3w.title: Gittens returning to Chelsea after suffering injury with England U21s
1pnrn2gfgmlef1rvhmj39ofd3w.subtitle: Jamie Gittens' time with England Under-21s has been cut short by injury, with Lee Carsley confirming his withdrawal from the squad.
paragraphs: Chelsea have been dealt a potential injury blow after Lee Carsley confirmed Jamie Gittens was returning to the club for treatment after sustaining an injury with England Under-21s.
Gittens was forced off with an apparent ankle injury during England's 4-2 win over Kazakhstan in European Championship qualifying.
The winger made way in the 39th minute and was later spotted on crutches, and he has already been ruled out of their final two qualifying games.
Head coach Lee Carsley explained that Gittens had returned to Chelsea, with England unwilling to take any risks with the youngster's fitness.
"Jamie got a kick on his ankle. We never take any risks," Carsley said, as quoted by The Sun.
"With the age of these players, we don't ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back."
Gittens has made just two appearances for Chelsea since Xabi Alonso took over, with both of those coming in the EFL Cup, and only one coming from the start.
Indeed, he has been limited since joining the Blues from Borussia Dortmund at the start of last season, making just 29 appearances in total and netting only one goal.
The extent of Gittens' injury has not been disclosed yet, with Chelsea's next game coming against Bournemouth on October 10.
1pnrn2gfgmlef1rvhmj39ofd3w.html:
Chelsea have been dealt a potential injury blow after Lee Carsley confirmed Jamie Gittens was returning to the club for treatment after sustaining an injury with England Under-21s.

Gittens was forced off with an apparent ankle injury during England's 4-2 win over Kazakhstan in European Championship qualifying.

The winger made way in the 39th minute and was later spotted on crutches, and he has already been ruled out of their final two qualifying games.

Head coach Lee Carsley explained that Gittens had returned to Chelsea, with England unwilling to take any risks with the youngster's fitness.

"Jamie got a kick on his ankle. We never take any risks," Carsley said, as quoted by The Sun.

"With the age of these players, we don't ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back."

Gittens has made just two appearances for Chelsea since Xabi Alonso took over, with both of those coming in the EFL Cup, and only one coming from the start.

Indeed, he has been limited since joining the Blues from Borussia Dortmund at the start of last season, making just 29 appearances in total and netting only one goal.

The extent of Gittens' injury has not been disclosed yet, with Chelsea's next game coming against Bournemouth on October 10.

1pr03pzljn3n518lpy767ucc3q.title: Lampard to bring Coventry 'back down to earth' after Tottenham defeat
1pr03pzljn3n518lpy767ucc3q.subtitle: Coventry City and Fulham square off in the Premier League this weekend, with both aiming to earn a huge three points early in the season.
paragraphs: Frank Lampard insisted Coventry City's 3-1 defeat to Tottenham would not affect his team, but he said the players would be brought "back down to earth" this week.
After back-to-back wins over Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United, Coventry were beaten by Spurs on Monday, handing them their first Premier League win of the season.
Jack Rudoni had cancelled out James Maddison's 14th-minute stunner, but goals in the second half from Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies were enough to beat the Sky Blues.
Coventry face a crucial run of league games against the sides around them, with the first of those coming against a struggling Fulham team at Coventry Building Society Arena.
They also face Sunderland, Everton, Crystal Palace and Leeds United, and Lampard is hoping to see a response from his team when Alvaro Arbeloa's side come to town.
"This result won't affect us. I can speak positively about the defeat because I saw the performance," Lampard said.
"I will bring the lads back down to earth in a way to say we have to produce this now. We've moved on a lot, Fulham will come and give us different problems and expectations."
Coventry were only able to register an expected goals (xG) total of 0.77 from their 12 shots against Spurs, with only one of those attempts, Rudoni's goal, hitting the target.
"Maybe the clinical edge and sometimes stuff just doesn't fall for you and that's football," Rudoni said of Coventry's struggles in the final third against Spurs.
"All we can do is keep applying pressure and working hard in the right areas and stuff. We're away from home. They're league position probably doesn't reflect where they are."
Fulham, meanwhile, picked up their first Premier League victory of the season last time out, with Alex Iwobi scoring the only goal in a narrow 1-0 win against Hull City.

The Cottagers had 76.2% possession against Hull, their third-highest on record (since 2003-04) in a Premier League match after April 2023 against West Ham (76.6%) and September 2023 against Luton Town (77.6%).
It was a result that relieved the pressure on Arbeloa, with reports suggesting that his job was under threat after an underwhelming start to his tenure at Craven Cottage.
Fulham youngster Josh King acknowledged the importance of the result, and he hopes it can be a platform for the club to build on in the coming weeks.
"I think we were really brave," King said. "We played as a team who knew what we had to get the three points. We worked so hard for each other from 0 to 90 minutes.
"That's where we have struggled before, getting the lead and keeping it.
"[Alex Iwobi] is a really special player and a joy to play with; for him to get the goal and help the team is massive.
"I think I would have liked to come away with something more for myself, like a goal or assist; they will come, but it was all about the team."
Coventry – Jack Rudoni

Rudoni became the first player to score in back-to-back Premier League appearances for Coventry since John Hartson netted in four consecutive games between March and April 2001 against Spurs last time out.
He also finished with team-high totals for crosses (six) and successful dribbles (two), and you feel he will be key if Coventry are to return to winning ways in the Premier League.
King has been Fulham's brightest spark in an underwhelming start to their Premier League campaign, scoring more goals (two) than any other Cottagers player this season.
He has had more touches in the opposition box than any other player in the Premier League this season (48), and King will need to be at his best once again here.
MATCH PREDICTION: COVENTRY WIN

This is just the third ever top-flight meeting between Coventry and Fulham – they met in the 1967-68 season, with the Cottagers unbeaten in both (W1 D1). The Sky Blues were relegated from the Premier League in 2000-01 before returning this season, while Fulham's first season was 2001-02.

Coventry are backed to win this one, despite losing five of their seven Premier League games this season (L2), their most defeats at this stage of a league campaign since 1996-97 (also 5). They avoided relegation from the top flight on the final day of the season in that campaign.

Lampard's side have also conceded seven goals from outside the box in the Premier League this season – including three against Spurs last time out – more than twice as many as any other side. Only in 1992-93 and 1999-00 (both eight) have they shipped more from distance in a top-flight campaign.

Fulham picked up their first Premier League win of the season against Hull last time out. However, the Cottagers are winless in their last eight away league games, alternating between a draw (four) and defeat (four) each time.

They also lost to Ipswich Town and beat Hull City in their last two Premier League games. They are the first side to face all three promoted clubs in consecutive matches since Bournemouth in March 2024 (W2 D1).

This century, the only league season Coventry and Fulham have faced off was in 2021-22 when the Cottagers won the Championship title. However, Coventry completed a league double over them that season (4-1 home, 3-1 away), one of two sides to do so, along with Sheffield United.

1ps0628xpkz71s7k7d0s51yme.title: 'We cannot always go at full speed' – Fabregas explains Paz benching in Como win
1ps0628xpkz71s7k7d0s51yme.subtitle: Although Nico Paz was an unused substitute on Saturday, Como were able to secure a 2-0 victory over Sassuolo in Serie A.
paragraphs: Cesc Fabregas insisted his Como side "cannot always go at full speed" after benching star player Nico Paz in their win over Sassuolo.
Paz was an unused substitute as Como defeated Sassuolo 2-0 in Serie A, with Tasos Douvikas scoring both goals in the second half.

Douvikas scored in a home Serie A match for the first time since last March (against Pisa), while he has scored in at least four consecutive games in all competitions for the first time in his career since his debut in Europe's top five leagues.

Como have won 17 points in Serie A this season, a record for the club after eight matchdays of a single Serie A campaign. They have also scored 14 goals, their best return after their first eight matches of a season (also 14 in 1950-51).

Como have kept four clean sheets in their last five Serie A home games, as many as they managed in their previous ten; since the start of last season, only Roma (13) have kept more home clean sheets than Como (12) in Serie A.
Despite their impressive start to 2026-27, Fabregas believes he must rotate his squad if they want their strong form to continue.
"We cannot always go at full speed, but if we want to be this team, then we've got to find the energy from somewhere," Fabregas told DAZN Italia.
"That is only possible if the coach trusts every member of the squad, knowing he can change and give everyone an opportunity.
"There are thousands of moments in a season; we are learning every day, and the team is going through a growth process.
"Sassuolo had eight days to prepare for this match; now we've got Torino coming up, who played on Friday and have 24 hours of added rest.
"This is a big difference this season, and we're still getting used to it."

1q0h8v941hzfk1t856hyynk2ak.title: Caicedo keen to regain Chelsea consistency after injury return
1q0h8v941hzfk1t856hyynk2ak.subtitle: Chelsea visit Everton this weekend in the Premier League, and after returning from injury, Moises Caicedo wants to build some momentum.
paragraphs: Moises Caicedo wants to continue repaying Chelsea's faith in him after returning from injury to make his first start of the season, with a trip to Everton being the Blues' next test.

Having initially suffered a calf injury during pre-season before aggravating the same issue, Caicedo was restricted to just 14 total minutes of action prior to the international break, as a substitute in a 4-3 win over Brighton in August.
But on Saturday, he started as Xabi Alonso's side routed Bournemouth 5-1 at Stamford Bridge to halt a three-match winless streak (D1 L2) and go sixth in the Premier League.
Following his injury lay-off, the Ecuador international now wants to get back to the level that prompted Chelsea to spend £115m on him in January 2024.
"It has been a great journey for me, more than three special years at one of the best clubs in the world," Caicedo told Chelsea's website.

"In my first season, I passed some tough moments, I would say. They helped me to grow, to keep developing, and to be in the position I am in right now. I can look back and say it’s a pleasure, with what I passed.
"Now, I'm just enjoying trying to do everything for this club, because they gave me everything. They helped me in every way, and I've grown up a lot because of them.
"I have more experience now, I'm more mature, and I just want to keep learning and keep doing what I'm doing.
"I feel very grateful to Chelsea, and I want to keep showing the fans and everybody at the club what I am capable of."
Chelsea's next opponents are only above them on goal difference, having won two and drawn four of their last six matches, sharing four goals equally with Hull City last time out.

The positive feeling surrounding Everton's on-pitch performances contrasts starkly with the criticism reserved for their transfer strategy, after The Friedkin Group – who recently put the club up for sale – almost sanctioned the sale of promising youngster Harrison Armstrong.

Armstrong looked set to join Nottingham Forest after a bid for his services was accepted, but fan outcry led Everton's hierarchy to perform a U-Turn, and the 19-year-old is glad to still be at his boyhood club.

"The support has meant the world to me and my family," Armstrong told EvertonTV. "I understand it's part of the game and you're going to have to experience moments like that, but for a fanbase to get involved and show as much support as they did, is special.
"I don't think I've seen that before. I've given me confidence, it's made me feel loved and it's cemented that this is the place to be for me."
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Everton – Thierno Barry

After a run of just one goal in seven Premier League games, Barry has now scored in his last two appearances in the competition. He last scored in three consecutive league games back in August 2024, in the Swiss Super League with Basel.
Chelsea – Danny Welbeck
Welbeck has scored against Everton in the Premier League for Sunderland (twice), Manchester United, Arsenal and Brighton (once each).

There are seven instances of a player scoring against a club with five different teams in the competition, with Nicolas Anelka the only player to do so against the Toffees (Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City, Bolton Wanderers and Chelsea).
MATCH PREDICTION – EVERTON WIN

Although Everton boss David Moyes has never won in 21 attempts at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League, he has won eight of his last 13 home games against the Blues (D2 L3), with those victories split between Everton and West Ham (four each).

Furthermore, Chelsea have won just one of their last nine away Premier League games against Everton (D2 L6), a 1-0 victory in August 2022. They have failed to score in seven of those games, including the last three.
And though they are the third-highest goalscorers in the Premier League this season, no side has conceded more so often this term than Chelsea (13).
The Blues have conceded in each of their last 22 league games, only once having a longer run without a clean sheet (31 games between November 1960 and August 1961).
With Everton still unbeaten and boasting home advantage, Moyes may just fancy his chances of masterminding another upset.
Chelsea – 30.4%

1q5f31jv8jlzr12qwv5o6tzu69.title: Iraola: Feed Isak and he will score
1q5f31jv8jlzr12qwv5o6tzu69.subtitle: Alexander Isak has netted in three straight Premier League matches for the first time since January 2025, after his goal against Brighton.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola is confident Alexander Isak will maintain his fine run of form as long as Liverpool keep creating chances for him.
Isak made it six goals in the Premier League this season as he netted the Reds' second in a 2-0 win over Brighton at Anfield.
He nudged in from close range after meeting Bradley Barcola's low centre.
The Sweden international has scored in three straight top-flight matches for the first time since January 2025, when he went on a run of eight consecutive games with a goal for Newcastle United.
Isak struggled for form last season following his record-breaking transfer from Newcastle, but Iraola feels the striker is getting back towards his best.
"Alex is threatening, especially if we can get him in those positions," said Iraola.
"In this case, it's a matter of [Barcola] winning the duel and being faster than the opposition to get us in that position.
"If we can put him in those positions, we can provide him [with] good crosses, good situations; he will score the goals."

Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Isak, who told Sky Sports: "The performance was really good against a really good team. The first half is what we want to be about: winning balls and the intensity."
Liverpool recorded their first Premier League home win since April (v Crystal Palace), ending a run of five without one (D4 L1), as Iraola picked up his first top-flight triumph at Anfield.
Yasin Ayari missed a great early chance for in-form Brighton, but Florian Wirtz's strike then deflected in off Pascal Gross.
Ayari hit the woodwork after Isak had made it 2-0, but Liverpool were relatively untroubled as they saw out the three points.
However, Wirtz did have to go off due to an ankle issue.
"Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle," Iraola said of Wirtz.
"It doesn't look very bad, but we are playing every three days, so we need to see where he is."
Liverpool take on Chelsea in the EFL Cup on Wednesday, before facing Arsenal in the league next weekend.

1q7bx1qitosbz1f4dnlhbk8ew4.title: West Ham still 'building momentum' after crucial win over Swansea, says Nuno
1q7bx1qitosbz1f4dnlhbk8ew4.subtitle: West Ham closed the gap on Championship leaders Swansea City to just one point after victory in Wales on Saturday.
paragraphs: Nuno Espirito Santo said his West Ham side are still building momentum after their win over Championship leaders Swansea City.
The Hammers moved up to second in the league, just a point behind Swansea, after a 1-0 victory on Saturday.
Divine Mukasa was the match-winner for West Ham, slamming in from near the penalty spot after a clever pass from Mohamadou Kante.
It was a tight contest, with the Hammers edging the expected goals (xG) battle 1.2 to 1.0, though Swansea failed to get any of their 11 attempts on target.
Swansea's main threat came from set-pieces, with such situations responsible for 0.9 of their xG, but Nuno was pleased with what he saw from West Ham.
"I think the players did a very good job. Overall, a very good performance, organised, creating chances, also we had luck in moments," Nuno told BBC Radio London.
"Swansea are a very good team; they are fast, dynamic, it's not easy to control them, but overall I think we were organised and caused a lot of problems too.
"It was a very entertaining game, very intense; it was a nice football match.
"There were some amazing saves, maybe because of my past [as a goalkeeper] I always credit them, but they were some amazing saves [from Lawrence Vigouroux].
"I think we are building momentum. The table is important but more important is how we keep improving. I still believe there are a lot of things we should have done better."
Elsewhere in the Championship, Middlesbrough failed to go top after being held to a 2-2 draw with Cardiff City.
Boro did find themselves 2-0 down at half-time, but Tommy Conway and Will Lankshear scored after the break to salvage a draw.

"There were some amazing saves, maybe because of my past [as a goalkeeper] I always credit them, but they were some amazing saves [from Lawrence Vigouroux].

"I think we are building momentum. The table is important but more important is how we keep improving. I still believe there are a lot of things we should have done better."

Elsewhere in the Championship, Middlesbrough failed to go top after being held to a 2-2 draw with Cardiff City.

Boro did find themselves 2-0 down at half-time, but Tommy Conway and Will Lankshear scored after the break to salvage a draw.

1q8lgyn5wojce11sb5vt3kfmq2.title: Lyon 0-0 Chelsea: Super Hampton save preserves Champions League point
1q8lgyn5wojce11sb5vt3kfmq2.subtitle: After a dramatic second half at Groupama Stadium, Lyon and Chelsea had to settle for a share of the points after a goalless stalemate.
paragraphs: A stunning late save from Hannah Hampton preserved a point for Chelsea as they played out a 0-0 draw with Lyon in the Women's Champions League.
Salma Paralluelo had a second-half goal ruled out for offside, while Chelsea had two penalties overturned by VAR, but it was Hampton's last-gasp heroics that salvaged a point.
Chelsea made a strong start and had the first shot on target as Melvine Malard brilliantly improvised by looping an overhead volley towards goal, but it was an easy catch for Mala Grohs.
Lyon did not take long to grow into the game, though, and Melchie Dumornay threaded it through to Paralluelo, who forced a smart save out of Hampton.
Dumornay drilled narrowly wide shortly after, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto then scuffing her attempt straight at Hampton.
Selma Bacha and Caroline Weir both failed to hit the target as Lyon finished the half on top, and the cagey nature of the game carried over after the break.

Chelsea were awarded a penalty after Tarciane caught Sjoeke Nusken late in the box, but after the referee initially pointed to the spot, a VAR review spotted Lucy Bronze offside in the build-up, and the penalty was overturned.

Lyon thought they had found a potential winner in the 72nd minute after Paralluelo raced onto another superb Dumornay pass and swept her finish past Hampton, but she set off too early, with the offside flag denying her.
Chelsea had another penalty overturned moments later after Lauren James went to ground, but there was not much in the challenge from Damaris Egurrola.
Grohs was fully behind James' first-time effort to deny Chelsea a winner, and just moments later, Hampton made a brilliant save at full stretch to keep out Ada Hegerberg's looping header.
Both sides struggle to find their golden touch

Chelsea have made a stuttering start to the season, struggling to find their free-flowing best in front of goal, but the same cannot be said of Lyon, who beat Servette 8-0 last time out in the Champions League.

The chances at Groupama Stadium on Wednesday were few and far between, though, with both sides ultimately finishing with nine shots apiece after the game opened up in the last five minutes plus stoppage time.

Lyon tested Hampton four times, while Paralluelo scored a lovely goal, if only she had slowed her run behind Bronze slightly better. The expected goals (xG) told the biggest story, with Lyon's 0.78 xG just bettering Chelsea's 0.73.

Ultimately, it was Hampton's late intervention that proved the most vital for Sonia Bompastor on her return to Lyon, as Hegerberg's header looked to be heading in until the goalkeeper got her fingertips to the ball.
Both Chelsea and England will have breathed a sigh of relief that her game did not come to a premature end after a heavy collision with Tabitha Chawinga.

While neither side managed to find a winner in France, Bayern Munich got their first Champions League win of the campaign, beating Benfica 3-0, scoring all of their goals from the 74th minute onwards.

1qh777ogzeb9j1a3ltxl78p5qa.title: 'Role model' Yamal continues to delight Spain staff and team-mates
1qh777ogzeb9j1a3ltxl78p5qa.subtitle: Lamine Yamal has only just turned 19, but Luis de la Fuente already sees the Barcelona superstar as the ideal role model in Spain's squad.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal is already a "role model" for Spain, despite his tender years, so says coach Luis de la Fuente.
Yamal has enjoyed another fantastic year for both club and country.
He registered 41 goal involvements in all competitions last season for Barcelona, as the Blaugrana successfully defended their LaLiga crown.
Yamal then went on to play a key role as Spain followed up their Euro 2024 triumph by winning the World Cup.
Spain have made a flying start to their Nations League campaign, winning all three of their games, and Yamal is their leading scorer, with four goals.
And De la Fuente says Yamal is already an inspiration for the rest of La Roja's squad, despite only being 19.
"Lamine always wants to play, like all the players. We evaluate and analyse whether it's advisable or not," De la Fuente told reporters ahead of Tuesday's clash with Croatia.
"Lamine is in fantastic form. He's a role model and a born competitor. He's in good shape to play the match. But so are other team-mates, who are all in perfect condition.
"Lamine wants to be the best. He's very competitive, and that's normal; he has the anxiety of a genius who always wants to be at the level he knows he can achieve."
De la Fuente's sentiment was echoed by Dani Olmo, who plays alongside Yamal at Barca.
Olmo said: "Lamine continues to improve with each match. He seems to be getting better and more mature every season.

"At the start of this season, he's helping us not only with his play but also by scoring goals, which is something he demands of himself. He's very important for us both at the club and with the national team."
Yamal has already scored eight goals and laid on six assists in eight appearances for Barca this season.

1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.title: Palmer and Rice withdraw from England squad as Gibbs-White, Garner come in
1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.subtitle: Thomas Tuchel will be without Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Marcus Rashford for England's upcoming Nations League fixtures.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer and Declan Rice are part of a quintet of players who have withdrawn from England duty.
Palmer, who missed out on England's World Cup squad, was selected by Thomas Tuchel for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League matches.
He has already registered four Premier League goal involvements this season (two goals, two assists).
However, the Chelsea playmaker has now opted out of the squad as he nurses an injury.
It is the same case for Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo.
Tuchel has called up Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner as replacements.
No player has scored more Premier League goals in 2026 than Nottingham Forest attacker Gibbs-White (13, level with Erling Haaland).

Garner, meanwhile, made his England debut during the March international window, and impressed against Uruguay and Japan, but the Everton midfielder ultimately missed out on a call-up for the World Cup.
The pair will now get a chance to impress in fixtures against world champions Spain, with a double-header against Czechia following, either side of a clash with Croatia.

1qm1h1gzv4y6g16xoopqleujvf.title: Mbappe leaves France camp after suffering tendon injury
1qm1h1gzv4y6g16xoopqleujvf.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe went off injured just before the hour against Turkiye, and he will play no further part in France's Nations League camp.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has left France's camp following their 1-0 win over Turkiye in their Nations League opener through injury.
Zinedine Zidane made a winning start to life as France's head coach, with Mbappe scoring the only goal of the game nine minutes into the second half.
However, he pulled up immediately after scoring and was taken off the pitch within five minutes, having received treatment, seemingly with a knee problem.
Mbappe scored his 12th goal for France in 2026, equalling the highest total for a Les Bleus player in a single calendar year in the 21st century (also Mbappe with 12 in 2022).

He will not play any further part in this extended international break, however, with France confirming on social media that "he is suffering from a tendon injury and will return to [Real] Madrid for treatment".
Asked about Mbappe's situation shortly after the victory, Zidane told TF1: "It's not going well, unfortunately.
"I think he'll have to go back. We're not going to take any risks. He developed hypertension in his knee during the shot.
"It's not exactly encouraging for him to be able to continue."
Zidane is the first coach to win his first match in charge of France since Aime Jacquet against Italy in 1994 (D4 L1).
France sit second in Group A1, only behind their next opponents, Belgium, on goal difference.
But Zidane was thrilled to get off the mark with three points.
"It's very emotional. It's a successful debut," he added.
"It's not easy to come and play in Turkiye, with such a complicated atmosphere. We played the game we needed to.
"We played well; we pressed them high up the pitch. I saw a lot of interesting things even though we've only had three and a half training sessions.
"It's encouraging. I'm happy with what they did. It was good to see everyone."
As for Turkiye, they were in the game throughout and had their chances to get on the scoresheet, with Ismail Yuksek's unmarked diving header forcing a superb save out of Mike Maignan.
They had 12 shots, like France, and only had a marginally smaller expected goals tally (1.1 xG to Les Bleus' 1.2).
"I am proud; it's a shame we were unable to leave the field with a positive result," head coach Vincenzo Montella told Sky Sport Italia.
"It was an incredible performance, one of our best, especially considering who we were up against.
"We knew that you cannot afford even half a mistake against sides like this, but I thought we had our chances too, and it was a very even game.

"I saw a great team spirit, and that is something we need to carry with us into the next matches. It won't be easy to recover physically and mentally so quickly, so we need that spirit first and foremost.
"I feel sorry for my lads, because they really did give it their all."

1qn73t3mg2d8k1qbqvhjkwqf3o.title: Joao Pedro 'out for a few weeks', confirms Chelsea boss Alonso
1qn73t3mg2d8k1qbqvhjkwqf3o.subtitle: Chelsea face Liverpool in the EFL Cup round of 16, but will be without top scorer Joao Pedro due to a thigh injury.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso revealed Joao Pedro will "be out for a few weeks" ahead of Chelsea's EFL Cup last-16 clash with Liverpool.
Joao Pedro has been Chelsea's top performer this season, directly contributing to eight goals (five goals, three assists) in six Premier League.

Only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (six) have scored more in the English top-flight than Joao Pedro this term, and only Haaland (nine) has directly contributed to more goals than the Brazilian.
However, Joao Pedro missed Chelsea's defeat to Tottenham on the weekend, and Alonso has now revealed the extent of the thigh injury.
"He has an injury in his thigh and he's going to be out for a few weeks," said Alonso about Joao Pedro.
"Let’s see how many; we don't want to predict that. But he will not be ready for the next games.

"He is a key player and we will miss him, but we have to be ready to deal with the injury, be competitive and try to win games with the players we have available, starting against Liverpool, a cup game.
"This is the situation and we are ready to fight for it and prove we can show a good level."
The last two EFL Cup meetings between Liverpool and Chelsea have been in finals, with the Reds lifting the trophy in both 2021-22 and 2023-24 after winning on penalties.

In the last two seasons, Chelsea's EFL Cup matches have seen the most goals of any side (31 – 19 scored, 12 conceded), with their third-round tie against Leeds United this season seeing them come from 2-0 down to win 6-3.
Alonso played Morgan Rogers in the striker role against Spurs, but the Spaniard could opt for a different option at Anfield, with summer arrival Emmanuel Emegha potentially in line for a debut.
"For sure it's important that we have him available because he has special qualities," added Alonso of Emegha.
"He needs to feel fully fit. He has been training for the last two weeks, ten days, in a good way that has allowed him to build a strong base of fitness.
"We tried with Morgan playing close to Cole [Palmer], and sometimes we need to be creative and try a few things to see if they are going to work well.

"I assess all the possibilities we have and what we have been preparing during the week, and with the qualities all players have, to choose the best team for each game. That was the case for Saturday and that is the case for Wednesday."

1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.title: 'No gameplan and no ideas' – Makelele slams Mourinho's Madrid after derby defeat
1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.subtitle: Jose Mourinho criticised Ortiz Arias after Real Madrid's loss to Atletico Madrid, but Claude Makelele says the referee was not to blame.
paragraphs: Ex-Real Madrid midfielder Claude Makelele did not hold back on his former team's performance in their derby defeat to Atletico Madrid, saying they had "no gameplan and no ideas."
Madrid slipped to a 2-1 loss against their cross-city rivals on Sunday, their second in the first seven games of their LaLiga campaign.
With defending champions Barcelona making a perfect start, Los Blancos are already six points off the title pace, and Makelele feels there are glaring issues in their side.

During Sunday's game, Madrid only managed eight shots and 0.3 expected goals, compared to Atleti's 18 attempts and 2.35 xG, though that latter figure was boosted by the penalty from which Alejandro Grimaldo opened the scoring early in the second half.

Dean Huijsen was sent off and conceded that spot-kick for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, though Madrid had been flat in attack even with 11 men on the pitch, only posting 0.16 xG and one shot on target in the first half.
And Makelele, who represented Madrid 145 times between 2000 and 2003, before working under Mourinho at Chelsea, was bemused by their lacklustre display.
"There is no understanding between the players, nor with the coach. Mourinho must talk to them," he told ESPN.
"The team is weak, there is no gameplan and no clear ideas. There is nothing. Nothing, nothing, nothing... Absolutely nothing. We must demand more from them."

In stark contrast to Madrid's stuttering performance, Atleti scored their second goal – via Jonathan David – at the end of an 18-pass move – the most for any goal scored by either team in a Madrid derby in LaLiga since at least 2005-06.

Afterwards, Mourinho said "the story of the game" was an inept refereeing performance from Ortiz Arias, arguing both Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, prompting Atleti to hit back on social media, posting: "Stop referee harassment now."
But Makelele was not interested in playing the blame game, saying: "The problem is not the referee; there is an obvious deficiency in the team."
After the extended international break, Madrid host Villarreal in LaLiga on October 10, before visiting Roma in the Champions League four days later.

1qotyczxokwan1i4corupg1mg9.title: 'Things starting to click' for Bournemouth under Rose, says Hill
1qotyczxokwan1i4corupg1mg9.subtitle: After a tough start under Marco Rose, Bournemouth have recorded four straight wins, the latest of which came at Old Trafford.
paragraphs: It was only ever a matter of time before things clicked for Bournemouth under Marco Rose, defender James Hill declared after their 3-0 victory over Manchester United.
The Cherries piled further pressure on embattled United head coach Michael Carrick on Sunday, with Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson on target at Old Trafford.

While United are now 16th in the Premier League, having made their worst start to a campaign since 1986-87, when they had four points from seven matches, Bournemouth are up to 13th after piecing together back-to-back wins.

Bournemouth failed to win their first six league games under Rose, but they are now on a four-match winning streak across the Premier League and the Europa League – their best run since December 2023.
And Hill always expected their results to turn, telling the club's website: "It was a really special performance. Coming here and getting three points is hard for any team.
"But for us to come here and keep a clean sheet as well and score the three goals, credit to the whole team, they were brilliant.

"They [United] are in a difficult position, but we didn't focus on that, we focused on putting a good performance in. We focused on ourselves coming into a massive fixture against a team with a lot of quality.
"We've been really good recently and we're pleased with our clean sheets recently. We were outstanding to a man.
"We have had lots of games recently, but we wouldn't want it any other way, it's been an incredible journey.
"It was an incredible performance from everybody and a good confidence builder for the team. I am absolutely delighted.
"We were unlucky at the start of the season. but things are starting to click under Marco and we have momentum now. It was only a matter of time."

Bournemouth's victory made them just the third team to go seven Premier League games unbeaten against United (W3 D4), along with Chelsea (eight between May 2013 and October 2016) and Liverpool (eight between December 2018 and April 2022).

The Cherries have scored 18 goals in 10 games at Old Trafford in the Premier League and have the best goals-per-game ratio of any side to play away at Man Utd more than once in Football League history (1.8).
They are at home to Aston Villa in the EFL Cup fourth round on Wednesday, before hosting Leeds United in the Premier League three days later.
