Bournemouth failed to win their first six league games under Rose, but they are now on a four-match winning streak across the Premier League and the Europa League – their best run since December 2023.

And Hill always expected their results to turn, telling the club's website: "It was a really special performance. Coming here and getting three points is hard for any team.

"But for us to come here and keep a clean sheet as well and score the three goals, credit to the whole team, they were brilliant.

"They [United] are in a difficult position, but we didn't focus on that, we focused on putting a good performance in. We focused on ourselves coming into a massive fixture against a team with a lot of quality.

"We've been really good recently and we're pleased with our clean sheets recently. We were outstanding to a man.

"We have had lots of games recently, but we wouldn't want it any other way, it's been an incredible journey.

"It was an incredible performance from everybody and a good confidence builder for the team. I am absolutely delighted.

"We were unlucky at the start of the season. but things are starting to click under Marco and we have momentum now. It was only a matter of time."

Bournemouth's victory made them just the third team to go seven Premier League games unbeaten against United (W3 D4), along with Chelsea (eight between May 2013 and October 2016) and Liverpool (eight between December 2018 and April 2022).

The Cherries have scored 18 goals in 10 games at Old Trafford in the Premier League and have the best goals-per-game ratio of any side to play away at Man Utd more than once in Football League history (1.8).

They are at home to Aston Villa in the EFL Cup fourth round on Wednesday, before hosting Leeds United in the Premier League three days later.

1qp9dymp1h5ms16dr2xnfomhgl.title: West Ham's 'hesitation' proved costly, says Nuno
1qp9dymp1h5ms16dr2xnfomhgl.subtitle: West Ham missed the chance to go top of the Championship after losing at home to Southampton, who closed in on the top two.
paragraphs: Nuno Espirito Santo believes his West Ham side hesitated during their defeat to Southampton on Saturday.
The Hammers missed the opportunity to go top of the Championship after losing 3-2 at home to the Saints.

Kuryu Matsuki and James Bree struck inside the opening 11 minutes to give Southampton a 2-0 lead, and though Kyle Walker-Peters pulled a goal back soon after, Lewis Dobbin scored a third for the Saints before half-time.
Tomas Soucek scored a late consolation for West Ham in second-half stoppage time, but it was not enough to inspire a dramatic comeback, with the Hammers now third in the table.
"We're disappointed. We started not the way we wanted and we conceded," said Nuno.
"We were looking at the situations with hesitation, bouncing balls, too many chances for Southampton to have a second phase, third phase and achieve a goal.
"We were not good in that moment, but the reaction was good. After you start playing, you start combining, you create enormous situations.
"We tried, again, many, many situations that we could have done better. The boys fought till the end. The atmosphere was good.
"The fans helped us. All of us were having the feeling that we were able to react and revert the game, but it was not to be. It was disappointing."
While Southampton moved within three points of West Ham, second-place Swansea City were thrashed by QPR.
Richard Kone scored a hat-trick after just 15 minutes, while Jummy Dunne also scored a brace as QPR pulled off a stunning 5-0 win.
Kone’s hat-trick is the earliest scored in an EFL match (15th minute) since the rebrand in 2004-05.
Those results mean Middlesbrough are top of the league, following their 5-1 rout of Bolton Wanderers on Friday.

1qpbmk3xuwfm61ouf8n55ikg6z.title: Marsch urges Canada to be 'cleaner' despite win over Chile
1qpbmk3xuwfm61ouf8n55ikg6z.subtitle: Canada made a winning return to action, edging past nine-man Chile 1-0 thanks to Jonathan David's early goal.
paragraphs: Despite Canada returning to action after the World Cup with a win, Jesse Marsch is keen to see a "cleaner" performance than the one he got against Chile.
Canada edged to a 1-0 victory over their nine-man opponents in the friendly at BMO Field despite dominating for large parts of the match.
Jonathan David scored the winner in the 12th minute. Jacob Schaffelburg's cross was met by Cyle Larin, who saw his shot saved, but it rebounded off him to David, who coolly tapped home.
Lucas Cepeda was then shown a straight red card 35 minutes in after a high boot on Richie Laryea.
Gabriel Suazo also made an early exit, receiving his second booking five minutes after the break – his first was for dissent before his late foul on Niko Sigur.

Canada pushed to try and make the most of their advantage in the second half, but even though they finished with 22 shots worth 2.6 expected goals (xG), with 16 of their attempts coming after the break, they could not get a second goal.
And it is that part of their game that Marsch wants to see an improvement on as they continue to build on their round-of-16 exit from the World Cup.
"Chile makes it hard," Marsch said. "I don't think [our] second half was very good.
"Chile remained aggressive even down two men. The way to make them pay was to be cleaner with the ball and cleaner with ideas and actions around the goal.
"We were too wild, not enough shots on frame, not enough final actions with good connections."
Canada also hit the woodwork twice, with Laryea and Jamie Knight-Lebel going close in the final six minutes of the 90.
Larin was a constant threat for them, having a game-high four shots, 12 touches in the opposition box, two 'big' chances, and winning two of his four aerial duels.
"Every game we play is a must-win," Larin said.
"You don't come here to play and just to draw or get a result."

1qpjmos8n9s6b1rg2zabt5xc01.title: Poznan draw a 'good experience' for youthful Sunderland, says Le Bris
1qpjmos8n9s6b1rg2zabt5xc01.subtitle: Sunderland had to settle for a point in their Europa League clash with Lech Poznan, but Regis Le Bris said there was plenty of positives.
paragraphs: Regis Le Bris hopes Sunderland's youthful team will benefit from playing in a cauldron-like atmosphere at the Enea Stadion following Thursday's 1-1 draw with Lech Poznan.
Sunderland failed to make it three wins from three to begin their Europa League campaign, with Tymur Tutierov's early goal cancelled out by Leo Bengtsson's 70th-minute strike.
The Black Cats made the perfect start after 78 seconds when Mateusz Lis' poor pass was picked off by Nilson Angulo, who crossed for Tutierov to head into the bottom corner.

It was Sunderland's earliest major European goal and the second-earliest away goal by an English side in the Europa League after Bobby Zamora for Fulham in April 2010 (20 seconds), and the visitors should have been further ahead by the break.
Granit Xhaka and Nordi Mukiele passed up presentable opportunities, but Poznan hit back in the second half when Bengtsson rifled in the equaliser at Robin Roefs' near post.

Neither side were able to find a win as Sunderland became the first English side to score inside the opening two minutes of a Europa League game and failed to go on and win the match (seven out of seven before Thursday's game).

Sunderland also had 11 shots on target, tallying an expected goals (xG) total of 2.97 from their 25 attempts overall, which was their most in a game in all competitions since May 2021 against Plymouth Argyle in League One (also 11), though Le Bris was keen to look at the positives.
"We expected this atmosphere, this style of play from our opponent," Le Bris told BBC Radio Newcastle.
"I think they are a good team and after the first goal, they showed that they had quality to build up under pressure, to go through our block when we were a bit open.
"They created chances as well. After that, we created our chances. We deserved to score the second goal.
"We didn't and in a nice stadium like this against a good team, the momentum can shift and switch really quickly and it happened.
"So a good experience. We started the game with seven players under 23 years old, so they need to experience those situations against good teams to get better."
The result saw some of Sunderland's fringe players given the chance to impress, with Angulo one of the standout performers for the Premier League strugglers.

Angulo has now registered two assists in his last four games for Sunderland in all competitions, after managing none in his previous 14 appearances for the club, while he also finished with team-high totals for chances created (five), crosses (four) and successful dribbles (two).
Tutierov, meanwhile, scored his first goal for Sunderland in his fourth appearance in all competitions for the Black Cats.
He is also the first Ukrainian to score for an English club in the Europa League since Andrii Yarmolenko for West Ham against Sevilla in March 2022.
"It felt so good," Tutierov said. "I had goosebumps. At first, I didn't think I had scored, but then I did and ran to the cameras.
"Everyone said to me, imagine scoring a goal, because when the moment comes, you will put the ball in the net. That is what happened."

1qw9rjyxcph9w1sg24xvvcerms.title: United States 4-1 Peru: Pochettino's youngsters shine in friendly win
1qw9rjyxcph9w1sg24xvvcerms.subtitle: The United States' stunning second-half performance secured a big friendly win over Peru in their first match since the World Cup.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino's new-look United States team rallied in the second half to secure a 4-1 friendly win over Peru at Inter.co Stadium.
Gianluca Lapadula cancelled out Justin Ellis' early opener in the first half, but Malik Tillman, Julian Hall and Sebastian Berhalter all scored after the break to secure the victory.

It took less than four minutes for debutant Ellis to score on his home ground in Orlando on his debut, as he met Giovanni Reyna's left-sided free-kick with a glancing header that went in off the far post.
But Peru responded well to the setback and equalised within 11 minutes. Yoshimar Yotun looped a lovely cross into the far post, and Lapadula sent his header back across goal to restore parity.
Tillman had the chance to restore the USA's lead in the 20th minute after meeting Peyton Miller's delivery first-time, but Pedro Gallese was well-placed to thwart him.

Mathis Albert's introduction added a spark, and he won a penalty after cutting inside from the left, getting a shove right on the edge of the box in the 64th minute, though Peru believed the contact happened outside.
Tillman stepped up to guide his spot-kick into the bottom-left corner, with Gallese unable to get a touch despite diving the right way.
And Hall then got a debut goal of his own, getting between two defenders at the far post to tap in Berhalter's brilliantly dangerous low cross from the right in the 72nd minute.
Berhalter then rounded off the goalscoring in the 90th minute with a stunning long-range finish that nestled into the top corner, giving Gallese no chance.
United States make strong post-World Cup start
The buzz of the World Cup was strong in the USA, leading to quite a bit of disappointment when they were knocked out of the tournament in the round of 16 by Belgium.

But having lost three of their last four friendlies before the tournament, Pochettino shook up his pack, bringing on a lot of debutants, and he has now been given a good headache by his young players.

Ellis, who had a joint-team-high three attempts, wasted little time making an impact on a pitch he knows well, and in the second half, Hall took less than 10 minutes to score his first international goal after coming off the bench.
Pochettino made 10 changes, making sure to see as many in his squad as possible, and they impressed, having 16 shots, worth 2.39 expected goals (xG), with six of those on target.
And while they impressed offensively, they also looked strong at the back, only facing two shots on target, though Lapadula's header was a well-taken goal.

1qxo18bqectvr14l24hckiuzz8.title: Ronaldo rules out international retirement but apologises for Portugal exit
1qxo18bqectvr14l24hckiuzz8.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo released a lengthy statement about leaving Portugal's Nations League squad, but he is not thinking about retirement.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo has promised to have "one or more farewell matches" after confirming he will not retire from international duty with Portugal following a rift with Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo announced he had left Portugal's Nations League squad ahead of their 4-2 win over Denmark last week and said he would "tell people the truth" about his decision.
The 41-year-old started in the Selecao's 1-0 win over Wales but was taken off in the 67th minute before being an unused substitute in Portugal's 2-1 victory against Norway.
In a lengthy statement posted on social media, Ronaldo said that Jesus had "broken his word" after saying that he would play him for the final 30 minutes against Stale Solbakken's side.
But has now apologised for his actions and said he would accept whatever punishment came his way, but Ronaldo refused to draw the curtain on his career with Portugal.
"I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further breach of word," one part of Ronaldo's statement read.
"For me, the truth is still the most important thing in the relationship between people. However much it hurts, let them tell me the truth.
"Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of my career.
"I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.

"I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach's word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine.
"On this subject, I have heard a great deal of talk about farewell matches, that I must have a dignified farewell and that the Federation wants to give me that opportunity.

"I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone. I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.

"Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals, I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team. This is, believe me, the purest of truths."
Ronaldo's 146 goals in 234 caps are the most by any male player in international football history, while he is one of only two players to feature in six editions of the World Cup.

However, since the start of 2025, Portugal have won 80% of their matches when Ronaldo has not appeared (P5 W4 D1), compared to just 59% when he has featured (P17 W10 D4 L3), also averaging almost twice as many goals per game without the five-time Ballon d'Or winner (3.4) than with him (1.9).
Jesus has left the door open for a potential return to Portugal's squad, with the defending Nations League champions next in action against Denmark on November 14.
Portugal have already qualified for the next round of the Nations League having taken 12 points from their opening four Group A4 games.

1qxy5qmaxymps192e00dnfjqtn.title: Barcola backed to hit best form by Liverpool boss Iraola
1qxy5qmaxymps192e00dnfjqtn.subtitle: Bradley Barcola has yet to fire on all cylinders since joining Liverpool from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal that could rise to £123m.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola has no doubt Bradley Barcola will soon come good despite a slow start to life at Liverpool.
Barcola joined the Reds in a deal that could eventually be worth £123m from Paris Saint-Germain at the end of the transfer window.
The France international played a key role in PSG's back-to-back Champions League triumphs.
Barcola made 152 appearances for PSG following his move from Lyon in August 2023, scoring 39 goals and providing 35 assists.
However, he is yet to score or assist for Liverpool across his five appearances. Indeed, Barcola has only created two chances, while he has completed just one dribble, having attempted nine.
Barcola also came under criticism for his displays for France in the recent international window, but Iraola is unconcerned.
"I don't think he's in a bad moment – the problem with wingers or strikers is if they don't score a goal, 'they haven't played well'," Iraola said of Barcola.
"We have to see the games, we have to watch. I said it the first game against Atletico Madrid, he missed two or three quite clear chances. I don't care. Honestly.
"With the national team, I have seen he has had a couple of good situations to score; he hasn't scored, but I want him to be there."
Iraola also feels Barcola can play well in numerous positions across Liverpool's attacking line.
"He is a top player for us. I think he can play in any position up front," Iraola said.
"He probably has played more as a left winger but has played a little bit as a striker, has played even more as a right winger. I think he can cover the three positions up front.
"He's a super valuable player for us."
Barcola will be aiming to break his Liverpool duck when the Reds host Manchester City on Sunday.

1qykhcrq7ltzz1njtyfqfzoj0w.title: James says Leeds cannot get carried away with unbeaten start ahead of Arsenal test
1qykhcrq7ltzz1njtyfqfzoj0w.subtitle: Leeds United have nine points on the board after five Premier League games, and they face champions Arsenal this weekend.
paragraphs: Dan James has urged Leeds United not to get carried away with their unbeaten start to the Premier League season, as they prepare to visit champions Arsenal on Saturday.
Leeds are one of five teams yet to taste defeat in the top flight this campaign, having won two and drawn three of their opening five matches.
They went into the extended international break off the back of a goalless draw with Crystal Palace, having thrashed Newcastle United 4-1 in their previous match.

And James – who appeared in three of Wales' four Nations League matches during the hiatus – says everyone around Daniel Farke's squad will be switched on and ready to go at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.
"It is a long season. We have started well and I think it is easy to get carried away," James told LUTV.
"But as I said, we have got tough opponents coming and we have just got to take every game as it goes. You can't underestimate anyone in this league. Anyone can beat anyone.

"We have got a brilliant squad. Winning really helps that environment. We have made good additions to the squad to help with that, and winning games does really help drive us along and keeps us working to be better."

It is the first time Leeds have started a league campaign at any level unbeaten in their first five matches since 2019-20, when they won the Championship under Marcelo Bielsa, and James says starting strongly was a clear aim after Farke's side had to finish well last season.
"We have set really set a high standard, and it is about progressing now in these next five games before the next internationals. We really want to push on," he added.
"We have got tough games coming up, but we really believe that we can go into every game and perform.
"Last season, we didn't quite get off to a good start. It was really that start to the season that stopped us from getting any higher in the table. We have got to keep on that."
Arsenal, meanwhile, lost 3-0 to Brighton in their final game before the break, having started their title defence with four straight victories.

Gunners midfielder Eberechi Eze is yet to start a Premier League match in 2026-27, tallying a mere 85 minutes of action, but he is happy to play either centrally or on the left flank in order to get more gametime.
"I don't mind. They both have pros and cons and come with different challenges," he told BBC Sport when asked about the two positions after England's 3-0 win over Czechia.
"I enjoy both of them. I enjoy finding space and finding ways to score, assist and create things. I enjoy both, so I don't really mind which one I play."
Arsenal – Martin Odegaard

Odegaard, like his team-mate Kai Havertz, has scored in both of Arsenal's home Premier League games this term. With Havertz suffering an injury while representing Germany, it is the Norwegian who may provide the Gunners' foremost goal threat here.
After only netting one goal in all competitions in 2025-26, Odegaard has already found the net four times in 2026-27.
Leeds United – Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Calvert-Lewin is one of only two players to rank in the top 10 for aerial duels won (24), runs ending in the box (33) and high-intensity pressures in the opposition half (187) in the Premier League this season, alongside Everton's Thierno Barry.
The striker has netted three times in his last five outings for Leeds, while he also made a pair of substitute appearances for England during the international break.
MATCH PREDICTION – ARSENAL WIN
Arsenal have won nine of their last 10 Premier League games against Leeds (D1), including each of the last seven by an aggregate score of 24-5.
In addition, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta – who signed a three-year contract extension on Wednesday – has won all four of his Premier League games against Daniel Farke.
It is his joint-best 100% win rate against a manager in the top flight (level with Gary O'Neil), and Farke's worst 100% loss rate against a manager during his career in England.

Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton last time out, their heaviest defeat since May 2023 (also 3-0 vs Brighton). However, since the start of 2024, the Gunners have only lost back-to-back Premier League games once (in April 2026), with Saturday's match being their 100th league game since then.

Leeds have won just one of their last 17 away league games against the reigning English top-flight champions (D6 L10), although that was the last time they visited Arsenal as title holders, a 3-2 victory in May 2003.

1qypb24zfarua12z1dgfcxnpiy.title: Cherki eyeing more responsibility with France in future
1qypb24zfarua12z1dgfcxnpiy.subtitle: Rayan Cherki enjoyed a positive cameo off the bench against Belgium, helping France to an emphatic comeback victory.
paragraphs: Rayan Cherki is keen to take on even more responsibility within the France national team, claiming he "learned to play in a new position" during this break.
Cherki has played a key role in Zinedine Zidane's unbeaten start to his life as Les Bleus' boss and scored his first international goal since June in their 4-1 win over Belgium in the Nations League.
The 23-year-old was one of three players to come off the bench to score, with his goal giving them the lead after Desire Doue had equalised. Michael Olise also netted twice.
In the four games during this break, only Ousmane Dembele (11) has created more chances than Cherki (seven), who has a joint-team-high two assists.
Cherki has been involved in Zidane's three-man midfield on the right, playing behind Olise to create an impressive link-up.
"People talk about my dribbling, but I'm now playing in a role that requires me to play complete, clean matches, and true football connoisseurs understand that," Cherki told TF1.
"During this training camp, I learned to play in a new position. It's a different style of play: I can't lose the ball.
"I like this position, and you'll see, as time goes on, that I'll take on even more responsibility."
France sit top of Group A1 with 10 points and are in a strong position to qualify for the quarter-finals during the November break.
It has been a strong start to life as France head coach for Zidane, who has been without the injured Kylian Mbappe for the last three games, and Cherki was full of praise for his new boss.
"Honestly, it's fantastic. We have an extraordinary relationship," Cherki said of Zidane.
"He treats all the players the same; he chats with everyone about anything and everything. He teaches us the fundamentals, especially the importance of having the ball."

1r1xmy6tref7s1ng89wqretka6.title: Grimsby inspired Fleetwood's EFL Cup victory over Arsenal, says Lynch
1r1xmy6tref7s1ng89wqretka6.subtitle: Fleetwood Town made history by dumping out Arsenal in the EFL Cup on Tuesday, following in the footsteps of Grimsby Town from last season.
paragraphs: Fleetwood Town hero Jay Lynch said the inspiration behind his team's shock EFL Cup win over Arsenal came from Grimsby Town's upset against Manchester United last season.
League Two Fleetwood booked their place in the quarter-finals of the competition with a 5-3 penalty shoot-out win on Tuesday following a 1-1 draw in normal time.
Aaron Loupalo-Bi had given Fleetwood a 21st-minute lead at Highbury Stadium, but Viktor Gyokeres levelled things up for the Premier League champions in the second half.
However, Mikel Arteta's side were reduced to 10 men when Max Dowman kicked out at Fleetwood's Harrison Neal following a strong tackle on the teenager in the 85th minute.
Both teams had been perfect in the shoot-out until Bruno Guimaraes was denied by Lynch, with Conor Haughey stepping up to spark wild scenes among the home supporters.
Fleetwood eliminating Arsenal is the first time a fourth-tier side has knocked out the reigning English champions in a domestic cup since Wrexham beat the Gunners 34 years ago in the FA Cup (1992).
They have also now emerged victorious from their last four penalty shoot-outs in all competitions, converting each of their last 16 spot-kicks across those shoot-outs.

Speaking after the famous win, Lynch said Fleetwood "took heart" from Grimsby dumping out Man Utd in the second round of last year's competition, when they followed up a 2-2 draw with a dramatic 12-11 win on penalties.
"The whole team throughout the game were magnificent. To beat the English champions . . .," Lynch said.
"We took heart from Grimsby beating United last year. We kind of compared it. We thought if we give it a good go late on, let’s see what happens.
"It's a typical night in Fleetwood! We were expecting a storm, we knew the conditions would be horrible, and it might work in our favour.
"It's amazing for the club and the town, it means everything for everyone."

Arsenal's elimination by Fleetwood was only the second time in EFL Cup history that the reigning top-flight champions have been knocked out by a fourth tier opponent, along with Leeds United, who lost 3-0 to Chester City in 1974-75.
There are 84 places between Fleetwood and Arsenal in the English football pyramid, with Matt Lawlor's team languishing at the bottom end of League Two.
Fleetwood had not won any of their previous five meetings with Premier League opponents, and they only managed three shots compared to Arsenal's 26 during the encounter.
Arsenal's expected goals (xG) total of 2.21 dwarfed Fleetwood's tally of 0.26, but Haughey's winning penalty capped a performance showing plenty of courage and endeavour.
"Don't know. Just pick my spot and put it in it. Top corner and run like f***!," Haughey said of his spot-kick.
"I don't even know what’s going on. I'm so proud of the boys, it just shows – we've just beaten the champions of England – it just shows how good the team were.
"We'll think about [the quarter-final] after partying."

1r2qk7n1dlhsd1915rgs064svi.title: Seattle Sounders 2-1 Sporting Kansas City: Roldan grabs last-gasp winner
1r2qk7n1dlhsd1915rgs064svi.subtitle: Cristian Roldan scored in the 90th minute to propel the Seattle Sounders to a 2-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City.
paragraphs: The Seattle Sounders made it three straight MLS wins as their surge up the Western Conference continued with a last-gasp 2-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City.
Cristian Roldan grabbed the decisive goal at Lumen Field for the Sounders, who sit seventh in the West and are unbeaten in eight games.

SKC goalkeeper Stefan Cleveland was busy early on when he denied Peter Kingston, tipping a long-range attempt over the crossbar, before the visitors went close through Calvin Harris, who forced Alex Roldan into a goal-line clearance.

A flurry of SKC chances followed, and they eventually broke the deadlock when Andre Luiz struck on the cusp of half-time, just after Seattle's Andrew Thomas had made a sprawling save to keep out Stephen Afrifa's attempt.
Yet Seattle drew level just six minutes after the restart, with substitute Sebastian Gomez capitalising on Jordan Morris' fantastic work in the build-up.
Caden Clark went close to nudging the Sounders ahead, but Thomas was called upon to thwart Taylor Calheira at the other end.
That save paved the way for Cristian Roldan to come up with the goods in the 90th minute, as he pounced on a defensive mix-up to clinch all three points.
Sounders flip the script
This is the first time since May that Seattle have won an MLS game that they were trailing at half-time.
And after a 13-match winless streak, it is now three victories on the spin for the Sounders, who are looking good for a playoff place.

Seattle are now unbeaten in five straight matches against SKC (W4 D1). The Sounders managed to avoid defeat only three times in their previous ten games against Kansas City (W3 L7), dating back to 2019.
Sporting, who sit bottom of the West, may consider themselves unfortunate, though, considering they had the better chances, creating opportunities worth a combined 2.05 expected goals to 1.7 xG.
Luiz was in the thick of the action again for SKC.

He has been involved in three goals in his last two appearances, after becoming the first player to record a goal and an assist in a regular-season away match for Sporting since Dejan Joveljic against LA Galaxy in March, when he netted and laid one up against the Houston Dynamo in SKC's previous outing.

1rasmp0wsqkky1b4si49v1hw2h.title: Tielemans calls for togetherness amid Man Utd's recent slump
1rasmp0wsqkky1b4si49v1hw2h.subtitle: Manchester United are without a win in their last five games across all competitions, with a testing trip to Leeds United up next.
paragraphs: Youri Tielemans stressed the importance of the Manchester United squad sticking together after their midweek defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid.
The Red Devils' campaign hit a new low at the Metropolitano on Tuesday as they were beaten 2-0 by Atletico, with Leny Yoro's red card further compounding their misery.
Pablo Barrios opened the scoring with just 47 seconds on the clock, with Ademola Lookman capitalising on Yoro's dismissal in the 79th minute to seal a comfortable triumph.
United have now lost three of their last five games in all competitions (D2), as many as in their previous 21 games under Michael Carrick (W14 D4), piling the pressure on him.
Their five-game winless run is their longest stretch since a six-game streak in January 2025 (D2 L4), with a testing trip to Leeds United in the Premier League up next.

Tielemans made the move to Old Trafford this summer from Aston Villa, and while he is still getting used to his surroundings, he said his new team-mates must continue to trust each other if they are to turn their fortunes around.
"We did well in spells and our character and energy was very good," Tielemans said. "It is very hard to say after a defeat that there are positives.
"We just have to work hard, to keep working and keep trusting in our structure. We have to keep working, keep trusting each other and be together on this.
"[It is a] tough one. When you concede after a minute it is hard to get into the game straight away.
"We had more compactness at times. At times we were found out as they had the quality and were going to play through us."
Leeds, meanwhile, saw their unbeaten league run come to an end at the hands of Arsenal, with Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes completing the comeback in a 2-1 win.
The result saw Leeds lose a Premier League game in which they opened the scoring in the second half for the first time since October 1992 (1-2 vs QPR).
But Daniel Farke's side remain in the mix at the right end of the table, with Leeds seventh on nine points and just a point behind the top four in the early-season standings.
Farke was not surprised by what his players produced against the champions because of their consistency in recent months and had no complaints with the performance.

"[The result] has to do with the quality of players they could bring in," Farke said. "Once you're in the lead and push for the second, sometimes as a team not used to winning titles you can be a bit over-excited in possession.
"We could have been tidier and not given the ball away so easily. Sometimes it's [down to] a little bit of luck, there was not a big mistake, just a few details not spot on for the goal.

"They're able to bring quality players in to be so clinical in a difficult game for them. We're not in a position to speak about fighting for the Champions League or the title like Arsenal. I can't ask them for much more. No complaints."
Leeds United – Noah Okafor

Okafor scored both of Leeds' goals in their 2-1 win over United in April – the last Whites player to score in consecutive league appearances against the Red Devils was Mark Viduka between March 2001 and March 2002 (three in a row).
Viduka is also the only Leeds player with more than two Premier League goals against the Red Devils, netting four.
Manchester United – Bruno Fernandes
Fernandes has gone four Premier League games without scoring or assisting, his longest run since going seven in April and May 2025.
He has, however, been involved in nine goals in seven Premier League appearances against Leeds (two goals, three assists), the most by a United player against the Whites.
MATCH PREDICTION: LEEDS UNITED WIN

Leeds ended a run of 10 winless Premier League games against United with a 2-1 win at Old Trafford in April. The Whites haven't secured consecutive league wins over their rivals since winning both games in the 1971-72 campaign.
Farke's side are also unbeaten in their last seven Premier League home games (W4 D3), last having a longer unbeaten run at Elland Road between January and December 2001 (15 games).

Leeds go into the game ahead of United in the Premier League table for the first time in this fixture since September 2002 (excluding MD1), when they won 1-0 at Elland Road. A win for the Whites will put them six points clear of their rivals in the table as late as the seventh game of a season for just the second time.

United and Carrick, meanwhile, are desperate for a win. They have just six points in six Premier League games in 2026-27 (W1 D3 L2), their lowest after six league games since 1986-87 under Ron Atkinson (four).
For a second consecutive season, the Red Devils have no clean sheets in their first six games, the first time they’ve done so in back-to-back campaigns since 1930-31 and 1931-32.
The Red Devils are, however, unbeaten in their last seven away games against Leeds (W5 D2) since losing 1-0 in the Premier League in September 2002.
Manchester United – 31.6%

"They're able to bring quality players in to be so clinical in a difficult game for them. We're not in a position to speak about fighting for the Champions League or the title like Arsenal. I can't ask them for much more. No complaints."

PLAYERS TO WATCH

Leeds United – Noah Okafor

Okafor scored both of Leeds' goals in their 2-1 win over United in April – the last Whites player to score in consecutive league appearances against the Red Devils was Mark Viduka between March 2001 and March 2002 (three in a row).

Viduka is also the only Leeds player with more than two Premier League goals against the Red Devils, netting four.

Manchester United – Bruno Fernandes 

Fernandes has gone four Premier League games without scoring or assisting, his longest run since going seven in April and May 2025.

He has, however, been involved in nine goals in seven Premier League appearances against Leeds (two goals, three assists), the most by a United player against the Whites.

MATCH PREDICTION: LEEDS UNITED WIN

Leeds ended a run of 10 winless Premier League games against United with a 2-1 win at Old Trafford in April. The Whites haven't secured consecutive league wins over their rivals since winning both games in the 1971-72 campaign.

Farke's side are also unbeaten in their last seven Premier League home games (W4 D3), last having a longer unbeaten run at Elland Road between January and December 2001 (15 games).

Leeds go into the game ahead of United in the Premier League table for the first time in this fixture since September 2002 (excluding MD1), when they won 1-0 at Elland Road. A win for the Whites will put them six points clear of their rivals in the table as late as the seventh game of a season for just the second time. 

United and Carrick, meanwhile, are desperate for a win. They have just six points in six Premier League games in 2026-27 (W1 D3 L2), their lowest after six league games since 1986-87 under Ron Atkinson (four). 

For a second consecutive season, the Red Devils have no clean sheets in their first six games, the first time they’ve done so in back-to-back campaigns since 1930-31 and 1931-32.

The Red Devils are, however, unbeaten in their last seven away games against Leeds (W5 D2) since losing 1-0 in the Premier League in September 2002.

OPTA WIN PROBABILITY

Leeds United – 41.8%

Draw – 26.6%

Manchester United – 31.6%

1rcdfqtp0mepz13ff9xr39u36a.title: Modric 'ashamed' of Croatia's heaviest-ever loss to England
1rcdfqtp0mepz13ff9xr39u36a.subtitle: England's attackers ran riot in a 7-0 victory over Croatia, leaving experienced midfielder Luka Modric furious.
paragraphs: Luka Modric said Croatia's historic 7-0 defeat to England in the Nations League represented the first time he had felt "ashamed" in his illustrious international career.
Croatia slumped to the heaviest loss in their history on Saturday, in front of a crowd mostly made up of schoolchildren in Rijeka, due to UEFA-enforced restrictions on the home side.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka all scored before half-time, marking the first time England had seen four different players get on the scoresheet before the interval since March 2013 against San Marino (Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain).
Kane and Saka then got another goal apiece as Thomas Tuchel's side refused to ease up after the break, while Morgan Rogers came off the bench to score England's seventh.

Croatia had never previously lost a home game by more than a three-goal margin, going down 4-1 to the same opponents in September 2008, while a 6-0 loss in Spain in 2018 was their previous worst-ever defeat.
And the scoreline was no fluke, either, with England putting up a huge expected goals (xG) figure of 6.43 to Croatia's 1.39.
That is the largest figure ever amassed by any team in a Nations League game by some distance, surpassing Belarus' 4.89 xG against San Marino in September 2018.
And Modric did not mince his words concerning Croatia's display after full-time, saying: "You can't play football like that. We looked like we had four or five less players.
"It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance, without winning duels, making fouls, showing aggressiveness and togetherness.
"I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time, I feel ashamed after a game.
"You can lose, or you can play against an opponent who is better – and they are right now.
"But losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable. I feel ashamed."

Things do not get any easier for Croatia, either, as they host Spain in their final game of this international break on Tuesday, knowing a defeat would almost certainly end their chances of qualifying for the last eight.
"We need to come together and stay united because another difficult game awaits us," Modric added.
"We have to show our true selves, that we have fight and pride, desire, willpower and unity. You can't lose that overnight."
Head coach Slaven Bilic, meanwhile, was at a loss to explain Croatia's complete loss of organisation.
"It is difficult to say anything after a night like this. We are sad, disappointed, and I feel sorry for the fans and the children who were at the game," Bilic said.
"We talked, it is hardest for us, and we did not expect this would happen. I don't know what to call it, whether it's a blackout, but it's hard to analyse a game when you lose 7-0.
"We knew they were a top team, but that we couldn't match them in any way... that attacks your confidence, your will, and everything falls apart and goes the wrong way."

1rrmwt2hbhkj91tfxap38uxmjj.title: David enjoying 'breath of fresh air' since joining Atletico
1rrmwt2hbhkj91tfxap38uxmjj.subtitle: Jonathan David is in fine form for club and country, and he credits his move to Atletico Madrid as a key reason for his change in fortune.
paragraphs: Jonathan David believes joining Atletico Madrid this summer has given him a "breath of fresh air".
The 26-year-old joined Diego Simeone's side on a season-long loan from Juventus on deadline day, with Atletico reportedly having the option to make the move permanent for €25m.
David struggled at Juve last term, scoring eight goals across 46 appearances and providing five assists, though he has enjoyed a much better start to life in LaLiga.
The Canada international has directly contributed to four goals in as many games for Atleti (three goals, one assist), scoring in each of his three LaLiga appearances.
Before the international break, in which he has already scored the winner in Canada's 1-0 victory over Peru, David netted the match-defining goal in a 2-1 win in the Madrid derby.

David is the only player to have scored in each of his first three matches with Atleti in LaLiga in the 21st century, and the only Atleti player to have scored on his LaLiga debut and on his debut against Real Madrid in the competition since 2000.
"Maybe it’s a breath of fresh air. Maybe it helps that it’s a bit of a change of environment," said David when asked about his recent form.
"I play with a lot of players that have that quality to find the last pass. They make it pretty simple for me, to be honest. All I have to do is finish."
Canada head coach Jesse Marsch also revealed he played a small role in David's transfer to Atleti.
"I know Simeone from playing against him, from watching him over the years," said Marsch.

"[I said to him] if you want an attacking player that can score goals, has a lot of quality, and also [to] work for the team and give everything he has to the team, I can't think of a better striker than Jonathan David."

1rulmf99rtuh71pbh22wn95juw.title: Simeone confident Alvarez is 'getting closer to the player we want to see'
1rulmf99rtuh71pbh22wn95juw.subtitle: Julian Alvarez made little impact in Atletico Madrid's win over Manchester United, but Diego Simeone came to the striker's defence.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone believes Julian Alvarez is "getting closer to the player we want to see", despite his lacklustre display for Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.
Atleti defeated Manchester United 2-0 on Tuesday, with Pablo Barrios and Ademola Lookman scoring either side of half-time at Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
Barrios’ opener for Atleti after 47 seconds was their second-earliest goal in the Champions League, behind only Conor Gallagher’s strike against Real Madrid in March 2025 (27 seconds).
Since the start of 2023-24, only Arsenal and Bayern Munich (both 16) have won more home games in the Champions League than Atleti (P19 W15 D1 L3).
However, Alvarez cut a frustrated figure. He hit the woodwork, but lost all three of his duels and recorded the fewest touches of any starter for the hosts (34).

The 26-year-old, who wanted to leave Atleti in the summer and was the subject of interest from both Real Madrid and Barcelona, is yet to score at club level this season, but Simeone insists the striker is on the right path.
When asked about the mixed reception Alvarez received in front of the home fans, Simeone said: "What the fans do is related to what the players give.
"They want to see the best of the players, and Julian is giving that. He had the chance to score. He's getting closer to the player we want to see.
"We need him."
This was Alvarez's first start for Atleti since their defeat to Liverpool in their Champions League opener in September, following his brief injury before the international break.
He has been jeered at times so far this term by Atletico fans, who were unimpressed by his desire to leave.
Atleti now face two away trips across all competitions, first against Espanyol in LaLiga before a trip to Stuttgart in the Champions League.

1ry2cnu06y6yv1s6w7fz2va4cq.title: Belgium 3-0 Turkiye: De Bruyne steals the show with two stunners
1ry2cnu06y6yv1s6w7fz2va4cq.subtitle: Belgium returned to winning ways in the Nations League as Kevin De Bruyne scored twice in a 3-0 victory over Turkiye.
paragraphs: Kevin De Bruyne scored two stunning goals as Belgium defeated Turkiye 3-0 in the Nations League.

The Napoli midfielder scored either side of half-time at Stade Maurice Dufrasne, while Romelu Lukaku came off the bench to also get on the scoresheet and help Mark van Bommel secure his first home win as Belgium head coach.
De Bruyne needed just 10 minutes to break the deadlock, playing a give-and-go with Dodi Lukebakio before poking through the legs of Abdulkerim Bardakci and finding the bottom-right corner.

Both sides had their chances before half-time; Lukebakio saw a powerful strike pushed onto the woodwork by Ugurcan Cakir, while Merih Demiral inexplicably fired over from inside the six-yard box from Zeki Celik's low cross.

Lukebakio struck the frame of the goal again early in the second half before Senne Lammens got down quickly to keep out Yunus Akgun, and the goalkeeper's efforts were repaid by De Bruyne at the other end.
After Youri Tielemans regained possession just outside the box, he teed up De Bruyne, who wonderfully curled into the top-left corner from distance to give Belgium some much-needed breathing room.

Lukaku then wrapped up the victory in the 76th minute, converting from Charles De Ketelaere's low centre with ease, while Belgium also managed to hold onto their clean sheet despite late pressure from Turkiye.
Belgium's veterans thriving in new era

Van Bommel's introduction as head coach marked a new era for Belgium, and while the likes of Mika Godts and Lukebakio are proving their worth under the new boss, it was the familiar faces of De Bruyne and Lukaku who made the crucial difference.

Although Belgium's 1.24 expected goals (xG) tally was lower than Turkiye's 1.33, De Bruyne's two goals accounted for just 0.17 xG, highlighting the quality of the midfielder's strikes to give the hosts a 2-0 lead.
De Bruyne also created three chances, a tally only bettered by Godts (four) for Belgium, while he also won five of his 10 duels before being replaced in the 82nd minute.

For Turkiye, meanwhile, it was the same old story. They failed to take their opportunities in front of goal, which is what caused their group-stage exit at the World Cup, despite Arda Guler creating a match-high five chances.

1s0vejma7m6161a0bf5945j9fb.title: 'Don't make a big deal out of it' – Jesus shuts down reports of rift with Ronaldo
1s0vejma7m6161a0bf5945j9fb.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo cut a frustrated figure on Portugal's bench last time out, but Jorge Jesus attempted to assuage any fears of a rift.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus insisted there is no rift between himself and Cristiano Ronaldo after the 41-year-old was an unused substitute against Norway in the Nations League.
Ronaldo featured from the start in Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales, though he was taken off in the 67th minute and replaced by Goncalo Ramos.

Jesus had stated before the 2-1 win against Norway that he planned for Ronaldo to participate, but he did not bring him on during the victory, with Portugal's captain then training away from his team-mates on Monday and Tuesday.
Media reports suggested there had been a "crisis" meeting between Jesus, Ronaldo and the Portugal Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca to clear the air.
But at a press conference ahead of Portugal's clash with Denmark on Thursday, Jesus, who also managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, insisted there were no issues between the pair.
"I don't have one player; I have 23 players," Jesus said.
"Regarding Ronaldo, let me ask two questions; I won't answer any more. The main thing is Denmark.
"It's true that I made an agreement with him, just like I made a plan with Bruno Fernandes. I told Cris that he wouldn't play in the games in Norway and Denmark.
"I know his physical condition well; I was with him in Saudi Arabia. In games every three days, he rarely played. He never trained on the first and second days after the games.
"I agreed with him. That's what happened. I don't go to the bench thinking that, at the 60th minute, I'm going to take Carlos Daniel off. That's not how I am on the bench.
"The game dictates what I'm going to do. I agreed that he wouldn't play, but I might also need him in the final minutes... If the game required it.

"I worked with Cris for a year. It seems like there's already something going on between me and him. Don't make a big deal out of it; there's nothing going on. It was the same plan with Bruno Fernandes.
"Status is one thing; the rules are another."
Asked again about the friction between the pair, Jesus added: "Any player who warms up and then doesn't come on – no one is happy.
"Much less Cris, Pele, [Diego] Maradona. 'Warm up for thirty minutes, me?' Then, as the coach, I decided they weren't included."
Portugal are looking to continue their perfect start to the Nations League in Copenhagen, having taken six points so far to sit top of Group A4.
Denmark, meanwhile, are third, having followed up a 3-2 defeat to Norway with a 2-0 victory over Wales last time out.

1s4tz93967h5n1e5fvk2uf62ww.title: De la Fuente: Spain have recovered the spirit of 2010
1s4tz93967h5n1e5fvk2uf62ww.subtitle: Spain are showing no signs of slowing down as they prepare to play their first match on home soil since winning the World Cup.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente believes Spain have "recovered the spirit of 2010" with their recent exploits as his side prepare to host Croatia in the Nations League.
Spain are the reigning European and world champions, having lifted the World Cup for the second time in July by beating Argentina in the final.
On their way to clinching both titles, they have strung together a 39-game unbeaten streak (across 90 minutes), winning 30 of those matches (D9).
They extended their run with a stunning 3-2 comeback win over England, with Mikel Oyarzabal coming off the bench to haunt the Three Lions once more by scoring the winner.
Spain's next match will see them play on home soil for the first time since winning the World Cup, as they will host Croatia in Seville.
"For us, it is a pride to see our country committed to the national team," De la Fuente said in his press conference.
"Where we are going, we have recovered the spirit of 2010; people are proud to be Spanish.
"I am honoured to be the national coach of my country. I have a house in Seville, and it causes me a very special emotion."
Spain are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Croatia, winning two and drawing the other – though they eventually won that match on penalties in the Nations League.
Like La Roja, Croatia also opened with a win on Saturday, beating Czechia 2-1, which only leaves them behind Spain on goal difference in Group A3.
"Of course, I think Croatia can compete, and the first ones who have to believe it are them," De la Fuente said of their opponents.
"If not, they would not run. There is no rival or perfect day. The height of these situations is that even if you are superior to the opponent, you can lose.
"We know Croatia well; we have played a lot with them. They have world-class players and a very competent new coach.
"We have to give a better version of the one we gave in London. Footballers understand it that way. Every day we demand more from ourselves because the opponents are more complicated every day."

1s8jganrd6uma1osrapgyc7pp7.title: Bournemouth 3-0 AC Milan: Rose's side stay perfect with famous victory
1s8jganrd6uma1osrapgyc7pp7.subtitle: Bournemouth blew 10-man AC Milan away at Vitality Stadium, with a fast start setting them up for a brilliant victory in the Europa League.
paragraphs: Bournemouth cruised to a famous 3-0 victory over 10-man AC Milan at Vitality Stadium in the Europa League to maintain their 100% start.

Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier both netted from the penalty spot in the first 32 minutes, with Mike Maignan sent off after giving away the second, before Amine Adli capped the win with a stunning free-kick late on.
It was a dream start for Bournemouth, who won an early penalty after Koni De Winter's raised arm blocked a right-sided cross.
The spot-kick was given following a VAR review, and Kluivert coolly slotted into the bottom-right corner to give the hosts an eighth-minute lead.

Ryan Christie, Evanilson and James Hill all saw chances saved by the increasingly frustrated Maignan before things went from bad to worse for Ruben Amorim's side when the goalkeeper's temper boiled over.
During a corner, Maignan needlessly pushed out at Hill, shoving the defender's face, with the referee sending off the Milan captain in the 27th minute and awarding Bournemouth a second penalty.

Lorenzo Torriani's first touch after coming on saw him pluck the ball out of his net after Tavernier emphatically finished into the bottom-left corner five minutes after Maignan was shown the red card.
Bournemouth's dominance continued after the break, with Kluivert's whipped cross almost sneaking in at the far post before Rayan got caught under a header that he thumped over.

Christie saw more chances go begging, with Adrien Truffert also firing over from distance, but Adli added the late gloss to the scoreline when he bent a sublime 20-yard free-kick over the wall 84 minutes in.
It almost got better for the Cherries late on as Rayan forced a great save out of Torriani from a tight angle, but Bournemouth had already got the job done.
Bournemouth look completely at home as they make history
Marco Rose finally got his first Premier League win last weekend, and they followed it up with another incredible result in the Europa League, where they have looked completely at ease this term.

They are the first English side to win their first three matches in major European competition since Sunderland in the 1973-74 Cup Winners' Cup, and it means they are one of just five teams left with a perfect record in the competition after three games, leaving them third in the table.

From the very first whistle, they looked in total control at Vitality Stadium, putting Milan on the ropes from the get-go, and the visitors were not helped by De Winter's handball or Maignan's moment of madness.

It was a tough situation for Torriani to step into, and it means two different Milan goalkeepers have conceded penalty goals in the same European match for the first time since the data has been available (from 2009-10, when the Europa League was rebranded).

Bournemouth barely gave Milan a moment to breathe, firing 20 shots at their goal (seven on target) worth 3.11 expected goals (xG). Milan failed to test Michele Di Gregorio with any of their three attempts at the other end (accumulated just 0.11 xG).

It was a sorry return to England for Amorim, who failed to beat Bournemouth in any of his three games as Manchester United boss, while this is the first time he has lost an away game in the group/league phase of the Europa League, and Milan sit 24th with only one win to their name (L2).

1sexch8cprg911c57jhr1vh2gd.title: Aston Villa sack Arroyo following winless WSL start
1sexch8cprg911c57jhr1vh2gd.subtitle: Having been thrashed 4-0 by Tottenham on Sunday, Aston Villa have relieved Natalia Arroyo of her duties.
paragraphs: Aston Villa have sacked manager Natalia Arroyo following their winless start to the Women's Super League season.
Villa sit 13th in the 14-team table after four games, having played out two draws and two defeats.

Things started promisingly as they held title favourites Chelsea to a 1-1 draw on the opening matchday, but a pair of heavy defeats to Manchester City (1-4) and Tottenham (0-4), either side of another 1-1 draw at Brighton, have left them marooned in the relegation play-off spot.
And on Tuesday, Villa confirmed Arroyo had been relieved of her duties, with women's technical advisor Brian Sorensen taking charge until a permanent successor is found.
The club said: "Everyone at Aston Villa would like to thank Natalia for her efforts and wish her all the best in her future endeavours."

Arroyo, who previously coached Real Sociedad for four years, took the reins in January 2025 and oversaw a strong end to that season, with Villa finishing sixth after being discussed as potential relegation candidates.
Villa then finished ninth in 2025-26 and failed to kick on at the start of the current campaign, despite making nine new signings in a busy transfer window.

1shh76g3nm75i1cl4upo3vxppe.title: Napoli 4-3 Bodo/Glimt: McTominay brace helps Allegri to first Champions League win
1shh76g3nm75i1cl4upo3vxppe.subtitle: Massimiliano Allegri finally has a first Champions League victory with Napoli under his belt as they edged a thriller against Bodo/Glimt.
paragraphs: Napoli earned their first win of the 2026-27 Champions League after edging Bodo/Glimt 4-3 in a topsy-turvy clash at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
Matteo Politano struck in the opening minute, before the two teams traded goals between Jens Petter Hauge, Scott McTominay and Andreas Helmersen.
McTominay's second of the match was then followed by an Odin Bjortuft own goal, which eventually proved the winner after Sonder Fet set up a nervy finale with a 94th-minute header.
There were only 54 seconds on the clock when Politano rifled in Leonardo Spinazzola's pinpoint cross with a stunning volley.
Noa Lang and Rasmus Hojlund both passed up presentable opportunities before Hauge equalised against the run of play with a lovely low curler through the crowded Napoli box 27 minutes in.

But Napoli were back in front four minutes before the break after McTominay combined with Kevin De Bruyne and got a stroke of luck as his strike looped in despite Nikita Haikin getting a full hand on it.
McTominay then struck the post with a first-time effort on the hour, and it proved a costly miss as Bodo equalised again in the 62nd minute when Helmersen drilled his low strike past Alex Meret.
Bodo continued to push but McTominay put Napoli back in front against the run of play 13 minutes later, rising high to nod Politano's cross past a helpless Haikin.

With two minutes of the 90 remaining, Bjortuft slid in to try and block Giovane's low cross from the left, but his touch inadvertently helped it sneak in at the near post, as Haikin had been poised to collect behind him.

Fet, who had an impressive game as he also racked up assists for the first two goals, nodded in from a yard out after Bjortuft's looping volley struck the underside of the bar, but there was not enough time for Bodo to find a late equaliser.
Allegri eases some pressure as Italian sides enjoy Champions League
Massimiliano Allegri has found himself under some pressure after his start to life at Napoli, but he now has a first Champions League win under his belt that moves the team into the play-off places.

In fact, the win ended a five-game winless streak in the competition (D1 L4), and they bagged four goals in a Champions League match for the first time in 25 games since beating Ajax 4-2 in October 2022.
At 54 seconds, Politano's opener for Napoli was their fastest-ever goal in the Champions League, but it was McTominay who stole the show.

He has scored 29 goals in all competitions since joining the Partenopei, 11 more than any other player for the club in that time (Hojlund has 18). He also now has seven Champions League goals, the outright most by a Scottish player (Kenny Miller next on five).

But Napoli were not the only team that netted four goals, with Roma also getting off the mark in the competition as they brushed aside Slovan Bratislava 4-0, with Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina, Niccolo Pisilli and Donyell Malen doing the damage.

Elsewhere, though, there was disappointment for Atletico Madrid, whose six-game winning streak in all competitions came to an end. They came from behind to draw 1-1 with Stuttgart – who had dominated the first half – with Julian Alvarez scoring, though they had to hold onto the point after Morten Hjulmand's sending-off.

1srlhmbq04sel1lw9qkv72t7pg.title: Premier League predictions: All eyes on Anfield as Man City renew Liverpool rivalry
1srlhmbq04sel1lw9qkv72t7pg.subtitle: Manchester City are the only side with a 100% record in the Premier League, but that will be put to the test against Liverpool at Anfield.
paragraphs: With the return of Premier League action following the international break, the Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 season.
Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record after Arsenal were thumped 3-0 by Brighton, who are flying high in third.
Brentford, Leeds United, Liverpool and Everton are the other unbeaten clubs, while at the other end, Tottenham prop up the table.
Roberto De Zerbi's side are still yet to win in the Premier League this term – though they did get their first league goals of the campaign in their 3-2 loss to Aston Villa.
Fulham and Bournemouth are also yet to win, while Coventry City got off the mark before the hiatus after they beat Nottingham Forest.
Matchday 6 sees fixtures take place on Saturday, Sunday and Monday across a bumper weekend.
Ahead of what should be another intriguing group of Premier League fixtures, let's check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.
ARSENAL V LEEDS UNITED
Arsenal get the Premier League action back underway on Saturday, looking to bounce back from their disappointing loss to Brighton against Leeds United.

That was their heaviest defeat since May 2023 (also 3-0 vs Brighton), but since the start of 2024, the Gunners have only lost back-to-back Premier League games once (in April 2026), with this being their 100th league game since then.

The good news for Arsenal is that they have won nine of their last 10 Premier League games against Leeds (D1), including each of the last seven, while the Whites have won just one of their last 17 away league games against the reigning top-flight champions (D6 L10).

Arsenal are our predictive model's most confident pick of MD6, with a 68.9% win probability to Leeds' 13.7%, but Saturday's visitors have started a league campaign unbeaten in five matches (W2 D3) for the first time since their promotion-winning campaign of 2019-20.

Mikel Arteta – who signed a three-year contract extension with Arsenal this week – has won all four of his Premier League games against Daniel Farke, his joint-best 100%-win rate against a manager in the top flight (level with Gary O'Neil), and the German's worst 100% loss rate against any manager during his career in England.
ASTON VILLA V BRENTFORD
Later in the day, Brentford (26.2%) are looking to continue their fine start away to Aston Villa (47.8%), who finally got their first league win against Spurs.

Brentford have kicked off a league campaign unbeaten in five games (W2 D3) for the first time since 2013-14 in League One, last having a longer unbeaten streak at the start of a season in 2006-07 (first seven in the third tier).
They're unbeaten in their last seven top-flight matches (W2 D5) overall and are looking for a third straight Premier League win over Villa, after doing the double over them last term.
But the Villans have lost just one of their last 11 home league games against Brentford (W4 D6), though that was a 1-0 defeat in this exact fixture last season.
Villa have recorded the fewest shots (48), shots on target (12) and touches in the opposition box (81) in 2026-27, stats Unai Emery will be keen to improve upon.
CHELSEA V BOURNEMOUTH
It has been a tumultuous start for Xabi Alonso at Chelsea, who are looking to end their three-match winless streak in all competitions against Bournemouth.

Chelsea's five league games under Alonso have seen 22 total goals (10 for, 12 against), and they are the first team to score 10+ goals and concede 10+ goals across that span of matches in a Premier League campaign.
The Blues, who are given a 51.8% win likelihood, are unbeaten in their last nine top-flight meetings with Bournemouth (W4 D5), with each of the last three ending level (22.9% chance of another draw).

Marco Rose is the second manager to fail to win his first five top-flight matches with the Cherries, alongside his predecessor Andoni Iraola (first nine), but only Arsenal (27) and Man City (23) have won more away points in the Premier League in 2026 than Bournemouth (20 – W5 D5 L1), who were victorious in 25.3% of our pre-match simulations.
IPSWICH TOWN V FULHAM
Fulham are another team still seeking their first win after being denied by a last-gasp Manchester United equaliser last time out, and they travel to Ipswich Town next.

Ipswich are the favourites at 44.8%, but they are winless in their last seven league games against Fulham (D3 L4), though both meetings in the 2024-25 campaign ended level, and there is a 26.9% chance of another draw.

Fulham are winless in all four of their top-flight games against Ipswich (D3 L1), the joint-most they have faced a side without ever winning in the competition (also four versus Watford), but they are assigned a 28.3% chance of ending that run on Saturday.

The Cottagers have not failed to win six successive league games in the same season since their final 10 matches of 2020-21 (D2 L8), and they have lost just one of their last 15 Premier League games against promoted sides (W9 D5).
SUNDERLAND V BRIGHTON
The final 15:00 kick off pits Sunderland against Brighton, with Fabian Hurzeler's visitors looking to pick up where they left off before the international break.
Brighton have won their last two Premier League games by an aggregate score of 8-0. Only in October 2018 have they won three successive matches in the competition without conceding.
The Seagulls have been hugely impressive this season, leading all teams in the Premier League for high turnovers (56), passes allowed per defensive action (7.4), and possession share (64.8%).

But while Sunderland have suffered back-to-back defeats, might the Black Cats' direct style nullify their opponents' high press? Only Man City (19) have had fewer high turnovers against them in the Premier League this season than Sunderland (20).
The Opta supercomputer still favours Brighton, who hold a 41.3% win probability, but Sunderland should not be ruled out at 33.1%.
MANCHESTER UNITED V TOTTENHAM
Saturday's late kick-off sees two under-pressure managers face one another at Old Trafford, as Manchester United host Tottenham.
With five points on the board, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League season through five matchdays, also picking up five points in 2014-15.
Michael Carrick's men are only averaging one point per game this campaign, after the Red Devils averaged 2.3 points in their 17 matches under the former midfielder last season.

Spurs, meanwhile, could fail to win their first six games of a league season for just the fourth time in their history, after 1912-13 (first 12), 1955-56 (first six) and 2008-09 (first six). Among all ever-present Premier League sides, they have accumulated the fewest points in 2026 (18).
Spurs have lost 25 away games against United in the Premier League, with only Everton against Arsenal (26) losing more on the road against a single opponent.
And the predictive model is siding with the Red Devils, who are assigned a 54.1% chance of victory.

Spurs are only given a 22.3% chance of taking all three points, though De Zerbi did win his only previous away Premier League game against United, with Brighton in September 2023. Only four visiting managers have won on their first two trips to Old Trafford in the competition – Sam Allardyce, Ronald Koeman, Pep Guardiola and Iraola.
CRYSTAL PALACE V NOTTINGHAM FOREST
There are two early kick-offs taking place on Sunday, one of which is a grudge match between Crystal Palace and their former boss Oliver Glasner, now at Nottingham Forest.

Though Glasner oversaw the most successful period in Palace's history, winning the FA Cup, the Community Shield and the Conference League, his move to Forest – who replaced Palace in last season's Europa League after they were expelled over a breach of multi-club ownership rules – left something of a sour taste.
At 28.8%, this is deemed the most likely draw of MD6, with Palace (36.3%) assigned a slightly higher chance of victory than Forest (34.9%).

Managers to have formerly taken charge of Palace in the Premier League have only won one of seven previous matches against them in the competition after leaving (D2 L4), with Allardyce beating them with Everton in February 2018.

However, the Eagles have lost both of their Premier League games at Selhurst Park this season; only in 1997-98, 2004-05, and 2017-18 have they ever lost their opening three home matches of a league campaign.

And Forest have only lost one of their last seven away league games (W4 D2), scoring 2+ goals in all seven, their longest ever such run in the top flight. There have been just seven instances of any team scoring multiple goals in 8+ consecutive away Premier League matches, most recently Bournemouth from November 2024 to February 2025.

Hull City have been one of the surprise packages this season, only suffering their first loss on matchday five against Newcastle United. They will look to get back on track at home to Everton, who are yet to suffer defeat.

Hull have made no apologies for going direct – in fact, their possession share of 32.3% is the lowest on record (since 2003-04) by any team during a single Premier League campaign, and their 203 successful passes per game are the fewest since Cardiff City in 2018-19 (172).

The Tigers are the only team yet to concede at home in the Premier League this term, though, and they could become only the third promoted side to keep clean sheets in their first three home games of a season, after Swansea in 2011-12 (first four) and Watford in 2015-16 (three).
Everton are winless in their last seven Premier League away games (D4 L3), yet the supercomputer still assigns them a 45.7% chance of victory to Hull's 28.4%.
LIVERPOOL V MANCHESTER CITY
The international break was an eventful one for Manchester City, who take centre-stage for Sunday's late kick-off as they face rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

Having been found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, City must turn their attention back to on-pitch matters, as they look to continue their perfect start under Enzo Maresca.

Maresca could become just the fourth manager to win his first six matches in charge of a club in the competition, after Carlo Ancelotti with Chelsea, Guardiola with City, and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer with Manchester United.
And his team are slight favourites at 40.7%, with Liverpool assigned a 34.6% chance of victory and a 24.7% hope of earning a point.

The away side has won two of the last three Premier League games between Liverpool and City, as many times as in the previous 32. Only in 2002-03 have there been back-to-back away wins in this Premier League fixture, and City triumphed 2-1 on Merseyside in February.

Though they have drawn three of their opening five games, Liverpool are still unbeaten, and Iraola could become only the third permanent Reds boss to avoid defeat in his first six top-flight matches in charge, after Bob Paisley in 1974 and Joe Fagan in 1983.

This will be the first Premier League match between Liverpool and City without Jurgen Klopp or Guardiola in the dugout since March 2015, when Brendan Rodgers' Reds beat Manuel Pellegrini's Citizens 2-1 at Anfield.
COVENTRY CITY V NEWCASTLE UNITED
There is also a Monday night matchup at the Coventry Building Society Arena, as Frank Lampard's Coventry City look to back up their first win of the campaign at home to Newcastle United.

Coventry could become only the second team in English top-flight history to lose their opening four games of a season without scoring before winning their next two, after Derby County did so way back in 1899-00.
But with a 29.8% win probability, the Sky Blues are outsiders – Newcastle are assigned a 44.8% chance of taking all three points.
Matthias Jaissle's eight points are the most by a manager in his first five Premier League games in charge of Newcastle since Alan Pardew in January 2011 (nine).
Another win here would give the German the most points in his first six in charge of the club in the competition since Allardyce in September 2007 (11).
