Fulham are another team still seeking their first win after being denied by a last-gasp Manchester United equaliser last time out, and they travel to Ipswich Town next.

Ipswich are the favourites at 44.8%, but they are winless in their last seven league games against Fulham (D3 L4), though both meetings in the 2024-25 campaign ended level, and there is a 26.9% chance of another draw.

Fulham are winless in all four of their top-flight games against Ipswich (D3 L1), the joint-most they have faced a side without ever winning in the competition (also four versus Watford), but they are assigned a 28.3% chance of ending that run on Saturday.

The Cottagers have not failed to win six successive league games in the same season since their final 10 matches of 2020-21 (D2 L8), and they have lost just one of their last 15 Premier League games against promoted sides (W9 D5).

SUNDERLAND V BRIGHTON

The final 15:00 kick off pits Sunderland against Brighton, with Fabian Hurzeler's visitors looking to pick up where they left off before the international break.

Brighton have won their last two Premier League games by an aggregate score of 8-0. Only in October 2018 have they won three successive matches in the competition without conceding.

The Seagulls have been hugely impressive this season, leading all teams in the Premier League for high turnovers (56), passes allowed per defensive action (7.4), and possession share (64.8%).

But while Sunderland have suffered back-to-back defeats, might the Black Cats' direct style nullify their opponents' high press? Only Man City (19) have had fewer high turnovers against them in the Premier League this season than Sunderland (20).

The Opta supercomputer still favours Brighton, who hold a 41.3% win probability, but Sunderland should not be ruled out at 33.1%.

MANCHESTER UNITED V TOTTENHAM

Saturday's late kick-off sees two under-pressure managers face one another at Old Trafford, as Manchester United host Tottenham.

With five points on the board, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League season through five matchdays, also picking up five points in 2014-15.

Michael Carrick's men are only averaging one point per game this campaign, after the Red Devils averaged 2.3 points in their 17 matches under the former midfielder last season.

Spurs, meanwhile, could fail to win their first six games of a league season for just the fourth time in their history, after 1912-13 (first 12), 1955-56 (first six) and 2008-09 (first six). Among all ever-present Premier League sides, they have accumulated the fewest points in 2026 (18).

Spurs have lost 25 away games against United in the Premier League, with only Everton against Arsenal (26) losing more on the road against a single opponent. 

And the predictive model is siding with the Red Devils, who are assigned a 54.1% chance of victory. 

Spurs are only given a 22.3% chance of taking all three points, though De Zerbi did win his only previous away Premier League game against United, with Brighton in September 2023. Only four visiting managers have won on their first two trips to Old Trafford in the competition – Sam Allardyce, Ronald Koeman, Pep Guardiola and Iraola. 

CRYSTAL PALACE V NOTTINGHAM FOREST

There are two early kick-offs taking place on Sunday, one of which is a grudge match between Crystal Palace and their former boss Oliver Glasner, now at Nottingham Forest. 

Though Glasner oversaw the most successful period in Palace's history, winning the FA Cup, the Community Shield and the Conference League, his move to Forest – who replaced Palace in last season's Europa League after they were expelled over a breach of multi-club ownership rules – left something of a sour taste.

At 28.8%, this is deemed the most likely draw of MD6, with Palace (36.3%) assigned a slightly higher chance of victory than Forest (34.9%).

Managers to have formerly taken charge of Palace in the Premier League have only won one of seven previous matches against them in the competition after leaving (D2 L4), with Allardyce beating them with Everton in February 2018.

However, the Eagles have lost both of their Premier League games at Selhurst Park this season; only in 1997-98, 2004-05, and 2017-18 have they ever lost their opening three home matches of a league campaign.

And Forest have only lost one of their last seven away league games (W4 D2), scoring 2+ goals in all seven, their longest ever such run in the top flight. There have been just seven instances of any team scoring multiple goals in 8+ consecutive away Premier League matches, most recently Bournemouth from November 2024 to February 2025.

HULL CITY V EVERTON

Hull City have been one of the surprise packages this season, only suffering their first loss on matchday five against Newcastle United. They will look to get back on track at home to Everton, who are yet to suffer defeat.  

Hull have made no apologies for going direct – in fact, their possession share of 32.3% is the lowest on record (since 2003-04) by any team during a single Premier League campaign, and their 203 successful passes per game are the fewest since Cardiff City in 2018-19 (172).

The Tigers are the only team yet to concede at home in the Premier League this term, though, and they could become only the third promoted side to keep clean sheets in their first three home games of a season, after Swansea in 2011-12 (first four) and Watford in 2015-16 (three). 

Everton are winless in their last seven Premier League away games (D4 L3), yet the supercomputer still assigns them a 45.7% chance of victory to Hull's 28.4%.

LIVERPOOL V MANCHESTER CITY

The international break was an eventful one for Manchester City, who take centre-stage for Sunday's late kick-off as they face rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

Having been found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, City must turn their attention back to on-pitch matters, as they look to continue their perfect start under Enzo Maresca.

Maresca could become just the fourth manager to win his first six matches in charge of a club in the competition, after Carlo Ancelotti with Chelsea, Guardiola with City, and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer with Manchester United.

And his team are slight favourites at 40.7%, with Liverpool assigned a 34.6% chance of victory and a 24.7% hope of earning a point.

The away side has won two of the last three Premier League games between Liverpool and City, as many times as in the previous 32. Only in 2002-03 have there been back-to-back away wins in this Premier League fixture, and City triumphed 2-1 on Merseyside in February.

Though they have drawn three of their opening five games, Liverpool are still unbeaten, and Iraola could become only the third permanent Reds boss to avoid defeat in his first six top-flight matches in charge, after Bob Paisley in 1974 and Joe Fagan in 1983.

This will be the first Premier League match between Liverpool and City without Jurgen Klopp or Guardiola in the dugout since March 2015, when Brendan Rodgers' Reds beat Manuel Pellegrini's Citizens 2-1 at Anfield.

COVENTRY CITY V NEWCASTLE UNITED

There is also a Monday night matchup at the Coventry Building Society Arena, as Frank Lampard's Coventry City look to back up their first win of the campaign at home to Newcastle United.

Coventry could become only the second team in English top-flight history to lose their opening four games of a season without scoring before winning their next two, after Derby County did so way back in 1899-00.

But with a 29.8% win probability, the Sky Blues are outsiders – Newcastle are assigned a 44.8% chance of taking all three points. 

Matthias Jaissle's eight points are the most by a manager in his first five Premier League games in charge of Newcastle since Alan Pardew in January 2011 (nine). 

Another win here would give the German the most points in his first six in charge of the club in the competition since Allardyce in September 2007 (11).

1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.title: Sunderland hand Le Fee new five-year contract
1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.subtitle: Having helped Sunderland qualify for the Europa League and scored their first European goal in 53 years, Enzo Le Fee has penned a new deal.
paragraphs: Sunderland's creative midfielder Enzo Le Fee has signed a new five-year contract with the club.
Le Fee joined the Black Cats on loan from Roma in January 2025, with that deal containing a purchase obligation if they were to be promoted from the Championship.
The Frenchman immediately assumed a key role under Regis Le Bris, starting in a 2-1 play-off final victory over Sheffield United, which led to him becoming a permanent Sunderland player for £19m.
And he has continued to shine in the Premier League, making 41 appearances in the competition while scoring six goals and providing seven assists.

His 13 goal involvements and 61 chances created are both team-high totals since the start of 2025-26, and those figures helped propel Sunderland to a seventh-place finish and Europa League qualification last term.
Last week, Le Fee scored from the penalty spot to secure a 1-0 victory over AZ at the Stadium of Light, in Sunderland's opening match in that competition.

That made him the Black Cats' first goalscorer in Europe since October 1973, when Micky Horswill scored their second goal in a 2-1 victory at home to Sporting CP in the Cup Winners' Cup, only for the Lisbon giants to recover in the return fixture and progress 3-2 on aggregate.
"I'm really happy to have signed a new contract with Sunderland," Le Fee told the club's website, having agreed fresh terms to run until 2031.
"From the moment I arrived, I've felt the passion of the supporters and the ambition of everyone at the club – I've loved my time here.
"We've achieved something special together over the past couple of seasons, but I believe this is just the beginning.
"I feel very settled here and I'm excited to continue developing, competing at the highest level and helping the club move forward.
"I'm very proud to wear the Sunderland shirt and I can't wait to see what we can achieve together in the years ahead."

Having lost 5-3 to Manchester City in a thrilling encounter prior to the international break, Sunderland have four points from five Premier League games this season, with Brighton their next opponents on October 10.

1sx1zurasqtk41pnunepb1n4qu.title: Czechia 0-2 England: Gordon and Kane score again as Tuchel's side get off the mark
1sx1zurasqtk41pnunepb1n4qu.subtitle: England are off the mark in the 2026-27 Nations League, using their numerical advantage to earn a 2-0 victory over Czechia.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both hit the back of the net for the second game running, this time helping England to a 2-0 win over 10-man Czechia in the Nations League.
England were aided by Pavel Sulc's first-half red card, and this time, when Gordon and Kane gave them the lead, they held onto it for their first victory in Group A3.

Czechia gave England an early scare after Elliot Anderson failed to intercept a long pass down the left wing and Sulc raced onto it, but James Trafford rushed out to smother the shot while one-on-one.

Lukas Cerv then volleyed wide of the target before England got their first clear opening when Morgan Rogers turned in the box and bent an effort onto the far post, with Anderson's follow-up blocked by Robin Hranac.
But the momentum changed in the 25th minute; Sulc caught Anderson above the ankle with his studs, and his yellow card was upgraded to a red following a VAR review.
Gordon saw a tight-angled shot parried just after the half-hour mark, while Kane forced Matej Kovar into a fine stop on the stroke of half-time.
But it took England just 67 seconds after the restart to break the deadlock, with Trent Alexander-Arnold whipping in a stunning cross, which Gordon nodded past the goalkeeper.

Lewis Hall sent the ball trickling narrowly wide as England upped the pressure, which told in the 68th minute as Kane latched onto the loose ball after Rogers tripped and swept a low finish into the bottom-right corner.
Czechia were not out of the game, though, with Adam Hlozek forcing Trafford into a fine stop nine minutes later from the edge of the box after a quick counter-attack.
Eberechi Eze and Jude Bellingham tested Kovar late on, but the Czechia goalkeeper kept the score down; though with a numerical disadvantage, they could not take advantage of that.
England find their groove in Prague
After losing their opener, there was slightly more pressure on England to get a win in this game, though Thomas Tuchel was insistent pre-match that it did not fall into the "must-win" category.
Either way, it was three points that England needed after the disheartening loss to the world champions.
Czechia, despite starting brightly, were up against it after the red card - the last side to beat England with 10 men were France in June 2017 (3-2 home win).

It was two in-form players that ultimately proved the difference. Gordon now has four goals and four assists across his last nine appearances, while he was assisted by Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first England appearance in almost two years.
As for Kane, he has now netted five goals in seven Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition.

Despite having 22 shots worth 1.37 expected goals (xG) in a strong attacking display, Tuchel will be keen to focus on the clean sheet, given England had conceded 13 goals in their six games before this.

Trafford - the first England goalkeeper other than Jordan Pickford to start consecutive games since Nick Pope in September 2022 - made two big saves, though the Three Lions only conceded six shots worth 0.33 xG overall.

1sz3yrxhrxq9l1m5bdvxy0ni7i.title: Luis Enrique lauds 'almost perfect' PSG
1sz3yrxhrxq9l1m5bdvxy0ni7i.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain beat Le Mans 3-1 on Saturday, and Luis Enrique feels his team are finally hitting their stride.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique feels Paris Saint-Germain were "almost perfect" in their 3-1 defeat of Le Mans.

PSG, who made a poor start to the season, made it three Ligue 1 wins on the spin thanks to goals from Lucas Beraldo, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Maghnes Akliouche, while Desire Doue missed a late penalty.
The European champions created chances worth 4.25 expected goals, albeit only 1.72 xG came from open-play opportunities.
Le Mans, however, finished with 1.55 xG, the highest tally for a promoted side at the Parc des Princes in a Ligue 1 match since Troyes in May 2022 (1.75).
PSG are now into fifth in Ligue 1, three points behind leaders Monaco, and Luis Enrique thinks his team are beginning to hit their stride.
"It was an almost perfect result. We conceded a goal, and it was tough," he said.

"But I think that if we talk about what we did, knowing that we expected to face difficulties, we can say that the team was brave. We controlled the match, and it wasn't easy because I have to highlight the way Le Mans played. They showed a lot of courage.
"It was very difficult, but it's a pleasure to play against such a courageous team. It was important for us to get these three points. We still need more to climb up to the top of the league."
Akliouche was particularly impressive for PSG, as he scored his first goal for the club.
Three of his last four goals in all competitions have been scored at the Parc des Princes (also two with Monaco in Ligue 1 and the Champions League).
"I love everything Maghnes Akliouche does," Luis Enrique said. "The way he plays as a striker, winger, midfielder, his technical ability, his physicality. I'm very happy to have him."
While Le Mans offered plenty of resistance, they ultimately fell short after Louis Mafouta equalised in the 54th minute.
And coach Patrick Videira was disappointed with his team's display after their leveller.
"From the moment we equalised, we entered a kind of euphoria and lost our tactical discipline," he said.
"We could have done much better with our technical quality, in terms of width, stretching them in depth. We showed a good side, but I want much more."
Le Mans have lost only four of their 25 matches in all competitions in 2026 (W9 D12). All four of these defeats have come away from home.

1t0cpu6hn8gl51fynrrop3q17x.title: Fabregas relishing Como's 'dream' Champions League tie with Man Utd
1t0cpu6hn8gl51fynrrop3q17x.subtitle: Como are preparing for their second-ever Champions League home game on Wednesday, with three-time winners Manchester United up next.
paragraphs: Cesc Fabregas said it would have been "unthinkable" to imagine Manchester United coming to face Como in the Champions League when he first joined the club.
The Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is the venue for Wednesday's clash in what will be the first-ever meeting between the two sides, with both on three points heading into MD3.
Como's first European campaign began with a thumping win over RB Leipzig, but they were on the end of a 3-2 defeat against Feyenoord last time out.
United, meanwhile, were unable to build on their 4-0 victory over Sabah, going down 2-0 against Atletico Madrid as their underwhelming 2026-27 continued.

Fabregas and Michael Carrick will face each other as opposition managers, 17 years after playing on opposing sides in both legs of the 2008-09 Champions League semi-finals between Arsenal and United (won 4-1 on aggregate by the Red Devils).

Como are looking to become the first Italian team since Lazio in 1999-00 to win their first two home games in the European Cup or Champions League, and Fabregas is relishing the occasion against the Premier League giants.
"They are a great team. Just three years ago, when we were in Serie B, it would have been unthinkable that Manchester United might come to the Sinigaglia," Fabregas said.
"Yet, on Wednesday, that is exactly what will happen. For us, it's a dream come true; we'll take our chances."

Since the start of last season, the six matches between Italian and English sides in the Champions League have been won by the Premier League outfit on five occasions (L1 – Atalanta 2-1 Chelsea the exception).
However, United come into the clash in a wretched run of form, having failed to win in their last six matches across all competitions (D4 L2).
They have also won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4 L2), their fewest number of victories at this stage of a league campaign since 1986-87.
Como, on the other hand, are flying high in Serie A, sitting fifth, five points behind leaders Inter after Sunday's 3-1 victory over Fiorentina.

They have equalled their record for points gained in their first seven Serie A matches of a season during the three-points-for-a-win era, matching the 14 they managed in 1950-51 (W4 D2 L1 in both cases).
"Getting ready for such wonderful games is fantastic, but we must never forget that Serie A is the most important thing for us," Fabregas added.
"For us, every day is an important step in our growth. We are a new club, not in terms of our history, but because we started from scratch three years ago.
"Consequently, we have to be careful in how we manage a great many situations."

1t1fm0z5afgp810bw86xxwv83e.title: Manchester City 2-4 Paris Saint-Germain: Guardiola's Etihad return soured by European champions
1t1fm0z5afgp810bw86xxwv83e.subtitle: Reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain blew Manchester City away in the first half, and a second-half fightback proved fruitless.
paragraphs: Pep Guardiola took in a Champions League thriller on his return to the Etihad Stadium as Paris Saint-Germain beat Manchester City 4-2.
Guardiola returned to his former stomping ground for the first time since his departure at the end of last season.

But despite a raucous pre-match atmosphere in City's first home game following the guilty verdict in the Premier League's case against them, Guardiola saw his old team fall 3-0 down inside 32 minutes.
Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha were on target in an inspired first-half display from PSG, but Erling Haaland's double saw City threaten a fightback.

The crossbar spared Matvey Safonov's blushes when he palmed against it in the 12th minute, with Antoine Semenyo blazing over on the rebound, though Marc Guehi was penalised for a foul on PSG's goalkeeper.

Yet PSG hit the front less than two minutes later. Fabian Ruiz fed Doue on the counter-attack, and the France winger skipped in from the left before picking out the bottom-left corner with a drilled strike.
PSG were 2-0 up just 99 seconds later, with Doue and Dembele combining to devastating effect as the latter headed home from point-blank range.
Vitinha tested Gianluigi Donnarumma, who could then do nothing to deny Achraf Hakimi, but the full-back clipped a header against the woodwork.

PSG did go three up in the 32nd minute, however, with Vitinha slamming in first-time from the edge of the box, as City shipped three goals in the first half of a competitive home game for the first time since 2015 v Liverpool (4-1 loss).

Joskov Gvardiol headed wide and Jeremy Doku shot tamely at Safonov, and Enzo Maresca wasted no time in shuffling his pack at half-time. Matheus Nunes, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye came on, and the latter crossed in for Haaland to head beyond Safonov in the 53rd minute.
Semenyo hit the crossbar, albeit from an offside position, and Ndiaye went close as City urgently pressed for a second, but a Donnarumma blunder dented their hopes.
Donnarumma got a big hand to Maghnes Akliouche's shot, yet the former PSG man only managed to spin the ball up and into the net, and he was unable to scramble it clear.
Gvardiol saw an effort cleared off the line and Enzo Fernandez rattled the frame of the goal, while Haaland then hit the top of the bar with a towering header.

1t25uxxygvpl01g1a1oy6o66a3.title: Kovac reiterates demand for Dortmund to rediscover clinical edge
1t25uxxygvpl01g1a1oy6o66a3.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund only had two goals to show for their 22 shots against Sabah, and Niko Kovac wants to see improvements in the final third.
paragraphs: Niko Kovac urged his team to be more clinical in the final after squandering several opportunities to score past Sabah in their narrow 2-1 win in the Champions League.
Ahead of kick-off, Kovac said a trip to the Azerbaijani minnows was the perfect chance to end their attacking struggles, having failed to score in each of their last two games.
Serhou Guirassy capitalised on some poor goalkeeping from Stas Pokatilov to score a 10th-minute opener, but Sabah hit back through Aden McCarthy just before the break.
But eight minutes after the restart, Guirassy was in the right place at the right time to tuck home Joey Veerman's cross, and it was his double that proved decisive for Dortmund.

However, it was yet another frustrating outing in front of goal for Kovac's side. The Bundesliga giants registered an expected goals (xG) total of 3.73 from their 22 shots, with only nine of those on target.
"We played a really good attacking game and created a lot of chances," Kovac told reporters.
"If we had even capitalised on half of them, we no doubt would have won by three or four goals.
"We made small mistakes here and there, which allowed our opponent back into the game. It was a tough battle, but totally deserved."
Kovac's comments were backed up by Dortmund sporting director Ole Book, who urged his team to be more "ruthless" moving forward.
"When you travel this far — and not just us, but the fans as well — it only makes it sweeter to get the three points, which were also critical because of our loss in Norway," he said.
"Of course, it feels good to get a victory after three winless games. We definitely could have helped ourselves out today by being more ruthless.
"On the other hand, we took a significant step forward in terms of the way we played football."

Despite Kovac and Book's concerns, Dortmund were able to end a run of four consecutive away Champions League defeats, with this their first away win for 364 days, since beating Copenhagen 4-2 in October 2025.
And key to their triumph was Guirassy, who became only the second player to score 20+ Champions League goals for Dortmund (now 21), after Marco Reus (24).
In reaching that tally in 27 games, Guirassy scored 20 goals in the second-fewest appearances for a German club, behind Harry Kane for Bayern Munich (20 in 26).
Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Guirassy is the fourth player to score 20+ Champions League goals (21), after Kane (28), Kylian Mbappe (24) and Erling Haaland (20).

But even the Dortmund number nine could not look past his team's struggles in the final third, with Guirassy having more shots (eight) than any other player for Kovac's side, with four of those on target.
"I'm obviously happy with the win because it was so important for the team. The last two games were tough, which is why it was so important to win," Guirassy added.

"And that's exactly what we did. Congratulations to the entire team, and thanks also to the fans for their support. But we missed a few chances. If we can all be consistent, I believe we can achieve a lot this season."

1t2n2hegjqlq31lb7ykbrb0q0l.title: Inter 1-0 Shakhtar Donetsk: Augusto ends winless European run despite Bastoni red
1t2n2hegjqlq31lb7ykbrb0q0l.subtitle: Although Alessandro Bastoni was sent off for Inter, Cristian Chivu's side edged past Shakhtar Donetsk in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Ten-man Inter picked up their first Champions League win of the season with a 1-0 victory over Shakhtar Donetsk.
Despite seeing Alessandro Bastoni sent off in the 68th minute after two quick yellow cards, Carlos Augusto netted the winner in the 77th minute as Inter took all three points at San Siro.

Inter started on the front foot and twice went close inside the opening five minutes, but Marcus Thuram's low drive was tipped wide by Dmytro Riznyk and Hakan Calhanoglu saw an attempt from distance whistle past the post.

Ange-Yoan Bonny almost broke the deadlock before the half-hour mark, but was kept out by Riznyk, while Shakhtar could have taken a surprise lead ahead of half-time, though Josep Martinez was equal to Valerii Bondar's header.
The Shakhtar goalkeeper was called upon again in the second half to push wide a deflected strike from Thuram, though the contest then swung in the visitors' favour moments later.
Less than three minutes after receiving a yellow card for dissent, Bastoni was sent off for a second booking after hitting out at Oleh Ocheretko during an Inter free-kick.
However, the Nerazzurri would not be denied at home, with Augusto running in behind to latch onto Henrikh Mkhitaryan's pinpoint and poking past Riznyk to give Inter the lead.

Shakhtar did push for a point against the Serie A champions, but Martinez first kept out Newerton at the near post before also saving Mykola Matviienko's header from the resulting corner as Inter held on for the victory.
Inter get the job done

It would have been far from the performance Cristian Chivu would have hoped for from his side, but after going winless in their previous four Champions League outings, he will just be relieved to get back in the win column.
Inter still produced more expected goals (xG – 0.99 to 0.56) despite their numerical disadvantage, though they still only created one Opta-defined 'big' chance, which was dispatched by Augusto.

Augusto has scored in each of his last two games in the Champions League, after scoring just one goal across his first 27 outings in the competition, while Mkhitaryan (37 years and 273 days) became the oldest player to assist a goal in the competition for an Italian side since Francesco Totti (37y 355d) against CSKA Moscow in September 2014.

Bastoni, however, became the first Inter player to receive a red card in a Champions League game since Alexis Sanchez against Liverpool in March 2022, with only two minutes and 18 seconds elapsed between Bastoni's first and second yellow cards.
The centre-back will miss their trip to Feyenoord on MD4, but Chivu will no doubt remain focused on the three Serie A fixtures before their next Champions League outing.

1t3c92y8vo2m14ln5ra1i3efy.title: Bayer Leverkusen 2-1 Freiburg: Schick scores again in comeback victory
1t3c92y8vo2m14ln5ra1i3efy.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen sealed a 2-1 comeback win over Freiburg on Sunday, with Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick on target.
paragraphs: Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick grabbed a goal and an assist each as Bayer Leverkusen came from behind to seal a 2-1 victory over Freiburg on Sunday.
The win kept Leverkusen in touch with the Bundesliga's early frontrunners, moving them within a point of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund and level with Freiburg.
Leverkusen went behind after 14 minutes when Philipp Treu's centre picked out an unmarked Derry Scherhant, who slid a first-time finish through Mark Flekken's legs.

But the visitors' lead did not last long as Maza restored parity just five minutes later, capping off a superb team move that involved a clever flick from Moussa Diaby and a brilliant back-heel from Schick with a powerful low effort into the bottom corner.
Schick nearly completed the turnaround in the 38th minute but failed to direct his header on target, while Keisuke Goto squandered a similar opportunity at the other end.

Scherhant twice threatened as he teed up Igor Matanovic for a pair of headers but the Freiburg striker could not test Flekken from close-range on either occasion, before Maximilian Eggestein saw a lovely left-footed strike parried at the last second by the Leverkusen goalkeeper.

Leverkusen then completed their comeback with 14 minutes to spare as Maza showcased some superb footwork down the right wing and teed up Schick, who calmly slotted past Mio Backhaus from point-blank range.
Maza nearly doubled his tally in the dying minutes, but his blasted shot was parried by Backhaus, who was then called into action moments later to keep out Schick's ambitious long-range strike.
Schick's scoring streak powers Leverkusen to victory

Both Leverkusen and Freiburg have been among those to set an early marker in the final third in the Bundesliga this season, finding the net in all six of their respective league matches, though much of the Werkself's attacking success has come through the in-form Schick.

Schick is now the Bundesliga's joint-leading scorer alongside Werder Bremen's Niclas Fullkrug, with six goals apiece, while he has found the back of the net in each of his first six top-flight outings so far in 2026-27.

In doing so, he became only the third player to score in each of the first six matchdays of a Bundesliga campaign, with Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang doing that in 2015-16 for Dortmund, with Robert Lewandowski also achieving the feat in 2019-20 during his time at Bayern.
Leverkusen have also demonstrated their resilience this season, recovering four points from losing positions in the Bundesliga, a tally bettered only by Bremen (six).
Martinez's side were worthy winners on this occasion, generating 1.63 expected goals (xG) from their 12 shots compared to Freiburg's 1.06 xG from their 11 attempts.

1t4mz1zeypxyb1g5ybxdunw0es.title: Cucurella reveals attempt to try and tempt Rodri to join Real Madrid
1t4mz1zeypxyb1g5ybxdunw0es.subtitle: Rodri was of interest to Real Madrid before joining Barcelona, with Marc Cucurella saying he tried to tempt him to the Spanish capital.
paragraphs: Marc Cucurella revealed he sent Rodri a "subtle message" to join him at Real Madrid this summer before the midfielder opted to join Clasico rivals Barcelona.
Cucurella was a part of a summer rebuild at Madrid, with the Spanish international joining Los Blancos for a reported €55m (£47.5m) transfer fee from Chelsea.
The likes of Yan Diomande, Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries and Bernardo Silva also moved to the Spanish capital, with Rodri another player linked with a move to Madrid.
However, Rodri decided against linking up with Jose Mourinho and instead joined Hansi Flick at Barcelona, signing for a reported €76.5m (£65m) from Manchester City.
Cucurella and Rodri's moves came after helping Spain to the second World Cup crown this summer, with the latter scooping the Golden Ball along the way for his performances.
Spain are preparing for their first match since beating Argentina in the final, with England their opponents in the first match of their Nations League campaign this Saturday.
But speaking ahead of their trip to Wembley Stadium, Cucurella said that he openly tried to sway Rodri's decision in an attempt to play alongside him at club level.
"I don't really like pressuring or influencing team-mates," Cucurella said. "These are personal things.
"It's true that I sent him a subtle message, before the news broke, saying I hoped we'd become team-mates.
"He replied, but didn't give anything away. I'm happy for him [at Barca], though I hope he doesn't have too much success."
Rodri has enjoyed a perfect start to life with Barcelona, helping the Blaugrana begin their LaLiga title defence with seven wins from seven matches so far.

Only Pau Cubarsi (456), Eric Garcia (393), Pedri (391) and Gerard Martin (378) have completed more successful passes in the league for Barcelona than Rodri (368), while he also ranks third in Flick's squad for tackles won (eight).

Barcelona have started a LaLiga season with seven wins in their first seven games for the fourth time, after doing so in 2013-14, 2017-18 and 2024-25, and they already find themselves six points ahead of Madrid in the table.
Madrid lost their second league game of the season last Sunday, going down 2-1 to city rivals Atletico Madrid after Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half.
Mourinho is already coming under pressure early in his second stint in the Madrid dugout, though Cucurella believes his team are more than capable of turning things around.
"We didn't finish the period before the break in the best way," Cucurella added. "It's all a process, but the important thing is to build a solid foundation.
"Let's see if we can find a good balance and build a strong, united group. If the season ends the way we all want it to, no one will remember the start."

1te3035tqghan1tv19sssrbvr3.title: Joao Felix planning European return but happy at Al-Nassr for now
1te3035tqghan1tv19sssrbvr3.subtitle: Joao Felix is halfway through a two-year deal with Saudi Arabian champions Al-Nassr, but he misses competing in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Joao Felix admits he often thinks about returning to Europe to compete in the Champions League, though the Portugal forward is happy at Al-Nassr for the moment.
Joao Felix joined Al-Nassr last year and helped them win the Saudi Pro League title in his first season, providing 33 goal involvements in as many games (20 goals, 13 assists).

Having been one of European football's hottest properties when he broke into Benfica's side in 2018-19, he made a blockbuster €126m move to Atletico Madrid at a young age but struggled in the Spanish capital.

After scoring 20 goals in 43 outings for Benfica in 2018-19, Joao Felix has never netted more than 10 times in a single season in Europe's top five leagues, enduring up-and-down spells with Atleti, Chelsea, Barcelona and AC Milan.
The 26-year-old only has one year remaining on his contract with Al-Nassr, who appointed Ange Postecoglou as their new head coach in July, as Jorge Jesus took the Portugal job.
He is hoping to help Cristiano Ronaldo pass the 1,000-goal mark in the coming months, with the 41-year-old netting to hit the net another 21 times.

1tebltqd12o4i1l7bd2e2oec30.title: The Numbers Game: Glasner's misfiring Forest take on Arsenal
1tebltqd12o4i1l7bd2e2oec30.subtitle: Nottingham Forest and Arsenal have drawn 0-0 in their last two meetings at the City Ground, but will there be goals on Sunday?
paragraphs: Manchester City might lead the way in the Premier League after winning their opening six games of the season, but defending champions Arsenal are just three points behind them.

Having only dropped points away to Brighton, the Gunners will feel quietly confident about their position, and that is to say nothing of the prospect of Man City receiving a penalty after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's rules.
On Sunday, Mikel Arteta takes his team to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest, who have struggled in the early stages of Oliver Glasner's reign and only have five points on the board.
But which way will the game go? After consulting Opta insights, we pick out the key players and storylines to watch in our data-powered preview.
The Opta supercomputer is firmly behind Arsenal for this game, with their win probability standing at 58.3%.
Across the model's 10,000 pre-match simulations, Forest won 20.4%, while the remaining 21.3% finished level.
And in our 2026-27 season predictions, Arsenal's 44.7% chance of winning the title makes them slight favourites, ahead of Man City's 42.5%.
The last two Premier League meetings between Forest and Arsenal at the City Ground have ended goalless, with 40 combined shots being attempted without success.
Forest have only won one of their last 11 Premier League matches against Arsenal overall (D2 L8).

That victory came by a 1-0 scoreline in May 2023, with Taiwo Awoniyi's goal sealing a result that not only secured Forest's Premier League status for another season, but also mathematically crowned Man City as champions.
Forest have failed to score in each of their last four meetings with Arsenal, with Awoniyi netting another goal against them in a 2-1 home defeat in January 2024.
Forest must find shooting boots as Glasner's slide continues
When Glasner masterminded a 2-1 victory over Fulham on December 7 last year, his Crystal Palace side sat fourth in the Premier League table.
Of course, the Austrian has had more highs since then, leading the Eagles to Conference League glory in May to rubber-stamp his standing as their greatest-ever manager, before leaving for Forest.
But very few of those positive moments have been in the Premier League. Since that victory over Fulham, Glasner has only overseen five wins in 29 matches in the English top flight (D9 L15).

Since the start of that 29-game sequence, on matchday 16 of 2025-26, Glasner's 17% win ratio is the second-worst among all managers to oversee at least 20+ Premier League games, with only former Wolves boss Rob Edwards (13%) faring worse.

Last Sunday's 3-1 defeat at his former home of Selhurst Park will have particularly stung Glasner, especially with Forest firing off 24 shots and racking up 3.36 expected goals (xG). Their eight big chances in that game were the most by any team to lose a Premier League game since Blackburn Rovers against Newcastle United in February 2012.
And things do not get much easier for them this weekend, as they go up against the Premier League's reigning champions and joint-best defence so far this season, in Arsenal.

Forest's underlying metrics so far this campaign have been broadly positive. Their per-game averages in the Premier League for shots (17.7), expected goals (1.72 xG), touches in the opposition box (27.3) and big chances (3.5) are their best in any of the last five seasons.
However, they have scored with just 4.7% of their shots and have the worst xG differential in the division this season, netting five times from 10.3 xG (-5.3).
Dan Ndoye is the only Forest player to net twice in the Premier League this campaign, with Liam Delap, Igor Jesus and Morgan Gibbs-White all netting once apiece.

Delap was guilty of a particularly glaring miss against Palace, and he has a conversion rate of just 7.1% from 14 shots this campaign, only hitting the target with two of those efforts. If Forest are to turn their form around, it will likely need to start with their misfiring forwards.
Arsenal finding new ways to win as set-piece prowess wanes

Arsenal have responded strongly since their 3-0 defeat at Brighton going into the international break, fighting back from 1-0 down to beat Leeds United 2-1 last time out in the Premier League, with Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes on target.
The Gunners have now gone 1-0 down three times in their last four Premier League matches, as many times as they did in their previous 25 combined.
They have won two of those three games, though, and no team has won more points from losing positions this season than the Gunners' six.
Arsenal have now won 14 of their last 17 Premier League games (L3), with nine of those wins coming via a one-goal margin.
In the last two seasons, they have won 17 matches by a single-goal margin, the most of any side in Europe's big five leagues, so their knack for grinding out wins remains in place.
However, somewhat curiously, Arteta's side have not really been able to rely on their set-piece prowess in the early stages of this season.

The Gunners, who scored 25 non-penalty set-piece goals in the Premier League last term, including a single-season record 19 from corners, are yet to find the net from a set-piece (excluding penalties) after six Premier League matches in 2026-27.
It is their longest run without one since a seven-match streak between January and March 2025, and the first time they have not netted one in their first six games of a campaign since 2011-12.
But they did the job from open play in the second half of Tuesday's Champions League clash with Lille, as Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka scored in a 3-0 win.

Saka now has 19 goals in major European competitions for Arsenal, the second-most in their history behind Thierry Henry (42), while his nine assists in the Champions League are their third-most ever, behind Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14).
Nottingham Forest – Morgan Gibbs-White
Gibbs-White may feel like he has been let down by his team-mates at times this term, as only Brighton's Pascal Gross (18) has created more chances in the Premier League than his 17.
The England international also leads all players for open-play chances created (15), big chances created (seven) and expected assists (1.87 xA).
Arsenal – Bruno Guimaraes
In the last two seasons, Guimaraes has scored in three of his five substitute appearances in the Premier League, netting three goals overall, including the winner against Leeds.
Both of his two Arsenal goals have been as a substitute, with Leandro Trossard being the only Gunners player to score his first three Premier League goals for the club off the bench.

1tkx8luzo1i6o1i8iccy2volgr.title: Simeone welcomes goals from Atletico defenders
1tkx8luzo1i6o1i8iccy2volgr.subtitle: Atletico Madrid defenders Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero both scored in their 2-1 win over Alaves.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone is delighted to see goals coming from his Atletico Madrid defenders after their LaLiga victory over Alaves.
Atleti won 2-1 on Saturday, with Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero scoring either side of Lucas Boye's penalty for Alaves, who saw Angel Perez sent off in the second half.
Six of Atleti's 18 LaLiga goals this season have now come from defenders, with Grimaldo scoring in three of their last four league games.
Grimaldo is the only defender in LaLiga to have scored more than once this season, while Romero, Marc Pubill and Robin Le Normand have also netted for Atleti this term.
Simeone insisted he does not care where the goals come from, as long as they arrive in the end.
"It's always important that the goal comes from wherever it comes, as long as it arrives," said the Atleti boss.
"Beyond Grimaldo's and Cuti's [Romero] goals, the team played the game well in the first half, tried various approaches, withstood the opponent's attack effectively, and created some good play.
"We were stuck at 1-1 after the penalty, and it felt like a small consolation prize given what we were doing. In the second half, they defended very well, very organised.

"The game progressed, and we kept pressing with [Alex] Baena, [Lee] Kang-in, Giuliano [Simeone], [Alexander] Sorloth, Julian [Alvarez]. The sending-off made it even more difficult because the opponent sat back even more.
"It seems easier when they have one less player, but the opponent becomes more focused, and you need to find the spaces. We looked for them in every way possible."
Atleti remain second in LaLiga after eight games, five points behind leaders Barcelona, but Simeone insisted his side are not the finished product just yet.
"I still think we're a work in progress, trying to find the players who are adapting to what Atletico is all about and what it takes to make history with the club," added Simeone.
"There's a certain level to play for Atletico, and another level to make history with them. Hopefully, we can get on that path."

1tll0yvmicf7516l9hkwg7pdzz.title: New England boss Mitrovic expects playoff intensity in remaining MLS games
1tll0yvmicf7516l9hkwg7pdzz.subtitle: The New England Revolution have sealed a playoff place, and the Chicago Fire are close to joining them ahead of their clash on Saturday.
paragraphs: New England Revolution boss Marko Mitrovic says every game for the rest of the MLS season will be played with a playoff-like intensity, though he did not realise his own team had clinched a postseason spot in midweek.
The Revs beat FC Cincinnati 3-2 on Wednesday, with young United States international Peyton Miller laying on two assists for Dor Turgeman, either side of Joshua Wynder's goal.
They sit third in the Eastern Conference and, having guaranteed a playoff place with five regular-season games to go, are now simply jostling for seeding.
But when asked for his reaction to New England clinching their playoff place, Mitrovic said: "I didn't even know, to be honest!
"It might sound silly, but I'm not checking what's going on around the league. We don't talk about the playoffs."
But Mitrovic believes the rest of the Revs' games, starting with Saturday's visit to the Chicago Fire, will have the feel of a postseason encounter.
"Every game now has a high level of urgency for the teams around it, and you know, at the beginning of the season everyone can see the time that lies ahead, but there is no time left now," he said.

"I feel like now, every game will feel like the playoffs. I think that the last two or three games before the international break, it already felt like teams were playing with a high level of urgency.
"And now everyone's competing to survive and there's no hiding behind that. Every team has to match that intensity that everyone else has."
The Fire are only one place and one point behind New England and only need one more point to secure their own playoff berth, though they were beaten 3-1 by the Philadelphia Union in midweek.

Maren Haile-Selassie put Chicago ahead at Soldier Field, but Jack Elliott's red card in first-half stoppage time paved the way for Philadelphia to fight back, via a goal from Milan Iloski and a brace from Bruno Damiani.
New England Revolution – Carles Gil
Gil achieved a landmark during the Revs' midweek win, with his assist for Wynder's goal taking him to 10 for the season.
The 33-year-old is just the second player in MLS history to register at least 10 assists in six consecutive seasons, after Preki (eight).
Chicago Fire – Robert Lewandowski
Lewandowski will be hoping for a bounce-back performance on Saturday, having only managed one shot with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.1 against the Union on Wednesday.
MATCH PREDICTION – DRAW
Although Chicago were beaten last time out, they were up against a Philadelphia side who are on an eight-match winning run and played the entire second half with 10 men.
So they will be confident of putting up a fight against New England, who have four wins and two defeats in their last six MLS games.
The Revs have managed nine wins, two draws and three defeats on home soil this campaign, with Chicago having five wins, five draws and four losses on the road this year.
New England Revolution – 39.4%

1tnjgqgnuzdgf1uzwgiwv77zcv.title: 'I might take another vacation', quips Dembele after PSG overwhelm Man City
1tnjgqgnuzdgf1uzwgiwv77zcv.subtitle: Ousmane Dembele was given some time off last week, but he returned to action in style as Paris Saint-Germain beat Manchester City.
paragraphs: Ousmane Dembele joked about taking another vacation after he helped Paris Saint-Germain dismantle Manchester City in the Champions League.
Dembele was given some time off by PSG boss Luis Enrique last week, meaning he missed a 3-1 win over Le Mans in Ligue 1.
But the Ballon d'Or winner returned to the fold against Man City on Wednesday, and he went on to score and assist in a 4-2 victory for the two-time European champions.
Desire Doue opened the scoring in the 13th minute, before crossing in for Dembele to head home PSG's second just 99 seconds later.

Vitinha put PSG 3-0 in the 32nd minute, though City threatened a second-half comeback. Erling Haaland scored twice, either side of Gianluigi Donnarumma gifting the visitors a fourth, which ultimately proved enough to get the job done, despite Ferran Torres missing a late penalty.

PSG have already scored 10 goals in the Champions League this season – no side has ever scored more in the first two matches of a campaign in the competition – and Dembele had a laugh at the expense of their critics.
"We don't care at all that people doubted us," Dembele told Canal+.

"It's October, it's the second Champions League match, and we're staying focused. We know that in the first part of the season, we have to be on track and then prepare for the second half of the season.
"Did I want to set the record straight? Not at all, there was the international break and then I went on vacation.
"Besides, I might ask for another vacation! I've been criticised for 10 years, so that's not going to change, is it?"
Dembele assisted PSG's fourth goal, with Maghnes Akliouche benefiting from Donnarumma's blunder.
The France forward has now been directly involved in 33 goals in 42 Champions League games for PSG (20 goals, 11 assists).
Only Kylian Mbappe (65 in 64 games) and Neymar (37 in 41) have recorded more goal involvements for PSG in the competition, with Dembele now level with Edinson Cavani (33 in 54).
PSG are unbeaten in 10 Champions League matches against English opponents (W8 D2), scoring 26 goals while conceding just 10 in this run.
But Luis Enrique suggested his team were fortunate.
"I love our attitude, our commitment," he told TNT Sports. "We try to win every match, we don't stop at one or two goals.
"We try to continue scoring and continue playing the same way. It's nice to feel that.
"We were lucky, because in the second half we could have conceded four goals."

"Did I want to set the record straight? Not at all, there was the international break and then I went on vacation.

"Besides, I might ask for another vacation! I've been criticised for 10 years, so that's not going to change, is it?"

Dembele assisted PSG's fourth goal, with Maghnes Akliouche benefiting from Donnarumma's blunder.

The France forward has now been directly involved in 33 goals in 42 Champions League games for PSG (20 goals, 11 assists).

Only Kylian Mbappe (65 in 64 games) and Neymar (37 in 41) have recorded more goal involvements for PSG in the competition, with Dembele now level with Edinson Cavani (33 in 54).

PSG are unbeaten in 10 Champions League matches against English opponents (W8 D2), scoring 26 goals while conceding just 10 in this run.

But Luis Enrique suggested his team were fortunate.

"I love our attitude, our commitment," he told TNT Sports. "We try to win every match, we don't stop at one or two goals.

"We try to continue scoring and continue playing the same way. It's nice to feel that.

1twbfxyd5yw5516lnegkirv86p.title: Spence could make long-awaited Inter debut against Parma
1twbfxyd5yw5516lnegkirv86p.subtitle: Djed Spence's last appearance was in England's World Cup third-place play-off against France, but he could now be set for his Inter debut.
paragraphs: Djed Spence could finally make his Inter debut when the Scudetto holders welcome Parma to San Siro on Saturday, having not featured since the World Cup.
Spence joined the Nerazzurri from Tottenham in a €35m (£30m) deal in August, as the Serie A giants moved to replace Denzel Dumfries following his move to Real Madrid.
However, a persistent injury caused him to miss the first five games of Inter's title defence, from which they took 13 points to sit second, only behind Roma on goal difference.

Spence enjoyed a hugely impressive World Cup campaign as England finished third, making 19 tackles at the tournament – the most by a Three Lions defender at a single edition since Ashley Cole in 2002 (25).
And on Friday, head coach Cristian Chivu confirmed Spence will now be eased into his line-up over the coming weeks.
"He's been training with us for a week; we couldn't just ignore his rehabilitation period, plus the holidays after the World Cup," Chivu said.
"If I add it all up, he's missed two months of work on the pitch. He's available, he will be called up, and we're pleased that he's back."
Chivu was also asked whether Inter might move away from their 3-4-3 system in order to adopt a back four, after Spence impressed in both full-back places for his country this summer.
"It's not a guarantee that playing with a back four makes you win, nor is it with a three," Chivu said.
"The most important thing is the principles you have in the game. We are built to play a certain type of game."

Having fought back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Roma in their final game before the international break, Inter know a victory on Saturday will take them three points clear of the Giallorossi, at least temporarily ahead of their meeting with Como on Sunday.
Parma, meanwhile, are 15th with four points from their opening five games, having beaten Genoa 2-1 last time out.
Inter – Lautaro Martinez

Martinez has scored consecutive braces in Serie A against Napoli and Roma, and he could become the first Inter player to score multiple goals in three successive appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95) in the competition.

The last Nerazzurri player to achieve this was Carlo Muraro, between December 1976 and January 1977 (against Napoli, Roma and Bologna). Martinez (136 goals) is also just two goals away from equalling Benito Lorenzi (138) in second place in Inter's all-time Serie A top scorers list – Giuseppe Meazza is first with 197 goals.
Romero has scored in his last two league appearances against Genoa and Como.
The last Parma player to find the net in three consecutive Serie A matches was Dejan Kulusevski in July 2020.
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER WIN

Inter are unbeaten in their last nine Serie A games against Parma (W6 D3), winning four of the most recent five (D1). Parma's last victory against the Nerazzurri in the competition was in September 2018.

The Scudetto holders have also scored at least two goals in each of their last eight Serie A matches against Parma. Only against Verona (11 between 1997 and 2015), Sampdoria (11 between 1947 and 1951) and Cagliari (10 between 1996 and 2006) have they registered a longer run of consecutive games with at least two goals in the top flight.

Chivu's side could also win all of their first four home Serie A matches of the season for only the third time in the last 35 years, after 2017-18 (under Luciano Spalletti) and 2005-06 (under Roberto Mancini).
However, Inter have lost two of their last four league matches following an international break (W2), after remaining unbeaten in all eight such games before that (W6 D2).

Parma, meanwhile, have lost all of their last four away league games. The last time they endured a longer run of consecutive away defeats in Serie A was between April 2021 and August 2024 (six in that instance).

Alberto Gilardino returns to Parma, where, as a player, he scored 50 goals in 96 Serie A appearances between 2002 and 2005. He is the club's second-highest scorer in the top-flight, behind only Hernan Crespo (72).

1twdmh7vjkste1gmvx8lyl7rzc.title: Schlotterbeck describes Dortmund's win over Frankfurt as 'a ton of fun'
1twdmh7vjkste1gmvx8lyl7rzc.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund climbed to the top of the Bundesliga table with a narrow victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday.
paragraphs: Borussia Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck described their Bundesliga victory over Eintracht Frankfurt as "a ton of fun".
Dortmund won 1-0 at Signal Iduna Park on Saturday courtesy of Maximilian Beier's fantastic finish in the 80th minute, which also sent them top of the table.
BVB have won more Bundesliga matches (53) and home Bundesliga matches (40) against Frankfurt than against any other opponent.
Dortmund have also won 15 of their last 16 home league games against Eintracht, with the exception being a 1-2 defeat in April 2021.

Niko Kovac's side have 17 points from their opening seven games, their best start to a Bundesliga season in three years (also 17 in 2023-24); the last time they had more at this stage was in 2017-18 (19 points).
Dortmund accumulated 1.5 expected goals (xG) while restricting Frankfurt to just 0.9, with only 0.09 of that total coming in the second half.
"It was a ton of fun," Schlotterbeck told Sky Germany.
"We allowed a few chances in the first half, and then none whatsoever in the second half. We’ve now kept five clean sheets in seven games.
"If we had held on for two more minutes against Bremen, we'd be talking about six out of seven. That's really good.
"The four of us in the back work really well together. We dominated the second half and earned the win through compact defending.
"Maxi [Beier] put his quality on display. That shot into the far corner is his speciality. We're not perfect yet, but we're making progress."
Dortmund have kept five clean sheets in their first seven Bundesliga games this season, equalling their club record at this stage (also five in 2020-21).
Beier's goal was also Dortmund's fourth from a substitute in the league this season, with only RB Leipzig (seven) scoring more such goals.

1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.title: Luis Enrique not taking Classique triumph for granted
1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.subtitle: Marquinhos struck the winner as Paris Saint-Germain overcame Marseille in Sunday's matchup between France's two most successful clubs.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain can never take a win over Classique rivals Marseille for granted, after they battled to a 2-1 success at the Stade Velodrome.
Marquinhos' 74th-minute strike settled the contest as PSG claimed back-to-back Ligue 1 victories, having started their campaign with three winless games.
The Brazilian's goal came just two minutes after Angel Gomes got Marseille back on level terms, with that strike also coming hot on the heels of Ferran Torres' opener.
Marseille had captain Timothy Weah sent off shortly after going 2-1 down, with the United States international hauling Nuno Mendes down from behind while already on a yellow card.

PSG have now won 10 of their last 14 away Ligue 1 games against Marseille (D3 D1), though Nayef Aguerd missed a huge chance to snatch a point for OM deep into stoppage time, as he headed wide on the stretch.
And Luis Enrique says three points will never come easily for any visiting side at the Velodrome.
"It was the match we had planned for, with a lot of difficulties. Everyone said it would be easy, but playing at the Velodrome is not an easy thing," he told Ligue 1+.
"We tried to play, we created fewer chances in the first half because the opponent defended very well. In the second half, everything changed, we made a very good effort."

The result piles more pressure on Bruno Genesio, who is the first Marseille boss to lose four of his first five league games in charge of the club since the duo of Willy Kohut and Andre Gascard in 1938.

Marseille will spend the three-week international break 17th in the Ligue 1 table, with this the latest point into a season that they have sat in the relegation zone since 2011-12, when they were 20th with three points after six games and ultimately finished 10th.
But Luis Enrique expects them to come good eventually, saying: "Nothing was easy, we saw a very good OM team, with the way they defended. They have a great coach, I'm sure they will improve."
Genesio himself, however, admits Marseille's results have fallen well short of the required standard and has revealed he will hold talks with the club's hierarchy during the break.
"It's funny, everyone wishes me good luck. I'm a coach, so obviously I'm linked to the performances and results, especially at a club like OM," he said.
"This is insufficient, I assume my share of responsibility, as others will have to assume it too.
"I'm not there yet, I'm going to digest this defeat, talk to my staff, talk to my directors.
"Because I think – and I'm trying to weigh my words – that it's not normal for OM to be in this situation."
While PSG host Le Mans in their next Ligue 1 game on October 10, Marseille go to Troyes the following day.

1tytdnqt0jdlu181prjod107ue.title: Richter: Sporting KC comeback proved Philadelphia are far from perfect
1tytdnqt0jdlu181prjod107ue.subtitle: The Philadelphia Union are the team in form in the MLS, and their 11-game unbeaten run is on the line against Orlando City SC this weekend.
paragraphs: Ryan Richter described the Philadelphia Union's thrilling comeback against Sporting Kansas City as "outrageous", but said it was a warning sign to not get complacent.
Philadelphia's unbeaten run in MLS extended to 11 matches at Sporting Park last weekend, despite finding themselves three goals down against Sporting KC.
Andre Luiz's brace and a goal from Wyatt Meyer blew the Union away in the opening 16 minutes, with their sensational stretch under interim boss Richter looking set to end.
However, Philadelphia turned the game on its head in the space of four second-half minutes, with Bruno Damiani, Cavan Sullivan and Milan Iloski hauling their team level.
The turnaround was complete thanks to an own goal from Zorhan Bassong, with the result helping Philadelphia move up to sixth in the Eastern Conference.

And while he was pleased with the mentality of his players to complete the turnaround against Sporting KC, Richter acknowledged that better sides in the division will punish them should Philadelphia hand them an advantage like that again.

"The mentality of this group is outrageous," Richter said. "It would have been easy for us to quit at half-time. We're on the road, long journey, down 3-0, guys going away with their national teams after the game.

"But the way the guys responded in the second half was fantastic. I am proud of them and congratulations to them for showing again the way they believe in each other right now and what is possible with this group.
"It's fun to be a part of, and it's fun to watch, but we have to keep going. We got a reminder that we're not perfect and when we're not at our best, any team can beat us."
Philadelphia's next MLS outing sees them welcome Orlando City SC to Subaru Park this weekend, with the Lions also in the hunt to secure their spot in the playoffs.
Just two points and one place separate the two sides in the standings after Orlando fell to a 4-2 defeat against the New England Revolution last time out.
Martin Perelman's side saw their three-match winning run in the league come to an end, with late goals from Peyton Miller and Carles Gil sealing the win for New England.

"Very frustrated, of course, with the result. It was a big challenge for us because we came here after the game on Wednesday and were facing, of course, a team that is doing well in the league," Perelman said of Orlando's defeat to the Revolution.
"The context of the game was difficult. We knew that. Taking that into account, I think we made a very big effort. We made some mistakes, especially in the first half.

"And then we were able to come back in the second half, compete, tie the game, and then, I think there we have some gaps to improve as a team. I think we grew a lot during this season in many things. We are competing. We are up there. Everybody knows how we started.

"I think the process of the team is there, but if something we need to improve is this. We need to close these kinds of games. So, that's the frustration, but I also need to recognise the effort of the players. I have to do it because it was there."
Philadelphia Union – Bruno Damiani
With the in-form Sullivan away on international duty with the United States, the emphasis will fall on Damiani to continue Philadelphia's excellent run of form under Richter.
Only Iloski (13) has scored more MLS goals for Philadelphia than Damiani's eight, though the Uruguayan does have five goals in his last three league appearances.
Orlando City SC – Martin Ojeda
Ojeda recorded his team-leading 12th MLS goal of the season and his 46th across all competitions this year against New England last time out.

The Argentine has recorded three goal contributions in his last four matches across all competitions (two goals, one assist) and he is now just one goal short of tying Facundo Torres' club record of 47 goals across all competitions.
MATCH PREDICTION: PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN
As predicted, Philadelphia are the clear favourites in the Opta supercomputers pre-match simulations. The Union are now 11 games unbeaten in the MLS, tying the club record.

However, wins at Subaru Park against Orlando have proved hard to come by in recent years. Indeed, Philadelphia have failed to win their last three home league matches against the Lions (D1 L2) since a 5-1 victory back in September 2022.

But they come up against an Orlando side that have managed just three away league wins all season, though prior to their defeat to New England in their last such match, had drawn against Minnesota United and beaten Atlanta United.
Philadelphia Union – 65%
Orlando City SC – 16.4%

1u05b3hp5sign1kt8f0qhsjiid.title: Australia 1-1 Brazil: Rayan nets last-gasp equaliser for Ancelotti's new-look side
1u05b3hp5sign1kt8f0qhsjiid.subtitle: Australia came within touching distance of stunning Brazil, but Rayan popped up with a late equaliser to seal a share of the spoils.
paragraphs: Brazil denied Australia a famous victory in Queensland as Rayan's stoppage-time header earned the Selecao a 1-1 draw in Thursday's international friendly.
Carlo Ancelotti said the match was the beginning of a new generation for Brazil, but his team fell behind to Nestory Irankunda's stunning second-half free-kick.
However, Bournemouth forward Rayan made Brazil's late pressure count, with the two sides squaring off once again next Tuesday at Suncorp Stadium.
Connor Metcalfe helped Australia make a quick start, with his shot whistling over Hugo Souza's crossbar after Vinicius Junior was cheaply dispossessed by Jacob Italiano.

Irankunda then fired way wide before the Australian defence put their bodies on the line to keep out Vinicius and Raphinha, with the hosts going close to the opening goal just before the break, but a deep corner just evaded Alessandro Circati at the far post.

Brazil thought they had taken the lead on the stroke of half-time when a neat one-two between Endrick and Estevao saw the latter finish past Patrick Beach, but the goal was ruled out after a VAR review for a foul on Harry Souttar by Bruno Guimaraes in the build-up.
Ancelotti's side built on that momentum after the break, with the in-form Raphinha first seeing his shot smothered by Beach before he drilled narrowly wide of the right post.

Estevao then fired over after Vinicius' attempt deflected kindly to him, and Australia made the most of that reprieve in the 68th minute through Irankunda, who curled a sensational free-kick past Souza and into the top-left corner.

Brazil penned Australia back into their own penalty area in their search for a late equaliser, and their persistence was rewarded in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time, with Rayan's thunderous header from a Raphinha corner going in off the crossbar.
Irankunda and Herrington star for Australia's young guns

With both nations playing in their first matches since their respective exits from this summer's World Cup, many predicted Brazil's quality in the final third to be too much for Australia, but Popovic's side proved they are more than capable of mixing it with the established nations.

And Australia's combative performance at the back was spearheaded by Lucas Herrington. After becoming the youngest player to start a knockout match at the World Cup for the Socceroos this summer, he proved why he was worthy of his switch to the Premier League with Hull City.

Herrington won all three of the duels he contested, while only Circati (eight) and Souttar (six) made more clearances than his four. He also made two interceptions, but it was another exciting talent in Irankunda that shone at the other end.

Irankunda was handed a third consecutive start, his longest such run for Australia, and he delivered by becoming only the second player to score against Brazil for the Socceroos, after Shaun Murphy back in June 2001.

1ugouwltxz6qhz6qvzbk0q4tv.title: Italy 0-2 Belgium: Godts and Lukebakio condemn Mancini to losing return
1ugouwltxz6qhz6qvzbk0q4tv.subtitle: Roberto Mancini was unable to mark his Italy return with a victory, as Belgium won their first match under new boss Mark van Bommel.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini lost on his return as Italy boss after a 2-0 defeat against Belgium in the Nations League.

Mika Godts struck in the 20th minute before substitute Dodi Lukebakio secured all three points in the second half as Mark van Bommel made a winning start to his reign as Belgium boss at Stadio Olimpico.

After Gianluigi Donnarumma and Senne Lammens made early saves at either end, with Charles De Ketelaere and Moise Kean denied respectively, Godts opened the scoring after sending Gianluca Mancini and Diego Coppola to the ground before slotting into the bottom-right corner.

Belgium dominated the first half after taking the lead, but could not add to their advantage as Donnarumma pulled off a brilliant double save to keep out De Ketelaere and Nicolas Raskin, while the Italy captain also saved a powerful header from Godts moments after Diego Moreira miscued a simple finish.

Maxim De Cuyper flashed a shot wide of the right post before the break, but Italy were the bigger threat in the second half as Kean forced Lammens into a clever save with his right leg just two minutes after the restart.

Francesco Pio Esposito then went close twice, first seeing his header go straight at Lammens before the Belgium shot-stopper pulled off a strong save to deny the Inter striker's first-time effort from Nicolo Cambiaghi's cut-back.

However, Italy were made to pay for their wastefulness in the 69th minute as Lukebakio drove forward from the halfway line, cut inside past Sandro Tonali and Daniel Maldini and curled into the bottom-left corner from distance.

The hosts had late chances to force a nervy ending, but Riccardo Calafiori saw his shot with the outside of his boot go wide of the right post, while Giorgio Scalvini inexplicably missed the target from inside the six-yard box.
Contrasting emotions for Mancini and Van Bommel

A better second-half display from Italy offered some hope for Mancini, with 1.22 of their 1.52 expected goals coming after the break, but the Azzurri were unable to turn things around against Van Bommel's Belgium.

Both Donnarumma and Lammens made six saves in what almost proved to be a tale of two halves in Rome, but Lukebakio's timely second for the Red Devils was enough to clinch a winning start to their Nations League campaign.

There was plenty for Van Bommel to be pleased with, as Kevin De Bruyne led the match in chances created (five), while Godts led the way in dribbles attempted (five) and, among Belgium players, possessions won (four) to go along with his goal.

The new Belgium boss will know Lammens' saves early in the second half played a huge role in the victory, especially after Belgium's missed opportunities before the break, though he will certainly be the happier of the two managers.
Up next for Belgium in the Nations League is a home match against France, while Mancini will be looking for the first win of his second stint when Italy travel to Turkiye next.

1umg60acgeijv1q9zpi8wpq0oj.title: Mead thrilled by 'seamless' transition at Man City
1umg60acgeijv1q9zpi8wpq0oj.subtitle: While Beth Mead was not on the scoresheet against Charlton Athletic, she played a big role in helping Manchester City get over the line.
paragraphs: Beth Mead says her transition to Manchester City has been "seamless" after she helped the team extend their perfect start to the Women's Super League.
City were made to work hard for all three points on Saturday but edged to a 1-0 win over Charlton Athletic to make it four wins from four so far.
Alex Greenwood scored the only goal of the game in the first half, bending in a free-kick for her first league goal since April 2024.
Mead more than played her part, though, as she finished with game-high totals for chances created (four), touches (98) and passes in the final third (47).
"It's a different way of playing [at City from Arsenal]; I've been playing in a different role here for most of the games," Mead told BBC Sport.
"It's a very good team who like to play football, and that's how I like to play. It's been a bit seamless fitting in, but very different players to play with; you have to get used to.
"I'm just trying to do the right things, recover well and go again. I'm trying to play as many minutes as I can. I'm never going to complain about that.

"It was difficult. It's hard off the back of a Champions League game. Charlton were really hard to beat; they defended really well. Our intensity could have been better on the ball, but we got the three points."
City have won each of their first four WSL matches in a season for the first time since 2019-20.
And the Citizens have now won 29 of their 30 games against newly promoted teams, winning eight in a row since a 2-1 loss at Liverpool in 2022-23.
Andree Jeglertz opted to make six changes to his starting line-up from their win over Liverpool last weekend, with Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp starting on the bench.
With Women's Champions League matches adding to their schedule, he noted how important it is to be able to shuffle his pack given the quality of his squad.
"It's a good performance; we should have created more scoring chances," he said.
"Sometimes the last pass wasn't there, but there was also players who haven't played together as much. We have rotated a couple of players.

"You can't say a player is a full-back because they need to be able to play in different areas. For me, it's about how can I get the best out of players like Alex Greenwood; sometimes she plays better in different areas."

1uoqcfnwyqxw01hs2mfcba6p1e.title: Galatasaray 2-1 Fenerbahce: Osimhen brace secures bragging rights
1uoqcfnwyqxw01hs2mfcba6p1e.subtitle: Galatasaray came out on top against fierce rivals Fenerbahce, with Victor Osimhen scoring twice to secure all three points.
paragraphs: Victor Osimhen's first-half brace was enough to earn Galatasaray a 2-1 win over fierce rivals Fenerbahce in the Turkish Super Lig, despite Irfan Can Kahveci's stunning overhead kick.
Osimhen opened the scoring just before the half-hour mark and added his second just before the break, and it was enough to send Galatasaray back to the top of the table.
Baris Alper Yilmaz forced Ederson into a couple of early saves, but he turned provider for Osimhen's 29th-minute opener.
The Turkiye international prodded it through to Osimhen, who had three Fenerbahce defenders around him, but he rifled into the bottom-right corner.
Osimhen, on the stretch, saw another effort tipped wide of the post, but he was in the right place to help Davinson Sanchez's rasping strike past Ederson with a glancing header in the 44th minute.
Ederson tipped away Aleksey Batrakov's low drive, and Archie Brown turned the rebound onto the post to deny Osimhen what would have been a simple tap-in on the stroke of half-time.
Osimhen nodded in what he thought was a hat-trick goal six minutes after the break, but had strayed marginally offside.
Fenerbahce, who failed to have a shot before the break, attempted to make the most of that reprieve, with Ugurcan Cakir smothering a Romelu Lukaku chance immediately after.

Ismail Jakobs then headed against the woodwork at the other end before Kahveci got Fenerbahce back into the match with a moment of quality. He met Oguz Aydin's cross with an overhead kick, and Cakir could not keep it out despite getting a hand to it.

That goal opened the game up, with Lucas Torreira, Leroy Sane and Rafael Leao all seeing chances go begging for Galatasaray, while Fenerbahce could have snatched a late draw, but Milan Skriniar's 90th-minute header was cleared off the line by Mario Lemina.
Galatasaray open the gap to rivals
Galatasaray went back to the top of the table, moving two points clear of Amed SFK, but Fenerbahce sit fifth, already six points behind them after a sluggish display.
The hosts looked up for it from the very start at RAMS Park and racked up 11 of their 23 shots before the break, with Fenerbahce offering virtually nothing going the other way.
In fact, they became the first team in a Super Lig match this season to prevent Fenerbahce from taking a single shot in the first half, while also having the most on-target shots against them (six).

Osimhen alone had seven shots, more than Fenerbahce managed as a team across the 90 minutes (four, three on target), while he also accumulated 0.62 expected goals (xG) of Galatasaray's 2.27 total – the visitors, by contrast, mustered just 0.31 xG.
Okan Buruk (W5 D3 L1) became just the third manager in Galatasaray's history, after Fatih Terim (seven) and Gunduz Kilic (five), to defeat Fenerbahce at least five times in the Super Lig.
