1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.title: 'Stop referee harassment now' – Atleti hit back at Mourinho following derby comments
1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.subtitle: Jose Mourinho launched into a rant about refereeing standards following Real Madrid's defeat to Atletico Madrid, who have now hit back.
paragraphs: Atletico Madrid have hit back at Jose Mourinho following his rant about referee Ortiz Arias in the aftermath of their derby win over Real Madrid.
Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David were on target on Sunday as Los Colchoneros overcame their cross-city rivals 2-1 at the Estadio Metropolitano.
The victory lifted Diego Simeone's side to second in LaLiga, five points behind leaders Barcelona, going into the three-week international break, with Los Blancos a point further back in fourth.

But their win was not without controversy, as Madrid had centre-back Dean Huijsen sent off for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Mourinho felt Atleti were fortunate to keep all 11 men on the pitch.
Lee Kang-In avoided punishment for a high challenge that caught Federico Valverde on his ankle, leaving the Uruguay international requiring medical tests.
Cristian Romero, meanwhile, was only cautioned for what Madrid believed was a stamp on Jude Bellingham's knee, despite Arias being sent to the VAR monitor to check the incident.

Mourinho appeared at his post-match press conference with printed images of both incidents, saying they were both "clear red cards" and arguing Arias was not equipped to handle the pressure of such a big game.
Simeone subsequently said it was important that referees are protected and told his Madrid counterpart: "Not everything goes, even for Mourinho."
And on Monday, Atleti's club account on X posted an image of Mourinho discussing the incidents at his press conference, along with the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Atleti have only lost one of the last eight derbies between the teams in LaLiga (W3 D4), winning four of the last six meetings to take place at the Metropolitano (D1 L1).
Los Colchoneros have also won seven straight home games against teams from the Community of Madrid, the longest such winning streak in their history.

1uuwiu0m1wfda1vd9kejfeivg6.title: Pulisic targets new Milan deal after positive signs under Amorim
1uuwiu0m1wfda1vd9kejfeivg6.subtitle: Christian Pulisic's AC Milan contract runs out at the end of this season, but he hopes to extend his deal after working with Ruben Amorim.
paragraphs: Christian Pulisic hopes to extend his AC Milan contract soon as he is "very positive" about their future under Ruben Amorim.
Amorim's Milan are fifth in Serie A after the opening five games, just two points behind leaders Roma, as the Rossoneri remain unbeaten in the competition (W3 D2).
Milan did lose their Europa League opener 2-0 against Benfica, but they bounced back ahead of the international break with a 3-0 league victory over Lecce.
Pulisic scored against Lecce; it was his first Serie A goal in 266 days, since December 2025 against Hellas Verona.
Between those strikes, the American had attempted 39 shots without finding the net in the league, before finally scoring with his 40th attempt.
The 28-year-old struggled for form under Massimiliano Allegri last season, scoring 10 goals and providing four assists in 34 games, 20 of which came as a starter.
However, after missing the start of the 2026-27 campaign with injury, Pulisic has found his feet quickly under Amorim.
Pulisic's current deal with the Rossoneri expires next summer, though reports suggest the club hold an option to extend by another year, and the forward is eager to continue in Milan.
"It has been a strange start to the season," Pulisic told Sky Sport Italia.
"I was coming back from an injury and I really wanted to play, but it took time. I worked with the team and coach to get back on the field.
"We are learning his system, how he wants to play. I am very positive about him. Our most recent match was one of the best, so we want to build on that.

"He wants us to find certain positions, especially when we have the ball, and to make specific movements. Obviously, we are also given some freedom in attack, but there are principles and positions to keep to.
"I am very happy at Milan. The club is giving me everything, it helps me a great deal. I am concentrating on playing, but we'll talk about it [new contract], I hope soon.
"I feel really happy at Milan and want to continue here."

1uv22lpxfehyc1vmx09d4tngy9.title: 'This team just doesn't quit' – San Jose's never-say-die attitude excites Jasinski
1uv22lpxfehyc1vmx09d4tngy9.subtitle: The San Jose Earthquakes are close to securing their playoff place, but they come up against MLS leaders Nashville SC next at PayPal Park.
paragraphs: San Jose Earthquakes' Jack Jasinski believes the team's never-say-die attitude will be what carries them into the postseason as they look to extend their unbeaten streak against Nashville SC.
San Jose have not lost any of their last eight MLS outings, with a 1-1 draw at Real Salt Lake extending that run thanks to Jasinski's late equaliser.
They sit fourth in the Western Conference despite drawing their last two outings and could secure their playoff place this weekend if they beat the league leaders.
The 'Quakes are no strangers to late drama in their games this campaign, and Jasinski says it is that approach which will ensure a strong finish to the regular season.
"We've had a bit of a formation change, and since then we haven't lost in a while and have managed to squeak out draws and get some wins," Jasinski said after the draw with RSL.
"This team just doesn't quit until the end, and over a long season, that starts to pay off.
"It's a quick turnaround to Nashville on Saturday, but we've used the whole squad well, and we'll continue to do that going forward."
As for Nashville, the Supporters' Shield could be in their hands by the end of the weekend if they beat San Jose.
Even a draw or a loss could be enough if the Vancouver Whitecaps and Inter Miami drop points, but there is also a place in the record books on the line.
Nashville need just nine points from their final five matches to set a new single-season points record (Miami – 74 in 2024).
They currently sit 14 points clear of the Herons in the East and have won their last four matches, including a thumping 4-0 win over Sporting Kansas City last time out.
San Jose Earthquakes – Jack Jasinski
Jasinski came off the bench to score the equalizing goal for San Jose against Real Salt Lake, his second career MLS goal on what was San Jose's second shot on target of the match.
RSL had attempted the game's previous nine shots before Jasinski's leveller.
Nashville SC – Sam Surridge

1uv7la8e2fj8o1pwm899c6zg4z.title: Herrington: Australia's performances against Brazil show how far we've come
1uv7la8e2fj8o1pwm899c6zg4z.subtitle: Australia drew and lost to Brazil during their two friendly matches, but Lucas Herrington was full of praise for how they fought.
paragraphs: Australia defender Lucas Herrington is optimistic about the team's future, saying their performance in their 4-2 defeat to Brazil "shows how far we've come".
The Socceroos came within minutes of a shock win in the first of their two friendlies with Brazil but were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw last Friday after Rayan's stoppage-time leveller.
In Brisbane on Tuesday, Australia briefly led, with Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe both scoring to flip the script after Vanderson's third-minute opener.
However, Raphinha equalised just before the break from the penalty spot, before goals from Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior – again from 12 yards – secured the win in the second half.
Australia became just the second team from the AFC confederation to score twice against Brazil in a game in the last 21 years, after Japan beat the Selecao 3-2 last October.
The hosts finished the game with just seven shots – scoring with both of their attempts on target – but posted 1.5 expected goals (xG) and had 51 final-third entries, more than Brazil's 44.
And Herrington was thrilled to see the fight Australia put up against Carlo Ancelotti's side across both matches, as he believes team and fan morale is at an all-time high.
"It's so special; you can see the support around the stadium," Herrington said.

"It's awesome, the first time playing for the Socceroos in Brisbane. It means everything. I would see them growing up in Brisbane, I know how big the football community is here. It's been so nice to come home and see the reception we've got.
"All I've ever wanted is to play for the Socceroos, so to do that so early and with such great people is amazing.

"You want to play these types of games, and I think it's a credit to Australia and the Socceroos and the fans that Brazil want to come here and play us. It was a great game; we really put them under pressure.
"It shows how far we've come. Since I've been a Socceroos fan, this is the biggest reception and the most excitement that's been around the team."

1v0edv0wojk4h1mvn4ekjy98c4.title: Tah: Germany prepared to 'walk through fire' for new boss Klopp
1v0edv0wojk4h1mvn4ekjy98c4.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's Germany tenure began with a draw against the Netherlands, but Jonathan Tah has been impressed with his new boss.
paragraphs: Jonathan Tah praised Jurgen Klopp for his immediate impact since taking charge of Germany, saying that the players are ready to "walk through fire" for their new boss.
Klopp's first game in charge of Germany ended in a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands, with the former Liverpool boss denied a win by Cody Gakpo's stoppage-time equaliser.
The 59-year-old is now preparing to oversee his first game on home soil at WWK Arena, with Greece their opponents in the second game of their Nations League campaign.
Germany were perhaps fortunate to leave with a point against the Netherlands, with Xavi, also making his international bow, masterminding a dominant second-half display.
The Oranje finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.6 from their 14 shots after the break, while they were also able to restrict Germany to a tally of 0.2 from their five attempts.
But Tah is confident Klopp is the right man to take Germany forward, citing his success at club level with Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool behind his reasoning.
"It's the experience he brings from every club, that mix of fun and passion, that absolute will to win, and also the way he brings the team along. He can really fire us up," Tah said.
"I think after our initial meeting, everyone walked out thinking, 'Okay, we're ready to walk through fire together now'.
"He just has this ability to galvanise a team. We've seen that in the past too. That's something he does exceptionally well, and I think that's why he's been so successful."
Another player Tah was asked about was Liverpool's Florian Wirtz, who has again come under fire for a string of underwhelming performances so far this season.
Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt have been called up one game earlier than expected to replace Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala, who sustained injuries against the Netherlands.
At club level, Wirtz has managed just one assist in six appearances in all competitions, though his 12 chances created are the third-highest total in Andoni Iraola's squad.
The former Bayer Leverkusen forward is yet to hit the form he showed during his time in the Bundesliga, but Tah has backed Wirtz to rediscover his spark.
"I find it pretty extreme the way he's been attacked," Tah said of Wirtz. "I know the kind of player he is and that he's going to shine even more.
"I know what he's capable of and, eventually, everyone will understand."

1v73fnlfejezb18lqr5h7899b0.title: Farke: Sunderland's position at the bottom is false
1v73fnlfejezb18lqr5h7899b0.subtitle: Sunderland sit bottom of the Premier League ahead of hosting Leeds United, but Daniel Farke knows his team are in for a stern test.
paragraphs: Sunderland are in a false position at the bottom of the Premier League, so says Leeds United boss Daniel Farke.
Leeds visit the Stadium of Light on Sunday, with Sunderland sitting bottom of the pile.

Sunderland have won just four points in seven Premier League games this term (W1 D1 L5), their lowest at this stage of a league season since 2016-17, when they had two points and eventually finished bottom.
According to Opta's expected points model, however, Sunderland should be in 15th. They are approximately four points worse off than their underlying metrics would suggest.
Sunderland have made a positive start to their Europa League campaign, taking seven points from their opening three games, and Farke anticipates a stern challenge.
"I know exactly what to expect. I'm pretty sure they won't finish in the position in which they currently are. I expect them to play to their DNA and their plan," he said.
"We expect a Sunderland side who will be highly motivated and back to their best. But we want to make sure that we will be successful ourselves."
Dominic Calvert-Lewin netted for Leeds in the corresponding fixture last season, though the England international is a doubt due to a bruised foot.
Since November 29 last year, only Erling Haaland (21) has more Premier League goals than Calvert-Lewin (17), who has the best conversion rate of the 52 players to have 40+ shots in that time (24.6%).
However, Farke feels Lukas Nmecha is more than capable of stepping up, if required.
"For a back-up striker, I think Lukas Nmecha has scored seven goals. Bayern Munich would be happy if a back-up for Harry Kane scored seven goals. I think it's a really good record," he said.

"Lukas is similar in strength to Dominic. He is capable of scoring goals sometimes out of nothing. I trust them both. I can trust Lukas if he comes in or starts. I totally back my strikers to do the job."
Sunderland – Brian Brobbey
Brobbey has been out in recent weeks due to a hamstring injury he sustained while on international duty with the Netherlands.
He is Sunderland's leading scorer in the league this term, though all three of his goals came against Manchester City last month.
Leeds United – James Trafford

No goalkeeper has made more saves in the Premier League this season than Trafford (26), while the Leeds shot-stopper has the best save percentage (80%) of any goalkeeper to play more than once this term.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Sunderland won 1-0 against Leeds in their most recent Premier League meeting, last beating the Whites consecutively in the league in 2006-07.
In the top flight, they last managed it with wins separated by 10 years in April 1947 and April 1957.
Leeds have only lost on one of their last eight top-flight visits to Sunderland (W6 D1), losing 2-0 in November 2001.

No side has drawn more Premier League games than Leeds in 2026 (13), while it’s their most in the league in a year since 2015 (15 in 46 Championship games). It’s the Whites’ highest share of league games drawn in a single year in their history (13/27 – 48%).

Sunderland have lost their last four Premier League games, last having a longer losing run in December 2015 (five). All four of their defeats have been by a margin of two goals, last losing more in a row by that margin or greater in the league in September 1930 (five).

1v7grwu078eb91cajins4auyol.title: France 4-1 Belgium: Super-subs spark Nations League rout
1v7grwu078eb91cajins4auyol.subtitle: Belgium were holding out valiantly against France, but three substitutes flipped the script at the Stade de France.
paragraphs: Desire Doue, Rayan Cherki and Michael Olise scored in a remarkable finale to propel France to a come-from-behind 4-1 win over Belgium.
With just 13 minutes of normal time left in Monday's Nations League contest at the Stade de France, Zinedine Zidane's unbeaten start as France coach was in real jeopardy.
The visitors led through Dodi Lukebakio's 35th-minute strike, with the forward having burst clear on the counter-attack and finished brilliantly.
Without Kylian Mbappe, France lacked a clinical touch in the first half, with Ousmane Dembele, Maghnes Akliouche, Eduardo Camavinga and Esteban Lepaul seeing half-chances pass them by.
France's profligacy continued after the break, with Lepaul denied from point-blank range, yet Les Bleus' luck changed when Zidane turned to his bench.
Cherki and Olise were the first changes, and though they helped build the pressure, it was not until Doue entered the fray that they finally made the breakthrough.
Doue superbly created space on the edge of the box and, on the turn, drilled a sublime finish into the bottom-right corner.
The turnaround was complete four minutes later, as Olise drove to the byline and steered it back for Cherki, who duly finished.
Olise got in on the act in the 88th minute, nudging home from Doue's cutback.
And the same pair combined to complete a stunning rout in stoppage time, with Olise sliding in a crisp effort after latching onto Doue's sumptuous pass.
Super-subs to the rescue
France had all the ball, all the territory and all the intent for the vast majority of the second half, yet it really did seem as though they were short of ideas.
It seemed like Zidane would be left to bemoan Mbappe's absence, and that France's hopes of qualifying from Nations League Group A1 could be in the balance heading into the November fixtures.
Instead, their star power off the bench proved just too much for Belgium to handle.
Doue, Cherki and Olise were all spellbinding. Each of them crafted two chances, while Olise ended up having four shots, a total bettered only by Dembele (five).

Zidane made 10 changes to his starting XI, but he always knew he had real, world-class quality in reserve. This win did not come easy, but once France's talent clicked into gear, there was nothing Belgium could do.
France finished with 23 shots for a combined 2.0 expected goals, but that does not tell the whole story.
Belgium created opportunities worth a combined 0.59 xG, yet their second-half xG came in at just 0.04, as they were completely dominated.
It is now three wins from four for Zidane to start his tenure, while Mark van Bommel's Belgium sit on six points from a potential 12.

1v87htdasrkiv1dtfe17aj4pp2.title: Mainz 3-4 Bayer Leverkusen: Diaby caps thrilling win with first Bundesliga goal in three years
1v87htdasrkiv1dtfe17aj4pp2.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen emerged with all three points from a topsy-turvy clash with Mainz, with Patrick Schick and Moussa Diaby among the goals.
paragraphs: Moussa Diaby scored his first goal since returning to Bayer Leverkusen as they earned a thrilling 4-3 victory over Mainz in the Bundesliga.

Diaby – who returned to Leverkusen last month following spells at Aston Villa and Al-Ittihad – curled a sumptuous strike into the top-left corner to ultimately put Saturday's contest behind Mainz, who had rallied from 2-0 down in the first half.
Carles Martinez's side, who went into the international break on the back of a 2-0 win over RB Leipzig, came racing out of the traps and went two goals up inside nine minutes.

Robert Andrich opened the scoring in spectacular fashion, thumping a volley into the roof of the net when Mainz could only half-clear a fifth-minute corner, then Patrik Schick finished clinically after Ibrahim Maza cleverly dummied Aleix Garcia's pass through to him.

But Mainz slowly grew into the game and halved the arrears when Anthony Caci prodded home in the 33rd minute, having reacted quickest to Andrich blocking Eric Martel's header. Caci then got the hosts level four minutes before half-time, finishing across Mark Flekken after being picked out by the impressive Nadiem Amiri.

Amiri fired wide from the first shot of the second half, but Martinez's team talk clearly had the desired effect as Leverkusen restored their lead through Jarell Quansah. Amid a scramble, the England international saw a fierce strike saved brilliantly by Alexander Schwolow, but when the ball bounced back to him, he looped a header into the far corner.

Mainz then came out of their shell in search of another fightback, but Diaby extended Leverkusen's lead further in the 65th minute as he received Afonso Moreira's pass in a central area, got the ball out of his feet, then curled out of Schwolow's reach.
And despite Mainz substitute Benedict Hollerbach popping up with a predatory finish in stoppage time, Leverkusen would not be pegged back for a second time.
Schick matches Kiessling and Berbatov, Diaby ends long wait

Leverkusen's first campaign under Martinez got off to an inauspicious start as they lost 3-2 to newly promoted Elversberg on matchday one in the Bundesliga, but since then, they are unbeaten in five games in all competitions (W4 D1).

With their Bundesliga victories over Leipzig and Mainz coming after a 2-0 Europa League win against Celje, they have won three straight matches in all competitions for the first time since February (a run of four).

They have also scored at least twice in all seven of their games under Martinez overall, only netting multiple goals in more consecutive matches to start one previous managerial reign (eight under Bruno Labbadia in 2008).

Schick also continued his excellent form, becoming just the third player to score in the first five games of a Bundesliga campaign for Leverkusen, after Stefan Kiessling in 2009-10 and Dimitar Berbatov in 2005-06 (all five goals each).
But Diaby's goal was the standout moment, as he found the net in the Bundesliga for the first time in 1,278 days (versus Eintracht Frankfurt in April 2023).

Leverkusen's first campaign under Martinez got off to an inauspicious start as they lost 3-2 to newly promoted Elversberg on matchday one in the Bundesliga, but since then, they are unbeaten in five games in all competitions (W4 D1).

With their Bundesliga victories over Leipzig and Mainz coming after a 2-0 Europa League win against Celje, they have won three straight matches in all competitions for the first time since February (a run of four).

They have also scored at least twice in all seven of their games under Martinez overall, only netting multiple goals in more consecutive matches to start one previous managerial reign (eight under Bruno Labbadia in 2008).

Schick also continued his excellent form, becoming just the third player to score in the first five games of a Bundesliga campaign for Leverkusen, after Stefan Kiessling in 2009-10 and Dimitar Berbatov in 2005-06 (all five goals each). 

But Diaby's goal was the standout moment, as he found the net in the Bundesliga for the first time in 1,278 days (versus Eintracht Frankfurt in April 2023).

1vaoprf9pquai1lh03n83rgf65.title: Gibbs-White confident wins will come despite Forest's shooting struggles
1vaoprf9pquai1lh03n83rgf65.subtitle: Nottingham Forest had to settle for a point against Ipswich Town at Portman Road after more wastefulness in front of goal.
paragraphs: Morgan Gibbs-White is confident Nottingham Forest will start winning games despite another poor performance in front of goal.
Forest were held to a 1-1 draw by Ipswich Town on Friday, though the point was enough to move Oliver Glasner's side out of the Premier League relegation zone ahead of the weekend's action.
Neco Williams fired Forest into an early lead, but a poor backpass from Nikola Milenkovic allowed Julio Enciso to equalise before half-time.
Forest have dropped seven points from losing positions in the Premier League this season, the fourth-most of any side, and only one fewer than they lost in the whole of last season (eight).
Both Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye saw shots cleared off the line by Leif Davis, while Callum Hudson-Odoi dragged wide of the right post late on.

Forest accumulated 2.31 expected goals (xG) from their 17 shots; only Manchester United (138) have recorded more shots in the league than the Tricky Trees (137), who have scored the joint-least goals (six).
When asked about Forest's wastefulness in the final third, Gibbs-White told Sky Sports: "This is a question we have been asking ourselves in training.
"We have been doing shooting drills and if you had seen how they were going in yesterday, it was top.
"But they just were not in the game. It is a topic of discussion and it is not good enough but I am proud of the boys for keeping going and performing high.

"It is a massive mentality and this is a bad phase that we are going through but we need to stay positive, keep the togetherness and mentality and performances. If we keep performing like this, surely we will have to win.
"The second-half, we were completely dominant and we should have won the game in my eyes. As long as we keep performing like this surely we have to win."
Forest are back on the road again next weekend when they take on Brentford, while their final game before the international break is at home to Manchester City on November 7.

1vdbz2qe7f5h112epxk2r6i5lq.title: Mancini insists patience is needed for new Italy era
1vdbz2qe7f5h112epxk2r6i5lq.subtitle: Roberto Mancini lost on his second debut in charge of Italy, but he was confident of turning things around against Turkiye on Monday.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes patience will be needed at the start of his second stint with Italy after their defeat to Belgium in their Nations League opener.
Macini's return to the Azzurri dugout did not go to plan, with goals in either half from Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio sealing the win for Mark van Bommel's side.
The result saw Italy lose a home match while conceding two goals without scoring any for the second time in the last 40 years, after a 2-0 defeat against Croatia in August 2006.
Italy ended the match with 1.5 expected goals (xG), though only 0.3 of their tally came in the first half, while Belgium accumulated 2.5 of their 2.7 xG before the break.
Gianluigi Donnarumma made six saves to try and inspire a comeback for Italy, but Senne Lammens also made six stops at the other end to ensure Belgium emerged victorious.
Following the defeat, Mancini conceded that his team fell below expectations at the Stadio Olimpico, with a trip to Matli Stadyumu Ataturk Spor Kompleksi to face Turkiye up next.
Mancini's main request was to allow his Italy team time as they begin a new era, though he said the congested Nations League schedule was difficult for his players to navigate.
"I expect the team can put in a good performance against Turkiye, improving the pressing and the aggression," Mancini told reporters.
"In these days we haven't had time to prepare anything new, so I'm not expecting any great novelties.
"Above all, we need time to work to get to know each other and to build a team that can be competitive. We don't need anything else."
Mancini's comments were echoed by Sandro Tonali, who was a part of the team that failed to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup earlier this year.
It is a new-look Azzurri side, with the likes of Michael Kayode, Alessandro Romano, Issa Doumbia, Alessandro Vergara and Mohamed Ali Zom called up for the first time.
"The important thing now is to react, and we can do that within a few days. The group is very healthy, with a lot of young players," Tonali said.
"Having everything immediately is difficult, we don't have the star player. Time is there, we have to spend time together, work and enjoy ourselves together.
"We are healthy, strong men. With time our qualities will come out."
Following their clash with Turkiye, Italy face France next Friday before concluding the international break with a home game against Vincenzo Montella's side.
Because of the quick turnaround, Mancini revealed there would be several changes to the team that were beaten by Belgium.
"I think we have to stay calm and not get agitated in the way that is happening," Mancini added.
"We played against a strong side in Belgium, who did cause us difficulty, but then the team reacted well.
"Matches are made of episodes, the game could have changed, even if Belgium deserved to win in the end. In terms of personnel, we will definitely change.
"It is impossible to have one player available for four games this close together. We can also assess other players in matches this important."

1vgf4agol08i51l0fjduskzf9l.title: Cagliari 1-1 Juventus: Kolo Muani's first league goal rescues visitors
1vgf4agol08i51l0fjduskzf9l.subtitle: Randal Kolo Muani finally got off the mark in Serie A on Sunday as his late equaliser earned Juventus a draw away to Cagliari.
paragraphs: Randal Kolo Muani was Juventus' late hero as his 81st-minute header salvaged Luciano Spalletti's side a 1-1 draw against high-flying Cagliari at Unipol Domus.
Juventus appeared set to lose back-to-back Serie A away games for the first time since October 2025 when the in-form Daniel Maldini put Cagliari ahead in the 20th minute.
But an improved second-half display, helped by the introduction of Edon Zhegrova, was rewarded when Kolo Muani headed in his first league goal since returning to Juventus.
Juventus started brightly, but Pape Matar Sarr and Francisco Conceicao's shots from distance failed to trouble Elia Caprile, with Cagliari taking the lead against the run of play.

A break down the right saw Maldini cut inside but see his initial shot blocked by Bremer. However, the loose ball ricocheted off Pierre Kalulu, allowing Paul Mendy to control and flick possession back to the Italian, who finished past Guglielmo Vicario.
Harry Winks' long-range drive then had to be tipped over by Vicario, before Nico Gonzalez's bending free-kick at the other end was punched away from the danger by Caprile.

Spalletti made two changes at the break as Kerim Alajbegovic and Zhegrova were thrown into the action, with the latter stinging the palms of Caprile in the 52nd minute before seeing his left-footed effort tipped behind by the Cagliari goalkeeper.
Zhegrova continued to cause havoc as another curling attempt was repelled by Caprile, but Juventus' persistence eventually prevailed with nine minutes of the match remaining.

Alajbegovic's dangerous cross was glanced into the bottom-right corner by Kolo Muani for the leveller, though the Frenchman should have completed the turnaround moments later, but he could only head onto the crossbar from another teasing Alajbegovic delivery.
Andrea Cambiaso came close to snatching Juventus the win in the closing stages, but his shot from a tight angle was thwarted by Caprile, with the spoils shared on Sunday.
Kolo Muani delivers for Juventus after Spalletti criticism

Ahead of kick-off, Kolo Muani was told by Spalletti to put his best skills into practice after a difficult start to his second spell with Juventus, but he came up trumps with an important late equaliser, and he could have even won the game late on.

It was his first Serie A goal since May 2025 against Venezia, though it was Zhegrova who turned the tide. The half-time substitute finished with team-high totals for shots (six), shots on target (five) and successful dribbles (two).

But Juventus were forced to settle for a point, and despite winning 47 Serie A matches against Cagliari (only Inter and AC Milan, both with 48 have more), the Bianconeri have now only won two of their last six league games against the Rossoblu (D3 L1).

Cagliari stay inside the top four following their first draw of the season, but their strong start has been helped by Maldini. He is the first Cagliari player to score in at least four consecutive appearances in Serie A since Joao Pedro, who reached five between October and November 2020.

Juventus will, however, feel they should have made their dominance count. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.92 from their 22 attempts, 10 of which were on target, compared to Cagliari's 0.51 from their four shots.

1vh6f0lv0ctw71vbxhhagggahj.title: Sage: Palace's win over Forest was not about revenge against Glasner
1vh6f0lv0ctw71vbxhhagggahj.subtitle: Crystal Palace picked up their first Premier League win of the season against Nottingham Forest, much to the delight of Pierre Sage.
paragraphs: Pierre Sage insisted Crystal Palace's victory against Nottingham Forest was not about revenge over Oliver Glasner upon his return to Selhurst Park on Sunday.
Glasner returned to Palace for the first time since leaving the Eagles at the end of last season to join Forest, but the Austrian watched on as his team were beaten 3-1.
Dan Ndoye had given Forest the lead after just three minutes, and though the visitors dominated most of the first half, they found themselves behind going into the break.
Daichi Kamada and Jefferson Lerma scored twice in eight minutes at the end of the first half, with Yeremy Pino sealing Sage's first league win in charge just before the hour.
For the first time in 13 attempts, Palace beat Forest in the Premier League (D8 L4 prior) – the Eagles have now beaten all 35 sides that they've faced 5+ times in the competition.
It was a result that moved Palace up to 12th in the Premier League on seven points, though Sage said his team's victory was not about getting one over the Eagles' former boss.
"It's not about revenge, a confirmation or something like this for every individual player," Sage told Sky Sports.
"It's only about one game in a big series. The game is not against Oliver. The game is against Nottingham and that's the most important thing.
"We just have to be respectful with [Glasner], with what he did here. He helped me a lot because this team knows and is able to do a lot of things, and I have to thank him for that.

"It's not normal to concede too many chances as we conceded today. We had a problem in the first half, especially in the area of Ndoye. We have to be more efficient in one-vs-one situations when we defend.
"We have to be honest with what happened on the pitch. Everybody is aware of that, every player is aware of that, but I want to underline one thing: they give their life on the pitch."
It was also a show of great resilience from Palace, who have now recovered more points from losing positions than any other side in the Premier League (six).

Forest, meanwhile, suffered their first away league defeat to Palace since December 2003. The Tricky Trees had previously remained unbeaten across their prior nine visits to Selhurst Park (W3 D6), while also winning their last four Premier League matches in London before Sunday's loss.
"I think in total we played our best performance in the entire season," Glasner told Sky Sports, with Forest now just two points above the relegation zone.
"But again, if you don't score from all these chances, there's nobody to blame, because the effort was massive. I'm 100 per cent encouraged by this.
"Today I saw many positive performances, but it's not shown by the result, because we missed the most important thing: scoring goals in the right moments."
Despite the defeat, Forest created eight big chances in total, with only Blackburn Rovers (against Newcastle United in February 2012) having recorded more in a Premier League defeat (since 2010-11).

"I also want to say a huge thank you to the Crystal Palace supporters for this great reception," Glasner added. "I didn't know what I could expect, but it just shows the wonderful memories we created together here."

1vj9a3vafo6cs1a6krcb93q86u.title: 'Alvarez is the past' – Barcelona move on from summer target
1vj9a3vafo6cs1a6krcb93q86u.subtitle: Barcelona were open about their pursuit of Julian Alvarez in the summer, but have closed the door on the Atletico Madrid striker for now.
paragraphs: Barcelona sporting director Deco insists their interest in Julian Alvarez "is the past" after failing to sign the Atletico Madrid striker this summer.

Barca reportedly saw an offer of over €100m rejected by Atleti, who later revealed they would refuse to negotiate with their rivals due to the Blaugrana's public pursuit of the Argentina international.
Real Madrid's €150m bid was also rejected by Atleti, while reports suggested Alvarez turned down interest from Premier League side Arsenal.
Alvarez has featured four times for Diego Simeone's side this term, with only one of those appearances coming as a starter, registering just one assist across all competitions.
The 26-year-old made his return from a brief injury in Atleti's Madrid derby before joining up with the Argentina national team.
Barca managed to sign Gabriel Jesus late on in the window after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and Deco revealed any immediate interest in Alvarez is now over.
"Julian Alvarez is the past," Deco said at the Portugal Football Summit.
"Barcelona now have to look forward. It wasn't possible in the end. We made an offer. [Atleti] said they would not transfer him and we had to look for other solutions.
"I hope things go well for him and that he can help his club."
Barca have also been linked with a move for 15-year-old Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel in recent weeks.
Widespread reports emerged stating Gabriel had asked to leave United, with Barca and Madrid among the teams said to be monitoring the situation.
Deco, however, has put an end to the speculation, saying: "There's nothing to say about this boy.
"It's normal that players are linked with us. It always happens. There's a huge market for that with a lot of interests involved, even when [players] are young.
"But we are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that.
"First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

1vospb7qu65a1ac0d5isypkq0.title: Man City found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules
1vospb7qu65a1ac0d5isypkq0.subtitle: After being found guilty of multiple charges, Manchester City insisted they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League."
paragraphs: Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18 by an independent Commission, the league has said.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Premier League said City had been found guilty of all charges that related to serious breaches of the financial rules and the majority of charges which were "in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League's investigation".
Following widespread reports surrounding the verdicts last Friday, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak insisted he was still confident of proving the club's innocence.
City have until October 2 to exercise their right to appeal, and the club suggested that they plan to do so as part of a robust statement published after the verdict.
It read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission that has been published.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League, and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.
"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

The Commission found that during the nine-season period, among other breaches, City "arranged 'sham' contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on 'sham' agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs".
It added that "Manchester City was significantly in breach of both the Premier League’s and UEFA's spending limits".
Comments from Premier League Chief Executive Richard Masters were included in the league's statement. He said the issue of sanctions would be dealt with at a later stage.

"It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.
"Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans."
The statement also made clear the Premier League's desire to move through the next stages of the process swiftly.

It added: "The club has the right to appeal the independent Commission's findings and has until Friday 2 October to exercise that right. The Premier League Board's intention is that the full process (including any appeals and publication of relevant decisions) is concluded as soon as possible."

1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.title: Aguirre returns to Spain with LaLiga strugglers Valencia
1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.subtitle: After spending two years away from LaLiga, Javier Aguirre is back in Spain, being tasked with trying to turn Valencia's fortunes around.
paragraphs: Javier Aguirre has been appointed as the new head coach of Valencia on a contract that will run until the end of the campaign.
Aguirre arrives at the Estadio de Mestalla following a two-year stint in charge of Mexico, who he led to the round of 16 at this summer's World Cup.
The 67-year-old's deal contains an option for him to remain at the helm for a second season in Valencia, who have made a dismal start to 2026-27.
Valencia are 19th in LaLiga with four points from their opening seven games, with Carlos Corberan sacked just two months after extending his deal until 2028.
Oscar Sanchez took interim charge and helped Valencia to their first win of the season against Alaves, before overseeing a 3-2 defeat to Real Sociedad last Sunday.
Aguirre arrives with plenty of experience. He has managed 468 matches in LaLiga, the fifth-highest total of any foreign coach in the history of the competition.

The Mexican will be the fourth foreign manager to coach seven different teams in LaLiga, after Roque Olsen (seven), Ferdinand Daucik (nine), and Marcel Domingo (11), having previously taken charge of Osasuna, Atletico Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganes and Mallorca.
Aguirre's arrival comes after he announced ahead of this summer's World Cup that he would be leaving Mexico, with Rafael Marquez coming in to take over.
He was unable to end Mexico's wait for a first quarter-final appearance since 1986, after they were beaten 3-2 by 10-man England on home soil.

The defeat was Mexico's first at the Azteca in a competitive match for 13 years, since losing to Honduras in a qualifier for the 2014 World Cup, while it was the first time they had conceded three goals at the venue since a 4-3 triumph over Brazil in August 1999.
But Aguirre will now turn his attention back to club football, having last been in charge of Mallorca, who he helped avoid relegation from LaLiga in 2021-22.
Aguirre also led Mallorca to the Copa del Rey final in 2024, but they were beaten on penalties by Athletic Club before he parted ways with the club that summer.
His first home game in charge will come against Athletic on October 17, but he will make his bow for Valencia six days earlier, away to Racing de Santander.

1vto8kb3cop9319kaeodae6plh.title: 'Very early' to talk about permanent Liverpool move, says Araujo
1vto8kb3cop9319kaeodae6plh.subtitle: Having impressed early on in his loan spell with Liverpool, Ronald Araujo has been tipped to make his move to Merseyside permanent.
paragraphs: Ronald Araujo says it is still too early to discuss whether his loan move from Barcelona to Liverpool will become permanent at the end of the campaign.
Araujo joined the Reds on a season-long deal in August, when they were enduring something of an injury crisis in defence with Joe Gomez, Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Jeremy Jacquet all out.
Jacquet has recovered to make an excellent start to his Liverpool career, partnering Virgil van Dijk at centre-back, while Araujo has mostly featured at right-back.

No player has made more appearances for Liverpool this season than Araujo's 10 in all competitions (level with Jacquet and Alexis Mac Allister), and with Jeremie Frimpong suffering an injury during Saturday's 2-1 win at Brentford, his place in the team looks secure for now.

Eight of those appearances have been starts, and he has contributed to two clean sheets while contesting more aerial duels than any other Reds player (36, winning 25, the joint-most alongside Van Dijk).
Speaking ahead of Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Villarreal, Araujo acknowledged he is very happy at Anfield, though he does not know what the future holds.
"It's very early to talk about these things," Araujo told reporters. "I'm just trying to enjoy every day, continue to grow and develop every day to have that confidence.
"I'm really happy to be here, my family are also very happy, but it's a bit early to be talking about these things.
"I'm very happy because, since I arrived, I've been welcomed just as another player, not just by the people at the club but by the fans.
"I am very grateful to them. I want to give back to them by giving everything in training and every match."
Arajuo has won 35 of his 60 total duels in a Liverpool shirt, with only Jacquet (48), Mac Allister (40) and Milos Kerkez (39) winning more for the Reds this campaign.

1vuv5mkgrzipo1d6tds6vmxjoq.title: Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City: Premier League leaders respond to guilty verdict with clinical Anfield win
1vuv5mkgrzipo1d6tds6vmxjoq.subtitle: After a turbulent two weeks, Manchester City returned to action with an emphatic 3-0 defeat of 10-man Liverpool at Anfield.
paragraphs: Manchester City delivered a statement of intent in their first game since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations, swatting aside 10-man Liverpool 3-0.
Sunday's contest at Anfield came amid the backdrop of the Premier League winning their case against Man City, who have appealed the result and maintain their innocence.

A vociferous home crowd jeered every touch and pass from City's players throughout, yet the league leaders demonstrated their class with a clinical, ruthless showing in the wake of Ryan Gravenberch's 62nd-minute red card.
Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku scored in the space of three minutes, before Rayan Cherki capped off a sensational team move.
Liverpool started brightly, yet City went closest to an opener when Antoine Semenyo's drilled cross skimmed through the six-yard box.
Gianluigi Donnarumma was forced into action at the start of the second half, with Liverpool having three shots in the space of a minute.
Donnarumma denied Lewis Koumas and Gravenberch before Alexis Mac Allister curled wide.
Haaland then spurned a brilliant chance when he was put through by Semenyo, but the match turned as Gravenberch received a harsh second booking for a challenge on substitute Doku.
City did not look back from there. Within three minutes, Haaland had slammed in a first-time finish after Doku's shot was deflected into his path.
Three minutes later, Doku curled a sublime finish over the top of Alisson.

Cherki added further gloss in the 78th minute, slotting home after a sensational move that involved 41 passes, which is the longest sequence resulting in a Premier League goal since Phil Foden netted against Nottingham Forest in September 2023 (46 passes).
Man City's show of defiance

While City lodge their appeal against the guilty verdict, their Premier League rivals will want to know what punishment is going their way, and there is definitely a shadow cast over the competition as it stands.
But all Enzo Maresca's team can do is focus on the here and now, and the here and now has them top of the Premier League, three points clear of Arsenal.
There were just two minutes and 37 seconds between Gravenberch's dismissal and Haaland putting City 1-0 up, and it truly was a clinical showing from the visitors from then on.
Haaland has scored eight goals in his last eight appearances against Liverpool in all competitions – no other player has scored more than five goals versus the Reds since he joined City in 2022.

Doku scored his 12th Premier League goal, but only his second as a substitute (also October 2024 v Fulham) – he is the third sub to score at Anfield for City in the competition after George Weah in September 2000 and Bernardo Silva in January 2018.
Liverpool, meanwhile, are now winless in eight in the Premier League when facing the team starting the day top of the league (D6 L2), their second-worst run behind nine matches between 2002 and 2008.
Andoni Iraola, whose unbeaten start has come to an end, may point to that dubious decision to send Gravenberch off, but overall, his team were second-best.

The Reds only registered 0.86 expected goals, with just 0.38 xG coming from open play. For a team littered with big-money attackers such as Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, and backed by a fierce crowd, more might have been expected.

1vxm1vww1isok138ypj7prtukq.title: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds United: Le Bris' men still bottom after bore draw
1vxm1vww1isok138ypj7prtukq.subtitle: Leeds United drew away from home for the ninth time this calendar year, as they played out a low-key 0-0 draw at Sunderland.
paragraphs: Sunderland were held to a 0-0 draw by Leeds United as difficult conditions made for an underwhelming contest at the Stadium of Light on Sunday.
Storm Boelo has battered much of the United Kingdom over the past few days, and neither team could really gain a foothold as the winds made it difficult to play liquid football.
Brian Brobbey had Sunderland's best efforts in the first half, while Sean Longstaff twice went close late on for Leeds, but a goalless draw was a pretty fair reflection of the game.

Netherlands striker Brobbey, playing a league game for the first time in a month due to a hamstring injury sustained on international duty, saw a deflected attempt well saved by James Trafford low to his right in the seventh minute.
Nordi Mukiele dragged one wide of the left-hand post from 30 yards, and Brobbey stole ahead of Jaka Bijol before prodding at Trafford after Harry Wilson had the ball pinched.
Leeds did not register an effort on target until Tarik Muharemovic tamely headed at Robin Roefs from Wilson's corner in the 56th minute.
Trafford then did well to get down low to Nilson Angulo's curling shot, and also parried away the Sunderland winger's deflected strike from the edge of the box.

Omar Alderete saw his blushes spared by the offside flag when he woefully side-footed Granit Xhaka's clipped free-kick wide, while Roefs did well to keep out Ao Tanaka's shot on the spin at the other end.
Former Newcastle United midfielder Longstaff came off the bench to test Roefs from 20 yards, then had another goal-bound effort blocked by his own team-mate Lukas Nmecha deep into injury time.
Leeds draw on the road again, as Sunderland stay bottom
The conditions really made for a difficult outing for both of these teams, which was reflected in an expected goals (xG) total of 0.91 for Sunderland to Leeds' 0.57.
There were four shots on target apiece, but truthfully nothing that you would have expected to yield a goal.
For Leeds, it represents a ninth away league draw in 2026, the most of any Premier League side and their most in a calendar year since 1995 (also nine).
Daniel Farke's side are proving tough to beat, but games involving Leeds this season have seen the joint-fewest goals struck in the opening 20 minutes (one for, zero against).

Regis Le Bris' Sunderland are still bottom of the table despite ending a four-match losing streak in the league. They did, though, avoid racking up their longest losing streak in the competition since 2015 (five), last having a longer losing run in December 2015 (five).

And there was a nice milestone for Chris Rigg, who made his 100th appearance for Sunderland (22nd in the Premier League), reaching a century of games for the club at the age of just 19 years and 129 days.

1vyqa1mr1581317ddnrqy1c0e8.title: Bayer Leverkusen 5-2 FC Nurnberg: Tapsoba double inspires cup comeback
1vyqa1mr1581317ddnrqy1c0e8.subtitle: Edmond Tapsoba scored twice as Bayer Leverkusen recovered from an awful start to hammer FC Nurnberg 5-2 in the DFB-Pokal.
paragraphs: Bayer Leverkusen surged back from 2-0 down to cruise into the last 16 of the DFB-Pokal with a 5-2 rout of FC Nurnberg.
Edmond Tapsoba scored twice and Lucas Vazquez capped off the victory with a wonderful volley in the 89th minute, but at one stage, it looked as though Leverkusen would be on the end of an upset.
Nurnberg, who sit second in the second tier and are coached by Germany and Bayern Munich great Miroslav Klose, raced into a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes at BayArena.
Rafael Lubach opened the scoring with an excellent 13th-minute finish, before Sigurd Haugen tucked in from close range at the end of a rapid breakaway.
However, new Leverkusen captain Tapsoba headed home from Aleix Garcia's corner to reduce the deficit before half-time.
And that paved the way for a superb second-half showing from Leverkusen.
Tapsoba doubled his tally four minutes after the restart, prodding home at the second attempt after Nurnberg failed to clear from a corner.
Patrik Schick, on as a half-time substitute, then swung the tide fully in Leverkusen's favour when he slotted in from a penalty that he won, having been felled by Alexis Kalogeropoulos.

Jonas Hofmann brilliantly picked out the bottom-right corner from the edge of the box to extend Leverkusen's advantage in the 78th minute, and former Real Madrid man Vazquez then rounded things off with an immaculate strike.
Tapsoba leads by example
Tapsoba has been a regular for Leverkusen since he joined the club in 2020 as a youngster. Now 27, he was handed the captain's armband this term, and he led the way in some fashion.
The centre-back had four attempts, getting three of those on target. Only Hofmann (five) had more shots for either team.
Tapsoba did not have lots to do defensively, given Leverkusen largely dominated, with Nurnberg only having five attempts to their hosts' 25, but he also led Leverkusen for clearances (two).
Garcia was also hugely influential in midfield, creating a game-leading four chances and having a whopping 132 touches, 42 more than any other player (Tapsoba had 90).

While it was ultimately a convincing win for Leverkusen, who generated chances worth 3.07 expected goals (xG), Nurnberg suffered their first DFB-Pokal defeat in a game in which they led at half-time since January 2011, when they lost to Schalke, ending a run of seven such games.

1vz5oaxqeh6kc1mqlet5m9i0o1.title: 'There was no game' for Milan after Maignan red card, says Amorim
1vz5oaxqeh6kc1mqlet5m9i0o1.subtitle: AC Milan were beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth in the Europa League, and they had to play over an hour with 10 men after Mike Maignan's red card.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim said Mike Maignan's red card "changed everything" in their 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth in the Europa League, adding "there was no game" for his team after that.
Milan's difficult start to their European campaign continued on Thursday at the Vitality Stadium, with the Rossoneri finding themselves behind after just eight minutes.
Koni De Winter was penalised for handling the ball inside the penalty area, with Justin Kluivert stepping up to score from 12 yards, and it only got worse from there for Milan.
Maignan was sent off in the 27th minute after shoving Tyler Adams in the face ahead of a corner, with another spot-kick awarded that Marcus Tavernier confidently dispatched.
Bournemouth were able to add further gloss to the scoreline six minutes from time through Amine Adli, who bent a superb free-kick past substitute goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani.
The result saw Marco Rose's side become the first English team to win each of their first three games in major European competition since Sunderland back in October 1973.

For Milan, meanwhile, they conceded two penalty goals in the first half of a major European game for the first time since April 2012 against Barcelona in the Champions League, both of which were netted by Lionel Messi.

They were also the first team to face two penalties and have a player sent off in the first half of a major European game since Ajax did so against Chelsea in the Champions League last October, though Amorim said going down to 10 men altered the match entirely.
"The penalty on the corner and the red card changed everything, so it was not a game. It was not a game," Amorim told Sky Sport Italia as quoted by Football Italia.
"We didn't have time to recover from the first penalty. We tried to push in the end, but the third goal made it even harder for us. There was no game.
"It's not about rhythm or Salzburg, there was no game. It is a different team, you cannot have a penalty in that corner, and you cannot get sent off in that situation."
Maignan became the first ever Milan goalkeeper to be sent off in a major European game, while it also continued the Serie A giants' dismal record in England.

They have won just two of their 23 away matches against English sides in major European competition (D7 L14) and remain winless on the road against such opposition in the UEFA Cup/Europa League (P7 D3 L4).
But Amorim said costly errors proved to be Milan's downfall, adding: "That is true, we cannot do that.
"We need to keep 11 players on the pitch, there are more experienced players, but now we need to recover and get ready for the next game.
"We have to run a lot with one less player, try to press at the right moment in that situation, so it was a negative in all respects."
The encounter on Thursday marked 100 days since Amorim took charge of Milan, who are unbeaten (W4 D3) and fourth in Serie A ahead of facing Udinese this Sunday.
"This is part of the journey. If you look at the history of Milan, we are at a different point," Amorim said of his tenure.
"Fabio Capello is talking about the history of Milan, and I understand that, but we must be realistic.
"I appreciated the way we fought, we tried to do something, to help each other out, so we must learn from these moments, realise this is football."

1w0o5nhnbh8861fsqhoj2bts1f.title: Manchester City 5-1 AEK Athens: Foden hits hat-trick in five-star victory
1w0o5nhnbh8861fsqhoj2bts1f.subtitle: Erling Haaland was left on the bench for Manchester City as Phil Foden starred with a Champions League hat-trick against AEK Athens.
paragraphs: Phil Foden scored a sensational hat-trick to help Manchester City return to winning ways in the Champions League after they thumped AEK Athens 5-1 at Etihad Stadium.
Enzo Maresca's side produced the perfect response to their 4-2 defeat against Paris Saint-Germain last time out, with Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki also scoring on Tuesday.

The hosts' early dominance was rewarded in the 12th minute when Enzo Fernandez's free-kick beat Alberto Brignoli but cannoned against the crossbar, with Anderson the quickest to react to the loose ball and turn it into the net.
City hit the woodwork again soon after when Allan thundered against the frame of the goal from a tight angle, but the Premier League leaders did double their tally through Foden.

Fernandez spread the play out wide for Foden, who played a neat one-two with Rico Lewis before firing into the roof of Brignoli's net, scoring in successive appearances for the Citizens, having gone 35 outings without a goal beforehand.

Cherki almost rounded off a wonderful team move, but he was met with a strong stop by the AEK goalkeeper at his near post before the break, and the visitors reduced the deficit seven minutes after the restart when Stavros Pilios picked out the bottom-right corner.

But AEK's hopes of a comeback were dashed in the space of seven minutes. First, Cherki collected Foden's pass on the edge of the box, sending Kervin Arriaga onto his backside before curling a left-footed shot beyond the grasp of Brignoli.

Foden then scored his second and City's fourth in the 65th minute when Cherki's searching ball over the top of the AEK defence was brilliantly cushioned by Lewis and into the path of Foden, who arrowed first time into the top-left corner.
And the win was sealed 14 minutes from time as Foden completed his hat-trick. The Englishman was in the right place at the right time to tuck home Ryan McAidoo's cross and seal an emphatic victory.
No Haaland? No problem for City as Foden delivers statement performance

Having made a blistering start to the season for City, Erling Haaland started on the bench amid concerns about an injury sustained in Saturday's 3-2 win over Ipswich Town in the Premier League, but the Norwegian could sit back and relax as Foden took the reins.

Before lining up against AEK, Foden had managed just three goal involvements (one goal, two assists) in seven appearances across all competitions this season, but he bettered that entire tally in just one match here (three goals, one assist).

Foden became the third Englishman to score a hat-trick and assist a goal in a Champions League match, along with Wayne Rooney (September 2004 against Fenerbahce, for Manchester United) and Raheem Sterling (October 2019 against Atalanta, for City).
It was also the first time a City player scored a Champions League hat-trick since March 2023, when Haaland netted five against RB Leipzig, while Foden has now scored 23 times in the competition.

The result also continued Maresca's fine start in charge of the Citizens. He has 10 wins in 12 games as City manager in all competitions (L2), becoming one of six managers in the Premier League era (since 1992-93) with 10 wins in as few as 12 games with a club, along with Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea (12), Pep Guardiola at City (10), Unai Emery at Arsenal (12), Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Man Utd (11) and Arne Slot at Liverpool (11).

Despite Pilios becoming the first Albanian player to score in the Champions League since Berat Djimsiti in October 2024 for Atalanta, it was a comfortable outing for City, who finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.84 from their 17 shots to AEK's 0.72 from 11 attempts.

1w2ez5c95zm8s1n4q1e7fhnui5.title: 'Concern has never been a thing' for St. Louis boss Damet
1w2ez5c95zm8s1n4q1e7fhnui5.subtitle: St. Louis City will be aiming to extend their unbeaten run in MLS to 17 games when they face the New York Red Bulls on Wednesday.
paragraphs: St. Louis City boss Yoann Damet insisted "concern has never been a thing" for him this season as his side prepare to take on the New York Red Bulls.
After a slow start to the 2026 campaign, St. Louis are now fifth in the Western Conference, and they could go level on points with second-place FC Dallas if they beat the Red Bulls.
St. Louis defeated Toronto FC 3-1 last time out, conceding deep into second-half stoppage time, while they have also reached the final of the U.S. Open Cup in recent weeks.
Damet's side are on an 18-game unbeaten run across all competitions, but the Frenchman believes his players have been threatening a run like this one all season.
"I look at these guys and they have been the same since January," said Damet. "Concern has never been a thing.
"Focus and preparation has been a thing since the start of the year. I think every new day is a new day to get better and to prepare for our next game.
"I think those guys have been like that since day one, so this week has been no different.
"We know we have another big game in New York and everybody is excited and locked in preparing for that game."
NYRB, meanwhile, are eighth in the East after back-to-back 1-0 wins over the Columbus Crew and rivals New York City FC.
Julian Hall scored the lone goal in their win over NYCFC, the 18-year-old’s 10th goal of the season and fourth match-winner.
This match with St. Louis was scheduled to take place on Saturday, but was postponed due to adverse weather conditions.
New York Red Bulls – Cade Cowell
With top scorer Hall unavailable after being called up to the United States squad, Cowell will look to step up for NYRB.
The 22-year-old, who has scored twice in 2026, has six assists this term, with only Emil Forsberg registering more (seven).
St. Louis City – Simon Becher
Seven different St. Louis players have at least five goal contributions during the team's current 16-game unbeaten run, led by Becher's nine (seven goals, two assists).
Nine different St. Louis players have scored a match-winner in that time, with Tomas Totland (two) the only one with multiple (one own goal winner).
MATCH PREDICTION – ST. LOUIS CITY WIN
This will be St. Louis City's 148th match in all competitions and 130th in the regular season, but their first-ever match against the New York Red Bulls.
St. Louis extended their regular-season unbeaten run to 16 games (W11 D5) with a win over Toronto, equalling NYRB's 2016 run for the third-longest in a single regular season in MLS history.
The only longer single-season unbeaten runs in regular-season play in MLS history are 19 straight by Dallas in 2010 and 18 straight by the Crew in 2004.

NYRB have posted back-to-back wins for the third time this season with victories over Columbus and NYCFC. The Red Bulls have won three straight regular-season matches only once over the last three seasons, doing so in May 2025.
New York Red Bulls – 27.3%

1w2hwfnp1ojxm1tncfbiwtxyla.title: ​Leeds United 1-1 Manchester United: Carrick's men pegged back as winless run continues
1w2hwfnp1ojxm1tncfbiwtxyla.subtitle: Manchester United are now winless in six matches in all competitions, and five in the Premier League, after a 1-1 draw with Leeds United.
paragraphs: Manchester United failed to ease the pressure on Michael Carrick as their winless run stretched to six games in all competitions following a 1-1 draw at Leeds United.

After seeing Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancel out Bryan Mbeumo's strike, the Red Devils have still not tasted victory since beating Sabah in their Champions League opener in early September, while they have also gone five Premier League matches without a win.
And things could have been even worse as Leeds had the better chances to win Sunday's game in the second half, with Anton Stach wasting arguably their clearest opportunity.

Though there were no major chances in the opening 25 minutes, there was no shortage of commitment from both sides, with Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson among those to put in tough early tackles.

Leeds almost drew first blood when Nico Elvedi's downward header from a Stach free-kick was pushed away by Senne Lammens, but Man Utd soon passed up an even bigger chance as Mbeumo headed Youri Tielemans' searching cross wide.
Mbeumo would make no mistake when the same player provided a pinpoint, low delivery from the right flank in the 35th minute, though, as he stretched and flicked the ball into the bottom-left corner.

Leeds had a couple of half chances before the interval, but Calvert-Lewin was unable to trouble Lammens with a header and James Justin failed to get enough power behind his shot following a marauding run.
But the hosts' pressure paid dividends six minutes into the second half, with Calvert-Lewin well-placed to volley past Lammens after Tarik Muharemovic flicked Stach's corner on.

Ao Tanaka, Noah Okafor and Stach all fired efforts into the stands as Leeds remained in the ascendency, with the latter's chance being the clearest after Diogo Dalot headed the ball straight to him, just inside the Man Utd area.

At the other end, Fernandes went close to finding the bottom-left corner, but Carrick's side were lacklustre even after the introduction of Matheus Cunha, and Lukas Nmecha and Stach both had opportunities to win it for Leeds amid a late goalmouth scramble.
Man Utd pegged back again as Calvert-Lewin maintains home form
United failed to cling on for a morale-boosting victory after Mbeumo put them in front, and that has been something of a theme in the early stages of 2026-27.
Three of Mbeumo's four Premier League goals this season have put Man Utd 1-0 up, with only Erling Haaland (four) boasting more such goals this term.
However, on each of the last three occasions where the Cameroonian has given them the lead, the Red Devils have gone on to draw (also versus Everton and Tottenham).

When Leeds needed a goal, it was no surprise to see Calvert-Lewin step up – he has now scored in six of his last seven home Premier League games (seven goals overall) and boasts eight Premier League goals since the start of April – only Haaland (13) has more in that span.

Furthermore, since Calvert-Lewin's first home game for Leeds last season, his 12 Premier League goals at Elland Road are the third-most scored by any player at a particular venue, after Haaland at the Etihad Stadium (19) and Igor Thiago at the Gtech Community Stadium (14).

And after all is said and done, Carrick may be relieved to even leave Yorkshire with a point, after Leeds edged the expected goals (xG) tally by 1.44 to 0.91 – 1.19 of that tally came in the second half.
