1w54mq0tmlk8e1or9zevnm6w3o.title: Borussia Dortmund 1-0 Eintracht Frankfurt: Beier stunner lifts Kovac's side to Bundesliga summit
1w54mq0tmlk8e1or9zevnm6w3o.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund secured a late win over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday, courtesy of a Maximilian Beier wonder-strike.
paragraphs: Maximilian Beier came off the bench to score a sensational late winner as Borussia Dortmund moved to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday.
Ahead of Bayern Munich's clash with Freiburg on Sunday, Niko Kovac's side piled the pressure on their rivals by opening up a three-point lead at the summit.

Fabio Silva sent a header whizzing over the crossbar nine minutes in as Dortmund looked to set an early marker at Signal Iduna Park, with Serhou Guirassy seeing a low drive from range parried by Noah Atubolu.
Atubolu was on hand to deny Guirassy again moments later, while Frankfurt's first real moment of promise came from Jonathan Burkardt, whose 20-yard strike flew past the right-hand post.

Midfielder Joey Veerman then posed a strong threat for Dortmund with his set piece delivery, sending a pair of dangerous crosses into the box in quick succession in the 31st minute, with both Guirassy and Felix Nmecha heading off-target.

Gregor Kobel was then called into action for the first time three minutes later to block Younes Ebnoutalib's close-range poke, before diving at full stretch to parry Fares Chaibi's top-corner strike from distance immediately after the restart.
Dortmund went close again when Veerman supplied another pinpoint cross for Guirassy, whose header crashed against the crossbar.
Further half-chances for Ramy Bensebaini and Julian Ryerson went begging as Dortmund appeared destined to settle for a point, but substitute Beier produced a moment of magic late on.

The German controlled Jobe Bellingham's pass on the edge of the area before curling a spectacular effort into the top corner beyond a helpless Atubolu, sending Signal Iduna Park into raptures and lifting Dortmund to the Bundesliga summit.
Dortmund dazzle at home
While Bayern's dominance has often left Dortmund playing second fiddle in the Bundesliga, Kovac's side have announced themselves as strong title contenders this season.
And victories like Saturday's, even when far from convincing, could prove crucial if Dortmund are to mount a sustained challenge for the title.

Indeed, Kovac's side have collected 17 points from their opening seven Bundesliga games – their best start to a campaign since 2023-24, when they also had 17 at this stage. They last amassed more points after seven matches in 2017-18 (19).
Dortmund have also enjoyed remarkable success against Eintracht Frankfurt, recording more Bundesliga victories (53) and home wins (40) against them than any other opponent.
In fact, they have now won 15 of their last 16 home league meetings with Frankfurt, with their only defeat across that run coming in April 2021 (2-1).
The Black and Yellow have also kept five clean sheets in their opening seven Bundesliga matches this season, equalling their club record at this stage of a campaign, previously achieved in 2020-21.
And while their wastefulness in front of goal nearly threatened to prove costly, Dortmund ultimately made their dominance count, generating 1.54 expected goals (xG) to Frankfurt's 0.82.
1w54mq0tmlk8e1or9zevnm6w3o.html:
Maximilian Beier came off the bench to score a sensational late winner as Borussia Dortmund moved to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday. 

Ahead of Bayern Munich's clash with Freiburg on Sunday, Niko Kovac's side piled the pressure on their rivals by opening up a three-point lead at the summit. 

Fabio Silva sent a header whizzing over the crossbar nine minutes in as Dortmund looked to set an early marker at Signal Iduna Park, with Serhou Guirassy seeing a low drive from range parried by Noah Atubolu. 

Atubolu was on hand to deny Guirassy again moments later, while Frankfurt's first real moment of promise came from Jonathan Burkardt, whose 20-yard strike flew past the right-hand post. 

Midfielder Joey Veerman then posed a strong threat for Dortmund with his set piece delivery, sending a pair of dangerous crosses into the box in quick succession in the 31st minute, with both Guirassy and Felix Nmecha heading off-target.

Gregor Kobel was then called into action for the first time three minutes later to block Younes Ebnoutalib's close-range poke, before diving at full stretch to parry Fares Chaibi's top-corner strike from distance immediately after the restart. 

Dortmund went close again when Veerman supplied another pinpoint cross for Guirassy, whose header crashed against the crossbar. 

Further half-chances for Ramy Bensebaini and Julian Ryerson went begging as Dortmund appeared destined to settle for a point, but substitute Beier produced a moment of magic late on. 

The German controlled Jobe Bellingham's pass on the edge of the area before curling a spectacular effort into the top corner beyond a helpless Atubolu, sending Signal Iduna Park into raptures and lifting Dortmund to the Bundesliga summit.

Dortmund dazzle at home  

While Bayern's dominance has often left Dortmund playing second fiddle in the Bundesliga, Kovac's side have announced themselves as strong title contenders this season. 

And victories like Saturday's, even when far from convincing, could prove crucial if Dortmund are to mount a sustained challenge for the title. 

Indeed, Kovac's side have collected 17 points from their opening seven Bundesliga games – their best start to a campaign since 2023-24, when they also had 17 at this stage. They last amassed more points after seven matches in 2017-18 (19). 

Dortmund have also enjoyed remarkable success against Eintracht Frankfurt, recording more Bundesliga victories (53) and home wins (40) against them than any other opponent. 

In fact, they have now won 15 of their last 16 home league meetings with Frankfurt, with their only defeat across that run coming in April 2021 (2-1). 

The Black and Yellow have also kept five clean sheets in their opening seven Bundesliga matches this season, equalling their club record at this stage of a campaign, previously achieved in 2020-21. 

And while their wastefulness in front of goal nearly threatened to prove costly, Dortmund ultimately made their dominance count, generating 1.54 expected goals (xG) to Frankfurt's 0.82.

1wd9bkjla64o91u30x07ttqix9.title: Arsenal 3-0 Lille: Saka stars off the bench for Premier League champions
1wd9bkjla64o91u30x07ttqix9.subtitle: Arsenal were frustrated by Lille in their Champions League clash, but Bukayo Saka inspired a brilliant seven-minute spell to ensure the win.
paragraphs: Arsenal's perfect start to their Champions League campaign continued as Bukayo Saka starred off the bench in the Gunners' 3-0 win over Lille at the Emirates Stadium.
Jurrien Timber scored the first of Arsenal's three goals in seven second-half minutes, with Saka then teeing up Eberechi Eze two minutes after replacing Noni Madueke.
Saka got in on the act in the 71st minute after combining with fellow substitute Kai Havertz, as Arsenal followed up their win over Napoli with a more convincing display here.

Arsenal did, however, struggle to find their groove early on, though they carved out two chances in quick succession, with Bruno Guimaraes turning Timber's cross wide from inside the box, before another delivery from the Dutchman was headed straight at Berke Ozer by Mikel Merino.

The visitors then had a goal ruled out for offside against Ayase Ueda, who finished calmly past David Raya, but the Spaniard's clean sheet was preserved on the day he went level with David Seaman for most European Cup/Champions League games played for Arsenal among goalkeepers (38).

Eze then shot straight at Ozer before Guimaraes' swerving strike in first-half stoppage time almost caught out the Lille goalkeeper, who jumped quickly to his feet to swat the ball behind with Viktor Gyokeres waiting to pounce on the rebound.

Lille continued to frustrate Arsenal in the second half, and just as Mikel Arteta was preparing to bring on Saka, Havertz and Martin Odegaard, the Gunners hit the front in the 64th minute when Timber collected Madueke's pass before lofting the ball over Ozer.
Saka wasted little time in making his mark on proceedings as he pulled the ball back for Eze to brilliantly stroke home a bouncing effort that nestled into the bottom-right corner.
And the result was sealed four minutes later by Saka, who curled into the back of the net to round off a flowing Arsenal move that saw Havertz and Odegaard heavily involved.
Guimaraes almost capitalised on a mistake by Benjamin Andre, but his shot was saved by Ozer, and Arsenal's blistering seven-minute spell was enough to seal all three points.
Saka underlines Arsenal's quality after tepid first half

Despite leaving the likes of Saka, Havertz and Odegaard on the bench, Arteta was still able to field a front line that consisted of Merino, Gyokeres and Madueke, but the Arsenal boss was forced to turn to his first-team regulars to click his side into gear.

Arsenal have now failed to score a first-half goal in any of their last five games in the Premier League or Champions League. Their last goal before the break was against Chelsea on September 6, which led to Arteta making a triple change just after the hour.

Timber got the Gunners ahead before Saka came to the party. The England international has now scored 19 goals in major European competition for Arsenal, the outright second most of any player at the club after Thierry Henry (42).

In addition, only Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14) have more Champions League assists for Arsenal than Saka (nine, level with Alexis Sanchez and Theo Walcott), while he is the fifth Arsenal player to both score and assist a goal as a substitute in a Champions League match.

And the Gunners were deserving of their win too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.85 from their 16 shots compared to Lille's 0.38 from their four attempts, with Bayern Munich up next for Arsenal in the competition on October 21.

1wen8p5681sv519ncmwf5khg39.title: Man City had to overcome 'mental battle' to beat Liverpool, says Haaland
1wen8p5681sv519ncmwf5khg39.subtitle: Manchester City were greeted by a vociferous atmosphere at Anfield, but on the pitch, they brushed aside Liverpool with a comfortable win.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland said Manchester City's 3-0 win over 10-man Liverpool was a "mental battle" as they played their first game since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations.

There was a hostile atmosphere at Anfield, with every touch by a City player being jeered amid the backdrop of the Premier League winning their case against the club, who have appealed the result and maintain their innocence.
The game turned on Ryan Gravenberch's 62nd-minute red card, which he received for a second-bookable offence, having clumsily brought down Jeremy Doku.
And within six minutes of Gravenberch's dismissal, City were 2-0 up, with Haaland and Doku both clinically finishing past Alisson Becker.

Rayan Cherki then added some late gloss to the scoreline, finishing off a stunning team move consisting of 41 passes as he danced through Liverpool's defence to slot in their third and move City three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

Haaland has now scored eight goals in his last eight appearances against Liverpool in all competitions – no other player has netted more than five versus the Reds since he joined City in 2022 (Ismaila Sarr – five).
"Every single person part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time," Haaland told Sky Sports.
"It was tough, it was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.
"It's always tough to come here; if you look at the record, it's tough. With the Pep [Guardiola] and [Jurgen] Klopp era, it was tough for both teams; always has been.

"Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about, and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do.
"You want to win games; it's as simple as that. Perform well, play good football and win games. This was a mental battle, never easy coming back from internationals.
"Proud that we managed to stick together; we are mentally strong. Plenty of games coming up, so time to recover and go again."
A team have started with six straight wins in just two of the last seven Premier League seasons (since 2020-21): City in 2023-24 and again this term.
Having won at Anfield with Nottingham Forest in 2024-25 (1-0) and 2025-26 (3-0), Elliot Anderson is the seventh player to win his first three away starts against Liverpool in the Premier League.
He controlled the game, having more touches (100), accurate passes (71/78) and successful duels (11/17) than any other player on the pitch.
"Togetherness, fight, a tough place to come, and we stuck together and fought for each other. We've showed courage," he told Sky Sports.

"[The atmosphere] was more than normal; arriving into Anfield and the first 10 minutes of the game, we did well to quieten the crowd. Struggled first half, but second, we were better and then the goals came.
"It's a game you have to stick together more than ever.
"I just enjoy it. I enjoy the crowd, the noise; I thrive on it, and that's when I come alive. It gives me confidence."

1wffhfzxrr1k21fu9irduxetun.title: Kovac relieved to be back at home after Dortmund's long away trips
1wffhfzxrr1k21fu9irduxetun.subtitle: After trips to Norway and Azerbaijan, Borussia Dortmund are back at home this weekend as they host Eintracht Frankfurt.
paragraphs: Niko Kovac is relieved to be "finally playing at home again" after three consecutive away games for Borussia Dortmund.
BVB have had their fair share of travel since returning from the international break, facing Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League before going to Union Berlin last time out in the Bundesliga.
And ahead of their home clash with Eintracht Frankfurt this weekend, Dortmund completed a long trip to Azerbaijan as they defeated Sabah in the Champions League.
Kovac is delighted to be back at home, but is wary of the task ahead in Frankfurt on Saturday.
Kovac lost his last Bundesliga meeting with Eintracht coach Adi Hutter 5-1 in November 2019 while in charge of Bayern Munich, a result that led to his dismissal.
Kovac has only conceded more goals in a single Bundesliga match as a manager once: in May 2023, his Wolfsburg side lost 6-0 to BVB.
"We're finally playing at home again. It's good to play in front of our own fans. I hope they'll cheer us on to victory," said Kovac.
"They'd [Eintracht] certainly like to have one or two more points, but their play has been inconsistent in recent games. A draw, a loss, a win – they've had it all.
"It's a team that will finish in the top third of the table at the end of the season. I'm convinced of that."
Eintracht are 11th in the Bundesliga, following up a 6-0 defeat to RB Leipzig with a 1-0 win over Koln.
Frankfurt have fielded the youngest players in the Bundesliga this season, with an average age of 24 years and 176 days.
Dortmund have fielded the fourth-youngest side (25y 72d) and are the only team to have used seven different teenagers.
Borussia Dortmund – Waldemar Anton
Waldemar Anton has made 54 clearances in the Bundesliga this season, while Eintracht's Robin Koch has made 55.
Only two players in the league have recorded more clearances than the pair (Lukas Pinckert 57, Nikola Katic 75).
Eintracht Frankfurt – Younes Ebnoutalib

Younes Ebnoutalib has scored half of Eintracht's league goals this season (five of 10), the joint-highest share of any player for their team in the Bundesliga, level with Werder Bremen's Niclas Fullkrug (50%).
Ebnoutalib's only Bundesliga goal prior to this season came on his debut against Dortmund in January 2026.
MATCH PREDICTION: BORUSSIA DORTMUND WIN
Dortmund have won more Bundesliga games against Eintracht than against any other opponent, both in total (52) and at home (39).
BVB have won 14 of their last 15 Bundesliga home games against Frankfurt, with the only exception being a 2-1 defeat in April 2021 during Hutter's first spell in charge of the Eagles.

Eintracht have conceded at least three goals in each of their last six Bundesliga top matches (25 in total), the second-longest such streak since the top match format was introduced in the 2009-10 season, behind only Schalke's run of eight consecutive games between 2020 and 2021.
Dortmund have drawn their last two Bundesliga matches and could now go three league games without a win for the first time under Kovac; they last went three games without a win in January 2025.

Following their 1-0 win against Koln, Eintracht could win consecutive Bundesliga matches for the first time since November 2025. They last won back-to-back league games while keeping a clean sheet in November and December 2024.
Borussia Dortmund – 60.8%
Eintracht Frankfurt – 19.4%

1wh053on6th8q14mbaxsz7eqs8.title: The Numbers Game: Barcelona eye LaLiga history, Madrid seek Mourinho magic in El Clasico
1wh053on6th8q14mbaxsz7eqs8.subtitle: Barcelona face Real Madrid in LaLiga this week, with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe among the stars hoping to make a Clasico statement.
paragraphs: Few, if any, rivalries in world football can match the animosity, theatre and sheer level of quality on show in El Clasico.
And with Jose Mourinho being reintroduced to the mix, Real Madrid's clashes with Barcelona this season should be appointment viewing.
The first of those takes place on Sunday at Camp Nou, and with Barca winning their first nine games to assume early control of the LaLiga title race, it is a crucial one for both teams.
Defeats to Real Betis and Atletico Madrid have left Madrid playing catch-up, with six points separating the teams ahead of their head-to-head meeting.
Who will come out on top, and which superstars will have a decisive impact? Here, we delve into Opta's best insights to provide a data-powered preview.
Given Barcelona's swashbuckling start to the campaign, it is no surprise to see them favoured by the Opta supercomputer on home soil.

Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the model, Hansi Flick's team were victorious in 56% of scenarios, with Madrid assigned a 24.8% chance of an away win and a 19.2% likelihood of earning a point.
In the supercomputer's 2026-27 season predictions, Barca are currently assigned a 77.1% chance of successfully defending their crown, with Madrid's title hopes down at 15%.
But those probabilities could swing significantly on Sunday, depending on who emerges with the bragging rights.
Barcelona have won their last two home games against Madrid in LaLiga – a 2-0 triumph in May that clinched the title for 2025-26, and a thrilling 4-3 triumph 12 months earlier.
Only once in the 21st century have Barca achieved three consecutive home victories against Madrid in the competition, doing so under Pep Guardiola between 2008 and 2010.

However, Madrid have won three of their last six away games against the Blaugrana in LaLiga (L3), as many victories as they managed across their previous 16 visits to Camp Nou in the league (W3 D6 L7).
Barca out for historic 10
Madrid might be viewing Sunday's clash as a must-not-lose if they harbour realistic ambitions of dethroning Barca.
But for Flick's team, the match offers a huge opportunity to put real daylight between themselves and their arch-rivals.

Indeed, this is Madrid's biggest negative points difference to the LaLiga leaders this early in a campaign since 2012-13, when they sat eight points behind Barca after nine matchdays and ultimately finished 15 points adrift in second, also under Mourinho.
And Barca, having won the title as a direct result of a Clasico victory just five months ago, could cause their foes more embarrassment by making history against them this weekend.

They are just the second team to win their first nine games at the start of a LaLiga season, after Madrid did so way back in 1968-69, and they could now become the first side in the competition's history to start a campaign with 10 straight wins.
Barca have always been easy on the eye under Flick, but their attacking returns this season have been truly special, plundering 39 goals in their nine LaLiga games.

Only one team in the competition's history has managed a better goalscoring start, with no side doing so since the Second World War – Sevilla netted 42 times in nine games at the beginning of 1940-41.

Barca were on the wrong side of a six-goal thriller in the Champions League on Tuesday, losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain, but Lamine Yamal still made his mark with a wonderful solo goal, and he has been at the forefront of the Blaugrana's hot start.
Yamal has eight goals in nine LaLiga appearances this campaign, which is the most by any player aged 20 or younger at this stage of a season in the 21st century.
It is easy to forget that Yamal failed to provide a goal involvement in Barca's first two games, with the winger tallying eight goals and six assists in his last six outings in LaLiga.
Since that run began on August 31, Yamal's 14 total goal involvements are the most by any player in Europe's top five leagues, with team-mate Raphinha (11) the only other player in double figures.
Mbappe and Mourinho must provide magic for Madrid

With this game taking place on the eve of the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, a match-up between Yamal and Kylian Mbappe, another of the foremost contenders to be named the world's best player, should grab everyone's attention.
Mbappe has a phenomenal record versus Barcelona, scoring 12 goals in 10 games against them in all competitions throughout his career (four in three outings for PSG, eight in seven for Madrid).
The only players to find the net more often against the Blaugrana this century are former Madrid icons Cristiano Ronaldo (20 goals) and Karim Benzema (16).

Mbappe was on target against RB Leipzig in a 4-1 Champions League victory on Wednesday, having scored a brace against Sevilla last time out in LaLiga – the first was an incredible spin and finish, with the second being a penalty he won himself.

The France captain has won eight penalties and scored 17 in LaLiga, in 74 games. Since his arrival at the start of 2024-25, only Ante Budimir has won (11) or scored more spot-kicks (18) in the competition.

And the France superstar will have an even more significant role to play, with Vinicius Junior still suspended for this game, having been banned for four domestic games following his red card for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba.
It should be said that Vinicius has been far from his electrifying best this season anyway, only scoring once – and supplying three assists – in 11 matches across all competitions.
And given how strong Barca have looked this campaign, it would be little surprise to see Madrid sit deep and attempt to carve out chances for Mbappe on the break, in true Mourinho fashion.
Mourinho ended his first stint in charge of Madrid by going unbeaten throughout his last five matches against Barca in all competitions (W3 D2).

And he could now become just the third Madrid coach to enjoy a six-game unbeaten streak in this fixture, after Miguel Munoz between 1962 and 1965 (seven matches, W7) and Vicente del Bosque between 2001 and 2003 (seven matches, W2 D5).
Excluding the obvious pair of Yamal and Mbappe, Raphinha is surely the other standout attacker to watch in this match.

The Brazilian, who is fit again after sustaining a thigh issue while on international duty, has 17 direct goal involvements in just 10 matches this season, across all competitions (14 goals, three assists).
His team-mate Yamal (10 goals, 10 assists) is the only player from Europe's top five leagues with more combined goals and assists in 2026-27.
Real Madrid – Jude Bellingham
Bellingham memorably scored two goals – one of which was a stoppage-time winner – in his first Clasico back in October 2023, as Madrid triumphed 2-1.
Since then, he has hit the net twice in nine appearances against Madrid's rivals, and both of those goals have proved to be the match-winner.
He popped up with another stoppage-time strike in April 2024 as Los Blancos triumphed 3-2, also scoring the decider in the 43rd minute as Madrid won 2-1 in October 2025.

Who will come out on top, and which superstars will have a decisive impact? Here, we delve into Opta's best insights to provide a data-powered preview. 

What's expected?

Given Barcelona's swashbuckling start to the campaign, it is no surprise to see them favoured by the Opta supercomputer on home soil.

Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the model, Hansi Flick's team were victorious in 56% of scenarios, with Madrid assigned a 24.8% chance of an away win and a 19.2% likelihood of earning a point.

In the supercomputer's 2026-27 season predictions, Barca are currently assigned a 77.1% chance of successfully defending their crown, with Madrid's title hopes down at 15%.

But those probabilities could swing significantly on Sunday, depending on who emerges with the bragging rights. 

Barcelona have won their last two home games against Madrid in LaLiga – a 2-0 triumph in May that clinched the title for 2025-26, and a thrilling 4-3 triumph 12 months earlier.

Only once in the 21st century have Barca achieved three consecutive home victories against Madrid in the competition, doing so under Pep Guardiola between 2008 and 2010.

However, Madrid have won three of their last six away games against the Blaugrana in LaLiga (L3), as many victories as they managed across their previous 16 visits to Camp Nou in the league (W3 D6 L7).

Barca out for historic 10

Madrid might be viewing Sunday's clash as a must-not-lose if they harbour realistic ambitions of dethroning Barca.

But for Flick's team, the match offers a huge opportunity to put real daylight between themselves and their arch-rivals. 

Indeed, this is Madrid's biggest negative points difference to the LaLiga leaders this early in a campaign since 2012-13, when they sat eight points behind Barca after nine matchdays and ultimately finished 15 points adrift in second, also under Mourinho. 

And Barca, having won the title as a direct result of a Clasico victory just five months ago, could cause their foes more embarrassment by making history against them this weekend.

They are just the second team to win their first nine games at the start of a LaLiga season, after Madrid did so way back in 1968-69, and they could now become the first side in the competition's history to start a campaign with 10 straight wins. 

Barca have always been easy on the eye under Flick, but their attacking returns this season have been truly special, plundering 39 goals in their nine LaLiga games. 

Only one team in the competition's history has managed a better goalscoring start, with no side doing so since the Second World War – Sevilla netted 42 times in nine games at the beginning of 1940-41. 

Barca were on the wrong side of a six-goal thriller in the Champions League on Tuesday, losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain, but Lamine Yamal still made his mark with a wonderful solo goal, and he has been at the forefront of the Blaugrana's hot start.

Yamal has eight goals in nine LaLiga appearances this campaign, which is the most by any player aged 20 or younger at this stage of a season in the 21st century.

It is easy to forget that Yamal failed to provide a goal involvement in Barca's first two games, with the winger tallying eight goals and six assists in his last six outings in LaLiga. 

Since that run began on August 31, Yamal's 14 total goal involvements are the most by any player in Europe's top five leagues, with team-mate Raphinha (11) the only other player in double figures.

Mbappe and Mourinho must provide magic for Madrid

With this game taking place on the eve of the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, a match-up between Yamal and Kylian Mbappe, another of the foremost contenders to be named the world's best player, should grab everyone's attention.

Mbappe has a phenomenal record versus Barcelona, scoring 12 goals in 10 games against them in all competitions throughout his career (four in three outings for PSG, eight in seven for Madrid). 

The only players to find the net more often against the Blaugrana this century are former Madrid icons Cristiano Ronaldo (20 goals) and Karim Benzema (16).

Mbappe was on target against RB Leipzig in a 4-1 Champions League victory on Wednesday, having scored a brace against Sevilla last time out in LaLiga – the first was an incredible spin and finish, with the second being a penalty he won himself. 

The France captain has won eight penalties and scored 17 in LaLiga, in 74 games. Since his arrival at the start of 2024-25, only Ante Budimir has won (11) or scored more spot-kicks (18) in the competition.

And the France superstar will have an even more significant role to play, with Vinicius Junior still suspended for this game, having been banned for four domestic games following his red card for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba. 

It should be said that Vinicius has been far from his electrifying best this season anyway, only scoring once – and supplying three assists – in 11 matches across all competitions.

And given how strong Barca have looked this campaign, it would be little surprise to see Madrid sit deep and attempt to carve out chances for Mbappe on the break, in true Mourinho fashion.

Mourinho ended his first stint in charge of Madrid by going unbeaten throughout his last five matches against Barca in all competitions (W3 D2).

And he could now become just the third Madrid coach to enjoy a six-game unbeaten streak in this fixture, after Miguel Munoz between 1962 and 1965 (seven matches, W7) and Vicente del Bosque between 2001 and 2003 (seven matches, W2 D5).

PLAYERS TO WATCH

Barcelona – Raphinha

Excluding the obvious pair of Yamal and Mbappe, Raphinha is surely the other standout attacker to watch in this match.

The Brazilian, who is fit again after sustaining a thigh issue while on international duty, has 17 direct goal involvements in just 10 matches this season, across all competitions (14 goals, three assists).

His team-mate Yamal (10 goals, 10 assists) is the only player from Europe's top five leagues with more combined goals and assists in 2026-27.

Real Madrid – Jude Bellingham

Bellingham memorably scored two goals – one of which was a stoppage-time winner – in his first Clasico back in October 2023, as Madrid triumphed 2-1.

Since then, he has hit the net twice in nine appearances against Madrid's rivals, and both of those goals have proved to be the match-winner.

He popped up with another stoppage-time strike in April 2024 as Los Blancos triumphed 3-2, also scoring the decider in the 43rd minute as Madrid won 2-1 in October 2025.

1wkg668m5srfv1boc5t3m6ndrl.title: Resilience 'runs very, very deep' at Man Utd, says under-pressure Carrick
1wkg668m5srfv1boc5t3m6ndrl.subtitle: Michael Carrick and Manchester United are preparing for a huge clash in the Premier League, with Bournemouth the visitors to Old Trafford.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick insisted resilience "runs very, very deep" into the foundations of Manchester United amid their poor run of form that has put his position under threat.
United's 2026-27 campaign reached a new low on Wednesday, going down 4-1 to Champions League debutants Como, leaving them without a win in their last seven matches.
It is the first time they have gone this long without a victory since between November and December 2015, when they went on a run of eight matches without success.
That stretch could be equalled this Sunday when they welcome Bournemouth to Old Trafford, and another poor result here could spell an end to Carrick's time at the club.

Carrick's side are 13th in the Premier League and just one point above Bournemouth, with reports linking Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte to the club, though the latter has since said he is not in "advanced negotiations" with any club in response to those rumours.
But ahead of a crucial clash for both United and Carrick, the Red Devils boss believes the club can find their way back after a dismal start to their season.
"The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years," Carrick told reporters.
"I totally understand, and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, working hard and being really proud to live up to those values.
"There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time.
"Whether that's bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep."
However, Carrick and United come up against a Bournemouth side riding high after their Europa League win against AC Milan, who are now under Ruben Amorim's guidance.
Bournemouth became the first English side to win each of their first three games in major European competition since Sunderland back in October 1973 with a 3-0 triumph.
Their form in Europe has been completely different to the one they have shown in the Premier League, with Bournemouth taking just six points from their first seven matches.
But Rose is hoping Bournemouth's "brilliant" performance against Milan can be used as a solid foundation to build on ahead of making the trip to Old Trafford.
"I feel really good. I'm proud of the club, happy for the fans and proud of the lads. It was a great evening, a great result and a brilliant performance in every aspect," Rose said.
"We were really sharp in everything, played our game, and it's a deserved win.

"The way we got into the game, the effort, the attitude, the way we won balls and put pressure on Milan was great. We created chances, scored an early goal and kept the pressure high. This was Bournemouth, and this is what we wanted to show."
Manchester United – Bryan Mbeumo
Mbeumo has scored six goals in his last nine Premier League appearances for Man Utd, having gone 11 without a goal beforehand.

He's scored in his last two, both 1-1 draws, with Bruno Fernandes in April 2024 the only Red Devils player to score in three in a row without winning any, a sequence which ended with two goals in a 2-2 draw with Bournemouth.
Bournemouth – Evanilson
Evanilson has been involved in six Premier League goals for Bournemouth this season (two goals, four assists), making up 67% of the Cherries' overall total (6/9).
This is the highest share of goals scored or assisted by one player for a club so far this season in the division.
MATCH PREDICTION: MANCHESTER UNITED WIN

Despite being considered the underdogs here, Bournemouth are unbeaten in their last three Premier League visits to Old Trafford (W2 D1), scoring at least three goals in every match, the only team to ever achieve that in three visits in a row to the Red Devils in the league.
The last team to score 3+ goals in four away Premier League games in a row against an opponent were Manchester City at Newcastle United from 2020-21 to 2023-24.
Bournemouth also registered their first Premier League win of the season last time out against Sunderland. The Cherries are looking for consecutive league wins for the first time since May.
Man Utd won nine of their first 12 Premier League matches against Bournemouth (D1 L2), but they are winless in six against the Cherries since then (D4 L2).

Carrick's side have seven points in seven Premier League games this season (W1 D4 L2), their worst start to a league season since 1989-90 (also seven in seven). It's only the second time in the last 54 seasons they’ve had one win at this stage, along with 1986-87.
The Red Devils have drawn their last three Premier League games. They last had a longer string of stalemates in September and October 1992, when they drew five in a row.
Manchester United – 46.2%

1wldigej39ke01e82a1wjkmmc5.title: Chelsea goalkeeper Martinez hopes for quick return after sustaining fractured jaw
1wldigej39ke01e82a1wjkmmc5.subtitle: Having suffered a nasty jaw injury against Everton, Emiliano Martinez has undergone surgery and will be sidelined for several games.
paragraphs: Emiliano Martinez hopes to return to action in "a few weeks" after fracturing his jaw during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton.
Saturday's game at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, which the Blues won 2-0 following Pedro Neto's brace, was paused for eight minutes in the second half for Martinez to receive medical treatment.
Following a nasty clash of heads with Everton centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite, Martinez was taken straight to hospital.

Mike Penders took Martinez's place from the bench, and after Chelsea confirmed that their first-choice goalkeeper had undergone successful surgery on a fractured jaw, the 21-year-old Belgian is likely to enjoy a run in the team.
Chelsea face Tottenham, Manchester United and Sunderland in the Premier League prior to the next international break, in addition to an EFL Cup tie away at Liverpool.
Alongside an image of himself in a hospital bed, Martinez wrote on Instagram: "Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well.
"The most important thing is that we won and kept a clean sheet. In a few weeks we'll be back."
Since joining Chelsea from Aston Villa this summer, Martinez has conceded 11 goals in six appearances in all competitions, and he is yet to see out a single clean sheet.

1wn54tsih5751bpu2n7ej54il.title: Spain 3-1 Czechia: World champions still perfect as Krejci red card halts fightback
1wn54tsih5751bpu2n7ej54il.subtitle: Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Merino scored for Spain as they defeated 10-man Czechia 3-1 in the Nations League on Saturday.
paragraphs: Spain maintained their 100% record in the 2026-27 Nations League with a hard-earned 3-1 victory over Czechia, who had captain Ladislav Krejci sent off late on.

Following England's 7-0 humilation of Croatia elsewhere in Group A3, the world champions did not have things anywhere near as easy in Oviedo, after Luis de la Fuente made nine changes to his starting lineup.

After first-half goals from Lamine Yamal and Rodri, Jiri Slama's strike got the visitors – managed by Spaniard Santi Denia – back into the contest, only for Krejci's 85th-minute dismissal and a poacher's finish from Mikel Merino to kill their hopes of a fightback.

Yamal only needed six minutes to have an impact, as he exchanged passes with Dani Olmo, got the ball out of his feet near the right corner of the area, then curled a sumptuous effort past Antonin Kinsky.
Despite Spain dominating possession, they did not create another major chance until just beyond the half-hour mark, when Kinsky showed great reactions to deny Olmo.

But the Tottenham goalkeeper was beaten again in the 35th minute, with Rodri feeding his fellow Barcelona midfielder Olmo, continuing his run into the area, then finishing calmly when the ball deflected into his path.

Alex Baena also worked Kinsky late in the first half, but De la Fuente's withdrawal of Yamal at the interval removed some of Spain's attacking impetus, and Czechia got back into the game when Slama was slipped in by Adam Hlozek and finished unerringly across David Raya.

Czechia thought they had an unlikely equaliser in the 79th minute, as Raya spilled Krejci's looping header and Ryan Naderi prodded over the line, but Lukas Cerv was penalised for holding Robin Le Normand when the initial cross came into the area.

Krejci was booked for dissent following that incident, having screamed in the face of referee Vassilios Fotias, and that moment proved costly as the Wolves defender then dragged Roberto Fernandez back to stop a counter-attack and was shown a second yellow card.

Victor Munoz went agonisingly close to making it 3-1, but Spain's clinching goal did arrive in the 89th minute, with the Liverpool winger involved. He kept the attack alive following Stepan Chaloupek's terrible tackle on Fernandez, and when Kinsky parried his shot, Merino was waiting to fire into the empty net.
Czechs lose their cool as Barcelona stars dominate

Despite the one-sided look of the stat sheet, with Spain accumulating 1.99 expected goals (xG) to Czechia's 0.49, outshooting their visitors by 18 to five and having a 69% possession share, this game was far from straightforward for the World Cup holders.
Czechia looked to have La Roja on the ropes when Slama's goal halved the deficit, but Krejci's loss of composure ultimately cost them.
Ultimately, it was Spain's Barcelona stars that did the damage as they extended their record unbeaten run to 41 games and put themselves on the brink of the quarter-finals.

Yamal now has 12 goals in his last nine games for club and country (four for Spain in the Nations League, eight for Barcelona in all competitions), with a 3-1 LaLiga win over Sevilla being the only game in which he has failed to find the net in that period.

Spain's second goal was the result of a lovely combination between Rodri and Olmo, who were the only players remaining from their starting lineup the last time they faced Czechia, also in the Nations League in June 2022.

1wqmn38ub4o7i15hq6yesgc9cr.title: De Zerbi: Tottenham's Stamford Bridge woes to be used as motivation
1wqmn38ub4o7i15hq6yesgc9cr.subtitle: Tottenham have not won at Stamford Bridge since 2017-18, but Roberto De Zerbi is hoping to flip the script against Chelsea on Saturday.
paragraphs: Roberto De Zerbi revealed he intends to use Tottenham's poor record against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge as motivation ahead of this weekend's Premier League clash.
Spurs earned their first league win of the campaign on Monday by beating Coventry City 3-1, with James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies all on target for the hosts.
But since the start of last season, only twice have they won consecutive league matches (August 2025 and May 2026), with a trip to a venue they have struggled at up next.

Spurs have won just one of their last 36 league visits to Stamford Bridge (D11 L24), a 3-1 victory in 2017-18 under Mauricio Pochettino. They have only picked up two points in eight visits since then (D2 L6).
In addition, they have lost each of their last six London derbies in the Premier League. In their entire league history, they have never lost seven such games in a row.
Chelsea have also won each of their last six top-flight matches against Spurs, their joint-longest-ever winning league run against their London rivals (also six between January 2000 and March 2002).
De Zerbi, however, believes his team have enough qualities to end their dismal run at Stamford Bridge, though he acknowledged Xabi Alonso's Chelsea pose a difficult test.
"I think it's not just this negative record; there are many, many negative records, but for me, it's one more motivation for the players," De Zerbi told reporters.
"I want this negative record to give us more motivation and more mentality, more energy to win a game and play well, because we have enough qualities to win this game.
"It's against a very good team, a very good coach, and they have a clear style of play with great players.
"But also, the Tottenham players are very good; the level of the players is high. We have to show together as a team as well as individuals."
The Chelsea versus Spurs rivalry has seen many heated clashes over the years, none more so than the "Battle of the Bridge" back in 2017, which ended with a 2-2 draw.
Gary Cahill and Eden Hazard cancelled out goals from Harry Kane and Son Heung-min to hand Leicester City the Premier League title, but that was from the full story.

Several flashpoints popped up throughout the contest, most notably Danny Rose's late challenge on Willian, which saw Mousa Dembele receive a six-match suspension for violent conduct following an altercation with Diego Costa.

And when asked about managing discipline at Stamford Bridge after Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off against Manchester United for a headbutt, De Zerbi responded: "The balance is always difficult to fix – a balance between energy, spirit, mentality.
"If you have confidence in the players, you leave the players to decide their behaviour, to decide the reaction.
"For sure, I prefer one 'too strong' reaction to one player without blood, without reaction."

1wrp7lzqo8je81mup9pt0psejb.title: Netherlands 1-1 Germany: Gakpo denies former Liverpool boss Klopp in stoppage time
1wrp7lzqo8je81mup9pt0psejb.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp was just a minute away from a debut win in charge of Germany, only to be denied by his former Liverpool attacker Cody Gakpo.
paragraphs: A stoppage-time equaliser from Cody Gakpo denied his former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp a winning start with Germany, as the Netherlands salvaged a 1-1 draw in the Nations League.

It looked like Felix Nmecha's 32nd-minute strike would settle an entertaining and at times fractious affair between two old rivals under new coaches, with Barcelona great Xavi also making his Netherlands bow.
But in the second of three minutes of second-half stoppage time, Gakpo met a cross from debutant Ruben van Bommel brilliantly on the stretch, ensuring the points were shared in Group A2.

The first moment of drama came after 12 minutes, as Virgil van Dijk – another of Klopp's former Liverpool stalwarts – glanced Tijjani Reijnders' inswinging corner beyond Marc-Andre ter Stegen. But a VAR review led to the goal being chalked off, due to Brian Brobbey backing into the Germany goalkeeper.

Germany then saw Kai Havertz limp off following a high challenge from Quinten Timber, the twin brother of his Arsenal team-mate Jurrien, though substitute Younes Ebnoutalib almost made an immediate impact as Bart Verbruggen blocked his near-post drive.

And another injury to a Premier League forward played a role in the opening goal. As the Netherlands appealed for a foul on the stricken Brobbey, Germany looked set to kick the ball out, but Nadiem Amiri and Joshua Kimmich instead kept the attack going, and Nmecha swept home after Nathaniel Brown's centre flicked into his path.
A glaring miss from Karim Adeyemi prevented Germany from going 2-0 up late in the first half, but it was one-way traffic from then on with the Oranje laying siege to Ter Stegen's goal.

He thwarted Denzel Dumfries from close range with his right boot, then Mexx Meerdink – another Netherlands debutant – put the ball in the net but saw a foul given against Van Dijk. The young AZ forward also turned Dumfries' cross wide on the slide as Germany closed in on a big three points, but they would be denied with time almost up.

Gakpo showed tremendous athleticism to divert Van Bommel's cross past Ter Stegen while in mid-air, though the Dutch forward was arguably fortunate to avoid a very late red card after the restart, when he trod on Yannik Engelhardt.
Gakpo denies Klopp as the Netherlands impress
Few international coaching debuts in recent years have been as eagerly anticipated as this one.

Indeed, Klopp oversaw 674 games as a manager in the Bundesliga and the Premier League across spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, the most matches in Europe's top five leagues that any Germany coach had accumulated before taking charge.

But this game showed the size of the task awaiting him, as Germany were penned back throughout the second half by an impressive Netherlands side. The Oranje racked up 3.12 expected goals (xG) and 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 xG from 10 attempts.
And in the end, it was Gakpo – who played 79 games under him for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – that made Klopp wait for his first victory in charge of his country.

There was at least a notable landmark for Klopp's captain Kimmich, who was at the centre of the controversy leading up to Nmecha's goal, on his 115th cap. He has now surpassed Toni Kroos (114) to sit seventh outright in Germany's all-time charts.

Both teams are back in action on Sunday, with Germany hosting Greece and the Netherlands visiting Serbia, but with Havertz and Brobbey both hobbling off, both came out of a bruising encounter with injury concerns.

1wvcavi56k9c01qejx9p1bpohz.title: Jaissle warns Newcastle that Palace 'want a reaction' at Selhurst Park
1wvcavi56k9c01qejx9p1bpohz.subtitle: Newcastle United and Crystal Palace are both desperate for wins in the Premier League, and the two teams meet at Selhurst Park on Sunday.
paragraphs: After a difficult week on and off the pitch, Newcastle United boss Matthias Jaissle fully expects a reaction from Crystal Palace when his team visit Selhurst Park on Sunday.
Palace are 14th in the Premier League and just one point behind Newcastle, but have endured a difficult few matches, which started with a 5-0 thrashing by rivals Brighton.
The Eagles then squandered a lead in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday, despite the Turkish giants being reduced to 10 men in the 77th minute.
It's a run of results that have seen Pierre Sage's job put at risk, with reports suggesting that the Frenchman potentially has just two more games to prove he is worthy of staying.
"There are always times when you would and wouldn't like to play against an opposition. They had a heavy defeat and then drew. They will want a reaction," Jaissle said.
"We can only focus on ourselves, what we can control. We are fully focused on Crystal Palace, to deliver the match plan."
Newcastle are another team out for a return to winning ways after back-to-back defeats to Coventry City and Aston Villa, though they have been given a boost ahead of kick-off.
Jaissle revealed that Anthony Elanga could return for Newcastle this weekend, while Jacob Ramsey is also in line to be integrated back into the first-team picture soon.
"Anthony has trained this week and worked really hard. He won't be able to play 90 minutes, but he is hopefully ready, at least, to be able to join the squad," Jaissle added.
"I am happy Jacob Ramsey is back on the pitch. We need to take it step-by-step with him, manage his load management, we don't want to take too many risks.
"I am pleased that slowly we are getting the players back and the next question is the physical level."
Palace are another side who welcomed back a long-term absentee last week, with Jean-Philippe Mateta scoring his first goal since returning against Besiktas.
Since his debut for the Eagles in February 2021, Mateta has scored 63 goals in all competitions for the club, 26 more than any other player (Eberechi Eze next on 37).
The Frenchman could start this Sunday after coming off the bench against Brighton last time out, though Mateta hopes if he scores again, he is on the right side of the result.
"I always feel good [when I score], but it's better when we win in the end," Mateta said.
"I think we did everything to win the game, and in the end, when you let them have chances, they are a very good team, they scored.
"But I think we deserved better, we played hard, and we showed a good face, and it's a draw, we take that point.
"The aggression was back, the team was so strong, and like I said, we let them have two chances and they scored."
Crystal Palace – Chris Richards
Richards could make his 100th Premier League appearance in this match.
He would be the 14th American (USA) player to reach this milestone, and, at 26 years and 211 days on the day of the game, the second-youngest, after Jonathan Spector in 2010 (23y 359d).
Newcastle – Yoane Wissa
Despite making a promising start to the season, Wissa has scored just one goal from 18 shots in the Premier League this season.
Of all players to have found the net at least once, only two have a lower shot conversion rate than Wissa (5.6%).
MATCH PREDICTION: CRYSTAL PALACE WIN

Having won 2-1 in April in their most recent Premier League clash, Palace are looking for consecutive league wins over Newcastle for the first time since a run of three between August 1971 and September 1972.

And after their 3-1 win over Nottingham Forest, Palace are also searching for back-to-back Premier League victories at Selhurst Park for the first time since April 2025 (three in a row), with this their 26th home league game since (W6 D11 L8).

But Palace have conceded at least twice in 11 of their last 13 Premier League games, with the exceptions being a 0-0 draw with Leeds United and a 3-1 win over Forest. The previous 11 times they’ve conceded at least twice came over a period of 36 matches.
Newcastle, meanwhile, have won one of their last 11 away league matches against Palace (D6 L4), winning 2-0 in 2020-21 under Steve Bruce.
They have lost 4-1 at Leeds and 4-1 at Coventry City in their last two away league games. They last conceded 4+ goals in three consecutive games on the road in September 1929 (four in a row).
And there could be little goalmouth action. Only Palace (-5.4) and Coventry (-4.2) have a lower expected goal difference than Newcastle (-3.95) in the top flight this season (8.15 xG, 12.1 xGA).
Crystal Palace – 40.6%

1wyyx7kypvzng1kqcxsqdpbbbk.title: Sweden 3-1 Poland: Gyokeres scores again for Potter's men
1wyyx7kypvzng1kqcxsqdpbbbk.subtitle: Sweden made it two wins from two as they continue their bid for promotion to League A, with Viktor Gyokeres on the scoresheet once more.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres was on target for Sweden once again as Graham Potter's side stayed perfect in the Nations League with a 3-1 win over Poland.
Sebastian Szymanski had cancelled out Benjamin Nygren's early opener, but Yasin Ayari and Gyokeres both struck after the break to make it two wins from two in Group B4.
Piotr Zielinski and Patrik Walemark saw a shot saved at either end within the opening four minutes before Nygren nodded in Victor Lindelof's flick-on from a recycled corner eight minutes in.

Walemark was denied by a smart Marcin Bulka save at the near post shortly after, but Poland kept the pressure on and, after Matty Cash saw a driven shot pushed away by Viktor Johansson, they found an equaliser.

Nicola Zalewski shook off his defender on the left of the area and fizzed a dangerous cross into the six-yard box, with Szymanski sprinting forward to tap in from close range with two minutes of the first half remaining.
Ayari had already seen a curler touched behind in the second half before he got his 63rd-minute goal, this time bending his shot into the bottom-right corner after ghosting past Szymanski.
Gyokeres then made sure of the three points nine minutes later, volleying in unmarked at the far post after Walemark's perfectly weighted right-sided cross.
Gyokeres finds his groove with Sweden

It is no secret that Gyokeres has had a difficult start to the season, with the Arsenal striker restricted to a few appearances so far for the Gunners, though that might change following Kai Havertz's injury while away with Germany.
But with Sweden, who were without the injured Alexander Isak, he has already scored two goals in two games, making him their top scorer at the halfway stage of the international break.

Overall, he has now contributed to goals in his last five Nations League games (eight goals, two assists), but he was once again on the outskirts for large periods, having just two shots in total. His five touches in the opposition box were the second-highest total in the team, though.

Poland enjoyed a strong first half, with only one goal to show for it despite their 13 shots – which were more than Sweden managed throughout the entire 90 minutes (12) – but even after throwing on Robert Lewandowski in the closing stages, they could not mount a fightback.

1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.title: Martinez: Argentina must forget World Cup heartache and celebrate Messi
1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.subtitle: Lionel Messi will make his farewell appearance for Argentina during the international break, before he steps away from the Albiceleste.
paragraphs: Lisandro Martinez says Argentina's players are determined to put their World Cup final heartache behind them and savour Lionel Messi's international send-off next month.

The Albiceleste could have become the first back-to-back winners of FIFA's showpiece tournament since Brazil in 1958 and 1962, after Messi inspired them to a final appearance in North America this summer.
However, Enzo Fernandez's red card proved costly as Spain beat them 1-0 in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the all-important goal.

Argentina have now been World Cup runners-up four times (also in 1930, 1990 and 2014), the joint-most of any nation alongside West Germany/Germany, and they became the first team to not attempt a single shot in regulation time of a World Cup final.
But Manchester United defender Martinez says the time has come for Lionel Scaloni's side to put that defeat behind them, as they prepare to say goodbye to a legend.
Having announced his decision to retire from international football following the World Cup, Messi will make a farewell appearance at a friendly against Benin on October 5.

Bolivia and Burkina Faso will be Argentina's opponents before that match, which will see members of the 2022 World Cup-winning squad come together for a celebration of Messi's career at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.
"There's a lot of pain, preferably we don't remember it, but we must also highlight the tremendous effort we made throughout the tournament," Martinez told ESPN Argentina.
"Without a doubt, we had a great World Cup, but it hurts us all to have lost the final.
"Now we are here, back in our country, and we are going to enjoy ourselves."

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina, leading his country's all-time charts in both categories, with his last strike coming in their dramatic World Cup round-of-16 victory over Egypt this summer.
No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight), while only Kylian Mbappe (22 goals) has netted more often, though Messi was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals this year.

1x6wy3i0mkftp1abn66df9h20h.title: 'Liverpool will be happy' – Wirtz 'brimming with joy', says Klopp
1x6wy3i0mkftp1abn66df9h20h.subtitle: Florian Wirtz scored in Germany's 2-0 win over Serbia, and Jurgen Klopp believes those at his old club Liverpool will be delighted.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp reckons those involved at his former club, Liverpool, will be thrilled with Florian Wirtz's performances for Germany.
Wirtz scored in Germany's 2-0 win over Serbia in the Nations League on Thursday.
The playmaker also leads the way within Germany's squad for chances created (six) over this international break.
Wirtz has had a tough time of it at Liverpool since his mega-money switch from Bayer Leverkusen, and his performances this season have seen him come in for criticism.

However, the 23-year-old is the only player to rank in the top 10 in the Premier League this season for each of: High-intensity pressures in the opponent's half (181, joint-seventh), runs ahead of the ball (34, first) and defensive line-breaking passes (16, eighth).
And Klopp feels Wirtz hit his stride against Serbia.
"The way we want to play suits Flo Wirtz," Klopp said.
"I think everyone [at] Liverpool is very happy today. The boy is brimming with the joy of playing and has worked incredibly hard."
Germany were dominant, with Serbia managing just one shot, worth only 0.01 expected goals.
Klopp's team, meanwhile, accumulated chances worth 3.81 xG and had 32 shots.
Germany recorded 20 high turnovers, their most ever in a Nations League game and also more than in any match under Julian Nagelsmann.
They have allowed an average of just 8.7 opponent passes across their first three Nations League matches before a defensive action occurred. It is the lowest PPDA value of all teams in League A.
Asked what he enjoyed about the performance, Klopp said: "Everything! The opening stages, the middle part, the ending.
"The positioning in the box was incredible. To have that courage and know that we can allow ourselves to be cheeky and take risks if we win the ball back together.
"Everyone was there in our pressing moments. The last line defended really well by pushing up.

"Without the ball, it was outstanding, and with the ball, we played wonderful football. That has to be our baseline. Whether we can always manage that remains to be seen. This game will go into my archive. The next step in our development. We are learning. Learning under pressure."

1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.subtitle: Having seen their unbeaten Serie A start halted by Sassuolo on matchday four, Juventus bounced back with an impressive win over Atalanta.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti admitted Juventus' defeat to Sassuolo last week had created doubt in the Bianconeri's ranks, and he was delighted to see them banish that feeling by beating Atalanta.
Juve suffered their first defeat of the Serie A campaign on matchday four, conceding a stoppage-time winner to Vasilije Adzic in a 3-2 loss to Sassuolo.
However, they bounced back in style on Sunday with a 2-0 success against Atalanta and their former head coach Maurizio Sarri, with Francisco Conceicao and Bremer on target.

paragraphs: The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season, with the table beginning to take shape.
Amid all the off-pitch noise, Manchester City continue to set the pace after extending their 100% start to the season with a resounding 3-0 win over 10-man Liverpool last weekend.
Arsenal remain three points behind them after ending Leeds United's unbeaten start on MD6, leaving Brentford and Everton as the only other teams yet to taste defeat.

At the other end of the table, Fulham, Tottenham – who came from behind with 10 men to earn a draw with struggling Manchester United – and Bournemouth are the only teams without a win, while Coventry City catapulted themselves out of the relegation zone with a huge 4-1 victory over Newcastle United.
Matchday seven sees fixtures take place on Saturday, Sunday and Monday across a bumper weekend.
Ahead of what should be another intriguing group of Premier League fixtures, let's check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.
The weekend's action starts at Hill Dickinson Stadium as Everton look to preserve their unbeaten start against Chelsea.

Only in 2006-07 have Everton (W2 D4) had a longer unbeaten run from the start of a campaign in the competition (first seven games), and David Moyes will be keen to match that against the Premier League's biggest entertainers.
Our predictive model makes them slight favourites to pick up a third home win of the campaign, edging 42.9% of our pre-match simulations to Chelsea's 30.4%.
Chelsea have won one of their last nine away top-flight games against Everton (D2 L6), a 1-0 win in August 2022. They've failed to score in seven of those games, including the last three.

But finding the net has not been Chelsea's problem this term, as they are the third-highest scorers (13), adding to that tally with a huge 5-1 win over Bournemouth last time out. Joao Pedro has led that charge, having been involved in more goals than any other player in the Premier League this season (five goals, three assists).
BRENTFORD V LIVERPOOL

Having suffered a disappointing 3-0 loss at home to Man City last weekend, Liverpool bounced back in the Champions League with a 6-3 victory over LASK, aided by Bradley Barcola's first three goals for the club, and the first hat-trick of his senior career for club or country (in his 238th game).
The Frenchman will hope to continue that form against Brentford, although the unbeaten Bees are actually favourites with Opta's predictive model, boasting a 37.9% win likelihood to Liverpool's 35.7%.
Reds boss Andoni Iraola only earned two points from six matches against Brentford while in charge of Bournemouth (D2 L4), his lowest points-per-game figure versus any club in the Premier League.

Iraola's 23-game unbeaten run in league play was halted last weekend, though Liverpool have won their last two on the road – they last had a longer away winning run at the start of their title-winning 2024-25 season (four).

Overall, the Bees are unbeaten in eight Premier League games, which is the longest ongoing run of any side (W2 D6).

This is the 100th meeting between Fulham and Hull in all competitions – the Cottagers have won their last four against the Tigers (three in the Championship, one in the FA Cup), the best winning run by either side in this fixture, and they have a 45.4% chance of getting another on Saturday.
However, in the top flight, Fulham have won just one of their six Premier League matches against Hull (D1 L4), a 2-0 home triumph in October 2009 under Roy Hodgson.

Maresca could become the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a club, while only Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight) have ever won their first seven matches to start a campaign – both went on to win the title.

Ipswich are coming off the back of a huge win over Fulham, though, and all three of their Premier League victories this term have come via 90th-minute goals – as many 90th-minute winners as they scored in their first six campaigns in the competition combined.

Saturday's late kick-off pits Newcastle United (41.5%) against Aston Villa (31.8%) at St James' Park, where the Magpies have gone 12 Premier League games without a clean sheet.

They last endured a longer run without a shutout on home soil between December 1998 and August 1999 under Ruud Gullit (13 matches), and their defensive fragility was also on show at Coventry City last time out, as they were thrashed 4-1.
Newcastle have already conceded 13 Premier League goals this season, their third-most after six matches of a campaign, after 1999-00 (18) and 2021-22 (14).

Marco's Rose wait for a first league win with Bournemouth (50%) is predicted to come to an end this weekend when they host struggling Sunderland (24.8%).

Brighton were the latest side to inflict defeat on Sunderland, and they are looking to stretch their three-game winning streak to four against rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Man Utd's tally of six points is their worst return after six league games since 1986-87 under Ron Atkinson (four), and with a win likelihood of just 31.6%, the supercomputer makes them underdogs. Leeds have a 41.7% chance of victory and a 26.7% probability of taking a point.

Leeds provided Arsenal with a real scare at the Emirates Stadium last time out, holding a 1-0 lead with more than an hour gone. After fighting back to win that match 2-1, then beating Lille 3-0 in the Champions League, Mikel Arteta's champions visit Nottingham Forest.
At 58.3%, the Gunners boast the highest win probability of any away team on MD7, with Forest only assigned a 20.4% chance of springing a surprise.
Forest laid siege to Crystal Palace's goal for long periods last Sunday without reward, ultimately losing 3-1.

Oliver Glasner has only overseen five wins in 29 games (D9 L15) since a 2-1 win at Fulham put his Crystal Palace side fourth in the league on 7 December last year. Since the start of this 29-game sequence (MD16 last season), Glasner's 17% win percentage is the second-lowest of any manager with 20+ Premier League games, ahead only of Rob Edwards (13%).

Arsenal have gone 1-0 down in three of their last four Premier League matches, as many as in their previous 25 games combined. They have recovered to win two of those, however, with no side winning more points from losing positions this season than their six.

There is also a Monday matchup to look forward to, with Coventry City hoping to replicate their heroics from last Monday against winless Tottenham.

After storming to a 4-1 victory over Newcastle United on MD6, Coventry have won their last two Premier League matches, last enjoying a longer top-flight run in January and February 1998, when they won five in a row under Gordon Strachan.

Coventry could now become just the fourth team in English top-flight history to open a campaign by losing four consecutive games before winning their next three, after Derby County in 1899-00, Arsenal in 1923-24 and Aston Villa in 1997-98.

1x9zh2pp9s2l516nqef5vdzot0.title: Slegers concedes Arsenal are not in WSL title conversation
1x9zh2pp9s2l516nqef5vdzot0.subtitle: Arsenal are winless in their last four Women's Super League games, with a loss to Manchester City leaving them off the title pace.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers insists Arsenal are not in the conversation for the Women's Super League title race after a damaging 4-2 defeat to Manchester City.
Arsenal have made a stuttering start to the campaign, having been tipped as one of the favourites to challenge City for top spot before the season began.
Sunday's loss to City, who have a 100% record so far in the WSL in 2026-27, leaves Arsenal 10th in the table with just five points (W1 D2 L2), 10 behind the reigning champions.
The Gunners had twice led at the Etihad, through Lisa Baum and Alessia Russo, but Lauren Hemp, Kerstin Casparij and Khadija Shaw ensured the hosts snatched all three points.
One of Arsenal's biggest problems across all competitions has been their lack of goals, with only bottom club Charlton Athletic (two) netting fewer times than their four in the WSL.

Against City, Slegers' side had 16 shots, with their nine attempts on target matching the hosts' overall tally, and they won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.6 to 1.0, but they could not hold out for the win.
It comes after a disappointing outing in the Women's Champions League in midweek, too, when Arsenal threw away a 2-0 lead to draw with Paris FC last Wednesday.
And Slegers, who is under pressure after Arsenal's worst start to a WSL season since 2014, is determined to figure out what has gone wrong during the international break.
"It is a tough result," she told Sky Sports. "First half goes back and forth.

"Two teams that have momentum and create. Second half we start well, score a good goal. A lot changes when they make their three changes; they bring an energy, and one of the changes [Casprij] makes the goal.

"After that, it's more difficult. But it's quite an even game, two really good teams going against each other, but we didn't get the margins in the critical moments on our side. We can't concede four goals. We're not happy with that.
"After their changes, they became dominant.
"It's been a lot of games where we feel like we have it and then we don't. That's really pressing, demanding mentally.
"It's good the players go away, go to their national teams, get some new energy, change of environment, and they'll come back, and then we have the next game to prep for.
"There's a lot to review. How we've been doing things, from all aspects. Training programme, bigger things in the background. We're going to do everything we can to see where we can be better.
"At the moment we're not in the [title] conversation, no."
Arsenal will be looking to end their four-match windless streak in the WSL against Birmingham City when they return to domestic action on October 17.

Sunday's loss to City, who have a 100% record so far in the WSL in 2026-27, leaves Arsenal 10th in the table with just five points (W1 D2 L2), 10 behind the reigning champions.

The Gunners had twice led at the Etihad, through Lisa Baum and Alessia Russo, but Lauren Hemp, Kerstin Casparij and Khadija Shaw ensured the hosts snatched all three points.

One of Arsenal's biggest problems across all competitions has been their lack of goals, with only bottom club Charlton Athletic (two) netting fewer times than their four in the WSL.

Against City, Slegers' side had 16 shots, with their nine attempts on target matching the hosts' overall tally, and they won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.6 to 1.0, but they could not hold out for the win.

It comes after a disappointing outing in the Women's Champions League in midweek, too, when Arsenal threw away a 2-0 lead to draw with Paris FC last Wednesday.

And Slegers, who is under pressure after Arsenal's worst start to a WSL season since 2014, is determined to figure out what has gone wrong during the international break.

"It is a tough result," she told Sky Sports. "First half goes back and forth.

"Two teams that have momentum and create. Second half we start well, score a good goal. A lot changes when they make their three changes; they bring an energy, and one of the changes [Casprij] makes the goal.

"After that, it's more difficult. But it's quite an even game, two really good teams going against each other, but we didn't get the margins in the critical moments on our side. We can't concede four goals. We're not happy with that.

"After their changes, they became dominant.

"It's been a lot of games where we feel like we have it and then we don't. That's really pressing, demanding mentally.

"It's good the players go away, go to their national teams, get some new energy, change of environment, and they'll come back, and then we have the next game to prep for.

"There's a lot to review. How we've been doing things, from all aspects. Training programme, bigger things in the background. We're going to do everything we can to see where we can be better.

"At the moment we're not in the [title] conversation, no."

Arsenal will be looking to end their four-match windless streak in the WSL against Birmingham City when they return to domestic action on October 17.

1xc50pp6fhrz314hm9k0qome7w.title: Juventus 2-2 Rennes: Lucumi denied late Europa League winner by VAR
1xc50pp6fhrz314hm9k0qome7w.subtitle: Zeki Celik and Nick Woltemade were on target for Juventus against Rennes in the Europa League, but they had to settle for a 2-2 draw.
paragraphs: Juventus' 100% start in the Europa League came to a halt as they drew 2-2 with Rennes, with Jhon Lucumi seeing a potential late winner disallowed for offside.

Having beaten NEC 5-0 and Celta Vigo 2-1 to sit top of the league-phase standings going into matchday three, the Bianconeri had to settle for a share of the spoils on Thursday, in a game that saw Boulaye Dia and Nick Woltemade both score penalties awarded for handball.

Luciano Spalletti's team made the ideal start, striking in the fifth minute. Zeki Celik made a good third-man run and, after Woltemade linked up with Weston McKennie, the Turkiye international latched onto the German's throughball to slot into the bottom-left corner.
However, Rennes were only behind for 10 minutes as Bryan Reynolds headed Aboubakar Nagida's cross back across goal towards Mousa Al Tamari, whose clever flick beat Guglielmo Vicario.

Brice Samba made a big save to thwart Federico Gatti, but it was Rennes who inched ahead late in the first half as Douglas Luiz was penalised for blocking Nagida's rocket of a shot with his hand, allowing Dia to slot the resulting spot-kick home.

Juventus were on the right end of a similar decision made by referee Morten Krogh in the 66th minute, though, as Reynolds was deemed to have handled a back-post knock-down by Nico Gonzalez. Woltemade made no mistake from 12 yards, as he sent Samba the wrong way.
Woltemade missed a decent chance to put Juventus in front shortly afterwards, as his header deflected wide off Charlie Cresswell, but it was Lucumi who came closest to winning it for the hosts.

Amid a scramble in the area, the Colombian saw his left-footed shot on the swivel hit Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal and wrong-foot Samba, but following a VAR review, the substitute was deemed to have come back from an offside position.
Woltemade's European run continues, but Juve held
Juventus came into Thursday's game having scored 12 goals in their last four European home matches, winning each of those contests, but they found things much tougher against a stubborn Rennes side.
Juve ended the game slightly behind on the shot count but ahead on expected goals, generating 14 attempts and 2.21 xG, compared to Rennes' 16 shots and 1.71 xG.
They were just unable to find a winner after fighting back to make it 2-2, though Spalletti will be delighted with the form Newcastle United loanee Woltemade has shown in Europe.

Having also found the net against NEC and Celta Vigo, Woltemade has scored in all three of his Europa League appearances for Juventus. He is just the third Bianconeri player to net on his first three outings for the club in major European competitions, after Darko Kovacevic in 1999 and Roberto Baggio in 1990.
The next task will be for the German to show the same form in Serie A, having failed to net in five league appearances, albeit all of those outings have come from the bench.
