1xcl7kve2hnpz1adp8wxyz1ro5.title: Philadelphia 'set the standard' in sixth straight win, says hat-trick hero Iloski
1xcl7kve2hnpz1adp8wxyz1ro5.subtitle: The MLS history books had some new names entering after Saturday's results, with Milan Iloski helping Philadelphia Union to another big win.
paragraphs: Hat-trick hero Milan Iloski was thrilled that the Philadelphia Union "set the standard" in their 4-2 victory over Orlando City SC in MLS on Saturday.

Philadelphia were missing some of their young United States stars, including Cavan Sullivan, but Iloski stepped up with a brilliant hat-trick in 51 minutes, with Indiana Vassilev also getting on the scoresheet.
The 27-year-old's first goal came from the penalty spot before Vassilev set up his other two on either side of getting on the scoresheet himself.
Orlando attempted a late fightback, with Ivan Angulo scoring their first goal in the 78th minute before Martin Ojeda netted their second in the 90th minute.
Philadelphia were dominant in their victory and moved up to sixth in the Eastern Conference after a sixth consecutive win that stretched their unbeaten streak to 12 games.
"A lot of hard work. We made sure we set that standard first," Iloski, who became only the third player in Philadelphia's history to score multiple hat-tricks in the same season, told Apple TV.
"Of course, scoring a hat-trick is great. But a lot of guys really stepped up and played really well.
"So, it is a full team effort, and we really showed our depth. It is a big performance for the team."

Philadelphia also entered the MLS record books thanks to their post-World Cup form, having racked up 32 points over their last 12 games, matching the Seattle Sounders for the most points in any 12-game span in league history.
The Sounders also came out on top, with a 3-1 victory over Minnesota United, moving them up to ninth in the Western Conference.
Jordan Morris, Hassani Dotson and Paul Arriola were all on target for Seattle, with the former's acrobatic 16th-minute finish making him the club's outright top scorer in the regular season (73).
It was also a historic win for Brian Schmetzer, who became the third-fastest head coach to reach 150 wins in MLS history (334 games, behind Bruce Arena and Bob Bradley).
And there was another landmark to celebrate, this time for Nashville SC's Hany Mukhtar, who scored his 100th MLS goal thanks to a first-half brace in their 2-0 win over Toronto FC.

He is just the 16th player in league history to reach a century, and the first German-born player to do so, while Nashville currently sit 14 points clear at the top of the East ahead of Inter Miami playing on Sunday.
Vancouver Whitecaps, meanwhile, remain top of the West despite a 3-3 draw with D.C. United, sitting three points clear of FC Dallas in second.
Dallas beat Los Angeles FC 1-0 to leapfrog their closest challengers, taking advantage of Houston Dynamo's 2-0 loss to Sporting Kansas City.

1xdp391twdn6b19zt8idw42e2k.title: Maresca 'completely happy' with Guehi
1xdp391twdn6b19zt8idw42e2k.subtitle: Marc Guehi has been prone to mistakes as of late, but Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has no concerns about his centre-back.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca insisted he is "completely happy" with Marc Guehi amid recent criticism of the defender.
Guehi's defending was called into question during City's 2-1 Premier League defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday after he was dispossessed in the lead-up to Nicolas Jackson's opener.
Since the start of last season, only Bart Verbruggen (five), Jan Paul van Hecke (four) and Robin Roefs (four) have made more errors leading to goals in the Premier League than Guehi (three).
The England international, who was taken off at half-time at Villa Park, also made an error during the Three Lions' Nations League defeat to Spain during the previous international break.
Nevertheless, ahead of City's EFL Cup tie with Brighton, Maresca came to Guehi's defence.
"I'm completely, especially in this moment, happy with Marc," said Maresca.
"The way he reacted was fantastic. He is a top guy, a leader, one of the captains and I love Marc to be honest.
"When they make some mistakes, they recognise them. Marc is aware now.

"He's played all minutes since the start of the season with us and the international team. In the last two weeks he didn't play the Champions League game, he played 45 minutes the other day so he's completely okay."

City have won their last seven EFL Cup matches, their joint-best ever winning run in the competition. Only six teams have won eight in a row, most recently Newcastle United (nine between October 2024 and December 2025).
The only previous EFL Cup meeting between City and Brighton was in the second round in 2008-09; after a 2-2 draw at Withdean Stadium, the Seagulls won 5-3 on penalties.
Maresca's side will face Brighton twice this week, with the two sides also going head-to-head in the league on Saturday.
"First of all, they are doing very well so both games will be tough," Maresca said.
"They are very brave, aggressive and when they have the ball they attack with so many players.
"They create so many chances. We need to do the right things offensively and defensively."

1xk8absue9h6o1d0mru17h4obr.title: Gasperini revels in Roma's 'precious' victory over Cagliari
1xk8absue9h6o1d0mru17h4obr.subtitle: Roma's strong start to their Serie A season continued against Cagliari, but they were made to work for their win at the Stadio Olimpico.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini said the difficulties Cagliari caused during Roma's 4-2 victory made the win "even more precious" as their strong start in Serie A continued on Tuesday.
Roma ensured they remained on the tails of league leaders Lazio by scoring two late goals to battle past Cagliari, with substitute Rodrigo Mora starring in the closing stages.
M'Bala Nzola's 10th-minute penalty had put Cagliari ahead, but two quickfire strikes from Emanuele Lulli and Niccolo Pisilli ensured Roma went in at half-time with the lead.
But Cagliari thought they had salvaged a point nine minutes from time when Daniel Maldini finished past Pierluigi Gollini, but it was Roma who would have the last laugh.
Mora headed Daniele Ghilardi's cross home in the 85th minute before top scorer Donyell Malen sealed the win, having seen his first attempt blocked by Juan Rodriguez.

Roma are now unbeaten in 17 consecutive Serie A home matches (W13 D4), their longest such run since a 24-game streak between December 2015 and February 2017 under Rudi Garcia and Luciano Spalletti (W20 D4).

They have also scored 23 goals in their first nine matches of this Serie A season, last netting more than 20 at this stage of a campaign in 2016-17, when they also scored 23 under Spalletti, with Gasperini relishing his team's latest victory.
"Undoubtedly, we had a few difficulties today," Gasperini confessed to DAZN Italia, as quoted by Football Italia.
"They were fresher in attack and created problems for us. We are also using the same elements in midfield for every game and the fatigue is starting to show.
"That makes our victory even more precious, because everyone was involved."
Gasperini also saw two Roma academy products link up for their second goal of the match, with Pisilli volleying in Lulli's teasing cross from inside the penalty area.
Pisilli has scored three goals in eight appearances in this Serie A season, one fewer than he managed in 55 combined appearances across his previous four top-flight seasons.

Lulli, meanwhile, is one of two defenders born in 2007 or later to have been involved in at least three goals in the top five European leagues this season, with three (two goals, one assist) – level with Xavi Espart (one goal, two assists).

"They are extraordinary lads," Gasperini said of the two Roma youngsters. "In the Roma youth team there are always players who love the club so much and that gives them the dream of making their debut here.
"They are still very young and certainly have talent. Lulli scored with a header. He was training on that yesterday, because it is not his greatest strength."
Gasperini has had to rotate his Roma side of late, with injuries and their Champions League commitments seeing plenty of rotation within his ranks.
The likes of Paulo Dybala, Mile Svilar, Manu Kone and Lorenzo Pellegrini are all unavailable through injury.
"It's not easy to play games without Dybala and Kone, so we can make mistakes, but winning against a difficult side like Cagliari is something to be proud of," Gasperini added.

1xmy1nrf25lhp1wnb8jvsekj5n.title: Martinez's outburst in the past, says Maguire
1xmy1nrf25lhp1wnb8jvsekj5n.subtitle: Lisandro Martinez made headlines for his comments on the Manchester United hierarchy, but Harry Maguire said it has now been forgotten.
paragraphs: Harry Maguire insisted that Lisandro Martinez's outburst was in the past as he aims to turn Manchester United's fortunes around.
Martinez launched a scathing review of the United hierarchy in the aftermath of a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last week.
The Argentina international suggested the Red Devils did not have a team capable of competing in Europe, pointing the finger towards technical director Jason Wilcox and the owners of the club.
But Martinez later took to social media to clarify his outburst, saying the responsibility for United's poor results starts with the squad, while also apologising for his comments.
Michael Carrick decided to start Martinez in Sunday's 1-1 draw with Leeds United, though the defender was replaced at half-time by Noussair Mazraoui because of an injury.

"Obviously, there has been a lot of noise around the club [in the past week], as there is every week, but more so [in the past week]," Maguire told Sky Sports in response to a question about Martinez. "Lisandro has come out and apologised. We have moved on from it.
"He played, and I thought he was brilliant in the first half. Credit to him. Fingers crossed that he hasn't picked up a serious injury, and we can have him back."

United have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4 L2), their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87 – also one victory after seven games.
In fact, the Red Devils last tasted victory in all competitions on September 10 against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah in the Champions League, with Cesc Fabregas' Como up next.
United have just one win in their last 10 away Champions League matches (D3 L6) and have only kept one clean sheet in their last 15 on the road.
Maguire was also asked if the dressing room spirit had been challenged by Martinez's criticism.
He said: "When you play for this club it is always tested, especially when you're not winning football matches.
"We haven't played anywhere near well enough to win as many football matches as we did last season.
"We get tested every week, and the boys have got to get used to that. They've got to find something within themselves to help the group.
"We'll stick together, we'll go again. We have got another big game on Wednesday, and we look forward to it."

1xrmktb8xi4ac18zojw4lwyok0.title: Leverkusen determined to 'carry on in exactly the same way' with stellar home form
1xrmktb8xi4ac18zojw4lwyok0.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen have turned BayArena into a fortress this season, with struggling Stuttgart the next to test that perfect record.
paragraphs: Carles Martinez is keen to make sure Bayer Leverkusen continue to stay at the top of their game at BayArena, with Stuttgart the next visitors in the Bundesliga.
Leverkusen have won all of their home games across all competitions this season, with that form helping them to sit fourth in the Bundesliga table after seven matches.
They were on a five-game unbeaten streak before losing 3-0 to Hoffenheim last weekend, but they head into their clash with Stuttgart on the back of a morale-boosting DFB-Pokal victory.
Having trailed 2-0 to second-tier Nurnberg in the second round on Wednesday, they roared back to earn a 5-2 win thanks to a stunning second-half performance at home.
"The mood is good. Our main priority now is to recharge our batteries. With such a tight fixture list, every hour counts," Martinez said.
"The bond between the team and the fans is crucial. Together, we are a strong unit. That helps us in every match, especially at home.
"The fans give us a massive boost, even when we're behind, as was the case against Nurnberg. They've been able to enjoy themselves at the BayArena so far.
"We want to carry on in exactly the same way against Stuttgart."
Stuttgart have made a stuttering start to the campaign and are sitting down in 16th with only two wins to their name so far.

They have never lost three consecutive Bundesliga matches under Sebastian Hoeness. This is the seventh time they have lost two in a row under him, but a victory always followed on each previous occasion.
And Martinez remains wary of their opponents despite their recent struggles.

1xtlt43i941f5z86ei0imxat6.title: Gattuso worried by Lazio defence despite thrashing of Sassuolo
1xtlt43i941f5z86ei0imxat6.subtitle: Lazio moved three points clear at the top of Serie A by beating Sassuolo 6-2, but Gennaro Gattuso was not pleased with his defenders.
paragraphs: Gennaro Gattuso was left concerned by his Lazio defence despite thumping Sassuolo 6-2 on Tuesday, adding the mentality of his players told him a lot.
Lazio moved three points clear at the top of Serie A ahead of Inter's clash with Venezia on Wednesday with an entertaining triumph at MAPEI Stadium.
The visitors found themselves 3-1 up inside the opening 16 minutes, with Kenneth Taylor, Gustav Isaksen and Romano Floriani Mussolini all on target for Lazio.

Kristian Thorstvedt was then sent off for Sassuolo, but Sebastiano Esposito was able to reduce the deficit in the 43rd minute, only for Mattia Zaccagni to restore Lazio's two-goal cushion in first-half stoppage time.
Missed penalties from Zaccagni and Davide Frattesi came either side of Tijjani Noslin's 55th-minute strike, with the Dutchman sealing the win after the hour for Gattuso's side.

Before their win over Sassuolo, the last time Lazio had scored with five different players in a Serie A match was in March 2018 against Benevento, though the concern for Gattuso was at the opposite end of the pitch.

Lazio dominated the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 3.57 from their 16 shots to Sassuolo's tally of 0.76 from their nine attempts, but Gattuso said his side's superiority was helped largely by Thorstvedt's red card in the first half.
"The thing I will take from this is the mentality," Gattuso said, as quoted by Football Italia. "When we are not being aggressive, we have to learn how to block defensively.
"Sassuolo are a very dangerous side, and we weren't very good on that front. It helped that they were down to 10 men.
"But, when we work and link well, we make it difficult for our opponents. We're not looking at the standings, otherwise we'll get vertigo. We're taking things game by game."
Lazio's result saw them avoid defeat in their first nine games of a Serie A campaign for the fifth time in their history.
It was the first time they had managed to do so since 1999-00, the season they last lifted the Scudetto.
Lazio's win was also their fifth consecutive league triumph, a feat they last achieved under Marco Baroni between October and November two years ago.
But Gattuso was not getting ahead of himself when asked about Lazio's title credentials this season, adding: "I'm superstitious, but we also have to look at reality.
"If we think about trying to manage the game or see it out, we start finding it difficult.
"We have to go and keep creating the situations that we are creating. We haven't had any kicks in the teeth yet, so we'll see when it happens.
"There's only one way to go about it and that is by working hard."

1xvq6lg40che81k8avrhzazg9o.title: Toronto boss Fraser highlights Pereira's professionalism
1xvq6lg40che81k8avrhzazg9o.subtitle: Just three points separate play-off chasers New York Red Bulls and Toronto FC ahead of their clash at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
paragraphs: Toronto FC head coach Robin Fraser praised the professionalism of defender Matheus Pereira after his eventful display against Orlando City.
The Reds drew 3-3 with Orlando on Wednesday, with Pereira scoring an 89th-minute equaliser for the home side, which was also his first goal for the club.
However, that moment came after Pereira conceded a penalty in first-half stoppage time, with Martin Ojeda converting the spot-kick after the Brazilian's handball.
Despite the mistake, Pereira put in a strong performance for Toronto, leading his side in possessions won (eight) and touches (64) to go along with his goal.
Ahead of their Eastern Conference clash with the New York Red Bulls, Fraser highlighted Pereira's resilience.
"He is a very good player who has really good game understanding, knows what to do when within the game," said Fraser about Pereira.
"Things are going to happen and you can’t let a mistake affect you. As a seasoned and experienced professional, he didn't.
"He played well, he obviously contributed in many other ways, and that's what I would expect.
"It's certainly pleasant to see that players can stay focused, even if they make a mistake or they're involved in an erroneous moment, they continue to be focused and play well."
The New York Red Bulls are eighth in the East, just three points and three places ahead of play-off chasing Toronto.
Michael Bradley's side saw their momentum halted during the week after a 2-1 defeat against D.C. United – their second loss in three MLS matches (W1).
New York Red Bulls – Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting
Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting has scored in back-to-back regular-season matches for the first time since May 2025.
Choupo-Moting has never scored in three straight regular-season matches, as the last Red Bull player to score in three consecutive league games was Cameron Harper in May 2024.
Toronto FC – Daniel Salloi
Daniel Salloi has seven goals and seven assists this season after setting up Theo Corbeanu on Wednesday.
Salloi is the second player in the last six seasons with at least seven goals and seven assists for Toronto (Federico Bernardeschi – eight goals, eight assists in 2024).
MATCH PREDICTION – NEW YORK RED BULLS WIN

NYRB are unbeaten in 14 straight regular-season meetings with Toronto (W9 D5), last losing to the Reds in July 2019. This equals the longest regular-season unbeaten run by one team against another in the post-shootout era (since 2000).

The Red Bulls won their last home match 4–1 against San Diego FC, just the club’s fifth home win of the 2026 regular season. It has been over a year since NYRB won two straight home league games, defeating Real Salt Lake and Philadelphia Union in August 2025.
Toronto scored an 89th-minute equaliser to draw with Orlando after scoring twice in stoppage time to beat Montreal 2–1 on Saturday.
It is the second time in the last 15 seasons that Toronto have avoided defeat in two straight matches despite trailing entering the 89th minute in both (May-June 2019).
New York Red Bulls – 46.5%

1y0e1ga2z9kgs1n3k5h3la5oh1.title: Maddison revels in Spurs injury comeback after overcoming 'dark days'
1y0e1ga2z9kgs1n3k5h3la5oh1.subtitle: James Maddison marked his first Premier League start since April 2025 against Liverpool with a goal as Tottenham beat Coventry on Monday.
paragraphs: James Maddison said his goal-scoring return to the Tottenham starting line-up was a "dream" after enduring several "dark days" during his recovery from injury.
Maddison marked his first Premier League start since April 2025 against Liverpool with a stunning 14th-minute opener in Spurs' 3-1 win over Coventry City on Monday.
Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies were also on target for Roberto De Zerbi's side, having seen Jack Rudoni level things up for the Sky Blues early in the second half.
But it was Maddison who got things up and running at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a superb finish as he curled his effort over Carl Rushworth and into the top-left corner.
Since making his Premier League debut in August 2018, Maddison has now scored 21 goals from outside the box, at least two more than any other player (Kevin De Bruyne and James Ward-Prowse, 19 each).
It was a result that saw Spurs earn just their sixth win in their last 37 home Premier League games (D10 L21), and their fourth league victory overall in 2026 (P27 D10 L13).

The match was Maddison's first competitive start for the club since their 2024-25 Europa League semi-final against Bodo/Glimt, having gone through a nightmare recovery following an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury sustained last August.
On his goal, Maddison became quite emotional, telling Sky Sports: "They're just a bit blurry. They're the ones you dream of. Recovering from the ACL last year, those dark days.
"They are the ones you dream of, those goals. Always the light at the tunnel for you. And for Dejan Kulusevski, I felt proud for him because I knew exactly how he felt.
"Those moments and those goals make it all worth it."

For the first time in 36 games, Spurs scored more than 2+ goals in a Premier League match, while it was the first time they scored 3+ goals on home soil in the league since MD1 last season against Burnley (3-0).
Spurs also became the first side to score three goals from outside the box in a single Premier League game since Fulham against Leicester City in May 2023.

There was also a touching moment for Kulusevski, who was named in a Premier League matchday squad for the first time in 526 days, and he came on to a standing ovation from the home supporters when he replaced Mohammed Kudus in the 87th minute.
It's a result that relieves the pressure on De Zerbi ahead of this weekend's clash with Chelsea, and the Spurs boss is confident his team can build on this morale-boosting win.
"I am delighted with the result, the attitude, the spirit and the reaction after the goal we conceded," De Zerbi said. "Honestly, we did not play as well as in the last games.
"But now, because of our responsibility, they deserve credit as they defended very well and compact.
"When we went outside from Kudus and Robertson, we didn't push the ball with the right speed. We were too predictable, maybe playing three at the back.
"We played three at the back for injury reasons, first. We play with Kudus on the right wing and Robertson on the left wing, and with three number 10 with different characteristics.
"We scored two goals with these players, but we can't forget Solanke as he played very well.
"Fantastic moment and fantastic human [Dejan]. We celebrated him in the dressing room after the game. He is maybe the most important thing after this win.

"Now we have to understand whether we are able to win because, after two or three seasons like this, the mental aspect is crucial. We have to thank the fans, especially in the last part of the game. They were fantastic.
"They have suffered a lot. We have to push, we have to improve the quality of the play for sure, but we are a good team, a very good team."

1y0xdhz6tkq3s1bue8cn5piztx.title: Fabregas: I've never thought about leaving Como
1y0xdhz6tkq3s1bue8cn5piztx.subtitle: Following their impressive Champions League win over Manchester United, Como host Sassuolo in Serie A on Saturday.
paragraphs: Cesc Fabregas insists he has "never thought about leaving" Como, despite reported interest in his services.
Since becoming head coach, Fabregas has led Como to promotion to Serie A and last year guided them into the Champions League places.

The Spaniard was linked with the Inter and Bayer Leverkusen roles in 2025, while reports emerged suggesting there is a clause in his contract which would allow him to join Arsenal, Chelsea or Barcelona – all of whom he represented as a player.
Off the back of a memorable Champions League win over Manchester United, Como host Alberto Aquilani's Sassuolo in Serie A.
Como president Mirwan Suwarso recently spoke highly of Aquilani, and Fabregas was asked if the Sassuolo boss could one day replace him at Como.
"I've never thought about leaving. If I started thinking about it, maybe that would be the end for me here, but I've never done it," Fabregas said.
"I can certainly say positive things about him [Aquilani]. His football is very similar in terms of ideas.
"You're making me think about it now, but I'm very relaxed about his career and what he'll go on to do.
"I really like Alberto as a coach, for his ideas and his courage, and for how his teams play football.
"He called me last summer because he really wanted Rispoli at Catanzaro. Rispoli was the first player I ever had as a coach, so sending him to Alberto gave me complete peace of mind."
Como are fifth in Serie A, five points off early leaders Inter, and six ahead of 13th-place Sassuolo.
Sassuolo lost 4-2 to Frosinone last time out and are winless in their last three Serie A games (D1 L2).

Nico Paz became the third-youngest midfielder to reach 20 goals in Serie A in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95) when he scored against Fiorentina at 22 years and 40 days old, with only Domenico Morfeo (22 years, 23 days) and Marek Hamsik (22 years, 34 days) doing so at a younger age.
Aged 22 years and 46 days for this match, he could become the youngest midfielder to surpass the 20-goal threshold in the three-points-for-a-win era.
Sassuolo – Domenico Berardi
Domenico Berardi scored on the last Serie A matchday and is looking to score in consecutive games for the first time since November 2025.
Since 2013-14 (his first goalscoring season in Serie A), only Ciro Immobile (196) and Lautaro Martinez (136) have scored more goals than the Sassuolo forward (132) in the competition.
MATCH PREDICTION: COMO WIN
Como and Sassuolo have only previously met in Serie A last season, with one home win apiece; Como won 2-0 in November 2025, while Sassuolo secured a 2-1 victory in April 2026.

Como have gained 14 points in Serie A this season; only in 1950-51 have they collected as many points after their first seven matches in the competition (14 on that occasion too), considering three points for a win.
Sassuolo are the only team to have both scored and conceded in every Serie A game this season; they have scored 12 goals and conceded 14, an average of 3.7 goals per game in total.

Aquilani's side are winless in their last 10 Serie A away games (D3 L7); they have only ever had a longer run without a victory on the road in the top-flight once before, a 15-match streak between December 2023 and September 2025.
Como have conceded just one goal in their last four Serie A home matches, keeping three clean sheets; the same number of shutouts they registered in their previous nine home games in the competition.

Domenico Berardi scored on the last Serie A matchday and is looking to score in consecutive games for the first time since November 2025.

Since 2013-14 (his first goalscoring season in Serie A), only Ciro Immobile (196) and Lautaro Martinez (136) have scored more goals than the Sassuolo forward (132) in the competition.

MATCH PREDICTION: COMO WIN

Como and Sassuolo have only previously met in Serie A last season, with one home win apiece; Como won 2-0 in November 2025, while Sassuolo secured a 2-1 victory in April 2026.

Como have gained 14 points in Serie A this season; only in 1950-51 have they collected as many points after their first seven matches in the competition (14 on that occasion too), considering three points for a win.

Sassuolo are the only team to have both scored and conceded in every Serie A game this season; they have scored 12 goals and conceded 14, an average of 3.7 goals per game in total.

Aquilani's side are winless in their last 10 Serie A away games (D3 L7); they have only ever had a longer run without a victory on the road in the top-flight once before, a 15-match streak between December 2023 and September 2025.

Como have conceded just one goal in their last four Serie A home matches, keeping three clean sheets; the same number of shutouts they registered in their previous nine home games in the competition.

Como – 61.4%

Draw – 19.9%

Sassuolo – 18.7%

1y1gd72jgzddn1c6u26arjsply.title: Gerrard has 'no regrets' over rejecting Madrid, Inter and Bayern
1y1gd72jgzddn1c6u26arjsply.subtitle: Steven Gerrard spent the majority of his career with Liverpool, despite interest from some of Europe's biggest clubs.
paragraphs: Steven Gerrard insisted he has "no regrets" over turning down interest from Real Madrid, Inter and Bayern Munich to stay with Liverpool.
The former Reds captain made 710 appearances for the club, scoring 186 goals and winning eight trophies during his 17-year spell on Merseyside.

He led Liverpool to Champions League glory in 2005, when they staged their famous comeback over AC Milan in the final, while also winning two FA Cups, three EFL Cups, one UEFA Cup (Europa League) and one Super Cup.
Gerrard never managed to win the Premier League, however.

Madrid and Inter both held interest in Gerrard when Jose Mourinho was their head coach, while Bayern saw him as a possible replacement for Bastian Schweinsteiger in 2015. Chelsea were also linked with him on several occasions.
Despite seeing the likes of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham enjoy success abroad, Gerrard stood by his decision to stay at Anfield.
"I had some interest from foreign teams and the majority of that was through Jose Mourinho," Gerrard said on The Overlap Daily.
"Inter, Real Madrid, on a couple of occasions, and at the back end a few conversations with my agent when [Bastian] Schweinsteiger was leaving Bayern [in 2015].
"I wasn't really that interested in it because I was never going to leave Liverpool at the time.
"I was enjoying my football under Brendan [Rodgers] when that one came but yes, three of four of the big teams showed some interest during my career, which is flattering, of course it is.
"When you watch the likes of Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane and you see them winning loads of trophies with foreign teams, it does cross your mind and you go back and you think.
"But I have no regrets in terms of the decisions I made. No regrets."

21A20FE3CBCFABEA39EDC9CA18F367B4.title: The MLS Wrap: Messi and Suarez hit form for Inter Miami
21A20FE3CBCFABEA39EDC9CA18F367B4.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Messi and Suarez hit form for Inter MiamiShareLionel Messi and Luis Suárez showed signs they might be hitting peak form for Inter Miami at just the right time, with the MLS Cup Playoffs in sight.
Most teams have just six games to play before the regular season ends, and Inter Miami will no doubt be a threat in the postseason.

But they are still not the best team in the league currently, or even the second or third-best, as a trio of teams continue to impress week in, week out, in the latter stages of the 2026 season, setting records of their own.
It’s safe to say Inter Miami have been unspectacular as a team in 2026 so far, but with Lionel Messi in their ranks, they are always capable of spectacular moments.
There were a couple of those from himself and Suárez as Inter Miami defeated DC United 4-0.

Messi was not down in the dumps following his emotional retirement from international football during the previous international break, and instead put in a performance that makes you think he’d still have plenty to offer Argentina.
Two old friends just out there enjoying themselves… pic.twitter.com/R0EwANfjTx
Suárez retains the striking instincts that made him the best in the world in his position at one point in his career.
Even as the speed is now gone, for as long as he can reach a canter, he will still score goals in MLS, fool defenders, and get assists, too, as he did for Messi’s first.
Messi’s second, meanwhile, was a reminder that he remains world-class, as he danced past multiple defenders before slotting past the goalkeeper.
It was a first win for Inter Miami’s latest head coach, Kily González, and a first clean sheet in 11 league games.
Danish winger Carlo Holse is the highest-rated player (9.7) of the round after scoring a hat-trick for St. Louis in their Sunday night game against LA Galaxy.

The 6-2 win saw St. Louis continue an unbeaten run that now stretches to 20 games, tying the record for an MLS team in all competitions, joining Red Bull New York, who also managed 20 games unbeaten in 2016.
Holse, 27, joined St. Louis as a designated player this summer and has gradually been introduced to the team over the past two months.

He’s had a run of four starts since mid-September, having mostly been limited to appearances off the bench late in games prior to that, and in these most recent games has scored five goals and registered one assist.
The third goal for his hat-trick this weekend was particularly good, as he did brilliantly to control a long ball from Chris Durkin on his chest before turning and shooting.
Fellow summer signing Rafael Navarro wasn’t far behind him with a FotMob rating of 9.5 thanks to two goals and two assists of his own.
His all-round centre-forward play combined with the runs of Hulse could be a great combination for St. Louis in the playoffs.
Their 20-game unbeaten run also includes wins in the US Open Cup. They’ll face Columbus Crew in the final next week, giving them a chance to have a trophy to show for this impressive form.
A cup win would be good accompaniment to their climb to second place in the Western Conference, where they are now just a point behind Vancouver Whitecaps.

2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.title: The FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and Semenyo
2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and SemenyoShareMatchday 5 of the Premier League season is done and dusted, with Manchester City establishing a three-point advantage at the top of the table courtesy of Arsenal’s defeat against Brighton.
It will be a sad time when Alisson finally leaves Liverpool, especially as he is still more than capable of producing excellent displays like the one against Bournemouth.

The Brazilian made two saves during the game, including an impressive effort to prevent Evanilson from opening the scoring in the first half – a shot worth 0.78 xGOT. That was his third Premier League clean sheet in a row.
The Barcelona loanee makes it into FotMob’s Team of the Week for the second time in three weeks thanks to another solid display.

Araújo wasn’t quite at his best in the final third, yet the right-back made five defensive contributions including two tackles, while also registering six recoveries throughout the game. He even won 86% of his aerial duels and played a massive part in Liverpool keeping that clean sheet for Alisson.
Everton kept their fifth clean sheet across seven matches in all competitions against Ipswich at the weekend and James Tarkowski played a big part in the 1-0 win.
The defender provided the assist for Everton’s only goal while also notching up 12 defensive contributions throughout the 90 minutes.

Seven of those were clearances, and Tarkowski was also a rock when it came to duels, winning 100% of his ground and 83% of his aerial duels in the contest. He was certainly more than deserving of his 8.5 rating.
Brentford’s 3-0 victory over Chelsea was arguably the result of Matchday 5 and Jannik Schuster was rock solid at the heart of the defence.

With 16, the Austrian centre-back registered the most defensive contributions in the game, and he even chipped in at the other end of the pitch, grabbing an assist and making three passes into the final third.
Aged just 20, Schuster could be the future of Brentford’s defence over the next few years.
Jay Dasilva’s thumping effort against Nottingham Forest gave Coventry their first Premier League win since 2001 and he fully deserves his spot in the Team of the Week.

The left-back was a menace on the left flank, succeeding with 100% of his dribble attempts while also making six passes into the final third. Frank Lampard will be expecting more of the same when domestic action returns next month.
Chema Andrés provided an assist on his Premier League debut last weekend, but he went one better against Arsenal, netting the third goal in Brighton’s victory against the champions.
It was a splendid performance by the midfielder who looked equally adept whether he was defending or trying to make things happen in the final third against the Gunners.
Five passes into the final third, nine defensive contributions, and winning five out of five aerial duels ensure he makes his FotMob Team of the Week debut.
Pascal Groß is ageing like a fine wine, isn’t he? The German midfielder covered the most ground against Arsenal (12.6 km), despite being the oldest player on the pitch.
He not only scored, but provided an assist during the contest, and also made eight passes into the final third.
Groß added five defensive contributions and was well deserving of making the Team of the Week for the second consecutive matchday.
🤯 Pascal Gross has won FotMob Man of the Match in ALL of Brighton’s last three games, averaging a rating of 8.8!He’s 35-years-old, by the way. pic.twitter.com/i2tV5QHRht

          Liverpool vs Everton Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 27, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Can the Reds bounce back from a WSL defeat to the champions? We look ahead to Sunday's Merseyside derby at Anfield with our Liverpool vs Everton prediction and preview.

Anfield will welcome Gareth Taylor’s Liverpool with plenty of excitement and anticipation for Sunday's Merseyside derby with Everton on Sunday, particularly after they pushed champions Manchester City to the limit last weekend.
The Reds head into the derby with one win from their opening three Women's Super League games, but the results don’t tell the full story of their start to the new campaign.
There have already been encouraging signs of the more ambitious and attacking side Taylor is trying to build, with the biggest transformation coming in attack.

Liverpool have already scored seven times in the WSL this season, more than they managed across their opening 10 matches last term (six). Excluding the 2017 Spring Series, it is their best goal tally after three games of a WSL campaign.
Everton sit just above their neighbours after taking six points from their opening three matches, but the league table masks an extraordinary start in front of goal.
The Toffees have taken 41 shots and generated 2.9 xG, though they are yet to see one of their own players score this season.
Both of Everton’s victories have come courtesy of own goals, making them the first team in WSL history to win two matches 1-0 via an own goal in the same season.
Their victory over Charlton was particularly remarkable. Everton attempted 13 shots without registering a single effort on target, and yet they still walked away with the win.

Everton are only the second team in WSL history to score fewer than three goals across their opening three matches of a season and still collect as many as six points, after Sunderland in 2017-18. It is also the Toffees’ best points return at this stage of a campaign since 2022-23 (also W2 L1).
It creates a fascinating contrast at Anfield, with Liverpool's seven goals coming from 5.0 xG.

New signing Vivien Endemann has contributed to that. The Germany international became the first player in WSL history to both score and assist in two of her first three appearances in the competition. Only Khadija Shaw (5) can better her four goal involvements across the early weeks of 2026-27.
Endemann could join Caitlin Foord (6) and Alessia Russo (5) as the only players to register at least five goal involvements in their first four WSL appearances since 2020-21.

On top of improving Liverpool's attacking potency, Taylor’s influence can also be seen in the way Liverpool are trying to win the ball back higher up the pitch, with only Chelsea (56) and Arsenal (44) recording more high turnovers than Liverpool (39) in the WSL this season.
That approach was evident even in defeat to City, as Liverpool became the first team since Everton in November 2025 to record 15+ high turnovers against City in a WSL match.

For a side who struggled for goals last season, the early signs suggest Taylor has not simply added more attacking quality, but is building a team more capable of controlling games higher up the pitch.
Liverpool may have won the last Merseyside derby, but recent history at Anfield has belonged to Everton.
The Toffees have won each of their last five WSL games at Liverpool, their joint-longest winning run away to a single opponent in the competition (also Aston Villa).

Indeed, Liverpool have lost eight of their nine WSL matches at Anfield, with their only victory coming against Manchester United in March 2025. Five of those eight defeats have come at the hands of Everton.

The Reds can take confidence from the most recent meeting, though as they ran out 3-2 winners at Everton in March. They could now record consecutive WSL victories over their neighbours for the first time since winning three in a row across 2013 and 2014.

22CA79AD6DAFDF84DE8ABA6769AA4878.title: Greece could be the upstarts of this UEFA Nations League cycle
22CA79AD6DAFDF84DE8ABA6769AA4878.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesGreece could be the upstarts of this UEFA Nations League cycleShareWhisper it softly, but the Greek national team might just be finally waking up from its 12-year slumber.

After group-stage exits in their first two major tournaments – 1980 Euros and 1994 World Cup – third time proved the charm for Greece, who pulled off one of the greatest shocks in football history by defeating Portugal in the final of the 2004 Euros. They built on that by reaching the next two Euros and two of the next three World Cups, culminating in a Round of 16 penalty shootout defeat to Costa Rica in the 2014 World Cup. Since then, however, the Ethniki have been absent from every major tournament.

Euro 2004 papered over the cracks in their domestic game, caused by economic turmoil, systemic corruption, fan hooliganism, and structural mismanagement. Unlike many European leagues with balanced ownership models, Greek clubs are heavily privatized, and the power struggle over the Hellenic Football Federation (HFF) and refereeing appointments created an uneven playing field and eroded public trust. Scandals involving match-fixing, leaked audio tapes, and political interventions to rescue favoured clubs from relegation would turn domestic competitions into an arena of continuous controversy, alienating a generation of fans.

Greece’s financial crisis saw historic clubs like AEK Athens suffer relegation in order to clear massive debts, and it also saw the Greek league go from sixth in the UEFA coefficients in 2002/03 to an all-time low of 20th in 2020/21. Numerous lower-tier clubs left players unpaid for months, in addition to being without proper training facilities and basic infrastructure. And as the heroes of Portugal ‘04 retired, Greece struggled to find adequate replacements and finished bottom of their Euro 2016 qualifying group (including not one but two defeats to the Faroe Islands).

As it turned out, it was merely darkest before the dawn. With budgets slashed, Greek clubs pivoted from signing big-name veterans and focused on shoehorning teenage talents into the first team. Teams like PAOK overhauled their youth setup, hiring elite European coaching and sports science staff and constructing state-of-the-art training facilities. PAOK’s refurbished academy gave rise to future internationals like Christos Tzolis, Giannis Konstantelias, Konstantinos Koulierakis, and Stefanos Tzimas, all of whom are playing in Europe’s top five leagues. This youth investment has been mirrored throughout the nation, with the number of UEFA-licensed youth coaches nearly tripling from 665 in 2020 to 1,886 in 2023. Top-tier clubs have established an extensive network of 13 regional scouting centers across the country to provide room, board, and education for elite teenage players.

Christos Tzolis has started 4 games for Arsenal so far, and registered a goal involvement in every game! 🤯👏🏼4 assists and a goal, including 2 assists and a MOTM rating in the Community Shield today! 🏆He only cost £34 million… 🤯 pic.twitter.com/z87ZCgLtrx

After years of being defined by conservative, gritty tactics, Greece have shifted to a more modern, attack-minded style of play across all youth levels. They’re no longer focused on which players will be able to win the most U15 tournaments, but which players will be able to excel in a high-intensity, possession-based setup at the professional level several years down the line. They’re prioritizing individual creativity over immediate team results, with U6 players playing 2v2 in order to get as many touches as possible and fine-tune their dribbling, before moving up to 3v3, 5v5, 8v8, and only reaching 11v11 at U14 level. The HFF has ensured that these youngsters get early exposure by forcing third-tier clubs to field at least two U18 players in every single XI, as well as mandating at least one homegrown Under-21 player on the pitch at all times in the Greek Cup.

Slowly but surely, these seeds have started to bear fruit, with Olympiacos winning the 2023/24 UEFA Youth League (the same year that their first team won the Conference League). Greece earned promotion to League B in the UEFA Nations League but missed out on a spot in Euro 2024 following their penalty shootout defeat to Georgia, but they responded by earning promotion to League A. This season, however, there is a brand-new aroma to Greek football. After a summer that saw Konstantinos Tzolakis, Christos Mouzakitis, Tzolis, Konstantelias and Karetsas earn lucrative transfers, Greece’s squad is filled with players who are flourishing in Europe’s top five leagues.

This talent was on full display in Belgrade as Greece erased an early deficit and prevailed 2-1 against Serbia via late goals from Tzolis and substitute Anastasios Douvikas (the second-top scorer in Serie A last season). They did even better in their second Nations League match, winning 1-0 in Augsburg via a late goal from substitute Dimitris Kourbelis, the first time that Greece had beaten Germany in 11 attempts. Greece sit atop League A, and if they can continue their winning streak at home against the Netherlands and Germany, they will be all but guaranteed to qualify for the Nations League quarterfinals in March.
🇬🇷 That Greece front line is absolutely stacked with attacking talent. pic.twitter.com/lpgRCnuCwV

“It's exciting with all of these players going to these big, big leagues and big teams,” stated Hellas Footy host Stephen Kountourou. “It gives us hope that, if they play at a higher level, the national team can be elevated to a higher level, and they'll have that experience to then take us, finally, to a major tournament. A lot of people are saying ‘This is Greece's golden generation,’ but we can't start calling them a golden generation until they've actually reached a tournament. That's the aim: we're not expecting them to go and win the World Cup or Euros, but if they could start competing again in these major tournaments, I think that would be success for Greece. I don't see the success of this national team depending on what they win: if they can get there first, then we'll see what happens. It’s baby steps.”

It’s taken a while, but Greek football is thriving both in terms of domestic competitiveness and youth production. After winning 19 of 21 championships, Olympiacos have since won the title in four of the last nine seasons, with AEK Athens and PAOK laying claim to top honours. Whereas players like Vangelis Pavlidis used to have to leave home for Germany in order to receive a world-class football education, that’s no longer the case: elite talents like Charalampos Kostoulas and Christos Zafeiris are popping up wherever you look in Greece. And six years after ranking 20th, Super League Greece ranks 12th in the UEFA coefficient.

Greece have been here before: they kicked off their 2026 World Cup qualifying with a 5-1 demolition of Belarus before losing their next three and falling short of qualification. It’s one thing to start solid, but now, can they find some consistency and finally reemerge on the world’s biggest stage?

          Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal Stats: Rice Salvages Late Draw to Deny Kane Winner
        
      
                          
                      Oct 21, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Harry Kane and Declan Rice were among the goals in this tight Champions League encounter. Look back on the action with our Bayern Munich vs Arsenal stats page.
Declan Rice struck late to earn a point for Arsenal, claiming a thrilling 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich at Allianz Arena.
It looked like the game would belong to Harry Kane, who orchestrated the comeback after Eberechi Eze – an early replacement for the injured Bukayo Saka – opened the scoring.
Kane set up Alphonso Davies‘ equaliser before netting from the penalty spot, but Rice finished off a pacy move down Arsenal's right to take a share of the spoils.
Serge Gnabry had the first clear opening, with Kane launching a goal-kick over the top to Davies, who squared it into the middle. Ismael Saibari helped it onto Gnabry, who tamely shot at David Raya.
But it was Arsenal who broke the deadlock 25 minutes in, as Eze latched onto Martin Ødegaard‘s wonderful pass to slot under Manuel Neuer into the bottom-right corner.
Their lead lasted just 10 minutes, though, with Kane once again showing his range with a lovely through ball for Davies to chase, and he coolly slotted past Raya.

It was a frenetic start to the second half, with Neuer making a point-blank save on his line to tip Bruno Guimarães‘ header onto the crossbar, before Raya brilliantly pushed away Dayot Upamecano‘s effort at the other end following a blistering counter-attack.
Eze almost got a second goal when he skipped through the left of the box before trying his luck from near the byline, but Neuer was once again equal to it.

Kane was then at the heart of Bayern's second goal in the 61st minute. His shot was blocked by Jurriën Timber‘s arm, and the former Tottenham man stepped up from 12 yards to emphatically finish past Raya.

Kai Havertz saw a poked effort blocked on the line before Luis Díaz‘s curler was well-saved by Raya, and that set Arsenal up to find their 82nd-minute equaliser as Rice raced onto Viktor Gyökeres‘ lay-off to drill into the bottom-left corner.

Timber, looking to make up for conceding the earlier penalty, could have won the game in the 91st minute, but Neuer got a strong hand behind the bending shot from just outside the box to keep it level as both teams settled for a well-earned point apiece.
Kane has always enjoyed playing against Arsenal, but could not prove the difference despite scoring his 16th goal against them – only versus Leicester City (20) has he scored more.
This is the ninth Champions League match in which he has both scored and assisted, two more than any other Englishman has managed.
Kane is also just the second player to score in 10 consecutive Champions League appearances, along with Cristiano Ronaldo from June 2017 to April 2018 (11).

The 33-year-old was showing off all of his attributes with some incredible passes opening Arsenal up. Only Barcelona's Lamine Yamal (10) has set up more goals in Europe's big five leagues in all competitions than Kane (7) this term.

Arsenal started well, though, especially considering Saka's early exit, with Eze getting a much-needed goal. He scored the earliest goal by a substitute in a Champions League game since Junior Adamu in February 2022 for Salzburg – also against Bayern (21st minute).
And they finished strong after riding the pressure. No Premier League side has had more goal contributions from substitutes in all competitions this season than Arsenal (five goals, four assists).
Rice scored his sixth Champions League goal, but his first-ever away from home, and in the end, it was a fair result with both sides preserving their unbeaten starts to the competition.

257387683964B2C1903D4A98BE49BBAA.title: Pochettino is bringing through the USA’s brightest crop of youngsters since Pulisic and co.
257387683964B2C1903D4A98BE49BBAA.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPochettino is bringing through the USA’s brightest crop of youngsters since Pulisic and co.ShareMauricio Pochettino has called up a youthful squad for the USA’s first fixtures since co-hosting the 2026 World Cup.

The hype around Cavan Sullivan has been intense for years. From the moment the American wonderkid joined Manchester City at the age of only 14, Sullivan has been built up as the USA’s greatest individual hope for the future. Now 16 years old, the future is now with Sullivan expected to make his national team debut in the current international break.

Picked by Mauricio Pochettino for the friendly matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, Sullivan is part of a youthful contingent the US men’s national team head coach has turned to as part of his process to prepare his side for the 2030 World Cup. A new cycle signifies a fresh start for the USMNT.

Sullivan earned his call-up by catching the eye for the Philadelphia Union. The teenager is on a run of six goals in six games with only Lionel Messi more impactful as an individual difference-maker in Major League Soccer right now than Sullivan. The wonderkid is in wonderful form and could become the USMNT’s youngest debutant since Freddy Adu.

RBNY's Adri Mehmeti is another teenage talent called up by Pochettino for the first time. The 17-year-old is the sort of midfield pace-setter the USA have lacked for years, decades even. Physically, Mehmeti still has some growing to do, but the potential is clearly there for him to become a key figure for the national team.

Neil Pierre’s emergence for Philadelphia is timely for the USA considering their desperate need for defensive reinforcement. Tim Ream has been a reliable performer for the national team, but the former Fulham centre back is now 38. He will be into his 40s by the time of the 2030 World Cup.

Justin Ellis has broken through as a key figure for Orlando City this season with the Red Bulls’ Julian Hall yet another teenage talent who has made a profound impact in MLS recently. The number of young players using the league as a platform has been a big storyline of the 2026 season.

No fewer than 13 uncapped players have been called up by Pochettino for the September and October international window. Among them are a contingent of youngsters who appear ready for regular game time. Sullivan could be in this group. So too could Zavier Gozo who made the move to Crystal Palace from Real Salt Lake this summer.

There is also another contingent who might not be ready for prime time for a number of years. Prospects like Brooklyn Raines, Mathis Albert and Diego Kochen must use the experience of being involved in a USMNT camp to continue their development. Pochettino is firmly focused on the future.

Noahkai Banks might have been another young player called up. Pochettino courted the Augsburg defender only for Banks, who played for the USA at youth level, to file a one-time switch to represent Germany last week. Supporters reacted with disappointment, but Pochettino made clear that he wouldn’t dwell on Banks’ rejection.

“We want players who show commitment,” said Pochettino when asked about US Soccer’s recruitment of dual-nationals which will surely continue even after the failure to land Banks. “Commitment is not 50%, it’s 200%. It’s good, he was honest. We want players who want to commit and are desperate to play for the badge. That’s the most important thing.”

While the USMNT’s 2026 World Cup campaign ended abruptly with a heavy (and controversial) defeat to Belgium in the last 16, Pochettino established a tactical framework for the tournament that will give him a headstart now that he is at the start of a new cycle. A lot of the hard work has already been done.

Now, it’s about finding players who can execute his instructions at an even higher level. Pochettino is bringing through the most exciting crop of young American talent since Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Tyler Adams surfaced. He could elevate the USMNT’s level by integrating new players in a position or two.

The squad for the September and October international window is unashamedly experimental. Pulisic hasn’t been called up despite the fact he is the USA’s most reliable attacking difference-maker. Folarin Balogun has been given the time to settle back into life at Monaco after his failed deadline day transfer to Everton. McKennie is similarly out of this current squad.

Pochettino will call on these established stars again, but the next three weeks are about finding new players for the USMNT to build around. The road to the 2030 World Cup (via a possible Copa America, a Gold Cup and an Olympics) starts here. Sullivan and co. are ready to step up.

270CEB4B295CBC991B193424F43F2832.title: Preview: Liverpool will be kicking off early against LASK in Austria
270CEB4B295CBC991B193424F43F2832.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Liverpool will be kicking off early against LASK in AustriaShareLiverpool travel to Austria on Wednesday to face LASK in the Champions League. All eyes will be on how the Reds react to their first defeat of the season following their 3-0 loss to Manchester City on Sunday.

The hosts have stalled a little over recent weeks. LASK are winless in four, losing three of those matches and drawing the other 3-3. This run includes their Champions League opener which ended in a 1-0 loss to AEK Athens in a game they did deserve to lose.

Away in Greece, the Austrian side managed to carve out an Expected Goals total of just 0.72. Bizarrely, prior to that defeat, scoring goals had not been a problem for Dietmar Kühbauer’s men. In their eight matches across all competitions preceding that Champions League clash, they’d scored a minimum of three in six of those outings.

This run included a 5-1 win over Celtic to knock the Scottish champions out of the Champions League play-offs. Despite their winless run, they’ve actually scored 19 goals in just eight league matches this term. They tend to be a threat going forward.
Liverpool’s unbeaten run across all competitions came to an abrupt end on Sunday as Manchester City ran out 3-0 winners at Anfield.

The Reds fielded a weakened XI with Cody Gakpo, Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai all ruled out. They initially did well before Ryan Gravenberch’s red card resulted in a collapse with the away side scoring three goals across a 15 minute period.

Prior to that, Liverpool hadn’t been that convincing but they’d been picking up wins. Andoni Iraola was trying to bed in a new system as well as fresh faces and he’d yet to strike a balance. He had, however, made the Reds a lot more resilient in the interim. They’d kept three clean sheets on the bounce in the Premier League before City ran riot. They’ve also managed to overturn a 1-0 deficit against Atlético Madrid in their Champions League opener.
Their bubble has now burst though and there’s going to be a big focus on how Iraola and his players react, especially given it’s a game they should be winning on Wednesday.

Though he’s yet to score this season, a big player for LASK could well be former Wolves striker Saša Kalajdžić. He made his first start of the season for the Austrian side over the weekend and he completed 87 minutes. He had a decent international break, scoring and assisting for Austria. The 29-year-old is 6 ft 7 in and will cause issues for Virgil van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet, despite their aerial dominance. The only question is whether or not the 29-cap international will start the game or whether he’ll be used as an impact sub. Regardless, he’s got the quality to change the game for the hosts.

For Liverpool, the focus will, once again, be on Florian Wirtz. He struggled against Manchester City and there are calls for him to be dropped. European football suits the German playmaker and it might be an ideal opportunity for him to play his way back into some sort of form for the Reds.

LASK are expected to be without Ramiz Harakaté but he would be the only absentee for the home side. Liverpool, meanwhile, are expected to still be without Isak, Gakpo and Szoboszlai for the trip. Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley are all definitely ruled out meaning Iraola’s hands are tied in some key positions.
We’re going with a narrow 2-1 win for Liverpool, a Champions League confidence builder for a depleted Reds side.

          Clásico Win, Sky-High Team Spirit, and Real Madrid in the Title Race: José Mourinho is Back
        
      
                          
                      Oct 26, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Against the odds, José Mourinho took Real Madrid to Camp Nou and came away with a much-deserved win. The title race is on in La Liga.
Sunday’s Clásico wasn’t quite, well, a classic, in the context of this storied fixture’s history.
But it was still an encapsulating affair from start to finish, largely because this was two high-quality teams, both of whom went all out to win the match.

In normal circumstances, José Mourinho, returning to this fixture for the first time in more than 13 years, might have set up not to lose. After Raphinha’s equaliser on the hour mark, there might have been a flurry of substitutions to shut up shop and avoid a loss that would have opened up a surely unassailable nine-point gap to Barcelona.

But the Real Madrid manager knew even a draw here wasn’t really enough. A win was needed to close the gap to three points and breathe life into a title race that, given Barcelona had won La Liga for the last two seasons and Madrid had lost two of their opening seven games, threatened to turn into a procession before we even reached November.

But in the face of all that pressure and widespread doubts about his suitability for another role at one of the biggest clubs in the world because he hasn’t won a league title since the 2014-15 Premier League with Chelsea, the 63-year-old stood up. There was nothing about Madrid’s performance at Camp Nou, where Barcelona had not failed to win a single game since their return there a year ago, that suggested any fear of losing.

Mourinho proved his doubters categorically wrong with a daring display of attacking intent and a fully deserved win that extended his unbeaten run in Clásicos to six games (W4 D2) in all competitions. He is only the third Madrid manager ever to achieve that feat, after Miguel Muñoz (1962-1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001-2003).

He is a different person and different manager these days, but this win was classic Mourinho. There was a full acknowledgement of the quality their opponents possessed and little attempt to beat them at their own game: Madrid had just 37.8% of the ball and their threat was almost entirely based around swift, direct breaks upfield.

Madrid put together four direct attacks – quick breaks up the pitch that end with a shot or a touch in the opposition’s box – against Barcelona on Sunday night. That is two fewer than Barcelona’s first nine opponents in La Liga had managed combined (six) this season. Madrid progressed up the pitch an average of 15.1 metres with each passing sequence, which was by far the most anyone has managed against Barça this season.

They did this almost exclusively through the wide areas, playing almost no passes straight through the middle of the pitch, but instead getting the ball out to Arda Güler on the right or, more often, Yan Diomande on the left to drive forwards before either shooting or putting a low ball across goal.

Both Madrid goals came from balls into the channel: first for Diomande to chase and square for Kylian Mbappé (via a big slice of luck through a failed Gerard Martín clearance) and later for substitute Eduardo Camavinga to race down the right and pull the ball back for Mbappé's 87th-minute winner.

Mourinho has always meticulously tailored his game plans depending on the opponent, and he is clearly not doing things any differently these days. There was an awareness that Lamine Yamal would not track back as hard as another winger might, and a focus on attacking down that flank as a result. Madrid had 45.4% of their attacking touches down the left flank.

The teenage Diomande, who has grown into his role since his big-money summer move, was a constant threat, shining once again in the absence of the suspended Vinícius Júnior, who, as it happens, may not have worked as hard without the ball as his understudy. After this display, it will be fascinating to see how Mourinho handles the Brazilian's return given there’s certainly an argument they have looked a more complete team without him. Two-goal match-winner Mbappé insisted afterwards that this was “a team victory”.

“If we want to achieve things this year, we have to do it as a group and as a team because the quality is here,” he said. “When you see the players we have, anyone who says there’s no quality is lying. But we have to do everything as a team and as a group because that’s how we’re going to achieve the things we want to achieve.”

The collective endeavour showed a level of buy-in to what Mourinho is doing that bodes well for a team who have gone two years without winning a single major trophy – since Mbappé signed, coincidentally or not. The last time they went three years without one, Mourinho was still enjoying his first spell at Chelsea.

There was also the inevitable sprinkling of underhanded play that was always going to be present for a Mourinho-led Madrid team playing in a Clásico, with two players who joined alongside him this summer front and centre.

Marc Cucurella was tasked with keeping Spain teammate Yamal quiet and he largely did an exceptional job, although fouls were a common sight. He made the joint-most fouls of any player on the pitch (four), along with the other main protagonist, Bernardo Silva.

Silva was handed his first start in La Liga since 12 September and was a cool, calming presence in front of the Madrid defence, a big-game player who was in no way overawed by the magnitude of the occasion, completing 91.7% of his passes while also breaking up play well, legally or not.
Perhaps most impressive about either of Cucurella or Silva’s performances was the fact they played a combined 170 minutes and both avoided bookings.

Madrid and Mourinho will know they need to be sensible. They can’t glean too much from this single result. They remain three points off top spot and are even still behind city rivals Atlético in the table, too. There’s loads of work still to be done.

                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Barcelona's winning start to the season is over after defeat in a Champions League thriller. Look back on the action with our PSG vs Barcelona stats page.
Vítinha and Fabián Ruiz struck in the last 10 minutes at the Parc des Princes to clinch Paris Saint-Germain a 4-2 win and end Barcelona’s perfect start to the season.
Both sides were guilty of wasting chances on Tuesday, but Désiré Doué gave PSG a half-time lead that Xavi Espart cancelled out early in the second half.
After Lamine Yamal then levelled after Lucas Hernández had put the reigning champions back in front, Vitinha and Fabian both scored late on to settle a Champions League thriller.

PSG almost got off to a dream start as Pedri was caught in possession and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Ousmane Dembélé latched onto the rebound and blazed wide of the empty net, but the offside flag spared his blushes.
Ferran Torres – an early replacement after Dembélé pulled up holding his hamstring – was played in behind Barcelona's defence, but Joan García was equal to his former teammate's scuffed volley.
And García's inspired form continued as he again denied Ferran from point-blank range before getting back to his feet to push away Fabián's bouncing volley.
The breakthrough came in the 38th minute, as João Neves cut out Yamal's dinked pass from defence, and Doué skipped away from his marker to curl past García.
Fermín López should have equalised a few moments later, but Matvey Safonov stood his ground to block the chip when one-on-one.
PSG started the second half on top as well, with Doué picking out the unmarked Achraf Hakimi, who could only aim his first-time effort at García.
Barcelona punished their hosts' profligacy in the 55th minute as a lovely flowing team move resulted in Fermín sliding in Espart to drill past Safonov.
But momentum was soon back with PSG. Ferran struck the post from close range, and from the next corner, Doué picked out Hernández to head past the helpless García.

Barcelona were not done yet. Yamal dragged them level with a piece of individual brilliance, rifling into the roof of the net from a tight angle after bursting past Warren Zaïre-Emery – who'd initially gifted him possession – with 11 minutes to go.

But Vitinha restored PSG’s advantage two minutes later; Hakimi's cross was only half cleared by Gerard Martín, and Vitinha smashed home from the edge of the box after chesting the ball down for himself.
Fabián made sure of all three points in the 86th minute, Hakimi's deflected cross finding the unmarked Spaniard for a tap-in.

If this fixture promised one thing, it was goals. The previous 15 European/Cup Champions League meetings between these sides saw a combined 57 goals scored, and this one arguably should have had even more than the six it produced.
PSG dominated the first half and got 10 of their 12 shots on target, the highest number of attempts on target Barcelona have faced before the break in the competition since at least 2003-04.
Despite being on the losing side, García proved a key part of Flick's side as he made 10 saves in total.
Flick's side have been the ones to beat in 2026-27, but their perfect record across all competitions has now ended – they had won all of their previous 11 games while scoring 50 goals.
The two teams combined for 40 shots (22 for PSG, 18 for Barça) and had 11 Opta-defined ‘big' chances between them (six for PSG, five for Barcelona).

          Diego Gómez, Brighton and the Rise in Premier League Shots from the Halfway Line
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz, Jonathan Manuel / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After Diego Gómez’s goal against Crystal Palace, Brighton are closing in on the Premier League record for shots from 50 metres or more in a season. So, we ask: why?

It’s impossible to know whether the increased adoption of expected goals is the sole reason, part of the reason, or plays no part whatsoever, but it's intriguing that the metric’s popularity has coincided almost perfectly with shots being taken closer to goal.

Perhaps this would have happened regardless of the advancement of football analytics. As coaching improved and became more detailed, teams may well have trained to get the ball closer to goal simply because what xG tells us is already obvious: the closer to goal you shoot from, the more likely you are to score.

Whatever the reason, though, the data proves Premier League football has been based less around shooting from long distance in recent years. The first six seasons for which this data is available (from 2003-04) are the six highest for the proportion of shots taken from outside the penalty area. They are the only seasons on record that have seen more than 45% of shots attempted from range.

And the five most recent, from 2022-23 to 2026-27, have produced the lowest numbers of all seasons on record, each seeing 35% or fewer shots attempted from outside the penalty area. That fits with what we’d expect, given the aforementioned focus on getting the ball closer to goal.

Whether they have been the main driving force behind the change, data-savvy clubs have played a big role. Thomas Frank spoke about “making the chance bigger” while in charge of Brentford, and for three seasons running, his side were among the Premier League’s top two teams for the average xG value of each shot they attempted.

In other words, Brentford, a club known for and who have had huge success with their data-led approach, consistently waited patiently for opportunities to create high-quality chances rather than shooting from long range.

Doing so is the sign of a good team. Teams who can work the ball closer to goal to “make the chance bigger” are going to be able to score goals more reliably. Shooting from distance is a high-risk strategy that has become increasingly unpopular over the years because it is less likely to bring reward.

However, Brighton, another of the Premier League’s most noteworthy and successful proponents of a heavily data-led approach in both their recruitment and their tactics, appear to be bucking the trend.

Diego Gómez’s remarkable strike in the 5-0 win over Crystal Palace on Sunday was struck from 51.3 metres out, putting it eighth on the list of Premier League goals scored from furthest out over the period for which this data is available (from 2006-07).
Eight of the other nine goals were scored nine seasons or more ago. And when it comes to the players to take the most shots from more than 50m, Charlie Adam is miles clear at the top.

The fact he is so far clear, with 25 attempts, and the kind of names alongside him on this list shows how much more common shooting from this distance was in a different time. It’s not something teams have tended to do in recent years.
In the days of Adam, these were largely pot shots that were perhaps a little ill-advised; his Blackpool side attempted a record nine in 2010-11 without hitting the target even once, for example.

But could it be the case that there is some consideration to Gómez’s attempts? It’s certainly curious he is doing it for a team as data focused as Brighton. Little that the club does happens by chance, after all.

Interestingly, most of the shots from distance this season have been by Brighton players. Of the 14 attempted from 50 metres or more in the Premier League in 2026-27, six have been by Brighton players. That’s 42.9%. They account for 6.5% of all shots from anywhere on the pitch.
Their total of six shots from 50m+ just seven games into 2026-27 is already the second-highest total by a team on record in a Premier League season, behind that Blackpool team mentioned above.
So, is there something else at play here? Have Brighton’s analysts spotted an opportunity from which they are trying to gain an edge. Is there a plan in place to threaten from very long range?
Manager Fabian Hürzeler was asked about the topic after Gómez’s goal on Sunday and was unequivocal in his response. “We don't train shots from 50 metres,” he said.

This kind of attempt must have some degree of opportunism around it, and some of Brighton’s long-range shots are particularly optimistic attempts to take advantage of an out-of-position goalkeeper. One example is Chema Andrés’ attempt against Arsenal when David Raya was way out of his goal after sweeping up.
But the numbers we’ve just looked at suggest there may be some instruction – or at the very least, an allowance – for Brighton players to try scoring from far out in normal play.
