          Women's Champions League: Five Subplots Ahead of Matchday 3
        
      
                          
                      Oct 27, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The UEFA Women's Champions League returns for Matchday 3 on Wednesday evening. What should you be keeping an eye on? We discuss the subplots ahead of this week's action.
The UEFA Women's Champions League returns this week and, with only six games in the league phase, Matchday 3 already represents the halfway point for Europe's elite.

Barcelona have made a flying start, winning both of their opening matches and scoring 11 goals in the process. They are the only side with maximum points, but behind them, the race for direct qualification to the quarter-finals is harder to call.
Chelsea and Arsenal have four points apiece, while Manchester City, Bayern München and OL Lyonnes are also unbeaten after two matches, albeit with City down in 10th after two draws.
According to the Opta supercomputer, Barcelona are overwhelming favourites to secure a top-four finish, while Arsenal and Manchester City already appear slightly up against it.
Let's dive into five key talking points ahead of MD3.

Alessia Russo is closing in on a place in the history books, with Arsenal’s clash against Benfica offering the England striker an opportunity to draw level with Fran Kirby as the highest-scoring English player in the history of the Champions League.
Russo has scored 20 goals in the UWCL, leaving her just one short of Kirby’s record of 21.

Although unbeaten so far, the Gunners have made an unconvincing start to the league phase. A late penalty secured a 1-0 victory over HB Køge on Matchday 1, before they surrendered a two-goal advantage to draw 2-2 with Paris FC.

Those performances have come amid an unusually subdued attacking start domestically. Arsenal have scored just seven goals in their opening seven WSL matches, with only five coming from open play. It's a modest return for a side who usually rank among the competition’s most prolific attacks, and Renée Slegers will be keen to build on the momentum of their North London Derby victory over Tottenham.

There are reasons for optimism here. Arsenal have won each of their last six home matches in the Champions League and scored in 15 consecutive group-stage or league-phase games in the competition. Benfica, meanwhile, have gone 10 European matches without keeping a clean sheet.
Russo also scored against the Portuguese side in Arsenal’s 2-0 victory in Lisbon last season, making them a familiar opponent as she approaches the landmark.

The Opta supercomputer gives Arsenal just a 28.7% chance of finishing in the top four and qualifying directly for the quarter-finals, projecting a final league-phase total of 10.4 points. With automatic qualification far from assured, securing maximum points against Benfica could prove crucial to their European ambitions.
Some might even argue that Arsenal’s most viable route to qualifying for next season’s Champions League could be to win the competition itself.
Chelsea’s pursuit of a first Champions League title continues, and it's underpinned by a remarkable level of consistency in the competition’s league/group phase.

The Blues have lost just one of their 32 group-stage matches in the competition, winning 23 and drawing eight. They are currently unbeaten in 26 consecutive games at this stage, a run stretching back to December 2021.
Their home record is even more formidable. Chelsea have never lost a group-stage or league-phase match on home soil, winning 12 and drawing four of their 16 fixtures.
They have carried that reliability into the current campaign, opening with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Austria Wien, before grinding out a goalless draw away to European heavyweights Lyon.

Despite dropping points in France, Chelsea remain well placed to progress directly to the quarter-finals. The Opta supercomputer gives them a 76.6% chance of finishing in the top four, projecting a final league-phase total of 13.13 points.
Chelsea’s wait for their first European crown goes on, but their consistency at this stage of the competition continues to provide a strong platform for another serious challenge.

          Five Knee-Jerk Reactions to Premier League 2026-27 Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re back with our weekly dose of knee-jerk reactions to the weekend’s Premier League action.
Every week here on Opta Analyst, we do something we don’t normally do and come to a load of conclusions based on just a single round of Premier League matches.
We usually rely on large data sets to make our judgements, but in this weekly column we react quickly and maybe a little too hastily.
It’s all a bit of fun, and many of our five reactions for this week will swiftly prove to be nothing more than exactly what we called them: knee-jerk.
But some might just hold up in the weeks to come. Read on to see which way you think these week’s conclusions will eventually go.

Coming into Matchday 5, it felt like there was no stopping Arsenal. They’d won all four Premier League games, as well as three more in other competitions, and few of their opponents had caused them any real problems at all.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side had produced some impressive results early in the season, but nobody expected them to blow Arsenal away quite like they did on Saturday.

They pressed the champions with a vicious and suffocating relentlessness that meant Arsenal just could not get any kind of grip on the game. Brighton forced a colossal 15 high turnovers (winning possession within 40 metres of the opposition's goal line), which is the second most by any team in the Premier League this season, behind only Brighton against an Aston Villa side who played most of that game with just 10 men (19).

They also recognised how difficult it is to carve out clear-cut chances against this Arsenal side, so shot on sight, often from distance. They scored twice from range to take Arsenal’s total to a league-high three goals conceded from outside the box this season.

Was this the blueprint for how to take the champions down, or a mere – and very natural – day off for the best team in the world right now? We’ll see if anyone else can do this to them after they’ve gathered their thoughts during the international break.
Some say you make your own luck, but there’s no denying that Spurs have been incredibly fortunate not to be relegated in the last two utterly dismal seasons.

In 2024-25, they were entirely reliant on the dreadful form of the promoted sides, who were so bad that there was never really a relegation battle of any sort. Then, last season, they escaped by the skin of their teeth after failing to address their myriad of problems in either transfer window.

Now, five games into 2026-27 and after a summer of upheaval, they are bottom of the table and staring at the very real possibility of another flirtation with the drop despite spending more than £300 million.

They have a lot of talent in their squad now, and certainly appear to have more potential, particularly in attack, than they did last term. Against Aston Villa on Saturday, they created more than enough, notably when the game was still level, to take control of the game, but failed to take their chances and were punished in brutal fashion. They won on xG but remain winless in actuality, with just two points from five games and a goal difference of -6.
It is now their worst ever start to a Premier League season and has left them with a lot of improving to do to avoid the possibility of another 17th-place finish – or worse.

We’ve learned over the last two years that nothing can be taken for granted with this club, and with no other team looking anything like as hopeless so far this season, there is every chance they get themselves into yet more trouble.
Brian Brobbey isn’t the most fashionable of footballers, and his physical approach to the game may mean he never gets the chance to play for a big-six club.

But even if he doesn’t play for a Champions League club that never lifts the ball off the floor and always has more than 60% possession, there is absolutely no denying what a handful he is. He deserves far more respect than many give him.

In Sunderland’s defeat to Manchester City this weekend, he scored three times from just five shots and became only the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler vs Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt vs Manchester United in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku vs United in May 2013.

He was extremely unfortunate to also end up on the losing side, too, becoming the sixth player ever to score a hat-trick and lose a Premier League game, and the first since Roque Santa Cruz for Blackburn vs Wigan in December 2007.

2c7hipzzm7ng1hwkildq0rgj2.title: Leverkusen aiming to build on European win against leaders Freiburg
2c7hipzzm7ng1hwkildq0rgj2.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen and Freiburg have both enjoyed strong starts to their Bundesliga campaign, and they square off at the BayArena this Sunday.
paragraphs: Carles Martinez described Bayer Leverkusen's 4-0 victory over Lech Poznan as an "important win" ahead of facing Bundesliga leaders Freiburg this Sunday.
Leverkusen made it two wins from two to begin their Europa League campaign, with Patrik Schick's fine form in 2026-27 continuing with two first-half penalties.
Malik Tillman had opened the scoring in the 32nd minute before Schick notched his brace, and Ibrahim Maza sealed the win late on for Martinez's side at Enea Stadion.
But now Leverkusen's attention turns to the Bundesliga, with surprise league leaders Freiburg the visitors to the BayArena in what is set to be an entertaining encounter.
Leverkusen are fourth in the table after last week's thrilling 4-3 win away to Mainz, with just three points separating the top four in the table heading into MD6.
Martinez is hoping his team's victory in the Europa League will serve as a timely confidence booster against Freiburg, highlighting the importance of rebuilding their energy.
"That was an important win, for our confidence and for the team spirit. We want to carry on exactly like this and keep pushing ourselves further," Martinez told reporters.
"The important thing now is to build up our energy, both mentally and physically, for Sunday."

When asked about Afonso Moreira, who missed a big chance in Poland shortly before the final whistle and was immediately consoled by his team-mates, Martinez continued: "A very good example of our team spirit. Our club culture, where we act as a group and a family, is brilliant.
"You always have to pull together if you want to be successful. Of course, there's always room for improvement. But you have to approach that with self-confidence.
"Knowing that these are just minor details, and that, overall, a great deal is going well and on the right track. That mindset is important to me."
Martinez did, however, acknowledge the difficulties of facing Freiburg, who sit level with Borussia Dortmund on 13 points at the summit.

The key to their strong start has been consistency, with Freiburg naming the same starting line-up in each of their last four Bundesliga matches and making only one change to their XI all season, which is fewer than any other team.
However, they are forced into a change against Leverkusen following the suspension of Yuito Suzuki, who is their top scorer in the Bundesliga this season with four goals.

2dyldap4a9cf1e36lzhpuggso.title: Union Berlin 0-0 Borussia Dortmund: Kovac's side frustrated in second straight draw
2dyldap4a9cf1e36lzhpuggso.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund played out a draw for the second weekend running in the Bundesliga, with both sides struggling for clear-cut chances.
paragraphs: Borussia Dortmund extended their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season, but they were frustrated in a 0-0 draw with Union Berlin.
Niko Kovac's side temporarily moved top of the table, but they missed a chance to pile some real pressure on Freiburg and Bayern Munich following their second straight draw.
Both sides struggled to create clear-cut chances in the first half, with Tim Skarke and Janik Haberer both firing wide for Union.
Dortmund threatened just before the break with some lovely one-touch link-up play down the left, but Ethan Nwaneri could not finish it off, firing straight at Frederik Ronnow.
Dortmund upped the pressure after the break as Maximilian Beier got in front of his marker to meet Julian Ryerson's cross, but he volleyed wide under no pressure.
Skarke and Nwaneri both fired wide at either end as both sides continued to toil and the match became increasingly gritty.
Serhou Guirassy had two late chances to find a winner, but he awkwardly volleyed straight at Ronnow before his off-target header hit Mathis Albert, only to bounce narrowly wide.
Union and Dortmund forgot their shooting boots
Despite both teams getting into good positions in the final third, this was a match that lacked quality.
Union and Dortmund combined for 23 shots (11 for the hosts, 12 for BVB), but the visitors were responsible for the only two shots on target, with Union failing to test Gregor Kobel.
Kovac's side have enjoyed another strong start in the Bundesliga, just as they did last season, but BVB have stalled somewhat since the international break.

They conceded two late goals against Werder Bremen last weekend, but they at least showed off their defensive strengths at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei as they kept their fourth clean sheet of the Bundesliga season.
It was a second consecutive shutout for Union, who have conceded the second-most goals in the top flight, and Mauro Lustrinelli will certainly be the happier of the two managers.

2iv9ayqx2ee31fvr9tnwso0b8.title: Como 0-0 Roma: Visitors miss chance to go top after Malen's red card
2iv9ayqx2ee31fvr9tnwso0b8.subtitle: Roma saw Donyell Malen sent off early in the second half, and Como failed to capitalise on their numerical advantage in a goalless draw.
paragraphs: Roma missed the chance to go back to the top of the Serie A table as Donyell Malen was sent off in a 0-0 draw with Como.
Both sides had chances in a lively first half, but Malen's late challenge and resulting sending-off put Roma on the back foot, though Como could not find a late winner.
Jean Butez held Paulo Dybala's tame first-time shot before Nico Paz went down the other end and attempted to chip Pierluigi Gollini, who smothered the chance.
And the end-to-end opening continued as Lorenzo Pellegrini dug out a curler on the edge of the box, but it clipped the outside of the right post.
Maxence Caqueret piled the pressure on Gianluca Mancini, who could not get any purchase on his clearance, but the Frenchman fizzed his low effort narrowly wide.
Malen then raced onto a long ball to round Butez, but the angle was against him on the right of the box, and he could only find the side netting.

The Dutchman's game came to an end in the 53rd minute; he held off two challenges during a driving run through Como's half but then leapt into a tackle on Kaiki after losing control of the ball, and the referee went straight to his pocket for the red card.

Como aimed to make their numerical advantage count. Maximo Perrone blazed over, and Tasos Douvikas lashed into the side netting before Gollini acrobatically kept out Paz's snap-shot from the edge of the box.
Cesc Fabregas' side kept pushing, with Jesus Rodriguez drilling a low strike just past the post as Como had to settle for a point.
Roma's attack blunted as Malen walks
Coming into this match, Roma were the second-highest scorers in Serie A this term, but for the first time this season, they were shut out.

They were on top in the first half, having seven shots to Como's five, though both sides only managed to get one of those on target, and Gian Piero Gasperini, who is on the brink of 300 wins in Serie A, would have been confident of turning the screw after the break.
However, Malen received his first red card in the top 10 European leagues (in his 234th match) for a needless challenge, piling the pressure on Roma.
Como ultimately dominated the closing stages, finishing the game with 19 shots worth 1.48 expected goals (xG), but Gollini was largely comfortable keeping them at bay.

While the attacking play was sometimes lacking, both teams continue to show their defensive strengths; among the teams present in Serie A over the last two seasons, Roma (34) and Como (35) have conceded the fewest goals in the tournament during this period.

This is the first draw between the sides in 11 meetings, with the previous stalemate between them coming all the way back in January 1987. And it is the first 0-0 draw in the current Serie A season (match number 54).
It also means Roma missed the chance to leapfrog Inter back to the top of Serie A, sitting two points behind the leaders, while Como sit in sixth.

2ncvj5vcyw7n1ml6kanm08jnc.title: Klopp aiming to 'bring German football back to where we all want it to be'
2ncvj5vcyw7n1ml6kanm08jnc.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp is still rebuilding with Germany after just two games, and he will be keen to get his first win in charge against Serbia.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp says his focus remains on "bringing German football back to where we all want it to be" as he continues his search for a first win in charge.
Klopp's side have made a winless start to their Nations League campaign, drawing 1-1 with the Netherlands before they suffered a surprise 1-0 defeat to Greece.
No Germany head coach has ever failed to win each of their first three matches in charge.
Next up for Germany is a clash with Serbia, and Klopp will get the chance to see his second squad of players across the last two games of this international break.
"We will build a team that can cause problems for all teams," Klopp said.
"We're just getting started in this process. We are all interested in bringing German football back to where we all want it to be."
While Germany sit third in Group A2 with one point, Serbia prop up the table having lost their opening two matches against Greece and the Netherlands by 2-1 scorelines.
Serbia faced 51 shots across those two matches, and despite their recent struggles, Klopp is still confident they will provide a stern test for Germany.
"Serbia's approach won't be much different from what Greece did," Klopp said of their opponents.
"What makes Serbia particularly difficult to play against is their experience. They also have some excellent footballers. They know all the tricks of the trade, so we have to be prepared for that.
"They have a special mentality. It's not the best period in Serbian football at the moment, but the players themselves know what's at stake and have fought for one another.
"An opponent that sits deep is a major challenge for any team, at any stage of development."
While Klopp did not confirm who would act as captain in Joshua Kimmich's absence – with the 31-year-old only included in the first squad – he did disclose one starter.
Jonas Urbig will make his senior team debut on Thursday, and the goalkeeper is excited to get his first cap.
"I found out in training and was, of course, very happy," he said.
"It will be a very special moment for me."

2snnj539arg718opngf6xnb2k.title: Feyenoord 3-2 Como: Hadj Moussa denies Fabregas' men in Champions League
2snnj539arg718opngf6xnb2k.subtitle: Despite taking the lead at Stadion Feijenoord, Como fell to a narrow defeat against Feyenoord in the Champions League on matchday two.
paragraphs: Anis Hadj Moussa starred for Feyenoord as they defeated Como 3-2 in the Champions League.

After Gjivai Zechiel quickly cancelled out Assane Diao's opener in the first half at Stadion Feijenoord, Hadj Moussa put his side ahead early in the second half before playing a key role in Robert Sanchez's own goal late on.
Como were ahead after just 18 minutes through Diao, who shrugged off a challenge from Javi Lopez after getting on the end of a long ball from Jacobo Ramon before curling past Tjark Ernst.
However, Feyenoord were level less than three minutes later. Luciano Valente fired a pass into Zechiel, who received on the swivel before thundering in a strike from the edge of the box.

Sanchez was on hand to deny Lopez's close-range header on the stroke of half-time, but the Como goalkeeper could not keep out Hadj Moussa seven minutes after the restart as the winger caught the Spaniard out at his near post.
Cesc Fabregas turned to his bench and nearly found an equaliser through Tasos Douvikas, who headed over while completely unmarked, while another substitute in Lucas Da Cunha fired straight at Ernst.

Hadj Moussa saw an effort tipped onto the post by Sanchez in the 80th minute, but just 69 seconds later, the Feyenoord man saw his shot deflected onto the post by Ramon, and the ball then ricocheted in off Sanchez.
Douvikas did force a nervy final minute after Feyenoord failed to clear a long ball from Ramon, allowing the Greek striker to score at the near post, but the Dutch side held on for the victory.
Feyenoord back on track in Europe

Feyenoord were thrashed 5-1 by Barcelona in their league phase opener this season, but Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side got into the win column with a clinical display against Como, which was inspired by Hadj Moussa.
The 24-year-old recorded more shots than any other player (five), while he completed the most dribbles of any Feyenoord player (two) and recorded the most touches in the opposition box (10).

His heroics helped Feyenoord come from behind to win a home game in the Champions League for just the second time, after their 2-1 victory over Napoli in December 2017, with manager Van Bronckhorst also in charge on that occasion.
Feyenoord have now scored 31 goals in their first 10 matches of a season across all competitions for the first time since 1995-96 (also 31), while Como have lost their second match this season.

Fabregas' team won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.24 to 0.54 despite recording fewer shots (11 to 13), but they were left too open at the back, while Diao's injury in the first half also made a noticeable impact.

2t2aun4dnboh1lmsv3ka22z8u.title: Augsburg 2-2 Bayern Munich: Neuer's blushes spared by late Brown equaliser
2t2aun4dnboh1lmsv3ka22z8u.subtitle: Manuel Neuer had a day to forget as Bayern Munich could only draw with Augsburg, with Nathaniel Brown coming to the rescue late on.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich twice came from behind to preserve their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season as Manuel Neuer's errors proved costly in a 2-2 draw against Augsburg.
Robin Fellhauer scored the Bundesliga's fastest-ever goal following a mistake from Neuer, though Ismael Saibari hauled the champions back level in the 55th minute on Saturday.
Augsburg hit back when another blunder from Neuer handed Rodrigo Ribeiro a simple finish, but Nathaniel Brown came off the bench to score the leveller in the 80th minute.

No sooner had Bayern got things underway at WWK Arena, they found themselves behind. Neuer aimed to recover from his loose touch with an attempted chip, only for Fellhauer to steal possession and roll the ball home after just eight seconds.
Augsburg should have doubled their lead in the 35th minute when a corner made it to Chrislain Matsima, but he skewed his effort behind from two yards out.

Harry Kane then turned Aleksandar Pavlovic's teasing cross onto the woodwork in the final action of the first half, and Bayern thought they had got themselves level six minutes after the restart when Luis Diaz acrobatically volleyed Saibari's cross into the net.
But Finn Dahmen, who saw Diaz's effort squirm under his grasp, had his blushes spared after the goal was ruled out for an offside earlier in the build-up.
However, the visitors did find their equaliser soon after, with Saibari sweeping into the bottom-left corner from Kane's pass.
Yet Augsburg regained their lead nine minutes later through Ribeiro, who finished from close range after Neuer failed to deal with Calvin Brackelmann's shot from range.

Bayern were then denied a second twice by the assistant's flag. First, Serge Gnabry tucked home Kane's cross, though the England captain had strayed just beyond the Augsburg defence, before Diaz had a second goal chalked off after Alphonso Davies collected possession in an offside position.
But Vincent Kompany's team restored parity for a second time when Kane's centre was turned in by Brown, and Bayern had their chances to snatch all three points.
Gnabry had the best of them, seeing a goal disallowed and also hitting the post.
Neuer's landmark day soured by errors

2y2lr7p8tlb11htx9bg38gumv.title: Martinez hails Leverkusen's passion in DFB-Pokal comeback
2y2lr7p8tlb11htx9bg38gumv.subtitle: Despite finding themselves 2-0 down to second-tier FC Nurnberg, Bayer Leverkusen turned things around to progress in the DFB-Pokal.
paragraphs: Carles Martinez lauded his Bayer Leverkusen side after they "showed a lot of passion" in their DFB-Pokal victory over FC Nurnberg.
Nurnberg threatened to cause an upset at BayArena after goals from Rafael Lubach and Sigurd Haugen saw the second-tier side take a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes.
However, Edmond Tapsoba scored either side of half-time before goals from Patrik Schick, Jonas Hofmann and Lucas Vazquez secured a 5-2 win and a spot in the last 16.
Tapsoba scored his first brace for the club in what was his 282nd Leverkusen appearance, while Aleix Garcia contributed with two assists.
It was a dominant performance from Leverkusen, who accumulated 3.07 expected goals (xG) from 25 shots, six of which were Opta-defined big chances.
"We didn't get off to the start we wanted," said Martinez.
"Nurnberg played brilliantly. But I'm very pleased with the second half. We didn’t lose belief in ourselves and we turned the game around.
"The players did a good job and showed a lot of passion. I particularly liked that!"
Along with his goal, Hofmann recorded more shots than any other player (five) and created the most chances (five).
Despite their slow start, the midfielder took pride in Leverkusen's resilience.
"We faced a strong opponent," said Hofmann.
"Although we had chances of our own, we didn't manage to get a foothold in the first half as we would have liked.
"However, Eddy's goal just before half-time gave us the chance to get back into the game. We didn't let our heads drop. That was important.
"You really feel the connection with the fans. It's absolutely brilliant. I couldn't stop smiling [after scoring]."

2yffltvwa5kz1bc6i3oz1pawx.title: Sarr's move to Liverpool was 'never going to happen', says Parish
2yffltvwa5kz1bc6i3oz1pawx.subtitle: Ismaila Sarr was the subject of interest from Liverpool this summer, but the reported £50m bid fell way below Crystal Palace's valuation.
paragraphs: Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish said Ismaila Sarr's proposed summer switch was "never going to happen" due to a huge gap in valuation of the Crystal Palace forward.
Sarr was linked with a late move to Liverpool in the transfer window, with the Reds aiming to strengthen the right side of their attack following Mohamed Salah's departure.
The Senegal international registered 22 goal involvements (21 goals, one assist) for Palace in all competitions last term, leading them to the Conference League title.
He has netted 33 goals and provided eight assists in 94 appearances across all competitions for Palace since joining them in 2024, earning him interest from Liverpool.
Sarr was reportedly the subject of a £50m bid from Andoni Iraola's side, a figure Parish said Palace did not consider remotely sufficient to sanction a departure to Anfield.
"It's unfortunate for Ismaila, but that wasn't really a situation that was of our doing," Parish told The Athletic.
"A club came in and, with the amount of money they bid, they couldn't seriously think in that market it was going to get done at that level.
"If you're selling players for £90m, and then you want to bid us half of that for the replacement, it's fine, you can do it. But it's never going to happen."
Liverpool's move for Sarr came after failing in their attempt to sign Brighton's Yankuba Minteh, while they also attempted to lure Yan Diomande and Ibrahim Mbaye to Anfield.
Sarr had also attracted interest from Turkiye earlier in the window, with Palace rejecting an offer reportedly worth around £26m from Galatasaray.

He had made a habit of scoring against Liverpool, too. Since the 2019-20 season, only Ollie Watkins and Erling Haaland (both eight) have netted more goals in all competitions against the Reds than Sarr (seven).
Palace remain in a strong negotiating position should Liverpool or another club renew their interest, given he has three years remaining on his current contract.
Sarr missed Palace's first four games of the 2026-27 campaign because of a groin injury, but has since returned for their win over Lech Poznan and draw with Leeds United.

          Liverpool vs Brighton Prediction: Premier League Preview

We look ahead to this Premier League match at Anfield with our Liverpool vs Brighton prediction and preview. Can the Seagulls continue their impressive form?
Liverpool will hope their new-found momentum will help them stop Brighton & Hove Albion in their tracks when they meet in the Premier League on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola's side bounced back from a 3-0 loss at home to Manchester City after the international break by coming from behind to beat Brentford 2-1 last weekend. The goals from Víctor Muñoz and Alexander Isak arrived after the Bees were reduced to 10 men at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The Reds backed that up by beating Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. That time they had to recover from two goals down, but still managed to seal a 4-3 victory that kept their 100% record in Europe this season intact.

Villarreal boss Iñigo Pérez acknowledged that the Anfield atmosphere played a role in his team's capitulation, even though it has not been quite as much of a fortress for Liverpool in the Premier League.

They are winless in their last five Premier League home matches (D4 L1), their only worse runs at Anfield being a seven-game stretch from November 2002 to February 2003 and an eight-game streak between December 2020 and March 2021.

Florian Wirtz has been a target for criticism for a perceived lack of threat, but the Germany international has created the most chances both overall (20) and from open play (18) in the Premier League this season, while he came off the bench to score his first goal of the season on Tuesday.

Isak finally appears to be hitting his stride at Anfield too, having scored five goals in as many Premier League appearances. The Swede lost four of his first five games for Liverpool but they are unbeaten in his past 15 appearances (W9 D6).

Yet Brighton's recent form means that Liverpool ending their wait for a home victory in the top flight is in no way a given. Fabian Hürzeler's side have been in stunning form, leading the Premier League scoring charts and winning their past four top-flight fixtures by an aggregate score of 15-0.

That includes a 3-0 win against reigning champions Arsenal and 5-0 victories over Coventry City and rivals Crystal Palace, in which Diego Gómez scored an incredible goal from the halfway line. With two victories by at least five goals in their past four matches, Brighton have equalled the amount they managed across their prior 376 league games combined.
A much-changed line-up was held to an uneventful 0-0 draw by Jablonec in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday, ending their six-game winning run in all competitions.

But Hürzeler used the game – his 100th in charge of the club – to rest some key players. One of those was Charalampos Kostoulas, who has scored and assisted in two of his last three Premier League appearances.

Kostoulas is the first teenager to score and assist in the same game more than once in a season since Kelechi Iheanacho for City in 2016-17, and could become the first since Michael Owen in 1998-99 to do it three times.

The Greek will likely play from the start after being an unused substitute against Jablonec, but Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas, Kaoru Mitoma, Zadok Yohanna and Yankuba Minteh – reportedly a summer target for Liverpool – remain sidelined.
Mats Wieffer could recover from his knee injury in time to feature, while Femi Azeez and Pascal Struijk will also hope to play a part after missing out on Thursday.

Liverpool have slight concerns over Bradley Barcola and Muñoz, while Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai remained sidelined along with long-term absentees Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitiké.

Brighton are in a rich vein of form and have performed well against Liverpool recently, winning two of their last three Premier League meetings with the Reds – as many as they won in their first 15 encounters with them.

While the Seagulls were 2-1 winners in their most clash at the Amex Stadium in March, Liverpool beat them twice at Anfield last season – triumphing 2-0 in the Premier League in December and 3-0 in the fourth round of the FA Cup two months later.
In total, Liverpool have lost just one of their last 13 home games against Brighton in all competitions, winning each of the last four at Anfield.
Liverpool's strong recent home form against the Seagulls is likely a contributing factor in the Opta supercomputer's calculation that they have a 46.8% win probability.

32tf60szlel71myx78fb2seah.title: Amorim fumes at Milan's defensive lapse for Sassuolo equaliser
32tf60szlel71myx78fb2seah.subtitle: AC Milan were forced to settle for a point away to Sassuolo on Sunday, though Ruben Amorim believed his team should have defended better.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim was left disappointed by his AC Milan defence after Sassuolo's equaliser on Sunday, saying his team could not afford to concede the way in which they did.
Amorim's unbeaten start to life in the Milan dugout continued with a 1-1 draw at MAPEI Stadium, though it is now three stalemates in the Rossoneri's last four league games.
Milan had taken the lead in the 63rd minute when substitute Luka Modric slipped Adrien Rabiot into the box, with the French midfielder rifling in at Arijanet Muric's near post.
However, Sassuolo hit back through Cas Odenthal five minutes later, with Kristian Thorstvedt then seeing a goal ruled out late on for a foul on Goncalo Ramos in the build-up.

Milan were able to leave with a point, ensuring they remained unbeaten in each of their first six Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23. However, they have also drawn three times in their first six matchdays for the first time since 2018-19.
And Amorim was left to rue a momentary lapse in concentration which saw Odenthal sweep in from close range after Milan failed to deal with a low corner into the penalty area.

"We deserved to take the lead, but then, after the goal, we didn't control the game, and we needed to control the game with the ball," Amorim told DAZN Italia as quoted by Football Italia. "We could drop or try to defend.

"We continued to push, because the momentum was with us, but not in the right way. When we had the ball, we lost it really fast. That can happen, but what cannot happen is to concede that goal from the corner."
The introduction of Modric at half-time allowed Rabiot to play in a more advanced midfield role, and the Frenchman continued his fine run of form in front of goal.
Only Roma's Donyell Malen (six) has registered more goal involvements than Rabiot (five – three goals, two assists) in Serie A this season.
"I don't think it's about individual players, it's the rotation of the team, and they have different characteristics," Amorim said of his decision to replace Pervis Estupinan with Modric.
"You know Rabiot is going to get the ball down near the midfielders, Moreira is a completely different player in that position. Modric gave us more possession with the ball.
"But then we suffered a little more in transitions. It becomes us trying to control the game in their half and them going just for transitions, even on corners.
"I think we defended quite well man-versus-man, but when we scored, we needed to kill time a little bit, and we didn't do that."

There was a tough moment for defender Matteo Gabbia in the first half, with the Italian leaving the field on a stretcher and in tears after sustaining an injury when stretching to try and retrieve possession.
"I don't know what kind of injury Gabbia has, but I'm really sad for [him]," Amorim said of Gabbia, whose first league start of the season lasted just 20 minutes.
"Because he works really hard, he deserved his spot in the team, and then to have this situation so early is hard for him.
"We had a few weeks with no games and everyone was fit. Now we have games, we have the situation with Alexis Saelemaekers and Gabbia. We'll just have to wait and see."

333A3870481D32B531C1FD496D4DC37A.title: Can Robinson work Hampden magic against McInnes' Rangers?
333A3870481D32B531C1FD496D4DC37A.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsScottish League CupScores & FixturesTableTop ScorersScottish FootballCan Robinson work Hampden magic against McInnes' Rangers?Image source, SNSImage caption, Stephen Robinson has a good record against Derek McInnes in cup competitions
Ten months ago Stephen Robinson could have walked into a Paisley pub and expected a standing ovation and to drink for free all night.
In December the Northern Irishman masterminded St Mirren's second ever League Cup triumph, when his relentless and perfectly drilled side dismantled Celtic.
The pictures in the Hampden dressing room afterwards showed Robinson jumping and singing with his team after reaching the crowning moment of his tenure at the club.

It was an altogether different Robinson which appeared in front of the cameras on Wednesday night, after his Aberdeen side lost at home to Falkirk, the fourth time in six home league games they have failed to score.
Questioned about his future, his answers were short and deflated but he acknowledged patience with his team is wearing thin.
There would be no free drink forthcoming in the Pittodrie Bar for the Aberdeen boss after three wins in 11 to start the Premiership season.
Nonetheless, the arrival of Saturday's Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Rangers represents an opportunity to change the gloomy narrative.
Premier Sports Cup semi-final: Rangers v Aberdeen
Listen on SoundsLive commentary on BBC Radio Scotland, and follow the action on BBC Sport app and website.
Robinson was more bullish in his media conference on Friday, pointing to his Hampden record and ability to motivate players for big occassions, and he has a point.
As a manager, he is unbeaten in semi-finals at Scotland's national stadium.
He must now channel that to try to upset Rangers and overcome Derek McInnes, a familiar rival who he has bested in cup competitions before.
Last season Robinson's St Mirren knocked out McInnes' title-chasing Hearts, on penalties, in this very competition on their way to lifting the trophy.
When in charge of Motherwell in 2017-18, his team reached both national cup finals, hammering McInnes' Aberdeen 3-0 in the quarter-finals of the League Cup and the semi-finals of the Scottish Cup.
Pedro Caixinha's Rangers were beaten 2-0 in the semi-final of the former that same season.

In the League Cup semi-finals 12 months ago he constructed a gameplan to completely overrun Motherwell. One of the standout sides of last term under the innovative Jens Berthel Askou, the Steelmen were demolished 4-1 at Hampden.
Then came the crowning achievment, the 3-1 final win over Celtic which was as comprehensive a final defeat the serial trophy winners have had at Hampden in over a decade.
Robinson's ability to prevail in a one-off test should not be underestimated, and McInnes said as much this week. Beware of Robinson the underdog.
"I have done it before - every semi or final I have been in the teams that I was with, Motherwell and St Mirren, were not expected to win," Robinson said.

338esj5f88ji1bkrzypb8hkcj.title: Greece 2-2 Netherlands: Reijnders rescues late draw in hard-fought comeback
338esj5f88ji1bkrzypb8hkcj.subtitle: Despite seeing two goals disallowed in the second half, the Netherlands snatched a point at the death against a dangerous Greece side.
paragraphs: Tijjani Reijnders scored an 89th-minute equaliser as the Netherlands came back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Greece.

After stunning Germany last time out, Greece looked set to make it three wins from three in the Nations League following first-half goals from Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgos Masouras, but Virgil van Dijk and Reijnders ensured the points would be shared at Stadio Toumbas.

Greece thought they were ahead inside the opening quarter of an hour when Christos Tzolis picked out the bottom-right corner, but the strike was ruled out as Vangelis Pavlidis obstructed Bart Verbruggen's view from an offside position.
Tzolis was soon forced off with an injury, but his replacement Masouras made an immediate impact in the 23rd minute as his flick-on allowed Ioannidis to run through on goal and curl past Verbruggen.

Ioannidis then returned the favour in first-half stoppage time, regaining possession after intercepting a blind back pass from Ruben van Bommel and squaring for Masouras to tap in from close range, though Greece's decision to sit on their lead after half-time proved costly.

Van Dijk halved the deficit for the visitors with a powerful header from Joey Veerman's floated corner in the 59th minute, while Denzel Dumfries saw a potential equaliser ruled out for offside soon afterwards.

The Real Madrid right-back would again be denied by the offside flag in the 73rd minute, moving beyond the final defender before turning home Van Dijk's knockdown, but there was no stopping Reijnders late on.

Gjivai Zechiel's acrobatic attempt from Noa Lang's cross was blocked by Konstantinos Mavropanos, but Reijnders was able to volley the rebound past Konstantinos Tzolakis from the edge of the six-yard box.
Greece made to pay for defensive mindset

Greece were brave on the ball in the first half and committed numbers forward on the counter, but Ivan Jovanovic's side offered almost no attacking threat in the second half; 0.93 of their 0.95 expected goals (xG) tally came in the opening 45 minutes.

Greece attempted two more shots than their opponents before half-time (seven to five), with the Netherlands attempting 13 more than Greece in the second half (14 to one); Greece's only shot after the break came in the 63rd minute and did not hit the target.
Credit must still go to the Netherlands, who did not give up their search for a point, despite seeing two goals narrowly disallowed against Dumfries after the break.
They have now scored late equalisers in two of their three Nations League games to remain unbeaten (W1 D2).

Greece can still take plenty of positives in knowing they are also unbeaten (W2 D1), sitting top of Group A2 and after causing plenty of trouble for both Germany and Netherlands so far in the competition.

34p7x1w2mryx1d30uxb50a7qb.title: Chivu admits Inter played 'without conviction' against Venezia
34p7x1w2mryx1d30uxb50a7qb.subtitle: Despite turning out a below-par performance, Inter managed to secure a 2-0 win over Venezia to move back to the top of Serie A.
paragraphs: Cristian Chivu admits Inter were lucky to beat Venezia in Serie A, declaring that his side went into Wednesday's clash "without enough conviction."

Inter struggled for much of the match at the Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, before late own goals from Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal helped them seal a 2-0 win and move back above Lazio at the top of the table.

After a slew of half chances at the other end, Moreno inadvertently turned Marcus Thuram's cross into his own net in the 71st minute, while Carlos Augusto fired in a header three minutes later that ricocheted in off Halhal.
Chivu put out a heavily rotated lineup, likely with an eye on the upcoming Milan derby on October 31, but the Nerazzurri were far from convincing.
"We lacked energy and were slow in certain aspects, and we were a little surprised by their low block, even though we were expecting it," the Inter boss said.
"We were lucky to come away with the win today. I don't know whether that's what matters; what matters is that we stayed in the game and kept believing, but we were lucky too.
"These are the kinds of games you get through the season, two or three a year, when you go into them without enough conviction.
"Credit to Venezia, they stopped us from making the right runs or creating one-on-one situations.
"We had some scares too. [Ivan] Provedel kept us in the game, and our experience and quality helped us find a way to win."
Though the Nerazzurri may have been fortunate, they have now scored in each of their last 19 Serie A games – their longest scoring streak since a run of 25 from May 2024 to February 2025.
Inter's tally of 25 points after nine games is also their best start to a Serie A campaign in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95).
Chivu's side were, however, the first team to benefit from two own goals in the same Serie A game since Lazio did so against Benevento in April 2021.
"We can and must improve. It's never easy to begin a season like this and show that level of commitment," Chivu continued.
"You must never lose it after a season in which you've won. I have a group that never stops working or believing and gives everything it has.
"We need to improve and find that extra spark to bring out the determination that so many games require.
"We can improve in many areas because the season is long, expectations are high, and what you did in the previous season often counts for little or nothing."

35150u6icz251sd7qww98gnfj.title: Lionel Messi 'at peace and proud' after Argentina farewell on 'saddest day of my career'
35150u6icz251sd7qww98gnfj.subtitle: Argentina legend Lionel Messi thanked supporters in Buenos Aires after he represented his country for the 208th and final time.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi says retiring from international football with Argentina is "the saddest day of my career", but the forward bows out with no regrets.
Argentina beat Benin 3-0 in front of a packed Estadio Monumental crowd on Tuesday in Messi's 208th and final senior international appearance.
Messi marked the occasion with a couple of assists – for Nicolas Otamendi and Nico Paz – plus a goal of his own from the penalty spot.
The Inter Miami ace, who will continue playing at club level, announced his plans to retire in August after an Argentina career spanning 21 years.
He addressed the crowd in Buenos Aires after the match, which was also his first for his country since the death of his father Jorge.
"It was a huge source of pride for me to defend this jersey for more than 20 years," Messi said.
"Even in the worst moments we went through, I never stopped fighting, never stopped being here. Not coming any more is going to be painful.
"I'd like to play for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you.
"Now I'm here on the saddest day of my career, which is the day I have to say goodbye to the national team, goodbye to all of you.
"But now I’ll be on that side [with the fans], supporting all the boys, everyone who comes in. Always united."
Messi showed no signs of slowing down as he led the way against Benin for the most shots (nine), shots on target (nine) and expected goals (1.97).
He also had the most touches in the opposition box (12), created the most chances (four) and registered the most final-third passes (41).

After a slow start to his Argentina career, Messi won two Copa America titles and the World Cup in 2022, while also losing in the showpiece final twice – including defeat to Spain after extra time three months ago.
"I leave grateful, proud and at peace. Thank you for everything," added Messi, who scored 126 goals in the famous blue and white strip.
"Even though I want to be here all my life, I feel that this is the moment. The last World Cup was too much, everything I had to live through.
"We had the dream of fulfilling my dream and the dream of the whole country, of becoming world champions again.
"In the last World Cup we were very close, and the reality is that nothing strange happened, as people say.
"The match against England took a huge toll on us physically, and emotionally it was very big.
"We arrived with just enough and fought like we always did with this jersey, with all the team-mates I got to share things with. We were very close.

"There are so many emotions going through me right now. I'm surely forgetting many things I would like to say because this is a very difficult moment for me. The first person who comes to my mind is my dad."
Benin threatened to ruin the party on Messi's big night in front of 85,000 buoyant supporters, with Argentina struggling to get going in the first half.
Otamendi's goal inside three minutes of the second half settled the hosts, though, before further goals followed from Paz and man of the moment Messi.
Head coach Lionel Scaloni later admitted his players struggled with nerves on a rather unique occasion.
"Everything was very emotional in the first half," Scaloni said.
"The players did not know what play to make and they were nervous, because it was a special night. It was not easy when they had a team-mate [Messi] who wants to leave in the best way.
"For them, it is unparalleled and that is why the first half was not good, because we all wanted him to do his best.
"I never thought I'd be the coach of the best footballer in history and it has been a dream come true. We are eternally grateful to him for giving us the opportunity to be with him.
"Not seeing him any more will be sad, but he leaves us with an incredible legacy.
"The feeling of having Messi on your side is incomparable. I've never seen that aura in anyone else in my life."
Some of Messi's team-mates were in tears as Messi addressed the fans in his speech after the match, saying he did not want to leave the pitch.
Along with the match, to mark the huge occasion, fans were treated to a light show, live music and presentations.

          From Serie D to the Champions League: Como's Rise Has Been Remarkable But Not Universally Appreciated
        
      
                          
                      Oct 21, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Ruben Diaz / Design, Danny Dinsdale / Data Viz, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It wasn't so long ago that Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia was hosting Serie D matches; on Wednesday, it hosts to Manchester United in the Champions League. It's been a rapid rise for Como.

San Siro, Delle Alpi, Olimpico, Artemio Franchi; Manchester United have played in some of Italy’s most iconic stadiums over the years in European competition. On Wednesday, they’ll add another to the list.

Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia may not be among the more recognisable names to the uninitiated when it comes to Italian grounds, but the home of Como 1907 certainly has a rather unique allure and charm that’ll at the very least leave a mark on the United fans who make the trip.

Positioned literally a stone’s throw from the resplendent Lake Como and with the Italian Alps forming a spectacular backdrop, you’ll do well to find many more picturesque football locations in Europe’s big five leagues.

This is our home. And this is where we’ll play in Europe. 💙For almost 100 years, the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia has been part of Como 1907, our city and our supporters.Now, for the first time, Champions League nights are coming to the shores of Lake Como.It starts here on… pic.twitter.com/L56xDadNhh

And while the stadium is undergoing redevelopment, part of which was rapidly completed in the summer to make it UEFA compliant, for the moment it retains an intimate, rugged and unpretentious aura, with its capacity still just 13,602.

The stadium’s rather modest appearance and size may be at odds with the club’s long-term ambition, but that is also illustrative of a rapid rise that's seen Como go from below 3,500th in the Opta Power Rankings seven years ago to 29th as of Wednesday.

Now, it should be noted from the outset that Como’s ascent is hardly a ‘Cinderella’ story based purely around smart recruitment, great coaching and building gradually. The club was purchased in 2019 by Djarum Group, a subsidiary of PT Djarum, one of the world’s biggest cigarette manufacturers.

Although they began the 2019-20 season in the third tier, the takeover meant they suddenly had the richest owners in Italian football. If they were serious about transforming the club’s fortunes on the pitch, it was surely only a matter of time until Como were back in Serie A.

Nevertheless, Como’s ascent is still an impressive achievement, and the visit of Manchester United in the Champions League will provide many supporters with a pinch-yourself moment, even if United aren’t the force they once were.

Just after the takeover, Como secured promotion from Serie D to Serie C, where they went on to spend two seasons before returning to Serie B, a level they’d only played at for one year since the club’s legal predecessor was liquidated in 2005.

Former Chelsea captain Dennis Wise played an important role in Djarum’s early ownership, going from “consultant, before taking on the CEO role and becoming president”, he told the Guardian earlier this year.

“I took total control of the football club, from top to bottom, employing every single person in the building,” he added. “There wasn’t too much interest from afar at that stage – and [the owners] left me to my own devices, really.

“I never had much to spend in the transfer market, so I had to try to do some really good deals. We had 14 loans at one stage – it was about filtering in and out, because there wasn’t money to spend. Then, all of a sudden, it started to grow.”
Como’s return to Serie B in 2021 proved crucial to the greater interest alluded to by Wise. Soon, he wasn’t the only big-name former Premier League player involved.

Ahead of the 2022-23 season, former Barcelona, Arsenal, Chelsea and Spain midfielder Cesc Fàbregas joined as a player, also becoming a minority stakeholder in the club. The Spaniard’s old Arsenal teammate Thierry Henry also invested soon after.

Although Fàbregas only played there for a season before retiring at the end of 2022-23, he remained at the club initially coaching youth and reserve teams for a few months. Then he was fast-tracked to the first-team role on an interim basis before the end of the year.

His lack of a UEFA Pro coaching licence meant Fàbregas was only allowed to take the head coach job for a month – and even that required an exemption. Once that expired, he officially became the assistant of Osian Roberts, even if he was effectively still in charge.
It wasn’t until the summer of 2024, after he’d been admitted onto a UEFA Pro course by the FIGC (Italian Football Federation), that he was formally confirmed as Como’s head coach.

By that point, however, he and Roberts had already overseen promotion back to Serie A thanks to a second-place finish. It marked the end of the club’s 21-year absence from the top flight and vindicated the club’s decision to take something of a gamble by appointing Fàbregas in the first place.

360C501C7CFF704BDCBE8EBF63B79A2D.title: Preview: Arsenal face a tough away day against Nottingham Forest
360C501C7CFF704BDCBE8EBF63B79A2D.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Arsenal face a tough away day against Nottingham ForestShareArsenal have won just once in their last six visits to the City Ground, and will be keen to improve that record as they currently sit three points behind the league leaders.

When Oliver Glasner’s move to the City Ground was announced, those who had closely followed the Austrian tactician’s work could already have predicted what his Nottingham Forest side would look like. They would look to defend in a compact block and be tough to break down, and threaten going forward by being pretty direct in their attacking.

Six games in, those traits are already evident in this Forest side. They have the second-lowest xG conceded tally in the league – trailing only this weekend’s opponents – and have created a fair amount of presentable chances even with a possession average of less than 49%. Yet, they are currently 15th in the standings with just five points.

The main problem has been their forwards’ form in front of goal. They have scored just five goals from an xG tally of 10.6 and lead the league in terms of big chances missed. Forest are sure to make their way up the table the moment some more of those efforts start going in.

Arsenal have picked up three points in all but one of their matches so far this season, but they haven’t quite been coasting to victories. In fact, they haven’t scored in the first half of five of their last six games, with the only outlier being a 4-2 win against newly-promoted Ipswich.

The Gunners’ strength in depth has proven vital during this run. Just in the last week, Bruno Guimarães came off the bench to score the winner against Leeds United in the league, while Bukayo Saka’s contributions after coming on in the 65th minute against Lille were instrumental in putting that Champions League contest to bed.
Nicolò Savona and Igor Jesus are confirmed absentees for Forest, while centre-back Nikola Milenković is a major doubt.

Arsenal will be without a few players in different positions as well. William Saliba is yet to feature this season after aggravating a back injury at the World Cup. Piero Hincapié and Martín Zubimendi picked up minor issues recently, while Christos Tzolis’ absence leaves the left wing spot open.

Morgan Gibbs-White will be central to the hosts’ attacking plans; he leads the league for big chances created. Daniel Muñoz will need to put in a big shift on the right flank, and Murillo will have to produce an excellent all-round display at the back.

Noni Madueke looked the most threatening of Arsenal’s attackers last weekend and assisted the opener against Lille, so he will be keen to continue making telling contributions. Riccardo Calafiori’s dynamic movement could be the wildcard that throws Forest’s defenders off, while Myles Lewis-Skelly will look to make inroads through the middle of their defensive block.
Arsenal should have enough quality to come away with a victory by a narrow margin.

Add FotMob as a preferred news source on Google by clicking – here.
Arsenal have won just once in their last six visits to the City Ground, and will be keen to improve that record as they currently sit three points behind the league leaders.

When Oliver Glasner’s move to the City Ground was announced, those who had closely followed the Austrian tactician’s work could already have predicted what his Nottingham Forest side would look like. They would look to defend in a compact block and be tough to break down, and threaten going forward by being pretty direct in their attacking.

Six games in, those traits are already evident in this Forest side. They have the second-lowest xG conceded tally in the league – trailing only this weekend’s opponents – and have created a fair amount of presentable chances even with a possession average of less than 49%. Yet, they are currently 15th in the standings with just five points.

The main problem has been their forwards’ form in front of goal. They have scored just five goals from an xG tally of 10.6 and lead the league in terms of big chances missed. Forest are sure to make their way up the table the moment some more of those efforts start going in.

Arsenal have picked up three points in all but one of their matches so far this season, but they haven’t quite been coasting to victories. In fact, they haven’t scored in the first half of five of their last six games, with the only outlier being a 4-2 win against newly-promoted Ipswich.

The Gunners’ strength in depth has proven vital during this run. Just in the last week, Bruno Guimarães came off the bench to score the winner against Leeds United in the league, while Bukayo Saka’s contributions after coming on in the 65th minute against Lille were instrumental in putting that Champions League contest to bed.
Nicolò Savona and Igor Jesus are confirmed absentees for Forest, while centre-back Nikola Milenković is a major doubt.

          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 1 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the AI-powered Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions across Matchday 1 in 2026-27.

The Opta supercomputer will be with us every step of the way in the 2026-27 UEFA Women’s Champions League as the model works to provide you with data-backed predictions for all matches and season outcomes.

Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday 22 September with five games, including the reigning WSL champions Manchester City’s return to the UWCL after a one-year absence. Andrée Jeglertz's side will take on seven-time German Frauen-Bundesliga winners Bayern Munich away from home.
Four more matches follow on Wednesday, when the reigning European champions Barcelona host Paris FC, and eight-time UWCL winners OL Lyonnes travel to Swiss side Servette.
Below, Opta Analyst provides predictions for each game from MD1, powered by thousands of simulations from the Opta supercomputer.

The 2026-27 competition gets underway on Tuesday with two early 5.45pm kick-offs in Milan and Munich. The most eye-catching fixture of the two is between the reigning league champions in Germany and England, as Bayern Munich host Manchester City.

It is a daunting opening assignment for City. Bayern are ranked second in Opta's Power Rankings (95.9) and boast an enviable record on home soil in this competition. They went unbeaten across their five UWCL home matches last season (W4 D1) and have lost just one of their last 16 at home in Europe (W11 D4), a 2-0 defeat to Lyon in the quarter-finals of the 2024-25 campaign.

The supercomputer expects Bayern to make the most of that home advantage, with the German champions winning 52.4% of its 10,000 pre-match simulations. City, meanwhile, came out on top in 23.3%, underlining the size of the challenge awaiting them on their return to the competition.

The other early kick-off on Tuesday is between Inter and Häcken, with the home side making their UWCL debut in front of their own fans. While the Italians will be hoping to mark the occasion with a statement result, the Swedish club are slight favourites according to the supercomputer, winning 55.9% of simulations as they return to the competition for the first time since reaching the quarter-finals in 2023-24.
Arsenal, winners of the competition in 2024-25, begin their latest European campaign at home to HB Køge.

The Gunners have yet to fully hit their stride domestically, opening the WSL season with a 1-0 win at Brighton before being held by Crystal Palace and Manchester United at Emirates Stadium. Despite registering 47 shots across those two home matches, Arsenal scored just once, relying on a stoppage-time equaliser against United to extend their unbeaten run.

No English team have lost to Danish opposition in the UWCL since the north London club’s 5-1 defeat to Fortuna Hjørring in the 2002-03 semi-final (W7 D3 since), and the Opta supercomputer expects Arsenal to secure all three points in this one. Renée Slegers' side won 81.1% of its pre-match simulations – the highest percentage of any side playing on Tuesday night.

The supercomputer struggled to find a clear winner in its pre-game sims for Juventus vs Benfica, but the Portuguese club have the slight edge (39.9%). That's despite Juve beating Benfica 2-1 in last season’s league phase thanks to a brace from Cecilia Salvai.

Tuesday’s other clash is between Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, with PSG looking to end a miserable eight-game winless streak in the UWCL (L6 D2) – their longest such run in the competition. The Opta supercomputer isn’t confident of them doing that though, as Madrid won 45.6% of its 10,000 pre-game sims.
Record UWCL champions, and last season’s losing finalists, OL Lyonnes make their 2026-27 bow on Wednesday night, travelling to Swiss club Servette in one of the early evening kick-offs.

It’s a daunting start for Servette, with Jonatan Giráldez's side unbeaten across their last 23 group/league stage games in the UEFA Women’s Champions League (W18 D5) since a 5-1 defeat to Arsenal in 2022-23.

Considering all of Lyon’s previous UWCL meetings with Swiss sides have ended in big wins (all vs Zürich: 8-0, 9-0, 3-0 and 4-0) it’s understandable that Lyon are given a 73.7% chance of victory on MD1 – the biggest chance of an away win across the two nights of action.
The Opta supercomputer also makes the away side favourites in the other early Wednesday fixture, with Roma travelling to Belgium to face OH Leuven.

The Italian side came out on top in 60.8% of the model's pre-match simulations, reflecting both their growing European pedigree and OH Leuven's struggles in last season's competition, where the Belgians won just one of their eight matches (D3 L4).

Attention then turns to Wednesday's later kick-offs, which feature two of the three highest-ranked teams in the women's Opta Power Rankings. Defending European champions Barcelona host Paris FC, while Chelsea welcome Austria Wien to The Cherry Red Records Stadium.

39A7F7426A8D89908F9B628E2A20321A.title: Mikel Oyarzabal: A one-club man thriving for his national team
39A7F7426A8D89908F9B628E2A20321A.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesMikel Oyarzabal: A one-club man thriving for his national teamShareJust as he did in Spain’s previous meeting with England in the final of Euro 2024, Real Sociedad’s Mikel Oyarzabal came off the bench to score the winner – this time, ensuring his country got their 2026/27 Nations League campaign up and running with a 3-2 victory at Wembley.

That was his 31st international goal – only five players have ever scored more for Spain; his goals-per-game average is better than legends like Raúl and Fernando Torres – yet still, Oyarzabal goes somewhat underappreciated.
Some players just thrive when playing for their country, shining brighter than they do at club level. Oyarzabal is one – but the dismissal of his club career is wildly unfair.

To dismiss Oyarzabal’s club career – the fact he’s never moved to a ‘bigger’ club; that he’s stayed a one-club man – is to dismiss a fundamental part of his identity. Oyarzabal is Basque, and he’s remained loyal to his roots.

Born in Eibar, less than hour’s drive from Donostia / San Sebastián, the town Real Sociedad call home, Oyarzabal has spent his entire career in the Basque Country, starting out in the youth system of Eibar then joining Real Sociedad aged 14 and ultimately going on to captain them. In his first year as a senior Spain international, he played and scored for the Basque national team against Tunisia.

Oyarzabal’s commitment to his heritage is not unusual: the latest Spain squad includes six players of Basque origin; three of them – Oyarzabal, and Athletic Club duo Unai Simón and Nico Williams, Spain’s other goalscorer in the Euro 2024 final – have never played for clubs outside the Basque Country.

And perhaps therein lies a key driver of Oyarzabal’s consistency. Free from the pressure of having to prove himself at a new club or in a new league, he’s been able to get on with what he does best: score goals – of all kinds.

Oyarzabal passed the 100-goal mark for Real Sociedad two seasons ago. Second on the club’s all-time scorers list, the 29-year-old is now up to 133 goals in the colours of Erreala – with only one man left to catch: another one-club legend, Jesús María Satrústegui – who, 45 years before Oyarzabal did likewise, scored for Spain against England at Wembley, in La Roja’s first-ever win at the iconic stadium.

And for all his consistency in club football – of his 11 seasons in the Real Sociedad first team, he’s scored 13 or more goals in eight of them – Oyarzabal has proved to be something of an international specialist in recent months.

He’s yet to add to his Real Sociedad tally this term; in fact, he’s gone 11 club appearances without a goal, stretching back to May. But since then, he’s struck seven times in 11 outings for Spain – with five of those goals coming en route to World Cup glory this summer, including the opener in the semi-final triumph over France.

In a mark of clinical nature, Oyarzabal’s six goals across the World Cup and Spain’s opening two Nations League games – have come from 4.63 Expected Goals (xG). His last 10 competitive international goals – dating back to last October – have come from 9.87 xG. Strip out the three penalties he’s scored (a penalty is typically worth around 0.79 xG) and he’s found the net seven times from roughly 7.5 xG in 13 competitive Spain matches over the last 12 months – as well as notching a further three goals in friendlies.

Oyarzabal is enjoying a purple patch in the red of Spain: he’s accumulated just under 42% of his international goals since this time last year. He’s netted a career-best nine times in each of the last two calendar years – and Spain still have two games to go in 2026…

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente said of Oyarzabal after his brace in La Roja’s 4-0 thrashing of Saudi Arabia, their first win of the World Cup: “He’s a great among greats. Finally we’re starting to recognise him in Spain, my goodness.”
De la Fuente also made a point of highlighting Oyarzabal’s superb footballing brain, adding: “Few players understand football like him. And at goalscoring, he’s extraordinary.”

A total of 24 international goals in just under three years represents quite the return for a player who has only really been converted from a winger into a centre forward relatively recently. And when you consider Oyarzabal is not a pure No. 9 – in fairness, Spain have historically been at their best when deploying someone more in the false nine role – his goalscoring figures become all the more impressive.

He posted a career-best haul of 15 LaLiga goals last season, and he has tended to score in clusters in recent years – so the drought is unlikely to last, although it’s understandable it’s happened in the first place when you consider he played the majority of minutes in Spain’s eight-match run to lifting their second World Cup.

Besides, when it comes to the crunch, Oyarzabal still produces the goods in some shape or form: a few weeks before that decisive goal at Wembley, he provided both assists as Real Sociedad recovered from successive defeats at the start of the LaLiga campaign to register their first win against Espanyol.

He’s created 10 chances – of his club teammates, only Carlos Soler (11) has fashioned more – and that’s in a side who, so far, rank towards the lower end of LaLiga for xG (8.6 at an average of 1.22 per game). You can take the winger out of the role, but you can’t take the role out of the winger, it seems.

But whatever box one wishes to put Oyarzabal in (usually the opposition’s), he’s demonstrably a player for the big moments and more – and a model professional who deserves to have more respect put on his name.

39cc0xssc61i10jsrfcqdfqjs.title: Ancelotti impressed by Brazil youngsters but Australia win marred by Raphinha injury
39cc0xssc61i10jsrfcqdfqjs.subtitle: Brazil earned their first victory since the World Cup on Tuesday, with several young players contributing to their 4-2 win over Australia.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti said Brazil's young players were "seizing the moment" following Tuesday's 4-2 friendly win over Australia, though the game was marred by an injury to Raphinha.
The Selecao edged a six-goal thriller against the Socceroos at Suncorp Stadium, just four days on from a 1-1 draw between the sides in Townsville.

Vanderson's glorious third-minute volley put Brazil – who made seven changes to their starting line-up – in front, only for Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe to strike for Australia in a five-minute spell and flip the match on its head.

Raphinha equalised from the penalty spot late in the first half before exiting the game at the interval, with what the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) described as "discomfort in his right thigh".
But the Selecao were superior after the restart as Bruno Guimaraes finished off a polished move and Vinicius Junior won and converted another penalty to secure the victory.

Ancelotti did not address Raphinha's withdrawal – which will be a major concern for Barcelona ahead of meetings with Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month – in his post-match comments, instead focusing on the performances of his young players.

Twenty-year-old Cruzeiro goalkeeper Otavio won his first cap between the sticks, with Gabriel Bontempo also making his debut while Jair Cunha and Mauro Junior started for the first time at senior international level.
"It was a good game – we had difficulties, but we also showed good quality in our play," Ancelotti said. "We started well, then we lowered the pace of the game a little.
"But in the second half, I think the team reacted well, scoring a fantastic goal – the third – with a fantastic combination. We are happy.
"The best way is for the Selecao to perform well, to try to play a beautiful game and continue with this clear idea, with the progression of our youngsters.
"They are seizing this moment. I'm very clear with them: it's not a test. They're not here for me to see what they are like or what they can't do.
"They are very good and have to take advantage of this opportunity. We will monitor their progression.
"I repeat – I am very confident in these young players, and others will be involved in the next squad."
Sao Paulo midfielder Bontempo assisted Vanderson's opening goal and created the joint-most chances of any player, with two (level with Vinicius).
PSV full-back Mauro, meanwhile, led all Brazil players for duels contested (14), duels won (nine), tackles contested (five, two of which were successful) and aerial duels (seven).
Brazil face India in another friendly on Saturday, before taking on Japan and Singapore during the November international break.

39tgblbq0c2019c0bq7ugdoka.title: 'Money can't buy you the Champions League' – Chivu urges Inter to work for European glory
39tgblbq0c2019c0bq7ugdoka.subtitle: Inter hosts Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday, aiming to bounce back from their defeat to Real Madrid on matchday one.
paragraphs: Cristian Chivu believes "money can't buy you the Champions League" and has urged his Inter side to work hard for European success.
Inter have not won the competition since 2009-10, when Chivu started the final against Bayern Munich during Jose Mourinho's tenure.

The Nerazzurri started their 2026-27 Champions League campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid; despite dominating the possession battle (64.4%), Inter conceded nine big chances against Madrid  – their most in a Champions League game on record (since 2010-11).
Ahead of hosting Club Brugge on matchday two, Chivu outlined what his Inter side must do to end their wait for Champions League glory.
"The status of this club requires you to try and achieve every goal," said Chivu.
"When it comes to dreams, you don't necessarily have to achieve it, but you have to make a good job of it.
"Talking about dreams doesn't mean that we're talking about winning the whole thing, but it is part of our responsibility to try and achieve a goal like that.
"Money can't buy you the Champions League. There are no players or coaches who give you that guarantee. You need to have the courage, but the work you put in is the most important thing."
This will be the first meeting between Inter and Club Brugge, who lost 3-2 to Aston Villa in their Champions League opener.
Inter come into this fixture on a three-game losing streak in the Champions League, having lost both legs against Bodo/Glimt in last season’s play-off round and this season’s opener at Madrid.
Inter have never lost four consecutive matches in their European Cup/Champions League history, and Chivu refused to underestimate Brugge's threat.

"We don't underestimate anyone," added Chivu. "We have a level of maturity and always go onto the pitch with a sense of responsibility and with the right attitude, a desire to dominate. At the same time, we also want to have fun.
"We have room for improvement, that's our ambition. We can do certain things better and we will try to do them better.
"The group is of a high level, we have competition and that raises the level of training and the level of our ambitions."
