3CC2AB55BA4AB60AE826990C0350804E.title: The FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 6’s Best XI features Henderson, Anderson, and Rice
3CC2AB55BA4AB60AE826990C0350804E.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 6’s Best XI features Henderson, Anderson, and RiceShareAfter a three-week hiatus due to the recent international break, matchday six is finally finished, with Manchester City maintaining their 100% record and a three-point advantage at the top of the Premier League table.
The Italian was in imperious form against Liverpool, making six saves in total across the 90 minutes as his side triumphed 3-0.
He also succeeded with 100% of his ground and aerial duels, while succeeding with his only dribble attempt and this marks his second inclusion in FotMob’s Team of the Week already this season.
Ouattara was making just his second Premier League start for Ipswich at the weekend, yet the defender ended up scoring the equaliser against Fulham in the dying minutes.
Furthermore, the youngster also made four passes into the final third, wasn’t dispossessed and registered four defensive contributions throughout the clash.
While Ouattara brought Ipswich back level against the Cottagers, it was centre-back Dara O’Shea who netted the winner with just seconds left on the clock.
His header gave Ipswich all three points, but it was his defensive display which justifies the defender making it into the TOTW.
Indeed, he made nine defensive contributions along with seven recoveries, while the Irishman took 76 touches throughout, indicating that he was aiming to control the game from the back.
His rating of 8.2 is the best of any defender in the league this weekend.
Bobby Thomas registered a staggering 22 defensive contributions in the 4-1 win against Newcastle United, the most of any player on the field (does anyone have him in their FPL team?).
There were 16 clearances among that total, showcasing his ability to consistently repel opposition attacks.
Thomas was also keen on getting his side going in the final third, making nine passes into this area as he too celebrates making it into the TOTW for the second time this season.
Calafiori came to Arsenal’s rescue against Leeds, netting the equaliser a few minutes after the Yorkshire side took the lead.

That was his second goal of the season and for a left-back, his attacking stats weren’t bad at all, creating two big chances, registering two shots and taking four touches in the opposition penalty area.
He will be vital for Mikel Arteta this term, especially given Arsenal’s issues at left-back in recent seasons.
Jordan Henderson rolled back the years in Chelsea’s 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth. The Englishman not only scored twice and provided an assist, but he also took the joint-most shots (3) of anyone.

Despite his age, Henderson managed 79 touches, signifying that he was still looking to get on the ball as much as possible and he even covered the most distance across both teams (11.9km) during the game.
For his display, he received a 9.2 FotMob rating – the highest in this week’s TOTW.
Anderson is another regular in our TOTW and he is certainly filling the void left by Rodri at Manchester City.
The midfielder dictated the tempo of the game, having the most touches (104) of any player, while also covering the most distance (11.4km) in the match.

3EAF76DCC4FAA38CEAF01E81A485CAF1.subtitle: BBC

QuizGrealish dropped over 'breach of club discipline' - what now?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jack Grealish has featured six times for Everton this season
David Moyes says it was the club's decision to leave Jack Grealish out of Everton's Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United because of "a breach of club discipline".
Everton did not disclose any further details, but the decision is understood to have arisen from an unauthorised absence from training.
"You probably know I'm not going to give any details," said Moyes after Everton's 3-1 win at Hill Dickinson Stadium set up a quarter-final tie at League Two Fleetwood Town.
"It's a club decision, it's something I don't want to speak too much about."
Moyes made it clear he supported the decision to leave out England winger Grealish, 31, who is on loan from Premier League rivals Manchester City.

Grealish spent a large chunk of last season with the Toffees under a similar arrangement, scoring twice and providing six assists in 20 appearances, before sustaining a season-ending foot injury in January.
He returned to City and came on as a substitute during their 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal at Wembley in August.
The former Aston Villa player, who cost City £100m in 2021, also featured as a substitute during their 2-1 win over Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.
He rejoined Everton before the transfer window closed and has featured five times for them this season in the Premier League.
Grealish also played in Everton's EFL Cup third-round win over Wolves.
Asked if Grealish would return for the Premier League game at Newcastle on Monday, Moyes added: "I wouldn't give any team news away."
Everton cruise past Newcastle to reach EFL Cup quarter-finals

David Moyes discusses Jack Grealish and transfers
Grealish is in the final year of his reported £300,000-a-week contract at Manchester City.
He was discarded by Pep Guardiola in the Spaniard's final season in charge, being allowed to join Everton on a season-long loan deal.
There were moments where he looked to be getting back to his best while playing for the Toffees before his foot injury.
Such was his form at the beginning of last season, he claimed the Premier League's player-of-the-month award for August and quickly became a fans' favourite.

"He is a player who has fallen in love with the right shade of blue, but ultimately he is a City player and we have to respect that," Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear told BBC Radio Merseyside in August.

3a3ixw4gjfhgz5rbo8v5473v.title: Argentina 4-0 Bolivia: Post-Messi era begins with emphatic victory
3a3ixw4gjfhgz5rbo8v5473v.subtitle: In their first game since Lionel Messi confirmed his international retirement, Argentina swatted aside Bolivia 4-0 in Cordoba.
paragraphs: Argentina hammered Bolivia 4-0 as they got the post-Lionel Messi era going in style at Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes.
Lautaro Martinez, Nico Paz, new captain Cristian Romero and Flaco Lopez were all on target for Lionel Scaloni's team on Wednesday.
The friendly in Cordoba marked Argentina's first match since the iconic Messi had announced his international retirement.
It was also Argentina's first game since their 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup final.
Martinez's drilled finish got them going in the 19th minute, with Como star Paz then dinking home to make it 2-0.
Gianluca Prestianni hit the bar with a cross-shot before half-time, but Argentina got their third when Romero headed in from Paz's free-kick in the 54th minute.
Lopez then grabbed a maiden Argentina goal from the bench late on, just after he had seen a strike disallowed for offside.
There will be much tougher tests to come for Argentina in the wake of Messi's retirement and, technically, the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner is not done yet.
Argentina will give Messi a farewell when they take on Benin next week.
However, Scaloni's team were utterly dominant in this win. They conceded just three shots, none of which were on target, and had 18 attempts of their own.
Argentina's dominance is reflected by their expected goals tally of 2.24 compared to Bolivia's 0.11.
With Messi out of the picture, much of the attacking onus is going to fall on Martinez, Paz and Julian Alvarez.
Paz and Alcaraz had a team-leading three shots each, while Martinez led the way for touches in the opponent's box (seven).

Playmaker Paz also crafted three chances, which was the joint-most for Argentina, along with Franco Mastantuono, another youngster who will be looking to help fill the void left by one of the best to grace the game.

3fas5rmj8v1s1kt74kkfz5ogp.title: 'They won't hand it over on a silver platter' – NYCFC boss Jansen wary of Montreal threat
3fas5rmj8v1s1kt74kkfz5ogp.subtitle: New York City FC kept their playoff hopes alive in dramatic fashion last time out, and now prepare to host eliminated CF Montreal.
paragraphs: New York City FC boss Pascal Jansen insisted CF Montreal "won't hand it over on a silver platter" to them when they face off on Saturday.
NYCFC kept their play-off hopes alive with a dramatic 2-1 victory over Atlanta United on Wednesday, with Benie Traore scoring a 95th-minute winner.

It marked the second consecutive game in which they scored a result-changing goal in second-half stoppage time, after Jonathan Shore scored a 99th-minute equaliser in their 2-2 draw with Orlando City SC.
NYCFC are 12th, but only three points off ninth-place Columbus Crew, who currently occupy the final wildcard spot in the Eastern Conference.
After previously lamenting their lack of confidence in front of goal, Jansen hopes their recent late strikes can make a difference with two regular-season games to go.
"We have talked about it quite a bit during this season," said Jansen about their previous confidence problems.
"It's not only the Atlanta game; you saw it last Saturday as well, with the late goal from Johnny Shore.
"The fighting spirit has always been there. But sometimes you need a little spark in order to get it going again.

"We got lucky because in the first half we were not allowed to get our rhythm. But the fighting spirit was there in the second half, and that is the basics you need, especially in the phase we are in as a team, trying to achieve what we are trying to achieve still.
"I think it's a huge boost going into this weekend against Montreal. Because even though they are finished, they won't hand [the win] over on a silver platter."
Montreal are bottom of the East and already out of playoff contention.
Their poor form continued midweek as they were thrashed 4-0 on the road by Charlotte FC.
New York City FC – Benie Traore
Traore scored the game-winning goal for NYCFC in Wednesday's win at 94:42.
It was the latest goal from outside the box in an MLS match in NYCFC history, besting David Villa's strike at 92:54 against Columbus in October 2016.
CF Montreal – Hennadii Synchuk
Hennadii Synchuk had Montreal's lone shot on target in the loss to Charlotte.
Over the club's last four matches, Synchuk has five shots on target, while only one other Montreal player has even two in that time (Alexis Sanchez – two).
MATCH PREDICTION: NEW YORK CITY FC WIN
Both of NYCFC's goals in their win over Atlanta came from outside the box, with the goals coming in the 70th minute and in second-half stoppage time.
It was the second time NYCFC have scored multiple outside-the-box goals in the 70th minute or later in an MLS match (October 2016 v Columbus).

Montreal's defeat to Charlotte marked the fifth MLS match this season that they have allowed four or more goals. That is the second-most such games in an MLS regular season for the club, trailing only their seven such matches in 2024.

However, Montreal have won four straight meetings with NYCFC, keeping clean sheets in all four, after winning just two of the first 20 meetings in all competitions (D5 L13). No team in MLS history has recorded five straight shutout wins over a single opponent in regular-season play.
New York City FC – 59.4%

3ffh20m7fvrr114wvr2tkc73s.title: Lampard looking to build on 'pleasure' of Coventry's first Premier League win
3ffh20m7fvrr114wvr2tkc73s.subtitle: Coventry City are looking to make it back-to-back wins in the Premier League when they welcome Newcastle United to CBS Arena.
paragraphs: Frank Lampard says it was a relief for Coventry City to earn their first Premier League win but admitted there is still work to do ahead of facing Newcastle United.

Coventry lost each of their first four Premier League matches following their promotion without scoring a goal but ended both droughts with their 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest before the international break.
It was a first top-flight win in 25 years, but Lampard's side have slipped down to 19th in the table following the rest of the weekend's results.

Only against Crystal Palace (five) has Lampard won more Premier League games as a manager than he has versus Newcastle (three), and he is confident he can add to that tally, as long as Coventry continue to build on their progress.
"It was really a relief and a real pleasure as it sunk in for the players to feel that feeling of winning a Premier League game," Lampard said.

"I have to understand why, [for] the players, that's a big deal for them, so as long as we remember all the reasons why they got there and keep doubling down on all the work we're talking about and what we do, then it's good.
"There will be things that they will naturally learn as they go, and my job is to be there to support them and understand if they keep going, keep working, belief will grow with that."
Newcastle, meanwhile, sit 11th in the table, having lost just one of their five league matches under Matthias Jaissle so far.
They responded well to their resounding 4-1 defeat to Leeds United, heading into the break on the back of a 2-1 win over high-flying Hull City.
Jaissle is not getting ahead of himself just yet, though, and is wary of the threat that a buoyant Coventry can pose to the Magpies.
"Every team is capable of winning against every opponent," Jaissle said.
"Coventry have the momentum, as they won their last match, and confidence. They also have quality and a clear playing style.
"If we perform at our best, then it will be difficult to beat us. We want to make it as difficult for them as possible."
Coventry City – Jay Dasilva
Jay Dasilva scored Coventry's first Premier League goal of the season and scored on his 127th appearance across all competitions.
His goal ended a run of 599 minutes without a goal in the Premier League for Coventry.
Newcastle United – Lewis Hall
Only Kobbie Mainoo (40) has won possession more times than Lewis Hall (38) in the Premier League this season.
Hall also ranks top among all full-backs/wing-backs for carries (64) and carry distance (803.5m).
MATCH PREDICTION: NEWCASTLE UNITED WIN

Coventry have lost seven of their last eight league games against Newcastle (W1), including their last five in a row. This is the first time the two sides will face each other in the league since 2009-10 in the Championship, and first in the Premier League since 2000-01.
Newcastle won both of their last two league visits to Coventry by 2-0 scorelines in September 2000 and December 2009 but have never won three in a row before.
Coventry have struggled at home this term, as well, losing both such league games by an aggregate score of 0-6.

Only five sides in the competition's history have lost each of their opening three home matches of a campaign without scoring: Everton in 2005-06 and 2023-24, Crystal Palace in 2017-18, Burnley in 2020-21 and Wolves in 2021-22.

Since the start of May, only Arsenal (eight) and Manchester City (seven) have won more Premier League games than Newcastle (four), who are looking to win successive games in the competition for the third time in 2026, after doing so in January and in March.
Coventry City – 29.8%
Newcastle United – 44.8%

3fujh5arvz8o1s2bnno8i5dqq.title: Espanyol 0-1 Atletico Madrid: Baena's stunner secures sixth straight win
3fujh5arvz8o1s2bnno8i5dqq.subtitle: Atletico Madrid were struggling to get the better of Angel Fortuno at RCDE Stadium, but Alex Baena found the winner in the 89th minute.
paragraphs: Alex Baena scored a 90th-minute winner as Atletico Madrid defeated Espanyol 1-0 at RCDE Stadium.

Espanyol goalkeeper Angel Fortuno frustrated Atleti for large parts of the clash, making five saves, but Baena found a late breakthrough to secure a sixth consecutive win in all competitions and fifth straight in LaLiga.
The first half did not produce much action, but Jonathan David went close to breaking the deadlock when his shot from a tight angle was pushed wide by Fortuno.
Marcos Llorente saw a fierce effort tipped against the top of the crossbar by Fortuno just after the hour mark, and the Espanyol goalkeeper was very busy in the closing stages.
He smothered another chance from David before denying Julian Alvarez twice, with the second a brilliant fingertip save to turn behind a trivela from the Argentina international.
However, with the clock winding down, Alvarez teed up Baena just outside the box, and the latter rifled into the top-left corner to snatch all three points in the 89th minute.
Baena enjoying strong start to 2026-27
Diego Simeone will feel his side deserved what they got at RCDE Stadium, with Atleti producing 1.34 expected goals (xG) from 19 shots to Espanyol's 0.53 from 10 attempts.
In the end, Baena's 28-minute cameo proved to be the difference, with the midfielder also creating two chances before netting the winner.
Baena has contributed to seven LaLiga goals for Atleti in 2026-27 (five goals, two assists), two more than in the entire previous season (two goals and three assists in 27 matches).
He is now just two goals away from his single-season scoring record in the competition, achieved with Villarreal in 2024-25 (seven goals).
Atleti's defence also played a key role while their attackers looked for a breakthrough; they did not concede a single shot on target in the first half, and just two overall.
Alvarez may also breathe a sigh of relief after registering his first assist in LaLiga this term, but the striker is still waiting for his first goal of 2026-27.

3i1ka9lnppzj1dmaod57qiny9.title: Rose wants to lead 'relentless' Bournemouth to trophies
3i1ka9lnppzj1dmaod57qiny9.subtitle: Bournemouth have won five consecutive matches across all competitions, and they face Leeds United in the Premier League next.
paragraphs: Marco Rose described his Bournemouth team as "relentless" after they put together five consecutive wins during their EFL Cup victory over Aston Villa.
Bournemouth booked their place in the quarter-finals, and a tie with Liverpool, with a 3-0 win at the Vitality Stadium. Amine Adli, Lewis Cook and Alvaro Rodriguez were on target.
The Cherries have enjoyed a superb recent run of form, with last weekend's triumph over Manchester United moving them up to 13th in the Premier League ahead of MD9.
Rose's side welcome Leeds United to the Vitality this Saturday, before they continue their Europa League campaign against Sparta Prague next week.

Speaking after their win over Unai Emery's team, captain Lewis Cook said Bournemouth have the squad to compete for silverware this season, with Rose making eight changes to the side that emerged victorious at Old Trafford.

And the Bournemouth boss agreed with Cook, saying: "Clean sheet and three goals again – I could get used to it, but it's hard work. It was a nice game to watch from both sides, and we are happy that we won.
"We had eight changes, and everyone played at a really good level. We are relentless, so it's the attitude and the effort.
"It showed we have competition, quality and that everyone is ready. That's what we are working for. To create special moments.
"We have had some special moments in the last couple of weeks, but in the end, if we have something to put up in the air, then it's much more special."
Leeds, meanwhile, were forced to settle for a point in their goalless draw with Sunderland last time out, with the conditions not helped by Storm Boelo at the Stadium of Light.
Daniel Farke's side have played out the joint-most draws of any team in the top flight in 2026 (14 – level with Brentford), while their five nil-nil draws are the outright most this year.
They did, however, have several chances to beat Sunderland, including right at the death, but Sean Longstaff saw his goal-bound effort blocked by team-mate Lukas Nmecha.

Ao Tanaka turned in another industrious display in midfield, and he said: "I want to play more minutes and experience more years here. In order to do that, I know I have to continue to show my quality on the pitch so that is my target.
"It is a massive opponent [Bournemouth] for us and it will be a tough game. We will put everything into it, especially as we haven't won in four games.
"We want to get the three points. We have to keep positive though and remember that if we get one point, it is a good point. I will deliver my best performance."
Bournemouth – Marcus Tavernier
Tavernier has been one of Bournemouth's standout performers so far this season, scoring six goals in his last nine Premier League games for the Cherries.
This has comprised of three different runs of scoring in consecutive games, but he has never scored in three in a row before, something he will be hoping to change here.
Leeds – James Trafford
Only David Raya, Bart Verbruggen (both five) and Alisson Becker have kept more clean sheets in the Premier League this season than Trafford's three.

Trafford also has the highest save percentage in the top flight this term (82.4%), the second-highest number of saves (30) and (based on Opta’s xGOT model) the third-highest number of goals prevented (1.9).
MATCH PREDICTION: BOURNEMOUTH WIN
Both Premier League meetings between Bournemouth and Leeds ended 2-2 last season – the four games between the sides in the top-flight have seen 20 goals scored at an average of five per game.

After a run of eight winless Premier League games, Bournemouth have won 2-0 against Sunderland and 3-0 against Manchester United in their last two. They last won three in a row between August and September last season, while they have never done so without conceding in the competition.

Leeds, meanwhile, won 10 of their first 13 league games against Bournemouth (D2 L1) but they are winless in three against the Cherries (D2 L1) since a 4-3 victory in November 2022 in which they came from 3-1 down.

But this game promises to be entertaining, given there's been a 90th-minute goal scored in three of the four Premier League meetings between Bournemouth and Leeds, with the last two being equalising goals by the away side in 2-2 draws in 2025-26.
However, Bournemouth (13) and Leeds (14) are two of the top three teams for most Premier League draws so far in 2026 (Brentford also 14).
Five of Leeds' last seven league games have ended level (W1 L1), with the Whites losing just two of their last 17 (W6 D9).

"We had eight changes, and everyone played at a really good level. We are relentless, so it's the attitude and the effort.

"It showed we have competition, quality and that everyone is ready. That's what we are working for. To create special moments. 

"We have had some special moments in the last couple of weeks, but in the end, if we have something to put up in the air, then it's much more special."

Leeds, meanwhile, were forced to settle for a point in their goalless draw with Sunderland last time out, with the conditions not helped by Storm Boelo at the Stadium of Light.

Daniel Farke's side have played out the joint-most draws of any team in the top flight in 2026 (14 – level with Brentford), while their five nil-nil draws are the outright most this year.

They did, however, have several chances to beat Sunderland, including right at the death, but Sean Longstaff saw his goal-bound effort blocked by team-mate Lukas Nmecha. 

Ao Tanaka turned in another industrious display in midfield, and he said: "I want to play more minutes and experience more years here. In order to do that, I know I have to continue to show my quality on the pitch so that is my target.

"It is a massive opponent [Bournemouth] for us and it will be a tough game. We will put everything into it, especially as we haven't won in four games.

"We want to get the three points. We have to keep positive though and remember that if we get one point, it is a good point. I will deliver my best performance."

PLAYERS TO WATCH

Bournemouth – Marcus Tavernier

Tavernier has been one of Bournemouth's standout performers so far this season, scoring six goals in his last nine Premier League games for the Cherries.

This has comprised of three different runs of scoring in consecutive games, but he has never scored in three in a row before, something he will be hoping to change here.

Leeds – James Trafford

Only David Raya, Bart Verbruggen (both five) and Alisson Becker have kept more clean sheets in the Premier League this season than Trafford's three.

Trafford also has the highest save percentage in the top flight this term (82.4%), the second-highest number of saves (30) and (based on Opta’s xGOT model) the third-highest number of goals prevented (1.9).

MATCH PREDICTION: BOURNEMOUTH WIN

Both Premier League meetings between Bournemouth and Leeds ended 2-2 last season – the four games between the sides in the top-flight have seen 20 goals scored at an average of five per game.

After a run of eight winless Premier League games, Bournemouth have won 2-0 against Sunderland and 3-0 against Manchester United in their last two. They last won three in a row between August and September last season, while they have never done so without conceding in the competition.

Leeds, meanwhile, won 10 of their first 13 league games against Bournemouth (D2 L1) but they are winless in three against the Cherries (D2 L1) since a 4-3 victory in November 2022 in which they came from 3-1 down.

But this game promises to be entertaining, given there's been a 90th-minute goal scored in three of the four Premier League meetings between Bournemouth and Leeds, with the last two being equalising goals by the away side in 2-2 draws in 2025-26.

However, Bournemouth (13) and Leeds (14) are two of the top three teams for most Premier League draws so far in 2026 (Brentford also 14).

Five of Leeds' last seven league games have ended level (W1 L1), with the Whites losing just two of their last 17 (W6 D9).

Bournemouth – 50.6%

Draw – 25%

Leeds – 24.4%

3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.title: Spain extend De la Fuente's contract through to Euro 2032
3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.subtitle: After he led Spain to European and world titles, Luis de la Fuente's future is secured for another six years.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente will stay on as Spain's head coach through to 2032, after the Spanish Football Federation extended his contract.

De la Fuente took over in December 2022 following Luis Enrique's resignation in the wake of Spain's disappointing showing at the World Cup in Qatar, and he has enjoyed huge success in his first four years.

The 65-year-old, who spent nine years with Spain's youth teams before taking over the senior team, led them to the 2022-23 Nations League title, as well as triumphs at Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
La Roja beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the World Cup final in July to secure their second title.
De la Fuente's current deal was due to run until the end of Euro 2028, but he will now remain in his post for an additional four years, which includes a World Cup title defence as co-hosts in 2030.
"We are seeking a project of stability and confidence," RFEF president Rafael Louzan said.
"This proposal is based on confidence in Luis de la Fuente and the sporting project he leads, for a multi-year cycle of competitions and major tournaments.
"We are talking about the most decorated coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, Luis de la Fuente deserves a long future at the RFEF."
Spain are unbeaten in their last 38 matches in all competitions, the longest-ever run by any European or South American team in history.
At this summer's World Cup, they lifted the trophy having conceded just one goal in their eight games, the fewest goals conceded by any team in a World Cup-winning campaign.
In total, De la Fuente has taken charge of 49 matches across all competitions, winning 37 of those (D10 L2). His team have scored 126 goals during that time and conceded just 35.
He will now look to reach another Nations League final – having also done so in 2024-25 before losing to Portugal on penalties.
Spain begin their new campaign away to England on September 26, with a double header against Croatia to come on either side of hosting Czechia.

3n1my5dh3edy1lu9f0n2w5z7i.title: Como 2-0 Sassuolo: No Paz, no problem as Douvikas grabs a double
3n1my5dh3edy1lu9f0n2w5z7i.subtitle: Nico Paz did not feature from the bench, but Como did not miss their star man as Tasos Douvikas netted twice against Sassuolo.
paragraphs: Tasos Douvikas' double propelled in-form Como to a 2-0 victory over Sassuolo on Saturday.
Three days on from their rampant 4-1 win over Manchester United in the Champions League, Cesc Fabregas' team made it back-to-back Serie A victories.
Nico Paz, who was the star of the show against Man Utd, did not come off the bench for Como at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, but Fabregas' men did not need their star player.
Instead, Douvikas did the damage as Como closed the gap, at least temporarily, on Serie A leaders Inter.
Lucas Da Cunha strayed offside, resulting in an early Como goal being ruled out.
Douvikas struck the post with a deflected attempt, before Sassuolo had a goal disallowed when Kieron Bowie was flagged offside as he teed up Darryl Bakola.

Jayden Addai, Luis Milla and Jacobo Ramon were brought on at half-time by Fabregas, and those changes had the desired impact, with Como taking a 49th-minute lead when Maxence Caqueret set up Douvikas to finish.
Douvikas doubled up on the hour after latching onto Kaiki's cutback, wrapping up another win for high-flying Como.
Douvikas rediscovers home comforts
It was a surprise to see Fabregas decide not to turn to Paz at half-time, but he clearly felt there was enough quality on the pitch to get the job done for Como.
Douvikas proved his point, as he netted for the fourth straight game in all competitions. It is the first time in his career he has achieved that while playing in one of Europe's big five leagues.
These strikes were his first in a home Serie A match for the first time since last March (against Pisa); his previous six goals had all come on the road.
Douvikas is just the second player, and first non-Italian, to score 20 or more goals for Como in Serie A (21), after Vittorio Ghiandi (32).
And though Fabregas had to make some changes at half-time, Como were ultimately comfortable. They generated chances worth 1.65 expected goals, while Sassuolo only registered 0.24 xG.

Como are now on 17 points, which is a record for the club after eight matchdays of a Serie A campaign. They have also scored 14 goals, their best return after their first eight matches (also 14 in 1950-51).

3nyybvcksjnt1qb7txyfg2qsd.title: De la Fuente tips Yamal for future Ballon d'Or glory after missing out to Kane
3nyybvcksjnt1qb7txyfg2qsd.subtitle: Lamine Yamal finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting, but Luis de la Fuente expects him to win the award in the future.
paragraphs: Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has tipped Lamine Yamal to win the Ballon d'Or on multiple occasions in the future, after the winger was beaten to the 2026 prize by Harry Kane.
Having helped Barcelona retain their LaLiga title and Spain win the World Cup during the voting period, Yamal finished third, with Kane scooping the prize and Kylian Mbappe placing second.
Yamal tallied 41 goal involvements across all competitions in 2025-26 (24 goals, 17 assists), with only five players from Europe's top five leagues managing more.

The teenager also attempted (429) and completed (225) more dribbles than any other player in that group, as well as ranking joint-sixth for chances created (118) with 59 of those coming after a carry – only Vinicius Junior (60) had more.

In the lead-up to Monday's award ceremony in London, De la Fuente repeatedly said the prize should go to a Spain player, with Yamal, Pau Cubarsi, Marc Cucurella, Rodri, Ferran Torres and Fabian Ruiz all nominated.
And the Roja boss does not expect missing out on this year's award to affect Yamal in the future.

"Lamine Yamal is going to win many Ballon d'Or awards, many individual trophies, but more importantly, he is going to win many more team trophies. I know he values that more," he said, as quoted by ESPN.
"He needs to be calm because we know who he is and what he represents. We know the potential he has, the great footballer he is and the great person he is."

Yamal did win the Kopa Trophy – awarded to the best player under the age of 21 – for a third straight year, and Barcelona president Joan Laporta expects him to be motivated by missing out on the top prize.
"What Lamine has done is unique," Laporta said in an interview with Cadena Cope. "He's won the young player award for the third consecutive time.
"We are very proud of him. He deserves everything. We will all help him to be even more motivated next year to get this award.
"Now we have to give him love, which he deserves. All of us, together, will cheer him on so he can win this award next year."

3onk266gtfe91qldkgs86idkv.title: ​Arsenal 2-0 Everton: Konsa and Gabriel goals take champions level with Man City
3onk266gtfe91qldkgs86idkv.subtitle: Arsenal took advantage of Manchester City's slip-up against Aston Villa, as they beat Everton 2-0 to pull level with the league leaders.
paragraphs: Goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes helped Arsenal to a 2-0 win over Everton, taking them level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

In teeming rain at Emirates Stadium, Arsenal's centre-backs provided the key moments in front of goal, with Konsa netting for the first time since his arrival from Aston Villa and Gabriel making the points safe midway through the second half.

Everton had some brief moments in attack, most notably when David Raya won a one-v-one duel with Thierno Barry at 1-0, but Mikel Arteta's side held on to take advantage of City's earlier defeat at Aston Villa.

Arsenal had been uncharacteristically poor from set-pieces at the start of this season, failing to score from a dead ball in 12 matches across all competitions (excluding penalties), but their old strength returned in the seventh minute.
Gabriel's flick-on from a Martin Odegaard delivery had Jordan Pickford scrambling, and with Vitalii Mykolenko falling to ground at the far post, there was nobody to stop Konsa from prodding home.
Tyrique George curled wide as Everton threatened on the break, though Arsenal also had chances to extend their advantage through Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke.

Everton were almost gifted an equaliser when Ben White's lacklustre header played Barry through, but Raya was equal to his outside-of-the-boot flick, then Mikel Merino nodded over from a Declan Rice free-kick in the final action of the first half.
The start of the second half saw the opportunities dry up at both ends, with Gabriel playing on following an injury scare and Pickford falling on a threatening left-wing centre from Eze.

But Arsenal doubled their advantage when a neat move culminated in White making an overlapping run and crossing to the far post, where Gabriel rose highest to head into the left side of the goal with 68 minutes on the clock.

Everton never really looked likely to cause any late nerves among the home fans, with Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall heading wide from their best chance and eight minutes of stoppage time passed without incident.
Arsenal defenders show forwards how to finish
Arsenal are still yet to settle on a favoured formula up front this season, with Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz battling it out to start as their striker.
Matters worsened in midweek, too, as key winger Bukayo Saka suffered a quadriceps injury that could keep him out for two months, during the Gunners' 2-2 UEFA Champions League draw with Bayern Munich.

Luckily for Arteta, he has defenders who are very capable of threatening in advanced areas. In Konsa and Gabriel, Arsenal saw two centre-backs score in the same game for the first time since February 2024, when Gabriel and William Saliba netted in a 6-0 rout of West Ham.
Gabriel's goal was his 21st in the Premier League, but his first that has not come from a set-piece.
The Gunners were ultimately good value for their victory, having racked up 20 shots and 1.77 expected goals, compared to Everton's eight attempts and 0.48 xG.
Arteta's side put up 0.79 xG from set pieces alone, with their physicality proving too much for an Everton side that was without Jarrad Branthwaite due to concussion protocols.

          England vs Czechia Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 6, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Tuesday's UEFA Nations League matchup with our England vs Czechia prediction and preview, as Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions look to make it three straight wins.
England hit a magnificent seven against Croatia on Saturday, making it back-to-back wins in their UEFA Nations League campaign in some style.
Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice each, while Jude Bellingham was also on target and laid on three assists. Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also scored in an emphatic victory.
Thomas Tuchel's side have scored 11 goals in the three games across this extended international window, with one more match to come as Czechia visit Wembley on Tuesday.
England beat Czechia 2-0 in Prague last week, with Gordon and Kane scoring, and the Three Lions should be confident of another victory in this encounter.
It was a routine win for England, aided by Pavel Sulc's red card midway through the first half.
Tuchel has plenty of positives to take from the past couple of weeks, particularly in attack.

Across their last four games in all competitions, England have won 6-4 against France and 7-0 against Croatia. It's the first time they've scored 6+ goals in two different games in a calendar year since 2019, while they last did so in three different games in 1908.
Gordon has scored in each of his last four England appearances. The last player, other than Kane, to score in five in a row for the Three Lions was Wayne Rooney between October 2014 and March 2015.

The Barcelona winger has actually netted two headed goals in his last two England appearances. Those goals seem to have even come as a surprise to him, with the former Newcastle player joking, “I’m probably the worst header of the ball you will ever see” after nodding in his first against Czechia last week. Across 248 total club appearances, he has not scored a single header.
Other than Kane, Gordon is the only player to be directly involved in a goal in five consecutive England appearances across the last 10 years (four goals, two assists).

Against Croatia, Saka scored two right-footed goals in a match for the first time in his senior career for club and country (378 appearances). Bellingham, meanwhile, was directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time. He is the first player to record three assists in a game for England since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.

The captain is set to equal a record in this match. If he features, he will make his 125th England appearance, which will see him equal Peter Shilton as the all-time most-capped player in the Three Lions' history.
With his double last time out, Kane became the first player to score 10+ goals in three different calendar years for England: 11 in 2026, 16 in 2021 and 12 in 2019.
Kane has netted 89 goals across his 124 caps to date, and a flurry here could take him even closer to the century before 2026 is up.
They sit bottom of the group after losing their opening three games, going down 2-1 to Croatia and 3-1 to Spain, either side of that defeat to England.
Santi Denia has lost all three of his games in charge of Czechia, and could be the second manager to lose their first four matches with the nation after Václav Ježek in 1973, then as Czechoslovakia.
In fact, Czechia have lost five of their last six games in all competitions (D1), including each of the last four in a row. They last lost five consecutively between July 1972 and March 1973.

Czechia's recent poor form is not the only thing going against them heading into this match. They have lost six of their eight competitive meetings with England (W2), though they have always responded to back-to-back losses with a win, and have lost their last two.
England are also unbeaten in all eight of their games against Czechia at Wembley (W6 D2). In the most recent of those, the Three Lions finished their Euro 2020 group-stage campaign with a 1-0 win.

          PSG vs Barcelona: UEFA Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Dan Edwards / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Goals are guaranteed as two of Europe’s best attacking teams tussle in Paris. We look ahead to Tuesday's UEFA Champions League game with our PSG vs Barcelona prediction and preview.

The decision to modify the early rounds of the UEFA Champions League to a new, expanded Swiss model three seasons ago was not universally popular, but its habit of producing regular fixtures between Europe’s super clubs is no doubt creating a growing list of admirers.

For the second week running, back-to-back champions Paris Saint-Germain are facing one of their likeliest usurpers. They defeated Manchester City 4-2 at the Etihad Stadium on Matchday 2, producing a near-perfect opening 30 minutes that saw them open up a three-goal lead before the home fans had time to inflate their bananas.
They are now unbeaten in 12 Champions League games, one short of their record run in the competition. And despite a slow start to the season, they have won six games in a row in all competitions.

But on Matchday 3, their three-peat potential will be tested to the fullest as they play host to a Barcelona side who many would argue are currently Europe’s form team. Hansi Flick’s side have won all 11 games they have played this season, scoring a mammoth 48 goals in the process at an average of 4.4 per game. That is, of course, the most of any team from Europe’s top five divisions.

They put five past Feyenoord in the opening round of the league phase before scoring four times against Galatasaray last week. They have now scored at least four goals in four consecutive league/group phase games in this competition, the longest such run in European Cup or Champions League history.

It’s the arrival of Flick which has taken their attacking play to its current level, although their style does leave them susceptible in defence. Indeed, Flick has both the best goals-per-game ratio (3.0) and worst goals-conceded-per-game ratio (1.6) of any Barcelona manager to take charge of at least five games in the Champions League.

Barcelona's games have seen 130 goals in the Champions League since Flick took over ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. The only team to be involved in games with more goals in that time? PSG, with 134 goals.

Both squads are stacked with attacking talent. Since the start of the 2024-25 season, nine players have averaged at least one goal involvement per 90 minutes in the Champions League, and five of them play for either PSG (Ousmane Dembélé, Désiré Doué, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia) or Barcelona (Raphinha, Fermín López).

And that list doesn’t even include Europe’s most prodigious talent, Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old has already been involved in five goals in two Champions League appearances in 2026-27 (one goal, four assists), assisting two goals in each appearance. He is the youngest player to assist 2+ goals in consecutive appearances, while Raúl in 2002 is the only player in Champions League history to assist 2+ goals in three games in a row.
Of fixtures played at least 10 times in European Cup or Champions League history, only Ajax versus Bayern Munich (3.9) has a higher goals-per-game ratio than PSG versus Barcelona (3.8).

This will be the 17th time PSG have faced Barcelona (W6 D4 L6), which will be the joint-most games they have played against an opponent in major European competition (also 17 v Bayern Munich – W7 D1 L9).

PSG have won their last two games against Barcelona, while only Bayern Munich have won three consecutive matches against them in the European Cup or Champions League (a run of six – May 2015 to October 2022).

This game looks a hard one to call on paper, and the Opta supercomputer agrees. PSG are slight favourites, with a 39.7% of beating Barcelona for a third game in a row. But Barcelona are close behind, with a 37.7% chance of winning in Paris.
The game was drawn in 22.6% of simulations.
PSG: Matvey Safonov, Achraf Hakimi, Willian Pacho, Illia Zabarnyi, Lucas Digne, Fabián Ruiz, Vitinha, João Neves, Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.
Barcelona: Joan García, João Cancelo, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, Xavi Espart, Rodri, Pedri, Dani Olmo, Lamine Yamal, Raphinha, Anthony Gordon.

4187436E1239850926CE3036282E6B20.title: James Trafford’s inclusion hints at how Thomas Tuchel wants to evolve England’s style
4187436E1239850926CE3036282E6B20.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesJames Trafford’s inclusion hints at how Thomas Tuchel wants to evolve England’s styleShareJames Trafford has been given an opportunity to prove himself as England’s first-choice goalkeeper of the future.

Had it not been for James Trafford, Spain might have been out of sight before England could even threaten a comeback from 1-0 down in their UEFA Nations League opener on Saturday. The 23-year-old’s stop to deny Ferran Torres from doubling the world champions’ lead after only 16 minutes was particularly important.

That Trafford was handed the start by Thomas Tuchel in the first place surprised many. While it was expected that the England manager would experiment with a handful of different options due to injury and a willingness to broaden horizons after the World Cup, few had predicted a change of goalkeeper.

And yet Tuchel’s selection of Trafford to face Spain hinted at an evolution of England’s playing style. Jordan Pickford might be something of an icon for the Three Lions, earning 91 caps over nine years, but he has never been the most adept with his feet. This is where Trafford offers something different.

It hasn’t been easy for Trafford to get to this point in his career. He had to leave Manchester City to gain first team experience, which he received over two seasons at Burnley. When Trafford returned to City last year, it was on the promise that he would be first-choice at the Etihad Stadium. A shaky start to the season, however, pushed Manchester City into the market for Gianluigi Donnarumma.

A lesser goalkeeper, and a meeker character, might have shied away from taking on another challenge after such a disappointment, but Trafford has shone for Leeds United this season, joining the Elland Road club for a reported £40m this summer. Tuchel clearly likes what he sees in the 23-year-old, and there’s a lot to admire.

Trafford’s save percentage of 87% is the highest of any goalkeeper in the Premier League this season with only Emi Martínez averaging more saves per 90 minutes. The 23-year-old has been a big part of Leeds’ early-season success with Daniel Farke’s team flying high in fifth place. Some have speculated they could contend for European qualification.

A strong start to the season has seemingly pushed Trafford more firmly into Tuchel’s thoughts. While Trafford was part of England’s World Cup squad, there was never any realistic chance of Pickford losing his place. He’s been a key part of the national team for the majority of the past decade.

At the World Cup, though, Pickford wasn’t at his best. He might have done better in certain moments. Some fans still argue he should have saved Enzo Fernández’s goal for Argentina in the semi-final. Jude Bellingham seemed to make this point as he mouthed to Pickford “It’s [in] the middle of the goal” in the immediate aftermath.

Pickford also let in a shot at the near post against DR Congo. Even when the Everton goalkeeper kept the ball out of his net, he contributed to the defensive nervousness that characterised many of England’s performances at this summer’s World Cup. Pickford wasn’t immune from criticism.

For the first time in a number of years, the opportunity is there for someone else to grab the starting jersey and Trafford made the most of his chance against Spain, even if the match ended in defeat for England. Tuchel is expected to stick with Trafford for Tuesday’s follow-up match against Czechia.

🧤 Konstantinos Tzolakis is the only goalkeeper who has a higher rating than James Trafford in the Premier League this season! James Trafford is STARTING for England tonight, displacing the regular Jordan Pickford… who’s third in the ratings! 👀 pic.twitter.com/mT1ZD0CmGl

“We use the Nations League to see where we are with the other goalkeepers,” said Tuchel when asked to explain why he decided to start Trafford and bench Pickford with Jason Steele another option. “There was no reason from performances to open up this position for competition.

“I think it’s necessary with every other player that we are aware of ‘what if’. If a player that starts a season well, like Traff at Leeds, [he] has the chance to prove it and to play in our style. We just need to see it at some point. We use this competition to actually give him the chance to push on.”

Trafford wasn’t the only experimental selection for the match against Spain. Jarell Quansah started at right back while Myles Lewis-Skelly was deployed in central midfield. Both players demonstrated why they should be taken seriously as important figures for the future. Lewis-Skelly in particular who was missed when he was withdrawn after 70 minutes.

Further opportunities will be given to other young players between now and Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup beyond that. It is, however, difficult to envisage another goalkeeper emerging with a stronger case than Trafford’s to be England’s next number one, although Dean Henderson might have something to say about that.

Tuchel bore the brunt of the criticism for England’s World Cup failure. The German still hasn’t fully accepted culpability for what went wrong in the semi-final against Argentina, but his team selection in the loss to Spain at least demonstrated a willingness to try something different.

          LASK 3-6 Liverpool Stats: Barcola Bags Hat-Trick in Big Champions League Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Liverpool enjoyed a 6-3 win over LASK in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, with Bradley Barcola starring, though Andoni Iraola may be concerned by their defending.
Bradley Barcola opened his Liverpool account with a hat-trick, though Andoni Iraola's team were found wanting at the back in an entertaining 6-3 Champions League victory over LASK.
Barcola had made a slow start to his Liverpool career following his big-money move from Paris Saint-Germain, but the two-time European champion put those troubles behind him at Raiffeisen Arena.

His hat-trick goal put Liverpool 5-1 up midway through the second half, with Lewis Koumas then nudging the visitors into an even more commanding position, though some dismal Reds defending allowed LASK a glimmer of hope heading into the latter stages.
Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the 22nd minute, heading home from Kostas Tsimikas' inswinging corner.
And Liverpool doubled their advantage within 96 seconds, as Koumas wriggled free and teed up Barcola, who confidently swept into the left-hand corner.

Liverpool's stand-in captain Tsimikas did brilliantly to pick out Koumas soon after, but the youngster's neat finish was disallowed for offside, before Ryan Gravenberch's low shot bounced out off the post.
But there was no denying Barcola in the 37th minute, with the Frenchman coolly slotting in his second Liverpool goal after latching onto Florian Wirtz‘s sliderule pass.
Liverpool had their fourth as Jeremie Frimpong headed in from Tsimikas' centre six minutes into the second half.
Iraola switched his centre-backs on the hour, with Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez coming on. Within moments, Yvan Dibango found Robert Ljubicic, who drilled in.
Yet Liverpool swiftly restored their four-goal cushion as Barcola slammed into a gaping net after meeting Frimpong's cross.
Barcola went close with a cheeky lob as he hunted down a fourth, but the Reds did not have to wait long to score again, with Koumas tucking Frimpong's cross under Lukas Jungwirth.
Dibango grabbed his second assist as he lobbed in for Florian Flecker to head into an open goal, with Van Dijk and Gomez again caught out.

Liverpool's defence was found wanting once more in the 77th minute. Dibango put another brilliant ball into the box, and Flecker hammered in, though there was to be no famous comeback for the Austrian champions.
Liverpool suffered their first defeat under Iraola when they went down 3-0 to Manchester City last weekend, so a trip to a Champions League minnow was an ideal opportunity to get back on track.

Iraola took the chance to rest Van Dijk from the start, naming Liverpool's third-youngest team in a Champions League game, but he stuck with Barcola and Wirtz, with the latter having come in for criticism from Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher in the wake of the defeat to Man City.

But Wirtz and Barcola were Liverpool's chief threats as they recorded the most shots by an away team in the first half of a Champions League match on record (19), and went three goals up by half-time in a match in the competition for the first time since April 2018, when they led Man City 3-0.
Wirtz pulled the strings before the break, though it was the excellent Tsimikas who led Liverpool creatively, laying on six chances, including his two assists.
Barcola helped himself to his first senior hat-trick on his 206th appearance – he is Liverpool's first treble scorer in any competition since Luis Diaz vs Bayer Leverkusen in November 2024.
Koumas, meanwhile, became the youngest player to score and assist in a Champions League game for Liverpool, breaking the record of Steven Gerrard.

44qjlbx404q1qynlpaghvn8v.title: Hell is Real derby just another game for Denkey and playoff-chasing Cincinnati
44qjlbx404q1qynlpaghvn8v.subtitle: FC Cincinnati and the Columbus Crew are in the mix for a spot in the playoffs, and they square off in the Hell is Real derby at TQL Stadium.
paragraphs: Kevin Denkey insisted the rest of FC Cincinnati's regular-season matches need to look like playoff games as they prepare to take on rivals Columbus Crew this weekend.
The TQL Stadium is the venue for the latest instalment of the Hell is Real derby, with both sides aiming to boost their hopes of reaching the postseason in 2026.
Cincinnati were beaten 3-2 by the New England Revolution in midweek, with Tom Barlow's opener cancelled out by a Dor Turgeman brace and Joshua Wynder's strike.
It's a result that leaves Pat Noonan's side ninth in the Eastern Conference and three points ahead of New York City FC as the end of the regular season draws nearer.
"We need to take points. We need to win. It's against Columbus, we need to win," Denkey said of Cincinnati's clash with Columbus. "I'm not even looking at it as a derby.
"We just need to win games and not lose games and take points to go to the playoffs. There is urgency. These games need to look like playoff games from us."
Noonan, however, bemoaned his team's inability to follow up their 3-1 win against Atlanta United against New England, adding consistency would be key down the final stretch.
"Disappointing follow-up to what was a strong road win, and just can't carry momentum in back-to-back games, and certainly in front of our home crowd," Noonan conceded.

"It hurts losing. Forget having to push late to try to find a win. We need to find ways to not have to push so much towards the end and take as much risk by conceding less goals. At this stage, we need to defend in a better way and not rely on late dramatics to carry us."
Columbus come into the clash after a statement victory, beating Charlotte FC 3-1 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field to stay within touching distance of the postseason places.
Idan Toklomati had given Charlotte a 17th-minute lead, but Brais Mendez's left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner hauled Columbus level just before the break.
And two goals in two minutes from Anass Zaroury and Taha Habroune turned the game on its head, with the Crew now four points behind ninth-place Cincinnati in the East.
Laurent Courtois lauded his team for their display, describing their victory as an "incredible performance", highlighting his team's togetherness in both attack and defence.
"Obviously, they had an incredible performance," interim head coach Courtois said. "Really happy because they worked hard and they try a lot. Yeah, it's good to see.
"We tried to put in a structure where they could express their best individual quality. A lot of players can go forward and have the quality to create chances and score.
"You want to keep a balance and structure where we are solid defensively, too. Last time out they did both, so it was great."
Cincinnati – Kevin Denkey
Denkey (six) and Tom Barlow (three) have combined to score nine of Cincinnati's last 10 regular-season goals dating back to September 12, including the last seven in a row.
Both players have scored at least once in each of Cincinnati's last two matches, though Denkey is the club's top scorer in the MLS in 2026 with 17, four more than Evander.
Columbus Crew – Brais Mendez
But Columbus have a dynamic duo of their own in Mendez and Habroune, who have each scored in the club's last two matches.
One of Mendez or Habroune has scored five of the Crew's last eight goals dating back to September 19, and they will be hoping to have a similar impact here.
MATCH PREDICTION: CINCINNATI WIN

Including last season's playoffs, Cincinnati and the Crew have alternated wins over the last five meetings, with Columbus recording a 2-1 home win in July. The only time either team won multiple regular-season matches against the other in a single season was the Crew in 2020 (two wins in four meetings).

Cincinnati's defeat to New England took the total number of goals scored in their matches this regular season to 128 (68 scored, 60 conceded), an average of 4.6 per match. The most goals scored and conceded by a club in a single MLS season is 136 by Inter Miami in 2025.

Columbus, meanwhile, have won four of their last five matches in all competitions (L1) after losing seven of the previous eight (W1). Only one of those four wins has come on the road as the Crew have failed to win nine of their last 10 away from home (D2 L7).
Columbus Crew – 28.1%

Cincinnati's defeat to New England took the total number of goals scored in their matches this regular season to 128 (68 scored, 60 conceded), an average of 4.6 per match. The most goals scored and conceded by a club in a single MLS season is 136 by Inter Miami in 2025.

Columbus, meanwhile, have won four of their last five matches in all competitions (L1) after losing seven of the previous eight (W1). Only one of those four wins has come on the road as the Crew have failed to win nine of their last 10 away from home (D2 L7).

          Bayern Munich vs Borussia Dortmund Prediction: Bundesliga Der Klassiker Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 29, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
This season's first edition of Der Klassiker takes place at the Allianz Arena with the two teams sitting level on points. We look ahead to the game with our Bayern Munich vs Borussia Dortmund prediction and preview.
It has been a positive week for everyone connected to Bayern Munich.

Harry Kane‘s Ballon d'Or triumph made him the first Bayern player to win football's top individual prize since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981, and the first Bundesliga recipient overall since Borussia Dortmund icon Matthias Sammer in 1996.

And things could get better for Bayern on Saturday, as they host Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker, which will be Kane's first game back since Monday's award ceremony. He was an unused substitute for Wednesday's 6-1 DFB-Pokal rout of Magdeburg.
Both teams have 17 points on the board after seven matchdays (both W5 D2), making them the only remaining unbeaten teams in the 2026-27 Bundesliga.

In two of the last three Bundesliga seasons, Bayern have handed BVB their first defeat of the campaign – they beat their rivals 2-1 in Munich on Matchday 7 of 2025-26, having triumphed 4-0 in Dortmund on MD10 of 2023-24.

In addition, Bayern are unbeaten in their last 21 league matches when playing as leaders against the side in second place (W13 D8), the longest such run by any team in Bundesliga history. Their last defeat in such a fixture came in January 2015, 4-1 at Wolfsburg.

And when you have the best player in the world on your side, you will always feel you have a chance. Kane has scored six goals in his six previous Bundesliga matches against Dortmund, including a hat-trick in his first Klassiker (November 2023) and a brace in February.

But Kane, clearly, is not the only star attacker that Niko Kovac's visitors must keep a close eye on. His nine goal involvements (four goals, five assists) in the Bundesliga this season is only matched by teammate Michael Olise (six goals, three assists).
Olise has recorded at least one goal and one assist in three of his last four Bundesliga matches, as many games with one of each as he managed in his previous 23 outings.

The former Crystal Palace star scored the clinching goal as Bayern defeated Freiburg 3-1 last weekend, with assistant coach Aaron Danks overseeing that game in place of Vincent Kompany, who is still recovering after collapsing at the club's training ground last week.
Kompany was discharged from hospital on Wednesday and is “doing well” according to club director Max Eberl, but it will be a while longer before the Belgian is back in the dugout as he recovers.
Bayern's 25 goals this season is the most in the Bundesliga, while they also boast the second-best defensive record in the division with six goals conceded.

And a remarkable 18 of those 25 goals have been scored in their first three home matches of the season, a new record by any club at this stage of a campaign. Bayern have scored at least five goals in each of their last four Bundesliga home games dating back to last season, the first time they have done so in their history.

Dortmund, though, are the one Bundesliga side with a better defence than Bayern; in fact, their four goals conceded is the fewest by any team in Europe's top five leagues. BVB kept five clean sheets in their opening seven matches, equalling their club record set in 2017-18 and 2020-21.

Maximilian Beier could be their player to watch, having tallied 13 Bundesliga goal involvements in 2026 (seven goals, six assists). The only German player with more this year is Deniz Undav (17), and 11 of Dortmund's 12 Bundesliga goals this campaign have been scored while Beier has been on the pitch.
This will be the 141st competitive meeting between Bayern and Dortmund since the formation of the Bundesliga in 1963 – it is the most-played fixture in German professional football.
Bayern have suffered more defeats against Dortmund than they have versus any other opponent in all competitions (33).

However, they have lost only one of their last 17 meetings (W13 D3 L1), suffering a 2-0 home defeat under Thomas Tuchel in March 2024, which virtually ended their title hopes as Bayer Leverkusen went on to claim the trophy.

Bayern did the double over BVB last season, triumphing 2-1 at home last October and earning a thrilling 3-2 success on the road in February, with Joshua Kimmich scoring an 87th-minute winner in the latter game.

          Liverpool's Evolution: From Survival Mode to WSL Top-Four Contenders
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Are Liverpool genuine top-four contenders in the WSL? We look at the transformation behind their impressive start, the performance that almost earned them a result against Man City, and how their players are helping to drive renewed hope.
Just four months ago, the idea of Liverpool challenging for a UEFA Women's Champions League place would have seemed improbable.
The Reds finished 11th in the Women's Super League in 2025-26, ending the season eight points clear of bottom-placed Leicester City but recording their second-lowest finish in the competition.
Their 2025-26 campaign began in disastrous fashion under the former Manchester City boss Gareth Taylor, as the Reds failed to win any of their opening 12 league matches (D4 L8).
A six-game losing streak at the start of the season set the tone, including an opening weekend loss to rivals Everton at Anfield (4-1) followed by a shock defeat at Leicester City on MD2.
Liverpool found themselves rooted to the foot of the table across the winter break with just three points collected, and facing serious questions about their future direction.
Their struggles continued into the start of 2026 as Liverpool's winless league run reached 15 matches, the longest in their WSL history.
Yet, even amid the poor results, there were signs they could compete.

During that difficult run, Liverpool lost to both Arsenal and Man City by just a single-goal margin, with both winning goals coming in the final four minutes. It was enough to suggest that the gap to the league's elite was not quite as wide as the table implied.
There were also off-field circumstances surrounding the club that cannot be ignored when looking back at Liverpool's 2025-26 WSL campaign.

The passing of former manager Matt Beard in September 2025 cast a shadow over the season. Beard was one of the most influential figures in the club's history, overseeing 106 WSL matches across two spells and guiding them to back-to-back league titles in 2013 and 2014. Against that backdrop, Liverpool's struggles became easier to contextualise.
Taylor’s first WSL victory with the Reds came at home against Tottenham in January, and while Liverpool won only three more league matches across the campaign, it proved enough to secure survival.
Now, less than a year later, the picture looks very different.

Liverpool began 2026-27 with a convincing 4-0 victory over Charlton Athletic, their first win in a season opener since 2023. The four-goal margin was also their biggest in a WSL match since a 4-0 victory over Leicester in May 2024.

They followed that with a 1-1 draw against Tottenham on MD2, a result that arguably failed to reflect the balance of play, before pushing Man City all the way on MD3. An unfortunate 89th-minute own goal by Grace Fisk ultimately denied Liverpool what would have been their first point against City since May 2023.

Results alone, however, only tell part of the story. The underlying numbers point to a Liverpool side that are playing with greater ambition than we saw for much of last season. They are pressing higher, spending more time in possession, and showing a greater willingness to take the game to their opponents rather than simply react to them.

Of course, there are still areas to improve, but the early season data suggests a meaningful shift in Liverpool’s approach. A side that spent much of last season battling at the bottom end of the table are showing signs of being better equipped to compete with the division’s leading teams.
So, can Liverpool turn that promising start into a genuine push for a top-four finish?
They may have left Manchester empty-handed on Friday night, but Liverpool's performance arguably told a more encouraging story than the result itself.

Too often in recent seasons have meetings with the WSL's elite been exercises in damage limitation. Liverpool's approach at the Joie Stadium was markedly different. They pressed aggressively, played through City's pressure and repeatedly forced the hosts into uncomfortable situations.

          La Reina Rules: The Case for Alexia Putellas’ Third Ballon d’Or
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Alexia Putellas has her sights set on a third Ballon d’Or crown after spearheading Barcelona’s quadruple-winning campaign, but does her 2025–26 season make her the rightful frontrunner?
It is football’s most prestigious individual honour, and one of its most hotly disputed.

The Ballon d’Or has long divided opinion, with winners ultimately decided by an international panel of journalists across FIFA’s top 100 ranked countries. Every year, the shortlist sparks fresh debate over who has done enough to claim the sport’s most coveted individual prize and, just as importantly, who has been overlooked.
The 2026 women’s shortlist is no exception.

Questions have already been raised over the representation of the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), with only a handful of its players making the final 30. In a league that continues to produce some of the world’s most influential talent, the lack of recognition has reignited a familiar criticism: is the Ballon d’Or still too Eurocentric?

There is a compelling case that the NWSL’s calendar complicates the picture. Running from February to November, its season does not align neatly with the European football calendar, potentially leaving its players at a disadvantage when performances are assessed across a season spanning 3 August 2025 to 19 July 2026.
And the omissions are difficult to ignore.

Washington Spirit’s Trinity Rodman ranked first among NWSL players for goal involvements (21) and second for goals (14) during the assessment period yet failed to make the cut. Cloé Lacasse, Croix Bethune and Pietra Tordin, who each registered nine assists, were also left off the 30-player shortlist. Their absence has fuelled debate over whether the Ballon d’Or voting process gives sufficient weight to performances beyond Europe, though it is a continent with plenty of valid contenders.

Manchester City lifted their first WSL trophy in over a decade last season, spearheaded by the prolific Khadija Shaw, whose 21 goals and 25 goal involvements ranked first and second respectively across all players within Europe’s top five leagues.
Bayern Munich’s Klara Bühl also made her mark, leading the way across Europe’s top five leagues for assists (14) and chances created (60) over the same period.
Then there'sClàudia Pina cementing herself as a premium striker for Barcelona as she topped the 2025-26 Liga F scoring charts.
The competition is formidable, but one name continues to command attention: Alexia Putellas.

The current London City Lionesses midfielder has already etched her name into football history, claiming back-to-back Ballon d’Or Féminin titles in 2021 and 2022. A third Ballon d’Or would further cement her legacy, but past glory can only carry a player so far.
So does Putellas deserve the crown for her performances across her final campaign with Barcelona?

La Blaugrana completed a quadruple in 2025–26, lifting the Liga F, UEFA Women’s Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España titles, all while three-time Ballon d’Or winner Aitana Bonmatí spent five months sidelined. At the heart of their success was Putellas, whose influence extended far beyond the scoresheet.

Putellas – nicknamed La Reina – finished the campaign with 21 goals and 13 assists across all competitions, ranking third and second respectively among all players. She created 89 chances, 19 of which were big chances, and completed 965 passes ending in the final third – the highest tally among players across those four competitions. Her expected assists figure of 13.1 was also the highest.
In Liga F, she finished joint-sixth for assists (7) and fourth for open-play chances created (40).

Putellas was equally influential in Barcelona’s build-up in open-play across 2025-26. Across Europe’s top five leagues, only Pina (199), Vicky López (183) and Georgia Stanway (168) recorded more sequence involvements ending in an open-play shot than Putellas (151).

Only teammate Clara Serrajordi, with 1,317 attempted and 1,188 completed passes, and Bayern Munich’s Stanway, with 1,283 attempted and 1,088 completed, surpassed Putellas’ respective totals of 1,140 and 931 passes in the opposition half across Europe’s top five leagues. Putellas ranked first for passes ending in the final third (780) and third for successful passes into that zone (599). These figures underlined her ability not only to orchestrate Barcelona’s possession but to turn it into sustained attacking pressure.
Her campaign, however, did not begin at quite the same pace.

480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.title: Greenwood: Man City there to win in Champions League
480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.subtitle: Manchester City return to the Women's Champions League after a season-long absence, and Alex Greenwood is eyeing a deep run.
paragraphs: Alex Greenwood says Manchester City are "going to give it absolutely everything" to try and win the Women's Champions League this season.
City were absent from last season's campaign, but they are back in the competition following their Women's Super League title success in 2025-26.
Andree Jeglertz enjoyed a stellar first season with the team, and they have started their title defence in equally fine form, having won all three of their league games so far.
But their attention now turns to the Champions League, and they will begin their campaign away to Bayern Munich on Tuesday.

City are given the fourth-highest chance of winning the Champions League by the Opta supercomputer, though their 9.1% win probability is significantly lower than outright favourites Barcelona (41.2%).
Greenwood insists City have their eyes on the trophy, though.
"To qualify was massively important; it's an expectation that we have at this football club," Greenwood told UEFA's website.
"But every competition that we play in, we're there to win.

"We know it's going to be a challenge, but it's fantastic for the club. We're going to give it absolutely everything, like we do in every other competition, take it game by game and see how far we can go."
City are facing a German side for the first time in the Champions League.

Bayern, meanwhile, have won seven of their previous 11 matches against English teams in the competition (L4), including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
On their last Champions League appearance in 2024-25, City lost their last two away games, both by a 3-0 scoreline to Barcelona and Chelsea, respectively.
"I've played in this competition enough times to know what it presents and what the challenges are," Greenwood added.
"We worked really hard to get back in this competition where I think we belong. I'm just excited to embrace the challenge.
"Champions League, Women's Super League, whatever competition we're in, we're in it with a real elite mindset to go and win, and that's been our mentality for the last 18 months."
