          Tottenham vs London City Lionesses Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Sunday afternoon’s London derby with our Tottenham vs London City Lionesses prediction and preview, as Spurs look to cement second place in WSL table.

Since the start of April, only Chelsea (2.7) and Manchester City (2.6) have averaged more points per game in the Women's Super League than Tottenham Hotspur (2.4) and London City Lionesses (2.1). With two of the division's current top four sides going head-to-head, Sunday's clash promises to be one of the standout fixtures of the weekend.

Tottenham have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the new season, but their impressive start under Martin Ho is increasingly looking like something much more significant than simply a strong opening to the campaign.

Spurs have carried their momentum from last campaign into 2026-27, establishing themselves among the league's best in its early stages. Wins against West Ham (3-1), Crystal Palace (7-0) and Aston Villa (4-0) as well as a respectable draw at Liverpool (1-1) have them in second place.

Not only have Tottenham collected their second best points total (10) at this stage of a WSL season, but Ho has added real quality to his squad, and the transformation is evident in how his side are playing.

Each of the four longest passing sequences leading to goals in the WSL this season have belonged to Spurs. They are the only side to score following a sequence of 10 or more passes, and lead the competition for goals from build-up attacks (4), while only Manchester City (23) have produced more build-up attacks than Tottenham’s 22.
That control is translating into extraordinary attacking dominance.

Tottenham have attempted 77 shots while accumulating an expected goals (xG) of 9.3 , becoming the first team in WSL history to register 35 or more shots in consecutive games – 42 against Crystal Palace and another 35 against Aston Villa.
At the heart of that attacking transformation is a squad combining proven WSL quality with exciting young talent.

Victoria Pelova is the joint-leading scorer in the WSL this season after hitting braces in each of Tottenham’s last two matches. Another double against London City would make her just the fifth player to score multiple goals in three consecutive WSL appearances, and the first since Rachel Daly in May 2023.

Alongside her, 21-year-old Signe Gaupset has made her presence felt. Against Aston Villa on MD4, the Norwegian became the youngest player in WSL history to create eight chances from open play in a single match. She leads the competition this season for both chances created (18) and assists (three).

So this isn’t simply a Tottenham side getting results. Ho has built a team capable of controlling possession, constructing attacks patiently and overwhelming opponents, and the early evidence suggests Spurs are becoming an increasingly serious force in the WSL.
London City Lionesses have lived up to much of the early hype following another ambitious summer transfer window that brought a host of established stars to the club.
But if their ambition is to challenge the WSL’s leading sides and compete for Champions League qualification, these are the games in which they will want to make a statement.

They arrive at the BetWright Stadium with momentum after a 2-0 victory over Brighton on MD4, a  result delivered their first clean sheet in 14 league matches, although they have only once previously recorded successive WSL shutouts, against Liverpool and West Ham in October 2025.
There was also a significant moment at the other end of the pitch, with former Ballon d'or winner Alexia Putellas scoring her first goal for the Bromley-based side.
The Spaniard’s strike ended her longest top-flight goal drought since 2017, having gone seven league appearances without scoring.
And history suggests that when Putellas finds the net, her team usually wins: she has finished on the winning side in 129 of the last 130 league matches in which she has scored.
Putellas (19) also leads her London City teammates for attacking sequence involvements in the WSL this term, though Daniëlle van de Donk (18) and Grace Geyoro (17)  follow close behind.
With London City’s star names beginning to make their mark, Sunday represents another important test of just how quickly this ambitious team can establish itself among the WSL’s leading sides.

          Brentford 1-2 Liverpool: Muñoz and Isak Earn Reds Three Points Against Nine-Man Bees
        
      
                          
                      Oct 17, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Brentford were beaten in the Premier League for the first time this season after having two players sent off. Re-live this clash with our Brentford vs Liverpool stats page.
Yehor Yarmoliuk and Vitaly Janelt were both sent off for Brentford as Liverpool came from behind to win 2-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday.
Yarmoliuk saw red for thrusting his head into Jérémy Jacquet eight minutes into first-half stoppage time, shortly after Keane Lewis-Potter‘s thumping header had given the Bees the lead.

And that moment proved costly as Brentford suffered their first defeat of the Premier League season, with Víctor Muñoz and Alexander Isak – the latter on his return from injury – scoring to flip the game on its head.

The hosts caused Liverpool a few nervy moments even with 10 men, but Janelt's second yellow card in second-half stoppage time killed their hopes of an equaliser as the Reds leapfrogged them to go fifth in the table.

Jacquet made a strong block to thwart Michael Kayode from Brentford's first chance, but Liverpool should have scored on the counter from the resulting corner, with Bradley Barcola‘s lob drifting wide after Janelt's poor header gifted him possession.

Another excellent recovery challenge from Jacquet put Igor Thiago off after Dango Ouattara unselfishly attempted to square the ball for his teammate, before Liverpool had a penalty overturned following a VAR review.

Referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Ouattara slid in on Alexis Mac Allister, but replays showed the Brentford man flicked the ball away with his heel and the spot-kick was cancelled after review.
Brentford then hit the front in the 44th minute, with Liverpool's defence standing off Thiago and allowing him to cross for Lewis-Potter, whose header sailed into the top-right corner.
But the Bees would have to play the entire second half with 10 men due to a petulant act from Yarmoliuk, who headbutted Jacquet while the players were jostling in preparation for a Liverpool corner.

The visitors did not truly threaten their former goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher until Mac Allister had a long-range attempt beaten away just before the hour mark, but their next attack resulted in the equaliser as Muñoz raced onto Florian Wirtz‘s pass, cut back onto his left foot, then steered his finish into the bottom-left corner.
It was 2-1 soon after, with Isak drilling home from the left side of the area after Barcola nodded Mac Allister's deep delivery down.

Barcola almost put the game beyond Brentford when his curling attempt bounced off the crossbar, but when an enterprising run from substitute Rio Ngumoha ended with a cynical foul from Janelt, who received his marching orders, Liverpool could finally breathe easily.

Having suffered a minor thigh injury while representing Sweden during the international break, Isak was forced to sit out Liverpool's 3-0 Premier League loss to Manchester City, in addition to their 6-3 UEFA Champions League victory over LASK.
But the striker will have been relishing his return to action this weekend, as Brentford are among his favourite teams to face in the Premier League.
He has now scored on all five of his appearances against the Bees in the competition (four for Newcastle United), only scoring in as many matches against Nottingham Forest and Tottenham.
Andoni Iraola, meanwhile, had never beaten Brentford in six attempts in charge of Bournemouth (D2 L4), so Saturday's win should be a cathartic one for the Liverpool boss.

And another assist for Wirtz – who has been fiercely criticised in the early weeks of the campaign – will give Iraola another reason to smile. This is the first time he has assisted in back-to-back games for Liverpool across all competitions.
The major negatives for the Reds were injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong, the latter of whom only lasted seven minutes as a half-time substitute.

Brentford, meanwhile, will have a pair of suspensions to deal with when they visit Hull City next week, having received two red cards in the same league game for the first time since April 2013, against Sheffield United in League One.

          Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Five Key Subplots That Could Decide El Clásico
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
José Mourinho is back in the dugout and he needs a Clásico victory to keep pace at the top of La Liga, but where will Barcelona vs Real Madrid be won and lost?
By the end of the weekend, most teams in La Liga will have played just 10 matches, but the title race may be very nearly over for another season.

The frontrunners and reigning champions Barcelona head into Sunday's El Clásico already six points ahead of fierce rivals Real Madrid. It’s Madrid’s biggest points difference to the league leaders at this stage of the competition since the 2012-13 season.
Hansi Flick’s side have won all nine of their games, and if they make it 10 from 10, they will have opened up a nine-point gap that could well prove unassailable.

It’s obviously too soon to say the title race would be over this early, and Atlético Madrid’s position in second place means there is quite obviously still plenty to play for regardless of the result.
But there is no escaping just how big Sunday’s match feels for Real Madrid. Lose, and they will be a long, long way back, potentially surrendering a third straight title to Barcelona.

So, can Madrid win at the Camp Nou and ignite the title race? Or will Barça extend their winning start and continue their procession towards another league trophy? Here are five key factors that may influence the result.
This game is always box office, but the return of José Mourinho to the Madrid dugout adds another layer of intrigue to this weekend’s match.

Even during the era of peak Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, Mourinho still sometimes managed to grab the headlines. The most infamous of his Clásico contributions was his eye gouge on Barça assistant Tito Vilanova in the aftermath of an August 2011 Super Cup defeat.

Mourinho has naturally mellowed with age and there will (probably) be no repeat of that kind of behaviour, but there’s no questioning how much he will want to win this match. He has plenty of history with Barcelona, having once worked there as an assistant and later been turned down for the manager’s role.

His presence will add an extra spice to the game, and while these meetings are less vindictive occasions these days, Mourinho will have no problem with resorting to some of the game’s darker arts if he believes they will help his team win. That will only add to the entertainment for the neutral.
It’s worth noting how good his record is against Barcelona despite the fact that his last spell at Madrid meant facing Messi, Xavi, Andrés Iniesta and Pep Guardiola.

When he left Madrid, he was on a five-game unbeaten streak in Clásicos in all competitions (W3 D2), so he could become only the club’s third manager ever to remain unbeaten in six consecutive games against Barcelona, after Miguel Muñoz between 1962 and 1965 (seven games, W7) and Vicente del Bosque between 2001 and 2003 (seven games, W2 D5).

It’s a stark contrast to the 5-0 defeat in his first match in this fixture, which remains Madrid’s heaviest league defeat this century. That result will have stung Mourinho badly and may even still hurt 15 years on. He’ll be desperate to get a result here.
But while a win would be monumental, a draw may be far more achievable…
Barcelona are a very, very good team, and they are very, very, very good at home.

They have four wins from four at home in the league this season, having won all 19 last term. That’s 23 consecutive home league wins and counting. If they win two more, they will be on the second-longest home winning streak in La Liga history.
The last time they failed to win at home in La Liga was a 3-2 defeat to Villarreal in May 2025, though that was really just a dead rubber after they’d already won the 2024-25 title.
The last time they failed to win at home in La Liga in a meaningful game was a 1-1 draw with Real Betis on 5 April 2025.
The last time they lost a meaningful game at home in La Liga was 21 December 2024 against Atlético Madrid. That’s an extraordinary run.

49zdwmxm439c1gdwnjvn3nzxl.title: 'Erling said he was OK' – Maresca not worried by Haaland's injury
49zdwmxm439c1gdwnjvn3nzxl.subtitle: Erling Haaland limped off during Manchester City's win over Ipswich Town, but Enzo Maresca provided a positive update on the striker.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca believes the injury Erling Haaland sustained in Manchester City's 3-2 win over Ipswich Town is not as serious as first feared.
Haaland's electric start to the season continued on Saturday, with the Norwegian scoring twice to help City make it seven wins from seven in the Premier League.
City's number nine has now netted 100 non-penalty goals in the Premier League, reaching the milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139).
The previous fewest was 150 appearances, by Alan Shearer in 1996, while Haaland also scored for the sixth consecutive top-flight game.

Haaland has been key to City's strong start, scoring 12 goals in 10 outings across all competitions, with Ruben Dias (855) the only outfield player to play more minutes in 2026-27 than the 26-year-old's 853.
But towards the end of their win over Ipswich, Haaland was involved in a challenge with Jack Clarke and looked in some pain as he limped off the pitch at full-time.
Maresca, however, played down fears surrounding his talisman, saying: "We will see. Erling said he was OK. I don't have any news at the moment."
Maresca has become the first manager to win each of his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team.
City are also the third team to win each of their opening seven games of a Premier League season, after Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight) and Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine).
But the win was overshadowed by several injuries, with Nico O'Reilly, Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Antoine Semenyo all sustaining issues along with Haaland.
"Unfortunately, in 10 minutes we had four or five players [injured] – Matheus, Kova, Erling, Antoine and Nico also – but they are inside now, and we will see," Maresca added.
"I asked all of them. Mateo and Kova said they were OK. Erling also said he was OK and Nico, it's still his back.
"It's still the same problem. The only one we need to wait for is Antoine."

                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Which team will win the Premier League this season? Stay up to date with our live Opta supercomputer predictions for the 2026-27 Premier League title race.

Arsenal entered the 2025-26 season as reigning champions for the first time since 2004, with Mikel Arteta hoping to oversee the Gunners’ first successful defence of the top-flight crown since way back in 1934-35.
Defending the Premier League title is notoriously tough.

Only three clubs – under three managers – have ever accomplished that feat. They are Manchester United under Alex Ferguson (four such streaks, including two instances of three in a row), Chelsea under José Mourinho, and Manchester City under Pep Guardiola (two streaks, including four in a row from 2020-21 to 2023-24).

Based on results in the early part of the season, Man City look to be Arsenal's closest challengers. They have, however, been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and the majority of charges in relation to their failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation. City deny all the allegations and have appealed against the charges.
We're yet to find out if, how and when they'll suffer a punishment for this, with that potentially enough to affect their 2026-27 title charge.

Liverpool and Chelsea have new managers in the dugout in the form of Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso, with both clubs hoping to challenge at the top of the table this time around. Man Utd, meanwhile, gave Michael Carrick the job permanently in the summer following a successful period as caretaker boss. Will that appointment prove to be enough to get the Red Devils back to the top of the Premier League?

4CB0BD470F5E902AC81C97D7FFDFDB94.title: Preview: Leeds United host their Manchester rivals at Elland Road
4CB0BD470F5E902AC81C97D7FFDFDB94.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Leeds United host their Manchester rivals at Elland RoadShareManchester United are sliding back into ‘crisis’ mode, which makes a trip across the Pennines to play in form Leeds United a particularly daunting looking fixture.

For Manchester United fans, history is starting to repeat itself. Beaten comfortably by Atlético Madrid in the Champions League in midweek, they’re without a Premier League win since the end of August – their only one of the season so far – and the pressure is starting to build under head coach Michael Carrick.

As such, this is probably about the worst time to be having to travel across the Pennine hills to take on a Leeds United team who will be gunning to only increase the pain for their bitter rivals, and who have been in the sort of form this season which may facilitate such a result, with defeat at Arsenal last weekend being their first in the league.

The last time these two sides met, at Old Trafford in April, Leeds recorded their first win against Manchester United since they knocked them out of the FA Cup in January 2010. Between those two fixtures, the two sides had met each other eight times, with Manchester United winning five and three draws.

All eyes will be on Lisandro Martínez on Sunday, in light of the explosive comments that he made following Tuesday night’s defeat in Madrid. Martínez’s form has been such that some may be tempted to think “physician heal thyself” when it comes to criticism of other players, and the atmosphere in the dressing room may have been somewhat frosty once he returned to it following that already notorious post-match interview.

With four goals in all competitions and a recall to the England squad, Dominic Calvert-Lewin has continued the strong form he showed last season following his transfer from Everton. He got eight minutes as a substitute against Czechia and has the capability to do some serious damage to a creaky-looking Manchester United defence.

Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw are the latest injury doubts for Manchester United, who will. also be missing Benjamin Šeško, Patrick Dorgu, Matthijs de Ligt, Manuel Ugarte and Tom Heaton, while Noussair Mazrauoi is still being assessed. Mainoo isn’t expected back until the end of the month while Shaw, whose injury problems precede him, is a big loss for a club who didn’t strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.

The big question mark hanging over Leeds ahead of this match concerns Daniel James, who missed their trip to Arsenal and may not be available for this match either. This would be a huge disappointment for the winger, who started his senior career at Old Trafford. Mateo Joseph and Joe Rodon are longer term absentees for Leeds.

The great irony of the palaver that followed Manchester United’s midweek defeat in Madrid was that this wasn’t their worst performance of the season by a long chalk. It was certainly an improvement on their lacklustre display against Spurs last weekend.

But that doesn’t mean that the pressure is starting to build under Michael Carrick. He certainly exceeded expectations at Old Trafford last season in returning the club to the Champions League, but doubts were raised over his suitability for the position in a long-term sense at the time and those doubts seem to be manifesting in real time.

Ironically, what’s happened to his Leeds counterpart Daniel Farke offers a cautionary tale in terms of sacking managers. Farke was largely believed to be on borrowed time even after Leeds returned to the Premier League in 2025, but he steadied them last season and has built a team with a spine of steel this time around, who’ve defied expectations.

In that case, the decision to stick with Farke turned out to be the right one, though only hindsight offers the clarity of vision required to be able to see that. But the situation at Old Trafford is different. There’s no obvious replacement for Carrick, but Manchester United have tricky-looking fixtures against Chelsea and Aston Villa to come before the November international break. He needs improvement from his team, and he needs it immediately.

But if Leeds United are fired up for any fixture throughout a Premier League season, it’s always against Manchester United, and although they lost at Arsenal last week they put in a good performance and will be unhappy at not having taken something from that fixture. That in itself says something profound about the improvement they’ve shown this season, so I’m going to call this one as a 3-0 win for Leeds and for Carrick to be a couple of steps closer to the exit door by the end of the weekend.

4E2CA91ABC6004E292CA74DA9CF1949B.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsWomen's FootballScores & FixturesTableTop ScorersWSL Fan ChatFamilies v loyal fans - women's football's attendance dilemmaImage source, GettyImage caption, Women's football fans say a welcoming environment matters most to matchday enjoyment, more than performance on the pitch
Average Women's Super League attendances surged by 192% in the season after the Lionesses' Euro 2022 triumph, but the speed of the boom has stalled.
Median crowds have risen by just 166 fans, from 3,070 in 2023-24 to 3,236 in 2025-2026, according to a 2026 report from YouGov and architecture firm Populous, external.
Some of the biggest fixtures are now attracting significantly smaller attendances.
Arsenal against Manchester United at Emirates Stadium fell from 46,603 in 2024-25 to 29,853 this season, while Chelsea v Arsenal dropped from 34,302 to 19,349 over the same period.

The Gunners, who averaged 34,000 at the Emirates last season - almost four times the next-highest club, Chelsea, and higher than eight Premier League sides, external - had just 19,546 for their October match against Birmingham City.
There are bright spots, including a sold-out 4,000-ticket Arsenal away allocation at Tottenham for the first time, but the wider trend for some matches is clear.
Manchester United against Manchester City was hosted at Leigh Village in October with a crowd of 5,361. The same fixture was held at Old Trafford in March 2026 with 24,983 fans.
So what is behind the decline? Marketing, scheduling, matchday experience, stadium design, product or something else?

When supporters were asked what mattered most to their enjoyment of a women's football match in the report, a "welcoming, family-friendly environment" ranked above team success and the quality of on-pitch performance for both established and potential fans.
The research found only 15% of fans who have attended a women's match in the past five years do so at least monthly.
Meanwhile, 43% describe themselves as casual followers who engage more with major international tournaments than domestic club football, while just 10% identify as devoted supporters.
The findings suggest there is a possible matchday "experience gap" in the domestic game, with some clubs seeking to address it through family-friendly initiatives.
However, some fans have voiced their frustration at the family-friendly marketing.
Tottenham fan Dakota said "I'm almost glad I can't make it" in relation to a Spurs social media advert about the north London derby, which listed DJs, drinks, face painting and freestylers.
Image source, Tottenham HotspurShe added: "We'll never grow as a women's club if the entire marketing is for kids and families rather than young adults with disposable income."
Spurs fan Rosewen had similar views: "They can offer attractions to tempt people through the gates but we're losing sight of football and the importance of winning."

On the recent low crowd for the north London derby, one fan wrote on X: "Attendances across the WSL are down so this isn't a Spurs specific issue. However, the club has used a one-dimensional family-friendly marketing strategy for years."

Brighton took a similar family-focused approach for their October match against West Ham at the Amex, promoting a "Saturday Spooktacular" with attractions including a haunted house, face-painting, hair braiding, costume competitions and other activities taking up the majority of the advert.

Image source, Brighton and Hove AlbionHow does scheduling impact crowd numbers? Premier League football has long owned the 3pm Saturday slot while the WSL has varied kick-off times, making it harder for fans to establish a regular routine.

          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 8

                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Ready for another instalment of The 10% Club? Well, we’ve got some picks for you ahead of Gameweek 8 in Fantasy Premier League.
The 10% Club enjoyed one of its best returns last weekend. So, why not take note of our Fantasy Premier League picks for Gameweek 8?
With Evanilson (12 points), Luka Vuskovic and Johan Manzambi (both 11) all recording double-digit hauls, three of our five GW7 differentials delivered last time out.
Using Opta data, we’ve got another five under-the-radar gems for the next round of fixtures, and all are in fewer than 10% of squads worldwide.
Ipswich Town may not have kept a clean sheet in 26 Premier League games, but we’re still backing Leif Davis to return when Nottingham Forest visit.
Oliver Glasner’s side are the lowest scorers this season, finding the net just five times. However, Davis is more likely to make a difference in attack rather than banking on a clean sheet.
No defender can beat Davis’ two league goals this campaign, with Maxime De Cuyper and Tyrick Mitchell also twice on target.

Playing out of position on the wing for Brighton, De Cuyper (1.8) is the only defender with a higher expected goals (xG) than Davis’ 1.6. Based on that, chances should continue to flow for our GW8 selection.
The Ipswich full-back is also impressing compared to other budget options. Only Bobby Thomas (31) and Ryan Giles (27) have managed more points than Davis’ 26 among all defenders priced £4m or lower.
Thomas is another tempting pick, but Coventry City have kept just one clean sheet ahead of their meeting with Fulham. Meanwhile, Hull City’s Giles has a tough fixture at home to Brentford.
Davis then visits Hull before a home clash with Bournemouth, and his influence going forward could be key for both Gary O’Neil and prospective FPL managers ahead of the November international break.
Somehow, Leeds United’s defence continues to go under the radar. Only Arsenal and Brighton (five each) have conceded fewer than the six allowed by Daniel Farke’s side.
The 10% Club has already pointed readers towards Tarik Muharemović once, but James Justin is another interesting pick ahead of Leeds’ visit to Sunderland.
Justin scored in his last away game, firing past David Raya at Arsenal and has 34 points in total (Muharemović also has 34). No Leeds defender has had more than his seven shots either.
Jayden Bogle (45) is the only Leeds player with more points this campaign as well, though he has now moved out of reach due to his ownership percentage.

But Justin isn’t just impressing compared to his Leeds teammates. Mentioned last week, Brighton’s Vuskovic (51) is the only player with greater returns than Justin among all FPL defenders owned by fewer than 10% of managers.
Justin, meanwhile, is at least £0.5m cheaper than him and Muharemović. Plus, Sunderland haven’t scored in their last two league games, raising the chances of a Leeds clean sheet.
FPL success is largely about picking players based on either individual form or a promising set of fixtures.

Jack Rudoni falls into the form bracket for Coventry before Fulham travel to the CBS Arena. The midfielder scored from the penalty spot against Newcastle United before equalising against Tottenham last time out.
In doing so, Rudoni became the first player to score in back-to-back Premier League appearances for Coventry since John Hartson netted in four consecutive games between March and April 2001.

We look ahead to Sunday's WSL showdown with our London City Lionesses vs Manchester City preview. Can London City prove they are genuine contenders for the WSL crown, or will City underline why they remain the team to beat?

Since Michelle Kang acquired London City Lionesses in December 2023, the club's transformation has been nothing short of remarkable, and this fixture could provide the clearest indication yet of their title credentials.
Their Spanish superstar Alexia Putellas has been back in the headlines this week after claiming her third Ballon d'Or, reflecting the increasingly international identity of this London City side.
Seven of the Lionesses' starting XI against Liverpool last weekend were Spanish, with Putellas and Daniela Arques joining an entirely Spanish back five, including goalkeeper Elene Lete.

It marked the first time in WSL history that a team had named seven players from the same non-British nation in their starting lineup. However, that recruitment strategy has also meant limited opportunities for English players.
Freya Godfrey, with five, is the only England international to have started more than twice in the league for Eder Maestre’s side this season.
Yet, whatever the makeup of their squad, the results suggest Kang's investment is beginning to pay off.
London City have won their last five WSL home matches, a run bettered only by City's remarkable sequence of 16 such victories.
Another win on Sunday would see the Lionesses become the first team outside the traditional ‘big four' to win six successive WSL home games.
On the other hand, the reigning champions remain unbeaten after seven league matches (W6 D1) and could avoid defeat in their opening eight games of a WSL campaign for the first time since 2018-19.
But, there is evidence that Maestre’s team are learning how to match the division’s elite.
Having lost each of their first seven league encounters against those teams, London City have collected four points from their last two.
Now comes arguably their biggest test yet against the reigning champions.
One of the keys to London City's success has been their fast starts. They've already scored eight goals inside the opening 30 minutes of WSL games this season, the most of any side.
Such an approach means Maestre’s side have spent a league-high 68% of their total playing time in a winning position.

And Man City will need to pay particular attention to the Lioness’s threat down the left; a league-high 44% of London City’s attacking touches have come down that flank, while in each of their last three league matches, the player starting on the left wing has found the net.

That threat down the left could prove particularly significant on Sunday, especially given City's recent defensive uncertainty in that position, having changed their starting right-back in each of their last five WSL matches.
But while there may be questions about City's defensive consistency in wide areas, there are few doubts about their attacking fluency.

Jeglertz’s sidce remain one of the WSL's most accomplished possession-based teams, recording the third-highest average possession (61%) and the joint-most open-play sequences of 10 or more passes (116) this season.
Their sequences also average more passes (4.3) and last longer (12.2 seconds) than those of any other side, highlighting their ability to control possession and dictate the tempo of matches.

4ap1n1mxoqqa13sntb2jdzqjl.title: Zidane backs Dembele to lead France in Mbappe's absence
4ap1n1mxoqqa13sntb2jdzqjl.subtitle: Ousmane Dembele is set to captain France for their Nations League clash with Belgium, something Zinedine Zidane has full confidence in.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane is confident Ousmane Dembele can step up and be France's captain after Kylian Mbappe withdrew from the squad due to injury.
Dembele took the armband during France's 1-0 win over Turkiye in their Nations League opener, with Mbappe forced off after scoring the only goal in the 54th minute.
It has since been confirmed that the Real Madrid star suffered a hyperextension in his left knee, though the severity of the issue has not been disclosed at this time.

Mbappe will prove to be a big miss, not only for his leadership, but also for his quality on the pitch. He netted his 12th goal for France in 2026 last time out, equalling the highest total for a French player in a calendar year in the 21st century, set by himself in 2022.
Dembele also played his part at Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadyumu, finishing with team-high totals for chances created (four) and touches in the opposition box (seven).
"He is already doing it. He's vice-captain; he has that role, even when he's not captain," Zidane told reporters about what Dembele brings to the team as a captain.
"He is, he's a good guy, always there for others, and you have to take his experience. I expect something from everyone, not just the captains. It's a group that lives well.
"We've been together for a week; I can see that they're happy to be together. It's the French team; there are some great matches. Football goes so fast.
"I'm 54 years old; I'm here. I can't play any more, so I tell them to enjoy the moment, because it's flying. The French team is so beautiful that I want them to live these moments."
Zidane became the first coach to win his first match in charge of France since Aime Jacquet against Italy in 1994 (four draws and one loss in between).
The former Madrid boss said it was an emotional feeling to lead his country for the very first time, though he said there was still plenty to improve on for his team.
He revealed ahead of their trip to the Stade Roi Baudouin on Monday that he would be making several changes to his team given the tight turnaround.
France are second in Group A1 but level on points with Belgium after they beat Italy in their opening match.

It was put to Zidane whether the result or the performance was more important against Mark van Bommel's side, and he said: "Everything is important, but the most important thing is to get to know each other.

"We rested more, and we thought more about getting treatment than training because we don't have time. The idea is to prepare for the matches and afterwards, of course, to win the match. We are competitors, and what we want to do is win the match, above all.
"We have to improve; we will improve. But the idea is to get the ball back as quickly as possible and, above all, to have the ball, to run with the ball and not without the ball."

It has since been confirmed that the Real Madrid star suffered a hyperextension in his left knee, though the severity of the issue has not been disclosed at this time. 

Mbappe will prove to be a big miss, not only for his leadership, but also for his quality on the pitch. He netted his 12th goal for France in 2026 last time out, equalling the highest total for a French player in a calendar year in the 21st century, set by himself in 2022. 

Dembele also played his part at Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadyumu, finishing with team-high totals for chances created (four) and touches in the opposition box (seven). 

"He is already doing it. He's vice-captain; he has that role, even when he's not captain," Zidane told reporters about what Dembele brings to the team as a captain. 

"He is, he's a good guy, always there for others, and you have to take his experience. I expect something from everyone, not just the captains. It's a group that lives well.

"We've been together for a week; I can see that they're happy to be together. It's the French team; there are some great matches. Football goes so fast.

"I'm 54 years old; I'm here. I can't play any more, so I tell them to enjoy the moment, because it's flying. The French team is so beautiful that I want them to live these moments."

Zidane became the first coach to win his first match in charge of France since Aime Jacquet against Italy in 1994 (four draws and one loss in between). 

The former Madrid boss said it was an emotional feeling to lead his country for the very first time, though he said there was still plenty to improve on for his team. 

He revealed ahead of their trip to the Stade Roi Baudouin on Monday that he would be making several changes to his team given the tight turnaround. 

France are second in Group A1 but level on points with Belgium after they beat Italy in their opening match.

It was put to Zidane whether the result or the performance was more important against Mark van Bommel's side, and he said: "Everything is important, but the most important thing is to get to know each other.

"We rested more, and we thought more about getting treatment than training because we don't have time. The idea is to prepare for the matches and afterwards, of course, to win the match. We are competitors, and what we want to do is win the match, above all.

"We have to improve; we will improve. But the idea is to get the ball back as quickly as possible and, above all, to have the ball, to run with the ball and not without the ball."

4d3cpltr98m71202fmb9qzol9.title: Greece 1-3 England: Le Tissier and Russo propel Wiegman's side to first-leg win
4d3cpltr98m71202fmb9qzol9.subtitle: England put themselves in a strong position in their first Women's World Cup play-off, with a big win over Greece at Pankritio Stadio.
paragraphs: Quickfire goals from Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo helped secure England a 3-1 win over Greece in the first leg of their Women's World Cup play-off semi-final.
Georgia Stanway broke the deadlock for the European champions in the first half before Le Tissier and Russo added to their tally just after the hour-mark.
Greece set up a slightly nervy ending when Kallisti Brouksair pulled one back, but Sarina Wiegman's side held onto a two-goal cushion to take to King Power Stadium for the second leg on Tuesday.
England started well, with Stanway dragging a low shot wide of the left post and Laura Blindkilde Brown scuffing a tame shot straight at Rafailia-Dimitra Petaloti.
Moments later, the space opened up for Keira Walsh just outside the box, though her powerful drilled effort was pushed away by Petaloti.

James had the ball in the back of the net in the 19th minute, latching onto Stanway's throughball before dinking a lovely finish over Petaloti after spotting the goalkeeper off her line. However, it was ruled out following a VAR check as James was offside.
Ioanna Papatheodorou gave England a scare, dancing her way through their half before taking aim from range, only to hit the corner of the goal frame.
Stanway then broke the deadlock six minutes before half-time, with a slick England move exploiting the pockets in Greece's defence as Russo teed up her Arsenal team-mate for a poked finish.

Le Tissier forced a sharp stop from Petaloti to spark the second half into life before finding space on the right of the box and, from the angle, beat the goalkeeper for power to score her first England goal in the 63rd minute.
Beth Mead dragged wide moments after the restart, but was unselfish when she got the ball in the 67th minute, skipping past two challenges to tee up Russo for a pinpoint effort.
Greece burst back into life in the later stages, with Papatheodorou squaring it back to Brouksair, who sent her low shot across goal into the bottom-right corner 77 minutes in.
England kept pushing for a fourth towards the end, and substitute Jess Park powered her strike against the underside of the bar, though it bounced the wrong side of the goal line.
England make their dominance count
England enjoyed a largely successful World Cup qualifying campaign, but it was a 4-0 defeat to world champions Spain that proved costly.
With a place in next year's tournament on the line, though, England made a strong start to their play-off campaign as they aim to use that path to a major tournament for a fifth time.

Greece had an impressive record of their own in qualifying, having gone through their League C campaign with a 100% win record, and they showed their fight until the end to ensure they got a goal on the board.

The Lionesses were utterly dominant, having 26 shots worth 2.07 expected goals (xG), with seven of those on target as Petaloti kept her team in the game for large parts. England also had 58 touches in the opposition box.
Greece, by contrast, mustered just 0.16 xG and scored with their only shot on target, giving England a worry in the final 15 minutes to cut the deficit ahead of the second leg.
Stanway got the scoring going, meaning she has now scored against 23 different nations for England and has netted five goals during their qualifying campaign – more than any other player in the team.
The Lionesses have now gone unbeaten in their last 42 fixtures when facing an opponent for the very first time (W35 D7), and Wiegman will be hoping for a similar performance next week.

4d435n3bkqfu1iiva8cbi2pvv.title: Jesus to reveal reason for Ronaldo's Portugal exit after international break
4d435n3bkqfu1iiva8cbi2pvv.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo abruptly left Portugal's Nations League camp, but Jorge Jesus is not willing to discuss his row with the forward just yet.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says he will explain the reasons behind Cristiano Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal squad after the final match of this international break.
Ronaldo abruptly left the Portugal camp ahead of their Nations League meeting with Denmark, after widespread reports suggested tensions had been building since their previous win over Norway.
The 41-year-old was an unused substitute as Portugal ran out 2-1 winners on Sunday, with Joao Felix and Goncalo Ramos both getting on the scoresheet.
After the victory, Jesus said it was a "tactical choice" to leave Ronaldo on the bench, with Norway dominating most of the proceedings despite losing.

The Portugal captain trained away from his team-mates on Monday and Tuesday, with media reports suggesting there was a "crisis" meeting being held between Ronaldo, Jesus and Portugal Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca to clear the air.
Jesus insisted he would not "hide or run away" from the topic, but he was not willing to discuss the matter in depth ahead of Thursday's match with Denmark.
"I will explain everything after the last game," said Jesus in his pre-match interview.
"I have spent many years in football and I know that I did nothing that should have caused things to go differently.
"After the Norway game [this coming Sunday], we will talk about this subject. I will not hide or run away from it.
"Nobody can take away what Cristiano represents. He’s an icon and that’s not in question."
Portugal's final match of this international break comes at home against Norway on October 4.

4eqailkp9p3g1ebv389gbhn4f.title: 'There's no noise inside Palace' – Sage remains defiant after loss
4eqailkp9p3g1ebv389gbhn4f.subtitle: The pressure continues to pile on Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage after they suffered defeat to Newcastle United in the Premier League.
paragraphs: Pierre Sage struck a defiant tone, insisting there is "no noise inside the club" after Crystal Palace succumbed to a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United at Selhurst Park.
The visitors went ahead two minutes after the break, with William Osula poking home Jacob Murphy's excellent right-wing centre.
Joe Willock thought he had doubled Newcastle's lead moments later, but his strike was disallowed for offside after a VAR review.
However, there was nothing wrong with Harvey Barnes' goal, with the attacker thrashing a close-range finish past the helpless Walter Benitez.
The Eagles looked to score a late consolation, but Lukas Hornicek was in top form to deny Adam Wharton and Dario Osorio in the closing stages.

The loss means Palace, who sit 17th in the Premier League table, have now lost five of their eight Premier League matches this season, only losing more in that span in 1971-72 (six), 1980-81 (seven), 2013-14 (seven) and 2017-18 (seven).
Their 19 goals conceded is also their second-most after eight top-flight games, after 1980-81 (22), and the pressure is piling on Sage.
"The boos are normal because we don't have the result. The noise is the consequence of the result of the team, and at the moment we don't have what we expect," said Sage.
"Inside, we are just really focused on solutions. How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work, and there's no noise inside, if you want.
"It's normal that people lose patience when you lose, because everybody wants to win. [Against Newcastle], it was not the case.
"For me, the noise around the team, the noise around the club, it's only noise."
For Newcastle, they have now won and kept a clean sheet in consecutive away matches in London (also 2-0 v Tottenham in August) for the first time in a single Premier League campaign since 2013.

The Magpies were clinical in front of goal, scoring with both of their shots on target on Sunday. Interestingly, in three of the last four Premier League matches in which Newcastle scored 2+ goals, they have scored with 100% of their shots on target (2/2 v Palace, Bournemouth and Spurs).
Victory on Sunday alleviates the pressure on Matthias Jaissle, who has come under fire from sections of the Newcastle fanbase.
"It was a tough game, especially in the first half. We couldn't get ourselves the reward for the intensity we put in out of possession after the ball wins," said Jaissle.
"In the second half, it was much better. We were more target-orientated, we threatened the opposition more and, therefore, I think when it comes to the second half and that improvement.
"In the end, also that willingness to defend and to have that clean sheet. It was a deserved win."

4hsxoe5qjf4817jfh5wxmih0w.title: Van Dijk: 'Electric' Ngumoha has 'much more to come' for Liverpool
4hsxoe5qjf4817jfh5wxmih0w.subtitle: Rio Ngumoha starred in Liverpool’s Champions League win over Villarreal, and he will be hoping to have a similar impact against Brighton.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk believes there is still "much more to come" from Rio Ngumoha after the talented teenager starred during Liverpool's Champions League victory in midweek.
Ngumoha put on an impressive display during Liverpool's 4-3 win over Villarreal, a result that made it three wins from three to begin the Reds' European campaign.

Aged 18 years and 52 days, Ngumoha became the third-youngest player to provide multiple assists in a Champions League game behind Warren Zaire-Emery against AC Milan in 2023 (17y 231d) and Theo Walcott against Hamburg in 2006 (17y 250d).

He is also the youngest player for Liverpool to either score or assist for the club in the Champions League, while Ngumoha is the youngest player on record since 2008-09 to complete 5+ dribbles (seven), have 10+ touches in the opposition box (12) and register an assist (two) in the competition.
But Ngumoha has been restricted to just one start in the Premier League this season, and he has failed to register a goal contribution for the Reds over those appearances.

Liverpool's clash with Brighton this weekend could be an opportunity to start, with Andoni Iraola saying it would be difficult for Victor Munoz to recover in time from an issue with his knee, though Bradley Barcola, who was doing an individual training programme earlier in the week, trained as normal on Friday.
"He's pretty electric at times and he showed it again. He was a complete threat constantly and their defenders had a tough time," said Van Dijk on Ngumoha's midweek display.
Asked who has taken Ngumoha under their wing since the departure of Liverpool stalwart Mohamed Salah in the summer, Van Dijk added: "A few senior players.
"I would say Cody [Gakpo] is definitely part of that. But everyone has that role in order to help the youngsters in the group, the players who have not had so much experience.

"Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo [Salah] last year was obviously massive, as Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything, so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities?
"I think he has shown it this season, but there is still much more to come."
Brighton, meanwhile, are riding high in the Premier League, with Fabian Hurzeler's side sitting in third following their thumping 5-0 win over rivals Crystal Palace last time out.

The Seagulls became the ninth side in Premier League history to score three goals in the first 10 minutes of a match before Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood concluded the rout after the break.
In the Conference League in midweek, Brighton were forced to settle for a point after a goalless draw with Jablonec, though they are still ninth in the 36-team standings.

Given Brighton's strong start to the season, many have questioned whether they can challenge for the Champions League places or even the Premier League title, with Hurzeler a man in demand amid uncertainty among the teams around him.
There have been reports linking him to the Manchester United job with Michael Carrick under pressure, but Hurzeler remained focused on his duties with the Seagulls.

"I'm really focused on my job here. I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, besides that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season," Hurzeler said.
"He's a great human being, a great personality. There's nothing more to say about that."
Liverpool – Alexander Isak
Isak has five goals in his last five Premier League appearances, as many as he scored in his previous 20 combined for Newcastle United and Liverpool.
The Sweden international has not ended on the losing side in any of his last 15 league appearances (W9 D6), having lost four of his first five in a Liverpool shirt.
Brighton – Charalampos Kostoulas
Kostoulas has scored and assisted in two of his last three Premier League appearances.

He's the first teenager to do so more than once in a season since Kelechi Iheanacho for Manchester City in 2016-17, while the last teenager to achieve it three times in one campaign was Michael Owen in 1998-99.
MATCH PREDICTION: LIVERPOOL WIN
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 13 home games against Brighton in all competitions (W9 D3), winning each of their last four against the Seagulls at Anfield.

But with two draws and a defeat at Anfield in the Premier League this season, Liverpool could fail to win each of their opening four home matches of a league campaign for only the fourth time, after 1894-95, 1911-12, and 2012-13.

The Reds are also winless in their last five home Premier League matches (D4 L1), only twice having worse runs at Anfield: seven from November 2002 to February 2003 and eight from December 2020 to March 2021.

Brighton, meanwhile, have won each of their last four Premier League games by an aggregate score of 15-0. The last side to win five successive matches in the competition without conceding were Liverpool in April 2022.

Hurzeler's side are also one of only eight teams to have scored 23 goals in their opening seven Premier League games of a season, and the first since Man City in 2022-23 (23). The last side to have a goal difference of +18 after seven matches were the Citizens in 2019-20 (20).
The Seagulls have won two of their last three Premier League matches against Liverpool (L1), as many as they won in their first 15 against the Reds (D4 L9).

4jikbwtyvot1ka7zjol4z8ww.title: Inter Miami 2-2 FC Cincinnati: Filipi's late equaliser rescues a point for Messi and Co.
4jikbwtyvot1ka7zjol4z8ww.subtitle: Inter Miami squandered a one-goal lead before Riquelme Fillipi netted a late leveller against FC Cincinnati to cap a frenetic ending.
paragraphs: Riquelme Fillipi's first goal for Inter Miami proved decisive as his 90th-minute equaliser salvaged Cristian Gonzalez's side a point in their 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati.
Cincinnati seemed set to boost their playoff hopes when quickfire goals from Kenji Mboma Dem and Samuel Gidi cancelled out Luis Suarez's 61st-minute opener.

But Miami were saved by substitute Fillipi, with Cincinnati now looking nervously over their shoulders to secure their postseason spot, with Columbus Crew, New York Red Bulls and Toronto FC closing in with two matches of the regular season remaining.
Teenage Hadebe headed over an early chance for Cincinnati before Gidi put his body on the line to deny Lionel Messi as a tepid first half petered out at Nu Stadium.

Suarez spurned a glorious opportunity in the 55th minute as he dragged German Berterame's cutback just past the post, with the first shot on target coming on the hour when Rodrigo De Paul's drive from distance was beaten away by Roman Celentano.

And 67 seconds later, Miami found their breakthrough. De Paul's pass was cushioned into the path of Suarez by Casemiro, with the Uruguayan taking a touch before bending a superb effort in off the crossbar.

However, Cincinnati levelled with a stunner of their own in the 80th minute after Mboma Dem cut inside of Gonzalo Lujan and curled a glorious left-footed shot that just evaded the outstretched dive of Dayne St. Clair.
Pat Noonan's side then thought they had won it four minutes from time when Gidi picked out the bottom-left corner after being teed up by Tom Barlow on the edge of the box.

But Miami responded again on the stroke of full-time through Fillipi, who, just seven minutes after being brought on, made his way past Alvas Powell and bent his attempt into the bottom-right corner to seal a share of the spoils.

4llpo7fpmdgo1rppajl8yz96p.title: The Numbers Game: England bid to equal away-day record against old foes Croatia
4llpo7fpmdgo1rppajl8yz96p.subtitle: England head to Croatia for their third game in the Nations League on Saturday, with both teams having three points on the board.
paragraphs: England and Croatia have become very familiar foes in recent years.

Luka Modric and company were responsible for the first heartbreaking tournament defeat of the Gareth Southgate era in 2018, with Ivan Perisic and Mario Mandzukic scoring to cancel out Kieran Trippier's memorable free-kick.
Since then, the Three Lions have started two tournaments – Euro 2020 and the 2026 World Cup – with victories over Croatia, and Saturday's reunion in Rijeka may be pivotal for both teams.
Having both beaten Czechia and lost to Spain in their opening two games in Nations League Group A3, their head-to-head clashes could decide who progresses to the last eight next March.
But who will come out on top this weekend? Here, we preview the game using Opta insights.
What's expected?
The Opta supercomputer is siding with England ahead of this game, albeit not decisively.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations run by the Opta model, the Three Lions triumphed in 48.6% of scenarios, with Croatia winning 27.4% and the remaining 24% of simulations finishing level.
And if you look past that 2018 semi-final defeat, an England win would continue a theme of dominance in recent head-to-head meetings with Croatia.
Since that game in Moscow, Croatia are winless in all four of their meetings with the Three Lions (D1 L3), including two Nations League fixtures in 2018 (0-0 home, 1-2 away).
In fact, England have won five of their last seven matches against Croatia in all competitions (D1 L1), dating back to a 3-2 defeat in 2007, which cost them qualification for Euro 2008.
The Three Lions have scored at least four goals in three of those wins, triumphing 4-1 in September 2008, 5-1 in September 2009 and 4-2 at the World Cup this June.
Croatia facing historic low
Following nine years under Zlatko Dalic, Slaven Bilic made a winning return to the Croatia job against Czechia last weekend, with Modric and Marco Pasalic scoring in a 2-1 away win.
But they were then blown away by Spain in Seville on Tuesday, losing 4-1 after briefly getting back on level terms in the first half, via Dion Beljo's first international goal.
Croatia could have no complaints about their margin of defeat, having only attempted five shots to Spain's 16 and put up 0.47 expected goals (xG) to their opponents' 1.81.
They have only produced a lower xG figure in three previous Nations League fixtures – versus France in March 2025 (0.18), Sweden in November 2020 (0.3) and England in October 2018 (0.42).
After that reality check, Croatia have now lost five of their 10 matches overall in 2026 (W5).
It is only the third time they have suffered that many defeats in a single calendar year (also 2018 and 2020), though they have never previously lost six in one year.

They will hope a return to home soil at Stadion HNK in Rijeka provides some comfort, having won eight of their last nine competitive home matches (D1) since a 1-0 loss to Turkiye in a Euro 2024 qualifier back in October 2023.
However, despite Croatia only losing four of their last 41 competitive games at home, three of those losses have been in the Nations League, against France and Portugal in 2020 and Austria in 2022.
Will Tuchel experiment with away-day record in sight?
Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane were on target on Tuesday as England, helped by a first-half red card for Czechia midfielder Pavel Sulc, emerged as 2-0 victors in Prague.

That win was England's sixth in their last eight Nations League matches (L2) across the top two tiers, having scored 20 goals in that span. That is more victories and goals than they managed in their first 18 games in the competition overall (W5 D6 L7, 18 goals).
It was also England's eighth straight away win in all competitions, giving them an opportunity to match an all-time team record this weekend.
Only once have they ever won nine away games in a row, doing so under World Cup-winning manager Alf Ramsey between December 1965 and October 1967.

It will be intriguing to see how Tuchel approaches his team choice for this game, after he handed Trent Alexander-Arnold his first England start since October 2024 – in a Nations League win over Finland under Lee Carsley – at right-back.
Alexander-Arnold teed up Gordon's opening goal with a trademark delivery to the far post, which was also his first assist in international football since that Finland game two years ago.

Tuchel had gone with the more conservative option of Jarell Quansah on the right side of defence against Spain, but with Alexander-Arnold ranking second among England players for chances created (three, behind Gordon with four) and passes into the final third (32, behind Elliot Anderson with 40), might the England boss favour his creativity from deep areas?

He also has options in midfield after handing Myles Lewis-Skelly back-to-back starts in the absence of his Arsenal club-mate Declan Rice, with Alex Scott winning his first senior cap in Prague and Morgan Gibbs-White making another lively cameo appearance.
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Czechia – Ivan Perisic
Perisic, who provided a goal and an assist against England the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, has started both of Croatia's games during this international break.
The 37-year-old has 15 goal involvements in his last 18 starts for Croatia, netting six times and registering nine assists.
Kane – who smacked a penalty off the crossbar after losing his footing in England's loss to Spain – has enjoyed playing on the road lately.
The England captain has found the net in each of his last five away internationals.

He could now become just the fourth player to score in six consecutive away games for the Three Lions, after James Windridge (six from March to June 1908), Tom Finney (seven from September 1946 to May 1948) and Stan Mortensen (six from May 1947 to October 1948).

4nx4zbo2ey2t16yy2zy4ufmuu.title: Aston Villa boss Emery 'honoured' to receive Ballon d'Or nomination
4nx4zbo2ey2t16yy2zy4ufmuu.subtitle: Unai Emery is on the shortlist for the Ballon d'Or Men's Coach of the Year award after a stunning 2025-26 season in charge of Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Unai Emery expressed his honour at being nominated for the Ballon d'Or Men's Coach of the Year award, but the Aston Villa boss does not expect to lift the title.
Emery is part of a five-man shortlist after ending Villa's 30-year wait for a trophy by winning the Europa League, as well as delivering a fourth-place finish in the Premier League.
The 54-year-old is up against some tough competition, with Luis Enrique, Mikel Arteta, Luis de la Fuente and Vincent Kompany also nominated for the award.
Carlo Ancelotti scooped the title in 2024, while Paris Saint-Germain's Luis Enrique was the winner last year, having led the Ligue 1 giants to their first Champions League crown.
"Being nominated for the Ballon d'Or is something to be proud of," Emery told Diario de Sevilla about his nomination. "Sometimes people tell me: 'Unai is undervalued in football'.
"No, I feel very valued in the places I've been, I feel very valued in football in general, and I don't feel like I'm lacking anything.
"I feel like I have a very important place, and for me, it's an honour and a source of pride. I don't know who they'll give it to.
"I imagine the Champions League winner carries a lot of weight, and it could be Luis Enrique, or even winning the World Cup like De la Fuente did.
"That would also have its significance, but I don't know. I think the Europa League winner does too, and that's why I'm in the running, but a little less so."
The winner will be announced at the ceremony on October 26, but Emery's attention will now switch to this weekend's clash with Brentford in the Premier League.
Villa claimed their first win against Tottenham before the international break, while Keith Andrews' side are flying high as they sit fourth in the standings and still unbeaten.
Brentford thumped London rivals Chelsea 3-0 in their last league match, moving them up to nine points after five games, with Vitaly Janelt key to their strong start.
Janlet has started all five of Brentford's Premier League matches, while also boasting team-high totals for successful passes (184) and tackles won (10).
His fine form saw him called up to Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the very first time, and Janelt believes his time at Brentford has been the best in his career so far.
"We feel very comfortable here," Janelt said. "The journey is not just being promoted and playing Premier League football – it's the other side as well.
"Having a nice life outside of football, having a baby and a good wife. It's all a big puzzle. I can't complain at all. It's the best time in my football career.
"I'm at a point now where I know what matters and what I want to do. I feel more clearly about what is right for my family."
Aston Villa – Johan Manzambi
Against Spurs last time out, Manzambi became the second player to both score and assist on their first Premier League start for Villa, after Kevin Phillips in 2005-06.
The 20-year-old could become the youngest player to net on both of their first two starts for the Villans in the competition, and the first overall since Danny Ings in 2021-22.
Brentford – Dango Ouattara

Last season against Villa, Ouattara became the first player to score home and away in 1-0 wins against the same team in a Premier League campaign since Raheem Sterling for Manchester City against Arsenal in 2020-21.
No Bees player has netted three winning goals against the same opponent in the competition, though Ouattara will be out to change that at Villa Park.
MATCH PREDICTION: ASTON VILLA WIN
Villa have lost just one of their 11 home league games against Brentford (W4 D6), though it was a 1-0 defeat in this exact fixture last season.

The Villans have, however, lost both of their top-flight games at Villa Park this season. Only in 1946-47 and 1969-70 have they ever been beaten in their opening three home matches of a league campaign.

Emery's side have also recorded the fewest shots (48), shots on target (12) and touches in the opposition box (81) in the 2026-27 Premier League. They also rank bottom for overall expected goals (4.65 xG) and xG from set-pieces (0.39).

Brentford, meanwhile, are unbeaten in their last seven league games (W2 D5), the longest active run in the Premier League. Only between October 2022 and March 2023 have they had a better streak without defeat in the competition (12 in a row).
The Bees also completed the double over Villa last season, having won just one of their first eight Premier League games against them (D3 L4).

Andrews' side have also kicked off a league campaign unbeaten in five games (W2 D3) for the first time since 2013-14 in League One under Uwe Rosler, last having a longer unbeaten streak at the start of a season in 2006-07 under Leroy Rosenior (first seven in the third tier).
Aston Villa – 47.8%
Brentford – 26.2%

4odxjun3uz1r17qbem5clhp7m.subtitle: Espanyol's shock Copa del Rey loss to fourth-tier Sestao has prompted a change in management, with Eder Sarabia replacing Manolo Gonzalez.

The club sacked Manolo Gonzalez on Tuesday, following their shock Copa del Rey first-round exit at the hands of fourth-tier Sestao, who won 4-3 after extra time.
They have also struggled in LaLiga, currently sitting 18th after 10 matches with just eight points (W2 D2 L4), failing to win any of their last five (D1 L4).
And it is Sarabia who has been tasked with turning things around for the club.
Sarabia was most recently in charge of Elche, for whom he secured LaLiga safety on the final day of last season thanks to a 1-1 draw with Girona before announcing his shock exit.
He spent just one season in LaLiga – with Elche – during his managerial career, winning just 10 of his 38 matches in the competition (D13 L15) to leave him with a 26.3% win rate.
Sarabia, who is also a former assistant coach at Barcelona, is not set to be in the dugout against Villarreal on Friday, as he will be officially presented next Tuesday.

4sv8g3qeperh1e4w49upqy18l.title: Women's Super League predictions: Can Man City pull clear as Chelsea and Arsenal face off?
4sv8g3qeperh1e4w49upqy18l.subtitle: Manchester City's 100% start will be put to the test against Charlton Athletic, while Chelsea face Arsenal in the blockbuster clash of MD4.
paragraphs: After three matchdays in the Women's Super League season, defending champions Manchester City remain the only team with a 100% record, following their frantic 4-2 victory over Liverpool last time out.

After drawing 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their Champions League opener on Tuesday, City visit Charlton Athletic – who are the only team yet to pick up a point – to kickstart the week's action on Saturday, before the focus turns to their potential title rivals.
Neither Chelsea nor Arsenal have suffered a defeat yet this term, but with both sides already off City's pace, their head-to-head clash at Stamford Bridge on Sunday looks vital.
There is also a Merseyside derby between Liverpool and Everton, while Manchester United will look to finally earn their first league victory under Eva Olid, at home to West Ham.
Who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend? We have a look at the Opta supercomputer's predictions for matchday four.
CHARLTON ATHLETIC V MANCHESTER CITY

With Manchester City making a perfect start and Charlton recording three straight defeats since their promotion, it should come as little surprise that our predictive model makes Andree Jeglertz's champions the clearest MD4 favourites, with a 75.6% win probability to Charlton's 10.6%.
Only once in the last eight campaigns have City enjoyed a longer winning start than this one, winning each of their first four matches in 2019-20.
But they will be supremely confident of matching that feat at The Valley, in what will be their first competitive meeting with Charlton in the WSL era.
Promoted sides have won just one of their last 28 meetings with the reigning champions in the competition (D3 L24), with Liverpool recording a 2-1 home victory over Chelsea in September 2022.

Last time out, Khadija Shaw became the first player to score in each of City's first three games of a WSL campaign, and she could become the fifth player to do so in the first four matches of a season for any club, after Kim Little in 2018-19 (four for Arsenal), Vivianne Miedema in 2020-21 (five for Arsenal), Martha Thomas in 2023-24 (four for Tottenham) and Aggie Beever-Jones in 2025-26 (four for Chelsea).
LONDON CITY LIONESSES V BRIGHTON
Charlton's last game was a thumping 4-1 defeat to the ambitious London City Lionesses, who have six points on the board after three games and sit fourth in the table ahead of facing winless Brighton.
Alexia Putellas and company are assigned a 52.9% win probability on Saturday, with Brighton only winning 23% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations.

London City's three wins in their last four WSL matches (L1) are more than they managed across their previous 12 in the competition (W2 D3 L7), and their nine 'big' chances against Charlton last week were the most by any team in a WSL game since October 2020 (when Man Utd had 10 versus Brighton).

The Seagulls could fail to win their opening four matches of a WSL campaign for the third time after 2018-19 (first six) and 2019-20 (first five), and they have lost seven of their last nine league games in London.
MANCHESTER UNITED V WEST HAM

4ued3nzwi76n1hbx4tjx150jv.title: Scotland suffer 'big setback' in 'new chapter', says McGinn after defeat to Switzerland
4ued3nzwi76n1hbx4tjx150jv.subtitle: Ten-man Scotland fell to a 3-0 defeat at Hampden Park against Switzerland, leaving Sebastien Pocognoli winless after two games.
paragraphs: John McGinn believes Scotland suffered a "big setback" in their "new chapter" under Sebastien Pocognoli after losing 3-0 to Switzerland in the Nations League.

Scotland were dealt a huge blow just 11 minutes into Pocognoli's first home game in charge after Jack Hendry was shown a straight red card for a last-man challenge, and matters were made worse when Ricardo Rodriguez arrowed in the resulting free-kick.

Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouni netted for the visitors at Hampden Park after half-time, seeing Pocognoli (D1 L1) become the first Scotland manager to fail to win his first two games in charge since George Burley in May 2008 (D1 L1).

Scotland (two shots) failed to have a shot on target in a home game for the first time since September 2023 against England (seven shots), while they have failed to score in four consecutive games for the first time since 1971.
They are also without a clean sheet in eight home games, their worst run since going 10 in a row without a shutout between October 2001 and September 2003.

McGinn, who made his 91st appearance for Scotland, moving him alongside Jim Leighton in joint-third place for the most caps for his country, has urged his team-mates to learn from the humbling defeat.
"We could have done better at times, but we're starting a new chapter, learning to play a different way. That was a big setback for us," McGinn told BBC Scotland.
"We've got a lot to learn from, but a lot to take from it as well.
"I thought Oli McBurnie was outstanding. He's had a lot of criticism in a Scotland shirt, but [this game] was a thankless task and he gave everything for us.
"Going down to 10 men, it's a test of character; you need to dig in. It's a huge learning curve for us, and when we play them away, we need to win now."
Scotland will now face North Macedonia on Saturday, with the early pressure already piling on Pocognoli.

4ugjg5li8qod1oy7dyoc6i1kb.title: Juventus goalkeeper Grabara undergoes successful ACL surgery
4ugjg5li8qod1oy7dyoc6i1kb.subtitle: Kamil Grabara faces up to seven months on the sidelines after sustaining a serious injury on his debut for Juventus in the Europa League.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Kamil Grabara has undergone successful surgery to reconstruct the anterior cruciate (ACL) ligament in his knee.
Grabara sustained the injury during a training session just two days after making his debut for Juventus during a 5-0 victory over NEC in the Europa League.
The 27-year-old, who is on a season-long loan with the Serie A giants from Wolfsburg, provided the assist for Nico Gonzalez's opener at Allianz Stadium.
However, it is believed the Poland international will now face up to seven months on the sidelines, following a summer of changes in the goalkeeping department at Juventus.
The Bianconeri allowed Michele Di Gregorio and Mattia Perin to leave the club, while also bringing in Guglielmo Vicario on loan from Premier League side Tottenham.
"Kamil Grabara underwent surgery this afternoon to reconstruct the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee," Juventus said in a statement.
"The procedure, performed at the Guardian Clinic in Konin by Dr Andrzej Pyda, in the presence of Juventus Club Doctor Dr Marco Freschi, was a complete success.
"The player will begin his rehabilitation programme in the coming days, with a view to returning to competitive action."
With the transfer window now shut, Juventus are reportedly close to agreeing a deal with Neto, who previously played in Turin between 2015 and 2017.
Neto is a free agent following the termination of his contract with Botafogo in June, and he is set to sign until the end of the season, according to reports.
The Brazilian played 22 times across all competitions during his previous stint with Juventus, keeping 12 clean sheets and winning five major honours.
Since his exit from Juventus nine years ago, he has gone on to represent Valencia, Barcelona, Bournemouth, Arsenal and most recently, Botafogo.
Juventus are seventh in Serie A after their first five games of the season, and they return to action after the international break against Cagliari on October 11.

4x2jogj427ih1sthlaz3k388x.title: Hall says Newcastle contract renewal was 'a no-brainer' amid Man Utd rumours
4x2jogj427ih1sthlaz3k388x.subtitle: Manchester United were tipped to move for Lewis Hall this summer, but the left-back eventually signed a new contract with Newcastle United.
paragraphs: Lewis Hall says it was "a no-brainer" to sign a new long-term contract with Newcastle United, despite attracting interest from Manchester United throughout the summer.
Earlier this month, Hall ended speculation over his immediate future by penning fresh terms with the Magpies, with his new deal reportedly running until 2031.
Having joined his boyhood club from Chelsea in 2023, Hall has made 109 appearances for Newcastle in all competitions, with 82 of those being starts.
He helped Newcastle end their 70-year domestic trophy drought by winning the EFL Cup in 2025, though a foot injury caused him to miss their victory over Liverpool in the final.
Hall has also started 2026-27 strongly under new boss Mathias Jaissle, providing two assists in all competitions and scoring his first goal of the campaign in Saturday's 2-1 home win over Hull City.
Asked by Chronicle Live if he ever felt like he had a difficult decision to make amid loud transfer speculation, Hall said: "No, honestly, it didn't.
"I guess whenever you're linked to another team, you know that you're doing something right. It's a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, and how you are as a person.
"I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I love playing here and since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.
"After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club.
"I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer to sign."

Hall was recently recalled to the England squad by Thomas Tuchel ahead of Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (home and away) and Croatia, having missed out on the Three Lions' group for the World Cup.
And looking long-term, Hall believes being at St James' Park allows him to fulfil his ambitions, saying: "When you're with a team, you don't think too far into the future.
"Obviously, I'm really grateful for the contract that I've received and the trust that I've been given from the board and from the manager.
"I'm just taking it game by game, just trying to do the best I can for this club. We've got ambitions and as long as we achieve what we want to achieve, I'm sure I'll be here for a long time."
With eight points on the board from five Premier League games, Newcastle face Coventry City in their first game after the international break, on October 12.
