50D8E5F6D50030B36E27C4C6F51ACF5D.title: Raphinha: The most in-form player in Europe has made a blistering start to 2026/27
50D8E5F6D50030B36E27C4C6F51ACF5D.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesRaphinha: The most in-form player in Europe has made a blistering start to 2026/27Share“It’s a joke!” Luis García didn’t mince his words following Sevilla’s 3-1 defeat to Barcelona at the weekend. And no, he wasn’t referring to a dodgy refereeing decision, or a defensive mishap that caused his side to crumble on home turf. Rather, he was referring to the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

Specifically, Raphinha’s omission from 30-man nomination list. Barcelona are well represented in the lead up to the individual award. Spanish trio Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Pau Cubarsí are the Blaugrana contingent in the running for the accolade, though in truth; only the former pair are genuine contenders for the 2026 award.

Even so, Raphinha at present is outperforming the trio, and, in truth, the other 27 players to make the cut for the prestigious gong. Indeed, the brilliant Brazilian has been directly involved in a goal in every competitive appearance for Hansi Flick’s men this season. He’s scored in all but one of eight outings, and even then; he provided a brace of assists as the defending LaLiga champions claimed a 4-2 win at Levante.

Saturday’s perfect hat-trick – the former Leeds United scored one with his right, another with his left, and the third with his head – took him to 12 league goals for the season. Even the great Lionel Messi failed to achieve the feat after the opening seven games of a league campaign at Barcelona.

What’s all the more important is that Raphinha’s form has come at a time when Barcelona ended the summer transfer window, arguably, a forward short. Marcus Rashford was replaced by Anthony Gordon. Karim Adeyemi’s arrival eased Ferran Torres’ move to Paris Saint-Germain. They ruthlessly pushed for Atlético Madrid hitman Julián Alvarez in their quest to replace Robert Lewandowski.

Naturally, Barcelona were never going to trigger Alvarez’s €500m release clause, and they needn’t have bothered with their pursuit of the Argentine. Turns out Barcelona had the perfect Lewandowski successor the whole time.

Joining for £69.3m, Gordon was never going to sign as a backup for the Brazil international on the left. Yamal is one of the first names on the team sheet down the right. Crowbarring Raphinha into the side could have backfired on Flick and Barcelona. In hindsight, it’s proven a masterstroke.

The 29-year-old has been granted the license to drift across the pitch not just in search of possession, but in order to drag markers out of position. Flick deploys inverted widemen in his favoured 4-3-3 setup. Left winger Gordon favours his right foot. Right winger Yamal prefers his left.

Raphinha’s willingness to drop a little deeper opens up space for the pair to exploit. He’s not a conventional number nine by any stretch, so there is no point acting like one. What is key, though, is that Raphinha is also capitalising upon the space he creates.

Speed has so often been a strong point of the forward’s game. When Raphinha switches on the afterburners, good luck keeping up with him. In wide areas, he had to cover greater distances to get into goalscoring areas. Now, his speed off the mark means he really comes alive inside the opposition box when he makes darting runs into the penalty area.

42 touches inside the opposition box ranks fifth in LaLiga this season. For context, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé (85) tops this metric. The Frenchman spends more time in the area, because this plays to his strengths. For Raphinha, that lightning quick turn of pace so often bamboozles opposition defences.

It’s no coincidence that all 12 of his league goals this season have been scored inside the penalty area. Granted, three of them are penalties. Yet even so, Barcelona are proving even more potent when they break forward then last season, which is some going for a team that scored more goals (95) than any other team in the 2025/26 LaLiga campaign.

After all, their average of 4.43 league goals per game is almost double last season’s haul (2.5). Much of that is due to the speed of their attack having scored more counter-attacking goals (4) than any other team in Spain’s top tier. Raphinha has struck two of those. 14 shots following a counter attack is the third most in the division.

Crucially, too, is that not only is Raphinha able to get on the end of the ample chances that are created by this rampant Barcelona side, he’s proving incredibly efficient in front of goal. Of the 135 players to have managed at least five shots, only Pape Gueye (50%) boasts a better conversion rate than Raphinha (48%). The former has managed six shots. The latter has had 25. 11 of his 12 goals have been deemed big chances.

Back to García’s comments, however, and recency bias does play a part. That’s not suggesting Raphinha doesn’t deserve his flowers. He’s the most in-form player in Europe at present. Rather, over the course of the calendar year, the Barca star hasn’t quite hit the lofty heights, and that is through no fault of his own.

Injuries have wreaked havoc on both his playing time and his consistency. It’s denied Raphinha the chance to gain a head of steam for both club and country. As such, Flick’s use of the forward will prove beneficial for the player as he relies on shorter, sharper bursts rather than prolonged sprints that increase the likelihood of muscle injuries.

And if he can avoid a reoccurrence of those pesky problems going forward, then he’ll undoubtedly be in the running for the 2027 award. Barcelona are tearing opponents to shreds without showing a modicum of sympathy. If he can fire them to domestic and continental glory, then he’ll be in the running.

paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesArsenal reunion is a chance for 40-year-old Olivier Giroud to show he can still produce at the top levelShareOlivier Giroud will return to the Emirates Stadium to take on his former side in the Champions League this evening.

Olivier Giroud knows the Emirates Stadium well. It’s where the Frenchman called home for six years as the focal point of an Arsenal team stuck between the latter years of the fading Arsene Wenger era and a fresh start for the North London club that never truly got started until Mikel Arteta returned as manager.

By then, Giroud had departed. His illustrious career has seen him play for several notable clubs including Chelsea, AC Milan and Los Angeles FC, but it was in red and white while playing for Arsenal that Giroud made the greatest impression. During a difficult period in the club’s history, Giroud still managed to shine.

He will surely be given a warm reception by his former fans when Giroud returns to the Emirates Stadium as a Lille player on Tuesday. At 40-years-old, Giroud is still a key player at a high level, starting four of Lille’s six Ligue 1 games so far this season. He will surely feature in some capacity against Arsenal in the Champions League.

It wasn’t so long ago that Giroud’s career at the top level looked to be over. Indeed, the Frenchman scored just four goals for LAFC, even losing his place in the starting lineup of the Major League Soccer outfit. Giroud struggled to make any sort of impact on the other side of the Atlantic.

By returning to his homeland with Lille last year, though, Giroud was revitalised. While the veteran might not boast the mobility he possessed earlier in his career, Giroud remains an extremely effective focal point in the final third. There’s a reason Davide Ancelotti continues to use him in the biggest games.

Ancelotti might favour Ayase Ueda from the start against Arsenal due to the Japanese international’s ability to get in behind opposition defences. The Premier League champions will almost certainly control the bulk of Tuesday’s match, limiting Lille to quick-transition moments and counter-attacks. Ueda might be a better fit for this approach than Giroud.

Nonetheless, there could be a role for Giroud to play if Lille want to use the veteran’s experience and nous to unsettle the normally formidable Arsenal backline. As a facilitator and a centre forward willing to occupy opposition defenders, Giroud has proven himself over countless seasons.

Arsenal will have no regrets over their decision to move on from Giroud in 2018. Since then, the Gunners have grown into a team that expects to challenge on all fronts for silverware. Giroud won the FA Cup three times over the course of his six years at the club. Now, though, Arsenal are Premier League champions and Champions League contenders.

In Kai Havertz, there is overlap between the German’s current role in the Arsenal side and what Giroud was expected to do in red and white. Havertz is also a facilitator, helping the bring the best out of others around him such as Martin Ødegaard and Bukayo Saka. He’s also strong in the air, as Giroud was and still is.

“First of all, a great character and a great person to have around the dressing room,” said Arteta when asked about his reunion with Giroud, a player he played alongside for the Gunners. “I remember when he came in, he won Ligue 1 with Montpellier. He came here and he really impacted the team in a very different way, a completely different profile than we were used to. What a career he had, and he definitely earned it as well.

“He was extremely intelligent at first and he was really, really a handful as a player. Every time you had him on the pitch, you had a massive threat inside the box. He was very smart. He was so good at connecting with other players as well and his work rate was phenomenal.”

When Giroud does retire, whenever that day comes, he will be able to reflect on a glittering career at the top level. At times, though, the Frenchman hasn’t always been appreciated, sometimes even by his own fans. There were points at which the Arsenal support bemoaned not possessing a striker who could be counted on to score 20 goals every single season.

It didn’t help Giroud that he arrived at the Emirates Stadium as the direct replacement for Robin Van Persie, arguably the most potent centre forward in the Premier League at the time. He was unfairly seen as a symbol of Arsenal’s inability to compete for the biggest prizes as Wenger’s influence waned.

As a World Cup winner with France in 2018 and a player whose longevity has ultimately earned him respect, Giroud should be appreciated for what he is rather than what he is. Arsenal’s fans will have, most likely, one last chance to show the gratitude their former striker deserved all along.

          The Best Starts to a Premier League Season
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Which teams have made the best starts to a Premier League season? We use Opta's historical data to find out.

9 Wins: Chelsea in 2005-068 Wins: Liverpool in 2019-207 Wins: Manchester City in 2026-276 Wins: Newcastle United in 1994-956 Wins: Chelsea in 2009-106 Wins: Manchester City in 2016-176 Wins: Liverpool in 2018-196 Wins: Manchester City in 2023-245 Wins: Arsenal in 2004-055 Wins: Chelsea in 2010-115 Wins: Manchester United 2011-125 Wins: Manchester City in 2015-165 Wins: Chelsea in 2018-195 Wins: Arsenal in 2022-235 Wins: Liverpool in 2025-26
Chelsea hold the record for the best start to a Premier League season with nine consecutive wins.

In what was a golden era for the club, the defending Premier League champions set out to retain their crown in ravenous fashion and José Mourinho's side had the rest of the pack panting in their wake within just a few weeks.

Wigan Athletic, Arsenal, West Brom, Tottenham, Sunderland and Charlton Athletic were their first six victims, seeing them equal the Premier League record for most successive wins at the start of a season.

Then, a 2-1 comeback triumph at home to Aston Villa courtesy of a Frank Lampard double saw Chelsea set a new record, which was then extended with 4-1 and 5-1 hammerings of Liverpool and Bolton Wanderers, respectively.

They were halted in their pursuit of the all-time top-flight record (more on that later…) by Everton on Matchday 10, only able to leave Goodison Park with a 1-1 draw. Manchester United inflicted their first defeat of the season in early November, but Chelsea ended up coasting to the title with an eight-point lead over Sir Alex Ferguson's side.
Having gone agonisingly close to a Premier League and UEFA Champions League double the season before, only winning the latter, Liverpool began 2019-20 with a vengeance.

Norwich City, perennial lambs to the slaughter at Anfield, were gutted 4-1 on the opening day of the campaign, and Jürgen Klopp's side ploughed on thereafter. They didn't fall behind until Matchday 5 when an early Jetro Willems goal put Newcastle United 1-0 up on Merseyside, though a Sadio Mané double turned things around prior to half-time and Mohamed Salah sealed a 3-1 win.

Three more wins followed, the last of which – 2-1 at home to Leicester City – required a 95th-minute James Milner penalty. They were within touching distance of equalling Chelsea's 14-year-old record, but a ninth consecutive victory eluded them as they salvaged a 1-1 draw away to Manchester United thanks to Adam Lallana's late leveller.

That was a mere momentary blip in an otherwise tremendous season, however. They then embarked on a remarkable 18-match winning run in the top flight and went on to win their first league title in 30 years, and a first Premier League crown ever.
Manchester City started the 2026-27 Premier League campaign with seven wins from seven, giving new boss Enzo Maresca a perfect start after replacing Pep Guardiola in the summer.

Maresca was the first manager to win each of his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team, but that run came to an end in their eighth game of the campaign; losing 2-1 to Aston Villa at Villa Park.

It is, however, crucial to mention that City are at the centre of one of the biggest storms British sport has ever seen, after they were found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and the majority of charges relating to their failure to co-operate with the investigation. City deny all the allegations and have appealed against the charges.
Long before dignitaries of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund started fluttering eyelashes towards St James' Park, Newcastle had been one of the early powers of the Premier League.

But their 1994-95 season is a cautionary tale to any team who begin to believe their own hype. They were, after all, the first team to win each of their first six games of a Premier League campaign, and they did so in thrilling fashion.

Manager Kevin Keegan was renowned for his rather gung-ho tactics, and this run encapsulated them perfectly. Each of their opening six games saw at least four goals and they only kept one clean sheet. They crushed Coventry City (4-0) and Southampton (5-1) within the space of a few days; they also beat Chelsea 4-2 and Arsenal 3-2, the latter being at Highbury.

And yet, the wheels soon fell off. A 1-1 draw at Liverpool ended the winning run in late September, and they only earned another six league victories before the end of January. Another bad run towards the end of the season consigned them to a sixth-placed finish.
Carlo Ancelotti's Chelsea became only the third team in Premier League history to win their opening six games of a season en route to securing the 2009-10 title in record-breaking fashion.

A largely kind fixture schedule during the early weeks helped Chelsea set the tone. They beat Hull City, Sunderland, Fulham, Burnley and Stoke City, before then sweeping Spurs aside 3-0 on 20 September.

          Chelsea vs Tottenham Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 23, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Saturday's Premier League clash at Stamford Bridge with our Chelsea vs Tottenham prediction and preview. Can Roberto De Zerbi's team get their second win of the 2026-27 campaign?

Tottenham finally ended their wait for a Premier League win this season on Monday, beating Coventry City 3-1 at home, and they will hope to follow that up with another positive result at Chelsea on Saturday.

James Maddison scored a stunner on his first competitive start since May 2025, Omar Marmoush netted his maiden Spurs goal and Ben Davies came off the bench to grab the contest-settling goal in stoppage time.
Dejan Kulusevski also made his long-awaited return to action to rapturous applause from the stands, having been out injured since May 2025.
It was not the most convincing of 3-1 wins, but it got the job done, as Tottenham scored more than two goals in a Premier League match for the first time in 36 games.
In fact, it was the first time they scored 3+ goals on home soil in the league since MD1 last season against Burnley (3-0).
But Roberto De Zerbi's team are back on the road this weekend as they aim to build on that first win, heading across London to Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea also won last weekend, beating Everton 2-0 thanks to a pair of Pedro Neto goals. In doing so, they kept their first clean sheet in a Premier League match since January.
The Blues are looking to win three consecutive Premier League games for the first time since a run of four in January/February. They last recorded back-to-back shutouts in December last year.
Since the start of last season, meanwhile, Spurs have only won consecutive league matches twice (August 2025 and May 2026).
In addition, Tottenham have lost each of their last six London derbies in the Premier League. In their entire league history, they have never lost seven derby games in a row.
Spurs had not scored a league goal earlier than the 86th minute this season before Maddison struck from the edge of the box in the 14th minute against his former side Coventry.
Chelsea, on the other hand, have been one of the league's most potent teams this term. They have scored 17 goals, which ranks behind only Manchester City (19) and Brighton & Hove Albion (23).

However, Chelsea have actually outperformed their xG (9.9) by 7.1. That is the second-highest xG overperformance of any team in the division, after Brighton (+8.1), and demonstrates the quality of attackers Xabi Alonso has at his disposal, with Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer forming a formidable front three.

In fact, João Pedro (+2.0) and Rogers (+1.9) are the fourth and fifth highest xG overperformers in the competition; they do not need to be in an excellent position to come up with a moment of magic, while Neto is the sixth-highest xG overperformer (+1.8).

Rogers has been involved in six goals in six games against Spurs (four goals, two assists), all while an Aston Villa player. Since the 2024-25 season, only Eberechi Eze has been involved in more goals against Spurs in all competitions (seven).
Spurs, meanwhile, have recorded the third-lowest xG in the Premier League this term, with their 7.5 xG ahead of only Coventry (7.1) and Hull City (6.8).
Against Coventry, though, Spurs became the first side to score three goals from outside the box in a single Premier League game since Fulham vs Leicester City in May 2023.
It was the first time Spurs have scored 3+ goals from outside the box in a league game since September 2022 vs Leicester.

Tottenham have scored a higher share of their goals from outside the box than any other side in the Premier League this season (50% – 3/6). And in Maddison, they have a player adept at finishing from range.

          How Would a Points Deduction Affect Manchester City’s 2026-27 Premier League Season?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After the Opta supercomputer ran 100,000 simulations of Manchester City’s 2026-27 Premier League season, we‘ve calculated the precise impact of every possible points deduction.
Ever since Manchester City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules, speculation has been rife as to what their punishment might be.
The club maintain their innocence, and on Friday confirmed they have lodged an official appeal against the Premier League’s ruling.

It’s a completely unprecedented situation in many ways, and there are so many unknowns that it's impossible to say with any certainty what’s going to happen next. But the widely held view seems to be that any appeals process will mean it’s a long time before any final decision is made on what sentence City will serve (if they fail in their appeal).

The range of punishments being mooted is vast, and we’re not here to say where on the scale it should fall, but given that Everton and Nottingham Forest were both handed points deductions for financial rule-breaking in recent years, there is a real possibility that City will also face one this season.

Whether they are also given further sanctions remains to be seen and is not for us to speculate on. But what we can do here at Opta Analyst is use the wisdom of the Opta supercomputer to tell us precisely what impact any points deduction would have on the Premier League in 2026-27.

City are top of the Premier League at the time of writing with the only remaining 100% record, having become only the 14th team in the history of the competition to begin a season with five wins from five. But a points deduction could completely derail their season.
That said, they would have had a lot of work to do to go on and win the title regardless, given that only four of the previous 14 teams to begin with five wins went on to win the title.

Clearly, a fast start doesn’t necessarily bring success, and the Opta supercomputer currently makes them second favourites, with a 39.9% chance of winning the title, behind Arsenal’s 44.2% (based on no points deduction, as is currently the case).

But how exactly would a points deduction affect their chances? The Opta supercomputer has run 100,000 simulations of the rest of the season, before then applying every possible points deduction and spitting out a final league position for City. We can then look at the percentage of simulations in which City finish in each position to assign a likelihood of each eventuality, depending on the size of the points deduction.

So, we are now able to say the extent to which their title chances would drop depending on the points deduction, as well as their chances of qualifying for the Champions League. But perhaps most interestingly, how big the deduction would need to be to make it likely that City are relegated.  Inspired by the fine work of Aurel Nazmiu on X, we used the Opta supercomputer to create this visualisation with numbers from our own model:

This is, of course, entirely speculative. It is still unclear what City’s punishment will be or if their appeal will be successful, given they maintain their innocence. We at Opta Analyst have no way of knowing how the punishment will be decided, whether there will even be a punishment, or if any sanctions will extend into future seasons.
But they could quite feasibly face a punishment that includes a points deduction, and with that comes the possibility of relegation from the Premier League this season.

According to the supercomputer’s findings, City’s chances of relegation are only certain – meaning they were relegated in every single one of the 100,000 simulations – when they were given a 74-point deduction. For every possible deduction of fewer than 74 points, there was at least one simulation in which City avoided the drop.

That means that the supercomputer saw (rare) circumstances in which City were docked 73 points but won enough games to still finish on a higher total than three other teams. That would likely require them to win almost all of their remaining games, which isn’t impossible, but it is very, very unlikely.

It took a deduction of 40 points to tip City over a 50% likelihood of relegation, with a steady increase from there up to 60 points, at which point their chances of relegation get very close to – but not quite – 100%.
For every deduction of 30 points of fewer, City were relegated in fewer than 20% of simulations. Anything up to 20 points, and their chances of relegation remain under 5%.

For Champions League qualification, it took a 38-point deduction to reduce City’s chances to under 1%, based on the Premier League’s top four making it into that competition. If a fifth spot is up for grabs – as it has been in the last two seasons – City would have slightly more wiggle room: a 40-point deduction would be needed to reduce their chances to less than 1%.

As for the title race, the supercomputer reckons City would retain a chance of more than 10% with anything under 10 points deducted, while it took 25 points being taken off their total for them to be reduced to complete outsiders, with less than a 1% chance of winning the league.
For now, there’s no knowing what City’s punishment will be, but the Opta supercomputer is able to give us a little more idea of the impact of any potential points deduction.

51tvegbakana1ct70djfg6wbe.title: ​Newcastle United 0-1 Aston Villa: Manzambi downs former suitors as Jaissle's struggles continue
51tvegbakana1ct70djfg6wbe.subtitle: Johan Manzambi almost became a Newcastle United player this summer, but instead, he was Aston Villa's hero as they won 1-0 on Tyneside.
paragraphs: Former Newcastle United transfer target Johan Manzambi was the match-winner as Aston Villa earned a 1-0 victory over Matthias Jaissle's side at a disgruntled St. James' Park.

Manzambi had looked set to join Newcastle from Freiburg in July, only for that deal to be successfully hijacked by Villa, and on Saturday, he continued his superb start to Premier League life at the Magpies' expense.
His 36th-minute header gave Unai Emery's side a lead they would not relinquish, with Newcastle being booed off following their second Premier League defeat in a row.

It was Villa who started on the front foot as Nicolas Jackson shot straight at Lukas Hornicek with the outside of his boot, while Sven Botman was arguably fortunate to avoid a red card after clattering the former Chelsea and Bayern Munich forward.
Jackson continued to be heavily involved as his curler flicked off Botman and faded wide, but it was Manzambi who opened the scoring.
He was left totally unmarked when Joao Gomes floated a cross in from the right flank, and though Hornicek got a hand to his header, there was simply too much power for the Czech to keep it out.

Newcastle had a huge reprieve when Emiliano Buendia's shot smacked off the post and hit Hornicek on the back, with no claret shirts ready to pounce on what would have been a tap-in, and the half-time whistle brought boos from the disgruntled home fans.

Having scored a wonder-goal in Newcastle's 4-1 defeat at Coventry City five days earlier, Botman almost repeated the trick with a well-struck effort that Zion Suzuki had to push wide, while Yoane Wissa headed over as the hosts grew increasingly desperate.
Hornicek tipped a drive from Villa substitute Ross Barkley around his right-hand post, as Villa combined their resolute defensive work with incisive counter-attacking.
Ibrahim Mbaye had two opportunities to get a clinching goal off the bench, one of which saw him power over at the near post, while the second saw his reverse shot fade wide following a mazy dribble.

But with Wissa planting his final attempt wide of the right post and Victor Lindelof throwing himself in front of the ball amid a late scramble in the Villa area, Newcastle were unable to find an equaliser.
Manzambi shows Newcastle what they are missing
Things could have been very different had Manzambi signed on the dotted line at St. James', but the draw of UEFA Champions League football lured him to Villa.
And the Switzerland international has now been directly involved in five goals in four starts for Villa in all competitions, scoring three and assisting two.

Manzambi is just the fourth player to either score or assist on each of his first three Premier League starts for Villa, after Dalian Atkinson in August 1992, Dion Dublin in November 1998 and Danny Ings in August 2021.

By contrast, Newcastle's big-money attacking signing – Matias Fernandez-Pardo – has only had two shots in five Premier League games this campaign (one on target) and is still yet to score. He was quiet again on Saturday before being withdrawn in the 56th minute.

The Magpies were truly dismal in the first half, with Villa goalkeeper Suzuki completing more passes prior to the interval (24) than any home player, and Newcastle's 16-game run without a clean sheet at home (in all competitions) is now the longest in their history.

Emery, meanwhile, was left to celebrate his 100th Premier League win across spells with Arsenal and Villa, reaching that tally in 197 games (D44 L53) – he is the joint-ninth fastest manager to reach a century of victories in the competition.

5260A198D817B369DE6CC7483FC62088.title: Joao Felix finally showing what the fuss is about in an expanded role for Portugal
5260A198D817B369DE6CC7483FC62088.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesJoao Felix finally showing what the fuss is about in an expanded role for PortugalShareThe career of the 26-year-old, which has taken many of Europe’s biggest clubs, has been one of modern football’s greatest curiosities.

Portugal’s new era looked a lot like the old one as Jorge Jesus picked his first lineup as manager. There was still a place, initially, for 41-year-old Cristiano Ronaldo whose fading contribution undermined Portugal’s entire 2026 World Cup campaign. João Félix was also selected to face Wales and Denmark.

The days of Félix being the face of Portuguese football’s next generation seemed long gone. Written off as a flop after a meandering route that took in many of Europe’s biggest clubs, Felix joined Al-Nasser in the Saudi Pro League last year. It was a move that appeared to indicate Felix had given up on making an impact at the elite level.

Against Wales and Denmark, though, Félix was Portugal’s best player. The 26-year-old found the back of the net in both games, demonstrating the sort of composure in front of goal that evaded Ronaldo. If there was one player who looked to have scored 146 international goals in his career, it wasn’t the 41-year-old.

Only Erling Haaland had more shots than Félix in Sunday’s meeting between Norway and Portugal while only Ronaldo had more in the win over Wales in Lisbon. At a time when it would have been easy for Félix to be pushed aside due to the location of his club, he is finally showing what he can do at international level.

Félix has long been a mystery box of a player. He became the second-most expensive teenager in football history after Kylian Mbappé when he joined Atlético Madrid for €126m in 2019, but was never a good fit for Diego Simeone’s playing style. While there were glimpses of Félix’s talent, he struggled for form.

From there, Félix made the ill-advised decision to join Chelsea when the Stamford Bridge club lacked any sort of direction. A loan to Barcelona similarly did little to help the Portuguese attacker’s development with a short stint at AC Milan possibly the most forgettable of his career.

Amid all these bouncing around, Felix failed to nail down a position. Some managers used him in a wide role despite the fact Félix has never been much of a one-on-one dribbler. Others deployed him as a second striker where his knack for finding space between the lines is useful.

To use Félix as a roaming number 10, though, the teams he played for required a rock-steady midfield platform to compensate. His selection frequently put too much strain on other parts of the side and so it was easier to use Félix as a depth option off the bench. That has been his role at several clubs.

In the Saudi Pro League, though, Al-Nasser have built around Félix who scored 20 league goals in 33 games in his debut season. Then the coach of his club side, Jesus embraced Félix in a way no manager had done since the attacker’s Benfica days and the results have been astonishing. It took a move to Saudi Arabia for Félix to show his potential again.

In Jesus, Félix has found a father figure. The veteran coach has put his arm around the shoulder of a widely misunderstood player who not so long ago was considered one of the most exciting in Europe. When Félix broke through at Benfica, he was compared to Johan Cruyff. That’s how much promise he had.

Since then, Félix has paid a heavy price for several bad career decisions, but he’s still only 26. There is still time for him to become the player many predicted he would be. Portugal are certainly benefiting from Félix operating in a free role that makes the most of his natural talent as a creator and a finisher.

“That’s where I can make things happen,” said Félix when asked about the second striker role Jesus has trusted him in for club and country. “He’s played me there since last year and everyone can see the results. I hope it will be the same in the national team – that things go well and people will see the real me.”

In Félix’s own words, he would entertain a return to Europe at some point in the future. “I’m happy and enjoying my soccer, but it’s true that I’m also thinking about returning,” said the 26-year-old. “I don’t know whether it’ll be next year, in two years, three or four, but I’d like to play in European competitions again.”

When Jesus was hired as Roberto Martínez’s replacement after the World Cup, many cynically – and perhaps fairly – looked at how the former Al-Nasser boss would favour Ronaldo. Instead, Ronaldo was benched for the win over Norway with Félix the main man in the number 10 role.

Perhaps more significant than Félix scoring in back-to-back games against Wales and Norway was the fact he played the full 90 minutes in successive matches as a Portugal international. A Saudi Pro League star is responding well to Jesus as Portugal’s new manager, but not the obvious one.

paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsRangersScores & FixturesTableScottish FootballMcInnes defends Fernandez before League Cup semiTo play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.This video can not be played
Rangers manager Derek McInnes defends Emmanuel Fernandez
Rangers manager Derek McInnes has defended Emmanuel Fernandez, saying the centre-back "has been a big part" of their strong displays this term.
The Nigeria defender has come under some criticism after some high=profile mistakes, including during Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Hearts at Tynecastle in the Scottish Premiership.
The 25-year-old has started every match for Rangers, who have kept the most clean sheets in the league so far this season.

"I only get asked about Fernandez when he has a poor game. Nobody asked me about Fernandez on Saturday, he was outstanding on Saturday [against St Johnstone]," McInnes said before Saturday's League Cup semi-final against Aberdeen.
"Wednesday night wasn't on Manny Fernandez, Wednesday night was a collective.
"I never get asked about Manny when he does really well and he's been a big part of our better performances this season."
To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.This video can not be played
Rangers head to Hampden on Saturday - where Aberdeen await in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup - and McInnes is hoping to get the better of his old club.
Rangers have won three trophies since 2012 and have finished the last two seasons without any silverware.
McInnes, who took charge in June, is the latest manager charged with turning around that poor return and has the chance to make his mark, having defeated Celtic 3-0 in the quarter-finals at Ibrox.
"To get the first trophy would be so important, reinforcing confidence, reinforcing belief," the Rangers boss said.
"Traditionally, semi-finals can be fraught with a lot of nerves and tension and sometimes they're not the best games, because of what's at stake."
Aberdeen's poor form makes Rangers strong favourites to progress to December's final against either Hearts or Hibernian.
However, Dons boss Stephen Robinson did lift the trophy last term when in charge of St Mirren, and McInnes is wary of their opponents' ability to perform in a one-off game.
"They've got a good, experienced manager in Robbo and they've got some good players, experienced players, in Aberdeen and they'll be relishing the opportunity as well," McInnes added.
"People might view us as favourites for it and I understand that but we've' still got a game to win and Aberdeen are capable of a big performance.
"I'm just concentrating on us, if we get to our levels then hopefully it's going to be enough to win the game but a strong 90-minute performance is going to be required, I feel."

          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 6
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Looking for an edge with under-the-radar picks in Fantasy Premier League? Well, The 10% Club is back to help following the international break.
The extended international break is finally over, and although you might have a few new injury concerns, that also means Fantasy Premier League returns this weekend.
Indeed, managers opening up their teams may be greeted with red and yellow hazard signs galore after numerous players withdrew either before or during the international window.
However, we have some options in The 10% Club to cover those potential gaps. Using Opta data, here are our five under-the-radar picks for Gameweek 6.
A hard-fought goalless draw away to Leeds United may have slightly eased the pressure on Pierre Sage, and he will be desperate for Crystal Palace to improve further after the break.
Having kept their first clean sheet of the season at Elland Road, Tyrick Mitchell is an interesting pick for when goal-shy Nottingham Forest visit south east London.
Forest, managed by former Palace boss Oliver Glasner, have scored just four times this season, with only two sides – Tottenham (2) and Coventry City (1) – finding the net on fewer occasions.
No Palace player can better Mitchell’s 24 points this season either, partly due to the attacking threat he can pose.

He's never been a particularly frequent source of goals, though his two in the league this term is the most of any defender. That could easily have turned to three goals as well, if not for a VAR review seeing Mitchell’s sumptuous strike against Leeds ruled out for an Anan Khalaili offside in the build-up.

It's worth saying, however, that Mitchell’s two biggest points hauls – 15 against Fulham and 7 against Leeds – came away from home. Sage will have designs on Palace turning around their home form this weekend, though.

Mitchell’s affordable price point could also help managers find room for the likes of James Tarkowski, Josko Gvardiol or Riccardo Calafiori, with the option to leave Mitchell on the bench when Palace visit free-scoring Brighton on GW7.

Many managers this season are opting to target whoever is playing Coventry. Their 1-0 away win last time out over Forest may have perturbed some, but those sticking to that plan will note they host Newcastle United.
Lewis Hall and Yoane Wissa are both off the cards due to their ownership proportions, but Harvey Barnes has scored the second-most points (28 – behind only Hall’s 31) for Newcastle.
Barnes claimed nine points against Hull City before the break after assisting twice in one Premier League match for the first time since May 2022 (for Leicester City against Norwich City).

He has been Newcastle’s main creative threat this term, leading the way with six chances created and all of them were from open play. Hall is second on the list with five, but that is aided by two from set-pieces.

More goals may not be far away for Barnes. Only Joe Willock (10) and Wissa (9) have had more than his eight shots for Newcastle, though Barnes has just one goal – a stunning strike against Bournemouth on GW3 – to show for his efforts.
Barnes then faces Aston Villa (H), Palace (A), Everton (H) and Fulham (A), and that fairly favourable run may see FPL players splashing out on Newcastle assets.
With Ipswich Town next hosting Fulham, Gary O’Neil will see it as a great chance to pick up three points against Álvaro Arbeloa’s winless side.
Although Julio Enciso is yet to score this season, we believe he could make the difference for Ipswich on GW6. The Paraguayan did also manage two assists from his opening two games.

No Ipswich player has attempted more shots than Enciso’s 17, while his four shots on target is only matched by Emersonn. Abdul Fatawu (1.1) has marginally bettered his 0.9 expected assists (xA), but the winger is suspended after his red card at Everton.

          Kane, Yamal, Mbappé or Messi: Who Should Win the 2026 Men's Ballon d'Or?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Thirty players are on the shortlist for the 2026 Men's Ballon d'Or, but who's actually in contention for the award?
Who will win the 2026 Men's Ballon d'Or? Well, we don't have to wait much longer to find out.
The ceremony will take place on Monday, crowning one player as the best in the world based on their performances between 3 August 2025 and 19 July 2026.
The shortlist for the men's award stands at 30 strong and includes three former winners: Ousmane Dembélé (2025), Rodri (2024) and Lionel Messi (2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021, 2023).

But some have far more realistic chances of winning this year's prize than others. Ahead of Monday's ceremony, it would seem there are four clear frontrunners; here, we assess their respective chances.

It may not count for much given Vinícius Júnior was hotly tipped before losing out to Rodri in the 2024 Ballon d’Or, but ahead of Monday’s ceremony, Harry Kane is the favourite to take home the prize this year.
That might even be something of a surprise to many. Not because there’s any doubt about just how good Kane is, rather that he would buck a fairly established trend.

In World Cup years since the start of the 1990s, there have only been two instances of a player not winning the Champions League/European Cup or being a world champion but taking home the Ballon d’Or: Hristo Stoichkov in 1994 and Messi in 2010.

Not that he had a bad year on either front. His Bayern Munich side reached the semi-finals of the Champions League, while he captained England to the last four of the World Cup. And, unsurprisingly, he played a major role in both runs.
Kane scored 14 times for Bayern in the Champions League, bettered only by Kylian Mbappé (15), and he netted six in the World Cup; just four players scored more.
Kane’s 14 UCL goals came amid a generally exceptional season at club level, helping Bayern stroll to the Bundesliga title with a 16-point cushion and success in the DFB-Pokal.

He scored 61 times in 51 appearances across all competitions, 19 more than anyone else playing in the top five European leagues; in fact, the only player to net more in a single campaign for a club from one of Europe’s top leagues was Messi (73) in 2011-12.
Thirty-six of Kane’s 61-goal haul came in the Bundesliga, securing him the European Golden Shoe for a second time, with only Messi (6) and Cristiano Ronaldo (4) having won it more often.
Although Kane won’t have won the prize while playing for a Premier League club if he is ultimately crowned on Monday, such a success would be momentous for English football.
No English player has won the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. Before him, the country’s only recipients were Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) and Bobby Charlton (1966).

It’s fair to say Kane’s decision to leave Tottenham – and specifically for Bayern – has long been vindicated from a trophies perspective. Winning the Ballon d’Or would provide him with the ultimate personal recognition that would probably have never arrived if he’d stayed at Spurs.

The most realistic challenger to Kane’s Ballon d’Or bid? It seems that way; he did win the World Cup after all, and as noted before, football’s biggest individual prize is ordinarily won by a world champion on applicable years.
It also shouldn’t be forgotten that Lamine Yamal enjoyed an excellent 2025-26 season at club level with Barcelona. But, like Kane, he didn’t win the Champions League.

For some voters, the very fact Yamal was in the World Cup-winning Spain side will have been enough to earn points. For others, though, the question being asked will be how critical was his contribution to Spain’s glory?

Obviously it’s pretty difficult to work this out definitively; an attacker may not record many goals or assists but their input could have still been vital for many goals. But people will, most of the time, be led by the topline numbers.

          Man City Head to Anfield – the Worst Place They Could Possibly Go After All That’s Happened
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City always get a rough reception at Anfield, but this weekend, Liverpool fans will surely be even less welcoming.
With all that’s gone on in the past couple of weeks, Manchester City’s players could have been forgiven for hoping to make an inconspicuous return to the pitch.
But rather than going straight back to the sanctity of the Etihad Stadium, they face arguably the most intimidating trip imaginable, to the bearpit that is Anfield.

The players and new manager Enzo Maresca are caught at the centre of one of the biggest storms British sport has ever seen, after City were found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation. City deny all the allegations and have appealed against the charges.

But following the verdict, there is going to be a sizeable and unavoidable backlash. Many other clubs and their fans feel aggrieved that they lost out on trophies, prize money, league positions, signings and more to a club who have been found guilty of operating outside of rules that they were following and restricted by.

Liverpool will feel that they are among the clubs to have most reason to feel hard done by, having missed out on the title to City in 2013-14 and the League Cup in 2015-16. Since the 2009-2018 period for which City have been charged – a time during which there is no accusation of cheating – Liverpool also finished second to them in 2018-19 and 2021-22, with mammoth points totals of 97 and 92 respectively. Their fans have missed out on a lot of joy to City over the years, and may well feel some bitterness towards them.

Anfield has always been a notoriously difficult place for visiting teams to go to anyway, and at least some part of that is down to the atmosphere created. The fans are often said to be among the loudest in the world, and the atmosphere is roundly thought of as among the very best.

Speaking to BBC Sport in 2021, former Man City defender Micah Richards said as much. “When you're playing, you feel confident, but when you go to Anfield it is like you have your legs on backwards,” he said. “You cannot play a simple ball. It is like a fortress. I never had a great memory from Liverpool. They were just too good.”
And in 2020, France Football ranked Anfield second in the world to Boca Juniors’ Bombonera in a list of the grounds with the best atmospheres in football.
As the COVID-affected Premier League 2020-21 season proved, home crowds make a difference, and the impact of the Liverpool fanbase showed in their results.

Though they have consistently been at the very least a good team, Liverpool have not been the outright best side for much of the Premier League era, and yet away sides have a lower win percentage at Anfield (12.5%) than at any other stadium in Premier League history. Liverpool have lost just 82 of their 654 games there in the competition, with visitors averaging a paltry 0.62 points per game.

There are many teams who struggle at Anfield. Newcastle have won only one and lost 25 of their 31 Premier League trips there, giving them a loss rate of 80.6%. West Ham have won only one of 30 games and Spurs have won just two of 34. Six teams have lost every single one of their games away to Liverpool in the Premier League.

This Sunday was always going to be a tough assignment for City. When the fixture list for the season was confirmed in the summer, Maresca would have circled this as one to have his eye on, facing an opponent who could well be a title rival. Or, at the very least, provide one of the biggest tests of City’s title credentials.

That is because City, like so many others, also have a dreadful record at Anfield. It’s not quite as terrible as the teams mentioned above, but it isn’t great and doesn’t bode well for them for Sunday.

Of grounds City have played at more than once, they only have a worse points-per-game rate at Highbury (0.22) than they do at Anfield (0.59), and they have played more than three times as many games at Liverpool's home (29) as they have at Arsenal’s old ground (9).
They also played at Highbury back when, well, they weren’t very good at all, while their visits to Anfield have included the entire Sheikh Mansour era.

In total, City have won only three of their 29 Premier League trips to Anfield, giving them one of their worst win rates (10.3%) at any stadium. They have also lost 18 of those games, meaning at Anfield, they boast one of their worst loss rates (62.1%) as well.

They did win there last season, though, coming from behind with two late goals to snatch a 2-1 win, but that came with Liverpool at a particularly low ebb, during a run of one win in seven games as their title defence fell to pieces.

City also won at Anfield in February 2021, in the COVID season during which games were played with no fans in the ground. That was their first win there in 18 visits. Clearly, City, like many other teams, struggle with playing at Anfield, especially when there are supporters present.

Then, this weekend, add into the mix that it is City’s first game since the independent commission’s guilty verdict was announced, and you have an almighty challenge for the group of players and staff who are on the frontline.

          UEFA Champions League Match Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer’s Picks for This Week
        
      
                          
                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the AI-powered Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Champions League match predictions for every game across the 2026-27 competition.

The Opta supercomputer will again be with us every step of the way in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League as the model works to provide you with data-backed predictions for all matches and season outcomes.

Paris Saint-Germain have won back-to-back Champions League crowns after their penalty-shootout win over Arsenal in last season’s final, and they are among the favourites once again this time around. Real Madrid were the last team to win the UCL in three consecutive seasons, doing so in 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18.

The Spanish giants, alongside rivals Barcelona, will be among the leading contenders in 2026-27, along with a host of Premier League clubs. There will be five English top-flight teams competing in the league phase this time around, with Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool among the favourites, and Manchester United alongside Aston Villa in the chasing pack.

Bayern Munich haven’t won the Champions League since 2020, but will undoubtedly be in the mix again this season, while Serie A clubs Inter Milan, Como, Napoli and Roma will be hoping to end a 17-year wait for an Italian winner.
Below, Opta Analyst provides detailed predictions for each game from Matchday 2, powered by thousands of simulations from the Opta supercomputer.
After a record-breaking matchday last week, the UEFA Champions League returns for gameweek three of the league phase.
There were more goals scored on MD2 (78) than on any previous matchday in UCL history, and fans will hope to see many more as the action kicks off with two early games in Turkey and Azerbaijan.

Sabah earned their first-ever win in the UEFA Champions League (outside of qualifiers) last week, beating Slavia Prague 2-0 thanks to two second-half goals. They face a much harder test in front of their own fans this week, though, coming up against Bundesliga side Borussia Dortmund.

Borussia Dortmund have won all four of their matches against Azerbaijani opponents in European competition (including qualifiers), and the Opta supercomputer is backing them to make it five from five this week. BVB won 68.9% of its 10,000 pre-game simulations.

After that defeat to Sabah on MD2, Slavia Prague head to Fenerbahçe looking to win their first points of the UCL campaign. The Opta supercomputer isn’t too confident on their chances of doing that, though, with the Turkish side winning 55.1% of its pre-game simulations.

Fenerbahçe were comprehensively thrashed 6-0 at Aston Villa last week, but they might be facing the perfect opponent to bounce back. Slavia have now gone 21 consecutive Champions League matches without a win (D7 L14).

The standout match on Tuesday night is Paris Saint-Germain vs Barcelona, with two of the biggest clubs in world football currently occupying first and second place in the league-phase table after two matchdays.

Reigning champions PSG will be looking for a third successive win against Barcelona. Only Bayern Munich (May 2015-October 2022) has ever done that previously in UCL history. The Opta supercomputer had a hard time picking a winner in this tie, but PSG just edged it (39.7%) over Barcelona (37.7%) in the pre-match sims.

Most eyes on Tuesday will be on this game, and for good reason. Of fixtures played 10+ times in European Cup/Champions League history, only Ajax vs Bayern Munich (3.9) has a higher goals-per-game ratio than Paris Saint-Germain vs Barcelona (3.8 – 57 goals in 15 meetings).
Manchester City lost 4-2 in an action-packed meeting with PSG last week and will look to return to form with a home game against AEK Athens.

The last team from outside of Europe’s big five leagues to win away at Man City in the Champions League was Basel in March 2018 (1-2). Since then, they are unbeaten in 15 (W12 D3), averaging three goals per match (3.1 – 46 in total).

AEK will also come up against the red-hot Erling Haaland, who now has 61 goals in 60 UEFA Champions League appearances, including 27 in 22 matches against teams from outside the top five European leagues.
The threat of Haaland is one reason for the Opta supercomputer’s lopsided match prediction, with City winning 83.0% of its simulations and the Greek club winning just 6.8%.
Liverpool are another side heavily backed to win at home on MD3, with the Premier League side defeating Villarreal across 61.4% of 10,000 pre-match simulations.

577ct7z5vig2z566vq5e9itf.title: England 3-0 Czechia: Kane doubles up on record-equalling appearance
577ct7z5vig2z566vq5e9itf.subtitle: Harry Kane marked his record-equalling appearance by being involved in all of England's goals in a 3-0 Nations League defeat of Czechia.
paragraphs: England swatted aside Czechia 3-0 as Harry Kane played a starring role on his landmark appearance.
Kane played his 125th game for the Three Lions on Tuesday, matching Peter Shilton as England's joint-most-capped player.
And Kane marked the occasion in style, playing a role in all of England's goals in a routine Nations League triumph at Wembley Stadium.
England made a dominant start, though they were not rewarded for their efforts until the 27th minute, when Kane swung in a cross, aiming for Eberechi Eze.
Eze stalled his run, but Vladimir Coufal was unaware and, under no pressure, the former West Ham defender slid in and diverted the ball into the back of Czechia's net.

England doubled their lead in sumptuous style 13 minutes later. Elliot Anderson swept a sublime pass over the top for Morgan Rogers, who cushioned a wonderful first-time pass into Kane's path, and the Three Lions captain made no mistake with his finish.

Kane struck the top of the crossbar with a swerving strike at the end of a slick move shortly after half-time, but he helped himself to his second when he headed home unchallenged from Lewis Hall's corner.

Thomas Tuchel took the chance to hand some of his fringe players a chance late on, including Rio Ngumoha, who became the second-youngest player to feature for England at Wembley (18 years, 38 days), behind Jude Bellingham (17 years, 136 days).
Czechia offered little threat, bar a stinging long-range drive from Roman Macek, as England eased onto nine points in Nations League Group A3, three behind leaders Spain.
Another special Wembley showing for Kane
Kane will have to wait until at least November for his record-breaking England cap, but he was always likely to have a say on the day he equalled Shilton.
The 33-year-old has now scored 2+ goals in six different matches for England at Wembley, now the outright most of any player, overtaking Alan Shearer (five).

He has also netted at least twice in 18 different games for the Three Lions, which is another record, while Kane is the oldest player in England's history to score a brace in consecutive appearances (33 years, 70 days tonight).
Kane's 13 goals in 2026 are now the second most any England player has scored in a single calendar year, behind the 16 he netted in 2021.
That goal tally is also the most among any European player in 2026, with Kane now ahead of France's Kylian Mbappe (12).
It was about as comfortable as you can get for England, who created chances worth 1.83 expected goals but allowed Czechia to have just five shots, which were worth a combined 0.17 xG.
England will need just a point from their last two games to join Spain in qualifying for the quarter-finals, while Czechia have lost five matches on the bounce.

581xez1qykid1ibegdrpzwdxs.title: Portland boss Cifuentes wary of experienced Charlotte side
581xez1qykid1ibegdrpzwdxs.subtitle: The Portland Timbers will be hoping to end their torrid run of form in MLS when they host Charlotte FC on Saturday.
paragraphs: Portland Timbers boss Marti Cifuentes insisted he understood the challenges that come with facing more experienced teams such as upcoming opponents Charlotte FC.
The Timbers have been in poor form, with their last MLS win coming on September 5 against Minnesota United.
Portland's recent results have seen them drop to 11th in the Western Conference, five points behind the Colorado Rapids, who occupy the final postseason spot.
Next up for the Timbers is a home matchup against Charlotte, whose roster features the likes of Allan Saint-Maximin, Tim Ream and Ashley Westwood.
Cifuentes acknowledged the challenge of facing more experienced sides and has urged his players to always be focused.
"When you approach a younger team, you know that they are capable of having a fantastic game," said Cifuentes. "But, at the same time, it can be a little bit up and down.
"While when you face a more experienced team, they know how to handle different situations.
"So even if they don't start the game in the best way, they are more calm, they are more composed, and that's what makes them a difficult team to beat.
"They don't need a lot of possession. They don't need a lot of situations around the box to create chances, because they rely on this composure and this experience that they have with many players."
Charlotte are fifth in the East and still have a chance of finishing second in the conference.
They were held to a 2-2 draw by the Philadelphia Union last time out, which came after a 3-1 defeat against the Columbus Crew.
Portland Timbers – David da Costa
David da Costa leads the Timbers in assists this season (eight), and Portland will need the midfielder to be in top form for the remainder of this season.
Since the beginning of the 2024 campaign, the Timbers have been shut out at home in six regular-season matches, and four of those have been in the month of October.
Charlotte FC – Idan Toklomati
Idan Toklomati has scored four goals over his last three matches, netting at least once in all three games.
Toklomati is the fourth different Charlotte player to score in three consecutive MLS matches, and he is looking to be the first to do so in four straight.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Charlotte earned a draw against Philadelphia despite trailing 1-0 at half-time. Charlotte have lost just one of their last six MLS matches when conceding first (W3 D2) after earning 11 total points in their previous 25 such regular-season matches.
Portland are winless in their last seven outings (D3 L4), most recently a 0-0 home draw against Colorado on Saturday.
The only longer regular-season winless streaks by the Timbers were a nine-game streak in 2024 and eight-game streaks in both 2012 and 2014.

The lone previous meeting between Charlotte and Portland was a 2-0 home win for Charlotte in 2024. Charlotte have won two of their 15 all-time MLS road games against Western Conference teams (D5 L8), with their last win coming in May 2023 at LA Galaxy.
Portland Timbers – 38.5%

          Conference League Predictions 2026-27: The Opta Supercomputer Projections
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Ahead of the 2026-27 Conference League getting started, the Opta supercomputer has run 10,000 simulations of the season. But who won the competition most often?
A European campaign starting in mid-October? It must finally be time for the UEFA Conference League.

Like the Champions League and Europa League, the Conference League has 36 participating teams, but the league phase for the latter only consists of six games per team rather than eight. So while we’re already onto the second round of games in the UCL and UEL, the Conference League only just begins this Thursday.

The last two (and three of the last four) Conference League crowns have been won by English sides, with Crystal Palace lifting their first European trophy back in May as they beat Rayo Vallecano in the final.
Will Palace’s fierce rivals Brighton & Hove Albion make it three in a row for the Premier League, or will someone else step up?
Using the Opta supercomputer, we have run 10,000 projections of this season’s competition to see which teams are likeliest to be successful in the final in Istanbul on 2 June 2027.
Despite having never won a European trophy before, Brighton are huge favourites to lift this season’s Conference League trophy before a ball is kicked.
There are many reasons the Opta supercomputer is leaning so heavily in the Seagulls’ favour, but mostly because of their high placing in the current Opta Power Rankings.

Thanks to consistent performances in the strongest league in the world (also according to Opta’s rankings), and their particularly excellent start to this season – including an emphatic 3-0 win over #1 ranked Arsenal – Brighton are eighth in the global Power Rankings. That has them above teams like Chelsea, Inter and Manchester United. Indeed, they are only three places below Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain.
Fabian Hürzeler will need to navigate a European campaign alongside their domestic one, though, and Brighton’s ability to manage the extra games will be key in how successful they are on both fronts.
According to the Opta supercomputer, though, they have a great chance of going all the way in Europe, winning the Conference League in a whopping 43.8% of simulations.
The south-coast club have an incredible 98.2% chance of making it to the last 16.
No other team won it even 10% of the time, but let’s run through who else could enjoy success should Brighton stumble.
Monaco have also made a strong start domestically, sitting top of Ligue 1 after six games played, taking advantage of PSG’s poor form.

Filipe Luís has his team playing good football, and their significantly greater experience in Europe could give them an advantage over Brighton, whom they play at home on Matchday 5 of the league phase.
The supercomputer gives Monaco a 9.6% chance of winning the Conference League, just behind Freiburg, whom Monaco are also scheduled to face.

The Bundesliga side were beaten in the Europa League final by Aston Villa last season but will hope to put that right in this competition as third favourites. Like Monaco, Freiburg top their domestic league somewhat surprisingly, and Julian Schuster will be confident his team can manage both European and domestic action as they did so well last term.
The Breisgau Brazilians avenged their Europa League final loss by winning the Conference League this season in 9.9% of simulations.

One team who had a bit more joy in recent Europa League seasons is Atalanta, who won the competition in 2023-24. La Dea were in the Champions League last season, reaching the round of 16, but they were dumped out 10-2 on aggregate by Bayern Munich.
They won’t have to face anyone of that quality in this competition, though, and they have a 5.9% chance of adding Conference League glory to their previous Europa League success.

          Man City vs PSG: Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 12, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Wednesday's UEFA Champions League clash with our Man City vs PSG prediction and preview, as the two-time reigning European champions head to the Etihad Stadium.
Manchester City responded to a tumultuous couple of weeks on Sunday, as they beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield.

Man City fans in the away end soaked in the victory and revelled in their team's show of defiance, after the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018. City have lodged an appeal, while awaiting news of a sanction.
Perhaps fittingly, then, it is another state-backed club next up for City, as they host Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League.
PSG have gone from the Champions League's nearly men to two-time winners of the competition in the last couple of years.
Luis Enrique's team have not made the best of starts in Ligue 1, but they can probably afford a sluggish couple of months before clicking into gear.
They started their quest for a third straight Champions League crown in style with an emphatic 6-1 hammering of Slovan Bratislava last month.

Ousmane Dembélé became the third PSG player to score 2+ goals and provide 2+ assists in a Champions League game, after Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi; only Liverpool have also had three different players achieve this in the competition (Roberto Firmino, Mohamed Salah and Yossi Benayoun).

Dembélé has been directly involved in 31 goals in 41 Champions League games for PSG (20 goals, 11 assists), now the fifth most for the club in the competition, trailing only Mbappé (65 in 64 apps), Neymar (37 in 41 apps), Edinson Cavani (33 in 54 apps) and Ángel Di María (32 in 54 apps).

Former City forward Ferran Torres, meanwhile, became the first player to score a hat-trick on their Champions League debut for a side since Robert Lewandowski for Barcelona against Viktoria Plzen in September 2022.
PSG made the most high turnovers (14) and shot-ending high turnovers (7) of any side on MD1 of the new Champions League campaign, as well as averaging the most possession (72.1%).
But PSG's free-flowing attack will be tasked with breaking down a City defence that has already kept five clean sheets this term.
Not that City are lacking in the attacking department.

Rayan Cherki has averaged 4.1 defensive line-breaking passes per 90 for City in the Champions League. Since the start of last season, this is the second-highest average of any player in the competition (min. 300 minutes played), only behind Lee Kang-In (4.5).
And if he scores in this match, Erling Haaland will overtake Sergio Agüero (36 goals in 64 apps) to become City’s top scorer in the Champions League (Haaland currently on 36 goals in 40 apps).
Haaland has also scored 42 goals in 39 appearances in the group stage/league phase of the Champions League, the most of any player since his first season in the competition in 2019-20.
But the key to this contest could end up being who comes out on top in what promises to be an enthralling midfield tussle.
PSG's Vitinha has arguably been the top-performing midfielder in Europe over the past two seasons.
In fact, since the start of last season, Vitinha leads all midfielders in the Champions League for completed passes (1,703), line-breaking passes (327) and possession won (106 times).

But going up against PSG's mighty midfield will be City duo Enzo Fernández and Elliot Anderson. The latter, in particular, has had a fantastic start in a City shirt, as he looks to help fill the void left by Rodri's departure to Barcelona.

          Atlético Madrid 2-0 Man Utd Stats: Pressure Mounts on Michael Carrick After Latest Defeat
        
      
                          
                      Oct 13, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Atlético Madrid are up and running in the Champions League after Pablo Barrios and Ademola Lookman scored the goals to see them past Manchester United.
Atlético Madrid earned their first win in the Champions League this season as they brushed aside 10-man Manchester United.
The Metropolitano had something to cheer about in the first minute as Pablo Barrios broke the deadlock within 47 seconds, while Johnny Cardoso had a second goal disallowed before the break.
Though United tried to push for an equaliser, Leny Yoro’s sending-off made it an uphill battle, and Ademola Lookman duly punished Michael Carrick’s struggling side.

Atlético made a dream start as they cut open United’s defence with minimum fuss and Álex Baena squared it to Barrios. His low shot sneaked in after a deflection off Ayden Heaven, with Senne Lammens unable to scramble back and keep it out.
Bryan Mbeumo had United’s two best chances of the first half. He had a low drive blocked, while Jan Oblak covered his near post well to smother a tight-angled effort.
Atlético soon turned up the pressure again, though, as Alejandro Grimaldo curled a free-kick from 20 yards out against the corner of the goal frame.

And on the stroke of half-time, Cardoso thought he had doubled the hosts’ lead by sweeping in Barrios’ lay-off, but the goal was ruled out following a VAR review as Marcos Llorente handled the ball as he bundled past Heaven in the build-up.

The woodwork denied Atlético again in the 54th minute as Julián Alvarez volleyed past a helpless Lammens against the post, while at the other end Bruno Fernandes fired wide and curled a looping effort off the top of the crossbar.

But United were given a mountain to climb in the 74th minute. Jonathan David was originally penalised for handling the ball as he broke through on goal, but Yoro was sent off following a VAR review for denying the Canadian a goalscoring opportunity moments before.
And it took Atlético just five minutes to use their numerical advantage. Grimaldo surged forward and picked out David, who was denied by Lammens, but Lookman reacted quickest to turn in the rebound.
United almost got a late consolation through Matheus Cunha after a poor clearance, but after Joshua Zirkzee teed him up, Oblak denied the former Atlético man with an outstretched leg.
A disappointing draw with 10-man Tottenham at the weekend piled extra pressure on Carrick, who knew how important a morale-boosting victory would have been here.

But Atléti ensured the Red Devils made the worst possible start; United conceded in the opening minute of a Champions League game for the fourth time, while it was the hosts’ second-earliest goal in the competition after Conor Gallagher against Real Madrid in March 2025 (27 seconds).
When Lookman came on, it took him just eight minutes to find an opening. In his six Champions League appearances as a substitute, he has been involved in four goals (three goals, one assist).
United are a favourite opponent for Atlético, however, as they have never lost to the Red Devils, with this being their fifth meeting (W3 D2).

It was a fairly even game, at least until Yoro became the third-youngest United player to be sent off in a Champions League game. Atléti had 11 shots worth 1.42 expected goals (xG), with five of those on target, while United racked up nine attempts worth 0.98 xG and tested Oblak four times.
Carrick’s men could not find a breakthrough, though, meaning Atlético kept a precious clean sheet – just their second in their last 16 home Champions League games.
Our Opta match centre delivers you all the Atlético Madrid vs Man Utd stats from their Champions League meeting at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium on Tuesday 13 October.
The match centre below includes team and player stats, expected goals data, passing networks, an Opta chalkboard and more. It gives you everything you need to do your own match analysis.
