          Newcastle vs Aston Villa Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 16, 2026
          
                      Chirag Sharatkumar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After a scintillating Champions League win in midweek, Unai Emery’s side will look to carry their momentum into domestic action. We look ahead to Saturday's Premier League clash with our Newcastle United vs Aston Villa prediction and preview.

After picking up hugely contrasting results in their last respective outings, Newcastle and Aston Villa meet in the Premier League on Saturday, with both sides looking to improve their domestic performances after inconsistent starts.

Matthias Jaissle’s side fell to a 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Frank Lampard’s Coventry City on Monday, with Sidiki Cherif, Ellis Simms, and Stephen Mfuni striking in the second half to seal victory after Jack Rudoni’s sixth-minute penalty.
Sven Botman netted a second-half consolation, but that will have meant precious little to Jaissle, whose biggest challenge at present is surely plugging his side’s leaky defence.

The Magpies have conceded 13 Premier League goals this season – their third-highest total after six matches, behind only 1999-00 (18) and 2021-22 (14). They went on to finish 11th in both of those campaigns.

Beyond the goals, though, Jaissle will be further concerned by how many shots his team have allowed. Newcastle have faced 34 shots on target this season, with only Chelsea (36) facing more in the competition.

It has been an especially concerning issue at home, with the Magpies now going 12 Premier League matches without a clean sheet at St. James’ Park. They last endured a longer run between December 1998 and August 1999 under Ruud Gullit (13 games).

Perhaps most worrying for Jaissle is that only Tottenham (13) have lost more Premier League games in 2026 than Newcastle’s 12, while the Magpies have conceded the joint-most goals in the competition this year (44, level with Chelsea).
Aston Villa, meanwhile, will be riding the high of yet another spectacular European performance.
Unai Emery’s side thrashed Fenerbahce 6-0 in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both netting braces alongside goals from Johan Manzambi and Tammy Abraham.
While that victory has lifted them towards the upper reaches of the Champions League standings, the Villans’ domestic form tells a different story.
They sit 16th in the table with just six points and have won just one of their six matches so far, squandering a late lead against Brentford last time out to eventually settle for a 2-2 draw.
Like Newcastle, Villa have faced similar, though perhaps not quite as extreme, defensive struggles this season.
They have shipped 11 goals across six Premier League matches so far – their most at this stage of a season since 1986-87 (16), when they eventually finished bottom of the table.
The Villans have also faced an uncharacteristic 15.8 shots per game this season – their most since the 2019-20 season, when they allowed an average of 16 per game.
Still, faith in Emery to guide Villa up the table will remain high, especially with the Spaniard on the cusp of recording his 100th Premier League victory.
He has won 99 of his 196 matches in the competition (D44 L53), and victory over Newcastle would make him the joint-ninth-fastest manager to reach 100 Premier League wins.
Villa will, however, have to be wary of Harvey Barnes, who has become a constant thorn in their side in recent times.

The Newcastle winger has contributed to 10 goals in 13 Premier League matches against Villa (six goals, four assists) – his joint-most against a single opponent along with West Ham. He has only found the net more against Leeds United (seven goals).
Villa, meanwhile, will hope Jackson can build on his recent good form.

Manchester United reporterPublished2 hours agoManchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes is "fully committed" to the club and will continue as captain.
Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after the Portuguese questioned the tactics used in a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.
The defeat by Bournemouth left Carrick's future hanging by a thread, but the 45-year-old will be in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea.
It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will return to the starting line-up, but the pair held clear-the-air talks at United's Carrington training ground on Tuesday in a bid to move forward.
Carrick says there is "no decision to be made" over whether Fernandes remains captain.
"We are clear with the situation of the team, and as a football club," said Carrick.
"He [Fernandes] is an important player for this group. He has been and he will be.
"We've got to make a difference and we've got to push things in a good direction.
"He's fully committed to this football club; he's fully committed to making things better. There are absolutely no issues with that.
"It doesn't change for me. It was a decision for what we felt for the [Bournemouth] game. That's it.
"He's the one that's led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he'll continue to do that. There are absolutely no issues with that."

Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks
Published1 day agoCarrick 'doesn't need assurances' over futureUnited have gone eight games without a win as they head to Chelsea - their worst run of results since 2015-16.
Not since the 1988-89 campaign have they had a sequence of nine matches without a win.

Nearly 40 hours passed between United losing against Bournemouth on Sunday and the club providing clarification on Carrick's future, with the Englishman being given a chance to turn things around at Old Trafford.
Talks involving the Glazer family, minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox took place before Carrick's immediate future was confirmed.

It seems likely he will remain in post for next Tuesday's Champions League match against Roma, and the Premier League encounter with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on 8 November, after which there is a two-week international break.
Carrick, though, says he does not need guarantees over his position.

          Premier League Fixture Difficulty vs Results: Which Teams Have Defied Expectations?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look back at pre-season expectations for Premier League clubs' first five matches and assess how well they've done relative to the supposed difficulty of their fixture schedules.
Five matchdays is all it takes to dramatically alter perspectives and expectations in the Premier League.

Think back to pre-season, that fantastical time of renewal, hope and excitement. Intrusive thoughts about the campaign ahead barely register for most. Instead, brain power is dedicated to thinking about what could be achieved.
Reality can come at you quickly, however.
The 2026-27 Premier League season may only be in relative infancy, but pre-season already feels like a long time ago now, especially for certain clubs.

A good or bad start isn’t always indicative of what’s to come, though. There can be a whole host of reasons for either, and most won’t be permanent. For instance, fixture difficulty is something you cannot ignore – not every start to the season is equal.
On the eve of 2026-27, we used the Opta Power Rankings to determine which clubs had the easiest and toughest opening schedules.
Now, we can look back on those findings to see how they correlate with the real Premier League table after five matchdays.
Generally, there is a loose correlation between fixture difficulty and the points teams earned across the first five matchdays of the season.
For example, the 10 teams deemed to have the easier schedules averaged 8.2 points, whereas the 10 with the toughest have averaged 5.2. But it’s the extremes that are most interesting to look at.

Manchester City lead the fledgling table, of course, having won their first five games. Considering they came into the season with a fair amount of uncertainty surrounding them due to player churn and Pep Guardiola’s exit, their start to the campaign – on the field at least – couldn’t have gone much better.

But it must be pointed out that, according to the pre-season Opta Power Rankings, they had the second-easiest start with an average opponent rating of 91.4. Their opening slate wasn’t without challenges; beating Manchester United away from home despite having 10 men for over an hour was impressive, though most would’ve expected them to take close to maximum points from Bournemouth (H), Crystal Palace (A), Coventry (H) and Sunderland (H).

Liverpool were deemed to have the easiest schedule (91.2). Nine points from those five games probably left most fans slightly underwhelmed, though we must remember the Power Rankings can’t exactly account for elements like adapting to a managerial change with Andoni Iraola now in the hot seat.
In terms of most disappointing start to the season, Man Utd are certainly up there. The Opta Power Rankings suggested they had the third-easiest schedule, but they’ve amassed just five points.

A Matchday 1 defeat to promoted Hull City was alarming. They did at least follow that up with a 5-2 defeat of Ipswich Town at Old Trafford, but that remains their only victory. Sitting 12th after statistically the third-easiest start is understandably concerning.
Brighton are another of the outliers, but for completely different reasons to Man Utd.

With an opening slate of Aston Villa (H), Chelsea (A), Leeds (H), Coventry (A) and Arsenal (H), any nervousness from supporters would’ve been logical. The Opta Power Rankings assessed that as the fourth-hardest start.
But they took 10 points from those games, including an immensely impressive 3-0 dismantling of the champions in their last game before the international break that left them third in the table.

One caveat is that they have spent more time (87 minutes) this season playing against 10 men than any other club, though in fairness to them, they were at least 2-0 up when Villa and Coventry had a man sent off.
If Brighton have been the story of the season so far, then Hull have at least given them a run for their money.

5b25pj5kbwf01pxecuvudq5hy.title: Lampard concedes two 'outstanding' Tottenham goals beat Coventry
5b25pj5kbwf01pxecuvudq5hy.subtitle: Coventry City were beaten 3-1 by Tottenham on Monday, with James Maddison and Omar Marmoush both scoring stunners past Carl Rushworth.
paragraphs: Frank Lampard believes two "outstanding" moments of individual quality from James Maddison and Omar Marmoush were the difference in Coventry City's defeat to Tottenham.
Coventry saw their two-game winning run in the Premier League come to an end on Monday, with Roberto De Zerbi's side earning a 3-1 win at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Maddison opened the scoring with a stunning, sweeping finish into the top-left corner in the 14th minute, but the Sky Blues hit back through Jack Rudoni early in the second half.
But the hosts reclaimed their lead just before the hour when Marmoush fired in his first Spurs goal from just outside the box, though Carl Rushworth got a touch on the shot.
Coventry pushed for a leveller that never came, with substitute Ben Davies sealing the win in the 96th minute to move Spurs one place above their opponents in the standings.

The Sky Blues have begun a league campaign with as many as five defeats from their first seven games for the first time since 1996-97 (W1 D1 L5 in the Premier League – however they did manage to avoid relegation that season).

Lampard, however, took the positives from his team's display, adding that two bits of magic proved decisive as Spurs became the first side to score three goals from outside the box in a single Premier League game since Fulham against Leicester City in May 2023.
"Very pleased with the performance. We were in the game to say the least," Lampard told BBC Sport. "Two outstanding goals for them.
"The second was questionable because the arm was up in the face but a quality finish. I am proud of the performance. 3-1 feels nasty at the end because of the last goal.
"We created some good moments. We wanted to start well, as they started well in every game they have played here but haven't got what they deserved.

"The feeling and flow of the game we were brave and getting people up on their top line. Individuals were showing their quality with Rudoni and Thomas-Asante – eight of the boys played in the Championship last year, and now they have shown they have grown.
"I don't like the fixture list games, they are all hard. Are we happy? We will always want more, we feel there are a couple more points we feel we could have had."
Coventry had their chances against Spurs, but were only able to muster an expected goals (xG) total of 0.82 from their 12 shots, though only one of those tested Antonin Kinsky.
The Sky Blues have also now failed to win any of their last 48 Premier League games when conceding first (D6 L42) since a 2-1 win against Charlton Athletic in March 1999.

Rudoni's display was another positive for Lampard, with the midfielder becoming the first player to score in back-to-back Premier League appearances for Coventry since John Hartson netted in four consecutive games between March and April 2001.
"Yeah, it's frustrating, we felt we did well as a team. We took the game plan to them well. At the end it really could've been 2-2," Rudoni conceded.
"We've got to take the positives. We have a big game on Saturday so we'll just look at the positives and get ready for that."
Coventry face a crucial run of league games against the side around them, with two home matches against Fulham and Sunderland coming between now and the end of October.

They also face Everton, Crystal Palace and Leeds United next month, and when asked about Coventry's upcoming run of fixtures, Rudoni added: "I think we've shown we can compete and, like you say, it's the little differences like shots on target.
"We've shown we can compete. We just need to get points on the board. We need to really get points on the board."

5e5um3oqqh6115ghuf7u69dax.title: Richter relishing challenge of facing Lewandowski as Philadelphia defend unbeaten run
5e5um3oqqh6115ghuf7u69dax.subtitle: The Philadelphia Union visit the Chicago Fire in MLS on Wednesday, with both teams on course to make the playoffs.
paragraphs: Philadelphia Union boss Ryan Richter is excited to see his players test themselves against an "all-time" great in Robert Lewandowski, as they put their club-record unbeaten run on the line against the Chicago Fire.
The Union have enjoyed a meteoric rise up the Eastern Conference ahead of their midweek trip to Soldier Field, having gone unbeaten in 13 games since the World Cup break.
They have registered 11 wins in that time, the latest of which came by a 2-1 scoreline against Real Salt Lake on Saturday, with Bruno Damiani and Milan Iloski scoring.

The Union are sixth in the East with six regular-season games to play, three places and six points below Chicago, who themselves are just a point behind second-placed Inter Miami after beating New York City 2-1 last time out.

When asked if his side had enjoyed something of a kind of run in recent months, ahead of a big test against a direct rival, Richter said: "If we don't take points from those teams, then they'd be higher in the table.

"So that's also part of the reason why we're positioned where we are, and some of the teams we've played against, the reason we've been able to jump them is because we've had these head-to-head matchups.
"It's not like we've been playing against bad teams. Chicago is going to be a real test and it's one we have to be up for."
Chicago boss Gregg Berhalter can call upon former Bayern Munich and Barcelona striker Lewandowski, and Richter is relishing the task of going up against him.
"Yeah, it's another chance for us to play against a world-class player. And that's a pretty good opportunity for our centre-backs in particular," he said.
"But for our team as a whole, it's a guy that has the quality and the level where he can win a game with one touch at any time.
"So for us, we have to make sure that we're always aware of where were at. Don't give him space to operate.
"He's one of the best strikers of all-time and we have to make sure we do a really good job with him."
Chicago Fire – Robert Lewandowski
Lewandowski has scored five goals in 13 appearances in MLS, with his time on the pitch only adding up to 300 minutes.
He has overperformed his expected goals (xG) figures of 3.79, while hitting the target with 10 of his 27 shots thus far, posting a conversion rate of 18.52%.
Philadelphia Union – Cavan Sullivan
Having made history as the United States' youngest-ever goalscorer during the international break, Sullivan laid on an assist during Philadelphia's victory over Real Salt Lake.

With that strike, Sullivan equalled the single-season record for MLS goal contributions by a teenager (20), surpassing Alphonso Davies (19 for the Vancouver Whitecaps in 2018) and going level with Diego Fagundez (20 for the New England Revolution in 2013).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
The Philadelphia Union's 35 points won since the World Cup break are the most any team has collected in a span of 13 matches within a single MLS season in the post-shootout era (since 2000).
But they face a difficult task on Wednesday, against a Chicago side that have won nine of their 14 home games in MLS this year (D1 L4).
The Fire have also won three of their last six matches in MLS play (D1 L2), while they also won the last meeting between the sides, triumphing 2-1 at Subaru Park in March.
Given the Union's recent form, they will back themselves to leave Soldier Field with at least a point, in a game that could be a dress rehearsal for the playoffs.
Philadelphia Union – 30.1%

5eqmxcyuorrv1qkbm3416epvm.title: Hull City 2-2 Everton: Belloumi equaliser caps entertaining draw
5eqmxcyuorrv1qkbm3416epvm.subtitle: Hull City and Everton could not be separated at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Mohamed Belloumi making an impact off the bench.
paragraphs: Hull City preserved their unbeaten start at the MKM Stadium in the Premier League this season as Mohamed Belloumi came off the bench to earn a 2-2 draw against Everton.
Joe Gelhardt, who replaced Belloumi in Sergej Jakirovic's starting line-up on Sunday, opened the scoring early in the second half with his first top-flight goal in over four years.
But Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall led Everton's comeback, scoring a 55th-minute equaliser before he teed up Thierno Barry to put the Toffees in front.
However, Hull hit back when substitutes Elliot Stroud and Belloumi combined, with the latter's left-footed strike proving too much for Jordan Pickford.
Everton started brightly, with Konstantinos Tzolakis tipping James Garner's early free-kick before Jack Grealish sent a tame effort into the arms of the Hull goalkeeper.

The visitors thought they had taken the lead in the 34th minute when Tzolakis' dropped Jarrad Branthwaite's cross. Harrison Armstrong's shot was cleared off the line, with Brennan Johnson blocking Ryan Giles' attempted clearance into the net, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against the Welshman.

Hull and Everton both had chances at the end of the first half, but just three minutes after the restart, the Tigers took the lead when Ainsley Maitland-Niles presented the ball to Sorba Thomas, who slipped in Gelhardt to dink home the opener.

Maitland-Niles quickly atoned for his error when his cross was headed in by Dewsbury-Hall, with Everton then going ahead through Barry, who curled past Tzolakis having missed an open goal minutes earlier.

But Hull clawed themselves level in the 74th minute when Stroud skipped past Maitland-Niles and Garner before pulling the ball back for Belloumi, who took a touch before generating enough power to beat Pickford.
Big chances missed by both sides

Both Hull and Everton had made strong starts to their respective Premier League campaigns, and while a point is not a bad result for either side, both will feel they perhaps could have come away with a victory.

Everton's 10 shots during the first half were their most in an away match in the Premier League this season, but they once again failed to score in the first half of four consecutive top-flight games on the road for the first time since December 2024 under Sean Dyche.

And though they fell behind, David Moyes will be pleased by the response from one of his key players. Despite missing several chances, Barry netted in back-to-back Premier League games for the third time, and first since January last season.

But Everton were undone by Belloumi, who has now scored (three) or assisted (two) five of Hull's eight Premier League goals this season (63%), and his inclusion from the start could have been crucial to the Tigers' chances of victory.

Everton, though, will feel they should have been more clinical in the final third. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.71 from their 15 attempts, compared to Hull's tally of 1.33 from their nine shots.

Moyes' side have, however, now avoided defeat in their opening six games of a Premier League season for the third time, after 2006-07 (first seven) and 2013-14 (six), while Hull remain unbeaten in their first three home games of a top-flight season for only the second time, after previously doing so in 2013-14.

Big chances missed by both sides

Both Hull and Everton had made strong starts to their respective Premier League campaigns, and while a point is not a bad result for either side, both will feel they perhaps could have come away with a victory. 

Everton's 10 shots during the first half were their most in an away match in the Premier League this season, but they once again failed to score in the first half of four consecutive top-flight games on the road for the first time since December 2024 under Sean Dyche. 

And though they fell behind, David Moyes will be pleased by the response from one of his key players. Despite missing several chances, Barry netted in back-to-back Premier League games for the third time, and first since January last season.

But Everton were undone by Belloumi, who has now scored (three) or assisted (two) five of Hull's eight Premier League goals this season (63%), and his inclusion from the start could have been crucial to the Tigers' chances of victory. 

Everton, though, will feel they should have been more clinical in the final third. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.71 from their 15 attempts, compared to Hull's tally of 1.33 from their nine shots.

Moyes' side have, however, now avoided defeat in their opening six games of a Premier League season for the third time, after 2006-07 (first seven) and 2013-14 (six), while Hull remain unbeaten in their first three home games of a top-flight season for only the second time, after previously doing so in 2013-14.

5f3te9ge6hyk1dia3ufms1lxc.title: Pocognoli using experience of Belgium's 'golden generation' to handle Scotland pressure
5f3te9ge6hyk1dia3ufms1lxc.subtitle: Scotland start the Sebastien Pocognoli era on Saturday, and he wants pressure to become something that motivates, not hinders, his team.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli feels his experiences in the early days of Belgium's "golden generation" can help him manage expectations with Scotland, as he prepares for his first game in charge.

Scotland open their Nations League campaign in Slovenia on Saturday, with Switzerland and North Macedonia their other opponents in Group B1, having been relegated from the competition's top tier under Steve Clarke in 2024-25.

Clarke did lead Scotland to a second successive major tournament – and a record third under his watch – at the World Cup, but they suffered a meek group-stage exit following defeats against Morocco and Brazil.
Pocognoli is returning to international management, having coached Belgium's under-18 side before having stints in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco in the club game.
And he feels he has learned plenty about managing the pressure that comes with the international game, having been part of Belgium's much-feted "golden generation".

Pocognoli played alongside Vincent Kompany, Thomas Vermaelen, Jan Vertonghen and Mousa Dembele at the 2008 Olympic Games – a tournament where Belgium lost the bronze-medal match – before winning 13 senior caps between 2008 and 2014.

He never appeared at a major tournament for his country, with his final cap coming in 2014 World Cup qualifying, but he saw how the pressure to deliver silverware weighed on a squad that also featured Eden Hazard, Kevin De Bruyne and Romelu Lukaku.
"In my own case, I was part of the 'golden generation' at the start," he said. "I made the first step. We made the Olympic Games, and I was part of the [2014] qualification.

"But for me, there were high expectations on the Belgian players – an over-expectation. It was too much. It is a country of 12 million people, and you have to deal with France and Germany next to you, and England.
"There were fantastic players and that Belgium team reached third place in the [2018] World Cup. Fantastic. They were first in the FIFA rankings for five or six years. You can't do more than that.
"Maybe with some luck you can win a medal, but there was over-expectation and I think that generation reached its best, to be honest."
Though the expectations surrounding Scotland are not as sky-high as those that Belgium failed to meet, Pocognoli wants to make pressure a motivating factor for his team.
"Yes, the bar is very high," Pocognoli said. "I know this. But you have to deal with this heritage. The heritage is massively positive, so use it.
"If I put this as a pressure, we are not going to go the right way. I have to use it as a benefit to embrace."
Scotland – who are building towards a home European Championship campaign in 2028 – will welcome Switzerland to Hampden Park next Tuesday, for their first home game under Pocognoli.

5fofrtnkt92g1w9ts2vwwyfvh.title: Flick confirms Raphinha's return for Barcelona
5fofrtnkt92g1w9ts2vwwyfvh.subtitle: After a brief spell on the sidelines, Raphinha is set to return for Barcelona in their LaLiga clash against Real Betis this weekend.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick confirmed Raphinha is available for selection when Barcelona take on Real Betis in LaLiga on Saturday.
Raphinha missed Barca's 3-0 league win over Getafe and 4-1 Champions League victory over Galatasaray after picking up an injury during the international break.

The 29-year-old scored 12 goals in Barca's first seven LaLiga games this season; only one player has scored more goals after his club's first seven games of a campaign in the competition in the 21st century: Cristiano Ronaldo for Real Madrid in 2014-15 (13).

Raphinha's imperious form was highlighted by his perfect hat-trick against Sevilla before the extended international break, during which he both scored and assisted for Brazil across two games against Australia.
While Raphinha is ready to make his return, Flick insisted the club will be cautious with the forward.
"If you ask him, he'll tell you he's ready to start, but I have to take it step by step," Flick said about Raphinha.
"He trained well with the group, but we have to manage him. The good news is that he'll be available, and so will [Frenkie] De Jong."
Lamine Yamal took more responsibility during Raphinha's absence, assisting three of Barca's seven goals across their last two games.
Flick explained he will have to manage Yamal's minutes, with the teenager starting in each of their 10 games this season and featuring four times for Spain during the break.
"It's not an easy question to answer. We have to manage his playing time," Flick added on Yamal.
"But the most important thing is that he enjoys playing football, and that's what he's doing."
Upcoming opponents Betis are third in LaLiga after eight games, level on points with second-place Atletico Madrid (19).
Manuel Pellegrini's side also enjoyed some success in Europe during the week, defeating Porto 3-2 in the Europa League.

Isco has scored three goals in his four LaLiga games for Betis against Barcelona; he has not scored more goals for the Verdiblancos against any other opponent in the competition (also three against Getafe and Osasuna).
Barcelona – Lamine Yamal

Yamal has been involved in 12 goals in eight LaLiga games in the 2026-27 season (seven goals and five assists), the most by a Spanish player after his team's first eight matches of a campaign in the competition in the 21st century.
MATCH PREDICTION: BARCELONA WIN

Barca have won their first eight LaLiga games of a season for the second time in their history, after previously doing so in 2013-14 under Gerardo Martino. Only one team has managed to win their first nine in the competition's history: Real Madrid in 1968-69.
Betis have not won any of their last 15 home games against Barca in LaLiga (D4 L11), their worst winless run at home against a single opponent in their entire top-flight history.

Barca have also scored in each of their last 20 away games against Betis in LaLiga (52 goals in total), their best scoring run away from home against an opponent in their entire history in the competition.

However, Betis have earned 19 points from their first eight LaLiga games in 2026-27 (W6 D1 L1), equalling their best record at this stage of a campaign in the competition (assuming three points for a win), achieved in 1934-35 (W6 D1 L1), when they were champions.
And this could be a high-scoring contest; Barca (six) and Betis (four) are two of the three teams that have reached 20+ shots in the most different LaLiga games this season, alongside Madrid (five).

5i98nbtmoh971f65jytkt8dn5.title: Perelman 'hurt' by Orlando's failure to close out NYCFC clash
5i98nbtmoh971f65jytkt8dn5.subtitle: Orlando City conceded late on in their 2-2 draw with New York City FC, leaving them in a perilous position in the playoff race.
paragraphs: Orlando City interim head coach Martin Perelman was left "hurt" by his team's inability to close out their game against New York City FC.
Orlando seemed set to seal a 2-1 comeback win on Saturday, and those three points would have seen them consolidate seventh place in the Eastern Conference.
Yet NYCFC substitute Jonathan Shore popped up with an equaliser in the ninth minute of second-half stoppage time.
The draw left Orlando In seventh, but on the same points as eighth-place FC Cincinnati and only four points better off than the Columbus Crew, who occupy 10th spot.
Now, Orlando head north to take on the Chicago Fire, and Perelman lamented last weekend's result and display.
"The game was tough. Again, it wasn't our best night, and that's it," he said.
"Unfortunately, they tied on the last play. That hurts a lot.
"But it's time to digest it. We are used to being at home. We came from, I think, [nine wins] and two [draws] since we've been here, so now it's 9-3. We like to win at home.
"Sometimes these things happen. The opponent plays. They had good players, and that's it."
Chicago snapped a two-game losing streak by beating Atlanta United 3-2 last time out.
Chicago Fire – Philip Zinckernagel
Zinckernagel recorded his 16th goal contribution of the season (seven goals, nine assists) against Atlanta.

After recording 30 goal contributions last season, Zinckernagel is the third player in club history with 16+ goal contributions in consecutive campaigns (Ante Razov 1997 to 2002, Nemanja Nikolic 2017 and 2018).
Orlando City – Antonie Griezmann
Griezmann scored against NYCFC, marking his 11th straight game with a goal contribution.

This is the third streak of 11 or more consecutive matches with a goal contribution in MLS this season (also Hugo Cuypers and Lionel Messi) after there were just two such streaks in the league's first 30 seasons (by Josef Martinez and Sebastian Giovinco).
MATCH PREDICTION – CHICAGO FIRE WIN
The Chicago Fire have won three straight matches against Orlando, including a 3–1 home triumph in the wild-card round of last year's playoffs.
The Fire had gone winless in eight straight against Orlando (D2 L6) prior to winning those last three meetings.
In addition, Chicago's win over Atlanta took them 51 points for the season, after totalling 53 points in 2025.
This is the second time in club history that the Fire have recorded 50 points in consecutive MLS seasons, also doing so in 2000 and 2001.
Orlando have only won three of their last 19 regular-season away matches (D5 L11) dating back to August 2025, conceding 61 goals in those games at an average of 3.2 per match.

5qex50wszn2b18escme5w3fh7.title: 'We want to climb the table' – Luis Enrique and PSG eyeing third straight Ligue 1 win
5qex50wszn2b18escme5w3fh7.subtitle: After failing to win their first three league games, Paris Saint-Germain are aiming to continue their winning run against Le Mans.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique's sole focus is for Paris Saint-Germain to continue climbing the Ligue 1 table as they continue to recover from a slow start to the season against Le Mans.
The reigning Ligue 1 champions failed to win any of their first three league games this season, drawing their opening two before suffering a 2-1 loss to Monaco.
However, since then, they have earned back-to-back wins over Brest and Marseille to move up to sixth in the table, though they remain five points off early pace-setters Monaco.
PSG have not been short of a goal threat in their opening five games, having had the most shots (106) and the most touches in the opposition box (175) in Ligue 1 this season.
But Luis Enrique is keen to ensure they keep up the performances in order to get more wins on the board.
"I remember well the game we played against them in the Coupe de France [a 2-0 win in February 2025]," Luis Enrique said.
"They're a real team who plays good football. But we're at the Parc des Princes, with our fans, and we want to climb the table.
"That's why we're going to go for the three points.

"As a coach, you always try to show that we're a team. I'm the first to be critical of my players, but in analysing the start of the season, we would have deserved to have more points than we currently do.
"It's important to pick up points to build confidence. We started the season in a different way, and it's an exciting challenge for us."
Le Mans have impressed since their promotion from Ligue 2, losing just one of their five matches so far (W1 D3).
They beat Lorient 2-1 before the international break to get their first win on the board, and sitting 10th on six points, they would leapfrog PSG if they were to earn a win.
Paris Saint-Germain – Vitinha

Two of the three players with the most shots from outside the box in Ligue 1 this season play for Paris Saint-Germain: Vitinha (10) and Ousmane Dembele (eight), though the Portuguese midfielder has scored just one goal this term.
Le Mans – Adil Bourabaa
Adil Bourabaa is the only player to have scored more than one goal in the opening 15 minutes of Ligue 1 matches this season (two).
MATCH PREDICTION: PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN WIN
PSG have won 10 of their 15 matches against Le Mans in all competitions (D3 L2), but they have not faced the Sarthe club in Ligue 1 since May 2010, when they suffered a 1-0 away defeat.

Luis Enrique's side have won their last two Ligue 1 matches (1-0 v Brest, 2-1 v Marseille) but have not managed a longer winning run since a sequence of seven consecutive victories between December 2025 and February 2026.
However, PSG have lost three of their last seven home games in the French top-flight (W3 D1), as many as they had in their previous 45 (W33 D9).
As for Le Mans, they have lost just two league matches in 2026 (W9 D11); no team currently in Ligue 1 or Ligue 2 has suffered fewer defeats among those present throughout the period.
And Le Mans have lost just one of their last eight away Ligue 1 matches (W3 D4), a 2-3 defeat at Rennes on August 30.
Paris Saint-Germain – 80.8%

5r3uw0xb0bzq1l0vn49kubyiq.title: Women's Super League predictions: Man Utd to beat Liverpool, Man City backed against Arsenal
5r3uw0xb0bzq1l0vn49kubyiq.subtitle: Manchester City take on Arsenal in the headline tussle of matchday five in the Women's Super League.
paragraphs: The Women's Super League table is starting to take shape after the first four matches of the 2026-27 campaign.
Reigning champions Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record still intact, after four straight wins to open the campaign.
Behind them, Chelsea and Tottenham are the only other teams yet to taste defeat, while London City Lionesses are also in touching distance of the top.
Arsenal have made a stuttering start, which was compounded by a 1-0 loss to Chelsea last time out, and things do not get any easier as they travel to City this weekend.
Things were more positive for Manchester United, who held out for their first league win under Eva Olid last time out, moving up the table and leaving four clubs without a victory.
So, who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend?
MANCHESTER UNITED V LIVERPOOL
The action begins on Saturday, with Manchester United and Liverpool both looking to build on morale-boosting wins, against West Ham and Everton, respectively.

Gareth Taylor (81) is aiming to tie former United boss Marc Skinner (82) for the second-most managerial wins in WSL history – only Emma Hayes (151) has recorded more – and our predictive model gives that a 17% chance of happening.
As it stands, United are heavy favourites to take all three points at 63.6%, given they have won four of their five WSL home matches against the Reds (L1).
United have conceded in each of their last 11 home league games, though, which might give Liverpool hope of earning consecutive WSL wins for the first time since March 2025 under Amber Whiteley.
Despite a 19.4% chance of a draw, there has never been a stalemate between these teams in the competition in nine previous meetings (six United wins, three Liverpool victories).
ASTON VILLA V CRYSTAL PALACE
It has been a tough start to the season for Aston Villa, who have gone winless in their four games (D2 L2), leading to Natalia Arroyo’s dismissal on Tuesday.
Brian Sorensen is in interim charge and will be in the dugout when Villa host Crystal Palace.
The hosts are the favourites to take the points, however, with a 45.2% win likelihood to Palace’s 27.9%.

Villa could go winless across their opening five matches of a WSL campaign for the third time (after 2023-24 and 2024-25), but they have won three of their last five league meetings with Palace (D1 L1).
Palace, meanwhile, have lost just one of their opening four league matches this term (W1 D2) – the fewest defeats of any promoted side at this stage of a single WSL campaign.
BRIGHTON V CHARLTON ATHLETIC
Two teams still searching for their first win go head-to-head at the Amex, with Brighton and Charlton Athletic desperate for their maiden victory of 2026-27.

Charlton are the only team still without a point – they could become the third team to lose their first five matches in the competition, after Yeovil Town (first seven in 2017) and Leicester City (first nine in 2021-22).
But Brighton are also winless in their last seven WSL games (D4 L3). Only once before have they endured a longer streak: nine between November 2022 and April 2023.
The Seagulls are tipped to come out on top, winning 58.6% of Opta's pre-match simulations, while Charlton only triumph in 19.8%.
EVERTON V BIRMINGHAM CITY
Birmingham City (23.7%) are another team still searching for a first victory, while Everton (51.8%) are looking to bounce back from their Merseyside derby defeat.
Everton are unbeaten in each of their last five WSL games against Birmingham (W3 D2), while they won the most recent meeting 2-0 in the League Cup last month.
Birmingham went unbeaten in their first seven away games against Everton in the WSL (W3 D4), but they did lose 3-1 in the most recent of those, in September 2021.

5rub7z2ah5zy1di2j84n7m2bn.title: Alonso not rushing James' recovery after latest injury setback
5rub7z2ah5zy1di2j84n7m2bn.subtitle: Reece James could be out until the new year after having knee surgery, but Xabi Alonso is not setting a timeline for his captain's return.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso has no intention of rushing Reece James back following knee surgery, though he does not expect to need to sign a replacement in January.
James’ career has been plagued by injury since he first broke into Chelsea's first team, and he could be set for up to three months on the sidelines.
The right-back suffered a knee injury in training, which has seen him miss the Blues' last two matches – a 3-0 defeat to Brentford and a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth.
Alonso refused to set a timeline for James' return or confirm reports on his expected recovery time but offered his support to the 26-year-old.

"We are all disappointed, especially for him [James]. He wanted to have a good start after the international break, but he picked up an injury," Alonso said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Everton.
"The surgery has been successful. We are supporting him.
"I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks.
"It's not going to be short. Whether it's before or after Christmas, then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.
"We have a big squad to deal with injuries. We have four more games until the next [international] break, so I think we can manage well with the players that we have."
Alonso is yet to settle on a regular formation with Chelsea and had deployed James in midfield while switching between a back four and back three.
Against Bournemouth last time out, Pedro Neto played as the right wing-back, with Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson making up the midfield duo.
Chelsea's defence has proven shaky so far this term, with no side conceding more than their 13 goals.
In fact, the Blues have conceded in each of their last 22 league games, only once having a longer run without a clean sheet (31 games between November 1960 and August 1961).
But Alonso is confident James can help Chelsea while he is sidelined, and at this stage, does not anticipate having to dip into the market in January to bring in specific reinforcements.
"I don't think so; we expect by that time he will be back. It doesn't affect [that]," Alonso said when asked if he might need to sign cover for James.
"He is still a very important player. He is the captain, he is a great influence, and hopefully, after he recovers from this injury, he will be available for many games.
"He has a good mentality, and we need him."

5shq40tllrkf1lri1z3qwciz8.title: Gyokeres not influenced by criticism after scoring for Sweden
5shq40tllrkf1lri1z3qwciz8.subtitle: Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal of the season for Sweden against Romania, but he acknowledged his displays had to improve.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres insisted he was not fazed by the criticism he has faced this season with Arsenal after ending his recent goal drought for Sweden in the Nations League.
Gyokeres was on target in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania at Strawberry Arena, with his strike proving to be the winning goal for Graham Potter's side.
Alexander Isak opened the scoring in the 20th minute, only for Dennis Man to level things up nine minutes later as both teams played out an entertaining first half an hour.
However, Gyokeres sealed the win two minutes before half-time, tucking home from close range after Lucas Bergvall's shot from distance was spilled by Ionut Radu.
It marked the Arsenal striker's first goal of the 2026-27 campaign for club and country, having failed to score in any of his five appearances in all competitions for the Gunners.

Gyokeres has only played 207 minutes of football for Arsenal this season, starting just two matches, despite netting 21 times across all competitions in his debut season for Mikel Arteta's side following his big-money move from Sporting CP.

Kai Havertz's injury while playing for Germany could open the door for more opportunities at club level for Gyokeres, who said recent criticism of his performances was something he was not interested in reading.
"If there is a lot of [criticism] and you read it, of course you can be influenced, but that is not something I do," Gyokeres said.
"If you do well, you get praise and if you don't score goals as a striker and play as they expect, there is criticism. That is how it is for all footballers. It goes up and down.
"It is normal. It's always nice to score a goal. It was a good finish from Lucas [Bergvall] and I was in a good position at the far post. I received it and got it in."
Gyokeres did, however, acknowledge his performances for Arsenal had to improve. He has only managed to muster one shot across all of his outings so far in 2026-27.
"I obviously need to do better, and yes, I want to do it, so that's no problem. It's good [the dialogue with Arteta]," Gyokeres added.
"I just try to do well when I get the chance and score goals. You always want to be on the field as a football player, that's just how it is.
"I haven't played a lot, but I've had a few games. It felt okay then, but it's clear that you want to play football, and you want to play as much as possible. If I focus, that will come."
But one player who is not short on confidence is Liverpool forward Isak, who made it five goals in eight matches for club and country so far this season.

Isak also finished with team-high totals for shots (three), touches in the opposition box (seven) and passes in the final third (26), while also playing the full 90 minutes against Romania, with Gyokeres replaced instead by Benjamin Nygren.
There was, however, a moment of concern for Isak, who went down and looked in some discomfort, but he revealed the issue was just some blood on his toe.
"You can see it," the Liverpool man told Sportbladet – who added that he "limped and grumbled badly for a good while" after the tackle – while pointing towards his toe.
"It was a real punch. Those of you who have played may know that it [the pain] takes a few minutes before it releases, but it was okay."

5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.title: Wales have 'puncher's chance' against Portugal and 'alien' Ronaldo, says James
5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.subtitle: Wales visit Portugal for their opening Nations League match on Thursday, with the Selecao still led by Cristiano Ronaldo.
paragraphs: Wales have a "puncher's chance" of upsetting Portugal in their Nations League opener on Thursday, even if the Selecao can still call upon an "alien" in Cristiano Ronaldo.
That is the view of midfielder Jordan James, as Craig Bellamy's side prepare for their League A campaign following promotion from the second tier in 2024-25.
Wales topped Group B4 in the last edition of the Nations League, ahead of Turkiye, Iceland and Montenegro, and their reward is a place in Group A4 this time around, with Portugal, Denmark and Norway.
While Wales went unbeaten in the 2024-25 Nations League (W3 D3), their last campaign in the top tier saw them go winless and earn the fewest points of any nation (D1 L5).
Portugal are, of course, the reigning Nations League holders, having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024-25 final to win the competition for the second time.

And ahead of Thursday's matchup at Sporting CP's Estadio Jose Alvalade, they have won 11 of their 14 home matches in the competition overall (D1 L2), only losing to France (in November 2020) and Spain (September 2022).
But James – who has helped Wolves make a strong start in the Championship after arriving in a loan-to-buy deal from Rennes – says that fixture will hold no fear for Wales.
"Obviously, they're the best players in the world at the end of the day, you can't really sugarcoat it," James said, as quoted by BBC Sport.
"They've got Champions League winners, they've got these kinds of things. I think we're always underdogs. We're used to it, so hopefully we can use that to benefit ourselves.
"You can't count us out. We've got a puncher's chance at the end of the day and we're going there to cause an upset."
Thursday's game will be Portugal's first under Jorge Jesus, who succeeded Roberto Martinez following their round-of-16 exit from the World Cup.
Jesus previously managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner scoring 29 goals in 33 appearances under him, hitting the net once every 99 minutes on average.

Ronaldo opted against following Lionel Messi's example and retiring from international football following the World Cup, with the 41-year-old set to continue representing his country for the time being.
Asked about Ronaldo's quality, James said: "We're all trying to achieve the same thing, to be the best player in the world. But you get those aliens that don't seem human.

"You look at Messi, Neymar, Ronaldo – they've just got that extra little quality where, in big moments, they turn up and can do it again and again and again. I think that's the main thing. The longevity of how they're able to do it is unbelievable."

Wales missed out on the World Cup after losing on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina in a play-off semi-final in March, and their current four-match winless run (D3 L1) is both their worst under Bellamy and their worst start to a calendar year since 2012 (five straight losses).

607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.title: Malen withdraws from Netherlands squad through injury
607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.subtitle: Donyell Malen will not get the chance to extend his brilliant start to the season with the Netherlands, with injury ruling him out.
paragraphs: Donyell Malen has withdrawn from the Netherlands' squad for their upcoming Nations League matches.
Malen has been in red-hot form for Roma in Serie A so far this season, and despite playing the full 90 minutes against Inter on Saturday, he will not represent his country due to injury.
It has not been specified what Malen's issue is, but he is one of two withdrawals, with Justin Kluivert also pulling out.

Since his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances, at least twice as many as any other player in the competition in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).
Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.
Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.
The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

          WSL Matchday 5: The Opta Stats That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Oct 5, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal’s difficult start continued, Man City and Chelsea stayed unbeaten and London City delivered the result of the weekend . Using Opta data, we uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
After five matchdays, there have already been 111 goals scored in the WSL – the second-most at this stage of the season behind just the 2020-21 campaign (115).

The opening weeks have seen league positions swap and change, but we head into the international break with Manchester City setting the pace. They have a perfect 15 points from 15, with Chelsea two points behind on 13 and highly anticipated newcomers London City Lionesses making their presence felt in third on 12 points.

The real story of these opening weeks, though, has arguably been Arsenal’s alarming start. The Gunners head into the international break down in 10th, with just five points from five games and back-to-back defeats leaving Renée Slegers under mounting pressure.
But, as ever, the results only tell part of the story. We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and remarkable numbers that defined Matchday 5.
Arsenal’s alarming start to the season hit a new low on Sunday as they threw away a lead to lose 4-2 to Manchester City.

Having gone ahead, the Gunners were beaten in a WSL match for the first time since February 2024 against West Ham, ending a 37-game unbeaten run when scoring first and underlining the fragility that has defined their campaign.
There have not been many bright sparks during Arsenal’s difficult start, but summer signing Lisa Baum has provided a glimpse of what could be to come if they can turn things around.
The last younger player to do so was Ebony Salmon in November 2020, aged 19 years and 285 days.
In finding the net, Baum also helped Arsenal carve out a unique piece of WSL history.

For City, it was a very different story. They came from behind twice to beat Arsenal, securing their first WSL victory over the Gunners after conceding first since December 2020. In the five such meetings between those victories, City failed to win, drawing one and losing four.
It was also the fastest substitute goal in the competition since Pernille Harder against Everton in May 2023 (62 seconds).

Her leveller against the Gunners also meant the Dutchwoman also became the first defender in City’s WSL history to come off the bench and score a goal that either levelled the match or put City ahead.
City head into the international break with a perfect record and a growing sense of inevitability that whatever position they find themselves in, they can find a way to win.

Against Arsenal, Jeglertz's side generated just 1.01 xG to Arsenal's' 1.61, finishing the match with a -0.60 xG differential. It was the second-largest negative xG differential City have overcome in a WSL victory, and their first league win despite being second best on xG since a 2-1 victory over Brighton in March 2025 (-0.22).

With just one place separating the sides at kick-off, London City Lionesses seized the opportunity to overtake Tottenham in emphatic fashion. Spurs had begun the season in impressive form and sat second heading into the weekend, but a stunning 6-1 victory saw Eder Maestre's side move above them in the table.

They wasted little time taking control. Alexia Putellas’ third-minute opener was London City’s fastest WSL goal, while it was the earliest Tottenham have conceded in the league under Martin Ho, and their earliest since facing Arsenal in November 2024.

It means that Putellas has won 130 of the last 131 league matches in which she has scored, so once the ball hit the back of the net in the third minute, history suggested Spurs were already in trouble.

Diani was joined on the scoresheet twice by Putellas, with the pair making a little piece of WSL history in the process. It was the first time a French international and a Spanish international have both scored 2+ goals in the same WSL match.
For Tottenham, the scale of the defeat was particularly remarkable given their form coming into the game.

630E932EF07ECB32463149AB07D7EE06.title: Preview: Chelsea meet Spurs in London Derby
630E932EF07ECB32463149AB07D7EE06.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Chelsea meet Spurs in London DerbyShareChelsea and Tottenham Hotspur face each other at Stamford Bridge on the back of morale-boosting victories.
Last weekend’s 2-0 win over Everton was Chelsea’s most complete and controlled performance of the Xabi Alonso era so far, building on the 5-1 victory at home to Bournemouth the week before.

The Blues are finding some much-needed stability and could add to their momentum with a third win in a row at home to Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. This would indicate Alonso’s side have truly turned the corner.
Spurs might not be at that stage yet, but Monday’s win over Coventry City hinted they might finally be heading in the right direction under Roberto De Zerbi.

It was certainly their most uplifting result and performance of the season so far with James Maddison making a long-awaited goalscoring return to the lineup. Sandro Tonali was also very impressive in the centre of the pitch.
Chelsea and Spurs have experienced tough times of late, but there is hope on both sides that the dark days are a thing of the past and that Saturday’s match will be a catalyst for greater success.

Moisés Caicedo and Jordan Henderson have forged an unlikely partnership in central midfield – something we looked at in more depth here – and are expected to continue as Chelsea’s first-choice double pivot after starting in the wins over Bournemouth and Everton.
João Pedro has scored three goals in his last three games, giving Chelsea cutting edge in the final third. The Brazilian will be supported by Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers as dual number 10s.

Levi Colwill and Maxence Lacroix will fill two of the three spots in Chelsea’s backline with Josh Achempong most likely to complete the defensive unit which has been vulnerable in several games this season.
Maddison showed Spurs what they had been missing in his comeback performance against Coventry and the 29-year-old is expected to start again. Without him, Tottenham lack creativity on the ball.

Dominic Solanke will likely lead the line with Mohammed Kudus and Omar Marmoush on the left and right. Meanwhile, Mateus Fernandes could come into the central midfield unit to offer more security on the ball.

Emi Martínez is recovering from surgery after sustaining a head injury against Everton and so Mike Penders will start in goal for Chelsea. The highly-rated Belgian youngster must step up in the absence of the World Cup winner.
Reece James is sidelined with a knee injury while Pep Chavarrií is a doubt. Otherwise, Alonso has a fully fit and available squad to choose from for the visit of Spurs.
Rodrigo Bentancur will miss Saturday’s match through suspension while Sávio, Xavi Simons, Lucas Bergvall, Mykhaylo Mudryk and Wilson Odobert are also unavailable through injury for Tottenham.
Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie both missed Monday’s win over Coventry City, but could be fit enough to feature in some capacity at Stamford Bridge this weekend.

Dejan Kulusevski made his much-anticipated return from injury against Coventry and could feature against Chelsea, although the Swede won’t be fit enough to start. He will be limited to another cameo off the bench.
Spurs have won just one of their last 36 league games at Stamford Bridge, and we think that damning stat might just extend to one in 37: Chelsea 3-1 Tottenham.

639234B2CA21039A0A8846627E3F126B.title: Preview: Man City look to continue winning streak on trip to Villa Park
639234B2CA21039A0A8846627E3F126B.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Man City look to continue winning streak on trip to Villa ParkShareEarly in the season it may be, but Aston Villa have the Premier League’s joint-worst home record so far – so a visit of Manchester City might be the last thing they need…but have they turned a corner?
Unai Emery will hope so. After starting the season with a Super Cup defeat and one point from four Premier League games, they are now on a much stronger run without a loss in seven.

There has been a bit of conjecture around whether the ongoing redevelopment of Villa Park has contributed to the less-than-stellar results on home soil, with just a point taken so far this term – but back-to-back Champions League wins will boost confidence and quieten any mental doubts. Still, Emery has more than that to contend with. If last season’s success was built around the Onana-Tielemans midfield axis, both parts are missing this term, for different reasons, and that means putting a new foundation in place for the team to build from. A whole host of new signings, a revamped front line and in truth a very different-looking spine is in place and that takes time to gel: from the well-established Emi Martinez-Ezri Konsa-Youri Tielemens-Ollie Watkins line, they’ve moved to Zion Suzuki, a mix of centre-backs, Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson. It looks promising, but needs time.

Man City themselves haven’t wasted much energy on the charges they’re appealing against and keep racking up the wins – a three-point lead at the top is cosmetic at this stage, but beating the boos and jeers they’ll doubtless face on each road trip this term is going to bring the lineup more together, make it more resilient and determined. That, at least, is what Enzo Maresca will be banking on, and he certainly has the firepower at his disposal to ensure City should go out and attack every opponent into submission.

Six wins in the last seven across all competitions for Villa, but just one point from three home league matches this term. It’s seven played, seven wins for Man City in the league, plus an easy midweek romp in Europe.
Full-backs Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Matteo Ruggeri are out for Villa, while Amadou Onana is a long-term injury absentee.

City will be without Antoine Semenyo, but each of Mateo Kovačić, Nico O’Reilly and Matheus Nunes could be passed fit to join the squad. Erling Haaland will undoubtably return following his midweek rest for the Champions League win over AEK.

Getting Manzambi into key areas where he can attack the City defence, link with Jackson and be a goal threat is key. He's had minimal gametime so far but he’s had more shots per 90 than other top-flight midfielders this term, while over the last year he’s ahead of 97% for shots compared to midfielders around Europe and 96% for goals. If those two forge a partnership, Villa will always have an out-ball and a goal threat.
Villa have struggled on home soil but they should at least give their visitors a run for their money: Villa 2-3 City.

65tjd0h4aodq1kqwdrrkfwvla.title: OFI Crete 0-2 Bayer Leverkusen: Hofmann at the double for in-form visitors
65tjd0h4aodq1kqwdrrkfwvla.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen still have maximum points in the league stage of the Europa League, following Thursday's 2-0 away win over OFI Crete.
paragraphs: Jonas Hofmann's quickfire brace was enough to guide Bayer Leverkusen to a 2-0 win over OFI Crete, lifting them to nine points from three Europa League games.
Hofmann scored twice in the space of 174 seconds late in the first half to decide Thursday's game, with the Bundesliga giants never looking to be in any trouble against their Greek opponents.

Carles Martinez's visitors were arguably unfortunate not to go ahead earlier, with Klidman Lilo forced to push a Hofmann sighter to safety and Malik Tillman unable to beat the OFI shot-stopper from close range.
But the deadlock was broken in the 35th minute, with Hofmann perfectly placed to slot home after Lilo failed to hold Afonso Moreira's 25-yard attempt.

Hofmann's second goal, which arrived just under three minutes later, was more impressive as he struck Tillman's pass without breaking stride, sending a lovely finish skidding into the bottom-left corner from just outside the area.

Hofmann almost secured the match ball early in the second half, with Lilo equal to his efforts this time around as he punched his curler beyond the post, while Miguel Gutierrez came off the bench to force another strong save out of the home shot-stopper.
But Leverkusen ultimately did not need a third goal, and Janis Blaswich was only called into two routine saves at the other end as OFI were held at arm's length.
Lilo kept busy as Leverkusen impress
This match looked like a potential banana skin for Leverkusen, after OFI registered an eye-catching 2-0 win at home to their Bundesliga rivals Hoffenheim on matchday one.

In fact, the Greek side had won nine of their first 11 home games in major European competitions and were hoping to become the first team to reach 10 home wins in as few as 12 matches since Middlesbrough in 2004-05 and 2005-06.
But Leverkusen – who have now won six straight games in all competitions – passed that test with flying colours.
They racked up 33 shots, 15 of which hit the target, and tallied 3.1 expected goals. OFI, meanwhile, were restricted to six attempts, two of which hit the target, and 0.23 xG.

Just to underline the extent of Leverkusen's dominance, Lilo in the OFI net was forced into 12 saves – the joint-most by any goalkeeper in a Europa League game since August 2020, when Copenhagen's Karl-Johan Johnsson made 13 in a 1-0 quarter-final loss to Manchester United.

          Liverpool vs Man City Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The standout Premier League fixture of Matchday 6 sees two old rivals square off at Anfield. We look ahead to Sunday's heavyweight clash with our Liverpool vs Man City prediction and preview.
It is fair to say Manchester City had an eventful international break.

The Premier League was thrown into turmoil following confirmation that City had been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the competition's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and the majority of charges in relation to their failure to co-operate with the league's investigation. City deny all the allegations and have appealed against the charges.

As difficult as it may be amid all the talk of hefty punishments, Enzo Maresca and his players must turn their attention to on-pitch matters this Sunday, when they are sure to receive a vociferous welcome from Liverpool‘s fans at Anfield.

During the tenures of Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola, fixtures between these teams were circled in the calendar far in advance, but for the first time in 11 years, they will face off without either of those iconic coaches in the dugouts.
The last time that was the case, in March 2015, Brendan Rodgers' Reds beat Manuel Pellegrini's Citizens 2-1 at Anfield.
Neither Andoni Iraola nor Maresca have tasted defeat in the Premier League with their new clubs, though it is the City boss who has made the more impressive start.

With Sunday's visitors emerging from the international break with the only 100% record in the Premier League, Maresca could become only the fourth manager to open a spell in charge of any club with six straight wins in the competition, after Carlo Ancelotti with Chelsea, Guardiola with City, and Ole Gunnar Solskjær with Manchester United.

Prior to the international break – which may feel like a lifetime ago to City fans – Maresca's men earned a chaotic 5-3 victory over Sunderland, with Antoine Semenyo grabbing a brace while Enzo Fernández, Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland joined him on the scoresheet.

Maresca said afterwards that he would “prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3”, and though the Italian will yearn for greater control over games, he will surely be delighted with how his attackers have started the campaign.

Haaland leads the Golden Boot race already, with five goals to his name, and after finding the net against Sunderland, he has scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the Premier League. The Norwegian failed to score on his first three Premier League trips to Anfield, finally finding the net on the fourth attempt in February, in a 2-1 triumph for City.

Cherki and Semenyo, meanwhile, rank first and second among all Premier League players for their expected goals overperformance this campaign. Cherki has scored three goals from 0.72 xG (+2.28), while Semenyo has struck twice from 0.34 xG (+1.66).

In what is sure to be a red-hot atmosphere, City will have to keep clear heads. After starring for England in Declan Rice's absence during the international break, Elliot Anderson will look to calm things down and dictate proceedings.
Anderson leads all midfielders in the Premier League this season for line-breaking passes (105), progressive carries (64), and duel success (60.7%, minimum 50 contested).

Having won at Anfield with Nottingham Forest in 2024-25 (1-0) and 2025-26 (3-0), Anderson could become the seventh player to win on his first three away starts against Liverpool in the Premier League, and the first since Martin Kelly with Crystal Palace between 2015 and 2017.

Liverpool are six points off the early pace being set by City, having won two and drawn three of their opening five games of 2026-27, though they did go into the hiatus in positive spirits after winning 1-0 at Bournemouth.
Iraola could become only the third permanent Liverpool manager to avoid defeat in each of his first six top-flight matches in charge, after Bob Paisley in 1974 and Joe Fagan in 1983.

But the Spaniard is still seeking his first home Premier League victory, having overseen draws with Nottingham Forest and Fulham. There have only been seven previous instances of Liverpool failing to win any of their first three home games in a season, and just two since the First World War – in 1963-64 and 2012-13.

There have certainly been signs that the Reds learning Iraola's high-octane style, having applied high-intensity pressures to 48.9% of their opponent's touches in the opposition's half in the Premier League this season – the highest rate of any side.
City, though, are completing 83.0% of their passes attempted while under high-intensity pressure in the competition this term, the best accuracy of any side.

          All-Action Ronald Araújo Looks Right at Home at Liverpool
        
      
                          
                      Oct 27, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Some eyebrows were raised when Liverpool signed Ronald Araújo on loan from Barcelona this summer, but he is more than justifying the faith shown in him by Andoni Iraola.
They say you should never fall in love with a loan player.
Like a library book or a rental car, you simply can’t get too attached when the agreement is only short-term.
However, the Anfield crowd couldn’t help themselves on Sunday. Ronald Araújo was just too endearing.
Two main things fans want to see from their players are ability and passion, and when those are combined to lead to victory, there’s not much more that can be asked for.

Liverpool were unsurprisingly made to work hard for their 2-0 win by in-form Brighton & Hove Albion, and their pair of first-half goals were cheered raucously. First came a Pascal Groß own goal forced by Florian Wirtz’s shot, and then Alexander Isak buried Bradley Barcola’s cross as the ruthless Reds raced into a two-goal lead after just 21 minutes.

But those decibels were almost equalled in the second half as Araújo set about tackling Brighton players in an almost comically aggressive but successful fashion to ensure Liverpool’s sheet remained clean and that their first three points in a home league game this season were collected.

That was after the Uruguayan had produced a moment that later went viral in the first half when he blocked a shot from Maxim De Cuyper, before taking the choice while still on the floor to tackle his opponent with his head. It was a moment enjoyed by everyone associated with Liverpool, except perhaps for the medical team who may have broken out in a cold sweat at Araújo's flagrant disregard for keeping his head un-kicked.
Ronald giving EVERYTHING to secure the clean sheet 💪😅 pic.twitter.com/lPNASzhw22

It was another solid outing for Araújo, who had more touches than any other Liverpool player in the game (59), won possession six times – only Alexis Mac Allister (7) did so more often for the hosts – and made eight clearances, second only to Virgil van Dijk (10).

Araújo was something of a surprise signing from Barcelona in the summer. Liverpool rarely pick up players on loan, and bringing in a 27-year-old defender for just one year seemed unusually knee-jerk for a club who usually pride themselves on long-term planning.

That said, it wasn’t entirely without justification. Araújo had been captain at Camp Nou, came with plenty of top-level experience, and he largely impressed during his time in Spain. He did struggle with form last season, culminating in a red card in Barcelona’s defeat at Chelsea in the Champions League. Following that game, the player decided to take a break to work on improving his mental health.

In a recent interview with The Times, Araújo opened up on what was “a very difficult time,” adding: “I felt that what I needed to do was take a step back. I hadn’t felt right for a long time, and I wasn’t enjoying the thing I love most, which is football.

“I realised I had to put my hand up, ask for help and talk not just to the people closest to me, but to professionals as well. Sometimes you bottle things up and try to be the strong man, but in life you have to talk about things and open up about what you’re going through.”
If his early form for Liverpool is anything to go by, that break and fresh surroundings have been exactly the tonic Araújo needed.

When you sign a player from Barcelona, you don’t necessarily expect to receive a blood-and-thunder type, but many who had watched Araújo closely in La Liga did suggest he may suit the Premier League given the more physical style of play. That appears to have been spot on, as he has warmed to things quickly England, and it is really benefitting Andoni Iraola and Liverpool.

His new boss has shown plenty of faith in him even though he’s only a loan player. Araújo is one of only three players to have featured in all 12 of Liverpool’s games this season along with Jérémy Jacquet and Mac Allister.

One of the reasons he has had so many opportunities is his versatility. Araújo was predominantly a centre-back for Barcelona, but he has played more than three quarters of his minutes for Liverpool this season at right-back (76%). The long-term injury to Conor Bradley and the form/fitness of Jeremie Frimpong opened up a spot in the back four, and Araújo has filled it seamlessly.

He is providing extra strength and defensive nous for Liverpool, who at times last season looked like they were a bit too easy to play against, but there hasn’t had to be much compromise in terms of attacking output. Araújo has two goals and an assist in his 12 games, with all three of his goal involvements coming in the Champions League.

He produced a cheeky assist for Dominik Szoboszlai in the home win over Atlético Madrid, backheeling the ball to the Hungarian to score, while he headed in the opener in the 6-3 victory in LASK, and then grabbed an equaliser in the 4-3 success over Villarreal last week.

682BE6BD912AF4C40D6C094CE3BE281C.title: Time to invest in Bournemouth? - FPL gameweek nine dilemmas
682BE6BD912AF4C40D6C094CE3BE281C.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsFootballScores & FixturesTablesPremier LeagueChampions LeagueWomen's FootballTeamsLeagues & CupsGossipTop ScorersEuropeanQuizzesTime to invest in Bournemouth? - FPL gameweek nine dilemmasImage source, Getty ImagesPublished34 minutes agoBBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek nine.
Yes, I think so. They face Leeds at home in gameweek nine, followed by a very appealing run of fixtures over the next few gameweeks.
Marcus Tavernier (£6.4m) is my favourite pick. He's been attracting plenty of attention after recent performances and offers a good combination of goal threat and creativity from midfield.

Evanilson (£6.2m) is another one I'd consider. He's a decent budget forward who should get opportunities to score in this run of fixtures. If you're after a cheaper route into Bournemouth's attack, he's worth a look.
Antonio Silva (£5.0m) is my defender of choice as he's great for defensive contributions, but I won't be rushing to triple up on the Cherries.
Nicolas Jackson (£6.7m) is certainly an interesting option after a strong run of recent form - scoring four in his past four Premier League matches.
He looks to be finding his feet at Aston Villa and he's an appealing alternative to some of the other budget forwards in the game.
Aston Villa face Fulham at home in gameweek nine, which is the start of a very nice run of fixtures to back him in.

My only concern is his minutes. There's a slight risk of him being hooked early, especially with Villa juggling Champions League football and promising young striker Brian Madjo (£5.4m) back from injury.
However, with his recent form and price in mind, he's definitely worth considering.

Image source, Fantasy Premier LeagueIs Haaland still the obvious captain choice?Yes, absolutely. Erling Haaland (£15.7m) remains the standout captaincy option for me, even after Manchester City's first Premier League defeat of the season.
He scored again against Aston Villa in gameweek eight and continues to be the player I'd back to deliver the biggest points haul in any given match.

This doesn't mean you have to captain him every single gameweek of course - there will be opportunities to look elsewhere at times. However, he's the only reliable premium asset in the game right now.
Joao Pedro (£7.8m) is an easy sell following Xabi Alonso's comments ruling him out for weeks.
Some may be thinking of holding the Chelsea forward through his injury and simply benching him. I can see why this is tempting, because when he's fit, he's one of the best assets in the game.
However, we don't know how long this could go on for, so I won't be holding him hoping for a speedy recovery.
Another reason he's an easy sell is the mid-priced forwards are actually enticing right now.
Alternatives such as Jackson and Evanilson have excellent form and favourable forthcoming fixtures.
The likes of Dominic Calvert Lewin (£6.1m), Thierno Barry (£5.6m) or if you have the money Alexander Isak (£9.1m) are all worth considering, too.
It's likely I'll be selling Rayan Cherki (£8.0m) this week. He's clearly a talented player, but his minutes are becoming a real concern and there are better options available at a cheaper price.
