          Celebrating 1,500 WSL Matches: Looking Back on the League's Most Statistically Significant Games
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the 1,500th WSL game set to be played this weekend, we look back at some of the matches that hold statistical significance across the competition’s history.
This weekend will see the 1,500th game in English Women’s Super League history played when Manchester City host Arsenal in one of the most anticipated fixtures of the 2026-27 season.

Ahead of Matchday 5 of the campaign, there have been 1,493 matches played across 17 seasons of WSL action – including the 2017 Spring Series. With six games scheduled before Sunday's showdown at the Etihad Stadium, Manchester City and Arsenal will have the distinction of contesting the league's landmark 1,500th fixture.
To mark the occasion, we look back at some of the most memorable matches in WSL history and the statistics that made them stand out.
The first ever WSL fixture took place on 13 April 2011 with Chelsea hosting Arsenal at Imperial Fields, Mitcham.

Arsenal edged a 1-0 victory thanks to Gilly Flaherty's 35th-minute strike, though chances were at a premium throughout. The two sides combined for just 13 shots and five efforts on target, making it one of the least open contests of the campaign.
The win was one of 10 Arsenal recorded during the inaugural 2011 WSL season, as they went on to finish three points clear of Birmingham City and win the league's first title.
Arsenal are also the team to have secured the biggest margin of victory ever seen in WSL history (+10), as they thrashed Bristol City 11-1 at Meadow Park in December 2019 under Joe Montemurro.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, this is also the highest-scoring WSL fixture of all time (12).

The warning signs were there for Bristol City. Rooted to the foot of the table without a single win to their name, they travelled to face the reigning champions knowing they were up against one of the most dominant sides in the league.
What followed was a mismatch of historic proportions.

Ten of Arsenal’s goals were either scored (6) or assisted (4) by Vivianne Miedema, who set WSL records for the most goals, assists and goal involvements by a player in a single WSL match. Those records still stand, although Chelsea’s Guro Reiten equalled the Dutch forward’s single-game assist record with four against Leicester City on 3 December 2022.

Two WSL matches have featured as many as nine different goalscorers, excluding own goals: Chelsea's 9-0 victory over Bristol City in September 2020 and Brighton & Hove Albion's thrilling 7-3 win against the Robins in March 2024.

Chelsea’s first home game of 2020-21 was a treat for their fans at Kingsmeadow. The Blues ran riot, scoring nine times from as many different players. Millie Bright, Sam Kerr, Niamh Charles, Maren Mjelde, Fran Kirby, Melanie Leupolz, Erin Cuthbert, Pernille Harder and Bethany England all found the net in a historic display.

Three and a half years later, Brighton's 7-3 victory at Ashton Gate produced another game with nine different goalscorers. Of the 10 goals scored, only Elisabeth Terland (two) found the net more than once.

Katie Robinson, Madison Haley, Pauline Bremer, Tatiana Pinto and Vicky Losada were Brighton's other scorers, while Amalie Thestrup, Brooke Aspin and Megan Connolly found the net for Bristol City in defeat, making it one of the most entertaining and free-scoring matches in WSL history.
One other WSL record was set in a match between Chelsea and Bristol City, too.

Chelsea's 6-0 win over Manchester City in February 2019 remains the only WSL match to feature two hat-trick scorers. Bethany England and Fran Kirby shared the six goals between them, taking turns to find the net throughout the contest. Kirby scored Chelsea's first, third and fifth goals, while England struck the others.
Kirby scored another hat-trick in their next game, a 4-0 win over Liverpool, meaning two of her three hat-tricks in the competition came in back-to-back appearances.
Only Vivianne Miedema (five) and Khadija Shaw (eight) have recorded more WSL hat-tricks than Kirby and England, who remain tied on three apiece.

693bsc3bo3l21juf0y4de3ikp.title: Hurzeler urges Brighton to 'stay humble' after emphatic win over Palace
693bsc3bo3l21juf0y4de3ikp.subtitle: Fabian Hurzeler has stressed his players need to remain "humble" after Brighton thrashed rivals Crystal Palace 5-0 in the Premier League.
paragraphs: Fabian Hurzeler has implored his Brighton players to "stay humble" after they thumped rivals Crystal Palace 5-0 to continue their excellent start in the Premier League.
Brighton raced into a three-goal lead inside 10 minutes after an own-goal from Jaydee Canvot, a wonder-strike from Diego Gomez and Yasin Ayari's composed finish.

The Seagulls became the ninth side in Premier League history to score three goals in the first 10 minutes of a match, and first since Newcastle United against Tottenham in April 2023, and it only got better from there.
Charalampos Kostoulas found the back of the net four minutes after the restart before Jack Hinshelwood added further gloss to the scoreline six minutes from time.

The result saw Brighton extend their winning run in the Premier League to four matches, while also taking their goal tally to 23, their most ever at this stage of a campaign in the top four tiers. Incredibly, only Barcelona have scored more goals than the Seagulls across the top five leagues this term (39).
And when asked about his side's performance, Hurzeler said: "I am very happy for our supporters, our fans. They have waited long enough for this feeling, beating our rivals.
"We had another good performance, another clean sheet which was important, and I am happy for the boys.
"Although it is important to celebrate the goal and the win, there is room for improvement. We have to stay humble and understand why we are where we are at the moment."
The contest was best known for Gomez's halfway finish with the strike already being touted as an early goal of the season contender.
Gomez's stunner was from 51 metres, the furthest range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney for Everton v West Ham in November 2017 (58 metres).
But for Palace boss Pierre Sage, it was a day to forget after his team registered five shots in this game, their lowest total in a single match in the Premier League this season.
The Eagles have now lost their fourth league game of the season and currently sit 14th, two points ahead of 18th-placed Fulham.
Palace have also now conceded 17 goals across their opening seven Premier League matches, with the Eagles last letting in more at this stage of a season in the top four tiers in 1980-81 (21).
When asked about his feelings after the contest, Sage said, "Only one feeling – shame. When you play this kind of game you have to show another face. It was our worst face.
"We cannot accept that, especially at the beginning of the game. We didn't fight at that moment. Once it was 3-0 after nine minutes, the game was really different.
"It's my fault because I am the coach, I gave the angle to the players. I gave the motivation. I prepare the situations. We played so badly. It's my fault."

6B3034AA7CCFF7AF652E92A828694C37.title: Preview: Barcelona look to get back to winning ways against Deportivo Alaves
6B3034AA7CCFF7AF652E92A828694C37.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Barcelona look to get back to winning ways against Deportivo AlavesShareAfter suffering their first domestic defeat of the season in El Clásico, Barcelona will be keen to add three more points to their tally against Alavés.

Barcelona got off to a record-breaking start this season, winning each of their first 11 matches across all competitions. That run included nine in La Liga, matching Real Madrid’s league record from the 1968/69 campaign. They were subsequently brought down to earth by losses to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and their biggest rivals domestically.

It has been over a decade since the Blaugrana lost three straight matches, with the last such run coming in 2016 when they succumbed to Real Sociedad and Valencia either side of a Champions League quarter-final elimination at the hands of Atlético Madrid.

Alavés also came out of the blocks very well by their standards, amassing 10 points from their first four league games with wins over Getafe, Villarreal and Osasuna. They have subsequently slowed down significantly, though, picking up just two more points with four losses in their last six. Even so, they are sitting pretty in the table as they occupy seventh place.

Having escaped relegation by just a couple of points in each of the last two seasons, competing for a European spot may be too lofty an ambition for Alavés. At the very least, they should look to avoid being sucked back into the battle at the bottom at the end of the term.

Xavi Espart’s ankle issue last weekend compounded Barcelona’s back line injury crisis. Eric García, Andreas Christensen and Jules Koundé are also out, leaving Hansi Flick with just four senior defenders. Among attackers, Dani Olmo and Roony Bardghji will be unavailable.
Alavés will be without Facundo Garcés and Mikel Rodríguez, who are expected to miss not just this match but the remainder of the season.

Pau Cubarsí will have a big job to do in marshalling Barcelona’s threadbare back line, which has conceded eight goals across the last three games. Even if they give up one or two, though, they will be confident that Raphinha and Lamine Yamal can add to their league goal involvement tallies of 16 and 14 respectively.

Alavés do have some attacking firepower to trouble the opposition defenders. Striker Lucas Boyé has five goals this season, while former Real Madrid forward Mariano Díaz has three in addition to four assists. Their most important player on this night will likely be Antonio Sivera, though, as his goal will probably be peppered at some point.
Barcelona have made a habit of blowing away domestic defences so far this season as they are averaging four goals per game in the league, so they should have far too much for Alavés to handle.

          Newcastle 0-1 Aston Villa: Manzambi Downs Magpies as Jaissle's Struggles Continue
        
      
                          
                      Oct 17, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Johan Manzambi's header secured three points for Unai Emery's side. Re-live this Premier League clash with our Newcastle vs Aston Villa stats page.
Former Newcastle United transfer target Johan Manzambi was the match-winner as Aston Villa earned a 1-0 victory over Matthias Jaissle's side at a disgruntled St James' Park.

Manzambi had looked set to join Newcastle from Freiburg in July, only for that deal to be hijacked by Villa, and on Saturday, he continued his superb start to Premier League life at the Magpies' expense.
His 36th-minute header gave Unai Emery's side a lead they would not relinquish, with Newcastle being booed off following their second Premier League defeat in a row.

It was Villa who started on the front foot as Nicolas Jackson shot straight at Lukás Hornícek with the outside of his boot, while Sven Botman was arguably fortunate to avoid a red card after clattering the former Chelsea forward.
Jackson continued to be heavily involved as his curler flicked off Botman and faded wide, but it was Manzambi who opened the scoring.

He was left totally unmarked when João Gomes floated a cross in from the right flank, and though Hornicek got a hand to his header, there was simply too much power for the Czech stopper to keep it out.

Newcastle had a huge reprieve when Emiliano Buendía‘s shot smacked off the post and hit Hornicek on the back, with no claret shirts ready to pounce on what would have been a tap-in, and the half-time whistle brought boos from the disgruntled home fans.

Having scored a wonder goal in Newcastle's 4-1 defeat at Coventry City five days earlier, Botman almost repeated the trick with a well-struck effort that Zion Suzuki had to push wide, while Yoane Wissa headed over as the hosts grew increasingly desperate.
Hornicek tipped a drive from Villa substitute Ross Barkley around his right-hand post, as Villa combined their resolute defensive work with incisive counter-attacking.
Ibrahim Mbaye had two opportunities to get a clinching goal off the bench, one of which saw him power over at the near post, while the second saw his reverse shot fade wide following a mazy dribble.

But with Wissa planting his final attempt wide of the right post and Victor Lindelöf throwing himself in front of the ball amid a late scramble in the Villa area, Newcastle were unable to find an equaliser.
Things could have been very different had Manzambi signed on the dotted line at St James', but the draw of UEFA Champions League football lured him to Villa.
And the Switzerland international has now been directly involved in five goals in four starts for Villa in all competitions, scoring three and assisting two.

Manzambi is just the fourth player to either score or assist on each of his first three Premier League starts for Villa, after Dalian Atkinson in August 1992, Dion Dublin in November 1998 and Danny Ings in August 2021.

By contrast, Newcastle's big-money attacking signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo has only had two shots in five Premier League games this campaign (one on target) and is still yet to score. He was quiet again on Saturday before being withdrawn in the 56th minute.

The Magpies were truly dismal in the first half, with Villa goalkeeper Suzuki completing more passes prior to the interval (24) than any home player, and Newcastle's 16-game run without a clean sheet at home (in all competitions) is now the longest in their history.

Emery, meanwhile, was left to celebrate his 100th Premier League win across spells with Arsenal and Villa, reaching that tally in 197 games (D44 L53) – he is the joint-ninth fastest manager to reach a century of victories in the competition.

          Liga F, Frauen-Bundesliga, Première Ligue, Serie A Opta Supercomputer Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 16, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We explore the Opta supercomputer’s predictions for Europe’s women’s leagues: the Frauen-Bundesliga, Liga F, Première Ligue and Serie A.

As the first international break of the second half of the year comes to a close, domestic football across Europe resumes this weekend, and the Opta supercomputer has simulated the season ahead across the continent’s leading women’s leagues.

Having already explored our WSL season predictions, we now turn our attention to the rest of Europe’s top five leagues: Spain’s Liga F, Germany’s Frauen-Bundesliga, Italy’s Serie A and France’s Première Ligue.
Six matches have been played in Spain and Germany, France has completed four rounds of fixtures, and Italy’s campaign is only just getting under way after kicking off at the end of September.

Barcelona are overwhelming favourites to retain their Liga F crown, while OL Lyonnes and Bayern Munich look firmly in control in France and Germany. Italy, meanwhile, appears to offer us the closest title race of the four.
Using 10,000 simulations for each league, we break down the Opta supercomputer’s predictions to assess who is best placed to claim silverware, secure European qualification and avoid relegation.

The Frauen-Bundesliga may not command the same global attention as the NWSL or WSL, but Opta’s Power Rankings place it as the third-best league in the world. With the German season kicking off on 21 August, we're already six games into the new campaign.

The Opta supercomputer forecasts a two-horse race between Bayern Munich and VfL Wolfsburg, although whether the contest will prove competitive remains to be seen. Bayern finished 16 points clear last season, the largest winning margin in league history, and are overwhelming favourites to retain their crown.

The Bavarians are projected to win the title in 92.9% of the supercomputer’s 10,000 simulations. They are the only side to have maintained a 100% record after six matches. Bayern are bidding to become the first team in the division’s history to win five consecutive league titles.

Wolfsburg remain their closest challengers, though they only have a 6.4% probability of lifting the trophy. They have collected 15 points from a possible 18 so far, though, after losing to TSG Hoffenheim 2-1 on Matchday 5, their first loss against the side since March 2024.
It means that Stephan Lerch’s side are projected to finish second in 67.5% of simulations and have a 93.3% chance of qualifying for the UEFA Women’s Champions League (UWCL).

Wolfsburg’s attacking quality has been evident, with Ella Peddemors leading the league for attacking-sequence involvements (42) and goals scored (four), while teammate Svenja Huth has created more chances than any other player (29). They also top the league for high turnovers (76) and shots following high turnovers (17), underlining their ability to win possession high up the pitch and turn pressure into clear-cut opportunities.
The battle for Europe sees four clubs competing for the three available UWCL places.

Bayern are guaranteed to qualify according to the model, while Wolfsburg (93.3%), Eintracht Frankfurt (62.8%) and Bayer Leverkusen (35.6%) are the other leading contenders. However, qualification does not guarantee a direct route into the competition: only the Bundesliga champions secure direct entry to the UWCL league phase, with the other places entering through earlier qualifying rounds.
Leverkusen look increasingly dangerous this season, particularly away from home, having won six consecutive matches on the road; their longest such streak in league history.

Erëleta Memeti has been instrumental in their progress, leading the league for goal involvements (seven), expected assists (3.68), big chances created (four) and successful dribbles (16), highlighting her influence as both a creator and a ball-carrier.

The 2025-26 campaign also marked a significant change for the division, which expanded from 12 to 14 teams, mirroring the WSL’s recent expansion. This season has brought two historic arrivals, with VfB Stuttgart and 1. FSV Mainz 05 competing in the top flight for the first time.
Stuttgart have made an encouraging start to life among the elite, sitting eighth with eight points after six matches.

Their games included a narrow 2-1 defeat to Wolfsburg, demonstrating their ability to compete against established Bundesliga sides. Their points tally is the most by a promoted team at this stage since Bayern Munich collected 12 points after six games in 2000-01.

That promising start is reflected in Opta’s projections. Stuttgart have just a 2.9% probability of finishing bottom and a 13% chance of relegation, placing them among the more secure sides in the lower half of the table.

          Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal: An Avoidably Fractious End to One of International Football’s Greatest Careers?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 2, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After leaving Portugal's training camp, it would seem Cristiano Ronaldo's international career has come to a tense end. It didn't need to be like this.
Cristiano Ronaldo was – surprisingly to some – philosophical, realistic about his standing in the Portuguese national team.

Following years of debate about whether Portugal were better off with or without him in the starting XI, their former talisman appeared to accept that his role under strong-willed new coach Jorge Jesus – whom he’d previously worked with at Al Nassr – might be somewhat diminished, on the pitch at least.

“If the coach decides the best thing for the team is for me to start on the bench, I’ll accept that perfectly,” he told RTP after starting last week’s 1-0 UEFA Nations League win over Wales. “I’m here to help the national team in whatever way is needed. If I don't get to play, that’s no problem either; the most important thing is for the team to win and for the group to be united.
“I’ve always said that the group is above any individual player and I am fully available to fulfil whatever role is assigned to me.”
Fast-forward a week and Portugal are embroiled in a Ronaldo-shaped crisis, with the world-record holder for men’s international caps unlikely to feature for his country again.

Despite being “fully available to fulfil whatever role is assigned to me”, Ronaldo didn’t appear to appreciate being an unused substitute during Sunday’s 2-1 win away to Norway. At full-time, he marched straight down the tunnel instead of joining his teammates in acknowledging the travelling Portugal supporters.

Then, everything came to a head on Wednesday. Ronaldo confirmed he’d left the Portuguese training camp following “a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation” regarding Jorge Jesus’ pre-match press conference ahead of Thursday’s clash with Denmark.

Ronaldo had, predictably, been a key topic in the press conference. While Jesus acknowledged he “made a mistake” asking Ronaldo to warm up for 30 minutes, also insisting reports of his captain refusing to train were wide of the mark, he made it abundantly clear who was calling the shots.
“I can say to any player that you’re starting on the bench,” he said. “If I need you for 30 minutes, you’re going to play; if I don’t need you, you’re not going to play.
“The way I was reading the game [against Norway], [Ronaldo] didn’t come on. Because it’s not Cristiano, just like it will never be any player that will change my ideas as the coach. Never.
“Not him, not anyone in football. Not him, not anyone, not any president. Never. Zero.”

Could Jesus have taken a softer approach? Perhaps, but there’s also a strong argument Portugal have required a coach with such a personality for a long time, someone with the conviction and bravery to make tough – maybe even controversial – decisions.

Fernando Santos had seemingly paved the way for Ronaldo to be phased out when he dropped the centre-forward for Portugal’s last-16 clash with Switzerland at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. His replacement, Gonçalo Ramos, scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 win.
But after losing to Morocco in the quarter-finals, Santos left his post and was ultimately succeeded by Roberto Martínez, under whom Ronaldo remained one of the first names on the team sheet.

He started nine of Portugal’s 10 Euro 2024 qualifying games and all five of their matches at the finals. Ronaldo was also in the line-up for five of their six qualifiers for the 2026 World Cup, plus all five of their outings at the tournament in North America as Portugal finished second in their group and made it only as far as the last 16.

Ronaldo did, in fairness, have a good goalscoring record under Martínez, but long before he was hired there’d been debates about whether the former Real Madrid and Manchester United forward offered enough to the wider team to justify starting so often. In a modern age where out-of-possession intensity and pressing are almost sacrosanct, deploying a player who contributes little to that is a luxury few teams can afford against the best opposition. And those who can must build a team capable of shouldering the extra workload, like Argentina did for many years, successfully, with Lionel Messi.
Against Spain at the 2026 World Cup, Ronaldo had just 19 touches in 90 minutes, and none of those came after the 80th minute despite the game being 0-0 until stoppage time.

A few days earlier, however, Martínez had withdrawn Ronaldo – much to his apparent displeasure – in the 81st minute against Croatia with the score 1-1. Ramos had been introduced a little earlier, but with Ronaldo out of the way, he became the focal point of the attack and scored a dramatic late winner to send Portugal through.

Who’s to say the outcome against Spain would have been any different had Ramos (or anyone else for that matter) started instead of Ronaldo, though it was peculiar he didn’t get on at all, even if Martínez was reserving him for 30 minutes of extra-time that never materialised as Spain scored a late winner. It felt like the Portugal coach failed to heed a valuable lesson from the Croatia game.

6F718B35260A7493149F46D91A9FD8A3.title: Preview: Liverpool face in-form Brighton at Anfield
6F718B35260A7493149F46D91A9FD8A3.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Liverpool face in-form Brighton at AnfieldShareBrighton can cause yet another upset this weekend as the high-flying Seagulls make a trip to Merseyside to take on Liverpool on Sunday.

The Reds have had a strange start to the season. You’d be hard pressed to find anyone who would say Andoni Iraola’s side have been great and yet they’ve lost just once across all competitions. And their 3-0 defeat to Manchester City arrived in difficult circumstances after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off. They drew their opening two matches against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest but other than those three games, the Reds have triumphed in every other outing.

Iraola’s men have a knack for coming from behind this season to claim points. They fell behind twice against Newcastle to salvage a point and did the same against Nottingham Forest. Overturned a 1-0 deficit in wins over Atlético Madrid and Brentford before coming from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal 4-3 last time out.

Perhaps surprisingly, Liverpool have the third best defensive record in terms of Expected Goals Against. They rank eighth for xG and they’ve been underperforming in attack despite having three £100million forwards in Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz.
They’re facing one of the most in-form teams in Europe right now.

Brighton lead the way for goals scored in the Premier League this season with 23. They’ve also conceded the joint fewest goals (five). They’re bossing it at both ends of the pitch. As a result, only Arsenal (18) and Manchester City (21) have taken more points than the Seagulls (16).

Their only defeat of the season in the English top-flight arrived in August when they fell to a 4-3 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Still, it’s a game they scored three times in. Fabian Hürzeler’s side have 16 goals in their last five games in the Premier League too. The goals are flying in at an alarming rate.
They rank second for Expected Goals and top for Big Chances. They’ve kept the most clean sheets (five) and have the third highest possession average (60%). The Seagulls mean business.

For the Reds, all eyes will be on Rio Ngumoha. He changed the game off of the bench against Brentford last weekend and then ran riot against Villarreal in mid-week, notching two assists and completing nine of his 10 attempted dribbles. With Víctor Muñoz a doubt, expect the 18-year-old to start on the right for the Reds. Especially with momentum on his side.

For the visitors, it has to be Pascal Groß. The 35-year-old has the joint-most assists (four) and only Erling Haaland and João Pedro (both on eight) have more goal involvements than him this season. He’s the main man for the Seagulls. Everything good they do revolves around him and if he can pull the strings at Anfield, they’re in for a positive result.

The hosts are without Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai. Muñoz missed the game against Villarreal but could be back for the game at Anfield. He probably won’t be risked from the start though.
The away side have issues too. They’re without Yankuba Minteh, Stefanos Tzimas, Femi Azeez, Mats Wieffer, Kaoru Mitoma and Evan Ferguson.
We’re going with a 2-2 draw. The Reds keep finding ways to pick up points and despite the injuries, their attack still looks like it can cause problems.

6a120odjg59w1wmpjbecxi0ap.title: Allegri says Napoli need run of victories coming out of international break
6a120odjg59w1wmpjbecxi0ap.subtitle: Napoli have made an inconsistent start to their first campaign under Massimiliano Allegri, and they host Frosinone coming out of the hiatus.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri says Napoli need to produce a run of victories coming out of the international break, with Saturday's meeting with Frosinone kickstarting a congested schedule.
Napoli are ninth in Serie A five games into their first campaign under Allegri, having drawn 1-1 with Fiorentina in their most recent match.
Their two defeats this term came in back-to-back games, against fellow title hopefuls Inter and Como, and the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 3% chance of winning the Scudetto.

6hu2ov9cwc3d1hx0xwcnri4jc.title: Emery determined to turn home advantage into first Villa Park win
6hu2ov9cwc3d1hx0xwcnri4jc.subtitle: Aston Villa have not tasted victory at Villa Park so far in 2026-27, but Unai Emery wants that to change against Fenerbahce.
paragraphs: Unai Emery is determined to turn around Aston Villa's home form and pick up their first victory at Villa Park this season against Fenerbahce in the Champions League.
Across all competitions this season, Villa have won three games – one in the Premier League, one in the EFL Cup and one in the Champions League – but they have all come away from home.
At Villa Park, they have picked up just one point, drawing 2-2 with Brentford last time out following back-to-back losses.

But Villa have won each of their last 10 European home matches – only twice this century has an English side had a longer home winning run in major European competition: 12-game streaks by Manchester City (2022-2024) and Manchester United (2006-2008).

There is currently building work taking place in the North Stand at Villa Park, meaning fewer supporters are in the ground, but Emery is confident the rest of the crowd will make up for those missing.
"Our handicap is fewer supporters for the situation, but the club decided it; it is something to improve us for the future," Emery said.
"We must try to be together, and without 7,000 supporters we must push everyone. We must play better football, compete better than we did, be more focused than we did.

"We are realistic about how we are working and improving things. But it is not enough yet, so we are having lots of conversations with the team, in meetings and with videos, practising too, to show improvements in matches.

"At Villa Park, we have not won yet, so it is very important how we can improve things to be closer to winning. It is a very good opportunity to do one step forward in those improvements and the players as well, to get confidence and feel comfortable.
"Villa Park is for us something very, very special. It should be like the four years that we are here – how we achieved this as a special place, our fortress. It is a new challenge to show it."
Villa have won all three of their meetings with Fenerbahce to date, with the most recent of those coming earlier this year: a 1-0 away win in the Europa League in January.
Only against Bologna (4/4) do the Villans have a better 100% record than they do against Fenerbahce.
But injuries have also hindered Villa's start to 2026-27, with Matteo Ruggeri added to that list after he came off at half-time against Brentford.
Ian Maatsen also remains out, leaving a gap at left-back, though summer signing Leon Goretzka could make his debut, having recovered from a knee injury to be in the squad.
"There are negative ways for some players, because they are injured like Ruggeri," Emery added.
"We must try to find solutions as Maatsen is not available. I think he should be in a few days, one week or two weeks joining us.
"Ruggeri, we don't know exactly how long it's going to be, but it will be some weeks that he's going to be out, more than one month.
"Leon Goretzka is in the squad; George Hemmings is still being with a small pain – not [available], but maybe on Saturday he can come back."

6i3c6t3qbebm1hu2np4w6844x.title: Bologna 1-3 Inter: Chivu’s side go top after brilliant turnaround
6i3c6t3qbebm1hu2np4w6844x.subtitle: Inter came from behind to defeat Bologna 3-1 on Saturday, moving them three points clear at the Serie A summit.
paragraphs: Inter moved to the top of Serie A after coming from behind to beat Bologna 3-1 at Stadio Renato Dall'Ara on Saturday.
Cristian Chivu’s side piled the pressure on second-placed Lazio ahead of their clash with Juventus on Sunday, with Marcus Thuram, Carlos Augusto and Ange-Yoan Bonny all on target.

Bologna made a dream start inside 10 minutes as Juan Miranda dispossessed Luis Henrique before picking out Tommaso Pobega, who surged past Inter's defence and rifled a sensational effort beyond Josep Martinez at the near post.
The hosts were dealt a blow on the half-hour mark when Roberto Piccoli was forced off through injury, though that did little to disrupt Raffaele Palladino's side.
Pobega continued to threaten, going close to doubling his tally in the 40th minute after Nicolo Cambiaghi's strike was parried into his path, only for his follow-up to rattle the top of the crossbar.

That miss proved costly just four minutes later as Inter levelled the scores through a delightfully simple move involving an unmarked Thuram, who rose highest to nod Nicolo Barella’s pinpoint cross into the top corner.

Bologna goalkeeper Lukasz Skorupski was then called into action to prevent Inter from completing a swift turnaround before the break, reacting sharply to tip Francesco Pio Esposito's header over the bar.
Inter continued to build on their momentum after the break, with Esposito failing to make the most of a close-range chance before Petar Sucic sent a tame effort straight into Skorupski’s hands.

Those missed chances proved mere warning signs, though, as substitute Carlos Augusto completed the turnaround in the 69th minute, less than a minute after coming on, tapping home at the back post from Piotr Zielinski's centre.
Sucic then squandered a golden opportunity to put the result beyond doubt after Bonny's effort was parried into his path, only for him to strike the outside of the post.
Bonny thought he had added a third in the 82nd minute after drifting past Matteo Darmian and beating Skorupski, only for his effort to be ruled out for offside.
The Ivorian was not to be denied, though, as he put the result beyond doubt less than a minute later, thumping Carlos Augusto's cross past Skorupski and into the net.
Chivu’s substitutes shine in comeback win
Inter’s bid to seal back-to-back Scudetto titles has started strongly with Chivu’s side sitting comfortably in the upper reaches of the Serie A table across the opening weeks of the season.
But the Nerazzurri were handed a stern test when Pobega broke the deadlock inside 10 minutes, though they responded emphatically to maintain their unbeaten start.

Inter have now collected 19 points from their opening seven league matches for just the fourth time in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95), having previously done so in 2017-18 under Luciano Spalletti, 2002-03 under Hector Cuper, and 1997-98 under Luigi Simoni. Interestingly, though, they failed to win the Scudetto on each of those three occasions.
On this occasion, Inter were no match for Bologna in the final third, registering 3.35 expected goals (xG) to the Rossoblu’s 0.90 xG.
Chivu will be particularly pleased with the contributions of his substitutes, with Carlos Augusto and Bonny both playing decisive roles in the comeback.
The Brazilian has now contributed to three goals off the bench, with a goal and an assist against Bologna, while Bonny has found the net twice as a substitute this term.

6k2gcmpc3vm31pnvkqpp253ra.title: Isak and Gakpo both doubtful for Liverpool-Man City clash
6k2gcmpc3vm31pnvkqpp253ra.subtitle: Having withdrawn from their national squads, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo both face a battle to be fit for Liverpool's clash with Man City.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola has revealed Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo are both doubtful for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City on Sunday due to injuries they sustained on international duty.
Having made an unbeaten start to Iraola's tenure, winning two and drawing three of their first five Premier League games of 2026-27, Liverpool face an enormous test this week.
Their first game after the extended international break is against a City side who boast the Premier League's only remaining 100% record, having won five from five under Enzo Maresca.
And the Reds could be without two of their most important attacking players at Anfield.
Isak, whose four goals in all competitions are the most of any Liverpool player this term, only appeared once for Sweden during the hiatus before withdrawing from their squad due to a thigh issue.

And Gakpo, whose six combined goal involvements (two goals, four assists) are more than any of his Liverpool team-mates have managed this season, appeared in two games for the Netherlands but took a knock in the second of those, against Serbia.
Asked for updates on the duo during an interview with the club's website, Iraola said: "Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo both had to leave the national teams with injuries.
"Now it's a matter of if they are going to recover in time to help us in the next game or not. But right now, they are both injured."
The away side has won two of the last three Premier League games between Liverpool and Man City, as many times as their previous 32 meetings.
City triumphed 2-1 on Merseyside in February, but the only time there have been two consecutive away wins in the fixture in the Premier League was in 2002-03.

Sunday's clash will be the first between Liverpool and City without either Jurgen Klopp or Pep Guardiola in the dugout since March 2015, when Brendan Rodgers' Reds beat Manuel Pellegrini's Citizens 2-1 at Anfield.
But given the flying start Maresca's men have made, Iraola is anticipating a real test of his team's progress.
"I think the goal is quite clear, everyone understands what we are trying to build. To try to be more intense, more vertical, but you also want to control the games," he said.
"We've been unbeaten, but they've won all of their games, so that makes a big difference on their side.
"I think we need to be very, very good if we want to beat City, because they've been scoring a lot of goals lately. We know the names that are very dangerous.
"But I think also we've shown good defensive improvements lately, and I hope we can defend the threats that they have and also hurt them on the other side."

6lmuspwn4fw91g6o759ij8g42.title: Colombia youngsters are adapting quickly, says Lorenzo after win over Peru
6lmuspwn4fw91g6o759ij8g42.subtitle: Colombia earned their first win since James Rodriguez's retirement on Tuesday, with Nestor Lorenzo being impressed by their young players.
paragraphs: Nestor Lorenzo was impressed by the way Colombia's young players adapted during the first international break since the World Cup, which they ended with a 2-0 win over Peru.
Samuel Velasquez and Daniel Arcila both scored their first senior international goals as Lorenzo's side claimed a deserved success at Inter Miami's Nu Stadium on Tuesday.
Colombia accumulated 1.53 expected goals from their 16 shots, five of which were on target, compared to Peru failing to hit the target from five attempts with an xG value of 0.36.
Peru had substitute Miguel Araujo sent off at 1-0, as he conceded possession cheaply to Camilo Duran before hauling him down as the last man.

Lorenzo did not call up star forward Luis Diaz for the current international break, with an agreement reached with Bayern Munich to allow him to rest, while former captain James Rodriguez retired from Colombia duty last month.

And even with Tuesday's win coming off the back of a 1-1 draw with Mexico and a 1-0 defeat to Paraguay, Lorenzo believes the last few weeks have allowed Los Cafeteros to build important foundations for the future.
"I'm happy with the attitude and what has happened in these 15 days together, with the new guys," Lorenzo said after Tuesday's game.
"During the three games, we maintained a structure that allowed the youngsters to adapt.
"Sometimes that happened, sometimes it didn't, and I would have liked the football to flow a little more, especially in the first games, in which we finished badly."
Of the 26 players called up by Lorenzo, only two – Royer Caicedo and Oscar Perea – did not feature at any point across their three games.
And with home and away friendlies against Chile to come next month, the Colombia boss plans to continue experimenting.

"The balance is very positive, because even with those who did not play, we had them close to us and we saw that they have the potential to be called up at some point, when the team needs them," Lorenzo said.

6pyrf1g2k7641rccm9dl76vcw.title: Noonan thrilled with Cincinnati's morale-boosting victory in MLS double-header
6pyrf1g2k7641rccm9dl76vcw.subtitle: FC Cincinnati beat D.C. United 2-1 on Wednesday, and they are looking for a clean sweep when the sides meet again at Audi Field on Saturday.
paragraphs: Pat Noonan was thrilled FC Cincinnati got a much-needed win over D.C. United in midweek as attention now turns to the second part of their rare MLS double-header.
Cincinnati came out on top with a 2-1 victory at TQL Stadium on Wednesday, bouncing back from consecutive losses to the New England Revolution and Columbus Crew.

It put them eighth in the Eastern Conference, leaving their playoff hopes largely in their own hands, and they now travel to D.C. to try to earn a win that could potentially boost them into the automatic qualification spots.
Noonan did not shy away from the importance of the victory, but he is not ready to rest on his laurels with only four games left of the regular season.
"Like we've talked about, we needed three points, and we got that. So pleased with the group effort," he said after Wednesday's win.

6xyp8t0o0jmn1u6k76r836lkm.title: De Ketelaere reveals talks were held with PSG over summer transfer
6xyp8t0o0jmn1u6k76r836lkm.subtitle: Charles De Ketelaere was of reported interest to Paris Saint-Germain this summer, but he said a move from Atalanta failed to materialise.
paragraphs: Charles De Ketelaere revealed he came close to joining Paris Saint-Germain from Atalanta this summer, but the Ligue 1 champions instead chose to sign Ferran Torres.
De Ketelaere joined Atalanta from AC Milan permanently two years ago following a productive loan spell in 2023-24, when he scored 14 goals in 50 outings in all competitions.
Since his initial loan spell with Atalanta, only Nicolo Barella (251) and Federico Dimarco (283) have created more chances than De Ketelaere's 244 among Serie A players.

The Belgium international has amassed 63 goal contributions in that time (32 goals, 31 assists). Only Christian Pulisic (68), Marcus Thuram (75) and Lautaro Martinez (90) have managed more, with De Ketelaere's performances attracting interest.

PSG were credited with an interest in De Ketelaere this summer as they reshaped their attack, with Goncalo Ramos, Bradley Barcola, Ibrahim Mbaye, Randal Kolo Muani and Kang-in Lee all departing the Parisiens.
Atlanta named a price of €50m for De Ketelaere, but PSG were unwilling to match that valuation, instead choosing to sign Ferran from Barcelona for a reported €48.5m fee.
"Yes, I think it was around that amount," De Ketelaere confirmed. "But, we have to find a team that is willing to spend that amount.
"Several teams could do it in the Premier League, but it didn't happen. I spoke to PSG, but in the end they chose Ferran Torres.
"I'm happy at Atalanta, I know how important it is to play regularly as a starter following my time with Milan.
"I'd like to fight for titles one day. I have that ambition, but I'm only 25 and still have time."
De Ketelaere is yet to score for Atalanta in his six outings across all competitions in 2026-27, with Maurizio Sarri's side sitting 11th in Serie A heading into the international break.
He did, however, provide an assist during Belgium's 2-0 win over Italy in the Nations League on Friday, teeing up Dodi Lukebakio's 69th-minute winner at the Stadio Olimpico.

In what was Mark van Bommel's first game in charge of the Red Devils, only Kevin De Bruyne (five) created more chances than De Ketelaere (four), while the Atalanta midfielder also finished with team-high totals for successful dribbles (two), duels won (eight) and aerial duels won (two).
Belgium's Nations League campaign continues on Monday against France, with a clash against Turkiye to come before they face Zinedine Zidane's side again on October 5.

6z63q8jbc4gh1iufjqn29hn5j.title: Amorim: Milan still far from our potential
6z63q8jbc4gh1iufjqn29hn5j.subtitle: AC Milan are unbeaten in Serie A under Ruben Amorim, but the Portuguese coach knows there are still plenty of things to improve upon.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim believes AC Milan are "still far from our potential" despite making an unbeaten start to their Serie A campaign.
Milan have won three of their opening five league games in 2026-27 (D2), leaving them fifth in Serie A, two points behind leaders Roma.

Amorim (W3 D2) is only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to remain unbeaten in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.
Overall, he is the first Rossoneri manager to achieve this since Massimo Giacomini (W2 D3) in 1979-80.
However, Milan made a losing start to their Europa League campaign after a 2-0 defeat at home to Benfica.
Amorim acknowledged there are plenty of improvements needed when his squad return from the international break.
"We try to dominate the games consistently; we play well at times, but there's still a lot of work to do," Amorim told Sky Sport Italia.
"I don't like to hear people talk about this Milan as Amorim’s Milan. Milan is Milan.
"The club has a story and an identity that go beyond a coach’s name. I want to see a team with an identity that can win even when things don’t run perfectly.
"We are still far from our potential, but we need time and continuity. We have many games, we must win and improve at the same time, it's not easy.
"Many things are missing; I can say it without any problem. I think we have to improve as a team to create more chances."
Milan face Sassuolo in their first Serie A game after the extended international break before taking on Salzburg in the Europa League.

72h16gdzvilm19yxyshhdmad2.title: Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle United: Osula and Barnes seal return to winning ways
72h16gdzvilm19yxyshhdmad2.subtitle: After a tepid first half showing, Newcastle United stunned Selhurst Park after the break to secure a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace.
paragraphs: Newcastle United climbed up to seventh in the Premier League table as they earned a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace to put their recent losing run behind them.
After back-to-back league defeats against Coventry City and Aston Villa, Newcastle did the damage in the second half through strikes from William Osula and Harvey Barnes.

Palace, however, started well and came close to taking the lead after three minutes. Adam Wharton chipped a dangerous cross from a free-kick, sparking a scramble in front of goal as Jean-Philippe Mateta twice tried to bundle home, only to be denied by Lukas Hornicek's sharp reflexes.

Spurred on by a lively Selhurst Park crowd, the hosts continued to push forward, registering eight shots inside the opening 26 minutes – their most in the first half of a Premier League match this season – though Mateta, Daichi Kamada and Dwight McNeil could not properly test Hornicek.
Yeremy Pino proved a threat just before the break, darting an inviting cross into the box that just narrowly evaded the onrushing Axel Disasi before Hornicek was able to smother.

Pierre Sage's side were quickly made to regret spurning those chances as the Magpies emerged from the break a different side, taking the lead in the 47th minute through Osula, who powered home first-time off a pinpoint Jacob Murphy cross.

Willock thought he had put Newcastle further ahead six minutes later as he raced onto Joelinton's weighted through-ball and slid a tidy finish past Walter Benitez, but the goal was ruled out for offside against the Magpies' midfielder after a VAR review.

After consistent pressure, the visitors eventually found their second through a superb attacking move – Nico Gonzalez held up the ball strongly before finding Amar Dedic, who teed up Barnes in space for an emphatic finish into the left corner.
Palace began to show signs of life midway through the second half, with Wharton testing Hornicek with a curling effort just past the hour mark.

The Newcastle goalkeeper was called upon again moments later, diving at full stretch to keep out a swerving, long-range strike from Dario Osorio to secure three points and preserve the Magpies' clean sheet.
Magpies flex their muscles in the second half

Newcastle might not have got off to a superb start to the season, but Sunday's victory could provide the spark for a turnaround, with the Magpies producing a clinical second-half display to take all three points.
Osula continued his fine form, taking his tally to seven goals in his last 13 Premier League appearances, having managed just two in his first 50 matches in the competition.

Murphy also made his mark, registering his 31st Premier League assist for Newcastle with the opener. That moved him level with Robert Lee in joint-third on the club's all-time list in the competition, behind only Nolberto Solano (54) and Alan Shearer (35).

Barnes was another standout performer. Since the start of last season, he has been involved in 12 Premier League goals (nine goals, three assists), with only Bruno Guimaraes (14) registering more for Newcastle in that period.

The visitors were ruthlessly efficient in front of goal, scoring with both of their shots on target. Remarkably, Newcastle have now converted 100% of their shots on target in three of their last four Premier League matches in which they have scored at least twice, doing so against Palace, Bournemouth and Tottenham.

For Palace, meanwhile, the defeat will only add to the pressure on Sage. The Eagles have now conceded 50 Premier League goals in 2026, at least four more than any other side in the competition, though they did register an expected goals (xG) total of 1.69 from their 17 shots, but only four of those were on target.

          Possession Is No Longer Nine Tenths of the Law in the Premier League
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Teams with less possession are winning more often than they’re losing in the Premier League. Is this just a quirk or is there something deeper to the numbers?
We check the stats after a game, and if one team has had considerably more possession than the other and lost, we raise a quizzical eyebrow wondering how on earth that happened.

The best teams have more of the ball, right? The more possession you have, the more opportunities you have to create chances and score, and for a long time, that was broadly borne out in results in the Premier League.
We have seen the pendulum swing a bit in recent times, though. Having less possession than your opponent might actually now be more conducive to winning in England’s top flight.

Opta has detailed Premier League possession data since the start of the 2005-06 season, and it was a surprise to see what occurred in that first year of recorded numbers. In the 2005-06 campaign, 149 games were won by the team who had more than 50% possession, but 152 were won by the team with less than 50% possession.

Of course, in a match where the split was something like 51-49%, the difference is minimal so you can’t hang your hat on that too much, but looking at games where one team had at least 55% of the ball, it was still 80 wins to 77 in favour of teams who had less than 45%.
However, the next 19 seasons saw teams with more possession win more games than those with less.

You can see from the graph below that it has tended to work in cycles. After every season when the number of wins evened out, it then swung back to favouring those with more of the ball. That was until last season, which followed the 2024-25 campaign in which wins for teams with more/less possession was broadly even. In 2025-26, though, the trend carried on and saw more teams with lower possession win games for the first time since 2005-06.

Across the 2025-26 Premier League campaign, 137 games were won by teams with over 50% of the ball, while 139 were won by teams with less than 50%. Again, though, you could argue those numbers might be skewed by games where there is minimal difference in possession.

However, 83 were won by teams with over 55% possession, and 89 were won by teams with under 45%; also, the first time there were more wins for under 45% possession than over 55% since the 2005-06 season.

This season, there has been an even split between games won by teams with over/under 50% possession (17-17), though 15 of those won by teams with a minority of possession were done with less than 45%. Only 12 of those won by teams with more possession were won with over 55%.
So, are we seeing a change in approach in England’s top flight, or is it just our good friend, variance?

It could be argued some of it is simply due to teams who take the lead then naturally having less of the ball as they try to cling on to victory, but then that would also have been the case in previous seasons when the numbers were vastly different.

You cannot talk about possession trends in the Premier League without mentioning the profound impact of Pep Guardiola. Not that teams didn’t dominate the ball prior to his arrival in England, but the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss certainly took it up a notch.

Between 2005-06 and the Spanish coach’s first season in the Premier League with Manchester City in 2016-17, there had only been four instances of a team averaging at least 60% possession across a PL campaign (Chelsea – 60.2% in 2008-09, Arsenal – 60.0% in 2010-11, Arsenal – 60.1% in 2011-12, Manchester United – 61.4% in 2014-15). In each of the first eight seasons after Guardiola joined City, there were at least three teams who did so.

During his 10 seasons at Man City, there were 28 total instances of a team averaging over 60% possession over a full campaign (including all 10 for City). However, only City themselves managed it in 2024-25 and 2025-26, which may have been a factor in Pep deciding to leave at the end of last season, seeing the direction of travel in style of play.

After five matchdays of this season, though, City, Brighton and Tottenham are all averaging over 60% possession. That could of course change with more games, and bottom-place Spurs are certainly proving that having lots of the ball isn't the be all and end all.

It’s still early in 2026-27, but of the 50 games we’ve had, 22 have had a team record at least 60% possession; on only eight occasions has that side gone on to win. That equates to a win rate of just 36.4%, the third lowest in a Premier League season on record for teams with that much possession, and follows last season’s record-low rate of 34.1%.
Since the start of 2005-06, there have been 1,470 Premier League games won by teams who had at least 60% possession, 263 of which were Manchester City (17.9%).

And that’s something to consider. Some of the numbers around the decade of Guardiola’s dominant City could perhaps skew these stats a bit as they account for a significant number of Premier League matches where a team had over 60% possession in that time. While Guardiola was at City, there were 862 Premier League games won by a team who had over 60% possession, 205 of which were City (23.8%), almost a quarter.

          Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth Stats: Michael Carrick on the Brink After Another Thumping Loss
        
      
                          
                      Oct 25, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick appears to be on borrowed time after falling to a heavy home defeat to Bournemouth.
Evanilson's stunning second-half strike capped a memorable Premier League win for Bournemouth at Manchester United to pile even more pressure on Michael Carrick.

Rayan and Marcus Tavernier scored in five first-half minutes to put United – who left captain Bruno Fernandes on the bench – on the back foot, leading to boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time.

Evanilson then had a goal disallowed from the kick-off, but he got his goal later on, rounding Senne Lammens to finish brilliant into the empty net from out wide and extend United's winless run to eight games in all competitions.
Bournemouth started on the front foot without testing Lammens, as Rayan and Evanilson both sent headers wide either side of Diogo Dalot blazing over the bar at the other end.
Ayden Heaven threw himself into a dangerous tackle – luckily without making contact with Evanilson – to give away a free-kick, which led to Bournemouth's 38th-minute opener.

7 – Manchester United have won just seven points from eight Premier League games this season (W1 D4 L3), their lowest at this stage of a league season since 1986-87 (4).Nightmare. pic.twitter.com/9IpGCx77xo

Justin Kluivert whipped his right-sided set-piece to the far post, and Rayan was completely unmarked to drill it past Lammens into the bottom-right corner to end his nine-game goal drought in the league.

Bryan Mbeumo was denied by Djordje Petrovic as United sought an equaliser, and Bournemouth doubled their lead in the 43rd minute. Adrien Truffert profited from an untimely Leny Yoro slip to tee up Tavernier to tap into an empty net.
Things almost got even worse 21 seconds after the break when a loose Harry Maguire pass was cut out by Tavernier on the edge of the box, but Evanilson was offside when he slotted in.
United tried to make their possession count in the second half, but Mbeumo fired just over on the turn before Lisandro Martínez's low fizzer was comfortably held by Petrovic.

But Bournemouth still remained a threat on the break, as they proved in the 71st minute. Lewis Cook went long, and Lammens was not quick enough to get there before Evanilson, who curled a stunning effort into the unguarded net from out on the right wing.
Andrey Santos saw a header blocked on the line, while Mason Mount saw a tame shot saved in stoppage time as Bournemouth easily held out for a clean sheet.
After Fernandes seemingly criticised Carrick's tactics in midweek, he was named on the bench for a Premier League game for only the sixth time, and the first since May 2025 against Brentford.
In fact, it is the first time Carrick has not named the club captain in his starting line-up in the top flight since he got the caretaker job in January (this is his 27th such game in charge).

It was a must-win game for United, who remain with just one league victory to their name this term (D4 L3), and they have triumphed in just one of their last 11 outings without Fernandes in the starting line-up (D3 L7).

Nothing should take away from Bournemouth's performance, though, as they became just the third side to score 2+ goals in four consecutive Premier League away games against United, after Manchester City (2011-12 – 2014-15) and Brighton (2022-23 – 2025-26).

3 – This is the third time that Bournemouth gone 3-0 up in a Premier League game at Old Trafford (also in December 2023 and December 2024).Only Liverpool and Man City have done so as many times in the competition (3).Dreamers. pic.twitter.com/6EO4byrwCw
Rayan's first top-flight goal of the season opened the scoring, and he led the team throughout, having five of Bournemouth's 10 shots, and it paid off as he got his first league goal of the season.
Bournemouth look to be hitting their stride after three straight wins, while United cannot escape the spotlight, having failed to take any of their 17 chances.

          Everton vs Newcastle Prediction: EFL Cup Fourth Round Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 28, 2026
          
                      Jonathan Davies / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Thursday's EFL Cup fourth-round clash at Hill Dickinson Stadium with our Everton vs Newcastle prediction and preview. Can the Magpies reach their fifth straight quarter-final?
Newcastle United bid to reach their fifth consecutive EFL Cup quarter-final when they face Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
This is the first of two showdowns between the sides in less than a week, with the pair due to reconvene at St James' Park in the Premier League on Monday.
The EFL Cup has provided Newcastle with some wonderful memories in recent seasons, as well as a welcome distraction from their domestic endeavours.

Eddie Howe led the Magpies to the 2022-23 final, where they were beaten 2-0 by Manchester United. However, they were not to be denied two years later, beating Liverpool 2-1 at Wembley in 2024-25 to finally end their 70-year major silverware drought.

Newcastle's gallant defence of the trophy was ended by Manchester City in last season's semi-finals, and they have started this campaign with a pair of narrow victories over Championship sides West Bromwich Albion (3-2) and Millwall (1-0).

Since the start of the 2022-23 season, the Magpies have won 18 ties in the EFL Cup, six more than any other team during that span. To put that into perspective, their 18 previous wins came over a period of 14 years between 2008-09 and 2021-22.

Newcastle have also won their last seven ties in the EFL Cup fourth round. They were last unsuccessful at this stage in the 2013-14 season, with Manuel Pellegrini's Man City beating them 2-0 after extra-time at St James' Park on their way to eventually lifting the trophy.
Matthias Jaissle's side go into the tie fresh from a 2-0 victory over a struggling Crystal Palace on Sunday as they got back to winning ways after back-to-back defeats.
Jaissle is waiting on the fitness of Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Miley for this game, though will definitely be without Tino Livramento and Ewen Jaouen.
Everton, meanwhile, will hope Jack Grealish has recovered from a virus, and that Jarrad Branthwaite is available after concussion.
Both were absent on Saturday for what was Everton's second 2-0 defeat in as many weekends, as they were beaten by reigning champions Arsenal.
David Moyes' side previously saw their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign ended by Pedro Neto's brace against Chelsea, though they are yet to concede a goal in this season's EFL Cup.
The Toffees opened with a 4-0 rout of Preston North End, including a Thierno Barry hat-trick, before edging out Wolves 1-0 in round three.

Yet Moyes has endured mixed fortunes in the fourth round of this competition. Everton have only progressed to the quarter-finals once in seven fourth round ties under his tutelage, doing so when they beat Luton Town in 2007-08.

Furthermore. his side have been eliminated from seven of his last 10 EFL Cup ties against Premier League opposition, though two of the three he progressed from were in round four. Both came during his time at West Ham, who he guided to victories over Man City (in 2021-22) and Arsenal (2023-24).
This will only be the second time the two sides have faced off in the EFL Cup.
Their only previous encounter – in round three of the 2002-03 competition – brought a six-goal thriller at St James' Park, playing out an entertaining 3-3 draw after 120 minutes of play.

Moyes, in the first full season of his maiden spell in charge, saw his side twice come from behind to force a penalty shootout, where Richard Wright saved from Hugo Viana and Laurent Robert as the Toffees prevailed 3-2.

Yet Newcastle, who were 4-1 winners at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last November, could record successive away victories over Everton for the first time since a run of three straight successes between 1958 and 1960.

77z0rr8atbgg16z4f6an1e0na.title: Spalletti determined to keep Juve's opponents guessing after change of formation
77z0rr8atbgg16z4f6an1e0na.subtitle: Luciano Spalletti wants to keep Juventus' opponents on their toes, having been flexible with his tactical setup in recent matches.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti believes Juventus must remain tactically flexible after switching from a 4-2-3-1 formation to a back-three system, ahead of Wednesday's trip to Genoa in Serie A.
Juve have not won back-to-back matches since the first two games of this Serie A campaign, though they have an opportunity to do just that following Sunday's 2-0 success at Lecce.
Having deployed a back four in the opening four games of Juve's campaign, Spalletti has used a back three for five of their last seven.
But he says Juve's tweaks have been more subtle than they might appear and plans on alternating between the two shapes in the future.
"This is a good setup, and it starts from the evaluation of our players, but it doesn't make us forget the composition of our squad," Spalletti said, as quoted by Football Italia.
"We can't penalise those who have a different set of characteristics – a small rotation is all that is needed for it to become a 3-4-2-1, and anyone can fit into the two.
"Randal Kolo Muani can play in that space and almost be like an attacking midfielder or an outside forward. He's one of those players.
"It's a solution that is designed to take us into the future, not to just play these games or to try and motivate one or two players.
"When some people said that the group requested this approach, that is something that is not up to the players."
While Juve are seventh in Serie A going into the midweek slate of fixtures, Genoa are 16th, having earned just their second victory of the season against Venezia last time out.
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Genoa – Mikael Ellertsson
Ellertsson has scored one of his four Serie A goals against Juventus, netting for Venezia on December 14, 2024.

The Genoa midfielder has already equalled his goal involvement tally from the whole of last season (one goal, one assist in 36 games for Genoa) in just eight Serie A appearances this term (one goal, one assist).
Juventus – Bremer
Bremer scored his first Serie A goal against Genoa at the Ferraris in November 2019, while playing for Torino.

Genoa are one of the Brazilian's favourite opponents in the competition (three goals, level with Cagliari) and are also one of two teams against whom he has won the most matches in the Italian top flight (seven, level with Sassuolo).
MATCH PREDICTION – JUVENTUS WIN
Juventus have won more Serie A games against Genoa than they have versus any other side, with 71 victories, compared to 22 for Genoa and 23 draws in 116 matches.
Furthermore, Juve have also scored more goals against Genoa in the competition than any other team (233).

Juventus have not repeated the same result in their last eight away Serie A games (W4 D3 L1) and, after their win against Lecce, they could win consecutive away league games for the first time since March and April 2026 (against Udinese and Atalanta on that occasion).
Genoa have won two of their last three Serie A matches (L1), as many victories as they managed in their previous 14 games in the competition (D3 L9), but they are up against it here.

Genoa have lost their two most recent home Serie A matches against Juventus without scoring, and they could suffer three consecutive home defeats against the Bianconeri for only the third time, after doing so between 1958 and 1960 and between 1949 and 1953.

          Leeds vs Man Utd Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 16, 2026
          
                      Tom Webber / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to this Premier League match at Elland Road with our Leeds vs Man Utd prediction and preview.
Manchester United will aim to dispel some of the dark clouds hanging over the club when they travel to rivals Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday.
The Red Devils are in the midst of yet another tumultuous period after Lisandro Martínez‘s comments following their 2-0 loss to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead within a minute and, after Leny Yoro was shown a red card in the 74th minute, Ademola Lookman made it five games in all competitions without a win for Michael Carrick's side.
“We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete,” Martínez told Amazon Prime. “I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox].”
The Argentina international issued an apology on Thursday after meeting with the club's leadership, but the episode has put an even sharper focus on his team's dismal start to the season.
Carrick's men have just six points from as many Premier League games this season, which is their lowest at this stage since 1986-87 under Ron Atkinson (4).
And just like last season, they have not managed to keep a clean sheet in their first six games – the first time that has happened in successive campaigns since 1930-31 and 1931-32.

A key factor in Man Utd's struggles has been a dip in form for Bruno Fernandes. The club captain has not been involved in a goal in any of his past four appearances – his longest such run since a seven-match stretch that ended in May 2025.
Fernandes has, however, played a part in nine goals in seven top-flight appearances against Leeds (6 goals, 3 assists), so he will hope to recapture his form when the teams meet at Elland Road.

Leeds have turned Elland Road into a fortress, though. They are unbeaten there in seven games in the Premier League, a run that stretches back to a 1-0 loss to Sunderland on 3 March. The last time they went on a longer unbeaten run at Elland Road was a 15-game streak in 2001.
Daniel Farke's side also impressed away from home in their previous outing, taking the lead against reigning Premier League champions Arsenal before succumbing to a 2-1 defeat.

Despite that loss, Leeds (7th) go into a meeting with the Red Devils (13th) while ahead of them in the Premier League table for the first time since September 2002 (excluding MD1), when they won 1-0 at Elland Road.
A win for Leeds would put them six points clear of their rivals after seven games or more for just the second time – they were seven points ahead in December 2001 after playing 15 games.

Man Utd will hope to have Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw available for selection after they sat out against Atlético, but all eyes will be on whether Martínez retains his place in the centre of defence after apologising publicly for his comments. Yoro being banned for the trip to Como in the Champions League next Wednesday also gives Carrick a footballing reason to leave the Argentine out of the side.
Noussair Mazraoui and Benjamin Sesko could be in contention to return, but Manuel Ugarte and Patrick Dorgu remain long-term absentees.
Leeds are expected to still be without Joe Rodon and Daniel James.
Leeds ended a run of 10 winless Premier League games against rivals United with a 2-1 win at Old Trafford in April thanks to Okafor's double.
Farke's men will now look to secure consecutive league wins over their rivals for the first time since winning both games in the 1971-72 campaign.
The Red Devils are unbeaten in their last seven away games against Leeds (W5 D2), though, with their previous defeat a 1-0 loss in the Premier League in September 2002.

          Man Utd Defence Showed Some Fight at Leeds, But Its Makeup Supports Martínez Rant
        
      
                          
                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It was nowhere near perfect, but Manchester United's draw at Leeds in the Premier League on Sunday saw them show some fight at the end of a taxing week.
At the end of a long week for Manchester United, a trip to Leeds United and Elland Road was the last thing many would think they needed.
Or maybe it was exactly what their situation required?

Last weekend’s dismal draw with struggling 10-man Tottenham was followed in midweek by a 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid. And while the display in Madrid actually wasn’t that bad, the fallout from it plunged United deeper into crisis.
The Argentina defender publicly criticised United’s decision makers in multiple television interviews, most vociferously in an extraordinary exchange on Prime Video.

Among his quotes was this particularly incendiary targeting of United’s technical director, Jason Wilcox: “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”
Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 pic.twitter.com/OGo25Pzd30

The actual content of Martínez’s comments – those above and the rest of the interview – largely resonated with a fanbase who’ve little love for those in charge at the club. But the centre-back was criticised for his timing, with the subsequent circus ultimately a key subject of focus for Carrick in the build-up to the trip to Elland Road, a difficult journey at the best of times.
It was also noted by many that his outburst came during easily his worst run of form personally since joining the club in 2022.

A public apology from Martínez drew a line under the matter, at least officially, and he was named in United’s starting XI on Sunday. Whether that would’ve been the case had the club actually strengthened to the degree he seemingly desired is another matter, but the fact is Carrick didn’t have much choice.

Most have perceived Martínez’s comments to have referenced a lack of investment in defence. After all, the Atlético defeat saw centre-back Ayden Heaven make his Champions League debut at left-back, a position he’d never started a senior game in. He was doing so because Luke Shaw and his deputy, Patrick Dorgu – also not a nominal left-back – were out injured.
And, fittingly, there were more defensive selection issues on Sunday.
Centre-back Leny Yoro started at right-back; right-back Diogo Dalot started at left-back; Martínez was taken off at half-time due to injury.
United finished the game with a back four (going from right to left) of Yoro, Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Dalot; only one of the four was playing in what you’d call their natural position.
As it happened, though, United’s defence deserved praise for the fight they put up in difficult circumstances and against a good, in-form Leeds side. That goes for Martínez, too.

There’ll have been more eyes than usual on him, and having seen Tottenham's Dominic Solanke cause him so much trouble last weekend, it wasn’t surprising to see Leeds target him a couple of times early on with Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
But Martínez made some timely tackles and came out on top in a couple of physical duels. It was a blow to lose him at the break.
Yoro acquitted himself well, not for the first time this term, tucking inside as Leeds lumped numerous crosses in from their right, with the Frenchman clearing nearly all of them.

His eight clearances over the 90 minutes was his second most in a league game for United (second only to tallying 9 vs Leeds in April), and he helped keep Noah Okafor – who scored twice at Old Trafford last term – very quiet.

Dalot, a regular source of frustration among fans, came out with credit, too. Although clearly uncomfortable attacking on his left foot, he showed a willingness to get forward and one of United’s few bright moments in the second half came via solo burst through the middle following a corner.
