          Premier League Match Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer's Picks for This Week
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author, Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our Premier League match predictions for Matchday 8 of the 2026-27 season.
The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season, with the table taking shape.

With seven wins from seven, Manchester City sit top of the Premier League table and are the only team left in the competition yet to lose a game this term after their 3-2 win over Ipswich Town last Saturday.

Everton were beaten by Chelsea, and Brentford suffered a late loss to Liverpool as their unbeaten starts came to an end, while there were also first wins of the campaign for Fulham, Bournemouth and Tottenham.
Reigning champions Arsenal edged past Nottingham Forest to stay three points behind City, and Brighton continue to impress after their 5-0 thrashing of Crystal Palace.
But who can make moves up the table this weekend? Matchday 8 sees fixtures take place across Friday, Saturday and Sunday in a bumper weekend.
Ahead of what should be another exciting group of Premier League fixtures, let's check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.
The action begins at Portman Road on Friday, as Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest both aim to get back to winning ways.

Forest have lost their last three Premier League games, more than they had in their previous 14 (W5 D7 L2), and have drawn a blank in four different matches this season, including last time out against Arsenal.

Ipswich won their first two Premier League games against Forest in the 1992-93 season, but they have since lost all four against them, though our predictive model suggests they will end that run, with a 43.2% win probability.

Forest, who have a 30.1% chance of victory, won 4-2 on their last visit to Ipswich in 2024-25, but have not won on consecutive league visits since 2010-11 and 2011-12 in the Championship. At 26.7%, this is one of the most likely draws of the weekend, though, so a stalemate could be on the cards.

Onto Saturday, and Aston Villa will be the next team to try and end Manchester City’s perfect start, after Enzo Maresca made history last weekend by becoming the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a club.

City could become the eighth side to win each of their first eight games of an English top-flight season, after Everton in 1894-95 (first eight), Sheffield United in 1903-04 (eight), Tottenham in 1960-61 (11), Manchester United in 1985-86 (10), Liverpool in 1990-91 (eight), Chelsea in 2005-06 (nine), and Liverpool in 2019-20 (eight).
And with a 43.2% win probability, they are the most likely away winners of the weekend.

However, City – who thrashed AEK Athens 5-1 in the UEFA Champions League in midweek – have lost their last two league games against Villa, last losing three straight to them between August 1962 and September 1966.

Villa, whose win probability sits at 31.6%, are unbeaten in their last three home league games against sides starting top of the table (W2 D1), while they are in good form, having won two of their last three league games (D1) and beaten Viking 3-1 in the Champions League.
Arsenal will be waiting to pounce on any potential Man City slip-up, so they’ll be determined to walk away with three points against Everton.

The Gunners, who battled back to draw 2-2 with Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday, won 69.6% of the supercomputer’s simulations and are the most likely winners of the weekend. They are also unbeaten in their last seven league matches against Everton (W5 D2).

Arsenal have won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games (L1), winning all six at the Emirates Stadium in that run, while their defensive record continues to impress; no side has conceded fewer league goals than them (5), while they’ve also faced fewer shots on target (21) and have a lower xGA figure (5.6) than any other side.
Everton were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea last time out to end their unbeaten start, and are winless in their last eight away league games (D5 L3), with all three on the road this season ending level.

          Arsenal’s WSL Season is in Peril, But Can They Find Answers?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 21, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal’s season is threatening to unravel, with defensive frailties, a blunt attack and increasingly puzzling selection decisions leaving Renée Slegers under growing pressure. Can the Dutch coach find the answers, or do the problems run deeper than results suggest?

The noise around Renée Slegers is becoming impossible to drown out. Every poor result adds another decibel, and when the boos rang out at the Emirates on Saturday, the discontent was no longer confined to social media; it had reached the stands.

Arsenal’s 1–1 draw with Birmingham City, a side still searching for its first win of their new WSL era, laid bare a team short of attacking conviction and defensive authority, while becoming the second time this season that Slegers side have failed to beat newly promoted opposition at home – their longest such run against those teams in the competition. The Gunners only found any real impetus after falling behind.

The result extended their winless league run to five games, the longest in the club’s history. The irony is stark: barely three matches earlier, Arsenal had been celebrating a record 20-game unbeaten league run. Now, their season is unravelling just as quickly as it once gathered momentum.
Slegers remained composed in her post-match interview, but her words carried a significance that her demeanour concealed.

For the first time, she openly acknowledged that change might be necessary: “Everything I want is the best for us, and all the best for these players,” she said. “I think if that’s not the case anymore, then a change needs to happen. But I have belief in knowing where we can go with this team.”

The question is whether that belief is being matched by evidence on the pitch. Arsenal look increasingly susceptible defensively and toothless against low blocks. Their attacking patterns lack variation, their personnel and positional roles invite questions, and Slegers’ continued reshuffling of the starting XI raises doubts over whether she has identified a system capable of consistently getting the best out of it.

Before the international break, the Arsenal boss insisted that the title race was “not in the conversation.” Now, the more immediate concern seems to be whether Arsenal can salvage their push for Champions League qualification, with a nine-point gap to close on third-place London City Lionesses. Europe is far from a foregone conclusion and complacency is no longer an option.

The question, then, is not simply whether Slegers can turn Arsenal’s season around, but whether the problems run deeper than just results; into the team’s tactical structure, the leadership, and their ability to impose themselves on opponents. Because until Arsenal find answers to those questions, the noise is unlikely to subside.

Arsenal’s defence has been assailable at times, rarely more illustrated than the bizarre decision made by vice-captain Leah Williamson in the Champions League to handle the ball in the penalty area against Paris FC to inadvertently allow a late equaliser.

It was the second time since last season that Arsenal had failed to win a Champions League match after leading by two or more goals. They had never done so in the competition between 2001-02 and 2024-25.
Though interestingly, their defensive problems are not necessarily reflected in the volume of chances they are conceding. Instead, the concern is the quality of those opportunities.

Against Birmingham, Arsenal were exposed by fast breaks for the second consecutive game, with Ona Batlle unable to recover and Lotte Wubben-Moy failing to intercept Neve Herron's ball that split the Gunners' defence in two.

Birmingham attempted three shots from fast breaks against Arsenal; only Aston Villa, with four also against the Gunners in April 2025, have managed more in a WSL match. More concerningly, Birmingham did not win possession in Arsenal’s final third for any of those opportunities, demonstrating how effectively they could threaten from deeper positions.

Indeed, Arsenal have now conceded six shots from fast breaks this season, with only Liverpool conceding more (seven). They have also conceded two goals from such situations, the joint-most in the league alongside Liverpool and London City.
One explanation for that is their carelessness on the ball.

Arsenal are losing possession 147.8 times per game, their highest average since 2023-24 (151.4). Yet, they are facing just seven shots per game, the second-lowest average in a WSL season in their recorded history, behind only 2025-26 (6.9).
That apparent contradiction is revealing. Arsenal are not allowing opponents to shoot frequently, but their defensive lapses are proving costly when they do.

The broader expected-goals (xG) data reinforces the concern. Arsenal are conceding 0.91 expected goals against (xGA) per game, their second-highest figure after the 2024-25 campaign (0.95). Moreover, the Gunners' 0.94 expected goals on target against (xGOT) per game is also among their highest seasonal averages, while their xG per shot faced of 0.13 is a record high for the club.
Williamson’s role in this decline deserves scrutiny, although the data offers a more nuanced picture than a straightforward loss of form.

paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsManchester UnitedScores & FixturesTableLive Match UpdatesOn BBC SoundsTop ScorersWho Am I? QuizHow talking about Man Utd's cycle of doom became an industryImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Gary Neville and Michael Carrick were Manchester United and England team-mates
Manchester United. More a high-volume content farm than a football club these days.

Michael Carrick's starring role in what has become one of the nation's favourite soap operas has been extended for at least another week, with the 45-year-old set to be in charge for Saturday's visit to Chelsea.

Good news - you'd think - for Carrick. But even better news for Amazon's All or Nothing camera crews, who have been given "unprecedented" access to document the behind-the-scenes goings-on at Old Trafford this season.
United fans will presumably be relieved when the football resumes on Saturday, if only to break up the constant stream of opinion for 90 minutes.
But while the wall-to-wall reporting of one of the world's biggest football clubs is hardly new, the unrelenting coverage from former players is a growing phenomenon.

It is easier to name the Manchester United legends who don't have a platform from which they scrutinise the club's every move than those that do - and it begs the question whether the club's demise has been industrialised into a content-creating machine.
Whether supporters feel comments from ex-players are damaging or not differs from fan to fan, but what cannot be denied is how difficult it is to escape their views.

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville provided scathing on-air commentary during United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last Sunday, before conducting a post-match podcast in the Old Trafford gantry in which he accused some of their players of being unprofessional.
"There's a couple of them... I live in Manchester and they're not that professional, some of them," Neville stated.
"I've got no time for them. There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time. Don't eat the right things. Don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every single day."
But it's digital and streaming platforms that are re-defining a new age of analysis.
Neville launched The Overlap in 2021, and its success across video and podcast platforms has seen the channel become one of the most influential outlets in sports media.
On Tuesday, Wayne Rooney appeared on Neville's Manchester United-dedicated YouTube channel 'Stick to United' where he said Carrick's players "need a firework up their a***".

Neville has since hosted his own The Overlap show where he said managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good", while ex-United captain Roy Keane said Carrick and his backroom staff are "lucky boys" to still be in jobs.
Neville acquired a network of YouTube channels from United influencer Mark Goldbridge last summer, which has significantly increased the channel's coverage of the club.
Largely known for viral clips of his expletive-laden rants during streamed 'watchalongs' of their matches, Goldbridge's YouTube channels had amassed more than 3.7million subscribers.
Goldbridge - whose real name is Brent di Cesare - now co-hosts the 'Stick to United' show with Rooney, the club's record goalscorer.
But Neville, Rooney and Keane are far from the only ones setting the agenda.
Class of '92 pair Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt co-host their own podcast called 'The Good, The Bad & The Football'.

          Liverpool 0-3 Man City Stats: Premier League Leaders Respond to Guilty Verdict With Clinical Anfield Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 11, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After a turbulent two weeks, Manchester City returned to action with an emphatic 3-0 defeat of 10-man Liverpool at Anfield.
Manchester City delivered a statement of intent in their first game since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations, swatting aside 10-man Liverpool 3-0.
Sunday's contest at Anfield came amid the backdrop of the Premier League winning their case against Man City, who have appealed the result and maintain their innocence.

A vociferous home crowd jeered every touch and pass from City's players throughout, yet the league leaders demonstrated their class with a clinical, ruthless showing in the wake of Ryan Gravenberch's 62nd-minute red card.
Erling Haaland and Jérémy Doku scored in the space of three minutes, before Rayan Cherki capped off a sensational team move.
Liverpool started brightly, yet City came closest to an opener when Antoine Semenyo's drilled cross skimmed through the six-yard box.
Gianluigi Donnarumma was forced into action at the start of the second half, with Liverpool having three shots in the space of a minute.
Donnarumma denied Lewis Koumas and Gravenberch, before Alexis Mac Allister curled wide.
Haaland then spurned a brilliant chance when he was put through by Semenyo, but the match then turned as Gravenberch received a harsh, second booking for a challenge on substitute Doku.
City did not look back from there. Within three minutes, Haaland had slammed in first time after Doku's shot was deflected into his path.
Three minutes later, Doku curled a sublime finish over the top of Alisson.

Cherki added further gloss in the 78th minute, slotting home after a sensational move that involved 41 passes, which is the longest sequence resulting in a Premier League goal since Phil Foden netted against Nottingham Forest in September 2023 (46 passes).

While City lodge their appeal against the guilty verdict, all Enzo Maresca's team can do is focus on the here and now. And the here and now has them top of the Premier League, three points clear of Arsenal.
There were just two minutes and 37 seconds between Gravenberch being sent off for Liverpool and Haaland putting City 1-0 up, and it truly was a clinical showing from the visitors from then on.
Haaland has scored eight goals in his last eight appearances against Liverpool in all competitions – no other player has scored more than five goals versus the Reds since he joined City in 2022.

Doku scored his 12th Premier League goal, but only his second as a substitute (also October 2024 vs Fulham) – he is the third sub to score at Anfield for City in the competition after George Weah in September 2000 and Bernardo Silva in January 2018.
Liverpool, meanwhile, are now winless in eight in the Premier League when facing the team starting the day top of the league (D6 L2), their second-worst run behind nine matches between 2002 and 2008.
Andoni Iraola, whose unbeaten start has come to an end, may point to that dubious decision to send Gravenberch off, but overall, his team were second-best.

The Reds only registered 0.86 expected goals, with just 0.38 xG coming from open play. For a team littered with big-money attackers such as Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, and backed by a fierce crowd, more might have been expected.
Our Opta match centre delivers you all the Liverpool vs Man City stats from their Premier League meeting at Anfield on Sunday 11 October.

7aqj7codpmxw1fjaac27zttmd.title: 'We should've killed it off' – Kane rues Bayern's missed chances in Arsenal draw
7aqj7codpmxw1fjaac27zttmd.subtitle: Bayern Munich came from behind to lead against Arsenal, but despite having chances to seal the victory, they were instead pegged back again.
paragraphs: Harry Kane believes Bayern Munich should have killed off the game against Arsenal after being held to a 2-2 draw in the Champions League.
Kane led Bayern's fightback after Eberechi Eze had given Arsenal a first-half lead as he set up Alphonso Davies for the equaliser before putting them ahead from the penalty spot.
However, Declan Rice netted in the 82nd minute to snatch Arsenal a point and condemn Bayern to a second straight draw in Europe, having been shocked in a 3-3 stalemate by Viking last week.

Former Tottenham striker Kane scored his 16th goal against Arsenal in all competitions (14 in 19 games for Spurs, two in four games for Bayern). He only has more goals against Leicester City (20 in 20 matches) in his entire career.
The Englishman also became the sixth player in Champions League history to score or assist in 10 consecutive appearances, and the first since Serhou Guirassy between November 2020 and February 2025.
Bayern had one fewer shot than Arsenal (14 to 13), and both sides managed five attempts on target overall, though Vincent Kompany's side won the expected goals battle with 2.5 xG to the Gunners' 1.4.
And Kane was left to rue those missed opportunities as Bayern now sit 14th in the Champions League table after dropping points.
"It was a good performance," Kane said. "Especially at the start of the second half, we came back out with high intensity and scored the goal.
"In that spell, we should've killed it off – we had the chances. We tried to keep the ball in the last 20 minutes, but Arsenal punished us with their goal.
"The draw was fair overall. We've got a lot of players who are missing, so we'll take the point."
Kompany felt similarly to Kane but was hesitant to dwell on the disappointment for too long with a trip to Freiburg next up on Sunday.
"We had the feeling that we could, or maybe even should have won the game, but we're up against strong opponents, and the game was never over," he said.

"It's obviously a shame in the moment when you concede the equaliser, but it was an intensive match against a top team, and next we face the team second in the Bundesliga, and that's the most important as of now."

7dm65s3l6gg41bdy60xf5fshc.title: Inter 3-4 Club Brugge: Tresoldi hits hat-trick in famous Champions League win
7dm65s3l6gg41bdy60xf5fshc.subtitle: Club Brugge claimed the first win of their Champions League campaign after Nicolo Tresoldi's hat-trick led them to victory against Inter.
paragraphs: Nicolo Tresoldi inspired Club Brugge to a famous Champions League victory as he scored a hat-trick to help his team edge a seven-goal thriller 4-3 against Inter.
Tresoldi's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Lautaro Martinez, but the German netted twice to put Brugge in control before a manic end to proceedings on Tuesday.
Martinez's second of the match was quickly followed up by Romeo Vermant's fine finish, but even after a late Ange-Yoan Bonny, Brugge were able to see out the victory.

Brugge survived an early wave of pressure from their hosts and came close to taking the lead when Inter's failure to clear a flat corner into the area saw Tresoldi crash a strike against the upright, though San Siro was stunned into silence moments later.

Carlos Forbs led a lightning break from an Inter corner with a driving run from his own half before he was chopped down inside the penalty area by Hakan Calhanoglu, with Tresoldi stepping up to ruthlessly dispatch the spot-kick into the top-right corner.

Calhanoglu came within inches of atoning for his earlier error, but his swerving attempt cannoned against the crossbar, with Martinez then denied an equaliser by the offside flag, with the Inter captain just beyond the Brugge defence when he headed in Calhanoglu's free-kick.
But Inter were able to draw level at the end of a frenetic first half through Martinez, who shrugged off Brandon Mechele before prodding past Yann Sommer in the 44th minute.

Sommer then produced a stunning stop to repel Martinez early in the second half, and that save proved crucial for Brugge who retook the lead just after the hour. Josep Martinez was too slow to get a ball over the top, allowing Forbs to steal in and feed Tresoldi, who stroked into the empty net.

And Tresoldi completed his hat-trick in the 74th minute. Forbs cut inside and saw his shot saved by Martinez, only for Brugge number seven to tuck home the rebound in off the post to net his fourth Champions League goal of the season.

Inter threatened a comeback when Martinez brought up his brace when he finished from close range after Petar Sucic's shot was saved, but Brugge restored their two-goal lead in the 87th minute through Vermant's delicate loft over Martinez.

Cristian Chivu's side hit back again in the third minute of second-half stoppage time as Bonny cut inside and picked out the top-right corner, but Brugge were able to hold on to claim an incredible win at San Siro.
Tresoldi leads Brugge to another Italian Job

In what was the first-ever meeting between the two sides, Brugge and Inter delivered one of the standout games from this year's Champions League, though the Belgian giants would have fancied their chances coming to this iconic stadium.

Brugge have now won three of their last four Champions League games against Italian sides (L1), becoming the first Belgian team to defeat Inter in the competition, and their victory was inspired by a brilliant performance from Tresoldi up front.

Tresoldi became the first ever Brugge player to score a hat-trick in the Champions League, while he is also the first player from the club to score in the Brugge's opening two matches to start a Champions League campaign since Hans Vanaken in September 2021.
And at 22 years and 54 days, Tresoldi from Brugge is the youngest German to score a hat-trick in the Champions League, replacing Karim Adeyemi, who was 22 years and 257 days at the time.

For Inter, however, they have now lost four consecutive matches in the Champions League/European Cup for the first time, though they had more than enough chances. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 3.93 from their 30 shots to Brugge's tally of 4.26 from their 18 attempts.

7e6gdtkifln617w8eymsyttlm.title: Neville expects Man Utd to give under-fire Carrick until January
7e6gdtkifln617w8eymsyttlm.subtitle: With Manchester United's winless streak across all competitions extending to six matches on Sunday, Michael Carrick is under real scrutiny.
paragraphs: Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick's future will be in real doubt if Manchester United's poor form persists until January, but for now, he expects the Red Devils to give their embattled head coach time.

Having been pegged back in a 1-1 draw with old rivals Leeds United on Sunday, Carrick's side are now winless in six matches in all competitions, since beating Sabah 4-0 in their Champions League opener in early September.
In the Premier League, United have failed to win any of their last five games (D4 L1) and have only won one match all campaign – 5-2 against Ipswich Town in August.
The last time they recorded just one win in their opening seven games of a league season was in 1986-87, under Ron Atkinson in the old First Division.
They ended that campaign in 11th, having replaced Atkinson with Alex Ferguson in November.
Carrick's side are currently 13th in the table, already five points adrift of Liverpool in fifth, and Neville says missing out on Champions League qualification is not an option this term.
Asked about United's expectations on the Gary Neville podcast, he said: "I would say fourth would be a birdie, fifth would be par, and sixth would be a bogey.
"They can't finish outside the top five, because then you're missing out on the Champions League and it becomes a vicious cycle.
"Then you can't get players because they want to play in the Champions League, and you can't get the money from it, and you've lost £60m to £70m, and you're in the Europa League.
"Fifth is a must for Michael Carrick to continue to grow and Manchester United to continue to grow with investment. If they're 13th in January, he's got a problem.
"I think it's still early enough, with seven points from seven games, to say, 'okay, it's still early' – you can't say that after 15 games.
"It has to change in the next few weeks: Bournemouth [on Sunday] is really important and so is Chelsea away [on October 31].
"You've got to say fifth. You know that anything less than fifth is going to be a disappointment and a drop in standards from where everybody expected them to finish.
"And at the moment, they're well short of that because you look at Brighton, Liverpool, Aston Villa – they look like they're picking up a little bit. It's difficult."
Despite another underwhelming performance, Carrick said on Sunday that taking a point from Elland Road represented a step in the right direction for his team.
And Neville understands that assessment, saying: "There's a depressed standard and low expectations right now.
"But it'll feel like a stepping stone for Michael Carrick, and it'll feel like the first step on the ladder in the Premier League."

7f7vw8sd056e14cgu0lejgtqu.title: Mac Allister says 'no firm decision' over Liverpool future amid contract dispute
7f7vw8sd056e14cgu0lejgtqu.subtitle: Alexis Mac Allister recently said he had opportunities to leave Liverpool during the summer transfer window, with no new contract on offer.
paragraphs: Alexis Mac Allister says there is still "no firm decision" on his future with Liverpool, with the Reds yet to offer the midfielder a new contract.
Earlier this month, Mac Allister made headlines by saying Liverpool had informed him they were not in a position to offer him fresh terms, after he entered the final two years of his deal.

Mac Allister, who has won a Premier League title and the EFL Cup since arriving from Brighton in 2023, said he was "very sad" to have had no negotiations with the club, after his fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai penned new deals.
Mac Allister has retained a key role for Liverpool since Andoni Iraola took charge, making seven appearances in all competitions this season with five of those being starts.

The 27-year-old has now linked up with Argentina for a series of friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin, the latter of which will serve as a farewell match for Lionel Messi after he announced his international retirement.
And in an interview with ESPN, Mac Allister said there had been no progress on resolving his contract stand-off.
"There's no firm decision yet. I still have two years left on my contract. As I said, I'm going to give it my all. A lot can happen in that time; there are plenty of options," Mac Allister said.
"Hopefully it'll be for more years, but if it's just two, I'll have to enjoy them with my family, because I have no doubt that I'm at one of the best clubs in the world."

The nature of Messi's involvement in the game against Benin – set for October 5 at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires – remains unclear, but it will bring the curtain down on one of the all-time great international careers.
Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for La Albiceleste, with eight of those coming at the 2026 World Cup.

No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34). Messi's 12 assists at FIFA's flagship competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight, since 1966).
And though he fell narrowly short of delivering a second straight title in North America this year, Mac Allister feels Messi should be in contention for a record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or.
"Obviously, as Argentines we'd love for Messi to win it. He had an incredible World Cup and I don't see why he shouldn't be awarded it," he said.

"Also, it's understood that these days the numbers play a big part – something that didn't carry as much weight in the past – and you don't know exactly what people are voting for either. But everyone in the running is a great player; anyone who comes close will deserve it.
"We all know that Leo has always prioritised the team over individual achievements, so it wouldn't be a big deal for him."

7hm5xdmmefsy13b5vntbu54rb.title: Quill backs Dallas to 'be better' than in Austin draw
7hm5xdmmefsy13b5vntbu54rb.subtitle: Both FC Dallas and Los Angeles FC are looking to get back to winning ways after draws last time out, with hopes of climbing the table.
paragraphs: FC Dallas head coach Eric Quill is confident his team will "be better" than their last performance when they host Los Angeles FC in MLS on Saturday.
Dallas head into the match on the back of a five-match unbeaten streak, but after three straight wins, they were held to a 0-0 draw by Austin FC last time out.
It was just the seventh time this season they have been shut out – as they are the second-highest scorers in the Western Conference.
They currently sit fourth in the West, but are one of three teams on 44 points, and they know a win could help them close the gap to the leaders Vancouver Whitecaps.
Quill is looking for a big improvement from the performance against Austin, especially in the final third.
"It wasn't our typical game," Quill said of the draw with Austin. "I think everybody's used to four goals from us, so it wasn't there.
"But it wasn't for a lack of trying or a lack of opportunities that we created.

7pi8k9av8r9q1gg83djbub5li.title: Hull boss Jakirovic left with regret despite maintaining unbeaten home record
7pi8k9av8r9q1gg83djbub5li.subtitle: Despite Hull City maintaining their unbeaten home record, Sergej Jakirovic was left to rue what might have been against Brentford.
paragraphs: Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic was left with "regret" after his side were held to a 1-1 draw by Brentford at the MKM Stadium on Sunday.
Hull went ahead in the 24th minute, thanks to Oliver McBurnie's penalty after Aaron Hickey bundled over Tim Iroegbunam inside the box, following Caoimhin Kelleher’s poor pass.
Dango Ouattara blazed over the woodwork shortly afterwards, but he eventually brought Brentford level midway through the second half.
That all came after Ryan Giles failed to clear Jaidon Anthony’s left-wing centre, allowing Igor Thiago to pick up the loose ball and square it to Ouattara for a tap-in at the back post.
Anthony almost won it for the Bees, but his fierce strike flew inches past the upright before Mohamed-Ali Cho forced Kelleher into a smart stop at the other end.
Hull moved up to 10th in the Premier League, having earned 10 points from their opening eight games.
The Tigers are unbeaten across their last 15 home Premier League games in which they have netted the opening goal (W9 D6), since a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham in November 2014.
Jakirovic, though, was left wanting more.
"I think we played a good game, especially in the first half," said Jakirovic.
"We were much more aggressive in duels, we won a lot of first and second balls.
"Maybe there were some cheap mistakes, bad passing, bad receiving, but you see how fast they are – in five seconds they were in our box.
"We should have scored one or maybe two more with better decisions.
"I can regret the chance we had through Mohamed-Ali Cho and [Joe] Gelhardt, maybe it should have been 2-1, but in the end I think it's a fair result."
Brentford, meanwhile, are now winless in three Premier League games.
McBurnie's penalty marked the first time Brentford have conceded the first goal in a league game this season, making them the 20th and final team to suffer that fate in 2026-27.

"It was a tough game and it was always going to be a tough game. I’ve got a lot of respect for Sergej and the journey he’s taken this team on – I think it's been remarkable," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews, a former Hull player.
"We reacted well at half-time, the impact from the bench was pretty good but it was a tough game.

"We lacked a bit of cohesion at times in how we played, we've got very good players and good players on the bench and I think it's important that when they come on they realise that they have to impact the game.
"It's nice today that they had that impact."

7qnwzr4ovt1g14hhg42jy1uj5.title: Fabregas insists Man Utd not in crisis ahead of Champions League clash
7qnwzr4ovt1g14hhg42jy1uj5.subtitle: Manchester United are without a win in their last six games in all competitions, but Cesc Fabregas says the club are not in a crisis.
paragraphs: Cesc Fabregas said, "I don't believe in crises", when asked about Manchester United's recent form ahead of Como's Champions League clash with Michael Carrick's side.
The Serie A side welcome the Red Devils to the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, with both clubs enduring different starts to their respective campaigns in 2026-27.
Como are fifth in Serie A with 14 points from their opening seven games, while they also marked their Champions League debut with a 4-1 thrashing of RB Leipzig on MD1.
After then losing to Feyenoord in Europe last week, Como responded with a 3-1 win away to Fiorentina in the league. For United, however, things have gone from bad to worse.

Following a 1-1 draw with Leeds United on Sunday, Carrick's men have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4 L2), their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87 – also one victory after seven games.

In addition, they are without a win since the first match of their Champions League campaign, when they beat Azerbaijani minnows Sabah, with MD2 seeing them fall to a 2-0 defeat against last year's semi-finalists, Atletico Madrid.

After that loss in the Spanish capital, defender Lisandro Martinez launched a scathing review of the club's hierarchy, saying United did not have a squad capable of competing in Europe and pointed the blame towards technical director Jason Wilcox and the club's owners.
Fabregas, however, refused to say the club was in crisis, telling reporters: "I don't believe in crises in football.
"You have a game every three days, it's 11 against 11, and you've got to give your best.
"A crisis is invented by you journalists, but we are professionals; we've wanted to compete since the day we were born. I don't believe in any crisis."

This will be the first meeting between Como and United – since the start of last season, the six matches between Italian and English sides in the Champions League have been won by the Premier League outfit on five occasions (L1 – Atalanta 2-1 Chelsea the exception).
Como are looking to become the first Italian side since Lazio in 1999-00 to win their first two home games in the European Cup/Champions League.

It's a match that will see Fabregas and Carrick face each other as opposition managers, 17 years after playing on opposing sides in both legs of the 2008-09 Champions League semi-finals, between Arsenal and United (won 4-1 on aggregate by the Red Devils).
"It is another historic day for the club, the fans and the city," Fabregas added. "We've got to play with focus and ambition.
"This is Manchester United we are up against, so let's enjoy it, play our game and try to win. It's an incredible group of players.
"We must be humble and realise there is much to learn. We'll see how it goes, but respect our opponents.
"There are different ways of attacking; we try to study their weaknesses, but also don’t forget what we do best.
"They have a specific system and principles, but football is ultimately about the players. We tend to forget that, as directors and coaching staff."

7vg9y74erar31ej3v2zweeuo4.title: Germany 0-1 Greece: Kourbelis spoils Klopp's home debut
7vg9y74erar31ej3v2zweeuo4.subtitle: Germany remained without a win under Jurgen Klopp and in the Nations League as Dimitrios Kourbelis proved to be the hero for Greece.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp's wait for a first win in charge of Germany continued on Sunday as Dimitrios Kourbelis' second-half goal earned Greece a famous 1-0 victory in the Nations League.
Klopp was denied by Cody Gakpo's stoppage-time equaliser against the Netherlands in their Nations League opener, and his home debut at WWK Arena ended in a shock defeat.
Germany are third in Group A2 having taken just one point from their opening two games, with a home game against Serbia, who are also without a win, up next this Thursday.
It took until the 25th minute for Germany to carve out their first clear-cut opportunity, but Younes Ebnoutalib was unable to steer Kevin Schade's dangerous delivery on target.

Karim Adeyemi then fired over after being set free by Joshua Kimmich, with the Barcelona forward then forcing Konstantinos Tzolakis into making his first save of the match minutes later with a curling left-footed strike that was pushed behind.

The hosts' dominance continued after the break, with Bambase Conte dispossessing Christos Zafeiris and seeing his shot saved by Tzolakis, with the Greece goalkeeper then on hand to keep out Ebnoutalib and Kimmich's free-kick.

Greece came within inches of taking the lead against the run of play in the 67th minute through Fotis Ioannidis. Kimmich lost possession to Vangelis Pavlidis, who sent through Ioannidis, but his first-time attempt whistled past the left post.

But the visitors took the lead in the 74th minute when Christos Tzolis' deflected cross fell kindly to Kourbelis on the edge of the box. He skipped around Felix Nmecha before firing an effort at goal that took a knick off Kimmich on its way into the net.

Serge Gnabry attempted to get his team back into the match, but his shot was held by Tzolakis, with Germany's possession yielding little in the shape of chances as Greece held on to go top of Group A2 with six points from their first two games.
Plenty to ponder for Klopp

Ahead of sitting in the Germany dugout for the first time against the Netherlands, Klopp refused to make any promises of silverware and instant success during his time in charge, and this result proves there is still plenty of work for the former Liverpool boss to do.

Klopp made five changes to his team, and they were perhaps unfortunate not to find themselves in front after wasting a string of glorious chances, and their profligacy in front of goal was punished in the second half by Kourbelis.

Germany's dominance with the ball was backed up by the metrics, too. Thanasis Androutsos had the most accurate passes of any Greece's outfield players that started the match with just 21, with the hosts also ending the contest with 75.5% possession.

But the statistic that matters is the scoreline, and Greece will be delighted with their victory. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 0.77 from their eight shots, scoring with the only one they had on target, compared to Germany's tally of 1.34 from their 16 attempts.

7vi4y3bk6y931q5bkugmc3ydd.title: Record-setting Osorio focused on Toronto's playoff push
7vi4y3bk6y931q5bkugmc3ydd.subtitle: Jonathan Osorio scored his first goal of the season last time out, making MLS history in the process.
paragraphs: Jonathan Osorio is fully focused on Toronto FC's push for the playoffs, despite making MLS history in his last outing.
Osorio netted for Toronto in their 2-1 win over D.C. United on Wednesday.
In the process, the 34-year-old became the first player in MLS history to score in 14 successive campaigns for a single club.
But Osorio, who helped Toronto win a treble, including MLS Cup, in 2017, is firmly focused on the club's push to qualify for the playoffs.
Toronto sit 11th in the Eastern Conference, though they are only two points behind the wildcard slots with two games to go in the regular season.
When asked if he was celebrating the milestone, Osorio said: "No.
"You look at it, and it's something that for sure is to be proud of, but honestly my focus right now is trying to make the playoffs for this team.
"It's great, 14 seasons, playing and being able to contribute for this club that I love; I've said it many times. But right now, my focus is just helping this team get into the playoffs.
"Our fans deserve it. These fans are one of the best in the league. They're amazing. The way they show up for the team, year in, year out, highs, lows, these fans deserve a competitive team.
"We're doing everything we can to get this team into the playoffs and to give the fans what they deserve."
Toronto take on Atlanta United this weekend.
Atlanta sit 14th in the East, well out of the playoff picture.
Atlanta United - Breel Embolo
Embolo scored Atlanta's only goal on Wednesday with an 88th-minute header.

Since the beginning of September, Embolo has scored four goals in the second half of matches, while all other Atlanta United players have three total goals in the second half in that time (excluding own goals).
Toronto FC - Josh Sargent
Sargent scored the winner on Wednesday for his ninth goal of the regular season.

He joins team-mate Daniel Salloi with nine goals this term, but no Toronto player has reached double-digit goals in a single regular season since Alejandro Pozuelo (12) and Jozy Altidore (11) both did so in 2019.
MATCH PREDICTION: ATLANTA UNITED WIN
Their 2-1 win over D.C. marked the third time this season that Toronto won an MLS match after trailing at half-time. The Reds had two such wins over the previous four seasons combined entering 2026.
Atlanta, meanwhile, attempted 19 shots in their 2-1 loss to New York City FC while allowing just 11.
They have outshot their opponents by at least eight attempts in three of their last four matches.
And Atlanta have lost only two of their last 12 meetings with Toronto dating back to the start of the 2021 season (W5 D5), including a 2-1 road win on April 25.
However, Atlanta's only set of consecutive wins over Toronto came in the 2021 season, winning in August and October.
Atlanta United - 41.9%

7w024drvhsnw1ugmwfjj6f3t5.title: 'We expect more from the top' – Martinez slams Man Utd hierarchy after Atletico defeat
7w024drvhsnw1ugmwfjj6f3t5.subtitle: Manchester United's season hit another low after losing to Atletico Madrid, but Lisandro Martinez suggested the blame lies elsewhere.
paragraphs: Lisandro Martinez launched a scathing review of the Manchester United hierarchy, saying Michael Carrick does not have a team capable of competing in the Champions League.
Martinez's rant came in the wake of a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, a match that saw the LaLiga giants take the lead after 47 seconds through Pablo Barrios.
It was the fourth time – and the first time since November 2002 against Basel – that United had conceded inside the opening minute of a Champions League encounter.
Carrick's side responded well to going behind, with Bryan Mbeumo, Marcus Rashford and Carlos Baleba all spurning good chances to equalise during an open first half.

But United's task was made even more difficult when Leny Yoro was sent off for a last-man foul on Jonathan David, and Atletico made their numerical advantage count in the 79th minute when Ademola Lookman finished past Senne Lammens on the rebound.

The Red Devils have now lost three of their last five games in all competitions (D2), as many as in their previous 21 games under Carrick (W14 D4), with their last victory coming against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah on MD1 of the Champions League.

However, Martinez pointed the finger towards technical director Jason Wilcox and the owners of United, saying his team were not backed in the transfer window across all areas of their team, with Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Baleba their only notable arrivals this summer.
"Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it is a reflection of the mirror of how our club is at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime.
"We had a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete, because many teams bring many players as well.
"Atletico have an amazing team, and they deserve to win. I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox].
"I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."
When questioned about what areas should be strengthened, Martinez added: "In general. Last season we did everything; we created the base to create an amazing team.
"It is annoying, disappointing coming here, and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here."
United's five-game winless run across all competitions is their longest since a six-game streak in January 2025 (D2 L4), putting Carrick under pressure.
A testing trip to rivals Leeds United is on the horizon for the Red Devils, but Martinez leapt to the defence of his boss, suggesting other parts of the club need to change.
"I don't think so. He does his best," Martinez said when asked if the problem was Carrick not being backed. "Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.
"The teams know how you play; they know every detail. If you don't change, next season is a big problem.
"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can't say more.
"It is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas."

7xtz5a1hwege1re10jdr61ozg.title: Lech Poznan 1-1 Sunderland: Super sub Bengtsson ends visitors' perfect start
7xtz5a1hwege1re10jdr61ozg.subtitle: Despite taking the lead at Enea Stadion, Sunderland were held to a 1-1 draw by Lech Poznan in the Europa League.
paragraphs: Sunderland failed to maintain their perfect start in the Europa League following a 1-1 draw with Lech Poznan.

Tymur Tutierov headed the Black Cats into an early lead, but Leo Bengtsson came off the bench to salvage a point for the visitors, who were denied victory by a late double save from Robin Roefs at Enea Stadion.

Sunderland were ahead after just two minutes in Poland after Nilson Angulo intercepted a poor pass from Mateusz Lis before crossing into the middle, where Tutierov was on hand to head in from close range.
The hosts immediately pushed for an equaliser and went close through Daniel Hakans, who poked wide of the target with the outside of his boot after going one-on-one with Roefs.

Granit Xhaka had his head in his hands after shooting straight at Lis following a lay-off from Malick Fofana, and the Poznan goalkeeper was called upon again after the break to keep out Nordi Mukiele's fierce drive from distance.

Bengtsson almost made an immediate impact off the bench, flashing a volley narrowly wide, but he scored the equaliser in the 70th minute as Sunderland failed to clear their lines from a corner, allowing the substitute to fire in at the near post.

Poznan's best chance to win the contest came shortly after when Mikael Ishak sent a low cross into the six-yard box, but Roefs saved Patrik Walemark's initial effort and managed to get back up to deny Michal Gurgul on the rebound.
Black Cats' European momentum stalls

With his side currently sitting bottom of the Premier League, Regis Le Bris would have hoped Sunderland could at least extend their winning start in the Europa League, but they were made to cling on for what could still be an important point.
The Black Cats will no doubt regret their missed chances before Bengtsson's equaliser, though both sides may feel they should have scored more than once.
Sunderland accumulated 2.76 expected goals (xG) from 25 shots, 11 of which were on target, while Poznan produced 2.47 xG from their 16 attempts as both goalkeepers made important interventions.

Lis certainly atoned for his early error, making 11 saves to keep Poznan in the contest, while Roefs' five saves at least keeps Sunderland unbeaten in the competition ahead of hosting Dinamo Zagreb on MD4.

Twenty-one-year-old Tutierov will also take positives from the match; after seeing a goal ruled out against Torreense last time out in the competition, the Ukrainian scored his first goal for the Black Cats.

          Leeds 1-1 Man Utd Stats: Carrick's Men Pegged Back as Winless Run Continues
        
      
                          
                      Oct 18, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
A bruising Premier League encounter captured the imagination at Elland Road, but the teams couldn't be separated. Look back on it with our Leeds vs Man Utd stats page.
Manchester United could have done more to ease the pressure on Michael Carrick at their winless run stretches to six games in all competitions with a 1-1 Premier League draw at Leeds.

After seeing Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancel out Bryan Mbeumo‘s strike, the Red Devils have not won since beating Sabah in their UEFA Champions League opener in early September, while they have also gone five Premier League matches without a win.
And things could have been even worse on Sunday as Leeds had the better chances to win in the second half, with Anton Stach wasting arguably their clearest opportunity.

Though there were no major chances in the opening 25 minutes, there was no shortage of commitment from both sides, with Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson among those to put in tough early tackles.

Leeds almost drew first blood when Nico Elvedi's downward header from a Stach free-kick was pushed away by Senne Lammens, but Man Utd soon passed up an even bigger chance as Mbeumo headed Youri Tielemans‘ pinpoint cross wide.
Mbeumo made no mistake from Tielemans’ next cross, a low delivery from the right flank in the 35th minute, stretching to guide the ball into the bottom-left corner.

Leeds had a couple of half chances before the interval, but Calvert-Lewin was unable to trouble Lammens with a header and James Justin failed to get enough power behind his shot following a marauding run.
The hosts' pressure paid dividends six minutes into the second half, with Calvert-Lewin well-placed to volley past Lammens after Tarik Muharemovic flicked on Stach's corner.

Ao Tanaka, Noah Okafor and Stach all fired efforts into the stands as Leeds remained in the ascendency, with the latter's chance being the clearest after Diogo Dalot headed the ball straight to him just inside the Man Utd area.

At the other end, Fernandes went close to finding the bottom-left corner, but Carrick's side were lacklustre even after the introduction of Matheus Cunha, and Lukas Nmecha and Stach both had opportunities to win it for Leeds amid a late goalmouth scramble.
United failed to cling on for a morale-boosting victory after Mbeumo put them in front, and that has been something of a theme in the early stages of 2026-27.
Three of Mbeumo's four Premier League goals this season have put Man Utd 1-0 up, with only Erling Haaland (four) boasting more such goals this term.
However, on each of the last three occasions the Cameroonian has given them the lead, United have gone on to draw (also versus Everton and Tottenham).

When Leeds needed a goal, it was no surprise to see Calvert-Lewin step up; he has now scored in six of his last seven home Premier League games (seven goals overall) and boasts eight Premier League goals since the start of April, a figure only Haaland (13) can better in that time.

Furthermore, since Calvert-Lewin's first home game for Leeds last season, his 12 Premier League goals at Elland Road is the third most scored by any player at a particular venue, after Haaland at the Etihad Stadium (19) and Igor Thiago at the Gtech Community Stadium (14).
And after all is said and done, Carrick may be relieved to even leave Yorkshire with a point, after Leeds edged expected goals (xG) by 1.44 to 0.91 – 1.19 of that came in the second half.

          Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth Stats: Jordan Henderson Rolls Back the Years to Inspire Rout
        
      
                          
                      Oct 10, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Veteran midfielder Jordan Henderson scored twice and set up another as Chelsea ran riot against a beleaguered Bournemouth.
Jordan Henderson scored twice and teed up another as he set Chelsea on their way to a thumping 5-1 win over Bournemouth in the Premier League.
Chelsea needed fewer than three minutes to race into a 2-0 lead, with Henderson and Morgan Rogers both scoring early, while João Pedro added their third within the first minute of the second half.
Evanilson pulled one back for Bournemouth, but João Pedro and Henderson both scored again to get Chelsea their first top-flight win since the end of August.

Chelsea flew out of the blocks, and Henderson took just 66 seconds to break the deadlock. Cole Palmer – for whom a new eight-year deal was announced on Saturday – powered forward before laying the ball off for Henderson for a first-time finish that flew in off the post.

And just 83 seconds after the restart, Chelsea had a second. Pedro Neto was denied by Djordje Petrovic, but the Blues kept it alive, with Henderson helping it to Rogers, who floated a shot into the goal via a flick off António Silva head to help it over the goalkeeper.
The fast start continued as Bournemouth exploited space down the left, but Rayan was selfish and watched his effort sail into the stands.

Only twice before in Premier League history has a team gone 2-0 up earlier than Chelsea vs Bournemouth today (2:29).▪️ Leicester vs Derby County, April 1998▪️ Luton vs Brighton, Jan 2024Both of those sides went on to win 4-0. pic.twitter.com/92sFSHChbh

Emiliano Martínez ensured Chelsea went into the break with their two-goal cushion, making a double save to keep out Rayan and Ryan Christie just after the half-hour mark before holding onto Silva's header.
And Chelsea wasted no time in the second half, either. Within 30 seconds, João Pedro had the ball in the back of the net after Neto latched onto a poor attempted clearance from Silva.

But Bournemouth responded well as they exploited Chelsea's set-piece struggles. Moisés Caicedo tried to hook a corner clear, but Evanilson stuck out a leg to send it flying past Martínez 51 minutes in.

It took João Pedro just 16 minutes to restore Chelsea's three-goal advantage, with Pep Chavarria taking Bournemouth's defence out of the game with his low cross, and the Brazilian was on hand to emphatically turn it in.
And Henderson added the late gloss. Palmer won the free-kick, but caught Bournemouth out by not taking it, and Henderson curled it over the wall and past Petrovic at his near post.

After failing to win three straight Premier League games before the international break, Chelsea returned to action with a bang and even more early goals. There have been five goals scored in the opening three minutes of games in the competition this term, and Chelsea have scored four of them.

Henderson got his first goal for the Blues in the process, becoming the club's oldest English goalscorer in the Premier League (36 years, 115 days) since John Terry against Watford in May 2017 (36y 159d).

His assist for Rogers meant that only once (Emile Heskey against Derby County in April 1998 – in the opening two minutes) has a player both scored and assisted in a Premier League game earlier than Henderson (2:29).

36 – Jordan Henderson (36y 115d) is the oldest @ChelseaFC player to be directly involved in 3+ goals in a Premier League match (2 goals, 1 assist), and oldest for any side since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022 (37 v Norwich).Twilight. pic.twitter.com/OdCRuSQRTi

And he also became the oldest Chelsea player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game, overtaking Gianluca Vialli (33y 245d), and the oldest for any side since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022 (37 v Norwich City).

This was only the second time Henderson has registered three goal involvements in a single game in the competition, last doing so back in April 2013 for Liverpool against Newcastle United (also two goals, one assist).

João Pedro missed out for Brazil during the international break through injury but looked strong on his return to the side; only Bruno Fernandes (22) has now been involved in more top-flight goals in 2026 than the Brazilian (19 – 14 goals, five assists).

          Arsenal v Everton Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Jonathan Burnett / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to this Premier League match at the Emirates Stadium with our Arsenal vs Everton prediction and preview. Will the Gunners overcome an Everton side who suffered their first league loss of the season last week?

The Premier League table is starting to take shape as champions Arsenal return to domestic action, hosting Everton at the Emirates following a 2–2 draw with Bayern Munich in their midweek Champions League clash.

Declan Rice rescued a point for the Gunners eight minutes from time after Eberechi Eze had given them a first-half lead at Allianz Arena, with Bayern bouncing back via goals from Alphonso Davies and Harry Kane.

Viktor Gyökeres came off the bench to assist Rice's equaliser, and with Eze replacing Bukayo Saka early on before scoring in the 25th minute, no Premier League side this season has more goal contributions from substitutes in all competitions than Arsenal's nine (five goals, four assists).

Domestically, Arsenal have bounced back from their 3–0 defeat at Brighton just before the latest international break, with one-goal wins over Leeds United and Nottingham Forest. But the defending champions failed to truly convince in either of those victories.

Second-half strikes from Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimarães earned Arsenal a 2–1 comeback victory over Leeds in their last home league outing. They then needed a deflected 80th-minute goal from Noni Madueke to seal a 1–0 win at the City Ground last weekend.

Set up by a league-leading fourth assist of the season from Rice, Madueke became the third substitute in a row to score the decisive goal in a Premier League game for Arsenal, after Guimarães also came on to net late winners against Sunderland and Leeds.

The Gunners have ground to make up on Manchester City at the summit and could trail Enzo Maresca's side by six points once they kick-off as the leaders face Aston Villa in Saturday's early kick-off. Everton sit eighth, six places and eight points further back.

The Toffees also made a strong start to their campaign and were fifth after two wins and four draws in their first six games, but their unbeaten run came to an end in a 2–0 home defeat to Chelsea last time out.
They didn't do much to help their cause, with only six shots in total, their fewest in a Premier League game since hitting just five against Arsenal in December 2025.
Goals could indeed be at a premium in this game, given Arsenal and Everton have recorded the joint-most 1-0 wins (32 each) in the Premier League since Arteta was hired by Arsenal in December 2019.
However, recent form also suggests Arsenal have good reason to be confident having won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games, including six from six at the Emirates over the course of that run.
Everton, meanwhile, have won just one of their last 30 Premier League away games against Arsenal, a 1–0 victory in the behind-closed-doors 2020-21 season under Carlo Ancelotti.

Across David Moyes' two spells, the Toffees have never enjoyed victory in 13 attempts at Highbury or the Emirates, losing on 10 occasions, while the Scot has lost 11 of his last 12 Premier League matches against the reigning champions.

In terms of team news, Arsenal are still without William Saliba for the long term, and Saka has joined him and Christos Tzolis in the treatment room after injuring his thigh in Wednesday's 2–2 draw in Munich. Piero Hincapié‘s ankle is being assessed ahead of a potential return at left-back.

Everton, meanwhile, have a fully fit squad to choose from at the time of writing after Christian Nørgaard – who moved from Arsenal while carrying an injury over the summer – finally made his Toffees debut off the bench against Chelsea.
Everton's dismal record against Arsenal didn't let up last season, with Moyes' side losing 1–0 and 2–0 respectively in December (at home) and March (at the Emirates).

Arsenal come into this game unbeaten in their last seven against Everton in the Premier League – winning five – which is their best run against the Toffees since going 13 without defeat between December 2007 and December 2013.
The Opta supercomputer is in little doubt when it comes to predicting the outcome of this game, with Arsenal understandably seen as overwhelming favourites.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations, the Gunners came away with victory in 69.5% of the outcomes, suggesting there'll be a very expectant home crowd at the Emirates.

85hazl7pib641t15vaedmrwwb.title: Iraola glad to build positive Anfield energy as Liverpool overcome Chelsea
85hazl7pib641t15vaedmrwwb.subtitle: Liverpool's upturn in fortunes at Anfield continued on Wednesday, as they beat Chelsea on penalties in the EFL Cup's fourth round.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola acknowledged the importance of Liverpool correcting their poor home form early on in his reign, after his side eliminated Chelsea from the EFL Cup at Anfield.
Wesley Fofana missed the decisive penalty as Liverpool won 6-5 in a dramatic shoot-out to book their spot in the quarter-finals, where Iraola's former club Bournemouth await them.

Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo had both found the target from 12 yards during a 1-1 draw in regulation time, while Kostas Tsimikas and Emmanuel Emegha missed opportunities to win the shoot-out for their respective teams before Fofana blazed wildly into the Kop.
Wednesday's game was Liverpool's third in eight days at home, following victories over Villarreal (4-3) in the Champions League and Brighton (2-0) in the Premier League.

And, after the Reds only won two of their first five home games under him in all competitions (D2 L1), Iraola felt it was important to build a winning feeling on their own turf, particularly with Premier League champions Arsenal visiting on Sunday.
"It's three in a row at home, which is very important. We were struggling a little bit at home," Iraola told Sky Sports.
"Now, we have the confidence of winning three in a row and we have the biggest one against Arsenal on Sunday.
"We don't have a lot of time. Some of the players who played most of the minutes will need a very good rest. Then, we'll see who is available on Sunday."
Iraola went with a relatively strong starting lineup, though he did hand starts to four youngsters in Trey Nyoni, Rio Ngumoha, James McConnell and Lewis Koumas.

And the Spaniard was impressed with the level they showed. Nyoni's performance was particularly eye-catching, as he tallied the most touches (86) and completed the most passes (65/76) of any player on the pitch.
Ngumoha, meanwhile, completed a game-high four dribbles (from four attempted) and won eight of the 11 duels he contested – the most of any Liverpool player.
"I think they did a good job. I think they deserved the right to play because they were also very good against Spurs in the last round," Iraola said of Liverpool's youngsters.
"We told them that they are first-team players and we are confident if they have to play. They showed us they have a very good level and they helped us a lot.
"I think it was quite a level game. It was very competitive, not a lot of chances for both teams. There were moments for us, moments for them.
"We are really happy with the performances of a lot of the players and obviously happy to finish on the right end of the penalty shoot-out because it gave us the chance to be in the draw."

8648l5v0unw71w31ghmaw4sn8.title: Vanney backs fully-fit LA Galaxy to defeat anyone in playoffs
8648l5v0unw71w31ghmaw4sn8.subtitle: With the fight for the playoff spots in the Western Conference heating up, the LA Galaxy face Austin FC in their final home game.
paragraphs: Greg Vanney believes his fully fit LA Galaxy side "can play against anyone" in the playoffs.
The Galaxy are yet to secure their place in the postseason, currently sitting 10th in the Western Conference with two regular-season matches to go.
They host Austin FC on Saturday, before taking on ninth-place Real Salt Lake in their final match on Decision Day.
The Galaxy are just one point behind RSL, who occupy the final wildcard spot, and Vanney is confident in his side's quality.
"The key here is to get ourselves into the playoffs, and then I think we can play against anyone," said Vanney.

"As we're healthy, and we get Chucky [Hirving Lozano] back, and we get Kyogo [Furuhashi] back, and we have Marco [Reus] back, we have a great team that can start, and we have great guys who could come in.
"We've lost like three of our last fourteen or something like that. So, we've been pretty stingy. We've been hard to beat.
"Obviously, we rotated and got beat up a little bit in St. Louis, but I felt like that was an anomaly.
"In general, I feel like nobody should want to play us as we get into the playoffs, and it's a team that's come together a little bit late because of all the movement in the summer.
"But I still think if we can do the business the last couple weeks, we are a very dangerous team going into the playoffs."
Austin's playoff hopes were dashed midweek after they lost 2-1 at home to RSL.
Austin took the lead through Jorge Alastuey, but could not hold on for the three points they needed to stay in playoff contention.
LA Galaxy – Joseph Paintsil
Joseph Paintsil recorded his first multi-goal match of the season on Sunday, scoring both of LA Galaxy's goals in their draw with Los Angeles FC.
It was the first multi-goal performance by a Galaxy player since before the World Cup break, when Gabriel Pec scored twice against Atlanta United on May 9.
Austin FC – Jorge Alastuey
Playing in his 15th career MLS match on Wednesday, Alastuey recorded his first career goal contribution with a goal in the second half.
Alastuey has recorded at least one shot in three straight matches after going six straight MLS matches without one prior to his current streak.
MATCH PREDICTION: LA GALAXY WIN

LA Galaxy are unbeaten in seven straight home matches (W4 D3), last losing at Dignity Health Sports Park in late July. This is their longest home unbeaten run in all competitions since a 12-match stretch (W11 D1) that culminated in winning the 2024 MLS Cup Final.
However, Austin have taken 13 points over their last six away matches (W4 D1 L1), including a 2-1 victory at Sporting Kansas City in their last road game.
Austin recorded a 2-1 victory at Dignity Health Sports Park in their last road match against LA Galaxy in July 2025, their first points at the Galaxy after losing the first four visits.
Austin had managed two goals in their first four away games against the Galaxy before scoring twice in their last visit.

867tayfi2f0r1ccqj3oifli5s.title: Jansen insists NYCFC 'will deal with' international absentees
867tayfi2f0r1ccqj3oifli5s.subtitle: Both New York City FC and Atlanta United will be without key players for their MLS clash at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Saturday.
paragraphs: Pascal Jansen expressed his disappointment in losing New York City FC players to the international break, but insists they "will deal with it" ahead of their trip to Atlanta United.
NYCFC are 10th in the Eastern Conference with just one MLS win since the Leagues Cup break after losing to rivals New York Red Bulls last time out.
Jansen will now be without goalkeeper Matt Freese against Atlanta, as well as defender Tayvon Gray and midfielder Aiden O'Neill, among a group of five players on international duty.
Jansen admitted some adjustments will be needed when they face Atlanta, but he is eager to pick up three points at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
"That's something that still amazes me in this league, that we have to play during a national team break," said the NYCFC boss.
"But it is what it is and we will deal with it. Unfortunately, we're coming off a tough game against Red Bull [a 1-0 loss]. I think we deserved more from that game.

"But now it's all full focus on Atlanta and we know we have a chance there, but we have to adjust a couple of things because there’s a few guys not available and this time not because of injury, because of international duty."
Atlanta, meanwhile, ended a four-game winless run in MLS with a 1-0 win over the Portland Timbers last time out.
The Five Stripes will also be missing key players against NYCFC, with Miguel Almiron and Aleksey Miranchuk both on international duty.

Since the start of last season, Miranchuk has recorded 95 chances created while Almiron has 87. They are the only pair of teammates to each create 80 or more chances since the start of the 2025 campaign, with both players setting up at least 40 shots for team-mates in each of the last two seasons.
Atlanta United – Matt Edwards
Due to players on international duty, Matt Edwards could start in defence for Atlanta.
After coming off the bench against Portland last time out, Edwards led his team-mates in interceptions (three) and aerial duels won (two), while winning five of his 10 duels overall.
New York City FC – Nicolas Fernandez Mercau
Nicolas Fernandez Mercau has been involved in 22 goals in his first full season with New York City FC (15 goals, seven assists).
Only three players in club history have contributed to more goals in a single regular season (David Villa, Maxi Moralez, Valentin Castellanos) with Castellanos the last to do so, in 2021 (27).
MATCH PREDICTION: ATLANTA UNITED WIN

Atlanta have suffered only two defeats in eight matches since returning from the Leagues Cup break in August (W4 D2). Only four Eastern Conference teams have collected more points than the Five Stripes (14) over that time.
And they have lost only one of nine all-time home matches against New York City FC (W4 D4), including a 4-3 win in the last meeting at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in March 2025.
Atlanta are one of two Eastern Conference teams (also Nashville SC) against whom NYCFC do not have multiple road wins.

NYCFC have managed just one win in their last nine regular-season matches (D4 L4), while their defeat to NYRB was their 10th loss of the year. NYCFC have lost 11 or more games in each of the previous five seasons after recording 10 or fewer losses in five straight seasons from 2016 to 2020.
Atlanta United – 44.4%
New York City FC – 31.3%

          Man City's Resilience, Lyon Dominate, Questions for Chelsea & Arsenal: UWCL Matchday 1 Lessons
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Yash Thakur / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Matchday 1 of the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League delivered drama, dominant displays and plenty of talking points. We dive into the data to analyse the key stories from the action.
The 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League is underway and Matchday 1 delivered a little bit of everything.
There were narrow wins, thrashings and end-to-end contests as Europe's elite began their quest for continental glory.
Using Opta data, we break down the standout performers and biggest talking points from the opening matchday of this season's UWCL.
The reigning WSL champions began their UWCL campaign with one of the toughest assignments possible, travelling to Munich to face a Bayern side ranked second in the Opta Power Rankings.
The contest delivered everything expected of two European heavyweights: goals, a missed penalty and late drama, with the points ultimately shared in a 2-2 draw.
In doing so, City became the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.

It was the first time in City’s history in the competition they had avoided defeat when trailing by two or more goals, while it was just the second time Bayern had failed to win a UWCL game in which they had led by 2+ goals, last doing so against Roma in November 2023.
José Barcala's team asserted themselves early, racing into a two-goal lead before the break. Their aggressive pressing forced City into mistakes, with Bayern recording 16 high turnovers.
Since 2019-20, only against Barcelona in December 2024 (25) and March 2021 (17) have City conceded more high turnovers in the competition.
City struggled to gain a foothold before half-time, managing only three attempts. But Beth Mead's goal shifted the momentum after the interval.

The visitors were then handed a golden opportunity to level from the penalty spot, only forEna Mahmutovic to brilliantly deny Khadija Shaw. It was the first penalty Shaw has missed since joining Manchester City.

Despite that setback, City continued to push and their persistence was rewarded in the 86th minute when Carlotta Wamser found the equaliser to complete the comeback with her first goal in light blue, and secure a valuable point on the road.
Andrée Jeglertz's influence from the bench again proved significant, as had been the case against Liverpool.

Second-half substitute Laura Blindkilde Brown provided the assist for Wamser's goal and helped City gain greater control in possession, offering composure against Bayern's intense press as the visitors finished the stronger of the two sides.
Arsenal and Chelsea both opened their European campaigns with 1-0 victories against HB Køge and Austria Wien respectively, but neither performance fully convinced.
With a heavyweight WSL meeting at Stamford Bridge looming this weekend, both sides left MD1 with three points, but just as many questions remain.
Arsenal needed a stoppage-time Mariona Caldentey penalty to overcome Danish champions Køge in a game they largely controlled but struggled to break open.
Renée Slegers' side monopolised possession, recording 69.7% of the ball and completing 620 passes at an 86% success rate, but their dominance rarely translated into clear-cut opportunities.

Despite attempting 19 shots, Arsenal generated only one big chance and managed just a single effort on target prior to Caldentey's winning penalty. It was another example of a recurring issue for the Gunners: controlling games without creating enough high-quality chances.
