          Triple Threat: Can London City Lionesses' Attacking Trio Make WSL History?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Alexia Putellas, Kadidiatou Diani and Daniëlle van de Donk have hit the ground running in London City Lionesses’ first five WSL matches of 2026-27. But how does their goal and assist output compare with the league’s most prolific attacking trios across history?

London City Lionesses’ 6-1 demolition of Tottenham last time out was more than a statement victory. It was a glimpse of what the club could become: an ambitious disruptor capable of unsettling the WSL’s established order.

Eder Maestre’s side did not simply outscore Spurs, but they repeatedly turned possession into dangerous attacks. The result was London City’s largest ever WSL victory, with the visitors recording 5.99 expected goals (xG) – the highest total by an away team in the competition since Opta’s records began in 2017-18.

They also scored six times from just 10 shots on target, the fewest by a team scoring 6+ goals in a WSL game since Chelsea’s 6-0 victory over Man Utd in May 2024 (nine shots on target), highlighting both the quality of their chances and their clinical finishing.

At the heart of the performance was the attacking trio of Alexia Putellas, Kadidiatou Diani and Daniëlle van de Donk. Putellas scored twice, Diani added two goals and an assist, while Van de Donk scored once and provided two assists. Between them, they contributed eight goal involvements in a performance that exposed the threat of London City’s revamped attack.
Just as striking was the fluidity between the three.

Diani held the right flank, Van de Donk drifted in from the left channel to attack the penalty area, and Putellas moved across the pitch to link play and create opportunities. Their roles were complementary giving Spurs few straightforward defensive tasks.

Although their stats stood out in the win over Spurs, in truth, the trio have displayed that form across the whole campaign. Over the first five WSL matchdays, the three players have registered 14 goal involvements in total: five for Van de Donk, five for Diani and four for Putellas. Their output has helped London City collect 12 points from a possible 15 and climb to third in the table before the international break.

That points tally is significant in its own right. No team to have collected at least 12 points after the opening five matches has finished below fifth in WSL history. For a club looking to build on last season’s sixth-place finish, the early signs suggest another step forward, with their attacking firepower central to the progress.

Their influence is clearest in the penalty area. Van de Donk leads London City with 30 touches in the opposition box, followed by Putellas (24) and Diani (19). The figures reflect their complementary roles, but also a shared strength: all three are consistently finding dangerous positions and putting themselves in a place to influence the outcome.

But how does this trio compare with the most prolific attacking combinations in WSL history? And if Putellas, Diani and Van de Donk can sustain anything close to their current rate of production, could they join the competition’s greatest ever trios?
Fourteen goal involvements in five matches is an impressive return. It's also a useful benchmark against some of the league’s most memorable attacking units.
Across WSL history, these are the standout combinations across total goal involvements to provide a measure of the challenge ahead:

The Chelsea trio of Sam Kerr, Fran Kirby and Bethany England set a formidable benchmark in 2020-21. Kerr and Kirby each recorded 28 non-penalty goal involvements, while England added 15 herself, taking their combined total to 71 – the highest of any three-player attacking combination in our comparison.

Arsenal’s holy trinity of Vivianne Miedema, Beth Mead and Van de Donk amassed 67 in 2018-19, while Man City’s Khadija Shaw, Chloe Kelly and Lauren Hemp combined for 53 in 2022-23. These are among the most well-known attacking combinations of the WSL era, offering a useful benchmark for London City’s new-look forward line.
The early-season numbers make for an intriguing comparison.

Across their first five matchdays, Chelsea’s 2020-21 trio and Man City’s 2022-23 combination each recorded 13 goal involvements. Arsenal’s three in 2018-19, however, had already amassed 25 – a reminder that blistering starts can take different paths over the course of a season.
The early return of the London City trio therefore offers a reason for optimism, not a reliable prediction of what is to come.

The expanded 14-team WSL season comprises 26 league matches. If the trio maintain their current average of 2.8 involvements per match, a simple extrapolation would give them 72.8 goal involvements across the campaign, enough to edge the Chelsea benchmark in this comparison.

But, the more meaningful question is whether London City can sustain enough of their current production to remain in the conversation as the season develops; their total 15 goals is only bettered by Tottenham and City on 16.

89F663B59BAF72C78C43E5A350AE9B66.title: Preview: Man United head to Stamford Bridge for Chelsea clash
89F663B59BAF72C78C43E5A350AE9B66.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Man United head to Stamford Bridge for Chelsea clashShareThe onus is on the Red Devils to end their eight-match winless run (3D, 5W), while the Blues will be eager to get over their recent setbacks.

Chelsea were enjoying a fine start to the season until last weekend, when Xabi Alonso‘s squad suffered a defeat in a London derby vs. Spurs, then were knocked out of the Carabao cup via a penalty shoot-out at Liverpool in midweek. With Chelsea without a domestic trophy since 2018, the Spaniard labelling the Carabao Cuo as “the least important competition for us” did not go down well with the fanbase.

The players, on the other hand, will benefit from a lighter schedule and will look to improve on their solid start – only Brighton & Hove Albion (23) and Manchester City (20) have scored more goals than the Blues, who currently sit fifth in the league.

To the surprise of many, Michael Carrick is set to lead Manchester United at Stamford Bridge after Jason Wilcox & co. decided to give the head coach another chance to turn the club's fortunes around following their worst start to a season in 40 years. With the under-fire squad sitting just a point off the relegation zone ahead of the London trip, the pressure is on the players to deliver on Saturday, as the passionate match-going supporters made their feelings crystal clear at Old Trafford last weekend. Interestingly enough, 13 of the 14 players which featured in United's victory at Stamford Bridge back in April are still part of the team.

Cole Palmer is enjoying life under Xabi Alonso and the 24-year-old is one of the front three (alongside Morgan Rogers and João Pedro) that has started the season well. The Manchester-born playmaker is the joint-top assist provider (3) and leading chance creator (17) in the squad, while only Morgan Gibbs-White (7) and Pascal Groß (7) boast more big chances created than the England international across the league. With the boyhood United fan missing the midweek action, the so-called ‘Cold Palmer' will be rested and eager to pile on the misery on the Red Devils.

Despite his questionable antics on and off the pitch lately, Bruno Fernandes remains the captain and arguably, the best player in United's squad on paper. Subsequently, the spotlight will be on the out-of-form Portugal international and the 32-year-old will get an opportunity to contribute and support the coaching staff's bid to turn things around after clearing-the-air with the coach. Last season's Premier League POTY is still our highest-rated player among his teammates, averaging a FotMob rating of 7.53. At the same time, all four of his goal contributions (3 goals, 1 assist) came in a single 90-minute appearance against Ipswich, which speaks volumes about the drop off in his numbers.

João Pedro joined Emiliano Martínez, Reece James and Jamie Gittens on the sidelines, but Cole Palmer is back after serving a one-match suspension and Emanuel Emegha finally made his return from injury in midweek.
Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Šeško are still unavailable for United, but Kobbie Mainoo is back in first-team training and ready to provide a huge boost in midfield.

It would take a monumental shift in both form and confidence for the Red Devils to leave Stamford Bridge with anything more than a point, and judging by their recent history and performances amid similar slumps, I expect Chelsea to celebrate a win despute their vulnerabilities at the back.

          Breaking Lines and Building Bonds: Pascal Groß is Leading Brighton's Impressive Start
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author, Reem Sarraf / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Brighton & Hove Albion have made an excellent start to the 2026-27 Premier League season, and their 35-year-old creative spark has been at the centre of it.
Age catches up with all of us, but it seems like footballers are getting labelled as ‘past their best’ earlier and earlier these days.
There are even players in their late 20s being hit with the infamous ‘his legs have gone’ accusation, a claim which often just seems to mean ‘he’s not playing very well and is over the age of 25’.
However, some Premier League ‘uncs’ are fighting back, and this past weekend was a particularly good one for some golden oldies.

At 36 years and 115 days, Jordan Henderson became the oldest Chelsea player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game, overtaking Gianluca Vialli (33y 245d), with his two goals and an assist against Bournemouth.

Meanwhile, another Premier League player of a similar vintage was also instrumental in his team’s victory. Like Henderson, Brighton’s Pascal Groß probably sometimes feels a bit like the famous Steve Buscemi ‘how do you do fellow kids?’ meme from 30 Rock when lining up alongside his much younger teammates. But he is more than justifying his place in the team.

After producing two assists in the 5-0 thrashing of Coventry City, and another in the 3-0 win over Arsenal before the international break, at 35 years and 117 days, Groß became the oldest player to provide an assist in three successive Premier League games since Ryan Giggs in February 2012 (38y 68d) when he set up Maxim De Cuyper for the opener in a 2-0 win at Sunderland.

It was the latest in a string of excellent performances by the German international since his return to Brighton last season. They say you should never go back, but Groß is absolutely thriving in his second spell in East Sussex.

Between joining the club from Ingolstadt in 2017 and leaving for Borussia Dortmund in 2024, Groß managed 32 goals and 52 assists in 261 games for Brighton. Since his return in January of this year, he has five goals and seven assists in 30 games, but eight of those goal involvements (four goals, four assists) have come in just nine games this season.
Groß is rolling back the years for his manager Fabian Hürzeler – who is two years his junior – helping Brighton to make a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign.
“I said, I think in my last press conference, that you can compare him a little bit with a good wine. The older he gets, the better he is,” Hürzeler told reporters after the win over Arsenal.

“He’s not only a player who makes his teammates better, he’s not only a player who really understands the game so well. I think the things you can’t measure are the things we see in the daily business and on the training ground.

“He has the skill of creating social bonds between all the players we have. We have so many different nationalities, so many different generations, and he has an understanding of all these dynamics. He brings these different backgrounds together and I think that’s something we sometimes underestimate.”

The Seagulls are flying high, sitting third in the Premier League, and through to the fourth round of the League Cup after a comeback win over Manchester United at Old Trafford. They have won their last three league games by a combined aggregate of 10-0, including the aforementioned 3-0 thumping of champions Arsenal.
And Groß is not just adding vital experience in the midfield, but is pulling the strings and producing moments of quality when it matters.

He has created 18 chances in the Premier League this season, the most of any player, while six of those have been defined as ‘big chances’ – a chance from which a team would be reasonably expected to score – which has only been bettered by Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White (7).
While he takes set-pieces, not all of Groß’ chances are coming from dead-balls; he has created 13 chances from open play, which, again, only Gibbs-White (15) can better in the Premier League.

That follows on from his previous spell at the club. In each of his seven seasons with Brighton prior to joining Dortmund in August 2024, Groß created a minimum of 52 chances in the Premier League. The only other player to have made as many in a single campaign for the club in the competition is Solly March (67 in 2022-23).
He remains as cultured on the ball as ever, and while he isn’t topping the charts for line-breaking passes, he is making incisive and dangerous passes when he does attempt them.

Groß has made 62 line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, the joint-41st most, but only Bruno Fernandes (19) and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (14) have made more line-breaking passes leading to a shot in the next 10 seconds than him (13), while he has the joint-most line-breaking passes leading to a goal in the next 10 seconds (3).

8A88090C0A1D9C785B08E716F507010D.title: Alexander Isak is back to his best and the key to Liverpool having a successful season
8A88090C0A1D9C785B08E716F507010D.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesAlexander Isak is back to his best and the key to Liverpool having a successful seasonShareAfter his Premier League-record transfer from Newcastle, Alexander Isak is finally showing signs of his best form as Liverpool’s number nine.

For £125m, Liverpool expected Alexander Isak to be one of the best strikers in the Premier League. After all, that’s what he had been for Newcastle United. Isak’s capture last year was meant to elevate the Reds’ forward line to another level and yet it’s only recently that Isak has started to show signs of his old form.

Isak’s goal against Brighton last Sunday was his sixth in his last six Premier League outings. While Liverpool’s form under new manager Andoni Iraola has been inconsistent, their Swedish centre forward is growing in stature. Isak is looking more like the player that lit up St James’ Park.

“Alex is threatening, especially if we can get him in those positions,” said Iraola when asked about Isak’s recent impact. “In this case [of the goal against Brighton], it's a matter of [Barcola] winning the duel and being faster than the opposition to get us in that position. If we can put him in those positions, we can provide him [with] good crosses, good situations, he will score the goals.”

Iraola is right to highlight how Isak’s output largely depends on the players around him. Liverpool have completely revamped their forward line over the last two seasons with Mohamed Salah, Luis Díaz and Darwin Núñez leaving to be replaced by Isak, Hugo Ekitike, Bradley Barcola, Víctor Muñoz and Florian Wirtz.

When everyone is fit, it’s not clear how Iraola will accommodate everyone. Ekitke was one of the bright spots in an otherwise dull season for Liverpool last term with the French forward most impactful in a central role. It’s difficult to envisage how Iraola can possibly field Ekitike and Isak in the same team without shifting one of them out wide.

Iraola is also still working on the balance of his left and right wingers. Against Brighton, Barcola played on the right side despite being more comfortable on the left. This created space for Cody Gakpo to start in his favoured role as an inside-out left winger, but dropped Muñoz to the bench when the Spaniard has started well for Liverpool this season.

At Newcastle, Isak played best when he had Jacob Murphy, a right-footer, to get crosses into the box from the right side. Barcola, also a right-footer, is increasingly picking up on Isak’s movements inside the penalty area, as demonstrated by the Swede’s goal against Brighton which was set up for him by the former Paris Saint-Germain player.

Isak is having to adapt his game to suit Liverpool’s playing style. At Newcastle, the Swede had open space to attack due to their emphasis on transition moments. Isak is among the best in the Premier League at breaking into space behind an opposition backline. Once he’s through, there’s no catching him.

Liverpool, however, are a more possession-orientated side. Iraola’s instincts as a coach might be to tip the Reds towards the transition-heavy style that worked so well for him at Bournemouth, but the talent level inside the Anfield dressing room means Liverpool are naturally expected to operate within the opposition half.

This explains why Isak hasn’t always been the most involved for Liverpool this season. Even as the 27-year-old has found a rich vein of scoring form, he has been a peripheral figure in his team’s possession play – against Brighton, Isak registered just 20 touches of the ball, the lowest of any starting Liverpool player.

Erling Haaland has altered expectations of how involved a centre forward should be in the modern age. It’s common for the Norwegian to be an afterthought in Manchester City’s build-up. Inside the penalty area, though, Haaland has the sharpest instincts of any striker in Europe. Isak is developing a similar quality.

Not every part of Liverpool’s new-look team is functioning so well. There are questions over the balance of the midfield and whether Dominik Szoboszlai and Wirtz can be accommodated in the same team. At left back and right back, there are concerns too, although on-loan Ronald Araújo has proved a good stop-gap solution on the right.

When Ekitike returns from injury next year, Iraola will have a headache over who to favour as his first-choice centre forward. Ekitike was the obvious pick before his layoff, but Isak is now delivering in the way Liverpool expected to when they broke the Premier League transfer record to sign him.

That, however, is a good problem to have and Isak increasingly feels like the key to Liverpool enjoying a positive first season under Iraola. A title challenge might be beyond them, but Isak in such free-scoring form raises the level of what is possible for the Anfield outfit. A transitional season can still be a successful one.

          Is This Where Tottenham’s Season Turns For the Better?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After Spurs made their worst ever start to a Premier League season, they need an immediate and stark improvement. So, is that what we are about to see?
It can hardly get any worse than this, right?
That will be the thought – no, the hope – of Tottenham fans as their team returns to action this weekend.

Spurs have started the season miserably. With just two points and a goal difference six goals the wrong side of zero, they are bottom of the table having made their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign.

Until the 86th minute of their fifth game, at which point they were 3-0 down at home to Aston Villa, they hadn’t even scored a single goal in their previous seven hours and 26 minutes of league action this season.

It’s been a tough watch. An expensively assembled squad of very talented players who are – and very much looked – entirely unfamiliar with one another have combined to form far less than the sum of their parts. This is a brand new £300 million team almost completely incapable of finding the back of the net.

It started off with a dire display in defeat at Brentford. Then came a 2-0 loss at Newcastle, before one goalless draw that was very nearly a defeat at Nottingham Forest but for a controversial VAR intervention, and another, this time at home to Everton, that was about as uninspiring as they come. Then, last time out, they were cut through by Villa before a late rally made the scoreline even the slightest bit respectable.

The decision to disallow a would-be Neco Williams winner for Forest aside, just about everything that could have gone wrong has done. And if Spurs don’t turn their season around soon, before they know it, they will be in a third relegation battle in three years following back-to-back 17th-place finishes.
So, this three-week international break that comes without precedent must act as a turning point for Roberto De Zerbi and his team.
The fact it is without precedent is important because we have no previous experience of how teams will react to this long a break, and so it has the potential to act as the chance for a hard reset.

Spurs must turn into a positive the fact that many of their players have been underperforming so badly that only 13 members of their first-team squad were called up for international duty, and at least two of them have no chance of playing this weekend (Ben Davies and Martin Dúbravka). De Zerbi gave the rest of his players a week off initially, but since then he has had two full weeks of training with plenty of key players. There has to be a reaction to their woeful start and the threat of another season fighting it out at the bottom of the table, and an impact of having so much time training together.

De Zerbi might argue things aren’t as awful as the table suggests. Spurs ‘won’ on expected goals in three of their five games – Newcastle, Villa and Forest – and their underlying numbers are in some sense reasonably positive. They are placed far higher up Opta’s expected points table, for example.

The xPts model uses xG data from each match to calculate how games deserved to finish based on the quality and quantity of chances at each end. It simulates the number of goals each team scored in the match based on the chances they created and then simulates the match 10,000 times to work out how often the game is won, lost and drawn. Teams are then awarded between zero and three xPts based on the proportion they win, draw and lose.
Spurs headed into the international break 13th in the xPts table, suggesting they created enough chances to take enough points to be safely in mid-table.

There are a few sidenotes worth considering here, most notably that Spurs haven’t, in reality, been finishing their chances off, and that is precisely why they are bottom of the actual table. That needs to change.

Also, some of their superiority when it comes to xG is down to game state. They had more reason to attack than Newcastle after Anthony Elanga’s opener, as well as for the whole second half against Villa, having conceded on the stroke of half-time. Only three teams have been losing for a greater proportion of their Premier League matches this season than Spurs (36%), so they have been forced to chase the game more than most.

That said, there have also been periods when Spurs have dominated with the scores level. They might have won at Forest on another day, spurning a couple of very good chances, while at home to Newcastle they could and probably should have gone ahead in the first half. It was the same against Villa, when the early performance and the chances they had were even better.

Arguably their best display of the season, however, came in the EFL Cup defeat at Anfield. Though it came against a weakened Liverpool side and still ended in an early exit from one of only two competitions Spurs had any chance of winning, their display was still worthy of some praise. They created a couple of huge early chances, the type of which they simply must start putting away with even the slightest regularity. They could have been out of sight after half an hour but, as has been a theme of their season so far, they were punished ruthlessly for failing to build on a positive start.

That has become a bit of a problem, and they simply have to become more resilient, more durable, when it comes to the defensive side of things. Consecutive clean sheets against Forest and Everton were positive signs, but the ease with which Villa tore through the Spurs defence last time out was concerning.
“I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated for the performance,” De Zerbi said after that defeat. “We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal.”

          Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé Strikes Twice as José Mourinho Claims Clásico Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 25, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Kylian Mbappé was the hero as Real Madrid cut the gap at the top of La Liga with a deserved win at Barcelona. Check out all the best Clásico numbers with our stats page.
Kylian Mbappé scored twice, including an 87th-minute winner, as Real Madrid claimed a huge 2-1 victory over their Clásico rivals Barcelona at Camp Nou.

Barça were hoping to become the first team to ever start a season in one of Europe's top five leagues with 10 straight victories, having already built a six-point buffer to Madrid ahead of Sunday's clash.

Hansi Flick's hosts were up against it when Gerard Martín's attempted clearance ricocheted in off Mbappé in the 41st minute, although Raphinha's 13th league goal of the season drew them level shortly after the hour mark.
However, Mbappé was on hand to slot into an empty net following a lightning quick Madrid break late on, prompting wild celebrations from manager José Mourinho on the sidelines.
Madrid quickly got on the front foot as they looked to quiet a raucous Catalan crowd, but no white shirts were lurking for a tap-in when Joan García could only parry Arda Güler's drive.

Raphinha had three efforts at the other end, the second of which was the most threatening as his first-time strike whistled over the crossbar following some industrious work from Pedri, while Andrii Lunin – standing in for the ill Thibaut Courtois – denied Anthony Gordon at his near post.

Yan Diomande was one of Madrid's brightest sparks in attack, and their opening goal came from him being slipped into the area by Marc Cucurella. The Ivorian's centre was far from his best, but Martín blasted it straight off Mbappé and into the net.
Barça should have had a quickfire equaliser when Lamine Yamal scuffed an uncharacteristically poor finish wide, but Flick's team were cut open on two more occasions before the interval.
Mbappé rifled against the inside of the post, only for the offside flag to go up against him, but Diomande was onside when he broke in behind and hit the side netting moments later.
Madrid spurned another excellent counter-attacking chance early in the second half, with Jude Bellingham failing to get his pass off when Mbappé was supporting him against an isolated Martín.
And Barça made those reprieves count when Raphinha's shot proved too hot for Lunin to handle, after the Brazilian was cleverly found by Pedri on the right side of the area.
Lunin made a terrific, one-handed save to keep out Martín's header shortly afterwards, though he was lucky to see one Yamal effort drift narrowly wide and another smack Dean Huijsen in the face.

However, there was a cruel twist to come at the other end as, after some superb work from the outstanding Bellingham, substitute Eduardo Camavinga burst down the right flank and centred for Mbappé, who simply could not miss.
Just 24 hours before the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony takes place in London, Sunday's Clasico saw two of the main contenders for the prize – Yamal and Mbappé – go head-to-head.
And though the voting has long since been finalised, it was Mbappé who provided one final reminder of his credentials to be crowned the best player in the world.

There may have been a huge slice of fortune about Mbappé's opener, but his brace took him to five goals in two visits to Barça as a Madrid player. That is the most by any Blancos player since the start of 2013-14, surpassing Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema (four each).

Yamal, meanwhile, missed a glaring chance to equalise in the first half and was unable to hit the net with any of his five shots, which were worth a team-high 0.51 expected goals (xG). He also failed to create a single chance and only completed 76.6% of his passes (47/76)
And, on a night where Barça could have opened up a huge nine-point gap to Madrid and made La Liga history in the process, it was Mourinho who earned the bragging rights.

His unbeaten run in Clásico matches – which dates back to his previous spell in charge of Madrid – now stands at six games (W4 D2). He is just the third Blancos coach to enjoy such a run, after Miguel Muñoz (1962 to 1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001 to 2003) both had seven-match streaks.

          Jérémy Jacquet Showing That Not Every Player Needs a Bedding-in Period
        
      
                          
                      Oct 10, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It has been an up-and-down start to the season for Liverpool, but one huge positive has been the early form of new arrival Jérémy Jacquet. So, just how good has the French defender been?
When you get praise from Zinedine Zidane, you know you’ve made it.
Jérémy Jacquet earned his first call-up to the France national team in this latest international break, starting UEFA Nations League games against Türkiye and Italy, and impressing in both.

When asked about the impact of the 21-year-old centre-back in the draw with Italy, Zidane said: “Very good. Very, very good. Brave. He wasn’t afraid to come out a long way. Very good in the duels. He was, once again, very good. I said it four times.”
Unfortunately, Jacquet had to be left out of the return game against Italy on Monday due to what Zidane described as a “slight knock”, but he had already made a solid impression.
That call-up was merited, too. Jacquet has made an excellent start to the season with new club Liverpool, taking to the Premier League like a canard to eau.
When Liverpool signed Jacquet in January, the assumption was he would be eased in slowly.

He was lined up to join the Reds this summer in a reported £60 million deal from Rennes, but with compatriot Ibrahima Konaté leaving for Real Madrid, a gap opened up that Jacquet has gleefully stepped into.
Despite being just 21 years old and playing in France’s second tier just two seasons ago, Jacquet has slipped seamlessly into Premier League football at Anfield.
Liverpool also brought Ronald Araujo in on loan from Barcelona, but he has been deployed at right-back more often than centre-back, with Jacquet trusted by Andoni Iraola to partner Virgil van Dijk.

Jacquet suffered a shoulder injury in his first game for Rennes after confirming his summer switch to Merseyside, then also had a setback ahead of pre-season. But Iraola still backed him from the beginning, even though he was signed before the Spaniard’s own arrival. Jacquet started Liverpool’s opening game of the campaign, and though he came off early in the 2-2 draw at Newcastle United as well as in the stalemate with Nottingham Forest, it was clear he was just having his minutes managed as he got up to full fitness.
Jacquet has started all five of Liverpool’s Premier League games this season, as well as the UEFA Champions League win over Atlético Madrid.

The 1-0 win at Bournemouth last time out made it three consecutive clean sheets in the Premier League for Liverpool for the first time since September 2024, and Jacquet played a significant role in that achievement.
So, just what has made Jacquet’s first couple of months in England so impressive?

Back in January, we analysed his game to see why Liverpool were willing to fork out so much money for an inexperienced young defender. Jacquet had shown in his time in France that he was aerially dominant, composed on the ball, and a front-foot defender who could win the ball often.
He has been all that and more already for Liverpool, too.

Jacquet won 75.5% of his aerial duels in Ligue 1 last season, the most of any player to contest at least 40. He has carried that on in England, winning 10 of 13 aerials in the Premier League (76.9%), more than both Van Dijk (71.4%) and Araújo (72.0%). Only Manchester United’s Harry Maguire (17 of 22 – 77.3%) has won a greater proportion among players to have contested 13+ aerials.

He has also been outstanding in ground duels, winning 19 of 25 (76.0%). Of Premier League defenders to have contested 15+ ground duels this season, only Everton’s James Tarkowski has won a greater share (19 of 21 – 90.5%).

A metric called ‘true tackles’ can give an even better idea of his ability. It’s the sum of successful tackles (where possession is regained or when the ball goes out of play and is safe), challenges lost (where a player attempts a tackle and doesn’t connect with the ball) and fouls when attempting a tackle. Jacquet has attempted 15 true tackles in the Premier League this season, with a success rate of 73.3%; no player to have attempted as many has a higher win percentage.

His ability in possession has also made him suited to Iraola’s style of play. At Bournemouth, the Spaniard loved his centre-backs getting the ball forward with their progressive passing, and that has continued at Liverpool. Jacquet has played 57 passes into the opposition’s final third in the Premier League this season; only Van Dijk (76) and Tottenham’s Jan Paul van Hecke (62) have attempted more.

8aqj1c1phdxczwjolw9tv6cf.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Manchester City: Wamser rescues draw in Women's Champions League opener
8aqj1c1phdxczwjolw9tv6cf.subtitle: Bayern Munich led 2-0 against Manchester City, but the Women's Super League champions fought back to salvage a point at Uhlsport Park.
paragraphs: Khadija Shaw missed a penalty but Carlotta Wamser's late goal saw Manchester City rescue a 2-2 draw in their Women's Champions League opener against Bayern Munich.
Bayern, last season's semi-finalists, charged into a 2-0 lead inside the first 28 minutes at Uhlsport Park.
Giulia Gwinn was played in by Linda Dallmann and made no mistake with a crisp, powerful finish.

Bayern were then in cruise control when they capitalised on a defensive mix-up from Man City, with Pernille Harder's cross causing havoc, and Kerstin Casparij was only able to turn it into her own net.
Yet, on the cusp of half-time, Beth Mead dragged City back into the contest as Casparij's cross found its way through to her, and she duly tucked home.
City looked all set to draw level around the hour mark, after Aoba Fujino was brought down by Ena Mahmutovic in Bayern's box.
Shaw, though, showed unusual profligacy as she saw her attempt saved by Mahmutovic, who atoned for her mistake.
Yet City did get their equaliser in the 86th minute, with Wamser whipping a fine effort in at the near post after she met Laura Blindkilde Brown's tee-up.
Man City show powers of recovery
City have made a fantastic start to their Women's Super League title defence, winning all three of their matches so far, but they endured a miserable opening half-an-hour of their European campaign.
This was their first meeting against Bayern, or indeed any German team, in this competition, although City should probably have expected their hosts to make a fast start.
After all, Bayern had won seven of their previous 11 Champions League matches against English teams, including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
Harder is just one off scoring her 50th Women's Champions League goal. She is aiming to become only the third player to reach this milestone, after Ada Hegerberg (69) and Eugenie Le Sommer (50).
And though Harder did not score, she was a threat throughout, and she laid on two great chances late on for Edna Imade, who could have done better with her finishes.
As it was, Andree Jeglertz will at least be able to reflect on a spirited City comeback, and they rounded out with a fairly even stat sheet.

Bayern created chances worth 2.03 expected goals from 15 shots, while City had opportunities worth a combined 2.31 xG from just eight attempts. Room for improvement, but definitely a decent showing in attack.

8jljkcpyeu961qu54un6ky8hs.title: Sessegnon says winless Fulham must take 'a hard look' at themselves
8jljkcpyeu961qu54un6ky8hs.subtitle: Fulham are in desperate need of a win against Hull City, with Alvaro Arbeloa's future already in major doubt just six games into the season.
paragraphs: Ryan Sessegnon says everyone at Fulham must take a hard look at themselves amid their winless start to the season, but he also stressed togetherness is key ahead of facing Hull City.
Fulham conspired to lose a game they had led with 88 minutes on the clock last time out, as Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea struck to clinch a remarkable 2-1 win for Ipswich Town.
That late turnaround made Sessegnon's rasping strike from distance inconsequential and left Alvaro Arbeloa's side bottom of the Premier League with just two points on the board.

With two more games against newly promoted opposition to come in the next two weeks – at home to Hull and away to Coventry City – there is mounting speculation that Arbeloa's spell in charge could be a short one.
Only once have Fulham endured a longer winless start to a top-flight campaign, failing to win any of their first seven games in 1951-52, and Sessegnon says they must present a united front.

"We need more togetherness, to demand more from each other and set higher standards for ourselves, because it's going to be a hard season, so we need to stick together," Sessegnon told the club's website.
"Obviously, we're very frustrated, disappointed and we need to take a hard look at ourselves. We need to stick together and keep going.
"The gaffer even said before the game, the last two wins they [Ipswich] have had, they've scored in the last minute, and it happened again.

8kytbfesbabv1coa49h5j3z94.title: Carrick determined to lead Man Utd back to their best after 'losing our way'
8kytbfesbabv1coa49h5j3z94.subtitle: Manchester United are on a torrid run of form, and Michael Carrick delivered an impassioned speech to start his latest press conference.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United have "lost our way" this season, but he remains confident they will find their groove once more.
Carrick took over at United in January and enjoyed a successful caretaker spell, leading the club back to the Champions League, and was made the permanent boss back in May.

However, it has been a dismal start to 2026-27 for United, who have won just two games in all competitions, with their most recent victory coming on September 10 against Sabah in UEFA's premier competition.

United have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4 L2), their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87 – also one victory after seven games.
They are winless in their last seven matches in all competitions (D3 L4) heading into their Premier League clash with Bournemouth on Sunday.
It is their worst such streak since a run of eight matches without victory between November and December 2015.

But Carrick, who is coming under increasing pressure with reports suggesting the club's hierarchy are starting to look at potential replacements, was not shying away from their poor form and is confident the club will get back to their best.
"I think recently we haven't had a good time; I think that's pretty obvious," Carrick said in a passionate statement to start his press conference.

"I totally accept that. What we're going through at the moment. We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things that I was seeing and that we were doing as a team.
"We haven't done well enough lately, I think that's pretty obvious to say, and we've had a spell that we're really not happy with.
"Wednesday was a bad night; it was a bad night for a lot of reasons, and it was a bad night that hurt a lot. It hurt me to see us play that way, to see how the game panned out.
"As I said, after the game it was really unacceptable for us to play like that and to be like that.
"My responsibility is to get a team on a pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters, and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show.

"We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I'm totally, fully aware of and definitely doing something about. I think it's important that we all recognise that; I certainly recognise it.

"Our supporters are of the utmost importance to me and this football club, and for them to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year, for us to have that about us and that connection and that real vigour and intensity and enjoyment and passion that we all felt through that period was something that we need to get back to, and we will get back to it.
"I fully believe that, but I think it's important that we recognise that we haven't been doing that.

"I said it after the [Como] game, Manchester United is always bigger and always has been, always will be bigger than any single individual. Bigger than me, bigger than any of the players, and it always has been.
"It was based on being humble, having humility and hard work, and we can never lose that, and I won't let us lose that. We've had it for a spell; I feel very strongly about that."
Things do not get any easier for United, with Bournemouth next up; they are winless in their last six against the Cherries (D4 L2).
United then face Chelsea, Aston Villa, rivals Liverpool and high-flying Brentford in their next four Premier League games.
"I think it inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players and the group that we've shown for a good period of time and that we're capable of it.

"We're in a moment where it's not gone well, so we need to show exactly what it means. Respect this football club, respect what it takes to be here, respect what it takes to win, what you have to do to win. I'm not entitled to be here; entitlement cannot be at this football club. We're not entitled to win.
"We've won in the past, we've got an incredible history, but that doesn't mean that you're entitled to just win. I'm fully aware of that; it takes hard work; it takes a lot of sacrifice.
"You've got to invest yourself in the football club, and you've got to do a lot of things that maybe aren't so nice, but you've got to do it for each other, and you've got to win.

"I think it's important we live up to that, and it's important for me to push those values, and it's important for our supporters to feel that. Moving forward, we've had it; we've kind of lost our way a little bit, if I'm totally honest, and we'll get it back. I'm totally confident we'll get it back.
"Respect this football club, respect what it takes because it's very, very important to me."
Another talking point after the Como defeat was captain Bruno Fernandes' comments, where he appeared to criticise Carrick's tactics when it came to applying pressure on Como.
It follows Lisandro Martinez's criticism of the United hierarchy and technical director Jason Wilcox.
Fernandes is not set to be stripped of the captaincy after, with Carrick determined to move on from both incidents.
"We need to move forward in the right direction, and we need to do things to enable us to do that," he said.
When pressed if he would strip Fernandes of the captaincy, he said: "The most important thing for me is the team and the dynamics in the squad. It is about the football club.
"Whatever the situation is, I will always do what is best for the football club."

8ngntlgn90de1kwy3ivf5fnfm.title: Bayern defender Tah refuses to underestimate Viking threat in Champions League
8ngntlgn90de1kwy3ivf5fnfm.subtitle: Bayern Munich will be targeting another big win in the Champions League when they face Norwegian side Viking on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Jonathan Tah insisted Bayern Munich will "never underestimate an opponent" as they prepare to face Viking in the Champions League.

This will be the first time that a team has faced two different Norwegian opponents in their opening two matches of a European Cup or Champions League campaign, with Bayern already beating Bodo/Glimt 5-0 on matchday one this term.
Jamal Musiala, Harry Kane, Alphonso Davies and Michael Olise were all on target in a stunning second-half performance against Bodo.
Bayern have scored 62 goals across 22 games since a team last managed to keep a clean sheet against them in the Champions League (0-3 loss to Feyenoord in January 2025).
Since the start of last season, the only teams that have held Bayern to under two goals in the competition are Arsenal (3-1 loss) and Paris Saint-Germain (1-1 draw).
Despite their impressive record, Tah believes Viking will pose plenty of threats of their own.
"We know they'll be confident. They're champions and top of the [Norwegian] table," said Tah about Viking.
"They're really good at set-pieces. They won't hide, even if it's against Bayern.
"We also saw against Stuttgart [on Matchday one] that they didn't just sit back. That's not their style of play, and we're not expecting that, either.
"It's always important that we never underestimate an opponent. There's always a lot of talk about favourites, but we don't talk like that.
"We focus on our potential and our game. We always want to do that. It doesn't matter who the opponent is. We always want to give 100%."
This will be the 10th time Bayern have faced a Norwegian opponent in European competition, going unbeaten in the previous nine (W7 D2) and averaging 3.3 goals per game (30 goals in total).
Viking have lost each of their four games against German sides this century, while failing to score in three of them.
Their opening game of this Champions League campaign was an away defeat at Stuttgart (1-3).
"It's the Champions League. Every game is a challenge," said Bayern boss Vincent Kompany.
"If we come here and say we want to be Bayern, then that's a question of mentality.
"It's a special game for Viking, but I don't want anyone to feel like it's not important for us.
"No matter what the game brings, we'll go into it thinking that anything can happen."

8nw3v3yjb9ns1u5qpusbsjcz1.title: Real Madrid struggle inevitable after Kroos retirement, claims former assistant Ancelotti
8nw3v3yjb9ns1u5qpusbsjcz1.subtitle: Real Madrid have not won silverware across the past two seasons, and Davide Ancelotti feels Toni Kroos' retirement is the reason why.
paragraphs: Davide Ancelotti believes Real Madrid's struggles in recent seasons have stemmed from the retirement of midfielder Toni Kroos.
Kroos spent 10 seasons with Madrid after joining from Bayern Munich, winning four LaLiga titles and five Champions Leagues among 22 trophies during his time in the Spanish capital.
He made 465 appearances for Los Blancos, scoring 28 goals and providing 93 assists while forming a formidable midfield partnership with Luka Modric and Casemiro.
Madrid have failed to win any major silverware across the last two seasons under Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa, with Jose Mourinho now at the helm to try and change things.
Lille boss Davide Ancelotti, who formerly served as Madrid's assistant, insisted trying to replace someone like Kroos would be a mistake for Los Blancos.
"I don't want everything I say about Madrid to be interpreted as criticism, but when Modric or Kroos were there, every movement into space was followed by a ball arriving there," he told AS.
"I'm not saying that the footballers they have now don't have that ability. What I'm saying is that, to play vertically, you need someone who knows how to deliver the ball.
"Being vertical doesn't mean having eight runners. It also means having someone who can launch them. It's a style of play.
"You lose something that you will never get back. The best player in the world in his position. You can’t say, 'I need another Kroos,' because there isn’t another one.
"He was the owner of the match. He controlled the tempo. The game was played at the rhythm he wanted. He decided things, and he was fundamental because he managed the pace of the match.
"Inevitably, for the way Real Madrid played, losing Toni was extremely difficult. Suddenly, they lost so many things."

8r4cscg9vsoe11iz2zvr06c76.title: Tuchel: England have a plan for Spain
8r4cscg9vsoe11iz2zvr06c76.subtitle: England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain, and Thomas Tuchel is determined to start with three points.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel revealed England "have a plan" to defeat Spain in their Nations League opener on Saturday.
The Three Lions host the world champions at Wembley Stadium in both of their first matches since the World Cup in the summer.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final, while England beat France 6-4 in the third-place play-off – their best finish at the tournament since 1966.
Luis de la Fuente's side are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest-ever such streak by a European nation.
Tuchel conceded England will have their work cut out against Spain and believes La Roja's possession-based style is a disadvantage for his side.
"I think it is an advantage in general. Not only against us, but against everyone," said Tuchel.
"This is how they play. I think they rely on that. This is how they train and they were brought up. This is clearly part of them.
"But at the moment, I think the more you analyse Spain and their last matches they played in, you have to admire the way in which they defend. They added this to their game.
"It is so difficult for every single team in the world to create chances against them. We have a plan, and we have ambition, and we want to prove the opposite.
"We want to be the exception to the rule, but at the moment they are a very complete team."

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2); those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
Spain have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
England winger Anthony Gordon previously stated the Three Lions must play to their own strengths, but captain Harry Kane believes they can mirror Spain's style if needed.

"I get what he's saying," Kane said about Gordon's comments. "It's culture for Spain, playing a certain style from five, six or seven years old until they're professionals. In England, it's not so much like that.
"It doesn't mean we can't play under pressure or keep the ball. We still have a lot of amazing technical players – but we have a lot of strengths that they don't have; physicality, pace and power.
"They way we press and win duels, a lot of Premier League style football in a way.
"I think at our best we combine both. We're not just a team that play like Spain, but we have a lot of strengths that we can showcase."

8udkrq0y8no1fnmxnu6yujk8.title: Gordon: 'I've been dying to play with Trent for England'
8udkrq0y8no1fnmxnu6yujk8.subtitle: Trent Alexander-Arnold marked his England return with an assist against Czechia, and Anthony Gordon enjoyed playing alongside him.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon said he had been "dying" to play with Trent Alexander-Arnold for England, after the duo combined to great effect in Tuesday's Nations League win over Czechia.
The Three Lions bounced back from their 3-2 defeat to Spain with a 2-0 victory in Prague, with Gordon and Harry Kane on target following Pavel Sulc's red card.
Gordon's goal – which was the first he has scored with his head for his country – took him to eight goal involvements in his last nine appearances for England (four goals, four assists).
Gordon was also on target against Spain on Saturday, and he is just the second Barcelona player to score in back-to-back games for England, after Gary Lineker in 1989.

He was picked out superbly by Alexander-Arnold's deep delivery to the far post, with the Real Madrid full-back winning his first cap in over a year, having been omitted from Thomas Tuchel's squads throughout last season and for the World Cup.
Alexander-Arnold's assist was his first for England since September 2024, against Finland in the last edition of the Nations League, under Lee Carsley.

"I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass," Gordon said of Alexander-Arnold, talking to ITV Sport after the game.
"That's why he's so good and I've been dying to play with him for that reason.
"He's had his own journey with England. He would've liked to have played more than he has, but he's been a great character during this camp, I've really enjoyed being around him."
When those comments were put to Alexander-Arnold, he replied: "It's a great compliment, and he's great to play with.
"I spoke to Ant at half-time and said, 'if I'm getting into those spaces, make sure you get to the back post'. You don't expect to get it that fast, but we did and it worked.
"I try to get the ball and try and see what the best play is, to try and play forward and create something, and I was able to make that pass.
"When they go down to 10 men there's more pressure on us to win the game, but actually it makes it more difficult, they get very compact and defend.
"It was very hard to break them down, but we got that early on in the second half, which is what we needed."
Reflecting on his time out of the England setup, Alexander-Arnold – who has won on 20 of his 27 international starts – added: "It's always an honour to represent my country.
"It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England. It was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, and hopefully he is happy with how I played."

8wxwp6t0j00l1a7ppgt10cly5.title: Rogers rates start to Chelsea career '10 out of 10'
8wxwp6t0j00l1a7ppgt10cly5.subtitle: Chelsea are preparing to resume their Premier League campaign, and Morgan Rogers has enjoyed every minute since arriving from Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Morgan Rogers would rate the start of his Chelsea career as a 10 out of 10, even if the Blues' results have been mixed ahead of Saturday's meeting with Bournemouth.
After winning their first two Premier League games under Xabi Alonso, Chelsea went into the international break on a three-game winless run (D1 L2), being trounced 3-0 by Brentford last time out.
They sit 10th in the table ahead of hosting Bournemouth, who are themselves 17th with three points, having failed to win any of their first five games under Marco Rose.
Rogers' individual statistics have been strong, though, as he has three goals and one assist already this season, following his British-record £117m move from Aston Villa.
Only Joao Pedro (three goals, three assists) has more goal involvements for the Blues in the Premier League this campaign.
During an interview with The Standard during the international break, the England midfielder was asked to rate his start to the season and replied: "10 – I've enjoyed it.
"I'm feeling as good as I've ever felt. I'm playing, contributing, scoring goals, assists, creating chances, as good as I have ever done in my career. So why would it not be a 10?
"It was time for me to take that next step and I feel like I want to be seen as one of the best players in the Premier League, one of the best players in the world.
"To do so, I needed to take that next step and start that next chapter.

"I need to play with the best players in the world and compete with the best players in the world, and on that bigger stage, and I just feel Chelsea brings that different level of pressure of having to win and having to perform in each game.
"I think people will judge me on a higher pedestal because of what I'm delivering. I want to show what I'm about."
Alonso said prior to the international break that he hoped Joao Pedro would recover from injury in time to face Bournemouth, but the Cherries have their own selection issues.

Midfielder Alex Scott is expected to miss between six and eight weeks after sustaining a quadriceps tendon injury on his England debut, having played 70 minutes of the Three Lions' 7-0 rout of Croatia last Saturday.
Bournemouth are reportedly unhappy with England's handling of Scott's condition, but Thomas Tuchel insisted earlier this week that there was no wrongdoing on their part.
"With Alex, it's a strange one, I'm very sad about it," Tuchel said.
"He trained in full before Croatia, he did extra work after the training sessions. We knew he was having treatment, but there were only green lights from him and the medics.

"When we were aware there was slight discomfort during the match and asked if he wanted to come off, he said no. After the match, he said he could have played 90 minutes and didn't feel an injury. It's a strange one. There was zero risk taken from our side."
Chelsea – Morgan Rogers
Only Gonzalo Garcia (32) and Erling Haaland (27) have made more cross-option runs in the 2026-27 Premier League than Chelsea midfielder Rogers (20),

Meanwhile, only Garcia (23), Bryan Mbeumo (21), and Matheus Cunha (18) have made more in-possession runs ending in a shot for their team than Rogers' 18, a figure that puts him level with team-mate Cole Palmer.

Chelsea's five league games under Alonso have seen 22 total goals scored (10 for, 12 against), while the Spaniard's six managerial meetings with Rose have averaged 3.8 goals per game (12 for, 11 against).
Should Saturday's contest become stretched, Rayan – who scored just his second goal for Brazil during the international break, against Australia – could provide a major threat.
MATCH PREDICTION – CHELSEA WIN
Chelsea are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League games against Bournemouth (W4 D5), with each of the last three ending level.
Three of Bournemouth's four Premier League wins against Chelsea have come away from home, though, with those three victories being their only clean sheets at Stamford Bridge.
Bournemouth have opened a Premier League campaign with five winless matches for only the second time, after also drawing three and losing two in 2023-24.
Rose is the second manager to fail to win his first five top-flight matches in charge of the Cherries, though the other was his predecessor Andoni Iraola (first nine).
Whatever the result, goals appear to be guaranteed when Chelsea are involved.

Chelsea have conceded the most goals in the Premier League this term (12) and could become the third team to ever concede multiple goals in each of their opening six matches of a campaign, after Everton in 1994-95 and Derby County in 2000-01.

          Tottenham vs Arsenal Prediction: WSL North London Derby Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to the first WSL north London derby of the 2026-27 season with our Tottenham vs Arsenal prediction and preview.

The season could hardly be going worse for Renée Slegers and her Arsenal side as they travel to Tottenham with their hopes of salvaging a disastrous start to the Women's Super League campaign hanging in the balance.
For the first time in league history, Spurs will begin a north London derby above Arsenal in the league table, though both sides will both be looking to arrest their recent form.

Arsenal are on the brink of making more unwanted history, without a win in five WSL matches for the first time (D3 L2) and have drawn more English top-flight games than any other side since the start of last season (9).
They have also never failed to win at least two of their opening seven matches of a WSL campaign, a record now under serious threat.

Having started the campaign so promisingly, unbeaten in their first four matches (W3 D1), Martin Ho will also be desperate for a response from his side after two bruising league outings at London City and Chelsea. In doing so, Spurs became just the second team in WSL history to concede six or more goals in consecutive matches, following Doncaster Rovers Belles in 2013.

While those recent results have exposed some worrying defensive vulnerabilities, scoring goals has certainly not been Tottenham's problem. Only Manchester City (19) have scored more WSL goals than Spurs (18) this season, but only Charlton (18) have conceded more than their 14.
It is an extraordinary contrast. Before this season, no team in WSL history had scored at least 15 goals while conceding 10 or more in their opening six matches.
At the heart of Spurs attacking masterclasses has been captain Drew Spence (215 currently), who could equal Millie Bright (216) for the most appearances made in WSL history.
The contrast with Arsenal could hardly be greater.

While Tottenham have been scoring freely despite their defensive struggles, the Gunners have been remarkably toothless in front of goal, with their inability to turn chances into goals becoming one of the defining problems of their season.

Despite attempting the third-most shots in the WSL this season (121), Arsenal have the worst shot conversion rate in the competition (4.1%), alongside the third-worst shooting accuracy (30.6%) and third-lowest average expected goals (xG) per shot (0.09).
It represents a dramatic decline for a side that ranked among the top two in the WSL for shot conversion in each of the previous two campaigns.
Perhaps nowhere is that struggle more evident than with Alessia Russo.

Last season's golden boot runner-up has found goals hard to come by with just one to her name across six matchdays, and her frustrating afternoon against Birmingham City summed up Arsenal's attacking difficulties. Russo managed just two attempts, neither of which tested the goalkeeper. Remarkably, she has already gone three WSL matches without registering a shot on target this season, having done so only four times across the whole of 2025-26.

Nonetheless, her record against their rivals offers promise; she has scored more league goals against Tottenham (eight) than any other side, and never has she failed to score at least two goals across her first seven top-flight outings of a campaign.
Furthemore, Slegers is unbeaten in all 17 of her WSL games against English managers(W11 D6), with only Sonia Bompastor (18) facing English coaches moreoften without losing in the competition.
Saturday could also bring an unwanted milestone, with the Dutchwoman at risk of going five matches without a win as Arsenal manager in all competitions for the first time.

Their inability to find a breakthrough is reflected in how their matches have unfolded; the Gunners have spent 61% of their playing time with the scores level, more than any other WSL side this season.
Even more remarkably, when matches are tied, Arsenal boast the best shot difference per 90 minutes in the competition (+15), yet still have a negative goal difference per 90 (-0.25).

906gclj3mc4r12g7iexwmsiy4.title: Simeone eases Atletico expectations after five consecutive wins
906gclj3mc4r12g7iexwmsiy4.subtitle: Atletico Madrid will be hoping to extend their winning run across all competitions to six games when they take on Espanyol in LaLiga.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone insisted Atletico Madrid are not "doing everything perfectly" after their five-game winning run.
After four consecutive wins in LaLiga, Atleti extended their winning streak during midweek with a 2-0 Champions League win against 10-man Manchester United.
Their current run of wins also features victories over rivals Real Madrid and Real Sociedad, with Atleti second in the league after eight games.
Only league leaders Barcelona (34) and Madrid (19) have outscored Atleti (18) in LaLiga this season, while three of the eight goals they have conceded have come from the penalty spot.
This is only the second time in the 21st century Atleti have conceded three penalties in the first eight league games of a season, after the 2008-09 campaign (also three).
However, Simeone has tempered expectations of his side ahead of their league meeting with Espanyol.
"Winning five games doesn't mean you're doing everything perfectly," said Simeone.
"There are always mistakes at every stage. I understand that being able to take the lead in games is working in our favour.
"Overall, I think we have things to improve both offensively and defensively.
"We're still building. We try to manage our playing time as best we can, aiming to win the game."
Espanyol are 12th in LaLiga after their 1-1 draw with Malaga last time out; they are winless in their last three league matches (D1 L2).
Espanyol have won just twice in LaLiga this term, with their only home win coming on the opening day against Levante.
Espanyol – Javi Hernandez
Espanyol midfielder Javi Hernandez has provided five assists in eight LaLiga games.
It is the most by a player after their first eight appearances in the competition since Goncalo Guedes for Valencia in October 2017 (also five).
Atletico Madrid – Jonathan David
Jonathan David has been involved in at least one goal in his four LaLiga appearances so far (three goals and two assists).

He could become only the third player to score or assist in his first five appearances in the competition since 2000, after Rafael van der Vaart for Real Madrid in 2008 (four goals and four assists) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic for Barcelona in 2009 (five goals and two assists).
MATCH PREDICTION: ATLETICO MADRID WIN
Espanyol have won just one of their last 10 LaLiga meetings with Atleti (D5 L4), a 2-1 victory in August 2025 during Atleti's last visit to the RCDE Stadium.
Espanyol have not won two consecutive home games against Atleti in the competition since May 2019 (W2).

However, Atleti have not won any of their last three away LaLiga games against Espanyol (D2 L1) since a 2-1 victory in September 2021; they have not gone four consecutive away games without defeat against Espanyol in the competition since May 2007 (D1 L3).

Simeone has drawn four of his 12 visits to the RCDE Stadium in LaLiga (W4 D4 L4); he has only recorded five or more draws at three other away stadiums in the competition: the Estadio Bernabeu, the Ciutat de Valencia and La Ceramica (six).

Espanyol have scored in each of their eight league games this term (11 goals), their best scoring start to a season in the competition since 1992-93, when they netted in their first 10 matches of the campaign (17 goals).
Atletico Madrid – 53.9%

93xk30jysn77zgdkem0o1kez.title: Robertson: Scotland 'outfought' in Nations League defeat to Slovenia
93xk30jysn77zgdkem0o1kez.subtitle: Scotland's wait for a first home win under Sebastien Pocognoli continued after Slovenia came from behind to win at Hampden Park.
paragraphs: Andy Robertson conceded Scotland were "not good enough" and "outfought" during their 2-1 defeat at home to Slovenia in the Nations League on Tuesday.
Following Sebastien Pocognoli's first win in charge against North Macedonia last time out, Scotland started well and took the lead through Ryan Christie in the 31st minute.
However, Slovenia hit back just before the hour when Aljosa Matko collected Danijel Sturm's pass before squeezing his left-footed shot beyond the grasp of Angus Gunn.
Matko and Sturm combined again for Slovenia's winner in the 71st minute, with the latter tucking home from close range as jeers rang out among the home supporters.
Scotland have now lost three of their last four home matches in all competitions (W1), as many defeats as in their previous nine matches at Hampden Park (W4 D2).

In what was meant to be a memorable match for Robertson, who was presented with a shirt by Gordon Strachan, Alex McLeish and Steve Clarke to mark his 100th appearance for Scotland last week, the Tottenham full-back was left far from impressed by the effort on the pitch.
"Not good enough. The whole team on the pitch, I don't think it was a good performance at all," Robertson told BBC Scotland.

"We didn't do the good things we did on Saturday. I don't know what that's down to. They caused us a lot of problems, and we have to find the reasons why. I don't care about myself too much with personal achievements.
"It was amazing that my three ex-managers came – I can't thank them enough. It was a really nice touch from everyone at the SFA to organise that for me.

"That moment will never be taken away from me, but at the end of the day when the whistle goes, I don't care if it's my first cap or my 101st cap. We wanted to kick on from Saturday because we had a really positive feeling about what we were doing and where we were going. We didn't do that.
"It's been a long camp, I don't know if it was down to tiredness, but as far as I'm concerned, Slovenia have played the same number of games as us.
"They looked a lot fresher, a lot hungrier. As Scotland, we might lack quality or make mistakes, but people don't accept being outfought. I think that's what happened."
The result leaves Scotland third in Group B1 and three points behind Slovenia after their first four matches, with the pressure already mounting on Pocognoli.
Pocognoli is the fourth Scotland manager to lose his opening two home games in charge of the national team and the first since Berti Vogts in August 2002.
Scotland won the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 2.17 from their 12 shots to Slovenia's 1.33 from their 10 attempts, but their quality was not enough up front.
And speaking after the defeat, Pocognoli echoed Robertson's comments, adding that his team were far from the level he expects from them.
"We didn't deserve to get the win, that's the reality. We didn't deliver a great game. On the ball and off the ball, we were below the level we expected," Pocognoli said.
"We were not proactive enough, on and off the ball. Probably the structure off the ball needs to be more proactive, front-footed to push the line higher.
"On the ball we were not clever enough. We were far from strong enough in the duels.
"It's a process about being brave, trying to defend forward, and we were not compact in our defensive shape.
"The reality is each game teaches us some information. We will try to go through the process we want and learn from this one and do better in the next one."
Scotland return to action on November 13 at home to North Macedonia before they make the trip to face group leaders Switzerland three days later.

Andy Robertson conceded Scotland were "not good enough" and "outfought" during their 2-1 defeat at home to Slovenia in the Nations League on Tuesday. 

Following Sebastien Pocognoli's first win in charge against North Macedonia last time out, Scotland started well and took the lead through Ryan Christie in the 31st minute. 

However, Slovenia hit back just before the hour when Aljosa Matko collected Danijel Sturm's pass before squeezing his left-footed shot beyond the grasp of Angus Gunn. 

Matko and Sturm combined again for Slovenia's winner in the 71st minute, with the latter tucking home from close range as jeers rang out among the home supporters. 

Scotland have now lost three of their last four home matches in all competitions (W1), as many defeats as in their previous nine matches at Hampden Park (W4 D2).

In what was meant to be a memorable match for Robertson, who was presented with a shirt by Gordon Strachan, Alex McLeish and Steve Clarke to mark his 100th appearance for Scotland last week, the Tottenham full-back was left far from impressed by the effort on the pitch. 

"Not good enough. The whole team on the pitch, I don't think it was a good performance at all," Robertson told BBC Scotland.

"We didn't do the good things we did on Saturday. I don't know what that's down to. They caused us a lot of problems, and we have to find the reasons why. I don't care about myself too much with personal achievements.

"It was amazing that my three ex-managers came – I can't thank them enough. It was a really nice touch from everyone at the SFA to organise that for me.

"That moment will never be taken away from me, but at the end of the day when the whistle goes, I don't care if it's my first cap or my 101st cap. We wanted to kick on from Saturday because we had a really positive feeling about what we were doing and where we were going. We didn't do that.

"It's been a long camp, I don't know if it was down to tiredness, but as far as I'm concerned, Slovenia have played the same number of games as us.

"On the ball we were not clever enough. We were far from strong enough in the duels.

"It's a process about being brave, trying to defend forward, and we were not compact in our defensive shape.

"The reality is each game teaches us some information. We will try to go through the process we want and learn from this one and do better in the next one."
