          What Did We Learn From Jürgen Klopp’s First Game Back in Management?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After over two years away from the dugout, Jürgen Klopp returned to the touchline on Thursday as Germany boss. How did it go, and were there signs that he can revive Die Nationalelf?
For a long time, Jürgen Klopp insisted he may never return to football management.

The 59-year-old left Liverpool in May 2024 after admitting he was “running out of energy” following nine years at Anfield. After a break from the game altogether, he returned with Red Bull as its head of global soccer, overseeing the running of their various teams around the world.
The managerial bug can be infectious, though, and following Germany’s disappointing 2026 World Cup and the departure of Julian Nagelsmann, Klopp was asked to come to the rescue.
On Thursday, he took charge of his first game since May 2024 as Germany travelled to face old rivals the Netherlands in their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League opener.

Expectations were high. Klopp leading the German national team always felt like it would happen eventually, and there is optimism the former Mainz and Borussia Dortmund boss can have the same revolutionary impact he had at all three clubs he’s managed.

As mentioned, Germany had a poor World Cup this summer. They started by thrashing Curaçao 7-1, though they needed a late winner to overcome Ivory Coast after that, before losing 2-1 to Ecuador in their final group game.
That was not ideal preparation for a tough last-32 clash with Paraguay, and so it proved. Germany struggled with their opponents’ physical approach and were ultimately eliminated on penalties.
Klopp signed a four-year deal to take over from Nagelsmann, overseeing the Euro 2028 and 2030 World Cup campaigns. His primary challenge is the Nations League, though, and it was a big test first up.

Not only was he taking on the Netherlands in Amsterdam, complete with their own new gaffer in Xavi Hernández – also managing his first game since May 2024 after leaving Barcelona – but he was set to face three of his former Liverpool players. Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Cody Gakpo all started for the Dutch, and one of them went on to deny his old boss a debut victory.

Klopp took the unusual step of naming a 44-man squad, with Augsburg goalkeeper Finn Dahmen the only player set to be present for all four Nations League games in this international window. One group of players will be available for the first two (vs Netherlands and Greece) and then others will join up for the last two (vs Serbia and Greece).

The move was met with general approval in Germany, allowing Klopp to look at many players, introduce new and exciting faces, and also protect players from too much football across the elongated international break.

That doesn’t entirely eradicate the risk of injury, though, and that was apparent when Jamal Musiala pulled up in the warm-up in Amsterdam. On top of that, Kai Havertz could only play the first half hour after being on the receiving end of a nasty challenge by Quinten Timber, the brother of Havertz’s Arsenal teammate Jurriën.

An early scare came from one of Klopp’s former charges, with Van Dijk converting a Tijjani Reijnders corner, only for the goal to be ruled out after a VAR check judged Brian Brobbey to have fouled Marc-André ter Stegen.
There was some familiarity in the first XI Klopp named as Germany manager. Joshua Kimmich was handed his 115th cap, taking him past Toni Kroos (114) and into seventh place outright.

There was also a new face in the side, with Freiburg right-back Philipp Treu earning his first cap, and he played a key role in the first goal of the Klopp era. Treu’s low cross into the Dutch box from the right was blocked by the sliding Jan Paul van Hecke, but the loose ball fell kindly for Felix Nmecha, who finished calmly. It was somewhat appropriate that a Dortmund player scored the first goal under Klopp, given the outstanding success he had with BVB between 2008 and 2015.

It wasn’t without some controversy. Brobbey was down hurt on the turf at the time and Germany played on while Dutch players were imploring them to kick it out. Ultimately, it was at the referee’s discretion and despite some disagreements between Denzel Dumfries and Kimmich, Klopp’s side were well within their rights to play on, and it was 1-0.

It was familiar shape from Klopp’s side. Havertz was the striker but dropped deep – indeed, Nadiem Amiri had a more advanced average position in the first 30 minutes – while the two full-backs got forward with regularity. The wide forwards, Karim Adeyemi and Kevin Schade, were the two most-advanced German players in that first half hour before Havertz was forced off.

Another new face, Younes Ebnoutalib, replaced Havertz, and if anything, Germany looked even better with the Eintracht Frankfurt man up top. It wasn’t entirely polished but there was energy, there was effort, and there was counter pressing so synonymous with Klopp.
After the game, Treu told RTL: “We wanted to press them from the front, put them under pressure, be difficult to play against and play with intensity.

          Five Knee-Jerk Reactions to Premier League 2026-27 Matchday 8
        
      
                          
                      Oct 26, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We round up the weekend’s Premier League action by jumping to five conclusions based on a single round of matches.
Every week here on Opta Analyst, we do away with our usual approach of diving deep into the data and instead come to a load of conclusions based on a single round of Premier League fixtures.
Will any of our latest five knee-jerk reactions hold up in the weeks to come, or will they be disproven as the season goes on? Read on to see what you think.
There was a great deal of change at Chelsea over the summer but there have been plenty of indications in the early part of the Xabi Alonso era that his could be a productive reign.
But in Saturday’s dismal home defeat to Tottenham, this was Chelsea back to their self-destructive worst.

Yes, they were missing first-choice goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez and first-choice number nine João Pedro. And yes, Tottenham were very good and fully deserved the win. But this was a defeat in a game that Chelsea just do not lose – before this they had lost only once at home to rivals Spurs in the Premier League era.

Concerningly, though, losing has become too normalised for this club, and although it was a shock to see them beaten by Tottenham of all teams, the fans have had to grow used to seeing their team lose. In fact, since the start of March, Chelsea have lost 14 games – more than any other side not just in the Premier League, but in any of the top five European leagues.
14 – Since the start of March, Chelsea have lost more games in all competitions than any other side in Europe's big-five leagues (14).Stormy. pic.twitter.com/sOjWHQt0lo

Discipline remains a major issue, too, and several managers have been unable to resolve it. After Cole Palmer’s dismissal, Chelsea have picked up nine red cards since the start of last season, four more than anyone else. Morgan Rogers might have been sent off late on, too for a challenge on Conor Gallagher.
They have consistently had problems in goal, too, and on the evidence of his own goal here, Mike Penders could be yet another error-prone goalkeeper.
There are still big problems for Alonso to fix.

Last week, we can’t have been the only ones wondering what had happened to Arsenal’s set-piece threat. After breaking the Premier League record for goals from corners last season, they had gone seven games this season without scoring a single goal from a corner, or any kind of set-piece, for that matter.

That said, Arsenal had been more than making up for any issues with enough goals in open play, often scoring after long passages of possession with all of their players involved. They had won all but one of their games and looked far more convincing than last season, too.
But they were always going to run into some difficulties at some point, and Bukayo Saka’s injury is a hurdle they’ll have to navigate.

He is integral to their attacking play and Arsenal always look slightly less fluent without him. So it was no surprise that the display against Everton this weekend with Saka absent was a little more disjointed than some of their other performances this campaign.

But with Ezri Konsa’s seventh-minute opener, Arsenal proved they haven’t entirely lost their set-piece mojo. It was their first set-piece goal (excluding penalties) since May, ending a run of 13 games without one, and set them on their way to a win that felt like it belonged to last season, in that they broke the deadlock with a set-piece and then always looked like holding on.

They are a better team than last season, and set-pieces won’t be as necessary a route to goal, but winning through them is something they need to keep on doing, because they will have off days. If they do this many more times, they’ll stroll to the title.

The 10 teams involved in Sunday’s games completed just 75.8% of their passes. It was the lowest pass completion rate on a single day of Premier League football with at least five matches played since 14 December 2019, nearly seven years ago.

Some might assume the stormy conditions were the reason for so many passes going astray, and they might well be right. But there was also some really poor football on display, a lot of unconvincing performances and, most strikingly, almost everyone showed they have real weaknesses. That wasn’t limited to Sunday, either.

75.8% – The combined pass completion rate from today's @premierleague matches was just 75.8%.This is the lowest on a single day with 5+ matches played since 14th December 2019 (75.1%).🌪️ Boelo. pic.twitter.com/34WdKllPCH

          How Problematic is Manchester City’s Leaky Defence?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City are top of the Premier League with a perfect record of five wins from five, but they haven’t been entirely convincing at the back. Is there any cause for concern?

Enzo Maresca’s comments after watching his Manchester City side’s rollercoaster victory over Sunderland on Sunday afternoon sparked an interesting philosophical debate. Rather than lean towards the are-you-not-entertained ethos of an Ange Postecoglou, Maresca intimated he would like to see rather more control from his team, and a little less excitement than they provided in this win.

The Italian may well prefer to watch a game with lots of goals, but he was likely stating this preference on this particular occasion because the chaos of City’s win, in which they needed to retake the lead three times in the first half alone – something that has only happened six times in Premier League history to any team – was not exactly the mark of champions. As the scoreline suggests, City allowed their opponents far too many opportunities to score.

Sunderland are a very good team but not one that routinely creates a lot of chances. On this occasion, away to title hopefuls, they had chances worth 3.57 expected goals, which is by far their highest since their return to the Premier League last year.

In fact, in 43 games since the start of last season, they’ve only managed more than 2.0 xG twice, with their previous best being 2.44 vs Newcastle in March. They’ve had under 1.0 xG in more than half (22) of their matches.

But they carved City open time and again. Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick of what were essentially tap-ins, allowed into areas where he could not miss, time and time again. And at 4-3, Sunderland came within a Rúben Dias goal-line clearance of equalising again.

While match-going fans got their money’s worth and neutrals were thoroughly entertained, even though City won and kept up the only remaining 100% record in the Premier League, it's understandable that Maresca came away a little dismayed at his side’s defensive display.
“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals.
“So that means that we created enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

It is a fact that City had kept four successive clean sheets before the Sunderland game, but it was slightly disingenuous of Maresca to try and reframe their form that way. That run included the midweek win over Championship side Norwich in the EFL Cup and a 1-0 win at home to newly-promoted Coventry, who caused City all manner of problems and could quite feasibly have scored three goals, let alone one.

Credit where it’s due: City were mightily impressive defensively in their 1-0 win at Manchester United, keeping their rivals at arm’s length despite playing most of the derby with 10 men. But across that four-game run of clean sheets, they conceded chances worth 2.82 xG. So, in other words, they could reasonably have been expected to concede three goals.
They do have Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal, so perhaps they just felt confident that they could rely on one of the best shot-stoppers and most commanding goalkeepers of his generation.

But the evidence from the Sunderland game suggests that is not a reliable method of defence. Sunderland’s 3.57 xG is the third highest ever by a team that went on to lose a Premier League game since xG data is available (2013-14). On another day, Sunderland would have won that match, just like United will feel aggrieved not to have won the derby, and Coventry were left rueing missed chances against City.
On the opening weekend of the season, too, City required 84th- and 91st-minute goals to come from behind and rescue a win at home to Bournemouth.

In other words, their ‘perfect’ record of five wins from five has been rather less convincing than it might appear from a quick glance at the league table. They are clearly feeling the loss of Rodri from the base of their midfield.

They have, though, still won each game, which is something no other team can say. They are able to rely on the goalscoring of perennial golden-boot winner and early leader in the top-scorers’ stakes, Erling Haaland (five goals).

Rayan Cherki (three goals, two assists) and Antoine Semenyo (two goals, three assists) have started the season very well, too, while Enzo Fernández (one goal) provides further attacking threat from the double pivot. Iliman Ndiaye looks to have settled well following his summer move from Everton, and Phil Foden (two assists) is another exceptional attacker when he’s not kicking Bruno Fernandes in the you-know-wheres.

But is their arguably unrivalled attack enough? Can they rely on being bailed out often enough to win the title? “Attack wins you games, defence wins you titles,” as goes the famous Sir Alex Ferguson quote. If that’s true, then City might have something to worry about.

Indeed, only Brighton (who have played two halves of football against 10 men) have scored more goals (16) in the Premier League this season than City (13), but six teams have conceded fewer than them (5). Those teams are Leeds, Everton, Brentford, Hull and, perhaps crucially, likely title rivals Arsenal and Liverpool.

“There’s no way Manchester City win the league,” Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson said after the Sunderland game. “Going forward, [they] were good but at the back they were all over the place. [That] catches up with you.”

95tsyxnmg9ls1n7w9rbhy85pk.title: United States 0-2 Spain: World champions hold on after fast start
95tsyxnmg9ls1n7w9rbhy85pk.subtitle: Spain scored twice early on, but had to show their defensive strength in order to hold on for the win against the United States.
paragraphs: World champions Spain scored two early goals and held off late pressure from the United States to earn a 2-0 friendly win at Audi Field.
Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro were both on target for Spain, who finished with 10 players after Athenea del Castillo's late red card, while Lily Yohannes saw a second-half penalty saved.

Spain made a lightning-fast start as Edna Imade spread play out to Guijarro on the right and, after realising she had space for a shot, she let fly into the top-left corner from range just three minutes in.
And La Roja doubled their lead just 11 minutes later; it was great work from Salma Paralluelo down the left, and she picked out the unmarked Navarro, who rifled her volley into the roof of the net.
The USA almost pulled one back moments later, with Alyssa Thompson getting the better of Adriana Nanclares, but Lucia Corrales was on the line to clear the danger.
Nanclares made smart stops to deny Sophia Wilson and Lindsey Heaps shortly after, before the former fired narrowly wide of the post before the break.
The USA continued to pile on the pressure after the break, and Wilson thought she had halved the deficit in the 54th minute, but the goal was disallowed for offside following a VAR review.
Nanclares continued to impress, keeping out Trinity Rodman, Wilson and Rose Lavelle before she also got down to Yohannes' penalty after Natalia Ramos was penalised for a shirt pull in the box.
In the first minute of stoppage time, Del Castillo was shown a straight red card following a VAR review after she pulled Michelle Cooper's hair, but Spain held out for a clean sheet and a win.
Nanclares impresses as USA fail to find golden touch
Spain have already booked their place in next year's Women's World Cup, meaning this was the perfect warm-up for the United States ahead of their own qualifiers.
And though Emma Hayes' side were undone by the early goals, she will have seen plenty of positives from this performance to take forward.

All of Spain's six shots came in the first half, as did their two goals, and they looked set to run riot after going 2-0 up inside 14 minutes, but the USA recovered, albeit without hitting the back of the net.

The USA finished with 13 attempts overall, with seven of those coming after the break, but they came up against an inspired Nanclares, who made six stops after the break, including that key penalty save.
Sonia Bermudez will definitely want to see an improvement when the two sides face off again on Tuesday, while Hayes' main aim will be to unlock her attacking force.

97nrlwxxzagjzh1hcv763rmt.title: Kane is England's best ever, claims Bellingham
97nrlwxxzagjzh1hcv763rmt.subtitle: Harry Kane, on his record-equalling England appearance, scored twice as Thomas Tuchel's side eased to a 3-0 win over Czechia at Wembley.
paragraphs: Jude Bellingham labelled Harry Kane as England's greatest ever player in the wake of another star showing from the striker.
Kane made his 125th appearance for England on Tuesday, which saw him equal Peter Shilton as the Three Lions' most-capped player.
The England captain marked the occasion in style, scoring twice as well as playing a key role in creating the opening goal in a 3-0 Nations League win over Czechia.
Kane is now on 91 goals for his country, while he became the oldest player in England's history to score a brace in consecutive appearances.
He has netted 13 international goals in 2026, which is the most in a calendar year for an England player since Kane himself struck 16 goals in 2021.
And Bellingham feels Kane is clear as England's best ever player.
Bellingham told ITV Sport: "There's not much more you can say that hasn't already been said.
"From my perspective, first and foremost, he is an unbelievable human being, as a captain and a man.
"He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him. He is pretty unmatched.
"He's scoring goals for fun, he goes deep and he gets tackles in. He's only getting better."
Bellingham won his 36th cap while playing for Real Madrid, the joint-most of any England player in history alongside David Beckham.
Only Kane at Bayern Munich (41) and Owen Hargreaves at Bayern (39) have won more caps while playing for a non-English club.
England have scored 39 goals in 16 games in 2026 – only in 2021 have they netted more goals in a single calendar year (52).
They sit second in Nations League Group A3, behind Spain, but are just one point away from qualifying for the quarter-finals.
"It was what we needed," Bellingham said of England's display.
"I know it is difficult when teams come here because they either sit deep and try and frustrate us. We had just come off the 7-0 [win v Croatia] and we were itching for more but we got the job done."
Thomas Tuchel, meanwhile, added of Kane: "It's what he does. I don't take it for granted, it's just exceptional every single match."

9872F5C2498CEC4FC48B141BC14416AF.title: Preview: Man City host Brighton for the first of two meetings this week
9872F5C2498CEC4FC48B141BC14416AF.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Man City host Brighton for the first of two meetings this weekShareManchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion face off against each other for a second time in less than three days at The Etihad on Saturday afternoon.

With changes made to both teams from their usual starting XIs, Manchester City edged past Brighton in the League Cup on Wednesday night without looking particularly convincing. It took a penalty shootout to separate the two teams, and both may feel that the second meeting between them in three days at The Etihad on Saturday afternoon is clearly the more consequential of the two encounters.

And there’s a case for saying that yes, if the early season whispers about whether Brighton could “do a Leicester” this season are to have any substance about them, this is a fixture the visitors need to win. City and Arsenal are tied at the top with Brighton five points behind them. A Brighton win would make this Premier League season really start to look like a three-horse race. Defeat, and the eight-point gap would already look insurmountable.
😅 Manchester City missed first in the penalty shootout… but they have made it past Brighton in the EFL Cup! pic.twitter.com/bD5xdjYVBd

It remains the case that Brighton are unbeaten in their last four league matches against Manchester City, with the last two meetings between the two sides at The Etihad having ended in draws and Brighton having won their last two at The Amex.

One little peculiarity of this fixture is that Manchester City went unbeaten against Brighton for 55 years. The teams met for the first time in the the FA Cup in 1924, with City winning 5-1 at The Goldstone Ground. Subsequent to this, though, they didn’t play each other again until August 1979, when City won 3-2 at Maine Road, but that five and half decade long run ended at the end of December that year, when Brighton won 4-1 at The Goldstone Ground. In 1983, it was City who formalised Brighton’s relegation from the old first division with a 1-0 win.

Manchester City’s goalscoring options aren’t all about Erling Haaland, you know. Rayan Cherki has scored six goals in 13 appearances for City already this season, the sort of goalscoring form that could see him end the season with 20+ goals, if he can avoid injury. The unusual stat about Cherki – for someone who plays in his position – is that he’s far more likely to score goals than create them, having scored twice as many goals as he’s registered assists.

One of the more perplexing sales of the summer was Spurs’ decision to sell Luka Vušković to Brighton without giving him a shot, even though the defender earned rave reviews last season on loan. His early performances this season have indicated, not for the first time, that Brighton have seen something in this young defender that Spurs were unable to.

Manchester City have three injury concerns for this match. Antoine Semenyo is expected to be out until December with a leg injury, while Matheus Nunes was left out of their squad on Wednesday night after suffering a groin injury and Ilian Ndiaye found himself in the same boat after suffering what was reported as cramp. Both could potentially return for this match.

Brighton didn’t suffer any fresh injuries on Wednesday night, but they still have a lengthy list of absentees. Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas, Kaoru Mitoma, Femi Azeez, Pascal Struijk, Mats Wieffer, Yakuba Minteh and Zadok Yohanna will all be missing. It’s not all bad news, though. Ferdi Kadioglu and Chema Andres have both been passed fit to play.

It would be easy to put either too much or too little emphasis on Wednesday night’s meeting between these two teams, given how many changes both teams made to their starting XIs. But the ultimate takeaway from it is that there wasn’t very much between these two, and this seems borne out by the fact that there are only two points between them in the Premier League table as we reach the end of October.

It does remain the case that Brighton have stuttered since beating Crystal Palace 5-0 at The Amex a couple of weeks ago. Their goalless draw away to Jablonec in the Europa Conference League was less than inspiring, though their performances against both Liverpool and Manchester City were decent, although they ended up losing both fixtures.

But City have looked less imposing with each passing game since their 3-0 win at Liverpool in the first match after their guilt over systematic cheating was first confirmed. They got past Ipswich, but they were uninspiring away to Aston Villa, while Brighton’s under-strength team matched their under-strength team all the way in the Carabao Cup.

The question of whether the adrenaline boost they took from their performative outrage over having been found guilty of financial doping is already wearing off is as valid as it was before the midweek meeting between these two teams. So I’m going for a draw, this time. 1-1 doesn’t sound unrealistic, giving Arsenal a chance to reclaim top place in the table for the first time since the middle of September.

988D8D3BC2D6CD44930AF18D7D74C656.title: Why managers must put their own fitness first - Pulis
988D8D3BC2D6CD44930AF18D7D74C656.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsPremier LeagueScores & FixturesTableFollow Your TeamTransfersTop ScorersGossipWhy managers must put their own fitness first - PulisPublished43 minutes agoA lot has changed for football managers over the past few decades but Vincent Kompany's recent health scare was a reminder it is still an all-consuming occupation that takes its toll physically and mentally.

From the tragic death of Scotland manager Jock Stein after a World Cup qualifier against Wales in 1985, to the different heart issues suffered by Graeme Souness, Sir Alex Ferguson, Gerard Houllier, Joe Kinnear and Harry Redknapp down the years, I've always been aware of the dangers of my job.

It is 25 years since then Leicester boss Dave Bassett and Bolton manager Sam Allardyce took part in an experiment that saw them wired up to heart monitors during a game between the teams, and both their heart rates reached critical levels.
It's not just during games when management can have an adverse effect on your health, either.
The stress you are under is relentless and you have to find a way of looking after yourself. Fortunately this was something I realised very early on in my management career.

Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Kompany collapsed at Bayern Munich's training ground and the cause has been identified as meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord

I had worked under and alongside managers for my entire working life as a player and then coach, but it was only when I got my first management job - at Bournemouth in 1992 - that I realised the workload you undertake and just how time consuming and stressful a job it is.
In those days, and in fact throughout my whole career, I wanted to be the person who made all the footballing decisions at my club.

That meant I did everything from scouting players to signing the ones I wanted, and organised my staff at every level from first-team to the reserve and youth teams, all within the club's financial restraints.

I saw the first-team performances as being my main responsibility so I never wavered from my work on the training ground either, coaching a certain way that suited the players and gave them the best chance of winning games - which would ultimately determine my future.
All of the above was generally the way most English clubs were run so it was not just me doing it. But the demands were relentless, and I had to learn how to look after myself properly to cope.
During those early days, my management of myself personally was really poor.

It starts with your diet. At that time I would be driving up and down the motorway to watch players, trying to find a fish and chip shop or fuelled only by a half-time pie or a sandwich from a local shop.
I was young and could deal with it, so it never crossed my mind that I wasn't eating well or getting the exercise I needed to retain my own fitness levels.
But, at the same time, the pressure on the team to win games ultimately fell on my shoulders so the pressure of being the person responsible for results and performances every week really built up.
I had never realised how stressful that part of management was until we started to lose a few games and every bit of criticism was directed on to my lap.
That part has not changed for managers now.

They may have less to do with the way their clubs are run now but they still have to deal with people they have never met criticising their ability to do a job they love to media outlets, without taking into consideration any other factors that might be contributing to those performances and results.
That's why it's so stressful. All the arrows and guns are pointed in your direction, and you have no way of protecting yourself, apart from by winning games.
Image caption, Pulis was player-coach at Bournemouth under Harry Redknapp before getting his first management job with the Cherries at the age of 34, when Redknapp left for West Ham in 1992

          Aston Villa 2-1 Man City Stats: Jackson Punishes Guéhi and Donnarumma Errors to End Leaders' Perfect Start
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Opta Analyst / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City's perfect Premier League start under Enzo Maresca ended on Saturday, as they slumped to a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa.
Nicolas Jackson punished two sloppy errors from Manchester City as their perfect start to the Premier League season was halted by a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa.
Jackson scored in either half at Villa Park, aided by a dismal touch from Marc Guéhi for his sixth-minute opener and some weak goalkeeping from Gianluigi Donnarumma for his second goal on the hour.

Erling Haaland briefly got City level at the start of the second half, but Enzo Maresca's side were unable to respond after falling behind for a second time, as they failed to become only the third team to start a Premier League campaign with eight straight victories.
It did not take long for the suspect defending that has plagued City this season to rear its head, as a dreadful individual error from Guéhi led to Villa's breakthrough.

Guéhi was under no pressure as he looked to bring down a chipped pass from Rúben Dias, but he knocked the ball off his standing leg and into the path of John McGinn, who immediately released Jackson. The Senegal international still had plenty to do, but he skipped inside Elliot Anderson then lashed into the roof of the net from close range.

Jackson dragged another effort wide, but it was City who spent much of the first half pushing for a goal. Zion Suzuki did brilliantly to tip Iliman Ndiaye's curler around the post and was later fortunate to see a near-identical effort from the same player strike the upright.
Between those close calls, Suzuki held Rayan Cherki's shot under pressure from Haaland, while Abdukodir Khusanov also called the in-form Villa goalkeeper into action.

City's 29 touches in the Villa area during the first half were the most by any team in the first 45 minutes of a Premier League game this season, and their pressure finally told in the 52nd minute, as Ndiaye's hanging cross from the right was nodded home by Haaland.
City had a glorious chance to go 2-1 up when Josko Gvardiol's shot was pushed onto the crossbar by Suzuki, but Villa then struck at the other end – with another error costing the visitors.

Jackson's clever pass released Ibrahim Mbaye down the right flank, and when the Villa substitute supplied a return ball into the middle, Jackson's shot was straight at Donnarumma. However, the Italian went down awkwardly and let it squirm beneath him.

City were restricted to half chances from then on, with Suzuki smothering the ball at Gvardiol's feet and Ian Maatsen clearing a Haaland header off his line, as Unai Emery's men clung on for another statement win.
Villa always seem to relish these fixtures at Villa Park, and they are now unbeaten in their last four home games against teams starting the day top of the Premier League table.
Prior to Saturday's victory, they also beat Arsenal 1-0 in December 2023 and 2-1 in December 2025, either side of a 2-2 draw with Liverpool in February 2025.
And City only had themselves to blame, with both goals being the direct result of lapses in concentration at the back.

Since the start of last season, Jan Paul van Hecke (four) is the only outfielder to make more errors leading to goals in the Premier League than Guéhi (three), and the centre-back was hooked at half-time by Maresca, who sent on Rico Lewis in his place.

Donnarumma's error was his third leading directly to a goal in the Premier League since he joined City last season. The only goalkeepers to commit more in that time are Bart Verbruggen (five) and Robin Roefs (four).

And it was Jackson who profited, becoming the first Villa player to score a Premier League brace against the league leaders since Andreas Weimann versus Manchester United in November 2012. Jackson has seven goals in all competitions this term, with Haaland (13) the only Premier League player to outscore him.

9A8F3097F19B774FA1DCAA9AE8F5B896.title: What have we learned from first round of Premiership?
9A8F3097F19B774FA1DCAA9AE8F5B896.subtitle: BBC
paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsScottish PremiershipScores & FixturesTableTop ScorersScottish FootballWhat have we learned from first round of Premiership? Image source, SNSImage caption, Hearts are aiming to challenge the Old Firm duopoly again this season
It's a common answer from managers - they do not look at the league table until at least every team has faced one another.
That point is now here in the Scottish Premiership after Wednesday's dramatic full card marked the first circuit of games in Scotland's top flight.
Plenty of managers, whether their team is going well or not, are still saying how early it is in the 38-game campaign and they are right.
But nonetheless where the league table sits after 11 matches can instructive of how it ends up in May.
In two of the last three seasons for example, the teams sitting in the top six at this stage ended up staying there.
So what has the season so far taught us about what might lie ahead?

Image source, BBC SportThree-way title race big askHearts were one of the major stories of European football last season when they came within minutes of being the first non-Old Firm side to win the league since 1985.

Wouter Vrancken's new-look team have made a strong start as they sit third, eight points behind Celtic and four behind Rangers despite a big summer rebuild and the Belgian implementing a new style of play which he has described as "organised chaos".

They have certainly delivered on that - as only Celtic have scored more goals, and Hearts are a formidable opponent at Tynecastle where they are unbeaten in the league since April 2025, a run of 26 games.
Beatings have been handed out to Dundee United and St Mirren already in Gorgie.

Wednesday's 2-2 draw at home to Rangers should have been a victory for Hearts which brought them closer to the top two - but ultimately their injury-ravaged squad was exposed late on and they remain closer to Dundee in fourth.

Those key injuries, while juggling European football, plus an unconvincing away record which included a 7-1 clobbering at Celtic Park, means Hearts might struggle to hang on to the pace set by the Old Firm.
Despite Celtic supporters being wholly unconvinced by their team, they are on course  to reach over 90 points this season, having won the title with 82 last season, the lowest tally since 2017-18.
Likewise Rangers have doubters among their own, but they and their rivals are in the top two positions of a lot of key performance metrics.

Whether it's expected goals for and against, shots on target per game, chances created, Celtic and Rangers are comfortably in the top two positions and are the only sides conceding fewer than one goal per game on average.
As they should be, given their financial advantages, and with Rangers not playing in European football this season they should be extra rested and focused on domestic duty.
Kilmarnock are bottom of the table, but by no means cut adrift as they sit level on points with Hibernian and only one behind Motherwell.
Despite that, they are the bookmakers favourites for automatic relegation. The main reason is simply the goals against column.
Neil McCann's side have conceded 26 goals already, the most at this stage of the season since Dundee in 2018-19, who let in 28 in 11 games and went down.

9ABA411B5A1E6512E8ED2396DD019CA9.title: Preview: Villarreal are the visitors as Liverpool look to maintain 100% start in the Champions League
9ABA411B5A1E6512E8ED2396DD019CA9.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Villarreal are the visitors as Liverpool look to maintain 100% start in the Champions LeagueShareLiverpool are going to be put to the test this week with Andoni Iraola’s injury hit squad welcoming Villarreal to Anfield in MD3 of the Champions League, just five days before clashing with a high-flying Brighton team.

Liverpool have reacted well following their 3-0 loss to Manchester City last weekend. The Reds romped to a 6-3 win over LASK in the Champions League before overturning a deficit at the Gtech Community Stadium to claim a 2-1 win over Brentford last time out.

It wasn’t the most convincing showing against the Bees and Andoni Iraola’s men were aided by two red cards for the hosts. A win is a win though, isn’t it? Liverpool have now won three and drawn three in the Premier League. They’re two from two in the Champions League after defeating Atlético Madrid on MD1 before romping to an easy win in Austria last week.

It’s potentially starting to click in attack for the Reds, too. Bradley Barcola netted a treble in the Champions League while Alexander Isak fired in the winner on Saturday afternoon. In both matches, Florian Wirtz claimed an assist.
How they navigate this fixture against Villarreal will be interesting though.

Iñigo Pérez’s side have started the season slowly, claiming nine points from nine matches. They are a threat though, having finished third last season. They’ve also been okay in the Champions League too. Yes, they fell to a 3-2 loss to Borussia Dortmund but they did beat Napoli 3-1 last time out.

Despite their erratic form, they’ve scaled their game against superior opposition. They claimed a 2-2 draw with Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital and managed to limit Real Madrid to just one goal.

This is the first time that Pérez and Iraola have faced off. The former used to be the latter’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano and was supposed to follow him to Bournemouth before work permit issues prevented it from being formalised.

For Liverpool, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak following his winning goal at the Gtech Community Stadium. The Swedish striker showed sharpness in key moments, and the Reds will need him to maintain that lethal touch to unlock an organised and resilient Spanish defence. He missed the game in LASK but he has been the match winner on three occasions already this season. Don’t be surprised if he makes it four on Tuesday night.

For Villarreal, they have a number of attackers who can pose a threat. Alberto Moleiro might be the pick of the bunch for this particular match. The fleet-footed left-sided attacker will be up against a robust Ronald Araújo, and his nimble style might give him the edge against the powerhouse Uruguayan.

The hosts are without a number of players. Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong were both substituted against Brentford with hamstring issues and Iraola revealed he fears both will be out for a number of weeks. The pair join Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni on the sidelines.
The visitors are without Tajon Buchanan and Nicolas Pépé. Aside from those two, they have a full squad to pick from.
We're going with an entertaining 2-1 home victory for Liverpool, with the Reds building on their weekend comeback to edge a tightly contested affair at Anfield.

9B038310A629ED8C7AFAB5C6F143B334.title: Preview: Man City host AEK Athens in the Champions League
9B038310A629ED8C7AFAB5C6F143B334.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Man City host AEK Athens in the Champions LeagueShareManchester City took a heavy beating last time out in the Champions League, but even with some injury concerns they’ll be big favourites to dish out the same treatment to AEK Athens.

Defeat at home to PSG will have served as a reminder that despite their bullishness at dealing with off-field issues domestically, Man City might remain on the sidelines for European glory this term, in what is only Enzo Maresca’s second season managing in the elite competition.

In the Community Shield back in summer, a heavy drubbing at the hands of Arsenal had some suggesting that City were too far off the pace to challenge for the Premier League title; fast forward to mid-October and it looks like only a failed appeal and subsequent stern punishment for financial cheating will stop them from doing so. But the loss to PSG, while a first of the season in matches which matter, highlighted a few of the defensive frailties that Sunderland and Ipswich have also been able to exploit.

Against that? A near-unstoppable front line which has plundered 18 goals in the last five games – but Antoine Semenyo is now out for two months and Erling Haaland could miss this midweek fixture in particular. It surely won’t be enough for a loss to make a difference to where the points go, but it will be something for Maresca to manage as the campaign rolls on nonetheless.

There won’t be any excuse for Athens to turn up and not be energised – they requested, and were granted, a free weekend domestically in preparation for this fixture. Even so, it’s unlikely they pinpointed a trip to Manchester as one where points will come from in the search to finish in the top 24. For that they’ll need nine or ten points; there's three are on the board after beating LASK but after this game comes Real Madrid, Como, Galatasaray, Roma and Dortmund – and it's hard to see where at least six more will come from.

City beat Ipswich at the weekend to make it nine wins and one defeat – that PSG game – in ten this term. Shakhtar Donetsk are the only team to beat the Greeks, meanwhile, though they have drawn a couple domestically too. AEK didn’t play at the weekend as they had requested a postponement.

Nico O’Reilly remains a doubt and Semenyo is out. Haaland is available, says Maresca, but that doesn’t mean he’ll definitely start. Former Brentford goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha is out for AEK with a wrist injury so veteran backup Alberto Brignoli probably plays.

With no Semenyo and an alternative goal source maybe required, Rayan Cherki will become even more valuable. He’s ahead of 98% of attacking midfielders in Europe over the past year for chances created and top for touches – after being kept back at the weekend he’ll surely be let loose here, all guns blazing as chance-creator and -taker alike.
Haaland or no Haaland, City should walk it by a distance: Man City 3-0 AEK Athens.

League Two side Fleetwood Town will face Everton at Highbury in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.
The lowest-ranked side left in the competition have already made history by reaching the last eight after they stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties on Tuesday.
Everton confirmed their place in the quarter-finals on Thursday night, with a 3-1 win over Newcastle in an all-Premier League tie.
Holders Manchester City will host the only other non-Premier League side - League One Bradford City - at Etihad Stadium after they needed penalties to get past Brighton in the last 16.

The other two fixtures will be all-Premier League affairs with Liverpool, who also required a penalty shootout to beat Chelsea, hosting Bournemouth and Crystal Palace taking on Sunderland at Selhurst Park.
Quarter-final fixtures will take place in the week commencing 14 December.

          Winning Starts and WSL Titles: Are Manchester City on Course to Retain Their Crown in 2026-27?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 16, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Reigning WSL champions Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record after five matchdays of the 2026-27 season. Is there any stopping Andrée Jeglertz’s side?
Manchester City’s impressive 4-2 victory over Arsenal just before the international break at the Etihad Stadium continued their 100% start to the 2026-27 league campaign.
The reigning WSL champions have made it five wins from five, with Andrée Jeglertz’s side holding a two-point lead at the top as league action resumes this weekend.
But how often does a fast start lead to a team winning the WSL title? We look across history to see if it's mattered or not.
Man City have become the 10th team in WSL history to win their first five games of the season.

The more surprising statistic is that only three of the previous nine sides have followed up their fantastic start to the season with a WSL title at the end of that campaign; one apiece for Man City, Arsenal and Chelsea.

The most recent example was Chelsea in 2024-25. In what was Sonia Bompastor’s first season at the club, the Blues enjoyed a phenomenal start, winning each of their first nine games in the WSL before going on to lift the league title for the sixth successive season.
That nine-game winning streak at the start of the campaign equalled the best-ever start by a team in a WSL season, set by Arsenal in 2018-19 on the way to lifting the league title.
The third occasion of a team winning the top-flight title after winning their first five games of the season came in 2016 via Man City under Nick Cushing.
The Citizens went on to extend their winning start to six games in 2016 before securing the title in a 16-game season by five points over Chelsea.
City went one game better at the start of 2017-18, winning their first seven WSL matches that season, but then won just five of their final 11 games and finished second to Chelsea.

Arsenal are the only side to finish outside the top two places in the WSL table after winning all of their opening five games in a season – and they did it twice. They won their first five games in both 2020-21 and 2022-23 before eventually finishing in third.

Excluding the 2017 Spring Series, only one of the previous 15 WSL champions have gone on to lift the title after taking fewer than 10 points from their opening five matches, with Liverpool's remarkable 2014 triumph the sole exception.

That season, the Reds collected just six points from their first five games (W1 D3 L1) before mounting a remarkable turnaround to finish level on points with Chelsea and claim the title on goal difference.

Man City, meanwhile, are already in stronger territory than they were during their title-winning 2025-26 campaign. They lost one of their opening five matches last season (W4 L1), collecting 12 points before going on to secure a second WSL crown. Indeed, City are one of only six champions in the competition's history to have lost any of their first five league games, while no team has ever won the WSL after losing more than once in that span.

With 21 games still left to play in 2026-27, there will be more twists and turns in the WSL title race, but Man City have made the perfect start in their quest to win back-to-back crowns for the first time in their history.

9cna4pd5zgf3zcjqd3ndy6j5.title: Semenyo confident he can be Man City's Haaland backup
9cna4pd5zgf3zcjqd3ndy6j5.subtitle: Having scored twice against Sunderland, Antoine Semenyo backed himself to play as a makeshift number nine for Manchester City if needed.
paragraphs: Antoine Semenyo is confident he has the attributes to deputise for Erling Haaland as Manchester City's striker if required, following his brace against Sunderland.
Semenyo netted either side of half-time as City claimed a thrilling 5-3 victory over the Black Cats on Sunday, maintaining their 100% Premier League record going into the international break.
The Ghanaian also laid on an assist for Rayan Cherki, scoring and assisting in the same Premier League game for the fourth time in his career, and the second as a City player.

Since joining from Bournemouth in January, the Ghana international has scored 13 goals in 34 appearances for City in all competitions – only Haaland (19 goals in 32 games) has outscored him in that span.

In that same time, Semenyo has overperformed his expected goals (xG) total of 7.74 by a greater margin than any other City player (+5.26), while his conversion rate of 20.6% is slightly better than Haaland's 20.4%.

With City not signing another recognised striker in the summer transfer window, some have suggested Semenyo may have to deputise as a number nine at some point this season, and he is up for the challenge.
"I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from! But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem with doing that," he said, as quoted by ESPN.
"I think that [finishing] just comes naturally. Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner with a good connection, I know it will go in."
Another City attacker who has enjoyed an outstanding start to the season is Cherki, who showed quick feet inside the Sunderland area to score City's second goal on Sunday.
The Frenchman's six goal involvements in all competitions this season (four goals, two assists) are the second-most of any City player, behind Haaland (seven goals).
"I'm very happy because it was the goal to make it 2-1. I needed to help my team-mates," Cherki told City's website. "I want to give them good passes.
"I need to score a lot of goals for my team. I love the fans. And I think the fans saw a big game, so I'm very happy about that."

City now have three weeks off before travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool in their next Premier League game on October 11, having started a top-flight season with five straight wins for only the fifth time (also 1912-13, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2023-24).
"Everyone feels good," Semenyo said of the mood around Enzo Maresca's squad.
"It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent or too relaxed. We know there are a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning; we just have to keep going. It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games, and we'll keep improving."

9jtzg32iryds13tvegizu12bp.title: 'Fragile' Napoli still concerning Allegri despite Champions League win
9jtzg32iryds13tvegizu12bp.subtitle: Napoli earned their first Champions League win of the season in a thriller with Bodo/Glimt, but Massimiliano Allegri was left wanting more.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri conceded his Napoli team still caused him concerns despite getting their Champions League campaign up and running with a 4-3 win over Bodo/Glimt.
After losses to Arsenal and Villarreal in their first two games, Scott McTominay's brace proved decisive at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
Matteo Politano gave Napoli the dream start when he sensationally volleyed home after just 54 seconds, but Bodo hit back through Jens Petter Hauge in the 27th minute.
Napoli went into the break ahead through McTominay, but Bodo pegged them back again when Andreas Helmersen beat Alex Meret.
But the hosts were able to get over the line as McTominay and then Odin Bjortuft's 88th-minute own goal rendered Sondre Fet's stoppage-time strike a consolation.
Napoli secured a win in the Champions League for the first time in five games (D1 L4), while they scored four goals in a European match for the first time since beating Ajax 4-2 in October 2022.
Allegri has come under pressure early on in his Napoli tenure, and he acknowledged his team still looked "fragile".
"Naturally, the more quality players you have on the field, the better, but it's also true that results change your opinion," Allegri said, as quoted by Football Italia.
"In Florence and Venice, we had scoring opportunities where we got the final pass wrong. The same was true against Inter and Como.
"What we absolutely must improve is the sense of fragility. When you are fragile, you don't attack or defend as effectively."
Napoli came into Tuesday's clash on the back of defeats to Villarreal and Venezia.

Bodo got the better of the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 2.67 from their 15 shots compared to Napoli's tally of 1.53 from their 17 attempts, though eight of those did force Nikita Haikin into making a save.
"We made a lot of mistakes at the start of the game, and it is never easy in the Champions League," Allegri added.

"When we are close to the penalty area, we allow too many balls to get through easily, but this is work we must do with patience to read and intercept those passing channels, because that is what allows you to then go on the counter-attack."
One positive Allegri was keen to highlight was the performance of Kevin De Bruyne, who operated in a deep-lying midfield role alongside Frank Anguissa and McTominay.

De Bruyne provided the assist for McTominay's first goal just before the break, while he also finished with team-high totals for chances created (seven) and passes in the final third (24), while only Rafa Marin (102) had more touches than the Belgian's 82 (level with Amir Rrahmani) for Napoli.
"Kevin is an extraordinary player, I told him he's going to really enjoy himself playing in front of the defence," Allegri said of De Bruyne's position change.
"We also needed to rest [Stanislav] Lobotka, who did well when he came off the bench.
"Anguissa played 60 minutes, but he was making his first start, so inevitably the defence dropped a little deeper too. McTominay scored two goals, but he is not the real Scott yet.
"Fortunately, we have a lot of games and can get everyone back to match fitness, but defending deep we still let the ball through too many times."

9kd6rrgse05s10zvt9osppm8q.title: Inter boss Chivu desperate for victory amid Champions League struggles
9kd6rrgse05s10zvt9osppm8q.subtitle: Inter have lost both of their Champions League matches this season and the last four overall ahead of hosting Shakhtar Donetsk.
paragraphs: Cristian Chivu has urged his Inter side to "be ready to bring home the result" ahead of their Champions League meetings with Shakhtar Donetsk.
Inter has struggled in the competition this season, losing to Real Madrid and Club Brugge in their opening two league-phase games.
They are currently on their longest-ever losing streak in the European Cup/Champions League (four matches).
Inter have also lost seven of their last eight (W1), which is more than they did in their previous 41 in the competition combined (six).
"We are aware of the defeats in the Champions League; there's no need to keep reminding us," said Chivu.
"We lost two matches; we want to rediscover the energy that goes hand in hand with our ambitions.
"There's too much talk of the past and what we didn't do. We need to think about Shakhtar and be ready to bring home the result."
Including qualifiers, Inter are unbeaten in their seven games against Shakhtar (W3 D4), while keeping six clean sheets (only one goal conceded).

Of fixtures played at least three times in the European Cup/Champions League, none have a lower goals-per-game ratio than matches played between Inter and Shakhtar (0.5 – two goals in four games, both scored by Inter).

However, Shakhtar remain unbeaten in the Champions League so far this season (W1 D1) – only twice in their previous 19 appearances in the competition have they avoided defeat in each of their first three games, doing so in 2012-13 and 2014-15.
"Shakhtar are strong, they play in the Champions League, and those who play in the Champions League are evolved and have quality," added Chivu.
"They have quality, legs, intensity. The coach positions them well on the pitch; they have intensity with the ball and without the ball and a precise identity.
"We must be ourselves; we must be the team with a certain self-esteem, knowing that the past counts for little at this moment. What matters is today to prepare for Wednesday."

9ktfcq7vynfq1itjoek2qh0aa.title: Denmark 2-0 Wales: Isaksen stars to get Riemer's side off the mark
9ktfcq7vynfq1itjoek2qh0aa.subtitle: Denmark got their first win of the 2026-27 Nations League, with two second-half goals helping them past Wales in Copenhagen.
paragraphs: Denmark earned their first win of the Nations League after cruising to a 2-0 victory over Wales at Parken.
A Ben Davies own goal broke the deadlock before Gustav Isaksen added some insurance, as Denmark moved onto three points in Group A4, leaving Wales bottom with none.
Isaksen and Patrick Dorgu gave Wales a couple of early warnings, flashing efforts just wide of the left post before the former thought he had broken the deadlock 24 minutes in.

A pacy counter-attack saw Rasmus Hojlund lift a delicate cross between the defenders and Isaksen superbly volleyed past a helpless Danny Ward, but it was chalked off following a VAR review for an offside in the build-up.
From a quick throw-in, Hojlund then teed up Mikkel Damsgaard on the edge of the D, but his fizzing drive struck the foot of the left post.

Connor Roberts saw an instinctive flick tipped over by Filip Jorgensen in Wales' best chance of the first half, while Neco Williams' deflected drive flew into the goalkeeper's gloves just after the break.
Damsgaard's whipped right-sided free-kick caused chaos in the 53rd minute, and in trying to block Hojlund from getting to the ball, Davies deflected it into the back of his own net.

It was another Damsgaard free-kick that led to the second goal, too. Joachim Andersen's header was cleared off the line, but Isaksen put his laces through the rebound to send a deflected volley over Ward in the 66th minute – this one survived the VAR check.

Two late goals were both ruled out, with Hojlund drifting offside before turning past Ward with four minutes of the 90 remaining, while Williams' finish did not count after the referee blew his whistle early for a foul by Ethan Ampadu in the build-up.
Isaksen piles more misery on Wales
Craig Bellamy was proud of what he saw from his side against Portugal on Friday, but Wales fell just short again in Copenhagen after Denmark turned on the style.
While Isaksen will be pleased to finish with his name on the scoresheet, he could easily have had a double – the offside against Hojlund denied him a spectacular first goal.
Since his senior Denmark debut in March 2024, Isaksen is the joint-top scorer for the nation (seven, level with Hojlund), with six of his goals coming at Parken.
Davies, meanwhile, left with an unwanted mark against his name - in his 102nd appearance for his country, he scored his first own goal.

The lack of goals at the other end may prove to be a worry for Wales, who have failed to score in the first half of any of their six games in 2026 in all competitions, attempting 30 shots without success.
They had 10 attempts in total on Sunday, worth 0.65 expected goals (xG), while Denmark had double the number of shots, racking up 1.31 xG from those.

9pmbx3r5ywbe12bwyy8afk2au.title: Aston Villa 2-2 Brentford: Ajer salvages point in four-goal thriller
9pmbx3r5ywbe12bwyy8afk2au.subtitle: Aston Villa and Brentford shared the spoils in a thrilling 2-2 draw at Villa Park, with quickfire goals in both halves.
paragraphs: The points were split in a breathless Premier League encounter between Aston Villa and Brentford, which finished 2-2.
Saturday's contest at Villa Park featured two sets of quickfire goals, with Brentford going ahead early on, being pegged back and, eventually, having to rescue a draw themselves.
Tyrone Mings' sloppy pass gifted Brentford a chance in the 10th minute, with Yehor Yarmoliuk on hand to drill home from the edge of the Villa box.
Yet Nicolas Jackson restored parity within two minutes when he latched onto a deflected effort and coolly tucked in.
Caoimhin Kelleher made a superb double save on the stroke of half-time, denying Jackson and John McGinn.
McGinn, however, seemed to have put Villa on course for their first home win of the season in the league when his effort deflected in off Kristoffer Ajer in the 77th minute.

Ajer, though, had the final say, brilliantly cutting inside from the left flank to meet Jaidon Anthony's pass, before dribbling his way through a crowd of defenders and slotting home a sublime equaliser just two minutes later.
Quickfire goals galore
The old adage says a team is never more vulnerable than they are after they have just scored. And that was certainly the case here.
There were only 88 seconds between Yarmoliuk's opener for Brentford and Jackson's equaliser for Villa.
And in the second half, just 146 seconds separated the McGinn and Ajer goals.

Brentford became the first side since Liverpool in 2018-19 to open the scoring in each of their first six Premier League games of a season, while the Bees are unbeaten when scoring first in their last 17 league matches, since November 2025 against (W10 D7).

Villa, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their opening three home games in a league campaign for the first time since 2015-16, when they were without a win in their first nine league matches at Villa Park (D3 L6).
But Unai Emery will be buoyed by Jackson's form.

Jackson has scored in successive Premier League games for the first time since December 2024, while he now has three goals against Brentford in the competition, only registering more against Tottenham (five) and West Ham (four).

9tje2qt2giqs1j8limk6xtqk3.title: Manchester United 1-0 Liverpool: Zigiotti Olme strike secures back-to-back WSL wins
9tje2qt2giqs1j8limk6xtqk3.subtitle: An early mistake by Khiara Keating was punished by Julia Zigiotti Olme as Manchester United defeated rivals Liverpool 1-0.
paragraphs: Julia Zigiotti Olme was the matchwinner for Manchester United in their 1-0 victory over Liverpool in the Women's Super League.

The Swedish midfielder scored the only goal at Progress with Unity Stadium in the sixth minute, with Liverpool unable to beat Phallon Tullis-Joyce at the other end after an inspired performance from the United goalkeeper.

United's opener came after a blunder at the back from Khiara Keating. The Liverpool shot-stopper passed the ball straight to Zigiotti Olme, who composed herself with a few touches before lifting over a backtracking Keating.

Liverpool responded well to that mistake with Cornelia Kapocs and Beata Olsson denied by a brilliant double save from Tullis-Joyce, while Jess Park saw a deflected effort hit the crossbar for United before the break.
Marie-Therese Hobinger saw a well-struck shot from distance saved by the Red Devils' goalkeeper, before Jenna Clark failed to direct Natalia Ramos' corner on target.
United squandered a golden opportunity to double their lead as Elisabeth Terland's curler was pushed away by Keating, but it mattered little as Eva Olid's side held on for all three points.
Olid's United hit their stride

After failing to win any of their first three WSL games (D1 L2), which included a 5-0 defeat to Chelsea, there was some early pressure mounting on Olid's United, but they have responded in impressive fashion.

A 10-1 win over Sheffield United in the League Cup was followed by a 2-1 victory over West Ham in the WSL, with United now winning back-to-back games in the league and four in a row across all competitions.

Their performance against Liverpool, however, was far from perfect. The visitors won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.36 to 0.58 and recorded almost as many shots on target (eight) as United had attempts overall (nine).

Nevertheless, Tullis-Joyce's eight saves proved crucial as the Red Devils kept a clean sheet in a WSL home game for the first time since September 2025, ending an 11-game run of conceding in such games.

9vlzkzlzx76w132ohhn99dphy.title: 'Anything is possible' for Brighton as owner eyes major trophy
9vlzkzlzx76w132ohhn99dphy.subtitle: Brighton have hit the ground running in 2026-27 so far, and owner Tony Bloom has high hopes for what they can achieve this season.
paragraphs: Brighton owner Tony Bloom says "anything is possible" as the club target silverware following a stunning start to the 2026-27 season.
Brighton are currently third in the Premier League with 10 points, having lost just one of their matches so far (W3 D1).
They have also secured their place in the Conference League after winning their play-off, with their European campaign beginning next month.
And Brighton are also through to the fourth round of the EFL Cup after a superb 3-2 comeback win over Manchester United after going 2-0 down in the opening 10 minutes.

The Seagulls entered the international break with another statement result, thrashing reigning Premier League champions Arsenal 3-0, and Bloom has aspirations of emulating Leicester City's fairytale this season.

"The biggest teams in the league have a massive financial advantage, but in any one season, anything can happen, as you saw with Leicester City, so it's good to have dreams and goals for us as a club, and also for our fans," Bloom told Sky Sports.
"It's really difficult for teams outside those top six to win the Premier League.
“But anything is possible.
"We're after a major trophy, so obviously any major trophy would be a massive achievement for the football club.
"The Premier League is the bread and butter, and we're really optimistic that we can at least finish in the European places if not a bit higher than that."
Brighton are the highest goalscorers in the Premier League this season, with their 16 goals the most by a side in their first five games since Manchester City in 2022-23 (19).
No player has been involved in more top-flight goals this term than Pascal Gross (six – three goals, three assists), after he scored and assisted against Arsenal.

Fabian Hurzeler, who extended his contract through to 2029 back in May, has also been key to their current dominance, and Bloom was full of praise for his head coach, who led Brighton to an eighth-place finish last term.
"I have huge confidence in Fabian and our group of players," he said.
"As you say, we had 10 players out for most of August, so we've got some key players coming back, with some expected to return after the international break.

"It's very early to start predicting anything, but as Fabian always says, we've got to get the process right. We've got to prepare properly and always look to improve in every aspect of what we do. If we consistently do that, we have a very good chance of having a successful season.
"He's had to cope with lots of different situations in each of the two seasons, including a couple of bad runs when there would have been pressure on him.
"There's always pressure on elite head coaches at elite football clubs in elite football leagues, but he's come through both those situations extremely well.

"We, as a club, have helped him where we can, but he has had to do most of it himself. He's brought the players through with him and, now in his third year, he's gaining a huge amount of experience. I expect him to go from strength to strength."

9wtrdg18wrqk1da8o0h66zw4d.title: Roma 3-4 Real Madrid: Rudiger completes seven-minute comeback in Champions League thriller
9wtrdg18wrqk1da8o0h66zw4d.subtitle: Roma seemed to be heading for a famous victory over Real Madrid in the Champions League, but Jose Mourinho's men had other ideas.
paragraphs: Antonio Rudiger and Jose Mourinho came back to haunt Roma as Real Madrid scored three goals in seven minutes late on to claim a thrilling 4-3 Champions League win.
Los Blancos were trailing 3-1 before Carlos Espi struck in the 83rd minute.
From there, Endrick and former Roma defender Rudiger completely flipped the script at Stadio Olimpico as Mourinho got one over on his old club.

Roma, encouraged by a roaring home crowd, made a fast start as Matias Soule curled narrowly wide after just 48 seconds before Mario Hermoso's curling effort was tipped away by Thibaut Courtois at full stretch.

Paulo Dybala poked wide from Nahuel Molina's cutback, and though Roma received a blow when Manu Kone was forced off with an injury, they took a deserved lead when Marten de Roon's first-time strike from outside the box was deflected past Courtois in the 20th minute.

However, Madrid equalised against the run of play as Kylian Mbappe, on his 100th Champions League appearance, capitalised on an error from Mario Hermoso before lashing past Pierluigi Gollini, bringing up his 500th goal involvement in club football in the process (378 goals, 122 assists).

Jude Bellingham missed a huge opportunity before half-time, sweeping past the right post, and it looked to be costly when Donyell Malen scored twice in six second-half minutes; he first beat Courtois at the near post after a brilliant pass from Rodrigo Mora, while his second was a routine finish following a clever pass from Soule.
Mbappe had a goal disallowed after the hour-mark, but substitutes Espi and Endrick swung the tide.
Endrick's initial header from a corner was kept out by Gollini, but Espi was on hand to tap in the rebound.
Roma were undone again two minutes later when Endrick headed in unchallenged from Arda Guler's corner, and Rudiger had the final say as he volleyed past Gollini in the 90th minute.
Endrick stakes his claim as Mbappe breaks Messi record
Mourinho was asked about Endrick's lack of minutes in his pre-match press conference and the Portuguese insisted the youngster has a bright future at the club, which was perhaps proven by this cameo.
The Brazilian's two shots proved crucial, with the first leading to Espi's goal and the quickfire second giving Madrid hope of snatching all three points rather than settling for just a point.

While Endrick, Espi and Rudiger will take most of the headlines, it was another substitute in Guler who was the unsung hero. His two assists were crucial as his pinpoint crossing proved to be the difference in the end.

Only Lamine Yamal (40), Michael Olise (36) and Florian Thauvin (33) have created more chances in Europe's top five leagues this season than Guler (31), who will surely regain his starting position in Mourinho's team now.
Endrick, though, will likely have to still settle for a role as a super-sub, given he is behind Mbappe in the pecking order.

Mbappe became the youngest player to reach a century of European Cup/Champions League games, aged 27 years and 298 days, surpassing the record previously held by Lionel Messi (28 years, 84 days in 2015).

The France superstar became the eighth player to mark their 100th appearance in the competition with a goal, and the third to do so while playing for Madrid, after Cristiano Ronaldo in 2014 and Toni Kroos in 2019.

9yfpse1nligw17hy08vvewifd.title: Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth: Henderson leads the way in five-star victory
9yfpse1nligw17hy08vvewifd.subtitle: Chelsea returned from the international break with a statement victory, with Jordan Henderson paving the way for their win over Bournemouth.
paragraphs: Jordan Henderson scored twice and teed up another as he set Chelsea on their way to a thumping 5-1 win over Bournemouth in the Premier League.
Chelsea only needed three minutes to take a 2-0 lead, with Henderson and Morgan Rogers both scoring early, while Joao Pedro added their third within the first minute of the second half.
Evanilson pulled one back for Bournemouth, but Joao Pedro and Henderson both scored again to get Chelsea their first top-flight win since the end of August.

Chelsea flew out of the blocks, and Henderson took just 66 seconds to break the deadlock. Cole Palmer – whose new eight-year deal was announced on Saturday – powered forward before teeing up Henderson for a first-time finish that went in off the post.

And just 83 seconds after the restart, Chelsea had a second. Pedro Neto was denied by Djordje Petrovic, but the Blues kept it alive, with Henderson helping it to Rogers, who floated a shot into the goal, with Antonio Silva's header helping it over the goalkeeper.
The fast start continued as Bournemouth exploited space down the left, but Rayan was selfish and watched his effort sail into the stands.

Emiliano Martinez ensured Chelsea went into the break with their two-goal cushion, making a double save to keep out Rayan and Ryan Christie just after the half-hour mark before holding onto Silva's header.
And Chelsea wasted no time in the second half, either. Within 30 seconds, Joao Pedro had the ball in the back of the net after Neto latched onto a poor attempted clearance from Silva.
Bournemouth responded well, exploiting Chelsea's set-piece struggles. Moises Caicedo tried to hook a corner clear, but Evanilson stuck out a leg to send it flying past Martinez 51 minutes in.

It took Joao Pedro just 16 minutes to restore Chelsea's three-goal advantage, with Pep Chavarria taking Bournemouth's defence out of the game with a low cross, and the Brazilian was on hand to turn it in.
Henderson added some late gloss. Palmer won a free-kick, but caught Bournemouth out by not taking it, and Henderson curled it over the wall and past Petrovic at his near post.
Henderson rolls back the years

After failing to win three straight Premier League games before the international break, Chelsea came back with a bang and even more early goals. There have been five goals scored in the opening three minutes of games in the competition this term, with Chelsea scoring four of them.

Henderson got his first goal for the Blues in the process, becoming the club's oldest English goalscorer in the Premier League (36 years, 115 days) since John Terry against Watford in May 2017 (36y 159d).
In fact, only Emile Heskey against Derby County in April 1998 – in the opening two minutes – has a player both scored and assisted in a Premier League game earlier than Henderson (2:29).

And he also became the oldest Chelsea player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game, overtaking Gianluca Vialli (33y 245d), and the oldest for any side since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022 (37 v Norwich City).

This was only the second time Henderson has registered three goal involvements in a single game in the competition, last doing so back in April 2013 for Liverpool against Newcastle United (also two goals, one assist).

Joao Pedro missed the international break through injury, but looked strong on his return to the side; only Bruno Fernandes (22) has been involved in more top-flight goals in 2026 than the Brazilian (19 – 14 goals, five assists).

Marco Rose's wait for a first league win with Bournemouth continues, having now suffered back-to-back losses, but they had their chances. They actually won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.46 to 1.08, but could not finish off their chances.
