          Czechia vs England Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 28, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Tuesday's UEFA Nations League game at Fortuna Arena with our Czechia vs England prediction and preview. Thomas Tuchel’s side are looking to bounce back after a disappointing opening loss to Spain.
Both Czechia and England made a losing start to the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign, giving this fixture a must-win feeling early on in Group A3.

Luka Modrić rolled back the years to undo Czechia, helping Croatia to a 2-1 win on Saturday, while at the same time, England threw away a second-half lead to lose 3-2 at home to world champions Spain.

It was a disappointing return to action for the Three Lions, who made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive match for the first time since June 2019 against the Netherlands, which was also in the Nations League.

They were haunted once again by Mikel Oyarzabal, who popped up with the winner, just as he did in the Euro 2024 final. Harry Kane’s unsuccessful penalty attempt shortly after the break, when England were leading 2-1, proved particularly costly.
England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions – also their heartbreaking World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina – as many as in their previous 23 combined.
They’ve not lost consecutive games since June/September 2022, also in the Nations League against Hungary and Italy.

But England’s recent defensive record will be the biggest worry for Thomas Tuchel. His team have conceded 13 goals in their last six games, almost double the amount they had in their first 17 under the German coach (7).
Indeed, they’ve conceded 3+ goals in their last two matches, last doing so in three in a row in February 1927.

At the other end of the pitch, England look just as strong as usual, and Kane has netted four goals in six Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition. That's more than he scored across the first three editions of the competition he played in (3 in 18 games – 2018-19, 2020-21, 2022-23).

And he’s scored 17 goals in 19 appearances under Tuchel – since the German took charge in March 2025, only Erling Haaland (26), Kylian Mbappé (19) and Oyarzabal (18) have hit the back of the net more often than Kane in all competitions for European nations.
Jude Bellingham wasn’t on the scoresheet against Spain, but he did set up Anthony Gordon’s opener before winning the penalty after the break.
Bellingham has been involved in nine goals in his last nine international appearances (7 goals, 2 assists), more than any other England player since the start of the World Cup.

But Czechia have a goal threat of their own, and they will be hoping  Adam Karabec can make an impact against England. He averages a goal or an assist every 89 minutes for Czechia (3 goals, 1 assist in 355 minutes), netting in the loss against Croatia.
But Czechia are in desperate need of a win themselves after a difficult recent period that saw them exit the World Cup in the group stage with only one point to their name.
They’ve lost their last two games in all competitions, last losing more consecutively between June and September 2022 (4).
And that defeat to Croatia last time out ended a 19-game unbeaten home run (W14 D5) – they have not lost consecutive home matches since June 2016, a record they will be keen not to match.
This will be England’s first away game against Czechia since October 2019, a 2-1 defeat in a Euro 2020 qualifier.
Only three other teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (3), France (2) and Sweden (2).
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on that last visit in 2019.

A28A7CFA3C3253257A444144589CD8CA.title: Preview: Real Madrid face RB Leipzig on Matchday 3
A28A7CFA3C3253257A444144589CD8CA.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Real Madrid face RB Leipzig on Matchday 3ShareReal Madrid host RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday as they look to secure their third win from three in the competition.

It's been a perfect start to the Champions League campaign for José Mourinho‘s side, and despite some hiccups in LaLiga, they're starting to look back to their best. Madrid secured a phenomenal 4-1 victory against Sevilla last time out in the league, and they'll be hoping to continue that fine form in the Champions League.

Meanwhile, it's been a mixed season for RB Leipzig so far. They suffered a 4-1 defeat against Como in their opening game of the Champions League, while they also lost 6-1 to Bayern Munich in their previous Bundesliga clash.
The last time these two sides met was back in 2024, with a 1-1 draw being played out.

Real Madrid will be without Rodrygo, Ferland Mendy, and Raúl Asencio once again, as the trio continue their recoveries from injury. Vinícius Júnior will be available once again after he missed the previous LaLiga match due to suspension, but he's available for the Champions League – the only question is whether Mourinho will favour him over Yan Diomande, the man they they brought in from Leipzig over the summer?
Christoph Baumgartner and Assan Ouedraogo should be the only Leipzig players who will miss this game due to injury.

It's only been a couple of games for Madrid in the Champions League so far, but we've certainly seen an interesting setup from Mourinho. The Spanish side are used to completely dominating games, even in the Champions League, but Mourinho has them sitting back and allowing the opposition to have the ball.

Only five sides in this season's Champions League have had less of the ball than Madrid so far. Against Inter in their opening match, Madrid had just 36% possession but still managed to create 2.76 expected goals.
As we saw last time out against Bayern Munich, Leipzig have struggled defensively so far this season. They've conceded 1.8 goals per game, but there's no doubt it could have been more.

No side in the Bundesliga has had to make more saves than Leipzig so far this season. In the Champions League, it's not been much better, considering they conceded four times against Como in their opening match.

Of course, the likes of Vinícius and Kylian Mbappé will be some of the players to watch against Leipzig, but Arda Güler could be the wildcard. Against Roma in their previous Champions League match, the Turkish international came off the bench to set up two goals, earning himself a start against Sevilla.

Playing in a deep role, Güler hit a phenomenal strike to give Madrid the lead against Sevilla, while he also created the joint most chances in the game. That could have earned him another start against Leipzig, as he's arguably been one of Madrid's best players this season.
With Madrid being at home, we're going for a 3-1 victory for Mourinho's side

We’re five matches into the 2026-27 Premier League season, meaning we now have more information than we did at the start of the campaign. So, how have the title predictions changed in the Opta supercomputer’s model?
It’s still very early days, but the nascent Premier League table is beginning to take shape as we head into the international break.

With five wins from five, Manchester City sit at the summit as the only team with a 100% winning record. Opta’s pre-season favourites, Arsenal, are second, three points behind, with Brighton and Brentford, who have both made hugely impressive starts, rounding out the top four.
But how have those early-season results affected the Opta supercomputer’s predictions for the title? Let’s find out.
As a reminder, Arsenal were the model’s pre-season favourites. The Opta supercomputer gave them a 40.6% chance of defending their 2025-26 title on the eve of the season.
Manchester City (19.6%) were comfortably second favourites, followed by Liverpool (9.2%) and Manchester United (6.6%).
Despite suffering a heavy defeat to Brighton at the weekend, Arsenal remain the Opta supercomputer’s favourites to lift the trophy, with a 43.7% chance of winning the title.

Manchester City (39.8%) are hot on their heels. Their perfect start, as well as Arsenal’s weekend defeat, means the title race is now definitely a two-horse contest in the supercomputer’s eyes, rather than the procession many thought it might be for Arsenal.
Together, Arsenal and Man City account for 83.4% of all the title equity in the supercomputer’s predictions.

Liverpool (5.7%) are the model’s third favourites. They are currently unbeaten under new manager Andoni Iraola, but have drawn three of their five games so far. As a result, their title hopes have fallen by 3.5 percentage points, from 9.2% before the season to 5.7% now.

Brighton, the architects of Arsenal’s downfall this weekend, have made a hugely impressive start. They are the division’s top scorers with 16 goals, boast the best goal difference at +11 and handed Arsenal their first defeat since 19 April, 155 days ago. They look like the real deal.
The Seagulls are now fourth in the Opta supercomputer’s title predictions, with a 4.2% chance of winning an improbable Premier League title.
From there, a multitude of teams are clustered around the 1% mark. Brentford have a 1.2% chance, Everton 1.1%, Chelsea 1.0%, and Manchester United are given a 0.9% chance.
Manchester City’s title chances have increased by 20.2 percentage points, more any other team across the first five matchdays.
As mentioned, City began the season as the supercomputer’s second favourites, but they have made a perfect start to life under Enzo Maresca.

Maresca is the sixth manager to win his first five Premier League games in charge of a club, after Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea (six), Pep Guardiola at Manchester City (six), Craig Shakespeare at Leicester City (five), Maurizio Sarri at Chelsea (five) and Ole Gunnar Solskjær at Manchester United (six).

Arsenal’s title chances have also increased, rising 3.0 percentage points from their pre-season figure. That might seem surprising given their defeat to Brighton, but several of the teams that started the season among the favourites have already faltered.
Chelsea and Manchester United, for example, have both made poor starts, while Liverpool have dropped points in three of their first five games.
Brighton are the only other team to rise significantly. Their chances of winning the Premier League title have more than doubled (2.0% to 4.2%) following their excellent start.
It’s been a disappointing start to the campaign for Manchester United.

A475FA5C266AB656576E0EE0F13BF5C1.title: Preview: Barça take their 100% record to Real Betis
A475FA5C266AB656576E0EE0F13BF5C1.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Barça take their 100% record to Real BetisShareIt’s not often that a top-three clash in LaLiga doesn’t involve at least one club from the capital city, but the exciting Real Betis host title favourites Barcelona with just two places between them on Saturday.
Hansi Flick’s side look the real deal this season and the term “free-scoring” could have been hand-crafted for their start to 2026/27.

Averaging well over four goals a game so far, the roaming and roving of Raphinha, Dani Olmo and Fermín López has proven near-impossible to stop. Adding more pace on the flanks has been a great move too, with Anthony Gordon settling well, and that’s before considering the class of Lamine Yamal.

A huge 43 goals in the first ten games of the campaign has included scoring five times in three of their first four outings, then also seven against Santander. Unsurprisingly they are top for xG (30.5) but it’s eye-opening to see them well over ten clear of their nearest challenger already (Real Madrid, 19.9) and a similar gap for possession: 70% average, with Villarreal next at 60%. They are LaLiga’s dominant force in the first third of the season, and it’s not just for in-possession metrics – they lead the clean sheets table and the lowest xG conceded, too.

But for all Barcelona’s excellent start, this will be a real test. Two months into the league season and two games into the Champions League campaign, and their opponents in green and white have lost just once – that should tell you everything about the quality, but also the resilience, on show at the Estadio La Cartuja these days.

They’ve beaten Real Sociedad, Valencia and Real Madrid, won at Lille and saw off Porto – though that does make the 5-2 loss at Levante more puzzling. Manuel Pellegrini’s side are well-balanced, have threats from in-form attackers in Troy Parrott and Abde Ezzalzouli, have experience throughout the team and look capable of improving on last year’s fifth-place finish.

Betis have only lost three games since the end of March, including a Europa League semi-final – and one against Barcelona near the end of last term. This term it’s eight wins from ten in all competitions.
Barcelona themselves have a perfect ten from ten.
Júnior Firpo misses out again for Betis and Aitor Ruibal is closing in on a return. Barcelona will be missing Andreas Christensen, Frenkie de Jong and long-term absentee Roony Bardghji.

Betis will look to shut down Barça’s talented attackers by preventing the supply line – which means Rodri will need a huge showing both on and off the ball. Not often a problem for him but this is the game to show his immense worth: against LaLiga midfielders this season he’s ahead of 95% for recoveries, 92% for interceptions, 94% for winning duels, 98 for touches, 93% for headed shots and the full 100% for successful passes.
The hosts will play with no fear but it’s also hard to see them keeping Barça at bay all game long: Betis 1-2 Barcelona.

          Top Scoring Players For Each Club in the Premier League
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
There have been 51 different clubs to play in the Premier League since it began in 1992-93, but who is the top-scoring player for each of those sides? We look at the all-time top Premier League goalscorers for each club.

Ollie Watkins‘ goal for Aston Villa against Bournemouth on 10 May 2025 took him to 75 Premier League goals for the club, moving him past Gabby Agbonlahor as the top scorer in the competition for the Villans.
The English forward left the club in August 2026 to join Saudi side Al-Hilal after reaching 91 Premier League goals in a Villa shirt.
With Watkins the most recent player to become his club's outright top scorer, which other players have scored the most goals for each club to play in the Premier League?
Below are the players to score the most goals for each of the 51 clubs to have played in the Premier League since it began in 1992.

Harry Kane is the only player to have scored at least 200 goals for a single club in the competition, with the England captain scoring 213 times for Tottenham before he departed in 2023 for Bayern Munich.

Only 10 clubs have seen at least one player score 100 times for them in the Premier League, while Alan Shearer is the only player to have scored at least 100 goals for two clubs in the competition, netting 148 for Newcastle after previously scoring 112 in the competition at Blackburn.

Shearer is one of only two players to top the Premier League scoring charts for two separate clubs, alongside Chris Wood. The New Zealander has 37 goals for Nottingham Forest, and also leads the way for Burnley, with 49 goals in the competition for the Clarets.
Cardiff City have the lowest scoring top goalscorer in Premier League history with Jordon Mutch scoring seven goals for the Welsh club in the competition in 2013-14.

A5723EB80EAEC7130F7C5ECC1C129F11.title: Preview: Galatasaray face in-form Barcelona in Champions League clash
A5723EB80EAEC7130F7C5ECC1C129F11.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Galatasaray face in-form Barcelona in Champions League clashShareTurkish Super Lig league leaders Galatasaray welcome Barcelona to Istanbul in the Champions League on Tuesday evening.
Both sides have begun their European campaigns in contrasting fashion, but the intimating atmosphere at the Rams Park Stadyumu could prove crucial for the Turkish outfit.
Domestically, Galatasaray are sitting pretty at the top of the Turkish Super Lig having won five of their opening seven matches.

Over the weekend, the capital side defeated Kasimpaşa 3-1, despite playing the final 25 minutes with 10 men. The scores were level until Barış Alper Yılmaz and Mario Lemina netted in the dying moments to seal all three points.
That victory could be vital, especially considering the mighty Barcelona visit the Turkish capital on Tuesday evening.
You have to go all the way back to November 1994 for Galatasaray’s last win over the Catalan side, losing four of the six subsequent meetings since.
While domestic form has been solid enough, Okan Burak’s men suffered a disappointing 3-1 defeat to Sporting CP in their first Champions League tie of the campaign.

Despite taking the lead after just five minutes, the Portuguese outfit netted three goals without reply. Another defeat on matchday two will make progression to the knockout stages even more difficult.
Nine games. Nine wins. Barcelona have been utterly ruthless during the opening few weeks of the 2025/26 season under Hansi Flick.
Across those nine games, the Spaniards have scored a staggering 39 goals, conceding just eight goals in the process.
How long can this winning streak continue? Who knows, but Flick has his team playing some scintillating football and they are certainly showing no signs of slowing down anytime soon.

Raphinha and Lamine Yamal have been the star men this term for the club, registering 17 and 15 goal contributions so far. Summer signings Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon have also settled in rather well, while Gabriel Jesus has scored three goals in just five games since joining from Arsenal.
Flick’s attacking players are doing the business and on this note, Barcelona are surely one of the favourites to win a first Champions League crown since 2015 come May.
Perhaps a tad too early to be labeling Flick’s men as the team to beat, but if they can continue this sort of form over the coming months, who can stop them?
Wilfried Singo is a doubt for the home side, while Victor Osimhen is being monitored, despite coming on as a substitute last time out. It remains to be seen whether he is ready to start.
Raphinha is absent for Barcelona, alongside Andreas Christensen and Rooney Bardghji. Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong also looks likely to miss the tie due to injury.
Barcelona shouldn’t be affected by the boisterous atmosphere inside Rams Park on Tuesday evening as they chase a tenth successive competitive victory this term.

The Spanish side last managed nine consecutive wins to start a season back in 1935/36. Can Galatasaray cause a shock by securing all three points when the two sides meet? Given the European form of both sides, that looks unlikely: Galatasaray 0-3 Barcelona.

          Goals at a 60-Year High, Swans Flying, and Burnley's Breakdown: The Championship's Biggest Early-Season Storylines
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Following an extended break for international football, the Championship returns this weekend. After almost three weeks off, here‘s a recap of the need-to-know stats before the action gets back under way.
There have already been 277 goals scored in the Championship in 2026-27, with this the highest total after eight matchdays of a season since 2012-13 (295).
With 95 games played, the goals-per-game average is 2.92, higher than any full Championship season since the competition rebranded in 2004-05 (the highest for a completed season is 2.74 in 2010-11).
In fact, this is currently the highest goals-per-game average the second tier in England has witnessed since 1966-67 (2.95).

West Ham lead the way in the goalscoring stakes, with 22 goals after eight games. That equals Coventry City’s tally at this stage last season. The previous team before them to score that many goals after eight matches in the Championship was QPR in 2010-11 (22). The only team to score more after eight games in a season than West Ham since the Championship rebrand in 2004-05 were Wolves in 2008-09 (23).
All three of those sides went on to win the league title that season – that's certainly a good omen for the Hammers.

Swansea City sit top of the Championship table as we return to action following the extended international break. It’s the first time that Swansea have been top of the league this late into a season since October 2019, when they eventually finished sixth and lost in the play-off semis.

Their tally of 17 points is quite low for a league leader after eight games of a season. Across 22 years of the Championship since it rebranded in 2004-05, this is just the eighth occasion that a team have been top of the league with 17 points or fewer, with only one of those teams having a lower points total – Brighton in 2012-13 (16).

Swansea have been winning for the biggest proportion of match time in the Championship this season (44.2%) and will hope to keep their strong form going in order to earn a spot back in the Premier League for the first time since their relegation in 2017-18.

Interestingly, while there are 10 points and 20 places between Swansea and rivals Cardiff City in the real Championship table, Opta’s expected points table places Cardiff a spot above the Swans (7th vs 8th). That suggests Swansea’s current league position is slightly inflated compared to their underlying performances at both ends of the pitch.

There’s no doubt that boss Vitor Matos has turned his side into one of the most intense teams out of possession in the attacking half, though. They rank first in the Championship for possession won in the final third (40) and lead the league rankings for total high turnovers (70) as well as shots (16) and goals (3) from high turnovers too.
The jump from League One to the Championship feels small compared to that of the Championship to the Premier League.

While teams promoted from the Championship have struggled to compete overall in the top flight over recent seasons, the same can’t be said for teams that were promoted from the third tier to the second tier.

Since 2022-23, just one of 12 promoted teams has been relegated back to League One in the first season as a Championship club. That team were Wigan Athletic in 2022-23, and the Latics did have a six-point deduction, but that didn’t end up making a difference.
We’re potentially on course for a fourth successive Championship season without a single promoted side being relegated back to League One.

Last season saw as many as two promoted clubs finish inside the top half of the Championship table – Wrexham in 7th and Birmingham City in 10th – for the first time since 2017-18, and there’s every chance that feat might be achieved again.

Lincoln City (11) and Bolton Wanderers (10) have reached double-figures for points already and sit around mid-table, while Cardiff are just above the relegation zone on seven points. Both Cardiff (7th) and Lincoln (9th) are inside the top 10 for expected points, however.

Before this season, Burnley’s last four appearances in the Championship have all ended in automatic promotion at the end of the campaign (2013-14, 2015-16, 2022-23 and 2024-25). The last two of those have seen them accrue 100+ points – the only club to reach a century of points more than once in the second tier in history.
In basic terms, when Burnley have been a Championship club, we’re used to seeing them at the top of the table. But not this time.

The Clarets sit bottom of the table after eight matchdays and are the only team without a win in the Championship. Their tally of four points is their lowest after eight games of a season outside the top flight since 1997-98 in the second tier (also 4), when they ended the season 20th.

ABCD31EB225836237D72B5DA76BF2BA5.title: Preview: Manchester United face Como in early KO
ABCD31EB225836237D72B5DA76BF2BA5.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Manchester United face Como in early KOShareCesc Fàbregas’ Serie A side host Manchester United on the banks of Lake Como as Michael Carrick’s team tries to stay afloat.

Como’s rise to the top level of European football has been remarkable and their recent showings prove Cesc Fàbregas’ side have the potential to make an even bigger impact on the Champions League this season.

The 4-1 thumping of RB Leipzig in Como’s first-ever Champions League fixture made a big statement even if they came back to earth with a loss to Feyenoord last time out. Manchester United have been warned.

Times have been tough for Michael Carrick and his players of late. United are winless in their last six games in all competitions with tension within the dressing room exposed by Lisandro Martínez’s explosive comments.

The 1-1 draw away to Leeds United on Sunday hinted at Carrick adopting a more pragmatic approach to turn around his team’s poor form, but victories are needed to truly prove Manchester United’s slide has been halted.
While this has the appearance of a David versus Goliath clash in terms of the stature and history of the two teams, Como have the quality to pile more misery on United.
Martin Baturina and Nico Paz are two of the best young attacking midfielders in the game with the pair both expected to start as potential difference makers for Como in the attacking third.
Barutina and Paz will likely play off Anastasios Douvikas as Como’s attacking focal point. The Greek striker will be a handful for the United defence such is his skill at holding up the ball.
Promising young defender Jacobo Ramón is expected to start at the heart of Como’s back three while Lucas Da Cunha and Luis Milla will be charged with controlling things in the centre of midfield.
Carrick could stick with the midfield set-up that showed encouraging signs against Leeds, meaning Bruno Fernandes might be in line to start on the left side again.

Bryan Mbeumo has scored two goals in his last three outings and so Carrick might not want to move the Cameroonian from the centre forward spot, especially given the lack of other options in that area.
Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans have shown signs of a partnership in central midfield while Martínez could start again in the backline despite his remarks about the club’s front office.
Trevoh Chalobah and Moise Kean are both injury concerns for the Serie A outfit while Assane Diao will be sidelined for the visit of Manchester United on Wednesday.
Benjamin Šeško, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte are currently missing for the Old Trafford outfit through injury with Leny Yoro set to miss the match following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Ayden Heaven is struggling with illness while Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw and Martínez are also carrying knocks that could limit their involvement. Martínez came off before the end at Elland Road on Sunday.
We could easily see United's miserable start to the season continue in Italy: Como 2-1 Manchester United.

B04DCCBBDB57B8C7531644880664EEF6.title: Yan Diomande is starting to live up to his massive price tag for Real Madrid

paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesYan Diomande is starting to live up to his massive price tag for Real MadridShareAfter a blockbuster €140m summer transfer, Yan Diomande is starting to show why he belongs at Real Madrid.

In Real Madrid’s collection of glittery, shimmering attackers, it can be easy to get lost. This is, after all, Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham’s club. Walking into the Santiago Bernabéu dressing room for the first time, Yan Diomande surely wondered how he would possibly stand out in all-white.

Recently, though, the Ivorian has started to show he belongs at Real Madrid, scoring his first goal for the club in the weekend win over Villarreal and subsequently impressing in a stunning Champions League comeback win against Roma. Diomande has found a role for himself when many doubted he would be able to.

Diomande was one of the breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup, shining for Ivory Coast as an irrepressible dribbler quick to take on a man down the wing. Before the tournament, there was talk of a €100m transfer from RB Leipzig. After four games at the World Cup, the Bundesliga club raised their asking price. This reflected his summer showing.

Real Madrid were first in line to pay that asking price, although it wasn’t immediately clear why. They were already well stocked for wingers, particularly on the left side where Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior prefer to operate. Real Madrid’s need appeared to be in other areas of their squad.

Some took the signing of Diomande as a sign that Real Madrid were preparing for Vinícius’ exit. The Brazilian spoke to Arsenal about a summer switch to the Premier League, but ultimately decided to stay at the Bernabéu, signing a new contract until the summer of 2032.

Two months later, it’s not exactly obvious how Diomande will fit into the same lineup as Mbappé and Vinícius. José Mourinho has tried using Diomande on the right side without much success – although he was able to contribute from this area against Roma. The 19-year-old has been deployed as an impact sub off the bench, but he has more recently forced his way into Mourinho’s XI over Vinícius.

It was with Mbappé, Vinícius and Diomande all on the pitch together that the latter scored his first goal in all white. The Ivorian drifted into a central position to receive a pass from Fede Valverde before turning and striking the ball into the far corner of the net. The sequence was a demonstration of the teenager’s adaptability.

This coupled with Vinícius’s slow start to the season has quickly increased Diomande’s importance to his new team even if the latter faced some criticism for his shaky first few performances as a Real Madrid player. The teenager’s response since then has been impressive.

Vinícius’s red card for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in Real Madrid’s win over Villarreal likely means Diomande will get an extended run in the team as the Brazilian serves a suspension. Such has been the extent of Vinícius’s dip in form that this could be a good thing for Los Blancos who face a critical run of fixtures culminating in a trip to Barcelona on 25 October.

The goal-scoring performance against Villarreal demonstrated how Diomande might be a better fit than Vinícius for Mourinho’s team. Primarily, the Ivorian combines more naturally with Mbappé in the final third, giving the Frenchman more space than Vinicius does when he is on the pitch.

While Vinícius’ first thought is usually to cut inside off the left side, Diomande offers more verticality. He can get to the byline which gives Real Madrid a different dimension in the attacking third. Rather than playing on top of Mbappé, Diomande has a profile that allows him to play around the French forward.

Individually, Diomande has a lot to his game that makes him potent in his own right. The Ivorian is averaging more dribbles per 90 minutes than any other Real Madrid player this season. On top of this, only Arda Güler, Jude Bellingham, Vinícius and Mbappé have created more chances, all of whom have started more league games.

There is still rawness to Diomande’s final product. He doesn’t always make the best decision in the final third, but the potential is clearly there for the teenager to develop into one of the most consistently dangerous wide forwards in the game. It’s why so many clubs spent the summer chasing him.

Real Madrid’s inherent chaos is a risk to Diomande’s development. If Mbappé and Vinícius are at the club for the long term, it’s difficult to envisage how Diomande will ever be more than just a supporting act. Three naturally left-sided attackers simply can’t fit into the same starting lineup.

Even if the Ivorian is outperforming his teammates, the internal politics of the situation could restrict him. He could be squeezed out of the Bernabéu because someone will surely have to be. For the time being, though, Diomande is establishing a platform for himself. One at the very highest level of the game, where he clearly belongs.

          England 5-0 Greece Stats (8-1 agg): Lionesses Storm Through World Cup Qualifying Tie
        
      
                          
                      Oct 13, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
England booked their place in the next round of Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs with a resounding five-goal win in Leicester.
England powered into the next round of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs after a 5-0 second-leg victory at King Power Stadium, which secured an 8-1 aggregate win.
Lauren James starred with two goals and an assist, with Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway also on the scoresheet as they set up a meeting with Ukraine in the next round.

It took just over two minutes for Russo to break the deadlock; James profited from a midfield mix-up and teed up the Arsenal striker, who skipped away from Eleni Markou's challenge to coolly slot past Styliani Katergiannaki.

Moments later, Hannah Hampton was alert to keep out Ioanna Papatheodorou at the other end before James doubled England's lead 16 minutes in, rifling a stunning strike into the top-right corner after meeting Maya Le Tissier's lay-off.
Le Tissier then blazed over from two yards out under pressure in the 29th minute, but it mattered little as England got two more goals in the following five minutes.
Stanway got in front of her defender to glance in Lauren Hemp's cross in the 30th minute before James ghosted in behind Greece's defence to meet Hemp's low delivery shortly after.

Lexi Potter thought she had marked her England debut with a goal on the stroke of half-time, as her drilled strike nestled into the bottom-right corner, but Stanway was penalised for a foul in the build-up.

Stanway continued to prove a threat, though, and had a goal disallowed herself after the break. She leapt to bring down Alex Greenwood's long pass before volleying past Katergiannaki, but she had just strayed marginally offside.
Stanway and Beth Mead both had chances to add to England's tally, but it was Russo who added some more gloss to the scoreline.
Freya Godfrey also came close to a debut goal, with her low curler pushed away by Katergiannaki, and despite England piling on the pressure late on, they could not find a sixth.
Despite scoring three goals in the first leg, one thing Sarina Wiegman highlighted as an area for improvement for the Lionesses was their finishing, having had 26 shots in Crete.
The first half proved England still have the golden touch in front of goal with four first-half goals, and they could have had more with two more disallowed on either side of the break.

James only played the first 45 minutes, but impressed, having three shots worth 0.66 expected goals (xG), scoring with both of her efforts on target, as well as getting an assist with the one chance she created.
But Stanway's fine form in World Cup qualifying continued as she is now England's top scorer under Wiegman with 33 goals, edging away from Mead (32).
Stanway is also just the second player to reach 50+ goal involvements (also 17 assists) under the Dutch manager, after Mead (58 – 32 goals, 26 assists).

Greece offered little going the other way, accumulating just 0.07 xG to England's 4.75, and the Lionesses have now won their last seven home matches in all competitions without conceding (24-0 on aggregate) for the first time in their history.

England will now face Ukraine for the second time in World Cup qualifying, having been in their group originally. They won both of those meetings by an aggregate 9-1, and they will be hoping for something similar with a place in the tournament on the line.

B24AF92EFF71C1370ECFF3F52A77B841.title: Preview: England host World Champions Spain at Wembley
B24AF92EFF71C1370ECFF3F52A77B841.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: England host World Champions Spain at WembleyShareEngland return to action for the first time since the World Cup with a Nations League match against opposition that couldn’t be more challenging.

Given the peculiarly timid manner in which they were eliminated from the World Cup against Argentina in July, there’s a case for saying that England’s first match of the 2026/27 season is more important than it might otherwise have been. The heat has turned up slightly under Thomas Tuchel as a result of the nature of that defeat, and he needs a decent performance in this match, if the pressure under him isn’t to build further.

Spain are their first opponents in Group A3 of the Nations League, and in theory the challenge couldn’t be much greater. Their head coach Luis de la Fuente certainly faces none of the pressures that could be set to build up behind the scenes for England. The visitors haven’t lost to anybody in two and a half years, while their last match saw them lift the World Cup trophy.

Given how strong Spain have been over much of the last two decades, England’s record against them isn’t completely terrible, though it’s been 15 years since they last beat them at Wembley and they’ve only won one of their last five meetings with them.

These two teams met in the first iteration of the Nations League in 2018, and away wins were the order of the day that time around, with Spain winning 2-1 at Wembley in September of that year and England winning 3-2 in Sevilla six weeks later.

Their last meeting came in the final of Euro 2024 in Berlin, when goals from Nico Williams and Mikel Oyarzabal handed Spain a 2-1 and the Henri Delaunay Trophy. In losing this match, England became the first team in the history of the European Championships to lose two consecutive finals.

One of the players who should know his opponents better than anyone else is midfielder Jude Bellingham, who is now up to almost 150 appearances for Real Madrid since his big money move to the Bernabéu from Borussia Dortmund in 2023. Bellingham saw his popularity soar during the World Cup, and he’ll be expected to take a leading role, if England are to find a way through Spain in this match.

One Spain player worth watching who may be back in their team for this match is Barcelona’s Fermín López. He missed the World Cup after fracturing his foot shortly before the start of the tournament, but he’s recovered and has worked his way back into a Barcelona team that is flying at the start of their domestic season. López has recently been subject to speculation that Manchester United could be preparing a £129 million move for him. The international break gives him a valuable opportunity to clear that background noise from his head for a couple of weeks.

There’s something almost traditional about a rash of withdrawals at the very start of an international break, and the Premier League hasn’t let us down this time. Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, and Tino Livramento have all been withdrawn from the England squad, while Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have both received late call-ups.

Spain have made changes from their World Cup squad for their opening Nations League matches, with Inter goalkeeper Josep Martínez, Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen, and Espanyol striker Roberto Fernández joining the squad along with Fermín López. Fernández is of particular interest, having started his season with six goals in seven matches in LaLiga. Joan García (knee), Marcos Llorente (retired from international football), Gavi (precautionary), Pedro Porro (hamstring) and Borja Iglesias (fitness) have all been omitted from the squad.

The mood surrounding the England team following the World Cup finals has been a peculiar one. On the one hand, there’s nothing ‘disgraceful’ about losing a World Cup semi-final. But on the other, the team’s performances throughout the tournament were patchy at times, and losing to Argentina in such a supine manner calls into question whether they’ll be able to go further, take that final step, and actually win a major tournament. Co-hosting the next Euros means that expectations will be sky-high again in two years’ time, but the evidence that they have the capability to do this remains patchy.

Kicking off their 2026/27 matches against Spain is a huge challenge, but there’s a case for saying that these are the best circumstances to do so. La Roja proved what they needed to prove in the summer, and with this match being at the exact half-way point between being a friendly and a competitive match, their opponents are unlikely to be as fired up for this match as they might have been had they been meeting under just about any other circumstances.

Home advantage helps, though Spain are unbeaten on their last two trips to Wembley, and a desire to stay fit throughout the club season may lead to the players from both teams deciding that going full throttle in this match isn’t the wisest of ideas, especially considering that, with the other two teams in the group being Croatia and Czechia, there are no ‘easy’ games in this Nations League group. A 1-1 draw with no serious injuries on either team would leave everybody feeling that they’ve got through it relatively unscathed.

          Chelsea vs Arsenal Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 27, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
While they are both unbeaten, Chelsea and Arsenal have not been at their best in 2026-27. Can either side apply pressure on Manchester City? We preview a heavyweight showdown at Stamford Bridge that could have major ramifications for the early WSL title race.
Heading into Matchday 4, only one team in the Women's Super League have a perfect record, with champions Manchester City setting the pace in 2026-27.

Chelsea were the pre-season favourites for the title, winning 40.8% of the Opta supercomputer's simulations, with Arsenal also expected to be challengers. But neither have matched their rivals' fast start.
There is still a very long way to go in the title race and both teams are unbeaten, but Sunday's clash at Stamford Bridge already feels pivotal for Chelsea and Arsenal.

Chelsea come into this match after a narrow 1-0 win over Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday, while Arsenal prevailed by the same scoreline against Køge on Tuesday, needing a 93rd-minute Mariona Caldentey penalty to secure the three points.
So, can either of them kick into gear in the WSL this weekend?
After a disappointing 1-1 draw with Aston Villa, Chelsea have strung together two wins, hammering Manchester United 5-0 before beating Birmingham City 2-0.
While they looked comfortable against Eva Olid's struggling United, there was plenty to be desired against Birmingham, namely their finishing.
They accumulated 3.9 expected goals (xG) from 22 shots, with eight of those on target and one hitting the woodwork. They also recorded five Opta-defined ‘big chances' but could only score twice.
Melvine Malard came off the bench to net on her WSL debut for the club in the second half, settling the nerves after they failed to get the goals their early dominance deserved.
But while there may be question marks over their chance conversion, they have started the season well defensively, conceding just one goal and keeping two clean sheets.
No team have faced fewer shots (14), while the Blues have also limited their opponents to just 1.3 expected goals against (xGA).

With a record like that, if they score the first goal, Arsenal could be in trouble; Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 45 WSL matches when leading at any stage (W38 D7), the longest run in the competition's history.
Arsenal, meanwhile, were expected to pick up where they left off at the end of last season, but it has been a stuttering start to their title charge.
They edged a 1-0 win over Brighton on the opening weekend, before drawing with Crystal Palace and Man Utd.

At this point, they are hoping to avoid matching an unwanted record: the Gunners could win as few as five points from their first four matches for the second time in the last three seasons after 2024-25, when the fourth game was a defeat to Chelsea (W1 D2).
In the WSL, they have netted just two goals – only promoted duo Palace and Charlton Athletic have scored fewer (both one) – and have massively underperformed their 5.9 xG.
The Gunners' shot conversion rate of 3.3% this term is also the worst seen in the WSL since bottom-of-the-league Yeovil Town in 2017-18 (2.2%).
They rank fourth for shots (60), with 10 of those classed as ‘big' chances, and have had 22 attempts on target.
It was a familiar story against Koge as they racked up 19 attempts worth 1.9 xG – a figure inflated by their late penalty – but only two of those shots were on target.

B44A8D222BC9D97A3C33B30EE5E986ED.title: Preview: Liverpool face Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea at Anfield
B44A8D222BC9D97A3C33B30EE5E986ED.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Liverpool face Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea at AnfieldShareThere are a number of eye-catching match-ups in the Carabao Cup this week but the pick of the bunch might be the game at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea.
What reception is Blues boss Xabi Alonso going to get?

Chelsea have been hot and cold. They recorded a 4-3 win over Brighton and an emphatic 5-1 win over Bournemouth. They hit Leeds United for six goals in the Carabao Cup. They have also given up two leads against Hull City at Stamford Bridge and had to settle for a draw. They’ve lost to Brentford and Spurs, too.

They find themselves in fifth position in the Premier League but it’s a bit of a false position. The xG table, for example, has them in 12th. They’re higher in the table as a result of their huge overperformance in attack. They’ve scored 6.7 more goals than they’ve been expected to. Brighton (+6.8) are the only team in the Premier League with a greater overperformance in attack.

The form table (last five Premier League matches) has Alonso’s side in eighth spot with two wins, two losses and a draw. They head to Anfield lacking real momentum. They’ve kept just one clean sheet all season too.
Liverpool, meanwhile, have been a little more steady. They’re sixth in the xG table and have the third best defensive record when looking at the underlying numbers.

The Reds are four from four following the loss to Manchester City. Andoni Iraola’s men dispatched Brighton over the weekend, recording a 2-0 win over the high-flying Seagulls. Alexander Isak found the back of the net again to make it six goals in the Premier League this term.

Things are starting to click for the Reds in attack and relationships are forming. They’re going to want to keep things moving in the right direction and making it five wins from five, as well as into the next round of the Carabao Cup, would be massive.

For the hosts, the focus will likely be on Rio Ngumoha. Iraola has done a good job managing his minutes and after the young winger was benched for the win over Brighton, the expectation is that he’ll start on Wednesday against his former club.

For the Blues, Jordan Henderson will want to make some sort of impression on his return to Anfield. He’s been in good form for Chelsea, bossing the midfield and even chipping in with goals and assists. The middle third has been an area of concern for the home side this term and Henderson will want to take advantage of this.

The away side have some personnel issues as they head to Anfield. Cole Palmer is suspended following his red card against Tottenham. The Blues are also without João Pedro, Emiliano Martínez, Pep Chavarría, Reece James, Jamie Gittens and Emanuel Emegha.
Liverpool meanwhile, are still without a host of names. Dominik Szoboszlai, Jeremie Frimpong, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are all missing while Víctor Muñoz remains doubtful.
We’re going to go with a home win, but it might be tight. Either 2-1 to Liverpool or they’ll progress via a penalty shootout.

What reception is Blues boss Xabi Alonso going to get?

Chelsea have been hot and cold. They recorded a 4-3 win over Brighton and an emphatic 5-1 win over Bournemouth. They hit Leeds United for six goals in the Carabao Cup. They have also given up two leads against Hull City at Stamford Bridge and had to settle for a draw. They’ve lost to Brentford and Spurs, too.

They find themselves in fifth position in the Premier League but it’s a bit of a false position. The xG table, for example, has them in 12th. They’re higher in the table as a result of their huge overperformance in attack. They’ve scored 6.7 more goals than they’ve been expected to. Brighton (+6.8) are the only team in the Premier League with a greater overperformance in attack.

paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Arsenal restart title defence against unbeaten LeedsShareThe longest-ever international break perhaps came at a good moment for champions Arsenal, and despite injury concerns arising during it they’ll emerge with renewed optimism.
That comes after Mikel Arteta signed a new long-term deal to stay as manager, taking him towards a decade in charge -and he’ll certainly be hoping to add more to last season’s Premier League title.

Leeds United will be a tough enough first opponent back, but two quickfire home games – with Lille midweek – against beatable sides will be a welcome remedy after the Gunners were dismantled by Brighton before the break. That game came after seven straight wins, but against both Sunderland and Ipswich immediately before the Seagulls, Arsenal had looked vulnerable and were perhaps fortunate to take maximum points.

That makes the reset moment an opportune one, with Arteta well aware that a return to winning ways is vital but also handily timed: Arsenal might go under the radar a little, given the focus and fury around Manchester City. Higher-profile opponents for the guilty-pending-appeal club will have them in the spotlight and maybe leave Arsenal to thrive in the shadows – something they’ve been adept at in previous campaigns. Still, there are questions to answer, including how to get Bruno Guimarães consistently into the side and who fills in for the injured internationals.

It’s easy to dismiss only five games in, but Leeds are fifth in the table and more pertinently, unbeaten. This will of course be their hardest test, but they thoroughly deserved their resounding win over Newcastle and their 3-5-2, in place since midway through last term, looks well-organised, hard to break down and capable of posing a big threat on the break.

Daniel Farke is getting the best out of a few key players, but it’s the fully-functional midfield which impresses most. Ethan Ampadu is a big defensive protector and Anton Stach is an all-action menace in both halves. They set the platform for success higher upfield, but this is very much a team-wide effective setup that the manager has put in place.

Arsenal have already kept six clean sheets this term including the Community Shield. It’s four wins from five in the league. For Leeds, a cup loss to Chelsea comes alongside two wins and three draws so far.

Kai Havertz, Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis picked up injuries on international duty, but Declan Rice is likely fine after missing the entire break. Ben White and William Saliba are also out, as is Joe Rodon for the visitors. Harry Wilson is a doubt.

Martin Ødegaard was in rampant form before the internationals and clocked four assists during it – in league terms he’s top 4% for line-breaking passes, top 6% for chances created and top 8% for expected assists among midfielders this term.
Not an easy one but a narrow home win wouldn’t be a shock, if Leeds can’t quickly regain momentum: Arsenal 1-0 Leeds.

          Liverpool vs Man City: Six Key Subplots Ahead of Sunday’s Charged Anfield Encounter
        
      
                          
                      Oct 10, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Reem Sarraf / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
All eyes will be on Anfield this Sunday when Liverpool host Manchester City in the Premier League. Leading into the game, we identify the key narratives to look out for.
Sunday’s clash between Liverpool and Manchester City is one of the most fascinating Premier League matches for years.
While there will be the usual intrigue of a heavyweight duel, the heat for this one has been dialled up by off-field matters that developed significantly during the international break.

On 29 September, the Premier League confirmed an independent commission found “Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation”.

City deny the allegations and confirmed on 2 October they had lodged an appeal, with any potential sanctions still to be determined. Nevertheless, it was a seismic development and one that could have a monumental impact on English football.
Sunday’s game will be City’s first outing since, and they can look forward to an especially vociferous welcome to Anfield.
Ahead of the match, we’ve identified several aspects that might gives clues as to which way the game goes – and there’s only one place to start…

Given what happened during the international break, City would’ve been expecting a hostile reception wherever they were playing next. But if they could’ve picked any ground not to play their first match following the guilty verdicts, Anfield – if not Old Trafford – would probably be the one.
For starters, there are few top-flight grounds in England as hostile as Anfield when the home fans are in the mood. And you can guarantee they’ll be up for this one.
But on top of that, City, like so many others, have a dreadful record at Anfield even at the best of times.

Of grounds they have played at more than once in the Premier League, they only have a worse points-per-game rate at Highbury (0.22) than they do at Anfield (0.59), and they have played more than three times as many games at the latter (29) as they have at Arsenal’s former home (nine).

In total, City have won only three of their 29 Premier League trips to Anfield, giving them one of their worst win rates (10.3%) at any stadium. They have also lost 18 of those games, equating to a 62.1% loss rate at Liverpool.

City did win there last season, coming from behind with two late goals to snatch a 2-1 win, but that came when Liverpool were in a particularly difficult moment that saw them manage one win in seven games, their title defence crumbling.
There was also a City win at Anfield in February 2021, though that was when games were played with no fans present due to the COVID-19 pandemic. That was their first win there in 18 visits.

Anfield is simply a very tough place to go. Even though Liverpool haven’t been the outright best side for much of the Premier League era, away sides still have a lower win percentage at Anfield (12.5%) than at any other stadium.
City will at least be going into the match in decent form.
After five matches, City are top of the Premier League having won all their matches, including a 1-0 victory at Manchester United in the derby despite spending over an hour with 10 men.

However, it is a little difficult to know how much City’s start will count for because, well, these are uncharted waters. Firstly, we’ve just had an unprecedented three-week international break, and secondly, we’ve no idea to what degree the off-field matters will have distracted Enzo Maresca’s team.
City’s situation might stoke something of a siege mentality in the squad, or it might overwhelm them.
Either way, despite obviously making a good start to the season (on the pitch), City haven’t looked unbeatable and can certainly consider themselves fortunate to have 15 points.

          Michael Carrick's Stay of Execution? Four Big Questions Facing Man Utd Over Next Nine Days
        
      
                          
                      Oct 30, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
When all seemed lost for Michael Carrick, Manchester United opted against dismissing him. But are they actually just biding their time ahead of the international break?

In the same week, Manchester United were battered by Como and Bournemouth, while the captain – who was dropped for the latter game – appeared to publicly criticise the coaching staff’s tactics. Somehow, Michael Carrick survived this.

The pressure was already on Carrick following a dismal start to the season, and there seemed to be no way out for him after the loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford. But the United hierarchy opted to stay their blade; Carrick avoided the axe for the time being.

It’s plausible the vociferous backing of Carrick from fans at Old Trafford – and the intense fury directed specifically at the players and club decision-makers – persuaded the club to give him more time. But with the next international break just around the corner and such moments typically seen as opportune times to change managers, Carrick is by no means out of the woods.

Whether the club actually want to give him more time or if this is just a stay of execution, only time will tell. But the overriding sense is that Carrick has a maximum of three games to save his job.
These are the key questions facing United over the next week or so…

Given how disappointing United’s performances have been, particularly against Como and Bournemouth, it’s difficult to see a way out for Carrick right now. They were so comfortably beaten in both games that the upturn in performance level needs to be incredibly dramatic and swift for him to save himself.
Obviously Carrick has managed to get a tune out of United before; their 39 points won last season after his appointment was more than any other club.

But the atmosphere clearly isn’t great, confidence is shot, and the situation with Bruno Fernandes going rogue during/after the Como game hardly gives the impression that the players are fully behind Carrick.
United’s outlook also isn’t helped by having a difficult run coming up before the international break.

In the Opta Power Rankings, their three upcoming opponents in all competitions (Chelsea, Roma, Villa) have an average rating of 93.2 out of 100; only three Premier League clubs have tougher opposition before the international break. And of the nine English clubs competing in Europe, all facing three matches in the next nine days, none have a tougher schedule than Manchester United.
If Carrick can get them back on track in the next 10 days, it will be genuinely impressive.

Match context has played a part, but it appears there’s been an attempt from United to have more control this season, straying slightly from the style that seemingly suited them so well under Carrick last term.

Possession is up from 49% to 56%, and they’re averaging an extra 43 final-third passes per game compared to the second half of 2025-26. So, that gives you an idea that they’re having more territory. Not that it's done them much good.

They have had more shots than anyone else, though the average xG value of those attempts is just 0.08, the second worst after Tottenham (0.07). And when they do create clear opportunities, they’ve not been clinical enough; only three teams are underperforming in relation to their xG to a greater degree than United (-2.8) this season.
The outlook in attack is pretty bleak, then, and it’s not much better at the other end.
Their opponents’ average xG per shot of 0.14 against United is the highest in the division, and their 40.2% of shots faced landing on target is the second-highest.
So, even though they aren’t conceding that many shots, the chances they are giving up are of high-quality.

There are numerous potential causes for this, and it’s fair to suggest their backline and midfield being so disrupted won’t have helped. But there’s an argument they could have done more to help themselves.

For instance, instead of moving for a greater degree of control, they might have decided that collectively sitting deeper to prioritise being compact and protecting their own goal while looking for transition opportunities was the best course of action.

B8593B52ED98D7F173134AB0C95DE0AF.title: How will Zinedine Zidane change France’s playing style after years of Deschamps-ball?
B8593B52ED98D7F173134AB0C95DE0AF.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesHow will Zinedine Zidane change France’s playing style after years of Deschamps-ball? ShareZinedine Zidane will take charge of his first matches as France’s new manager in the extended September and October international break.

Zinedine Zidane just had to bide his time. The three-times Champions League-winning manager could have taken any other job after leaving Real Madrid (for a second time) in 2021. He surely had offers. Zidane, however, remained patient as France’s next national team manager in waiting.

That patience paid off when the 54-year-old was officially named Les Bleus boss after the World Cup, confirming the worst kept secret in international football. Zidane was long seen as the natural heir to Didier Deschamps and now the former midfielder will get his chance to reshape the French national team in his own image.

What that image is, though, is unclear. While Zidane enjoyed incredible success as a manager over two spells at Real Madrid, winning three Champions League titles and two LaLiga titles, as well as two European Super Cups and two Club World Cups for good measure, he never had much of an identifiable playing style.

Zidane was the ultimate man-manager during his two managerial stints at the Santiago Bernabéu. The former Ballon d’Or winner instantly commanded the respect of Real Madrid’s superstars in a way some of his successors in the job were never able to do. Zidane managed by aura, and it worked.

At no point, however, did Zidane have an overarching tactical philosophy. Under his stewardship, Real Madrid played in quick transition. They were never able to control games through possession. Most of the time, they didn’t need to, but Zidane’s Real Madrid certainly weren’t revered for their tactical structure.

In many ways, Zidane’s Real Madrid played a similar brand of football to the style professed by Deschamps over 14 years as France boss. This should make the handover of managerial power a smooth one. There is a lot of stylistic overlap between Zidane’s game and Deschamps-ball.

The problem for Zidane, though, is that after nearly a decade-and-a-half of stodgy, conservative football under Deschamps, many French fans are ready for something different. They broadly want a more modern style of play and Zidane, for all his glittering success as a player and manager, might not be the man to deliver this.

Zidane has picked five new faces in his first France squad for the UEFA Nations League matches against Türkiye, Belgium and Italy. Liverpool centre back Jérémy Jacquet is expected to feature while Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul, Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha, Inter Milan’s Andy Diouf and Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes have all been included.

France’s squad is one of the most talented in the international arena right now. Their forward line is terrifying with Les Bleus capable of out-scoring any opponent. Zidane’s lack of tactical principles might not matter due to the level of attacking talent of his new team just as it didn’t matter much for Deschamps.

In Kylian Mbappé, Zidane has inherited one of the best players in the world. The Real Madrid forward hasn’t always been the easiest to coach as an individual and doesn’t offer much on the defensive side of the ball, but France has always seen the best version of Mbappé. He is at his most influential in the blue of his national team.

“For French people, he means a great deal – he’s a legend, he’s the nation’s ‘Zizou', he represents elegance, greatness,” said Mbappé when asked for his opinion on Zidane’s appointment. “⁠He ​made his mark on the history of the national team as a ​player and he had some truly iconic moments. He’s perhaps the player who most embodies the France team. He’s one of those players who ​transcended generations. He left an indelible mark on the history of French football.”

As the most iconic member of the France team that won the World Cup on home soil in 1998, Zidane’s legacy as a national hero is already secure. In a sense, he has nothing to lose by taking over as Les Bleus boss. Zidane has more credit in the bank than any new France manager in history.

Zidane is an anomaly in the modern game. At a time when every manager at the elite level seemingly has a philosophy and consistent values that underpin their view of the game, the Frenchman’s approach is vibes-based. That could work for him as an international manager even better than it did for him in the club game.

France under Deschamps were successful, but not always entertaining. Some fans believed Deschamps restricted Les Bleus as an attacking outfit when Mbappé and co should have been unleashed. Zidane might decide to do that. He might not. Nobody really knows what to expect from the great enigma of modern management now that he’s finally taken on a new challenge.

          Como vs Man Utd Prediction: Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      Jonathan Davies / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Wednesday's Champions League clash at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with our Como vs Man Utd prediction and preview. Can the Red Devils end their winless streak?
Manchester United will look to ease the pressure on Michael Carrick and put their recent struggles behind them when they resume their Champions League campaign against Como.

Following Sunday's 1-1 draw with cross-Pennine rivals Leeds United, in which Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo‘s first-half effort, Carrick has now overseen a six-match winless run in all competitions (D3 L3).
The Red Devils have been unable to build on the momentum of their 4-0 rout of Sabah on Matchday 1, beaten 2-0 by Atlético Madrid in Spain last week.

Pablo Barrios struck after just 47 seconds as United conceded in the opening minute of a Champions League game for only the fourth time – also doing so against Juventus in October 1997, Barcelona in November 1998, and Basel in November 2002.

Leny Yoro was sent off for a professional foul in the 74th minute – meaning he will miss Wednesday's trip to Italy – before Ademola Lookman condemned the Red Devils to their sixth defeat in nine Champions League matches (W1 D2).
Man Utd only lost 21% of their 190 matches in the competition under Alex Ferguson (W102 D49 L39). Since his retirement, though, they have been beaten in 38% of their 56 games (W24 D11 L21).

Last week's reverse at the Metropolitano also marked a sixth defeat in 10 Champions League outings away from Old Trafford (W1 D2), while they have only kept a single clean sheet in their last 15 such matches on the road (a 2-0 victory over Villarreal in November 2021).

United did have their chances in Madrid, though. They created four big chances without scoring any, their most without scoring in a Champions League game since September 2012 against Galatasaray (also 0/4).

Carrick will be looking for inspiration in Lombardy from the likes of Marcus Rashford, who could make his 50th Champions League appearance (34 for Man Utd, four for Aston Villa, 11 for Barcelona). Harry Kane (34), Raheem Sterling (20) and Andrew Cole (18) are the only English players to better Rashford's tally of 17 goals in their first 50 games in the competition.
Meanwhile, Como and Cesc Fàbregas will hope Assane Diao can shine again following his impressive start to the Champions League campaign.

After scoring in the 4-1 win over RB Leipzig and last week's 3-2 defeat at Feyenoord, the Senegal international became only the third player to find the net in an Italian club's opening two Champions League matches, after Alessandro Del Piero for Juventus in 1995, and former Man Utd striker Edinson Cavani for Napoli in 2011.
At 21 years and 37 days old, Diao also became the youngest African player to find the target in both his first two appearances in the competition.
However, his exploits last week in Rotterdam were not enough to prevent Como from becoming the 10th successive Italian side to fail to win their first away game in the Champions League (D4 L6).

I Lariani did make history, though, as only the second team not to name a single player from their own nation in the starting XI for either of their first two matches in the competition, after Sheriff Tiraspol in 2021-22.

Yet, Italy under-21 international Mattia Liberali did his hopes of featuring from the start on Matchday 3 no harm on Sunday, as he scored in a 3-1 victory at Fiorentina that ended his side's three-game winless streak in all competitions.

The only negative from Florence was the early withdrawal of Trevoh Chalobah, who faces a race to be fit for this game, with Fàbregas' side looking to become only the second Italian team after Lazio in 1999-2000 to win their first two home games in the European Cup/Champions League.

This will be the first ever meeting between Como and Man Utd, but it is not the first time the two coaches have faced off in the competition. The former midfield maestros were on opposing sides as players in the 2008-09 semi-finals, with Carrick and United beating Fàbregas' Arsenal 4-1 on aggregate.

Since the start of last season, there have been six meetings between English and Italian sides in the Champions League. The Premier League team has prevailed on five occasions, with the exception being Atalanta's 2-1 win over Chelsea in the league phase last term.
The Opta supercomputer marginally favours a Como victory, with the Serie A side given a 41.7% chance.

          Xabi Alonso Has ‘No Explanation’, So Why Are Chelsea Scoring So Many Early Goals?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Chelsea have started the Xabi Alonso era by scoring a remarkable number of goals very early on in their games. Why do they start so well, and why do they then fade?
Even though they’ve done it so many times already, it is still a surprise every time Chelsea repeat the trick.

On Saturday, Xabi Alonso’s side went into their meeting with Bournemouth having scored three goals in the opening five minutes of their first five league games this season. The other 19 Premier League teams had just two such goals between them.
And yet, it was still a shock to see them add to their total, but largely because of how they did it.

For starters, they didn’t just score once within the first five minutes of the game, but twice. And they didn’t just do it inside five minutes, but inside three. With goals from Jordan Henderson and Morgan Rogers by the time the clock read 2:29, Chelsea had raced into the third-earliest 2-0 lead in Premier League history (after Leicester vs Derby in April 1998 and Luton vs Brighton in January 2024).

Given Alonso’s reign had begun with João Pedro’s goal after 31 seconds of the season opener against Fulham, Roméo Lavia’s fourth-minute goal against Brighton, and Rogers’ second-minute strike at Arsenal, subsequent opponents might have been well advised to set up with Chelsea’s fast starts in mind. But they scored inside seven minutes against Hull and then twice within the first three minutes against Bournemouth.

The problem for their opponents is there is no pattern to follow. Chelsea don’t attack in a particular way from the early stages. There isn’t some single thing or theme that future opponents should be looking out for.

In fact, only once this season have Chelsea started off with a clear intention to put their opponents on the back foot by booting the ball straight out from kick-off for a throw-in deep in opposition territory. That was the 3-0 defeat at Brentford, the only game in which Chelsea didn’t score an early goal (or score at all for that matter).

Their manager insists there is no gameplan to start quickly, no intention to begin games with a focus on scoring early. “I have nothing to do with it, so I don’t have the answer,” Alonso said after the win over Bournemouth. “I have no explanation, so I can take no credit.”

Rogers disagrees. “I put it down to the manager’s team talks,” the midfielder said after he scored against Bournemouth this weekend, his third goal inside the first seven minutes of a Premier League game since joining Chelsea.
“He gets us firing, gets us going,” he continued. “We always want to start off on the front foot. It is about starting well and getting the lead.
“A lot of games, especially at home, we have won after jumping on the back of early goals. It’s a good trait to have which we need to keep doing.”
Alonso may not realise he is doing it, but Rogers’ comments suggest the manager is having an impact with his pre-game words.

Also, there may well be a feeling of momentum among the players. Reports from inside the dressing room suggest there is confidence they can score an early goal, and joking among the players as to who is going to score it, not as to whether the team will get one at all.
Whatever the reason, what's certain is the impressive volume of early goals and the efficiency with which they are finishing off chances at the start of games.

They have four goals inside the first three minutes of Premier League games this season, while the other 19 teams have just two between them. Chelsea’s four goals in this time have come from just five shots and 0.71 xG. The two goals scored by everyone else have been scored almost perfectly in line with the expected goals value of the shots (1.92 xG).
Inside the first five minutes of games, they have five goals from 1.52 xG. Expand things to the opening 15 minutes, and they have seven goals from 2.28 xG.

Chelsea have outperformed their xG so comprehensively early on because their early goals have almost exclusively been difficult chances. João Pedro’s goal at Fulham was a gorgeous chipped finish over the goalkeeper. Rogers’ strike at Arsenal was a volley from the edge of the area, while his opener against Hull was a fine low finish from the corner of the box. And both early goals against Bournemouth last weekend were from distance with several opponents in the way.

Perhaps Chelsea players feel at the start of games that they have more licence to shoot from distance, emboldened to take things on that they might not later in games because there is less pressure to make their chances count. And this, along with the confidence that Alonso gives them could just be an effective combination.

Clearly, Chelsea also have an abundance of talented attacking players, all of whom have started the season in form, and it might just be a coincidence that they are performing so well early on in games.
