          Perfect Starts and Premier League Titles: Is There Any Correlation?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author, Yash Thakur / Design, Emily Millen / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City may have started the season with five wins from five, but as the Premier League has proved many times in the past, it’s a marathon, not a sprint.
The first international break of the season always gives us time to take stock and try to make sense of what’s happened in the early matchdays of the season.
Of course, 2026-27 isn’t much different to usual, but this time around clubs have got longer to stew on whether they’ve started well or struggled given the extended September/October pause.

Sitting at the top of the Premier League table, Manchester City are the only team to have won all five of their matches in 2026-27, with the club starting life after Pep Guardiola in the best way possible on the pitch.
They’ve already opened up a three-point gap over biggest title rivals Arsenal, but does their fast start necessarily mean a first Premier League title in three years is expected for City?

Now, there’s obviously the small matter of City reportedly being found guilty of 114 of the 115 financial rule breaches they were charged for and which they deny, but for the purposes of this article, we’ll try to ignore all the potential ramifications of that.
Enzo Maresca’s side became the 15th different team to win their opening five games of a Premier League season, and it’s the fourth occasion City have managed it.

They have only won the title in one of the three previous seasons they’ve made a 100% winning start from five games, though. They won the league in 2023-24 but failed to capitalise on five wins from five to start both 2015-16 and 2016-17.
That follows a wider trend across the league when looking at teams to win their opening five matches of a season.

Only four of the 14 teams to win their first five matches of a Premier League season have gone on to win the title that season (29%): Man City in 2023-24, Liverpool in 2019-20 and Chelsea in both 2009-10 and 2005-06.

Perhaps most importantly, all four teams went on to add to their winning streak to start those seasons. Chelsea in 2009-10 and Man City in 2023-24 extended their run by another game (six wins), while Liverpool (8 wins in 2019-20) and Chelsea (9 wins in 2005-06) went on the two longest winning runs by a club to start a Premier League season.
Tottenham hold the record for the most consecutive wins to start a top-flight league season, winning their first 11 games in 1960-61. Unsurprisingly, they won the title that campaign.

But a winning start doesn’t guarantee success, as Manchester United found in 1985-86. Despite winning their first 10 games that season (and remaining unbeaten in their first 15) under Ron Atkinson, the Red Devils collapsed and ended the season in fourth place.

It must be said, City’s start this season has been helped by having one of the easiest five-game openings for the 2026-27.According to the Opta Power Rankings, City had the second-easiest start this season, with their opponents having an average Opta Power Rating of 91.2. Only Liverpool (91.1) were handed a simpler start to the season by the Premier League fixture computer.
However, as many say, there are no easy games in the Premier League, so maybe City’s start shouldn’t be downplayed.
One stat to potentially worry City is that none of the previous seven clubs to start a Premier League season with exactly five wins have gone on the win the title in that campaign.

The most recent of those was Liverpool last season. Arne Slot’s reigning champions won games against Bournemouth, Newcastle, Arsenal, Burnley and Everton to open the 2025-26 Premier League campaign with five wins from five before losing four in a row. The fact Liverpool won four of their first five games with goals scored after the 83rd minute or later pointed to their run being slightly unsustainable, and so it proved.

Question marks about City’s defensive qualities in their opening five games this season have pointed to the possibility of this being another case of an unsustainable winning run. Their credentials will be tested upon the return to Premier League action on MD6 when they head to Anfield to play Liverpool, who are still unbeaten under new boss Andoni Iraola.
The lowest position a team have finished after winning their first five games of a Premier League season is sixth (Newcastle United in 1994-95), although that did come in a 42-game campaign.

Looking back across all English top-flight history, City’s current streak is the 40th different occasion of a team winning their first five games in a season. Just 14 of the previous 39 have gone on to win the league title (36%).

BA79AC69ABBC2EBF9177C12F91C035D5.title: Preview: Arsenal are back home for clash with Everton
BA79AC69ABBC2EBF9177C12F91C035D5.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Arsenal are back home for clash with EvertonShareArsenal host Everton in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon as they look to climb to the top of the table.
The Gunners start the day three points behind leaders Manchester City, and they'll need a big goal-difference swing in order to climb to first place.
They face an Everton side that only lost their first game of the season last time out against Chelsea, but they are still searching for their first win on the road this campaign.
Arsenal will certainly fancy their chances, given their record at home against Everton of late, conceding just twice across the last five meetings.

Arsenal were dealt a crucial blow heading into this game after Bukayo Saka was substituted due to a quad injury against Bayern Munich during the week. He looks set to be out for six to eight weeks, which is a huge disappointment for Arsenal.
Saka joins William Saliba and Christos Tzolis on the sidelines, but Piero Hincapié has been passed fit.

David Moyes refused to provide any injury updates heading into this game. Jarrad Branthwaite couldn't be seen in the training footage earlier this week, but that's the only injury concern we know of for the Toffees.

It's not quite clicked for Arsenal in the final third just yet, especially in comparison to their competitors at the top. Manchester City have bagged 19 goals, while Brighton have a phenomenal 23, but Arsenal are sitting on just 11.

Injuries all across the front line have hampered the Gunners this season, while they have lost two final-third threats in Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard. They face a resolute defence in Everton this weekend, so Mikel Arteta will be hoping it finally clicks.
Creating and scoring chances has been a major issue for Everton so far this season. Moyes’ side have created just 9.4 expected goals, finding the back of the net on eight occasions.

Everton don't create an awful lot, but when they do, it tends to be a big chance. No side in the Premier League has missed more big chances than Everton this season, as they sit level with Bournemouth on 18.
Eberechi Eze has struggled for regular minutes so far this season. The England international has started to become a threat in the final third for the Gunners, scoring twice in his last three games.

The injuries to Saka and Tzolis almost guarantee Eze a start in this game, and it's a real opportunity for him to prove himself to Arteta. Eze has struggled to make a huge impact off the left-hand side so far this season, but it's a position he's going to have to get used to. He's going to find it difficult to displace Martin Ødegaard in the number 10 role.
Everton held Arsenal for 89 minutes the last time these two sides met. They'll likely be strong defensively again, but Arsenal should nick it. We're going for a 2-0 home win.

          Manchester City vs Arsenal Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 3, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With just five points and two goals to their name in the WSL this season, Arsenal are under increasing pressure ahead of facing Man City. Can the Gunners show up here? We look ahead to this crucial showdown with our Man City vs Arsenal prediction and preview.
Arsenal were Manchester City's closest challengers for the Women's Super League title last season, with Andree Jeglertz's team finishing five points ahead of the Gunners.

Just four games into the 2026-27 campaign, however, the gap already stands at seven points. City are the division's only team with a perfect record, while Arsenal's title ambitions are in danger of slipping away before the first international break of the season.
If Renée Slegers' side are to have any hope of mounting a genuine challenge at the top of the table this season, avoiding defeat at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday feels essential.
City have made a solid start to their title defence, beating Birmingham City (3-1), Aston Villa (4-1) and Liverpool (4-2), before battling to a 1-0 win at Charlton Athletic last weekend.
Jeglertz's team have averaged over 3.0 expected goals (xG) per game this term, putting up a tally of 12.2 (only bettered by Chelsea's 12.4) across the first four matchdays.
Though, they have looked a little more vulnerable than the Swede would like at the other end, with three WSL teams having lower expected goals against (xGA) totals than their 3.96.

Home has certainly been a fortress. City have won each of their last 14 WSL matches on home soil, with only Chelsea enjoying a longer home winning streak in the competition's history, recording 22 straight victories between March 2022 and February 2024.

Sunday's game will also represent a landmark appearance for City captain Alex Greenwood. She will become the 10th player to reach the 200-game mark in the WSL, and if she starts, could overtake Gemma Bonner (192) for the most starts made in a player’s first 200 outings in the competition.

Meanwhile, Arsenal have endured a remarkably slow start; the Gunners are only the third side in WSL history to score two goals or fewer and concede two goals or fewer across their opening four matches of a season, after Liverpool in 2014 and Chelsea in 2018-19. Both of those teams recovered to finish third.
Slegers' side are winless in their last three league matches (D2 L1) and could equal their longest winless run in the competition, previously recorded in May 2014 and October 2023.

Arsenal generated just 0.79 xG in last Sunday's 1-0 defeat to Chelsea before surrendering a 2-0 lead in a 2-2 UEFA Women's Champions League draw with Paris FC on Wednesday. The Gunners created just 1.16 xG from open play compared to Paris FC's 1.44, making the result difficult to argue with, despite the controversial ending that saw the hosts equalise from a penalty given against Leah Williamson for handball.
Their attacking struggles are becoming increasingly clear. Arsenal are not creating enough high-quality opportunities and when chances do arrive, they are not taking them often enough.
Alessia Russo has underperformed her xG by 2.14 goals, the largest negative differential of any player in the division, although she did at least find the net in Paris during the week.

Given Arsenal's attacking woes, they may look to Stina Blackstenius for inspiration against an opponent she has consistently troubled. The Swede has scored four goals and provided two assists across her last five WSL appearances against City, recording a goal involvement in each game.

That is the joint-longest such streak against the Citizens in the competition's history, alongside Lee Geum-Min, while Blackstenius is also the only player to have scored three winning goals against City in the WSL.

An intriguing battle could also unfold down the flanks. Only Lauren Hemp (nine) has created more chances following a carry of at least five metres than Arsenal's Lisa Baum (five) this season. The pair also rank joint-top in the league for shot-ending carries (eight each), alongside Lauren James.
Historically, few WSL rivalries have been as evenly contested as Manchester City and Arsenal.

This is one of only two fixtures in the competition's history in which both teams have recorded 10 or more victories against the other, with the Gunners holding a narrow 12-11 advantage, alongside two draws.
The fixture is also one of the league's most familiar matchups.

          Greece 1-3 England Stats: Le Tissier and Russo Propel Wiegman's Side to First-Leg Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
England put themselves in a strong position in their first Women's World Cup play-off, with a 3-1 win over Greece in Crete on Friday evening.
Quickfire goals from Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo helped secure England a 3-1 win over Greece in the first leg of their Women's FIFA World Cup play-off semi-final.
Georgia Stanway broke the deadlock for the European champions in the first half before Le Tissier and Russo added to their tally just after the hour-mark.
Greece set up a slightly nervy ending when Kallisti Brouksair pulled one back, but Sarina Wiegman's side held out for a two-goal cushion to take to King Power Stadium for the second leg on Tuesday.
England started well, with Stanway dragging a low shot wide of the left post and Laura Blindkilde Brown scuffing a tame shot straight at Rafailia-Dimitra Petaloti.
Moments later, the space opened up for Keira Walsh just outside the box, though her powerful drilled effort was pushed away by Petaloti.

James had the ball in the back of the net in the 19th minute, latching onto Stanway's throughball before dinking a lovely effort over Petaloti after spotting the goalkeeper off her line. However, the goal was ruled out following a VAR check as James was offside.
Ioanna Papatheodorou gave England a scare, dancing her way through their half before taking aim from range, only to hit the corner of the goal frame.
Stanway broke the deadlock six minutes before half-time, with a slick England move exploiting the pockets in Greece's defence as Russo teed up her Arsenal team-mate for a poked finish.

Le Tissier forced a sharp stop from Petaloti to spark the second half into life and then found space on the right of the box and, from the angle, beat the goalkeeper for power to score her first England goal in the 63rd minute.
Beth Mead then dragged wide moments after the restart, but was unselfish when she got the ball in the 67th minute, skipping past two challenges to tee up Russo for a pinpoint effort.
Greece burst back into life in the later stages, with Papatheodorou squaring it back to Brouksair, who sent her low shot across goal into the bottom-right corner 77 minutes in.
England kept pushing for a fourth towards the end, and substitute Jess Park powered her strike against the underside of the bar, though it bounced the wrong side of the goal line.
England enjoyed a largely successful World Cup qualifying campaign, but it was a 4-0 defeat to world champions Spain that proved particularly damaging.
With a place in next year's tournament on the line, though, England made a strong start to their play-off campaign as they aim to use that path to a major tournament for a fifth time.

Greece had an impressive record of their own in qualifying, having gone through their League C campaign with a 100% win record, and they showed their fight until the end to ensure they got a goal on the board.

The Lionesses were utterly dominant, having 26 shots worth 2.07 expected goals (xG), with seven of those on target as Petaloti kept her team in the game for large parts. England also had 58 touches in the opposition box.
Greece, by contrast, mustered just 0.16 xG and scored with their only shot on target in the match, giving England a worry in the final 15 minutes to cut the deficit ahead of the second leg.
Stanway got the scoring going, meaning she has now scored against 23 different nations for England and has netted five goals during their qualifying campaign – more than any other player in the team.
They have now gone unbeaten in their last 42 fixtures when facing an opponent for the very first time (W35 D7), and Wiegman will be hoping for a similar performance next week.

          The Florian Wirtz Debate: Were Jamie Carragher’s Criticisms Harsh or Fair?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Florian Wirtz has not had the impact many expected at Liverpool, and the criticism is getting louder. Has the Germany international really been that bad, though?
When Florian Wirtz signed for Liverpool in the summer of 2025, there was only one logical assumption.

The Premier League champions at the time had recruited one of the hottest young talents in world football, one who played a pivotal role in winning a historic double with Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24, and was already a star of the German national team at just 22 years old.
An exciting and productive attacking midfielder being added to the best team in England? How could this not work?
Football has a habit of flipping the script, though, making the impossible possible, and ensuring that something that seems so obviously right is somehow wrong.

The 2025-26 season was difficult for several reasons at Anfield, and Wirtz, along with other new arrivals, struggled to make as much of an impact as expected for the fee agreed (£100 million + £16m in add-ons).

There were conversations among fans this summer as to how long he and fellow nine-figure signing Alexander Isak should be given before difficult questions needed be asked. The broad consensus was ‘until Christmas’.
As it turned out, the real answer was ‘after the opening game of the season’ as Wirtz and Isak laboured in Liverpool's 2-2 draw at Newcastle United and loud doubts began to surface.
Jamie Carragher spoke on the first Monday Night Football of the season about Wirtz’s signing in 2025 potentially being part of the “worst transfer window in Premier League history”.

The former Liverpool defender was criticising a few players that time – and Isak has since gone on to score four times in his last four Premier League appearances to somewhat silence his doubters – but Carragher did focus his ire solely on Wirtz on Sunday in the first episode of his new podcast for Sky Sports.

🗣️ "I don't think Florian Wirtz is in poor form, what we're seeing is what he is"Jamie Carragher says he is worried for Florian Wirtz and doesn't see how he will hurt teams ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/umgZ0ZgfzK

“The reason I worry is, I don’t think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we’re seeing is what he is,” he said. “The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he’s given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

“The gap he’s got to [close] to justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can’t get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it’s still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.
“I think [Andoni] Iraola’s got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.”

Carragher particularly derided Wirtz – who has just one assist in six games this season – for his performance in Sunday’s 1-0 win at Bournemouth, labelling it “one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt.”
Reds boss Andoni Iraola was a little more generous in his review of Wirtz’s outing, though did accept when speaking to reporters that the German had struggled in the first half.
“He started the game slowly, I agree,” Iraola said. “After that first phase, I think we improved. Florian has helped us also to improve.
“Second half he was playing much better, he was finding better spots to receive and turn… I’m much more happy with his second half.”

On paper, Wirtz’s numbers from the game weren’t that bad. He created three chances, the joint-most of any Liverpool player along with Cody Gakpo, won six of his eight duels, and won possession four times: only Alexis Mac Allister (7), Ronald Araujo (6), and Jérémy Jacquet (6) did so more often for the visitors.
Perhaps we shouldn’t be saying this, being Opta and all, but data doesn’t always tell the whole story.

BD59A84223401E057B114CD7C24530FF.title: Ever-improving Johan Manzambi embodies Aston Villa’s new direction after summer rebuild
BD59A84223401E057B114CD7C24530FF.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesEver-improving Johan Manzambi embodies Aston Villa’s new direction after summer rebuildShareAston Villa’s Swiss winger is improving with every match he plays for his new club as a key member of Unai Emery’s revamped team.

The script writers were never going to let Johan Manzambi leave St James’ Park without making an impact. In another world, the Swiss winger would have joined Newcastle United in the summer. The Magpies chased Manzambi in the belief he would be perfect for the Premier League. They were right about that.

Indeed, Manzambi has hit the ground running in England’s top flight, registering four goal contributions in his last four league outings. Those outings haven’t been for Newcastle, though. Instead, Manzambi is an Aston Villa player and increasingly the embodiment of Unai Emery’s vision for his new-look side.

The summer transfer window could hardly have been any more disruptive for Villa. They lost key players such as Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Emi Martínez and Youri Tielemans to direct rivals as no fewer than six first team figures headed for the exit door. Emery was faced with the biggest rebuild of his Aston Villa career.

In their place, the likes of Nicolas Jackson, Ibrahim Mbaye, João Gomes, Zion Suzuki, Leon Goretzka and Taylor Harwood-Bellis arrived, but it’s Manzambi who has most thoroughly captured the imagination. The 21-year-old is exactly the sort of difference-maker Villa needed in the final third.

Manzambi is averaging more shots per 90 minutes than any other Aston Villa player this season while only Ross Barkley and John McGinn have created more chances. No Villa player has scored more goals or contributed more assists. Manzambi is thriving as an all-round attacking threat.

“He's a good guy, he's very professional, he loves, with passion, football. He wants to play in the way we are and the demand we have,” said Emery after Manzambi’s match-winning performance against Newcastle which saw the Swiss international score the only goal of the game against the team he might have joined instead.

“He decided to join us in summer because he understood here he can progress, he can as well have his own challenges and quality challenges to improving in his career as a player.” Emery’s words accurately reflect how quickly Manzambi has settled in his new surroundings since joining from Freiburg.

While Aston Villa’s summer rebuild might have been more comprehensive than Emery had originally envisaged, it presented an opportunity to retool the squad for the future. In the short term, Villa might fall back from the standard they have set for themselves in recent seasons, but their long term could be brighter for it.

Manzambi is a superstar in the making. He was one of the breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup, shining for a Switzerland side that came within a questionable refereeing decision or two of beating Argentina to reach the semi-finals. Manzambi didn’t begin the tournament as a starting figure, he certainly finished it as one.

Among the likes of Lamine Yamal, Jérémy Doku and Lionel Messi, Manzambi was up there as one of the World Cup’s most prolific dribblers. It was no wonder that several clubs lined up to sign the youngster whose natural ability to beat an opponent is so valuable at the elite level of the game.

Emery’s new-look Villa is a work in progress. Saturday’s away win over Newcastle improved their league standing, but 12th place isn’t where the Villa Park outfit wants to finish this season. With so many new players in the team, though, consistency might be difficult to find, especially with Champions League fixtures congesting the schedule.

Nonetheless, recent performances against Coventry City, Tottenham Hotspur, Fenerbahçe and Newcastle have offered a glimpse of an exciting future. The intensity in Villa’s performances have increased in recent weeks as Emery’s methods have started to take root. The improvement is undeniable.

It’s not just Manzambi who has impressed. Suzuki has settled in so quickly that the Japanese goalkeeper is being talked about as an upgrade on Martínez. Gomes has nailed down a starting spot as Villa’s first-choice number six-and-a-half in central midfield while Mbaye has started to show why he was so highly rated as a teenager at Paris Saint-Germain.

Jackson has also caught the eye of late, scoring four goals in his last four games. The Senegalese striker has a long way to reach the numbers Watkins achieved during his time as Aston Villa’s starting number nine, but Jackson might be an even better fit for Emery’s transition-heavy approach.

In Manzambi, though, Villa boast a talent on an upward trajectory that could take him to the very top. The Swiss winger is exactly the sort of player that could elevate Aston Villa to new heights now that Aston Villa’s early-season struggles are fading. His signing alone could make the summer rebuild worth it.

          Arsenal 2-0 Everton Stats: Konsa and Gabriel Goals Take Champions Level With Man City
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal took advantage of Manchester City's slip-up against Aston Villa, as they beat Everton 2-0 to pull level with the Premier League leaders.
Goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães helped Arsenal to a 2-0 win over Everton, taking them level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

In teeming rain at the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal's centre-backs provided the key moments in front of goal, with Konsa netting for the first time since his arrival from Aston Villa and Gabriel making the points safe midway through the second half.

Everton had their moments in attack, most notably when David Raya won a one-v-one duel with Thierno Barry at 1-0, but Mikel Arteta's side held on to take advantage of City's earlier defeat at Aston Villa.

Arsenal had been uncharacteristically poor from set-pieces at the start of this season, failing to score from a dead ball in 12 matches across all competitions (excluding penalties), but their old strength returned in the seventh minute.
Gabriel's flick-on from a Martin Ødegaard delivery had Jordan Pickford scrambling, and with Vitalii Mykolenko falling to ground at the far post, there was nobody to stop Konsa from prodding home.
Tyrique George curled wide as Everton threatened on the break, though Arsenal also had chances to extend their advantage through Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke.

Everton were almost gifted an equaliser when Ben White's lacklustre header played Barry through, but Raya was equal to his outside-of-the-boot flick, then Mikel Merino nodded over from a Declan Rice free-kick in the final action of the first half.
The start of the second half saw the opportunities dry up at both ends, with Gabriel playing on following an injury scare and Pickford falling on a threatening left-wing centre from Eze.

But Arsenal doubled their advantage when a neat move culminated in White making an overlapping run and crossing to the far post, where Gabriel rose highest to head into the left side of the goal with 68 minutes on the clock.

Everton never really looked likely to cause any late nerves among the home fans, with Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall heading wide from their best chance and eight minutes of stoppage time passing without incident.
Arsenal are still yet to settle on a favoured formula up front this season, with Viktor Gyökeres and Kai Havertz battling it out to start as their striker.
Matters worsened in midweek, too, as key winger Bukayo Saka suffered a quadriceps injury that could keep him out for two months, during the Gunners' 2-2 UEFA Champions League draw with Bayern Munich.

Luckily for Arteta, he has defenders who are very capable of threatening in advanced areas. In Konsa and Gabriel, Arsenal saw two centre-backs score in the same game for the first time since February 2024, when Gabriel and William Saliba netted in a 6-0 rout of West Ham.
Gabriel's goal was his 21st in the Premier League, but his first that has not come from a set-piece.
The Gunners were ultimately good value for their victory, having racked up 20 shots and 1.77 expected goals, compared to Everton's eight attempts and 0.48 xG.
Arteta's side put up 0.79 xG from set-pieces alone, with their physicality proving too much for an Everton side who were without Jarrad Branthwaite due to injury.

paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsCelticScores & FixturesTableScottish FootballO'Neill agrees with McGregor about Celtic issuesImage source, SNSImage caption, Captain Callum McGregor said Celtic's games are a "bit basketball"
Manager Martin O'Neill says he is in "full agreement" with captain Callum McGregor's assessment of Celtic's issues, but insisted they will "sort it out".
McGregor was asked about the team's struggles after Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Dundee United, describing some moments in games as being "a bit basketball" as Celtic lacked their usual control.
The 33-year-old also noted playing strikers like Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran as wingers may be contributing to those issues amid a run of three wins in nine games.

When O'Neill was asked about those comments before Sunday's match with Falkirk, he said he had "no idea" what McGregor said, but when the context was put to the Celtic manager he said he agreed with his captain's diagnosis.
"I totally agree that Callum Osmand is actually really a centre forward, I've said this at the press conference, that he is essentially a centre forward," O'Neill said.
"He probably would play off somebody strong alongside him, I'm not so sure that he could lead the line on his own.
"And that Camilo Duran is really a centre forward, so the players are getting to know each other, it's as really simple as that there, so I'm in total agreement with Callum."
Celtic & Rangers Scottish Cup stadium closure upheld
Published21 hours agoWhat have we learned from first round of Premiership?
Published18 hours agoCeltic still hold a four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership, and will extend that to seven if they beat Falkirk on Sunday, with Rangers in League Cup action.

The defending champions have only lost once, at home to Rangers, in the league but have three Europa League defeats from three amid fan discontent and a boycott of some games by the Green Brigade fans group.

McGregor is not the first senior player to speak about Celtic's lack of control in games, with defender Cameron Carter-Vickers saying after their Glasgow derby loss that the team were "too random" in their play.
O'Neill, though, says the group will improve as more players get up to speed across the course of the winter and in the meantime are doing enough in the league.
"I come in here [to the press conference] every single week and I'm most of the time pretty buoyed by things," the Northern Irishman said.
"Don't try and throw a lot of divides in at the end of the day, we're doing fine.
"A lot of lads here didn't even do pre-season with us. A number of players came in quite late on, so it will take time for us.
"So we need to hang in there, and at this minute I think we're hanging in."

BF45A0588DC67BB46C769FE9FCB649A0.title: Preview: Bayern Munich host Arsenal for a titanic clash
BF45A0588DC67BB46C769FE9FCB649A0.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Bayern Munich host Arsenal for a titanic clashShareAfter Tuesday night’s heavyweight showdown between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, two more of the world’s strongest clubs will face off on Wednesday as Bayern Munich face Arsenal.

Although Bayern Munich have dropped a few points with draws here and there – contributing to their worst Bundesliga start since 2010/11 – they remain a frightening prospect for opponents. They have broken positive records too, such as one for the most goals scored in their first three home league games (an astonishing 18). That accounts for half of their tally across all competitions, meaning they are currently averaging 3.6 goals per game.

Vincent Kompany’s side have been unbeaten at home since their loss to Augsburg in January, winning all but one of their 15 subsequent matches at the Allianz Arena. The outlier was a draw with Heidenheim at the end of last season, an effective dead rubber with the title already lifted.

Arsenal tasted defeat in their last three visits to Munich, twice suffering 5-1 losses. But those were close to a decade ago; Mikel Arteta’s side are a much-changed outfit now. The Gunners have maintained the best defensive record in the English Premier League over the last three seasons, averaging under 0.8 goals conceded per game across them.

Last term’s losing Champions League finalists have won both matches with clean sheets in the new season so far, but are now set to face their toughest test against Bayern Munich’s free-scoring front line.
Bayern Munich will be without two of their key creators, namely the suspended Michael Olise and injured Jamal Musiala. Veteran goalkeeper Manuel Neuer’s status is uncertain due to a foot injury.

On the flip side, Arsenal will miss a couple of defenders. William Saliba has returned to individual training as he continues to recover from his back injury, but is still some way away from returning. Piero Hincapié is the other absentee in the back line, while Christos Tzolis’ unavailability leaves the left wing somewhat depleted.

Former Tottenham striker Harry Kane has been breaking records at a frightening rate in Germany, recently crossing 150 goals for Bayern at an average very close to one per game. For once, someone else stole the spotlight in their last match, as Luis Díaz bagged a hat-trick against Leipzig. The midfield battle will be just as important in this game, so Aleksandar Pavlović will have a big role to play.

On the other side, Declan Rice will hope to dominate proceedings in the middle of the park. Gabriel will have a huge job to do in marshalling the back line, while Bukayo Saka will want to spearhead Arsenal’s attacking threat.
With home advantage on their side, Bayern Munich might just have enough to come away with a victory.

BF54A458404B8EE9C0E7E4B74BA14A4A.title: The MLS Wrap: Griezmann matches Messi in goal-tastic weekend
BF54A458404B8EE9C0E7E4B74BA14A4A.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Griezmann matches Messi in goal-tastic weekendShareLionel Messi lit up MLS once again with two brilliant goals for Inter Miami against Atlanta United, but the performance of another former star of the European leagues arguably eclipsed the Argentine in Matchday 31.
There are only a few weeks of the league season left to go before the playoffs begin, and we are on the verge of crowning the MLS regular season champion for 2026.
There’s also another trophy to play for this week as St. Louis City and Columbus Crew face off to see who will become US national domestic cup champions in the US Open Cup final.
Inter Miami officially secured their place in the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 win over New York City in midweek as Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez assisted goals for Rodrigo De Paul and Germán Berterame.
They followed it up this weekend with a 3-1 win against Atlanta United in Georgia, where Messi bagged a brace, Berterame scored again, and Suárez added a couple more assists to his season stats.

Messi’s magic can sometimes be taken for granted. There is no longer a surprise when looking at an Inter Miami scoreline and seeing his name mentioned multiple times among the list of goals and assists.
😮‍💨💫 Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez, and Germán Berterame were all in the goals as Inter Miami beat Atlanta 1-3 overnight. Messi keeps delivering. 👑 pic.twitter.com/WsPatY2XzK
His goals on Saturday were world-class, as he dribbled past defenders and finished with aplomb.
Though this now seems normal for Messi, it’s worth stepping back now and again to remember how impressive this all is for the 39-year-old who recently retired from international football.

Messi currently tops the charts for both goals and assists in MLS. He’s five ahead of the next most prolific goalscorer, Petar Musa, on 25, and level with Anders Dreyer, Son Heung-min, and Cristian Espinoza, on 12 assists.
MLS’s own stats definitions, which count some secondary assists, have Messi level with Son on 15 assists.
Messi has the highest average FotMob rating in MLS by some distance on 8.32, and also tops the charts for goals per 90, expected goals, shots per 90, expected assists, and xG + xA per 90.
Though Messi topping the table for all these metrics and more is not particularly unexpected, it’s sometimes worth a reminder that it’s still happening and shows no sign of slowing up.
With Messi in the league, even the biggest-name players at other teams can fly under the radar somewhat as the focus regularly lands on Inter Miami alone.
Even in the same state of Florida, there is another player who might normally be a leading light in MLS in other, non-Messi circumstances, playing his part in leading his team to a playoff spot.
Antoine Griezmann scored twice in Orlando City’s 4-1 win at home to DC United, and assisted Martín Ojeda’s outstanding strike. It was a victory that puts them more comfortably in a playoff spot.
😍💫 Perhaps the best goal you will see on your timeline this year. https://t.co/7lxqWLxGEt
Orlando have a very useful pair of wins and a draw from their last three games that could prevent them from being drawn into a tight race for the playoffs come the final games of the season.
Griezmann has 11 goals in his last nine games for Orlando, having joined the team in the summer, not far off Messi’s recent record.
His signing looks set to be one of the more successful acquisitions of an aging European star by an MLS side, and he edges Messi as the player of the round per FotMob’s ratings.

          More Football, Less Timewasting: The New Premier League Rules on Throw-Ins and Goal-Kicks Are Working
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Ithiel Piñero / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
New laws were brought in this summer to try and speed up restarts in games. Have they worked? After five matchdays of the 2026-27 Premier League season, we look at the data to see.
Well fine, maybe not love, but sometimes they can change things for the better.

Football follows trends, and a rather annoying one in more recent years was an apparent increase in timewasting, with players finding new innovative ways of running the clock down, testing the patience of referees and fans alike by trying to either break up the momentum of an opponent, or make sure as little football is played as possible in the pursuit of grinding out a result.

The International Football Association Board (IFAB), the organisation that oversees the laws of the game, decided enough was enough, and used this summer’s World Cup to introduce new directives to try and limit the opportunities players would have to take time out of a game.

That included a five-second rule on both throw-ins and goal-kicks. Not a literal five-second deadline to take them, but from a point where the referee suspects a liberty is being taken, they can start counting down by throwing their hand up in the air like it’s the WWE and Stone Cold Steve Austin is struggling to get back into the ring to avoid being counted out.

There was also a new rule for substitutions, whereby if a player takes longer than 10 seconds to get off the pitch, the player coming on must wait an extra 60 seconds before being allowed to enter the play.

It seemed to have an impact, too. The average time taken on goal-kicks and throw-ins went down, from 27.7 and 15.7 seconds respectively at the 2022 World Cup to 23.7 and 13.2 seconds at the 2026 tournament. The average time of substitution stoppages barely changed, though (from 65.6 seconds in 2022 to 65.5 in 2026).

At the 2026 World Cup, there were four occasions when a goal-kick was turned into a corner after taking too long, while 12 throw-ins were overturned for the same reason. And there was just one instance of a substitute who had to stay off for 60 seconds. So, in the main, the warnings were heeded. Or the laws weren’t being implemented properly.
Either way, the new laws were generally seen as a success, and the Premier League agreed to introduce them from the start of the 2026-27 season.

We are just five matchdays in (50 games played), but with a gigantic international break to navigate, we thought it was a perfect time to see what impact the new rules are having in England’s top flight.

We are yet to see a goal-kick turned into a corner in the Premier League. The closest we’ve come is a goalkeeper holding onto the ball for too long in open play, which also leads to a corner being awarded. That came in the Leeds United vs Crystal Palace game last weekend when referee Adam Herczeg, making his Premier League debut, decided Palace goalkeeper Walter Benítez had held onto the ball for longer than the allotted eight seconds. That rule was introduced last season, though, when it was enforced eight other times.
There has also been just one occasion when a substitute coming on has had to stay off for 60 seconds due to the player coming off taking too long this season, and it was also Crystal Palace.

During their 4-1 home defeat to Manchester City in late August, Anan Khalaili was judged to have taken too much time going off, so Óscar Mingueza was made to wait a full minute to come on. It did seem a bit harsh to issue a punishment intended to stop timewasting to Palace, given they were 3-1 down at the time, but rules are rules.

There have been four instances of a player being punished for taking too long with a throw-in and conceding it back to the opposition: Jorrel Hato for Chelsea against Fulham, Neco Williams for Nottingham Forest against Aston Villa, Riccardo Calafiori for Arsenal against Sunderland, and Olivier Boscagli for Brighton against Arsenal.
That doesn’t seem too bad from 50 games, so are the rules really having an effect on timewasting?

Here at Opta, we have ball-in-play times for the Premier League since the start of the 2015-16 season, and can see exactly how much football has been played, as well as how long various actions are taking on average.
After MD5, the average time the ball has been in play in Premier League games in 2026-27 is 57.7%. That’s the highest since the 2020-21 season (58.0%).

As for the overall ball-in-play clock, we have seen 56 minutes and 35 seconds of in-play action per Premier League game this season, which is the third highest on record (after 2023-24 – 58:11, and 2024-25 – 56:59). It was just 55 mins, 23 seconds last season, so we’re currently getting over a minute more per game.

Interestingly, there does seem to be a knock-on effect in terms of added time. We are getting eight minutes and four seconds of added time per game on average this season, which is the lowest in the Premier League since the 2021-22 campaign (7 mins, 29 secs).
As for the average times to restart play, they seem to be down across the board, suggesting the new rules are indeed having an impact.

          Man Utd 4th, Spurs 12th, Newcastle 20th? Premier League Expected Points Table After Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re five games into the 2026-27 Premier League season. That gives us some data to work with, but it’s still a small enough sample for luck and variance to have played a significant role in the results. So, which teams have been fortunate, and which might feel hard done by?
Is the early-season Premier League table lying to us?

With five wins from five, Manchester City sit top as the only team with a 100% winning record. Opta’s pre-season favourites, Arsenal, are second, three points behind. Brighton and Brentford, who have both made hugely impressive starts, round out the top four.
Tottenham prop up the table, sitting bottom of the league with just two points. Fulham and Coventry City join them in the relegation zone.

In many ways, absolutely. The table is a perfect reflection of how matches have gone so far this season. The aim of the game is to win football matches, and there is no more hard-hitting proof of success than the league table.
In other ways, though, it might be slightly skewed. Some teams might feel they have performed better than their results suggest. For others, the opposite might be true.
This is where Opta’s expected points model can add a little more nuance.

The expected points model simulates the number of goals scored by each side in each match based on the expected goals (xG) value of every shot taken. It then uses those simulated goal totals to determine the outcome of the match, whether that is a win, draw or defeat. Each match is simulated 10,000 times.
The expected points for each team can then be calculated based on the proportion of simulations they win, draw or lose.

We’re aware this is not an exact science. Expected goals data doesn’t account for every factor at play during a football match, including game state and dangerous periods of possession that don’t result in shots. We’re also very much aware that real points matter infinitely more than expected ones.
Nevertheless, the expected points table can give us some interesting additional context on what we have seen across the opening five matchdays.
The first major talking point is that Arsenal sit top of the expected points table.

They remain favourites to win the title according to the Opta supercomputer, and their underlying numbers are still strong. They have the highest expected goals difference (+4.44) of any side in the Premier League.

Man City are second according to the expected points model. They have made a hugely impressive start under new manager Enzo Maresca, but the model suggests they have collected 5.8 more points than the underlying data from the chances they have created and conceded would normally warrant.

Sunderland generated 3.57 expected goals against them on MD5, the third-highest figure ever recorded (since 2013-14) by a losing team in a Premier League game, while the chances in City’s game against Manchester United (won 1-0) were essentially even.

There is important context to add here, though. City have spent a greater proportion of their game time leading (52.5%) than any other Premier League side this season. That means they have had less need to chase matches and push numbers forward, which could naturally reduce their overall xG output.

That’s something we need to bear in mind when analysing the expected points table, and one of the model’s limitations. A team protecting a lead doesn’t necessarily need to generate chances at the same rate as one searching for a goal.
So, which teams might feel they should be higher up the league?

Michael Carrick has come in for plenty of criticism following Manchester United’s poor start to the season. United have taken just five points from their opening five league games, their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign alongside 2014-15.

Their underlying numbers, however, are far more encouraging. United lead the Premier League for total shots (113) and touches in the opposition box (182). Their total xG of 9.89 is the fourth-highest in the division.

          Arsenal Ease Pressure, Chelsea Take Top Spot, and Man City’s Perfect WSL Start Ends: Five Talking Points From Matchday 7
        
      
                          
                      Oct 26, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The WSL title race took an intriguing turn as Chelsea capitalised on Man City’s dropped points, Arsenal found much-needed respite with a derby-day triumph over Tottenham, Aston Villa continued their upward trajectory, and Liverpool denied London City Lionesses another victory.
Matchday 7 brought another significant shift in the WSL landscape, with plenty of talking points across the division.

Arsenal finally ended their frustrating wait for a league victory, overcoming Tottenham in the north London derby to claim their first win since the opening day and ease some of the pressure on their faltering campaign.
Elsewhere, Manchester City’s perfect start was ended by cross-city rivals Manchester United, allowing Chelsea to move top of the table for the first time this season.

Sonia Bompastor’s side, however, had to work harder than expected to take advantage, coming from behind at half-time to beat Crystal Palace. It marked the first time under the French manager that Chelsea had overturned a half-time deficit against an opponent outside the traditional elite (Arsenal, Man City and Man Utd).

Aston Villa, meanwhile, secured consecutive league victories for the first time since the end of the 2024-25 season, while Liverpool fought back to earn a point against London City Lionesses, bringing their opponents’ record-breaking winning streak to an end.
Here are our biggest takeaways from the latest round of action.
Chelsea are top of the WSL for the first time this season after surviving a stern examination from Crystal Palace and producing a late turnaround to claim all three points.
The Blues’ French contingent proved decisive, with Melvine Malard at the heart of the comeback. However, the result was far from straightforward.

Molly Bartrip’s opener was a landmark moment for the Eagles, representing the first goal Crystal Palace have ever scored against Chelsea. It also placed the Blues in an unfamiliar position: trailing at half-time against a promoted side.

Chelsea had conceded the opening goal to a promoted team on only four previous occasions in WSL history, with the most recent instance coming in May 2023, when Liverpool took the lead before Chelsea recovered to win 2-1.

Palace, however, will be disappointed by their inability to maintain their advantage. They have now conceded six goals in the final 15 minutes of WSL matches this season, the highest total in the division.
Malard was the standout performer as she recorded five shots on target, equalling the highest individual tally in a WSL match this season alongside Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw.

Her opening goal was particularly spectacular, marking only the third time she has scored from outside the box in the WSL and her first such effort since the beginning of last season, when she found the net against Leicester City.

The French striker was a constant presence in dangerous areas, recording more touches inside the opposition penalty area than any other player over the weekend (15). She also accumulated 1.7 xG, the highest total of her WSL career. Despite her impressive performance, the French forward may feel she could have added further goals to her tally.

The comeback was also shaped by the quality of Chelsea’s wide play. Katie McCabe recorded 34 successful passes ending in the final third, more than any other player across the weekend, illustrating her influence in sustaining pressure around Palace’s defensive block.

Sandy Baltimore proved effective from the bench, embarking on an incisive run and delivering the ball into a dangerous area for Malard's second, while her penalty sealed a 3-1 away victory for Bompastor's side.
Malard's brace made her only the second French international in Chelsea’s history to score more than once in a WSL match, following Baltimore’s achievement in January earlier this year.
The result was a significant one for Chelsea, who have now capitalised on Manchester City dropping points to move to the top of the table.

Arsenal delivered a much-needed result, coming from behind to defeat Tottenham 2-1 in the north London derby and ending their five-match winless run in the WSL. The victory marked the first time the Gunners had overturned a deficit to win a league match since September 2025, when they defeated West Ham 5-1.

          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 7
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Looking for an under-the-radar pick in Fantasy Premier League? The 10% Club has you covered for FPL Gameweek 7.
Tempted by a triple Chelsea attack; considering moving away from double Arsenal defence; or still expecting Brighton’s run of form to end?
Those may be just a few of many questions floating through the minds of Fantasy Premier League managers as Gameweek 7 approaches. But, as always, we’re to help.
Using Opta data, we’ve picked out five under-the-radar stars – all owned by fewer than 10% of managers – to help go against the FPL template this weekend.
Tottenham may be winless this campaign, but an improved performance in their draw away to Manchester United may give Roberto De Zerbi hope.

Coventry are their next visitors, and although Frank Lampard’s side backed up their first win over Nottingham Forest with a 4-1 thrashing of Newcastle United, De Zerbi will clearly see this as a good opportunity to get Spurs on track.
A lack of attacking options, with Spurs scoring just three goals so far, pushes us towards looking at their defence, where Jan Paul van Hecke continues to shine.
The Dutch defender’s 27 points are the most of any Tottenham player. He's registered DEFCON returns twice in 2026-27 and also scored in his last home outing in GW5.
Van Hecke also seems to be Spurs’ set-piece target. His 1.1 expected goal involvements are only bettered by Dominic Solanke (1.3) and Sávio (1.5) among all of De Zerbi’s squad in the competition.
Although Van Hecke travels to free-scoring Chelsea next weekend, a favourable run then sees Spurs face Palace, Ipswich Town and Fulham in their next three home games.
Not many sides have a better upcoming swing of fixtures before the November international break, and if De Zerbi can get Spurs firing, Van Hecke’s 6.3% ownership will only soar.
Brighton duo Pascal Groẞ and Maxim De Cuyper continue to lead the way, with their 53 points each the most of any player this season.
Bart Verbruggen is another to impress, with the third-most points of all goalkeepers (32). But the Brighton trio are all in more than 10% of squads ahead their home fixture with Crystal Palace.

However, Luka Vuskovic continues to go under the radar. His 40 points put him fifth on the list of all defenders, and three of the four above him (Joško Gvardiol, James Tarkowski and De Cuyper) are all owned by a significant proportion of managers.

The Croatian defender has hit the threshold for defensive contributions in 50% of his matches. However, those DEFCON returns could easily have increased if Coventry City and Aston Villa hadn’t received red cards to dampen their attacking threat.
Vuskovic has also picked up a clean sheet in four of six league outings, while he scored against Leeds United for a mega 12-point haul on GW3.

His attacking threat, largely from set-pieces, shouldn’t be a surprise. Only Alejandro Grimaldo, who scored eight times as Bayer Leverkusen’s attacking full-back, could better Vuskovic’s six Bundesliga goals among all defenders last season.

Despite tough upcoming trips to Liverpool and Manchester City, those visits only heighten Vuskovic’s DEFCON appeal. Plus, a clean sheet isn’t completely off the cards considering Brighton’s 3-0 dismantling of Arsenal on GW5.
Despite waiting until GW5 for his first start, only Emiliano Buendía (25) and John McGinn (27) have more points than Johan Manzambi’s 19 for Aston Villa.

The Switzerland international has two assists and one goal in his first two Premier League starts, racking up 13 points against Tottenham before adding five more against Brentford with his assist for McGinn.

C1899563BC4357EB7E3C338814B09A22.title: Preview: Manchester City host Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain
C1899563BC4357EB7E3C338814B09A22.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Manchester City host Champions League holders Paris Saint-GermainShareManchester City’s first home match after the guilty verdict sees them face fellow sovereign wealth fund-owned Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.

Manchester City have remained absolutely defiant throughout the investigation into their alleged financial breaches, and that does not appear to be changing after the guilty verdict. While everyone awaits the completion of the appeal process, the club’s internal approach seems to be to create an us-against-the-world mentality. They have openly acted this way throughout the process, and certainly showed it quite clearly in their post-match reaction to the win over Liverpool.

For other teams and fans alike, though, this creates a rather jarring situation. Particularly in the Premier League, no one is quite sure as to how meaningful Manchester City’s games are this season, and therefore can’t fully react to the on-pitch result. The Champions League is a slightly different beast since the current investigation falls outside UEFA’s jurisdiction, though any domestic sanctions could well affect City’s future qualification to the premier European competition as well.

Things are looking a lot rosier for Qatar Sports Investments’ Paris Saint-Germain project, even if their start to the season has not been up to the mark. In the bigger picture, they will be delighted to have captured consecutive Champions League titles after ‘the big one' eluded them for so long. In the process, they have become accustomed to such slower starts before kicking into gear around the turn of the year.

Luis Enrique’s side did win their Champions League opener 6-1, but their domestic form hasn’t been quite so scintillating. They failed to win their first three matches of the Ligue 1 season and are yet to put together a statement performance. The Ligue 1 holders only narrowly defeated Brest and Marseille in recent weeks, and allowed newly-promoted Le Mans back into the game before overcoming them last weekend.
The only expected absentee across both camps is Senny Mayulu, who is out with a short-term thigh injury. Both head coaches otherwise have full-strength squads to pick from.

Erling Haaland remains on fire for Manchester City. He has found the back of the net in each of his last six appearances for them, taking his season tally to eight goals. The Norwegian international also scored three times in four games for his national team over the last couple of weeks.

In support of him, Antoine Semenyo will have an important job to do going both ways on the wing. At the back, former PSG shot-stopper Gianluigi Donnarumma could well be called into action by the French champions’ star-studded attack.

Speaking of PSG’s front line, the dynamic Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will definitely be one to watch. Summer signing Ferrán Torres has slotted in well, notably netting a hat-trick in the previous Champions League round. On the right, Achraf Hakimi will have a role to play in defence and attack.

While this is a heavyweight clash, the nature of the Champions League’s Swiss model format means that it does not have a particularly great deal riding on it. So, the two teams may produce a relatively open score draw.

C2BBC49B52ACC8F11A366C7CBDC963F4.title: Preview: Brentford host Liverpool with just a point separating the two teams
C2BBC49B52ACC8F11A366C7CBDC963F4.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Brentford host Liverpool with just a point separating the two teamsShareThis weekend will tell us a lot about Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool side as the Reds travel to Brentford on Saturday afternoon to take on the fourth placed Bees.
Keith Andrews’ side are one of three unbeaten teams in the Premier League, winning two and drawing four of their six outings so far. They’re averaging two goals per game and conceding just one.
At home, they’ve been impressive, winning two and drawing one. They racked up 3-0 wins over both Chelsea and Spurs in victories that made people take notice of Brentford.

Only Brighton, Chelsea and Manchester City have scored more than Brentford’s 12 goals. The Bees are spreading the goals about too with nine different scorers already this term. Incredibly, last season’s top scorer, Igor Thiago, has just one goal to his name this time around but it does highlight how dangerous they are as a collective that he’s firing blanks and yet they’re still scoring goals as a team.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are finding goals hard to come by in the Premier League. They blanked last time out in a 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield, their first defeat of the season. It means they’ve scored just seven in their opening six matches. They’ve also conceded seven.

Andoni Iraola’s men either keep a clean sheet or they concede a minimum of two. That seems to be the pattern this season. If Brentford find the back of the net on Saturday, expect them to not stop at one.

The Reds did bounce back following the loss last Sunday, racking up a 6-3 win over LASK in mid-week. Bradley Barcola netted a hat-trick and the attack seemed to click, albeit against inferior opposition. However, the confidence gained from that game might play a part in the outcome on Saturday.
Interestingly, despite being far from convincing, Liverpool have the second best away record in the English top-flight with seven points from nine. Only leaders Man City (nine) have taken more.

For Liverpool, the focus will be on Barcola after his hat-trick in the Champions League. The Reds need him to show that sort of form in the Premier League and if he manages to impress against Brentford, he’ll have done a good job and the likelihood is the away side will have picked up maximum points.

For the hosts, with top scorer Kevin Schade ruled out, all eyes will be on Thiago. He netted against this opposition last season and he’s always a handful, even for physically robust defenders like Virgil van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet.
Both sides have injury issues. Brentford are without Nathan Collins, Mikel Damsgaard and Schade. They’re key players in their respective positions.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are missing Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley while Ryan Gravenberch is suspended following his red card against Manchester City. There is some positive news though with Dominik Szoboszlai, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak all potentially returning after missing the last two.
We’re going with an entertaining 2-2 draw and for Brentford's unbeaten start to continue.

C3119566CEEEB64743E2203626E7378D.title: The FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 7’s Best XI featuring Haaland, Neto, and Wirtz
C3119566CEEEB64743E2203626E7378D.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 7’s Best XI featuring Haaland, Neto, and WirtzShareMatchday 7 of the Premier League is in the books and Manchester City maintained their 100% record thanks to a 3-2 win over Ipswich.
Arsenal remain hot on their heels thanks to a win over Nottingham Forest, while Sunderland prop up the table following another damaging defeat.
Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki kept his second clean sheet in the space of four days – and third overall this season – in the victory against Newcastle.

The Japanese international may have made only one save during the game, but he also succeeded with 100% of his total duels contested and took 65 touches, indicating how comfortable he was with the ball at his feet.
Castagne was impressive in Fulham’s 1-0 win over Hull and he deserves his spot at right-back in the Team of the Week (TOTW).
The defender had the most touches out of anyone on the pitch (123), completed the most dribbles (4) and covered the most distance (12.4km) throughout the game.
His performance contributed to a second clean sheet of the season for the Cottagers.
Bournemouth sealed their first league win under Marco Rose and James Hill played a massive part in that.
The defender made nine defensive contributions during the game, including seven clearances, and two tackles.
He demonstrated his strength in one-on-one battles, winning 100% of his ground duels and 88% of his aerial duels contested during the game, as he makes the TOTW for the first time this term.
Luka Vušković could turn out to be one of the signings of the season for Brighton. The defender took the most touches of anyone (103) as he aimed to build attacks from the back.
Indeed, he made six passes into the final third, created one chance and registered three shots. Not bad going for a centre-back.
Defensively, Vuskovic recorded three interceptions, seven clearances and six recoveries, and we expect him to remain a familiar face in our TOTW going forward this season.

Vušković is joined in the team by Olivier Boscagli, as the French defender notched his first assist of the season during the 5-0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace at the weekend in what was a standout showing at left-back.
He created three chances, made 14 passes into the final third and registered six defensive contributions in total as Brighton made it five wins from seven league games this season.
His 8.3 match rating was the best across the back four in the TOTW for matchday seven.

Chelsea sealed a solid win over Everton as Pedro Neto netted both goals during the game. Surprisingly, this was the first time he had scored a brace in a Premier League match and it couldn’t have come at a better time.
The winger was a livewire throughout the game, recording the most touches (5) in the opposition box than anyone else, while also creating the most chances (5) in the 90 minutes.

Not just content with being a nuisance in the final third, Neto even recorded nine defensive contributions, which included five recoveries, to help his side when they didn’t have the ball. As such, Neto is the star man this week with a match rating of 9.3.
Much has been said about Florian Wirtz’s performances for Liverpool, but he was impressive in the win over Brentford.

          Is Lisandro Martínez Right to ‘Expect More’ From Manchester United?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez reacted to defeat at Atlético Madrid by complaining about a lack of investment by the club.
We’re not even halfway through October, and frustration has already boiled over at Manchester United.

Following Tuesday night’s Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid, United are now without a win in five games in all competitions. It’s their longest run since a six-game streak in January 2025 (D2 L4), and pressure is mounting on manager Michael Carrick.

This defeat in the Spanish capital was no major disaster on its own. Losing away to a very good team like Atlético, who have more home Champions League wins since the start of 2023-24 (15) than any other team apart from Arsenal and Bayern Munich (16 each), is no reason for a full-blown crisis, especially given United also had to play with 10 men for the last part of the game after Leny Yoro was given a very harsh red card.

Yes, United aren’t on a great run and this loss added to concern about Carrick’s suitability for the manager’s job in the long-term, but this game could have been glossed over. There were enough positives from the performance in a tough environment with several players missing through injury that, of all the mishaps this season, this wasn’t the one to throw the club into crisis. United created four Opta-defined ‘big chances’ – opportunities you’d reasonably expect them to convert – but failed to score. Atléti had just two but won 2-0.

But Lisandro Martínez’s post-match interview ensured attention would not quickly turn to Leeds away on Sunday. The Argentine centre-back used his chance in front of the media as an opportunity to complain about the lack of investment in the United playing squad.
Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 pic.twitter.com/OGo25Pzd30

“I have to control myself a lot,” he said. “But sometimes it is the reflection, the mirror, for our club at the moment. A fantastic season last season, but now we are far from the top. We have to bring in more players to compete. Look at Atlético, they had an amazing team, they deserved to win.
“I expect more, from everyone. More investment? Yes, 100%. I expect more from our technical director, I have to be honest.”

His outburst was always going to divide opinion. For some, it felt rich for the Argentine to be complaining about a lack of signings given he had just started a Champions League game behind an entirely new £155 million midfield of Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. The summer before, United spent big on a new-look forward line of Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko.

It may also have been hard for some to hear these words coming from Martínez, who has made an inconsistent start to the season, highlighted most starkly and most recently by how easily he was beaten by Dominic Solanke for 10-man Tottenham’s injury-time equaliser at Old Trafford at the weekend.

But it certainly struck a chord with many United fans who believe more work needed to be done to improve the squad after qualification for the Champions League when United played a grand total of just 40 games in 2025-26. “Last season we created a base to build an amazing team,” Martínez said.

While United did buy a few players this summer, they also tried and failed to sign all of Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali, Matheus Fernandes, Alex Scott, Aurélien Tchouaméni and Lewis Hall. They weren’t at all decisive in the transfer market.

The most glaring issue is surely in defence, though, which may have been precisely where Martínez’s frustrations lie. The most obvious of the problems is at left-back, where after early-season injuries to Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu, who can fill in in defence, United were left with 20-year-old centre-back Ayden Heaven for the trip to Atlético. It was his first ever senior start at left-back in his first ever Champions League appearance.

Shaw was fit for the whole of last season but his injury record made it impossible that he would be able to contend with the demands of midweek European fixtures. That was obvious to just about everyone apart from, seemingly, the United hierarchy in the summer, and they failed to act.

It is especially galling given rivals at the top of the table just would not neglect a problem position in this way. For example, Arsenal spent £50m on Ezri Konsa after seeing William Saliba suffer an injury that would keep him out of the first part of the season even though they already had Cristhian Mosquera as back-up.

Perhaps United weren’t in a financial position to sign anyone else, but that would be surprising given the extra money brought in by qualification for the Champions League. United’s net spend in the summer was lower than any of Ipswich, Spurs, Hull and Coventry, and was only just above that of Brentford.

The club may have concluded there was nobody available on the market who was worth spending on to reinforce at left-back, but not signing anyone at all was surely not the correct approach. Everyone else could see that some kind of reinforcement was needed.
The final option may be that they simply could not attract anyone, but if that is true for a club the size of United, then something major is going wrong at the top.

At right-back and in central defence, meanwhile, it’s arguable that United could have done with at least one more player. For a team playing in four competitions this season, they are not blessed with a great deal of depth anywhere, but most strikingly in defence.

C583B2BF7EDE971FDC2C60CB736EB8A7.title: Preview: Barcelona aiming to make it 8 wins from 8 against Getafe
C583B2BF7EDE971FDC2C60CB736EB8A7.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Barcelona aiming to make it 8 wins from 8 against GetafeShareBarcelona will be looking to continue their perfect record in LaLiga this weekend as they host Getafe.

The Barcelona supporters can’t have asked for much more from Hansi Flick’s side sit top of the LaLiga table with seven wins from seven. They’ve scored a whopping 31 goals, averaging over four per game.

Despite a reasonable start to the season, Getafe will be heading into this game with plenty of dread. Not only are they facing a Barcelona side in red-hot form, they are also winless in their previous eight trips to the Spotify Camp Nou.
Getafe’s last trip to Barcelona saw them suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Flick’s men incredibly comfortable that day.

Barcelona have suffered a crucial blow heading into this game, with Raphinha ruled out. The Brazilian forward picked up a thigh injury during the international break, and Flick has confirmed he’s unavailable.
Frenkie de Jong, Rooney Bardghji, and Andreas Christensen will also be missing for Barcelona.
Getafe have some injury problems of their own, with Christantus Uche and Juanmi unavailable once again. Abdel Aqbar and Kiko Femenía could also miss out.

Raphinha has been deployed in a relatively new position so far this season, with Flick opting to play the former Leeds man as a central striker. It’s a decision that has certainly paid dividends, with Raphinha scoring 12 league goals while providing three assists.

Raphinha’s injury could see Gabriel Jesus come into the side in the centre-forward position, but it wouldn’t be a surprise if Flick had another trick up his sleeve. Anthony Gordon has played as a striker at times during his career, while Karim Adeyemi has also been a regular up front in the past.

Getafe are well-known for their defensive solidity, often having one of the best defensive records in LaLiga under José Bordalás. This season, they’ve conceded just seven times, with three of those coming on the opening day of the campaign.

Going forward is where Getafe really struggle. No side has created fewer expected goals (4.8) this season, with Getafe bottom of that metric by some distance. Bordalás’ side have found the back of the net just four times, and that lack of creativity must improve against a team like Barcelona.

The injury to Raphinha is likely to open up an opportunity for Jesus to prove himself to Flick. The Brazilian has had minimal chances so far this season, due to the form of Raphinha, but he’s been a threat in front of goal during his minimal amount of minutes.

The former Arsenal man has played just four times for Barcelona this season, playing a total of 41 minutes. Despite the lack of game time, he’s found the back of the net twice, and he could now be in line for his first start.
Getafe are going to struggle to score, and that’s something Barcelona certainly know how to do: Barça 4-0 Getafe.
