C64CCAB51ABB6F08686AF689D0940E06.title: Preview: Unbeaten Manchester City host Ipswich in the Premier League
C64CCAB51ABB6F08686AF689D0940E06.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Unbeaten Manchester City host Ipswich in the Premier LeagueShareManchester City take on Ipswich Town in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon as they look to make it seven wins from seven.
Ipswich, however, are exceeding expectations thus far, occupying tenth in the league table after six matches.
Up until the clash against two-time defending Champions League winners PSG on Wednesday evening, City had won eight consecutive matches in all competitions.

Taking three points off PSG was always going to be a tough ask, despite this strong start and Luis Enrique’s men proved why they are the best team in Europe. Indeed, the French giants raced into a 3-0 lead after just 30 minutes and the game eventually finished 4-2.
The defeat isn’t the end of the world for Enzo Maresca, with thoughts now turning to the Premier League clash against the Tractor Boys.
City won both matches against Ipswich during the 2024/25 campaign by an aggregate score of 10-1, but this tie could be tighter.

Maresca will be counting on Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki to provide the cutting edge at the Etihad. The duo have scored ten and five goals respectively this season, with the performances by Cherki particularly impressive.
The Frenchman has six goal contributions across six league matches and has found the net in back-to-back matches. Keep an eye out for him this weekend.
Gary O’Neil might not have been the most glamourous option to lead Ipswich into the Premier League season, but he knows how to keep a club in the top flight.

Two wins from their opening four games was more than respectable, especially as the defeats against Man United and Liverpool were expected. The victory against Fulham last time out proves that the Tractor Boys have what it takes to avoid relegation this term.

Despite going behind early in the second half, O’Neil’s men didn’t panic. Right-back Abdoul Ouattara netted the equaliser in the 88th minute, before Dara O’Shea headed home the winner with just seconds left.
That result leaves Ipswich tenth in the table with nine points and while no one expects the club to take anything from the Etihad, they might well cause a surprise.
Watch out for Emersonn. The Brazilian has scored twice in the league this term and he could be a real handful for the City backline.
Man City have no new injuries concerns ahead of this clash, giving Maresca plenty of room to mix things up after the PSG defeat in midweek.
O’Neil looks set to welcome back Abdul Fatawu following his suspension and he could start on the right wing against City.
Elsewhere, the manager has a full strength squad to choose from this weekend.
Maresca will still be hurting after the loss to PSG, which could spur his side on this weekend against Ipswich.

With a full squad to choose from, the Italian might be tempted to rotate and this could see the likes of Iliman Ndiaye and Ayyoub Bouaddi coming in to the starting XI. Extra motivation may stem from the fact that should City win, Maresca will become the first manager in the Premier League era to win his first seven league games in charge of a new club.
It is hard to see Ipswich taking anything against a City side with that much strength in depth. Given their recent displays, however, they could spring a shock or two: Man City 3-1 Ipswich Town.

          Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal Stats: Mac Allister, Ngumoha Star in Another Anfield Comeback
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      Oliver King / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Andoni Iraola's men may have defended poorly, but they clinched an exciting win in the Champions League. Look back on a thriller with our Liverpool vs Villarreal stats page.
Liverpool came from two goals down to produce another memorable Champions League comeback at Anfield as they beat Villarreal 4-3 to keep their perfect record intact.
Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona had put Villarreal in a strong position by the 29th minute, but Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo levelled things before the break.
Mac Allister scored his second after being teed up by the impressive Rio Ngumoha, with Florian Wirtz netting a confidence-boosting goal before Tani Oluwaseyi's late consolation.

Andoni Iraola made six changes to the side that beat nine-man Brentford, though it was one of their most dependable players who gifted Villarreal a shock fourth-minute lead, with Virgil van Dijk's wayward header back to Alisson pinched by Mikautadze, who tucked home from a tight angle.

Villarreal doubled their lead with relative ease just before the half-hour mark, when Nathan Saliba's pass carved open the hosts' defence, allowing Cardona to race through and slot into the bottom-left corner.
However, Liverpool hit back quickly through Mac Allister, who glanced Kostas Tsimikas' in-swinging corner home, with the Argentine then firing inches wide moments later.

And on the stroke of half-time, Liverpool were level. Ngumoha whipped a teasing ball into the penalty area that Cardona let run, and Araújo steamed in at the back post to nod past former Reds goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi.
Liverpool maintained their momentum early in the second half with Cody Gakpo and Wirtz testing Gulacsi before Trey Nyoni's arrowed drive whistled past the right post.

The comeback was complete just after the hour. Ngumoha again terrorised the Villarreal defence, this time providing a pinpoint low cross for Mac Allister to sweep home his second and Liverpool's third off the crossbar.
Wirtz, who had yet to score for Liverpool this season, continued his good recent form with a left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner in the 68th minute.
Villarreal threatened a nervy finish when Oluwaseyi tucked in from Ayoze Perez's delivery , but the Reds held on to make it three wins from three in Europe this season.

Ahead of kick-off, Iraola emphasised the importance of building a winning feeling at Anfield, having failed to win at home in the Premier League since taking charge of the Reds, and he would have been fearing the worst when his side found themselves two down early on.

Indeed, Cardona's goal, timed at 28:08, was the earliest Liverpool have been two goals down in a major European competition since April 2016 against Borussia Dortmund in the Europa League (08:20). However, this is Anfield in the Champions League.

Every time Liverpool have gone 2-0 down this early in a major home European match, they have come back to win – April 1976 vs Club Brugge (12th minute, won 3-2), October 1996 vs Sion (23rd minute, won 6-3) and April 2016 vs Dortmund (ninth minute, won 4-3) – and that trend continued here.

Two players in Mac Allister and Ngumoha took the game by the scruff of the neck, with the latter, at 18 years and 52 days old, becoming the third-youngest player to provide multiple assists in a Champions League game after Warren Zaïre-Emery against AC Milan (17y 231d) and Theo Walcott against Hamburg (17y 250d).

Ngumoha also completed seven of his eight dribbles, while Mac Allister popped up with two big goals. All eight of his strikes in the Champions League have come at Anfield, including one already this season against Atlético Madrid on MD1.

Liverpool were ultimately worthy winners here, finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.37 from their 22 shots to Villarreal's 1.58 from 14 attempts. Iraola will, however, feel there is plenty to work on ahead of this weekend's clash with in-form Brighton in the Premier League.

C809A51B41B1E87C0673DB0621C45BFB.title: Preview: The Mourinho Reunion Tour takes Madrid to Roma
C809A51B41B1E87C0673DB0621C45BFB.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: The Mourinho Reunion Tour takes Madrid to RomaShareRoma and Real Madrid go head-to-head in the Champions League, as José Mourinho returns to his former club for the first time.

Mourinho departed Roma back in January 2024 after he was sacked, with the Italian side sitting in ninth position in the Serie A table. The experienced manager was seen in tears as he left the Roma training ground just over 18 months ago, and it will be a special evening for him as he returns.
It’s business as usual, though, for Real Madrid, as they focus on securing their second victory of the Champions League league phase stage.
The last time these two sides met in this competition was back in 2018, when Real Madrid secured a 2-0 win thanks to goals from Gareth Bale and Lucas Vázquez.

Bryan Cristante will be pushing for a return to the squad following a knee injury, but there’s no guarantee he’s fit enough to face Madrid. Roma will be without Mile Svilar between the sticks, which is a crucial blow for the Italian side.

Once again, Real Madrid are without Éder Militão, Ferland Mendy, Rodrygo, and Raúl Asencio. Dean Huijsen will be available following his domestic suspension, but it remains to be seen whether he will start.

It’s been a bright start to the Serie A season for Roma, who sit in third position in the table after six games. They are yet to lose in the league, winning four times while drawing twice. They started in phenomenal fashion, winning four on the bounce, but they’ve drawn their last two league games – against champions Inter, and Como.

Roma have been one of the strongest defensive sides in Italy so far this season, and they’ll need that to continue against Madrid’s deadly attack. In their opening Champions League fixture, they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fenerbahce.

It’s no secret that Real Madrid have one of the best attacks in Europe. There are arguments to suggest it still hasn’t quite fully clicked for Mourinho’s side, but there is undoubtedly a ridiculous amount of quality in their forward line.
Unsurprisingly, Barcelona are the only side to have created more expected goals than Real Madrid this season, though Mourinho’s men have produced a whopping 19.9 in just eight matches.
It’s going to be an interesting encounter against a strong defensive side in Roma.

It’s been a slow start to the season for Yan Diomande since his move to Madrid from RB Leipzig. The tricky winger hasn’t been a guaranteed starter under Mourinho this season, but he was given an opportunity to impress against Villarreal.

The 19-year-old created three chances and scored Madrid’s only goal in a 1-0 victory last time out. He’ll be looking to impress once again, and Mourinho must be tempted to give him another start in the Champions League.
We’re expecting a tight game, but Madrid will edge it. 2-1 to the Spanish side.

          How Long Has Your Premier League Team Been Leading, Level or Losing in 2026-27?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Which teams have held a winning position the longest in the Premier League this season, and which have spent the most time trailing? We look at every team’s time in each game state after five matchdays of 2026-27.
Manchester City have started the 2026-27 campaign with five wins from five and are the only team with a 100% record in the competition.

Therefore, it’s hardly a shock to see Enzo Maresca’s side lead the rankings for proportion of game time spent in a winning position.City are the only side to have been winning for over half (52%) of match minutes this season, but their opening game of the campaign at home to Bournemouth was a different story.
Trailing after a 27th-minute goal from Marcus Tavernier, City worked their way back into the game with an 84th-minute Marc Guéhi strike, before Josko Gvardiol won the game in added time.

That match saw them hold the lead for only four minutes and 52 seconds. The 60 minutes and 52 seconds that they were behind is the longest by any team that’s gone on and won a match in the Premier League this season.

City led the Premier League ranking for proportion of game time spent in a winning position across last season too (48.6%), but that was irrelevant in the end. Arsenal, who spent 44.5% of match time winning, ended up with the league title, finishing seven points clear of their rivals.

Bournemouth are yet to win a match in the Premier League this season but they have only been in a losing position for 9.3% of game time – the third lowest proportion. They have, however, lost a league-high nine points from winning positions, which might explain their winless run under new boss Marco Rose.

In three games so far, the Cherries have held a lead for more than 50 minutes before eventually failing to pick up all three points: Man City on MD1 (60:52), Everton on MD2 (52:29) and Newcastle on MD3 (82:11).
Arguably the most eye-catching number after five matchdays of this season is Brentford’s time spent in a losing position.
Keith Andrews’ side have been losing for just three minutes and 10 seconds of match action this season – that coming in the 2-2 away draw with Bournemouth on 12 September.
That means that they have been losing for just 0.6% of Premier League game time this season (rounded up to 1% in the viz above), which is substantially lower than the next lowest: Leeds on 8.6%.
At the other end of the spectrum, it’s been a miserable start to the season for Tottenham, who sit bottom of the Premier League table as we reach the extended international break.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team failed to score in their first four league games of 2026-27, and when they did finally find the net in the MD5 defeat to Aston Villa through Conor Gallagher in the 86th minute, they were already 3-0 down. That means that they haven’t led for a single second of Premier League action this season – the only team yet to do so.

Sunderland have only been in a winning position for 3.9% of their match time this season. That all came in the final 19 minutes and 24 seconds of their game against Fulham on MD2 after Wilson Isidor’s strike decided a tight game at the Stadium of Light.

CADC1A9AF1D12DBC834BBF7BB0F33D93.title: Ronald Araujo is giving Liverpool exactly what they need as a different sort of right back
CADC1A9AF1D12DBC834BBF7BB0F33D93.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesRonald Araujo is giving Liverpool exactly what they need as a different sort of right backShareAndoni Iraola probably didn’t plan on using Ronald Araújo as his starting right back this season.

Partly because the Uruguayan didn’t join Liverpool until mid-August, supposedly as a central defensive option with the Reds so short of depth at the back. Also partly because Iraola already had Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong in his squad to utilise.

Now, though, that the pieces are starting to settle into place and Iraola is getting closer to gaining a true understanding of his team, Araújo is considered Liverpool’s first choice at right back. It would be a shock if anyone other than the 27-year-old started in that position against Manchester City this weekend.

Araujo started five matches in a row for Liverpool before the current international window. The Reds won four of those five matches with Iraola’s side starting to show signs of improvement. Araújo has been key to that improvement even if he is a different sort of right back to the kind fans at Anfield have been used to.

Liverpool’s issues at right back can be linked to Trent Alexander-Arnold’s departure in the summer of 2025. So much of the Reds’ creative play flowed through the England international and so his exit left a void in the Liverpool lineup that proved difficult to fill no matter what Arne Slot tried.

Jeremie Frimpong arrived from Bayer Leverkusen, seemingly as a direct replacement for Alexander-Arnold. However, the Dutchman’s game could hardly be more different to that of his predecessor in that Frimpong offers vertical threat. Alexander-Arnold, on the other hand, was someone whose ability on the ball opened up different angles in the final third.

At Leverkusen, Frimpong thrived as a right wing back. Xabi Alonso gave the Dutchman the freedom to get forward without any defensive burden. At Liverpool, though, Frimpong was used as an orthodox right back in a back four and it exposed his lack of defensive nous. The Reds were left exposed too many times.

Bradley demonstrated promise as Alexander-Arnold’s deputy, but struggled for form and fitness when asked to step up as Liverpool’s first-choice right back. Still only 23, the Northern Irishman clearly has potential. As a reliable starting figure at this moment, though, Liverpool clearly needed better.

Joe Gomez and even Dominik Szoboszlai were played at right back by Slot over the course of last season, highlighting the scale of Liverpool’s plight in that position. This was the desperate situation Iraola inherited upon arriving at Merseyside from Bournemouth this summer.

Araújo is a purer defender than Liverpool’s options at right back. The Uruguayan broke through as a centre back at Barcelona and was initially seen as next in line to a lineage of great defenders to have played for the club that includes the likes of Gerard Piqué and Carles Puyol.

Injuries and managerial uncertainty saw Araújo lose his starting spot at Barcelona, but the loan move to Liverpool has reminded everyone of the Uruguayan's talent. He is a natural defender whose ability on the ball as a former Barça player means he can perform a role in possession play on the right side.

This isn’t to say Araújo is anywhere near as creative as Alexander-Arnold in that role for Liverpool. The Uruguayan is yet to create a single chance in the Premier League so far this season and is averaging just 44.2 passes per 90 minutes, ranking him well below defensive teammates Virgil Van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet for this metric.

With Araújo generally a stay-at-home right back, Milos Kerkez has been given more freedom to get forward down the opposite wing. The Uruguayan has steadied Liverpool, offering greater security in defensive transition and balancing out Iraola’s team which would otherwise risk being top-heavy.

“I think he needed this kind of change,” said Iraola about Araújo, addressing the Uruguayan's resurgence since joining on loan from Barcelona where many had written him off. “[He] has come with humility and is also coming from a big club. He’s an experienced player.

“Especially when you are a centre back and you have to play wide as a right back, the demands physically are different. I like his spirit. Now I'm pushing him to learn a little bit of the language because a good way for us to use his experience is if he could communicate better with the teammates and use all the experience that he has, but I suppose it will take some time.”

This season is shaping up to be a transitional one for Liverpool and Araújo is a stop-gap solution. Regardless, he has helped give Iraola a steadier platform to build on when a shaky start to the season might have spiralled. Araújo might not be the right back Liverpool envisaged replacing Alexander-Arnold, but he’s had the best stab at the job so far.

          Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal Stats: Late Madueke Strike Rewards Gunners' Patience
        
      
                          
                      Oct 18, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It wasn't a vintage performance but Arsenal got the job done at the City Ground. Look back on a hard-fought Premier League win with our Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal stats page.
Noni Madueke came off the bench to make the difference for Arsenal as his deflected effort clinched a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.
The reigning Premier League champions were largely flat at the City Ground on Sunday, yet they had the quality to get the job done in the end.
A low-key first half saw Kai Havertz head over from Declan Rice‘s free-kick, but little else of note occurred at either end.
Forest, shorn of the injured Morgan Gibbs-White, were quick out of the blocks after the interval, with Liam Delap almost setting up Neco Williams.
But Arsenal did have openings. Gabriel Magalhães headed over from a corner, before Rice blasted over the crossbar from inside the Forest box.

The deadlock was then finally broken in the 80th minute as Madueke, who replaced Eberechi Eze at half-time, skipped in from the left, took on Daniel Muñoz and found the top-far corner courtesy of a deflection off Jair Cunha.
Oliver Glasner's team came on strong in the closing stages, with Rice denying Chris Wood a free shot before Murillo, on his 100th appearance for Forest, fired just over at the end of a brilliant run.
But their fate was sealed when Ezri Konsa made a fine recovery challenge on Delap, condemning Forest to a third straight defeat.
Madueke has scored 13 of his 17 Premier League goals away from home (76%), including all four for Arsenal. This is the highest away ratio of any player with 15+ goals in Premier League history.
The England winger is also coming up big in the key moments, too. Three of his last five goals in the top flight have been the first of the game.

It was far from a classic, as evidenced by both teams managing just three attempts on target between them. Forest had two of those, but Arsenal made theirs count, even if they did get lucky with Cunha's deflection.

This is a familiar scoreline for the Gunners, though. Since Arteta took charge in December 2019, Arsenal have registered 32 1-0 wins in the Premier League, the joint most of any team, along with Everton.
Forest, meanwhile, find themselves in the relegation zone with just five points from their seven games.
And they are particularly struggling at home.
Forest are one of just two sides without a home league goal in Europe’s big-five leagues this season, along with Schalke.

They are just the fifth side in English top-flight history to fail to score in their first four home matches of a campaign, after West Brom in 1921-22, Everton in 1998-99, Crystal Palace in 2018-19 and Huddersfield Town in 2018-19.
In fact, Forest have won just one of their last 15 Premier League games at the City Ground (D8 L6) since the first of these matches.

CC5F12220B5C8213383092A31CE32B21.title: The MLS Wrap: Wonderkids go international and another Messi golazo isn’t enough for Inter Miami
CC5F12220B5C8213383092A31CE32B21.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Wonderkids go international and another Messi golazo isn’t enough for Inter MiamiShareAs is regularly the case, MLS fixtures continued during the international break, and some of the league’s in-form teams managed to put in strong showings despite missing several players to national team duty.
Lionel Messi leads the highlight reels once again, and two of the best teams in the division continued their good performances.
But the most notable MLS story from this round of games comes not from those league matches, but from the international window itself and the United States team that defeated Peru 4-1 on Saturday.
Mauricio Pochettino selected a squad of promising young players, including one who’s been a regular feature in this column of late, Cavan Sullivan.
The Philadelphia Union teenager, who turned 17 today, made his national team debut versus Peru and put in an impressive display, having been selected in the starting XI.
There were performances throughout the US team that showcased the homegrown talent coming through in MLS in 2026.

🇺🇸 Mauricio Pochettino gives youth a chance and the USMNT beat Peru convincingly. The starting line-up had an average age of 23. And from the bench, both Sebastian Berhalter (25) and Julian Hall (18) scored and assisted goals. pic.twitter.com/5Hl10rvsdr
The opening goal was scored by Orlando City 19-year-old attacker Justin Ellis, while the 18-year-old New England Revolution winger, Peyton Miller, started at left-back and grew into the game.
There were then numerous MLS-based international debutants off the bench, with one of them, Red Bull New York’s 18-year-old striker Julian Hall, getting the third goal in the 4-1 win.

There were also international debuts for young MLS stars Adri Mehmeti (17 years old, Red Bulls), Neil Pierre (18, Philadelphia), Brooklyn Raines (21, New England), and Frankie Westfield (20, Philadelphia).

Other foreign-based youngsters, Mathis Albert (17, Borussia Dortmund), Zavier Gozo (19, Crystal Palace), and goalkeeper Diego Kochen (20, Lyngby) also made their first senior international appearances.
But from an MLS perspective, it was encouraging that so many homegrown players have made the step up this season.

Not just to first-team football at club level, becoming regulars and in some cases key players for their teams, but also being recognised by Pochettino for international call-ups and then playing their part in a good win.
FC Dallas’ good form started to show in the overall MLS table following their 1-0 win at home to Los Angeles FC this weekend.

Both sides were missing key attackers, most notably Denis Bouanga and Son Heung-min for LAFC and Petar Musa for FC Dallas, but the team from Texas managed to keep their run going, making it four wins from their last five games.
Musa has been the outstanding player for Dallas this season. He’s ahead of Messi for goals per 90 minutes, at 0.95, and is second only to Messi for shots on target per 90.
In his absence, the FC Dallas goal came via a header from centre-back Osaze Urhoghide from a Joaquín Valiente corner.
Goalkeeper Daniel has been one of the better stoppers in MLS for several years now, and has performed well in his last two games, having joined FC Dallas from San Jose this summer.
This latest win saw them overtake St. Louis City, Houston Dynamo, New England Revolution, and Inter Miami to claim third spot in the Supporters’ Shield standings.
On the other side of the coin, this latest defeat saw LAFC make the decision to sack head coach Marc Dos Santos.

          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 9
        
      
                          
                      Oct 29, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Gameweek 9 awaits in Fantasy Premier League, and The 10% Club returns with five more under-the-radar picks.
João Pedro’s injury and Cole Palmer’s red card dampened many Fantasy Premier League plans last weekend, but we have some solutions here in The 10% Club.
There are some interesting differential options for Gameweek 9, including a Bournemouth defender, a surprising Tottenham choice, and a striker who has only just come back into the fold.
Using Opta data, we’ve picked out five under-the-radar gems – all in fewer than 10% of squads worldwide – that could get you ahead of your mini-league rivals.
With David Raya proving his worth as the most expensive, highest owned, and top-scoring goalkeeper, many FPL managers will be settled on the Arsenal man.
However, there is a differential option should you wish to go against the template when Mikel Arteta’s champions have a tough trip to Liverpool at Anfield this week.
After ending Manchester City’s perfect start last Saturday, a favourable run sees Aston Villa face Fulham (H), Manchester United (A), Sunderland (H), Ipswich Town (A) and Everton (H).
So, we’d suggest looking at Zion Suzuki as a different selection between the posts. The Japanese goalkeeper may rank eighth for points (30) in his position, but there is a key caveat.

Suzuki has finished in the bonus points (3 against Hull City, 2 against Newcastle United) whenever Villa have kept a clean sheet this season (twice). More shutouts could be likely with a friendlier set of fixtures, too.
Averaging 3.6 saves per 90 minutes, Suzuki is also a strong contender for at least one additional point that FPL awards goalkeepers for a minimum of three saves per match.
Plus, after Johan Manzambi (11 points on GW7) and Nicolas Jackson (13 points on GW8) delivered for this column, you don’t want to miss out on another Villa pick.
Bournemouth may have endured a tough start to life under Marco Rose, but there have been signs of revival in the last two weeks.

Rose’s side earned their first win and clean sheet of the season with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Sunderland on GW7, before hammering Manchester United 3-0 on GW8. They also beat Milan 3-0 in the UEFA Europa League in between those league victories.
So, having already highlighted the potential of Marcus Tavernier (GW5) and Evanilson (GW7), we’re now considering Bournemouth’s defence.

António Silva has secured an additional two points for defensive contributions in six of eight games so far. No defender can better his 75% DEFCON hit rate either, while he is £0.5m cheaper than teammate James Hill for largely the same points output.

Leeds United’s visit should see Silva tested in duels by FPL favourite Dominic Calvert-Lewin, before a presentable run of fixtures boost his chances of a clean sheet against Ipswich (A), Nottingham Forest (H) and Fulham (A).
Brighton’s Luka Vuskovic (52 points) and Maxim De Cuyper (60) are in a similar price bracket, but with the Seagulls away to Man City, Silva is our defender locked in for this weekend.
Much like Silva, Kristoffer Ajer is another reliable defensive option for Brentford ahead of their home clash with Forest.

Although Ajer has reached the DEFCON threshold in just three of his eight games, he has been close to greater success. Ajer finished one short of 10 defensive contributions in three straight matches against Bournemouth, Chelsea and Villa.
The Norwegian defender also chipped in with his first goal of the season in that Villa draw, and he remains a consistent threat from both corners and throw-ins with Brentford’s set-piece proficiency.

          Spain Built the Youth Development Pathway England Still Crave
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Peter McKeever / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Spain have won successive major international men's tournaments. The pathways from academy football to senior teams at La Liga clubs has undoubtedly helped.
Drastic, nationwide reviews of football development in specific countries are ordinarily associated with prolonged fallow periods or short spells of extreme underperformance.
Two relatively recent high-profile examples would be Germany and England.

For Germany, a disappointing quarter-final exit to Croatia at the 1998 World Cup proved a pivotal moment for a re-think and increased investment behind the scenes in youth football. So, when there was outrage and calls for root-and-branch investigations in the wake of the national team failing to get out of their group at Euro 2000, strides had actually already been made. Germany went on to finish as runners-up at the 2002 World Cup, third at both the 2006 and 2010 World Cups, before winning it in 2014.

England, meanwhile, failed to even qualify for Euro 2008, and that was followed by an exit to Germany in the last 16 of a thoroughly underwhelming 2010 World Cup campaign. About six months after the latter, the FA unveiled its Youth Development Review, which provided 25 recommendations intended to improve the standard of football at every level, but especially in the grassroots game.

This review is broadly accepted as being a major catalyst for England's significantly improved results at major men's international tournaments in recent times, with the Three Lions reaching as many semi-finals (4) across the World Cup and European Championship since 2018 as they had in their entire history before Russia 2018.
How does any of this relate to Spain, then?
Well, if you're looking for similarities with respect to underperformance, it doesn't really relate at all, and that's the point.

Over several years, Spain did their own review of youth development and is currently in the second phase of a 10-to-12-year La Liga-led National Plan for the Optimisation and Improvement of Youth Academies, essentially a strategy to professionalise them. But as Juan Florit, La Liga's head of football projects, explains, academy reform in Spain was different to the prior examples because it was not triggered by a crisis.

“Traditionally, when a country, an organisation such as La Liga or a football association begins such a project, you start it from a position of weakness, from a problem or from a negative situation,” he says when asked by Opta Analyst about the initiative's grounding. “But if we think that with this it will be enough for the first decade, sooner or later we will be behind other countries [again].”
In 2016, clubs from the top two divisions began hosting annual Youth Academy Meetings with the intention of sharing knowledge, methodology and tools, hoping to improve competitiveness.

Granted, at this point Spain had recently underwhelmed at Euro 2016, having also failed to impress at the 2014 World Cup. But still, this was only four years on from winning Euro 2012, their third successive triumph at a major international tournament. Spanish football was hardly in crisis.
The Youth Academy Meetings ultimately led to the 2022 creation of the aforementioned ‘National Plan', which set out to take “grassroots football to a new level”.

It comprised five key principles: infrastructure, resources and technology; comprehensive player care; development and transition to professional football; training model and transition to competition; and structure and professional development.

This wasn't a reaction to any extreme underperformance either. The senior side had got to the semis of the delayed Euro 2020 a year earlier and the final of the 2021 Nations League. And at youth level, their Under-19s and Under-17s had each reached at least the last four of their most recent respective Euros in 2019 (youth tournaments in 2020 and 2021 were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic).

While the phrase “if it isn't broken, don't fix it” does spring to mind, Spanish clubs and authorities spotted an opportunity to help themselves. If all academies were more professionally run, every club could potentially stand to benefit. At the very least, the steady stream of domestic players coming through and supplying the national team would be maintained.
“We thought that we needed to do something,” says Florit. “Other countries like Germany, Austria and Sweden were starting good projects with a solid base and a long-term vision.
“[Before] there was no real collective plan, collective vision, or collective strategy to work within the academy system and to strengthen the development of young talents [across Spain].”

And while that may have been the case, the domestic contingent in La Liga was already very strong and remains as such, perhaps to a degree most won't be fully aware of. This is their position of strength.

For the 10 seasons prior to 2026-27, the average number of Spanish players to play more than 450 minutes (so, the equivalent of five full matches) in a campaign is 236.6, a figure that dwarfs the rest of the big five leagues. The next closest is Italians in Serie A (152.2), followed by French players in Ligue 1 (149.9), Germans in the Bundesliga (142.6) and then English players in the Premier League (117.7).

paragraphs: BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportEarthReelWorklifeTravelCultureFutureMusicTVWeatherSoundsClose menu BBC SportMenuHomeFootballCricketFormula 1Rugby UTennisGolfCyclingAthleticsMoreA-Z SportsAmerican FootballAthleticsBasketballBoxingCricketCyclingDartsDisability SportFootballFormula 1Gaelic GamesGolfGymnasticsHorse RacingMixed Martial ArtsMotorsportNetballRugby LeagueRugby UnionSnookerSwimmingTennisFull Sports A-ZMore from SportEnglandScotlandWalesNorthern IrelandQuizzesNews FeedsHelp & FAQsPremier LeagueScores & FixturesTableFollow Your TeamTransfersTop ScorersGossipSutton's predictions v Bad Day At The Office star John HannahPublished5 hours agoPremier League champions Arsenal endured one of the most embarrassing nights in their history when they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by League Two side Fleetwood Town on Tuesday, but can they bounce back at Anfield on Sunday?
"Arsenal put a pretty strong team out but were humiliated by Fleetwood, and at Highbury too," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.
"Liverpool seem to be getting it together so this will be a big test for Mikel Arteta's side after the week they have had."
Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.
For week eight, he takes on actor John Hannah, star of new action thriller Bad Day At The Office, who is an Arsenal fan.
Bad Day At The Office will be in UK and Irish cinemas from 30 October.
Do you agree with their predictions? You can pick your own below.
The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.
A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.
Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Image source, Bad Day At The OfficeImage caption, Mostly filmed from a first-person perspective using GoPro cameras, Bad Day At The Office follows a man who wakes up in a wrecked hotel room with no memory of the night before
Hannah, also known for his roles in Four Weddings and a Funeral, Sliding Doors and The Mummy, has been an Arsenal fan since he moved to London from Scotland more than 40 years ago.
As a boy growing up in East Kilbride he had hopes of becoming a footballer long before realising his acting aspirations.
Many of his childhood friends, including Rangers legend Ally McCoist, would go on to forge professional careers.
"I'd like to compare myself to Bukayo Saka," Hannah explained when describing what kind of player he was. "I played on the right wing and I was quite small and fast and I scored a lot of of goals.
"My dream was to be a footballer, and it was all I ever thought about. I played or trained all the time  - but, like many dreams, it didn't come true.
"As I got a bit bigger I kind of segued back into midfield but when I discovered women and beer then I kind of stopped playing.
"Once I went to drama school I got very focused on that and then with moving to London and working away, around probably 20 years passed without me kicking a ball.
"But then in 2013 I did a film called Shooting for Socrates, where I played Northern Ireland manager Billy Bingham at the 1986 World Cup.
"We were down in Spain doing some filming there and had a bit of a kickaround and I remember thinking 'yeah, I've still got it you know!'

          Manchester City 2-4 PSG Stats: Guardiola's Etihad Return Soured by European Champions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain blew Manchester City away in the first half, and a second-half fightback proved fruitless as the French side prevailed 4-2 at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday night.
Pep Guardiola took in a UEFA Champions League thriller on his return to the Etihad Stadium as Paris Saint-Germain beat Manchester City 4-2.
Guardiola returned to his former stomping ground for the first time since his departure at the end of last season.

But despite a raucous pre-match atmosphere in City's first home game following the guilty verdict in the Premier League's case against them, Guardiola saw his old team fall 3-0 down inside 32 minutes.
Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Vitinha were on target in an inspired first-half display from PSG, but Erling Haaland‘s double saw City threaten a fightback.

The crossbar spared Matvey Safonov's blushes when he palmed against it in the 12th minute, with Antoine Semenyo blazing over on the rebound, though Marc Guéhi was penalised for a foul on PSG's goalkeeper.
Yet PSG hit the front two minutes later. Fabián Ruiz fed Doué on the counter-attack, and the France winger skipped in from the left before picking out the bottom-left corner with a drilled strike.
PSG were 2-0 up just 99 seconds later, with Doué and Dembélé combining to devastating effect as the latter headed home from point-blank range.
Vitinha tested Gianluigi Donnarumma, who could then do nothing to deny Achraf Hakimi, but the full-back clipped a header against the woodwork.

PSG did go three up in the 32nd minute, however, with Vitinha slamming in first-time from the edge of the box, as City shipped three goals in the first half of a competitive home game for the first time since 2015 vs Liverpool (4-1 loss).

Joskov Gvardiol headed wide and Jérémy Doku shot tamely at Safonov, and Enzo Maresca wasted no time in shuffling his pack at half-time. Matheus Nunes, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye came on, and the latter crossed in for Haaland to head beyond Safonov in the 53rd minute.
Semenyo hit the crossbar, albeit from an offside position, and Ndiaye went close as City urgently pressed for a second, but a Donnarumma blunder dented their hopes.
Donnarumma got a big hand to Maghnes Akliouche‘s shot, yet the former PSG man only managed to spin the ball up and into the net, and he was unable to scramble it clear.
Gvardiol saw an effort cleared off the line and Enzo Fernández rattled the frame of the goal, while Haaland then hit the top of the bar with a towering header.
There was no denying Haaland 57 seconds later, as he coolly swept in from Bouaddi's cutback to reduce the arrears.
Haaland seemed all set to net his hat-trick in the 83rd minute, only to direct an on-the-slide attempt at Safonov.

Former City striker Ferran Torres squandered a golden chance to put the result beyond all doubt when he sent a tame penalty at Donnarumma following Nunes' foul on Nuno Mendes, but the hosts could not make that reprieve count.

PSG put on a clinic in the first half, and even Guardiola, who was so animated he looked as though he wanted to go and join Maresca down on the touchline, must have been slightly in awe of what Luis Enrique's team produced.
It marked the first time City trailed by three goals at half-time in a home game since January 2012, with PSG having hit the target with seven of their 10 first-half shots.
Yet Maresca can at least look at the second-half response with some positivity. He changed the shape, and City dominated.

          WSL Matchday 3: The Opta Numbers That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Gareth Boyes / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the season, while Arsenal dropped points at home for the second successive match. We use Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
There was no shortage of entertainment across the third matchday of the Women’s Super League, with goals flying in around the league, though Arsenal’s struggles continued in front of goal.

Manchester City maintained their perfect start in a six-goal thriller against Liverpool, Tottenham ran riot with seven against Crystal Palace, while London City Lionesses bounced back from defeat, firing in four goals at Charlton.

Elsewhere, Chelsea made it back-to-back wins, Everton edged past West Ham, and Brighton and Aston Villa shared the points. At the Emirates, Arsenal were frustrated at home once again as Manchester United responded from their difficult start to the season to earn a 1-1 draw.
But, as ever, the scorelines only tell part of the story.
We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout individual performances and numbers that defined Matchday 3.
We’re three games into the new WSL season and Man City are the only side still with a perfect record. But Liverpool made them work for it.
City took the lead before falling 2-1 behind, only to turn the game around and eventually claim a 4-2 victory.
It was just the second time in their WSL history that City have scored first, subsequently trailed and still gone on to win, after their 3-2 victory over Reading in the 2017 Spring Series.
Khadija Shaw continued her flying start to the campaign, becoming the first player to score in each of Manchester City’s opening three matches of a WSL season.
And Liverpool remain one of her favourite opponents.

Alongside Shaw, Lauren Hemp continues to underline her status as one of the WSL’s most devastating attacking talents – and the 26-year-old reached another significant landmark after hitting 100 goal involvements last weekend.
Only Bethany England (69), Vivianne Miedema (67), Beth Mead (60), Nikita Parris (58), Shaw (55) and Fran Kirby (54) have scored in more, while Hemp is now level with Sam Kerr.
And home continues to be a particularly happy place.
Liverpool may have left Manchester empty-handed, but there was another hugely encouraging performance from summer signing Vivien Endemann.

The Germany international is making quite the impression in her first season in England. Three appearances into her WSL career and Gareth Taylor looks like he may have uncovered a real gem for this reshaped Liverpool side.

The Reds pushed City harder than anyone has so far this season, but the league leaders still found a way to win. They have won three from three, scoring 12 goals in the process. Their perfect start rolls on.
Arsenal may have extended their unbeaten run to record-breaking territory against Manchester United, but for the second successive home game, it took late drama just to rescue a point.
After being held to a goalless draw by Crystal Palace on Matchday 2, the Gunners looked set for a first league defeat of the season before finding an equaliser deep into stoppage time.
Nonetheless, that late intervention preserved an impressive record.

          Bayern Munich vs Arsenal Prediction: UEFA Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Two of the pre-season UEFA Champions League favourites go head-to-head in Bavaria on Wednesday, and we look ahead to that clash with our data-powered Bayern Munich vs Arsenal prediction and preview.
Going into Matchday 3 of the league phase in this season's UEFA Champions League, Arsenal and Bayern Munich are the Opta supercomputer's top two favourites to become European champions.
The predictive model gives Arsenal a 20.7% chance of lifting the trophy for the first time, while Bayern have a 15.2% probability of clinching their seventh continental crown.
And with the teams going head-to-head at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday, both will face an early test of their credentials.

Bayern got back to winning ways in convincing fashion in the Bundesliga on Saturday, as a Luis Díaz hat-trick helped them thump RB Leipzig 6-1. The Bavarian giants had a staggering 17 shots on target in that match, their most in any league game since tallying 20 against Borussia Mönchengladbach in August 2022.

That dominant victory must have been cathartic following a frustrating return from the international break for Vincent Kompany's side, who had to come from behind twice to draw 2-2 with Augsburg in their previous Bundesliga game, before sharing six goals equally with Norwegian champions Viking on MD2 in the Champions League.

Michael Olise‘s red card was costly in that game, not only because it allowed Viking to play the final 16 minutes with a numerical advantage, scoring a late equaliser, but also because the France superstar will now serve a one-match ban against Arsenal.

Olise will leave big shoes to fill. Since the start of last season, he has created more chances than any other player in the Champions League (44), while also making the joint-most defensive line-breaking passes (43). Only Lamine Yamal (55) has completed more dribbles than the Frenchman (54).

Either Arsenal academy graduate Serge Gnabry or promising youngster Lennart Karl will likely come in on the right flank, and the good news for the hosts is that they still have plenty of firepower in their ranks, even with Olise missing.

This will be Harry Kane‘s penultimate game before he discovers whether he has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001, with the winner of football's most prestigious individual award announced next week.
And Kane, who marked his 100th Bundesliga appearance with his 102nd goal in the competition on Saturday, has an excellent record against Arsenal.
The former Tottenham hero has scored 15 goals in 22 career appearances against the Gunners, only netting more against Leicester City (20) and Everton (16).

England's captain will be going up against the Premier League‘s best defensive unit, with Arsenal remaining within three points of Manchester City domestically following Sunday's hard-earned 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.

Noni Madueke came off the bench to settle that encounter with a deflected strike, and although there were a few nervy moments late on, Arsenal held on for their 32nd 1-0 win in the Premier League under Mikel Arteta – the joint-most of any team since he took charge in December 2019 (alongside Everton).

The Gunners are one of nine teams to have maximum points on the board in the Champions League, following last week's 3-0 victory over Lille. Bukayo Saka played a starring role in that success, coming off the bench to provide a goal and assist, and he is primed to play a key part here.

Just four of Saka's 14 Champions League goals have come away from home, though two of those were against Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain. Only two players have ever scored away against all three of Bayern Munich, Real Madrid and PSG in the competition – Didier Drogba and Erling Haaland.

Given Bayern's commitment to dominating possession, it remains to be seen just how aggressive Arsenal will be – they attracted criticism for their tentative approach in last season's final versus PSG, recording the lowest possession share on record by any team in a Champions League showpiece (since 2003-04, 24.7%).
However, 73% of Arsenal's high-intensity pressures in the Champions League this season have been in the opposition half (373/508), the highest percentage by any team through the first two matchdays.
The Gunners also led all teams for high turnovers (25) and shot-ending high turnovers (9) in the opening two rounds of fixtures, so they certainly have it in them play proactively.

Arsenal have also won each of their last 14 league-stage matches in UEFA's top-tier competition, with only PSG and Real Madrid (28 each) having won more Champions League games overall than the Gunners since their 2023 return (27, level with Bayern).

          Barcelona vs Real Madrid Prediction: La Liga El Clásico Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The first Clásico of the season upon us, and with six points already splitting the teams in La Liga, it's an important one. We look ahead to Sunday's game with our Barcelona vs Real Madrid prediction and preview.

Few rivalries in world football can match the animosity, theatre and sheer level of quality provided by El Clásico, and with José Mourinho back in the mix, Real Madrid's clashes with Barcelona this season should be appointment viewing.
The first Clásico of the campaign takes place on Sunday at Camp Nou, with the pressure firmly on Madrid ahead of their trip to Catalonia.

While Barcelona have won their opening nine games in La Liga, making a serene start to their quest for a third straight title under Hansi Flick, Madrid are already six points off the pace as a consequence of defeats to Real Betis and Atlético Madrid.

Indeed, this is Madrid's biggest negative points differential to the La Liga leaders this early in a campaign since 2012-13, when they sat eight points behind Barça after nine matchdays, and ultimately finished 15 points adrift in second, also under Mourinho.
So, Madrid's margin of error is already slim coming into this game, and Mourinho has made no secret of his belief that Los Blancos have had things tough lately.

Following Wednesday's 4-1 UEFA Champions League win over RB Leipzig, Mourinho immediately pointed out that Barça will have an extra 24 hours to prepare for Sunday's match, having lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in a thriller on Tuesday.

Mourinho previously expressed outrage at the news that Vinícius Júnior will miss Sunday's match, having been handed a four-game domestic ban following his red card for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair during the recent win over Villarreal.

So, Mourinho must find alternative sources of attacking spark against the Blaugrana, although it should be said that Vinícius has been far from his electrifying best this season, only scoring once – and supplying three assists – in 11 matches across all competitions.

On the eve of the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, Sunday's match will see two of the main contenders go head-to-head, with Kylian Mbappé hoping to inspire Madrid and Lamine Yamal headlining Barça's star-studded attack.
Mbappé has a phenomenal record against Barcelona, scoring 12 goals in 10 games against them in all competitions throughout his career (four in three outings for PSG, eight in seven for Madrid).
The only players to find the net more often against the Blaugrana this century are former Madrid icons Cristiano Ronaldo (20 goals) and Karim Benzema (16).

Yamal, meanwhile, has built on his FIFA World Cup success with Spain by taking things to a new level at the start of 2026-27. The teenage sensation has eight goals in nine La Liga appearances this campaign, the most by any player aged 20 or younger at this stage of a season in the 21st century.
Since 31 August, Yamal's 14 total goal involvements are the most by any player in Europe's top five leagues, with teammate Raphinha (11) the only other player in double figures.
Barcelona have always been easy on the eye under Flick, but their attacking returns this season have been truly special, plundering 39 goals in the opening nine La Liga matchdays.

Only one team in the competition's history has managed a better goalscoring start, with no side doing so since the Second World War – Sevilla netted 42 times in nine games at the beginning of 1940-41.

Barça are just the second team to win their first nine games at the start of a La Liga season, after Madrid did so way back in 1968-69, and they now have a chance to make history, as no team has ever won their first 10.

Now, the prospect of making a piece of Spanish football history at their arch-rivals' expense, while opening up a nine-point gap in the table in the process, will offer huge motivation to everyone of a Blaugrana persuasion.

Barcelona have won their last two home games against Madrid in La Liga. The most recent Clásico, in May, saw Flick's side wrap up the title as since-departed duo Marcus Rashford and Ferran Torres netted in a 2-0 victory that sparked huge celebrations in Catalonia.
Only once in the 21st century have Barça achieved three consecutive home victories against Madrid in the competition, doing so under Pep Guardiola between 2008 and 2010.

          Como 4-1 Man Utd Stats: Red Devils Thumped in Italy as Pressure on Carrick Grows
        
      
                          
                      Oct 21, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Cesc Fabregas' Como tore Manchester United apart in their Champions League meeting on Wednesday. Look back on the action with our Como vs Man Utd stats page.
Nico Paz was instrumental as Como blew Manchester United away with a 4-1 win at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in the Champions League.
The 22-year-old got the ball rolling with the opener in just the second minute, and ended the game with a brace and an assist after a stellar performance.

Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramón were also both on target in the thumping victory, which piled further pressure on Michael Carrick, whose side are now winless in their last seven games in all competitions, though they did pull a goal back late on through substitute Joshua Zirkzee.
Diogo Dalot passed up a presentable chance with 84 seconds on the clock; having initially mis-controlled the ball, he recovered but bent his shot wide of the far post.
And 34 seconds later, Como made them pay for that miss. The hosts went straight up the other end, and Paz curled a stunning strike into the left corner of the net.

United failed to muster a response, and Como finished the half on top. Douvikas had the beating of Matthijs de Ligt – making his first appearance in 325 days – and fired a tight-angled effort at Senne Lammens, who brought the forward down on his next attack, but the offside flag meant no penalty was awarded.

Como picked up where they left off after the break as they easily cut through United's defence in the 49th minute, with Paz laying it off to Douvikas, who profited from a De Ligt stumble to brilliantly finish past Lammens.
And things went from bad to worse for United 57 minutes in. Paz pounced on Carlos Baleba‘s blind pass, and raced down the right to finish into the bottom-left corner.
United's urgency grew after that, with substitute Amad Diallo finding space on the edge of the box to test Jean Butez with a dipping strike that was tipped over the crossbar.
Como soon wrestled back momentum, though, and Ramon finished off a wonderful team move after Kaiki chipped a lovely cross into the box 76 minutes in.

Zirkzee netted a late consolation for United, plucking Diallo's cross out of the air before scuffing his strike through Butez's legs in the 91st minute, but it was the only bright spot in an otherwise chastening night for Carrick and his men.

Como's starting XI have made a combined 62 Champions League appearances (prior to this match), compared to the 242 in United's starting line-up, but based on their respective performances, that was not evident.

Cesc Fabregas' side came flying out of the blocks, and their early goal meant United had conceded two goals in the opening two minutes of Champions League games this season, already their most in this time period in a single edition.
In fact, they are the first English team to concede in the first two minutes of consecutive major European matches.

Paz caused all their problems, as he became just the fourth player to be directly involved in at least three goals in a Champions League game against United, and the youngest to do so (aged 22 years and 43 days).
The Argentinian also became the second-youngest South American player to find the net in competition against United, after Lionel Messi (21y 337d in the 2009 final).
Como have settled into the Champions League brilliantly, becoming the first Italian side to win their first two home games since Lazio in 1999-00.
For United, though, it leaves more questions as their torrid away form in UEFA's premier competition; they have won just one of their last 11 games on the road in the Champions League (D3 L7).
They mustered 1.05 expected goals (xG) from 12 shots to Como's 2.04, with Fabregas' side getting eight of their 11 attempts on target.

D56842C51C2D69AE3206E201234AE1D5.title: Preview: Real Madrid return to action against Villarreal
D56842C51C2D69AE3206E201234AE1D5.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Real Madrid return to action against VillarrealShareBoth Real Madrid and Villarreal did not open the season as well as they would have liked, so they will be keen to hit reset on the other side of the long international break.

The one thing fans would have expected from José Mourinho on his return to Real Madrid would have been a solid defence, but that has not yet materialised. Los Blancos currently rank eighth in terms of goals conceded in LaLiga this season. They have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last five games, with their only shutout of the campaign coming against newly-promoted Málaga.

The record Spanish champions certainly aren’t short of attacking quality, though finding the right balance is a challenge. Before they can focus on that, though, their experienced Portuguese tactician will need to prioritise shoring the team up at the back if they are to pose a serious title challenge.

At the time the move was announced, Villarreal and Iñigo Pérez seemed to be a match made in heaven. After consecutive Champions League qualifications playing a solid yet attractive brand of football under Marcelino, the club went for an exciting young coach who had a track record of overperforming at Rayo Vallecano. The idea must have been that his intense pressing approach could help the team develop even further.

In fairness, the early days of such a tactical shift can be rough, but both parties would definitely have been left disappointed with their start to the season. Villarreal failed to win their first six games across all competitions, only picking up two points. They did climb up the table before the international break, but their only wins came against relegation-battlers.
The Yellow Submarine are yet to produce a proper statement performance under their new head coach, and what better place to do it than the Bernabéu?

All eyes will be on the Real Madrid teamsheet to see where Kylian Mbappé’s name is. He sat out most of the international break due to a knee hyperextension, but is expected to be fit for this fixture. His compatriot Ibrahima Konaté did not feature for Les Bleus but will also be available. Federico Valverde picked up an injury in the Madrid derby that might limit his involvement. Éder Militão and Ferland Mendy have returned to training, but Raúl Asencio and the suspended Dean Huijsen are definitely out. Rodrygo remains unavailable.
Villarreal’s only absentee is Tajon Buchanan.

Vinícius Júnior hasn’t looked anywhere near his sharpest lately. After just one goal involvement in his last five club matches, he will be keen to make an impression here. Jude Bellingham will want to bring his excellent England form back to Madrid, with Aurélien Tchouaméni holding the midfield down behind him.

Villarreal right-back Alex Freeman will need to bring his A game to the capital, while Pape Gueye will have a big job to do in midfield as well. Further forward, Alberto Moleiro could produce a moment of quality to unlock the opposition defence.
Real Madrid’s attacking quality may just be enough to come away with a win from a goal-laden game.

D5B75AD01099F7214842C8017D7B82DA.title: Preview: Man City head to Liverpool for Anfield showdown
D5B75AD01099F7214842C8017D7B82DA.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Man City head to Liverpool for Anfield showdownShareOnly five teams remain unbeaten in the Premier League this term and two of them face off at Anfield on Sunday afternoon as Liverpool host leaders Manchester City.

Under Enzo Maresca, Manchester City have a 100% record. They’re five from five in the Premier League, they’re into the next round of the Carabao Cup and they got their Champions League campaign off to a winning start over Porto.

Yes, the Citizens are having off field issues right now, but on the pitch, they just keep on winning. Granted, it hasn’t been the prettiest this term, the fact is it doesn’t have to be. They find themselves three points clear having not really been as convincing as they would’ve liked after spending lavishly during the summer transfer window.

We’ll address the elephant in the room here now as well. City are riding their luck at both ends of the pitch. They’re overperforming their Expected Goals total by 2.5 and they’ve conceded just five goals despite giving up chances with an xG Against total of 7.2. It’s been a case of good finishing by those in blue and poor finishing from those Maresca’s men have come up against.
At some point, that bubble will burst. Is it going to happen at Anfield?

Liverpool, in truth, are due some good fortune in front of goal. The Reds have an xG haul of 8.3 but have just seven goals to their name in the Premier League so far this season. Chances have been missed. Points have been dropped. Despite this, Andoni Iraola’s side are still unbeaten and could finish the weekend just three points behind their opponents.

Over recent weeks, the former Bournemouth boss has made some tweaks to his team and in the process, he’s shored things up. Liverpool conceded four across their opening two matches before keeping three successive clean sheets. A resilient backline coupled with Alexander Isak scoring goals has seen them climb the table.

Liverpool have a few injury concerns heading into this game but even if everyone was fit, the key player would remain the same. It’s Alexis Mac Allister. The Argentine midfielder has been a revelation this term and looks to have rediscovered his form from the title winning campaign. He leads the way amongst the squad for tackles and he’s been deceptively good in possession. If he’s bossing things in the middle third, the hosts have a foothold in the game and they can use that to build.

For the visitors, there’s only one man and it’s Erling Haaland. The City No. 9 leads the way for goals this season with five and he’s going to want to improve his Anfield record. He has just one goal away to Liverpool, though it was a last minute winner last season.

Alexander Isak could miss this game with a slight thigh issue sustained while away with Sweden. Manager Graham Potter confirmed the issue, saying: “He’s got a small problem with his thigh. It’s not a big one but because of the amount of games we’ve got in a small space of time, he won’t be able to make those.” It is touch and go whether the No. 9 will be risked. The Reds are already without Cody Gakpo, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Fede Chiesa.
City, meanwhile, are without the suspended Phil Foden while Nico O’Reilly and Antoine Semenyo are both listed as doubts but could feature on Merseyside this weekend.
We’re going with a score draw so goals for boths sides, and about 500 banners and cards held up on the Kop reminding City of their current predicament: Liverpool 1- Man City.

The previous record holder, Köln legend Dieter Müller, took 129 Bundesliga games to score 100 goals – hitting that milestone in 1977. Harry Kane has managed the feat in just 98 appearances; he could have gone until April without registering a league goal and he’d still have broken the record.
It’s been a history-making September for the England captain, whose winner against Elversberg took him to 150 goals in all competitions for Bayern – in only 153 appearances.

The 33-year-old has picked up where he left off last season, when he enjoyed a career-best 61-goal campaign, finishing as Bundesliga top scorer for the third time in as many years since joining Bayern from Tottenham.

We already knew Kane was one of the best strikers in the world, if not the best – but what we’re seeing now is that he might actually still be getting better, an astonishing possibility for a player who, based on your typical centre-forwards, should be some years past his peak (of course, Kane isn’t your typical centre-forward).

Speaking after his latest landmark achievement, Kane – who amassed 213 goals in 317 Premier League outings for Spurs, placing him behind only Alan Shearer in the competition’s all-time scoring charts – said: “I’m very proud, to be honest, to reach 100 goals in the Bundesliga. Obviously, I’ve done it in the Premier League, so now to have it in a different league is something I’m really proud of. All I can say is a big thanks to the team.”
Kane’s 101 Bundesliga goals have come at a truly prolific average of 1.03 per game. He’s already averaging 0.75 goals per game in the league this season and 0.85 in all competitions.

And none of this should come as any kind of surprise: his overall goals-per-game average for Bayern is 0.98. Were he to score a hat-trick in his side’s first match after the international break, away to local rivals Augsburg, he would pull himself to exactly a goal a game.

It’s little wonder Kane, who has found the net 44 times for club and country this calendar year, is considered one of the frontrunners to win the Ballon d’Or – an individual accolade he’s yet to claim in a career full of them. Oh, and he’s done it at exactly a goal a game.
More goalscoring milestones feel like an inevitability for Kane, who has reportedly been in talks over extending his stay at Bayern, where his current deal expires next summer.

He’s one of 56 players with 100 or more Bundesliga goals to their name – but one of only eight non-Germans. Barring a lengthy injury lay-off or unfathomable loss of form, he’ll almost certainly pass 106-goal Ailton (Brazil) and Stéphane Chapuisat (Switzerland) this term in the ranking of leading foreign Bundesliga scorers – and probably 127-goal Vedad Ibišević (Bosnia and Herzegovina) as well.

Kane can also keep working his way up Bayern’s list of top Bundesliga goalscorers – on which he currently ranks sixth. Next in his sights is Dieter Hoeneß (102 goals), followed by fellow 1980s star Roland Wohlfarth (119).

Another couple of par scoring seasons by his standards and Kane will catch two more Bayern icons: Thomas Müller (150 goals) and two-time Ballon d’Or winner Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (162). Only the top two goalscorers in Bundesliga history are – unless he keeps playing for Bayern and producing these levels into his 40s – out of his reach: Robert Lewandowski (312) and perhaps the greatest No. 9 of all time, Gerd Müller (365).

It’s also not out of the question that Kane will become Bayern’s second-highest Champions League scorer ever. He currently sits second with 34 goals, nine ahead of Arjen Robben and 23 behind Thomas Müller – and with his goals-per-game average for the club in that competition an expectedly high 0.87 as things stand, he could well surpass Müller by the end of next season if Bayern go even reasonably deep into the knockout stage.
And if contract talks progress as both parties will hope, Kane is bound to keep tearing up the division for a number of years yet.

          DEFCONs, Set Pieces, Budget Picks, Wildcards? Six Key FPL Questions Ahead of GW6
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Dan Edwards / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The international break has given Fantasy Premier League managers plenty to think about. Using Opta data and Solio's projections, we assess six of the biggest questions ahead of GW6, including fixture difficulty, defensive contribution points, budget forwards and whether it's too late to jump on Pascal Groß.

Brentford’s 3-0 dismantling of Chelsea, Brighton’s shock undoing of Arsenal by the same scoreline, and Brian Brobbey’s Etihad Stadium hat-trick all feel like a lifetime ago, but in Fantasy Premier League terms, they occurred only last week.

After the longest international break on record, you’d be forgiven for forgetting the contents of your Fantasy Premier League squad, but it’s time to get your head back in the game, because a lot has happened – on and off the field.

To help you get back in business, we’ve combined Opta data with Solio FPL’s projections to answer six common questions Fantasy managers are likely to have after looking at their squads following the long break.
If you want to skip ahead to a certain question, just click on it.
The introduction of defensive contribution points in Fantasy Premier League ahead of the 2025-26 season was arguably the most seismic change ever made to the format.

Defenders now earn two additional points by combining for at least 10 tackles, interceptions, clearances, and blocks in a single game. The threshold for midfielders and forwards was set at 12, but recoveries also counted towards their total.

While Elliot Anderson and Marcos Senesi, for example, may have previously had limited Fantasy relevance, players of their profile were suddenly thrust into the spotlight, expanding the practical player pool as a result.

Having started 2025-26 priced at £5.5m, Anderson ended up as the game’s fifth-highest-scoring midfielder, largely as a result of his league-leading 52 points from defensive contributions. To put this into context, a forward has to score 13 goals to earn 52 points.

It was a similar story for Senesi, who ranked third among defenders last season for total points despite being priced at £4.5m on the opening day. He earned 50 points from defensive contributions, second only to Anderson.

The impact of defensive contributions was perhaps greater than initially anticipated. In 2024-25, the season prior, players would have reached the threshold for defensive contribution points in 16.8% of their starts on average. That hit rate rose sharply to 19.3% in 2025-26, a figure which saw this method of points-scoring become a necessary focus.

But are defensive contributions as important this season as they were last? It’s debatable. The hit rate five rounds into this season is 16.9%, seemingly falling back in line with the season before last – but that number doesn’t tell the whole story.

In each of the previous three seasons, the hit rate after five rounds has been lower than at the season’s culmination. Indeed, this season’s figure is actually higher than it was at the same point last season (16.7%).

The tendency for DEFCON hit rates to increase as the season progresses is especially evident among defenders. Looking at the last three seasons, comparing figures after GW5 with end-of-season totals, defenders' DEFCON hit rates increased by an average of 10.3% over the course of the campaign.
This could be for myriad reasons. Perhaps systems become more distinct, games become more consequential, and players become more desperate towards the end of the season.
Either way, there is enough evidence to suggest it’s an element of the game which could become more and more important as the season progresses.

If this is the case, which players should Fantasy managers be targeting? The leaders for points earned via defensive contributions this season are Kobbie Mainoo, António Silva and Murillo, with eight each. Mainoo has reached the threshold in all four of his starts.
Solio’s projections page gives us an insight into which players are likely to prosper in the near future, and you can even look at a player’s chance of reaching the threshold on a game-by-game level.

Kevin Danso and Tarik Muharemovic lead Solio’s projections with an average hit rate of 64% across the next six games, with both players noticeably clear of any teammate. By way of comparison, Senesi reached the threshold in 70% of his appearances last season.

Anderson is the highest-ranking midfielder by this measure using Solio’s projections, with a forecasted average hit rate of 51% over the next six gameweeks. Meanwhile, Exequiel Palacios’ projected hit rate of 47% makes him a noticeable outlier among midfielders at his price point (£5.0m).
