          Arsenal vs Leeds Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Tom Webber / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Saturday's Premier League match at the Emirates Stadium with our Arsenal vs Leeds prediction and preview. Can the champions return to winning ways?
Arsenal will be hoping to have another reason to celebrate when they take on Leeds United in the Premier League in their first match since Mikel Arteta signed a new contract at the club.
Arteta, who took over the Gunners in 2019 and led them to FA Cup glory in 2020 and the Premier League title last season, put pen to paper on a new contract on Wednesday that runs until June 2030.

The news of Arteta's extension will no doubt mean the Emirates will be buzzing when the Gunners get back to action after the three-week international break, even though their last outing was a shock 3-0 defeat to Brighton.

That was their heaviest defeat since May 2023, when they also went down 3-0 to Brighton. But since the start of 2024, Arteta's men have only lost back-to-back Premier League games once (in April this year).
The defeat to the Seagulls ended Arsenal's seven-game winning streak from the start of the season, a run that included a 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield.

Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz have both scored in each of Arsenal’s two home league games this season – a 3-0 success against Coventry City to start the campaign and a 2-1 victory versus Chelsea in September.
The only time a pair of teammates have both scored in each of their opening three home matches in a Premier League season was when Andy Cole and Rob Lee managed it for Newcastle United in 1994-95.
Havertz, however, is expected to miss out against Leeds after sustaining a hamstring injury while on Germany duty – a fate shared by Greece winger Christos Tzolis.
There were also concerns when Ødegaard sustained an ankle injury in Norway's 2-1 loss to Portugal in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday, but he is expected to be fit.

Viktor Gyökeres could therefore make his first Premier League start of the season, and will be hoping to continue the form that saw him score four goals in as many matches for Sweden during the international break.

Another striker who may feel like he has a point to prove in this game is Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who returned to the England set-up but only featured for a total of 17 minutes across their four Nations League fixtures.

Calvert-Lewin's recall came after a strong start to the Premier League season with Leeds, which made him one of only two players (alongside Everton's Thierno Barry) to rank in the top 10 for aerial duels won (24), runs made ending in the box (33), and high-intensity pressures made in the opposition half (187).

He will hope to help Leeds remain one of just five teams who are yet to taste defeat in the Premier League this season, although they have only scored three times and went into the international break on the back of a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace.
But Daniel Farke's men are heading into a run of five Premier League fixtures coming against teams with an average Opta Power Rating of 93.6 – the fifth hardest upcoming stretch in the top flight.
Harry Wilson missed out against Palace with a thigh injury but could be fit to return after withdrawing from Wales duty, but Joe Rodon is not expected to play any part.
There are also doubts about Jean-Mattéo Bahoya‘s availability after he sustained an ankle injury while representing France Under-21s.
Arsenal have won nine of their last 10 Premier League games against Leeds (D1), including each of the last seven by an aggregate score of 24-5.

They have often been prolific against Leeds, scoring at least four goals in nine different Premier League meetings with them, including both last term. The only fixtures in which a team has managed that feat on more occasions are Arsenal vs Everton (12) and Manchester United vs Newcastle (11).
Leeds have not won at Arsenal since a 3-2 victory in May 2003, a result that meant the Gunners could no longer defend the Premier League title and the Whites were effectively safe from relegation.

F68F9BE550EE327448B543172E8ABC89.title: Preview: Man United return to Old Trafford to face Bournemouth
F68F9BE550EE327448B543172E8ABC89.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Man United return to Old Trafford to face BournemouthShareMichael Carrick’s position at Manchester United is hanging by a thread and now he has to run the gauntlet of Old Trafford against Bournemouth.

Following a mildly improved performance at Elland Road last weekend against Leeds United, Manchester United crashed back into crisis mode with a 4-1 humbling at Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night and further indecorous comments from a senior player after the match.

Still without a league win since the 30th August and without a win in any competition since they beat Sabah 4-0 on the 10th September, the misgivings that were commonplace among onlookers when Michael Carrick was given the job on a full-time basis in the summer have been starting to manifest.

They play a Bournemouth team who registered their first Premier League win of the season last weekend at home against Sunderland, and who won 3-0 in the Europa League on Thursday evening against former United manager Ruben Amorim’s new club, Milan. There was little talk of the Cherries being in ‘crisis’, despite it having taken them six games to register a league win, and they’d also kicked off their Europa League campaign with two straight wins, even before the Milan match.

It’s been three and a half years and six games since Manchester United last beat Bournemouth, with last season’s matches ending in a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford in the middle of December, just as United’s last head-coach-crisis was reaching its apogee, and a 2-2 draw at The Vitality Stadium in March. Bournemouth also won thee first ever league meeting between the two sides, 2-1 in December 2015.

Prior to that, the most famous meeting between the two teams came in the FA Cup Third Round in January 1984, when the then cup-holders United travelled down to Dorset and were beaten 2-0 by a Third Division Bournemouth team managed by a young Redknapp named Harry, thanks to goals scored by Milton Graham and Ian Thompson.

Bruno Fernandes has Manchester United’s highest average ranking and second-most goals and assists, and it feels a little unfair to call on by far their best player to get them out of a hole of their own creation, in some respects. And he’s the one who’s landed the club in a fresh pot of hot water by speaking critically about the tactics used during the Como match, thereby banging another nail into the coffin of the career of his current head coach.

But the truth remains that he’s the player through whom their best football normally flows, and their best chance of taking all three points from this match. So which Bruno will turn up for this match? The one who can dig them out of their problems, or the one who can dig them in still further?

One of Bournemouth’s players in form this season is Marcus Tavernier, who converted a penalty against Milan to add a fifth goal of the campaign, maintaining his position as their top goalscorer. Tavernier is unlikely to dislodge Anthony Gordon from the starting left-wing spot for England, but he’s been capped at U19 and U20 levels, and he may be hoping to make a push for the Euro 2028 squad.

Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Šeško, Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Tom Heaton were already missing for Manchester United, and their injury problems seem to be building. Lisandro Martínez is unlikely to start, while Ayden Heaven and Marcus Rashford are being assessed over illness and a hip issue respectively.

Alex Scott has had an excellent start to the season and is clearly an outstanding talent, so it comes as no surprise to establish that big clubs such as Liverpool and Chelsea are already forming into a fairly undignified scrum to take him away from The Vitality Stadium at the earliest available opportunity.

He’s also out for the next couple of weeks with a thigh injury, which is bad news for Bournemouth. In addition to Scott, Julian Aráujo is a longer-term absentee – he’s likely to be out for another month – but Junior Kroupi may be back following an ankle injury which has kept him out since the summer.

By most accounts, Michael Carrick may already be a dead man walking at Old Trafford. The question facing Manchester United’s players is do they want to play for him, or do they down tools and get the job done as quickly and painlessly as possible?

It’s difficult not to have sympathy with Carrick. He came back when Manchester United were having one of their periodic meltdowns, steadied the ship, and took them back into the Champions League, and their reward for this was to hand him one of football’s most poisonous chalices.

As a head coach rather than a manager, he’s not responsible for another extremely mixed summer in the transfer market in which the defence – which has subsequently leaked like a sieve – was not remotely upgraded, and all this while he also faced the prospect of a Champions League campaign as well as the Premier League.

But the Como defeat plumbed new depths for this Manchester United season, a one-sided loss which started with them conceding in the first couple of minutes – for the second time in a row in this competition – and which they never looked likely to get back into. If the Leeds performance was one tentative step forward, then Como was several steps back.

Despite their lowly position in the Premier League, Bournemouth are no pushovers. Their slovenly approach to holding onto a lead has been one of the memes of the season so far, but against Sunderland last weekend they got the job done reasonably efficiently, and their performance against Milan was excellent. Their European performances have been solid and they’ve been let down by lapses from winning positions, which can be fixed. It doesn’t seem likely that they’ll be near the foot of the Premier League table for that much longer.

At this stage in the Manchester United crisis cycle, there’s no way of predicting a win for them, though they have at times in the past shown a tendency to be surprisingly bloody-minded at such moments. Bournemouth are better than their league position suggests, and their first win of the season was the result they needed to overcome that phobia about holding onto a lead. 3-1 to Bournemouth, and the reading of the last rites for Michael Carrick’s spell as the head coach of Manchester United to become so loud that they can no longer be ignored.

F7DCC6E843721A39D4F3296F94E92022.title: The MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s Miami
F7DCC6E843721A39D4F3296F94E92022.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s MiamiShareThe latest round of MLS matches came amid a moment of celebration for several first-time call-ups to Mauricio Pochettino’s United States team, including one for the league’s standout young star, Cavan Sullivan.

A few of those young players put in notable performances in the latest round of MLS matches, but it was Sullivan and his Philadelphia Union team who once again stole the limelight with a sensational comeback win in Kansas.
Was a wondergoal from Son Heung-min enough to give LAFC a much-needed win? And which team has come up on the rails to overtake Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami?
The latest MLS Wrap answers these questions and has the latest headlines, as well as unearthing some of the more under-the-radar stories in the North American league.
There have been points throughout the last three years when you simply can’t do a weekly roundup of MLS without mentioning Inter Miami and Messi.
The individual performances, coinciding with a team regularly winning games and challenging at the top of the table, meant they could not be ignored.
Even if you try to mix it up to give all the teams some coverage at some point, Messi and Miami demand inclusion most weeks.
Few other players have put in consecutive performances that necessitate such constant attention for their team, but one who is doing so currently is Cavan Sullivan at Philadelphia Union.

The Union’s run since Ryan Richter took over as interim coach is outstanding. They are yet to lose an MLS game during his tenure, and this weekend took that unbeaten run to 11 games in the league, featuring nine wins.

Their run of consecutive wins currently stands at five games thanks to a remarkable 4-3 win against Sporting Kansas City this weekend, coming back to take all three points despite having gone 3-0 down.
What's more, all four of their goals were scored in the space of ten second-half minutes.
A Sporting KC collapse or an unbelievable Philadelphia Union comeback?
Either way, Sullivan, who scored one of those goals to take him to six in his last six games, and the Union are in the headlines once again.

They haven’t stormed up the table like Philadelphia Union, and aren’t one of those teams having a season of two halves that can be separated neatly into pre and post-World Cup narratives, but New England Revolution have gone about the business of winning more games than they lose or draw in 2026, and have sneaked above Inter Miami in the table as a result.
They also boast a teenage American star of their own in 18-year-old Peyton Miller.
The winger scored twice in this weekend’s 4-2 win against Orlando City, building on the one he scored last week against Chicago Fire, and on the three assists in three games he managed in August.
Precise finishes on the break showed his composure even when running at speed with plenty of time to think. Not bad for a player who started out as a left-back.
On the back of such performances, he received a deserved first call-up to the USMNT for the upcoming international window.

The Revolution also have Carles Gil, who has consistently been one of the best players in MLS for eight seasons now, regardless of the kind of form in which the New England team as a whole have been in those years.

Gil contributed a brace of his own to go with Miller’s, and if they can continue with this combination of individual talent and teamwork and results, they may well remain above Inter Miami for the rest of the season and be a threat in the playoffs.

FA7185AA481FBBE1C6E08CA2CE7D5886.title: Preview: Arsenal prepare for Champions League MD2 clash against Lille
FA7185AA481FBBE1C6E08CA2CE7D5886.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: Arsenal prepare for Champions League MD2 clash against LilleShareArsenal have an opportunity to make it two from two in their first Champions League home match of the 2026/27 season.
After an extraordinarily long international break, Arsenal will play their first home Champions League match of the season and their first of three matches in the competition over the next month.

Mikel Arteta’s side started their continental campaign on the front foot with an away win over Napoli and have the opportunity to make it from two to two, which could help them rotate their team later on in the league phase.

On the other hand, Lille have had a long time to simmer on a disappointing defeat to Real Betis in their opening Champions League fixture. Another loss would leave the Ligue 1 side swimming against the tide to make the knockout rounds.
Lille have lost all of their last eight away games against English opponents, which doesn’t bode well for their chances against the Premier League champions.

Arsenal’s record in the league phase of the Champions League is remarkably strong. Indeed, the Gunners have lost two out of 31 league phase games and it’s difficult to envisage that record changing on Tuesday.
Declan Rice was at his imperious best in Arsenal’s weekend win over Leeds United, controlling the match in the centre of the pitch. The England international could be asked to go again on Tuesday.

Riccardo Calafiori was also impressive, scoring the goal that got the Gunners back on level terms. The Italian has become Arsenal’s first choice at left back this season due to the attacking dimension he brings.
Bukayo Saka has still to find top form this season, but remains an important source of creativity and attacking threat down the right side for the Premier League champions.
On-loan Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa scored the only goal of the game for Lille against Le Havre on Saturday and will pose a threat to the Gunners’ backline.

40-year-old Olivier Giroud could feature against his former club after starting in the win over Le Havre. Alternatively, Davide Ancelotti (son of the Don!) could favour Ayase Ueda as a striker more likely to expose space in behind the opposition backline.

Arsenal’s injury situation for Saturday’s match against Leeds wasn’t as severe as feared with Rice, Max Dowman, Ezri Konsa and Kai Havertz all passed fit to feature despite withdrawing from international duty.

Christos Tzolis and William Saliba are still sidelined for the time being with Piero Hincapié also unavailable for the Gunners. Bruno Guimarães, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyökeres could be in line for a start as rotational options.
Ethan Mbappé’s red card against Real Betis means he will miss Tuesday’s match in North London through suspension. Defender Tiago Santos was also stretched off against Le Havre in Lille’s last outing.
Striker Hamza Igamane is a long-term absentee with an ACL injury while left back Romain Perraud is another doubt. Ancelotti has a number of injury concerns to contend with.
We don't expect the French visitors to improve on their poor record against English opposition: Arsenal 2-0 Lille.

          Not Yet an All-Rounder, But Match-Winner Alexander Isak Proving His Worth at Liverpool
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It was a third consecutive Premier League away game in which Alexander Isak scored the winner for Liverpool. The Swede is finally proving his worth after a turbulent first season on Merseyside.
All three of Liverpool’s wins in the Premier League this season have come on the road, and all three have been courtesy of winning goals from Alexander Isak.

Saturday always looked like it could be tough for Andoni Iraola’s men. Facing unbeaten Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium just three days after a European away game had all the hallmarks of a difficult afternoon.

The Bees beat Chelsea 3-0 in their previous home game, and Liverpool were coming into the contest off the back of a loss by the same score against Manchester City the previous weekend at Anfield. They scored six against LASK in the Champions League in midweek, but Keith Andrews’ side would surely present more of a challenge.

The first half didn’t exactly dampen those fears either. After Bradley Barcola missed a glorious one-on-one chance to give Liverpool the lead, they lost Dominik Szoboszlai to injury and had a penalty award overturned after a VAR review. Just moments later, Keane Lewis-Potter headed Brentford in front.

Everything was going wrong, until Yehor Yarmoliuk had a moment of madness and decided to headbutt Jérémy Jacquet while jostling ahead of a corner being taken. Unsurprisingly, he was shown a red card just before half-time.

That changed the game entirely, and in the second half, Liverpool took advantage. First, Florian Wirtz fed Víctor Muñoz, who raced away down the right, before chopping inside and finishing well to equalise.
Then eight minutes later, Isak, who had been quiet up to that point, controlled Barcola’s header back to him and finished well to score what ultimately proved to be the winner.
It wasn’t the first time Liverpool’s £125 million striker had not done much until he made the most important contribution of the game.

Isak’s first goal of the season was to equalise against Nottingham Forest on Matchday 2 at Anfield, while he hit a quickfire brace early on at Ipswich Town in what proved to be the only two goals of that victory.

He scored the only goal of the win at Bournemouth just before the international break, and though he missed the home defeat to Man City through injury picked up during that break, he was back in the starting line-up at Brentford, justifying his involvement with another winner.

There was, of course, a lot of attention after Isak’s move to Liverpool in the summer of 2025: the manner of how he left Newcastle United, the money involved, and a thoroughly underwhelming return in his first campaign on Merseyside.
A lack of pre-season, generally poor performances from Liverpool under Arne Slot, and terrible luck with injuries meant Isak produced just four goals in 22 games last season.
We’re only in mid-October and he already has five goals this season in just eight games.

He has already racked up a personal expected goals total (xG) of 4.1 in those eight games, just shy of the 4.2 he managed in 22 outings last season, while his xG per shot has gone up to 0.21 from 0.15, meaning he is taking his shots from much better positions on average.
More important than these numbers, though, is his ability to decide tight matches, and especially tricky away matches.

As Opta’s Michael Reid pointed out on X after the game, Isak became just the second Liverpool player in the 21st century to score the winning goal in three consecutive Premier League away games, after Roberto Firmino (Dec 2019 to Jan 2020).
Alexander Isak is only the second player in the 21st century to score the winner in 3 consecutive Premier League away games for Liverpool, after Roberto Firmino from Dec 2019 to Jan 2020. #LFC

Isak also continued his perfect record against Brentford. The Swede has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against the Bees (5 goals, 4 for Newcastle); only Erling Haaland vs Crystal Palace (6) has a better 100% rate in the competition.

That ability to be quiet in a game before pouncing to score a crucial goal is something Haaland gets praised for all the time, and rightly so. Isak perhaps had a reputation from his time at Newcastle for being more involved in build-up play, arguably more of an all-round forward than the Norwegian.

          Arsenal Have Hit Their First Bump in the Road – Here’s Why They Should Bounce Back
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
A heavy defeat to Brighton was followed by injuries to some key players during the international break, but Arsenal have spent years building a squad capable of absorbing such setbacks. Now it‘s time for their depth to shine through.
It’s been a long three weeks for Arsenal fans. Three weeks to stew over their club’s worst result, and arguably poorest performance, in a very long time.

Mikel Arteta’s side were completely blown away by Brighton on Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 Premier League season. They lost 3-0 on the south coast, unable to cope with the intensity and relentlessness of Brighton’s press.
It was Arsenal’s biggest defeat in any competition for more than three years. The last time they lost a game by three or more goals was also against Brighton, back in a 3-0 home defeat in May 2023.
Then came the international break and the dreaded injuries that can accompany it.

Kai Havertz was forced off in Germany’s first game against the Netherlands with a suspected hamstring injury. Christos Tzolis then suffered the same fate against the same opposition for Greece last week. Both had started the season excellently for Arsenal; they could each now miss multiple weeks of action.

Ezri Konsa, who has slotted in superbly at the heart of the defence amid William Saliba’s continued absence, also had to withdraw early from England’s Nations League squad after sustaining a knock in training.
Suddenly, three members of Arsenal’s first-choice starting XI are doubts for this weekend. In the cases of Havertz and Tzolis, their absences could stretch well beyond that.

Heading into MD5, it felt like there was no stopping the Gunners. They had won each of their first four Premier League games, as well as three more in other competitions, and few of their opponents had caused them any real problems. Then Brighton completely outplayed them, and they have now lost several first-choice players to injury.

But if any side has the resilience and squad depth to handle setbacks like these – and it's worth saying that Arsenal are hardly the only team to have suffered injuries during the international break – it's this one. Arteta will not be overly worried, and neither should the fans be.

The very fact the Brighton game was Arsenal’s heaviest defeat in more than three years shows just how rare it is for Arteta's men to have an off day. It was only the second time in their last 158 matches in all competitions that they had conceded three goals. It's also their only defeat in their last 16 games in all competitions.
This is a side who have been consistently dominant for more than 12 months, and defensively dominant for even longer.

Arsenal have typically responded well to setbacks, too. Since the start of 2024, they've lost back-to-back Premier League games just once, against Bournemouth and Manchester City in April this year. Saturday’s meeting with Leeds will be their 100th league game since the beginning of that year.
For context, City have suffered consecutive league defeats on three separate occasions over the same period.

There is every chance, then, that Arsenal bounce back strongly when the action returns. Leeds have done well this season and are one of only five unbeaten teams, but Arsenal have an excellent record against them.

The Gunners have won nine of the two teams' last 10 Premier League meetings (D1), including the last seven by an aggregate score of 24-5. Last season, they won 5-0 at the Emirates and 4-0 at Elland Road.
That home meeting saw Viktor Gyökeres score the first goals of his Arsenal career, and he has netted more Premier League goals against Leeds (3) than any other opponent.

For all the harm the international break has done to Arsenal's squad, the former Sporting CP striker is one player returning from a very productive few games, scoring in all four of Sweden’s Nations League matches. With Havertz sidelined, Gyökeres is his natural replacement.

The Swede has unfortunately become something of a figure of amusement among rival fans, having failed to fully live up to the lofty expectations that came with his big-money move to north London. While he has hardly been a slam-dunk signing, he remains a capable alternative to Havertz, is in good form, and should be able to lead the line effectively in upcoming fixtures against Leeds, Lille and Nottingham Forest.

It's also worth remembering what he achieved last season. Gyökeres became the first player to score 20 or more goals in all competitions during his debut Arsenal season since Alexis Sánchez hit 25 in 2014-15. The only other player to do so for the club in the Premier League era is Thierry Henry, who scored 26 in 1999-2000. However you spin it, his goals undoubtedly helped Arsenal win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final.

          Brighton 5-0 Crystal Palace Stats: Seagulls' Stunning Start to Season Goes on With Astonishing Win
        
      
                          
                      Oct 18, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Brighton enjoyed a memorable Premier League victory over their bitter rivals on Sunday. Look back on a huge win with our Brighton vs Crystal Palace stats page.
Diego Gómez scored one of the all-time great Premier League goals as Brighton surged to a 5-0 victory over rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday.
Brighton were 3-0 up inside 10 minutes at the Amex Stadium, where Gómez grabbed the Seagulls’ second goal in stunning fashion.

Jaydee Canvot turned into his own net in the fourth minute, before Gómez caught Walter Benítez off his line when striking from just inside Palace’s half, sending an audacious attempt in over the stranded goalkeeper.
Yasin Ayari added a third for Fabian Hürzeler’s men, with his deflected strike leaving Palace shellshocked on the south coast.
Palace’s already slender hopes of a comeback were completely extinguished four minutes after the break, with Charalampos Kostoulas turning home from Ayari’s deflected pass.
Honest Ahanor crucially blocked Gómez’s stinging volley before Ferdi Kadioglu saw a fierce first-time strike tipped over the bar as Brighton pressed for more.
Jean-Phillipe Mateta should have got Palace onto the scoresheet when he was left unchallenged to get a shot off, but the France international’s effort struck the crossbar.
Jefferson Lerma then saw a header clip the post after he met Adam Wharton’s centre, and Palace’s misery was compounded in the 84th minute.
Luka Vuskovic met a deep cross and header it back over for Jack Hinshelwood, who was on hand to nudge beyond Benitez and cap a sparkling Brighton display.
Since the start of the 2006-07 season, Gómez’s goal ranks as the eighth longest-range in the Premier League at 51.3 metres.
It is the furthest out from which a goal has been scored in the competition since Wayne Rooney (57.7m) for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

But Gómez has been trying his luck from distance plenty during his time at Brighton. The Paraguayan has already tallied four attempts from over 50m out in the Premier League, though this is was the first to result in a goal.
Brighton became the ninth side in Premier League history to score three goals in the first 10 minutes of a match, and first since Newcastle United against Tottenham in April 2023.

They have already scored 23 Premier League goals this season – their most ever at this stage of a campaign in the top four tiers. Indeed, only Barcelona have scored more goals than the Seagulls across Europe’s big-five leagues this term (39). Brighton’s last four league wins have come by an aggregate score of 15-0.
This was Hürzeler’s first victory over Palace, however, with Leicester City the only one of 29 opponents he has failed to beat across all competitions as Brighton boss (P2 D2).

Palace, meanwhile, have already shipped 17 league goals this term, with the Eagles last conceding more at this stage of a season in the top four tiers in 1980-81 (21), and the pressure may well be mounting on Pierre Sage.

The match centre below includes team and player stats, expected goals data, passing networks, an Opta chalkboard and more. It gives you everything you need to do your own match analysis.
Underneath the match centre you can find the official Opta stats on the game as well.

          Make or Break for Renée Slegers? Man City Test Awaits Under-Pressure Arsenal Boss
        
      
                          
                      Oct 2, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal’s poor start has raised bigger questions than their results alone. We examine the data behind their lack of cutting edge ahead of a crucial trip to the Etihad on Sunday.

After finishing second in the Women's Super League last season, Arsenal would have been looking to build on their potential and bring home the title in 2027. However, with four matches played, the Gunners are already seven points behind leaders Manchester City in the league table.
Defeat to City this weekend would leave them 10 points off the top after only five matchdays. Arsenal have never trailed the league leaders by as much as 10 points after five games of a WSL season.
The same issues surfaced in Wednesday’s UEFA Women's Champions League 2-2 draw with Paris FC.

Arsenal had 69.5% possession and established a two-goal lead, but once again their control failed to translate into complete command of the game. Their performance in Paris highlighted a side still short on confidence and, at times, guilty of being their own worst enemy.

An inability to put the contest beyond doubt allowed Paris back into the match, with the French side generating 1.44 expected goals (xG) from open play compared to Arsenal's 1.16. While the penalty that sparked the comeback may have been unfortunate, the Gunners had already allowed Paris a foothold long before the equaliser arrived.

Given they've built their deepest squad in years with significant summer recruitment and have few injury concerns, not many would have thought Arsenal would have endured such a difficult start to the campaign.

They began with a hard-fought 1-0 win at Brighton, before a shock 0-0 home draw with newly-promoted Crystal Palace. Another game at the Emirates required a late equaliser against Manchester United, a late penalty against HB Køge saw them just about win their opening Champions League game, before suffering a 1-0 defeat at Chelsea last weekend.

The pre-season projection from the Opta supercomputer gave them a 25.6% chance of winning the WSL title across its 10,000 simulations; that figure has now fallen to 7.0%. A defeat at City on Sunday would leave their title hopes hanging by a thread.
Yet there is a familiar element to Arsenal’s struggles.

As was the case last season, the results are falling short of what the underlying numbers suggest. The Gunners' actual WSL points tally is already 2.4 points below their expected total this term, the second-largest underperformance in the league behind Brighton (5.9 points below).

Arsenal are averaging just 1.25 points per game, their lowest rate in any WSL season and are winless in three league matches. Only twice in their history have they endured a longer winless run in the competition, with four-game stretches in May 2014 and October 2023.

Their 97% field tilt against Crystal Palace was perhaps the clearest illustration. Arsenal dominated territory without translating that control into meaningful chances, recording the highest field tilt in a WSL match since the start of 2023-24.
For a team that went 20 WSL matches unbeaten before this run, the speed of the change is striking.

Arsenal are spending 54% of their playing time level — the highest proportion in the division, and a familiar sight for a team that accumulated eight draws last season out. Meanwhile, they have spent just 23% of games in a leading position, the eighth most in the WSL.

The question, then, is not simply whether Arsenal can recover their title challenge, but why a team with greater depth, significant recruitment and few injury concerns are once again struggling to turn control into results.
The most alarming aspect of Arsenal’s start is not simply that they are failing to score, but how little threat they are generating when they have the ball.
Sleger's side are dominating territory without consistently creating the openings that should follow.

The Gunners have scored just two goals from 78 shots across their four WSL matches. Only Charlton (1) have scored fewer goals, while Arsenal’s average of 39 shots per goal is currently the second-highest recorded by any team across a WSL season, behind only Yeovil Town in 2017-18 (46 per goal).
Indeed, Brighton are the only side underperforming their xG total by more than the Gunners – with a differential of -5.3 to the Gunners' -4.6.

a6b5quefmea11nqh9jbab1pao.title: Run of clean sheets should give Liverpool confidence, says Alisson
a6b5quefmea11nqh9jbab1pao.subtitle: Liverpool have gone three Premier League games without conceding ahead of the extended international break, with Alisson buoyed by that run.
paragraphs: Alisson says Liverpool's run of three straight clean sheets in the Premier League should give them confidence for the rest of the season, having ironed out their early defensive woes.
Liverpool started the Andoni Iraola era with back-to-back 2-2 draws against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, never leading either game at any point and looking shaky at the back.

It has been a different story since they beat Ipswich Town 2-0 with an Alexander Isak brace on September 4, though, having drawn 0-0 with Fulham before overcoming Iraola's former club Bournemouth 1-0 on Sunday.

Only Arsenal (4.04) and Forest (4.8) have given up a lower expected goals against (xGA) figure than Liverpool's 6.12 in the Premier League this season, with Leeds United and Everton (three apiece) the only sides to concede fewer goals than their four.
Alisson, meanwhile, has registered the fifth highest save percentage in the league (77.8%), also preventing 0.8 goals according to Opta's expected goals on target (xGoT) model.

The Brazil international made one superb save at the Vitality Stadium, getting down to his right to tip Evanilson's improvised attempt around the post, and he can feel the Reds' backline growing more assured with every shutout.
"I think every Premier League match away from home is tough to play. You have to fight a lot, and this wasn't any different for us," he told Liverpool's website.

"It wasn't the cleanest performance I think we've had, but those games, if you don’t play so well and then you still win it – and keep the clean sheet – I think this brings confidence for the rest of the season as well."
Another key factor in Liverpool's defensive improvement has been the form of new centre-back Jeremy Jacquet, who was named Player of the Match following Sunday's win.
Only Alexis Mac Allister (seven times) won possession more often for Liverpool than the 21-year-old (six, level with Ronald Araujo), while he also won three of his four duels.
But as Alisson noted, playing alongside a defender of Virgil van Dijk's calibre has made the youngster's adaptation smoother.
"I think Jeremy played really well. Virgil, the back four, Ronald, Milos [Kerkez], the midfielders as well, they helped us a lot defensively. Everybody fights a lot," Alisson continued.
"Jeremy has so much quality, of course, but I don't think it's the hardest job in the world to play alongside Virgil van Dijk! Virgil helped him a lot as well.
"I tried to help Ronald as well, someone who came to make us more solid defensively, and he's delivering as well. So, we are really happy to have them in our side."

Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983, and he will look to keep his positive start going against Manchester City on October 11.

aces2nwr38sc1nbmhwfl12xdl.title: Van Dijk wants Liverpool's post-Salah frontline to step up
aces2nwr38sc1nbmhwfl12xdl.subtitle: Mohamed Salah left as one of Liverpool's greats, and Virgil van Dijk hopes the club's new-look frontline can reach the Egyptian's level.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk has urged Liverpool's new frontline to keep stepping up as they continue to find their groove in the post-Mohamed Salah era.
Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season, cutting his contract short by a year, to bring down the curtain on a glittering stint at Anfield.
He scored 257 goals in 442 games for the club, with only Ian Rush (346) and Roger Hunt (285) above him in Liverpool's all-time charts.

Salah was also the 10th player to become a single club's leading all-time scorer and assister in the Premier League, with his 191 goals putting him a long way clear of second-placed Robbie Fowler (128) for the Reds.
However, Liverpool have not been crying out for Salah this season, with Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Bradley Bracola and Florian Wirtz seemingly starting to find their groove under Andoni Iraola.
They also have the impressive Rio Ngumoha, who has proven a game-changer when he has featured.
"I think it is the reality. What Mo has done for so many years as a winger, I don't think anyone can replicate that," Van Dijk said.
"Hopefully it is going to happen, but what he did was incredible. The same goes with Sadio [Mane] and Bobby [Roberto Firmino].
"Hopefully that is going to happen again, and that is what we work for, but now it is time for others, and others have to step up.
"We can always think it was better back in the day, but that is not the mentality that it should be at a club like Liverpool, and I don't feel it has ever been.
"The club will always move on at a certain point, and there are always players who will shine and perform for the club.
"It is down to these players who are here now to show it every three or four days.
"The second goal was class, but there are plenty of moments already this season that they have been very good.
"At a club like Liverpool, you have to do it every three or four days. That is always the challenge, but it is a nice challenge. I'm pretty confident that it is going to be fine."

Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Isak (six), who has scored in three consecutive appearances in the competition for the first time since January 2025 for Newcastle United (run of eight).
Isak scored in their 2-0 win over Brighton – with Barcola getting the assist – to help move Liverpool up to fourth in the table, six points behind leaders Man City.

afq0a50xqv8w1rqkhtfsr5w1q.title: Milan's hat-trick scorer Cisse owes Amorim nothing
afq0a50xqv8w1rqkhtfsr5w1q.subtitle: Alphadjo Cisse netted a hat-trick as AC Milan dispatched Salzburg 4-0 in the Europa League.
paragraphs: AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim says Alphadjo Cisse owes him nothing after the teenager's hat-trick against Salzburg.
Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory in the Europa League on Thursday, with Cisse putting them 3-0 up by the 49th minute.
Goncalo Ramos then got in on the act at Red Bull Arena, as Milan bounced back from their MD1 loss to Benfica in style.
Cisse got all four of his shots on target, and he now leads Milan's scoring charts this season, with five goals.
And Amorim says the 19-year-old is responsible for his breakthrough.
"He doesn't owe anything to me, he deserves the chances he's getting because of what he’s doing on his own," Amorim told Sky Sport Italia, as quoted by Football Italia.
"He knows how to be explosive. He has a lot of heart, but he can do better in training and in games as well. All the congratulations go to him, but he has a lot of potential and things to improve."
Milan have now won 10 of their 14 major European matches against Austrian sides (D3 L1). They also beat Salzburg 4-0 in the Champions League in 2022.
The Serie A giants were clinical, getting 10 of their 15 shots on target and creating chances worth a combined 3.38 expected goals.
But Amorim feels there is a lot for his team to work on.
"We've had more control in other games, but we managed to score goals," he said.
"We've played better in other games, but we focus too much on the result. There are things to improve, but it was a nice evening."

alu2nib5vst61p8s1rcbjfi3t.title: Carrick calls Leeds draw a step in the right direction for Man Utd
alu2nib5vst61p8s1rcbjfi3t.subtitle: Manchester United's slow start to the season continued as they drew 1-1 with Leeds United, but Michael Carrick saw plenty of positives.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick believes Sunday's draw with Leeds United was a step in the right direction for Manchester United, even with their winless streak now standing at six matches.
Bryan Mbeumo's 35th-minute opener put Carrick's men in front against their old rivals at Elland Road, but Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised early in the second half.
Leeds had the better chances to take all three points in the second period, finishing with 1.44 expected goals (xG) to the Red Devils' 0.91, but they could not find a second goal.
United are now winless in six games in all competitions, since a 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah early in September, while they have not tasted victory in five Premier League matches.

Their only victory in the league this season was at home to Ipswich Town (D4 L2), with this the fewest wins they have managed after seven games of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they also had one victory after seven matches in the old First Division.
But when asked if the performance represented a step in the right direction for United, Carrick told Sky Sports: "It definitely was. If there's any weakness, it gets found out today.
"I could feel before the game that the players were ready for it. It wasn't perfect. Our confidence isn't sky-high, but the players were trying to do the right things.
"In moments, we looked really good. We defended really well as a team. Credit to Daniel [Farke] and his team. They are a very good side.
"They test you and ask a lot of questions. If you are not ready for it, you get found out, and I thought the boys stood up to it."

Sunday's game marked the 19th instance of Man Utd scoring first in a Premier League game against Leeds but just the third occasion on which they were pegged back and failed to win, along with two more 1-1 draws in March 2001 and February 2004.
And centre-back Harry Maguire offered a more negative assessment of their display, lamenting their struggles when attempting to play through Leeds' midfield.
"We worked on it this week. We wanted to match them up without the ball and go quite aggressive," Maguire said. "It was a back five without the ball and a four with the ball.
"We knew we could get a lot of joy in the middle of the pitch with them only playing two in there.
"That's probably the area of the game where we could've done more. We could've been a bit braver with the ball and taken the ball under pressure.
"But we're in a circumstance where we are not as brave as we should be, and we have to get that back because to win games for Man Utd we have to have that bravery and composure."
Man Utd visit Cesc Fabregas' Como in the Champions League on Wednesday, with their next Premier League game pitting them against Bournemouth four days later.

amdayj0u9fm61khip38ldi6ut.title: Carrick: Man Utd must learn to 'love' pressure
amdayj0u9fm61khip38ldi6ut.subtitle: Michael Carrick has come under fire amid a stuttering start to Manchester United's season, ahead of a daunting trip to Atletico Madrid.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick says everyone at Manchester United must start viewing pressure as a privilege rather than a burden, though he admits the Red Devils have fallen well short of expectations this season.
After squandering a 1-0 lead to draw 1-1 with winless Tottenham – who were also down to 10 men – on Saturday, United have six points from as many games in the Premier League.

Their only domestic win this season came at home to promoted Ipswich Town, with their EFL Cup campaign also ending at the first hurdle as they surrendered a two-goal lead to lose to Brighton at Old Trafford.
A 4-0 thrashing of Azerbaijani champions Sabah at least gave them a winning start in the Champions League, but with a trip to Atletico Madrid to come on Tuesday, the pressure is firmly on.
United are still seeking their first win against Atletico (D2 L2) – the only side they have faced more often in major European competitions without winning is Sevilla (five – D2 L3).

Carrick's side were booed off by their own fans following the Spurs game, but he prefers to look forward and focus on their opportunity to start a Champions League campaign with back-to-back wins for just the third time in the post-Alex Ferguson era.
"Of course, we hoped for a lot more, we expected a lot more, but we are where we are," Carrick told reporters.
"I was aware there was going to be a period when it was going to become a bit more challenging, a bit stickier. That's part of it. You've got to overcome things.
"I understand that when it's not going too well, there's a real clamour and a real feeling of 'it's a disaster, it's all wrong and everything needs to be changed.'
"I get that, but that's not our mindset – or it's certainly not mine."
United previously won their first two games in the Champions League under Jose Mourinho in 2017-18, and under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2020-21.
Asked if he was starting to feel the pressure, Carrick added: "It depends on how you define pressure. We know what we want and what we're capable of doing as a team.

"We want to be part of something successful; there's no negativity about that. There's going to be times when it's a bit of a struggle, but to get anywhere, to do something good, something great, you've got to be able to do something difficult and get through it.
"I love this part. When it's going against you, you see who's really there within the group, who wants to be here for the long term.
"The supporters are desperate for it and we've got to give them something. You've got to embrace challenges to get where you want to be. I totally believe we'll come through it."

Across 132 matches in the Champions League, Atleti boss Diego Simeone has only faced one English manager previously, with his side eliminating Craig Shakespeare's Leicester City in the quarter-finals of the 2016-17 edition (won 1-0 at home, drew 1-1 away).

anil5wqtoq5a1jltql8l28jie.title: Fabian eager to follow up World Cup triumph with Nations League success
anil5wqtoq5a1jltql8l28jie.subtitle: Fabian Ruiz won the World Cup with Spain in the summer, and is now determined to progress in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Fabian Ruiz has welcomed the challenge of "winning again" as Spain prepare for their Nations League opener against England on Saturday.
Spain's clash with Thomas Tuchel's side at Wembley Stadium will be their first since defeating Argentina in the World Cup final back in July.
It marked La Roja's second triumph in the competition, while they now simultaneously hold the World Cup and the Euros, as they did from 2008 to 2012.
Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest-ever streak by a European nation.
Despite their recent success, Fabian acknowledged how difficult it will be to continue winning trophies on the international stage.
"The manager has already told us that the past is forgotten; it's history, and that's wonderful, but now it's time to focus on the present," Fabian told AS.
"The hardest thing in football is winning again. Winning once is great, but doing it again is the difficult part.

"That's the challenge we have now: to want to win again, to keep winning. It's very difficult, but this team has what it takes to do it, and we're going for this title with a lot of enthusiasm; we also consider it very important.
"We hope to be in the final four [of the Nations League]."

Spain have reached the final in three of the last four Nations League tournaments, losing on penalties in the most recent in 2024-25; excluding penalties, La Roja have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).
Luis de la Fuente's side have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
Their last away game against the Three Lions also ended 2-1, at Wembley in the Nations League in September 2018.

atijk1c41fqw1v8o4fwmj69vr.title: Tuchel: Bellingham better if he plays with a bit of rage
atijk1c41fqw1v8o4fwmj69vr.subtitle: Jude Bellingham impressed once again for England in their defeat to Spain, and Thomas Tuchel wants the midfielder to play with emotion.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel claimed "it's better" for England if Jude Bellingham "plays with a bit of rage" as he did against Spain.
Despite losing 3-2 to Spain in their Nations League opener, Bellingham impressed in midfield against the likes of Rodri and Fabian Ruiz.
As well as assisting Anthony Gordon at Wembley Stadium and winning a penalty, which Harry Kane missed, Bellingham created a match-high five chances and competed in the most duels (15).
Bellingham has been involved in nine goals in his last nine international appearances (seven goals, two assists), more than any other England player since the start of the 2026 World Cup.
The midfielder was involved in a heated exchange of words with Real Madrid team-mate Marc Cucurella during their clash with Spain, and Tuchel believes such situations can help Bellingham.
"He likes that," Tuchel said ahead of England's Nations League encounter with Czechia on Tuesday. "He gets better if that happens.
"It's better if he plays with a bit of rage. It's what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going."
And when asked about the encounter between Bellingham and Cucurella, Tuchel added: "I think he doesn't know any team-mates when he is in the national team.
"He wants to win. He doesn't know any team-mates. He is still friends with them but not for the 90 minutes."
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on their last visit to the nation in October 2019 (2-1).
Only three other teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (a run of three), France (two) and Sweden (two).

England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions, as many as in their previous 23 combined. They have not lost consecutive games since June/September 2022, also in the Nations League against Hungary and Italy.
atijk1c41fqw1v8o4fwmj69vr.html:
Thomas Tuchel claimed "it's better" for England if Jude Bellingham "plays with a bit of rage" as he did against Spain.

Despite losing 3-2 to Spain in their Nations League opener, Bellingham impressed in midfield against the likes of Rodri and Fabian Ruiz.

As well as assisting Anthony Gordon at Wembley Stadium and winning a penalty, which Harry Kane missed, Bellingham created a match-high five chances and competed in the most duels (15).

Bellingham has been involved in nine goals in his last nine international appearances (seven goals, two assists), more than any other England player since the start of the 2026 World Cup.

The midfielder was involved in a heated exchange of words with Real Madrid team-mate Marc Cucurella during their clash with Spain, and Tuchel believes such situations can help Bellingham.

"He likes that," Tuchel said ahead of England's Nations League encounter with Czechia on Tuesday. "He gets better if that happens.

"It's better if he plays with a bit of rage. It's what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going."

And when asked about the encounter between Bellingham and Cucurella, Tuchel added: "I think he doesn't know any team-mates when he is in the national team.

"He wants to win. He doesn't know any team-mates. He is still friends with them but not for the 90 minutes."

England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on their last visit to the nation in October 2019 (2-1).

Only three other teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (a run of three), France (two) and Sweden (two).

England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions, as many as in their previous 23 combined. They have not lost consecutive games since June/September 2022, also in the Nations League against Hungary and Italy.

avfjticl1eri1fmx9gjtlqwsz.title: Patience pays off for Rose after first Premier League win
avfjticl1eri1fmx9gjtlqwsz.subtitle: Bournemouth boss Marco Rose breathed a sigh of relief after recording his first Premier League victory in a 2-0 win over Sunderland.
paragraphs: Marco Rose hailed Bournemouth's patience after he snapped his wait for a first Premier League win.
Bournemouth finally got their first top-flight win of the season as they outclassed 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality Stadium.
The Cherries have lost just one of their last 15 home games across all competitions (W6 D8).

Bournemouth took a sixth-minute lead thanks to Marcus Tavernier's diving header before Kevin Danso made a Sunderland comeback difficult after receiving a straight red for bringing down Evanilson as the last man.

After Robin Roefs made a string of brilliant saves to thwart Rayan and Evanilson, it was the latter who sealed victory, intercepting Omar Alderete’s underhit back pass before rounding Sunderland's goalkeeper and slotting into an empty net.
The Cherries registered 29 shots in this contest and Rose was impressed with the way his team responded after suffering a 5-1 thrashing at the hands of Chelsea last week.
"Congrats to everyone at the club, to the lads, to our fans. They were really patient the last couple of weeks, even [though] we didn't get the points out of the game. Important win,” said Rose.
"We were quite sharp in these kinds of moments and that's why we have a clean sheet, we scored two goals and we won the game.
"We were quite dominant, we were intense. I felt even in the locker room and yesterday in training that we wanted to force this win with everything we have. It's a mentality."
Meanwhile, Regis Le Bris was left disappointed after his Sunderland side only mustered three attempts, worth a combined 0.07 expected goals.

Sunderland are now on a barren run, with the Black Cats having lost each of their last four Premier League games, their longest losing run in the competition since a five-match stint in December 2015 under Sam Allardyce.
"Tough game, disappointing game, really clear," said Le Bris.
"We were below the level, it's really clear. It's hard to take, hard to digest. It's very painful because we were not Sunderland and it's not acceptable.
"We will have ups and downs in the season, this one is a big down. I'm very disappointed for the fans.
"They were with us until the last minute, but they were not on the pitch, which is a big problem in the Premier League because the opponent is strong."

avhmd819nfm7zehpr5vff0sr.title: Carnesecchi accepts Italy role as Donnarumma's back-up
avhmd819nfm7zehpr5vff0sr.subtitle: Marco Carnesecchi has become one of Serie A's top goalkeepers in recent seasons, but he is happy to be Italy's second-choice shot-stopper.
paragraphs: Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi insisted he is "not disappointed" to be Italy's second-choice option behind Gianluigi Donnarumma.
Carnesecchi was called up by Roberto Mancini during the last international break, but he did not play any minutes as Donnarumma started all four of their Nations League matches.
After losing 2-0 to Belgium in their opening game, the Azzurri defeated Turkiye 4-1 and 3-1, either side of a draw with Zinedine Zidane's France.
Since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Mile Svilar (37) and Yann Sommer (28) have kept more clean sheets in Serie A than Carnesecchi (27).
And among goalkeepers to have faced 500+ shots in the competition in the same time frame, Carnesecchi ranks second for saves (241) and save percentage (75.5%).
When asked about his role with Italy, Carnesecchi said: "For us, Donnarumma is an added value for Italy.
"I'm not disappointed about not playing because, right now, the good of the Italian national team comes before individuals.
"Italy need to rebuild on solid foundations. We're happy to have him, and I'm pleased with what he's doing."
And when asked how he can improve his own game, the 26-year-old said: "One thing that drives me mad is dealing with high balls. I need to do more of it.
"I want to be dominant in the air too. It's true that I improved a lot last year, but I want to do more because it will pay off, with the hard work I'm putting in.
"I aspire to become one of the best, and that pushes me to keep improving. I've improved a lot with my feet and in goal, but I want to become even more dominant."
Italy will face France at home and Belgium away in the Nations League during the November international break.

azcutfhhtftd1vhx3kyvqezya.title: Rose has full belief in Bournemouth squad
azcutfhhtftd1vhx3kyvqezya.subtitle: Bournemouth are yet to win a Premier League game this season, but they have made a fine start in Europe.
paragraphs: Marco Rose has full belief in his Bournemouth side despite their poor start to the Premier League season.
Bournemouth were hammered 5-1 by Chelsea last weekend, as the Cherries' winless start under Rose in the top flight rolled on.
They sit in 18th in the Premier League, with just three points from six games.
Yet Bournemouth have made an excellent start in the Europa League, following up last month's win over Real Sociedad by beating Sturm Graz 3-0 on Thursday.
And Rose has full confidence in his squad.
"I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation," Rose told TNT Sports.
"The squad is working, everyone is keen to play, everyone deserves to play and its good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad.
"If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it's hard to beat us. That's what we should take into the next game."
Bournemouth are the first English team to win their first two matches in major European competition since Bolton Wanderers in the 2005-06 UEFA Cup.
The Cherries have lost just one of their last 14 home games in all competitions (winning five and drawing eight).
Rose's team host Sunderland on Sunday, with the Black Cats having also been involved in Europa League action this week. They beat Torreense 2-1.

b267vi5msmzf172fjr4df8dv4.title: Knowles determined not to underestimate Sporting KC
b267vi5msmzf172fjr4df8dv4.subtitle: Minnesota United still have an outside chance of reaching the MLS playoffs, but their fate is out of their own hands with three games left.
paragraphs: Cameron Knowles refused to rule Minnesota United out of the playoff race and warned there are "no easy games" ahead of hosting Sporting Kansas City in MLS.
Sporting KC are already out of the playoff picture, but Minnesota still have an outside chance of making it through to the postseason after going unbeaten in their last four outings (W1 D3).
They currently sit 13th in the Western Conference with only three games remaining and are six points behind ninth-place LA Galaxy, meaning their fate is out of their hands.
A loss could see them ruled out completely depending on results elsewhere on Wednesday, but Knowles is not ready to give up the fight just yet.
"We have to wait and see," Knowles said. "We see what the other results are, and we look at the games ahead of us, and maybe we win out.
"We don't know. There's still games to be played. So, we just have to look at the one that's in front of us and really attack it and go for the three points.
"There are no easy games, and it would be naive of us to say there is one coming up at any point."
Sporting KC sit bottom of the West with just 22 points to their name, and they are winless in their last five matches (D1 L4), including losing each of the last three.
They threw away a lead to lose 2-1 to Austin FC last time out, and head coach Raphael Wicky felt they did not deserve to walk away empty-handed.
"The creation of chances is obviously the positive thing, but at the end of the day, you have to kill these games," he said after the loss.
"You have to become a team who doesn't need five or six chances to win a game. I think that was a game we should have won with the chances we've created.
"In the end, we did not, and that's disappointing."
Minnesota United – Drake Callendar
Last time out, Minnesota kept their first clean sheet in 14 games, with Drake Callendar shutting out the Houston Dynamo's attack in a 0-0 draw.

He only had one save to make, with Houston only mustering 0.8 expected goals (xG) from their 10 attempts, but it will have been a morale-boosting clean sheet for the team, who had shipped 31 goals in the 13 games beforehand.
Sporting Kansas City – Stephen Afrifa
Stephen Afrifa netted Sporting KC's goal in their loss to Austin, netting for the fourth time this season.

He was a constant threat, having nine shots in total, the highest total for a Sporting player in a single MLS game this season, while he also topped the charts for attempts on target (four) and touches in the opposition box (12).
MATCH PREDICTION: MINNESOTA UNITED WIN
Minnesota were unbeaten in five straight MLS matches against Sporting KC (W4 D1), but they lost the most recent meeting 2-1 back in July.

The Loons' home form has been a problem throughout 2026, as they have won just 16 of the 45 points on offer to them at Allianz Field, though they did beat St. Louis City SC last time out on home soil (3-2).
The supercomputer is backing Minnesota to come out on top, given Sporting KC have endured a miserable run on the road. They have suffered 12 losses away from home in MLS, recording just three wins.

bb9mws7965rz1tzrewvuyeavl.title: New York Red Bulls 0-3 St. Louis City SC: Late show extends unbeaten streak
bb9mws7965rz1tzrewvuyeavl.subtitle: St. Louis City SC are now unbeaten in 19 straight games in all competitions after they claimed a 3-0 victory over the New York Red Bulls.
paragraphs: St. Louis City SC closed in on the Vancouver Whitecaps at the top of MLS' Western Conference with a 3-0 win over the New York Red Bulls.
In a match that was postponed from Saturday to Wednesday due to bad weather, St. Louis ultimately stormed to a victory that extends their unbeaten streak to 19 games.
Rafael Navarro finished from close range to open the scoring in the fifth minute at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
Roman Burki made a smart stop to deny Jorge Ruvalcaba, before Emil Forsberg squandered a gilt-edged chance to level the scores.
Eric Choupo-Moting saw an attempt cleared off the line, though Ethan Horvath then had to make a superb save to keep the Red Bulls in the contest.
Yet two substitutes sealed the points for St. Louis City. First, Simon Becher drilled in from the edge of the box, paving the way for Tomas Ostrak to finish off the job in stoppage time.
St. Louis City are within three points of the Whitecaps at the summit of the West, but they are one of the form teams in the competition.
That is now 17 straight MLS games without a defeat for St. Louis City, who have also scored in each of those matches.
Only two teams in MLS history have ever gone on a longer unbeaten run than this current streak managed by St. Louis City (W12 D5).
They are FC Dallas in 2010 (19 games) and the Columbus Crew in 2004 (18 matches).
Becher played a decisive role from the bench. He leads the way for goal involvements during this brilliant St. Louis run, with 10 (seven goals, three assists).

bbnzjlqmzd351cfu6080eqjoq.title: Peixoto: Wolves' Molineux form must improve after draw with Portsmouth
bbnzjlqmzd351cfu6080eqjoq.subtitle: Wolves were denied a third home league win of the season by Portsmouth's Terry Devlin, much to the disappointment of Cesar Peixoto.
paragraphs: Cesar Peixoto conceded his Wolves team need to earn more wins at home after his team squandered a lead to draw 1-1 with Portsmouth at Molineux on Tuesday.
In a game lacking quality in the final third, half-time substitute Jordan James put Wolves ahead in the 62nd minute when he fired his shot in at Nicolas Schmid's near post.
Wolves looked set for their first home league win since September 20, but Portsmouth snatched a point four minutes from time through Terry Devlin, who brilliantly volleyed home.
A win would have lifted Peixoto's side up to fifth in the Championship table and above rivals West Brom, but they now sit seventh and five adrift of leaders Swansea City.

The result was a reoccurring theme for Wolves at Molineux since dropping to the second tier. They have managed just two home wins from five so far in 2026-27 (D2 L1), and Peixoto said that had to change if they are to challenge for promotion this season.
"It's disappointing to get only one point. We need more victories at home," Peixoto told BBC Radio West Midlands.
"In the first half we have to do much more. We didn't attack the spaces. But we made two substitutes for the second half.
"We were the better team all game, but we only scored one goal, we did not get a second goal, and then we defended too deep in the last few minutes.
"I hope Adam Armstrong is fit for Saturday. Kieran Trippier felt something and I hope it is only a little injury. When we have injuries, we need to find solutions."

One positive was that Wolves did not lose successive home games in the Championship for the first time since February 2017, having lost to Bolton Wanderers 3-1 at Molineux in their last such fixture, though there was not much to get excited about here.
Wolves only mustered an expected goals (xG) total of 1.01 from their 15 shots, with only two of those on target, compared to Portsmouth's total of 0.65 from their eight attempts.
But for Portsmouth, however, they extended their unbeaten league run against Wolves to seven matches (W3 D4) since a 3-2 defeat against them back in January 2002.
Pompey have also not lost in their last three Championship outings, having played some difficult fixtures against the likes of Sheffield United and Norwich City during that run.
They moved up into 15th in the standings, and Portsmouth boss John Mousinho applauded his players for the start they have made to their campaign.
"We've played four top sides in 10 days, and with the injuries we have, then it's a great point. 15 points from the first 11 games? I'll take that," Mousinho told BBC Radio Solent.
"If you add in the fact that we were a goal down under immense pressure, then it's a brilliant result.
"Wolves' goal was a kick in the teeth, but Terry Devlin has shown us time and time again over the last few years what can happen when the ball falls to him."

beudl2re2izv12vpq9dgm6kz4.title: Gasperini: Roma feel like they dropped two points in Napoli draw
beudl2re2izv12vpq9dgm6kz4.subtitle: Roma had to come from behind twice to draw with Napoli, but Gian Piero Gasperini still felt they deserved all three points.
paragraphs: While Gian Piero Gasperini believes Roma's 3-3 draw with Napoli was a "positive confidence booster", he felt they could have won the game.

Frank Anguissa – who scored a stunning bicycle kick – and Scott McTominay had put Napoli into a 2-0 lead by the 48th minute, but Matias Soule and Leonardo Balerdi both struck in the space of five minutes to level the score by the 74th minute.
McTominay restored Napoli's lead nine minutes later, but with two minutes of the 90 remaining, Balerdi finished off his brace to ensure Roma did not walk away empty-handed.
The Argentinian is only the second defender in Roma's history to net multiple goals in a Serie A match against Napoli, after Agostini Di Bartolomei in February 1983.
Roma remain third in the Serie A table after the draw, and are four points behind leaders Lazio for the time being.

"Apart from the first half-hour, where Napoli were superior, and we struggled playing out from the back, we already started to do better towards half-time, and then in the second half it was wide open with many chances," Gasperini told DAZN Italia.
"We felt that we could win the game, so that third Napoli goal could've destroyed us, but instead, we got back on track and felt this great conviction we could bring home three points.

"The lads were not frenetic; they didn't panic; we maintained our positions and our style of football. The goals came from quality football too; we had fresh energy with Balerdi, [Nahuel] Molina and the others who came off the bench.
"We have real self-belief; we play good football, and after this game we really feel as if we've dropped two points, even though, considering we were 3-2 down, we'll take it.

bfklrj0mtfyz1eaw5sr080xon.title: Yamal feels World Cup triumph should aid Ballon d'Or bid
bfklrj0mtfyz1eaw5sr080xon.subtitle: Lamine Yamal has continued to make his case for winning the Ballon d'Or, and he feels Spain's World Cup success should be a consideration.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal believes lifting the World Cup with Spain should aid his hopes of winning the Ballon d'Or, with Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe viewed as his main rivals.

Yamal helped La Roja win their second world title in North America this year, although his individual impact at the tournament was limited after his 2025-26 season was ended prematurely by a hamstring injury.

He registered 24 goals and 17 assists in 45 outings across all competitions last season, helping Barcelona retain their LaLiga title, with his 41 combined goal involvements being the sixth-most of any player from Europe's top five leagues.
Yamal also attempted (429) and completed (225) the most dribbles of any player, while his 59 chances created following carries were also the most.
On Tuesday, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente declared one of his players should win the prize, just as Rodri did when they triumphed at Euro 2024.
And Yamal, who has not been shy about making his case as the October 26 ceremony inches closer, concurs with that view.

"It's the award for the best player of the year, a player who is different, who is a pleasure to watch play, the one who has that magic, who makes you smile, who makes you want to watch a game just for him," Yamal said in an interview with L'Equipe.
"I think my way of playing is my strongest argument and what makes me different.
"It's very important, in addition to being a good player, that you make your team win.
"The advantage I have is that I have been able to win the World Cup this year and, obviously, that is a plus for me.
"But if a person says, 'Lionel Messi deserves it' or 'Rodri deserves it', that's totally respectable."
Having come through the ranks at Barca, Yamal has faced plenty of comparisons to Messi, who he outshone in the World Cup final as Spain edged out Argentina in extra time.
But the 19-year-old wants to be remembered on his own terms, saying: "I play to make history, so that in 30 years' time, young people will say, 'he was really very good too'.
"But I don't want to compare myself to anyone. I want to be Lamine Yamal, I want to be remembered as Lamine Yamal, and I hope to be among the greats."

Yamal will be in action for Spain on Saturday, as they go to Wembley to face England in their opening Nations League fixture, defending a 38-game unbeaten run (W29 D9), which is the longest ever streak by a European nation.

bhh5cf70r3o61gj47k7td791s.title: Czechia clash too early to be a 'must-win' game for England, says Tuchel
bhh5cf70r3o61gj47k7td791s.subtitle: England and Czechia face off in their quest for a first Nations League win on Tuesday, but Thomas Tuchel said victory was not a must.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel believes it is too early to label England's Nations League clash against Czechia as a "must-win" game following their defeat to Spain.
England make the trip to Fortuna Arena on Tuesday, aiming to get their Nations League campaign back on track after they were beaten 3-2 by Luis de la Fuente's side.
The result saw the Three Lions lose a match they led at half-time for the first time since June 2019, which also came in the Nations League against the Netherlands.

It will be England's first away game against Czechia since October 2019 – a 2-1 defeat in a European Championship qualifier. Only Spain (a run of three), France and Sweden (both two) have won consecutive matches against the Three Lions this century.
England come into the game having conceded 13 goals in their last six games, almost double the amount they had in their first 17 matches under Tuchel (seven).

Following their meeting with Czechia, England travel to Croatia before facing Santi Denia's side again at Wembley Stadium on October 6, though Tuchel believes that failure to win the first clash was not the end of the world for his team.
"It's a bit early for must-win. I know what you mean, but it is a bit early in the group for a must-win," Tuchel told reporters.
"We always arrive and prepare the team with a target to win. It was the target against Spain, and it is the same [against Czechia].
"We respect the quality and the challenge it brings. You play in Prague against Czechia; it is difficult. There will be support for the home team.
"We always prepare for the win; we want the win. It is too early to speak for a must. It would be ideal. The problem is the opponent on the other side."
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2), though it was on their last visit to the nation in October 2019 (1-2).
But Czechia are another team who are looking to get their Nations League campaign up and running after they were beaten 2-1 by Croatia in their opening match.
Czechia have lost their last two games in all competitions, last losing more consecutively between June and September 2022 (four), but Tuchel is expecting a tough test.
"We only analysed one game from the Czech team, as they have a new coach," Tuchel added. We saw a flexible midfield of three. A lot of changes in position.
"Wingers, attacking full-backs and a team that was well-organised. Full of motivation to take their chance, that is what we saw.
"I feel I always need a result; you always need a result in football to get confidence, to get the support and belief.
"Especially after a defeat. If everyone in the camp truly believes, even then you still need it for yourself. The best reaction is if you can prove it in a result."
Tuchel also refused to rule out Nico O'Reilly and Ezri Konsa from playing against Czechia after the pair missed training because of minor injuries.
"I am not sure yet [will they play]. They missed training because of minor issues, but they are still issues," Tuchel said.
"They need to be assessed, and we will see [on Tuesday]."
