blzjyjvf6m8e19peb688fslxv.title: Rayan targets Brazil improvement after snatching late draw against Australia
blzjyjvf6m8e19peb688fslxv.subtitle: Brazil avoided a scare against Australia in their first friendly of the international break, with Rayan's last-gasp goal salvaging a draw.
paragraphs: Rayan says Brazil know they must improve after his late goal snatched a draw with Australia in a friendly in Queensland.
Australia looked set to claim a famous victory over the Selecao, but instead Brazil earned a 1-1 draw.
Nestory Irankunda gave Australia the lead midway through the second half with a stunning free-kick, but Rayan's powerful header from Raphinha's corner ultimately pulled Brazil back into the match.
Brazil also had a goal ruled out by VAR on the stroke of half-time, as Bruno Guimaraes was deemed to have fouled Harry Souttar in the build-up to Estevao slotting home.
It was a new-look side for Carlo Ancelotti, who opted against picking his old guard following their World Cup exit.
Rayan believes it was a fair result in the end, though, and is determined to make sure Brazil end up on the winning side when they face off for the second time on Tuesday.
"We don't step onto the field to lose; we step onto the field to win," Rayan told Sportv.
"But it wasn't possible. Although we have another chance against them and we'll go for the win.
"We know that we have to improve our defensive side. We also knew how to play, but we know that we have to improve."

Brazil will feel they deserved not to walk away as the losing side, given they finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.2 from their 16 shots to their opponents' tally of 0.5 from their seven attempts.
While Brazil's superstars failed to hit the heights they have often shown in the past, Irankunda caught the eye of both coaches, with Ancelotti heaping high praise on him.
"We knew this, fantastic player," Ancelotti said.
"We watch a player with a lot of talent who is doing very well in Europe. We knew this kind of situation on set pieces, but his shot… fantastic."
And Australia head coach Tony Popovic was equally as complimentary of the 20-year-old, who he believes has benefited hugely from his move to Sporting CP from Watford.
"Nestory knows what we think of him. He's 20 years old. He started three games at a World Cup, played half a game in the other, and he's moved to a bigger club," Popovic said.
"There's a clear difference in Nestory already. He's matured so quickly in a short space of time in terms of what's expected at Sporting.
"What he's learning is that the transfer is one part. Now you go to a new club. They don't give you minutes, they don't guarantee you minutes, they give you nothing. You have to earn everything.
"So, he delivered, played very well, and he'll only get better. He's a young kid. I expect by the next World Cup, hopefully, he gets a lot of minutes at a bigger club; there'll be a big improvement.
"But yeah, just a wonderful person. Nothing's changed for us in how we feel about him and how we are together."

bv28u61uw71j1fkrgeps3xmg3.title: Foster 'a piece in the puzzle' as he targets silverware with Houston
bv28u61uw71j1fkrgeps3xmg3.subtitle: Houston Dynamo are looking to get their playoff push back on track against Minnesota United, who are also struggling for form in MLS.
paragraphs: Lyle Foster has his eyes on silverware with the Houston Dynamo, who continue their push for a top-four spot in the Western Conference against Minnesota United.

Houston's form has slipped in recent weeks, and they currently sit fifth in the West, though they are only six points behind the leaders, the Vancouver Whitecaps, and one off the fourth-place San Jose Earthquakes.
The Dynamo have won just one of their last seven games (D3 L3), and are winless in their last three, including a 2-0 loss to Sporting Kansas City.
However, Foster, who joined in the recent transfer window, believes Houston have the quality to be challenging for the MLS Cup and is determined to do his part to help them.
"I saw where they were in the table. Immediately you think the guys are doing this; why is there no reason that we can go all the way?" Foster said in an interview with Houston's media team.
"But obviously, we take it a training session at a time, with the way that we've been playing.
"The qualities I believe I have, I believe that I can just be a piece of a puzzle that fits into the team and hopefully try our best to bring [a title] to the H."
Minnesota, meanwhile, are 14th in the West with 29 points, seven points behind the LA Galaxy in the final wildcard spot.
They are currently winless in their last six games – losing each of the last five – and conceding 20 goals during those six outings.
Head coach Cameron Knowles acknowledged their defensive record as the major worry and noted it is something they have worked on during the international break.
"We've conceded too many goals in recent games," Knowles said. "The guys have put in a really good shift over last week and into this week."
Minnesota United – Kelvin Yeboah
Yeboah has scored in three straight regular-season home matches.
Only three Loons players have scored in more consecutive home league matches: Darwin Quintero (five – 2018), Christian Ramirez (four – 2017) and Robin Lod (four – 2021).
Houston Dynamo – Jonathan Bond
Bond has kept 10 clean sheets so far this season.
He is the fourth goalkeeper in Dynamo history to record double-digit clean sheets in a single campaign and the first since Steve Clark in 2023, when he matched Tally Hall's club record with 12.
MATCH PREDICTION: MINNESOTA UNITED WIN

Minnesota and Houston split the series in 2025, with each team posting a victory by two goals. There have never been three straight matches decided by multiple goals in the fixture's history across all competitions.

Minnesota have scored in each of their last 10 regular-season matches, their longest streak of games with a goal since a 12-game stretch from June to September in 2024. The Loons are one of five MLS teams currently on a streak of double-digit regular-season matches with a goal.

As for the Dynamo, since the end of the World Cup break, they have conceded the fewest league goals (nine) of any MLS team while being tied for the most shutouts (seven, with Nashville SC). For comparison, Minnesota have allowed 27 goals and kept one clean sheet in that time.
Minnesota United – 44.3%
Houston Dynamo – 28.9%

bv9wbwe9i5bl14wrpiww4bins.title: Brighton 5-0 Crystal Palace: Gomez stunner headlines five-star rout
bv9wbwe9i5bl14wrpiww4bins.subtitle: Diego Gomez netted a goal-of-the-season contender as Brighton cruised to a dominant 5-0 win over rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday.
paragraphs: Brighton secured their fourth straight Premier League win with a dominant 5-0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium, where Diego Gomez scored a screamer.

Fabian Hurzeler's side wasted little time asserting their dominance in the pouring rain, taking the lead inside four minutes as Jaydee Canvot inadvertently diverted Pascal Gross' low, near-post cross into his own net.

Matters quickly unravelled further for Palace as Gomez produced a moment of brilliance less than three minutes later. Spotting Walter Benitez stranded off his line, the midfielder fired off a spectacular piledriver from the halfway line that soared into the net.
Yasin Ayari piled more misery on Palace in the 10th minute as he was picked out keenly by Charalampos Kostoulas' exquisite backheel before bundling home a low effort off Canvot's legs.

Any hopes of a Palace fightback were swiftly extinguished as Brighton struck again after the interval, with Kostoulas reacting quickest to a fortunate deflection off Ayari's effort to slide home from point-blank range.

Palace spurned two golden opportunities to reduce the deficit in the second half, with Jean-Philippe Mateta crashing an unchallenged effort against the crossbar, while Jefferson Lerma could only flick Adam Wharton's cross onto the outside of the post.
Brighton had the final say as Luka Vuskovic calmly nodded a deep cross back into the danger area, allowing Jack Hinshelwood to poke past Benitez from a yard out and complete the rout.
Gomez finds his range in Brighton blitz
The Seagulls had come into Sunday's clash in fantastic form, but even Hurzeler must have been surprised by just how quickly his team asserted their dominance.

Brighton raced into a three-goal lead after nine minutes and 30 seconds – the earliest any Premier League side has scored three since Newcastle United put three past Tottenham inside eight minutes and 12 seconds in April 2023.
Indeed, Brighton became just the ninth side in Premier League history to score three goals inside the opening 10 minutes of a match, and the first since Newcastle against Tottenham.
Gomez, meanwhile, will deservedly grab all headlines for his stunning effort from the halfway line.
The Paraguay international found the net from 51.3 metres out, the longest-range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 57.7 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

Brighton's attacking prowess has been evident throughout the season, with only three teams in Premier League history scoring more goals in their opening seven matches than the Seagulls' 23 this season: Arsenal in 2009-10 (24), Manchester United in 2011-12 (24) and Manchester City in 2019-20 (27).

The Seagulls have now won four consecutive league matches by an aggregate score of 15-0, while they comfortably outperformed their 1.98 expected goals (xG) against Palace, who generated just 0.75 xG in response.

Brighton had the final say as Luka Vuskovic calmly nodded a deep cross back into the danger area, allowing Jack Hinshelwood to poke past Benitez from a yard out and complete the rout. 

Gomez finds his range in Brighton blitz

The Seagulls had come into Sunday's clash in fantastic form, but even Hurzeler must have been surprised by just how quickly his team asserted their dominance.

Brighton raced into a three-goal lead after nine minutes and 30 seconds – the earliest any Premier League side has scored three since Newcastle United put three past Tottenham inside eight minutes and 12 seconds in April 2023. 

Indeed, Brighton became just the ninth side in Premier League history to score three goals inside the opening 10 minutes of a match, and the first since Newcastle against Tottenham. 

Gomez, meanwhile, will deservedly grab all headlines for his stunning effort from the halfway line.

The Paraguay international found the net from 51.3 metres out, the longest-range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 57.7 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017. 

Brighton's attacking prowess has been evident throughout the season, with only three teams in Premier League history scoring more goals in their opening seven matches than the Seagulls' 23 this season: Arsenal in 2009-10 (24), Manchester United in 2011-12 (24) and Manchester City in 2019-20 (27). 

The Seagulls have now won four consecutive league matches by an aggregate score of 15-0, while they comfortably outperformed their 1.98 expected goals (xG) against Palace, who generated just 0.75 xG in response.

bwuwiz16ykez17jp2kafh0xdu.title: Cincinnati ended winless run at 'a very important time', says Noonan
bwuwiz16ykez17jp2kafh0xdu.subtitle: FC Cincinnati ended a six-game winless run last time out as they look to hold onto their postseason spot in the MLS' Eastern Conference.
paragraphs: FC Cincinnati head coach Pat Noonan believes his side ended their winless MLS run "at a very important time", as they now prepare to take on the New England Revolution.
After a run of six games with a victory (D3 L3), Cincinnati defeated Atlanta United 3-1 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Kevin Denkey scored twice for The Orange and Blue in the second half, while Tom Barlow also got on the scoresheet to help secure all three points.
Cincinnati are ninth in the Eastern Conference with seven regular-season games remaining, five of which come at home.
"It came at a very important time, and hopefully it's a win that can help propel us to a good stretch here, but I'm pleased for the guys, that they get to experience a win," said Noonan.
"There are a lot of factors that make it feel special. It might be drastic, but it was important.

"It's about winning on the road, which we haven't done consistently, beating an Atlanta team that's right behind us in the table and got a lot of new pieces and you can tell are improving considerably with Tata [Martino] in what they're doing now, and so they're a very difficult opponent for us at this moment.
"So I'm pleased about that. I'm pleased that defensively things are looking better."
New England, meanwhile, are fourth in the East and just three points behind second-place Inter Miami.
The Revs, however, fell to a 3-0 defeat at home against the Seattle Sounders last time out.

Denkey's brace against Atlanta took his goal tally in MLS this season to 16, the sixth-most of any player in the league.
In addition to his goals, he also led his team-mates for shots (six), touches in the box (11), and duels won (7/11), while also completing 100% of his dribbles (3/3).
New England Revolution – Peyton Miller
Miller failed to find the back of the net against Seattle after scoring three times in New England's prior two games before the international break.
He recorded five shots against Seattle, the most of any Revs player, hitting the target with four of those attempts and racking up 0.38 expected goals (xG).

Cincinnati have the seventh-best home record in the Eastern Conference this season, picking up 24 points from 12 matches at TQL Stadium in 2026.
The Orange and Blue are unbeaten in all five of their home MLS matches since returning from the World Cup break (W3 D2), drawing 3-3 with Charlotte FC in their last such fixture.
New England, meanwhile, have lost both of their last two matches by a 3-0 scoreline, after a run of three consecutive wins in the league.
Nevertheless, when the two sides met back in March, the Revs thrashed Cincinnati 6-1 at Gillette Stadium.
FC Cincinnati – 50.1%

byqjsyt2cbsk14ga5q47tn1mh.title: Reus urges LA Galaxy to 'stick to the plan' in playoff push
byqjsyt2cbsk14ga5q47tn1mh.subtitle: The LA Galaxy are in a strong position to qualify for the MLS playoffs, with San Diego FC, who are also aiming for the postseason, up next.
paragraphs: Marco Reus has urged the LA Galaxy to "stick to the plan" as they continue their push for a playoff spot against San Diego FC in MLS.
The Galaxy currently sit eighth in the Western Conference – occupying one of the wildcard spots – and are just two points behind the seventh-place Seattle Sounders.
Greg Vanney's side have lost just one of their last five league outings (W3 D1) and bounced back from a thumping 6-2 loss to St. Louis City SC by beating Portland Timbers 2-0.
The composed victory after such a heavy defeat means the Galaxy remain in charge of their own playoff destiny, and Reus is determined to avoid any more major setbacks.
"The focus is clear," Reus said. "Everybody can see the table.

"We, as a team, we're really honest to each other every day, and it's just about really every day to put the work in, to stick together, stick to the plan, and just getting better every day, and then at the end you get a result."
As for San Diego, they are currently without a win in their last seven league games (D3 L4), though they did come from behind to snatch a late 3-3 draw with the Houston Dynamo.
It is a result that leaves them 12th in the West, five points behind the playoff places, and head coach Mikey Varas wants to see more consistency.
"Very disappointed that we're not winning games because we feel that we've had spells of football that could win games," he said after the draw with Houston.
"But at the same time, we'll get our heads up in terms of motivation to make that next step. It just hasn't happened yet.
"We've just got to keep investing in ourselves and investing in that intention to find that moment that it clicks. And we need to be more consistent over the course of 90 minutes."
LA Galaxy – Marco Reus
Marco Reus had a goal and an assist in the Galaxy's win over Portland, taking him to 36 goal contributions (22 goals, 14 assists) in 55 regular-season matches.
It is more than any other player for the Galaxy since he made his debut with the club in September 2024 (Gabriel Pec – 35).
San Diego FC – Anders Dreyer
Anders Dreyer scored from the penalty spot for San Diego on Wednesday, his fourth straight match with a goal involvement.
He has contributed to at least one goal in 39 of his 62 career regular-season appearances.
MATCH PREDICTION: LA GALAXY WIN
San Diego won each of their first three meetings with the Galaxy, outscoring them 7-2 in those matches.
The Galaxy are the only Western Conference opponent that San Diego has a 100% record against in regular-season play.

However, San Diego won 13 of their first 20 away matches in all competitions from when the club joined MLS in 2025 to early March this year. Since then, they have just one win in 15 on the road in all competitions (D5 L9), including going winless in five straight on the road (D2 L3).
The Galaxy have won three of their last four regular-season matches. They have not kept consecutive regular-season clean sheets in over two years, since a run of three in a row in June 2024.

byuabj05c6b31trebts7mifbh.title: Xavi seeks more improvement after first win as Netherlands boss
byuabj05c6b31trebts7mifbh.subtitle: The Netherlands defeated Serbia 2-1 in the Nations League on Sunday to earn Xavi his first win as head coach.
paragraphs: Xavi believes the Netherlands "have to play better" despite their victory over Serbia in the Nations League on Sunday.
Mexx Meerdink scored twice as the Netherlands won 2-1 at Stadion Rajko Mitic, seeing Xavi pick up his first win since taking over from Ronald Koeman.

It was a dominant display from Xavi's side, who created 2.74 expected goals (xG) from 25 shots while restricting Serbia to 1.32 from 11 attempts, with the visitors also creating six Opta-defined big chances.
Meerdink impressed in just his second appearance for the Netherlands, while Joey Veerman controlled proceedings from midfield.

Veerman led the match in touches (135), passes (117 – level with Jan Paul van Hecke) and chances created (five), while also leading his team-mates in interceptions (three) and winning six of his nine duels.
Xavi drew plenty of positives from his maiden victory at the helm, but knows there is still plenty to improve upon.
"We have to be honest: we have to play better," said the Spaniard.
"But there were good things and I'm happy with the attitude and the effort.
"We dominated and created more chances than them. We maintained our positions, we were organised, and thanks to that we were able to make better use of the spaces."
There was a concern, however, for both Xavi and Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola after Cody Gakpo was forced off with an ankle injury in the first half.

As well as scoring a late equaliser in the Netherlands' 1-1 draw with Germany in Xavi's first match in charge, Gakpo also leads Liverpool players in direct goal involvements this season (six – two goals, four assists).
When asked if Gakpo's injury was serious, Xavi responded: "I don’t think so.
"It's his ankle, that's all I know. Tomorrow [Monday] we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

c0hd9l7b83ij1qbud2sl1i05q.title: Ipswich Town 1-1 Nottingham Forest: Glasner's wasteful side settle for a point
c0hd9l7b83ij1qbud2sl1i05q.subtitle: Nottingham Forest missed a host of chances to earn a win at Portman Road, with Ipswich Town digging in to earn a point.
paragraphs: Nottingham Forest could not turn their late pressure into the winner as they had to settle for a 1-1 draw with Ipswich Town in the Premier League.

Neco Williams gave Forest an early lead which Julio Enciso cancelled out before the break, but despite numerous chances in the second half, Oliver Glasner's side had to settle for a share of the spoils.
Forest were on the front foot at the start, with Jair Cunha setting himself up on the spin from a Nikola Milenkovic nod down, but his volley was straight at Christian Walton.

Former Ipswich man Liam Delap then sliced wide before playing his part in the 13th-minute opener, holding play up well for Daniel Munoz to clip in a cross for Williams, who turned past Walton with a fine first-time finish on his 150th Premier League appearance.
Jaden Philogene and Enciso both tested Matz Sels at the other end before Morgan Gibbs-White slid in to meet Dan Ndoye's delivery, but Leif Davis reacted brilliantly to hook it off the line.
And Forest's missed chances were punished in the 41st minute as Milenkovic took a poor touch and then played a loose backpass, which was pounced on by Enciso, who coolly slotted past Sels one-on-one.

Just three minutes after the break, Ipswich were given a worry when VAR looked at a late tackle from Issa Diop on James McAtee, but he was only given a booking, with the challenge not deemed to be denying a goalscoring opportunity due to the midfielder taking a touch away from goal.
Forest turned up the pressure once more, with Walton pushing away Murillo's dipping volley before then nodding wide from the next corner.
An unmarked Ndoye arguably should have restored Forest's lead in the 64th minute, but Davis was once again well positioned to clear the poked effort off the line.
Delap and Callum Hudson-Odoi both fired wide as late chances went begging, while Jack Clarke also failed to hit the target at the other end when Ipswich tried to snatch a win at the death.
Forest's profligacy proves costly

Forest's struggles in attack have been well-documented this season, and they once again struggled to build on an early lead, despite some great openings throughout the game, even after they were pegged back.
Despite now scoring the joint-fewest goals in the Premier League (six), Forest rank second for shots attempted in the competition (137 – 17 against Ipswich).

However, their profligacy was not helped by an error just before the break; since the start of last season in the Premier League, Jan Paul van Hecke (four) is the only outfield player to commit more errors leading to goals than Milenkovic (three).
But the points were there for the taking after the break, and Forest had 11 shots in the second half to Ipswich's one, though they only managed to get one of those on target.

The Tricky Trees have now dropped seven points from winning positions in the Premier League this term, the fourth-most of any side, and only one fewer than they lost in the whole of last season (eight).

Ipswich, by contrast, continued their fine start to life back in the top-flight; they have now gained more points from losing positions than any other side in the competition (seven), while they have hit double figures for points after eight games (10).
Indeed, they now have as many points at Portman Road in the Premier League this season as they managed in the entirety of their previous campaign (seven in 2024-25).

c1nvus18key19tk11fokigd3.title: Chivu puts Thuram's 'devastating' form down to France omission
c1nvus18key19tk11fokigd3.subtitle: Marcus Thuram is in fine form for Scudetto holders Inter, but Cristian Chivu does not believe his own coaching has made the difference.
paragraphs: Cristian Chivu has refused to take personal credit for Marcus Thuram's "devastating" recent form, saying the forward has shown extra motivation since he was omitted from the France squad.
Thuram scored a 91st-minute equaliser as Inter fought back to beat Fiorentina 2-1 in Serie A on Sunday, with Piotr Zielinski's penalty eight minutes into stoppage time proving decisive.
He has now scored five times in Serie A this campaign, with each of those goals coming in his last six appearances.
Since the start of September, he has only failed to find the net in a 2-2 draw with Roma.
Thuram's form has helped Inter gain 22 points from their first eight games of the campaign.
Should they beat Venezia on Wednesday, they will set a new club record for their best start through nine matchdays in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95), with 25.
And Chivu quipped that being left out of Zinedine Zidane's first France squad had done as much for Thuram's form as his own coaching.
"I don't know if it's my merit or Zidane's. Without Lautaro Martinez, he took on the responsibility," Chivu said as he reflected on Sunday's fightback against Fiorentina.
"I was with him for three weeks and he had a rest, which is why I said I don't know if it's my merit or Zidane's.
"He would even sprint in the 90th minute, entering the penalty area with devastating ferocity. When he attacks you with that speed, there's a risk that something will happen.
"We're happy; we gave him a day off. Not being called up gave him extra motivation."
While Inter are battling at the summit, Venezia are bottom of the pile with just three points on the board, achieving one win and losing their other seven matches in 2026-27.
Venezia – Filip Stankovic
Only Marco Carnesecchi (37) has made more saves than Stankovic (36) among goalkeepers in Serie A this season.
More specifically, Stankovic has made the most saves from opposition shots attempted from inside the box (26).
Inter – Marcus Thuram
Thuram has been involved in a goal in each of his last six Serie A appearances (five goals and two assists in this period).
The Frenchman could be involved in a goal in seven straight games for the first time in his career in Europe's big five leagues (also six in a row between last April and May).
MATCH PREDICTION: INTER WIN
Inter have remained unbeaten in 47 of their last 48 Serie A matches against newly promoted sides (W40 D7), winning their last eight such games in a row.
The Nerazzurri's only such defeat in this period was on April 15, 2023 against Monza (0-1).
Inter have also won their last four Serie A matches against Venezia and have only once recorded five consecutive top-flight victories against them, doing so between November 1962 and January 1999.
Their last four away Serie A games against promoted teams, meanwhile, have all been victories to nil – by an aggregate score of 11-0.
Inter are clear favourites with the Opta supercomputer, though things have not always been smooth for Chivu's men this campaign.

Inter have gained 13 points from losing positions in Serie A this season, at least five more than any other side in one of Europe's top five leagues and the most by any team in the first eight matchdays of a Serie A season in the last 20 years.

c50g0doseq1s19o515ehjlwok.title: Salzburg 0-4 AC Milan: Hat-trick hero Cisse stars in Europa League win
c50g0doseq1s19o515ehjlwok.subtitle: Alphadjo Cisse made European history on Thursday as his stunning hat-trick helped AC Milan breeze past Salzburg in the Europa League.
paragraphs: AC Milan got their Europa League campaign up and running in style as a hat-trick from Alphadjo Cisse earned a 4-0 win over Salzburg to ease the pressure on Ruben Amorim.
Cisse, and Goncalo Ramos' 72nd-minute strike, had Milan cruising before Filippo Terracciano was sent off late on, with the Serie A giants seeing out the closing stages comfortably.
Christian Zawieschitzky was on hand to jump at the feet of Cisse before Omari Hutchinson curled over the Salzburg crossbar as Milan aimed to stamp their authority early on.
And Amorim's side did just that in the 15th minute through Cisse, who guided a bullet header from Hutchinson's cross past Zawieschitzky and into the bottom-right corner.

Ruben Loftus-Cheek then saw his shot smothered by the Salzburg goalkeeper, with Hutchinson's effort on the rebound cleared off the line by Kevin Boma, before Haris Tabakovic then saw a goal ruled out at the other end after Leandro Morgalla failed to keep the ball in play.

Milan went on to double their lead just after the half-hour mark, with Cisse in the right place at the right time to steer Davide Bartesaghi's first-time cross into the net after the full-back was brilliantly picked out by Adrien Rabiot's pinpoint loft over the top.

Rabiot was involved again for Milan's third goal four minutes after the restart, with his delivery across the six-yard box helped in by Cisse, whose hat-trick goal was confirmed after a lengthy VAR check against the Rossoneri youngster.
Salzburg attempted to get back into the game, but Milan's quality in attack proved too strong, with Hutchinson denied a goal his performance merited by the feet of Zawieschitzky.
Milan put the result beyond doubt when Bartosz Mazurek's loose touch allowed Ardon Jashari to pounce, with the ball breaking for Ramos, who finished coolly into the net.

The visitors were, however, forced to see out the final seven minutes with a man less after Terracciano was penalised for a last-man foul with a shove on the edge of the box on Dominik Schmid, but the damage had already been done.
Cisse makes European history in much-needed win

After losing their Europa League opener against Benfica, coupled with three draws in their last four Serie A outings, the pressure was on Amorim to deliver a positive result in Austria, and the Milan boss had a talented teenager in Cisse to thank.

At the age of 19 years and 358 days, Cisse became the youngest Italian player in the history of the major European competitions to have scored three or more goals in a single match, while his first-half brace saw him become the youngest player in Milan history to score multiple goals in a single half in one of Europe's major competitions.

Milan have won 10 of their 14 major European matches against Austrian sides (D3 L1), with this result a morale-boosting one ahead of this weekend's Serie A clash with Atalanta, with their next Europa League clash seeing them face Premier League side Bournemouth.

Salzburg, meanwhile, saw their struggles against Milan continue. They have failed to win in their last five major European encounters against them (D1 L4), and Danny Rohl's side were comfortably second best at Red Bull Arena on Thursday.

Milan finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 3.99 from their 15 shots, 10 of which were on target, compared to Salzburg's tally of 0.79 from their 14 attempts, though only two of those forced Mike Maignan into action.

c9phospand8315zrml1m0squg.title: Richter predicts Sullivan will only get better for Philadelphia
c9phospand8315zrml1m0squg.subtitle: Cavan Sullivan has lit up MLS in 2026, and he will be looking to make an impact for Philadelphia Union against New England Revolution.
paragraphs: Philadelphia Union head coach Ryan Richter believes there is still more to come from Cavan Sullivan following his stellar breakout campaign.
The 17-year-old has been a revelation for the Union and has netted seven goals as well as providing 11 assists in 2026, putting him in the spotlight.
This week, he topped the MLS' 22 Under 22 ranking, becoming the youngest winner of the award, breaking Alphonso Davies' (17 years 255 days) record by some way (17y 22d).
Richter, who took over at Philadelphia in May, knew Sullivan from earlier in his career, and he has been impressed by his development, but remains confident he has more levels to reach.
"He's different than anything I've seen over the last 10 years working in this club and first team level, academy level, second team level; he's different," Richter told GOAL.
"But no one can predict that he was going to have even just the production overall.
"I'm happy for him, proud of him, but he needs to keep his head down. And he will because he has big goals and he's a driven kid.
"But we need to keep him going and pushing for more, keep getting better, keep impacting games more, and let's see what we can do."
Next up for Philadelphia, who are sixth in the Eastern Conference and on a 15-game unbeaten streak, are the New England Revolution, who are flying high in third.
After back-to-back losses on either side of the international break, the Revs have responded with consecutive wins, edging past the Chicago Fire 1-0 last time out.
Carles Gil has led their playoff charge this term, setting up the winner in that game, and he is keen to keep their winning run going.

"The most important thing is to win," Gil said. "It's difficult, because we start the [regular] season and there are 30 teams looking for that, to win [MLS Cup], and just one can do it so it's difficult.
"We need to continue step-by-step. The most important thing in the beginning was to be competitive, and for sure we are right now.
"Like I said, continue. I think, first try to be in the best place possible. Hopefully, we can play the games in the playoffs at home and then try to win."
Philadelphia Union – Cavan Sullivan
Sullivan did not get on the scoresheet in the draw with Charlotte, but he still led Philadelphia's attack with a game-high five shots and 11 touches in the opposition box.
He also created two chances for his team-mates and had the second-most touches (61), but he will be determined to hit the back of the net to add to his seven MLS goals against New England.
New England Revolution – Matt Polster
Matt Polster scored his second goal of the campaign to help New England to victory over Chicago, netting with his only shot of the game.
However, the midfielder was also influential in breaking up and linking the play, winning possession back seven times (a team high) and playing 10 crosses, with only Carles Gil (23) attempting more.
MATCH PREDICTION: PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN
Philadelphia were on a six-match winning run against New England in MLS, but the Revs snapped that streak with a 2-1 victory back in May.
On home soil this season, the Union have secured 26 points from a possible 45 on offer in 15 MLS contests and are unbeaten in their last 12 matches at Subaru Park (W7 D5).

New England have six wins, two draws, and seven losses on their travels this season in league matches, but they have won three of their last four such matches, meaning Philadelphia will be given a tough test.
Philadelphia Union – 57.2%
New England Revolution – 20.6%

cfj0jdvhsdcw17mwti4ku8wmu.title: Cucurella: Spain and Real Madrid situations not comparable
cfj0jdvhsdcw17mwti4ku8wmu.subtitle: Marc Cucurella is enjoying plenty of success with Spain, and he hopes to do the same at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho.
paragraphs: Marc Cucurella does not believe it is fair to compare the situations of Spain and Real Madrid, with the latter in a different "process".
Spain are flying under Luis De la Fuente, adding the World Cup to their cabinet after already winning the European Championships in 2024.
La Roja are unbeaten in their last 40 games across all competitions (W31 D9), while their current nine-match winning run is their joint-best under De la Fuente.
Madrid, meanwhile, are fourth in LaLiga and six points behind leaders Barcelona after seven games, with Jose Mourinho returning to the helm this summer.
Cucurella insisted it is too early to judge Real Madrid's season, insisting they need time to improve under Mourinho.
"Everything is a process. We've been together here for a long time, and we have to accept that we're in a process at Real Madrid," said Cucurella.
"We started with a new coach. The beginning may not have been what we expected, but this is a process, and we'll have to assess everything at the end of the season."
Spain continue their Nations League campaign with a trip to Czechia on Saturday.
La Roja are currently top of Group A3 after a 3-2 win over England and 4-1 victory over Croatia last time out.
De la Fuente will be without both Ferran Torres and Nico Williams due to injury, while Alejandro Grimaldo and Eric Garcia pulled out of the squad earlier in the extended break.
Playing a total of four matches during this extended international break, De la Fuente feels injuries were inevitable.
"The drawback of this format is that it's difficult to recover," said De la Fuente.
"We always prioritise the players' health and want everyone to be in perfect condition. Because there's no time to recover."

cgf1xyl6s8er1209uhspvqfao.title: Adams urges Bournemouth to carry Europa League momentum into Sunderland clash
cgf1xyl6s8er1209uhspvqfao.subtitle: Bournemouth have made a fine start to their Europa League campaign, but Marco Rose's team are without a win in the Premier League.
paragraphs: Bournemouth must carry the positive momentum from their winning start in Europe into their Premier League meeting with Sunderland, so says Tyler Adams.
The Cherries have won both of their Europa League fixtures in what is their first-ever continental campaign.
Yet they have not won any of their opening six Premier League games in 2026-27, leaving them in the bottom three ahead of welcoming Sunderland to the Vitality Stadium on Sunday.

Bournemouth, who lost 5-1 at Chelsea last weekend, are eight points worse off than they were at this stage last season when they had 11. Sunderland, meanwhile, are seven worse off now (four points) than at this stage in 2025-26 (11).
And Adams has urged Bournemouth to put that right.
"In the beginning, we had some performances where we were saying we were playing well but not getting results," he said.
"That can only happen for so long. Sometimes having a result like Chelsea is the wake-up call that you need.
"You can be playing as good football as you want, but if you're not getting three points at the end of it, what does that really mean?
"We had a moment of reflection and talked as a team about how you have to do everything it takes to win.
"I think the reaction was what we needed against Sturm Graz, but now we need to carry that momentum into the weekend."
Sunderland were also involved in Europa League action on Thursday, as the Black Cats beat Torreense 2-1.
Bournemouth - Evanilson
Evanilson has been involved in 57% of Bournemouth’s Premier League goals this season (one goal, three assists).

However, he has only ended on the winning side in seven of the 21 games he has scored or assisted in (33%), the lowest ratio of any of the 736 players to score or assist in 20+ games in Premier League history.
Sunderland - Robin Roefs

In the Premier League this season, the two goalkeepers with the worst goals prevented differential are Sunderland's Robin Roefs (-3.77, 12 conceded from 8.23 xGoT) and Bournemouth's Djordje Petrovic (-3.71, 13 conceded from 9.29 xGoT).
Roefs was a star of the season last term for Sunderland, and Regis Le Bris will be aiming for his goalkeeper to find form sharply.
MATCH PREDICTION: BOURNEMOUTH WIN

No side has faced fewer shots in the Premier League this season than winless Bournemouth (64). It is the fewest shots faced by a team in their opening six games without winning any on record since 2003-04.

Bournemouth have not lost three consecutive Premier League matches since May 2024, while manager Marco Rose has only twice suffered three top-flight defeats in a row, losing four on the spin with Borussia Monchengladbach in March 2021 and three with RB Leipzig in January 2024.
Sunderland have lost their last three Premier League matches. The Black Cats last suffered four consecutive top-flight losses in December 2015 under Sam Allardyce.
Meanwhile, only in 1994-95 in the third tier (eight games) and 2023-24 in the Premier League (nine games) have Bournemouth endured a longer winless start to a league season.
Bournemouth have won two of their 10 league games against Sunderland (D3 L5), though both were in the Premier League in September 2015 and April 2017.

ci4uhlo6b7nr1cldraznzj5kx.title: Van Bommel refuses to fault 'seven out of 10' Belgium after France defeat
ci4uhlo6b7nr1cldraznzj5kx.subtitle: Belgium were beaten 1-0 by France in their second Nations League game, but new head coach Mark van Bommel was determined to remain upbeat.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel refused to criticise his Belgium players following their agonising Nations League defeat to France, rating their performance a "seven out of 10" and arguing they are on the right track.
Michael Olise's solo goal in the 88th minute settled Monday's contest in Brussels, as France went top of Group A1 in the Nations League with two wins from two games.
While Les Bleus boast a perfect record under new boss Zinedine Zidane, Belgium have registered one win and one loss under Van Bommel, having triumphed 2-0 in Italy on Friday.
France had 18 shots to Belgium's 12 and hit the target on seven occasions, compared to the hosts' two, while Zidane's team also won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.22 to 0.69.
But Van Bommel was still broadly pleased with the Red Devils' efforts, ahead of a home game against Turkiye on Friday and a return trip to France next Monday.
"They all deserve at least a seven out of 10," Van Bommel noted. "I have nothing to fault them for. These are intelligent and quality players.
"We should not be critical; we are on the right track. Our way of pressing, our changes on the wings, and our way of creating chances were good.
"We can see the idea behind our actions. You could feel that everyone was enjoying themselves. The details are well mastered. We simply didn't manage to score."
France were without captain Kylian Mbappe due to a hyperextension in his left knee, while Olise, Ousmane Dembele and Rayan Cherki were all introduced from the bench.

Esteban Lepaul and Maghnes Akliouche started in attack, alongside Paris Saint-Germain's Desire Doue and recent Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola, but Van Bommel was still under no illusions regarding the strength of France's lineup.
"We cannot say that we played against a B team. It was a solid team," he added. "Of course, France are further ahead than us. I can't deny that.
"On Monday, we might be even more challenged at their place. This is only our first week together, we must not forget that.
"Our goal is the Euros in two years, but I am very happy with our performance."
While Belgium host Turkiye in their next Nations League fixture, France welcome Roberto Mancini's Italy to the Stade de France on Friday, with Mbappe still sidelined.

cuvnxabgh98v1wg07zvgbsrph.title: Austin must turn draws into wins during play-off push, says Sabovic
cuvnxabgh98v1wg07zvgbsrph.subtitle: Twelfth-place Austin FC host 11th-place San Diego FC as both teams push for a play-off spot in the MLS' Western Conference.
paragraphs: Austin FC midfielder Besard Sabovic believes they "need to start winning if we're going to make it to the play-offs".
Austin are 12th in the Western Conference, just two points off the postseason places and one point behind upcoming opponents San Diego FC.
After a goalless draw with FC Dallas last time out, Austin are unbeaten in seven games in MLS, though four of those games have ended as a draw.
With just eight games to go in the regular season, Sabovic is determined to win as many as possible in their search for a play-off spot.
"We're seven games [unbeaten], and we should do everything we can to continue this streak, but of course, it's getting closer and closer," said Sabovic.
"The season's ending soon, so we need to start winning if we're going to make it to the playoffs, which is everyone's goal."
For the first time this season, San Diego earned a result in a league match they trailed in the 75th minute or later when they played to a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami on Sunday.
Dating back to last season, San Diego had lost 13 straight regular-season matches when trailing in the 75th minute or later.
Despite the result against the reigning MLS Cup champions, San Diego remain winless in their last four MLS games (D1 L3) ahead of facing Austin.
Austin FC – Jon Gallagher
In the 0-0 draw with Dallas, Jon Gallagher registered two of Austin's three shots on target, tying for the most in any of his 200 career MLS regular-season matches.
As a team, the Verde have not attempted more than three shots on target in any of their last five MLS matches.
San Diego FC – Anders Dreyer
Anders Dreyer scored both of San Diego's goals against Miami, his 18th MLS regular-season game with multiple goal contributions.

cwhh5v785n54101uogqsf0ufx.title: 'It's our own fault' – Kompany laments 'stupid' errors from Bayern
cwhh5v785n54101uogqsf0ufx.subtitle: After Bayern Munich were held to a disappointing 3-3 draw in Norway by Viking, Vincent Kompany said individual mistakes were to blame.
paragraphs: Vincent Kompany admits Bayern Munich only have themselves to blame for their back-to-back draws against Augsburg and Viking, with indefensible errors costing them.
Having played out a 2-2 draw against Augsburg in the Bundesliga on Saturday, Bayern were again left to settle for a share of the spoils in the Champions League on Tuesday.
They shared six goals equally with Norwegian champions Viking, dropping points in a league-phase match for just the second time in their last 10 such outings (W8 L1).

Bayern fell behind after one minute and 11 seconds through Gianni Stensness' header. That goal was the fourth-fastest they have ever conceded in the Champions League, having also conceded the earliest goal in Bundesliga history on Saturday, after a mere eight seconds.

Peter Christiansen doubled Viking's advantage, and though Harry Kane's brace and a Luis Diaz strike put Bayern in front, they conceded a last-minute equaliser to Herman Haugen, after Michael Olise was sent off for two bookable offences.
Olise's second caution came when he needlessly pulled back Henrik Heggheim deep inside Viking territory, leaving Kompany to rue a series of individual errors from his players.
"It's our own fault. We were very dominant, like we were at the weekend," the Bayern boss told the club's website.
"There are certainly things where you can say the substance of our performance isn't that bad, but we're just making lapses in concentration and aren't smart enough in these moments.

"Against Augsburg we conceded after eight seconds, today after one minute. In that situation, we maybe didn't need to play it out from the corner and could've looked for the longer option. There was a bit of overconfidence there.

"At the moment, it feels like every chance for the opponents leads to a goal. That's no excuse, though, because we're causing these situations ourselves. The sending-off was obviously stupid, and we've spoken about it quite clearly.
"However, it's important to me that I don't see a lack of energy in the team. The players are working hard, and mentally they're always at it, too.
"Nevertheless, things like this shouldn't happen. It makes it difficult to win matches, even when you're clearly superior and don't play that badly throughout the whole game.
"But because of these isolated situations, which we're bringing about ourselves, it obviously turns out differently."

Bayern have never won an away match in the Champions League or European Cup after trailing by multiple goals, with Tuesday's game representing the 38th time they have trailed by two or more goals on the road in the competition (D3 L35).
Viking are just the second Norwegian team to score three times against a German side in the Champions League, after Rosenborg versus Borussia Dortmund in 1999 (3-0).
Captain Joshua Kimmich echoed Kompany's sentiment in his own post-match assessment, saying: "We're making too many mistakes.
"Our play isn't bad. We have to acknowledge that something is amiss at the moment, and that's down to the fact we’re making too many individual errors.

"It's not down to effort. We're lagging a bit behind now because of the points we've dropped, which we need to make up, but it's still too early to say much about it. Nevertheless, we have to admit that we're a bit away from where we want to be."
Bayern return to Bundesliga action against RB Leipzig on Saturday, before taking on 2025-26 runners-up Arsenal in their next Champions League match on October 20.

cyhuti0bvht81ff1qrkw1dqf1.title: Zidane: France players are the protagonists, not me
cyhuti0bvht81ff1qrkw1dqf1.subtitle: France will get the Zinedine Zidane era underway in Turkiye on Friday, but the ex-midfield icon does not want to be the star attraction.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane insists he will not be the "protagonist" of France's new era, instead taking a back seat to his star-studded squad.
France face Turkiye in their Nations League opener at Kocaeli Stadium on Friday, with Zidane managing his country for the first time following 14 years under Didier Deschamps.
Deschamps led Les Bleus to their second World Cup triumph in 2018 – as well as runner-up finishes at the 2022 edition and at Euro 2016 – during his illustrious spell in charge.
He oversaw 187 matches in total, having also represented his nation 103 times as a player, with his 26 World Cup games being the most of any coach in the competition's history.
Zidane's appointment, though, has come with much fanfare, given his status as an icon of French football.
He scored a brace against Brazil in France's first World Cup final triumph in 1998, while he is also the most recent Frenchman to win the Ballon d'Or, claiming the prize that year.

And, across two spells as the head coach of Real Madrid, Zidane won three Champions League crowns in a row, two LaLiga titles, two Club World Cups, two UEFA Super Cups and two editions of the Supercopa de Espana.

Yet the former midfielder does not see himself as the star of the France setup, telling reporters: "After 14 years of Didier, this is new. But the protagonists are the players. I'm going to stay in my role.
"I feel a huge emotion to be able to be here as a coach, maybe even more than before my first game as a player."
One of Zidane's foremost tasks will be finding a way to keep several big-name attackers happy.

At this summer's World Cup, where France finished fourth, Kylian Mbappe set a new record for goal involvements at a single edition (14 – 10 goals, four assists) and became the competition's all-time leading scorer (22 goals).
Michael Olise recorded more assists than any other player has had at a single World Cup (seven, since 1966), while Ousmane Dembele scored six goals and assisted two.
Asked where he would field Dembele in particular, Zidane replied: "You'll see tomorrow. We have put things in place. The idea is to do interesting things.
"We're not going to talk about Zidane's touch. We only had three training sessions. We put two or three things in place. We will have to be good tomorrow."

Adrien Rabiot appeared alongside Zidane at France's pre-match press conference, and the AC Milan midfielder believes Deschamps' team were tactically outclassed by eventual champions Spain in their World Cup semi-final, which La Roja won 2-0.
"I'm thinking about the Nations League. We know that things in football move fast," Rabiot said. "The coach is here for four years. We have to take this competition and use it.
"It wasn't a lack of quality. We have no less quality than Spain, with all humility. They were better tactically; they may have prepared better for that match.
"Spain were able to put us in difficulty. If we play them again, we will have to find the key. We will have to work on this tactical point – we have collective and individual talent."

paragraphs: Jesper Sorensen has come to the defence of his Vancouver Whitecaps side after their recent attacking struggles.
Vancouver are top of the Western Conference, but have not won any of their last four games following a goalless draw with second-place St. Louis City SC.
The Whitecaps previously drew 1-1 with Los Angeles FC, when defender Tristan Blackmon received an early red card, and lost 3-1 to the Chicago Fire.
However, against St. Louis on Wednesday, Vancouver also restricted their high-flying opponents to just eight shots, which amounted to 0.8 expected goals (xG).
The Whitecaps have already secured their playoff place, doing so after the draw with LAFC, and Sorensen is not concerned about their attacking output ahead of their trip to Austin FC.
"I don't think that's fair to say," said Sorensen when asked if Vancouver's defensive strengths are affecting their attacking play.
"I think we generated chances [against St. Louis]; it was a difficult team we were up against.
"Also, considering we played 10 against 11 for almost the entire game in LA, I think we actually produced more chances than you would expect to begin with.
"So, I think the fluidity in our game is okay. We create some good chances; we don't concede much as well."
Austin, meanwhile, are 14th in the West and seven points off the playoff places with five games to go.
They lost 3-1 to LAFC last time out, extending their winless run in MLS to four games.
Austin FC – Brandon Vazquez
Brandon Vazquez has scored in three straight regular-season matches for the third time in his MLS career and the first since he was at FC Cincinnati in 2022 (four straight).
The only longer streak by an Austin player is Sebastian Driussi's seven-game run from July to September 2022.
Vancouver Whitecaps – Oliver Larraz
Vancouver failed to hit the target despite attempting 16 shots against St. Louis, with Oliver Larraz recording the joint-most shots (four) and second-most xG (0.2).
It equalled the second-most shots attempted by a team who did not hit the target in a regular-season match since 2010, with only Real Salt Lake v Houston Dynamo in 2017 taking more (21).

d67498ismzaz1ulipuxd9hj0i.subtitle: Yoann Damet has already won silverware in his first season as St. Louis City SC boss, but he has his eyes set on more success.
paragraphs: St. Louis City SC boss Yoann Damet wants to see "how far we can go in year one" after already winning silverware this season.
St. Louis defeated the Columbus Crew on penalties to win the U.S. Open Cup midweek, securing their first-ever trophy and clinching a spot in next season's Champions Cup.
They have also impressed in MLS action, recently stringing together a 19-game unbeaten run to move up to second in the Western Conference.
Damet's side face Real Salt Lake this weekend, and he has pushed his team to achieve even more success in 2026.
"Listen, it means a lot for the club," said Damet.
"Obviously, it's the fourth year of existence of the club. You always want to fill the trophy cabinet. But it takes time; it’s not easy.
"Success is not built overnight. So we started the year thinking: let's implement a clear vision, a clear identity of how we want to do things, and let's see how far we can go in year one.

"I'm super happy that these guys are going to be remembered to be the first doing it for the club. It's amazing. I hope we will all look back in 20, 50 years, and be really proud of what we've accomplished together.
"We wanted to write the history for the club."
Real Salt Lake, meanwhile, are three points off the playoff places in the West with four games to go.
They defeated Sporting Kansas City 3-1 last time out and have now won two of their last four games (D1 L1) after losing each of their previous four.

Morgan Guilavogui scored two career MLS goals prior to his brace against Sporting Kansas City.

Rafael Navarro has recorded multiple goal contributions in four of his eight MLS matches with St. Louis, including a goal and assist on Saturday.

d6765eyx536j1ru5vr5jzx9b0.title: 'A player like him deserves this' – Scaloni pushed for Messi's Argentina farewell
d6765eyx536j1ru5vr5jzx9b0.subtitle: Despite announcing his international retirement after the World Cup, Lionel Messi will play for Argentina one more time on October 6.
paragraphs: Lionel Scaloni revealed he did everything in his power to ensure Lionel Messi would return to the Argentina national team one more time for a farewell match.
Messi announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, bringing an end to a glittering career with his country.
He retires as Argentina's all-time leading appearance-maker (207) and scorer (125), while also captaining his country to the World Cup in 2022 and two Copa America crowns.

The 39-year-old has played more games (34), registered more goal involvements (33) and laid on more assists (12) than any other player in World Cup history, while only Kylian Mbappe (22) has bettered his 21 goals at FIFA's flagship tournament.
The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner also leads the all-time World Cup charts for shots (140), shots on target (64), chances created (99) and dribbles (250).
However, Messi was called up to Scaloni's latest Argentina squad, and he will play one final time against Benin at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on October 6.
"I ​believe that a player like him deserves this. Personally, I did my part ​because I wanted to be at his farewell," Scaloni told reporters.
"Since I don't know if I would be here later, we pushed hard so that he could ​be in this match.
"We knew everything he was going through and ​even so, he put in the desire and effort to want to come and ‌be able ⁠to say goodbye to the people who love him so much.
"If we have to pay tribute, we have to do it at this moment. With him, it will never stop, but later, the magic ​might not be ​the same."
Messi was pivotal to Argentina's first World Cup success since 1986 in 2022, scoring twice in their penalty shoot-out win against France following a 3-3 draw in normal time.
He followed that up with a sensational tournament this summer, scoring eight goals, including his first-ever World Cup hat-trick against Algeria.
"For me, getting to coach him was the ultimate experience. It was a dream. I told him so, and I'll say it for the rest of my life. There will never be anyone like him," Scaloni added.
"It's very rare for a player like that to come along – not just because of what he does on the pitch, but because of everything he conveys off it. Let's enjoy this.
"After the World Cup he just played, there isn't much more to add. If the award is for the best player, there's no doubt. It's already spoken for, the statistics prove it.
"As long as he's on a football pitch, it's hard to argue that he doesn't deserve it."
With Messi's international future already decided, the same cannot be said for Scaloni, whose contract will run out this December.
Asked if he had received an update on his ​future, ⁠Scaloni said he would meet with Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia in the coming days.
"It is a dream come true, but that doesn't mean I ⁠have to ​cling to the job forever," Scaloni said.
"There are certain conditions we need to discuss with the president, and we'll see if we ​can reach an agreement."
d6765eyx536j1ru5vr5jzx9b0.html:
Lionel Scaloni revealed he did everything in his power to ensure Lionel Messi would return to the Argentina national team one more time for a farewell match. 

Messi announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, bringing an end to a glittering career with his country. 

He retires as Argentina's all-time leading appearance-maker (207) and scorer (125), while also captaining his country to the World Cup in 2022 and two Copa America crowns. 

The 39-year-old has played more games (34), registered more goal involvements (33) and laid on more assists (12) than any other player in World Cup history, while only Kylian Mbappe (22) has bettered his 21 goals at FIFA's flagship tournament.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner also leads the all-time World Cup charts for shots (140), shots on target (64), chances created (99) and dribbles (250). 

However, Messi was called up to Scaloni's latest Argentina squad, and he will play one final time against Benin at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on October 6.

"I ​believe that a player like him deserves this. Personally, I did my part ​because I wanted to be at his farewell," Scaloni told reporters. 

"Since I don't know if I would be here later, we pushed hard so that he could ​be in this match.

"We knew everything he was going through and ​even so, he put in the desire and effort to want to come and ‌be able ⁠to say goodbye to the people who love him so much.

"If we have to pay tribute, we have to do it at this moment. With him, it will never stop, but later, the magic ​might not be ​the same."

Messi was pivotal to Argentina's first World Cup success since 1986 in 2022, scoring twice in their penalty shoot-out win against France following a 3-3 draw in normal time.

He followed that up with a sensational tournament this summer, scoring eight goals, including his first-ever World Cup hat-trick against Algeria. 

"For me, getting to coach him was the ultimate experience. It was a dream. I told him so, and I'll say it for the rest of my life. There will never be anyone like him," Scaloni added.

"It's very rare for a player like that to come along – not just because of what he does on the pitch, but because of everything he conveys off it. Let's enjoy this.

"After the World Cup he just played, there isn't much more to add. If the award is for the best player, there's no doubt. It's already spoken for, the statistics prove it.

"As long as he's on a football pitch, it's hard to argue that he doesn't deserve it."

With Messi's international future already decided, the same cannot be said for Scaloni, whose contract will run out this December. 

Asked if he had received an update on his ​future, ⁠Scaloni said he would meet with Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia in the coming days.

"It is a dream come true, but that doesn't mean I ⁠have to ​cling to the job forever," Scaloni said. 

"There are certain conditions we need to discuss with the president, and we'll see if we ​can reach an agreement."

d7qtkbyeoigu1nwlfv7pw2yzb.title: Marquez concedes Mexico must get better after being booed off versus Chile
d7qtkbyeoigu1nwlfv7pw2yzb.subtitle: Mexico have not won any of their first four games under Rafael Marquez, who saw his team booed off in Los Angeles on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Rafael Marquez conceded Mexico have much work to do after a dispiriting 2-0 defeat to Chile extended his winless start in charge of El Tri.
Having taken over when Javier Aguirre resigned following July's World Cup round-of-16 defeat to England, Marquez is yet to taste victory as his nation's head coach.

Mexico opened the extended international break with back-to-back 1-1 draws against Colombia and Peru before losing 3-0 to the United States last Saturday, and they concluded their tour of the USA with another poor display on Tuesday.

Second-half goals from Maximiliano Gutierrez and Vicente Pizarro saw Chile leave the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum as deserved victors and led to Mexico being jeered by the majority of the 56,000-strong crowd.
Chile won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.2 to 0.63 and had two Opta-defined big chances to Mexico's zero, despite only having a 35.8% possession share.

But while Marquez knows Mexico's performances have not been acceptable thus far, he believes his policy of squad rotation has given him a good idea of what will be needed against Jamaica next month, in a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie.
"We maybe struggled a bit in our defensive execution. We maybe started to have some doubts; it was really easy for them to get behind us," Marquez said.
"We tried to put the best team out there, especially because of the workload we've been carrying over these past few weeks, but it was clear that maybe wasn't the best way to go about it.
"The reality is that yes, we have to obviously keep working at this, we have to keep improving. There is a lot of room for improvement; we will address that.
"I think we have more clarity now going into the next matchup, which is a lot more meaningful. We will have to bring the players we need for these types of games."
In the other CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals, the USA will face Haiti, Canada will take on Guatemala and Curacao have been drawn against Panama.

d88327xzdisj1o9dh79ld7gmr.title: Amorim proud of AC Milan's response after bounce-back win
d88327xzdisj1o9dh79ld7gmr.subtitle: AC Milan were well beaten by Bournemouth in the Europa League on Thursday, but they responded by seeing off Udinese 2-0 in Serie A.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim was full of pride after his AC Milan team responded to their European disappointment in style.
Milan were hammered 3-0 by Bournemouth on Thursday, as former Manchester United boss Amorim endured a miserable return to England.
Yet Milan got back on track with a relatively routine 2-0 win over Udinese on Sunday, as Amorim extended his unbeaten start in Serie A to eight games.
It is the third time in the last 20 top-flight seasons that Milan have gone this long without defeat, after 2020-21 and 2021-22, as goals from Christian Pulisic and Omari Hutchinson got the job done.

"I am really happy for them and really proud, because everything we talked about before the game, being competitive from the first minute, I think we did that today," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.
"Even when we got tired in the second half, we controlled the game, so I am really happy with the team. Now we have to think about the next game."
Milan are fourth in Serie A, four points behind leaders Inter, whom they face on Saturday.
Amorim had to shuffle his pack due to a big injury list, with Sankhoun Diawara and Fikayo Tomori given their first league starts of the season.
And Amorim is delighted with how his team are handling the hectic fixture list.
"If you see the schedule in Europe, it's impossible," said Amorim.
"Everyone needs to be prepared. My job is not just to prepare to win the next game, that is what people want, but my job is also to help Milan in the future.
"For that, they need to play, they need to have the opportunity and feel that they are important.

"They need to work really hard, we have a lot of injuries today, and they showed they are ready to cope with the pressure of playing for this club. That's also why I am really happy and proud, because when we are on the field, it is my responsibility.
"We need time to work on several things, but we don't have time even to address the problems we had in the last game.
"We are learning in the games, with videos, in team meetings, because for three weeks we have barely had any training. I am proud of these lads, because they are paying attention to everything."
Before facing Inter, Milan host Bologna on Wednesday.

d9y1o8jngad71l61cx4ss24e4.title: Muller tips Olise or Mbappe for Ballon d'Or
d9y1o8jngad71l61cx4ss24e4.subtitle: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal are the favourites for the Ballon d'Or, but Thomas Muller has picked another top contender.
paragraphs: Thomas Muller has backed either Michael Olise or Kylian Mbappe as the top two candidates to win the Ballon d'Or this year.
The winner of the award will be announced on October 26, but Muller has overlooked favourites including former Bayern Munich team-mate Harry Kane and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.
Instead, he has tipped a different Bayern player to claim the award, looking to Olise, whose performances in 2025-26 helped the club win the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal titles.
Olise ended the Bundesliga season with 34 goal involvements (15 goals, 19 assists), a new record for a winger since Opta data collection began in the German top-flight in 2004-05.
Only Kane (41) directly contributed to more Bundesliga goals than the Frenchman, who also scored five goals and provided seven assists in 13 Champions League games.
He also carried his form into the World Cup, becoming the first player on record (since 1966) to register seven assists in a single edition.
As for Mbappe, this summer he became the all-time top scorer at World Cups (22 goals) and has scored 50 goals in 52 games for Real Madrid since the start of last season.
Of players in Europe's top five leagues, only Kane (67) has netted more club goals than Mbappe in that time.

"For me, there are two candidates whose individual performances have impressed me the most, and those are Michael Olise and his brilliant World Cup partner Kylian Mbappe," Muller wrote in his newsletter, as quoted by Sky Sport Germany.
"The two combine spectacle with goal threat. In detail, they manage to be efficient with their finesse and power, and to make the whole thing look incredibly easy.
"For me, that's the stuff of a world-class footballer. It simply needs a touch of magic."
Muller also highlighted Olise's impressive start to the 2026-27 campaign.
Olise has registered 11 goal involvements across all competitions so far this term (eight goals, three assists), including a hat-trick in a 7-0 rout of Union Berlin before the international break.
"It's nothing new how he converts those chances from outside the penalty area, but it's still always a sight to behold," Muller added.

df7aadf87i6d12mt97dhvw31m.title: Napoli 3-3 Roma: Balerdi snatches late draw in Serie A thriller
df7aadf87i6d12mt97dhvw31m.subtitle: Despite taking the lead twice at home, Napoli had to settle for a point in an end-to-end encounter against Serie A title contenders Roma.
paragraphs: Leonardo Balerdi scored an 89th-minute equaliser as Roma fought their way to a 3-3 draw with Napoli.
The defender came off the bench to score twice for Roma, who found themselves 2-0 down at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona after goals from Frank Anguissa and Scott McTominay in this Serie A encounter.
Matias Soule triggered the comeback from Balerdi got his first equaliser, and the substitute got his second late on after McTominay though his brace had secured all three points for Napoli.

Napoli had the better chances in the early stages, with Rasmus Hojlund seeing a shot blocked and McTominay volleying straight at Pierluigi Gollini, while Giovanni Di Lorenzo saw a low cross expertly cleared away by Devyne Rensch.

Alex Meret was alert to keep out Donyell Malen's driven effort with his legs, and Napoli eventually got their deserved opener in the 28th minute as Anguissa sent a bicycle kick into the bottom-right corner after Marten de Roon initially cleared a cross.

Gollini pulled off an incredible save to deny Mathias Olivera from close range, with Bryan Cristante also clearing the rebound off the line, but Napoli doubled their lead three minutes after the restart as McTominay headed in from Matteo Politano's cross.
McTominay managed to deflect Soule's shot wide at the other end, though the Argentine would not be denied in the 69th minute, when he curled into the far corner following a tidy one-two with Malen.

And just five minutes later, Roma were level. Evan Ndicka won the initial header from De Roon's corner, and though the defender was blocked by team-mate Santiago Castro, Balerdi was on hand to lash in the loose ball.
Massimiliano Allegri made a host of changes in the hopes of regaining the lead, but it came from one of his starters, as McTominay took in a pass from Olivera and arrowed into the bottom-left corner.
However, there was time for one last twist as Balerdi timed his run perfectly to head Wesley's right-wing cross past Meret and snatch a point for the visitors.
Napoli denied statement win
Sitting mid-table in the early Serie A standings, Napoli would have hugely benefited from a hard-earned victory against Roma, but Gian Piero Gasperini's side proved why they are title challengers.
Gollini made five saves to ensure Roma had a chance to win at least a point, with Napoli accumulating 2.34 expected goals (xG) to the visitors' 1.86, which came from 24 shots.

Not many would have imagined Balerdi, who had not scored a league goal since the 2023-24 season, when he was at Marseille, to bag a brace off the bench, but Roma must have contributions from plenty of players if they are to mount a serious title charge.
It seemed Napoli's ever-reliable McTominay earned them another invaluable win in the 83rd minute, but the Scotsman was denied the headlines.

Since his move to Serie A (2024-25), McTominay is the midfielder in the top five European leagues who has scored the most headed goals across all competitions: 11 - followed by Casemiro and Corentin Tolisso with 10.

Nevertheless, Roma keep themselves within touching distance of Inter and Lazio for the time being, while Napoli could drop into the bottom half of the table by the end of the weekend, placing more pressure on Allegri's shoulders.

dfiikiain1y515wmqip89nrpn.title: Aston Villa 3-1 Viking: Emery's side stay perfect in Champions League
dfiikiain1y515wmqip89nrpn.subtitle: Aston Villa are second in the Champions League table after making it three wins from three with a comfortable victory over Viking.
paragraphs: Aston Villa extended their perfect start to the Champions League season with a confident 3-1 win over Viking at Villa Park.
Ross Barkley and Emiliano Buendia were both on target in the first half, with a Henrik Heggheim own goal helping to secure the points even before Peter Christiansen's late consolation.
Villa started brightly, with Nicolas Jackson seeing two headers saved in the opening seven minutes.
A deflected Alysson cross looped onto the crossbar just before Barkley broke the deadlock from a 23rd-minute corner as he rose highest to glance in Ibrahim Mbaye's set-piece.

Buendia then headed over from point-blank range and forced a smart stop out of Arild Ostbo before Alysson was clumsily felled in the box. A penalty was given following a VAR review, and Buendia finally hit the net from 12 yards out after 37 minutes.
Viking – who snatched a shock 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich last time out in the Champions League – looked stronger after the break, with Tobias Moi calling Zion Suzuki into action for the first time.
However, Villa put the game beyond their visitors in the 62nd minute, with Alysson once again seeing a cross deflected, though Heggheim inadvertently turned it into his own net.

Jesper Daland and Alejandro Garnacho went close at either end before Viking denied Villa a clean sheet as Christiansen finished Kristoffer Askildsen's cross first-time, with the goal standing after it was initially ruled out for offside.
Viking fail to breach the Villa Park fortress
Villa have won each of their last 12 major European home games, the joint-longest run by an English team this century (also Manchester City in 2022-2024 and Manchester United in 2006-2008).
It was another impressive showing by the Villans, who are the second-quickest team to record 20 wins in the European Cup/Champions League (30 matches), behind only Real Madrid (20 games).
They are also the first Europa League holders to win their first three games of a Champions League campaign since Man Utd in 2017-18.

Fresh off recording their biggest-ever European win last time out against Fenerbahce, Villa looked like they could run away with this one in the first half as well. They recorded 14 first-half shots, their joint-most in a game under Unai Emery (four other times).

Buendia became the first Villa player to score in four consecutive appearances in major European competition, while Barkley has now scored in three consecutive starts across all competitions for the first time since October 2020.

Villa ultimately dominated, having 21 shots worth 2.67 expected goals (xG) to Viking's 10 attempts (0.75 xG), and they will next put their 100% start to the test against LaLiga leaders Barcelona next month.

dfn5x6f2dqmq1hnvjpnwqemno.title: PSV 'back in the mix' after huge victory against Porto, says Bosz
dfn5x6f2dqmq1hnvjpnwqemno.subtitle: Porto and PSV played out an entertaining clash in the Champions League, but Guus Til's second-half strike was decisive for the visitors.
paragraphs: Peter Bosz said his PSV team "dared to play football" during their away win against Porto, a result he believes has got them "back in the mix" in the Champions League.
PSV entered MD3 with just one point from their opening two games against RB Leipzig and Shakhtar Donetsk, but they emerged from the Estadio Do Dragao as 1-0 victors.
Ivan Perisic headed over a glorious early chance for PSV before Oskar Pietuszewski shot wide at the other end moments later following an error from goalkeeper Matej Kovar.
The best chance of the first half went to the Eredivisie side, with Alberto Costa's loose pass allowing Filip Kostic to steal in, but his effort struck the base of the left post.

PSV struck the woodwork again through Esmir Bajraktarevic in the second half, but the visitors took the lead in the 57th minute when Sven Mijnans' attempted shot at goal was tucked in at the back post by Guus Til.

But Porto should have drawn level when Kovar's poor ball presented an opportunity to Hwang In-Beom. He squared the ball to Andre Silva, but his shot was brilliantly stopped by the PSV goalkeeper, before Victor Froholdt's attempt on the rebound was cleared off the line.
Some heroic defending from Sergino Dest spared Kovar's blushes once again with a last-ditch tackle to deny Costa, with PSV holding on despite Porto's late flurry of chances.
The result saw PSV end a five-match winless run in the Champions League this evening (D1 L4), with this their first victory in the competition since beating Liverpool 4-1 in November 2025.
"This is who we are; we are PSV. We want to play good football and work hard," Bosz said.

"It was up to us to continue playing a role in the Champions League, because with one point from three matches, it is going to be difficult. We wanted at least a draw, but winning is, of course, even better. Now we are back in the mix.
"I'm proud that we were able to hold on. We dared to play football, and we won the ball back very quickly.
"Defensively, we weren't good in the first few minutes, but when Mauro [Junior] and Kodai [Sano] started pressing, we got it under control again."

It was also PSV's first victory away in Portugal in European competition since March 1975, a 2-1 win against Benfica in the Cup Winners' Cup. The Dutch side had failed to win on any of their last seven visits to the country prior to Tuesday's win (D2 L5 – including qualifiers).

PSV attempted 18 shots, tallying an expected goals (xG) total of 1.91, their joint-most on record in a Champions League away match (since 2003-04), equalling the 18 they managed against Brest in December 2024.

For Porto, however, they have now lost each of their last four Champions League matches, which is their joint-longest run of defeats in the competition along with a run of four between November 2021 and September 2022.

And after failing to score against Man City on MD1 and against PSV, Porto have blanked in consecutive home matches in the Champions League group stages for the first time since 2004-05, though Francesco Farioli said his team ran out of luck in their quest for a goal.
"Honestly, the feeling is that even if we'd played for another 25 minutes, we would have created dangerous situations but still wouldn't have scored," Farioli conceded.
"That's the feeling we had, and of course it's frustrating. We created enough to deserve more than a defeat.
"In the second half, I think we had a very positive reaction and did enough to deserve a different result.

"But this is the third time I've come here after a Champions League game and said we deserved a different result, yet we're still not getting it. So there's definitely something we need to do better."
