di4bcg7hnqt1lcnz7ql2gnxs.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina 1-1 Sweden: Gyokeres dampens Dzeko's farewell party
di4bcg7hnqt1lcnz7ql2gnxs.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres scored once again for Sweden, who drew 1-1 with Bosnia-Herzegovina in what was Edin Dzeko's final international appearance.
paragraphs: Edin Dzeko's final appearance for Bosnia-Herzegovina ended in a 1-1 draw with Sweden in the Nations League.
Kerim Alajbegovic's 80th-minute equaliser ensured Dzeko would not bow out with a defeat after Viktor Gyokeres gave Sweden the lead just after the hour at Stadion Bilino Polje.

Sweden started on the front foot as Gyokeres' low drive towards the bottom-left corner was kept out by Salko Hamzic, and the Arsenal striker then saw a goal ruled out in the 17th minute by VAR after the ball touched his arm before he scored.
The home fans erupted when Dzeko found the back of the net before half-time, but his goal was also chalked off as the ball had gone out of play in the build-up.

Graham Potter's side then scored with their first shot of the second half after Alexander Bernhardsson regained possession and played Gyokeres through on goal, with the forward lashing into the roof of the net.

Bernhardsson, Gyokeres and Besfort Zeneli all missed chances to double Sweden's lead, and it proved costly as Alajbegovic's in-swinging cross evaded all the players in the box and nestled into the far corner.
Gyokeres oozing confidence in Sweden shirt

Gyokeres entered the international break low on confidence after a poor start to the season with Arsenal, but the 28-year-old is in exceptional form for Sweden, providing the goods again in Alexander Isak's absence.

Gyokeres has scored in all three games during this international break, seeing him become the first-ever player to score in six consecutive Nations League matches, with Potter's side still top of Group B4 after three games.

Bosnia, meanwhile, paid farewell to one of their greatest players. Dzeko exited the pitch to a guard of honour from his Bosnia team-mates, though he would have loved to leave with one last goal to his name.

Dzeko bows out as Bosnia's all-time leading appearance maker (152) and top scorer (73), though this game could signify a change in guard, with 19-year-old Juventus forward Alajbegovic scoring an important goal.

dk0qq7ilan321xjaeic3eof9f.title: 'This is Anfield' – Perez says Villarreal failed to deal with Liverpool atmosphere
dk0qq7ilan321xjaeic3eof9f.subtitle: Villarreal were 2-0 up in their Champions League clash with Liverpool, only for Andoni Iraola's side to turn the game on its head.
paragraphs: Inigo Perez said his Villarreal players failed to deal with the "huge reaction" from the Anfield crowd as they let a two-goal lead slip in their Champions League defeat to Liverpool.
Perez watched on as his team capitalised on some woeful defending from Liverpool to pull two goals clear by the 29th minute through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona.
It was the earliest Liverpool have been two goals down in a game in major European competition since April 2016 against Borussia Dortmund in the Europa League (08:20).
But by half-time, Andoni Iraola's side had hauled themselves back level thanks to two headers from Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, and they carried on their momentum.
Mac Allister notched his second of the match just after the hour, with substitute Florian Wirtz scoring his first goal of the season in the 67th minute to put the Reds in control.

Tani Oluwaseyi netted what proved to be just a consolation in the 87th minute, with Villarreal on the end of a 4-3 defeat. They have now lost 11 of their last 13 games in the Champions League (W1 D1), including each of their last seven in the road.
All four times Liverpool have been two goals down at home in major European competition inside the opening 29 minutes, they have gone on to win the game.

Those instances came in April 1976 vs Club Brugge (12th minute, won 3-2), October 1996 vs Sion (23rd minute, won 6-3), April 2016 vs Dortmund (9th minute, won 4-3) and against Villarreal (29th minute, won 4-3), with Perez saying "simple mistakes" cost his side.
"When they're trailing, and they score, they always generate a huge reaction," Perez conceded. "I don't think either team was ever out of the game at any point.
"If we avoid simple mistakes, I think we will be closer to winning these kinds of games.
"[Leading at half-time] would have helped us a lot in terms of how we approached the second half. In the end, we conceded the equaliser and they gained momentum.
"This is Anfield, and you're playing against Liverpool. These are the details that end up working against you."

Liverpool's comeback also saw them win a European Cup/Champions League game in which they were two goals down for the second time, previously doing so against Villarreal in the semi-finals in May 2022.

The Reds have now avoided defeat in five of their six games in all competitions this season in which they’ve conceded the opening goal (W3 D2 L1), already more than across the entirety of 2025-26 (W2 D2 L18) under Arne Slot.
"If you score three goals in the Champions League, even if it's at Anfield, you expect to get something from the game," Villarreal goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi said.
"We could have had a bit more control after going 2-0 up. That period was probably more frustrating than the goals themselves."
Former Liverpool goalkeeper Gulacsi singled out Rio Ngumoha for praise, with the talented teenager producing a stunning individual display to lead his team's turnaround.

Ngumoha (18 years and 52 days) became the third-youngest player to provide multiple assists in a Champions League game behind Warren Zaire-Emery against AC Milan in 2023 (17y 231d) and Theo Walcott against Hamburg in 2006 (17y 250d).

He is also the youngest player on record since 2008-09 to complete 5+ dribbles (seven), have 10+ touches in the opposition box (12) and register an assist (two) in a Champions League match, with Gulacsi labelling his performance as "amazing".
"He [Ngumoha] was amazing to be honest," Gulacsi added. "We knew he's very strong one-v-one on both sides, he can go past the defender.
"It's not just him. On the other side, Gakpo had a good game. It was not easy to defend them one-v-one, it's just the quality of the opponent."

dk65ccpokuc21utgxmi266fi1.title: Flick hails Gordon's impact after first Barcelona goal
dk65ccpokuc21utgxmi266fi1.subtitle: Anthony Gordon and Lamine Yamal both played big parts in Barcelona's comfortable 3-0 win over Getafe, keeping their 100% start intact.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick hailed Anthony Gordon's impact on Barcelona and revealed Lamine Yamal asked to stay on the pitch, wanting to "give it his all" against Getafe.
Barcelona continued their perfect start to their LaLiga campaign, recording an eighth straight win by beating Getafe 3-0.
Gordon netted his first Barcelona goal in just 78 seconds, with Gabriel Jesus and Jules Kounde also getting on the scoresheet for the league leaders.

Gordon's goal is the earliest one scored in LaLiga this season and also marks Barcelona's quickest goal in the competition since May 2023, when Ansu Fati hit the back of the net against Real Mallorca after 49 seconds.
He is also the third English player to score for Barcelona in LaLiga, after Gary Lineker (42 goals) and Marcus Rashford, who netted eight times last term in the competition.
"For me, he's doing very well, even before when he didn't score," Flick said about Gordon.

"We're happy. You could see it with the national team; he was confident. He scored. He contributes a lot: he's fast, controls the ball well, always gets to difficult balls, dribbles, creates opportunities.
"Gordon brings a lot to the table."

Yamal played the full 90 minutes despite featuring in all four of Spain's Nations League matches over the international break, and he is the only Barcelona player to have started all eight league matches so far this term.
By setting up Kounde's goal, the teenager registered his fifth assist in LaLiga in 2026-27, the joint-most in the competition alongside Espanyol's Javi Hernandez.
Overall, he has been involved in 12 goals in the top flight (also scored seven goals), with only Raphinha (15 goal involvements) having a hand in more.
"He wanted to give it his all," Flick added about Yamal. "I asked him if he wanted me to substitute him, and he said no.
"He loves to play. We have to manage his workload, but the first half was easier for him, and in the second half he created more chances.
"I'm happy with his attitude. He's recovering well; he's doing his treatments."
Barcelona have won their opening eight LaLiga games in a season for just the second time in their history, after also doing so in 2013-14 under Gerardo Martino.
"It's difficult to achieve, but we're focused solely on the next match," Flick said about Barcelona's start.
"Now, it's Galatasaray [in the Champions League]. It won't be easy, and we want to win.
"We want to make history, and everyone shares that attitude. It's fantastic to see the quality and intensity with which we train. We enjoy it; the players enjoy it. It's fantastic to see."

dlarc9hxu6if1meej5jyjaehb.title: Man City must be more efficient in attack, says Maresca
dlarc9hxu6if1meej5jyjaehb.subtitle: Manchester City were beaten by Aston Villa despite dominating the shot count, leaving Enzo Maresca frustrated with their finishing.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca has challenged his Manchester City players to be more efficient in the final third, after their perfect Premier League start was halted by Saturday's loss to Aston Villa.
City slumped to a 2-1 defeat at Villa Park, with Nicolas Jackson profiting from mistakes committed by Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma in either half.

City briefly drew level through Erling Haaland at the start of the second period, but despite amassing 15 shots to Villa's eight and winning the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.56 to 0.61, Maresca's men never truly looked like fighting back for a second time.
After conceding eight goals in their opening nine matches of the 2026-27 season in all competitions, City have since shipped nine times across their last four games.
But Maresca feels their issues may lie at the other end of the pitch, even with Haaland plundering nine goals in just eight Premier League outings in 2026-27.
"For sure, if you see the amount of time we spent in their box, sometimes we need to be more accurate and precise in the final third and score more goals," Maresca said.
"We spent most of the game in their side, in their box, in the final third.
"Sometimes you have to be more clinical when you have chances but also more precise on the last pass. We have to learn from that."
City's overall attacking statistics this season have been positive, though, as they have overperformed their total of 27.12 xG comfortably, netting 34 times in 13 games across all competitions.

They have hit the target with 81 of their 207 shots overall, recording a 53.29% shot accuracy, while their shot conversion rate of 16.43% is the second-best among Premier League clubs in all competitions, after Chelsea's 16.78%.
Maresca continued: "I felt like we were dangerous on many occasions. Even if the finish wasn't there, we arrived in dangerous places but were not able to play.
"A word of appreciation to the boys, because we kept fighting to the end. It is what it is. Whatever happens, we need to react to it. The team had a very good reaction.
"The second goal was tough because it was very close to our equaliser. We kept going and tried to create chances. It was not our day, but we keep moving forward."
City are next in action in the EFL Cup on Wednesday, when they host Brighton with a quarter-final place on the line, before the exact same fixture takes place in the Premier League on Saturday.

dn28cyhn5d6q12z85vtjecne2.title: Neymar pays tribute to Messi: Thank you for making me love football even more
dn28cyhn5d6q12z85vtjecne2.subtitle: Lionel Messi will play his final game for Argentina on Tuesday, and his great friend Neymar has paid tribute.
paragraphs: Neymar has hailed Lionel Messi ahead of the 39-year-old's final game for Argentina.
Messi confirmed his retirement from international football last month.
However, the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner will make a farewell appearance for Argentina against Benin on Tuesday.
And Neymar, who formed a formidable attack alongside Messi at Barcelona and also played with him at Paris Saint-Germain, has paid tribute to his close friend.
"Anyone who loves football has enjoyed you throughout all these years…" Neymar posted on Instagram.
"Today is your final game wearing the shirt of your national team, your country, and I hope you enjoy every second of it and that all the tributes today make you happy.
"It's not only Argentina that thanks you, the whole world thanks you for everything you’ve done for football.
"Thank you for making me love football even more. It was an honour to have played against you, and even more so to have made history alongside you.
"THANK YOU, Leo Messi."

drqmg75mbkg21f54gx4apzldp.title: Under-pressure Napoli boss Allegri wants 'big performance' against Bodo
drqmg75mbkg21f54gx4apzldp.subtitle: The pressure is mounting on Massimiliano Allegri in the early stages of his Napoli tenure, with Bodo/Glimt up next in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri said only a "big performance" from Napoli would be enough to get the better of Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League and kickstart their campaign.
Napoli welcome the Norwegian side to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday, fresh from a damaging defeat to bottom-of-the-table Venezia in Serie A last weekend.
Allegri's side have lost five of their last nine matches in all competitions (W3 D1 L5), as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 29 games (W16 D8 L5).
Indeed, it is the first time since 2001-02 that they have lost as many matches at this stage, with the club operating in Serie B back then.

The result saw Napoli lose against a newly-promoted side in Serie A for the first time since February 2025 (1-2 vs Como), ending a nine-game unbeaten run against such opponents in the competition (W7 D2), piling the pressure on Allegri.
And things have not been much better in the Champions League for Napoli. Defeats to Arsenal and Villarreal leave them 32nd in the 36-team standings heading into MD3.
Napoli have never previously suffered three consecutive home defeats in major European competition, and Allegri is expecting a reaction.
"The game will be complicated, regardless of the other results," Allegri told reporters. "Last year, Bodo had a good Champions League [campaign], and they're good on the counter-attack.
"They're a strong side, very quick. In Munich, despite the result, they played a good game. They're dangerous when they win the ball back, so it will take a big performance."

Allegri has lost eight of his last nine Champions League matches (W1), as many as in his previous 40 combined (W24 D8). He has lost five in a row – the worst ever losing run by an Italian coach in the competition, and Bodo will provide tough competition.
Bodo have won six games in the Champions League in 2026 – already the most victories by a Norwegian side in a single year in the European Cup/Champions League.
They beat Bundesliga heavyweights Borussia Dortmund 1-0 last time out, responding well to their 5-0 thrashing against Bayern Munich in the first match of their campaign.
And they have previous against Serie A sides in the competition, too. Bodo won both legs against Inter in the play-off round last term.
Prior to this, Norwegian teams had only won once against Italian opponents in the European Cup/Champions League (D4 L8): AC Milan 1-2 Rosenborg in December 1996.
"Only we can get ourselves out of this," Allegri added on Napoli's current form. "If we manage to win, we'll see things differently.
"You have to question yourself every day. I've always done that, and I'll keep doing it as long as I enjoy this job. I'm sorry the players have been criticised in a certain way.
"Players must be defended and helped, even in difficult moments. They all have my unconditional trust. But when things are difficult, they mustn't be thrown overboard.
"They have to lift their heads and show they're worthy of Napoli."

dslzy2l7msrj12uqh4her5gca.title: Haaland calls for Man City to 'stick together' after Premier League verdict
dslzy2l7msrj12uqh4her5gca.subtitle: After Manchester City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's rules, Erling Haaland called for unity from everyone at the club.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland says everyone at Manchester City must "stick together" when they visit Liverpool on Sunday, off the back of the club being found guilty of breaching Premier League rules.

During the international break, it was confirmed that City had been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and the majority of charges in relation to their failure to co-operate with the league's investigation.

While City have appealed the verdict and continue to maintain their innocence, it has thrown the Premier League into turmoil, with the Citizens having lifted the title three times in the period covered by the breaches.

A trip to Anfield on Sunday is sure to mean a frosty reception for City's players, but Haaland – who scored the winner when they last visited Liverpool in February – is determined to enjoy the occasion.
"We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive," Haaland told City's media channels.
"No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile. We have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game.
"We have to spread the love to each other. So yeah, stick together, enjoy the ride and smile."
Haaland joined City in 2022 from Borussia Dortmund and has gone on to win eight major honours, including two Premier League titles and the 2022-23 Champions League.
During that time, he has scored 169 goals in 205 appearances across all competitions, further proving his credentials as one of the deadliest finishers in world football.
The 26-year-old, the son of former City player Alf-Inge Haaland, also referenced his love for Man City amid all the uncertainty around the club, while also expressing his affection for Manchester.
"I care a lot about this place – and the UK generally. My mother as well as my father, they lived here for 10 years – they lived in Nottingham and Leeds.
"They never lived in Manchester, but obviously my father trained over at Carrington every day.
"I spent my first four years here, my brother nine and my sister six, so it's a special place for us. I care a lot about City, I have to say.
"I care a lot about the fans because I'm a fan myself – I feel it with them as well."

dwgglypi015r10pbsf872bw5l.title: Alvarez apologises to Atletico fans over push to join Barca
dwgglypi015r10pbsf872bw5l.subtitle: Julian Alvarez was vocal about his wishes to leave Atletico Madrid at the World Cup, and he has now apologised for his comments.
paragraphs: Julian Alvarez netted the winner for Atletico Madrid against Deportivo A Coruna and then apologised for trying to force a move to Barcelona over the summer.

The transfer saga surrounding Alvarez was the talk of the recent transfer window, as he said he wanted to leave Atletico during an interview at the World Cup, with Barcelona his preferred destination.
The striker ultimately stayed at Atletico and has been eased back into action by Diego Simeone.

He scored his first goal of the season in their 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in the Champions League in midweek and followed that up with a 48th-minute goal to secure a 1-0 win over Deportivo to move Atleti within two points of leaders Barcelona, who face rivals Real Madrid on Sunday.
"I want to apologise to our fans for my words during the World Cup," Alvarez told Movistar, as quoted by ESPN. "It was a mistake in terms of how I expressed myself and the timing.
"I understand the fans' [anger], especially given how they've supported me since I arrived. They have been very generous toward me. Now it's time for me to get to work and give everything I've got.
"I'm feeling better and better. I've always had support. I'm working on improving. I'm feeling better physically.
"When you feel good in life, it shows on the pitch. Even though we are professionals, everything has an impact."

Alvarez has scored in two consecutive matches for Atletico in all competitions for the first time since April, when he scored in the Copa final against Real Sociedad and in the first leg of the Champions League semi-finals against Arsenal.
Simeone has maintained his support for Alvarez throughout the whole saga and noted how important he is to the club's continued development.
"I have a great deal of respect for people who apologise, because apologising is not easy," Simeone said. "I'm very happy for [Alvarez]; he must feel a great sense of peace.
"When someone says something like that, it's because they truly mean it. As for the player, I'm absolutely delighted. We need him.
"If the club wants to reach the heights the fans dream of, we need Julian Alvarez to be at his best."
Atletico have now won each of their last six LaLiga matches, keeping a clean sheet in the last two.

dwhshekgvvba13w6xy4o6d9le.title: Messi will leave Argentina legacy that is 'unequalled', says Scaloni
dwhshekgvvba13w6xy4o6d9le.subtitle: Lionel Messi will pull on an Argentina shirt for the very last time against Benin, capping a stunning international career.
paragraphs: Lionel Scaloni says Lionel Messi is leaving behind "something incomparable" as he prepares to play his final match for Argentina.
Messi announced his international retirement in the aftermath of Argentina's World Cup final loss to Spain but will play one last game for the Albiceleste on home soil to say farewell to the fans.
The 39-year-old will face Benin on Tuesday, earning his 208th cap – the most of any player in the nation's history.
He also has more goals for Argentina than any other player (125) and more goal involvements at the World Cup than anyone else in history (33 – 21 goals, 12 assists).
Over the summer, he became the only man to start three World Cup finals, having led Argentina to glory in 2022, and also lifting two Copa Americas on either side of that triumph.
And as he prepares for his final-ever Argentina appearance, Scaloni once again heaped praise on his team's talisman.
"Messi leaves behind something unequalled," Scaloni said.
"We have to keep playing, but the feeling of having him on the pitch is unique. I've never seen anyone else convey what he does on a football field, and that is what we're going to miss.
"Only nostalgia remains now that he won't be there. He is an incredible example. The first to arrive, the last to leave, how he takes care of himself, how he faces each game.
"You can see he is a phenomenon just by how he plays, but he has things behind him that his team-mates see, and he is the best example there can be.
"He has left – or is leaving, because he has one more game – something incomparable."
Argentina have a so-far perfect record without Messi in the side, having beaten Bolivia 4-0 and Burkina Faso 7-0 across their two friendlies.

dwzioag14i691fct96u5wlzj9.title: Pochettino: Young stars like Sullivan do not come around often
dwzioag14i691fct96u5wlzj9.subtitle: Cavan Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in the United States' history on Saturday, drawing big praise from Mauricio Pochettino.
paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino admits it is difficult to find young players with the quality of Cavan Sullivan, and he knows the United States need to nurture the 17-year-old's talent.
The USA thrashed rivals Mexico 3-0 in Arizona on Saturday, earning their third victory in as many games during this extended international break.
Their young stars shone brightly once again, with 18-year-old Julian Hall scoring for the third time in his first three senior caps, while Sullivan made a piece of history in the second half.
Having intercepted an errant pass from Raul Rangel and lobbed the Mexico goalkeeper from distance, Sullivan – at the age of 17 years and five days – became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.
He surpassed Borussia Dortmund's Mathis Albert just four days after he claimed the record from Christian Pulisic, netting at the age of 17 years and 131 days against Chile.
The USA have one more game to play this month, against Canada in Minnesota on Tuesday, and Pochettino is determined to give his young players further chances to impress.
"It's amazing to have these talented players that appear now, and it's important for us – it is a big, big moment," Pochettino said.
"It's a big moment because we need to get it right with them. We need to protect them. We need to support them.
"Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction. Today, they were so exciting.
"We need to continue with that idea, to keep that feeling – every time that they can be part of this national team, it's the most important thing."

Asked about Sullivan specifically, Pochettino said of the Philadelphia Union's breakout star: "He's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession.
"He's a fighter. He's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player, no?"
Sullivan told TNT Sports of his history-making strike: "These are moments you dream of since you're three, four, five or six years old. I manifested this moment.
"I probably shouldn't have pressed the goalie; it felt like there was not really anybody pressing behind me. But that's why you go and that's why you put the work in, and I was rewarded for doing so.
"From there, it was sort of a blackout. I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn't hit the crossbar or go over. I was getting nervous when it was in the air!"
Sullivan has also had a tremendous campaign for the Union in MLS, breaking single-season records for the most assists (12) and total goal involvements (19, seven goals) by a teenager.

e0vzkxwnwopq1e9klizsa5qxg.title: Chivu: Inter now ready to suffer in the Champions League
e0vzkxwnwopq1e9klizsa5qxg.subtitle: Inter defeated Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 for their first Champions League win of the season, and Cristian Chivu saw positive signs.
paragraphs: Cristian Chivu believes his Inter side "were ready to suffer" in their Champions League meeting with Shakhtar Donetsk.
Having lost their opening two games in the league phase this season, Inter finally got into the win column after defeating Shakhtar 1-0 at San Siro.
Carlos Augusto scored the winner in the 77th minute for the Nerazzurri, who saw Alessandro Bastoni receive two yellow cards in two minutes and 18 seconds after the hour mark.
Inter ended their four-game losing streak in the Champions League, as well as their four-game losing streak in home games in the competition.
Augusto has scored in each of his last two games in the Champions League, after scoring just one goal across his first 27 games in the competition.
Chivu praised his side's resilience in the win, claiming Inter lacked fight in their previous defeats.
"I think our Champions League results in the last year and a half left some traces and it showed in the first half," Chivu told Sky Sport Italia.

"It wasn't a bad start, but as the match went on, we got a bit worried about maintaining organisation against a quality side that can pass it well. We did hold back a bit, but rediscovered a little energy, mobility and the right runs with the triple substitution.
"After that, we went down to 10 men and were able to add that something extra we had been lacking. We rolled our sleeves up, realised we needed to do everything to stay united.
"It's not always the prettiest football that gets you results, sometimes you need heart and mentality, accepting that extra effort. It's what the lads did.
"We were ready to suffer and I feel that was something we'd lacked before."

e1pbr50nzgu1f27y3zy4bhwj.title: 'It is still his house' – Maresca welcomes Guardiola's Man City return
e1pbr50nzgu1f27y3zy4bhwj.subtitle: Manchester City face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, with former boss Pep Guardiola expected to be in attendance.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca welcomed the attendance of Pep Guardiola at Manchester City's Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain, maintaining "it is still his house".
City return to the Etihad Stadium for the first time since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations against the European champions on Wednesday.
The Citizens produced a statement performance in their first outing since the verdict was released, beating Liverpool at Anfield 3-0 to maintain their perfect start in the league.
But now their attention turns to the Champions League, with Luis Enrique's side the visitors to Manchester in a match that will see former boss Guardiola return to the club.
Guardiola resigned as City's manager in May following a trophy-laden stint with the club, and he has been vocal in his support of the team he managed for a decade.
In a post on social media last month, Guardiola addressed the City fans and said they would "get through this together", adding he would always "be behind my club".
The Spaniard won 20 major trophies during his time with City, including six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five EFL Cups and the Champions League in 2022-23.

Maresca had made a strong start to life in Manchester, winning eight of his first nine games across all competitions, but the City boss is looking forward to welcoming Guardiola back to the club he enjoyed so much success at.
"I spoke with Pep, as I said a few days ago, after the [Manchester] United game. I didn't speak with him after that," Maresca told reporters.
"If he is coming, it is a nice feeling, especially for him; it has been his house for 10 years. It is still his house because of what he has done here. I think it is exciting for everyone."
Maresca added that he did not know Guardiola's exact plans, whether he intended to go into the home dressing room before the game or on to the pitch.
But with the noise off the pitch, Maresca's full attention was on matters on it ahead of facing PSG, with the Ligue 1 giants aiming to continue their strong start to their title defence.
This will be the ninth meeting between City and PSG, with the Citizens winning four of the last eight (D2 L2) and going unbeaten in the four matches they have hosted (W3 D1).

Of the teams they have faced 5+ times in major European competition, only against Bayern Munich (52.9% – 9/17) have the Parisiens lost a higher percentage of their matches than against City (50% – 4/8), but Luis Enrique's side are in fine form in the Champions League.
PSG are unbeaten in their last 11 games in the competition (W7 D4), only once having a longer run without defeat, when they put together a 13-match streak between October 2012 and November 2013.

They could also become just the second team to go 10+ consecutive games against English sides in the European Cup/Champions League without losing (currently unbeaten in nine – W7 D2), after Real Madrid between 2011 and 2017 (11 games), and Maresca acknowledged City had to be "perfect" to win.
"The message for [Wednesday] is quite easy, in terms of winning the perfect game, because they're the best team in Europe in this moment," Maresca added.
"They won the last two Champions Leagues, so that shows how good they are, so we need the perfect game but, at the same time, doing our best.
"I think we can beat them and be happy at the end."

"I spoke with Pep, as I said a few days ago, after the [Manchester] United game. I didn't speak with him after that," Maresca told reporters.

"If he is coming, it is a nice feeling, especially for him; it has been his house for 10 years. It is still his house because of what he has done here. I think it is exciting for everyone."

Maresca added that he did not know Guardiola's exact plans, whether he intended to go into the home dressing room before the game or on to the pitch.

But with the noise off the pitch, Maresca's full attention was on matters on it ahead of facing PSG, with the Ligue 1 giants aiming to continue their strong start to their title defence. 

This will be the ninth meeting between City and PSG, with the Citizens winning four of the last eight (D2 L2) and going unbeaten in the four matches they have hosted (W3 D1).

Of the teams they have faced 5+ times in major European competition, only against Bayern Munich (52.9% – 9/17) have the Parisiens lost a higher percentage of their matches than against City (50% – 4/8), but Luis Enrique's side are in fine form in the Champions League. 

PSG are unbeaten in their last 11 games in the competition (W7 D4), only once having a longer run without defeat, when they put together a 13-match streak between October 2012 and November 2013.

They could also become just the second team to go 10+ consecutive games against English sides in the European Cup/Champions League without losing (currently unbeaten in nine – W7 D2), after Real Madrid between 2011 and 2017 (11 games), and Maresca acknowledged City had to be "perfect" to win. 

"The message for [Wednesday] is quite easy, in terms of winning the perfect game, because they're the best team in Europe in this moment," Maresca added. 

"They won the last two Champions Leagues, so that shows how good they are, so we need the perfect game but, at the same time, doing our best. 

"I think we can beat them and be happy at the end."

e4urb2jfczeg1puiz58kg2vu5.title: Brighton boss Hurzeler claims only 'one team' tried to create chances at Anfield
e4urb2jfczeg1puiz58kg2vu5.subtitle: Brighton's fantastic run of form in the Premier League came to an end as they were beaten 2-0 by Liverpool at Anfield.
paragraphs: Fabian Hurzeler took a swipe at Liverpool's performance as he claimed his Brighton side were the only team trying to play attacking football at Anfield on Sunday.
Brighton went into the contest on the back of four straight Premier League wins, with those victories having come with an aggregate score of 15-0.

Yet the Seagulls' soaring form was snapped as they lost 2-0, with Liverpool's goals coming in a four-minute spell in the first half. Pascal Gross turned into his own net before Alexander Isak tucked in from Bradley Barcola's cross.
Yasin Ayari squandered a golden chance early on, before he hit the post after Liverpool had taken a 2-0 lead.
Brighton had 66.7% possession in the second half but failed to get any of their nine attempts on target, although Trey Nyoni did make a crucial block to frustrate Maxim De Cuyper.
Hurzeler's team finished having created chances worth a combined 1.35 expected goals (xG) to Liverpool's 0.87, although Brighton only had one attempt on target all game.
However, the German felt his team were the ones focused on creating opportunities.
"I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game, and therefore I have to praise my players," Hurzeler told reporters.
"I think everyone in the stadium, and you as well, felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it's not only after the goal or the goals they scored.
"Also, before they scored, we had one or two big chances and I think it was just the difference that they scored, [and] we didn't score.
"They kept a clean sheet because they defended well with their centre-backs, with full-backs [Ronald] Araujo and [Milos] Kerkez.

"I think they blocked a lot of shots. They really defended the box well. We didn't have that efficiency. We couldn't keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes; we lost some important personal duels."

Brighton have suffered their joint-most away defeats in the Premier League against Liverpool (seven – also Manchester City), with this now their joint-longest run of defeats at Anfield in the competition (four).
Their 17 shots were their most in a match in the Premier League when managing one or fewer attempts on target.

Liverpool’s possession (35.6%), meanwhile, was their second-lowest on record (since 2003-04) in a Premier League home win, and their lowest in an Anfield league victory since November 2010 (35.3% v Chelsea).
And Hurzeler conceded it felt like a chance missed for Brighton.
He added: "Overall, I saw a team with a lot of good things to take away.

"I saw a team that really had belief in our approach, that stuck to the match plan, that always kept going, and that is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity."

edyuf1luv2sy1s1ww8cv0lxcl.title: Sullivan always 'finds a way' to help Philadelphia, says Richter
edyuf1luv2sy1s1ww8cv0lxcl.subtitle: Teenage sensation Cavan Sullivan played a big part in helping the Philadelphia Union to a seventh straight win.
paragraphs: Philadelphia Union interim head coach Ryan Richter hailed Cavan Sullivan's ability to "find a way to create goals" after the youngster racked up more assists in their 2-1 win over Real Salt Lake.
The Union are now up to sixth in the Eastern Conference after continuing their impressive winning streak, stretching it to seven games.
Bruno Damiani and Milan Iloski scored the goals for Philadelphia, with Sullivan playing a big part in both, before Saba Lobjanidze netted a 96th-minute consolation.
The Union are unbeaten in their last 13 matches, since a 6-4 loss to Inter Miami before the World Cup break.

With his two assists, Sullivan set the MLS single-season record for goal contributions by a teenager (21), surpassing Alphonso Davies (19 in 2018 for the Vancouver Whitecaps) and Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013 for the New England Revolution).
He had three shots – worth just 0.1 expected goals (xG) – and only four touches in the opposition box, though he created a joint-team-high two chances against Real Salt Lake.
And though Ritcher did not believe Sullivan was at his best, he was still impressed by the youngster's impact.
"I did not think it was his best game," said Richter. "He was solid, I would say.

"Even in a game where he wasn't electric in the way he has been in most games, he still has a hand in the first goal for the assist, and then he kind of makes the play that leads to the action for the second goal.
"Even when everything is not coming off perfectly… he still finds a way to create both goals that we had."
While Philadelphia have boosted their postseason hopes, Vancouver clinched their playoff berth in the West after a 1-1 draw with Los Angeles FC.
Despite having Tristan Blackmon sent off in the sixth minute, Vancouver scored first through Oliver Larraz and held out for a point after Denis Bouanga's equaliser.

Toronto FC also closed in on the playoffs after a stunning comeback against rivals CF Montreal, scoring twice in second-half stoppage time to win 2-1 and move within four points of ninth-place FC Cincinnati.
And Antoine Griezmann starred for Orlando City, who are up to seventh in the East, as he got a goal and an assist in their last-gasp 3-2 win over the Columbus Crew.

efwf044viaw185tmz9yaupc2.title: PSG hunting down Champions League three-peat
efwf044viaw185tmz9yaupc2.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain have enjoyed great success under Luis Enrique, and the Spaniard is hunting a third straight Champions League title.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique is convinced Paris Saint-Germain are capable of a Champions League three-peat.
PSG have won back-to-back Champions League crowns under Luis Enrique, who has also guided the French club to three Ligue 1 titles and two Coupe de France triumphs.
Luis Enrique's team started their Ligue 1 campaign poorly, but have now won three straight top-flight games.
They opened their Champions League campaign with a 6-1 thrashing of Slovan Bratislava, with a trip to Manchester City next up on Wednesday.
The only team to win the Champions League in three successive seasons were Real Madrid, between 2016 and 2018.
And while Luis Enrique feels there is now even more pressure on him to deliver, he has no doubt his team have the quality to go again in Europe this term.

"I've extended my contract, and now I'm under even more pressure to show that I'm ready to carry on and that I still want to win many more trophies for Paris Saint-Germain," he told PSG's official channels.

"I am not calmer or more relaxed simply because people tell me they are very happy. Parisians often tell me: 'You have changed our lives', but we have to be careful not to exaggerate the importance of football. There are many things in life that are more important.
"We've won it [Champions League] twice in a row, but that's no reason to stop.
"We're built to play in the Champions League. We have an extra incentive: to try and achieve something that only Real Madrid has managed to do so far. It's a special goal.
"That was our primary objective when we arrived here: to make history.

"Everyone knew the club had already won major trophies, but there was no trophy more important to us than the Champions League. For me, as a manager, just as for the players, the desire to win constantly is an essential characteristic of the very highest level."
PSG's clash with City is then followed by another heavyweight contest against Luis Enrique's former club Barcelona next week.
"These [Man City and Barcelona] are two teams that love winning the Champions League, who have already won it and who are among the favourites," Luis Enrique said.
"There are six, seven or eight teams capable of winning this Champions League. We're one of them, but it'll be tough, and we're not the clear favourites."

Since Luis Enrique took charge in July 2023, PSG have scored 439 goals in 183 competitive matches. That is the third-highest goal tally of any team from Europe's top five leagues, behind Bayern Munich (485) and Barca (467).
PSG rank second for expected goals (413.2) in that time, behind Bayern (430.6), while they average the highest possession (66.9%).
And Luis Enrique has no plans to alter his playing style.
"I am fully convinced that this way of playing is the best way to win," he added.

"Normally, I don't always manage to establish this connection. In Paris, it was different. There was a real connection with the fans, with the club, and with this shared desire to improve. There's also the trust Luis Campos placed in me, the quality of the players we recruited, and their ability to adapt to our vision of football.

"This is the first time in my coaching career that this story has lasted this long. It's not easy to stay two, three, or four years at a club. You're constantly connected, always preoccupied with the team's preparation and everything that's important to it."

eli7e22tu9pp1led95m09wxtb.title: Simeone: Atletico's away league form forgotten ahead of Stuttgart trip
eli7e22tu9pp1led95m09wxtb.subtitle: Atletico Madrid have won four of their five away matches in LaLiga, with a clash away to Stuttgart in the Champions League up next.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone insisted Atletico Madrid's excellent away form in LaLiga has been forgotten ahead of their trip to Stuttgart in the Champions League on Tuesday.
Atletico have made an excellent start to their league campaign, taking 22 points from their opening nine games, though they are still five adrift of league leaders Barcelona.
Simeone's side arrive into this clash fresh from a 1-0 victory over Espanyol, with Alex Baena's 89th-minute winner making it four wins from their first five league away games.
Their only top-flight defeat on the road this season came on September 5 against Athletic Club (3-0), though they were beaten on MD1 of the Champions League by Liverpool.

Atletico have also lost each of their last five away games against German sides in the Champions League, as well as eight of their last nine trips overall (W1). The only exception in this run was a 4-2 win at Bayer Leverkusen in February 2017 (last 16).

They have also failed to win their third group/league phase game in the Champions League since a 1-0 win over Leverkusen in 2019-20, losing on MD3 in four of the last six seasons (D2), something Simeone is aiming to change.

Simeone's side won 2-0 against Manchester United on MD2 but they have not kept consecutive clean sheets in the Champions League since February 2020, and the Argentine is expecting another difficult test for his players against a Stuttgart team that have won their opening two matches in Europe.
"The truth is that I have forgotten everything that happened before," Simeone said. "They will quickly forget what they are praising and will value us for what they do tomorrow.

"We're facing a tough match against a physically strong team, one that clearly understands the concept of pressing in the opponent's half, almost always man-to-man, and that drops very deep when it has to defend."
Atletico's travelling squad for their trip to Germany was named earlier on Monday, with Cristian Romero the most notable absentee in Simeone's ranks.
Romero, who joined Atletico from Tottenham this summer, has sustained a muscle injury and has not been risked, while club captain Koke is also unavailable.
"The importance of Cuti is clear, but the whole makes us all better," Simeone added on Romero's absence.
"We are not going to go out of this line, the team is more important than the individual."
Atletico have never won the Champions League but have been close on several occasions, losing in the final twice in 2013-14 and 2015-16, both against rivals Real Madrid.

They reached the semi-finals of the competition last season, losing to beaten finalists Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate, and defender David Hanko believes their near-miss in Europe in 2025-26 will only help improve their chances this year.
"The feeling from last season is that we were so close to achieving so much: the cup, the Champions League," Hanko said.
"We were left with the feeling of reaching the end but not quite making it. We're using that experience to improve this year."

er93r6j9ultq1rdi16m9e8gnh.title: Emery and Villa chasing consistency to challenge the top teams
er93r6j9ultq1rdi16m9e8gnh.subtitle: Aston Villa and Fulham are both moving in the right direction after poor starts to the season, and a winning streak apiece is on the line.
paragraphs: Unai Emery highlighted the importance of consistency for Aston Villa as they continue to attempt to challenge at the top of the Premier League, with Fulham up next.
Villa have been in and around the Champions League places in the last few seasons and flirted with a title challenge last term before falling out of contention and finishing fourth.

They initially struggled at the start of the season – as they did in 2025-26 – failing to win their first four games, but they have since won three of the four since (L1), including a 2-1 win over league leaders Manchester City last time out.
They did lose 3-0 to Bournemouth in the EFL Cup in midweek, missing out on a place in the quarter-finals.

Villa are currently ninth in a congested mid-table, but they have their sights set higher up the standings, and Emery is confident his team can continue to challenge the notion of the competition's 'big six'.

"I think the Premier League is very, very difficult because there are a lot of teams not in the contender positions at the beginning of the season, to be in the top positions, but every year, they are always fighting with the teams who should be there," Emery said.
"We are one of the teams, and last year, we achieved it. So, this is the target. This is, as well, the process. We want to try to get consistency, but each year is a test.
"Fulham as well, last year, they were being consistent in the table, in the middle positions, but always fighting to be close with the top seven, top six teams."
Fulham also endured a tough start to life under Alvaro Arbeloa, failing to win their first six Premier League outings, but they have since beaten Hull City and Coventry City.
Like Villa, Fulham come into this game on the back of an EFL Cup defeat – despite dominating against Crystal Palace, they lost 1-0 on Wednesday.
Ahead of Saturday's clash, Arbeloa was full of praise for his opposite number.
"When you see his career, his titles, the job that he did at every club, I think he is one of the best Spanish coaches in our history," Arbeloa said.
"I think right now he is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good; he improves everything every year.

"He knows what he wants from his players, and obviously when some new players came, it's a new process, it's like almost a new team, and he needs time. It's normal, but you can see right now how they are performing."
Aston Villa – Nicolas Jackson

Nicolas Jackson has scored four goals in his last four Premier League appearances for Villa, as many as he had managed in his previous 24 games in the competition (four in 21 for Chelsea, 0 in three for Villa).
Only Man City duo Erling Haaland (2.92) and Rayan Cherki (2.32) have outperformed their xG more than Jackson this season (2.02).
Two of the four players with the most touches in the opposition box in the Premier League this season are Josh King (52, first) and Oscar Bobb (43, fourth).
King is averaging 7.1 per 90 minutes, with only one Fulham player on record (since 2008-09, 500+ mins played) averaging more in a season – Bobby Zamora in 2010-11 (8.6).
MATCH PREDICTION: ASTON VILLA WIN
Villa have lost just one of their 18 home Premier League matches against Fulham (W12 D5), a 2-1 defeat in April 2014.
And they are looking to win three consecutive Premier League matches for the first time since a run of eight in November and December last season.
Fulham did, however, win their last top-flight game against Villa and have registered consecutive wins against them just once before in the competition, winning both games in 2013-14.
But Fulham are also looking for three Premier League wins in a row for the first time since December 2025, while they last achieved that without conceding a goal back in April 2019.
Villa have only won two of their last 12 Premier League matches in August and September (D5 L5), compared to eight wins in their last 10 games across October and November (D1 L1).

Nicolas Jackson has scored four goals in his last four Premier League appearances for Villa, as many as he had managed in his previous 24 games in the competition (four in 21 for Chelsea, 0 in three for Villa).

Fulham – Josh King

Two of the four players with the most touches in the opposition box in the Premier League this season are Josh King (52, first) and Oscar Bobb (43, fourth).

King is averaging 7.1 per 90 minutes, with only one Fulham player on record (since 2008-09, 500+ mins played) averaging more in a season – Bobby Zamora in 2010-11 (8.6).

Villa have lost just one of their 18 home Premier League matches against Fulham (W12 D5), a 2-1 defeat in April 2014.

And they are looking to win three consecutive Premier League matches for the first time since a run of eight in November and December last season.

Fulham did, however, win their last top-flight game against Villa and have registered consecutive wins against them just once before in the competition, winning both games in 2013-14.

But Fulham are also looking for three Premier League wins in a row for the first time since December 2025, while they last achieved that without conceding a goal back in April 2019.

Villa have only won two of their last 12 Premier League matches in August and September (D5 L5), compared to eight wins in their last 10 games across October and November (D1 L1).

evfncmhqwgeg1xgdmv21cayfj.title: Wirtz not set for an immediate introduction to Germany team, says Klopp
evfncmhqwgeg1xgdmv21cayfj.subtitle: Florian Wirtz was one of two call-ups to replace injured players in Germany's squad, but Jurgen Klopp plans to ease him into the fold.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp has no intention of throwing Florian Wirtz straight into his starting line-up for Germany against Greece in the Nations League.

Wirtz had initially been named in Klopp's second squad for the extended international break, but following injuries to Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala, he was brought into the fold a game earlier than planned.
He arrived at the team's training base on Friday and has only had time for one training session with Germany as they prepare for their next match.
It will be Klopp's first on home soil as Germany's head coach – following a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands in his opener – but Wirtz will not be starting the match.
"That would really be a huge ask," Klopp replied when asked if Wirtz was an immediate candidate to start.
"He found out [Friday] morning, arrived here in the evening, and then we say: now that you're here, go straight in and play.
"That would certainly be the worst thing we could do right now."
Wirtz has had a difficult start to this season, coming under criticism for his Liverpool performances so far this season, particularly after their 1-0 victory over Bournemouth.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool in all competitions this term, registering just one assist, despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
But Klopp, while wary of talking about a Liverpool player as the club’s former manager, is confident Wirtz will only improve.
"No matter what I would say, whether positive or negative, it would be a huge story in this case," Klopp said of Wirtz's situation at Liverpool.
"Flo Wirtz's footballing abilities are beyond any doubt. We will work together on making sure he can show them on the pitch again every three days.

"We will absolutely try whatever we can contribute towards that. In general, I think he is on a very good path. But the world we live in is basically such that things never happen quickly enough for people."
Klopp's debut as Germany boss did not go exactly to plan, with the Netherlands equalising in the 92nd minute, through his former player Cody Gakpo, to deny him all three points.
But Klopp will be determined to make a winning start in Augsburg as he gets the chance to lead the team in front of the home fans for the first time.
Marc-Andre ter Stegen played a huge role in making sure Germany stayed in the game, making nine saves against the Netherlands, who had 22 attempts in total worth 3.2 expected goals (xG).
However, Klopp confirmed he will be making a change to his goalkeeper for the clash with Greece, as Alexander Nubel is set to come in.
"I heard that Marc was viewed critically – that surprised me after a game where the opposing coach said he saved our bacon," Klopp said.
"He made some outstanding saves, but twice he played a ball he didn't intend to – it happens. I'm not at all critical about it, but very happy with his performance.
"Alex will still get to play, not because of that. He deserves it too. I hope he enjoys it and keeps a clean sheet."

evjv177sn6az1n5tofp8cv5dq.title: Ronaldo-Jesus row cannot divide Portugal, says Fernandes
evjv177sn6az1n5tofp8cv5dq.subtitle: Bruno Fernandes says Cristiano Ronaldo remains Portugal's 'greatest symbol', even amid the fallout from his explosive exit from their camp.
paragraphs: Bruno Fernandes says Portugal's players, staff and fans cannot allow the row between Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus to divide them.

Earlier this week, Ronaldo abruptly left Portugal's camp amid reports that he was disgruntled with Jesus making him an unused substitute during a 2-1 Nations League win in Norway, saying he would tell his side of the story in due course.
Jesus has refused to go into detail about his disagreement with Ronaldo, only saying that he would never allow any player to dictate his decisions as a coach.
Without Ronaldo, Fernandes wore the captain's armband for the Selecao on Thursday, as they earned an entertaining 4-2 win over Denmark.
They have won each of their first three games in Nations League Group A4, with some supporters asking whether their attacking play is more fluid without the 41-year-old.

Since the start of 2025, Portugal have won 80% of their matches when Ronaldo has not appeared (P5 W4 D1), compared to 59% when he has featured (P17 W10 D4 L3), also averaging almost twice as many goals per game without Ronaldo (3.4) than with him (1.9).
But Fernandes, a former club-mate of Ronaldo's at Manchester United, says people should avoid taking sides amid the controversy.
His main concerns are that those who remain in the Portugal camp stay united, and that Ronaldo is remembered as Portugal's greatest-ever player if his international career is over.

"I had a conversation with Cristiano, and what I told him, which I'll repeat here, is this: 'The most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country,'" Fernandes told reporters on Saturday.
"He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things.
"[The players] are outside this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices and respects all sides.
"But, at the same time, Cristiano is and will be the biggest icon of our national team. He deserves everyone's respect, regardless of who likes him more or less."

Ronaldo's 146 goals in 234 caps are the most by any male player in international football history, and he and great rival Lionel Messi became the first players to play at six different editions of the World Cup this year.

But while Messi led Argentina to a second straight final, scoring eight times and becoming the first player to start three showpiece matches at FIFA's flagship tournament, Ronaldo was restricted to three goals – a group-stage brace against Uzbekistan and a penalty against Croatia in the round of 32.
That spot-kick is the only goal Ronaldo has ever scored in a knockout-stage match at the World Cup, with his other 10 goals at the tournament coming in the group stage.
Porto's Estadio do Dragao will be the venue for Portugal's reverse fixture against Norway on Sunday, with Stale Solbakken's team only having three points on the board so far.

ew0wjim58mdx1tcayvn238nmg.title: Celtic boss O'Neill remains optimistic despite thrashing at Benfica
ew0wjim58mdx1tcayvn238nmg.subtitle: Celtic fell to a heavy defeat against Benfica in the Europa League, but Martin O'Neill is confident his side can bounce back.
paragraphs: Martin O'Neill is confident his Celtic side can still reach the knockout rounds of the Europa League despite their defeat to Benfica.
Celtic were thrashed 4-1 at Estadio da Luz after a brace from Jhon Duran and goals from Vangelis Pavlidis and Alexander Bah, leaving the Scottish side with 0 points after two games.

Benfica took the lead after just five minutes as Duran won a penalty and scored a Panenka against Viljami Sinisalo; it is the earliest penalty goal Celtic have ever conceded in major European competition.
Gianluca Prestianni then came to the fore, assisting Bah and Duran before half-time as Marco Silva's side were cruising to a big win.
Camilo Duran managed to pull a goal back for Celtic, but Benfica still had the last say as Pavlidis scored in the 89th minute.
In all competitions, Celtic have lost four of their last five games (W1) – as many as in their previous 36 games combined (W28 D4 L4).
Celtic have also kept just five clean sheets in their last 54 major European matches, while they have kept just two in their last 30 in the Europa League.
Nevertheless, O'Neill felt their second-half display provided reason for optimism, despite Benfica striking the woodwork twice after the break and creating more chances (14 shots to Celtic's nine).
"Last thing you want to do is concede so early on. We could've capitulated, but I thought the second-half performance was terrific. We created chance after chance," O'Neill told TNT Sports.
"The second-half performance gives me the determination. I think we can still qualify. We can still do it.
"We came roaring back, the subs came on and did brilliantly. We could've scored a number of goals. It changed because two wide players really wanted to get at people.
"I accept on the break they could have scored themselves, as they did with their fourth goal."

eybpt7bgxlie16rhj71am0tgg.title: Le Bris has confidence in Sunderland backups as Brobbey misses Brighton clash
eybpt7bgxlie16rhj71am0tgg.subtitle: Sunderland will be without Brian Brobbey against Brighton, but Regis Le Bris expects his team to cope while he is out injured.
paragraphs: Regis Le Bris is confident Sunderland have the attacking depth to cope with Brian Brobbey's absence versus Brighton, who he feels have made a near-perfect start to the season.
Sunderland emerge from the international break 14th in the Premier League table with four points from five games, the most recent of which was a 5-3 defeat to Manchester City.

Brobbey scored a hat-trick in that match, becoming the first player to score a Premier League treble and finish on the losing side since December 2007, when Roque Santa Cruz did so for Blackburn Rovers against Wigan Athletic.

Brobbey then suffered a hamstring injury while representing the Netherlands, but he is not expected to miss a significant amount of time, and Le Bris is confident the Black Cats can handle his short-term absence.
"I'm happy – we set a clear picture of this position with three strikers. I think Brian is in a really good place and he's started the season really well," Le Bris said.
"A small injury is not a problem, but it's true we'd like to have him fit.
"We have Wilson [Isidor], who is a really good striker with a different style of play but really competitive for the Premier League and showed his qualities last season."
Brighton have been one of the stories of the season so far, and they spent the international break in third place after routing champions Arsenal 3-0 in their most recent game.
The Seagulls, who also crushed Coventry City 5-0 on matchday four, are the Premier League's leading scorers this term with 16 goals, and their dazzling form led to a monthly award double.
Head coach Fabian Hurzeler was named Manager of the Month and midfielder Pascal Gross earned the players' prize, which Le Bris said was richly deserved.
"They are good – the Player of the Month and Manager of the Month were well deserved. It was a perfect start," he said of Brighton.
"A really good team, well coached, good energy, with a high press – they are modern and really efficient. We like this challenge.
"This is the Premier League and it is relentless. We don't want fear, we are just excited for the challenge and it's going to be a tough test."
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Sunderland – Granit Xhaka

Only Youri Tielemans (37) has made more line-breaking passes into the final third this season than Sunderland captain Xhaka (36), while only three players have made more line-breaking passes leading to shots than his 12.
Brighton – Pascal Gross
In 2026, only Bruno Fernandes (98) and Dominik Szoboszlai (58) have created more Premier League chances than Brighton midfielder Gross (54), who also ranks sixth for expected assists (4.68 xA).
He could now become only the second midfielder to both score and assist in three successive Premier League games, after Cesc Fabregas for Arsenal in September 2007.
MATCH PREDICTION – BRIGHTON WIN
Sunderland have won just one of their eight top-flight meetings with Brighton (D2 L5), beating them 3-0 at Roker Park in May 1982.
But the Seagulls have a poor record away against Sunderland, with a 1-0 win in this exact fixture last campaign being their only victory in their last 10 league trips (D2 L7).
Sunderland have lost their last two Premier League games, against last season's top two in Arsenal (0-2) and Man City (3-5).
They only lost three in a row once in 2025-26, doing so in February against the Gunners (0-3), Liverpool (0-1) and Fulham (1-3).
Brighton, meanwhile, have won their last two Premier League games by an aggregate score of 8-0; only in October 2018 have they won three successive matches in the competition without conceding.

eyjsro6ino351x8tu8qcyqbs7.title: Alaba ready to 'build a new chapter' at Udinese
eyjsro6ino351x8tu8qcyqbs7.subtitle: David Alaba has been officially unveiled as an Udinese player following his signing in September, and he is raring to go.
paragraphs: David Alaba is fit and ready to start his time at Udinese, and he is looking forward to building a "new chapter of my career".
Alaba joined Udinese as a free agent in September, following his departure from Real Madrid at the end of last season.
The 34-year-old brings with him a wealth of European experience, having also spent 13 years with Bayern Munich before making the move to Madrid in 2021.

He won 25 trophies with the Bundesliga giants before going on to win two LaLiga crowns and two Champions League titles, in addition to a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana, a UEFA Super Cup, a Club World Cup and an Intercontinental Cup with Los Blancos.
However, Alaba's later years in Madrid were hampered by injuries, and he managed just 575 minutes across all competitions last term, but he insists there are no issues with his fitness.
"I feel good, and I feel ready to play," Alaba said, as reported by TuttoMercatoWeb.

"I've already been training with the team for about a week, and I trained hard in the previous months. I've spoken often with [Kosta] Runjaic about my role. I've played a lot as a centre-back, and I feel comfortable there.
"I've played in other positions too, but mainly I feel good as a centre-back. As for the clubs, I can say that yes, I spoke with other Italian clubs.
"I know what kind of player I am, and I'm here to play football. I'm here to write the next pages of my story as a footballer.
"I have a lot of experience, and I want to put it at the team's disposal. I'm less interested in the rumours."
Alaba has said he has high ambitions for what he can achieve with Udinese, who are currently 13th in Serie A after five matches.
But Alaba is looking forward to helping the team this season.
"I spoke mainly with the coach, Runjaic, and he convinced me of the project here," Alaba said.
"I took my time to make a decision, and over time I became convinced that this was perhaps the right path. I believe it's the right step for my career.
"I decided to come here not because of my past, but because I'm ambitious and I always want more. It's an important project, and I think it's the right step for my career.
"I don't need to prove anything to myself, but I came here to build a new chapter of my career and to help the team with my quality and experience."
Alaba could make his Udinese debut on Monday when they return to Serie A action against Torino.

eytwkdcmcjzb18fk8aiwfoso3.title: USWNT defender Fox signs new contract with Arsenal
eytwkdcmcjzb18fk8aiwfoso3.subtitle: Arsenal have handed a new contract to Emily Fox, who has been an ever-present for them in the opening three games of their WSL season.
paragraphs: United States defender Emily Fox has signed a new contract with Arsenal, reportedly to run until 2029.
Since arriving from the North Carolina Courage in January 2024, Fox has made 93 appearances for the Gunners in all competitions, scoring three goals from right-back.
She has helped Arsenal win three major trophies during that span, lifting the League Cup in 2023-24, the Champions League trophy in 2024-25 and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup earlier this year.
Fox played the full 90 minutes as the Gunners overcame Barcelona 1-0 in the Champions League final 16 months ago, with Stina Blackstenius scoring the all-important goal in Lisbon.
Fox, who has 78 senior caps for the USWNT at the age of 28, appeared in 20 Women's Super League matches last term as Arsenal finished as runners-up to Manchester City, starting 18 of those games.

Only Alessia Russo (1,832) and Mariona Caldentey (1,747) played more WSL minutes than Fox (1,605) for Renee Slegers' team in 2025-26, and she has also been an ever-present at the start of 2026-27, with Arsenal taking five points from their opening three matches.

f1dxe0lrw1iw1j1x7yn4bk245.title: Ronaldo motivated by 1,000 goals milestone and leading new Portugal generation
f1dxe0lrw1iw1j1x7yn4bk245.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo hinted at international retirement after Portugal's World Cup exit, but he decided against doing so with more to achieve.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo believes he can still help Portugal to further success ahead of their Nations League campaign as he closes in on reaching 1,000 career goals.
Ronaldo had already confirmed that this summer's World Cup would be his last, with Portugal losing to eventual champions Spain in the last 16 of the tournament.
The 41-year-old said he would not make any "rash decisions" over his immediate international future, and he was selected in Jorge Jesus' first Portugal squad.
He reunites with Jesus, who he won his first Saudi Pro League title with at Al-Nassr in 2025-26, and he has a fine record under the new Portugal boss.
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 appearances under Jesus for Al-Nassr in the 2025-26 campaign, averaging a goal every 99 minutes.

Throughout his career, the only managers under whom Ronaldo has a better goals-per-game average in league play are Carlo Ancelotti (1.22) and Jose Mourinho (1.13) at Real Madrid, and Luis Castro and Rudi Garcia at Al-Nassr (both 1.1).

He is currently on 979 career goals, 833 of which have come for clubs and 146 for Portugal, but when asked if he had thought about retiring from international duty after the World Cup, Ronaldo responded: "Yes, I did.
"Of course, I'm always thinking about my decisions, my future, the present also. I'm a thinker, you have to think.
"I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to achieve what they want.
"I think I can give the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football."
Portugal are the reigning Nations League holders, beating Spain on penalties in 2024-25, with Ronaldo also winning the title in 2018-19.
Ronaldo said that adding a third title was also an aim alongside his personal ambitions, adding: "Both aims are important.
"One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it's a new age."
Portugal welcome Wales to the Estadio Jose Alvalade in the first match of their Europa League campaign and the beginning of a new era under Jesus.
It will also be the first meeting between the two nations since the semi-finals of the 2016 European Championship, with the eventual champions Portugal winning 2-0.
Following their clash with Wales, Portugal will face Norway, away first and then at home, either side of a trip to Denmark.

Jesus has also included the likes of Fabio Silva, Renato Veiga, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves and Francisco Conceicao in his 25-man squad, and Ronaldo revealed the decision behind continuing for Portugal was to help guide the nation's up-and-coming talents.
"This is a new young generation. But for me, the basic point is to be on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games," Ronaldo said.
"For me, the most important thing, I know what I am. I know what I do to be here, to have the success that I have.
"I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired in 10 years!
"I'm happy with myself. It doesn't matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest for the next game. For me, the most important thing is that I feel good."

f3cz6xyhync7zw37e3rdhz04.title: Clark relishing 'best experience' despite Seattle Sounders' long winless run
f3cz6xyhync7zw37e3rdhz04.subtitle: The Seattle Sounders and Real Salt Lake are on long winless runs dating back to before the World Cup break, ahead of facing off in MLS.
paragraphs: Caden Clark says the Seattle Sounders' locker room is the best he has ever been part of, despite their MLS winless run standing at 13 games ahead of their clash with Real Salt Lake.
After losing eight games in a row, the Sounders have now played out five consecutive draws, coming from behind in three of those, including in Saturday's 3-3 draw with the Colorado Rapids.
Ahead of welcoming RSL to Lumen Field on Wednesday, Seattle have tumbled all the way down to 13th in the Western Conference, three points adrift of the playoff picture.
Clark scored a last-gasp leveller against Colorado on his debut for Brian Schmetzer's side, having arrived from D.C. United earlier this month.
And despite the Sounders still being without a win in MLS since the World Cup break, Clark told the club's website: "It's been probably the best experience I've had so far being a part of a team.
"The way they go about things, the culture they have, they've been successful in the past for a reason. There's no secret to that.
"They have such a bond and have played together for so long and have high standards.
"Coming into that, I was very fortunate, just trying to learn from them and take that with me and put my best foot forward."
RSL are on a long winless streak of their own, spanning 12 games since they beat the Rapids in May, also prior to the World Cup break.

They are only above Seattle on goal difference, making Wednesday's game a pivotal one in the playoff race, though they have been boosted by Saba Lobjanidze, Morgan Guilavogui and Kobi Henry electing to remain with them during the international break, rather than joining up with their nations.

Head coach Pablo Mastroeni said: "It gives me hope. It gives me belief that the culture is intact, where they would be willing to stay and play for a team that hasn't had a win in... I don't know how long.
"We've got to be dogs. We've got to be disciplined. We've got to work so hard for the guy next to us."
Seattle Sounders – Albert Rusnak
Rusnak assisted two of Seattle's three goals in their draw with Colorado on Saturday, including the stoppage-time equaliser scored by Clark.
He has now assisted five of Seattle's last eight goals, setting up five different players on those goals.
Real Salt Lake – Sergi Solans
Having lost their last two games to nil, RSL are at risk of going three straight MLS games without a goal for the first time since May 2023.
If they are to avoid that fate, then Solans – who leads all of his team-mates for goals (nine) and expected goals (11.4 xG) this year – will have a key role to play.
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
Real Salt Lake have only lost two of their last 12 meetings with the Seattle Sounders in all competitions (W7 D3), including a 2-1 home win on February 28.
RSL are looking to sweep a season series against Seattle for just the third time, after doing so in 2018 and 2022.
And they will be going up against a Sounders team that are on their longest-ever winless run in regular-season play (13 – D5 L8).
But RSL are themselves enduring the joint-longest single-season winless streak in their MLS history, also going 12 without winning in 2005.
So, with home advantage on their side, Seattle could hardly ask for a more ideal fixture to end their rut.
Seattle Sounders – 52.7%
Real Salt Lake – 24.9%

f8fr19a72bf81qm6goqdto6sz.title: Arteta says 'this is only the beginning' after signing new Arsenal contract
f8fr19a72bf81qm6goqdto6sz.subtitle: Mikel Arteta's contract with Arsenal was due to expire at the end of this season, but he has now agreed fresh terms to run until 2030.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta declared last season's Premier League title triumph was "only the beginning" for Arsenal after signing a three-year contract extension at the Emirates Stadium.
On Wednesday, the Gunners confirmed Arteta had agreed to fresh terms to run until 2030, after entering the final year of his previous deal.
Having taken charge of Arsenal – who he represented 150 times as a player between 2011 and 2016 – in November 2019, Arteta has overseen their return to the top of the domestic game.
Following three straight Premier League runner-up finishes in 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, Arteta finally ended Arsenal's 22-year wait to become champions of England in 2025-26.
He also led them to the finals of the FA Cup and the Champions League, though they fell short in both instances, against Manchester City and Paris Saint-Germain respectively.

Arteta's other major trophy came in his first season at the helm, overseeing an FA Cup final success over Chelsea in 2020, and the Gunners have progressed year-on-year under his management, finishing eighth in the Premier League in 2019-20 and 2020-21, fifth in 2021-22, second in each of the next three seasons, then ending their title drought.
Arteta's win rate of 61% through 361 games in charge (W220 D67 L74) is the highest of any manager in Arsenal's history (minimum 25 matches), and he feels there is still more to come.
"This club is unique, with its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue," Arteta told the club's website.
"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together.
"This is such a proud moment for me and my family. I feel the love and respect from our fantastic supporters, and they have mine – and ours – in return."
Arteta has overseen 253 Premier League games with Arsenal, with only Arsene Wenger (828) leading the club for more.

In August, he became only the 10th manager in the competition's history to oversee 250+ games in charge of a single side, after Wenger, Alex Ferguson with Manchester United (810), David Moyes at Everton (now 489), Pep Guardiola at Man City (380), Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool (334), Joe Kinnear with Wimbledon (278), Harry Redknapp at West Ham (269), Alan Curbishley at Charlton Athletic (266) and Sean Dyche at Burnley (258).
The only managers among that group with a better win rate than Arteta (60%) are Ferguson (65%), Guardiola (71%) and Klopp (63%).

Arsenal suffered their first Premier League defeat of the season prior to the international break, going down 3-0 to high-flying Brighton, but they will look to get back on track at home to Leeds United – who are still unbeaten – on Saturday.
