f8xsw4vsq3sw18czoqqjzm11a.title: Kane: Ballon d'Or triumph beyond my wildest dreams
f8xsw4vsq3sw18czoqqjzm11a.subtitle: After beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the 2026 Ballon d'Or, Harry Kane reflected on how far he has come.
paragraphs: Harry Kane admitted winning the Ballon d'Or was an achievement beyond his wildest dreams, after edging out Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to be crowned the world's best player.

The Bayern Munich and England striker claimed football's most prestigious individual prize at a star-studded award ceremony in London on Monday, becoming the fifth English player to do so and the first in 25 years.
Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966), Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) and Michael Owen (2001) had previously claimed the trophy.
Kane's award came after a year in which he helped Bayern Munich retain their Bundesliga crown and captained England to a third-place finish at the World Cup – their best-ever on foreign soil.

He plundered a remarkable 73 goals for club and country in 2025-26, with the only other instance of a player from Europe's top five leagues scoring 70+ goals in a single campaign coming in 2011-12, when Lionel Messi netted 82 en route to one of his eight Ballon d'Or triumphs.
Speaking on stage after receiving the prize, Kane said: "I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special – that made it a good omen for me.
"Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year. There are some world-class players in the room tonight."
Kane's triumph capped a remarkable rise to the top of the game, for a player who had loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City in the early stages of his career.

And Kane, who netted 280 times for Tottenham before joining Bayern in 2023 and finally halting his personal trophy drought by winning two Bundesliga crowns, one DFB-Pokal and two DFL Supercups, admits he could never have foreseen his triumph.
"Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even myself, I wouldn't have thought I'd get this far," Kane said.
"I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar, like some of the guys.
"I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it.
"I had to show self-belief, determination. I think that grounded me, even when I did make it at the highest level, to keep improving and keep getting better.
"No matter what I achieve, how many goals I score, winning the Ballon d'Or, it's always about getting better. This is a showcase of that."

Mbappe finished as the runner-up after becoming the World Cup's all-time leading scorer earlier this year, with Spain duo Yamal and Rodri placing third and fourth while Messi rounded out the top five.

f99pjpwxvbv13p4hi6cagmxf.title: De la Fuente says Ballon d'Or winner should be Spanish, makes Yamal case
f99pjpwxvbv13p4hi6cagmxf.subtitle: While Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe are major contenders for the Ballon d'Or, Lamine Yamal is also in the mix after Spain's World Cup win.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente believes a Spain player should win the Ballon d'Or following their World Cup triumph, arguing Lamine Yamal has done enough to be crowned the world's best player.
The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony will take place in London on October 26, with Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane currently seen as the frontrunner.
Kane plundered a remarkable 65 goals in all competitions for Bayern in 2025-26, then hit the net on six occasions at the World Cup as England finished third.

Kylian Mbappe is also deemed a major contender after a 50-goal campaign for Real Madrid and a World Cup where he managed 14 goal involvements (10 goals, four assists) – a new single-tournament record – and overhauled Miroslav Klose and Lionel Messi to become the competition's all-time leading scorer (22 goals).
But De la Fuente has been firm in his insistence that a Spain player should collect the prize following their World Cup win, just as Rodri did after they triumphed at Euro 2024.

Having signed a new contract to run through Euro 2032 on Monday, ahead of Spain's opening Nations League clash with England on Saturday, De la Fuente used an interview with El Larguero to argue the case for his players.
"I think it has to be won by a Spaniard, because they are the best in the world in many respects, including their understanding of the game," the Roja boss said.
"The Spanish footballer is an almost perfect player. They have more than enough merit this year, but it seems that it is difficult to give that recognition to our players."
Thirty players have been included on the Ballon d'Or shortlist, with six of those – Yamal, Rodri, Ferran Torres, Fabian Ruiz, Marc Cucurella and Pau Cubarsi – being Spanish.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian was the only player to win the World Cup and the Champions League trophies this year, while Rodri claimed the World Cup Golden Ball and Cubarsi was named Young Player of the Tournament.

But if there is to be a Spanish winner, Yamal seems the most likely recipient. He managed 24 goals and 17 assists for LaLiga champions Barcelona in 2025-26, with his 41 combined goal involvements being the sixth-most of any player from Europe's top five leagues (in all competitions).
Yamal also attempted (429) and completed (225) the most dribbles of any player, while his 59 chances created following carries were also the most.
Making his case in a recent interview, Yamal said the Ballon d'Or was "not about who has scored 80 goals", in comments seen as a jab at the prospects of Kane and Mbappe.
But De la Fuente does not believe Yamal meant to offend any of his rivals and expects the winger to battle Mbappe for Ballon d'Or honours for years to come.
"I think you have to see what he said in context. I think Lamine said it simply because he has enough merit, just like Mbappe," De la Fuente said.
"They are two players with a different touch and who, in the coming years – while respecting other players – will mark football.
"It does not seem like a lack of respect to me that both players say they have done enough to win it."

But De la Fuente has been firm in his insistence that a Spain player should collect the prize following their World Cup win, just as Rodri did after they triumphed at Euro 2024.

Having signed a new contract to run through Euro 2032 on Monday, ahead of Spain's opening Nations League clash with England on Saturday, De la Fuente used an interview with El Larguero to argue the case for his players. 

"I think it has to be won by a Spaniard, because they are the best in the world in many respects, including their understanding of the game," the Roja boss said. 

"The Spanish footballer is an almost perfect player. They have more than enough merit this year, but it seems that it is difficult to give that recognition to our players."

Thirty players have been included on the Ballon d'Or shortlist, with six of those – Yamal, Rodri, Ferran Torres, Fabian Ruiz, Marc Cucurella and Pau Cubarsi – being Spanish.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian was the only player to win the World Cup and the Champions League trophies this year, while Rodri claimed the World Cup Golden Ball and Cubarsi was named Young Player of the Tournament.

But if there is to be a Spanish winner, Yamal seems the most likely recipient. He managed 24 goals and 17 assists for LaLiga champions Barcelona in 2025-26, with his 41 combined goal involvements being the sixth-most of any player from Europe's top five leagues (in all competitions).

Yamal also attempted (429) and completed (225) the most dribbles of any player, while his 59 chances created following carries were also the most. 

Making his case in a recent interview, Yamal said the Ballon d'Or was "not about who has scored 80 goals", in comments seen as a jab at the prospects of Kane and Mbappe.

But De la Fuente does not believe Yamal meant to offend any of his rivals and expects the winger to battle Mbappe for Ballon d'Or honours for years to come. 

"I think you have to see what he said in context. I think Lamine said it simply because he has enough merit, just like Mbappe," De la Fuente said. 

"They are two players with a different touch and who, in the coming years – while respecting other players – will mark football. 

"It does not seem like a lack of respect to me that both players say they have done enough to win it."

faxe0kdcqvcz1nbxfkjmppf7i.title: Como 4-1 Manchester United: Carrick's worries mount after Paz inspires thumping win
faxe0kdcqvcz1nbxfkjmppf7i.subtitle: Manchester United's winless run stretched to seven games after Nico Paz led Como's charge in a stunning Champions League win.
paragraphs: Nico Paz was instrumental as Como blew Manchester United away with a 4-1 win at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in the Champions League.
The 22-year-old got the ball rolling in the second minute and finished the game with a brace and an assist after a stellar performance.

Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon were also both on target in the thumping victory, which piled further pressure on Michael Carrick, whose side are now winless in their last seven games in all competitions.
Diogo Dalot passed up a presentable chance with 84 seconds on the clock; having initially miscontrolled the ball, he recovered but bent his shot wide of the far post.
And 34 seconds later, Como made them pay for that miss. The hosts went straight up the other end, and Paz curled a stunning strike into the left side of the net.

United failed to muster a response, and Como finished the half on top. Douvikas had the beating of Matthijs de Ligt – making his first appearance in 325 days – and fired a tight-angled effort at Senne Lammens, who brought the forward down on his next attack, but the offside flag meant no penalty was awarded.

Como picked up where they left off after the break as they easily cut through United's defence in the 49th minute, with Paz laying it off to Douvikas, who profited from a De Ligt stumble to brilliantly lob Lammens.
And things went from bad to worse for United 57 minutes in. Paz pounced on Carlos Baleba's blind pass, and raced down the right to finish into the bottom-left corner.
United's urgency grew after that, with substitute Amad Diallo finding space on the edge of the box to test Jean Butez with a dipping strike that was tipped over the crossbar.
Como soon wrestled back momentum, though, and Ramon finished off a wonderful team move after Kaiki chipped a lovely cross into the box in the 76th minute.
Joshua Zirkzee netted a late consolation for United, plucking Amad's cross out of the air before scuffing his strike through Butez's legs in the 91st minute.
Paz lights up the stage as United's woes go on
Como's starting XI had made a combined 62 Champions League appearances (prior to this match), compared to the 242 in United's starting line-up, but based on performance, it was not evident.

Cesc Fabregas' side came flying out of the blocks, and their early goal means United have now conceded two goals in the opening two minutes of Champions League games this season, already their most in this time period in a single edition.
In fact, they are the first English team to concede in the first two minutes of consecutive major European matches.

Paz caused all their problems, as he became just the fourth player to be directly involved in at least three goals in a Champions League game against United, and the youngest to do so (aged 22 years and 43 days).
The Argentinian is also the second-youngest South American player to find the net in competition against United, after Lionel Messi (21y 337d in the 2009 final).
Como have settled into the Champions League brilliantly, becoming the first Italian side to win their first two home games since Lazio in 1999-00.
For United, though, it leaves more questions as their torrid away form in UEFA's premier competition; they have won just one of their last 11 games on the road in the Champions League (D3 L7).
They mustered 1.05 expected goals (xG) from 13 shots (helped by their last goal) to Como's 2.04, with Fabregas' side getting eight of their 11 attempts on target.
And it was not the only big-scoring match in the early kick-offs on Wednesday, with Galatasaray giving up a lead and then coming from behind to earn a 4-2 victory over Lille.

fgkxn6o2tfjc1dzumqiem2xut.title: Borussia Dortmund 2-2 Werder Bremen: Fullkrug ends hosts' perfect Bundesliga start
fgkxn6o2tfjc1dzumqiem2xut.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund scored two goals in five minutes late on, but Werder Bremen launched a comeback in the dying stages to earn a draw.
paragraphs: Niclas Fullkrug's stoppage-time goal put an end to Borussia Dortmund's 100% Bundesliga start as he salvaged a 2-2 draw for Werder Bremen.
Daniel Svensson and Nico Schlotterbeck scored two quickfire goals to put Dortmund in control, but Ludovit Reis and Fullkrug struck even later to earn a point.
Both sides made a slow start to the game, with Reis having the first clear-cut chance of the first half when he drilled narrowly wide just after the half-hour mark.
Marcel Sabitzer then flashed a free-kick past the post before Maximilian Beier forced a smart sprawling stop out of Karl Hein from a tight angle on the right of the box.
Ethan Nwaneri also called Hein into action just after the break, while Fullkrug volleyed a bouncing clearance from the goalkeeper against Gregor Kobel's outstretched leg.

Dortmund continued to up the pressure, though, and Serhou Guirassy saw a glancing header cleared off the line before Nwaneri's overhead kick thundered in off the near post, but it was disallowed for a foul in the build-up.

The hosts eventually got the breakthrough in the 80th minute; a lightning-quick counter-attack saw Guirassy skip down the right before pulling it back into the box and Fabio Silva helped it onto Svensson, who rifled it into the roof of the net first time.
Five minutes later, Dortmund had doubled their lead, with Schlotterbeck nodding a towering header past Hein, who claimed he was being impeded, but the goal survived a VAR check.
However, Dortmund's deficit was halved just three minutes later after Oskar Wojcik intercepted a loose pass and Reis weaved into the box before firing past Kobel.
And in the second minute of stoppage time, Fullkrug got the decisive goal. He timed his run perfectly on a Marco Grull free-kick and flicked his header over Kobel to settle the game.
Dortmund's late collapse opens door in Bundesliga
It has been an impressive start to the 2026-27 season by Dortmund, who remain unbeaten and top of the Bundesliga, but these two dropped points will feel like a loss to Niko Kovac.
The game was a slow burn, with few chances to shout about in the first half, but it sparked to life after the break.

Of Dortmund's 21 shots, 16 came after the break, with Werder firing nine at the hosts' goal in that same time (11 in total). Kovac's side accumulated 2.42 expected goals (xG) overall, with their opponents over-performing their 1.13 xG.
Schlotterbeck eventually got his goal and led the team's attack, having a joint-game-high four shots (level with Sabitzer) and the second-most final-third entries (23 behind Waldemar Anton's 31).

But it was a former Black and Yellow player who came back to haunt the team. Fullkrug has scored in four consecutive Bundesliga matches for the first time in his career, taking his tally to five goals since his return to Werder.
Dortmund are now three points clear at the top of the Bundesliga table ahead of the rest of the weekend's action, opening the door for Bayern Munich to close the gap on Saturday.

fjfpxnab1ruo1fun6208k05kh.title: Marmoush confident Spurs' first Premier League win is 'just the beginning'
fjfpxnab1ruo1fun6208k05kh.subtitle: Tottenham earned a vital win over Coventry City on Monday, and Omar Marmoush is confident Roberto De Zerbi's team will build on that result.
paragraphs: Omar Marmoush believes Tottenham's first Premier League victory of the season is "just the beginning", arguing they deserve to have more points on the board.
Spurs finally got in the win column at the seventh time of asking on Monday, with Marmoush netting his first goal for the club in a 3-1 success against Coventry City.
James Maddison and Ben Davies were also on target for Roberto De Zerbi's men, who scored all three of their goals from outside the box.

They became the first team to score three times from outside the area in a single Premier League game since Fulham versus Leicester City in May 2023. Tottenham previously did so in September 2022, also against Leicester.
The victory was just Spurs' sixth in their last 37 home Premier League games (D10 L21) and their fourth overall in the competition in 2026 (P27 D10 L13).
But Marmoush hopes they can now move on from a miserable period and pick up the consistent results he feels their performances have warranted.
"We are so, so happy. We have had good performances in that last week but haven't had the end result of a win," Marmoush told BBC Sport.
"We're very happy to win our first game today, and I'm also happy to score my first goal for Tottenham. We will build on this.
"In every game, we learn. As you said, we've played amazing in the first few weeks, but the result just wasn't there. It is just the beginning."

All 11 of Marmoush's Premier League goals have been scored in home games (10 for Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium, one for Spurs at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium) – the most goals a player has scored in the competition's history without any coming away from home.

Marmoush's strike – which inched Spurs into a 2-1 lead after Jack Rudoni had equalised for Coventry – eased the pressure on De Zerbi greatly, and he has enjoyed his first few weeks working with the Italian.
"I feel amazing. With the coach, he helps us all and teaches us small details. He also helps us on a personal basis," he said of De Zerbi.
"I love the intensity and passion that he brings, we believe in the system that we play. On the pitch, we are like a big family, and we will fight for each other until the end."
Spurs, who climbed to 16th in the table as a result of their win, face rivals Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, before hosting Crystal Palace a week later.

fldh9fffnxfz10nydsvr6u05x.title: Kane urges Bayern players to step up in Olise's absence for Arsenal clash
fldh9fffnxfz10nydsvr6u05x.subtitle: Bayern Munich will be without the suspended Michael Olise when they host Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday.
paragraphs: Harry Kane has called on his Bayern Munich team-mates to "step up" in the absence of Michael Olise when they face Arsenal in the Champions League.
Olise is suspended for the league-phase clash at Allianz Arena after receiving a red card in Bayern's 3-3 draw with Viking last time out.

Since the start of last season, Olise has created more chances than any other player in the Champions League (44), made the joint-most defensive line-breaking passes (43), and only Lamine Yamal (55) has completed more dribbles than the Frenchman (54).
Across Bayern's last 23 Champions League matches, the only team to beat them by more than one goal is Mikel Arteta's Arsenal (3-1 win in November 2025).
With Olise unavailable, Kane believes this is the perfect opportunity for someone to prove their worth in the side.
"When one of your key players is missing, you definitely feel the difference. But that's exactly when other players have to step up and make the most of this opportunity," Kane told the club website.
"Whoever plays has to be ready. That's the nature of the competition at Bayern – and it's a key factor. Everyone trains to an extremely high standard.
"Others can step in and, hopefully, do a really good job."

Former Tottenham striker Kane has plenty of history with Arsenal; he has scored 15 goals in 22 career appearances against the Gunners – his third-highest total against an opponent in his career, only netting more against Leicester City (20 in 20 games) and Everton (16 in 17 games).

Bayern have only lost one of their seven Champions League home games against Arsenal (W5 D1), winning the last three in a row, and two of which by at least four goals (5-1 in both November 2015 and February 2017).
Kane is relishing the chance to play at home against one of the top teams in Europe, with Arsenal finishing runners-up in the competition last season.
"When you're playing against one of the best teams in Europe, you always have to savour moments like this," added Kane.
"We're up for the challenge. We're playing here at home – the energy, the fans – it's sure to be a special night."

fmx5esrj33is1nub7gdcvk2x9.title: Allegri: Napoli know where we need to improve
fmx5esrj33is1nub7gdcvk2x9.subtitle: After squandering multiple leads in their draw with Roma last time out, Napoli are looking to bounce back against Monza in midweek.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri insisted his Napoli side know where they have to improve ahead of their trip to Monza on Wednesday.
Napoli have struggled in Serie A as of late, winning just one of their last four games in the competition (D2 L1) following a 3-3 draw with Roma on the weekend.
The Partenopei twice led in that match (2-0 and 3-2) but could not hold onto either advantage, after more struggles at the back.
Napoli have faced an average of 16.6 shots per game in Serie A this season (3.9 on target); last season, they faced an average of 10.2 shots per match (3.0 on target).
They have also conceded six goals across their last two Champions League matches, but Allegri is confident his side have learned their lesson.
"We had a good game against Roma. We need to do better in terms of distribution," said Allegri.
"At times, we forced it against Roma when we could have managed possession better. At 2-0, we should have controlled it better.

"In the first halves, we have only conceded two goals this season. In the second halves, we've conceded eight, so there's data that shows us where to improve and that helps us understand that we need to be better in certain moments.
"I've seen some data. We're conceding an average of four shots on target per game, but that doesn't tell you how we concede them or where we're conceding them from.
"The data says we concede every four shots on target, so we have to work on ourselves when we are defending our own area, like for [Matias] Soule's first goal or the third goal against Roma.
"We have to work on that, there will be some mistakes, we will be better at other times."
After a 4-0 win over Cagliari, Ivan Juric's Monza side lost 3-2 against Torino last time out in Serie A.
Monza – Gustavo Varela

Varela (seven goals in seven games played) could become only the second player in the three-points-for-a-win era to score at least eight goals in his first eight Serie A appearances, after Krzysztof Piatek (nine goals in his first eight games in 2018-19).

The Portuguese could also be the second-youngest to achieve this (21 years and 271 days on the date of the match) in the competition's history, after Otello Torri (eight goals in eight matches for Novara between 1936 and 1937 at 19 years and 364 days).
Napoli – Scott McTominay
McTominay has scored consecutive braces in the Champions League and Serie A.

Since his debut for Napoli in September 2024, he is the midfielder from a Serie A team with the most goals in all competitions (31) and the most multiple-goal games (six), with Hakan Calhanoglu second in this ranking with three.
MATCH PREDICTION: NAPOLI WIN
Napoli have won four of their six Serie A matches against Monza (W4 D1 L1), including each of the last three by an aggregate score of 7-2.
And against no side have Napoli kept more clean sheets in Serie A than against Monza (four), level with Atalanta and AC Milan.
However, Napoli have lost two of their last three Serie A away games (D1), as many defeats as they registered in their previous 12 (W7 D3).
After their 1-0 loss against Venezia, Napoli could record two consecutive away defeats without scoring for the first time since December 2023 and January 2024 (three in a row under Walter Mazzarri).

Monza have won their last two Serie A home games (2-1 v Sassuolo and 4-0 v Cagliari) and have never recorded three consecutive home wins in the competition (also two between September and October 2022 and in November 2022).

Varela (seven goals in seven games played) could become only the second player in the three-points-for-a-win era to score at least eight goals in his first eight Serie A appearances, after Krzysztof Piatek (nine goals in his first eight games in 2018-19).

The Portuguese could also be the second-youngest to achieve this (21 years and 271 days on the date of the match) in the competition's history, after Otello Torri (eight goals in eight matches for Novara between 1936 and 1937 at 19 years and 364 days).

Napoli – Scott McTominay

McTominay has scored consecutive braces in the Champions League and Serie A.

Since his debut for Napoli in September 2024, he is the midfielder from a Serie A team with the most goals in all competitions (31) and the most multiple-goal games (six), with Hakan Calhanoglu second in this ranking with three.

MATCH PREDICTION: NAPOLI WIN

Napoli have won four of their six Serie A matches against Monza (W4 D1 L1), including each of the last three by an aggregate score of 7-2.

And against no side have Napoli kept more clean sheets in Serie A than against Monza (four), level with Atalanta and AC Milan.

However, Napoli have lost two of their last three Serie A away games (D1), as many defeats as they registered in their previous 12 (W7 D3).

After their 1-0 loss against Venezia, Napoli could record two consecutive away defeats without scoring for the first time since December 2023 and January 2024 (three in a row under Walter Mazzarri).

Monza have won their last two Serie A home games (2-1 v Sassuolo and 4-0 v Cagliari) and have never recorded three consecutive home wins in the competition (also two between September and October 2022 and in November 2022).

OPTA WIN PROBABILITY

Monza – 24.5%

Draw – 24%

Napoli – 51.5%

fqpttzn6qdk11h6bhf9x1prip.title: Emery and Aston Villa not underestimating 'dangerous' Viking
fqpttzn6qdk11h6bhf9x1prip.subtitle: Aston Villa have made a strong start to their Champions League campaign, but Viking arrive at Villa Park fresh from stunning Bayern Munich.
paragraphs: Unai Emery said he was not getting carried away by Aston Villa's "amazing" start to their Champions League campaign, with "dangerous" tournament debutants Viking up next.
Villa return to Villa Park on Wednesday to take on the Norwegian minnows fresh from recording their biggest-ever win in European competition against Fenerbahce last time out.
Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both scored twice in a 6-0 thrashing, but they will come up against a Viking side that had Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich on the ropes.
Gianni Stensness and Peter Christiansen had put Viking two goals up by half-time, but Ballon d'Or favourite Harry Kane scored twice in quick succession to level things up.
Bayern then took the lead through Luis Diaz, but after Michael Olise was sent off soon after, Herman Haugen popped up with a 90th-minute equaliser to seal a share of the spoils.

This will be just the third time Viking have faced an English opponent, after two meetings with Chelsea in the first round of the 2002-03 UEFA Cup (lost 1-2 away, won 4-2 at home), as they look to become the first Norwegian side ever to win away to an English side in European competition.

However, if Villa win here, they will be the second-fastest team to reach 20 European Cup/Champions League victories (in their 30th game), only behind Real Madrid (won 20 of first 29), while they could win four consecutive games for the first time in the competition.
But Emery was not underestimating Viking, telling reporters: "Champions League. Every team that plays Champions League because they deserve it, and they are dangerous.
"Viking, they drew against Bayern Munich last week; they lost against Stuttgart. They are with Bodo/Glimt in the league, first and second with the same points.
"Bodo/Glimt has been a successful team in the last few years in Europe, performing well, getting good results, playing in the Champions League, beating important teams.
"So Viking is now a new team as well, with the capacity to draw against Bayern Munich, the capacity as well to compete against Stuttgart and to compete against us.
"This is the Champions League, and it is very difficult. We now have six points. It's something amazing, but very difficult, and to keep the same way we are is our challenge."
During last week's win over Fenerbahce, Johan Manzambi marked his Champions League debut, and his 21st birthday, with a goal and another impressive display.

In doing so, he became the second player, after Spartak Moscow's Romulo vs Barcelona in September 2012 (22 years old), to find the back of the net on his first appearance in the competition on his birthday.

Manzambi followed that up with another goal against Newcastle United in the Premier League, becoming the fourth Villa player to either score or assist in each of their first three Premier League starts after Dalian Atkinson in August 1992, Dion Dublin in November 1998 and Danny Ings in August 2021.

Since his first start for the club (September 19 against Tottenham), only Manchester City's Erling Haaland (six) has been involved in more goals among Premier League players in all competitions than Manzambi (five – three goals, two assists).
However, the Switzerland international was replaced by Ibrahim Mbaye in the 72nd minute at St. James' Park with what Emery described in his pre-match press conference as a "minor injury".
Manzambi's absence adds to mounting medical issues, with Matteo Ruggeri expected to miss roughly two months and Aaron Wan-Bissaka sidelined for three to four weeks.
But Emery refused to use Villa's series of injuries as an excuse, adding: "We are accepting of the injuries we had before.
"So many players we had injured in our process here, and now we're still having some, like [Amadou] Onana for a long time, like Matteo for more or less two months.
"Coming back and joining us is Ian Maatsen. He's joined us and is training with us this week.
"Manzambi has a small injury. He's not available [against Viking]. Aaron [Wan-Bissaka] has an injury as well. More or less, we expect three or four weeks.
"We have enough players, no excuses, and we'll find solutions if we need to achieve our performance, of course, collectively and individually in each position."

fquqhqqn4njk1tac5auh40nlg.title: Fermin confident of Barcelona's Clasico chances despite PSG defeat
fquqhqqn4njk1tac5auh40nlg.subtitle: Fermin Lopez insists Barcelona remain favourites for Sunday's Clasico despite their midweek Champions League defeat to PSG.
paragraphs: Fermin Lopez believes Barcelona are favourites for Sunday's Clasico against Real Madrid despite their recent Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

Hansi Flick's side fell to a 4-2 defeat against the reigning European champions on Tuesday, with Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal scoring in the second half before Luis Enrique's side stole the show late on.
But Fermin is confident that the setback will not affect Barcelona heading into the Clasico, and their recent record against Madrid gives him reason for optimism.

Under Flick, Barcelona have won six of their seven meetings with Madrid across all competitions (D1), having managed just four victories in their previous 15 Clasicos before the German's arrival (D1 L10).

Barca also hold a six-point lead over Madrid at the top of LaLiga, having become just the second side to win their opening nine league matches of a season, after Madrid in 1968-69. No side has ever won their first 10 matches in a LaLiga campaign.
"It's never good to lose any match, especially in the Champions League, but ultimately it's just one game and three points," Fermin said.
"Our focus is now completely on El Clasico. It's an extremely important match, and we're very eager to get back to winning ways.
"I don’t think we played badly against Paris. They’re also a great team and made things difficult for us, but I don’t think we were far from winning.
“We need to know how to control Real Madrid, but I think if we execute our style properly, we’ll have a great chance of winning.
“We have to play our usual way and maintain our good rhythm, while paying attention to the small details because they have players with enormous individual quality.
“I feel like time is passing very slowly because it’s a match I’ve always loved playing.
“Since I was a child, I dreamed of playing in El Clasico. This will be my second time playing it at Camp Nou, so I’m very excited and can’t wait.
“I’ve scored at the Bernabeu before, but we didn’t win, and that still leaves a bitter taste. I hope I can score at Camp Nou on Sunday and that we win. That’s what matters most to me.”

ftbpro_01jax2mzy0nw.title: The 30 Best Real Madrid Players of All Time—Ranked
ftbpro_01jax2mzy0nw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffOct 23, 2024Legends litter Real Madrid’s storied history.  / Gerard Julien/AFP/Getty ImagesThe greatest Real Madrid players of all time are also some of the biggest superstars to ever lace up a pair of boots.

Over the course of the last century, generational players at every position have represented Real Madrid. Whether they came to the Spanish capital in a blockbuster transfer or rose through the La Fábrica ranks, legends of the game have contributed to the legacy of Spain and Europe’s winningest club.

After all, lifting 36 La Liga trophies and 15 Champions League titles was only made possible by the moments of magic created on the pitch throughout every era of football. In some cases, the greats who have donned the white shirt can only be separated by their silverware.
Here are the 30 best Real Madrid players of all time.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Jr has been key to Madrid’s recent success. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty ImagesA scorer in two Champions League finals, Vinícius was named The Best FIFA Men’s Player in 2024 and finished runner-up in the Ballon d’Or the same year.The heights he has reached would’ve seemed near-unthinkable after a rocky start, but he eventually added serious end product to his bubbling potential to establish himself as a global icon and one of the club’s most decisive players of recent times.

Santamaría was a colossus at the back.  / imago images/HorstmüllerNicknamed “The Wall” for his rugged, uncompromising defensive displays, Santamaría won a whopping 12 Spanish league titles as well as three European cups for Real Madrid between between 1957 and 1966 and was a key figure in the club’s first golden age.Born in Uruguay to Spanish parents, he represented both countries at international level.

Amancio was known as “the Wizard”. / IMAGO/NurPhoto“The Wizard”, as he was known, was a key figure at Madrid in the ‘60s, helping the club reach the summit of European soccer once again after a transitional period.Amancio made over 450 appearances for Los Blancos across 14 years, scoring 154 goals—including the opener in the 1966 European Cup final win over Partizan Belgrade.The two-time Pichichi winner would later be credited with discovering the iconic Quinta del Buitre (The Vulture Squad) during his spell as reserve team coach.

Zárraga is a five-time European Cup winner. / IMAGO/HorstmüllerOnly the great Paco Gento and Dani Carvajal have won more European Cups than Zárraga.A stalwart of Madrid’s continental dominance across the ‘50s and into the ‘60s, the midfielder starred in five consecutive European Cup final wins.He also made over 200 appearances for the club in total, and lifted La Liga six times.

Carvajal first joined Real Madrid as a 10-year-old. / IMAGO/ZUMA Press WirePerhaps the biggest success story of La Fábrica, Carvajal spent almost all of his career with his boyhood club and is as synonymous with the club as anyone. Made club captain in 2025, the son of a police inspector made over 400 appearances and was part of four La Liga title wins. However, he is best known starting on the winning side in a ridiculous six Champions Leagues.He ranked fourth in the 2024 Ballon d’Or after a stellar season in which he scored the opener in the 2–0 final win over Dortmund.

Gareth Bale won five Champions League titles with Real Madrid. / Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty ImagesAlthough his tenure at the Spanish capital ended with a whimper, Gareth Bale’s contributions to Real Madrid cannot be overlooked. The Welshman scored 106 goals and won five Champions League titles in a white shirt, playing his part in one of the most dangerous attacks in European history. Bale’s stunning bicycle kick to secure the club’s 13th Champions League trophy will stand the test of time, as will his blistering run and finish against Barcelona to secure the Copa del Rey title in his debut campaign.

Vicente del Bosque won 16 titles as a player and manager with Real Madrid. / IMAGO/ColorsportVicente del Bosque might be better remembered for his days on Real Madrid’s touchline; the former boss led the club to Champions League glory in 2000 and 2002, along with five other trophies.Yet his time on the pitch produced even more silverware for Los Blancos. Del Bosque, who was known for his intelligence, versatility and ability to organize the team’s midfield, lifted nine trophies, including five league titles, with Real Madrid.

Ronaldo bagged 104 goals for Real Madrid. / Javier Soriano/AFP/Getty ImagesThe greatest moments of Ronaldo’s career undoubtedly came during his time representing Barcelona and the Brazil national team, but that does not diminish his accomplishments at Real Madrid. The striker was a true Galáctico, tallying 104 goals in just 177 appearances. Ronaldo helped the Spanish giants top La Liga in his debut campaign in 2002–23 and then won the Pichichi Trophy in his second season.The icon was the club’s leading goalscorer in all four of his full seasons before he left for Milan in 2007.

Marcelo spent 16 seasons on the left flank for Real Madrid. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesRoberto Carlos left nearly impossible boots to fill on the left flank for Real Madrid, but his fellow countryman Marcelo soon rose to the occasion. The Brazilian’s attacking flair and creativity paired with his stout defending turned him into a club legend.Marcelo owns the second-most trophies in club history, behind only Luka Modrić. Atop his résumé are the five Champions League crowns he helped the club claim over the course of his 16-year stint.

José Antonio Camacho played nearly 600 matches for Real Madrid. / IMAGO/Ferdi HartungIt took less than one season playing for Real Madrid Castilla for José Antonio Camacho to secure his place in the first team. There, he began building his legacy as one of the great defenders in club history. His defensive prowess was matched by his immense will to win, eventually earning the title of Real Madrid’s “great captain.” Camacho ended his career in a white shirt with 577 appearances to his name and 19 titles in his trophy cabinet.

Iván Zamorano sat atop the Real Madrid record books for 32 years. / IMAGO/AlbumIván Zamorano did more in four seasons with Real Madrid than some players with double his number of appearances. The Chilean scored 101 goals in 173 matches for Los Blancos; 28 came in the club’s 1994–95 campaign, which ended with the La Liga title for Los Blancos and the Pichichi Trophy for the forward. For 32 years, Zamorano held the record for the most goals (37) scored in a debut season for Real Madrid until Kylian Mbappé broke it in 2024–25.

Emilio Butragueño won the Pichichi Trophy in 1991. / IMAGO/Ferdi HartungThe fact that a player of Emilio Butragueño’s quality only ranks in 19th place on this list is perhaps the best evidence to showcase just how many superstars have played for Real Madrid.The Spaniard was brilliant with the ball at his feet, whether he was blowing by defenders with his dribbling ability or sending sensational goals into the back of the net. Butragueño led the Quinta del Buitre (the Vulture’s Cohort), which stands as one of the best generations in club history. The forward’s crowning individual achievement for Real Madrid came when he won the Pichichi Trophy for his 1991–92 campaign.

Roberto Carlos spent 11 seasons with Real Madrid. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesRoberto Carlos carved an identity on the left flank that puts him in the pantheon of the best fullbacks to ever don a white shirt. The Brazilian’s left foot, lethal speed and powerful shot helped Real Madrid win three Champions League titles.Beyond his silverware, Carlos remains in the club’s history books with 527 appearances to his name, the fourth all-time most by any foreign player.

Toni Kroos retired as a Real Madrid great. / Matthias Hangst/Getty ImagesReal Madrid signed one of the best midfielders of all time for just €25 million ($28.9 million). Toni Kroos joined the Spanish giants after winning the 2014 World Cup with Germany and the rest is history.The midfield metronome completed Spanish football in his 10-year stint with Los Blancos, lifting 23 trophies, five of which were Champions League titles. Kroos’s vision, expert passing and unwavering composure made him an irreplaceable piece of Real Madrid’s XI.

Ricardo Zamora is one of the club’s best goalkeepers of all time. / Central Press/Getty ImagesThere is a reason Ricardo Zamora was known as the “divine one.” The goalkeeper quickly become a hero for Real Madrid, leading the club to its first two La Liga titles in 1931–32 and 1932–33.Remembered as one of the greatest goalkeepers in history, Zamora conceded the least amount of goals in the Spanish top-flight in 1930, 1932 and 1933. His legacy lives on through the Zamora Trophy, awarded to the goalkeeper who concedes the fewest goals in La Liga every season.

ftbpro_01jbcfav7b5p.title: Ballon d’Or: Full List of Winners, Most Wins of All Time
ftbpro_01jbcfav7b5p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 29, 2024Harry Kane (left) and Alexia Putellas were the big winners at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.   / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesThe most coveted individual prize in world soccer—and perhaps in world sport as a whole—is the Ballon d’Or.

First awarded in 1956, the Ballon d'Or award is given to the sport's top player, voted by a panel of soccer journalists representing the top 100 countries in the FIFA Men's rankings and the top 50 countries in the FIFA Women’s rankings.

Previous winners span from Alfredo Di Stéfano and Johan Cruyff to Marco van Basten and Zinedine Zidane, but arguably soccer’s two greatest players of all time, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, are the standard bearers when it comes to multiple wins. Much in part to their success, Barcelona and Real Madrid are the two clubs with the most men's Ballon d'Or wins (12) in history.
On the women’s side, Barcelona are the dominant force since the award’s inception in 2018—they provided the winner for four straight years between 2021 and 2026.
Here’s a full rundown of the award’s history.
Next. Ballon d’Or Winners. 2025 Ballon d’Or: Complete Rankings for Every Award. dark
Harry Kane took home the 2026 Ballon d’Or. / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesYear

Lionel Messi has won the Ballon d'Or more often than any other player, scooping the gong an incredible eight times. Cristiano Ronaldo is his nearest challenger with five, with three other players winning the award on three occasions—Michel Platini, in three consecutive years between 1983 and 1985, Johan Cruyff and Marco van Basten.
A further five players have won the Ballon d’Or twice, including Brazil legend Ronaldo.
Alexia Putellas won her third Ballon d’Or Feminin.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesYear

Aitana Bonmatí previously broke her tie with Alexia Putellas to become the player with the most Ballon d’Or Femínin wins in history. Bonmatí took home the honor three times, with her most recent win coming in 2025.
But Putellas answered right back in 2026, claiming her third Ballon d’Or Femínin for captaining Barcelona to their historic quadruple.
Ada Hegerberg was the inaugural winner in 2018, followed 12 months by USWNT superstat Megan Rapinoe. The award was not handed out in 2020 because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

ftbpro_01jtjef10z8g.title: The 30 Best Barcelona Players of All Time—Ranked
ftbpro_01jtjef10z8g.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffMay 6, 2025Andres Iniesta (left), Lionel Messi and Xavi are all among Barcelona’s greatest-ever players. / IMAGO/PanoramiCBarcelona is more than just a soccer club—as the words spelled out across the seats at Camp Nou proudly proclaim: “Més que un club.”

One of the most storied sides in soccer history, Barça has claimed 29 La Liga titles, five Champions Leagues and a long list of other major honors. But beyond the silverware, the club has become a symbol of Catalan identity and a standard-bearer for a distinct footballing philosophy—one defined by technical brilliance, youth development and an unshakable commitment to style.
Over the decades, countless players have personified that identity—whether by rising through La Masia, giving everything on the pitch or simply playing the game the “Barça way.”
Here are the 30 greatest players ever to wear the famous garnet and blue, based on ability, impact and lasting legacy.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Patrick Kluivert won La Liga in 1999. / IMAGO / KolvenbachOne of many Dutchmen to suceed at Camp Nou over the years, Patrick Kluivert was a mainstay of Barcelona’s attack for six seasons during the late ‘90s and early ‘00s.A complete striker who beat his marker as easily on the ground and in the air, Kluvert scored 122 times in 257 outings for Barça and still ranks as the club’s eighth-highest all-time scorer.

Raphinha has developed into one of the globe’s most prolific strikers. / Jose Luis Contreras/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesA modern great. It’s fair to say expectations were limited when Raphinha arrived from Leeds United back in the summer of 2022.However, the Brazilian, who once attended Ronaldinho’s birthday party as a child, quickly stepped up to become a key player for La Blaugrana, while winning three La Liga titles in his first four seasons.Though signed as a winger, the former Rennes star has become a goalscoring sensation as a center forward and was named the team’s captain ahead of the 2026–27 season.

Lamine Yamal inherited the iconic No. 10 shirt at Barcelona. /  BSR Agency/Getty ImagesOnly time will tell how high Lamine Yamal ends up on this list, but there’s every chance he will be very close to the summit by the end of his career, if he carries on at his current trajectory.The teenage sensation first made the Barcelona first team as a 15-year-old and has gone one to break record after record as the club’s finest academy product since a certain Argentinian.Already a three-time La Liga winner, as well as a European Championships and World Cup winner before his 20th birthday, only the Champions League is missing for the budding superstar who was voted second in the 2025 Ballon d’Or vote.

David Villa was a generational finisher. / IMAGO / GEPA picturesPerhaps the finest finisher of his generation, David Villa was already established as La Liga’s best striker when he made the move from Valencia in the summer of 2010. However, there were question marks over how he would fit in Pep Guardiola’s super team—particuarly after the exit of Samuel Eto’o. The doubters needn’t have worried and Villa took to Barça like a duck to water, bagging 23 goals in his first season as he helped his new side to the treble.While he stayed only three seasons, Villa remains beloved for his supreme quality as a goalscorer and team player.

Dani Alves revolutionized the right back position at Barcelona. / Jasper Juinen/Getty ImagesBrazil have produced some of the greatest fullbacks of all time and Dani Alves is very much one of them. His tireless engine was only matched by his vision and brilliant technique, contributing to him having the fifth most assists in club history.  The chemistry Alves developed with Lionel Messi on Barcelona’s right flank made him one of Messi’s greatest ever sidekicks. Together, they formed one of the greatest right wings the sport has ever witnessed. He remains the third foreign player with the most caps in Barça history and collected 23 major trophies during his time in Catalonia.

Luis Enrique played for both Barça and Real Madrid. / IMAGO / Camera 4Though born in Asturias rather than Catalonia, Luis Enrique became a symbol of Barcelona after crossing the divide from Real Madrid in 1996.Previously a versatile and tenacious midfielder, “Lucho” developed into a serious goalscoring threat at Camp Nou—celebrating every goal he bagged against his former club in the Clásico especially passionately.In 300 games across eight years, he scored 108 goals for Barcelona and won two La Liga crowns, two Copas del Rey and the UEFA Cup Winners Cup.Adding to his credentials as a club legend, he returned to manage Barça to a famous treble in 2014–15.

Romário’s stint with Barcelona was brief but memorable. / Chris Cole/Getty ImagesRomário needed only two seasons in Catalonia to leave an enduring mark with Barcelona, infatuating club supporters with his otherworldly talent that is on par with the all-time greats.  The Brazilian scored 30 goals in 33 La Liga games as Barcelona cruised to the title in his first season with the club. Once described as “a comic book player,” he was the cherry on top of Johan Cruyff’s “Dream Team." Agile, skillful, fast and devastating in front of goal, Romário was a sight to behold.

Neymar was pure magic during his time at Barcelona. / Etsuo Hara/Getty ImagesThe hype surrounding Neymar Jr. upon joining Barcelona from Santos in 2013 was unlike anything the world had ever seen. Yet, the Brazilian winger lived up to the hype ... and then some.  Neymar collected 105 goals and 76 assists in his 186 appearances for the club. He formed arguably the greatest attacking trio the world has ever seen next to Messi and Luis Suárez, lifting every trophy available in his four seasons with the club, including a treble in 2014–15.  The Brazilian was simply electric down the left wing, one of the most naturally gifted players ever to step foot on the Camp Nou pitch. He was the mastermind behind one of the greatest nights in Barça folklore when they overcame a four-goal deficit to eliminate Paris Saint-Germain in the 2016–17 Champions League round of 16. Neymar left for PSG a season later with a record transfer fee worth €222 million ($264 million). His controversial exit still pains many Barcelona fans, who sometimes describe him as “the prince that never became king.”

Gerard Piqué played 669 games for Barcelona. / IMAGO/ANPA strong, brash, charismatic and sometimes even controversial personality sometimes makes people forget that Gerard Piqué is one of the most talented center backs the game has ever seen.The La Masia product returned to Barcelona in 2008 and quickly established himself as a cornerstone of the most successful era in club history. At his peak, he was one of the best central defenders in the world. He amassed 669 appearances, collected 30 major trophies in his decade-plus stint at Barça and his 56 goals are the second most by a defender in club history. Few players in Barcelona history better personified the club than Piqué, who was a true leader and an undisputed legend.

Carles Rexach (right) played 16 seasons for Barcelona. / IMAGO/BSR AgencyCarles Rexach was an ever-present figure in Barcelona during the second half of the 20th century, spending 44 years straight at the club as a player or as a member of the technical staff, later helping sign the top player on this list.The former winger was deadly with the ball at his feet, especially with set-pieces, becoming Barcelona’s ninth all-time goalscorer in his 672 appearances as a Blaugrana. He was a one-club man that later managed the Catalans in 2001–02 before becoming a consultant for the club in 2010.

Luis Suárez Miramontes (left) was the first Spanish player to win the Ballon d’Or. / IMAGO/AlbumThe first of two players named Luis Suárez on the list. Suárez Miramontes was a fearless yet elegant attacking midfielder that is widely considered as one of the best players of his era. He was the first Spanish player to win the men’s Ballon d’Or in 1960.The Spaniard led Barcelona to two La Liga titles and to the club’s first ever European final in 1961. An economic crisis forced Barça to sell Suárez shortly after winning the Ballon d’Or. Still, Suárez left a lasting legacy with 141 goals in 253 appearances.

Andoni Zubizarreta is one of the greatest Spanish goalkeepers in history. / IMAGO/Ferdi HartungThe definition of consistency. Andoni Zubizarreta was never one for the spotlight, but he answered the call whenever he was needed.“Zubi” was the guardian of the ”Dream Team” and his performance in the 1992 European Cup—now Champions League—will forever be remembered as nothing short of extraordinary, helping Barcelona conquer their maiden Champions League trophy. He won 11 major trophies with Barça including four La Liga titles where he missed only four games throughout the four title-winning campaigns. To this day, no player has more La Liga appearances than his 622. Not to mention he also played in four World Cups for Spain.

Michael Laudrup was one of the finest players of Barcelona’s Dream Team. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesAlthough he had a falling out with childhood hero turned manager Cruyff that resulted in him leaving for bitter rivals Real Madrid, Michael Laudrup was perhaps the greatest artist within the ensemble that was Barcelona’s “Dream Team.”The Danish superstar was a player ahead of his time. An elegant attacking midfielder who was just as capable as a creator than as a finisher; he was elegance on the football pitch personified. There’s a reason a banner with the phrase “Enjoy Laudrup” embellished the Camp Nou stands for years. Laudrup won four consecutive La Liga titles and Barça’s maiden Champions League title in his five year stint at the club. He added that bit of magic to one of the greatest sides in club history.

Many consider Diego Maradona as the greatest player of all time. / Joel Robine/AFP/Getty ImagesDiego Maradona was a shooting star in Barcelona. He was a true lightning rod that never managed to live-up to his potential with the club, but still left an undeniable mark and showed glimpses of the talent that make him the greatest player ever in the eyes of many.Maradona’s two seasons with the club were injury-ridden and probably best remembered by the fights he incited on the pitch. Yet, there was still a number of brilliant moments, including when was the first ever Barcelona player to get a standing ovation at the Santiago Bernabéu after a sublime El Clásico goal in the 1982–83 season. His brief two season stint in Catalonia still saw him leave with three major trophies won. Maradona at Barcelona was the definition of a rebellious genius, one that raised the club’s status and left behind clues of his eventual all-time great status.

Ronaldo Nazário was at the peak of his powers during his single season with Barcelona. / Claudio Villa/Getty ImagesIt’s rare for a player to be considered one of a club’s greatest ever after just a single season, but Ronaldo Nazário's 1996–97 campaign at Barcelona makes a compelling case. In one of the most remarkable individual seasons in both Barcelona and Spanish soccer history, the Brazilian striker scored an astonishing 47 goals in just 49 games across all competitions. Many of those goals saw him bamboozle La Liga defenders and goalkeepers alike, often rounding the keeper and calmly slotting the ball into an empty net—a finish that would become his trademark.Ronaldo’s explosive form helped Barça secure a cup treble of the Copa del Rey, Supercopa de España, and UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup. Even more impressive? He was just 19 years old, offering the world its first true glimpse of a player who would go on to become one of the all-time greats.

ftbpro_01jzcj9k8cf9.title: USMNT vs. Mexico: The All-Time Record of North America’s Biggest Rivalry
ftbpro_01jzcj9k8cf9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasJul 5, 2025Meetings between the North American giants are always feisty. / John Dorton/ISI Photos/USSF/Getty ImagesFew rivalries in international soccer match the intensity and passion of Mexico vs. the U.S. men’s national team. The stakes are sky high whenever these two Concacaf giants meet. History, honor, prestige and the identity of both nations are put on the line.

For a soccer-crazy nation like Mexico, losing to their northern neighbors in a sport that is far from their most popular is unforgivable. For a rising soccer country like the U.S., which is obsessed with winning, overtaking Mexico as the region’s dominant force is a must.

It marks a bitter rivalry. From a 50-year Mexican dominance, to “Dos A Cero,” to El Tri finally conquering Columbus in 2016 and, of course, that afternoon in Jeonju, South Korea in 2002. The animosity goes back nearly a century.
Sports Illustrated looks back at the historic head-to-head record of the enormous rivalry between the USMNT and Mexico.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

This rivalry has taken on many forms over the years. / IMAGO/ZUMA Press WireGames Played: 79Mexico: 38 winsUnited States: 24 winsDraws: 17Mexico still leads the all-time head-to-head by a considerable margin. However, the USMNT has managed to close the gap significantly since El Tri went on a 24-game unbeaten run following the first meeting between the sides, which ended 4–2 to the Stars and Stripes in 1934.

Overall, Mexico has the upper-hand in the rivalry in friendly games and almost every other official competition where it’s faced the USMNT. One of the few exceptions is the most important tournament of them all.

The USMNT defeated Mexico 2–0 in the last 16 of the 2002 FIFA World Cup. / GREG WOOD/AFP via Getty ImagesOn July 17, 2002, the USMNT defeated Mexico 2–0 in the round of 16 of the 2002 FIFA World Cup—the only time these two nations have met in the sport’s most prestigious competition.
Brian McBride and Landon Donovan were the goalscorers on the day, with the latter scoring one of his six career goals vs. El Tri—the most of any USMNT player in the rivalry.

That afternoon in South Korea will forever live in infamy as one of the darkest moments in El Tri’s history. For the USMNT, on the other hand, it’s one of its greatest ever results, one that secured bragging rights over its bitter rivals for generations to come and gave birth to the “Dos A Cero” folklore.

The nations have frequently collided in the Gold Cup. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesGames Played: 9Mexico: 6 winsUnited States.: 3 winsMexico is the record champion in the Gold Cup, having lifted the trophy 10 times compared to the USMNT’s seven. Six of those El Tri titles came by defeating the USMNT in the final, including the 2011 championship, where Giovani Dos Santos scored one of the most memorable goals in the history of the rivalry.

Mexico has dominated the USMNT in World Cup qualifiers. / Icon Sportswire via Getty ImagesGames Played: 31Mexico: 16 winsUnited States: 7 winsDraws: 8Mexico and the USMNT have faced each other the most in World Cup qualifiers. El Tri has the overwhelming advantage over its neighbor.

The “Dos A Cero” mantra began even before the 2002 World Cup. It all started when the USMNT decided to start hosting its qualifying matches against Mexico in Ohio in 2001. The Stars and Stripes have defeated Mexico 2–0 in five of the six qualification matches played in that state since.

However, Mexico did manage to win at the Columbus Crew stadium once. El Tri defeated the USMNT 2–1 on its own patch in 2016, a result that played a significant role in the U.S. failing to qualify for the 2018 World Cup.

Home form has proven key for Mexico, too, with the USMNT having never won this fixture in an official match on Mexican soil. That includes 11 unsuccessful tries at El Tri’s fortress in Mexico City, the mythical Estadio Azteca.

Mexico triumphed in the 2025 Gold Cup final. / Ron Jenkins/USSF/Getty ImagesThe 2025 Gold Cup final provided the most recent clash between these bitter foes, with Mexico enjoying the last laugh following a comeback 2–1 victory at NRG Stadium in Houston.

Chris Richards had fired the USMNT into a dreamy lead after just four minutes, but Raúl Jiménez would bite back midway through the first half, blasting a shot beyond Matt Freese to restore parity for El Tri.
The match appeared to be heading for extra time, but Edson Álvarez’s header in the 77th minute decided the contest and clinched a 10th Gold Cup title for Mexico.
The USMNT will be seeking revenge when it hosts Mexico on Saturday night in Glendale, Ariz. Although technically a friendly, the clash will be anything but warmhearted.

ftbpro_01jzmwwdcn1n.title: The 25 Best Left Backs in World Soccer—Ranked
ftbpro_01jzmwwdcn1n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJul 14, 2025Nuno Mendes has fulfilled his early career potential.  / Franco Arland/Getty ImagesFor years, the left back position was overlooked, often seen as a defensive afterthought rather than a key role.

But the modern game has completely flipped that script. Thanks to tactical innovators like Pep Guardiola and others, the left back role has become one of the most challenging and influential positions on the field. Today’s left backs are expected to do it all: defend with discipline, cover endless ground and contribute creatively to the attack.
This evolution has produced a new breed of left back—versatile, dynamic and often among the standout players on their teams.
Here’s Sports Illustrated’s look at the current best in the business.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Andy Robertson joined Spurs in the summer. / Steve Christo/Corbis/Getty Images.Andy Robertson may now be past his blistering peak—the form that once had many calling him the best left back in the world—but make no mistake: he still has plenty to offer.Sure, the explosive pace that once defined his overlapping runs may have dipped slightly, dulling some of his impact in the final third. Yet the Scotsman remains a tenacious defender—solid in every challenge, relentless in recovery and never giving an opponent a moment’s peace.He’s also an unapologetically vocal leader. Make a mistake near him? You’ll hear about it immediately—and probably get a detailed rundown on how to fix it next time.That, perhaps, is why Tottenham Hotspur decided to acquire him after several difficult seasons.

Ian Maatsen. / Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty ImagesOne of many former Chelsea full backs on this list, Ian Maatsen is growing in importance for Aston Villa, particularly following Lucas Digne’s return to PSG.An electric force going forward, Maatsen excels at progressive ball-carrying and high-tempo build-up play, giving both Villa and the Netherlands, when given the chance, plenty of energy in the final third.He’s also more than happy to drift inside and operate as an inverted full back—or even a midfielder—to get more involved in the build-up. That versatility makes him a fascinating tactical weapon, capable of creating overloads in midfield before bursting forward into the space in front of him.He may not be the most imposing defender on this list, but his recovery pace is fierce. Even when he gets caught high up the pitch, Maatsen has the speed to make up ground in a hurry and get himself back into the defensive picture.

Wesley is increasingly influential for club and country. / Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesOriginally schooled as a right back, Wesley has been increasingly deployed on his unnatural flank by Gian Piero Gasperini during Roma’s flexible evolution under the cerebral Italian.“He’s a growing player,” Gasperini beamed last year. “Very strong.”The tenacious and versatile Brazilian was unfortunate to miss the 2026 World Cup through injury, thus missing an opportunity to showcase his talents to an even wider audience. But his performances for Roma, which involve him scuttling up and down the field as a flying wing back, surely won’t go under the radar for much longer.

Maxi Araújo has been superb for Sporting. / Torbjorn Tande/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesAt the 2026 World Cup against Cape Verde, Maxi Araújo became the first Uruguayan player in 56 years to register both a goal and an assist in the same World Cup match. The last to achieve the feat was Juan Martín Mujica in 1970.Araújo also found the net in Uruguay’s tournament opener against Saudi Arabia, underlining just how much of an attacking threat he can be from the left flank. Those qualities have been on full display for Sporting CP too, with the versatile full back thriving since his move from Mexico in 2024.Explosive, direct and always looking to make something happen in the final third, Araújo has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting attacking players in his position.It feels like only a matter of time before one of Europe’s giants comes calling.
Next. Best Current PL Defenders. The Best Current Premier League Defenders—Ranked. dark

Lucas Digne has returned to Paris. / Aurélien Meunier/PSG/Getty Images.There are certainly bumps to Lucas Digne’s game. The left back can make rash and costly decisions, but those odd lapses in concentration don’t overshadow the quality he provides. Wicked deliveries into the penalty area are a staple of his game, with that excellent distribution often showcased at corners and free kicks for France and, previously, Aston Villa.  Digne’s entering the twilight of his career and continues to divide opinion somewhat, but there’s a reason he’s represented Lille, PSG, Roma, Barcelona, Everton and Villa over the years.

Myles Lewis-Skelly is a smooth operator. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesMyles Lewis-Skelly plays—and carries himself—with the kind of swagger that some find off-putting. But like Jude Bellingham, it’s that very self-belief that allows him to perform at such a high level despite his age. Call it arrogance if you want, but when you’ve got the talent to back it up, who’s really complaining?And Lewis-Skelly does have the talent. He’s a fierce competitor, relentless in and out of possession and refuses to let any cause die. But he’s not just grit and drive—technically, he’s elite. He can glide past players with ease, pick out teammates with precision and break lines with his dribbling and passing. That combination of tenacity and technical brilliance is exactly why he’s been trusted in midfield roles (that arguably suit him better) despite his youth.

Andrea Cambiaso is an underappreciated talent. / Francesco Scaccianoce/Getty ImagesVersatile wingback Andrea Cambiaso has been like a Swiss Army knife for Juventus since breaking into the first team in 2023–24, able to fill multiple roles with ease. Over the past two seasons, he’s been used not only as a traditional full back, but also in an inverted role and further forward on the wing, showing his tactical flexibility.Cambiaso is a do-it-all performer: solid defensively, dynamic going forward and comfortable adapting to multiple positions. His versatility, combined with relentless work rate, has made him indispensable during a period of transition at the club, as Juventus have navigated squad changes and sought to redefine their identity.He may rarely grab the headlines with flashy moments, but Cambiaso’s consistent impact on the pitch makes him one of the most valuable and reliable players in the Juventus squad.

Maximilian Mittelstädt has thrived at Stuttgart. / Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesMaximilian Mittelstädt is a late bloomer in comparison to many of his positional peers, but the left back’s switch to Stuttgart in 2023 helped propel him toward his potential. Flourishing in Sebastian Hoeneß’s high-octane, Mittelstädt has been super consistent for one of the Bundesliga’s resurgent forces, particularly catching the eye with his explosive displays in the final third. Each campaign with VfB has yielded more goal involvements than the last, with seven followed by 11 and then, in 2025–26, an impressive 13. Such stellar showings have earned him plenty of appearances for Germany, too.

Rayan Aït-Nouri has stagnated at Man City. / Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesRayan Aït-Nouri is a serious baller.The Algerian dazzles with silky feet that could easily be mistaken for those of more attack-minded countrymen like Riyad Mahrez and Saïd Benrahma. He can turn on a dime, glide past defenders with jaw-dropping ease and make dribbling look effortless.But Aït-Nouri isn’t simply a flashy winger trapped in a fullback’s body—he pairs that flair with the vision and creativity of a top-tier playmaker, making him a constant threat whenever he gets forward.Defensively, there’s still room for improvement, which perhaps explains why he has struggled for minutes at Manchester City behind Nico O’Reilly, whom we’ll get to later. Still, Aït-Nouri remains a stellar player, even if his future may ultimately lie elsewhere.

Milos Kerkez has had a tough start to life at Liverpool. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesMilos Kerkez hasn’t quite lived up to the lofty expectations he set at Bournemouth since his 2025 move to Liverpool.Part of that, however, can be attributed to the chaos surrounding him at Anfield. Managerial changes and an evolving squad have hardly provided the ideal environment for a young player to settle, and with plenty of time still on his side, Kerkez has every opportunity to prove the doubters wrong.Because there’s no doubting the talent. Explosively quick, physically imposing and armed with a delivery that could make David Beckham do a double take, Kerkez has all the ingredients of a modern full back. Now, it’s simply about finding that level consistently for the Reds.

Adrien Truffert has quickly impressed in England. /  Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesWhen it became apparent that Milos Kerkez’s stint at Bournemouth would be relatively short and sweet, thoughts quickly turned to who could replace the impressive Hungarian. It didn’t take long for the Cherries to settle on Rennes captain Adrien Truffert.It didn’t take Truffert long to show exactly why he had been one of Ligue 1’s standout performers, either. The Frenchman is not only highly capable in one-vs-one situations defensively, but also a tremendous attacking threat who loves to whip the ball into the penalty area.Throw in his dynamism and athleticism, which see him charge up and down the pitch with a seemingly never-ending battery life, and Bournemouth don’t miss Kerkez at all.

Alejandro Balde has fallen down the pecking order in Catalonia. / David Ramirez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIt once looked like Barcelona had found the perfect heir to Jordi Alba’s throne in Alejandro Balde.That hasn’t quite been how things have transpired so far, but the potential is still there.Balde broke out in style during the 2022–23 season as Xavi’s side stormed to the La Liga title. The following year proved more difficult, however, with injuries and inconsistency halting his momentum and eventually forcing him to the sidelines.Since then, though, Balde has bounced back. Fully fit and firing, he has re-established himself as one of Barça’s most important players, playing a key role in their back-to-back La Liga triumphs in 2024–25 and 2025–26. His trademark bursts down the flank, improved decision-making and ever-growing defensive maturity have made him a constant asset at both ends of the pitch.

David Raum is so consistent. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesLike many modern left backs, David Raum excels with his head down, bursting toward the opposition goal. That attacking threat has made him one of Germany’s most impactful defenders over recent years. RB Leipzig have benefitted from his fierce speed, relentless running and turbo-charged left boot. He delivered 12 goal involvements for the Bundesliga outfit in 2025–26, which was his second-best return since joining the club. Defensively, Raum is very solid, too. The physicality which makes him deadly in the opponent’s half also helps snuff out danger and thwart a band of tricky right wingers in Germany and beyond.

Álvaro Carreras joined Real Madrid in 2025. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesManchester United have long been desperate for a reliable left back. Yet somehow, they let one of the brightest young talents slip right through their fingers: Álvaro Carreras.Signed by United in 2022, he was quietly sold to Benfica just a couple of years later for a bargain price after a few loan spells. Carreras quickly blossomed into one of Portugal’s hottest young prospects—and arguably its best left back—so it was perhaps no surprise when Real Madrid paid the big bucks to take him home to Spain.Carreras has that rare blend of sharp tactical awareness, blistering pace and flair that turns defence into attack. His progressive passing and fearless runs down the flank have made him a standout performer for Los Blancos.

ftbpro_01jzqbnmw1ah.title: The 25 Best Defensive Midfielders in World Soccer—Ranked
ftbpro_01jzqbnmw1ah.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJul 18, 2025Rodri has forged quite the legacy. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesIn today’s fast-paced game, defensive midfielders are often the unsung heroes—the relentless engine powering every great team.

They’re not just ball-winners; they’re tacticians, distributors and masters of the tempo. From breaking up attacks to launching precise passes, these players control the game’s rhythm while covering every blade of grass with stamina and smarts.

The role demands total commitment for the full 90 minutes, blending grit with grace and aggression with intelligence—and often, a top-class No. 6 is the difference between victory and defeat, progression or elimination or lifting a trophy instead of settling for second best.

Some players have evolved from classy defensive midfielders into world-beating central midfielders, but there’s still an abundance of quality remaining from those who sit a little deeper. Here, Sports Illustrated ranks the current best in the business.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Andrey Santos traded Chelsea for Man Utd. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesJack of all trades, master of none. Usually a withering insult, it’s actually a complimentary assessment of Andrey Santos and his value in the middle of the field. The Brazilian will never be the glitziest name on any team sheet, but he’s super consistent and boasts the ability to plug many roles within the engine room. Chelsea saw glimpses of his precocious talent during his stint in west London, but Manchester United supporters will be eager to see more frequent servings of his ability. He’s still young, with plenty of time to hone his craft.

Nico González has enormous potential. / Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesNico González was drafted in as Manchester City’s Rodri replacement midway through the 2024–25 season due to an injury to the Ballon d’Or winner. Those are not easy shoes to fill and the Spaniard initially struggled to replicate the lofty standards of his compatriot. However, the enforcer has bucked up his ideas since, and while he’s still operating far below the level of his World Cup-winning compatriot, he’s beginning to find a more consistent level.  González was deemed surplus to requirements as Enzo Maresca ushered in a new era at the Etihad Stadium, resulting in a move to Newcastle United for more regular minutes. Luckily, time is on the midfielder’s side, and he could become a hero on Tyneside.

Ayyoub Bouaddi captured the imagination at the 2026 World Cup. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesMan City set about rebuilding their midfield ahead of Maresca’s first campaign, splashing an absolute fortune on three leading talents: Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi. The latter is the youngest and least experienced of the trio, yet his reputation is sky high after an exceptional 2026 World Cup campaign at the base of Morocco’s midfield. Despite his tender age, Bouaddi delivered a stream of graceful yet combative performances—those more fitting of someone 10 years his senior. Bouaddi’s already a terrific midfielder. He should get even better in the years to come.

James Garner has blossomed on Merseyside. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesManchester United have allowed some talented academy graduates to slip through their fingers over the past decade, and James Garner is yet another example of their negligence. Ironically, many of the club’s recent difficulties in midfield could have been solved by the Englishman, whose no-nonsense performances for Everton have earned him widespread acclaim. Garner is a formidable presence in the No.6 position with his endless energy reserves and crunching challenges, but he’s also a classy distributor with terrific vision. It’s no surprise he’s now a senior England international.

N’Golo Kanté continues to deliver year on year. / Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu/Getty ImagesHe might be deep into the twilight of his career and playing his soccer in Türkiye, but trust us when we say—N’Golo Kanté has still absolutely got it.Kante may be racking up the miles, but the engine’s still running at full throttle. The French midfielder covers every single blade of grass, motoring around the center of the field extinguishing fires and reclaiming possession. The World Cup and two-time Premier League winner might be playing outside of Europe’s elite divisions, but Fenerbahçe supporters can attest to his consistently excellent performances. Everybody seemingly has a soft spot for Kanté.

Morten Hjulmand is ever so consistent. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAfter honing his craft at Admira Wacker and then Lecce, Morten Hjulmand earned his big break with a move to Portuguese giants Sporting CP in the summer of 2023.The Dane quietly became one of the most important pieces in Sporting’s setup, playing a central role in historic back-to-back Liga Portugal titles. While goal-machine Viktor Gyökeres grabbed the headlines each week, Hjulmand was one of the squad’s unsung heroes.A defensively intelligent midfielder with an excellent read of the game, Hjulmand anticipates danger before it fully develops. Time and again, he’s the one to break up opposition attacks, turning defense into swift counter attacks that often end with a ball in behind.Hjulmand has taken his talents to Atlético Madrid, where Diego Simeone is certain to put them to effective use.

Carlos Baleba finally earned his Old Trafford move. / Dan Mullan/Getty ImagesDefensive midfielders are usually known for being strong, powerful and—if we’re being honest—a bit rigid. Carlos Baleba is anything but that. He combines sheer athleticism with the traditional traits of a holding midfielder, making him one of the most unique talents around.Baleba brings defensive resilience in spades—breaking up play with real bite, blocking everything in sight—but pairs it with exceptional ball-carrying ability.
