ftbpro_01m41nn3fgje.title: ‘What He Means’—Bruno Fernandes Sends Cristiano Ronaldo Plea Amid Portugal Turmoil
ftbpro_01m41nn3fgje.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 3, 2026Bruno Fernandes (right) took over as Portugal captain following Cristiano Ronaldo’s exit.  / Diogo Faria Reis/MB Media/Getty Images Cristiano Ronaldo’s abrupt and unceremonious exit from the Portugal national team has been one of the major storylines of the ongoing international break, but teammate Bruno Fernandes is pleading for him not to retire from the team ... not like this.

Last Wednesday, Ronaldo left Portugal’s training camp after a falling out with manager Jorge Jesus, who benched him in the clash against Norway and later stated that no player can pressure him into making any decisions.

Following Ronaldo’s departure, Fernandes took over as captain and helped Portugal defeat Denmark 4–2. The Manchester United playmaker has played with Ronaldo both at the club and international levels, and on the eve of Portugal’s Sunday match against Norway, he pleaded for Ronaldo not to make any hasty decisions, because this isn’t how his illustrious international career should end.

“I spoke with Cris out of respect, because I know what he means to us Portuguese and because my hope is that he doesn't make rash decisions and want to leave the national team altogether,” Fernandes revealed to RTP3. “If he wants to do that, it has to be on a celebratory day, not in a way like this.

“He deserves it; he's the greatest icon of our football and of our country, someone who took the country's name to a place and level it had never been before, with all due respect to Eusébio and Luís Figo.

“If Ronaldo ever has to leave the national team, it has to be on a celebratory day, not on a day when the country is divided. Being in the national team has to be a place for everyone and a place for all, where these kinds of divisions don't exist.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Bruno Fernandes (left) had a conversation with Cristiano Ronaldo after he left the Portugal national team.  / Michael Reaves/Getty Images Unsurprisingly, Ronaldo’s decision to abandon Portugal’s camp has resulted in mixed reactions that have divided the nation. Some fans have turned on Jesus and erected billboards supporting Ronaldo, while the manager has doubled-down on his stance. Fernandes called for unity.

“The most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cris will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, our football and surely, of our country, not only for what he did not only in Portugal but all over the world,” Fernandes told assembled media prior to Sunday’s clash.

“He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of the Portuguese people. And I think what’s most important now is to stop dividing the waters because there are no divisions here in the national team. The national team is one and it will continue to be one.

“Independently of the outside rumors and noise, I think all parts should resolve things behind closed doors. I think that’s how the national team should work and I think that’s how it will work. The most important thing is that it all ends well.”
If this is the end, it wasn’t meant to end this way. pic.twitter.com/IoHayRTesH

Fernandes added: “We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not take sides, that it respects all sides. At the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone’s respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less.”

Portugal will face Norway looking to make it four wins from four during a highly scrutinized September-October international camp. Jesus’s side will reconvene in November for the last two games of 2026, and all eyes will be on Ronaldo and whether or not he is included in the roster—though more chapters of the saga will surely be written before then.

ftbpro_01m41v92qjt9.title: Tyler Adams Is the Man Tasked With Pioneering the USMNT’s New Era
ftbpro_01m41v92qjt9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 3, 2026Tyler Adams was named the USMNT’s new captain. / Luke Hales/Getty ImagesJust days after long-time U.S. men’s national team captain Tim Ream announced his retirement from international soccer, manager Mauricio Pochettino chose a new man to command the Stars and Stripes.

27-year-old midfielder Tyler Adams was bestowed the captain’s armband on Friday ahead of the USMNT’s clash with Mexico, its toughest battle yet of the post-World Cup era. It is a title Adams is anticipated to hold throughout the next four-year cycle, which has quickly become regarded as the new dawn of the USMNT.
“[We’re] so happy to announce and for everyone to know that [Adams] is going to be our leader and our captain,” Pochettino told reporters.

“We’ve been [in] a very good relationship in the last two years. We were talking a lot, and I think he knows what I expect, and he’s a perfect role model for everyone in the way that the philosophy, the future, representing that amazing country ... He’s the player and the person that can lead that period that we have ahead. And I [say] congratulations.”

It came as no surprise when Pochettino announced a new, long-term captain. Not only was 38-year-old Ream on his way out, but everything the Argentine boss has done since the end of the 2026 World Cup has been with an eye to the future. The USMNT enjoyed a largely dreamy run on home soil this summer; however, Pochettino has been adamant to use that success as just a small foundation on which to enact incredible change.

Pochettino’s need for a “fresh start” has manifested most abundantly in his roster decisions this fall, calling up just half of his World Cup stars and a whopping 12 newcomers, including eight teenagers. And it now manifests as a new man at the helm.

Adams will play a central role in guiding the USMNT through Pochettino’s complete renewal, including helping the youngsters acclimate to the grand stage that they have just been thrust upon. But who is Adams, and is he capable of bearing this huge responsibility?
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Tyler Adams is no stranger to commanding the Stars and Stripes. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAmid a team of fresh-faced and energetic newcomers, Pochettino needs a strong and steady force he can rely on, which makes Adams the perfect fit for the captaincy.

“I'm extremely honored and grateful for the opportunity,” Adams said upon being named. “I think that, like Mauricio said, we’ve obviously built an amazing relationship over the past two years with all the staff, with my teammates here, going into this past World Cup.
“As we start a new cycle, I’m excited to be able to help my teammates and the staff in any way possible in order to win, grow the federation and ultimately take that next step. So, I appreciate it.”

The defensive midfielder is no stranger to being the team’s anchor. He has done so throughout the center of the park ever since his senior debut in 2017 and for the majority of his 58 caps with the national team, including at the World Cup this summer. His play is defined by his ability to pull the team’s strings—nothing happens in the midfield without his say-so. His communication style is frequent and direct, and his consistency on the defensive side of the ball allows those in front him to have more creative liberties.

Adams is also no stranger to donning the captain’s armband. At just 23 years old, he was named the USMNT’s captain for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, the youngest of all of the nations’ captains at the prestigious competition. He played every minute of that tournament, earning U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year honors for his contributions on and off the pitch.

Adams was the youngest captain at the 2022 World Cup. /  Brad Smith/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAlthough the captaincy went to Ream for the 2026 tournament, Adams continued to play a valuable role for the team. He started four of the USMNT’s five matches en route to the round of 16 on home soil, helping the Stars and Stripes win out the group stage and secure a first knockout stage win in 24 years. Adams then served as the team’s captain in last week’s international friendly against Peru, the team’s first match post-World Cup.

Another strength of Adams is his experience at soccer’s highest levels. Aside from playing in two World Cups, the New Yorker currently plays overseas in the English Premier League for Bournemouth, a team he has been with since 2023. Adams has likewise established himself as a key starter for the Cherries and has, on occasion, donned the captain’s armband for them. In addition to navigating England’s top flight—one of, if not, the most competitive domestic leagues in the world—Adams is competing in the Europa League this season, Bournemouth’s first-ever time in European competition.

Perhaps what Adams’s teammates value most about him, though, is his fierce intensity. He is the first to defend his teammates in any situation, a tendency he has already put on display twice this fall. In the match against Peru, USMNT debutant Cavan Sullivan got into a minor scuffle. Adams immediately interjected, coming to the defense of the 17-year-old. In the following match against Chile, a much larger fight broke out, seeing Adams rush to the defense of Chris Richards and pull a Chilean player off of the USMNT center back.
Adams may have a lot more responsibilities to bear, but he is more than capable of handling them.

ftbpro_01m41vkec9fq.title: Former Real Madrid Manager Explains ‘Irreplaceable’ Catalyst for Los Blancos’ Downfall
ftbpro_01m41vkec9fq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 3, 2026Davide Ancelotti (right) was his father’s assistant coach during his second stint at Real Madrid.  / Jean Catuffe/Getty Images Former Real Madrid assistant manager Davide Ancelotti admitted that when Toni Kroos called it a career after the 2023–24 season, Los Blancos “lost something they will never recover.”

Now at the helm of Lille in Ligue 1, Ancelotti served as the main assistant to his father, Carlo Ancelotti, during the latter’s second chapter at the helm of Real Madrid between 2021–25, a period in which Los Blancos conquered two Champions League titles.
Recently, the younger Ancelotti spoke with AS and revealed that when Kroos retired in 2024, he left a massive hole in Real Madrid’s squad that has been impossible to fill.

“You can survive, but they lost something they will never recover,” Ancelotti said. “[You lose] the best player in the world at his position. You can’t be like ‘I need another Kroos’ because there isn’t one.”
Official Announcement: Toni Kroos.#RealMadrid | #GraciasKroos

“He owned games,” Ancelotti added. “He owned the rhythm. The game was played as he wanted, if he wanted the possessions to be sideways or vertical, he decided, and he was fundamental because he dictated the rhythm of the game.
“And then he also covered ground. Toni was a player that ran 11 kilometers per match. And he defended, he had tactical understanding. I loved it whenever he played as a No. 6.”

Kroos hung up his boots in the summer of 2024 after conquering Europe and La Liga in his final season. The 2025 FIFA Intercontinental Cup is the only piece of silverware Los Blancos have added to their trophy case since.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Davide Ancelotti (right) believes Real Madrid need more than just superstar attackers. / Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images Although Ancelotti is right in his assessment that replacing Toni Kroos is easier said than done, Real Madrid haven’t really tried. Even after Luka Modrić left the club a year later, Los Blancos still haven’t significantly investing in a midfield rebuild, sticking with players that were already in house when Kroos was still at the club.

Kylian Mbappé was Real Madrid’s marquee signing in the summer of Kroos’s retirement. Los Blancos have revamped their backline over the last two years, but instead of signing a top-tier midfielder, Madrid completed the most expensive transfer in club history this summer to acquire exciting winger Yan Diomande.
“I don’t want everything I say about Madrid to be taken as a criticism,” Ancelotti said. “But when you have Modrić and Kroos, the ball will get there every time someone runs into space.

“I’m not saying the players they have now don’t have that ability. What I’m saying is that to play vertically, you need someone that knows how to place the ball. Playing vertically doesn’t mean you need to have eight sprinters, it also means you need someone that can release them. It’s an idea of how to play.”
“Inevitably, for Real Madrid’s dynamic style, losing Toni has been very complicated, because suddenly so many things get taken away,” Ancelotti added.

Aurélien Tchouaméni (left) and Fede Valverde continue to feature regularly in Real Madrid’s double pivot.  / Denis Doyle/Getty Images Aurélien Tchouaméni, Federico Valverde, Eduardo Camavinga and Bernardo Silva are seemingly Real Madrid’s top central midfield options during the 2026–27 season. The first three were already at the club during the Kroos–Modrić era and Silva, 32, joined this summer as a free agent and is already looking like nothing more than a rotational piece.
For much of the spring and summer, the expectation was that Real Madrid would address their midfield needs by signing one of the best players in the world at the position: Rodri.

But the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner ended up swerving Los Blancos to join bitter-rivals Barcelona—though Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has an alternative version of events. For Ancelotti, though, Rodri would’ve been a brilliant addition for Real Madrid.
“Yes, Rodri fits in every team in the world,” Ancelotti said, before later adding that “with or without Rodri, Real Madrid will be competing until the very end as always.”

The Lille manager also recognized that “Real Madrid’s recent history shows why Mourinho is the ideal manager for this moment.” When the Portuguese manager arrived for his first stint at the Bernabéu, he was tasked with ending Barcelona’s dominance over Spanish soccer—a similar situation to the one he encountered upon his return this summer.
Now though, Mourinho must do what Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa have been unable to do over the past two years: lead Los Blancos to their first major trophy in the post-Kroos era.

ftbpro_01m4290e6dj4.title: USMNT Player Ratings vs. Mexico: Two Stars Are Born in Dream Night for U.S. Soccer
ftbpro_01m4290e6dj4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas12:40 AM EDTJulian Hall (left) and Cavan Sullivan (second from left to right) stole the show vs. Mexico.  / Chris Coduto/Getty Images        The U.S. men’s national team enjoyed a fairytale Saturday night with a 3–0 win against arch-nemesis Mexico, thanks to a pair of goals from teenagers Julian Hall and Cavan Sullivan.

It wasn’t the easiest of starts for the USMNT, who struggled to string together passes to bypass Mexico’s aggressive press. Mauricio Pochettino’s men had to dig deep, but they slowly started to settle into the match.

When the Stars and Stripes finally managed to manufacture a sustained possession, they pounced. Alex Freeman freed a charging Giovanni Reyna who got away from his man and whipped a powerful cross that Raúl Rangel couldn’t handle, leaving the rebound on a platter for 18-year-old rising star Julian Hall to introduce himself under the bright lights of North America’s biggest rivalry to give the USMNT the lead 28 minutes in.

The USMNT improved in the second half, and just when Mexico seemed to get back in the game, it was 17-year-old wonderkid Cavan Sullivan’s turn to announce himself on the biggest stage. Sullivan intercepted an egregious Rangel pass, and without any hesitation, he kept his cool and lobbed a shot over the goalkeeper to double his side’s lead just past the hour mark.

Mexico completely collapsed, and Mateo Chávez was sent off after slapping Sebastian Berhalter. Then, Malik Tillman added the cherry on top of a sensational night with a powerful hit into the roof of the net in the 85th minute.

The Stars and Stripes categorically erased Mexico from the pitch in the second half and could’ve easily inflicted more harm. Still, in one of the greatest nights of Pochettino’s tenure, the Argentine boss got his first win in North America’s biggest rivalry and the USMNT’s 2030 cycle is off to to a perfect start.

Julian Hall’s dream start to his international career continued.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images Pochettino’s side looked uncomfortable for much of the first half against an intense El Tri that dominated possession, swarmed to the ball and generated the most dangerous chance of the early exchanges.

But when Mexico looked like the superior side, the USMNT responded by suddenly slowing the game down and manufacturing its longest possession of the first half. Sebastian Berhalter dropped deep to quarterback the team’s buildup, and players up the pitch freely exchanged possessions to confuse Mexican markers.

Freeman, operating almost as a right winger, threaded a pass to an unmarked Reyna down the channel—on the opposite side flank from where he started the game. The Strasbourg man whipped in a cross, and Hall brilliantly sniffed out the open area to tap-in the USMNT’s opener off a rebound.

After a difficult start, Hall gave the hosts the lead with their first and only shot on target of the first half. Against a team that wasted the few important chances it created, the Stars and Stripes had made the most of theirs.
The opener stunned El Tri, and it was never able to restore its initial superiority. The USMNT, meanwhile, grew into the game and was far and away the better side in the second half.
The USMNT produced a full team effort on Saturday night.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images *Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Diego Kochen—7.3: A shaky performance from the 20-year-old goalkeeper, who was lucky Santiago Gimenez didn’t pounce on a rebound he left served on a platter. Had some nice passes from deep but also a couple of risky ones. Nice save in the only shot on goal he faced.
RB: Alex Freeman—8.3: Pocketed Orbelín Pineda and was a threat whenever he ventured forward. A clever flick for a charging Reyna started the action of his team’s opener.
CB: Chris Richards—6.8: Dominant in the air and calmly dealt with Mexico’s threat.
CB: Auston Trusty—7.8: Like his partner alongside him, Tursty didn’t put a foot wrong defensively. He was often the first pass out of the back and was effective with his distribution.
LB: Antonee Robinson—7.7: Extremely lucky that a poor clearance didn’t turn into Mexico’s early opener.

RM: Cavan Sullivan—8.3: Came alive in the second half, fearlessly taking on markers and often getting the better of them. His dream night was crowned when he became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history with a classy finish.
CM: Sebastian Berhalter—7.4: Suffered early, especially out of possession, but the USMNT looked at its best when the midfielder dropped to organize possessions from deep.

ftbpro_01m42aw8j39n.title: USMNT Teenager Julian Hall Accomplishes on First Try What Christian Pulisic Never Could
ftbpro_01m42aw8j39n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 3, 2026Julian Hall (left) has scored in three-consecutive matches. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images (Julian Hall); Alex Grimm/Getty Images (Christian Pulisic)I promise it’s harder than Julian Hall makes it look.

That was no doubt the thought swirling through the head of Christian Pulisic on his couch Saturday night, watching the 18-year-old striker score his third-consecutive goal for the Stars and Stripes, a feat he himself has never achieved.

Hall earned his first-ever call-up for the USMNT this fall, joining 27 other players for the four-game September-October international window, while the USMNT’s poster player, Pulisic, was shockingly left at home.

Manager Mauricio Pochettino’s bold gamble paid off immediately, though, seeing the New York City kid score in each of his first three caps. Hall came off the bench in his debut against Peru last week, and just 10 minutes after taking the pitch, he found the back of the net with his knee. He also provided an assist in the 90th minute, guiding the USMNT to an emphatic 4–1 victory.

Hall was even more dazzling in the following friendly against Chile, his first-career start. He facilitated the USMNT’s opening goal with a sneaky “dummy” move that left the Chilean backline utterly confused, before finding the back of the net himself off of a leaping header in the 51st minute.  Although the USMNT added two more goals before the final whistle, it was ultimately because of Hall that the team was able to gain its attacking edge and walk away with a 4–2 victory. Hall became the youngest player in USMNT history to score in back-to-back games.

But the teenager wasn’t finished. His third act of heroism came in Saturday’s marquee match against bitter-rival Mexico. Once again cracking the starting lineup, Hall capitalized on a fumbled ball in the penalty box to put the USMNT ahead in the 28th minute. Midfielder Giovanni Reyna had taken a near-post shot from the goal line, which El Tri goalkeeper Raúl Rangel spilled out of his hands. Hall was waiting patiently in front of the goal mouth to capitalize on it, blasting it first-time into the net.

Hall became just the third player in USMNT history to score a goal in each of his first three caps and the first player to do so in over 20 years. Eddie Johnson achieved the feat in 2004–05, while Alexander Rae did so back in 1937.
Next. Julian Hall’s Swift Rise to MLS Stardom and USMNT Stature. Julian Hall’s Swift Rise to MLS Stardom and USMNT Stature. dark

Malik Tillman (left) and Hall are the only two USMNT players in the past decade to score in three-consecutive matches. / Rich Storry/Getty ImagesHall joins the more recent company of teammate Malik Tillman as the only two USMNT players in the past decade to score in three-consecutive appearances.

Prior to Tillman, it was a feat last achieved by USMNT legend Clint Dempsey back in 2016 in Copa América play, and it is one that Pulisic has attempted and failed his entire international career. “Captain America” has scored in two-consecutive games three times in his career (June 2017, October 2017, October 2023) but never extended the streak to a third match.
Hall will look to make it four-consecutive in the USMNT’s final game of the September-October window against Canada on Tuesday.

ftbpro_01m42fkfrcnv.title: Cavan Sullivan Achieves the Inevitable, Becoming Youngest Goalscorer in USMNT History
ftbpro_01m42fkfrcnv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely12:05 AM EDTCavan Sullivan scored his first USMNT goal. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesTo be the future you must rewrite history.
It’s something teenage phenom Cavan Sullivan has become all too good at it, and there is no doubt he is the future of the U.S. men’s national team.

At 17 years and five days old, Sullivan became the youngest goal-scorer in USMNT history, finding the back of the net on Saturday night against Mexico. He overtook the record set just days ago by teammate Mathis Albert, who scored in Tuesday’s friendly against Chile at just 17 years, 131 days old.

“These are the moments you dream about since you are three, four, five, six years old,” Sullivan said after the victory to TNT Sports. “I manifested this moment not just these past couple of hours when I found out that I was starting, but my whole life.
“So this is an incredible moment for my family, for me. What an honor it is, just really grateful the coaches trusted me and gave me this opportunity.”

He intercepted a pass from El Tri goalkeeper Raúl Rangel, before brilliantly lofting the ball over his head into the back of the net. The 62nd minute finish brought the USMNT to a 2–0 lead against its Concacaf arch nemesis, before Malik Tillman later added a third.

“I remember I probably shouldn’t have pressed the goalie,” Sullivan reflected, chuckling. “It felt like there was not really anybody pressing behind me, but you know, that’s why you go and that’s why you put in the work, and I was rewarded for doing so.
“From there, it was sort of a blackout. I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn’t hit the crossbar or go over. I was getting nervous when it was in the air and then it was a blur.”

Sullivan has his fair share of records in MLS. / Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images“He is a fighter. He is a warrior,” manager Mauricio Pochettino said of Sullivan after the win against Mexico. “It is difficult to find this type of player, with a tremendous quality with the ball in possession ... It is unbelievable to have a player like this. This is fantastic news for the U.S.A. I hope that he continues in that way, growing.”

Sullivan has never done anything by the standard of others. Just two days before his 17th birthday, Sullivan became the youngest player to debut for the USMNT in over 20 years, earning a start in the friendly against Peru.

The youngster has also made his fair share of history at the domestic level in Major League Soccer. At just 14 years, 293 days old, the Philadelphia Union homegrown became the youngest player ever to debut in the league—or any major league in North America for that matter. He broke the 20-year record of American prodigy Freddy Adu, who first debuted in the league at 14 years, 306 days old back in 2004.

Sullivan has enjoyed an unprecedented campaign with the Union this season, the reason he has been thrust firmly into the limelight and earned the call from Pochettino this fall. He has racked up six goals and eight assists in the last eight MLS matches alone, helping the Philadelphia side to a club-record 12-game unbeaten streak. For his heroics, he earned MLS Player of the Month for September, beating out the likes of Lionel Messi and becoming the youngest player to ever earn the honor. In just four September outings, he had a whopping nine goal contributions (four goals, five assists).

Earlier this month, he also broke Adu’s record for the most goal contributions by a player aged 16 or younger in a single season (10), notching his 11th in a Sept. 13 clash with San Diego FC. And there are still more games to be played.
The best is yet to come for Sullivan, who will no doubt continue to write his name all over history and leave American soccer forever changed.

ftbpro_01m435y5zesf.title: Bellingham Rolls the Clock Back 33 Years to Earn the Greatest Praise Imaginable
ftbpro_01m435y5zesf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath7:00 AM EDTJude Bellingham is on fire. / Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty ImagesJude Bellingham can become one of the best players of all time, according to legendary midfielder turned pundit Roy Keane.
The 23-year-old, who was named England Men’s Player of the Year 2025–26, scored one and set up three in England’s 7–0 rout of Croatia in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday.

A key player under manager Thomas Tuchel, Bellingham was one of the standout performers of the 2026 World Cup, scoring seven times as England finished the tournament third. He has continued his international form into the Nations League campaign and now has 13 goal involvements in his last 11 matches.

Meanwhile, for his club, the Real Madrid superstar has started 2026–27 strongly with three goals and two assists in seven outings, operating as the designated No. 10 in new manager José Mourinho’s system.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Roy Keane insists there is more to come from Bellingham. / Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty ImagesITV pundit and former Manchester United captain Roy Keane—a man notoriously hard to please—was among those hugely impressed by Bellingham’s performance in Rijeka, which contributed to Croatia’s biggest-ever defeat.
“There’s still a lot more to come from [Bellingham],” Keane said. ”Bellingham can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time.
“His attitude for England recently... I have been praising him for being fantastic in possession, but what he is doing out of possession, that lifts all these players.

“If you have a player who is that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and is playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball, that will inspire all the other players.”

Bellingham’s England teammate Bukayo Saka was similarly enthused, telling reporters postmatch: “He [Bellingham] was amazing tonight to be fair. He deserved player of the year and he probably deserves man of the match tonight as well. He was special. Happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team.”
Jude Bellingham is playing his own game. pic.twitter.com/QYajplqsbm
As a result of his goal and hat trick of assists in Croatia, Bellingham became the first player since 1993 to register four goal involvements in a single game for England.
The last player to achieve the feat was David Platt was back in 1993, in a World Cup qualifier against San Marino—then 122nd in FIFA’s rankings, as reported by Opta.
The Three Lions famously conceded first in that match when Davide Gualtieri stunned the visitors inside the first minute. However, England rallied to win 7–1, with Platt getting four assists.
This week’s win over Croatia feels far more significant for England and Bellingham and their 7–0 scoreline marks the Three Lions’s biggest margin of victory against a top 50 ranked nation since 1992.
England faces Czechia in its final outing of the September-October international break on Tuesday with Bellingham in the mood for even more records.

ftbpro_01m436eskj67.title: ‘Greedy B------’—Man Utd Legend Hits Back at Rooney Over Man City Verdict
ftbpro_01m436eskj67.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:15 AM EDTWayne Rooney (left) and Paul Scholes are both serial Premier League champions. / Matthew Peters/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United’s legendary former midfielder Paul Scholes has bluntly clashed with Wayne Rooney’s rejection of a retroactive Premier League title, describing himself as a “greedy b------“ who would happily accept another medal at the expense of Manchester City.

In the aftermath of City’s stunning guilty verdict in their case with the Premier League regarding mass accusations of financial breaches, one of the most potent areas of discussion has been a relitigation of the past.

City have been found to have misreported their revenues by more than $1.2 billion (£900 million) across the nine seasons between 2009–10 and 2017–18. During that period, the Etihad outfit won three league titles, the first of which was snatched away from a Manchester United side containing Rooney and Scholes with the last kick of the 2011–12 season.
Rooney has admitted that he “wouldn’t feel comfortable” receiving a medal for that title. “I don’t think we deserve it. We didn’t do enough that season to win the league,” he explained.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
“Keep hearing ex-teammates saying they want trophies taking off them but they don’t want their medals...” Scholes wrote on social media, “f--- that I’m a greedy b------ I want my medal.”

With 11 titles to his name, the Manchester United academy graduate already stands out as the second-most successful player in the history of the Premier League, falling two shy of his teammate Ryan Giggs. A dozen top-flight triumphs would take Scholes onto the same haul as a certain Lionel Messi (who won 10 La Ligas and a pair of Ligue 1 crowns), but it would appear that his hunger will not be sated.

Manchester City won the first of their eight Premier League titles in 2011–12, at Manchester United’s expense. / PAUL ELLIS/AFP/Getty ImagesThe first point to stress is that City’s guilty verdict—which is not an “opinion,” as the club keep on saying, but the finding of an independent judicial commission after two years of deliberation—is subject to an appeal.

As City’s CEO Ferran Soriano was keen to stress in a wide-eyed message to all employees, the club are also prepared to explore “all other legal avenues” available, be that a further challenge to the Premier League or even involving the High Court of England and Wales.

It remains to be seen at what point of that process, if ever, City are handed any punishments by the Premier League. However, if it does come to that, then England’s top flight has the power to do absolutely anything, including giving Scholes a medal Rooney doesn’t want.

Nevertheless, the initial response to the official verdict was that Premier League clubs had “little appetite” to see City stripped of their titles, let alone to have those championships redistributed, per BBC Sport. Between the start of the period of investigation into City and the guilty verdict, almost half of the Premier League’s entire history has elapsed. Rewriting the record books for such a long period could bring the whole competition into disrepute.

On an individual level, there is an argument that redistributed titles would inspire little satisfactory retribution for the players. Former Liverpool center back Jamie Carragher made the compelling case that a title is not defined by the pot of silver which it brings.

“I’ve been very lucky to win a few medals,” Carragher outlined. “I never look at the medal years later. But my mind goes back to a moment, I get a feeling in my stomach. I remember the referee blowing a final whistle of a big game. Those players will never get that feeling and it was robbed by Manchester City. That’s what they haven’t got.”

ftbpro_01m437sc06ba.title: ‘He’s Different’—Jose Mourinho’s Biggest Critic Completes Surprise U-Turn
ftbpro_01m437sc06ba.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath8:05 AM EDTHas José Mourinho really changed? / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesFormer Real Madrid captain, and one-time adversary of José Mourinho, Iker Casillas has has claimed the 63-year-old manager has returned to the Bernabéu “different.”

Goalkeeper Casillas was a key member of the roster during Mourinho’s first tenure at Madrid between 2010 and 2013. They won both the Copa del Rey and La Liga together, but an apparent rift between the two led to Casillas being benched during the 2012–13 season as Mourinho and Madrid unraveled.

To this day, there is much speculation about what exactly happened between the pair. In the recently released Netflix series bearing his name, Mourinho insinuated Casillas had become “spoiled,” while he disagreed with Real Madrid players maintaining close friendships with their Barcelona counterparts as the two clubs battled for honors during the season.
The fallout of the Casillas-Mourinho issue had a detrimental effect on the locker room as Madrid ended the season trophyless and the manager departed under a cloud.
“With José Mourinho, it was a marriage that ended badly,” Casillas told L’Equipe.

When Mourinho’s name began being linked with a sensational return to the Bernabéu earlier this year, Casillas posted on X: “I have no problem with Mourinho. He seems like a great professional to me. I don’t want him at Real Madrid. I think other coaches would be better equipped to coach at the club of my life. Personal opinion. Nothing more.”
Casillas was also tipped to re-join Madrid in a senior leadership role under defeated presidential candidate Enrique Riquelme, who opposed Mourinho’s return.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Casillas and Mourinho’s “marriage” ended badly. /  YASSER AL-ZAYYAT/AFP/GettyImagesCasillas’s latest comments on Mourinho, however, appear to suggest he has taken on a different perspective.
Speaking to former Atlético Madrid assistant manager Germán Burgos on his own YouTube channel, Casillas claimed to see a “different” Mourinho to the one who helmed Madrid the last time around.
“He’s a different José. He doesn’t look like... He looks like the same successful coach, with his talent and all, but he’s come with a different idea,” Casillas said.
“The one who has come to Madrid is a different Mourinho, he is the same successful and talented coach, but he has arrived in a different way.”
The legendary goalkeeper held back from getting into the issues of the past, only adding: “I still laugh about it, I remember a lot of things.”
Casillas ultimately outlasted Mourinho at Madrid by two years, going on to win the third Champions League of his career in the season after the Portuguese manager departed.

Mourinho was left incensed by the Madrid derby defeat. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty ImagesCasillas is striking a more hopeful tone these days, but there have been signs that Madrid could be about to repeat history.

When Mourinho returned to Madrid this summer, he introduced himself as “more mature now, less emotional, more controlled.” Many fans have been hopeful that one of soccer’s most combustible figures had left his more destructive tendencies at his former employers and mellowed to become the coach Madrid needs to get back on track.
However, just a month into the 2026–27 season, there are signs that the turbulence that has become a hallmark of much of Mourinho’s career may not be far away.
The 63-year-old brought printouts to his postmatch press conference following the Madrid derby defeat in order to hammer the match officials and played into conspiracy theories against Los Blancos.

“If ‘they’ leave us in peace, and let us compete on an even playing field, there’s a long way left,” he told reporters, when asked if his team could still fight for the title, despite being six point behind at the first international break.
What has not happened yet is any major breakdown in relationships with his own players. Time will tell if Mourinho really is different.

ftbpro_01m4390g54he.title: England vs. Czechia—Nations League: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4390g54he.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 5, 2026England sauntered to victory in the reverse fixture. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images (England), Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Czechia)England is brimming with confidence ahead of Tuesday’s return Nations League fixture against Czechia.

Thomas Tuchel’s Three Lions pulled off a stunning 7–0 demolition of Croatia at the weekend, which saw the fearsome forward quartet of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon run riot.

England has offered the perfect response to a frustrating 3–2 defeat to Spain in its opening match in Group 3 of League A. The demolition of Croatia was preceded by a convincing 2–0 win over 10-man Czechia on the road.

Pressure has certainly eased on Tuchel after the shocking late implosion to Argentina in the 2026 World Cup semifinal, and another triumph over Czechia, this time at Wembley, would certainly boost morale further.

Santi Denia’s reign has commenced with three successive defeats, although Czechia haven’t been blown away in any of those losses. That being said, a miracle would be required to claim a point or more from the upcoming clash in London.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
England has been in fine attacking form. / Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesIt’s unlikely that England will rack up another seven goals, but a handsome victory is still expected when Czechia comes to town.

There are 44 places between the two nations in the FIFA rankings—and for good reason. England boasts an arsenal of superstars who have flexed their creative muscles during the current break, while Czechia are technically limited and missing a talisman capable of propelling it to loftier heights.
England should put Denia’s side to the sword and entertain the home supporters inside Wembley.

Tuchel will make changes from the Croatia win. / FotMobTuchel will be without the impressive Alex Scott against Czechia. The Bournemouth midfielder suffered a quad injury on his first senior start against Croatia and will now be out of action for around six to eight weeks—meaning he will miss the November international break, too.
Nico O’Reilly is another who recently dropped out due to injury, joining the likes of Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Declan Rice and Marcus Rashford as withdrawals.

Rico Lewis has been added to the squad, but the versatile full back appears unlikely to start at Wembley. James Garner or Myles Lewis-Skelly are most likely to replace Scott in the midfield, joining Elliot Anderson in the double pivot.

Tuchel could rest some key members of his team, with Bellingham potentially making way for Morgan Rogers in the No. 10 position. Eberechi Eze could feature on the left wing in place of Gordon, while Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrad Branthwaite and Trevoh Chalobah might all come into the defense.
Harry Kane will lead the line once again, making a joint-record 125th appearance for the Three Lions.
England predicted lineup vs. Czechia (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Chalobah, Branthwaite, Hall; Anderson, Lewis-Skelly; Saka, Rogers, Eze; Kane.

Denia has been dealt another suspension blow. / FotMobWhile Pavel Šulc will return from his one-match ban picked up for a red card against England, Wolverhampton Wanderers defender Ladislav Krejčí is now suspended after being sent off against Spain last time out.
Tottenham Hotspur’s Antonín Kinský started in goal against La Roja and could earn another start in a familiar city, while Robin Hranáč will come back into the XI to replace Krejčí.
Michal Sadílek and Lukáš Červ should return in midfield, but Adam Karabec remains a doubt to feature with a knock and Vladimír Coufal could miss out through a knee issue.
Czechia predicted lineup vs. England (4-2-3-1): Kinský; Sácek, Chaloupek, Hranáč, Sláma; Sadílek, Červ; Radosta, Šulc, Lingr; Hložek.

ftbpro_01m4390gffn1.title: France vs. Belgium—Nations League: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4390gffn1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 4, 2026Les Bleus won the reverse fixture by a single goal. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images.Age-old rivals France and Belgium collide in the fourth round of UEFA Nations League fixtures in Saint-Denis on Monday.

Les Bleus currently lead the standings in Group 1 of League A after an unbeaten start to Zinédine Zidane’s reign. The 1–0 win over Türkiye in his dugout debut was followed by victory by the same scoreline against Belgium, although a first home match for the ex-Real Madrid manager then ended in a 1–1 draw with Italy.

The Red Devils are just one point behind their rivals as new coach Mark van Bommel makes an encouraging start on the touchline. The late loss to France was sandwiched in between convincing triumphs over Italy and Türkiye which have regalvanized the Belgians after a tumultuous World Cup campaign.

This will be the 80th meeting between the sides, with their first clash dating all the way back to 1904. Slightly less drama is projected than on that occasion, however, as the nations played out a thrilling 3–3 draw in Brussels.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Belgium will push France hard on Monday. / Alex Nicodim/NurPhoto/Getty Images.France might have been reliant on Michael Olise to snatch them an 88th-minute victory in the reverse fixture, but its triumph could have been more convincing if not for a wasteful performance in the final third.
Les Bleus produced more expected goals, shots and shots on target, as well as hitting the woodwork twice. They are clearly the stronger of the two sides.

The main issue for the Red Devils is the absence of Youri Tielemans and Kevin De Bruyne, who are suspended for the upcoming clash. That leaves a gaping hole in the Belgium midfield and ensures chances will be much harder to create.
France has already kept two clean sheets this international break. Perhaps a third is on its way against a weakened opponent.

France will be forced into at least one change. / FotMob.Zidane will have to reshuffle his defense after Dayot Upamecano was sent off against Italy. The center back is now suspended for the Belgium match, meaning the impressive Jérémy Jacquet will likely be partnered by Maxence Lacroix.
Pierre Kalulu has been used ahead of Jules Koundé at right back during the last two matches, while Adrien Truffert appears set to keep his starting place on the other side of the defense.
Eduardo Camavinga could come into the midfield for Lucas Da Cunha, but the same front three of Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Olise appears primed to torment the Belgian backline.
Of course, Kylian Mbappé remains sorely missed after picking up an injury in the opening match with Türkiye.
France predicted lineup vs. Belgium (4-3-3): Maignan; Kalulu, Jacquet, Lacroix, Truffert; Cherki, Camavinga, Rabiot; Olise, Dembélé, Doué.

A weakened midfield could cost Belgium. / FotMobAs mentioned, Belgium will have to cope without both Tielemans and De Bruyne. The latter was particularly effective against Türkiye, scoring twice before picking up a needless yellow card which means he’s suspended for the trip to France.
Roméo Lavia is likely to enter the team in their place, as should Nicolas Raskin. They will join Hans Vanaken in a three-man midfield.

Van Bommel has used Charles De Ketelaere and Mika Godts in each of his three starting lineups, but there will be a battle between Dodi Lukébakio and Diego Moreira for a place on the right-hand side of a front three.

Lammens will continue in goal after Thibaut Courtois made himself unavailable for the Nations League despite not being injured, while Maxim De Cuyper should come back into the back four to join Timothy Castagne, Nathan Ngoy and Brandon Mechele.
Belgium predicted lineup vs. France (4-3-3): Lammens; Castagne, Ngoy, Mechele, De Cuyper; Raskin, Lavia, Vanaken; Lukébakio, De Ketelaere, Godts.

ftbpro_01m439m045sp.title: Five Pieces of USMNT History Rewritten in Record-Breaking Mexico Victory
ftbpro_01m439m045sp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:50 AM EDTThe USMNT was on fine form against Mexico. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesHistory is written by the victors and the U.S. men’s national team put together a very flattering story of its triumph over Mexico on Saturday night. Yet, it could have been a completely different tale.

Rafael Márquez’s visitors were much the better team across the opening 25 minutes, stringing together some slick sequences of play against a U.S. midfield which could scarcely pick each other out of a lineup. Unfortunately for El Tri, it could not capitalize upon this dominance and crumbled after Julian Hall’s 28th-minute opener against the run of play.

That was the USMNT’s first shot on target of the match and Mexico set about handing Mauricio Pochettino’s side an ample number of opportunities to bolster its tally. Mateo Chávez’s brainless red card for a slap on Sebastian Berhalter summed up the implosion but, as Pochettino would argue, you have to accept the gift even if it is being forcefully offered to you.
What could have been a night which saw the burgeoning optimism of the USMNT’s new era punctured instead turned into a 3–0 thumping to savor. That’s at least how history will remember it.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mauricio Pochettino has enjoyed some strong post-World Cup form.  / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesPochettino accepted his expanded new contract as the face of U.S. Soccer for the next four years preaching about sweeping changes. Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie can attest that the Argentine coach was not bluffing, but some recurring themes have been retained.

Intensity is the identity that Pochettino has fostered throughout his coaching career. Whether that’s his side’s press or the look in his eye when he talks about the crate of lemons on his desk, there is little subdued about the USMNT manager. And so, Pochettino can take great satisfaction from the sustained record of spearing through the start of matches.

Hall’s opener ensured that the USMNT has now scored in the first half of 10 consecutive matches, a feat never before achieved in the program’s history. This run stretches back to the 3–2 friendly victory of Senegal in May and encompasses all five World Cup fixtures. Against Mexico, the U.S. managed to carry on scoring after the break.

Mexico is ranked 10th in the world by FIFA. / Chris Coduto/Getty ImagesOne of the sticks that has so often been used to beat Pochettino during his tenure in the States is his record against elite opposition. The former Tottenham Hotspur and Paris Saint-Germain coach had never previously overseen a win against Mexico or any nation ranked within FIFA’s top 10. Both those feats were toppled in one fell swoop on Saturday.

Remarkably, this triumph represented the USMNT’s first victory against any opposition considered to be among the world’s best since a friendly win over reigning world champion Germany in June 2015. It’s been 11 years crashing against that glass ceiling which finally shattered in Arizona this weekend.

As ever, tensions flared in a USMNT match. / Chris Coduto/Getty ImagesThe USMNT actually won the first ever clash between these two North American outfits back in 1934, but it would be another 46 years and 24 games before the Stars and Stripes could secure a second victory in this fixture.

The balance of this rivalry has been gradually addressed since the turn of the century, while this decade promises to be the USMNT’s most successful yet. Mexico has only beaten its neighbor twice in eight encounters since 2020, losing as many as six times. Only once before has the USMNT ever enjoyed a run of results as impressive as its current sequence.
Given that this latest result was achieved at the expense of Márquez, a player upheld by many U.S. fans as the chief villain of this rivalry in the modern era, the victory was even sweeter.
CAVAN SULLIVAN SCORES IN HIS FIRST USA-MEXICO GAME 😤He's now the USMNT's youngest ever goalscorer. pic.twitter.com/uV4i6g26hO

Before a ball had even been kicked, Cavan Sullivan had already made history as the youngest American to ever start against Mexico. He made sure to mark the occasion with another landmark, lobbing the helpless and hapless Raúl Rangel from 35 yards to become the USMNT’s youngest ever scorer.

“These are the moments you dream of when you’re a 3, 4, 5 or 6-year-old,” the 17-year-old breathlessly revealed postmatch. “I manifested this moment, not just these past couple of hours when I found out I was starting, but my whole life.”

Sullivan spent the afternoon in the buildup to his big moment visualizing his goal, closing his eyes and seeing himself wheel away to celebrate. When the actual moment came around in reality, he couldn’t even remember it.
“I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn’t hit the crossbar or go over,” teenager grinned. “I was getting nervous when it was in the air and then everything was a blur.”
updated the cover photo pic.twitter.com/lt60vDG4UI

Before Sullivan’s heroics, Hall carved out his own piece of history. The 18-year-old—another member of Pochettino’s international crèche—scored his third goal on his third appearance for his country, becoming just the third player in the history of the USMNT to achieve such a blistering start to his career after Eddie Johnson and Alexander Rae.

ftbpro_01m43ba9ep1s.title: Zlatan Ibrahimovic Clashes With Thierry Henry Over His 2026 Ballon d’Or Pick
ftbpro_01m43ba9ep1s.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath9:30 AM EDTZlatan Ibrahimović (left) and Thierry Henry don’t always see eye-to-eye. / Jean Catuffe/Getty ImagesWhile Thierry Henry didn’t even include him in his top two, Zlatan Ibrahimović deemed Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal to be the worthy winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or.
The 19-year-old superstar is among the frontrunners for what is widely considered to be soccer’s top individual prize, having shone for both Barcelona and Spain last season.
Yamal scored 25 goals and registered 20 assists in 57 matches for club and country in 2025–26, and lifted both the La Liga title and World Cup. He was also named La Liga Player of the Year.

The youngster, who came second in last year’s voting, has been campaigning ahead of the vote. Laying forth his case in a series of interviews last month. “There have been big stars in football, like Leo [Messi], Cristiano [Ronaldo], Diego [Maradona]... but no one had won so much so early,” he argued. “There was the instance of Pelé, but not more recently.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

One man clearly persuaded by Yamal is legendary former forward Ibrahimović, who named the teen phenom as his would-be pick. Asked a series of quick-fire questions by ESPN at the FC 27 launch in New York, the former Barcelona star replied “Yamal” when asked for his Ballon d’Or choice.

Henry, by contrast, plumped for Yamal’s Real Madrid rival. “It’s Kylian Mbappé,” Ibrahimović’s fellow Fox Sports pundit claimed earlier this month. “And yes, people will tell me that he didn’t win anything. I think it happened in history. I think some people need to do their research on that one.

“But for me, it’s Kylian. When you see what he has achieved individually ... Top goal scorer in the Champions League, top goal scorer in La Liga and also the World Cup. Michael Olise has the same thing in terms of assists.”

“I just wanted to explain that there are a lot of people that are candidates and they’re not like Mickey Mouse candidates, in all fairness,” Henry added. “But I will personally go with [Mbappé]. Michael Olise, close.”
Zlatan's picks for some of the biggest awards and league winners in Europe are spicy 👀🔥 pic.twitter.com/PC75L9skMQ
Yamal is currently ranked as the second favorite for the prize by most bookmakers, behind only Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane.
Kane lifted the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal in 2025–26 and scored a phenomenal 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country.
With his tally, the England captain became only the first player since Lionel Messi in 2011–12 to surpass the 70-goal mark in a single season.

Next on most of the favorites lists is Real Madrid and France striker Mbappé, the man who became the top scorer in World Cup history this summer, followed by the likes of Rodri (Barcelona/Spain), Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (Paris Saint-Germain/Georgia) and Lionel Messi (Inter Miami/Argentina).
Were 19-year-old Yamal to win the award he would become the youngest ever Ballon d’Or winner—surpassing the previous youngest player, Ronaldo Nazario, who won in 1997 and the age of 21.

The Ballon d’Or will likely have a new winner this year. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThe Ballon d’Or ceremony, organized by France Football magazine, has been held at the Théâtre du Châtelet in Paris since 2019, but a change of venue has been confirmed ahead of the 2026 festivities.

For the first time ever, the U.K.’s iconic London Palladium will host the ceremony on Oct. 26, a decision made to honor inaugural Ballon d’Or winner Stanley Matthews, one of only four Englishmen to have scooped the prize, 70 years on from the first ever award.

ftbpro_01m43d5jpdv8.title: Italy vs. Turkiye—Nations League: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m43d5jpdv8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 4, 2026The Azzurri were victorious when the sides clashed last week. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Italy), Aytac Unal/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images (Türkiye)Italy finishes off an extended three-week international break by hosting Türkiye in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

After missing out on yet another World Cup and enduring a chaotic spell over the summer, the Azzurri turned back to Euro 2020-winning manager Roberto Mancini in a bid to steady the ship. While performances have not been perfect upon the 61-year-old’s return, they did thrash Türkiye 4–1 to put defeat to Belgium behind them, after which they managed a draw at France.

Türkiye was involved in last summer’s World Cup, but might have well have stayed at home after a dismal group stage campaign yielded an early exit. Things have hardly improved for the under-fire Vincenzo Montella since, with three successive defeats in the Nations League thus far.

The upcoming encounter will be the 15th time Italy and Türkiye have locked horns on the international stage, and it’s the former who have been utterly dominant—dating all the way back to their first duel in 1962. The Azzurri have never lost this fixture, with 10 wins and four draws to their name previously.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Italy are strong favorite ahead of the clash in Bologna. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesItaly might not need to be at its best to triumph in Bologna. Türkiye has been dreadful in the Nations League, suffering three straight losses and conceding eight goals as it struggles without the absent duo of Kenan Yıldız and Hakan Çalhanoğlu. Even Real Madrid gem Arda Güler has been unable to spare its blushes.

The Azzurri, meanwhile, are on the up after two games unbeaten, which kicked off with a rousing win over Türkiye. Italy blew its host out of the water after racing into a three-goal first-half lead and it will expect to notch a couple more goals at the Stadio Renato Dall’Ara.

Italy is in confident mood.  / FotMobMancini could make several alterations to the team which drew with France, especially considering the quick turnaround between fixtures. However, the core of the side should remain unchanged.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will likely continue between the posts, while Alessandro Bastoni will feature in the heart of defense after scoring in the last two matches. The Premier League pairing of Michael Kayode and Riccardo Calafiori should start in the fullback positions.
Sandro Tonali and Davide Frattesi could be joined by the returning Nicolò Barella in midfield, while Gianluca Mancini could replace Giorgio Scalvini in the defense.
The Esposito brothers, Pio and Sebastiano, should once again start alongside Moise Kean in attack.
Italy predicted lineup vs. Türkiye (4-3-3): Donnarumma; Kayode, Mancini, Bastoni, Calafiori; Frattesi, Tonali, Barella; S. Esposito, P. Esposito, Kean.

Türkiye will be forced into attacking changes. / FotMobTürkiye need to make significant improvements from recent matches, but Montella will be without the services of his most influential performer, Güler, through suspension. The Real Madrid star picked up his second Nations League booking in the defeat to Belgium last time out.

Barış Yılmaz is also absent through suspension, meaning Montella will be forced to field a significantly weakened forward line. Deniz Gül should come into the team to start up top, potentially being flanked by Kerem Aktürkoğlu and Yunus Akgün.
Salih Özcan could come back into the midfield to provide Türkiye’s defense with greater protection.
Türkiye predicted lineup vs. Italy (4-3-3): Çakır; Çelik, Demiral, Bardakcı, Kadıoğlu; Elmaz, Özcan, Yüksek; Akgün, Gül, Aktürkoğlu.

ftbpro_01m43dc85eep.title: Endrick’s Potential Destinations for Real Madrid January Exit—Ranked
ftbpro_01m43dc85eep.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 PM EDTEndrick is likely to have options this January. / Albert Perez/Getty Images)“The problem for Brazilian boys is that they do not improve because they do not play,” Carlo Ancelotti lamented to reporters during the international break.

“It is happening to Endrick, but also to other talents such as Estêvão: they go to Europe at 18 or 19, they arrive at big clubs and do not find space. Without playing they cannot progress. We have very promising young players and we have to follow their development.”
Endrick, 20, was meant to be the poster boy for Brazil’s next generation, but is instead becoming a warning to his contemporaries about the dangers of moving abroad too soon.

Since joining Real Madrid for big money in the summer of 2024, Endrick has struggled to make an impact on the first team, while his limited game time has threatened to stunt his progress from wonderkid to top talent.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

A productive spring out on loan at Lyon in the second half of 2025–26 showed that the potential is still there, but the arrival of new signings Yan Diomande and Carlos Espí along with new manager José Mourinho have pushed Endrick further out of the picture at Madrid—where he has made just one substitute appearance so far this season.
Madrid resisted loaning the young forward out this summer, but a January transfer now appears inevitable with several clubs reportedly interested in a loan deal.

Endrick impressed in France. / Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesEndrick’s half-season spell in Ligue 1 was a success, with the forward scoring eight times and assisting eight in 21 matches for Lyon.He also learned a new position, thriving out on wide on the right—a role he was initially expected to reprise for Madrid this term, before the blockbuster arrival of Diomande and unstoppable form of Arda Güler blew that plan to smithereens. A return to Lyon for another six months would not be the worst idea, though Endrick would be required to fight for minutes with in-form Ernest Nuamah and Loïs Openda.

Mikel Oyarzabal has yet to score this season. /  Ivan Terron/Europa Press/Getty ImagesReal Sociedad were among the Spanish clubs mooted as a possible destination for Endrick over the summer and could well be in the picture for a January move.Of all of La Liga’s current top 10, only Athletic Club have scored fewer than La Real’s nine goals this season, and it’s clear Pellegrino Matarazzo’s team could use another outlet with Mikel Oyarzabal struggling for form post-World Cup.

Endrick at Villa could be mutually beneficial. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesHaving had their roster decimated over the summer, Aston Villa have endured a difficult start to 2026–27, with their first win of the campaign coming just prior to the international break.Given Unai Emery’s record and experience, there is a sense that Villa will turn things around and both Nicolas Jackson and Brian Madjo are exciting options in attack.Villa were another club rumored to have made enquires over the summer, and Endrick could add a boost to the flanks for the run-in, while allowing John McGinn to reprise a more natural role in the center. There are also few better coaches to learn under than Emery, and no place better to boost your price tag than the Premier League.

Liverpool lack right-sided options. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesLiverpool, famously, signed two predominantly left wingers this summer but have no natural option on the right—besides Federico Chiesa.Following in the footsteps of Mohamed Salah would be a tall order for Endrick, but given the dearth of options at Anfield, the young Brazilian would surely be welcomed with open arms by the fans on at least a short-term basis.With Alexander Isak’s fitness likely needing to be carefully managed, the 20-year-old could also provide a useful rotation option at center forward, especially while Hugo Ekitiké gets back up to speed following long-term injury.

Donyell Malen is in red-hot form for Roma. /  Silvia Lore/Getty ImagesGazzetta Dello Sport claims that Roma have made contact with Endrick’s representatives and remain keen on a deal.Gian Piero Gasperini’s team have started the 2026–27 well with Donyell Malen on fire in attack.However, a lack of attacking depth gives Endrick room to make a mark on a thriving team and rebuild his reputation at a historic European club. Roma will have the chance to speak with Real Madrid about their transfer target during their Champions League meeting on Oct. 14 at the Olimpico.

Omari Hutchinson has made just two appearances for Milan this season. / Giuseppe Cottini/AC Milan/Getty ImagesThe same report claims AC Milan are also monitoring Endrick ahead of January.The seven-time European Cup winners were warned off making a move in the summer and instead signed Omari Hutchinson on loan from Nottingham Forest—though the former England U-21 star has featured little so far.Manager Ruben Amorim typically prefers a 3-4-2-1 formation, meaning Endrick would likely have to slot in as one of the two No. 10s—a somewhat new position for the forward. A major advantage for Milan in any transfer race is the Italian club’s strong relationship with Roc Nation, the agency which manages Endrick.

ftbpro_01m43j83bjfk.title: ‘This Is Why Everyone Hates America’—Jesse Marsch Puts USMNT on Blast
ftbpro_01m43j83bjfk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:30 AM EDTJesse Marsch is never one to pull his punches. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesCanada’s American manager Jesse Marsch once again let his emphatic emotions be known when discussing the country of his birth, describing the perceived entitlement behind the Folarin Balogun World Cup controversy as a prime example of “why everyone around the world hates America.”

Marsch had been tipped to take over the U.S. men’s national team (USMNT), which he twice represented as a player, before Mauricio Pochettino was surprisingly appointed in 2024. The former Leeds United boss would quickly pivot to the top job in Canada, leading his adopted nation to its best ever performance at a men’s World Cup over the summer.

The USMNT would exit the competition staged across North America in the same round of 16 as Canada, although under wildly contrasting circumstances. While Marsch’s side was simply beaten by the better team in a 3–0 reverse to Morocco, the U.S.’s capitulation at the hands of Belgium was played to a backdrop of febrile controversy thanks to Balogun’s inclusion.

An unprecedented FIFA ruling, aided by a phone call from U.S. President Donald Trump, saw Balogun’s red card ban suspended for reasons which still remain unclear. The world united in its disgust at the decision, while Belgium used it as extra motivation ahead of a 4–1 pummeling. Marsch argued that this was just one example of a national trait which, to use his words, “infuriates the rest of the world.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

It’s long been forgotten, but Folarin Balogun did step on Tarik Muharemovic’s Achilles. / Michael Steele/Getty Images“What I feel when the Balogun ruling happens is that would never happen in any other country in the world,” Marsch told The Guardian, “and this is why everyone around the world hates America.”

“We, as Americans, have been inundated with propaganda since we were young,” the former midfielder from Wisconsin claimed. “We’re the No. 1 country in the world, we deserve everything, we dominate everything, No. 1 in every aspect of life. This is what we’ve been told.

“So, when things happen and we don’t feel like we’re in control of it ... we feel like we deserve to be treated differently because we’re Americans. That is one of the things that infuriates the rest of the world about Americans. And Americans don’t know that if they don’t ever leave the country.”

Marsch spent his college and senior playing career exclusively in the U.S. before heading abroad as a manager. Club jobs in Canada, Austria, Germany and England has provided the ex-USMNT assistant coach with a global, and often unflattering, view of his home nation.
“The U.S. had had a good World Cup, was doing well,” he reflected back to that Balogun decision. “All that switched in one moment.”

The leaders of Canada and England are both Everton fans. / Paul Cooper/WPA Pool/Getty ImagesMarsch has rarely hidden his disdain for President Trump, taking particular issue with his branding of Canada as the “51st state.” The Canucks boss would appear to be far fonder of Mark Carney, Trump’s Canadian counterpart, with his support of a middling Premier League club working in his favor.
“I heard you’re an Everton fan?” Marsch asked Carney when they first met. In a sharp retort to the President’s confirmation of that fact, he shot back: “I’m sorry about that.”
“Why does everybody say that?” Marsch recalled Carney responding. “Everybody has to pick their team and stick by them.”
The former U.S. international “appreciated” that loyalty. “There’s something so genuine [about] that,” he explained. “Could a President of the U.S. ever be an Everton fan? No chance.”

In a further comparison of Carney and the U.S. heads of state who Marsch has met, he revealed: “Carney, compared to all of them, the closest would be [Barack] Obama. A real air of intelligence, but a real air of being a regular guy. I think that that’s perfect for this country and this moment.” Obama, however, doesn’t have the added bonus of cheering on the Toffees.

ftbpro_01m43jphx6fj.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s 7 Most Spectacular Tantrums for Club and Country—Ranked
ftbpro_01m43jphx6fj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:00 PM EDTHe’s had it up to here. /  Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesCristiano Ronaldo will not go gently into that good night. That much is clear.

The 41-year-old superstar’s walkout from the Portugal national team is just the latest example of his absolute refusal to be anything other than the main character in any given situation, with the tail-end of his career pockmarked by a series of increasingly petty (yet entertaining) grievances, sideshows and outbursts.

When Ronaldo does finally hit 1,000 career goals and siuuuuus off into the sunset—shirtless and abs-tensed—we will of course remember the trophies, the leaps, the moments of wonder... But we will also remember the tantrums, for they too are a big part of his gift to soccer.

Nothing to siuuu here. /  pedja milosavljevic/AFP/Getty ImagesRonaldo thought he’d won a tight World Cup qualifier against Serbia deep in stoppage time when he nipped in to finish past the keeper, only for defender Stefan Mitrović to clear the ball out from (clearly) behind the goal line.With no VAR to step in, the referee waved play on much to Ronaldo’s fury. The Portugal captain ended up throwing his armband to the ground after being booked for dissent—a move which raised eyebrows in his homeland.He later attempted to explain his actions on social media posting: “There are difficult times to deal with, especially when we feel that an entire nation is being harmed.”U O.K. hun?

The armband takes the brunt again. / Jasper Juinen/Getty ImagesThat was not the first time the armband had felt the full force of Ronaldo’s ire.Back in a 2010 friendly against neighbors Spain, the then-Real Madrid superstar twisted and wriggled his way through the defense and lifted the ball over keeper Iker Casillas for one of the all-time great international goals... Or, it would have been if Nani had not dived in to head the ball over the line from an offside position.The goal was correctly ruled out and Ronaldo did a weird little dance on the spot before making his armband get up close and personal with the Lisbon grass.Portugal ended up winning 4–0 and Nani sheepishly told reporters he didn’t mean to do it and he was very, very sorry, but neither fact was likely to have shortened Ronaldo’s sulk.

“What are you doing here?” / Angel Martinez/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesWhat we’re learning is that Ronaldo really does not like anyone to get in the way of his goals.Future Fulham manager Álvaro Arbeloa found this out during a routine win over Almería in the latter stages of the 2014–15 season when the defender poked home a cross into the box, nudging in front of Instagram’s most followed man, who had been poised at the back post to add to his own goal tally.As the rest of the Real Madrid players celebrated the novelty of an Arbeloa goal, Ronaldo hammered the ball back into the net angrily with a face like thunder.“I’m not upset about Cristiano’s gesture,” Arbeloa lied after the game.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Tackling the screen-time epidemic, one fan at a time. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesRonaldo’s Manchester United return in 2021 was not quite the glorious homecoming many had hoped it would be.The forward was still banging in goals during the the 2021–22 season, but couldn’t bring United any closer to a trophy, while tensions on and off the field bubbled. A frustrating 1–0 defeat away at Goodison Park proved too much for Ronaldo, who was caught on camera swiping a phone out of a young fan’s hands as he walked down the tunnel after the final whistle.He later received a two-match ban for the incident and was even cautioned by the police. Naughty naughty.

Benched. / Rico Brouwer/Soccrates/Getty ImagesPerhaps the point it all changed for Ronaldo.Up until the 2022 World Cup, you could legitimately make the case that Ronaldo was still one of the very best strikers around and deserved his place in the Portugal lineup on merit. Once the tournament in Qatar got going... Well, it was much harder.The then-37-year-old scored just once (from the penalty spot) in the group stages and was subbed by manager Fernando Santos in a 2–1 defeat to South Korea—an indignity he took with a typical lack of grace and stoicism.Ronaldo huffed, puffed and hung his head on the sidelines, prompting Santos to say of his captain’s conduct postmatch “I didn’t like it, not at all. I didn’t like it.”Santos then benched Ronaldo for the round of 16 clash with Switzerland, with replacement striker Gonçalo Ramos scoring a hat trick. Oops.

See ya never. / Liselotte Sabroe / Ritzau Scanpix/AFP/Getty ImagesThe latest in the Ronaldo catalogue of tantrums is a biggie.After being left on the bench (shock horror) by manager Jorge Jesus for a Nations League win over Norway, the 41-year-old went nuclear.After clear-the-air talks with the Portugal FA that clearly did not clear any air, Ronaldo exited the national team camp, posting on his socials: “In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure.”Portugal went on to beat Denmark 4–2 in their next match without Ronaldo on the roster and Jesus has since refused to back down.Reports suggest Ronaldo may have already played his final match for the national team—an ignominious end for one of soccer’s greats.

It all fell apart at United the second time around. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesThe GOAT of Ronaldo’s grumps.With relations increasingly tense with new manager Erik ten Hag and goals ever more scarce, Ronaldo decided he’d had enough of it all at some point roughly midway through United’s 2-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.The five-time Ballon d’Or winner reportedly left Old Trafford before the match was done, effectively calling time on his time at the club.A couple of weeks later an explosive interview with chief sycophant Piers Morgan dropped, during which Ronaldo lashed out at Ten Hag and the United hierarchy, while Wayne Rooney’s looks also caught strays for some reason.Morgan pushed back hard of course, telling Ronaldo at one point: "I know about your aftershave, I use it, it’s very successful, I have to say. People say ‘Ooh, you smell like Cristiano.’”

ftbpro_01m43n44r0v3.title: ‘Unbelievable’—Mauricio Pochettino Breaks His Own Rule With Cavan Sullivan
ftbpro_01m43n44r0v3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:30 AM EDTCavan Sullivan had a night to remember on Saturday. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesIt was telling that Mauricio Pochettino had to be reminded to comment on Cavan Sullivan’s sensational 35-yard lob after an effusive outburst of praise for the teenager’s overall performance against Mexico. Having rattled through all his tenacious technical qualities, the goal that made him the youngest scorer in U.S. men’s national team history had slipped Pochettino’s mind.
That the USMNT manager was willing to spend any time discussing an individual player is a sign of how high Sullivan already sits in Pochettino’s estimations.

Back in the spacious press room at SoFi Stadium after the USMNT’s emphatic World Cup opener against Paraguay this summer, once the whirr of an air conditioning unit had been silenced at his request, Pochettino shut down every line of questioning into any individual performance. It was not a night to hail Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun or Tim Ream. The team (and the fans) earned the praise of a manager constantly wary of dishing out too many accolades.
Sullivan, it would appear, is an exception to that rule.

“Talented,” “tremendous,” “unbelievable” were some of the superlatives which Pochettino used to hail the 17-year-old’s showing in Saturday’s historic 3–0 victory over Mexico. Sullivan is being treated differently because he is doing things differently to every other U.S. star to cross paths with Pochettino.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
To be the future you must rewrite history. pic.twitter.com/MID0hojIEy

“He’s a fighter. He’s a warrior,” Pochettino gushed when uncharacteristically opening up about the performance of Sullivan. “It’s difficult to find this type of player with tremendous quality with the ball, in possession, and then [he enjoys] when he needs to chase people and recover the ball. That is my impression after [two] weeks. And that is unbelievable to have a player like this.”
It’s that quality of “balance,” that shared intensity when he is attacking or defending, which has so endeared Sullivan to Pochettino.

The Philadelphia Union phenom earned the chance to humiliate Raúl Rangel with a long-range lob by pressing the Mexican goalkeeper. Pochettino and his coaching staff had actually been imploring Sullivan to keep on charging toward the wandering custodian shortly before his moment of brilliance. The forward instinctively delayed his dart to sucker Rangel into a stray pass which he would ruthlessly punish.

“He’s relentless in the way that he presses, his counter-pressing, all those things,” the USMNT’s new captain Tyler Adams beamed postmatch. Sullivan managed to rack up as many defensive contributions against Mexico as Adams, the team’s ballast at the base of midfield, despite playing 25 fewer minutes. A fact which won’t have passed Pochettino by.
USMNT Player Ratings vs. Mexico—Two Stars Are Born on Dream Night. dark. Next. USMNT ratings Mexico October 2026

Cavan Sullivan scored the USMNT’s second goal against Mexico on Saturday. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesPochettino was not only besotted by Sullivan’s behavior on the pitch. “I liked what he said after the game, ‘The most important [thing] was the result.’ [He’s] learning every day,” the U.S. boss beamed, “that is the good thing.”

Sullivan may have only turned 17 on Monday but he is a mature character with a feverish work ethic and clear idea about his career. This is a kid who does the dishes and goes to training rather than partying—he celebrated his recent birthday in the U.S. camp with a small cake.

That dedication has been apparent throughout his embryonic career. In preparation for a youth tournament in Spain, the then-13-year-old took a proactive approach to combating jet lag by progressively waking up half an hour earlier each day.
The occasion of his first senior international goal almost overwhelmed Pochettino’s new star pupil, but not quite. “If it wasn’t so hype,” Sullivan smiled, “I think I would’ve probably shed a tear.”
