ftbpro_01m46a5hrj9g.title: Why End of Wrexham Women’s Unbeaten Run Could Actually Be a Good Thing
ftbpro_01m46a5hrj9g.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay1:30 PM EDTWrexham Women are the reigning champions of the Welsh Adran Premier. / Wrexham AFCWrexham Women’s unbeaten start to the new Adran Premier season came to an end at the weekend as they suffered a dramatic 3–2 defeat at home to The New Saints.
Wrexham fought back from two goals down to level the scores in stoppage time, only for Fiona Barry to score a spectacular winner in the final seconds and secure a memorable away win for the visitors.

The result brought Wrexham’s unbeaten start to the season to an end, while TNS’s perfect record continued as they moved top of the table with five wins from their opening five matches. Jenny Sugarman was quick to stress at fulltime that the title is not decided after five games, while club captain Jodie Bartle reiterated that the season is a “marathon, not a sprint.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Wrexham saw their flawless start to the league season end dramatically. / Wrexham AFCWrexham remain favorites to win the league title they claimed for the first time in March, but this time it would appear TNS, rather than Cardiff City, are their main rivals for the accolade. For a top flight which only has eight teams, that can only be a good thing for the development of the domestic game, even if it is tough for Wrexham to take right now.

“When the season started this year, there was just more expectation of Wrexham,” former Wrexham defender and current pundit Mia Roberts told Sports Illustrated. “Especially after what they did in the Champions League as well over the summer, and the signings they've made. Wrexham were by far and away the favorites to not only win the league, but probably both cup competitions as well.”

Jenny Sugarman’s side have already been playing competitive matches for three months, since their debut European campaign ended at the hands of Latvian side Riga FC in the Women’s Champions League qualifying second round. There was also extensive investment in the squad over the summer, with a host of new recruits arriving.

One of those signings, Natasha Thomas, thought she had rescued a precious point against TNS with her seventh league goal of the season, while Wrexham also added former Manchester City midfielder Millie Davies to their squad last month.
Wrexham hope those additions will help them go a step further in Europe next season, but that will only happen if they manage to win the Adran Premier again. It is far easier said than done.
It's a marathon, not a sprint.We will see you all next week down in Swansea, Cochion 🫶🔴⚪️ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/olw7THU6kj

Roberts added: “TNS have proven that they’re going to be right with us, and that’s what we want to see. I think Cardiff have certainly dropped off, which you would expect after the manager Iain Darbyshire moved on over the summer.

“Swansea, too. I have to say I was really impressed with Swansea. They’re at a new ground, and they’re also building something really good there under Yzzy Taylor. I think it would be great for Wrexham to run away with this league, but equally, you want to see that competitiveness. The 7–0, 8–1 wins week in, week out—who are they really benefiting?

“Obviously, it’s great that we’d be winning by those sorts of margins, and we have beaten teams by those margins already this season. There’s that bigger picture in terms of the Welsh women’s game. I think it’s going to be a real race.”
Wrexham Women were backed by a bumper crowd of roughly 700 fans at The Rock over the weekend, with the Red Dragons the first women’s team in the Welsh leagues to outright own their own stadium.

The foundations are in place for another incredible season, and Roberts believes the experience of already winning the league once could make all the difference when the campaign reaches its conclusion.

She added: “That squad that Jenny has at her disposal is arguably the strongest we’ve seen in the Welsh domestic game. I look at it and you see the likes of, obviously, Katie Barker and what she’s already done. Natasha Thomas coming in, formerly Ipswich’s leading goalscorer, Lydia Sallaway. These players have got such great records, not only now in a Wrexham shirt, but also previously.

“With that double trophy experience from last year, if TNS are the ones, if it does become a bit of a two-horse race, I think that goes in Wrexham’s favor massively because they’ve been there and done it. Whereas TNS haven't had that recency in the league. So maybe that’s the difference.
“I hope it’s exciting. I hope it goes down to the wire, and I hope it goes Wrexham’s way.”

ftbpro_01m46asefrx2.title: Mexico vs. Chile—International Friendly: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m46asefrx2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 5, 2026El Tri is obliged to defeat an inferior Chile side.  / Visionhaus/Getty Images  Mexico hosts Chile at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Tuesday night, desperately seeking its first win of the Rafa Márquez era.

The fond memories of Mexico’s strong 2026 World Cup campaign were swiftly washed away over the weekend in an embarrassing 3–0 defeat to the USMNT. El Tri was demolished by its biggest rival in the second half in what was far and away the worst Mexico performance of the past year.

The heat is now firmly placed on Márquez just three games into his tenure, as critics were deafening following Saturday’s debacle. With no victories through his first three games in charge, Márquez’s men must deliver a convincing performance against Chile to ease the rapidly building tension surrounding El Tri and its new manager.

Chile is a significantly weaker side than the USMNT. Nicolás Cordova’s side is in a period of reconstruction and has lost its opening two games of the window against the other two 2026 World Cup co-hosts.
In their first meeting since 2021, Mexico must answer the call and beat Chile to end a subpar September-October international window on a high.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Rafa Márquez needs a win to ease the pressure on his shoulders.  / Chris Coduto/Getty Images Mexico’s form has nosedived since the start of the fall window. After a strong showing against Colombia, El Tri was underwhelming against Peru and then dreadful against the USMNT, with multiple comical errors making an already poor performance exponentially worse.

Results usually shouldn’t be the main objective of international friendlies, but the match against Chile is as close to a must-win game as a friendly can be for Márquez. El Tri is a superior side than its South American foes, so failing to beat an inferior team would only further sour the mood around Márquez.

Márquez has almost completely rotated his XI’s through the first three games of his tenure. Significant changes are expected again, but some key players could keep their place in the lineup to go all-out for victory.

Rafa Márquez will make a number of changes as he continues to assess his alternatives.  / FotMob Mexico will be without the suspended Mateo Chávez and the injured duo of Hirving Lozano and Gilberto Mora, with the trio expected to leave El Tri’s camp before Tuesday’s clash.

Jesús Gallardo and Jorge Sánchez should keep their place in the XI as the fullback pairing, and Erik Lira could also get the nod again in midfield. With the attack misfiring, Roberto Alvarado could also keep his place, given he is El Tri’s chief creator at the moment.

Athletic Club goakeeper Álex Padilla is poised to make his senior international debut against Chile. Everardo López and Víctor Guzmán have established themselves as the backup center back partnership and should get the nod after getting the night off on Saturday,

Exciting 19-year-old talent Hugo Camberos could make his first start for Mexico on the left wing. Finally, Armando González will lead the line hoping to finally translate his club level to the national team.
Mexico predicted lineup vs. Chile (4-3-3): Padilla; Sánchez, Guzmán, López, Gallardo; Vargas, Lira, Fidalgo; Alvarado, González, Camberos.

Nico Córdova’s is integrating a crop of young talents. / FotMob Chile will be boosted by the return of captain Gabriel Suazo and Lucas Cepeda, who both missed the clash against the USMNT last time out while serving a suspension.
Córdova has settled for the Colo Colo center back duo of Iván Román and Jonathan Villagra, while Francisco Salinas could make his first start of the window at right back.
In midfield 21-year-old Agustín Arce could make his first start of the window, with the talented Universidad de Chile playmaker trying to solidify his place in Córdova’s squad.
Up front, Crystal Palace winger Darío Osorio is Chile’s most dangerous player and English Championship journeyman Ben Brereton will spearhead the attack.
Chile predicted lineup vs. Mexico (4-3-3): Vigouroux; Salinas, Villagra, Román, Suazo; Loyola, Pizarro, Arce; Cepeda, Brereton, Osorio.

ftbpro_01m46d3dw90d.title: Premier League Clubs Dominate Full List of 2026 Golden Boy Nominees
ftbpro_01m46d3dw90d.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom2:05 PM EDTIt’s an illustrious pool of Golden Boy nominees this year. / PATRIK STOLLARZ/AFP/Getty ImagesAlmost one-third of this year’s 25 Golden Boy nominees for the best U-21 male player on the planet ply their trade in the Premier League.
While Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City all boast burgeoning young stars, it is the data-driven duo of Bournemouth and Brighton & Hove Albion who share four of the nominees between them.

Beyond the Premier League borders, Barcelona have an unrivaled three nominees within their own ranks—although Lamine Yamal is not one of them. While the World Cup winner’s focus will be on the adult version of this award, the Ballon d’Or, his compatriot and clubmate Pau Cubarsí is the favorite to claim the baby brother iteration at the ceremony in November.

Pau Cubarsí was voted the best young player of the 2026 World Cup. / Alex Pantling/FIFA/Getty ImagesPau Cubarsí (Barcelona)Ayyoub Bouaddi (Manchester City)Warren Zaïre-Emery (Paris Saint-Germain)Yan Diomande (Real Madrid)Luka Vuškovic (Brighton)Victor Froholdt (Porto)Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal)Rayan (Bournemouth)Jorrel Hato (Chelsea)Lennart Karl (Bayern Munich)Estêvão (Chelsea)Endrick (Real Madrid)Junior Kroupi (Bournemouth)Gianluca Prestianni (Benfica)Konstantinos Karetsas (Borussia Dortmund)Saïd El Mala (FC Köln)Jon Martín (Real Sociedad)Marc Bernal (Barcelona)Kerim Alajbegović (Juventus)Finn Jeltsch (Stuttgart)The top 20 in the Golden Boy award are decided by the organizer’s partner Transfermarkt. The soccer statistics website has progressively updated a list of the best players on the planet across the previous 12 months through a data-led methodology to spew out a shortlist.

The final snapshot was taken at the start of October and included a glut of intriguing youngsters. Stuttgart’s Finn Jeltsch, the darling of the transfer rumormill, is joined by fellow gossip column staples Endrick, Junior Kroupi and Jon Martín.

The World Cup boosted the profile of several nominees. Kerim Alajbegović’s unprecedented run to the knockouts with Bosnia and Herzegovina didn’t hurt, while the Ivorian Yan Diomande and Morocco gem Ayyoub Bouaddi all shone this summer. They all also managed to secure lucrative transfers to some of Europe’s elite, which represents a more tangible reward than the Golden Boy trophy.

Gianluca Prestianni undoubtedly represents the most intriguing nominee. The Benfica forward reached a global audience for his alleged racial abuse of Vinícius Júnior in a Champions League tie against Real Madrid. Prestianni’s argument, which UEFA accepted, was that he had actually used a homophobic slur.
On top of the top 20, there are five additional slots awarded to “wild cards” selected by a shadowy panel to complete the nominees.

The Golden Boy award has been dished out since 2003. / Richard Sellers/EMPICS/Getty ImagesThis award, which was originally launched by the Italian paper Tuttosport, has undergone many various guises. The current iteration takes on a similar system to its Ballon d’Or counterpart, with the fan say going to journalists.
A total of 50 different reporters from across Europe will be polled to decided who gets to keep the imaginatively named “Absolute Best award.”

There is a separate award dished out by an online vote known as the Golden Boy Fan Web Award. Intriguingly, Olympiacos midfielder Christos Mouzakitis is the defending champion of a prize previously claimed by the likes of Kenan Yıldız and Jude Bellingham.

ftbpro_01m46jt1qr1p.title: USMNT Star Julian Hall in Elite Company of Pele After Record-Setting Victory
ftbpro_01m46jt1qr1p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely4:30 PM EDTJulian Hall (left) has stunned in his debut camp with the USMNT. / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Julian Hall); Evening Standard/Hulton Archive/Getty Images (Pelé)By now, you’ve heard of Julian Hall. The 18-year-old sensation for the U.S. men’s national team, a true striker in every since of the word.

He’s been at the forefront of the Stars and Stripes’ success this fall, a key reason for the squad’s three-consecutive victories to kick off a post-World Cup era of dominance. Due to his latest heroics in the 3–0 thumping of bitter foe Mexico, Hall now joins the elite company of Brazilian soccer legend Pelé.

The teenager opened scoring in the Concacaf rivalry match with a 28th-minute blast, preying on the shaky hands of Mexican goalkeeper Raúl Rangel for an emphatic rebound. It signified his third-consecutive goal, scoring one each in his first three caps for the senior squad.

Hall became just the third player in USMNT history to score in each of his first three appearances and the first in over 20 years. More significantly though, he became the youngest player since a 16-year-old Pelé (nearly 50 years ago) to achieve such a feat.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Pele is the most legendary players in Brazil’s history. / Pictorial Parade/Archive Photos/Getty ImagesBack in 1957, Brazil may have lost 2–1 to Argentina at Maracaña Stadium, but a teenaged Pelé (16 years, eight months) stepped onto the pitch in canary yellow for the very first time and scored his first international goal. Thanks to that 76th-minute finish under the hot July sun, he remains the nation’s youngest goalscorer to this day.

Pelé added his second international goal just three days later against Argentina, the second and final match of the 1957 Roca Cup, the two-legged tournament between the South American foes. His 20th-minute finish guided the Seleção to an eventual 2–0 win.

The young phenom didn’t return to the pitch for Brazil until the following May for a friendly against Paraguay, yet he found the back of the net once again. He had an 81st-minute tap-in to lift his side to a 5–1 victory back at the hallowed Maracaña Stadium.

Those three goals ignited Pelé’s prolific career with Brazil. The famed soccer icon ended his international career with 77 goals between 1957 and 1971, the second-most goals behind Neymar (80) for Brazil. Yet while Pelé needed just 92 appearances to achieve such a feat, Neymar needed 125.

Hall is already making a name for himself. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesThe blistering start to Pelé’s career was quickly followed by his dominance at the 1958 World Cup in in Sweden, the first of a record-three (1962, 1970) he would go on to win for Brazil. Then 17, Pelé scored six goals that summer: the game-winner against Wales in the quarterfinals, a hat-trick against France in the second half of the semifinals and two goals against Sweden in the World Cup final. His awe-inspiring performances earned him global fame and a spotlight that never faded.

The USMNT and manager Mauricio Pochettino will certainly hope so, although Hall won’t be granted the opportunity to dazzle on soccer’s most prestigious stage until the 2030 World Cup, at which point he will 22 years old.
THREE GAMES. THREE GOALS. JULIAN HALL.#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/IPGeTrZ7wR

Pochettino’s clear intention is that Hall, among the other top young prospects, will be completely acclimated to competing at the senior international level by 2030 and, thus, will be in a position to bring the USMNT to heights never before reached at the sport’s premier tournament.

Coupled with consistent development from the Argentine boss over the next four years, the inevitable move to European soccer will bring Hall’s game to the next level. The New York City-native currently plays for New York Red Bulls, where he has enjoyed a breakout MLS campaign with 10 goals and three assists this season. Although the Homegrown recently signed a new contract through the 2029–30 season, there is no doubt that European clubs will be probing for a transfer before then.

Even if he doesn’t reach the legendary status of Pelé—very few have—Hall is nonetheless on track to become a rare and deeply influential gem for the American side. This fall, he has already become the youngest player in USMNT history to score in back-to-back matches and just the second player in the last decade to score in three-consecutive games (Malik Tillman). The latter accomplishment is one that U.S. Soccer poster boy Christian Pulisic has attempted and failed throughout his entire international career. Meanwhile, Hall did it on his very first try.
There is no telling the heights Hall will reach, making the USMNT’s future more exciting than ever before.

ftbpro_01m46qaz055n.title: ‘Barbecue’—Emiliano Martinez Reveals Argentina’s Plan for Lionel Messi’s Farewell
ftbpro_01m46qaz055n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:30 PM EDTEmiliano Martínez wants Lionel Messi to enjoy his final Argentina game as much as possible.     / Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/Getty Images The entire soccer world is preparing for Lionel Messi’s last dance with the Argentina national team on Tuesday night, but Emiliano Martínez revealed that La Albiceleste’s squad already got the party started, welcoming Messi home with “cuddles and a barbecue.”

Messi will bid farewell to Argentina in the match against Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. La Albiceleste destroyed Burkina Faso 7–0 on Saturday in its final match before the landmark occasion, after which Martínez addressed how the squad planned to welcome Messi to camp and ensure he has a proper send-off.

“We spoke, and he’s arriving to camp on Sunday night,” Martínez said post-victory. “We’ll make an asado [barbecue] at our base camp with him, and we’ll try to cuddle him for the little time he has left.”

The goalkeeper stuck to his word and posted a video on social media on Sunday night showing the barbecue preparations to get Messi’s celebrations started. Martínez, like the rest of Argentina’s squad, is trying to make sure Messi’s farewell as joyous an occasion as possible for the greatest of all time.
“We’ll try to make sure he enjoys it as much as possible,” Martínez said. “Fill him with cuddles, kisses and for him to be happy.”

Emiliano Martínez (left) was in goal during the most successful era of Lionel Messi’s international career.     / Ian MacNicol/Getty ImagesEmiliano Martínez became Argentina’s starting goalkeeper under Lionel Scaloni back in the summer of 2021, exactly one month before the 2021 Copa América. The rest is history.

With Martínez in goal, Messi finally put behind years of international heartbreak, and Argentina won two Copa América titles and the 2022 World Cup. Martínez was essential as Argentina won four penalty shootouts on the road to lifting those three titles, and his point-blank save against Randal Kolo Muani in the 2022 World Cup final is now one of the most memorable saves in soccer history.
“I tried to help him as much as possible, he knows it, we always speak about that,” Martínez said. “It was one of the greatest honors of my career, trying to help him achieve what he wanted to badly.
“He’s the greatest player of all time, and I feel part of [his career], thank God. On Tuesday, I want to see him enjoying himself and smiling.”

Emiliano Martínez admitted it took a while to get over losing the 2026 World Cup final.  / Ryan Pierse/FIFA/Getty Images “El Dibu” is poised to become one of Argentina’s main leaders of the post-Messi era, but only a few months ago, the 34-year-old’s own international career was in serious doubt. “We will have to see if it’s time to step aside,” Martínez included in his Instagram post after La Albiceleste fell to Spain in the World Cup final.

“Obviously losing a World Cup final was very hard for me,” Martínez admitted. “The pain stuck with me for a long time. I needed a change of scenery at the club level to try to ease the pain I had after the final.
“I achieved that, and now I come here and I feel good, happy, with a lot of energy. In the end I have to represent my country, my family, and I have to do it as well as I possibly can.”

Martínez left Aston Villa for Chelsea in the twilight of the summer transfer window. Re-energized, he is now fully committed to La Albiceleste as the 2030 cycle starts. Although he is aware that Messi’s absence will be strongly felt, Martínez is confident that other players will step up.
“He leaves a very big pit,” Martínez said about Messi’s retirement. “But there are guys here that have strong personalities.”

ftbpro_01m46y08eza9.title: ‘No Plan’—Benin Hilariously Admits Defeat to ‘the God’ Lionel Messi Ahead of Farewell Match
ftbpro_01m46y08eza9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:34 PM EDTLionel Messi completed his final Argentina training session.      / Juan Mabromata/AFP/Getty ImagesBenin will fact Argentina on Tuesday night in Lionel Messi’s final game for La Albiceleste, and center back Mohamed Tijani hilariously revealed his team’s strategy entering the game: none. There was nothing to be done to prepare for the likes of Messi, who he described as “God.”

Tijani and the rest of Benin’s squad were caught by Argentine media shopping around the streets of Buenos Aires. After showing off the Albiceleste-themed yerba mate cup he bought for his kids, Tijani spoke about Messi’s farewell match in a comedically blunt interview with outlet C5N.

“F---, he’s the best in the world,” Tijani said when asked what Messi means to him. The next question revolved around how the No. 89 globally-ranked Benin planned to defend Messi in his farewell match, prompting an even funnier response.
“We shouldn’t mark Messi,” Tijani confessed. “We are going to enjoy this match. There’s no special plan to defend against Messi, we just have to enjoy this game, and that’s it.”
“I’m going to look at him like this,” Tijani added, laughing. “Messi, you are the God. To me, he’s the best in the world, like I’m telling you.”
Not to be outshined by Tijani’s excitement, Benin’s team doctor interrupted the interview to shout: “He’s the best in the world! He’s the God of football!”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
Anticipation continues to grow in Argentina, as an entire nation prepares to bid farewell to Messi in a date that will forever be engraved in La Albiceleste’s history.

Countless tributes have gone viral on social media in the lead-up to the match. In Messi’s home city of Rosario, a massive Argentina No. 10 shirt was placed at one of the city’s landmarks, with “Thank You” replacing Messi’s name.
🥹 🩵 ¡EL HOMENAJE PARA MESSI EN ROSARIO! La enorme playera que pusieron en Argentina para agradecer a su ídolo. (vía rosariolaciudad) pic.twitter.com/nqKFXR5rzW

A number of tributes will take place before and after the match against Benin. Messi will be accompanied by his family, his teammates and the players from Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning side—minus a couple of absentees.
The match will start at 8 p.m. local time (7 p.m. ET), and live musical performances will take place before and after the contest, as well as at half time.

Tickets for the match were sold out almost instantly, meaning River Plate’s Estadio Monumental will be packed to its 85,000 capacity. A Fan Fest has also been installed at Buenos Aires’s university for those who were unable to secure a ticket to gather in numbers for the momentous occasion.
Argentina will wear a special jersey dedicated to Messi for the first and only time. After the match, a video tribute will be displayed on the stadium’s screens.
The stage is set for Messi’s last dance with Argentina, a watershed moment for the country and world soccer as a whole.

ftbpro_01m472c7nzm4.title: USMNT Star Folarin Balogun Breaks Silence on Failed Everton Transfer
ftbpro_01m472c7nzm4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas8:30 AM EDTFolarin Balogun has played just one competitive match since the 2026 World Cup.         / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images Folarin Balogun opted against joining Everton this summer when his transfer appeared all but complete, but the U.S. men’s national team striker revealed that returning to the Premier League in the future is still “definitely an option” for him.
Over the weekend, the Arsenal academy graduate attended the first NFL London game 2026 and was asked if the Premier League was something that still interested him. Balogun’s answer was telling.
“Yes, potentially,” the player confessed to talkSPORT.
“Football has many twists and turns as we’ve seen after the World Cup. I was close to a transfer, it didn’t materialize, but for sure it’s definitely an option.”

The summer started with Balogun bagging three goals for the USMNT during the 2026 World Cup before he found himself in the eye of the storm for FIFA’s now infamous red-card U-turn following intervention from U.S. President Donald Trump to suspend his ban after getting sent off in the round of 32. It is a topic that still won’t go away.

The summer ended with Balogun headlining the wildest Deadline Day saga of the summer transfer window, as his essentially finalized move from Monaco to Everton collapsed not once but twice in a matter of hours. He remains a Monaco player but has only played 14 minutes this season was left off of Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT roster for the September-October international window.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Folarin Balogun was excellent for Monaco in 2025–26.  / Valery Hache/AFP/Getty Images Ultimately, it was the 25-year-old who pulled the plug on the Everton transfer after the Merseyside club raised concerns over his medical, leading to Balogun not feeling “comfortable to sign a long contract here,” per Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro.
To make matters worse, the striker was left out of Monaco’s UEFA Conference League squad due to the uncertainty that surrounded his future at the time the club had to submit the list.

Still, Balogun is expected to return to Monaco’s plans and could be registered once the knockout rounds of the third-tier European competition arrive. For now, though, the USMNT striker must rediscover the form that saw him bag 19 club goals for just a season ago.

Monaco currently sit atop the Ligue 1 standings through five games, and 20-year-old Germany international Paris Brunner has six goals across all competitions already, making his case to take over as the team’s starting center forward.

Julian Hall has had a record-breaking start to his USMNT career.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images It’s not only at the club level that Balogun must be prepared to compete for his place in the lineup, though.

Balogun wasn’t included in Pochettino’s USMNT fall roster because he hadn’t played a single game since the 2026 World Cup when the Argentine boss unveiled his squad. Instead, Pochettino granted maiden opportunities to young strikers to impress, and they’ve done exactly that.

Julian Hall, 18, became the youngest player since Pelé to score in his first three international appearances. The Red Bull New York teenager has deservedly stolen headlines over the past two weeks, but he’s not the only young frontman that’s impressed.

Justin Ellis has formed a strong partnership at Orlando City with Antoine Griezmann and then opened his USMNT account just four minutes into his senior international debut. The explosion of young, exciting attackers has been the story of the USMNT’s international window, with multiple debutants instanty delivering for the Stars and Stripes.

It’s imperative that Balogun returns to form for Monaco on the other side of the international break, or else failing to secure a Premier League return in the near-future could be the least of his worries.

ftbpro_01m484ks5yr2.title: Can Cristiano Ronaldo Get to 1,000 Goals Without International Soccer?
ftbpro_01m484ks5yr2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath7:30 AM EDTCristiano Ronaldo has 21 goals to go. / Hassan al Raisi/Anadolu via Getty ImagesCristiano Ronaldo’s goal count stands at an almighty 979.

That’s 979 times the five-time Ballon d’Or winner has scored in senior, competitive soccer for club or country since making his debut way back in 2002. It’s an incredible haul—and more than any professional has ever (officially) managed in the history of the sport. But it’s not quite enough.
“This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo told Vogue at the outset of this season.
The 41-year-old has set himself two targets for his swan song: 1,000 career goals and winning the UEFA Nations League with Portugal for a third time.
He reiterated his dual goals prior to Portugal’s 1–0 win over Wales at the end of September, just days before everything started to go awry.

Ronaldo stormed out of Portugal’s camp after a disagreement with manager Jorge Jesus, who left the veteran striker on the bench for the subsequent win over Norway, and then refused to apologize in a subsequent press conference. Reports suggested Ronaldo felt “betrayed” by the manager.
Behind the scenes, Portugal officials are frantically looking at ways to rebuild Ronaldo’s relationship with the national team, but the superstar’s international future hangs in the balance.

With the Nations League goal now in serious doubt, Ronaldo’s other target of reaching 1,000 goals could also be affected. If the superstar can’t be wooed back to international duty, can he still get the final 21 goals he needs?
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
If this is the end, it wasn’t meant to end this way. pic.twitter.com/IoHayRTesH
If this is to be Ronaldo’s final season as he suggests, his remaining games are finite.
With seven matches played of the Saudi Pro League this season, he has a maximum of 27 more fixtures to play with club side Al Nassr in the division in 2026–27.

On top of that, Al Nassr have a guaranteed seven more AFC Champions League Elite fixtures, during which Ronaldo would be expected to play if fit, with the opportunity to extend that up to 14 more matches if they were to reach the final.

The domestic cups are the only other opportunities for Ronaldo to add to his goal tally. The King’s Cup offers the chance for up to five more matches, but potentially only one if Al Nassr lose in the Round of 32, while there could be another two in the 2026 Saudi Super Cup.

With a minimum of 36 matches still to play before the end of the season (and his career), Ronaldo would need to need to average around 0.58 goals a game to hit his target. This figure will, of course, reduce if Al Nassr get further in their cup competitions.
In each of his three full seasons in Saudi Arabia, he has far exceeded the 0.58 ratio, hitting 0.81 goals per game in 2025–26.
Only a serious drop off in form, or injury, is likely to stop Ronaldo from getting the goals he needs now, regardless of whether he is coaxed back into international duty.
Ronaldo would be the first to hit 1,000. /  Octavio Passos/Getty ImagesNot for the first time, Ronaldo stands on the brink of history.
By reaching four figures, the Portuguese superstar will break a barrier officially untouched by anyone else before in soccer.

Three-time World Cup winner Pelé is often cited as having scored 1,279 goals (including by Guinness World Records) but many of the Brazilian’s strikes came in non-competitive matches and his widely accepted official final tally for club and country is actually 762.

ftbpro_01m4888q9sbe.title: Ranking All 25 Nominees for the 2026 Golden Boy Award
ftbpro_01m4888q9sbe.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack11:00 AM EDTLa Masia is set to produce another Golden Boy winner. / David Ramirez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesTwenty-five of European soccer’s brightest starlets are up for the 2026 Golden Boy award, with Tuttosport releasing its final shortlist for the prize, handed out in November.

Award season is upon us, folks, and the best U-21 player in the world will be crowned by the Italian newspaper for the 24th time. Rafael van der Vaart was the first victor in 2003, and the esteemed honor has since been bestowed upon the likes of Lionel Messi, Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham.

Leading Ballon d’Or contender Lamine Yamal was the recipient of the prize in 2024, and although the 19-year-old fits the age requirement for the latest edition, previous winners cannot be crowned more than once.
As a result, Yamal and last year’s Golden Boy winner Désiré Doué have been omitted from Tuttosport’s shortlist. Still, that doesn’t mean there isn’t an array of dazzling alternatives in contention.
Here’s Sports Illustrated’s ranking of the 25 Golden Boy nominees.
Xavi Espart has emerged in Catalonia. / Maciej Rogowski/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesRank

Popular statistics website Transfermarkt teamed up with the award’s organizer to create a top 20 shortlist for the 2026 Golden Boy. However, these 20 players have been accompanied by five “wild cards” selected by a nameless panel.

While none of these five are seriously in contention, Xavi Espart’s emergence at Barcelona this season means he could tease a top-10 finish. Franco Mastantuono’s tough first term in Madrid has made way for glimmers of hope in Florence, while Borussia Dortmund’s Joane Gadou, only 19, could be a strong contender in 2027 and 2028 should he continue on his upward trajectory.

Rodrigo Mora looks set on delivering on his early career promise since joining Roma in the summer, and Brighton & Hove Albion’s Charalampos Kostoulas is in exactly the right place to further his development.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Espart’s Barcelona teammate, Marc Bernal, is another La Masia gem who looks at ease at the highest level and continues to be trusted by Hansi Flick despite the arrival of Rodri in midfield.

Bernal and Espart could soon be joined by Stuttgart’s Finn Jeltsch in Catalonia, given that the center back has started to earn transfer attention from the La Liga leaders. Jeltsch has appeared 57 times for Sebastian Hoeneß’s side and looks set to take the next step in 2027.

German international Saïd El Mala similarly impressed in the Bundesliga last season, scoring 13 times for FC Köln. He was close to joining Dortmund in the summer, but the deal fell through. Still, BVB did land another nominee, Konstantinos Karetsas, who’s at the forefront of an exciting generation of Greek starlets.
Real Sociedad’s Jon Martín is another stellar young center back with ample senior experience, but unlikely to garner great recognition from voters.

Kerim Alajbegović’s cause was aided by his World Cup exploits and subsequent switch to Juventus, while high-profile figures Endrick, Estêvão and Jorrel Hato may rank higher than they perhaps deserve. Endrick was at least briefly prolific for Lyon, but Estêvão has been hindered by a hamstring injury for much of 2026 and is yet to work his way into Xabi Alonso’s plans at Chelsea.

Gianluca Prestianni will be recognized by many due to his altercation with Vinícius Júnior earlier this year. The Brazilian alleged that he was racially abused by the Benfica winger, but Prestianni was instead charged by UEFA for homophobic conduct. He served a six-match suspension and now has the task of helping his country mourn the international retirement of Lionel Messi. Prestianni is one of Argentina’s brightest young stars.

Karl has proven himself on the biggest stage. / Reinaldo Coddou H/UEFA/Getty ImagesLennart Karl’s 2026–27 campaign is yet to kick into gear, but the young German’s stellar season last time out means he’s worthy of a top-10 finish. The Bayern Munich academy graduate earned his big break under Vincent Kompany, playing second fiddle to the Belgian’s array of thriving attacking stars, particularly Michael Olise down the right. Karl, a majestic dribbler in tight spaces and adept in various roles, notched double-digit goal contributions in a little over 1,200 Bundesliga minutes, and also scored four times in the Champions League as Bayern reached the semifinals.

The Frenchman enjoyed a landmark debut campaign with Bournemouth. / Getty ImagesIt took just one year of Premier League soccer for Eli Junior Kroupi to be considered a $100 million forward. The French sharpshooter produced a landmark campaign with Bournemouth on the English south coast, primarily operating as a second striker working off Evanilson’s shoulder.Kroupi’s outstanding ball striking helped him became the first teenager in over two decades to score 10-plus goals in his debut Premier League season. A significant ankle injury sustained in preseason denied him a big summer move, but the continent‘s elite will doubtless be sniffing around again in 2027.

Rayan has looked the part since arriving on the south coast of England. / Ibai Tudanca/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesRayan’s work with the Brazilian national team is bound to satiate voters. The winger has looked the part ever since he joined Kroupi at the Vitality Stadium in January, immediately settling into Andoni Iraola’s framework. Rayan had been regarded as one of Brazil’s brightest prospects after scoring 14 times in Série A for Vasco de Gama last year, and the imposing winger, who earned starts for Carlo Ancelotti’s Seleção at the World Cup, will lead the Cherries’ quest for Europa League glory this term.

Lewis-Skelly’s reintegration helped Arsenal to the Premier League title. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesMikel Arteta’s reintegration of Myles Lewis-Skelly down the stretch last season played an underrated role in Arsenal getting their hands on the Premier League title.Lewis-Skelly broke into the first team as a left back, but spent his youth dominating in midfield. He offers bite and verticality in the engine room, and  Arteta eventually saw the light. His resurgence wasn’t enough to earn him a spot on England’s World Cup roster, but he’s back in Thomas Tuchel’s thinking at the start of the next tournament cycle.

ftbpro_01m488y28khj.title: ‘Enormous Potential’—Jose Mourinho’s View of Yan Diomande Explains Lack of Real Madrid Starts
ftbpro_01m488y28khj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath9:30 AM EDTYan Diomande has started just twice for Real Madrid. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesExactly two months on from his signing, Yan Diomande’s Real Madrid career has yet to really take off.
The 19-year-old has started just twice out of seven matches in La Liga (in wins over Rayo and Elche) and played just 47 minutes of the big matches against Inter Milan and Atlético Madrid.
He is in the weird position of being both Madrid’s most expensive transfer of all time, but also the most low-key arrival of the summer; a galáctico and a project player.

It was clear that Florentino Pérez needed a statement signing this summer following his re-election as president. After two years without a trophy and his authority coming under challenge, the playbook response was to project strength with a shiny new toy. When it became clear that Michael Olise was immovable, Pérez turned to the next best thing: Diomande.

Market inflation demanded Madrid break their own transfer record to sign the Bundesliga Rookie of the Year, but the $140 million (€125 million) price tag has created extra hype and expectation for a player who only made his pro debut in March 2025.

As yet, Madrid fans have only fleetingly seen the four-pronged attack featuring Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior, Jude Bellingham and Diomande that got them so excited in preseason. Meanwhile, the Côte d’Ivoire international has just one assist so far.
AS reports that José Mourinho is deliberately treating Diomande as “a young player with enormous potential” rather than a ready-made superstar.

Yan Diomande is yet to get a run in the team with Madrid. / Issouf SANOGO/AFP/Getty ImagesAsked about his game time (or lack thereof) during the international break, Diomande told local broadcaster NCI: “Even though I don’t play much, I train a lot, and the training sessions are intense. It’s gratifying that the coach [Mourinho] puts his trust in me.”
He added: “I love pressure, because it gives me a chance to surpass myself. And I also play at a club where there are big demands.”
Thus far, Mourinho has often seemed reluctant to call on Diomande, with Arda Güler—arguably Madrid’s best player so far this season—the preferred option on the wide right.

While dropping the Türkiye international to the bench may not be the most sensible option, Diomande’s versatility could put him in line for more starts on the opposite side of the Madrid attack amid the team’s ongoing struggles.
Best Real Madrid Ever. The 25 Best Real Madrid Players Ever—Ranked. dark. Next

Vinícius Jr. has admitted to suffering from a crisis of confidence post-World Cup and has been a regular target of the Bernabéu’s wrath at the outset of 2026–27, due to his protracted contract renewal saga as much as his form.

Diomande was signed amid growing fears that Vinícius Jr. might not renew his deal, with Arsenal lurking. The young Ivorian—who featured on both wings for RB Leipzig last season—was seen by many as both an insurance policy and statement to Vinícius Jr.’s camp as the saga headed towards brinkmanship.

With the Brazilian staying and signing new terms, it had been expected that Diomande would take up a primary role as a right winger in Mourinho’s preferred 4-2-3-1 system, but those plans could yet change. As a natural right-footer, Diomande remains an option to slot in on the left side as another option for Mourinho amid Vinícius Jr.’s barren run.
Yan Diomande holds the highest dribble success rate (72.0%) across Europe's top five leagues this season (18/25 completed, min. 20 attempted). 🕺 pic.twitter.com/yrMB9awp1Y

Diomande was given just 36 minutes to impress in a near-impossible situation in the Madrid derby—subbed on with Los Blancos both a goal and a man down. However, the teenager was a rare bright spark for Madrid at the Metropolitano, playing off the left.

He completed four out of six dribbles, completed 90% of his passes, won nine out of 12 duels and forced a shot on target during his cameo. He looked like Madrid’s best attacking outlet on the day, and is consistently a dribbling machine for club and country.

Vinícius, by contrast, was practically anonymous before being substituted before the hour, with his troubles continuing on in the international break, as the Brazilian threatens to become a major problem for Mourinho to solve.

ftbpro_01m48csvv7y7.title: Jacquet Sparks Injury Fears for Liverpool Days Before Huge Man City Clash
ftbpro_01m48csvv7y7.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:45 AM EDTJérémy Jacquet is a new injury doubt for Liverpool. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesThose whom the gods wish to destroy they first call promising.

Jérémy Jacquet was riding high this fall. After making a strong start to his new Liverpool career, the freshly capped France international swiftly earned the acclaim of Zinédine Zidane. After a watching brief against Türkiye, the 21-year-old played every minute against Belgium and Italy in a pair of performances which his revered international boss hailed as “very good” four times in the same sentence. As ever, this sport’s fickle fates soon intervened.

Jacquet had been expected to start for France again in Monday’s clash with Belgium but failed to even make the matchday roster. The national team would confirm a muscular problem for Liverpool’s starting center back just a handful of days before the almighty Premier League return against current top-flight leaders Manchester City on Sunday.

If that fixture wasn’t fraught enough with the swirling crisis of City’s guilty verdict raging angrily in the background, Andoni Iraola may have to brave that storm without his first-choice partner for Virgil van Dijk.

Jérémy Jacquet doesn’t hold back. / Nico Vereecken/PhotoNews/Getty ImagesThe exceedingly brief update offered by the French soccer federation described Jacquet’s problem as a “strain to his left hamstring.” Zidane was more dismissive when reviewing his center back’s absence, writing it off as a “a knock.”

Jacquet’s embryonic career has been blemished by mercifully minor muscular injuries. The former Rennes rampager has only ever complained about a calf problem during his senior playing days, sitting out just two games in the middle of 2025 with a minor issue.

The big problem for Jacquet lately had been a serious shoulder injury which brought a premature conclusion to his Rennes career. Shortly after signing his pre-agreement with Liverpool, the youngster had to undergo surgery on an issue which kept him out for four months.

Wary of overloading a player starved of match sharpness, Iraola had been keen to ease him into Liverpool’s high energy setup. “In the first games, he was feeling the change of rhythm physically. He was finishing with cramps and really tired so we had to sub him,” the Reds boss explained last month.
Liverpool’s most recent win against Bournemouth was hailed as “a step forward” for Jacquet by Iraola. “He looked solid until the end and I think he’s finished physically also in a good place.”
Unfortunately, he now appears to have taken a step back.
Jérémy Jacquet has arrived. pic.twitter.com/XN55tb5Rxy

Given the vagaries of the updates offered about Jacquet, it’s difficult to judge how severe his injury is. Recovery from a hamstring strain could vary from three days to three months or anywhere in between. That Jacquet was able to finish both of his international appearances over the break would suggest that his absence on Monday was precautionary, rather than a reaction to anything serious.

Iraola will certainly be hoping so. The summer recruit has started all six of Liverpool’s Premier League and Champions League fixtures already this season, forging an encouraging partnership alongside Van Dijk, who has looked more like his imperious self with Jacquet next to him.

“So far, it is good,” the wary veteran warned last month. “He is 21 years old and very promising, but it is up to him to keep working hard and staying calm. It’s a big credit to him how he started his Liverpool career, but we are in September. Hopefully there are years of his Liverpool career left.”
The long-term future for Jacquet is bright, but it still remains to be seen if he can recover in the short-term.

ftbpro_01m48dhwfr48.title: Lionel Messi’s Landmark Argentina Moments in Pictures
ftbpro_01m48dhwfr48.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath12:30 PM EDTIt’s been some ride. / Jabin Botsford/The Washington Post via Getty ImagesLionel Messi’s 21-year international career has reached its end.

The iconic Estadio Monunmental in Buenos Aires will play host to a piece of soccer history as the 39-year-old superstar signs off with his 208th and final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin on Tuesday.
There will be fireworks and waterworks in equal measure at the big farewell for one of Argentina and the world’s greatest-ever players.
From 2005 to 2026, here’s a look back at the Argentina moments that made Messi, from the significant and the spectacular. It’s been some ride.

Messi received a red card on his Argentina debut. / Michael Mayhew/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty ImagesIn a quirk of fate, a floppy-haired, 18-year-old Messi makes his senior Argentina debut against Hungary—the very same opponent Diego Maradona had faced in his first appearance for the national team back in 1977.

The match is not exactly the anointing of Maradona’s successor many had anticipated. Messi comes on after 63 minutes and was sent off by German referee Markus Merk on 65, having been judged to have thrown an elbow at defender Vilmos Vanczak (above) in a tussle for the ball.

Messi soon bounced back from his sending off. / ATTILA KISBENEDEK / AFP via Getty ImagesThe BBC’s South American soccer expert Tim Vickery calls the controversial sending off a “crime against football.”
Messi scored the sixth against Serbia & Montenegro. /  Tony Marshall - PA Images via Getty ImagesMessi is not yet 19 when he scores his first World Cup goal.
Argentina confirmed its spot in the knockout stages with an emphatic 6–0 win over Serbia & Montenegro in Gelsenkirchen, with Messi making his tournament debut off the bench.

The teenager only had 15 minutes of the second half to make an impact but set up Hernán Crespo for the fourth, before adding the sixth himself—darting into space at the edge of the box and striking neatly across goal, with what would soon become a trademark finish.

Messi soon became the main man for Argentina. /  MIGUEL ROJO/AFP via Getty Images)AFP via Getty ImagesGrizzled veteran Juan Sebastián Verón is reduced to a giddy fanboy as Messi made it 2–0 in the Copa América semifinal against Mexico.

Messi—with shoulder-length hair and wearing the number 18 on his back—loops one over Oswaldo Sánchez from the edge of the 18-yard box. It is as aesthetically pleasing a goal as you are ever likely to see and one which announced Messi as the superstar everyone in Argentina and Barcelona told the world he would be.

Diego Maradona link-up with Lionel Messi did not bring success. /  DANIEL GARCIA / AFP via Getty ImagesThe attempt to pair with Messi and Maradona as player and manager proved a flawed experiment as Argentina is eliminated at the 2010 World Cup quarterfinal having been torn to pieces by Germany in a 4–0 defeat.

Having played lighter as the exciting, up-and-coming prospect at previous tournaments, 2010 was the first time Messi—by now a Champions League and Ballon d’Or winner—felt the crushing weight expectation to replicate the heroics of the man in the dugout. He ended the 2010 tournament with no goals in five games.

Messi scored his first international hat-trick against Brazil. / Tim Clayton/Corbis via Getty ImagesMetLife Stadium was the venue for Messi’s first-ever international hat trick, with more than 80,000 watching live as the superstar powered Argentina to an all-time classic of a 4–3 friendly win against Brazil—a clash that was billed as Messi vs. Neymar in the buildup.

Close but not close enough. /  Chengdu Economic Daily/VCG via Getty ImagesMessi glumly accepted the Golden Ball as the 2014 World Cup’s best player moments after Argentina fell to an extra-time defeat to Germany in the final in Rio de Janeiro. Meanwhile, photos are snapped of the forward looking on at the trophy he really wanted.
With the forward in his peak years and three tournaments in, questions are beginning to be asked about how many more chances he would get at soccer’s grand prize.

The 2014 World Cup final starts a run of painful final defeats. / ALFREDO ESTRELLA/AFP via Getty ImagesThe World Cup final loss triggers a run of painful final defeats, with Messi’s Argentina falling short in back-to-back Copa América tournaments—both times on penalties, both times to Chile.
In the 2016 Centenario tournament held in the United States, Messi scored five times but missed the opening penalty of the shootout the final.

Messi’s first retirement triggered an outpouring of national grief. /  Amilcar Orfali/LatinContent via Getty ImagesMessi, then 29, retires from Argentina duty following the heartbreak, saying: “For me, the national team is over. I've done all I can. It hurts not to be a champion.”

ftbpro_01m48gm85hw3.title: Disrupted USMNT Out to Avoid 58-Year Humiliation Against Canada
ftbpro_01m48gm85hw3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:00 AM EDTMauricio Pochettino doesn’t have a good record against Canada. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesMauricio Pochettino has admitted that his U.S. stars will be battling the hidden foe of fatigue while also trying to avoid a third consecutive defeat at the hands of Canada on Tuesday.

The Stars and Stripes have typically dominated this rivalry. Between 1985 and 2019, Canada went 17 consecutive matches without toppling its neighbor. However, Jesse Marsch’s punchy current generation has twice beaten the USMNT, winning the last friendly between the pair in September 2024 before claiming third place in the 2025 Concacaf Nations League.
Should Canada prevail again in Minnesota, it would be the first time since 1968 that the Canucks have claimed three consecutive victories over their nearest rivals.

If history was not enough to inspire Canada, Marsch has the added ammunition of being snubbed for the USMNT job before Pochettino took over. “There’s definitely not a grudge. People want to take it that way, which is fine,” he shrugged ahead of Tuesday’s not-so-amicable friendly.

“So, for me personally, I can honestly say this, in all three of the matches where we’ve been tasked with playing the U.S. is I know that the U.S. is a good team and they’re someone that we measure ourselves against and I want to do everything I can to give these guys the best opportunity to go out and play at their best and win the match.”
Canada is clearly amped, but Pochettino’s hosts are tired.
To be the future you must rewrite history. pic.twitter.com/MID0hojIEy

Pochettino struck a balance between caution and confidence in his preview of Tuesday’s friendly. The Argentine coach pointed out that the team’s flight from Phoenix had been delayed, disrupting preparation for a set of players who had grown weary from a condensed slate of fixtures this fall. While all these conditions would “affect” his roster, Pochettino was still optimistic.

“It’s about to keep growing and I think supporting the players and to finish the [window] in a very good condition,” the USMNT boss warned, hinting that there may be some rotation to avoid overloading any of his stars heading back to a demanding club schedule.

“But I am sure that the players, even if we were competing a lot and traveling, that can affect, we are going to be ready for [Tuesday], with fresh energy. And I think it’s a good opportunity for continuous growing in that camp.”

ftbpro_01m48khy56fc.title: Lionel Messi's Soccer Portfolio: Every Club the Argentina Legend Owns
ftbpro_01m48khy56fc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack6:00 PM EDTLionel Messi is “just starting out” in the business world. / Hector Vivas/FIFA/Getty ImagesLionel Messi has cultivated a sporting legacy unlike any other. To the majority of the soccer world, he’s the greatest player who has ever lived, seemingly immune to Father Time and still capable of hanging with the very best at the age of 39.
World Cup glory in Qatar saw Messi, in the words of English commentator Peter Drury, “conquer his final peak”, ensuring his glittering career wouldn’t end with a nagging sense of cruel unfulfillment.

His work in North America this summer merely enhanced his standing, even if a flawed, chaotic Argentine outfit came up just short and Kylian Mbappé harshly snatched the Golden Boot away from his grasp. Now, a soccer-crazed nation is preparing for a state of consternation.

Messi may no longer be the beating heart of La Albiceleste, having called time on his international career after 208 matches and an endless list of records that surely won’t ever be topped. Nevertheless, the 39-year-old has no intention of riding off into the sunset and leaving soccer behind.

He’s setting himself up for a life that continues to revolve around his first love, tying soccer in with a developing business interest. "I would like to keep learning [about business] because I know nothing, and I am just starting out," Messi told the America Business Forum last year.
Messi’s going down the club ownership route, and he’s already got his fingers in a few pies.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Deportivo LSM was launched by Luis Suárez in 2025. / DANTE FERNANDEZ/AFP/Getty ImagesMessi has been involved in a joint-venture with former Barcelona and current Inter Miami teammate Luis Suárez. Together, they established a new club, Deportivo LSM, in Uruguay, Suárez’s homeland.

It’s Suárez’s initiative, with the center forward’s project starting out with the funding for a 20-acre sports complex built in 2018. It is home to a synthetic turf stadium that boasts a capacity of 1,400.

“I’m proud and happy that you chose me, so I hope to contribute everything I can to continue growing and, above all, to be by your side in this,” Messi said to Suárez after his involvement in the project came to light.

The newly established club is located in Ciudad de la Costa, the second-most populous city in Uruguay, and they’re now competing in the third tier of Uruguayan soccer after earning promotion in year one.

However, the owners have already cut ties with inaugural manager Rafael Cánovas after a disappointing start to the new season. Former Nacional striker Álvaro Apólito was sworn in as his successor at the end of September.
Cornellà is one of Catalonia’s most historic clubs. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesWhile Messi is supporting Suárez’s project in Uruguay, he has full ownership of UE Cornellà.

The Argentine completed his purchase of the club in April, with Cornellà currently competing in Spain’s fifth tier. Founded 75 years ago in 1951, it’s one of Catalonia’s most historic clubs, and upon the new owner’s arrival, Cornellà wrote: "This move reinforces Messi’s close ties to Barcelona and his commitment to the development of sport and local talent in Catalonia."

Messi has spent much of his adult life in Catalonia, given that he joined Barcelona as a 13-year-old in 2000 and didn’t leave the Blaugrana until the club’s financial woes forced him to move on to Paris Saint-Germain in 2021.
Spanish journalist Guillem Balague says Cornellà is the "nursery where young players grow", with Arsenal’s David Raya and outstanding left back Jordi Alba among the most notable alumni.
It’s a club built around progress, with Messi thinking long-term.
Eldense announced Messi as their new owner on Oct. 1. / Francisco Macia Martinez/Getty ImagesCornellà may have been Messi’s first purchase, but CD Eldense is the Argentine’s baby.
Eldense announced Messi as their new owner at the start of September, and Balague writes that the Spanish second-tier club will "lead Messi’s football operation".

"The arrival of one of the most important figures in the history of the sport as owner of CD Eldense marks the beginning of a long-term project aimed at promoting the club’s sporting, institutional, and social development," Eldense wrote after Messi’s arrival was made official.

ftbpro_01m48pcagygr.title: Two European Giants ‘Monitoring’ Noni Madueke Amid January Transfer Speculation
ftbpro_01m48pcagygr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer11:30 AM EDTNoni Madueke has fallen down Arsenal’s pecking order. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesNoni Madueke’s struggle for Arsenal starts this season could push the England international winger towards the exit, with the likes of Juventus and Atlético Madrid reportedly in the mix.

The Gunners spent heavily on Madueke a little over 12 months ago, committing to pay up to $69 million (£52 million) to Chelsea in July 2025. He started around half his 43 appearances across all competitions, but one-third of his 12 goal contributions came in three Carabao Cup ties.

Madueke is backup to Bukayo Saka in his favored right-wing position and faces increased competition from 16-year-old Max Dowman. He also serves as cover for Christos Tzolis on the left flank, although is yet to play there this season. Tzolis was injured while playing for Greece last week but Eberechi Eze had been getting his leftover minutes previously.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

With an underwhelming start to the season, Madueke was left out by England manager Thomas Tuchel for the September-October internationals, despite playing five times at the 2026 World Cup. It demonstrates the need to be playing—and performing—at club level.

Other clubs, including Juventus and Atlético Madrid, are now said to be “monitoring his situation” with an eye on the January transfer window, per The Telegraph. England staff supposedly view Madueke as “among the best one-on-one forwards” at Tuchel’s disposal, but that wasn’t enough for a call this time. Perhaps a move may do the job.

Diego Simeone has recruited English players before. / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesPlaying wide for Atlético Madrid can come with differing demands. Diego Simeone’s primary formation this season has been 3-4-2-1, which means possibilities as a wingback or narrow winger. Marcos Llorente and Lee Kang-in are the current starters in the right-sided roles, respectively, with Giuliano Simeone another option to rotate in.Simeone Sr. has shown a liking for English players in the past, taking Kieran Trippier and Conor Gallagher to the Spanish capital. But while Madueke is versatile enough to play on either flank, actually forcing his way into a starting position might be very challenging.

Rio Ngumoha is not suited to the right wing. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesLiverpool spent big money to replace Mohamed Salah during the summer without actually replacing the departed Anfield legend. There is hope that Bradley Barcola will recapture his Paris Saint-Germain form of old to become the dual-threat winger on the left side of the pitch, but there is gaping hole on the right that Andoni Iraola is yet to figure out how to fill.Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz have both struggled in the position, while Cody Gakpo—a player previously suited to left wing and No. 9 roles—has done the best job thus far.Madueke is actually a right winger and, should Liverpool be able to negotiate favorable terms, it could make sense. The problem is that the 24-year-old is objectively worth less, according to Transfermarkt, than what Arsenal paid for him—even a mid-season loan might have to factor that in. Then, there is there is trying to do business with a direct rival.

Madueke would be competing with Francisco Conceição. /  Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesJuventus are credited with longstanding interest in Madueke. The right flank is locked down by Francisco Conceição, but the quality and competition behind the Portugal international is arguably lacking—unlike on the left where Juve added Kerim Alajbegović during the summer.Madueke has previously shown no fear of heading abroad to further his career, leaving the comfort of home in London aged 16 to join PSV Eindhoven in the Netherlands.Juve would likely have to offload at least one other wide forward if this is to last more than a short-term loan arrangement.

Scott McTominay has thrived since swapping England for Italy. / Ivan Romano/Getty ImagesA better fit in Italy could be Napoli, a destination flush with ex-Premier League names and where select British players—Scott McTominay, Billy Gilmour—are becoming part of the furniture.The team’s starting right winger is 33-year-old Mateo Politano, who remains reliably available but doesn’t bring impressive numbers. Last season, it was two goals and five assists in 34 Serie A appearances, 26 of which were starts.David Neres was threatening his place in the first half of 2025–26 but missed the final five months of the campaign because of an ankle injury and has begun slowly this season.Madueke has never been on fire in the goal and assist columns, but he potentially offers more. At his best for Chelsea in 2024–25, it was seven goals and four assists in 32 Premier League matches.

An excellent manager awaits at Aston Villa. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesUnai Emery has already gone cold on Alejandro Garnacho at Aston Villa, whose wings have a considerably youthful look this season, with 18-year-old Ibrahim Mbaye among several statement signings.Still, with the club competing in the Champions League and expecting to progress from the league phase, attacking depth and experience could use a boost after the departures of both Jadon Sancho and Leon Bailey during the summer.Villa are at the wrong end of the table after a poor start to the new campaign, but that was exactly what happened 12 months ago and they finished fourth in the Premier League and lifted the Europa League. It remains an attractive club to join.

ftbpro_01m48rfr61x4.title: Man City Punishment Timeline: How Long Will Appeal Take, When Will This End?
ftbpro_01m48rfr61x4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom2:00 PM EDTManchester City are in a limbo period. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesManchester City’s confidence is infectious. The underfire club reacted to the guilty verdict delivered by an independent panel by defiantly declaring their innocence and stressing: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted.”

The rhetoric was so convincing even a spokesperson for the U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham considered the matter to be far from closed. “If wrongdoing is established...” a statement read. It had to be subsequently altered to, “Wherever wrongdoing is established...”

Wrongdoing has been established after a thorough investigation of more than two years, however the idea that this is far from over is also correct. City have appealed and warned that no stone will be left unturned in their fight against this “Premier League conspiracy theory.”
Untangling all those webs will still take some time.

The appeal process could get Enzo Maresca’s thumbs up. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesThanks to new regulations brought in by the Premier League, there is a clear timeline which the appeal process has to follow. A new three-person panel will have to conduct a five-day hearing within 12 weeks of the appeal being lodged.
From that point—which just so happens to fall on Christmas Eve—the independent body has 30 days to deliver their verdict. At the latest, we will have an answer before the end of January.

Manchester City are preparing a new legal case. / Mike Morese/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThis is not a retrial. Manchester City can only appeal on the basis of any procedural errors or material errors of law. The club hinted at what this may be in a spiky response to the official verdict:

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence. The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.” The implication being that independence, impartiality, fair-mindedness or non-partisan influence was not adhered to.

Historic cases offer an example of what City could be looking for. The Chinese three-time Olympic gold medallist Sun Yang had an eight-year doping ban briefly overturned by Switzerland’s highest court after successfully arguing that one of the arbitrators on the panel was not impartial. After combing through thousands of old social media posts, Sun’s lawyers found that the arbitrator “castigates a Chinese practice of dog slaughter and denounces the consumption of this meat at a local festival in China.”
It remains to be seen what City’s legal team can dig up about the independent commission’s panel. The appeal board have almost every available power at its disposal, including:

Lord Pannick KC’s work isn’t over. / Lucy North/PA Images/Getty ImagesShould City fail with their appeal, they can still take the case to an independent arbitrator. However, this can only happen if a verdict has been:
After that, there is the break-glass emergency option of taking the case to the High Court where City could question if the Premier League’s rules adhere to U.K. competition law.

Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) and Ferran Soriano will not let this lie. / Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesThis affair doesn’t look like being wrapped up any time soon. The sports law specialist, Paul Gilroy KC, appeared on a recent recording of Stick to Football. “I heard Jill [Scott] saying this morning, ‘It’d be great to have this finished by the end of the season.’ Good luck with that one,” he scoffed.
“Never mind this season or the next or maybe the next five seasons.”

In the unblinking address to camera Manchester City CEO Ferran Soriano delivered to club staff in the wake of the verdict, he warned: “We will now be relentless in our work. We will focus on the independent appeal process and also all other legal avenues available to us in order to win the case, and we will take all necessary action to protect the club and seek compensation from any party that tries to damage it now, and in the future.”

It took almost eight years from the start of the Premier League investigation to reach a first guilty verdict. Yet, as City have been keen to tell anyone who will listen, the process is still ongoing.

ftbpro_01m48twd2hzw.title: ‘This Kind of C---’—Canada’s Jesse Marsch Takes Shot at President Trump
ftbpro_01m48twd2hzw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer12:00 PM EDTJesse Marsch is an American working in Canada. /  Omar Vega/Getty ImagesJesse Marsch is “honored and really proud” to be Canada men’s national team coach. As an American abroad, he feels he is able to have a “unique perspective” on things, like Donald Trump’s executive order from August renaming Lake Ontario.
“Here we are now, the big talk in America is Lake Ontario, Lake America, this kind of c---,” Marsch said this week, ahead of Canada preparing to face the USMNT in Minnesota.

A day earlier, Marsch claimed: “We, as Americans, have been inundated with propaganda since we were young. We’re the No. 1 country in the world, we deserve everything, we dominate everything, No. 1 in every aspect of life.

As a result, he said, Americans “feel like we deserve to be treated differently because we’re Americans” if things happen a certain way and “we don’t feel like we’re in control of it.” Marsch used the example of the Folarin Balogun red card to illustrate his point, adding more broadly, “That is one of the things that infuriates the rest of the world about Americans. And Americans don’t know that if they don’t ever leave the country.”

Canada, Marsch said, is a “little bit more European than the U.S. anyway,” politically, economically. He backs the possibility of Canada, debuting as an entrant in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2027, becoming an associate member of the European Union—“I like that aspect.”

“There’s a uniqueness to Canada in terms of how truly multiethnic this country has become. You can see that Canada is not just a North American country any more, you know? That bodes well for our sport and for the makeup of our team, the makeup of our fans.”

Marsch has led CanMNT since 2024. / Ayman Aref/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe next day, Marsch told reporters at a press conference he is still “not afraid to say things that sometimes need to be said or that I feel should be said ... whether people agree or not.
“I get that it’s not always the job of a sports person to put themselves in the forefront of the political environments and everything else, but I’ve had a unique perspective.”
Marsch, who played his whole career in America but has since worked as a coach in Austria, Germany and England, insisted there is “definitely no grudge” towards the USMNT.
“People want to take it that way, which is fine,” he said. “I don’t mind. People can, I think you know me well enough to know that I don’t really care what people think too much.”
No grudge does not mean no rivalry. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesThere is, however, a rivalry and it’ s a “big” one.

“[The players] don’t need reminders when we play the U.S.,” Marsch offered. “But, to be fair, it’s different with Mexico, but because we have respect for the U.S., because we have respect for Mexico, we want to continue to show that we are on the level that they are or above them. And the best way to do that is to perform and win."

“If you look at recent tournaments, we did better [than the USMNT] at Copa América. We were equal to Mexico and the U.S. in the World Cup. I think institutionally, Concacaf still looks at this as a region that’s about Mexico or U.S. … where we need to continue to establish ourselves.

“If we want to step into those moments and have that respect, you need to beat them sometimes. I think of course a lot of the people in the U.S. talk about Mexico being their biggest rival, but we know we feel like we’re in that conversation as well in terms of our quality and what we’ve done not only in the past, but what we can do leading up to as well.
“You’ve seen some of these games get feisty and be a fight because they don’t want to lose either. I think when you’re at the top, you don't want anyone that’s below you to take that power.
“I think the rivalry is better than it’s ever been, more because the two teams are good.”

Canada is on the brink of equaling its longest-ever winning run against the USMNT. The Canucks have won the last two meetings, compared to 17 meetings without a win from 1985–2019, but hasn’t won three in a row against its southern neighbor since 1968.

ftbpro_01m497andqnv.title: ‘Love Football More’—Neymar Issues Emotional Lionel Messi Tribute Ahead of Argentina Farewell
ftbpro_01m497andqnv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas4:14 PM EDTNeymar is one of Lionel Messi’s closest friends in soccer.     / Gustavo Pagano/Getty Images Countless tributes and messages have been directed Lionel Messi’s way in the hours leading up to his final game for Argentina. Long-time teammate, rival and close friend Neymar wrote a tribute of his own, stating Messi made him “love football even more.”

Neymar shared the pitch with Messi at the club level for Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain and was even present when Messi lifted his maiden Argentina trophy, given it came at the expense of Brazil in the 2021 Copa América. Before Messi’s farewell, Neymar took to social media to celebrate his friend’s illustrious international career.

“Anyone who loves football has enjoyed you throughout all these years,” Neymar posted to Instagram. “Today is your last game with the shirt of your national team, of your country, and I hope you enjoy every second, may all the tributes today make you happy.

“It’s not only Argentina that thanks you, the whole world thanks you for everything you’ve done for football. Thank you for making me love football even more. It was an honor to have played against you, and even more so to have made history alongside you. THANK YOU, Leo Messi,” Neymar finished, adding an emoji of a goat at the end of his message.

Neymar and Messi won everything there was to win during their four seasons together at Barcelona, forming a lasting friendship and two-thirds of the greatest attacking trio in soccer history. The final head of that three-headed monster also paid homage to Messi before his last dance with La Albiceleste.

Lionel Messi (left) and Luis Suárez have established a bond that extends beyond the pitch.  / Luis Robayo/AFP/Getty Images Alongside Messi and Neymar, Luis Suárez also won it all at Barcelona. The legendary Uruguayan striker then followed Messi to Inter Miami, and the duo are even co-owners of a soccer team in Suárez’s home country.
The pair of lethal South American goal scorers have been close friends for over a decade, and on Messi’s landmark day, Suárez made sure to pay his respects with a video tribute.

“Gordo! (chubby),” Suárez started, via DSports. “I just wanted to send you a big hug. I hope you enjoy your last match wearing your country’s national team shirt very much—which was so important for your career.

“You lived incredible things. You won things that every player wishes they could win representing your country. So you have a more than deserved recognition from all the people in appreciation of your career and what you represented for your country.
“Feel very proud of yourself. I send you a very big hug, and enjoy your day.”

Oct. 6, 2026 is a day that will live forever in Argentina’s folklore: the day the whole nation bid farewell to the man that marked an entire era for Argentina. The landmark occasion started with adidas posting a video in which Messi shared a few words to Argentina, thanking the nation’s supporters for “loving me so much.”
“The moment has arrived,” Messi said to start the video. “I leave in peace. I gave it my all. This jersey was my dream, my pride and my life.
“Thank you for loving me so much. I’m going to miss you.”

Argentina will face Benin on Tuesday night at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. Messi will make his 208th and final appearance for La Albiceleste, dropping the curtain on the international career of the greatest player of all time.
