ftbpro_01m4b54xgdp3.title: Why Are Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi Ending Their International Careers So Differently?
ftbpro_01m4b54xgdp3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath8:00 PM EDTRonaldo and Messi’s careers have taken different paths. / Pat Elmont/Karl Bridgeman/FIFA/Getty ImagesEver since they finished first and second in the Ballon d’Or vote back in 2008, the careers of Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have been irrevocably intertwined.
From that moment, a previously unseen breed of superstar ushered in a new age for soccer as they went on to dominate, change and then transcend the sport itself.

Powered by the rise in social media and its rabid, fiercely tribal fanbases, the Messi-Ronaldo era brought forth a fresh obsession with stats, individualism and the GOAT question—keeping the two men locked and linked for all eternity. If you’re reading this then you already have a side in the debate.
For many years, their careers seemed to run parallel in a constant game of one-upmanship. Then things changed.

As of the start of October 2026, Messi has just been given a lavish, tear-filled, highly indulgent send off by Argentina after his 208th and final appearance—complete with a drone-led light show and fireworks in Buenos Aires. Meanwhile, several thousand miles away Ronaldo is locked in a war of words with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus amid a self-imposed exile from the national team.
It’s hard to think of two more contrasting ends for the two greatest players of all time.

Lionel Messi scored at his farewell party. / Martin Zabala/Xinhua/Getty ImagesThe September-October international break would hardly have been a key marker in anyone’s calendar at the start of the year, but it could yet go down in history as the moment when both Messi and Ronaldo exited the international soccer stage.

Messi’s last tango had been carefully choreographed since the summer, with the 39-year-old making it clear that the 2026 World Cup would be his last. When Argentina lost in the final to Spain, the Argentine Football Association (AFA) made sure to set up a friendly match specifically to give their departing hero a fitting farewell.

Benin was the chosen opponent, with 85,000 attending the Monumental Stadium to give thanks to Messi, say goodbye and be a part of a moment in soccer history. With the Benin players acting as little more than props on Messi’s big day, the man himself capped a 3–0 win with a late penalty.

It was the dream send off for any player and a grand tribute to a player whose success was not pre-ordained, but someone who earned his legend—overcoming a series of failures with the national team to become a double Copa América winner and world champion.

Messi could’ve played for Spain. He could’ve stayed retired in 2016. In the early years, he left some fans cold. Ultimately, the 39-year-old superstar had to fight for a long time to become beloved by his country, but by the end there was not a dry eye in the house.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Watching on from the other side of the world, Ronaldo may have wondered: “Why not me?”

After all, only Ronaldo has more international caps and more international goals than Messi in all of men’s soccer. He has played in as many World Cups as the Argentine, won the European Championship in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League titles.

And yet, instead of being indulged, celebrated and cried over, the 41-year-old is being cast aside. After being left on the bench for the Nations League win over Norway, Ronaldo made the decision to leave the Portugal camp, later releasing an extraordinary statement accusing manager Jesus of breaking his promises.

In one particularly ill-advised segment of the statement was an eight-point plan Ronaldo and others had agreed for Jesus to say at a press conference, which featured the toe-curling wording: “I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pelé or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game. If it were today I would not do it.”
The full statement—declared as the “purest of truths”—bristles with ego and hurt feelings. Had Messi’s love-in not been running parallel, might Ronaldo’s almighty tantrum have been avoided entirely?
Ronaldo is beloved by Portugal fans. / Diogo Cardoso/Getty ImagesRonaldo may yet make a comeback.

His teammates will never say a bad word about him and he appears willing to take his medicine over what happened. He is adored as a deity in Portugal for everything he has done, given and continues to represent. The love is there, as it strong as it is for Messi. Both players will be remembered as all-time greats long after they are gone. But the uncomfortable truth is that Ronaldo just isn’t integral to the team’s success anymore—and hasn’t been for some time.
After a full decade as numbers one and two in the Ballon d’Or standings, Ronaldo has not made the podium since 2019, while Messi has pulled away with an overall total of eight awards to five.

ftbpro_01m4b8ayfv0b.title: The Winners, Losers From USMNT’s Faultless World Cup Return
ftbpro_01m4b8ayfv0b.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:30 PM EDTCavan Sullivan (left) and Christian Pulisic have had a very different few weeks. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty Images (Sullivan), Marco Luzzani/Getty Images (Pulisic)Mauricio Pochettino may have extended his stay at the U.S. men’s national team but the Argentine manager has made it abundantly clear that this is very much a new regime. The program would be “starting from zero” he warned.

Four wins while jumping around five states in three time zones has afforded Pochettino’s new project the perfect platform from which to build. Results were never at the forefront of the manager’s mind but a faultless return from a somewhat underwhelming World Cup on home soil has given some time for experimentation.

Almost every gamble which Pochettino made paid off during a series of wildly varied victories over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. Yet, for each winner on the roster, there was a bitter victim of the USMNT’s success watching from the sidelines.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

From Russell Crowe to Mick Jagger, Mauricio Pochettino has changed his fashion choices this fall. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesAfter signing a bumper contract through the 2030 World Cup, Pochettino is in a position of power. Nevertheless, a less daring manager would perhaps have picked at least one of Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie or Folarin Balogun and fewer than 13 uncapped youngsters. However, Pochettino is in the business of blooding a new generation of talent. There is no time to lose and he came through the biggest leap of faith without a single “L” to his name.
Beyond the tally of 12 goals scored and three conceded across the four straight wins, the USMNT retained that full-throttle approach which has defined the nation’s best performances under Pochettino.

“We played four games in two weeks, and to play always with the same intensity, with the same commitment, with the same passion, that is a thing that we keep,” the demanding manager understandably beamed.
To be the future you must rewrite history. pic.twitter.com/MID0hojIEy

Cavan Sullivan was not the USMNT’s best performer this fall; he wasn’t even the best teenager on the roster. However, it is Philadelphia Union’s peroxide-blonde 17-year-old who has been the face of this window for his dexterity as well as his industry.

Pochettino’s star pupil played with an infectious energy which coursed through the entire team. His record-breaking goal against Mexico may have come from a boneheaded blunder by goalkeeper Raúl Rangel, yet the modern perception of players is so often a collection of moments rather than a monument to consistency. Sullivan delivered the clippable content while also running hard enough to win the approval of Pochettino. Job done.
The USMNT are handing the keys to the kids. pic.twitter.com/cpWbBzfEFb
There were 13 players on Pochettino’s roster who started the international window without a single senior cap. By the end of the intense schedule, the entire baker’s dozen had been given a run-out.
“I think obviously there are a lot of new faces, and they all had great energy and worked very hard while they were here,” mused Gio Reyna, a veritable veteran at the ripe old age of 23.

The hard work doesn’t stop here. If this kindergarten class hopes to have any chance of being reunited in November, their toughest job is only just getting started. “The most difficult thing is how we support these young players,” Pochettino explained.

“The easier thing always is to arrive there and make their debut. But now, how we are going to evolve with them, and how we are going to protect [them]? ... How are we going to make them understand that now they have more responsibility? That is one of the things that we were talking [about] in the dressing room, too.”

Gio Reyna has always been a Mauricio Pochettino favorite. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesAvailability is the best quality and one which has been lacking for so much of Reyna’s young but tumultuous career. However, this window offered some unprecedented whiffs of consistency. Pochettino’s pet project was an ever-present member of an ever-changing starting XI.

That quartet of starts followed on from a run of form for Strasbourg which has now seen Reyna start eight straight matches for club and country for the first time in his entire senior career. For context, he made his professional debut in January 2020.

Rather than dwell on that landmark, Reyna shifted the focus forward. “Honestly, [I’m] more just thinking about keep going now ... just keep building what I’ve been doing, keep showing up every day, training, recovering, doing everything I need to prepare mentally and physically for every training and game,” he shrugged.
“[I] feel good, though. Feeling more confident every time I step on the pitch. It was a good amount of minutes, so just very happy with obviously how this window went, as well.”

Christian Pulisic was not called up. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIt’s easy to cast those who fall in the shadows of angels as devils. A fully fit and scoring Christian Pulisic was left at home and the biggest story was that it wasn’t much of a story at all.

ftbpro_01m4b8qcye40.title: Arsenal Injuries: Four Changes Mikel Arteta Has to Make on Premier League Return
ftbpro_01m4b8qcye40.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack2:00 PM EDTArsenal have had several injury casualties during the bumper international break. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesAn extended international break has offered Mikel Arteta plenty of time to ruminate over Arsenal’s emphatic defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion on Sept. 19.

It had been a borderline procession at the start of the Gunners’ title defense, with those who projected Arteta’s men to waltz to a retention of their crown feeling rather smug after a gritty 2–0 victory at Sunderland maintained a 100% start to the Premier League season through four games.

But Brighton’s beatdown of the champions manifested a fallibility that few had expected. In one fell swoop, Arsenal’s credentials were questioned. The most neurotic supporters suddenly feared that not enough had been done in the summer to resist the pushes of their volatile contenders.

“This can’t happen again,” Arteta asserted post-match, and the Spaniard, who recently signed a contract extension with the Gunners that makes him the highest-paid manager in the division, has ample opportunities for rectification before the next break.

However, Arsenal’s quest to rid themselves of shuddering Seagull-inflicted memories will be made tougher by several injury casualties. The break hasn’t been kind to the Gunners, and Arteta will be forced into multiple personnel changes when Leeds United visit Emirates Stadium this Saturday.
Out—expected to be available in late October

Arsenal entered the break with William Saliba out for the long haul due to a back issue, while Ben White had sustained a groin injury during the victory at Sunderland. Thomas Tuchel bemoaned the right back’s absence and then had to deal with Declan Rice’s withdrawal for England’s opening four 2026–27 UEFA Nations League matches.

Rice has been suffering with neural pain in his hamstring throughout 2026. After he started all but one of the Three Lions’ World Cup outings in the summer off the back of a 55-game season with Arsenal, load management is being prioritized at the start of the new campaign.
The midfielder spent much of the break in Dubai, and is expected to be available for Leeds’ visit on Saturday. White should also be back in action after he was spotted in training pictures last week.
Havertz suffered a hamstring injury on Jürgen Klopp’s managerial bow for Germany. / Federico Gambarini/picture alliance/Getty ImagesThen come the casualties.

Kai Havertz and Christos Tzolis both sustained hamstring injuries while playing for Germany and Greece, respectively. There have been positive updates following scans, but the pair are set to be sidelined for the next couple of weeks. Returns could be on the cards before the end of October.

Ezri Konsa was also forced to withdraw from the England camp after sustaining a dead leg. The setback isn’t serious, and the defender could be available this weekend. However, Arteta should have Cristhian Mosquera to call upon for the first time since Matchday 2. The Spanish center back has recovered from a hamstring problem sustained in August.

Teenage starlet Max Dowman was in action for England’s U-19s during the break, picking up a red card in its victory over the U.S. Dowman was unavailable for the final match against Belgium after suffering a contact injury, but the issue is unlikely to sideline him this weekend.

Viktor Gyökeres scored in all four of Sweden’s games during the extended break. / Vasile Mihai-Antonio/Getty ImagesArteta believed that the depth of his roster would allow his team to compete fiercely on multiple fronts last season, and he certainly wasn’t wrong. After securing a first Premier League title in 22 years, Arsenal took Paris Saint-Germain the distance in the Champions League final before losing in a penalty shootout.

And while a superstar addition to the attack wasn’t made in the summer, the club made a huge midfield signing in Bruno Guimarães and further bolstered its defense with the arrival of Konsa. If there’s any club capable of dealing with a litany of injury setbacks, it’s Arteta’s Arsenal.

However, Arsenal’s scrutinized frontline will be hindered by the absences of Havertz and Tzolis. While Bukayo Saka made it through the break unscathed, Arteta will likely pivot to Viktor Gyökeres to replace Havertz up front and be forced to fit a square peg in a round hole down the left.

With Gabriel Martinelli departing for Saudi Arabia and Vinícius Júnior signing a contract extension at Real Madrid, Arteta has limited options behind Tzolis. Eberechi Eze has been used there without much impact since he joined the club, while Noni Madueke primarily functions off the right but could offer a direct, straight-line running threat on the opposite flank.
In defense, Arteta won’t hesistate in returning Mosquera alongside Gabriel if Konsa isn’t fit. White can also share the load with Jurriën Timber at right back.
Timber’s minutes are being carefully managed by Arsenal and the Dutch national team after undergoing groin surgery in the summer.
Given their injury situation, Arteta will likely be forced into four changes from the defeat at Brighton when an impressive Leeds team visit north London this weekend.

ftbpro_01m4baszb7zf.title: Ranking the USMNT's Eight Teenage Debutants After Perfect Fall Friendlies
ftbpro_01m4baszb7zf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell1:30 PM EDTMauricio Pochettino’s youngsters stole the show this fall.  / Alex Menendez/USSF/Getty ImagesMauricio Pochettino flipped the script for the U.S. men’s national team’s fall friendlies, trusting eight teenagers to round out a new-look squad to kick off the 2030 World Cup cycle.

Without previous mainstays like Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun making the cut, Pochettino put the pressure on his wide-eyed youngsters to usher in a new era for the Stars and Stripes. Fans were desperate for bounce-back performances after an embarrassing round of 16 exit  at this summer’s World Cup on home soil.

Friendly matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada loomed large for such a group of inexperienced players, but the USMNT walked away with four strong victories in the newly combined September-October international break.

A handful of debutants bloomed under the bright lights, while others wilted in front of sold-out home crowds. Once the final whistle sounded against Canada to end the international window for the Stars and Stripes, it was very clear which emerging talents staked their claim to stay—and which need more time to prove themselves.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Zavier Gozo failed to leave his mark. / Alex Menendez/USSF/Getty ImagesSecuring a transfer from MLS to the Premier League as a teenager takes a special talent. Zavier Gozo bid farewell to Real Salt Lake to join Crystal Palace this summer, and already has three senior appearances for the Eagles to his name.The move set high expectations for Gozo this international break, but he failed to measure up. The 19-year-old made one appearance off the bench in the USMNT’s 4–1 win over Peru and then did not log another minute in the next three matches. Gozo shines at right wingback, a position rather void now that Pochettino has returned to a back four. The American can play at right midfield or on the right wing as well, but he was never going to displace Sergiño Dest or Cavan Sullivan—at least this time around.

Adri Mehmeti needs more time to break into the team. / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAdri Mehmeti was done no favors by Pochettino this international break. The 17-year-old only logged two minutes in his senior debut against Peru before he was thrown into the XI against Chile next time out ... out of position.Pochettino started the natural midfielder on the left wing, where Mehmeti looked out of sorts. He committed costly turnovers, did not register a single shot and lost five of his six duels on the night. It was no surprise Mehmeti did not appear against Mexico and then only came on in the dying stages against Canada.

Neil Pierre is still raw around the edges. / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesNeil Pierre came into the September-October international break as one of the most exciting youngsters on Pochettino’s roster. The towering center back was billed as the long-term replacement for the recently retired Tim Ream. Except it became clear rather quickly Pierre still has plenty of work to do before he can cement himself as Chris Richards’s partner in central defense. The 18-year-old clumsily made it through his first-ever start in the team’s 4–2 win against Chile, where he looked overwhelmed and indecisive in his 63 minutes on the pitch.Pierre was then benched against Mexico, before he came on and held his own for 16 minutes to protect his side’s 1–0 lead against Canada. He has a high ceiling, but is still nowhere near the end product Pochettino needs from a defender.

Peyton Miller had a strong USMNT debut. / Mark Thorstenson/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesPeyton Miller faces similar challenges to Gozo. The New England Revolution man got the nod in the USMNT’s first match and did well commanding the left flank against Peru. He misplaced just one pass and created two chances in his senior debut.But the left flank belongs to Antonee Robinson. The Fulham star is rightfully Pochettino’s first-choice left back and that will not change until after the 2030 World Cup.  Miller is then left trying to scrap for playing time, competing with Auston Trusty as well. The 18-year-old was an unused substitute against Chile and Canada, and only made an eight-minute cameo against Mexico.The best Miller can hope for moving forward is locking down the role of Robinson’s backup.

Mathis Albert got his moment this fall break. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesAs one of three 17 year olds called up for the September-October international break, Mathis Albert arrived to camp desperate to prove himself worthy of the senior squad. Previous managers might have only given him one or two opportunities, but Pochettino awarded the teenager minutes in all four of the USMNT’s friendlies this fall.Albert had a quiet debut against Peru before he opened his account just three days later. The Borussia Dortmund youngster bagged a stoppage-time insurance goal against Chile to briefly become the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history—though that record didn’t last long.Pochettino awarded Albert with his first senior start in the team’s 1–0 victory over Canada, but the winger struggled to get much going in his 61 minutes on the pitch; he only completed 12 passes, did not create a single chance and did not even take a shot before he was pulled.There’s still growth needed for Albert to solidify a permanent place in Pochettino’s squad, but his raw talent promises a bright future.

Justin Ellis gave Mauricio Pochettino plenty to consider ahead of the November international break. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images“It’s a fantastic problem for us,” Pochettino said when asked about having so many young players show up and show out this break. Among the standouts was Justin Ellis. The No. 9 marked his senior debut with a goal against Peru, before he found the back of the net again against Canada. Two goals in three appearances was no doubt enough to leapfrog the likes of Haji Wright and Josh Sargent in Pochettino’s striker pecking order. Ellis still has some work to do before he can climb the ladder any further, but  playing club soccer alongside the great Antoine Griezmann at Orlando City will continue shaping the 19-year-old into a consistent, reliable goalscorer.

Cavan Sullivan made USMNT history in his first camp. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesOver the last two months, Cavan Sullivan became a household name in MLS, routinely putting on shows with the Philadelphia Union. At just 17 years old and already with a place at Manchester City upon his coming of age, the American came into the the fall camp with plenty of hype.And he lived up to his budding reputation. Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history when he found the back of the net against Mexico just five days after he celebrated his 17th birthday. He also impressed with his gritty work rate and relentless nature, earning high praise from Pochettino. “I think he’s a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession," the Argentine said about Sullivan. “He’s a fighter, he's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player with a tremendous quality.“And then I think Cavan showed in possession with the ball on the field [and] when he need to be chasing people and recover the ball. That is my impression after maybe three weeks together. And that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it’s a fantastic news for USA. Hope that continues in that way.”

Julian Hall stole the show this fall for the USMNT. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesJulian Hall had a dream first camp with the USMNT. The 18-year-old tallied three goals and one assist in four appearances, looking more comfortable in red, white and blue than some of the most experienced players in Pochettino’s ranks. Finding the back of the net in his senior debut would have been magical enough for Hall, but he then went on to score against Chile and Mexico as well. The Red Bull New York striker became just the third player in USMNT history to score in each of his first three appearances, and the youngest ever to do so since 16-year-old Pelé accomplished the feat for Brazil in 1957. Hall’s ascendance is great news for a USMNT side that lacked consistent scoring in the past. The injury-prone Pulisic and Ricardo Pepi have too often fallen flat for the USMNT, and Balogun hasn’t looked the same since the World Cup.  Now, Pochettino has a young, hungry weapon at his disposal, one capable of making a statement off the bench or leading the line with a poise far beyond his years. There is no doubt Hall is here to stay.

ftbpro_01m4bc9777cb.title: What Next for Lionel Messi After Argentina Retirement?
ftbpro_01m4bc9777cb.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 PM EDTMessi ended his Argentina career with 208 caps. / Luis ROBAYO/AFP/Getty ImagesSo that’s it. Lionel Messi is 208 and out. The 39-year-old called time on his 21-year international career with a 3–0 friendly win over Benin on Tuesday.

There were 85,000 fans packed into the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires to be there for a moment of history, as Messi scored a penalty to get his 126th Argentina goal on his final outing. In truth, the actual soccer was little more than an excuse to honor and celebrate the departing captain.
“Today, I am likely facing the saddest day of my career, because this is where I say goodbye to the national team and to all of you,” Messi told the crowd in a tear-jerking speech.

“I don’t want to leave, I don’t want to walk off the pitch. I just want to tell you that I love you, I’m going to miss you, and I am grateful to God that we are Argentine—proud to be Argentine and to have fulfilled my dreams with all of you.
So, now that it’s over for one of the greatest international players of all time ... what happens now?

Messi is under contract for two more years. / Michael Brown/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesWhile he has retired from international soccer with Argentina, Messi has not quit playing altogether and will continue to turn out for his club team Inter Miami in MLS for a while yet.
The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner remains under contract until the end of the 2028 season, by which time he will be 41 years old.

However, his deal is reviewed year by year and he could yet walk away earlier, or even extend his time in MLS further should he wish. As part of his contract, Messi will keep shares in the club when he does finally retire.
Currently, Messi’s Miami sit third in the Eastern Conference standings and are in a strong position to qualify for this season’s playoffs with the aim of retaining the MLS Cup won in 2025.

❤️💙💻 Lionel Messi, on his laptop to follow his new club CD Eldense against Real Oviedo.Messi bought the club on Thursday owining 100% of the Segunda División side from Spain.Eldense won 4-1 tonight. 🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/qlPF4G3gZc
Messi will continue to stay in soccer even after retirement and is already the owner of two clubs in Spain’s lower divisions: UE Cornellà and CD Eldense.
The forward took a controlling stake in both clubs this year and could end up with a network of teams around the world.

Messi is known to follow second-tier Eldense closely on his laptop and has set out to save them from relegation this season with the appointment of former Villarreal boss Javi Calleja. The long-term goal is to get the Valencian team promoted into La Liga.

Meanwhile over in Uruguay, Messi joined the project of friend and teammate Luis Suárez in 2025, becoming co-owner of Deportivo LSM. The club went on to win promotion to the country’s third division in its first season.

Messi doesn’t see himself as a manager. / Sebastian Hipperdinger/Europa Press/Getty Images“I’m not planning to become a manager when I will retire. That’s not something I’m considering to do,” Messi said back in 2024.
And yet, his name is already one of the favorites to succeed Lionel Scaloni as the next coach of Argentina and will likely remains so for all of eternity.
A similar fate befell fellow Argentina icon Diego Maradona, who eventually did become national team manager between 2008 and 2010.
Maradona’s spell in charge of Argentina wasn’t a particularly successful one and his contract was not renewed after a 4–0 defeat to Germany in the 2010 World Cup quarterfinal.
While some sort of role within Argentinian soccer is not beyond the realms of reality, for now, Messi has promised to remain a diehard fan.

ftbpro_01m4bdzem4q7.title: Four Premier League Clubs Gilberto Mora Could Join—Ranked
ftbpro_01m4bdzem4q7.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack4:30 PM EDTGilberto Mora reportedly has Europe’s elite on his tail. /  Omar Vega/Getty ImagesReports suggested there was more than met the eye regarding Gilberto Mora’s withdrawal from the Mexico camp ahead of its defeat to Chile.
A 1–0 loss concluded a worrying start to the Rafael Márquez era off the back of an impressive World Cup campaign led by veteran Javier Aguirre on home soil.

Supporters are keen to see the new manager, who ended his career with El Tri as the joint-fourth-highest appearance maker in team history, usher in Mexico’s brightest young stars: chief among them Mora.

After he became the youngest player in Mexico’s World Cup history this summer, the 17-year-old scored his first goal for the national team in a 1–1 draw with Colombia on Sept. 27. After that, though, Mora was an unused substitute against Peru and absent for the clash with the USMNT before his withdrawal from camp.

“Physical discomfort” was the official explanation, but plenty have cried conspiracy. Mora turns 18 on Oct. 14, thus making him eligible for an overseas transfer, and those skeptical about the nature of Mora’s withdrawal believe an impending move to a “major European club” was the primary reason for his absence.

Club Tijuana are set to earn a record Liga MX fee for his sale, and Mora’s camp understandably don’t want an injury to scupper negotiations. ESPN expect an announcement regarding his future to arrive on his birthday next week.
Could a Premier League move be in the cards for Mexico’s next great hope? Here are four possible English destinations for the playmaker, ranked by likelihood and compatibility.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Man Utd are reliant on Bruno Fernandes’ creativity. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesThe financial might of the Premier League means there’s scope for Mora to be attracted by an array of proposals. A burgeoning middle class has proven itself to be adept at harnessing bright young talent and evolving them into stars, but transfer rumor mills have yet to associate Mora with the likes of Brighton & Hove Albion and Bournemouth. Instead, the Mexican’s talent has been deemed worthy of the elite right away, and Manchester United are among the ’Big Six’ clubs linked with the soon-to-be 18-year-old, who was too young to have enjoyed Javier Hernández’s impish brilliance at Old Trafford.While the Red Devils are over-reliant on the ever-present reigning PFA Player of the Year Bruno Fernandes for creativity, a gamble on Mora doesn’t seem to be on INEOS’s agenda in 2027. Man Utd rejuvenated their midfield in the summer and will focus on retooling Michael Carrick’s defense next year.

Player trading has been a feature of the BlueCo regime.  / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesChelsea have been hoarders of talent since BlueCo came to power in 2022. Such dramatic stockpiling has led to an excess of players at the club’s disposal, even if it can dump either those unwanted or those deemed not quite ready on Ligue 1 club Strasbourg, also owned by BlueCo.Given the long list of clubs supposedly chasing Mora, the teenager is unlikely to be interested in a switch to Chelsea if it means his short-term future lies in France—no matter how beneficial the loan move could be for his development in Europe. You could certainly envisage Chelsea being interested in the Mexican playmaker—they rarely aren’t in the mix when transfer season rolls around. However, Mora is likely to be more intrigued by alternative proposals. Another hotshot, Estêvão, is struggling for minutes with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers thriving in unison with João Pedro.

Arsenal will pursue if Mikel Arteta is smitten. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesReports linking Mora with Arsenal have merely been tenuous up to this point. Fraz Fletcher, via AS, understands that the Premier League champions are “stepping up their interest” in the Mexican, having scouted the youngster at the World Cup.The club has supposedly been engaged in talks with Mora’s agent, Rafaela Pimenta. Both Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta are convinced by the teenager’s talent. AS speculates that Mora could emerge as Martin Ødegaard’s successor in north London, although the Norwegian’s start to the 2026–27 season suggests he’s determined to make up for a pair of disappointing individual campaigns. Moreover, Arsenal supporters believe they already have the heir to Ødegaard’s throne, and he’s currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund. Ethan Nwaneri differs in profile from both Mora and Ødegaard, but could nonetheless blossom into a productive final-third operator, given his fearsome ball striking. Mora is the exciting, X-factor talent fans are after, but he’s not a player Arsenal desperately require.

Liverpool may add another starlet to the mix. / Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty ImagesMora to Liverpool is certainly gaining the most traction online. TUDN’s David Faitelson reported Pimenta had passed on an offer from the Reds to Tijuana supposedly worth as much as $50 million. However, Mora’s agent gave nothing away when she was directly asked about Mora’s future.“Please understand that I don’t comment on transfer rumors,” Pimenta told Portuguese outlet Record. “I won’t say anything at all about the transfer of any player. Thank you very much for your understanding.”The North American market is one Liverpool have historically seldom dipped into, and if Mora were to join, he’d be the first Mexican player to represent the club. In truth, a Premier League move for the slight playmaker Mora at this stage of his career just doesn’t seem right. Liverpool have been the most strongly linked, but a move to Anfield doesn’t make much sense. The Reds are currently trying to eke the best out of another creator in Florian Wirtz, who has struggled to acclimatize after dominating in Germany across multiple seasons. That doesn’t mean Mora shouldn’t be heading across the Atlantic. He absolutely should venture out of Liga MX and into the rigors of Europe, but the current climate of Premier League soccer, laden with physicality and supreme athletes, just isn’t compatible with a 5’6" teenager boasting so little experience at the elite level.He needs a stepping stone on the continent.

ftbpro_01m4bev7y9jx.title: ‘Major Hurdle’—JJ Gabriel’s Extraordinary Demands Revealed Amid Bayern Links
ftbpro_01m4bev7y9jx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer1:30 PM EDTJJ Gabriel wanted more sooner than it was coming. / Manchester United/Getty ImagesJJ Gabriel’s chance to be the first 15-year-old to play a competitive match for Manchester United came and went last month, ending with a request to cancel his registration the day before Michael Carrick was intending to use him in the Carabao Cup.

Now that the teen prodigy has celebrated his 16th birthday, his likely departure appears closer than ever. United don’t have to adhere to the request made in September—apparently not out of nowhere—but that only stops him joining another English club before the summer.
The Red Devils would be powerless to stop him heading abroad more or less immediately.

FIFA rules prevent players younger than 18 from undertaking international transfers unless their families relocate for non-soccer reasons. But there is a concession for European Union (EU) citizens moving to other member states aged 16. Gabriel, although born in the United Kingdom—no longer part of the EU, has access to Irish and Cypriot passports through his family.

According to Sky in Germany, he intends to get a passport from Cyprus to unlock Europe. Bayern Munich are now firmly on the scene, with the same report noting that Gabriel’s representatives have already met with officials from the Bundesliga champions. The Times adds that previous contact between the parties had earlier taken place as far back as May.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Signing Gabriel could require some serious investment. /  Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesBarcelona appeared to distance themselves from the Gabriel links last month, when sporting director Deco said publicly: “We are not interested in any player in his situation.” Ironically, Gabriel is thought to have been training in the affluent Castelldefels suburb of the city while this saga unfolds. Real Madrid have also been heavily linked, as have Paris Saint-Germain.
Sky in Germany states that Borussia Dortmund, where Jude Bellingham, Erling Haaland and Jadon Sancho flourished as teenagers, RB Leipzig and Bayer Leverkusen have cooled interest.

The similarities to the Martin Ødegaard saga of 2015, culminating in his 2016 arrival at Real Madrid are growing smaller. The Norwegian seemingly had every major club across Europe on his tail, with pretty much a free choice of his eventual destination.
Gabriel might soon be at risk of overplaying his hand. Sky says the “financial demands are considered a major hurdle” to a prospective deal with Bayern.

The club would only have to pay a nominal compensation fee to Manchester United to take over his registration, but “salary and signing fees” ensure nothing about it would be a steal. The alleged request of a “seven-figure” salary is, according to The Times, not something Bayern are willing to agree to. Instead, they hope “development and future game time” will suffice as persuasion.
Next. JJ Gabriel Feature. JJ Gabriel Is a Child Who Needs Protecting. dark

Lennart Karl, aged 17 on his first-team debut in June 2025, is a recent example of how a talented young player can flourish in Munich. Jamal Musiala was 16 when he joined Bayern from Chelsea’s academy in 2019, debuting for the senior side 11 months later, after turning 17.
At least a degree of patience would be required from Gabriel’s side of the table.

Gabriel—or more likely his family—are reported to have demanded a minimum of 20 minutes in predetermined first-team games against Sabah, Brighton and Bournemouth across September and October. He was denied the Sabah opportunity when his name was not included on the club’s Champions League squad submitted to UEFA, requiring List A status because of his age.
Instead, he became the club’s youngest player to score a hat-trick in the U-19 version of the competition earlier that day instead. But it seemingly wasn’t enough.

His face in Manchester United’s official first-team photograph for 2026–27, published this week around a month after being taken, served as a stark reminder of the status well beyond his years he already had.

ftbpro_01m4bjcrfwq6.title: What Does the Future Hold for Christian Pulisic With the USMNT?
ftbpro_01m4bjcrfwq6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell5:45 PM EDTChristian Pulisic’s place with the USMNT is uncertain like never before. / Maja Hitij/FIFA/Getty ImagesWhile the U.S. men’s national team put together a perfect September-October international break, Christian Pulisic was stuck at home watching it all play out from across the Atlantic Ocean.

Unlike in previous windows, the 28-year-old was not sidelined with an injury or fresh off a recent recovery. Pulisic was fully fit and ready to represent the Stars and Stripes in friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

Except Mauricio Pochettino overlooked the AC Milan man, along with Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie. The Argentine boss instead put his trust in a wealth of young players, calling up eight teenagers and 13 total debutants for the first international window after the 2026 World Cup.
Four games and four wins later, no one is really even talking about Pulisic anymore, leaving the once-face of the team in complete purgatory.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Christian Pulisic has scored two goals for the USMNT under Mauricio Pochettino.  / Getty ImagesWhen Pochettino took over the USMNT in September 2024, Pulisic was the undisputed leader of the team. He was coming off a brilliant debut season at Milan and was one of few Americans to come out relatively unscathed from a disastrous Copa América campaign that summer.

Despite some injury hiccups, Pulisic got off to a strong start under Pochettino’s rule. The forward tallied one goal and two assists in three appearances to close out 2024, helping the Stars and Stripes advance to the 2024–25 Concacaf Nations League semifinals.

Once the calendar flipped to 2025, things took a sudden turn for the worst. More fitness concerns, along with two dreadful displays against Panama and Canada in the Concacaf Nations League, saw Pulisic’s stock decrease drastically.

Adding to the rapid decline was his decision to skip the Gold Cup to prioritize his rest and recovery ahead of the 2025–26 season. Pulisic was adamant about being in his best form for the approaching World Cup on home soil, but what soon followed was anything but.

The former Chelsea man tallied just one assist in his next six appearances for the USMNT, all while going through a career-worst goal drought at Milan in the second half of 2025–26. A goal against Senegal in a World Cup tune-up match finally broke the rotten run of form, only for Pulisic’s struggles to come right back during this summer’s showpiece event.

He only managed one assist in four appearances at the 2026 World Cup, providing the same amount of goal contributions as defender Auston Trusty. Pulisic was battling through injury at the tournament, but falling flat while the entire world—literally—watched was the exact last thing he needed after such a poor spell for the national team.

Mauricio Pochettino (left) and Christian Pulisic have previously clashed.  / John Dorton/USSF/Getty ImagesIt would be easy to blame Pochettino for Pulisic’s lackluster production. After all, the Argentine’s predecessors got the most out of Pulisic, while he could only lead the Champions League winner to two goals in two years.

The surface-level argument is easily debunked, though, when looking at how Pochettino elevates his players in red, white and blue. The manager took a squad largely of unknown MLS players to the Gold Cup final. He got the absolute best out of Balogun up top this summer, as well as Malik Tillman, Tyler Adams and Freeman.

In the September-October international break, Pochettino saw Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis, three teenagers nowhere near the pedigree of Pulisic, score six of his team’s 12 goals. The Stars and Stripes also only conceded three goals across their four wins against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

New faces on the USMNT are taking center stage. / Patrick Mulligan/USSF/Getty ImagesOf course, the strained relationship between Pochettino and Pulisic could be contributing to the forward’s poor form, but then what was Pulisic’s excuse last year with the Rossoneri? What was his excuse for the start of this season, when new Milan manager Ruben Amorim kept him on the bench for three straight games?

The USMNT is starting a new era, one that is spearheaded by young, exciting, passionate players, ready to give everything for the badge on their chests. It doesn’t matter if it’s a friendly or the Gold Cup or the World Cup; the new crop of talent at Pochettino’s disposal, combined with veterans like Adams and Chris Richards, want to play every second possible for the national team.
Pulisic might want the same despite his previous reluctance, but the decision is no longer his, especially after the team put together four convincing victories without him logging a single minute.

Christian Pulisic needs to earn his spot back. / Luke Hales/Getty ImagesDespite the USMNT’s top form this international break, it would be a major—and dramatic—leap to say this is the end of Pulisic’s time in red, white and blue. The 28-year-old is only 10 caps away from hitting the century-mark with the Stars and Stripes and is the team’s fifth all-time leading goalscorer with 33 goals to his name.
There will come a time, perhaps as early as the November international break, where Pulisic suits up again for his country. But things have changed.

Pulisic’s name and past performances are no longer enough to guarantee himself a place in Pochettino’s XI. In all actuality, its many of those past performances working against him. The production is simply not there at the moment, and when others can provide better creativity or finishing in the final third, it’s an easy decision for Pochettino to overlook the 28-year-old.

ftbpro_01m4bkbcrdv4.title: Four Things We Learned From USMNT’s Perfect World Cup Response
ftbpro_01m4bkbcrdv4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:30 PM EDTThe USMNT bounced back from the World Cup with four straight wins. / Rich Storry/Getty ImagesThree months ago, the U.S. men’s national team was standing in front of a disappointed crowd in Seattle, heads hanging low after a humiliating World Cup exit to Belgium.

Mauricio Pochettino’s squad, often heralded as the “golden generation” of American players, crashed out of the showpiece event in the round of 16 after a lopsided 4–1 defeat. The loss was the cure to the soccer fever taking over the United States this summer—but not for long.

A new-look roster, featuring eight teenagers and led by new captain Tyler Adams, represented the Stars and Stripes during the September-October international break and once again captured the attention of the nation with four strong wins against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

History was made along the way and stars were born during the faultless run this fall. Pochettino also learned some valuable lessons that could shape how the 2030 World Cup cycle unfolds for the USMNT.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Christian Pulisic was left off Mauricio Pochettino’s roster. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesMuch was made about Pochettino’s head-turning omissions before the international window got underway. The Argentine boss left Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun at home, three mainstays of the team.

For so long, Pulisic and Co. were expected to unlock the best version of the USMNT. The common perception was if they weren’t donning red, white and blue, the team stood little chance of overcoming solid opposition.

Yet with a newly blended squad of youth and veterans, the Stars and Stripes did more than just overcome solid opposition—they dominated their opponents. Pochettino’s men scored 12 goals and conceded just three in four consecutive victories, all without the three biggest names on the team.

Instead of making the same mistakes as his predecessors, Pochettino put his faith in other talents and was rewarded immensely. The Argentine got more from his debutants in the final third than he has from Pulisic throughout his entire time in charge of the USMNT. Had Pochettino forced the out-of-form AC Milan star into his XI, he could have witnessed much different score lines this fall.

What this says about Pulisic’s future with the team remains to be seen, but the burden is now on the American to prove himself worthy of a call-up; the Stars and Stripes are no longer desperate for his services.
The USMNT are handing the keys to the kids. pic.twitter.com/cpWbBzfEFb

Leaving home veterans made room for a wealth of youngsters to stake their claim with the USMNT—and they did just that. Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis found the back of the net a combined six times, accounting for half the team’s goals this international break.

Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history at 17 years and five days old, while Hall became only the third American player to score in three consecutive international games. The 18-year-old also is the youngest player to reach the milestone since the legendary Pelé did so for Brazil in 1957 at age 16.

Seventeen-year-old Mathis Albert found the back of the net as well, opening his account in just his second-ever appearance for the Stars and Stripes. Peyton Miller also showed his worth at left back, impressing in his one start against Peru.

There will be bigger tests for the youngsters to come, especially once the USMNT faces European opposition on the road to the 2030 World Cup, but Pochettino has a group of teenagers who look ready for the challenge.

Tyler Adams is the new leader of the USMNT. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesThe captain’s armband was not left vacant for long following Tim Ream’s retirement. Pochettino handed the honor to Adams, who previously captained the USMNT at the 2022 World Cup.

“I think he knows what I expect,” Pochettino said of Adams, “and he’s a perfect role model for everyone in the way that the philosophy, the future, representing that amazing country ... He’s the player and the person that can lead that period that we have ahead.”

Adams is indeed a natural leader. The 27-year-old comes with 62 international caps to his name—a number only that low due to multiple injury issues over the years—and has the unique experience of playing in MLS, the Bundesliga and now the Premier League. He can relate to many of the young stars filling out Pochettino’s ranks and is an exemplary model for how to conduct himself on and off the pitch.

The Bournemouth standout, who was one of the few USMNT veterans to play in the 2025 Gold Cup, is calm under pressure, relentless out of possession and willing to do all the dirty work in midfield. Adams showed as much in his elite performances against Peru and Mexico, in which he highlighted  his accurate passing as well.

Even when he came off the bench against Chile and Canada, he hardly put a foot wrong and helped the team close out both victories without any late drama. The ability to lead a new-look, inexperienced team to four consecutive victories cast away any doubt of his leadership abilities.

ftbpro_01m4brxrwm8a.title: ‘Forever’—Ronaldo Pays Touching Tribute to Messi After Emotional Retirement
ftbpro_01m4brxrwm8a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell4:00 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo (left) is one of many who showed his support for Lionel Messi. / Luis Loureiro/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images (Ronaldo), Luis Robayo/AFP/Getty Images (Messi)Cristiano Ronaldo paid homage to Lionel Messi following the Argentine’s farewell to international soccer, commending his long-time rival on writing a “story that will live on forever.”

Messi played his last minutes for Argentina on Tuesday evening in front of a sold-out crowd in Buenos Aires. The 39-year-old pulled down the curtain on a legendary career for La Albiceleste, one that brought home a World Cup title and two Copa América trophies, among other honors.

There wasn’t a dry eye in the Estadio Monumental when Messi celebrated one last victory for his country, a 3–0 win over Benin in which the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner tallied a goal and two assists. Support across the globe flowed in as the all-time great took his final bow on the international stage.

Fans, managers, players and even rivals delivered heartfelt statements to Messi, including Ronaldo. “Leo, so many years defending your country and a story that will live on forever,” the Portugal captain wrote on Instagram. “You have all my respect for everything you’ve achieved with Argentina. A hug.”
Although the two headlined one of the greatest rivalries in sport for over a decade, they did not let the Clásico divide sour their relationship or respect for one another off the pitch.

Ronaldo even seemed in line to hang up his boots alongside Messi after his sudden exit from Portugal’s camp, but the 41-year-old silenced any retirement rumors with a lengthy statement just hours before Messi’s farewell match.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Messi already gave a profound farewell speech following Argentina’s win on Tuesday, touching on everything from his best moments with the national team to World Cup conspiracy theories that ran wild this summer.
Not even 24 hours after his address did he take to social media to issue another goodbye message. “Yesterday was my last game and I already miss wearing blue and white,” Messi began.

“I know I’m making the right decision. It was an incredible road, filled with joys and also some sorrows, but I’m clear that it was worth every step I took. And I’m left with a lot to say. It is impossible for me to express everything I feel in a few words or in a post.

“This trip would have been impossible without my family, who always stood by my side and supported me, especially during the difficult times, when I needed it most. My friends were also essential, as were all the teammates and coaches I had, along with their coaching staffs. I don’t want to forget Diego [Maradona], who put our country where it deserved to be and who, as I always say, I know helped us by being there with us, also from heaven, every step of the way.

“Thank you to all the clubs I played for, for always respecting my feelings and allowing me to dedicate myself to my country whenever it was time to put on the national team shirt. And, of course, thanks to God: without His guidance and His will, we wouldn’t even be dreaming of having made it this far.
“I’m grateful. I love you all very much, I’m going to miss you and I’ll always thank you for being by our side, by my side.”

Luka Modrić (left) had nothing but great things to say about Lionel Messi. / Matthew Ashton/AMA/Getty ImagesReal Madrid legend Luka Modrić, another one of Messi’s former rivals from his Barcelona days, joined Ronaldo in honoring the Argentina captain.
“What can I say about him? It’s a shame he’s retiring, but it’s his decision and we have to respect it,” Modrić told Cadena SER.

“He’s achieved something incredible with the national team; he’s won the World Cup he wanted so much. He’s one of the best players in the world, a one-of-a-kind player, and it’s been a pleasure to watch him play, even though I’ve suffered a lot against him, both with Croatia and with Real Madrid.”

En route to 2022 World Cup glory, Messi and Argentina defeated Croatia 3–0 in the semifinals to deny Modrić and Co. a second straight World Cup final. The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner opened the scoring from the spot before Julián Alvarez’s brace sealed the game.
“I wish him the best of luck,” Modrić added.

ftbpro_01m4bsz5e20h.title: ‘Panic Button’—Man Utd Make Decision on Carrick As International Break Ends
ftbpro_01m4bsz5e20h.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff6:00 PM EDTMichael Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis in the summer. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesThere reportedly appears to be no “immediate threat” on Michael Carrick’s position as Manchester United manager, even if the Red Devils deliver a disappointing result on their return to Premier League action following the extended September-October international window.

United face a Tottenham Hotspur team rooted to the foot of the standings, even after a monstrous summer spend in the transfer market, seeking to build some positive momentum after taking five points from five matches to start the league campaign.

Carrick’s 17 games in charge last season yielded more points than champions Arsenal achieved over the same period. He will feel that his team isn’t a million miles away from the results he expects, given  single lapses in two games and an objectively shocking refereeing mistake in another have been responsible for costing United five points so far. The Red Devils have had the ball in the right areas of the pitch and are equaling Arsenal in the attacking third.

According to the Daily Mail, there is “no appetite for change” from those above him in the Old Trafford hierarchy. Ruben Amorim, who was overseeing gradual improvement off the back of an extremely poor 2024–25 season, ended up digging his own grave by airing his frustrations in public last January and wasn’t going to be fired until that happened.

It’s a results-based business but increased scrutiny should the Spurs match not end in victory still wouldn’t see the club “hit the panic button” over Carrick’s position. It was reported at the end of September that the players by and large still back and support the incumbent.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Carrick will feel Man Utd should have more points than they do. / Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty ImagesTottenham ought to be the perfect opponent for United at this juncture. They sit in last place after failing to win any of their opening five Premier League matches and taking just two points. United are the division’s joint-sixth highest scorers at this stage, while they should benefit from Spurs possessing the second weakest attack—only two goals so far and blanks in four matches.

Momentum and confidence are everything in professional sports but United will be tested over the coming weeks purely because of how busy the schedule is. Between the now concluded September-October international window and the next one in mid-November, the Red Devils play eight times in two competitions over the space of just four weeks.

Leeds United at Elland Road on Oct. 18 is a tricky one in the Premier League given the Yorkshire team’s strong start to the season. More challenging is that it’s sandwiched between Champions League trips to Atlético Madrid and Como. A visit from Bournemouth to follow ought to be more straightforward, but then comes Chelsea away, before successive home matches against Roma and an improving Aston Villa coming out of their own slow start.

ftbpro_01m4byk7zy0r.title: Man Utd Injuries: Three Changes Carrick Has to Make on Premier League Return
ftbpro_01m4byk7zy0r.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer5:15 PM EDTMichael Carrick will take on former club Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. /  Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesManchester United signed off before the first international break of the season by rescuing a late draw against winless Fulham, making it five points from the first five games of 2026–27.

Michael Carrick would have hoped for more points on the board at this stage of his first full season in charge, especially after leading the Premier League in the final 16 games of the previous campaign. But he’s been keen to take the positives.

“It has been pretty fine ­margins [so far this season] that have flipped it [the wrong way],” Carrick told reporters at Craven Cottage. “I know we can do better … we need to do better at certain things. But I’m not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs.”
The Red Devils host Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford when the domestic club schedule resumes on Saturday, with Roberto De Zerbi’s team propping up the entire division.
But one of the other issues Carrick must now deal with is picking a team to win the match when the squad’s injury list swelled even more so during the international break.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

United had a handful of injuries before the international break. Amad Diallo has been missing since preseason, while Manuel Ugarte suffered a long-term injury at the World Cup. Matthijs de Ligt has not played at all in 2026 because of a back problem that eventually required surgery in May, although he has returned to training and his recovery is nearing completion.
Of that trio, only Amad has a chance of featuring in some capacity against Spurs. The Ivorian’s absence from the right flank has been felt in the early weeks of the campaign.

Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford didn’t make it to England’s camp, withdrawing after suffering injuries against Fulham. Each is expected to return for the Spurs clash but should also be considered doubts until the first concrete update post-internationals later this week.

Benjamin Šeško is in the same boat, withdrawing from Slovenia’s squad before a ball was kicked on the training field. The striker, reported to be nursing a shin injury like the one that prematurely ended his 2025–26, was missing against Fulham and has only featured as a substitute in the Premier League so far this season to help slowly ease him back into action. He has told fans he is “getting there” in terms of recovery. But even if Šeško is healthy by Saturday, it is unlikely he will start the game.

Patrick Dorgu was injured playing for Denmark. / Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesPatrick Dorgu was released by Denmark after appearing to suffer a hamstring injury in his country’s second of four internationals. He started the match in question against Wales but was forced off after 30 minutes. Noussair Mazraoui is another whose status isn’t fully known, sent home by Morocco after getting hurt against Lesotho on Sept. 29. Both are doubts to face Spurs.

If neither Karl Darlow nor Tom Heaton have recovered from what are assumed to be relatively minor problems, a place on the bench as backup goalkeeper to No. 1 Senne Lammens could go to Dermot Mee for only the second time this season.

Shea Lacey could be one to benefit. / Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesIf Mainoo is not available by Saturday, it could signal a debut for summer signing Carlos Baleba. The Cameroon international arrived injured from Brighton & Hove Albion and spent his first few weeks in Manchester recovering from that ankle problem.

Should Rashford not start, there could be an attacking reshuffle from Carrick that sees Matheus Cunha moved back to the position on the left where he spent much of last season. With Bryan Mbeumo then potentially leading the line through the center, there might be an opportunity on the right for Shea Lacey to start in the Premier League for the first time in his career.

Baleba was an unused substitute against Fulham and has had three further weeks since then to build his fitness on the training field. He ought to balance the midfield as the only true destructive force in the center of the pitch and the closest match to the departed Casemiro.
Baleba also participated in the behind-closed-doors friendly against INEOS-owned Lausanne-Sport.

The back four could remain unchanged from facing Fulham, although Leny Yoro or Ayden Heaven might be pushing for Lisandro Martínez’s place, depending on the Argentine’s condition after traveling back from South America this week. Yoro started France’s 4–1 win over Belgium on Monday for his senior international debut, but is ideally a right-sided center back.

ftbpro_01m4dbsrrg03.title: Premier League Predictions: Man City at Liverpool, Man Utd Host Tottenham
ftbpro_01m4dbsrrg03.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 9, 2026Manchester City face the music at Liverpool in their first post-guilty verdict match.  / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesAfter an agonizing three-week hiatus, the Premier League is finally back—the first round of action since Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of severe financial rule breaches.

The punishment for the eight-time Premier League winners is not yet known, but what’s guaranteed is a hostile, box-office reception when table-topping City travel to former title rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

In case you’ve forgotten about how things have played out on the field so far, here’s a quick reminder: City are being closely pursued by Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea are still finding their feet under new managers and Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are barreling toward crisis.

There have been plenty of upsets, too, with Brighton & Hove Albion, Brentford and Hull City all punching above their weight, but fewer surprises when it comes to the likes of Fulham and Crystal Palace struggling under untested Premier League coaches.
With a full weekend of action to look forward to, here’s Sports Illustrated’s predictions for Gameweek 6.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Arsenal return to action with a home fixture. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesPrediction: Arsenal 2–0 Leeds

Arsenal re-emerge with an unfamiliar feeling in the pit of their stomach. It’s been quite some time since the reigning champions were humiliated, but there’s no other way to describe their dismal 3–0 defeat to Brighton before the international break.

The Gunners had enjoyed a perfect start to the season before being deservedly thrashed on the south coast, and it’s now up to Mikel Arteta, fresh from signing a new contract, to inspire a return to winning ways.

Leeds United will be an awkward visitor in Saturday’s early kickoff. Currently fifth in the table and unbeaten in the Premier League thus far, they journey to north London brimming with belief and ready to capitalize on any uncertainty in the Arsenal ranks.

After being gutted during the summer transfer window, Aston Villa can be forgiven for taking time to adjust this season. Following three wins from their last four in all competitions, however, Unai Emery’s men appear to have hit their stride.
They’ve scored three times in each of those victories and will expect another triumph in front of the excited Villa Park faithful. It might not be forthcoming, though.

Keith Andrews continues to work miracles with Brentford, who have claimed nine points in the Premier League this season and hammered Chelsea 3–0 before the international period. They will set out to frustrate their hosts this weekend—and they might just succeed in doing so.
Chelsea are aiming to bounce back from humiliation. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesPrediction: Chelsea 3–2 Bournemouth
Brentford’s joy was Chelsea’s misery during Gameweek 5.
A weakened midfield and the absence of João Pedro proved costly at the Gtech Community Stadium, where Xabi Alonso oversaw his third consecutive league match without victory.
Chelsea’s exceptional forward line continues to instil fear in opposition backlines, but the club’s woeful defensive record undermines their progress. It’s a problem Alonso must fix soon.

Luckily for the Spaniard, he faces one of three winless sides remaining in the Premier League. Bournemouth surrendered leads in all four of their opening matches, before their profligacy cost them in the 1–0 defeat to former manager Andoni Iraola and his Liverpool team before the break.
Their last two trips to Stamford Bridge have ended in 2–2 draws. They might just miss out on another stalemate this weekend.

Gary O’Neil will be very content with six points on the board at this stage of the season, especially considering Ipswich Town have faced Manchester United and Liverpool already. The Tractor Boys have shown signs of life in chaotic wins over Sunderland and Crystal Palace.

ftbpro_01m4dcgbb5yp.title: Could Kylian Mbappe Really Leave Real Madrid in 2027?
ftbpro_01m4dcgbb5yp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath5:00 PM EDTKylian Mbappé’s future is being called into question. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesNot for the first time, Kylian Mbappé’s actions while injured have attracted criticism, while questions are now being asked about his desire to remain a Real Madrid player.
Back in spring, the superstar forward came under fire for his decision to take vacation to Sardinia with his girlfriend Ester Expósito while recovering from a hamstring issue.
Though given club permission, some fans and sections of the media took issue with the timing of the trip, which came amid a particularly trying section of the season for Madrid.
The discontent even led to an online petition calling for Mbappé to leave the club, which garnered tens of millions of online signatories.

Five months on—and despite an exceptional start to the 2026–27 season—Mbappé has riled people up once again with his antics while injured. After hyperextending his knee on international duty with France, Mbappé was allowed to recover away from Madrid.
However, Instagram images of the striker riding a bike in Switzerland—despite manager José Mourinho’s personal preferences—have been interpreted by some as Mbappé deliberately acting out.

Seemingly such a seemingly innocuous incident barely worthy of stopping your scroll let alone serious news coverage quickly blew up in the Spanish press, with MARCA vox popping fans for their take on “bicycle-gate.”

L’Équipe say that some people close to Madrid are “criticizing Mbappé for not keeping a low enough profile,” adding that Mourinho asked his player to be “more discreet” in his communication style—without going into specifics of what that means exactly.
The incident has added fuel to bubbling rumors of Mbappé’s long-term unhappiness in the Spanish capital after two turbulent, trophy-free years.

RMC journalist Daniel Riolo is among those to have questioned his motivation levels, sensationally claiming a parting of the ways between the world’s biggest club and player at the end of the season “cannot be ruled out.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Kylian Mbappé doesn’t have a whole lot of options. / David S. Bustamante/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesAssuming at least one of Mbappé or Madrid did want a change at the end of the season, a transfer would not be an easy lift.

Mbappé has flirted with other clubs in the past and regularly talks up his mother’s love of Liverpool. However, he remains under contract at the Bernabéu until the summer of 2029, and is Europe’s highest-paid soccer player on a reported salary of around €30 million ($33 million) per year.

According to soccer financials site Capology, Liverpool’s current highest-paid player is captain Virgil van Dijk on £18.2 million ($24 million) a year and Mbappé’s arrival would require a massive, financial-structure breaking outlay.

In reality, the number of clubs that could accommodate the World Cup top scorer’s wages as well as a nine-figure transfer fee is vanishingly small in today’s market—with Madrid and his former club PSG, perhaps the only European options able to.

In theory, Mbappé would be a huge prize for the Saudi Pro League, where finances would be less of an issue. However, it feels unlikely that a player openly chasing the Ballon d’Or and a first Champions League title would opt to leave Europe in the prime of his career. He already turned it down in 2023.

Mbappé has seven goals in as many La Liga games in 2026-27. / JOSE JORDAN/AFP/Getty ImagesDespite the regular talk of unrest, Mbappé retains the “unwavering support of president Florentino Pérez” according to L’Équipe.
The president is known to be a fan of the forward and spent a decade trying to land him.

After 94 goals in 111 games and two Pichichi trophies, Mbappé has dazzled as a galáctico but not yet clicked in a great Real Madrid team. Abandoning the Mbappé project now would be a major loss of face for Pérez, who tends to forcefully resist the option of selling superstars when still at the peak of their playing and commercial powers.

ftbpro_01m4de7dsxza.title: Man City Legend Makes Shock Return to Football After 3-Year Retirement
ftbpro_01m4de7dsxza.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:00 AM EDTDavid Silva is heading back to the pitch. / Laurence Griffiths/Getty ImagesFormer Manchester City midfielder David Silva has come out of retirement at the age of 40 to join Hong Kong side Supreme Sha Tin, but only for one game.

Silva, widely hailed as one of the greatest playmakers of his generation, won four Premier League titles with City and the 2010 World Cup with Spain among many other trophies, but retired in the summer of 2023 just days after suffering a serious knee injury.

After three years out of the spotlight, Silva is heading to the Hong Kong Premier League, where the increasingly ambitious Supreme Sha Tin announced his signing with a statement that opened with: “Yo! Absolute madness!”
The news came as a significant surprise, with many questioning the logic behind Silva’s latest career move.
After Silva’s move to Sha Tin was announced, the legendary midfielder appeared on COPE to answer some of the many questions sent his way.
Silva quickly ruled out the prospect of a career resurgence, instead insisting he has only signed on to play a single match with the team.
“They reported it as if I’d signed for the whole season, but no, in the end I’m only going to play one game,” Silva stressed.

The 40-year-old also laughed off suggestions that he is simply chasing money, adding: “People are quick to pull the trigger at the slightest provocation, but that’s not the case here. I’ve been doing well thanks to my father and my advisor of 20 years, with whom we’ve invested wisely.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Silva owns a winery in his native Gran Canaria, Bodegas Tamerán, and has already ruled out a long-term return to the world of soccer in favor of focusing on the wine business.

Sha Tin, who failed with an approach for former Chelsea and Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata earlier this summer, did appear to hint at the possibility that their agreement with Silva will only be a brief one.
“The Spanish maestro will first suit up for one match,” the club added, seemingly hoping that Silva could choose to extend his stay in Hong Kong if all goes to plan.

Silva’s appearance for Sha Tin looks to have been booked in for Nov. 7, when the club are due to host Hong Kong Rangers in a league fixture, although player-owner Jim Wong Chi-chuen told the South China Morning Post that, if Silva can prove his fitness, the game against Hong Kong Football Club on Oct. 18 could be an earlier target.

ftbpro_01m4dgj88670.title: Pep Guardiola Set for Man City Return After Guilty Verdict
ftbpro_01m4dgj88670.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer10:00 AM EDTPep Guardiola is coming back to visit. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesPep Guardiola continues to ally himself with Manchester City in the wake of the club’s guilty verdict for breaking Premier League financial regulations.

Guardiola stepped away as manager after 10 years with City at the end of last season. He maintained public support for the club throughout the Premier League’s investigation and independent panel hearing. The Spaniard also maintains a close working connection with the club as a global ambassador for the wider City Football Group parent company.

Guardiola has not attended a City match this season, but BBC Sport reported that is expected to change next week when back-to-back reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain visit the Etihad Stadium. Guardiola is set to be there as a spectator, cheering for his former team like the 50,000–60,000 or so other supporters.

In what will be City’s first home match since the verdict and the Premier League’s statement referring to “sham” contracts and close to a decade of sustained financial cheating—which the club continues to fiercely deny—it is a significant show of support from the former boss.
It remains to be seen if he will spectate from the shadows or be paraded in the spotlight.

When the verdict was formally published last week, Guardiola took to social media to firmly make clear his position on the matter. “I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever,” he posted on Instagram, alongside a picture of himself with long-serving club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

“I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

When he was preparing for his final game as manager in May, Guardiola had said of the club and the conduct of those above him: “I trust them. I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did. What happened, happened.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

The majority the charges related to a time before Guardiola was appointed in 2016, with the first accusation of financial cheating dating back to the 2009–10 campaign. But the Spaniard ended up being the main beneficiary, equipped with an expensively-assembled team that became the first in the history of English soccer to achieve 100 points in a season.

There is no suggestion that Guardiola, his coaching team or players did anything wrong, going about their daily jobs on the training field and on the pitch. But his and their successes, even that which came in the seasons that followed the 2009–2018 period—including an unprecedented four in a row, cannot be separated from what was going on behind the scenes, because the financial conduct was what made all of that possible.

The way City went about business, against the Premier League’s rules with the “sham” contracts artificially driving up revenue and increasing spending power, provided the platform from which Guardiola created his dynasty.
For him to deviate from anything other than full public support would be to admit there is an asterisk on everything he achieved.
