ftbpro_01m4dhdpc2y6.title: ‘How It Has to Be’—Cole Palmer’s England Hopes Scuppered by New Tuchel Outburst
ftbpro_01m4dhdpc2y6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:30 AM EDTCole Palmer is under real pressure. / Harvey Murphy/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFor all the excitement Cole Palmer generates at Chelsea, it is safe to say his reputation with the England national team is lagging behind.

Having already seen fitness cost him valuable chances to impress England manager Thomas Tuchel in the past, this September-October window felt like a turning point when Palmer was called up to the roster. “I think he has a point to prove,” Tuchel said.
Just days later, Palmer was heading back to Chelsea. No formal explanation for his withdrawal was ever given but reports at the time put it down to the cryptic idea of “load management.”

While Palmer was resting up at home, he could only watch on as all those in front of him in the pecking order raised their reputations even higher. The Three Lions scored 14 goals in just four matches, catching the eye with a flair that has not been seen with England in years.
Forcing his way back into Tuchel’s thinking is not going to be easy, particularly after the England boss admitted the “train is rolling” without Palmer.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
“It’s always like this,” Tuchel said when asked whether those that were not with the England squad this break had fallen down the pecking order. “This is how it has to be.

“Everyone should be eager to come, desperate to come because the train is rolling and full credit to the players who bought into that. It can only work like this. We can only put our full energy into the camp and the players who are in camp make the camp special. This will never change.”
Asked how Palmer or Manchester City’s Phil Foden, who was not selected for the squad in the first place, fit into England’s future, Tuchel was equally blunt.
“I don’t know, is the honest answer,” he said. “They are not here. This team took another step and it’s always about the guys who are here.”

The bar for Palmer is higher than ever. / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesIf it was not already clear from previous international windows, Tuchel is a manager that is more than happy to rely on a trusted group of players. If you perform well in an England shirt, your form at club level becomes secondary.
That works in the opposite direction, too. Tuchel has openly admitted that Foden’s failure to impress on England duty continues to work against the 26-year-old, and the same goes for Palmer.

Tuchel’s faith in Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon, Bukayo Saka and Morgan Rogers is clear. As it stands, it is Arsenal’s Eberechi Eze and Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha who have played their way into reserve roles—the latter called up largely after impressing Tuchel during the summer and not because of his 37 minutes across the Reds’ last four Premier League games.
For Palmer, the mission is clear. If he wants to get back into the England squad, he is going to have to put up the sort of numbers that would make him impossible to ignore.

“Cole has his numbers back, assists, decisive goals ... ” Tuchel said when Palmer was called up. He wants Chelsea’s superstar to be winning games, flexing his quality and enjoying himself on the pitch like he was in the first few weeks of the season before things turned sour for the Blues.

When Palmer is at his best, he is exactly that sort of player. He was unstoppable during the first few weeks of the season, bringing back memories of the youngster that ended the 2023–24 campaign with 27 goals and 15 assists across all competitions.

The argument Palmer will make is that, by prioritizing his body over the past three weeks, he will be capable of becoming that player once again. The toll a groin injury took last season is no secret—Palmer said he “had one leg for 10 months, f---ing hell,”—and something did look off about his performance in the 3–0 defeat to Brentford before the international break.

If he has caught an injury early and rested his way back to full fitness, Palmer’s withdrawal from the England squad will look like a stroke of genius, but it is only going to pay off if he becomes the guy again. Anything less will not be good enough in Tuchel’s eyes.

ftbpro_01m4dj7fcn3y.title: 5 Storylines to Watch When the Premier League Returns
ftbpro_01m4dj7fcn3y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 8, 2026Liverpool host table-toppers Man City on Sunday. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesAs far as international periods go, this extended three-week break was one of the more entertaining. Regardless, it’s wonderful to see the Premier League return this weekend.
October’s first taste of top-flight action brings with it some tantalizing duels up and down the country. It’s the perfect reward for our patience during club soccer’s lengthy hiatus.
Naturally, the division’s big-hitters will steal focus, especially with two fixtures staged between traditional ‘Big Six’ sides. There are awkward clashes for Arsenal and Chelsea, too.
With that in mind, here are five storylines to keep an eye on during Gameweek 6 of the Premier League campaign.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Arsenal suffered their first defeat of the season before the break. / Clive Rose/Getty ImagesExactly five months separated Arsenal’s previous Premier League defeat and their shock implosion at Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break. A perfect start to the new season was smashed to smithereens on the south coast during a humbling and deserved 3–0 loss.

Given just how excellent the Gunners have been over the past year, they can be forgiven for having an off-day. After all, Brighton are more than capable of upsetting the odds with their high-octane pressing and raft of unassuming stars.
But Arsenal’s response will be definitive. Will they make an immediate recovery? Or will uncertainty linger?

Leeds United are hardly ideal visitors to the Emirates Stadium this Saturday having made an unbeaten start to the season. They’re currently fifth and just three points behind Mikel Arteta’s men, as well as one of just two teams to have actually conceded fewer than Arsenal’s usually watertight defense.
History suggests Arsenal will be fine, though. They have won their last eight matches against Leeds across all competitions, scoring 13 times during the three most recent triumphs.

Xabi Alonso has failed to win his last three league games. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesChelsea joined Arsenal in suffering a humiliating 3–0 defeat on the road during Gameweek 5. Brentford were their conquerors as Xabi Alonso’s weakened side self-destructed late in proceedings at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Unlike Arsenal, however, this was not a one-off for Chelsea. In fact, it was their third successive league match without victory, as well as the third time they have conceded three goals in a match this season.
It’s Alonso’s defense that continues to undermine his progress in the Stamford Bridge dugout and Bournemouth will prove no pushovers this Saturday, either.

Marco Rose’s side might be winless in the Premier League, but the Cherries have taken points off Chelsea in four of the last six matches between the sides. With the likes of Evanilson, Rayan and Marcus Tavernier in their offense, they will capitalize on any rustiness in the home defense.

Chelsea have injury issues to contend with, too, as a host of important first-team faces await late fitness tests. Alonso is sweating over the fitness of João Pedro, Cole Palmer, Moisés Caicedo and Reece James for Bournemouth’s visit—four crucial assets whose absences could prove decisive.

Man Utd are coming under increasing scrutiny. / Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty ImagesManchester United supporters have been forced to endure familiar struggles at the start of the new season. The summer’s midfield rebuild and positivity manufactured by last term’s impressive resurgence under Michael Carrick offered hope to the Old Trafford faithful before a ball was kicked. Unfortunately, the Red Devils have reverted to type.
But things could be worse for the club’s fanbase—they could support Tottenham Hotspur.

Spurs have been in crisis for quite some time after narrowly avoiding relegation last season and starting the current campaign in similarly worrying form. A trip to Old Trafford this weekend appears likely to end in yet more misery for Roberto De Zerbi and his players.
Both sides enter the upcoming clash under significant pressure and the loser—if there is one—is certain to come under unbearable scrutiny.

Tottenham need the points more. They’re currently bottom of the Premier League table following two goalless draws and three dreadful defeats, with their army of expensive new signings failing to deliver early in their Spurs careers.

ftbpro_01m4djwxq8ez.title: Real Madrid Predicted Lineup vs. Villarreal: Injuries Aren’t Mourinho’s Only Issue
ftbpro_01m4djwxq8ez.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath2:00 PM EDTMadrid have a 100% home record so far this season. /  M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesThe international break is over and Real Madrid return to action with a point to prove.
The hiatus came at an inopportune moment for José Mourinho and his men who have been left to stew on their Madrid derby defeat for three whole weeks.
The honeymoon period is definitively over for Mourinho, who now finds himself fighting to make up a six-point gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona, while managing a number of issues within the club.

The visit of last season’s third-placed finishers Villarreal to the Bernabéu is a chance to keep up their 100% home record while quietening some of the doubting voices ahead of a key period in the calendar.
Here’s how Real Madrid could line up for this La Liga encounter.

ftbpro_01m4dm878h2s.title: ‘Who Knows What Else?’—Former Man City Star Fuels Uncertainty With Shock Claim
ftbpro_01m4dm878h2s.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:00 AM EDTManuel Akanji is nervously watching. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesFormer Manchester City center back Manuel Akanji has admitted he fears being stripped of the two Premier League titles he won with the club between 2022 and 2025 as he refused to rule out more rule breaches from the Cityzens.

City have been found guilty of breaking a large number of the Premier League’s financial rules between 2009 and 2018—four years before Akanji joined the club—and are still awaiting a punishment, which could include stripping City of the trophies won during that period.

The trophies won after the period in question, while built on questionable foundations, are not thought to be in danger, although Akanji confessed he could not rule out his own period at the Etihad Stadium attracting further scrutiny.

“I hope I don’t lose my titles,” said Akanji, who swapped City for Inter Milan this summer after spending last season on loan with the Italian side. “That would be a bit of a shame. But I only see everything in the news.”
Asked whether he felt his titles were in genuine danger, Akanji added: “Who knows what else they’ll find out. You’re still looking for things related to Corona that happened five years ago.”
Akanji’s final line was in reference to the recent investigation into Switzerland teammate Granit Xhaka, who admitted last month to obtaining a fake Covid-19 vaccination certificate back in 2022.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Akanji won two Premier League titles with Man City. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesCity have appealed the guilty verdict against them and hope to be proven innocent. If successful, that would end the fear of any punishment whatsoever.

However, if City are unsuccessful, they are expected to face enormous sanctions. Those could range anywhere from fines to points deductions and, crucially, stripping City of the titles won during the period in question.

It would appear that Akanji’s titles won during his later period with the club are safe, but the concern for City is that the Premier League rules also include the ability for the league to dish out “such other penalty as it shall think fit.”

The Premier League are, in essence, permitted to apply any punishment deemed suitable for the crime. If league officials decide City’s successes since 2018 is also tainted by what came before, they have the power to wipe more from the record.

At this point, the early suggestions are that any punishments would be forward-thinking, rather than looking back at the past, but until the appeal verdict comes in, Akanji is one of many simply left in the dark.
“We were told to remain calm, that they had everything under control, that nothing major had happened,” Akanji concluded. “I trust the people in charge at Man City that this is true.”

ftbpro_01m4dn4m67jz.title: ‘Recover in Time—Andoni Iraola Hints at Potential Liverpool Striker Crisis
ftbpro_01m4dn4m67jz.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer10:00 AM EDTAlexander Isak and Cody Gakpo have carried the flag this season. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images (Isak), Liverpool FC/Getty Images (Gakpo)Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo are “both injured” as Liverpool prepare to return to Premier League action this weekend with a pointed game against Manchester City at Anfield.

Manager Andoni Iraola has not ruled either player out of contention, but each man is a doubt and this is potentially the price of the September-October international window for the Reds. Center back Jérémy Jacquet is also coming back to Merseyside with an injury.

Liverpool are still finding their way under the guidance of Iraola, a step away from Arne Slot and back towards a more ‘Jürgen Klopp’ style of soccer. The Reds remain unbeaten across all competitions seven games into the new era, yet have drawn the majority of their league fixtures.

Isak and Gakpo are two players who have carried the flag in the opening weeks of the season. The Swedish striker has netted four goals in the Premier League, already better than his tally from his entire 2025–26, while the Dutchman has overcome his own disappointing form and immense personal strife to perform with impressive consistency so far in 2026–27.
Both returned early from international duty.

“Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo both have had to leave the national teams with injuries. Now it’s a matter of if they are going to recover in time to help us in the next game or not,” Iraola told beIN SPORTS in the days leading up to hosting Manchester City.
“Right now, they are both injured,” the Spaniard concluded.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Crucially, there is time for that to change, but it also doesn’t offer much confidence that either at this stage can be considered more than a doubt to play.

Isak was seen with a bloody toe after scoring in Sweden’s Sept. 25 win over Romania, before pulling out of the squad. But it wasn’t the toe that was the cause of the problem, with manager Graham Potter putting the decision down to a minor thigh issue. “Given the number of matches we have in a short period, it’s not feasible [to keep him in the squad],” Potter said.

Gakpo started for the Netherlands against Germany and Serbia in September, scoring a late equalizer against the former. But he lasted only 17 minutes in the match with the latter because of an ankle concern and had to be withdrawn.

Lewis Koumas is in line to start if Isak and Gakpo cannot. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesIraola has a headache if Isak is ruled out because Liverpool don’t have another true No. 9 in the first-team squad. Hugo Ekitiké remains sidelined with the Achilles injury he suffered in April and cost him his place at the 2026 World Cup. Gakpo would ordinarily be a sound option to step in at center forward were he too not also potentially going to miss the match.
In the only game so far this season that Isak hasn’t started—the Carabao Cup victory over Tottenham Hotspur on Sept. 15—Iraola used Lewis Koumas in the No. 9 role.

Koumas, although not a stranger to playing centrally, has seen most of his minutes for Liverpool and loan clubs Hull City, Birmingham City and Stoke City over the past two years in wide positions—particularly the left. It would be a huge ask of the 21-year-old to start up front against a Manchester City side in red-hot form, even with the shadow of the Premier League verdict.
Koumas did replace Isak for the final few minutes against Bournemouth.

Liverpool’s only other striker is academy graduate Jayden Danns, who is nursing a suspected hamstring injury. The locally born 20-year-old, who would alleviate any danger of the Reds losing a piece of club history in the wake of Curtis Jones’s summer exit, was on the bench for the Champions League win over Atlético Madrid, but his last first-team appearance was more than a year ago in the Carabao Cup against Southampton in September 2025.

ftbpro_01m4drtjda17.title: The Two International Games Lionel Messi Played Against Cristiano Ronaldo
ftbpro_01m4drtjda17.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath4:00 PM EDTArgentina vs. Portugal is a rare fixture. / PA Images via Getty ImagesStories about Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have dominated the international break, with the former calling time on his Argentina career and the latter seemingly on the brink of ending his with Portugal.

While Messi is definitively retired, Ronaldo’s story remains up in the air for now. Regardless, it will not be much longer before the two greats of the modern game are being talked about only in the past tense.

Messi and Ronaldo’s rivalry defined an age in soccer. At club level, they faced off regularly for Barcelona and Real Madrid in La Liga and the Champions League. Yet curiously, in 442 collective international appearances, the two players only met twice—and never in a competitive fixture.
Much to the chagrin of many World Cup organizers and sponsors, Portugal and Argentina never crossed paths once between the years 2006 and 2026, when both players were active at the tournament.

The closest they came to a showdown in six World Cups came in 2018 when Portugal and Argentina would’ve met in the quarterfinal in Nizhny Novgorod, but both teams ended up losing their preceding Round of 16 fixtures against Uruguay and France, respectively.
In the end, the only times Messi and Ronaldo ever played one another at international level was in two exhibition matches in 2011 and 2014.

The first meeting of Ronaldo and Messi was a thriller. / Ben Radford/Corbis/Getty ImagesArgentina Starting XI: Romero; Znetti, Burdisso, Milito, Rojo; Banega, Cambiasso, Mascherano; Di María, Lavezzi, Messi (Subs: Gago, Zabaleta, Pastore, Biglia, Martinez)
Portugal Starting XI: Eduardo; Pereria, Alves, Rolando, Coentrão; Martins, Moutinho, Meireles; Nani, Almeida, Ronaldo (Subs: Patrício, Danny, Postiga, Quaresma, Veloso, Machado)
The first meeting of the pair came at the height of their Barcelona-Real Madrid glory years.

Already a Champions League winner with Barça, Messi would end the 2010-11 campaign with Europe’s biggest trophy once again, as well as his third successive Ballon d’Or. Meanwhile, Ronaldo was on course for a staggering season of scoring with 53 goals and 54 games under José Mourinho.
The glamorous, money-spinning battle of world’s best took place during the February international break in Geneva of all places, with Messi coming out on top in a thrilling back-and-forth encounter.
Next. Greatest Soccer of All Time. The Greatest Soccer Players of All Time. dark

The Argentina star threaded through the pass for Ángel Di María for his side’s opener after quarter of an hour. While Ronaldo equalized shortly after, the night belonged to Messi who won the match from the penalty spot late in the second half.
Speaking after the match Messi tried to play down the rivalry, saying: “This wasn’t a game between Barcelona and Real Madrid or between Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.
“We don't compete with each other to see who is the better player, we do so for the benefit of our teams.”

The two superstars played just 45 minutes in Manchester. / Laurence Griffiths/Getty ImagesArgentina Starting XI: Romero; Roncaglia, Otamendi, Demichelis, Ansaldi; Mascherano, Biglia; Messi, Pastore, Di María; Higuaín (Subs: Gaitán, Lamela, Tevez, Pereyra, Silva)
Portugal Starting XI: Beto; Bosingwa, Alves, Pepe, Gomes; Nani, Mendes, Gomes, Moutinho; Danny, Ronaldo (Subs: Fonte, Guerreiro, Carvalho, Silva, Quaresma, Éder)
Almost four years later, Messi and Ronaldo lined up against one another again for another eye-catching exhibition—this time at Old Trafford in Manchester.

Going into the match, Ronaldo was on the ascendency as the Ballon d’Or holder and fresh from Real Madrid’s first Champions League crown in 12 years. Messi, meanwhile, had won the Golden Ball at the 2014 World Cup as the tournament’s best player, but left Brazil a beaten finalist.

The match itself was a little piece of history, but not an entertaining one. Ultimately a drab affair, it was decided by stoppage-time header from substitute Raphaël Guerreiro long after the two men the majority of the fans had come to see had already left the pitch.

paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 9, 2026Arsenal return from the international break looking for revenge. / Visionhaus/Getty Images.Arsenal have a point to prove when they return from the international break to face Leeds United in the Premier League on Saturday.

The Gunners were humiliated in their final outing before club soccer’s hiatus as they suffered a shock 3–0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion. The bruising loss brought their perfect start to the season to a conclusion and allowed Manchester City to leapfrog them in the standings.

Mikel Arteta, who has recently penned a contract extension with Arsenal, will demand significant improvements at the Emirates Stadium in the first of six matches before the end of October. While there might be one eye on the Champions League tie with Lille next Tuesday, any complacency this weekend will be punished by an in-form Leeds side.

The Yorkshire outfit are unbeaten during their opening five Premier League matches and begin the upcoming round of fixtures in fifth place. Clearly inspired by Arsenal, defense has been key to the club’s swift start, with no team having conceded fewer than the three goals they have allowed thus far.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Arsenal should bounce back immediately. / Francesco Scaccianoce/UEFA/Getty ImagesBrighton gave Arsenal a bloody nose before the international period, exactly five months on from the club’s last Premier League defeat. But, as good champions do, the Gunners should return to winning ways at the first time of asking.
Leeds will prove an awkward visitor and one capable of springing a surprise with their direct counter-attacking style, but Arsenal, especially with home advantage, should overpower them.

Even with several injury concerns ahead of the clash, Arteta can call upon a raft of superstars in every department. The Spaniard will be certain to tighten things up defensively after being outsmarted by Brighton and those solid foundations will give the likes of Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard the freedom to strut their stuff.

Arteta will have been cursing his luck during the international period, with Ezri Konsa, Kai Havertz, Christos Tzolis and Max Dowman all withdrawing form their respective rosters early due to fitness issues.

Konsa’s dead leg is expected to heal in time for the Leeds match, where he should start alongside Gabriel. Elsewhere at center back, William Saliba remains sidelined and Cristhian Mosquera could miss out again.

Tzolis and Havertz could well be absent in the forward line, opening the door for Eberechi Eze to line up on the left wing and Viktor Gyökeres to lead the line. The latter is in strong form after scoring in all four of Sweden’s UEFA Nations League matches.

Declan Rice missed the international window with England, but he’s expected to feature in midfield alongside either Myles Lewis-Skelly or Bruno Guimarães. With Ben White still a doubt at right back, Jurriën Timber should start a second consecutive match.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Leeds (4-2-3-1): Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Saka, Ødegaard, Eze; Gyökeres.

Leeds endured just one casualty over the break, with summer recruit Jean-Mattéo Bahoya leaving France’s Under-21s prematurely after spraining his ankle. However, Farke has confirmed there’s a “chance that he is available” for the Arsenal trip.

Harry Wilson should make his comeback after returning to team training on Tuesday. He missed the chance to team up with Wales over the break due to a thigh problem. Wilson’s compatriot Dan James will be absent, however, after sustaining a back injury on international duty. He’s joined another Wales international, Joe Rodon, in the treatment room.

Farke could name an identical team to the one that drew with Crystal Palace before the break, with a forward partnership of Noah Okafor and Dominic Calvert-Lewin essential to Leeds coming away from north London with a point or more.
Leeds predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (3-5-2): Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemović; Bogle, Stach, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Calvert-Lewin, Okafor.

ftbpro_01m4dy3kqk15.title: Gio Reyna, Claudio Reyna Add Another Family Member to U.S. Soccer Dynasty
ftbpro_01m4dy3kqk15.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell1:00 PM EDTThe Reynas are continuing their story with U.S. Soccer. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images (Gio), @carolinaareynaaa on Instagram (Carolina), Dale MacMillan/Soccrates/Getty Images (Claudio)The Reyna legacy for the Stars and Stripes is continuing beyond U.S. men’s national team legend Claudio and his son, Gio. 17-year-old Carolina Reyna will soon be donning the Stars and Stripes on the world stage.

Carolina was named to Ciara Crinion’s squad for the 2026 U-17 Women’s World Cup, where the U.S. is hoping to top the competition for the first time this fall. The team is set to take on Samoa, Kenya and China PR in Group E.

For Carolina, it’s a rather full-circle moment. At 10 years old, she watched her older brother, Gio, compete for the Stars and Stripes at the 2019 U-17 World Cup in Brazil. Now, it is her turn to forge her own path at the tournament—and make a little history in the process

Carolina and Gio are the first-ever brother and sister to represent the U.S. at the U-17 showpiece event. Carolina will hope to get further than her brother, given the men’s U-17 side crashed out in the group stage seven years ago.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The pressure is on Carolina to not only contribute but also live up to the name on the back of her shirt. But she’s well used to that by now. The teenager, who has represented the Stars and Stripes from the U-15 through the U-17 levels, took home the Golden Boot at the 2024 Concacaf Girls’ U-15 Championship.

She also is already committed to play collegiate soccer at the University of North Carolina in 2027, following in the footsteps of her mother Danielle, who starred for the Tar Heels and eventually represented the U.S. women’s national team at the senior level (six caps).
The path is set for Carolina, and there’s no better time to officially announce herself than on the world stage in Morocco.

While most kids her age are worried about high school classes and college applications, Carolina’s focus is on a women’s World Cup. Even at the youth level, the stakes of the tournament are higher than ever before, especially for players who want to catch the attention of USWNT manager Emma Hayes.
Throw in Carolina’s family ties, and a unique, massive adventure awaits.

“It’s an incredible honor to be able to represent the United States and for me and my teammates to be able to compete against the best teams in the world,” the midfielder told FIFA. “We know that it will be a once in a lifetime experience for all of us.

“It’s super incredible to be able to follow in my dad and brother’s World Cup path for the U.S. and to be the first-ever brother-sister duo to be able to compete at a U-17 World Cup is also super incredible,” Carolina added.

When asked what she’s most looking forward to, Carolina embraced the entire experience looming for her and her teammates. “On the field, I am looking forward to competing against countries we have never played before, give everything for our team and have a strong successful tournament,” she said.
“Off the field, it’s going to be amazing to experience a beautiful country like Morocco with my teammates and coaches and the rest of our staff there.”

Gio Reyna is enjoying his resurgence with the USMNT. / Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesIt’s a rare advantage for Carolina to be so close to a brother who has gone through all the ups and downs of representing the U.S. Gio went from being a wonderkid to an afterthought and now back to a starter for the USMNT, all while she came up through the ranks of the women’s youth system.

After a very public scandal involving the Reyna family and previous USMNT manager Gregg Berhalter, Gio fall out of favor with the Stars and Stripes, all while his club career took a downward spiral. New boss Mauricio Pochettino believed in the 23-year-old, though, and brought him along to the 2026 World Cup, where Gio bagged a sensational trivela goal in the team’s 4–1 win over Paraguay.
Next. Gio Reyna Feature on Family Drama. Once at Center of Drama, Gio Reyna Is Writing Different Story. dark

“Being able to experience watching him play at a World Cup this summer and at his U-17 World Cup in person, it’s super cool to have that role model so close to me,” Carolina said, “and learning how much hard work and dedication it takes to reach the highest level and to continue to develop even at the highest level.”

Although the 2026 World Cup ended in a humiliating round of 16 exit against Belgium, the future is bright for the USMNT, and Gio’s resurgence plays a large role in the team’s success. The American, who joined French side Strasbourg this summer, started all four of the Stars and Stripes’ friendlies this fall and tallied two assists across four convincing wins.
With the September-October international break officially done and dusted, the Reyna family can now switch their attention to Carolina and the U.S. women’s plight in Morocco.

The Gunners were grateful for club soccer’s hiatus following their disastrous 3–0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion last time out, which marked their first loss of the season in any competition. Mikel Arteta, who has just penned a contract extension with the club, will demand an emphatic response.

The Spaniard will have some tough decisions to make in the search for three points, though. Already without several injured players before the international break, he’s been dealt further setbacks over recent weeks.
With that in mind, here’s how Arsenal could line up this weekend.

ftbpro_01m4e1bk2b67.title: Harry Kane’s MLS Future Gets a Boost From League Commissioner
ftbpro_01m4e1bk2b67.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas3:30 PM EDTHarry Kane is still one of the world’s best players.  / Alex Pantling/The FA/Getty Images Major League Soccer commissioner Don Garber revealed that Harry Kane showing an interest in one day joining MLS represents “the fulfillment of a dream.”

Kane recently revealed he wants to look at the possibility of one day becoming an NFL kicker “a bit more seriously.” The Bayern Munich striker admitted this potential future career depends on different factors, but did state that moving to MLS would be favorable for his ambitious long-term goal.

An argument can be made that Kane is currently the best player in the world—certainly the best, most complete striker. For Garber, the England international simply mentioning MLS as a potential destination is incredibly meaningful.

“I’d love for him to do that,” Garber said about Kane’s NFL dreams, via ESPN. “I think, for me, it is the fulfillment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

“We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say ‘I’d kind of like to play in MLS.’ And I think Messi proved that. That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barça, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Harry Kane is close to extending his stint in Munich.  / Alexandra Beier/AFP/Getty Images As much as Kane might consider becoming the latest big-name player to cross the Atlantic Ocean to join MLS, it’s unlikely it happens any time soon.

Yes, his current Bayern Munich contract expires at the end of the season, but Kane recently admitted a renewal agreement is “fairly close.” Sky Germany report an agreement in principle for Kane to sign a new contract with Bayern until 2029 has been reached.

Kane is coming off a 73-goal 2025–26 season for club and country and is among the favorites to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or award. At 33, he’s showing no signs of slowing down, and it’s clear that his current focus remains in producing for one of the best teams in Europe.
But things can change three seasons from now in the summer of 2029. Kane will be 36 by then, which is the exact same age Messi was when he bid farewell to Europe and joined Inter Miami in 2023.
If the reports are true and Kane does ink a new three-year deal, then MLS fans could be forced to wait until that agreement expires for the Englishman to seriously consider a move to North America.

Don Garber is entering the final months of his tenure as MLS commissioner.  / Getty ImagesNobody knows MLS’s ins-and-outs better than Garber, who’s been league commissioner since 1999—the second longest tenured commissioner in major U.S. sports leagues. MLS has grown leaps and bounds during his tenure, going from an almost experimental league to a division that attracts some of the biggest names in the sport. But Garber knows there’s still plenty of room for improvement.

“We just went from a country road, now we’re getting onto the highway,” Garber said. “And we’ve got to get better. We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games.
“Miami won one. Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world.”

After 27 years, Garber will step down as MLS commissioner at the turn of the year to assume a new role as league chairman. He’ll hope the foundations he helped build to boost MLS’s reputation will continue to attract players of Kane’s caliber.

ftbpro_01m4e38jcjx5.title: ‘No Matter What Happens’—Haaland Breaks Silence on Man City’s Guilty Verdict
ftbpro_01m4e38jcjx5.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell2:30 PM EDTErling Haaland is keeping his focus on the present with Manchester City. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesErling Haaland had a rousing message for Manchester City fans in the wake of the Premier League’s sweeping guilty verdict: “We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive.”

For three years, City were under investigation for breaching the competition’s financial regulations. The club was ultimately found guilty of 114 of 115 charges, all related to infractions committed between the 2009–10 and 2017–18 seasons.

City compiled “sham” contracts and agreements to inflate revenue and reduce costs by £900 million ($1.2 billion). Still, they maintain their innocence and already launched an official appeal, dragging on the saga even further and delaying potential punishments that could see the 10-time English champions vacate titles or be relegated.

The scandal has left the club, the players and the fans in a state of disarray and uncertainty, but Haaland is trying to keep spirits high—an already tough job made even harder by a trip to Anfield looming this weekend.

“No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile,” Haaland added after encouraging the fans to stick together. “So we have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game.”

He then repeated the phrase ”stick together” twice more, as if he was trying to convince himself as well as the fans, before adding, “We have to spread the love to each other ... and enjoy the ride and smile.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Liverpool are still searching for a signature win this season. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside/Getty ImagesFor the neutral fan, it couldn’t be written any better: the first team City must play since the guilty verdict is Liverpool. Oh, and the clash will unfold at Anfield.

As if the fixture needed any more stakes, the Reds are one of three clubs that could retrospectively win the Premier League in the unlikely event City are stripped of their titles. Liverpool finished as the runners-up in 2013–14, 2018–19 and 2021–22.

“It’s always special to play against Liverpool, especially with Pep [Guardiola] and [Jürgen] Klopp,” Haaland said. “I remember sitting in Salzburg and Dortmund and watching the games, how much they pushed each other. It’s always special games there.
"I won there, I drew there, I lost. So it’s always special, and every Premier League game is different, and every game against Liverpool is always special.”
City came out on top in both Premier League clashes with Liverpool last season, winning by an aggregate score of 5–1. The Cityzens also demolished Arne Slot’s men 4–0 in the FA Cup quarterfinals.

This time, Andoni Iraola is the man in the dugout at Anfield, searching for his first signature win since taking over Liverpool. Taking any points from the encounter would be seen as a success, considering City remain the only perfect team in the league.

Erling Haaland (center) is off to another brilliant start for City. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesWith what could be a lengthy appeal process underway, Haaland and his teammates are keeping focus on the current season. After losing the Community Shield to Arsenal, City have strung together seven straight victories across all competitions under the leadership of Enzo Maresca.

As always, Haaland has been at the center of the club’s success. The Norway international already has seven goals in as many appearances in 2026–27. He then added three more to his tally during the international break.

Losing Haaland would be a worse punishment than some sanctions looming over City. The No. 9 is critical to the team’s success, as evidenced by the massive nine-and-a-half-year contract extension he signed in January 2025.

But if the team’s appeal fails and its guilty verdict gets upheld, Haaland might have no choice but to leave the Etihad Stadium for a new home, especially if City get relegated. Real Madrid and Barcelona’s interest in the 26-year-old is well-documented, and other clubs throughout Europe would jump at the chance to sign the best striker in the game.

It’s hard for City fans to follow Haaland’s request to “stay positive” when this entire scandal could end with him—and other superstars in sky blue—leaving. The silver lining is that reality is likely far down the line.

ftbpro_01m4e3q0edd5.title: FIFA’s World Rankings After Fall Window: Portugal Rises As Brazil, Germany Sink
ftbpro_01m4e3q0edd5.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTPortugal rose in the standings after four straight wins. / Joao Gregorio/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThere were more matches than usual across an extended three-week international window and that has resulted in movement in FIFA’s world rankings.
Countries from Europe, Africa and the Americas were in competitive action over the break, but many nations also spent their time traversing the globe to compete in friendlies.

There was a healthy balance of high-profile clashes—predominantly in Europe—and lesser-seen matchups, such as Brazil’s first-ever battle with India and Argentina’s maiden clash against Benin in what was Lionel Messi’s farewell match.

At its most basic, FIFA rankings are determined by the outcome of a country’s matches. Nations have a running points total which gets added to or subtracted from using the Elo method of calculation depending on whether a team wins, draws or loses a fixture.
Obviously, the more matches a country wins, the more its points total increases and, in turn, its FIFA ranking improves.

But not all matches are made equal. As per FIFA: “The points which are added or subtracted are partially determined by the relative strength of the two opponents, including the logical expectation that teams higher in the ranking should fare better against teams lower in the ranking.”

Competitions also influence the point-scoring system. For example, Spain earns more points for beating Argentina in the World Cup final than it would winning an ordinary friendly, with different tournaments having unique values.
This system to calculate rankings was first introduced in August 2018.

The USMNT shone during September and October. / Mark Thorstenson/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesMauricio Pochettino’s youthful roster for the recent international window produced four successive victories in matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. The USMNT was particularly impressive going forward, finding the net 12 times across those fixtures.

However, while the Stars and Stripes gained 3.85 points for such triumphs, they failed to rise in the rankings and have stayed put in 16th place. The fact that all of the fall matches were friendlies limited the ability to earn more points.
The USMNT’s current running points total is 1705.47, some distance behind Italy in 15th (1713.04).

Spain is still the best around. / MARKO PERKOV/AFP/Getty ImagesIt’s little surprise that world champion Spain still tops the FIFA rankings by a considerable margin. After winning all four of its UEFA Nations League matches over the window, including wins over fellow top 20 nations England and Croatia (twice), it’s gained a further 3.72 points and is currently the only country with more than 2000 points (2011.57).

La Roja remain ahead of the team toppled in the World Cup final: Argentina. Three friendly wins against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin boosted its points total by just 0.63 due to the low level of opposition.

France and England gained some ground on La Albiceleste in third and fourth respectively. The former added 5.14 points to its tally to move onto 1958.86 during Zinedine Zidane’s first window in charge, which yielded three wins and a draw against tough opposition.
The Three Lions also managed three victories, but two of those came against 51st-ranked Czechia. Wins added 2.16 points and now has them on 1925.59 overall—way, way ahead of Portugal in fifth.

A tumultuous international period off the field courtesy of Cristiano Ronaldo’s latest tantrum was not mirrored by on-field displays. The Seleção das Quinas won all four matches in the Nations League under new manager Jorge Jesus, ensuring a leap ahead of Brazil and Morocco in the rankings.
While Morocco lost points, Brazil did manage to add 0.6 to its total by securing wins over Australia and India in friendlies. That wasn’t enough to avoid dropping out of the top five, however.

Belgium lost 5.14 points during Mark van Bommel’s first international window in charge, but have just stayed ahead of the Netherlands, behind in ninth. Despite losing 7.56 points following a winless first camp with Rafa Márquez at the helm, Mexico has held onto its spot in the top 10.

Switzerland jumped up two places into 12th after four consecutive wins, moving above Jürgen Klopp’s new-look Germany. The four-time world champion only managed to win one of its Nations League matches and failed to triumph in either of its games against 41st-ranked Greece.

ftbpro_01m4e69rx46y.title: ‘Do Something’—Man Utd Outcast Outlines What Must Change to Avoid Hojlund Fate
ftbpro_01m4e69rx46y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer1:15 PM EDTRasmus Højlund ended up leaving Old Trafford.  / Kevin C. Cox/Premier League/Getty ImagesManchester United forwardJoshua Zirkzee has put the onus on himself to change his situation at Old Trafford, admitting it was a “big surprise” to get a call from the Netherlands for the September-October international break after not playing much at club level.

Zirkzee is yet to start for United this season and has played only 70 minutes across his four appearances in three different competitions. Still, he got his first two national team caps in almost two years this month and almost matched those club minutes in the space of a few days.
Zirkzee came off the bench for Nations League clashes with Greece and Serbia, accumulating 65 minutes and scoring just his second international goal against the latter.
While it surprised the 25-year-old forward to be reporting to camp this fall, it would similarly be a shock to see him drafted into Michael Carrick’s starting XI when the club schedule resumes.
“At the moment, [competition] means I am mainly coming on as a substitute. And in the end, I have to do something about that myself, even if it isn’t easy,” Zirkzee told ESPN this week.
That means working harder in training and taking his opportunities when they do come. The minutes might be infrequent at first, but Zirkzee playing well would force Carrick’s hand.

Zirkzee proved he can do it in a Netherlands jersey. / STEFAN KOOPS/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAs it stands, Zirkzee has suffered at United through lacking a defined role. He has the physical stature of Erling Haaland, which has long been deceiving because he is not naturally a penalty-box striker like the Norwegian. Zirkzee is much more of a technician, preferring to operate from a deeper position on the pitch and play an active role in creation and buildup.

That side of him came out during preseason, scoring and assisting by showcasing great vision and skill during the July win over Rosenborg in Norway, when many usual starters were on post-World Cup vacation. He also found the net three weeks later against Leeds United.

He was able to function in the same team as Bryan Mbeumo. The problem is that Zirkzee is otherwise fighting for space with Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha. Benjamin Šeško, although a different kind of forward and more of a traditional No. 9, is also a chief source of competition. Mason Mount is also in that mix and appears to be Carrick’s first Fernandes alternative at No. 10.

Zirkzee has to give the manager a reason to hand him minutes at the expense of others. He is certainly capable. This was someone who graduated the academy at Bayern Munich and was pivotal in Bologna upsetting the established order in Italy to qualify for the Champions League.
When the minutes come—and they will, given that United have eight games between now and the next international window in four weeks—use them. Zirkzee knows that, now he just has to action it.
Rasmus Højlund ultimately failed that test, but Zirkzee still has the chance to rewrite his future.

ftbpro_01m4e83xh217.title: Predicting the USMNT’s 2030 World Cup Starting Lineup After Flawless Fall Window
ftbpro_01m4e83xh217.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell5:30 PM EDTThe USMNT is entering a new era. / Patrick Mulligan/USSF/Getty ImagesThe 2030 World Cup might be four years away, but it’s never too early to start dreaming of another explosive run for the U.S. men’s national team, especially after such a successful September-October international break.

The Stars and Stripes kicked off the new cycle with four wins in four friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. A newly blended mix of fresh faces and trusted veterans handled business with poise, swagger and flare—all while the likes of Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun watched from home.

The international break proved one thing: A new era of the USMNT is here. Mauricio Pochettino is giving young stars the opportunity to prove themselves worthy of a major role at the 2030 World Cup, which will unfold mainly across Spain, Portugal and Morocco.
The exciting youngsters have an uphill battle trying to replace some of the more experienced players, but the door is wide open for the starlets to bully their way into Pochettino’s XI.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Tyler Adams will captain the USMNT at the 2030 World Cup. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesIn four years’ time, a handful of the same Americans that led the USMNT on home soil this summer will once again return to Pochettino’s lineup, at the peak of their careers. Chris Richards is undoubtedly starting in central defense, as is Antonee Robinson at left back.
Newly crowned captain Tyler Adams will command the midfield, where Malik Tillman will reprise his role as well. Despite his recent setbacks at Monaco, Balogun is the man who will lead the attack.

Gio Reyna is fighting for a spot in the XI. /  John Dorton/USSF/Getty ImagesJust a few months ago, Pulisic and McKennie would have been locks in Pochettino’s XI. The two players are pillars of the USMNT and were two of the most talented Americans in the game at one time.

But both stars, who will be 32 years old at the 2030 World Cup, have seen their stocks drop after this summer’s showpiece event. Pulisic especially is on the outside looking in, desperate to rediscover his form after scoring just two goals in the two years under Pochettino. At the moment, his goalscoring woes for both club and country—Pulisic has found the back of the net just twice in 2026—keeps him out.

Then there’s Gio Reyna. The midfielder has had a strong resurgence under Pochettino after years of USMNT purgatory. He brings a burst of creativity to the team and a wicked right foot, but his inconsistent form and fitness could reduce him to just a role player.
Julian Hall and Justin Ellis put in impressive camps this time around as well, but there’s still a long way to go before either can fully command the attack—and beat out Balogun along the way.

Neil Pierre, though, has a strong chance of potentially breaking into the XI. The center back is billed as the long-term successor to Tim Ream, but he has a lot of improving to do before he is solid enough to start alongside Richards against some of the top attacks in the world.
Winners, Losers From USMNT’s Faultless World Cup Return. dark. Next. Winners, Losers From USMNT’s Faultless World Cup Return

FotMobGK: Brian Schwake—Matt Freese’s days between the posts are over. Schwake won the goalkeeping battle during the September-October international break and should be ready to be Pochettino’s No. 1.

RB: Alex Freeman—It’s hard to imagine anyone doing enough to displace Freeman on the right flank. The Villarreal man, who will only be 25 during the 2030 World Cup, is speedy, strong defensively and an impressive playmaker.

CB: Chris Richards—In case it wasn’t already obvious, Richards is the leader of Pochettino’s defense. The center back is elite in the air, unafraid to put his body on the line and reads the game better than any other player in red, white and blue.

CB: Auston Trusty—Trusty is by no means a sure-thing in Pochettino’s XI, but he comes with experience, both on the international stage and playing club soccer in Europe. He is reliable and consistent, unlike the raw Pierre.

LB: Antonee Robinson—Like Trusty, Robinson has a young American—Peyton Miller—breathing down his neck, but the Fulham star has the left flank on lock. He is one of the most underrated defenders in the Premier League and always delivers in a major way for the Stars and Stripes.

CM: Tyler Adams—Pochettino knew what he was doing when he handed Adams the captain’s armband. The midfielder is a leader both on and off the pitch and is a staple in the lineup. There’s plenty of reason to believe his third World Cup will be his best yet.

CM: Sebastian Berhalter—In four years’ time, Berhalter will have solidified his place in the XI. The 25-year-old has had a storybook rise under Pochettino and is simply too good, both in midfield and the final third, to keep on the bench. Throw in his set-piece deliveries, and he gets the nod alongside Adams.

ftbpro_01m4e84ntjmv.title: Ranking the USMNT’s Best Goalkeepers for the 2030 World Cup Cycle
ftbpro_01m4e84ntjmv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 8, 2026Mauricio Pochettino got to assess four different goalkeepers over the last two weeks.  / Mark Thorstenson/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Kochen), Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images (Schwake), Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Brady), Alex Menendez/USSF/Getty Images (Freese) The U.S. men’s national team began the 2030 World Cup cycle with four wins from four games in which four different goalkeepers featured for Mauricio Pochettino’s side.

The September-October international window couldn’t have gone much better for the USMNT. With a roster full of young, exciting talents, Pochettino’s side enjoyed nothing but dominance over the last two weeks, including marquee wins against Mexico and Canada by an aggregate score of 4–0.

Beyond results, though, the first camp after the 2026 World Cup was essential for Pochettino to trial players who will headline positional battles over the next four years. Internal competition is essential for every team, and some very interesting ones are already taking shape for the USMNT in the infancy of the 2030 cycle.

Goalkeeper is one of the main ones. Matt Freese, Diego Kochen, Chris Brady and Brian Schwake all played at least 45 minutes during the four friendlies, and there are already signs regarding how the goalkeeper battle will develop in the near and long-term future.
Here, Sports Illustrated ranks the USMNT goalkeeping options after the first international window of the 2030 World Cup cycle.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

The 2026 World Cup starter had a reduced role.       / Alex Menendez/USSF/Getty Images By far the biggest loser in the infancy of the goalkeeper battle has to be the man that started between the sticks for the Stars and Stripes at the 2026 World Cup: Matt Freese.

Keen on making amends after a nightmare performance that significantly contributed to the USMNT’s calamitous elimination against Belgium in the last 16, Freese started the first match of the fall against Peru.

Pochettino gave him a vote of confidence to get rid of any lingering stage fright he might’ve still been feeling. Freese likely could’ve challenged in the air to try to intercept a cross that led to the one goal he conceded, but he was otherwise fine against Peru.

The concerning thing is that he was withdrawn at halftime and never saw the pitch again in the next three games. Freese will be 31 by the time the 2030 World Cup comes around, and with much younger talents already proving their quality, it seems Pochettino is placing his focus elsewhere when it comes to finding his top-choice goalkeeper of the future. Freese’s big chance came during the summer, and it ended in embarrassing fashion.
dark. Next. Matt Freese Responds to Rampant Boos, World Cup Criticism. Matt Freese Responds to Rampant Boos, World Cup Criticism

Chris Brady was Pochettino’s third-choice goalkeeper in the 2026 World Cup.  / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty Images Like Freese, 22-year-old Chris Brady also managed just 45 minutes during the four friendlies, starting against Chile in the second match of the window.

The Chicago Fire man has plenty of MLS experience, but this was only his second-ever appearance for the USMNT after making his debut in a pre-World Cup friendly against Senegal. Although he had six saves against Chile, his showing wasn’t overly positive.

His best save of the night came in a one-one-one where his strong reflexes saw him get a hand to deflect a powerful shot; however, that action shouldn’t have never even occurred. Had he decided not to remain stuck between his posts, he would have easily beaten the attacker to the long-range ball in the first place.

He was also shaky in the air and was eventually punished for two egregious clearance attempts from a corner, resulting in the ball bouncing in the area and chaos ensuing before Diego Ulloa bagged Chile’s temporary equalizer. That was Brady’s final action before being replaced at halftime.
Brady’s mix of youth and top-flight experience will surely see him get more opportunities in the 2030 cycle, but it wasn’t the best of starts for a goalkeeper that already earned a World Cup call-up.

Diego Kochen kept a clean sheet against Mexico in his first USMNT start.  /  Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images An argument could be made that 20-year-old Diego Kochen could top this list. The Barcelona academy graduate made his senior USMNT debut and was the only one of the four goalkeepers that didn’t concede a goal.

Kochen made his debut against Peru, replacing Freese at halftime. Although Peru didn’t muster a single shot on target in the second half, Kochen’s quality as a distributor from deep was on full display, completing all 12 passes he attempted, including two long balls.

Then came his landmark moment. Kochen started the USMNT’s biggest test of the window and kept a clean sheet against Mexico in a 3–0 win. It was a dream night for U.S. Soccer, and Kochen became the youngest goalkeeper in Stars and Stripes history to start a game against El Tri.

However, he only faced one shot on goal all night—which he handled well—and started the game understandably nervous, misplacing routine passes he was lucky Mexico didn’t capitalize on. That shaky start is the reason why he is second on this list.

ftbpro_01m4ecbf1kzd.title: Don’t Be Fooled by Victories—The USMNT Still Has Several Questions Left to Answer
ftbpro_01m4ecbf1kzd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 8, 2026Mauricio Pochettino still has many tactical problems to solve. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team looks fantastic. This fact cannot be denied, and the team has four-straight wins to back it up.
Nonetheless, two things can be true. The USMNT can be categorically perfect post-2026 World Cup, yet still harbor several imperfections.

Manager Mauricio Pochettino is undoubtedly proud of the way the Stars and Stripes dominated in their first regrouping since the summer’s tournament; however, he is left with just as many questions as when the team was unexpectedly thrashed by Belgium in the round of 16.

There are several unknowns that relate to individual American players, such as the future status of once-leader Christian Pulisic or former stalwart Tim Weah. There are also several broader, team-centered and positional problems Pochettino must puzzle through.
Here are three big questions Pochettino still has left to answer. Thankfully, he has four years to do so.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Matt Freese could be on his way out. / Mark Thorstenson/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesPochettino has dreams of turning the USMNT into one of the “most powerful” international teams in global soccer, one that can repeatedly contend for regional trophies and advance deep into World Cup competition.

That is a dream he will never achieve without an elite goalkeeper. Not only is a stellar shot-stopper the difference between beating good teams and great teams, it also sets the entire mood of a team’s play. Having unwavering confidence in one’s last line of defense enables a squad to be carefree enough to reach a flow state and take chances.

The Stars and Stripes have not had a world-class goalkeeper of longevity on their roster in nearly 10 years, back when Tim Howard retired in 2017. The Premier League star and two-time World Cup starter (2010, 2014) had 42 clean sheets in 121 total caps for the national team, amounting to nearly 35% of his appearances.

Meanwhile, the 2026 World Cup starting goalkeeper, Matt Freese, has five clean sheets in 19 total caps (26%), an underperformance compared to Howard’s statistics and a sincere lack of experience to be handed the keys to the net at soccer’s most prestigious affair. The reality that Freese was in over his head manifested most obviously in the round of 16 loss, when he whiffed a clearance to gift Belgium its third goal of the night, the nail in the coffin for a runaway victory.
Next. Matt Freese Responds to Rampant Boos, World Cup Criticism. Matt Freese Responds to Rampant Boos, World Cup Criticism. dark
Pochettino has had wavering faith in Freese, and even called him up for the fall. Freese played just 45 minutes against Peru, though, in a rather uneventful outing that saw him make a single save.

The rest of the goalkeeping ranks aren’t promising either. World Cup third-stringer Chris Brady and newcomers Brian Schwake and Diego Kochen all underwhelmed. To be fair, none of them were heavily tested. Nevertheless, there were not even glimpses of world-class play. At best, they were solid, but that’s not enough to turn Pochettino’s team into a global superpower.
Chris Richards is the heartbeat of the backline. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesThank goodness for Chris Richards.

The seasoned veteran has been a constant in the center of the backline since early 2025, impressing with his distribution skills of unfathomable accuracy, his aerial dominance, his one-on-one defending and, most importantly, his poise. He sets a tone of cool confidence across the entire defense that can then instigate dangerous attacking motions.

He can’t do it alone, though. With the recent international retirement of 39-year-old Tim Ream, the need for a suitable partner has never been clearer, yet no obvious contender has presented himself thus far.

There’s Mark McKenzie and Auston Trusty, both of whom are fringe players. Trusty did partner well with Richards when called upon this fall, though. There is also Miles Robinson; however, the more minutes he accrues on the international stage, the more he seems incorrect for the job.

Pochettino will certainly be holding out hope for Neil Pierre, who has held down the Philadelphia Union’s backline since their MLS resurgence this summer. Except the 6'7" teenager struggled in his debut camp this fall, proving he still has a lot of work to do before he can even begin to enter the starting lineup conversation. He made one start in the win against Chile and continuously gave the ball away, resulting in unnecessary counter attacks for the South Americans. Pochettino ultimately couldn’t trust him again, granting him zero minutes against Mexico and just 16 against Canada.

The USMNT is a tight-knit group. / Maja Hitij/FIFA/Getty ImagesThe gap between the USMNT’s most successful moments at the World Cup this summer and the catastrophe that ensued against Belgium can be chiefly attested to one factor: the team’s identity.

At its peak, the USMNT played with a rugged grit that manifested into a high-press, aggressive attacking strategy. From the opening whistle, the Americans jumped down their opponents’ throats and didn’t give them any other choice but sit back and be dictated by their rhythm of play. In all three group stage matches, they found the back of the net within the first 11 minutes.

ftbpro_01m4ehfz86zr.title: Four Takeaways From Worrying, Winless Start to Rafa Márquez Era With Mexico
ftbpro_01m4ehfz86zr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas10:00 AM EDTRafa Márquez had little to smile about in his first four games as Mexico manager.      / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty Images The Rafael Márquez era as Mexico national team manager got off to a worrying start, with El Tri managing just two draws to go alongside two defeats during the September-October international window.

Spirits were sky-high entering the international window following Mexico’s strong 2026 World Cup performance. Even after a draw against Colombia in Márquez’s debut where El Tri outplayed the South Americans for long stretches, fan support and overall confidence remained unharmed given there was reason to believe the team was building from the foundation it laid this summer.

Thing quickly unraveled after that, though. An unconvincing draw against Peru was followed by an embarrassing defeat against the arch-rival USMNT. Instead of responding after this dreadful setback, El Tri dropped its final game of the window against an inferior Chile side.

The positive momentum harnessed during the World Cup disappeared in just two weeks. Only four games into his tenure, Márquez and his entire squad are under fire. It’s still early, but it’s been far from an ideal start to a new era for Mexico.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mexico lost for the first time against Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT. / Chris Coduto/Getty Images It’s not that some of the shine from Mexico’s fairytale 2026 World Cup campaign wore off, but it became clear that El Tri’s brilliant form during the tournament—in which it pushed a team of England’s caliber to the absolute limit—was the exception rather than the norm. Over the past two weeks, Mexico experienced a drastic reality check.

Let’s not forget, Mexico entered 2026 immersed in a six-game winless streak that spanned the last six months of 2025, almost limping toward the World Cup. Results to start the summer were good, but it wasn’t until the second half of the final group stage match against Czechia that former manager Javier Aguirre finally struck the right chord, which allowed Mexico to perform at its best.

Aguirre found his best XI at the perfect time as the knockout rounds started and, fueled by unprecedented levels of support and the intimidating Estadio Azteca, Mexico played two of its best games in World Cup history against England and especially Ecuador in the round of 32.

Throughout history, Mexico has shown it’s capable of raising its level depending on the stage. It required a playoff win against New Zealand to qualify to the 2014 World Cup after a dreadful qualifier campaign, but then it drew against host nation Brazil and was five minutes away from besting the Netherlands in the round of 16.

It’s the process between big tournaments when Mexico and its managers often suffer the most, and Márquez already is no different. In four games, any notion of El Tri sustaining the level it showed over the summer disappeared. It’s time to build back up.

Orbelín Pineda (right) struggled as a winger against the USMNT.       / Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images Outside of the home-field advantage, it also quickly became clear that Mexico’s summer success came in large part thanks to a clear-cut best starting lineup Aguirre discovered on the fly. Take away a couple of pieces, and El Tri’s lack of depth and talent deficiencies become glaring.

Mexico’s talent pool is simply not deep enough. Against Colombia, with seven players who started both World Cup knockout games, Mexico played its best minutes of the fall. Márquez deployed an entirely different lineup againt Peru three days later and El Tri could only muster a draw against a vastly inferior team.

Ultimately, results obtained during Márquez’s first four friendly matches in charge were never that important. How El Tri’s entire operation on the pitch looked under him and how he profiled the players at his disposal were the most important things to evaluate as his tenure started. This is perhaps the most worrying part.
#VocesTricolor after our game in LA. 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/0bStF5bgnE

Outside of 50–60 minutes against Colombia and the opening 25 minutes against the USMNT in which the team performed similar to its World Cup version, Mexico was borderline unwatchable the rest of the window. One of the main reasons? Márquez misprofiling his players.

Orbelín Pineda has been one of the best organizing midfielders in Liga MX this season, yet Márquez almost exclusively used him as a touchline winger and he suffered. Álvaro Fidalgo won three Liga MX titles as Club América’s version of Pedri, yet Márquez insists on mostly using him as a No. 10. Fresh faces such as Jeremy Márquez, Santiago Sandoval, and even Inter Miami’s Germán Berterame operated away from the positions where they’re at their best for significant periods.
Without quality depth, it’s essential for Márquez to maximize the talent at his disposal, not compromise it by misplacing it on the pitch.

Overall, though, El Tri’s stellar World Cup version sustained itself thanks to an XI that, without a couple of key players, could collapse like a house of cards. That became abundantly clear at one position in particular.

Mexico missed Raúl Jiménez dearly.  / Luke Hales/Getty Images Take away 35-year-old Raúl Jiménez and Mexico has a major problem at center forward. The Wolverhampton Wanderers frontman missed the start of Márquez’s era through injury and El Tri scored only two goals in four games. The first was a brilliant solo effort from 17-year-old Gilberto Mora and the second came thanks to a center back winning an aerial duel at a set-piece.

Armando González, Santiago Giménez and Berterame all had a chance to impress Márquez and did the exact opposite. It’s true that Mexico, especially without Mora, struggles to create chances, but the trio of strikers didn’t convert the few they had and otherwise struggled significantly in every other aspect of the game.

ftbpro_01m4ehhkckry.title: Report: Man Utd Offer JJ Gabriel Last-Gasp Deal As Real Madrid Circle
ftbpro_01m4ehhkckry.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell6:00 PM EDTJJ Gabriel is inching toward a Manchester United exit. / IMAGO/Crystal PixManchester United have reportedly presented wonderkid JJ Gabriel with an official scholarship contract offer in a last-ditch attempt to keep the teenager in red—and from leaving for free.

16-year-old Gabriel made waves far beyond Manchester when he requested the cancelation of his registration with United back in September. Reported broken promises of first-team minutes and heavy family involvement led to the stunning fractured relationship, with the Red Devils scrambling to find a solution.

Losing such an exciting talent, who lit up the U-21s as a 15-year-old, would be bad enough for the club. But according to Premier League youth guidelines, Gabriel would have been able to leave the club in January for free had United not offered him a scholarship for next campaign.

The Guardian report United has indeed come back to the table with such an offer, ensuring any Premier League club must now negotiate a fee with the Red Devils for Gabriel’s signature. If no agreement can be reached, the Professional Football Compensation Committee can determine the final package in a case similar to when Rio Ngumoha left Chelsea for Liverpool.

If that possibility becomes a reality, United hope to receive a fee “in excess” of £3 million ($4 million), as well as 20% of Gabriel’s next transfer fee, per The Guardian. It would hardly be ideal for the Red Devils to watch their homegrown talent join a Premier League rival, but it would at least ensure  decent compensation—unlike if the teenager chooses another destination across Europe.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

José Mourinho would love to have another young weapon at his disposal.  / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesAs soon as Gabriel opened the door to a transfer, European giants descended upon the prodigy. Links with Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are running wild, but it’s the 15-time European champions on the front lines.

According to The Guardian, Los Blancos are the “favorites” to sign Gabriel. It’s not entirely surprising given the teenager’s ambitions; going from the biggest club in England to the biggest club in Spain—and the world—makes sense on paper for a youngster desperate to make his name under the brightest of lights.

United are of course hoping to keep Gabriel in their ranks, but they must come to terms with how “unlikely” that looks. Worsening the blow could be the low sum coming their way if the youth England international chooses a club in Europe.
Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich or any other European side only must pay “FIFA training compensation” for Gabriel’s signature, which is typically around £200,000–300,000 ($265,000–397,000).

JJ Gabriel is eyeing a blockbuster move to the Bernabéu. / Manchester United/Getty ImagesAt the crux of Gabriel’s issue with United was his playing time—or lack thereof—with the first team. Yet he could choose a new home with even less opportunity.

In the last two summers alone, seven Real Madrid Castilla products left the Bernabéu to try their luck elsewhere. Even promising stars who had a place in the first team, like Gonzalo García, bid farewell to the Spanish capital, where they could never truly break into the XI.

Take a look at Endrick and Franco Mastantuono. Both players were highly sought after, and promised to be the future of Real Madrid. Well, Endrick is closer to another loan than any significant minutes in a white shirt, and Mastantuono had to escape to Fiorentina to get playing time.

Then there’s Yan Diomande. Los Blancos struck a club-record agreement, worth up to €140 million ($157 million), for the winger’s signature this summer, and he cannot even secure a place in José Mourinho’s XI.

Gabriel has less experience and a lesser pedigree than all the aforementioned players. What’s to make his experience at the Bernabéu any different? There are even veteran superstars, like Trent Alexander-Arnold, currently wasting away on Mourinho’s bench.
Even in a few years, the teenager would still be climbing uphill to make a name for himself at Real Madrid.
