ftbpro_01m4epw94pb0.title: Who’s in, Who’s Out? Analyzing the USMNT’s Depth Chart After Perfect Fall Window
ftbpro_01m4epw94pb0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely, Amanda LangellOct 11, 2026The U.S. has been in fine form since the World Cup. / Kohjiro Kinno/Sports IllustratedU.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino has trialed no shortage of stars, yet only some have made their mark donning the red, white and blue.

The 2030 World Cup might still be four years away, but every international break is a chance for Pochettino to zero in on his best squad, one capable of finally making a deep run on the biggest stage in soccer. From established veterans to exciting, unproven teenagers, the Argentine boss has plenty of talent at his disposal—but where do they all stack up?

Sports Illustrated’s deep dive into the USMNT’s depth breaks down the Stars and Stripes’ best players at every position. The guide only includes players that have been rostered in the last 12 months, dating back to October 2025. Former captain Tim Ream is excluded following his retirement.

The rankings are not only based off current success, but also level of potential, especially when it comes to young players like Brooklyn Raines, Neil Pierre and Mathis Albert, all of whom have a high ceiling.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Brian Schwake is in line to be the USMNT No. 1 moving forward. / Brace Hemmelgarn/USSF/Getty ImagesBrian Schwake (Nashville SC)Diego Kochen (Lyngby)Chris Brady (Chicago Fire)Matt Freese (NYCFC)Patrick Schulte (Columbus Crew)Roman Celentano (FC Cincinnati)Jonathan Klinsmann (Cesena)Matt Turner (New England Revolution)At the 2026 World Cup, it was Matt Freese between the posts for the USMNT. But a disastrous outing against Belgium was the final straw for the inconsistent, mistake-prone goalkeeper. He might’ve still logged 45 minutes against Peru this fall, but he soon watched three other names jump above his on the depth chart.

Chris Brady and Diego Kochen both got looks this camp, but the latter made the better impression. Kochen played the full 90 minutes and kept a clean sheet in the team’s 3–0 win against Mexico. The 20-year-old also became the youngest goalkeeper to ever start a game for the USMNT.

Still, it’s Brian Schwake who emerged from the international window as the favorite to become Pochettino’s No. 1. The American shot-stopper has had a fantastic season with Supporters’ Shield favorites Nashville SC and was the only goalkeeper to make two starts for the USMNT this fall.
Schwake has a ways to go before he truly proves himself capable of locking down top attacks on the international stage, but he’s no doubt leading the race at the moment.

Alex Freeman was a breakout star at the World Cup. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAlex Freeman (Villarreal)Antonee Robinson (Fulham)Peyton Miller (New England Revolution)Joe Scally (Borussia Mönchengladbach)Francis Westfield (Philadelphia Union)John Tollkin (Holstein Kiel)Fullback is no longer a problem position for the USMNT. The ever-reliable and experienced Antonee Robinson owns the left flank while breakout star Alex Freeman commands the right.

Freeman’s impressive form for Orlando City earned him a place in Pochettino’s squad last year and he quickly became a starter. There were doubts over whether he could hang with the best at the World Cup, but the 22-year-old, who had since made the move to Villarreal, silenced all doubters this summer—and continued his strong form during the team’s fall friendlies.

Joe Scally is the man tasked with the near-impossible job of displacing Freeman, much like Peyton Miller’s uphill battle trying to take minutes from Robinson. But the latter is gaining Premier League attention after his first senior camp and at age 18, his career is just beginning.

Chris Richards is the leader of Mauricio Pochettino’s defense.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesChris Richards (Crystal Palace)Auston Trusty (Celtic)Mark McKenzie (Toulouse)George Campbell (West Bromwich Albion)Neil Pierre (Philadelphia Union)Miles Robinson (FC Cincinnati)Cameron Carter-Vickers (Celtic)There’s no shortage of center backs at Pochettino’s disposal, but the long list of names are all essentially fighting for one spot. Chris Richards is irreplaceable in the USMNT’s XI; the Crystal Palace standout is the team’s defensive leader, both on and off the pitch.

There is a Ream-shaped hole alongside him in central defense. Auston Trusty’s experience with the USMNT and playing in Europe at the club level makes him the most trustworthy—no pun intended—option for Pochettino. He is also versatile enough to play at left back as well.

Keep an eye out for Pierre, though. The 18-year-old got his first call-up this fall and is billed by many to be the best long-term option to replace Ream. The towering center back is brilliant in the air and has a knack for goal, but he has plenty of growing to do before he is strong enough to beat out Trusty, Mark McKenzie or George Campbell.

Tyler Adams is the new USMNT captain. / Luke Hales/Getty ImagesTyler Adams (Bournemouth)Weston McKennie (Juventus)Sebastian Berhalter (Middlesbrough)Johnny Cardoso (Atlético Madrid)Brooklyn Raines (New England Revolution)Yunus Musah (AC Milan)Tanner Tessmann (Lyon)Aidan Morris (Middlesbrough)Timothy Tillman (LAFC)James Sands (NYCFC)Cristian Roldan (Seattle Sounders)Pochettino experimented with multiple formations during the most recent four friendlies, but there was always one constant: The Argentine boss deployed two defensive midfielders.

New captain Tyler Adams is a lock in the middle of the park, but his partner in Pochettino’s double pivot is up for grabs. Weston McKennie has the pedigree and the World Cup experience, but his absence this fall allowed other players to stand out.

Sebastian Berhalter staked the biggest claim for a starting role moving forward, continuing his impressive rise with the USMNT ever since his breakout 2025 Gold Cup campaign. There is a wealth of competition, though.

The young Brooklyn Raines started two of the USMNT’s four wins during the September-October break and played beyond his 21 years. His defensive prowess outranks what Yunus Musah has brought lately, and he has better vision with the ball at his feet than Tanner Tessmann.

Johnny Cardoso is arguably more well-rounded than all three of the aforementioned options, but he has to get himself back into Pochettino’s plans after missing the 2026 World Cup with an ankle injury.

ftbpro_01m4eqy15t6t.title: USWNT vs. Spain: 4 Reasons to Watch Double Header Between Two Powerhouses
ftbpro_01m4eqy15t6t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Theo Lloyd-Hughes8:31 AM EDTTrinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Mallory Swanson talk to the media during press conference at the U.S. women’s national team’s hotel on June 3, 2026 in Sao Paulo, Brazil. / Brad Smith / Getty ImagesThe October FIFA women’s international window is here, and that means two friendly matches for the U.S. women’s national team against Spain. These will be the final two matches before the USA plays its World Cup qualifier against El Salvador on Nov. 27.

First up, the USA host Spain at Audi Field in Washington, D.C., on Saturday, Oct. 10. The game will kick off at 2:30 p.m. ET and can be watched on TBS and HBO Max in English and on Telemundo, Universo, and Peacock in Spanish.

Then attention turns to Subaru Park in Chester, Penn., where the USA and Spain face off once more on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET and will be broadcast on TNT and HBO Max in English and on Universo and Peacock in Spanish.
Here’s four reasons why these are a pair of international friendlies you can’t afford to miss.
🇺🇸 𝗪𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗗𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗠.#JugarLucharYGanar pic.twitter.com/tQbcrAYOWw

It doesn’t get much bigger than this. The USA vs. Spain will see the world's two top-ranked teams go head-to-head. It’s also a meeting between the two nations that are the oddsmakers’ favorites to win the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. The USA are narrowly pulling ahead, with some betting companies setting their odds at +350 compared to Spain at +400.

To increase the narrative of a battle between the world’s two biggest heavyweights further, this is also a tantalizing contest between the reigning World Cup champions, Spain, and the reigning Olympic Gold Medalists, the USA.

Of course, there will be no silverware at stake over the next week, but points in the FIFA rankings will be up for grabs, as well as bragging rights. Whatever the results are over the next few days, they will surely dictate the conversation as hype builds for next year’s World Cup.

Believe it or not, these will be just the fifth and sixth meetings between the USWNT and Spain. The previous four meetings have all occurred in the last seven years. The historical record stands at three wins for the USA and one win for Spain.

The first two meetings both came in 2019. The USA won the first meeting, a friendly 1-0. The USA then knocked Spain out of the World Cup 2-1 in the Round of 16 that summer. The next meeting came in another friendly in March 2020, and again the USA came away 1-0 winners. However, the tables turned in 2022, when the USA traveled to Spain and were outplayed in a 2-0 win for the hosts.

Now, four years later (almost to the day), Spain are the World Champions and the USA are the contenders. The USA will be out for revenge to set the record straight. Particularly the American players who are still in the squad and featured in that loss to Spain: Sophia Wilson, Trinity Rodman, Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Ashley Sanchez.
This next chapter of a new rivalry is a can’t-miss.

During a stunning Gold Medal triumph at the 2024 Olympics, the USA’s fan-favorite attacking trio of Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Wilson were dubbed ‘Triple Espresso’. However, due to Rodman’s past injury issues, in addition to Swanson and Wilson becoming mothers, we haven’t seen ‘Triple Espresso’ all on the pitch together since that Gold Medal match on August 10, 2024.

This camp will be just the second time the trio has all been called in together since then. In the previous international window, which the USA spent in Brazil this past June, Rodman and Wilson both saw action. Meanwhile, Swanson was an unused substitute.

Should Hayes opt to play ‘Triple Espresso’ against Spain, it would end a more than two-year wait for fans to catch the trio on the pitch. And what better time and place to do it than at home games against the reigning World Cup champions? Buckle up, get caffeinated.

Roster News: @ChelseaFCW defender Naomi Girma has been ruled out of the upcoming USWNT matches vs Spain due to a muscle injury. A roster replacement will be named at a later date. pic.twitter.com/Vne6q64jtj

While the anticipation around a return for ‘Triple Espresso’ intensifies, the conversation leading up to these friendlies against Spain has been dominated by the unavailable players. The USWNT will be without Emily Sonnett and Olivia Moultrie until next summer at the earliest, while Catarina Macario, Naomi Girma and Sam Coffey are also unable to report for duty in the shorter term. That’s four USWNT starters right there.
Of course, in soccer, absences mean opportunity. Who will step up in their place against Spain?

With neither of the starting center-backs, Sonnett and Girma, available, who Hayes deploys in the middle of the defense will be particularly intriguing. The experienced Tierna Davidson and the in-form Kennedy Wesley are the likely deputies. Coffey’s role in the midfield should be filled by Claire Hutton. Macario’s striker role is also up for grabs and could be filled by any one of ‘Triple Espresso’.

There are also five players who could make a debut for the USWNT: Jordan Silkowitz, Evelyn Shores, Kate Del Fava, Pietra Tordin, and Trinity Byars. However, Hayes throwing them straight into the fire against one of the world’s most elite teams would be surprising.

ftbpro_01m4exmbsj79.title: Two-Time NBA MVP Joins Atletico Madrid Ownership Group
ftbpro_01m4exmbsj79.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas9:00 AM EDTShai Gilgeous-Alexander is an NBA champion and reigning back-to-back MVP.  / Zach Beeker/NBAE/Getty Images Reigning two-time NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has joined Atlético Madrid’s ownership group with a minority stake in the club, the club announced Thursday.

Gilgeous-Alexander has dominated the NBA over the past two years, winning the 2025 NBA title with the Oklahoma City Thunder to go along with his pair of MVP awards. Now, Atlético Madrid appears delighted to have such a successful sportsman join the club’s ownership.

“Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has joined Atlético de Madrid’s ownership group,” Atlético Madrid said in a statement. “The partnership is grounded in shared values: ambition, excellence and the belief that every result must be earned.”

The 28-year-old joins fellow Canadian Jonathan David at Atléti and is excited for what the future holds. “I’m excited to officially join Atlético de Madrid’s ownership group.” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “This is a club with a long-standing presence at the top of European football, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future.”
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander x @Atleti ❤️🤍📸@okcthunder pic.twitter.com/GZNCkxJRO1

Back in April, the Thunder posted pictures of the Canadian superstar boarding the team plane wearing an Atlético Madrid jumpsuit. How involved and how much his ownership stake is worth remains unknown, but he’ll join the ownership group of a team that includes 11 board members, one of which is Spain legend and former player David Villa.

“Beyond the numbers, his ability to perform under pressure and commitment to constant growth align with Atlético de Madrid’s values of intensity, pride and ambition. His investment reflects an interest in the club’s long-term vision and international growth,” Atléti’s statement finished.
After becoming an Atléti minority owner, Gilgeous-Alexander will now develop a strong rivalry with one of his close friends.

Recent history suggests there’s perhaps no player in the world Atlético Madrid feel more animosity towards—outside of their own striker Julián Álvarez—than Real Madrid star Vinícius Jr. It just so happens that Gilgeous-Alexander is close friends with the Brazilian superstar.

Over the years, the duo of global stars have shared pictures on social media on vacation, training or simply spending time together socially. Vinícius Jr has gone to watch Thunder games in the past, posting images of a signed Gilgeous-Alexander jersey to his feeds.

Furthermore, the new Atlético Madrid owner has visited enemy ground. Gilgeous-Alexander joined his friend at Real Madrid’s training ground and even had some fun on the pitch, scoring a penalty against Vinícius Jr before doing Cristiano Ronaldo’s celebration. He’s also visited the Bernabéu and was pictured on the pitch with Vinícius Jr and fellow Real Madrid player Éder Militão wearing the jersey of Los Blancos.

Atlético Madrid supporters won’t tolerate any hint of Real Madrid support from their new owner. Now, Gilgeous-Alexander and his close friend Vinícius Jr are on opposite sides of one of the fiercest city rivalries in all of European soccer.

LeBron James has been part of Liverpool’s ownership group for over a decade.  / Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC/Getty Images Gilgeous-Alexander becomes the latest in a growing list of big-name NBA players in ownership groups of some of the biggest teams in European soccer.

LeBron James was a trailblazer in this regard when he became Liverpool minority-owner in 2011, buying a 2% stake in the club for $6.5 million. In 2021, the now Philadelphia 76er officially became a partner of Fenway Sports Group—the Reds’ majority ownership group.

In 2025, former Oklahoma City Thunder star Kevin Durant became a minority shareholder of back-to-back Champions League winners Paris-Saint Germain. Later that year, Giannis Antetokounmpo joined the investment group that became Chelsea Women owners once BlueCo sold the team.
Russell Westbrook, arguably the most loved player in Oklahoma City Thunder history outside of Gilgeous-Alexander, is part of the 49ers Enterprises group that owns Leeds United.

With U.S. investment groups turning their attention to European soccer clubs regularly nowadays, it’s also become an attractive venture for some of the most high-profile athletes in U.S. sports. Gilgeous-Alexander joining Atlético Madrid’s ownership group is the latest example.

ftbpro_01m4g04pdw1y.title: Chelsea Predicted Lineup vs. Bournemouth: Caicedo, James Bolster Alonso’s Midfield
ftbpro_01m4g04pdw1y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack11:00 AM EDTChelsea are set to be drastically improved in midfield for Bournemouth’s visit. / Chelsea Football Club/Getty ImagesHorrid memories of the Gtech Community Stadium are in the distant past for Chelsea thanks to the bumper international break, and Xabi Alonso’s Blues are out to ignite their campaign in October.
However, the Premier League seldom throws up walkover fixtures, and Bournemouth will have no interest in making life easy for the porous west Londoners on Saturday.

A depleted Chelsea were bullied by Brentford last time out, succumbing to a 3–0 defeat, with drastic action required from Alonso to stiffen his outfit. Some have called for a switch to a back four, and now would be a great time to revert after the three-week break.
However, with the statuses of several key players still in doubt, it seems unlikely that Alonso will opt for a drastic systematic alteration when the Cherries come to town.
Here’s how Chelsea could line up on Saturday.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Chelsea’s engine room should be bolstered by two key injury recoveries. /     GK: Emiliano Martínez—Chelsea’s new No. 1 had a more emotional international break than most, as he and Argentina bade farewell to its greatest since Diego Maradona. Alonso will hope that Martínez isn’t still hung up on Lionel Messi as he attempts to deny Evanilson and Co.
CB: Wesley Fofana—It’s been a stuttering start to the season for Fofana, but he would’ve been aided by staying in west London during the break.

CB: Maxence Lacroix—Lacroix was a busy man for Zinédine Zidane’s France, starting three of its four games in William Saliba’s absence. The early signs suggest Lacroix could be an important figure for Zizou’s Bleus.

CB: Levi Colwill—The left-footed defender has insisted that all the adversity he’s been through at the start of his senior career has made him “more experienced and a more mature head than probably most 23-year-olds.” Chelsea supporters are waiting for Colwill to emerge as the leader of their defense.
RWB: Pedro Neto—Neto remains a useful outlet for the national team, and may well have enjoyed not having any wing back duties for a couple of weeks. Now, it’s back to reality.

CM: Reece James—Chelsea’s captain was among the key personnel absent for the trip to Brentford, and James subsequently missed out on England selection as a result. He’s expected to be fit in time for this encounter.

CM: Moisés Caicedo—There will be no Jordan Henderson in the engine room this weekend, with Moisés Caicedo poised to make his first start of the season. He’s been carefully managed, and Alonso has confirmed the midfielder is finally ready.

LWB: Pep Chavarría—The jury’s out on the summer arrival at the start of his Chelsea career, but he’s at least more energetic than converted center back Jorrel Hato. Marco Palestra may also be an option for Alonso.

AM: Cole Palmer—His withdrawal from the England roster shouldn’t see him miss any time for the Blues. Palmer was pictured heading to Cobham ahead of Saturday’s bout, and he’ll be out to inspire the hosts against the Cherries.

AM: Morgan Rogers—Rogers’s productive start at his new home hit a brick wall against Brentford, and he was used only sparingly by Thomas Tuchel during the break. He did, however, record an assist for Harry Kane against Czechia on Tuesday—a pinpoint first-time ball across the box.

ST: Danny Welbeck—João Pedro is the biggest question mark for Chelsea heading into the match, with conflicting reports emerging. Some think his knee injury will keep him out until the end of October, while others believe the Brazilian could be ready as early as Saturday. Welbeck is waiting in the wings, no matter what.

ftbpro_01m4g18x8mp0.title: Maresca Reveals Haaland Injury Plan for Huge Liverpool Game
ftbpro_01m4g18x8mp0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:45 AM EDTErling Haaland is Manchester City’s perennial top scorer. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images“Finally!”

Amid a barrage of questions about Manchester City’s seismic guilty verdict and the potential fall out from the 100-plus breaches of Premier League financial regulations, Enzo Maresca was relieved to be faced with an inquiry which he had a definitive (and positive) answer for: Erling Haaland will be fit and available for Sunday’s trip to Liverpool.

On top of all the talk of unprecedented points deductions, transfer bans and Premier League expulsion, City fans had to briefly deal with the more immediate prospect of an injured Haaland. The Norway international could not finish his nation’s final fixture of the extended fall break, hobbling to the side before his manager bemoaned the “insane” schedule which had overloaded his star.
However, Haaland’s exit has proven to only be precautionary. All he needed was a few days in the sun before making his return to Manchester.
“He’s good. He’s good,” Maresca repeated, relieved to finally land upon a new topic. “He went to Marbella, two, three days off, play golf, recovery, and ready for Anfield. He is good. Thank you.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Phil Foden will not be involved. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesMaresca was only permitted a brief break from the charges chat to discuss Haaland’s fitness and so did not provide an update on any of City’s other doubts. Antoine Semenyo picked up an ankle injury which kept him sidelined for Ghana’s fixtures this fall while Nico O’Reilly had to pull out of England’s camp with what Thomas Tuchel described as a “minor issue.” Both remain doubts for Sunday’s test.

Phil Foden will definitely not be involved. The overlooked England international is serving the third and final match of the three-game ban he received after petulantly kicking Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes in the chest during last month’s derby.

Foden’s absence could be balanced by the full return of Jérémy Doku. City’s bag of tricks and jinks on the flanks may be in line for his first Premier League start of a season derailed by a calf injury sustained against Arsenal in the Community Shield. Doku was left off Belgium’s roster for the fall fixtures but did make a cameo against Sunderland before the Premier League shutters came down last month.

Erling Haaland had a happy trip to Anfield last season. / Michael Regan/Getty Images“It will be a tough game for sure, tough test,” Maresca admitted of the challenge facing his players at Liverpool’s inhospitable home ground. The Reds were denied the 2013–14 title by Manchester City during the period under investigation while Jürgen Klopp’s teams were repeatedly and narrowly pipped to multiple Premier League crowns in the following years. If there is any set of fans most eager to launch an audio assault on City’s players, it’s those who will assemble at Anfield.

“We need to be ready,” Maresca warned. “The focus has to be the game, but we know the environment in Anfield is nice. It will probably be even worse because of the situation. It will be our duty to do our best and win the game.
“Absolutely we can face the pressure. We have players who played in a similar situation. Enzo Fernández played in Argentina, it's always every game like going to Anfield. It's not a problem.”

“Just try to manage the noise,” was Maresca’s approach, echoing the sentiment Haaland had offered the day before. “It’s something serious but at the same time we just need to manage that and focus on what we can do and what we can control, which is try to control the game in the best possible game, go to Anfield and win the game.”

ftbpro_01m4g1fjzhw1.title: Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Getafe: Flick Chooses Raphinha Stand-In
ftbpro_01m4g1fjzhw1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray4:00 PM EDTGabriel Jesus could benefit from Raphinha’s injury. / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesBarcelona are aiming to extend their perfect start to the campaign when facing Getafe in La Liga on their return from the extended international period.

La Blaugrana have been in blistering form this season as they’ve soared to the summit of Spain’s top flight, winning all seven of their domestic matches courtesy of some frightening attacking performances. While their momentum was halted by the break, they’re expected to secure another handsome victory at Camp Nou this Saturday.

Hansi Flick does have some dilemmas to overcome, however, with several important first-choice options forced to withdraw from their international teams with injury issues. The Barça boss will also have one eye on next Tuesday’s awkward away day at Galatasaray in the Champions League.
Here’s how the Catalan giants could line up against Getafe.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Joan García—The goalkeeper missed the Sevilla victory and international break through injury, but he’s expected to return in between the posts this weekend. He hasn’t lost a competitive match he’s played in since April.

RB: Jules Koundé—Flick will be reluctant to take any risks with Eric García, who withdrew from the Spain squad prematurely with discomfort in his knee. As a result, Koundé could make his second La Liga start of the season.

CB: Pau Cubarsí—Cubarsí is on an impressive run, winning his last 16 matches for club and country. The youngster racked up three triumphs with Spain in the UEFA Nations League against England and Croatia (twice).

CB: Gerard Martín—With the injury-prone Andreas Christensen having suffered another setback, Martín is expected to partner Cubarsí against a Getafe team who have scored just four times in seven La Liga games.

LB: Xavi Espart—Fresh from signing a contract extension until 2030, Espart might be handed another opportunity to impress Flick. The versatile 19-year-old has been excellent when called upon this term.

CM: Rodri—The midfielder might have to field some awkward questions about his former club Manchester City in the coming weeks after they were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. That’s unlikely to impact his super consistent performances on the field, though.
CM: Pedri—Pedri will line up alongside his fellow countryman in the engine room and his sharp playmaking skills will prove essential to unlocking a deep-lying Getafe defense.

RW: Lamine Yamal—Yamal is in truly devastating form for club and country. The sorcerous left winger has now provided a goal or assist in nine of his last 10 matches across all competitions, during which time he’s registered 19 goal involvements.

AM: Fermín López—With López fresher than Spain teammate Dani Olmo after being used sparingly by Luis de la Fuente, he might be selected to start the Getafe match in the No. 10 position. He already has six goal contributions in as many league appearances this term.

LW: Anthony Gordon—The speedy winger has made an electric start to life in Catalonia and the confidence was oozing when he donned an England jersey over the break. Gordon scored in each of his three appearances, including against Spain.

ST: Gabriel Jesus—With matches coming thick and fast during October, Flick will be determined to ease the in-form Raphinha back into action after his injury scare with Brazil. Therefore, his compatriot Jesus is set to earn a first start for his new employers against Getafe.

ftbpro_01m4g3mbyeer.title: Man Utd Predicted Lineup vs. Tottenham: Baleba Makes Red Devils Debut
ftbpro_01m4g3mbyeer.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:00 PM EDTCarlos Baleba arrived at the club carrying an injury. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesThe extended international break allowed Michael Carrick to breathe, reset and prepare for the hectic run of fixtures that lie ahead for his Manchester United team.
The heavily scrutinized Red Devils boss can feel his seat starting to warm at Old Trafford, even if he rightfully laughed off sack talk before the break.

Carrick inspired Man Utd to a third-place finish and a return to the Champions League last season, and his first full campaign at the helm was always going to bring about stiffer challenges. He hasn’t coped particularly well thus far, but the first block of five league outings was merely the opening act in a long 2026–27 season.
Still, he’ll be feeling the pressure when a worse-off Tottenham Hotspur visit the Theatre of Dreams on Saturday. For many, this is a contest Carrick simply cannot lose.
Here’s how Man Utd could line up against bottom-of-the-table Spurs this weekend.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Carlos Baleba is expected to make his Man Utd debut. /    GK: Senne Lammens—It was a busy break for Lammens in Thibaut Courtois’s absence, and the Belgian goalkeeper returns to Manchester keen to quieten the likes of Paul Scholes.
RB: Diogo Dalot—Dalot looks set to be Man Utd’s steady and unspectacular right back option for another season. The versatile Noussair Mazraoui is operating in reserve.
CB: Harry Maguire—While Leny Yoro impressed on the international stage for France, he’s unlikely to work his way into Carrick’s plans for Spurs’ visit.

CB: Lisandro Martínez—Martínez saw compatriot Cristian Romero pick up his fourth Premier League red card in this fixture last season, and he heads into this contest having said a tearful goodbye to Lionel Messi in Buenos Aires.

LB: Luke Shaw—After an injury-free 2025–26, Shaw dealt with a fitness setback during the first month of the new season, and it cost Man Utd. Possession dynamics just aren’t as smooth when he’s out of the team, with Carrick forced to fit a square peg in a round hole. The position will be addressed in January.

CM: Carlos Baleba—The signs are pointing toward the third of Man Utd’s midfield arrivals making his debut this weekend. Baleba has impressed in training and was involved in a friendly against Lausanne-Sport over the break. He’ll be up against a Spurs midfield tandem that set the Lilywhites back almost $250 million.

CM: Kobbie Mainoo—While Mainoo withdrew from international duty, the dynamic young midfielder is expected to be fit for Spurs’ visit. There’s potential for him to develop a stellar relationship with the physically impressive Baleba in midfield.

RW: Bryan Mbeumo—With Amad Diallo out of action, we’ll likely see Mbeumo start down the right again. The role doesn’t get the best out of him, but he loves playing against Spurs. In 10 meetings, Mbeumo’s scored six times.
AM: Bruno Fernandes—The reigning PFA Player of the Year is waiting for his season to ignite, and you get the feeling that a vulnerable Spurs outfit could allow Fernandes to flourish at Old Trafford.

LW: Marcus Rashford—Rashford is an injury concern after pulling out of the England camp. Like Mainoo, though, there’s an expectation that he won’t miss any time for the Red Devils. The winger is still waiting for his first goal since Carrick brought him back into the fold.

ftbpro_01m4g56997n3.title: Barcelona vs. Getafe: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4g56997n3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 9, 2026La Blaugrana return from the international break with an appetizing home fixture.  / Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Barcelona), X/Getafe C.F. (Getafe)Barcelona can equal their best-ever start to a La Liga campaign by beating Getafe when they return from the international break on Saturday.

La Blaugrana have already clinched seven wins on the spin to kickstart their title defense, moving them five points clear of second-placed Atlético Madrid already. Their attack has been particularly devastating, overpowering every defense that’s attempted to block its path.
Only once in their history (2013–14) have Barça won all eight of their opening La Liga matches, meaning they stand on the edge of history at the Camp Nou this weekend.

The international break has taken its toll on Hansi Flick’s roster, which has been weakened by recent injuries. However, the German has ludicrous quality across his team and the necessary depth required to overcome any fitness issues.

Getafe, who have collected eight points to date, will be fearing the worst as they head to Catalonia. José Bordalás has prioritized defensive structure over creative flair and that will at least help the Azulones keep the score down in what seems an inevitable defeat.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lamine Yamal will lead the charge to victory. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesBarça could hardly be more confident heading into their first match of October and, especially on home soil, they will be expecting to secure their umpteenth high-scoring victory of the campaign.

Raphinha, their leading star this season, will be absent due to fitness issues, slightly weakening Flick’s fearsome forward line. But with Lamine Yamal in an utterly unstoppable mood and Anthony Gordon reaching peak performance, La Blaugrana should still notch a fair few goals when Getafe come to town.

Flick will demand a high level from his players at the Camp Nou, but with one eye on the upcoming Champions League game away at Galatasaray, Barça could take their foot off the gas once the match is won.

Flick confirmed Raphinha will miss the clash as Barcelona proceed with the utmost caution following the Brazilian’s injury scare while on international duty. The German boss could instead call upon summer signing Gabriel Jesus to lead the line.

Joan García should return from injury to start in net, while there might be several changes to the defense in front of him. With Andreas Christensen injured and Eric García battling a minor knee issue, Gerard Martín and Jules Koundé could replace them.

Martín will earn his 100th senior Barcelona appearance should he feature against Getafe, while Koundé will become the club’s most capped French player of all time if he turns out—leapfrogging Eric Abidal on 193 appearances.

Xavi Espart might celebrate his new contract by starting ahead of João Cancelo at left back, while Anthony Gordon should feature ahead of him on the wing having been rested in England’s final UEFA Nations League outing of the break.
Frenkie de Jong and Roony Bardghji are still sidelined.
Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Getafe (4-2-3-1): J. García; Koundé, Cubarsí, Martín, Espart; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, López, Gordon; Jesus.

Mario Martín returns from suspension. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesGetafe are also battling several injury issues ahead of the weekend’s match. Juanmi and Christantus Uche are still missing with long-term injuries, while there are question marks over the availability of Abdel Abqar and Kiko Femenía.
Ex-Real Madrid academy graduate Mario Martín will return in midfield after missing the win over Málaga before the international break through suspension.

At age 34, Nemanja Gudelj provides some invaluable experience elsewhere in midfield following his summer move, while Enes Ünal should start up front yet again following three goals so far during his second stint with Getafe.
Getafe Predicted Lineup vs. Barcelona (4-5-1): Soria; García, Djené, Romero, Mojica; Azón, Terrats, Gudelj, Martín, Satriano; Ünal.

ftbpro_01m4g5xpx0cf.title: Man Utd vs. Tottenham: High-Pressure Fixture Could Shape the Season
ftbpro_01m4g5xpx0cf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack2:00 AM EDTMichael Carrick suddenly finds himself under pressure. / Tiego Grenho/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWe’ve not entered ’El Sackico’ territory yet, but there’s no overlooking the significance of Saturday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur for both managers.
It’s a battle of the crisis clubs, as Michael Carrick’s 12th-placed Red Devils welcome Roberto De Zerbi’s bottom-of-the-table Lilywhites.
These two have struggled to escape mediocrity and outright incompetence for much of their recent histories, even if Man Utd haven’t yet sunk to the depths Spurs flirted with last term.

But there’s a sense that the Red Devils, after the highs overseen by Carrick during the second half of last season, are merely in the midst of an all-too-familiar cycle that will ultimately end with another manager losing their job.
As for Spurs ... well, they just want something to cling on to.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Carrick’s first full season was always going to bring about stiffer challenges. / CARLOS JASSO/AFP/Getty ImagesCarrick was robust in his response to talk of his potential firing before the break, labeling it “nonsense.” But that came before Man Utd’s draw at Craven Cottage, an indifferent display barely salvaged by Matheus Cunha’s late deflected strike.

It was a performance that drew fierce, hyperbolic criticism from prominent Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville, who said Man Utd’s early second-half performance against Fulham was the “worst 15 minutes” he’d seen from any Red Devils outfit.

Neville’s slander was predicated on the lack of effort and intensity shown by Carrick’s players, decrying their dynamism while they sat in a zonal 4-4-2 mid-block. But Man Utd’s walking out of possession is instructed. Carrick’s zagging, with an absence of man-to-man, while the rest of the division zigs with high-octane affairs predicated on out-dueling and outrunning the opposition.

And as Michael Cox pointed out in an article for The Athletic, league leaders Man City sit alongside the Red Devils with the joint-fewest high-speed runs and sprints. Liverpool and City have also covered less ground than United through five games. More running doesn’t equate to an improved performance.

Still, the role Neville and Co. play in shaping public opinion shouldn’t go unnoticed. They’re remarkably influential. Although plenty suggested Neville’s criticism was over the top, such comments can sow seeds of discontent, perhaps indirectly.

The modern-day manager has such a short shelf life, with results demanded from the outset. Clubs are desperate for their Jürgen Klopp or Mikel Arteta equivalent, but are so often unwilling to let the project marinate. We’re all so impatient.

And the job Carrick has taken on condemns him to win. "This is Manchester United Football Club we’re talking about here." His excellent work as interim manager was predicated on a common-sense approach that allowed United’s best player, Bruno Fernandes, to flourish. He didn’t reinvent the wheel, and nobody should ask him to either. It worked! No Premier League team earned more points last season after Carrick’s arrival than the Red Devils.

Bruno Fernandes thrived under Carrick during the second half of last season. / Catherine Ivill/Getty ImagesUltimately, he’s a victim of heightened expectations that are perhaps unjust, no matter the size of the institution he currently leads. His first full season at the helm was always going to bring about stiffer challenges with extra games, having benefited from free midweeks during the second half of last season.

INEOS rebuilt his midfield astutely, but was enough done in the summer to compete fiercely on multiple fronts? There are holes in defense, and Carrick is struggling to find the right attacking balance in the absence of Benjamin Šeško.

New issues are seemingly cropping up with each passing week, but Carrick has earned the right to be given the chance to fix them. Defeat here, though, and there’s no doubt that Eddie Howe, masquerading as the Grim Reaper, will feel as if it’s time to start knocking on the Manchester United manager’s door.

Club-record signing Sandro Tonali hasn’t yet found his feet. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesAnge Postecoglou may have provided one of the best moments in Spurs’ modern history, but at what cost? By sacrificing Premier League results in favor of Europa League prioritization, he paradoxically desensitized a club to losing. It became habitual.

The decision to part ways in the aftermath of Bilbao, ushering in Thomas Frank, proved horribly erroneous, yet plenty at the time understood why such a course of action was taken. Postecoglou was unlikely to ever build something long-term, even if he was one of the very few managers who seemingly understood what it meant to lead Tottenham Hotspur.

The extent of their demise last season meant an under-pressure and unpopular hierarchy felt they had no choice but to hand Roberto De Zerbi the keys. It took a mammoth salary and a guarantee of borderline total control for the Italian to take the job on, but it did pay off. Spurs remain a Premier League club as a result.
Yet by dancing with the combustible De Zerbi, questions have resurfaced regarding Spurs’ long-term outlook.

ftbpro_01m4g69h5b25.title: ‘Ridiculous’—Jose Mourinho Slams Treatment of Kylian Mbappe in Trademark Rant
ftbpro_01m4g69h5b25.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:30 AM EDTKylian Mbappé (left) has attracted unwanted attention. / Pressinphoto/IMAGOReal Madrid manager José Mourinho lashed out at what he described as a media campaign to scrutinize Kylian Mbappé over the Frenchman’s conduct during the international break.

Mbappé was criticized for his behavior after suffering a knee injury during France duty. He was photographed outside a nightclub in Paris and also posted a video of himself cycling in Switzerland just days after Mourinho insisted players should not ride bikes because of the injury risk.

It has led to shock, speculative claims that something is brewing beneath the surface at Madrid, with some suggesting Mourinho and Mbappé were not seeing eye-to-eye and even raising the idea of a potential departure from the Bernabéu for the French forward.
Clearly, Mourinho is not interested in the noise.
“It’s ridiculous,” Mourinho said of the criticism of Mbappé. “I thought there were enough real ‘cases’ in the football world in the last few weeks, but it seems like they weren’t enough.

“There are giant cases like the [Manchester City] one, like the old story you don’t like to talk about [the Negreira case], like the difficult situation in my country with Cristiano Ronaldo and his coach. But it hasn’t been enough. Real Madrid is Real Madrid. I thought the first question might be about real things, a difficult game, but here we are.”

Mbappé (center) has been training with the team. / Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty ImagesMourinho refused to let the issue rest and, instead, offered an explanation for everything that had been ruthlessly picked apart by those he accused of intentionally trying to stir the pot.

“I don’t lie,” he said. “The truth is that in this period, Real Madrid’s players have been exemplary in their professional situation. Those who were injured came straight to Valdebebas, got their diagnosis and got their rehab plan.

“Mbappé was here, he got his diagnosis, he went to an external consultant—his knee has a history that you can’t forget—and there was total agreement with Real Madrid’s diagnosis and this external consultant. In terms of his recovery, you don’t have to know all the details. But then we get into the area of looking for problems.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“[In Paris] it was a club that wasn’t a club. It was a club that had been transformed for a private event. Then in Switzerland, it was just a hotel, with little houses, and each house had some bikes to get to where the restaurants and spa was. It was absolute tranquility.
“You don’t have to be Einstein to see that [getting fans to boo Mbappé] is the objective. I hope the Bernabéu can be fair, and that means being intelligent, being able to read between the lines.

“One thing I promise is that when a Real Madrid player doesn’t behave like a Real Madrid player, they won’t see that player on the bench. They won’t have the chance to whistle, because they’ll be at home.”
Mbappé suffered a knee injury on international duty. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesAt the end of everything came an actual update on Mbappé’s injury.
Mourinho refused to reveal the specifics of the Frenchman’s recovery plan, but did confirm fans can expect to see Mbappé in the starting lineup when Villarreal visit the Bernabéu on Saturday.
“So tomorrow, Mbappé will play,” Mourinho concluded. “He won’t be on the bench, and if he plays, it’s because I’m sure that he hasn’t failed Real Madrid. He hasn’t failed to fulfil his obligations.”

ftbpro_01m4g8ty4xvx.title: Hansi Flick Reveals the Barcelona Games Raphinha Will Miss—and His Replacement
ftbpro_01m4g8ty4xvx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:30 AM EDTRaphinha transforms the way that Barcelona play. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesHansi Flick has confirmed that Barcelona will be without the most in-form player on the planet for at least the next two matches.

Raphinha flagged an issue in his right thigh during Brazil’s draining tour of Australia last month. The prolific forward withdrew from the camp before even making it to the Indian leg of the team’s continent hopping, sparking fears as to how Barcelona would be able to replace a player with 14 goals in eight club games already this term.

Flick allayed concerns over the severity of Raphinha’s issue. “The picture [scan] showed something, but it’s not a big injury,” he assured assembled reporters at Friday’s press conference. “He is doing well, has no pain and can do everything.”
However, precaution would have to be exercised. “He needs a bit more time,” Flick added. “It’s something we have to take care of because last season he had three injuries there.”
That sense of concern has taken the form of Raphinha’s immediate benching.

Galatasaray fans always put on a show. / Elif Ozturk/Anadolu/Getty ImagesFlick will be without La Liga’s leading scorer for two games of differing difficulty; a league clash with Getafe and a daunting trip to Türkiye to take on Galatasaray.

Getafe head to Camp Nou on Saturday with a woeful record and other priorities perhaps on their mind. The Madrid club have never beaten the Catalan giants at their spiritual home since first heading to the venue in 2005 (19 defeats, four draws). Getafe have only spent 70 combined minutes leading Barcelona across 34 and a half hours of soccer at Camp Nou (3.4%).

José Bordalas’s battlers, who tend to give every other club in the division a bloody nose aside from Barcelona, also have the added distraction of their first UEFA Conference League league phase tie on the following Thursday.

Barça are also in European action next week and Raphinha will have to sit out the club’s descent into the bear pit of Galatasaray’s RAMS Park. The defending Turkish champions have lost just one home match across all competitions in the last 11 months, fending off the likes of Atlético Madrid, Juventus and Liverpool during that run of riotous form.
The absence of Raphinha, Flick’s self-appointed captain, for such a daunting fixture will test the skills of Barcelona’s remaining leaders, including 19-year-old Lamine Yamal.

It remains to be seen if Raphinha will be back for the following weekend’s trip to Real Betis. There is a flurry of key games on the horizon, including a Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain (Oct. 20) and the first Clásico of the season against Real Madrid (Oct. 25).

Gabriel Jesus and Raphinha could be trading places. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesFlick clearly doesn’t value the element of surprise. After letting Getafe and Galatasaray know that they wouldn’t have to deal with the unique threat posed by Raphinha, Barcelona’s manager revealed that “the idea” was for Gabriel Jesus to take the place of his compatriot.

The former Arsenal striker made a hurried move to Catalonia at the end of the summer transfer window once Barça belatedly accepted that Julián Alvarez could not be pried away from Atlético Madrid. Jesus has been limited to four substitute appearances at this early stage of his career at Camp Nou, but the two goals he has managed to score in that time has convinced Flick of his qualities.
“He has improved a lot and adapted to our style and how we want to play,” Flick said of the new recruit. “Gabriel has trained really well the last few weeks, and we are very happy with him.”

Despite his scoring start, Jesus’s main task as Raphinha’s stand-in will be applying Flick’s feverish high press. “As captain, he goes and everyone follows,” the manager has gushed when reviewing Raphinha’s performances. “We always start with the No. 9 and he has that incredible hunger and intensity, the mentality and attitude we need.” Replicating that energy will be Jesus’s biggest challenge.

ftbpro_01m4g9e7tv8v.title: Liverpool vs. Man City: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4g9e7tv8v.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 10, 2026Sunday’s headline fixture promises entertainment. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Liverpool), Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Man City)Liverpool and Manchester City will stage a tantalizing Premier League duel at Anfield this Sunday, one that is brimming with narrative on and off the field.

This is the first outing for the Cityzens since they were found guilty of financial doping over a nine-year period. The verdict has united the soccer world against them and the Reds will be the first side to attempt to deliver their own form of justice this weekend.

Liverpool, who have finished runner-up to Premier League-winning City teams on three occasions since 2009, are seeking a statement victory to help ignite the Andoni Iraola era and lift them up the standings. They remain unbeaten under the new manager, but have so far won just two of their five matches in the league.

City, meanwhile, have won all five of their Premier League matches under Enzo Maresca, who is remarkably confident that the club’s appeal against its financial misconduct charges will prove successful. He’ll hope his players mirror his belief when stepping onto the Anfield turf this weekend as they bid for a sixth straight win. The welcome is sure to be hostile.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Man City won all three games against Liverpool last season. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesWell, where to start with this one?

Liverpool’s matches with City always deliver fireworks, no matter the venue or competition, but the upcoming clash carries significant weight following recent revelations about the scale of City’s financial misconduct between 2009 and 2018.
The Reds, who have every right to feel particularly aggrieved by City’s cheating, will be determined to enjoy the last laugh in front of a deafening Anfield crowd which will spur on Iraola’s side.

It’s impossible to predict exactly how City’s players will react to the verdict on the field. Erling Haaland urged supporters to “stick together, enjoy the ride and smile,” but will his teammates be able to stay so composed? Only time will tell.
No matter the outcome, this appears an unmissable occasion.

Iraola has ruled Isak and Gakpo out of contention for the match, with the former battling an ankle issue and the latter a thigh problem. It remains to be seen when they will return to the fold, with Liverpool in Champions League action next Wednesday against LASK.

With Hugo Ekitiké also sidelined and Federico Chiesa still a doubt in the final third, Iraola will have to find some creative solutions. As a result, Bradley Barcola could lead the line ahead of young Lewis Koumas, with Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz flanking the Frenchman.
In better news for the Reds, Iraola has confirmed that Jérémy Jacquet is available after suffering a slight hamstring injury with France. He will start alongside Virgil van Dijk in defense.

Florian Wirtz should continue in the No. 10 role despite his disappointing club form, with Alexis Mac Allister partnering Dominik Szoboszlai behind the German. Ryan Gravenberch will most likely be used from the bench.
Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are still recovering from long-term injuries.
Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Man City (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araújo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister; Muñoz, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Barcola.
With Haaland cleared to play at Anfield, Maresca’s only injury concerns center around Antoine Semenyo and Nico O’Reilly after they were both forced to withdraw early from international duty.

Semenyo has since returned to team training with City, recovering from the swollen leg which saw him leave the Ghana camp. O’Reilly, however, remains a major doubt and is unlikely to start at Anfield.
City will definitely be without Phil Foden, who is still suspended following his red card in the Manchester derby. Iliman Ndiaye will be deployed on the right wing as his replacement.
A new-look midfield of Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández will protect the back four, which should include Matheus Nunes, Rúben Dias, Marc Guéhi and Joško Gvardiol.

ftbpro_01m4gcp5srmr.title: Chelsea vs. Bournemouth: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4gcp5srmr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 9, 2026Chelsea welcome the Cherries to Stamford Bridge as the Premier League returns from an extended international break. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesA three-week international break means it feels like an age since Chelsea and Bournemouth were last in Premier League action, and the two teams meet at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Chelsea kick-started the previous gameweek with a torrid Friday night defeat at Brentford. Xabi Alonso’s depleted outfit were eventually bullied by the impressive Bees, having struggled to lay a glove on the hosts in a drab opening 45 minutes.
As a result, the Blues, regarded as outsiders for the title even after they fell at Arsenal on Sept. 6, are down in 10th, having failed to win any of their previous three encounters.

Bournemouth’s slow start to the domestic campaign after replacing Andoni Iraola with Marco Rose has slipped under the radar, yet there doesn’t seem to be much concern on the south coast. The Cherries are one of just three winless teams through five games, and were beaten by their former boss’s new side, Liverpool, in a forgettable encounter before the break.

Their first venture into Europe should take priority this season, but Rose won’t want this Premier League malaise to persist after the break. This is far too good a team to be slogging it out toward the foot of the table.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Chelsea’s attack has sung on home soil. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesRose shouldn’t be thinking too much about Sturm Graz’s visit on Thursday, even if it’s the first time the Vitality Stadium hosts a European fixture.

It’s about time Bournemouth moved up the Premier League table, with FotMob’s data suggesting they’re the joint-biggest underperformers in terms of points after five games. They should’ve collected seven, but have only mustered three.

And while Chelsea have appeared defensively vulnerable, the Blues are set to celebrate the return of crucial personnel that will elevate Xabi Alonso’s framework. They’ve got a good record in this fixture, too, and have proven to be tough to slow down on home soil. Alonso will already be feeling the heat if they’re beaten in front of their fans this weekend.

Chelsea should have two key players back in midfield. /    Some have suggested that now would be the ideal time for Alonso to revert to the back four we saw at the start of preseason, especially with a couple of key players still missing.

However, the Spaniard may not yet give up on the back three, and will perhaps want to see the efficacy of the system with a stronger midfield. Chelsea are expected to have Caicedo and James available this weekend. Caicedo is yet to make a single start for the Blues this season, while captain James missed the Brentford defeat due to injury.
Pedro skipped international duty because of a knee issue, and while he has been passed fit for this one, he may have to start off on the bench. Veteran striker Danny Welbeck is waiting in the wings.
Cole Palmer should be fine to feature from the outset, and new signing Marco Palestra could make his Premier League bow.
Chelsea predicted lineup vs. Bournemouth (3-4-2-1): Martínez; Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, James, Caicedo, Chavarría; Palmer, Rogers; Welbeck.

Alex Scott is a fresh injury absentee. /     Bournemouth were dealt a significant blow over the break, learning that Alex Scott, a target for Chelsea, will be sidelined for several weeks due to a thigh injury sustained on international duty.

Manager Rose refused to blame England for the setback, and the new Cherries boss should feel as if he’s well placed to deal with Scott’s absence, despite the fixture increase this month. Tyler Adams is expected to partner Lewis Cook at Stamford Bridge, although Ryan Christie could find himself in a deeper midfield role.

Eli Junior Kroupi is also out of action for the visitors, but Justin Kluivert, Veljko Milosavljević, Amine Adli and Julián Araujo could all return to Rose’s matchday roster. David Brooks is also fine despite pulling out of the Wales camp during the break.
Former Chelsea goalkeeper Đorđe Petrović will start between the posts for the away side.
Bournemouth predicted lineup vs. Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Petrović; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Cook, Adams; Rayan, Christie, Tavernier; Evanilson.

ftbpro_01m4gfw1te5d.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s Inspiring Postgame Team Talk Shows Off New USMNT Culture
ftbpro_01m4gfw1te5d.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell12:30 PM EDTMauricio Pochettino is forging a new identity with the USMNT. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesA new era is dawning for the U.S. men’s national team, one headlined by players who actually “want to belong” to Mauricio Pochettino’s squad—and the results are undeniable.

The Argentine boss turned heads when he omitted the likes of Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun from his roster for four fall friendlies, instead trusting a wealth of uncapped players and eight teenagers to take on Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

While the USMNT’s biggest names sat at home, Pochettino’s new blend of fresh faces and reliable veterans collected four convincing wins, scoring 12 goals and only conceding three in their first action since bowing out of the World Cup in the round of 16.

There was a noticeable swagger to the Stars and Stripes, who looked completely reborn and re-energized by the promising youngsters filling out Pochettino’s lineup. The manager largely attributed the strong results to his squad’s spirit, highlighting the culture shift in a rousing speech in the dressing room.
True love for this game we play ❤️⚽️Mauricio Pochettino's postmatch speech following an unbeaten fall camp 🎥 pic.twitter.com/63vETusljh

“It was an amazing [break] together. Now it’s our responsibility to keep that level,” Pochettino said. “It’s not win or lose. It’s to keep that atmosphere every time that we come here, every time that we are involved. That is the most important.

“It’s not a coincidence that we won four games. It’s not a coincidence. It’s not easy to play against Peru. It’s not easy to play against Chile. It’s not easy to play against Mexico. It’s not easy against Canada.
“Why? Why did we do what we did? Because the energy was amazing. And because you want to belong here. And it’s not conditional.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Christian Pulisic (right) is no longer a mainstay with the USMNT. / John Dorton/USSF/Getty ImagesFor so long, the USMNT had a culture problem. Even in Pochettino’s early tenure, many players in red, white and blue lacked any type of hunger or burning passion to perform.

Playing friendlies looked like a chore. Hardly any of the team’s biggest stars showed up to the 2025 Gold Cup. And when they did appear, they often fell flat, even in major tournaments like the 2024 Copa América.

The narrative chiefly haunted Pulisic, who came off like he wanted to pick and choose when he represented the USMNT. The 28-year-old, for instance, explicitly told Pochettino that he wanted to play friendlies before the Gold Cup, but not the actual Gold Cup in 2025.

Pochettino responded by leaving him at home for that entire break, reinforcing the idea that he only wanted players who wanted to represent the USMNT. If the big stars didn’t want to come out and compete for a trophy, then he would find the players who would.

Over a year later and Pochettino continues to make a similar statement, just now on a grander scale. MLS youngsters Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis earned a place in his squad over Pulisic, Balogun and Tim Weah. Sebastian Berhalter looks primed to be a starter in midfield for years to come, displacing McKennie. Gio Reyna is back in the fold as well, doing whatever he can to get back to the heights he once reached as a teenager.

As Pochettino said, representing the U.S. is no longer “conditional.” It’s every international break, every friendly, every minute on the pitch. Those who only want to show up for the big moments—and then fail to deliver—will not show up at all.

Mauricio Pochettino wants to build a team strong enough to make a deep run at the 2030 World Cup. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesIt would be easy to get carried away after such a faultless break, especially for the young stars riding the high of impressing during their debut camp. But Pochettino reminded his players the work is only just beginning.

“Our worry now, our responsibility now is to keep it this way,” Pochettino said. “You need to go back to your clubs, be humble, [take on] more responsibility because now you are internationals. And you need to come back and every day, be better, work hard—harder than your teammates.”
The Argentine cautioned his players against acting like the “top guy” following such a successful break and urged them to keep doing “more.”
“This is the only way we are going to increase our level and improve and improve and be better,” he finished.
The 2030 World Cup might still be four years away, but Pochettino is laying the groundwork early enough so this time, he has a squad of players who will not falter under the bright lights.

ftbpro_01m4gj6wxd8q.title: Man Utd vs. Tottenham: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4gj6wxd8q.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 9, 2026Manchester United host Tottenham on Saturday. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Man Utd), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Tottenham)The Premier League’s crisis clubs are back in action after a much-needed bumper international break, as Manchester United welcome Tottenham Hotspur to Old Trafford.

Saturday’s clash sees the underwhelming Red Devils take on the Premier League’s basement dwellers, with Spurs notching just a couple of points through five matches. Their first league goals of the season didn’t arrive until Aston Villa rocked up in N17 before the break, but they found themselves 3–0 behind before their late surge.
The underlying numbers suggest Roberto De Zerbi isn’t far away from getting things to “click,” having overseen a major rebuild in the summer with a record amount splashed on 10 fresh faces.
The drastic overhaul after last season’s frightening relegation flirt heightened expectations heading into the campaign, and Spurs, like Saturday’s hosts, are yet to deliver.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

No Premier League team earned more points than Manchester United after Michael Carrick arrived on an interim basis last term, with their ascent during the second half of the campaign earning them a return to the Champions League.

However, it’s been a struggle since Carrick took the job on full time. The Red Devils have already exited the Carabao Cup and earned just one league win—a 5–2 rout of the newly promoted Ipswich Town. Before the break, United lost to a 10-man Manchester City in the derby and needed a late deflected strike from Matheus Cunha to salvage a point at Fulham, who were then rooted to the foot of the table.

Carrick’s seat had started to warm before the break. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesThe two managers’ jobs aren’t quite on the line yet, but both are certainly feeling the heat. Carrick laughed off sack talk before the break, while De Zerbi still has the goodwill of the Tottenham fanbase after saving the club from relegation last season.

Still, the malaise cannot persist. For United, Saturday’s clash is the start of a hectic run before the end of October, with five games scheduled in 18 days. Given their indifferent opening to the new campaign, it feels like a pivotal month for the Red Devils.

And this is a fixture that hasn’t been too kind to them as of late. There’s been a lack of “Lads, it’s Tottenham” talk in Manchester, with Spurs enjoying an eight-game unbeaten run before United claimed a 2–0 victory earlier this year.
The Lilywhites have no reason to fear a trip to the Theatre of Dreams, and victory here would surely ignite a season that’s yet to get off the ground.
Carlos Baleba is expected to make his Man Utd debut. /   There have been a couple of concerning injury updates out of Manchester after the three-week break.

Carrick has confirmed that Patrick Dorgu, who missed a sustained period due to a hamstring injury last season, will spend another spell on the sidelines this month. The Man Utd boss also revealed that Noussair Mazraoui and Benjamin Šeško won’t be ready for Saturday’s game.

Šeško was among those who withdrew from international duty, but there’s more hope surrounding England duo Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford. Amad Diallo is also closing in on a comeback, while Carlos Baleba is set to make his debut for the club.
With Šeško absent, Matheus Cunha will likely lead United’s attack.
Man Utd predicted lineup vs. Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Baleba, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha.

It’s time for De Zerbi to use his two new midfielders in tandem. /   Tottenham escaped the international break relatively unscathed on the injury front, with De Zerbi confirming that Dutch defensive duo Jan Paul van Hecke and Micky van de Ven are available for the trip to Old Trafford.
Van Hecke withdrew from Xavi Hernández’s Oranje camp with a foot injury, while Van de Ven has been dealing with a hand problem.

Pedro Porro and Dejan Kulusevski will travel with the group, but neither are playing a part. Porro sustained a hamstring injury before the break, and Kulusevski is edging closer to a long-awaited comeback. The Swede has been out of action since May 2025, yet remarkably, he’s still started a Premier League match more recently than James Maddison.

The English No. 10 missed the bulk of last season with an ACL tear, and is being carefully managed at the start of 2026–27. De Zerbi said he suffered another fitness setback during the break but is still expected to feature at the Theatre of Dreams.

ftbpro_01m4gkv64e91.title: Iraola Teases Surprise Selection Against Man City After Isak Gut Punch
ftbpro_01m4gkv64e91.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray1:30 PM EDTAndoni Iraola has some selection dilemmas ahead of the weekend’s game with Manchester City. / Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesAndoni Iraola has confirmed that Liverpool will be without Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo for Sunday’s Premier League encounter with Manchester City following injuries sustained on international duty.

The forwards were both forced to withdraw from their national teams following fitness issues suffered during matches in the UEFA Nations League, and the weekend’s match will come too soon for them to be involved.
Isak left the Sweden camp prematurely following a thigh injury in his nation’s first match of the break, while Gakpo featured twice for the Netherlands before spraining his ankle.

“Unfortunately for us, both got injuries during the international break,” Iraola revealed on Friday. “As a club manager, you are always waiting until the games end, that the doctor doesn’t call you and then gives you bad news.
“But in this case we’ve been unlucky with Alex and Cody—both of them are injured and they are not going to be involved on Sunday.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The Spaniard added: “Cody has an ankle injury. He has had some before in his career and it’s a matter of him dealing with the pain because when you twist your ankle... it was a really bad tackle, I think. He is doing things individually but [he’s] not ready for Sunday.
“And Alex has a thigh injury. It’s a small injury but it’s a muscle injury. The same [as Gakpo], whenever he feels ready.
“They both don’t look like long-term [problems]—we will be analyzing day to day. But they are not going to arrive on Sunday.”

Lewis Koumas could be an unorthodox solution. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesWith Hugo Ekitiké among Liverpool’s long-term absentees, Iraola finds himself without a specialist center forward for City’s visit. Federico Chiesa, who is another option as a striker, could also miss out having yet to play this season due to injury.
That means Iraola will be forced to conjure a creative solution and academy graduate Lewis Koumas could provide an unorthodox answer.
“A full No. 9, it’s true we probably have only Koumas [vs. City], but we have some other options, wingers who have played up front in other teams.
“Koumas has our trust. He has already shown in important minutes that he is ready to go.”

The 21-year-old is appreciated by Iraola, who was key in the decision to keep him at the club for the current campaign rather than sanctioning another loan spell. He’s been used up front this season despite also being comfortable on the wings, and he recently started the 3–1 Carabao Cup victory over Tottenham Hotspur.

Bradley Barcola has played as a striker before. / Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesHowever, Bradley Barcola is perhaps the more realistic replacement for Isak this weekend. The summer signing featured up front infrequently for both Lyon and Paris Saint-Germain, but Iraola believes he’s capable of leading the line.

“He is a top player for us,” enthused Iraola. “I think he can play in any position up front. He probably has played more as a left winger but has played a little bit as a striker, has played even more as a right winger. I think he can cover the three positions up front.

Jérémy Jacquet is already a guaranteed starter. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesIt wasn’t all doom and gloom on the injury front for Liverpool as Iraola revealed that Jérémy Jacquet would be fit and available to start against City despite an injury scare while representing France.
The young center back, who made his senior debut for Les Bleus over the break, was omitted from their final Nations League match with a slight hamstring complaint.

“Yeah, he’s fit, he’s ready to go," Iraola revealed. “I think he didn’t play with the national team [in the] last game because of protection. But he should be fine. We still need to train tomorrow but he’s fine.”
Jacquet won plaudits for two fantastic performances with France in games against Belgium and Italy, echoing the significant praise he’s received early in his Liverpool career.

ftbpro_01m4gp306p2w.title: 'Closely Monitoring’—Chelsea Track Barcelona Star in Desperate Midfield Search
ftbpro_01m4gp306p2w.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 9, 2026Xabi Alonso needs a midfield reinforcement to get Chelsea back on top.  / John Walton/PA Images/Getty ImagesAnother flashpoint emerged in the summer for Frenkie de Jong at Barcelona, and its lasting impact could reportedly see the midfielder thrust into Xabi Alonso’s arms at Chelsea.
The Dutchman, who arrived with great expectations after playing a leading role in Ajax’s fairytale to the Champions League semifinals in 2018–19, has had a rather complicated career in Catalonia.

When fit and firing, De Jong is one of Europe’s finest midfielders, and Hansi Flick has constantly reiterated his importance to what the German sets out to achieve every week. Still, it’s fair to say that even seven years after his €75 million ($84 million switch), De Jong has struggled to garner universal support from Culers (and the local media).

Resentment has been rife throughout his time at the club, primarily because of the mammoth salary he was reportedly on after joining in 2019. It was the sort of contract that thrust Barcelona into its perilous financial situation, meaning they couldn’t retain the great Lionel Messi in 2021.

Injuries have often arrived at inopportune moments for De Jong, too, and his latest, sustained at the World Cup, reportedly sparked a disagreement between club and player regarding the best course of action to take for his recovery. De Jong opted against surgery and is progressing well.
It’ll be a crucial period for the Dutchman once he returns, with competition rife and transfer interest unlikely to ever go away. He may be forced into a big decision next year.

Chelsea are light in midfield. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesManchester United most memorably made a play for De Jong while his old Ajax manager Erik ten Hag was at the helm of the Red Devils in 2022. De Jong would later admit he considered United’s offer before deciding to remain at Barcelona, so Casemiro rocked up at Old Trafford instead.

Fast forward to this summer and Man Utd completed a midfield rebuild without thinking about De Jong. But a Premier League rival may tempt the 29-year-old next year as they aim to bolster their engine room.

SPORT report Chelsea are keeping an eye on De Jong‘s situation at Barcelona. The Blues lost Enzo Fernández during the final week of the summer transfer window and were unable to sign a replacement on Deadline Day.

As a result, Xabi Alonso is rather short-handed in midfield. In their 3–0 defeat to Brentford before the international break, veteran Jordan Henderson partnered Valentín Barco as Moisés Caicedo and Reece James sat out injured. Roméo Lavia was an unused substitute in west London and has struggled to stay fit throughout his Chelsea career.
Fernández has undoubtedly left a gaping void at Stamford Bridge, even if Alonso has changed to a 3-4-2-1 and thus needs just two midfielders.

De Jong’s injury record may not be great, but his quality cannot be denied. Multiple clubs have tried to bring him to the Premier League in recent years, and it’ll take a serious effort from Chelsea to convince the Dutchman to leave Barcelona, unless there’s a serious breakdown in relations before the end of the season.

De Jong is expected to return from injury this month. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesSPORT suggest De Jong remains committed to Barcelona, but there‘s no denying that he‘s reached a critical point in his career with the Blaugrana, even if his contract doesn’t expire until 2029.

The way De Jong and the Netherlands’ medical team handled his knee injury angered Flick, and although the club is ultimately happy with how the midfielder has recovered from the setback, local media would lead you to believe that tension is bubbling beneath the surface.

De Jong is confident that he’ll reclaim his starting role in Flick’s midfield, but he has his work cut out for him after Barça signed Rodri in the summer. With Pedri and Gavi both adored and Marc Bernal only getting better, the Dutchman doesn’t merely need to convince Flick. He also must prove to the skeptical factions of supporters that he’s worthy of playing a key role upon his return.

Flick believes the 29-year-old will be back in action slightly earlier than expected after he returned to training during the break. A first appearance of the season against Real Betis next weekend is in the cards, just in time for El Clásico on Oct. 25.
