ftbpro_01m4gphb5w5e.title: ‘Ready to Go’—Chelsea Receive Major Boost on Eve of Premier League Return
ftbpro_01m4gphb5w5e.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:15 PM EDTMoises Caicedo (right) has only played once this season. /  Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesChelsea will welcome Moisés Caciedo back into the matchday squad for Saturday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth after Xabi Alonso confirmed the midfielder’s recovery from injury.
An awkward start to Alonso’s reign has been exacerbated by Caicedo’s absence, with a calf injury limiting him to just 14 minutes played across the opening weeks of the campaign.

Without their midfield general, Chelsea have endured significant defensive struggles, conceding 10 times across their past four matches in all competitions. Luckily, the extended three-week international break has given the 24-year-old time to regain his fitness.

“Yes, he is ready to go,” Alonso confirmed when asked about Caicedo’s availability against Bournemouth. “We have used the time with Moi to get him back fit. He has been training well and he is okay to go.”

Alonso was forced to field an unorthodox midfield pairing of Valentín Barco and Jordan Henderson in the dismal 3–0 defeat to Brentford before the international window, but Caicedo’s comeback significantly eases his concerns in a department where Chelsea already find themselves short of options.

Chelsea will welcome back some key players on Saturday. / Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty ImagesThere was more positive news on the injury front, too, with João Pedro, Reece James and Cole Palmer all returning to training ahead of Bournemouth’s visit. Summer signing Marco Palestra, who has been battling injury all season, has also been involved as he closes in on his official Chelsea debut.
“They have all been able to train, some of them earlier than others—and Marco Palestra as well. That was the plan,” Alonso revealed.
“We knew that going into Brentford we had some players struggling but they have trained well and are ready to go.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

James and Pedro were both sorely missed during the Brentford defeat following injury setbacks, while Palmer withdrew from the England squad to manage his workload. Their imminent return could prove absolutely vital to the outcome of Saturday’s match at Stamford Bridge.

The only negative update issued by Alonso during his prematch press conference involved Jamie Gittens, who is sidelined “for a few weeks” with an ankle problem sustained while representing England’s U-21s.

Alonso has overseen three Premier League games without victory. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesAlonso will be buoyed by the return of some integral first-teamers ahead of a vital clash with Bournemouth. After three Premier League games without victory, it’s essential the west Londoners return to winning ways.
While the Spaniard is optimistic about the future for the Blues, he’s admitted that the club’s current form is unacceptable.

“It’s not just the defence, it’s the attack as well. The way we attack helps the way we defend, so everything is related. And many parts that are still in development,” Alonso told Stan Sport when quizzed about Chelsea’s issues.
“I have the feeling it will get better, but at the moment it’s not been good enough.”

Chelsea enter the sixth round of Premier League matches in 10th place after collecting just two wins to date. Swift improvements are required if the club are going to qualify for Europe at the end of the Alonso’s debut campaign.

ftbpro_01m4gpzs173k.title: MLS Commissioner Reveals How Messi, Beckham Changed the League Forever
ftbpro_01m4gpzs173k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:30 PM EDTLionel Messi and David Beckham have each helped transform MLS. / Chandan Khanna/AFP/Getty ImagesLionel Messi’s high profile transfer to Inter Miami might have brought millions of new viewers to MLS, but league commissioner Don Garber has insisted that without David Beckham, “there’s probably no Major League Soccer.”

To new viewers, Beckham’s connection to MLS lies in south Florida, where he acts as a co-owner to reigning MLS Cup winners Inter Miami. The Manchester United legend is often in a suit and tie, sitting in the stands at Nu Stadium while Messi & Co. put on a show for those watching in person and around the world.

But before he was an owner, Beckham was the biggest star to ever play in MLS. After four seasons with Real Madrid, the England international made the head-turning move to LA Galaxy in 2007, putting the MLS outfit—and the league—on the map in a way never done before.

Even 19 years later, Garber still credits Beckham with making MLS a desirable destination for European stars. “David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.,” he said, via ESPN.
“He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.
“It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there’s probably no Major League Soccer.”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Gareth Bale ended his career at LAFC. / Kevork Djansezian/Getty ImagesBeckham helped the LA Galaxy reach the pinnacle of MLS, starring alongside Landon Donovan to bring home two MLS Cups during his tenure with the Black & Gold. As the world watched the six-time Premier League winner tear up the league, others suddenly viewed playing soccer in the United States as a viable option.
As Garber mentioned, Henry eventually came and played for Red Bull New York. Although he never lifted an MLS Cup, he still helped the team claim the 2013 Supporters’ Shield.

Robbie Keane also made the move, joining Beckham in L.A. where he won three MLS Cups and was named the 2014 MLS MVP. His success was something Kaká could only dream of during his years struggling with Orlando City.
Frank Lampard and David Villa teamed up at New York City FC. Didier Drogba tried his luck CF Montréal, much like Steven Gerrard at LA Galaxy.

Wayne Rooney made D.C. his short-lived home, while Zlatan Ibrahimović spent two seasons with the Galaxy. Gareth Bale’s blockbuster move to LAFC ended after just 13 appearances, but he collected an MLS Cup along the way.
Despite the varying degrees of success, the superstars all helped elevate MLS’s standing in world soccer—but Messi made it explode.

Lionel Messi (center) and David Beckham (right) helped bring an MLS Cup home to Inter Miami. / Elsa/Getty ImagesFor all the credit Garber handed out to Beckham, he of course had to throw some Messi’s way as well. After all, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner is the best player to represent the league, even in the twilight of his career.
“Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi,” Garber said.

Indeed, Messi helped take MLS to new heights. Soon after he joined Inter Miami, the pool of superstars crossing the Atlantic Ocean to play in North America got even larger. Barcelona legends Sergio Busquets, Jordi Alba and Luis Suárez all teamed up for the Herons—and secured the club’s first-ever MLS Cup last season.

Rodrigo De Paul left Atlético Madrid to pitch in as well, and Casemiro made south Florida his home this summer after bidding farewell to Manchester United. Further west, Robert Lewandowski stars for Chicago Fire and Son Heung-min is the face of LAFC. Thomas Müller also just recently extended his stay with the Vancouver Whitecaps.

Even after Messi hangs up his boots, his impact on MLS will be felt for years and years to come. There are so many new fans tuning in to see not only the Argentine in action, but all the other stars who have made a once forgotten league into the best division in North America.
If Garber has his wish, Harry Kane will be the next big name to join the league.

ftbpro_01m4gv0shtj4.title: Man Utd’s Injury Boost Offset by Brutal Double Blow Ahead of Spurs Clash
ftbpro_01m4gv0shtj4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:00 PM EDTMichael Carrick is desperate to get Manchester United back to winning ways. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesIt was a mixed injury report from Michael Carrick on Friday. The Manchester United manager confirmed Patrick Dorgu and Benjamin Šeško are out against Tottenham Hotspur, while Carlos Baleba is in line to make his debut.

The last thing Manchester United needed during the international break were more injuries. The Red Devils were already dealing with a crowded infirmary, and things only got worse over the last three weeks.
Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford withdrew from England’s camp after sustaining injuries in the team’s 1–1 draw with Fulham. Šeško also withdrew from Slovenia’s squad due to a nagging shin injury.

Dorgu then picked up a hamstring injury while representing the Netherlands and Noussair Mazraoui was soon sent home from Morocco’s camp. All the while, Baleba, Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Manuel Ugarte, Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton remained sidelined.

Carrick didn’t exactly improve the mood at Old Trafford when he delivered dreaded injury updates on the eve of United’s clash with Spurs. “Patrick came off and it looks like he will be out for probably a number of weeks,” the 45-year-old said.
“[Mazraoui] came off and took a knock. He’s not quite right yet, so we’ll see how he is. Ben is further away, with the issue he has got. He won’t be ready.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Carlos Baleba is expected to make his debut in a red shirt this weekend. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesIt wasn’t all bad news from Carrick in his pregame press conference. The English boss shared some positive updates about his other stars ahead of Tottenham’s arrival.
“Carlos is improving,” Carrick said. “He’s trained a lot and is improving. Amad has done a little bit of training, Marcus has done a little bit of training, Kobbie has done a little bit of training.

Of the four players Carrick mentioned, Baleba is the one furtherest along in his recovery. The midfielder, who made the move from Brighton & Hove Albion in a deal worth up to £70 million ($92.6 million) in August, was already nursing an ankle injury before he made Manchester his new home.

As the most expensive of United’s three midfield signings this summer, Baleba comes into the team with high expectations, especially since fellow new arrival Andrey Santos has failed to acclimatize so far.

Baleba can now begin proving United were right to shell out such a lofty sum for his services. The Red Devils are desperate for the 22-year-old to hit the ground running and use that speed of his to help cover ground and intercept danger before it reaches Carrick’s shaky backline.

Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt for Saturday’s clash with Spurs. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesAlthough it’s not ideal, Carrick can replace many of his injured players easily enough; Baleba can take Mainoo’s place if need be, Matheus Cunha can lead the line in place of Šeško and Amad’s absence on the right is rather routine at this point. Shea Lacey is also an option up top should Rashford need extra time to rest.

The real issues lie in defense. United have kept just one clean sheet in seven matches across all competitions this season—and it came against Sabah in the Champions League. Against English opposition, Carrick’s men have conceded 11 goals in six matches.

Compounding an already dire problem are the injuries to Dorgu and Mazraoui. Diogo Dalot is the last man standing at right back, and should something also happen to the Portugal international, United are looking at a crisis on the right flank.

The good news is Spurs have been dreadful in the final third. Roberto De Zerbi’s men have scored just two goals in the Premier League so far this season, a trend the Red Devils will hope continues on Saturday.

United are desperate to collect three points from the marquee fixture after a subpar start to the season. Carrick’s side already got knocked out of the Carabao Cup and sits 12th in the table with just five points from five matches.

ftbpro_01m4h3eqatdp.title: Real Madrid vs. Villarreal: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4h3eqatdp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 9, 2026Real Madrid return to action against Villarreal. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Real Madrid, Villarreal crests)Three weeks after a nightmare Madrid derby, Real Madrid finally get the chance to chase away the bitter taste of defeat with what should be a relatively routine clash with Villarreal on Saturday.

The newly combined September-October international break came at the worst time for Los Blancos. They had just suffered a 2–1 loss to Atlético Madrid and had no chance to respond, forced to retreat to their various international camps until domestic action resumed in October.

Now back in the Spanish capital, José Mourinho’s men will be desperate to collect three points in front of a home crowd that will be ready to whistle the second things don’t go to plan. A victory is also crucial to keep the team in the vicinity of Barcelona atop the standings.
The defending Spanish champions have been perfect in 2026–27, and already have a six-point gap to Real Madrid. With El Clásico looming, the 15-time European champions cannot afford another slip up.

The good news is Villarreal have just two wins to their name this season. The Yellow Submarine started the campaign winless in their first six matches before collecting victories against Málaga and Levante before domestic action paused.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Real Madrid need Kylian Mbappé to punish Villarreal’s defense. / Florencia Tan Jun/Getty ImagesReal Madrid have been far from impressive under Mourinho so far, but that doesn’t mean they’ll fall to a struggling Villarreal side. It might not be a vintage win considering international rust and various absentees, but Los Blancos will get the job done at the Bernabéu.

Many of Mourinho’s best players put together strong international breaks, and will be raring to continue their run of form back at the domestic level. Jude Bellingham is undoubtedly back to his best, Marc Cucurella was elite for Spain and Arda Güler shined despite Türkiye’s turmoil.

Then there’s the likes of Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior, who will both be eager to get back to action after things didn’t exactly go their way the last three weeks. The stars in white should overwhelm a Villarreal side still seeking its identity.
Real Madrid escaped the international break relatively unscathed. Both Mbappé and Ibrahima Konaté avoided major issues, returned to training and are available for selection.

Still, Mourinho might feel inclined to leave Konaté on the bench with an eye on the team’s Champions League clash with Roma on Wednesday. Dean Huijsen will also miss out through suspension after he was sent off against Atlético Madrid last time out.

With the injured Éder Militão and Raúl Asencio also sidelined, Aurélien Tchouaméni could reprise his role as an emergency center back. Eduardo Camavinga, then, could take his place in midfield alongside Bernardo Silva while Federico Valverde recovers from an ankle injury.
Rodrygo and Ferland Mendy are inching their way toward their respective returns, but still have significant work to do before they return to Mourinho’s ranks.
Real Madrid predicted lineup vs. Villarreal (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Dumfries, Tchouaméni, Rüdiger, Cucurella; Silva, Camavinga; Güler, Bellingham, Vinícius Jr; Mbappé.

Alex Freeman is coming off a great international break for the USMNT. / Omar Arnau/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesCompared to the long list of absentees for Mourinho, Villarreal come into Saturday’s fixture with a relatively clean bill of health. Only Tajon Buchanan is ruled out of the clash with a hamstring injury.

Iñigo Pérez must decide who replaces the Canadian. Nicolas Pépé will hope it’s his number called after failing to start the team’s last two games before the break. Alberto Moleiro could also shift to the left, but after his sublime outing as the team’s No. 10 last time out, he is expected to retain his position.
Santi Comesaña is also in line to start after recovering from an ankle injury that kept him sidelined in Villarreal’s win over Levante.

Santiago Mouriño is competing to start at right back, but Alex Freeman is coming off a strong international break for the U.S. men’s national team. The American should retain his place on the right flank, where his speed will come in handy against Vinícius Jr.
Villarreal predicted lineup vs. Real Madrid (4-2-3-1): Gulácsi; Freeman, Navarro, Veiga, Cardona;  Gueye, Comesaña; Akhomach, Moleiro, Pepe; Pérez.

ftbpro_01m4jpcpks5a.title: ‘Big Role’—Cole Palmer Makes Bold Prediction After Signing New Chelsea Contract
ftbpro_01m4jpcpks5a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:10 AM EDTCole Palmer is sticking around. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesCole Palmer has predicted big things for Chelsea in the near future, admitting he signed a new contract with the Blues to ensure he remains a central part of that success.

Despite already being tied down until 2033, Palmer has added an extra 12 months to that contract to commit himself to Chelsea for the next eight years. He will be 32 by the time this new agreement expires.
“Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I’m delighted to sign and I’m obviously very happy,” Palmer told club media.
“Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign.
“Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Chelsea are ready to reward their top performers. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesMuch has been made of Chelsea’s approach to player contracts. Surprisingly long deals often include comparatively low wages, with the Blues well aware that clubs across the globe will gleefully pay higher salaries.
Chelsea’s approach has not been to block players from earning massive salaries, but rather to ensure those that do take home such high figures have truly earned it.

Plenty of factors went into deciding that strategy, including the contract handed out to Raheem Sterling when he joined from Chelsea in the summer of 2022. As a big name, Sterling’s contract included mammoth wages of £325,000 ($430,000) per week, which put him in the bracket of the Premier League’s top earners.

His debut season at Stamford Bridge yielded nine goals and four assists in all competitions—respectable numbers but nothing close to the expectations of a player brought in to take the team to new heights.

With the shift away from recruiting senior players came incentivised contracts. Those who join Chelsea typically agree to lower-than-average wages on deals that include bonuses for appearances, goals and a number of other milestones, with guarantees from the ownership that pay rises can be negotiated regularly if a player’s form justifies it.

This is now the second new contract Palmer has signed since joining Chelsea three years ago. Having quickly proven he deserved to be regarded as more than a high-potential youngster, Palmer is now an undisputed superstar and one of the team’s most important players, and with that elevated status comes a boost to his earnings.
If a player truly deserves to be paid huge wages, Chelsea will make it happen.

ftbpro_01m4jq0rwync.title: Liverpool vs. Man City Combined XI: Only Four Reds Selected
ftbpro_01m4jq0rwync.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray4:00 PM EDTSunday’s match will be brimming with superstars. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Van Dijk), Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty Images (Haaland)The Premier League weekend’s headline act delivers a superstar-laden contest between two of England’s behemoths: Liverpool and Manchester City.

Following a three-week international break, Sunday’s tantalizing clash at Anfield is the perfect tonic—even if the majority of the discourse surrounding the fixture centers around Man City being found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations on a mass scale.
Many of the division’s leading talents will take to the field on Merseyside, with both clubs boasting expensively-assembled rosters brimming with elite players.
With that in mind, here’s how a combined XI of available Liverpool and City players looks.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Alisson has set the standard over the past decade. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesLiverpool and City both have the luxury of exceptional first-choice goalkeepers and the battle between Alisson and Gianluigi Donnarumma is certainly not clear-cut. Two phenomenal shot-stoppers with the odd error coded into their game, they stand among the world’s best in their position.

But, when injury-free, Alisson just edges this particular duel with his more consistent showings in Liverpool’s goal. The Brazilian is superior with the ball at his feet and an unmatched master of one-vs.-one situations.

Matheus Nunes is super consistent. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesRonald Araújo has made an excellent start to his loan spell at Anfield as a repurposed right back, but the consistency and quality of Matheus Nunes still prevails. The Portuguese defender remains a hugely underappreciated talent.

Nunes has an incredibly complete game. Boasting endless energy reserves, terrific physicality and impressive defensive intelligence for a former box-to-box midfielder, he’s one of the most reliable fullbacks in the Premier League.

Rúben Dias is a calming presence. / Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesThere are some fantastic center backs prowling Liverpool and City’s defensive lines, but few possess the blend of power, composure and leadership owned by Rúben Dias. While perhaps not quite as imperious as during his earliest years at the Etihad Stadium, he’s still a formidable presence.

The 29-year-old is not blessed with super recovery speed or a goalscoring knack, but his defensive positioning and incredible understanding of his role makes him ever so reliable. Dias seldom puts a foot wrong for the Cityzens.

Virgil van Dijk is still going strong aged 35. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesMarc Guéhi and the emerging Jérémy Jacquet are both impressive talents, but Virgil van Dijk is the greatest defender of the past decade—even if, like Dias, he’s not quite as commanding or flawless as he was several years ago.
Van Dijk’s reputation was somewhat knocked by being forced to babysit Ibrahima Konaté for large stretches of last season, but Jacquet’s arrival has allowed Liverpool’s skipper to shine once again.
Plus, he’s always good for a vital goal from a set piece.

Man City’s left back options are far superior. /  James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesCity arguably have three left backs better than Liverpool’s Milos Kerkez. Nico O’Reilly and Rayan Aït-Nouri are quality options for Enzo Maresca, but it’s the effortlessly imposing Joško Gvardiol who has been trusted in the role by the Italian early in his reign.

The Croatian defender has the stature and physicality of a center half—a role he’s played regularly throughout his career—yet the grace and technical class to consistently grab goals and assists when rampaging up the flank.

Elliot Anderson’s ascent has been so impressive. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesWhen Elliot Anderson was sold to Nottingham Forest to help Newcastle United comply with the Premier League’s financial regulations, few predicted he would be valued at $153 million just two years later. Yet, here we are.

The Englishman’s ascent has been rather remarkable, with his place as a guaranteed starter for City and England well earned. The combative midfielder is capable of operating as a No. 6 and No. 8 courtesy of his relentless engine and unrivaled industry.

Dominik Szoboszlai was outstanding last season. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesThe Argentine duo of Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernández are both top-level midfielders, while the same can be said of Ryan Gravenberch. But Dominik Szoboszlai’s powerful, all-action performances make him the perfect partner for Anderson in a combined team.

The Hungarian generally thrives when operating closer to the opposition goal, but his displays at right back have underscored his defensive resilience. Few Liverpool players since Steven Gerrard have struck a ball more cleanly—or been more reliable providers of wonder goals.

ftbpro_01m4jr0nc7a3.title: Man City’s ‘Secret Settlement Talks’ Collapse for Comical Reason
ftbpro_01m4jr0nc7a3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:35 AM EDTMan City are under immense pressure. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesManchester City are reported to have held talks over a financial settlement with the Premier League prior to the revelation of their guilty verdict, only to have seen negotiations collapse over their continued proclamations of innocence.

City have appealed the ruling of an independent panel that found them guilty of the vast majority of the 115 financial charges made against them by the Premier League. Punishments could range from fines and point deductions to being stripped of trophies and even expelled from the division.
Prior to the guilty verdict, Bloomberg state City held talks with the Premier League over what would have been a sizeable financial settlement to bring the entire saga to an end.
The conversations are believed to have collapsed fairly quickly for one simple reason: City refused to admit defeat.

Soon after walking away from the negotiating table, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of inflating their finances to the tune of £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018. Any punishment is expected to be far greater than a simple fine.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

City are determined to prove their innocence. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesSince the charges were first brought against City nearly four years ago, the club have never shied away from their public confidence that everything would soon be forgotten.

City have spent years and years insisting they have “irrefutable evidence” to prove their innocence but, when presented with those documents, the panel ruling over the case picked them apart and ultimately found City guilty of major rule breaches.

Even that has not changed City’s stance. The club remain adamant of their innocence and that confidence was shared by manager Enzo Maresca, who told his first press conference since the verdict was handed out that it was a case of “when,” rather than if, the club win their appeal.

If City can prove their innocence, there would obviously be no sanctions. The club appear to be so confident in their ability to change the narrative that the chance to agree to a settlement with the Premier League was not tempting enough.

It is a bold strategy, to say the least. If punishments are handed out, they are expected to be far more severe than a fine. The Premier League has the right to serve whatever punishment it sees fit and the general consensus is that City could be facing an enormous points deduction, potentially serious enough to relegate them from the division.
That would, clearly, be far worse than any fine, but it speaks to the level of City’s confidence that they refused to budge when presented with the chance to soften the blow.

ftbpro_01m4jt2kgxte.title: ‘Not Quite’—Michael Carrick Offers Worrying Benjamin Sesko Injury Update
ftbpro_01m4jt2kgxte.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:35 AM EDTBenjamin Šeško is back on the sidelines. / James Gill - Danehouse/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick has confessed the club remain none the wiser as to the severity of Benjamin Šeško’s latest shin injury.
The striker pulled out of Slovenia’s international roster late last month after missing United’s 1–1 draw with Fulham, having suffered a problem with his shin.

A similar shin injury struck Šeško down in May and ended his 2025–26 season prematurely. He subsequently didn’t participate in preseason in order to focus on building his fitness back up during the summer and had primarily featured off the bench prior to this fresh setback. While the latest issue is not exactly the same, Carrick confessed it is eerily similar.
“It’s not the exact issue,” Carrick said of Šeško’s setback. “It’s a similar area, but it’s not the exact same thing again.
“And we’re kind of still working through it a little bit of seeing how long the issue will be. We’re hoping that it’ll be soon, obviously, but at this moment it’s still not quite clear.”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Michael Carrick (right) is still in the dark. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThe fact that this latest shin problem is even slightly connected to the problem from back in May will be of huge concern to United, who will be fearing a long-term injury that may have developed into something more serious.

Those fears are clear by the fact United still do not have a full grasp on what is going on with Šeško’s shin over three weeks after he suffered the new problem. The utmost caution is evidently being taken.
“I think he had recovered really well actually from the initial one, and there was a lot of time, and sometimes things get thrown up,” Carrick explained.
“The body does certain things, and we’ve got to react to that and try and get him back as quick as we can.”
Proceeding with caution is the right thing to do, even if Šeško’s ongoing, indefinite absence is a major blow to Carrick’s senior squad.

Joshua Zirkzee is in line for more minutes. / Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesŠeško has not actually started in the Premier League for United so far this season, with Brazil international Matheus Cunha leading the line up to this point in the campaign.
Cunha can continue to start games in Šeško’s absence, but the biggest concern for Carrick will be the depth options, or lack thereof.

Joshua Zirkzee is now the first reserve. The Dutchman was expected to leave Old Trafford in the summer, having underwhelmed with a return of just nine goals in 79 appearances across all competitions for United.

If Šeško needs another extended spell on the sidelines, plenty of faith is going to have to be placed in a player who, up to this point, has been available for transfer and could still leave the club in January if the right offer arrives.

Right winger Bryan Mbeumo also has experience playing in a central role, but he has played every minute of the season so far out wide. An injury to Amad Diallo, who has only just returned to light training, has tied Carrick’s hands in that regard.

ftbpro_01m4jyf7vr2p.title: Three Ways Arsenal Stopped Mikel Arteta’s Eyes From Being ‘in Pain’
ftbpro_01m4jyf7vr2p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom1:00 PM EDTArsenal had to come from behind to move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit. / Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty ImagesLONDON—There were many things Mikel Arteta stewed on over the three weeks since Arsenal’s humbling 3–0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion.

The quality of Brighton’s press, the flaws of his own players in possession and quite how confronting Fabian Hürzeler now looks without his toupée all offered food for thought. But it was the desperately unforgiving margins of the Premier League which stuck in his stomach. Arteta learned “how thin the line is, from being exceptional to becoming very average.”

For the first hour of Saturday’s return against Leeds United, it would have been charitable to describe Arteta’s side as very average. With the visitors 1–0 up at the hour mark, thoughts among the almost silent Emirates Stadium turned back to a display against Brighton which left Arteta to lament: “My eyes were in pain.”
Yet, as is the case with so many exceptional teams, Arsenal only needed to approach their best for a sustained burst to still sneak out of the contest with all three points.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Arsenal fans enjoyed the win. / Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty ImagesLunchtime kickoffs can always be sleepy affairs. There was the unusual edge of Manchester City’s guilty verdict hanging in the air ahead of kickoff. Replica Premier League medals won against “those cheats” were being sold by vendors outside the ground at a marked-up price. But that was soon blown over by the crisp gusts of wind rattling underneath the Emirates roof.

The Gunners sluggishly trudged through their return to club action. Across the opening hour, Arsenal had registered more offsides than shots and found themselves deservedly trailing to James Justin’s thump into the top corner. Even the way that Gabriel tried and failed to clear that effort off the line, aiming a glancing header into the side-netting rather than simply blocking it, was systemic of Arsenal’s sloppiness.

Everything about the goal was lackadaisacal. Tarik Muharemović started the move for the visitors by stumbling over the ball. Without any red shirt in the same postcode, he had time to regain his footing, adjust his hair, reply to any unread texts and then play a pass to an unmarked Gabriel Gudmundsson.
In stark contrast, Arsenal’s eventual winner began with Bruno Guimarães taking a free kick so quickly it almost caught Martin Ødegaard by surprise.

There’s nothing like a deficit to send a jolt of electricity through a dozy team. While the Emirates crowd were caught between groaning and goading immediately after Justin’s 55th-minute opener, Ødegaard had the ball on the center spot awaiting a swift restart.

Just seven minutes later, Noni Madueke continued to drive forward, willfully unfazed by the sight of Bukayo Saka prone on the turf inside Arsenal’s half, to send the ball into the box which ended with Riccardo Calafiori bundling an equalizer through Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.
“It’s down to their mentality,” Farke stubbornly admitted while hailing Arsenal as “the most consistent team in Europe.”

Riccardo Calafiori made the difference once again. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesArsenal’s rigidity can be a blessing and a curse. It’s a quality which affords them the best defense in the Premier League, but one which can also hamper their attacking threat. That tendency was abundantly apparent against opponents as well drilled as Leeds.

Daniel Farke’s side bounced into Saturday’s clash with the fifth-most Premier League points across the past 10 months, losing just five of their previous 30 top-flight matches—the same tally as Arsenal. "We haven’t won the lottery,” the Leeds boss scoffed. “It’s not coincidence.” At one point it felt as though the Gunners would need a quirk of fate to even test Leeds’ resolve.

In the end, it took Arsenal’s agent of chaos to force the breakthrough. Calafiori is a player Arteta credits with “a special energy, a special aura around him that makes him different.” The left back with the soul of a striker sniffed out where the ball would drop, arriving on the penalty spot to nod snaffle up a downward header from Ben White. That both Arsenal fullbacks combined within the confines of Leeds’ six-yard box demonstrated how expansive the hosts were willing to go.

Calafiori didn’t touch the ball in the buildup to Guimarães’s winner but it was his dart which distracted Nico Elvedi long enough to open up room for Declan Rice’s run into the box. The onrushing midfielder, freed to roam further forward after a chiefly defensive brief across the opening hour, rolled an impish flick into the stride of Guimarães, who deftly picked out the bottom corner.

Bruno Guimarães got the winner. / Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesIt’s still remarkable that Arsenal’s $100 million recruit can afford to be brought off the bench to win the game. The Gunners don’t necessarily have the absolute best players in the division but they undoubtedly boast the deepest collection of talent in England, if not Europe.

“I think all the players who were on the bench today expected to start,” Arteta admitted. The tide had begun to turn before he turned to his substitutes, but those “finishers” sealed a win an thinner squad would have had no chance securing.

Beyond the headline introduction of Guimarães, Arteta can take confidence from the performance of Madueke. Drafted in to make his first Premier League start of consequence since April, the left footer stationed on his unfavored left wing was one of Arsenal’s brightest performances.

Kai Havertz, Ødegaard and Saka all squandered chances set up by the forward trusted to stand in for the injured Christos Tzolis. “He deserved the chance that he got, he grabbed it with both hands,” Arteta gushed about the “best player in training over the last 10 days.”

ftbpro_01m4k1d3hcst.title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Bournemouth: Unlikely Hero Shines in Goal Fest
ftbpro_01m4k1d3hcst.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott12:15 PM EDTChelsea were relentless. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesChelsea got back to winning ways in style on Saturday with an emphatic 5–1 victory over strugglers Bournemouth.

The hot starts returned to Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fans were still celebrating Jordan Henderson’s long-range opener when Morgan Rogers’s deflected effort nestled in the bottom corner to put Chelsea 2–0 ahead after two-and-a-half minutes.
Not content with the speed of their start in the first half, Chelsea were celebrating just 30 seconds after the restart when Pedro Neto’s cutback was rifled into the roof of the net by João Pedro.

Evanilson deflected Moisés Caicedo’s clearance into the back of the net five minutes later as the tone of the match changed drastically, so there was significant relief around Stamford Bridge when Pedro crashed home his second of the afternoon from close range.
The excellent Henderson’s stunning free kick iced the game off with 20 minutes to go, capping off a glorious afternoon for the veteran midfielder and sealing a much-needed victory for the Blues.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Defending continues to be a major problem for Chelsea. / Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesChelsea got their attacking mojo back here. The Blues were sensational, deserved each of their goals and could have had a few more if things had fallen another way.
This team can go toe-to-toe with any attack on the planet, but at the other end of the field, things are not the same.

The frailties that have plagued Chelsea for the past 18 months remain problematic. Defending set pieces is a massive concern and the sight of Evanilson celebrating the death of Emiliano Martínez’s clean sheet from a corner will be a lingering memory from this game.
Since the start of last season, Chelsea have now conceded a total of 14 goals from inside their own six-yard box following set pieces. Unsurprisingly, that is a league-high.

It is not a Xabi Alonso problem, considering how big of an issue this was under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior as well, but it is the former midfielder’s responsibility to figure out a solution. Until fixed, it will continue to provide any opponent a route back into a match regardless of the circumstances.
The attack is better than it has been in years. Now, it’s the turn of the defense.
Jordan Henderson stole the show for Chelsea. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Emiliano Martínez—7.7: A bystander for the most part before being called into action with an excellent double save in the 35th minute. Could do nothing for Evanilson’s strike.

CB: Josh Acheampong—7.4: Excellent on the ball, with a decisive role in Chelsea’s third goal, but needs to eradicate the defensive concerns that were on show for Evanilson’s goal. Overall, a good showing.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—7.1: Seemed a little off here, but didn’t really do anything wrong. Chelsea need more composure from the senior figure at the heart of their backline.

CB: Levi Colwill—7.1: Like Lacroix, Colwill was objectively fine, but a handful of nervy moments ensured his mixed start to the season continued here. It feels like we’re still waiting for the real Colwill to return from his ACL injury.
RM: Pedro Neto—8.0: Lacked a bit of energy in the first half but quickly made up for that with an impressive assist for the third goal.
CM: Moisés Caicedo—7.4: Made an immediate impact on his return to the squad, with his defensive instincts predictably valuable.

CM: Jordan Henderson—9.2: A really impressive showing. Took his early goal well, got the assist for Rogers, bagged a glorious free kick and led by example with his energy and passion. Such a strong performance.

ftbpro_01m4k28zj2pr.title: ‘Disciplinary Proceedings’—Ronaldo Hit With Portugal Punishment After Walkout
ftbpro_01m4k28zj2pr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell11:15 AM EDTCristiano Ronaldo is facing the consquences of his actions.  / Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesThe Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has provisionally suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for abruptly leaving the Seleção das Quinas’ camp during the September-October international break.

Ronaldo packed his bags and left Portugal after just two matches this fall following a falling out with manager Jorge Jesus. The 41-year-old took issue with being benched against Norway and then cited more broken promises when his manager did not follow a list of pre-agreed talking points in his subsequent press conference.
With the international break now done and dusted, the FPF has taken action, opening up a disciplinary case against Ronaldo for his stunning walkout.

“Disciplinary proceedings have been initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro, following a decision by the Non-Professional Section on Oct. 9, 2026, for the purpose of determining the potential disciplinary relevance of the facts reported on Oct. 7, 2026,” the federation confirmed in a statement.

“Without prejudice to the automatic provisional suspension to which he was subject until the proceedings were opened, a non-automatic provisional suspension of the player was ordered, and the proceedings were classified as urgent.
“The case was sent on Oct. 10, 2026, to the FPF Disciplinary Investigation Committee, with public disclosure excluded until the conclusion of the investigation.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Cristiano Ronaldo is ready to accept Portugal’s punishment. / Alex Juarez/Anadolu/Getty ImagesRonaldo explained the root of his disagreement with Jesus and his reasonings for leaving camp in a lengthy statement. Among the thousands—yes, thousands—of words, Ronaldo acknowledged sanctions were likely on their way.

“The consequences of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I believe the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am a team captain, and that is an aggravating factor.
“I have already apologized, but I know that actions must have consequences. Anyone in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.”

The specific punishment remains to be seen, but the chances of the team hitting Ronaldo with a lengthy suspension are relatively low. In fact, president Pedro Proença already admitted he expects the Real Madrid legend to be back with the team for the November international break.

Jesus’s men have two more UEFA Nations League matches against Denmark and Wales on their calendar before the year ends. The Seleção das Quinas have not missed Ronaldo’s services as of late; Portugal won all four of their fall matches, and Ronaldo did not appear in three.
It will be very interesting to see what role he plays—and his relationship with Jesus—if Ronaldo indeed returns to the team in November.

Cristiano Ronaldo is a Portugal icon. / Diogo Cardoso/Getty ImagesRonaldo signed off his bombshell statement confirming the federation wants to give the him a proper farewell for when he decides to retire. A suspension would likely not change that matter, just potentially push it back.

Despite the rift between Jesus and Ronaldo, multiple reports indicate the federation is desperate to save its relationship with its all-time leading goalscorer. When the time comes for Ronaldo to hang up his boots, Portugal will undoubtedly give him the farewell he deserves.
But that moment might not be coming for a while yet. Many thought his falling out with Jesus would push Ronaldo into retirement, but he firmly shuts down those rumors.

“If I am physically well, playing for my club, hopefully with goals, after serving whatever suspension is imposed on me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team.”

ftbpro_01m4k2wgg8zs.title: Why Raphinha Isn’t Playing for Barcelona vs. Getafe
ftbpro_01m4k2wgg8zs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray11:30 AM EDTRaphinha is missing or the reigning champs. / Gongora/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesBarcelona have the chance to extend their perfect record in La Liga when facing Getafe on Saturday, but they will be without their leading goalscorer as they search for yet another win.

La Blaugrana will make history by beating their visitors to Camp Nou this weekend. If they taste victory, it will be only the second time they have ever won the first eight games of the La Liga campaign—previously doing so in 2013–14.

However, the absence of Raphinha will certainly weaken Barça. The winger has been redeployed as a central striker by Hansi Flick at the start of the current campaign and that tactical tweak has paid immediate dividends. He’s scored a staggering 14 goals in eight matches in his new-look role.
So, why will Barcelona be without their essential Brazilian?
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Raphinha will be sorely missed. / Omar Arnau/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesUnfortunately for Barça, Raphinha was a casualty of the extended three-week international break.

The 29-year-old was named in Brazil’s roster for their two friendlies against Australia and first-ever game against India, but he didn’t make it to the 4–0 victory in Greater Kolkata after suffering a thigh injury during the second outing against the Socceroos.
Raphinha only played the first half of the 4–2 triumph before being substituted and he subsequently left the Brazil camp early to return to Catalonia for treatment.
There was hope he would feature against Getafe as Barça continue their early march toward another La Liga crown, but Flick confirmed the forward’s absence during his prematch press conference.
“The picture [scan] showed something, but it’s not a big injury,” Flick revealed on Friday. “He is doing well, has no pain and can do everything.
“He needs a bit more time. It’s something we have to take care of because last season he had three injuries there.”

Flick (right) will have Raphinha back soon. / Jose Hernandez/Anadolu/Getty ImagesBarça will be understandably cautious with Raphinha’s reintroduction and Flick has admitted he will also sit out Tuesday’s Champions League clash away at Galatasaray.

Raphinha scored twice in the club’s first league phase outing against Feyenoord, but won’t have the opportunity to add to his European tally until Oct. 20 when Barça visit current holders Paris Saint-Germain for an all-star showdown.
While not guaranteed, Raphinha could return several days before the trip to Paris when the reigning La Liga champions visit Real Betis.
However, with the PSG clash so soon after and the Clásico with Real Madrid immediately following the seismic Champions League encounter, there’s every chance Raphinha is also rested in Seville.

ftbpro_01m4k694zht5.title: La Liga Match Abandoned Inside First Half Over Fan Protests
ftbpro_01m4k694zht5.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer1:30 PM EDTThe Rayo Vallecano president is the source of fan ire. / Alvaro Medranda/ Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesRayo Vallecano vs. Athletic Club in La Liga was forcibly suspended and abandoned on Saturday after protests from the home supporters directed at club president Raúl Martín Presa.

The match at Estadio de Vallecas in Madrid’s Puente de Vallecas district—south east of downtown—was stopped by referee José María Sánchez Martínez three times, the last of which resulted in it being called off altogether with only half an hour on the game clock.

The first suspension followed what appeared to be a pre-planned protest 13 minutes in, as Rayo fans threw paper planes and marbles onto the field. Captains from both teams were in discussion with the referee and efforts from ground staff were made to clear the playing area of the debris. The clock wasn’t stopped and the play resumed on 21 minutes.

Only a minute later, more planes and balls rained down and the game was stopped again. At that point, the players returned to the locker rooms and it was announced that play would resume in 10 minutes. But it came with a warning that further disruption would result in abandonment. Rayo team captains Óscar Valentín and Isi Palazón were seen approaching and talking to fans, but it had no impact. Once the players re-emerged and the match resumed, it was almost immediately stopped, with referee Sánchez Martínez also consulting the police.

The decision was made not to keep trying, prompting Rayo’s most radical fans to celebrate the abandonment as though a goal had been scored. They had wanted to take a stand against Presa and getting a match called off is the most disruptive action possible. The club’s unofficial anthem, La Vida Pirata—The Pirate Life, was sung, although efforts were also made to congratulate and thank the Athletic Club players, unwittingly caught up in a longstanding, increasingly ugly feud.

La Liga released a statement soon after that confirmed the match was “suspended by the referee's decision following repeated objects being thrown onto the pitch.” That update also made clear that La Liga “strongly condemns this type of behavior, which jeopardizes safety and makes the normal course of the competition impossible.”

It was briefly rumored that the match could be quickly rearranged for Sunday, but that proved not to be the case and the Athletic Club party headed for the airport to return to Bilbao. The match will now have to be scheduled for another time, confirmed in due course.
Spain’s soccer federation (RFEF) could order a “total or partial closure” of Rayo’s stadium for up to three matches, as per the code of conduct.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Raúl Martín Presa attended the match. / Angel Perez Meca/Europa Press/Getty ImagesMadrid-born businessman Raúl Martín Presa has been Rayo Vallecano president since 2011, but there have long been issues between the club’s senior hierarchy and its fans.

The Athletic’s Dermot Corrigan wrote in 2020: “Internal conflict at the Estadio de Vallecas is nothing new. Strife between Rayo’s left-leaning fanbase and conservative ownership has been constant for decades. It is part of what makes one of Madrid’s biggest clubs such an object of fascination inside and outside the city.”

This was the first home match of the season that Rayo have been able to play at Estadio de Vallecas due to safety concerns. Until this weekend, home fixtures had to be relocated to Leganés on the southwestern outskirts of Madrid. Presa is being blamed for apparent neglect of Rayo facilities, as well as complaints over poor management going back years.
The pitch itself was a concern last season when a La Liga visit from Real Oviedo was called off by the match officials on the grounds of player safety being compromised.
Last weekend, a group of Rayo fans decided on a visual indication of their displeasure, breaking into the stadium and vandalizing the VIP box where the president and his associates sit.

Before the match, Rayo vice-president José María Sardá de Abreu told Movistar+: “Little has changed. A few things have had to be tweaked, but tweaked, not changed. It makes no sense to go through what we’ve been through. Of course we're going to sit in the VIP box. What happened was despicable. This is sport, not politics. We can do things better or worse, but to reach this point of violence ... It’s a top-flight club, with sound finances ... Sure, things aren’t entirely right socially, but there are people who provoke this situation.”

Paper plans and other debris rained down on the field /  Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images“What happened today during the match against Athletic Club is an inevitable reflection of the anger, frustration and outrage felt by thousands of supporters after years of disastrous management by Raúl Martín Presa,” read a statement from the Rayo Vallecano Fans' Association published in the wake of the abandonment.

“The fanbase has reached an unsustainable situation after 15 years of neglected facilities, chaotic management, a loss of identity, and continuous contempt for employees and supporters, as well as for the working-class neighborhood of Vallecas and its values. What is happening today is the consequence of a fire that has been allowed to burn for far too long, without anyone trying to put it out.”

The fans’ association insisted the protest was “legitimate and democratic,” as well as “necessary and peaceful.” The statement added: “It is the consequence of three decades of putting the safety and health of 15,000 people at risk every fortnight.”

Supporters described the “loss” of Estadio de Vallecas in July as the “final straw” in this saga, making accusations that fans were “denied the opportunity to claim back money that belongs to them. But there are hundreds of other examples. That is why we will continue protesting.”
Rayo Vallecano needs, they say, “a change of direction.”

ftbpro_01m4k7fc1ek3.title: Peyton Miller: The USMNT Breakout Star Linked With the Premier League
ftbpro_01m4k7fc1ek3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:00 PM EDTPeyton Miller could be the next American in line of a move overseas. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesBig things are coming for the breakout stars of the U.S. men’s national team. Peyton Miller is the latest youngster linked with a major move abroad after an impressive first camp with the Stars and Stripes.

Mauricio Pochettino turned heads when he called up eight teenagers and 13 total uncapped players for the USMNT’s fall friendlies with Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. The Argentine boss made it clear he is trusting the next generation to help the Stars and Stripes usher in a new era.

Goalscorers Julian Hall, Cavan Sullivan and Justin Ellis stole the show in the team’s four wins during the September-October international break, but there were other lesser-known names that impressed as well.
Peyton Miller led that list, so much so that recent reports claim top Premier League clubs are circling around the 18-year-old.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Peyton Miller already made a name for himself in New England. / Geoff Stellfox/MLS/Getty ImagesLike most of the young stars infiltrating Pochettino’s roster, Miller plays in Major League Soccer. The dynamic fullback came up through the academy ranks of the New England Revolution and has been making history every since.

Miller soon became the youngest player in club history to ink a professional contract at age 15. It only took one year with the club’s reserve side before he made his first-team debut in 2024, becoming the second-youngest player in club history to do so.

Over the next two years, Miller firmly established himself as an important pillar of the Revolution’s system. Despite his age, he already has 60 MLS appearances to his name—and 51 have been starts. Only three other players in the league’s entire history have started 50 matches before celebrating their 19th birthday.

As a fullback, Miller is never going to gain the flashy headlines of a forward like Hall or Sullivan. But those paying attention to his play in New England knew it was only a matter of time before the world also noticed his talent.

Peyton Miller is a fan-favorite in New England. / Zoe Davis/Getty ImagesMiller is strong defensively, unafraid to make a daring tackle or use his athleticism to challenge a player inside his own half. His speed allows him to quickly track back in transition and intervene before any danger reaches his fellow defenders.

Even more impressive are his instincts in the final third. The teenager has nine goals and seven assists in his 60 MLS appearances. The numbers are even more head-turning when you take into account just how bad New England were in 2024 and 2025.
This season, though? They sit second in the Eastern Conference standings, and Miller’s rise is a big reason why. In fact, his seven goals in 2026 are the second most on the team—and he’s a defender.

Peyton Miller impressed in his one start with the USMNT. / Mark Thorstenson/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesWhen Pochettino called up Miller, it really came as no surprise. What might have, though, is that he got the nod on the left flank in the USMNT’s first friendly against Peru.

While undisputed starter Antonee Robinson watched from the bench, Miller made his senior debut for the Stars and Stripes. He might not have gotten on the scoresheet, but he still delivered an impressive 62 minutes.

Miller misplaced just one pass and created two dangerous chances—one of which should have  ended in an assist. Nevertheless, he played his role to near perfection, doing his job inside his own half while also pushing forward and linking up with his attackers.

Robinson then took the starting job against Chile and Mexico, while Pochettino gave Auston Trusty the nod against Canada. Miller had to settle for just cameo appearance in the team’s 3–0 win over El Tri.

Still, he can be proud of how he performed in his first real opportunity with the USMNT. He might not be displacing Robinson anytime soon, but Miller can certainly fight to become his backup and a permanent name Pochettino calls up as the 2030 World Cup cycle unfolds.

Peyton Miller has interest from the Premier League. / Tim Austen/Getty ImagesMiller is not the only young MLS star linked to the Premier League. Sullivan, who just recently turned 17, already agreed to join Manchester City upon his coming of age. Zavier Gozo also bid farewell to Real Salt Lake to join Crystal Palace this summer.

When the Premier League comes knocking, it’s impossible not to open the door. Miller would likely follow in the footsteps of his fellow Americans and secure a move to the English top flight if something indeed materializes.

The question isn’t whether Miller will accept a potential offer, but rather if he is ready to. Eighteen years old is very young to play abroad in the most competitive, unforgiving league in the world. It also wouldn’t exactly benefit the Connecticut-native if he joined a club and then just wasted away on the bench, third or fourth in a manager's pecking order.

ftbpro_01m4khzs3myh.title: ‘Invest in Myself’—The Premier League Player Accepted into Harvard
ftbpro_01m4khzs3myh.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer3:30 PM EDTHarvard Business School has a special program for pro athletes. / Mel Musto/Bloomberg/Getty ImagesTottenham Hotspur playmaker Xavi Simons wants to use the extra time on his hands during a long-winded ACL rehab to improve other aspects of his life.

The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain talent, unlikely to be back playing for Spurs until February 2027 at the earliest, is now a Harvard student, having been accepted onto Harvard Business School’s Crossover Into Business Program.
It describes itself as a “semester-long program in which professional athletes develop their business acumen by working with MBA student mentors.”

“Built” with professional athletes in mind, the program promises to make them “better prepared for business activities during and after their active sports careers.” The mentors “empower them to make better business decisions, all in a way that fits the athletes’ busy lives.”
Like a true business person, Simons used LinkedIn as his platform of choice to announce this.

“I’m going back to school,” he said. “During my recovery, I’ve been trying to use my time in the best way possible. Football is still my main focus, but I also want to keep learning and improving away from the pitch. I’m happy to share that I’ve been accepted onto the Crossover Into Business Program at Harvard Business School.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

The Netherlands international was forced to miss the 2026 World Cup because of his knee injury but has still spent time on both coasts of the United States—including Boston, where he linked up with Dutch-American economist and HBS professor Anita Elberse.

“We first met during my time at FC Barcelona, and later again at Paris Saint-Germain. We’ve stayed in touch over the years, so it was great to see her again and visit Harvard while I was in Boston,” Simons said. “Getting back on the pitch is still my number one priority. At the same time, I want to use this period to keep learning and invest in myself beyond football.”

Harvard lists all manner of professional athletes who have taken the Crossover Into Business Program. Simons is by no means a lone representative from the sport of soccer, but the graduate carrying the flag is 11-time NBA All-Star and two-time NBA champion Chris Bosh. Indeed, the program was originally launched nine years ago in partnership with the NBA.

Xavi Simons is young but it’s never too early to think about what’s next. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesA lot of professional soccer players who retire stay in the sport as coaches or managers. That will be an option for Simons, too, but he seems to be looking higher.

The 23-year-old said he has “always been interested in more than just football” and wants to “understand the business side of the game better, learn from people in different industries and keep developing as a person.”

Some ex-professionals do go down the soccer business route. Simons’s fellow Dutchman, Edwin van der Sar, did exactly that. He joined Ajax as marketing director in 2012 and was promoted to CEO in 2016, going on to oversee the club’s Champions League resurgence.

David Beckham is arguably as well known for his post-playing business career as what he did on the field, becoming a club owner when he co-founded Inter Miami in 2018. He also recently made history in 2026 as the U.K.’s first billionaire sportsman.
Ex-Barcelona and Spain defender Gerard Pique, meanwhile, is building a multi-club empire with teams in Spain’s soccer pyramid and has other business interests in sports and media.

ftbpro_01m4kj5mr1bn.title: ‘Overbearing and Arrogant’—Barça President Attacks Real Madrid Over Negreira Case
ftbpro_01m4kj5mr1bn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 10, 2026Joan Laporta held nothing back against Real Madrid.  / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Barcelona president Joan Laporta didn’t hold back in a brutal tirade against Real Madrid, accusing Los Blancos of trying to “discredit Barça” and “harming football” with their insistence to extend the Negreira case.

During the recent international break, UEFA announced Real Madrid submitted “a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira.” Los Blancos president Florentino Pérez promised this would happen soon after winning Real Madrid’s presidential elections early in the summer.

Barcelona are accused of paying over €7 million ($7.9 million) in bribes to a company owned by Negreira, the former vice president of Spanish soccer’s refereeing committee, in an effort to get favorable refereeing decisions. The Catalans maintain their innocence and have even filed a lawsuit against Pérez, but with the topic back stealing headlines, Laporta unleashed against Real Madrid.

“On the Negreira case,” Laporta said on Saturday, “I’ve grown tired of saying it but I won’t stop making it clear that they tried to condemn us before judging us. Now that they are judging us, it’s being shown that there is nothing to what they accused us of and that this will end, as I fully believe, with Barça’s acquittal.

“They have relentlessly and constantly tried to discredit us and harm Barça’s image and they are going to have to rectify. There will be time to speak about this once there’s a sentence, but as you know, they are trying to extend this case as much as possible to keep the flame alive.
“But it’s going nowhere. They are trying to discredit Barça, but I don’t think they are doing it innocently. They want to harm football.”

Joan Laporta (left) has a fierce rivalry with Florentino Pérez.  / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Getty Images  Defending Barça’s stance in regards to the Negreira case wasn’t the only topic Laporta covered; he also took his Real Madrid attack a step further, saying the 15-time European champions are “losing prestige.”

“They [Real Madrid] are against everything,” Laporta stated. “You go to every institution, you go to UEFA, to the Euro League and they are against everything and everyone. This says a lot about the attitude of a team that is losing prestige, recognition and credibility on a national and international level.

“This is just some evidence, the other day I was at the general assembly of the European Football Clubs and they didn’t even have representation. They adopt a very prepotent, overbearing and arrogant attitude and they’ll know what they’re doing, but this creating them a massive loss of credibility.”
“I think they should analyze and be self-critical about this,” Laporta added. “Because to me it’s completely out of place and improper.”

Barcelona have had a dream start of the 2026–27 season.  / David Ramos/Getty Images Barcelona have dominated Spanish soccer over the past two years, winning back-to-back La Liga titles plus another three domestic trophies to Real Madrid’s zero since Hansi Flick took over. Under the German boss, the Catalans have won six Clásicos to Madrid’s one, including three wins in finals.

The 2026–27 season has started in similar fashion, with Barça perfect through nine games in all competitions and already six points clear of an unconvincing Real Madrid. As a result, Laporta believes Los Blancos’ constantly bringing up the Negreira case is a strategy to divert attention from what’s happening on the pitch.

“At Madrid they talk about other topics to divert attention,” Laporta said. “In that sense, Barça is going through a sweet moment. We are enjoying football, enjoying the club, enjoying a beautiful moment in our history or important worldwide recognition.

“We have nine players that were in the squad of the World Cup champion, we have a team that makes people fall in love with their football, players at certain positions that are a reference in the football world. We receive praise from everywhere. From Madrid they are trying to minimize all of this.”

It’s unknown when UEFA will reach a final verdict on the Negreira case, but what’s true is that the levels of bad blood between Spain‘s biggest rivals are reaching sky-high levels with less than a month to go before their first meeting of the season.

ftbpro_01m4kk8d4k7v.title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. Villarreal: Vinicius Junior Red Card Overshadows Crucial Win
ftbpro_01m4kk8d4k7v.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 10, 2026Vinícius Júnior (center) was handed his marching orders in the second half. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesReal Madrid squeaked out a 1–0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday, persevering with 10 men after Vinícius Júnior was sent off in the 74th minute.

When Los Blancos kicked off under the lights at the Bernabéu, the team was nine points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona. Collecting three points was absolutely imperative for José Mourinho’s men in their return to domestic action, but the only thing they produced in the first half were thousands of whistles from the home crowd.

Yan Diomande finally gave the fans something to cheer when he bagged his first goal to put the hosts up 1–0 in the 62nd minute. The teenager collected a clever ball from Federico Valverde on the turn and then fired a right-footed strike into the back of the net.

Vinícius Jr was the next man on the scoresheet nine minutes later, but a VAR review chopped off the goal for a foul in the build-up. The replay showed the Brazil international pull the hair of Nathan Saliba before he was off to the races and was promptly shown a red card, leaving Real Madrid down to 10 men.

The 15-time European champions dug deep and saw out the win, withstanding a flurry of chances from Villarreal to bring the gap to Barcelona back to six points. The win hardly felt like a triumph, though, given how the game turned in the final stages.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Yan Diomande delivered when Real Madrid needed it most. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesMourinho turned heads when he benched Vinícius Jr for Saturday’s clash. The decision could have simply been because the winger logged heavy minutes during the international break for Brazil and also had to travel back to Spain from India. But there was no ignoring just how poorly the No. 7 has played for club and country in 2026–27.

Yan Diomande instead got the nod on the left wing. The stage was set for the blockbuster summer signing to make a statement in the rare opportunity, but apart from a few blistering runs forward, there wasn’t much to celebrate about his opening 45 minutes.

Mourinho could sense the team was in desperate need of a boost as the game unfolded scoreless, so he introduced Vinícius Jr in the 52nd minute. But instead of replacing Diomande, the Portuguese boss moved the teenager to the right wing—and it paid off 10 minutes later.

Diomande buried a clinical finish and then Vinícius Jr soon doubled Real Madrid’s lead. It looked like the attack was finally finding its footing after a lackluster start to the season ... but Vinícius Jr’s goal was wiped away and he was sent off.

The team went from a group hug around Vinícius Jr to a group attack on the referee. What could have been a turning point for the winger—and the frontline—this season is now just another moment shrouded in controversy.
Real Madrid were all smiles before controversy followed.  / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Thibaut Courtois—8.2: Could have gone for a stroll around Spain in the first half and no one would have noticed. Called into action more after the restart and had to stand on his head to keep a clean sheet.

RB: Trent Alexander-Arnold—7.0: Delivered sensational service to Mbappé. A bright spot pushing forward on a team that looked all out of ideas for long stretches. Harshly taken out of the game early in the second half.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—7.3: Played without any signs of a lingering injury. Continues to deliver a solid debut campaign. Read danger well, especially when the team went down to 10 men.

CB: Antonio Rüdiger—7.9: Turned back the clock to step up in Huijsen’s absence. Always the one making a timely clearance or shutting down a promising sequence from the visitors. Won all but one of his duels.
LB: Álvaro Carreras—7.1: Time on the bench has done him well. Looked sharp from the opening whistle and linked up well with Diomande down the left. Didn’t deserve to come off at halftime.

DM: Federico Valverde—8.2: Started the game in midfield, then went out to the right wing and  ended up at right back all before the game reached the hour-mark. Guess where he was at his best?The position he hates playing.
DM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—7.2: Tidy in possession and crucial in defense. Enjoyed more progressive passing, continuously looking to get the ball into the final third.
RW: Arda Güler—6.9: Not one of his better outings on the wing. Eventually dropped into midfield to try and dictate the flow of play for his side with mixed results.

ftbpro_01m4kn7a7jnp.title: Man Utd Sink to 40-Year Low, Giving Michael Carrick Nowhere to Hide
ftbpro_01m4kn7a7jnp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffOct 10, 2026Man Utd had to accept a draw from a winning position. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesThe last time Manchester United started a season this poorly, the manager was soon fired and a hot, young recruit named Alex Ferguson was handed the reins.
Ferguson was at the helm for 27 years, has been retired for 13 and will celebrate his 85th birthday on New Year’s Eve. That is how long it’s been.

Saturday’s 1–1 draw against a Tottenham Hotspur team that started the weekend bottom of the Premier League and was reduced to 10 players after falling a goal behind less than 20 minutes from the end means the Red Devils have taken six points from the first six games in 2026–27.

It was previously the joint-slowest start the club had experienced in the Premier League, matching 2014–15’s five points from the opening five matches. But that iteration of Manchester United, guided by Louis van Gaal, crucially won the sixth game.

This few points through six matches, an average of one per game, now makes it the worst start since the Premier League era began in 1992. You have to go further back to fall 1986 to find anything worse—back then, Ron Atkinson led United to four points over the same timeframe.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

It got worse before it got better 40 years ago. Games seven and eight also ended in defeats at the hands of Everton and Chelsea, before a Nottingham Forest draw left United with only five points from nine matches and 21st out of 22 in the league standings.

A brief upturn that followed kept Atkinson in a job until Nov. 4, with Ferguson arriving two days later. He’d broken the established order in Scotland with Aberdeen and even led the Dons to a European trophy, beating Real Madrid in the 1982–83 UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup final.
It was a slow burn to begin with—United initially sank further. But Ferguson reset the culture and had almost completely overhauled the playing squad by the end of the decade.

Something has gone wrong since last season finished on a high. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesThrough this season’s underwhelming start, Michael Carrick has been holding onto the idea that small margins have been responsible for dropping points. Everton scored a late equalizer to capture a draw at the start of last month, while Manchester City’s derby winner objectively should not have stood. It was an own goal that cost them victory against Fulham, while another stoppage-time equalizer took away two more points against Spurs.
“That’s two late goals that have hurt us a little bit this season—everything looks very different if they change. But the reality is what it is, and we need to accept it and do better,” he said.

The weird thing is it makes no sense. United had the best points haul in the entire Premier League during Carrick’s 17-match audition in the second half of last season and the on-field personnel is close to identical.

But there is a pattern emerging. Manchester United are not performing. Former club captain Gary Neville called the first 15 minutes after halftime against Fulham in the final match before the international break the worst he’d seen in 45 years of being a fan. By halftime against Spurs, the team had accumulated just 0.05 expected goals (xG) and still only finished with 0.77.
In those last two games alone, it’s been failure to beat a team in the relegation zone. And Spurs have had as many managers as league wins in 2026—three of each.

Things also aren’t about to get easier. United are already starting to face accusations about not being up for the fight. The team ranks towards the bottom of the Premier League for distance covered per game this season and the next two opponents—Atlético Madrid in the Champions League and Leeds United—work hard and will try to take advantage of that.

The Red Devils looked sluggish rather than refreshed following an international break in which a number of players either weren’t called up by their respective countries or withdrew. Yet the games now come thick and fast, with seven more in total before the next pause for international in four weeks, Como, Roma, Chelsea and Aston Villa among them.
