ftbpro_01m4kspbj3p7.title: Reece James Injury: Progress, Potential Return Date for Chelsea Star
ftbpro_01m4kspbj3p7.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 10, 2026Reece James is set for a spell on the sidelines. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images Chelsea have been faced with a handful of injury issues during the first few months of the season, with Reece James the latest to be forced into a spell on the sidelines.

James was unable to represent England during the international action as Thomas Tuchel confirmed the Chelsea captain wasn’t included in his roster due to injury. The 26-year-old also missed Chelsea’s defeat against Brentford right before the international break and sat out the 5–1 win over Bournemouth immediately after.
A final verdict on his fitness is in, and unfortunately for Chelsea, the news is not good.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Reece James is Chelsea’s leader. / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images Alonso was the first to reveal James had suffered a knee injury during training. After being sent for scans, it was subsequently decided that surgery was the only option.

Chelsea did describe the process as “minor,” which initially offered some relief to fans fearing his season may already be over, but no formal details about the injury have been revealed at this point.
Knee injuries have not been common in James’s career thus far. He has battled hamstring problems on a number of occasions, giving him an unwanted reputation in the process.

Reece James has struggled to remain fit throughout his career.  / Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images When Chelsea confirmed James’s surgery, they did not offer a timeframe for his return. Blues boss Alonso had said he would be assessed “week by week,” but it soon became clear that would not be possible.

Indeed, reports quickly put an estimate of three months on James’s recovery, which may well be more of a reflection on the need to proceed with the utmost caution when it comes to a player with his difficult injury record.

“We don’t have the exact, it will be several weeks for sure, it’s not going to be short,” Alonso said. “It's not going to be two, three weeks things, it’s going to be longer and after we will see before Christmas, after Christmas time will tell but things have to be done properly, that he feels right and that needs in the best possible condition.
“A disappointment for everyone, for him but we need to ... we have a squad to follow that to deal with the injuries.”

Jordan Henderson scored a brace in his home Chelsea debut.  / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images     James has operated almost exclusively as a central midfielder in the infancy of the Alonso era. Fortunately for Chelsea, previously injured midfielders have not only returned to full fitness—they are already producing on the pitch.

Jordan Henderson and Moisés Caicedo formed Alonso’s double-pivot against Bournemouth and thrived, with the pair only recently returning from injury themselves. In his first Chelsea start at Stamford Bridge, Henderson scored a brace and picked up an assist, while Caicedo looked solid in his first start of the campaign.
Alonso was delighted with how his starting midfielders performed, and Roméo Lavia also looked sharp during his cameo after suffering an injury scare during the international break.

If Alonso also needs cover at right-center back or wingback—positions James can also operate in—Josh Acheampong and Pedro Neto have both impressed this season. Furthermore, summer recruit Marco Palestra is back available after starting his debut season with his own fitness concern.

ftbpro_01m4kzskmggw.title: ‘No Restrictions’—Manager Teases Big Things to Come for USMNT Record Breaker
ftbpro_01m4kzskmggw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas9:00 AM EDTMathis Albert is one of the most exciting young USMNT talents.  / David Berding/USSF/Getty Images Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovač revealed that 17-year-old U.S. men’s national team rising star Mathis Albert will get “a lot more minutes” with the German giants moving forward.

The Greenville, S.C. native has been at Dortmund since 2024, joining the academy and slowly making his way to the first team. Back in April, he broke Gio Reyna’s record and became the youngest U.S. player to play in a Bundesliga match, making his Dortmund debut at 16.

Albert is now firmly part of Kovač’s squad and played 90 minutes in his season debut for the club when Dortmund defeated HEBC Hamburg in the opening round of the DFB Pokal. As Dortmund returned to action following the international break, Kovač admitted Albert is ready for an increased role.

From the academy to the big stage.18-year-old Italian Samuele Inácio debuted as a starter, while US-born 16-year-old Mathis Albert made his senior debut.Dortmund’s next generation has arrived. pic.twitter.com/XoxMOql8jn

“There are no restrictions,” Kovač said about Albert, via Bundesliga. “He is a very talented young man who is already showing really good signs in training, who has already played a cup game, and who sooner or later, probably sooner, will get a lot more minutes here at Borussia Dortmund than perhaps half a year ago.”
Albert was an unused substitute in Dortmund’s draw against Wolfsburg on Saturday, but he could start getting more regular playing time before the end of the year.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mathis Albert was briefly the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.            / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images Although the 90 against HEBC Hamburg are the only minutes Albert has played at the club level this season, Mauricio Pochettino included him in the USMNT’s first post-2026 World Cup roster.

Albert made his senior USMNT debut against Peru and featured in all four wins Pochettino’s side collected during the September-October international action. Against Chile, in the second game of the window, the young forward found the back of the net, becoming the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

“It’s like a dream come true for sure,” Albert told Telemundo soon after his maiden USMNT goal. “Ever since I was young I’ve been dreaming to score for the national team, and yeah, I was really happy. I didn’t expect it to happen so fast, but I’m just very happy to be part of the team and make an impact from on the bench or if I start, whatever happens.”
The former LA Galaxy academy player admitted it was hard for him to sleep on the night he scored the record-breaking goal, a record that lasted only four days.
BAR DOWN AND IN FOR MATHIS ALBERT! 💥#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/gF5OvCaiqh

Fellow 2009-born U.S. talent Cavan Sullivan broke Albert’s record when he found the back of the net against Mexico. The pair of teenagers are two of the most exciting young talents Pochettino appears keen on integrating to the national team.

Sullivan is already bound for Manchester City when the turns 18, but there have been whispers that the Cityzens are also interested in poaching Albert from Dortmund to add another USMNT talent to their ranks.

For now, though, Albert will be hoping Kovač’s words are true and he starts slowly earning himself a more prominent role with the German giants. If he takes advantage of his opportunities and continues his development, then it could only be a matter of time before some of European soccer’s powerhouses come knocking.

ftbpro_01m4n6thk2az.title: Haaland Shows What He Thinks of Man Utd With Brutal Three-Word Admission
ftbpro_01m4n6thk2az.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:50 AM EDTErling Haaland (left) has never been slow to offer his disdain for Manchester United.  / Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC/Getty Images (Haaland), Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty Images (badge)Erling Haaland briefly dropped the mask of Manchester City’s charismatic spokesperson to offer an insight into his thoughts on Manchester United—or rather, his lack of thoughts.
During an interview with beIN Connect aired this weekend, Haaland couldn’t recall what City’s fiercest rivals were called. “What’s their name?” he damningly asked before arriving at the answer.
When this mischievous wrinkle was thrown back at City’s striker, he laughed: “I had to think about the name.”

While United have historically dominated their city rivals, with former Red Devils boss Sir Alex Ferguson notably dismissing the blue half of Manchester as nothing more than “noisy neighbors,” there has been a distinct power shift in the last decade. Haaland has only known United as distant challengers during his four years at City, with the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool his club’s closest contenders.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Before misplacing United’s name, Haaland had been previewing City’s daunting trip to Anfield on Sunday. The Premier League’s most potent forward was not only anticipating a hostile reaction from a Liverpool crowd baying for blood after the official announcement of City’s guilt regarding more than 100 breaches of financial regulations, he was looking for to it.
“I hope it’s like that [hostile],” Haaland insisted, “it should be like that when Man City go to Liverpool and Anfield.”
Erling Haaland you are built different. pic.twitter.com/rDmbDDzoOM

Accepted wisdom would claim that the odds are stacked against Manchester City heading into Sunday’s trip to Anfield. It has been widely predicted that fans on Merseyside will make their home ground an insufferable bear pit for the visit of a club who, according to an independent commission, have systematically cheated for almost a decade to build the foundations of a team which has denied Liverpool more than most.
In the face of this wall of negativity, City are expected to wilt. Yet, that ignores some inconvenient realities.

Anfield has a formidable reputation on certain European nights but the fizz of Liverpool’s home ground has been distinctly lacking for an extended period. On a chilly Sunday afternoon, rather than under the bright lights of a Champions League affair, there’s only so much hostility that can be summoned.
Next. Liverpool Man City Combined XI 2026. Liverpool vs. Man City Combined XI. dark

Whatever takes place in the stands is still secondary to the actual action on the pitch. City, lest it be forgotten, are top of the league with a perfect record under Enzo Maresca. Liverpool, by contrast, have dropped points to Newcastle United, Nottingham Forest and Fulham, three clubs who started the day in the bottom half of the Premier League table.
With all that in mind, Haaland’s confidence that City fans are “going to have a good time” at Anfield comes with some justification.

“We have to stick together,” City’s No. 9 told Sky Sports. “We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive. No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile. So we have to stay positive, look ahead, and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game.
“We have to stick together; we have to spread the love to each other. So yeah: stick together, and enjoy the ride and smile.”

ftbpro_01m4n96ezn87.title: Will Vinicius Jr Miss El Clasico After Crazy Red Card for Hair Pull?
ftbpro_01m4n96ezn87.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack9:30 AM EDTVinícius Júnior has found himself in hot water. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesJust for moment, the shackles were released.

Vinícius Júnior’s finish was simple. The Brazilian has scored more impressive and significant goals, but his close-range strike against Villarreal felt like a necessary cathartic release. Nine games and six weeks had passed since he last found the back of the net from open play.

His dip hasn’t merely been a source of concern for club and country, but the extent of his demise at the start of the 2026–27 season has ignited wild conspiracy theories regarding a potential body double. Genuinely.

Viní’s moment of joy against the Yellow Submarine would ultimately prove to be a cruel false dawn. Soon after, referee Isidro Díaz de Mera was summoned to the monitor, with the infringement initially unclear. There was no offside, but Real Madrid’s suffering goalscorer had instead drawn attention to a possible dismissal.
The fourth red card of Vinícius Jr’s senior career followed, thus chalking off his goal and immediately thrusting his status for the first Clásico of 2026–27 into doubt.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Madrid are expecting to be without Viní Jr for El Clásico. /  Jose Manuel Alvarez/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesThat’s the million-dollar question, and the referee’s match report will be key. De Mera has indicated that Vinícius Jr’s red card was an off-ball incident, which means he’s likely to be subject to more than the automatic one-match ban.
According to Spanish outlet COPE, Madrid are preparing for Vinícius Jr to serve a three-game suspension, meaning he’ll miss the trip to Catalonia on Oct. 25.

He’ll also sit out next week’s clash with Sevilla and the duel against Racing Santander at the start of November. The winger will be available for Madrid’s upcoming Champions League fixtures against Roma and RB Leipzig, however. Domestic suspensions do not carry over into Europe.

Madrid could appeal, but it’d be unlikely for Vinícius Jr to have his suspension reduced to just a single match. In May, Mallorca’s Johan Mojica received a two-match ban for pulling Roger Brugue’s hair.

So, the signs are pointing toward José Mourinho not having his struggling Brazilian star on hand for the first Clásico of the season. In the opinion of some Madrid supporters, that may not be such a bad thing, especially after Yan Diomande scored his first goal for the club in Saturday’s victory.

Hair pulling falls under Violent Conduct in IFAB’s laws.  / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesAfter passing to Jude Bellingham on the halfway line, Vinícius Jr’s long burst into the Villarreal box resulted in what he thought was his first goal since he struck in Madrid’s 4–1 victory over Real Sociedad on Aug. 26.

However, before making the aforementioned burst, the Brazilian, while trying to make his way around Nathan Saliba, pulled the Villarreal substitute’s hair. Saliba’s head briefly jerked back, but he didn’t kick up a fuss. The incident was spotted by the video assistant referee.
Under Law 12 of the IFAB Laws of the Game, pulling an opponent’s hair falls under violent conduct, warranting a straight red card.

Such punishment can appear harsh, most notably when Manchester United’s Lisandro Martínez was sent off against Leeds United in April, but Vinícius Jr, despite his strong remonstrations, could have no complaints.
Madrid’s No. 7 later apologized, writing on social media: “The joy continues. My apologies to my team and the fans.”

ftbpro_01m4n9kq0x2e.title: ‘They Forgot’—Vini Jr’s Contrasting Public, Private Response to Real Madrid Red Card
ftbpro_01m4n9kq0x2e.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:45 AM EDTVinícius Júnior (second from right) did not initially accept his red card well. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesVinícius Júnior offered a public apology after he was sent off for pulling the hair of Villarreal defender Nathan Saliba during Real Madrid’s hotly controversial 1–0 win on Saturday night. However, the Brazilian’s camp reportedly questioned the consistency of La Liga’s referees in a response with a different tone.

It was quite the two minutes for Madrid’s No. 7. With the hosts already in front thanks to Yan Diomande’s crisp swipe into the bottom corner, Vinícius Jr thought he had doubled their lead and broken his seven-game goal drought. Wild celebrations ensued, with José Mourinho awkwardly making his way across the pitch, half-running, half-jogging with all the commitment of a commuter vaguely embarrassed to be running after their bus.

That scrum was soon broken up by referee Isidro Díaz Mera, who was directed to the touchline by the video assistant referee (VAR), Alejandro Muñiz, to take another look at the footage. Upon review, it was clear that Vinícius Jr had a handful of Saliba’s hair before darting past him to meeting Jude Bellingham’s deft cutback in the penalty box.
The goal was chalked off and, to the consternation of a boiling Bernabéu, Vinícius Jr was shown a straight red card.
Madrid hung on to all three points across the final 20 minutes and Vinícius Jr saw the bright side on social media. “The joy continues,” he wrote on Instagram. “My apologies to my team and the fans.”
However, a separate response offered up by “a source close to” Vinícius Jr told The Athletic: “It [the red card] is fair, but they forgot the rule against Valencia.”

This is in reference to Real Madrid’s 2–1 win away to Valencia in January 2025. On that occasion, the hosts’ goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski appeared to pull the hair of Vinícius Jr, who reacted by shoving him to the ground. Madrid’s divisive forward was dismissed for violent conduct while Dimitrievski went curiously unpunished.

“It’s difficult being in his shoes,” Real Madrid’s manager at the time, Carlo Ancelotti, said of Vinícius Jr. “It’s not easy to endure everything he goes through, including the insults. It’s not simple, but he’s trying to improve. He’s upset about it and has apologized.”

Vinícius Júnior (left) didn’t have much of a case. / ESPN UK/Disney+Hair pulling has become an oddly hot topic in recent years. Three players were sent off for the offense in the 2025–26 Premier League season alone, prompting England’s law makers to apply a more lenient approach when judging these tugs. Yet, given the force with which Vinícius Jr yanked Saliba’s mass of curls, he didn’t have much of a defense.

As per Law 12, hair pulling is considered violent conduct, which is described as “when a player uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball.” This results in a straight red card and, typically, a three-match ban.
Considering Real Madrid face Barcelona in two weeks’ time, Vinícius Jr’s indiscretion could have serious repercussions.

ftbpro_01m4ncwwmysp.title: Arsenal Dealt ‘Shock Injury Blow’ After Final Whistle of Leeds Win
ftbpro_01m4ncwwmysp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:45 AM EDTMikel Arteta couldn’t be entirely happy with Saturday’s win. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesPiero Hincapié reportedly suffered an injury while going through his normal postmatch routine to sour Arsenal’s 2–1 victory over Leeds United on Saturday.

A collective exhale greeted the sharp parps of the final whistle at the Emirates. Arsenal had wobbled through a sloppy performance against an in-form Leeds side and still emerged with three points. The pain in Mikel Arteta’s eyes had been soothed by yet another demonstration of the quality the defending Premier League champions boast from the bench, with Bruno Guimarães coming on the score the winning goal.
However, it was another substitute which has come to Arteta’s attention for all the wrong reasons.

Piero Hincapié is a very useful squad option. / Ivan Romano/Getty ImagesHincapié was only called upon for the final eight minutes of Saturday’s league match. As is typical for the players on the matchday roster who did not start the fixture, the Ecuador international joined his teammates in a cool-down session. Yet, this injury prevention sent Hincapié to the treatment room. The Athletic cite a privately ascertained video showing the 24-year-old unable to put any weight on his right side while being helped off the pitch.

Arsenal are yet to offer an official diagnosis and it remains unclear how long Hincapié could be sidelined for. If the left back is forced to skip any upcoming fixtures, Arsenal’s strength in depth will actually be tested.

Myles Lewis-Skelly’s versatility could be needed. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesHincapié had already been struggling with a fitness issue before this latest setback. Without the combative left footer, Arteta’s only natural left back option is Riccardo Calafiori. That’s no bad thing; the Italian is enjoying a brilliant start to the season as Arsenal’s deft weapon of destruction. However, Calafiori has repeatedly proven to be vulnerable to niggles of his own, especially if he is overworked.

Arteta could turn to Myles Lewis-Skelly to pitch in at fullback. This was the teenager’s route into the first team before he graduated to midfield, where Lewis-Skelly has been playing so well in tandem with Declan Rice that Guimarães isn’t even guaranteed a start. Yet, the presence of the Brazilian would offer Arteta scope to rotate in the middle if Lewis-Skelly is shunted back.
Jurriën Timber could alternatively moonlight on his unnatural left hand side, even if the right footer never looks quite so comfortable on that wing.

Beyond fullback, Arteta isn’t blessed with an abundance of defensive options. While William Saliba continues his tentative return from a serious back injury, Arsenal only have three center backs to choose from; Gabriel, Ezri Konsa and Cristhian Mosquera. The last of those options, however, has not been included in a matchday squad since August while recovering from a hamstring injury.

The fixtures arrive in a deluge for Arsenal. The Champions League returns on Tuesday with a visit from French outfit Lille before the Gunners head on the road; taking on Nottingham Forest and German champions Bayern Munich in the space of four days. There are five games crammed into the remainder of October and November begins with the hardly gentle task of traveling to face Liverpool at Anfield.
For the sake of Hincapié and his teammates, there is abundance of hope that this injury isn’t as severe as it seems.

ftbpro_01m4ne2dw9rp.title: Reports: Why Mourinho Snubbed Postmatch Duties After Real Madrid Win
ftbpro_01m4ne2dw9rp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 11, 2026José Mourinho has quickly dropped the nice guy act. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIn the same interview with El Chiringuito, when José Mourinho suggested he was “more mature now, less emotional, more controlled,” the 63-year-old hinted that, ultimately, a leopard can’t change its spots.
“I’ve still got the same DNA,” he added. “Obviously, I can’t hide or try to be who I’m not.”

It hasn’t taken long at all for Mourinho to drop the faux Mr. Nice Guy act. He was in vintage form before the international break, producing a pair of printouts in his press conference to pinpoint the two red cards Atlético Madrid should’ve received before Real Madrid’s Dean Huijsen was dismissed at the start of the second half, tilting a drab derby firmly in Atléti’s favor.

And the extended international break hasn’t done an awful lot to mellow out the Madrid manager. In Saturday’s 1–0 victory over Villarreal, Mourinho joined in with his players’ celebrations after Vinícius Júnior thought he’d ended a six-week wait for a goal.
However, Mourinho’s jog down the touchline was merely a sequence that preceded unfortunate events.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mourinho was agitated throughout Saturday’s match. / Oscar DEL POZO/AFP/Getty ImagesYan Diomande may have scored his first Real Madrid goal, but Vinícius Jr’s red card for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in the build-up to his eventually disallowed finish was the major flashpoint of Los Blancos’ victory.

The Brazilian could have no complaints about the decision, with hair pulling falling under violent conduct in Law 12 of IFAB’s laws of the game. He’s now expected to miss El Clásico in two weeks, likely as part of a three-match suspension.

And a supposedly incensed Mourinho had no interest in joining Viní Jr on the suspension list for the trip to Barcelona. Mundo Deportivo and The Athletic reported that Mourinho told club officials after the match that he wouldn’t be speaking to the media due to the fear of potentially allowing his frustrations regarding the officiating to spill over.
“I want to be there against Sevilla and Barça,” Mourinho reportedly said.

The 63-year-old has quickly resorted to his favored “us-vs.-the world” ploy in a bid to galvanize a Madrid side that looks hopelessly second best to an imperious Barcelona in La Liga. Hansi Flick’s back-to-back champions won again at the weekend, before Madrid’s contentious triumph over Villarreal, and are six points clear of Mourinho’s men.
Atléti earned their fourth league victory in succession on Saturday, too, so they’re still a point better off than their cross-city rivals in second.

Yan Diomande scored his first Madrid goal. /  Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesWhile the nature of it was unimpressive and marred by Vinícius Jr’s red card, Madrid nonetheless secured a necessary victory against an opponent that finished third in La Liga last season.

But there’s so far been little to suggest that Mourinho is the man to help Los Blancos dethrone La Blaugrana. Flick’s Barça are defined by their ferocious intensity out of possession, telepathy with the ball and magic of Lamine Yamal down the right flank. Madrid still look like a muddled outfit waiting for their supreme individuality to shine through.

And one of their stars, Vinícius Jr, is in the midst of a rough patch—the sort that has led conspiracy theorists to wonder whether the Brazilian was replaced with a body double after the World Cup. Kylian Mbappé also has a remarkable knack for frustrating supporters every time he takes to the field despite his stellar scoring record for the club.
We’re still waiting for solid evidence that the pair can harmoniously coexist as part of a winning machine.

A tricky period is on the horizon, too. The first Clásico of the season is on everyone’s minds in the capital, evidenced by Mourinho’s postmatch play on Saturday, but by honing in on the champions, Madrid risk falling asleep at the wheel when they continue their Champions League campaign against Roma and RB Leipzig. Sevilla and Racing Santander are unlikely to be pushed over either.

ftbpro_01m4nezqwnht.title: ‘We’ve Seen Enough’—Gary Neville Puts Man Utd Duo on Blast After Spurs Stumble
ftbpro_01m4nezqwnht.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby Lane11:35 AM EDTYouri Tielemans has endured a testing start to his Liverpool career. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesManchester United were held to a frustrating 1–1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, leaving former defender Gary Neville questioning the effort and energy of Michael Carrick’s side, with two midfielders, Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo, coming under particular scrutiny.

Despite Spurs being reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal, United failed to hold on to their lead after Bryan Mbeumo’s 73rd-minute opener. Dominic Solanke struck a stoppage-time equalizer to deny Michael Carrick’s side all three points, leaving United 12th in the Premier League after six games.
The disappointing result prompted boos from the Old Trafford crowd, with Neville offering a scathing assessment of United’s performance on The Gary Neville Podcast.

Neville identified the midfield partnership of Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo as a problem. While acknowledging the quality of both players individually, he questioned whether they possess the dynamism needed to operate effectively alongside each other in the Premier League.

Tielemans had a game to forget against Spurs. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images“With Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we’ve seen enough of it now,” Neville said. “I’m not calling time on it because I think that’s probably too drastic—but I’ve seen enough of it to think it’s not dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.
“They are both good players individually, but sometimes you have players who just don’t quite knit together and suit each other.”

Neville also pointed to the impact of summer signing Carlos Baleba, who came off the bench against Spurs with just over half an hour remaining. The former United defender felt the midfield looked more energetic when Baleba partnered Mainoo, suggesting Carrick may need to reconsider his options in the middle of the pitch.

“When Baleba came on with Mainoo, that certainly looked more like there was more energy, but there is going to have to be something done in there, and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip,” he added.

Heads were hung on Saturday. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesThe former defender questioned the team’s work rate and intensity, arguing that their lack of effort was becoming a major concern.

United have come under scrutiny for their physical output this season, ranking among the Premier League’s lowest teams for distance covered, sprints and high-intensity running. Tielemans himself has also admitted that the team did not do enough work in that area during preseason.
Neville questioned whether United’s struggles were down to a loss of confidence or a deeper issue within the squad.

“The shake of Carrick's head will be ... are they doing it for me? What’s happening with that lot?” Neville said. “Have they lost their confidence? Have they switched off? Are they going under? What is going on? Because these aren’t the players I was working with last season.”
The pressure is on for Carrick. / Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty ImagesUnited’s midfield concerns could become even more significant as the team prepares for a demanding run of fixtures.
They face Atlético Madrid in the Champions League in midweek before traveling to Elland Road to take on an in-form Leeds United next weekend.

With the schedule set to intensify, United are approaching a period in which they will play almost twice a week until the next international break in mid-November. Given their struggles against Spurs, Neville is worried about whether the squad has the physicality and mental resilience to cope with the increased demands.
“It is a real concern, going into a slog where you are playing every three days and the Champions League is going to hit you hard,” he said.

“You’ve got tough matches, and all of the games coming up are going to need real personality and character. It needs a group of players who are resilient, and at the moment, you do worry about them going into that run of matches and how they are going to come out of it.”

ftbpro_01m4nhggnz2v.title: Three Takeaways From Man City’s Act of Defiance Against Liverpool and Anfield
ftbpro_01m4nhggnz2v.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby LaneOct 11, 2026Cherki produced a piece of magic. / Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesManchester City extended their lead at the top of the Premier League with an ultimately comfortable 3–0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, making it six wins from six to maintain their perfect start to the season.

Heading into the game, the focus was as much on City’s ongoing financial case as it was on the soccer itself. With the club found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them, questions over potential punishments—including points deductions and stripped titles—continued to dominate the headlines.

It was perhaps fitting that their first game since the verdict should come against Liverpool, who were so often denied by City. Could the Reds get some kind of redemption? Could they halt a City side that had won all five of its opening league games? The atmosphere at Anfield certainly suggested the home crowd believed an upset was possible.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
The answer, however, was a resounding no.

While City were not at their fluent best throughout, they capitalized on Ryan Gravenberch’s second-half sending-off to take control and secure a convincing victory thanks to goals from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki.
Haaland scored again. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesCity were unsurprisingly met with a hostile reception at Anfield, with the club’s impending punishment looming large over the occasion.

Fans lined the streets outside the stadium to make their feelings known, while boos rang out around the stadium as the teams took to the pitch. Liverpool’s players also appeared fired up, with a few heated exchanges and flashes of confrontation adding to the tension in the opening stages.

After the early hostility subsided, the game settled into a more familiar pattern. City were far from their best, but still dominated possession and created the clearer chances, as they so often do. Liverpool threatened in spells of their own, but Gravenberch’s dismissal for a second bookable offense midway through the second half shifted the balance firmly in City’s favor.

Haaland broke the deadlock with a fierce finish, before Doku curled home a superb second to put City in control. A moment of Cherki magic then capped off the victory, sealing an ultimately comfortable 3–0 win for Enzo Maresca’s side.
Despite the hostility and noise surrounding the club, City let their soccer do the talking.

Their performance may not have been flawless, but the result sent a clear message: whatever challenges await them off the pitch, they remain focused on winning—and their perfect start to the season shows no sign of slowing down.

Wirtz didn’t make an impact. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesDespite the scoreline, it was not all one-way traffic, particularly before Gravenberch’s red card. Liverpool started both halves brightly and showed enough attacking intent to suggest they could cause an upset.

Much of Liverpool’s attacking play ran through Florian Wirtz, but the big-money signing from Bayer Leverkusen last summer struggled to make his involvement count. The German repeatedly made poor decisions in promising positions, often passing when he had a chance to shoot and shooting when a teammate was better placed. His indecision was frustrating to watch and appeared to test the patience of those around him.
He also gave possession away on several occasions, struggled to impose himself physically and looked short of the confidence that made him such an exciting prospect at Leverkusen.

The bigger concern for Liverpool is that Wirtz’s struggles are becoming difficult to ignore, yet their options for replacing him are limited. That leaves Iraola with little choice but to keep backing the German and trust that he can eventually find his feet.
For now, though, Wirtz is continuing to fall well short of expectations.

Guéhi was too good for Koumas. / Isaac Parkin/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesWith Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Hugo Ekitiké all unavailable, Iraola handed young Lewis Koumas his first-ever Premier League start against City.

The Wales international showed plenty of effort, covering ground and chasing long balls while leading the line alone. However, the 21-year-old is simply not yet at the level Liverpool need to compete with the Premier League’s strongest sides.

That was particularly evident in his battle with Marc Guéhi. The City defender comfortably held Koumas off and kept him under control, while the young forward also missed a clear-cut chance in the second half.

ftbpro_01m4nhq9q8jw.title: President Trump Receives Tribute From U.S. Owner of European Soccer Giants
ftbpro_01m4nhq9q8jw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom1:00 PM EDTPresident Donald Trump (left) would appear to have a supporter in the form of Milan owner Gerry Cardinale (far right). / Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images (Trump), Giuseppe Cottini/AC Milan/Getty Images (Pulisic and Cardinale)AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale arrived at his manager Ruben Amorim’s prematch press conference this week wearing a cap clearly inspired by U.S. President Donald Trump’s famous slogan. Rather than the country of his birth, the white lettering on Cardinale’s red hat read: “Make Milan Great Again.”

There is a distinctly American twang to Milan these days. Cardinale, the club’s owner since a $1.2 billion acquisition in August 2022, was born in Villanova, Pa., an hour and a half drive west of Hershey, Pa. where the team’s No. 11, Christian Pulisic, was raised.
Pulisic’s U.S. compatriot Yunus Musah has appeared in every Milan fixture this season after winning his spot back.

Pulisic has dished out his own nods to Trump in the past. The U.S. men’s national team’s former figurehead caused controversy when he celebrated a goal for the Stars and Stripes in 2024 with a series of contortions inspired by the President. “Well obviously that’s the Trump dance,” Pulisic said at the time. “It was just a dance that everyone’s doing. He’s the one who created it. I just thought it was funny.”

Former USMNT star Tim Howard derided the move as “stupid” and dismissed any claims at impartiality from the forward. “I don’t buy that,” he scoffed. “Any show of support for Donald Trump is political.”
Cardinale has done little to hide his interest in Trump’s politics.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Gerry Cardinale has spoken openly about President Trump in the past. / Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg/Getty ImagesCardinale’s quest to make Milan “great again” has not been without its difficulties. After inheriting a side which had just been crowned Serie A champions, the U.S. founder of investment group RedBird Capital is yet to see the capture of a major title, with Milan slipping to eighth and fifth in the last two seasons.

It’s been a frustrating adaptation for a businessman who has found “enormous resistance to evolving” in the soccer world. Cardinale’s approach as a disruptor has served him well in other spheres and is why he speaks so favorably about Trump’s administration.

In an interview with the Financial Times earlier this year, Cardinale explained: “Trump is taking the lead in re-underwriting the public-private partnership. We have so much expertise in the private sector in America and the President is harnessing that for the country. That’s what I’m talking about over here in Italy. That’s what I want to see.”

This very week, Cardinale laid out why he would consider it counterintuitive for someone in his position to not have a relationship with Trump’s White House. “You have an administration that’s pro-business. Anybody in corporate America should have a relationship with that administration,” he told the Bloomberg Screentime conference in L.A.
“And that’s not because it’s Trump. Trump is pro-business, he’s very interested in the technology community.”

ftbpro_01m4njf3z5w7.title: Why Vinicius Jr Isn’t Suspended for Real Madrid’s Next Match After Red Card
ftbpro_01m4njf3z5w7.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 11, 2026Vinícius Júnior picked up the fourth red card of his senior career. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesFor just the fourth time in his senior career, Vinícius Júnior was shown a red card. His latest indiscretion was rather bizarre, given that it came directly after he’d seemingly handed Real Madrid a 2–0 lead in their La Liga encounter against Villarreal.

The simple strike, which arrived courtesy of Jude Bellingham’s brilliance down the left flank, was set to end a six-week wait for a goal from open play. Vinícius Jr celebrated as usual, joined by José Mourinho, who, at the age of 63, didn’t quite move with the vigor he once did, but the Brazilian’s joy was short-lived.

Intervention from the video assistant referee didn’t merely chalk the Brazilian’s goal off, but replays also showed that Vinícius Jr’s advantageous position when running beyond Nathan Saliba was gained via a hair pull.
And according to IFAB’s Law 12, that’s violent conduct. A red card was just.

A livid Mourinho refused to speak to the media postmatch, with Vinícius Jr now on course to miss the first Clásico due to suspension. However, Madrid will have their struggling Brazilian star available for upcoming their next match.

Viní Jr will still be available for Madrid’s upcoming European bouts. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesIsidro Díaz de Mera’s report is unlikely to do the player any favors, and Madrid, who will appeal, are expecting Vinícius Jr to receive a three-match ban.

Los Blancos have two Champions League games scheduled during that period, but domestic suspensions do not carry over into European competitions. The Brazilian has to serve his ban in La Liga, meaning if a three-match ban is his punishment, he’ll miss games against Sevilla, Barcelona and Racing Santander before returning against Valencia on Nov. 8.

The Champions League really gets rolling over the next few weeks. After just one league phase gameweek scheduled during the season’s opening act, Madrid have three European fixtures before the national teams convene again next month. Roma, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens all await. Assuming he avoids injury, Viní Jr will be available for all three games.

It’s a critical period for Mourinho, who hasn’t yet convinced the majority that he’s the right man to help Los Blancos usurp Barcelona domestically. Moreover, anything but another total conquest of Europe is regarded as a failure for the 15-time European champions, and Mourinho hasn’t gotten his hands on the Champions League since he inspired Inter Milan to the treble in 2010.

One of Madrid’s upcoming opponents, Roma, will be breathing a sigh of relief after Donyell Malen was sent off in their Serie A draw with Como on Sunday. Malen, who’s been one of the most prolific performers on the planet this calendar year, will serve a domestic ban, but line up when the Giallarossi hosts Mourinho’s side on Matchday 2 of the league phase on Wednesday.

ftbpro_01m4nmm46p4p.title: Liverpool vs. Man City Player Ratings: Premier League’s Villains Embrace Their Role
ftbpro_01m4nmm46p4p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:48 PM EDTMan City took full advantage of Ryan Gravenberch’s red card.  / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesManchester City ran amok after Ryan Gravenberch was shown a second yellow card on the hour of Sunday’s eagerly anticipated Premier League clash at Anfield, with superb goals from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki seeing the visitors home.

The Cityzens were, of course, in action for the first time since an independent comission ruled that the club were guilty on almost all counts of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations.

A hostile, bitter Anfield thus met the defiant visitors, who were aiming to respond to Arsenal’s come-from-behind victory against Leeds United. And while many will question the significance of these points in the long run, there’s no denying that City’s response was emphatic.

It was control versus chaos, and Maresca’s facilitation of the former won out on Merseyside. Liverpool were bright enough but hindered by key absences, particularly in attack. They offered plenty of bark but little bite, and City made them pay after Gravenberch’s dismissal.

The Reds collapsed, in truth, but City’s goals were of the highest quality. Within six minutes of Gravenberch solemnly strolling down the tunnel, strikes from Haaland and Doku handed Maresca’s side a 2–0 lead. Cherki’s goal 13 minutes later was typical of the Frenchman, and wrapped up the perfect day out for the almost-universally resented Cityzens.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Anfield was vociferous in its reproach of the visitors. / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesThis was the fixture the soccer world had waited ever so patiently for since Manchester City’s guilty verdict came to light two weeks ago. A trip to Anfield just had to be on the horizon, didn’t it?

The extent of City’s financial doping has brought the sport, particularly the Premier League, into disrepute, with its consequences catastrophically far-reaching. Liverpool have every right to feel most aggrieved, given that the number of duels lost to Pep Guardiola’s Cityzens during Jürgen Klopp’s reign.

And this was the first meeting between the two clubs without either of the aforementioned managers in over a decade. In truth, the on-field action almost felt secondary. Much of the intrigue surrounding the pre-match histrionics and Anfield’s reaction to the great injustice.

Evasive action was taken by the visitors, who took an unfamiliar route to the ground and were keen to offer their show of defiance. Supporters ’Poznan-d’ in the face of “You’ll Never Walk Alone,” booed the Premier League anthem and waved inflatable bananas in homage to bleaker times in a pre-Premier League world. They’re victims in all this, too; but on Merseyside, they sided with those boasting the “irrefutable evidence” that’s yet to come to light.

And ultimately, Enzo Maresca’s side would prove that, despite the animosity, they remain an excellent soccer team. Fans will relish the short-term glee, but the majority will wonder what this all means
Lewis Koumas led Liverpool’s attack. / Paul ELLIS/AFP/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—4.9: There wasn’t all that much Liverpool’s goalkeeper could’ve done here. He was beaten by some outrageous quality from the away side.
RB: Ronald Araújo—6.5: Antoine Semenyo certainly felt he had the beating of the Barcelona loanee, who is proving a surprisingly valuable asset in the final third.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—5.9: There were some masterful defensive sequences from the Frenchman, but City did have plenty of joy exploiting the channel Jacquet was supposed to be manning.

CB: Virgil van Dijk—5,8: Van Dijk was forced into a rather unfamiliar role due to City’s midfield overload. The Dutchman sought to quell this threat by stepping out of Liverpool’s defense and playing a key role in Iraola’s heavy man-to-man approach.
LB: Milos Kerkez—6.1: Ignored as an attacking outlet, and struggles to fill you with any confidence defensively.
CM: Ryan Gravenberch—6.5: This was Gravenberch of 2024–25... right up until he received a second yellow card just after the hour mark.
CM: Alexis Mac Allister—6.5: An up-and-down afternoon for Mac Allister, who scrapped around for the opening hour but struggled to offer any security thereafter.
RW: Víctor Muñoz—6.7: A real livewire who the Anfield faithful have quickly taken to. Nico O’Reilly had his work cut out all afternoon.

ftbpro_01m4nn9sm1vs.title: Andoni Iraola Dealt Third Huge Injury Blow for Crunch Man City Clash
ftbpro_01m4nn9sm1vs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:53 AM EDTDominik Szoboszlai is a surprise absentee. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesNot content with the absences of Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, the fickle fitness fates have robbed Liverpool of Dominik Szoboszlai thanks to a reported hamstring injury.

The legendary former Reds boss Bob Paisley used to say: “You keep your fingers crossed about injuries. That is in the lap of the gods.” Those looking down upon Andoni Iraola have not been favorable this weekend.

The Basque boss was already denied the chance to field his leading scorer and most prolific creator, with short-term injuries sustained on international duty ruling out Isak and Gakpo. Liverpool’s reigning Player of the Season can be added to the list absentees, with The Athletic’s James Pearce first to report of a hamstring injury for the midfielder.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Szoboszlai had previously started all six of Liverpool’s Premier League and Champions League fixtures this season, operating in a range of roles in an area of the pitch which Iraola hasn’t quite figured out yet. Hungary’s captain dutifully started all four of his country’s Nations League fixture this fall and was spotted back in Liverpool training this week.
Nevertheless, he clearly wasn’t fit enough to make Sunday’s squad, let alone the starting XI.
Starting XI: Alisson; Ronald Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet, Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch; Víctor Muñoz, Lewis Koumas, Bradley Barcola.
Substitutes: Giorgi Mamardashvili, Joe Gomez, Wataru Endo, Federico Chiesa, Kostas Tsimikas, Jeremie Frimpong, Trey Nyoni, James McConnell, Rio Ngumoha.

In place of Szoboszlai, Iraola was left with Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch in a midfield pairing behind Florian Wirtz. While Liverpool’s No. 8 had been an ever-present, his two defensively minded colleagues were fighting for the spot next to him.

Gravenberch started the season alongside Hungary’s skipper but his natural inclination to push up the pitch only exposed the yawning chasms which can readily appear in Iraola’s front-footed system. Mac Allister was brought in to shore up that central slice of the pitch and has helped Liverpool keep three consecutive Premier League clean sheets. Now the duo will have to work together to shut out the likes of Erling Haaland.

Lewis Koumas has won Andoni Iraola’s heart. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesIronically enough, it was Szoboszlai who insisted earlier this season that Lewis Koumas, the 21-year-old academy graduate with scarcely any senior experience, “deserved to play” ahead of some of Liverpool’s expensively acquired forwards.

Iraola has openly shared this stance, repeatedly lauding the industry, rather than dexterity, of the hard-running forward who, prior to Sunday, had just 22 minutes of Premier League soccer under his belt.
“The energy he shows is contagious for the rest,” Iraola gushed last month. “When they see the ones up front doing it, they are forced to go from behind.”

ftbpro_01m4np0chx7v.title: ‘A Lot of Interest’—Endrick’s Agent Takes Clear Stance on Real Madrid Future
ftbpro_01m4np0chx7v.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby Lane12:30 PM EDTEndrick is struggling for minutes. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesEndrick’s Real Madrid future appears settled for now, with the agent of the Brazilian forward dismissing speculation that he could leave the Santiago Bernabéu in January despite “a lot of interest.”

The 20-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Lyon, scoring eight goals in 21 appearances. However, he has struggled for opportunities this term under José Mourinho, playing just four minutes and prompting speculation that another move could be on the cards.
AS Roma, AC Milan and Manchester United have all been linked with the Brazil international, who could be tempted to seek regular first-team soccer elsewhere.
Speaking to Italian publication Adnkronos, Alan Redmond, Global Head of Football at Roc Nation Sports International, the agency representing Endrick, dismissed the prospect of an imminent departure.

“In Endrick’s case, he’s always said he wants to stay at Real Madrid, and I’m convinced that this season, when he gets the chance, he’ll score a lot of goals. I can confirm that there was a lot of interest in him in the summer, from various countries, but his goal was never to leave Spain,” Redmond said.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
He added: “The financial aspect isn’t important; the player evaluates the club’s project. We’re talking about a player with the qualities to be at Real Madrid—he just needs opportunities.
“Endrick came from a loan spell at Lyon and played very well in France, then he had some problems, and I think it was also quite frustrating for him not to be at his best physically.

“However, the idea has always been to stay in Madrid. We’ll see what happens in the future, but honestly, I think he’ll stay at Real Madrid for a long time. That’s my opinion. I don’t think he’ll move.”

Endrick can’t catch a break lately. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesRedmond’s comments suggest that Endrick remains committed to making his mark in Madrid, despite his limited involvement this season. However, with the young forward having already demonstrated his potential during his spell in France, questions remain over whether staying at the Bernabéu is the best move for his development.

For a striker at this stage of his career, regular minutes can be crucial if he is to fulfil his potential. If opportunities remain scarce, another loan spell or even a permanent departure could become increasingly appealing.
So, how can Endrick force his way into Real Madrid’s plans? And if regular first-team soccer remains out of reach, would leaving the Spanish giants ultimately be the best decision for his career?

Mourinho is a fan of Espi. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesEndrick has endured a frustrating start to the 2026–27 season at Real Madrid, with a combination of injury problems and competition for places limiting his opportunities under José Mourinho.

The Brazilian began the campaign nursing a recurring hamstring injury, which ruled him out of selection for Madrid’s first four games of the season. During his absence, young Spanish striker Carlos Espí featured on the bench, coming on in three matches and scoring once.

Since Endrick returned to fitness in mid-September, however, neither youngster has been given much playing time. Both have remained on the bench for every game since, making just one appearance each as late substitutes in a 3–2 win over Elche.
Endrick was introduced on the right wing, while Espí came on in his preferred central striking role and ultimately stole the headlines by scoring a stoppage-time winner.

For now, Mourinho has two young attacking options competing for opportunities, but Espí appears to have the edge as a central striker, particularly given his recent form. Endrick, meanwhile, is still waiting for a meaningful chance to prove himself.

That does not necessarily mean Mourinho has lost faith in the Brazilian. In fact, the Madrid boss previously explained why he chose to keep Endrick at the club over the summer, suggesting he believes the youngster has a bright future in the Spanish capital.

Asked why he did not allow Endrick to leave Madrid during the summer, Mourinho told TNT Brazil: “Because of the qualities he possesses, the positions he can play in ... He’s a goalscorer and teams need goals. And he’ll obviously have plenty of opportunities to play and develop. Then, with the national team, he’ll find another manager who can really help him develop.”
Mourinho also acknowledged that Endrick was not yet ready to play extended minutes, adding that “he is not in condition to play for more than five or 10 minutes.”

ftbpro_01m4nsyr7xjs.title: Supercomputer Predicts Premier League Table As Man City Send Arsenal Title Statement
ftbpro_01m4nsyr7xjs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 11, 2026Amid all the uncertainties surrounding this season, Manchester City can always rely upon their guarantee of goals. / Isaac Parkin/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesErling Haaland has chosen his words well this week.

Manchester City’s most convincing voice won the hearts and minds of supporters reeling from the seismic Premier League verdict before thrashing in the opening goal of Sunday’s win over Liverpool. Rather than focusing on the clash of flesh which he had just endured, Haaland tellingly called the contest a “mental battle.”

Until City’s appeal is heard and a punishment is dished out, every Premier League match involving the club lambasted as a “sham” by their own competition will require some mental gymnastics. The meeting between Liverpool and City was rightly billed as the most important game of the weekend but if the Etihad outfit are deducted enough points to guarantee relegation, it will have been an entirely meaningless endeavor.
In light of the few certainties which exist in this legal limbo, there is always Opta’s supercomputer to turn to.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Liverpool slipped on this banana peel of a fixture. / Isaac Parkin/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesPredicted Position / Club

In a world where City aren’t sanctioned—the reality which the club’s owners refuse to leave—Arsenal still remain favorites to claim a second successive Premier League, but only just. The Gunners labored to a win against Leeds United on Saturday which still left them three points adrift of Enzo Maresca’s faultless leaders by the weekend’s finish. Mikel Arteta has a formidable roster of talent, but City aren’t exactly short of star power themselves—and still will be thanks to the lack of relegation clauses in players’ contracts.

Remarkably, Brighton & Hove Albion are third favorites to win the Premier League title. The Seagulls dismantled Arsenal before the international break and returned from the three-week hiatus to claim a fourth win from six top-flight fixtures. They also dumped Manchester United out of the Carabao Cup.

However, Fabian Hürzeler is keen to avoid getting ahead of himself. “Maybe I sound a little old school now but there’s an old phrase: Defense wins championships—and we’re not speaking about championships,” he quickly interjected, “don’t get me wrong, but defense wins also games.”
Chelsea could do with learning that lesson. Xabi Alonso’s free-wheeling entertainers haven’t kept a Premier League clean sheet since January.
Bruno Fernandes has ambitions beyond Champions League qualification. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesPredicted Position / Club

Once again, any sporting sanction for Manchester City will surely disrupt the race for Champions League qualification. Yet, at this point in time there would appear to be a clear top four, with Liverpool ranked as one of the likeliest European qualifiers despite their teething problems under Andoni Iraola.

Manchester United, by contrast, have a long road ahead if continental competition is to be on the cards next season. The Red Devils have made their worst start to a league season in 40 years. They would finish that campaign with the club’s greatest ever manager at the helm but even Sir Alex Ferguson could only oversee an 11th-place finish.

The likes of Brentford, Everton and Newcastle United habor lofty dreams of their own after making strong starts. The Bees appear best-placed to mount the strongest challenge, while Everton and Newcastle may struggle to maintain their form with such thin squads.
Tottenham’s first challenge is survival. / Jan Kruger/Getty ImagesPredicted Position / Club

Hull City and Ipswich Town have the same points as Liverpool after six games of the new season. The two freshly promoted clubs are still focused on survival but it’s been an encouraging start to life back in the top flight. The same cannot be said of Coventry City, even if Frank Lampard’s side did end a 25-year wait for a Premier League win before the international break.

Tottenham Hotspur are still waiting for that sweet taste of victory, but at least Roberto De Zerbi’s side are predicted to avoid relegation. It’s a testament to the new realities of N17 that the manager can take heart from his midfielder heatbutting an opponent simply because it shows some character. Spurs will have to balance that fight with some finesse if they are to fulfill the supercomputer’s prediction.

ftbpro_01m4ntmq5tnx.title: Liverpool vs. Man City: Everything That Happened Off the Pitch in Gripping Psychodrama
ftbpro_01m4ntmq5tnx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom1:28 PM EDTManchester City fans were defiant in the face of fierce opposition. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesManchester City’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday could never be about the on-pitch action.

As soon as the Premier League dropped its explosive statement revealing how an independent commission had found City guilty of concocting “sham contracts,” “sham agreements” and “sham commercial deals” over nine seasons during the international break, the club’s next away game was always going to be hostile.

The fact their hosts would be Liverpool, a team with a fearsome and vocal fanbase enraged as direct victims of City’s “disguised funding scheme,” cranked up the anticipation of the occasion even more.

City would reestablish a three-point lead at the Premier League summit, Ryan Gravenberch skirted between hero and villain while Rayan Cherki delivered a contender for the most impish goal of the season. But plenty of focus was rightly directed away from the rectangle of green.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Circumstance meant that Merseyside on a sunny Sunday afternoon was never going to be mistaken for the seventh circle of hell, but Liverpool’s fans made sure there was the smell of sulfur in a red sky pregame.

Manchester City have had their run-ins with Liverpool’s fanbase on previous occasions. Bottles, cans and fireworks were infamously aimed at the club’s team bus ahead of a Champions League tie in 2018.
In order to avoid a repeat—or an escalation—of those scenes, City’s coach was steered to a second Anfield entrance away from the largest concentration of Liverpool fans.
City’s supporters weren’t kept quite as far away from their red counterparts, with some jostling and an exchange of jibes (rather than jabs) as police managed to contain the animosity.

There were tense scenes as a large group of City fans were escorted into the away end a few minutes ago. There were a couple of minor scuffles with stewards and some beer was thrown but other than that order was maintained pic.twitter.com/tGWKyjtd96

The fans who were not distracted by the prospect of a fight had the chance to mark this memorable occasion with a souvenir. The streets leading up to the stadium were lined with stalls teeming with pieces of memorabilia at City’s expense.

Some Liverpool fans were trying to cash in. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesThere was an Oasis flavor to a lot of the apparel, given the band’s famous support of City. Some of the visiting fans were inclined to make a few purchases of their own.
‘Guilty’ flags and ‘cheats’ scarves are among the merch being sold outside Anfield today pic.twitter.com/BfL57K1eYo
Liverpool fans boo the City players, the City fans boo the PL anthem. ‘We know what you are’ from the Kop, a Poznan in the away end. It’s had the lot! pic.twitter.com/NF3tfmY2DD

If there had been any doubt about the position of Liverpool’s supporters in regards to Manchester City’s guilt, they let it be known on Sunday. While most Premier League managers danced around the topic, Anfield was awash with flags and banners that spelled out the fans’ indignation in giant letters.
Liverpool had come prepared. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesThe Kop has a banner with 114 pound signs (probably, I didn’t count) pic.twitter.com/Lba6P9Pka5

Man City’s owner come under fire. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesConsidering the limited goal threat from both sides across a scrappy opening 45 minutes, there was more creativity in the stands than on the pitch.

Liverpool fans got creative. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesThere was more creativity in the stands than on the pitch. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesBanner in the Kop: ‘After All You Really Robbed Us All.’ pic.twitter.com/n2u5N20AXi

Ferran Soriano faced the music. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesCity have taken a front-foot approach throughout these proceedings. The club still vehemently insist their innocence and chief executive Ferran Soriano was in the Anfield stands as a show of defiance.
Those above Soriano in City’s hierarchy didn’t brave the wall of noise, although chants and masks of the club’s owner Sheikh Mansour were prevalent on Merseyside.

ftbpro_01m4p14z927t.title: USMNT Star Alex Freeman Outshines Real Madrid’s Galacticos, Other Americans Dazzle Overseas
ftbpro_01m4p14z927t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack2:30 PM EDTAlex Freeman (right) impressed in Villarreal’s defeat to Real Madrid. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIt was a perfect fall for the U.S. men’s national team, who claimed four victories as manager Mauricio Pochettino successfully capitalized on the momentum gained from an impressive World Cup campaign on home soil.

The burgeoning American youth reminded senior figures that their spots within Pochettino’s framework are not guaranteed. Thus, there was plenty of intrigue as European club soccer returned to the fold after a three-week absence.

There’s no longer a premier division across the Atlantic bereft of American interest, and much of this weekend’s attention was cast on the Santiago Bernabéu, as Alex Freeman’s Villarreal faced up against mighty Real Madrid.

Amid the milestones and chaos in Spain’s capital, USMNT supporters would’ve been greatly encouraged by Freeman’s showing for the Yellow Submarine. However, the fullback was just one of several impressive USMNT performers across Europe this weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Ligero como una moto, potente como un camión. Gran carrera y rectificación de Alex Freeman para evitar el tiro de Diomandé.#RealMadridVillarreal | #LaLigaHighlights pic.twitter.com/0DvzTqvX4E

Orlando City sold homegrown Freeman to Villarreal for a franchise-record fee in January, and the 22-year-old, despite limited La Liga action during the second half of last season, was included on Pochettino’s 26-man World Cup roster in the summer.

Freeman started all but one of the USMNT’s matches at the tournament (the anomaly being the group stage dead rubber against Türkiye) and scored in the Matchday 2 victory over Australia. He’s become an indispensable figure for the Argentine boss, who has spoken glowingly of the dynamic fullback throughout his tenure at U.S. Soccer.
During the World Cup, the USMNT manager went as far as to say Freeman could become “one of the best players at his position in the world.”

To garner such recognition, Freeman will first need to establish himself at Villarreal, and it seems the 22-year-old is finding his feet. Under the newly appointed Iñigo Pérez, once Andoni Iraola’s right-hand man at Rayo Vallecano, Freeman has started four of Villarreal’s previous five La Liga outings, and his performance against Real Madrid earned lofty praise from Spanish outlet Marca, which said Freeman “dominated” Los Blancos on Saturday.

Freeman has become a starter for the Yellow Submarine.  /  Pedro Salado/Getty ImagesDespite tasting defeat, Freeman was named FotMob’s Man of the Match with an impressive stat line. He ended the match with the most defensive contributions (18), most touches (93), a 75% ground-duel success rate and a 60% aerial-duel success rate.

Freeman was able to showcase his standout athleticism and stellar recovery speed during a first-half sequence in which a slight misjudgment was initially seized upon by Real Madrid’s Yan Diomande. Freeman recovered, though, and timed his challenger brilliantly with a sweeping slide tackle.

As the son of former Green Bay Packers wide receiver Antonio Freeman, it’s no surprise that Freeman is an elite athlete; however, the 22-year-old has also earned praise for his tactical astuteness and efficiency in the build-up phase.

Given the extent of Pochettino’s endorsement and Freeman’s recent success, the young talent is a sure bet to remain a staple down the USMNT’s right-hand side. The World Cup, combined with the autumnal youth revolution, offered a glimpse into an exciting future for Pochettino’s side, with Freeman among the key cogs.

Joe Scally scored on Derby Day. / Lars Baron/Getty ImagesJoe Scally was included on Pochettino’s World Cup roster but was absent this fall. Determined to swiftly work his way back into the fold, the defender found himself on the scoresheet in Borussia Mönchengladbach’s derby defeat to FC Köln in the Bundesliga. It was just the eighth goal of the 23-year-old’s senior career but the second he has scored this season.

Atlético Madrid midfielder Johnny Cardoso was also omitted from Pochettino’s most recent roster and hasn’t yet found his feet in Diego Simeone’s engine room. However, Cardoso produced an assured display in La Liga on Saturday, as Atléti scored late on to defeat Alavés 2–1.

Bryan Reynolds has been away from the USMNT for three years, but the 25-year-old produced a standout performance out of the blue at the weekend. The Rennes fullback recorded two assists in a 4–1 victory over Auxerre in what was his first Ligue 1 start. Reynolds is unlikely to be considered by Pochettino any time soon, but how about that for a blast from the past?
