ftbpro_01m4p63rkx05.title: How Lionel Messi's Players to Watch From 2024, 2025 Have Fared
ftbpro_01m4p63rkx05.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 17, 2026Lionel Messi has tipped several Argentinian hotshots for great things. / Luis ROBAYO/AFP/Getty ImagesThe twilight of Lionel Messi’s glittering career has thrust him into conversations that transcend mere greatness.

After inspiring Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022, Messi, at the age of 39, almost single-handedly guided a distinctly flawed Albiceleste side at the end of its tether to back-to-back successes on the biggest stage. He subsequently bade a dignified farewell to the national team this fall and is continuing to dominate Major League Soccer with Inter Miami.

For all his majesty, Messi has seldom portrayed himself as a soccer obsessive. You couldn’t imagine him churning out a multi-hour Football Manager session, for example, or even tuning into a match in which he doesn’t have a vested interest.

Yet adidas would lead you to believe that Messi is spending his downtime, of which he does have more of nowadays, watching AZ Alkmaar’s latest Eredivisie encounter, keeping tabs on their exciting young midfielder, Kees Smit.

Smit is one of the 10 rising stars backed by Messi in adidas’s latest campaign. The Argentinian great has provided such lists sporadically since 2015; the latest batch of rising stars follows two sets of 10 offered in both 2024 and 2025.

It may be too soon to discern whether Messi—or rather adidas, given that the players included are all adidas-sponsored—“knows ball,” as the chronically online generation would say. Nevertheless, enough time has elapsed to gauge whether he/they were onto something.
Here’s a breakdown of how Messi’s tipped future stars from the previous two years have since fared.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Ndala didn’t make the grade at Manchester City. / Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty ImagesJoel Ndala joined Manchester City in 2017 and garnered plenty of buzz after a string of impressive performances for England at the U-17 World Cup in 2023.

The winger travelled with Pep Guardiola’s senior team on its preseason tour the following summer, but joined PSV Eindhoven at the end of the transfer window. The Dutch club, however, didn’t fulfill their obligation to buy, and Ndala, who struggled in PSV’s reserves for half a season, subsequently endured forgettable loan spells at Nottingham Forest, Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday.
He failed to make a single Premier League appearance during his loan spells, and even had his Wednesday loan terminated early due to disciplinary issues.
The 20-year-old joined Belgian club Cercle Brugge for an undisclosed fee in the summer.

Messi showed some love for his young compatriot. / Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesThere’s much for Argentinians to be exciting about in a post-Messi world, but it remains unclear whether the once-highly regarded Claudio Echeverri will be part of the Albiceleste’s long-term plans.
Nicknamed "El Diablito" (little devil) for his impish playmaking abilities, Echeverri grew up idolizing Messi but failed to share the field with his hero before the 39-year-old’s retirement.

Manchester City had great success converting River Plate’s Julián Alvarez into a star, and they perhaps thought that Echeverri would embark on a similar path once he wound up in Pep Guardiola’s grasp. The creative midfielder remains on City’s books, but he’s still trying to find himself on European soil.
Echeverri had rather uninspired loan spells at Bayer Leverkusen and Girona, and is spending the 2026–27 campaign with Benfica. The early signs haven’t been promising.

Juventus‘ No. 10. / MARCO BERTORELLO/AFP/Getty ImagesKenan Yıldız was already well-established when he received Messi’s endorsement. The Turkish starlet dazzled for Juventus’ Next Gen outfit and made his debut for the first team in 2023.

Yıldız was a hit right away, becoming the club’s youngest foreign goalscorer and taking the club’s venerated No. 10 shirt previously worn by the likes of Alessandro Del Piero, Roberto Baggio and Paulo Dybala.
You wouldn’t say superstardom has been acquired yet, but the sharpshooting Yıldız is well on his way.

Shaw made USWNT history in 2024. / Brad Smith/ISI Photos/USSF/Getty ImagesEmma Hayes’s snub of Jaedyn Shaw for the USWNT’s October matches garnered plenty of attention, even if the manager assured that the Gotham FC forward remains central to her plans.

ftbpro_01m4qpy12rjw.title: Champions League Predictions: Man Utd, Barcelona Face Tough Away Gigs, Arsenal at Home
ftbpro_01m4qpy12rjw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 12, 2026Barcelona made a red-hot start to this season’s Champions League—but they won’t have Raphinha available for Matchday 2.  / Judit Cartiel/Getty Images More than a month has passed since the 2026–27 Champions League got underway, with an extended international break meaning we’re easing back into the new season after a rather brief opening act.

And while players will again convene with their national teams next month, Europe’s premier club competition finds its groove over the coming weeks, as the continent’s elite vie to place themselves toward the summit in a bid to avoid two extra games in the new year.
Matchday 1 was split across three evenings, and we’re back to two sets of nine matches until the chaotic final slate of league phase fixtures.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Tuesday’s Matchday 2 games to play out.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

A dip seemed inevitable for Lens this season, given the turnover in the summer off the back of a second-place Ligue 1 finish. They’ve already parted ways with Pierre Sage’s successor, Dino Toppmöller, and are now being led by the inexperienced Yannick Cahuzac.

Cahuzac did oversee a domestic victory over Lyon at the weekend, and the French club are targeting back-to-back wins to start their league phase campaign. They’re unlikely to prevail quite as dramatically as they did on Matchday 1, when two stoppage-time goals saw Les Sang et Or overturn a 2–1 deficit at Slavia Prague.

Sporting CP are seasoned in this competition, and were quarterfinalists last time out after stunning Bodø/Glimt in the second leg of their round of 16 tie. The Primeira Liga side are unbeaten so far this term, but a habit of drawing has left them third in the league through eight games. Galatasaray were cast aside during their league phase opener.
Competition debutants Sabah had quite the welcome on Matchday 1, and they offered a pretty admirable account of themselves at Old Trafford, even in a 4–0 defeat.
Sabah will find points hard to come by during their maiden league phase campaign, but they’ll surely view this fixture as a huge opportunity to claim a first Champions League victory.

Slavia remain dominant domestically, but hardly rank among Europe’s top dogs. Their frailties, even at home, were laid bare on Matchday 1, capitulating against Lens. The visitors are facing a Sabah team that’s won seven straight on home soil, with Valdas Dambrauskas’s side likely to be buoyed by the occasion.
Arsenal saw off Napoli on Matchday 1.  / Alberto Lingria/Xinhua/Getty ImagesPrediction: Arsenal 3–1 Lille

Arsenal’s quest to complete their linear progression in this competition started with a convincing victory in Naples. On another night, the Gunners would’ve ran out emphatic winners, but a profligate showing from Mikel Arteta‘s side meant Martin Ødegaard’s second-half strike proved the difference.

While questions continue to be raised regarding the potency of Arsenal’s frontline, it’s evident that they’ve acquired a difference-maker in midfield. Bruno Guimarães was again decisive off the bench at the weekend, helping Arsenal overturn a home deficit to Leeds United.

The Brazilian will be expected to showcase his best under the bright lights on Champions League nights, and while Lille have enjoyed a strong start to their domestic campaign, the Ligue 1 side, with a 40-year-old Olivier Giroud leading their line, is unlikely to compete fiercely with the Premier League champions.

The pressure certainly didn’t ease on Michael Carrick after Saturday’s draw at home to Tottenham Hotspur. Spurs were dominant at Old Trafford against a Manchester United team bereft of energy, and were unfortunate to leave the Theatre of Dreams with just a point.
The game was there for the Red Devils after Bryan Mbuemo’s strike and Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card, but Dominic Solanke bullied Lisandro Martínez late on to head home and earn the visitors a point.
A daunting test welcomes Man Utd next, with Atlético Madrid heading into Tuesday’s bout off the back of a four-game winning run since they were beaten at Anfield on Matchday 1.
Atléti seldom lose at the Metropolitano, and the United we've seen at the start of 2026–27 doesn’t look like a team capable of producing a brave away performance garnering a victory.

Hansi Flick’s juggernaut was at it again upon their return from the extended break. There’s no one in La Liga that can compete with Barcelona right now, and Getafe were merely the last to succumb to their every whim.

ftbpro_01m4qqrn8nd4.title: Arsenal vs. Lille: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4qqrn8nd4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 12, 2026The hosts are big favorites to win in north London.  / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Arsenal’s badge), Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Lille’s badge)Arsenal return to Champions League action on Tuesday when hosting Lille in their second match of this year’s league phase.

The Gunners were humiliated in their final outing before the international break, losing 3–0 at Brighton & Hove Albion, but they responded with a hard-fought 2–1 victory over Leeds United in their first game back. Now attention turns to Europe as they seek to build on their opening round win away at Napoli last month.

Profligacy almost proved costly for Arsenal in Naples, who were ultimately indebted to Martin Ødegaard’s winning goal. They conjured 4.05 expected goals—the second-most of any team on Matchday 1—and should have departed with a scoreline far greater than 1–0.

Mikel Arteta and his players know they must be more clinical against an in-form Lille side, who currently sit second in Ligue 1 after six matches. They even lead reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain in the standings after an impressive start to the campaign—although they were beaten 3–2 by Real Betis on their Champions League return.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Arsenal overcame Napoli on Matchday 1. / Alberto Lingria/Xinhua/Getty ImagesLille shouldn’t be underestimated. They’ve hit the ground running under new manager Davide Ancelotti—son of legendary coach Carlo—and have been incredibly efficient, scoring just nine times but conceding only four in Ligue 1 thus far.
However, traveling to Arsenal will require them to reach an entirely new level.
The Gunners are particularly exceptional on home soil and have won seven of their eight competitive matches across all competitions, with defeat at Brighton an unexpected outlier.

Arteta boasts the superstar quality that Ancelotti simply doesn’t possess, while also having an immensely deep roster. The Spaniard will be able to rotate his lineup without harming its quality and that spells big trouble for Les Dogues.

Arsenal will continue without William Saliba and Christos Tzolis midweek. The former has missed the entirety of the campaign with a back problem, while the latter is absent for several weeks courtesy of a hamstring issue sustained on international duty.
Cristhian Mosquera is close to making his return, yet was missing from the matchday squad for the Leeds match. As a result, Ezri Konsa could partner Gabriel in defense yet again.

Piero Hincapié sustained an injury in the post-match warm-down after the Leeds match, which forced him to hobble off the field. He will likely sit out the upcoming game, meaning Riccardo Calafiori will feature at left back once more.
Bruno Guimarães could be promoted into the XI after his match-winner at the weekend, while Mikel Merino might enter the team to give Declan Rice another opportunity to rest.
Viktor Gyökeres and Eberechi Eze could feature in a refreshed attack.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Lille (4-2-3-1): Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Merino; Saka, Ødegaard, Eze; Gyökeres.
Ancelotti will be without several players himself for the journey to north London.

Ethan Mbappé is absent with an ankle injury suffered just before the international break, while Hamza Igamane is still unavailable due to an ACL tear. To make matters worse, Tiago Santos will sit this one out after being stretchered off against Le Havre on Saturday, while Romain Perraud also came off injured at left back.

Nathan Ngoy, traditionally a center back, could come into the team at right back to replace Santos, while the likes of Benjamin André, Ayase Ueda and Hákon Haraldsson should all re-enter the team after only being used as substitutes against Le Havre.

Former Arsenal striker Olivier Giroud could make an impact from the bench. The 40-year-old, who spent six years at the Emirates and scored 105 goals for the club, is still a major threat with his aerial prowess and finishing ability.
Lille predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Özer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Verdonk; André, Bentaleb; Bakwa, Haraldsson, Perrin; Ueda.

ftbpro_01m4qwrw13bd.title: Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Galatasaray: 10th Win in a Row in Sight
ftbpro_01m4qwrw13bd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray12:00 PM EDTRaphinha (far right) is absent but Barça still have significant firepower.  / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Barcelona can clinch their 10th consecutive victory of the 2026–27 season in the Champions League on Tuesday—but a difficult encounter awaits in the form of Turkish giants Galatasaray.

Hansi Flick’s Barça have enjoyed a perfect start to the season and can’t stop scoring goals. Eight straight La Liga wins sees them top the standings, while they were emphatic 5–1 victors over Feyenoord in their opening league phase match in the Champions League.
Even without the injured Raphinha in their ranks, Barcelona fired three unanswered goals past Getafe to extend their winning run on Saturday, but things will be decidedly tougher in Istanbul midweek.
Here’s how Barça could line up for their game.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: Joan García—The Spaniard returned from injury against Getafe and couldn’t have faced a much simpler comeback. Keeping a fifth clean sheet of the season here will be well earned.

RB: Jules Koundé—A self-confessed “drop in standards” has seen Koundé in and out of the team this season, but a morale-boosting performance against Getafe should stand the Frenchman in good stead moving forwards.

CB: Pau Cubarsí—After a busy international window with Spain, Golden Boy favorite Cubarsí was offered a well-earned rest at the weekend. The youngster might be worked hard in Türkiye, however, with Victor Osimhen recently returning from injury.

CB: Gerard Martín—Another injury setback for Andreas Christensen opens the door for Martín to make his 101st Barça appearance at RAMS Park. The repurposed left back has already earned plenty of minutes this season.

LB: João Cancelo—Another match, another terrific showing from Xavi Espart at the weekend. But it could be Cancelo who starts at left back in a hostile environment, with his vast experience coming in handy against his former Manchester City and Bayern Munich teammate Leroy Sané.
CM: Rodri—Rodri is made for matches like these. Among the deafening whistles and jeers of the home crowd, the World Cup winner will keep a cool head and organize proceedings from the midfield.
CM: Pedri—Like compatriot Cubarsí, the midfielder should make his comeback to the XI against Galatasaray. Flick will need as many classy, unflappable technicians as possible on a difficult away day.

RW: Lamine Yamal—After scoring in nine matches on the spin for club and country, Yamal has now blanked in his last two outings. Unfortunately for Galatasaray, he seldom goes three games without finding the net.

AM: Dani Olmo—Olmo has still not scored this season for Barça or Spain, but assists have not been in short supply. The former RB Leipzig playmaker’s delivered five across his last nine matches in all competitions.
LW: Anthony Gordon—After a blistering start for La Blaugrana, the Englishman finally opened his Barça goal account with a fortuitous strike against Getafe. Expect more to follow.

ST: Gabriel Jesus—Raphinha will sit this match out as he recovers from a thigh injury, meaning Jesus will start for the second successive game. Despite having played just 119 minutes this season, he already has three goals for his new employers.

ftbpro_01m4qx69dwbt.title: Atletico Madrid vs. Man Utd: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4qx69dwbt.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 12, 2026Atlético and Manchester United are in contrasting form heading into the game.  / Alex Caparros/UEFA/Getty Images (Atlético’s badge), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Man Utd’s badge) Manchester United’s Champions League league phase campaign restarts with a tough test away at Atlético Madrid.

Michael Carrick inspired the Red Devils back into Europe’s premier club competition after his appointment as interim manager in January, but the now-full-time boss hasn’t enjoyed the added challenges at the start of the 2026–27 campaign.

United were deservedly pegged back by the 10 men of Tottenham Hotspur at the weekend, extending their winless run in domestic competitions to four matches. Carrick’s side are currently plagued by distinct issues without possession, and while running statistics aren’t the be-all and end-all, United are unlikely to win many matches playing with the intensity they’ve offered in recent outings.
A switch of environment could benefit the under-fire Red Devils, even if few enjoy their trips to the Metropolitano.

Atlético enter this bout having won each of their previous four games, and one of their notable summer arrivals, Cristian Romero, was the match-winner at the weekend. Romero’s 88th-minute goal fired Atléti past Alavés on Saturday, keeping Diego Simeone’s side above cross-city rivals Real Madrid in the La Liga table.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Carrick is feeling the heat. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesMan Utd at least got their Champions League campaign up and running on their first attempt, easing past debutants Sabah 4–0. Atlético Madrid, meanwhile, were beaten 2–1 at Anfield.

While United have appeared ever so easy to play against on either side of the extended break, this competition may suit Carrick’s side. On Tuesday, there will be less onus on Carrick’s side to assert control, and they’ll be happy to play on the counterattack, even in Benjamin Šeško’s absence.

Ultimately, United have generally been most successful over the past decade when they’ve played a transitional game. Thus, the opening goal feels crucial in the Spanish capital, given Atléti’s own counterattacking threat.

You never quite know what you’re going to get from Simeone’s side nowadays, but the Argentine will hope that the summer arrival of Romero and continued development of Marc Pubill will help shore up a defense that was leaky last season.
/    Simeone is set to have a full cohort of players available for Man Utd‘s visit. The Argentine must thus decided upon the correct configuration.

They’ve switched between a back three and four at the start of the new season, with a 4-2-3-1 installed against Alavés at the weekend. That could be retained here, with Álex Baena operating behind Alvarez as the No. 10.

Simeone has Alexander Sørloth to call upon in reserve, as well as Jonathan David, if Alvarez’s quiet start to the campaign continues. Kang-in Lee and Ademola Lookman offer dynamic threats out wide, and Koke is still going strong in midfield alongside the excellent Pablo Barrios.
Romero was sent off on his previous encounter against the Red Devils earlier this year, and he’ll lead Atléti’s improved defense on Tuesday.
Atlético Madrid predicted lineup vs. Man Utd (4-2-3-1): Oblak; Llorente, Romero, Pubill, Hancko; Koke, Barrios; Lee, Baena, Lookman; Alvarez.
Man Utd have been dealt a couple of fresh injury blows heading into Tuesday’s league phase clash.

Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo didn’t train with the rest of the team on Monday, throwing their availability for the match into doubt. As it stands, it seems unlikely for either to feature, given the quick turnaround and their respective injury histories. Mainoo, of course, withdrew from Thomas Tuchel’s England roster due to a fitness concern.

Carrick will have to reshuffle his defense as a result of poor depth at left back in Shaw’s absence. Diogo Dalot could come across to the opposite flank, allowing Leny Yoro to keep his place at right back.

Carlos Baleba is almost assured of a first Man Utd start after impressing off the bench against Spurs on his debut. Youri Tielemans may partner his fellow new arrival, despite his struggles at the weekend.
The visitors are also still without Patrick Dorgu, Benjamin Šeško and Noussair Mazraoui.

ftbpro_01m4qxtd4d91.title: Ranking All 20 Premier League Teams’ Performances on Matchday 6
ftbpro_01m4qxtd4d91.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 12, 2026Bruno Fernandes (left), Florian Wirtz (center) and Erling Haaland all had differing weekends. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Fernandes, Wirtz), Michael Regan/Getty Images (Haaland)In this post-verdict world, Premier League points no longer have the same heft to them.

Manchester City currently lead the division with a faultless record from the first six games of the season, but what good will that do them if the independent commission dolls out a swingeing points deduction?

The tangible reward for City’s second-half romp through a crumbling Liverpool could soon be erased, but the quality of their performance, that strike from Erling Haaland, the ingenuity of Rayan Cherki, is crystallized in the moment.
On these shifting sands, everyone has to hold onto the few certainties there are.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

It wasn’t a good day for Sunderland. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesAny team stripped of their top scorer and talismanic defender is going to suffer but Régis Le Bris was rightly concerned by Sunderland’s distinct lack of “quality or composure” in possession. The Black Cats had 62% of the ball against a team so used to being the protagonist but came up short of ideas without Brian Brobbey to look for.

Marco Rose needs a win. / Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesBournemouth have played better than their meager points total of three, but they were never in danger of earning that elusive first win under Marco Rose at Stamford Bridge.“The last games we had some good performances,” the incoming manager admitted, “but today we struggled.”
If this was a clip from the Bundesliga it'd have 50k likes. pic.twitter.com/23QX4zKhlM

Manchester United have so many problems that people can get bogged down by the irrelevant ones.Rather than running statistics, Michael Carrick would be wise to dwell on how his collection of players (or strangers?) can look so woefully exposed against a Tottenham Hotspur side that started the game in 20th. Old Trafford has been a far more forgiving atmosphere than most grounds throughout the club’s 13 years of angst since Sir Alex Ferguson but even match-going fans are starting to lose their patience. Carrick has no defense, in a metaphorical or literal sense. “I understand the disappointment,” he shrugged, “the reality is what it is.”

The walls are closing in on Álvaro Arbeloa. / Justin Setterfield/Getty Images“Maybe you don’t know me,” an increasingly prickly Álvaro Arbeloa put it to a journalist this weekend, “but I played for the best team in world. I have coached the best team in the world. Maybe you don’t know, but just to let you know, that pressure is part of my life since I was a kid.”The former Real Madrid player and manager (for all of four months) is being subjected to a torrent of deserved pressure after another listless display and more dropped points.

Monday’s win offered Matthias Jaissle plenty of food for thought. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesAnother Monday night and another 4–1 thumping. Matthias Jaissle could be forgiven for channeling The Boomtown Rats but Newcastle’s hefty reverse against Coventry City was nowhere near as damning as their implosion at the hands of Leeds United in September.For large swathes of the weeknight clash, the Magpies had Coventry City on the ropes, creating a glut of chances they found creative ways to spurn. “The result is not what happened in the game,” Nico González fairly claimed. Yet, the backdoor was constantly left open during Newcastle’s attacking raids and the newly promoted hosts were in ruthless mood.

Liverpool collapsed after Ryan Gravenberch’s red card. / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesPutting aside the mental gymnastics of what this result means in the grand context of the Premier League’s existence, this was an excellent game decided by the referee—as Andoni Iraola has been at pains to point out. For all Liverpool’s promise across that opening hour of numerical parity, the extent to which the Reds collapsed after Ryan Gravenberch’s dismissal cannot get lost in the fog of another refereeing controversy. Liverpool may have only had 10 players but they still collectively completed fewer passes than Cherki managed on his own across those final 30 minutes.
Another day at the office for Walter 😅 pic.twitter.com/LbP6mXgI2Z

Despite getting royally outplayed by their visitors, Crystal Palace’s players were still given a reward by the forgiving Pierre Sage. Sunday’s win ensured that they could have Monday off, sparking very loud festivities bursting out the locker room. Considering the roster were initially facing just a single rest day throughout the entirety of a busy October, some celebration is understandable—even if it wasn’t deserved.
https://t.co/IrHjItUkMl pic.twitter.com/egGdiN5hTx

One of the old clichés that David Moyes has fallen upon one or two times during his 1,202 matches of management is the need for a team to be at their best in both boxes. Well, Everton were guilty of two defensive blunders while Thierno Barry missed even more chances in the attacking penalty area. Against that backdrop, it’s impressive the Toffees were able to emerge with any points.
Some finish from Mo! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/RDHkGJ08Hr

Hull haven’t been declawed just yet. The Tigers have bolstered an unexpectedly bright start in the Premier League’s glamor ties with the kind of dogged battles for points which could be enough to evade a relegation the vast majority had predicted.Sergej Jakirović captured the mood of one point well earned on Sunday when he concluded: “Congratulations to both teams.”
Come for the goal, stay for John McGinn’s celebration 😅 pic.twitter.com/X8vYwvnaLf

Things are tentatively crawling in the right direction for Aston Villa, even if the sort of form which propelled them to fourth place last season is still some way off. As Unai Emery tellingly admitted: “We need to build the team.” Some vague semblance of structure looked a little clearer on Saturday.

ftbpro_01m4r030ykae.title: Galatasaray vs. Barcelona: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4r030ykae.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 12, 2026Barça are unbeaten in six matches against Galatasaray this century / Instagram/galatasaray (Galatasaray), Alex Caparros - UEFA/Getty Images (Barcelona)Barcelona’s perfect start to the season comes under threat this Tuesday when they visit Galatasaray in the Champions League.

La Blaugrana have been flawless during their eight-match winning streak in La Liga, destroying every opponent in their path with ease. Their sole European test of the term didn’t prove any more challenging, either, with their 5–1 demolition of Feyenoord propeling them to third in the league phase table.

Having been utterly irresistible going forward, even the odd lapse in concentration at the back has proved immaterial. Hansi Flick’s side is operating at the peak of its powers and will be favorite to clinch another victory in an inhospitable environment midweek.

RAMS Park in Istanbul is always a fierce arena to adapt to for visiting teams, and Galatasaray enter the upcoming duel with Barça as table-toppers in the Süper Lig. While they were defeated by Sporting CP in their Champions League opener, they have won five of seven domestic matches and remain unbeaten on home soil since April.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Barça have been unstoppable this season. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesBarcelona’s trip to “Hell” on Tuesday will not be without its challenges. Gala are mightily impressive at home—beating Liverpool (twice) and Juventus on their own patch last season—and could welcome Victor Osimhen back into their forward line following their talisman’s recent injury return.

The Catalan giants have been in absolutely devastating form this season and have already scored 39 times across just nine games—an average of 4.3 per outing. Their midfield has been further bolstered by the grace and guile of Rodri, while an aggressive defensive line can prove difficult to penetrate when functioning properly.
Okan Buruk’s side will need a miracle to avoid defeat and might simply be content in escaping with their dignity—and goal difference—intact.

Osimhen made his first appearance since the beginning of September when coming off the bench in last Friday’s 3–1 win over Kasımpaşa and he’s in line to re-enter the starting XI for such a seismic clash.
Leroy Sané should come into the team on the right wing, too, joining Rafael Leão and Osimhen in a fearsome forward trio.

Mario Lemina should also return to the midfield, featuring alongside Gabriel Sara and Lucas Torreira. The latter was sent off against Kasımpaşa but his suspension will only be served in domestic competitions.
Wilfried Singo is a major doubt to feature having been sidelined since the end of August.
Galatasaray predicted lineup vs. Barcelona (4-3-3): Çakir; Sallai, Sánchez, Bardakcı, Jakobs; Lemina, Torreira, Sara; Sané, Osimhen, Leão.

Barcelona will continue without long-term absentee Roony Bardghji and while Frenkie de Jong is close to returning in midfield, Flick has insisted he’s most likely to make his comeback against Real Betis at the weekend.
Raphinha has been ruled out of the match, meaning Gabriel Jesus will lead the line once again, while Andreas Christensen is back in the treatment room to further limit Flick’s center back options.
Pau Cubarsí and Pedri should return to the starting lineup after being benched for the victory over Getafe, but the fabulous front four should stay exactly the same.
João Cancelo will compete with the impressive young Xavi Espart for a start at left back, while a similar battle could play out between Eric García and Jules Koundé at right back.
Barcelona predicted lineup vs. Galatasaray (4-2-3-1): J. García; Koundé, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, Olmo, Gordon; Jesus.

ftbpro_01m4r4mxyf49.title: MLS Goals of the Week: Vintage Lionel Messi, Carlo Holse Heroics
ftbpro_01m4r4mxyf49.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely12:51 PM EDTLionel Messi (left) gave a vintage performance. / Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Lionel Messi); Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Carlo Holse)Matchday 29 saw the 2026 MLS season back in full swing as international stars returned to the fold.

There was no shortage of excitement over the weekend, with the Vancouver Whitecaps becoming the first Western Conference team to clinch a playoffs spot and a whole host of comeback victories as Decision Day looms.
Lionel Messi continued his attacking dominance, scoring a brace on Saturday to lift Inter Miami to a dominant 4–0 victory. His latter finish was a vintage, must-see Messi effort.

Meanwhile, St. Louis City’s Carlo Holse had a dazzling performance on Sunday. The winger scored three goals in the span of just 21 minutes, the second-fastest hat trick in MLS history. Thanks to Holse, St. Louis thumped LA Galaxy 6–2 with a whopping five goals in the first half alone. The team is now on a 20-match unbeaten streak, tying the league record.
Here are the top five goals from the weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
CARLO HOLSE BAGS HAT TRICK 21 MINUTES INTO THE GAME! 🤯🎩@stlCITYsc fans erupt at Energizer Park. pic.twitter.com/KSZvy9JutX
After scoring in the second and seventh minutes of the game, Holse solidified his hat trick just 14 minutes later.

The 27-year-old attacker settled a launched ball with his chest, before outmuscling Galaxy defender Justin Haak to get the shot off. It signified Holse’s most emphatic display in MLS, and after transfrering to the league in mid-August, he is now up to six goals.
END TO END FOR @OrlandoCitySC and they've surely won it! 🫨Maxime Crépeau save ➡️ Iván Angulo's finish at the end of a beautifully-worked play! pic.twitter.com/FNxTM4YJ4I
The Columbus Crew thought it was about to take a last-gasp lead in the 88th minute, yet just 15 seconds later, Orlando City had reversed fate.

Making the most of Orlando City goalkeeper Maxime Crépeau’s save, the Lions quickly regained possession and sprinted up the pitch into the final third. A quick give-and-go with Martín Ojeda set up  Iván Angulo beautifully in front of the goal mouth for a first-time finish. Orlando walked away with the 3–2 win, leaving the Crew shaking their heads in disbelief.
Kelvin Yeboah gets his 15th of the season!Big response from the Loons to start the second half. 💪📺 Apple TV: https://t.co/4PjpANnTy3 pic.twitter.com/QnmX7hrEjp

It was a willful goal from Minnesota United’s Kelvin Yeboah, who slid into the back post to meet a launched ball from teammate Morris Duggan. His highlight-reel finish equalized the match early in the second half. Another goal from each side would mean the game remained level by the final whistle.
Minnesota will have wanted the win, but it will take the integral point, its first in six games. Yeboah is now up to 15 goals this season.
Messi magic 🪄Two goals for the World Cup Champion. pic.twitter.com/PMA1l5tyZk
In his first outing since his tearful international retirement ceremony with Argentina last week, Messi proved, once again, that he is far from retirement form.

Messi scored twice against DC United, the latter of which saw him skirt three players at the top of the box with his savvy dribbling skill. The emphatic victory was a much-needed confidence boost as it was Inter Miami’s first league win since August.
The Argentine legend is now up to 23 goals this season, increasing his distance in the lead of the thrilling Golden Boot race. FC Dallas’s Petar Musa has the second-most goals with 19.
"Zlatan Ibrahimovic-like finish!" 👀Brandon Vázquez halves the deficit and gets some momentum going for @AustinFC! 💪 pic.twitter.com/lo6OpLn2qr

ftbpro_01m4r67fbe8j.subtitle: SI

ftbpro_01m4r7aztp1h.title: ‘Never’—Iraola Promises to Keep Vendetta for Entire Season After Man City Loss
ftbpro_01m4r7aztp1h.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray1:00 PM EDTAndoni Iraola was livid with Chris Kavanagh after the fulltime whistle. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesAndoni Iraola fumed over Ryan Gravenberch’s costly red card following Liverpool’s 3–0 Premier League defeat to Manchester City, insisting referee Chris Kavanagh gave out several cheap yellow cards. The bitter Basque boss promised to make sure that this low bar was maintained throughout the remainder of the season.

Sunday’s encounter at Anfield was finely-poised at the hour mark as the match remained goalless, but when Gravenberch was shown a second yellow card for a cynical foul on Jérémy Doku, the game completely swung in City’s favor.
Liverpool conceded three goals in the space of 13 minutes as they crumbled with a numerical disadvantage, but Iraola believes Gravenberch’s first booking of the match was extremely harsh.

“I think the first foul of Ryan is never a yellow card, never,” said the Spaniard. “These kinds of games, just a stomp on the big toe, or something minor. He doesn’t even call the foul straight away. He lets bit go, I think Elliot Anderson does a couple of steps. He decides to go down. I don’t know why after he shows the yellow card, because it’s not a situation where it leaves advantage.

“We had nine players behind the ball. It’s like they had a lot of, you know, it was in the middle of the pitch, no danger there. And then you put, as a referee, yourself in trouble, and also you put us in trouble.”

Iraola’s frustrations weren’t limited to that one decision, either. He added: “Also, at the beginning of the game, yellow card of Ronald [Araújo], I know he complains, he does this. But in these kinds of games, if you are going to start after a handball of [Marc] Guéhi, the punishment is for Ronald complaining.

“You put it straight away at the beginning of the game, the right back with a yellow card. I think you are in the textbooks, yes, perfect. He complains, you can show a yellow card, but then I will be very careful all the season. Every time someone complains, it has to be a yellow card.”

Liverpool players were vexed by the decision. / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesGravenberch can have few complaints about his second booking at Anfield. After hauling down the turbo-charged Doku in the 62nd minute as the winger raced free toward the Liverpool half, it was a textbook yellow card.
Regardless of whether the first yellow was merited, Gravenberch’s decision to foul Doku remains inexcusable.
However, the Dutchman certainly has a right to feel aggrieved about the first caution.

Gravenberch was booked for standing on the toe of Anderson in the 47th minute in the center of the field, despite the fact that contact was incredibly minimal and he actually attempted to pull out of the challenge.
Anderson took several steps before falling to the turf, where he proceeded to clutch his knee, and it was nothing more than an innocuous foul one witnesses dozens of times a match.
When speaking with Sky Sports, former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher disagreed with Kavanagh’s decision to book Gravenberch for his first offense.
“I think it’s really harsh,” said Gallagher. “I think the problem for Chris, in his view, I think he thinks that he clips his knee, but he doesn’t. If you look again, he clips his foot.

“I think from Chris’s position, he thinks he’s clipped his knee, so he thinks it’s a high boot and a yellow card. But on reflection, you see the replay, he catches the top of boot. So he’s very unlucky.”

ftbpro_01m4r85p3c69.title: NFL Kicker Cam Little Gives Ode to Jude Bellingham After Wild Winning Moment in London
ftbpro_01m4r85p3c69.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:30 PM EDTCam Little was Jacksonville’s hero in London. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesThe Jacksonville Jaguars pulled off a stunning last-gasp win over the Philadelphia Eagles in London, courtesy of Cam Little’s 57-yard field goal with no time left on the clock.

A back-and-forth game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium was seemingly won by the depleted Eagles when kicker Jake Elliott nailed a 48-yard field goal to give the two-time Super Bowl champions a 17–16 lead with just eight seconds remaining.

However, Ameer Abdullah gained 53 yards from the subsequent kickoff to set up Little’s winning kick. Little knew it was good from the moment he struck it, immediately discarding his helmet and running off in celebration.

The ice-cold sequence prompted a nod to the English-hosted occasion, as Little encouraged his on-rushing teammates to give him a moment to pose in front of the Philly-dominated north stand. He put his arms out wide, imitating Jude Bellingham’s iconic goal celebration.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Cam Little 🤝 Jude BellinghamThe Jaguars kicker HAD to pull out the Real Madrid and England star's iconic celebration! pic.twitter.com/vRzubs0pKf

Manchester United supporter Little joked after his heroics that his clutch kick was the unofficial winner for the Red Devils after they’d surrendered two points to a 10-man Spurs in stoppage time on Saturday evening.

The 23-year-old, a sixth-round draft pick in his third year in the league, holds the record for the longest-successful field goal in NFL history (68 yards), which he set last November. Still, he ranked Sunday’s kick as the greatest moment of his career to date.

“A hundred percent. Like, the record was cool and all, but it still gives me goosebumps because I don’t think you guys realize I wake up every Saturday morning watching the Premier League, every Saturday, and then to play soccer from ages five to 16—I didn’t touch a football until I was almost 17. So my whole life was soccer up to that point,” Little said post-game.
“To do it in the stadium, it feels like I’ve achieved my dream of playing professional soccer, even though I’m playing pro football.”
UNBELIEVABLE. JAGS WIN. WHAT JUST HAPPENED?!?! pic.twitter.com/O7x8JTgPeK
It was the first game-winner in regular time of Little’s already-stellar career, and he admitted to reporters that he didn’t quite know how to celebrate if his kick was good.

Baltimore Ravens kicker Tyler Loop hit Cristiano Ronaldo’s “Siuuu” celebration after his winning moment against the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil on Sept. 27, and earlier in the day, Little’s teammate, Parker Washington, paid homage to Wayne Rooney’s mock boxing punch and Cole Palmer’s “cold” celebration after scoring a pair of touchdowns.

Little stuck with the English theme by doing “the Bellingham,” and the Jaguars kicker was keen to make sure that everyone was aware of it: “Hey, I know you all saw the Bellingham celebration back there, too!” he shouted as media congregated on the field.
The 23-year-old’s ode was recognized by the man himself, who commented “Clutch Cam!” with a salute emoji on an Instagram post showing off Little’s work.

Iconic. / Richard Pelham/Getty ImagesThere really isn’t that much to it, and Bellingham himself has previously admitted the celebration has no specific inspiration or meaning. “The truth is that I don't know exactly where it comes from,” he told RMTV in 2023. “I started doing it in Birmingham, and from there I have continued it, but there is no reason.”
As he stands there, in front of adoring or hostile supporters in all his glory, perfectly still with his arms outstretched, Bellingham emanates a distinct sense of self-assurance.

The Real Madrid and England midfielder is one of the world’s best, and he reinforced that notion on the biggest stage in the summer, inspiring the Three Lions to their best World Cup performance since 1966. Bellingham scored seven times on North American soil as England finished third.

ftbpro_01m4rb5pb0fw.title: Barcelona Edge Toward Matching Extraordinary 58-Year Real Madrid Record
ftbpro_01m4rb5pb0fw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTBarcelona have been unstoppable at the start of the season. / Lluis GENE/AFP/Getty ImagesBarcelona can make history by matching a 58-year-old La Liga record held by Real Madrid when they play their next domestic match this coming Saturday.

La Blaugrana have made an utterly astonishing start to the season after winning all nine of their competitive fixtures. Eight of those triumphs have come in La Liga, with a 5–1 destruction of Feyenoord in the Champions League sandwiched in between some mightily impressive victories.

The Catalans matched their own club record for most wins at the start of a La Liga season by beating Getafe 3–0 last weekend, with their eighth consecutive victory equaling the success enjoyed at the beginning of the 2013–14 season under Tata Martino—although it was actually Atlético Madrid who won the title that season.
However, if Barça can beat Real Betis on the road in their next league outing on Oct. 17, they will become only the second side to win their first nine La Liga matches in a campaign.

Real Madrid are the only club to have previously achieved the feat, doing so back in the 1968–69 season. Their ninth win came in El Clásico before a goalless draw with Pontevedra ended the victorious streak.

Los Blancos went on to be champions that season, nearly going the entire year unbeaten. Only Elche were able to topple them en route to the crown.

Barça, who are currently five points clear at the summit, will be eying the all-time record if they beat Betis, and, rather poetically, they could make it 10 La Liga wins on the spin against Real Madrid when the sides meet on Oct. 25.

Barça won their last trip to Betis. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesBefore grand dreams of a record-breaking win in El Clásico, Barça must first overcome Betis at the Estadio La Cartuja—and former Real Madrid manager Manuel Pellegrini has them in terrific form.

Currently third in the standings and only five points off Barça, the Andalusians have managed six victories from their first eight league matches, as well as a win over Lille on their long-awaited Champions League return last month.
Winning in Seville won’t prove straightforward for Flick and his players, especially given they must first overcome an awkward away day at Galatasaray this Tuesday.

However, Barça can take belief from their hugely impressive record against Betis in recent times. In fact, they have won 14 of their last 17 games against them in all competitions and both meetings last season—including a chaotic 5–3 win away from home.
Their record at La Cartuja is pretty impressive, too, with their 2–2 draw at the venue in 2024–25 the only occasion they have failed to win there over the past 10 visits.
Given Barça’s current form, even a confident Betis side shouldn’t block their path to history.

ftbpro_01m4rshgrhkd.title: ‘Love It’—How Lionel Messi Could Complete Trophy Set at Inter Miami
ftbpro_01m4rshgrhkd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely5:15 PM EDTLionel Messi could have a new trophy in his future. / Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesWhen you’ve won every trophy in sight, there’s only one solution: Expand your view.

That could be the fate of soccer legend Lionel Messi, who has won 48 official trophies across his 20+ years of play for both club and country. He has only gone trophy-less in two seasons (2013–14, 2019–20) since he began his professional career in 2004.

Since joining his current team Inter Miami in 2023, Messi has won the Leagues Cup (2023), MLS Supporters’ Shield (2024), MLS Cup (2025) and the Campeones Cup (2026). The Herons have only failed to win the Concacaf Champions Cup, reaching as far as the semifinals in 2025.
In short, Messi needs more hardware to fight for, and a big opportunity may present itself to Inter Miami soon enough: the Copa Libertadores.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

The South American competition may be on the horizon. / CHANDAN KHANNA/AFP/Getty ImagesTraditionally a competition between South America’s most premier soccer clubs, Conmebol chief Alejandro Dominguez has flirted with opening up the tournament to MLS teams—specifically Inter Miami—sometime in the future, pending an agreement with Concacaf. “The door is open to them,” Dominguez said in January, after Miami owner Jorge Mas publicly expressed his “dream” of competing in the tournament.
While no MLS team has ever featured in the Libertadores, two Liga MX teams participated each year between 1998 and 2016. Due to scheduling clashes, the agreement was brought to an end after 18 years.

“It has been done in the past, but we are very respectful of the other confederations, Dominguez added back in January. “But yes, it is an honor that teams from other confederations have the Libertadores as a reference for international and world competition.”

Dominguez resurfaced the conversation just last week, though. He teased Messi about the possibility of competing in Copa Libertadores during the forward’s farewell match for Argentina in Buenos Aires. It is an idea current Miami manager Kily González is fully in favor of and one Messi is “excited” about himself.

Kily Gonzalez is Miami’s new manager. / Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images“My understanding is that we’ve been exploring this possibility for years now,” González said on Friday. “Obviously, we'd love it because it would be amazing; plus ... it's one of the few trophies Leo is missing, so I think that really got him excited too. We'll see, the decision-making process is a bit of a formality at this point, but we're ready for anything, and he certainly is.”

Gonzalez emphasized Messi’s desire to fight for trophies, adding: “I see [Messi] every day, and the level he demands is incredible; he pushes us to give our all. He even gets angry when a play doesn't come off right. He demands so much of us that none of us can afford to slack off. It constantly challenges us to improve, as a club, as a staff, as a coaching team, and as colleagues.”

Messi is currently under a three-year contract extension with Miami that expires at the end of the 2028 season, after which he may opt to retire. The 39-year-old has already retired internationally and has hinted that he does not have much longer at the club level. Therefore, Conmebol must act swiftly if it seeks to reach an agreement with both Concacaf and FIFA to have Messi and his teammates compete in the annual tournament.
The Concacaf Champions Cup is also annual, meaning the clock has not run out for Messi to win that competition too.

ftbpro_01m4t7rs314a.title: Champions League Predictions: Man City Host PSG, Liverpool & Real Madrid on the Road
ftbpro_01m4t7rs314a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 13, 2026Holders Paris Saint-Germain got off to a fast start on Matchday 1.  / Aurelien Meunier/PSG/Getty Images Matchday 2 of the Champions League league phase got underway on Tuesday with some engrossing matchups—and Wednesday delivers yet more drama.

The headline fixture undoubtedly occurs at the Etihad Stadium in one of seven later kickoffs, with Manchester City playing host to reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain in a battle of petrostate-owned powerhouses.
But there are an array of intriguing duels elsewhere, too, with Borussia Dortmund, Liverpool and Real Madrid all looking to prosper during uncomfortable away days.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Wednesday’s Matchday 2 fixtures will pan out.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Como made their Champions League debut in style during last month’s opening round. Cesc Fàbregas’s high-flyers thrashed RB Leipzig 4–1 to ignite their maiden campaign as the likes of Nico Paz and Martin Baturina shone.

This time they’re on the road, however, journeying to Rotterdam to face Eredivisie leaders Feyenoord. The Dutch giants are unbeaten from their eight domestic matches this season, clinching six wins en route to top spot. Their 5–1 defeat to Barcelona in the Champions League only briefly bruised their ego.

The clash at De Kuip will be fiercely competitive as both sides eye three crucial points in the hunt for a knockout berth, but Como’s superior attacking quality should give them the edge in a battle of fine margins.
Liverpool opened their Champions League campaign with victory. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesPrediction: LASK 0–2 Liverpool

Liverpool endured a humbling return from the international break on Sunday. Despite missing key players through injury, Andoni Iraola’s men fought valiantly against Manchester City for the first hour at Anfield, only for a red card to result in their implosion and, ultimately, a 3–0 loss.

LASK, who the Reds beat home and away during the 2023–24 Europa League group stage, should provide a simpler test of their credentials, though. They’re an ideal opponent to help Liverpool regain some belief and return to winning ways.

The Austrians are winless in their last four matches, including their 1–0 loss to AEK Athens in their European opener. They’re currently third in the Austrian top flight and shouldn’t realistically cause Liverpool any major problems.

After a chaotic summer in which they were stripped of their best players, Aston Villa are beginning to find some consistency. While they were unable to get over the line during their 2–2 draw with Brentford at the weekend, they have won three of their last five matches and started to find the net routinely.
Club Brugge were the victims of Villa’s attacking resurgence during the first round of league phase matches, with Unai Emery’s men firing three past the Belgians en route to a frenetic victory.

Fenerbahçe will cause problems. They have a host of aging stars in their roster, including Ederson, Nathan Aké, N’Golo Kanté, Romelu Lukaku and former Villa loanee Marco Asensio. But the hosts should have enough in the tank to power to victory.
Prediction: Bodø/Glimt 2–2 Borussia Dortmund

Trips to the Arctic Circle have proven extremely tough for Europe’s giants since Bodø/Glimt’s Champions League arrival. Man City, Atlético Madrid, Inter Milan and Sporting CP were all beaten at Aspmyra Stadion last season.

Borussia Dortmund must be wary as they continue their yellow-themed European campaign—BVB beat Villarreal 3–2 in their league phase opener—even if Bodø were smashed 5–0 by their Klassiker rivals Bayern Munich on Matchday 1.

Dortmund are unbeaten since their Supercup defeat to Bayern and won’t expect to lose in Norway. But they might be forced to accept a point in a difficult environment, repeating the 2–2 scoreline from the only other meeting between the sides last term.
Man City’s guilty verdict didn’t affect them at the weekend. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesPrediction: Man City 1–1 PSG

ftbpro_01m4tczjravh.title: Premier League Clubs ‘Discuss’ Immediate Man City Expulsion Before Appeal Verdict
ftbpro_01m4tczjravh.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:00 AM EDTEnzo Maresca’s team are dominating the headines for all the wrong reasons. / Isaac Parkin/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesThose hoping to see Manchester City begin to suffer the impact of their guilty verdict were left bitterly disappointed this weekend when Enzo Maresca’s side roared to victory over Liverpool.

Many have been left wondering whether there is even any point to going ahead with a season that is being played out amid perhaps the biggest controversy the Premier League has ever seen. Having been found guilty of a significant number of financial rule breaches between 2009 and 2018, City are potentially facing a seismic punishment that could alter the landscape of the English game as we know it.

As it stands, no punishment has been handed out, with City appealing the verdict and repeatedly proclaiming confidence that their innocence will soon be proven. It has left the Premier League in limbo, but teams do actually have the power to force through the harshest of punishments—expulsion from the division.

Per Rule B6 of the Premier League’s regulations: “The League may expel a Club from membership upon a special Resolution to that effect being passed by a majority of not less than three-quarters of such members as (being entitled to do so) vote by their representatives or by proxy at a General Meeting of which notice specifying the intention to propose the Resolution has been duly given.”

Simply put, that means a total of 15 clubs could come together and vote to kick City out of the competition immediately. According to The Independent, such conversations have already been held among a number of club executives.

“This is a farce that will lead to protest, damage to the integrity and reputation of the competition, and possibly even violence,” one is quoted as saying. “The board has a duty at law to its shareholders to protect, enhance and promote the interests of the Premier League.”

A dark cloud hangs over Man City. / Isaac Parkin/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesBy the letter of the Premier League’s law, it is possible that City could be kicked out of the Premier League if enough clubs believe it would be in the competition’s best interests. After all, that is exactly why the rule exists.
That being said, it is recognized that such a push would almost certainly fail in the current circumstances.

While City await the outcome of their appeal, it is expected that any legal challenge of a hypothetical expulsion would be successful, which would only increase the uncertainty and the tension surrounding the current situation.

Executives are, however, continuing to push for immediate action against City, with many believing the season cannot be allowed to continue on its current trajectory.

The deadline for a final verdict on City’s appeal is Jan. 23, 2027. Given the extended length of the initial case, there is every reason to believe things will take right up until the final second of that window.

That date is currently marked for an away trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on what would be the 22nd match of City’s Premier League season, one week before title rivals Arsenal are due to visit the Etihad.

ftbpro_01m4teyknhsf.title: ‘People Don’t Realise’—The Impossible Fernandes Injury Conundrum Facing Carrick
ftbpro_01m4teyknhsf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:30 AM EDTMichael Carrick is facing the impossible conundrum. / James Gill - Danehouse/Getty ImagesBruno Fernandes continues to play through an injury first revealed on international duty, according to Manchester United manager Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s dazzling interim spell was largely built around Fernandes, who racked up 13 of his record-setting 21 assists under his guidance to drag United from mid-table obscurity all the way back to the Champions League.

That form has not continued this season. Fernandes has not contributed to a goal in five of United’s six Premier League matches so far, with a hat trick and assist in the 5–2 win over Ipswich Town doing a lot of heavy lifting in the stats column.
Portugal manager Jorge Jesus revealed during the international break that Fernandes had been playing through a “complicated” injury, potentially explaining his struggles since the World Cup.
“People maybe don’t realize it, but it happens a lot,” Carrick confessed after Fernandes failed to light up Saturday’s 1–1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur. “Players play with issues.
“I probably played 80% of my games with some sort of issue. It’s not ideal but it’s kind of manageable.”
As it turns out, “managing” that issue is proving to be somewhat impossible for Carrick.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Bruno Fernandes has fallen well below expectations this season. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesThere is a pretty easy way to guide Fernandes through this injury. A spell on the sidelines would do him wonders.

Fernandes’s injury is evidently not particularly serious, so a few weeks of rest would likely set him up for a return to his physical peak. The problem for Carrick is that if Fernandes does not play for United for a few weeks, there is no guarantee he would still be the manager when he returns.

The Portugal international is United’s best player and, with all due respect to the rest of United’s stars, that is hardly a tough debate. You need your best players to drag you out of the sort of rut in which the Red Devils currently find themselves, so leaving Fernandes out of the matchday squad when it is not medically necessary to do so would be a hugely controversial decision—the sort of thing that could cost a manager their job.

Carrick’s faith in Fernandes is already clear. He has played every minute in the Premier League so far this season and even got 90 minutes in the Champions League victory over Sabah, despite the fact the game was won by half time.

The only match this season in which Fernandes did not start was the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion, in which Carrick turned to his captain off the bench in a desperate attempt to salvage something from a game that had already proven the perils of trying to go without the team’s talisman.

If Carrick rests Fernandes for the next two weeks, he would miss a total of five matches: two Champions League games against Atlético Madrid and Como, as well as Premier League outings against Leeds United, Bournemouth and Chelsea.

Those are all, given the circumstances, must-win games for Carrick, who knows the need to keep turning to Fernandes. The Portugal international will hardly be kicking up a fuss against his continuation in the lineup, clearly the sort of player ready to give his all for the club he loves.
Fernandes is running himself into the ground. Until the pressure on the club starts to ease, neither he nor Carrick will see any other way out of the situation.

ftbpro_01m4thtry5gr.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: The Five-Year Financial Battle With Former Club
ftbpro_01m4thtry5gr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott10:00 AM EDTThe legal battle is not over yet. / Abdullah Ahmed/Getty ImagesJuventus have launched one final appeal of the case against them involving unpaid salary to Cristiano Ronaldo, the Serie A club have revealed.

When Ronaldo left Juventus for Manchester United in the summer of 2021, it was argued that he was entitled to a total of €19.6 million ($21.9 million at the current exchange rate) in deferred wages leftover from the Covid-19 pandemic.

Three years later, a court found in Ronaldo’s favor and ordered Juve to pay half of that sum. It was decided that the club had not intentionally tried to sabotage Ronaldo’s earnings, while the player himself did not actually request the money when he left the club.

That brought about an appeal from Juve which was, once again, settled in Ronaldo’s favor earlier this year—Ronaldo did lose his own appeal for the full amount to be paid—and the case is not over just yet as Juve have opted for one final appeal to Italy’s Court of Cassation, the highest level of appeal available.
In the club’s financial report for the 2025–26 season, Juve confirmed they are still awaiting a date for their final appeal.

“The decision was limited to a review of the formal defects in the award reported in the appeal, and is not a decision on the merits of the case,” Juve stated. “As such, it does not entail a change to the conclusions reached by the award.

“In any case, the economic and financial effects resulting from the award have already been reflected in the Company’s accounts since the 2023–2024 financial year and therefore no negative impacts on the current or future financial statements are expected.
“Juventus has appealed against this ruling to the Supreme Court, which was duly notified on March 27, 2026, and a hearing date is pending.”

Juventus are fighting to avoid paying out to Ronaldo. / MIGUEL MEDINA/AFP/Getty ImagesDuring the Covid-19 pandemic, it was not uncommon for clubs that lost all matchday income due to closed stadiums to strike agreements to defer their players’ salaries to help them navigate a financially challenging period. Documents shown to the courts proved such an agreement between Juventus and Ronaldo in the 2020–21 season.

The issues started after Ronaldo left the club in 2021. Juventus did not pay the leftover salary, arguing the forward had confirmed they had no further financial commitment to him, and Ronaldo did not immediately request the funds until sending a letter which became infamous in Italian media with the not-so-creative nickname of “the Ronaldo letter.”

The details only came out during a separate investigation into financial misconduct against Juve in 2022, which brought the resignations of president Andrea Agnelli, vice-president Pavel Nedvěd and the entire board of directors.
It subsequently emerged that the agreement between Juve and Ronaldo did not actually include the Portugal international’s signature and was not therefore legally binding.

Juve continue to argue that, because there was no official deferral agreement and Ronaldo did not request the funds in negotiations over his exit, they should not have had to pay. That argument already failed to win over one court but they are trying one final time.

ftbpro_01m4tkza96hk.title: Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. LASK: Three Crucial Starters Missing for Iraola
ftbpro_01m4tkza96hk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray11:45 AM EDTLiverpool must bounce back from the hefty defeat they suffered on Sunday. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesLiverpool return to Champions League action against one of the competition’s four debutants on Wednesday, with LASK their hosts on Matchday 2 of the league phase.

The Reds opened their campaign with a hard-fought 2–1 victory over Atlético Madrid and will expect consecutive triumphs when visiting the Austrian minnows—who they beat home and away during the 2023–24 Europa League group stage.

Aiming to bounce back from the weekend’s bruising defeat to Manchester City, Andoni Iraola has some intriguing selection dilemmas to overcome. Missing several key performers through injury and tempted to rotate his team with tougher games ahead, the Spaniard has some big calls to make.
Here’s how Liverpool could line up in Linz.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: Alisson—The Brazilian was helpless as Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki each fired exquisite finishes beyond him. LASK are unlikely to net such world-class strikes.

RB: Jeremie Frimpong—Liverpool have games against Brentford, Villarreal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Chelsea before October concludes, meaning Iraola must rotate wherever possible. This is an opportunity to rest Ronald Araújo in favor of Frimpong.
CB: Joe Gomez—Jérémy Jacquet played at the weekend despite an injury scare over the international period. Liverpool need to manage his minutes carefully, with Gomez on standby and ready to fill in.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—The Dutchman captained Liverpool to their 3–1 victory away at LASK in September 2023 and will want a clean sheet on this occasion.

LB: Kostas Tsimikas—Make no mistake about it, left back is an area of weakness for Liverpool. With Milos Kerkez having played six full matches for club and country over the past month, Tsimikas might get a run out in Austria.

CM: Ryan Gravenberch—Gravenberch will be suspended for the upcoming league game with Brentford, meaning there’s little doubt he will start on Wednesday. He’d played rather well until his harsh but costly dismissal against City.

CM: Trey Nyoni—Dominik Szoboszlai has stayed at home due to injury, Wataru Endō was omitted from the Champions League squad and Alexis Mac Allister could be rested. That opens the door for a first European start for the highly-rated Nyoni.

RW: Rio Ngumoha—With Cody Gakpo sidelined, Ngumoha is the only realistic way that Iraola can refresh a forward line that fell flat against City. The youngster could replace Victor Muñoz on the right wing, despite preferring the left-hand side.

AM: Florian Wirtz—The knives are being sharpened for Wirtz as he continues to flounder for the Reds. But with Szoboszlai missing, there’s no real alternative to the out-of-form German in the No. 10 position.

LW: Bradley Barcola—After an underwhelming showing at the weekend, Barcola could really use a morale-boosting performance against LASK. The 24-year-old will hope that comes in the form of a goal or an assist.

ST: Lewis Koumas—The academy graduate buzzed around with admirable intensity against City and nearly scored the opening goal with a fierce effort. With Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké injured, Koumas could lead the line for the first time in Europe.

ftbpro_01m4tp1hnfxw.title: ‘What Makes Him Unique’—Arteta Reacts to Messi’s Bold Max Dowman Prediction
ftbpro_01m4tp1hnfxw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer11:00 AM EDTMax Dowman has sky-high potential. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images (Dowman), Rich Storry/Getty Images (Messi)Mikel Arteta hopes Lionel Messi’s new ad campaign that named teenage prodigy Max Dowman among 10 players tipped to write soccer’s next chapter is accurate in its prediction.

Now that Messi is winding down his career—the first step of which was his recent farewell to the Argentina national team—attention is turning to the burgeoning superstars who could attempt to fill his shoes in the relatively near future.
Pushing that narrative of one era making way for the next, a new adidas commercial has seen Messi supposedly choose the emerging talents he believes can light up the next generation.

The cynical viewpoint questions how organic or authentic it could be—all 10 are conveniently adidas-signed athletes and more likely the recommendation of the brand’s marketing department than Messi himself. But the impact that Arsenal’s Dowman, by the age of 16, has already had in his fledgling career suggests he has the potential to reach world-class levels in due course.
Still, the question was put to Arteta this week about Messi’s apparent opinion on Dowman.
“If Messi, who is the best ever player, says that … his eyes are I think better than anybody else’s. Hopefully he’s right,” the Arsenal boss replied.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

But whether it’s actually Messi’s personal opinion or not is irrelevant when it comes to Dowman. He played Under-18s soccer for the Gunners aged 13, and then for the Under-21s aged 14. He is the Premier League’s youngest ever goalscorer and its second youngest player. Dowman is additionally the youngest Premier League champion and the youngest ever Champions League player.

So far this season, Dowman has scored twice in a Carabao Cup victory for Arsenal and made one Premier League appearance, as he splits his time with the Under-21s. The Essex-born talent doesn’t celebrate his 17th birthday—and therefore cannot legally drive a car in the U.K.—until Dec. 31.
“In the few appearances he’s had, he’s already done remarkable things. That’s somebody that is touched with a special gift,” Arteta offered.
“He’s a joy to watch. The way he moves, the way he touches the ball, the way he carries himself, it’s just different. And that’s what makes him unique.”

At 16 years old, Dowman’s minutes are still inconsistent. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesWe may have seen JJ Gabriel and his family get itchy feet at Manchester United, but there is absolutely no rush for Dowman at this stage of his career.

Arteta clearly values his talent and he’s getting far more senior opportunities than anyone his age usually would. Jack Wilshere, once an Arsenal prodigy himself and the club’s Under-18s manager when Dowman debuted in that age group, recently gave an insight into his potential.

“Don’t get into a duel, take one or two touches, move it around,” Wilshere, during a guest appearance on Stick to Football, revealed were his instructions to a then 13-year-old Dowman, facing players up to five years older. “He picked up the ball, dribbled round five players, squared it and we [scored]. I have never seen anything like it.

“He went on with us and developed a bit more, and physically his numbers were a joke … the metrics they use now—high-speed running, sprints, total distance—were Premier League level and he was 14. He can be what he wants. He’s got a good family around him as well.”
Wilshere said the next crucial step for Dowman is to “get into the team and stay in the team,” which may have to result in a compromise with regard to his position on the pitch.

“When he played with me, we played him in all the midfield positions and he can play all of them,” Wilshere explained. “It’s pretty normal for a young player to get into the [senior] team on the wing. He’ll probably have to play on the sides if he wants a run in the team.”

Arteta (left) has such trust in Dowman already.  / Xavi Bonilla/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesOverall, Wilshere agreed with the offering of podcast host Gary Neville that Dowman will ultimately thrive in a No. 10 role like current Gunners captain Martin Ødegaard. Displacing Bukayo Saka for any length of time on the right will be as tricky as ousting Ødegaard, although both players have a less than perfect injury history. The left flank, where Arsenal failed to land a superstar target during the summer, might be an avenue for a better run in the team.
“We haven’t seen much of Max on the left,” Arteta said on that subject. “We need to throw him in a new position at some point. I think he will have the capacity to adapt.”

Dowman has plenty of eyes looking out for him. Aside from guidance from Arteta, Ødegaard was another former teen prodigy, thrust into the limelight at 16 when he had all of Europe’s major clubs on his tail and opted to join Real Madrid. He’s seen how this this works from the inside.

ftbpro_01m4trwx7g44.title: Haaland Will Overtake Mbappe, Messi With Champions League Goalscoring Record
ftbpro_01m4trwx7g44.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell1:00 PM EDTErling Haaland is rewriting the history books. / Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesManchester City star Erling Haaland only needs to make an appearance against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday to add another Champions League record to his résumé.

The prolific striker will become the player with the most goals scored in Europe’s premier club competition in 60 appearances—and he doesn’t even have to find the back of the net against the defending cup holders to do so.

Haaland already has 59 goals in 59 Champions League appearances. No other player, not even all-time leading goalscorer Cristiano Ronaldo, has ever managed 50 goals in their first 60 appearances. The 26-year-old essentially owns the record already, but he will formally etch his name in the history books when he plays his 60th Champions League game this week.

City host PSG in their second league phase match of the 2026–27 campaign. Enzo Maresca’s men come into the fixture on an eight-game winning streak, collecting their most recent triumph against Liverpool after being found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations.

Haaland’s 65th minute strike sealed all three points in the 3–0 victory, bringing the Norway international’s season tally to eight goals in as many appearances. If he adds more against PSG, he will only increase the cushion between himself and the other legendary names in the Champions League scoring charts.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Erling Haaland will have another record to his name. / Clive Brunskill/Getty ImagesRank

Haaland is about to join an exclusive club. Come Wednesday, his name will sit above Ruud van Nistelrooy in the record books, boasting a minimum of 11 goals more than the Manchester United legend over the same number of games.

The company only gets better as the list goes on. Harry Kane managed 45 goals in his first 60 Champions League appearances, while Kylian Mbappé bagged 40. Lionel Messi and Robert Lewandowski both had 39 to their name when they reached 60 matches played.

The new league phase helps Haaland inflate his tally, but the No. 9 was making history long before the competition’s format change. The Norwegian scored the most Champions League goals in his first 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 appearances.

Every haul is a Champions League record, as is his 59 (or more) goals in 60 appearances. Haaland also is guaranteed the record for the most goals scored in 70 appearances; Van Nistelrooy currently owns that title with 55 goals, a tally Haaland has already surpassed.

Cristiano Ronaldo is the best goalscorer in Champions League history. / Angel Martinez/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesAt just 26 years old, Haaland’s 59 Champions League goals make him the eighth all-time leading goalscorer in the competition’s history. He already sits above the likes of Thierry Henry, Mohamed Salah and Kane in the goal charts.

Still, there are Champions League giants higher up in the record books. Ronaldo’s 141 goals leads the way, followed by Messi’s 129 and Lewandowski’s 109. The three legends are the only players to ever exceed the century mark on Europe’s biggest stage.

At the rate he is scoring, Haaland will eventually reach that milestone as well. Only time will tell if he can dethrone Ronaldo, a race Mbappé is also running. But he will surely continue to climb up the charts.
One more goal for Haaland puts him level with Van Nistelrooy. Then, he can begin chasing down Mbappé, the only other player in the top 10 still playing Champions League soccer.
