ftbpro_01m4tx05wr3y.title: LASK vs. Liverpool: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4tx05wr3y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 13, 2026Liverpool have triumphed in both previous meetings with LASK. / Instagram/LASK (LASK), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Liverpool)Liverpool face the simplest of their eight Champions League league phase matches this Wednesday, although they can’t afford complacency against competition debutants LASK.

The Reds were triumphant in their opening European match of the season, coming from behind to beat Atlético Madrid 2–1 under the Anfield floodlights. The Raiffeisen Arena doesn’t boast the same allure as the fabled Merseyside venue, but just under 20,000 supporters will make their voices heard during a seismic occasion for LASK.

The Austrians were narrow 1–0 losers to AEK Athens in their first-ever match in the Champions League proper, and they will be forced to raise their level a fair few notches for Liverpool’s visit. They were unable to do so during the other meeting between the sides in Linz, when Jürgen Klopp’s men ran out 3–1 victors in the 2023–24 Europa League group stage.

Liverpool might have conquered Atlético Madrid in their continental opener, but they enter the upcoming fixture deflated from Sunday’s bitter 3–0 defeat to Manchester City. Ryan Gravenberch’s costly red card contributed to Andoni Iraola’s first loss as Reds manager, with the Spaniard determined to witness a response from his injury-stricken team on their European travels.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

The Reds fought hard for victory over Atléti in their first outing. / Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesLiverpool are still finding their feet under Iraola following an unspectacular start to his reign and recent injuries haven’t helped his players adapt to the demands of his approach. But against a side like LASK, they shouldn’t need perfection to walk away with three points.

Their hosts are on a four-game winless streak which has seen them sink to third in the Austrian first division, and there are few recognizable faces within Dietmar Kühbauer’s roster. In contrast, Liverpool will field an arsenal of superstars in Linz.
Even without some key personnel, the Reds should prove simply too powerful for the home side.

LASK will definitely be without three players for Wednesday’s gargantuan encounter. Spare a thought for Moses Usor, George Bello and Ramiz Harakaté, who will all sit out a memorable occasion against the six-time European champions.

Former Wolverhampton Wanderers man Sasa Kalajdžić should start up front as he searches for his first goal of the campaign, with the towering striker potentially causing issues for Virgil van Dijk and Co. with his aerial prowess.

Kühbauer tends to favor five at the back and will certainly lean on this formation against Liverpool’s band of speedy forwards. Young goalkeeper Lukas Jungwirth will be busy between the posts if the defense in front of him can’t frustrate the Reds.
LASK predicted lineup vs. Liverpool (5-3-2): Jungwirth; Jørgensen, Mbuyamba, Alemão, Andrade, Dibango; Ljubičić, Bogarde, Horvath; Kalajdžić, Lang.

Liverpool have been forced to travel without the influential trio of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai. They are “not far” from returning, according to Iraola, but no exact timeline has been put on their recoveries.

Without Isak and long-term absentee Hugo Ekitiké, it could be academy graduate Lewis Koumas leading the line once again. Szoboszlai’s absence opens up a space in midfield, which could be filled by young Trey Nyoni as Iraola looks to rotate where possible.
Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endō are unavailable having been omitted from the Champions League roster, while Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley remain missing in defense.
To keep things fresh ahead of a busy run of tough fixtures, Iraola could make changes from the weekend. Jeremie Frimpong, Kostas Tsimikas, Joe Gomez and Rio Ngumoha could all enter the starting XI.
Gravenberch will be suspended for Liverpool’s next Premier League match following his dismissal against City, but he’s available for Iraola in Europe.
Liverpool predicted lineup vs. LASK (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Frimpong, Gomez, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Nyoni; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas.

ftbpro_01m4txrea26c.title: Man City vs. PSG: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4txrea26c.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 13, 2026The back-to-back champions take on the Premier League leaders in a blockbuster duel. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images/VisionhausDespite the surrounding circumstances, Manchester City’s Champions League affair with back-to-back winners Paris Saint-Germain is an unmissable occasion.

All the Cityzens can do, as they await the outcome of their appeal to being found guilty of systematic financial fraud by an independent commission, is knuckle down and go about their work as if there isn’t the darkest of clouds lingering over their heads.

The situation is utterly bizarre, but the show goes on. Their upcoming opponents PSG are hardly saints either. Back in 2014, they, along with Man City, negotiated with UEFA’s General Secretary at the time, Gianni Infantino, to receive reduced punishments for breaching UEFA’s Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules. The two clubs got away with slaps on the wrist, yet the debacle was remarkably prescient given what’s come to light.

A strange, almost nefarious alliance has formed between the two clubs, which have been at the forefront of European soccer for the past decade. While Luis Enrique has created a juggernaut in Paris, Man City eventually got their hands on the Champions League to complete a historic treble in 2023.
Pep Guardiola, the mastermind behind City’s dominance, is expected to be in attendance on Wednesday night, as he continues to back the club’s hierarchy in their quest to prove City’s innocence.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

PSG and Man City last met during the 2024–25 league phase. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesWhile the context is hard to dismiss, this should be a belting match between two undeniably superb teams. PSG failed to relinquish their grip on the trophy last season for a reason, and Man City have so far been perfect under Enzo Maresca.

Maresca has seemingly added more strings to his coaching bow since arriving in Manchester, with the Cityzens performing with a unique fluidity that we seldom saw from his Chelsea teams. City have been almost impossible to stymie thus far, and they’ll be confident of bypassing a PSG outfit that tends to ease their way into the new season.

The Parisians are sixth in Ligue 1, having won only half of their six matches. They’re yet to hit their stride, but they so often find an extra gear when the lights shine brightest on European nights. Slovan Bratislava were put to the sword on Matchday 1, while Man City eased past Porto.
become just the second team to go 10+ consecutive games against English sides in this competition without losing.
Maresca is set to have a clean bill of health for PSG’s visit on Wednesday, but that doesn’t mean the Italian won’t tinker with the team that won so impressively at Anfield.

Jérémy Doku changed the game off the bench, having recovered from a calf injury, and is likely to come in down the left flank. Phil Foden could also make his first appearance since he was sent off in the Manchester Derby. Foden won’t displace Rayan Cherki, but he could combine with the Frenchman while drifting in from the right.
Joško Gvardiol may replace Nico O’Reilly at left back, but other defensive alterations could be saved for the weekend, when Ipswich Town travel up to Manchester.

Erling Haaland is aiming to become the club’s outright leading goalscorer in this competition on Wednesday; he’s currently level with Sergio Agüero on 36 goals. If he scores twice against the Parisians, he’ll become the seventh-highest scorer in Champions League history.
Man City predicted lineup vs. PSG (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, Gvardiol; Fernández, Anderson; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.
Like their hosts, PSG are healthy heading into Wednesday’s game, which only adds to the anticipation.

Enrique offered extended breaks to Ousmane Dembélé and Nuno Mendes after the three-week international window, and PSG won in their absence at the weekend. Both, however, are ready to return to the PSG team on Wednesday.
Désiré Doué’s exploits for France were praised by the manager, so he may get the nod in attack alongside Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Ferran Torres should also feature against his former club.
Senny Mayulu, who picked up an injury on duty with France’s U-21s, is set to be the only absentee.
PSG predicted lineup vs. Man City (4-3-3): Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes; Vitinha, Neves, Fabián; Doué, Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia.

ftbpro_01m4v1bpe6q6.title: Roma vs. Real Madrid: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m4v1bpe6q6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack9:00 PM EDTSerie A title contenders Roma welcome Real Madrid to the Olimpico. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesReal Madrid travel to the Italian capital for the first time since 2018, as they face a Roma team celebrating their Champions League return at the Stadio Olimpico.
Long-time Atalanta manager Gian Piero Gasperini inspired Roma to a third-place finish in Serie A last season, and they look primed to compete with Inter Milan for the Scudetto this term.

Gasperini’s side is unbeaten through six league outings, and they were forced to impressively grind out a point at fellow Champions League participants Como at the weekend after top scorer Donyell Malen was sent off.
In Europe, their league phase campaign started with an admirable 1–1 draw at Fenerbahçe last month, while Madrid edged past Inter 2–1 at the Santiago Bernabéu.

José Mourinho, of course, had a special affinity with the Nerazzurri, and the Olimpico faithful are sure to give the ‘Special One’ a warm welcome on Wednesday evening. Mourinho, on his 2021 return to Italy after more than a decade away, guided Roma to Conference League glory at the end of his first season in the Eternal City. He departed at the start of 2024 after two-and-a-half years at the helm.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mourinho left Roma at the start of 2024. / Paolo Bruno/Getty ImagesThis occasion will undoubtedly mean plenty to Mourinho, given what his Roma team achieved in Tirana in May 2022. Rome has fallen for Gasperini as it did José, and the current boss will hope to improve a rather uninspiring head-to-head record against the returning Real Madrid manager.

Mourinho’s Madrid haven’t exactly convinced on either side of the extended international break, with Los Blancos claiming a necessary but stodgy victory over Villarreal at the weekend to remain six points behind Barcelona in La Liga.

Yan Diomande’s first goal for the club was overshadowed by Vinícius Júnior’s red card and Mourinho’s refusal to speak to the press postgame. Already, it seems as if he’s reverting to a familiar playbook. It’s his team against the world.

Donyell Malen’s red card at the weekend doesn’t mean he’s suspended for Wednesday’s match. The Dutchman will serve his ban in Serie A. Malen will lead Roma’s attack in tandem with Paulo Dybala, who’s been able to stay injury-free at the start of the new season.

Star goalkeeper Mile Svilar is expected to be out until November with a broken finger, and Bryan Cristante also isn’t available. Manu Koné and Marten De Roon are set to line up in Gasperini’s midfield.
Former Atlético Madrid defender Mario Hermoso faces a familiar foe, having been involved in 13 Madrid derbies during his time in the Spanish capital.
Roma predicted lineup vs. Real Madrid (3-4-2-1): Gollini; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Rensch, De Roon, Koné, Wesley; Dybala, Soulé; Malen.
Madrid are in a better spot in terms of availability for this encounter, with Bernardo Silva and Arda Güler both eligible for the match after serving suspensions.

However, the two players may find themselves on the bench in Rome. Aurélien Tchouaméni looks set to partner Federico Valverde in midfield, and Vinícius Júnior’s domestic suspension will only encourage Mourinho to start the Brazilian in Europe.
Yan Diomande should also keep his place after scoring his first goal for the club at the weekend.
On the injury front, the visitors are currently without Éder Militão, Ferland Mendy, Rodrygo and Raúl Asencio.
Real Madrid predicted lineup vs. Roma (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Dumfries, Konaté, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Tchouaméni; Diomande, Bellingham, Viní Jr; Mbappé.

ftbpro_01m4v23g3b4q.title: Two Ways Liverpool Can Fix Struggling Florian Wirtz Amid Growing Criticism

paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray12:00 PM EDTFlorian Wirtz continues to frustrate supporters. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesJamie Carragher has yet again vocalized his displeasure with Florian Wirtz, calling on Liverpool to drop the $158 million attacking midfielder in the coming matches.

Things are looking increasingly hopeless for the 23-year-old, who, over 12 months after joining the Reds, continues to deliver underwhelming performances in England. During the weekend’s 3–0 defeat to Manchester City, he was particularly disappointing.

Another ineffective showing prompted rage from one of Wirtz’s biggest critics over recent months, former Liverpool defender Carragher, who blasted the playmaker for having “absolutely no goal threat whatsoever.”

Carragher fumed on Sky Sports: “What Florian Wirtz is doing for Liverpool is not enough right now. He’s played 55, 60 games for Liverpool. If we were looking at [Bradley] Barcola, he has played four or five. You would want more but hold your horses. If you were critical of him, it would be over the top, but not the guy that has played 60 games.”
He added: “He shouldn’t be in the Liverpool team right now. I don’t want to hammer Liverpool players. But we’re not saying this after five to 10 games, we’re saying this after 50 to 60 games.

“Wirtz never looks like scoring a goal. You don’t come away thinking he missed chances or he worked the goalkeeper. There was absolutely nothing where you thought he put someone through, or nearly scored. There’s absolutely no goal threat whatsoever.”

Liverpool supporters were willing to give Wirtz the benefit of the doubt during his debut season, allowing for an adjustment period within a struggling team under Arne Slot. But patience is now running very, very thin.

Wirtz has delivered only one goal involvement this season in seven appearances, adding to just 15 produced last term. Given the price Liverpool paid for him—a club record at the time—much more is needed to silence growing criticism.
So, how could Liverpool re-energize their No. 7?

Dropping Wirtz could benefit everyone. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesLiverpool have already tried playing Wirtz through long stretches of poor form. He started 40 of his 49 appearances during his maiden year with the club, often being selected despite his mediocre displays in domestic and European competitions.
One thing Liverpool haven’t tried, however, is dropping him.
Carragher is right: currently, Wirtz is not worthy of his starting position. Perhaps Liverpool should heed the advice of their former center back.

An injury sustained by Dominik Szoboszlai certainly makes this option less appealing, with the Hungarian the obvious replacement for Wirtz as a No. 10, but the German can have few complaints if he drops to the bench once Szoboszlai returns.

Not only would Szoboszlai provide a greater goal threat in the role—he’s already scored three times this season—he would also provide Liverpool with greater defensive security courtesy of his impressive defensive acumen.

Perhaps a break from the pressure that comes with being Liverpool’s aspiring playmaker would benefit Wirtz. Bringing him off the bench for the final half-hour of matches could see him thrive against tiring defenses, offering the Reds some poise and finesse as games become increasingly stretched.
If he can serve up some goals and assists late in matches, it could provide a much-needed confidence boost that would facilitate a return to the starting XI.

Could Iraola reinvent Wirtz? / Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC/Getty Images“I see him more probably in that position behind the striker. We know that he has played with Germany more on the left sometimes. But, I think we’re going to start working with him in that position behind the striker,” Iraola enthused in back in July when quizzed about the best use of Wirtz.

However, after a slow start under the Spaniard, perhaps Liverpool’s only alternative strategy to reignite Wirtz’s career requires some trial and error. A shake-up in his role could be the last resort.

Wirtz has been used off the left wing by Liverpool and Germany previously, albeit it’s not his preferred position. He started on that flank 14 times for the Reds last season, scoring once and providing two assists, with a number of those showings come in late December and early January—the period during which Wirtz played his best soccer.

ftbpro_01m4v4xayat2.title: How Kylian Mbappe Compares to Messi, Ronaldo After 100 Champions League Matches
ftbpro_01m4v4xayat2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 14, 2026Kylian Mbappé (middle) is putting up Champions League numbers that are similar to what Ronaldo and Messi produced.  / Pierre-Philippe Marcou/AFP/Getty Images (Messi), Victor Carretero/Real Madrid/Getty Images (Mbappé), David Ramos/Getty Images (Ronaldo) Kylian Mbappé celebrated becoming the youngest player in history to feature in 100 Champions League games in Real Madrid’s incredible 4–3 comeback win against Roma on Wednesday night.
The Frenchman scored the first of the night for Jose Mourinho’s men, making it 72 goals in 100 games on Europe’s biggest stage.

It feels like only yesterday that the now Real Madrid forward burst into the scene with Monaco during the 2016–17 season, bagging his first career Champions League goal in a memorable 5–3 win away against Manchester City in the round of 16.
Mbappé moved to Paris Saint-Germain a season later and has since only enhanced his status as one of the greatest players in competition history.

The most prestigious trophy in club soccer continues to evade the Frenchman, but at only 27, Mbappé has spent almost a decade scoring goals for fun, and he’s keeping pace with the greatest goalscorers in Champions League history through 100 games.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kylian Mbappé won the 2025–26 Champions League Golden Boot.  / Nicolò Campo/LightRocket/Getty Images Through 100 Champions League appearances, Mbappé has found the back of the net 72 times to go along with 25 assists. His strike against Roma saw him overtake Real Madrid legend Raúl to stand alone as the fifth greatest goalscorer in competition history.

Mbappé still has a long way to go before he’s even close to Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, the top two goalscorers in Champions League history. But given his age and how he compares through 100 games, there’s reason to believe he’s capable of matching or even overtaking the two all-time greats when it’s all said and done.

Ronaldo, the all-time leading scorer in the competition, had only bagged 66 of his eventual 140 goals when he played his 100th Champions League match. Messi ended with 129 goals and had scored 77 after 100 games. Mbappé is sandwiched between the pair at 72, and given the expanded tournament format, he still has plenty of time to close the gap.
Robert Lewandowski is the only other player to eclipse the century goal-mark in the Champions League. The legendary Pole, though, had a staggering 81 goals through his first 100 appearances.
But beyond the individual statistics, both Messi and Ronaldo were Champions League winners inside their first 100 games played in the competition.
Mbappé came closest in 2019–20, when PSG lost 1–0 in the final against Bayern Munich. The Frenchman hasn’t made it past the semifinal round since.

Champions League glory continues to evade Kylian Mbappé. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty Images Only days after Real Madrid won their record 15th Champions League title in 2024, Mbappé joined Los Blancos and many expected them to build yet another European dynasty. But since he landed in Spain’s capital, Mbappé and Madrid have failed to make it past the quarterfinals.
Mbappé was won a World Cup and is the competition’s all-time top goalscorer, but now he admitted that winning the Champions League with Real Madrid is what he wants “more than anything.”

“That’s the objective, that’s the goal [to win the Champions League],” Mbappé told CBS Sports after Madrid’s opening day win vs. Inter Milan. “That’s what I said yesterday about the Ballon d’Or, but the Champions League is even more important.
“I play for the club of my dreams. It’s really important for me to win the Champions League here in Madrid. I want it more than anything.”

Although Real Madrid haven’t been overly impressive to start 2026–27, they’re still among the best teams in Europe and Mbappé is a player capable of winning games almost single-handedly. Only time will tell if this is the year when the already legendary Frenchman accomplishes the thing he wants more than anything.

ftbpro_01m4v8fb081m.title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Lille: Rotated Gunners Extend Brilliant League Phase Record
ftbpro_01m4v8fb081m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack5:12 PM EDTArsenal eventually cruised to another Champions League victory at the Emirates. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal’s outstanding Champions League home record under Mikel Arteta continued on Tuesday evening, as three second-half goals saw the Gunners ease past Lille 3–0.
Arteta’s men thus followed up their victory in Naples with another triumph, as they aim to avoid two extra matches in the new year by finishing inside the top eight of the league phase table.

Lille had been relatively comfortable in the opening hour, with a varied approach in possession limiting the damage a rotated Arsenal could inflict with their press. However, the Gunners slowly turned the screw after an uninspired first half, and Jurriën Timber’s smart finish proved to be the spark a frustrated Emirates crowd sorely needed.

Arteta subsequently pivoted to Bukayo Saka and Martin Ødegaard as part of a triple-change, and the former teed up Eberechi Eze for Arsenal’s second almost immediately after his introduction. Saka then got on the scoresheet himself as the hosts threatened a walkover, but Lille were at least able to prevent Arsenal from running up the score in the closing stages.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Arsenal are far better when Viktor Gyökeres isn’t on the field. / John Walton/PA Images/Getty Images“The happiest thing, the thing we can do to be the happiest, is to win football matches. That’s the best medicine for everybody,” Arteta asserted in the build-up to Lille’s visit, explaining how the Gunners will overcome their heartbreak in Budapest.

There has been only one blip in Arsenal’s season to date, but the boss cannot be overly pleased with his side’s level of performance on either side of the extended international break. At the moment, the Gunners are delivering in spurts, but that’s been enough in back-to-back games.

Once again, those in reserve huffed and puffed their way through proceedings, struggling to assert themselves in the contest and hardly instilling fear in those above them in the pecking order. Viktor Gyökeres was anonymous, and we can’t exactly say the Swede is desperate for a goal. He scored four for his country during the recent break.

Timber’s strike broke the shackles and forced a relatively comfortable but increasingly frail Lille, boasting the joint-best defensive record in Ligue 1, to change tack slightly. However, the visitors ultimately succumbed to a Gunners outfit that drastically improved once Arteta made changes that were planned before Timber’s opener.

From then on, it was a familiar Champions League night for the Emirates faithful since Arteta guided the club back into Europe’s premier club competition three years ago. Still, the Spaniard won’t be overly thrilled with the level shown by a tinkered attack for an hour.
Gabriel faced off against his former club. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: David Raya—6.7: Rarely is Arsenal’s No. 1 tested on such occasions, and it was more of the same here.
RB: Jurrïen Timber—8.6: Timber was keen to contribute going forward all night, and his perseverance paid off by opening the scoring with a cultured touch and finish.
CB: Ezri Konsa—7.4: A night of few issues for Konsa, who wasn’t tested by an imbalanced and lightweight Lille attack.

CB: Gabriel—6.7: Gabriel made a superb block to deny Dilane Bakwa early on, and it seemed as if Arsenal would at least be put to the test by the visitors in transition. However, that was as good as it got for Ancelotti’s side.

LB: Myles Lewis-Skelly—7.8: Back to where it all began in the senior team, Lewis-Skelly wasn’t troubled all that much despite Bakwa’s bright start, and he was a threat in the final third toward the end of the first half.
CM: Declan Rice—7.7: Nothing spectacular from Arsenal’s captain on the night, who went about his work without fuss.
CM: Bruno Guimarães—8.2: Probed unrelentingly, especially at the start of the second half, and he looked like making something happen. Had a couple of shots on goal, too.

RW: Noni Madueke—7.8: Offered plenty of threat and dominated his duel one-on-one with former Southampton defender Romain Perraud. The combination with Timber eventually bore fruit, but he’d be much better off if he looked up before he delivered into the box.
AM: Mikel Merino—6.6: Merino earned a rare start, but he was no Martin Ødegaard. The Spaniard offers something completely different, and he should’ve headed Arsenal into a first-half lead.

ftbpro_01m4v9bzk6hg.title: Barcelona Player Ratings vs. Galatasaray: Barca Ace Season’s Toughest Test Yet
ftbpro_01m4v9bzk6hg.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:24 PM EDTFermín López (right) completed Barcelona’s comeback from a Lamine Yamal assist.        / Yasin Akgul/AFP/Getty ImagesThree second-half goals saw Barcelona complete their comeback and defeat Galatasaray 4–1 away in the Champions League in what was surely their biggest test of the campaign so far.

Inside the boiling cauldron that was Galatasaray’s “hell” at RAMS Park, Barcelona started the game positively, matching the hosts’ intensity but failing to capitalize on the opportunities they created. It proved costly, as Galatasaray struck in the first action they caught Barça out of shape; Rafael Leão quickly found a charging Aleksey Batrakov, whose deflected shot found the back of the net 28 minutes in.

The opener shook Barcelona and had it not been for a marginal offside call, Galatasaray would’ve doubled their just five minutes later. When Hansi Flick’s side was at its worst, Dani Olmo pounced on a rebound and threaded a pass to an incoming João Cancelo, who buried the equalizer into the far post on the verge of halftime.

Then Lamine Yamal took over in the second half. In a matter of eight minutes, the teenager created three big chances, two of which were converted by Fermín López and Anthony Gordon to complete Barça’s comeback in a blink of an eye.
The Catalans completely erased Galatasaray from the pitch after that and Karim Adeyemi added Barça’s fourth with a powerful finish into the bottom corner just past the hour-mark.
Barcelona will spend the night atop the Champions League standings and have now won their opening 10 games of 2026–27 in all competitions. Flick’s men look like the best team in the world currently.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Eric García (bottom) suffered against Rafael Leão. / Burak Kara/Getty ImagesThe eventual outcome was decisive, but there was as stretch in the first half where the Catalans significantly suffered. It’s still very early in the season, but the defensive flaws that have defined Barcelona throughout the Flick era resurfaced.

As it became a trend especially in 2025–26, if opponents are able to bypass Barça’s high-press and force the backline to run significant distances towards their own goal, then Flick’s men are easy to harm.

The action of Galatasaray’s opener looked eerily similar to the many goals Barça have conceded over the past two seasons, especially in Europe. Quick transitions in which Flick’s defenders are tasked with defending in open space are the team’s kryptonite, as the backline loses its shape quickly and incoming runners go untracked.
It’s now 17 straight games without a Champions League clean sheet for Flick’s Barça, and the Catalans have now conceded 19 goals in their last nine away trips in Europe.

Barcelona have been arguably the best team in the world to start 2026–27 and RAMS Park is one of the most difficult away grounds in Europe. Still, the exploitable Achilles’s heel of Flick’s side was uncovered once again, bringing back concerns of what could happen come the latter stages of the competition.
Anthony Gordon (bottom) has scored in consecutive matches after the international break.     / Arif Hudaverdi Yaman/Anadolu/Getty Images *Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Joan García—7.7: Still waiting to collect his first Champions League clean sheet but García was excellent as a sweeper on Tuesday night.
RB: Eric García—7.4: Completely undone by the speed of Leão the entire game. Simply unable to keep up with the Portuguese winger as evidenced by the action of Galatasaray’s opener.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—7.0: His shakiest performance of the season, struggling to track incoming Galatasaray attackers and at times being a step too late to deploy the offside trap successfully.

CB: Gerard Martín—7.2: Like his partner alongside him, he was erratic at times in his attempt to intercept passes and although he got his wins, he struggled at times in a tasty battle with Victor Osimhen.

LB: João Cancelo—8.5: One of Barça’s biggest threats all game and has now scored in his three most recent appearances for club and country. His current form is on par with the best moment of his career.

CM: Rodri—7.6: Settled into the match and once he started to feel comfortable, him and Pedri ignited Barça’s reaction, slowing down the chaos that came after Galatasaray’s opener. He misplaced only three of the 116 passes he attempted.

CM: Pedri—7.5: Barcelona’s chief creator. Whether as a deep-lying playmaker or further up the field, the midfield maestro threaded a handful of passes that could’ve easily ended up as assists. He’s having a sensational start of the season.

ftbpro_01m4v9tddxgj.title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Atletico Madrid: Wasteful Finishing Undermines Improved Outing
ftbpro_01m4v9tddxgj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer5:38 PM EDTMan Utd could not make the most of chances created. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United are five games without a win in all competitions after suffering a frustrating 2–0 defeat at the hands of Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Red Devils ironically put in a much better performance at the Metropolitano in Spain’s capital than the 1–1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur on Sunday, and yet return home to England’s northwest with nothing to show for it.

After the weekend, it was not the start Michael Carrick wanted. World Cup winner Álex Baena raced clear down Atlético’s left flank, the United defense drawn to him, pulling the ball across the box into the path of Pablo Barrios. Ayden Heaven was in the right place to block the shot back across destined for the bottom corner, but the ball still squeezed through.

There was less than one full minute on the clock and Atlético kept looking for similar passes over United’s backline. Still, Bryan Mbeumo went close to an equalizer 12 minutes in, seeing his goal-bound effort deflected wide after a clever nutmeg on Cristian Romero to create the chance. Soon after, Marcus Rashford hoped to do better with an attempted volley.

The visitors had responded positively to falling behind but Jan Oblak was in a good position to deny  Mbeumo and then Carlos Baleba’s free header from the resultant corner, midway through the first half. And yet, Atlético nearly went 2–0 ahead as Álex Grimaldo clipped the angle of post and crossbar with a whipped, curling free kick.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Atlético were even closer to pulling further ahead when USMNT midfielder Johnny Cardoso blasted the ball into the bottom corner, but the goal didn’t survive a VAR review—the ball hit the arm of Marcos Llorente in the immediate build-up.

It was a slower start to the second half until Julián Alvarez struck the post on the volley nine minutes after the restart. Almost straight after, Bruno Fernandes was agonizingly close to converting from Youri Tielemans’s raking pass, guiding the ball just the wrong side of the post.
The captain later struck the bar from distance as the search for an equalizer continued, although substitutions from both managers began to disrupt the flow of the contest.

A VAR review had come to United’s aid in the first half, but Carrick’s team finished the match with 10 players when the referee was advised to take a second look at a battle for the ball between Leny Yoro and Jonathan David. The French defender was harshly penalized for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity when the Canadian tumbled under pressure.

Without Yoro on the field, it took Atlético five more minutes to kill the game off. David was heavily involved, forcing Senne Lammens into a save that offered up a rebound to fellow substitute Ademola Lookman. In the circumstances, there was no way back.
Bryan Mbeumo missed two good chances to score. / Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty ImagesThe outcome of the match hinged on chances that were taken and chances that were not.

Lammens wasn’t as busy as Oblak. Atlético’s early opener was not statistically a ‘big chance’ and, with three-quarters of the match played, the leading hosts hadn’t created one. That was in stark contrast to Manchester United, who made four big chance by that stage of the match and missed all of them. Two fell to Mbeumo, one to Rashford and the other to Fernandes. There is a feeling they probably did enough to win.
But whether more ruthless, or just more confident, Atlético did what the Red Devils couldn’t—find the back of the net.
Andrey Santos made a case for more starts. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesAn improvement in midfield felt like a significant reason for the better performance.

Without the injured Kobbie Mainoo and Fernandes pushed into a wide position, there was opportunity to advance Youri Tielemans into a No. 10 role and line up with a brand-new central midfield pairing: Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos.

This was a less technically-skilled midfield, but one that crucially offered more mobility and a greater physical presence—something United have lacked. Baleba’s integration had been delayed by a preseason injury, while Santos has been a curious omission more often than not. Both will hope this performance will be reason enough to give them more opportunities.
Youri Tielemans was more attacking. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Senne Lammens—7.0: Not a bad performance despite conceding twice.
RB: Diogo Dalot—6.8: Caught cold by Baena’s run that led to the first-minute opener.

ftbpro_01m4vbdk5t31.title: Silva Was Set Up to Fail at Real Madrid—But His Time May Finally Be Coming
ftbpro_01m4vbdk5t31.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell4:44 PM EDTBernardo Silva is scrapping for opportunities at Real Madrid. / Florencia Tan Jun/Getty ImagesThe 2026–27 season hadn’t even started yet, and Real Madrid boss José Mourinho had already publicly targeted Bernardo Silva. “He arrived for preseason with much lower physical fitness, and he has to improve,” the manager said in the early days of August.

Mourinho veiled the jab by insisting Silva is a “very important player for us,” but the ensuing months proved otherwise. The Portugal international has only made four appearances greater than 15 minutes in a white shirt—and those all came when Aurélien Tchouaméni was not fit enough to start.

Any hopes of breaking into the team following the September-October international break were quickly dashed at the weekend. Silva was an unused substitute in the team’s 1–0 win over Villarreal, rooted to the bench for the second time in three games.

It was the last thing the midfielder needed after playing just seven minutes for Portugal over the break. He couldn’t even see the pitch against Wales and Denmark, and he only came on in the dying, dying stages in the team’s two clashes with Norway.

It’s a sudden fall from grace for Silva, who was a consistent, vital starter during his nine years at Manchester City. Just last season at age 31, he played 90 minutes in both the Carabao Cup final against Arsenal and the FA Cup final against Chelsea. The Cityzens lifted both trophies in Silva’s final months at the club.
He soon joined Real Madrid as a free agent and is learning the hard way just how difficult it is for even the most established stars to break into Los Blancos’ XI.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Bernardo Silva has yet to make any impact at Real Madrid. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesAfter back-to-back seasons without a major trophy, Real Madrid came into the summer transfer window with one major problem area: midfield. The club never replaced the legendary Toni Kroos and Luka Modrić, and signing a deep-lying playmaker was the top priority.

Except Los Blancos addressed nearly every other area of the pitch instead. They signed a left back in Marc Cucurella, a right back in Denzel Dumfries and a center back in Ibrahima Konaté. They signed Carlos Espí at striker and the speedy young winger Yan Diomande.

Amid the flurry of new signings was Silva. The midfielder was expected to be a depth option, with Rodri taking up the No. 6 position. But the newly crowned World Cup winner chose Barcelona instead, leaving Mourinho with the same midfielders Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa could not win anything with—plus Silva.

Suddenly, the team was looking at the 32-year-old to help fix a broken system ... without even giving him the proper opportunities to do so. Silva started three of the team’s first five La Liga matches, playing alongside Federico Valverde in Mourinho’s double pivot.

Real Madrid won all three matches, scoring 10 goals along the way, all while Tchouaméni was largely sidelined. Then as soon as the Frenchman was fit enough to start, Silva saw his minutes rapidly dwindle, all so Mourinho could start Valverde and Tchouaméni together, a duo whose largest contribution last season was a dressing room altercation.

Aurélien Tchouaméni (left) and Fede Valverde struggle to deliver results. / Denis Doyle/Getty ImagesMourinho is falling victim to the same thing his three predecessors did at Real Madrid: believing the team can win major trophies with Valverde and Tchouaméni commanding the midfield.
It’s the definition of insanity at the Bernabéu, to keep trying the same thing over and over again expecting different results. But Mourinho has made it clear the two players are in his XI.

Since the Portuguese boss favors a 4-2-3-1, there is simply no place for Silva in his plans. The midfielder can play as a No. 10, but he’s surely not displacing Jude Bellingham or Arda Güler. He can also line up on the right wing, but he’s not beating out the Türkiye international there either, nor Diomande.

Silva, the team’s only midfield signing this summer, is then forced to sit on the bench, waiting for scraps that aren’t even coming as of late. Real Madrid could undoubtedly use his precise passing, calmness under pressure and his playmaking, but they’re determined to let Valverde and Tchouaméni run the show.

It’s no coincidence Los Blancos were slow, uninspired and poor in their return to action against Villarreal. The team was booed off the pitch at halftime after managing just one shot on target in the opening 45 minutes. What changed in the second half? Mourinho altered his double pivot. Valverde was eventually moved to right back and Güler dropped into midfield—and Real Madrid had a goal 10 minutes later.
All the while, Silva was nothing more than a spectator.

José Mourinho is on the hot seat. / Denis Doyle/Getty ImagesPressure is constant at Real Madrid, especially when the team is underperforming like it is now. Los Blancos are already six points behind league-leaders Barcelona and are barely winning games against wildly inferior opposition.

Another season without a major trophy would be an absolute disaster and catastrophic failure for a team with some of the biggest and best players in the world. But all the attacking firepower in Europe cannot carry a team without a midfield.

ftbpro_01m4vbgmmr3p.title: Viktor Gyokeres Emphatically Responds to Mikel Arteta With the Wrong Answer
ftbpro_01m4vbgmmr3p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:00 PM EDTIt was not VIktor Gyökeres’s night on Tuesday. / John Walton/PA Images/Getty ImagesLONDON — Before coming up against a Sporting CP side spearheaded by Viktor Gyökeres during his final goal-laden season in Lisbon, Estrela da Amadora defender Ferro claimed the only way to stop the relentless finisher was with a “magic potion.” Whatever he cooked up didn’t work. Gyökeres scored twice and set up the other goal in a 3–0 win.
At the minute, it seems as though it would take a magic potion to get Gyökeres scoring.

Arsenal’s beleaguered striker endured a bizarre debut campaign, managing to somehow underwhelm while putting up deceptively impressive numbers. Gyökeres is struggling for minutes as much as goals at the start of his second season.

After Arteta turned to a slightly injured Kai Havertz against Leeds United on Saturday instead of the Sweden international fresh from a prolific burst of form for his country, the question of what Gyökeres would have to do was put to the Arsenal manager.

“He will play games and he will have minutes,” Arteta promised, “and the best way [to earn more] is when they enter the pitch, show how good they are. That’s it.” Gyökeres showed how good he was in Tuesday’s Champions League victory over Lille. Not very.
Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Lille. dark. Next. Arsenal Lille Ratings

Viktor Gyökeres can’t even get into position to miss. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesGyökeres was given the task of leading the line for a much-changed Arsenal for their first Champions League home game of the season, but fans could be forgiven for failing to spot the bumbling figure wearing No. 14. The Swede managed just 12 eminently forgettable touches. Less than half as many as his goalkeeper David Raya.

The focal point of Arsenal’s attack simply couldn’t make the ball stick, acting as a fleshy vortex where all forward forays went to die. Gyökeres even managed to get flagged for offside without touching the ball or being the intended recipient of a pass; his run in the eye-line of Berke Özer rendered Eberechi Eze’s first-half shot on target entirely null and void.

In isolation, anyone can be forgiven for an ineffective performance. Lille are hardly helpless patsies, currently lying second in Ligue 1 above Paris Saint-Germain. But this is the distressing normality for Gyökeres, a striker who not only fails to score but struggles to even shoot. It’s been almost 200 minutes of Premier League and Champions League action since Gyökeres last even attempted an effort in anger for Arsenal.

Anger has given way to apathy at the Emirates. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesToward the end of the goalless opening 45 minutes, Gyökeres folded in half while jumping under a long ball forward. It was the first sign that even the crowd had lost patience with their frontman, letting out a groan of frustration rather than any appeals for a non-existent foul.

When Arteta finally put Gyökeres out of his misery with a substitution in the 65th minute, seconds after the striker watched Jurriën Timber deliver a deft turn and finish he can scarcely dream of, there was a notable silence from the Emirates. The absence of noise befitting an absent performance which has turned whatever anger may be directed toward an $85 million misstep to apathy. Havertz’s arrival was greeted with a roar.

However, an even bigger cheer was saved for Olivier Giroud coming off Lille’s bench. There were was a thin smattering of boos from those who had not forgotten the Frenchman’s contributions for Chelsea, but the overwhelming response was one of warmth for a striker who scored 105 goals for Arsenal.

Giroud serves as a fitting counterpoint for Gyökeres. The towering forward was never a reliable finisher and could inspire frustration from fans but supplemented his game with the type of silky combination play that would give Gyökeres crossed eyes. Arteta hailed his former teammate as “extremely intelligent” before their reunion. “He was so good at connecting with other players.” Those are not traits which can be naturally assigned to Gyökeres.

Mikel Arteta’s first-choice XI is coming into focus. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesIf the Emirates is starting to turn on Gyökeres, Arteta certainly wasn’t impressed. Midway through the first half, the Basque boss almost ventured onto the pitch, such was the anger with which he implored his striker to drop back after Lille had played through their disjointed press.

In fairness to Gyökeres, he was not the only understudy to underwhelm on a night when Arteta changed half of his outfielders from Saturday’s league win. The entire frontline was disheveled, particularly off the ball. At one point Declan Rice was left with both arms outstretched in fury, questioning where were the red shirts who had been supposed to press Lille.

Davide Ancelotti cleverly sent Hákon Arnar Haraldsson infield from his perch on the left wing, operating in that corridor of uncertainty between three Arsenal players. Lille were allowed to complete 85% of their passes in an unintentionally passive first half.

Arsenal found the breakthrough before Arteta had brought on his cavalry, but the moment of brilliance came from Timber, who would hardly look out of place in the team’s first-choice XI. It was concussive how quickly the balance of the game shifted after the goal was swiftly followed by the introduction of Martin Ødegaard, Bukayo Saka and Havertz.

Ødegaard is Arsenal’s leader on and off the pitch, with the captain orchestrating the team’s press. Within minutes of his introduction, the area of the pitch which Lille had repeatedly overloaded was precisely where they lost the ball, presenting Saka with the chance to slide a pass across the box for Eberechi Eze. Saka completed the seven-minute burst of scoring himself to wrap up all three points.
By then, Gyökeres had taken his familiar place on the bench, panting and looking around with a gentle sigh of personal defeat. Perhaps Ferro had managed to slip him that magic potion after all.

ftbpro_01m4vm55wn80.title: ‘I Expect More’—Martinez Launches Spectacular Transfer Attack on Man Utd Bosses
ftbpro_01m4vm55wn80.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:30 AM EDTLisandro Martínez had plenty to say. / Amazon Prime Video SportManchester United center back Lisandro Martínez unloaded against the club’s board and especially the club’s director of football Jason Wilcox for their 2026 summer transfer window business in a spectacular rant following Tuesday’s 2–0 Champions League defeat against Atlético Madrid.

After a stellar second half of 2025–26 that resulted in United removing the interim tag from Michael Carrick’s job title and appointing him as permanent manager, the Red Devils have started 2026–27 with just two wins in nine games. After the match against Atlético, a visibly enraged Martínez took aim at United’s hierarchy.

“Really poor,” Martínez told Amazon Prime Sport after the match. “Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment. We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.”
When asked if he expected more investment in reinforcing United’s squad over the summer, Martínez gave a vicious, brutally honest response.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“[I expected more] yeah, 100%,” the Argentine confessed. “I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”

Martínez didn’t specify which areas he would’ve liked the club to add more reinforcements, but did say that, “Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team. It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here.”

Lisandro Martínez (right) defended Man United manager Michael Carrik. / Visionhaus/Getty Images The dreadful start of the season has firmly placed Carrick on the hot seat just two months into the campaign. However, Martínez believes that replacing the manager isn’t the answer, and hinted at others on Man Utd’s board as the people that should face the consequences in the event anyone gets replaced.

“I don't think so,” Martínez said when asked about Carrick. “He does his best. Every season is different. You can’t stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don’t change next season is a big problem.

“You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can’t say more.” But he did say more. “Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas,” Martínez said pointing up, seemingly referencing United’s higher-ups.
Soon after, Carrick also spoke to Amazon Prime Sport and admitted he hadn’t heard Martínez’s comments before briefly addressing the situation.

“I think after a game like this you come here to trying and get something out of the game and we’re disappointed,” Carrick said. “Sometimes you can be a little bit emotional as well. I have not seen it so I don’t think now is the right time for me to comment on it.

Carrick added: “I fully know we all care and we show that in different ways. But now is certainly the time to be together and work through it. We got a big a big game now Sunday and we’ve got to prepare for that properly.”

Youri Tielemans joined Manchester United from Aston Villa this summer.  / Gokhan Taner/PS Images/MB Media/Getty Images Manchester United completed four first-team signings during the summer window while also welcoming back Marcus Rashford after 18 months on loan. The bulk of United’s transfer window efforts centered around rebuilding the midfield, spending $207.2 million (£155 million) on midfielders Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans.

The trio of midfielders started for the first time together in the defeat against Atléti. Although it wasn’t a dominant display, there was overall improvement in the middle of the park. The problem is that United failed to address other areas of need.
Backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow was the only other reinforcement United secured this summer, completely ignoring glaring holes in both defense and attack.

The Red Devils targeted a left back all summer, namely Lewis Hall, but failed to acquire a new defender. Starting left back Luke Shaw has already missed time through injury, and 20-year-old center back Ayden Heaven started covering the left flank against Atléti.

Jason Wilcox (left) and Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada are in charge of the club’s recruitment.  / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images Up front, United were closer to unloading Benjamin Šeško’s backup Joshua Zirkzee than signing another solid alternative at center forward. Šeško is now injured yet Zirkzee hasn’t started a game all season and both Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha are better operating as second strikers than spearheading the attack.

Overall, though, the lack of investment becomes glaring when looking at United’s depth. That issue was masked last season due to United playing only Premier League matches since Carrick took over in January. Now that there’s Champions League soccer on the schedule plus domestic cup competitions, United’s lack of quality depth has already been exposed.

“We have a plan, we know what we can invest, and we have to stick to that,” Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada said regarding the club’s strategy during the summer transfer window. So far, that plan appears to have been insufficient.

ftbpro_01m4wrtevpd1.title: Harry Kane Surpasses Lionel Messi Landmark to Close on Cristiano Ronaldo Record
ftbpro_01m4wrtevpd1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:00 AM EDTHarry Kane (center) has overtaken Lionel Messi (left) and is chasing down Cristiano Ronaldo. / PAU BARRENA/AFP/Getty Images (Messi), Ole Martin Wold/UEFA/Getty Images (Kane), Helios de la Rubia/Real Madrid/Getty Images (Ronaldo)Harry Kane had played in League One, sat on the bench for Leicester City, and was consistently overlooked at Tottenham Hotspur in favor of transfer bust Roberto Soldado before he even made his Champions League debut. Once he was belatedly given his chance on club soccer’s grandest stage, he has made up for lost time.

The living Spurs legend managed to consistently find the net despite the Premier League club’s limitations and his output has exploded since joining a genuine contender in Bayern Munich. Kane had turned 30 by the time he arrived in Bavaria, making his staggering production during the autumn of his career all the more impressive.

After knocking in a brace for Bayern in Tuesday’s chaotic 3–3 draw with Viking, Kane’s record now stands at 36 goals in 40 Champions League games since he hit the big 3-0. For comparison, the legendary Bayern Munich striker Gerd Müller amassed 34 European Cup goals across every age of his career—as did Kane’s compatriot Wayne Rooney.
To put in perspective how impressive Kane’s record is, even Lionel Messi was only able to muster 35 Champions League goals past his 30th birthday.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Cristiano Ronaldo was prolific in the second half of his Champions League career. / VI Images/Getty ImagesAs Cristiano Ronaldo would no doubt be keen to point out, the former Real Madrid, Juventus and Manchester United poacher racked up 68 Champions League goals in 74 appearances after turning 30. Kane has some way to go to topple that record but the Bayern Munich forward is just two games away from matching another Ronaldo landmark.

Kane has now scored in nine consecutive Champions League appearances, a streak only Ronaldo has ever been able to surpass since the competition’s rebrand in 1992. The England international’s run began back in January with a brace against Union Saint-Gilloise and carried through Bayern’s entire knockout run, including both unsuccessful semifinal legs against Paris Saint-Germain.

Bayern are next up against one of Kane’s favorite opponents: Arsenal. The former Gunners academy reject turned Spurs icon has scored 15 times against his perennial north London rivals. “Arsenal are a strong team and I had a lot of great battles against them over the years,” Kane mused earlier this month. “I can’t completely ignore this background, but I’ve also played against Arsenal with Bayern a number of times now. The main thing for me is doing my job and winning the game.”

Should Kane extend his impressive run, he could fittingly match Ronaldo’s record in Madrid. Atlético host Bayern on Nov. 3 in the stadium where Kane endured in 2019 his lowest moment in the competition, toiling through a Champions League final defeat to Liverpool while half-fit.

ftbpro_01m4wv89svmz.title: Jose Mourinho Reveals Why Struggling Vinicius Junior Is Breaking His Heart
ftbpro_01m4wv89svmz.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath7:30 AM EDTVinícius Jr’s form is a problem for Madrid. /  Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesReal Madrid manager Jose Mourinho admitted seeing Vinícius Júnior in poor form is heartbreaking, with the forward also in danger of missing the first Clásico of the season after his red card at the weekend.
Vinícius Jr’s recent displays have been the subject of much scrutiny, and he has scored just once and registered one assist for his club in 2026–27.

The 26-year-old, who signed a big new contract extension until 2032 this summer, opened up on his struggles during the international break, revealing he is suffering from a lack of confidence. The Brazilian’s issues were compounded in Madrid’s most recent La Liga outing when he was sent off for pulling the hair of Villarreal player Nathan Saliba.

José Mourinho wants Vinícius Jr to be more decisive. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesAsked about his No. 7’s travails this season ahead of the Champions League clash with Roma, Mourinho expressed his hope that the “real Vinícius” will soon reappear.

“I’ve said that it breaks my heart to see Vini in this situation,” Mourinho told Sky Italia on Tuesday. “He’s happy every day, he works hard, but so far this year he hasn’t yet found the joy of making a decisive impact.
“Let’s see if, in the Champions League — given that he’s suspended for the league — he can get back to being the real Vinícius”.
The forward’s domestic suspension means he is in line to start in Rome, after having been dropped from the lineup to face Villarreal.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Jr has rarely looked so peripheral at Madrid. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIt has been a tricky few months for Vinícius Jr, who has struggled more than any other big-name player at the outset of the new Mourinho era.
Once arguably Madrid’s most important player, he has become peripheral this season—even while still starting.

Out wide left in a 4-2-3-1 formation, he has had to contend with Kylian Mbappé for his preferred spaces. While this is far from a new issue at Madrid, it has only become more pronounced this season, with Mbappé excelling and Vinícius shrinking.

The arrival of record signing Yan Diomande—who scored his first goal of the season in the win over Villarreal—adds to the growing pressure on Vinícius, whose place in the lineup is under genuine threat for the first time in years.
He recently admitted that Brazil’s disappointingly early World Cup exit took a toll on him, while the protracted contract saga may have proved an unwelcome distraction.

The forward, who was voted the Ballon d’Or runner-up in 2024, has been booed and whistled on several occasions so far this season by the Bernabéu crowd. However, he the fans did show their support when he received a red card in the win over Villarreal.
After the match, he posted on Instagram: “The joy continues. My apologies to my team and the fans.”

Vinícius Jr could miss Madrid’s most important match of the season so far. / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesVinícius Jr received a straight red card on Saturday in one of the more unusual moments of the season so far.

The forward, who came off the bench in the match, thought he had put Madrid 2–0 up in the second half after tapping home Jude Bellingham’s pass, only to have his goal ruled out and replaced with a straight red after a VAR review for pulling Saliba’s hair in the build-up.

The direct red means Vinícius could miss several matches, pending the referee’s report. La Liga rules state that red cards from situations in which there was no genuine attempt to win the ball will bring an automatic suspension of two matches. Furthermore, the VAR audio described the incident as “violent conduct,” adding to the likelihood that the forward will be out for more than one game.
If suspended for more than just one match, he will miss the home game against Sevilla (Sun, Oct. 18) and the Clásico against Barcelona at Camp Nou (Sun, Oct. 25).

ftbpro_01m4wx37bshe.title: Lisandro Martinez’s Rant Followed Up by Explicit Post From Man Utd Teammate
ftbpro_01m4wx37bshe.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:00 AM EDTAmad Diallo had his own say on an interesting night. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesIf Manchester United weren’t already reeling from Lisandro Martínez’s blunt criticism of the club’s transfer business this summer, Amad Diallo didn’t exactly quell the tension by taking to social media to lament what he called a “f---ing disgrace.”

It’s curious that this fallout has come after an improved performance. United created a glut of chances after tumbling behind early to Atlético Madrid and could comfortably have been level if not ahead before Leny Yoro’s harsh second-half red card.

Michael Carrick had taken the bold approach of reshuffling his entire team, sending Bruno Fernandes into an unfamiliar right wing position while starting all three of the club’s midfield summer signings together for the first team. “We feel the game was there for us,” the manager fairly admitted, “so we could and should have got more from it.”

Yet, the green shoots have been bulldozed by Martínez’s scathing attack on United’s recent recruitment. The center back “expected more” than three first-team midfield additions without explicitly naming the other areas in need of reinforcement. One might argue that his area of the pitch ought to fall into that bracket of consideration.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Martínez had plenty to say to whichever broadcaster was willing to hand him a microphone, yet his teammate Amad claimed: “I have no words,” on a Snapchat post. The winger had managed to find some vocabularly before that line, writing: “F---ing disgrace.”

It’s unclear what particular aspect of last night Amad found so disgraceful; United’s 2–0 defeat, the referee’s decision to send off Yoro, Martínez’s comments, Jason Wilcox’s transfer business, Bryan Mbeumo’s finishing.
Whatever the target of Amad’s frustration, the willingness of United’s players to vent in public inspired the ire of the club’s all-time top scorer.

Wayne Rooney wasn’t impressed. / Maciej Rogowski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesWhile Wayne Rooney is naturally inclined to encourage any response from a player which isn’t bland, media-trained drivel, United’s former forward wasn’t impressed with the timing or content of Martínez’s diatribe.

“Something like that will rip that dressing room apart,” Rooney warned during his duty as an Amazon Prime Video pundit. “That interview is not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute. That’s going to bring a greater noise around it; the players are not happy, they’re not settled, they don’t trust in their teammates. That’s not going to help at all.”
Rooney added, “I think he has maybe gone a bit too far. That’s for the manager, and that should really stay internal.”

Martínez’s outburst may have proved that “he cares”—which would seem to be a low bar for praise—and Rooney accepted that there was some justification to his frustrations: “I think in some ways he is right in terms of the club needs to invest more, at the top end of the pitch and in defense as well.”
Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans

Yet, Rooney argued that Martínez is in no position to start making public demands given his recent displays on the pitch. “He is probably one of the players who is out the door through his performance. His performances haven’t been good enough,” the retired striker scoffed.
“Bruno [Fernandes] is the only one who has any right to come out and say anything like that as captain. And even then it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen.

“It looks like that was a bit of an agenda; he’s wanted to say that, because that doesn’t mirror the performance,” Rooney concluded. “I thought the performance was better. It’s a bit disrespectful to his teammates as well. He is disrespecting his teammates because he’s saying the team isn’t good enough.”

ftbpro_01m4wy2vqz9s.title: How Liverpool ‘Failed’ in Attempt to ‘Divert’ Anthony Gordon From Barcelona
ftbpro_01m4wy2vqz9s.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer8:30 AM EDTBradley Barcola cost almost twice as much as Anthony Gordon. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images (Barcola), Ahmet Okatali/Anadolu/Getty Images (Gordon)In an ideal world, Liverpool might have signed Anthony Gordon during the summer transfer window, instead of getting close to matching their transfer record to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman, whose $163 million fee was only marginally less than the $168 million the Reds agreed to pay for Alexander Isak, is still yet to produce in a Liverpool shirt. He’s six matches in and the dual-threat winger who put down 42 goals and assists for Paris Saint-Germain in 2024–25 so far has zero for his new club. It’s still early days, but a transfer fee that demands more straight off the bat.
Right now, Barcola is threatening become another Florian Wirtz—even without Mohamed Salah stealing focus the German has only one assist and no goals to his name this season.
It might have been different for Liverpool, given interest was held in Gordon.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Unlike Barcola, Gordon is a dual-threat winger who is flying right now. It’s six goals and assists in nine appearances since joining Barcelona—for a new club in a new league, not unlike Barcola’s circumstances, but with very different results at this stage. He also got four goal contributions in three England appearances during the international window. Barcola had none for France.

Andoni Iraola is backing his horse. “Sometimes we have to focus not just on the numbers,” the Liverpool manager said on Tuesday. Rightly or wrongly, he has “100% trust” in both Barcola and Wirtz. “Bradley and Florian have had good games, bad games this season, but we know their level, and we are sure they’ll give us good performances.”
Data from FotMob: La Liga, Premier League, Champions League, Nations League, Carabao Cup

Barcelona acted quickly and efficiently. / Adria Puig/Anadolu/Getty ImagesA serious Liverpool pursuit would have made a lot of sense. Gordon was born and raised in the city, into a Liverpool-supporting family. He made his professional breakthrough with rival club Everton, but he’d been with the Reds for five years before that as a young child. Liverpool needed someone to replace Salah and Gordon wanted a step up from Newcastle United.

Barcelona were quickly on the scene, sensing an opportunity for a more financially sensible investment than simply triggering the option to buy in Marcus Rashford’s loan agreement. The Catalans announced on May 29 that Gordon would be signed, only five days after the Premier League and La Liga seasons finished. According to The Times, “efforts” were made by Liverpool to “divert” the 25-year-old—only 19 months older than Barcola—from his path to Camp Nou. But the Reds were “late to the party” and those attempts obviously failed.

Barcelona’s total outlay for Gordon could just eclipse $93 million if conditional add-ons are hit. All add-ons for Barcola make his transfer to Liverpool worth $163 million. Only one of them is performing right now and there is no question at this stage which club got the better deal.

The Champions League is sometimes an easier transition. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesBarcola might find over the next few games that the Champions League will be kinder to him than the Premier League. Not only is it a less physically intense and more technical stage, the caliber of opposition will be an opportunity to get into gear and build confidence.

Liverpool travel to Austria to meet LASK on Wednesday, one of the league phase’s least threatening teams. Next week, it’s Villarreal at Anfield—only seven teams in La Liga have conceded more goals (13) through seven domestic matches so far this season.

Conversely, Liverpool’s next Premier League fixture is away against Brentford, fourth in the standings and allowing only one more than the joint-best defensive record in the division. Brighton & Hove Albion are one of the five teams with that superior record and visit Anfield on Oct. 25. The Seagulls embarrassed Arsenal last month and sit third.
After a Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea on Oct. 28, in which there could be plenty of goals, Liverpool start November by hosting Arsenal, the defending champions.

ftbpro_01m4wy46mv8t.title: ‘A Bit of a Fluke’—Lamine Yamal Teased About Stunning Rabona Skill
ftbpro_01m4wy46mv8t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath10:30 AM EDTLamine Yamal dazzled against Galatasaray. /  BSR Agency/Getty ImagesRodri joked that Lamine Yamal’s viral skill in the 4–1 Champions League win over Galatasaray on Tuesday night was “a fluke.”
Barcelona made it 10 wins from 10 at the start of 2026–27, with victory over the Turkish giants in Istanbul in the second gameweek in the Champions League.
Hansi Flick’s side recovered from a goal down to take home three points on the road, with Yamal once again dominating the headlines after the match.

The 19-year-old did not score, but was named player of the match after assisting twice—the second of which came after a sublime piece of skill that captured attentions around the globe. Spanish commentary described the action as a “magic trick,” while AS later dubbed the move the “304 dribble”—in homage to the neighborhood where the player grew up.

Darting into the box, Yamal appeared to pull off a rabona-cum-croqueta in one fluid motion before teeing up Anthony Gordon to finish. However, replays show that Barça’s No. 10 gets slightly fortunate with a deflection back off the defender.
Speaking after the match, Yamal’s teammate Rodri teased the forward about his trickery, questioning how intentional the aesthetically pleasing move actually was.
“We were saying that he got the ball a little bit on the rebound, we don't know if it was intentional or not, a bit of a fluke,” Rodri laughed.
“But well, in the end I always say, you have to go for it. He always has that intention of wanting to get past his man and he created the second one.”

Speaking to CBS Sports Golazo, Yamal explained his thinking with the unconventional maneuver: “Lately I’ve noticed that when I get out wide, the defenders dive to the ground, and I saw an opportunity and thought I could take it. It’s more beautiful and it was effective.
“I always try to use feints to create space because the defenders try to close down.”
Meanwhile, Fermín López hailed the forward for his other assist on the night, saying: “The cross he gives me is half a goal. Lamine is the best in the world.”

Lamine Yamal made history on Tuesday. / Ferda Demir/Getty ImagesWith his brace of assists against Galatasaray on Tuesday, Yamal went past 25 goal contributions in the Champions League—making him the youngest-ever player to achieve the milestone, according to Transfermarkt.
At 19 years and 92 days, Yamal is more than a year younger than Kylian Mbappé who was 20 years and 206 days when he hit 25 goals and assists.
Manchester City’s Erling Haaland is the third-youngest player in the competition’s history to reach 25 goal contributions at 21 years and 139 days.

ftbpro_01m4x0bk340d.title: ‘Watch the First Minute’—Mourinho Delivers Familiar Criticism As Narrative Builds
ftbpro_01m4x0bk340d.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath10:00 AM EDTJosé Mourinho is keeping the spotlight on refereeing decisions. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images“I invite you all to watch the first minute against Villarreal. Just one minute is enough.”

That was José Mourinho’s unusual request to the gathered journalists during an evasive and enigmatic pre-match press conference ahead of Real Madrid’s Champions League clash against Roma this Wednesday.
Asked about the refereeing decisions in the 1–0 win over Villarreal at the weekend, Mourinho instead decided to assign homework to those giving him questions.
“For those who know, the first minute is enough,” Mourinho added.
So what was the incident that left the manager so upset?
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kylian Mbappé was called offside after little more than a minute. /  Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesMourinho’s Madrid saw out a 1–0 win at the Bernabéu on Saturday, bouncing back from defeat to rivals Atlético Madrid prior to the international break.

Summer signing Yan Diomande scored the only goal of the game early into the second half, while Vinícius Júnior had a strike ruled out for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba—an action that earned him a straight red card, after a VAR review.
The sending off on 73 minutes was the big talking point post-match, but Mourinho did not engage in discussions about the red, instead directing reporters to the very first minute of the game.

Notably, the only refereeing intervention in the very early stages of the game is a marginal offside call against Kylian Mbappé at 1 minute and 4 seconds in, after the forward is played through by Federico Valverde. Spanish outlet MARCA claims to have confirmed that this is the incident Mourinho was referencing, with the manager seemingly incensed that the linesman raised his flag early rather than letting play run and waiting for the automated review.

Mourinho is leading the conspiracy charge.  / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesMourinho’s highlighting of one incidental, long-forgotten decision is part of a clear strategy from the manager to play into a narrative of potential bias against Real Madrid.
It’s a familiar playbook from Mourinho, who often works hard to instil an ‘us against the world’ mentality in the clubs he manages.

By drawing attention to one debatable incident in the first minute, Mourinho is hoping fans and media will infer a wider meaning, sowing seeds of doubt about refereeing neutrality—a hot-button topic among many Madrid fans given the ongoing Negreira case.

This is not the first time this season, Mourinho has put the match officials in the spot light. Prior to the match against Elche in September, the 63-year-old ended a press conference with the remark: “No questions about the penalties? Strange, no?”
Then, following the Madrid derby defeat, he brought printouts of contentious decisions to the press conference and lambasted referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias’ performance.
"We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," Mourinho said as he held up the images to the media.
Later asked if Madrid could still challenge for the title, he responded: “If ‘they’ leave us in peace, and let us compete on an even playing field, there’s a long way left.”

ftbpro_01m4x3r6hpwq.title: ‘Treble Is Possible’—Lamine Yamal Doesn’t Think 10 Out of 10 Barcelona Can Be Stopped
ftbpro_01m4x3r6hpwq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:18 PM EDTBarcelona are looking imperious. /  Ferda Demir/Getty Images“It’s always possible. We’re the best team in the world.”

That was Lamine Yamal’s emphatic response when asked by CBS Sports analyst Thierry Henry whether the treble is a target this season. Based on the evidence of the first two months of 2026–27, it is more than just possible.
Barcelona have started the season on fire, with Tuesday night’s 4–1 victory over Turkish champions Galatasaray making it 10 wins from 10.
Yamal bagged two assists in Istanbul—including one after a viral rabona skill—as Barça continued to score freely even in the absence of injured top scorer Raphinha.
Across all games in La Liga and the Champions League, Barcelona—powered by an unstoppable forward line—have bagged 43 goals (an average of 4.3 per game) and conceded just nine.
As a result, Hansi Flick’s side sits top of both La Liga and the Champions League’s League Phase, laying down a marker as the team to beat in Europe this year.

The additions of Rodri and Anthony Gordon this summer have bolstered an already impressive roster, while the shift of Raphinha to center forward has proved a masterstroke—albeit an enforced one.
Meanwhile, Yamal continues his ascendency to soccer greatness as the poster boy of a hugely talented generation of academy graduates that form the backbone of the team.
Barcelona’s lightning pace out of the blocks has not been matched by any club in 2026–27, with no other side in Europe’s top five divisions enjoying a 100% record across all competitions.

Barça also matched their own best-ever start to a La Liga campaign by making it eight wins from eight in the 3–0 win over Getafe on Saturday—a game in which they enjoyed an astonishing 82.7% possession.

Should Barcelona beat Real Betis on the road in their next league outing on Saturday, they will become only the second team in history to win their first nine La Liga matches of a season. Somewhat unsurprisingly, Real Madrid are the only club to have previously achieved the feat, doing so back in the 1968–69 season. No one has ever made it 10 in a row.

Though there is a long way still to go this season, Flick’s team will also be quietly keeping an eye on a whole host of La Liga records. It could even become the first club to enjoy an ‘invincible’ campaign since Athletic Club in 1929–30.

Barça have yet to face one of La Liga or Europe’s big boys this season. / Ferda Demir/Getty ImagesBarcelona have been unstoppable so far this season, but a busy month may determine whether they are simply an in-form team or a truly great one.
As yet, Barça have not faced any of last season’s top six in La Liga—a fact which changes this Saturday, with the trip to La Cartuja.
Betis are a tricky test for any visiting team, with José Mourinho’s Real Madrid already suffering defeat against Manuel Pellegrini’s charges this season.
