That match comes just three days before the Champions League trip to holders Paris Saint-Germain on Oct. 20.
The big games continue to come thick and fast with the first Clásico of the season following the next weekend, while a visit to Atlético Madrid’s Metropolitano is also on the horizon.

ftbpro_01m4x4w262pf.title: ‘What They Have Done’—PSG Boss Delivers Unsurprising Reaction to Man City Verdict
ftbpro_01m4x4w262pf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer9:30 AM EDTLuis Enrique has come to bat for Pep Guardiola. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIf Manchester City could count on support from any club at this time, it was always likely to be Paris Saint-Germain and their manager Luis Enrique.

In 2011, PSG were the subject of a similar takeover. For Abu Dhabi, swap in Qatar. Both clubs were fined by UEFA back in 2014 over breaches of financial rules—the reason City fans have spent more than a decade booing and jeering the Champions League anthem.

In Enrique, PSG also have a manager who has been close friends with Pep Guardiola for a long time. Although they lined up on opposite sides of the Clásico divide in the early 1990s, the pair were colleagues on Spain’s Olympic roster on home soil in 1992.

They graduated to the senior national team around the same time and later became club colleagues in 1996 when Enrique controversially swapped Real Madrid for Barcelona as an early beneficiary of the new Bosman ruling. Enrique managed Barcelona B when Guardiola was in charge of the first team and took over the main job himself from 2014 onwards.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Enrique was naturally asked for his opinion on the Premier League’s guilty verdict hanging over Manchester City before the teams meet on the field in the Champions League on Wednesday—Guardiola is expected to attend for the first time since stepping down as manager in May.
The PSG boss expressed “hope” that “everything works out well” for this week’s opponent.

Luis Enrique values the soccer his friend had Man City play. / QUIQUE GARCIA/AFP/Getty ImagesEnrique is seemingly willing to look past almost a decade of financial cheating that built a platform from which the club later dominated English soccer and even conquered Europe, because of the way his friend set up a team of expensively assembled stars to play.
As a minimum, he doesn’t want to see trophies being stripped.

“We just have to wait and see what the final decision will be,” he said. “I hope everything works out well for Manchester City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win on the pitch all the trophies they have won. Now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide.”
City have lodged an appeal against the guilty verdict reached by an independent panel following a multi-year Premier League investigation relating to the period 2009–2018.
"The first thing that you hear, it is a surprise, but we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision,” Enrique admitted. “The authorities are responsible for making these decisions.

“But, speaking only about football, they deserved those trophies. I love their football. Beyond that, we have to wait for the decision. The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction. But we have to wait.”

Man City have to keep playing as if things were normal. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesThe soccer calendar doesn’t stop because Manchester City have been found guilty of cheating the system to artificially inflate spending power but won’t be hit with formal sanctions until the appeal process is concluded. Other appeals to higher bodies could follow if, come late January when the initial appeal verdict is due, City are still found guilty.
City could face wide-ranging punishments for years of orchestrated cheating, from a huge fine, to both retrospective and forward-looking points deductions.
In the meantime, they have to keep playing, not knowing what or when the end result will be—or how any sanction might be applied if it comes to that point.
City emerged as rampant victors over Liverpool in the Premier League last weekend, a scene dominated by joyous defiance from the fans revelling in the role of pantomime villain.

“We are very good at focusing on our work and being happy whenever we come to work. Our minds are only on that. These are the things we can control and that we have always enjoyed doing so much,” Rúben Dias said this week. “We have complete confidence in the club.”

ftbpro_01m4x66q22wc.title: ‘You Know What I Like’—Thierry Henry Can’t Get Enough of USMNT’s Next Superstar
ftbpro_01m4x66q22wc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:00 AM EDTThierry Henry was impressed by the USMNT’s recent window. / Ercin Erturk/Anadolu/Getty ImagesThierry Henry was full of praise for U.S. men’s national team’s young gem Cavan Sullivan, singling out the same quality which so enamored the teenager to Mauricio Pochettino.

Sullivan had an international break to savor. The Philadelphia Union forward made his senior debut, turned 17 and became the youngest scorer in the history of the program this fall. Pochettino doesn’t tend to single out individuals but made an exception to hail the grit, rather than the glitz, Sullivan had demonstrated. Henry was similarly impressed.

“You know what I like, is his demeanor, his attitude,” Henry gushed on CBS Golazo this week. “Swagger,” was another trait offered up by presenter Kate Abdo which the former Arsenal and Barcelona forward accepted.
“He plays, he goes about it, he will put his foot in,” Henry added. “He also has an eye for a pass or for a goal. But he will not back down for anyone, although he’s young.”

Sullivan’s star is on the rise. Each game seems to bring a new record for the royally in-form teen, who has directly contributed to at least one goal in each of his previous seven club appearances. Yet, Henry’s expectations haven’t been sated: “I think he can do even more.”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
To be the future you must rewrite history. pic.twitter.com/MID0hojIEy

Henry also shifted the spotlight toward the manager who called up Sullivan and a hoard of other youngsters. “You have to a lot of credit to Pochettino: He allowed those guys to come,” the retired France international pointed out.

Sullivan was one of eight teenagers handed his debut during fall’s four friendlies, with six of that contingent plying their trade in Major League Soccer. Unlike some previous USMNT managers who have prioritized players with minimal European experience above any domestic action, Pochettino has wholeheartedly embraced home-based talent.
“It will be good for the MLS, because I think some of the guys coming from the MLS were not looked at so much, some times before,” Henry pointed out. “And now that’s not the case.

“Sometimes, I feel that I believe more—more, more, much more—in the talent of the players here in the USA than people that talk in the [U.S.] media,” Pochettino claimed earlier this month. “Because I think it’s so important to translate that you really trust. And then because we [have] expertise, that is why we are here, don’t worry that we are going to make the best decision.
“It’s so important that the people really trust in the process, trust in our decisions, but trust in the players and respect the players.”

Pochettino has an admirer in Henry, although his faith isn’t concrete just yet. “It looks like it can be a bright future,” the Premier League icon concluded, “but it remains to be seen if it can carry on.”

ftbpro_01m4xat711ph.title: ‘Remote in the Extreme’—Decision Made on Lisandro Martinez’s Man Utd Future
ftbpro_01m4xat711ph.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff12:30 PM EDTLisandro Martínez has stunned the Man Utd community. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesLisandro Martínez may have dug his own grave at Manchester United with explosive comments after Tuesday’s Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid that openly questioned the club’s senior management and the ability of many of his teammates.

“I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox],” he said during Prime Video’s postgame broadcast, a clear criticism of the summer’s recruitment. “As players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.
“Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team. It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result.
“Changing, changing, changing manager? What about other areas? I can’t say more. It’s easy to blame the coach, it’s easy to blame the players, but what about other areas?”
That last comment was made with his index finger pointing up, as if to gesture to senior bosses. He doubled down shortly afterwards when speaking to CBS.

According to Sky Sports, “at least one other player” challenged Martínez as the squad boarded their flight back to Manchester. “Anger and bemusement” is said to be the reaction both from the club hierarchy and his colleagues in the locker room. Other players have unsurprisingly not taken the defender’s dim public assessment of their ability very well.

Amad Diallo made an ambiguous Snapchat post after the game: “I have no words. F---ing disgrace.” It’s not completely clear what it was in reference to. But Youri Tielemans appeared on the Prime Video broadcast after Martínez, was asked for his opinion and refused to comment.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Wayne Rooney, booked as a Prime Video analyst, warned, “Something like that will rip that dressing room apart.” The Old Trafford legend added: “It looks like that was a bit of an agenda [from Martínez] … he’s wanted to say that, because that doesn’t mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better. It’s a bit disrespectful to his teammates as well. He is disrespecting his teammates because he’s saying the team isn’t good enough.”

Rooney suggested that Martínez’s own poor performances don’t give him the status or position to make the comments he did. “Bruno [Fernandes] is the only one who has any right to come out and say anything like that as captain. Even then, it should be behind closed doors.”

Martínez was keen to follow Cristian Romero to Spain. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesMartínez was reportedly keen on leaving Manchester United during the 2026 summer transfer window, ironically with Atlético Madrid his preferred destination after watching Argentina colleague Cristian Romero make the same move. He may now get his wish to depart, with the decision on whether to offer a new contract potentially made easier.

United could have viewed it as an opportunity in the summer to cash in and raise further funds to reinvest in the squad, but Sky Sports writes that “no suitable bid” ever arrived. That doesn’t seem surprising considering Martínez managed only 110 appearances in his first four seasons at Old Trafford because of injuries—some players could hit that number in two.

Now, the former Ajax center back, so desperate to join United in 2022 that he publicly called the Dutch club’s technical director a “f---ing nobody” for trying to keep him in Amsterdam, has entered the final year of his contract. United have a clause to push that to 2028, but the possibility of being released next summer seems real. The Athletic writes, “The prospect of him extending terms in the wake of his interviews is remote in the extreme.”
The opportunity may be there to sell in January and it remains to be seen what will unfold.

Matthijs de Ligt is back from injury. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIt’s hard to envisage how Michael Carrick could pick Martínez for the next game, a challenging Premier League clash at the home of fierce rivals Leeds United, as if nothing has happened.
Ruben Amorim went up against Wilcox in the days before he was fired last January.

The aforementioned report from The Athletic cites club sources to suggest it is “inevitable that Martínez will be fined” for his outburst. Last season, Chelsea internally suspended Enzo Fernández as punishment for openly flirting with a transfer to Real Madrid. Whether any response needs to be so formal is up for debate.

But the other side of the coin is that United still need Martínez. Due to a transfer strategy that has seen the club target forwards and then midfielders in successive summers in 2025 and 2026 respectively, no true defenders have been recruited since 2024. In that respect, much has been made about starting this season with the same back four as began 2022–23 four years ago.

If Martínez is left out of the team as punishment—even just for one match—it makes an already challenging situation more difficult. Luke Shaw and Noussair Mazraoui are both injured, meaning that left back has to be covered in other ways. Center back Ayden Heaven, the first point of cover for Martínez, started on the left in Madrid.

If Heaven has to move inside, it forces Diogo Dalot across from right back and takes Leny Yoro out of the middle—the young Frenchman had a good game against Atlético until a harsh red card—to cover there. Harry Maguire cannot play every match, with care being taken to manage his physical load, and Yoro is suspended for the next Champions League fixture.

ftbpro_01m4xbwe1dy3.title: Virgil van Dijk Joins Illustrious Liverpool Group After Champions League Rout
ftbpro_01m4xbwe1dy3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell4:30 PM EDTVirgil van Dijk is furthering his legacy in a red shirt. / Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/DeFodi/Getty ImagesLiverpool center back Virgil van Dijk donned the captain’s armband for the 200th time when the Reds breezed past LASK on Wednesday.

The Dutchman, who was appointed club captain in July 2023, joined the exclusive company of only seven other Reds to reach the impressive milestone. Van Dijk now boasts the eighth-most games as Liverpool captain in club history.

Of course, Steven Gerrard leads the way; it’s hard to see another player touching his 470 games as captain any time soon, especially now that the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold, Mohamed Salah and Ibrahima Konaté have all left Merseyside.
Ron Yeats is the only other player to wear the armband for over 400 games. Emlyn Hughes comes in at third with 335 games, followed by Donald McKinlay, Jordan Henderson, Alex Raisbeck and Sami Hyypia.
Van Dijk will inevitably pass Hyypia in the coming weeks; the center back only needs five more appearances to claim sole possession of seventh place.

Whether he gets the chance to continue his ascent remains uncertain. Van Dijk’s contract with Liverpool expires at the end of the season, and he has yet to ink an extension. Recent reports claim the Reds have no intention of offering the 35-year-old a new deal, a stance that was perhaps strengthened after his performance against LASK.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Virgil van Dijk was at the scene of the crime for Liverpool. / Jasmin Walter/UEFA/Getty ImagesMaking his 200th appearance as club captain should have been a night to celebrate for Van Dijk. After all, Andoni Iraola’s men walked away with a thumping 6–3 win over LASK to keep their early league phase record unblemished this season.
Bradley Barcola bagged a hat-trick, Florian Wirtz put in a redemptive performance and even the young Lewis Koumas tallied a goal and an assist. But Van Dijk had another night to forget.
The Dutchman started the game on the bench, relishing in some much-needed rest before he came in for Jérémy Jacquet in the 62nd minute. By the 77th minute, LASK had three goals to their name.

It’s unfair and rather harsh to put all the blame on Van Dijk; Liverpool looked wildly uninterested in defending once they harnessed such a massive lead. But leisurely strolls back, lackadaisical positioning and poor awareness put the spotlight on the Liverpool skipper for all the wrong reasons.

The Reds have now conceded six goals in their last two matches, and only have three clean sheets to their name in 2026–27. If the club wants to hoist silverware in Iraola’s debut campaign, than it needs much, much more from its leader.

ftbpro_01m4xd63vtq0.title: Ranking the Best and Worst Signings Made by Jason Wilcox at Man Utd
ftbpro_01m4xd63vtq0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTJason Wilcox has signed eight senior players for Man Utd.  / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images (Mbeumo, Tielemans), Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty Images (Wilcox)Jason Wilcox was first handed Manchester United’s company credit card in June 2025, when he was promoted from technical director to director of football, and has since made eight additions to the club’s first-team roster.
But, shortly after the conclusion of his second summer transfer window, the 55-year-old’s competence and ambition have been called into question.

Following yet another poor result for the Red Devils at the beginning of the 2026–27 season, this time at the hands of Atlético Madrid in the Champions League, center back Lisandro Martínez launched a remarkable postgame rant, during which he criticized Wilcox and his recruitment.

“I expect more from our technical director [Wilcox],” Martínez fumed. “I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”
With that in mind, here’s an assessment—and ranking—of Wilcox’s senior signings since becoming United’s director of football.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Karl Darlow was signed for zilch. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesSigning second-choice goalkeepers is rarely glamorous—and Karl Darlow’s acquisition proved no different. After growing weary of André Onana and Altay Bayındır’s error-laden performances, United have been forced to reshuffle their goalkeeping department, and Darlow was signed as backup on a free transfer during the most recent transfer window. So far, the Wales international has donned the gloves for just one competitive appearance, hardly covering himself in glory as United slumped to a dismal 3–2 defeat at home to Brighton & Hove Albion. The 36-year-old will be limited to outings in the domestic cups, meaning United supporters are unlikely to see much of him before his contract expires in 2028.

Andrey Santos was signed to bolster a weak midfield. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesIt’s still early days for Andrey Santos, who only arrived for $64.3 million in July, but the early signs suggest he’s likely to be fourth-choice in United’s new-look midfield. Santos has started just three competitive appearances since moving to Manchester and appears set to fulfil a peripheral role similar to that endured at former club Chelsea. The 22-year-old is an all-rounder capable of making a difference for United, adding depth and potential to Michael Carrick’s roster, but whether he can live up to his billing with inconsistent minutes remains to be seen. Right now, it’s just too early to tell how his United career will pan out.

Youri Tielemans has struggled at Old Trafford thus far. / Gokhan Taner/PS Images/MB Media/Getty ImagesYouri Tielemans was an opportunistic and clever addition. For just $47 million, United were signing a midfielder with Premier League experience, technical craft and at least several years remaining at the top level. The Belgian, who was tipped by many as the best value-for-money signing of last summer, has made an unconvincing start to his United career, however, with his lack of mobility and physicality hardly complementing the skillset of Kobbie Mainoo. Tielemans needs more opportunities to adapt at Old Trafford, but it’s already clear that United will struggle if they continue to partner him with Mainoo in the double pivot. Perhaps that was an oversight when United signed Tielemans, but the 29-year-old should still come good over the coming weeks and months.

Injuries have hampered Benjamin Šeško. / Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesWilcox entered his first summer in charge with one mission: completely reinvent an underperforming United offense. One key position that required strengthening was center forward, with the club willing to gamble on  Slovenian talent Benjamin Šeško. Having seen Rasmus Højlund and Joshua Zirkzee stumble before him, the pressure was on Šeško to hit the ground running. While his debut season in England was hardly flawless—Šeško took time to settle and was repeatedly hindered by injury issues—there were plenty of encouraging signs. Scoring 11 goals in the Premier League, despite starting just 17 of his 30 appearances, helped ease initial concerns. Šeško’s speed, physicality and clutch strikes endeared him to the United crowd and hinted at his $89 million price tag being justified. Finding consistency and staying injury-free are the next steps for the 23-year-old en route to greatness.

United were willing to wait for Carlos Baleba. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesUnited were patient when it came to signing Carlos Baleba from Brighton. After being quoted over $135 million for the midfielder in the summer of 2025, the Red Devils declined those demands and instead waited until that valuation dropped. In the 2026 summer window, they finally got their man for $96 million. Baleba arrived at Old Trafford with an injury which delayed his debut until after the first international break of the season, but there’s no doubt he’s exactly the kind of midfielder Carrick needs to bolster his engine room. With endless stamina, enviable defensive intelligence and uncanny ability to regain possession no matter the circumstance, he should prove to be one of United’s most successful signings of recent years. While he can’t be properly assessed so early in his United career, Baleba could prove a transformative addition.

Matheus Cunha been moved around the forward line.  / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesMatheus Cunha’s debut season with United was not without its hiccups, especially considering the $85 million paid to Wolverhampton Wanderers, but the Brazilian ultimately made himself at home. One difficulty for Cunha was an ever-changing role. He started as a central striker, before dropping into an attacking midfield position. Once Carrick arrived to replace Ruben Amorim, he was shunted over to the left wing. Naturally, Cunha took time adapting, but there remained plenty of terrific individual performances littered throughout the season. He finished up with 10 goals and two assists in the Premier League and ended the term with three strikes in his final four outings. There still remain question marks over where Cunha fits in at United, especially when the club inevitably signs an orthodox left winger, but his recruitment has proven successful thus far.

Bryan Mbeumo has been a regular goal-getter for the Red Devils. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesSimilar to Cunha, things were not always straightforward for Bryan Mbeumo in year one at United. The $96 million winger endured some sticky spells, chiefly his final few months of the campaign, but still managed to be a regular provider of goals. As a right winger or center forward—the latter a position in which he played regularly under Carrick—Mbeumo’s tenacity and goal threat ensured he was a constant nuisance for opposition defenses. Whether he has merited such a large transfer fee is arguable and will be determined within the coming seasons, but he certainly improved United’s misfiring attack significantly. With 12 goals in his first year and a further three so far this term, Mbeumo has delivered what was promised following several impressive campaigns with Brentford.

Senne Lammens has proven an excellent addition. / Gokhan Taner/PS Images/MB Media/Getty ImagesThere were understandable fears when United chose to replace the mistake-prone Onana with Senne Lammens—someone who was unknown outside of Belgium, where he was representing Royal Antwerp. But United clearly saw something in the stopper and parted ways with $24.5 million late in Wilcox’s first summer window. Any fears over his competence were quickly allayed. Lammens proved an immediate upgrade on Onana as his self-assured, composed performances with both his hands and feet won him admirers. Instead of costing United points, their goalkeeper was actually starting to win them some. There are still elements of Lammens’s game that require cleaning up, notably his distribution under pressure, but there have been few better value signings made by United over the past decade—based on his first campaign at the club, at least.

ftbpro_01m4xfwafn25.title: Lisandro Martinez’s Man Utd Future ‘in Doubt’ After Explosive Rant
ftbpro_01m4xfwafn25.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 14, 2026Lisandro Martínez’s time at Manchester United could be nearing its end.  / Marc Atkins/Getty Images Following a spectacular, all-out attack on Manchester United’s board and overall recruitment strategy, Lisandro Martínez’s future at Old Trafford is very much in doubt.
The Argentine center back held nothing back in a spectacular rant following United’s 2–0 defeat against Atlético Madrid that condemned the Red Devils to a five-game winless stretch.

According to The Athletic, Martínez’s outburst is almost guaranteed to earn him a significant fine, but the long-term ramifications of a palpably fractured relationship between the player and the board could be more severe.
The 28-year-old’s contract runs until the end of the current season and United have an option to extend it for a further year.

Sky Sports state there is anger towards Martínez from those upstairs at Old Trafford, who are now considering his future at the club. ESPN, meanwhile, add that club officials have discussed the situation and will deliver a verdict soon.

Martínez joined United in 2022 and between injuries, collective underperformance and other factors, his tenure at the club has been a rollercoaster. Still, coming off a brilliant 2026 World Cup performance for Argentina, the tenacious defender wouldn’t be short of suitors if he hits the open market.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Milan manager Ruben Amorim could make a push to reunite with Lisandro Martínez.  / Claudio Villa/AC Milan/Getty ImagesGiven his age, contract situation and clear fractured relationship with his current club, teams likely won’t need to break the bank for Martínez, opening the door for more economically handicapped clubs pursue his signature. Enter Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Reports over the summer suggested the Portuguese manager was interested in recruiting Martínez to the Rossoneri. Amorim knows Martínez from his time with United, which ended soon after the manager also called out the club’s lack of investment.
Martínez has familiarity playing in Amorim’s trademark three center back system. Plus, the Milan boss also deployed him as a defensive midfielder at certain times due to his quality on the ball.

Milan might not be the juggernaut they were during their glory years, but they remain an attractive destination, and Amorim pushing to reunite with his former center back could help the club in their pursuit.

Barcelona are exploring the center back market to bring competition for Gerard Martín.  / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Although they’ve explored the market, Barcelona haven’t signed a left-footed center back since Iñigo Martínez left the club in the summer of 2025. Martínez could be the man that finally ends their search.

Overall, Martínez fits the profile of a Barcelona center back. He’s a fantastic passer in the build-up as he showed when he aced 117 of the 120 passes he attempted against Cabo Verde in the World Cup. His aggressiveness, speed and ability to defend in open space are also necessary traits to deliver in Hansi Flick’s bold defensive system.

Former left back Gerard Martín has been converted to full-time center back and has operated as Pau Cubarsí’s primary partner over the last two years. Although Martín has been solid overall, the left center back is arguably the one position Barcelona could use an upgrade at.

The club appears to think so as well and they’ve publicly revealed they are exploring the market for a left-footed center back. Martínez might not be a youngster anymore, but he’s still got plenty left in the tank and Cubarsí has always looked at his best with a veteran presence alongside him.

Lisandro Martínez (left) could join Argentina center back partner Cristian Romero in Madrid.  / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images By far the favorite to land Martínez is the team that handed United the defeat that led to his spectacular tirade. It’s almost too easy to envision Martínez wearing Atlético Madrid’s shirt, joining the large contingent of Argentine players at Diego Simeone’s side.
Reports state Martínez wanted to leave United for Atlético Madrid during the summer but no offer arrived that the Red Devils were willing to accept.

It’s not hard to see why the Metropolitano is an appealing landing spot for Martínez. There, he’d be reunited with close friend and Argentina center back partner Cristian Romero, plus a few other Argentina internationals.
Simeone’s tenacious, aggressive, impassioned and energetic style also mesh well with the center back’s personality and play style, making him a natural fit at Los Rojiblancos.

Atlético Madrid aren’t afraid to sign players despite having other alternatives at the position already in house and they have more than enough funds to make a deal happen. Replicating Argentina’s top center back pairing at the club level seems like something Simeone’s side would do.

ftbpro_01m4xh4t9cp2.title: Transfer Rumors: Man Utd’s €100 Million Bidding War; Real Madrid Hijack Yamal’s Dream Target

paragraphs: By SI FC StaffOct 14, 2026Aleksandar Pavlović (left) and Lamine Yamal headline today’s gossip. / F. Noever/FC Bayern/Getty Images (Pavlović), Yagiz Gurtug/PS Images/MB Media/Getty Images (Yamal)Sports Illustrated rounds up the latest transfer rumors and gossip from around the world.

ftbpro_01m4xmmc7tfp.title: Arsenal Handed Massive Boost for Bayern Munich Champions League Clash
ftbpro_01m4xmmc7tfp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell5:00 PM EDTMikel Arteta is surely breathing a sigh of relief. /  Julian Finney/Getty ImagesAfter Arsenal defeated Lille in the Champions League, the defending Premier League champions were given another reason to celebrate on Tuesday: Michael Olise was sent off for Bayern Munich.

The Frenchman saw red for the first time in his senior career, picking up two yellow cards in rapid succession during Bayern’s frustrating night in Norway. Olise knew the first caution was coming his way after a slight tug prevented Viking from breaking free in transition.

But he then threw the ball at Viking captain Zlatko Tripić, earning an immediate second yellow in the 74th minute. Bayern, who had gone ahead 3–2 just a few minutes prior, were suddenly down to 10 men and ultimately conceded a 90th-minute equalizer.

Vincent Kompany’s men had to settle for a point on the night, but bigger consequences loomed large. Olise is now suspended for Bayern’s next Champions League clash, which comes against Arsenal on Wednesday, Oct. 21.
It’s a nightmare scenario for the defending German champions, but a welcome turn of events for the Gunners.

Arsenal are an unstoppable force in the league phase. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesIf Eberechi Eze and Gabriel converted their penalties in May, Arsenal would finally have a Champions League title in their trophy cabinet. Instead, they just have a sensational run of form to their names.

The reigning English champions have won their last 14 league phase matches. Mikel Arteta’s side closed out the 2024–25 league phase with four consecutive wins, went perfect last season and now started 2026–27 off with two victories over Napoli and Lille.

One of Arsenal’s eight wins last campaign came against Bayern. The Gunners secured a decisive 3–1 win over the German giants at home, enacting some sweet revenge after Bayern eliminated Arsenal in the 2023–24 quarterfinals.

To make it 15-consecutive league phase wins, last season’s Champions League runners-up will have to get past a Bayern side that has one of the most formidable attacks in Europe. But so much of the team’s success comes from the vision and left foot of Olise, who will now be forced to play spectator.

It’s great news for Arteta’s men. They have not looked like their dominant selves from last season as of late, falling 3–0 to Brighton & Hove Albion before squeaking out a 2–1 win over Leeds United at the weekend. The team’s 3–0 win over Lille was also nowhere near as impressive as the scoreline suggests.

Harry Kane will be under more pressure to carry Bayern’s attack. / Carina Johansen/NTB/AFP/Getty ImagesThe last thing Bayern needed for such a marquee match with Arsenal was losing one of their best players. Olise is coming off a sensational sophomore season in which he recorded 22 goals and 26 assists in 52 appearances.

The 24-year-old then tallied a record-seven assists for France at this summer’s World Cup, earning himself a nomination for the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Olise kept up his scorching form in 2026–27, recording eight goals and three assists in nine appearances for Bayern.
Without his services, the pressure will be on Harry Kane and Co. to command the attack in his absence. The captain spoke out on Olise’s sending off, towing the line between frustration and diplomacy.

“He’ll have to take responsibility obviously, he’ll have to learn from it," Kane said after the game. “It’s a shame because obviously we have big games coming up in the Champions League now, and he’s going to be gutted to miss those games.
“But this is football. Sometimes mistakes can happen; it’s life.“

ftbpro_01m4xq7c79s9.title: MLS Decides Fate of Man City Sister Club After Financial Breaches
ftbpro_01m4xq7c79s9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 14, 2026New York City FC shares the same owners as Manchester City.        / Vincent Carchietta/Getty ImagesAlthough Manchester City were recently found guilty of breaching financial regulations, Major League Soccer confirmed that the sister club New York City FC won’t be investigated for potential breaches of their own.

The soccer world is still reeling after the Premier League confirmed Man City “sham,” finding them guilty of nearly all charges related to financial fair play regulation breaches between 2009 and 2018. Although City maintain their innocence, significant sanctions are expected to be levied on the club before the end of the campaign.

City was bought in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and in 2013, the holding company City Football Group was founded in an effort to add more teams to their portfolio. NYCFC became the first team to join City’s ownership group, before entering MLS as an expansion team in 2015.

Although both teams have separate executive boards, NYCFC chief financial officer Andrew Widdowson was City’s financial director during the entire period when the club broke the Premier League’s financial rules, via The Athletic.

With such glaring links to City, questions had emerged over whether or not NYCFC will be investigated by MLS for similar breaches. However, it appears the 2021 MLS Cup champions will escape unscathed from their sister club’s scandal.

MLS commissioner Don Garber praised City Football Group’s involvement in the league.  / Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images When asked about City’s guilty charges and any potential investigations the league could launch on NYCFC, MLS commissioner Don Garber not only denied that possibility but also praised City Football Group for their commitment to helping MLS grow.

“We’re fortunate we have owners in our league that own multiple teams throughout every league,” Garber said at the Front Office Sports Tuned In summit on Wednesday. “We have [Colorado Rapids owner] Stan Kroneke owning Arsenal, and we have owners that own teams in Spain, in Italy, throughout the rest of the world.

“MLS is looking at how owners act in accordance with our rules here in Major League Soccer. I will say that what NYCFC has done through their own ownership, the City Football Group and investing in our league, building a great team in NYCFC, building an MLS NEXT Pro stadium in New Jersey and obviously their stadium that will open up in Queens is something we’re thankful for and appreciative of.
A special visit from a legend of the game 🧠⚽️Pep Guardiola joined us for the Hudson River Derby this past weekend and spent some time talking to fans. pic.twitter.com/1zjyqL8LxL

“But we’re not in the business of looking at what our team owners do in other leagues, and frankly, I don’t think any league would view what other owners do when they have multiple investments throughout other sports.
“The concept of multiple-team ownership is something that we all live through, manage through, and we have our own governance as it relates to what their behavior is.”
New York Red Bulls, Inter Miami and Real Salt Lake are among other MLS franchises whose owners also have stakes in European soccer clubs.

City and their ownership group might be in the eye of the storm with potentially unprecedented sanctions looming on the horizon, but on the other side of the Atlantic Ocean, NYCFC appear safe from any scrutiny.

ftbpro_01m4xr8as9fg.title: Vinicius Junior Learns El Clasico Fate After La Liga Hands Out Red Card Ban
ftbpro_01m4xr8as9fg.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:30 PM EDTVinícius Júnior (center) will not return to La Liga action for over a month. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesReal Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior was handed a four-match ban for his red card against Villarreal, ruling the Brazil international out of a must-win Clásico for his side.

Vinícius Jr—and the entire Bernabéu—experienced a whirlwind two minutes in Saturday’s 1–0 win. The No. 7, who started the game on the bench, came on in the second half and scored his first goal for Real Madrid since late August.

The goal was soon chopped off after a VAR review showed Vinícius Jr pulling the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba. The 26-year-old then charged at the referee and had to be held back by his teammates before he headed down the tunnel in a fit of rage.
A direct red card for an action not involving the ball is already a two-match ban, and then Vinícius Jr’s reaction, deemed “aggressive,” tacked on another two games to his suspension.
Now the forward can only play spectator when Real Madrid face off with Barcelona for the first time this season, as well as three other opponents in the upcoming weeks.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Júnior (right center) is in a cycle of poor form and bad decisions. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesSunday, Oct. 18: Sevilla (H)Sunday, Oct. 25: Barcelona (A)Sunday, Nov. 1: Racing Santander (A)Saturday, Nov. 7: Valencia (A)Real Madrid will be forced to take on Sevilla this weekend without Vinícius Jr, as well as Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia.  The latter three matches will unfold away from home, where the team has struggled under José Mourinho this season.

Los Blancos’ two defeats came at Real Betis and at Atlético Madrid, and they barely squeaked out victories away at Espanyol and at Elche. The task of upending a perfect Barcelona side at the Camp Nou was already a steep challenge—and now without Vinícius Jr, the task is even tougher.

Mourinho’s men should be fine to get past a struggling Racing side and an even worse Valencia team, but by the time those matches roll around, they could already be nine points behind Barcelona if they lose El Clásico. The gap could be even larger if they drop points against the formidable Sevilla the week prior.

The silver lining is Vinícius Jr will be available for Champions League action. He got the nod against Roma on Wednesday and will likely return to the lineup when Real Madrid take on RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in Europe’s premier club competition before the November international break.

Vinícius Júnior is stuck in a cycle of poor form and bad decisions. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesA four-game ban keeps Vinícius Jr out of domestic action until after the November international window. The next time the Brazilian plays a La Liga fixture will come on Sunday, Nov. 22, when Real Madrid face off with Celta Viga.

It’s just the latest blunder in a nightmare 2026–27 for Vinícius Jr so far. The winger has scored just one goal in 10 appearances across all competitions—and that came against Real Sociedad back on Aug. 26.

The international break was no better for the struggling No. 7. Vinícius Jr’s only goal contribution in three matches for Brazil was a penalty gifted to him by Bruno Guimarães because he needed “confidence.”
The lack of production combined with such a needless red card intensifies the pressure on Vinícius Jr, who now must sit and watch the electrifying Yan Diomande try to make the left wing his home.

ftbpro_01m4xvg50hf0.title: Man City vs. PSG Player Ratings: Superstar Forwards Light Up Champions League Classic
ftbpro_01m4xvg50hf0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 14, 2026PSG edged an epic affair. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesParis Saint-Germain ran out 4–2 winners during an utterly breathless Champions League classic with Manchester City on Wednesday.

The Cityzens had reveled in their role as pantomime villains during an emphatic win over Liverpool at the weekend, but a first home match since their damning guilty verdict for breaching the Premier League’s financial rules proved far less enjoyable. PSG produced one of the most complete first-half performances in recent Champions League history and deservedly boasted a three-goal halftime lead at the Etihad Stadium.

An astonishing move which started by PSG’s corner flag culminated in Désiré Doué firing an exquisite opener into the bottom corner, and the Frenchman turned provider two minutes later as he teed up Ousmane Dembélé’s far-post header. Vitinha proceeded to sweep home a pinpoint finish from the edge of the box to widen the advantage.

City came roaring back after halftime, though, creating an abundance of opportunities as they sought to stage an incredible turnaround. Erling Haaland scored either side of Maghnes Akliouche’s strike from range, but profligacy and a shocking first-half display ultimately proved costly for the home team.

Despite Ferran Torres missing a late penalty, PSG still clinched a second-successive European victory following their demolition of Slovan Bratislava last month. But for City, a first competitive defeat under Enzo Maresca leaves them with just three points from their league phase campaign so far.

PSG were unplayable during the first half at the Etihad. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesThis was an otherworldly first-half performance from PSG as they tore the Premier League leaders to shreds on their own patch courtesy of some extraordinary attacking sequences. An emphatic reminder of why they remain the world’s best team.

City were pulled from pillar to post during a chastening 45 minutes. On every occasion, they pushed high up the field to press their visitors, who were bypassed with alarming ease and sent scuttling back toward their own goal with a sense of dread in the pit of their stomachs. Unfortunately for Enzo Maresca and his players, PSG were not in a merciful mood.
Each of their three goals were beautiful, with the first the pick of the bunch. An impeccable one-touch move from back to front eventually found Doué and, seconds later, the back of Donnarumma’s net.

The second was similarly well-worked as Doué, instead of firing another effort toward goal, dinked a delicate cross to Dembélé, who made no mistake from a tight angle as he nodded PSG further in front.

PSG’s third epitomized their swagger. Another awe-inspiring move ended up at the feet of Vitinha after Warren Zaïre-Emery’s audacious flick, and the midfielder calmly bent his shot into the near post to cap an electric spell.
It’s fair to say PSG’s first-half performance will live long in the memory.
City were well beaten on home soil. / Ryan Pierse/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—5.4: Bruised by his former employers. Caught out at the near post by Doué for PSG’s opener and then endured an embarrassing moment as he ultimately parried Akliouche’s shot into his own goal. At least earned some redemption by saving Ferran Torres’s spot kick.
RB: Abdukodir Khusanov—5.8: Doué outsmarted him repeatedly throughout the first half, but Khusanov improved after moving to center back.
CB: Rúben Dias—5.5: Among the City defenders completely incapable of stifling a fearsome PSG forward line. Withdrawn at the break.
CB: Marc Guéhi—5.5: An evening to forget for Guéhi as PSG’s attack ran riot.
LB: Joško Gvardiol—7.1: Coped relatively well with Maghnes Akliouche, yet found it much tougher to handle Achraf Hakimi’s overlapping runs.
CM: Elliot Anderson—6.7: Often outnumbered by PSG’s classy three-man midfield. Received more support once Ayyoub Bouaddi entered the fray.
CM: Enzo Fernández—7.5: Readily involved in the final third as he spurned a huge chance and crashed the woodwork.

ftbpro_01m4xvvf3n87.title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. Roma: Youngsters Rescue Jose Mourinho in Vintage Comeback
ftbpro_01m4xvvf3n87.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 14, 2026Substitutes Arda Güler (left) and Endrick had three goal involvements combined in the last 10 minutes.  / Filippo Monteforte/AFP/Getty ImagesReal Madrid overcame a two-goal deficit inside the last 10 minutes of the game to defeat Roma 4–3 in a simply remarkable, trademark Champions League comeback on Wednesday night.

Roma were on the front foot from the start, taking the game to a visiting Real Madrid side that looked outclassed in terms of energy, intensity and aggressiveness. After a couple of brilliant Thibaut Courtois saves, the hosts finally went ahead thanks to a long distance Marten de Roon strike that took a slight deflection 20 minutes in.

Donyell Malen was inches away from doubling the lead minutes later, but when Real Madrid looked at their worst, a poor clearance attempt left the ball bouncing for Kylian Mbappé to fire a rocket from distance to equalize just five minutes later.

But Los Blancos never looked like the better side, and they crumbled in the first 15 minutes of the second half. A costly Vinícius Júnior turnover led to Malen restoring Roma’s lead and then he bagged his brace with a calm finish that was initially waved off for offside.

Then came Jose Mourinho’s substitutions that completely changed the game. The introduction of Endrick and Carlos Espí revitalized Madrid’s attack, and inside the final 10 minutes, the pair scored in a matter of seconds to equalize. In stoppage time, it was Antonio Rüdiger who won from a corner to complete a simply incredible Real Madrid comeback.

In arguably the best game of the young season, Real Madrid pulled off a historic comeback to make it two wins on the bounce to start their Champions League campaign. The performance for much of the game was beyond worrying, but the 15-time European champions showed they’re still capable of producing miracles out of nowhere in their favorite competition.

Federico Valverde struggled significantly against Roma.  / Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty Images At what point will Real Madrid finally give up on deploying an Aurélien Tchouaméni–Federico Valverde midfield double pivot? There is plenty of evidence that suggests it just doesn’t work, and the midfield duo was once again lackluster on Wednesday night.

Make no mistake, Tchouaméni and Valverde are good players, but they don’t work together as a pairing. Neither is capable of controlling game through their passing, nor disciplined enough positionally to avoid Madrid from playing basketball games defined by transitions.

Against a Roma side that aggressively man-marks, having two midfielders that aren’t exactly press-resistant led to dangerous turnovers in build up. Halfway through the first half, Courtois and Madrid’s defenders opted to stop looking for their midfield duo and instead lobbed long balls up the pitch for the forwards to win. The midfield pairing finished the first half with just 33 completed passes combined—Courtois had more accurate passes (19) than Tchouaméni (17) and Valverde (16).

Real Madrid are simply unable to control games with this midfield duo. They also clearly lack an organizer capable of resisting press and conducting possessions from deep, something Bernardo Silva might be able to offer if Mourinho didn’t seem uninterested in giving him significant minutes.

There’s plenty of issues Real Madrid must fix, but it’s incredibly puzzling that as managers come and go, Valverde and Tchouaméni continue to start together in midfield. It’s an indictment on the club’s recruitment, but it’s also on the manager to change something that’s clearly not working.
As a consequence of Madrid’s uninspiring double pivot, Roma were the better team for much of the night, looking unthreatened defensively and capable of creating danger at any given moment.
Antonio Rüdiger (bottom) won the game for Real Madrid at the death.  / Paolo Bruno/Getty Images *Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Thibaut Courtois—6.4: The five-minute mark still hadn’t arrived, and Courtois had already produced two magnificent saves to deny the hosts from taking an early lead. Despite conceding three, he was vital in keeping his team in the game.

RB: Denzel Dumfries—5.7: Undisciplined in his marking of Paulo Dybala all game, allowing the Argentine time and space to manufacture Roma’s attacks. Caught out of position routinely in a dreadful evening for the Dutchman.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—6.2: After a solid start he was completely dominated by Malen in the second half.
CB: Antonio Rüdiger—7.4: Tried to jump forward to intercept passes and left plenty of open space behind him routinely. Nevertheless, all of it will be forgotten after he scored the dramatic winner.
LB: Marc Cucurella—6.3: Characteristically stout defensively but missed the clearest chance of the night, alone against the goalkeeper but dragging his shot wide.

DM: Federico Valverde—7.2: Spent much of the game just jogging around the middle of the park without making any notable contributions. His bursts of speed to try to win possession back high up the pitch were unsuccessful and left Los Blancos exposed in midfield.

ftbpro_01m4xxwc6wgr.title: Real Madrid Almost Make a Mess of Kylian Mbappe’s Historic Champions League Night
ftbpro_01m4xxwc6wgr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell6:00 PM EDTKylian Mbappé is writing his name in Champions League folklore. / Ivan Romano/Getty ImagesAnother dreadful, uninspired opening from Real Madrid on Wednesday evening was briefly forgotten when Kylian Mbappé rifled a sensational right-footed strike from distance into the back of the net.

The Frenchman burned his marker with a clever spin and then was headed toward goal as four players in red converged around him. Instead of taking on his defenders or dribbling into the box, Mbappé tried his luck from 25 yards out and saw his shot loop over the outstretched hand of Roma goalkeeper Pierluigi Gollini.

A deflection along the way helped the ball find its end target, but no one in white—least of all Mbappé—cared. It was the equalizer Real Madrid desperately needed after going down 1–0 to Roma at the Stadio Olimpico.

It was also a moment of magic Mbappé summoned to breathe life into a team wildly uninterested in maintaining possession, creating chances or tracking back. A team that looked wildly uninterested in playing at even half the level necessary to win a Champions League match away from home.

By the time the halftime whistle sounded, Mbappé’s strike was the only goal Real Madrid managed in a withering opening 45 minutes. Things went from lackluster to dire soon after the restart; the visitors were on the wrong end of a 3–1 scoreline before a vintage comeback fueled by José Mourinho’s substitutes saved the team from embarrassment.
It was hardly a victory to celebrate, considering just how poor the team played—again—but Mbappé walked away with plenty of accolades to celebrate his 100th Champions League appearance.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Kylian Mbappé is chasing Cristiano Ronaldo. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesMbappé has received his fair share of criticism ever since he made the move to Real Madrid—and rightfully so. For all the goals he scores, the team looks no closer to winning a major trophy than it did two seasons ago during his debut campaign.

But his production on Europe’s grandest stage is simply undeniable. At 27 years old, Mbappé is already in the pantheon of the greatest Champions League forwards. His goal against Roma was his 72nd in the competition, pushing him further up the goalscoring charts.
Cristiano Ronaldo is the greatest Champions League goalscorer of all time. / Marco Bertorello/AFP/Getty ImagesRank
In 100 appearances, Mbappé is now the fifth all-time leading goalscorer in Champions League history. He has more goals to his name than the likes of Raúl, Thierry Henry and Mohamed Salah.

To make the momentous night even sweeter, 27-year-old Mbappé also became the youngest player to reach a century of appearances in the competition. Lionel Messi previously held the record when he made his 100th appearance at 28 years and 84 days old.

It’s only a matter of time before Mbappé becomes the fourth player ever to score 100 goals in the Champions League, joining Cristiano Ronaldo, Messi and Robert Lewandowski in the exclusive club. It also feels like just a matter of time before the France international overtakes at least two of those names in the record books.

The elephant in the room is Mbappé’s failure to ever win the Champions League. He came to Real Madrid to fulfill that dream, a sure bet considering the club lifted the prestigious trophy five times in the last decade alone.
Except nothing has gone right at the biggest club in the world since his arrival, and Wednesday’s match was the perfect microcosm of the team’s biggest problems.

Vinícius Júnior was invisible yet again. / Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty ImagesIn the opening 45 minutes against Roma, Real Madrid managed a single shot on target—Mbappé’s goal. The visitors were either unimaginative with the ball or making the wrong decisions in the final third.

Mourinho’s double pivot of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde completed less passes than goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois in the first half. Marc Cucurella lost his head and pulled a strike wide instead of squaring the ball across the face of goal to an unmarked Mbappé. Vinícius Júnior did not attempt a single shot.

Those who do not watch Real Madrid’s La Liga matches might have been surprised, but those tuning in week in and week out know this is how the team plays: without cohesion, without structure and without intensity.
Once Los Blancos were trailing 3–1, who came off the pitch? Vinícius Jr and Denzel Dumfries led the way, before Cucurella, Tchouaméni and Yan Diomande ultimately followed.

Aurélien Tchouaméni (center) needs to be better for Real Madrid. / Tullio M. Puglia/Getty ImagesThe team then scored three unanswered goals to walk away with three points they had no business collecting. Who was at the center of the comeback? The player Real Madrid handed a massive six-year extension to this summer? The player who commanded a club-record fee this summer? The newly crowned World Cup winner?

ftbpro_01m4y80vdz6b.title: Devastating Raul Jimenez Injury Update Could Prove Catastrophic for Mexico
ftbpro_01m4y80vdz6b.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas9:00 AM EDTRaúl Jiménez will be sidelined for the rest of 2026.       / Richard Pelham/Getty Images Mexico national team striker Raúl Jiménez will undergo knee surgery on Friday that will keep him sidelined for the rest of the year.

The veteran striker has been out of action since mid-September with an MCL injury he hoped to overcome with conservative treatment. On Wednesday, Wolverhampton Wanderers released a lengthy statement, confirming the worst possible outcome for Jiménez.

“Raúl injured his left MCL against Everton,” Wolves director of performance Phil Hayward said in the statement, “which was four weeks ago now and unfortunately the injury has not responded as we expected, so we've decided that the best thing is to have surgery to repair that ligament.

“Normally the ligament for a fairly low-grade injury would heal on its own, however this has not responded as we were expecting, and after regularly scanning for the last three weeks, the ligament is not healing in the anticipated way.

Raúl Jiménez (bottom) has been sidelined since suffering a knee injury against Everton on Sept. 16.  / Brett Patzke/WWFC/Wolves/Getty Images“We’ve consulted with several knee specialists and decided the best course of action is to move to surgery to ensure that we are back in control of the time frames and have a clear idea of when he will be back.”
“So, he’ll have the surgery on Friday in London, and then he’ll have around three months of rehabilitation before he’s ready to play again,” Hayward added.

It’s a significant blow for Wolves who are currently 10th in the Championship standings and now will be without their legendary striker for an extended period. But it’s perhaps even more painful news for El Tri.

Rafael Márquez (middle) had a poor start to his tenure as Mexico manager.  / Jim Sabo/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesThe knee injury prevented Jiménez from featuring as the Rafael Márquez era as Mexico manager got underway during the September-October international action.

El Tri failed to collect a single win in its first four games following the 2026 World Cup and dropped its last two matches of the window in embarrassing fashion against the USMNT and against an inferior Chile side. Mexico scored just two goals in four games, but neither came courtesy of a center forward and they blanked in the two defeats.

At 35, Jiménez remains vital to El Tri’s attack. The nation’s second all-time leading scorer has bagged 11 out of Mexico’s last 25 goals in its three most recent official tournament appearances (44%). Other strikers account for just two strikes in that span.

“He [Jiménez] went to see a specialist yesterday and it was decided he will have surgery on Friday,” Mexico national team director Duilio Davino said on Wednesday. “We hope he returns to the pitch is as soon as possible because he’s a very important player for the national team, that we all want to have and that still has a lot of football left to give.”
Jiménez will miss at least two games for Mexico because of his surgery, two vital matches early in Márquez’s tenure.

Raúl Jiménez had been mostly injury free over the last two years.  / Carl De Souza/AFP/Getty Images Mexico will be without Jiménez when it faces Jamaica in the two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals in November to wrap up El Tri’s 2026 action. The first two official games of Márquez’s tenure look manageable on paper, but Mexico knows how difficult these games can be.

El Tri visits Jamaica in the opening leg of the tie having lost in its two most recent away first legs in the tournament 2–0 against Honduras in 2023 and 2024 despite boasting a vastly superior side. Without Jiménez, the task at hand becomes considerably harder.

Armando González, Santiago Gimenez and Germán Berterame are the favorites to lead El Tri’s line in November, but the trio underperformed in the recent friendlies and only solidified the notion that Mexico can’t come close to its best version without the Wolves frontman on the pitch.

Still, Márquez will have nowhere to hide if the reigning nations league champion exits the competition against Jamaica, especially since El Tri will host the second leg at the Estadio BBVA in Monterrey on Nov. 17.

With Jiménez watching from home, the rookie manager must steer Mexico past Jamaica in his first official games at the helm, or else he could come under immense pressure just six matches into his tenure.

ftbpro_01m4z9r9925q.title: President Trump Gets His Lasting World Cup Legacy With Proposed Rule Change
ftbpro_01m4z9r9925q.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:10 AM EDTThe 2026 World Cup will always have a tinge of the Presidents Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino about it. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesFor better or worse, the 2026 World Cup staged across North America will forever be associated by some with U.S. President Donald Trump.

As he was so keen to point out, it was during Trump’s first administration that the United States, Canada and Mexico secured hosting rights for a tournament which would be plagued by governmental controversy. Besides the prices, visas and travel bans, Trump also planted himself at the center of the Folarin Balogun red card scandal.

The President freely admitted that he intervened during an unprecedented protest which ultimately saw the U.S. men’s national team striker have his one-match ban suspended, allowing him to play in the round of 16 tie against Belgium. ESPN are among a number of outlets to have reported that the FIFA council is set to vote on a motion which will prohibit this action going forward.
The issue for many is that no amount of rewriting future rulebooks will change the tainted past.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

That would not be the last red card Donald Trump had an influence over. / Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesWhen Balogun inadvertently landed on Tarik Muharemović’s ankle in the USMNT’s round of 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, the issue could have been quashed in the bowls of Levi’s Stadium. A FIFA spokesperson informed assembled media waiting for Mauricio Pochettino’s press conference that there was no mechanism for the U.S. to appeal Balogun’s red card and he would thereby be forced to serve the automatic one-match suspension it brought.

Pochettino initially claimed that the team would appeal the decision before Peter Rutzler of The Times promptly informed him of the brief everyone had just received. The USMNT coach turned to his director of communications, Michael Kammarman, earned a stern nod, and swiftly accepted Balogun’s fate. But it would not end there.

Trump would freely admit that he subsequently “asked for a review” of the incident after reaching out to FIFA president Gianni Infantino. “I didn’t think it was a foul. I’m good at this stuff,” he shrugged. “I didn’t tell [Infantino] what to do. I can’t tell him what to do, but I don’t believe he made the decision.”

The decision was examined by FIFA’s disciplinary committee who agreed to suspend Balogun’s impending ban by citing Article 27. This little-known clause states: “The judicial body may decide to fully or partially suspend the implementation of a disciplinary measure.”

Infantino, a self-confessed ally of Trump who would have no jurisdiction to rule on Balogun’s suspension, was at pains to stress that “FIFA’s judicial bodies are independent” even if he admitted to “regularly” discussing World Cup matters with Trump.

“I read the decisions of the FIFA disciplinary committee when they are issued,” Infantino added. “Sometimes I am surprised by them. Sometimes I agree with them, and sometimes I disagree.” Many disagreed with this decision.

FA Chair Debbie Hewitt has been an outspoken critic. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesOne of the chief concerns about Balogun’s suspended suspension is the vagaries involved. Besides citing Article 27, itself devoid of much description, there was little explanation as to why the U.S. striker was spared.

The England Football Association’s chair, Debbie Hewitt, has demanded a release of all documentation relating to the decision—as well as Infantino’s aborted World Cup private investment scheme. The Belgiun FA had previously seen a similar appeal overlooked.
This storm will come to a head in Thursday’s session of FIFA’s 37 council members, which will be chaired by Infantino. Balogun’s red card will just be one of many hot topics on the docket.

ftbpro_01m4zg592m9j.title: ‘I’m Convinced’—Martinez Names the Only Way Man Utd Can ‘Move Forward’
ftbpro_01m4zg592m9j.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff7:45 AM EDTLisandro Martínez could be looking to a future without him in it.f / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesLisandro Martínez has attempted to clarify his explosive comments made in the immediate aftermath of Manchester United’s Champions League defeat to Atlético Madrid, insisting he believes the way forward is to “keep working together, with ambition and commitment.”

In two postgame interviews, Martínez admitted frustration at what he felt was insufficient recruitment during the summer transfer window to build on what was a strong end to the 2025–26 campaign that brought a return to the Champions League.
Sporting director Jason Wilcox seemed to take the brunt of his ire, although what he said could also have been perceived as throwing his current colleagues under the bus.
It’s not a complete climbdown, but posting a written statement as an Instagram story, Martínez said his initial comments were born out of “anger and frustration” following a disappointing result.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don’t go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United,” he said.

“My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honors. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.”

The defender went public with his blunt frustrations. / Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA/Getty ImagesThe 2022 World Cup winner said “wanting more” is about the “ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.”

Wayne Rooney spoke in the aftermath of the Prime Video interview about it being fine for ambitious players to demand more from their club and teammates—he himself very famously did in 2010 in a move that threatened to pave the way for his departure—but he took issue with that coming publicly from someone like Martínez, who hasn’t performed well.

Martínez addressed the backlash over his own form and questions over the team’s stark decline; the same club that took more points than any other in the final 17 Premier League games of last season has suddenly only been able to win two games out of nine in all competitions at the start of this one.

“I know that, first and foremost, it’s us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility,” he said. “We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

“I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment. My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge.”
Three Potential Destinations For Lisandro Martinez. dark. Next. Three Potential Destinations For Lisandro Martinez

Martínez has a contract until 2027 that has an option through 2028. / Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesDoubts have been cast over Martínez’s future at Old Trafford. His contract runs out next summer but includes an option for an extra 12 months until 2028. The Athletic notes the defender doesn’t want his contract extended beyond this season and would still prefer to head to Spain, after an unfulfilled desire to join Atlético Madrid this past summer. United have similar doubts.

But the player’s camp appears insistent this week’s comments were not a way to force his way out, with the same report explaining that people close to him claim he would have made the same comments regardless of the time remaining on his contract.
It is implied that Martínez is not necessarily alone in his frustration, but the outburst was met with “surprise” and at least one teammate confronted him about it.

There has been no decision on any formal punishment at present, but a fine is expected. Michael Carrick may have a tough choice to make over his inclusion for the weekend clash with Leeds United, because the defense is already stretched thin.
There is a suggestion from The Athletic that “none of” Wilcox, chief executive Omar Berrada or co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe will “allow Martínez’s comments to go unchecked.”

ftbpro_01m4zgzj7v6e.title: ‘I’m Angry’—Vinicius Jr Opens Up As Real Madrid Struggles Hit New Low
ftbpro_01m4zgzj7v6e.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath11:00 AM EDTVinícius Júnior was off the pace again. / Isabella Bonotto/Anadolu/Getty ImagesVinícius Jr has spoken out on his rut, admitting he is angry with himself following another poor showing in the 4–3 win over Roma on Wednesday.
The Brazilian superstar’s form has been the subject of much consternation at Real Madrid this season, with the 26-year-old scoring just once and assisting once in 10 matches played.

Vinícius Jr has cut a peripheral figure in José Mourinho’s team in 2026–27, often struggling to affect games from out wide. The Bernabéu crowd, seemingly in part irked by the player’s protracted contract saga which dominated this summer, have responded with regular boos and whistles.

A low-key start to the campaign became a major issue after a limp showing in the Madrid derby defeat prior to the international break. That was then followed up with a red card for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in the win over Villarreal on Saturday—an offense which resulted in a four-match suspension.

Vinícius Jr spoken out about his bad run of form. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesWednesday’s comeback win in the Champions League was spectacular but brought no respite for Vinícius, who was largely anonymous against Roma before being substituted.
The forward created one chance, had zero shots and managed just 22 touches in total before being taken off, while also committing an error that led to Roma’s second goal.

For the third time in as many Madrid games, Vinícius did not make it to the hour mark and was benched with Los Blancos trailing 3–1 in Rome. His replacement, Endrick, went on to play a pivotal role in the stunning turnaround that saw the visitors score three times in 10 minutes.
The performance of the team in his absence adds to a growing narrative that this Madrid side are more coherent and productive without their No. 7.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Jr won’t play in La Liga until November. /  Michael Regan/UEFA/Getty ImagesSpeaking after the victory, Vinícius Jr, who reacted with obvious frustration to being taken off by Mourinho, admitted to being angry with himself.
Asked about his reaction to being benched, he responded: “I was angry after the substitution because I always want to be at my best and help the team.

“The substitutions changed the team. Endrick changed the dynamic and was the best player. And Carlos [Espí] came on for a few minutes but scored. I’m angry with myself for not being at my best. In the end, Vini always comes back and I have no doubt that I will.”
Vinícius Jr also suggested that the news of his four-match suspension—which will see him miss the Clásico on Oct. 25—disrupted his match preparation.

“I think the suspension came at a bad time,” he said. “They had all day to issue the suspension, and I only found out when I arrived at the stadium. The rule is new, and La Liga officials always come to explain new things to us, but they didn’t explain this one. I’ve never committed an act of violence against another player. I get fouled quite a bit, and a yellow card is always enough for me.”

It’s not quite going to plan for Real Madrid’s main man. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesVinícius Jr has been a lightning rod for the Bernabéu’s frustrations this season and has been on the receiving end of audible jeers and whistles from his own fans at home games in recent weeks amid his rut.

The Brazilian addressed the fans, saying: “The boos certainly don’t help me, but people pay for their tickets. We play better when we have the fans behind us. Jude [Bellingham] plays better, [Kylian] Mbappé plays better, I play better. I think it’s easier to boo me because I’ve been here longer and I’m one of the captains.”
He added: “I’m going to be back. When I arrived young, many laughed at me, and in the end, I have over 100 goals for Real Madrid.”

Vinícius Jr’s next opportunity to arrest his slump will be when Madrid face RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday, Oct, 21. He will not be available for selection in La Liga until Madrid host Celta on Nov. 22.

ftbpro_01m4zhf5hgck.title: Cavan Sullivan’s Elite Mentality on Show As USMNT Star Breaks Huge MLS Record
ftbpro_01m4zhf5hgck.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:30 AM EDTYet another record for Cavan Sullivan. / Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesDespite breaking the record for the most goal contributions by a teenager in a single Major League Soccer season in Wednesday’s 3–1 win over the Chicago Fire, Cavan Sullivan insisted he was struggling to care because he played “sort of terrible.”

Perhaps a victim of his own high standards over the past few months, Sullivan was disappointed to walk away with just one assist from the victory and could not celebrate the fact he was now sitting on 21 goal contributions from the season.
A total of seven goals and 14 assists means no teenager has ever contributed to more goals in a single MLS season than Sullivan, breaking a record that had been held by Diego Fagúndez since 2013.
“It seems like every week something else is popping up for him,” interim manager Ryan Richter laughed.

“I’m so happy for him, and a big emphasis for him is to continue to be decisive in games, and when he’s chipping in with goals and assists, the way that he has over this last stretch, he’s making the difference.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Sullivan was not in the mood to celebrate. / Harry Figiel/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesIt would be easy for Sullivan to get caught up in his own hype. The 17-year-old has been one of the best players in MLS this season, is now a star for the USMNT and has already got a transfer to Manchester City wrapped up for an 18th birthday present.
However, there will be no celebrating this latest feat for Sullivan, who was eager to confront his belief that his performance in the game did not deserve such an accolade.
“I played sort of terrible tonight, so I’m not really focused on any records or stats like that, to be honest,” Sullivan said.

“I’m happy with the win, but I’ve sort of got to look in the mirror and watch some film and see what I have to do better. I’m not really happy with my personal performance, but, like I said, great win.”

That is the sort of mentality USMNT and Philadelphia fans want to see from Sullivan. Standards must be pushed higher if the teenager is going to realize his sky-high potential and, while one must be wary of putting too much pressure on his young shoulders, this is the only way Sullivan can push himself to the next level.
It is not about records. Those are simply a byproduct of on-field dominance. Instead, the priority is making a decisive impact and being the reason the Union and the USMNT win games. So far, so good.
“His mentality is great,” teammate Neil Pierre said. “Obviously, he thinks he can do better, but obviously we support him in any way possible.”

Preston have endured an even worse start to the new season, collecting just four points from a possible 30 across their first 10 matches. They were thumped 4–0 by Birmingham City on Tuesday and will also be searching for a morale-boosting result in North Wales this weekend.

Preston are in their 12th-consecutive season in the Championship, with their immediate focus on staying in the division before they can start thinking about promotion to the Premier League.
