ftbpro_01m4zmvsaaaw.title: Report: Chelsea, Liverpool Face Record-Breaking Alex Scott Price Tag
ftbpro_01m4zmvsaaaw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:30 AM EDTAlex Scott could be moving on in January. / Adrian DENNIS/AFP/Getty ImagesBournemouth have reportedly (and reluctantly) accepted that their star midfielder Alex Scott would be allowed to leave the club as soon as January if one of his numerous suitors is willing to stump up £100 million ($132.6 million).

Scott has been a man in demand for months. The Cherries had the luxury of newfound Europa League revenue to lean upon when assessing bids for the mobile midfielder over the summer. Chelsea’s offer of £64 million ($84.8 million) is thought to have been rejected out of hand.

However, interest in the England international has only intensified thanks to his ever-improving performances this season, with the likes of Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City all credited as admirers.

Faced with the prospect of forcibly keeping an unhappy player, discussions with Scott’s representatives have convinced Bournemouth to accept offers next year, although only if a record-shattering fee of £100 million is on the table, BBC Sport has reported. Antoine Semenyo’s £64 million move to Manchester City last January stands as Bournemouth’s largest ever sale, representing a landmark Scott would have to obliterate.

Chelsea’s attentions are thought to persist while Liverpool are billed as the Blues’ closest challengers. Now that the two clubs have been given a clear price tag, one simple question remains: is Scott worth it?
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
The ball from Rayan ▶️The deftness of Evanilson ✨The strike from Scott 🎯Our first home goal of 2026/27 was a superb piece of play 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Ry5fhkGjjO
There are two strands to Bournemouth’s valuation; Scott’s talent and the reality of the modern market.

Scott is a modern day midfielder. While he may be billed as the ‘Guernsey Jack Grealish’ thanks to his roots on the island in the English Channel and a center-parting, the 23-year-old bears no resemblance to the former Manchester City winger. Scott offers a brilliant blend of dexterity and industry, gobbling up prodigious amounts of ground often while rolling the ball under his studs.

No midfielder in the Premier League could match the 61.3 miles Scott covered while running last season, per FotMob. In the type of high-pressing system which Andoni Iraola deployed on the south coast, having a player with three lungs helps plug the gaps that can form—as Liverpool have discovered already this term.

Beyond the brawn, Scott has the brain power to know when to press, a crucially undervalued attribute in a discipline which is about far more than running blindly. Bournemouth’s No. 8 may chip in with a few goals from the outside of the box but he is not the player to deliver the final pass; across his entire Premier League career, Scott has mustered two assists, one fewer than Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson.

The transfer market will always value end product but this modern iteration of player trading has seen a boom in the demand for mobile midfielders. Of the 10 most expensive players signed by Premier League clubs this summer, seven were defensive or central midfielders, the same position as Scott.
This evidence presents Bournemouth with a compelling case for any suitor. If the likes of Enzo Fernández, Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali can all cost around £100 million, why can’t Scott?

Alex Scott (left) hit his best form for Andoni Iraola. / Jacob King/PA Images/Getty ImagesChelsea have already demonstrated their eagerness to sign Scott and Xabi Alonso’s need for a central midfielder over the coming years has scarcely been sated by the acquisition of a 36-year-old Jordan Henderson, not withstanding his heroics against Bournemouth, ironically enough.

No amount of money appears to be beyond Chelsea’s free-spending ownership and the prospect of Scott dovetailing with Moisés Caicedo is a daunting prospect for any opposition midfield. If the Ecuador international already appears to have the capacity to materialize in multiple positions at once, he and Scott should be able to cover every blade of grass between them.

For all the attraction of playing under a former World Cup-winning midfielder like Alonso, the allure of a reunion with Iraola could tilt Scott toward Liverpool. “He’s a great head coach, a great person,” the Cherries Player of the Season said of his former manager. “He has helped me a lot and improved me a lot, so obviously I am going to be grateful for him.”

The admiration is mutual and could be hugely beneficial to Liverpool, whose engine room has repeatedly appeared undermanned during Iraola’s early days on Merseyside. On top of his innate qualities, Scott’s familiarity with the Basque manager’s demands would surely soothe some of the teething problems he’s had this term.

While Scott would be a huge boost for both clubs, it would still take some drastic action for either Chelsea or Liverpool to offer a nine-digit fee mid-season. Only two players in the history of the sport have ever been transferred for more than £100 million in a January window; Philippe Coutinho’s Liverpool exit in 2018 and Fernández’s arrival at Chelsea five years later.

The Blues are a very different proposition to that chaotic early BlueCo era, when the now-departed Todd Boehly was the face of the ambitious new owners. Despite Liverpool’s willingness to splash the cash on big names, the likes of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola have all been bought in summer windows.

Scott is talented enough to force a change of approach, it’s just a question of whether Chelsea or Liverpool feel their 2026–27 season could be significantly improved by taking the plunge this winter rather than waiting for the campaign’s conclusion.

ftbpro_01m4znzcdx0a.title: Endrick Drops Transfer Bombshell After Inspiring Comeback Win Over Roma
ftbpro_01m4znzcdx0a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath10:00 AM EDTEndrick is open to a transfer away. / Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty ImagesEndrick has opened the door to a January exit from Real Madrid, despite manager José Mourinho’s insistence that the forward will remain at the club.

Endrick came off the bench to help inspire Madrid to a stunning 4–3 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, scoring the late equaliser with a header, before Antonio Rüdiger bagged the winner from another corner right on 90 minutes.

The 20-year-old’s inclusion at the Stadio Olimpico at the hour mark changed the game, with Madrid trailing 3–1 at the time. The opportunity to play the hero was a rare one for Endrick who had been restricted to just four minutes of game time all season prior to Wednesday.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Endrick bagged the equalizer on Wednesday. / Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty ImagesSpeaking after he match, the young forward told reporters of his “hunger” to impress when called upon.

He said: “’I’m very happy. It was a very difficult match. I was on the bench, just thanking God to be here. When the boss called me, I was actually surprised because it was so early. I hadn’t played here for a long time and I had so much hunger. That’s what I brought, and I did well.”
Asked about his future, Endrick admitted he is open to a transfer in January when the window arrives.

“I take it day by day. If I have to leave in January, I’ll leave; if I have to stay, I’ll stay,” he said. “I will do whatever God puts in my heart. I’m very grateful to Mourinho. He is one of the first coaches who has genuinely spoken to me. I trust him with open arms.
“While I’m here, my job isn’t to play for the manager to win, but for Real Madrid. But because of everything he is doing for me, I’m going to fight for him and for Real.”

Endrick is open to an exit, Mourinho is not. / Danilo Gemito/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesEndrick’s comments come in stark contrast to those of Mourinho, who name-checked the Brazilian in his pregame remarks, insisting a January loan move is not a possibility.
“Forget it, forget it. Forget any interested clubs,” he said. “They had better sit down, otherwise they will get tired waiting.

“He is a player I love, with incredible potential. He is very important to us. Anyone interested in him will have a serious fight on their hands with me, because I believe he doesn’t need to go out on loan and will achieve tremendous success here.”

Despite Mourinho’s high praise, he has yet to put much faith in Endrick, with super sub Carlos Espí often preferred as Madrid’s ‘plan B’ striker. Meanwhile, out wide the former Palmeiras starlet has to compete with the likes of Arda Güler, Yan Diomande and Brahim Díaz, complicating his path to regular minutes.

The forward spent the second half of the 2025–26 season on loan at French club Lyon, where he scored eight times and registered eight assists in 21 matches—a run of form that saw him included on Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil roster for the World Cup.
During the recent international break, Ancelotti warned that Brazil’s young players like Endrick need to play regularly in order to develop, amid his Real Madrid travails.
Madrid’s Champions League opponents Roma have been linked with Endrick, as have as AC Milan.

ftbpro_01m4zp9djwza.title: Arsenal Respond As Star Player Left Out of 2026–27 Team Photo
ftbpro_01m4zp9djwza.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer9:30 AM EDTArsenal posed for the group snap. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesSomething was off when Arsenal published their official squad photograph for 2026–27.
It featured 24 players—among them a slightly awkward-looking Max Dowman—the Premier League trophy and Community Shield, and a proud Mikel Arteta.
But William Saliba, a cornerstone of Arsenal’s improvement and, ultimately, their success as England’s soccer champions last season for the first time in 22 years, was missing.

Saliba was a slow-burn investment for the Gunners, signed as a teenager in 2019 but not becoming a first-team regular until three years later. His injury absence during the final months of 2022–23 was a major factor in Arsenal’s collapse in that title race, losing out to Manchester City, and there is no question that he’s among the best center backs in the world.

But a back injury sustained during the 2026 World Cup means Saliba is yet to kick a ball this season. And that was also the unfortunate reason behind his omission from the team photograph. Arsenal were quick to explain the player’s absence. It was nothing sinister, but the scheduled shoot clashed with a pre-existing medical appointment for Saliba.
Due to a medical appointment, William Saliba was not available this afternoon.

William Saliba last played on July 14. / Stefan Koops/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesSaliba suffered his injury, seemingly aggravating a pre-exiting back complaint, in France’s semifinal loss to Spain at AT&T Stadium on July 14 and was loosely ruled out for an “extended period.” That has bled into months, but the 25-year-old is potentially nearing the end of his recovery.
Saliba resumed individual training on grass, always a significant step in any major rehabilitation, in early October. Arteta’s recent update on the situation gave fans reason for optimism.
“We’re managing that load. He’s building his capacity to good standards, and let’s see in the next few weeks,” the Gunners boss explained.
“We’re still talking about weeks. When that happens, it’s very different whether he would play just before or just after [the next international break in November]. I cannot tell you exactly.”

Arsenal visit Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 1, but their final two fixtures before the November international window are Slavia Prague (Nov. 4) and Hull City (Nov. 7). The Gunners return to action following that break on Nov. 21 against Newcastle United on the road.

Arsenal signed Ezri Konsa during the summer in the knowledge that Saliba would be ruled out for some time. The former Aston Villa defender has filled in admirably, but the sooner Arsenal can reintegrate one of the premier defenders in world soccer, the better.

paragraphs: By Rich Fay12:00 PM EDTHumphrey Ker stepped down from his position on the Wrexham board of directors last month. / Variety via Getty ImagesHumphrey Ker admits his shock exit from Wrexham was a “complicated” issue, but ultimately something he felt he had to do.

Ker stepped away from the club’s board and his role as a trustee of the Wrexham AFC Foundation last month, bringing an end to his official five-year association with the club. The 43-year-old played a key role in the Red Dragons’ rise, initially getting Rob Mac interested in the sport and drawing up a list of potential clubs to buy.

Ker then became Mac and Ryan Reynolds’s man on the ground during the takeover process, putting his comedy career on hold as the Hollywood duo set about transforming the former National League club. The British actor quickly became a major part of the local community and famously helped convince the owners to break the bank to sign legendary striker Paul Mullin.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Humphrey Ker convinced Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds to buy Wrexham in February 2021. / Getty ImagesKer believes the club’s current structure made it progressively harder for him to make a positive contribution, with his role diminishing following Wrexham’s promotion to the EFL Championship.

Despite his popularity among supporters, Ker gradually stepped back from the boardroom as the club made several other high-profile appointments and evolved from a community club into a global phenomenon.

“It’s a bit complicated, but it was something that I just felt I had to do,” he told The Leader about his decision to step away. “Not necessarily because of other things in my life, but I am excited to see what happens in the future.

“I thoroughly enjoyed my six years at Wrexham. I will be watching on closely from further afield and wish everybody at the club all the best. I am not quite sure when I will next be there, but I will definitely be coming back when I can.”

Ker leaves the club at a time of transition as Wrexham look to establish themselves among the Championship’s strongest teams and secure promotion to the Premier League. After three successive promotions, the final step is likely to be the hardest, though Ker is confident they will fulfill their lofty ambitions under Mac and Reynolds.

He added: “Rob and Ryan are committed to do this for a long time. All the ingredients that made us successful before are still there and hopefully they will bear fruit as they have done over the last five years.

“It couldn’t have gone any better, really. Genuinely, when we started out, I don’t think we ever expected to have got to where we have now. But I am very glad we have got to where we have got to. I think it is an achievement to be proud of.”

ftbpro_01m4zrqyhad9.title: Real Madrid’s Comeback Against Roma Was the Most Real Madrid Thing Ever
ftbpro_01m4zrqyhad9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath2:00 PM EDTMadrid will not be denied. / Kazimierz Koper/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images“Their comebacks in matches are not convincing, and you feel as though everything is collapsing or not going well,” was CBS Sports analyst Jamie Carragher’s assessment of Real Madrid’s 4–3 win over Roma on Wednesday.
The 2005 Champions League winner added bluntly: “They are barely holding themselves together. They could well lose to Barcelona [on Oct. 25] and then lose the La Liga title.”
It’s a viewpoint many would agree with following Madrid’s turbulent start to the 2026–27 season.

Despite a summer makeover, new manager José Mourinho hasn’t been able to keep pace with Barcelona—Europe’s form team—while old issues over balance in attack and midfield have continued to cause problems. The recent Madrid derby defeat laid bare the shortcomings of the team, while two wins from two in the Champions League paper over some obvious cracks.

And yet, the comeback win at the Stadio Olimpico was thrilling, madcap and spectacular—serving as a reminder that Real Madrid’s Champions League aura is unaffected by rhyme or reason. Write them off at your own peril.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Antonio Rüdiger completed the eight-minute turnaround. /  Giuseppe Bellini/Getty ImagesWith Madrid seemingly down and out at 3–1, super sub Carlos Espí bagged his third of the season to give the visitors hope on 82 minutes.

Three minutes on, Endrick, another substitute, headed in from a corner to equalize, while Antonio Rüdiger did the same thing to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat on the stroke of 90 minutes. Another player brought on from the bench, Arda Güler, was key in all three goals.

In coming from two goals down on 82 minutes to win the match 4–3, Real Madrid completed the fastest three-goal turnaround in the club’s history. Madrid’s performance also ranks as the fastest away comeback (of two or more goals) in Champions League history.
They take that achievement off Liverpool who previously held the record with a 12 minute, 48 second-turnaround against Villarreal back in 2022.
Next. Best Real Madrid Ever. The 25 Best Real Madrid Players Ever—Ranked. dark

Mourinho’s men had been outplayed for large periods of the evening in Rome, with Gian Piero Gasperini's team dominating the first hour. And yet, it was Madrid—15-time European champions—who came away as victors.

Even when they are objectively poor, Los Blancos will simply not be written off in their favorite competition. Both Zinedine Zidane and Carlo Ancelotti’s Madrid sides built an feeling of inevitability in Europe that would not be removed by mediocre league form. The sense of destiny around the club is such that a “prophecy” went viral in Spain last season predicting Madrid would still win the Champions League despite looking far off the pace of the continent’s best.
Wednesday night was perhaps Mourinho’s first vintage Madrid moment since returning as manager.
Incredible Real Madrid comeback 🤯#UCL pic.twitter.com/Pj1OhAsMVG
“It was two games in one,” Mourinho told Prime Video after the match. “Roma were superior in every aspect for the first half, and then we were impossible to stop for 20 minutes.”
“After going 3-1 down, perhaps everyone thought the game was dead, but the only ones who were dead were the Roma players.

“It is very difficult to play with this intensity and the style of football that they have. We made some changes, because conceding three, four or five goals doesn't make much difference. Roma were unable to handle that avalanche of attacking football.”

While the overall performance may leave a lot to be desired—as Carragher put it, the club looks to be barely holding itself together at times—Madrid can still take a lot from Wednesday’s result. Even when things appear to be collapsing, you can thrive in the chaos.

The depth on the bench and the hunger of Mourinho’s backup options is highly promising, and a reminder that Madrid do have a world-class roster for all the minor complaints. The euphoria of the remontada will also give fans and the players an obvious boost going into a key period of the season, with the Clásico now just ten days away.

ftbpro_01m4ztek49b8.title: Malik Jakupovic Could Follow in Cavan Sullivan’s Footsteps With Premier League Switch
ftbpro_01m4ztek49b8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell1:05 PM EDTMalik Jakupovic is gaining attention from clubs abroad.  / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCavan Sullivan might be stealing the show at Philadelphia Union, but there’s another teenager slowly making a name for himself at Subaru Park: Malik Jakupovic.

The 17-year-old, who is under contract through 2030 with an option to extend another season, has operated quietly in the shadows, making cameo appearances for the first team. He’s not breaking records like Sullivan, nor is he commanding starting minutes like fellow young American Neil Pierre.

Jakupovic is more of a slow burn. The Michigan-native only made his MLS debut back in March, and he is still waiting for his first start. Only two of his last five appearances have been for longer than one minute.

But the potential is there, so much so that clubs across Europe are paying close attention to Jakupovic. The striker already received interest from Borussia Dortmund over the summer, with reports claiming the Union rejected a bid from the German outfit for their young gem.

Now even more clubs are coming to the party, eager to potentially snatch up the next young American goalscorer. Links to the Premier League are swirling, while Bundesliga ties seemingly remain strong.
This much transfer activity, for a player with one senior goal to his name, speaks volumes, as do Jakupovic’s contributions in MLS NEXT Pro.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Malik Jakupovic bagged his first MLS goal in September.  /  Orlando Ramirez/Getty ImagesThree years ago, Jakupovic joined the Union’s academy. At 14 years old, the forward made Philadelphia his new home, hoping to rise through the ranks and one day help the club lift its first-ever MLS Cup.

By the time 2025 rolled around, Jakupovic was staking his place with the Union’s reserve team. The teenager made 19 appearances in MLS NEXT Pro and found the back of the net eight times along the way, becoming the team’s second-highest goalscorer in his first campaign.

The Union took notice, calling up Jakupovic for their early Concacaf Champions Cup clashes in 2026. He made his official senior debut in the team’s 7–0 rout over Defence Force, and then started a trend.

Jakupovic would get called up for first team action, feature off the bench or not at all, and then return to the Philadelphia Union II, where he would impress enough to get called back up again to the senior squad.

The back-and-forth continued as the months progressed this season. Jakupovic would score a goal in MLS NEXT Pro, get an opportunity to rub shoulders with the first team and then go back to starring in the second tier.

It wasn’t until September that Jakupovic retained his place in Ryan Richter’s team, and the consistency did him a world of good. In his third consecutive appearance with the Union, the 17-year-old bagged his first MLS goal, a close-range finish in stoppage time in Philadelphia’s 5–0 win over San Diego FC.

Malik Jakupovic is behind a lot of good players at the Union. / Seth Garber/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesOpportunities are proving to be rare, though. You would think Jakupovic’s goal would earn the youngster more playing time moving forward, but he logged just one minute in the Union’s two wins over Real Salt Lake and Chicago Fire following the September-October international window.

Patience is required for Jakupovic to fully stake his claim with the first team. The Union’s attack is firing on all cylinders at the moment, scoring 23 goals in the team’s last six matches. Sullivan is in sensational form, Bruno Damiani is scoring for fun and somehow Milan Iloski is upstaging them both.
Realistically, there’s no room for Jakupovic to slot into Richter’s XI, especially with the MLS Cup playoffs less than a month away. The good news is the young American is the ultimate professional.

“Malik has shown great growth since joining our academy, and his maturity at just 16 years old speaks to his professionalism and commitment,” Philadelphia sporting director Jon Scheer said of Jakupovic back in April.

Scheer highlighted how excited the club is to keep developing Jakupovic. But as interest from European teams continues to mount, the striker could instead choose to take his development abroad, where more opportunities, more money and greater stakes lie.
Making noise in one of Europe’s top five leagues is also an assured way to get U.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino’s attention.

Mauricio Pochettino is giving more opportunities to young stars. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesJakupovic was left sitting at home while Pochettino called up eight teenagers and 13 total uncapped players for four fall friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. His fellow Philadelphia teammates Sullivan and Pierre were among the young contingent taking center stage during the September-October international break.

ftbpro_01m4zw0jf6z4.title: ‘I Don’t Remember’—Vinicius Jr’s Outburst at Suspension Misses the Point
ftbpro_01m4zw0jf6z4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:10 PM EDTVinícius Júnior will miss Real Madrid’s next four matches. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesVinícius Júnior’s pointed remark claiming to have never before seen a player receive a four-game ban for pulling an opponent’s hair misses the point. Only half of his suspension was a result of his unwise tug.

Real Madrid’s misfiring forward endured another unwanted moment in the spotlight over the weekend when he was sent off for grabbing the hair of Villarreal defender Nathan Saliba. This constitutes violent conduct—and has done for years—and the fact it was away from the ball necessitated an automatic two-match ban.

However, the authorities in Spain sidelined Vinícius Jr for four matches; two for the hair pull and another pair for his reaction to the red card. The Brazilian forward had to be restrained by his teammate Antonio Rüdiger after making a beeline for referee Isidro Díaz de Mera following a VAR review.

“I don’t remember any player ever getting a four-game suspension,” Vinícius Jr scoffed after another underwhelming performance against Roma in midweek. “I tried to get past the player in front of me and ended up grabbing his hair.

“The rule is new. The CTA [Spain’s governing body of referees] always comes to Valdebebas [Madrid’s training ground] to explain things to us, and they’ve never said anything about this—they’re changing the rules. That’s it—a red card. That’s why I was so surprised, but I didn’t say a single bad word to the referee to deserve a four-game suspension.”

Vinícius Júnior turned to his rivals to make his defense. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIt’s hard to grasp quite how Vinícius Jr can defend himself given the damning evidence in front of him; he is caught in 4K with a fist full of Saliba’s curls and was quite clearly unhappy with the decision. As the referee’s report fairly outlined, the winger “continued to protest my decision loudly, approaching the area where I was standing with an aggressive attitude.”

Nevertheless, Vinícius Jr can be excused some frustration given how often he is the subject of grappling without any severe consequence. “With Vini, everything’s very easy because the other team’s fans are going to say it’s O.K.,” he argued, in the third person. “The press is going to say it’s O.K., too. I understand that. I’m here to keep growing and improving because I know where I came from and how far I can go.”

“The opposing fans have to boo me because I’m here to score goals against their team,” the divisive figure accepted. “But I don’t understand the referees. I saw a statistic: I’ve been fouled 500 times, resulting in five red cards, and over 500 fouls against me have led to I don’t know how many yellow cards. In the end, the yellow cards always go to Vini, to the forwards.

“We have to defend players who do things differently in soccer, like Lamine [Yamal] at Barcelona or Julián [Alvarez] at Atléti. The defenders have every right to tackle me the whole game, and in the end, I’m the one who gets the card.”

José Mourinho came up with another immortal line. / Silvia Lore/Getty ImagesDespite hooking Vinícius Jr before the hour mark after berating his forward for losing the ball cheaply in the buildup to Roma’s second goal, José Mourinho came to his player’s defense concerning the announcement of the suspension.

“May I ask you a question?” Mourinho interjected during his postmatch press conference on Wednesday. “Is it normal for a player to find out two hours before the game that he’s been suspended for four matches? You don’t have to answer me. Is it normal? Couldn’t they have announced it now, or tomorrow morning? Did they have to do it while we were on our way to the stadium?”

In the eyes of the Portuguese coach, this was simply another example of the grand conspiracy against Madrid, the club’s players and Mourinho himself. The beleaguered manager claimed that these shadowy powers weren’t even bothering to hide their influence any more.

“In Portuguese, they say: ‘A cat hiding with its tail sticking out.’ It seems to me that now the cat isn’t hidden anymore,” Mourinho whimsically claimed. “The cat’s running wild; things are being done without any shame. It’s running wild.

“Two hours before a game, a player from a Spanish team that has earned three points for the prestige of Spanish soccer—that doesn’t seem normal to me. But now it does seem normal, because the cat isn’t hidden anymore.”

ftbpro_01m4zyjjef5b.title: U.K. Government Satisfied With ‘Most Extreme’ Outcome in Man City Case
ftbpro_01m4zyjjef5b.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer12:30 PM EDTMan City could be at the mercy of the Independent Football Regulator. / Loannis Alexopoulos/Anadolu/Getty ImagesThe U.K. government is happy to see Manchester City’s owners forced to sell the club if that is what the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), created in 2025 and empowered to intervene and act in situations like this, considers the correct thing to do.

City have been found guilty of almost all of the charges against them for breaching financial rules, following a multi-year Premier League investigation and hearing overseen by an independent commission. The club continues to deny wrongdoing and has filed an appeal, a process expected to conclude sometime in January 2027.

U.K. prime minister Andy Burnham has found it difficult to condemn Manchester City. In his former role as Mayor of Greater Manchester—office he held from 2017 until this past summer—he welcomed the impact of Abu Dhabi investment into his city beyond just the football club.

Even since the guilty verdict, which outlined “sham” contracts disguising owner investment to bump up spending against the rules, Burnham said he would be “really concerned” if Sheikh Mansour was forced to sell the club. “They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and building Manchester City into the global force that it is.”

But Manchester City was built into that “global force” by orchestrated cheating for nine years. The club began cooking the books a year after the 2008 takeover and didn’t stop until City were in a position to dominate from a platform constructed through dishonesty.
This is not a case of low-level rule breaking, or even cheating on the field—the players themselves won match after match in good faith.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Sheikh Mansour (right) has owned Man City since 2008, served by club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesLisa Nandy, the U.K. government’s culture secretary, offers a harder voice than Burnham.

“I want to be crystal clear that, whilst we are really grateful to investors who come from all over the world to invest in our clubs and help to ensure their viability and their success, they are custodians, both of their clubs and of the game,” she told talkSPORT.
“They have a responsibility to play by the rules and uphold the rules.”

The government itself will not intervene in the process. The original guilty verdict has been made and it will now be for the appeal panel to preside over. Nandy is clear that the government’s only role is to ensure that integrity is respected and protected.

“That is the right and proper role governing, it’s to protect that integrity and put the fans back at the heart of football where they belong,” she added. “That’s what we’ve done with the Football Governance Act and the Independent Regulator, and it's now for football to step up and make a determination in this case, and really meet this moment.”
One of the jobs of the Regulator is to protect clubs from bad or rogue owners.

“If the allegations are upheld [at appeal], the Independent Football Regulator can intervene. He can investigate the ownership and, at its most extreme, he can compel the owners if he believes they're not fit [to run] the club,” Nandy stated.

“We’re not there yet. It's absolutely right that Manchester City get the right to defend themselves and they do strongly refute the allegations. But in the event that they do not believe that a club is in safe hands, we’ve fought tooth and nail to give the Independent Regulator the power.”

Despite concerns from onlookers about the risk for soured relations between the United Kingdom and United Arab Emirates potentially leading to government intervention to soften the blow on Manchester City, there appears to be little appetite for it.
The Regulator, led by David Kogan, is confident that interference is not an issue and will use the full extent of the power it has if deemed necessary.

“The prime minister’s capable of saying whatever he wants to say,” Kogan told Times Radio this week. “You asked me whether we have had any interference politically in any of the judgments we’re making, and I’m telling you, categorically, we have not.

“We will take a judgment based on evidence. Once the appeal has been heard by the independent commission of the Premier League, we’re going to look at that evidence closely, we’re going to actually have powers of investigation ourselves, and that will be what governs what we [the IFR] do.”

ftbpro_01m500cf8qj2.title: Jose Mourinho’s Bullish Team Decisions Are Costing Real Madrid
ftbpro_01m500cf8qj2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew HeadspeathOct 15, 2026José Mourinho is persisting with a team selection that doesn’t work. / Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP via Getty Images“The first half was the coach’s fault; the second half was the players’ fault,” José Mourinho told reporters after Real Madrid’s exhilarating 4–3 win over Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, spreading the blame for the shortcomings that left his team needing to overturn a two-goal deficit inside ten minutes.

Mourinho was welcomed as a returning to hero to the Stadio Olimpico and left as a victor. And yet, the result raised questions about whether “the Special One” still knows how to set up a team for success.

Madrid found themselves outclassed in the opening half against Roma and were fortunate to go in 1–1 at the break. Operating between the lines, attacking midfielder Matías Soulé was left free far too often, while Wesley regularly strode forward from right wingback unmarked.

Mourinho swapped over his wingers, Vinícius Jr and Yan Diomande, at halftime but the problems persisted and Los Blancos—through a combination of defensive lapses and a lack of intensity—found themselves 3–1 down by the hour mark.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
The decision to hook off Vinícius Jr and Denzel Dumfries for Endrick and Arda Güler swung the momentum back in Madrid’s favor, while Roma retreated and retreated until the comeback felt unstoppable.

The final eight minutes of the 90 will be consigned to history as one of the great Champions League comebacks—statistically the fastest turnaround of a two-goal deficit—and turned a major embarrassment into a moment of triumph for Madrid.
In the end, Mourinho’s subs dug Madrid out of a hole in Rome, but the manager’s lineup choices put them there in the first place.

Vinícius Jr’s form is a worry. / Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty ImagesMourinho went to Italy set up to counter, with both Vinícius Jr and Diomande on the wings, instead of Arda Güler—who has been, by some distance, Madrid’s most creative player this season.

Vinícius, amid a foul run of form, regularly failed to track back against the threat of fellow Brazilian Wesley, leaving Marc Cucurella exposed and was anonymous again in attack. No player other than Manu Koné—who played only 17 minutes—had fewer than the No. 7’s 22 touches all game.

The 26-year-old is becoming a serious headache for Mourinho; one that he doesn’t seem to quite know how to deal with. Mourinho has handled Vinícius Jr with kid gloves so far, but hasn’t been able to get a tune out of the misfiring superstar.
With each passing game, it gets harder and harder to justify why he is still in the lineup beyond the fact he is a huge name who has just signed a huge contract extension.

Madrid’s midfield balance is still not right. / Danilo Di Giovanni/Getty ImagesMeanwhile, in midfield Mourinho persists with a double pivot of Federico Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni—a duo that has struggled to provide the kind of game control Madrid have badly needed since Toni Kroos’s exit in 2024.
Both players are willing runners and effective at what they do, but together they lack the balance and nous to dominate the engine-room battle in the bigger games.
Neither was able to impose themselves on Wednesday and—though it is not Mourinho’s fault—the failure to land Rodri this summer remains the elephant in the room.

The one midfielder who did arrive from Manchester City, Bernardo Silva, has been little more than a relief option, while Mourinho hasn’t felt inspired to try other, more creative combinations such as Güler in a deeper role.

Mourinho has persisted with Dumfries this season. / Danilo Gemito/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty ImagesIn defense, Denzel Dumfries has seemingly become the manager’s preferred right back option, starting seven of 10 matches so far this season. However, it is yet to become clear what the Netherlands international offers going forward or backward, while Trent Alexander-Arnold—a genuine creative outlet—languishes on the bench.

Güler’s introduction for Dumfries helped change the game, with the Türkiye star grabbing two assists. Meanwhile, Endrick—a player starved of minutes all season—made Madrid fans question why he has been left unopened in the box for so long, after his own decisive cameo.
The positive takeaway is that the bench is deep at Madrid. The negative is that Mourinho doesn’t seem to have the measure of his best starting XI.

ftbpro_01m500w9eqnm.title: ‘Failed’—Landon Donovan Sent Scathing Social Media Attack From Ex-USMNT Teammate
ftbpro_01m500w9eqnm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 15, 2026Landon Donovan was called out on social media this week. / Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty Images (Donovan), Ronald Martinez/Getty Images (Johnson)Former U.S. men’s national team striker Eddie Johnson has unloaded on his compatriot Landon Donovan, taking to social media to berate the prominent pundit for talking “so much s---” about the current generation of American talent despite supposedly having “failed” himself.
Johnson also used his Instagram post as a vehicle to tell his ex-teammate: “I did everything you did with fewer opportunities.”

There are multiple layers to this fascinatingly vicious takedown from Johnson, who won 33 of his 63 international caps alongside Donovan between 2004 and 2014. To begin with, there is the source of the 42-year-old’s ire; Donovan’s discussion about unfulfilled talent on a recent episode of his podcast, Unfiltered Soccer.

The former USMNT striker played down the expectations surrounding Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old phenom who became the youngest male senior goalscorer in the history of the national team over the fall friendlies. “I am measured and calm because I, unlike a lot of new soccer fans, have seen this story happen over and over,” Donovan warned.

“I saw it with Freddy Adu. I saw it with a guy you won’t even remember, Santino Quaranta. I saw it with Eddie Johnson. I saw it with Gio [Reyna] and seen how it’s progressed. There will be the next superstar at some point. It might be Cavan. I’m hoping it’s Cavan, or maybe it’s Julian Hall.”

Johnson’s post leads with a screenshot of an article carrying these quotes, although the top line of the editorial is surreptitiously doctored to cover the writer describing Donovan as “a formerly hyped teenager who made it big.”
The caption offers Johnson’s rebuttal to Donovan.

Landon Donovan barely made an impression at Bayer Leverkusen. / Lars Baron/Bongarts/Getty Images“I can’t speak for Freddy Adu or Santino Quaranta or Gio Reyna but I will speak for myself Landon Timothy Donovan. You talk so much s--- about every other young upcoming player in the past but yourself lol why don’t we talk about the five years you were in Germany and failed and ran back to MLS [because] you weren’t good enough? Why don’t we speak about this?”

This is in reference to the time Donovan spent on the books of German top-flight side Bayer Leverkusen between 1999 and 2005—that much is evident thanks to a screenshot of the player’s Wikipedia page Johnson has included on the second slide of his post.

Donovan became one of the youngest Americans ever to sign a professional contract with a European club by joining Leverkusen in February 1999 at 16. After two years in the reserves without making a single senior appearance, the Californian forward spent almost four years on loan with MLS outfit San José Earthquakes.

Donovan would return to Germany in 2005. “I am ready for everything that Europe has to throw at me,” he said at the time. Playing opportunities were not one of those things flying his way; the forward could only muster nine appearances, earning just a pair of starts while failing to score a goal.

A move back to MLS in his early prime at 23 with LA Galaxy brought Donovan the playing time he so craved. “I didn’t care about playing at Bayer Leverkusen—they were in the Champions League and all this—I didn’t give a f---, I just wanted to play soccer,” the outspoken forward would later reveal to The Guardian. “So I’m glad I got out of there as quickly as I could, because I wanted to play. I needed to be happy.”

Landon Donovan doesn’t pull his punches. / Steph Chambers/FIFA/Getty Images“One of the best considerably (sic) players in our country failed in Europe early in his career no one killed him but he’s killing all these young players that have done more then he ever has done in Europe.”

Donovan is as forthright on the topic of other players’ career as he is about his own. The notable podcaster, pundit and color commentator famously ripped apart USMNT superstar Christian Pulisic after it emerged that the AC Milan forward had asked to skip the 2025 Gold Cup.
Pulisic’s father was unimpressed while his teammate Tim Weah called the cluster of retired pros in the media, with Donovan as their figure, “those guys chasing checks” who are “really evil.”

Eddie Johnson never quite made it in Europe. / Ezra Shaw/Getty Images“I got time today. You played in a World Cup, I played in a World Cup, you played in a U-17 World Cup, U-20 World Cup, Olympics, I did the same—what make (sic) you different then a kid from Bunnell Florida. I did everything you did with fewer opportunities and [I’m] still considered one of the best strikers this country has seen!!”

Thanks to Johnson’s light schedule in midweek, he found time to conclude with a defense of his own career. The former Fulham and Preston North End forward did not take kindly to being used as an example of a wonderkid who fizzled out.

There’s no doubt that Johnson started quickly. The proud Floridian was the youngest ever player drafted into MLS at 16 before making his debut for Dallas Burn three months later. Johnson scored in his first four USMNT appearances and would have eight goals across his opening eight games for the national team. Over his remaining 55 internationals, Johnson scored just 11 times.

After turning down advances from Portuguese giants Benfica, Johnson joined Premier League outfit Fulham aged 23. The striker made just six appearances before he was loaned to Cardiff City, where he became a cult hero despite scoring only two goals in 32 games. A spell in Greece and a loan at Preston never saw Johnson rediscover his best MLS form.

ftbpro_01m503fdwcag.title: Wrexham Are Going Around in Circles As Phil Parkinson Faces Familiar Questions
ftbpro_01m503fdwcag.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay1:00 PM EDTWrexham were booed by some supporters after defeat to West Brom. / PA Images/Getty ImagesIt was hoped Wrexham had turned a corner after their record $48 million summer transfer spend. Instead, it looks like they might be going around in circles.

Almost a month after defying the odds to win when it mattered most against Southampton, questions are once again being asked of manager Phil Parkinson after his men collected just one point from their last two matches. Some sections of the Racecourse Ground crowd even booed the team at full-time on Tuesday, so disappointed by the lackluster performance against West Bromwich Albion.

What is worrying is how many similarities there are to Wrexham’s poor start to last season. What is reassuring is that they went on to record their best-ever finish in the second tier, finishing seventh—a position that would secure a playoff spot under this season’s revised format.

It is that paradox that makes for such an interesting mood among supporters. For some, patience is key. There is a belief that once the new signings are properly settled and key players return from injury, it might take just one win for the Red Dragons to find their form and take flight once again.

For others, the fact that Wrexham are back in this position after a record summer of spending is simply not good enough. They are no longer underdogs, and with such clear ambitions of reaching the Premier League, they cannot afford to spend the early stages of the season playing catch-up.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Phil Parkinson has guided Wrexham to three promotions. / Matthew Ashton/AMA/Getty ImagesParkinson will get more time to turn things around and retains the faith of co-chairmen Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds. There is an acceptance that results and performances have not been good enough, but the league table can be easy to sensationalize this early in the season, when a single win can dramatically alter a team’s standing.

The Red Dragons are theoretically just one win away from 10th place, a position that would likely change the mood and silence some of the alarm bells that continue to ring. Of the teams in the top 10 after 10 matches last season, only four finished there. Four others ended the campaign in the bottom 10.

However, the same argument works in reverse: Wrexham are also just one defeat away from the relegation zone and have yet to beat any of the four teams currently below them in the table this season ahead of their home match with bottom side Preston North End this weekend.
It all feels like déjà vu. Wrexham were 18th at this stage last season, with 10 points from their opening 10 matches. They are currently 17th, with 11 points from their first 10 games.

Ipswich Town were 11th at the same stage last season and went on to secure automatic promotion. Derby County, who sat 21st, finished eighth, while Norwich City climbed from 20th to ninth. It is only fair to point out, though, that the team occupying Wrexham’s current position last season went on to be relegated.

Parkinson believes the division remains as congested and competitive as it was last season. Wrexham were 15th heading into Boxing Day before a remarkable festive run propelled them up the table and back into the playoff picture, where they ultimately fell agonizingly short.

There are crumbs of comfort for the optimists willing to look for them, though it is understandable why others want to brush them aside when they were promised a greater feast this season. The Red Dragons remain inferior to the league’s best teams and have yet to evolve tactically beyond the foundations they laid last season.

All too often, the game plan relies on moments of individual quality to produce positive results, even when that quality is unreliable. Kieffer Moore looked to have delivered another such moment against West Brom in midweek.

It was a similar story last season, when Josh Windass almost single-handedly dragged Wrexham into playoff contention by scoring seven of their 13 goals during the closing weeks of the campaign. That was a remarkable contribution, but one they could not count on being repeated this season—a concern compounded by Windass’s current injury problems.

Mike Williamson took the lead on the transfer front this summer. / Cody Froggatt/PA Images via Getty ImagesQuestions also need to be asked about the summer recruitment, during which CEO Michael Williamson took charge of transfer negotiations while the club awaited the arrival of sporting director Steve Nickson.

Williamson insisted the club was “comfortable” with its striking options as Wrexham stuck with Moore and Sam Smith. Meanwhile, it was baffling that they allowed defenders Dan Scarr and Lewis Brunt to leave but brought in only one replacement for the pair.
Those problems should not be repeated now that Nickson is at the club. However, the elephant in the room is that Wrexham now have a CEO and a sporting director who did not appoint Parkinson.

Although both are understood to have good working relationships with the manager—Nickson even went for a pint with Parkinson two days after Wrexham were thrashed by West Ham—their own success ultimately depends on the first team’s fortunes.

Wrexham reached a low point against West Ham United. / Harvey Murphy/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesParkinson still has time to turn things around, and he has done so before. But Wrexham know this cannot continue indefinitely when there is so much momentum behind the club.

ftbpro_01m50800s5cs.title: The 10 Best Players of Champions League Matchday 2—Ranked
ftbpro_01m50800s5cs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 15, 2026Europe’s biggest names headlined this week’s Champions League action. / Ferda Demir/Getty Images (Yamal), Branislav Racko/AFP/Getty Images (Barcola), Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty Images (Saka)The stars were out on Europe’s biggest stage this week, lighting up the Champions League across two chaotic days of league phase fixtures.

The return to club soccer following the September-October international break got even better when the top teams on the continent faced off in Europe’s premier club competition. Eighteen matches unfolded during Matchday 2, headlined by a marquee clash between Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester City.

The back-to-back Champions League winners carved apart the Cityzens, while Real Madrid completed a vintage comeback against Roma. Barcelona breezed past Galatasaray, much like Liverpool’s dominant win over LASK. Arsenal also collected three points, as did Club Brugge and Aston Villa, among others.

The common thread among all the matches? Players, across all areas of the pitch, stepped up under the bright lights, earning a place in Sports Illustrated’s rankings of the top players from this week’s European action.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Arda Güler saved the day for Real Madrid. / Isabella Bonotto/Anadolu/Getty ImagesJosé Mourinho raised eyebrows when he left Arda Güler, Real Madrid’s best playmaker, on the bench against Roma. The Türkiye international could only sit and watch as his team went down 3–1 before an hour had even eclipsed on Wednesday. Güler was promptly thrown onto the pitch and tasked with spearheading a comeback at the Stadio Olimpico. The 21-year-old answered the call in dramatic fashion, using his magical left foot to breathe life back into Los Blancos. It was his expert ball from the corner flag that Endrick headed home to make it 3–3 in the 85th minute. Five minutes later, it was once again Güler’s sublime delivery—this time from the opposite corner flag—that Antonio Rüdiger buried to steal all three points.

Erling Haaland bagged a brace in Manchester City’s lopsided defeat.  / Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesIt was a frustrating and embarrassing night for Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium. The Cityzens faced off with defending cup holders Paris Saint-Germain and were quickly humbled after stringing together eight consecutive victories.  The silver lining for Enzo Maresca’s side was Erling Haaland. Without the Norway international, an already dreadful night would have turned downright humiliating. When City were down for the count, Haaland leapt into action—literally. The No. 9 beat goalkeeper Matvéi Safónov with a powerful header to get the hosts on the scoresheet and then bagged his brace with a calm right-footed finish.He honestly could’ve had a hat-trick if the crossbar didn’t deny another header. Haaland’s goals weren’t enough as City fell 4–2 to PSG, but he was the long bright spot for a team already under a microscope.

Bukayo Saka (center) put on his cape for Arsenal. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal boss Mikel Arteta rolled the dice against Lille on Tuesday and started a largely rotated side at the Emirates Stadium. The gamble did not pay off for the Spanish tactician, who was likely as underwhelmed as the sea of the red shirts in the crowd once the halftime whistle sounded. Once Jurriën Timber broke the deadlock in the 64th minute, Arteta made a triple-change that included Bukayo Saka. The winger replaced Noni Madueke and instantly made his presence felt.From the right wing, Saka picked out Eberechi Eze with a pinpoint ball that was slamming into the back of the net seconds later. Then, the England international got on the scoresheet himself, slotting home a cool strike to solidify Arsenal’s 3–0 win.

Stas Pokatilov bagged his first-ever Champions League clean sheet. / Stu Forster/Getty ImagesChampions League debutants Sabah picked up their first win in Europe’s premier club competition on Tuesday, defeating Slavia Prague 2–0. The hero  in Baku? Stas Pokatilov.The goalkeeper stood on his head to keep a clean sheet. He made six saves, becoming the first man across all competitions to blank Slavia Prague this season. The 33-year-old faced 18 shots in a game the visitors tallied an xG of 2.14, yet he made sure they walked away without a single goal. Pokatilov earned a place in the official Champions League Team of the Week for his heroics between the posts.

Achraf Hakimi (right) put in a stellar display against Manchester CIty. / MB Media/Getty ImagesIn reality, this entire list can be full of PSG players after their dominant win over City. A few truly stood out, though, and one was Achraf Hakimi. The right back so often earns the most praise for his efforts going forward, but he put on a defensive clinic on Wednesday in Manchester. Hakimi drew the unenviable task of keeping the electrifying Jérémy Doku quiet—and he did his job so well that the winger was hooked at halftime.Hakimi was not fooled by any of Doku’s quick moves or cheeky footwork. He held his ground every time, inviting the 24-year-old to get by him one-on-one. The City man found no success against the fullback, who hardly broke a sweat locking down one of the Premier League’s best attackers.

Ross Barkley put on a show for Aston Villa. / Marc Atkins/Aston Villa FC/Getty ImagesNo, it’s not 2016. Ross Barkley turned back the clock in tremendous fashion on  Wednesday, playing like a man possessed in Aston Villa’s 6–0 win over Fenerbahçe.The 32-year-old commanded Unai Emery’s midfield double pivot and left his mark all over the pitch. He set up Nicolas Jackson’s second goal in the 39th minute, converted a penalty after the restart and then made it 5–0 with a left-footed strike from the top of the box.Barkley’s impressive outing would be further down this list had it come against tougher opposition. Still, his three goal contributions dished out a worthy reminder of the skill he so often displayed at Everton and Chelsea in the prime of his career.

Ousmane Dembélé continued his Champions league exploits.  / Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesAdditional rest is doing Ousmane Dembélé a world of good. The Frenchman sat out of PSG’s Ligue 1 clash with Le Mans at the weekend, prolonging his return to club soccer to Wednesday night in Manchester.By the 15th minute, he was already on the scoresheet, finishing off a sequence he started down the right with a simple header. Dembélé was once again at the heart of the action soon after Haaland pulled one back for City, diminishing any hope of a comeback for the hosts when he picked out Maghnes Akliouche through a swarm of sky blue shirts.  He wasn’t the only player in blue and red to tally two goal contributions on the night, but he was all over the pitch for the defending cup holders, shading a heat map like it was a watercolor painting. The way Dembélé leads the attack is why Luis Enrique’s men were able to put four past the Premier League-leaders.

Lamine Yamal is in a league of his own. / Ahmad Mora/UEFA/Getty ImagesThere’s no one in the world playing like Lamine Yamal right now. The Barcelona phenom is a walking highlight reel, adding a new otherworldly trick to his arsenal nearly every time he laces up a pair of boots.Yamal couldn’t find the back of the net in the Catalans’ 4–1 rout over Galatasaray, but his pair of brilliant assists was more than enough to earn him the Man of the Match honors. Hansi Flick’s side went down the tunnel deadlocked at 1–1 and then the teenager took over the second half. Yamal lofted a pass onto the head of Fermín López, who easily headed home the team’s go-ahead goal. Then the winger faked a rabona, dribbled down the byline and found Anthony Gordon to make it 3–1 in the blink of an eye.It was nothing more than a skills display in the second half from the newly crowned World Cup winner.

Nicolò Tresoldi carried Club Brugge to victory. / Marco Bertorello/AFP/Getty ImagesThe final two spots on our list go to the hat-trick kings. Nicolò Tresoldi is up first after he found the back of the net thrice in Club Brugge’s chaotic 4–3 win over Inter on Tuesday. The 22-year-old showed out for Germany’s U-21 side during the September-October international break and carried his form right to the Champions League. Tresoldi answered the call for his team every time it needed a big moment. The forward opened the scoring against Inter with a successful penalty in the 30th minute. He then scored Brugge’s go-ahead goal after finishing off a great play from Carlos Forbs, beating his defender for pace to send the ball into a gaping goal. Tresoldi made it 3–1 just 11 minutes later when he buried the rebound from Forbs’s saved shot. Brugge needed every one of his goals—and another from Romeo Vermant—to survive against Inter.

Bradley Barcola finally delivered a statement performance for Liverpool. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesThe pressure was mounting on Bradley Barcola. The blockbuster signing was without a single goal contribution in his first six games for Liverpool this season, adding to the team’s woes up top. It felt like only a matter of time before a player of Barcola’s skill figured it out—and he did just that in Tuesday’s 6–3 win over LASK. The France international scored his first goal for the Reds ... and then his second and third.Barcola rifled home a sublime first-time strike to open his Liverpool account and then bagged his brace 13 minutes later. He completed his hat-trick in the second half, using his speed to blow by his marker inside the box and get on the end of a tantalizing ball from Jeremie Frimpong. LASK were hardly at the same level as Andoni Iraola’s men, but take away nothing from Barcola’s breakout performance.

ftbpro_01m508w41kdy.title: ‘Very Complicated’—Ronaldo’s Portugal Career in Fresh Doubt After Sister’s Revelation
ftbpro_01m508w41kdy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer2:30 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo felt disrespected during the recent international window. / Lise Åserud/NTB/AFP/Getty ImagesIt is “more likely” than not Cristiano Ronaldo has already played his last match for the Portugal national team, according to the icon’s sister.

The bold claim follows Ronaldo storming out of camp earlier this month after an apparent disagreement with manager Jorge Jesus. The 41-year-old, Portugal’s greatest ever player and the world record holder in men’s international soccer for both caps and goals, is though to have felt disrespected, accusing Jesus of an “absolute breach of trust.”
Ronaldo later apologized to the Portuguese people and his teammates, and said he would accept punishment from the nation’s soccer federation for his conduct.

Taking his medicine appeared to draw a line under the situation for the Al Nassr superstar. He was provisionally suspended, as per the federation’s rules on walkouts, and could be banned from representing his country for between one and six months.

Ultimately, a return for the UEFA Nations League knockout phase from March onwards—Ronaldo has said his final two dreams in pro soccer are claiming another Nations League title and hitting 1,000 career goals—seemed plausible.
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future with Portugal is as uncertain as ever. / Carlos Rodrigues/Getty ImagesBut fresh doubt has been thrown onto that by the words of his eldest sister, Elma Aveiro.

“It’s more likely a ‘no’ than a ‘yes,’” she said, via A Bola, in reference to Ronaldo returning to the Portugal roster. “I think both [Cristiano and Jesus] are hurt. They experienced it, not me. I’m speaking for my brother. I think it's a situation that’s stalled. We’ll see what happens.
“It’s very complicated. When we’re betrayed, it’s very difficult to go back to normal.”

If Ronaldo doesn’t return, it remains to be seen whether the future would include a standalone farewell match, like the one great rival Lionel Messi just had with Argentina. Either way it would still be a sad and abrupt end to one of the greatest international careers there has ever been.

“My feeling is one of sadness because the Portuguese people unfortunately forget what has already been done and think that things should be done differently now,” Aveiro said, clearly believing the five-time Ballon d’Or has been mistreated. “I'm speechless. It’s very difficult to see my brother go through this. He is one of the people who least deserved this.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Ronaldo is increasingly ineffective at this level. / Joe Buvid/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesRonaldo’s other sister, Kátia Aveiro, claimed with confidence that the 2026 World Cup would be his ‘last dance’ with Portugal, so it was slightly surprising to see his association with the national team continue as normal at the first opportunity following the tournament. Clearly, the words of his immediate family members don’t always ring true on this particular subject.

But Messi went out on his own terms, choosing the 2026 World Cup final to be his last meaningful action in an Argentina jersey. There is an argument to suggest that Ronaldo should have hung up his Portugal jersey and walked away some time ago, before it reached this point.
Ronaldo is an all-time great and a freak of nature. But playing at an objectively easier level in Saudi Arabia has undoubtedly helped prolong his club career—which he plans to end in 2027.

His numbers started to decline from superhuman level once he left Real Madrid aged 33, but spiked once more upon leaving Europe behind. It’s surely no coincidence that Ronaldo’s 2023–24 season with Al Nassr, during which he turned 39, was the first for nine years in which he averaged at least 1.0 goals per game in league play—something he managed five times for Real Madrid.
At the international level, his impact has been in decline for a while. Ronaldo was ineffective at the 2022 World Cup, aged 37, and was eventually dropped during the tournament.

He has maintained a record of scoring against much weaker teams, typically in a qualifying context, but failed to score at all at Euro 2024. Ronaldo was a hindrance more than a help in a frustrating 2026 World Cup opener against DR Congo in June, and two goals against a debuting Uzbekistan ended a humiliating run of blanks in major tournaments at 10 matches.
Clinging on like he has done lacks the dignity Ronaldo deserves.

ftbpro_01m50cy4440j.title: ‘I Apologize’—Martinez Walks Back Explosive Man Utd Rant After Emergency Meeting
ftbpro_01m50cy4440j.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 15, 2026Lisandro Martínez is trying to rectify a tense situation at Old Trafford. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United center back Lisandro Martínez revealed he had a “positive conversation” with Michael Carrick and the club’s leadership on Thursday in a new statement that contained a public apology.

Martínez turned heads when he went on a spectacular tirade after the Red Devils’ 2–0 defeat to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League. The Argentine targeted sporting director Jason Wilcox and Co. for the club’s underwhelming summer transfer window and subsequent dreadful start to the 2026–27 season.

The explosive rant threw Martínez’s future into question, especially since his contract expires at the end of the season, though United have the option to extend it another year. Significant backlash followed, prompting the defender to release a lengthy statement on social media in which he  explained his point further and shouldered the blame for the players’ not delivering on the pitch.
Less than 24 hours later, another Instagram story appeared on Martínez’s profile that contained a new statement, one taking on a very different tone than his previous comments.

Lisandro Martínez let it rip after Manchester United’s Champions League defeat. / Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA/Getty Images“Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager,” he wrote. “It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after the game.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologize.

“Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognize that my words in that moment did not help with that. I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.
“With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together.”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Manchester United are on a five-game winless run. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesMartínez’s new statement was clearly meant to instill a sense of unity back at United after the player  criticized the club’s hierarchy. In a matter of two days, he went from calling out Wilcox for not doing more this summer to asserting “every single person” at the club is “doing everything possible” to get the Red Devils back to their former glory.

Despite walking back his comments and claiming the situation is now in the past, Martínez’s original point still rings true. United had an underwhelming summer window, focusing on a midfield rebuild instead of bringing in much-needed defensive reinforcements.

Overlooking the backline was bad enough, but the club’s midfield signings have wildly underwhelmed in the early stages of the season. United paid £48 million ($63.7 million) for Andrey Santos who is simply not up to the task. Carlos Baleba only has two appearances to his name after a lengthy ankle injury. Youri Tielemans has looked like the best new addition—and that’s not saying much for the inconsistent, slow Dutchman.

All the while, Carrick’s backline is repeatedly abused, conceding in all but one of the team’s nine matches across all competitions this season. United’s lone clean sheet came against Champions League debutants Sabah back in September.
Sure, United might have moved on from the tense situation with Martínez, but the problems he highlighted and hinted at are still defining the Red Devils, who are winless in their last five matches.

Manchester United are desperate to get back to winning ways. / Denis Doyle/Getty ImagesAfter such a tirade against his own club, Martínez was likely looking at some sort of internal punishment. Last season, Mohamed Salah was dropped by Liverpool manager Arne Slot for a similarly explosive rant at Elland Road. Chelsea also suspended Enzo Fernández for openly flirting with a transfer.

Dropping Martínez for this weekend’s match against Leeds United would not have been a surprise, given the circumstances. But now that things have seemingly been smoothed over, Carrick cannot afford to keep the Argentina international out of his lineup.

United’s already thin defensive ranks are even worse off after a cruel international break. Carrick is once again expected to be without Luke Shaw, Noussair Mazraoui and Patrick Dorgu for the Premier League clash. Matthijs de Ligt is back available after a lengthy spell on the sidelines, but throwing the Dutchman into a tough game against Leeds is rather unwise, considering he hasn’t played a second of soccer since November 2025.

Carrick needs Martínez, and United need a win. The two simple facts have the power to brush a rather volatile situation under the rug, especially now that the center back issued a public apology and emphatic backed the club.

ftbpro_01m51znc8men.title: Arsenal Plot Wildly Unpopular Job Cuts Days After Bumper Arteta Contract Extension
ftbpro_01m51znc8men.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:30 AM EDTArsenal are making some tough cuts. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal are preparing to make no fewer than 60 staff members redundant just weeks after handing Mikel Arteta the biggest salary of any manager in the Premier League, multiple reports state.

Arteta will take home over £20 million ($26 million) annually after putting pen to paper on a lucrative new contract earlier this month, with those negotiations held while an external consultancy group was brought in to find ways to cut costs elsewhere.
A report from theThe Telegraph says this has led to 60 imminent redundancies across off-field areas. The specific roles involved have not been made clear.

News of Arsenal’s decision has been widely panned, particularly given the timing in relation to Arteta’s new contract and news that midfielder Declan Rice is closing in on his own new deal with a salary that could eclipse £350,000 ($460,000) per week.

Clearly, those funds will dwarf anything earned behind the scenes at Arsenal, where revenue increased by £319 million ($423 million) between 2022 and 2025, and has left many questioning the ethics behind the decision.

Indeed, Arsenal pride themselves on club values that include “championing each other,” “acting for a winning culture” and “doing the right thing (even when no one is looking).” The news that 60 members of that community are being jettisoned was destined to be met poorly, regardless of how Arsenal can dress it up.
Mikel Arteta’s new contract comes at an awkward time. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesArsenal may be a soccer club, but above all, it is a business. It would not exist without money.

Club accounts show that, despite the positive feeling on the pitch, Arsenal have actually made a loss for seven years in a row, including in 2024–25, when record revenues of £691 million ($917 million) were posted.

Operating costs have also risen, from £148 million ($196 million) up to £201 million ($266 million) across the 2024–25 campaign, with last season’s accounts potentially showing another rise when they are eventually released.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Bringing those costs down is crucial and so, with the mind-spinning finances on offer in the first team, it is never easy to see clubs looking at other areas of the business. Manchester United received a similar response when cutting over 300 jobs between the summers of 2024 and 2025 as part of a series of unpopular financial decisions.

Arsenal will argue sustainability and, without knowing the inner workings of the entire workforce, it is impossible to know whether they are right or wrong, but doing so while continuing to contribute to the wild finances of manager and player salaries is certainly a choice.

ftbpro_01m51zndbwmb.title: Chelsea Predicted Lineup vs. Everton: Sterner Test for Alonso’s Winning Formula

paragraphs: By James Cormack12:30 PM EDTChelsea ran amok against Bournemouth after the extended break. / Mike Hewitt/Getty Images“Complete performance” is how Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso described the thumping win over Bournemouth last weekend, so the bar is set high for the trip to Everton in Saturday’s early game.
The Blues capitalized on another quick start to put five past Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge, with Alonso’s subtle tactical changes facilitating their most impressive outing of the season to date.
Everton’s new ground was the site of a bleak nadir for Chelsea last term, as the now-departed Beto struck twice in a 3–0 victory for the Toffees.

The Blues suffered on their previous away day at Brentford with a depleted group, and although the travelling side have been hit with a significant injury blow ahead of this encounter, last week’s emphatic triumph should allow confidence to exude from Alonso’s side when they meet the unbeaten Merseysiders.

ftbpro_01m5227n0v4z.title: Lisandro Martinez Learns Punishment From Man Utd Outburst
ftbpro_01m5227n0v4z.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:45 AM EDTLisandro Martínez did not help ease the pressure at Man Utd. / Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/Getty ImagesManchester United are reported to have fined center back Lisandro Martínez for his public criticism of club officials earlier this week.

In the aftermath of Tuesday’s 2–0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, a furious Martínez suggested those responsible for transfers should take more of the blame for the club’s recent struggles, insisting the squad were not set up for success after an impressive end to the 2025–26 season.

A lengthy statement on social media saw Martínez acknowledge frustration may have got the better of him, but contained no apology. United had to wait until Thursday for that, with Martínez posting another statement and insisting the situation was now “behind us.”
BBC Sport report the process of moving forward also includes a fine for Martínez, who accepted formal punishment for speaking against the hierarchy.
Manager Michael Carrick will, therefore, be free to pick Martínez for Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Leeds United. Just what role the Argentina international will play remains to be seen.

Navigating this issue is the latest challenge for Michael Carrick (left). / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesUnited are, understandably, keen to move on from this, but the fallout is likely to drag over well into 2027.

Central to this issue is Martínez, whose contract is due to expire at the end of the campaign. United do have the option to extend it by a further 12 months and would likely to do to preserve his value, but working out a way to keep him in the squad beyond next summer is going to be tricky, with Martínez clearly unhappy with the direction of the club.

That narrative has gone viral over the past few days and will undoubtedly have landed on the social media feeds of the world’s biggest players, some of whom would now have second thoughts about joining United if their ambitions are as lofty as those proudly boasted by Martínez.
Resolving both issues falls on the shoulders of United’s sporting department—the very same people whose every move will now be in the spotlight. Any bump in the road would only make things worse.

Despite what those upstairs at Old Trafford might want you to think, the aftermath of Martínez’s comments will be felt for a long time. The only real ways to move on and rebuild trust is to either splash the cash in the transfer market or, more reliably, to simply start winning matches.

Pressure is unsustainably high on United and manager Michael Carrick right now. Sunday’s trip to old rivals Leeds will not provide the hospitable environment the Red Devils would appreciate right now, and any more negativity could have drastic consequences.
