ftbpro_01m5241y6g3f.title: Andoni Iraola Provides Injury Updates on Key Trio of Isak, Gakpo & Szoboszlai
ftbpro_01m5241y6g3f.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:35 AM EDTCody Gakpo (left) and Alexander Isak (right) have both been battling issues. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesAndoni Iraola is seeking an immediate response from his Liverpool side when they travel to face Brentford on Saturday—and the Spaniard could be boosted by returns of key personnel from injury.

A tough 3–0 defeat to Manchester City saw the Reds boss taste defeat for the first time since his summer switch to Anfield, with a handful of fitness issues undoubtedly causing him a real headache since the return from the international break.
Liverpool have been thin both in attack and in midfield, with some massive names forced onto the sidelines in recent weeks. Thankfully, those trying times look to be coming to an end.
Here’s the updates on Liverpool’s injury list after Iraola’s prematch press conference.
Alexander Isak’s comeback is imminent. / James Gill - Danehouse/Getty ImagesInjury: ThighPotential Return Date: Oct. 17 vs. Brentford

Striker Alexander Isak was enjoying a hot run of form before being struck down by a thigh problem on international duty. He has missed the last two games across all competitions, with his absence even more noteworthy considering Hugo Ekitiké is also sidelined. Lewis Koumas, 21, has been thrust into the limelight.
It is hard to see Isak starting against Brentford, but Iraola confirmed the Sweden international is in with a chance of returning off the bench if he can prove his fitness before kickoff.
“We have to wait and see, I think it is still very early but the same way I said that they were not available for the previous games, I will leave the chance open this time.”
Cody Gakpo was struck down with the Netherlands. / Stefan Koops/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesInjury: AnklePotential Return Date: Oct. 17 vs. Brentford
Iraola offered a similar update on Cody Gakpo, with the message of “wait and see” suggesting the winger could be about to make his return from an ankle injury.

Gakpo, like Isak, was threatening to turn the difficult narrative that has surrounded his stint at Anfield before being struck down. He has two goals and four assists in his six appearances this season and Iraola would love to get that sort of productivity back to his forward line.
Dominik Szoboszlai’s stint on the sidelines could be a short one. / Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty ImagesInjury: HamstringPotential Return Date: Oct. 17 vs. Brentford

The final member of the trio flirting with a comeback is midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai, whose imminent return would arguably be more important than either Isak or Gakpo because of other issues in Iraola’s squad.

Ryan Gravenberch is suspended for the match after his red card last time out against Manchester City, leaving Alexis Mac Allister as the only senior midfielder available alongside youngsters Trey Nyoni and James McConnell. Getting Szoboszlai back would be huge.

Hugo Ekitiké still has a long way to go. / Michael Miller/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesInjury: AchillesPotential Return Date: TBC
A ruptured Achilles tendon back in April left Liverpool playing the long game with striker Hugo Ekitiké, well aware his absence could extend into 2027.
The Frenchman is not expected back in training any time soon, but Iraola was eager to remind fans: “That was always the plan. He is still doing very well according to the plan.”

ftbpro_01m524jesyns.title: Premier League Predictions: Everton Host Goal-Crazy Chelsea, Man Utd at Rivals Leeds
ftbpro_01m524jesyns.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 16, 2026João Pedro’s in terrific form for Chelsea.  / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty Images It won’t be long until we’re lamenting another international break, folks, so enjoy this run of Premier League fixtures while they last.

England’s top tier returned after a three-week absence last weekend, with much of the discourse surrounding Manchester City’s trip to Anfield off the back of their guilty verdict for breaching the competition’s financial rules over a nine-year period. The extent of City’s indiscretions means the division is seemingly in flux until we learn of the sanctions and outcome of the club’s appeal.
Still, like Enzo Maresca’s side, we must navigate the upcoming period as if the darkest of clouds aren’t looming overhead.

A full slate of Premier League fixtures is upon us once more, with Gameweek 7 starting in Merseyside and culminating in the considerably more desperate half of north London. There’s scope for plenty of thrills and spills in between.
Here are Sports Illustrated’s predictions for how things might pan out.
Chelsea thrashed Bournemouth last weekend. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesPrediction: Everton 1–2 Chelsea

Xabi Alonso hailed a "complete performance" from his heavily scrutinized Chelsea side last weekend in their 5–1 rout of the winless Bournemouth, who were the latest to succumb to an early blitz from the Blues.
Jordan Henderson scored a rare brace in Chelsea’s feel-good victory, as João Pedro and Morgan Rogers each continued their productive starts to the campaign.

They’re kicking off the weekend‘s action at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, where they were comprehensively beaten in March. Everton’s goalscorers in that 3–0 victory, Beto and Iliman Ndiaye, are no longer at the club, but the Toffees are yet to taste defeat in the Premier League and are on course for their longest unbeaten run to start a season since 2006–07.
They’ll be emboldened by their impressive record at home to Chelsea, with the visiting Londoners winning on just one of their previous nine visits to Everton.
Bradley Barcola has arrived. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesPrediction: Brentford 2–2 Liverpool

Liverpool had the chance to blow off some steam midweek, putting LASK to the sword in a 6–3 victory. It certainly wasn’t an occasion for defensive purists, but Reds supporters were left hugely encouraged by Bradley Barcola’s official arrival and the performance of Florian Wirtz.

Barcola, who didn’t have much of a preseason due to the World Cup and lingering transfer interest, failed to step up against Manchester City last weekend before scoring his first three Liverpool goals in Austria.

The French winger will aim to take that form into Saturday’s contest away at Brentford, where Liverpool were beaten 3–2 last season. The Reds have had their issues at the Gtech Community Stadium over the years, and Keith Andrews‘s side are unlikely to make this bout an enjoyable one for the visitors, given the physical make-up of their roster.

Hull City are now just a victory away from topping Derby County’s record-low points haul of 11—a tally that plenty thought they’d struggled to bypass once their return to the Premier League was confirmed via a scrappy playoff final victory over Middlesbrough.

The Tigers fought back to earn a result against Everton last time out, taking their tally up to nine from six games. It’s 2008–09 all over again, just without a manager who dons an earpiece. Sergej Jakirović has proven himself to be a canny tactician at the highest level, elevating a roster that isn’t exactly laden with talent and extracting every ounce of potential.

Hull are a difficult team to beat, and they arrive at Fulham feeling as if they belong. The Cottagers, on the other hand, are in a state of consternation. Álvaro Arbeloa is struggling to garner widespread backing, and defeat could add to his growing number of detractors. The former Real Madrid boss desperately needs to win here.
Enzo Maresca’s Cityzens were humbled midweek. / Lexy Ilsley/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesPrediction: Man City 4–1 Ipswich
Paris Saint-Germain were hardly the saviours of soccer midweek, given the nature of their rise to European soccer’s summit, but plenty were undoubtedly content with Man City’s midweek defeat.
It was a first-class affair that could’ve 5–5. PSG‘s early exhibition set them on course to victory, yet City created enough in the second half to earn an unlikely point.

ftbpro_01m525ccrj0t.title: Agent Reveals Why Nico Williams Barcelona Transfer Fell Apart
ftbpro_01m525ccrj0t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 PM EDTNico Williams’s agent has had his say on what really went on with Barcelona. / Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty ImagesNico Williams’s agent has revealed that his client’s proposed move to Barcelona fell apart over playing time concerns.
Williams was tipped to leave Athletic Club in consecutive summers in 2024 and 2025, with a host of Europe’s usual suspects circling the winger who played a major role in Spain’s Euro 2024 triumph.

Barcelona’s interest reached the most advanced stage in 2025, with the La Liga champions prepared to pay Williams’s €58 million ($65 million) release clause to unite him with his Spain teammate Lamine Yamal in attack. The proposed move sparked fury among Athletic fans who famously defaced a mural of their star player.
Ultimately, the deal fell apart with Williams going on to sign a surprise contract 10-year contract extension, keeping him locked in at San Mamés until 2035.

The true reasons for Williams transfer U-turn were not fully clear at the time, though Athletic posted a video to their social channels of the star announcing: “When you have to make decisions, for me, what weights most is the heart.
“I am where I want to be, with my people, this is my home. Aupa Athletic!”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Nico Williams is the one that got away for Barça. / Ion Alcoba Beitia/Getty ImagesWilliams’s agent Félix Tainta has claimed that concerns over playing time were behind Williams opting not to move to Camp Nou, more than emotional ties to Athletic.

Going deep on the transfer saga on the podcast Los Fulanos, he said: “We all know about Barça’s interest in the summer of ’24, after the European Championship. Barça, Arsenal, Bayern, Liverpool, PSG … I could name them all. Everyone wanted Nico, and it’s not easy for a player to say no to all these clubs.
“From there, we talked to Barça. Athletic knew because I kept them informed about the situation at all times, even though Athletic and Barça... Athletic was angry with Barça for their methods.

“From then on, I initiated conversations, and there came a point in the negotiations, in the situation, where Nico couldn't be without playing. Nico is a Formula 1 car, and if I go to your house, I can't take on your problem, and I made that clear to Barça.

“We decided that if there weren't certain guarantees, we couldn't risk Nico not going there to play, with a World Cup coming up, and not just with a World Cup, but because he's a professional who has to perform his duties.”
After the deal collapsed, Barcelona ended up signing left-sided forward Marcus Rashford on loan in 2025, while they paid €80 million ($90 million) for Anthony Gordon last summer.

Iñaki and Nico Williams have become symbols of Athletic Club. /  Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesWilliams, 24, is tied down at Athletic Club until 2035—one of the longest professional contracts of any player in Europe’s major leagues. However, his new deal does still include a release clause.

At the time, it was reported that the new buyout number had been set at more than 50% higher than it was previously, thus suggesting it would take at least €87 million ($98 million) to be able to start negotiations.
In the same interview, Tainta defended Williams’s loyalty to Bilbao but insisted his client did seriously consider leaving Athletic Club prior to renewing his deal, calling the winger “ambitious.”
“Nico had the idea of ​​leaving,” Tainta added. “He's ambitious, and at Athletic you know the limitations, you know you're not going to win a Champions League, maybe a league title.

“In the end, when he kept saying 'not here, not here, not here, maybe here, but the situation and what it entails doesn't add up,' there's another twist where you think, 'what if I renew?' I brought it up with him, I said, 'This is what it is, do you want me to fight for it?' And he agreed. And that's how we renewed.”

Raised in the Basque Country and having joined Athletic’s academy at the age of 11, Williams is a symbol of a club with a one of the strongest senses of community in European soccer. His older brother Iñaki, 32, has also spent his entire senior career at the club despite regular transfer links away.

ftbpro_01m52780za88.title: Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Brentford: As Many As Four Key Players Could Miss Out
ftbpro_01m52780za88.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath9:30 AM EDTRyan Gravenberch (left) is suspended after his red card vs. Manchester City.  / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesLiverpool return to Premier League action this Saturday, desperate to bounce back after the crushing disappointment of last weekend’s hammering against Manchester City.

Wednesday’s 6–3 win over LASK in the Champions League was a necessary morale booster for Andoni Iraola’s team, who must get their domestic campaign back on track after seeing their unbeaten run ended emphatically by City 3–0 at Anfield.

The Reds are ninth in the Premier League table and are already nine points off the pace just six games in—a trip to the Gtech Communituy Shield to face in-form Brentford one of the last venues Iraola would choose to get things back on track.
Indeed, the Bees haven’t lost in 12 matches, have beaten both Chelsea and Tottenham handily at home in recent weeks and currently sit above Liverpool in the table for the first time since 1938.

With Alexander Isak, Dominic Szoboszlai and Cody Gakpo all likely out through injury and Ryan Gravenberch suspended, the task at hand gets even more complicated for Iraola. Here’s how he could line his side up.

GK: Alisson—The Brazilian is virtually unimpeachable as Liverpool’s No. 1, but he will not be happy with conceding three times in each of his last two outings.
RB: Ronald Araújo—Despite Jeremie Frimpong shining from full back during the week against LASK, Araújo’s defensive stability is likely to be preferred for the tougher test of Brentford.

CB: Jérémy Jacquet—21-year-old Jacquet has been thrown in at the deep end on his first season as a Liverpool star, but has excelled in the role. He was substituted after an hour against LASK presumably with an eye on the weekend.

ST: Lewis Koumas—With Isak, Ekitiké and Gakpo all absent, it’s another big chance for the academy graduate who offers busy, youthful energy if not the elite goal threat Liverpool crave.

ftbpro_01m5295dfcxc.title: Chelsea Learn Crushing Reece James Injury Timeline After Knee Surgery
ftbpro_01m5295dfcxc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:30 AM EDTReece James is back on the sidelines. / Rob Newell - CameraSport/Getty ImagesJust as Chelsea thought they had escaped the era of Reece James injuries, the Blues have been sucked right back in.

The Blues captain has a horrible history of fitness problems, missing a total of 97 matches across 2022–23, 2023–24 and 2024–25 before what looked like a turnaround last season, when a hamstring injury in March was his only real issue.
Unfortunately, James is now back on the sidelines once again, having been struck down during training with another injury that appears destined to derail his current campaign.
The specifics of James’s injury are not yet known. As Chelsea revealed his latest issue, they simply confirmed he had a knee problem.
James has subsequently undergone what Chelsea described as “minor” surgery on his knee, kickstarting another road to recovery for the right back.
James went down in training. / Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesChelsea refused to put a timeline on James’s recovery, but subsequent reports confirmed fans will not be seeing their captain for a little while.

The belief is that James is set for around three months on the sidelines, meaning he will not be back in action until January. That may not be a reflection of the severity of James’s injury but perhaps shows the caution that will be taken with his return.

Chelsea will know there can be no risks with James’s eventual return to the pitch and are likely to take it far slower than they would with any other player, even if it means keeping him sidelined for a longer period.

A comeback in mid-January would see James return shortly after the midway point in the Premier League season. Sunderland on Jan. 16 would represent three months but subsequent meetings against Leeds United, Nottingham Forest or Manchester United could prove more realistic targets.

Xabi Alonso (left) has had plenty of different ideas for James. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesPin-pointing Chelsea’s exact plan to cope without James is complicated by the fact it is hard to work out his position on the pitch.

James is a natural right back but has spent just 22 minutes in that role under Xabi Alonso, who tended to use him as a central midfielder. We saw similar from Enzo Maresca last season as the Blues sought to manage James’s ongoing fitness issues.

A semi-permanent transition to midfield appeared to be on the cards with Chelsea’s summer transfer business. Marco Palestra was recruited from Atalanta to operate as a star right back, while the Blues put a huge price tag on Malo Gusto. Ironically, neither have actually been regular starters in that position, with Pedro Neto transitioning from winger to wingback.

Chelsea are stocked at right back but are likely to feel James’s absence in midfield, where the collapse of Lamine Camara’s Deadline Day move has left Alonso’s squad slightly short.

Early injury issues to Jordan Henderson and Moisés Caicedo look to have been navigated, with the pair now options alongside 22-year-old Roméo Lavia—another whose long-term injury record is cause for concern—and summer signing Valentín Barco.
Chelsea will hope to have the options to cope with James’s injury until the January transfer window, when a fresh decision could be made if he hits any setbacks.

ftbpro_01m52a145hxt.title: Real Madrid Predicted Lineup vs. Sevilla: Diomande Primed to Start With Vinicius Jr Out

Last weekend’s 1–0 win over Villarreal was dominated by talk of Vinícius Jr’s red card, while José Mourinho’s men eventually recovered from 3–1 down to earn a spectacular 4–3 victory against Roma in the Champions League midweek.
With the return to domestic action this Sunday, Madrid would surely be keen for a nice, routine win over Sevilla with zero excess drama.
Leaving the Bernabéu with all three points this weekend will also ensure Madrid don’t lose any more ground on league leaders Barcelona prior to the Clásico on Oct. 25.
Here’s how Real Madrid could line up to face Sevilla.

ftbpro_01m52bzk204k.title: ‘Genuinely’—Carrick Reveals Man Utd Squad’s Reaction to Martinez Fiasco
ftbpro_01m52bzk204k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott10:30 AM EDTLisandro Martínez’s comments proved an unwelcome distraction for Man Utd. / Alex Livesey - Danehouse/Getty ImagesMichael Carrick says he couldn’t be happier with how Manchester United’s squad have reacted to Lisandro Martínez’s scathing criticism of the club’s hierarchy—and insisted he’s ready to move on with the center back as part of his squad.

A furious Martínez pulled no punches in a postmatch interview following Tuesday’s 2–0 loss to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League, criticizing United’s summer transfer activiity while singling out technical director Jason Wilcox.
A public apology was subsequently released and reports state Martínez was fined by United for his behavior. As far as Carrick is concerned, the matter is settled.

“It’s done, really,” he stressed in his Friday news conference. “We’ve moved on from that. It was one of those things, I think Licha’s come out and acknowledged the situation, and as a group, we’ve moved on.

“It’s really not a drama for us as a group. I think the boys have trained really well. This morning, there was a really good feeling around this squad. A really good feeling, I have to say they were in really good spirits and trained really well, so we’ve moved on pretty quickly.”
Asked specifically whether Martínez would be part of his matchday squad for Sunday’s meeting with Leeds United, Carrick confessed: “He’s part of the squad, yeah.”

Jason Wilcox (left) was at the heart of the controversy. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesThe most surprising thing about Martínez’s rant was his mention of United’s technical director, slamming Wilcox for his recruitment plans during the summer and accusing those responsible for making decisions of failing to build on the team’s strong end to last season.
When Martínez apologized, there was no direct mention of Wilcox, but Carrick warned critics not to read into the situation and insisted everyone at United was satisfied with the outcome.

“I think he’s released his statement and realized he’s made a mistake,” Carrick said. “That’s enough for all of us to move on with. From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what’s been done has certainly been enough. We’ve moved on. We’re definitely not looking back at it now.

“I understand emotion at times. We ask for passion. We ask for emotion. We ask for fire. We ask for players to care. There’s a way of doing that, and that’s already been acknowledged. We need to carry that intensity and that willingness and that togetherness and that spirit and everything else you can bring with that. As a group, we’ve got to use that and we’ve got to use it in the right way.”
Carrick also insisted he does not have any issues with the rarity with which Wilcox speaks to fans.

“I’ve got absolutely no problem with how that’s ... for me, sitting here, talking to you guys, leading the group, leading the team, leading the football club from this position ... we’re all in it together. We’re a really tight-knit group, so I’m happy to face anything you want to ask me.”

Michael Carrick was delighted by the response. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesAs part of the process, Martínez is understood to have held clear-the-air talks with Carrick and those involved from above.
Carrick was pressed for details of that meeting but assured those in attendance that they had not missed much, with all parties quickly moving on after Martínez’s apology.

“From the outside, you’re after some big information about big discussions,” he laughed. “It was pretty simple, we all understood the situation and what it meant. Licha’s made his statement and he acknowledges that it was a mistake from him, and that was it.

“We’ve got a really good feeling within the club, from the inside. Results-wise, it hasn’t gone to plan as of late, but the spirit, the togetherness ... again, I said it today, today was one of the better training sessions we’ve had and you can see there was a real sense and a feeling in the group that we want to do something about this situation and we want to do something about it really quickly, hence why I’m saying about moving on.

“We all acknowledge where we’re at, we accept that, we understand the situation that came up after the game, but it’s been dealt with. We have moved on. Genuinely moved on. There’s actually a freshness about the group today that I really like.”

paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath9:00 PM EDTBrentford have enjoyed the superior start to Liverpool.  / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images (Brentford’s badge), Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Liverpool’s badge) It’s back to Premier League business for Liverpool this Saturday, with the high-scoring Champions League victory over LASK In midweek a much-needed salve following the bruising defeat to Manchester City.
It’s still somewhat difficult to get a read on where Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are at in their development currently, after a mixed bag of an opening to the new era.
Brentford will provide a thorough inspection of the Reds’s credentials on Saturday, with the Gtech Community Stadium ranking as one of the least charitable places to visit in the league these days.

The fact that Liverpool travel to London with several key players missing only make the challenge greater, but this is exactly the sort of game Iraola needs to be targeting for three points if his team are to be taken seriously as more than just top-five contenders.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Liverpool need Bradley Barcola on song. / Karl-Josef Hildenbrand/PA Images via Getty ImagesLiverpool need a spark to get their Premier League campaign going, but Brentford away is far from the ideal fixture to go looking for it.

The Bees are one of only three teams left unbeaten this season and have swatted aside Chelsea and Tottenham at the Gtech Community Stadium already in 2026–27. Incredibly, Brentford currently sit above Liverpool in the table for the first time since March 1938.
Still, Keith Andrews’s side have drawn four of their six matches in the Premier League so far, and have made a habit of leaving points on the table—see the games against Leeds and Sunderland.
With several big Liverpool names out, Bradley Barcola will need to bring his midweek hat trick boots for this one.
Nathan Collins remains a major doubt as he continues to recover from a calf injury, while summer signing and fellow center back Jannik Schuster is also a question mark with a knock.

Further forward, Brentford are set to be without Mikkel Damsgaard (ankle), Antoni Milambo (ACL) and Kevin Schade (shoulder). In the absence of top scorer Schade, Dango Ouattara could get a start out on the left.

Former Liverpool forward Fábio Carvalho is also in contention after scoring during his brief cameo in the win over Chelsea. He is one of three former Reds on the Bees roster along with Caoimhín Kelleher and Sepp van den Berg.
Brentford predicted lineup vs. Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Kelleher; Kayode, Ajer, Van den Berg, Diouf; Yarmoliuk, Janelt; Anthony, Lewis-Potter, Ouattara; Thiago.
Liverpool likely remain without Alexander Isak (thigh), Cody Gakpo (ankle) and Dominik Szoboszlai (hamstring), who have all missed the last two matches through injury.
Ryan Gravenberch’s red card against City last weekend adds to Iraola’s selection headache with the midfielder another player unavailable for the trip to London.
As a result, academy graduates Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni are in line to feature—with the latter set for his first-ever inclusion in a Premier League starting lineup.
Conor Bradley, Hugo Ekitiké and Giovanni Leoni are Liverpool’s long-term absentees.
Liverpool predicted lineup vs. Brentford (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araújo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Nyoni, Mac Allister; Muñoz, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas.

ftbpro_01m52fnrhxqq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 16, 2026The hosts have seen 13 goals scored in their six games this season—the visitors a huge 28.  / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Everton’s badge), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Chelsea’s badge) Chelsea make the trip up to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton in Saturday’s early Premier League kickoff.

Despite a wretched end to their summer transfer window, leaving themselves short in attack and at fullback, the Toffees are a game away from enjoying their longest unbeaten run to start a Premier League season since 2006–07. David Moyes‘s side slumped toward the finish line last season, meaning they missed out on European soccer. Still, they’ve returned with a rejuvenated presence at the start of the new campaign.
A 10-point haul leaves them fifth in the table at this early juncture, and they’re only ahead of their upcoming opponents on goal difference.

Chelsea’s sole blemish was a 3–0 defeat at Brentford before the international break, when Xabi Alonso was without an array of stars for a tricky away encounter. The Blues responded last weekend by producing what the manager described as a “complete performance” to thrash Bournemouth 5–1.
While plenty have scrutinized the start of Alonso’s reign, Chelsea are in a pretty good place and will eventually benefit from their free midweeks.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

João Pedro is in superb form. / Steffan Bowen/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesChelsea’s first trip to Everton’s new home returned a 3–0 defeat. Robert Sánchez had a nightmare between the posts, as the energetic Toffees bullied a team briefly managed by Liam Rosenior.

Early kickoffs can often be dreary affairs, benefiting the away side. The Blues have struggled on their days out to the blue half of Merseyside in recent years, winning on just one of their previous nine visits. The bulk of these woes came at Goodison Park, yet their defeat here in March suggested it wasn’t merely Everton’s classic amphitheatre that was the issue. It’s something in the air.
Perhaps this time things will be different.

Everton should have Vitalii Mykolenko back in action. /   Moyes offered a "much better injury update" ahead of Chelsea’s visit, with Everton potentially having starting left back Vitalii Mykolenko available for the game.

Mykolenko missed last week’s draw at Hull due to a knock he sustained while playing for Ukraine during the recent break, forcing Jarrad Branthwaite into a wide position as cover. While Moyes must decide whether to take a chance on Mykolenko’s fitness or take a cautious stance given the lack of alternatives, Everton are pretty settled elsewhere.

Thierno Barry missed a bucketload but did get his goal at Hull last weekend, and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is building on an excellent debut season with the Toffees. The midfielder, who lines up against his former club here, scored and assisted in Everton’s 2–2 draw.
Everton predicted lineup vs. Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry.

Chelsea could be unchanged from last week’s beatdown of Bournemouth. /   There’s every chance Alonso names an unchanged team for Satuarday’s trip to Merseyside, given how well Chelsea performed against Bournemouth last week.

Moisés Caicedo’s return to the Blues’ midfield proved imperative, and the Ecuadorian will likely be partnered by Jordan Henderson again after he struck twice against the Cherries. While Alonso has Roméo Lavia to call upon, captain Reece James has undergone knee surgery that’s set to sideline him for months.

Summer arrival Marco Palestra made his Premier League bow last weekend, and he’ll be pushing fellow newbie Pep Chavarría for a starting role before the November international break. Young defender Josh Acheampong replaced Wesley Fofana last time out, and there’s no reason for Alonso to make another change.
Emmanuel Emegha remains sidelined for the visitors, and Jamie Gittens will spend a few weeks on the sidelines after picking up an injury on international duty.
Chelsea predicted lineup vs. Everton (3-4-2-1): Martínez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Henderson, Caicedo, Chavarría; Palmer, Rogers; Pedro.

ftbpro_01m52j0mk46p.title: ‘Red Flag’—USWNT Legend Tobin Heath Slams State of Current Team
ftbpro_01m52j0mk46p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely1:30 PM EDTTobin Heath held nothing back. / Dustin Satloff/NWSL/Getty Images (Heath); Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images (Emma Hayes)Eight months out from the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil, all eyes are on the four-time champion U.S. women’s national team. USWNT legend and two-time World Cup winner Tobin Heath doesn’t like what she sees.

Emma Hayes’s squad regrouped this month for the first time since June to battle reigning world champions Spain in two-consecutive friendlies on home soil. La Roja, ranked No. 1 globally, secured a 2–0 victory in the first clash last Saturday, while the No. 2-ranked Stars and Stripes managed a late comeback for a 2–2 draw three days later. Many considered the series to be a preview of the World Cup final, which is set to be played out at the hallowed Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro next July.

“I feel like you could really feel the sense that these were the top two teams in the world going against each other,” Heath said on The RE—Cap Show podcast, hosted after the first friendly alongside fellow USWNT legend Christen Press. “... But there’s still a lot more questions than there are answers for the U.S. women’s national team.”

For Heath and Press, Spain outclassed the USWNT in so many fundamental ways, all of which have been glossed over—or completely disregarded—by the current players and staff and, as a result, could prove detrimental come World Cup time.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Spain was missing one of its best players, Aitana Bonmati.  / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty Images“The biggest red flag is losing to Spain 2–0 at home against a Spain team that was missing some of their biggest, most important pieces,” Heath pointed out. “And yes, you can argue that we were missing [Naomi] Girma and [Emily] Sonnett and [Catarina] Macario, Sam Coffey, but then you go down the list of who Spain was missing: [Mariona] Caldentey, [Aitana] Bonmatí, Claudia Pina, Cata Coll, Esther González, Olga Carmona, Vicky López, Mapi León, that’s a lot of players, that’s a lot of star power that Spain was missing.”

Perhaps Spain’s biggest absence was Barcelona midfielder Bonmatí, who is a three-time Ballon d’Or winner and FIFA Women’s Player of the Year (2023–2025). She also won the 2023 World Cup Golden Ball. The 28-year-old is currently sidelined as she continues to recover from a broken leg suffered last winter, but is expected to return to action in the coming months and certainly by the World Cup.

Despite missing several stars, Spain still cruised to victory in the first match, scoring both goals within the span of the first 15 minutes. Nevertheless, it wasn’t because Spain played particularly well at Audi Field. Rather, the USWNT wasn’t up to par—a reality Spain was abundantly aware of and eager to expose, no matter how disrespectfully.

USWNT was outclassed in every part of the field. / Brad Smith/ISI Photos/Getty Images“I actually thought Spain didn’t have a good game at all,” Heath added. “Not just that, Spain playing the high aggressive line that they played with, to me, was the biggest slap in the face to the U.S. team.

“To a [USWNT] front line of Alyssa Thompson, Sophia [Wilson] and Trinity Rodman, to play a high line in international football against those types of attacking players was, to me, so disrespectful. The fact that they still held us to not scoring was their coach saying, ‘How aggressive can we be against this U.S. team in terms of a back line and not get punished for it?’”

Spain’s back four were adamant to push aggressively up the field, which suggests that they didn’t see the USWNT’s forwards as a threat. It is a tactic the defenders also employed in the second friendly. The Spanish defenders ultimately had good reason to do so, as the USWNT’s star-studded front line failed to exploit the space in behind Spain for the entirety of the first friendly and for much of the second one as well.

One could look at the stat line of the first game and see that the USWNT still ended the affair with 13 total shots, 10 of which were on target—way more than Spain’s six total, and assume that the Stars and Stripes did their part attacking-wise. Even in the second friendly, the USWNT had 14 total shots,  six on target. The loss was simply poor luck, and as for the draw, it easily could have been a win with a couple extra minutes. That was certainly the stance manager Hayes took; however, Heath and Press illuminated something much more damning to the storyline.

Trinity Rodman underwhelmed. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images“When you hear Emma speak at the press conferences and you hear the players speak after the game, it’s funny. They’re really hung up on this idea of xG and all of the chances we created,” Heath said of the USWNT’s 3.0 xG compared to Spain’s 0.68, per Hayes.

She added: “Emma says, ‘It’s all about details and execution in the final third.’ I actually don’t even think the U.S. is close to being able to talk about details and execution because I think that fundamentally, the attack is so off in what they are trying to do.”

The USWNT may have generated a lot of chances against Spain; however, they weren’t the right ones. They weren’t the ones that will win games and certainly not a World Cup. To Press, it wasn’t a surprise that none of the 10 shots on target on Saturday actually found the back of the net.

“The biggest difference is watching the Spanish attack progress the ball up into the final third, slow their bodies down, pick their heads up ... play the right pass, the right decision and the right amount of control,” Press said. “Whereas we got a lot more chances, but every single time, you see us run full speed ahead, heads down. We’re not actually picking out the right pass, we’re not picking out the right shot, we are swinging.”

“We went for one out of 10 chances, and we missed nine. Those are the odds ... We have to get higher percentage chances by making better decisions in order to execute ... The best shot you can take is the worst shot that still goes in. That’s how you play the odds.”

Alyssa Thompson (left) struggled to generate meaningful chances on Saturday. / Georgia Soares/USSF/Getty ImagesThere was a similar frenetic energy in Tuesday’s affair. When the USWNT advanced up the field, it was treated as a chaotic rush—as if it were some miracle to have the ball. When the Spanish advanced up the field, it felt inevitable. The only time the U.S. had any sense of control was in the final 10 minutes, which was what enabled the team to knot the game at the very end.

Nevertheless, for the majority of the international window, the USWNT was fundamentally erroneous in the way it progressed up the field, leading to wasteful chances that were never going to find the back of the net. For Heath and Press, this problem extends way beyond minute details and must require a tactical overhaul offensively.
That’s not even the team’s biggest concern, though.

ftbpro_01m52k3xxbt3.title: Man City vs. Ipswich: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m52k3xxbt3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack9:00 PM EDTMan City are out to respond to their Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain. / Kristian Skeile/UEFA/Getty Images (Man City), Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty Images (Ipswich)Manchester City welcome Ipswich Town to the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon as they aim to win their first seven matches of a league campaign for the first time since 1897.

The Cityzens had been perfect (on the field, at least) across all competitions until they encountered the back-to-back Champions League winners on Matchday 2 of the league phase midweek. PSG were mesmeric for 35 minutes on Wednesday, racing into a 3–0 lead that could‘ve easily been five.

However, Enzo Maresca atoned for his starting lineup oversights and made the necessary changes at half time. City’s improvement was drastic, and although they were eventually beaten 4–2, few would have been surprised had they fought all the way back to earn a result. It was a wonderful game of soccer.

Saturday’s clash with the Tractor Boys is unlikely to be so thrilling, but the newly promoted visitors have certainly offered more than mere competence during the first six weeks of the season. Their spirit was crucial to overturning a goal deficit late on against Fulham last weekend, with a 2–1 victory over the struggling Cottagers lifting Gary O’Neil’s side up to 10th in the Premier League table.

After struggling to compete at the highest level under Kieran McKenna two seasons ago, Ipswich seem far better prepared for the rigors of top-flight life this time around. However, that doesn’t mean they should be expected to walk away from the Etihad Stadium with their newfound self-assurance still intact.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Man City have the chance to bounce back against the newly promoted Tractor Boys. / MB Media/Getty ImagesMan City were undeterred by the resentment last weekend, and they should expect the hostilities to gradually fade as we naturally forget about their guilty verdict and wait patiently for the outcome of their appeal and subsequent sanctions.

They’re aiming to join an exclusive club by winning this weekend, with only Chelsea (2005–06) and Liverpool (2019–20) maintaining a 100% start to the Premier League season after seven games. Both, of course, went on to win the title, but neither had 114 financial breaches lingering over them.
Maresca has asserted that this fixture is the perfect “get right” game for the Cityzens after Wednesday’s defeat, and Ipswich may well feel the wrath of the hosts on Saturday.

Phil Foden is ready to make an impact after serving a three-match domestic suspension for his petulant act in the Manchester derby. Foden wasn’t called upon against PSG in the week, but could displace Rayan Cherki in the No. 10 role on Saturday.
Maresca has hinted at rotation in City’s upcoming games, but there will likely be more changes when AEK Athens visit the Etihad on Matchday 3 of the league phase on Tuesday.

Erling Haaland should start against Ipswich, but there could be respite for Elliot Anderson in midfield. Ayyoub Bouaddi was impressive off the bench last time out and is in contention to make his first Premier League start on Saturday.
Enzo Fernández, Marc Guéhi and Rúben Dias are the other players who could earn rests over the next few days.
Man City predicted lineup vs. Ipswich (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, O’Reilly; Fernández, Bouaddi; Ndiaye, Foden, Doku; Haaland.
O’Neil belives his roster will be at full strength on Saturday, even if several players are set to undergo late fitness checks to determine whether they can play a part in Manchester.

Jack Taylor has been out of action since March with a knee injury and is closing in on a return. This fixture may arrive too soon, but he should be back in action before the November international break.

Zian Flemming is pushing Emersonn for the starting role in attack, and marquee midfield signing Exequiel Palacios should come back into Ipswich’s midfield after starting on the bench against Fulham. The Argentine will likely partner Saša Lukić in the engine room, with Florentino Luís making way.
O’Neil has publicly showcased how he’s stymied Haaland and Co. before using a back five, but the Ipswich boss isn’t expected to change shape on Saturday.
Ipswich predicted lineup vs. Man City (4-2-3-1): Walton; Ouattara, Diop, O’Shea, Davis; Lukić, Luís; Maeda, Enciso, Clarke; Flemming.

ftbpro_01m52kp3m8y1.title: Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Real Betis: Red-Hot Champions Chase History
ftbpro_01m52kp3m8y1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas4:00 PM EDTLamine Yamal (left) and Fermín López have had stellar start of the campaign.  / Jose Jordan/AFP/Getty ImagesBarcelona are looking to make La Liga history on Saturday night, but they must overcome a red-hot Real Betis to do so.

The Catalan giants enter the weekend perfect though 10 games across all competitions to start the campaign. Eight of those wins have come in La Liga, and if Barcelona make it nine in a row against Betis, they’ll match a 58-year Real Madrid record as the only teams ever to start the term with a perfect record through nine games in Spain’s top-flight.

Continuing the unprecedented start will be the priority, but Hansi Flick will also have next Tuesday’s gargantuan away Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain on the back of his mind. With such a massive game on the horizon, the German boss could be tempted to rotate his lineup on Saturday.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

/        GK: Joan García—Though rarely tested this term, García has been phenomenal operating almost as a third center back. The Spaniard has swept up every through ball to go in behind Barcelona’s backline, providing the kind of reassurance the champions need to perform at the other end.

RB: Jules Koundé—Eric García struggled significantly against Galatasaray and after a very impressive performance last weekend, Koundé could make consecutive starts in La Liga for the first time this season.

CB: Pau Cubarsí—The potential Golden Boy award winner wasn’t at his best last time out, but the Spaniard’s the star turn in this defense. It’s been an otherwise flawless start of the campaign for Cubarsí.
CB: Gerard Martín—Martín will continue to operate alongside Cubarsí in the heart of defense after yet another injury stopped Andreas Christensen’s quest to challenge him for the starting job.

LB: Xavi Espart—João Cancelo has started consecutive games only once this season and a lot of it has to do with the emergence of Espart. Flick has full confidence in the teenager, who could get the nod to make his seventh start of the term.

CM: Rodri—Barcelona’s midfield anchor completed 113 passes against Galatasaray, but his main assignment on Saturday will be to try and nullify his former Spain teammate Isco, who’s the key to Betis’s attack.
CM: Pedri—Pedri played his best game of the term against Galatasaray. Any notion that him and Rodri don’t work in the same XI has been disproven.

RW: Lamine Yamal—Barça’s No. 10 is simply unplayable at the moment. Yamal’s two assists in the comeback win midweek made it 17 goal involvements already, and only a fool would bet against more coming here.

AM: Fermín López—López might play second-fiddle to Dani Olmo with Spain, but the energetic playmaker is seemingly Flick’s favorite at the No. 10 position currently. His understanding of when to attack the open space is a major reason why Barça have been so devastating.

LW: Karim Adeyemi—Adeyemi’s dream start to life in Catalonia continued with his sixth goal involvement of the term on Tuesday. The German’s bolt of energy and speed stretches defenses all game, making a potential rest for Anthony Gordon all the more tolerable.

ST: Gabriel Jesus—A second start in Barcelona colors awaits Jesus, who has already hit the back of the net three times since stepping in to Raphinha’s shoes up top. The latter is nearing fitness and may see minutes with that PSG clash next.

ftbpro_01m52mby4c0f.title: Real Madrid vs. Sevilla: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m52mby4c0f.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew HeadspeathOct 17, 2026Real Madrid host Sevilla. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Real Madrid), Kristian Skeie - UEFA/Getty Images (Sevilla)This weekend is the game before the game for Real Madrid—the last match in La Liga before a Clásico showdown later this month that really could make or break the season even before Halloween hits.
Los Blancos welcome Sevilla to the Bernabéu this Sunday, needing to make sure they don’t lose any more ground in an already fading title race.

The midweek win over Roma in the Champions League was both exhilarating and confusing. Mourinho could also do with a statement win that quietens some doubters after a shaky few weeks. A third loss already this season would be devastating.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Madrid’s forward line should be too strong for Sevilla despite the issues. /  Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesAfter the abject disappointment of the Madrid derby defeat, Mourinho’s team have responded with back-to-back wins over Villarreal and Roma, but not fully convinced in either.
After preseason relegation fears, Sevilla have started the season relatively strongly, only losing to Atlético Madrid and Barcelona, and sit one place below Los Blancos in fifth.
Luis García’s side won’t be pushovers for a team needing a confidence boost but are unlikely to be able to cope with the attacking might at Madrid’s disposal.
Vinícius Jr’s four-game ban starts the weekend, with the Brazilian now unavailable until November.

In truth, the absence of the badly out-of-form winger may actually help the hosts with Arda Güler, who bagged two assists in the midweek comeback win over Roma, and Yan Diomande—last weekend’s match-winner—set to start out wide.
Real Madrid’s only other absentees are long-term injured trio Ferland Mendy, Raúl Asencio and Rodrygo, but Mourinho has confirmed Éder Militão will make his long-awaited return to the matchday squad.
Real Madrid predicted lineup vs. Roma (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Dumfries, Konaté, Huijsen, Carreras; Valverde, Tchouaméni; Güler, Bellingham, Diomande; Mbappé.
Robbie Ure got off the mark for his new club last weekend. / Clive Brunskill/Getty ImagesSevilla are expected to be missing Marcão (thigh), Jon Guridi (adductor) and Miguel Sierra (shoulder).
Midfielder Giorgi Kochorashvili trained this week and could be available for selection, as could Lucas Stassin and Arouna Sangante.
Scotland international and summer signing Robbie Ure will be looking to build on his first goal for the club, after netting in the 3–3 draw at Levante last time out.
Sevilla predicted lineup vs. Real Madrid (4-1-4-1): Vlachodimos; Igelsias, Castrín, Salas, Suazo; Agoumé; Ejuke, Kochorashvili, Fofana, Correia; Ure.

ftbpro_01m52qvahm4t.title: Man Utd Predicted Lineup vs. Leeds: Carrick Makes Big Martinez Call After Outburst

paragraphs: By James Cormack3:00 PM EDTLisandro Martínez has already faced his punishment for Tuesday’s outburst against the hierarchy. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesLisandro Martínez’s outburst after Manchester United’s 2–0 defeat to Atlético Madrid may have been exactly what supporters wanted to hear, but rarely does such public outcry spark an upsurge.

All is not well with the Red Devils after their bitterly disappointing start to the season continued in the Spanish capital. They’re out of the Carabao Cup and only have wins against newly promoted Ipswich Town and Champions League debutants Sabah to show for their campaign so far. They were fortunate to draw at home to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur last weekend, too.

The issues are staring Michael Carrick in the face, and although he did superbly well to guide Man Utd to third last season, plenty are questioning whether the former midfielder is of the requisite ilk to lead the Red Devils going forward.
Carrick desperately needs some respite from somewhere, and Leeds United won’t have any interest in giving it to him on Sunday.
Here’s how Man Utd could line up at Elland Road.

Martínez drops out of the team. /   GK: Senne Lammens—Carrick at least has stability between the posts, even if Lammens hasn’t been particularly great at the start of the new season.
RB: Diogo Dalot—The ol’ reliable right back will likely retain his spot, given the lack of alternatives.
CB: Leny Yoro—Despite his soft midweek dismissal, Carrick should retain his faith in the young Frenchman at Elland Road.

CB: Harry Maguire—Martínez is on the travelling roster, but it wouldn’t be a surprise if Carrick takes the limelight off the defender for a little while. Maguire is comfortable on the left-hand side of defense.
LB: Luke Shaw—Shaw missed the trip to Spain due to injury and is a doubt for Sunday’s clash. If he’s fit, he has to play.
CM: Kobbie Mainoo—Like Shaw, Mainoo is 50/50 after his midweek absence. Neither of their injuries were significant, and there‘s every chance he makes a swift return to the starting lineup.

CM: Carlos Baleba—It’s been quite the whirlwind for Baleba over the past week, who made his first start for the club on Tuesday after making his debut in the draw with Spurs. Baleba is an imperative figure in Man Utd’s midfield.
RW: Amad Diallo—Amad is easing his way into the season after playing for the first time last weekend. Given Man Utd’s intensity issues, the Ivorian has a big role to play in helping set the tone.

AM: Bruno Fernandes—Carrick’s tinkering with his star playmaker’s role during the week failed to spark Fernandes into action, but he does have an excellent record in this fixture. Man Utd’s No. 8 has nine goal contributions in seven outings against Leeds.

LW: Matheus Cunha—The Brazilian came off the bench against his former club and may find himself back down the left-hand side on Sunday. With Shaw overlapping, Cunha can drift inside. He scored in this fixture last season.

ST: Bryan Mbeumo—Benjamin Šeško may be weeks away from an injury return, and Mbeumo looks considerably more comfortable as Man Utd’s leading man compared to when he’s shunted out wide. He’s no one-on-one dribbler. Get him in the box.

ftbpro_01m52qz4tzps.title: Real Betis vs. Barcelona: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m52qz4tzps.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 16, 2026Barcelona haven’t lost away at Betis since 2011.  / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Betis badge), James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images (Barcelona badge)Barcelona’s perfect season faces its toughest challenge yet, as the unstoppable Catalans visit a very impressive Real Betis on Saturday on the doorstep of making La Liga history.

The reigning La Liga champions have been performing like the best team in the world and are coming off their 10th-straight victory with a 4–1 result against Galatasaray midweek. Against Betis, they have a chance to make history.

Hansi Flick’s Barcelona could become only the second team ever to win its opening nine games of a La Liga season, matching what Real Madrid achieved 58 years ago. The Catalans haven’t just won, they’ve destroyed Spanish opposition to start the term, but the level of difficulty raises significantly on Saturday.

Manuel Pellegrini’s Real Betis are in red-hot form, having lost just once in 2026–27. Betis have already dispatched Real Madrid at home and are currently third in the La Liga standings, just five points adrift of the perfect Barça.
The bout between the two most in-form teams in Spain will be the highlight fixture of La Liga’s weekend action.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lamine Yamal is playing like the best in the world.  / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Betis might be undefeated in their last seven matches, but Barcelona simply look unstoppable at the moment.

Flick’s men have been vastly superior in every game they’ve played this season, and even when there’s been complicated stretches at specific points during games, they’ve always found a way to quickly overcome them and impose their unparalleled dominance.
Betis is a very serious and capable side, but they’ll likely have to outscore the prolific Catalan attack, exposing themselves at the back.
Both teams will throw haymakers, but Barcelona are simply too potent right now. They will escape Seville with their ninth La Liga win on the bounce.

Isco is aging like fine wine with Real Betis.  / Angel Martinez/Getty Images Pellegrini will have a mostly healthy squad, with Junior Firpo, Aitor Rubial and Iker Losada the only notable players not available for Saturday’s clash.
The Argentine boss is expected to deploy his strongest XI, unlike a number of other La Liga teams playing against Barça this season, practically conceding defeat before the game is even played.

Two former Barcelona players should get the nod: Hector Bellerín at right back and the dangerous Ez Abde on the left wing, with the latter fresh off scoring an absolute screamer in the Champions League.

Natan and Diego Llorente will be the center back pairing, with former Real Madrid left back Fran García tasked with containing Lamine Yamal. Speaking of former Real Madrid players, the timeless Isco will operate in the no. 10 role with Marc Roca and Pablo Fornals behind him.
Antony and Juan “Cucho” Hernández complete Betis’s attack, obliged to try to outscore Barça.
Real Betis predicted lineup vs. Barcelona (4-2-3-1): Vallés; Bellerín, Llorente, Natan, García; Roca, Fornals; Antony, Isco, Abde; Hernández.

/      Frenkie de Jong, Roony Bardghji and Andreas Christensen remain unavailable, but Flick’s side could be bolstered by the return of Raphinha, who could resume his record-breaking start of the term after missing the last two games. Still, he’ll likely feature from the bench with fellow Brazilian Gabriel Jesus getting the nod.
Starting center backs Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín will be flanked by a different fullback duo than against Galatasaray, with Jules Koundé and Xavi Espart in line to get the nod on Saturday.
Karim Adeyemi will start, as his personal battle with Anthony Gordon at left winger continues. Yamal is untouchable on the right wing.

Barcelona’s strongest midfield trio should start on Saturday, with the Rodri–Pedri double-pivot looking better every single game and Fermín López operating at the No. 10 with the freedom to push forward whenever Jesus drops deeper.

ftbpro_01m52wev9e95.title: ‘Judged Incorrectly’—USMNT Star Defends Christian Pulisic Amid Heightened Backlash
ftbpro_01m52wev9e95.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 16, 2026Christian Pulisic underwhelmed this summer. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesThe fate of Christian Pulisic has been at the forefront of America’s mind.

For the better part of a decade, the 28-year-old forward has long been considered the face and heartbeat of the U.S. men’s national team; however, he failed to deliver when the Stars and Stripes needed him most. At the 2026 World Cup this summer, he picked up more injuries (two) than goal contributions (one) and possessed nothing of the magic that has come to define his career at soccer’s highest levels.

The team had to lean on new stars, such as Malik Tillman and Folarin Balogun, to still have a magical summer. Pulisic had just 45 minutes of solid play on home soil, and when he hit the ground with yet another injury in the round of 16 against Belgium, it almost felt inevitable.

Pulisic’s lackluster performance followed an even more disheartening spring, in which he suffered a career-worst goal-less drought that dated back to 2025, going 20 matches without a goal for club side AC Milan.

Only exacerbated by Mauricio Pochettino’s youth revolution, many fans and members of the media have been quick to assert that not only should Pulisic no longer be the face of the USMNT, but actually he doesn’t belong on the roster at all. Some have gone even farther to claim that his injury exit in the ultimate 4–1 thrashing by the Belgians was evidence that he has personally quit on the national team.

Former USMNT star Kellyn Acosta has since rushed to his former teammate’s defense. The two are close friends, having played together at the 2022 World Cup, and Acosta believes that what Pulisic brings to the squad is invaluable.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Kellyn Acosta knows a thing or two about soccer fandom. / Tim Nwachukwu/Getty ImagesAcosta took particular issue with people questioning Pulisic’s allegiance to the national team. In his mind, there is nobody more committed.

“That’s so harsh,” Acosta told Herculez Gomez on Vamos Network. “For a guy that’s done so much for the national team, for people just to turn on him as quickly as they have. It’s just spreading like wildfire.

“There’s a difference between saying he’s not performing well and what not, but saying that [he] gave up on [his] team is questioning his character and his love for his teammates, the game and the national team. That gives me a sour taste because I know him personally, and I know that’s not who he is. He is judged incorrectly.”

Pulisic fell to the ground in the 57th minute against Belgium. In attempt to kick the ball, he instead collided with the lower leg of his Belgian opponent, Youri Tielemans, twisting his ankle and knee in the process. Despite initially attempting to play through the pain, he limped off the pitch just before the hour mark. It proved to be the nail in the coffin of the horrific loss, and Pulisic was shown on the bench with his head in his hands in disbelief for much of the remainder of the match.

The star would come to discover that he had suffered a bone bruise and a micro-fracture in his tibia/fibula; nevertheless, critics asserted that he should have played through the pain in the biggest game of his career to date.

Pulisic had to exit the round of 16 match after suffering a leg injury. /  Carl Recine/Getty Images“Obviously he has different circumstances as to why things have happened in the way that they have, [like] him getting injured in the World Cup,” Acosta said. “Sometimes things happen. This is football. This is life.“

In the aftermath of the World Cup, Pulisic has struggled to recover. He remained an unused substitute in AC Milan’s first three matches, a situation that had “upset” him according to Milan manager Ruben Amorim. He has since slowly worked his way back into the starting lineup, yet still has just one goal.

He was also not called up by Pochettino for the fall international window, seeing the Argentine boss select 13 uncapped players, including eight teenagers, instead of the seasoned veteran. Despite Pulisic’s absence, the youngsters cruised to four-straight victories.
Pulisic is experiencing nothing more than a dip in form, according to Acosta, and shouldn’t be so hastily discredited by the soccer community.

“To criticize him at the level that people have, that’s crazy unfair,” Acosta exclaims. “And to even question that he’ll still be in the [player] pool ... I’m like, ‘You guys are crazy.’ A person of his caliber, you’re gonna say that he doesn’t belong within the team, and he shouldn’t be there. You guys are crazy.
“People are just so fickle. I mean, it’s up and down. It’s like they love you when you’re at your best and they hate you at your worst.”

Pulisic will be 31 years old during the 2030 World Cup. / Mao Siqian/Xinhua/Getty ImagesMany have written off Pulisic for the 2030 World Cup. He will be 31 years old at that time, the current age of Acosta. Despite still being an active player for Polish side Pogoń Szczecin, Acosta himself hasn’t featured for the Stars and Stripes since 2023, before his 28th birthday.

ftbpro_01m52yhjhvj3.title: Soccer Fandom in U.S. Sees Unprecedented Surge Following 2026 World Cup
ftbpro_01m52yhjhvj3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 16, 2026The USMNT experienced unprecedented levels of support during the 2026 World Cup.  / John Dorton/USSF/Getty Images When the U.S. won the bid to co-host the 2026 World Cup, one of its main missions was to foster greater interest in soccer across the nation The outcome of that mission has been nothing short of a spectacular success, per a recently released report.

According to research insights group Nielsen, the number of soccer fans in the U.S. has grown by almost 10 million over the past year. Their report indicates that the number of U.S. people who identify as soccer fans rose from 66.8 million to 75.2 million from July 2025 to July 2026, representing a growth of 13%.
The U.S. men’s national team’s thrilling journey to the World Cup round of 16 on home soil no doubt helped ignite that flame of popularity.

“The FIFA World Cup 2026 has served as a powerful catalyst for soccer's explosive growth across North America,” Nielsen’s global head of sports Seth Ladetsky said, per The Athletic. “Our data shows that fandom is not only reaching record highs, but it is also expanding rapidly among younger, diverse audiences and carrying over into major domestic and international leagues.”

In a matter of four years between World Cups, there’s been a 27% increase in soccer fandom across the U.S., with soccer welcoming 16 million new fans. That surge is further evidenced by the unprecedented 2026 World Cup viewership numbers.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Spain’s victory over Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final is the most watched soccer game in U.S. history.  / Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty Images Prior to 2026, the most watched non-USMNT soccer match in U.S. history was Argentina’s win over France in the memorable 2022 World Cup final, with a viewership of 22.3 million. Fast forward four years, and that record was shattered in Spain’s victory against Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final, a game that registered a viewership of 62.8 million in the U.S., per Nielsen.
The 2026 World Cup final is the most watched soccer game in U.S. history, and February’s Super Bowl LX is the only 2026 broadcast with a higher U.S. viewership number this year (124.9 million).

The NFL remains king among sports leagues in the U.S.; however, to put soccer’s rising viewership numbers further into perspective, three 2026 World Cup games broke the previous record for the most-watched non-NFL sports broadcast in U.S. history. The record was previously owned by Game 7 of the 2016 World Series between the Chicago Cubs and the now-Cleveland Guardians, which had a record audience of 40 million.

Millions of fans in the U.S. gathered at FIFA Fan Zones top watch the 2026 World Cup.  / Kevin Carter/Getty ImagesThe challenge now is to progress soccer’s surging popularity in the U.S. over the next four years before the 2030 World Cup comes around. For now, this mission is trending in the right direction.
According to Nielsen’s report, MLS viewership on Fox and FS1“is up 55% among men 18–34 and 29% among adults 18–34 compared to before the tournament [2026 World Cup].”

Other league such as La Liga and the Premier League—the most watched soccer league in the U.S.—have enjoyed significant spikes in U.S. viewership since the start of the 2026–27 season, of no less than 30%.

“People ask us all the time: ‘How’s it going after the World Cup?’” MLS commissioner Don Garber said recently during the Front Office Sports summit. “But that was only a few months ago—leaders of businesses need to think generationally. We started working on our World Cup plan in 2018 when U.S. Soccer won the bid.

Don Garber (right) attended the 2026 World Cup final with Gianni Infantino.  / Eva Marie Uzcategui/FIFA/Getty Images“I keep telling our owners,” Garber added. “‘This is not about tomorrow. It’s about weeks and years after the World Cup when we’ll really capture the opportunity’. That said, our attendances are up, ratings are up, social media is up, merchandise is up—it helps to have Leo Messi—but the future of soccer is super bright because of all the things our stakeholders have done and a World Cup that will be remembered as the best of all time.”

There’s reason to be optimistic about American soccer. The USMNT won its first four post–2026 World Cup matches, thanks in large part to a crop of young debutants—many of them teenagers—that should become key players for Mauricio Pochettino during the 2030 cycle.

The majority of these young talents, such as record-breaking attackers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall, play for MLS clubs, and the league has already started to market its young USMNT stars as a new strategy to maintain its growing audience and perhaps even reach more fans.
Soccer has never been better platformed to finally establish itself among the most popular, mainstream sports in the U.S.

ftbpro_01m535e58z3b.title: ‘Morally Repugnant’—Real Madrid Demand La Liga President’s Resignation Following Nazi Comparison
ftbpro_01m535e58z3b.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:00 AM EDTReal Madrid have long been at war with La Liga president Javier Tebas.  / Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Real Madrid badge), Irina R. Hipolito/Europa Press/Getty Images (Tebas) Real Madrid have called for the “immediate resignation” of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he accused Los Blancos of running a propaganda campaign against referees that reminded him of the “techniques exploited in Nazi Germany.”

Real Madrid TV, the club’s in-house media channel, often broadcasts videos depicting actions Los Blancos believe they’ve been wronged by referees in Spain as part of their strategy to validate their claims against Barcelona in the Negreira case.

The constant attacks from Real Madrid TV prompted Tebas to take to social media to slam Los Blancos, comparing them to the Nazi regime and even mentioning Joseph Goebbels, the propaganda minister of the Nazi party. Real Madrid responded swiftly with a lengthy, five-point statement that ended with them calling for the president’s resignation.

“In response to the statements made by Javier Tebas, president of La Liga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, in which he compares the methods of the Real Madrid management to those employed by Joseph Goebbels, the Minister of Propaganda of the Nazi regime, and points to Real Madrid TV as an instrument of this alleged strategy, Real Madrid declares the following:

“Real Madrid considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone holding two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football resorts to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television. The clarification that he is not referring to Nazi ideology does not mitigate the deeply offensive, morally repugnant, and institutionally unworthy nature of his statements.

Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez has been at was with Javier Tebas since he proposed the European Super League.  / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty Images“It is especially concerning that Tebas uses these statements to question the legitimate actions of Real Madrid and Real Madrid TV in relation to the Negreira case,” the statement said before going on to explain the details of the Negreira case and how Madrid have, in their eyes, been forced to take the matter directly to UEFA because of Tebas’s lack of response.

“Javier Tebas’s repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities,” Real Madrid added. “His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those demanding transparency and regeneration represent, in our club’s view, a genuine scourge for Spanish football.

“For all these reasons, Real Madrid considers that the repeated statements and behaviors of Javier Tebas would be unacceptable in any European sports institution governed by principles of respect, neutrality and integrity, and that they disqualify him institutionally from continuing to hold the positions he occupies.

“Consequently, Real Madrid demands his immediate resignation as president of La Liga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation. Real Madrid. will continue to defend its rights, its institutional prestige, the full clarification of the Negreira case, and the necessary regeneration of Spanish football.”

Javier Tebas has been La Liga president since 2013.  / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesTwo hours after Real Madrid called for his resignation, Tebas responded with another lengthy post on social media, accusing Los Blancos of trying to “destroy” La Liga.

“I’ve lost count of the amount of times that, in 13 years, Real Madrid directors have asked for my resignation or tried to disqualify me,” Tebas wrote. “Complaints with the Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD), directly or through third parties, criminal complaints ... today, again. What’s still yet to come are answers. They confuse neutrality with independence.”

Tebas went on to defend La Liga’s Negreira case investigation and accused Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez of only turning against Barcelona after the Catalans separated themselves from his infamous European Super League project.

“My conclusion: they seek to DESTROY the national competition,” Tebas added. “What they haven’t achieved so far with the Super League, they’re trying with a distorted narrative from their media and their lapdogs. They call it renewal while attacking the prestige of the competition they participate in.”
Tebas finished: “All of this [Real Madrid calling for his resignation] has a name: intimidation. Wrapping it in an official statement doesn’t make it regeneration.”

No doy crédito a la noticia de que el CSD esté estudiando actuar de oficio por mis declaraciones. Si se confirma, espero que ese estudio empiece por leer lo que escribí y por revisar algunos antecedentes.Mis palabras fueron estas:«Ese método recuerda a mecanismos de… pic.twitter.com/AuvLwgxpF9
According to MARCA, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) is considering taking action against Tebas over his comments.
It’s unknown whether the investigation CSD is expected to launch will lead to Tebas’s resignation, but the La Liga president reacted to the news with yet another social media statement.

“I can’t believe the news that CSD is considering taking action for my declarations,” Tebas wrote. “If confirmed, I hope the investigations starts by reading what I wrote and reviewing some background.”

Tebas went on to defend his comparison by stating that he only compared Real Madrid’s communication and propaganda strategy with the Nazi regime, but that “this comparison is only with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology nor, of course, with Real Madrid fans.”

ftbpro_01m53apxy1xe.title: USMNT Wonderkid Mathis Albert Could Be on the Move As European Giants Lurk
ftbpro_01m53apxy1xe.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas11:30 AM EDTMathis Albert has played just once game for Dortmund in 2026–27.  / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images U.S. men’s national team wonderkid Mathis Albert is reportedly considering leaving Borussia Dortmund in the near future in search of more playing time.

The 17-year-old wants regular minutes to continue his development at the highest level, according to Sky Sports Germany. After becoming the youngest U.S. player to feature in the Bundesliga back in April, Albert has played no Bundesliga minutes this term, with his only appearance for Dortmund coming against fifth-tier HEBC Hamburg in the German Cup.

Albert featured in all four games the USMNT played during the September–October international action, becoming the youngest goalscorer in team history when he found the back of the net against Chile. His record was broken a game later when fellow 2009-born star Cavan Sullivan struck against Mexico.

“Sooner or later, probably sooner, [Albert] will get a lot more minutes here at Borussia Dortmund than perhaps half a year ago,” club manager Niko Kovač said after the youngster’s impressive senior international debut.
Yet, Albert hasn’t played a single minute in the two games since Dortmund’s return to action, prompting his interest in a new club.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Mathis Albert (front) instantly made an impact with the USMNT.  / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAccording to Sky Sports, Dortmund have already fended off suitors interested in poaching Albert away from Germany. And not just any suitors.
The report indicates that Paris Saint-Germain tried to sign Albert after winning their first-ever Champions League title in the summer of 2025.

Last winter, Premier League giants Manchester City and Chelsea were reportedly willing to offer up to €20 million ($22.4 million) to acquire Albert. Dortmund were unwilling to let go of the former LA Galaxy academy player, but if Albert pushes for an exit, the German club’s stance might soften.
Still, any move to the Premier League could only materialize next summer after Albert turns 18. And despite his current lack of minutes, the teenager is still highly regarded at Dortmund.

Mathis Albert joined Borussia Dortmund’s academy in 2024.  / Getty ImagesAmid the speculation surrounding Albert’s potential departure, Borussia Dortmund sporting director Nils-Ole Book addressed the teenager’s situation and confirmed the club has a plan to progress his development.

“We really do see huge potential in Mathis,” Book told Sky Sports. “He’s got something truly special about him. He’s a player who likes to take on opponents boldly in one-on-one situations. It’s basically something you can never have enough of, and we certainly don’t have too much of it either.

“That’s why we’re delighted he’s part of our team. We have a clear plan for him. I think it’s really important to keep improving in every aspect, because at 17, you’re certainly not at your peak yet. His chances to play will definitely come, he’s got the talent for it. We’re looking forward to that time.”

Book has a point. At 17, Albert isn’t at an age in which he should expect to be a starter at a club like Dortmund. Switching clubs could actually complicate Albert’s development, forcing him to adapt to a new environment with such little senior experience.
Furthermore, although it‘s exciting for him to be linked with some of the best teams in the world, minutes would also be incredibly hard to come by for him with any of these other reported suitors.

For now, staying at Dortmund to follow Book’s plan could be in his best interest. If he does leave, going to a less demanding European side where he would feature regularly at the highest level could be the way to go.

ftbpro_01m54mp74yx3.title: ‘Definitely’—Michael Carrick Teases January Signings for Man Utd
ftbpro_01m54mp74yx3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:00 AM EDTMan Utd fans have high hopes for the upcoming windows. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick has confirmed the club will look to improve in the January transfer window, sensing a potential “opportunity” to take the next step in their squad rebuild.

Lisandro Martínez’s heated outburst against United’s summer recruitment has put the spotlight firmly on those upstairs at Old Trafford, with technical director Jason Wilcox attracting particular scrutiny after being called out directly by the Argentina international.
The first chance for United to address those concerns will come in January, when Carrick admitted the Red Devils will be exploring their options.
“When the next transfer window comes, you want to plan and you want to make the best of it,” the United boss explained.
“Whatever that looks like at this stage, we don’t quite know. But without doubt, there’s opportunity because the transfer window is open.
“So we’ll definitely be looking at that and trying to come out stronger in whatever way that looks like.”
