Lisandro Martínez’s United future is in doubt. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesThe summer of 2025 was all about the attack. Benjamin Šeško was the headline addition alongside Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo, with a total of £210 million ($280 million at current exchange rate) spent to fix that area of the field.

This year, it was the turn of the midfielders—much to Martínez’s frustration. United struck early to sign Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, before Carlos Baleba arrived from Brighton & Hove Albion to take the total spend on the trio to £155 million ($206 million).

United’s plan is now to switch their attention to defense over the next two transfer windows. A new left back is a priority, with the Red Devils keen on Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall during the summer before ultimately deciding to focus their spending elsewhere. Hall signed a new contract at St James’ Park in September.

A new center back is also on the agenda, and that need is only likely to have grown following Martínez’s outburst. The 28-year-old’s contract expires in the summer, but United do have the option to extend it by a further 12 months.

High-level signings are notoriously difficult to find in the January transfer window, when clubs often over-value their players due to the challenges of finding suitable replacements, but occasional opportunities can be found with players struggling for minutes.

The summer window saw United explore a late move for Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde, only to snub a permanent deal for the Spanish star. Balde has since played just 12 minutes and is expected to be available when the winter window opens.

ftbpro_01m54qqc71gv.title: The ‘Irrefutable Evidence’ Man City Believe Will Prove Their Innocence
ftbpro_01m54qqc71gv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:45 AM EDTMan City are publicly confident. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesManchester City are effectively challenging an appeal panel to question the legitimacy of official Abu Dhabi government documents as they seek to prove their innocence, a report has revealed.

City claimed to have “irrefutable evidence” of their innocence even before they were found guilty of more than 100 major financial rule breaches and have continued to point to that same body of evidence ahead of their formal appeal, with club officials unashamedly confident that they will ultimately win this case.
According to The Telegraph, City’s argument revolves around an attempt to prove that the initial panel were wrong to dismiss a series of Abu Dhabi government documents and key witnesses for the case.

City believe these documents prove that the Abu Dhabi government, of which City owner Sheikh Mansour is a member, was the source of funding for the sponsorship deals being scrutinized and will argue that the panel conducting the initial investigation were wrong to bluntly dismiss them as evidence.

There is also believed to be fresh evidence from the Abu Dhabi government that backs up that argument, which City expect to effectively challenge the appeal panel to decide whether Abu Dhabi officials can be trusted.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Man City’s confidence will be put to the test. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesThe first obstacle for City is securing a date for their appeal. The process is currently still at the stage of appointing a panel to hear the appeal, after which a formal timeline will be set.
Rules state the appeal must be heard no later than 12 weeks after it is lodged. In this case, that would set a deadline of Jan. 21, 2027.

When City officials do get in front of that panel, they will be gambling that the new panel will entertain the same arguments that were bluntly dismissed initially. Their case revolves largely around alleged misinterpretations of the law and claims that their “irrefutable evidence” was wrongly dismissed.

It is a bold strategy, considering the first panel specifically responded to those allegations with a blunt dismissal. “We concluded that it was an ‘explanation’ that the Club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme,” the commission argued.
The appeal panel can reexamine documents and witness testimonies, but is unlikely to hear directly from witnesses again.

At the end of the appeal, the panel will decide whether to uphold the initial verdict, overturn some of the charges against City or perhaps even order a retrial if there is a belief that the case needs hearing in its entirety once again.
City remain adamant with their stance and hope to have cleared their name before the end of the season.

ftbpro_01m54r7m77s8.title: Nottingham Forest vs. Arsenal: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m54r7m77s8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby LaneOct 17, 2026Nottingham Forest host Arsenal on Sunday. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Nottingham Forest), Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images (Arsenal)Arsenal travel to the City Ground on Sunday to close out the weekend’s Premier League fixtures, with Mikel Arteta’s side looking to maintain their strong start to the season.
Although the Gunners have yet to consistently reach the heights of their title-winning campaign last year, five victories from their opening six matches have kept them firmly in the hunt.

They sit second in the standings heading into the weekend, and with league-leaders Manchester City facing the prospect of a points deduction, Arsenal could yet see their position improve without needing to make up much ground on the pitch.

For Nottingham Forest, the priority is finding a way to turn promising displays into victories. Oliver Glasner’s side remain in the bottom half of the standings and need to start picking up points to avoid being dragged further down the table.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kai Havertz could prove the difference maker. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesArsenal have yet to find consistent rhythm following their defeat to Brighton, but Arteta’s side have still managed to get results. The Gunners recovered from a slow start to overcome Leeds before securing a comfortable Champions League victory over Lille.

Forest, by contrast, head into this contest looking to bounce back from consecutive defeats against Coventry City and Crystal Palace. Their loss to Palace will be particularly frustrating, as they controlled much of the first half but squandered several opportunities before eventually being punished for their lack of cutting edge.

Recent history suggests Arsenal could face another stubborn afternoon at the City Ground. The Gunners have been held to goalless draws on their previous two visits, and their occasional struggles in front of goal this season may offer Forest encouragement. Aside from the Palace setback, Forest have generally looked organized defensively and will likely prioritize keeping Arsenal at bay.
However, Arsenal do possess the individual quality to find a breakthrough, even if they have to work hard for it.
Prediction: Nottingham Forest 0–1 Arsenal
Forest are managing several injury concerns heading into their clash with Arsenal.
Striker Igor Jesus is ruled out through injury, as is Nicolò Savona, while Nikola Milenković is also unlikely to return after spending a few weeks on the sidelines.

The biggest blow, however, could be Morgan Gibbs-White. Having suffered a minor muscle injury against Crystal Palace, his potential absence would be difficult to overcome. Gibbs-White has created the most big chances (seven) and open-play chances (15) of any Forest player in the league this season, while only Pascal Groß (18) has created more chances overall heading into the weekend.
His absence could pave the way for Gustavo Sá to earn a start.
Nottingham Forest predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (3-4-2-1): Sels; Cunha, Diomande, Murillo; Muñoz, Schalger, McAtee, Williams; Ndoye, Sá; Delap.
Arsenal also have several selection headaches to contend with.

William Saliba remains sidelined by a back injury, while Piero Hincapié is unavailable after suffering an ankle problem against Leeds. Christos Tzolis is another absentee, having sustained a hamstring injury while representing Greece during the international break.

Martín Zubimendi is a more uncertain case. The midfielder picked up an injury in the same incident as Hincapié, but his recovery has progressed sufficiently to leave the door open for a possible return.

Should Zubimendi miss out, Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães could form the midfield partnership in front of a reconfigured defense. Ezri Konsa is expected to join Gabriel Magalhães at center back, while Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Eberechi Eze could operate behind Kai Havertz in attack.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Nottingham Forest (4-2-3-1): Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice; Saka, Ødegaard, Eze; Havertz.

ftbpro_01m54t4scm8a.title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Everton: Ugly Injury Sours Blues Victory
ftbpro_01m54t4scm8a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby Lane10:01 AM EDTPedro Neto was the difference maker. / Lewis Storey CFC/Getty ImagesChelsea came through a tight encounter with Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium with all three points, courtesy a first-ever Premier League brace from Pedro Neto, although it was a nasty head injury for goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez that remained in fans’ thoughts after the final whistle.

For much of the first half, it was a case of the irresistible, if inconsistent, force meeting the immovable object. Chelsea dominated possession, as they have so often this season, but found little joy against a stubborn Everton defense that offered precious little space to exploit.

The deadlock was finally broken just seconds after the restart, when Jorrel Hato surged down the left and fizzed a low cross into the box. Neto was on hand to apply the finishing touch, giving Xabi Alonso’s side the breakthrough their possession had threatened to deliver without ever quite guaranteeing.

The sight of Martínez leaving the second half on a stretcher added some real tension to proceedings, so there was significant relief as Neto fired home his second in stoppage time, calmly guiding a loose ball into the corner after a free kick to put the result beyond doubt and secure all three points.
Back-to-back victories and a first clean sheet in nine months are certainly cause for encouragement, but this was hardly a statement performance.
Chelsea still looked vulnerable whenever Everton broke forward, and had Thierno Barry shown greater composure in front of goal, the visitors might have left Merseyside with a very different result.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Emiliano Martínez suffered a gruesome head injury. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesRegardless of whether fortune played its part, Chelsea deserve credit for recording their first clean sheet of the Alonso era.

Life under the Spaniard has been something of a rollercoaster so far. Goals have flowed at one end, but defensive lapses have been just as frequent at the other. Against one of the Premier League’s more defensively disciplined sides, however, the balance appeared to shift closer to the middle: perhaps a little less spectacular, but certainly more controlled.

Emiliano Martínez has faced plenty of scrutiny since arriving from Aston Villa in the summer, but a couple of solid saves against Everton, coupled with some assured distribution, offered encouraging signs that Chelsea made the right call in bringing him in to replace Robert Sánchez.
Unfortunately, a nasty head injury in the second half forced Martínez off just as he appeared to be finding his feet, interrupting what could have been an important step forward.
While fans nervously await an update on a head injury that certainly looked like a nasty one, it is over to 21-year-old Mike Penders to build on this clean sheet.
Jorrel Hato was excellent. / Lewis Storey/CFC/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Emiliano Martínez—7.7: Kept his first clean sheet as a Chelsea player, making a couple of solid saves along the way. His injury will come as a big blow for the Blues.
CB: Josh Acheampong—7.7: Acheampong recorded more defensive contributions than any other Chelsea defender, coming out on top in an intriguing battle with the experienced Jack Grealish.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—7.3: After a shaky performance against Bournemouth last time out, Lacroix did very little wrong here, making several vital headed clearances to help keep Everton at bay.
CB: Levi Colwill—7.1: Defensively sound throughout, but Colwill’s distribution left plenty to be desired, completing just one of his six attempted long passes.

RM: Pedro Neto—9.3: Given more freedom from his defensive duties, Neto made the most of his attacking license, repeatedly driving forward and causing problems for Everton. His brace was a deserved reward for an influential attacking performance.
CM: Moisés Caicedo—7.7: Combative as ever in the middle of the park, Caicedo’s defensive contributions became increasingly valuable as the game wore on and Everton pushed harder for a goal.

CM: Jordan Henderson—7.5: After his midfield masterclass against Bournemouth, Henderson had a quieter outing against Everton. He remained reliable in possession and kept things ticking over, but offered little in the way of forward thrust.

ftbpro_01m54v4h88sr.title: ‘Sorry’—Bayern Munich Chief Reveals Stance on Florian Wirtz Transfer
ftbpro_01m54v4h88sr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:30 AM EDTFlorian Wirtz has struggled in England. / Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesBayern Munich president Herbert Hainer has heaped praise on Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz, but distanced the German giants from an attempt to sign their one-time target.

As is often the case with emerging Bundesliga stars, Bayern attempted to force their way to the front of the queue when Wirtz left Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025, only to miss out on the $158 million midfielder to Liverpool.

Since moving to England, however, Wirtz has looked a shadow of his former self, prompting major criticism from fans and rivals alike. Manager Andoni Iraola has even been forced to navigate calls to drop the German international from his starting lineup.
Reports have flirted with a potential transfer exit to Bayern, but Hainer was quick to cool suggestions of such a move.
“First of all, I think Florian Wirtz is an outstanding player, there’s absolutely no question about that,” Hainer said.
“I almost feel a little sorry for him that he hasn’t yet reached the same form in England that he had at Leverkusen, because we also need him for the German national team.
“[Bayern] have such a top-class squad, we’re incredibly happy at the moment, and therefore [a transfer] not an issue for us.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Wirtz is trying to figure it out. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesLiverpool have undoubtedly had to be patient with Wirtz. He hit 16 goals and 15 assists in his final season with Leverkusen but has come nowhere close to matching those heights in his 18 months at Anfield.

That can be expected from a young player, but a price tag of $158 million makes staying calm a nearly impossible task. After all, it is that price tag that creates the expectations that Wirtz is failing to meet.

Liverpool believed they were signing one of Europe’s premier attackers and Bayern were devastated to miss out on his signature. To hear Bayern so openly dismissive of signing the 23-year-old now shows just how far he has fallen in 18 months.

Fans expect Wirtz to have adjusted to life in England by now, and many are worried that he simply never will. At some point, Liverpool will have to decide whether it is worth continuing to invest time and money in his development.

Wirtz’s contract at Anfield runs until the summer of 2030, so there need not be any rush from Liverpool to make a decision, but the clock is ticking. His value is dropping and Liverpool will be aware that cutting their losses will increasingly be viewed as the only option if Wirtz cannot change the narrative soon.

The Gunners have banished their reputation as set-piece specialists and have been scoring at will this season, although manager Mikel Arteta needed his big guns to keep that momentum going after a handful of fringe players failed to ignite the midweek victory over Lille.

Attention now turns back to the Premier League. Arsenal are already playing catch-up to Manchester City in the title race and cannot afford to stumble against a Forest outfit struggling towards the bottom of the table.
Here’s how Arteta could set up for this one.

ftbpro_01m54zjfwv5e.title: Chelsea Lose Key Starter to Horror Head Injury Against Everton
ftbpro_01m54zjfwv5e.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:27 AM EDTA scary head injury for Emiliano Martínez. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesChelsea have been left sweating over the wellbeing of goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez after he was stretchered off against Everton with a head injury.
With just over 20 minutes to go, Martínez came out to try and claim an Everton free kick, only to collide with Toffees center back Jarrad Branthwaite in a nasty clash of heads.
Branthwaite was sat up shortly after but there was immediate concern for Martínez, with medical staff racing onto the pitch to help Chelsea’s stopper, who was in obvious distress on the turf.
After lengthy treatment on the pitch, Martínez was taken off on a stretcher and went straight to hospital for scans on the injury. As he left the pitch, he appeared to be moving his arms.

On in his place came young Mike Penders. The 21-year-old became the youngest goalkeeper in Chelsea’s Premier League history in what club officials expect to be the first of many appearances over the coming years.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Martínez went straight to hospital. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesChelsea will need the formal diagnosis of Martínez’s condition before even starting to come up with a return timeline for the goalkeeper, but it would come as a huge surprise to see him playing again before the end of the month at the very least.
Clearly, anything more serious would extend that spell on the sidelines, with Chelsea now waiting for the results of the scans on Martínez to know exactly how to proceed.

Xabi Alonso could be without his starting goalkeeper for some big fixtures. A visit from Tottenham Hotspur is on the cards next weekend before a Carabao Cup clash with Liverpool, for which Martínez may have been rested anyway.
October comes to an end with a visit from Manchester United, before a trip to Sunderland takes Chelsea into the November international break.

Any extended absence for Martínez would provide Penders a lengthy run in the side. The towering 21-year-old impressed on loan with Strasbourg last season and Chelsea decided against loaning him out again this season, instead opting to keep him around as competition for Martínez.

Penders has started both of Chelsea’s Carabao Cup games so far. After his debut, a 2–0 win over Luton Town in the second round, Alonso assured fans that the Belgian will soon have a major part to play.
“Talking about Mike, for sure, he will have games with more work,” Alonso said. “You could see in some moments he was under pressure and he was calm. He has security of his football.
“He didn’t make many saves but he’s a great prospect for the future and the present as well.”

ftbpro_01m55020sp1b.title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Brentford: Moment of Madness Breaks 238-Day Streak
ftbpro_01m55020sp1b.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:23 PM EDTAlexander Isak scored the decisive goal. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesLONDON — Liverpool had Alexander Isak, Víctor Muñoz and, most of all, Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk to thank for a 2–1 win at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday.

Andoni Iraola’s visitors were deservedly trailing 1–0 before Yarmoliuk became enveloped in a cloud of red mist on the cusp of halftime, delivering the gentlest of headbutts that would have a far more profound impact on the contest than its intended recipient, Jérémy Jacquet.

Liverpool warrant credit for overcoming the stop-start contest Brentford had tried to construct at the start of the second half, striking twice in eight minutes to secure three crucial points and become the first side since Feb. 21, 2026 to beat the Bees on their own patch.
Vitaly Janelt would earn Brentford’s second red card of the match with only minutes remaining, but the real damage had been done by the game’s first dismissal.

Referee John Brooks was in the spotlight. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesThere was a collective gasp of incredulity which swept around the Gtech when the giant screen flashed up to signal a VAR review for a possible red card was ongoing right at the end of first-half stoppage time. Plenty of the crowd’s whispers were asking which team, let alone which player, was at risk of being dismissed.
As the replays (which weren’t shown to the in-stadium fans) would reveal, Brentford’s Yarmoliuk had been lured into a brainless brush of his head against Jacquet while preparing to defend a corner.

Minutes earlier, VAR had rightly denied Liverpool a penalty, but the fates of Stockley Park rarely side with one team for long. This distant intervention came after a first-half which Brentford had fairly won, limiting their visitors to one big chance which Bradley Barcola fluffed before converting the single clear sight of goal that they created.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

The halftime substitutions set the tone for the second 45 minutes. While Keith Andrews reinforced his rearguard before sending on the jet-heeled Kevin Schade to offer a threat in transition, Iraola went all out. Víctor Muñoz, Liverpool’s right winger, replaced Ronald Araújo, a natural center back, in a very loose interpretation of the right back role. Fittingly enough, it would be Muñoz who equalized for the visitors shortly after the hour mark.

Brentford’s bold positioning had pinned Liverpool back in the first half, helping the hosts rack up more shots on target and touches in the opposition penalty area than their illustrious visitors. Yet, with their number reduced, the Bees were either penned inside their own area or left exposed when they dared to venture forward.

Muñoz’s electric speed would exploit this disorganization while Isak benefited from the field being tilted towards Kelleher’s box. The sheer volume of black shirts ensured that Barcola’s header had a decent chance of picking out a teammate. Isak was first onto the scene, taking a deft touch before swiping the ball into the far corner.
After watching their 10 men crumble, Brentford fans could scarcely be blamed for chanting: “To the referee, 2–1.”
Florian Wirtz’s ball control is not the issue. / Liverpool FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—7.0: Deceived by Keane Lewis-Potter’s clever header from range but otherwise not unduly troubled.
RB: Ronald Araújo—6.1: Skirted around the fringes of the contest before he was sacrificed for a far more front-footed approach from the visitors in the second half.

CB: Jérémy Jacquet—7.9: It’s hard to describe the regal Frenchman as anything other than classy; be it the way he strode forward on the ball, clipped passes over befuddled red and white shirts or got his toe to any loose pass. Jacquet even managed to tussle with Igor Thiago without getting his shirt wrinkled.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—8.0: Forced out of his leisurely stroll more often than he would perhaps care but did the grubby part of the game well.

LB: Milos Kerkez—7.7: Seemed to benefit from having his countryman Dominik Szoboszlai in such close proximity to him, constantly adjusting his position while being peppered with instructions. Kerkez looked a little more unsettled after his compatriot’s enforced removal.
CM: Dominik Szoboszlai—6.6: Uncharacteristically disciplined defensively during his brief cameo.
CM: Alexis Mac Allister—8.4: It was his sloppy pass that allowed Brentford to keep Liverpool pinned in before Keane Lewis-Potter nodded in the opener.

ftbpro_01m550a53bvc.title: ‘I Know’—Flick Braced for Lamine Yamal Minutes Issue
ftbpro_01m550a53bvc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely11:00 AM EDTLamine Yamal is a permanent fixture in the Barcelona setup. / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesNo matter how prized Lamine Yamal is on Barcelona’s right flank, manager Hansi Flick knows he must give the 19-year-old some respite to go the long haul. He just doesn’t know when.

The star winger has started every match for Barça this season, playing the full 90 minutes in eight of them and contributing massively to the club’s historic start of 10 consecutive wins with eight goals and nine assists in that span.

“Lamine is a special player, and I know we have to balance his minutes, but for him the most important thing is to enjoy playing football, and at the moment that’s the case and I don’t want to interrupt that situation,” Flick told reporters.

Barcelona face their most important match yet, traveling to Seville on Saturday with the hope of making history. Should the unstoppable Catalans defeat Real Betis, they will become just the second team ever to win its opening nine games of a La Liga season.

Barcelona may be playing like the best team in the world, but Manuel Pellegrini’s side won’t be an easy foe. Real Betis are in red-hot form, having lost just once in 2026–27. Any chance of victory will require the continued magic of Yamal. So, when will he get his rest?
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Lamine Yamal will be needed for the foreseeable future. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesA hamstring injury last April saw Yamal miss the rest of the 2025–26 season and almost impeded his ability to represent Spain at the 2026 World Cup this summer, seeing his minutes heavily managed in the group stage, and it curbed his stardom for months as he struggled to regain fitness.
Flick will be eager to avoid any relapse of that overuse injury; however, he will need his star man in the coming weeks. After the clash with Real Betis, Barcelona’s schedule only intensifies.

A Champions League clash with two-time victors Paris Saint-Germain is on the horizon. Barcelona will head to Parc des Princes on Tuesday to face the team that embarrassed Premier League leaders Manchester City midweek.
After that comes the first Clásico of the new season, a pivotal clash with Real Madrid at Camp Nou that could have serious implications on the rest of the La Liga season.

This means that respite for Yamal may not come until the end of the month when Barcelona host Deportivo Alavés. The Spanish side currently sits seventh in league standings but defeated the Catalans in their most recent clash back in May, 1–0.

ftbpro_01m5536zr634.title: Leeds vs. Man Utd: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5536zr634.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby LaneOct 17, 2026Leeds host the latest chapter in this famous rivalry. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesManchester United rarely relish a trip to Elland Road to face fierce rivals Leeds United, but this Sunday’s visit could hardly come at a worse time for the Red Devils.
There is little doubt that Man Utd are a club in crisis.

Michael Carrick’s side sit 13th in the league heading into the weekend and have gone over a month without a win in all competitions. Tensions reached a boiling point following a Champions League defeat to Atlético Madrid, after which defender Lisandro Martínez publicly criticized the club’s hierarchy.

Although Martínez has since been formally punished, the fallout from the incident is unlikely to disappear overnight. His comments hardly paint the picture of a harmonious dressing room, and a hostile trip to Elland Road is unlikely to provide the ideal remedy for Carrick’s struggling side.

Meanwhile, Daniel Farke’s stubborn Leeds outfit have shown plenty of fight this season. After giving Arsenal a scare last weekend, the hosts will be eager to build on that performance and strengthen their credentials as potential contenders for European qualification.
Given United’s recent struggles, another difficult afternoon could await the visitors.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Dominic Calvert-Lewin could be the difference maker. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesLast season, Leeds held Man Utd to a 1–1 draw at Elland Road before going on to beat their rivals at Old Trafford later in the campaign.

With Farke’s side looking considerably stronger than they did last term, thanks in part to some smart summer transfer business, and enjoying a solid run of form, the hosts will be confident of extending that unbeaten run against the Red Devils.

That said, even in their current predicament, Man Utd possess enough quality to hurt Leeds, particularly through captain Bruno Fernandes. The Portuguese midfielder has a habit of delivering against the Whites, registering nine goal contributions in seven Premier League appearances against them.
Prediction: Leeds United 2–1 Manchester United
Leeds have no fresh injury concerns heading into their clash with Man Utd, meaning Daniel Farke could name an unchanged lineup from the defeat to Arsenal and draw with Crystal Palace.
That would see James Trafford start in goal behind a back three of Tarik Muharemović, Nico Elvedi and James Justin, with Gabriel Gudmundsson and Jaden Bogle operating as wingbacks.
Anton Stach, Ao Tanaka and Ethan Ampadu are expected to form the midfield trio, while Calvert-Lewin leads the line with support from Noah Okafor.
Leeds predicted lineup vs. Man Utd (3-4-2-1): Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemović; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Stach, Justin; Okafor, Calvert-Lewin.
As mentioned earlier, Martínez is likely to drop out of the starting lineup, paving the way for Yoro to partner Harry Maguire at the heart of United’s defense.

Elsewhere, following a strong cameo in the draw with Tottenham, Carlos Baleba could earn his first Premier League start for United in place of the struggling Youri Tielemans. He would partner Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield as Carrick looks to find a more effective balance in the middle of the park.

ftbpro_01m554dx4y64.title: Iraola Provides Worrying Three-Word Update on Szoboszlai Injury
ftbpro_01m554dx4y64.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:00 AM EDTDominik Szoboszlai barely lasted half an hour against Brentford. / Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty ImagesLONDON — Dominik Szoboszlai’s return to Liverpool’s starting XI lasted for just 32 minutes before he was forced off after aggravating an existing injury against Brentford, prompting Andoni Iraola to predict that he will be out “for some time.”
The all-action Hungarian midfielder had missed Liverpool’s previous two fixtures with a hamstring issue, failing to even travel to Austria for the midweek Champions League win over LASK.

Andoni Iraola had been uncertain of Szoboszlai’s fitness heading into Saturday’s trip to Brentford but was convinced by Thursday and Friday’s training sessions to start his first-choice midfielder alongside Alexis Mac Allister. That decision spectacularly backfired.

Szoboszlai crumpled in a heap on the turf half an hour into the Premier League clash in west London, entirely unconnected to any other player. Liverpool’s medical staff made the short trip from the dugout to the nearside of the halfway line but the player’s mind had been made up. With a disconsolate shake of his head, Szoboszlai trudged off the pitch and down the tunnel.

Liverpool were already understaffed in the middle of the pitch by Ryan Gravenberch’s suspension and promptly conceded a cheap header to trail during the interval. They would recover to win 2–1 but Iraola ominously described the victory as “very expensive.”

Dominik Szoboszlai cut a disappointed figure. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesThere had been no contact on Szoboszlai—the midfielder had in fact been sticking to a more disciplined deeper role during a promising half-hour of action—and the worst fears of a recurrence of his recent muscular issue were realized.
Iraola admitted that the quick turnaround in fixtures had afforded his players “not the proper recovery” and Szoboszlai’s ailment had “not healed enough.”

The 25-year-old had been mercifully spared any serious injuries over the last few years. The hamstring problem which forced him to miss the thumping from Manchester City and win over LASK was his first fitness complaint since February 2024.
Back then, Szoboszlai missed 10 Liverpool matches in quick succession with a hamstring issue which has not flared up again—until now.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Andoni Iraola cannot catch a break. / Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty ImagesOnly the fullness of time will reveal a detailed timeline but Iraola admitted that he will be without the Hungary international “for some time.” That Szoboszlai has just come back from such a recent setback will be a concern.
Iraola already has personnel issues in the middle of the pitch given Gravenberch’s current suspension—although the Netherlands international will be available from Monday onward.

“We need everyone,” Iraola breathlessly warned, “we will need everyone in one moment or the other. Everyone has to be ready because we will need him probably.” Szoboszlai won’t be ready in the immediate future.

ftbpro_01m5558q4qbn.title: ‘All the Offers He Had’—Jose Mourinho Makes Surprise Vinicius Jr Transfer Admission
ftbpro_01m5558q4qbn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott2:00 PM EDTVinícius Júnior is going through a rough patch. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesJosé Mourinho has insisted nobody should doubt Vinícius Júnior’s commitment to Real Madrid after he rejected several offers from elsewhere in favor of extending his contract, going as far as to admit he would have forced an exit from the club had he been in the winger’s shoes this summer.

Questions about Vinícius Jr’s future at the Bernabéu were swirling this summer. Interest from Saudi Arabia has been around for years, but Arsenal joined the race after the World Cup, and some reports went as far as to state many at the Emirates genuinely believed he would make the move.

A new contract was ultimately signed, but it has not ended the debate about Vinícius Jr’s future at the club. A series of disappointing performances and a four-match ban for a red card last time out in La Liga has seen many question whether Madrid made the right decision to keep hold of the Brazil international.
It is a delicate moment for Vinícius Jr right now, and Mourinho was eager to remind disgruntled fans of just how devoted to the club the under-fire winger is.
“He’s a spectacular guy, very easy to get along with,” Mourinho began. “I like him a lot, and he’s fantastic.

“He has tremendous value because he manages to live and survive with a smile. If it were me, he probably wouldn’t be here. Last summer, I would have forced a move to a country or group of clubs and rivals where he’d be respected. Out of love for the club and the city, because he believes things can improve, he renewed his contract and continues with that smile.
“People might influence him negatively because he's human, but I don't think anyone can take away that joy.”

He added: “When I arrived, he renewed his contract, showed that Madrid is his home and expressed his desire to continue making history and winning titles. He gets along well with everyone in the locker room; he’s a source of joy.
“I have no serious doubts about whether he has the strength to stay here with all the offers he had.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

José Mourinho (left) was happy to fuel the conspiracy theories against Vinícius. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe four-match ban handed out to Vinícius Jr was the latest obstacle in the winger’s ongoing quest to return to his best.

He was furious to learn that his dismissal for pulling the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba brought a suspension of four games—ignoring the fact only two came from the incident and a further two stemmed from his aggressive reaction to the referee.

Vinícius subsequently failed to make the most of what is going to be a rare outing midweek when he was substituted with his side 3–1 down to Roma. An emotional reaction to the substitution did not help his situation, and neither did the fact he watched his side turn things around from the sidelines.

“Vinícius had a very difficult match,” Mourinho acknowledged. “The main culprit for his performance is [Roma manager Gian Piero] Gasperini, who attacked us down only one wing. Three men against [Marc] Cucurella and him...

“What bothered me was the nature of the second goal, at a time when the game was calm and balanced. We knew how they would man-mark, and Vini had to secure the ball or draw a foul. But that’s it. It’s not a big deal. I made five changes; it’s part of football. The intensity is extremely high, and it’s difficult to play at 200 miles an hour for 90 minutes.
“Vini’s future lies in working harder than those who have to play every match. Without promising anything, I think he’ll start in the Champions League on Wednesday.”
Mourinho concluded by admitting his surprise that Vinícius’s suspension was only four games as he returned to the Portuguese idiom of a “hidden cat” to suggest a conspiracy against the winger.

“Regarding the four-match suspension, I’m happy because I thought he was going to be suspended longer,” he laughed. “I thought that the hidden cats were going to score another game or two against them.”

ftbpro_01m555xfgbs3.title: Barcelona Player Ratings vs. Real Betis: Lamine Yamal Scores Stunner in Record-Setting Thriller
ftbpro_01m555xfgbs3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby Lane2:57 PM EDTYamal scored a stunner. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesBarcelona survived a seven-goal thriller to beat Real Betis 5–2, extending their unbeaten start and becoming only the second team ever to win its opening nine games of a La Liga season, matching what Real Madrid achieved 58 years ago.

This was Hansi Flick’s Barcelona at full throttle: goals flying in at both ends, outrageous individual brilliance, disallowed strikes and barely a moment to catch your breath. Lamine Yamal provided the standout moment just 10 minutes in, bamboozling Facundo Bernal with sublime footwork before curling a sensational effort from the edge of the box into the top corner.

Betis refused to go quietly, though, with Valentín Gómez first leveling the score, before former Barcelona player Ez Abde made it 3–2 after the visitors had surged into a 3–1 lead, courtesy of goals from Rodri—his first for the club—and Gabriel Jesus.

However, Betis’ hopes of a comeback took a major hit shortly after the break when Bernal was shown a straight red card, leaving the hosts with 10 men. Barcelona made their numerical advantage count, with substitutes Eric García and Dani Olmo both finding the net to put the result beyond doubt and seal a comfortable victory.

Defensive concerns remain, but Barcelona’s relentless attack continues to deliver. Nine games, nine wins and a staggering 39 goals scored. Can anyone stop them from racing to a third-consecutive La Liga title? On current evidence, it is already looking like a tall order.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Rodri was at the heart of everything good for Barcelona. / Joaquin Corchero/Europa Press/Getty ImagesHeroesYamal will grab the headlines for his jaw-dropping strike, but Rodri was the real conductor of Barcelona’s orchestra. The midfielder scored his first goal for the club and ran the show from start to finish, seeing more of the ball than anyone else while effortlessly dictating the tempo and carving open Betis with his forward passing.

Raphinha’s substitute cameo was also met with a hero’s reception from the Barcelona faithful. Although he didn’t get on the scoresheet, the in-form Brazilian’s return comes at the perfect time, with El Clásico against Real Madrid just around the corner next week.

Karim Adeyemi had a golden opportunity to stake his claim to a regular starting spot but did precious little to seize it. The German winger never stopped running and was always willing to take on his man, yet his final ball repeatedly let him down. Wayward crosses, wasted dribbles and frustrating decisions summed up an evening of effort without reward.
Yamal shone once again. / Jesus Ruiz/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Joan García—7.2: Will be frustrated by the nature of the goals conceded, but more than made up for it with an excellent sweeper-keeper display. His sharp reading of the game and willingness to rush off his line repeatedly bailed out Barcelona’s high defensive line.

RB: Jules Koundé—7.5: Caught out at the back for Abde’s goal, but otherwise excellent, particularly when joining in the build-up play. The Frenchman made plenty of progressive passes to help Barcelona move the ball forward.

CB: Pau Cubarsí—8.7: Looked off the pace in the first half, losing several duels and struggling to assert himself defensively. However, he grew into the game after the break, finishing with Barcelona’s most defensive contributions and registering two assists for good measure.
CB: Gerard Martín—6.5: Replaced by Eric García at halftime after a difficult first-half showing in which he lost every aerial duel.
LB: Xavi Espart—7.1: Lost a total of seven duels and misplaced numerous passes. Not his finest afternoon.
CM: Rodri—8.5: Scoring his first goal for Barcelona, seeing more of the ball than any other player and completing 98% of his passes—Rodri was the standout performer by some margin.
CM: Pedri—7.6: Quiet by his own standards, but didn’t do much wrong either.

RW: Lamine Yamal—8.9: His stunning goal alone was enough to justify the rating, but the teenager had plenty more to offer. He teed up Jesus for his goal and generally tormented the Betis defense throughout.
AM: Fermín López—7.6: Wasn’t quite at his electric best, but still made a telling contribution, registering the assist for Rodri’s goal.
LW: Karim Adeyemi—7.0: All gas, no end product. Adeyemi ran himself into the ground and repeatedly let himself down when it mattered most.

ftbpro_01m557y2kny3.title: Gio Reyna Makes Impressive Bid to Become USMNT Starter
ftbpro_01m557y2kny3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner4:00 PM EDTGio Reyna's future role with the USMNT is still up in the air. / Jane Gershovich/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesGio Reyna is finally where he needs to be, and the 23-year-old could become a core piece of the U.S. men’s national team’s next era.

After years of limited minutes and opportunities with Bundesliga sides Borussia Dortmund and Borussia Mönchengladbach as well as a fruitless loan spell at Nottingham Forest, the USMNT midfielder has finally carved himself out a consistent role for Ligue 1’s Racing Strasbourg.

At the same time, he’s become a beloved favorite of USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino, inspiring a shocking career rise to the 2026 World Cup after it seemed his time in the national team jersey might be coming to an end.

With solid footing for club and country, the next chapter of his career awaits. The USMNT has never had more depth in midfield than it does now, but Reyna has begun to prove himself as an integral part of the mix. The question looms: Where does he fit?

“It’s pretty simple: just keep building on what I’ve been doing,” Reyna told GOAL of his rise, following the USMNT’s four wins in four games in the September-October international window. “Keep showing up every day, training, recovering, doing everything I need to prepare mentally and physically for every training and game. I feel good, though, and I’m feeling more confident every time I step on the pitch.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Gio Reyna has always been a Mauricio Pochettino favorite. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesAhead of the 2026 World Cup, even as Reyna struggled for club minutes, Pochettino hailed the midfielder as a “very special talent.” Despite harboring a greater emphasis on club form, Pochettino made an exception for Reyna, calling him up for pre-tournament friendlies against Belgium and Portugal in March.

While Reyna and the USMNT struggled in those two defeats, it became clear that Pochettino saw the then-Bundesliga man in a different echelon than others in the player pool. He included Reyna in his World Cup squad, where the young star served as an important off-the-bench reinforcement and even scored in the tournament opener against Paraguay.

Since then, his two goals in seven games with Strasbourg have offered a glimpse into the potential Pochettino saw all along. He most recently scored against reigning UEFA Champions League winners, Paris Saint-Germain, on Saturday, punishing the European champions with a skillful turn and finish inside the box to open the game’s scoring.

His rise has only been further evidenced by the veteran role he played in the fall international window. Reyna was the only USMNT player to start all four victories, playing among an otherwise heavily rotated, youth-driven lineup.
Next. Gio Reyna Feature on Family Drama. Once at Center of Drama, Gio Reyna Is Writing Different Story. dark

While speaking to former USMNT attacker Herculez Gomez, one of Reyna’s former USMNT teammates, Kellyn Acosta, said Reyna was “back to his best” and believes he can be an “important figure” for the USMNT moving forward.

“He’s a player that is so talented, with his natural ability,” Acosta exclaimed. “Gio has been through a lot of hardships, and he's come out of it. Now we're seeing a guy that's playing consistently with his club, and now he's back with the national team doing what he does best.”

Acosta added: “He sees the game a bit differently than most. He glides. He's clever. Has a bit of an edge to him too ... He's a guy that checks all the boxes, and he's an important figure for our team.”

Sebastian Berhalter (left) is one of the many midfield options Gio Reyna (right) now has to contend with in the USMNT.  / Jared C. Tilton/FIFA/Getty ImagesThe recent international window gave a strong indication regarding where Pochettino sees Reyna in the plans—likely as a No. 10. Nevertheless, he will need to outperform several other USMNT stars for that position.

In a 4-2-3-1, Reyna played as the creative playmaker in wins against Peru and Chile, where the USMNT controlled the game throughout. It’s a similar role to what he has taken on at Strasbourg, and it lets him slow the game down to showcase his individual skills, rather than relying on more physical elements. He was highly successful, recording an assist in each friendly.
Although against tougher opponents Canada and Mexico, Reyna struggled to make a similar impact as a deep-lying midfielder or on the wing.

His main competition for the No. 10 spot will be Malik Tillman, who excelled in all four friendlies. The Bayer Leverkusen man first impressed as the No. 10 at the World Cup and is expected to claim that position as a starter moving forward. The 24-year-old can seamlessly shift wide or take on a deeper role—two positions of strength in the USMNT player pool, whereas Reyna has comparatively struggled to adjust from the No. 10.

Most importantly, though, Reyna is finally where he needs to be: playing consistent soccer. He will continue to grow and develop throughout these increased opportunities and will be well-positioned to a stake a claim in the USMNT’s burgeoning midfield. Next up, he will have the chance to prove himself in November’s Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti.

ftbpro_01m558xs6dph.title: Wrexham’s Emphatic Win Delivers Perfect Response to Latest Phil Parkinson Claims
ftbpro_01m558xs6dph.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay12:43 PM EDTWrexham bounced back from defeat to West Brom in style. / Wrexham AFCWREXHAM, Wales — Wrexham were in a bit of a no-win situation against Preston North End. It is a huge credit to manager Phil Parkinson that their 4–1 victory still felt so euphoric.

A win would come with the caveat that it was against the team at the bottom of the EFL Championship, while a failure to win would only have intensified the scrutiny around Parkinson's side after two matches without a win.

Wrexham somehow avoided both scenarios, though, securing their first win by a three-goal margin on home soil since they earned promotion to the Championship with a 3–0 victory over Charlton Athletic back in April 2025.

It was far from a perfect performance, but it offered enough positives to show why the board remains firmly behind Parkinson. Wrexham scored four goals, picked up another three points, played with two strikers and conceded just once. If there was ever a time for a confidence boost, this was it. There is no ignoring, though, that tougher tests are waiting just around the corner.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Ben Whiteman left Preston to join Wrexham in the summer transfer window. / Wrexham AFCAfter a similarly slow start a year ago, Wrexham surged up the table with a run of four wins in nine matches, establishing themselves as playoff contenders. They will hope to repeat that feat this season, but they are also aware that they will earn little praise for beating a Preston side that has won just once all season.

The Red Dragons made four changes from their midweek defeat to West Brom, bringing Joe Worrall, Danny Imray, Matty James and Sam Smith into the starting lineup. Preston were just as desperate for a win and came flying out of the blocks, forcing Wrexham to clear a cross off the line before seeing a header flash wide within the opening two minutes.

Wrexham were unconvincing defensively throughout the afternoon, but the visitors were even worse. Callum O'Hare and Smith both tested Preston goalkeeper Daniel Iversen with decent efforts before the deadlock was finally broken after half an hour.

Preston dealt with the initial corner, but Wrexham made the most of the second phase as Worrall headed home his first goal since joining the club in the summer. Fellow summer signing Imray provided an excellent cross for the defender to finish. The goal extended Preston's unwanted run without a clean sheet to 27 games, with their last shutout coming 252 days earlier.

Wrexham hoped to build on that solid foundation, but they were pegged back just five minutes later. Moore was guilty of a slack pass inside his own half, which Johnny Kenny pounced on. His deflected shot fell into the path of Alfie Devine, who fired home at the back post.

Devine signed permanently for Preston in the summer, partly because he was convinced to join by former club captain Whiteman. Just weeks later, Whiteman signed for Wrexham instead, much to the frustration of the Preston supporters who made the trip to the Racecourse Ground.
Next. ‘Crossed a Line’—Ben Whiteman Put on Blast By His Own Manager. ‘Crossed a Line’—Ben Whiteman Put on Blast By His Own Manager. dark

It was fitting, then, that Whiteman restored Wrexham's lead three minutes before halftime. His driven effort took a deflection off a defender before finding the inside of the post. He celebrated his first Wrexham goal by blowing the Preston supporters a kiss.

Wrexham struck again just before the hour mark when Smith headed one home from close range, and before Preston could regroup, the hosts added a fourth. Worrall turned the ball over the line after a driven free kick from Callum Doyle. The 29-year-old had not scored since netting a last-minute winner for Besiktas in May 2024. Now he has two goals in a Wrexham shirt—unless Moore manages to claim the latest one as his own.

Parkinson's substitutions were jeered in the closing stages of Tuesday's defeat to West Brom, but there were no complaints this time when Moore, James and O'Hare were given a rare rest in the final minutes, with victory already secured.

In a week when Wrexham were sensationally linked with Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard as a potential future manager, Parkinson made sure the pressure did not get to him. His side delivered another win when it mattered most.

ftbpro_01m55bn8x63t.title: Florian Wirtz and the Most Misleading Statistic of the Premier League Season
ftbpro_01m55bn8x63t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 17, 2026Florian Wirtz’s Liverpool career is very confusing. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesLONDON — Paco Jémez, the manager Andoni Iraola replaced at Rayo Vallecano, had a great line last year. “Statistics are like thongs,” the Spanish tactician mused, “they show a lot, but cover the most important thing.”

Liverpool’s 2–1 win over Brentford on Saturday threw up one of the season’s most deceptive statistics thus far this season: Florian Wirtz created an unrivaled and remarkable nine chances for his teammates.

It’s been more than half a decade since anyone racked up so many scoring opportunities in a single Premier League match, while no Liverpool player has ever surpassed that statistic since Opta’s advanced data collection began in 2003–04, per Michael Reid.

For those who didn’t watch the game—and that is everyone in the United Kingdom, to begin with, given it was televised during the Saturday, 3 p.m. blackout—it would be easy to conclude that this was therefore a sublime performance by Wirtz. After 15 months of nearly’s and not-quite’s, Liverpool’s $154 million (£116 million) had finally gone nuclear, exploding with a performance of such attacking creativity that the record books have to be rewritten. Well, no.

Wirtz was decent but by no means devastating, alright and quite a long way from awesome. Like Liverpool as a collective, it took Yehor Yarmoliuk’s bone-headed red card on the cusp of halftime for the playmaker to really get into the contest, and even then, the source of acclaim shifted his way, that eye-opening statistic, doesn’t stand up to any scrutiny.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Dominik Szoboszlai started an early trend. / BrentfordThis set the tone for the vast majority of the chances Wirtz created: rolling a sideways or backward pass for a teammate to blaze over.

Alexis Mac Allister also wanted a crack. / BrentfordLiverpool’s beleaguered No. 7 shouldn’t be blamed for the poor choices of his colleagues, but he also shouldn’t be praised for teeing up hopeful pot shots.

Bradley Barcola spurned one of many chances. / BrentfordDuring an even opening 45 minutes, in which Brentford took a 1–0 lead, Wirtz was left to gently prod at the tight stitching of the hosts’ rearguard. The mobile midfielder is at his best when given license to roam, tiptoeing laterally in search of the weak spot in the opposition’s defense.
To begin with on Saturday, Wirtz was lured toward the right halfspace, where he would invariably roll a pass across the face of the box rather than trying to find a way through Brentford’s shell.

Florian Wirtz can’t be blamed for his teammates’ poor choices. / BrentfordMost of the chances that Wirtz created were wild efforts from range, but two were concerningly from corners. Liverpool are one of only four sides in the Premier League yet to score from a set piece this season. For all Arne Slot’s complaining last term, the Reds still racked up 18 goals from this fruitful avenue, the fourth-most in the entire division.
If the best scheme that Iraola’s backroom staff can draw up is Wirtz rolling the ball back for Trey Nyoni to have a shot from 25 yards, then this could be a very long campaign.

Alexis Mac Allister didn’t have his radar tuned. / BrentfordIraola has been a fierce advocate of Wirtz, but even the Basque boss waved away his swollen tally of chances created. “In the second half, no?” Iraola clarified, correctly pointing out that Yarmoliuk’s dismissal preceded the majority of Wirtz’s questionable dexterity.

Trey Nyoni joined the act. / BrentfordWhile this was no performance worthy of an significant statistical celebration, it would be unfair to completely dismiss Wirtz’s virtues. Faced with the massed ranks of 10 Brentford players in retreat, Iraola could turn to his chief lock picker.

“There are very few spaces, small pockets and [very little] time on the ball,” Iraola said of that second half. “You have to find delicate things because Brentford is a team that defends the box really, really well. You need players like Flo.”
You also need players who can take advantage of being presented with the ball inside a crowded penalty area. Nyoni, for all his talent, isn’t yet one of them.

This was Florian Wirtz’s best moment. / BrentfordEven calling Wirtz’s pass for Víctor Muñoz’s equalizer an “assist” is somewhat overstating it. Liverpool’s flying right winger collected the ball 35 yards from goal and had to chop past Keane Lewis-Potter to create space to pick out the bottom corner with his weaker left foot.

Nevertheless, Wirtz showed an excellent deftness of touch to shift his weight away from Kristoffer Ajer with his first contact of the ball before quickly sliding it ahead of Muñoz, who had the beating of Brentford’s fullback for pace. At a time when Liverpool were still trailing and frustrated by the staccato nature of a contest their hosts were trying to see out any way they could, it was a crucial piece of play.

Florian Wirtz’s performance was inflated. / BrentfordThis is the most ridiculous case of a chance going down as “created.” Ajer headed the ball onto Wirtz’s shoulder, sending it ricocheting into the path for Barcola to slash wide.

ftbpro_01m55dy3ayc1.title: Phil Parkinson Finds Tactical Fix to Wrexham’s Injury Woes
ftbpro_01m55dy3ayc1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay2:15 PM EDTWrexham had four different scorers in their win over Preston North End. / PA Images/Getty ImagesWREXHAM, Wales — Phil Parkinson produced an astute tactical performance as Wrexham thumped Preston North End 4–1 in the EFL Championship on Saturday afternoon.

The Red Dragons had thrown away a one-goal lead to lose to West Bromwich Albion in midweek but bounced back in style with a convincing win over the league's bottom side. Although it was far from a perfect performance, Wrexham were much improved from Tuesday night and might have won by an even larger margin had they taken all their chances.

Parkinson was quick to point out that Wrexham secured their impressive victory despite an extensive injury list that currently has seven first-team players sidelined. He made four changes to the side that lost to West Brom and also introduced a rare tactical adjustment.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Wrexham scored all four goals from set-piece scenarios against Preston North End. / PA Images/Getty ImagesFor the first time since Wrexham returned to the Championship, Parkinson deployed two strikers from the start, reverting to the setup that helped the Red Dragons over the line during their League One promotion season. It meant top scorer Kieffer Moore led the line alongside backup striker Sam Smith, an approach that worked wonders against a Preston side low on confidence.

While Wrexham's long-ball approach did little to trouble West Brom in midweek, it caused plenty of problems for Preston, with all four goals coming from set-piece situations. Joe Worrall opened his Wrexham account with a looping header from a cross into the box. Ben Whiteman scored his first goal for the club with a deflected strike from distance from a throw-in routine. Meanwhile, Smith and Moore both scored from set-piece deliveries.

It might not always be an effective solution, but against physical opponents, Wrexham could be wise to risk fewer options on the bench by starting both senior strikers. The approach became even more appealing after the Red Dragons recorded their biggest winning margin at home since defeating Charlton Athletic to secure promotion from League One.

“Brilliant. Smudger [Sam Smith], I spoke to him this morning about all the stuff we needed from him,” Parkinson said post-match. “I thought he did exactly what we asked; he was a real handful. I like it when the opposition defenders come off and go, ‘Wow, he is a difficult player to play against.’

“He is physical when the ball goes up, he runs tirelessly in behind, and he gave them no end of problems today. I am so pleased for Sam. He is one of the lads who has been with us for a while and is a fantastic character. He had a brilliant second part of last season and a really good preseason. Kieffer’s form has been really good, and Sam hasn't quite had that moment, but he has been close to it. Today he got one, and he will go from strength to strength.”

Parkinson had no shortage of praise for Moore either. “[His] fifth goal in 11 games, nine starts. He is right at the top of his game. My job is to keep him at the top of his game, and it is his job as well.”

ftbpro_01m55kvjwnfc.title: Lionel Messi Receives Most Bizarre Tribute Yet After Argentina Retirement
ftbpro_01m55kvjwnfc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben SteinerOct 17, 2026Lionel Messi has had a plant named after him.  / MB Media/Getty ImagesLionel Messi is no stranger to honors. At Inter Miami’s Nu Stadium, he has a stand named after him. His boyhood club, Newell's Old Boys, has a similar section bearing his name.
While his name has graced crowd stands, shoes, apparel, sports drinks and more, the latest might be the oddest. Now, a newly discovered plant species has been named after him: the Salvia messii.

An academic study revealed a new species in the Andes mountain range of Peru, and it has been immediately classified as endangered. With its light blue and white flowers resembling Argentina’s national team kit and the discovery happening near the time of Messi’s international retirement, scientists were inspired to name the plant after the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner.

Paul Gonzales of the Natural History Museum of the National University of San Marco, alongside Argentine researcher Rolando Uria and biologist Jean Capcha-Ramos of Huarango Nature described the species and conducted the initial studies. The full name, written in Latin under international rules of botanical nomenclature, translates to “Messi’s plant,” with an added “i” to indicate possession. It can grow to 4'11" tall, not much shorter than the diminutive soccer star that stands at 5'7".

This plant species is not the first to be named after a soccer player in the wake of the 2026 World Cup. Spanish researcher Jesus Ortea named a marine mollusk Aldisa vozinhai after Cape Verde’s star goalkeeper, Vozinha, per The Athletic. It directly translates to “Vozinha’s sea slug”. Ortea previously named a marine snail species after legendary Costa Rica and Real Madrid goalkeeper Keylor Navas.

Lionel Messi was given an honorary doctorate before his Argentina retirment.  / MB Media/Getty ImagesMessi is really making a name for himself in the academic community. In addition to a new species named in his honor, he received an honorary doctorate degree from the University of Buenos Aires ahead of his international farewell match earlier this month. It honored his sporting career, his representation of Argentine identity on the global stage and his social contributions through the Leo Messi Foundation, UNICEF and other avenues.

While off-pitch honors in the twilight of his career are coming fast, Messi still has several goals on the pitch as he chases a third-straight MLS MVP title, a second-straight MLS Golden Boot and Inter Miami’s title defense of the MLS Cup, with the playoffs set to begin on Nov. 18.

ftbpro_01m55t0dfn26.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s Five Best USMNT Wingers for Long-Term Success—Ranked
ftbpro_01m55t0dfn26.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:45 PM EDTChristian Pulisic (left) and Cavan Sullivan (right) are some of the USMNT’s best winger prospects. / Sebastian Frej/Getty Images (Pulisic); Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images (Sullivan) If U.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino really has ambitions of turning the team into a global superpower by the 2030 World Cup, then he’ll need players that can dominate the wings.

I’m talking high quality attackers that can get end-to-end at the speed of light, isolate defenders to burn them one-on-one, create gaps in a backline and deliver brilliant services into the box. He’ll need players that poised on the ball, yet have enough edge to be brave and take dangerous chances.

Pochettino has several strong candidates in his player pool. As he scours the ranks, here are the best long-term wingers at his disposal that are capable of dominating the flanks at the 2030 World Cup.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Tim Weah is a two-time World Cup player. / Frederic J. BROWN/AFP/Getty Images26-year-old Tim Weah has been overlooked by Pochettino in recent time, but he has proved on countless occasions that he has what it takes to deliver on the international stage. Once a stalwart on the flanks for the USMNT and a founding member of the squad’s “golden generation,” Weah was a rather unused substitute at the 2026 World Cup. He featured just 18 minutes off the bench in the group stage opener against Paraguay before logging under an hour in the dead rubber loss to Türkiye.But he harbors several important virtues for Pochettino. On the one hand, despite his young age, he is now a two-time World Cup player that also has experience playing overseas in Europe. The Marseille star has competed at the highest levels, offering critical veteran experience and leadership amid the team’s youthful revolution. On the other hand, Weah is extremely versatile. He plays right back and right wingback in Ligue 1, having mastered the ability to get box-to-box, while still providing a strong defensive presence. His most recent club match against Angers is the perfect example. He had two assists off of seven passes into the final third, yet he also made seven defensive contributions, including a clutch slide tackle.

Mathis Albert has a bright future ahead of him. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesWhat is most exciting about young Mathis Albert is his pure potential.The 17-year-old Borussia Dortmund player, who, this spring, became the youngest American ever to play in the German Bundesliga, has showed glimpses of it at both the club and international levels.In his debut camp with the USMNT this fall, Albert played a key role in the wins over both Peru and Chile. Against Peru, just five minutes after substituting onto the pitch, he won the USMNT a penalty kick, which Malik Tillman easily buried. The youngster’s tenacity and immediate impact deeply impressed Pochettino.“First action on the pitch? Bang, aggressive. Receive and go,” Pochettino exclaimed post-match. “...He goes ‘I want to go, I want to play, I want to show.’ That’s what we need, and that’s why I’m so happy.”Then against Chile, Albert scored for himself in stoppage time, briefly becoming the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history at 17 years, 131 days old, before the record was reclaimed by teammate Cavan Sullivan.Albert’s promise has earned him the attentions of several of Europe’s premier clubs. By 2030, he could be simply unstoppable.

Sergiño Dest was a World Cup starter this summer. / Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAnother one of the founding members of the “golden generation,” 25-year-old Sergiño Dest claimed the right flank at the World Cup this summer, starting four of the five matches. Formerly a right fullback for the USMNT, including at the 2022 World Cup, and still fullback for club side PSV Eindhoven, Dest boasts the defensive capabilities that are often still important to have in a winger. It’s his explosiveness and dizzying foot skills that truly set him apart, though. He was unable to generate any goal contributions this summer; however, it was those two attributes in particular that put backlines on their heels, creating moments of weakness that Dest’s teammates then exploited.He was rather unused by Pochettino during the fall international window, suggesting his starting position is anything but secure.

Christian Pulisic has experienced a serious downturn in form but is nonetheless the face of the USMNT. / John Todd/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesNo matter how tumultuous Christian Pulisic’s career has been as of late, there is no way he wasn’t going to make the top half of this list. When “Captain America” is playing at his best, there is no one better. He is the epitome of the player that defenders fear most, harboring an ability to weave through a backline as if gliding on skates. The 28-year-old’s poor World Cup performance—failing to deliver more than 45 quality minutes on the grand stage—may have let the nation down and mean that he is no longer the face of the USMNT; however, Pochettino would be foolish to write him off completely. Pulisic is already in the process of reigniting his club career with AC Milan, cracking back into the starting lineup under new manager Ruben Amorim.

Cavan Sullivan is the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesIf Pulisic is no longer the face of the USMNT, then Sullivan is.The teenager may only have three caps at the senior level, but he has gained worldwide attention for his talents on the pitch, turning 17 years old just last month. The Philadelphia Union star took Major League Soccer by storm this summer and is now up to seven goals and 14 assists in 20 matches started. He had a run of 10 straight league matches with at least one goal contribution this fall and broke a whole host of league records.Some worried about how his talents would translate to the international stage; however, he proved equally impressive there. He became the USMNT’s youngest goalscorer in history at 17 years and five days old, scoring against the team’s biggest rival, Mexico, no less. Sullivan’s play is defined by his swagger. He is not afraid to take on players, no matter how much older or more experienced they are. He is ruthless and determined. He is the present and the future of the USMNT.

ftbpro_01m55vddx87n.title: Cavan Sullivan Can’t Extend Record As Union Barely Survive Clash With Charlotte
ftbpro_01m55vddx87n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben SteinerOct 17, 2026Cavan Sullivan couldn't build on his record MLS goal contributions total.  / Isaiah Vazquez/MLS/Getty ImagesCavan Sullivan had a fantastic chance to secure victory for the Philadelphia Union late into Saturday’s match, but the 17-year-old ultimately couldn't save his side’s win streak in a thrilling 2–2 draw with Charlotte FC at Subaru Park.

The draw snapped the Union’s eight-game win streak, which dated back to Aug. 29, but maintained their unbeaten streak, which now stands at a club-record 15 games. Their last loss came on May 23 in a 6–4 defeat to Inter Miami.

Sullivan—who broke Alphonso Davies’s record for the most goal contributions by a teenager (21) in Wednesday’s 3–1 win over the Chicago Fire—saw his own personal streak snap too. Saturday’s affair signified his first league match since Aug. 1 without a goal contribution, ending an unprecedented 10-game run.

It wasn’t for a lack of trying, though. Sullivan ended the match with the most shots (five) and the most touches taken in the opposition’s box (10). He even found the back of the net midway through the second half, before the play was called back for offside.

With the game tied 2–2 late, he linked up with his older brother, Quinn Sullivan, in the 93rd minute but failed to beat Charlotte’s goalkeeper Kristjan Kahlina, who made an impressive save to secure a point for the visitors.
Cavan Sullivan NEARLY wins it for @PhilaUnion in stoppage time! 😮 pic.twitter.com/RiTWkj6RUf

While Sullivan couldn’t bring a win, it was still an impressive day for the Union. Milan Iloski netted his 19th goal of the season to open the scoring in the 24th minute from the penalty spot, and Bruno Damiani smashed home a shot from the top of the box to level the game at 2–2 in the 73rd minute, after Charlotte’s two goals from Rodolfo Aloko and Idan Toklomati.

Bidding farewell to its win streak gives a little adversity to a Union side that hasn't had much since Ryan Richter took over as interim manager for Bradley Carnell back in May. Now, the reigning Supporters’ Shield winners will have to wait until at least the last four games of the season to clinch a spot in the MLS Cup playoffs.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

It's not an easy road forward for the Union and Cavan Sullivan. / Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesThe Union will have two home games and two more on the road in the hunt to qualify for the playoffs and contend for a coveted top-four seed in the Eastern Conference, which would assure them home advantage in at least the first round of the postseason.

The next two weeks, though, won’t be easy. On Matchday 32, they’re off to face Carles Gil’s New England Revolution, a side that ranked third in the Eastern Conference heading into its Matchday 31 clash with the fourth-place Chicago Fire.
Afterwards, Nashville SC, who are chasing the all-time regular-season points record, will provide the toughest test yet, before the regular season wraps up against FC Cincinnati and Toronto FC.

Likely to qualify for the playoffs despite the challenges ahead, the Union will be an outside contender to win the MLS Cup. Nevertheless, any dream run will likely lean on Cavan Sullivan’s exceptional talents against the competitive likes of Inter Miami, Nashville, New England, Chicago and more.

ftbpro_01m575e2gnqw.title: ‘Not for Me’—Michael Carrick Hits Back at Wild Claim From Man Utd Legend
ftbpro_01m575e2gnqw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:00 AM EDTMichael Carrick has been forced to comment on Nicky Butt’s claims. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick bluntly rejected the claim that he had told Nicky Butt that management was “not for me” before stepping in at Old Trafford earlier this year.

In Italy, they say, Piove sempre sul bagnato—It always rains on the wet. Carrick has been drenched by a deluge of controversy in recent days to which his former teammates and friends are unhelpfully adding.

Amid a dire run of form, questions about his job security and an open revolt between the locker room and technical staff, Carrick has now found himself having to comment on the veracity of private conversations.

Butt, a former England teammate of Carrick who spent more than a decade in Manchester United’s first team after graduating from the club’s academy, claimed that the current Red Devils manager had given up on getting back in the dugout prior to Ruben Amorim’s departure in January.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

“I was with Michael before he got the United job and speaking to him about management,” Butt told fellow club icon Paul Scholes on their podcast, The Good, The Bad & The Football. “He went, ‘No, it’s not for me. It’s too much and my head’s all over the shop. I’ll only do it for the big job and the big job is United.’”
Carrick bluntly contradicted this sequence of events.

“I definitely wouldn’t be here if that was the case, would I? At this stage?” he asked. “It’s the best job I could possibly have. I feel a real privilege of being in this position and a real responsibility, but equally a drive of wanting to make a difference and having success here. I’m loving it.

“I love the situation when actually you get a little bit of a struggle where you’ve got to find a way out of it. I actually really enjoy that because that’s part of what drives you to have success. If you’re not ready for that and you can’t do anything, that’s difficult. You’re never going to be great, so we’ve got to work our way through it and I’m enjoying it as we’ve gone.”

Can Michael Carrick bring back the glory days? / John Peters/Manchester United/Getty ImagesRather than dwell on the fact that United have endured their worst start to a league season in 40 years, Carrick was inclined to look upward, insisting that his side are “in the mix” for Premier League (and Champions League) glory.
“We’ve had a start where we haven’t won some football games,” the retired midfielder admitted. “Alright, but correct me if I’m wrong, we are five points off the top four.

“Perspective is important and football can change. I think when we came in, we were a lot further away from third spot and we ended up finishing third. So it depends what you focus on. You either focus on the things that may be issues or you focus on the things that are possible and what can be achieved. It’s a very different mentality.
“For us to win the Premier League is a massive step, of course it is. But it’s definitely something we’re striving for. We’ve got to keep pushing for it.

“We’ve won one game in the Champions League, we’ve lost one game. We’re still in the mix of that. And we’re certainly still in the mix of the Premier League, of finishing towards the top. That’s the challenge.
“It feels because of the results that everyone focusses on the negative side. It’s up to us to turn that corner and it's actually not that far away.”
