ftbpro_01m5776zw2zf.title: Emiliano Martinez Reveals Chelsea Return Timeline After Emergency Surgery
ftbpro_01m5776zw2zf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:00 AM EDTEmiliano Martínez posted from his hospital bed. / Instagram/emi_martinez26Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez predicted that he would be “back in a few weeks” despite undergoing emergency surgery in the hours after suffering a serious head-on collision against Everton.

It had been a grueling opening 75 minutes at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, with far more cynical fouls than silky footwork on display from both sides. However, there was no malice, just misfortune, when Jarrad Branthwaite tried to connect with a set-piece delivery and only served to find the face of Martínez.
While Everton’s unwitting center back managed to recover to finish the match, the Argentina international was stretchered off the pitch and taken straight to hospital.

Propped up on a bed in his medical gown, Martínez took to Instagram to allay any grave concerns held by fans. “Thanks to everyone for the messages; the surgery went well,” the 34-year-old wrote. “The most important thing is that we won, and with a clean sheet. We’ll be back in a few weeks.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Emiliano Martínez suffered a painful clash. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesThe full force of Branthwaite’s head connected squarely with Martínez, who was left with a fractured jaw, Chelsea have revealed. The goalkeeper was assessed on the pitch for eight minutes by medical staff before he was taken to hospital, while conscious.

Xabi Alonso revealed after the match that his summer recruit had also suffered a “concussion” while attempting to clear Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s cross. That additional diagnosis will only delay Martínez’s return.

Martínez’s prediction of a “few weeks” for his recovery is wisely vague. Players coming back from broken jaws can take all manner of different timelines, depending on the severity of the issue and the context of the season.

At this summer’s World Cup, for instance, Austrian defender Stefan Posch broke his jaw in his nation’s opening group game but made himself available to feature against Argentina five days later while donning a protective mask. Posch was fighting for minutes on the biggest stage the sport has and, crucially, did not require surgery.

Should Martínez be unavailable until the November international break, which begins for Chelsea on Nov. 9, just three weeks after his surgery, he would only miss four matches. However, they are big games.

The Blues host fierce London rivals Tottenham Hotspur next Saturday before traveling to Liverpool for the marquee fixture in the Carabao Cup fourth round. There is also a league visit from Manchester United on Halloween and a daunting trek north to Sunderland.

Mike Penders is set for a run in the team. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesBefore Martínez had even been signed, Alonso was toying with the idea of promoting Mike Penders above the error-prone Robert Sánchez. In the end, the option of signing a World Cup winner on the cheap proved too good to turn down, but Penders will now get his chance to shine.

“Mike has personality,” Alonso said of the 21-year-old uncapped Belgium call-up. “He’s brave and we have full trust ‌with him. He did well when he came on. He played in the cup games and whenever he’s ⁠needed. Like the other players, whenever they are needed they can perform.
“It’s all about the squad—that all the ​players feel important and can have ‌their moment whenever they are needed, ​and that’s very positive.” Penders is certainly needed now.

ftbpro_01m57ayrvj67.title: Barcelona Set Up Perfect Storm of Humiliation for Real Madrid in El Clasico
ftbpro_01m57ayrvj67.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:55 AM EDTLamine Yamal must be licking his lips ahead of El Clásico. / Jesus Ruiz/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images (Yamal), Visionhaus/Getty Images (badge)Barcelona’s record-breaking start to La Liga has brought them to the precipice of a new kind of humiliation for Real Madrid; having a 58-year club record broken under the white-hot spotlight of El Clásico.

Hansi Flick’s imperious entertainers romped to a 5–2 victory against Real Betis on Saturday, extending their perfect run to nine straight La Liga wins. No club in the history of the competition has ever made it to double digits, while the Real Madrid vintage of 1968–69 stands as the only other team to match Barça’s current run.
Thanks to that mischievous fixture computer, Barcelona have the chance to surpass Madrid’s high watermark in next Sunday’s Clásico against Los Blancos themselves.

Beyond the results Barcelona have achieved, the manner of these victories is all the more staggering. The handful of goals racked up against Betis was the sixth time this season that Flick’s side have scored five or more times in a single game. For comparison, Real Madrid have managed that feat just three times since the start of last season.

Barcelona are ticking along at a ridiculous average of 4.3 goals per game across all competitions, with 13 different goalscorers to thank for this output. Even in the absence of their talismanic forward Raphinha, the defending Spanish champions have continued to plunder all before them.
However, the chaotic triumph over Betis also exposed the weaknesses which exist in this winning machine.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Rodri hasn’t been blinded by Barcelona’s goals. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesFor all Barcelona’s abundant offensive threat, they remain defensively vulnerable. “The team consistently shows its attacking potential, but we’re conceding too many goals,” Rodri fretted after watching his side concede twice in Seville. “That’s an area where we can improve.”

Barcelona have kept just one clean sheet in their last seven games, conceding nine goals during that leaky span. This is no new phenomenon; Flick has not seen his side shut out a Champions League opponent since April 2025.

In a way, this is to be expected. Flick is taking a calculated risk by setting his side up with an adventurous high press which leaves so much space in behind their backline. The gamble is that Barcelona will, more often than not, win the ball back in the final third to catch the opposition in transition rather than give the opponent the chance to run through on goal themselves.

This season, the bet has come off every time: Barcelona are on a perfect run of 11 straight wins. Yet, elite clubs have repeatedly proven capable of finding a way to pierce the Catalans’ flimsy resolve.
Rodri’s signing was meant to shore up this side of the game, but as the summer recruit would freely admit, one player cannot change an entire system built with this inherent sense of risk.

ftbpro_01m57djh8cj8.title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Leeds: Red Devils Stop the Rot at Elland Road
ftbpro_01m57djh8cj8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack11:23 AM EDTManchester United shared the spoils at Elland Road.  / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United were held to a point by historic rivals Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday, as Dominic Calvert-Lewin canceled out Bryan Mbuemo’s opener.

Michael Carrick entered this fixture firmly in the hot seat after a woeful showing against Tottenham Hotspur was followed by defeat in the Champions League at Atlético Madrid. Lisandro Martínez’s postmatch comments all but confirmed United’s state of crisis, and many believed they were underdogs in West Yorkshire, given the impressive start to the season Leeds have made.

Daniel Farke’s side were beaten for the first time this term at Arsenal last weekend, yet they were made to work incredibly hard for a point against the Red Devils. In a throwback affair laden with grit, Man Utd competed fiercely and were good value for their first-half lead.

However, Leeds enjoyed waves of momentum that the visitors struggled to stymie, and Calvert-Lewin is proving inevitable in front of goal at Elland Road. He drew Leeds level from a messy corner sequence, and although there was plenty of time left in the game, both teams seemed pretty content with a point apiece.
There was an absence of big chances late in the game, and Carrick’s side will return to Manchester with something to build on.

Mbeumo delivered from a central position. / Paul ELLIS/AFP/Getty ImagesPlay Bryan Mbeumo centrally, and he will deliver.
The Cameroon international has spent much of the season to date shunted out wide, forced to create separation one-on-one all while limiting his touches in the opposition’s box. It’s not his game.

He worked superbly in tandem with Ivan Toney at Brentford, with the pair particularly proficient on the counterattack, and while his potency in transition has manifested only sporadically in Manchester, Mbeumo has shown that he possesses canny instincts in front of goal.

He missed a gilt-edged chance with his head from an excellent Youri Tielemans delivery, but atoned soon after. The previous mishap was no deterrent for Mbeumo, who finished ever so cleverly from another Tielemans cross, opening up his foot to steer the ball past James Trafford and into the corner.

This wasn’t exactly a standout performance from Man Utd’s goalscorer, who looked dazed and confused during Leeds’ goal sequence, yet the Cameroonian’s strike ultimately meant a result was earned at Elland Road.

Fernandes must’ve just smelt his performance at Elland Road. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesMan Utd were pretty impressive as a collective in a tough environment, with Leeds evolving into Chris Wilder’s Sheffield United when they dazzled the Premier League with their marauding center backs in 2019–20.
Carrick should thus be content with a point, even if a lead was surrendered, but United’s gritty result was claimed despite the efforts of their captain.

Bruno Fernandes loves playing against Leeds, yet the very worst of the Portuguese came to play on Sunday afternoon. He was petulant and argumentative, even castigating teammates for making the right decision (see his reaction toward Tielemans after Mbeumo headed his delightful cross wide).
He’s performing as if he knows he’s in a rut, trying to do too much to rediscover his best. At the moment, Fernandes’s apex appears a million miles away.
Mbeumo opened the scoring with a clever finish. / Stu Forster/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Senne Lammens—7.0: Wasn’t much he could’ve done to prevent Calvert-Lewin from restoring parity. While Leeds enjoyed bright spells, they failed to work Man Utd’s goalkeeper.

CB: Leny Yoro—6.9: The young Frenchman is certainly growing in comfort, even if he was asked to perform a different role here. Yoro had no issues defending space as one of the wide center backs in Man Utd’s back three.
CB: Harry Maguire—7.5: There was again no clean sheet for the visitors, although Maguire did deal with Leeds’ distinct threat from crosses rather well.

CB: Lisandro Martínez—6.1: The Argentine remained in the team despite his outburst on Tuesday, but he was only in the limelight for 45 minutes. Martínez was withdrawn at halftime, likely due to injury.

ftbpro_01m57ecthx2r.title: Maresca Reveals Haaland’s One-Word Update After Huge Man City Injury Scare
ftbpro_01m57ecthx2r.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom9:45 AM EDTErling Haaland hobbled off for Manchester City against Ipswich Town. / Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesManchester City manager Enzo Maresca revealed that Erling Haaland had provided a brief but positive update on his health after ending Saturday’s win over Ipswich Town hobbling off in visible distress. The No. 9 was “O.K.”

Haaland is playing a lot better than “O.K.” despite the ongoing turmoil surrounding Manchester City. The relentlessly prolific Norwegian nabbed another brace against Ipswich, taking his tally to a ridiculous 12 goals in his last eight appearances for the club. As Maresca laughed earlier this season: “How do you say in English? Happy wife, happy life? For us, happy Erling, happy life.”
Despite two more goals and another set of three points this weekend, Haaland was a picture of discontent at the Etihad Stadium.

Erling Haaland was chasing a hat trick. / Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesCity held a 3–2 lead over their newly promoted visitors deep in stoppage time but the Tractor Boys were pushing for an equalizer. In the face of this pressure, Haaland led a late counterattack to put the game to bed and complete his hat trick.

Haaland’s first touch got away from him just enough to give Jack Clarke the encouragement to go for the bouncing ball. The Ipswich substitute got his studs up, making contact with the ball and offering a spiky wall against which Haaland connected.
The striker still had a little over a minute to hobble around, appealing for full time before angrily trudging down the tunnel as soon as the whistle was blown.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Erling Haaland wasn’t Manchester City’s only concern. / Michael Steele/Getty ImagesThankfully for Haaland, Manchester City and almost every Fantasy Premier League player on the platform, no lasting damage would appear to have been done. “Erling said he was O.K. so hopefully it is nothing serious,” Maresca revealed. However, the City boss did add: “The one we need to wait on is Antoine.”

Antoine Semenyo was one of five City players who appeared to sustain some sort of fitness concern in the closing stages of Saturday’s bruising clash. The winger was only introduced in the 77th minute but still failed to come through the contest unscathed.

Mateo Kovačić, Nico O’Reilly and Matheus Nunes were all forced off with various niggles. Maresca played down the ailments for Kovačić and Nunes but warned that O’Reilly was still nursing a back complaint.

The relentless fixture list doesn’t afford much time for recovery. City host Greek outfit AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday before traveling to Aston Villa for Saturday’s early kickoff. While a double-header against a royally in-form Brighton & Hove Albion awaits at the end of October, Maresca may take the upcoming midweek clash as opportunity to fulfill his promise of resting Haaland.

ftbpro_01m57f0mn8m0.title: The Best Winning Starts in Premier League History—And How They Ended
ftbpro_01m57f0mn8m0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 18, 2026Chelsea’s record from 2005–06 is under threat. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesIt’s how every manager draws it up. After a summer of running and touring, they all dream of the perfect start to competitive action.
The Premier League is a cruel mistress, and every victory must be earned. One win is tough enough, a string of triumphs is an admirable feat and a lengthy winning run to open the season is utopia.

There’s typically a pace-setter, and an array of teams since the competition’s inception in 1992 have enjoyed dream starts to the campaign, teasing a runaway title victory. But history has shown that titles aren’t won in August, September or even October.
Here are the eight longest winning runs to start a Premier League season in the competition’s history, and how each of team has fared.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Man City rolled after securing the treble. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesManchester City were feeling pretty good about themselves entering the 2023–24 campaign, with Rodri’s strike in Istanbul ensuring they completed a historic treble the season prior. And City’s midfield enforcer ensured their winning run stretched beyond two matches at the start of the fresh campaign, striking late at the newly promoted Sheffield United to secure a 2–1 victory at Bramall Lane. Pep Guardiola‘s side defeated Burnley and Newcastle United without conceding, then trounced Fulham and eased past West Ham United before a Rodri red card forced them to work for a sixth consecutive victory.They were stunned by Wolverhampton Wanderers in Gameweek 7, and subsequently beaten by primary challengers Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium the following week. The Gunners would once again make a strong push for the title, but City embarked on a staggering 23-match unbeaten run, including 11 straight victories to wrap up the season, to lift a fourth-consecutive title.

Liverpool came up just short after an excellent start. / Laurence Griffiths/Getty ImagesThis was the season when Jürgen Klopp’s Liverpool truly emerged. The summer arrivals of Alisson and Fabinho proved transformative, as the Reds swiftly evolved into fierce title contenders after a fourth-place finish in 2017–18. The tone was set with six straight wins to start the season, as Liverpool downed West Ham United, Crystal Palace and Brighton & Hove Albion without conceding. Victory at Tottenham Hotspur (when Spurs were not an incompetent force) was a statement triumph, and although their winning start was halted by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, the Reds wouldn’t taste defeat until Jan. 3. Unfortunately, the 2–1 loss to Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium would prove decisive, as Klopp’s side cruelly missed out on the title despite amassing a whopping 97 points.

Pep Guardiola’s reign started with six wins. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesGuardiola’s dominant tenure in Manchester started with six Premier League wins on the bounce, although there was a prevailing sense that the Spaniard’s side would soon get figured out. Their winning run included just one clean sheet despite a tame fixture list, and a 2–0 defeat at Spurs was one that certainly felt as if it was coming. It was ultimately a disappointing debut season for Guardiola on English soil, with his porous City outfit so often exposed on the counter attack. They slipped to as low as fifth in January, but recovered to finish third and qualify for the Champions League. Then came the ‘Centurions.’

Chelsea regained the title during Carlo Ancelotti’s first season in charge. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesAfter a couple of years of managerial flux, Roman Abramovich turned to Carlo Ancelotti, with the Italian enjoying his first taste of English soccer after collecting a bucketload of silverware in his homeland. Ancelotti rolled with pretty much the same roster that had come within a whisker of the Champions League final the previous season, and Chelsea’s experienced squad got off to a flyer at the start of the new manager’s tenure. Didier Drogba’s cross-cum-shot ensured the Blues were victorious on the opening weekend against Hull City, and their six-game winning run was capped by a familiar beatdown of Spurs at the Bridge.Two defeats followed in their next three outings, and they slipped to third after drawing to Blackburn Rovers in March. However, seven wins from their next eight, including a 2–1 win at Old Trafford, meant they edged Manchester United to the title by a single point.

"That‘s entertainment." / Mark Leech/Getty ImagesKevin Keegan’s “Entertainers” were born. Newcastle United’s infamous title collapse would arrive the following season, but their start to 1994–95 offered a glimpse into the near-future. The Magpies scored 22 times in their opening six victories, keeping just the one clean sheet. The masses were dazzled, and the Toon Army believed.It wouldn’t last, even if their unbeaten start to the campaign extended until Gameweek 12. They endured a wretched festive period, winning just one of their 11 outings between Nov. 7 and Jan. 21. A poor end to the season meant Newcastle finished sixth.

The Cityzens have purred at the start of Enzo Maresca’s reign. / Kate McShane/Getty ImagesIt was a summer overhaul at the Etihad Stadium, as the Premier League’s supreme force over the past decade bade farewell to the mastermind of their dominance, Guardiola, as well as multiple imperative stalwarts. Guardiola’s former assistant Enzo Maresca was given the unenviable task of filling his boots, but the Italian looks set to continue the trend of Guardiola successors thriving. Man City are 100% through seven games, having played the previous two with the darkest of clouds lingering overhead. This all may count for nought after an independent commission found them guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. Still, their on-field work has undeniably been impressive. City’s perfect start so far includes victories at Man Utd and Liverpool, as well as high-scoring wins over Sunderland and Ipswich Town.

Liverpool romped to the title. / Laurence Griffiths/Getty ImagesA fifth conquest of the continent made up for their harsh second-place finish in the 2018–19 Premier League, and Klopp’s Reds entered 2019–20 with a single mission in mind. Liverpool were rampant from the outset, winning eight straight. They weren’t behind in a match until Gameweek 5, and although a Daniel James-inspired Manchester United took two points off them to end their 100% start, it’d be the only blemish on their Premier League record until Feb. 29. Klopp’s side ascended to the division’s summit on Gameweek 2, and they refused to relinquish that position. They were unrelenting and the runaway champions. Soccer was brought to a halt in March due to the Covid-19 pandemic, and their crowning wouldn‘t arrive until the summer as a result.A spotty conclusion to the campaign meant they didn’t breach the 100-point threshold, yet this was still one of the most dominant title triumphs in the competition’s history.

José Mourinho’s Chelsea successfully defended their crown. / ODD ANDERSEN/AFP/Getty ImagesMaresca’s City are two wins away from equaling Chelsea’s record. Liverpool threatened to match the Blues‘ perfect nine-game stretch to start their title defense in 2005–06. José Mourinho’s side romped to the trophy during the “Special One’s” debut season in west London, and very few projected Chelsea to relinquish their crown. Those predictions were vindicated by their supreme start, which included victories over London rivals Arsenal and Spurs. Frank Lampard’s double against Aston Villa helped Chelsea to their seventh-straight win to set a new Premier League record, and they’d then thrash Liverpool at Anfield and Bolton Wanderers on home soil to reach nine.A draw at Everton meant Mourinho’s side couldn’t quite reach the all-time top-flight record of 11 wins set by Spurs in 1960–61. Still, Chelsea would go back-to-back, with Mourinho’s second title wrapped up by virtue of a 3–0 win over Man Utd in April.

ftbpro_01m57f15bvc1.title: ‘We Have Done That’—Carrick Explains Martinez Decision After Transfer Tantrum
ftbpro_01m57f15bvc1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:50 AM EDTMichael Carrick (left) has not burned any bridges with Lisandro Martínez. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick has insisted that he and everyone else at the club have “moved on” from Lisandro Martínez’s explosive midweek comments by way of explaining the defender’s selection in Sunday’s starting XI against Leeds United.

In the immediate aftermath of Martínez’s stunning outburst on Tuesday night, when the Argentina international used his postmatch media duties to call out a perceived lack of investment in this summer’s transfer window, there were concerns that his Manchester United career may have ended in the bowels of Atlético Madrid’s stadium.
Yet, just five days later, Martínez hasn’t even been dropped to the bench.

“What’s done is done and we’ve moved on,” Carrick sternly told Sky Sports, pointing toward Martínez’s belated apology, which was the second clarification of his damning statement. “So we have done that and we’ve prepared the team. We know their threats, their strengths, we know that. We’ve got some as well, so we’ll get the balance right.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Carrick has taken a defiantly upbeat attitude despite United’s crumbling form. The manager who has insisted that his team remain “in the mix” for Premier League and Champions League glory was similarly confident about Sunday’s clash.

“It’s a challenging place to come, of course it is, but it’s a fantastic game to be involved with and we’re in a good place to come and attack it and look forward to it,” Carrick claimed. “You’ve got to bring a little bit of everything, and none more so than today. The atmosphere and the intensity that naturally is generated in a game like this is something that brings it out in us as well.”
Starting XI (4-2-2-2): Senne Lammens; Leny Yoro, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martínez, Diogo Dalot; Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba; Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans; Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo.
Substitutes: Karl Darlow, Harry Amass, Matthijs de Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui, Mason Mount, Shea Lacey, Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford, Joshua Zirkzee,

Matthijs de Ligt is working his way back. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesFor all Carrick’s talk of reconciliation, this is a decision of mutual convenience. United are desperately short of defensive options who could potentially replace Martínez and line up alongside Harry Maguire.

Leny Yoro would be the most obvious choice but the versatile Frenchman has been chosen at right back while Noussair Mazraoui continues to recover from a back problem sustained on international duty. Neither Ayden Heaven nor Luke Shaw have been even fit enough to make the matchday roster while Matthijs de Ligt is still short of match sharpness.

The Netherlands international has not played a single second of competitive soccer for almost 11 months. A nagging back problem required surgery which forced De Ligt to miss the World Cup and he has only recently been eased back into first-team training.

ftbpro_01m57mkw6ptq.title: Four Takeaways From Man Utd Result That Inspires More Questions Than Answers
ftbpro_01m57mkw6ptq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 18, 2026It was a mixed match for Manchester United. / Stu Forster/Getty ImagesLooking back on his experience of taking Manchester United to Leeds United’s formidable home ground, Sir Alex Ferguson once wrote: “The crowd invariably give us the impression that a lynching would be too good for us.”

Michael Carrick would have experienced a metaphorical assault from those in Manchester, let alone Yorkshire, had his United side fallen to defeat at Elland Road on Sunday afternoon. This was the club’s worst start to a league season since the dire sequence of results which led to Ferguson’s appointment 40 years ago. After a week spent fending off controversy and a calamitous run of form, the Red Devils managed to salvage a 1–1 draw on enemy turf.
Yet, rather than some grand show of rejuvenation under Carrick, United delivered a performance that threw up more questions than answers.

It was all change for Manchester United. / Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty ImagesLisandro Martínez’s takedown of Manchester United’s technical director Jason Wilcox stole the spotlight but his assessment of Carrick was damning with faint praise. “He does his best,” the World Cup winner shrugged.
“Every season is different. You can’t stay with what you did last season. The teams know how you play, they know every detail, if you don’t change next season [it] is a big problem.”
Carrick took that feedback onboard and went for something very different.

United deviated significantly from their favored 4-2-3-1 formation, lining up in a flexible system dictated by the phase of play and Leeds’ positioning. Off the ball, the Red Devils shuttled into a back five—the system which played a part in Ruben Amorim’s sacking earlier this year—with Amad Diallo following Leeds wingback Gabriel Gudmundsson on his forward raids.

The in-possession shape was even more flexible. Without a natural left winger or center forward in the starting lineup, Carrick went with a narrow front three of Bryan Mbeumo together with natural midfielders Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans. That unorthodox frontline combined well for United’s opener.

Tielemans lent the ball to Amad out wide before reluctantly running behind Leeds’ backline, the creaking of his joints as he slowly gathered speed almost audible above Elland Road’s roar. The Belgian slid a slick first-time pass across the face of goal for Mbeumo to convert. Moments earlier, the pair had combined for a chance which Mbeumo spurned.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lisandro Martínez (right) was trusted to start on Sunday. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesCarrick had little choice but to swallow Martínez’s apology after his midweek outburst, overlook the center back’s first statement which offered no remorse and keep him in his starting XI for Sunday’s derby. Any damage that decision could have done to his reputation, in and out of the club, was not as severe as the strain his absence would have taken on United’s defense, in the eyes of Carrick. That point was swiftly proven.

Martínez started and helped his team keep Leeds in check. The hosts were limited to just four shots and a puny 0.25 xG in the first half with the familiar pairing of Harry Maguire and Martínez in tact. That duo would be forcibly disbanded during the interval, when the Argentine was forced off after appearing to pick up a knock during the opening 45 minutes.

Noussair Mazraoui was brought on in place of Martínez and surprisingly lined up to the left of Maguire, leaving Leny Yoro in his hybrid right back/center back role. Within six minutes of the Morocco international’s introduction, he proved why Carrick had favored Martínez.

At a corner which Mazraoui cheaply conceded, the 28-year-old was out-jumped by Tarik Muharemović, who nodded the ball down for Dominic Calvert-Lewin to swipe in and equalize for the hosts. Martínez glumly watched on from the bench beneath his oversized hood.

Leny Yoro was busy on Sunday. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesNone of United’s contingent covered themselves in glory on their Champions League trip to Madrid in midweek but Yoro was left to stew over a clumsy red card. The 20-year-old’s response to the first red card of his senior career could scarcely have been more impressive.

Tasked with a complicated new role that forced him to shift between two different systems in the inhospitable atmosphere of a vengeful Elland Road, Yoro rose to the challenge, quite literally. The sprightly defender was everywhere, jumping off his invisible trampoline to head away the volley of crosses raining down upon United’s penalty area.
Yoro held firm, even as Leeds cranked up the pressure in a lopsided second half. If only his more senior teammates could have reacted as impressively.

It’s not been a great run for Bruno Fernandes. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesSince he rattled in a hat trick against Ipswich Town at the end of August, Fernandes has only provided a goal or an assist in one of his subsequent eight appearances for Manchester United—and that was against Azerbaijan upstarts Sabah FK.

Fernandes has been United’s bellwether throughout his career; the team is invariably at its best when its captain is. In an attempt to change the fortunes of the collective and his star individual, Carrick has experimented with Fernandes’s position in his last two games.

The club captain was shunted onto the right wing against Atlético Madrid midweek, when he twice came close to scoring but also failed to offer any discipline off the ball. Amad was tasked with holding the width on United’s right against Leeds, giving Fernandes licence to roam all over the pitch. That freedom didn’t translate to any real threat, with United’s playmaker-in-chief creating just one chance.

ftbpro_01m57mp13w62.title: Real Madrid Avoid Vinicius Junior Mistakes With Jude Bellingham’s New Contract
ftbpro_01m57mp13w62.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell11:05 AM EDTJude Bellingham is here to stay at the Bernabéu. / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Madrid and Jude Bellingham have reportedly reached an agreement on a new deal that keeps the midfield maestro at the Bernabéu through 2031.

Bellingham, who made the move to the Spanish capital in June 2023, came to the negotiating table at the end of the club’s trophyless 2025–26 campaign to hatch out details of a new contract. Now, just a few months later, the two parties are already shaking hands.

AS report Real Madrid agreed to prolong Bellingham’s stay in a white shirt for an additional two seasons, extending his contract that originally expired in 2029. The new deal comes with improved terms that likely includes a salary bump to reflect his “standing” both on the pitch and in the dressing room.

At just 23 years old, Bellingham has emerged as an unflappable leader for Los Blancos. The England international learned from playing alongside Toni Kroos and Luka Modrić what it takes to win at the Bernabéu, and he has since emulated the two club icons. Even when he wasn’t at his best last season, he was still playing with a work rate and tenacity many of his more senior players lacked.

Bellingham’s contributions also cannot be ignored. He dragged Real Madrid to the 2023–24 La Liga title in his debut campaign, and also played a massive role in the team’s Champions League triumph that season. The midfielder is constantly coming up with clutch goals in the biggest moments as well, no matter what position he’s playing.
A new deal for Bellingham is no surprise, but the efficient negotiating process is after the drawn out process of Vinícius Júnior’s renewal.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Júnior forced Real Madrid’s hand this summer. / Michael Regan/UEFA/Getty ImagesReal Madrid were previously locked in a standoff with Vinícius Jr for 19 months. The winger’s contract was set to expire at the end of this season, but the two parties could not agree on the financial terms of the deal.

Vinícius Jr was thought to have been asking for a salary of €30 million ($33.7 million) per year, a number Los Blancos were never going to approve given the implications it would have on the their wage structure. But the Brazilian held firm on his demands, dragging out a contract saga that came to a head this summer.

When the club did not bend to his wishes, Vinícius Jr flirted with Premier League champions Arsenal, which forced Real Madrid to come back to the table with an improved offer to keep him at the Bernabéu.

In the end, Vinícius Jr got the 15-time European champions to hand him a mammoth six-year extension with a reported salary around €24 million ($27 million), which was €4 million more than they wanted to pay.

This time around with Bellingham, the two parties were “on the same page from the outset,” per AS, and no games were played behind the scenes to come to an agreement. The club made quick work of locking down the 23-year-old before he too could begin shopping himself around to increase his salary.

Jude Bellingham is in top form again for Real Madrid and England. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesBellingham once called himself a “victim” of his own versatility at Real Madrid. The former Borussia Dortmund standout played as a false nine, a No. 10, a left midfielder, a central midfielder and a quasi-fullback all in his first three years with the team.
Previous managers rotated Bellingham all over the pitch to plug holes in an injury-riddled and depleted squad. José Mourinho, though, is not making the same mistake.

Bellingham is back to his favored No. 10 role, where he has five goal contributions in 10 appearances this season so far. His three goals are already a third of what he scored in the entire 2025–26 campaign.

Standout performances for England also helped Bellingham find his groove again. The midfielder was sensational for the Three Lions at this summer’s World Cup, bagging seven goals and one assist en route to a third-place finish.

Bellingham also walked away from the September-October international break with one goal and four assists. He is no doubt back to his top form, a great sign for an England side and a Real Madrid team desperate to hoist a major trophy.

ftbpro_01m57r4kzv9x.title: Are the Next Four La Liga Games Make or Break for Vinicius Junior at Real Madrid?
ftbpro_01m57r4kzv9x.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell12:45 PM EDTVinícius Júnior  / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesJust a few months ago, Vinícius Júnior was celebrating a massive six-year extension, pledging his loyalty to Real Madrid “forever.”

Fast forward to mid-October and the No. 7 is hard-pressed to find anything worth celebrating. Vinícius Jr has had a dreadful start to the season, finding the back of the net just once in 10 appearances across all competitions.

Perhaps even more concerning is his overall state of play for both club and country. Vinícius Jr is one-dimensional down the left flank, stuck on autopilot to try and dribble around three defenders only to lose possession. There’s little playmaking coming from his right foot, and even worse finishing. He’s also shown less interest in tracking back than ever before, which is saying something.

To make matters even more dire, Vinícius Jr saw red in the team’s 1–0 win over Villarreal and earned a four-game suspension for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba and then squaring up with the referee.

Now, the Brazil international cannot return to La Liga action until after the November international break, leaving the door open for blockbuster summer signing Yan Diomande to make the left wing his new home.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Júnior needs to fight for his place back at Real Madrid. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe concept of Vinícius Jr losing his place in Real Madrid’s lineup would have been laughable just two years ago. The Brazilian was the best winger in the world in a 2023–24 campaign that ended with the Champions League crown, La Liga title and Spanish Super Cup for Los Blancos.

He finished second in the Ballon d’Or voting and was the face of the biggest club in the world. But little has gone right for Vinícius Jr in the ensuing years. The 26-year-old struggled to gel with Kylian Mbappé, clashed with Xabi Alonso and now looks closer to being benched than scoring a goal.

Vinícius Jr admitted during the September-October international break he needed “some confidence”  amid his poor run of form, only to get sent off in his first match back for Real Madrid. He then was hooked after just 59 minutes against Roma midweek, forced to watch from the sidelines as his team completed a vintage Champions League comeback.

As Vinícius Jr well knows, results are bigger than any one player at Real Madrid. He had a front row seat when the club pushed legends like Sergio Ramos and Luka Modrić out the door. He arrived one season after Cristiano Ronaldo received the same treatment. He also watched as Los Blancos shopped around Rodrygo two summers ago after the once-trusted forward had a poor spell.

Trophies are the endgame. Trophies are the standard. It’s why the Bernabéu crowd has booed the team over and over again throughout the last two seasons. Vinícius Jr has received the brunt of the whistles during that stretch, a brutal reminder that past triumphs mean nothing at Real Madrid; it’s only about what title comes next, and if the biggest players are helping the team get there.

The pressure only gets worse when there is a young player eager to prove himself more capable than an underperforming veteran. The worst part for Vinícius Jr? He cannot even compete with Diomande now that he’s suspended.

Yan Diomande is playing better and better each game. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty ImagesThere’s a graveyard of left wingers who have tried and failed to displace Vinícius Jr at Real Madrid. Rodrygo had to learn to play on the right. Mbappé transitioned to a center forward. Eden Hazard had a notoriously horrible time trying to own the position. Diomande started this season on the bench, consistently overlooked despite his eye-watering price tag.

But now that Vinícius Jr is suspended for four games, Diomande gets the chance to stake his claim. The teenager already has a goal and two assists in his last three starts, and now has the full freedom of the left flank to show why Los Blancos signed him in a deal worth up to a club-record €140 million ($157.3 million).

Should Diomande impress, he has a real chance of keeping the starting job even beyond the team’s upcoming four La Liga games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Mourinho has been treading on eggshells with Vinícius Jr so far, but the Portuguese boss needs results more than he needs his superstar winger happy.

If Real Madrid go on a winning streak and somehow beat Barcelona without Vinícius Jr, then it would be nearly impossible to simply reinsert the struggling Brazilian into the lineup. The goals aren’t there. The assists aren’t there. The defensive work isn’t there. He would be logging minutes simply based on his past contributions, all while a player of Diomande’s quality potentially rots on the bench.

The best case scenario for Vinícius Jr would be for the young forward to struggle, making it so there is no controversy about the No. 7 taking back the left wing upon his return. But my, how far Vinícius Jr has fallen if he simply wins his starting job back by default.

Kylian Mbappé (left) and Vinícius Júnior have struggled to build chemistry.  / Mateo Villalba/Getty ImagesEven if Real Madrid go on a great run in the build-up to the November international break, it doesn’t automatically mean Vinícius Jr will remain out of the action once domestic play returns. After all, the team enjoyed its best stretch of performances last season while Mbappé was out, and the Frenchman still waltzed back into the XI when he recovered from injury.

Los Blancos went from winning five games in a row, beating Manchester City twice and Atlético Madrid along the way, to a four-game winless streak once Mbappé regained his starting position in the spring of 2025–26.
Despite the evidence to the contrary, the club was hellbent to make Mbappé work in the team. Vinícius Jr will hope he gets the same treatment when he returns from his suspension.

ftbpro_01m57sprmgq7.title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Nottingham Forest: Madueke Saves Underwhelming Teammates
ftbpro_01m57sprmgq7.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:45 PM EDTNoni Madueke was the match-winner at the City Ground. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal avoided a third consecutive stalemate at the City Ground thanks to Noni Madueke’s deflected strike, as the champions eked out a 1–0 victory against a depleted Nottingham Forest.

This was a dire contest that, in truth, probably didn’t deserve a winner. Oliver Glasner’s side proved mightily tough to penetrate, and in the absence of Morgan Gibbs-White, it was always going to be a challenge for the hosts the bypass Arsenal’s formidable backline.

Forest produced spurts on the counterattack in the wake of dreary spells of Gunners possession, and were seemingly the more likely to steal an advantage after a bright start to the second half. However, Mikel Arteta’s side are familiar with such slogfests, and muscle memory kicked in late on.

Madueke’s driving run from the left produced a shot that nicked off two Forest defenders to beat the previously untested Matz Sels and hand Arsenal a lead they wouldn’t relinquish with 10 minutes to play. The hosts certainly crafted enough in the dying embers to earn an unlikely point, but Liam Delap and Chris Wood were denied by some outstanding recovery defending from the visitors.
And so the champions moved back above Brighton & Hove Albion and into second, three points behind the perfect Manchester City at the Premier League’s summit.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The Gunners again struggled to get going in the first half. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesSlow starts have been a feature of Arsenal’s outings so far this season, and the Gunners once again toiled without much reward in the opening 45 minutes at the City Ground.

While Nottingham Forest have had a tough start to their campaign, Glasner-led sides are unyielding opponents. Here, Arsenal encountered a stubborn 5-4-1 defensive block that had little interest in surrendering space to the Gunners’ crafty midfield technicians and Bukayo Saka down the right.

And once again, they couldn’t get going early on. Excluding the Carabao Cup third-round win at Ipswich Town, Arsenal have failed to score in the first half of each of their previous six matches. Mere bursts have been enough for Mikel Arteta’s side since the 3–0 humbling at Brighton & Hove Albion, with supporters still concerned about the state of their forward line.

They remain an imperious defensive force and a team that’s ever so hard to play against from behind. However, the sluggishness that has defined their first halves this term, certainly after their opening-day victory over Coventry City, means it’s been a slog for the champions to achieve this game state.

So far this term, Arsenal have done enough to mask their summer oversight of not signing another left winger and that continued thanks to Madueke’s deflected strike. If they’re to achieve all they desire this term, there must be a push in the winter for a maverick in attack.
Arsenal encountered a stubborn Nottingham Forest. / Carl Recine/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: David Raya—7.7: Arsenal’s No. 1 wasn’t forced into anything extraordinary, with the bulk of his saves routine. Still, Raya didn‘t put a foot wrong.

RB: Ben White—6.8: Arsenal almost exclusively attacked down the right flank in the first half, yet White was unable to offer a source of penetration on the overlap. Fluffed his lines when he did get the opportunity to deliver.
CB: Ezri Konsa—7.5: Liam Delap was a handful, offering plenty of gusto on the counterattack. Konsa coped with him well enough one-on-one, as he continued his impressive start to the season.

CB: Gabriel—7.9: Like his partner, Gabriel was called into action sporadically, and he maintained his focus throughout to deal with Forest’s threat in transition. There were a couple of exemplary defensive sequences.
LB: Riccardo Calafiori—6.9: Arsenal’s attack was again limp, and they couldn’t get their maverick defender in the game at all.

CM: Declan Rice—8.0: Improving as a passer from deep, accessing his captain between the lines on a couple of occasions. Spurned a big chance midway through the second half, but made a big defensive intervention late on.

CM: Bruno Guimarães—7.6: The Brazilian’s best work is yet to arrive from the outset in Arsenal colors. A difference-maker off the bench, but Guimarães is still struggling to put together a complete 90 minutes.
RW: Bukayo Saka—6.9: Arsenal were far too reliant on Saka in the opening 45 minutes, with the winger attracting plenty of attention from the Forest defense as a result.

ftbpro_01m57xdmfz8r.title: Barcelona Suffer Unexpected Setback Ahead of Huge PSG Champions League Clash
ftbpro_01m57xdmfz8r.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 18, 2026Barcelona’s preparations for Tuesday’s clash went array.  / Burak Kara/Getty ImagesThe last thing Barcelona needed before their clash with Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday was a disruption to their training schedule, but that’s exactly what Hansi Flick’s men got thanks to storms along the Catalan coast.

The defending Spanish champions were all set to leave Seville on Saturday evening after their thumping 5–2 victory over Real Betis when the weather played spoiler. The team’s flight back to Barcelona was delayed until the early hours of the morning before the victors were forced to de-plane and return to the hotel for an unexpected extra night away from home.

According to Mundo Deportivo, the club even considered flying straight to Paris instead of trying to get back to Catalonia, but the decision was ultimately taken to fly home on Sunday afternoon. The change of plans forced Flick to alter his preparations for the marquee Champions League clash hurlting over the horizon.

The report claims the German boss had to cancel his full training session for Sunday and instead settle for an indoor light recovery session. The team will not train on the pitch, a massive setback considering its upcoming opponents.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

PSG can rest their starters every weekend. / Xavier Laine/Getty ImagesThe defending European and French champions were already coming into Tuesday’s clash with the upper hand. Not only do PSG get to host Barcelona at the Parc des Princes, but they also come into the match with their superstars well rested.

As has become the norm in Paris, Luis Enrique started a wildly changed XI for the team’s Ligue 1 clash with Strasbourg this weekend. Ousmane Dembélé, Vitinha, Désiré Doué, Achraf Hakimi, Nuno Mendes, Fabián Ruiz and Willian Pacho all started the game on the bench

The same group, minus Hakimi, was also kept out of Enrique’s XI last weekend against Le Mans ahead of the club’s Champions League clash with Manchester City, a game they won 4–2 at the Etihad Stadium.

Enrique has the luxury of managing his best players in a way many managers throughout Europe could only dream of. The best Flick could do was take out his most important stars, like Lamine Yamal and Fermín Lopez, in the second half against Real Betis. Still, a slew of Barcelona players logged the full 90 minutes, including Pedri, Rodri and Pau Cubarsí.

On top of that, the Catalans now must deal with a nightmare travel scenario, disrupted rest and missing out on a full training session in the build-up to their clash with the back-to-back Champions League winners.

Barcelona couldn’t get past PSG last season.  / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFor all of Barcelona’s dominance in Spain over the last two years, they have stumbled when the lights are the brightest in Europe. The Catalans have not made a Champions League final since 2015, let alone lifted the title.

The team has never had a better chance to get over the line in Europe than in 2026–27. Flick’s men look simply unstoppable, winning all 11 of their matches across all competitions so far. Even more impressive is they have found the back of the net four times or more in eight of those matches.

There is a swagger to the reigning Spanish champions that they lacked this time last year when they faced off with PSG. Barcelona lost 2–1 at home in that league phase clash, all while Dembélé was sidelined.

Disrupted training or not, Barcelona will come out ready to make a statement in the French capital on Tuesday. Defeating the defending cup holders would only inject more confidence into a team determined to lift a treble come May.

ftbpro_01m57zkpnv7a.title: Ranking All 20 Premier League Teams’ Performances on Matchday 7
ftbpro_01m57zkpnv7a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:30 PM EDTAlexander Isak (left) and Bruno Fernandes had very different weekends. / Marc Atkins/Getty Images (Isak), Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Fernandes)This was a Premier League weekend of landmarks.

Chelsea kept their first top-flight clean sheet since January; Dejan Kulusevski played his first Tottenham Hotspur match in 526 days; Manchester United had their first “fresh start” since midweek and Enzo Maresca became the first manager to win his opening seven Premier League games at a new club—ever.

It remains to be seen what fragments of history are preserved once Manchester City’s ongoing battle with the Premier League is brought to a merciful conclusion. But amid this legal limbo, the action on the pitch is the only solid ground we have to stand on.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Sunderland are struggling to balance Europe and the Premier League. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesKevin Danso’s 17th-minute red card can only partly be used as mitigation for this desperate implosion. Sunderland were already 1–0 down (thanks in part to a Danso blunder) and could have conceded another by the time the defender was dismissal. “If I have to be honest with you, we are not good,” the Black Cats fullback Nordi Mukiele damningly admitted. “Maybe because we became arrogant, maybe. This is what I think.”

This was a day for Pierre Sage to forget as swiftly as he can. / Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesPierre Sage summed it up pretty succinctly: “My feeling after the game is shame.” It would have been a common sensation in the Crystal Palace locker room.

There were no goals for Hull City. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images“It’s easy to analyze this game,” Hull City boss Sergej Jakirović quietly fumed. “We were out of everything.”The Tigers were dutifully outshot, outrun and out-thought by their under-pressure hosts. Fulham dominated every conceivable aspect of the contest, making a mockery of their 1–0 margin of victory. Jakirović offered a more telling reflection that the scoreline: “It was men against boys.”

This was not a fun one for those from Tyneside. / Stu Forster/Getty ImagesThis was an damning contrast of control and chaos for Newcastle United. While Aston Villa played with the collective calm of a team benefitting from a three-second radio delay, the Magpies were left to thrash around in real time, haphazardly haring about the place, never too near to goal. For a team that is so willfully gung-ho, and spent more than $225 million on forwards in less than two years, Newcastle were left to rely upon the 6'7" merchant of chaos, Dan Burn, as a late striker option.“We were not smart enough,” Matthias Jaissle curtly concluded.

Frank Lampard had an unfamiliar feeling in north London. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesDuring Frank Lampard’s playing days at Chelsea, Tottenham’s home ground was uncharitably known as “Three Point Lane” rather than White Hart Lane, such was the lopsided nature of the London rivalry at the time. Lampard’s Coventry City left the capital with zero points on Monday after failing to capitalize upon a strong start and fast finish to a night of rare euphoria for the hosts.

Harrison Armstrong (left) got his manager’s approval if not the referee’s. / Mike Morese/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIt says everything that David Moyes hailed Harrison Armstrong’s crunching challenge on Josh Acheampong as “the best part” of the goalless first half.Considering the Toffees conceded two cheap goals while taking just two shots in a tame second 45 minutes, that tackle was probably the highlight of Moyes’s afternoon. And it was a foul.

Referee John Brooks decided the game. / Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesThis game swung violently on the tamest act that could conceivably be deemed as violent conduct. Yehor Yarmoliuk’s timid brush of his head toward Jérémy Jacquet warranted the red card which it received, although his battling teammates scarcely deserved the change in momentum they would be unable to control thereafter.
Zian's second goal for Town. 👊 pic.twitter.com/eRB81mBOQI

“The aim was to come here and cause them problems and get points,” Dara O’Shea reflected. Ipswich achieved half of that, bloodying Manchester City’s nose without coming too close to getting that knockout blow.
🎯 "DCL WITH A CLINICAL FINISH!" pic.twitter.com/ScKix8gXjO

It says plenty about where Leeds are at that Daniel Farke could come away from a draw with Manchester United and be justifiably disappointed with a point. Yet, this was not a case of wasted chances or bad luck. Leeds played the occasion rather than the opposition in the first half, timidly prodding at a United side very much there for the taking. As underwhelming as the visitors have been, even this iteration of the Red Devils can’t be given a 45-minute head start and still lose.
Back-to-back #PL goals for @BMbeumo19 ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/tWTDqIXc3i

The bright lights perennially beaming down upon Manchester United seem to be more blinding than most. A much-improved display against Atlético Madrid inspired Lisandro Martínez to give Jason Wilcox a public job review. A performance at Elland Road worthy of little more than a disinterested shrug somehow convinced Michael Carrick to hail a “fresh start.”There was a fresh tactical approach which spelled out United’s place in the current hierarchy. Carrick didn’t deploy a new formation so much as set his players with 11 individual tasks, each one predicated on what their Leeds counterparts were doing at that exact moment. This grand show of inferiority did not tighten a leaky rearguard or improve their porous press but it did at least get a point.
Noni delivers the defining moment 🎯 pic.twitter.com/c8o1UErdlJ

The James Bond villain Auric Goldfinger tells 007: “Once is happenstance. Twice is a coincidence. Three times is enemy action.” Arsenal were their own worst enemies for the third match in succession at the City Ground.Just as in the wins over Leeds and Lille, Mikel Arteta’s champions didn’t bother turning up for the opening hour. Just as in those narrow victories, the team’s substitutes inspired a win which didn’t offer an overwhelming amount of confidence.Arteta has publicly vaunted the positives of this sequence, namely Arsenal’s strength in depth and an ability to “manage the emotional part” of matches. Yet, if fans hope to endure any overriding emotions aside from frustration (followed by relief) it may be an idea to start brightly for once.

Liam Delap had no shortage of spurned chances. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesThis was an 80-minute masterpiece in how to play Arsenal from Nottingham Forest. Martin Ødegaard was put in a jail of red fabric, Bukayo Saka shunted to the fringes and Eberechi Eze bulldozed into a halftime withdrawal. Matz Sels didn’t even have to make a save. Unfortunately, Forest’s goalkeeper would end the game without denying Arsenal’s only shot on target, which was diverted by a cruel double deflection.The only criticism for Oliver Glasner’s side was a familiar one: no clinical composure. It’s now more than eight hours of soccer since Forest last scored a goal in front of their home fans.

ftbpro_01m5817w0q4s.title: USMNT Star Gio Reyna Is Embracing His New York Roots, American Pride at Strasbourg
ftbpro_01m5817w0q4s.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 18, 2026Gio Reyna is making a name for himself in France. / Sathire Kelpa/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesAfter years stuck in purgatory for both club and country, U.S. men’s national team midfielder Gio Reyna is enjoying a major resurgence, buoyed by his summer transfer to Ligue 1 side Strasbourg.

Reyna became used to seeing his name splashed across headlines for all the wrong reasons. Whether it was for recurring injuries, a lack of playing time or a family scandal involving former USMNT manager Gregg Berhalter, the 23-year-old nearly saw his once promising career turned into nothing but a sideshow.

But then came Mauricio Pochettino. The Argentine boss put his faith in Reyna when he had no real reason to do so, controversially handing the former wonderkid a place in his 2026 World Cup roster when the likes of Tanner Tessmann, Diego Luna and Aidan Morris were left home.

Reyna repaid Pochettino’s gamble with a brilliant trivela goal in the team’s tournament opener against Paraguay, before he made four more appearances on home soil. Strasbourg took notice and handed the No. 10 a five-year deal this summer, giving him a much-needed escape route out of Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Gio Reyna is getting back to his best form for both club and country. / Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesIt marked a new challenge for Reyna, who had never played in France before. But the American is embracing his new home and the vibrant culture of his new dressing room.

“In Strasbourg, there are players from everywhere, with African, South American, Scandinavian roots ... So I try to absorb a little bit of everyone every day,” Reyna said in an interview with L’Équipe. “That’s the great strength of football: its ability to bring together people from all these cultures.”

Reyna has shown his strengths on the pitch as well in his new home. He has already found the back of the net twice in seven appearances, doubling his haul from 20 appearances at Mönchengladbach last season. On Saturday, he was the only player on his team to get on the scoresheet in a 3–1 defeat to reigning European and French champions Paris Saint-Germain.
He’s getting more and more comfortable each week in Ligue 1, but so much of his identity is still rooted to his native homeland.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Gio Reyna has become one of Mauricio Pochettino’s favorites.  / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesReyna has been to more places and experienced more cultures than most 23 years olds in the world. He was born in Sunderland, grew up in New York, played at Borussia Dortmund in Germany, had a spell in England with Nottingham Forest, then moved to Mönchengladbach before putting down some roots in northeastern France.

Plus, his mother Danielle, who played soccer at the University of North Carolina before representing the U.S. women’s national team, is of Irish descent. His father Claudio, who retired from the USMNT with 112 caps to his name, is of Argentinian-Portuguese descent.
Reyna touches on how each place has shaped his life and his mindset, but none had a greater impact than New York, where he revealed he feels most at home after living there from ages 5 to 16.

New York City FC is where Gio Reyna got his start. /  Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos/Getty Images)“That’s where I bought my house, where a large part of my family lives, where my wife is from and where I’ll live after my career,” Reyna said of New York. “I’m a true New Yorker! This city is a melting pot, and it’s precisely this multicultural aspect, this diversity of such different people, all very proud to belong to New York—myself included—that makes it the most beautiful place in the world.
“With the mentality of always wanting to keep moving forward, even when things get tougher, while remaining loyal and passionate. The stereotypes you see in movies are true.”

Reyna knows a thing or two about just keep moving forward. After a long road back to the USMNT, the midfielder now finds himself gunning for a starting place in Pochettino’s lineup. He got the nod in all four the team’s friendlies this fall, and collected two assists along the way.

Winning a place in the XI for the 2030 World Cup would be a dream for the player who started his career at New York City FC’s academy. Malik Tillman will be a tough man to beat, but Reyna is looking up to the task these days.

Gio Reyna (left) and Jude Bellingham previously starred for Borussia Dortmund.  / Stuart Franklin/Getty ImagesAs Reyna continues his ascent back to prominence on both the club and international stages, he is always keeping an eye on other talented stars who excel at being a No. 10, especially those he previously crossed paths with.

Reyna singles out Real Madrid maestro Jude Bellingham, who he calls a “great friend.” The two were teammates at Dortmund before the England international left to join Real Madrid in the summer of 2023.
“I’ve always gotten along well with the English. Jude, who can play at a very high level in many different positions, is incredibly inspiring to me,” Reyna said.

Indeed, Bellingham has made a habit of changing his positions for Los Blancos, despite his reluctance. He began his time in a white shirt as a false nine, then went back to being a No. 10, before he was used in a deeper role and even sometimes as a quasi-fullback.

ftbpro_01m5845q7xtg.title: ‘He’s an Alien’—Lionel Messi Stuns His Own Manager With New MLS History
ftbpro_01m5845q7xtg.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben SteinerOct 18, 2026Lionel Messi is favored to win the MLS Golden Boot and MLS MVP Award again this season. / Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesLionel Messi’s magic is inevitable. Less than two weeks after retiring from international duty with Argentina, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner brought back memories of his last standout moments for La Albiceleste on Saturday night in MLS action.

Playing at Mercedes-Benz Stadium for the first time since leading Argentina past England in the 2026 World Cup semifinal, Messi channeled his best to score a brace in a 3–1 win against Atlanta United, securing his side’s first three-game win streak since July.
At the same time, his 25 goals and 15 assists this season made him the first player in MLS history to have 15 assists in three straight seasons.

Yet, the goals weren’t ordinary; they brought flashes of the Messi of old, the player who once dribbled through the world’s best defenders in the greatest European competitions. While Atlanta United’s struggling backline may not measure up to those heights, Messi made them look equally foolish.

On his first goal, he picked up the ball in midfield and quickly dribbled nearly the entire half, before a quick layoff and first-time finish for his 24th goal of the season. Later on, he netted his 25th, further extending his lead atop the MLS Golden Boot standings.
Messi on the break 1v1? Good luck. Leo has his brace. 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/CoI15KzLpw
For new Inter Miami manager Kily Gonzàlez, nothing about it was surprising.

“I can’t believe this guy does what he does at 39 years of age," González said. “And what makes me happiest is that he’s happy ... So if he’s happy, he performs the way he performs; he enjoys ... Every day that I see him, I smile.”

Gonzàlez’s admiration for his new No. 10 has not quite matched the level of previous manager Guillermo Hoyos, who regularly praised Messi despite poor performances. He is more in line with 2025 MLS Cup-winning manager Javier Mascherano, who was rightly impressed but knew the team’s success had to be prioritized over the twilight of a legendary career.
“What do I admire about him? Everything,” added González. “He’s a player who never stops surprising you ... To me, he’s an alien.
“He’s a player who amazes me in every action, during every training session that I watch. And God willing, he’ll keep on amazing us until the day he decides to retire.”

Kily González (left) has Inter Miami on a three-game win streak.  / Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesPicking up a third straight win and allowing just one goal in the last three games, Inter Miami are pulling into form at the right time. Their early-season performances gave them enough cushion to get through a spell of one win in 10 games, and the recent uptick under González could set them up to defend their MLS Cup title.

Messi, meanwhile, is the favorite to claim a third straight MLS MVP Award and a second consecutive MLS Golden Boot as he eyes the postseason with his Herons. Before they can focus too much on that, though, they will look to secure second place in the Eastern Conference through remaining fixtures against Red Bull New York, FC Cincinnati, the New England Revolution and Charlotte FC.
“My idea is for the team to keep on improving,” added González. “Today, we showed our character away from home against an opponent coming off a 3–0 win and in need of a win.”
