ftbpro_01m585hbwc49.title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. Sevilla: Sensational Diomande Erases Vinicius Jr
ftbpro_01m585hbwc49.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 18, 2026Yan Diomande was sensational in place of Vinícius Júnior. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Madrid cruised to a 4–1 victory over Sevilla on Sunday, powered by wondrous goals from Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande.

José Mourinho ripped up his playbook for the La Liga clash, starting Endrick on the right wing, Federico Valverde at right back and Güler alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni in a midfield double pivot. Diomande also got the nod, taking the place of the suspended Vinícius Júnior on the left wing.

The Portuguese boss was cool, calm and collected as he watched his changes pay off. Güler curled home a stunning left-footed strike over Sevilla keeper Odysseas Vlachodimos to give the hosts a 1–0 lead in the 30th minute.

Then Kylian Mbappé left the Bernabéu in awe after he received a backheel pass from Jude Bellingham. The Frenchman did a 360-degree turn to burn his first marker along the edge of the box, drove forward past another red shirt and took one clever touch to round the keeper before finding the back of the net in the 37th minute.

Mbappé made it 3–0 with a successful penalty after the restart, but had to offer apologizes to his backline and goalkeeper for losing possession that allowed Manu Bueno to pull one back for Sevilla. Spirits were soon lifted again when Diomande unleashed a rocket to restore Real Madrid’s three-goal lead.
It was exactly the win Los Blancos needed with El Clásico looming next weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Arda Güler bagged a sensational goal.  / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesThe pressure was on Yan Diomande ahead of Sunday’s clash. The teenager took over Vinícius Jr’s left wing and made sure his team did not miss the No. 7. Diomande was bright from the opening whistle and had an assist to his name by the half-hour mark. His speed and dribbling made a mockery of Sevilla defenders all night long, and he got a well-deserved goal in the dying stages to bring his tally to five goal contributions in his last five appearances.

Arda Güler was a surprise omission from Mourinho’s XI midweek against Roma, but he reminded the manager exactly what he brings to the team in the dying stages of that Champions League comeback. A few days later, the midfielder was back in the lineup and on the scoresheet, curling home one of the best goals you’ll see all season. The Türkiye international must be a permanent starter moving forward.

Vinícius Júnior is serving his four-game La Liga ban. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesVinícius Jr was only a spectator on Sunday, serving the first of his four-game ban for the red card he received last weekend against Villarreal. As if the early months of 2026–27 couldn’t get any worse for the Brazilian, he now was forced to sit and watch Diomande light up the left flank, looking more at home in Mourinho’s system than Vinícius Jr has all season.

Little has gone right for Trent Alexander-Arnold since he left Liverpool for Real Madrid last summer. The England international’s debut campaign was marred by multiple long-term injuries and now he barely sees the pitch in his sophomore season. Already behind Denzel Dumfries in Mourinho’s pecking order, the fullback now must watch from the bench as Federico Valverde steals his minutes as well.
Kylian Mbappé bagged an impressive brace on Sunday. / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Thibaut Courtois—7.4: Rightfully enraged after Mbappé lost the ball inside his own half, opening the door for Bueno to ruin the clean sheet he deserved.

RB: Federico Valverde—7.3: Couldn’t help but smile when Mbappé accidentally blocked his strike destined for goal. Once again looked more comfortable and had a larger impact at right back than he has in midfield. Came up with a huge block in front of Courtois just before the hour-mark.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—7.1: Much more composed with Huijsen back alongside him instead of Rüdiger. Did his job with little fanfare, a welcomed sight after some midweek chaos.
CB: Dean Huijsen—7.5: Found himself at the center of a heated clash between both teams, but escaped with a yellow. Played like he knew Militão was coming to potentially take his spot in the future.
LB: Marc Cucurella—7.2: Linked up well with Diomande and was solid defensively. Still not at his best level, but it was more than enough for a struggling Sevilla side.

DM: Arda Güler—8.6: Bagged his second goal of the season in spectacular fashion. Few people in the world can curl a strike like the Türkiye international, who somehow went unpunished after an errant elbow caught Peque Fernández.
DM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—8.2: Played so much better alongside Güler. Made four tackles, tallied an assist and only misplaced five passes. Still dribbled past too easily, though.
RW: Endrick—6.5: Bright when he got on the ball in space. Danced past defenders down the right flank, but his final ball or shot left something to be desired.

ftbpro_01m587aprh4t.title: The Curious Case of Trent Alexander-Arnold: From Liverpool Hero to Real Madrid Outcast
ftbpro_01m587aprh4t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 20, 2026Trent Alexander-Arnold’s move to Real Madrid has not gone to plan. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesJust a few weeks after Trent Alexander-Arnold said his goodbyes to Liverpool, he was speaking fluent Spanish at his Real Madrid unveiling.

The boy who grew up on Merseyside, spent 20 years in a red shirt, celebrated every major honor at Anfield and was in line to become captain one day, left everything behind to start a new chapter of his career in the Spanish capital.

There was zero regret on Alexander-Arnold’s face as he stood at the podium in front of reporters, cameras and club president Florentino Pérez, speaking a new language and holding up a white No. 12 shirt. Memorable nights at Anfield were nothing more than a distant memory as he dreamed of epic evenings to come at the Bernabéu.

But fast forward two years and there’s been nothing epic about Alexander-Arnold’s time at Real Madrid. In fact, it’s almost like the player, once heralded as the best right back in the world, dropped off the face of the earth.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Trent Alexander-Arnold played a crucial role in Liverpool’s 2019 Champions League triumph. / Matthias Hangst/Getty Images“He is one of these stories that not a lot of clubs can write, but he is someone people will talk about in 20, 30 and 40 years,” former Liverpool manager Jürgen Klopp said of Alexander-Arnold back in 2024.

The German boss had a front row seat to the fullback’s class during his nine-year stint in the Reds’ dugout. Together, Klopp and Alexander-Arnold won eight trophies, including the 2018–19 Champions League title and the 2019–20 Premier League crown.

Along the way, Alexander-Arnold wrote his own legend with every sensational free kick or diagonal ball that showed off his elite playmaking. The defensive holes in his game were accepted so long as his magical right foot made up for his deficiencies.

Alexander-Arnold was soon named a vice-captain, putting him on the fast track to one day skipper his boyhood club. It just made sense for the Scouser who joined Liverpool at age 6 to eventually lead the team in front of fans that absolutely adored him.

Trent Alexander-Arnold won two Premier League titles with Liverpool. / Steven Halliwell/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesExcept it became increasingly obvious Alexander-Arnold had a different vision for his future. Links to Real Madrid always existed, but they became louder and louder as the 2024–25 season raged on, especially with each day the England international did not sign a contract extension.

Liverpool were romping their way to the Premier League title in Arne Slot’s debut campaign, but there were just as many headlines about Alexander-Arnold’s betrayal than there were about the team’s success. After 20 years and 354 appearances, the homegrown talent was really going to leave Anfield just because he couldn’t ignore the allure of Real Madrid?
Steven Gerrard would never. In fact, he didn’t. But Alexander-Arnold chose a new challenge over his loyalty to Liverpool—and he’s been paying the price ever since.

Trent Alexander-Arnold had a debut season to forget. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Madrid rushed to sign Alexander-Arnold before the 2025 Club World Cup. New boss Xabi Alonso wanted to see his new signing in action as early as possible.
At the time, it was simply a disappointment when Alexander-Arnold missed out on the team’s semifinal clash with Paris Saint-Germain due to injury. But in hindsight, it was a rather large omen.

Alexander-Arnold made just five appearances for Real Madrid in 2025–26 before he suffered a serious hamstring injury in September. He missed over a month’s worth of action, only to soon sustain a muscle tear in December that kept him out until February.
All the while, Real Madrid were floundering. The 15-time European champions saw their La Liga lead disappear, lost the Spanish Super Cup final, fired Alonso and then crashed out of the Copa del Rey.

Even once Alexander-Arnold returned to the pitch, spirits were so down in the Spanish capital that even a return to his best form wouldn’t have meant much. By the end of the season, Real Madrid were trophyless and their blockbuster summer signing had managed just 30 appearances and five assists.

As if things couldn’t get more dire for Alexander-Arnold, he was snubbed by England manager Thomas Tuchel for the 2026 World Cup. The 28-year-old was forced to watch the Three Lions mount a third-place finish on the sport’s biggest stage all while he sat at home, no doubt wondering if things would be different had he just stayed at Liverpool.

Trent Alexander-Arnold (left) is not valued by José Mourinho. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesSuch a lackluster debut campaign and missing the World Cup lit a fire under Alexander-Arnold. It was obvious from the early days of preseason he was hoping to change the narrative in his sophomore season, especially now that Dani Carvajal was no longer standing in his way.

Except new manager José Mourinho had other plans. Just when Alexander-Arnold thought he would be the undisputed starter on Real Madrid’s right flank, the Portuguese boss welcomed Denzel Dumfries to the Bernabéu.

ftbpro_01m58a0sw1dz.title: Christian Pulisic Remains a Nonfactor in AC Milan’s Strong Start Under Ruben Amorim
ftbpro_01m58a0sw1dz.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben SteinerOct 18, 2026Christian Pulisic hasn’t been productive for AC Milan this season. / Tiziano Ballabio/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAfter two years of dismal finishes in Serie A, it’s a good time to be part of the AC Milan world, as the club enjoys an unbeaten start through seven games after Sunday’s 3–2 win over Atalanta.

Yet, as much as the club seems on track for an improved finish this season after last year’s fifth-place disappointment or the previous season’s eighth-place finish, it hasn’t been all good for the Americans in the fold—especially Christian Pulisic. The forward has just one goal and an assist in four games after he was benched by new boss Ruben Amorim in the team’s first three matches of the season following an injury this summer.

Against Atalanta, Pulisic started and played 75 minutes but offered little attacking promise, failing to complete a dribble and giving the ball away four times. Meanwhile, his co-attacking midfielder Adrien Rabiot impressed by creating four chances and delivering a dominant creative performance that included a goal and an assist.

The performance, which saw Pulisic as the only attacking player to be subbed out, marked the third straight Serie A game that he has played over 69 minutes, and the third straight game across all competitions without a goal contribution.

In just 264 Serie A minutes this season, the once-superstar ranks in the lowest 20% of players in shots taken, the bottom 62% in xG per 90 minutes and the bottom 34% in successful crosses per 90 minutes.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Christian Pulisic was left off Mauricio Pochettino’s roster for the recent friendlies.  / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesPulisic’s club struggles come at a time when his future role and importance with the U.S. men’s national team is also in doubt.

The 28-year-old was lackluster on home soil this summer and also suffered an injury at the 2026 World Cup, dampening his tournament even further. Pulisic was also not one of the veterans brought into the youth-heavy roster for the September-October international friendlies.

In those four friendly wins, Pulisic’s stock dropped even further, while morale in the group appeared to improve as young players like Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall, Mathis Albert and Adri Mehmeti left their marks. Sebastian Berhalter and Gio Reyna impressed as well, making Pulisic nothing more than an afterthought.

When the November Concacaf Nations League comes around, Pochettino will face a decision on whether to call up Pulisic despite his poor form. If he does, Pulisic will have to show his dedication to the USMNT, given the unglamorous work required in a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie against Haiti.

Yunus Musah has had a resurgent year with AC Milan. / Giuseppe Cottini/AC Milan/Getty ImagesWhile Pulisic’s role with AC Milan and future with the USMNT remain in apparent flux, his fellow USMNT and Milan teammate Yunus Musah is enjoying his most consistent play in two years under Amorim’s tutelage.

Musah also played 75 minutes in the win over Atalanta, but has been a constant presence in Milan’s midfield alongside Croatian legend Luka Modrić. He completed all but one of his 56 passes, had one shot and contributed four defensive actions in a well-rounded effort.
The 23-year-old broke back into Pochettino’s ranks in the recent friendlies and should be a part of those plans moving into the team’s next era, especially as he enjoys regularity at the top level.
The question, though, is whether Pulisic will improve enough to stick alongside him, through to the 2030 World Cup and potentially beyond.

ftbpro_01m58j24c7hr.title: MLS Power Rankings: Inter Miami, Vancouver Whitecaps Surge After Matchday 31
ftbpro_01m58j24c7hr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner1:48 PM EDTLionel Messi (center) is the MLS MVP favorite.  / Matthew Maxey/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images, Andrew Katsampes/ISI Photos/Getty Images, Brett Davis/Getty Images (Messi), Rick Ulreich/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images, Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/GettyThe 2026 MLS regular season is in the final stretch, as teams look to secure spots in the MLS Cup playoffs, while others play out the schedule before looking ahead to the 2027 sprint season.

Matchday 31 brought plenty of thrills, from Yadaly Diaby’s impressive curling strike to push the Vancouver Whitecaps well beyond the chasing pack in the Western Conference, to another stunning performance from Lionel Messi amid Inter Miami’s recent surge.
With just three weeks to go until Decision Day on Nov. 7, nine of the 18 playoff spots have been clinched, with intense races remaining for seeding and the nine spots yet to be filled.
Here, Sports Illustrated dives into how teams stack up after Matchday 31, with most teams still having four games left to play.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

30. CF Montréal29. Sporting Kansas City28. Atlanta United 27. D.C. United26. Austin FC 25. Red Bull New York24. Columbus Crew23. Minnesota United 22. Real Salt Lake 21. San Diego FC 20. Portland Timbers 19. Toronto FC 18. L.A. Galaxy17. FC Cincinnati 16. Colorado Rapids15. LAFC 14. New York City FC 13. Houston Dynamo 12. Seattle Sounders11. Orlando City

Idan Toklomati scored in the 2–2 draw with the Philadelphia Union.  / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCharlotte FC slowed the momentum of the Philadelphia Union this week with a 2–2 draw against the Cavan Sullivan-led squad, and they should have no problem clinching a playoff spot next week against the Portland Timbers. The conversation, though, hasn’t really changed around Charlotte all season. Yes, Allan Saint-Maximin has been a more consistent offensive threat than Wilfried Zaha, but manager Dean Smith’s side still struggles to match the league’s elite teams and could be in for a short playoff run.

Robert Lewandowski will have to score more regularly if Chicago Fire wants to threaten in the playoffs.  / Andrew Katsampes/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesHindsight is always clearer, but would the Chicago Fire be in a better position if they had kept Hugo Cuypers instead of signing Robert Lewandowski? The publicity boost aside, he hasn’t scored in four games, has six goals in 12 and has struggled to match the impact of fellow summer signing Antoine Griezmann in Orlando. After three-straight wins, including a convincing 3–1 win over the Vancouver Whitecaps, the Fire have now lost to the Philadelphia Union and the New England Revolution in back-to-back weeks and will need to turn their form if they hope to maintain a top-four spot in the Eastern Conference.
NEVER COUNT US OUT 🫎 pic.twitter.com/XOYjMPRPgA

Picking up a late 2–2 draw with Texas rivals the Houston Dynamo on Saturday and clinching a playoff spot with a win over the Seattle Sounders on Wednesday made for a good week for FC Dallas. Sam Sarver, though, could be facing disciplinary charges after the forward appeared to throw a beer that had entered the pitch into the stands, nearly hitting supporters behind the goal. Luckily for Dallas, Petar Musa is finding his form again. It’s two goals in the last three games now, and the Croatia international is up to 20 on the season, after a slightly quieter spell. With him leading the attack, Dallas will now look to take over second place in the Western Conference when they face the San Jose Earthquakes in a pivotal fixture next week.

Preston Judd (right) kept up his impressive form. / Thien-An Truong/MLS/Getty ImagesThe San Jose Earthquakes are back in the MLS Cup playoffs and clinched their spot in thrilling fashion, securing a point in a 1–1 draw against Nashville SC, which, combined with Vancouver’s win over Austin, prevented Nashville from lifting the Supporters’ Shield.The result also puts manager Bruce Arena’s men back in the mix for the top spots in the Western Conference. They’re fourth for now, three points behind second-place St. Louis and third-place FC Dallas, but could take a big step forward in next week’s clash with Dallas. While much of its success has come down to a collective effort, the team’s MVP has been Preston Judd. The 27-year-old now has 16 goals with the Quakes and has seemingly become the player so many hoped Timo Werner would be this season.

Matt Polster scored the winning goal against Chicago Fire FC.  / Andrew Katsampes/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesTwo straight wins against FC Cincinnati and the Chicago Fire is quite the way to bounce back after back-to-back 3–0 losses. It wasn’t the most convincing result against the Fire, leaning on an impressive six-save performance from Matt Turner and Matt Polster’s lone goal, but it was enough to keep the Revolution in contention for second in the Eastern Conference. Next week’s clash with the Philadelphia Union will be a challenge on the road, but all eyes are on three weeks from now, when they meet Inter Miami.

Lionel Messi is favored to win the MLS Golden Boot and MLS MVP Award again this season. / Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesInter Miami are back to their best, and Lionel Messi is back to his most impressive influence. This weekend, he scored a brace in a 3–1 win over Atlanta United, bringing his total to 25 goals and making him the first player in MLS history to have three 15-assist seasons in a row. He’s driving Miami’s momentum right now, and the players around him have improved under new manager Kily González. Messi is the be-all-end-all for the team’s potential this season. He’s the favorite for the MLS Golden Boot and MVP once again and is showing no signs of slowing down in Heron’s pink.

Cavan Sullivan couldn't build on his record MLS goal contributions total.  / Isaiah Vazquez/MLS/Getty ImagesEven a youthful superstar like Cavan Sullivan can be stopped. That’s what Charlotte FC did to the Philadelphia Union in a 2–2 draw over the weekend, ending the Union’s eight-game win streak and keeping Sullivan off the scoresheet—even if they needed a fortunate offside flag. The Union’s momentum under interim manager Ryan Richter is still impressive though, even with the draw. It’s 15 games unbeaten now, Milan Iloski is up to 19 goals and in contention for the Golden Boot, and a top-four finish in the Eastern Conference isn’t out of the realm of possibility. The next two matches against the New England Revolution and Nashville SC are pivotal to their top-four hopes.

Tristan Blackmon returned from suspension to help the Whitecaps beat Austin FC.  / Daniel Jefferson/Getty ImagesThe Vancouver Whitecaps needed a stellar strike from Yadaly Diaby to secure a 2–1 win over Austin FC and return to winning ways.Combined with St. Louis’s 3–2 loss to Minnesota United, the Whitecaps extended their lead atop the Western Conference to a four-point buffer and have control of their own destiny heading into the final spell. At the same time, the result gives them a slim, albeit mathematically possible, chance of surpassing Nashville SC in the Supporters’ Shield race. Thomas Müller hasn’t played since Oct. 6, and manager Jesper Sørensen is clearly ensuring his German superstar is ready and healthy for the playoffs. Meanwhile, striker Brian White is out of form. Nevertheless, the Whitecaps seem to be on the uptick at the right time as they approach the end of a six-game road swing.

St. Louis CITY SC were unable to extend their unbeaten run.  / David Berding/Getty ImagesDon’t fret, St. Louis CITY SC fans, things will be alright. While St. Louis said farewell to their 21-game unbeaten run across all competitions by surrendering a 2–0 lead and losing 3–2 to Minnesota United, they went toe-to-toe with the Whitecaps midweek and are still favored to finish in the top four of the Western Conference. The big focus now is on Wednesday, when manager Yoann Damet—who should be in the MLS Coach of the Year conversation—looks to lead his men to a trophy in the US Open Cup final. Unfortunately for them, they won’t be able to lean on summer signing Rafael Navarro, who is cup-tied to the Colorado Rapids.

Hany Mukhtar has Nashville SC on the precipice of the Supporters' Shield.  / Thien-An Truong/MLS/Getty ImagesNashville SC have a confidence level like no other in MLS right now. While they fell short of becoming the first team in league history to win the Supporters’ Shield with four games remaining, the draw with the San Jose Earthquakes merely postponed that coronation. The goal now is to keep everyone healthy for the postseason, especially goalkeeper Brian Schwake, defender Andy Najar and the attacking foursome of Sam Surridge, Hany Mukhtar, Elias Saad and Cristian Espinoza. They’ll likely lift the Shield next week against CF Montréal, the league’s worst team, who will also be coming off of short rest after Wednesday’s Canadian Championship final.

ftbpro_01m59jw9ea0r.title: How Man Utd Would Line Up Under Antonio Conte
ftbpro_01m59jw9ea0r.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott4:00 PM EDTAntonio Conte has been linked with the Man Utd manager job. / Franco Romano/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Conte), Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images (Man Utd badge)The pressure is growing on the shoulders of Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, with reports continuing to link the Red Devils with a handful of alternatives.

Antonio Conte, a league champion with four different clubs and most recently of Napoli, has been tipped to make the surprise switch to the dugout as United search for a more experienced tactician. He won the Premier League with Chelsea in 2016–17 before his spectacular bust-up with those in charge at Tottenham Hotspur, making it pretty tough to predict what United would get from him.
We can, however, have a pretty good guess.
Here’s how United could line up if they end up turning to Conte.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Could Man Utd finally end up with Victor Osimhen? / Burak Kara/Getty ImagesGK: Senne Lammens—Conte often prefers more experience at the back but would appreciate Lammens’s no-nonsense approach. United have no desire to change in goal at the minute, nor should they.

CB: Matthijs de Ligt—There were suggestions that Conte wanted De Ligt during his time as Tottenham Hotspur manager. While the past few seasons have hardly boosted the Dutchman’s reputation, Conte may well still hold enough intrigue to give him another chance.

CB: Harry Maguire—Few players benefited from Ruben Amorim’s three-man defense quite like Maguire, who looked at home at the heart of that back line. Conte would likely lean on the Englishman to re-introduce a tactical system that has a pretty miserable recent history at Old Trafford.

CB: Alessandro Bastoni—We know a new center back is on United’s agenda, and a replacement for the disgruntled Lisandro Martínez seems certain to arrive. United would be aiming incredibly high with Inter’s Bastoni, but the Italian has spoken incredibly highly of Conte in the past and has given credit to the manager for effectively turning him into a superstar.

RM: Michael Kayode—Conte loves an all-action wingback and would expect a complete overhaul in this department. The Premier League-proven Kayode, 22, is the exact sort of profile he would love, with reports suggesting Conte wanted him at Napoli.

CM: Carlos Baleba—Questions would be asked of United’s midfielders ahead of the return of a two-man unit. We’ve not seen much of Baleba in that setup but his all-round approach to the game suggests he could fit in well.

Scott McTominay could follow Conte back to Man Utd. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesCM: Scott McTominay—Written in the stars, is it not? Conte turned McTominay into a star in Naples. His contract now has 18 months left to run, meaning his price tag will be dropping with each passing day to the sort of level at which a return to Old Trafford could be too tempting to ignore.

LM: Lewis Hall—Failure to sign Hall this summer could be a sliding doors moment for United, who now face having to dig deeper into their pockets to land the 22-year-old. Conte would love his energy and final-third impact, and would likely do whatever he could to convince United to finally go all-in.

RW: Bryan Mbeumo—We head into the forward line yet to find a place for Bruno Fernandes. That opportunity is unlikely to come on the right wing, where Mbeumo has proven to be one of United’s most dependable players over the past 18 months.

ST: Victor Osimhen—Conte would want a proven, cold-blooded goalscorer and is likely to take dim views of Benjamin Šeško and Joshua Zirkzee. Osimhen has previously admitted his desire to work under Conte, who wanted the Nigerian to remain at Napoli in 2025. Things could align in Manchester.

LW: Matheus Cunha—Could this be Fernandes’s spot? The Portugal international is hardly renowned for his work out wide and so might well be phased out altogether under Conte, who would likely keep his faith in Cunha on the left wing.
Antonio Conte would demand big changes at Man Utd. / FotMobREAD THE LATEST MAN UTD NEWS, ANALYSIS AND INSIGHT FROM SI FC. feed

ftbpro_01m59kcmprwr.title: Reports: The Real Reason Behind Marcus Rashford’s Man Utd Struggles
ftbpro_01m59kcmprwr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:30 AM EDTMarcus Rashford couldn’t get off the bench for Manchester United against Leeds. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesThere are a number factors behind Marcus Rashford’s wait for ignition during his second spell at Manchester United, but multiple reports have revealed how a secret injury has been holding the winger back.
Rashford left Manchester United through the back door and used the same hidden entrance to make his way back to Old Trafford.

There was no fanfare, no club statement, no corny social media video when the academy graduate returned to his boyhood club. Chiefly because this was a consequence of his failure to secure the permanent move to Barcelona which he had been so openly pining after.
By the time Rashford made his understated second debut at Old Trafford against Ipswich Town, he was the subject of the first chant. Rarely has there been cause for the song to be taken up again.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Rashford is yet to score or assist a goal in United colors this season. That win over Ipswich remains the only victory he has played in. Michael Carrick didn’t even give his former teammate a minute while United forlornly chased after a winner at Elland Road on Sunday.
Even without any buildup, Rashford’s return has still managed to underwhelm. In a way, it’s one of the few impressive aspects of his second United spell.

Marcus Rashford has been nursing a problem for months. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesContext is key when judging a soccer player. Like the flapping webbed feet of a swan hidden beneath the surface, so much goes on out of sight compared to the small proportion of what the world sees.

Unbeknownst to the wider public, Rashford has been nursing a hip injury since the World Cup, per Sky News. The winger continues to receive daily treatment on an ailment that forced him to skip the fall set of internationals. Since those fixtures, Rashford has been afforded just a single minute of Premier League action.
“He had the slight injury where he had to pull out of England, and we’ve managed that a little bit,” Carrick sheepishly admitted.

For a player whose game is chiefly based upon his physical gifts, principally being faster and stronger than so many of the defenders he faces, any injury can be detrimental, be that its actual physical impact or the psychological handicap of not being able to trust your body.

Marcus Rashford needs a goal. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesRashford may still be waiting for his first direct goal contribution, but it’s not as though his teammates have exactly been deconstructing the rest of the division. Bryan Mbeumo is the only United player to score in more than one Premier League match thus far, while Amad Diallo is also waiting for his first moment of meaningful impact.
Benjamin Šeško has been hampered by injury and Matheus Cunha has joined Rashford on the bench in Carrick’s latest tactical reshuffle. The most telling disappointment has been Bruno Fernandes.

Since nabbing a hat trick against newly promoted Ipswich, Fernandes’s only goal or assist has come against a Sabah FK side managed by a former coach at Manchester United Soccer Schools. Without the heartbeat of the side’s attack, everyone else is going to struggle. Fernandes created an unrivaled 136 chances last season, 89 more than any other United player. This term, he has only created three more than Rashford himself.

In the categories where Rashford has to rely upon the production and proficiency of others, there has been a drop-off. His underlying numbers in front of goal have demonstrably dipped compared to his prolific season at Barcelona. However, in the singleminded pursuit of driving toward the net, the direct runner still ranks as one of the most penetrative carriers of the ball in the division. Rashford is a symptom, rather than the cause, of United’s wider malaise.
The ball hasn’t quite fallen for Marcus Rashford. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images“Marcus has done a lot of good things,” Carrick has been keen to stress, with some justification.

Rashford has racked up 17 shots across all competitions, amassing an xG of 1.92. In most other spells, he would be sitting on two goals rather than a big fat zero. Only three Premier League players have taken more shots than Rashford this season without scoring a goal.

“He’s doing some good things, and it’s not quite getting that break, putting himself in good positions and having some good opportunities,” Carrick insisted. “He had the one the other night where maybe he’d feel he could have done better with. He’s in there to make a difference.
“If you keep doing the right things, you get the rewards in the end. As long as he keeps doing that, he’ll be O.K.”

Fortune is an all too overlooked factor in this sport. Rashford won’t always been denied by a stunning reflex save from an inspired goalkeeper and his teammates (probably) won’t continue to squander the chances he’s created.

ftbpro_01m59ppdncb2.title: Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Villarreal: Iraola Manages More Injury Concerns
ftbpro_01m59ppdncb2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack11:00 AM EDTAlexander Isak scored on his return to the Liverpool team. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesWhile Liverpool were undoubtedly aided by Brentford’s indiscipline over the weekend, securing a win at the Gtech Community Stadium is no mean feat.
The Reds fought back from a halftime deficit to triumph in west London, with Alexander Isak scoring on his return to the Liverpool team to snatch all three points.

There’s still a sense the Iraola era is yet to get off the ground, but the Reds have just one blemish on their record across all competitions to date. They’ve been perfect in Europe, too, with back-to-back victories against Atlético Madrid and LASK easing the pressure on upcoming continental bouts.
Iraola’s roster management will come to the fore amid a busy period before the November international break, with more changes to his starting lineup expected when Villarreal come to town.
Here’s how Liverpool could line up in the Champions League on Tuesday evening.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: Alisson—While there’s scope for midweek rotation, there’s no clear need for Liverpool’s starting goalkeeper to come out of the side.

RB: Ronald Araújo—The loanee scored his first goal for the club in the hectic triumph over LASK last week and has enjoyed a strong start to his Liverpool career. He’s an option at the heart of Iraola’s defense, but will likely retain his spot at right back after Jeremie Frimpong‘s injury.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—Jacquet’s importance to the Reds was evident late on in Austria, as his withdrawal led to two concessions.

CB: Virgil van Dijk—The Liverpool skipper has earned more respite than usual at the start of the new season, with Iraola smartly managing the 35-year-old. However, Liverpool’s strongest center back pairing should feature against a dangerous Villarreal side that defeated Napoli last week.
LB: Kostas Tsimikas—Tsimikas is still lingering on Liverpool’s roster. Milos Kerkez’s indifferent start to the new season means the Greek left back is getting chances to impress.

CM: Ryan Gravenberch—Gravenberch’s red card ultimately set the stage for Manchester City’s emphatic victory at Anfield after the international break, but the Dutchman was excellent for an hour. After missing the weekend’s trip to Brentford, he should slot back into Iraola’s engine room.
CM: Alexis Mac Allister—Liverpool desperately need an upsurge from Mac Allister after Dominik Szoboszlai pulled up again at the weekend. Trey Nyoni is waiting in the wings.

RW: Víctor Muñoz—The livewire was at it again in west London, drawing Liverpool level with a good left-footed finish. Muñoz has quickly found his feet and feels an obvious solution to the Reds’ right-hand side dilemma. Cody Gakpo may also be ready for minutes on Tuesday.
AM: Florian Wirtz—We’re likely to see the best of Wirtz in Europe, and his most impressive work of the season so far came in Linz, Austria last week. Don’t let the numbers fool you.

LW: Rio Ngumoha—Bradley Barcola earns some respite after notching his first career hat trick on Matchday 2. Ngumoha has only been used sporadically by Iraola, but he should be a prominent figure during the league phase.

ST: Alexander Isak—While Wirtz has struggled to offer an improvement on his debut season, Isak is starting to look like the striker that Liverpool paid $170 million for two summers ago. He was the match winner on Saturday, taking his goal tally for the season up to five in a little less than 600 minutes played.

ftbpro_01m59rmyymt8.title: ‘Not Too Sure’—Ngumoha Offers Update on Liverpool Future
ftbpro_01m59rmyymt8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:00 AM EDTRio Ngumoha’s contract has 18 months left to run. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesFinding a replacement for Mohamed Salah was an understandable priority for Liverpool this summer.

Víctor Muñoz was signed early in the window but the statement piece came in the form of Bradley Barcola, with a package worth up to $166 million (£123 million) struck shortly before Deadline Day arrived. Andoni Iraola’s squad was, suddenly, overflowing with young, talented wingers all looking to compete for minutes against 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha, widely hailed as one of the English game’s top young prospects.

Liverpool’s search for immediate success in the post-Salah era came with a reluctance to throw Ngumoha into the deep end. It was a huge risk to take considering a crowded pathway was among the reasons Ngumoha, whose Liverpool contract expires in 2028, chose to leave Chelsea in 2024.

Ngumoha has not started in the Premier League since the first day of the season, before Barcola had joined, but it seems as though the teenager is not losing his patience just yet as he confirmed talks over a new contract at Anfield are heading in the right direction.
“To be fair, that is all with my agent now,” he said of the ongoing contract talks.

“I think it is all going well. I am not too sure. I just let my football do the talking at the end of the day. I enjoy playing, and all of that stuff is in the back of my mind really. I just play for the club, and hopefully I can carry on doing well.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Ngumoha (right) is not shying away from competing against Bradley Barcola (left). / Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesHaving already made an impression at Liverpool last season, Ngumoha has a little more credit in the bank compared to your typical youngster. He is already a first-team player simply fighting for minutes, rather than scrapping for the opportunity to get noticed.

That logic is likely playing into Ngumoha’s thinking as he continues to battle against senior, expensive names like Muñoz and Barcola for minutes on either his favored left wing or what appears to be his new home on the right.
“I am enjoying the challenge and to be able to play off both sides is important,” he continued.

“Do I have a favorite position? No, not anymore. I am getting to grips with the right wing now, and I am liking it. It gives me a bit more unpredictability. I have been working hard on the training pitch.

“I went away with England, and I was playing on the right, so I learned a lot there as well. Watching the likes of Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka. I took on board some of the stuff they told me, and it’s really helpful.

“Andoni [Iraola] wants me to take on players in one-v-one duels. He wants me to be threatening. Off the ball, he wants me to help the team however I can. I am enjoying working with him and enjoying improving.

“Whether I start or come off the bench, I have the same mentality. I know the club are just trying to look after me. We have some of the best attackers in the world, so competing for places is not easy.
“It is all about healthy competition and we all just want to make the team win at the end of the day. So whatever minutes we get, we can’t be sulking, we just have to go out and show what we can do.”

Liverpool must continue to find space for Ngumoha. / Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty ImagesLiverpool have got very lucky with Ngumoha’s willingness to commit his future to the club at a time in which he is far from a guaranteed starter. He needs minutes to develop and, despite the competition, clearly feels capable of finding them at Anfield.

English soccer can be a cruel breeding ground for young players, with the demands of the Premier League so high that taking risks on emerging talents is not particularly common. By contrast, Barcola was starting for Lyon at 19 years old and joining Paris Saint-Germain at 20.

Ngumoha will know that is the next step in his career—shaking off the “wonderkid” label and proving himself as a consistent force of the game. He’s only going to get there with minutes, and Liverpool need to find a way to ensure he gets them.

It is easier said than done—one needs only to look at Estêvão’s return of 29 Premier League minutes so far under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea to see the struggles of developing youngsters in a team full of senior stars—but that is the mission facing Iraola this season and further down the line.

Ngumoha may sense an opportunity right now, with Barcola yet to ignite in England, but that patience is not going to last forever. Liverpool would live to regret losing the youngster at this stage of his emerging career.

ftbpro_01m59rvkrxq2.title: Man City Predicted Lineup vs. AEK Athens: Maresca Opts for Widespread Rotation
ftbpro_01m59rvkrxq2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack12:00 PM EDTPhil Foden scored on his return from suspension at the weekend. / Kate McShane/Getty ImagesManchester City are off to a record-breaking start in the Premier League, but there’s work for the Cityzens to do in Europe after they were beaten by Paris Saint-Germain last week.

The absence of jeopardy in the early stages of a Swiss-model Champions League means such blemishes are anything but fatal, with City claiming a top-eight finish in the league phase last term despite dropping points in three of their eight outings.

There’s little room for respite between the first two international breaks of the season for those competing in Europe, and Maresca, having made six changes at the weekend, is bound to rotate heavily again for the visit of AEK Athens, back in this competition for the first time since 2006–07.
Here’s how City could line up for Tuesday’s Champions League encounter.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—The criticism toward Donnarumma appeared harsh after he conceded four against his former club on Matchday 2, and Maresca may be tempted to give reserve goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli a run out here. The Italian will fancy a quiet night between the posts, though.
RB: Matheus Nunes—Some pillars from Saturday’s victory over Ipswich Town should remain, including right back Nunes.
CB: Abdukodir Khusanov—Rúben Dias was among the players Maresca suggested would soon be rested ahead of the Ipswich win, and the Portuguese defender played 90 minutes at the weekend.
CB: Joško Gvardiol—Gvardiol has performed a demanding left back role well so far, but could find himself at the heart of City’s defense on Tuesday.
LB: Rayan Aït-Nouri—Nico O’Reilly’s lingering back issue could keep him out until Saturday’s trip to Aston Villa, so there could be a rare appearance for the maligned Aït-Nouri.
CM: Elliot Anderson—Anderson featured off the bench at the weekend and should return to the team relatively fresh.

CM: Ayyoub Bouaddi—The young midfielder shone on his first Premier League start after offering stability off the bench against PSG. Bouaddi is a frightening talent at just 19 and will hope he gets the chance to build on his standout showings over the past week.

RW: Allan—We haven’t seen all that much of the Brazilian winger, with his sole start to date in the Carabao Cup victory over Norwich City. Some doubt whether Allan is of the requisite level after signing from Palmeiras in the summer.

AM: Rayan Cherki—Cherki’s out-of-possession flaws are unlikely to be ruthlessly exploited by AEK on Tuesday, as they were against the back-to-back European champions. The Frenchman has been up and down in recent outings, but this has the makings of a dominant Cherki outing worthy of a dazzling compilation.

LW: Jérémy Doku—Doku’s apex is as destructive as any winger on the planet, and he’s continuing to mature in the final third. His minutes must be carefully managed after recovering from a calf injury, but he could get an hour under his belt here.

ST: Phil Foden—Maresca will give Erling Haaland a breather after his double on Saturday, and Antoine Semenyo could miss two months injured. City are without a natural Haaland replacement, so it’s time for Foden, who opened the scoring against Ipswich, to reprise his false nine role.

ftbpro_01m59sydsg5s.title: ‘The Worst Run’—Parkinson Staring Down Seven Wrexham Injury Concerns
ftbpro_01m59sydsg5s.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay1:00 PM EDTPhil Parkinson thinks the current injury crisis is the worst he has experienced at Wrexham. / Lee Keuneke/PA Images/Getty ImagesWrexham were without seven injured players when they returned to winning ways against Preston North End at the weekend.

Phil Parkinson’s side secured an important 4-1 victory in the EFL Championship on Saturday, and the Wrexham manager was quick to point out after the match that his team had done so despite missing so many players.

“I am very confident we will have a strong season,” he said after the Preston win. “We’ve had, and it is good to mention the injuries when you’ve had a win, probably the worst run of injuries since I’ve been at the club. A lot of quality has come out of the team. You go to any team in the Championship and take seven or eight quality players out of the team, the level of performance is going to dip.”
Wrexham will hope to welcome some players back over the coming weeks as they look to climb the league table. Here’s the latest news on their injured players and their potential return dates.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Max Cleworth was playing very well before his injury setback. / Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesPotential return: Saturday, Nov. 21, vs. Lincoln CityCleworth has missed five matches since suffering a hamstring injury in the home draw with Burnley. The Wrexham academy graduate was initially ruled out for eight weeks, meaning he is not expected to be available again until next month. He could return during the November international break and be ready for the trip to face Lincoln City.

George Thomason hasn’t featured since August. / Richard Sellers/PA Images/Getty ImagesPotential return: Tuesday, Nov. 3, vs. MiddlesbroughThomason has missed nine matches since picking up a thigh injury in the closing stages of Wrexham’s draw with Watford in their second match of the season. He was ruled out for 10 weeks, meaning he could return just before the next international break. Parkinson won’t rush him back, but Thomason could be available to face either Middlesbrough or Wolves early next month.

Liberato Cacace has made just 13 competitive appearances for Wrexham. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesPotential return: UnknownCacace has not played a competitive match all season, with Parkinson even admitting that the circumstances surrounding his latest setback remain something of a “mystery.” The left wingback has made just 13 appearances since joining Wrexham a year ago and recently visited a specialist in London in an attempt to determine the cause of his ongoing fitness problems. At this stage, it is impossible to predict when he might return.

Seb Revan hopes to leave Wrexham on loan in the January transfer window. / Steve Christo/Corbis/Getty ImagesPotential return: January 2027Revan would have left Wrexham in the summer had he been fit, but he remains sidelined by a serious hamstring injury suffered while on loan at Burton Albion in February. Parkinson recently revealed that he hopes Revan will be fit enough to go out on loan again during the January transfer window.

Ben Sheaf only returned for one match before he suffered another injury setback. / Wrexham AFCPotential return: Saturday, Oct. 24, vs. Blackburn RoversSheaf has missed the last three matches after suffering a groin injury in training during the October international break. Parkinson insisted the injury was not “serious,” and Sheaf is not expected to be sidelined for long. He could return to action this month.

Nathan Broadhead is yet to score this season. / Andrew Lewis/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesPotential return: Saturday, Dec. 5, vs. Norwich CityBroadhead has missed four matches after suffering a thigh strain in training before the fall international break. The injury is understood to be serious, and he is not expected to return until December at the earliest. The Wales international might not play again this calendar year.

Josh Windass was seen in a protective boot at the weekend. / Cody Froggatt/PA Images/Getty ImagesPotential return: Friday, Oct. 30, vs. Sheffield UnitedWindass suffered an ankle injury in the opening stages of Wrexham’s recent draw with Derby County and has missed the subsequent two matches. The 32-year-old was seen wearing a protective boot after the weekend win over Preston North End. He won’t be rushed back into action, but the injury is not as serious as initially feared.

ftbpro_01m59vv87ypm.title: Champions League Predictions 10/20: PSG Host Barcelona; Man City, Liverpool in Action
ftbpro_01m59vv87ypm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack10:00 PM EDTParis Saint-Germain headline Tuesday’s fixtures. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesWe’re not yet at table-taking-shape territory, but the wheat will slowly start to separate itself from the chaff after the Champions League’s third matchday.

The upcoming slate has a lot to live up to after last week’s goal-fest, as the back-to-back champions sparkled in Manchester and Real Madrid triumphed in a manner that only the 15-time winners seemingly can.

A record 78 goals were scored on Matchday 2 to take the season tally up to 147 from 36 matches—an average of 4.08 goals per game. The scoring boom is taking us back to a bygone era and the formative years of the European Cup, with teams perhaps capitalizing on the lack of jeopardy facilitated by the format switch of three years ago.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Tuesday’s Matchday 3 fixtures will pan out.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Fenerbahçe were subject to a West Midlands beatdown on Matchday 2, as Aston Villa enjoyed a record-breaking victory over the Turkish side. Fener are celebrating their first Champions League appearance since 2008–09, seemingly boasting a roster capable of at least competing with Europe’s sub-elite.

A draw with Roma to kickstart the league phase was by no means a disaster, and they’ve got a great chance to notch their first win in this competition since beating Chelsea in the first leg of their round of 16 tie 18 years ago.

Czech giants Slavia Prague were one of the poorest league phase performers last season, and 2026–27 has started with a dramatic collapse against Lens and a defeat at debutants Sabah. There’s unlikely to be much of an improvement on their three-point showing from last term.
Fresh off securing their maiden Champions League victory, debutants Sabah welcome a perennial participant to Baku’s Olympic Stadium.

One-time winners Borussia Dortmund were surprise finalists just three seasons ago, and are seemingly always there or thereabouts in Europe no matter the extent of their indifference on the domestic front.

BVB enter Tuesday’s game without a win in three, having succumbed in the Arctic last week. They were merely the latest to fall to Kjetil Knutsen’s Bodø/Glimt, with their Bundesliga draws to Werder Bremen and Union Berlin on either side raising more concerns at Signal Iduna Park.
Niko Kovač is desperate for three points here, but the spritely and excited hosts are unlikely to roll over.
Bradley Barcola scored his first career hat trick in Liverpool’s Matchday 2 win over LASK. / Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesPrediction: Liverpool 2–0 Villarreal
Liverpool are continuing to find their feet at the start of Andoni Iraola’s reign, with the results perhaps more impressive than their level of performance through the first two months of the season.

The Reds aren’t yet pressing like an Iraola-led outfit, with the Spaniard needing more time to hone his team into a juggernaut without the ball. As a result, Liverpool are still relatively easy to play against, and Brentford had their way with them at the weekend until they were reduced to 10 men.

That triumph followed their six-goal outing in Linz, as Bradley Barcola scored his first senior career hat trick. Liverpool are more likely to see the best from their rookie and sophomore stars in Europe as opposed to the Premier League for now, although Villarreal did claim a long-awaited Champions League triumph last week.
Iñigo Pérez faces up against his former boss on the Anfield touchline, as these two teams meet for the first time since the 2021–22 semifinals.
Man City need to respond from last week’s defeat. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesPrediction: Man City 3–0 AEK Athens
Manchester City extended their winning run to start the Premier League season to seven games at the weekend, meaning they’re now just two wins adrift of Chelsea’s record.

However, their perfect start to the new campaign was compromised by the back-to-back champions at Etihad Stadium on Matchday 2. Paris Saint-Germain showcased their finest work in Manchester last Wednesday, racing into a 3–0 halftime lead that they threatened to relinquish,

ftbpro_01m5a1rpznv8.title: Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. PSG: Raphinha Returns for Blockbuster Clash
ftbpro_01m5a1rpznv8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:00 PM EDTRaphinha was back in action for the outstanding La Liga leaders at the weekend. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesTeams may well have to accept that there is simply no way of taming Hansi Flick’s Barcelona.

Some may have projected stagnation heading into year three of the German’s tenure after two convincing La Liga triumphs. However, instead of flirting with a dip, Barça have merely doubled down on their dominance.

They’re perfect after 11 games across all competitions, and their 5–2 win over Real Betis on Saturday saw Flick’s side equal a near-60-year record. Real Madrid had been the only team in the competition’s history to win their opening nine outings of a La Liga season, doing so in 1968–69.

Barcelona visited ‘Hell’ in Istanbul last week, and have been tested by the likes of Athletic Club and Betis. However, the ultimate challenge awaits this team ahead of El Clásico, which may appear rather tame in comparison. Paris Saint-Germain are the gold standard of European soccer, having retained their Champions League crown last season, and the rest of the continent received an ominous warning in Manchester on Matchday 2 of the league phase.
The soccer world is in an anctipitatory mood as Barça locks horns with Luis Enrique’s side. Here’s the team Flick could pick in the French capital.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Joan García—Clean sheets are hard to come by for Barcelona’s No. 1, and the Spaniard is expected to be busy in the French capital on Tuesday. PSG aren’t merely an outstanding collective force, they’re also remarkably efficient in front of goal.

RB: João Cancelo—Flick is navigating an injury crisis at full back for this fixture, but the German does have options in reserve. Cancelo, seemingly more comfortable on the left, is expected to start at right back. He scored a wonderful goal in Istanbul last week.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—Tuttosport’s next Golden Boy has his work cut out in Paris, given that Enrique’s telepathic and positionless unit tends to bring out the worst in opposing defenders.

CB: Gerard Martín—There will be concerns about Martín alongside Cubarsí given the level of opposition. The academy graduate is fine, but it’s in these sorts of fixtures that Barça’s summer oversight could hurt them.
LB: Xavi Espart—Flick has a lot of trust in the youngster, and there’s no underplaying the size of the task at Espart’s disposal. He’ll be asked to contain one of PSG’s electric attackers one-on-one.

CM: Rodri—Rodri said Barça must “adjust” to reach their “full potential” ahead of Tuesday’s match, and there have been reports of the midfielder potentially being utilized in defense. However, Flick is unlikely to shift the World Cup Golden Ball winner from his engine room on such an occasion.
CM: Pedri—Pedri is finding his groove alongside Rodri, and the midfield battle will be absolutely fascinating.

RW: Lamine Yamal—Gabriel Jesus’s reaction was perfect. Hands firmly behind his head in disbelief. Lamine Yamal had just opened the scoring with an otherworldly strike, and he’ll certainly be emboldened by Nuno Mendes’s absence for PSG in this one.

AM: Fermín López—It’s a 50–50 between López and Dani Olmo, who scored off the bench at the weekend. Olmo has a knack for the big occasion, but López is almost always in the right place at the right time, and he’s the man to exploit PSG’s poor midfield recovery running.

LW: Anthony Gordon—The Englishman is already adored in Catalonia, and he’s scored in his five previous starts for club and country. Gordon recorded double figures in Champions League goals last season, and he opened his account against Galatasaray last time out.
ST: Raphinha—While Gabriel Jesus is undoubtedly serviceable, Raphinha will surely lead Barcelona’s attack after returning from injury at the weekend.

ftbpro_01m5a2ycxrv6.title: Phil Parkinson’s Wrexham Revival Could Hinge on Return of Unsung Hero
ftbpro_01m5a2ycxrv6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay2:00 PM EDTWrexham had better control of the match against Preston North End. / Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty ImagesIt would be far too simplistic to put Wrexham’s thumping weekend win over Preston North End down to one player, but it is no coincidence that they improved significantly with one man’s return to the starting lineup.

Having been torn apart in midfield by both Derby County and West Bromwich Albion since returning to action, Wrexham were much improved against Preston, taking control of a match that ultimately delivered three comfortable points.

Phil Parkinson made four changes to his side and switched tactics, opting for two strikers instead of one. The change certainly gave the Red Dragons more firepower up front, but it was the return of Matty James at the base of midfield that really turned the game in their favor.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Wrexham have not lost a match Matty James has started in the league this season. / Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesThe stats speak for themselves. Wrexham are unbeaten in the five league matches James has started this season, with all three defeats coming when he was absent from the starting lineup.

Wrexham have a 40% win rate when James starts in defensive midfield, compared with just 16.66% when they are without the experienced midfielder. His impact is not limited to the final results, either.

The Red Dragons have conceded just three goals in the five matches James has started this season, an average of 0.6 per game. In contrast, they have conceded 13 goals in the six matches he hasn’t started, although those numbers are somewhat skewed by the 6–0 thrashing against West Ham. That was another game in which his experience and expertise were sorely missed in midfield.

Even beyond the small sample size of 11 league matches this season, James’s positive impact on Wrexham’s performances is clear. He also started the 1–0 Carabao Cup defeat to Middlesbrough, but Parkinson insisted he was treating that match as an additional preseason friendly.

Wrexham recorded a 45.83% win rate when James started in the Championship last season, compared with 36.36% when he was absent from the starting lineup. Even among the six defeats in which he started, one came against Millwall, when he was forced off with an injury after just 20 minutes, with the score still goalless.

Ben Whiteman has only been at the Racecourse Ground for a matter of months, but he already knows how good his midfield teammate is. The pair started together against Preston at the weekend, and although Whiteman scored once and provided two assists against his former club, it was James who received the postmatch praise.

“I think with Matty, you know what he is going to do and where he is going to be,” Whiteman said. “Matty James is going to stay in the middle of the pitch, he’s going to block the transitions, and I think that is where we have been poor. We’re right down there in terms of number of chances conceded in transition. He is a massive bonus when he plays in terms of his leadership. His quality on the ball, I don’t think it really gets said enough. The timing of the pass, when to go forward, when to recycle. He’s right up there.”

Matty James has earned the full trust of manager Phil Parkinson. / Terence Lewis/IIcon Sportswire/Getty ImagesJames leads not only through his experience on the pitch but also through the standards he sets off it. He played through the pain barrier and received an injection to make himself available against Preston despite completing only half a training session. Toward the end of last season, he even wore soccer cleats two sizes too big, borrowed from teammate Josh Windass, to ensure a swollen, broken toe wouldn’t keep him on the sidelines.
That old-school approach and dogged determination have made James a key part of Parkinson’s squad, with the Wrexham manager full of praise for his experienced midfield general.

“Matty coming back in secured the center of the pitch for us brilliantly,” Parkinson said after the weekend win. “Special mention for Matty because he’s had an injection; he’s only really trained half the session Thursday, but there was never a doubt in Matty’s mind that he was ready to put himself up to play.

“All the chats we have when we meet players, there’s got to be certain qualities in your character to come and play for Wrexham because everyone wants to beat us,” he added. “We’re a target; there’s an expectation. There’s noise at every club when you lose but it’s intensified here and you need people with mentality and strength of character, and Matty has got that in abundance.

“Not only that, he’s got real nous on the football pitch and he showed that in his performance. For the last 10 days, he’s had half, three-quarters of a training session, but you wouldn’t have really noticed that on the pitch.
“Now we’ve got a week with him; hopefully he’ll wake up tomorrow, and his back will be fine, and we’ve got a good week with him on the training pitch.”
If James is fit enough to start against Blackburn Rovers this weekend, Wrexham will fancy their chances of securing another three points.

ftbpro_01m5a3knqxqs.title: USWNT Stock Up, Stock Down: Trinity Byars’s Debut Can’t Be Far Off Now
ftbpro_01m5a3knqxqs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Theo Lloyd-Hughes1:30 PM EDTSan Diego Wave forward Trinity Byars (right) celebrated her 11th goal of the season.   / Matt Kelley/NWSL/Getty ImagesWelcome back to your weekly feature from Sports Illustrated that analyzes the women’s soccer weekend from a U.S. women’s national team perspective.

Last week, the USWNT players returned to their clubs licking their wounds after going winless across two friendlies with Spain. But disappointment can provoke a response. Lessons were certainly learned during the international break. There is work to be done for Emma Hayes and her team, and that means opportunities for hopeful players.

Several will be vying for a roster spot when the USWNT regroups for the World Cup qualifiers, which get underway on November 27. With league action back, let’s look at which American players saw their stocks rise and fall this past weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
SD’s Trinity Byars chips it and IT’S IN 💪 pic.twitter.com/z0VVpLEmEj

Sometimes, it is the work we don’t see that can show a player’s growth. After receiving her first-ever senior USWNT call-up this month, Trinity Byars did not lose any confidence after not making her international debut against Spain. The San Diego Wave forward was at her clinical best in their 2–1 win over the NC Courage on Saturday.

Byars is turning the one-on-one with the goalkeeper on a fast break into her special move. This was her 11th goal of the season in her 13th start, and it may be one of her most technical. The timing and execution of the lob was exquisite. She is counting the seconds in her head, keeping tabs on both the chasing defender and the charging goalkeeper. Composure and superb shot selection combined. One touch, goal.

Sophia Wilson remains the first-choice center forward for the USWNT, but Byars is rising through the ranks as a likely deputy or change-of-pace option off the bench. Even if, for now, she has yet to put a single USWNT cap to her name.
Taylor Suarez with the equalizer!From being down by two, to all square 🤩 pic.twitter.com/vLX7lwWxZq

A double-assist game for Angel City’s Gisele Thompson will have many moving the wide player up the depth chart on the USWNT and even into a starting role. The 20-year-old was excellent on the right wing for Angel City in their 3–2 win over the Denver Summit on Saturday. Her star just continues to rise and rise.
Thompson showcased her playmaking ability, as she set up Angel City’s equalizer in the 39th minute before creating the winning goal just four minutes later.

The first assist was a simple weighted pass into the right area to set Taylor Suarez off and running toward goal. The second assist was all about patience, as Thompson was part of a slick team move that shifted the ball left and right before teeing up Ally Sentnor from outside the box.

Even in the one Angel City goal that she didn’t assist, Thompson had a crucial forward pass to push the ball out of the defense and into the attack. To top it all off, she finished with a 92% pass completion.
Bay is right back in it 👊Caroline Conti roofs Karlie Lema's cross and Bay are level! pic.twitter.com/ooHXNB9EG6

From one winger with two assists this weekend, to another. Although Karlie Lema is a little bit of a way off the senior USWNT right now, her brilliant play in Bay FC’s 2–2 against the Portland Thorns will have caught some eyes.

Lema is a stretch player who keeps opposing defenders honest by not allowing too much space in behind. If she does get room to run, then she’s lethal in transition. These attributes were on display as Lema skillfully dribbled beyond onrushing Portland goalkeeper McKenzie Arnold, kept the ball in bounds and slid the ball across for an easy open-goal finish for Caroline Conti. Her second assist of the day, to put Bay up 2–1, was more about neat one-touch combination play with teammate Kennedy Fuller.

Bay’s most threatening outlet on the day, Lema finished the game with three chances created, two of those big chances, as well as a couple of shots of her own. A rare flawless outing, Lema had a 100% pass completion on 18 passes.
THE THORNS TIE IT 👀Caiya Hanks slots home her second of the season to tie it late!#NWSL pic.twitter.com/xRw1iYZsug

Bay FC goalkeeper Jordan Silkowitz linked up with the USWNT last week for the friendlies against Spain but didn’t see the field. After a brilliant first two-thirds of the 2026 season, her form is starting to drop off, and this weekend’s 2–2 draw with the Portland Thorns was one of her most frustrating games yet.

In the dying moments, with Bay leading 2–1, Silkowitz was beaten at her near post by a low, drilled shot from Caiya Hanks. The post-shot expected goals (PSxG) of Hanks’s equalizer was just 0.38. Morgan Weaver's opening goal was a belter from outside the box that, despite being further from goal, was a more difficult save for Silkowitz, with Opta stats showing 0.62 PSxG. In the end, Bay couldn’t hold on for the win, with Silkowitz making three saves from five total shots.

ftbpro_01m5a4ntt6hf.title: Iraola Reveals Liverpool Injury Blow With Szoboszlai Clarification
ftbpro_01m5a4ntt6hf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:30 AM EDTAndoni Iraola has some selection headaches to deal with. / Kate McShane/Getty ImagesAndoni Iraola downplayed the severity of Dominik Szoboszlai’s latest setback although warned that Jeremie Frimpong will be sidelined until the other side of the November international break.

Despite coming through the daunting ordeal of traveling to Brentford, Iraola was not entirely enthused in his postmatch press conference. The victorious Liverpool boss called it a “very expensive” victory, pointing toward the two players who had been forced off with muscular issues.

Szoboszlai was the most notable, dropping to the turf after half an hour with a recurrence of the thigh injury which had forced him to miss Liverpool’s previous two fixtures. Iraola had fretted that his star midfielder would be sidelined “for some time” but there was more optimism in his subsequent update in the week.

While a return for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Villarreal was out of the question, the Basque boss assured fans that their No. 8 had not sustained any more damage. “It’s not a new injury, it’s in the same place as last week, he has not worsened the injury, but we have to be a bit more patient until he recovers fully,” Iraola warned.
“It is not like we now have to wait a lot of time to come back.”

Frimpong’s recovery, however, will take some time. The fullback lasted just six minutes against Brentford, hobbling off shortly after his halftime introduction having initially been rested following the midweek trip to Austria. “Jeremie has a new muscle injury and we will have to wait until he recovers,” Iraola reflected. “It’s going to be difficult I think before the international break.”

Florian Wirtz is Liverpool’s marathon man. / Jasmin Walter/UEFA/Getty ImagesInjuries aside, Iraola has warned that he will have to use the full width and breadth of his roster during Liverpool’s pile of key fixtures over the coming weeks. The manager did well to win convincingly against LASK while rotating heavily and has teased a similar set of changes for the visit of Villarreal.
“I am thinking of putting the best starting XI that I can against Villarreal,” he told assembled media. “But maybe it is not the one that you are thinking, because some players are not fresh enough.
“Probably it is better if someone is more fresh to start but I am analyzing the game, how can I put a good starting XI and think in the second half, how can we affect [the game] with the changes?”
Data via Simon Brundish. The Fatigue Index is on a scale of 0–100, anything above 65 is in the ‘red zone.’

Using a combination of nine different statistics based upon what has historically preceded previous injuries, combined with the track record of the individual in question, Simon Brundish has created a ‘Fatigue Index’ which can offer a loose prediction of which players are at risk of breaking down.

Liverpool’s unusually susceptible goalkeeper Alisson could be rested in favor of Giorgi Mamardashvili in midweek to prevent yet another hamstring injury, while the tireless Florian Wirtz could be at risk of running himself into the ground. Putting his questionable chance creation to one side, there is no debate in his running statistics: Wirtz has covered six miles more than anyone else at the club.

The German playmaker boasted the most overworked odometer once again against Brentford, which was a draining contest for all involved. “I think it was the most demanding game in terms of the running stats that we have played, because Brentford demand this,” Iraola moaned. “It is important that every one that starts tomorrow feels ready to go and 100%.”
