ftbpro_01m5a4w282x5.title: ‘I’ve Asked Everyone’—Jose Mourinho Issues Strange Challenge Over Arda Guler Incident
ftbpro_01m5a4w282x5.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer10:00 AM EDTArda Güler avoided a potential red card and then scored the opening goal. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesReal Madrid is often the club complaining about referees and perceived injustices.

Only last month, Los Blancos blamed a referee for losing against city rivals Atlético. The club’s own match report was titled, “A dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby,” amid cries for two Atlético players to be sent off in the first half alone.
Real Madrid were also unhappy last weekend when Vinícius Júnior was sent off for a hair pull.

Towards the end of last season, the referees had hit back, filing formal complaints against Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez and Real Madrid TV in an effort to “combat any manifestation of violence, harassment or discrediting of refereeing.”
Hitting back at Real Madrid over the topic was even the source of a shocking Javier Tebas statement last week that prompted a furious response from the club.
It means plenty of irony now that it seems like the shoe is on the other foot and Real Madrid are accused of benefiting from a controversial decision in Sunday’s 4–1 win over Sevilla.

Sevilla wanted to see Arda Güler shown a red card in the first half, when the match was still tied at 0–0. The incident in question involved Güler and Sevilla midfielder Peque Fernández, with the latter appearing to pull back at the former during a passage of play.
Güler’s response seemed to be an attempt to free himself with the use of arm. Sevilla believe that was an act of violent conduct and should have resulted in his ejection.

Sevilla manager Luis García wanted to know why the VAR official did not intervene, going so far as to hint at some sort of conspiracy. “Why didn’t they call the VAR officials?” he fumed postgame. “Maybe so they don’t get nine points [behind Barcelona] ahead of the Clásico.”
García admitted Real Madrid deserved to win the 11 vs. 11 match that took place, but insists Sevilla were “deprived” of playing another with a “man advantage from the 25th minute.”

The manager continued: “At half time, Peque was telling me that [Güler] had hit him. It’s a red card. We need to talk to the VAR official more than the referee. The referee might not see it; he doesn’t have eyes in the back of his head. And even more so when Real Madrid, Atlético Madrid or Barcelona are playing, when there are more cameras.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Sevilla players wanted to see a punishment. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIt may have been cameras, or a lack of adequate cameras angles, that was the issue. The television replays captured the incident, but only from a distance and not in the detail required to determine whether intervention and punishment would be appropriate.

The radio station Cadena SER cited a source from Spain’s Technical Committee of Referees that explained: “VAR has the same cameras as the television broadcast. If there was no intervention, it’s because there is no clear and unquestionable evidence of violent conduct.”

Iturralde González, a refereeing expert for AS and Cadena SER, said the lack of available evidence to assess the incident was “pathetic” in a competition that has ambitions to be viewed as the best domestic league in the world. “It seems there was something there, but there wasn’t a clear replay to determine it. I see [Güler] throw his arm, but you can’t see it hit [Peque] in the face because the images are so poor.

“It’s pathetic … if we’re the best league in the world, this level of replay quality shouldn’t be the case. To send off a player, there can’t be any doubt, and with the available footage, you can’t say whether there was an elbow or not.”

José Mourinho claims to have seen no evidence it was a red card. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesThe lack of definitive proof is what José Mourinho also pointed to when the topic was unsurprisingly raised in his postgame interaction with reporters.
“Nobody has been able to show me what they say happened,” he shrugged.
“I don’t have a single image. I’ve asked everyone for images, including my staff, and I haven’t been able to find any footage of the things they’re talking about that have upset Luis.

“I’m telling you honestly that if something happens that has benefited us, I won’t have any problem coming forward and saying so. But I think the opposite is going to happen much more often because that's the natural tendency.

ftbpro_01m5a59t6mm6.title: Liverpool vs. Villarreal: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5a59t6mm6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 19, 2026Liverpool take on Villarreal for the first time since they met in the 2021–22 Champions League semifinals. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Liverpool), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Villarreal)Liverpool head into Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Villarreal off the back of two consecutive wins, as Andoni Iraola locks horns with a familiar face on the Anfield touchline.

The Yellow Submarine are now led by Iraola’s former assistant, Iñigo Pérez, who eventually took on the Rayo Vallecano job after Iraola left the Madrid club for Bournemouth in 2023, having initially tried to follow his boss to the English south coast only to be refused a work permit.

Pérez guided Rayo to the Conference League final last season, and was appointed as Marcelino’s successor at Villarreal in June. While the Yellow Submarine currently sit mid-table in La Liga, Pérez took the club to a first Champions League victory since 2022 last week, beating Napoli 3–1.

Six-time European champions Liverpool have started the league phase with a pair of wins, including a 2–1 triumph over Atlético Madrid at Anfield on Matchday 1. They subsequently put LASK to the sword in a 6–3 rout, and are in a bouyant mood after coming from behind to defeat Brentford at the weekend.
The Reds remain imperfect at the start of Iraola’s reign, but the results have been mostly impressive.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Alexander Isak scored on his return to the Liverpool team at the weekend. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesThis is a special occasion for both managers, with the long-time friends facing up against one another for the very first time.

“We’ve been through a lot of things together, so it is also a privilege for me to face him in a Champions League game,” Iraola said on Monday. He admitted Tuesday’s encounter will be a “little bit strange” given their close relationship, and noted that Villarreal’s boss “knows everything” about him.

Still, it will take a big effort from the visitors to secure victory on Merseyside. Iraola’s Liverpool remain a work in progress, but rarely do they come unstuck at Anfield on Champions League nights.
The Reds last faced off against Villarreal in the 2021–22 semifinals, claiming a 5–2 victory over two legs before falling to a Thibaut Courtois-inspired Real Madrid in the final.
Iraola confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong will miss Tuesday’s clash after both picked up injuries in Saturday’s comeback victory.

While Frimpong has a “new injury,” Iraola suggested that Szoboszlai’s hamstring issue is still lingering. "We will have to be a little bit more patient until he recovers fully,” the Liverpool boss said.

In his absence, Ryan Gravenberch is expected to slot back into midfield after serving a one-match suspension at the weekend. The Dutchman was excellent before receving his second yellow card on the hour mark against Man City.
While Iraola is likely to rotate, with Bradley Barcola among the players potentially earning respite, Alexander Isak is set to lead Liverpool’s line under the lights.
The Reds are otherwise dealing with long-term absentees, with Hugo Ekitiké, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley still sidelined for the hosts.
Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Villarreal (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araújo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Mac Allister; Muñoz, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Isak.
New manager Pérez hasn’t yet deviated from predecessor Marcelino’s preferred 4-4-2, and the Anfield faithful will likely be treated to two banks of four from the visitors on Tuesday.

Villarreal are without Canada winger Tajon Buchanan due to a hamstring injury, while Nicolas Pépé, who recorded 18 La Liga goal contributions this season, is sidelined after undergoing eye surgery. Without him, Pérez will turn to Georgian international Georges Mikautadze and veteran forward Gerard Moreno to lead the Yellow Submarine’s attack.

Nathan Saliba, the player involved in Vinícius Júnior’s hair-pulling incident, is expected to start in midfield, while Portuguese international Renato Veiga will man Villarreal’s defense on Merseyside.
Villarreal Predicted Lineup vs. Liverpool (4-4-2): Júnior; Mouriño, Navarro, Veiga, Romero; Saliba, Comesaña, Gueye, Moleiro; Moreno, Mikautadze.

ftbpro_01m5a9rz1e6p.title: How Man City Could Face ‘Swingeing’ Points Deduction Sooner Than Expected
ftbpro_01m5a9rz1e6p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom1:30 PM EDTErling Haaland may be staring down at least one season in the Championship. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesThe Premier League are leading the charge for Manchester City’s punishment to be announced before the verdict of their appeal, a new report has surprisingly claimed.

City, lest anyone forget, were found guilty by an independent commission of breaking more than 100 Premier League regulations, including all those relating to inaccurate reporting of their finances. As England’s top flight emphatically put it, City’s success between 2009 and 2018 was built upon “sham contracts,” “sham agreements” and “sham commercial deals.”

These charges were first leveled at City in February 2023 and the modern Premier League giants have forcefully pleaded their innocence throughout the process. Even in the wake of this official verdict—which the club described as an “opinion” thanks to a “Premier League conspiracy theory”—City are continuing to fight for their reputation.

An appeal has been lodged based upon the heavily cited “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence.” A large array of Abu Dhabi government documents is thought to be the basis of this argument, which claims that the “artificially inflated” revenue streams were swollen by funding from the state, rather than City’s owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan (who also happens to be vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, which counts Abu Dhabi as its capital).

This process is ongoing. Under new Premier League rules, a three-person panel has to hear the argument within 12 weeks of the appeal being lodged, which, in this case, falls on Christmas Eve. A verdict then has be made inside the next 30 days, giving the case until the third week of January. City could even argue that no deadline should be employed as these regulations were only brought in after the offending period.

In the face of these delays, and the current legal limbo gripping the division, the Premier League are “pressing” for the commission to publicly unveil the scale of City’s punishment before an appeal has even been decided, per the Daily Mail.

It would not be unprecedented for a punishment to be dished out before an appeal has been finalized. Everton were initially docked 10 points in November 2023 (for one uncontested breach) which was later reduced to six points the following February. It is expected that City will face a far sterner punishment.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Enzo Maresca has taken a bold stance on the charges. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesThe same Mail report claims that City’s “most likely” punishment is a “swingeing” points deduction severe enough to practically guarantee relegation. According to Opta’s supercomputer, that would take around 60 points given the caliber of the start made by Enzo Maresca’s side this season.

City’s punishment is not thought to end there. Once in England’s second tier, City would also be expected to receive another points penalty large enough to keep them adrift of promotion. It’s impossible to know how large that would have to be, and it would rely upon the English Football League accepting any Premier League interference in their own competition.
There are reportedly no relegation clauses in any City players’ contracts but the bulk of the star-studded roster would surely jump ship rather than face one, if not two, seasons in the Championship.
Beyond the sporting sanction, City are also in line for a “huge” fine, although that is hardly their biggest problem.

ftbpro_01m5aaazn6vj.title: Man City vs. AEK Athens: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5aaazn6vj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack8:30 PM EDTMan City take on AEK Athens for the first time.  / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Man City), Stefanos Kyriazis/SNS Group/Getty Images (AEK Athens)Manchester City remain perfect in the Premier League after seven matches, but they’re in need of a response in Europe after falling to Paris Saint-Germain on Matchday 2 of the league phase.

Fortunately, the Cityzens have been blessed with a ‘get-right‘ fixture against Greek outfit AEK Athens. Back fighting with Europe’s elite for the first time since 2018–19, AEK followed their slender victory over LASK with a 3–1 defeat to Shakhtar Donetsk’s samba stars at Stamford Bridge.

The 14-time Greek champions are unbeaten domestically after six games, but are down in fourth having drawn twice. They had their clash at the weekend with Athens rivals Atromitos postponed due to their European commitments, and it will take an almighty effort for Marko Nikolić’s side to snatch a result in Manchester this week.

Much of the soccer world is willing them on, however, given the guilty verdict that hangs over Man City’s head. The Cityzens have brought the sport into disrepute, and we remain in flux until sanctions are laid out and their appeal is heard.

Enzo Maresca will continue to operate with ignorance, focusing on the tasks at hand on the field. This is a good opportunity for the City boss to rotate after Saturday’s 3–2 win at Ipswich Town, with a trip to an improving Aston Villa looming.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Phil Foden celebrated his return to the Man City team with a goal. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesMan City were subject to a Parisian masterclass for 35 minutes on Matchday 2, but would have felt as if a result was theirs for the taking after improving drastically in the second half.

Still, the defeat was hardly disastrous for Maresca’s side, with the length of the league phase reducing the significance of these early encounters. City made the top eight last season despite dropping points in three games, and a trip to Barcelona represents the only major challenge left.

Maresca may switch things around and AEK are well-rested, but you wonder just how much of an impact the visitors being fresher will have against a vastly superior opponent playing their 150th Champions League match.
Maresca confirmed a big blow for the hosts ahead of Tuesday’s game, with Antoine Semenyo expected to miss the next two months as a result of the knee injury he picked up at the weekend.

There are fewer concerns surrounding Erling Haaland’s foot injury, but Man City’s No. 9 will likely be rested midweek anyway. Maresca said ahead of the Ipswich victory that Haaland, Rúben Dias and Marc Guéhi were prime candidates for respite after a busy start to the season.
Nico O’Reilly’s back injury still lingers, and the marauding left back is unlikely to feature.

If Maresca rotates heavily, there could be a rare opportunity for third-choice left back Rayan Aït-Nouri to impress, as well as the quickly forgotten summer arrival Allan. In the potential absence of Haaland, Phil Foden may be utilized as a false nine.
Man City predicted lineup vs. AEK Athens (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, Aït-Nouri; Anderson, Bouaddi; Allan, Cherki, Doku; Foden.

AEK head into Tuesday’s match healthy, with goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha likely to be the only absentee due to a wrist injury. The former Lazio shot-stopper is expected to be back in action by the time they face Real Madrid on Nov. 4.

The visitors do have an established strike pairing to lean on, with Luka Jović, once of Real Madrid, and Barnabas Varga working in tandem. The two forwards have each scored four league goals this season, and are awaiting to strike for the first time in this competition.

Croatian playmaker Lovro Majer is another one to keep an eye on. Majer hasn’t quite lived up to his potential after claiming Dinamo Zagreb’s No. 10 jersey as a 20-year-old in 2018, but he’s nonetheless blessed with a lovely left foot and is capable of servicing AEK’s two main goalscorers.
AEK Athens predicted lineup vs. Man City (4-4-2): Brignoli; Rota, Moukoudi, Relvas, Pilo; Majer, Kairinen, Marin, Vitális; Varga, Jović.

ftbpro_01m5ac438k0h.title: ‘My Time Will Come’—Ben Whiteman Hints at Untold Story Behind Wrexham Transfer
ftbpro_01m5ac438k0h.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay3:00 PM EDTBen Whiteman made sure he celebrated his first Wrexham goal in front of Preston supporters. / CameraSport/Getty ImagesWrexham midfielder Ben Whiteman insists his side of the story has yet to be told following his controversial move from Preston North End during the summer transfer window.

The 30-year-old was Preston’s club captain and criticized by former manager Paul Heckingbottom, who claimed Whiteman crossed a line when pushing for a move to the Racecourse Ground. It was suggested that the midfielder told club officials he had played his final game for Preston as he sought a switch to North Wales.

Whiteman was jeered by the vocal Preston supporters as Wrexham defeated their visitors 4–1 at the weekend. The midfielder scored his first goal for his new club and provided an assist, celebrating by turning toward the away end and blowing a kiss to add further fuel to the fire.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

It was claimed Whiteman refused to play for Preston North End as he pushed for a transfer. / Wrexham AFCSpeaking after his standout performance against Preston, Whiteman insisted he had no hard feelings toward his former club.
“I had a fantastic time there,” he tells Sports Illustrated. “...There’s always two sides to every story.
“Mine will get out one day, but there’s a time and a place for things. I understand the frustrations, because I’d have been frustrated if I read all that stuff in the media. Yeah, my time will come.”

Asked about the hostile reception he received from the away end, Whiteman added: “They were giving me stick all game, which again is part and parcel of the game. I actually found it really funny, to be honest. Yeah, they can have it back.”

Phil Parkinson has come to rely heavily on Whiteman. / PA Images/Getty ImagesWhiteman has established himself as a key member of the Wrexham side this season, starting all but one of the club’s Championship matches. His performance against Preston was arguably his best yet for the Red Dragons, and Phil Parkinson was delighted with how he handled the occasion.

“So pleased for Ben,” the Wrexham manager said. “That was tough for him today because, first of all, we came into the game on the back of a defeat, and the Preston fans are obviously really on his case.

“Ben’s got the utmost respect for Preston and all the supporters and everybody at the club. He wanted a fresh challenge and [was] told if a bid came in, they’d consider it. We put a bid in, they accepted it. That’s it.

“It certainly wasn’t a money thing for Ben, coming here. He was just ready at that stage of his career for a fresh challenge. I have to stress, he’s got so much respect for everybody at Preston, but he’s still tough.
“When you’re getting the kind of stick from the opposition fans he got today, all you can do is let your football do the talking. Making goals and scoring one is certainly a great way to do that.”

ftbpro_01m5adx737y8.title: PSG vs. Barcelona: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5adx737y8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack9:30 PM EDTA blockbuster awaits at the Parc des Princes.  / Visionhaus/Getty Images (PSG), James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images (Barcelona)An unmissable Champions League encounter beckons at the Parc des Princes with the backdrop of a riotous French capital, as holders Paris Saint-Germain host La Liga leaders Barcelona on Tuesday.

Both teams are two for two at the start of the league phase, and the back-to-back champions are the early pace-setters after putting Slovan Bratislava and Manchester City to the sword. Luis Enrique’s side were sensational in the opening 35 minutes of last week’s tie, racing into a 3–0 lead against a City team that had been perfect after eight games in all competitions.
PSG were eventually made to work for three points, claiming a 4–2 victory, yet the display served as a reminder of their majesty after a subdued start to Ligue 1.

And they were far from their best on the domestic front again at the weekend, with Enrique’s side staging a late surge to bypass Strasbourg 3–1. They’re now up to second, and have rattled off six consecutive victories since losing to Monaco on Sept. 4.

Barcelona, meanwhile, are continuing to soar. The back-to-back La Liga champions have enjoyed a record-equaling start to their campaign, becoming just the second team in the competition’s history to win their opening nine games of the season by thumping Real Betis 5–2 at the weekend.

Emphatic victories over Feyenoord and Galatasaray have complemented their supremacy on the home front, with the club desperate to claim a first Champions League crown in over a decade to cement Flick’s side as one of the great modern-day teams.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

PSG beat Barcelona in last season’s league phase. / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIt’s hard not to be incredibly excited for this matchup. PSG were involved in a Champions League classic less than a week ago, and the nature of these two teams should mean we’re in for something special on Tuesday.

PSG just show up when it matters most, and although Barcelona navigated their toughest challenge of the season with aplomb at the weekend, a trip to the Parc des Princes is unlike anything they’ve encountered amid their record-breaking start to the new campaign.
Flick has injuries to contend with at fullback, as do the hosts, so perhaps the team that best exploits the very few chinks in the other team’s armor will prevail in the French capital.
Enrique had to call on his bench to get PSG out of the mire at the weekend, with Ousmane Dembélé and Désiré Doué on the scoresheet to help the Parisians turn the tide at Strasbourg.

The likes of Warren Zaïre-Emery and Maghnes Akliouche impressed in the win at Man City last week, but Enrique could deploy his ‘strongest‘ front six against Barcelona on Tuesday. PSG’s fearsome front three will be supplied by an engine room comprising Vitinha, João Neves and Fabián Ruiz.

Nuno Mendes’s absence at left back is a huge blow, given his previous success one-on-one against Lamine Yamal. Mendes will spend the next few weeks on the sidelines due to a muscle injury, and will likely be replaced by summer arrival Lucas Digne.
The aforementioned Akliouche is a doubt due to an ankle injury sustained at the weekend, while youngster Senny Mayulu is dealing with a thigh issue.
PSG predicted lineup vs. Barcelona (4-3-3): Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Digne; Vitinha, Neves, Ruiz; Doué, Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia.
Flick’s primary concerns reside at fullback, but they have enough depth to cope with the absences of Jules Koundé and Eric García, who scored at the weekend.

La Masia graduate Xavi Espart had quickly earned the trust of the manager and will likely start at left back. João Cancelo generally prefers to operate from the left, yet is likely to find himself on the opposite flank in Paris.

Andreas Christensen and Roony Bardghji are also sidelined for the visitors, but Raphinha is back in action for the visitors after a brief injury absence. The Brazilian got minutes under the belt off the bench at the weekend, and will be desperate to regain the starting gig for this huge encounter.
Rodri should start in midfield despite reports he could drop into Barça’s defense, and Flick will have to decide between Fermín López and Dani Olmo for the No. 10 spot.
Barcelona predicted lineup vs. PSG (4-2-3-1): García; Cancelo, Cubarsí, Martín, Espart; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, López, Gordon; Raphinha.

ftbpro_01m5aftbgtj8.title: Man Utd’s Longest Winless Streak of All Time Still Some Way Off for Class of 2026
ftbpro_01m5aftbgtj8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer8:00 PM EDTMan Utd are six games winless. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesManchester United may be on a run of six consecutive matches without a win, but that’s still some way off threatening the club’s longest such streak.

For that, you have to go back almost a century to 1930. The world was a very different place. World War I was still fresh in the memory, the stock market had crashed and the Great Depression was in motion but the economy wouldn’t hit rock bottom for another two years, while John Steinbeck was still seven years away from publishing Of Mice and Men.

In English soccer, Manchester United was not the biggest name around. The club had climbed to the top of the mountain twice under the management of Ernest Mangnall, in 1907–08 and 1910–11, but fell away as a force almost as quickly again.
Mangnall joined Manchester City in 1912 and United were flirting with relegation from the top flight by the time the action was indefinitely halted for war at the end of the 1914–15 season.

Joe Spence played for Man Utd 1919–1933. / Barratts/PA Images/Getty ImagesWhen soccer resumed after the war that was supposed to end all wars but did nothing of the sort, United finished 12th, 13th and then 22nd, relegated in 1921–22. You can see it’s building into a pattern whereby it eventually became possible for the club to go 16 straight matches without winning a single one.

The club returned to the First Division—the name of English soccer’s top flight for over 100 years before the advent of the Premier League in 1992—after three seasons in the second tier, but continued to struggle competing against the heavyweights of the day—Huddersfield Town, Sunderland, Everton and an emerging powerhouse called Arsenal.

Manager John Chapman was mysteriously suspended by the Football Association in 1926 for “improper conduct” with no explanation given. At that point, Lal Hilditch was hastily appointed player-manager—Ryan Giggs in 2014 is the only other example of that in the club’s history. Herbert Bamlett, an ex-referee and among the worst United managers there has been, was the permanent successor, and things ultimately went from bad to worse.

In 1927, principal owner John Henry Davies—the man who had helped put up the money to stop Newton Heath going bankrupt in 1902 before changing the club’s name—passed away. His health had been failing for several years and it took United to the financial brink once more.

United finished the 1929–30 season in 17th place out of 22, two points clear of the relegation zone. The campaign concluded with four winless matches. That was fairly unremarkable considering the team had endured six straight losses during the September and October.

But the winless streak continued apace when 1930–31 began. United lost the opening 12 matches of that season, failing to pick up a single point until Nov. 1 when the winless streak finished at 16 games thanks to a 2-0 victory over Birmingham City at Old Trafford.

James W. Gibson eventually rebuilt Man Utd. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesFans had already made their frustrations known. The Manchester United Supporters’ Club issued a five-point demand to the board, asking for a new manager to replace Bamlett, a new scouting system, new signings, five new shareholders elected to the board and the issue of new shares to raise funds. Those demands were ignored, leading to the threats of a boycott when Arsenal—a few months away from their first league championship—visited Old Trafford on Oct. 18, 1930.

The boycott didn’t exactly happen, with 23,406 making it the best-attended home game of the season. But apathy had well and truly set in, because numbers plummeted thereafter and, come May 1931, fewer than 4,000 watched the final game as a top-flight team for five years.

Financially, United were saved when James W. Gibson took over post-relegation in 1931, although the on-field downfall didn’t immediately stop, going alarmingly close to relegation into the third tier in 1933–34. A promotion, another relegation and a promotion had United back in the top flight by 1938, with the club taking a new approach by founding the Manchester United Junior Athletic Club—a precursor to the modern-day academy—and not fully stabilized until the appointment of manager Matt Busby at the end of World War Two.
Never again, has the club gone 16 consecutive matches without winning.

ftbpro_01m5apb8g9zq.title: Portugal Imposes Official Sanctions on Cristiano Ronaldo After Shock Exit, Jorge Jesus Feud
ftbpro_01m5apb8g9zq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely3:31 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo has been slapped with a comedically small fine. / Octavio Passos/Getty ImagesWeeks after abruptly storming out of Portugal’s international camp, team captain and national icon Cristiano Ronaldo has been slapped with a suspension and fine. But it’s hard to tell which punishment is more comedic.

The Portuguese Football Federation imposed a 30-day suspension on Ronaldo and issued a €255 ($285.83) fine for his shock exit just two matches into the September–October international break. It followed a falling out with new manager Jorge Jesus that Ronaldo later attested to a “broken promise” that left him “hurt.”

A suspension of 30 days beginning Oct. 10—the day the Portuguese federation first ordered Ronaldo a non-automatic provisional suspension—makes the forward first available on Nov. 9, (coincidentally?) just in time for the November international window that kicks off the same day. Therefore, he actually wouldn’t miss any international play. Ronaldo would be available for Portugal’s remaining Nations League group stage matches against Denmark and Wales on Nov. 14 and Nov. 17, respectively.

Meanwhile, the fine of €255 ($285.83) is shockingly worth less than a single minute of Ronaldo’s time. The 41-year-old forward makes an estimated €208,400,000 ($233,000,000) annually from his basic Al Nassr contract, per Capology. That means his daily rate of pay is roughly €571,000 ($640,000), and his rate by the minute is around €397 ($445). And that doesn’t even include what he makes through additional bonuses, or his many outside business and endorsements.

So, for about 40 seconds of his time, Ronaldo can afford to pay the fine and still have plenty of money left over for a pastel de nata, a traditional Portuguese custard tart that is often priced somewhere between €1.20–€2.20 ($1.35–$2.37) on the streets of Lisbon.

Ronaldo was full of apologies. / Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesRonaldo was full of apologies to the nation and his teammates following his controversial decision. High-profile friends like Rio Ferdinand and Piers Morgan went to bat for him, yet he not only expected a harsh disciplinary action, but actually welcomed it.

“Despite the absolute breach of trust in the head coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it,” Ronaldo stated earlier this month in a long, 1,700-word statement. “The responsibility is entirely mine. I apologize to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of one’s word has, for me, a defining impact.”

He added: “The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I believe the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player. I am team captain, and that is an aggravating factor. I have already apologized, but I know that actions must have consequences. Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.”
The Portuguese Football Federation has, in fact, proven that they are not.

ftbpro_01m5aq8029cj.title: USMNT Starlet Mathis Albert Receives Glimmer of Hope After Broken Bundesliga Promises
ftbpro_01m5aq8029cj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner5:11 PM EDTMathis Albert finally made his Bundesliga season debut.  / Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFresh off an impressive debut camp with the U.S. men’s national team, wunderkind Mathis Albert is finally getting what he wanted in Germany with club side Borussia Dortmund: playing time.

The 17-year-old winger made his first Bundesliga appearance of the season for the Black and Yellow on Saturday, coming off the bench in the 70th minute in an eventual scoreless draw with Union Berlin.
Directly following the international break in which Albert (briefly) became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history, Dortmund manager Niko Kovač promised that Albert would receive increased minutes.

“There are no restrictions,” Kovač said on Oct. 9. “He is a very talented young man who is already showing really good signs in training, who has already played a cup game, and who sooner or later, probably sooner, will get a lot more minutes here at Borussia Dortmund than perhaps half a year ago.”

Albert didn’t play a single minute in the two games following Dortmund’s return to action, though. He served as an unused substitute in the Bundesliga match against Werder Bremen and in the Champions League clash with Bodø/Glimt, prompting reports of his interest in finding a new club.
That report seems to have gotten to Kovač, who finally made good on his promise to Albert, granting him significant minutes at the Stadion An der Alten Försterei this weekend.
Albert lived up to the task, racking up 18 touches, seven successful passes, two tackles, a clearance and three wins in his duels against the German foe.

Justin Ellis (right) continues to thrive in MLS alongside Antoine Griezmann.  / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesAs much as Albert’s first significant minutes of the season are a step in the right direction for him, it pales in comparison to the current achievements of some of the other USMNT youngsters who participated in their first international camps this fall.

Cavan Sullivan recently surpassed Alphonso Davies’s record for the most goal contributions in a single season by a teenager (21) with the Philadelphia Union and helped them secure a draw with Charlotte FC to extend their dominant undefeated run. Meanwhile, Orlando City’s Justin Ellis picked up an assist in a win over D.C. United, his 12th this season.

With the young talents easing into more responsibilities at the club level and rising to the challenge of some of the most intense games of their young careers, roster selection only grows more complicated for USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino. He will be forced to make some difficult decisions ahead of the November Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.

ftbpro_01m5awg1ch0b.title: ‘A Little Bit’—Michael Carrick Explains Halftime Lisandro Martinez Substitution
ftbpro_01m5awg1ch0b.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer6:00 PM EDTLisandro Martínez would be a loss from a defensive numbers perspective. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesIt was a roller coaster few days for Lisandro Martínez.
The Manchester United defender was openly critical of the club’s senior hierarchy and sporting director Jason Wilcox in the aftermath of Tuesday’s Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid.

He released an initial social media statement attempting to clarify his comments, then another explaining that there had been a “very positive conversation” with the club’s leadership and manager Michael Carrick. With reports of a formal punishment taking the form of a fine, the matter was considered dealt with by the time Carrick spoke to the press on Friday.
Martínez then started Sunday’s 1–1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road, but was only able to complete half the match before being withdrawn during the interval in West Yorkshire.
The Red Devils were already missing Ayden Heaven because of illness and appeared to switch to a back three when Martínez was replaced by returning fullback Noussair Mazroui.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Martínez  was suffering thigh discomfort. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesCarrick noted afterwards that Martínez had “felt his thigh a little bit.”

It appears that no chances were taken with a player who has suffered repeatedly with injuries since he joined the club from Ajax in the summer of 2022. His first four years with United yielded 110 appearances across all competitions, averaging fewer than 28 per season, while Transfermarkt estimates the Argentina international has spent a total of 632 days sidelined during that time.

Carrick offered no further details on Martínez’s condition, with a further update expected when the United boss next addresses reporters on Tuesday, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League encounter with Como on the shore of the famous lake in northern Italy.

Michael Carrick is counting on Martínez. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesWithout more information at this stage, it’s not clear when Martínez might return to the field. A minor issue that is being carefully managed might only warrant a short time out of action—it feels unreasonable to expect him to face Como so soon after being forced off against Leeds.
At best, he would be a doubt for that game, but would be in contention to return against Bournemouth when the Premier League schedule resumes on Sunday.
A more serious problem could bleed into weeks, or even months at the most extreme scenario. Given Carrick’s initial assessment, that seems unlikely, though.
The thing is, United need Martínez. The young Heaven, the reserve left-footed center back in the depth chart, won’t be out for very long, but he also remains a doubt for Como.

Leny Yoro will also be missing against Como because of the red card he was flashed against Atlético Madrid. Harry Maguire played the full 90 minutes against Leeds but only featured as a substitute in the Spanish capital due to ongoing efforts to manage his workload at the age of 33. Carrick might have no choice but to start the veteran in back-to-back matches. Matthijs de Ligt is back on the bench following an 11-month back-related layoff but has yet to play for now.

ftbpro_01m5b12sqph0.title: How Tough Fall Matches Impacted USWNT’s FIFA World Ranking
ftbpro_01m5b12sqph0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely10:10 AM EDTEmma Hayes’s side was thoroughly outclassed by Spain. / Scott Taetsch/USSF/Getty ImagesThe U.S. women’s national team recently concluded its fall international window, which consisted of two consecutive friendlies against reigning world champion Spain on home soil that were destined to impact FIFA’s global rankings.

The Spanish powerhouse, ranked No. 1 in the world, was expected to be the perfect foe for the No. 2-ranked Stars and Stripes. A battle of the two greats and perhaps even a preview of the 2027 World Cup final next summer. At the very least, it was a chance for the USWNT to prove itself in the pecking order, a chance to put pen to paper and begin rewriting its legacy of dominance on the world’s grandest stage.

But if anything, the series proved how dreadfully far ahead Spain is of everyone else, including the Americans. Spain first defeated the USWNT 2–0 in Washington D.C.—the home team’s first two-goal loss in over two years—before traveling north to Philadelphia to nearly do the same thing. The late heroics of Mallory Swanson pulled out a 2–2 draw three days later, but the game was anything but level.

The reality of Spain’s superiority was something even USWNT manager Emma Hayes herself couldn’t deny. “[Spain] is the best team in the world,” she said after the second friendly. “... We’re still in progress.” To former USWNT legend Tobin Heath, the situation was even more dire, presenting a ton of “red flags” that the Stars and Stripes must resolve before the World Cup.

Whether or not the USWNT can actually rise to the talent level of Spain in just eight months’ time remains to be seen. But in the interim, how did the team’s world ranking hold up following the tough fall window? FIFA published its updated world rankings on Oct. 20.

World rankings will play an integral role in the Women’s World Cup draw this December, determining which of four pots each competing nation is placed into. The high-ranked teams are placed in Pot 1, while the lowest-ranked teams are in Pot 4. Teams from the same pot are exempt from playing against each other in the group stage, making it imperative that the USWNT remains among the very highest-ranked teams in the world in order to have the easiest group stage competition.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The “Triple Espresso” attacking trio of Trinity Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Sophia Wilson will be called upon to bring the USWNT success. / Georgia Soares/USSF/Getty ImagesDespite not earning a win this fall, the USWNT maintained its place at No. 2 globally; however, Spain continues to skyrocket ahead points-wise, while No. 3 Germany and No. 4 England have closed the gap to the Stars and Stripes.

FIFA’s world rankings are based on a intricate points system that does not just evaluate a team’s match results, but takes into account the location of those matches, the importance of them as well as the difference in world ranking between the two opponents (which are used to create predictions for match results). According to FIFA, the “very best in the world can have rating points exceeding 2,000, while the absolute beginners score around 1,000 rating points.”

Spain sits in first with 2121.50 points, as of Oct. 20, while the U.S. is nearly 100 points back with 2042.38. Germany is ranked third globally and snapping at the Americans’ heels with 2034.62 points, while England is not far behind in fourth with 2025.47. The points alone highlight Spain’s world dominance, while showing the precariousness with which the USWNT holds onto second best.

The gap to the top wasn’t always so vast. Back in June, FIFA’s last official update, No. 1 Spain (2105.36 points) sat fewer than 50 points ahead of the No. 2 U.S. (2057.92). Meanwhile, No. 3 Germany (2028.99) and No. 4 England (2027.13) were each roughly 30 points back.

In April, the gap to the top was even smaller. No. 1 Spain (2083.09) was less than 30 points ahead of No. 2 U.S (2054.65); however, No. 3 England (2038.72) and No. 4 Germany (2021.78) were still close behind.

ftbpro_01m5b1ve2keq.title: USMNT Star Cavan Sullivan Makes More History With Major MLS Award
ftbpro_01m5b1ve2keq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner12:01 PM EDTCavan Sullivan has been ranked the best talent under 22 years old in MLS. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCavan Sullivan continues to rack up awards. Amid his incredible breakout season with the Philadelphia Union, the teenage winger has earned the top spot on Major League Soccer’s annual 22 Under 22 list, adding yet another honor to his early career.
The list is organized by MLS and surveys an expert panel of MLS coaches, general managers, sporting directors, broadcasters and select media, including Sports Illustrated.

At 17 years and 22 days old, Sullivan becomes the youngest player ever to earn the No. 1 ranking. Racking up seven goals and 13 assists in just 20 starts, he has successfully established himself as one of the most dangerous attackers in the league.

Sullivan’s success in MLS has drawn massive attention worldwide and reached new heights when he earned his first call-up to manager Mauricio Pochettino’s U.S. men’s national team for a series of four friendlies this fall.

He immediately proved himself on the world stage, starting two matches for the Stars and Stripes, including the clash with bitter rival Mexico. It was during that affair that Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history, producing an impressive strike to guide the Americans to a dominant 3–0 win. The USMNT concluded the window with a perfect four-win record, due in no small part to Sullivan’s attacking contributions. He gave Pochettino plenty of reasons to consider him for November’s Concacaf Nations League competition.

Among the players named to MLS’s 22 Under 22 list, Sullivan is one of 12 with international experience, joined by seven USMNT-capped talents as well as Chicago Fire center back Mbekezeli Mbokazi, who played for South Africa at the 2026 World Cup this summer.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Cavan Sullivan is the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesSullivan surpasses Bayern Munich and Canada superstar Alphonso Davies, who became the youngest player to win the top spot in MLS’s 22 Under 22 back in 2018 at just 17 years and 355 days old, while playing for the Vancouver Whitecaps. At the same time, Sullivan becomes the second Union player to win it, following Leeds United and USMNT midfielder Brenden Aaronson, who earned the honor in 2020.

While Sullivan made his MLS debut in 2024, beating out Freddy Adu as the league’s youngest debutant at just 14 years, 293 days, he only began enjoying regular playing time this summer, when interim manager Ryan Richter took over for Bradley Carnell, who had been hesitant to play the youngster.

Under Richter, Sullivan has become a consistent starter and a core piece of the Union’s dominant resurgence. After starting the season winless and at the bottom of the league, the Union are currently enjoying a 15-game undefeated streak, making them a bona fide MLS Cup contender in an exceptionally competitive Eastern Conference.

In the last six regular season matches alone, Sullivan racked up three goals and seven assists. He was named the MLS Player of the Month for September, beating out the likes of Lionel Messi and becoming the youngest player to ever earn the honor. He also recently broke the record for themost goal contributions by a teenager in a single MLS season (21).

Julian Hall (left) and Adri Mehmeti (right) cracked the top three of the rankings, fresh off their first USMNT camp alongside Cavan Sullivan.  /  Ira L. Black/MLS/Getty ImagesSullivan topping the coveted MLS list might have been expected, but seven fellow USMNT-capped players also made the cut.

Finishing second was Red Bull New York’s Julian Hall, who scored three goals in his first four USMNT appearances this fall. He has 11 goals and three assists in 29 MLS matches this season. His USMNT and Red Bull teammate, midfielder Adri Mehmeti, ranked third with over 2,200 minutes logged for manager Michael Bradley’s side.

Among the other recent USMNT call-ups was Orlando City’s Justin Ellis, who has a goal and 11 assists this season and has enjoyed a rapid ascent alongside French legend Antoine Griezmann. The 19-year-old ranked fifth, while also recently winning his own major MLS award. Meanwhile, speedy New England Revolution fullback Peyton Miller, who shined on the USMNT’s left flank last month, finished sixth in voting.

Towering 6'7" Union center back Neil Pierre earned seventh-place honors, after establishing himself as one of the USMNT’s best defensive prospects. New England’s Brooklyn Raines and Philadelphia’s Frankie Westfield also cracked the rankings, earning 10th and 11th respectively.

ftbpro_01m5bqj7g34j.title: Five Favorites to Win the 2026 MLS Cup—Ranked
ftbpro_01m5bqj7g34j.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner2:00 PM EDTCould the 2026 MLS Cup feature a 2025 rematch between Lionel Messi's (left) Inter Miami and Thomas Müller's (right) Vancouver Whitecaps? / Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Messi), Elsa/Getty Images (MLS Cup), Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images (Müller)The 2026 MLS regular season is coming down to wire, with most teams having four games left to battle above the playoff line.

This postseason will keep the system used since 2023: nine teams in each conference, with the eighth- and ninth-place finishers playing a one-game Wild Card match to determine who advances to face the top seed in the first round’s best-of-three series.

While some teams have thrived from the first kick of a ball back in February, others have adjusted and improved throughout the lengthy campaign. Now with just a few weeks left to go, it’s becoming clear which teams are the true contenders, most likely to hoist the MLS Cup on Dec. 15.
Here, Sports Illustrated ranks the five favorites to capture glory.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Cavan Sullivan has the Philadelphia Union in contention for MLS Cup. / Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesThe Philadelphia Union were at the bottom of the MLS table heading into the World Cup break. Interim manager Ryan Richter has turned things around in miraculous fashion, and the team sits sixth in the Eastern Conference with four games to go, enjoying a 15-game unbeaten run. The core of the project has been the trust in young players. Cavan Sullivan has taken on increased responsibility and is up to seven goals and 14 assists as a 17-year-old, breaking Alphonso Davies’s 2018 record for the most goal contributions as a teenager in a single season with 21. At the same time, 19-year-old towering center back Neil Pierre has proven to be a key defensive piece, while 20-year-old right back Frankie Westfield has made immense improvements. Beyond the young talent, midfielder Danley Jean Jacques and goalkeeper Andre Blake continue to play key roles in Richter’s setup. Meanwhile, the attacking partnership of Bruno Damiani and Milan Iloski has linked up for 31 goals.The Union have found an approach that works and seems nearly unstoppable these days, peaking perfectly for the postseason and potentially putting themselves in position for a coveted top-four spot in the Eastern Conference. However, with both Miami and Nashville standing in their way, reaching the MLS Cup could be a step too far for the starlets.
Cavan Sullivan Sets MLS Record With Stunning Goal. Cavan Sullivan Sets MLS Record With Stunning Goal. dark. Next

Rafael Navarro has elevated St. Louis CITY SC into true MLS Cup contention. / Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesSt. Louis CITY SC completely rebuilt their core midseason, and it’s worked. Manager Yoann Damet’s men are bona fide MLS Cup contenders entering the final stages of the season, especially after winning the U.S. Open Cup final midweek, the club’s first-ever trophy. While its recent 19-game undefeated run didn't set the record for the longest MLS regular-season run, it showed how quickly the team has adjusted to a key group highlighted by Carlo Holse and Rafael Navarro, alongside a mainstay between the sticks in Roman Bürki. Navarro has been the biggest difference-maker, though, racking up eight goals and three assists in eight games since coming over from the Colorado Rapids on a $12 million fee. With the consistency of results and the dominance shown through the recent run, St. Louis have elevated themselves from a sleeper pick ahead of the season to a true challenger, but will have to navigate a competitive Western Conference and avoid any hiccups that would test their depth.

Lionel Messi's Inter Miami are the defending MLS Cup champions. / ISI Photos via Getty ImagesInter Miami are the defending champions, but haven’t looked like MLS Cup-quality for much of the season, including a spell with just one win in 10 games. Now on their third manager, Kily González, they seem to have hit their stride and could be ready to peak at the perfect time in the playoffs. Lionel Messi remains the be-all-end-all factor of Inter Miami’s entire project. He is the favorite to capture a third-straight MLS MVP title and looks likely to defend his Golden Boot title as well. His influence has been unmatched, especially as he grows more comfortable under González.While Messi will determine the team’s fate, 2025 MLS Goalkeeper of the Year Dayne St. Clair has regained his confidence between the sticks in recent weeks. Meanwhile, Germán Berterame has improved—all while Luis Suárez defies reason as a consistent offensive threat with 15 goals in 26 games at nearly 40 years old. Miami won’t have it easy returning to the MLS Cup, likely having to take down Nashville—the team that knocked them out of the Concacaf Champions Cup—but they'd be favored if they reach that point.

Thomas Müller (center) has played alongside Ryan Gauld in 2026, unlike for most of 2025.  / Rich Lam/Getty ImagesThe defining decision of the Vancouver Whitecaps’ season was selling USMNT midfielder Seabtian Berhalter to Middlesbrough for $2 million after his starring performance at the World Cup. Since then, the 2025 MLS Cup finalists have struggled to match the dominance and consistency they showed throughout the first half of the season. Although rest assured, Whitecaps fans, this is still a very good team and a clear-cut favorite to win the Western Conference. While the club may have just two wins in its last six games, it remains on pace for a better points total than the 2025 campaign, the club’s best regular-season performance. The back end has conceded just 31 goals in 30 games, second only to Nashville SC among all teams. Brian White has continued to lead the offensive charge with 17 goals in 28 games, despite a dip in recent form. The most significant difference from the Berhalter-led 2025 and early stages of 2026 has been the return of Scottish Designated Player Ryan Gauld. Injured for most of the 2025 season, Gauld has four goals and two assists this year and has made significant strides in the second half of the campaign, particularly when Thomas Müller has not been fully fit. Even still, Müller has nine goals and eight assists of his own, and manager Jesper Sørensen is ensuring his German star is healthy for the playoffs. The Whitecaps should be confident in making a run toward another MLS Cup appearance.

Hany Mukhtar (right) and Sam Surridge (left) have been key pieces in Nashville SC's remarkable campaign.  / Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty ImagesNashville SC have been the top team in MLS all season and are still on pace to set the all-time regular-season points record, set by Inter Miami’s 74 points just two seasons ago. While the Herons flamed out in the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs that year, Nashville are better equipped for a lengthy run all the way to the title. The team's core remains the attack, with Hany Mukhtar’s goal-creation ability standing out even more than in his 2022 MLS MVP campaign. At the same time, Sam Surridge has maintained his stellar scoring rate, with 17 goals in 24 games, while enjoying more support than he did in last season’s 25-goal campaign. Add in Cristian Espinoza’s playmaking and Elias Saad’s transition ability, and it’s easy to see why they’ve ranked among the league’s best attacking powers all season. Unlike some past Supporters’ Shield winners, though, Nashville haven’t sacrificed defensive solidity. Through 30 games, they have conceded just 23 goals, and Brian Schwake’s impressive goalkeeping has come up clutch when an opponent breaks through the likes of Reid Baker-Whiting and Andy Nájar on the backline. With home advantage expected through the postseason, it feels like MLS Cup or bust for Nashville, as they look to become the first team since LAFC in 2022 to win both the Shield and MLS Cup in the same year.

ftbpro_01m5c53wf6tf.title: PSG vs. Barcelona: Complete Head-to-Head Record Ahead of Champions League Clash
ftbpro_01m5c53wf6tf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:00 AM EDTOusmane Dembélé (left) and Lamine Yamal are two figureheads of this rivalry. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty Images (Dembélé), Gongora/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Yamal)European fixtures do not come much bigger than Paris Saint-Germain vs. Barcelona.

The back-to-back European champions face off against the back-to-back winners of Spain’s La Liga on Tuesday evening in a battle of two of the strongest favorites to go on and win the Champions League. It promises to be an all-action affair that could easily be one of the best games of the entire season.

Honors have been remarkably even in this fixture across the years, with both PSG and Barcelona boasting periods of dominance in a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable moments in competition history.
Here’s a look at the complete head-to-head record between these two giants, as well as five of the most famous meetings.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

An emerging Lamine Yamal (left) helped see off PSG. / Tim Clayton/Corbis/Getty ImagesThe first leg of the 2023–24 Champions League quaterfinals saw Xavi’s Barcelona travel to a hostile Parc des Princes, where Raphinha made the breakthrough shortly before half time. Things changed dramatically after the interval, however, with PSG 2–1 ahead six minutes later and threatening to make it three, four or even five. Manager Luis Enrique claimed before kickoff that he played the Barcelona way “better” than Xavi and, on this evidence, it was initially hard to argue.Refusing to go down without a fight, Xavi brought Pedri off the bench to immediately turn things around with a glorious assist just seconds later, and Andreas Christensen proved to be the hero with a winning header to complete the comeback and seal the win in this grudge match.

PSG held firm. / Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty ImagesThe money-ball era at PSG featured a visit from an unbeaten Barcelona side that had not yet conceded that season in September 2014. There were concerns that the absence of injured striker Zlatan Ibrahimović would harm the Parisians, but that proved not to be the case.David Luiz’s opening goal marked the first time Barcelona had been trailing in a match for five months. Lionel Messi’s immediate response suggested it may have just been a temporary blip, but PSG roared back into the lead through Marco Verratti and Blaise Matuidi netted early in the second half to give the French giants an imposing lead.Neymar quickly pulled one back and triggered an all-out assault on the PSG goal in search of an equalizer, but the hosts stood firm to seal a famous victory.

It was the Kylian Mbappé show. / Alex Caparros - UEFA/Getty ImagesOne of many defining moments in Kylian Mbappé’s emergence into undisputed superstardom came in February 2021, when he dismantled Barcelona in utterly devastating fashion.Messi, still at Barcelona at the time, put the Blaugrana ahead from the penalty spot midway through the first half, but that did nothing other than inspire a ferocious response from a PSG side missing both Neymar and Ángel Di María. Mbappé ended the game with a beautiful hat trick and comparisons to the likes of Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo came pouring in. Soccer’s newest superstar had well and truly arrived.

Zlatan Ibrahimović (center) stole the headlines for PSG. / Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty ImagesThe meeting between these two in April 2013 was the first since PSG’s lucrative takeover propelled the French side into Europe’s undisputed elite. This was, arguably, the game to prove they belonged.With a 37-year-old David Beckham in midfield and a healthy Ibrahimović seeking revenge against his former employers up top, PSG put on a show. The Swedish striker scored and assisted in a game that swayed to and fro up until the very last second—Matuidi’s 94th-minute equalizer canceling out what looked like a winner from Xavi five minutes earlier.It was an enthralling tie and a true statement of intent from PSG.

Sergi Roberto (center) sealed one of the most famous comebacks ever. / Laurence Griffiths/Getty ImagesCould we end anywhere else? This is perhaps the most famous match in Champions League history.PSG had dismantled Barcelona 4–0 in the first leg of this round-of-16 affair. It was over. Barcelona needed to win by five goals to advance, and that was surely not going to happen. Surely.What followed was 90 of the most mind-boggling minutes we’ve ever seen in Europe’s top competition as Barcelona netted three times beyond the 88th minute to complete what is known today as La Remontada—“the comeback”—and become the first team in competition history to overturn a four-goal deficit.

ftbpro_01m5c6xbkad9.title: 2026 Ballon d’Or Ceremony Hosts Confirmed
ftbpro_01m5c6xbkad9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom5:45 AM EDTThe Ballon d’Or ceremony will be held in London this year. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesThe Ballon d’Or organizers have announced that the CBS Sports duo of Kate Scott and Thierry Henry will host this year’s ceremony.

Scott, a multilingual English broadcaster with a long track record of excellent coverage, was standing to the side of the podium performing this role just last year. 1987 Ballon d’Or winner Ruud Gullit was her right-hand man on that occasion, but this month Scott will be joined by her familiar partner-in-crime, Henry.

The affable pairing make up half of the immensely popular CBS Sports panel on Champions League nights in the U.S. Given the international edge Scott and Henry offer, it’s perhaps no surprise that the Ballon d’Or has continued to overlook Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards even in their post-playing careers.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Thierry Henry (left) and Kate Scott are a safe pair of hands. / Mark Sutton/Formula 1/Getty ImagesAs the brainchild of France Football magazine, whose name is not misleading, the Ballon d’Or ceremony has traditionally been held in Paris, with the spectacular Théâtre du Châtelet a favorite venue. However, for the first time since 2016, the award will venture beyond France’s capital.

London’s Palladium will be the venue this year, which is a special year for the award. On the 70th anniversary of the inaugural victor, England’s Sir Stanley Matthews, the organizers are taking the trophy back to the first country in which it was ever handed out.
Back in 1956, it was a compact version of the prize, a small ball glued onto a wooden stand, which was given to Matthews in Blackpool Town Hall.

All eyes will be on the Ballon d’Or. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesFor most viewers, the Ballon d’Or ceremony will be available for free by completing a straightforward sign-up for DAZN. This applies to all onlookers in the United States, Mexico, Canada and the United Kingdom.
Beyond simply crowning the best men’s and women’s players, prodigies, managers and goalkeepers in the world, the ceremony offers future stars of the game a chance to dream.
“We all watched that ceremony with those red carpet arrivals and said to ourselves: One day, that will be me,” Kylian Mbappé, one of the frontrunners for this year’s award, once gushed.

“I’m sure many dream of these moments, imagining the nerves of waiting for their ranking to be revealed, sitting next to the greatest players on the planet. In fact, that’s it: the Ballon d’Or reawakens our childhood dreams. We’ve won titles, other awards, but this one is the Holy Grail. It’s the ticket to the big world.”

ftbpro_01m5c8fjt9yb.title: ‘Broken Promises’—Ten Hag Breaks Silence on Ronaldo, Kane & Man Utd Chaos
ftbpro_01m5c8fjt9yb.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:55 AM EDTErik ten Hag’s Man Utd tenure was a rollercoaster. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty Images, Matthew Ashton - AMA/Getty Images, James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images, Uwe Anspach/picture alliance/Getty Images, Alex Dodd - CameraSport/Getty ImagesErik ten Hag arrived at Manchester United in the summer of 2022 as one of the most exciting young managers around, given the unenviable task of fixing a team whose decline had been nothing short of extraordinary.

His two years at the helm were anything but simple. The Dutchman won two trophies, fought with Cristiano Ronaldo and watched over some of the worst signings in club history. So, when he sat down with The Athletic to pull back the curtain on his tenure, it came as no surprise that he had plenty to say.
Here are five key takeaways from the interview.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Ten Hag was not happy with the direction of the club. / John Walton/PA Images/Getty ImagesTen Hag’s departure from United was a comedy, the sort of which you would pay to see in the theater.

An infamous end-of-season review into his position saw United speak with a handful of big-name alternatives before not only persisting with Ten Hag, but offering him a new contract. Three months later, he was fired.

“I wouldn’t go on with only one year left,” Ten Hag reflected. “So I said, ‘I need an extra year and we have to do it together.’ They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.”
Among the biggest broken promises to Ten Hag was the sale of homegrown midfielder Scott McTominay.

Only Bruno Fernandes and Rasmus Højlund scored more goals for United in 2023–24 than the Scotland international, who Ten Hag claims he was assured would remain at Old Trafford just weeks before he was flipped to Napoli.
“That’s why I got disappointed,” the manager explained. “In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, ‘No selling Scott McTominay.’ We would go aligned in the transfer window.

“I make an argument, a reason: we don’t have scoring abilities. Scott brings scoring abilities and great mentality. He has United in all his veins. So when they bring up the subject, ‘No.’ And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.”

Raphaël Varane (left) and Casemiro (right) both swapped Real Madrid for Man Utd. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesIn April 2022, as the club waited for Ten Hag to join, interim boss Ralf Rangnick argued United needed “open heart surgery” as he insisted everybody at Old Trafford had to get on the same page and address a culture of toxicity that had been allowed to breed.

The very same issue Rangnick tried to warn against reared its ugly head during Ten Hag’s reign and played a key part in the tenure of his successor, Ruben Amorim. There is even a case to suggest it is still alive and kicking to this day.
According to Ten Hag, United are responsible for allowing this culture to continue.
“They are continuing the toxic culture; they fuel it, they give the power to the players.”
“Players have to act, they have a big responsibility. Football is, for some, not the highest priority. And United for some wasn’t the highest priority.”

Ten Hag then touched on what he described as the “Madrid connection,” referencing a series of signing of former Real Madrid stars. Raphaël Varane and Cristiano Ronaldo were already at United when Ten Hag joined and Casemiro followed the pair over in the summer of 2022.
The Dutchman accused the trio of contributing to the issues at United with egos built from years of playing at the highest level.
“I can say I think that’s what the Madrid connection brought in, that players are powerful and they want to decide,” he said. “In my opinion it didn’t suit the phase United was in.
“The leadership wanted attacking, dynamic football and these players wanted to play what fitted themselves.”

ftbpro_01m5c9m35hvk.title: The Ballon d’Or Prize Ronaldo Is Still Fighting Messi for This Year
ftbpro_01m5c9m35hvk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom4:00 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo hasn’t won the Ballon d’Or since 2017. / Angel Martinez/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesA decade after he was last honored by France Football, Cristiano Ronaldo is back in the running for recognition this year as one of the contenders to be crowned the B.O.A.T., the Ballon d’Or of All Time.
The clunkily named prize is a new edition launched by the French magazine in honor of the award’s 70th anniversary. The task is simple, “Which was the ultimate golden year?”

Fans are given the chance to vote for the greatest single year performance delivered by any multiple Ballon d’Or winner in the award’s history. Was Ronaldo’s triumph in 2017 better than Lionel Messi’s 2015? What of the earlier vintages, should Michel Platini’s 1984 stand above Johan Cruyff’s triumph from a decade earlier?
This is the question facing anyone willing to pay €1 ($1.12) to vote on the official Ballon d’Or website.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Lionel Messi has won more Ballon d’Or trophies than any other player. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images1957: Alfredo Di Stéfano (Real Madrid)1959: Alfredo Di Stéfano (Real Madrid)1971: Johan Cruyff (Ajax)1972: Franz Beckenbauer (Bayern Munich)1973: Johan Cruyff (Ajax)1974: Johan Cruyff (Ajax)1976: Franz Beckenbauer (Bayern Munich)1978: Kevin Keegan (Hamburg)1979: Kevin Keegan (Hamburg)1980: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (Bayern Munich)1981: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (Bayern Munich)1983: Michel Platini (Juventus)1984: Michel Platini (Juventus)1985: Michel Platini (Juventus)1988: Marco van Basten (Milan)1989: Marco van Basten (Milan)1992: Marco van Basten (Milan)1997: Ronaldo (Inter)2002: Ronaldo (Real Madrid)2008: Cristiano Ronaldo (Manchester United)2009: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2010: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2011: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2012: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2013: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid)2014: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid)2015: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2016: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid)2017: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid)2019: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2021: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)2023: Lionel Messi (Barcelona)In terms of raw statistics, no one has ever enjoyed a more dominant round of Ballon d’Or voting than Messi in 2009. Of the 96 judges, 90 voted the impish figurehead of Pep Guardiola’s all-conquering Barcelona in first place. A perfect score at this year’s ceremony would have been 480 points, Messi’s ended the night with a swollen haul of 473.
Michel Platini’s heroics for France at the 1984 European Championships also earned him near universal acclaim while the more modern vintage of Karim Benzema was a widely accepted victor in 2022.

Yet, scarcely has there been a player with the blend of force and finesse in the mould of Ronaldo Nazário from 1997. The then-21-year-old trampled all before him during his maiden season in Barcelona, storming his way to the youngest ever Ballon d’Or triumph.
Cristiano Ronaldo in Manchester United blue. pic.twitter.com/VrZW311vUk

There’s an argument to be made that Ronaldo peaked during his penultimate year at Manchester United. The sharpened point at the tip of Sir Alex Ferguson’s last great team was instrumental in the club’s capture of the Premier League—setting a single-season scoring record—while also scoring in a triumphant Champions League final against Chelsea.

Ronaldo was most content eight years later, when he led Portugal to the national team’s first ever major trophy at Euro 2016. “I have cried three of four times already and my brother had to tell me to calm down. And I said: ‘Hugo, I can’t,’” the captain gushed after the final.
“It’s true, from the bottom of my heart, I swear on my son’s life, I am so very, very, very happy. I could repeat this 100 times. I am so happy. This is the trophy that was missing.”
The Ballon d’Or trophy has been missing from Ronaldo’s cabinet since 2017 but that could change this year.
