ftbpro_01m5c9mxgzcg.title: Jose Mourinho Sent Endrick Transfer Challenge by Rival Sporting Director
ftbpro_01m5c9mxgzcg.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:40 AM EDTEndrick is a wanted man. / Helios de la Rubia/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesReal Madrid manager José Mourinho warned that anyone trying to take Endrick away from the Spanish capital will have a “serious fight on their hands with me.” Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has made it clear that he’s up for the challenge.
Endrick scored in Madrid’s stunning 4–3 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League last week, but has been starved of minutes this season, starting only once in 2026–27.

After a productive loan spell at Lyon in the spring, there had been speculation that the 20-year-old would be shipped out temporarily again for this campaign. However, he stayed put past the transfer deadline, in spite of reported interest from a number of European clubs.
One of the linked parties was Roma and the Italians could revive their interest in January, with sporting director D’Amico addressing the speculation prior to his team’s Serie A clash with Genoa.

Tony D'Amico was asked about Roma’s interest in Endrick. / Antonietta Baldassarre/Insidefoto/LightRocket via Getty ImagesOn the question of January signings, D’Amico told Sky Sport Italia: “Certainly, to face certain competitions and compete in matches like Wednesday’s, but also to confirm our place in the Champions League, we’ll need to take another step and add something. We tried in the summer and weren’t able to for various reasons, but we’ll try again to improve.
Asked specifically about an Endrick move, he suggested a loan move could be an option.

“Our policy is to sign strong players,” D’Amico said. “Then, when you buy a player on loan, there are various options to include. As Roma, we want to have the option, at the end of the season, to be able to keep whoever we bring in on loan. That’s our approach.”
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
Endrick POTM 🏆#UCL pic.twitter.com/WoPPM8TRZd
Speaking after Real Madrid’s win over Roma, during which he was named UEFA Man of the Match, Endrick admitted he would consider a January transfer.
“I take it day by day,” he told reporters. “If I have to leave in January, I’ll leave; if I have to stay, I’ll stay. I will do whatever God puts in my heart.”
The young forward’s stance is apparently in opposition to that of Mourinho, who, despite being reluctant to play Endrick, is adamantly against the idea of an exit.
“Forget it, forget it. Forget any interested clubs,” the manager responded when asked about January transfer interest in Endrick. “They had better sit down, otherwise they will get tired waiting.

“He is a player I love, with incredible potential. He is very important to us. Anyone interested in him will have a serious fight on their hands with me, because I believe he doesn’t need to go out on loan and will achieve tremendous success here.”

Endrick could replace Vinícius Jr in the team. / Alberto Gardin/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesEndrick has cut a peripheral figure at Madrid under multiple managers since his 2024 arrival, when he was hailed as South American soccer’s top prospect.
Following his Champions League heroics off the bench, Endrick was handed his first start of the season in the weekend’s 4–1 win over Sevilla, beginning the game out wide on the right.

With Kylian Mbappé virtually unmoveable as Mourinho’s center forward—and now backed up by super-sub Carlos Espí—Endrick’s best hope for game time may well be as a winger—a role he performed to some success last season for Lyon.

Sunday’s victory at the Bernabéu saw a shuffling of the pack from Mourinho after some indifferent performances. Arda Güler was moved to central midfield for more creative control, while Vinícius Jr’s four-game suspension necessitated a change of wingers, with Yan Diomande also starting.
With three more games to go before his fellow Brazilian is available again, Endrick has a golden opportunity to show what he can do for this Madrid team.

His next chances will come in Wednesday’s Champions League visit of RB Leipzig and El Clásico at Camp Nou on Sunday, Oct. 25. Should he continue to impress as he did against Roma, he will give Mourinho and Madrid’s higher-ups plenty to think about.

ftbpro_01m5cc900v0g.title: ‘Provisional Measures’—Real Madrid’s Plot to Have Vinicius Jr Ban Reduced
ftbpro_01m5cc900v0g.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath8:50 AM EDTVinícius Jr has been banned for four matches. /  M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesReal Madrid are still hopeful of reducing Vinícius Jr’s four-match suspension and are intent on exhausting every possible avenue to challenge the punishment.
The Brazilian superstar is currently serving a four-match ban after receiving a straight red card during Madrid’s 1–0 win over Villarreal.

Vinícius Jr initally believed he had put his team 2–0 up after tapping in from Jude Bellingham’s pass, midway through the second half. However, upon VAR review the goal was disallowed and the Madrid No. 7 was sent off for yanking the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba in the build-up.
The moment was the nadir of Vinícius’s season so far, with the forward struggling for form in 2026–27.

To date, he has scored just once in 10 matches and drawn criticism for his ineffective displays. Manager José Mourinho has called Vinícius Jr’s poor run “heartbreaking,” while the player himself has admitted: “I’m angry with myself for not being at my best.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Jr reacted angrily to being sent off. /  Diego Souto/Getty ImagesVinícius has already missed Sunday’s 4–1 win over Sevilla and is due to be unavailable for the next three La Liga fixtures—Barcelona (Oct. 25), Racing Santander (Nov. 1) and Valencia (Nov. 7).

However, according to SPORT, Madrid consider the sanction “excessive” and have “not yet completely ruled out” the possibility of getting the 26-year-old back in time for Valencia as they continue to follow the appeals process.
Madrid’s initial appeal with the the RFEF Appeals Committee was unsuccessful last week, after the committee found no clear and obvious error in the referee's decision.
Vinícius was handed a two-match suspension for the incident itself, with a further two matches added for protesting in “an aggressive manner” towards referee Isidro Díaz de Mera.

As things stand, Vinícius Jr won’t play in La Liga until November. / Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty ImagesAfter the RFEF Appeals Committee rejected Real Madrid’s challenge, the club’s last throw of the dice is to take their case to the Sports Administrative Tribunal (TAD), and hope for a result which will see Vinícius available to face Valencia.

While the TAD has the power to overturn or reduce the punishment, SPORT’s report claims Madrid are also considering requesting “provisional measures" that would temporarily suspend the ban, allowing Vinicius to return to La Liga action while the case is examined.
As things stand, Vinícius Jr remains unavailable for selection in La Liga until after the November international break when his team face Celta Vigo on Nov. 22.

Yan Diomande excelled in Vinícius Jr’s absence. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)In Madrid’s first match without Vinícius, the Brazilian was hardly missed as Mourinho’s men ran out 4–1 winners at home against Sevilla on Sunday.
Arda Güler, who has often featured on the right wing, was moved into a deeper role as one of two midfield pivots, while Yan Diomande and Endrick started out wide.

Summer signing Diomande excelled in Vinícius’s preferred position on the left, scoring a rocket late on, while he also got himself an assist in the emphatic win. The 19-year-old Ivorian completed the most dribbles in the match and had the joint-most touches in the opposition box.
Diomande is the most natural replacement for Vinícius Jr on the left, while Endrick, Brahim Díaz and Güler can all operate from the right.
Should Mourinho choose to switch things up further, Mbappé could be moved to the wing—a role he has regularly operated in for his country—with either Endrick or Carlos Espí as the central striker.

ftbpro_01m5ce75zs4p.title: Gio Reyna Taken Into U.S. World Cup History Books by Family’s New Dynasty Member
ftbpro_01m5ce75zs4p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom9:00 AM EDTCarolina (left) and Gio Reyna have both been in the goals. / Judit Cartiel/FIFA/Getty Images (Carolina Reyna), Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images (Gio Reyna)Carolina Reyna’s brace in the U.S. women’s national team’s opening game of this summer’s U-17 World Cup could have gotten lost amid the torrent of goals in a 17–0 win over Samoa. Yet, those strikes will forever have a place in American soccer history.

A few months before Reyna’s role in the barn-storming battering, her brother Gio scored for the men’s senior national team on home soil in a 4–1 thumping of Paraguay. The two offspring of retired USMNT star, Claudio Reyna, now hold the distinction of the first brother-sister pair to ever score for the States at a World Cup.
Claudio never achieved the feat, be it at youth or senior level, but can take solace from having two of the current program’s brightest talents.

After a tumultuous falling out with former USMNT manager Gregg Berhalter, stoked by the flames of a feud started by Claudio, Gio Reyna has always been admired by Mauricio Pochettino. The versatile midfielder rewarded his manager’s World Cup call-up with that delicious outside-the-boot goal at SoFi Stadium to cap a rout. 4–1 remains the USMNT’s joint-largest ever World Cup win, although it pales in comparison to the feats of Carolina’s US U-17 WNT.

The Stars and Stripes were already 10–0 up before Reyna even came on against Samoa. The teenager only needed three minutes to pile on the humiliation, combining with Maddie DiMaria, who would end the game with six goals of her own, to pick out a tamely guarded net. Reyna made it 15–0 with a left-footed curler into the top corner in the 78th minute, allowing her teammates enough time to add another pair of goals.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Claudio Reyna went to four World Cups. / David Madison/Getty ImagesReyna

Carolina was only 10 when she saw Gio captain the U-17 side in 2019. A U.S. team spearheaded by fellow future senior international Ricardo Pepi would have a brilliant start to the tournament; Gianluca Busio scored inside just three minutes. Yet, no one else would find the net throughout a winless group-stage exit.

Claudio’s U-17 side in 1989 at least began its first-round elimination with a win over Brazil, although it wasn’t a vintage iteration of the Seleção—not a single member of the team that lost 1–0 to the USYNT would make a senior international appearance.

Reyna Sr. would have more success at senior World Cups. After sitting on the bench for the home tournament in 1994, the attacking midfielder was a regular starter in 1998 before captaining the nation in 2002 and 2006. Unlike his children, the central operator was unable to score, although he did surpass Gio by making it to the quarterfinals.

Given the hulking size of Monday’s result, Carolina would expect the U.S. youngsters to go far this summer. One win of such a large margin is almost enough to guarantee qualification for the knockout round already, with two group games against China and Kenya remaining. Should the U.S. U-17 WNT win its group, it would be up against the runner-up in Group D, which could be the likes of Japan or France, in the round of 16.

The U.S. has never won the women’s U-17 World Cup in its current guise, falling as early as the first knockout round last year. The Stars and Stripes’ best return was a third-place finish in 2008, when a team including future senior winners Sam Mewis and Crystal Dunn were involved. It remains to be seen if Carolina can ever aspire to those heights, but she’s already done her family proud.

ftbpro_01m5cf21c6x0.title: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal Combined XI: Gunners Narrowly Get the Edge
ftbpro_01m5cf21c6x0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott5:00 PM EDTArsenal and Bayern Munich faced off in 2025–26. / Julian Finney - UEFA/Getty ImagesBayern Munich vs. Arsenal is the headline fixture of Wednesday’s Champions League slate, and rightly so.

These are two of the best teams in Europe. Two of the favorites to go on and win the entire competition. The teams that finished first and second in last season’s group stage and could easily claim the same two spots again. As heavyweight clashes go, they don’t come much bigger than this.
Some of Europe’s best players will be on show here, even if a handful of big injuries and suspensions will rob audiences of the chance to see even more quality on show.
Considering all the players available for selection, here’s Sports Illustrated’s thoughts on a combined XI between Bayern and Arsenal.

David Raya is an elite stopper. / Maynard Manyowa/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesA foot injury has left Manuel Neuer doubtful for this game. Even if the legendary German is fit and healthy, Raya has done enough over the past few years to earn a place in nearly any combined XI you could imagine.
Neuer is given the sort of freedom that must seem alien to Raya and the rest of Arsenal’s backline. The stopper is there to save the ball and nothing more—and he’s amazing at doing exactly that.

Jurriën Timber has elevated his game under Mikel Arteta. / Maynard Manyowa/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesKonrad Laimer is one of the most underrated players around these days, but he’s in a battle with one of the world’s premier right backs in Timber here.
The Dutchman is a force to be reckoned with and will hope to build on his assist against Lille last time out in this competition.
Gabriel is an elite option. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal’s defense is perhaps the best on the planet, and Gabriel plays a huge part in that.

The towering Brazilian is imperious, bringing a combination of athleticism, ferocity and technical ability that few defenders can match. He’s even relished the need to elevate his game in the absence of the injured William Saliba.

Dayot Upamecano has finally realized his potential. / Oliver Kaelke/DeFodi Images/DeFodi/Getty ImagesThe arrival of Vincent Kompany, himself a legendary center back, has turned Upamecano’s career around.

Upamecano has listened to every word his illustrious mentor has offered up and has forced his way into the conversation for the best center back in the world alongside Gabriel. Whichever of these two has a better game on Wednesday is likely to come out on the winning side.

Riccardo Calafiori is flying for Arsenal. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThere’s a certain freedom about Calafiori’s game this season that we had not seen in his previous two years at Arsenal, and everyone involved seems to be profiting from that.

He might not be able to match up to Alphonso Davies in a running race—can anybody?—but Calafiori is now a genuine threat at both ends of the field, sweeping up at the back and contributing to goals at the other end of the field.

Joshua Kimmich does a thankless job in midfield. / Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty ImagesKimmich has been so good for so long now that his quality is often overlooked. “Yeah, he’s great, so what?”

His metronomic style of play provides the base from which Bayern can build in attack, where his star-studded teammates usually command the headlines. There are those that need to never forget to credit Kimmich for his understated importance.

Declan Rice was a target for Bayern in 2023. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesIn another timeline, Rice is turning out for Bayern Munich after speaking with Thomas Tuchel, now of England but formerly of Bayern, in the summer of 2023. Instead, he took his midfield dominance to Arsenal.
Rice was sensational when these two sides last met in the group stage last season, helping to inspire a 3–1 victory for the Gunners.

Aleksandar Pavlović has emerged as a genuine star. / Christina Pahnke - sampics/Corbis/Getty ImagesKompany will hope that Pavlović continues to avoid receiving the credit he deserves. The 22-year-old has quietly risen from academy gem to an undisputed superstar. He’s a tempo-setting passer who thrives in a possession-heavy setup, constantly looking for ways to get involved in the final third.

ftbpro_01m5cfww50s3.title: ‘One Rooster’—Barcelona President Strikes a Nerve With Mbappe, Vini Jr Swipe
ftbpro_01m5cfww50s3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath11:15 AM EDTKylian Mbappé (left) and Vinícius Júnior have failed to click at Real Madrid. / Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA/Getty ImagesAhead of this weekend’s Clásico, Barcelona president Joan Laporta has raised the temperature by criticizing Real Madrid’s transfer strategy of signing “very expensive players who aren’t delivering the expected results.” As he explosively claimed: “More than one rooster in the same henhouse can’t work.”

Eternal rivals, the bad blood between Spain’s—and the world’s—two biggest clubs has increased in recent times amid the ongoing ‘Negreira case’ and an open war of words between the two presidents Laporta and Florentino Pérez.

At the start of October, UEFA announced that Real Madrid had submitted “a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira.”

Barcelona are accused of paying over €7 million ($7.9 million) to a company owned by Negreira, the former vice president of Spanish soccer’s refereeing committee, in an effort to get favorable refereeing decisions. An investigation into the matter by the Spanish justice system remains ongoing, while the current La Liga champions have in turn filed a lawsuit against Pérez.
Laporta has previously accused Madrid of “trying to discredit Barça” and wanting “to harm football.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Jr have not won a trophy together. / Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty ImagesSpeaking to L’Equipe ahead of Barcelona’s Champions League glamor tie against Paris Saint-Germain, Laporta fired shots at Madrid once again.
Asked about his relationship with Los Blancos, the Barça president admitted “it doesn’t exist anymore.” When asked directly about the Negreira case, he deflected to his rivals’s transfer policy.

“They want to divert attention to that, but there’s nothing to it,” Laporta is quoted as saying. “Real Madrid has lost credibility, both institutionally and on the pitch. They no longer have any presence within the institutions. I think they've taken the wrong path, and they’re paying the price. They’ve opened their wallets to pay for many very expensive players who aren’t delivering the expected results.”
Laporta previously claimed that Kylian Mbappé’s arrival at Madrid back in 2024 couldn’t work—a remark he has now doubled down on.
“Yes, I said it. More than one rooster in the same henhouse can’t work, ever.”

“The priority in football is the team and team spirit. If you don’t have that, the project doesn’t work. That’s one of Barça’s strengths: having great talents, players from La Masía, players who come from other footballing cultures, and managing to create a team with a synergy that works.

“They preferred individual players, big-name signings. I think Real Madrid has lost credibility and they’re trying by all means to justify all this by lying about the Negreira case, because they haven’t won anything for two years. We are winners, and we are candidates to win everything.”

Laporta has claimed there is only room for one of Vinícius Jr or Mbappé. / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesAs much as Laporta’s words are an obvious attempt to take the focus away from the Negreira case, they will strike a nerve with his rivals.
Famously, since Mbappé’s arrival over two years ago, Real Madrid have not won a major trophy, with cohesion in attack between the club’s biggest stars an ongoing issue.
Mbappé—who was Pérez’s white whale before finally joining in 2024—was meant to improve the reigning European and Spanish champions and kickstart a new era of dominance.

However, despite bagging an incredible amount of goals and individual accolades, the Frenchman’s presence has clearly impacted Madrid as a team, and there is endless debate about whether the lineup can support both him and Vinícius Jr due to the similarity of their playing styles and positions.

Following the Madrid derby defeat prior to the international break, L’Equipe shared a damning graphic of each player’s average position on the field during play, with Mbappé and Vinícius virtually on top of one another.

Despite public protests to the contrary from both players, gossip persists that Mbappé and Vinícius do not see eye to eye, while managing egos remains an ongoing concern for whoever is the Real Madrid manager.
Madrid currently sit six points adrift of La Liga leaders Barcelona ahead of their Clásico showdown at Camp Nou on Sunday.

ftbpro_01m5cp7v0ecx.title: Report: Real Madrid Send Huge European Super League Bill to Six Premier League Clubs
ftbpro_01m5cp7v0ecx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:30 AM EDTThe Premier League’s traditional elite certainly have enough money to fund Real Madrid’s reported demands. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesReal Madrid reportedly expect the six Premier League clubs that signed up for the aborted European Super League venture in 2021 to cough up their share of the funds taken to mount this failed launch.

The ESL was doomed almost from its inception. In response to the strain put on club finances by the COVID-19 pandemic, Europe’s traditional elite concocted a closed shop competition, stripped of promotion or relegation, which would be governed by its founding members. A dozen clubs released a sensational joint statement on April 18, 2021 announcing the imminent scheme to rival UEFA’s Champions League.

Within three days, all six Premier League clubs had publicly withdrawn from a proposal which inspired fearsome fan backlash. They were soon joined by Atlético Madrid, AC Milan and Inter Milan in hastily back-pedalling.

Juventus would hold on to the plan until June 2023, while Barcelona didn’t reliquinsh their grip until February of this year. Real Madrid would soon after reach “an agreement of principles for the wellbeing of European club football” with UEFA to finally bring an end to the ESL. Or so everyone thought.

A new report from The Athletic, however, has claimed that Real Madrid “want” Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur to cover what they are thought to owe when it comes to the cost of setting up the ESL, given their swift withdrawals effectively brought the plan to an end.

That sum could amount to as much as €80 million ($89.9 million), which would require each of the 12 founding clubs to stump up about $7.5 million. Madrid, Barcelona and Juventus, the longest hold-outs in the ESL scheme, are thought to have been sharing the financial burden up to this point.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Florentino Pérez is the figurehead of the European Super League. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesWhile his grand plan to “save soccer” (from what, it’s never been quite established) was crumbling all around him in those days during the great exodus of clubs, Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez had a warning. “I’m not going to take my time to explain what a binding contract is here,” he snapped. “But the fact is, the clubs can’t leave.”

The dozen founders “signed a 120-page contract,” according to Juve’s ex-chairman Andrea Agnelli, when they settled on this ESL plot, ensuring they were not only conspirators but legally binding shareholders. It has been widely reported that 11 of the dozen remain indelibly tied to the project, with Inter Milan the only club to have managed to wangle their way out.

The finer details of the contract’s wording will ultimately dictate whether the clubs are forced to pay their share. Although, a savvy-enough lawyer could presumably argue either case given the vagaries which exist in even the most carefully studied documents.

ftbpro_01m5cpbhx18p.title: Real Madrid Predicted Lineup vs. RB Leipzig: Vinicius Jr Returns for Yan Diomande Reunion
ftbpro_01m5cpbhx18p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath3:30 PM EDTReal Madrid can make it three wins from three in the Champions League. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Madrid are out to make it three wins in a row at the start of their Champions League campaign, with RB Leipzig the visitors to the Bernabéu on Wednesday.

Depending on your outlook, Madrid’s two victories so far—Inter Milan and Roma—can either be described as unconvincing or the hallmark of champions who grind out wins in difficult circumstances without being at their best.

Their next match is unlikely to win over those that are still undecided on the true potential of José Mourinho’s team, but does offer up a strong opportunity for a morale-boosting victory ahead of the Clásico this weekend.

Leipzig are a team of extremes. Martín Demichelis’s side was demolished 4–1 by debutants Como in its European opener and has won or lost by three goals five times this season already—last suffering a 6–1 defeat to Bayern Munich at the weekend.
Here’s how Real Madrid could line up to face their German opponents on Wednesday.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
GK: Thibaut Courtois—No rest for the wicked; Courtois has played every minute of Real Madrid’s season. That fact should continue to be true after Wednesday evening.

RB: Trent Alexander-Arnold—Whoever starts at right back midweek is likely to be benched for the Clásico. Given Mourinho’s apparent preference for Denzel Dumfries in the big games thus far this season so, Alexander-Arnold may well get the nod here.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—Konaté was on media duties ahead of the Champions League clash, suggesting he will start. The Frenchman’s all-action style has gone down well with Mourinho since his summer move.
CB: Dean Huijsen—The Spain international had both the most touches and most defensive contributions in the weekend win over Sevilla.

LB: Álvaro Carreras—As with the right back position, Mourinho may wish to rest the legs of the men required to face off against Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon at the weekend. If Marc Cucurella is benched, Carreras will get another chance to impress.
CM: Federico Valverde—Moved to right back at the weekend, the captain may return to a more familiar central midfield role against Leipzig.

CM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—The Frenchman put in arguably his best performance of the season in the win over Sevilla, completing 93% of his passes, while bagging an assist as well as contributing seven defensive contributions.

RW: Yan Diomande—The 19-year-old sparkled from the left at the weekend, finally showing everyone why Madrid broke their transfer record to get him. He could be switched to the right for a reunion with the club he joined from this summer.
AM: Jude Bellingham—Having been made a key cog in Mourinho’s machine, Bellingham is thriving as the driving force from the No. 10 position.

LW: Vinícius Jr—The Brazilian’s suspension means he will be absent for the Clásico, but he can provide fresh legs midweek. The out-of-form superstar is looking for his first goal for Madrid since August.

ST: Kylian Mbappé—Just a hat-trick away from 100 Real Madrid goals, Mbappé will surely start. However, Endrick and Carlos Espí are waiting in the wings to give the Frenchman some rest before Sunday, should this game get wrapped up quickly.

ftbpro_01m5crtjtkaq.title: Real Madrid vs. RB Leipzig: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5crtjtkaq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew HeadspeathOct 20, 2026It’s a clash of cultures on Wednesday night. / Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Real Madrid), Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (RB Leipzig)Yan Diomande’s early reunion with his old RB Leipzig teammates is the big headline ahead of Real Madrid’s third Champions League match this season.

The 19-year-old got the Bernabéu to believe the hype on Sunday with his first real standout performance since his record-breaking arrival this summer, grabbing a stunning goal and assist in the 4–1 win over Sevilla.

Expectations have gone up a notch for Diomande, who now prepares to face the club where he made his name last season. He could be joined in attack by Vinícius Júnior—another of the major talking points lately, with the Brazilian available to feature in the Champions League despite a four-game domestic ban.
Madrid can make it three European wins in a row with a victory over Leipzig, but fans may hope for less of an edge-of-your-seat affair than the—admittedly thrilling—4–3 against Roma last time out.

A goal-heavy night could well be on the cards again one way or another; Leipzig shipped four away to Como in their Champions League opener and were thrashed by Bayern Munich at the weekend. They have also won by three or more goals on three occasions already in 2026–27.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Yan Diomande faces his former club. / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesThis encounter comes four days before the first Clásico of the season and, quite possibly, the match that will decide if Real Madrid are title contenders. You could forgive José Mourinho for having half a mind elsewhere.
In Leipzig, his Madrid side face a team of contrasts. One capable of brushing aside the likes of Frankfurt (6–0) and Hamburg (5–0) while also suffering heavy defeats to Bayern (6–1) and Como (4–1).

Madrid cannot afford to sleepwalk this one and Martín Demichelis’s side are undoubtedly dangerous. However, their open, attack-first style has seen them come undone time after time on the road and Madrid’s superstar frontline will get plenty of chances.
Madrid’s availability is as good as it has been all season, with only long-term absentees Ferland Mendy, Rodrygo and Raúl Asencio set to miss this one.
Diomande could face his old teammates from the right side of Madrid’s attack, rather than the left—as he did against Sevilla at the weekend—with Vinícius Jr an option for Mourinho again.
The main consideration for the manager will be making sure his team ends the night without any knocks or overly depleted batteries with the trip to Barcelona now so close.
Real Madrid predicted lineup vs. RB Leipzig (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Alexander-Arnold, Konaté, Huijsen, Carreras; Valverde, Tchouaméni; Diomande, Bellingham, Vinícius Jr; Mbappé.
Marc Guiu and Assan Ouédraogo are set to miss out with injury. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Christoph Baumgartner missed the weekend’s defeat to Bayern and is a doubt to start for Wednesday.
Brazilian striker Rômulo should return to lead the attack after being benched for the weekend. Top scorer Christopher Nkunku may move to a deeper role as a result.
Norway international Antonio Nusa and on-loan star Brajan Gruda provide danger from out wide and will likely look to exploit space on the break behind Madrid’s own attacking wingers.
RB Leipzig predicted lineup vs. Real Madrid (4-2-3-1): Vandervoordt; Baku, Orbán, Lukeba, Raum; Banzuzi, El Aynaoui; Nusa, Nkunku, Gruda; Rômulo.

ftbpro_01m5csd62v1y.title: Man Utd Predicted Lineup vs. Como: Carrick Manages Depleted Defense
ftbpro_01m5csd62v1y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack2:00 PM EDTMan Utd’s defense looks set to be short-handed in Italy. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesManchester United’s 1–1 draw at Elland Road was a fine result in isolation, but it was hard for Red Devils’ supporters to stomach given that it extended the team’s winless run to six matches across all competitions.
Man Utd only have wins over Ipswich Town and Sabah to show for their season to date, and they’re in need of bouncing back in Europe after falling to Atlético Madrid last week.

Michael Carrick suggested that Sunday’s showing at Leeds United felt like a “fresh start,” as he changed tack to counteract the hosts all while ensuring his team was far harder to play against. It was a step in the right direction, but it won’t count for all that much if the visitors are overwhelmed by a slick and dynamic Como outfit on Wednesday.
Here’s how Man Utd could line up for this Champions League clash.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Matthijs de Ligt makes his first appearance since last November. /   GK: Senne Lammens—While Lammens hasn’t quite built on a sturdy debut season, there’s no sense that his place between the posts is under threat.
RB: Diogo Dalot—After an impressive two-way showing on Sunday, Dalot is a sure bet to retain his spot in Carrick’s defense.

CB: Matthijs de Ligt—It’s likely going to have to be De Ligt time for Man Utd, given that Lisandro Martínez and Ayden Heaven are set to miss out due to injury, and Leny Yoro is suspended. The Dutchman has recovered from a back injury that’s kept him out for almost a year.

CB: Harry Maguire—Maguire stood up for the Red Devils at Elland Road, and he’s unlikely to be subject to the sort of crossing barrage that Leeds imposed at the weekend. Como will attempt to play through the visitors on Wednesday.
LB: Noussair Mazraoui—Mazraoui is hardly an ideal solution, yet he is the most likely course taken with Luke Shaw still sidelined.
CM: Andrey Santos—Similar to Lammens in goal, Andrey Santos is by no means a spectacular profile. You at least know what you’re going to get from him, and in a volatile Man Utd team, that’s valuable.
CM: Carlos Baleba—The best of Baleba is yet to manifest in Man Utd red, yet it’s already become clear just how important his legs are to Carrick’s midfield.
RW: Amad Diallo—Man Utd‘s attacking balance is enhanced when Amad holds the width down the right. Supporters would love the Ivorian to evolve into a regular final-third contributor, too.

AM: Bruno Fernandes—There’s a sense that Fernandes is trying just a little too hard to work his way back into form. Not even an outing against Leeds, one of his favorite opponents, could trigger an upsurge. Perhaps the European stage will bring it out of him.

LW: Matheus Cunha—Cunha is set to return to the team, with Marcus Rashford poised to miss out again. In the absence of Shaw, rotations will be imperative to ensure the dynamic between the Brazilian and Mazraoui is successful.

ST: Bryan Mbeumo—The Cameroonian star simply has to be the leading man without Benjamin Šeško. Mbeumo’s scored in back-to-back Premier League games, and his efficiency will be important to Man Utd securing a big result away from home here.

ftbpro_01m5ctcgmcd6.title: Report: Ronaldo Learns Portugal Stance Ahead of November International Break
ftbpro_01m5ctcgmcd6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott12:30 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo stormed out of the last Portugal camp. / Torbjorn Tande/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesThe September-October international break featured a handful of wild storylines, including Cristiano Ronaldo’s decision to walk out on Portugal.

A bust-up with manager Jorge Jesus over his minutes saw Ronaldo leave camp just two games into the four-match window. His punishment for doing so was a fine of €255 ($285.83)—no, that is not a mistake—and a suspension of 30 days.
Portugal is back in action in just a few weeks when club soccer pauses for another international break in November, leaving Ronaldo’s involvement in the games up in the air.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
The details of Ronaldo’s suspension are not clear. / Lise Åserud/NTB/AFP/Getty ImagesThis situation may need some clarification from the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF).

When the FPF confirmed Ronaldo’s punishment on Oct. 19, there was no clarification as to whether the 30-day suspension began on that date or when Ronaldo was initially given a provisional suspension back on Oct. 9.
The specifics are key here as the November international window kicks off on Nov. 9, with the team’s first game five days later against Denmark on Nov. 14.

If Ronaldo’s 30-day suspension includes time already served, then he would be clear to join up with Jesus’s next roster on Nov. 9. If it started when the statement was made, not only would he miss that fixture, but Ronaldo would miss the subsequent game against Wales on Nov. 17, too.

According to Sky Sports News, the belief is that Ronaldo’s suspension did start all the way back on Oct. 9, meaning he is expected to be cleared to play right before the next international window kicks off.

Jorge Jesus has a decision to make. / Horacio Villalobos/Corbis/Getty ImagesHere’s an entirely different debate. Just because Ronaldo would be legally cleared to play for Portugal, Jesus would face no obligation to involve the Al Nassr forward.
The heart of this entire issue is a disagreement between Ronaldo and Jesus, who would have to rebuild their relationship before even thinking about moving forward together.
Before Ronaldo learned of his punishment, Jesus had started a public quest to bury the hatchet.
“In the next call-up, if Cris is playing and wants to be in the national team, why not?” Jesus explained.

“[Ronaldo] is the one who decides what he wants for his life. As it was before the first call-up, it will be the same before the second. We shared before the first, and if he’s interested, we’ll share again in the second.”

Clearly, Ronaldo’s decision will be key, and there is no guarantee he will return. Indeed, his sister recently suggested the veteran forward may be about to call time on his international career, leaving fans nervously awaiting the revelation of Jesus’s roster next month.

ftbpro_01m5cvfac5qs.title: Arsenal Predicted Lineup vs. Bayern Munich: Madueke Earns Starting Berth
ftbpro_01m5cvfac5qs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack3:00 PM EDTNoni Madueke has played his way into the starting lineup. / Andrew Kearns/CameraSport/Getty ImagesTen wins from 11 to open their account this season would suggest that all is well on the red half of north London, but Mikel Arteta knows that his supposedly liberated roster still has gears to move through.

It was a grind for the Gunners at the City Ground, who required just one shot on target to defy a stubborn Oliver Glasner-led Nottingham Forest at the weekend. Last season, so many beat Arsenal with the set-piece over-reliance stick, and now that they’re still winning without dominating from dead-ball situations, the narrative has shifted to Arsenal’s performances being rather hard to watch.

Even without William Saliba, the Premier League champions lean on their defence. They remain remarkably stout, and have needed mere bursts of attacking thrust to earn three successive victories after the international break.

They’re likely to require more than a bright spell when they travel to Munich on Wednesday for a blockbuster Champions League duel. This could’ve been last season’s final, and Vincent Kompany’s high-powered Bayern Munich will provide a test that few on the continent can offer.
Here’s how Arsenal could line up at the Allianz Arena.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: David Raya—Raya is often kept quiet due to the outstanding defensive structure ahead of him, yet this feels like a game where Arsenal are going to need the Spaniard’s very best.

RB: Jurrïen Timber—The Dutchman has been a bright spark since recovering from injury, improving his work in the final third. Timber scored in the meeting with Bayern during last season’s league phase.
CB: Ezri Konsa—Arsenal are still without Saliba, but he hasn’t been sorely missed thanks to the club signing Konsa in the summer.

CB: Gabriel—Gabriel locks horns with Harry Kane again after keeping him in check last autumn. Kane has a supreme record against the Gunners, and he‘ll be itching to shine less than a week out from the Ballon d’Or ceremony.
LB: Riccardo Calafiori—Arsenal’s attacking X-factor will certainly be grateful that Michael Olise is suspended for Wednesday’s match.
CM: Bruno Guimarães—It’s only October, but Arsenal signed Guimarães to deliver on such occasions. His best has been shown off the bench so far.

CM: Declan Rice—Rice is evolving as a passer at the start of the new season, and the Englishman’s work with the ball in both the build-up phase and in transition will be imperative for the visitors in Munich.

RW: Bukayo Saka—Saka was unable to capitalize on Neco Williams’s early yellow card at the weekend, but he inspired Arsenal off the bench in their 3–0 victory over Lille. He has an excellent record in this competition, notching 23 goal contributions in 31 matches.
AM: Martin Ødegaard—Arsenal’s captain starred on Matchday 1 against Napoli, and the approach the visitors take without the ball will likely determine just how influential Ødegaard is on Wednesday.

LW: Noni Madueke—Eberechi Eze was so poor at the City Ground that Madueke probably would’ve started this fixture by default. However, the Englishman cemented his spot down the left by scoring the game’s only goal off the bench. He also found the back of the net in last season‘s clash with Bayern.
ST: Kai Havertz—Havertz will encounter plenty of familiar faces in Munich, and he’ll be keen to put a tough outing in Nottingham behind him.

ftbpro_01m5cwphzegy.title: ‘I Don’t Like’—Mourinho Fires Brutal Warning at Vinicius Jr Ahead of Leipzig Clash
ftbpro_01m5cwphzegy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 PM EDTVinícius Jr can’t play in La Liga until November. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty ImagesJosé Mourinho insisted no player on his roster is “untouchable” ahead of Real Madrid’s Champions League clash against RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

The manager made the remarks when asked directly whether Vinícius Júnior’s place in the Madrid starting XI was in doubt, with the forward out of form and now suspended from La Liga action until November.

The Brazilian is free to play in the Champions League and is expected start against Leipzig. However, with Los Blancos shining in his absence at the weekend in the 4–1 win over Sevilla, there have been suggestions that the team is actually better off without Vinícius Jr.
“Only the badge is untouchable,” Mourinho said in his press conference on Tuesday. “I don’t like the concept of ‘untouchable’ players.
“What makes players untouchable isn’t a captain’s armband, or how long they’ve been at the club, or their status. What makes a player untouchable is performance.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Vinícius Jr has scored only once this season. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesMourinho’s blunt words constitute a marked change in tone from the manager, who has—so far—backed Vinícius Jr this season amid a disappointing run of form that has seen him go without a goal since August.

Amid boos and whistles from the Bernabéu crowd towards the club’s No. 7 earlier this season, Mourinho responded by saying: “In Portugal there is a proverb: you only throw stones at trees that bear fruit.

“So what Vini has done here over recent years? How many Champions Leagues has he won, how many goals has he scored, how many balls has he won? His achievements speak for themselves so he is the tree that has a lot of fruit on it and people want to get a piece of Viní.”
Next. Best Real Madrid Ever. The 25 Best Real Madrid Players Ever—Ranked. dark

Ahead of the win over Roma, Mourinho then claimed it was “heartbreaking” to see his star in such a bad run of form, expressing his hope that the “real Vinícius” would reappear in the Champions League.
A week on, the manager seems to be making it clear he is ready to drop the superstar forward to the bench if needed.
For his part, Vinícius Jr has admitted to being “angry with myself for not being at my best,” while he suggested he was suffering with confidence issues during the last international break.

Vinícius Jr is a known favorite of club president Florentino Pérez and one of the locker room’s biggest fish. After signing a big-money contract extension back in August, Vinícius Jr essentially became unsellable. However, his recent performances mean he is not undroppable for Mourinho—as awkward as that may be to handle for all parties.

With Vinícius Jr banned in La Liga until Nov. 7—as a result of receiving a four-match suspension for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair (and his subsequent protests to the referee) in the win over Villarreal—the upcoming Champions League fixtures take on extra weight for the Brazilian.

The clashes with Leipzig on Wednesday and AEK Athens on Nov. 4 constitute the only opportunities Vinícius Jr will have to play for his club prior to the next international break. Those two games could end up being decisive for the 26-year-old’s season.

With Yan Diomande now shining—the teenage Ivorian has four goal contributions in his last three games, including a goal of the month contender against Sevilla—Vinícius Jr has genuine competition for the left wing for the first time in years.

A scorer in two finals, the Champions League has been the arena of Vinícius Jr’s biggest triumphs as a Real Madrid star. He will need to find a way to rekindle some of that magic against Leipzig to convince Mourinho that he still warrants his place in Los Blancos best XI.

ftbpro_01m5cxp01sbx.title: ‘They’re Better’—Fabregas Puts Pressure on Man Utd, Carrick Ahead of European Bout
ftbpro_01m5cxp01sbx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas4:30 PM EDTCesc Fàbregas has done a stellar job at the helm of Como.     / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesManchester United might be navigating through one of the worst starts to a season in club history, but Como manager Cesc Fàbregas considers the Red Devils favorites to collect three points when they meet on Wednesday in the Champions League.

It’s been well over a month since Man United last won a game, dropping points in their last six matches across all competitions. There’s still a long way to go before they match the club’s longest winless drought, but Michael Carrick’s men do hold the unwanted honor of producing United’s worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Nevertheless, Fàbregas isn’t downplaying United’s threat despite their rough patch. Although he couldn’t hide his excitement about hosting such a marquee clash, he also recognized the visiting Red Devils are superior.

“It’s a great match against one of the best and biggest teams in history,” Fàbregas said on the eve of the match. “It’s a match to dream about, but we must try to do our best to try to win and pick up the three points.

“We slowly have to understand what it’s like to face the top sides, when you know that they’re better than you, but you still have to compete with what you have,” he added. “Our inner strength and our mentality are what must make us strong and allow us to believe that we can do it.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Cesc Fàbregas (left) has been linked as Michael Carrick’s potential successor at Man United.     / John Peters/Manchester United/Getty ImagesWhat Fàbregas has been able to do at Como’s helm over the past three seasons—taking them from Serie B to the Champions League—has firmly placed him as one of the most wanted young managers in Europe.

The midfield-maestro-turned-manager is now on the radar of some of the biggest teams in Europe who are keen on poaching him away from Como. Man Utd are among the teams that have been linked with the Spanish boss as a potential replacement for the struggling Carrick.

Before the match, Fàbregas was asked about him potentially succeeding Carrick, the man he fought against on the pitch during his playing career. The Spanish boss was having none of it and decidedly refused to even entertain the question.

“I won’t answer that question because I think that’s not a very nice question,” Fàbregas said. “I don’t think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side.”

For now, Fàbregas’s full focus is on continuing to help Como’s rise among Italy’s elite. Wednesday’s clash against a historic side is the reward of the good job done so far, but Como and their manager remain hungry for more.

Cesc Fàbregas was delighted after Como’s 4–1 win over RB Leipzig in the club’s Champions League debut.  / Marco Canoniero/LightRocket/Getty ImagesRegardless of their nightmarish form to start the campaign, Man Utd remain one of the most historic clubs in world soccer. For Como, a team that until 2024 had spent over two decades away from Italy’s top-flight and had experienced not one but two bankruptcies, hosting a team of United’s caliber represents a milestone moment.

Never in the club’s 119-year history had a team of such status—outside of Italian giants—visited the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. Fàbregas is highly aware of this, which is why he’s not shying away from describing a landmark moment in Como’s history as a “dream come true.”

“They are a great team,” Fàbregas said about Man Utd. “Just three years ago, when we were in Serie B, it would have been unthinkable that Manchester United might come to the Sinigaglia. Yet on Wednesday, that is exactly what will happen. For us, it’s a dream come true. We’ll take our chances.”
What will be a dream night for Fàbregas and the Lombardy side could be a nightmare for United and Carrick if they’re unable to end their winless slump on Wednesday.

ftbpro_01m5cybffj9a.title: U.S. Teen Sensation Follows in Erling Haaland’s World Cup Footsteps
ftbpro_01m5cybffj9a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom2:30 PM EDTMaddie DiMaria has been prolific for U.S. Soccer’s youth teams. / Kenta Harada/USSF/Getty ImagesWhen Sweden took a 5–0 lead over Cuba at the 1938 men’s World Cup in France, French journalist Emmanuel Gambardella shut his typewriter and declared: “Up to five goals is journalism. After that, it is statistics.”

Gambardella would have stopped typing inside the opening half-hour of the U-17 U.S. women’s national team’s World Cup opener against Samoa on Monday. Had everyone else watching on in Morocco followed suit, they would have missed 12 more goals and the full scale of Maddie DiMaria’s remarkable achievement.

The 17-year-old high school prodigy kickstarted the scoring inside 63 seconds and would eventually end the match with six goals (plus one assist). No U.S. player has ever bagged a double hat trick in a competitive match at any age level, while DiMaria became the first individual since a certain Erling Haaland to score half a dozen goals at a World Cup.
Haaland, who starred for Norway’s senior men’s side at this summer’s World Cup on North American soil, famously rattled in nine goals against Honduras at the U-20 World Cup in 2019.

Erling Haaland could not be stopped by Honduras. / Alex Livesey/FIFA/Getty Images“That means everything—he’s an inspiration,” DiMaria gushed when confronted with this startling statistic. “Watching him play, watching him score goals and just his desire and ruthlessness around the box, he’s an amazing player and to be the next player behind that is just such an honor.

“I feel super, super excited and grateful just to be in this place. I don’t think I would be here, have been able to do it, without my teammates. Going out there, our goal is to just give it our best and I think we totally did that. Just go straight from the start and I think scoring early set us up for success for the rest of the game.
“I’m just super blessed to have all those girls behind me, supporting me, finding me in the right places and just celebrating me.”
While Samoa’s unwitting players clearly weren’t capable of stopping DiMaria (or her teammates) during the 17–0 rout, they would have known all about the threat she poses.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
A record breaking night for Maddie DiMaria 🔥 pic.twitter.com/6FquYvO8UT
“Maddie’s awesome.” U-17 USWNT manager Ciara Crinion had plenty more to say about her prolific striker, but those two words got the point across.

DiMaria has been a poorly kept secret for years. The proud native of Missouri became the first freshman ever to be crowned Gatorade National Player of the Year after racking up 30 goals and 21 assists en route to the state championship title with Cor Jesu Academy. DiMaria has only improved since—and at a rapid pace.

After rattling in a frankly ridiculous 67 goals on top of 25 assists while winning all 25 matches for Cor Jesu Academy her junior year, DiMaria transcended soccer. The 17-year-old was crowned the 2026 Gatorade Best Female Player across all sports, an honor she would later describe to NBC Chicago as “the best moment of my life.”

Previous winners of this cross-discipline recognition include Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone and Allyson Felix, who have 11 Olympic gold medals between them, as well as two-time World Cup winner Morgan Gautrat.

It’s a lofty reputation to live up to, but DiMaria has been born for this sort of scrutiny. The St. Louis kid, now committed to play collegiately for the North Carolina Tar Heels, comes from a long line of soccer stars.

The lineage can be traced back to DiMaria’s grandfather, Tom, a former goalkeeper who sits in the St. Louis Soccer Hall of Fame. Jeff, Maddie’s father, made it to MLS while her mother, Sara, ranks as one of the most prolific creators in the history of Division I Loyola-Chicago. DiMaria’s siblings, Ana and Jack, have also played college soccer.

“They’ve always pushed me to be the best version of myself on and off the field,” DiMaria told TopDrawerSoccer. “We’ve always played soccer in the backyard together, and I’ve grown up with them supporting me always.” That support has certainly paid off.

ftbpro_01m5cyhrj4qm.title: Champions League Predictions 10/21: Arsenal, Bayern, Real Madrid, Man Utd Feature
ftbpro_01m5cyhrj4qm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 20, 2026Arsenal headline Wednesday’s fixtures. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesThe Champions League is really starting to find its groove after a slow start.

A three-week international break meant there was plenty of distance between Matchdays 1 and 2 of this season’s league phase, but we’re getting into the swing of things before national teams reconvene in November.

After Tuesday’s action threw up a barnstorming encounter between two of the favorites, Wednesday is supplying another heavyweight duel. Moreover, plenty of intrigue surrounds Vinícius Júnior‘s return to Real Madrid’s starting lineup amid a lengthy domestic suspension, as well as Manchester United’s trip to the idyllic Como.
The lack of jeopardy at this early juncture seems to liberate those competing, so expect another night of goalscoring mayhem as Matchday 3 concludes.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Wednesday’s action to pan out.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
Cesc Fàbregas and Michael Carrick are familiar foes. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesPrediction: Como 2–1 Man Utd
A “dream” night beckons for Cesc Fàbregas‘s Como on Wednesday evening, as the Champions League debutants welcome the mighty Manchester United to the Giuseppe Sinigaglia.

Michael Carrick’s Red Devils are hardly the imperious force they once were, and the visitors are set to be without a litany of players for this encounter. It’s a fixture Carrick can ill-afford to lose, given that United are six games without a win, yet he described Sunday’s draw at Leeds United as a "fresh start" after a week of several flashpoints.

Lisandro Martínez, who remained in the starting lineup at Elland Road despite his public outburst after last week’s defeat to Atlético Madrid, is among those unlikely to travel to Italy due to injury, as a depleted United aim to build on their gritty showing in West Yorkshire.
The burgeoning Como are seemingly everything their visitors are not in terms of alignment, and their Champions League bow on home soil last month was quite the occasion under the lights.

Barcelona were at least made to work for their eventual emphatic victory in Istanbul last week. At one point, it looked like Victor Osimhen had given Galatasaray a 2–0 lead, but the striker’s effort was ruled out for offside. Then came the onslaught.

The Turkish champions have exclusively relied on their home form for any success in this competition as of late, and will have to find a way of making themselves much harder to beat on their travels if they’re to show any signs of discernible progress on the continent.

A trip to Lille is hardly the most intimidating of away days, and Davide Ancelotti’s side hit a couple of stumbling blocks last week. After succumbing to a second-half Arsenal blitz on Matchday 2, Lille were held at home by Brest in Ligue 1 at the weekend.
Aston Villa had themselves a record-breaking night on their previous Champions League outing, thrashing Fenerbahçe 6–0.

After a poor opening month, Unai Emery’s new-look Villans are starting to click. They’ve won two of their previous three Premier League games, and the fresh additions are coming to the fore. Nicolas Jackson scored twice in last week’s rout, and Johan Manzambi was Villa’s match-winner at Newcastle United on Saturday.

Another kind home fixture on paper awaits, although Viking head into the bout off the back of their hugely admirable showing against Bayern Munich on Matchday 2. After losing comfortably at Stuttgart, Viking rallied after allowing a 2–0 lead to slip. Michael Olise’s red card aided their late revival, as Herman Haugen headed home a 90th-minute equalizer.
Bayern are unlikely to be the last team to suffer in Stavanger, but Viking will find it tough throughout the league phase to earn points on their travels.
Arsenal defeated the Bavarian giants in last season’s league phase. / Tom Jenkins/Getty ImagesPrediction: Bayern Munich 1–1 Arsenal
It’s the matchday of blockbusters. The Champions League’s ‘Barbenheimer.’

ftbpro_01m5d0q89bcn.title: Where Man City’s Best Players Could End Up If They Are Relegated
ftbpro_01m5d0q89bcn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath4:00 PM EDTWhere’s next? / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesManchester City are stuck in a weird moment of Premier League history, perched in the purgatory between verdict and sanction.

The latest reports suggest the “most likely” punishment to befall City for their financial chicanery (appeal pending) is a “swingeing” (it means ‘very big’) points deduction that would effectively guarantee relegation from the top flight.

Interestingly, there are supposedly no relegation clauses in any City players’ contracts, which will surely make for some awkward conversations with agents in the coming weeks and months if that sanction does come to pass. Still, it’s near-impossible to imagine Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki slumming it in the EFL next season and City’s biggest names will already be planning their emergency exit routes.

Next summer could then feature the biggest exodus of top-level players from one club in a single transfer window since Juventus lost the likes of Zlatan Ibrahimović, Fabio Cannavaro, Patrick Vieira, Lilian Thuram and more in the summer of 2006 post Calciopoli.
But where could City’s top stars end up? Allow us to play match maker.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The two-time Yashin Trophy winner would be a good fit for Bayern. / PA Images via Getty ImagesBayern Munich are probably the only super-club in need of an elite keeper in the near future, with 40-year-old Manuel Neuer’s contract set to expire next summer. Start tailoring some extra long lederhosen for next Oktoberfest now.
A quality center back fast approaching his fourth decade? Sounds like a dream signing for Inter Milan, who can get the band back together alongside Manuel Akanji and John Stones.

Anyone still got Liverpool’s number? / Kate McShane/Getty ImagesIs Liverpool too obvious? With Virgil van Dijk’s contract up next summer it would make sense to dust off the signing posts the social media team quietly archived last year.

Barcelona have been near-faultless in 2026–27, but one (very) minor gripe is over the defensive depth. Adding a top-level operator like Gvardiol strengthens both the left back and center back positions.
The well-trodden path south. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty ImagesNobody hoards Man City academy graduates like Chelsea. It’s destiny.
Putting aside the possibility of a sentimental homecoming to Newcastle, soft-centered Liverpool could really use a midfield enforcer of this calibre.
Rayan Cherki points towards his next club. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesWell, actually yes they have and it’s Rayan Cherki. PSG double dip.

There are vanishingly few landing spots for a player like Fernández in today’s market. The box-crashing midfielder famously told some YouTubers he’d love to live in Madrid, while Real Madrid took the odd step of publicly ruling out a transfer last summer.

Fernández (smartly) didn’t specify which club in Spain’s capital city, however. A move to Atlético Madrid might be the best option to save him from a fate of feeding Ivan Toney in the Saudi Pro League.

An upgrade on Noni Madueke. / Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesDoku has all the jinky, darty, end product-y ingredients Arsenal seem to be missing in attack, and would be an ideal statement signing for the defending Premier League champions.
Like that episode of The Simpsons where the real Seymour Skinnner turns up, we simply pretend none of this ever happened: straight back to Everton. No questions asked.

Unai Emery could definitely use more quality wide options to take his Aston Villa side to the next level after the summer’s fire sale... That is if they can eat the wages without veering perilously towards their own financial issues.

Who wouldn’t want Erling Haaland? / Matt McNulty/Manchester City FC via Getty ImagesBarcelona or Real Madrid? How about a one-off Clásico playoff to decide, with the 6'5" Norwegian perched coquettishly on a plinth in place of a trophy?

In truth, Madrid surely can’t fit another superstar forward into their locker room as much as Florentino Pérez loves to play Galáctico Tetris with his roster. Barcelona did want a striker this summer—until Raphinha morphed into prime Ronaldo.

ftbpro_01m5d2vzds52.title: Why Barcelona Are Wearing 2025–26 Third Kit Against PSG in Champions League
ftbpro_01m5d2vzds52.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas2:50 PM EDTBarcelona’s vibrant 2025–26 third kit will make a comeback when the Catalans face off against PSG.  / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesBarcelona will bring back their 2025–26 neon orange third kit when they visit Paris Saint-Germain in a gargantuan Champions League bout on Tuesday night.

The meeting between the Catalans and the Parisians was instantly circled as arguably the  best game of the 2026–27 Champions League league phase following August’s draw. That sentiment has only intensified since as the reigning back-to-back champions welcome the most in-form team in Europe since the start of the campaign.
Although the stakes aren’t as high, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are expected to deliver fireworks in a match many consider a potential preview of the 2026–27 Champions League final.

But even though Nike manufactured three different Barcelona kits for the new season, the Catalans will wear the “bright mango” 2025–26 third kit that paid homage to the club’s iconic “sextuple” triumph in the winter of 2009.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
Back to the orange kit against PSG 🍊 pic.twitter.com/UxwBgWhvQ0

Despite notable differences between all three of Barcelona’s kits this season, UEFA believes none of them differ sufficiently from PSG’s home blue and red jersey. UEFA’s decision is also influenced by television broadcasters that have the rights to the match, per SPORT.

Barcelona’s home Blaugrana jersey clearly clashes with PSG’s home kit. Barça’s second kit, the black and purple Kobe Bryant-inspired get-ups, were also discarded. Even the teal 2026–27 third kit the Catalans wore for the first and only time in the win against Levante didn’t get the green light from UEFA.

“In order to minimize color clashes,” Article 9 of UEFA’s equipment regulations says. “There must be a clear contrast between each team’s first-choice and second-choice outfield player attires, to the extent that they could be worn by opposing teams in a match.

None of Barcelona’s three 2026–27 kist were given the green light by UEFA for their PSG visit.  / Alex Caparros/Getty Images (Raphinha), Pedro Salado/Getty Images (Lamine Yamal), Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images (Pedri) “If one playing attire comprises predominantly dark colors, the other must comprise predominantly light colors, or if one of the playing attires is hooped, banded, striped or checked, the other must not contain either of the colors of the hoops/bands/stripes/checks.”

PSG’s home kit this season has a lighter shade of blue than their traditional navy base from previous seasons. Although Barcelona’s teal jersey is lighter, UEFA and television broadcasters wanted to avoid any confusion and discarded that option as well.

Last week, PSG were allowed to use their home kit against Manchester City despite Enzo Maresca’s men wearing their traditional sky blue jersey. However, City’s sky blue is lighter than Barcelona’s teal jersey. Plus, the Premier League giants wear white shorts and socks, further adding contrast to the kit-clash to avoid any confusion.

Barcelona last wore their 2025–26 third kit against Basel in preseason.  / Sports Press Photo/Getty Images Barcelona’s “bright mango” kit made its last appearance when Hansi Flick’s side defeated Basel 5–2 in its second-to-last preseason game before the start of the term. At that point, though, this season’s third kit had yet to be unveiled.
Still, you don’t have to go far into the past to find the last time Barcelona were forced to wear a kit from the previous season.

Last year, Flick’s side played their opening two matches of the 2025–26 season donning the bright, lemon-green third kit from the 2024–25 term—famously used when Barcelona fell out of the Champions League in the semifinals against Inter Milan in Flick’s debut campaign.
Like UEFA, it was the powers that be at La Liga who didn’t allow Barcelona to wear any of their new kits in the first two games of last term.

Fast forward to the present and Barcelona have run into the same problem. Still, donning their neon orange kit from last season, the Catalans will hope to make it 12 wins from 12 games across all competitions to start the campaign in a mouthwatering clash against the reigning European champions.

ftbpro_01m5d586zd2q.title: U.S. Soccer Team Shatters World Cup Record, Chases Global Glory
ftbpro_01m5d586zd2q.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner4:19 PM EDTThe U.S. women dominated Samoa to open their World Cup journey.  / Judit Cartiel/FIFA/Getty ImagesU.S. women’s soccer is no stranger to making history. On Monday, the next generation made its mark, thrashing Samoa 17–0 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. It signified the biggest win at any level in World Cup history, surpassing a mark set in 2025 by Morocco, who picked up a 16–0 win over New Caledonia at the men’s edition of the U-17 tournament.

The U.S. youth squad had 10 different goal scorers, led by Maddie DiMaria, who scored six, including the first of the night just 63 seconds into the contest. With her scoring barrage, she became the first to score six times at any World Cup since Manchester City star Erling Haaland scored nine in a single game for Norway at the 2019 U-20 World Cup.

“That means everything; he’s an inspiration,” DiMaria said post-match about following in Haaland’s footsteps. ”Watching his desire and ruthlessness around the box ... to be the next player behind that is just such an honor. I’m super blessed to have all those girls finding me in the right places.”
DiMaria is also the first U.S. player to bag a double hat trick in a competitive match at any age level.

Outside of the goals record and DiMaria’s impressive output, the U.S. peppered the Samoan goal with 58 shots across the 90 minutes. Carolina Reyna, the younger sister of USMNT star midfielder Gio Reyna, and Lordana Paletta each scored braces, in addition to single goals from Mia Corona, Grace Murray, Amari Manning, Deus Stanislaus, Isa Ortiz, Melia Brewer and Gianna Hanf.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Maddie DiMaria (left) scored six goals for the U.S. in the win over Samoa.  / Judit Cartiel/FIFA/Getty ImagesDespite ample success from the U.S. women’s national team, who has won four titles on the senior World Cup stage, the nation has never triumphed at the U-17 edition of the tournament. It has only advanced to the final once in the inaugural 2008 edition, where the team fell to North Korea.

The North Korean program remains the tournament's headlining force, and the country has dominated the women’s youth soccer tournaments, winning the 2024 and 2025 U-17 tournaments as well as the 2016 and 2025 U-20 tournaments. North Korea also advanced to the 2026 U-20 final where it fell to Spain in penalty kicks.

After the confidence-boosting 17–0 win to open the tournament, the U.S. will look to continue its dominance in its next Group E matchup against Kenya, before wrapping up group stage play against China.

The top two teams in each group of the 24-team tournament as well as the four best third-place finishers will advance to the knockout stages, culminating in the Nov. 7 final at the Moulay El Hassan Stadium.
