ftbpro_01m5d5bcsw91.title: Como vs. Man Utd: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5d5bcsw91.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 20, 2026Manchester United travel to the idyllic Como midweek. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Como badge); Kristian Skeie/UEFA (Man Utd logo)Manchester United visit the idyllic site of Como’s Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, aiming to end a six-game winless run on Matchday 3 of the Champions League.
Another tough week for Michael Carrick concluded with some respite, as the Man Utd manager proclaimed his side’s valiant draw at Leeds United marks a “fresh start” for his turbulent outfit.

A 1–1 draw at Elland Road, given their previous two results post-international break, was hardly a bad outcome for the Red Devils. However, Carrick is desperately searching for just his third victory of the season, having inspired the club back into the Champions League with an excellent showing as interim boss during the second half of 2025–26.

As it stands, United risk losing another season. They’re in a state of drift, and things aren’t getting easier. After losing to Atlético Madrid last week, United can ill-afford their domestic slump spilling into Europe.

Como’s highs of Matchday 1 were certainly euphoric, as their Champions League debut ended in an emphatic victory over RB Leipzig. However, Cesc Fàbregas‘s side was brought back down to earth at Feyenoord last time out.
In Serie A, which Fàbregas asserts is the club’s priority, Como moved up to fifth after beating the struggling Fiorentina 3–1 on Sunday.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Michael Carrick is desperate to build on Sunday’s "fresh start". / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesComo are competing with Europe’s elite “five years ahead of schedule,” according to the manager, who has also described the upcoming encounter with Man Utd as a “dream come true” for the burgeoning Italian club.
Fàbregas’s performance by the famous lake has turned heads, and if Como are to perform with the slickness and verve that defined their triumph over Leipzig, United‘s woes will continue.

Carrick at least ensured they were harder to play against at the weekend, yet it remains to be seen whether their gritty draw in West Yorkshire was an anomalous showcase of resilience or, as the manager put it, the start of something new.

Fàbregas was able to offer a couple of players respite at the weekend, including Croatian playmaker Martin Baturina. The 23-year-old recovered from an illness during the international break and was an unused substitute in Florence on Sunday.
Baturina is expected to return to the starting lineup here, working in creative tandem with Nico Paz.

The hosts are somewhat hamstrung in attack, though, given that Moise Kean and Assane Diao are expected to miss out. Diao has scored in both of Como’s league phase outings, so his absence down the right will be keenly felt.
Fàbregas at least as Anastasios Douvikas to mitgate Kean’s injury.
Trevoh Chalobah is also a doubt for the hosts, but there’s an expectation that the former Chelsea man will be fit for Man Utd’s visit.
Como predicted lineup vs. Man Utd (4-2-3-1): Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramón, Valle; Milla, Da Cunha; J. Rodríguez, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas.
Man Utd are depleted in defense. /   Man Utd are in injury strife heading into Wednesday’s fixture, with their issues only worsening since their draw at Leeds.

Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw still haven’t trained with the Red Devils since they picked up knocks against Tottenham Hotspur 10 days ago, and the visitors are also without Benjamin Šeško and Patrick Dorgu.

Ayden Heaven and Lisandro Martínez weren’t involved in training ahead of the match, and there are doubts over Noussair Mazraoui’s status, too. Matthijs de Ligt is in contention to make his first appearance of the season, having finally recovered from a back injury that has sidelined him since last November. De Ligt could come in for the suspended Leny Yoro alongside Harry Maguire in defense.

Bryan Mbeumo should lead United‘s attack without Šeško, while Matheus Cunha could return to the fold. Youri Tielemans may earn some respite despite his impressive showing at the weekend, with Carlos Baleba’s legs needed in the middle of the park. The steady Andrey Santos is poised to sit alongside the Cameroonian in Como.

ftbpro_01m5d855h1xe.title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Villarreal: Reds Recover From Disastrous Start
ftbpro_01m5d855h1xe.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack5:14 PM EDTAlexis Mac Allister (left) scored twice in Liverpool’s victory. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesLiverpool overcame a wretched start to Tuesday’s Champions League encounter with Villarreal and claimed a 4–3 victory over the Yellow Submarine on Matchday 3 of the league phase.
The very worst of Andoni Iraola’s Reds manifested in the opening 35 minutes, as a Villarreal side familiar with Iraola’s ideals took full advantage of a team struggling to perform as instructed.

A Virgil van Dijk mistake was seized upon superbly by Georges Mikautadze after four minutes, and Iñigo Pérez’s visitors ventured toward dreamland on Merseyside when unlikely goalscorer Sergi Cardona doubled their advantage just before the half-hour mark.

Liverpool’s resurgence was crucially ignited before things worsened, and Alexis Mac Allister’s leap from Kostas Tsimikas immediately brought them back into the game. Cardona then cancelled out his strike at the other end by allowing Ronald Araújo to equalize at the back post, meaning the hosts boasted all the momentum entering the second half.

And Iraola’s side suddenly performed with newfound control with the contest level. Their assurance evolved into a final-third spurt, as Mac Allister scored his second and Florian Wirtz opened the floodgates. It seemed like a procession, but Tani Oluwaseyi’s late strike set up a nervy conclusion from nowhere.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Liverpool were terrible without the ball early on. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesIraola was up against a very familiar face in Iñigo Pérez, who was his assistant at Rayo Vallecano and was set to join him at Bournemouth, only to be denied a work permit.
The Liverpool manager said Pérez “knows everything” about him, and it certainly looked as if the apprentice had all the answers to the test at Anfield.

Iraola is defined by his work out of possession, and his Liverpool team is a work in progress. It was evident before Brentford went down to 10 at the weekend, and even more distinct during the opening 35 minutes on Tuesday evening. Pérez’s Villarreal rotated freely in a bid to disorient Liverpool’s man-to-man pressure, and the technical level of the visitors meant they seized upon the Reds’ confusion without the ball.

Villarreal’s second goal typified just how poor Liverpool were to begin this match, with a litany of players late to assignments as the Yellow Submarine went from back to front. Left back Sergi Cardona burst in behind to finish past Alisson.

At that moment, the Anfield faithful feared the worst. Fortunately, Iraola’s facilitation of chaos helped them back into the contest, and the control they asserted after the restart, with the match suddenly all square, showcased their volatility. We saw two completely different Liverpool teams on Tuesday.
Mac Allister’s header got Liverpool going. / Liverpool FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—5.7: Won’t be happy, given the three concessions. Issues laid ahead of him.

RB: Ronald Araújo—7.4: The Uruguayan scored in successive Champions League games, creeping in at the back post to head home from Rio’s teasing delivery left by goalscorer Cardona. Withdrawn at halftime.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—6.5: An imperfect showing from the gifted Frenchman. Jacquet was unnerved by Villarreal’s directness early on.

CB: Virgil van Dijk—5.5: No one was more relieved by Liverpool’s fightback than their captain, whose error directly led to Villarreal’s opening goal. There was much to dislike about the Reds’ display in the opening 35 minutes, and Van Dijk typified their shoddiness.
LB: Kostas Tsimikas—8.4: Few would argue that the Greek international boasts the requisite quality. Still, his set-piece delivery helped Liverpool back into the game.

CM: Trey Nyoni—7.9: There’s plenty for Nyoni to improve without the ball, but he’s ever so easy on the eye in possession. Performs like a mini-Gravenberch, given his ability to resist and roll past pressure.

CM: Alexis Mac Allister—9.3: The Argentine’s best work so far this term has arrived in this competition. Mac Allister’s header inspired his team, and he crashed the box brilliantly to hand Liverpool the advantage after the hour mark.

RW: Rio Ngumoha—8.9: This was a definitive showing from the teenager, who’s had a relatively slow start to the season. Rio is blessed with the skill set of a seasoned winger, and that came to the fore majestically on a sodden Anfield field. Villarreal couldn’t cope with the youngster’s ebullience.

ftbpro_01m5d8hbwg8m.title: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5d8hbwg8m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 20, 2026Bayern Munich are aiming to end Arsenal’s winning run in the league phase. / Visionhaus/Getty Images/Kristian Skeie/UEFAThe second Champions League heavyweight collision of the week arrives in Munich on Wednesday, as two more contenders for Paris Saint-Germain’s crown lock horns.

PSG have proven over the past week, with victories over Manchester City and Barcelona, that they aren’t going away, and Bayern Munich and Arsenal will expect that they’ll have to bypass the back-to-back champions to achieve their ultimate goal this season.

The two teams were semifinalists last time out, having met in the quarterfinals in 2023–24. Bayern progressed as 3–2 aggregate winners on that occasion, but Arsenal got revenge when they met in last season’s league phase, winning 3–1 at Emirates Stadium.

While Bayern are six-time European champions, Arsenal have never before gotten their hands on the trophy. They came ever so close in Budapest, and their trajectory since returning to the competition under Mikel Arteta suggests that this will be their year.

The Gunners’ imperious league phase record has continued at the start of 2026–27, with wins over Napoli and Lille proving simple enough. Bayern, meanwhile, were pegged back by Viking last week after thumping their Norwegian rivals Bodø/Glimt on Matchday 1.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Bayern were beaten by Arsenal in last season’s league phase. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesIt’s Bayern Munich’s high-powered offense versus Arsenal’s stubborn defense. What’s going to give?
The Gunners have yet to concede in this competition, while Bayern have scored 36 times in their previous 10 matches, including seven in two to kick off the league phase.
Arsenal proved in the Champions League final against PSG that they can keep any team quiet, and you’d generally back a strong defense over a firing offense in a clash between the two.

It’ll be so interesting to see how Mikel Arteta approaches the game, with Arsenal certainly having the capacity to smother Bayern and play the game on their terms. Their evolution suggests the Gunners can perform with such conviction at one of Europe’s most imposing amphitheaters, but game state will likely determine the extent of Arsenal’s confidence. An early setback could prove fatal.
There are doubts over whether Vincent Kompany will occupy the home dugout on Tuesday, with assistant Aaron Danks assuming pre-match media duties due to the Belgian’s viral infection.

Kompany may well be picking the team from home, and he’ll have to manage without superstar Michael Olise after his red card last week. Olise will serve a one-match suspension for his act of petulance.
Lennart Karl is the most likely candidate to replace the Frenchman, although Kompany could turn to former Arsenal man Serge Gnabry.

Jamal Musiala is absent for the hosts due to a muscle injury, while Manuel Neuer has been dealing with a foot issue. Jonas Urbig started between the posts in their rout of RB Leipzig on Saturday, and may be called into action again here. Neuer will want to play if he recovers in time, that’s for sure.
Bayern Munich predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Neuer; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Davies; Pavlović, Kimmich; Karl, Gnabry, Díaz; Kane.
Arteta confirmed in his pre-match press conference that Martín Zubimendi is back fit and will be involved in some capacity. The Spaniard won’t start, but could feature off the bench.
There was also a positive update on Piero Hincapié, whom Arteta expects to be available for the game against Everton at the weekend. Riccardo Calafiori will continue at left back in Munich.
Ezri Konsa will continue to deputize for the injured William Saliba alongside Gabriel, while Jurrïen Timber is expected to come back in for Ben White on the right side of Arsenal’s defense.
Noni Madueke has played himself into the team after scoring with Arsenal’s only shot on target in Sunday’s 1–0 win at Nottingham Forest. He’ll replace Eberechi Eze down the left.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Bayern Munich (4-2-3-1): Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice; Saka, Ødegaard, Madueke; Havertz.

ftbpro_01m5d8w59ajc.title: PSG vs. Barcelona Player Ratings: Reigning Champions End Barca’s Perfect Season in Thriller
ftbpro_01m5d8w59ajc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 20, 2026Fabián Ruiz (front) scored the dagger against Barcelona.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesIn one of the best games of the early season, reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain handed Barcelona their first defeat of the season with a brilliant 4–2 win that sends a statement of intent for the rest of European soccer: The Champions League monarchs remain the team to beat this season.
As expected, Barcelona and PSG traded blows in an end-to-end affair from the start. However, it was the hosts who looked the better side and created the most dangerous chances of the first half.

Joan García had done brilliantly to keep the game scoreless but there was nothing he could do to deny Désiré Doué’s perfectly placed shot from the edge of the box 38 minutes in following a dreadful Lamine Yamal turnover.

The second half was an absolute thriller. Xavi Espart equalized for an improved Barça 10 minutes after the restart before Lucas Hernández restored PSG’s lead with a powerful header 72 minutes in. Hansi Flick’s side responded in the 77th minute thanks to a stellar finish from Yamal.

But just when it seemed like Barcelona could complete their comeback, the reigning champions answered and Vitinha scored a wonderful goal just two minutes later. Fabián Ruiz buried the nail in Barcelona’s coffin when he strolled behind João Cancelo at the back post to tap-in an Achraf Hakimi cross.

The pair of European juggernauts delivered an epic clash on Tuesday, but in the end, Luis Enrique’s men showed Barcelona they still have plenty to improve on before they can truly challenge them for the Champions League crown.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Désiré Doué was unplayable against Barcelona.  / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesIn a game that featured some of the biggest stars in world soccer, none shone brighter than Désiré Doué. The winger scored a stellar opener, assisted his team’s second and was the best player on the pitch for his 78 minutes in the game. What a player.

PSG’s dominant midfield trio of João Neves, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz also stole the show against Barcelona. Although the Catalans didn’t have their top-choice midfield at any point during the game, the Parisian engine room showcased why it’s considered the best in the world—even above Barça’s stellar midfield.

Xavi Espart delivered a brilliant performance on the biggest stage of his young career. The La Masia graduate was flawless defensively and scored his maiden Champions League goal. His quality was never in doubt, but he demonstrated he is also capable of producing under immense pressure.

João Cancelo had a night to forget.  / Federico Pestellini/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesBarcelona suffered defensively throughout the game, but nobody had a worse performance than João Cancelo. The fullback’s known defensive deficiencies were exploited and he completely lost Ruiz in the action that sealed the result for PSG. On the ball, he equally struggled in what was his worst performance since returning to Barcelona earlier this year.

Both Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi have had stellar starts to the year, but the pair offered next to nothing on Tuesday. On the other end, Ferran Torres failed to make an impression, missing three clear chances against his former club.

The victory took a toll on PSG, with the trio of Ousmane Dembélé, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia exiting the pitch with injuries. For Barcelona, Dani Olmo also had to be withdrawn with an early injury.
Vitinha won the game for PSG with a rocket of a hit.  / Franco Arland/Getty Images *Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Matvey Safonov—6.3: Brilliantly held his ground one-on-one against Fermín López in the first half, but his positioning could’ve been much better to deny Espart’s and Yamal’s equalizers at his near-post.
RB: Achraf Hakimi—8.2: Essentially disregarded any defensive duties and spent much of the game creating in the final third, leaving Anthony Gordon for Marquinhos to mark. Assisted Ruiz’s dagger.

CB: Marquinhos—6.7: Continues to age like fine wine. He often found himself on an island against Gordon but more than held his own against the speedy winger. In the end, though, the taxing effort resulted in him leaving the pitch with a muscular issue.
CB: Willian Pacho—6.5: Put his body on the line and got kicked in the face in a heroic intervention to deny López.
LB: Lucas Hernández—8.0: Stayed tight on Yamal all game and then crowned his night with a powerful header to score PSG’s second.

CM: João Neves—8.7: After getting dropped against Manchester City last week, the diminutive midfielder looked back to his best in his return to the XI. Had a mouthwatering clash with Pedri all game. Crashed the box constantly and delivered a stellar performance overall.

ftbpro_01m5dcmkxef5.title: Carrick Confirms a Staggering Nine Man Utd Players to Miss Critical Como Clash
ftbpro_01m5dcmkxef5.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 20, 2026Michael Carrick has an injury crisis to navigate. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesManchester United will be severely shorthanded when they take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The Red Devils come into the European bout desperate to snap a dreadful six-game winless run. Michael Carrick’s men have not collected three points since their 4–0 victory over Sabah in their Champions League opener back on Sept. 10.

A win in Italy would raise the spirits at United, but getting past Como will be anything but easy for a team stuck in such a rut. Cesc Fàbregas’s young and exciting squad has a knack for pulling off magical moments, and a Champions League night against one of the biggest clubs in the world is the perfect stage to make a statement.
A devastating injury crisis is also working against United. Carrick gave updates on his sidelined players ahead of the clash, and it was bad news after bad news.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Leny Yoro (center) is suspended for the clash. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesSuspension: One GameUCL Return Date: Nov. 3 vs. RomaBefore we get into all the players stuck in the infirmary, let’s get the obvious out of the way: Leny Yoro is unavailable against Como. The center back was sent off in the team’s 2–0 defeat to Atlético Madrid last time out and is therefore suspended for Wednesday’s match.
Once he serves his one-game ban, Yoro will be free to feature in the Red Devils’ next Champions League clash against Roma on Nov. 3.

Lisandro Martínez is a big loss for United. / Michael Steele/Getty ImagesInjury: ThighPotential Return Date: Oct. 25 vs. BournemouthOne week ago, Lisandro Martínez was going on a tirade after United’s defeat to Atlético Madrid. Now, he will not even be present in Italy to play or comment on the team’s next European bout.

Martínez, who escaped with just a fine for his explosive rant, only lasted 45 minutes against Leeds United at the weekend. Carrick revealed the Argentine suffered a thigh injury, one that is keeping him in Manchester midweek.
“Licha [Martínez] is not too bad, but he is not with us,” Carrick confirmed on Tuesday. “We will have to see if he’s ready for the weekend or not.”

Marcus Rashford remains unfit. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesInjury: HipPotential Return Date: UnknownMarcus Rashford’s return to Manchester United hasn’t exactly gone to plan. The England international does not have a single goal contribution in eight appearances and is dealing with a lingering hip issue from the 2026 World Cup.
He was an unused substitute at the weekend against Leeds and is expected to miss out again against Como.

“Marcus is still feeling a little bit of a hip issue that we are trying to overcome,” Carrick revealed in his pregame press conference. The manager did not specify a recovery timeline for the forward.

Kobbie Mainoo is dealing with an unspecified problem.  / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesInjury: UndisclosedPotential Return Date: Oct. 31 vs. ChelseaThere’s a lot more uncertainty to what’s keeping Kobbie Mainoo sidelined. United have not been forthcoming with his specific injury, but the problem has kept the midfielder out for the team’s last two games, a trend that will continue.
“Kobbie, maybe 10 days or so but that’s not exact,” Carrick said on Tuesday, referring to how much longer the England international will be sidelined.
Should Mainoo recover relatively on schedule, he could be ready in time to face off with Chelsea at the end of the month.

Luke Shaw’s fitness woes are back. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesInjury: UndisclosedPotential Return Date: NovemberIt’s a pretty surefire bet to always expect Luke Shaw to feature on these types of lists. The fullback is as injury-prone as they come, and unsurprisingly returned to the infirmary after just one appearance following the September-October international break.

Shaw’s injury is undisclosed by United. Carrick also did not give a specific recovery timeline; instead, he just said the left back will be out a “little bit longer” than Mainoo, hinting a return in November at the earliest.

Ayden Heaven is still recovering from sickness. / Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesInjury: SicknessPotential Return Date: Oct. 25 vs. BournemouthAdding to United’s defensive woes is Ayden Heaven’s sickness. The center back missed out at the weekend due to the illness and has yet to recover.
Carrick confirmed the bug is keeping Heaven at home midweek. The good news is Heaven should be ready to feature against Bournemouth on Sunday.

ftbpro_01m5dhvbc2j6.title: Nashville SC Capture MLS Supporters’ Shield, Eye Historic Inter Miami Record
ftbpro_01m5dhvbc2j6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ben Steiner3:40 PM EDTSam Surridge opened the scoring. / Tim Austen/MLS/Getty ImagesThere wasn’t much of a Supporters’ Shield race in Major League Soccer in 2026: Nashville SC was always going to win, given the Tennessee side's dominance throughout the season.

On Saturday, the Coyotes clinched the title in historic fashion with a 2-0 win over CF Montréal, leaning on goals from Sam Surridge and Hany Mukhtar to bring them to 70 points after 31 regular-season games.

With the win and the title clinch, Nashville secures the title with three games left in the regular season and can rest its top talents as it prepares for a hopeful long run in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs.

Beyond the feat, Nashville has another within reach—Inter Miami’s all-time regular-season points record. Nashville are averaging 2.26 points per game, and are on pace to eclipse Miami’s 2024 campaign of 74 points and 2.18 points per game.  They could yet reach 79 overall.
Should they break the single-season points record, it would mark the third time in six years that a team has done so, with Miami’s 2024 season surpassing the 2021 New England Revolution.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Nashville SC’s rise under former U.S. men’s national team interim manager B.J. Callaghan has been swift. Last season, they became the first professional team in Tennessee history to win a trophy by lifting the U.S. Open Cup, led by star scorers Mukhtar and Surridge.

This season, after picking up Cristian Espinoza from the San Jose Earthquakes in the offseason and getting improved performances from Brian Schwake between the sticks, they’ve taken massive steps forward—including earning Schwake his first USMNT call in the recent September-October international window.

Now that they've secured the Supporters’ Shield, alongside last year’s U.S. Open Cup, Nashville can turn their attention to the holy grail of domestic soccer, MLS Cup later this fall, where they will hold home advantage all the way through as the highest-ranked team.

The win also clinched Nashville a spot in the Concacaf Champions Cup for next season, and they become the second MLS team after St. Louis CITY SC did so through a U.S. Open Cup win. CF Montréal were denied a berth following surprise Canadian Championship loss to CPL side Forge FC.

Toronto FC's 2017 MLS Cup marks the last time a team went all the way after winning the Supporters' Shield.  / Julian Avram/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesNashville SC’s dominance will now be tested in the MLS Cup playoffs. While Callaghan’s men have cruised through much of the campaign, the intensity and fragility of the playoffs could be more fickle than their regular season success.

No MLS team has won the Supporters’ Shield and MLS Cup since LAFC did so in their double-winning year of 2022. Toronto FC were the team to do it prior to them, with a treble-winning campaign in 2017 when they also lifted the Canadian Championship’s Voyageurs’ Cup. While the Tennessee side won’t have a triple in sight, securing a double would be a historic mark and would come just one year after winning the U.S. Open Cup.

The MLS Cup playoffs begin Nov. 18 with the Wild Card matches, which will determine Nashville’s opponent for the first-round best-of-three series, leading up to MLS Cup on Dec. 15, hosted by the highest-remaining seed in the Supporters’ Shield standings.

ftbpro_01m5exmqyd31.title: PSG Superstar Suffers Torn ACL to Overshadow Thrilling Barcelona Win
ftbpro_01m5exmqyd31.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:15 AM EDTKhvicha Kvaratskhelia will be out for the rest of the season. / Xavier Laine/Getty ImagesParis Saint-Germain have confirmed that Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) during Tuesday’s Champions League victory over Barcelona, which has effectively brought an end to his involvement for the remainder of the season.

The Ballon d’Or contender was in familiarly threatening form at the Parc des Princes, clanking the base of the post early on in a thrilling encounter between two of this season’s Champions League favorites. However, Kvaratskhelia’s night would conclude in agony inside an hour.

A tangle with Barça’s teenage fullback Xavi Espart saw the Georgian winger tumble to the turf. On his way down, Kvaratskhelia got his right studs caught in the grass, forcing a twist in the knee which has left him with one of the most severe injuries a soccer player can suffer.
PSG released a brief bulletin the day after the game confirming the tear and that their No. 7 would undergo surgery this week. The bad news did not end there.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has a long road of recovery ahead of him. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesACL tears used to be career-enders. Major advancement in arthroscopy and refined surgical techniques have spared players that fate and Kvaratskhelia will be back on the pitch again. Just almost certainly not this season.

Players typically take a minimum of nine months to get back into any form of competitive action—which would put his recovery at some point in July 2027, months after the Champions League final. Yet, even at that point the Kvaratskhelia coming back to action will not be the same bundle of jinks and feints which bamboozled Barcelona.

Rodri, who came onto the pitch for Barça just as Kvaratskhelia was being helped onto the sidelines, serves as a recent counterpoint. The former Manchester City midfielder tore his ACL in September 2024 and didn’t make a tentative return until May. Yet, fitness issues would dog Rodri throughout the following campaign, prompting his manager at the time, Pep Guardiola, to warn: “I said to him, and he maybe struggled to understand, it’s not about six, seven, eight months out, then playing and being the Rodri of before.
“No. Do you know when Rodri will be good? At the World Cup with Spain. At the World Cup he will be the best Rodri.”
Rodri was dutifully crowned the best player at the tournament as Spain lifted the title, finally returning to something close to his peak almost two years after his ACL tear.

Ousmane Dembélé was also forced off against Barcelona. / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesIf only Luis Enrique’s sole concern had been Kvaratskhelia. The hobbling forward was joined in coming off the pitch at the same time as Marquinhos, who pulled up clutching his hamstring. In the first half, Ousmane Dembélé had already been forced off holding the back of his leg.

PSG revealed that both players “will remain in treatment for the coming weeks,” which would suggest an absence until at least the other side of the November international break. First-choice left back Nuno Mendes had already been ruled out of the clash with Barcelona thanks to a hamstring problem that was given the same vague timeline.

Enrique operates an extreme injury prevention scheme, resting his stars for most domestic fixtures so they are fresh for the Champions League. Marquinhos, for example, racked up more European appearances (15) than domestic outings (14) last term. While that naturally reduces the workload, there is also the risk of players not being properly prepared for the maximum physical demands required when the occasion does call for it.
Kvaratskhelia’s ACL tear is a cruel freak accident but the proliferation of soft-tissue damage among his teammates could spark some consideration about a different approach going forward.

ftbpro_01m5eyw0tykw.title: Barcelona ‘Report’ PSG to UEFA After Champions League Defeat
ftbpro_01m5eyw0tykw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath7:15 AM EDTBarcelona were not amused by a banner at Parc de Princes. / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesBarcelona are thought to have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for an “offensive” prematch choreography in the stands displayed by fans ahead of their Champions League clash on Tuesday.

Supporters inside the Parc des Princes held up a giant Halloween-themed banner ahead of kickoff which depicted a masked Michael Myers-style figure cutting through the Barcelona badge with a bloody chainsaw, above the words “Parisian-style Massacre.”
Pyrotechnics were then produced from the stands to make it appears as though sparks were flying from the chainsaw as it destroyed the club badge.
Multiple outlets report that Barcelona have filed a complaint with UEFA regarding the display, which they considered to be “overly aggressive and offensive.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

PSG fans are known for their banners and pyrotechnics. /  David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesAccording to La Vanguardia, club delegates also requested the removal of several other banners during the game which featured explicit language against Barcelona.
Meanwhile, L'Equipe reports that the enormous tifo had PSG’s approval—a factor which is thought to have further provoked Barça.

It is said that the reigning Champions League champions denied permission for a banner in the Ligue 1 match against Le Mans that alluded to the social unrest in France, but gave the greenlight for the Halloween-themed one against Barça—even announcing it over the PA system before it was unfurled.

Hansi Flick admitted Barça were beaten by the better team. / Antonio Borga/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesOn the pitch, PSG came out 4–2 winners in the battle between arguably the two biggest contenders for the Champions League trophy this season.

Désiré Doué opened the scoring in the first half before youngster Xavi Espart leveled 10 minutes after the break. An intriguing match exploded with 20 minutes to go, as Lucas Hernández’s header was canceled out by a superb Lamine Yamal solo effort, only for PSG to add two more late on through Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz.

As PSG made it seven victories in a row, the defeat ends Barcelona’s 11-match winning run at the start of 2026–27—though Hansi Flick’s team still remain in the automatic qualifying spots in the league phase of the Champions League, for now.
The Best Barcelona Players of All Time—Ranked. dark. MUST READ. Best Barcelona
Speaking after the match, Flick insisted his team will learn from the very best, but played down the significance of the defeat with such a long way still to go this season.
“It was a fantastic match, from both teams,” he said in his postmatch press conference. “PSG showed they are a better team than us.

“We lost, but we learned. Mistakes happen. But what we’ve done in recent weeks is fantastic. Today wasn’t easy; the players ran a lot and tried to play. What happened after Sevilla, with the recovery, wasn't the best. It's not an excuse. We have to learn. It’s October, and you don’t win titles in October; the Champions League is won in June.”
Next up for Barça is the small matter of El Clásico at Camp Nou on Sunday, with La Blaugrana able to put nine points between themselves and Real Madrid with a win.

ftbpro_01m5f15037g4.title: ‘Wasn’t Right’—Alexis Mac Allister Takes Cutting Swipe at Arne Slot
ftbpro_01m5f15037g4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:50 AM EDTAlexis Mac Allister (left) won the Premier League with Arne Slot before enduring a noticeable dip in form under the same manager. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesLiverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister admitted that “something wasn’t right” under Arne Slot at Anfield last season and hailed the Dutchman’s managerial replacement, Andoni Iraola, for addressing the issue.

Slot could scarcely have enjoyed a better debut season on Merseyside. The calm and understated former Feyenoord boss filled the void left by Jürgen Klopp’s departure and immediately matched his haul of Premier League trophies, guiding Liverpool to just the club’s second league title in 35 years.

However, the good times would not last. A strong run of results to start the 2025–26 season masked some serious flaws, all of which were inextricably linked to the tragic passing of striker Diogo Jota last summer. Liverpool would sink into a historic rut, suffering their worst sequence of results since the times of rationing in the U.K. after the Second World War.

Despite repeatedly stressing the safety of his position, Liverpool shocked many by sacking Slot after he salvaged Champions League qualification. Iraola, who finished one place below the Reds with a Bournemouth roster built on a fraction of the funds, was promptly hired.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

There have been some teething issues under the incoming manager: After prioritizing control, there has been a demonstrative shift toward the chaos which Iraola inspires. It’s not been a straight-line upward trajectory but the general direction of travel is positive.

“Something wasn’t right in the group and this manager changed it,” Mac Allister told Amazon Prime after scoring twice in Tuesday’s 4–3 Champions League victory over Villarreal. “The way we play is different, I don’t like to compare,” he added, while in the process of making a damning comparison.

Alexis Mac Allister scored twice for Liverpool against Villarreal. / Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty Images“When I came here, the owners told me everything is not perfect,” Iraola admitted. The chief concern would have been defensive: Liverpool’s tally of 53 Premier League goals conceded was their worst record in the competition since 1993–94.

Iraola approach to combat that problem is a total revamp of Liverpool’s style. Rather than setting his players up in a clearly defined formation with the brief of covering specifically defined zones of a pitch, the Reds hunt individual opponents in a man-to-man system.

“Now it’s more man-to-man,” Mac Allister explained. “You have to communicate less. Last year, it was more like a zonal thing. I like both. In the national team, we do zonal and it works. It’s about us taking the responsibility. It’s one of the changes. Now it’s easier, you think less but run more.”

This shift from zonal to man-to-man is a common trend across Europe. PSG used it to win the Champions League in successive seasons, gambling on the idea that they would be individually superior to their opponents more often than not. Iraola proved at Bournemouth that singular qualities are not the defining factor in making this approach work, but having players of Mac Allister’s caliber certainly helps.

The affection is mutual. “From the first day, I started seeing something,” Mac Allister said of Iraola. “He’s a nice guy, and the coaching staff is too. We are going in the right direction but we need to work and put in everything. Hopefully, we can win some trophies.”

ftbpro_01m5f1k4xfrm.title: Three Things Barcelona Can Learn From PSG Defeat Ahead of El Clasico
ftbpro_01m5f1k4xfrm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 PM EDTXavi Espart was a bright spark in Barça’s first defeat of the season. / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesBarcelona’s Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday was blockbuster, appointment-viewing stuff. The kind of match usually reserved for the spring months rather than pre-Halloween.
It did not disappoint. There were six goals—several of extremely high quality—and a starting number of 10 Ballon d’Or nominees in the showdown between Europe’s two form teams.

Having a title-worthy game this early felt almost appropriate for Hansi Flick’s team who already boast an over 80% probability of winning La Liga, according to the calculations of Opta’s supercomputer, and can give themselves a nine-point lead over Real Madrid with a victory in El Clásico this weekend.
While Barça ultimately came out on the losing side against Luis Enrique’s defending champions, they can take lessons from the 4–2 defeat.
As manager Hansi Flick said: “We lost, but we learned... We have to learn. It’s October, and you don’t win titles in October; the Champions League is won in June.”
Trophies might not be won now, but the Clásico will be. Here are three key takeaways for Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s meeting with Real Madrid.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Xavi Espart handled the challenge of PSG’s wingers. / Jean Catuffe/Getty ImagesIt’s been some breakthrough for 19-year-old Xavi Espart, the latest starlet from Barça’s class of 2007 to make a splash in the first team.

Trained as a midfielder, Espart has shone at left back for most of this season, before being thrown in at right back after injuries to both Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde, with the unenviable task of stopping Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.
The youngster was not dribbled past once all night, even after Kvaratskhelia was replaced on the hour mark and Désiré Doué took up residence on his flank instead.
“How he defended tonight against the top players PSG have in attack ... just amazing,” Flick gushed postmatch.

With Yan Diomande likely to be lining up on the left for Real Madrid this weekend, Espart suddenly feels like the ideal candidate to deal with the Ivorian’s pace and trickery, while also exploiting the space left in behind the winger.
Espart was as good going forward as backward on Tuesday and showed his La Masia-stamped technical excellence with a fine equalizer early in the second half.

Barcelona missed Rodri’s metronomic qualities. /  David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesIt’s an obvious point to make, but without the world’s best midfield controller, Barcelona lacked... well, control against PSG.

Flick admitted prematch that the upcoming Clásico affected his team selection “a lot,” with Rodri ultimately only introduced after 60 minutes. Afterwards the manager insisted the decision to bench the World Cup-winning captain was “good for us and for him.”

Barça ultimately were made to pay the price for their team selection, with Pedri losing possession three times in the opening five minutes. By halftime PSG had managed 10 shots on target—the most against Barcelona in the Champions League since at least 2003–04, according to Opta.

Elite space-exploiters of Vitinha, João Neves and Fabián Ruiz were able to give the visitors the run around for much of the evening with supreme movement and passing. All three of PSG’s central midfielders ended the night with a goal or assist.

Madrid do not have the same caliber of midfield as PSG—in fact, the engine room balance remains a point of concern for José Mourinho since missing out on Rodri this summer. However, Tuesday’s match showed that even when Barça shade the possession, their midfield can be got at.
Lamine Yamal with another sensational finish 😮‍💨✨ pic.twitter.com/tpSGLfVhqO
It was a game of two halves for Yamal, who scored another superb individual effort but was sloppy in possession leading up to PSG’s opener in the first half.

ftbpro_01m5f4y1h1p9.title: Women’s Ballon d’Or 2026: Ranking the Favorites to Win
ftbpro_01m5f4y1h1p9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Theo Lloyd-Hughes11:00 AM EDTAlexia Putellas of Spain celebrates scoring her team's first goal against the United States.  / Scott Taetsch/USSF/Getty Images One of the biggest nights in global soccer is almost here. On Oct. 26 at the London Palladium, the most esteemed names from around the world will gather for the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.

The last three years have been ruled by one player: Aitana Bonmatí. However, with the 28-year-old missing the second half of the 2025-26 season due to a leg injury, she has not been nominated for this year’s prize.
So, who will rise in place of Bonmatí? That is the question on everyone’s lips.

Players are judged on both team and individual performance between August 3, 2025, and July 19, 2026, during which the Women’s Asian Cup is the only major international tournament. Thus, the UEFA Women’s Champions League (UWCL) will likely be the most high-profile competition that players draw acclaim from. After all, 27 of the 50 judges are based in Europe.

However, Scarlett Camberos, who won the equivalent continental tournament, the Concacaf W Champions Cup, with Mexican side Club América, is a welcome inclusion from further afield. She made history by becoming the first Mexican woman to be nominated for the Ballon d’Or.

30. Tessa Wullaert (Inter Milan/Como, Belgium); 29. Lorena (KC Current, Brazil); 28. Melvine Malard (Manchester United/Chelsea, France); 27. Manaka Matsukubo (NC Courage/Chelsea, Japan); 26. Scarlett Camberos (Club America, Mexico); 25. Momoko Tanikawa (Bayern Munich, Japan); 24. Esmee Brugts (Barcelona, Netherlands); 23. Wendie Renard (Lyon, France); 22. Kerstin Casparij (Manchester City, Netherlands); 21. Selma Bacha (Lyon, France); 20. Cata Coll (Barcelona, Spain); 19. Alex Greenwood (Manchester City, England); 18. Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain); 17. Caroline Weir (Real Madrid/Lyon, Scotland); 16. Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride, Zambia); 15. Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC, United States); 14. Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal, Spain); 13. Vivianne Miedema (Manchester City, Netherlands); 12. Alessia Russo (Arsenal, England); 11. Pernille Harder (Bayern Munich, Denmark)

Temwa Chawinga is a star for the Kansas City Current.  / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters ConnectWere it not for injuries and the 2026 Women’s African Nations Cup (WAFCON) being rescheduled, there’s a good chance Temwa Chawinga would have a better shot. As per usual, the 28-year-old forward is not benefiting from the awards’ use of the European calendar to determine the nomination window.Still, she brings a record-breaking NWSL Shield win with the KC Current and averages nearly a goal or an assist every match. Taking Malawi to the WAFCON final, which qualified them for their first-ever World Cup, is said to count towards next year’s Ballon d’Or.

Yui Hasegawa controls proceedings.  / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters ConnectWidely regarded as one of the best midfielders on the planet, Yui Hasegawa put together one of the best seasons of her career as Manchester City won the English Women’s Super League and FA Cup. In April, Hasegawa also played a crucial role in Japan's win at the Women’s Asian Cup. What will stop Hasegawa from being more in contention is her lack of UWCL soccer during the 2025-26 season, as well as her more modest statistical haul (six goals and seven assists). Of course, as a deep-lying midfielder, it’s just part of her role to start attacks lower down the pitch, be press-resistant and control the tempo. While coaches will laud a player like Hasegawa, voters may miss out on what makes her such a dynamo.

Ewa Pajor loves to find the back of the net.  / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty Images If there’s one thing you can always count on, it’s Ewa Pajor scoring goals. The Barcelona striker didn’t quite match her 2024-25 haul of 43 goals in 45 matches, but with 34 in 46 in 2025-26, she isn’t too far off her extraordinary high standard in this year’s contest.What could help Pajor’s case this year is Barcelona going one better than in 2025 in the UWCL, defeating Lyon 4-0 in this year’s final. The 29-year-old Pole was named player of the match in that triumphant final, netting two goals and also adding an assist. However, despite her goalscoring exploits, she remains the least high-profile player in the Barcelona contingent.

Caroline Graham Hansen delivers year after year.  / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty Images Another member of the quadruple trophy-winning Barcelona team. Caroline Graham Hansen brings more skill and individual brilliance to the foray rather than just goalscoring. She has a wonderfully balanced stat line of 17 goals and 16 assists. This proves she is just as good at finishing off an attack as creating chances for her teammates.In terms of individual profile, Graham Hansen is a more well-known figure than Pajor. She has dominated Europe for nearly a decade. That could be enough for her to pull in more votes than many others.

Patri Guijarro keeps everything ticking over in midfield.  / Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/Getty Images Often regarded as the heartbeat of both Barcelona and Spain, Patri Guijarro, like Hasegawa, will push the way in which voters categorize greatness. Will setting the tempo, scanning the pitch and keeping the ball be valued in the same way as game-defining goals? Although a foot injury did cost Guijarro 12 weeks of action, her absence may only have increased the appreciation of her game.In addition to all her glory with Barcelona, what could give Guijarro the edge is her national team dominance with Spain, which topped their World Cup qualifying Nations League group over England. The Barcelona midfielder was on the losing side just once during the entire 2025-26 campaign (a 1-0 loss for Spain against England at Wembley). She would get revenge with a virtuoso performance in the 4-0 win for Spain in the reverse fixture.

Melchie Dumornay’s stock may be affected by Lyon’s thumping defeat in the Champions League final.  / Franco Arland/Getty Images Had Lyon not been thrashed 4-0 by Barcelona in the UWCL final, then perhaps Melchie Dumornay would have a real shot at the Ballon d’Or. The extraordinary attacking midfielder/forward hybrid was one of the most electric players last season, netting 21 goals and 12 assists in just 36 matches, including a memorable hat trick in the French league final.Another player who will have to balance absences from key moments with sensational match-winning moments. In particular, missing the first leg of the UWCL semifinal against Arsenal, before then storming back with a defining performance in the second leg, where the London team couldn’t handle her. Playing her international soccer for Haiti, who did top the first round of their Concacaf World Cup qualifying group, will likely be missed by the voters.

Klara Bühl was a standout for Bayern until injury struck.  / EyesWideOpen/Getty ImagesIf Klara Bühl played for Barcelona, perhaps she could win the Ballon d’Or. For now, it feels unlikely that the German winger can go all the way despite having the single best season of her career. Across 37 matches, the 25-year-old scored 10 goals and assisted 23, while showing off tremendous skill and crossing ability for both club and country. An ill-timed injury at the time of the UWCL quarterfinals interfered with what could have been a record-breaking individual season for assists.Three domestic trophies with Bayern Munich probably won’t be enough to push her any further than the top five, but she is an attacking player on the rise who has plenty of admirers across Europe for her consistency, close control and vision. Should voters look beyond Barcelona, Bühl feels like an outside bet to grab attention.

Claudia Pina’s incredibly important to Barcelona.  / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesClaudia Pina was the second-highest-scoring Barcelona player last season with 32 goals, trailing Pajor’s total of 34. With nine assists, Pina was just one goal contribution behind her Polish teammate (who created eight goals). When it comes to volume and slickness on the ball in the attack, Pina is right up there.Like Bühl’s penchant for whipping in beautiful passes, what gives Pina an edge is the quality of her shooting, especially from long range. Playing for Spain will help Pina’s case, as the number-one-ranked team in the world continues to dominate the international landscape. But it feels like Pina could get more votes just for the quality of her goals rather than some other achievements. She is one of the most elite strikers in soccer in the world right now.

Khadija Shaw loves to score goals.  / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesFor the last three years, Khadija Shaw has been considered the best goalscorer in the English Women’s Super League. But what made last season so special was Shaw finally being able to add trophies to her personal accolades at Manchester City—a league and FA Cup double was secured as the 29-year-old scored 36 goals in 36 games, while also adding 10 assists.Like her City teammate Hasegawa, a lack of UWCL soccer will likely cool some voters from putting Shaw at the top of the list. Even though she has big moments, like her brace to snatch an improbable extra-time comeback against Chelsea in the FA Cup semifinals, it feels like more tried-and-tested European names will jump ahead of what many will say is the best striker on this list. Similarly, her national team exploits with Jamaica will not boost her chances with the judges all that much.

Alexia Putellas is favorite to continue Spain’s dominance.  / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters ConnectThis year’s Ballon d’Or feels like Alexia Putellas’s to lose. 2025-26 was a revival year for the midfielder who previously lifted the Ballon d’Or in both 2021 and 2022. With Bonmatí injured, the former Barcelona player, who moved to London City Lionesses this past summer, was allowed to rise back into a talismanic role as her hometown club lifted four trophies and conquered Europe.Putellas has the biggest brand and name recognition on this list, and that will help a considerable amount. So will her statistical dominance, as she led the UWCL in combined goals and assists with 14. Evolving into a captain for Spain as they continue to boss Europe will only increase her chances of being viewed as the best in the world. Last season truly was a vintage year for Putellas, where she was allowed to re-demonstrate her exceptional ability to see the field, dictate the game and conjure magic to unpick opponent’s defenses.For Putellas to return to her best in her final season with Barcelona (for now) will also add an extra narrative piece to this Ballon d’Or. The most memorable moment was her performance in the 4-2 UWCL semifinal win over Bayern Munich, where she scored two goals. As she left the pitch, she stepped away from Camp Nou one last time as royalty in Catalonia. There is a reason she is nicknamed La Reina after all.

ftbpro_01m5f73qpxs6.title: Ten Hag Comes Out Swinging on Sancho, Rashford, Garnacho & More
ftbpro_01m5f73qpxs6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:10 AM EDTThe bubble burst for Erik ten Hag at Manchester United. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesErik ten Hag had so much to get off his chest about his tumultuous Manchester United tenure that it could not be contained to just one explosive interview.

After tearing apart Cristiano Ronaldo’s work ethic, blaming Real Madrid’s cast-offs for the “toxic culture” at the club and fretting over his many missed transfers, Ten Hag still had so much more unloading to do.
The Dutch boss would belatedly finish his delayed debrief in a second interview with The Athletic which offered even more insight into his calamitous reign.

Jadon Sancho (right) did not have his best moment under Erik ten Hag. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesJadon Sancho was always a point of controversy during Ten Hag’s tenure. The expensively acquired winger would eventually be shunned from first-team duties after refusing to apologize for publicly calling out his manager. However, just two days before the “scapegoat” debate unfolded, Sancho caused Ten Hag an even bigger issue.
The Dutch boss took the surprising approach of blaming Sancho for inadvertently forcing United to waste more than $115 million (£86 million) on the acquisition of Antony.

“There came up a problem because Sancho didn’t want to play on the right side; he said that,” Ten Hag explained. “Which was very weird; he played often on the right. He said he felt more comfortable on the left. So there we had an issue, and we were late.”

United hastily plowed forward with an eye-watering agreement which never came close to being value for money. During his two-and-a-half underwhelming years in Manchester, Antony mustered 12 goals in 96 appearances.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag never had it easy. / David Fitzgerald/Sportsfile/Getty ImagesAccording to Ten Hag, the real problems behind Manchester United’s dire 2023–24 campaign, which saw them slip to eighth, their worst top-flight finish in 34 years at the time, began before Antony had even been signed.

“The tour was so much expectation on the players,” Ten Hag fretted about a preseason schedule spent zig-zagging across the United States. “We got exhausted from all the kilometers. We started in New York, we played in Houston, we played in Vegas, went back, we gave them a couple of days off, and then we didn’t train proper tactical and physical work for 10 days because they were totally killed ... We were never fit.”

For a manager as dedicated to the details as Ten Hag—this is a man, after all, who emailed his players telling them what color socks to wear to team meals—having such a large part of preseason taken out of his control was always going to grate.

It didn’t help United’s players either. Injuries forced Ten Hag to constantly reshuffle his squad. Only two outfielders made more than 30 Premier League starts for the Red Devils that season. “So it’s almost impossible to get automatism in,” he lamented. “But I know at the top, it’s about the result.”

Alejandro Garnacho (left) played some of his best soccer under Erik ten Hag. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesRalf Rangnick gave Alejandro Garnacho his senior debut but it was Ten Hag who saw the mercurial winger blossom into one of United’s brightest talents. During the Dutch boss’s second (and final) full season at Old Trafford, a 19-year-old Garnacho cracked double digits for club goals while amassing an impressive 50 appearances. Little more than two years later, Garnacho is riding Aston Villa’s bench. “I regret where he is now,” Ten Hag admitted.

“He’s a character, you have to manage him, but I had a strong connection with him,” Ten Hag gushed. “But it’s also up to him, of course, but he needs a coach, a particular coach, who will give him trust, who will give him love. He needs the love, definitely. But he’s an amazing player. What’s so special about him is he can run all day, high volume at really high speed, all game, back and forward.

“Sometimes his head is not on defending. So mentally, his mindset, you have to make sure he is focused and disciplined and does the job every transition, but he’s capable of doing it and attacking-wise he can go forward and do incredible things, making dribbles, finishing. He can do the final pass, but sometimes he’s a little bit selfish.”

Gary Neville has a voice with weight when it comes to Manchester United. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesThe job of playing for Manchester United is unlike most other clubs. Not only do you have to deal with the all the stresses of the modern game, but his every decision is ruthlessly dissected by a bevy of former players who now serve as prominent media personalities in the sport. The likes of Gary Neville and Rio Ferdinand, two trophy-laden defenders, were name-checked by Ten Hag.
“Sometimes it’s difficult for players,” the Dutch coach admitted. “Some of them get affected by it, get annoyed by it. They achieved massive successes.
“But also, they can help the club more, help the players more. There should be two ways that they support it. But I think always the thing you most love, you most criticize.”
Ten Hag had no issues himself with the talking heads. “It’s everywhere the same; they always want to protect their legacies,” he shrugged.

“It’s no different than Bayern Munich or Ajax; they do the same. But they are [part of United’s] history, and they do not always know what’s going on. Football evolves. For United, it’s clear: they had great contributions, they achieved massive results, trophies for the club and for themselves, so I respect them.”

ftbpro_01m5fa4z57zd.title: Yamal Equals Long-Standing Mbappe Champions League Scoring Record
ftbpro_01m5fa4z57zd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath10:30 AM EDTLamine Yamal continues to break records at every turn. / Ibrahim Ezzat/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesLamine Yamal placed his name alongside Kylian Mbappé’s in the Champions League history books  on Tuesday night after netting in Barcelona’s 4–2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

What ultimately proved a disappointing end to Barcelona’s unbeaten start to the season still had positives on a personal level for Yamal. The 19-year-old Ballon d’Or nominee produced another superb solo strike in the second half of the Champions League showdown, putting on the after-burners to power past makeshift left back Warren Zaïre-Emery before finishing past Matvey Safonov from an improbable angle.

With his strike, Yamal became the first player from any of Europe’s top five leagues to register at least 10 goals and 10 assists in 2026–27. As a result, he has been involved in 40% of Barça’s 50 goals so far this season.
Prior to the PSG game, Barcelona manager Hansi Flick declared his red-hot winger “the best player in the world right now.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
Lamine Yamal with another sensational finish 😮‍💨✨ pic.twitter.com/tpSGLfVhqO
Yamal’s goal in Paris on Tuesday was his 13th in the Champions League, drawing him level with Kylian Mbappé for the most in the competition as a teenager.
Mbappé—one of Yamal’s strongest competitors for the Ballon d’Or later this month—scored 13 times in 23 appearances for Monaco and PSG. Yamal, by contrast, achieved his total in 36 outings.
However, as he does not celebrate his 20th birthday until next July, he will surely become the outright leader very soon.
Looking further ahead, the Barcelona superstar needs eight goals to become the highest scorer before 21—a record currently held by Erling Haaland.

Lamine Yamal goes head to head with Kylian Mbappé this weekend. / Ibrahim Ezzat/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFollowing a first defeat in 2026–27, Barcelona enter a tough run of games with Real Madrid next up in the season’s first Clásico on Sunday, Oct. 25. It’s another fixture Yamal is used to setting records in.

The teenager is both the youngest player to feature and score in the Clásico, making his debut in the iconic match at the age of just 16 years and 107 days old. Exactly a year on, he scored the third in a crushing 4–0 victory at the Bernabéu to make history.
In a total of nine games played against Barcelona’s great rivals, Yamal has three goals and two assists to date.

Though voting is already concluded, one of the many narratives of Sunday’s match will be the showdown between two Ballon d’Or frontrunners: Yamal and Mbappé. Both superstars have campaigned extensively for soccer’s most coveted individual prize in the weeks leading up to the ceremony, which will take place in London the day after the Clásico on Oct. 26.
“I honestly believe there are two of us who are the best in the world, and this year I deserve it because of what I’ve won,” Yamal told Spanish broadcaster Movistar+ last month.

ftbpro_01m5fak74k1m.title: Liverpool Trailblazer Matches Remarkable Lamine Yamal, Cristiano Ronaldo Record
ftbpro_01m5fak74k1m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray11:30 AM EDTLiverpool boast one of soccer’s finest prodigies. / Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty ImagesLiverpool were indebted to 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha’s remarkable, history-equaling performance for their third successive Champions League victory on Tuesday.

The Reds were trailing by two goals come the half-hour mark of their league phase game against Villarreal at Anfield, yet Ngumoha’s brilliance helped them turn the tide and eventually run out 4–3 winners.

The youngster was one of few to shine in a red jersey during an unconvincing triumph and deservedly claimed UEFA’s official Player of the Match award courtesy of his stellar showing—which yielded assists for Ronald Araújo’s equalizer and Alexis Mac Allister’s second strike of the game.
The turbo-charged winger proved a constant thorn in Villarreal’s side and joined an esteemed list of record-setters en route to an important victory.

According to Opta, Ngumoha became just the fourth teenager to ever complete seven or more dribbles in multiple Champions League matches since records began in 2003–04, matching a feat managed by only Lamine Yamal, Cristiano Ronaldo and Arjen Robben previously.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Ngumoha completed seven dribbles during Liverpool’s thrilling 6–3 win away at LASK last week and actually bettered that tally against Villarreal, managing nine before being withdrawn in the 74th minute.
Opta’s Michael Reid also revealed Ngumoha matched a 28-year Liverpool record by becoming the youngest player to notch two assists in a single match for the club since Michael Owen back in 1998.
Not only that, Ngumoha also stole Owen’s record as the youngest player to ever assist a goal for Liverpool in a European competition.
Nobody can better Ngumoha’s 7.4 dribbles completed per 90 in the Champions League this season, either.

The sky is the limit for Ngumoha. / Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport/Getty ImagesLiverpool have long known they boast one of world soccer’s most precocious talents and Ngumoha appears to be improving with each passing match. However, after enjoying a breakout 2025–26 campaign, he’s been forced to adapt to a new position this season.
After being exclusively deployed on his preferred left flank, Andoni Iraola has shunted Ngumoha to the right-hand side to help cover for Liverpool’s lack of natural options in the role.
Unsurprisingly, Ngumoha has thrived despite his tender age, and he’s pleased with the progress he’s made since switching sides.

Asked about his positional tweak after the Villarreal victory, the England international responded: “It’s helping me a lot in training, the gaffer, all the coaching staff, all the players believe in me. Slowly and slowly I’m getting better on the right.”
He added: “It’s up there with one of the best I’ve played, I think. I enjoyed myself out there. The team helped me as well a lot. I enjoyed today.

“Whenever I get the ball and there’s an opportunity to go one-on-one or two-on-one sometimes, by all means I’ll do it. I believe in myself to do it. The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”

ftbpro_01m5fcsfbv6n.title: USMNT Given Major Injury Boost Ahead of Concacaf Nations League Quarterfinals
ftbpro_01m5fcsfbv6n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:00 PM EDTMauricio Pochettino will have his pick of strikers. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team will have one more striker available in its ranks for next month’s competitive action, as Ricardo Pepi is nearing recovery from a muscular injury he suffered last month.

Pepi sank to the ground, grimacing in pain, just eight minutes into club side PSV Eindhoven’s clash with Eredivisie foe FC Twente on Sept. 20. Although he was able to gingerly walk off the pitch and later called the injury “just a minor setback,” he was ultimately unfit to report to the USMNT’s September-October international camp and was replaced on the roster by striker Damion Downs.

After a month on the sidelines—missing the USMNT’s four friendlies as well as four club matches, including two Champions League games, Pepi is almost back to full health. He could be available as soon as Sunday for the battle with Dutch giants Feyenoord, according to PSV manager Peter Bosz.

His recovery timeline aligns with the USMNT’s November international camp, which kicks off Nov. 9 and concludes with the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie against Haiti. The first leg is on Nov. 14 in Kingston, Jamaica, and the second leg is on Nov. 17 in Cincinnati.

Ricardo Pepi suffered a muscular injury last month. / Dijks Media/MB Media/Getty ImagesShould Pepi be called up, it will signify a massive opportunity for the 23-year-old to re-establish himself within the pecking order.

When initially named to the September-October roster, he was the only 2026 World Cup forward that manager Mauricio Pochettino included, meaning he would have likely started the majority of the four matches. His abrupt absence, though, made way for teenage sensations Julian Hall and Justin Ellis to stake their claims to the starting lineups. The two had five goals collectively, making Pepi, who hasn’t scored for the USMNT since 2024, a sincere afterthought.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Patrick Agyemang tore his Achilles in the spring. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesAlthough Pochettino has reinforced his striker ranks with Hall and Ellis, he will be grateful for the return of Pepi, given the long-term injuries some of the other top strikers in his player pool have experienced recently.

Patrick Agyemang devastatingly suffered a serious Achilles tendon injury in April, just weeks before Pochettino named his final World Cup roster. After playing in both of the USMNT’s March friendlies, the Derby County star had seemed likely to earn a tournament spot. Agyemang is “on course” to return to the pitch in November, but not until “after the international break,” according to Derby manager John Eustace.
“It’s important we don’t rush him back,” Eustace told reporters last week. “Just having him training with us at the moment is brilliant. He is with the rehab team, but he is hitting all the markers.”

Haji Wright, who served as the USMNT’s third-string striker this summer, is also not expected to return to the pitch until next month, having suffered a “very serious” quad injury during preseason for Premier League side Coventry City.

“Haji won’t be back until November at best and I don’t want to put pressure on it because it’s an awkward injury,” the club’s manager Frank Lampard told reporters earlier this month, most likely ruling him out of the upcoming international window.

Although Pochettino will be without Agyemang and Wright, he has seen the return of World Cup star Folarin Balogun. Post-tournament, the 25-year-old was dealing with “a small issue in one of his legs,” according to Pochettino; however, the striker has already returned to the pitch for club side Monaco, featuring off the bench in the last three Ligue 1 matches. Whether or not he will be back to his best come November, though, remains to be seen.

ftbpro_01m5fd4tp08t.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Flops for Al Nassr After Erik ten Hag Takedown, Portugal Ban
ftbpro_01m5fd4tp08t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath12:30 PM EDTRonaldo missed a penalty against Neom. / Mohammed Saad/Anadolu/Getty ImagesA frustrating period for Cristiano Ronaldo continued as he failed to hit the target with a penalty and missed an open goal during Al Nassr’s 1–0 win over Neom in the Saudi Pro League on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old was handed a spot kick right on the stroke of halftime after teammate João Felix was brought down inside the box. Ronaldo, however lashed his penalty wide—missing the chance to edge closer to his much-publicized career target of 1,000 goals.

Things got worse for Ronaldo later on as he managed to volley Sadio Mané’s teed-up ball skywards from just a couple of yards out with the goal gaping. That chance was given an xG rating of 0.83, while the five-time Ballon d’Or winner finished the match without a single shot on target from six taken.
Al Nassr, who sit third in the Saudi Pro League standings after nine games, still won the match thanks to a second-half strike from Felix.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Cristiano Ronaldo got nothing going on Tuesday night. / Mohammed Saad/Anadolu/Getty ImagesStat

Cristiano Ronaldo was let off lightly with his Portugal punishment. / Kristian Tuxen Ladegaard Berg/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesRonaldo’s disappointing evening with Al Nassr follows a difficult week for the superstar striker.

The Pro League outing was Ronaldo’s first appearance since the news of his provisional suspension by Portugal after leaving the team over a dispute with manager Jorge Jesus during the last international break.
On Monday, the Portuguese FA hit Ronaldo with a fine of just €255 ($286) and a 30-day suspension—backdated so Ronaldo can re-join the team camp for the upcoming Nations League matches in November.

The light punishment suggests there are plans to quickly reintegrate Ronaldo into the Portugal setup and smooth over relations between player and manager, but doubts remain over who is calling the shots with the national team.

Ronaldo storming out of the Portugal setup and the subsequent fallout marked contrast to his great rival Lionel Messi’s tearful final Argentina match. The 39-year-old was given a heartfelt sendoff in his 208th and final game for his country as the Ronaldo drama unfolded half the world away.
Ronaldo is highly likely to still achieve his target of 1,000 goals, but his short-term Portugal future remains unclear, with successive managers grappling with how to manage the aging superstar.

Ten Hag didn’t hold back with his thoughts on Ronaldo. / Geoff Caddick/AFP/Getty ImagesMeanwhile, former Man United boss Erik ten Hag hit out at Ronaldo’s attitude in an explosive interview with The Athletic.

The Dutchman, who was in charge when Ronaldo sensationally left United in acrimony at the back end of 2022, claimed the forward did not want to train at the level required and encouraged his teammates to go easy during the manager’s sessions.

“He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said. “Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in.

“Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score.’ He was not capable to do this. It’s the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he’s exhausted. But he couldn’t. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn’t prepare himself.
“Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team.

“He was telling the players, ‘Save your legs at the training.’ I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.”

ftbpro_01m5fdfgpxxm.title: ‘Let’s See’—Andoni Iraola Responds to Liverpool Interest in Mexican Wonderkid
ftbpro_01m5fdfgpxxm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray1:30 PM EDTLiverpool are reportedly eager to sign Mexican teenager Gilberto Mora. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Iraola), Omar Vega/Getty Images (Mora)Andoni Iraola refused to pour cold water on intensifying transfer rumors linking Mexican sensation Gilberto Mora with a move to Liverpool.

The 18-year-old has risen to prominence with Tijuana in his homeland and bolstered his profile with four appearances for co-hosts Mexico at last summer’s World Cup. Naturally, the attacking midfielder’s future is the subject of significant discussion.

Mora has been strongly linked with a move to Spain, where he would most likely join either Barcelona or Real Madrid, but there is understandable interest from Premier League giants. Liverpool are among the English clubs linked with the teenager.
When speaking with TNT Sports Mexico after Liverpool’s 4–3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday, Iraola was quizzed about his side’s interest in Mora. The Spaniard didn’t rule out a future deal.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
“Let’s see, not only because of what he’s doing,” Iraola replied. “There are times when you ask me about players, but I can’t talk about players who aren’t ours, right? In the end, there’s respect.
“And there has to be respect between clubs and well, if you’ll allow me, I have my opinion, obviously, but I prefer not to comment, not about players who aren’t from Liverpool.”

The Reds have reportedly offered as much as $50 million for the youngster, as per TUDN’s David Faitelson, sparking hope among Liverpool supporters that a deal for one of world soccer’s most coveted talents could be on the cards.
While Iraola didn’t endorse a move for Mora, his coy response will allow fans to keep believing.

Mora has a long, long list of admirers. / Oscar Fuentes/Jam Media/Getty Images“I think Gilberto is very talented and has a bright future ahead of him. He just needs the right guidance. I believe he could fit in with any team.” Those were the enthusiastic words of recently appointed Mexico manager Rafael Márquez, who knows Mora better than most.

The 5'6" starlet boasts an extensive list of admirers for good reason. A diminutive frame may dissuade some suitors, but it’s his low center of gravity that allows him to twist and turn on a dime, before unpicking opposition defenses with his technical class and stellar passing range.

Mora is a steady goalscorer, too. Five goals in seven Liga MX appearances from the No. 10 position this season attest to that—albeit four were penalties—while he’s managed 15 in total across 62 outings for Tijuana.
Versatility is another of his major strengths, with Mora comfortable operating off the left wing as well as through the center.
Liverpool don’t particularly need extra bodies in attacking midfield or at left wing, but a potentially generational talent like Mora might change their mind.
