ftbpro_01m5fg5nxpmf.title: Barcelona’s Champions League Misery Made Worse by Significant Injury Blow
ftbpro_01m5fg5nxpmf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas2:00 PM EDTInjuries are starting to pile up for Hansi Flick.  / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesBarcelona endured their first defeat of the season against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday, but they also lost Dani Olmo for a month after tests confirmed he suffered an adductor injury.
The Catalans fell to a painful 4–2 defeat against the reigning holders  in the Champions League on Tuesday night, ending a brilliant run of 11 consecutive wins to start the 2026–27 season.
Olmo featured from the start for Barcelona at the Parc des Princes and looked sharp until he limped off the pitch in the 27th minute while the game was still scoreless.

Injuries have been synonymous with Olmo over the years even before he landed in Catalonia in the summer of 2024. After enjoying a mostly injury-free 2026, the playmaker is now bound for another considerable spell on the sidelines.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Dani Olmo (bottom) injured himself after colliding with Vitinha.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesWhile fighting for a loose ball, Olmo injured himself when he collided with Vitinha and landed awkwardly after taking a significant blow to the adductor. The 28-year-old stayed on the ground for a prolonged period until he exited the pitch gingerly and was replaced by Fermín López.
Additional tests carried out in the following hours revealed the extent of his injury, as Barcelona released a statement confirming Olmo will be out until at least the November international break.

“Tests carried out confirm that Dani Olmo is suffering from an injury to his left adductor muscle as a consequence of a collision with an opponent during the game against Paris Saint-Germain,” the statement said. “The player is expected to be out for around a month.”

The attacking midfielder will be sidelined during a busy portion of the campaign, with marquee La Liga and Champions League fixtures on the schedule over the next four weeks. The first match Olmo will miss is none other than the first El Clásico of the season when Real Madrid visit the Camp Nou on Sunday—but other big games also loom on the horizon.

Fermín López should get the bulk of Dani Olmo’s minutes. / Pedro Salado/Getty Images With Olmo on the sidelines, López should get an extended run of games starting as the attacking midfielder in Flick’s preferred 4-2-3-1 formation. The Spaniard has competed with Olmo for the starting job at the position over the past two years, with Flick often riding with the hot-hand.

However, given how exposed Barcelona looked out of possession against PSG, with their midfield double-pivot unable to contain the Parisians in transition, Flick could be tempted to tweak his set-up to a more traditional 4-3-3.

Pedri and Rodri have been the most utilized midfield pairing, but now that Frenkie de Jong is back from injury, the German boss could deploy a midfield trio, especially against the high-caliber opponents the Catalans will face in the coming weeks.

If Flick wants to stick to his 4-2-3-1 formation, another option could be to start Lamine Yamal in the No. 10 role. The teenager has operated more centrally than ever early in the season, and Flick might test him at a new position with Olmo sidelined, opening the door for Karim Adeyemi or even López to get minutes on the right wing.

Regardless of what Flick decides, Olmo’s injury is significant given he was coming off some of his best minutes of the season and bagging his first goal of the term. Plus, Barcelona’s attacking depth could be tested during a busy period.
Olmo joins Eric García and Roony Bardghji in the treatment room, with Barcelona hoping Jules Koundé can return for El Clásico after suffering a minor injury that sidelined him against PSG.

ftbpro_01m5fghn3xy7.title: ‘Absolute Power’—The Ultimate Threat Hanging Over Man City Revealed
ftbpro_01m5fghn3xy7.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:15 PM EDTMan City have been publicly warned over possible repercussions following their guilty verdict. / Kate McShane/UEFA/Getty ImagesThe Independent Football Regulator (IFR) could force Manchester City’s owners to sell the club after they were found guilty of financial misconduct across a nine-year period.

An independent commission ruled that the Cityzens had created “sham” contracts to artificially inflate their revenue and reduce costs by over £900 million ($1.2 billion dollars today) between 2009 and 2018.
The eight-time Premier League champions are now appealing the verdict, with the deadline for its outcome currently scheduled for Jan. 23, 2027.
If City’s appeal is unsuccessful, then they will be handed their long-awaited punishment—and things could get even worse for them thereafter.
According to David Kogan, chair of the IFR, his organization boasts “absolute power” to force City’s owners to sell the club should they be deem it an appropriate sanction.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
“We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” Kogan told The Rest Is Football podcast.
When asked if City, who are majority-owned by the Abu Dhabi United Group, could resist a sale, Kogan replied: “No, no, no. We’ve got absolute power to do so.”

However, no decision will be made until the appeal has been heard, with Kogan adding: “I am not going to get pushed into making any judgment on this until we’ve seen all of those questions being answered. Then we will have to decide whether we’re going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we’re going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake.”

Javier Tebas has been highly critical of Man City. / Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images For SportelAmong those to have been most publicly critical of City following their guilty verdict is La Liga president Javier Tebas, who has recently demanded “justice” for the Premier League and the rest of European soccer.
Tebas, who recently hit the headlines for comparing Real Madrid with Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels, refused to mince his words when speaking at the SPORTEL business conference in Monaco.

“I’m interested in understanding how this story will end. It is important for both the Premier League and the European football ecosystem,” Tebas said. “There are people who have had to leave UEFA because of Manchester City, so I think we need justice for the Premier League, for Europe and UEFA.”
Speaking about the matter at the FIFPRO performance summit last month, Tebas also demanded the strongest possible punishment for the Cityzens.
“I don’t know the exact rules, but I believe it should be the strictest punishment in the Premier League regulations regarding this matter,” the La Liga chief exclaimed.

“It should be a punishment intended to set an example. This isn’t a matter of a father and his children—it is a punishment to ensure rules are followed. And violating the rules for over 10 years—no matter how minor the infractions—is a very serious matter.
“Therefore, it has to be a severe punishment for the non-compliance. Not just to set an example, but because the rules were broken.”

ftbpro_01m5fj5fkeqf.title: La Liga Chief Javier Tebas Stands Ground After Real Madrid Nazi Comparison
ftbpro_01m5fj5fkeqf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:45 PM EDTReal Madrid have demanded Tebas’s resignation over the incident. / Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images/SportelLa Liga president Javier Tebas refused to apologize for drawing comparison between the communication strategy of Real Madrid and the “propaganda techniques” employed by Nazi Germany.
Last week, Tebas hit out at Real Madrid for aping the approach of Nazi Minister of Propaganda Joseph Goebbels by pushing claims of bias against the club through the media.

Against the backdrop of the ongoing Negreira case, Madrid, its in-house media channel and various sympathetic media sources have been particularly vocal on refereeing decisions, unfavorable scheduling and more so far this season, provoking Tebas—a long-time adversary of Florentino Pérez and Los Blancos’s higher-ups—into an eyebrow-raising statement.

Part of the 64-year-old’s social media post read: “Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing. Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

“That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative. The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase.”

Real Madrid hit back with their own statement that described Tebas’s choice of words as “morally repugnant”, while ending with a demand for the president’s resignation. Shortly after, the war of words continued with Tebas posting again on social media, accusing Madrid of trying to “destroy” La Liga.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Tebas has led La Liga since 2013. / NurPhoto/Getty ImagesTebas refused to express regret for his outrage-provoking comments, insisting he did not call anyone a Nazi.

“I simply did what others have done—Spanish politicians and those from other countries in the context of public debate, as well as journalists, and even [Former Vice-President of the European Commission] Josep Borrell when he discussed Putin’s communication strategy,” Tebas told L’Equipe.
“I simply did the same thing. Nothing more. I didn’t call anyone a Nazi, of course. I was talking about a communication strategy. I don’t see why I’m being questioned about it.”
Asked whether he was now fearful of losing his job over the remarks, Tebas remained unfazed.

“Look, I've lost count of the number of times they've tried to oust or sanction me,” he replied. “I think it's impossible. I'm not talking about the substance of the matter here, but rather the way they communicate.”

Tebas wants Rodri to win another Ballon d’Or but called Kylian Mbappé a worthy winner. /  Masashi Hara/Getty ImagesElsewhere in the interview, the La Liga chief revealed his pick for the Ballon d’Or, which is set to be awarded on Oct. 26. They were comments unlikely to be ignored in Madrid.

Asked whether Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé would be a worthy winner of soccer’s highest individual honor, Tebas admitted he would personally prefer to see it go to Barcelona’s Rodri, who was Spain’s World Cup-winning captain.

“I'd like Rodri to repeat his feat, but if Mbappé won the Ballon d'Or, I wouldn't mind. It's very close,” he said. “But if Mbappé wins, I wouldn't be surprised, and I think it would be a well-deserved title.”
He added: “Mbappé is one of the best players in the world. He's a global star, a phenomenal player who contributes enormously to his team and to the league in general.”

ftbpro_01m5fmrqmbqx.title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Como: Crisis Deepens As Red Devils Are Utterly Humiliated
ftbpro_01m5fmrqmbqx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:58 PM EDTMan Utd seriously struggled at Como. / Marco BERTORELLO/AFP/Getty ImagesThe pressure continues to grow on under-fire Michael Carrick after Manchester United were thrashed 4–1 by Como in the Champions League, extending their winless streak to seven matches in all competitions.

Torrential conditions briefly threatened a postponement at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, but the familiar sight of rain proved no advantage for the Red Devils. They were behind within just two minutes as apathetic defending allowed Nico Paz to curl an exquisite effort into the top corner.

Como completely outclassed United during the remainder of the first half in northern Italy. The visitors mustered just three shots—none of which were on target—and seldom enjoyed lengthy spells of possession. On the occasions they forayed forward, there was simply no goal threat.

Carrick tweaked his team at halftime, making two substitutions and moving to Ruben Amorim’s lamented 3-4-2-1 formation. But that decision swiftly backfired as Como sliced through United and Anastasios Douvikas fired a second beyond Senne Lammens.

Paz was once again the architect of United’s misery just before the hour as he put the game beyond doubt, intercepting Carlos Baleba’s pass and calmly converting Como’s third. The humiliation was complete for the away side in the 76th minute when Jacobo Ramón headed home a fourth, even if Joshua Zirkzee managed to score a consolation in stoppage time.
United have now collected just three points from as many league phase matches and must do some serious soul-searching ahead of Sunday’s Premier League match at home to Bournemouth.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Another dreadful showing from the Red Devils. / Marco Luzzani/Getty Images“We could’ve been a bit braver with the ball and taken the ball under pressure,” Harry Maguire fumed after United’s weekend draw with Leeds United. “But we’re in a circumstance where we are not as brave as we should be, and we have to get that back because to win games for United, we have to have that bravery and composure.”
The defender’s recent demands evidently fell on deaf ears, with his teammates exhibiting the familiar lethargy and lack of ambition that has underscored their dismal start to the season.

United struggled from the first kick. Their sleepy start facilitated Paz’s opener, and there were no improvements as the match wore on. Como were always a step ahead, moving the ball with envious speed and precision. Blue jerseys danced around their opponents, easily finding space as United’s disjointed press failed to close them down.

On the ball, there were typical frustrations. Zero penetration, a lack of movement, positional uncertainty, consistently misplaced passes—all of the weaknesses witnessed throughout the first two months of United’s campaign were on show here yet again.

Things were even worse after halftime as Carrick’s itchy feet resulted in an unsuccessful formation switch. Within 12 minutes of the second half commencing, United had conceded twice more as Como, and Carrick’s counterpart Cesc Fàbregas, completely humbled the record Premier League champions.
United were outfought, outmuscled and outsmarted as they failed to match the energy and enthusiasm of their hosts. There’s nowhere to hide after such an embarrassing performance.
Andrey Santos was sacrificed at halftime. / Nderim Kaceli/BSR Agency/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Senne Lammens—6.6: Continually undermined by the disastrous defense ahead of him. At least made a few saves.
RB: Diogo Dalot—5.3: Frequently bested by Martin Baturina and the overlapping Álex Valle, before switching to left wingback at the break. The positional change didn’t help him improve, though.

CB: Matthijs de Ligt—5.1: A first appearance in 11 months was littered with hiccups, one of which included him completely losing track of Douvikas as he doubled Como’s advantage. Not a pleasant return.
CB: Harry Maguire—7.1: Maguire should have been closer to Paz as he bent his first effort beyond Lammens, but, rather grimly, he was actually one of United’s better performers.
LB: Noussair Mazraoui—4.7: An unsuccessful stint at left back was followed by a similarly disappointing spell in central defense during the second half. Really, really poor.
CM: Mason Mount—6.2: Como completely overpowered United in midfield and Mount’s lack of defensive nous certainly helped the hosts.

ftbpro_01m5fn7bdwkr.title: How Lionel Messi’s Current Inter Miami Run Compares to His Best Barcelona Form Ever
ftbpro_01m5fn7bdwkr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas8:00 PM EDTLionel Messi is producing at near career-high levels despite his age.  / Brett Davis/Getty ImagesDespite being in the twilight of his career, 39-year-old Lionel Messi is currently immersed in one of his most productive runs of all time, scoring or assisting in each of his last 14 appearances in all competitions for club and country.
Messi has been in red-hot form ever since returning to Inter Miami following his simply jaw-dropping 2026 World Cup campaign for Argentina.
Although Miami doesn’t seem to be as formidable as they were a year ago when they lifted the 2025 MLS Cup, with Messi at his current level, they’re one of the favorites to repeat as champions.
Messi continues to perform as the best player in all of MLS, and he recently became the first player in league history to record 15 or more assists in three-straight seasons.
This run of goal involvements is flirting with the best of Messi’s career.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lionel Messi (left) is the most dominant force in MLS.  / Rich Storry/Getty ImagesIn a streak that began on August 15, Messi has registered 26 goal contributions in his last 14 appearances across all competitions, scoring 16 and assisting 10.

Only two weeks after the streak started, Messi announced his retirement from international soccer, even if his form and recent performances for Argentina suggest that he’s still more than capable of delivering for La Albiceleste.

The goal contribution run spans 12 MLS regular season games, plus the Campeones Cup final victory against Cruz Azul and his emotion last dance for Argentina in the friendly against Benin, in which Messi was directly involved in all three goals La Albiceleste scored.

It’s a simply staggering run from the timeless Messi. If he manages to extend it for three more games, then he’ll match the record for the longest run of consecutive games with a goal contribution of his entire career.

Lionel Messi (front) had his most productive run of consecutive games under Pep Guardiola.      / AFP/Getty ImagesMessi’s 14 consecutive games with a goal contribution is the second longest run of his career, only bested by the 17-match streak he produced back in 2011 for Barcelona under Pep Guardiola.

A then 23-year-old Messi opened up 2011 registering a goal involvement in 16 straight appearances for Barça, plus he also had a goal and an assist for Argentina in one of the two matches he played against Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal during his international career.
The 17-game run started in his first appearance of the year on Jan. 5 and ended on March. 8. In total, Messi had a simply otherworldly 19 goals and 10 assists during that time.
During 2010–11, Messi finished the season with 53 goals and 27 assists, helping Barcelona to the La Liga title and the second Champions League crown conquered during the Guardiola era.

With just four games remaining in the 2026 MLS regular season, Messi could potentially break his own record as Miami look to secure the highest seed possible in the Eastern Conference standings before their title defense reaches its climax in the MLS Cup playoffs.

ftbpro_01m5fns37etv.title: Four Takeaways As Michael Carrick Faces the Sack After Man Utd’s Dreadful Como Defeat
ftbpro_01m5fns37etv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:14 PM EDTMichael Carrick’s time at United could be coming to an end.  / Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty ImagesJust when things couldn’t get any more dire for Michael Carrick, Manchester United suffered a dreadful 4–1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The Red Devils came into the fixture desperate to snap their six-game winless run, but were out-classed from the opening whistle. It took just two minutes for Nico Paz to open the scoring for Cesc Fàbregas’s men, a tale of what was to come as the game stretched on.

Como scored three more unanswered goals in the second half, with Paz’s brilliance playing a part in almost every one. United were absolutely lifeless, drained of any fight or intensity across all areas of the pitch.
Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back for the visitors in stoppage time, but the consolation goal did nothing to relieve the toxic taste plaguing the once great club.
Next. Man Utd player ratings vs. Como. Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Como: Red Devils Utterly Humiliated. dark

Manchester United’s depleted defense let in four goals. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesIt feels only fitting to start with the way the game started—with Paz beating Senne Lammens to deny the Belgian yet another clean sheet. It wasn’t the goalkeeper’s fault; there was no stopping Paz’s stunning curler.

But the fact remains: Carrick’s defense looks utterly incapable of blanking opponents. The Red Devils have now conceded at least one goal in 10 of their 11 matches in 2026–27. The only team that failed to get on the scoresheet against United were Champions League debutants Sabah.

There was so much talk of Matthijs de Ligt returning to the XI for the first time since November 2025, but the center back was hardly the only problem on the night—even if his pace was wildly concerning, much like the way one ball split himself and Harry Maguire in the build-up to Anastasios Douvikas’s goal.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui were also at the scene of the crime over and over again. The former was beaten by Álex Valle for sport. On the other flank, Mazraoui was made a fool by Paz on more than one occasion, with Lucas Da Cunha and Kaiki joining in on the fun as well.

Perhaps things would have looked different had Luke Shaw been fit, but he remains sidelined, like so many other times in his United career. It truly is a wonder the club did not pull the trigger to bring in an additional fullback before the summer transfer window ended.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Carlos Baleba (left) had a nightmare appearance. / Mattia Ozbot/UEFA/Getty ImagesIt was clear from the opening whistle United were a step—or five—behind Como. The visitors were playing without any hunger, calmly watching Fàbregas’s men pass the ball like fans spectating a training drill.

There were countless moments when the Red Devils were literally just standing still, showing not a single ounce of interest in winning the ball back or disrupting the hosts in possession. Every now and then, a United player would briefly try to challenge for the ball, come up empty and then give up again.

United’s midfield double pivot of Andrey Santos and Mason Mount were helpless trying to gain any semblance of control on the game in the first half. Paz was running the show, so much so that Santos had to make a desperate, lunging tackle on the youngster to stop him from breaking free down the right, which earned him a place in the referee’s book.

The former Chelsea midfielder was hooked at halftime and replaced by fellow summer signing Carlos Baleba. Four minutes later, Como had their second goal of the night, cutting through United’s new midfield and depleted defense with ease. By the 51st minute, Baleba already had a yellow card to his name and before the hour-mark, he had his pocket picked by Paz, who then made it 3–0.

Would Carrick’s midfield have looked better with Kobbie Mainoo? Almost assuredly. But even if the England international were available and playing, what would that have done for the other nine outfield players who barely covered any distance on Como’s rain-soaked pitch?

Matheus Cunha (center) was hooked at halftime. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesA scoreline can be quite deceiving in soccer; a lopsided result is sometimes not entirely indicative of what unfolded on the pitch. That was not the case in Italy on Wednesday.

United did not have a run of bad luck in the final third. They did not fail to bury chances or get out-classed by a great goalkeeping performance. In truth, they never looked capable of even testing Como, let alone getting on the scoresheet, until Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 91st minute.

When the halftime whistle sounded, they did not have a single shot on target and had just six touches in the opposition’s box. Matheus Cunha might as well have not been on the pitch. Bryan Mbeumo was nearly just as anonymous, and Bruno Fernandes looked out of sorts.

Things improved just barely in the second half with the addition of Amad Diallo and Zirkzee, but there were still hardly any moments from the visitors that were worthy of finding the back of the net. In fact, Zirkzee only got free enough to score because Como stopped playing, convinced he was offside.

ftbpro_01m5fwmv2dz0.title: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal Player Ratings: Rice Saves Gunners From Rare European Defeat
ftbpro_01m5fwmv2dz0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 21, 2026Arsenal secured a decent result in Munich. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesDeclan Rice scored the all-important equalizer for Arsenal as they drew 2–2 away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Injuries and forced omissions dominated the discourse early in proceedings at the Allianz Arena. Bayern fielded a sub-par side without the likes of Michael Olise, Joshua Kimmich and Jamal Musiala, while Bukayo Saka’s concerning injury saw him substituted after just 10 minutes.

The absence of some glitzy superstars initially dulled a heavyweight contest, but Saka’s replacement, Eberechi Eze, sparked the match into life with his pinpoint strike in the 25th minute—which was initially ruled out for offside before VAR intervention.

Bayern responded 10 minutes later, however, as Alphonso Davies, playing in an unfamiliar left wing role, coolly converted Harry Kane’s sublime through ball. The latter then completed the turnaround on the hour as he thrashed home a penalty against his former north London rivals.

However, Kane’s international teammate delivered the final meaningful act of the match, with Rice lashing a strike beyond Manuel Neuer at the end of a well-worked move to maintain Arsenal’s unbeaten start to their European campaign.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Kane made his presence felt. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesKane has considered morphing into an NFL kicker when he retires from soccer, but the Englishman was Bayern’s quarterback in Bavaria. He touched every blade of grass, dropping deep to find space before unleashing some outrageous long-range passes—most notably the assist for Davies, which was executed with the utmost precision.
Oh, and there was his customary goal, too.

Arsenal boasted their own floating playmaker, however, with Martin Ødegaard matching Kane’s passing pedigree. The Norwegian delivered a sumptuous lofted through ball for Eze’s opener and was a constant source of invention for the away side. Everything was fed through the captain, who knew exactly when to speed up the tempo.

Arsenal will be fretting over Saka. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesTuesday’s action was littered with casualties as the likes of Ousmane Dembélé, Dani Olmo and, most tragically, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered injuries, and Saka joined a growing list of unfortunate forwards in Germany.

Arsenal will be fearing the worst considering Saka fell to the turf without any contact from a Bayern player, clutching his upper leg and leaving the field in serious discomfort. It could prove a sizeable blow for the reigning Premier League champions.

This wasn’t the best night for Saka’s clubmate Jurriën Timber, either. The Dutchman wasn’t dreadful by any means, but Davies left him for dead as Bayern equalized, and he proceeded to concede the spot kick from which Kane scored. Even the most consistent defenders can be bamboozled by Bayern’s fearsome forwards.
Davies made Arsenal sweat.  / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Manuel Neuer—6.6: The 40-year-old still boasts remarkable cat-like reflexes, as evidenced by his stunning close-range save to deny Bruno Guimarães.
RB: Konrad Laimer—5.9: Caught cold as Eze opened the scoring and found life challenging up against the England international. Perhaps he’d mentally prepared for a battle with Noni Madueke instead.
CB: Dayot Upamecano—7.6: Defensively sound throughout. One powerful foray forward would have culminated in a goal had it not been for an excellent David Raya save.
CB: Kim Min-jae—6.2: Rarely worked during the first half and was then substituted at the break.
LB: Josip Stanišić—6.6: Kept Eze narrowly onside by sitting too deep, but generally coped well against Madueke as the minutes ticked away.
CM: Tom Bischof—7.1: Robust in the center of the pitch against an industrious Arsenal midfield. Impressive given he’s just 21 years old.
CM: Aleksandar Pavlović—7.2: Another youngster in Bayern’s midfield which caught the eye. Pavlović has that beautiful blend of tenacity and grace.

ftbpro_01m5fwp3qdtr.title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. RB Leipzig: Los Blancos Dominate in El Clasico Rehearsal
ftbpro_01m5fwp3qdtr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:16 PM EDTIt was all smiles for Real Madrid on Wednesday evening.     / Diego Souto/Getty Images Real Madrid continued their perfect start to the Champions League season with a decisive 4–1 win against RB Leipzig at the Bernabéu on Wednesday night.

Los Blancos controlled the early exchanges but the visitors looked menacing in transition throughout the first half. Still, when it seemed the game was destined to go scoreless to the break, Bernardo Silva was perfectly positioned to pounce after the goalkeeper was unable to clear an Arda Güler shot. The Portuguese midfielder’s finish put Real Madrid in front 43 minutes in with his first goal involvement for the club.

The goal completely changed the game as Real Madrid emphatically dominated in the second half. Less than 10 minutes after the restart, Jose Mourinho’s men doubled their advantage when Güler tapped-in a Kylian Mbappé header, stealing a goal away from the Frenchman who simply laughed as the Türkiye international went to celebrate with him.

With a two-goal advantage, Madrid put the game on cruise control and managed their efforts. Still, Mbappé scored a brilliant goal late only to be erased by Tidiam Gomis, who bagged a consolation strike for the Germans two minutes later.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

But the cherry on top of the cake came in the 87th minute when Yan Diomande restored Madrid’s three-goal lead with a simply stunning volley against his former club to make it four straight games with a goal contribution for Los Blancos.

It was a mature performance from Real Madrid, who have collected three wins from three to start the Champions League campaign and will be full of confidence ahead of their mouthwatering trip to Barcelona for the first El Clásico of the season on Sunday.

Bernardo Silva (front) scored his first Real Madrid goal. / Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesAlthough Real Madrid had a better start, RB Leipzig slowly grew into the match and started looking like the more dangerous side late in the first half, trying to catch the hosts out of position with quick counter attacks.

One of these actions came 41 minutes in when Christopher Nkunku was played through on goal with a darting run behind Madrid’s backline. With only Thibaut Courtois to beat, the Frenchman failed to properly place his shot and the Belgian added another stunning save to his ever-growing catalogue.

The miss proved costly. Only two minutes later, when Real Madrid appeared to start suffering, they produced their first attacking combination of the first half which allowed an unmarked Federico Valverde to whip in a cross that Güler nearly scored from. Still, the goalkeeper’s rebound dropped kindly for an opportunistic Silva, who tapped-in his first Real Madrid goal to give the hosts the lead two minutes from halftime.

In a matter of 120 seconds, the 15-time European champions went from praying for the halftime whistle to grabbing the lead. Nkunku had an opportunity to put the visitors in a dream position for an upset but squandered it, and Los Blancos quickly responded with the latest example of why they’re a team you simply can’t waste chances against in the Champions League.
Arda Güler continued his strong run of performances.  / Ion Alcoba Beitia/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Thibaut Courtois—7.4: Another game, another couple of fabulous saves from the Belgian. His heroics between the sticks kept Real Madrid from falling behind in the first half.

RB: Federico Valverde—8.3: Struggled to contain the threatening Antonio Nusa one-on-one. Still, he was effective in possession and allowed Güler to drift centrally where he feels more comfortable. Dominated in the second half.

CB: Antonio Rüdiger—7.2: Strong in his defensive duties but not so much when he tried to turn creator with erratic long balls from deep. Fortunately for Madrid, the former is the German’s primary assignment. Was caught out of position in Leipzig’s goal.

CB: Dean Huijsen—7.7: Timed a number of interceptions brilliantly and had the most defensive contributions of any player on the pitch. Delighted the Bernabéu crowd with a handful of line-breaking passes.
LB: Álvaro Carreras—7.4: Had a very promising start but had his problems containing Brajan Gruda. Still, it was an overall solid showing from the Spaniard.

DM: Bernardo Silva—8.3: Routinely crashed the box whenever Real Madrid attacked and was rewarded for it with his first goal since joining the club to put his side in front. Comfortable on the ball as always.

DM: Eduardo Camavinga—8.2: A very solid showing from Camavinga, who was tidy in possession and was exceptional counter-pressing, forcing turnovers high up the pitch. One of his best performances in a while.

RW: Arda Güler—8.7: The best player on the pitch. Oozing confidence and toying with markers, creating chances for fun. The bulk of Real Madrid’s most dangerous actions started with the ball at his feet.

ftbpro_01m5fxhvb74q.title: ‘That’s on the Manager’—Fernandes Calls Out Carrick After Humiliating Como Defeat
ftbpro_01m5fxhvb74q.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell4:32 PM EDTBruno Fernandes had some telling words after Manchester United’s defeat. / Luca Rossini/PA Images/Getty ImagesThe final whistle had barely just sounded at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia before Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes condemned tactical “decisions from the staff” in the Red Devils’ humiliating defeat to Como.

United arrived in Italy with the hopes of finally securing their first win since Sept. 10, but they failed to show up under the Champions League lights, falling 4–1 to Cesc Fàbregas’s men. It was as lopsided a match as any, with the visitors looking wildly uninterested and underprepared for the bout.

“It’s not the first time,” Fernandes told TNT Sports about such a lifeless performance from United. “I think we started on the wrong foot; they scored very early. [There was] not much pressure on the ball, not really many good moments without the ball, many things not going our way.”

Indeed, Nico Paz got on the scoresheet within the first two minutes and the Red Devils had no answer for the majority of the match. They were statues as Como passed the ball with incredible ease, carving apart Michael Carrick’s team without hardly having to hit second-gear.
Next. Man Utd Como takeaways. Takeaways As Carrick Faces the Sack for Dismal Como Defeat. dark

Fernandes had some thoughts as to why it was so easy for Como to dominate. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball.

“But sometimes when you give the ball too much to these teams, they get confident. They have so many bodies behind that ball that make you run a lot, that makes people get frustrated. Then once you recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work.”

When pressed if he believes Carrick’s tactical decisions cost the team against Como, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and the staff to say it, that’s not on me. I just said I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure and trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable.”

Manchester United got nothing going against Como. / Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty ImagesCarrick’s postgame comments were not as incendiary as those from Fernandes ... initially. He started off by taking responsibility for the defeat.

“It was more than disappointing,” Carrick told TNT Sports. “Everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll 100% take responsibility for the overall team and the performance. That’s where it stops, it stops with me. I’m absolutely fine with that. I accept that totally.”
But the English manager quickly called out his team’s lethargic performance, a common theme amid United’s seven-game winless run across all competitions.
“To see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say. It’s the motivation, the intension, the purpose, the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that.

“You can’t turn it on and off. You can’t choose when you want to perform and when you don’t want to perform, or when you give absolutely everything or when you maybe don’t so, until you do that, you’re not going to win football matches.
“There’s no excuses at all. I think it’s just not acceptable.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Michael Carrick is facing the sack. / Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Ciancaphoto Studio/Getty ImagesCarrick ended his comments by sidestepping a question about whether he still has the backing of the club after such an embarrassing defeat. But pundits were quick to answer for him.

“It’s such a bad result and such a bad performance that it could have serious repercussions for the manager, unfortunately for him,” Liverpool icon Jamie Carragher said on CBS Sports. “It looks like another Manchester United manager is going to bite the dust.”
When fellow co-host Kate Scott asked Carragher to pinpoint whether the blame falls on the manager or the players, the former player had a sweeping response.

“It’s everything about Manchester United,” Carragher said. “Where do you start? It never ends. It’s a never-ending cycle. Is it the owners? Is It the manager? Is it the recruitment, the players? Nobody seems to be able to get this right.”

Carrick earned the permanent role as United’s manager after leading the club to a third-place finish once he took over for Ruben Amorim last season. Yet the results are not there in 2026–27; the club has won just two of 11 matches across all competitions—and a lopsided defeat like the one the Red Devils suffered on Wednesday could be the trigger that makes Carrick the first manager fired in the Premier League this season.

ftbpro_01m5fy86nvxd.title: Arsenal Rocked by Nightmare Saka Injury in Early Stages Against Bayern Munich
ftbpro_01m5fy86nvxd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 21, 2026Saka suffered an injury on Wednesday. / Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND/AFP/Getty ImagesIn the Champions League heavyweight clash with Bayern Munich on Wednesday, Arsenal were forced to go without the man they needed most.

Star winger Bukayo Saka went down inside the opening 10 minutes of the league phase match at the Allianz Arena, clutching his leg in pain after kicking a lofted ball across the pitch. Saka needed assistance from the training staff to stand up, before hobbling down the tunnel. He was replaced by Eberechi Eze while the match remained scoreless. The game ended in a 2–2 draw.

The loss of Saka comes as a major blow for the Gunners, who are chasing redemption on the European stage this season. Saka played an integral part in the team’s run to the 2025–26 Champions League final, registering five goal contributions in eight starts, including the game-winner in the second leg of the semifinals against Atlético Madrid.
Just last week againt Lille, he had a goal and an assist off the bench in Arsenal’s 3–0 win to make it 14 straight league phase victories under Mikel Arteta.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Saka seems to have suffered a muscular leg injury. /  Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND/AFP/Getty ImagesAfter breaking away on the dribble from Bayern’s Alphonso Davies, Saka attempted a long kick across the pitch, performing a scooping motion that caused an immediate muscular strain in his left leg.

He was later seen clutching his quadricep on the ground, indicating an injury to the front part of his thigh. He was also later shown patting his left quad while conversing with Arteta on the sideline.
“It doesn’t look good at all good,” Arteta told reporters post-match, confirming the quad injury. “But we will have to wait and see.”

Saka has no history of a major quad injury; however, he did have to deal with a nagging hamstring injury last season as well as during the 2024–25 season, which caused him to miss 26 total matches across all competitions during those years.

Saka’s timeline for recovery is at least six weeks. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesSaka could be out for a minimum of six weeks, Arsenal’s medical staff estimate, pending the results of further testing and another MRI scan. There is a buildup of fluid around the muscle, which is making an exact diagnosis difficult to obtain.

“We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists,” Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said Friday. “When a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, and is restricted to movement; it is not a good sign. Let’s be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive assessment.
“He’s got another MRI, as there was quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was quite difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more tomorrow.”

If Saka is out for six weeks, he will not return to the pitch until early December, missing several key clashes for Arsenal. He will be absent for Premier League matches against Liverpool (Nov. 1) and Manchester City (Nov. 29), among others, as well as Champions League bouts with Slavia Prague (Nov. 4) and Borussia Dortmund (Nov. 24).

ftbpro_01m5g5tb74df.title: Out of Nowhere, Mexico Might Have Found Its Replacement for Injured Raul Jimenez
ftbpro_01m5g5tb74df.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas9:00 PM EDTTahiel Jiménez can’t stop scoring for Santos.     / Manuel Guadarrama/Getty Images Santos Laguna’s 20-year-old striker Tahiel Jiménez is having a breakout moment in Liga MX, and his prolific form could earn him a maiden call-up to Mexico’s senior national team next month with Raúl Jímenez sidelined for the rest of the year.

A little over halfway through the Liga MX Apertura 2026 season, Santos have become one of the biggest stories of the campaign, thanks to five straight wins that have placed them firmly in the playoff race after finishing bottom of the league in three of the last four seasons.

After failing to register a single start for Santos since April, manager Renato Paiva finally gave Jiménez a chance to impress from the opening whistle in their most recent two games. The young striker grabbed his opportunity and ran away with it.

Jiménez scored a brace to lead Santos to a 2–1 win over Atlético San Luis on Oct. 11, before scoring a hat-trick on Saturday in the 5–0 pummeling of Querétaro. Five goals in his first two starts of the season have firmly placed Jiménez on El Tri’s radar, especially after Raúl Jiménez underwent knee surgery that will sideline him until 2027.
But who is this previously unknown striker now tearing up Liga MX?
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Tahiel Jiménez (left) played alongside Gilberto Mora (middle) in the 2025 U–20 World Cup.  / Martín Fonseca/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesJiménez is the son of former Liga MX star Walter “El Lorito” Jiménez, who won a league title with Santos in 2008. Although his father is Argentinian, Tahiel was born and raised in Mexico and joined Santos’s academy at 16.

Jiménez made his professional debut for Santos at 18 in April 2024. He has since featured 40 times during one of the worst periods in club history. With the club struggling for results, playing time was hard to come by—as is the case for many young talents in Liga MX.

Still, Jiménez was a regular for Mexico’s youth teams and led the line for El Tri in the 2025 U–20 World Cup, scoring his one and only goal of the tournament in the 4–1 win against host Chile in the round of 16. There, he played alongside coveted teenager Gilberto Mora, just like their fathers did during their playing days for the now defunct Jaguares de Chiapas in Liga MX.

Jiménez registered just two starts for Santos in the aftermath of the U–20 World Cup. But after bagging three goals in four games for Mexico in the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games this summer, Paiva finally granted him his golden opportunity.

Now, Jiménez is already Santos’s top goalscorer. His meteoric rise hasn’t gone unnoticed, with reports suggesting El Tri manager Rafael Márquez is considering rostering him for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.

Mexico manager Rafel Márquez is in desperate need of goals.  / Chris Coduto/Getty Images It might seem like two impressive performances is far too small of a sample size for Jiménez to merit a look with Mexico’s senior national team, but El Tri desperately needs alternatives at the position, given recent evidence.

With the veteran Wolverhampton Wanderers striker unavailable, Armando González, Santiago Gimenez and Germán Berterame all got extended looks with El Tri during the September–October international action. The trio of strikers failed to score and delivered uninspiring performances.

Henry Martín is the last Mexico center forward not named Raúl Jiménez to score a goal for El Tri in an official match, and those goals came two years ago in the second leg of the 2024 Nations League quarterfinal vs. Honduras.
Injuries have tormented Martín, and he hasn’t featured for El Tri since, but a surge in form for Club América has reportedly also placed the 33-year-old center forward back on Márquez’s radar.
Still, if the 20-year-old Jiménez continues his breakout, it will be almost impossible for Márquez not to pick up the phone.

It’s way too early to call Jiménez Mexico’s striker of the future, but his recent performances have at least demonstrated the 20-year-old has the potential to grow into a very capable goalscorer—something that isn’t minor in Mexico’s current landscape.

ftbpro_01m5hanvw4dn.title: ‘Actually’—Michael Carrick Bites Back at Bruno Fernandes Criticism
ftbpro_01m5hanvw4dn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:00 AM EDTMichael Carrick was not impressed. / Mattia Ozbot - UEFA/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick rejected criticism from captain Bruno Fernandes about his tactics in the aftermath of Wednesday’s brutal 4–1 defeat to Como.

Having seen their miserable run of form extended by a humiliating defeat to the Italian side, Fernandes stood in front of the cameras to criticize his team’s lack of pressing, specifically arguing it was Carrick’s decision not to press man-to-man.
Pressed on Fernandes’s comments after the final whistle, Carrick insisted not only did he deploy some of the man-to-man pressing Fernandes wanted, but it actually proved to be a bad idea.
“We actually half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that,” Carrick scoffed.
“There’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play—if you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Bruno Fernandes’s comments were met with a mixed response. / Luca Rossini/PA Images/Getty ImagesFernandes was the second United player to divert attention away from the squad in recent weeks, following center back Lisandro Martínez’s spectacular comments against technical director Jason Wilcox and the rest of the recruitment team.

To see Fernandes take a similarly scathing approach to his assessment of the situation came as a real surprise to CBS pundit Jamie Carragher, who accused the Portugal international of “killing” his own team with his actions on the pitch.
“We said Lisandro Martínez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy above him. For Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really,” Carragher said.

“When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn’t have got that award without Michael Carrick, because Michael Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he’s a talented footballer. But when you think of him as a footballer, he’s a talent, but in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it’s not right at all.

“And he’s reacted like that because he’s been brought off and he’s been embarrassed tonight by the manager as he brought him off. And when he talks about pressing, whether it’s man to man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can’t press because he does things for the crowd.

“I commentate on games watching Man Utd and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he’s working hard—he’s not. He’s killing the rest of the team doing it.”

It was a tough showing from Fernandes. / Marco Luzzani/Getty ImagesFew would argue with the statement that, from a technical perspective, Fernandes is United’s star. When firing, he’s a creative, goalscoring midfielder capable of picking apart any defense in the world, with a record-breaking 21 Premier League assists last season proving his worth.

Carrick has stayed loyal to Fernandes up to this point, hoping his out-of-form star will suddenly rediscover the quality that helped him land the permanent manager job this summer, but Wednesday’s game may have been a turning point.
Fernandes was, surprisingly, deployed as a striker against Como. While he had more touches of the ball than plenty of his teammates, the vast majority were largely ineffective.
Next. Best Man Utd players ever. The Best Man Utd Players of All Time—Ranked. dark

The Portugal international, now 32, boasts a relentless engine but isn’t blessed with the pace needed to stretch a defense and looked evidently uncomfortable in a new role, culminating in a frustrated reaction to his withdrawal in the 66th minute, when United were 3–0 down and still chasing a way back into the game.

It was the latest in a long line of frustrating performances from Fernandes, who is known to be playing through injury, and his response to Wednesday’s showing proved he is far from happy with the club’s current direction.

With a contract that expires in 2027, United will soon have a decision to make on Fernandes. They have the option to automatically extend his deal by a further 12 months but, as United have previously demonstrated with the likes of David de Gea and Casemiro, they are prepared to walk away from their highest-earners if the finances are not right.

ftbpro_01m5heswnf8a.title: Man Utd’s Heaviest Champions League Defeats of All Time
ftbpro_01m5heswnf8a.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray7:05 AM EDTMan Utd recently added to their list of worst European defeats. / Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesManchester United have been one of the Champions League’s key protagonists since the competition’s rebranding in 1992.

Despite their fall from grace following the departure of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, the Red Devils remain among Europe’s leading clubs and, naturally, have an overwhelmingly impressive record in the continent’s premier tournament.

However, there have been a fair few off-days, too. Even a club with the stature and reputation of United is occasionally humiliated on the European stage—as was the case during their recent trip to Como.
With that in mind, here are United’s six biggest Champions League defeats.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Man Utd were left stunned by an unfamiliar foe during the 2002–03 season.  / Mike Egerton/EMPICS/Getty ImagesThere were some mitigating factors around United’s shock defeat to Maccabi Haifa in the group stage of the 2002–03 Champions League.
Firstly, the Red Devils had already qualified for the next round of the competition following four straight victories. Secondly, Ferguson fielded an inexperienced and weakened side as a result.
However, having beaten the Israeli side 5–2 at Old Trafford, there were few signs that United would capitulate in such dramatic fashion during the reverse fixture.

Raimondas Žutautas proved the thorn in United’s side as he grabbed an assist and goal either side of the halftime whistle, with his 35-yard strike doubling the home side’s advantage. Eventually, a young Yakubu rounded off the scoring with a penalty in the closing stages.
An undoubtedly surprising result, but one without any consequence.

Man Utd were undone by an individual masterclass. / Jamie McDonald/Getty ImagesMuch like during their bruising defeat to Maccabi Haifa two years earlier, United had already qualified from their Champions League group when traveling to Fenerbahçe for their final outing. Yet again, Ferguson named a makeshift side, which proved unable to cope with one man in particular: Tuncay Şanlı.

The Fenerbahçe forward, who would late venture to England to play for Middlesbrough, Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers, scored a second-half hat trick to secure one of the Turkish side’s most memorable European triumphs.

Two clinical efforts bookended a header as the Türkiye international single-handedly downed United, who were making an unwanted habit of being humiliated during admittedly meaningless European away days.

The eventual champions proved too good at San Siro. / Etsuo Hara/Getty ImagesUnited found themselves one step away from the Champions League final in 2006–07 having motored to the semifinal stage. AC Milan were the final hurdle they had to overcome to reach the showpiece event.

Carlo Ancelotti’s side had reached the final two years earlier, succumbing to Liverpool in that match in Istanbul, and they were fueled by revenge as they once again came up against English opponents.

Kaká’s brilliance hadn’t been enough for the Italians during the first leg at Old Trafford, with Milan losing 3–2 following Wayne Rooney’s brace and a strike from Cristiano Ronaldo. But the Brazilian starred during a 3–0 victory at San Siro in the second leg.

Kaká opened the scoring after just 11 minutes to level the aggregate score, with Clarence Seedorf proceeding to double Milan’s lead on the night after half-an-hour. Alberto Gilardino then secured a place in the final for the Rossoneri in the closing stages.
United would have come up against Liverpool had they reached the final, but at least they witnessed their bitter rivals lose to Milan in Athens.

Lionel Messi humbled the Red Devils. / Etsuo Hara/Getty ImagesUnited had staged a heroic turnaround in the round of 16 of the 2018–19 Champions League to overcome Paris Saint-Germain at Parc des Princes, but a quarterfinal tie with Barcelona proved a step too far for Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s men.
Having been defeated 1–0 at home during the first leg, United journeyed to Camp Nou hoping for another dramatic comeback win, but Lionel Messi ensured there would be no such remontada.

ftbpro_01m5hf7x8qs6.title: Ballon d’Or 2027: Ranking the Early Favorites to Win, Latest Odds
ftbpro_01m5hf7x8qs6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby LaneOct 27, 2026A dynamic duo if there ever was one. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesThe 2026 Ballon d’Or may have only just been handed out—Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane ending England’s 25-year wait for a winner—but the race for next year’s prize is already heating up.
Can the Englishman get his hands on the game’s biggest individual prize once again, or is it time for a new name to steal the spotlight and take home the coveted trophy?

It’s still early days in the 2026–27 season, so making any firm predictions would be a fool’s game. But several superstars are already making their intentions clear, whether by scoring goals for fun, running the show from midfield or delivering when the stakes are at their highest.
With the race beginning to take shape, we rank the early favorites to win the 2027 Ballon d’Or and break down why each has a genuine shot at claiming soccer’s most prestigious individual honor.

Diomande is flying at Madrid. / Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesBefore we get into the top 10, there are a few players who have enjoyed brilliant starts to the 2026–27 season and could comfortably work their way into Ballon d’Or contention if they maintain their current form.

Unsurprisingly, Paris Saint-Germain—who are hunting a third consecutive Champions League title—have stars making an early impression. Ousmane Dembélé is chief among them and has shown more than enough to remind us of his world-class quality. Unfortunately, teammate Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has suffered a torn ACL and is unlikely to feature on the eventual 30-strong shortlist.

Over at Real Madrid, Vinícius Júnior will always be in the conversation, but it’s perhaps Yan Diomande who has emerged as the club’s surprise star so far. Signed from Leipzig in the summer, the young attacker arrived with plenty to prove. A string of stunning goals and a handful of eye-catching assists, however, have quickly silenced any doubters.

Elsewhere, Rayan Cherki is an outside contender if he can keep finding the net and producing moments of genius for Manchester City. England duo Declan Rice and Cole Palmer also deserve a mention, while Barcelona’s Pau Cubarsí may be the only defender currently making a convincing case for a place among the frontrunners.

Bellingham is thriving under Mourinho. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesAfter a difficult 2025–26 season for Real Madrid, Jude Bellingham is looking back to his commanding best.A force of nature in the middle of the park, the Englishman can power through opposition teams as if they aren’t even there. The goals and assists are flowing again, and he’s thriving under José Mourinho.

Kane is always among the goals. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesKane may not be in quite the same imperious form for Bayern Munich at the start of the 2026–27 season as he was last term, but the Englishman remains one of the world’s elite strikers.Not only is he a clinical finisher, capable of dispatching chances in just a couple of touches, but his link-up play and ability to drop deep and spray passes around are second to none.We’re confident the goals will start flowing again soon.

Vitinha’s turnaround has been remarkable.  / Franco Arland/Getty ImagesOnce considered something of a flop at Wolverhampton Wanderers, nobody is questioning Vitinha’s quality now.The PSG midfielder—who finished third at the 2025 Ballon d'Or—is the complete package: a superb playmaker, a silky dribbler and a dangerous goalscorer. The Portuguese international has already added a couple of stunners to his highlight reel this season.

Olise is pure magic. / Alexander Hassenstein/Getty ImagesIs there a better left foot in world soccer today than Michael Olise? We’d argue not.The Frenchman’s left boot is pure magic—a wand capable of conjuring something out of nothing, whether it’s a devilishly whipped cross, a silky piece of skill or a curling finish from range.Watch opposing teams face Bayern Munich and you’ll notice they almost always put two, if not three, men on Olise to try to contain him. That tells you everything you need to know about just how good he is.

Haaland is a goal machine. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesThe charges hanging over Manchester City continue to cast a shadow over the club, but Erling Haaland has refused to let the noise distract him.The Norwegian has hit the ground running under new manager Enzo Maresca, starting the 2026-27 campaign in imperious form and already looking well on course to claim his fourth Premier League Golden Boot in five seasons.

Rodri was made for Barcelona. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty ImagesRodri was made to play for Barcelona—and he’s already showing it.One of the finest passers in world soccer, no player controls a game quite like the Spaniard. Every pass is inch-perfect, timed to perfection and played with purpose, always keeping Barça on the front foot.If the Catalans can finally win the Champions League under Hansi Flick, don’t be surprised if Rodri turns out to be the missing ingredient they’ve been searching for.

There’s no stopping Desire Doue. / Julien De Rosa/AFP/Getty ImagesDoué may still be young, but there’s a strong argument that he’s already Paris Saint-Germain’s most important player.The supremely versatile winger-cum-midfielder came in clutch during PSG’s back-to-back Champions League-winning campaigns in 2024-25 and 2025-26—and he’s already picking up where he left off this season.Stunning strikes against Manchester City and Barcelona, both fired into the bottom corner from range, have been a timely reminder of just how dangerous Doué can be when given even the slightest bit of space.

Kylian Mbappe is a generational talent. / Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesOnce again, there’s no doubting Kylian Mbappé’s genius. Lightning quick, a clinical finisher and seemingly becoming less and less selfish in the final third, he’s always at the heart of everything Real Madrid do well.Whether he lifts the 2027 Ballon d’Or may well come down to one thing: can he fire Real Madrid to Champions League glory?

Yamal’s goal against Betis was a stunning. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesJust look at Lamine Yamal’s stunning piece of skill and curled opener against Real Betis in mid-October, and you’ll understand exactly why he’s among the favorites to win the 2027 Ballon d’Or.The Spanish sensation is an ethereal talent—the kind of generational prospect we haven’t seen since the emergence of a certain Lionel Messi.

Raphinha has enjoyed a strong start to the season. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesNo player in Europe has made a better start to the 2026-27 season than Barcelona’s Raphinha.Even with an injury setback, the Brazilian is already well into double figures for goals and assists combined, helping Barça enjoy a nine-game winning run to start La Liga as they chase a third consecutive title.While Raphinha was undoubtedly a star during his time in the Premier League with Leeds United, few could have predicted the heights he has reached at the Camp Nou.

ftbpro_01m5hfdccxvn.title: Kylian Mbappe Claims Vinicius Junior Being ‘Sad’ Is a Good Thing
ftbpro_01m5hfdccxvn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath7:30 AM EDTVinícius Jr went without a goal contribution again on Wednesday. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesReal Madrid striker Kylian Mbappé has claimed there’s no problem with Vinícius Júnior being “sad” because it simply means he “wants to give a lot to the team.”
Vinícius Jr’s form has been the topic of much concern at Real Madrid this season, with the 26-year-old struggling at the start of new manager José Mourinho’s second reign.

The Brazilian forward, named The Best FIFA Men’s Player in 2024, has scored just once in 2026–27—during a 4–1 win over Real Sociedad back in August—and his displays have drawn attention for the wrong reasons.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Vinícius Jr last scored in August. / Kazimierz Koper/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesA regular target of the Bernabéu boo boys this season—in part fueled by Vinícius Jr’s protracted contract saga and flirting with Arsenal—his ineffective performances have gone from being a peripheral concern to a major one for Real Madrid in recent weeks.

The forward was substituted before the hour mark during the Madrid derby defeat prior to the last international break, having failed to created a chance or register a shot on target. He was then shown a straight red in the 1–0 win over Villarreal after pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba—a dismissal that has earned him a four-game domestic suspension.
Mourinho called Vinícius Jr’s current rut “heartbreaking” but later issued a blunt warning that no player is “untouchable” in the team.
By contrast, Mbappé has thrived this season, scoring 12 times already, fueling theories that the team can only support one of the two superstar forwards at any given time.

Kylian Mbappé is on fire, as Vinícius Jr flounders. /  Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesVinícius Jr was not on the scoresheet again on Wednesday as Madrid ran out 4–1 winners over RB Leipzig in the Champions League.
Los Blancos’s No. 7 had two shots saved on the night and won four of five of his duels, but found himself substituted for Yan Diomande—who went on to score and assist—on 70 minutes.
Vinícius Jr cut a dejected figure as he left the field, a moment not missed by the TV cameras.
Asked about his teammate’s frame of mind after the match, Mbappé insisted it reflects well on Vinícius Jr if he is taking his poor form badly.

“It’s okay. It’s good that Vinícius is sad because he wants to give a lot to the team and the fans. He needs to stay calm and be proud of who he is. He’s a great player with great quality,” he told Movistar Plus on the pitch after the match.
Mbappé added that he has a similar mentality, saying: “I can do more. I’m one of those players who always needs to be pushed harder. It’s never enough for a player like me.”

Vinícius Jr is currently serving a La Liga ban after being sent off against Villarreal.  / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesVinícius Jr will definitely not be part of the team traveling to face Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday, Oct. 25, with the winger suspended for the first Clásico of the season.

The same goes for the following two La Liga matches against Racing Santander (Nov. 1) and Valencia (Nov. 7)—though Madrid are still appealing to get the suspension paused or reduced in order to free up Vinícius Jr to feature in at least the Valencia game.

As his ban does not apply to European competition, he will be available for Madrid’s next Champions League match away at AEK Athens on Wednesday, Nov. 4. However, with summer signing Diomande hitting his stride with six goal contributions in his last four outings, there is a very real case to be made that Madrid are currently better off without their second-highest paid player in the starting lineup.
Mourinho’s recent “untouchable” comments suggest that Vinícius Jr’s place in the team is no longer a given.

ftbpro_01m5hfws398g.title: ‘A Legend’—Former Chelsea Star Admits Regret Over Summer Exit
ftbpro_01m5hfws398g.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:00 AM EDTTrevoh Chalobah left Chelsea in the summer. / Oliver Kaelke/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesFormer Chelsea center back Trevoh Chalobah admitted he always dreamed of becoming “a legend” for the Blues before being forced to accept defeat this summer.

Chalobah came through the Blues academy and made 151 appearances for the club across all competitions, but he was sold to Serie A outfit Como this summer for an initial £25.7 million ( $34 million) after years of being made available by the club’s recruitment department.

His sale had been coming, with Chelsea often listening to offers for a player whose homegrown status represented pure profit in the transfer market, but Chalobah still told The Athletic it was tough to accept.
“Definitely,” he reflected. “The team didn’t achieve what we wanted to achieve last season, but I thought I had one of my best seasons, playing the most games and scoring a few goals.

“I’d been there since I was eight and I wanted to be a legend there, but sometimes the way we plan things is not how things work out. As footballers, you’ve always got to be ready to adapt. You could be here one moment, then the next moment you’re somewhere else. But I just thought that it was the best.
“Chelsea means everything to me. I’m still watching the games, keeping in contact with the players and staff.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Chalobah was a regular for Chelsea as recently as last season. / Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesWhen the BlueCo ownership group arrived in 2022, their willingness to invest in new signings meant there was always going to be a need for sales, and offloading academy graduates like Chalobah made the most sense from a business perspective because they are viewed as “pure profit”—the club can declare 100% of any transfer fee as profit as there are no fees to other clubs involved.

The summer of 2023 saw fellow academy graduates Mason Mount, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Ethan Ampadu and Callum Hudson-Odoi all sold. Ian Maatsen, Conor Gallagher, Lewis Hall and Omari Hutchinson followed 12 months later and both Armando Broja and Bashir Humphreys left in 2025. Tyrique George joined Chalobah in leaving this past summer.

Chelsea actually attempted to sell Chalobah on a number of occasions prior to his exit. He rejected a move to Nottingham Forest in the summer of 2023, before suitors failed to meet Chelsea’s asking price in both windows of 2024. That summer, he left on loan to Crystal Palace, only to be recalled in January and establish himself as a regular starter.

Fighting against adversity was a regular theme for Chalobah at Chelsea. While those upstairs were determined to sell him, manager after manager repeatedly put their faith in the center back on the pitch. He started 11 out of a possible 16 games following his return from Palace in January 2025, before that number rose to 31 out of 38 in 2025–26, when only Enzo Fernández, Moisés Caicedo and Robert Sánchez played more league minutes.

The chance to cash in on Chalobah proved too tempting for Chelsea this summer, with the Blues opting to replace him with Maxence Lacroix. Yet, there remains a sense that Chelsea are still in need of further improvement at the back.

Whether Chalobah was the right player to start week in, week out for Chelsea had been the subject of fierce debate for years, but there can be no denying his presence as a homegrown squad player with obvious love for the club was a positive last season.

When Chelsea return to the market for a new defender, they may well find themselves needing more than one. Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Josh Acheampong are all out of contract in 2029 and will all soon need to be the subject of discussions in the boardroom, with Fofana’s future seemingly particularly uncertain after struggling for minutes during the early months of Xabi Alonso’s tenure.

ftbpro_01m5hg52gake.title: Blackburn Rovers vs. Wrexham: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5hg52gake.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay5:30 PM EDTWrexham travel to face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. / Dan Mullan/Getty Images (Blackburn), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham)Wrexham hope to build on their solid foundations when they travel to face Blackburn Rovers in the Championship this weekend.

Phil Parkinson’s side returned to winning ways with a comfortable 4-1 victory over Preston North End last time out, but they face a tougher test against a Blackburn Rovers side sitting above them in the league table. Blackburn are 10th, one point ahead of Wrexham, after surrendering a two-goal lead in last weekend’s draw with West Bromwich Albion.

The Red Dragons could receive a boost with the return of a key player this weekend, as defensive midfielder Ben Sheaf is in contention to be included in the matchday squad. Wrexham were without seven injured players for the win over Preston and will hope their injury situation improves in the coming weeks as they look to climb the table.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Wrexham had four different scorers in their win over Preston North End. / PA Images via Getty ImagesWrexham and Blackburn appear evenly matched ahead of this weekend’s trip to Ewood Park. Although four places separate the two sides, there is only one point between them, with the Championship table tightly congested at this early stage of the season.

Both teams are just one win away from potentially moving into a playoff position. Conversely, a defeat could leave either side hovering just above the relegation places. One victory could therefore change the mood at either club and significantly alter the perception of their respective starts to the season.

Blackburn could revert to a back three against Wrexham. / FotMobTony Mowbray could switch to a back three and mirror the formation favored by Wrexham for this weekend’s clash. That could see Hayden Carter return to the starting lineup alongside Tom Atcheson and Sean McLoughlin, with Ryan Alebiosu and Harry Pickering operating as wingbacks.

Samy Morsy and Kristi Montgomery are almost certain to start in central midfield again. Todd Cantwell could be joined by Oladapo Afolayan in the attacking support roles, with Guðjohnsen likely to lead the line once again.
Blackburn predicted starting lineup (3-4-2-1): Toth; Atcheson, Carter, McLoughlin; Alebiosu, Morsy, Montgomery, Pickering; Cantwell, Afolayan; Guðjohnsen.

Wrexham could make a couple of changes to their starting lineup. / FotMobParkinson started with two strikers in the home win over Preston but could revert to a more conservative approach away from home. Joe Worrall should continue at the heart of the defense, with Dom Hyam and Callum Doyle on either side of him.

There could be a change at right wingback, with Issa Kaboré offering fresh legs in place of Danny Imray. Ollie Rathbone or Lewis O’Brien could also replace Sam Smith in an attacking midfield role. Sheaf could return to the squad but might not be risked from the start.
Wrexham predicted starting lineup (3-4-2-1): Patterson; Hyam, Worrall, Doyle; Kaboré, James, Whiteman, Ekomié; Rathbone, O’Hare; Moore.
