ftbpro_01m5hhy7mkwh.title: How Man Utd Would Line Up Under Julian Nagelsmann
ftbpro_01m5hhy7mkwh.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom GottOct 22, 2026Julian Nagelsmann is among those tipped to take over at Man Utd. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images (Nagelsmann), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Man Utd badge)The pressure on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is growing with each passing day.

A bruising 4–1 defeat to Como in the Champions League, followed by some scathing comments from captain Bruno Fernandes, have left the manager facing an increasingly uncertain future, with a handful of alternatives already being suggested.

Former Napoli manager Antonio Conte has previously been touted as a possible replacement for Carrick, but fresh reports have named Julian Nagelsmann, a long-time target for the Red Devils, as a leading contender. Both men are conveniently out of work and available immediately.
Here’s a look at how United could set up under the former Germany and Bayern Munich boss.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Nico Schlotterbeck could be a target for Nagelsmann. / Sebastian El-Saqqa/firo sportphoto/Getty ImagesGK: Senne Lammens—Nagelsmann wants composure from his goalkeeper and is unlikely to find a better source of that than Lammens, who prides himself on his calm head under pressure.

RB: Archie Gray—Among the most important tactical points for Nagelsmann is an overload in central areas, which he has often done through the use of an inverted fullback. None of United’s current options would appear to fit the bill, but Tottenham Hotspur’s Gray—a natural midfielder anyway—could easily slot into this role with perfection.

CB: Matthijs de Ligt—Big, dominant defenders are always popular under Nagelsmann, who was the manager that took De Ligt to Bayern Munich in the summer of 2022. The pair had a strong relationship during their short period together in Germany.

CB: Nico Schlotterbeck—The uncertainty surrounding Lisandro Martínez’s future means a new left-sided center back is likely to be needed. Nagelsmann could look to his German roots with the in-demand Schlotterbeck, and it would hardly come as a surprise to see Antonio Rüdiger considered as a squad option as he nears the end of his contract with Real Madrid.

LB: Lewis Hall—Hall’s ability as both a left back and a ball-playing midfielder would work well in a typically fluid Nagelsmann setup. United officials have set their sights on the Newcastle United star and would not have to try too hard to convince Nagelsmann of his worth.

DM: Carlos Baleba—Any new manager is going to have to find a way to make Baleba a core part of their squad. The Cameroon international is still going to have to work on his on-ball skills, but there can be no denying his potential if Nagelsmann can connect the dots.

Nagelsmann would enjoy working with Kobbie Mainoo. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesDM: Kobbie Mainoo—Mainoo would be one of the bigger winners of any move for Nagelsmann, who loves a deep-lying playmaker so much that his team regularly includes more than one. Keeping the ball moving, drawing players out of position and spraying passing to the forwards sounds like Mainoo’s ideal job.

RM: Bryan Mbeumo—In a system with one inverted fullback, Mbeumo would be tasked with holding the width on the right. The 27-year-old has been excellent since his move to Old Trafford in 2025 and would relish another tactical challenge.

AM: Bruno Fernandes—Nagelsmann is a manager that could easily try and build his team around Fernandes, a pass-first playmaker constantly looking to make things happen around him. It could be the tactical tweak that reignites Fernandes’s career.
LM: Matheus Cunha—One of Nagelsmann’s wingers often drifts inside to help with the possessional overload. That role lends itself perfectly to Cunha, who is more of a central-minded player anyway.

ST: Benjamin Šeško—If there is one thing Nagelsmann knows how to do, it is maximize a striker. At Hoffenheim, he brought 90 goals and 40 assists from Andrej Kramarić and Mark Uth over four seasons. Timo Werner and Yussuf Poulsen both shone at RB Leipzig, before Robert Lewandowski hit 50 goals in 46 games in Munich. Šeško has the tools to follow that crowd and may simply need some Nagelsmann guidance.
Nagelsmann’s arrival could bring big changes in defense. / FotMobfeed. READ THE LATEST MAN UTD NEWS, ANALYSIS AND INSIGHT FROM SI FC

ftbpro_01m5hj1sx88k.title: Do Real Madrid Still Have a Buyback Clause for Nico Paz?
ftbpro_01m5hj1sx88k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath9:00 AM EDTNico Paz is fast becoming a superstar. / Nicolò Campo/LightRocket/Getty ImagesWednesday was the night Nico Paz came of age, ascending to a new level of superstardom as he orchestrated Como’s historic 4–1 Champions League victory over Manchester United.
The 22-year-old Argentina international was awarded UEFA’s Player of the Match award after a game in whch he scored twice and bagged an assist against the three-time European champions.

It was a sit-up-and-take-notice performance from the young playmaker, once of Real Madrid, who has long been talked up as one of European soccer’s best young prospects and a potential lifeline for Argentina in a post-Lionel Messi world. After dismantling United—and possibly costing Michael Carrick his job—the wider soccer world is now aware that the hype is very real.
Speaking to Movistar Plus after the match, Madrid legend and former youth team coach Raúl González described Paz as “possibly the best player I’ve ever coached.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Nico Paz made eight appearances for Madrid during the 2023–24 season. / Florencia Tan Jun/Getty ImagesRaúl worked with Paz as a teenager at Madrid’s La Fábrica, which he joined as an academy player from Tenerife back in 2016.
The youngster went on to make eight first-team appearances for Los Blancos in the 2023–24 season, scoring his only goal in a Champions League win over Napoli.

That summer Paz made a $6.7 million (€6 million) move to Serie A upstarts Como, where he has gone on to become a leading light—scoring 13 times last season and being named the league’s Best Midfielder 2025–26.
Next. Best Real Madrid Ever. The 25 Best Real Madrid Players Ever—Ranked. dark

At the start of this summer, there was much speculation that Real Madrid would take advantage of a buyback clause of around €9 million ($10 million) to bring the fast developing attacking midfielder back into the fold at the Bernabéu. However, it was instead announced in June that Paz would be staying put for Como’s first season in the Champions League, with the Italian club and Madrid agreeing a new €60 million ($67 million) deal to retain the player’s rights and extend his stay in Italy to 2028.

The arrangement wipes out Madrid’s old buyout options and sell-on clauses, but gives Los Blancos the option of a new buy-out clause set at €80 million ($90 million), which only they and no other club can trigger. That clause is understood to be active only in the summer of 2027. Essentially, Madrid would only be paying €20 million ($22.5 million) net if they opt to re-sign Paz in a year’s time.

So Madrid can still bring Paz home next summer, but will they? The playmaker operates in a central No. 10 role for Cesc Fàbregas’s Como—a notably similar position to that of bona fide superstar Jude Bellingham. Los Blancos also have Arda Güler, another of Europe’s hottest young players, capable of operating behind the striker. As such, a genuine pathway to game time at Madrid is not immediately clear—though that is not necessarily an impediment to president Florentino Pérez.
Nico Paz is the man of the hour. / Nicolò Campo/LightRocket/Getty ImagesSpeaking after Wednesday’s head-turning victory over United, Paz hailed the night as unforgettable.

“It’s one of the most special nights of my life and career, for me and for the club,” he told TNT Sports. “I’m still young, but I’ll never forget it. It was a historic night because we played against one of the best clubs of all time, and to do this at home is incredible. We’re very happy with our performance.
“We have to enjoy every match like we did today. We have to try to repeat this performance. This is historic, it’s the first time we're in the Champions League and we have to enjoy it.”

ftbpro_01m5hmkh6ezj.title: Four Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Replacements PSG Could Sign After ACL Injury
ftbpro_01m5hmkh6ezj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTPSG could look for short-term solutions in the market. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesParis Saint-Germain might well have triumphed over Barcelona in their recent Champions League tie, but that victory came at a significant cost.

Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos both suffered muscle injuries which will sideline them for several weeks of action, but, most tragically, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his ACL at Parc des Princes, likely ruling him out for the remainder of the campaign.

Having allowed Bradley Barcola—it was Kvaratskhelia’s January 2025 arrival in the capital that derailed Barcola’s PSG career—and Ibrahim Mbaye to depart for the Premier League during the summer, the French giants now boast just three senior wingers in their roster. That is discounting Dembélé, who has been transformed into a central striker by Luis Enrique. Désiré Doué is the leader of the pack, supported by newer summer recruits Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts.

But if PSG are going to win their third successive Champions League crown and match what only Real Madrid have done in the post-1992 era, alongside sweeping up domestic titles this season, then Luis Enrique needs a replacement for his Georgian superstar—even if only for the short-term.
Here are four players that could be signed to fill Kvaratskhelia’s shoes.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Marcus Rashford is not a guaranteed starter for Man Utd. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPSG were regularly touted with interest in Marcus Rashford during his unhappy years at Manchester United. While the Englishman has now been reintegrated following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona, there’s still uncertainty over his long-term future at Old Trafford, especially considering his current contract expires in 2028.
As Michael Carrick’s side continue to suffer during their dismal start to the season, during which Rashford has failed to inspire confidence, perhaps the door is left ajar for another exit.

Barça benefitted from the temporary signing of Rashford last season, with the Englishman producing 25 goal involvements across all competitions. He’s exactly the kind of player who could thrive in a less competitive division like Ligue 1, while also boasting the versatility to occupy multiple roles across the front line, as was the case at Barcelona.
Rashford could prove a useful replacement for Doué and Akliouche, who appear the likely winger pairing during Kvaratskhelia’s lengthy road to recovery.

Endrick has starred in France previously. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesDespite Endrick’s agency dismissing speculation over his Real Madrid exit in the near future, the youngster’s limited involvement under José Mourinho points to a possible loan move during the second half of the campaign amid a raft of interest.

Endrick spent half of the 2025–26 campaign in France with Lyon, where he produced consistently eye-catching performances as a striker and wide forward. The 21-year-old scored eight goals and assisted as many during his 21 appearances on loan.

With Kylian Mbappé untouchable and Carlos Espí making a fine impression from the bench during his debut season at the Bernabéu, an imminent increase in game time appears unlikely for Endrick, who has played just four games for Madrid this term.

PSG’s fluid forward line could accommodate Endrick easily. Dembélé could be moved to the wing if necessary to make room in the No. 9 position, while the Brazil international could himself feature on the right flank as Doué shifts to the left-hand side.
Estêvão has been used sparingly by Xabi Alonso. / Harvey Murphy/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAnother Brazilian wonderkid struggling for minutes with European royalty is Estêvão.

Xabi Alonso’s arrival and frequent deployment of the 3-4-2-1 formation at Chelsea has restricted the 19-year-old’s involvement. While capable of playing as an attacking midfielder or right winger, he’s made just seven appearances under his new manager, starting none of the club’s Premier League matches.

With an established forward trio of João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers thriving, and no European soccer to facilitate rotation, it appears inevitable that Estêvão will be forced to accept a bit-part role in Alonso’s first campaign.

While Chelsea would be unwilling to allow a permanent exit for one of the world’s brightest talents, they could sanction a loan switch to Paris to further Estêvão’s development. Enrique would be an incredible tutor to help boost the teenager’s output and confidence.

Said El Mala could prove a relatively cheap solution. / Osama Faisal/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesIf PSG want something more permanent without breaking the bank, they could turn to up-and-coming Köln star Said El Mala.

The Champions League holders already splashed the cash on youthful reinforcements over the summer when recruiting Akliouche and Godts, but Kvaratskhelia’s injury could force them to re-enter the market in search for emerging talents with enormous long-term potential.

ftbpro_01m5hn0f75je.title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid Combined XI: Red-Hot La Liga Leaders Dominate
ftbpro_01m5hn0f75je.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath3:00 PM EDTThe biggest club game in the world features some of the game’s great stars.  / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesCircled in thick red marker pen since the fixture list was announced, the first Clásico of the season is upon us with Barcelona hosting Real Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday.
The meeting of Spain’s great rivals is always box office, but the match has reached new levels of anticipation this autumn, amid a sea of narratives.
José Mourinho returns to the fixture for the first time in 13 years, bringing all the bad blood, baggage and conspiracy theories that contribute to the creation of absolute cinema.

Amid the melodrama, Barcelona’s lightning start means Madrid really need to come out fighting in this game or face the uncomfortable reality that La Liga might be out of their grasp before Mariah Carey has even hit the airwaves.
With a who’s who of the game’s great and good on show, here’s a combined XI of the two rivals’ available players.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Thibaut Courtois is Madrid’s Mr. Dependable. / Alcoba Beitia/Getty ImagesIn reality, there is very little to choose from between two of the best keepers in the business. Joan García was handed both La Liga’s Zamora Trophy (for the league’s best goalkeeper) and the Save of the Season award in 2025–26 and has proven a remarkable signing for Barcelona since joining from Espanyol in 2025.

Courtois though, on his day, is arguably still the best keeper in the world. The 34-year-old has kept only two clean sheets all season, but can hardly be blamed for Madrid’s leakiness. The Belgian has made 29 saves so far in 2026–27 to García’s 15, and boasts a superior save percentage at 76.3% to 68.2%.

Xavi Espart is enjoying a breakthrough season. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty ImagesWith José Mourinho cycling unconvincingly between Denzel Dumfries, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Federico Valverde, the Barça option is the obvious choice.

A barely known quantity prior to this season, Espart—another gem from Barça’s fabled class of 2007—has shone on both sides of the defense this season, despite coming through the academy system as a midfielder.

An emergency option midweek, the 19-year-old shut down both Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué against PSG—he wasn’t dribbled past once all game—and popped up with a goal, showcasing his fine attacking instincts.

Pau Cubarsí is the favorite for the Golden Boy award. / BSR Agency/Getty ImagesNamed the Young Player of the Tournament at the 2026 World Cup, Cubarsí is the favorite to win the coveted Golden Boy award after a sensational year for Barcelona and Spain.

The 19-year-old played every minute of Spain’s triumph in North America and is now well-established as Barça’s key center back. No player in La Liga averages more passes per game this season than Cubarsí’s 98.8.

Dean Huijsen has earned José Mourinho’s trust. /  Ion Alcoba Beitia/Getty ImagesAfter a middling debut season last summer, Huijsen has looked more assured as the ball player at the heart of Los Blancos’ defense so far in 2026–27—Madrid derby red card aside.
The Dutch-born Spain international is regularly the player on the pitch with the most touches, passes and defensive contributions.

Marc Cucurella’s signing was seen as a coup for Madrid. /  Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesMuch was expected of Cucurella when he joined Real Madrid from Chelsea at the outset of the summer. However, the Bernabéu is still yet to see the very best of the World Cup winner.

During the last international break, Luis de la Fuente admitted Cucurella was among those stars who raise their game when pulling on a Spain jersey, saying: “With us, something happens... When they join the national team, they transform. Some sometimes show a level far superior to what they show at their club.”
Still, on his day Cucurella remains a tenacious pest of a defender; a two-way threat as capable of contributing to his team’s attacks as he is at snuffing out those of the opposition.

Rodri could’ve joined Madrid this summer. / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesCoveted by both Clásico clubs in the summer, Barcelona were the pick of the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner—and they are all the better for it.
There is simply no more complete midfielder in the game than Rodri—a one-man shield, conductor and metronome.

ftbpro_01m5hpa2j5na.title: Reimagining Man Utd’s Summer Transfer Window: How Red Devils Could Have Avoided Crisis
ftbpro_01m5hpa2j5na.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott12:00 PM EDTBig mistakes were made in Man Utd’s summer window. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Hall), Mike Morese/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Carrick), Alessio Morgese/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Éderson)The high spirits at Manchester United from the second half of the 2025–26 season have firmly disappeared.

Miserable results have raised questions about the future of manager Michael Carrick, while center back Lisandro Martínez turned the spotlight on the recruitment department with claims that they had not done enough to build on the exciting start of Carrick’s reign.
The issue is not that United were not active in the summer, but that their priorities may have been wrong at a period in which wider squad reinforcements were needed.
With the benefit of hindsight and the ability to live in a world of what-ifs, here’s how United should have approached the summer transfer window.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Losing Casemiro sent Man Utd into a spiral. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesUnited have taken a strangely segmented approach to their squad rebuild. In 2025, it was the year of the attack and 2026 was chosen as the time to fix the midfield, with the defense set to follow over the next two windows in 2027.
What that did was saturate the market for themselves and see them miss out on players whose arrivals would have had more significant impacts.

United wanted to rebuild in midfield this summer without much of a long-term plan. Baleba was always going to be a target, but the Tielemans deal came out of nowhere and the expensive acquisition of Santos was an unnecessary risk after the Brazilian’s quiet 18 months in English soccer.

With the benefit of hindsight, could United have walked back their decision to let Casemiro leave? His exit was announced in January, before a major upturn in form had the Brazilian looking like a superstar once again. BBC Sport state his mammoth wages—£350,000 ($469,000) per week—played a part in letting him go, and at a time in which United are trying to cut costs, perhaps that was unavoidable.

The focus on midfield appeared to be driven more by a lack of numbers, rather than a belief the weaknesses elsewhere were not so severe. Years of poor squad-building and the unfortunate timing of Manuel Ugarte’s World Cup injury saw United backed into a corner.

It is no hot take to suggest United needed a left back, while another center back would have been a huge help and even a cheap striker could have worked wonders in a team that has long held concerns about Benjamin Šeško’s battle with injury.
Those jobs were all pushed into the future, and United are now paying the price.

Éderson looked destined to join Man Utd. / Roberta Corradin/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFirst up, let’s not ignore the fact there was a pressing need for midfield reinforcements. Ugarte’s injury and Casemiro’s exit left Kobbie Mainoo as the only natural central midfielder in the first-team squad. Clearly, that needed addressing.

Tielemans was a nice, cheap acquisition and one that United were right to pursue purely from a cost perspective. It would be easy to rely on hindsight and criticize this move, but United were widely praised for getting this deal over the line at the time.

The Belgian should have followed Éderson through the door, but the Red Devils walked away from a $52 million (£39 million) deal for the Brazilian over fitness concerns. Éderson has since started nine out of Atalanta’s 10 games this season, brushing off whatever issue seemed so problematic.

Knowing midfield was on the agenda, United officials seemed laser-focused on Baleba, but that saw them pass up on players like Mamadou Sangaré or Morten Hjulmand. Cheaper options on the market this summer included Neil El Aynaoui, Chema Andrés or even Youssouf Fofana, who is reported to have caught United’s eye during a loan with Sevilla from AC Milan.
Had they saved a little money, United could have sped up their defensive rebuild.

Ezri Konsa would have been a dream signing. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesA move for Newcastle United left back Lewis Hall failed to materialize before he signed a new contract and boosted his transfer value. Could United have involved themselves in negotiations for Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde before a failed approach on Deadline Day? Would an early bid for Pep Chavarría have deterred Chelsea? Two more Spaniards, Alejandro Grimaldo and Miguel Gutiérrez, were both on the move this summer.

At center back, Aston Villa’s willingness to sell Ezri Konsa is the sort of deal United should have been all over, even if they had little hope of convincing him to snub Arsenal. Luka Vušković was a no-brainer of a signing that Brighton & Hove Albion were incredibly keen to wrap up when given the chance, while the Red Devils would likely have had enough muscle to beat Leeds United to Tarik Muharemović for $45 million (£34 million).

Would there have still been enough money in the bank to bring in a reliable, veteran striker like Danny Welbeck? His switch to Chelsea was a bargain but he may have been swayed by the chance to return to Old Trafford, where his dependable form would have eased pressure on Šeško and Joshua Zirkzee.

ftbpro_01m5hsx7qe5m.title: ‘It’s a Combination’—Youri Tielemans Reveals What Needs Fixing for Man Utd
ftbpro_01m5hsx7qe5m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff11:00 AM EDTMan Utd need to be better across the board. / Luca Rossini/PA Images/Getty ImagesYouri Tielemans was in no doubt after Manchester United’s humbling Champions League result against Como on Wednesday: “We need to try and do better at everything.”

The Red Devils haven’t won since Sept. 10, a run that now stretches to seven matches across all competitions. But while frustrating Premier League draws are one thing, it was quite another being “outplayed most of the game,” according to Tielemans, by a team debuting in the Champions League this season with a young squad. It finished 4–1 in Como’s favor.

Even with United removed from the glories of yesteryear, the scale of the upset was illustrated by comments from Nico Paz, the architect of their downfall on the shores of the lake. “It was a historic night because we played against one of the best clubs of all time.”

Bruno Fernandes took aim at manager Michael Carrick and the instructions from coaches. “That’s on the manager and the staff to say [if it cost the match],” he said, before offering his own opinion on what should have happened. “Sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure and trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable.”

Tielemans didn’t get into a blame game—he separately told MUTV: “We were disjointed as a team, we didn’t play well together, our press was off and when we were on the ball, we could not make the right decisions”—but his broader assessment of what is wrong is arguably just as damning for anyone associated with the team—players included.
“It’s a combination of everything, whether it’s tactical, technical, effort... We need to try and do better at everything,” the summer recruit acknowledged.

“You can be good tactically, but if the effort is not good, or the other way around, it doesn’t matter. You need to be good at everything and we were poor at everything. It’s down to that,” Tielemans added.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“It’s the motivation, the intention, the purpose, the intensity,” says Michael Carrick. / Marco Luzzani/Getty ImagesAsked how Manchester United fix that, Tielemans said it’s nothing different to anything already said. “It’s the same message as we’ve had the last few weeks,” he sighed.

“We can be here and talk about it but we need to show it on the pitch. We can only apologise to the fans. They’re disappointed, we’re disappointed, and the only thing we can do is try and show something on the pitch, which we didn’t do enough of the last few weeks.”

Tielemans’s assessment has echoes of “David Moyes says #mufc must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending,” the viral social media post sent from the club’s official X (then Twitter) account dating from December 2013.
David Moyes says #mufc must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending.

Back then, United had lost two in a row but were only three games without a win. It shows how much higher the standards used to be and what the definition of a crisis was at that time. They’d hammered Bayer Leverkusen 5–0 only two weeks prior and responded by reeling off six straight victories. It’s hard to see how the current team will do that.

Things aren’t about to get easier. Bournemouth visit Old Trafford on Sunday and are in better form after getting a first Premier League win of the season. United failed to beat the Cherries in six attempts during their Andoni Iraola era, twice losing 3–0 at home in that run.

Then comes Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, a Champions League clash with Roma, followed by the visit of Aston Villa to Old Trafford. Villa had their own poor start to the season but have got their act together in recent matches to now leapfrog United in the standings.

ftbpro_01m5ht7h0a5k.title: Wrexham Handed Major Fitness Boost Ahead of Blackburn Rovers Match
ftbpro_01m5ht7h0a5k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay10:11 AM EDTPhil Parkinson will be boosted by the latest injury news. / PA Images/Getty ImagesWrexham expect to have midfielder Ben Sheaf back from injury when they travel to face Blackburn Rovers in the EFL Championship this weekend.

The 28-year-old is arguably the club’s most influential midfielder but has been limited to just one appearance this season because of a series of issues. Sheaf missed all of preseason through injury before returning to action with a standout display in the 2-1 home win over Southampton last month.

Sheaf had hoped to hit the ground running after the recent international break but suffered a groin problem in training that forced him to miss three more matches. The former Coventry City star took part in a full training session Thursday and could return to the Wrexham squad when they travel to Ewood Park on Saturday.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Ben Sheaf only returned for one match before he suffered another injury setback. / Wrexham AFCWrexham could welcome Sheaf back to the matchday squad against Blackburn, while defender Max Cleworth and versatile midfielder George Thomason also took part in the latest training session. It may be too soon for the latter pair this weekend, but both appear to be closing in on a return.

Cleworth has missed five matches since suffering a hamstring injury in the home draw with Burnley, while Thomason has missed nine matches since picking up a thigh injury in the closing stages of Wrexham’s draw with Watford in their second match of the season.

“Sheafo was back in full training today, Tommo and Max did part of the session, so a huge lift for everybody to see those boys out there,” Parkinson told Sports Illustrated. “It really thickens up the numbers in the squad, and it’s a good start getting those lads back on the training pitch.”

Josh Windass suffered an ankle injury in the opening stages of Wrexham’s recent draw with Derby County and was spotted wearing a protective boot after the weekend win over Preston North End. He is set to take the next step in his recovery this weekend, while Nathan Broadhead, Liberato Cacace and Seb Revan remain long-term absentees.

Parkinson added: “Josh has got a boot on to protect his ankle at the moment, but I think that comes off at the weekend and then Kevin [Mulholland] and his team can then really start assessing the ankle and look to progress Josh.

“Broady is out on the grass still doing his fitness work. The next stage for him is striking the ball because it was a thigh injury, but Libby is in the gym at the moment; that's more of a long-term injury.”

ftbpro_01m5htkxj2kp.title: Real Madrid Injuries: Every Player Unavailable vs. Barcelona
ftbpro_01m5htkxj2kp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew HeadspeathOct 24, 2026Real Madrid have four first-team players missing for the weekend. /  Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty ImagesReal Madrid head to Barcelona this weekend knowing that really only a win will do, and not just for bragging rights.

Six points behind in the La Liga title race after just nine games, a defeat to their in-form rivals would be an enormous whack to José Mourinho’s team psychologically, even if the math doesn’t change all that much.
On the other hand, a galvanizing victory against the odds would be just the tonic for Madrid after a mixed start to 2026–27.
Fortunately for Mourinho, he can take a near-full strength squad to Catalonia this weekend as they aim to gain ground. Here’s all the latest Real Madrid injury news ahead of the trip to Barcelona.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Courtois has the flu. / Francois Nel/Getty ImagesIssue: FluPotential return date: Barcelona (A), Oct. 25.There’s late drama surrounding Real Madrid’s starting goalkeeper.

The club issued a statement on the morning of El Clásico saying that Thibaut Courtois would miss the game due to the flu. The Belgian has played every single minute of Madrid’s campaign so far, and his absence would be a devastating blow.
However, Courtois still hopes to play. He hopes to travel with the team to Catalonia and start between the posts.

Rodrygo has been out of the picture since March. / Helios de la Rubia/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesIssue: ACL injuryPotential return date: January 2027Rodrygo has become something of a forgotten man at Real Madrid, having not played for the club since tearing the anterior cruciate ligament of his right knee back in March.
A loose timeline has the Brazilian likely to return to action at the start of next year.

Ferland Mendy’s time at Madrid has been blighted by injury. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesIssue: Thigh injuryPotential return date: November 2026The 31-year-old’s injury problems have been almost constant over the last few seasons. He missed 45 games in 2025–26 alone.

Mendy’s latest setback saw him undergo surgery on a tendon tear back in May, and he continues to work towards full recovery. He recently started taking part in team training again, but is unlikely to be cleared to feature in matches until after the November international break.

Raúl Asencio had surgery in September. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesIssue: Leg injuryPotential return date: January 2027The center back not yet featured for Madrid this season and elected to go under the knife to fix a stress fracture on his right tibia at the end of September, having struggled with the issue for some time.
The exact details of the 23-year-old’s recovery timeline are unknown but he is not expected to return to availability until the new year.

Vinícius Jr will miss the Clásico. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesIssue: SuspendedPotential return date: November 2026A torrid start to the season got a whole lot worse for Vinícius Júnior when he was shown a straight red card for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in the win over Villarreal. That action—along with his subsequent angry remonstrating with the referee—earned Vinícius Jr a four-game ban domestically.
As a result, he was forced to miss the win over Sevilla and will sit out the Clásico, as well as the upcoming fixtures against Racing Santander (Nov. 1) and Valencia (Nov. 7).
The Brazilian will be available for selection again in La Liga for the home game against Celta Vigo on Nov. 21, following the next international break.

ftbpro_01m5hxnk94se.title: ‘We’ve Fallen Behind’—Phil Parkinson Gives Verdict on Crucial Wrexham Appointment
ftbpro_01m5hxnk94se.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay11:30 AM EDTWrexham and Phil Parkinson are getting into a new normal. / Cody Froggatt/PA Images/Getty ImagesPhil Parkinson believes Steve Nickson has “settled in well” after being appointed Wrexham’s inaugural sporting director last month.

The Red Dragons identified Nickson as the standout candidate for the newly created role as they look to revolutionize their transfer strategy and establish a global scouting network. The former Newcastle United head of recruitment has been tasked with building and leading Wrexham’s scouting and player recruitment operations as the club seeks to expand its reach in the transfer market.

Wrexham want to explore untapped global markets and sign high-potential players who can either make an immediate impact on the first team or be developed and sold for a significant profit. Parkinson has admitted that the club have “fallen behind” in recruitment during their remarkable rise through the divisions, with the transfer strategy yet to reach standards targeted in the Championship.

Asked about his relationship with Nickson, Parkinson told Sports Illustrated: “Yeah, good. I mean, the very early stages for Steve. Obviously, [it’s] an area where we’ve obviously fallen behind with the speed of our progress on the recruitment, both at home but more internationally, really. Having that knowledge of players which Steve brings with him, and a kind of ready-made knowledge and a network with him into the club, but obviously the benefits of that will be seen over a longer period of time. Steve’s settled in well at the club and we're enjoying working with him.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Steve Nickson is well known for his ability to spot young talent. / IMAGO/Aleksandar DjorovicWrexham have signed only two players from European clubs during the Hollywood era, with Liberato Cacace arriving from Empoli last year and Jacques Ekomié joining from Angers this past summer. Both players came from clubs competing in the Italian and French top flights, rather than from less-explored markets that could offer greater value for money.

The Welsh club have already identified Eastern and Northern Europe, South America and Central America as markets they want to explore, believing they could unearth hidden gems and secure better value for their investment.

Although the main focus is on signing high-quality, high-potential players for relatively low transfer fees to strengthen the first-team squad, Wrexham also recognize that developing players and selling them for a profit will be an important part of their long-term strategy. The proceeds could then be reinvested in the squad, helping make the club more sustainable.

That is where Nickson comes in. Wrexham interviewed several candidates for the sporting director role during the summer, but the former Newcastle man stood out for his ability to combine modern scouting methods with Parkinson’s more traditional approach. The 52-year-old was highly regarded at St. James’ Park, having built a reputation for identifying promising young talent and played a key role in signing Sven Botman and Joelinton before Newcastle’s Saudi-backed takeover in 2021.

“Bringing in a sporting director and building out a scouting department is the right thing for the football club,” Williamson told The Athletic last month. “Not just for now, but the next 10, 15, 20 years. Again, building something better.”

ftbpro_01m5hyzk5xhv.title: ‘Business’—Man Utd Make Michael Carrick Sack Decision After Como Disaster
ftbpro_01m5hyzk5xhv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell1:00 PM EDTMichael Carrick’s future at Manchester United is anything but certain. / Nderim Kaceli/BSR Agency/Getty ImagesDespite Manchester United’s dreadful run of form to start the season, Michael Carrick’s job is reportedly safe for now.

The pressure has been gradually increasing on the English manager with each passing week the Red Devils fail to collect three points, and he is firmly under fire following the club’s embarrassing 4–1 defeat to Como on Wednesday.

United are now winless in their last seven matches across all competitions, and have just two wins in 2026–27, which came against the recently promoted Ipswich Town and Champions League debutants Sabah.

Past managers have been fired for less, but Carrick woke up Thursday morning still in charge. The Daily Mail report it’s “business as usual” for the manager, who is expected to hold his typical  pregame press conference on Friday for United’s league clash with Bournemouth.
Carrick will no doubt face more questions about job security, as well as any follow-up thoughts on Bruno Fernandes’s incendiary comments concerning the team’s tactics in the lopsided Como defeat.
Takeaways As Carrick Faces the Sack for Dismal Como Defeat. dark. Next. Man Utd Como takeaways

Replacements are waiting to take Michael Carrick’s job. / Marco Luzzani/Getty ImagesFrom the outside looking in, it appears the club still has faith in Carrick to turn things around despite the Red Devils’ dismal run of form and public pushback from the likes of Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez.

It’s hard to deny, especially after United didn’t cut ties with Carrick following Wednesday’s Champions League disaster. The manner in which his team lost, combined with their other recent results and performances, would have been more than enough cause to sack the 45-year-old.
But the club could have ulterior motives for leaving Carrick in charge for at least this weekend’s Bournemouth game. The Daily Mail suggests the decision “buys United time” to solidify a replacement.
Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann are the two most recent names linked with the job, along with Fabian Hürzeler.
A new boss would mark the eighth permanent manager in United’s dugout since the departure of the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013.

Manchester United have a formidable stretch of fixtures coming.  / Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesCarrick and United are desperate for a lifeline, but their schedule is unrelenting. It’s not a great sign when the club’s best chance of a win before the November international break comes against Bournemouth, a team who has taken points from the Red Devils in their last six meetings.
Then, the 20-time English champions are headed to Stamford Bridge, where the likes of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro will be giddy at the chance to attack United’s bumbling backline.

After Chelsea comes a Champions League battle with Roma, who have lost just one match—a clash with Real Madrid they should have won—across all competitions this season. Rounding out the fixtures is a date with an Aston Villa side that has seemingly found their form after a poor start to the season.
By the time United return from the international window to take on Liverpool at Anfield, they could be in an even worse position than they are now.

ftbpro_01m5hza3c9z6.title: Barcelona Injuries: Every Player Unavailable vs. Real Madrid

paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath2:00 PM EDTJules Koundé is a major doubt for the weekend. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesIt could be a season-defining Clásico when Barcelona meet Real Madrid on Sunday.
Hansi Flick’s men have been faultless in La Liga after nine games and have the chance to go nine points clear of their great rivals with a win at Camp Nou this weekend.
While victory far from ends the title race, it would strike a deep psychological blow to Madrid and make Barcelona the first team in history to open the season with 10 straight wins.

Barça would naturally want to count on all their key players for such a pivotal game. However, Flick has several availability concerns to deal with. Here are all the injury issues the team is contending with ahead of the clash.

Roony Bardghji was struck down in preseason. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesIssue: ACL injuryPotential return date: May 2027The young Swedish winger suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear in preseason training is set to spend the entire campaign in recovery.
Bardghji was rumored to have been deemed surplus to requirements by Flick and could well be moved on when he returns to full fitness.

Andreas Christensen could return next month. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesIssue: Thigh injuryPotential return date: November 2026After missing more than half of last season with a serious knee injury, Christensen picked up a thigh strain in September and is set to be sidelined for over a month.
The center back, who has made six appearances so far in 2026–27, is slated to return to action after the November international break.

Eric García’s knock comes at an unfortunate time. / Gabriel Colchero/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesIssue: Thigh injuryPotential return date: November 2026García left the field in discomfort during the 5–2 win away at Real Betis and was later confirmed to have picked up a thigh issue.

The club put his recovery timeline at between three and four weeks, ruling him out of the clash with Real Madrid and likely to return either just before the November international break, or straight after.

Dani Olmo was forced off against PSG. / Ibrahim Ezzat/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIssue: Adductor injuryPotential return date: November 2026Olmo was a casualty of Barcelona’s 4–2 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain midweek, limping off in the first half and sparking fears over his availability for the weekend’s showdown with Madrid.
Barça later confirmed an adductor injury and have suggested the midfielder will be out for around a month as he recovers.

Two Barça right backs picked up injuries against Betis. / Gabriel Colchero/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesIssue: Ankle injuryPotential return date: October 2026Koundé was one of two right-back injuries during the Betis victory, along with García, creating a potential headache for Flick in the build up to the Clásico.

“We hope that maybe he [Koundé] could also be an option for the weekend, but we have to see. We have to wait,” Flick told reporters regarding the Frenchman’s minor ankle sprain, but that was before he missed even more training sessions.

ftbpro_01m5j1qa6ywx.title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid: Four Key Battles That Could Decide El Clasico
ftbpro_01m5j1qa6ywx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 AM EDTThis year’s Clásico is full of Ballon d’Or nominees. / Gongora/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Yamal), Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Mbappé)Monday night brings the Ballon d’Or, with the gala ceremony for soccer’s most coveted individual prize taking place in London on Oct. 26.

The real show, though, will be at Camp Nou the day before, where a fifth of all nominees for the main award—as well as pair of Kopa Trophy nominees and two for the Yashin Trophy—will take to the field for the first Clásico of 2026–27.

Sunday’s showdown promises to be quite the spectacle, with the seemingly unstoppable force that is Barcelona intent on breaking records for the most consecutive wins to start the season, while driving a stake into the heart of José Mourinho right before Halloween.

Madrid, meanwhile, need a statement performance to convince the world (and themselves) that they are serious about a title race in La Liga, or face the ignominy of being out of the running after just 10 games.

The backdrop of inter-club relations reaching new lows and Mourinho’s return have added an extra spicy dressing, but it’ll still all come down to what happens between the white lines. Here are four areas where the match could be won and lost.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Xavi Espart has been a revelation for Barcelona. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesXavi Espart, 19, began the season as a little-known academy graduate but has quickly blossomed into one of the breakout stars of the season so far.

Another of Barça’s burgeoning class of 2007, Espart came through as a midfielder but had been used largely as a left back before a mini injury crisis saw him thrown in at the very deepest of ends on the right side of defense up against Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.
Impressively, the teenager was not dribbled past once all night and even popped up with a fine goal.

With Eric García and Jules Koundé likely to still be out at the weekend, Espart will face off against another of Europe’s speediest wide players in Yan Diomande, who has found his feet at Real Madrid after six goal contributions in his last four games and has given Los Blancos’ attack new verve amid Vinícius Jr’s absence.
Kylian Mbappé has been in lethal form this season. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesInterestingly, Kylian Mbappé has only won twice in the nine matches he has played against Pau Cubarsí.

The last time the pair came up against one another was in the summer’s World Cup semifinal, when the teenage defender put in a defensive masterclass for Spain to keep Mbappé and the rest of France’s attackers at bay.
Repeating that kind of shutout at Camp Nou would be some achievement for the Golden Boy favorite, with Mbappé in unstoppable form in 2026–27.
The Frenchman has 12 goals in 12 appearances so far, and a record of six in seven games against Barcelona since joining Madrid in 2024.

Jude Bellingham is thriving as Madrid’s No. 10. / Alcoba Beitia/Getty ImagesRodri’s patrolling and controlling was badly missed during the first hour of Barça’s midweek defeat to PSG, with the summer signing rested ahead of the weekend.
While Hansi Flick’s team struggled with tracking the space invaders of Vitinha, Fabián Ruíz and João Neves on Tuesday, they face an altogether different challenge against Madrid.

Possession-based engine-room dominance is not Los Blancos’ speciality, but Rodri will be kept busy with stopping Jude Bellingham slaloming about in space and crashing into the box with the all the devastating subtlety of a meteor.

While Rodri quietly herds play in the direction he wants it to go, there are few in the world who can grab a game by the scruff of the neck quite like Bellingham, with the Englishman having seemingly reverted to his 2023–24 performance levels since the World Cup.

Lamine Yamal has double figures in goals and assists already this season. / Ibrahim Ezzat/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesTwo Ballon d’Or nominees and Spain teammates will go shoulder to shoulder on Sunday, with Marc Cucurella given the unenviable task of stopping Lamine Yamal on Barça’s right wing.

The 19-year-old looked uncharacteristically off the pace against PSG—even helping gift the French champions the game’s opener—but still rallied in the second half to score a magnificent individual goal. He is now the first player in Europe’s major leagues to achieve both 10 goals and 10 assists this season.

ftbpro_01m5j210aha2.title: ‘Probably Yesterday’—USWNT Legends Address Problem Emma Hayes Should Have Already Fixed
ftbpro_01m5j210aha2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell12:30 PM EDTEmma Hayes has some puzzles to solve for the USWNT. / Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesThe U.S. women’s national team was hit with a few reality checks this fall, and two-time World Cup winner Becky Sauerbrunn delivered another: It’s time for the Stars and Stripes to stop experimenting and start “building chemistry” ahead of next summer’s showpiece event.

All eyes were on the reigning Olympic champion this October as it faced off with reigning world champion Spain in two blockbuster friendlies. Many viewed the matches as a preview of the 2027 World Cup final, and banked on the USWNT giving a La Roja team without Aitana Bonmatí and Mariona Caldentey a proper fight.

Except Emma Hayes’s squad suffered a poor 2–0 defeat to Spain in the first friendly and then settled for a 2–2 draw in the second. The matches highlighted just how much work needs to be done if the USWNT wants to dethrone the defending cup holders in Brazil.
Sauerbrunn, alongside fellow two-time World Cup winner Sam Mewis, dove into a key aspect hurting the USWNT’s preparations for soccer’s grandest event coming next summer.

The USWNT was outclassed by Spain. / Scott Taetsch/USSF/Getty Images“The idea of building chemistry versus building depth. When is it time to focus on the chemistry part?” Mewis asked on The Women’s Game podcast.

“It’s probably yesterday,” Sauerbrunn answered. “It’s tough because Emma has probably not had her first-choice roster since the [2024] Olympics. There have been a slew of injuries and so it is kind of by necessity that she is trying so many different combinations.
“The most successful teams are not the best players that are in the XI; it’s the best team that makes up the XI. At some point, you just have to go with chemistry.

“Going into a World Cup year ... with not many training camps left, with not many games, I’ve seen as many partnerships as I can see. I’m going with that. I’m building reps. I’m building chemistry. And if I can get all my players back, that’s great. That will provide depth when I need depth. I’m figuring out my best partnerships right now.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The USWNT is expected to follow up Olympic gold with a World Cup title. / Brad Smith/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesExpectations are always high for the USWNT, but they are exponentially higher following the team’s gold medal triumph at the 2024 Olympics. The U.S. is hungry to celebrate a record-extending fifth World Cup, but Hayes’s team cannot climb the mountaintop without chemistry.

After the Stars and Stripes’ defeat to Spain, Hayes made five changes to her XI for the rematch. Phallon Tullis-Joyce came in between the posts, Gisele Thompson commanded the left flank, Ashley Sanchez got the nod in midfield and Trinity Rodman and Claire Hutton came into the attack.

Mallory Swanson, the hero for the USWNT against Brazil at the Paris Olympics, did not start either game. Naomi Girma, Emily Sonnett, Catarina Macario and Sam Coffey were also missing from Hayes’s roster.

There is less than a year until the USWNT is expected to make a run to the World Cup final, and Hayes is still playing with her lineup, trying to find winning combinations while missing key members of her XI. It’s hardly ideal, considering the behemoths waiting on the world stage.

Getting by the likes of England or Spain without true chemistry and team cohesion will be near-impossible. When the USWNT reunite in November, Hayes must seriously consider heeding Sauerbrunn’s advice and start rolling out the best XI at her disposal.

ftbpro_01m5j3c09k2h.title: The 10 Highest Paid Soccer Players in 2026
ftbpro_01m5j3c09k2h.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 22, 2026There are few surprises among the world’s highest-paid stars. / Tnani Badreddine/DeFodi Images/DeFodi/Getty Images (Yamal), Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Messi), Fayez NURELDINE/AFP/Getty Images (Ronaldo)It’s no secret that soccer players now sit among the richest athletes in the world as wages, transfer fees and the value of commercial contracts all increase exponentially.
From modest beginnings, the sport has reached an eye-watering financial state, with its leading performers reaping the benefits of the vast sums pumped into the game.
Courtesy of Forbes, we can now see exactly the riches on offer to the planet’s most famous soccer stars, as they have collated a list of the 10 highest-earning players for the 2026–27 season.
So, without further ado, here is a full breakdown of the richest in the business.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Cristiano Ronaldo’s pay packet cannot be matched. / Fayez NURELDINE/AFP/Getty ImagesThe longstanding rivalry between Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi has fueled the modern era, and despite the fact their illustrious careers are edging to a conclusion, they remain the biggest earners soccer has to offer.

Debate has long raged over which of the serial Ballon d’Or winners was better, but there’s no contest when it comes to their earnings. Ronaldo dwarfs his nemesis when comparing their respective pay packets, as he’s projected to earn an astonishing $300 million through his Al Nassr wages—which are reportedly around $4.5 million per week—and commercial partnerships during the current campaign.

In fact, Messi is predicted to earn less than half as much as Ronaldo, although sympathy will be non-existent when the Argentine collects $145 million in total come the end of the season. Interestingly, he will earn more off the field ($75 million) than on it ($70 million) following a flurry of recent endorsements, including with OpenAI and Duracell.

Kylian Mbappé rounds out the star-studded top three as the only other player to hit nine digits. The Real Madrid forward’s astronomical wages ($673,000 per week) account for much of his $100 million earnings, but his recent partnership with Swiss shoe brand On has bolstered his bank balance significantly.

The Frenchman is one of three Real Madrid players in the top 10. Vinícius Júnior, fresh from signing a bumper new contract with the Spanish giants, sits in fifth place at $76 million for the 2026–27 season, which is three places above teammate Jude Bellingham on $45 million—the highest-earning Englishman in world soccer.

Real Madrid have the most representation in the top 10. / M Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesBellingham’s compatriot Harry Kane pockets slightly less at Bayern Munich, taking home $42 million overall. The leading soccer ambassador for shoe brand Skechers also has partnerships with Crayola and Google Gemini which contribute to his extraordinary wealth.

Another devastating sharpshooter is perched in fourth, with Erling Haaland the only current Premier League player within the top 10. The Manchester City dynamo will earn $85 million for the season, with his profile having been boosted by significant social media activity in recent years.

Lamine Yamal might only be 19 years old, but he’s already soccer’s sixth-highest earner on $55 million. That total looks set to rise and rise as the years pass, with Barcelona already paying him just shy of $500,000 every seven days. Brands will be desperate to work with the teenage sensation and that can only be positive news for his bank account.

Former Liverpool forwards Sadio Mané and Mohamed Salah round out the list in seventh and 10th respectively. The former’s massive wages at Al Nassr have propelled him into the equation, placing him just behind Yamal on $54 million, while even a wage reduction at Trabzonspor hasn’t removed Salah from the rich list as he prepares to claim $40 million across the campaign.

ftbpro_01m5j79qazpw.title: ‘S--- Talkers’—Ex-USMNT Striker Bashes Alexi Lalas Over Landon Donovan Takedown
ftbpro_01m5j79qazpw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 22, 2026Alexi Lalas (left) got caught in the crossfire of Landon Donovan’s row with Eddie Johnson.  / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty Images (Lalas), Elysia Su/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Donovan)Former U.S. men’s national team striker Eddie Johnson turned his attention from Landon Donovan to Alexi Lalas in a scathing new rant, calling out his fellow countryman for sitting “behind a mic” and “talking s---.”

Donovan—perhaps unknowingly—started a war of words following the September-October international break when he cautioned fans about getting too excited about the new, young prospects starring for the U.S. men’s national team. The legendary striker then named dropped many players who he believed never reached their full potential, including Johnson.

Johnson came swinging back, criticizing Donovan for putting down the current generation and then picking apart Donovan’s failed European career. He also insisted: “I did everything you did with fewer opportunities.”

Lalas soon joined the conversation, coming to Donovan’s defense on his State of the Union podcast. “Just because you’re Eddie Johnson and you stayed longer over in Europe doesn’t make you better [than Donovan].”

Johnson was quick to respond with a new scathing social media attack. “Now I only speak when these s--- talkers mention my name. Earlier today I saw a post where Alexi Lalas was saying I’m comparing my career to Landon Timothy Donovan and that was never the case.”
The 42-year-old then unleashed again on Donovan, summarizing his major points from his last takedown.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Landon Donovan failed to make his mark in Europe. / Alexander Hassenstein/Bongarts/Getty ImagesJohnson made sure to clarify the intent of his original message was to “stop criticizing everyone else that were young and promising during their careers for not reaching their potential.” He then used it as a segue to ruthlessly rip Donovan’s career ... again.

“Why don’t we talk about you not living up to the hype in Germany after receiving the Golden Ball in the U-17 World Cup. Where he went to Leverkusen and struggled and ran back to MLS where it was easy and less pressure,” Johnson wrote.

Indeed, a 16-year-old Donovan joined Bayer Leverkusen in February 1999, but never made a single senior appearance for the German team before he was sent on loan for nearly four years with the San Jose Earthquakes, where he started building his MLS legacy.

Such an underwhelming stint at Leverkusen was a trend on the European stage for Donovan; he failed to leave his mark at Bayern Munich and Everton as well. But the former USMNT star ultimately became a legend in MLS with the LA Galaxy.

Landon Donovan (center right) won four MLS Cups with La Galaxy. / Jeff Gross/Getty Images“To me that’s a failure, got tested against the big dogs and folded. Why don’t he speak about that or why don’t we speak about that?” Johnson continued. “No one took away from the work he did in the MLS or with the national team until he took that sabbatical.”

Johnson is referring to the 144-day break Donovan took back in December 2012 that lasted until March 2013. Donovan previously said he “needed” the time away. “I was a little overwhelmed at the time, and I knew if I did not stop it would not be good for anybody,” he said after he returned to the game.

Johnson viewed the lengthy absence differently. “I worked my ass off scoring goals for Jurgen [Klinsmann] when he took that break during the most important time for our country during World Cup qualifiers lol but he kills Pulisic in the World Cup bc he thought he was faking a injury in the Belgium game when he came off talking about you wrap that up you try to get back out there for your country you do what you have to and he took a sabbatical lol make it make sense. If the shirt meant so much play through it you hypocrite.” [sic]

Alexi Lalas starred for the USMNT at the 1994 World Cup. / Lutz Bongarts/Bongarts/Getty ImagesAlmost like Johnson suddenly remembered the purpose of his new post was to call out Lalas, he then shifted the focus to the former defender.

“Lalas who struggled in Europe as well why do we talk about that? This guy sits behind a mic talks s--- as well, played in a World Cup and most successful years were in MLS and he’s a considered a great and a Hall Of Famer? What did he do that I didn’t do?”

Johnson seemingly didn’t learn his lesson when inserting his name next to Donovan. The former striker only ever lifted two Gold Cups with the USMNT and never won any other club trophies across his stints in MLS and Europe.

Lalas won four honors with the LA Galaxy, including the 2002 MLS Cup and the 2000 Concacaf Champions’ Cup. He also won the 1995 U.S. Cup and a gold medal at the 1991 Pan American Games with the Stars and Stripes. The defensive stalwart appeared 96 times for the USMNT and starred in the 1994 World Cup as well.
There’s also nine goals for the USMNT on Lalas’s résumé, only 10 less than the 19 Johnson scored in his 63 caps.

ftbpro_01m5j7nykpst.title: Jurgen Klopp Reveals Which Team He Is Supporting in Sunday’s Clasico
ftbpro_01m5j7nykpst.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew HeadspeathOct 22, 2026Jürgen Klopp is backing Barça this weekend. / Christian Charisius/picture alliance/Getty ImagesJürgen Klopp has revealed he will be supporting Barcelona when he watches the Clásico this weekend, as he tends to favor the “better team” in the fierce rivalry.
Barça and Madrid face off for the first time in 2026–27, with the two due to lock horns at Camp Nou this Sunday for what promises to be blockbuster viewing.

Hansi Flick’s team can put nine points between themselves and Madrid with a win, which would also see Barça break the record for the most consecutive victories at the start of a La Liga season—they’re currently perfect through nine games and are seeking to make it 10.
José Mourinho and his men, meanwhile, are out to spoil the party and prove that they are still title contenders after a mixed start to the campaign.

Jürgen Klopp has had some run-ins with Real Madrid during his career. / Sven Hoppe/picture alliance/Getty ImagesMatches between Barcelona and Madrid are always appointment viewing in the soccer calendar, but this particular meeting has added significance due to Mourinho’s return and the form of Ballon d’Or nominees Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé among others.
Germany manager Klopp will be among the many fans watching worldwide on Sunday, as he revealed to DAZN during halftime of Bayern Munich’s 2–2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League.
“Of course I’ll watch El Clásico between Barcelona and Real Madrid. I’ve watched this game at every stage of my life,” he said.
Best Barcelona. The Best Barcelona Players of All Time—Ranked. dark. MUST READ
Asked about his personal preference, the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund manager admitted he has historically leaned more towards Barça.
“In the past, I was more of a Barcelona supporter because I was against the actions of Pepe and other Madrid defenders,” he is quoted as saying.
“Today, I support the better team. And looking at things at the moment, that is probably Barcelona.”

Klopp reportedly rejected interest from Real Madrid prior to joining Liverpool in 2015, while he went on to lose two Champions League finals (2018, 2022) to Los Blancos during his spell on Merseyside.
While he will be watching as a fan, Klopp will have a vested interest in the performance of one player on show on Sunday: Barcelona’s German forward Karim Adeyemi.
Madrid could also lineup with Antonio Rüdiger, although the German defender retired from international duty earlier this year.

Lamine Yamal and Barça are red hot going into the weekend. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesShould Barcelona win at home on Sunday, they will become the first team in La Liga history to win 10 consecutive matches at the start of a season.

With their 5–2 victory over Real Betis last week, Barça equalled the nine-match winning run set by Real Madrid under Miguel Muñoz at the outset of the 1968–69 campaign—a record they have the chance to surpass against their great rivals this weekend.
It has been a lightning start for Flick’s side who have averaged 4.33 goals per game so far and may quietly have their eyes on a whole host of league records this season.
Just as he was 13 years ago, Mourinho will be desperate to stop the parade.

ftbpro_01m5j8mwge59.title: ‘He’s Crazy’—Ashley Young Sends Man Utd Stern Warning About Antonio Conte
ftbpro_01m5j8mwge59.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff2:30 PM EDTAntonio Conte has won 10 national championship as player and manager. / Francesco Pecoraro/Getty ImagesFormer Manchester United captain Ashley Young has warned the club that hiring Antonio Conte to potentially replace Michael Carrick would be a “disaster.”
In short, his style and demands are the antithesis to the group of players he would inherit.

The serial-winning Italian, who won five Serie A championships as a player with Juventus, five more as a manager with Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, and the Premier League with Chelsea, is currently available after leaving Napoli by mutual consent in May.

Carrick is thought to still retain the support of the Manchester United hierarchy, despite Como handing the club its second-worst Champions League-era defeat ever on Wednesday night and extending an ongoing winless slump to seven matches.

Immediately after the final whistle in northern Italy, Carrick made a beeline for corner of the stadium where the traveling United fans were housed, apologizing for what had just happened. He prioritized that over engaging with his players and was critical of the effort he saw—“If you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

The current streak bizarrely follows a remarkable run last season during Carrick’s interim leadership when the team took more points from the final 17 games than champions Arsenal. What’s weird is it’s mostly the same players now getting massively different results.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Success comes at a price. / Claudio Villa/Inter/Getty ImagesBut would Conte, who revolutionized Chelsea off the back of a dreadful 2015–16 season to take them to the Premier League title in his first year in charge, be the right person instead? Young, who spent just shy of nine years at Old Trafford and then 18 months at Inter with Conte, thinks not.
“He is crazy,” the 2020–21 Serie A champion said on The Overlap Daily show.

Conte is intense and demanding, which brings success, but it doesn’t last. He is famously a short-term fix, having held 10 positions in 20 years as a manager, and his longest appointment lasted three seasons at Juventus more than a decade ago. The retired midfielder has otherwise done two years or less everywhere else he’s been.
Young questions whether Manchester United players already accused of lacking physical capacity would thrive to that style of management.
Next. How Man Utd Would Line Up Under Conte. How Man Utd Would Line Up Under Conte. dark

“[Conte] is a bit like Diego Simeone on the sidelines. You hear him non-stop,” Young said. “Training is intense, there’s a lot of running. There was a lot that he did. The training sessions were a lot of 11 vs. 11, at times a little bit boring.

“Meetings were long. If we lost a game, we could go into a meeting and stop literally everything [else]. You could be in there three or four hours. I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places because, not just the players, the board he tries to test mentally. I think people get annoyed at him and they’re like, no it’s time for you to go.”
One of Conte’s coaching mantras is getting his players to “eat grass,” as he’s said in the past. Not literally, of course, but metaphorically by the amount of ground they cover in a match.
“A lot has been talked about Manchester United’s running stats. If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster,” Young concluded.

ftbpro_01m5jdc4rg4t.title: Report: Real Madrid Make Ballon d’Or Boycott Decision After Two-Year Absence
ftbpro_01m5jdc4rg4t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 22, 2026Kylian Mbappé is one of the favorites to win the Ballon d’Or. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty Images (Mbappé), Franck Fife/AFP/Getty Images (Mbappé)Real Madrid have reportedly ended their Ballon d’Or boycott and will be in attendance for soccer’s biggest ceremony next week.

Los Blancos have not attended the lavish event since Rodri lifted the Men’s Ballon d’Or over Vinícius Júnior back in 2024. Once the club learned the Brazilian winger finished second in the voting after winning the Champions League, La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup, it condemned the proceedings and refused to show up to the ceremony.

The boycott bled into 2025, with not a single representative from the Real Madrid men’s team and the club’s hierarchy making an appearance for a second year in a row. Reports emerged before the festivities claiming the club and France Football failed to reestablish relations after their monumental rift.
Los Blancos’ self-imposed exile is seemingly coming to an end, though. According to L’Équipe, Real Madrid plan to attend the 2026 ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre on Monday, Oct. 26.
The club’s nominees are expected to make the trip to England just one day after a potentially league-defining Clásico at the Camp Nou on Sunday.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Kylian Mbappé is gunning for his first Ballon d’Or award. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesOne of the favorites to take home the Men’s Ballon d’Or award this year is Kylian Mbappé. The France international was the top scorer in La Liga—where he won a second straight Pichichi Trophy—and the Champions League in 2025–26.
Mbappé was also the top scorer at the 2026 World Cup, where he buried 10 goals en route to France’s fourth-place finish. In total, the forward scored 58 goals for club and country.
Mbappé followed Real Madrid’s lead the last two years and did not attend the ceremony. But he already confirmed he will be in London on Monday.
“El Clásico and then Ballon d’Or ceremony? Let’s go for it,” Mbappé said after Real Madrid’s thumping 4–1 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Should he win the award for the first time in his career, Mbappé is going to make sure he is there to collect in person.

Jude Bellingham starred for England at the 2026 World Cup. /  Jared C. Tilton/FIFA/Getty ImagesIt’s no surprise Real Madrid’s four nominees for the Men’s Ballon d’Or award are the four stars who showed up for club and country in 2025–26. Jude Bellingham earned the nod after a sensational World Cup for England off the back of a tireless season in a white shirt.
Mbappé is one of the only other individuals who had just as impressive a World Cup campaign. The Frenchman became the competition’s all-time leading scorer at just 27 years old.

Then there’s Vinícius Júnior, who was Real Madrid’s best player in the second half of the season and also Brazil’s best player at the World Cup. Summer signing Marc Cucurella rounds out the list for his exploits with Spain en route to World Cup glory.

Marc Cucurella won the 2026 World Cup with Spain. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesCaroline Weir might play for OL Lyonnes now, but she is nominated for the Women’s Ballon d’Or for her efforts during her final season with Real Madrid. It’s her second consecutive year up for the honor.

Los Blancos are also well-represented for the Kopa Trophy, with Yan Diomande and Felicia Schröder picking up nominations. It’s the Barcelona duo of Lamine Yamal and Vicky López expected to take home the prizes, though.
Thibaut Courtois is up for the Yashin Trophy for the fourth time in his illustrious career. The goalkeeper previously added the award to his cabinet in 2022.

ftbpro_01m5jhx3tcak.title: Bruno Fernandes’s Home Burglarized After Como Defeat, Police Launch Investigation
ftbpro_01m5jhx3tcak.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 22, 2026Bruno Fernandes was the victim of a crime on Wednesday. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester United captain Bruno Fernandes’s house was reportedly burglarized on Wednesday night, with thieves getting away with “a number of items” from the midfielder’s residence.

Fernandes was in Italy during the time of the break-in, representing United in the Champions League. Following the Red Devils’ 4–1 loss to Como, Cheshire Police responded to an incident at his residence.

According to The Athletic, “three unknown men” were spotted in the rear garden of a neighboring property. The police headed to the scene after receiving tips of the “suspicious activity,” but the perpetrators got away before the authorities arrived.

United confirmed to The Athletic Fernandes’s family was fortunately not home at the time of the break-in, which occurred around 8:30 p.m. BST (3:30 p.m. ET). Items were stolen from the property, though, and a formal police investigation is underway.

The incident is latest break-in at the home of a high-profile Premier League player. Manchester City center back Rúben Dias had his Cheshire home burglarized back in January while he was playing an away Champions League game as well.
Jack Grealish and Raheem Sterling have also been victims in the same area.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United are massively struggling.  / Stefano Guidi/Getty ImagesThe burglary comes amid a particularly trying time for Fernandes, who publicly called out United manager Michael Carrick after Wednesday’s lopsided defeat to Como. The Portugal international expressed his frustration at the team’s tactics after the Red Devils were embarrassed in Italy.

Carrick delivered fighting words back, insisting no tactics will help “if you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back.” The traded blows from the two figureheads only added to the crisis plaguing the Red Devils.

United find themselves amid a seven-game winless run, with their last victory coming back on Sept. 10 against Champions League debutants Sabah. The only other win Carrick’s men have claimed this season was against the newly promoted Ipswich Town.

The dreadful run of form has players pointing fingers. Lisandro Martínez called out the club’s director of football Jason Wilcox in a sensational rant following United’s 2–0 loss to Atlético Madrid, questioning the lack of sufficient recruitment done in the summer.

Now, Fernandes has placed the blame on the coaching staff. Carrick is still in charge, but it remains to be seen for how long, especially if United cannot get past Bournemouth at Old Trafford this weekend.
