ftbpro_01m5jnrkcf9t.title: USMNT Receives Major Advantage for Concacaf Nations League Quarterfinals
ftbpro_01m5jnrkcf9t.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 22, 2026The USMNT is coming off a perfect fall international window. / Vanessa Luna/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team will now play both legs of its Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie against Haiti on home soil during the November international break.
Concacaf approved Haiti’s request to move the first leg to Inter Miami’s Nu Stadium, as part of a larger motion from the country to play its “home” Concacaf matches on the territory of its opponent.

Haiti has not been able to play within its borders since July 2021 after the assassination of president Jovenel Moïse. Political unrest made the conditions unsafe, and in March 2024, gangs took over the Stade Sylvio Cator, Haiti’s national stadium.

Since then, Haiti has been hosting matches throughout the Caribbean. Its clash with the USMNT on Nov. 14 was supposed to unfold in Kingston, Jamaica, but the Haitian Football Federation (FHF) requested the ability to now have “home” venues in North or Central America.

“Under this exceptional arrangement, the FHF may be permitted to play its designated home matches in Concacaf-sanctioned competitions in the territory of its opponents, rather than being limited to the Caribbean region as required under the current regulations,” Concacaf said in a statement.

“This flexibility will remain in place for as long as the security situation in Haiti persists. However, each match will require separate approval from the Concacaf Administration, agreement of the respective opposing Member Association and confirmation that the selected host stadium fully complies with Concacaf's stadium guidelines.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

The USMNT has not played away from home in two years. / Charlotte Wilson/Getty ImagesThe Stars and Stripes now get to play both legs of their quarterfinal tie in front of home crowds. They will kick off the November international window against Haiti in Miami before they head to Cincinnati for the second leg on Nov. 17.

It extends a staggering run on home soil for Mauricio Pochettino’s men. They have played 32 consecutive games in the U.S. across the last two years, and by the time the next window ends, that number will increase to 34.
The USMNT benefited from hosting the 2025 Gold Cup and co-hosting the 2026 World Cup. It also hosted the 2024–25 Concacaf Nations League finals.

The last time the Stars and Stripes had to play in front of a visiting crowd came on Nov. 14, 2024, when they faced off with Jamaica in Kingston for the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals. The match, which ended in a 1–0 win for the Americans, was only the third match of Pochettino’s tenure.

The Argentine has since gotten very used to playing on U.S. soil and his team has reaped the awards. In the September-October international break, the USMNT won all four of its friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, backed by emphatic crowds across the country.

Mauricio Pochettino is hoping to end 2026 with a bang. / David Berding/USSF/Getty ImagesThe November international break will be the last bit of competitive action for the USMNT this year. It will also mark the last appearances for many of the team’s biggest names before the calendar flips to 2027.

But there will be a December camp, in which the Stars and Stripes will take on Jamaica at Chase Stadium in Fort Lauderdale. Since there is not a designated December international break, American players who belong to European clubs will not be able to attend.

Pochettino will instead have a squad of MLS players for the international friendly on Dec. 13. New faces that made a splash during the fall friendlies could be back in the Argentine’s ranks, like Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis.
Those still alive in the MLS Cup playoffs, though, will remain with their clubs on the quest for glory.

“As we continue to build our group, this is an excellent opportunity to work with many of the MLS players and potentially see some new faces,” Pochettino said. “Jamaica is the type of team we could see in upcoming tournaments including World Cup qualifying, so it’s a great opportunity and experience for these players.
“Of course, we love to play in Fort Lauderdale and to have the support of the amazing fans in the area.”

ftbpro_01m5m1kq3nyc.title: ‘Selfish Babies’—Wayne Rooney Lets Rip at Man Utd Duo for Publicly Burying Club
ftbpro_01m5m1kq3nyc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:50 AM EDTWayne Rooney (right) took aim at the under-fire duo. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images (Fernandes, Martínez), The United Stand (Rooney)Wayne Rooney has hit out at Manchester United duo Lisandro Martínez and Bruno Fernandes for their recent criticism of the club, accusing the pair of being “babies” and throwing the rest of the team under the bus.
Just as United were trying to move on from Martínez’s comments against the recruitment department, a tough 4–1 defeat to Como led to Fernandes questioning Michael Carrick’s tactics.

It has turned into an ugly situation, with the pressure on Carrick’s shoulders growing with each passing minute. In Rooney’s eyes, this past week has shown exactly what is going wrong at Old Trafford.

“When Martínez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart, and that was the start,” he told The United Stand. “We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players, they don’t want to take responsibility.

“You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and never mind who your manager was. There were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson didn’t talk, but I’d run through a brick wall for him on the pitch because I want to play for myself, I want to play for the club, I want to play for the fans.
“These players, they’re selfish. They care about themselves, they don’t care about their teammates, don’t care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

“If they're not getting what's right for them ... they’re like babies and just throwing their toys out of the pram and go and try and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves. If they’ve looked at themselves, if they’re honest with themselves, then start looking at other people.”

Rooney believes the pair should be playing for their futures. / Stefano Guidi/Getty ImagesRooney went on to claim that this United squad is full of enough talent to succeed, but challenged the players to prove their worth to the team.

“Martínez, for instance, as much as the fans will agree and say, ‘oh yeah, this is brilliant, he’s coming out and speaking against the club,’ he’s doing it to take heat off himself,” Rooney continued.

“Bruno, he’s having probably the worst run of form he’s had since he’s been at the club and again, it’s no coincidence, he’s putting pressure on someone else because he doesn’t want to face it. He doesn’t want to deal with it himself.

“If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martínez looks himself in the mirror, all the players ... they’ll find what is looking back at them is them and it’s not good enough. They need to show more.

“They’ve been brought into this football club for a reason, because they are good players. World Cup winner, Premier League Player of the Year last year ... where are you? Show me. Show me why you deserve that title.”

The pressure remains on Carrick heading into Sunday’s visit from Bournemouth. He is expected to remain in charge for that fixture, but an extension to a seven-game winless run would undoubtedly raise further questions about the manager’s future.

ftbpro_01m5m2j0krme.title: Arsenal vs. Everton: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5m2j0krme.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray8:30 PM EDTArsenal vs. Everton has been an ever-present Premier League fixture for the past 34 years. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesArsenal face their 226th match against Everton when returning to Premier League action at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners, fresh from their 2–2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, are aiming to keep within touching distance of Manchester City, who currently lead the standings by three points. Hard-fought victories over Leeds United and Nottingham Forest since the international break haven’t been enough to usurp the perfect Cityzens.

Meanwhile, Everton journey to north London off the back of their first defeat of the campaign at the hands of Chelsea, and David Moyes will demand a more resilient performance this time around. The Toffees have only won two of their seven Premier League matches, but they would be thrilled to add to a collection of four draws when facing Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta, who represented both clubs during his playing career, knows his players will have to improve in the final third if they’re to overcome a stubborn defense. The defending champions managed just one shot on target during their unspectacular 1–0 win at the City Ground last weekend, with a more polished display required in front of their own supporters.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Arsenal are strong favorites for this one. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesThere’s little time for Arsenal to rest as their hectic October continues. They have already played four matches since the international break concluded, and the Everton clash is the first of five more games before the next hiatus in November.

But Arteta’s squad depth has allowed him to navigate the busy calendar with few issues, with the Spaniard able to rotate personnel against Everton without reducing the quality of his starting lineup. That’s a luxury Moyes simply doesn’t possess.

This encounter is unlikely to be filled with goal-mouth action considering the impressive defensive records and tame attacking returns of both teams in the Premier League this season. The more efficient side should enjoy the greater success—and that’s almost certain to be Arsenal.
The Gunners have the superior roster, greater confidence and home advantage for the upcoming duel.
Arsenal will continue without the injured duo of William Saliba and Christos Tzolis, while Piero Hincapié could sit out another match following the ankle injury sustained in his post-Leeds warm-down.

However, the big disappointment for Arsenal is the quad injury sustained by Bukayo Saka against Bayern midweek, with the Englishman lasting just 10 minutes before being replaced. Arteta confessed that “it doesn’t look good at all” for Saka after the match, and some reports have suggested he may be missing for around two months.
Noni Madueke will take over from Saka on the right-hand side after scoring the winning goal against Forest last Sunday. Eberechi Eze, who netted at Bayern, will line up on the other flank.
Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly might be optional changes made by Arteta, who will be keen to keep his team as fresh as possible against an Everton team which didn’t play midweek.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Everton (4-2-3-1): Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Ødegaard, Eze; Havertz.
Everton’s XI has been settled for much of the season and any changes from the Chelsea defeat will be subtle. Moyes is fortunate to have an entirely healthy squad for the trip to the capital.

Thierno Barry will be aiming to continue his strong goalscoring form, supported by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in the No. 10 position. Behind the Englishman will be his compatriots James Garner and Harrison Armstrong, with Jack Grealish on the left wing.

The defense should be unchanged from last weekend, meaning Ainsley Maitland-Niles will line up against his former side at right back. Christian Nørgaard could also feature from the bench against the club he departed over the summer.
Jordan Pickford will be tasked with keeping out a number of his England teammates at the Emirates.
Everton predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Röhl, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry.

ftbpro_01m5m3cgh8f2.title: ‘The Only One’—Enzo Maresca Reveals Erling Haaland Return Plan for Aston Villa Trip
ftbpro_01m5m3cgh8f2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:10 AM EDTErling Haaland is back in contention. / Lexy Ilsley/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesManchester City manager Enzo Maresca has confirmed Erling Haaland is “100%” available for Saturday’s Premier League trip to Aston Villa.

Haaland picked up a foot injury last weekend in his side’s 3–2 win over Ipswich Town and, amid doubts over his fitness, went unused on the bench in Tuesday’s victory over AEK Athens in the Champions League—a fixture for which he could have feasibly been rested anyway.

The difficulty ramps back up this weekend when City travel to face Villa in Saturday’s early game, and with concerns still lingering over Nico O’Reilly, Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovačić, Maresca was delighted to confirm his star attraction will be back in the lineup.
“[The injured players] can all be available or not in terms of still doubt,” Maresca revealed. “Yesterday, they were all improving, and we’ll see this afternoon.
“For sure, Erling is the only one 100% available.”

Haaland already has eight goals in just seven Premier League appearances and sits three clear of both Alexander Isak and João Pedro in the scoring charts at this early stage of the season. A record-tying fourth Golden Boot to match Thierry Henry and Mohamed Salah is already in his sights.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

City are already battling injury issues elsewhere. / Matt McNulty/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesCity are still reeling from the news that winger Antoine Semenyo is going to miss two months of action through his own injury.

Maresca’s forward line has yet to be truly tested without Semenyo, with the AEK Athens game giving him chance to rotate as Allan came in on the wing and 17-year-old Floyd Samba started in place of Haaland. It was the Phil Foden show as the Englishman netted a hat trick and set up a goal for Rayan Cherki, who Maresca described as “one of the best players in Europe” when at his best.
Villa should provide a much sterner test for a City side searching for an eighth successive victory to start the new Premier League season.

Jérémy Doku should replace Semenyo on the wing against Unai Emery’s side, who face the daunting prospect of having to try and stop Haaland, although few teams boast a record against the Norway international as impressive as Villa.

In five appearances, Haaland has only netted once against the Villans, and that came in his first meeting all the way back in 2022. He has since gone four games without scoring, missing two more through injury and sitting out another on the bench.

Villa had a slow start to the season but have rediscovered the sort of form that took them into the top four again last year. Emery’s side have won five of their last six in all competitions, with a 2–2 draw against Brentford the only blemish on their record in over a month.

ftbpro_01m5m53tyweq.title: Man City Predicted Lineup vs. Aston Villa: Haaland Returns for Big Away Day
ftbpro_01m5m53tyweq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack12:15 PM EDTErling Haaland earned midweek respite.  / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesTame midweek opposition presented Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca with the perfect opportunity to offer key players respite, and the Italian will hope his roster is fresh in time for Saturday’s tricky trip to Aston Villa.

City extended their winning start to the Premier League season to seven games with a 3–2 victory over Ipswich Town last weekend. Chelsea’s record of nine successive wins to kick off their title defense in 2005–06 is certainly under threat, and Maresca’s side will draw level with 2019–20 Liverpool should they prevail in the West Midlands.

The Cityzens have had their issues with Unai Emery’s side over the years and have lost on their previous three visits to Villa’s home. So, the visitors are aiming to overcome a developing hoodoo at Saturday lunchtime.
Here’s how City could line up for their trip to a not-so-happy hunting ground.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—Clean sheets have been relatively hard to come by, and an improving Aston Villa team whose new arrivals are starting to purr are bound to test the under-fire Italian.

RB: Matheus Nunes—Rico Lewis impressed in the week, but he doesn’t appear to be a viable usurper at right back. Nunes should thus come back into the team, and likely deal with Villa’s forward forays from full back.
CB: Rúben Dias—The skipper was at least afforded some midweek respite, as Maresca took him off with 10 minutes to play.
CB: Marc Guéhi—It’s hasn’t exactly been the cleanest couple of weeks for Guéhi, who won’t want to develop an ‘error-prone’ tag.

LB: Joško Gvardiol—Nico O’Reilly remains an injury doubt, so Gvardiol looks set to get the nod at left back. His positioning in possession will be key to stabilizing City’s rest defense and preventing Villa from running amok on the counterattack.
CM: Ayyoub Bouaddi—The young Moroccan has been outstanding in recent outings, and has likely played his way into Maresca’s starting lineup on Saturday.

CM: Elliot Anderson—It’d be risky for Maresca to go to Villa Park, given how proficient the hosts are at progressing the ball through the middle, with an Anderson x Enzo Fernández pivot. A combination of the former and Bouaddi makes more sense, providing the defense with sterner protection.
RW: Phil Foden—Strike while the iron’s hot. Foden hasn’t merely scored in back-to-back games since returning from suspension, he completed his fourth Man City hat trick in their midweek victory.

AM: Rayan Cherki—Cherki has worked in tandem with Foden before, and the pair will dovetail between the lines at Villa Park. The Frenchman provided another magical sequence in the week, scoring City’s third goal with a sumptuous reception and finish.
LW: Jérémy Doku—The X-factor wide man has to be carefully managed after returning from injury. There were no midweek minutes, so Doku should be fit and firing here.

ST: Erling Haaland—After hobbling off the field against Ipswich last week, Haaland was an unused substitute for the battering of AEK Athens. Maresca has since confirmed that the Norwegian is good to go for Saturday’s match, allowing FPL managers to breathe a collective sigh of relief.

ftbpro_01m5m570mcdm.title: ‘Civil War’—Man Utd ‘Divided’ Over Potential Carrick Replacements
ftbpro_01m5m570mcdm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:30 AM EDTMan Utd are considering a series of options. / Steve Bardens/Getty Images (Howe), Stefano Guidi/Getty Images (Carrick), Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty Images (Nagelsmann)Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is under immense pressure at Old Trafford and could well be fighting for his job.

A miserable start to the season has forced United to consider their options in the dugout but, according to the Daily Mail, there is significant discontent when it comes to these conversations, with key figures divided over the club’s next move.

Technical director Jason Wilcox, the target of Lisandro Martínez’s recent rant, is said to be at odds with recruitment chief Christopher Vivell, with the two influential figures pushing for different managers to be targeted in the event of Carrick’s departure, which in itself is still not a given.

United have drawn up a shortlist that reportedly stretches to six candidates, although there is an awareness that some are likely unattainable, further limiting the options to United if they decide to make a change.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Fabian Hürzeler has shone with Brighton. / Steve Bardens/AMA/Getty ImagesIt was early on in United’s current slump that Fabian Hürzeler’s name was first mentioned in this conversation, and considering his electric start to the season with Brighton & Hove Albion, it is not hard to see why.

Some reports have gone as far as to name Hürzeler as United’s top target for the role, although the excitement is usually short-lived. Not only are there doubts as to whether he would take the job, but The Telegraph recently revealed it would take a “world-record fee” to convince the Seagulls to terminate Hürzeler’s contract.
A fee of around $29 million took Julian Nagelsmann to Bayern Munich in April 2021, so United would have to dig deep if they want Hürzeler. Optimism is, predictably, slim.

Antonio Conte is perhaps the biggest name available. / Ivan Romano/Getty ImagesJust like Hüzeler, Antonio Conte was among the first names brought up as a potential replacement for Carrick. A handful of Italian outlets went hard early on, quickly describing him as the top target and suggesting talks over an agreement were already underway. Conte has publicly denied such contact at present, but generally open to considering his next move.
He is still widely accepted to be in the running. The former Napoli boss is said to be keen on the job and, unlike Hürzeler, is free to take over immediately, given he is currently unattached.

The Athletic point to potential concerns over Conte’s volatile management style and the prospect of high-profile issues, although many fans are hoping for somebody with his firm hand to come in and address any behind-the-scenes issues.
Kieran McKenna has similar connections to Carrick. / Robin Jones/Getty ImagesLinks to Kieran McKenna have been floating around for months without ever really going anywhere.

Touted as a candidate back in September, McKenna’s ties to United are similar to Carrick. He spent five years in various roles at Old Trafford, including as scout, U-18 manager and assistant to Ole Gunnar Solskjær in the same backroom staff as the current boss. He earned plenty of credit for his time with the first team and went on to catch the eye in his five-year stint with Ipswich Town.

McKenna has been out of work since the summer, having surprisingly quit Ipswich upon guiding the club back to the Premier League, and is another who could step in immediately. Just how interested United would be in replacing Carrick with a similarly inexperienced clubman is up for debate.

Eddie Howe has plenty of Premier League experience. / Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesUnited have an uncomfortable history with Eddie Howe, who was pushed as a candidate by former sporting director Dan Ashworth when Erik ten Hag was fired in 2024. Sir Jim Ratcliffe wanted Ruben Amorim instead and Ashworth was out of the door not long later.

It is now thought that Wilcox, who is leading the search for potential candidates, favors Howe and those with proven experience in the Premier League already. He is not alone in his admiration for Howe, who has been in the conversation for nearly every major job going for the best part of a decade after impressing with both Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

The gamble with Howe comes with the fact that he is yet to test himself at a club with the sort of pressure that comes with a move to Old Trafford. He has managed Newcastle in the Champions League, but the Man Utd monster is unlike any other in the English game. Is he ready?

Julian Nagelsmann left Germany after the World Cup. / Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesWhile Howe is yet to reach the very top level of management, Julian Nagelsmann knows all about it. He worked his way up from Hoffenheim to RB Leipzig and, eventually, Bayern Munich. That high-level experience is thought to be a decisive factor for United recruitment chief Vivell, who worked with Nagelsmann in Leipzig and has long searched for a reunion, including at former club Chelsea.

United looked at Nagelsmann in May, before Carrick was handed a permanent contract, and the links have recently resurfaced. Reports have named Nagelsmann as a “leading candidate” to replace Carrick, although it must be stressed that Vivell answers to Wilcox, not the other way around.
Still only 39 years old, Nagelsmann remains one of the most exciting young managers in the game, and his immediate availability, after resigning his Germany national team post, works in his favor.

ftbpro_01m5m7fs7ctd.title: Chelsea Predicted Lineup vs. Tottenham: Horror Martinez Injury Forces Big Change
ftbpro_01m5m7fs7ctd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack12:30 PM EDTMike Penders will fill in for the injured Emiliano Martínez. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesChelsea are improving under Xabi Alonso, and the Spaniard described their upcoming duel with London rivals Tottenham Hotspur as a "nice one" after celebrating victory at Everton.

Their 2–0 win at Hill Dickinson Stadium was the sort that the Blues haven’t had much of in recent years. They showed grit and resilience to defeat a previously unbeaten opponent thanks to a pair of opportunistic Pedro Neto strikes.

They broke a Merseyside hoodoo by claiming three points, and now they’re aiming to perpetuate their dominance over a familiar foe. Tottenham Hotspur have earned just one measly Premier League victory at Stamford Bridge in the 21st century, and were the last team in England’s top-seven divisions to notch their first win of the season—doing so on Monday night against Frank Lampard’s Coventry City.
Chelsea supporters must surely be looking forward to Saturday’s clash, and here’s the team Alonso could pick for Spurs’ visit.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Mike Penders—With Emiliano Martínez sidelined for weeks after undergoing jaw surgery, it’s time for young shot-stopper Penders to step up between the posts. The Belgian makes his first Premier League start this weekend.
CB: Josh Acheampong—Alonso is fond of the academy graduate and is likely to be preferred to the more chaotic Wesley Fofana on the right side of Chelsea’s defense.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—Lacroix will remain a stable presence at the heart of Alonso’s backline.
CB: Levi Colwill—Colwill has donned the armband in Reece James’ absence, but Moisés Caicedo was given the responsibility last weekend at Everton.

RWB: Pedro Neto—Remarkably, Neto scored his first Premier League brace on his 187th appearance in the competition. He now lines up against a club that has been tenuously linked with his signing in recent transfer windows.

CM: Jordan Henderson—The veteran Englishman has proven his worth since the international break, having struggled alongside Valentín Barco at Brentford in a 3–0 defeat. A far better partner certainly helps.

CM: Moisés Caicedo—It’s no secret that the Ecuadorian makes Chelsea infinitely better. He’s been excellent since returning from injury, and he’ll have to keep tabs on the wily James Maddison at the Bridge.

LWB: Marco Palestra—While Jorrel Hato teed up Chelsea’s opening goal last weekend and seems to have taken to a wing back role, Alonso could shake things up by introducing Palestra to the left flank. The Italian is comfortable on both sides, and supporters are intrigued to see what he can offer after arriving in the summer.

AM: Cole Palmer—Palmer has a good record in this fixture and will aim to take advantage of a Spurs defensive structure that tasks Sandro Tonali with so much to do in midfield. Their duel could be imperative to deciding the outcome.

AM: Morgan Rogers—Rogers was unable to continue his productive start in Chelsea colors last weekend, but he has the ideal fixture to return to the stats sheet on Saturday. The Englishman recorded six goal contributions in six matches against Spurs while at Aston Villa.

ST: João Pedro—The Brazilian international is in supreme form to start the new season and has spoken about his burgeoning friendship with Palmer ahead of Saturday’s match. Don’t be surprised if the pair combine to sink the Lilywhites in west London.

ftbpro_01m5m7jyk62k.title: Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Brighton: Four Changes From Midweek Chaos
ftbpro_01m5m7jyk62k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray9:00 AM EDTLiverpool will make alterations in attack against Brighton. / Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport/Getty ImagesLiverpool are searching for their first Premier League win at Anfield since late April when welcoming in-form Brighton & Hove Albion to Merseyside this Sunday.

The Reds have failed to win any of their three home matches in the league this season, stumbling to underwhelming draws with Nottingham Forest and Fulham before humiliation at the hands of Manchester City. They have been victorious in their three Anfield encounters in other competitions, however, including an utterly chaotic 4–3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday.

Andoni Iraola will be wary of the threat posed by Brighton, who currently sit four points above Liverpool, and the Spaniard must navigate an awkward encounter without a host of injured players—including the likes of Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong.
Here’s how the injury-stricken Reds could line up.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: Alisson—Despite the best efforts of Alisson, Liverpool have now conceded three goals in three of their matches since the international break. The Brazilian’s defense has undermined him.

RB: Ronald Araújo—Araújo made it back-to-back Champions League goals with his back-post header against Villarreal as he continues to impress in a red jersey. As things stand, Liverpool will be eager to make his loan permanent.

CB: Jérémy Jacquet—Jacquet has been excellent since trading France for England, but a nervy showing against Villarreal wasn’t the best preparation for Brighton. Sunday’s opponents lead the Premier League for goals scored this season with 23 in seven matches.

CB: Virgil van Dijk—Liverpool’s captain must improve on his error-strewn performance midweek, which included gifting Villarreal their opener with a dismal header back to Alisson. Brighton are certain to take advantage of any sloppiness in the home side’s defense.

LB: Milos Kerkez—For all his flaws, Kostas Tsimikas has been delivering what Kerkez hasn’t during recent weeks: assists for his teammates. The Hungarian could learn a thing or two about crossing from his fellow left back.

CM: Ryan Gravenberch—After missing the Brentford fightback through suspension, Gravenberch is available once more in the Premier League. He will be thankful for a return to the double pivot after featuring as a No. 10 and right back against Villarreal.

CM: Alexis Mac Allister—Mac Allister’s resurgence is proving essential for Iraola. The Argentine, who aimed a dig at his former manager Arne Slot recently, is back to his all-action best, epitomized by his well-taken brace on Tuesday.

RW: Rio Ngumoha—Mac Allister might have scored twice against Villarreal, but Ngumoha was deservedly the Player of the Match. The fleet-footed teenager tormented Liverpool’s visitors and even managed to match a record held by Lamine Yamal and Cristiano Ronaldo during the triumph.

AM: Florian Wirtz—Relief was the prevailing emotion around Anfield as Wirtz finally opened his account for the season, with the German’s fine finish the highlight of an impressive cameo from the bench last time out. Iraola will demand more of the same from his under-fire playmaker.

LW: Bradley Barcola—Barcola missed training on Thursday, but that was merely load management. The summer signing should return to the XI against Brighton, buoyed by his hat-trick against LASK in the Champions League last week.

ST: Alexander Isak—The Swede netted the winner against Brentford to take his tally to five for the campaign, and Brighton will be concerned by his resurgence. While never overly involved in build-up play under Iraola, he’s found his shooting boots at long last.

ftbpro_01m5m9tf24gw.title: Man Utd Predicted Lineup vs. Bournemouth: Major Fernandes Decision Made
ftbpro_01m5m9tf24gw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray12:30 PM EDTBruno Fernandes has come under fire after public criticism of his manager and coaching staff. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesPressure is reaching unbearable levels for Michael Carrick and his players as they prepare to face Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday.

Manchester United have played their last three matches on the road, but they return to Old Trafford with the aim of ending a seven-game winless streak across all competitions. The embarrassing 4–1 defeat to Como midweek was the ultimate low point of a disastrous run of performances and results.

Carrick’s life has been made all the more challenging by injuries across his roster, with some high-profile names set to miss Bournemouth’s visit. Therefore, the Red Devils aren’t able to make many changes from a disastrous evening in northern Italy.
Here’s how United could line up this weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GK: Senne Lammens—The Belgian looked on in disbelief as the defense ahead of him was frequently sliced to pieces by Como’s fluid forward line. He needs much better protection against Bournemouth.
RB: Leny Yoro—Yoro was absent on Wednesday through suspension, but he’s available for United’s next domestic test. He could enter the team at right back to help solidify a misfiring backline.

CB: Harry Maguire—United have conceded 10 times during their three most recent home matches against Bournemouth—two 3–0 defeats preceding a chaotic 4–4 draw. They need an imposing performance from Maguire to prevent further disaster.

CB: Ayden Heaven—After missing the last two matches through illness, Heaven could be immediately reintegrated into the starting lineup. With Lisandro Martínez potentially injured and Matthijs de Ligt being eased back into the action, Carrick might be forced to call upon the 20-year-old.
LB: Diogo Dalot—Noussair Mazraoui was among United’s worst performers midweek, with the Moroccan playing the first half at left back. Dalot could replace him to make room for Yoro’s introduction.

CM: Youri Tielemans—Despite Tielemans being an undeniably clever signing at the time, he’s done nothing to alleviate United’s glaring problems in midfield. Perhaps a partnership with the more cautious Carlos Baleba can benefit the Belgium international.

CM: Carlos Baleba—Within 12 minutes of his arrival off the bench against Como, Baleba had gifted the hosts their third goal of the game with a terrible pass. He can’t afford to make any such mistakes against Bournemouth.

RW: Amad Diallo—Perhaps the only United player who left the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with their dignity intact, Carrick desperately needs Amad’s infectious energy and dynamic dribbling against the Cherries.

AM: Bruno Fernandes—Carrick has refused to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy after his extraordinary rant on Wednesday, during which he criticized his manager and the coaching staff. For now, however, his place in the XI seems secure.
LW: Matheus Cunha—United are still waiting for Cunha’s campaign to spark into life. Whether as an attacking midfielder, false nine or left winger, the Brazilian has struggled to make his mark.
ST: Bryan Mbeumo—With Benjamin Šeško still injured, Mbeumo appears likeliest to lead the line against Bournemouth. He’s United’s top scorer in the Premier League this season with four goals.

ftbpro_01m5m9xfx6wp.title: Aston Villa vs. Man City: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5m9xfx6wp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack7:30 PM EDTAston Villa are out to bring Man City’s winning run to an end. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Aston Villa badge) Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Man City badge)Manchester City are aiming to become just the third team in Premier League history to win their opening eight games of the season when they take on Aston Villa away from home on Saturday.

The Cityzens secured their seventh successive league victory at the start of Enzo Maresca’s reign against the newly promoted Ipswich Town last weekend, although they were made to work by Gary O’Neil’s side.

Things came much easier in the week, as Maresca rotated and oversaw a convincing victory over AEK Athens on Matchday 3 of the Champions League, ensuring they bounced back from the 4–2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

Jürgen Klopp’s Liverpool at the start of their title triumph in 2019–20 and Chelsea, who began their title defense in 2005–06 with nine straight wins, make up the club Man City are desperate to join this weekend.

However, they’ll have to overcome a developing West Midlands hoodoo to do so. The Cityzens are winless on their previous four visits to Villa Park and have lost their last three. Combine that with Villa’s improvement over the past month, and this has the makings of a really tricky test for the visitors.
The hosts sit 12th in the table, and have won five of their previous six games in all competitions.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Erling Haaland will return to Maresca’s starting lineup at Villa Park. / Matt McNulty/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesAshley Young was a first half substitute for the Villans when Man City last escaped Villa Park with three points. Rúben Dias and Bernardo Silva were on the scoresheet in a 2–1 victory for the Cityzens back in December 2021.

This hasn’t been a happy hunting ground for the perennial Premier League champions since Unai Emery took the reins, but the Villa boss is no longer up against a City team led by Pep Guardiola. It’s Maresca’s show now. Discouragingly for the away side, Emery has won two of his three head-to-head tussles with their new manager.
It’s the sort of fixture that, if City win, they’ll truly believe themselves to be capable of dethroning Arsenal.

The hosts are set to be without Johan Manzambi for City’s visit due to a muscle injury. Last week’s match-winner at Newcastle United missed the win over Viking and has been doubtful for Saturday’s game since.

Emiliano Buendía should thus start as Villa’s No. 10, working in tandem with impressive summer arrival Nicolas Jackson. Manzambi’s absence means there’s likely to be room for either Alysson or Ibrahim Mbaye to start down the right flank.

Emery has concerns at left back, given that Matteo Ruggeri is sidelined and Ian Maatsen is recovering from an ankle injury. There‘s a chance Maatsen features, and Matty Cash is expected to be back on the opposite side.
Aston Villa predicted lineup vs. Man City (4-2-3-1): Suzuki; Cash, Lindelöf, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; Alysson, Buendia, McGinn; Jackson.

Maresca has confirmed that Haaland is 100% fit to play at the weekend, having been given a midweek rest. The Norwegian sharpshooter suffered a foot injury against Ipswich Town last Saturday, but there was never a sense that Haaland would miss any time as a result.

On the contrary, Man City are without Antoine Semenyo potentially up until Christmas due to a knee injury. Maresca has the likes of Iliman Ndiaye and Jérémy Doku to call upon as mitigation, and the in-form Phil Foden could also be used out wide.
Nico O’Reilly’s lingering back issue means Joško Gvardiol is set to start at left back, while Mateo Kovačić and Matheus Nunes may have to pass late fitness tests.
If Nunes isn’t fit, Rico Lewis could retain his spot after impressing against AEK Athens. Abdukodir Khusanov is another option.
Man City predicted lineup vs. Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Bouaddi; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

ftbpro_01m5m9z5vbx9.title: Liverpool vs. Brighton: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5m9z5vbx9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray8:00 PM EDTLiverpool have won their last four Anfield showdowns with Brighton. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Liverpool), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Brighton)Two of England’s form sides go head-to-head when Liverpool host Brighton & Hove Albion in the Premier League on Sunday.

Both clubs have triumphed in four of their last five matches across all competitions, but it’s the Seagulls who somewhat surprisingly lead their upcoming hosts in the Premier League. An exceptional start to the campaign has yielded 16 points and an impressive 3–0 win over defending champions Arsenal, while the Reds have only picked up 12 points from their seven outings.

Liverpool’s recent triumphs have been laced with imperfections, however, largely stemming from the defense. They have conceded three times to LASK and Villarreal in their last two European outings, while also benefitting from a numerical advantage in their comeback victory over Brentford last weekend.

Brighton have been much more convincing, despite their goalless draw with Czech side Jablonec in the Conference League on Thursday. The 5–0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace last Sunday marked a sixth successive victory in all competitions, during which time they scored 22 times and conceded just twice.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
There should be goals on Merseyside. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesThis one should be a whole lot of fun as two sides with frightening attacking potential lock horns.

Brighton have scored a staggering 23 goals across their Premier League outings this season—the most of any side in the first seven games—and while Liverpool have netted just nine in the competition thus far, they have scored 15 times in their four matches across the Carabao Cup and Champions League.

While Brighton’s defense has been impressively watertight—they’re currently on a run of five successive clean sheets—Liverpool have been less organized, as evidenced by them conceding three goals in three of their last four matches.
Both managers demand high-intensity, attack-first soccer, hopefully resulting in an end-to-end and frenetic contest. Which way will it go? Only time will tell.
Iraola has been dealt a host of injury blows for Brighton’s visit, including long-term absentees Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitiké.

But Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong have recently entered the treatment room, too, with neither available for the weekend. Victor Muñoz is also a doubt, according to Iraola, after missing the midweek victory over Villarreal with a knock.

Bradley Barcola missed training on Thursday as Liverpool seek to manage his workload, but Iraola has confirmed he’s “fine” for the weekend. He could come into the team on the left wing, replacing Cody Gakpo in the process.
Ryan Gravenberch is available in the Premier League once again after missing the Brentford match through suspension. He will partner the in-form Alexis Mac Allister in the double pivot.
Milos Kerkez, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz will all come back into the XI after starting on the bench against Villarreal.
Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Brighton (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araújo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.
Hürzeler made sweeping changes for the European trip to Czechia on Thursday, with only Groß, Bart Verbruggen and Olivier Boscagli likely to retain their places at Anfield.
Brighton could go unchanged from their thumping victory over Palace, with goalscorers Kostoulas, Diego Gómez and Yasin Ayari among those re-entering the team.

On the injury front, Brighton are still missing an array of players, including Liverpool transfer target Yankuba Minteh. The Gambian’s fellow wingers Kaoru Mitoma, Femi Azeez and Zadok Yohana are all still sidelined.
Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas and Mats Wieffer are long-term absentees, but there’s a chance that Pascal Struijk returns from injury in defense.
Brighton Predicted Lineup vs. Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Kadıoğlu, Vušković, Dunk, Boscagli; Groß, Chema; Gómez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas.

ftbpro_01m5maddbj68.title: How Man Utd Would Line Up Under Eddie Howe
ftbpro_01m5maddbj68.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott4:00 PM EDTEddie Howe is in the mix. / MI News/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Howe), Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images (Man Utd badge)Manchester United are keen to draw up a long list of potential replacements for under-fire manager Michael Carrick.

Antonio Conte is among the big names available, while reports suggest Julian Nagelsmann has increasingly strong support in the boardroom. There are, however, those that would prefer a Premier League-proven manager, and that is where Eddie Howe comes in.

Howe, 48, has been on the shortlist of nearly every top team in England at some point in the past decade, having made some serious noise at Bournemouth before taking Newcastle United into the Champions League. Somebody who knows how to win matches in the Premier League could be the difference.
If United do decide to cut ties with Carrick and offer Howe a route to the dugout, here’s how he could set up.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Hiring Howe would boost Man Utd’s chances of landing Lewis Hall. / Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesGK: Senne Lammens—United have no desire to move on from Lammens, whose composure would make him a dream asset for any manager on the planet.

RB: Jules Koundé—Defense is set to be United’s priority area in the upcoming transfer windows. Howe is likely to want a versatile right back who can fly forward when needed but is equally comfortable drifting into a central role. Considering that Koundé, unsettled at Barcelona, is a center back by trade, this one could work out nicely.

CB: Leny Yoro—Howe loves an athletic center back who can keep up with the pace of the modern game. Matthijs de Ligt and Harry Maguire are hardly blessed in that department but Yoro, who is still finding his feet in England, has the tools to develop nicely under the former Newcastle boss.

CB: Castello Lukeba—With Lisandro Martínez expected to leave, a new left-sided defender is needed. Micky van de Ven sounds like a dream but could prove to be too expensive, but RB Leipzig’s Lukeba might appeal to Howe. His profile is the sort of thing United would be looking for regardless of who is in the dugout. A move for Newcastle’s Dan Burn to add experience would come as no surprise.
LB: Lewis Hall—The stars have aligned. United want Hall. Howe gave Hall his big chance at Newcastle. Hiring him would give United their clearest path to landing their dream left back.
DM: Kobbie Mainoo—Howe enjoys using a tempo-setting midfielder, initially asking Bruno Guimarães to do so before Sandro Tonali’s move to St James’ Park. He should be quickly drawn to Mainoo.

Carlos Baleba has all the tools needed to succeed under Howe. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesCM: Carlos Baleba—Box-to-box engines are important to Howe in midfield, and so Baleba would be among the first names on the team sheet. The summer signing stands to benefit from a hypothetical move for Howe as much as anybody in the squad.

CM: Bruno Fernandes—Fernandes may not be a typical Howe player, but the former Newcastle boss would back himself to make it work. He does bring good energy to the midfield and would be given plenty of freedom to get forward, rather than sit in the sort of deep role in which he struggled under Ruben Amorim.

RW: Bryan Mbeumo—Mbeumo is a typical Howe forward, which is why he wanted him at Newcastle in 2025. He’s athletic and determined, ready to fly up and down the pitch to do whatever is needed of him. A significant upgrade on Jacob Murphy.
ST: Benjamin Šeško—Like Mbeumo, Newcastle were in the battle to sign Šeško last year. Howe described them as “outstanding players,” and would likely relish the chance to finally work with both.

LW: Amad Diallo—Howe would have loved to reunite with Anthony Gordon, but his recent switch to Barcelona takes that off the table. He would really enjoy working with somebody with Amad’s natural agility in attack, but could easily lean on Marcus Rashford in the early stages.
Howe would oversee changes in defense. / FotMobREAD THE LATEST MAN UTD NEWS, ANALYSIS AND INSIGHT FROM SI FC. feed

ftbpro_01m5mb1w6ksd.title: Right or Wrong? PL Panel Rules on Gravenberch Red Card vs. Man City
ftbpro_01m5mb1w6ksd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer9:00 AM EDTRyan Gravenberch committed two fouls punished by yellow cards. / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesThe Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel believes the red card shown to Ryan Gravenberch against Manchester City earlier this month was the correct decision.

Already a contentious fixture because it was the first for City since the Premier League’s guilty verdict over years of financial breaches was publicly revealed, Gravenberch was dismissed by referee Chris Kavanagh in the 62nd minute for two yellow-card offenses.

The score was tied 0–0 at the time. However, with the player advantage, City soon took the lead through Erling Haaland only three minutes later and had scored three times within 16 minutes of Liverpool losing the Dutch midfielder.

Andoni Iraola didn’t initially respond in-game to the red card, only sacrificing Florian Wirtz with the more defensive-minded Trey Nyoni after Liverpool had fallen behind. The second City goal from Jérémy Doku then came immediately, before the Reds had settled into their new shape.
Still, there was a sense of injustice from a Liverpool perspective because the first card shown to Gravenberch was deemed harsh and “not a yellow” in Iraola’s eyes.

“[Elliot] Anderson carries on a couple of steps [before falling]. [The referee] wasn’t even going to give a foul. I’ve no idea why he gives a yellow card. We have like nine players behind the ball,” the frustrated Liverpool manager told Sky Sports after the final whistle.
The KMI Panel is there to assess referees and officials over match incidents defined as ‘key,’ such as goals, penalties, red cards and second yellow cards.
According to BBC Sport, the panel made a judgement on both yellow cards shown to Gravenberch when assessing the dismissal—as per protocol.

The panel voted 4:1 in favor of supporting the decision made, with the one who voted against believing the foul on Anderson should not have led to the first yellow card. But once the Liverpool player had received the first yellow card, the panel then unanimously supported the VAR’s decision not to intervene on the second yellow card that resulted in the red.

Gravenberch has served his domestic suspension already. / Ed Sykes/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesThere is no real consequence, other than validating the actions of the match officials at the time. Gravenberch has already served the one-game suspension associated with the red card, sitting out last weekend’s road trip to Brentford. Liverpool won the match without him, ironically with the help of two Brentford red cards after initially falling behind in the first half.

Had the KMI Panel found a mistake, there could have been no recourse beyond an admission that the wrong call had been made and a vow to officiate better in the future. The match officials responsible might also have been put on ice for a week. But that isn’t the case here.

Gravenberch, who played 90 minutes in both of Liverpool’s Champions League wins against LASK and Villarreal either side of his domestic ban, is eligible to face Brighton & Hove Albion in his team’s next Premier League match on Sunday.

The Premier League has shared that following the sixth round of matches—so not including the most recent set last weekend—114 KMIs this season have been deemed correct 89% of the time, up from 86% at this stage of last season. For VAR interventions, 98% of decisions are considered correct.

ftbpro_01m5mg2p5ggj.title: Man Utd vs. Bournemouth: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5mg2p5ggj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray8:00 PM EDTThe Cherries have impressed at Old Trafford in recent years. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Man Utd), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Bournemouth)Manchester United are seeking to dig their way out of crisis over the coming weeks, beginning with Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford in the Premier League.

Sunday’s match could prove make-or-break for Michael Carrick, whose position as manager becomes increasingly untenable with each passing humiliation. The dismal 4–1 defeat to Como on Wednesday was the final straw for many, including captain Bruno Fernandes, who became the second player to voice their anger at the club’s staff and hierarchy.

Now seven matches without victory across all competitions, the Red Devils desperately need to clinch only their third win of the campaign when the Cherries come to town. Having amassed just seven points in as many matches, things are looking decidedly bleak in the red half of Manchester—and not for the first time in recent years.

Bournemouth made an underwhelming start under new manager Marco Rose, but things have begun to click since the international break. Back-to-back 3–0 victories over Sturm Graz and AC Milan in the Europa League—the latter coached by ex-United manager Ruben Amorim—sandwiched a first Premier League triumph of the season at home to Sunderland last weekend.
They know they will leapfrog their hosts with victory at Old Trafford, and they have an impressive record during recent visits to the venue.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Things could go from bad to worse for United. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesRight now, there seems no light at the end of the tunnel for United. Not only do they have to overcome Bournemouth, one of their current bogey teams, they then face matches against Chelsea, Roma, Aston Villa and Liverpool in their following four matches.

Beating the Cherries is essential to Carrick’s survival, with victory perhaps able to glue the dressing room back together—however temporarily. Unfortunately for the Red Devils, they have shown no genuine signs of turning the corner during recent apathetic and disjointed displays.
Their last three Premier League games have finished 1–1 and they might be forced to accept the same scoreline against Bournemouth, who have drawn three of their Premier League matches already.
Defeat? Well, that could be the end of the road for Carrick.
Injuries have been piling up for United, which has only exacerbated an ever-worsening situation. Carrick will again be without a host of first-teamers this weekend.

In defense, Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Lisandro Martínez are all missing, although United have been boosted by the recent return of Matthijs de Ligt after nearly a year on the sidelines. Third-choice goalkeeper Tom Heaton is also out.
Kobbie Mainoo will sit out another match in midfield having recently joined positional peer and long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte in the treatment room.

Up front, Benjamin Šeško is certain to be absent as he continues to battle a shin injury, while Marcus Rashford’s involvement remains in doubt after he missed the Como capitulation through a hip issue.
Carrick should still name Fernandes in his starting XI, despite the player’s outspoken comments sparking debate over whether he should remain club captain.
Carlos Baleba should come into midfield despite his disastrous mistake off the bench against Como, while Ayden Heaven has recovered from illness and might immediately return to the team.
Man Utd predicted lineup vs. Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Heaven, Mazraoui; Tielemans, Baleba; Diallo, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

There’s positive news for Bournemouth ahead of their trip up north, with Eli Junior Kroupi available for the first time this season following a lengthy absence. He should earn some minutes against United, although he’s almost certain to start on the bench.

Bournemouth will be without Alex Tóth, however, after the midfielder sustained a hamstring injury against Milan midweek. He joins Veljko Milosavljević, Julián Araujo and, more importantly, Alex Scott on the sidelines for the time being.

Rose selected a strong side against Milan, yet was still able to offer the likes of Rayan and Lewis Cook partial rests. Adam Smith was also given the night off, but he will return to the XI alongside Rayan at Old Trafford.

ftbpro_01m5mgqbz9qy.title: Michael Carrick Comments Leave Bruno Fernandes Sweating Over Man Utd Captaincy
ftbpro_01m5mgqbz9qy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott11:15 AM EDTBruno Fernandes was criticized for speaking out against Michael Carrick. / Luca Rossini/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the team’s captaincy following his public criticism—and insisted the club’s dressing room is not divided.

A frustrated Fernandes took aim at Carrick’s tactics following the dismal 4–1 defeat to Como in the Champions League, just days after center back Lisandro Martínez aimed higher with accusations that technical director Jason Wilcox and his recruitment team had let the club down.

Martínez is understood to have been fined for his comments, but Sky Sports News state no such punishment is coming Fernandes’s way. That was, however, before Carrick’s cryptic update in Friday’s press conference.

Asked whether Fernandes will be dropped or removed as captain for his comments, Carrick stressed: “The most important thing for me is the team and the dynamics in the squad. It is about the football club.
“Whatever the situation is I will always do what is best for the football club.”
All eyes will be on Carrick’s team selection for Sunday’s meeting with Bournemouth, with the Red Devils seeking to end a run of seven games without victory.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Harry Maguire would be the standout candidate. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesFans have long held concerns about the personalities in the United locker room, leaving them without too many obvious candidates to wear the captain’s armband.

Should Fernandes be removed from the position, it would likely be handed back to Harry Maguire. The center back was named captain by Ole Gunnar Solskjær in 2020 but was stripped of his post by Erik ten Hag three years later, with Fernandes promoted in his place.

Beyond Maguire, Carrick may struggle for options. Left back Luke Shaw could be a candidate when healthy, while Lisandro Martínez would likely have been considered had he not been the first to speak out against the club.

Summer signing Youri Tielemans has experience with the armband from his time with Aston Villa. Right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui joined backup goalkeeper Tom Heaton in a leadership group under Ruben Amorim and would be considered outside candidates.

Michael Carrick is confident there is no wider issue to address. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe fact that Fernandes was not the first United player to speak out was cause for concern for the legendary Wayne Rooney, whose brutal assessment of the pair included accusations of selfishness and questions about their passion for the club.
Rooney argued Fernandes, as captain, would “rip the dressing room apart” by speaking out, but Carrick was adamant the group remains together.
“It’s not divided,” he insisted. “We just need to get back to doing what we do best. And we will.”

ftbpro_01m5mgyydt6m.title: Chelsea vs. Tottenham: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5mgyydt6m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 23, 2026Two London rivals collide at Stamford Bridge. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Chelsea’s badge), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Tottenham’s badge)   A London derby concludes Saturday’s Premier League slate, as Chelsea welcome Tottenham Hotspur to Stamford Bridge.

The Blues have made discernible progress at the start of Xabi Alonso’s reign and have picked up back-to-back victories after the international break. After thumping Bournemouth 5–1, Alonso’s side secured a gritty victory at the previously unbeaten Everton last weekend.

Pedro Neto’s first Premier League brace on his 187th appearance fired Chelsea to the sort of victory they haven’t enjoyed under BlueCo. Remarkably, it was their first clean sheet in the competition since January, as Alonso’s shift to an asymmetric shape in possession paid dividends.

Spurs, meanwhile, breathed a sigh of relief after securing their maiden Premier League win of the season on Monday night over a Frank Lampard-led Coventry City. Roberto De Zerbi’s side had performed better without just reward earlier in the campaign, but three points were all that mattered for the Lilywhites.
Building on that result will be tough, though, given the club’s wretched record at the Bridge since the Premier League’s inception.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Chelsea have been dominant in this fixture over the years. / Mike Morese/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAlonso said after last week’s triumph at Hill Dickinson Stadium that he was looking forward to Saturday’s duel, and the Spaniard was complimentary of De Zerbi’s Spurs ahead of the derby.

"I have seen a good team in bad results. We are expecting a tough game. We need to be prepared. Early days for everything," he said in his press conference before the game, with Spurs down in 16th despite claiming a desperately needed win on Monday.

De Zerbi’s side still rank lowly on the xG front, but have notched the most touches in the final third in the division. This is a tidy outfit that’s good between the boxes, yet it’s at both ends of the pitch where matches are decided, and that’s ultimately where Spurs have underwhelmed at the start of the new season.
The visitors will be content with a point here, while Chelsea are targeting a third successive victory.
Alonso has confirmed that Malo Gusto is available for Saturday’s derby after missing the trip to Merseyside through illness.

Pep Chavarría remains sidelined for the hosts after sustaining an injury in the warm-up at Everton, so Alonso will likely decide between Marco Palestra and Jorrel Hato at left wing back. Pedro Neto is a certainty to keep his spot after his goalscoring antics last week.
Emiliano Martínez has undergone jaw surgery after his nasty collision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, so young goalkeeper Mike Penders will make his first Premier League start on Saturday.
Reece James is likely to be out until the new year, while Jamie Gittens and Emmanuel Emegha are also absent.
Chelsea predicted lineup vs. Tottenham (3-4-2-1): Penders; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Henderson, Caicedo, Palestra; Palmer, Rogers; João Pedro.
A more cautious approach to recovery hasn’t drastically altered Tottenham’s fortunes on the injury front, with a list of players out of Saturday’s match.

Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are recovering from ACL tears, while Destiny Udogie, Sávio and Lucas Bergvall are recent additions to the treatment room. Udogie was a surprise absentee against Coventry, and it’s unclear when he’ll be back in action.

Pedro Porro could recover from his hamstring injury in time for the trip to Stamford Bridge, but a start seems unlikely. Archie Gray could deputize for the Spaniard, especially if De Zerbi reverts to a back four.

The Spurs boss insisted that the injuries Andy Robertson and Tosin Adarabioyo sustained on Monday evening won’t keep them out of Saturday’s game. Dejan Kulusevski has also made his long-awaited return from a complicated patella injury that sidelined him for 526 days.
Tottenham predicted lineup vs. Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Maddison, Marmoush; Solanke.

ftbpro_01m5mmnrytj1.title: Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Real Madrid: High-Powered Offense Primed for Clasico
ftbpro_01m5mmnrytj1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack4:00 PM EDTBarcelona have been utterly rampant at the start of the new La Liga season. / Joaquin Corchero/Europa Press/Getty ImagesBarcelona have the chance to open up a nine-point advantage over Real Madrid when Spain’s two dominant forces lock horns in the first Clásico of the 2026–27 season.

Barça had been perfect in all competitions before they felt the wrath of the back-to-back European champions midweek. Hansi Flick’s side, who have won their opening nine La Liga outings, were beaten 4–2 by Paris Saint-Germain in an unsurprisingly frenetic Champions League encounter laden with quality.

Their first blemish has led naysayers to suggest that Barça’s bubble is starting to burst, and they are facing a Madrid team coming off the back of two convincing performances and results. With José Mourinho back in the fold, this esteemed fixture suddenly has a greater sense of box-office appeal.
Here’s how Barcelona could line up for Real Madrid’s visit this weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Joan García—García’s heroics couldn’t get Barcelona over the line midweek, as he tallied double-digit saves in defeat. Real Madrid’s superstars are likely to keep the Spaniard busy on Sunday, as long as they beat the offside trap.
RB: Xavi Espart—Barcelona have done it again. Despite their full back injury issues, they have nothing to worry about with Espart in the team.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—Cubarsí locks horns with Kylian Mbappé again, having gotten the better of the Frenchman in the World Cup semifinals.

CB: Gerard Martín—If there is a chink in Barcelona’s defense, it’s Martín. The academy graduate has stepped in admirably at the heart of Flick’s backline after breaking through at left back, but he’s a short-term solution alongside Cubarsí at best.

LB: João Cancelo—Cancelo’s coming off a tough evening in Paris, and he didn’t take too kindly to supporter criticism. “From the stands, everyone is an expert. I want to see you get into the game and take the pressure,” he wrote on Instagram. A big response is required in the Clásico

CM: Rodri—A surprise absentee from Flick‘s midweek starting XI, Rodri played the final 30 minutes in Paris ahead of the Clásico. It’s his first experience of the big game, and there’s no doubt the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner will relish the occasion.
CM: Pedri—The classy midfielder is in bounce-back mode after struggling in the French capital on Tuesday.
RW: Lamine Yamal—After an up-and-down outing midweek, Yamal takes to the field for the final time before the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.
AM: Fermín López—There’s bound to be a run in the team for the opportunistic Fermín after Dani Olmo sustained a groin injury that’ll keep him out until after the November international break.
LW: Anthony Gordon—Flick may well be tempted by Karim Adeyemi here, but the German is just so destructive off the bench that Gordon may retain his spot in the starting XI.

ST: Raphinha—Raphinha absolutely loves the Clásico. The Brazilian, who got through an hour midweek after recently recovering from an injury, has only scored more goals against Sevilla (nine) than Real Madrid (seven) in his senior career.

ftbpro_01m5mmy0t0nc.title: ‘Clarify My Position’—Antonio Conte Responds to Man Utd Links
ftbpro_01m5mmy0t0nc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer1:30 PM EDTAntonio Conte is currently a free agent. /  Francesco Pecoraro/Getty ImagesAntonio Conte has pushed back on speculation that he is in active negotiations with any club to return to management. It comes primarily amid a swell of talk about potentially replacing Michael Carrick at Manchester United as pressure builds on the Red Devils.

Conte, who has won six league championships with four teams in Italy and England, has also been tentatively linked with Juventus and AC Milan in his homeland. Juve, where he was previously in charge between 2011 and 2014, are already playing catchup on Serie A’s leading teams, although Milan have since recovered from a minor wobble in September.

The 57-year-old was most recently employed by Napoli, taking the team to the Serie A title in 2024–25. But he left by mutual consent at the end of last season and has not returned to work. His record of success and current availability naturally lends itself to intrigue.

Conte appears open to considering interest in hiring him, but he felt compelled on Friday to “clarify” the state of play. There are, he said in a social media statement, “currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.” The former Juventus midfielder added he plans to still “take the time to consider how and when to return to management,” which will only happen when the “conditions are right.”
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

He explained: “I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality.’ These reports are unfounded.

“Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties’ needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.”
Conte said that “assumptions” being reported about his “demands and professional future” are just that at this stage and “cannot be treated as fact.”

Conte won the Premier League with Chelsea 10 seasons ago. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesManchester United have been warned that Conte, while verifiably able to deliver results, can be tough to work with in the way he approaches jobs.

He is also a notoriously short-term fixer, rather than a long-term strategist, typically lasting two or fewer full seasons at every club. Juventus, where he spent three seasons more than a decade ago, is the only exception to that in 20 years of management.

Conte’s most recent Premier League appointment, at Tottenham Hotspur between Nov. 2, 2021 and March 26, 2023, blew up when he called his own players “selfish” in a furious response to a bad result against Southampton, bottom of the standings at the time.
“We are 11 players that go into the pitch. I see selfish players. I see players that don't want to help each other and don't put their heart [into it],” he said at the time.

“The most important thing if you want to become a strong team, if you want to become competitive, if you want to fight to win, is the desire, the fire that you need to have in your eyes, in your heart. And you have to show this in every moment. In every moment.
“To be a team, this the most important thing. To understand that we play for the badge. We have to play to make our fans proud of us. We have to play to show desire.”

ftbpro_01m5mpcb4zby.title: Vincent Kompany Collapses at Bayern Training Ground, Rushed to Hospital
ftbpro_01m5mpcb4zby.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas1:08 PM EDTVincent Kompany was rushed to the hospital on Friday.     / Leonhard Simon/Getty Images Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany reportedly had to be rushed to the hospital after collapsing in the club’s training center following Friday’s practice.

A medical helicopter was at the scene before the Belgian manager left Bayern’s Säbener Straße training center via ambulance, per Bild. The club has since released a statement offering an update on Kompany’s health status.

“Vincent Kompany had to undergo medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during Bayern Munich Amateur’s [Bayern’s second team] practice,” Bayern Munich said in a statement. “The first team manager had been observing the second team’s training session.
“Kompany will undergo exhaustive tests at the hospital and will remain under medical attention. For the moment, his technical staff will manage training sessions and match related activities.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl also commented on the situation: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure that he recovers quickly. Vinnie will receive all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs.
“His coaching staff, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.”

Vincent Kompany was on the touchline when Bayern Munich faced Arsenal on Wednesday.  / Sven Hoppe/picture alliance/Getty ImagesThere’s no official confirmation as to what caused Kompany’s medical emergency, but the manager has been dealing with a debilitating viral infection over the past week.

Kompany was on the touchline in Bayern’s 6–1 win over RB Leipzig last weekend, but reports indicate he had to lay down inside the locker room before the game and at halftime. The infection is causing problems in old scar tissue that makes it difficult for Kompany to walk up stairs, per BILD.

The virus forced the former Manchester City captain to miss Bayern’s last two training sessions plus the pre-match press conference ahead of the 2–2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following the match, Kompany shared some insight about what he’s been dealing with.

“As a manager, you always want to do everything and achieve everything,” Kompany said after Champions League match. “Last week, I caught a strong virus and, of course, I didn’t listen to my body until a certain point, in which my body said: ‘Stop now!’”
Bayern Munich face a tough visit against third-placed Freiburg on Sunday. It remains unknown if Kompany will be fit enough to be on the touchline for the Bundesliga clash.
