ftbpro_01m5mr95e7vz.title: Arsenal Fear Significant Bukayo Saka Injury Absence—Report
ftbpro_01m5mr95e7vz.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer1:00 PM EDTBukayo Saka is unlikely to be back quickly. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesArsenal want to carry out more tests on Bukayo Saka, but the Gunners are reported to fear their star winger could be absent for around two months because of a quad injury.

Saka suffered in the early stages of Wednesday night’s 2–2 draw against Bayern Munich what Mikel Arteta described after the final whistle as a “sharp” pain. The England international couldn’t continue, forced off the field only 10 minutes into the match.

Arteta spoke with reporters again on Friday, building up to Arsenal’s Premier League encounter with Everton this weekend, and revealed an MRI scan was scheduled for Saka. “He had a lot of fluid in the area, so it was difficult to understand the severity of the injury. We will know tomorrow.
“We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists, when a player is struggling to walk off the pitch and he's restricted in his movement, they are not good signs.”

BBC Sport reported that Arsenal have concerns of an absence that will last a minimum of six weeks, and potentially up to two months. The longer estimate could see Saka ruled out until Christmas. Even the best-case scenario might mean not returning until early December.
Still, Arteta called on patience for now, “so we can give a definitive assessment.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Saka has missed games almost every season because of muscle issues, peaking at a 99-day absence at a crucial point of the 2024–25 campaign. He was on course to shatter the Premier League’s single-season assist record but was sidelined from late December into March, while Arsenal wound up finishing second in the final standings for the third year in a row.

This has naturally put renewed focus on the ongoing debate about elite players being overworked. Arsenal played 63 matches out of a possible 65 in all competitions last season and ideally want to hit a similar number in 2026–27 as they target an unprecedented quadruple.
“Obviously the demands that we are putting to every player are immense,” Arteta admitted in reference to the schedule, which includes international play outside of club commitments.

“The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower. So, look at us now, we have to play on Sunday afternoon, then we have to go away, we have to play on Wednesday evening, then we have to play on Saturday. You go less than 66, 67 hours between games.”

Saka will miss potentially 15 matches for club and country. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesA six-week absence takes us into the start of December. Between now and then, Arsenal have nine matches to play across three competitions. Recovery on that timeline would potentially put Saka back healthy in the days leading up to the north London derby on Dec. 6. The Gunners face both Liverpool and Manchester City in that run. England also play twice in November.
A longer two-month absence adds the derby and four extra matches to the list of games Saka would miss, including Emirates Stadium visits from Real Madrid and Manchester United.

Carabao Cup quarterfinals are scheduled for the week commencing Dec. 14. Arsenal have a Premier League match that week, which would need rearrangement, so it may not add an extra game to what Saka could miss, should the Gunners beat Fleetwood Town in the fourth round next week.

The congested nature of the December schedule means that matches are played every few days, which could rule Saka out of more if he still needs extra time to train for fitness and conditioning once he is medically cleared to return.
Noni Madueke is the obvious cover option. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesFor all the talk about Arsenal’s squad depth, they aren’t blessed with a lot of strong wing cover.

Two left wingers were sold (Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli) during the summer and only one recruited (Christos Tzolis). Efforts were made to sign Morgan Rogers, with interest in Vinícius Júnior and Bradley Barcola, but Arsenal ultimately didn’t land a superstar recruit and yet Martinelli was still actively pushed through the door.

Eberechi Eze replaced Saka on the field in Munich—and actually scored—but is primarily a No. 10 and was chosen because Noni Madueke was already on the pitch covering the other flank, where an injured Tzolis should have been.
Tzolis is at least expected back soon, which relieves some of the pressure. But Eze and Madueke have put up consistent numbers since joining in 2025.

Eze has two Champions League goals this season, but no goals or assists in the Premier League. He is not considered a starter in Arsenal’s strongest team. Last season, five of his nine Premier League goal involvements came in just two matches against Tottenham Hotspur, meaning the other four were spread across 31 appearances. Madueke has three goal involvements in nine games so far this season, after 12 in 43 in 2025–26.

ftbpro_01m5msna65fs.title: Real Madrid Predicted Lineup vs. Barcelona: Mourinho Makes Bold Midfield Call
ftbpro_01m5msna65fs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 24, 2026Real Madrid is in need of a result at Camp Nou. / Jesus Troyano/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesThere’s a glint in the eye of the Clásico again, as José Mourinho takes his Real Madrid team to Camp Nou for their first outing of the season against La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday.

It’s merely October, yet this fixture feels season-defining. While Barça were beaten for the first time midweek, they’ve won nine straight to start the domestic campaign and are already six points better off than Mourinho’s side.

However, the vibes in the Spanish capital are high off the back of two convincing performances against Sevilla and RB Leipzig. Victory here and plenty will believe that Madrid are viable candidates for Barça’s throne. Defeat, though, and it’ll already start to look like a long way back.
Madrid are once again without the suspended Vinícius Júnior, but there’s still a collection of superstars at Mourinho’s disposal for the Clásico.
Here’s how Real Madrid could line up in Catalonia this weekend.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

GK: Andriy Lunin—Real Madrid’s reserve goalkeeper is set to make his first start of the season after Thibaut Courtois was taken ill with the flu. The Belgian still hopes to play despite the club ruling him out on the morning of the game.

RB: Federico Valverde—Valverde is seemingly more content to play at right back under Mourinho than he was under Xabi Alonso, and he could be deployed in Madrid’s defense in a bid to tame Barcelona’s high-powered offense.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—Mourinho has leaned on veteran Antonio Rüdiger from time to time, but Konaté is starting to develop a stout partnership with Dean Huijsen, and the pair should reunite on Sunday.

CB: Dean Huijsen—Huijsen enters the Clásico off the back of a strong performance against RB Leipzig midweek. However, the Spaniard has his work cut out for him here, given just how potent Barça have been going forward at the start of the new season.
LB: Marc Cucurella—Good luck. A day out against Lamine Yamal beckons.

CM: Eduardo Camavinga—Reports out of Spain suggest Mourinho has been convinced by Camavinga. The Frenchman is seemingly never too far away from doing something silly, yet the boss believes he’s the right midfield profile for this fixture.
CM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—We haven’t seen much of the French connection in Madrid’s engine room as of late. The visitors need a big game from Tchouaméni against Barça’s midfield supremos.

RW: Arda Güler—Güler will operate as an extra midfielder from the right with the hope of evening up the bodies in the center of the pitch. The young playmaker has enjoyed a superb start to the season, and his threat from distance is something the hosts must be wary of.

AM: Jude Bellingham—Paris Saint-Germain’s runs from midfield caused a Rodri-less Barcelona all sorts of problems in the week, so expected Mourinho to task Bellingham with penetrating in behind as much as he can.
LW: Yan Diomande—No Vinícius Júnior, no problem for Real Madrid. Diomande is finding his feet and poised to start in the Brazilian’s absence again.

ST: Kylian Mbappé—Mbappé has been troubled by Barça’s aggressive defensive line in the past, yet his record against the Blaugrana is impressive, dating back to his time with PSG. The French superstar has scored 12 times in as many games against Madrid’s fiercest rivals, and a productive outing on Sunday would certainly be timely.

ftbpro_01m5mv6eh451.title: Xabi Alonso Reveals Recovery Timeline for Emiliano Martinez Following Emergency Surgery
ftbpro_01m5mv6eh451.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas4:30 PM EDTEmiliano Martínez (left) suffered a scary injury when he collided with Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite.       / Alex Livesey/Getty Images Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez had to undergo emergency surgery after fracturing his jaw against Everton last weekend, and manager Xabi Alonso refused to give a concrete timeline for his return, simply stating that he’ll hopefully be back in “a few weeks.”
A scary collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite saw Martínez rushed to the hospital with a head injury following extensive medical attention on the pitch during Chelsea’s 2–0 win.

The Argentine goalkeeper posted a picture from the hospital after undergoing surgery, also stating he’d be “back in a few weeks.” In addition to the broken jaw, Alonso confirmed that Martínez suffered a concussion, which immediately sidelines him for a minimum of 14 days per English Football Association rules.
On the eve of Saturday’s London derby against Tottenham Hotspur, Alonso was asked about the condition of his starting goalkeeper.
“He's doing better,” Alonso said. “He had the surgery, and day by day, he's feeling better, but we still need to wait.”

“Few weeks, few weeks,” he repeated about Martínez’s projected return. “Hopefully less than more, but we need to wait. The good thing is that he's feeling better and that he wants to listen to his feelings, the opinion of the doctors, the specialists, the surgeons. Considering it was a bad one, he's doing good.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mike Penders will start for Chelsea in goal while Emiliano Martínez is on the mend.     / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesWith Martínez sidelined, 21-year-old Mike Penders will be between the sticks for Chelsea’s upcoming games. The Belgian got his first taste of Premier League action when he replaced Martínez late against Everton and made one save to help Chelsea keep their first clean sheet of the league season.

Penders started the season as Robert Sánchez’s backup and stayed second-choice when Martínez joined the club and Sánchez was shipped off to Como. Chelsea have always thought highly of Penders since they signed him as a teenager in the summer of 2024. Now thrusted into the starting role, Alonso is confident that Penders is prepared to deliver.

“He’s ready,” Alonso stated. “He's been training well, he's played a couple of cup games where he showed that he has a good level, even the day when he came on against Everton, in a few minutes he showed his personality, his qualities. That's why we have a squad to be ready for these kinds of situations, and we are fully convinced that Mike can play very well.”

Alonso was also questioned about why Penders wasn’t trusted to be the starter when the season began. The Spanish boss had a telling answer, admitting Penders is regarded as Chelsea’s goalkeeper of the future.

“We wanted to have the best possible options and once we decided that we would go for Emi, I think we have a good balance,” the Spaniard said. “I think Mike is our keeper for now and for the future. Having the support, learning with an experienced goalkeeper like Emi, he's having a great impact on the team and on Mike and looking forward to the next game. We are happy with his preparation.”

Mike Penders (middle) has often been compared to fellow Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois (left).  / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAlonso isn’t the first to tout Penders as Chelsea’s goalkeeper of the future. Ever since the Blues spent €20 million ($22.5 million) for his signing, he’s been sent out on loan to Genk and then sister club Strasbourg to continue his development with the hope of one day becoming Chelsea’s top-choice goalkeeper.

Penders has always been viewed as a star in the making, and he’s earned comparisons to former Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, especially due to his height and nationality. Alonso managed Courtois at Real Madrid and agreed that Penders reminds him of who many consider to be the best goalkeeper in the world.

“There are a lot [of similarities between Penders and Courtois],” Alonso confessed. “Not just for the nationality, for the stature, both left-footed, both dominant in the air. I spoke with Thibaut as well when he was in the World Cup, asking about Mike and he even said to himself that he could see resemblances with Mike.
“We need to help him, support him, but for sure he's a keeper for present and for the future.”
Chelsea will be hoping to welcome back Martínez as soon as possible, but for now, their goalkeeper of the future will get his first extended look between the sticks at Stamford Bridge.

ftbpro_01m5mvsemb42.title: Why Thibaut Courtois Isn’t Playing for Real Madrid vs. Barcelona
ftbpro_01m5mvsemb42.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack2:45 PM EDTThibaut Courtois would be a huge loss for Real Madrid. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesReal Madrid certainly aren’t shy of superstars. Yet if you asked Barcelona supporters who they’d most like their arch-rivals to be without for Sunday’s Clásico, they probably wouldn’t utter Kylian Mbappé or Jude Bellingham in response.

Vinícius Júnior is already ruled out through suspension, and there was drama surrounding Thibaut Courtois on the day of the big La Liga encounter. It’s the Belgian who Barcelona would have loved to sit out El Clásico, given his status as one of the world’s best goalkeepers and his knack for showing up for the big occasion.
Courtois had played every minute of Madrid’s campaign until Sunday, but his streak in the team has come to an end.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Courtois wants to play despite illness. / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIt initially appeared as if Real Madrid had suffered a devastating blow on the morning of the Clásico, as they released a statement confirming that Courtois would miss the match.
“Courtois is a late withdrawal from tonight’s La Liga match between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to the flu,” the club wrote. “Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place.”

Barcelona supporters rejoiced, while those desperate for a La Liga title race squirmed. Courtois’s absence would render Madrid’s already tough task that little bit harder, and this is a Clásico the visitors can ill afford to lose.

The back-to-back champions are already six points clear of Los Blancos, who sit behind Atlético Madrid in third. Atléti extended their domestic winning streak to six games on Saturday and are now just two points adrift of Barça at the summit. Still, the majority would suggest that José Mourinho’s side are the most likely challengers to Barça’s throne, yet a nine-point deficit, even at this early juncture, would feel insurmountable.

They need Courtois, and the Belgian knows it. Despite his illness, Madrid‘s No. 1 was desperate to play, with reports initially claiming that Courtois was pushing to travel to Catalonia and start between the posts. In the end, the 34-year-old couldn’t muster a miraculous recovery and had to watch from afar.

Andriy Lunin was called in as the club’s reserve. The Ukrainian shot-stopper has proven himself serviceable over the years but asking him to step up and play for the first time this season in the Clásico—against this Barcelona offense—is a huge ask.
4-2-3-1: Andriy Lunin; Federico Valverde, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen, Marc Cucurella; Aurélien Tchouaméni, Bernardo Silva; Arda Güler, Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomade; Kylian Mbappé.

ftbpro_01m5mvser9je.title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5mvser9je.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 24, 2026This Clásico could be season-defining. / Alex Caparros - UEFA/Getty Images (Barcelona), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Real Madrid)El Clásico is unlikely to ever fade from global relevance, but there’s no denying that one of Europe’s most illustrious fixtures has lost a bit of sparkle over the past decade.
This was once the pinnacle of the sport. The soccer world stopped when Barcelona and Real Madrid locked horns, and Pep Guardiola and José Mourinho paraded their respective dugouts.

Well, Mourinho is back, folks, and preparing himself for his first Clásico since 2013. His relationship with Barça dates back to his time as Sir Bobby Robson’s translator/assistant in the mid-90s, and the resentment that washed over him after the club he once adored opted to hire Guardiola as Frank Rijkaard’s assistant in 2008 has struggled to fade.

He was Barça’s arch-nemesis for a period, and he eventually broke Guardiola’s outstanding team, not to mention his Spanish counterpart on the touchline. However, Hansi Flick’s current Blaugrana are on track to smash the records set by Mourinho’s Madrid in 2011–12.

Sunday’s hosts head into the Clásico six points clear of the visitors and are threatening to run away with the division for a third successive year. Camp Nou was the site of Mourinho’s “most beautiful defeat,” but he can’t afford a loss of any kind this weekend. A nine-point deficit to this Barcelona team would feel unassailable, even at this early juncture and with the swathe of superstars Los Blancos possess.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The world’s best clash on Sunday. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesBarcelona have won six of the previous seven meetings against their Clásico rivals, including two of the three duels last season. Flick has generally had a hold over Real Madrid, but the return of Mourinho adds an extra layer of intrigue and potential scope for the unexpected.
Mourinho has locked horns with Flick just once in his managerial career, with his Tottenham Hotspur team losing 3–1 at Bayern Munich in 2019. Flick’s Bayern would go on to conquer all that season.

There‘s a sense that Madrid remain somewhat unsophisticated, certainly relative to Barça, but a Mourinho-led team in 2026 doesn’t require tactical perfection. It looks like the returning manager is going down the Carlo Ancelotti route, taking a more laissez-faire approach and ensuring his team has the right balance. They’ve been good over the past week, albeit against opponents incomparable to their upcoming test.
Barcelona are outstanding, but if Madrid click in Catalonia, we could be in for something special.

There were a couple of notable injury casualties at Parc des Princes on Tuesday evening. Most notably, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his ACL, but Barcelona were also struck by the bug. Dani Olmo sustained a groin injury that’ll keep him out for the next month.
The hosts at least have the opportunistic Fermín López to call upon in reserve.

Flick is also set to be without full backs Jules Koundé and Eric García, meaning João Cancelo and young Xavi Espart will likely retain their spots in defense. Espart was excellent in Paris, but Cancelo struggled.

Rodri played just 30 minutes in the week, with the Barcelona manager likely having an eye on this fixture. The Spaniard, preparing for his first taste of the Clásico, will start alongside Pedri in midfield.
Lamine Yamal and Raphinha are shoo-ins in attack, so Flick will have to decide between Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi down the left-hand side.
Barcelona Predicted Lineup vs. Real Madrid (4-2-3-1): J. García; Espart, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Gordon; Raphinha.

There’s drama surrounding starting goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who’s played every minute so far this season. He was ruled out due to flu on the morning of the game, but Courtois himself is still hopeful of playing. If he isn’t good to go, Andriy Lunin will most likely start between the posts.

Real Madrid are functioning just fine without Vinícius Júnior, who’s serving the second of his four-match ban on Sunday. The Brazilian was punished for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in Madrid’s 1–0 victory over Villarreal earlier this month and subsequently remonstrating with the referee.

The in-form Yan Diomande will start down the left in his absence, and Mourinho is poised to deploy a French midfield tandem comprising Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga. Federico Valverde will be shunted out to right back, and Arda Güler will operate freely from the right-side of midfield.
The visitors are missing Ferland Mendy, Raúl Asencio and Rodrygo due to injury.

ftbpro_01m5mx8dzt7n.title: ‘My Responsibility’—Michael Carrick Gives Six-Minute Speech to Open Strange Man Utd Press Conference
ftbpro_01m5mx8dzt7n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer3:30 PM EDTMichael Carrick is trying to break a winless streak on the field. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesIn his pregame press conference ahead of Manchester United’s clash with Bournemouth, Michael Carrick took the unusual step of speaking before any questions had even been asked.
The Red Devils go into Sunday’s match looking for a response to a 4–1 hammering by Como in the Champions League that Carrick labeled “unacceptable” in the aftermath.

On a wider scale, United find themselves on an alarming seven-game winless streak, which is in stark contrast to the way the team finished last season with the best record in the Premier League over the final 17 rounds—better even than champions Arsenal.

So, when he sat in the chair to face the media again, it was clear that the manager wanted to get some things off his chest, primarily talking about doing right by the fans—particularly those who spent time and money following the team to Italy this week, upholding the “values” of the club carved out over decades, the “humility” and “hard work” it demands, that “entitlement cannot” exist and United being more important than any individual.

“I’ll start today,” Carrick immediately told gathered reporters on Friday, rather than waiting for an opening question. Not reading from a script, he took a moment to compose his thoughts and then spoke without interruption for almost six minutes.
“Recently, we haven’t had a good time, I think that’s pretty obvious, so I totally accept that, what we’re going through at the moment,” he said.

“We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with things that I was seeing and what we were doing as a team. We haven’t done well enough lately, I think that’s pretty obvious to say. We’ve had a spell we’re really not happy with.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Man Utd suffered a heavy defeat in Italy. / Marco Luzzani/Getty Images“Wednesday was a bad night, it was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It was a bad night and that hurt a lot. It obviously hurt me to see us play like that, to see how the game panned out.

“It was, as I said after the game, it was really unacceptable for us to play like that and to be like that. The supporters are a huge part of this football club for me, the supporters have to make the effort and spend the time and the money to come and support us on Wednesday. And to have the feeling that we all felt after the game was a tough moment. I think that’s pretty obvious.

“My responsibility is to get a team on the football pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters, and [one] they can be proud of with the identity we showed. We have gone away from that, just recently in certain games, which I’m totally, fully aware of and definitely doing something about. I think it’s important that we all recognize that, I certainly recognize it, and our supporters are [of] the utmost importance to me and the football club.

“For them to feel like they’ve felt for five months at the start of the year, to have that connection and vigor, intensity and enjoyment and passion, that we all felt through that period, was something we need to get back to and we will get back to it, and I fully believe that, and I think it’s important that we recognize that we haven’t been doing that.”

Carrick admitted Man Utd are doing what they should. / Alessio Morgese/NurPhoto/Getty Images“The foundation of this football club and the values of this football club have been etched for many years, and I totally understand and get every one of them. And it comes down to humility, it comes down to being humble, it comes down to being hardworking, and being really proud to work hard and being proud to them values. There’s a resilience about this football club that’s been shown for a long, long time, whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, whether that’s comebacks, whether that’s late goals, whether that’s success, whether that’s sustaining success. There’s a resilience in this football club that runs very, very deep, and I’ve seen it with my own eyes, I’ve felt it.

“I’m aware of some of the individuals and know them closely who have been part of that history. I said it after the game, Manchester United’s always bigger, and always has been, always will be bigger than any single individual. Bigger than me, bigger than any of the players, and it always has been.

“I’m fortunate enough to know some players and played with some myself … Ryan Giggs, arguably one of the greatest to play for this football club. It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United. Wayne Rooney was top goalscorer of this football club, his biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team and what was good for Manchester United.”

Carrick spoke from a place of passion. / Marc Atkins/Getty Images“Sir Alex Ferguson, the best manager of all time, the greatest, for me, and working with him, and his main priority was Manchester United. And going back to Sir Matt [Busby], Sir Bobby [Charlton], the resilience was beyond belief for what they showed and the way they rebuilt this football club.

“Again, it was based on being humble, having humility, and hard work, and we can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that. We’ve had it for a spell. I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that, and keep driving to that with the players and the group, we showed [it] for a good period of time and that we’re capable of it.

“Yes, we’re in a moment where it’s not gone well, so we need to show exactly what it means and, you know, respect this football club, respect what it takes to be here, respect what it takes to win, what you have to do to win.

“I’m not entitled to be here, entitlement cannot be at this football club. We’ve got an incredible past, an incredible history. That doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win. I’m fully aware that it takes hard work, it takes a lot of sacrifice, you’ve got to invest yourself in the football club, and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other and you’ve got to win. I think it’s important we live up to that, and it’s important to push those values and it’s important for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve had it, we’ve kind of lost our way a little bit, if I’m totally honest, and we’ll get it back. I’m totally convinced we’ll get it back. I respect this football club, I respect what it takes, because it’s very, very important to me.”

ftbpro_01m5n11p04v1.title: ‘Something Ugly Happened’—Aurelien Tchouameni Reveals Truth About Federico Valverde Fight
ftbpro_01m5n11p04v1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas8:00 PM EDTAurélien Tchouaméni (left) and Federico Valverde had a headline-stealing altercation toward the end of the 2025–26 season.  / Denis Doyle/Getty Images Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni recently spoke on the altercation he and Federico Valverde had last spring, which ended with the Uruguayan in the hospital. Although they never came to blows, he admitted that “something ugly happened.”

The incident occurred during the chaotic final weeks of Real Madrid’s 2025–26 season. Reports indicated that Tchouaméni and Valverde got in a locker room fight that resulted in the latter requiring stitches for a cut in his head that forced him to miss three games.

Valverde addressed the situation immediately, and both players were fined €500,000 ($580,000) by the club. The Frenchman also spoke on the situation during the infancy of the World Cup; however, now nearly six months after the altercation, Tchouaméni appeared on The Bridge to speak more honestly about what happened.

“People talk a lot, but there was no fight between Valverde and I,” Tchouameni said. “Yes, it’s true that things happen in the locker room, but we never got in a fight. There might’ve been indirect comments or something like that, but I never came to blows with Valverde.

“It’s true that something ugly happened, but the problem is that it’s Real Madrid, so any issue, no matter how small, gets blown out of proportion and generates crazy high media attention. So, something that wasn’t necessarily a problem, becomes one.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Aurélien Tchouaméni (left) and Fede Valverde continue to feature regularly for Real Madrid.  / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesThe headline-grabbing incident prompted many to believe that one of the two midfielders would have to leave the club during the summer transfer window. In the end, both Tchouaméni and Valverde stayed in Madrid, and incoming manager José Mourinho stated that he didn’t even have to address the situation upon arrival, given the pair had a good relationship.
Tchouaméni echoed the words of his manager, revealing he is on good terms with Valverde and that the incident might’ve even helped them grow closer.

“If you walked into the locker room today, as Mourinho said, you’d see that Valverde and I are fine,” Tchouaméni said. “There’s no problem between us. On the pitch there’s no problem either, life goes on.
“In fact, things like this can actually bring you closer to the other person. We are fine, we have no problem.”

Aurélien Tchouaméni (right) is expected to feature in El Clásico on Sunday.  / Adria Puig/Anadolu/Getty ImagesTchouaméni and Valverde’s off-field relationship might be repaired; however, Real Madrid continue to struggle against strong opposition when the pair are deployed together in midfield—as has been the case for the past two seasons.

The pair remain key contributors under Mourinho, but after unconvincing performances, it seems like the Portuguese manager has recently found his best starting XI with both players on the pitch, just not together in the engine room.

Valverde might not love it, but he has been brilliant over the past two games operating as Real Madrid’s right back and is expected to continue featuring at the position. Meanwhile, although he didn’t play last time out, Tchouaméni looked significantly more comfortable and effective with Arda Güler next to him in midfield. He also looked more comfortable in the past next to fellow France international Eduardo Camavinga.
Both Tchouaméni and Valverde are expected to start when Real Madrid visit Barcelona at the Camp Nou on Sunday for the first El Clásico of the 2026–27 season.

Los Blancos are on a high after winning four in a row since the September–October international break; however, now comes the biggest test yet against their bitter rivals. Meanwhile, Real Madrid will fall nine points behind Barça in the standings if they lose on Sunday, significantly compromising their La Liga title hopes with over two-thirds of the season left.

ftbpro_01m5n5c27pa1.title: Christian Pulisic Rendered Helpless in Europa League Clash With USMNT Friend
ftbpro_01m5n5c27pa1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:00 PM EDTChristian Pulisic did not see the field on Thursday. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesChristian Pulisic could only watch from the sidelines as his team was crushed on Thursday afternoon.

The 28-year-old star forward was an unused substitute in AC Milan’s Europa League clash with AFC Bournemouth, watching as the 10-man Rossoneri were thrashed 3–0 by the English side at Vitality Stadium.

Thursday’s affair was supposed to be the battle of Americans—Milan’s Pulisic and Yunus Musah against Bournemouth’s Tyler Adams, the U.S. men’s national team’s newest captain. But while Musah clocked 90 minutes in his usual place in Milan’s central midfield and Adams played a key role in the Cherries’ victory, Pulisic did not touch the pitch.

It wasn’t surprising that Milan manager Ruben Amorim didn’t include Pulisic in the starting XI. The  Portuguese boss has been managing the player’s minutes since the start of the season; however, it was a bit of a shock that he didn’t see the pitch at all. The USMNT poster boy hasn’t been an unused substitute since early September, while still reaching full strength after two separate injuries at the 2026 World Cup this summer.
Next. Pulisic Remains a Nonfactor in AC Milan’s Strong Start. Pulisic Remains a Nonfactor in AC Milan’s Strong Start. dark

First-time European competitors Bournemouth were on the front foot from the starting whistle, opening scoring against the seven-time European champions in the eighth minute off of a penalty kick. The Cherries then doubled their lead, thanks to Adams’s ... face. The USMNT star midfielder was manning Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan on a corner kick, when Maignan two-hand shoved Adams right in the nose. The French goalkeeper was flashed red, earning Bournemouth another penalty, which they buried in the 32nd minute.

The Cherries added their third in the 84th minute on a free kick, all while holding Milan to zero shots on target and just three in total. Although Musah impressed with a 100% passing accuracy—further demonstrating his superior skills as a distributor, Milan had just 36% of the game’s possession, meaning he hardly accessed the ball.

Pulisic’s future remains uncertain.  / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesPulisic’s future at the international level with the USMNT has been in question ever since his lackluster display at the World Cup, leaving him with more injuries (two) than goal contributions (one).

But now, his future at the domestic level with Milan is unclear. Can Pulisic return to a consistent place in the Amorim’s starting lineup and prove to the manager that he is fit enough to handle the intensity of European competition in addition Serie A play? Or will he continue to be a spectator in key moments?

Pulisic is in dire need of a resurgence this season. He ended the 2025–26 campaign on a 19-game goal-less drought, dating back to December 2025. He has struggled to produce in his return to domestic play, notching just one goal and one assist across six appearances this fall.

Milan has had a strong start to the Serie A season, currently sitting fourth in league standings after going undefeated across the first seven matches; however, the Rossoneri will need Pulisic at full force to continue this momentum. Europa League play is also not over, seeing Milan battle Ferencváros next on Nov. 5, a game they desperately need to win.

If Pulisic can regain traction in Italy, he may also be able to regain the affections of USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino over in the States. Pochettino is set to name his roster for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals early next month, ahead of the two matches against Haiti on Nov. 14 and Nov. 17.

ftbpro_01m5n6wxh4fy.title: La Liga Chief Javier Tebas Faces Potential Punishment for Real Madrid Nazi Comparison
ftbpro_01m5n6wxh4fy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:30 PM EDTJavier Tebas has long been at war with Real Madrid and president Florentino Pérez.  / Pablo Cuadra/Getty Images Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) has elevated a complaint against La Liga president Javier Tebas after he compared Real Madrid’s communication techniques to the ones employed by Nazi Germany.

Real Madrid called for Tebas’s immediate resignation after he took to social media to equate the club and their in-house TV channel’s “propaganda techniques” to the ones employed by Nazi minister of propaganda Joseph Goebbels. Instead of backtracking and issuing an apology, Tebas double-downed on his comments days later.

CSD opened an investigation and, on Thursday, it acted on its own initiative and filed a complaint against Tebas with Spain’s Sports Administrative Tribunal (TAD), signed by Spain’s secretary of sport José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes.

CSD released a statement explaining its desire for TAD to consider if Tebas’s comments represent a major infringement of article 76.4.b of Spain’s sports law, which considers “notorious and public acts against sporting dignity or decorum” as grave infractions.
TAD must now decide whether CSD’s complaint has enough merit to open an investigation that could lead to Tebas facing serious punishments. How long that process could take is uncertain.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Javier Tebas could be forced to step down as La Liga president.     / Irina R. Hipolito/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIf TAD decides to act on CSD’s complaint and finds Tebas guilty, then the La Liga president could be in a world of trouble.
AS reports that according to Spain’s sports law, Tebas could face one of three different forms of punishment.

The first would be a public warning, which would be the least severe. Tebas could also receive a fine that doesn’t exceed €3,000 ($3,360). Finally, if TAD deems Tebas’s infraction severe, he could be disqualified from his current role for one month up to two years.

In the past, TAD ruled against former Spain Football Federation president Luis Rubiales and suspended him for three years for violating the same article Tebas is accused of breaching. Rubiales resigned as president even prior to TAD’s ruling in the aftermath of the intense controversy that erupted when he kissed Spain women’s national team player Jennifer Hermoso following La Roja’s 2023 World Cup title.

Since Tebas took over as La Liga president in 2013, CSD has opened over 20 investigations against him, and this is the fifth one to reach TAD, per AS. Of those five, the only sanction Tebas has ever faced is a public warning.

Javier Tebas continues to defend himself.     / Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images/SportelAs was the case when CSD first started its investigation, Tebas has once again taken to social media to respond to the filed complaint to TAD, and he once again called for action against Real Madrid.

“One more,” Tebas wrote. “Another request from CSD to TAD and, once again, headlines about my possible disqualification. The reasons change, but the insistence is the same. We expected it: any excuse was going to work.

“But there’s a silence that especially catches the attention. We haven’t heard the state’s secretary of sport nor any other CSD higher up say a single word of complaint against the accusations made by Real Madrid and their television channel.”

Tebas continues to call for action against Real Madrid after the club’s in-house channel called La Liga a rigged competition and accused him of corruption. He also once again clarified that he never meant to claim that Real Madrid and their fans follow the Nazi ideology; he was only comparing their propaganda techniques to the ones used by the Nazi regime.
“Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas added. “It’s part of my responsibility, and I will continue to enforce it.”

ftbpro_01m5nbncb35g.title: Real Madrid’s El Clasico Record Without Vinicius Junior
ftbpro_01m5nbncb35g.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas10:30 AM EDTVinícius Júnior (right) has been one of the main protagonists of El Clásico in recent times.  / Javier Soriano/AFP/Getty ImagesThe first El Clásico of the season is the headline fixture of the weekend as Real Madrid visit Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday. But Los Blancos will travel to Catalonia without one of the biggest difference-makers in the modern history of the rivalry: Vinícius Júnior.

Vinícius Jr was handed a four-match ban after getting sent off for pulling the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba a fortnight ago. In a matter of seconds, the Brazilian went from scoring a goal to seeing a straight red which resulted in an automatic two-match suspension before an additional two games were added to his ban due to his “aggressive” reaction.
The star winger already missed Real Madrid’s 4–1 thumping of Sevilla last time out in La Liga, but now he’ll have to watch from home as Los Blancos face league leaders Barcelona in Sunday’s Clásico.

Vinícius Jr had featured in Real Madrid’s most recent 21 matches against Barcelona, including the last 13 in La Liga. The first Clásico of 2026–27 will be the first the Brazilian misses since the turn of the decade, and given his record against Barça, his absence is significant.

Few players have been as decisive in El Clásico’s recent history as Vinícius Jr. Plus, his personality has also contributed to the theatrics of a rivalry that oozes drama and controversy. There’s no denying the Brazilian is one of the faces of El Clásico’s modern era and that, despite his recent struggles, he remains an integral part of Real Madrid’s current side.

His absence on Sunday will be sorely felt, especially considering you have to go all the way back to his first 18 months at the club to find the only two El Clásico’s he’s missed since he joined Real Madrid.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Luis Suárez scored a hat-trick against Real Madrid in the first El Clásico of 2018–19.  / Miquel Llop/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesReal Madrid Starting XI: Courtois; Nacho, Varane, Ramos, Marcelo; Kroos, Casemiro, Modrić; Bale, Benzema, Isco (Subs: Vázquez, Asensio, Mariano)
Barcelona Starting XI: Ter Stegen; Roberto, Piqué, Lenglet, Alba; Rakitić, Busquets, Arthur; Rafinha, Suárez, Coutinho (Subs: Semedo, Dembélé, Vidal)

Almost exactly one month after Vinícius Jr made his Real Madrid debut, he wasn’t even part of then manager Julen Lopetegui’s squad for the first El Clásico of the 2018–19 season in which Los Blancos were destroyed 5–1 by their bitter rivals.

Without an injured Lionel Messi, it was Luis Suárez who commanded Barcelona’s victory with the first and only hat trick of his Clásico career. Philippe Coutinho opened the scoring for the Catalans and Arturo Vidal completed Los Blancos’ humbling with a late fifth, even after Marcelo had bagged the consolation goal earlier in the second half.
The first Clásico of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era was an utter embarrassment for Real Madrid, and  Lopetegui was fired a day after the catastrophic defeat.
Vinícius was 18 when the match took place, and he’d go on to make his El Clásico debut the following February in the 1–1 draw at Camp Nou in the first leg of the Copa del Rey semifinal.

Lionel Messi (right) and Karim Benzema couldn’t avoid a scoreless draw in the first El Clásico of 2019–20.  / Pablo Morano/MB Media/Getty ImagesReal Madrid Starting XI: Courtois; Carvajal, Varane, Ramos, Mendy; Valverde, Casemiro, Kroos; Bale, Benzema, Isco (Subs: Modrić, Rodrygo)
Barcelona Starting XI: Ter Stegen; Semedo, Piqué, Lenglet, Alba; Roberto, Rakitić, De Jong; Messi, Suárez, Griezmann (Subs: Vidal, Fati)

The last Vinícius Jr–less El Clásico came in December 2019. Unlike a year prior, then manager Zinédine Zidane did include the Brazilian in the squad that traveled to Camp Nou for the first Clásico of the season, but the teenager was an unused substitute in a rare 0–0 draw between the rivals.

Despite a wealth of attacking talent on the pitch such as Barcelona’s newly formed trio of Messi, Suárez and Antoine Griezmann, plus Los Blancos’ front three of Gareth Bale, Isco and Karim Benzema, the scoreless draw saw a combined six attempts on goal between the two teams.
Interestingly, Real Madrid and Barcelona’s current captains, Federico Valverde and Frenkie de Jong, featured for the first time in a league Clásico in the scoreless draw.

The final Clásico of the 2010s was hardly a memorable one. It remains the last game of the rivalry that ended in a scoreless draw, and it’s also the last Clásico in which Vinícius Jr failed to feature until Sunday’s upcoming clash.

ftbpro_01m5pn62v0a4.title: Bayern Munich Chief Offers Worrying Vincent Kompany Recovery Timeline After Training Collapse
ftbpro_01m5pn62v0a4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:10 AM EDTVincent Kompany spent the night in hospital. / Stuart Franklin - UEFA/Getty ImagesBayern Munich sporting director Max Eberl has confessed he expects to be without manager Vincent Kompany for “weeks” as he continues to undergo tests after collapsing during training on Friday.

Reports suggest Kompany had been battling illness over the past few weeks, although the reason for his collapse has not yet been confirmed. A medical helicopter treated the manager at the training ground before he was rushed away to hospital in an ambulance.

Thankfully, Eberl confirmed Kompany is stable and communicating, but the sporting director expects this to be the start of a lengthy recovery process that may keep Kompany out of action for the foreseeable future.
“The good news: He’s stable,” Eberl said. “We’ve spoken. It wasn’t a pleasant moment for any of us.

“He’s in the hospital and will stay for a few days until everything has been checked out. This just goes to show that health is the most important thing in life—not football. We at Bayern Munich are all in this together. The most important thing is finding the cause. He shouldn’t come back until he’s fit. We have to protect him.
“The doctors are doing nothing but finding out what it is. Further tests are needed to determine the appropriate treatment. He is in the best hands. We can support him energetically and with love.
“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs; we’re not setting any timeframes. We need to figure out what it is. Then we can calmly consider what the recovery time means.

“We’re not talking about days, but weeks. Everyone should be clear about that. The coaching staff isn’t considering changing anything. They all have Vinnie’s spirit with them. That’s how we’ll approach the next few weeks.”

Aaron Danks will replace Kompany on the sidelines. / L. Vogt/FC Bayern/Getty ImagesIn Kompany’s absence, managerial duties will be left to his assistant, Aaron Danks. The pair first worked together at Anderlecht before reuniting at Bayern in the summer of 2024.
Danks has filled in for Kompany in the past but now appears set to oversee an extended run at the helm, beginning with Sunday’s trip to Freiburg.
October also brings a DFB Pokal meeting with second-tier Magdeburg, before a huge visit from Borussia Dortmund on the final day of the month.

Bayern then travel to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Nov. 3 and return to Bundesliga action four days later against Mainz before the November international break. Whether Kompany will be ready to return beyond that will be determined by the results of the upcoming medical tests.

ftbpro_01m5pp8wjb48.title: ‘Out of Control’—The Biggest Issue Facing Man Utd in New Manager Search
ftbpro_01m5pp8wjb48.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:45 AM EDTMan Utd are in the midst of a real crisis. / Marco Canoniero/LightRocket/Getty ImagesAs Manchester United weigh up the future of manager Michael Carrick, a number of those under consideration are reported to have major concerns about the atmosphere inside the dressing room.

Carrick will remain in charge for Sunday’s meeting with Bournemouth but will be well aware that extending their seven-game winless run could force United into making a tough decision on his future. The Red Devils have won just twice all season—besting newly promoted Ipswich Town in August and defeating Sabah of Azerbaijan last month.

A handful of big names have already been touted as possible replacements, but The Telegraph state several of those in United’s sights have significant concerns about the toxicity of the dressing room.

Club legend Wayne Rooney feared the dressing room would be “ripped apart” by Lisandro Martínez’s recent criticism of technical director Jason Wilcox and Bruno Fernandes’s dim assessment of Carrick’s tactics.
Bringing the dressing room back in line is seen as a priority for more than one of United’s potential candidates, who believe the squad is “out of control” and full of players who “talk too much.”

There are just two ways to fix that. United could hire a firm hand capable of drilling their high standards into the squad, or the players found to be contributing to the issues would have to be sold. Neither is a guaranteed route to success.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Michael Carrick is one of many to struggle. / Luca Rossini/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe need to quieten the noise coming out of the Old Trafford dressing room has plagued more managers than just Carrick.

It was back in 2022 that Ralf Rangnick, operating as interim manager following the dismissal of Ole Gunnar Solskjær, claimed the club needed “open heart surgery.” He pointed to a need for “strong leadership,” alongside players with the right attitude and a solid plan from those in the boardroom as well.

Erik ten Hag joined that summer and quickly kicked things off by feuding with Cristiano Ronaldo, recently claiming the Portugal international’s poor work rate was letting the team down. A brief upturn in fortunes soon faded and Ruben Amorim was next up to face the challenge in 2024.

While results were miserable during Amorim’s tenure, the current AC Milan boss did plenty of work when it came to stabilizing the dressing room. He took issue with both Marcus Rashford and Alejandro Garnacho’s performances in training and spoke openly about the long-term nature of his project, only for the team’s on-field showings to see him fired in early 2026.

By turning to Carrick as Amorim’s replacement, United hoped that his status as a club legend could be the secret to success, and that did appear to be the case during an electric end to last season, but things took a brutal downward turn this year as the same issues resurfaced for United.

Whoever ends this season in the Old Trafford dugout will have some tough decisions to make, particularly when it comes to contracts. Alongside Martínez and Fernandes, both Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are in the final year of their respective contracts, with the latter the only player whose deal does not include a 12-month extension clause.

ftbpro_01m5pr36wmtw.title: Ronaldinho to Make Spectacular Return to Professional Football With Confirmed Date
ftbpro_01m5pr36wmtw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:15 AM EDTRonaldinho is due to return to the pitch. / Sathire Kelpa/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesIconic Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho will return to competitive soccer next month in a game for Italian third-tier side Ravenna, the club have confirmed.

Ronaldinho, now 46, signed up with Ravenna back in June in a move that was met with significant scepticism. He was used in a handful of promotional appearances and a stint on the pitch was teased by some inside the club, even if vice-president Ariedo Braida argued it would not happen.
Months later, Ravenna have now confirmed Ronaldinho will take to the pitch for the first time in over 11 years in an official Serie C game against rivals Forlì on Nov. 15.

“The entire football world thought it was too good to be true, but instead we can officially announce a great return,” Ravenna said in a statement. “A return of magic, of a smile, of a talent capable of captivating generations of fans, beyond their colors and footballing allegiance.

“There are footballers who are remembered for what they’ve won, and others for what they’ve inspired. Ronaldinho belongs to that rare breed of champions capable of transforming football into happiness: an unexpected gesture, an invention, a smile that has united stadiums and generations. On Nov. 15, that same emotion will meet the passion of the Giallorossi and the atmosphere of a derby deeply felt by the city.

“For Ravenna, it will be a day destined to remain in the club’s and its fans’ memories. For fans around the world, it will be a chance to see one of the most beloved figures in football history back on the pitch.
“The wait is almost over. The magic returns to the field.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Ronaldinho has not played professionally since 2015. / Stefano RELLANDINI/AFP/Getty ImagesThe idea of seeing Ronaldinho back on the pitch is equally exciting as it is confusing.

The 46-year-old is widely considering to be one of the greatest players of all time—and undoubtedly one of the most exciting. Ronaldinho won the Ballon d’Or in 2005 and was part of the Brazil setup that won the 2002 World Cup, while he also enjoyed success at club level with Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan.
Crucially, however, his European peak came 15 years ago.

After returning to Brazil with Flamengo in 2011, Ronaldinho bounced around clubs before ultimately retiring with Fluminense in 2015. “He respectfully told us he didn’t feel he was able to perform as well as he wanted and that it was a bad situation for him,” sporting director Mario Bittencourt revealed at the time.
So, 11 years later, has Ronaldinho changed his mind?
Ravenna have long been adamant that their contract with Ronaldinho is more than a simple publicity stunt, but his impending return to the pitch will still be viewed as such until proven otherwise.

Ronaldinho will undoubtedly bring plenty of eyes to Ravenna, who sit second in their section of Serie C, but those expecting 90 minutes of glorious skill moves and flashes of the greatness that took over the world in the early 2000s are set to be sorely disappointed. After all, there is a reason players of his age are rarely seen at any level in the professional game.

ftbpro_01m5prnn5wc0.title: Man City Player Ratings vs. Aston Villa: Perfect Record Evaporates in Error-Strewn Display
ftbpro_01m5prnn5wc0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray9:50 AM EDTMan City suffered their first league defeat of the season. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesManchester City’s perfect Premier League record was extinguished on Saturday as they were beaten 2–1 by Aston Villa following a Nicolas Jackson brace.

The guilty verdict continues to loom over the Cityzens, repeatedly throwing into question what their Premier League matches really mean until a punishment is laid out, but they had little time for existential thoughts after falling behind to Jackson’s terrific opener in just the sixth minute.

City responded impressively at Villa Park, albeit without being able to find an equalizer before the break. They frequently forced Zion Suzuki into athletic saves either side of two half-hearted penalty appeals, and Iliman Ndiaye came closest when his wicked strike crashed off the outside of the post.

The visitors continued to pile on pressure after the restart and were swiftly rewarded when Erling Haaland’s towering header brought them level. But their joy was short-lived as Villa retook the lead when Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to rebuff Jackson’s fizzing drive.

Despite huffing and puffing for an equalizer to preserve their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign, City ultimately came up short against a resilient Villa rearguard—and that leaves the door ajar for title rivals Arsenal to move level on points with them at the summit.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Iliman Ndiaye was lively in the Midlands. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesWhile not City’s sleekest display of the current campaign, there were some encouraging individual showings worthy of praise. Iliman Ndiaye is one of those who stood out, taking advantage of Villa’s willingness to funnel the ball into wide areas when defending.

The summer recruit’s quick feet and explosive acceleration was City’s greatest outlet, so it was little surprise to see their equalizer stem from his creativity. An inch-perfect delivery into the penalty area found the grateful head of Haaland.
There were other moments of invention from Ndiaye, who enjoyed darting inside and taking aim. One of those efforts thwacked the woodwork, while another was impressively saved by Suzuki.

A tough day for Guéhi. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesIt’s been a tumultuous period for Marc Guéhi since City’s guilty verdict. Whether the ruling has had any genuine influence on his performances is unclear, but he’s been making errors for club and country regardless. After a disastrous mistake for England in its 3–2 defeat to Spain in late September, the center back gifted Jackson his opener at Villa Park almost exactly a month later.

An extremely poor touch from Enzo Fernández’s lofted pass across the defense ricocheted into the path of John McGinn, who in turn found Jackson. The finish was instinctive and clinical, but there would have been no such opportunity without Guéhi’s costly blunder—one of many instances where City, and Guéhi more specifically, struggled to handle the ex-Chelsea forward.
As Villa’s goalkeeper Suzuki continually proved his worth with some fantastic saves, Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to match the quality of his opposite number.

The Italian was undoubtedly at fault for Jackson’s second goal. Sure, the shot was struck with ferocity, but it was incredibly central when squirming beneath Donnarumma’s body. Not for the first time, the City stopper finds himself under the microscope.
Haaland did what Haaland does best. / Molly Darlington/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—3.9: Absolutely had to save from Jackson on the hour. Simply not good enough from a supposedly elite goalkeeper.
RB: Abdukodir Khusanov—8.1: Shifted into central defense after halftime following an entertaining battle up against the eye-catching Johan Manzambi. Proved an upgrade on Guéhi.

CB: Marc Guéhi—5.2: Moved to the right side of defense by Enzo Maresca, which seemed to rattle him. Consistently struggled in battles with the lively Jackson, alongside making the mistake which offered Villa their early lead. Withdrawn at halftime, too.
CB: Rúben Dias—6.2: One absolutely vital intervention denied an almost certain goal during the first half, but, like his teammates, he sometimes found life hard against Villa’s direct forwards.

LB: Joško Gvardiol—7.3: Caused issues by Alysson, who was desperate to dribble at every opportunity, but at least provided some serious attacking threat. Gvardiol would have been among the goals had it not been for several fantastic saves from Suzuki.

CM: Elliot Anderson—7.8: Such an impressive general in midfield, eating up ground and recovering possession with ease. Worth every penny of his $154 million fee—well, when it comes to modern transfer fees, at least.

ftbpro_01m5psnmmr1f.title: Jose Mourinho’s Full Record in El Clasico as Real Madrid Manager
ftbpro_01m5psnmmr1f.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 24, 2026José Mourinho has overseen plenty of battles with Barcelona. / Federico Titone/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesBarcelona have been one of José Mourinho’s most regular adversaries during his illustrious managerial career.

Only Liverpool have been more frequent opponents for the wily Portuguese coach, who was formerly on the books at Camp Nou as an aspiring manager. The majority of his previous battles with the Catalan giants he once also worked for have come in one of soccer’s grandest games: El Clásico.
During his original three-year stint with Real Madrid, he simply couldn’t escape Barcelona as the Spanish behemoths fought for supremacy on the domestic and continental stage.
Here’s Mourinho’s full record in the fixture.

Los Blancos were humiliated in Mourinho’s first derby. / Jasper Juinen/Getty ImagesThings started disastrously for Mourinho in El Clásico. As he ventured to Catalonia with his star-studded Real Madrid squad for the first time, few expected Los Blancos to be departing with their tails between their legs following a humiliating 5–0 defeat in La Liga—the club’s joint-heaviest loss margin in the fixture since the end of World War II.

Barça’s fearsome forward trio completely annihilated their visitors, with Pedro scoring the second goal of the match and David Villa then adding two more after the break courtesy of Lionel Messi assists. Either side of those strikes, Xavi and Jeffrén were on the scoresheet, with the latter compounding Madrid’s misery in stoppage time shortly before an inevitable Sergio Ramos red card.
Los Blancos endured mixed results during their four subsequent fixtures against Barcelona later that season—all of which took place over the course of a three-week period.

The sides would stage a stalemate at the Bernabéu in the reverse fixture in La Liga, a result which helped Barça to the title despite Madrid scoring 102 goals across the league season. They would, however, get some revenge in the Copa del Rey final.

A fiercely competitive occasion was goalless come the end of regulation time, but Cristiano Ronaldo provided the all-important winner in the 103rd minute. The decisive strike earned Mourinho his first of three pieces of silverware in Spain’s capital, but the bragging rights would soon return to Barcelona.

There were two Clásicos to be played in a Champions League semifinal and they finished in Barça’s favor. Madrid’s 2–0 defeat on home soil in the first leg meant they needed a miracle to reach the final, and their 1–1 draw at Camp Nou the following week was not enough to turn the tie around.
In the end, Barcelona beat Manchester United in the Champions League final, leaving Mourinho and his players in agony after being bested in Madrid’s favorite tournament.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Real Madrid all but won La Liga at Camp Nou in 2011–12. / Víctor Carretero/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesThe 2011–12 campaign kicked off with two Clásico meetings. On this occasion, the Supercopa de España would force them together, with the victor determined across two legs—one at the Bernabéu and the other at Camp Nou.

There was nothing to separate Mourinho and nemesis Pep Guardiola during the first match in Madrid, with Xabi Alonso’s second-half equalizer the final major act of a 2–2 draw. The second leg was decided by more Messi magic, though, with the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner assisting and then scoring twice—including an 88th-minute winner—to secure Barcelona’s 3–2 victory and 5–4 aggregate triumph.

The next three matches also went in Barça’s favor, beginning with a 3–1 win for them at the Bernabéu in La Liga. Despite Karim Benzema’s opener in the first minute, goals from Alexis Sánchez, Xavi and Cesc Fàbregas completed a dramatic turnaround to clinch an early Christmas present.

Mourinho again succumbed to Guardiola’s tiki-taka brilliance in the Copa del Rey quarterfinals at the beginning of 2012. Barcelona won at the Bernabéu during the first leg courtesy of unlikely strikes from Carles Puyol and Éric Abidal, before edging the aggregate score with a 2–2 draw on their own turf.

Following heartbreak in the copa, Mourinho had only won one of his first 10 Clásicos, but he was immensely grateful to triumph during his 11th. In only the fourth-last match of the La Liga season and with the title race still alive, Madrid secured a crucial 2–1 victory at Camp Nou which effectively won them the crown.

Ronaldo scored the winning goal after halftime as Madrid inched toward their second trophy under Mourinho. They eventually reached a century of points, scored 121 goals and managed 32 victories—all of which were La Liga records at the time.

Real Madrid started the campaign by conquering Barça in the Supercopa. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesMourinho’s final season of his first spell with Madrid was much more positive—well, Clásico-wise, at least. While the first showdown ended in a 3–2 defeat in the Supercopa de España first leg at Camp Nou, his side’s 2–1 win in the reverse fixture granted them he trophy via the away goals rule.

The opening La Liga Clásico was a case of Ronaldo vs. Messi. Both players scored a brace during the 2–2 draw in Catalonia on Matchday 7, and there was nothing to divide the foes when they collided the following January in the first leg of the Copa del Rey semifinal.

ftbpro_01m5pssed8m4.title: Jadon Sancho ‘Facing Huge Pay Cut’ to Salvage Career
ftbpro_01m5pssed8m4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:00 AM EDTJadon Sancho is still looking for a new club. / Marcel Bonte/Soccrates/Getty ImagesFormer Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho has been offered a contract by Getafe worth just 4% of his previous salary, a report has revealed.

When United signed Sancho from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2021 for a fee of $100 million (£73 million), they handed him a contract with a weekly wage of £250,000 ($334,000) that he held all the way up to his release in the summer.

Sancho struggled horribly in the Premier League, even failing to catch the eye during loans with both Chelsea and Aston Villa, before United declined to trigger an extension clause in his contract and allowed the 26-year-old to depart on a free transfer.
Spanish side Getafe made an offer to Sancho earlier this month which, according to The Telegraph, is on an entirely different planet financially to what he will have been used to in England.

Getafe’s offer to Sancho is an annual salary of just €400,000 ($448,000)—less than he would make across two weeks of his previous contract with United—on a contract that runs until the end of the current season.
Sancho has not ruled out taking the offer and is interested in playing in La Liga. He is expected to meet with club management in the coming days to formally assess the offer.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Sancho’s last United appearance came in August 2024. / Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesSancho has been a household name for nearly 10 years now.

His decision to swap Manchester City’s academy for Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2017 drew plenty of eyes, and his immediate impact on the senior side quickly commanded headlines. In 2018–19, he contributed to 30 goals in the Bundesliga and increased that to 34 the following year, at which point Europe’s elite were all lining up to throw money at him.

United’s victory in that transfer battle was widely praised at the time, with Sancho backed to be a transformational piece of the puzzle. The pressure that followed, boosted further by the finances involved, have kept Sancho in the spotlight ever since.
Unfortunately for Sancho, very little has gone right for him on the pitch in the last five years. His every move has been scrutinized to unsustainable levels.

A move to Spain would give Sancho a much-needed fresh start, while Getafe are hardly the sort of team that will command international attention. They would, instead, provide a platform quieter than anything Sancho has ever experienced before.

That would allow Sancho to try and rebuild his career in peace. While he may never hit his previous heights from his Dortmund days, the winger’s priority will simply be reversing the nosedive in which his career finds itself right now.

ftbpro_01m5pvrc7tak.title: ‘Just How It Is’—Mourinho’s Typically Bold Prediction Before El Clasico
ftbpro_01m5pvrc7tak.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:30 AM EDTJosé Mourinho is still backing his side. / Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesReal Madrid manager José Mourinho has insisted Sunday’s huge meeting with Barcelona will not define his team, simply proclaiming: “Real Madrid wins titles with Mourinho.”

Madrid find themselves third in La Liga after the first nine games of Mourinho’s second reign. Atlético Madrid enter the weekend one point ahead, with Barcelona a further five in front up in first. Performances have been mixed and there are genuine fears that Los Blancos could be out of the title race if Hansi Flick’s side are victorious on Sunday.
It was put to Mourinho that he will get a concrete understanding of where his side truly are after Sunday’s Clásico, but the Madrid boss was simply not interested as he set his sights even higher.
“It isn’t [a litmus test],” Mourinho warned the media. “Real Madrid wins titles with Mourinho.”

If that proclamation is to remain accurate, Madrid will need to find a way to stop Barcelona this weekend. The reigning champions could be nine points ahead after just 10 matches if they extend their perfect start. Barça ended last season eight points ahead of Madrid.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mourinho remains under immense pressure. / Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesOn paper, most teams on the planet would gleefully accept Madrid’s start to the season. Mourinho has overseen 10 wins and two losses from his first 12 games back at the helm, with a perfect record in the Champions League after three rounds of the league phase played.
The mood surrounding Madrid does not match that record.

In truth, a series of underwhelming performances and questions about the roles of several big names have left many questioning whether this iteration of Madrid is capable of living up to the high standards at the Bernabéu, with Mourinho’s own credentials under scrutiny.

“I have the feeling that’s just how Real Madrid is,” Mourinho said when asked if he feels he deserves more credit. “I don’t look for anything more than credit for my players when they do well and criticism for their coach when we don’t do so well.

“It’s the story of all coaches. Some matches are won by the players and others are lost by the coaches; that’s life. There are at least two Clásicos a season. The most important thing is the global dimension. There are other important ones, but this one is unique. The world stops to watch it.”
Mourinho went on to argue Madrid have been victims of comparison to a Barcelona unit that already has plenty of experience together.
“The fact that people speak well of Barça doesn’t bother me,” he said. “To be honest, there are matches where they obviously deserve to be praised because they do some really good things.

“In our case, we’re seen as a finished product. Finished products in football are difficult to define. If you’re talking about us at an advanced stage of the process, we’ve been working for three months. If you take away preseason, the international break ... we’ve been working for a month and a half.

“Far from being a finished product, we’re an initial product where we’re in a preliminary phase where the coach is getting to know us, analyzing and developing strategies ... The players are also getting to know me. Comparing a team like this with one that’s been around for longer doesn’t seem fair to me.”

ftbpro_01m5q25hb8bt.title: Wrexham Made to Pay for Summer Transfer Decision in Blackburn Defeat
ftbpro_01m5q25hb8bt.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay12:08 PM EDTBlackburn proved too much for Wrexham. / Lee Parker - CameraSport/Getty ImagesWrexham knew they would have to spend big just to remain competitive in the Championship this season, but they did not believe they needed to break the bank to sign a new striker.

The Red Dragons claimed they were “comfortable” with their goalscoring options in the summer and felt the priority should be improving the service to their two senior strikers. Meanwhile, Ryan Reynolds described the transfer business as a “home renovation show,” with the focus on improving the kitchen rather than upgrading everything.

Phil Parkinson has also been quick to point out that scoring goals was not the problem last season; keeping them out at the other end was. There was certainly logic to that argument, given the Red Dragons played with just one striker throughout the campaign. But with their recent switch to two strikers, there is now an even greater emphasis on finding the back of the net.
It is an area in which Wrexham need to improve significantly if they are to match their ambitions of reaching the playoffs by the end of the season.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kieffer Moore started in attack. / Cody Froggatt/PA Images/Getty ImagesWrexham stuck with two strikers for their trip to face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday, making just one change from the victory over Preston North End as Issa Kaboré replaced Danny Imray at right wingback. Kieffer Moore was again partnered by Sam Smith in attack for the second consecutive week.

Blackburn started strongly and came close to scoring a spectacular opener when Jayden Fevrier cut inside onto his left foot and curled a shot just wide of the post. The Red Dragons, however, managed to take the sting out of the game and push the hosts back into their own half.
Kaboré posed a constant threat out wide, regularly collecting the ball on the right and whipping crosses into the box for the two strikers waiting to attack them.

Although Wrexham struggled to create clear-cut chances in the opening stages, their aerial bombardment caused uncertainty in the Blackburn box. It culminated in a chaotic goalmouth scramble in which Callum O’Hare and Moore both saw close-range efforts blocked.
Wrexham were the more threatening side during an encouraging first half, but despite registering 10 shots, they failed to put any on target. Worse still, they went into halftime trailing.
Blackburn thought they had taken the lead when Hayden Carter’s mis-hit header bounced off the inside of the post and into the grateful hands of Anthony Patterson on the goal line.

The chance lifted the hosts, who took the lead just before halftime. Patterson parried a shot from Samy Morsy straight into the path of Andri Guðjohnsen, who reacted quickest to fire the loose ball into the bottom corner.

Blackburn were too much for Wrexham. / Lee Parker - CameraSport/Getty ImagesThe ball moved in the air, but Wrexham fans could hardly be blamed for expecting better from their $10.8 million club-record signing in goal, particularly when many had argued that the money spent on Patterson would have been better invested in a striker.

Patterson needed redemption, and he did not have to wait long for another opportunity. Just three minutes after the restart, Wrexham were careless in midfield once again, allowing the ball to reach Dapo Afolayan on the left wing. The Blackburn forward looked certain to double his side’s lead but was denied by an excellent save from the summer signing.

Wrexham continued to push for an equalizer and came close when Smith glanced a header wide after a superb delivery into the box from the lively O’Hare. The Red Dragons deserved a goal for their efforts, but creating chances and converting them are two very different things.
O’Hare linked up neatly with Jacques Ekomié on the left, only for Moore to see his effort blocked inside the box before center back Joe Worrall drilled a shot agonizingly wide of the post.

Parkinson turned to his bench in an attempt to gain a better grip on proceedings, but following a triple substitution, Wrexham’s hopes began to fade. They continued to surrender possession too easily in midfield, allowing Todd Cantwell to set up Guðjohnsen for a clinical finish and his second goal of the game.
The result means Guðjohnsen, son of former Barcelona and Chelsea forward Eidur, now has nine goals this season. That is three more than Moore and Smith have managed combined.

The Red Dragons continued to launch balls forward as they desperately searched for a way back into the game, but with just one of their 23 shots on target, their attacking efforts were driven more by hope than genuine conviction.
