ftbpro_01m5q338dgsw.title: Mikel Arteta Responds to David Raya’s Dream of Playing in La Liga
ftbpro_01m5q338dgsw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer11:00 AM EDTDavid Raya is in contention for the 2026 Yashin Trophy. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesMikel Arteta has joked the only way Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will be playing soccer in his native Spain any time soon is if it’s during a summer vacation.

Raya recently stoked intrigue about his future by revealing in an interview he would “love” to give La Liga a go. “For now, I’m very happy [at Arsenal], but I would certainly like to experience the Spanish league,” he told MARCA.
“Perhaps, in the future, I could play for a Spanish club. I’m Spanish and I’d love to play there.”

Raya is a relatively uncommon specimen among the elite, in that he has never played pro club soccer in his own country. The goalkeeper was born and raised in Barcelona, taking his first steps in the youth team at UE Cornellà, owned since April 2026 by Lionel Messi.

Raya left home aged just 16 in 2012, heading to England in the hope of making his career. Blackburn Rovers, Premier League champions in 1994 –95 but relegated at the start of that summer, became his landing spot. He progressed to the first team two years later and was the club’s starting goalkeeper for the 2017–18 and 2018–19 seasons.

From there, Raya was scouted by Brentford, before Arteta decided in 2023 he was an unmissable upgrade on Aaron Ramsdale that would elevate Arsenal to the next level. The goalkeeper has three Premier League Golden Gloves from the last three seasons and by Monday night could realistically win the Yashin Trophy at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony as the best in the world.
Although not a starter for his country, Raya has also been a fixture of Spain rosters for the last four years and is a European Championship and World Cup winner as a result.
Playing for a club in La Liga is therefore a conspicuous gap in his career achievements.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Mikel Arteta staked his reputation on signing Raya in 2023. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesBut, as far as Arteta is concerned, it will have to wait.

“I think David has to play in Spain at some point ... on the beach with his friends in the summer,” the Gunners boss joked when the question was raised at a press conference. “For the next few years, he needs to play here for Arsenal.”
Arteta himself spent most of his own playing career outside Spain, although he did still make 42 appearances at pro level for Barcelona B and later 17 with hometown team Real Sociedad.

Raya has entered the final two years of his Arsenal contract, which ends in June 2028. Aged 31, he is by no means old—especially for a goalkeeper—but is also long past the infancy of his career. He will be just shy of his 33rd birthday when that contract is expiring. Based on Arteta’s comments, Arsenal would be expected to soon attempt to secure his future until at least 2030.

This is perhaps not a crazy idea / David Ramos/Getty ImagesRaya would have to ask himself how badly he wants to play in Spain and at what stage of his career. Does he want to be in La Liga in his prime, or would he be satisfied with a retirement tour?

If it is the former, the time to go would be no later than 2028. Then, it’s a question of which clubs might be a good fit. The obvious answer is Barcelona from a style point of view and his childhood spent in the city. That falls down, however, when considering the club’s 2025 investment in Joan García, who is thriving and a nominee for this year’s Yashin Trophy alongside Raya.

Even though he is from Barcelona, Raya is on record stating he grew up not supporting a particular team. That could make Real Madrid a possibility and there might be a conveniently timed opportunity to replace Thibaut Courtois, aged 34, for Los Blancos in due course.
There is a similar situation with Jan Oblak at Atlético Madrid, although it is certainly plausible that both he and Courtois could both continue at this level into their late thirties.

If Raya waited a little longer to head back to Spain, he might consider Espanyol. The club has its home in the Cornellà de Llobregat neighborhood, where his soccer journey began. But what about UE Cornellà as the ultimate fairytale homecoming?

The team currently plays in the Tercera Federación, tier five in Spain’s league pyramid, but Messi didn’t invest his money just to let the club sit. La Liga is still four promotions away, yet it would be a magical story if a rise to the top division in the next few years is met with Raya returning. In that scenario, Arsenal get to keep him for at least four years, and everbody wins.

ftbpro_01m5q3warbpz.title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Everton: ‘Boring, Boring’ Gunners Are Back
ftbpro_01m5q3warbpz.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer12:18 PM EDTGabriel scored the second Arsenal goal after Ezri Konsa got the first. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesArsenal returned to Premier League action with a 2–0 win over Everton to move level with leaders Manchester City, who surprisingly lost to Aston Villa earlier in the day.

Any early concerns about a Champions League hangover, only three days removed from a titanic battle in Munich, were soon erased when Ezri Konsa turned the ball in following a corner. Everton managed to keep the initial effort out, as Ben White and Gabriel both attacked the initial in-swinging delivery at the near post. But Konsa was in the right place at the right time at the far post to prod the ball over the line from no more than a yard out.

Everton actually responded well to falling behind and a couple of opportunities in quick succession from Tyrique George and Thierno Barry might have brought them an equalizer on another day. Arsenal had last-ditch defensive actions to thank in both instances.

The Gunners had more of their own opportunities, with Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze flattering to deceive in auditions to pick up the slack from Bukayo Saka’s new injury. James Tarkowski at the heart of the Everton defense also proved a source of frustration, but Jordan Pickford was barely being tested. And the Toffees ought to have been level at halftime when White’s attempt at getting the ball back to David Raya was picked off by Barry. It had to be a good save from the Arsenal goalkeeper to prevent conceding in embarrassing fashion.

With open-play creativity limited once play resumed after halftime, Arsenal needed to strangle Everton by keeping the ball away from the visitors. That denied the Toffees a platform from which to play and threaten, paving the way for the champions to kill off the match.

Gabriel, who looked ready to come off nursing an injury just over 10 minutes earlier, was the man in the right place at the right time to head in White’s cross from inside the six-yard box after a good Arsenal had moved the ball into position to make a chance.
Everton could have made a game of it in the final 10 minutes when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall headed a chance wide of Raya’s post.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Set Piece FC. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesKonsa scored his first Gunners goal since arriving from Aston Villa in August. But, arguably more importantly, this was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season, reverting to the tried and tested.

Arteta’s team scored 35 times from set pieces across all competitions in 2025–26, accounting for 29% of their entire output. Arsenal haven’t had that reliance on similar situations so far in 2026–27, but this one felt like a struggle to make meaningful chances in other ways.
In the first 45 minutes alone, the Gunners had peppered the Everton box with 10 corners, in the same breath sending nearly all of 13 attempts on goal off target.

The second goal from Gabriel wasn’t the direct result of a set piece, but it might as well have been. Everton partially cleared an initial corner swung in by Declan Rice, with the ball recycled and worked across the pitch. By the time, White clipped a ball towards the far post, 28 seconds had elapsed from the original set piece, but Gabriel had stayed upfield.
Ultimately, it doesn’t matter how you win as long as you do. Arsenal have underlined here that even a performance lacking spark can still finish in a comfortable victory.
Eberechi Eze did a lot without doing much of anything. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: David Raya—7.7: Saved his team’s blushes with a crucial save at the end of the first half. The game could have become very different had the score gone to 1–1.
RB: Ben White—8.1: It was his gift that Raya took back, almost proving very costly. But he made up for that by involvement in the first Arsenal goal and providing the cross that sealed the win.
CB: Ezri Konsa—8.0: Looking to give Arteta every reason to keep him in the team as William Saliba creeps nearer to a recovery. Never under real threat and contributed his goal.
CB: Gabriel—8.5: There was genuine concern about the Brazilian early in the second half after appearing to hurt his knee, but he soldiered on and ended up getting the killer second.
LB: Myles Lewis-Skelly—7.6: A rest for Riccardo Calafiori meant a first Premier League start of the season at left back. Strong defensively, although it was a needless yellow card.
CM: Declan Rice—7.9: A fairly typical all-action performance.

ftbpro_01m5q65wexhv.title: Ranking All 20 Premier League Teams’ Performances on Matchday 8
ftbpro_01m5q65wexhv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom6:00 PM EDTThere was a real contrast of emotions across the Premier League weekend. / Dan Istitene/Getty Images (Dalot), Liverpool FC/Getty Images (Isak), Julian Finney/Getty Images (Gabriel)The Real Madrid legend Alfredo Di Stéfano used to say: “A game without a goal is like a day without sunshine.” There was no sun spotted on English shores as Storm Boelo washed across the nation, coating every match in a wall of rain powered by an unrelenting wind. But, fortunately for those of a Di Stéfano persuasion, there was only one 0–0 draw.
Some managed to tiptoe between the raindrops while others were caught in the deluge on a Premier League weekend which could have lasting ramifications.

The illusions of a pre-appeal title race took a twist on Saturday before Manchester United sunk to a new nadir 24 hours later. Liverpool’s signings actually started clicking and Tottenham Hotspur even managed to win a game at Stamford Bridge.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

It didn’t go Mason Mount’s way. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesWhile Michael Carrick’s precarious future could understandably distract from the machinations on the pitch, it should not be overlooked how dreadful Manchester United were, once again.Any whisper of threat which the hosts were able to muster came long after the result had been decided, with United—shorn of their divisive creative lynchpin Bruno Fernandes—resolutely devoid of any attacking spark. Bournemouth, by contrast, could afford to miss half of the Opta-defined “big chances” they created and still romp to a comfortable 3–0 win.

Xabi Alonso oversaw Chelsea’s first home defeat to Tottenham since 2018. / Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty ImagesThis was not a high spec contest of quality action. At times, it was reminiscent of two bald men fighting over a comb. Neither team had much use for the ball, which scarcely looked like finding the back of the net until Chelsea’s stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders handed Tottenham the lead. Cole Palmer capped off a night of infamy with two entirely needless yellow cards.A steely eyed Xabi Alonso made it abundantly clear what he thought of the performance by repeating the insistence that Chelsea “can do better” three times in a matter of seconds.

Coventry are desperately short of goals. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesFulham hardly tore Coventry apart but Frank Lampard’s hosts were typically toothless once again. The Premier League’s lowest scorers scarcely looked like adding to their meager tally with just two shots on target. The most trouble Coventry caused Fulham’s Bernd Leno was when Ephron Mason-Clark inadvertently kicked the goalkeeper in the groin.

Promising results and performances are hard to come by for Crystal Palace. / Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesCrystal Palace had denied Newcastle a single shot on target across the opening 45 minutes. Yet, they were trailing within 120 seconds of the restart.Pierre Sage’s team talk had a disastrous effect and the second half crumpling inspired boos from a restless Selhurst Park. Whether the beaten French boss will be around to deliver another address to his players is very much up in the air.

Thierno Barry had a thankless task at the Emirates. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesThe only people who took more of a battering at the Emirates on Saturday than Everton’s players were the luckless Arsenal fans exposed to the torrential downpour in the front row.The Toffees scarcely had a sniff, with their efforts punctured by an early concession. After tumbling 1–0 down, Everton bizarrely opted to press Arsenal—perhaps Bruno Fernandes had been on the phone—which only played into the hands of their hosts.
The bench getting around Enciso. 🙌 pic.twitter.com/kljs1LHQ8U

Ipswich spent the bulk of the contest shunted firmly onto the back foot. Nottingham Forest leaped upon the hosts’ sloppy buildup play in the first half and calmly dealt with the direct game Ipswich reverted to in the second 45 minutes. Neither approach worked yet the Tractor Boys still emerged with an even share of the spoils. As Forest’s Oliver Glasner shrugged: “It is football.”

Brentford had a battle on their hands on Sunday. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesFor a Brentford side whose only defeat of the season came against Liverpool after being reduced to 10 men, Sunday’s stalemate away to newly promoted opposition inspired an understandably frustrating reaction.“We have to be better,” manager Keith Andrews and wingback Michael Kayode both stressed, with some justification.

The wind caused havoc at the Stadium of Light. / Ian MacNicol/Getty ImagesThe conditions got the better of both teams at the Stadium of Light. The storm sweeping across the U.K. undoubtedly played a major factor in the technical flaws on display, with each side combining to complete just 73% of their passes (the Premier League average is above 82%). As Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford so eloquently put it: “The wind was obviously extremely windy.”

It was all a bit messy in Sunderland. / ANDY BUCHANAN/AFP/Getty ImagesSunderland’s Premier League winless streak may have extended to six games on Sunday, but Régis Le Bris was enthused by the performance behind a goalless draw. As he pointed out after watching a contest defined by more grit than grace, “We were Sunderland today.”
Another away game, another goal ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/DT39808mi2

Enzo Maresca had been able to rely upon two certainties during his record-breaking start to the Premier League season: Erling Haaland’s goals and Gianluigi Donnarumma’s saves. His striker continued to deliver but the Italian goalkeeper let Nicolas Jackson’s daisy-cutter scuttle under his huge frame.City were caught cold by Villa’s tactical setup and deservedly trailed 1–0 after six minutes. The visitors grew into the contest, taking advantage of that questionably funded wealth of playing talent, but the ball would not fall their way for once. “It was a good game, good performance,” Maresca insisted, “but unfortunately we lost.”
Continuing our unbeaten streak at the MKM 🔥 pic.twitter.com/tIx6TR0U6z

In a bitty game which will test the creativity of highlights package editors everywhere, Hull gave as good as they got. Both sides amassed 1.8 xG and two big chances, with one spurned apiece. The Tigers boss Sergej Jakirović was not alone in hailing a draw as “a fair result.”

Fabian Hürzeler was not impressed. / Jan Kruger/Getty ImagesFabian Hürzeler drilled to the heart of Sunday’s clash at Anfield. “The difference was just that they scored and we didn’t.” Brighton went close to breaking the deadlock through Yasin Ayari before Pascal Groß inadvertently picked out the back of his own net while trying to block Florian Wirtz’s shot. Alexander Isak’s second two minutes later whisked the contest away from Brighton, who would still out-shoot and out-run their illustrious hosts on a day of frustration.“It was a missed opportunity for us,” Hürzeler huffed.
Goodnight, Fulham fam. 🤍 pic.twitter.com/foItoNI8tf

ftbpro_01m5q88p5ncv.title: Why Joao Pedro Is Not Playing for Chelsea vs. Tottenham
ftbpro_01m5q88p5ncv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott11:45 AM EDTJoão Pedro is missing for Chelsea. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesChelsea head into Saturday’s London derby without leading scorer João Pedro in their matchday squad.

Losing Pedro, who has five goals and three assists to his name, comes as an enormous blow for the Blues. Rather than replace him with the natural alternative, Danny Welbeck, manager Xabi Alonso has got creative.
It is winger Morgan Rogers who starts up top for Chelsea against their fierce rival, opening the space for young Geovany Quenda to make his first Premier League start on the left wing.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Pedro is back on the sidelines. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesChelsea are yet to provide an explanation for Pedro’s omission from the squad, but Kieran Gill revealed the striker has picked up an injury which will require further scans.

A knee problem saw Pedro miss the 3–0 defeat to Brentford before the international break, and it also kept him out of the Brazil squad during the September-October window, but he did make his return immediately after.

Pedro netted twice against Bournemouth but went goalless last time out against Everton, playing 92 minutes before being replaced by Welbeck for the final stages. There was no obvious sign of injury and Alonso did not mention anything during his prematch press conference.

Malo Gusto returns to the squad after illness, but there is no place for the injured Pep Chavarría or Emiliano Martínez, who has undergone surgery on a broken jaw suffered last time out. Mike Penders replaces the Argentine in the lineup.

Summer signing Emmanuel Emegha also remains out of contention. The former Strasbourg man picked up an injury during preseason but is thought to be closing in on a long-awaited debut, which would have been welcome against Spurs because of Pedro’s surprise absence.
Starting XI: Penders; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Hato; Palmer, Quenda, Rogers.
Subs: Sharman-Lowe, Fofana, Gusto, Palestra, Barco, Lavia, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estêvão, Welbeck.

ftbpro_01m5q97wc7sk.title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Tottenham: Palmer Sent Off in Disastrous Derby
ftbpro_01m5q97wc7sk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:47 PM EDTCole Palmer cost his team. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesChelsea suffered only their second home league defeat to Tottenham Hotspur in the last 36 years on Saturday after being comfortably beaten 2–0 by their London rivals.

The Blues were searching for their third successive victory since the international break, but the surprise absence of João Pedro completely disrupted their flow. Despite the goalless scoreline in the first half,  Spurs, rather surprisingly, were the superior side at a rain-soaked Stamford Bridge, with Xabi Alonso’s team lacking their usual attacking spark.

It was the same story after the restart for Chelsea as they huffed and puffed with no reward, relying on Tottenham’s profligacy and a possible moment of inspiration. Things would soon get much, much worse, however.

A comical own goal from Mike Penders on his first Premier League start gifted Tottenham a deserved lead, before Cole Palmer was sent off for two quick-fire yellow cards. The first came when he could have been shown a straight red for petulantly barging Mateus Fernandes off the ball, while the second was awarded for an idiotic challenge on Conor Gallagher.

Any faint hopes of a dramatic equalizer were dashed three minutes from time as Mathys Tel’s terrific solo strike ended the contest and condemned Chelsea to their third Premier League loss this season.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Morgan Rogers (center) struggled in a new role. / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesPrior to Saturday’s derby, Chelsea had played just one match without Pedro spearheading their fearsome forward triumvirate in the Premier League this season. That outing ended in a 3–0 defeat to Brentford—the only game in which the Blues hadn’t scored during their first nine under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s eight goal involvements have been crucial for Chelsea, but the Brazilian’s significance stretches far beyond his output. He offers Alonso a necessary focal point at the top of his fluid 3-4-2-1 system, one which links seamlessly with Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

Without Pedro, as was the case at the Gtech Community Stadium, Chelsea found themselves short of ideas. Instead of using Danny Welbeck as an orthodox center forward, Alonso gambled on Rogers at No. 9, supported closely by Palmer and 19-year-old Geovany Quenda. Their lack of cohesion proved a stumbling block during a tepid first half, which yielded just four shots and 0.25 expected goals.

Alonso resisted the temptation to alter his misfiring forward unit for much of the second half, even when the same issues played out time and time again. Eventually, the Chelsea boss cracked, introducing Estêvão in the 72nd minute, but their struggles persisted without a traditional No. 9.
Welbeck arrived in the closing stages, but the damage had already been done. With Chelsea trailing and down to 10 men, there was nothing the veteran could do to spare their blushes.
There are plenty of questions for Alonso to answer after a disastrous display and result. One of those is how to organize his attack without Pedro, whose return date remains unknown.
Quenda was a surprise starter for Chelsea. / Ryan Pierse/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Mike Penders—5.8: Entirely to blame for Tottenham’s opener as he punched a routine cross into his own goal. A disastrous moment for the 21-year-old.
CB: Josh Acheampong—5.9: Given a tough ride by Tel and the overlapping Andy Robertson, with the former beating him as he raced through on goal to double Tottenham’s lead.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—6.7: Lacroix racked up an impressive number of defensive contributions, but Chelsea’s defense was pretty dire for the most part. Spurs played through them remarkably easily.
CB: Levi Colwill—6.5: Solid enough in his individual duels, but was unable to hold an underperforming rearguard together.
RWB: Pedro Neto—6.8: Often Chelsea’s brightest spark in the final third, although that’s hardly saying much.
CM: Moisés Caciedo—6.6: Thundered into challenges with typical ferocity, aided by the sodden turf. On the ball, however, Caicedo was far less impactful.
CM: Jordan Henderson—6.4: The 36-year-old was unable to match the impact he made during the 5–1 win over Bournemouth in his most recent home appearance. An unspectacular showing.

ftbpro_01m5q9mq26xk.title: ‘Needs to Stop’—Cavan Sullivan Sent Stern Warning After Receiving MLS Fine
ftbpro_01m5q9mq26xk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott1:00 PM EDTCavan Sullivan was handed a fine by MLS. / Isaiah Vazquez/MLS/Getty ImagesMajor League Soccer issued a fine to Philadelphia Union winger Cavan Sullivan for his dive in the late stages of his side’s 2–2 draw with Charlotte FC.

In the 84th minute of the game, Sullivan fell to the ground following a challenge from Charlotte defender Morrison, who immediately suggested there had been no contact. Veteran midfielder Ashley Westwood confronted the teenager about the incident on the pitch soon after.

After reviewing the incident, MLS said in a statement: “The MLS Disciplinary Committee has fined Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan for violating the league’s policy regarding simulation/embellishment in the 84th minute of Philadelphia’s match against Charlotte FC on Oct. 17.”
The exact details of the fine handed out to Sullivan have not been revealed.

It capped off a frustrating outing for Sullivan, who had a goal chalked off for offside earlier in the second half. It led to the blunt end of a streak of 10 games with at least one goal contribution as he marked his first MLS match without either a goal or an assist since Aug. 1.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
A tough outing for Sullivan. / Isaiah Vazquez/MLS/Getty ImagesSullivan may be the glamor name in MLS these days, but Charlotte captain Westwood knows all about life at the highest level of soccer.
The 36-year-old Englishman made 286 Premier League appearances across 10 seasons with Aston Villa and Burnley before his arrival at Charlotte in 2023.
Westwood admitted after the game that Sullivan has all the tools to make his own lengthy career in Europe, but he had one simple warning for the teenager: cut out the diving.
“I’ve only seen him today, really,” Westwood said. “He’s a talented player.
“I don’t like his diving. He needs to stop that. I said that to him. If he wants to go to the next level, he needs to stop that.
“He’s a top player. For someone his age, he’s got a very, very good future in the game. Like I said, he’s not scared to say things. He tries things. He runs around. He’s got all the attributes.”

This was not the first disciplinary issue Sullivan has faced this season. He was sent off in the 13th minute of injury time against Inter Miami in August after involving himself in a heated scuffle to defend brother Quinn.
However, the one-game suspension that should have followed was rescinded upon appeal by the Union.

ftbpro_01m5qb6h00rj.title: Supercomputer Predicts Premier League Table As Man City Suffer First Loss
ftbpro_01m5qb6h00rj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer5:30 PM EDTMan City have tasted Premier League defeat. /  Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAston Villa finally did it. Not only is Unai Emery’s team the first in the Premier League to beat Manchester City this season, they are the first to even take points from them.
Enzo Maresca’s City had been perfect through seven rounds of matches, even with the guilty verdict hanging over the club since the September-October international break.

Yet a sloppy performance at Villa Park, with Gianluigi Donnarumma and Marc Guéhi particularly poor, was punished by on-loan striker Nicolas Jackson. Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki also thwarted City with six saves over the 90 minutes.

City remain top of the current Premier League standings, but it was the first sign of any domestic weakness this season. Taking to the pitch shortly afterwards, Arsenal drew level on points with their greatest rival at the top of the table, held in second place only on goal difference.

The Gunners emerged victorious over Everton in what threatened to be difficult circumstances without star winger Bukayo Saka—sidelined potentially until Christmas. Arsenal lacked natural creativity, but it mattered little because last season’s set-piece prowess returned with a bang.
After those results and two others in the Premier League on Saturday, Opta’s supercomputer has updated its predictions once more.
Arsenal have a strong chance of going back-to-back. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesPredicted Position / Club

Arsenal’s statistical chance of winning the Premier League—thereby retaining an English championship for the first time since 1935—stands at more than 50%. Manchester City, on the other hand, are falling away, given less than a 35% chance now.

One thing is clear, the champion is one of these two. Brighton & Hove Albion are hanging in there as the only team with a greater than 5% chance. Liverpool little over 3% chance of a second title in three seasons, while Chelsea’s humbling defeat to Tottenham Hotspur has done their chance more harm.
Man Utd are given a smaller chance than Leeds at present. / Michael Steele/Getty ImagesPredicted Position / Club

In the hunt for the Champions League, it would take a colossal collapse for Arsenal and Manchester City to miss out, both rated with chances in excess of 90%. Top four is a guaranteed spot in the competition, but the Premier League is likely to again command a fifth due to the ongoing strong performance of English clubs in UEFA tournaments.

At present, Brighton have odds in their favour better than 50/50 of making into the Champions League for the first time ever. Liverpool are not far behind, with Chelsea also rated at more than a 30% chance of qualifying. Aston Villa have around a 21% chance, after which the likelihood drops quite sharply for Brentford, Leeds United and Everton.
Manchester United’s chance of being among Europe’s elite next season is falling on account of a five-match winless run in the Premier League. As of now, it is under 6%.
Tottenham have suddenly won back-to-back games. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPredicted Position / Club

Two wins in a row has suddenly made a massive difference for Tottenham Hotspur, whose chance of an unthinkable relegation is shrinking to 14%. Their predicted finish is now 13th place, which is still not very good, but worlds away from consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons.

There are six teams in much more danger, each with a greater than 25% chance of dropping out of the division into the EFL Championship. Ipswich Town and Hull City should survive immediate relegation but will be looking nervously behind them the whole way. Things can easily change.
Crystal Palace (28%) and Nottingham Forest (29%) are not in a good place. Fulham are almost at 31% chance of relegation, with Sunderland and Coventry City in excess of 40%.

ftbpro_01m5qef7ne61.title: ‘We Have to Look at That’—Phil Parkinson Concerned by Wrexham’s Attacking Woes
ftbpro_01m5qef7ne61.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay5:00 PM EDTWrexham have won just three of their last 15 competitive matches across all competitions. / Nigel French/PA Images/Getty ImagesPhil Parkinson admits he will need to examine why Wrexham failed to take their chances in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat to Blackburn Rovers.

The Red Dragons suffered their fourth league defeat of the season, leaving them 17th in the Championship with 14 points from their opening 12 matches. Wrexham had 50% possession at Ewood Park and recorded seven more shots than their opponents, but managed just one on target from 23 attempts.

Wrexham chose not to sign a striker during the summer transfer window, meaning both senior strikers started against Blackburn and leaving Parkinson with limited options to change the game from the bench as his team searched for a goal. Despite their volume of attempts, Wrexham created only a couple of genuinely dangerous chances and rarely troubled the Blackburn backline.

Wrexham were second best in rainy Lancashire. / Nigel French/PA Images/Getty Images“I still felt at halftime the game was there for us, but we couldn’t produce the quality we needed,” Parkinson told Sports Illustrated. “We’ve had 23 attempts, but to only have one of those on target, we have to look at that.

“I’ve got to give Blackburn defenders credit because they made nine or 10 blocks, defended crosses and defended set plays. It was a combination of good defending, but we couldn’t find that clinical moment to get us back in the game. The game was separated by two moments. When we analyze the positions we got into, we got into enough good positions today to have gotten something from the game, but we didn’t produce the quality.”

The defeat leaves Wrexham with just three wins in their last 15 matches, dating back to the end of last season, when they finished one point outside the playoffs. Only once in the last seven Championship seasons has a team that finished seventh gone on to finish higher than 17th the following campaign. That is where Wrexham currently stand after their latest loss.

Although there were positives in the number of chances Wrexham created at Ewood Park, they ultimately fell short again because of a lack of quality in attack. Andri Guðjohnsen, son of former Barcelona and Chelsea striker Eiður Guðjohnsen, scored both goals for Blackburn. He now has nine goals this season, three more than Kieffer Moore and Sam Smith have managed combined.

Parkinson added: “We just couldn’t find a kind of moment. The frustrating thing from our point of view is we haven’t tested the keeper enough in the game. When we look at the stats, because the stats don’t lie, 23 shots, one on target. There won’t be many teams this weekend that have had that many attempts and not either got a goal or tested the keeper out more. We’ve got to look at that.

“We’ve got to look at the crosses which came in; we’ve got to look at the movement of the front players. Were they that good defensively, or could we have done more? We need to analyze that, which we will.”

Another key factor is Wrexham’s absence of attacking talisman Josh Windass, who almost single-handedly helped drive the team towards the Championship playoffs last season. Windass finished the campaign with seven goals in his final eight appearances but missed the entire preseason schedule before suffering an ankle injury in the recent away draw with Derby County.

Any club would miss a player of his quality. However, Wrexham spent $48 million during the summer transfer window, knowing about Windass’s injury issues, and perhaps should have been better prepared to cope without him this season.

Parkinson said: “Josh is that player, like Guðjohnsen. The moments come and he takes them. That’s what he did for us time and time again. The division is so tight. You don’t watch games and think one team is so much better than the other on the day. You watch games and think it comes down to a moment of quality. Any team would miss their top scorer, but while we wait for him to come back, others have to step up to the plate.”

ftbpro_01m5qk8wcqcr.title: Senne Lammens Has a Theory Why Man Utd Lack ‘Fight’ This Season
ftbpro_01m5qk8wcqcr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer4:30 PM EDTMan Utd are seven games into a winless streak. / Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty ImagesSenne Lammens has admitted that Manchester United fans cannot see the desire behind the scenes from players to “do better,” insisting the locker room is also united behind Michael Carrick.

Lisandro Martínez spoke out against sporting director Jason Wilcox and what he claimed was a lack of support from above, before climbing down a few days later. Bruno Fernandes then openly questioned the tactical approach in the humbling Como loss.

United now head into Sunday’s encounter with Bournemouth at Old Trafford hoping to break a streak of winless games that is currently seven long. Carrick gave an unusual press conference on Friday, in which he spoke for almost six minutes before the first question was asked. The manager drew significant praise for the raw, honest assessment of the situation and what needs to happen.

Lammens admitted it is “easy” for players to speak out in frustration after a disappointing result. “We all really want to do better and we all want to win and then we might say sometimes things we don’t really mean or fully explain what we mean,” he told Sky Sports.

That postgame passion hasn’t necessarily been visible in on-field performances. “People at home can’t see that, so we need to try to look like that on the pitch, but I can assure you we’re doing everything we can and we’re all together behind the coach, as a staff, players, front office.
"Everyone knows they have to do better, but I think we are united, trying to get better as a team.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Michael Carrick has tried to adapt to stay ahead of opponents. / Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty ImagesDuring Carrick’s interim management, United led the Premier League. The team collected more points from those 17 games than every other team, including champions Arsenal. The squad is almost entirely the same, which makes it all the more surprising to see poor results now.
Lammens suggested that United actually played worse at times last season when results were better.
“Last season I felt like maybe we played sometimes better this season, but last season everything just clicked and went the right way for us,” he said.
Although extra fight is always helpful, an explanation for that appears to be a switch in style, from a counter-attacking approach to one focused more on buildup in possession.

Although admitting struggles against the press, the Belgian offered: “We didn’t concede that many goals, and then I think as a counter team a bit more last season we did really well. [But] everybody knew we had to improve, that teams were going to change the way they played against us.

“That’s why we had to evolve this season and in preseason, we tried to do some different things to get us in the best position to win games.” But Lammens still believes “fighting as a team and defending as a team” is something the group must “get back to.”

Does having more of the ball make it harder out of possession? /  Mairo Cinquetti/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesIs it something as basic as playing more with the ball means not having to fight as much to get it back? United were used to not having possession last season.

“With the ball we try to do a bit of different things, try to improve, because last season we weren’t always the best with the ball,” Lammens added. “I think we have improved in those sort of things, but maybe the mindset of having the ball and trying to play around has that mindset of when you don’t have the ball and try to fight for it the way we did last season.”

Balance is clearly important. “We need to get a bit of both. It is a fine line, to be honest, that aggressiveness. When you don’t have the ball and when you have the ball, you want that calmness, that being able to play from the back and being able to play through the press.
“I think it’s just finding that fine line in ourselves.”

ftbpro_01m5sawjp252.title: Real Madrid Gripped by Illness Uncertainty Just Hours Before El Clasico
ftbpro_01m5sawjp252.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:30 AM EDTJosé Mourinho has some selection headaches to manage. / Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty ImagesReal Madrid announced on the morning of Sunday’s Clásico against Barcelona that the club’s first-choice goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was a “last-minute withdrawal” from the roster after a bout of flu. Yet that was swiftly followed by multiple reports claiming that the Belgian had not yet given up hope of featuring.

Amid the constant flux of chaos which swirls around the Spanish capital, Courtois has been one point of reliable consistency. The towering Belgian routinely bails out the porous defense sat in front of him, making the spectacular appear serene after meeting those standards so often. In a position where mistakes are punished unlike any other, Courtois hasn’t made a single error leading to a La Liga goal in any of the past three seasons.

It’s no understatement to say that Courtois’s unexpected absence for Sunday’s trip to Camp Nou would serve as an almighty blow for José Mourinho’s side. If Vinícius Júnior’s suspension can be overcome by turning to the club’s record signing, Yan Diomande, the club’s goalkeeper reserves aren’t nearly as deep.
Madrid announced that the teenage Illia Voloshyn has been called into the squad to replace Courtois, but it will be the youngster’s Ukrainian compatriot who fills those large gloves.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Thibaut Courtois’s involvement is mired in uncertainty. / Angel Martinez/UEFA/Getty ImagesReal Madrid’s official statement appeared definitive, ruling Courtois out while announcing that the teenage Ukrainian Illia Voloshyn had been called up instead. However, multiple reports surfaced in the hours following claiming that nothing had yet been decided.

Courtois is thought to have been suffering from a virus which left him “completely wiped out,” according to MARCA. The same Madrid-based outlet would later report that the 34-year-old’s health would continue to be monitored on Sunday and, should he experience an improvement, he would fly to Barcelona.

It won’t be until a couple of hours before Sunday’s kickoff (4 p.m. ET / 1 p.m. PT) that Mourinho’s starting XI is unveiled. Yet, The Athletic go so far as to say that Courtois is “hopeful” of playing a role in El Clásico.
Even if his No. 1 doesn’t make a miraculous recovery, Mourinho doesn’t have the worst understudy to turn to.

Andriy Lunin will get his first minutes of the season. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesUnless Mourinho stuns everyone by handing Sergio Mestre his senior debut for the club in El Clásico, the biggest fixture of the year, the experienced figure of Andriy Lunin will get another run out.

The dutifully downcast Ukraine international has served as Courtois’s understudy for the last six years. In that time, thanks largely to his teammate’s various ailments and absences, Lunin has racked up a respectable 74 appearances for Real Madrid while winning a pair of Champions League and La Liga titles.

Lunin’s most prolific spell came during the 2023–24 campaign when Courtois tore his cruciate ligament on the eve of the season. Madrid initially drafted in Kepa Arrizabalaga as an emergency loanee from Chelsea but Lunin would soon win the trust of Carlo Ancelotti, eventually relegating the most expensive goalkeeper of all time to the bench.

The 6'3" custodian is not a showy shot-stopper or one of those modern keepers who thrives with the ball at their feet. Much like his perennially emotionless outward image, Lunin focuses on the basics and dispenses with flourishes. Even when he delivered two penalty saves in a shootout victory over Manchester City in the 2024 Champions League quarterfinals, the unlikely hero scarcely cracked a smile when he was mobbed by his teammates.

Sunday’s Clásico will be Lunin’s first appearance of the season but he amassed a dozen outings last term—mustering just one clean sheet in the process. The 27-year-old didn’t get on the pitch when Madrid clashed with Barcelona last October yet he still conspired to earn himself a red card after leaving the bench and approaching Barça’s substitutes “in an aggressive manner.”

ftbpro_01m5sdcqpwj6.title: Lammens Reveals Man Utd Dressing Room’s Stance on Carrick After Fernandes Rant
ftbpro_01m5sdcqpwj6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:30 AM EDTMichael Carrick’s days at Manchester United would appear to be numbered. / Marco Luzzani/Getty ImagesManchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens claimed that, despite being “very frustrated” with the club’s woeful run of form, the locker room remains “all together behind” Michael Carrick.

One week after the club’s upper hierarchy was torn apart by Lisandro Martínez, club captain Bruno Fernandes turned his ire toward the managerial staff. United’s outspoken skipper furiously dismantled Carrick’s tactics in Wednesday’s desperate 4–1 Champions League defeat to Como, criticizing the game plan of not pressing their hosts.

United have thus far resisted the urge to sack Carrick, who has overseen just two victories from 11 matches this season and is currently in the midst of a seven-game winless streak. Any coaches to tentatively consider taking over United have been reportedly put off by a locker room full of players who are viewed as “out of control.”
Lammens was keen to paint a different picture.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“I think it’s easy to see maybe after a game when players are very frustrated—and I get it, I’m very frustrated as well because we all really want to do better and we all want to win—and then we might say sometimes things we don’t really mean or fully explain what we mean,” the goalkeeper told Sky Sports this week.

“Of course, the people at home can’t see that, so we need to also try to look like that when we are on the pitch in the weekend, but I can assure you that we’re doing everything we can and we’re all together behind the coach, as a staff, players, front office.
“Everyone knows, of course, they have to do better, but I think we are united and we are trying to get better as a team and together.”

Michael Carrick (center) is under an enormous amount of pressure. / Michael Steele/Getty ImagesDespite notable outbursts from Martínez and Fernandes in recent weeks, as well as the distinctly less punchy performances on the pitch from the rest of his roster, Carrick continues to have “100%” trust in his players.

“I definitely trust them, yeah, 100% I trust them,” Carrick told assembled media before Sunday’s seismic meeting with Bournemouth. “It wasn’t a very good night at all [in Como] for so many reasons. We all know that. I think that’s pretty obvious. I definitely trust them.”

Carrick rejected the claim that Manchester United are “unmanageable” and struck a confident tone when looking ahead to this weekend’s Premier League return. “We’ll be a different team on Sunday,” he promised, “we have to be a different team on Sunday.”

Manchester United can scarcely afford another loss. / Mairo Cinquetti/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesUnited boasted the best record across the final 17 Premier League games of last season after Carrick took charge, yet have only been able to beat newly promoted Ipswich Town in the top flight this term. The dramatic change in results is not one which Lammens has seen in the team’s performances.
“Last season I felt like, playing-wise, maybe we played sometimes better this season, but last season everything just clicked and went the right way for us,” the goalkeeper argued.

The issue for United, as it has been for so many of Carrick’s predecessors, is a stalled evolution. “As a counter team a bit more last season we did really well, but you also know—I think everybody knew—that we had to improve as well from that, that teams were going to change the way they played against us,” Lammens outlined.

That progression has tried to take the form of pressing high up the pitch. Yet, be it a failure of coaching, application, endeavor or all three and more combined, United simply haven’t been able to consistently disrupt their opponents at the sharp end of the pitch. If anything, this attempt to win the ball high has left United exposed at the back, with far too much room between the lines of attack, midfield and defense.

Given how good Como are at playing through co-ordinated pressing units, Carrick’s reluctance to send his side blindly haring after the ball is understandable. Quite why United still couldn’t form a compact shape even without the demands of pressing is less clear.

Heading into Sunday’s clash with Bournemouth, Carrick was keen to shift the focus away from this tactical talking point. “We’ve won a lot of games over a period of time and this pressing thing—that suddenly everyone thinks about pressing: pressing is one small part of football,” the manager scoffed.

“There’s all sorts of different ways of what people class as a press. What actually is it? What are you doing it for? Is it to your strength? Is it covering up other spaces? It’s just thrown about as a bit of a word at the minute. You don’t necessarily need to press to win games of football. Sometimes you do, sometimes you don’t.”

ftbpro_01m5sj0esg09.title: ‘Pure Football’—Carrick Benches Fernandes With Scathing Revelation
ftbpro_01m5sj0esg09.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom9:37 AM EDTBruno Fernandes was a notable absentee on Sunday. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesAfter suffering from the sharpened tongue of Bruno Fernandes in midweek, Michael Carrick fired a subtle barb of his own toward Manchester United’s club captain.

When quizzed on why the Portuguese playmaker had been dropped for Sunday’s Premier League clash with Bournemouth, Carrick dismissed any suggestion that this was a result of Fernandes’s outspoken criticism of his tactics. Instead, he claimed this was a “pure football” decision.

That Fernandes was even part of the matchday roster at all was something of a surprise after he publicly lambasted Carrick’s instructions for Wednesday’s Champions League humbling at the hands of Como.

“It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind,” the midfielder scoffed. “I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure and trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Carrick dismissed Fernandes’s complaints when they were put to him on the shores of Lake Como and refused to rule out stripping him of the captaincy. “I’ll always do what’s best for the football club,” he warned.
Yet, for all his explosive talk, Fernandes has endured enough struggles on the pitch to vindicate his position out of the starting XI.

It’s not quite clicking for Bruno Fernandes. / PIERO CRUCIATTI/AFP/Getty ImagesIt’s been an almighty come-down for the reigning Premier League Player of the Season. After putting together the most creatively prolific campaign in the competition’s history, surpassing the single-season assist record of 20 jointly held by the illustrious pairing of Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, Fernandes has created just one goal for his teammates this term.

This is not simply a case of unfortunate finishing. Fernandes has gone from creating four chances per game to 2.3. His expected assists (xA) figures have followed a similar decline while the quality of the diminished opportunities he has been able to muster has also taken a steep dive.

During the 2025–26 Premier League campaign, Fernandes created one Opta-defined ‘big chance’ every 93 minutes he was on the pitch. The 32-year-old has created just one ‘big chance’ across the first 10 and a half hours of top-flight soccer he’s amassed this term.

Fernandes hasn’t been entirely prolific either, scoring in just two Manchester United matches this season; rattling in a hat trick against newly promoted Ipswich Town before nabbing the second in a 4–0 rout of Azerbaijan side Sabah FK.

Yet, the most damning aspect of the playmaker’s recent performances have come off the ball. Fernandes made it clear that United were told to not press Como, but the captain still charged around on his own upfront, tiring himself out while offering no real threat of winning the ball at any point. “We actually half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that,” Carrick pointed out.
As Ralf Rangnick, one of Carrick’s predecessors in the Old Trafford dugout, pointed out, you cannot press half-heartedly: “A little bit of pressing is like a little bit of pregnant.”

ftbpro_01m5sn741h93.title: Why Cole Palmer Will Be Allowed to Face Man Utd After Chelsea Red Card
ftbpro_01m5sn741h93.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:45 AM EDTIt wasn’t all bad for Cole Palmer on Saturday. / Steve Bardens/AMA/Getty ImagesThanks to the quirk that red-card suspensions are carried across domestic competitions, Cole Palmer will serve his one-game ban in Chelsea’s midweek Carabao Cup clash with Liverpool, ensuring he won’t miss a single Premier League encounter.

Chelsea are up against Manchester United next Saturday and in need of an emphatic response to this weekend’s dismal defeat at the hands of Tottenham Hotspur. Palmer may have collected the first red card of his senior career, but he wasn’t even Chelsea’s worst performer in a toothless 2–0 defeat to the club’s hated London rivals.

Stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the visitors in front with a disastrous own goal in the 77th minute, shortly before Palmer collected his second, entirely unnecessary, yellow card. Chelsea’s creative lynchpin had already been penalized for running into Mateus Fernandes—an act that could have warranted a red card on another day—which makes his decision to stand on Conor Gallagher’s ankle all the more unwise.
The quirk of the fixture list and the FA handbook has spared Palmer any Premier League absence, but he will sit out Chelsea’s next game: a daunting trip to Anfield.

Xabi Alonso will go up against his childhood friend and former youth team colleague when Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool host the fourth round Carabao Cup tie on Wednesday night. Chelsea have not won a game at Anfield in front of fans since 2018, when Eden Hazard inspired a Blues side managed by Maurizio Sarri to a Carabao Cup third round triumph. Unfortunately for Alonso, he won’t be able to call up Chelsea’s No. 10 this week.

Cole Palmer is usually one of Chelsea’s coolest customers. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesPalmer took to social media the morning after the night before to search for some forgiveness from Chelsea fans entirely unfamiliar with the sensation of losing to Spurs. “Not good enough by me,” he wrote on Instagram. “Live n learn. Apologies. On to the next.”

Alonso, who became the first Chelsea manager since Antonio Conte to lose a home game to Tottenham, refrained from piling on his playmaker. “I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure,” the manager offered up immediately after the match.
“I think that Cole, when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying, and today after the 1–0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

This was Chelsea’s 11th red card across all competitions since the start of last season, not including one shown to former manager Enzo Maresca. Alonso had already identified ill discipline as an area in need of improvement before the red mist melted Palmer’s cold exterior.

“I think that if you are focused on what you have to do, you are prepared for what’s going on,” Alonso had warned. “Normally you don’t make that many mistakes and you don’t overreact to certain situations. For me, this is a fundamental part of the game: to have that emotional control, to deal with all this. The momentum is coming, [but] we keep calm, I don’t lose my head, and I don’t get stupid yellow cards, make stupid penalties. You need to prepare for football to have better control of that.”

ftbpro_01m5snrfcaxp.title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Brighton: Big-Money Arrivals Deliver Huge Result
ftbpro_01m5snrfcaxp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack12:23 PM EDTLiverpool won their first league game at Anfield this season. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesAndoni Iraola notched his first Premier League win at Anfield as Liverpool boss, with his team overcoming the red-hot Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday afternoon.

The Reds were forced to recover from a disastrous start in the Champions League on Tuesday, fighting back from 2–0 down against Villarreal to win 4–3. There was no need for such a drastic recovery on this occasion, as Liverpool raced into a 2–0 first-half lead.

While there was an element of fortune with the opening goal, with Bart Verbruggen flummoxed by a Pascal Groß deflection from Florian Wirtz’s errant shot, Bradley Barcola’s hustle, speed and precision facilitated Liverpool’s second, with Alexander Isak converting from a couple of yards away.

Yasin Ayari had spurned a glorious chance beforehand, and Brighton unsurprisingly remained a threat throughout the contest. However, this just wasn’t the Seagulls‘ day in the final third, and as Fabian Hürzeler pushed to get his side back into the game, they risked more concessions on the counterattack in the second half.

Liverpool, too, were wasteful with their attacking moments as the game wore on, ensuring tension permeated across Anfield up until the final whistle, but Iraola will nonetheless be encouraged by his side‘s showing without the ball, as the hosts kept a clean sheet in a victory that, despite the scoreline, didn’t exactly feel routine.

Wirtz helped Liverpool open the scoring. / Paul Currie/AFP/Getty ImagesThis was the day when all Liverpool’s $100 million arrivals delivered.
Wirtz’s shot led to Groß’s own goal before Barcola expertly teed up Isak for the Reds’ second. The pair combined again, just as they did for the winner at Brentford last weekend.

Barcola has responded brilliantly to the criticism that came his way after failing to step up for Iraola’s undermanned side against Manchester City after the break. There was always a sense that the summer addition would take a little while to find his groove, having barely had a preseason due to rife transfer speculation. He’s certainly looked the part over the past couple of weeks, and there’s more to come.

Isak’s productive start to the campaign is going under the radar, and his first-time finish, while seemingly simple from close range, depicted a striker who’s brimming with confidence after a tough, injury-hit debut campaign. The Sweden international is now up to seven goals in all competitions this term in less than 800 minutes played.

The critics were all so keen to slander the former Newcastle United sharpshooter amid his woes, but are far less willing to give Isak his flowers for a productive start to year two. The same goes for Wirtz, who scored his first Liverpool goal since April in the week and was contributing again on Sunday.

ftbpro_01m5spea0ekt.title: ‘Let’s See’—Arteta Sends Bizarre Warning to Every Other Premier League Manager
ftbpro_01m5spea0ekt.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell11:15 AM EDTMikel Arteta is keeping tabs on the Premier League’s managers. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesAfter receiving his second yellow card of the season on Saturday, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta revealed he’s “clipping” all the other Premier League managers who also leave their technical area, but go unpunished.

The Spaniard entered the referee’s book in the 64th minute of the Gunners’ 2–0 win over Everton at the Emirates Stadium. Arteta strayed from his allotted area on the touchline to pick up his second caution of the season—the first came for a similar infraction at Sunderland back in September.
The tactician, who is always active and reactionary on the touchline, believes he is being unfairly treated by the referees when compared to his fellow managers in the English top flight.

“I do have to be careful,” Arteta said when asked about his caution in his postgame press conference. “And we need to have good sensors there. There are managers that have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes leave the touchline, no yellows.
“So I’m clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. So if somebody is going to say, ‘I’m not in the record yet, somebody else has the record.’
“Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the manager. I don’t know where we’re going to be. Let’s see.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mikel Arteta (left) already has two yellow cards to his name this season. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesIn isolation, picking up a yellow card as a manager is not a very big deal, so long as there is not another one coming before the final whistle sounds. But collecting multiple cautions across a span of matches comes with consequences.
Three yellow cards for a manager equal an automatic one-game suspension. Six cautions bring a two-match ban, and nine come with the punishment of three matches on the sidelines.

It’s only late October and Arteta already has two to his name. The next time he enters the referee’s book, he will be hit with a one-match ban, leaving Arsenal without their manager on the touchline for whatever the next game on the schedule is.
Even if Arteta pulls a José Mourinho and shows up to a press conference with his “massive storage of images” to plead his case, he will still be forced to watch from the stands.

Arsenal had to play Bayern Munich three days before facing off with Everton. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesArteta had more to complain about in his postgame press conference despite Arsenal’s gritty win over Everton. The 44-year-old hardly celebrated the victory that put his side back level with Manchester City atop the table before going in on the club’s schedule.

“We’re very happy with the victory, the performance and the week, because we were given a terrible schedule,” Arteta said. “Playing Sunday afternoon, then Wednesday night in Munich, coming here really late on Thursday and then having to play again in the Premier League against a really tough opponent on Saturday at 3 p.m.
“We have overcome some injuries, and I’m really proud of the mentality of the team in the conditions today.”

The defending Premier League champions went unbeaten during the run in question, defeating Nottingham Forest last weekend before managing a 2–2 draw with Bayern Munich midweek and then getting past Everton on Saturday.

There is hardly much time to recover, though, because Arsenal have a Carabao Cup clash with Fleetwood Town on Tuesday, Oct. 27. The good news is Arteta can rest many of his typical starters against the League Two side, leaving his biggest stars fresh for a date with Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, Nov. 1.

ftbpro_01m5sq4kt2gr.title: Man Utd Player Ratings vs. Bournemouth: Carrick’s Gamble Backfires Spectacularly
ftbpro_01m5sq4kt2gr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:07 PM EDTMichael Carrick had another afternoon to forget. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesMichael Carrick’s decision to drop his outspoken captain Bruno Fernandes resulted in Manchester United’s most toothless display of the season, as Bournemouth romped to a 3–0 win on Sunday.

Given the damning nature of the playmaker’s comments midweek, Carrick had little choice other than to drop Fernandes, who pointedly called out the tactics in Wednesday’s 4–1 thrashing against Como. United’s under-fire manager explained his skipper’s absence as a “pure football” decision. But even in his current underwhelming run of form, Fernandes remains the club’s best creator.

If that status wasn’t already abundantly apparent, Fernandes’s teammates rammed that point home at Old Trafford, failing to lay a glove on a Bournemouth side which represent everything that Manchester United lack. If Fernandes’s future is uncertain, Carrick’s is even more precarious.

Bruno Fernandes made his first appearance as a Premier League substitute since May 2025.  / Dan Istitene/Getty ImagesFernandes’s only Premier League goal contributions this season came in a 5–2 romp over newly promoted Ipswich Town. That hazy day in August feels an awfully long time ago. It’s been two months and six top-flight appearances of blanks for Fernandes and Manchester United as a collective, who have yet to record another Premier League win in that time.

Carrick left Fernandes to stew on the bench against Bournemouth but there was no response from his teammates. In truth, that is to be expected. For all his struggles, the captain leads his team for chances created and expected assists this season. Without the injured Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Šeško, Carrick’s decision to drop his last remaining source of creativity was always at risk of backfiring.
A series of calamitous, if not out of character, mistakes helped Bournemouth find the openings their cohesive system could very easily have picked out regardless.

As Fernandes has proven throughout this season, his presence would not have necessarily spared United from another humiliation—he was right there, huffing and puffing his way through a three-goal margin of defeat to Como in midweek. If anything, his spot on the bench underscored the futility of Carrick’s grand show of strength which aptly captures his impact on the club at large.
Andrey Santos lined up in midfield. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

ftbpro_01m5sqzje6t8.title: Man Utd Make Carrick Sack Decision As Two ‘Frontrunner’ Replacements Loom
ftbpro_01m5sqzje6t8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom3:31 PM EDTCould this be farewell for Michael Carrick? / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesThere is reportedly an expectation within Manchester United that Michael Carrick will be fired following Sunday’s dismal defeat to Bournemouth, with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann billed as the two leading “frontrunners.”

United’s demise at the hands of Bournemouth had been confirmed more than an hour before the final whistle. By the time the referee finally put the Old Trafford fans, players and Carrick out of their misery, the venom in the boos had faded.

Bournemouth’s traveling support had tired of chanting, “You’re getting sacked in the morning,” instead reveling in an entirely deserved 3–0 win just three days after recording the same scoreline against historic Italian giants AC Milan. United’s fans would instead fill the air with songs in support of Carrick, who may be the fall guy but is hardly the cause of the fault line running through this listing behemoth.
While the players, sporting directors and owners received a tongue-lashing from the crowd, it is the teary-eyed manager who is set to be relieved of his duties, Sky Sports News have reported.

Eddie Howe (left) and Julian Nagelsmann are both thought to be in the running. / Serena Taylor/Newcastle United/Getty Images (Howe), Joe Prior/Visionhaus/Getty Images (Nagelsmann)Conversations were already thought to be in the works surrounding the recruitment of a new Carrick replacement, but those have now been “accelerated.” Former Newcastle United boss Howe and recently departed Germany head coach Nagelsmann would appear to be the two names at the top of the shortlist.

Both are immediately available, but the similarities end there. While Howe offers Premier League experience from his time on Tyneside and at Bournemouth, Nagelsmann has never coached outside Germany. Howe took Newcastle into the Champions League with a fierce high press, while Nagelsmann revolutionized RB Leipzig by dialing down their chaotic work off the ball to focus on a possession game.

The calm outward demeanour of Howe clashes with Nagelsmann’s forthright reputation which earned him no favors at Bayern Munich. Howe wore the same club-shop tracksuit throughout his Newcastle tenure, and Nagelsmann cycled through four T-shirts during one match with Germany at the 2026 World Cup.
That United’s list of candidates can include two such contrasting characters says everything about the chaos gripping a club which can’t be solved by a simple managerial change.

Michael Carrick trotted around the turf at full time. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesAfter the 4–1 thrashing dished out by Como on the lake in midweek, Carrick made a beeline for the sodden Manchester United supporters who had stuck it out until the end, offering two hands of apology. There was a similar tone to Sunday’s interaction with the crowd, as the visibly emotional manager once again patted the fabric covering his broken heart.

It was such an emotive scene that Carrick was asked if he had just embarked upon a farewell lap of Old Trafford. “No, not from me,” he assured Match of the Day. “There wasn’t a tear, just appreciation for the fans and what they’ve showed me.”

“I’ve got the energy for sure—it means so much to me,” Carrick added. “You have games to focus on and gathering the players. The responsibility of doing that I enjoy that—I love it, it’s what I’m here for.”

How much longer Carrick will be here for remains to be seen. The retired midfielder promised to “take responsibility” for a dismal set of results—United’s worst in 40 years—while offering: “I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club.”

It wasn’t a great day for anyone at Manchester United. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesManchester United’s chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox, the subject of Lisandro Martínez recent rant and unflattering chants from the crowd, watched Sunday’s collapse from the stands. There could very well be some tough conversations to come, but Carrick revealed that he hadn’t had any serious exchange during his first interaction with the executives.
“No, [they] just briefly came down like they always do after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary,” Carrick shrugged.

When he was bluntly asked if he expected to get sacked, the beleaguered head coach shot back: “I’m not expecting anything. It’s just digesting today—we knew it was an important day to try and get us moving forward, and we haven’t done that. For me it’s just digesting that, and the emotions at the end of the game is something I’ve not really had before.”

Manchester United’s decision makers are coming under serious fire. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesBy the end of a spiky press conference, Carrick was quizzed on how Manchester United have found themselves at this stage of yet another downward spiral. After all, Bournemouth are unbeaten on their previous four visits to Old Trafford, earning victories against three different managers in the home dugout. As Carrick accepted, this is not just down the manager.

“If I really had the answers, I wouldn’t have let it happen,” he sighed. “If I could do something about it and there was something that I could really control, then I would’ve tried to do everything I can to not be in this position.”

It’s been 13 years since Manchester United were even in a Premier League title race, when all the failings of the club’s majority owners, the Glazer family, were covered up by Sir Alex Ferguson’s genius. Sir Jim Ratcliffe ploughed forward in 2024 to take control of sporting decisions to right this wayward tanker and has overseen even worse results than ever before.
At some point, someone in a position of power above the manager may, inadvertently or otherwise, consider their own role in this ongoing disaster.

ftbpro_01m5srz8ywfv.title: Cavan Sullivan Suffers Injury Setback Two Weeks Out From USMNT Competitive Matches
ftbpro_01m5srz8ywfv.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely1:30 PM EDTCavan Sullivan did not feature in the weekend’s action. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCavan Sullivan was sidelined with an ankle injury on Saturday, and the repercussions for the Philadelphia Union were felt immediately. But what will it mean for the U.S. men’s national team?

The Union saw their dreamy, 15-game unbeaten streak snapped, losing 2–1 to the New England Revolution at Subaru Park in a match that had significant implications on the MLS Cup playoffs and now puts a coveted top-four seed in the Eastern Conference much further out of Philadelphia’s reach. It was the team’s first regular season loss since May 24, a run that was first ignited on July 22 post-World Cup and aligned perfectly with Sullivan’s newfound spot in the starting lineup.

Prior to the World Cup, the 17-year-old winger started just six MLS matches for the Union dating back to February. Since the World Cup—and the appointment of interim manager Ryan Richter—Sullivan had been included in every single regular season starting lineup except one (Sept. 26), due to conflicting international duty with the USMNT.

Sullivan, who is now up to seven goals and 14 assists this season, suffered a knock to his ankle in last week’s draw with Charlotte FC. The fiery teenager fought through the pain, though, seeing out all 90 minutes. His condition had not improved by midweek, causing him to miss Wednesday’s training session. But when he returned to the pitch for practice the following day, it seemed as if he would be ready to battle the Revolution.

“He’s all good,” Richter told reporters Thursday, quelling any concerns. “He took a knock in the game on Saturday against Charlotte, and we’re just trying to manage that through this week. But he should be available for Saturday. So he was out on the field today, but like I said, just managing that through the week and trying to get him so that he’s at his best for this weekend.”

Except injury quickly proved more serious. Sullivan was listed as out in the league’s availability report on Friday night, and he could only watch from the bench as his team struggled unsuccessfully to mount a comeback against the Revolution.

Sullivan is expected to be called up next month. /  Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesThe status and severity of Sullivan’s ankle injury is not yet known, nor is his projected timeline for recovery, sources at the Union tell Sports Illustrated. The Union’s playoff push aside, Sullivan will be needed for the USMNT’s upcoming November camp. That leaves him only two weeks to return to full strength.

The Stars and Stripes are set to convene on Nov. 9, ahead of two-consecutive matches against Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, their first competitive fixtures since the 2026 World Cup. Manager Mauricio Pochettino will be adamant to continue the team’s perfect record after going 4–0 in the September-October international window. He’ll likely lean on the teenage prodigy to do so.

He was a true difference-maker last camp, earning a starting spot in the clashes with Peru and Mexico. At 17 years and five days old, he became the USMNT’s youngest goal-scorer in history, helping the team secure an eventual 3–0 win over El Tri, the first victory over its bitter Concacaf rival of Pochettino’s tenure.

ftbpro_01m5sshk8fg9.title: Yamal’s Hilarious Taunt to Real Madrid Star Will Be Tested in El Clasico
ftbpro_01m5sshk8fg9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath1:00 PM EDTLamine Yamal has a reputation for outspoken comments ahead of Clásicos. / JORGE GUERRERO/AFP/Getty ImagesLamine Yamal has a chance to make good on his promise of eating Marc Cucurella alive when the two face off in El Clásico on Sunday.
Among the many narratives running through the blockbuster clash at Camp Nou is the meeting of Spain international teammates Yamal and Cucurella.
Cucurella is set to make his debut in the famous fixture, having signed for Madrid from Chelsea in a €60 million ($60 million) deal at the start of the summer.

The news of the transfer broke on the eve of the 2026 World Cup when Spain’s stars were preparing for their first group-stage match in North America back in June. During one media session, Yamal was asked by Spanish radio show Tiempo de Juego if there had been any teasing between the soon-to-be enemies in training. He responded: “I told him he’ll start the first [Clásico] game and be a substitute in the second because I’m going to eat him alive.”
Yamal attempted to deliver the line deadpan, but couldn’t help breaking into a laugh.

Lamine Yamal and Marc Cucurella were both part of Spain’s World Cup-winning team. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesYamal vs. Cucurella out on the Camp Nou wing promises to be one of the most intriguing and, potentially, decisive battles this Sunday. Both players are on the 30-man shortlist for Monday’s Ballon d’Or and are among the very best in the world in their positions as right winger and left back.

There is quite possibly no better forward right now than Yamal, who became the first player in Europe’s major leagues to rack up both 10 goals and 10 assists this season with a superb individual effort in the midweek defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.
Cucurella, by contrast, has had a somewhat low-key start to life as a Madrid player, with Los Blancos keeping just two clean sheets so far this season.
The 28-year-old has not registered a goal or assist yet for his new side either, and looks some way off the World Cup-winning complete fullback Luis de la Fuente recently described as “sensational.”

And yet, Cucurella has a history of being a major irritant to the game’s best attackers in the big games. In last season’s Champions League encounter between Chelsea and Barcelona, for example, Cucurella put in a Player of the Match display up against his compatriot, which prompted Blues keeper Robert Sánchez to joke that his teammate “had Lamine Yamal in his pocket.”

Marc Cucurella made just one appearance as a Barcelona player. / Jose Breton/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesCucurella is poised to make his Clásico debut for Real Madrid, 10 years on from his one and only first-team appearance for Barcelona.

The left back was born and raised in Catalonia and joined Barça’s La Masia academy aged 14. Though a regular for the B team, Cucurella’s sole outing for the senior side came off the bench in the dying moments of a Copa del Rey win over Real Murcia.
Since then, he has represented Eibar, Getafe, Brighton & Hove Albion and Chelsea, before his big-money move to Spain’s other super-club this summer.
In the heat of El Clásico, the returning academy star is unlikely to be given a hero’s hero’s welcome.
