ftbpro_01m5sxkvew9f.title: Lionel Messi’s Hectic Travels Hurt Inter Miami—And Ballon d’Or Trip Signals More Trouble
ftbpro_01m5sxkvew9f.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:00 PM EDTLionel Messi only featured off the bench in Saturday’s defeat. / Jordan Bank/MLS/Getty ImagesInter Miami saw a three-game winning streak snapped by Red Bull New York on Saturday, and Lionel Messi is partially to blame for the Herons’ struggles at Sports Illustrated Stadium.

The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner had to fly to Spain on Wednesday to receive the Princess of Asturias Award for Sport the following day. Then, Messi made the long journey back to the United States in time for Inter Miami’s weekend MLS clash.

Except the heavy travel and time changes kept Messi on the bench at the start of the game, leaving reigning MLS Cup winners without their best and most influential player against a hungry Red Bull team.

The Herons were down 1–0 just seven minutes into the bout, thanks to an own goal from Casemiro, and finished the first half without a single shot on target. The team was crying out for Messi, who eventually came on the pitch just before the hour-mark.

In the end, it wasn’t enough time for the 39-year-old to pull off a moment of magic to get Inter Miami back into the game. The visitors ultimately suffered a 2–0 defeat, relinquishing the Eastern Conference’s second place to New England Revolution and falling to third.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lionel Messi received the Princess of Asturias Award for Sport. / Carlos Alvarez/Getty ImagesIt’s incredibly rare to see Messi not in Inter Miami’s starting XI. Even at age 39, the Barcelona legend is starting week in and week out for the Herons, putting on a show for home and away crowds more often than not.
Messi missed just two games after a grueling World Cup last summer with Argentina. He then only sat out of one match following the passing of his father.
Yet his recent travels forced Inter Miami to come up with a plan to manage his workload, even if it came at the detriment of the team.

“This was something that had already been agreed upon,” manager Kily González said after Saturday’s defeat. “Obviously, he’s been through quite a journey, time zone changes, temperature shifts and a whole host of other factors.

“We were fully aware of all of this, and we reached an agreement that this was the best approach to ensure he didn’t suffer any issues, specifically to avoid any injuries considering we have another match this Wednesday.
“The goal was for him to recover and get some minutes under his belt today; as always, he performed well.”

The Ballon d’Or ceremony unfolds in London this year. / Pascal Le Segretain/Getty ImagesAs González mentioned, Inter Miami have a match on Wednesday against FC Cincinnati. It is the team’s third-to-last regular season battle before the fight for the MLS Cup truly begins.
But before the Herons host Pat Noonan’s men at Nu Stadium, there is a much-larger event taking place across the Atlantic Ocean: the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Messi is one of 30 men nominated for soccer’s most prestigious individual prize, awarded this year in London. The Argentine is not expected to claim a record-extending ninth Ballon d’Or award, but he is expected to be in attendance at the London Palladium Theatre on Monday evening.

Should Messi indeed attend the ceremony, that means another long trip overseas coming just days before a crucial MLS clash. González then might be forced to limit the forward’s minutes again, leaving the Herons to potentially pay the price.

ftbpro_01m5szban322.title: Xabi Alonso Reveals Why He Chose Chelsea in Brutally Honest Look at Real Madrid Exit
ftbpro_01m5szban322.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas4:00 PM EDTXabi Alonso (left) lasted just half a season at Real Madrid’s dugout.  / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesXabi Alonso is fully focused on trying to bring Chelsea back to the summit of English soccer, but he couldn’t help and reflect on his turbulent Real Madrid tenure, admitting he feels like “it ended a little bit earlier” than expected, without knowing if he could’ve possibly led Los Blancos to success.

After getting appointed as Carlo Ancelotti’s successor at Real Madrid in the summer of 2025, Alonso lasted just eight months at the Bernabéu. Unconvincing performances, a fractured relationship with Madrid star Vinícius Júnior and puzzling team selections all contributed to the Spaniard getting sacked after losing to Barcelona in the Spanish Super Cup final in early January.

In an interview for Sky Sports with former Liverpool teammate Jamie Carragher, Alonso reflected on his brief stint at Real Madrid. Although he admitted he feels like it ended prematurely, he also holds no resentment toward the team despite how things unfolded.

“The feeling a little bit that it finished a little bit earlier,” Alonso said. “[Not] knowing if it was going to finish well or wrong. It was in the middle of the season, we were still in La Liga and the Champions League. But it was an experience to manage Madrid.

“Madrid is special in everything. It’s a little bit different to other clubs in everything. And I learned from that and I don’t look back with anger, I look back with ‘okay, I tried it, I tried to give my best’ and now focusing on the future. But I had to try it.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Xabi Alonso is now tasked with leading Chelsea’s resurgence.  / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesEven after his unsuccessful tenure at Madrid, Alonso remained a coveted managerial candidate, with a number of teams linked with trying to sign him in the months that followed. Given his Liverpool past as a player, many expected him to become the Reds’ new boss as the Arne Slot era at Anfield crumbled.

Nevertheless, Chelsea moved quickly and appointed Alonso as their new manager even before the 2025–26 season ended. Alonso’s decision to land at Stamford Bridge caught many by surprise, but he revealed that for him, it felt like the right place at the right time.

“It was about the timing,” Alonso said. “For me it was the right time after Leverkusen, after Madrid. I had my time off and I wanted to choose to have a good connection, a good feeling about where to go.

“And I knew Chelsea. I had no link but what I heard, what they had, the potential was here, few things could change. And I thought that we could start the journey together. I had a feeling that, a very strong base of the squad was very good.

“With some updates, improvements, new signings of different profiles we could have a solid team. And it was going to be a project; it’s not that in year one it’s already done. We know it might take some more years, but the first year is important and here we are, it’s just starting. The feeling is that we could be aligned, on the same page. That’s going to be important.”

Xabi Alonso (middle) has enjoyed an up-and-down start to his Chelsea career. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAlonso’s tenure at Chelsea has started with mixed results. The Blues have one of the strongest attacks in the Premier League and currently sit fifth in the standings, but only the newly-promoted Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Alonso’s men, who are coming off a dreadful home defeat against Tottenham Hotspur.
Still, the Spaniard admitted Chelsea are a work in progress, and that his team will look vastly different come the end of the season. Not only different—he’s sure the Blues are going to be better.

“The Chelsea we are now and the Chelsea we will be in May, it will be different,” Alonso said. “And I’m sure that it will be better, because on this way, there will be a lot of ups and downs. How to overcome those downs, how to take the positives from the ups, will make us, in this journey, get better.
“I’m sure of that. Even in this seven games I’ve felt [this]. In 38 games, there will be more. And with those experiences, with the players we try to get better. We improve together.”

Chelsea are obliged to bounce back from the unacceptable performance against Spurs with two marquee fixtures looming. Alonso’s men face a daunting trip to Liverpool on Wednesday in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup before hosting the struggling Manchester United at the weekend, looking to return to winning ways in the Premier League.

ftbpro_01m5szn6pwn2.title: Neymar Pushes Legendary Brazilian, Sent Off in Nightmare Outing for Santos
ftbpro_01m5szn6pwn2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath3:30 PM EDTNeymar was shown the red card ahead of the second half. / Ricardo Moreira/Getty ImagesNeymar fell victim to the ‘Vinícius Júnior rule’ during Santos’ 1–1 draw over Bahia in Brazil’s Serie A on Saturday, receiving a red card for covering his mouth during an altercation with an opposing player.

Played out on a near-waterlogged pitch in São Paulo, the match was an ill-tempered affair from early on, with Neymar being shown a yellow card in the first half for throwing the ball at Bahia defender Rodrigo Nestor after being fouled.

Brazil’s all-time leading scorer then escaped further punishment for shoving Bahia’s manager, the legendary former goalkeeper Rogério Ceni. With tempers raised, Neymar was eventually sent off after covering his mouth during an interaction with Nestor.
With the players getting ready for kick off ahead of the second half, Neymar was caught on camera seemingly trash talking his opponents, who appeared to be doing their best to ignore Santos’ No. 10.
Neymar was seen zeroing in on Nestor, before eventually covering his mouth, prompting the defender to alert the referee, who produced the red card after a VAR review.
After being shown the red, Neymar saw red. The incident sparked a mini-brawl, with the forward needing to be restrained by teammates before he eventually left the pitch.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
Neymar é expulso por falar com Rodrigo Nestor com a mão na boca.#futebol #santos #bahia #brasileirao #Neymar pic.twitter.com/9N1vRN3nNm
Speaking after the match, Neymar threatened revenge on Nestor, saying: “We were just chatting in the middle of the field, joking around, laughing with each other

“Then I went to speak to Nestor—I was wrong to put my hand over my mouth, sure, but I hadn’t even said anything yet when he raised his hand. It’s one of the dirtiest tricks in football! But I’ll get back at Nestor eventually.”

Nestor called the former Paris Saint-Germain superstar “disrespectful,” adding: “While he may be an idol to everyone as a player, today he failed—he failed miserably as a person—because of the way he spoke. You shouldn’t do things like that.”
Apparently having not cooled down later in the evening, Neymar took to social media to call out Nestor for being “underhanded” in taking advantage of the newly enforced law.

“What Nestor did to me today is, in my view, extremely serious,” Neymar wrote on Instagram. “It’s serious because there’s a law in place against racism, and he tried to gain an advantage in the match by claiming I said something—even though I had my hand over my mouth and didn’t say a word to him. Obviously, we were trading insults—taking jabs at each other—and that’s fine; it’s part of the game. But what he did is very serious.

“We were just messing around—I was joking with the two centre-backs—and he used that to try and gain an advantage. That is very serious. There’s a law against racism—how could he do something like this? It’s surreal. I’m very sad about what happened, because he was being completely underhanded.”

The rule was brought in after the incident involving Gianluca Prestianni and Vinícius Jr. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesBrought in by soccer’s lawmakers International Football Association Board (IFAB) ahead of the 2026 World Cup, referees were granted the authority to issue a red card if a player deliberately covers their mouth while speaking to an opponent or official during a heated exchange.

The rule follows the fallout of the high-profile incident involving Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni and Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior last season, and is intended to combat concerns that players may be attempting to hide abusive or discriminatory language from cameras and match officials.
During a Champions League clash between Benfica and Madrid at the Estadio da Luz, Prestianni was seen pulling his shirt over his mouth while speaking to Real Madrid’s No. 7.
Vinícius Jr immediately reacted to his opponent’s comments and informed referee François Letexier, who made the crossed arms gesture to signal the initiation of the racist abuse protocol.

Prestianni, who denied the accusations of racism, was provisionally suspended for one match—Benfica’s Champions League second leg against Madrid. After an investigation by UEFA, he was ultimately found guilty of homophobic conduct and received a six-match ban, with three games suspended.
Paraguay midfielder Miguel Almirón later became the first player in World Cup history to be sent off for covering his mouth during his country’s group stage match against Türkiye.

ftbpro_01m5t0mmt46j.title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid: Confirmed Lineups for First Clasico of 2026–27 Season
ftbpro_01m5t0mmt46j.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell2:56 PM EDTLamine Yamal (left) and Kylian Mbappé headline Sunday’s El Clásico. / Pedro Salado/Getty Images (Yamal), Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty Images (Mbappé)Barcelona and Real Madrid have both named their starting lineups for Sunday’s must-see El Clásico at the Camp Nou.

The hosts are hoping to make it a staggering seven wins in their last eight matches against Los Blancos. Hansi Flick’s men will also be desperate to bounce back after a humbling 4–2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain midweek.

Many of the same starters from the Champions League defeat are back in Barcelona’s XI at the weekend. Flick’s backline remains unchanged, with João Cancelo and Xavi Espart manning either flank while Jules Koundé and Eric García remain sidelined.
Lamine Yamal and Raphinha unsurprisingly lead the attack again, with Anthony Gordon back on the left wing. Fermín Lopez gets the nod at the No. 10 position, replacing the injured Dani Olmo.
Rodri is also back in the XI, partnering Pedri in midfield after only playing a conservative 30 minutes against PSG.

Starting XI (4-2-3-1): J. García; Espart, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Gordon; Raphinha.

José Mourinho shook up his XI for El Clásico. / Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty ImagesThe stakes of Sunday’s battle are infinitely higher for Real Madrid. The 15-time European champions already trail Barcelona by six points, and a defeat in Catalonia would spell disaster for their La Liga title hopes.
Making an already must-win game even more tense are the absences of Vinícius Júnior and Thibaut Courtois. The Brazilian is suspended for the clash, while the goalkeeper misses out due to illness.
Yan Diomande and Andriy Lunin were easy replacements for the two absentees; José Mourinho had much tougher decisions to make when it came to his midfield.

The Portuguese boss ultimately opted for a double pivot of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Bernardo Silva, a head-turning move considering Silva has started just four games this season—and now the 32-year-old is being thrown into the lineup against none other than Barcelona.

Mourinho had limited options regarding Tchouaméni’s partner, though; Federico Valverde is starting at right back, and Arda Güler is starting at right wing. The Uruguayan keeps Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold on the bench.

ftbpro_01m5t229dxgh.title: Is Landon Donovan an All-Time Legend of the Game? Not to His Former USMNT Teammate
ftbpro_01m5t229dxgh.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely5:30 PM EDTJermaine Jones (left) had a lot say about Landon Donovan’s career. /  Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty Images (Donovan); Jan Fromme/firo sportphoto/Getty Images (Jones)What does it take to be an American legend of the game? According to former U.S. men’s national team star Jermaine Jones, it should be so much more than the soccer career his old teammate, Landon Donovan, had. And there’s a distinct reason why he himself is not at the top of that list.

Sure, Donovan is the second-most capped player in USMNT history (157) and is tied with Clint Dempsey for the most goals scored (57). He is a six-time MLS Cup winner (2001, 2003, 2005, 2011, 2012, 2014) and a two-time Supporters’ Shield winner (2010, 2011). He was even named the FIFA World Cup Best Young Player in 2002, after leading the Americans to a historic quarterfinal finish at just 20 years old.

But to Jones, “greatness” is so much more than the factors that can be quantified—caps, trophies and honors. It’s the “the level you compete at, the challenges you face, and the path you choose,” he wrote on X this week.
And to him, Donovan intentionally chose “the easier path,” whereas he “competed at the level where [Donovan] clearly felt he couldn’t establish himself.”
“I know firsthand what it takes to compete at the highest level in European football, and I also know the difference between choosing the harder road and taking the easier one,” the midfielder added.

Both now 44 years old, Jones and Donovan had the briefest overlap at Bayer Leverkusen back in 2005 and spent four years competing together for the USMNT. This is not even the first time this month that Donovan has come under fire from a former USMNT teammate and certainly not the first time he and Jones have had their differences.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Donovan has a full trophy cabinet. / Victor Decolongon/Getty ImagesJones spent the bulk of his career competing overseas at the highest levels of the game in the Bundesliga, the Champions League and the Europa League. Meanwhile, an unfruitful stint at Bayer Leverkusen saw Donovan quickly return stateside, playing the majority of his career in MLS with the San Jose Earthquakes (2001–2004) and the LA Galaxy (2005–2014, 2016).

Donovan won two MLS titles with the Earthquakes (2001, 2003) and then a whopping four with the Galaxy (2005, 2011, 2012, 2014). Although impressive feats, Jones believes there is something crucial to consider about that trophy-laden stint.

“Let’s not forget which team he played for,” Jones warned. “He wasn’t playing for the Colorado Rapids or Real Salt Lake with all respect. He played for the LA Galaxy, a club that was the face of MLS for years, with some of the league’s biggest stars.

“We’re talking about a team with three top Designated Players [including David Beckham], league rules that were adjusted, and several other players earning top money.” Just another example of Donovan taking the “easier” road, according to Jones.

Donovan dominated MLS. / Harry How/Getty ImagesJones’s trophy cabinet may be significantly less exciting, winning just the German Cup and the German Super Cup with Schalke 04 back in 2011, but that’s not what defines “greatness” to him.

“There’s a difference between dominating a league and proving yourself against the best players in the world, week after week, at the highest level,” said Jones, who racked up 129 appearances with Schalke 04 between 2007 and 2014. “... My definition of greatness might be very different from all of yours.”
Although Jones ended his career in MLS—remembered for his time with the New England Revolution, he has no doubt that he “would have dominated MLS” had he arrived on American soil earlier.

Jones is a German-American dual national. /  Jamie McDonald/Getty ImagesJones is certainly regarded as one of the most talented players to represent the Stars and Stripes, anchoring the midfield on numerous occasions, including throughout the 2014 World Cup; however, he does not hold the same legendary stature in the U.S. that Donovan does.
It is a reality that can be explained by more than just the fact that Donovan was a glamorous forward that scored a lot of goals. To Jones, it is a result of his own status as a German-American.
“Would I be considered one of the greats if I had been born in the United States and played my entire career in Europe?” Jones wrote. “For sure, period!!!”

Jones was born in Frankfurt, West Germany to an American father and German mother and represented Germany at the youth levels and even at the senior level three times in 2008. He only switched allegiances and began playing for the USMNT in 2010 at 28 years old, before racking up 69 caps across seven years with the Stars and Stripes.
The midfielder believes his career as an American has been discredited precisely because he is a dual-national, perhaps as a result of Donovan’s own scathing remarks of the past.

After Donovan was shockingly snubbed by then-USMNT manager Jürgen Klinsmann for the 2014 World Cup roster, he and Klinsmann shared candid words to bury the hatchet, a conversation Donovan recounted in 2023 on CBS Sports.

ftbpro_01m5t352h2nn.title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid Player Ratings: Mbappe Hits 100 As Los Blancos Stun Camp Nou
ftbpro_01m5t352h2nn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:43 PM EDTThe night was all about Kylian Mbappé. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesReal Madrid put themselves right back into the La Liga title race with a stunning 2–1 win over Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday night.
In a match in which six Ballon d’Or nominees started, it was Kylian Mbappé who stole the headlines with his match-winning double, though the performance was as much about José Mourinho as any player.

As expected, Barça dominated the possession, but they struggled to break down their opponents, while Madrid got an unexpected breakthrough five minutes before half-time as Gerard Martín’s attempted clearance cannoned back off Mbappé and into the goal.

The hosts fought back after the interval with Raphinha’s equalizer and pushed frantically for a winner that never came. Instead, it was Madrid who came away with bragging rights and renewed hope as a superb late counterattack ended up at the feet of Mbappé, who tapped into an open net to silence the Camp Nou and dramatically change the narrative in La Liga this season.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

It was a classic Mourinho performance. / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe last time these two met, Barcelona ran out winners to officially confirm their La Liga title at the end of last season.

This time around—though neither manager would publicly admit it—the state of play prior to kick-off meant that a win for Barcelona would essentially end a floundering Real Madrid’s title hopes even before Halloween.
With Mbappé’s bizarre point-blank ricochet and late tap-in—his 99th and 100th goals for Real Madrid—Los Blancos are very much still alive and kicking in the race.

Barcelona did not face the same team that struggled to cope in the Madrid derby prior to the international break. Instead, the host came up against what felt like the archetypal, teak-tough, counter-heavy Mourinho side, only too delighted to play the role of party poopers. Hansi Flick’s team didn’t seem to know quite what to do with Madrid’s competence.
It’s a result that changes everything. Barça no longer look unstoppable, and Madrid are very much back.
Raphinha scored his 13th of the season. /  Lluis GENE/AFP/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Joan García—7.2: Made three saves on the night but nothing he could’ve have done about the first goal.
RB: Xavi Espart—6.2: Espart’s first Clásico lasted just half and hour, with the teenager trudging off after feeling the lasting effects of a heavy challenge from Aurélien Tchouaméni.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—6.3: Struggled in his duels and will be unhappy at how he was played around on the counter at times.
CB: Gerard Martín—6.3: In hindsight, it was a poor decision to clear a cross—without pressure—straight into the onrushing shins of the world’s best striker.
LB: João Cancelo—7.7: Started at left back and ended on the right, the Portugal international was effective in creating chances and did well in his battles with Yan Diomande.
CM: Rodri—6.9: Missed midweek, Rodri asserted control but not creativity here with Barça somewhat lacking.

CM: Pedri—7.7: As against PSG, he looked a soft touch in the first half, failing to win his duels and uncharacteristically sloppy in possession. A delicious disguised assist for Raphinha’s equalizer largely made up for all previous sins.
RW: Lamine Yamal—6.9: Off the pace. The Ballon d’Or contender skewed a gift of a chance to equalize right before half time and was ultimately outshone by the stone-cold Mbappé.
AM: Fermín López—6.3: A frustrating night for López, who was unable to affect the game against Madrid’s solid midfield.

ftbpro_01m5t5v9vpw3.title: Julian Alvarez Makes Barcelona Transfer U-Turn With Massive Atletico Apology
ftbpro_01m5t5v9vpw3.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas5:00 PM EDTJulián Alvarez is returning to form with Atlético Madrid after a chaotic summer saga.  / Angel Martinez/Getty Images Julián Alvarez has apologized to Atlético Madrid fans after publicly stating his desire to leave the club this summer, admitting “it was a mistake” to try to force his way out to Barcelona.

Barcelona pursued Alvarez for months in attempt to sign a new striker to replace Robert Lewandowski. Alvarez was also keen on the move, but Atlético Madrid refused to even negotiate with the Catalans.

In one of the most spectacular chapters of the prolonged transfer saga, while Alvarez was representing Argentina in the 2026 World Cup, he publicly stated the best thing for everyone was for him to leave Atlético Madrid because he wanted to “fulfill [his] dream.”

Despite his comments, Atlético never budged from their stance, and the transfer never materialized. Alvarez was showered with boos, whistles and insults when he made his season debut for Los Rojiblancos.

The relationship between the disgruntled striker and Atlético seemed to be broken beyond repair; however, Alvarez is slowly returning to form and recently went out of his way to mend things with the club.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Julián Alvarez (front) has scored in consecutive games for the first time this season.  / Jan-Philipp Strobel/picture alliance/Getty ImagesThe transfer saga took a toll on Alvarez, who had a very slow start to the 2026–27 season. Now, though, the Argentine is back to looking menacing, and after scoring his first goal of the term in the Champions League midweek, he scored Atléti’s winner against Deportivo A Coruña on Saturday.
Alvarez spoke with reporters post-match, and before answering any questions, he issued a heartfelt apology to Atlético Madrid for his public transfer plea.

“First of all, if I could, I want to say a few words,” Alvarez said. “I want to apologize to our fans for my words during the World Cup. The truth is that it was a mistake from my part, both in the ways and the moment.

“Most of all, I understand the anger from people, as a fan I would’ve also been angry too, especially because of how much they’ve supported me always throughout the years. These last few weeks they’ve also been very generous, and I really appreciate that.

“Now I have to focus on working and continuing to improve my form alongside the whole team, whom I want to thank because they have supported me all this time. So, it’s time to get to work because we have very important things to do with the team.”

Raphinha has been phenomenal as Barcelona’s striker this season.  / Lluis Gene/AFP/Getty ImagesBarcelona have also moved on from the Argentine and are thriving, despite failing in their summer pursuit.

Without Alvarez, Raphinha has been spectacular operating as Barça’s center forward. The Brazilian leads the Pichichi race in La Liga and is performing like one of the best players in the world, helping the Catalans quickly forget about Alvarez.

“Julián Álvarez is the past,” Barcelona sporting director Deco said in late September, via ESPN. “Barcelona now have to look forward. It wasn’t possible in the end. We made an offer. Atlético said they would not transfer him and we had to look for other solutions. I hope things go well for him and that he can help his club.”

Barcelona currently top the La Liga standings with Atlético as their nearest chasers in second. Following the highly publicized saga, the rivalry between the two Spanish giants has never been more intense. Their first meeting of the season is on Nov. 8 when Barça visits the Metropolitano.

ftbpro_01m5ta1vxb81.title: Kylian Mbappe Outshines Lamine Yamal in El Clasico, But Ballon d’Or Battle Has Yet to Come
ftbpro_01m5ta1vxb81.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 25, 2026Kylian Mbappé led Real Madrid to victory in the first Clásico of the season. /  Josep Lago/AFP/Getty ImagesIt was a tale of two Ballon d’Or favorites in Sunday’s El Clásico: Kylian Mbappé silenced the Camp Nou, while Lamine Yamal was held silent in the 265th edition of soccer’s biggest rivalry.

The two stars headlined Spain’s marquee fixture, where three points, bragging rights and potentially even the La Liga title were on the line. The cameras followed their every move, much like the defenders on either side of the pitch and the supporters watching from around the globe.

Yamal is no stranger to upstaging Mbappé. The teenager has helped Barcelona to six wins over Mbappé and Real Madrid in the last two years alone, and he starred for Spain in La Roja’s World Cup semifinal win over France last summer.
This time, though? It was all Mbappé. The Frenchman bagged a brace to lift Real Madrid to a euphoric 2–1 win over bitter rivals Barcelona in Catalonia, blowing the La Liga title race wide open.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kylian Mbappé scored his 100th goal for Real Madrid under the brightest lights.  / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesMbappé might not have any major trophies to his name since making the move to the Spanish capital, but he has surely found the back of the net. The superstar forward came into Sunday’s clash with 98 goals in a white shirt since he joined the club ahead of the 2024–25 season.

Six of those goals came against Barcelona, but they almost never delivered victories. Mbappé got on the scoresheet in the 2025 Spanish Super Cup final, only for Real Madrid to lose 5–2. Three months later, he scored a stunning free kick in the 2024–25 Copa del Rey final, only for Barcelona to win 3–2 in extra time. He then scored a heroic hat trick in a La Liga title-deciding Clásico, only for his team to lose 4–3 a few weeks later.
Mbappé finally broke the trend in the team’s 2–1 win over the Catalans last October, but it was Jude Bellingham’s winner that got most of the praise.

With the pressure mounting on Los Blancos in 2026–27, Mbappé made sure he would call game this time around. The France international benefited from some luck to open the scoring on Sunday after a poor clearance attempt from Gerard Martín ricocheted off his leg and past Joan García.

As the minutes ticked on, with his team needing a moment of magic to break a 1–1 deadlock, it was Mbappé again, surging forward on the counter and perfectly positioning himself in a pocket of space to rifle home the game winner in the 87th minute.

The goal secured all three points for José Mourinho’s men, got Los Blancos back in the title race and brought Mbappé to 100 goals for Real Madrid—eight of which have now come against Barcelona. The night unquestionably belonged to him.

Lamine Yamal got little going at the Camp Nou. / Pedro Salado/Getty ImagesMuch like Mbappé, Yamal knows a thing or two about scoring in El Clásico. After all, he became the youngest goalscorer in the fixture at 17 years and 105 days old when he found the back of the net in Barcelona’s 4–0 rout over Real Madrid back in October 2024.

But on Sunday night, he was neutralized. Yamal wasn’t going up against a battered Real Madrid backline this time around; he was dueling with his fellow countryman Marc Cucurella, one of the best left backs in the world.
Before the match, Yamal boasted: “I’m going to eat him alive.” By the time the final whistle sounded, the player who had been eaten alive was Yamal.

The teenager did not create a single chance or register a single shot on target in 90 minutes on the pitch. Honestly, Yamal might have pumped up the crowd more times than he shot the ball at the Camp Nou.

Cucurella was all over the Spain international, and even on the rare ocassions Yamal got the better of the fullback, he couldn’t make anything happen. The 19-year-old was completely unmarked inside the box, in acres of space and staring at a gaping goal in the 44th minute only to pull his shot horribly wide at the near post.
Now, Yamal was by no means the worst player on the pitch for Barcelona. But in a game of this magnitude and with the Ballon d’Or ceremony just 24 hours away, he completely failed to deliver.

Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé are two of the favorites to win the Ballon d’Or. / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesBy Monday night, there won’t be single person talking about this Clásico. Instead, all the focus will be on soccer’s most prestigious individual honor.
The biggest stars in the game are headed to London, where they will learn the 2026 Ballon d’Or winner. Mbappé and Yamal, along with Harry Kane, are the favorites to win the prize.

Yamal believes he deserves the award after helping Barcelona win La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup, before he lifted the World Cup title with Spain. Mbappé believes he deserves the award for finishing 2025–26 as the top scorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup.

ftbpro_01m5ta5kxqw6.title: Five Takeaways From Real Madrid’s Statement El Clasico Win That Exposed Barcelona
ftbpro_01m5ta5kxqw6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 25, 2026Kylian Mbappé (middle) scored a brace to lead Real Madrid’s El Clásico victory.     / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesReal Madrid made a mockery of the pre-match predictions and deservedly defeated Barcelona 2–1 at the Camp Nou in the first El Clásico of the season.

The dominant Barcelona showing that many expected didn’t come to fruition, and Real Madrid were the superior side from the start in Sunday’s heavyweight bout. Los Blancos dictated terms and took the lead on the verge of halftime when Kylian Mbappé was at the right place at the right time, as Gerard Martín’s clumsy clearance hit the Frenchman and rebounded into the back of the net.

Although Barcelona improved in the second half and found an equalizer through Raphinha’s La Liga-leading 13th goal of the term from a fabulous Pedri assist, Hansi Flick’s side looked far from their best version.

When it seemed like El Clásico was destined to end in a draw, a brilliant run from Eduardo Camavinga allowed him to square Mbappé, who tapped in his match-winning 100th goal for Real Madrid in the 87th minute.

It was a statement performance from José Mourinho’s side. A deserved victory for a team that’s on the rise and a concerning defeat for Barcelona, who after starting the season looking like the best team in the world now look alarmingly beatable against strong opposition.
Here are five takeaways from the thrilling and unexpected result.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Jose Mourinho (middle) had his team ultra-prepared for El Clásico.  / Jose Hernandez/Anadolu/Getty ImagesReal Madrid played their best game of the season, and Mourinho deserves a huge amount of credit for how he set up his side and how incredibly prepared Los Blancos looked.

Those who expected Mourinho to revert to his old ways and “park the bus” at the Camp Nou were mistaken. Like Paris Saint-Germain midweek, Real Madrid were aggressive, often pressing Barcelona inside their own half, forcing mistakes.

Furthermore, Madrid man-marked Barcelona all over the pitch, with each player jumping to press relentlessly. When the hosts managed to sustain long possessions, Los Blancos dropped to a 4-1-4-1 mid-block, with Jude Bellingham tasked with putting pressure on Rodri, making it hard for the usually brilliant midfielder to pull the strings from deep.

The introduction of Bernardo Silva in midfield also hinted at Madrid’s attempt to have more control when in possession. The Portuguese star struggled at times out of possession, but on the ball, he was excellent. He reduced Aurélien Tchouaméni’s responsibilities in possession—the Frenchman was sensational as well—but was essential for Madrid’s clear attacking plan: pounce in transition. A perfect Silva long ball started the action of the opener following a passage of sustained possession from Los Blancos.

Real Madrid were significantly more intense than Barça from the start, outworking and outrunning the Catalans—a trademark of Mourinho’s vintage style. With an intelligent game plan and a tenacious attitude, El Clásico was played on Mourinho’s terms.
In his highly expected El Clásico return, Mourinho outclassed Flick and handed the German boss his first home defeat of the rivalry.

Kylian Mbappé is a different beast against Barcelona at the Camp Nou.  / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesThere’s no other way around it, Mbappé owns Barcelona. At the Camp Nou, the Frenchman is a guarantee of goals.
The opener might’ve been fortuitous and his winner a tap-in, but all goals count the same, and on the biggest stage when Los Blancos needed him most, Mbappé delivered—again.

Mbappé has now scored 14 goals against Barcelona thoughout his career and 11 of them have come at the Camp Nou. He has now scored eight goals in his first seven appearances in El Clásico, the joint-fastest it’s taken a player to reach eight goals in the bitter match-up.
The Frenchman now has two braces in five El Clásico appearances in La Liga, already more than what Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema accomplished in their careers.

In the past, Mbappé’s brilliance hadn’t sufficed for victory, seeing Los Blancos dominated by Barcelona in recent meetings. But on the night in which Real Madrid played their best El Clásico in recent memory, it was still Mbappé who made the biggest difference.

Marc Cucurella (left) got the better of Lamine Yamal. / Josep Lago/AFP/Getty Images“Im going to eat him alive,” was the phrase Yamal used to describe what he was going to do to Marc Cucurella in the fullback’s El Clásico debut. In the end, it was the curly-haired defender who ate Yamal up.

In one of the tastiest individual battles on the pitch, Cucurella imposed his will on Yamal like few left backs have been able to. From the moment the game started, the summer recruit stayed tight on Yamal and was physical in his marking, nudging him constantly and even roughing him up with fouls.

ftbpro_01m5tj1grfvg.title: ‘Won’t Fail’—Why Cavan Sullivan Will Thrive at Man City Despite Guilty Verdict
ftbpro_01m5tj1grfvg.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 25, 2026Cavan Sullivan (left) is set to join Manchester City when he turns 18 years old. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty Images (Cavan Sullivan); Visionhaus/Getty Images (Man City badge)The fate of Cavan Sullivan has been hanging in the balance ever since the Premier League called “sham.”

The 17-year-old U.S. men’s national team prodigy, who is currently dominating MLS with the Philadelphia Union, is contractually obligated to transfer to Manchester City when he turns 18; however, the club’s future is looking more grim each day, in turn making his own future all the more unknown.

City are staring down severe punishments after being found guilty for breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations for nearly a decade (2009–2018)—arranging “sham” contracts and filing “misstated accounts” that reduced costs by £900 million ($1.2 billion).

What exact punishments the club will face remain unclear, but it could be anything from a hefty points deduction or an expulsion from the Premier League to even a retroactive removal of trophies. City are in the process of an appeal, demanding that they have “irrefutable evidence” to prove their innocence.
No matter what happens to City, though, USMNT legendary goalkeeper and Premier League broadcast analyst Tim Howard asserts Sullivan has nothing to fear.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Tim Howard played in the Premier League for over 10 years. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesSullivan has enjoyed the swiftest rise to stardom. He signed his first professional contract with the Union at just 14 years old in May 2024, which included the eye-widening agreement to transfer to Man City. Two months later, he took the pitch and became the youngest player in MLS history.

He is enjoying an especially prolific campaign this season, already up to seven goals and 14 assists in just 20 regular season starts. It will be up to City to continue his development and help him reach his full potential.
Even amid their legal battle and potential sanctions, it is a responsibility City can certainly handle.

“They’ve bought a lot of players, given the financial situation, but they also know how to produce players,” Howard said this week on his podcast with fellow USMNT legend Landon Donovan, Unfiltered Soccer. “They know how to get the best out of players. Their players don’t fail a lot.”
Next. Sullivan Is Just a Normal Teenager—That No One Can Stop Talking About. Sullivan Is Just a Normal Teenager—That No One Can Stop Talking About. dark

Howard pointed to the career rise of Oscar Bobb, who spent three years developing in the blue side of Manchester before signing to Fulham in January on a five-and-a-half year deal worth £27 million ($36 million). He is now a consistent starter at Craven Cottage.

Howard also pointed to Cole Palmer, who worked his way up through Man City’s youth ranks and played for the first team for three seasons. He signed to Chelsea in 2023 on a seven-year contract reportedly worth £42.5 million ($56.8 million). He is now the face of the Blues.
“Their players don’t fail, so he is not going to fail there because there is uncertainty,” Howard reiterated.

Man City could be slapped with a points deduction so severe that it forces them into the relegation zone and ultimately down to the Championship. Alternatively, an expulsion from the Premier League could see the English Football League (EFL) choose to accept City into the Championship. Either way, that would actually spell good news for Sullivan.

“If he gets more playing time because they are in the Championship, great for him,” Howard added. “If they are in the Premier League and want to play him, great. If they want to bring him over and loan him out to another European team, great.
“He’s okay. His development will not get hampered in any way, shape or form.”

ftbpro_01m5vqxjvexn.title: Michael Carrick Sets Miserable Man Utd Record in Bournemouth Defeat
ftbpro_01m5vqxjvexn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:50 AM EDTMan Utd are in real trouble. / Darren Staples/AFP/Getty ImagesThe pressure on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has been growing since the start of the season, and it may have reached an unsustainable level after Sunday’s disaster at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils were well and truly beaten 3–0 at home to Bournemouth to extend their winless run to eight games across all competitions—five draws and three losses—and leave United 16th in the Premier League table.

Since the start of the century, United have never gone nine matches without securing a victory, with Carrick tying the miserable eight-match run endured by Louis van Gaal across November and December 2015.

Interestingly, Van Gaal actually survived that run. The eighth of those matches was an entertaining 0–0 draw with Chelsea that seemingly convinced those upstairs to give him more time, and a 2–1 win over Swansea City to start 2016 sparked enough of an upturn in form to let the Dutchman see out the season.

Whether Carrick will get the same chance will soon be decided. His side have their own meeting with Chelsea coming up next weekend which, given the Blues’ awful performance against Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, could easily provide the sort of boost Carrick and United are desperately searching for.
Louis van Gaal oversaw eight games without a win in 2015. / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesManager
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Carrick insisted he was not saying goodbye on Sunday. / Darren Staples/AFP/Getty ImagesAnalysis by Tom Gott
The brutal nature of this game is that there is effectively nothing United can do to change things other than fire Carrick.

United need results now. Immediately. As a matter of urgence. Is there still belief that Carrick can produce those results? Considering the dreadful nature of recent performances, the former midfielder will not have too many supporters above him in the food chain.

The Red Devils have so many problems to address, and the board should be aware of that. Unfortunately, at this stage of the season, not a whole lot can be done to turn things around. The ownership need to settle on a direction, the recruitment team need to address their priorities and the team needs to be rid of a toxic culture that is only sending things spiraling further, but of all that takes months—if not years.

Many fans want accountability from the owners, but a sale of the club would be a hugely complicated, lengthy process. CEO Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox are both under pressure but firing, and then replacing, two of the most powerful people in soccer is another process that would take a comparative eternity.

The calendar does not wait for United, who are back in action next week against Chelsea. Next come Roma, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Sporting CP and Brentford. On current form, United’s winless run could almost double if nothing changes.

While Van Gaal used his draw against Chelsea to offer some hope, Carrick oversaw perhaps the worst of the worst against Bournemouth. There is no reason to suggest this will get better soon, and that will be the crucial factor when deciding his future.
Structural changes may come further down the line, but for now, it feels like Carrick’s time is up.

ftbpro_01m5vr6yzz89.title: USWNT Stock Up, Stock Down: Record-Breaker Croix Bethune Makes Her Case
ftbpro_01m5vr6yzz89.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Theo Lloyd-Hughes9:00 AM EDTCroix Bethune of the Kansas City Current takes a shot against the Washington Spirit. / Photo by Amy Kontras/Getty ImagesWelcome back to your weekly feature from Sports Illustrated that analyzes the women’s soccer weekend from a U.S. women’s national team perspective.

The 2026 National Women’s Soccer League has just one match remaining, and it is all to play for. Gotham FC and the San Diego Wave are battling it out for the NWSL Shield, the trophy handed out to the team that tops the standings at the end of the regular season. Meanwhile, the Seattle Reign, NC Courage and Denver Summit are in the hunt for the final playoff spot. The Washington Spirit, KC Current, Angel City, Utah Royals and Portland Thorns have now all booked their spots, in addition to Gotham and the Wave.

It is almost exactly one month until qualifiers for the 2027 Women’s World Cup get underway for the Americans. USWNT manager Emma Hayes will be zooming in extra close on the players who will not be featuring in the NWSL playoffs, as well as those with more soccer ahead of them.
Let’s take a look at how players’ stock rose and fell during league action this past weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Signature @haleyyhopkins pressure.Poise from @CroixBethune.Blast by @vdibernardo10.2-1 #KCBABY!!!! pic.twitter.com/xeOpsgNE8p

Thanks to Croix Bethune, there is a new record for the most assists in a single NWSL season. The KC Current midfielder got her 11th of the season when she teed up Vanesse DiBernardo after the Washington Spirit turned the ball over in their own box. That goal completed the comeback as KC ran away with a 2-1 win at home. The defeat knocked the Spirit out of the race for top spot.

The assist was trademark Bethune. Calm in the final third, with excellent radar to know where her teammates are. She then hit the pass with perfect weight, making it as easy as possible to hit the shot and score. The record has been a long-time coming for Bethune, who tallied 10 assists in her rookie season in 2024 before a knee injury ended that year prematurely. She overtakes USWNT legend Tobin Heath (2016 with the Portland Thorns) and the Utah Royals’ Cloe LaCasse (2026) as players to have reached 10.

After so much NWSL dominance, the next step is for Bethune to truly become a consistent creative option for Hayes on the national team. It has been over two years since she made her USWNT debut. But in that time, she has just seven appearances, one goal, and one assist for her country. Of course, the 25-year-old’s lack of minutes has, in large part, been down to injuries. Hopefully this magnificent 2026 season leads to Hayes giving Bethune more opportunities to be the playmaker for the Stars and Stripes.
Annie Karich sticks with it through traffic to score her first NWSL goal! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/1GpKDgaw1S

An underrated bright spark in the midfield for Boston Legacy this season, Annie Karich got her first-ever NWSL goal in the 2-2 draw against the San Diego Wave on Sunday. Beyond her close-range, right-place, right-time finish at the back post, she was a tidy force in the middle of the pitch. In 74 minutes, the 23-year-old completed 93% of her 43 passes, created two chances and had two interceptions.

Karich appears to be some way off cracking a spot in the USWNT depth chart at the moment, but the two-way central midfield position is not necessarily a strong point for the USA right now, especially after the Spain friendlies. Behind Claire Hutton and Sam Coffey, there’s room for Karich, especially due to her diligent nature on the ball, to push the likes of Jaelin Howell for opportunities. One to watch for 2027.
Gisele Thompson gets it DONE 😤Her fifth of the season puts Angel City in front! pic.twitter.com/UO6ADFUL6m

Following up on her superb two-assist performance from last week, Gisele Thompson scored her fifth goal of the season in a 2-0 win for Angel City over Bay FC. Right after halftime, the 20-year-old found a pocket of space between Bay’s backline and took off after receiving the ball. There was seemingly not too much on when Thompson picked up the ball, but she knew exactly what she wanted to do when she turned. The result was a spectacular finish that rocketed beyond Jordon Silkowitz at the near post—one the best players in the world would have been proud of.

Since the return of defender Savy King, interim manager Leif Smerud has pushed Thompson further forward into more of a wing role than her traditional fullback spot. The move has worked wonders, as Thompson is such a threat in the final third and has tremendous recovery speed to cover opponents' counterattacks. While we haven’t really seen much of an advanced Thompson on the national team, it feels like only a matter of time until her versatility hits the international stage. Thompson is yet to score for the USWNT in 13 appearances, but with finishes like this, she won’t be stuck on zero for much longer.

Pietra Tordin has missed her absent teammate.  / Soobum Im/NWSL/Getty Images It has been an incredible second season in the NWSL for Portland Thorns forward Pietra Tordin. With eight goals and nine assists, she has been a breakout star who also got a well-deserved first call-up to the USWNT. However, in last weekend’s 1-0 win for Portland over the NC Courage, Tordin had a tough go leading the line. She produced just one hopeful shot in the dying moments, across 90 minutes, and had an individual expected goals and assists of 0.03.

Thorns superstar Sophia Wilson has missed the last two games, and it is perhaps no surprise that Tordin has struggled to impact games. Relationships are important in soccer. Tordin is also a very unselfish player who did a lot of the hard yards against the Courage. She knew she had to press and entered into 12 ground duels, winning just three.
At 22, Tordin remains one of the most exciting prospects for the USWNT. But her hot-and-cold streaks remind us that she is full of potential and still developing into a consistent threat.

Emma Sears warming up for Racing Louisville in Denver, Colo. / Courtesy of the NWSLThe 2026 season is so nearly over for the lowly Racing Louisville and Emma Sears. Unfortunately, on the penultimate weekend of the year, the Kentucky club was thrashed 6–1 on the road at the Denver Summit. Sears cut a frustrated figure as she was taken off after 63 minutes, having not attempted a shot or created a chance. The score was already at 3–0 when she was hooked. Louisville would go on to concede twice in the five minutes immediately after Sears’s departure.

There are so many questions lingering over the future of Racing in the NWSL. Relocation rumours swirl as questions over investment from the ownership gain momentum. Sears is categorically one of the greatest Racing players in club history. There’s no dispute there. But her time in Louisville could well come to an end this winter, and it will be a shame for it to end in such dire circumstances. Outside of August, when Sears had five goals and two assists across five games, she has been poor all season. To keep her place on the USWNT, she will likely move on in the next transfer window.

ftbpro_01m5vvb9g8q9.title: Arsenal Predicted Lineup vs. Fleetwood: Mikel Arteta Turns to Dazzling Starlet
ftbpro_01m5vvb9g8q9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack2:00 PM EDTMax Dowman has played a limited role at the start of the new season. / Mike Egerton/PA Images/Getty ImagesArsenal are back to midweek action after easing to victory against Everton on Saturday. Their Carabao Cup campaign continues Tuesday against struggling League Two outfit Fleetwood Town.

The Premier League champions overcame Ipswich Town in the third round last month and are aiming to continue their rather impressive record in the competition since Mikel Arteta took charge. Arsenal haven’t yet gotten their hands on the trophy, but are two-time semifinalists and were runners up last season.

They’ve certainly been blessed by the draw-makers here, with Arteta having the luxury of handing key roster members respite ahead of Sunday’s trip to Anfield. Arsenal’s roster is deep, and the extremities of it will undoubtedly be used at Highbury Stadium.
Here’s how the Gunners could line up for their Carabao Cup fourth round tie.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
GK: Kepa Arrizabalaga—The Spaniard hasn’t yet been usurped by summer arrival Illan Meslier in the depth chart, so his opportunities between the posts will continue to arrive in the domestic cups.

RB: Jurriën Timber—Timber has been impressive since returning from injury, but he’s unlikely to get through 90 minutes on Tuesday. Nevertheless, he could be rotated back into the team after Ben White got the nod at the weekend.
CB: Marli Salmon—Academy graduate Salmon started at Portman Road in the third round, and Arteta won’t hesitate to start him again on Tuesday.

CB: Cristhian Mosquera—Ezri Konsa’s swift impact means Mosquera’s minutes have dwindled since his return from injury. The Spanish defender should make just his third start of the season here and his first since Aug. 31.

LB: Piero Hincapié—Hincapié was back in the mix against Everton but didn’t take to the field. He should be ready for a start against lower-league opposition, ensuring Riccardo Calafiori is preserved for Liverpool away.
CM: Martín Zubimendi—The midfielder was in the wars at the weekend, taking a nasty whack to the nose in the closing stages of the match. Still, he’ll travel north and ready himself for a rare start.

CM: Bruno Guimarães—Arteta is managing his marquee summer addition, given the fitness setbacks he endured at the start of the season. The Brazilian will surely start at Anfield this weekend, but could get an hour under his belt after coming off the bench against Liverpool’s fiercest rivals.
RW: Max Dowman—Dowman stole the show in the third round at Ipswich Town, and the youngster, arguably underused by Arteta at the start of the season, is a sure bet to start down the right at Highbury.
AM: Eberechi Eze—The former Crystal Palace star should get a chance to operate as Arsenal’s chief playmaker from a No. 10 position on Tuesday.

LW: Noni Madueke—Arteta’s options are slim with Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis sidelined. Assuming Eze drifts inside, Madueke could switch back to the left after starting on the opposite wing against Everton.

ST: Kai Havertz—Back-to-back games with assists for Viktor Gyökeres mean Havertz, seemingly the clear first choice not so long ago, has a little bit of pressure on him to perform ahead of Sunday’s significant bout.

ftbpro_01m5vwdpr4bb.title: ‘Liars’—Mbappe Goes on the Attack After Real Madrid’s Clasico Win
ftbpro_01m5vwdpr4bb.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath9:30 AM EDTKylian Mbappé’s double put Real Madrid back in the title picture. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesA defiant Kylian Mbappé insisted Real Madrid have the quality to go on and win La Liga after scoring twice in his side’s shock win over Barcelona on Sunday.
The striker bagged his 99th and 100th goals for Madrid in the Clásico, as Los Blancos won 2–1 at Camp Nou, ending Barcelona’s winning run and cutting the gap at the top to just three points.
Prior to the match, many had doubted whether this Madrid team could keep up with Barça who had started 2026–27 with a record-equaling nine straight league victories.
However, José Mourinho’s side put in a mature performance against their greatest rivals, with Mbappé’s double confirming a deserved victory against the odds.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Kylian Mbappé wants Madrid to harness the collective spirit that saw off Barça. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesSpeaking to Real Madrid TV after the match, Mbappé called on his teammates to channel the collective spirit for the rest of the season, while seemingly taking shots at Madrid’s detractors.

“If we want to expect things this year, we have to do it as a group, as a team, because in the end the quality is here,” he said. “When you see the players that are here, whoever says there is no quality is a liar, but we have to do everything as a team and as a group because that’s how we are going to achieve the things we want to achieve.”

Mbappé, who travels to London for Monday night’s Ballon d’Or ceremony, stole the show in Barcelona with his match-winning goals. However, the Frenchman was quick to highlight the team effort that got Madrid over the line.
Next. Best Real Madrid Ever. The 25 Best Real Madrid Players Ever—Ranked. dark
“The truth is that the protagonist of today’s match is the team,” he said.

“We had difficult moments in the match, moments that we dominated, and in the end, winning and still being in the title race is very important for us, but we have to keep going. We know that in the end, it’s a big match, but it counts as three points, and we have to collect many points to win the league.”

He added: ”[The win] means nothing, it’s Real Madrid, we have to keep going because five consecutive wins for us are nothing, we want to win every game. This victory at the Camp Nou sends a good message, but we can’t think the season is over. Next week in Santander, we have to bring the same intensity.”
Sunday night proved one of Mbappé’s best in a Real Madrid jersey as he fired his team to a vital victory with the eyes of the world on him.
Mbappé’s double takes him to exactly 100 Madrid goals in just 116 games. Only Cristiano Ronaldo has reached a century in fewer matches for the club since 2000.

The Frenchman also took his personal tally in games against Barcelona to 14, from just 11 appearances—including his years playing for Paris Saint-Germain. In terms of his favorite opponents, he has only scored more times against Montpellier (15 in 15).
Interestingly, 11 of Mbappé’s goals against Barça have come while playing away from home.

Regarding his record in the Clásico specifically, since his 2024 arrival, no player—on either team—has scored more goals than Mbappé. His eight strikes account for 58% of Madrid’s goals in the fixture during that period.

ftbpro_01m5vy3m5wsk.title: Why Man Utd Fans Were Singing Carrick’s Name After Brutal Bournemouth Defeat
ftbpro_01m5vy3m5wsk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott10:30 AM EDTMan Utd fans were full of support for their under-fire manager. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesHaving watched their team fail to win an eighth successive game, Manchester United fans would have had every reason to turn on manager Michael Carrick. Those in attendence for Sunday’s crushing defeat to Bournemouth did not.
As Carrick walked around the Old Trafford pitch following the 3–0 defeat for his latest round of apologies, he was met by an unusual sound: support.
“It’s Carrick, you know,” the Old Trafford faithful sang to the tune of Pilot’s 1974 hit Magic. “It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes.”

The second Carrick disappeared down the tunnel, however, the atmosphere changed drastically. A vicious chorus of boos was mixed with a series of explicit chants that quickly reminded the world that this group of supporters is far from happy.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Fans took the chance to continue protesting against the ownership. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesUnited fans have been protesting against the club’s ownership ever since the Glazer family took control on June 28, 2005. Midfield maestro Kobbie Mainoo was just two months old when the group assumed the helm of his future employers.

The Glazers have overseen massive investment in United, the sort of which rival fans would envy under normal circumstances, but the problem for the Red Devils was the nature in which the Glazers financed their takeover.

Most of the funding was sourced through loans against the club’s assets which came with enormous interest payments. Debts against the club were sent spiraling out of control, but the Glazers remained relatively shielded in the board room.
“Sell United and f--- off home,” has been the message for over two decades now, with fans clear in their belief that it is not Carrick who should be departing.

The general sentiment among fans is that the Glazers are here for money, not on-field success, and so there was genuine excitement when Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS arrived with a takeover offer in December 2023. Ratcliffe assumed full control of day-to-day sporting operations but only acquired 25% of the club’s shares, later taking that number up to 28.9%. The Glazers still remain, which is a source of significant frustration for a fanbase that has hardly been satisfied by the INEOS era, either.

INEOS has also overseen a handful of significant appointments behind the scenes, including the arrival of CEO Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, recruited to bring the soccer knowledge to a group that was, admirably, prepared to accept some of its own flaws.

Those brilliant minds are now on the cusp of needing a fourth permanent manager since INEOS’s arrival less than three years ago, having also overseen a series of underwhelming transfer windows that has left the squad struggling on the pitch. Center back Lisandro Martínez made sure the world knew that recently.

Bruno Fernander (center) has fallen well below expectations. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesCarrick can only do so much on matchdays. It is his duty to set the team up and provide the tactical blueprint to success. Once the whistle blows, however, it is over to the players.

United fans have been left thoroughly underwhelmed by the performances of a number of big names. Captain Bruno Fernandes, benched for the Bournemouth game after speaking out against Carrick’s tactics, is one of many players to have underwhelmed this season, but his decision to publicly question his manager left many questioning his value as the team’s leader.

The Red Devils have looked lethargic on the pitch this season and have been regularly outran by opponents. Fans can excuse poor form, but maximum effort is mandatory and the overwhelming belief is that the United squad are simply not producing that. Carrick cannot run for them.

It was not too long ago that the sun was shining on Carrick. His interim stint in the second half of the 2025–26 season brought some of the highest highs the club has experienced in the past decade, but this year’s players have looked like shadows of those who were stealing the headlines just a few months ago.

A banner demanding the “standards” of legendary former captains Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson was brought back out against Bournemouth in a clear message to the players that anything other than full commitment will not be tolerated.

Carrick is not the first manager to fail to produce change. / Kenzo Tribouillard/AFP/Getty ImagesAmong the biggest frustrations for United fans is that the club finds itself in this situation yet again.

INEOS arrived in late 2023 with the promise of change. Erik ten Hag was awarded a new contract, only to be fired shortly after when everything went wrong. In came Ruben Amorim, who won just 25 of his 63 matches in charge before being moved on. Now, a third manager seems destined to go.
Fans have been left wondering when that change is actually coming, or if it ever will at all.

ftbpro_01m5vya942e0.title: Jose Mourinho Ruthlessly Breaks Down How to Beat Barcelona
ftbpro_01m5vya942e0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath11:00 AM EDTJosé Mourinho kept up a strong Clásico record. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesJosé Mourinho revealed that telling substitute Eduardo Camavinga to “attack the space” was key to Real Madrid’s surprise victory over Barcelona on Sunday.
Madrid sensationally ended their rivals’ record-equaling nine-match winning run with a 2–1 victory against the odds, as Kylian Mbappé struck twice.
Far removed from some of Madrid’s shakier performances this season, Mourinho’s men were well-organized at Camp Nou, limiting the defending champions’ chances while carving out their own.

Los Blancos were fortunate with Mbappé’s first goal—a bizarre ricochet off of the striker from point-blank range after Gerard Martín’s failed clearance. But the winner came as the result of a superb counter attack less than five minutes from time, with Camavinga surging forward from midfield before deftly beating Pau Cubarsí and setting up Mbappé for a tap in.
It was a goal of quality for the visitors—who are now just three points back from the top of the standings—and one that, apparently, came as a result of Mourinho’s planning.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Eduardo Camavinga’s surging run swung the game late on. / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesSpeaking in his postgame press conference the manager—who has not lost in any of his last six Clásicos—identified how he instructed 80th-minute midfield sub Camavinga to help break lines, rather than relying on solely his forwards to cause problems in attack.
“I told Camavinga, go and attack the space,” Mourinho explained. “It is difficult for any attacker to attack space against Barcelona; the only solution is to do it with your midfielders.

“When your attackers do it, Barca's defense is prepared and coached for that, and your forwards either end up caught offside or the pass gets intercepted by Joan Garcia. The solution is to use midfielders like Camavinga and [Jude] Bellingham to break that line, and it worked.”
Next. Best Real Madrid Ever. The 25 Best Real Madrid Players Ever—Ranked. dark

Mbappé, whose double takes him to exactly 100 Real Madrid goals, was the Clásico’s main character once again, though Mourinho was quick to highlight some of Los Blancos more unsung heroes from the night.
“[Andriy] Lunin was unbelievable, yet no one asked me about him ... I'm sure you would have if we had lost,” he said.

“Let me speak about Fede Valverde. He continued playing despite being injured for over 40 minutes,” Mourinho added of his captain, who began the game at right back. “He refused to come off, fought through the pain, and gave everything he had for the team.”
👔 Mourinho 👔 pic.twitter.com/fg5uqWqdcp
Sunday at Camp Nou might have been the first time since returning to the job he left 13 years ago that Mourinho really felt confident with his Real Madrid team.

In his first months on the job, there have been nervy performances and missteps, but the Clásico victory was vintage Mourinho. His team—lambasted for ranking bottom of La Liga’s running charts earlier this season—snapped into tackles, cut out space, nullified the threats and countered efficiently against their biggest rivals.

The manager also seems to now have a better handle on how to balance the talent in his starting XI. With Vinícius Júnior suspended and badly out of form anyway, Yan Diomande and Arda Güler make more sense as the wingers, while Bernardo Silva’s inclusion in the engine room gives Madrid more passing control, without losing bite.

Valverde kicked up a fuss about playing right back under Xabi Alonso just last season, but appeared willing to put his body on the line in defense for Mourinho and gave Los Blancos a solidity and energy that suits the style of play more than Trent Alexander-Arnold or Denzel Dumfries.
Though it is just one result, there is now real optimism that Madrid can use this result as a launchpad for a serious title charge after two years in the doldrums.

As Mourinho himself put it: “Real Madrid do not play just to win at Camp Nou. Real Madrid play to win La Liga. This must be the mentality. We need to continue like this and not get carried away after this win.”

ftbpro_01m5vyd9703n.title: ‘Absurd & Ridiculous’—Harvey Elliott Slammed As Valencia Loan Reaches New Low
ftbpro_01m5vyd9703n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack10:00 AM EDTHarvey Elliott’s Valencia loan isn’t going to plan. / Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty ImagesHarvey Elliott was coming off his busiest and most productive senior season to date when Arne Slot took the reins at Anfield after almost a decade of Jürgen Klopp-led joy at Anfield.

Slot‘s task of succeeding the German was an unenviable one, yet his first preseason at the helm pointed toward a prosperous future. At the heart of Liverpool’s summer success, which included victories over Manchester United and Arsenal in the United States, was Elliott, who received lofty praise from Slot after recording two assists in the win over Arsenal.

Elliott was firmly on the periphery under Klopp, who trusted him in reserve. The young Englishman was waiting to ignite, having notched nine Premier League assists during Klopp’s final season at the helm. Life under Slot started with immense promise, but a broken foot sustained in September would prove to be the beginning of the end for Elliott under the Dutchman.

Eliott missed 15 games for club and country as a result, watching on as Liverpool quickly found their groove. He played no more than a bit-part role as Dominik Szoboszlai thrived in the position that some thought had been carved out for him. His only two Premier League starts arrived after the Reds had wrapped up the title.

Slot remained complimentary about Elliott throughout, but the following summer would see Liverpool spend a record amount and drift further away from a future with Elliott as their playmaker-in-chief. Florian Wirtz joined from Bayer Leverkusen in a eye-watering $156.75 million deal, and Elliott signed for Aston Villa on an initial loan at the end of the transfer window.
The switch represented a fresh start after six years on the cusp. However, Elliott’s career has since taken a turn for the worse.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Elliott received two bookings within a minute against Villarreal. / Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty ImagesThe fact that Elliott now finds himself at Valencia indicates how poorly his loan at Villa Park went. The Villans had an $46.7 million obligation to buy, but Unai Emery only used him sparingly to protect the club’s financial interests.

A permanent deal would‘ve been triggered had Elliott made 10 appearances, including five during the second half of the season. Elliott played 11 times for Villa, but played just 13 Premier League minutes in 2026. Emery admitted they’d “damaged” Elliott and tried unsuccessfully to renegotiate his buy clause with Liverpool.

It was essentially a wasted season for the 23-year-old, and he said upon his arrival at Valencia at the start of September that regaining his self-confidence was imperative in Spain. He was handed the No. 10 jersey once donned by Mario Kempes, Juan Mata, Éver Banega and Dani Parejo, depicting the faith a fading giant had in the young playmaker.

However, Elliott’s loan up to this point has been a disaster, and it reached a nadir on Saturday when he received two bookings within a minute for dissent. His “absurd and ridiculous” dismissal, as manager Javier Aguirre put it, cancelled out Pape Gueye’s 79th-minute red card, and Villarreal subsequently claimed a 2–1 victory thanks to Georges Mikautadze’s penalty in stoppage time.

Valencia, in their final season at the Mestalla, are 19th in La Liga, and Elliott now has more red cards for the club than starts. In 152 minutes of action, Elliott hasn’t recorded a goal contribution, meaning he has a lot of work to do to hit the goal of 10 to 20 he set out for himself after arriving on loan.
Aguirre had praised Elliott just a few days before the incident, telling Superdeporte he was “delighted” by the midfielder’s attitude and work rate, but there was no such protection coming afterward.

“I don’t know what he could have said to the referee, he barely speaks Spanish, so getting sent off for something he said just makes me angry,” Aguirre said. “It’s a ridiculous dismissal, and I told him as much.”

His recent indiscretion is a notable setback, with local media vilifying the Englishman. Elliott’s progress has been halted, and there’s much work for the young playmaker to do if he’s to inspire a wretched Valencia side out of relegation strife—a fate they’ve stared in the face for years.

Elliott is contracted to Liverpool until 2028. / Lewis Storey/Danehouse/Getty ImagesIn the immediate term, Elliott will sit out Valencia’s La Liga fixture against Elche this weekend and will be eligible to return when Real Madrid visit the Mestalla for the last time before the international break. Elliott is also available to play in their Copa del Rey tie against Tavernes on Wednesday.

Looking further ahead, Valencia have no option or obligation to buy the 23-year-old permanently at the end of his loan. Elliott is expected to return to Liverpool after the season, with his contract at the club expiring in 2028.

If Elliott’s woes continue in Spain, there‘d be little incentive to buy the midfielder next summer. He’s unlikely to receive a new contract on Merseyside, so the Reds may be resigned to letting Elliott leave on the cheap. Otherwise, they risk losing him for nothing the following year.

Assuming he remains out of Andoni Iraola’s plans, Liverpool may roll the dice one final time and send him out on loan again, perhaps in the hope that Elliott will reignite his career and enhance his stock. His contract situation renders that a big risk, though, with a short-term extension usually necessary for these last-chance loan moves.
