ftbpro_01m5w1m128sc.title: Four Candidates to Be First Premier League Manager Sacked
ftbpro_01m5w1m128sc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray8:11 AM EDTPierre Sage and Michael Carrick are under the cosh.  / Andrew Kearns/CameraSport/Getty Images (Sage); Zohaib Alam/Manchester United/Getty Images (Carrick) The cut-throat nature of the Premier League means it’s only a matter of time before the first manager is marched to the metaphorical guillotine.
There were 11 managers fired during a tumultuous 2025–26 campaign in England’s top flight, two of which had already been dismissed by the time October rolled around.
While no manager has yet been canned this campaign, the vultures are already circling above Premier League touchlines up and down the country.

The opening weeks of the new season have been arduous for a number of the division’s tacticians, who remain under pressure after a lackluster return to club soccer following the September-October international break.
With that in mind, here are the four Premier League managers most at risk of being fired first.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Man Utd have made a historically poor start. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesAfter masterminding Manchester United’s resurgence as interim manager last season, Michael Carrick earned himself a permanent position in the hot seat, and deservedly secured an abundance of good-will from the club’s decision-makers, players and, perhaps most crucially, supporters.

But the beginning of his first full season in charge has served as a reality check. United have regressed during the opening months, with thumping home wins over Ipswich Town and Sabah FK hardly glossing over some truly dire displays in defeats to Hull City, Manchester City, Brighton & Hove Albion and Atlético Madrid.
A 3–0 loss at home to Bournemouth seemed to set the stage for Carrick’s exit, with candidates to replace him now being strongly evaluated.

Carrick hasn’t been aided by the club’s recruitment department, who neglected to bolster the defense or attack when reinventing a tired midfield—a fact Lisandro Martínez highlighted in an explosive rant following the team’s defeat at the Metropolitano.
United fans proved they recognized that fact as they chanted Carrick’s name after the Bournemouth loss, only to immediately turn to boos as soon as the manager retreated to the tunnel.

Pierre Sage has made an unspectacular start in England. / Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesDespite guiding Crystal Palace to FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League titles, Oliver Glasner’s departure at the end of last season left a sour taste. The Austrian’s subsequent decision to join Nottingham Forest—rather than one of Europe’s bigger clubs—only added to the confusion and frustration among the Selhurst Park faithful.
No matter the manner of Glasner’s exit, though, he’s set an incredibly high bar—one that new manager Pierre Sage will struggle to reach or surpass.

The Frenchman worked miracles during his year with Lens in his homeland, winning them their first-ever Coupe de France title and guiding them through a title race with Paris Saint-Germain in Ligue 1. But those achievements will mean very little to his Palace prospects if results and performances don’t improve from the opening weeks of his reign in south London.

Wins against Fulham and Forest remain the only Premier League victories thus far, and the Eagles have conceded the second-most goals (19) in the league after eight games. Palace’s presence in the Europa League will only stretch a threadbare squad further as the season progresses.
Off the field, there have already been reports of a dressing room fallout, as well as rising tensions between Sage and the board following an unremarkable summer transfer window.

Fulham are yet to win in the Premier League under Álvaro Arbeloa. / Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty ImagesÁlvaro Arbeloa was an unorthodox replacement for Marco Silva at Fulham. The now Benfica manager had regularly over-performed in west London, ensuring stability and the odd scalp despite the club’s lack of genuine ambition. Turning to Arbeloa marked a seismic risk—one that seemed set to backfire in the early weeks of the season.

The Spaniard’s temporary, strange and ultimately unsuccessful five months as Real Madrid manager hardly inspired confidence in the decision, even if he’s been able to lean on his connections in Spain’s capital to improve Fulham’s roster.

Three Premier League defeats on the spin immediately raised alarm bells, with some comical defending culpable for two of those losses at the hands of Chelsea and Crystal Palace. He clawed back some faith from Fulham fans following draws with Liverpool and Manchester United, but his position once again became precarious after a late collapse against Ipswich Town.

Consecutive victories over Hull City and Coventry are not the sort of results that will set the world on fire, but they were much-needed results, and Arbeloa will hope to use them as a platform to steer further away from the drop zone.

ftbpro_01m5w7w1wr3m.title: MLS Goals of the Week: Griezmann’s Handsome Header, Mehmeti’s Fancy Footwork
ftbpro_01m5w7w1wr3m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely12:50 PM EDTAntoine Griezmann (left) has dominated MLS since signing this summer.  / Leonardo Fernandez/MLS/Getty Images (Griezmann); Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images (Mehmeti)Matchday 32 of the 2026 MLS season did not disappoint. Teams are doing anything and everything they can to clinch a playoff spot, and the clock is running out with Nov. 7’s Decision Day quickly approaching.
For fans and supporters, that meant big upsets, unlikely goals and nail-biting moments that didn’t end until the final whistle.

Orlando City’s Antoine Griezmann continued his dominance in the States, scoring his 13th goal in just 15 games since signing this summer and also became the second-fastest player in MLS history to reach 20 goal contributions, trailing only Lionel Messi, who achieved it in 14 games.

Meanwhile, Red Bull New York’s Adri Mehmeti showed off why he’s considered the bright future of American soccer. The 17-year-old’s mesmerizing footwork allowed his team to open scoring against Messi’s Inter Miami less than seven minutes into the match.
Here are the top five goals from the weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Bounced off the crossbar and stayed in play! 🤯Morgan Whittaker was right there to head home the late lead for @ColoradoRapids! 🌊 pic.twitter.com/fT2NJW7yim
As a forward, it’s just as important to see out every opportunity as it is generate one’s own.

Colorado Rapids attacker Morgan Whittaker proved that fact on Saturday. Even when it looked like teammate Donovan Phillip’s long shot—which ricocheted off the cross bar—was headed out of bounds, Whittaker continued his run into the box and capitalized on a wayward bounce that somehow kept the ball inbounds.

It was a simple header that proved the game-winner in the 81st minute against the mighty Vancouver Whitecaps, the top team in the Western Conference, and kept the Rapids’ playoff dreams alive and well.
Antoine Griezmann ties things up for @OrlandoCitySC! 🔥It's the Frenchman's 13th goal in 15 matches played. 🤯📺 Watch on Apple TV: https://t.co/T6zRJ7tAvp pic.twitter.com/9LKDpPhYDJ
Ever since landing in the States this summer, Griezmann has taken MLS by storm.
The Atlético Madrid legend-turned Orlando City star player is following in Messi’s footsteps with a goal nearly every match.

Hosting New York City FC on Saturday night, Griezmann found the back of the net again in the 32nd minute off a long header, redirecting a cross into the box from fellow Designated Player Martín Ojeda. It marked Griezmann’s fifth goal in the last four matches.
Although the match ended 2–2, Orlando City sit seventh in the Eastern Conference, above the playoff line.
Adri Mehmeti starts it with some filthy tekkers 😱Julian Hall opens the scoring against @InterMiamiCF! pic.twitter.com/sufccNHZub

17-year-old Adri Mehmeti is not only the heartbeat of Red Bull New York’s midfield, but the future of soccer in the U.S. Recently making his debut for the U.S. men’s national team, Mehmeti continues to prove why he belongs on the sport’s biggest stages.

It was his fancy footwork on Saturday, burning the likes of Argentine legend Rodrigo De Paul with a sneaky “L” move, that ignited the build up to the Red Bulls’ opener against Inter Miami in just the seventh minute of play. It was a true team effort, forcing a Casemiro own goal, but will be remembered most for Mehmeti’s silky moves.
The Red Bulls walked away with an astonishing 2–0 win over Messi and Co., a massive upset at Sports Illustrated Stadium that keeps New York in playoff contention.

ftbpro_01m5w8b6dv9h.title: ‘Everyone Saw’—Liverpool Accused of Playing Anti-Football to Beat Brighton
ftbpro_01m5w8b6dv9h.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer3:00 AM EDTAn efficient attack and strong defense underlined the victory. / Peter Byrne/PA Images/Getty ImagesLiverpool played a version of anti-soccer in the eyes of Brighton & Hove Albion manager Fabian Hürzeler to claim the win and three points at Anfield on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola guided the Reds to a 2–0 victory that inflicted only Brighton’s second defeat of the season and lifted Liverpool to within one point of the third-place Seagulls. But Hürzeler was insistent afterwards that his was the only team trying to win the match the right way.

“I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” the German said. “I think everyone in the stadium felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Also, before they scored, we had one, two big chances.”

Even as the visiting team at one of the Premier League’s traditional ‘Big Six’ and a team that won the division as recently as 2024–25, Brighton dominated all the meaningful stats—apart from the most important one, which is obviously goals scored.

The Seagulls, who scored three times past Arsenal in September to humble the champions and make the rest of the Premier League take note, had more of the ball, took on more shots, accrued higher expected goals (xG) and completed far more passes at much higher accuracy.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Jérémy Jacquet has made a fine start to life in England. / MB Media/Getty ImagesThe “difference” was that Liverpool had the clinical quality which Brighton didn’t. Hürzeler also felt the need to praise the defensive efforts of Iraola’s Reds. Suddenly, the Premier League’s best attacking team this season, averaging 3.3 goals per game prior to facing Liverpool, was blunt.
“They scored. We didn’t score,” Hürzeler sighed.

Iraola didn’t make his name as a defensive manager, seemingly chosen by Liverpool when Arne Slot was fired because of the similarities in his style Jürgen Klopp’s brand of ‘heavy-metal’ soccer. Last season, his Bournemouth team finished sixth in the final standings but had only the 14th-best defensive record. Conversely, the Cherries were the equal-fifth best scorers.
However, Liverpool finished 25 points off the pace set by Arsenal last season—a weak defense of their title—because they were defensively poor in comparison.
When much of the focus has been on extracting the best from the midfield and wingers, and unlocking the enigma that is Florian Wirtz, have the Reds turned a corner at the back?

Sometimes when a team is not performing fluidly with the ball, it’s about relying on defense and grinding it out. That’s what Arsenal did for much of last season—and even reverted to over the weekend when they faced Everton because general creativity was lacking. Goals win games, but defense wins championships and all that.

“[Liverpool] kept a clean sheet because they defended well with their center backs, with fullbacks [Ronald] Araújo and [Milos] Kerkez,” Hürzeler said. “I think they blocked a lot of shots. They really defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes [and] lost some important personal duels.”

ftbpro_01m5w8yvcb9p.title: Paris Saint-Germain Reign Supreme As 2026 Men’s Club of the Year
ftbpro_01m5w8yvcb9p.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell6:05 PM EDTOusmane Dembélé accepted the award on behalf of his club. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesFor the second consecutive year, reigning French and European champions Paris Saint-Germain took home Men’s Club of the Year at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.

The Parisians were one of the few surefire bets of the night after putting together a sensational 2025–26 campaign. Luis Enrique’s men hoisted a staggering five trophies last season, including the most prestigious prize in club soccer.

PSG became just the second team in the modern era to win back-to-back Champions League titles; they defended their crown against Arsenal at the Puskás Aréna in Budapest, Hungary and walked away with a 4–3 penalty shootout victory.

By then, Ousmane Dembélé and Co. had already won the UEFA Super Cup, the FIFA Intercontinental Cup, the Trophée des Champions and Ligue 1. None compared to the euphoria, though, of lifting the club’s second-ever Champions League title.
It was no surprise PSG earned a nomination for 2026 Men’s Club of the Year. Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Bodø/Glimt and Flamengo also got the nod, but there was only ever going to be one winner.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Paris Saint-Germain took home Men’s Club of the Year last year as well. / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesYear
The first iteration of the award was handed out at the 2021 Ballon d’Or ceremony. It is based not just on performances, but also trophies won, memorable moments, overachievements and fair play.

Chelsea lifted the inaugural award after they won the Champions League under Thomas Tuchel. Premier League rivals Manchester City snatched the honor the following year, becoming the first and only team to win the award without winning the Champions League.
The Cityzens made up for it by topping Europe’s premier club competition in 2022–23, completing a historic treble that also included the Premier League title and the FA Cup.

Real Madrid were the next club etched in the record books for winning their record-extending 15th Champions League title, as well as La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup. Except not a single representative from the club was in Paris to collect the award after Los Blancos boycotted the ceremony in solidarity with Vinícius Júnior, who they believed should have beaten Rodri for the Ballon d’Or.

There was much less controversy in 2025 when PSG added the prize to their trophy cabinet for winning their first-ever Champions League title, Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions. The club then waltzed back on stage a year later to go back-to-back.

ftbpro_01m5w9x50frk.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC Staff8:05 PM EDTBukayo Saka (left) and Erling Haaland (right) headline the gossip. / Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images (Saka), Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty Images (Haaland)Sports Illustrated rounds up the latest transfer rumors and gossip from around the world.

Marcus Rashford could be offered a Premier League escape route. / James Gill - Danehouse/Getty ImagesManchester United winger Marcus Rashford has admirers across the Premier League. Everton have been joined by Crystal Palace, Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur in tracking the England international. (Source: Hooligan Soccer)
Paris Saint-Germain’s quest to replace the injured Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has seen them draw up a shortlist that includes Chelsea winger Estêvão. (Source: But! Football Club)

Liverpool have a four-man list of center back targets: Borussia Dortmund’s Nico Schlotterbech, Nottingham Forest’s Murillo, Inter Milan’s Alessandro Bastoni and Barcelona’s Jules Koundé. (Source: Football Insider)
Luka Vušković of Brighton & Hove Albion is another being watched by Liverpool. (Source: TEAMtalk)
Galatasaray are ready to try to sign Man Utd goalkeeper André Onana, having been impressed by his form on loan with rivals Trabzonspor. (Source: Africafoot)

Newcastle have warned Man Utd it will now cost over £70 million ($94 million) to sign left back Lewis Hall, but a January sale has already been ruled out. (Source: Football Insider)

Likewise, Atlético Madrid have informed Arsenal that they will not sell striker Julián Alvarez midway through the season. The Argentine’s public apology to supporters over his transfer request has left Atléti convinced he can be reintegrated. (Source: TEAMtalk)
Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha is being tracked by both Brentford and Tottenham. (Source: Tuttomercatoweb)

Chelsea have been underwhelmed by 19-year-old midfielder Kendry Páez and are now looking to sell him back to a South American team for as much of their €20 million ($22 million) investment as possible. If that fails, a loan to an English Championship side would be considered. (Source: Bolavip)
Toulouse have opened talks over a new contract with in-demand goalkeeper Guillaume Restes to fend off interest from Aston Villa, Ipswich Town and Napoli. (Source: L’Équipe)

Vinícius Júnior’s future is far from clear. / Mateo Villalba/Getty ImagesHalf of Europe’s top sides are chasing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who could be made available for transfer as Los Blancos prepare for a future with Yan Diomande instead. (Source: Fichajes)
Real Madrid are not done trying to supercharge their attack and have expressed interest in both Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka and Manchester City playmaker Rayan Cherki. (Source: fussball-news)

Paris Saint-Germain are readying a bid of €80 million ($90 million) for Barcelona attacking midfielder Fermín López, whose underwhelming performance in El Clásico has led to questions about his future. (Source: El Nacional)
Trent Alexander-Arnold has requested a meeting with Real Madrid manager José Mourinho about his future at the club, having grown concerned by his lack of minutes this season. (Source: indykaila)
Erling Haaland continues to dream of a move to La Liga but is undecided between Barcelona or Real Madrid. The Man City striker will be playing in Spain “sooner or later.” (Source: Matteo Moretto)

Al Nassr are planning to complicate João Félix’s dream return to Barcelona by triggering an automatic two-year extension clause in his contract, preventing him from leaving for free at the end of the season. (Source: Al-Riyadiyah)

ftbpro_01m5wb33gvqb.title: The Worrying Championship Trend That Could Spell Trouble for Wrexham
ftbpro_01m5wb33gvqb.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich FayOct 26, 2026Phil Parkinson is under fresh pressure as Wrexham manager. / Leila Coker/Getty ImagesHaving missed out on the playoffs by just two points last season, Wrexham’s slow start to the new Championship campaign has been particularly hard to take. Had the Red Dragons turned just one of their 14 draws into a win, they would have finished above Hull City, who are now competing in the Premier League.

The reality is that they did not. After a summer of questionable recruitment and tactical issues that have become increasingly easy for opponents to exploit, Wrexham have struggled in the second tier. Their problems have been compounded by an extensive injury list that has kept attacking talisman Josh Windass sidelined for much of the campaign.

Phil Parkinson retains the backing of the club’s board, but with a sporting director and chief executive who were not responsible for his appointment, improvement is needed if he is to remain in the job. Wrexham might point to last season’s slow start as evidence that patience can pay off, but supporters have seen few reasons to believe things will turn around so easily this time.
Wrexham are far from the first club to find themselves in this position. In fact, their current predicament follows a trend that suggests turning the season around could prove difficult.

Wrexham need to turn things around quickly. / Leila Coker/Getty ImagesIt is easy to assume that a seventh-place finish provides a solid foundation for further progress. Recent history, however, suggests the opposite can be true.

Only once in the last seven Championship seasons has a team that finished seventh gone on to finish higher than 17th the following campaign. That is where Wrexham currently stand after their latest defeat. Even more concerning, across the last 15 Championship seasons, only once has a seventh-place finisher gone on to finish in the top half the following year.

The team that bucked the trend was Middlesbrough in the 2022–23 season, and even then, a managerial change was required. It is somewhat ironic that four years ago this month, Michael Carrick replaced Chris Wilder at the Riverside Stadium with Boro sitting 21st in the Championship.

Carrick introduced a new tactical approach centered on high-intensity attacking, which was further bolstered by the January loan signing of Cameron Archer. Boro climbed from 21st to fourth, with a managerial change and a more expansive style of play helping rejuvenate the squad.

A similar story unfolded with the last team to finish seventh and then secure promotion. Swansea City had narrowly missed out on the playoffs before manager Paulo Sousa left to take charge of Leicester City. They appointed Brendan Rodgers, who implemented a high-intensity, possession-based approach that suited the existing squad. Rodgers guided Swansea to third place and eventual playoff success before Liverpool hired him a year later following an impressive debut Premier League campaign.

One small comfort for Wrexham is that none of the teams in this period that finished below seventh were relegated, although several came perilously close to the drop. That is hardly the reassurance the club’s owners and investors will want, having spent $48 million in the summer transfer window while another $95 million is being invested in the new Kop Stand.

Wrexham will hope to break the curse. / Jon Hobley/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThere is no single explanation for the apparent seventh-place curse. Clubs have failed to build on their previous success for a variety of reasons, with financial problems, points deductions and protests against ownership featuring prominently in several cases.

Others have sold key players without adequately replacing them. Wrexham have not lost any major first-team players so far, but their questionable recruitment is a concern they share with several clubs that struggled to finish in the top half the following season.

Injuries, mental fatigue and tactical stagnation have also played a role. Perhaps the most common issue, however, has been complacency. From the outside, it is easy to assume that a team finishing seventh will be well placed to repeat that achievement the following season. That assumption can contribute to underinvestment in the transfer market, while the disappointment of narrowly missing out on the playoffs can also linger within a squad.

It is important to remember that Wrexham are only 17th in October and still have plenty of time to buck the trend. What may alarm supporters, however, is how frequently managerial changes have followed disappointing campaigns among teams in similar positions.

Blackburn failed to adequately replace key players Callum Brittain, Tyrhys Dolan and Lewis Travis. Defender Dom Hyam also moved to Wrexham on Deadline Day during the summer transfer window. Blackburn could easily have been relegated had Leicester City and West Bromwich Albion not suffered points deductions. Valérien Ismaël was sacked in February, although many supporters believe the club’s owners were ultimately responsible for its decline.

Hull survived only on the final day of the season after a turbulent campaign that included various transfer restrictions stemming from financial problems. Tim Walter was sacked and replaced by Ruben Selles, while key players Jacob Greaves and Jaden Philogene had to be sold to raise funds.

Blackburn missed out on the playoffs on goal difference and paid the price for a poor summer transfer window. Key players Adam Wharton, Ben Brereton Díaz and Thomas Kaminski departed without being adequately replaced. Jon Dahl Tomasson was sacked in February, with supporters increasingly frustrated by the ownership of the Venkys.

The exception to the trend, although a managerial change proved decisive. Michael Carrick was appointed in October and lifted Boro from 21st to fourth. His fresh coaching approach reinvigorated the squad, while the January loan signing of Cameron Archer provided an additional attacking threat.

Reading’s decline was heavily influenced by financial mismanagement. The club changed managers twice and was deducted six points for breaching profit and sustainability regulations. At one stage, player wages accounted for 234% of revenue. Reading would have been relegated had Derby County not received an even larger points deduction.

ftbpro_01m5wbhdwe8g.title: Harry Kane Rips Up the History Books With 2026 Gerd Muller Trophy Triumph
ftbpro_01m5wbhdwe8g.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell6:21 PM EDTHarry Kane scored 73 goals last season. /  FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesHarry Kane took home the 2026 Gerd Müller Trophy for his sensational 2025–26 campaign for club and country, becoming just the second player in history to win the prize twice.

Since its inception in 2021, the Gerd Müller Trophy is awarded to the player with the most goals scored across a singular campaign. Named after the late German legend, Gerd Müller, the honor recognizes the world’s best goalscorers on the domestic and international stages.

Kane arrived home in London on Monday knowing he would at least hear his name called out once at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony. The 33-year-old scored a stunning 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England last season, crowning him as the sport’s top goalscorer in 2025–26.
Along the way, Kane helped Bayern Munich add another Bundesliga title to their trophy cabinet. The defending German champions also won the DFB-Pokal and the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup.

For England, Kane was just as lethal, especially when it mattered most at the 2026 World Cup. The striker scored six goals in seven appearances en route to the Three Lions’ third-place finish. He could have added even more to his tally had he played against France in the competition’s frenetic third-place match, but he sat out while others inflated their hauls.
Still, it was more than enough to crown Kane the 2026 Gerd Müller Trophy winner.

Harry Kane first won the Gerd Müller Trophy in 2024. / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesYear

The inaugural winner of the Gerd Müller Trophy—back when it was called Striker of the Year—was Robert Lewandowski. It was a consolation prize for the lethal Pole, who was robbed of winning the Ballon d’Or a year prior when the whole event was canceled.

Lewandowski went back-to-back, claiming the award in 2022 as well. His 57 goals for club and country was enough to beat out the sport’s other top strikers, but it wasn’t enough to best his 69 goals from the year prior.

The crown changed hands in 2023, going to Erling Haaland. The Norway international led Manchester City to a historic treble in 2022–23, scoring 52 goals in a sky blue shirt. Four additional goals on the international stage gave him an untouchable tally of 56 that season.

History was made by Kane and Kylian Mbappé in 2024 when they had to share the honor. Both players found the back of the net 52 times for club and country, but only the English striker made the trip to Paris to receive the award in person after Mbappé and Real Madrid boycotted the ceremony.

Viktor Gyökeres became the next No. 9 to receive the Gerd Müller Trophy for a career-best season at Sporting CP. His 63 goals for the Portuguese outfit and Sweden were enough to earn him a blockbuster transfer to Arsenal.
Rounding out the winner’s circle is Kane again. Not only is he now only the second player to win the award twice, but he is also the only player to win the award with over 70 goals.

ftbpro_01m5wbhp45ey.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 Rankings Reveal As It Happened: Where Mbappe, Yamal, Kane Finished
ftbpro_01m5wbhp45ey.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Toby Cudworth, Amanda LangellOct 26, 2026The 2026 Ballon d’Or is an open race.  / Pressefoto Ulmer\ullstein bild/Getty ImagesKylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane all have the dream of becoming a Ballon d’Or winner. For one of them, that dream is surely about to become a reality. The superstar trio have been regarded as the overwhelming favorites ever since the 30-player shortlist was confirmed, having enjoyed tremendous years for club and country, but only one was able to walk out of London as the winner.

Kane took home the ultimate prize in soccer after claiming a domestic treble with Bayern Munich and leading England to a third-place finish at the 2026 World Cup. Mbappé had to settle for a runners-up finish, while Yamal ranked third.

Alexia Putellas, meanwhile, won a record-equaling third Ballon d’Or Féminin, snatching the award from her former Barcelona teammate Aitana Bonmatí, who after three years of domination could not defend her crown after injury ravaged her 2025–26 campaign.
Take a look back at Sports Illustrated’s live coverage as the Ballon d’Or winners across all categories were revealed on Monday.

ftbpro_01m5wcfdtcmy.title: Alexia Putellas Completes Ultimate Comeback, Wins 2026 Ballon d’Or Feminin
ftbpro_01m5wcfdtcmy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie SpencerOct 26, 2026Alexia Putellas won her third Ballon d’Or Féminin award. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesAlexia Putellas ensured the Ballon d’Or Féminin stays monopolized by Spain, claiming the 2026 prize on stage Monday night at the London Palladium in the city she now calls home.
The last player not named Alexia Putellas or Aitana Bonmatí to be presented with the Ballon d’Or Féminin remains USWNT icon Megan Rapinoe all the way back in 2019.

Bonmatí was out of the running to claim a fourth successive Ballon d’Or—which only Lionel Messi (2009–2012) has ever achieved in the history of either men’s or women’s soccer—because of a long-term injury that sidelined her for nearly six months last season.

But this feels like the ultimate comeback arc for Putellas, four years on from her own back-to-back Ballon d’Or triumphs in 2021 and 2022 as well as the ACL tear that threatened to keep her from ever returning to the very top of the mountain.

The injury happened on the eve of the European Championship in England in 2022, and Spain suffered without her in a case of what might have been. La Roja was on the cusp of the semifinals until succumbing to a late England comeback. Putellas missed most of the next season for Barcelona and was only a peripheral figure for Spain at a triumphant 2023 World Cup.

While the spotlight in recent years has been fixed on Bonmatí, Putellas has been rebuilding. Last season, she captained Barcelona to a quadruple, something that had somehow eluded the club until that moment. The final act with the team she had represented for 14 years was lifting the Champions League trophy in Oslo, Norway after humbling great rivals OL Lyonnes 4–0.

Putellas wrapped her Barcelona career in the ultimate fashion last season. / Daniela Porcelli/Sports Press Photo/Getty ImagesDuring this past summer, Putellas reflected that her “mentality changed” because of the injury.

“Since then, I’ve been living, enjoying everything as it was the last,” she told The Athletic. “My first goal after the injury was to compete again at the highest level, then to be able to be key in the squad again and then to win everything. Only three seasons after my ACL injury, all of that happened.”

If you can’t beat them, recruit them, thought OL owner Michele Kang. Putellas, aged 32 and at the end of her Barcelona contract, signed with Kang’s other team, London City Lionesses. It marks a bold new challenge for the final chapter of an era-defining career.

ftbpro_01m5wcg42gvy.title: How Suspended Vinicius Jr Reacted to Real Madrid’s Clasico Win
ftbpro_01m5wcg42gvy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath2:30 PM EDTVinícius Jr posted on social media after El Clásico. / Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/DeFodi/Getty ImagesReal Madrid’s Vinícius Jr was with his teammates in spirit as they stunned Barcelona to win 2–1 at the Camp Nou on Sunday, taking to social media after the match to post his reaction to the shock result.
The Brazilian did not travel with the team to Catalonia at the weekend, as he is unable to feature in La Liga for Madrid until Nov. 21 after seeing red in the 1–0 win over Villarreal last month.
In what was the nadir of a poor start to the season for the star winger, he was sent off after a VAR review for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba in the buildup to his subsequently disallowed goal.
The foul and Vinícius’ aggressive remonstrations with the referee earned him a four-match ban, forcing José Mourinho change up his attack.
The 2024 Ballon d’Or runner up has not been missed in Madrid’s last two outings, with Los Blancos seeing off Sevilla 4–1 last weekend, before the Clásico triumph on Sunday.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
🚨 VINI JR. ON IG. 🤣🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/gbpVlvWh8c
Despite missing out on the fun, Vinícius Jr is still, apparently, enjoying the success and posted an image of the night’s scoreline alongside four laughing emojis to his Instagram story.
Vinícius will miss Madrid’s next outing away at Racing Santander on Sunday, but can feature in the Champions League tie against AEK Athens on Nov. 4.
The final game of his ban follows shortly after when Madrid travel to Valencia on Nov. 7. He will be free to return to domestic action following the next international break.

Vinícius Jr is in danger of losing his place in the team long-term. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWhile Vinícius Jr reveled in Madrid’s surprise Clásico victory, he may secretly be concerned with how the team is clicking without him.
Prior to his sending off, the forward’s form had been the subject of much frustration at Madrid. He has scored just once in 2026–27—in the 4–1 win over Real Sociedad back in August.

Mourinho appears to have found a winning formula with his selection and started the Clásico with Arda Güler and summer signing Yan Diomande on the wings, a combination that provided pace, guile and results.

Güler has—Mbappé aside—been Los Blancos’ star performer this season and offers a level of creativity that few can match. Diomande, meanwhile, is hitting his straps after a relatively lowkey start. The 19-year-old now has six goal contributions in his last five matches.

In Diomande, Madrid have a superb ball-carrying outlet—no player completed more dribbles than his four on Sunday. The young winger’s confidence in possession comes in sharp contrast to Vinícius Jr who—according to Opta—hasn’t even attempted a dribble in his last two outings against Roma and RB Leipzig.

Vinícius Jr’s status at the club—and bumper contract extension—have created an awkward situation where he is hard to drop. However, Mourinho has been handed the perfect excuse to change a broken system with the suspension. It may be hard for the Brazilian to find his way back into this team, even when he is available again.

ftbpro_01m5wcz9e724.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 Winners: Full List
ftbpro_01m5wcz9e724.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 26, 2026Harry Kane (left) and Alexia Putellas were the night’s big winners. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images• PLEASE CLICK/TAP HERE TO REFRESH FOR LIVE UPDATES TO THIS ARTICLEAs Kylian Mbappé once gushed, capturing the modern obsession with this individual award, the Ballon d’Or is “the Holy Grail,” the “ticket to the big world.”

Real Madrid’s prolific striker was front and center on a night which saw not one, not two, but 13 different prizes dished out at The London Palladium. Yet, Mbappé didn’t receive a single gong. The standout men and women, youngsters, goalkeepers, coaches and clubs were all ruthlessly ranked and categorized by a panel of journalists which collectively overlooked the biggest advocate of the award anywhere.

“We all watched that ceremony with those red carpet arrivals and said to ourselves: One day, that will be me,” Mbappé has admitted. He joined the rest of the great and the good of the sport on that red carpet only to watch on as those golden tickets were handed out elsewhere.

It’s been a long-time coming for Harry Kane. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesAfter spending most of his acceptance speech teetering on the brink of tears, Harry Kane could afford to let out a triumphant cackle once the whole ordeal was over. Less than 15 months ago, Kane had never won a single team trophy in his senior career. Now he stands alone as the greatest player on the planet.

“Mum and dad, what a moment,” Kane croaked on stage. “All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you’re there. All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.”
Alexia Putellas was born to reign. pic.twitter.com/NlzNmcTJei

Three years after tearing her ACL on the eve of the 2022 European Championship, shortly before claiming a second successive Ballon d’Or, Alexis Putellas had worked her way back to the podium. Barcelona’s captain during another all-conquering campaign has since taken her talents to Bromley, lighting up the WSL with London City Lionesses.

“All the boys and girls around the world,” Putellas concluded, “if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn’t matter if you’re a boy or if you’re a girl. Doesn’t matter where you come from. Don’t listen if someone tells you, you can’t do it. Believe in yourself.”

Lamine Yamal managed to fight his way past his own outfit to the award. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesLamine Yamal was crowned the Kopa Trophy winner for a third year in succession but claimed that his Barcelona teammate was more deserving of the award. “This one should have been for Pau Cubarsí.”

Vicky López is a back-to-back winner. / Jeff Spicer/UEFA/Getty Images)Much like her male counterpart at Barcelona, Yamal, Vicky López is a multi-time Kopa Trophy winner. The 2025 victor claimed the prize again after blossoming into a figure of real importance for a Barça side which reestablished their dominance on the global game.
🫂🧤 #ballondor pic.twitter.com/DdepKZoosY

Peter Schmeichel claimed that there was “no surprise” Unai Simón was recognized for his individual efforts when handing the Spanish World Cup winner the award on Monday. Yet, there had been stiff competition from his compatriots David Raya—the best goalkeeper in the Premier League—and Barcelona’s title-winning Joan García. In the end, the panel of judges sided with Luis de la Fuente, who trusted Simón above his countrymen at the World Cup.
CATA COLL IS THE 2026 WOMEN’S GOALKEEPER OF THE YEAR! #ballondor pic.twitter.com/f38udAQxM2

It was a clean sweep of Spanish goalkeeper this year, with Barcelona’s Cata Coll taking the women’s prize after presiding over a parsimonious campaign in Catalonia. Coll unfortunately had the spotlight slightly shifted away from her thanks to the hasty work of the award’s presenter, Schmeichel, who insisted upon announcing both men’s and women’s winners at the same time.

This is a purely statistical award dished out to the top scorer men’s and women’s players from the 2025–26 season for club and country. Harry Kane outstripped everyone with a staggering haul of 73 for Bayern Munich and England while Mexico’s Charlyn Corral was recognized after another prolific year at Pachuca.
We're proud of you, Bukayo ❤️ pic.twitter.com/DK7RNiAHAc

Arsenal superstar Bukayo Saka was handed the most unique prize of the night. The Sócrates award ignores all action on the pitch to instead honor the individual (or collective) to “identify the best solidarity actions carried out by committed champions.”
Saka’s work for the international charity BigShoe saw him deservedly collect an award named after the legendary Brazilian whose commitment to social causes was as legendary as his playing career.
PSG continue to show there's levels to this game. pic.twitter.com/e16uls0VM6

Paris Saint-Germain were crowned the best men’s club of the year for a second season running. Manager Luis Enrique once again snubbed the ceremony so the duty of collecting the trophy for the defending Champions League winners fell to 2026 Ballon d’Or winner, Ousmane Dembélé.

ftbpro_01m5wdbrnr7y.title: Barcelona Plunge Further Into Crisis With Nightmare Injury to Breakout Star
ftbpro_01m5wdbrnr7y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas3:00 PM EDTXavi Espart had been one of the biggest stories of Barcelona’s dream start to the season.  / Pedro Salado/Getty Images Barcelona’s painful defeat against Real Madrid on Sunday night was made even worse when tests confirmed that the versatile Xavi Espart will be sidelined for the foreseeable future with an ankle injury.

The first El Clásico of the season remained scoreless when the 19-year-old fullback went into a duel with Real Madrid midfielder Aurelién Tchouaméni. The Frenchman went to ground and got the ball first; however, his momentum drove his pulled-back legs directly into Espart’s right ankle.

Espart was unable to lift his right leg, and his ankle buckled, stuck in the ground with the weight of the incoming Tchouaméni impacting him at full force. The game continued, but only seconds later, the teenager fell on the ground and had to be withdrawn half-an-hour into El Clásico.

Real Madrid stunned Barcelona and won El Clásico 2–1 thanks to a Kylian Mbappé brace. The result ended Barcelona’s perfect record to start the La Liga season and got Los Blancos within three points in the standings.
Espart’s injury, though, might be an even more significant blow than the defeat, simply given the state of Barcelona’s backline.

Xavi Espart will be out of action until late in the year.  / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Espart had been the breakout star of Barcelona’s season and was the best player in the recent defeat against Paris Saint–Germain. The defender, capable of playing right or left back, had played his way into Hansi Flick’s first-choice XI, starting nine of the team’s 13 games of the campaign. Now, the fresh injury blow will see him sidelined for an extended period.
Tests carried out in the aftermath of El Clásico revealed a far from encouraging diagnosis, and Barcelona released a statement confirming the La Masia graduate will miss significant time.

“Tests carried out have confirmed that Xavi Espart is suffering from an injury to the syndesmosis joint in his right ankle due to a collision with an opposing player in the game against Real Madrid,” the statement said. “The player will be out for around seven weeks.”

It’s a nightmare development for Barcelona and the surging Espart. Now, the teenager could miss up to eight games in the coming two months, including some massive clashes that will define the course of Barcelona’s season.

Eric García has missed two games already with an injury. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesEspart is now the fourth Barcelona defender currently sidelined with an injury, with Flick losing three defenders to physical issues in the last three games.

Andreas Christensen has been sidelined with a muscular issue since the final game before the September–October international break, and both Eric García and Jules Koundé have missed the last two games after sustaining injuries in the recent win against Real Betis.
With Espart unavailable, Alejandro Balde—the player many expected to leave the club this summer—is in line to get an extended look at left back, with João Cancelo operating at right back.
Still, given the injuries to four defenders, Barcelona have no other alternatives with senior team experience if they suffer yet another injury at the backline.

Flick confessed Barcelona will need to call up defenders from La Masia to try to navigate the growing injury crisis. But the German boss will be eager to get his senior players back to health as soon possible. Barça’s backline has started to show significant cracks in recent games, proving to be the team’s weakest area for the third season in a row.

ftbpro_01m5wevxx4d1.title: Fleetwood vs. Arsenal: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5wevxx4d1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 26, 2026Arsenal were blessed by the draw-makers.  / Joe Prior/Stuart Mac Farlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images/VisionhausArsenal are aiming to avoid a major Carabao Cup upset when they travel to struggling League Two side Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.
The Gunners are out to win this competition for the first time under Mikel Arteta, having twice been beaten in the semifinals and losing to Manchester City in last season’s final.
A 4–2 victory over Premier League rivals Ipswich Town ensured they progressed serenely into the fourth round, where the Cod Army awaits at Highbury.

Before their recent slump, Fleetwood started the new season on fire, overcoming Championship side Sheffield United to reach this stage of the competition for the very first time. Manager Matt Lawlor has waxed lyrical about their upcoming opponents, but has encouraged his players not to fear the Premier League champions.

“The champions are coming to town on our patch, and it’s on telly, so if you can’t get up for this game, you can’t get up for any game. The players need to be excited for it, but while respect is through the roof, the fear can’t be,” Lawlor told BBC Radio Lancashire.
It’s the first time these two clubs have met, with the hosts targeting a memorable giant-killing on home soil.

Max Dowman is poised for a start on Tuesday after starring in the third round. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenal enter this midweek bout off the back of a brilliant weekend. After seeing Man City lose for the first time this season at Villa Park, they took care of business at home against Everton. They’re now level on points with the naughty Cityzens at the Premier League’s summit.

And if that wasn’t enough, the Gunners then enjoyed Chelsea losing at Stamford Bridge (albeit to Tottenham Hotspur) and Manchester United‘s slump continuing via a 3–0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford.
Arteta will want to ensure business is taken care of professionally on Tuesday—and hopefully with no extra hassle—as they ready themselves for a clash with the in-form Liverpool this weekend.

Lewis McCann is suspended for the hosts. / Lewis Storey/Getty ImagesThe hosts are without suspended midfielder Lewis McCann, who picked up his second yellow card of the competition during the win over Sheffield United. On a brighter note, Fleetwood can welcome back defender Rhys Bennett from his ban.

Skipper Ched Evans has been key to the Fishermen’s progression so far, scoring three times in as many appearances. The veteran forward is expected to lead Fleetwood’s attack alongside Irishman Ronan Coughlan, who scored in the 2–1 defeat to Exeter City at the weekend.
Kane Thompson-Sommers misses out due to injury.
Fleetwood predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (3-5-2): Lynch; Rooney, Bennett, Potter; Cirino, McLean, Neal, Helm, Andrew; Coughlan, Evans.
Wholesale rotation is expected from Arteta in the midweek, especially with a trip to Anfield coming up.
Max Dowman’s opportunities have been limited in the Premier League, but he’s a sure bet to start down the right for the Gunners at Highbury. Dowman starred in their third round win at Ipswich Town.

Fellow academy starlet Marli Salmon could start at the heart of Arsenal’s defense alongside Cristhian Mosquera, who is hoping to make his first appearance since August. Piero Hincapié should also get the nod at left back, having made the matchday roster at the weekend.
Martin Ødegaard, Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, David Raya and Declan Rice are among the players expected to have nights off, while Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and William Saliba are out injured.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Fleetwood (4-2-3-1): Kepa; Timber, Salmon, Mosquera, Hincapié; Guimarães, Zubímendi; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Havertz.

ftbpro_01m5wga37m45.title: The Winners and Losers From Real Madrid’s Clasico Victory
ftbpro_01m5wga37m45.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath12:00 PM EDTKylian Mbappé was a major winner. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesThe La Liga title race is alive. Just as the world was ready to write the season off before Halloween, Real Madrid go and win at Camp Nou to make things interesting again.

El Clásico rarely fails to deliver on drama and Barcelona’s nine-match winning run came to an abrupt and unexpected end on Sunday, as Kylian Mbappé’s double cut the gap at the top to just three points.

While it is just one game, it’s a result that flips the script in La Liga, with Barça no longer seen as an unstoppable, runaway train careering towards their third straight title. Madrid, by contrast, have gone—overnight—from appearing disorganized and chaotic to controlled and clinical.
Amid a sea of narratives from Spanish soccer’s biggest league fixture, here are the winners and losers from the game.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

He’s still got it. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesMbappé’s goals stole the headlines but the night was all about Mourinho. The 63-year-old cuts a different figure from the last time he helmed a Clásico—he is older, whiter and newly bearded—but he seemed to pick up right where he left off in 2013.
Mourinho is now unbeaten in his last six Clásico encounters and relishes the occasion to get under the skin of the Catalan giants like nobody else in the business.
While many predicted spite and conspiracy theories from the manager pregame, it was his tactics that stole the show.
Mourinho opted for Federico Valverde at right back and Bernardo Silva in the middle, while setting up a team that could limit the spaces and counterattack at speed.
The manager revealed after the game that Camavinga’s dart for Madrid’s winner was part of his instructions to the midfielder as he identified that Barça struggled with picking up runners from deep.

Kylian Mbappé made it to 100 goals for Real Madrid. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesNow on 100 goals for Real Madrid—only Cristiano Ronaldo and Ferenc Puskás acheived the milestone for Los Blancos in fewer than Mbappé’s 116 games.
It’s a truly remarkable return for the Frenchman. With Lamine Yamal skewing his best chance, Mbappé stepped up as the man for the big occasion.
The Frenchman is now on 14 goals from 11 appearances against Barcelona—making them his second-favorite opponents by number of career goals, second only to Montpellier (15).

Marc Cucurella kept Lamine Yamal in check. / Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIt’s been a so-so start for Marc Cucurella who was reportedly handpicked by Mourinho to fix Madrid’s fullback issues at the start of the summer.

The swashbuckling, two-way defender has rarely been able to show off his World Cup-winning best in his early Madrid outings and has been rotated with Álvaro Carreras in the early months of the season.
Sunday night, returning to the club he came through as a youth teamer, was Cucurella’s arrival as a galáctico as he shut down Lamine Yamal out on the wing.
The summer signing completed 95% of his passes and made 12 defensive contributions, while pushing every boundary available as took a phsyical approach to Barça’s elite attackers.

Mourinho praised Cucurella after the match, saying: “It was a great team effort, but it's probably the toughest match Cucu has had, and he came out on top against a very good player [in Lamine Yamal].”
Lamine Yamal was off the pace. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesIf the match was being billed as Mbappé vs. Yamal pregame, it was Barça’s No. 10 who lost the battle of the superstars.
As it also was last week against Paris Saint-Germain, the teenager was short of his bottled-lightning best and struggled up against his international teammate Cucurella.

ftbpro_01m5whntvwm0.title: Harry Kane Ends 25-Year Wait to Win the 2026 Men’s Ballon d’Or
ftbpro_01m5whntvwm0.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 26, 2026It was a night to savor for Harry Kane. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesBayern Munich’s all-round forward Harry Kane became the first English recipient of the men’s Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen’s feat in 2001 on a night of great drama.
There are so few real surprises in modern soccer.

Every official confirmation of a major transfer is prefaced by countless reports detailing each stage of the negotiation. Managerial shortlists are similarly well documented while even starting lineups are leaked on a regular basis.

In this context of dispensed suspense, the Ballon d’Or offers a point of difference. The organizing body behind the most prestigious individual accolade in the sport prides itself on secrecy, with even most of those who work in the offices of France Football kept in the dark.

Even when it looked as though the Ballon d’Or’s official website had inadvertently leaked the winner by uploading a congratulatory article announcing Kane’s triumph hours before the ceremony had even begun, it soon emerged that Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal had been given the same treatment. Those on the site team were just like everyone else, completely unaware of the winner and had prepared accordingly. Unfortunately, somehow their prep work got aired.
In the end, it was Kane whose article had to be hurriedly republished.

Harry Kane was already a prize winner before the main prize was announced. / Jeff Spicer/UEFA/Getty ImagesAmid the slew of Ballon d’Or campaigning in the buildup to Monday’s ceremony, Yamal struck upon a bone of contention. The Barcelona star’s underlying argument was that numbers should not be the defining factor of this award. “I think the Ballon d’Or should go to the best player in the world, full stop. Not to a player who has scored 80 goals,” he scoffed.
“If you score 80 goals, you get the top scorer award for that. Those are two completely different things that people do not understand.”

Those words were interpreted as a not-so-subtle dig at Kane, who ended the 2025–26 season with a frankly ridiculous 73 goals for club and country. Those are staggering figures, the likes of which European soccer has only ever seen produced by a peak Lionel Messi.
Yet, to boil the Bayern Munich talisman down to nothing more than his sack of strikes does the all-rounder a gross disservice.
Stats via Transfermarkt. Only applies to players in Europe’s top five leagues.

Kane is as much a facilitator as a finisher. Only three players in the entire Bundesliga created more Opta-defined “big chances” than the most prolific striker on the planet. Just 14.8% of Kane’s touches were inside the penalty area for Bayern last season—Erling Haaland for comparison, averaged 26.8%—as the No. 9 roamed everywhere a traditional center forward would hate to venture. Popping up as a No. 10, in defensive midfield or at fullback, there is an omnipresence to Kane’s game. In the recent thrilling Champions League draw with Arsenal, he even took a goal kick to set up a huge chance.

Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany is openly in awe of a player who has improved immeasurably since he came up against him during his playing days at Manchester City. “He has become better with age,” the manager gushed, hailing his Benjamin Button striker as “a top player who wants to run and fight for the team like a youth player.”
The 33-year-old had the nerves of school kid on a night which would end with that childlike wonder after such a close race.

Lamine Yamal was up at the lectern early on at the London Palladium. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images“I told my friends I don’t dream of winning one Ballon d’Or,” Yamal revealed ahead of last year’s ceremony. “I dream of winning many.” For now, it will remain the stuff of dreams.

Time is on Yamal’s side in that regard. No player in the 70-year history of the Ballon d’Or has ever claimed the ultimate individual accolade before the age of 21. Yamal will still be a teenager at the end of this season.

It’s easy to forget quite how junior Yamal is. Given all that he has achieved and the importance bestowed upon him by Spain and Barcelona, it seems inconceivable that his compatriot Xavi Espart, the latest precocious young find from La Masia who made his Champions League debut just last week, is 53 days older than Yamal.

While he may not have been at his absolute peak for Spain during the World Cup, Yamal sacrificed his individual freedom for the greater collective, often acting as a decoy to create space for right back Pedro Porro. It was that type of interchange down the right which led to Ferran Torres’s winner in the final against Argentina.

The simple act of claiming the biggest trophy available is so often enough at the Ballon d’Or. Since the start of the 1990s, only two players— Hristo Stoichkov in 1994 and Lionel Messi in 2010—have won the Ballon d’Or in a World Cup year without winning the international tournament or the Champions League. Yet, not on this occasion.

Kylian Mbappé is a regular at the Ballon d’Or. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images“The Ballon d’Or, to me, is a true barometer,” Mbappé told France Football in one of the many interviews he’s given the publication that hands out the prize he has so openly craved for years.

ftbpro_01m5whyrxvht.title: Erling Haaland Secures Incredible Surge in 2026 Ballon d’Or Rankings
ftbpro_01m5whyrxvht.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas7:43 PM EDTErling Haaland had a sensational 2026 World Cup.    / Ian MacNicol/Getty ImagesErling Haaland’s stellar, goal-filled 2025–26 season for club and country was rewarded with a eighth-place finish in the 2026 Ballon d’Or award rankings.

The Norwegian striker is back in the top 10 of the Ballon d’Or rankings for the fourth time in the last six years. He finished ahead of players such as Jude Bellingham, Vinícius Júnior and Michael Olise. Kylian Mbappé and Harry Kane are the only center forwards ahead of him in the rankings.

Another year, another season in which goals came in bunches for the prolific Haaland. Although Premier League glory evaded Manchester City in 2025–26, Haaland bagged 27 league goals that saw him win the Golden Boot for the third time in four seasons. He was the only current City player among the list of 30 Ballon d’Or finalists.
The 26-year-old striker did help City add two more pieces of silverware to their trophy cabinet, though, conquering the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup in Pep Guardiola’s final season in charge.
But Haaland’s true masterpiece came in the summer. He led Norway to a historic World Cup performance in the nation’s first appearance on the world stage in the 21st century.
Next. Lionel Messi’s 2026 Ballon d’Or Ranking—Revealed. Lionel Messi’s 2026 Ballon d’Or Ranking—Revealed. dark

Erling Haaland was the heart of the 2026 World Cup.  / Hannah Peters/FIFA/Getty ImagesThe Norwegian striker scored seven goals, including three in the knockout rounds, to help Norway reach the World Cup quarterfinals. His brace to down five-time champions Brazil in the round of 16 will live on forever in tournament folklore. He stole the show in North America and became a the heart of the 2026 World Cup, thanks to with some simply jaw-dropping performances and his unique, charismatic personality.

In total, Haaland bagged 58 goals and 11 assists in 64 games for club and country in 2025–26. He remains one of the greatest goalscorers of the modern era and was deservedly recognized at the Ballon d’Or awards for the sixth season in a row.
“He’s the best goalscorer in the world, there is no doubt about that,” Norway manager Ståle Solbakken said during the 2026 World Cup, before adding that: “And no, I wouldn't swap him for anyone.”

After a significant drop in the Ballon d’Or rankings a season ago—finishing 26th following a trophy-less 2024–25 season, Haaland is back inside the top 10, returning to his deserved place as one of the world’s best.

Haaland made his maiden appearance in the Ballon d’Or rankings when he finished 11th in 2021 during his Borussia Dortmund days, climbing one spot the following year in the aftermath of his final season in Germany.

Man City won a treble during Haaland’s first season in England, and his sensational debut term under Guardiola likely would’ve seen him win the 2023 Ballon d’Or had Lionel Messi not won the 2022 World Cup. The Norwegian striker still finished runner up in 2023, in what remains his best-ever finish at the Ballon d’Or awards.

ftbpro_01m5wje62xgy.title: Carabao Cup Fourth Round Predictions: Liverpool Host Chelsea, Man City Face Brighton
ftbpro_01m5wje62xgy.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 26, 2026There’s an array of all-Premier League clashes this week in the Carabao Cup fourth round. / Paul Currie/AFP/Getty Images (Liverpool duo); Carl Recine/Getty Images (Haaland)While the Champions League and the rest of UEFA’s club competitions enjoy a week off, there’s domestic cup action to watch, with several of the Premier League’s top dogs taking center stage.

We’re in the midst of an unrelenting period up until the November international break, and plenty of those teams with European commitments remain keen to enjoy a cup run and have supporters dreaming of a Wembley day out.

13 of the 16 teams that remain in the Carabao Cup ply their trade in the top-flight, so there‘s an array of all-Premier League affairs to enjoy midweek, including a couple of potentially tantalizing tussles.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts the Carabao Cup fourth round to play out.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
Arsenal visit League Two Fleetwood. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesPrediction: Fleetwood 0–3 Arsenal

Arsenal were the big winners of the Premier League weekend, even if their fiercest rivals secured a rare victory at Stamford Bridge. The Gunners moved level on points with Manchester City at the division’s summit after easing to a 2–0 win against Everton and seeing the Cityzens beaten at Villa Park.
Mikel Arteta will undoubtedly have one eye cast on Sunday‘s trip to Anfield, where the Gunners have a wretched record, and he’ll have the chance to preserve key roster members at Highbury on Tuesday.

No, Arsenal aren’t traveling back in time to their old stomping grounds. Rather, they’re facing Fleetwood Town for the very first time. The Fishermen reached the fourth round for the first time in their history by beating Sheffield United last month, but their form has fallen off a cliff since.
Five defeats from their previous seven league outings mean Mark Lawlor’s men sit 18th in League Two.
Anything but a convincing away victory would be a surprise.
The Cityzens were beaten in the Premier League for the first time this season at the weekend. /  Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesPrediction: Man City 2–1 Brighton
There’s a ‘Big Six’ affair at Anfield slightly later in the evening, yet this may be the most intriguing tie of the round.

Both teams entered the Premier League weekend in red-hot form, but were both stopped in their tracks. Man City were undone by a Nicolas Jackson brace at Saturday lunchtime, meaning their winning streak to start the league season was snapped. It left Chelsea’s record of nine straight wins to begin their title defense in 2005–06 intact.

Brighton & Hove Albion, meanwhile, were made to rue missed chances on Merseyside, as two quick-fire Liverpool goals meant the Seagulls fell to a 2–0 defeat. Despite the shutout, Brighton remain the league’s top scorers, and they’re aiming to complete a Manchester double at the start of their Carabao Cup campaign.
Brighton rallied from a 2–0 deficit to beat Manchester United 3–2 in round three, while City thumped Norwich City at the start of their trophy defense.
Bournemouth manager Marco Rose is enjoying the team’s recent hot streak. / Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPrediction: Bournemouth 3–1 Aston Villa
Bournemouth and Aston Villa probably don’t mind games arriving thick and fast at the moment, given their respective moods.

The Cherries had quite the week, thrashing two mammoth insitutions in AC Milan and Manchester United in back-to-back games. Marco Rose’s men remain perfect in Europe and showcased at the weekend why any early-season panic was unfounded.

Villa, though, are equally buoyant. Unai Emery is at it again, folks. Just when you thought a rebuild was beyond him, he reminds everyone why he’s one of the most revered coaches in the sport. Villa’s wretched start to the campaign is a distant memory, and they travel down to the south coast on a four-game winning run.

ftbpro_01m5wjhg0tn2.title: Weekly MLS Winners and Losers: Matt Turner Makes Strong USMNT Case
ftbpro_01m5wjhg0tn2.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach Lowy12:15 PM EDTMatt Turner continued his stellar performance between the posts. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesWelcome to a new feature from Sports Illustrated that analyzes the biggest winners and losers from the week’s Major League Soccer action as the 2026 playoffs grow increasingly close.
With the league’s Nov. 7th Decision Day looming, the weekend’s play was bound to feature plenty of tight finishes and upset wins. It did not disappoint.

The Colorado Rapids narrowly clung above the playoff line with a win against Western Conference leaders Vancouver Whitecaps. Meanwhile, Austin FC stormed to a late comeback win at Sporting Kansas City, and San Diego FC and New York City FC equalized in the dying seconds against the Seattle Sounders and Orlando City, respectively.

Nashville SC secured their maiden Supporters’ Shield with a comprehensive 2–0 win against CF Montréal. The youthful New York Red Bulls put an end to Inter Miami's three-game winning streak, halting Lionel Messi and Co. in their tracks. And as usual, El Tráfico lived up to the billing with a pulsating 2–2 draw.

Across North America, there were several players who came up clutch for their teams, delivering vital goals, incisive passes, game-saving tackles and world-class saves. There were also quite a few who failed to get the job done, leaving fans wanting more out of their underwhelming individual displays.
Here are the week’s biggest winners and losers.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed
Assisting all around 🤩⚽Dylan Chambost became the sixth player in Crew history to deliver three assists in a match yesterday 🌟 pic.twitter.com/wdYPevGaSe

After suffering a heartbreaking penalty shootout defeat to St. Louis CITY in the U.S. Open Cup final last week, Columbus Crew needed to bounce back. They did just that, prevailing 4–2 against Toronto FC in a pivotal match between two teams on the fringes of the playoff positions.

Columbus raced to an early start with goals from Gonzalo Tapia and Malte Amundsen, the latter heading home Dylan Chambost’s corner kick. It was more of the same after the restart, with Chambost playing a corner short before whipping in a delightful delivery for Amundsen to tap in.

The French midfielder put the game to bed after unselfishly teeing up substitute Brooks Lennon's goal, matching his assist tally for the season in just 90 minutes. Chambost became just the sixth player in club history to deliver three assists in a single match. While Toronto attempted a late comeback after the expulsion of Sekou Bangoura, it was too little, too late as Columbus made it six wins from eight.

With two goals in tonight’s victory, @FCDallas' Petar Musa reached 56 goals across his first three @MLS seasons, tying Raúl Díaz Arce (1996-98) for the third-most goals by a player in his first three seasons in league history. pic.twitter.com/clWHsMkJLj

Lionel Messi has won nine Golden Boots across his time in La Liga and MLS, second only to Josef Bican in soccer history; however, if he is to claim the coveted No. 10 this year, he will have to overcome some serious competition from FC Dallas’ Petar Musa, whose career-best 22 goals this season are inching close to Messi’s 25.

After bagging a last-second equalizer at rivals Houston Dynamo last week, Musa continued his goal-scoring heroics. Musa broke the deadlock in the 82nd minute against the San Jose Earthquakes, patiently waiting at the edge of the box for a cutback before deftly firing into the right corner. He then doubled the game’s scoring from the penalty spot five minutes later, before teammate Santiago Moreno added a third unanswered.

Six years after becoming the Czech First League’s youngest-ever top scorer, Musa finds himself in another heated Golden Boot race. The Croatian striker has already obliterated Dallas’ single-season record for goals, but now, can he pip Messi to the Golden Boot?
Until the final whistle. 😤Matt Turner's massive save in the 16th minute of stoppage time is your @MichelobULTRA Superior Moment of the Match. pic.twitter.com/BpaoZFr1Wz

He may have lost his starting spot to Matt Freese and is now facing competition from young guns like Diego Kochen, Chris Brady, and Brian Schwake. But even at 32 years old, Matt Turner is showing that he’s still got plenty of fuel left in the tank and is capable of reclaiming his position as the U.S. men’s national team’s top shot-stopper.

Not called up to USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino's roster last month, Turner suffered a second-straight 3–0 defeat with the New England Revolution immediately after the international break. However, he has since responded in style with heroic displays against FC Cincinnati, Chicago Fire and Philadelphia Union, making 13 saves during that run.

For the third straight match, New England Revolution secured victory despite conceding more expected goals. He was at his brilliant best in the City of Brotherly Love, tipping over a ferocious shot from Agustin Anello and ensuring that Philadelphia’s unbeaten streak was snapped after 15 matches.
Final in Utah. pic.twitter.com/rA4NTvuKuE

ftbpro_01m5wprrvc5m.title: Lionel Messi’s 2026 Ballon d’Or Ranking—Revealed
ftbpro_01m5wprrvc5m.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 26, 2026Lionel Messi produced arguably his greatest World Cup campaign at 39 years old.  / Evrim Aydin/Anadolu/Getty ImagesEight-time winner Lionel Messi finished fifth in the 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings in what was likely his final appearance on the shortlist of the very best players in the world.

Even at 39 years old, Messi ranked ahead of current European soccer superstars, such as Michael Olise, Jude Bellingham, Erling Haaland and 2025 winner Ousmane Dembélé. Only Rodri, Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane finished ahead of him in the rankings.
The greatest player of all time turned back the clock and dominated the 2026 World Cup, carrying Argentina on his back to the third World Cup final appearance of his career.

Even if Messi couldn’t help Argentina win consecutive titles, he produced arguably the most decisive campaign of his World Cup career—unquestionably his most productive. The timeless forward bagged eight goals to go along with four assists as La Albiceleste reached yet another World Cup title match.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lionel Messi has won a record eight Ballon d’Or awards.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesA hat trick in the opening game against Algeria, his stunning late heroics against Egypt in the round of 16, completely taking over late in the semifinal against England to steer Argentina’s comeback with a pair of assists, this summer Messi showed that even in the twilight of his career he remains one of the best players in the world.

It might not carry as much weight as what others in European soccer achieved, but Messi was also the driving force of Inter Miami’s maiden MLS Cup title—extending his win record with the 47th title of his career. Messi was also named MLS MVP for the second season in a row with 29 goals and 18 assists in 28 games during the 2025 regular season.

Finishing fifth in the 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings wasn’t enough for Messi to attend the gala in London, with the all-time great staying back in Miami to attend the inaugural Messi Cup—a U-16 international youth tournament—and prepare for his side’s upcoming clash with FC Cincinnati.

It’s also unsurprising considering anything but winning the award probably doesn’t move the needle for him, given he already has eight Ballon d’Or awards resting inside his personal trophy cabinet—the most of any player in history.
RANKED. Messi’s Greatest Argentina Moments. Lionel Messi’s Most Iconic Moments With Argentina. dark

Messi’s most recent Ballon d’Or triumph came in 2023 after winning the 2022 World Cup, which was the last time he had been nominated until this year. Had he managed to help La Albiceleste defeat Spain in the 2026 final en-route to the nation’s fourth World Cup crown, he likely would’ve been in pole-position to win his ninth Ballon d’Or.

Still, Messi finishing fifth fifth at 39 is a remarkable tribute to his prolonged greatness and a landmark moment in the award’s history. Messi is nearing the end of his career, and after retiring from international soccer in incredibly emotional fashion, it’s unlikely that Messi will be among the 30 Ballon d’Or finalists ever again.
“He’s the best player in history,” Ángel Di María told Sports Illustrated in April. “And being able to be with him every day, training, everything, is something beautiful.”

Stars burn brightest in their final moments, and that’s exactly what Messi did in his last dance with soccer’s elite. After two years relegated from the list of Ballon d’Or nominees, a fifth-placed finish in 2026 further enhances his unparalleled legacy.

ftbpro_01m5wszrzxp1.title: Ballon d’Or Organizers Explain Shocking Claims of Leaked 2026 Winner
ftbpro_01m5wszrzxp1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom3:55 PM EDTLamine Yamal (left), Kylian Mbappé (center) and Harry Kane were both under the spotlight. / David Ramos/Getty Images (Yamal), Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Mbappé), THOMAS KIENZLE/AFP/Getty Images (Kane)The organizers of the 2026 Ballon d’Or have released an official statement explaining that any claims that the podium for the men’s award has been hurriedly unveiled are premature.

In the hours before Monday’s announcement, the official Ballon d’Or website published three separate pre-written articles hailing Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and Harry Kane each as the winner of the award.

Mbappé was hailed for being “consistency personified at the very highest level,” Kane’s goals were lauded while Yamal was dubbed “the new king of football.” All three articles were promptly taken down and an explanation was hurriedly sandwiched into the ceremony’s official live blog.

“Portraits of some Ballon d’Or nominees prepared by Ballondor.com were inadvertently published online,” a statement read. “These articles had been prepared in advance for all nominees in the event of a win. They do not, in any way, reveal the podium, which remains unknown to everyone at this time.”

Those three figures came into the evening as the favorites to prevail, although, in this most open of races, the likes of Lionel Messi, Rodri or even Khvicha Kvaratskhelia cannot necessarily be overlooked.

There’s one trophy everyone is haggling for. / Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesLike any awards night, it’s an elongated process to actually have any results delivered. The organizers revealed the first standings of the men’s Ballon d’Or at 12:45 p.m. ET (4:45 p.m. GMT), more than five hours before the top spot is expected to be unveiled.

The official broadcasters of the ceremony, DAZN, provided a helpful (and rough) schedule for the night’s action—which is set to stretch across more than 90 minutes. Some of Paris Saint-Germain’s nominees haven’t spent that long on a Ligue 1 pitch in years.

The winner of the men’s top prize is expected to be belateldy revealed at 5:46 p.m. ET (9:46 p.m. GMT) with a press conference for the winner to follow shortly thereafter. As the organizers have been at pains to point out, the identity of that champion is still anyone’s guess.

ftbpro_01m5wyfxvth6.title: How Did USWNT Star Rose Lavelle Fare at the 2026 Ballon d’Or?
ftbpro_01m5wyfxvth6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 26, 2026Rose Lavelle is the star of Gotham FC. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesThe 2026 Ballon d’Or saw just one American nominated for the title of best player in the world: Rose Lavelle, who ultimately finished 27th in the women’s voting.

The U.S. women’s national team star midfielder was included on the 30-player shortlist for the annual Ballon d’Or Féminin, the most prestigious individual honor in the women’s game, after leading club side Gotham FC to the 2025 National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) title match. She even scored the game-winner in the 80th minute against bitter rivals Washington Spirit.
Lavelle also led Gotham to the 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup as well as the semifinals of both the Concacaf W Champions Cup and the inaugural FIFA Women’s Champions Cup this spring.

It was actually the second time Lavelle had been included on the shortlist for the award founded by France Football, first nominated back in 2019 after the Stars and Stripes’ fourth World Cup triumph (1991, 1999, 2015, 2019). She finished eighth in voting that year, yet saw fellow USWNT star Megan Rapinoe take home the honor.

Although Lavelle did not break into the coveted top 10 this year, it was nonetheless impressive just for her to be nominated, especially considering it was not a World Cup year for the women’s game. She also does not compete in Europe domestically, following a spring-to-fall calendar with the NWSL as opposed to the traditional European calendar used by much of the rest of the world.She played less games during the award’s voting period, hindering her overall assessment.
Lavelle will look to build on her recent success and guide the USWNT back to global glory in just eight  month’s time at the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.

Alexia Putellas returned to the mountaintop. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesAlexia Putellas took home the honor, winning the Ballon d’Or Féminin for the first time since 2022 and the third time in her career (2021, 2022, 2026) to cement her resurgence in the women’s game.

The victory follows a historic quadruple with Barcelona last season, winning Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Supercopa de España and Champions League with the Catalan powerhouse. She now plays for the London City Lionesses in England’s WSL following a summer free transfer.

Putellas continues the trend of Spanish winners, following up on a three-peat from star midfielder and La Roja teammate Aitana Bonmatí (2023, 2024, 2025). The last time a non-Spanish player won the award was Rapinoe seven years ago.
