paragraphs: By Zach Lowy2:00 PM EDTAlex Freeman scored over the weekend. / JOSE JORDAN/AFP/Getty ImagesIt was a prolific week for the stars of the U.S. men’s national team, who play all around the world at the domestic level.
Quite a few Americans found the back of the net in Europe this weekend—and seven worldwide—while others helped their teams secure clean sheets with impressive defensive performances.

With just days remaining until USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino names his squad for the November international window, every player in the pool is adamant to deliver on the pitch and convince the Argentine manager of his merits.
Here are the USMNT stars that stole the show in Europe this weekend.

🥵🔥 ¡UFFF! ¡QUÉ MANERA DE DEFINIR!🇺🇸 El estadounidense Joe Scally hace el empate del Borussia vs Stuttgart, con enorme recurso de espalda al arcoEN VIVO 📺 @NBCUniverso y Peacock y📱 Telemundo APP ➡️ https://t.co/sGoZ6DdFZj#BundesligaTelemundo #Bundesliga #Stuttgart… pic.twitter.com/MFdBGDV6Lj

After kicking off the Bundesliga season with six straight defeats, Borussia Mönchengladbach finally got off the mark on Friday with a 3–2 win against VfB Stuttgart. Joe Scally was the star of the show, with the American wingback adeptly flicking teammate Zento Uno’s line-drive into the back of the net for a first-half equalizer.

Gladbach then took the lead after the interval, before doubling their advantage in the 66th minute, where, once again, Scally was at the heart of the action. After intercepting an attempted clearance, the 23-year-old jinked free of Stuttgart goalkeeper Dennis Seimen before dialing in an inch-perfect cross for Wael Mohya to head into an empty net.
Leading Gladbach to their first away win since Dec. 5, Scally will now seek to lead the team past Karlsruhe and into the third round of DFB Pokal. He will also be awaiting a call from Pochettino.
Su primer gol con el Villarreal ayudó a cambiar el rumbo del derbi.Gran actuación de Alex Freeman, MVP en Mestalla 💛 pic.twitter.com/fTnnMWXncV

While Scally is already up to three goals this season, his main competition for the USMNT's right back position, Alex Freeman, scored his first goal since September 2025. Freeman has dominated La Liga this fall and firmly worked his way into Villarreal’s starting lineup. Typically employed at the right back position, he was used in the fairly unnatural left back position on Saturday.

Facing off against rivals Valencia in the Derbi de la Comunitat, Villarreal fell behind early, but equalized in the 69th minute, thanks to Freeman, who cut inside to meet Sergi Cardona’s cross, heading home his first goal in European football.

Freeman held his nerve across a testy match which saw both teams see red. The 22-year-old made six recoveries and won seven ground duels, a versatile performance that earned him MVP of the Match honors.The Yellow Submarine emerged victorious, 2–1, after Georges Mikautadze’s extra-time goal.
Our recent form 📈 pic.twitter.com/LRWTgD0gXU

Bournemouth are beginning to find their footing after a shaky start to the Marco Rose era, and one player who has steadied the ship is Tyler Adams. After winning the midfield battle against fellow USMNT star Yunus Musah last week in the 3–0 Europa League win against Milan, Adams helped Bournemouth demolish yet another European giant by a 3–0 scoreline.

Adams ran circles around Manchester United's midfield of Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, both figuratively and literally: no player covered more ground than Adams (7.4 miles) at Old Trafford. He also made 13 defensive contributions and nine line-breaking passes for Bournemouth, who have now won four on the bounce, scoring 11 and conceding zero in that span.
Le premier but de Timothy Weah au @CEPACVelodrome 🇺🇸⚽️Le résumé de cet #OMHAC disponible : https://t.co/MWtHOOrqKq pic.twitter.com/Z5SJTlOiDX

Another American impressing as of late is Timothy Weah. After a disappointing World Cup, followed by a poor start to the season which saw him lose seven of his first eight matches and get sent off in a September match against Paris Saint-Germain, it seemed that Weah might be on his way out of Olympique de Marseille.

Instead, the team’s captain has responded brilliantly, taking his game up a notch in recent weeks, bagging two assists in a 5–2 win against Angers on Oct. 18. Against Le Havre on Sunday, Weah slalomed past three opponents and side-footed the second goal in an ultimate 4–3 victory. He’ll be hoping his recent form brings his back into Pochettino’s good graces.

ftbpro_01m5y90rpejw.title: The Biggest Surprises From the 2026 Ballon d’Or Results
ftbpro_01m5y90rpejw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:00 AM EDTHarry Kane lifted the 2026 Ballon d’Or. / Jeff Spicer - UEFA/Getty ImagesThe Ballon d’Or is done and dusted for another year, with Harry Kane standing tall when all was said and done.

The Englishman was a deserving winner after an outrageous season with both Bayern Munich and England, but while there can be few complaints about that honor, the overall ceremony still featured a handful of outcomes that left fans scratching their heads.
From surprising finishes in the Ballon d’Or voting to controversial award winners, here are five big shocks from the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

There was little love for Bruno Fernandes. / Dave Howarth - CameraSport/Getty ImagesLook, nobody’s arguing that Bruno Fernandes should have won the whole thing, but to see him as low as 27th, just one place ahead of Al Qadsiah’s Julián Quiñones, is mindblowing.

The Manchester United captain may well be a victim of his recent slump, which is unfair considering the judging period was supposed to end on July 19. Across the 2025–26 campaign, he broke the Premier League record for most assists in a single season and was crowned the division’s Player of the Year, only to finish lower than five different Premier League players in the Ballon d’Or voting.
Competition is fierce, but few would have complained had Fernandes landed in the top 15.

Fabián Ruiz has his trophy haul to thank. / Joachim Azouze/PSG/Getty ImagesWorking in Fabián Ruiz’s favor is the fact he won literally everything. He’s a regular starter for the Paris Saint-Germain side that retained the Champions League and lifted the Ligue 1 title, and he added the World Cup to his cabinet after a glamorous summer with Spain. Those accolades make him tough to ignore.
And yet, if you break it down, Fabián can consider himself fortunate to have landed as high as 10th.

Across the 2025–26 Ligue 1 season, Fabián played just 20 matches, 13 of which were starts. He then went to the World Cup and started four of Spain’s eight games. He ended the entire season with three goals and six assists in a total of 2,634 minutes for club and country. For comparison, Kane ended 2025–26 with 5,223 minutes in the tank.
You can’t argue with his trophy haul, but did he really have a better individual season than Jude Bellingham or Pau Cubarsí behind him?

Michael Olise is in the shadow of superstars. / Benjamin Faes/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesOne place ahead of Fabián in the voting was Michael Olise, who deserved to be in with a genuine chance to lift the trophy.

In 52 games for Bayern Munich last season, the Frenchman racked up 22 goals and 31 assists, and this summer brought a further seven assists at the World Cup—a tournament record. Those are utterly mindboggling numbers that perhaps suffered being compared to the even-more-mindboggling return from eventual winner Kane.

Unfortunately for Olise, when you think of Bayern Munich, you think of Kane. When you think of France, it’s Kylian Mbappé. Still, he had the sort of season that should have seen him pushing the top five.

Unai Simón was carried by Spain’s success. / Omar Arnau/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesUnai Simón conceded one goal en route to lifting the World Cup with Spain, and that accomplishment alone saw him crowned the best goalkeeper on the planet over the entire season.

If we actually consider the whole season, Simón will know he was fortunate. He conceded 54 goals in 37 La Liga games for an Athletic Club side that ended the season in 12th with a negative goal difference. Simón’s save percentage of 64.9% was bettered by no fewer than 16 stoppers in Spain’s top flight alone.
At the World Cup, Spain only conceded a total of 10 shots on target across the whole tournament, limiting Simón’s genuine involvement all summer.
The fact he started for Spain over Arsenal’s David Raya, who ended up in second, and seventh-placed Joan García of Barcelona, has won him this award.

And if you still don’t believe the World Cup has that much of an impact, García was La Liga’s best goalkeeper last season and ended up one place behind Cabo Verde’s Vozinha, who 99% of the voters did not even know existed until his stunning showing against, ironically, Simón’s Spain.

Time to change the rules? / Jeff Spicer - UEFA/Getty ImagesRight, objectively, this was the right call. Considering Lamine Yamal came third in Ballon d’Or voting, he was always winning the Kopa Trophy. That being said ... a bit boring, isn’t it?

Neither club will want to be eliminated in the fourth round—the sort of exit that puts anyone under pressure regardless of circumstance—and so we should expect an entertaining affair between two teams that hold genuine ambitions of winning this entire competition.

Liverpool arrive at this one in high spirits, having figured themselves out to the tune of eight wins and a draw from their last 10 games, and they will be heavy favorites against a Chelsea side that has toppled back into crisis after a dismal 2–0 defeat at home to Tottenham Hotspur at the weekend.
It’s still early in the season, but this is the sort of fixture that can really dictate the direction of a team’s campaign.

The Reds have found their footing after an uncomfortable start to the Andoni Iraola era. ftbpro_01m5ygfpg4jt.title: How Tom Brady Inspired Harry Kane to the Ballon d’Or
ftbpro_01m5ygfpg4jt.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom9:30 AM EDTTom Brady (left) served as a source of real inspiration for Harry Kane. / Adam Glanzman/Getty Images (Brady), FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images (Kane)Tumbling down dark YouTube rabbit holes can lead to founts of useless knowledge, inane conspiracy theories and, in the case of Harry Kane at least, the ultimate individual accolade soccer has to offer.

Thirteen years before Kane was stood in London, his home city, fighting off tears to accept the Ballon d’Or as the best men’s player on the planet, he had been sat on his couch in a rented apartment in Leicester contemplating his future in the sport.

A bright academy prospect at Tottenham Hotspur, the then-teenager was in the midst of his fourth loan spell in three years. It was not going well. Leicester City were in England’s second tier and locked in a sequence of one win in 13 games yet Kane still couldn’t force himself into the starting lineup.

“That was the first time in my career, I’d say, that the doubt crept in,” Kane would later tell The Players’ Tribune. “I just remember sitting in my flat and having this terrible realization of, like, If I can’t play for Leicester in the Championship ... how am I supposed to play for Spurs in the Premier League?”

Away from home in an unfamiliar city, Kane sank his spare time into his new hobby: NFL. The New England Patriots had caught the attention of the English forward who stumbled across an NFL Films documentary about star quarterback Tom Brady which had been illegally uploaded to YouTube. It would change his life.

The Brady Six followed the careers of the six quarterbacks drafted before Brady, who was infamously selected 199th overall before becoming the greatest in the history of the sport. Kane could not believe it.

“It just blew my mind—but in a good way. The film really struck a chord with me. Everyone was doubting Tom his whole life,” the striker reflected years later. “He reminded me of me. People were always making the same assumptions about me. [Saying:] ‘Well, you know, he doesn’t look like a proper striker.’”

Brady’s scouting report coming out of college read: “Poor build, skinny, lacks a really strong arm, can’t drive the ball downfield.” Kane was at the other extreme having been let go from Arsenal’s academy as an 8-year-old for being “a bit chubby.”
That rejection lit a flame in Brady—when the report is recanted to the quarterback in the documentary, he snipes: “That kind of gets me fired up.” It also sparked something in Kane.

“It was genuinely inspiring to me,” he recalled. “Brady believed in himself so much—and he just kept working and working, almost obsessively, in order to get better. It really connected with me. This might sound strange, but it really was like this light flicked on inside my head that day, right there on my sofa in Leicester—and all of a sudden, I said, ‘You know what? I’m going to do it. I’m going to work as hard as possible, and my chance is going to come, and I’m going to grab it.’”

It was an easy motivational tool for a player who has always prided himself on his work ethic. “I’m not a believer in it all being natural,” Kane’s former youth team coach at Spurs, Alex Inglethorpe, told BBC Sport when his former pupil first broke through. “I believe in working talent, and Harry is a working talent.” That attitude is why Inglethorpe described Kane as “his own best coach.” Although the player himself would point to a different manager.

Mauricio Pochettino (left) was key to Kane’s development. / Suhaimi Abdullah/International Champions Cup/Getty ImagesKane returned to Tottenham a few months after his Brady epiphany with an entirely new mindset. When manager André Villas-Boas suggested another loan away, he was stunned to hear his scarcely used youth team player say no.

“I’m gonna prove to you that I should be starting on this team,” Kane told the perplexed coach. “And you can tell me every Friday before the game that I don’t deserve that, and that I’m not going to play. And that’s fine. But I don’t want to go.”

It would not be until the final month of the season, following Villas-Boas’s departure, that Kane was belatedly given his chance. He scored in his first three Premier League starts for the club but was still considered third-choice when Mauricio Pochettino took over in 2014.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“When we arrived to Tottenham, when we saw Harry Kane, we said, ‘No, it’s a player that we need. He’s young. He needs to stay with us,’” Pochettino would later reveal. It still took 10 games of the new season for the current U.S. men’s national team coach to give the 20-year-old a regular run in the team but, as ever, Kane’s head never dropped. A 90th-minute winner against Aston Villa convinced Pochettino to take the gamble which would eventually present Tottenham with a new all-time top scorer and England with their first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years.

As much as Brady lit the match, Pochettino stoked the flames of Kane’s talent. “No one has had a bigger impact on my career than Mauricio,” he would claim, name-checking the Argentine in his Ballon d’Or acceptance speech.

Brady, intriguingly, did not get a mention, although the pair have since met on several occasions, exchanging tales of their battles against adversity. Such is Kane’s enduring admiration for Brady, there is talk of him even taking a turn in the NFL as a kicker once his soccer career concludes.
Perhaps even more credit should be saved for that anonymous YouTube account which flouted copyright regulations to put Brady’s documentary within Kane’s grasp. Where was their shout-out?

ftbpro_01m5yjvfc2mm.title: Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Chelsea: Rests Needed Before Arsenal

paragraphs: By Tom Gott12:30 PM EDTLiverpool are in strong form recently. / Paul Currie/AFP/Getty ImagesAndoni Iraola will learn a lot about his Liverpool side over the next week.
While a huge Premier League clash with Arsenal is on the horizon, first up on the agenda is a visit from Chelsea in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday.

The Reds are feeling good these days, particularly after a 2–0 win over Brighton & Hove Albion at the weekend. Iraola will back his side to see off a Chelsea team in a difficult moment under Liverpool legend Xabi Alonso, although the need to protect his big names ahead of the Arsenal game could easily complicate things.
Here’s how Liverpool could set up for this one.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Giorgi Mamardashvili—A season stuck behind Alisson in the pecking order is on the cards for Mamardashvili, who will be desperate to keep Liverpool in this competition considering it could be his only source of minutes.
RB: Ronald Araújo—Injuries to Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong limit Iraola’s ability to rotate here, particularly considering Araújo is already playing out of position.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—Chelsea thought they were going to land Jacquet’s signature back in January and will be particularly frustrated to see how well he has adjusted to life in the Premier League.

RM: Rio Ngumoha—Chelsea were left seething when Ngumoha walked away from the club’s academy to join Liverpool, and the sight of him grabbing an assist in the 1–1 draw between these two last season will not have helped.
AM: James McConnell—A big opportunity for the youngster here, with Dominik Szoboszlai injured and Florian Wirtz in need of a rest after complaining of a minor foot injury.
LM: Cody Gakpo—Big changes in attack will see Iraola demand even more from Gakpo, whose electric start to the season has cooled off in recent weeks.

ST: Lewis Koumas—Deciding whether to rest the in-form Alexander Isak is among Iraola’s biggest conundrums. The boss has put plenty of faith in young Koumas recently and may give him the ultimate test here.

ftbpro_01m5ym9wwxk1.title: Chelsea Predicted Lineup vs. Liverpool: Suspended Palmer Adds to Alonso’s Headache
ftbpro_01m5ym9wwxk1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott1:00 PM EDTThe pressure is on Xabi Alonso. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesAn immediate response is needed from Chelsea after their chaotic defeat to Tottenham Hotspur at the weekend, with manager Xabi Alonso searching for victory against former team Liverpool.

Alonso’s return to Anfield seemed destined to be the primary narrative for this one, but that was before the nightmare that was the Tottenham game. Make no mistake about it, the boss is under pressure now, with the cracks on show earlier in the season developing into craters.

Elimination in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup would come as a massive blow, considering Chelsea had genuine ambitions of winning this competition at the start of the season. Doing away with one of their biggest rivals would go a long way to raising spirits around Stamford Bridge.

ftbpro_01m5ypck55ww.title: Man Utd Reach ‘Final’ Michael Carrick Decision After Bournemouth Defeat
ftbpro_01m5ypck55ww.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:30 AM EDTMichael Carrick’s time at Manchester United isn’t over—just yet. / PIERO CRUCIATTI/AFP/Getty ImagesManchester United have given Michael Carrick a stay of execution, allowing the under-fire manager to take charge of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Chelsea according to numerous reports. That much would appear clear. Quite why—and for how much longer—is a little more complicated.

Carrick was christened a “dead man walking” after conducting an emotional lap of Old Trafford following Sunday’s thrashing against Bournemouth. The defiance of his prematch press conference had been replaced with a tone of resignation. “I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club,” he accepted.
Much to the surprise of those in and out of the club, the upper hierarchy have given Carrick “the opportunity to turn things around,” as first reported by Mike Keegan of The Overlap.

It’s not yet clear what that opportunity will look like. The pressure will only return again should United lose to Chelsea this weekend unless there is a public show of support from his employers—and even then that can often be the kiss of death. That eventuality will have to wait.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

The mood is toxic at Old Trafford. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAs Carrick waved a premature farewell to the Old Trafford stands on Sunday, Manchester United’s fans showed their deep affection for the former midfielder. The five-time Premier League champion was enthusiastically serenaded while the players and executives were viciously booed. There were explicit chants aimed at co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, majority shareholders the Glazer family as well as technical director Jason Wilcox. “Sell United and f--- off home,” was the refrain most heartily belted out.

This clear public show of faith in Carrick “did not go unnoticed” by those who weren’t given the same luxury, ESPN report. At a time of great toxicity, having a figurehead who is actually liked by the fans is no bad thing. Quite how Carrick may feel about being reduced to the role of a distracting mascot remains to be seen.

While the fans may support their beleaguered manager, the playing squad is more divided. Bruno Fernandes has already made his stance on Carrick’s suitability abundantly clear, but there is support for the Englishman. Senne Lammens offered his public backing before the Bournemouth defeat, making a point later echoed by Harry Maguire. “We’re fully behind Michael,” the center back declared. “As individuals, we’re not playing well enough.”

Eddie Howe is the leading contender. / David Davies/PA Images/Getty ImagesWilcox is billed by The Guardian as the driving force behind the decision to keep Carrick, however temporarily. The same technical director is also thought to be leading the case for Eddie Howe as his potential successor. It’s not yet clear whether Carrick’s tenure has been elongated to simply bridge the gap before the former Newcastle United manager can be officially acquired.

Howe is expected to cost £3 million ($4 million) after striking an agreement over future compensation with the Magpies during his summer exit. The delay could allow time for negotiations over the terms of his potential arrival but it’s come at an awkward time in the calendar.

Thanks to an earlier embarrassment this season, United are not involved in the Carabao Cup this midweek, giving the club’s hierarchy five clear days to make the managerial switch. This luxury is fleetingly rare in the modern sport; three days after traveling to Chelsea, United host Roma in the Champions League before a Premier League clash with Aston Villa that weekend.
The November international break which runs for the following fortnight could present United with a more inviting window.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (center) has already made some questionable managerial decisions. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesAt the end of what many had expected to be Carrick’s final press conference as Manchester United manager, he was asked why the club are facing the same struggles once again. “If I really had the answers, I wouldn’t have let it happen,” he shot back.
“If I could do something about it and there was something that I could really control, then I would’ve tried to do everything I can to not be in this position.”

Carrick is completely right: United’s overriding malaise is not in his control. The rot began when the Glazers conducted a leveraged buyout of the club in 2005, immediately plunging the institution into a negative financial spiral which has only accelerated since. United are more than $1.5 billion in debt and owe almost $500 million in outstanding transfer fees. According to Ratcliffe, the club was on the cusp of running out of any cash flow before he made sweeping cuts across all departments.

This financial strain has been compounded by more than a decade of sporting incompetence. Even after actually stumbling upon some signings of promise—the summer 2025 window which brought in Lammens, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Šeško was the most successful in decades—the Carrick is counting the cost of past mistakes.

Carrick’s tactics can be (and have been) questioned but he can only do so much with the tools at his disposal. After failing to sign a new left back this summer, Diogo Dalot was left to line up on his unnatural flank against Bournemouth, veering around the pitch like a broken dodgem. The desperately underwhelming 27-year-old has a contract until 2028—with the option for an extra year.

United’s players may still be playing for Carrick after Saturday’s trip to Stamford Bridge but, in the grand scheme of things, it’s almost irrelevant. For any real change to happen, there has to be root and branch reform from the top down. Unfortunately, that can only be enacted by those failing figures in positions of powers. It’s a lot more appealing getting rid of one person, however likeable, than doing yourself out of a job.

ftbpro_01m5yv91ft56.title: ‘Extremely Small’—How Close Mbappe, Yamal Came to Beating Kane to 2026 Ballon d’Or
ftbpro_01m5yv91ft56.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer11:00 AM EDTHarry Kane emerged victorious on Monday night. / Rasid Necati Aslim/Anadolu/Getty Images (Mbappé), FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images (Kane), Karwai Tang/WireImage/Getty Images (Yamal)France Football will publish the detailed 2026 Ballon d’Or vote results on Saturday, but it has already been teased by the magazine’s editor-in-chief that this was a closer battle between the top three than perhaps anyone even realized.
In truth, this always felt like the most open race in years. Harry Kane collected the famous golden trophy, breaking a 25-year absence of an English winner in the process.

He was a deserving recipient because of his goalscoring feats for Bayern Munich and England over the course of the 2025–26 season. But there were equally compelling arguments to be made for Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal, who finished second and third respectively.

The jury, consisting of one journalist from each of FIFA’s top 100 ranked nations, was initially backing Mbappé when the first votes were cast, France Football’s Vincent Garcia told sister publication L’Équipe following the ceremony.
Mbappé, he said, was “ahead in the race for most of the voting period.” But Kane then “came back strongly” to clinch the accolade instead.
“The gap in points between Kane and Mbappé is extremely small,” Garcia added, “even less than the gap between Rodri and Vinícius [Júnior] in 2024, which amounted to 41 points.”

That year, Rodri took the crown with 1,170 points, with Vinícius Jr on 1,129. Jude Bellingham was third with 917, before there was a sharp drop for the rest of the top 10. In 2025, Ousmane Dembélé was a much clearer winner, emerging with 1,380 points, over 300 more than Yamal in second place. This system of voting has been in place since 2016, after the Ballon d’Or split with FIFA and voting returned to the control of France Football, as it previously was from 1956–2008.

But it’s hard to compare winning points margins any further back than 2024 because of an adjustment to the voting. In 2023 and earlier, the jury would choose a top five from the 30-strong shortlist, awarding their first pick six points, down to one point for their fifth. Starting in 2024, the jury has been asked to select a top 10, with 15 points going to their each voter’s top selection, down to one for their 10th. It means more points and higher tallies.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

Lamine Yamal won another Kopa Trophy but ended up third in the main prize. / Gareth Cattermole/Getty ImagesThere were more Spanish players (6) in the 30-strong shortlist than any other nationality. What’s more, all six finished inside the top 18. In comparison, France had five nominees, but two (Dayot Upamecano and William Saliba) placed in the bottom five.

Garcia has a theory that because of Spain’s successes—particularly as a team unit—Lamine Yamal lost points that might otherwise have gone his way. The vote for Spanish players may have ended being split and the veteran journalist believes that Rodri, who finished fourth—one place behind the teenager winger, was the main culprit.
“I honestly believe that Rodri deprived Lamine of some votes,” Garcia theorized.
“In the World Cup-winning Spanish national team, there was a clear split in votes between Rodri and Lamine Yamal, and this split cost them a great deal.

“There was a great dispersal of votes among the Spanish players, and more importantly, the Spanish national team was a complete side and an astonishing collective machine. That is why it was almost impossible for the members of the jury to single out and favour one specific individual performance.”

ftbpro_01m5yyn9nn2n.title: Kylian Mbappe’s Ballon d’Or Snub Compounded by Wild ‘Dictator’ Fiasco
ftbpro_01m5yyn9nn2n.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom2:30 PM EDTKylian Mbappé has endured a testing 24 hours. / Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press/Getty ImagesWhen Kylian Mbappé descended upon the London Palladium for Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony, he could scarcely have imagined that his first public comments after the event would be a groveling apology to “the Chinese people and their history.”

A matter of hours after Harry Kane was crowned the best men’s soccer player on the planet, Mbappé was forced to address a wave of controversy which could have major reputational and financial implications for himself, Real Madrid and La Liga at large.

Back in April, while appearing on The Bridge, a show hosted by his compatriot Aurélien Tchouaméni, Mbappé was quizzed on his favorite internet meme featuring himself. “The one where I laughed the hardest was when they put up a video of some guy,” the French striker smiled. “I think it was a Chinese dictator.”

No name was mentioned but the edited clip produced an image of Mbappé mocked up as Mao Zedong, an original member of the Chinese Communist Party who founded the People’s Republic of China in 1949. He would lead the nation until his death in 1976.
姆巴佩称毛泽东为“中国独裁者”原视频+中英翻译 pic.twitter.com/A99iyoue0D

Criticizing a figure as prominent, if controversial, as Mao was not well received in China after the clip—initially released in April—was re-circulated over recent days. Amid strong backlash on social media, the foreign ministry released a stern statement: “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.”
Mbappé took to social media to offer his contrition. “During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself,” he wrote in a statement written in French, Chinese and English.

“My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”

Kylian Mbappé was a common sight in China during the World Cup. / Wang HE/Getty ImagesThe response to Mbappé’s comments was swift and potentially very costly as a stack of Chinese sponsors queued up to drop the French star.

Both Mengniu and beverage giant Dongpeng expressed “zero tolerance” for Mbappé’s remarks. The leading dairy manufacturer condemned “any words or actions that offend the feelings of the Chinese people,” while Dongpeng accused the striker of “offending national sentiments.”

Cheese maker Milkground promptly followed suit. Social platform RedNote felt compelled to stress that its relationship with the record World Cup scorer had expired more than 18 months ago and set about purging their platform of any related material.

Dior, Hublot and, most pertinently, On, have also removed any Mbappé content from the Chinese social media platform Weibo, per the Global Times. The Real Madrid superstar only recently announced the surprise decision to ditch Nike after a 20-year association for a lucrative new deal with On.
Mbappé is thought to make $30 million a year from various sponsorship deals, per Forbes. The same outlet describes China as a “major market” for On, which could now be closed to Mbappé.

Javier Tebas is no stranger to an explosive comment. / Arnold Jerocki/Sportel/Getty ImagesThe Chinese Football Association demanded an apology from Real Madrid, adding: “Internationally renowned athletes, in particular, should strictly adhere to ethical standards, speak rationally and cherish their public influence.”

The Chinese state broadcaster, China Central Television (CCTV), has immediately suspended “broadcasts of matches involving La Liga and Mbappé,” as reported by local outlet The Paper. While the CCTV agreement was a short-term deal only stretching between 2024 and 2026, La Liga committed to a four-year exclusive partnership with Migu, another state-owned carrier.
It’s not clear how much investment La Liga stand to lose but the effusive apology delivered by the competition and its president Javier Tebas hints at the importance of the arrangement.

“La Liga deeply regrets the dissatisfaction and offense caused in China by the remarks made by Kylian Mbappé,” Tebas wrote on social media. “We understand the harm caused by these remarks. On behalf of La Liga, I extend our sincere apologies to the Chinese people.

“Over the years, we have built a relationship of mutual respect, trust, and cooperation with China and its government departments, sports organizations, audiovisual media institutions and millions of fans who love Spanish soccer.
“We cannot allow individual actions to damage this relationship, nor can we let more than 20 clubs in our professional competitions and millions of Chinese fans be adversely affected as a result.”

ftbpro_01m5z2d3wh47.title: Portugal Set to Make Unsurprising Decision About Cristiano Ronaldo Exile
ftbpro_01m5z2d3wh47.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer1:30 PM EDTThere isn’t much left of Cristiano Ronaldo on a soccer field. / Octavio Passos/Getty ImagesCristiano Ronaldo’s international exile appears to already be over, reported in his native Portugal to be named on a preliminary roster for next month’s UEFA Nations League matches.

There were doubts as to whether Ronaldo would ever play for Portugal again after leaving the national team camp over a disagreement with manager Jorge Jesus regarding his involvement in September. His own sister even cast further uncertainty over his future.

For his part, Ronaldo at least admitted he was wrong to leave, despite blaming his manager for what happened, and the 41-year-old said he was ready to accept punishment for his behavior and put it behind him. Nobody expected the sanctions imposed by Portugal’s soccer federation to be so light.

Ronaldo was handed a 30-day suspension from the national team during a period in which there was no national team activity. He could have been suspended for up to six months, as per the federation’s disciplinary code, but was given the most lenient ban available.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

That suspension began in early October and helpfully concludes before the start of the November window. He was also fined €255 ($284.20)—you read that correct, two, five, five—which is worth about 40 seconds of his time based on his Al Nassr salary alone.

O Jogo writes that Ronaldo has been “pre-selected” for Jesus’s November roster, when Portugal faces Denmark and Wales to conclude the Nations League group phase. There is no indication of how many names on are that list in total, or how many might be cut. But Ronaldo being included at this stage strongly hints at being reintegrated at the first opportunity—naming him on the preliminary roster just to cut him would be unnecessarily antagonistic from Jesus.

CR7 is determined to make more history before leaving the sport for good. / Octavio Passos/Getty ImagesMany predicted the 2026 World Cup might be it for Ronaldo in a Portugal jersey—his other sister made that bold statement during the tournament, calling it his ‘last dance’ for the national team. But the former Manchester United and Real Madrid icon chose not to step back in the same way that Lionel Messi decided it was time to end his Argentina career.

Ronaldo has seen and done nearly everything in more than 24 years as a pro soccer player, rewriting the sport’s history along the way. The 2026–27 season is increasingly expected to be his last before complete retirement, teased by the player himself, but he is keen to mark it with a third Nations League success with Portugal after prior triumphs in 2018–19 and 2024–25.

Portugal has already clinched a quarterfinal berth after four straight wins in September and October. The two November fixtures are therefore meaningless from a competition standpoint, but can help Ronaldo in his other outstanding quest: becoming the first player to score 1,000 career goals. The quarterfinals are held in March 2027, with the semifinals and final to follow in June.

Ronaldo climbed to 981 goals when he scored for Al Nassr in an AFC Champions League Elite match against Neftchi Fargona from Uzbekistan on Oct. 12. He only needs 19 more to hit four figures, but the goals aren’t flowing as easily this season. It’s five in 12 appearances in total for club and country—and, at that rate of scoring, he will need all the help he can from extra games.

ftbpro_01m5z2vm0cse.title: Christian Pulisic May Be Finally Seeing a Major Breakthrough at AC Milan
ftbpro_01m5z2vm0cse.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach Lowy4:00 PM EDTChristian Pulisic is reportedly earning a contract extension. / Timothy Rogers/Getty ImagesWhisper it softly, but Christian Pulisic could be getting back to peak form at AC Milan, who is reportedly set to offer him a contract renewal in the coming days.

After a dismal second half of the 2025–26 season, followed by an inconspicuous display at the 2026 World Cup, Pulisic found himself still unable to inspire. He was unused substitute across the first three matches of the new Serie A season, not in peak form after suffering from a bone bruise and a micro-fracture in his lower leg this summer, a situation that left him deeply “upset”. But since assisting Diego Moreira’s goal off the bench in a come-from-behind 2–2 draw with Lazio last month, he has started in each of Milan’s last four Serie A matches.

Pulisic headed into the September-October international break full of confidence after breaking the deadlock in a 3–0 win against Lecce on Sept. 20, his first goal for Milan since December 2025. Being left off of U.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino’s roster for the team’s four fall friendlies may have been a blow to the ego, but it certainly seems like the extra rest has done him a world of good.

His most emphatic display thus far this season came on Sunday against Udinese. Pulisic opened scoring at Bluenergy Stadium just six minutes into the match, timing his run perfectly to meet Luka Modrić’s lofted free kick behind Udinese’s backline, controlling the ball with a brilliant first touch before slotting it past goalkeeper Maduka Okoye. He continued to jump down the hosts’ throats, creating the match’s joint-most chances (three) and taking the most touches in the opposition’s box (eight). Milan walked away with a 2–0 win, while Pulisic earned player of the match honors.
Although Pulisic certainly still has a way to go—yet to prove his worth on the European stage this season, things are looking up for “Captain America.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Pulisic dominated Udinese. / Timothy Rogers/Getty ImagesWith Pulisic heating up in form, it’s no surprise that Milan are now jumping to tie him to a new long-term deal.

His current contract expires in 2027, with an option to extend for an additional year; however, contract negotiations between both parties have been transpiring for a year and a half. According to Sky Sports Italia, Pulisic is now closing in on a deal that would see him earn €5 million ($5.5 million) per year, plus bonuses, until 2031, which is a significant raise compared to his current salary of €4 million ($4.4 million).

Pulisic has been able to achieve the best numbers of his entire career in Italy, racking up 44 goals and 28 assists in 141 appearances for Milan. In comparison, he had 19 goals and 26 assists in 127 appearances for Borussia Dortmund, followed by 26 goals and 21 assists in 145 appearances for Chelsea.

At 28 years old, Pulisic has finally found the main character energy that he always possessed at the USMNT level but desperately sought after in Germany and England. The Rossoneri fanbase has made him well aware of his importance, praising him as the club’s “Captain America”. More importantly, though, American owner Gerry Cardinale and new Portuguese manager Ruben Amorim regard him as integral to the team’s long-term success.

“Pulisic is a really talented player. He is perfect for the way I think about football,” Amorim said during preseason. “I know the strengths of Pulisic; he will be supported in our club. I know he had some criticism after the World Cup elimination, but I am here to say we believe a lot in him, have a clear plan to use all the qualities that he has, so I can say to you that Pulisic is really important for us.”

Pulisic has already represented three of the biggest clubs in European football, but if there’s one thing that he’s been lacking, it’s consistency in a manager. Since the start of 2022–23 season, he has played under Thomas Tuchel, Bruno Saltor, Frank Lampard, Stefano Pioli, Paulo Fonseca, Sérgio Conceição, Massimiliano Allegri and now Amorim. Can he finally find consistency with Amorim and reach his world-class potential at the San Siro?

ftbpro_01m5z6ar7z41.title: Man City vs. Brighton: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
ftbpro_01m5z6ar7z41.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 27, 2026Manchester City host Brighton on Wednesday. / Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Man City), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Brighton)Manchester City take on Brighton & Hove Albion in one of the most intriguing ties of the entire Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday.

Taken in isolation, a clash between the Premier League leaders and the division’s top scorers is always going to be appointment viewing; however, the cup tie gives an intriguing added dimension, thanks to the fixture list. The two sides are up against each other, again at the Etihad, as soon as Saturday.

Brighton will stay in Manchester for the week, “recovering, adjusting, adapting” to use the mantra set forth by manager Fabian Hürzeler. Enzo Maresca has promised a similarly flexible approach for City, who could spice things up even more with some unpredictable rotation.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Erling Haaland and Co. might fall prey to the Seagulls.  / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesBoth City and Brighton bounded into last weekend’s round of Premier League fixtures on a high. Maresca had won all seven top-flight matches, setting a new record in the process, while the Seagulls were soaring after four league wins by an aggregate score of 15–0. Both would have their bubbles burst despite not playing all that badly.

Maresca was left to curse two individual errors in Saturday’s defeat to Aston Villa. Hürzeler’s only criticism was for Liverpool’s pragmatic approach, pointing toward his side’s far superior statistics from an even encounter not reflected in the 2–0 scoreline.

These are two well-coached teams who are likely to produce a very entertaining encounter. Yet, the game could boil down to a matter of priorities. Brighton’s German coach has described the cup tie as “do-or-die” while Maresca shrugged it off as an option for some rotation. If both manager’s live up to their preview, the visitors could deliver another City loss.

Maresca’s team selection may very well have been made over the weekend. The Italian tactician gave five of his key first-team starters three days off so that they would “come back full energy and we go again.” How many of Erling Haaland, Rúben Dias, Joško Gvardiol, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Marc Guéhi start in midweek remains unclear.

Donnarumma is definitely on the bench, with cup goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli confirmed of a starting berth. Maresca defended Guéhi, who has been beset by a poor run of form since the charges against Manchester City were announced curiously enough, but may give his center back some respite.
Matheus Nunes is one of the few injury doubts alongside Antoine Semenyo, who will be sidelined for at least another seven weeks.
Man City predicted lineup vs. Brighton (4-2-3-1): Rulli; Lewis, Khusanov, Dias, Aït-Nouri; Bouaddi, Anderson; Ndiaye, O’Reilly, Doku; Foden.

It’s a mixed bag on the injury front for Brighton. Hürzeler has been mightily boosted by the return of Mats Wieffer and, for the first time this season, Yankuba Minteh, who are both set to travel with the squad. Whether either makes the starting XI is less clear.
Those returnees are balanced by doubts over Chema Andrés and Ferdi Kadıoğlu. The pair both suffered “very painful” during Sunday’s loss to Liverpool but remain in contention to feature against City.
Pascal Struijk and Kaoru Mitoma aren’t available.
Brighton predicted lineup vs. Man City (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Costinha, Vušković, Dunk, Boscagli; Groß, Hinshelwood; Gómez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas.

ftbpro_01m5z8pvceja.title: ‘We Will Miss Him’—Xabi Alonso Reveals Concerning Joao Pedro Injury Diagnosis
ftbpro_01m5z8pvceja.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie SpencerOct 27, 2026João Pedro looks set to miss at least three Chelsea matches. / Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport/Getty ImagesJoão Pedro’s importance for Chelsea is obvious. The guy found the net 23 times in all competitions in his first 12 months at the club, with assists taking that tally of tangible goal contributions to 32. So far in 2026–27, it’s eight goals and assists in seven games.

Chelsea had already lost without scoring against Brentford last month when Pedro was missing for the London derby with a knee injury. So, when he was unexpectedly absent from Xabi Alonso’s teamsheet this past Saturday against Tottenham Hotspur, the Blues struggled again.

If anything, not playing serves to underline just how important Pedro is. It’s not that Chelsea don’t have another consistent goalscorer—Cole Palmer is the next most prolific since the start of last season on 15 goals across all competitions. It’s just that Pedro serves to knit everything together.

That is something Morgan Rogers struggled to do leading the line as a No. 9 against Tottenham, removed from his favored inside forward position on the left. Danny Welbeck was brought in to offer occasional relief, primarily in the domestic cups, not make regular starts. And we have yet to see Emmanuel Emegha because of injury. Nicolas Jackson is in top form … but for Aston Villa.
Chelsea don’t function right without Pedro in the team, so losing him for any length of time is going to be a big, big problem.

“He is a key player. We will miss him,” Alonso told reporters on Tuesday, building up to the Carabao Cup tie against Liverpool. “But we will have to be ready to deal with the injury and to be competitive and to try to win games with the players that we have available.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Xabi Alonso explained the situation this week. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images“An injury in his thigh” was Alonso’s description of Pedro’s issue in that same press conference.

The former Brighton & Hove Albion star missed two games with a thigh problem during April of last season. Meanwhile, a hamstring injury saw him sidelined for almost two months while still a Seagulls player in the second half of the 2023–24 campaign. Pedro additionally suffered with his calf for around three weeks when playing for Watford in 2022–23.

These are occasional muscle issues rather than anything particularly worrying at this stage. He also isn’t someone who has missed a lot of games injured during his career to date. Transfermarkt estimates 28 games sat out in seven years as a pro.
If he starts to get more of the same kind of problems regularly, then it would obviously be of more concern in the long run.
A return before the November international break seems unlikely. / Steffan Bowen/Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThis particular injury is not a major problem, but it’s also not a very minor one either.

Alonso’s projection is “a few weeks sidelined,” although the Spaniard was reluctant to offer a more specific timeframe than that. “Let’s see how many [weeks] … We don’t want to predict that. But he will not be ready for the next games.”

That phrasing—“next games”—probably groups at least everything between now and the November international break, which begins following Chelsea’s Premier League encounter with Sunderland on Nov. 8. It means no Pedro, not only for the Carabao Cup tie this week against Liverpool, but for the league visit of Manchester United on Halloween as well.

Chelsea’s first match after the international break—Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Nov. 21—is just under four weeks away. Five weeks take the team past a trip to Nottingham Forest and up to the visit of Crystal Palace on Dec. 2. A Premier League match with Liverpool is just under six weeks from now, while the trip to Manchester City’s Etihad Stadium is seven weeks away on Dec. 12.

ftbpro_01m5zgwyx3j6.title: Arsenal Player Ratings vs. Fleetwood: Gunners’ Quadruple Dream Goes Up in Smoke
ftbpro_01m5zgwyx3j6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie SpencerOct 27, 2026Arsenal were beaten from 12 yards by an opponent 84 ranked places lower in the English soccer pyramid. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesArsenal are out of the Carabao Cup after a shock elimination at the hands of EFL League Two’s Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.

The Gunners floundered, failing to get the job done in 90 minutes after initially falling behind and finishing the contest with 10 players following Max Dowman’s first career red card. After ending 1–1 at regular time, they ultimately fell 5–3 in a penalty shootout that decided the fourth-round tie.

The Gunners should have felt a degree of comfort taking to the field at Highbury Stadium on England’s west coast, the venue sharing the name of Arsenal’s beloved home from 1913 until 2006. Fleetwood even play in red jerseys with white sleeves.

The match had to stop only a few minutes after kick off because of a drone being flown above the pitch. But Arsenal were unsurprisingly in control of the ball once the action did resume after the lengthy pause, and the visitors threatened without really putting Fleetwood in serious peril.

Then came the moment every Fleetwood fan dreamed of but probably doubted would become reality. There was nothing remarkable about the buildup, with Harrison Neal knocking the ball forward, and then Aaron Loupalo-Bi just using his strength to hold off 17-year-old Arsenal center back Marli Salmon and unleash a finish beneath stand-in goalkeeper Illan Meslier.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Arsenal never really looked like leveling the game until after halftime, when Martin Ødegaard was introduced and started asking more questions than his teammates had done.

The tide began to change, although there was nothing pretty about the 50th-minute equalizer from Viktor Gyökeres, getting enough on the ball after a cross from teenage debutant Ceadach O’Neill wasn’t dealt with by the Fleetwood defense.

Even then, Arsenal didn’t steamroll their opponent. Kai Havertz missed two excellent chances in the minutes that followed and the early second-half momentum slowed all too easily. Fleetwood looked like they would tire—it’s way more draining to play without possession—but continued to close spaces and fight for every ball.

It was a strong but ultimately fair challenge from Fleetwood’s Neal on Dowman that sparked the 16-year-old’s dismissal with five minutes of the 90 to play. There was no arm around the shoulder from Arteta as the academy gem trudged off the field towards the tunnel, instead receiving what appeared to be a few harsh words from the boss.
Arsenal tried to win it before the shootout, but goalkeeper Jay Lynch made two enormous saves in the final moments.

With no extra time, Fleetwood’s Ronan Coughlan began the shootout by converting with a Bruno Fernandes-esque hop. Ødegaard and Neal traded successes, before Havertz also found the net to make it 2–2 in the tiebreaker. Will Davies wasn’t fazed by the ball appearing to wobble on the spot in the wind, but neither was Gyökeres straight after. Andy Cannon restored Fleetwood’s lead, and then Bruno Guimarães wilted under the pressure, handing over match point. Conor Haughey took it.

Squad depth deserted Mikel Arteta when he needed it most. / Lewis Storey/Getty ImagesThe biggest of dreams is already over by the end of October. Arsenal were targeting an unprecedented quadruple, but where was the depth when it was needed?

Mikel Arteta gave the night off to the Gunners contingent who were at the Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday night. Even without them—Declan Rice, Gabriel, David Raya and the injured Bukayo Saka, it should not have been this hard.
Arsenal still started with seven internationals—with plenty more on the bench, a goalkeeper with 200 Premier League and Championship appearances and a generational teenager.

Fleetwood currently sit 18th in League Two, which makes them the 86th best team out of all 92 members of the Premier League and EFL. Arsenal are reigning English champions and are only off the top of the Premier League on goal difference.

Mikel Arteta’s ideal scenario for this match would have been his team comfortably leading, thereby allowing him to both protect his senior players and hand opportunities to emerging youngsters. In the end, he couldn’t risk using any of the kids on the bench, while none of the three teenagers who started the match finished it. The boss could have done with resting Martin Ødegaard, Ben White, Eberechi Eze, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa but was forced to use all five.
Jurriën Timber did not return for the second half. / Carl Recine/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Illan Meslier—6.2: A slightly surprising choice to start over Kepa Arrizabalaga when he hasn’t played a single competitive match in well over a year. Didn’t get close to a save in the shootout, allowing all five penalties to be scored.

RB: Jurriën Timber—6.5: Captained Arsenal for the first time but only lasted until halftime. He struggled, so it’s hard to say if it was in response to that or pre-planned given how his minutes have also been carefully managed this season.

ftbpro_01m5zmjpkvja.title: Cavan Sullivan Injury: Progress, Potential Return Date for USMNT Wonderkid
ftbpro_01m5zmjpkvja.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 27, 2026Cavan Sullivan won’t feature in Wednesday’s match. / Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCavan Sullivan will miss his second consecutive match this week due to injury, putting worry into American fans just weeks away from the U.S. men’s national team’s November camp.

Still fighting for a playoff spot, the Philadelphia Union trek to Geodis Park to clash with Nashville SC on Wednesday night. As if battling the league’s strongest team and recently crowned Supporters’ Shield winners wasn’t hard enough, the Union will have to manage without their brightest star, who was ruled out on Tuesday evening.

Sullivan has lit up MLS ever since interim manager Ryan Richter came in this summer and gave the 17-year-old winger a real chance. Seven goals and 14 assists later, the youngster has proven himself as a legend in the making and the future of American soccer.

He beat out the likes of Lionel Messi for the MLS Player of the Month for September and even became the youngest USMNT goalscorer in history in his debut camp under manager Mauricio Pochettino earlier this month.

The teenager may be defying all odds, but he’s still a mere mortal. Richter will need him healthy for the Union’s playoff push, and Pochettino will need him at full strength in order to name him for the upcoming Concacaf Nations League matches.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Sullivan suffered an ankle injury on Oct. 17. /  Isaiah Vazquez/MLS/Getty ImagesSullivan suffered an ankle injury on Oct. 17 in the 2–2 draw with Charlotte FC. Although the fiery teenager managed to fight through the pain and see out all 90 minutes, the injury has kept him out of match play ever since.

Richter had expected Sullivan to be available for the weekend’s bout with the New England Revolution, stating last Thursday: “He’s all good. He took a knock in the game on Saturday against Charlotte, and we’re just trying to manage that through this week. But he should be available for Saturday. He was out on the field today, but like I said, just managing that through the week and trying to get him so that he’s at his best for this weekend.”

Sullivan, however, was listed unavailable by Friday evening, and the teenager was helpless as his team suffered its first loss in 16 league matches, snapping an undefeated streak that dated all the way back to May.
The sixth-ranked Union fell 2–1 to the second-ranked Revs, and now Sullivan will miss the battle with first-ranked Nashville.

Sullivan helped the USMNT defeat bitter rival Mexico earlier this month. /  Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesIt is still uncertain how long Sullivan will remain sidelined; however, considering Richter regarded him as “questionable” in Monday’s press conference, it is likely that he is at least somewhat on the mend.

What remains to be seen is whether or not he can recover in time for the next international window, for which Pochettino is expected to name his roster sometime next week. The Stars and Stripes will convene on Nov. 9, ahead of two-consecutive matches against Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, their first competitive fixtures since the 2026 World Cup.
Sullivan will be eager to continue making a name for himself on the global stage, and Pochettino will certainly want to discover if he really is the future of the USMNT.

ftbpro_01m60w53swrd.title: ‘We Discussed’—Arteta Explains Angry Outburst at Dowman After Red Card
ftbpro_01m60w53swrd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:00 AM EDTMax Dowman (left) did not receive an arm around the shoulder from Mikel Arteta. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesThere was no arm around the shoulder, no consolatory word in the ear from Mikel Arteta for Max Dowman after Arsenal’s literal child received the first red card of his senior career in Tuesday’s humiliating Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

Instead, Arsenal’s manager kept his arms firmly crossed, cocking his head in the direction of the teenager before barking out a few choice words. “It’s something that we discussed before the game,” Arteta seethed by way of explanation for what he had said.

It had been a frustrating evening for all the visitors. After tumbling 1–0 down in the first half to a goal cheaply given away by fellow teenager Marli Salmon, Arsenal spent the rest of the contest raining down attacks on Fleetwood’s precariously guarded net, racking up 26 shots, with seven on target.

Dowman was involved in some of the most glaring misses, scuffing one clear opening across goal in the first half before teeing up Kai Havertz for a glorious chance which the ephemeral German conspired to squander.

Beyond his own wastefulness, Dowman was riled by a robust physical approach throughout the contest. Referee Michael Salisbury only whistled for one foul on the winger, which no doubt added to his frustrations, and that came in the 85th minute, with the score locked at 1–1.

Max Dowman gave in to the confrontation. / X/Sky Sports FootballHarrison Neal leaped into a full-blooded lunge by the touchline, scissoring the teenager’s standing leg. Dowman reacted, kicking out at the midfielder amid an almighty scrum of bodies. By the time the crowd dispersed, the referee was on the scene to brandish a red card.

As Dowman trudged down the tunnel, the jeers from a sell-out home crowd were bolstered by Arteta’s shouting. “We know when we prepare the context of the match, we’re very clear on what to expect,” the manager curtly added. “Emotionally, we have to dominate, but we’re very clear.”
While Arteta’s verbal parry was a consequence of the moment, its roots go a lot deeper.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER
Much like his player, Mikel Arteta (left) didn’t keep his emotions in check. / Carl Recine/Getty Images“Emotional dominance” has been a key talking point for Arteta this season.

Arsenal’s success under the details-obsessed coach has been defined by doing the simple things well. Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor tellingly hailed the Gunners as “the best team in the country, the most organized team in the country, the best at the basics.” Keeping your emotions in check is one of the basics that Arteta has focused on lately.
“We have to be emotionally dominant regardless of what the context is. It’s easy to say, very difficult actually to do,” the Basque boss explained earlier this month.

“It’s owning the moment, leading that moment and making sure that we are in the emotional state that the game requires and not something else,” Arteta added. “If the game requires a reaction, energy and spirit, a boldness, a courage to deliver something else or change it, that’s the way we have to act.
“If the game demands everybody to bring the temperature down, we have to be able to do that. In order to do that, we need to really understand what is happening.”

Max Dowman collected his first red card for Arsenal, but not the first ever. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesThis was Dowman’s first red card for Arsenal but his second dismissal of the month. The England U-19 international was dismissed in the second half of a 2–1 win over the U.S. during a behind-closed-doors friendly.

The official explanation for his red card was not provided, but the Daily Mail report that it was for “a little kick out when a player went past him.” Much like his exit against Fleetwood, that international red was described as “on the harsh side.”

Two events in entirely different circumstances does not make a trend, but this will not be the last time that Dowman is on the end of physical intimidation. At 16, he’ll have plenty of time to learn the art of managing his emotions—as Arteta proved with his own outburst, even 44-year-olds can let the heat of the moment get the better of them.

ftbpro_01m60wa09x3x.title: ‘Opportunity’—Liverpool & Chelsea Look to Pounce on Arsenal’s Carabao Cup Humiliation
ftbpro_01m60wa09x3x.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott7:30 AM EDTThe door has been opened to both Liverpool and Chelsea. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Iraola), Peksi Cahyo/Getty Images (Alonso)When Liverpool and Chelsea started preparing for the 2026–27 season, both teams will have been particularly interested in the Carabao Cup.

Neither team will genuinely see themselves as Premier League title contenders—not in an era of Arsenal’s ruthlessness and Manchester City’s efficiency—but both will still believe they have the chance to end the season with silverware in the wild west that is cup soccer.

The season may well only be two months old, but we can safely say the Carabao Cup and FA Cup are likely to be the main source of hope for Liverpool and Chelsea, but one team’s journey in the former is set to come to a brutal end on Wednesday when the pair face off in the Carabao Cup fourth round at Anfield.

With Arsenal no longer a threat following their stunning defeat to League Two strugglers Fleetwood Town on Tuesday, victory has become even more important for both Liverpool and Chelsea as they seek to take one step closer to lifting a trophy this year.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Arsenal are no longer a threat. / Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty ImagesThe majority of the fourth round of the Carabao Cup has not even been played yet, but every team left in the competition will now be sensing a genuine chance of victory.

Aside from Newcastle United’s triumph in 2025, the Carabao Cup has been won by a member of England’s “Big Six” in every year since 2013. Since Leicester City’s triumph in 2000, there have only been a further five winners not named Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United or Tottenham Hotspur.

Even at this early stage of the competition, we have already lost three of those teams. Man Utd and Tottenham both crashed out in the third round, and Arsenal are now going to be watching the rest of the tournament from home.
One more is guaranteed to drop out on Wednesday when Liverpool host Chelsea, meaning the quarterfinals and beyond will be played with no more than two of the Big Six.

The door has been blown open here for either Liverpool or Chelsea to take advantage, safe in the knowledge that they should, on paper, be the second-best team left in the competition at the very least. Man City, first in the Premier League, take on third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion in their own fourth-round clash on Wednesday, eliminating another of England’s biggest threats in the process.

Chances to win silverware are not handed out on a plate, but the 2026–27 Carabao Cup truly seems to be an open fight. Man City may well still be the strongest contender, but the unpredictable nature of cup soccer means they are far from guaranteed to seal a 10th triumph in this competition come the summer.

Andoni Iraola is chasing silverware in his debut season. / Shaun Brooks - CameraSport/Getty ImagesOf the four trophies available to Liverpool this season, it is hardly controversial to suggest the Carabao Cup is the least glamorous in a group that also includes the FA Cup, Premier League and Champions League.

We have seen plenty of teams over the years disregard this competition, but Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola clearly knows his best chance of winning a trophy in his debut year at Anfield may well have just been presented to him.
“I think every competition is an opportunity, especially when you are the coach of Liverpool,” Iraola admitted. “You have to take it like this.

“I would love to win [against Chelsea] and have the chance to get further in the competition. But I know that we have to play very well, we have to beat a very good team. It’s also a team that doesn’t play in Europe, so for sure for them this competition is also very important. So, it’s not going to be easy.”

ftbpro_01m611kwesky.title: Forgotten Chelsea Signing Ready to Replace Injured Joao Pedro
ftbpro_01m611kwesky.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:30 AM EDTEmmanuel Emegha has had to remain patient. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesXabi Alonso’s admission that Chelsea are set to be without injured striker João Pedro for “a few weeks” triggered alarm bells across the fanbase.

The Brazilian, who has five goals and three assists in seven appearances so far this season, missed the 2–0 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur because of a knee problem. It was the second game he has missed this season, the other being the 3–0 loss to Brentford. Those are the only two matches so far in which Alonso’s side have failed to score.
With that in mind, Chelsea fans would appear justifiably concerned as they head into a tough run of fixtures without their attacking talisman, but one man is looking to change that: Emmanuel Emegha.

Emegha’s work has all come behind the scenes. / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesIt was over a year ago that Chelsea announced the acquisition of Emegha to make him, at the time, the second player to make the move from Strasbourg since BlueCo’s acquisition of the French side.

Emegha finished the season with Strasbourg before heading to Chelsea in the summer. Left out of the Netherlands squad for the World Cup, he was among the first to work with Alonso and caught the eye during preseason, scoring in a handful of behind-closed-doors friendlies that fans did not get the privilege of watching.
By the time the squad hopped on a plane for their tour of Australia and Asia, however, Emegha was nowhere to be found as an injury forced him to miss out. The 23-year-old has not been seen since.
That could soon be about to change, with Alonso confirming Emegha will be “in the squad” for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup fourth-round clash with Liverpool.
“It's important that we have him available because he has special qualities,” Alonso said. “He has to feel fully fit.

“He’s been training for the last couple of weeks, 10 days, in a good way that allows him to build a strong base for his fitness and now gradually we want to see him and maybe [against Liverpool] he has the chance to play.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Emegha scored 31 goals in 78 games for Strasbourg. / Catherine Steenkeste - UEFA/Getty ImagesThe first thing fans will notice about Emegha is his physique. He stands at 6'5" but is far from a typical target man and leans more towards the likes of Erling Haaland or Alexander Isak with his combination of height and agility.

Movement is a key part of Emegha’s game. He makes excellent runs into the box and in behind defensive lines, begging for teammates to find him. His goals are rarely spectacular because they rarely need to be.

A two-footed threat, Emegha came into his own in the 2024–25 season when, under the guidance of Liam Rosenior, he struck 14 goals in 27 Ligue 1 appearances. Only five players in the division scored more, all of whom played more games.

Links to the Premier League surfaced that summer and cynics have suggested the only reason he was signed by Chelsea was to stop him joining a domestic rival instead. Newcastle United were strongly credited with interest on their search to replace Isak, adding the Dutchman to a shortlist that also included Benjamin Šeško, Hugo Ekitiké and Nick Woltemade. Clearly, they had a specific type of striker in mind.
Next. Best Chelsea Players Ever. The 25 Best Chelsea Players of All Time—Ranked. dark

Injury problems have plagued Emegha ever since his move to Chelsea was announced, restricting him to just four Ligue 1 starts last season. He did, however, still manage to contribute four goals before saying goodbye.

Emegha is, clearly, a different kind of striker to Pedro, who uses a telepathic understanding with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers to produce some devastating link-up play. Emegha is far less of a creator and will hope those around him can do the heavy lifting in that regard.

If Chelsea’s playmakers can figure out how to work alongside Emegha, in the same way that Diego Moreira and Dilane Bakwa did at Strasbourg, the results could easily soften the blow of Pedro’s absence.

ftbpro_01m6153qqpyw.title: Jadon Sancho ‘Finalising’ Surprise Next Move After Getafe Offer
ftbpro_01m6153qqpyw.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott9:00 AM EDTJadon Sancho remains without a club. / Angel Martinez - UEFA/Getty ImagesJadon Sancho is reported to have turned down the option to sign for La Liga outfit Getafe, with a move to Saudi Arabia seemingly emerging as his priority.

Having been released by Manchester United in the summer after two underwhelming seasons out on loan with Chelsea and Aston Villa, Sancho received an offer from Getafe last week worth just 4% of what he was earning at Old Trafford.

According to MARCA, Sancho is still holding out for more money. The report claims he is asking for €3 million ($3.3 million) annually, which is seven-and-a-half times more than Getafe were prepared to pay. As a result, the deal has fallen through and is considered dead.

In search of those funds, Sancho is said to have received a lucrative offer from Saudi Arabia, and his representatives are now in talks over a switch to the Middle East. No specific team is mentioned.
Because he is currently out of contract, Sancho is free to sign with any team outside the transfer window, although some leagues do enforce restrictions as to when players can be registered.

Sancho last played for Aston Villa. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesSancho has been forced to keep himself fit away from a club ever since his departure from United this summer, but his agents continue to work on finding a new home for the 26-year-old.

talkSPORT state Sancho has even been offered to West Ham United in the Championship, with a handful of other English clubs alerted to his availability on a free transfer. Whether any will take up the offer is an entirely different question.

Earlier reports insisted Sancho recognizes the benefits of playing outside of England after five tough years at United, where he remained under an intense spotlight even during his loans with Chelsea and Villa.

Moving overseas has never been a concern for Sancho, who swapped Manchester City’s academy for Borussia Dortmund in 2017 and returned to the Bundesliga side on loan in January 2024. A similar switch would not bring the same sort of pressure that he faced playing in England.

At only 26 years old, Sancho still has plenty of time to rebuild his career. While matching the hysteria that surrounded him when he joined United in 2021 is likely to be impossible, he will hope to find a stable landing spot in which he can prove he still has something to offer at a high level.

ftbpro_01m618g16h0z.title: ‘A Problem’—Arteta Gives Worrying Rice Injury Update Before Huge Liverpool Clash
ftbpro_01m618g16h0z.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:00 AM EDTDeclan Rice’s absence would be a major blow for the Gunners. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesMikel Arteta revealed that Declan Rice was suffering with “a problem” which forced him off against Everton last weekend and may impact his availability for Sunday’s almighty clash with Liverpool at Anfield. The talismanic midfielder is hardly Arsenal’s only selection concern.

Rice was one of three first-team regulars who failed to even make the matchday roster for Tuesday’s humiliating humbling at the hands of Fleetwood Town. Riccardo Calafiori and Noni Madueke were also unavailable through injury.
“Riccardo was out, Noni was out with an ankle and Declan Rice finished with a problem the other day,” Arteta bluntly told Sky Sports after the club’s Carabao Cup exit was confirmed on penalties.

Riccardo Calafiori (left) and Noni Madueke are both injury doubts. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesArteta’s fitness updates are infamously unreliable. This is a figure who actively encouraged injured players to walk off the team coach into the locker room just “to put the other manager off the scent,” according to his former player Oleksandr Zinchenko.

In truth, Arteta himself may not be aware of the most accurate recovery timelines before any further scans can be conducted this week. There are, however, some names which can already be crossed off his selection list.

Bukayo Saka won’t be back for weeks. / Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND/AFP/Getty Images)Bukayo Saka joined William Saliba on the slate of long-term absentees after damaging his left quad in last week’s Champions League draw with Bayern Munich. The Arsenal academy graduate is set to be sidelined for at least six weeks, putting him out of action until the start of December at the very earliest.

Saliba’s personal calendar is not so clear. The center back is yet to feature this season since undergoing surgery on a persistent back problem which eventually got the better of him at this summer’s World Cup. Arteta has gushed about the “very, very positive” signs of his recovery but has been unwilling to offer even the suggestion of a return date. The end of November has been put forward as a vague target.

Arsenal’s final major concern is Christos Tzolis. The exciting summer recruit sustained a thigh problem while on international duty with Greece in the fall, ruling him out for around three weeks. There is some hope that Tzolis could play some role on Sunday, but his status remains mired in uncertainty.

Max Dowman was shown his first Arsenal red card. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesMax Dowman won’t be able to win Arteta over with an appeal to the FA but Arsenal could secure the teenager’s availability by appealing his red card against Fleetwood.

The 16-year-old gave in to the frustrations of an infuriating night by kicking out at Harrison Neal. The force was minimal but still inspired a straight red card. There is no VAR at this stage of the Carabao Cup, so Michael Salisbury’s on-field decision could not be questioned in-game, which helps Arsenal’s case.

Dowman was found guilty of violent conduct, which the FA Handbook describes as “when a player uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball.”

This is ultimately a subjective decision and one which will be scrutinized by the appeals board. Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher was not optimistic about Arsenal’s case. “I think it will fail,” he told Sky Sports. “Because of the aggressiveness of Dowman, and you can see the intent.”

If Dowman is sidelined and Madueke can’t escape the treatment room already housing Saka, Arteta will be without a single senior right winger for the trip to Anfield. Tzolis, whose availability is also in doubt, could feasibly switch wings, while Kai Havertz may be forced out wide. Martin Ødegaard is another option, with his central position easily taken up by Mikel Merino.
