ftbpro_01m61bxhvstn.title: USMNT Stock Up, Stock Down: Christian Pulisic Turns Tides, Folarin Balogun’s Woes Worsen
ftbpro_01m61bxhvstn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely2:30 PM EDTChristian Pulisic (left) could be headed in the right direction, while Folarin Balogun has yet to find his way. / Giuseppe Cottini/AC Milan/Getty Images (Pulisic), NSJsport/Getty ImagesThe stars of the U.S. men’s national team had quite the week worldwide. Seven found the back of the net, while others anchored their squads for massive wins.

It’s a welcomed problem for USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino, whose job of naming a roster for the upcoming Concacaf Nations League action just became that much harder. The Argentine boss is taking notes, certainly scribbling down who is exceeding expectations and who is coming up short. He is anticipated to name his squad next week, determining those best suited to overcome Haiti in the tournament’s quarterfinals.
Here is Sports Illustrated’s weekly stock up, stock down analysis for USMNT players.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

WESTON MCKENNIE GETS JUVENTUS ROLLING! 🇺🇸⚪️⚫️️The American midfielder gets his first goal of the campaign to put Juventus in front away to Lecce 💥⚽️Watch Serie A on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/LNJnvbLTpq

Pochettino left Weston McKennie off of his fall roster last month, and although the USMNT still cruised to a perfect four wins in the star midfielder’s absence, Pochettino would be foolish to do it again.

The 28-year-old was the heartbeat of the Stars and Stripes’ midfield at the 2026 World Cup this summer and has been for several years. In the wake of the tournament, he has continued to flaunt his assets for club side Juventus.

McKennie had his first goal of the new season on Sunday, opening scoring against Serie A foe Lecce in the 29th minute. Tracking a free kick into the box, McKennie practically slid all the way into the goal mouth to see the ball through. Juventus left the Stadio Via del Mare with a 2–0 win and have lost just once in the last five league outings, all seeing significant contributions from McKennie.

Post-World Cup, Pochettino has been adamant to trial new, younger players in attempt to curate his perfect roster come the 2030 edition, prompting him to give opportunities to the likes of several midfielders, including Brooklyn Raines and Adri Mehmeti. Although newly named captain Tyler Adams can show those youngsters the ropes on the defensive side of the ball, they will need a player like McKennie to blueprint the creative flair that Pochettino so desires in the center of the pitch.
Pulisic could be returning to top form. / Timothy Rogers/Getty ImagesConsistency has not been Pulisic’s strong suit as of late, so perhaps take his recent progress with a grain of salt.

Nevertheless, a USMNT optimist will see the past week as a sign that Pulisic is successfully turning a corner. Now firmly re-established in AC Milan’s starting lineup (at least for Serie A matches), the 28-year-old attacker has grown more and more confident as the new season progresses.

He scored his second goal of the season on Sunday just six minutes into the league match against Udinese. He perfectly timed his run through the gap in the opponent’s backline in order to meet the end of a long ball from teammate Luka Modrić. A brilliant first touch settled the lofted ball and set up Pulisic for a damning finish.

Milan secured a 2–0 win on the road, and Pulisic was given Player of the Match honors. To compound an exciting weekend, he is reportedly now in the advanced stages of contract negotiations with the Rossoneri, a renewal that would see him earn a significant pay raise.
Is Pochettino paying close attention, or has the manager firmly written off “Captain America?”

Johnny Cardoso suffered another injury setback. / Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/Getty ImagesJohnny Cardoso simply can’t catch a break. After missing out on the 2026 World Cup due to injury, the star midfielder is sidelined once again with an ailment that could leave him out of Pochettino’s future plans.

The 25-year-old suffered a muscular injury in his thigh last week, experiencing discomfort in Atlético Madrid’s Champions League clash with Stuttgart on Oct. 20. He then missed Saturday’s La Liga bout with Deportivo A Coruña.

The setback is a massive blow when considering the success Cardoso was experiencing on the pitch. He played a pivotal role in the team’s recent wins over Manchester United and Real Madrid, clocking 90 minutes in the midfield during both affairs.

Although his recovery timeline is reported to be less than a few weeks—Atléti labelled his injury as “low grade,” he remained absent from Wednesday’s team training and may not return to fitness in time to be considered for Pochettino’s November roster.
Cardoso has not featured for the USMNT since March, missing the summer’s grand affair after undergoing ankle surgery just weeks before group stage play.

ftbpro_01m61dfdw756.title: Barcelona Hit Back at ‘Laughable’ Julian Alvarez Fine
ftbpro_01m61dfdw756.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:15 PM EDTJulián Alvarez (left) can’t escape Barcelona’s melodrama. / Angel Martinez/Getty Images (Alvarez), James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images (badge)Barcelona are reportedly refusing to pay a pitifully modest €602 ($670) fine for making an allegedly illegal transfer approach for Atlético Madrid striker Julián Alvarez as a matter of “principle.”

Alvarez found himself at the center of this summer’s most tumultuous transfer saga. Reports of Barcelona opening talks to sign Alvarez as early as May were publicly condemned by Atlético, whose official social media accounts retaliated with hoax posts about bids for Lamine Yamal, Pedri and Raphinha.

There was an oddly cordial and quickly forgotten bid from Real Madrid before Alvarez went public with his “dream” to leave the Spanish capital during the World Cup. Barcelona president Joan Laporta confirmed that an offer had been lodged while accusing his rivals of being “inflexible.”
This stubborn resolve would hold throughout the summer. Alvarez remains an Atlético Madrid player but the saga with Barcelona is still ongoing.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Julián Alvarez kickstarted this mess at the World Cup. / Maja Hitij/FIFA/Getty ImagesBarcelona have been accused—and found guilty—of approaching Alvarez without informing his current employers of their intentions, as per the Spanish soccer federation (RFEF).
This “failure to comply with orders, instructions, agreements, or regulatory obligations” carries a maximum fine of €602, which has been sent the club’s way.

“I don’t see the logic behind this,” Laporta scoffed when news of the complaint first surfaced. “All of Atlético’s representatives are very experienced, and I don’t know what their strategy is. They have our offer. If they want to accept, we’d be delighted.

“Atlético is being completely inflexible, and I hope they’ll change their minds and accept. If they don’t, they should say so, and we’ll see. But taking it to UEFA, FIFA ... I don’t know what the point is. Maybe there are people looking to stir things up. it doesn’t make sense.”

Joan Laporta is a wily operator. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesBarcelona would have no difficulty paying the fine. The club bragged about record revenues of €1.06 billion ($1.18 billion) this year. At that rate, it would take just 18 seconds to pay a fine which has been categorized by those inside the club as “laughable,” according to MARCA.

The same report states that the club have rejected the fine on “moral and conceptual grounds” and are confident in their appeal as they maintain that their “conduct was appropriate.” Atlético were supposedly “explicitly informed of [Barcelona’s] interest in the forward.”

Barça would have made their case when Atlético first launched their complaint and there is no suggestion that new evidence is about to come forward. RFEF clearly deemed the club’s indiscretion to be “minor” considering that only a fine was handed out; the governing body could also have suspended the club from playing or forced a closure of the stadium. Yet, whether they will completely remove any punishment entirely is another matter.

Things are looking up for Julián Alvarez. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesAlvarez has already tried to turn over a new leaf. The beleaguered forward was a shadow of his former self at the start of the season, visibly wilting under the weight of boos from a home crowd unimpressed by his very public desire to leave.

Bolstered by the constant backing of his manager Diego Simeone, Alvarez has belatedly rediscovered some of his old form. After scoring his second goal of the week on Saturday against Deportivo A Coruña, the Argentina international apologized for his comments for the first time.

This U-turn came shortly after a change in representation from Alvarez, who has now signed up with Pablo Barquero. While Atlético fans could take this as a positive sign, it’s not gone unnoticed that one of the few other clients on Barquero’s roster is a certain Rodri, who made the move to Barcelona just last summer.

ftbpro_01m61ez68bj8.title: ‘My Time’—Lamine Yamal Makes Ballon d’Or Vow in Defiant Statement
ftbpro_01m61ez68bj8.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:00 PM EDTLamine Yamal came third in Monday’s Ballon d’Or.  / Li Ying/Xinhua/Getty ImagesLamine Yamal has refused to let Monday’s Ballon d’Or disappointment dent his confidence, insisting his “time will come” to win soccer’s most coveted individual honor.

The Barcelona superstar was among three leading candidates for the award in one of the most open races in recent memory, but he eventually finished third behind Kylian Mbappé and first-time winner Harry Kane.
Yamal didn’t leave the ceremony empty-handed, clinching his third successive Kopa Trophy in London, but the 19-year-old will have to wait for the game’s most illustrious prize.
Following a frustrating career setback, Yamal has now responded to his Ballon d’Or snub on Instagram.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
“IT WILL COME,” the teenager wrote in capital letters. “Good things take time, I trust the path I’m building. Without a hurry, with excitement and with tranquility that someday my time will come.
“Congratulations to the winners, my focus is again on what’s important, to make FC Barcelona win again.”

Yamal would have been the youngest winner in Ballon d’Or history, with the record currently held by former Barcelona and Brazil striker Ronaldo, and that’s a feat he can still achieve by winning the 2027 award.
After two close calls—Yamal finished second in 2025—there’s nothing preventing him from scooping the Ballon d’Or next year.

Yamal would have been a worthy winner—but so was Kane. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWhile Yamal showed humility in defeat during yet more Ballon d’Or heartbreak, the player’s uncle, Abdul, was incandescent with rage as he slammed the decision to reward Kane with the trophy.
“My nephew was superb. He is the best player in the world, everyone knows that,” Yamal’s uncle told Cadena SER. “If you are a football fan, you must watch Lamine, not Harry Kane.
“The Englishman is a skillful striker, yes, but my nephew is the best player because of his striking brilliance on the pitch. He is the one who makes the difference.
“He did not win because Lamine is young, he is 19 years old, and he will win more. But Harry has only three days left on the pitch, and we gave him the award.
“He won the World Cup, La Liga and the Super Cup. He plays wonderfully, he had an amazing season, he scores goals no one else can score, passes, assists, everything.”

While Yamal enjoyed an undeniably excellent 2025–26 season for club and country, no unbiased onlooker can begrudge Kane the prize following a campaign in which he scored an astonishing 61 goals in 51 appearances for Bayern and won the domestic treble.
He also helped England to its best finish at the World Cup since winning the competition in 1966 by netting six times in just seven appearances at the tournament.

Yamal is currently the early front-runner for the 2027 Ballon d’Or, as per the betting odds, and has already made an excellent start to the current season with 20 goal involvements in just 13 outings for Barça.

ftbpro_01m61hz6718k.title: American Golden Boot Race: The USMNT Stars With the Most Club Goals This Season
ftbpro_01m61hz6718k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach LowyOct 28, 2026Cavan Sullivan (left), Julian Hall (center) and Sebastian Berhalter are dominating the domestic game. / Patrick Mulligan/USSF/Getty ImagesThe stars of the U.S. men’s national team are all too familiar with the back of the net.

American players across Major League Soccer have been scoring since February, given the 2026 season is now at its tail end, whereas those Americans overseas are only two months into the 2026–27 European season. Many of them have already opened their accounts, though, only adding to USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino’s selection headache for the upcoming international break.

Here, Sports Illustrated details all of the top American goal scorers of the various current club seasons, a running list that includes any player worldwide that has been rostered for the USMNT in the past 12 months and has scored at least one goal in their current club campaign. Although the MLS players have a significant head start on their teammates across the pond, it’s only a matter of time before those in Europe catch up.
Without further ado, let’s shed some light on the American Golden Boot race.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
GIVING US THE LEAD IN THE DERBY pic.twitter.com/gD8p2QH56h

It wasn’t long ago that Folarin Balogun was the USMNT’s undisputed starting striker after an impressive World Cup showing. But with Balogun out of AS Monaco’s starting XI following a failed Premier League transfer, the path is clearing for Julian Hall to assert himself as Pochettino’s favored No. 9.

He only turned 18 years old in March, but Hall has already racked up 14 goals and four assists in 33 appearances this season for New York Red Bulls. He has relegated a Champions League veteran in Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting to the bench, while he continues to make history. Two years after becoming the second-youngest scorer in MLS history, Hall became the youngest player to score a hat trick in MLS, getting three past Columbus Crew back in May.

It’s no surprise that both the U.S. and Poland have set their sights on the teenage forward, with Hall making his USMNT debut in last month’s friendlies. After becoming the third player to score in each of his first three USMNT matches, all signs point to him becoming officially cap-tied during November’s Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti.

Cavan Sullivan assists Bruno Damiani!Sullivan sets a new record for most goal contributions in a season by a teenager with 21 (and counting)! pic.twitter.com/JOmCDuVwi0

When Ryan Richter took charge on May 27, Philadelphia Union had the worst record in MLS. But after a 15-match unbeaten run, which only came to an end last weekend against New England Revolution, the Union now sit sixth in the Eastern Conference. One of the most pivotal figures in Philly’s turnaround has been Cavan Sullivan.

Two years after becoming the youngest ever to play for a major North American professional sports team, Sullivan has confirmed the early hype with a breakout 2026 season. The winger has racked up 10 goals and 11 assists in 33 appearances, a record sum for an MLS teenager, and this month, he became the USMNT's youngest goalscorer after scoring in just his third cap against Mexico.

The 17-year-old is emerging as one of the best players in the whole continent. Enjoy him while you can, Philly fans. Sullivan is scheduled to join Manchester City in January 2028 after his 18th birthday.

New England Revolution haven’t played in a playoff match since 2023, and they haven’t won in the postseason since 2020. However, both droughts could be set to end this year, with the Revs currently sitting second in the Eastern Conference. A lot of the team’s newfound success can be credited to one youngster: Peyton Miller.

The 18-year-old winger has thrived for Marko Mitrović’s side, racking up seven goals and seven assists in 29 appearances. It remains to be seen whether his future is on the flanks or at the left back position, but Miller’s high-octane style and elite acceleration ensure that he has a resplendent future for club and country.

There are a few players who have scored five goals this club season, including Seattle Sounders captain Cristian Roldan and Real Salt Lake playmaker Diego Luna. Unlike Roldan, Luna was left off the World Cup roster and then was unable to return to the squad this fall after suffering a season-ending knee injury.

ftbpro_01m61kazv9ag.title: Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes Hold ‘Clear-the-Air Talks’ Ahead of Chelsea Showdown
ftbpro_01m61kazv9ag.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray1:15 PM EDTMichael Carrick (right) has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes. / Darren Staples/AFP/Getty ImagesMichael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes have reportedly held talks to “clear the air” in order to restore their broken relationship following Manchester United’s dismal 3–0 defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes was an unused substitute during the humiliating defeat after his controversial criticism of Carrick and his coaching staff in the aftermath of the equally embarrassing 4–1 loss to Como four days prior.

United’s skipper launched a remarkable rant about the club’s tactical setup in the wake of a chastening evening in northern Italy, following in the footsteps of Lisandro Martínez after he publicly criticized director of football Jason Wilcox the previous week.

Sunday’s loss to Bournemouth seemed set to be Carrick’s final match in charge following a disastrous start to the current campaign, but the Red Devils have decided to keep him in place for the upcoming match with Chelsea in the Premier League this Saturday.

Following United’s decision regarding Carrick’s immediate future, The Guardian have revealed that the 45-year-old has reconciled with Fernandes following discussions held at the club’s training ground on Tuesday.

The Portugal international reportedly made “assurances that he is fully committed and intent on trying to turn the team’s season around,” which was followed by a whole squad meeting in which his teammates “made the same vow.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Fernandes has underperformed this season. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesOn paper, this is a fresh start for Carrick, Fernandes and the rest of the United squad. However, things are never so straightforward at Old Trafford.

As per the report from The Guardian, Fernandes is expected to start the game against Chelsea as he aims to bring his own disappointing run of form to an end. He’s managed just four goals and one assist so far this season—all of which have come during home games against Ipswich Town and Sabah FK.
As is the case for Carrick and many members of United’s dressing room, Fernandes desperately needs a swift upturn in performance.

The Red Devils currently languish in 16th and 21st in the Premier League and Champions League respectively, while they were also dumped out of the Carabao Cup following a shock implosion at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion.

Patience is running incredibly thin—as evidenced by boos following the Bournemouth game, which were aimed at the players rather than Carrick—and another loss at the hands of Chelsea could prove fatal for the current regime.

Carrick has been undermined by the poor performances of his players. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesCarrick will be hopeful that recent soul-searching sparks a positive response when United visit Chelsea this weekend, and there are signs he retains the backing of at least some players.
“The feeling is that we all want to put it right. Players, staff, everyone,” one unnamed United player recently told BBC Sport.

If Carrick is searching for a good omen ahead of the game at Stamford Bridge, he can take solace in the fact United secured back-to-back wins over Chelsea last season—including an impressive 1–0 win under his guidance back in April.
The Red Devils have a relatively strong recent record against the Blues, winning four of the seven past meetings, and they have only lost three times in this fixture since the 2017–18 FA Cup final.

ftbpro_01m61m8fetx1.title: ‘Ego Check’—Thierry Henry Responds to Lamine Yamal Ballon d’Or Controversy
ftbpro_01m61m8fetx1.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas3:00 PM EDTThierry Henry co-hosted the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards ceremony.  / Jeff Spicer7UEFA/Getty ImagesSoccer legend Thierry Henry has taken to social media to clarify the “joke” he made when he asked Lamine Yamal if the Kopa Trophy was the “one he really wanted” during the 2026 Ballon d’Or  ceremony, stating he was not checking the teenager’s “ego.”
The legendary Frenchman co-hosted the 70th Ballon d‘Or awards on Monday in which Harry Kane took home the most prestigious individual award in the sport. Yamal settled for third in the final voting.

Earlier in the night, Yamal took home the first award of the ceremony, winning the Kopa Trophy as the best young talent for a record third consecutive year. After giving a brief speech in which he said he wishes the award had gone to his teammate Pau Cubarsí, Henry intervened.

“That’s your third one,” Henry said. “But is it the one you really wanted tonight?” Henry was clearly alluding to the teenager’s public desire to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or. The London Palladium Theatre erupted in laughter, and Yamal also nervously laughed before saying he wanted “all of them.”

Henry was loudly criticized on social media, with many taking his question as a dig at Yamal, with some even describing the question as “disrespectful.” A day after the ceremony, Henry responded to the controversy.

Lamine Yamal 🤝 Thierry Henry 💙❤️ pic.twitter.com/hlSoC1bDzC
Henry suddenly found himself in the eye of the storm for his comments, and it didn’t take long for him to issue a response. He didn’t really apologize, but rather explained his intentions.

“I want to clarify some stuff as some people got really excited for actually nothing,” Henry said. “First and foremost with Lamine Yamal I wasn’t checking his ego at all. I just thought that as the third time he had won that [Kopa] trophy, I was just asking him if it was the one he truly wanted, and I brought out a laugh out of people.

“We all knew what he wanted. Unfortunately, he didn’t get it. I’m a big fan of Lamine Yamal; I wasn’t checking his ego at all. That you don’t like the joke, I can understand that, but please, don’t do that. He’s actually one of those players I will pay to watch. I love him.

“I was just asking if it’s the one he really wanted because I knew the winner prize [Ballon d’Or] was coming after and unfortunately he didn’t win it. Because he’s a hell of a player and I enjoy to watch and I will pay to watch him.”
But his comments toward Yamal weren’t the only controversial moment of Henry’s Ballon d’Or hosting debut.

Ballon d’Or co-hosts Kate Scott (left) and Thierry Henry have worked together for years in television.  / Jeff Spicer/UEFA/Getty ImagesHenry also landed himself in hot water when he corrected fellow co-host Kate Scott for her pronunciation of “Socrates” when announcing the award that bears his name.
The pair have worked together for years covering the Champions League for CBS Sports, and the Frenchman addressed the controversy, revealing Scott was in on the joke.

“Kate was with me on the joke,” Henry said. “And you can ask Kate by the way, by the way. She did it on purpose, to say Socrates, and I had to say Socrates. Again, that you didn’t understand the joke, I understand, but please stop saying that I disrespected Kate. I would never do that.”

The final moment Henry addressed was when, after Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, he admitted that, as a Frenchman, he was always going to root for his nominated countryman to win it. Many took this as a sign of disrespect towards the winner, so Henry made sure to explain any misunderstanding.

“If you don’t watch our show on CBS,” Henry said. “Harry Kane the other day, after the game Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal, called me out for supporting Kylian Mbappé. So I just told him the other day that although I’m French and I was always going to back and support my fellow countryman, I just said to him: ‘You are a worthy winner, you deserve it, you are the example of what of what I always call work-ethic is a talent.’

“I said ‘you are a worthy winner, well done, Harry Kane,’ and I call him Sir Harry Kane since the World Cup. So, please people out there, relax, relax. I love Harry Kane, I love Lamine Yamal and I didn’t disrespect Kate.”
Henry did his best to put an end to the controversy. Now, only time will tell if he’s back hosting the ceremony again in 2027.

ftbpro_01m61n5b4mep.title: How Much Kylian Mbappe’s Mao Zedong Blunder Could Cost Him
ftbpro_01m61n5b4mep.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom2:30 PM EDTKylian Mbappé’s comments have cost him. / Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesKylian Mbappé could stand to lose as much as $30 million in yearly sponsorship revenue after getting cut by multiple Chinese sponsors amid a social media storm of his own unwitting creation.

The Real Madrid superstar incited the wrath of millions when he was filmed reacting to a meme of his own face superimposed onto an image of Mao Zedong, the leader of the People’s Republic of China between 1949 and 1976. Mbappé does not mention the late, controversial figure by name, instead referring to him as “a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator.”

The use of the term “dictator” for a figure still held in high esteem was considered hotly offensive and, according to a number of the brands which have since distanced themselves from Mbappé, “offended the feelings of the Chinese people.”
Mbappé had been associated with major Chinese brands stretching across multiple industries, with his likeness attached to everything from beverages to dairy manufacturers.
Mark Dreyer, author of Sporting Superpower which examines the sporting ambitions of China, told The Guardian that those deals could be worth “as much as $30 million per year.”

“As soon as someone else has decided you’ve crossed the line, it’s a race to who can cut ties quickest, who can be the most patriotic,” Dreyer explained. “Then you have to kiss the ring—there really is no other way if you want to stay in the market.”

Kylian Mbappé’s social profile in China has taken a dip. / Jade GAO/AFP/Getty ImagesThe launch of the ‘Great Leap Forward,’ a plan for unprecedented industrialization at the expense of private food production coincided with a devastating famine. The National Library of Medicine estimates that 30 million people died from what “was largely a manmade catastrophe for which Mao Zedong bears the greatest responsibility.”
Yet, even half a century later, to criticize Mao is considered taboo.

“You don’t need to think like a ​Chinese person to succeed in China, but you do need to understand how Chinese audiences will react and the cultural implications of not self-policing,” MGI Group founder Michael MacRitchie, a figure who regularly connects international celebrities with Chinese brands, told Reuters.

Zak Dychtwald, founder of BridgeWorks Global, a ​multinational organization advisor, added: “If you ⁠are participating in this market, the expectation is that you respect China’s self-narrative and you have a basic understanding of what it is. Red line education should come at the foundation of it.” Mbappé clearly hadn’t done the required reading.

Kylian Mbappé is a common face in China. / Liu Junfeng/VCG/Getty ImagesMbappé offered a note of contrition on Tuesday that was well received by the government. A foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, said: “We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made.”
However, this controversy stretches beyond the individual. The Chinese state broadcaster that covers La Liga, China Central Television (CCTV), immediately suspended all Real Madrid matches.

The China Media Group (CMG), which oversees CCTV, released a punchy follow up. “We believe that Mbappé’s outrageous remarks have harmed the Chinese people, crossed a line, and exceeded the scope of freedom of speech,” a statement read.

“Mbappé is a Real Madrid player, and the club bears significant responsibility. Therefore, we do not accept Real Madrid’s explanation that Mbappé ‘never intentionally offended and asserted that players have the right to express their personal opinions,’ and we do not accept Real Madrid’s attitude.”

It remains to be seen how this saga will conclude but Mbappé and Real Madrid would not be the first Western sporting entities to fall foul of offending China. Former Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey offered support for anti-government protests in Hong Kong in 2019 which prompted China to pull all sponsorships and TV coverage. ESPN estimated the financial repercussions to stand at somewhere between $150–200 million.
By that measure, Mbappé has gotten away lightly.

ftbpro_01m61s1b1vxr.title: What Lamine Yamal Must Do to Win the 2027 Ballon d’Or
ftbpro_01m61s1b1vxr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas10:00 AM EDTLamine Yamal has been tantalizingly close to winning the Ballon d’Or, yet his wait will extend at least another year.  / David Ramos/Getty Images (Yamal), Li Ying/Xinhua/Getty Images (Ballon d’Or)Lamine Yamal was on the verge of tears when Harry Kane stood on stage delivering his speech after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or award, clearly devastated by once again coming up short in the race for a prize he believes should already be his.

“I think everyone who watches football knows what my arguments [to win the Ballon d’Or] are,” Yamal said during a lengthy public campaign in which he tried to convince voters around the world to anoint him as the best player in the world.

He had a solid case. The teenager sensational 2025–26 season for Barcelona, steering the Catalans to another La Liga and Spanish Super Cup title with the best statistical season of his career at 18-years-old, dazzling the soccer world with his prodigious talent week-in and week-out.

Then came the summer and after recovering from injury, he played a crucial role in Spain winning the 2026 World Cup. After dethroning Lionel Messi and conquering the most prestigious trophy in the sport, many thought Yamal was bound to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

In the end, it wasn’t to be for Yamal, who came in third in the 2026 rankings, completing the podium behind Kylian Mbappé and 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. Although he’s 14-years younger than the Englishman, it’s no secret the teenager believed 2026 was supposed to be the year he finally received the most prestigious award in the sport.

Lamine Yamal was named the best young player in the world—again.  / Jeff Spicer/UEFA/Getty ImagesSince the now 19-year-old burst into the scene at 16, he instantly inserted himself in the conversation of being one of the world’s best and, at this point, it’s hard to argue against his case as the greatest teenager in soccer history.

What Yamal has achieved in his first three full seasons as a a professional for Barcelona and Spain is unlike anything the soccer world has ever seen. He’s not only been a Ballon d’Or finalist every time during his three-year career, he’s been voted inside the top 10 all three years—a feat never before seen in Ballon d’Or folklore.
As a result of his greatness at such a tender age, Yamal has rightfully become synonymous with the Ballon d’Or’s Kopa Trophy, handed to the best young talent in the world under the age of 21.
This year, Yamal extended his own record of being the only player in history to win the Kopa Trophy multiple times, collecting the award for the third year in a row.
His reaction to the historic triumph? Stating he wished the award had instead gone to fellow 2007-born Barcelona and Spain teammate Pau Cubarsí.

After two podium finishes in the Ballon d’Or, it’s clear Yamal no longer feels like the KopaTrophy is enough validation for what he’s accomplished and produced on the pitch. It’s a prestigious award, no doubt, but for the last two years, Yamal has left the Ballon d’Or ceremony carrying the Kopa Trophy on his hands yet still feeling disappointed.
Lamine Yamal was a Ballon d’Or finalist for the first time in 2024, when he won his first Kopa Trophy.  / Gao Jing/Xinhua/Getty ImagesYear

Lamine Yamal won the 2026 World Cup with Spain. / Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images It’s easy to understand why Yamal thought the 2026 Ballon d’Or was going his way. After finishing runner-up to Ousmane Dembélé last year, Yamal went on to have the best season of his career in 2025–26.

Yamal continued his generational trajectory, leading Barcelona in both goals and assists in 2025–26 to help the Catalans defend their La Liga title and conquer the Spanish Super Cup crown. He was named the La Liga player of the season, edging out Mbappé for the recognition.
Statistically, Yamal also improved. After collecting 43 goal contributions in 2024–25, Yamal had 45 in 2025–26 and eclipsed the 20-goal mark for the first time in his career.

But the main reason why many—including himself—believed the 2026 Ballon d’Or was destined to be his is that Yamal won the 2026 World Cup title with Spain, featuring in all eight matches of La Roja’s journey to glory in North America.

Yamal recovered from a hamstring tear that ended his club season and made his World Cup debut this summer. Although he never truly returned to his pre-injury level, he was still an untouchable cog in Luis de la Fuente’s well-oiled machine en route to glory.

With dazzling, productive individual performances all season under his belt, plus domestic titles and the World Cup trophy on his résumé, it seemed like Yamal had done enough to improve on his 2025 Ballon d’Or runner-up finish. That didn’t happen, to the contrary, he finished one spot below in the 2026 rankings.

Lamine Yamal is currently the odds-on favorite to win the 2027 Ballon d’Or.  / David Ramos/Getty Images It’s become abundantly clear that Yamal was penalized in the 2026 Ballon d’Or voting because he lacked that marquee individual moment for Spain in the 2026 World Cup. Had the hamstring injury not happened when he was at the peak of his powers or had he managed to produce at least one goal contribution during the knockout rounds of the tournament, the 2026 Ballon d’Or outcome might’ve gone his way.

ftbpro_01m61tgmss8j.title: 2026–27 Carabao Cup Quarterfinal Draw: All Fixtures
ftbpro_01m61tgmss8j.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellOct 28, 2026The fight for the Carabao Cup is heating up. / Leila Coker/Getty ImagesOnly eight teams remain in the fight for the Carabao Cup, and a slate of intriguing quarterfinal fixtures is on the horizon.

The early stages of the competition already provided plenty of drama, with Manchester United’s stunning collapse against Brighton & Hove Albion headlining an action-packed third round. But that was just an appetizer for what was to come in the fourth round.

Reigning Premier League champions Arsenal were upended in a penalty shootout by League Two side Fleetwood Town, who pulled off the biggest modern upset in Carabao Cup history. Defending cup holders Manchester City then needed a late comeback and penalties to get past Brighton.

Spot kicks continued writing the story over at Anfield, where Liverpool and Chelsea traded blows through eight rounds until Wesley Fofana’s horrendously skied effort handed the Reds a place in the last eight.
The stakes will only get higher in the quarterfinals, where both favorable and daunting paths loom large for the remaining clubs fighting for a place at Wembley Stadium in March.

Enzo Maresca and Manchester City will love their odds of a semifinal berth. / Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty ImagesFleetwood Town vs. EvertonManchester City vs. Bradford CityCrystal Palace vs. SunderlandLiverpool vs. Bournemouth When Are the Carabao Cup Quaterfinals?Only eight teams remain in the fight for the Carabao Cup. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesThe Carabao Cup quarterfinals are set to unfold during the week of Dec. 14. It’s an unforgiving schedule for the qualified clubs; they now must balance an additional midweek fixture just before the hectic holiday calendar.

Liverpool, City, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace, who are all competing in Europe, will have to play a minimum of eight matches across all competitions in December—and that’s not counting the New Year’s madness waiting once the calendar flips to 2027.

Squad depth and smart rotations will be key for those clubs to survive such a jam-packed run of fixtures. It would be the worst possible time for injuries to mount, considering the Carabao Cup is likely the biggest chance some of the remaining clubs have of lifting silverware this season.
The quarterfinals will once again be knockout clashes before the semifinals unfold across two legs.

ftbpro_01m61w87fq33.title: Man City Player Ratings vs. Brighton: Holders Survive on Penalties
ftbpro_01m61w87fq33.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack5:55 PM EDTMan City beat Brighton on penalties to reach the quarterfinals. / Declan Lloyd/Manchester City FC/Getty ImagesReserve goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli saved two Brighton & Hove Albion penalties to send Carabao Cup holders Manchester City into the quarterfinals of the competition following a 2–2 draw after 90 minutes.

It was no surprise that an encounter between the Premier League’s two leading scorers returned multiple goals at both ends of the pitch, even if Erling Haaland wasn’t sniffing around Jason Steele’s goal on the night.
Enzo Maresca and Fabian Hürzeler opted for widespread midweek changes ahead of their Premier League tussle on the same field in three days, perhaps not wanting to show their hand.

Still, an entertaining back-and-forth contest played out, with Man City twice asked to come from behind. Brighton’s man-to-man pressing proved troublesome in spells, and a high turnover led to the visitors’ opening goal, converted by Malick Yalcouyé from close range.

Mateo Kovačić’s strike from distance ensured the hosts weren’t behind for long, but they were caught cold at the start of the second half by Georginio Rütter and were fortuitous to restore parity for a second time. Vitor Reis deflected Rayan Cherki’s free-kick cruelly beyond Steele to set up a thrilling finale, but an absence of late drama meant the cup tie went to penalties.
And although Steele denied Kovačić from 12 yards, Rulli saved back-to-back from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

There were chinks in Man City’s defense. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesIf you’re no tactical whizz and unfamiliar with the term ‘half-space’, just think of the vertical inside channels. It was a phrase popularized in Germany, and the zone was particularly important in Wednesday’s match.

The modern-day manager encourages players to penetrate this space as much as possible. In theory, this zone escapes the congestion of the center, but remains close enough to goal for surging attackers to do damage, either as a creator or finisher.

Jürgen Klopp once said it’s “really not easy to defend that position,” so teams often must make a concerted effort to protect this part of the pitch, forcing coaches to innovate regarding how they can manipulate a defensive structure to ensure these zones remain unoccupied.

However, Fabian Hürzeler didn’t need to reinvent the wheel to unlock City’s changed defense and find themselves in these spaces. It was a key avenue of exploitation all night. Rotations helped, as did stretching the pitch horizontally. There were times when City’s backline didn’t correctly shift across, or their midfielders/wingers failed to track runners from deep.
Brighton’s opening two goals were sourced from half-space runs that went unchecked until it was too late. It’ll be a key coaching point for Maresca ahead of Saturday’s rematch.
Rico Lewis was among the fringe roster members who earned a rare start. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Gerónimo Rulli—7.4: There were a couple of concessions, but Rulli did make an outstanding save from Rütter at 2–1 to keep Man City in the cup tie. Ended as the hero.

RB: Rico Lewis—6.6: Lewis’ clever movements in the build-up were a key man-to-man beater for City early on in the game, yet he departed proceedings in the second half feeling as if he hadn’t built on his impressive showing in the Champions League last week.
CB: Vitor Reis—7.7: Credited with the second goal, even if he didn’t know a whole lot about it. Reis looks the part, composed in possession and a lean physical presence.
CB: Marc Guéhi—6.9: There were at least no major mishaps from Man City’s captain on the night.

LB: Nico O’Reilly—7.0: Hasn’t quite found his best form this season, and was more of the same from O’Reilly here. Feels like he’s far less impactful in possession, even if he wriggled out of a tight spot brilliantly once or twice.
CM: Ayyoub Bouaddi—6.9: It wasn’t the cleanest 45 minutes for Bouaddi despite a couple of imperious driving runs. Withdrawn at halftime after picking up a booking.

CM: Mateo Kovačić—7.9: Kovačić turned the clock back and helped the hosts bypass Brighton’s fierce press at times, also scoring his first goal for the club since April 2025 with a pinpoint finish from range.

ftbpro_01m61yec6bct.title: 2026–27 Carabao Cup Quarterfinal Draw: Liverpool, Man City Learn Fates
ftbpro_01m61yec6bct.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell6:51 PM EDTThe Carabao Cup fourth round was full of drama. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesAn intriguing clash between Liverpool and Bournemouth at Anfield headlines Wednesday’s Carabao Cup quarterfinal draw.

The qualified teams all waited to find out their next opponents following Liverpool’s win over Chelsea at Anfield. Andoni Iraola’s men became the penultimate team to book a place in the quarterfinals, joining Premier League foes Manchester City, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace in the last eight, along with Fleetwood Town and Bradford City.

Everton and Newcastle United are the two clubs yet to play their fourth round fixture. They will meet under the lights at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, and the winner will face Fleetwood in the next round.

The marquee clash of the quarterfinals is Liverpool hosting the Cherries. Iraola will face off with his former club for the second time this season, and he will be hoping to lead the Reds to another victory, much like the one they claimed back in September at the Vitality Stadium.

Manchester City received a much more favorable draw, matching up with League One side Bradford City at the Etihad. Crystal Palace, meanwhile, will take on Sunderland just days before they play one another in the Premier League.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Andoni Iraola faces off with his former club again. / Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesFleetwood Town vs. Everton/Newcastle UnitedManchester City vs. Bradford CityCrystal Palace vs. SunderlandLiverpool vs. Bournemouth  2026–27 Carabao Cup Round DatesThere is a lengthy layoff before the Carabao Cup returns. / Leila Coker/Getty ImagesRound

There’s a rather lengthy layoff between the conclusion of the fourth round and the quarterfinals. Carabao Cup action does not return until mid-December, when the last eight will battle for a place in the semifinals just before all the holiday chaos kicks off.

Just when players will be desperate for a breather following frenetic Christmas, Boxing Day and New Year’s fixtures, they must gear up for the first leg of the semifinals on Jan. 11. The second leg will not be played until three weeks later on Feb. 1.
The two teams that survive the gauntlet run will face off at Wembley Stadium, where the victor will lift the Carabao Cup on March 21.

ftbpro_01m61zsrw67r.title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Chelsea: Reds Triumph in Chaotic Penalty Shootout
ftbpro_01m61zsrw67r.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray6:32 PM EDTLiverpool triumphed in the shootout. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesLiverpool reached the Carabao Cup quarterfinal on Wednesday after beating Chelsea 6–5 on penalties following a 1–1 draw in normal time.

It was a tale of two spot kicks which provided the only excitement of a tepid first half under the Anfield floodlights. Morgan Rogers opened the scoring from the spot following Ryan Gravenberch’s clumsy challenge, but the Reds responded just three minutes later as Cody Gakpo fired home to level proceedings.

The second half yielded more entertainment, with Liverpool forcing some smart saves from Mike Penders, courtesy of efforts from Ronald Araújo and Bradley Barcola. There were also stops for Giorgi Mamardashvili to make at the other end, but neither team was able to find a crucial winner in regulation time.

A hard-fought stalemate forced a penalty shootout, which Liverpool eventually won. Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch both skewed their efforts from 12 yards, but there were misses from Valentín Barco, Emmanuel Emegha and, finally with the 16th kick, Wesley Fofana, which secured a place in the final eight for Andoni Iraola’s side.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
Another stellar performance from Trey Nyoni. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesWith each passing match, Trey Nyoni appears increasingly destined for the top.

The 19-year-old has earned rave reviews for some seriously impressive showings in the double pivot, and he delivered another excellent display against Chelsea’s glitzy midfield. Nyoni’s punchy forward passes and defensive awareness shone through, but it’s his enviable composure that makes him such an eye-catching talent.
Of course, there are imperfections in his game which will need to be ironed out over time, but the sky really is the limit for the youngster.

Gravenberch’s silly challenge was punished.  / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesIraola’s rotated team was not without senior experience, and it was one of the club’s older heads who exhibited the rash immaturity of a teenager to gift Chelsea their lead. Moisés Caicedo was going nowhere inside Liverpool’s penalty area when Gravenberch needlessly clattered through the back of him, deservedly handing the visitors a spot kick.

Just over three weeks on from the Dutchman’s red card during the 3–0 defeat to Manchester City, another brainless decision proved costly for Liverpool. With Nyoni sparkling and Alexis Mac Allister back at his best, such errors threaten to cost Gravenberch his starting position in midfield.
Oh, and he missed his penalty in the shootout, too. An awful evening for the midfielder.
Rio Ngumoha thrived against his old side.  / Carl Recine/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Giorgi Mamardashvili—7.8: Helpless to deny Rogers from the penalty spot and made some important saves to keep Liverpool level. Then produced a vital shootout stop to prevent Emegha from winning it for Chelsea.
RB: Joe Gomez—7.0: There was the odd issue for Gomez up against Rogers, but he was generally effective against his English compatriot.
CB: Ronald Araújo—7.8: After a heroic performance at the weekend, this was another all-action display from the Uruguayan. Defends at a ferocious speed.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—6.9: Led by example in a much-changed defensive line, racking up some important interventions to snuff out Chelsea attacks.

LB: Kostas Tsimikas—6.9: The 30-year-old was erratic in possession, as Liverpool have come to expect, but there were no defensive lapses against the speedy Pedro Neto. Produced a shocking penalty in the shootout, though.
CM: Ryan Gravenberch—5.6: No excuses for his idiotic challenge on Caicedo, with little else memorable about his performance. Sloppy in possession, too.
CM: Trey Nyoni—7.1: It’s easy to see why Iraola already trusts Nyoni, who plays with the confidence of someone five years his senior.
RW: Lewis Koumas—6.4: Managed just 12 touches during his hour on the field. Zero impact on proceedings.

ftbpro_01m620p2nc57.title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Liverpool: Familiar Villain Ends Blues’ Carabao Cup Dreams
ftbpro_01m620p2nc57.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:57 PM EDTWesley Fofana (middle) missed the decisive kick in the penalty shootout. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesChelsea are out of Carabao Cup competition in round four, after losing to Liverpool 6–5 on penalties following a 1–1 draw at regular time at Anfield on Wednesday night.
The hosts looked slightly better from the start, but it was a vastly uneventful opening half, with both teams struggling to get much of anything going offensively.

That all changed in the final 10 minutes of the first half, thanks to some woeful defensive mistakes. Ryan Gravenberch brought down Moisés Caicedo inside the penalty area with a clumsy, unnecessary challenge. Morgan Rogers then converted from the spot to give Chelsea the lead 40 minutes in with the very first shot on goal from either team.

Chelsea’s joy was short-lived, though, as Wesley Fofana inexplicably put his hand up defending a corner, resulting in an egregious handball. Cody Gakpo capitalized on Fofana’s gift and equalized from the spot to send the game level into the break.

The second half was much more open, and both teams had clear chances that required the pair of goalkeepers to make crucial saves. Still, neither side could find a winner, and the game was decided in a penalty shootout.

The shootout went to sudden death after Chelsea’s Valentín Barco and Liverpool’s Kostas Tsimikas missed inside the opening five penalties taken. Chelsea had a chance to complete the upset, but Emmanuel Emegha missed what would’ve been the winning penalty—and it proved costly.
Needing to score to extend the shootout, Fofana sent his penalty into orbit to tie the bow on his nightmare of a game.

For the third time since 2019, Chelsea’s Carabao Cup dreams ended in a penalty shootout against Liverpool. Now, Xabi Alonso’s men have only the Premier League and the FA Cup to fight for in what remains of 2026–27.

Estévão was an unused substitute against Liverpool.  / Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesIt’s been only a year since an 18-year-old Estêvão scored a match-winner against Liverpool and then proceeded to steal the show with a dazzling performance against Barcelona in the Champions League. The Brazilian appeared destined to continue growing in importance for Chelsea in the coming months. That couldn’t be further from what actually happened.

Four days after Alonso picked fellow teenager Geovany Quenda ahead of him to replace João Pedro in the XI against Tottenham, Estévão was again omitted from the lineup against Liverpool—the first time he didn’t feature from the start in the Carabao Cup this season. Although first-choice attackers Pedro and Cole Palmer were unavailable, the Brazilian didn’t even feature from the bench.

Estévão hasn’t started for Chelsea since Sept. 9, and has played just 31 minutes in four appearances for the Blues since. In total, the Brazilian attacker has played 172 minutes for the Blues through 11 games across all competitions this term.

Last summer, Estévão was considered a superstar in the making and a potential future Ballon d’Or winner. He’s already shown he has the raw quality to blossom into a star, but he currently finds himself way down Alonso’s attacking pecking order.

Only Alonso knows the reasons why Estévão is barely getting opportunities, but it’s undeniable that the development of one of the most exciting young prospects in the sport is getting compromised. Alonso’s treatment of Estévão is starting to look eerily similar to how Carlo Ancelotti treated Endrick at both Real Madrid and Brazil.
If the situation doesn’t improve, then the noise surrounding his potential Chelsea exit in coming transfer windows—presumably on loan—will only intensify.
Morgan Rogers continued his incredibly productive start of the season.  / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*

GK: Mike Penders—7.8: Nervous on the ball, often lobbing the ball high up the pitch instead of playing an easy pass, leading to frustration from teammates. Still, he produced a couple of brilliant saves in the second half.

RB: Josh Acheampong—7.5: Had a tasty battle down the flank with Rio Ngumoha and more held his own. He also occasionally ventured forward and caught Liverpool by surprise with a couple of nice runs to the byline. Stunning block late to deny Bradley Barcola.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—6.6:  Was vigilant and diligent in his defensive duties until he was forced to exit the pitch injured on the brink of half time.
CB: Wesley Fofana—7.6: Cost his team by gifting away a penalty immediately after taking the lead and then missed the decisive penalty in the shootout. A nightmare evening for the Frenchman.

Matchday 34 of the 2026 MLS season is the second-to-last one, seeing Nov. 7’s Matchday 35 serve as the playoffs-defining Decision Day—the very last opportunity for teams to clinch a postseason berth.

Six teams from the Eastern Conference and six from West have already punched their tickets, meaning three from each side are still up for grabs. It will make for fierce battles that are anything but runaway wins.

Six teams—Red Bull New York, Toronto FC, New York City FC, LA Galaxy, Portland Timbers and Minnesota United—are staring down elimination, meaning they will bring extra scrappy energy to their respective clashes.
Here, Sports Illustrated dives into how it all may play out.

ftbpro_01m627qz844w.title: 4 Things Michael Carrick Must Do Against Chelsea to Save Man Utd Job
ftbpro_01m627qz844w.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack3:30 PM EDTMichael Carrick needs the best of Bruno Fernandes to re-emerge. / Michael Steele/Getty ImagesManchester United and Michael Carrick were briefly in limbo after a chastening week, with plenty expecting INEOS to pull the plug on his tenure as manager after the club’s on-field woes worsened.

The Red Devils were battered by Como before going out with a whimper at home to Bournemouth. It was the sort of defeat that felt like end times for the manager, even if the fanbase were clear about who they primarily blamed for their wretched start to the season post-match.

However, the announcement so many were expecting never arrived. Some have suggested that Man Utd simply can’t afford to dismiss Carrick and make a lucrative new appointment. Whatever the truth, Carrick remains at the helm, and a significant duel beckons against Chelsea.

The Blues were seemingly in the ascendancy after keeping their first Premier League clean sheet since January against Everton, but Xabi Alonso then became just the second Chelsea manager since 1990 to oversee a home league defeat to Tottenham Hotspur last week, and followed that by losing in the cup to Liverpool. Their most likely avenue to silverware has gone.
There’s pressure on Alonso, but the scrutiny is incomparable to what Carrick is under. The Englishman may well have one more ‘prove it‘ match in his locker before his firing is rendered inevitable.
Here’s how Carrick can save his job this weekend.

Carrick has cleared the air with his captain. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesCarrick felt he had no choice but to drop his captain for Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford. Bruno Fernandes had thrown him under the bus after the 4–1 defeat at Como, decrying the manager’s gameplan.

Fernandes’s public criticism left a sour taste, given that it was Carrick who facilitated his rise to claiming the Premier League’s single-season assist record and the PFA Player of the Year award last season. Fernandes had been restricted under Ruben Amorim, who was intent on converting him into an all-round midfielder. Carrick liberated the Portuguese as a playmaker, and United purred as a collective.

Ultimately, this iteration of the Red Devils require the very best of Fernandes to flourish. It’s no surprise that the midfielder’s individual struggles have coincided with a dismal start to the season, yet last week’s defeat to the Cherries proved that dropping him, while necessary, isn’t the solution going forward for the manager.
The pair have supposedly cleared the air this week, with Fernandes poised to return to the starting lineup on Saturday.

Dalot has had far too much responsibility as an attacking outlet. / Dan Istitene/Getty ImagesCarrick has the higher-ups to blame for his distinct left back issue. Man Utd were in the market for Luke Shaw mitigation toward the end of the summer window, but seemingly gave up when it became clear that Lewis Hall wouldn’t be leaving Newcastle United.

While Shaw was injury-free last season, the extra games on the schedule were always going to provide a stiffer challenge for the often unfit Englishman. So, it shouldn’t have come as a surprise that Shaw has already missed multiple games due to various setbacks, forcing Carrick to function with one hand tied behind his back.

United simply aren’t blessed with optimal solutions in reserve, and their woes without Shaw came to a head last Sunday. Diogo Dalot lined up in replacement, and asked to operate as an attacking outlet down the left flank while Mason Mount drifted infield. It was a combination that lacked dynamism, and generally looked awkward.

Carrick can’t rely on Dalot as an high and wide outlet down the left. It just doesn’t work. Either Marcus Rashford must start on Saturday to offer some thrust, or he gets creative at right back. In possession, Dalot or Noussair Mazroaui could play on the left-side of a three, with the right-sided defender asked to get forward and support the attack. Amad Diallo, maybe?

Shea Lacey has appeared in back-to-back games. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesThis is usually part of the playbook of an under-fire manager desperate to win over supporters. Carrick doesn’t need to convince the fanbase, they’re firmly in his corner.

Still, given what the seniors have produced at the start of the new season, Carrick wouldn’t hurt his standing by trusting the club’s academy. We’re not talking about Ayden Heaven, who joined from Arsenal, but instead the likes of Shea Lacey, who wasn’t given much of an opportunity to build on an impressive performance against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup.

Lacey has appeared off the bench in back-to-back games, and seems the most likely starlet to earn a start. However, Carrick also has Harry Amass, Jack Fletcher, Jariyah Shah and Jim Thwaites in first-team training at senior level.

If we’re talking about a potential solution at left back, perhaps Amass is the guy. The 19-year-old is the most experienced of United’s academy players, and has earned two senior appearances this season.
If Amass starts at left back, Dalot could play more of a marauding role on the opposite wing.

Carrick’s common-sense approach worked wonders during the second half of last season. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesUnderstandably, Carrick has sought to evolve his Man Utd team after earning the job full-time. As Lisandro Martínez said during his rant after the defeat to Atlético Madrid: “Every season is different. You can’t stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don’t change next season [it] is a big problem.”

paragraphs: By Rich FayOct 29, 2026Sheffield United and Wrexham both know a win this weekend could kickstart their season. / Morgan Harlow/WSL Football/Getty Images (Sheffield United), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham)Wrexham will hope to kickstart their season when they travel to face old foes Sheffield United in the Championship on Friday.

The Red Dragons have won just three of their first 12 league matches this season, with only one victory in their four games since the October international break. The Blades have fared only marginally better, with four wins from their opening 12 league matches. The hosts will also believe a victory this weekend could spark an eventual climb up the table.
Wrexham won both meetings with Sheffield United last season and should be prepared for a hostile reception against the team they faced in an epic FA Cup encounter as a National League club.

ftbpro_01m63p7pgxx6.title: Real Madrid Receive Huge Fitness Boost Ahead of Racing Santander Clash
ftbpro_01m63p7pgxx6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath11:30 AM EDTJosé Mourinho has few injury problems ahead of the weekend. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesReal Madrid No. 1 Thibaut Courtois could be in line to return to action this weekend, after revealing he is recovering well from the bout of flu that kept him out of El Clásico.
Courtois was a surprise absentee for Sunday’s showdown at the Camp Nou, after coming down with illness ahead of the match.

In the end, backup keeper Andriy Lunin stepped into the breach for Los Blancos, making five saves—including a one-handed stop to deny Gerard Martín’s close-range header—in the impressive 2–1 win over Barcelona.
The victory in Courtois’s absence puts Madrid right back in the La Liga title race, with José Mourinho’s men now just three points off Barcelona at the top of the table.
Mourinho singled out Lunin for praise after the match telling reporters the Ukrainian “played a game with great balance and calmness.”
While Real Madrid fared well without Courtois, they may not have to plan for life without him for much longer as the 34-year-old Belgian revealed he is back training with the team and feeling better.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Thibaut Courtois is back in training after illness. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesSpeaking to El Chiringuito on Wednesday, the player provided a positive update on his recovery and his potential participation against Racing Santander.
“I’m feeling much better now, thank God,” he revealed. “I’m training little by little to recover. There’s still time ahead of Sunday.”
Despite Lunin’s unexpected heroics last weekend, Courtois is likely to regain his starting spot against Racing Santander this weekend as long as he is deemed fit.
The 34-year-old, who now ranks as Madrid’s joint second-longest serving first-team star and one of the locker room leaders, is regularly cited as one of the club’s most important players.
He also has the second-highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in La Liga this season (76.3%) behind only Ionuț Radu of Celta Vigo.

Vinícius Jr is one of few players unavailable for the Santander match. / Helios de la Rubia/Real Madrid/Getty ImagesAssuming Courtois is flu-free and ready to go for Sunday, Madrid go into match away at newly promoted Racing Santander with few fitness concerns.

Raúl Asencio (tibia), Ferland Mendy (thigh) and Rodrygo (ACL) are all long-term absentees and none have played a minute this season. Otherwise it is only Vinícius Júnior set to miss the trip north as he continues his four-match suspension for the red card received in the team’s 1–0 win over Villarreal earlier this month.
Madrid will be aiming to keep up the pressure on Barcelona this weekend, with the gap at the top now cut down to just three points.

Los Blancos’ match follows Barça’s against Alavés the day before. After this weekend’s round of fixtures, Madrid take on Valencia on Nov. 7—the final game before the November international break and last of Vinícius Jr’s domestic ban.

ftbpro_01m63rqth90s.title: Ex-USMNT Star to Train Viral 3-Year-Old Soccer Prodigy After Police Incident
ftbpro_01m63rqth90s.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott10:00 AM EDTEddie Johnson (left) has stepped in. / JOE KLAMAR/AFP/Getty Images (Johnson), Martasia Griffin (Nevada)Former USMNT striker Eddie Johnson has offered a place in his EJE7 Soccer Academy to a 3-year-old who recently went viral after police were called during a recent youth league game in Winter Park, Florida.

Playing against children as old as 5, footage on social media showed Nevada Pierre dazzling on the pitch and scoring goal after goal before an incident which led to the police being called and Nevada and his family leaving the area.

Organizers for the i9 Sports league accused Nevada’s parents of creating a disturbance in response to seeing the 3-year-old repeatedly sent to the bench. Nevada was also accused of “pushing” the other players and the parents were told he was no longer welcome in the league.

No arrests were made by the police, who stressed the incident was a civil matter. They did reiterate the league’s request for Nevada’s parents to leave the area, which was eventually agreed after i9 Sports confirmed they would receive a refund on their registration fees.
With Nevada searching for a new team, USMNT icon Johnson quickly offered the 3-year-old a spot in his EJE7 training program.

“Nevada deserves to be around someone that looks like him that can understand him and it’s sad in youth soccer we don’t have enough of those programs for kids of color to have those examples around them because soccer is a rich suburban sport that’s controlled by privileged rich entitled parents and no one likes when the less fortunate kids are better then their kids,” Johnson wrote on social media. “One of the many issues with youth soccer in this country.

“l experienced it now he’s experiencing it. That’s one of the reasons I created EJE7 because we encourage freedom and creativity and that is what you see we you see Nevada. That’s why they call it the beautiful game. We should be praising a 3-year-old with his ability instead of tarnishing it.”
Next. MLS Talents. Why Is MLS Suddenly Producing So Many USMNT-Ready Teenagers?. dark
Johnson was not the only big name to reach out. According to Loren LoRosa, Nevada also received an offer of help from Jay-Z and his sports agency, Roc Nation.

Roc Nation, which boasts clients like the Real Madrid trio of Vinícius Júnior, Yan Diomande and Endrick alongside USMNT center back Chris Richards of Crystal Palace, is reported to have been offered a trip to Spain in December for “an impactful athletic experience.”
Nevada’s family are said to have already expressed interest in a permanent move to Spain, believing the youngster’s soccer journey would be taken more seriously there.
A GoFundMe campaign, set up by Nevada’s mother, Martasia Griffin, has already raised over $56,000.

ftbpro_01m63s81rnsp.title: How Ronald Araujo Rediscovered His Best Form After Barcelona Exit
ftbpro_01m63s81rnsp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath4:00 PM EDTRonald Araújo is a hit. /  Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty ImagesLiverpool and loan signings have not paired well in recent years.

There was Steven Caulker, the big center back thrown on as an auxiliary striker while Jürgen Klopp made kitchen sink signals from the touchline. Ozan Kabak, the injury crisis band-aid who was only marginally better than having no defenders at all. And who can forget all 13 cursed minutes of Arthur Melo’s temporary switch?

As a result of these signings’ performances, and several others, hopes were not especially high when Liverpool announced the arrival of Ronald Araújo on a season-long deal with an option to buy back in August.

Yes, the Uruguayan arrived as the Barcelona captain, but he had started only 11 La Liga matches in 2025–26. Once rated as one of the best defenders in Spanish soccer, question marks over his rashness, positional lapses and injury record had since turned into honking great exclamation points. General consensus was that Liverpool, unmoored by the dual exits of FSG’s CEO of Football Michael Edwards and sporting director Richard Hughes, had panic bought their defensive cover.
Less than three months on, Araújo has a very strong case to be considered as Liverpool’s player of the season so far.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC
The Araújo press 😤#UCL pic.twitter.com/SI2fjruc5N

Signed in part for his versatility, the 27-year-old has excelled at both right back and in the center of defense, starting six out of eight games in the Premier League so far, winning praise by the boat-load for his commitment and ferocity.

While defensive signings to the Premier League from La Liga are often critiqued for their perceived reluctance to get stuck in, Araújo plays like he was raised on Pure Barclays. It is his love of blood and thunder defending that has endeared him to the Anfield crowd and social media has been awash with love for “Big Ron” in the early months of this season.

In Sunday’s 2–0 win over Brighton, the defender was awarded Player of the Match after putting in a shift that included a rarely-seen sliding header tackle inside his own box to preserve the Reds’ clean sheet. He also won all five of his duels in that match, made 11 defensive contributions and recorded a top speed of 36.3 km/h—supposedly the fastest clocked in the Premier League this season so far.

It is not just at the back Araújo is excelling. The Reds’ new No. 33 already has two Champions League goals and an assist—the latter a delightful backheel to set up Dominik Szoboszlai in the comeback win over Atlético Madrid.

In that same outing, Araújo sprinted upwards of 70 yards—simply for the love of the press—forcing Jan Oblak to hoof it long. It was a moment reminiscent of Andy Robertson’s famous lung-busting run against Manchester City all those years ago that secured the Scotsman as a bonafide fan-favorite.
Viral moments help calcify a player’s reputation at a new club. There have been plenty of them for Araújo already, who is becoming Liverpool’s one-man meme machine.

Araújo’s short spell has been rife with viral moments. / Liverpool FC/ Getty ImagesAraújo’s find-a-man-who-does-it-all displays have been incredibly welcome in a Liverpool team in danger of slipping towards mediocrity during a transition period, helping provide a dynamism that has often been lacking.
But his arrival has also proven exactly the sort of fresh start Araújo found himself needing, half a year on from his leave of absence from Barcelona for mental health reasons.

Araújo has spoken positively of Barcelona’s support for him while dealing with his anxiety struggles, but sometimes a change of scenery is just what’s needed. With Liverpool, it appears to be a perfect match of player and environment.
“The fans have absolutely fallen in love with him straight away,” Jamie Carragher said of Araújo last month.

“Sometimes you have players like that. They’ve come, they’ve got a bit of a backstory. At Barcelona maybe they were happy to see him go, but the Liverpool supporters opened their arms and gave him a big cuddle, and he seems to be enjoying it.”

On the pitch, he is already diving into the crowd and kissing the badge. Off it, the defender is said to have embraced life on Merseyside, and he has multiple Spanish speakers supporting him in the Liverpool locker room.

Araújo lifted the La Liga title as Barcelona captain last season. / Eric Alonso/Getty ImagesAs it stands, Liverpool have a £47 million ($63 million) option to buy Araújo at the end of the season. On current form, it may seem like a no-brainer, but there are reasons why this love affair could end up being only a fling.

ftbpro_01m63t8hm1ey.title: ‘Moment Will Come’—Parkinson Backs Wrexham Star Ahead of Hostile Sheffield Return
ftbpro_01m63t8hm1ey.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay11:10 AM EDTWrexham signed Callum O’Hare on deadline day of the summer transfer window. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesPhil Parkinson is confident Callum O’Hare will become a key player for Wrexham as the attacking midfielder searches for his first goal for the club against former side Sheffield United this weekend.

Wrexham signed O’Hare for an undisclosed fee believed to be worth $9.5 million (£7 million) on Deadline Day of the summer transfer window. The 28-year-old signed an initial three-year deal at the Racecourse Ground, with an option for a fourth, and cited the club’s ambition to reach the Premier League as a key reason behind his move.

O’Hare has started Wrexham’s last six matches but has yet to register a direct goal contribution in any of his eight appearances for the Welsh club. The attacking midfielder scored twice in five starts for Sheffield United this season before moving to North Wales on the final day of the transfer window.
dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC

Callum O’Hare has yet to record a direct goal contribution for his new club. / Leila Coker/Getty ImagesSheffield United manager Chris Wilder accused Wrexham of taking a “blanket bomb” approach to the summer transfer window as they closed in on a deal for O’Hare. Wilder suggested the Red Dragons were “in for half the division” as they frantically looked to strengthen their squad in the closing days of the window.

It was not the first time Wilder had taken a dig at old foe Parkinson, with the pair having been apprentices together at Southampton as teenagers. Speaking ahead of Sheffield United’s clash with Cardiff City earlier in the season, a game in which O’Hare scored, Wilder accused Parkinson of disrespecting their Welsh rivals after they were held to a 1–1 draw on the opening weekend.

“I watched the game against Wrexham. I thought it was one-way traffic for 20 minutes,” Wilder said. “The second half, I didn’t agree with what the Wrexham manager said, I don’t usually anyway, in terms of that it was a one-sided game. I thought he should give the opposition a little bit more credit and respect.”

A hostile reception awaits O’Hare on Friday, with Wrexham likely to name both the midfielder and former Sheffield United striker Kieffer Moore in their starting lineup. Wilder did not want to sell O’Hare in the summer and admitted last season that, if it were up to him, Moore would still be playing for the club, too.

Kieffer Moore has become an integral piece of Phil Parkinson’s squad. / Cody Froggatt/PA Images/Getty ImagesWrexham need big performances from their forwards at Bramall Lane amid a difficult start to the season. Only three teams have averaged fewer than their 3.4 shots on target per match, while their expected goals (xG) total of 13.6 is the sixth-lowest in the Championship.

O’Hare has recorded an xG of 1.85 since joining the club, with Wrexham struggling to cope without the firepower of last season’s top scorer, Josh Windass. The 32-year-old missed the entirety of preseason because of injury and fitness issues and is currently sidelined with a separate ankle problem.

That puts even more pressure on O’Hare, who has operated as the lone attacking midfielder in each of Wrexham’s last two matches. However, Parkinson is confident that one goal could change the midfielder’s fortunes at his new club.

Phil Parkinson is hoping to get Wrexham back to winning ways. / Jon Hobley/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty Images“I think generally, his performances have been good: the Preston one (won 4-1) in particular,” Parkinson told Sports Illustrated. “I had a good chat with him this week; the moment will come for him. He just has to concentrate on his general all-around performance and not get frustrated that the moments haven’t come. In fairness, the goal we won the game with against Southampton was practically his. He has been so close on a number of occasions. His general play has been really good and his work for the team has been excellent.”
For O’Hare, it is business as usual. He knows he will receive plenty of abuse in front of his former fans on Friday but insists he will treat the match like any other.
“I’m looking forward to it. Good to see some faces, but we mainly just want to get three points and win,” O’Hare told Sports Illustrated after the weekend defeat to Blackburn.

Although he has yet to score for his new club, O’Hare pointed out that he is still getting into the right positions. He admitted, however, that he has not had the little bit of luck needed to find the net and secure what would undoubtedly be a significant confidence boost.
He added: “I mean, getting the chances, I feel like I am always going to get those. When one goes, I am going to get the chance to keep scoring. So I have just got to keep pushing to get that.”

ftbpro_01m63w5brcmr.title: ‘Not Well’—Fleetwood Star Digs at Arsenal’s Attitude After Carabao Cup Shock
ftbpro_01m63w5brcmr.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott10:30 AM EDTArsenal were dumped out in humiliating fashion. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesFleetwood Town goalkeeper Jay Lynch revealed, in his opinion at least, that Arsenal’s squad did not take Tuesday’s historic defeat particularly well.

Arsenal, the reigning English champions, were dumped out of the Carabao Cup on penalties as Fleetwood, struggling towards the bottom of England’s fourth tier, pulled off one of the greatest upsets in competition history.
Celebrations after the final whistle were wild, with Fleetwood fans rushing the pitch to join their heroes and leaving the Arsenal squad rushing off the pitch in a hurry.

“It’s obviously such a huge moment for us and all the fans ran on, no one actually got chance to speak to them,” said Lynch, who saved Bruno Guimarães’s penalty to set up his side’s victory, in an interview with talkSPORT.
“I think the gaffer spoke to their gaffer briefly, but because of all the fans we didn’t actually get a chance to ask for shirts or even speak to them or anything, to be honest.
“They didn’t take it well, let’s put it that way.”

Martin Ødegaard was unimpressed by the team’s performance. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesManager Mikel Arteta appeared to show Arsenal’s frustrations towards the game with his reaction to the red card shown to young Max Dowman, failing to hide his disappointment at the 16-year-old’s dismissal for a reaction to a heavy challenge.

That annoyance bled back into the Arsenal dressing room, where captain Martin Ødegaard confessed the team were well below the required standard in any match, regardless of the opposition in front of them.
“It’s very frustrating to go out,” the Norway international admitted. “Obviously, the way we’ve played was not on the level. We need to do much, much better than we did.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“Frustrating, but congratulations to Fleetwood and we look forward to the next game already and bounce back. They did well so we have to give them credit, but ... we need to do better. I thought we improved during the game, but again, we need to step up even more, so that’s a shame.”
The chance to respond comes in a big way this weekend. There are eight Premier League games on Saturday before Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool gets Sunday’s billing all to itself.

Andoni Iraola’s Reds are enjoying a strong run of form and are celebrating a place in the next round of the Carabao Cup after seeing off Chelsea on Wednesday, leaving them with just one defeat from their first 13 games of the season—one fewer than Arsenal.
