ftbpro_01m63wd74ytn.title: 5 Strikers Man Utd Could Sign in January After Benjamin Sesko Blow
ftbpro_01m63wd74ytn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTMan Utd must analyze short-term solutions to their No. 9 problem. / Sebastian Frej (Mateta), Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty Images (Endrick)Respite has been in short supply for Manchester United this season.

On-field performances have been disastrous, players have publicly lambasted club staff and, just to make matters even worse, injuries have poured fuel on a growing dumpster fire. When it rains, it pours—as those familiar with the Manchester climate know all too well.

The latest setback amid the ongoing crisis comes from the treatment room, as Benjamin Šeško’s return from a nagging shin injury has been reportedly delayed until January. That leaves the misfiring Joshua Zirkzee as the only orthodox striker available for the Red Devils, which is an alarmingly bleak prospect.

Šeško’s 12-goal debut season offered encouragement that United had finally clinched their long-term No. 9 after painful experiences with Zirkzee and Rasmus Højlund. Despite his worrying injury record, the Slovenian sharpshooter remains part of the club’s vision of a brighter future.

But nobody can deny United’s need for reinforcements. The club, as they should have over the summer, will need to sign an alternative to Šeško when the transfer market re-opens in January, preferably recruiting a short-term solution which will bolster their ranks without blocking the development of their injured 23-year-old.
Here are five strikers they could turn to in the winter window.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Jean-Philippe Mateta has long wanted to leave Crystal Palace. / BSR Agency/Getty ImagesPremier League proven and out of contract next summer, Jean-Philippe Mateta could be the perfect answer to United’s prayers.

It’s no secret the 29-year-old has long wanted to leave Crystal Palace, even coming close to joining AC Milan last winter before issues with his medical scuppered a move. He’s begrudgingly continued to represent the Eagles, and he finished last season with 16 goals across all competitions despite his itchy feet—the third successive campaign in which he’s hit double-digits.

Mateta won’t be signing a contract extension at Selhurst Park, meaning the upcoming January window is the last chance Palace have to cash in on him. Given his proposed move to Milan was valued at around $36 million, one would expect United to be able to sign him for even less this winter.

Old Trafford would certainly prove an attractive destination for Mateta, in spite of the Red Devils’ current predicament. The chance to join one of the world’s grandest clubs—one currently playing Champions League soccer—doesn’t arise every day.

The towering center forward would prove similarly appealing for United. Clinical, powerful, cost-effective and acutely aware of the demands of English soccer, Mateta would provide excellent competition for Šeško in both the immediate future and years to come.
Endrick is desperate for more game time. / Javier Borrego/Europa Press/Getty ImagesIf United desire an incredibly short-term remedy, then Endrick would be worth analyzing closely.

Real Madrid blocked a possible loan exit for their young Brazilian over the summer, but it’s been a familiar story for him at the beginning of the José Mourinho era. The continued brilliance of Kylian Mbappé and arrival of summer recruit Carlos Espí has resulted in a bit-part role, which has yielded just four appearances.

A dramatic increase in game time appears unlikely during the second half of the campaign, potentially forcing Endrick into another temporary departure. He spent half of the 2025–26 season on loan with Lyon in France, where he delivered an impressive eight goals and as many assists in 21 outings.
The raw talent is undeniable, and United could take a fairly risk-free punt on the 20-year-old as a result.

Whether Madrid will actually sanction his exit, either temporarily or permanently, remains to be seen, as does his effectiveness as a sole striker in the Premier League. But Endrick ticks a number of United’s boxes regardless.
Could Alexander Sørloth be a surprise solution? / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesErling Haaland lite, anyone?

Alexander Sørloth resembles his Norwegian compatriot in many departments. The 30-year-old has an imposing frame, excellent aerial ability and a ruthless streak in the penalty area—traits he’s regularly exhibited during his spell in Spain with Real Sociedad, Villarreal and now Atlético Madrid.

He’s registered 20+ goals in each of his past three seasons and finished in La Liga’s top four scorers in two of those campaigns, despite the fact he’s often not been a regular starter since moving to Atlético.

ftbpro_01m63zj5542y.title: Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez Help Set New MLS Goalscoring Record
ftbpro_01m63zj5542y.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell12:00 PM EDTLionel Messi (left) and Luis Suárez are lighting it up for Inter Miami. / Vaughn Ridley/Getty ImagesGoals are flowing in Major League Soccer like never before. The league has set a new single-season goals record—and the likes of Lionel Messi, Son Heung-min and Antoine Griezmann will surely continue running up the score.

As the regular season comes to a close, 14 matches across both the Eastern and Western Conference unfolded on Wednesday night. There were goals galore, with the league’s biggest stars and brightest young talents getting on the scoresheet, a common theme in a historic way this season.

Lucas Halter was among the long list of goalscorers, lifting the Houston Dynamo to a 1–0 win over the Seattle Sounders. His goal not only secured three points for his side, but also helped MLS reach a new landmark.

Halter’s goal was the 1,553rd scored in 2026, surpassing MLS’s previous single-season record of 1,552 from the 2024 campaign. Still with two more matchdays left to play, the overall haul will only keep increasing.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lionel Messi is eying his second straight MLS Golden Boot. / Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesReaching a new goals landmark wouldn’t be possible without the league’s top forwards finding lethal success in the final third—and there’s no player more lethal than Messi.

The Inter Miami captain has found the back of the net 25 times in 29 league appearances this season, which puts him in pole position in the Golden Boot race. Messi took home the prize last season for his 29 goals and will like his chances of defending his crown.

Only FC Dallas’ Petar Musa has a realistic chance of catching the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner. The Croatian, who has 22 goals to his name, is the only other player in the league to surpass the 20-goal mark this season.

Messi could see his three-goal lead erased if he fails to find the back of the net in Inter Miami’s final two matches against New England Revolution and Charlotte FC. But if he gets his name on the scoresheet, the trophy is as good as his.
Petar Musa is chasing down Lionel Messi. / Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesRank

Luis Suárez is Inter Miami’s second-leading goalscorer. / Megan Briggs/Getty ImagesTo reach a single-season goals record, there must be production beyond the top goalscorers in the league. Take a look at Inter Miami: They have scored a staggering 75 goals this season and only 25 belong to Messi.

It’s no surprise the Herons top the scoring charts. Luis Suárez has put together a massive bounce-back season and has 16 goals to his name. New signing Germán Berterame also has found the back of the net nine times. In total, the defending MLS Cup champions have had 15 people get on the scoresheet in 2026.
Five other clubs, including last season’s MLS Cup runners-up Vancouver Whitecaps, have scored more than 60 goals. Nineteen teams have bagged 50 or more.

ftbpro_01m646f2z4x6.title: Man Utd’s Dismal Transfer Record Laid Bare by Staggering Statistic
ftbpro_01m646f2z4x6.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 29, 2026Mason Mount is one of those who has failed to merit his price tag. / Dan Istitene/Getty ImagesManchester United’s disastrous on-field performances continue to dominate headlines, but it’s the club’s woeful record in the transfer market which has fueled its misery—as statistically confirmed by a recent study.

The Red Devils have made countless high-profile and expensive mistakes when recruiting new personnel, especially in recent years as the likes of Jadon Sancho, Rasmus Højlund, André Onana, Mason Mount and Antony failed to deliver after being signed for exorbitant fees.

Evidence of just how misguided their spending has been has now been revealed by the CIES Football Observatory, which recently ranked clubs across the world based on the “appreciation or depreciation in value of non-academy players signed over the past five years.”

For players who have already departed the club, the final calculation balances the fee paid and received. For those still at the club, their signing fee is marked against their current transfer value.
Only clubs whose spending and income exceeds $56 million since 2022 were analyzed, while add-ons were included regardless of whether they have been paid.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

The Red Devils have been careless when splashing large fees. / Michael Regan/Getty ImagesAs per the study, United officially rank as the European club that has lost the most on signings over the past five years.
In total, they have lost an extraordinary $452 million, with only Saudi Arabian giants Al Hilal (-$560 million) having conducted more wasteful business.

Of their final tally, $208 million has been lost on players who have already left the club on permanent deals—such as the aforementioned Sancho, Højlund and Antony—while $244.5 million has been sacrificed on those still representing the Red Devils.
Not only is this a colossal sum wasted on players, but it’s also significantly more than any other European side.

Tottenham Hotspur are the closest continental peer to United when it comes to the depreciation of player values, with the Lilywhites having lost a comparatively modest $210 million—less than half of United’s final total.

Just to rub salt in gaping wounds, local rivals Manchester City rank fifth, having gained just shy of $500 million in value over the last five years. They only trail Eintracht Frankfurt (+$588 million), Real Madrid (+$587 million), Paris Saint-Germain (+$547 million) and Benfica (+$545 million).

Despite splashing massive sums since BlueCo took ownership, Chelsea have a positive value of $200 million. Arsenal (+$123 million) and, to a lesser extent, Liverpool (+$14.5 million) have also seen their signings rise in value overall.

Andrey Santos was a surprisingly expensive addition last summer. / Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty ImagesDespite consistently losing massive sums on expensive signings, United have opted against a radical transformation of their transfer policy. While their spending has been less erratic over the past two seasons, they still forked out over $400 million on new additions—none of whom, barring the cost-effective Senne Lammens, have yet to live up to their price tag.
United’s decision to bolster one department of the field at a time has also had a negative effect on the team’s performances and, in turn, the value of the current roster.

They prioritized the attack by signing Benjamin Šeško, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha in 2025, followed by bolstering the midfield last summer with the additions of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos on Carlos Baleba. Presumably, the defense will follow next year.

Such a segmented transfer approach has proven costly on the field. United realistically could have added another left back, center back, left winger and striker to their squad last summer, but instead opted to focus solely on midfield (ignoring the signing of backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer).
As long as they continue to fumble their way through each passing transfer window, they’ll find themselves unable to shrug off the tag of Europe’s worst recruiters.

ftbpro_01m64ag4k008.title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo’s Latest Ballon d’Or Honor Is So Divisive
ftbpro_01m64ag4k008.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:30 PM EDTCristiano Ronaldo has five Ballon d’Or awards in his trophy cabinet.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesCristiano Ronaldo added another honor to his illustrious résumé on Wednesday when he won the B.O.A.T award.

The Portugal international is one of the most decorated players in history. Ronaldo has taken home five Ballon d’Or awards, the second-most behind only long-term rival Lionel Messi, and has two Best FIFA Men’s Player awards.

His trophies for club and country are even more impressive. Ronaldo collected silverware for fun at Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus, winning five Champions League titles, three Premier League titles, two La Liga titles and two Serie A titles, as well as dozens of other prizes. The superstar forward also lifted the 2016 European Championship with Portugal.
Just when it seemed like there was nothing left for Ronaldo could win—let’s ignore the elephant in the room—he collected the inaugural B.O.A.T award.
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Cristiano Ronaldo won his first Ballon d’Or award in 2008. / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesB.O.A.T stands for Ballon d’Or of All Time, a new award created to recognize the greatest Ballon d’Or triumph in history. The pool of nominees included previous winners who took home soccer’s most prestigious individual prize more than twice.

Ronaldo ultimately claimed the honor for his maiden Ballon d’Or win in 2008. The all-time great was recognized for his sensational 2007–08 season with United that ended in Premier League and Champions League glory.

Ronaldo scored 42 goals across all competitions that season, picking up the Premier League Golden Boot and the European Golden Boot. His most important goal was no doubt his opener in the Champions League final against Chelsea, which the Red Devils eventually won on penalties.
The 2008 Ballon d’Or triumph edged out Messi’s 2012 Ballon d’Or win, which came second. Completing the podium was Ronaldo’s 2017 win.
Whenever Ronaldo and Messi go head-to-head, debate will always follow. But Ronaldo beating out Messi was arguably the smallest reason dividing opinions in the aftermath of the win.
The real head-turner was the voting process. The B.O.A.T. was voted for by fans so they could have their say in the most iconic Ballon d’Or triumph of all time.
The participating fans also had to pay €1 to cast their votes, stirring up the narrative that the award was essentially paid for, especially by supporters casting multiple votes.

Then there’s also the fact that only players who won at least two Ballon d’Or awards were up for the honor. Therefore, the nominee pool was extremely limited, leaving out great wins belonging to the likes of Raymond Kopa, Ronaldinho, Michael Owen and Luka Modrić.

Ronaldo still happily accepted the award, commemorating the moment on social media. “Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon d’Or of All Time is also yours,” he wrote on Instagram.

ftbpro_01m64aj95gv5.title: Arsenal Learn Outcome of Ambitious Appeal to Overturn Dowman Red Card
ftbpro_01m64aj95gv5.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:30 PM EDTMax Dowman was dismissed in Arsenal’s shock Carabao Cup defeat. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesArsenal’s appeal against the red card shown to Max Dowman in the midweek defeat to Fleetwood Town has been dismissed by the Football Association (FA).
The Gunners suffered an extremely embarrassing Carabao Cup fourth round exit at the hands of their League Two hosts, with Fleetwood eventually winning on penalties following a 1–1 draw in regulation.

Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the 85th minute of the tie after kicking out at Harrison Neal. The 16-year-old was angered by a forceful challenge by the Fleetwood midfielder, which went unpunished by referee Michael Salisbury.
In response to Arsenal’s unsuccessful appeal, an FA statement read: “An independent Regulatory Commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Max Dowman.”
Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed

Dowman will be suspended for the weekend trip to Liverpool. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesUnfortunately for Arsenal, Dowman will now be suspended for the next three matches in domestic competition. The first of those games comes in the Premier League on Sunday, when the reigning champions visit Liverpool.

An almighty test of Arsenal’s credentials is followed by a more palatable away day at Slavia Prague in the Champions League. Dowman will be able to play in the Czech capital as domestic suspensions don’t carry over to UEFA competitions.
However, Dowman will then miss out on Premier League games either side of the November international break at home to Hull City and away at Newcastle United.
The next domestic encounter the teenager will be available for is the critical encounter with title rivals Manchester City on Nov. 29.

Mikel Arteta is already short of attacking options. / Henry NICHOLLS/AFP/Getty ImagesOrdinarily, Dowman’s absence wouldn’t concern Mikel Arteta too much. After all, the prodigious youngster remains a bit-part player who rarely features heavily in the Premier League or Champions League.
However, considering the club’s current injury list, Arteta will be deeply frustrated by the timing of Dowman’s three-match suspension.

Arsenal are already without their first-choice right winger Bukayo Saka, who suffered a thigh injury in the recent Champions League clash with Bayern Munich. The Englishman’s return date remains unknown, but he’s reportedly set to miss around two months of action.

To make matters worse, Christos Tzolis is still sidelined on the other wing. The Greek forward sustained a hamstring injury on international duty, with Arteta admitting he would be out for “weeks” in mid-October.
Noni Madueke is also a doubt ahead of the weekend showdown at Anfield having missed the Fleetwood match with an ankle injury. However, he’s expected to recover in time.

ftbpro_01m64hbjaym9.title: Carlo Ancelotti’s November Brazil Roster Is Bad News for Barcelona
ftbpro_01m64hbjaym9.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell4:30 PM EDTCarlo Ancelotti revealed his latest squad for Brazil. / Tom Weller/picture alliance/Getty ImagesBrazil manager Carlo Ancelotti unveiled his 26-player squad for the November international break on Thursday, confirming news every Barcelona fan has been dreading: Raphinha will join up with the Seleção in a couple of weeks.

Ancelotti made it clear he is using the final international window of the year to continue testing out young players as Brazil enters a new era following another World Cup disappointment. The Italian boss has moved on from previous pillars like Neymar and Casemiro to begin developing the next generation so the team is at its best for the 2030 World Cup.
“Right now, it’s time to observe, refresh the squad and help young players reach their full potential,” Ancelotti said on Thursday.

Barcelona fans hoped that meant Raphinha would be one of the names left off the manager’s roster in November. The winger only just returned to full fitness after suffering a hamstring injury during the September camp and surely could have used an additional two weeks to further recover.
But despite starting just two games for Barcelona since Sept. 19, Raphinha was still called up by Ancelotti for friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

Other veterans, like Alisson, were left out. “We don’t need to test Alisson. We know him very well. He is the best goalkeeper. When the Copa América begins, he will be called up, and it’s the same for the others,” Ancelotti confirmed.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Raphinha cannot seem to escape injury with Brazil recently. / Ayush Kumar/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesRaphinha has had a tough go in recent camps with Brazil. The last three times he was called up by Ancelotti, he returned with injuries.

During the March international break, Raphinha suffered a hamstring injury that kept him sidelined for over a month. He missed crucial clashes for Barcelona during that stretch, including both legs of the Champions League quarterfinals against Atlético Madrid, a tie that ended in elimination for Hansi Flick’s men.
Then, Raphinha suffered another hamstring problem during last summer’s World Cup. The 29-year-old did not feature in the Seleção’s final three matches of the tournament.
The bad luck continued during the September-October international break. Raphinha returned early to Catalonia with another hamstring injury that kept him out of action for nearly three weeks.

Important clashes for Barcelona loom following the final window of the year, none bigger than a Champions League battle with Manchester City on Dec. 8. Plus, the Catalans cannot afford another slip-up in La Liga now that they lost El Clásico to Real Madrid last weekend, which reduced their gap atop the table to just three points.
Flick will be crossing his fingers Raphinha avoids another setback and returns to Barcelona fully fit and ready to continue his stellar start to the season.

ftbpro_01m6642nqbfs.title: Liverpool Predicted Lineup vs. Arsenal: Isak and Barcola Return, Gakpo Decision Time
ftbpro_01m6642nqbfs.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray1:00 PM EDTAndoni Iraola was to rest key players midweek. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesLiverpool are hoping their hot streak of form continues into Sunday’s showdown with reigning Premier League champions Arsenal at Anfield.

Including the penalty shootout triumph over Chelsea midweek, the Reds have now seven of their last eight matches across all competitions. There are encouraging signs they’re finding their feet under Andoni Iraola, who won half of his six matches against Arsenal as Bournemouth boss.

After making wholesale changes to his starting lineup in the Carabao Cup, the Spaniard will restore some glitzy names to his starting XI. The club’s band of expensive attackers will make comebacks, but injuries will once again prevent Iraola from naming his strongest team.
Here’s how Liverpool could line up this weekend.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

GK: Alisson—Only Tottenham Hotspur (18) have been more regular rivals for Alisson than Arsenal (17) across his illustrious career. He averages exactly one goal conceded per match with the champions, with seven clean sheets in this fixture—two of which came last season.

RB: Ronald Araújo—Following Araújo’s stunning performance against Brighton & Hove Albion last weekend, the Barcelona loanee delivered another stellar display in the hard-fought victory over Chelsea. Liverpool fans are really starting to fall for the Uruguayan.

CB: Jérémy Jacquet—Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres pose vastly different threats as Arsenal’s leading man, but one would fancy Jacquet to deliver against either considering his excellent start to life in England.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—Liverpool remain reliant on the 35-year-old’s consistency and leadership at the back, and that’s more important than ever against Mikel Arteta’s wily Gunners.
LB: Milos Kerkez—Having enjoyed a complete rest midweek, Kerkez will be pleased by the guaranteed absences of Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman down Arsenal’s right wing.

CM: Ryan Gravenberch—Trey Nyoni really should start purely based on form, especially after Gravenberch’s horror performance on Wednesday. ftbpro_01m6676h4f8k.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Ridiculous Statistics After Achieving the Ultimate Scoring Feat
ftbpro_01m6676h4f8k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom8:30 AM EDTCristiano Ronaldo had plenty of reason to celebrate on Thursday. / Abdullah Ahmed/Getty ImagesWhen Cristiano Ronaldo scored his first goal of Thursday’s 5–3 win over Al Kholood, he looked mildly annoyed after finally finding the back of the net after two early efforts were disallowed. Within a quarter-hour, he was a picture of vein-popping ecstasy.

In the space of 15 second-half minutes, Ronaldo scored three times, sweeping in two cutbacks with his left and right foot on either side of a towering header. The act of converting with each part of his body saw Ronaldo achieve that rarest of feat in soccer: a perfect hat trick.

Even for a figure as goal-laden as world soccer’s most prolific player of all time, this unique type of treble is still hard to come by. Of all the hat tricks which Ronaldo has scored for club and country, only 11 have been “perfect.”

It’s been an intriguing few weeks for Ronaldo. After storming out of Portugal’s international camp, the 41-year-old endured a ruinous return to club action, delivering one of his most wasteful performances of the season against NEOM. Ronaldo had not yet scored a league goal since falling out spectacularly with Jorge Jesus and threatened to have another night to forget on Thursday.

Ronaldo first had the ball in the net inside 10 minutes only for VAR to intervene and spot that he had strayed offside. The forward, whose famous work ethic was questioned by his ex-Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag earlier this month, also failed to time his run on the cusp of halftime.
The floodgates would open for Ronaldo from the 66th minute onward as he wrote another chapter in his remarkable array of scoring statistics.

This was the 67th hat trick of Ronaldo’s career—37 of which have come since his 30th birthday. For comparison, the freshly crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane has ‘only’ scored 31 hat tricks across his entire senior career.
Ronaldo already stands out on his own as the recognized top scorer in professional soccer, but he has a clear target left to hit.
Cristiano Ronaldo is nearing his last goal. / Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images“I want to reach 1,000 goals,” Ronaldo declared in 2024. “If I don’t have any injuries, this for me is the most important.”

The veteran forward’s latest treble took him up to 985 for club and country, just 15 shy of that remarkable feat of four digits. Ronaldo would not be the first player to ever claim 1,000 goals—the legendary Brazilian forward Pelé is lauded by the Guinness World Records as having scored 1,279 career goals in 1,363 games. Yet, many of those occured in what would now be considered unofficial competitions. FIFA, world soccer’s governing body, lists Pelé’s final count at 767.

Al Nassr have 23 league matches remaining this season as well as at least six more fixtures in the first round of the AFC Champions League plus the next round of the King’s Cup. That’s a minimum of 30 club games before Ronaldo’s international duties are taken into consideration.

It remains to be seen how many minutes Jesus will afford his squabbling talisman but the expectation is that Ronaldo will be back in the international setup after accepting his pitiful fine. Portugal have two more Nations League matches in November and could be involved in the two-legged quarterfinals next March before the final tournament in June.

If Ronaldo maintains his remarkable fitness record to feature in the majority of these fixtures he would only need to score roughly one goal every other game to crack 1,000. Given his current average of one goal every 120 minutes for Al Nassr, he could conceivably have the record wrapped up by next spring.

Desperate to recover from Tuesday’s stunning Carabao Cup exit at the hands of fourth tier outfit Fleetwood Town, the Gunners know they will be pushed to their limits by their in-form hosts on Merseyside.

The Reds have won seven of their last eight matches and are steadily improving under Andoni Iraola, but Arsenal are still six points better off than them in the Premier League. Having won all but one of their matches in the competition, they entered Gameweek 9 in second place—only behind Manchester City on goal difference.

ftbpro_01m66bkcebjj.title: Martin Odegaard ‘Open’ to Arsenal Exit Amid Return to Europe Links
ftbpro_01m66bkcebjj.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom9:30 AM EDTMartin Ødegaard is Arsenal’s leader on and off the pitch. / Christina Pahnke/sampics/Getty ImagesArsenal captain Martin Ødegaard is reportedly “open” to a move to Bayern Munich in an unexpected twist which will cut deep for Mikel Arteta.

Bayern have been credited as long-term admirers of Arsenal’s captain, who has been hailed as one of Europe’s most effective attacking midfielders for years. The perennial Bundesliga champions could have a vacancy to fill in the final third next season as the prominence of Serge Gnabry (formerly of Arsenal himself) continues to diminish and Ødegaard would neatly slot in.
While previous links have always been spurious, there is “new momentum” in these latest reports thanks to Ødegaard’s supposed willingness to play in Bavaria, per Sky Germany.

There’s less than two years left on Ødegaard’s contract and, at 27, his next deal could very well be the biggest he ever signs in his career. Arsenal are thought to be keen on delivering those terms, but the Gunners are already in the midst of Declan Rice’s lucrative renewal.

Intriguingly, Bayern aren’t driving this interest, with the Bavarians content to bide their time amid Ødegaard’s contractual uncertainty. The fact that Arsenal’s star man is billed as open to leaving the reigning Premier League champions during their current spell of success will serve as a dagger to the heart of Arteta and his grand ambitions in north London.

Mikel Arteta has some big ideas for the club. / Henry NICHOLLS/AFP/Getty ImagesAfter scaling the peak of the Premier League last season, Arteta was not content to admire the view. All he could see was more heights to hit.

“It’s certainly the ambition of the club and the owners to be the best club in the world,” Arteta declared ahead of the current campaign. It took Arsenal 22 years to even be considered the best team in England but, thanks largely to the feverish ambition of their omnipotent manager, the club is set up to build upon that success.

Ødegaard is part of a core of star players very much in their prime years. There may be limitations to the attacking fluency that the frontline can conjure, but the defensive solidity instilled by Arteta has provided the foundations for a team with a very high floor and a ceiling that can still be raised.
Arteta wants “the best facilities, the best stadium, the best supporters” as well as “the best players in the world.” Crucially, the best clubs in the world do not sell their best players.

The likes of Real Madrid, Barcelona and, pointedly, Bayern Munich, would never consider losing their captain at his peak, especially if he was the one driving for the exit. It’s not yet clear to what extent—if any—Ødegaard will go in his desire for a move to Bavaria, but even the whispers of this intent will undermine Arteta’s ambition of turning Arsenal into one of the true elite.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

The affection between Martin Ødegaard (left) and Mikel Arteta would appear to be mutual. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesWhat makes this twist all the more painful is Ødegaard’s status as arguably Arteta’s most trusted lieutenant. Gabriel may be the defensive rock, Rice the engine in midfield and Bukayo Saka the lauded ‘star boy,’ but it is the impish skipper who serves as Arteta’s embodiment on the pitch.

Ødegaard is utterly fundamental to everything the team does on and off the ball. Arsenal’s chief creative force who has discovered his taste for goal this term is arguably even more influential out of possession by leading the press.

The 2–1 victory over Leeds United offered a recent example of how Ødegaard is not blindly scampering around the final third. The cerebral midfielder spotted the tactical inefficiency of Arsenal’s setup during the heat of battle—a reluctance to commit from Ben White and Saka constantly gave Leeds space down the left flank—and convinced his teammates to hurriedly correct the error of their ways.

Beyond the white lines, Ødegaard takes his duties as club captain incredibly seriously. The Norway international is the first player to reach out to new recruits and the last to remain in contact with those who have left the club. Whether it’s offering advice over houses, schools or how to not giggle during Arteta’s more eccentric team talks, Ødegaard is the point of reference. But for how much longer?

ftbpro_01m66ef6f52k.title: ‘Very Pleased’—Araujo’s Agent Reveals State of Play Between Liverpool & Barcelona
ftbpro_01m66ef6f52k.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom10:05 AM EDTRonald Araújo has made an excellent first impression at Liverpool. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesEdoardo Crnjar, the owner of the Excellence Sport agency which counts Ronald Araújo among its clients, has played down talk of an imminent decision about a permanent move to Liverpool for the Barcelona loanee despite being “very pleased” with the season thus far.

Amid two summer transfer windows of eye-watering extravagance, a loan deal seemingly out of nowhere has rapidly come to be one of Liverpool’s most celebrated moves. Araújo has quickly taken to the hearts of those on Merseyside with his blend of athleticism and endurance meshing well with Andoni Iraola’s draining demands.

The 27-year-old is one of just three players in feature in all 13 Liverpool fixtures this season, chipping in with two goals while serving as a priceless asset at both center back and right back. Unsurprisingly, whispers of Liverpool’s desire to make his temporary stay permanent have grown in volume over recent weeks. Crnjar was keen to temper those expectations.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark
“Ronald is performing well, and we are very pleased with his contributions,” the agent told winwin. “However, it is still far too early to discuss his future at this stage.
“He feels very good; he is happy playing for Liverpool and pleased to be helping the club and his teammates—just as he has already expressed himself.”

Earlier this month, Araújo admitted that it is “still early” to consider his long-term future even if he and his family are “very happy” with life in England. The Uruguay international still has a contract at Barcelona until 2031 and is playing well enough for those in Catalonia to regret letting him go.

Ronald Araújo (left) is already a favorite of Andoni Iraola. / Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesIn purely financial terms, Liverpool’s path to a permanent move for Araújo is straightforward. Barcelona baked a buy-option clause into his contract thought to be valued at €55 million ($61.4 million). If the Reds want him, they know how much it will cost.

There is always the prospect of Liverpool trying to renegotiate the terms of that arrangement once his loan expires next summer—an approach which Barcelona themselves adopted while discussing Marcus Rashford’s future with Manchester United. However, given the praise Araújo has already earned, Liverpool may struggle to argue for a discount.

The main point of contention will be whether new sporting director Julian Ward considers Araújo to be an investment that will retain his value for the duration of any contract he is offered. Still only 27, the Uruguayan has time on his side, while his versatility has already proven to be incredibly useful.

In an ideal world, Araújo probably isn’t considered a Liverpool starter when everyone is fit; the natural center back is an awkward fit when tasked with too much attacking responsibility at right back while Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk are Iraola’s first-choice central pairing. However, Arsenal have shown the benefit of stockpiling defensive talent in recent years. Van Dijk also can’t go on forever.

Despite his impressive availability this season, Araújo has a far shakier injury track record. Across his six years in Barcelona’s senior side, the towering figure missed 100 games through injury, an average of more than 16 per season.
With all the uncertainties that any transfer will bring, Liverpool would perhaps be best served following Araújo’s example of playing a waiting game.

ftbpro_01m66j9mn53x.title: ‘At Least’—Messi’s Future Takes New Twist Amid Shock Inter Miami Exit Talk
ftbpro_01m66j9mn53x.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:15 AM EDTLionel Messi remains Inter Miami’s most important creative force. / Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAmid wild claims of Lionel Messi returning to Argentina to represent his boyhood club Newell’s Old Boys, a new report has claimed that the Inter Miami forward is committed to his MLS future, with the prospect of an extension tentatively raised.

Messi is in the endgame of his legendary career. The most trophy-laden player in the history of the sport has no more worlds left to conquer and has already retired from international duty. At this point, Messi could be forgiven for letting sentimentality dictate his next moves.

This week, the Argentine journalist Gonzalo Calvigioni claimed that “Messi has never been so close” to joining Newell’s Old Boys, with a potential transfer set for January 2027. Messi famously grew up as a Newell’s fan and lit up the club’s youth teams only to be told by senior management that they would not pay for his costly growth hormone treatment, thereby forcing him to Barcelona as a 13-year-old.
It is one of the curiosities of his career that the greatest Argentinian player of all time has never made a single appearance in his nation’s top flight.

Any stir that this talk may have caused was quashed by Fabrizio Romano, who confidently reported that Messi is “very happy at Inter Miami,” where he intends to remain until the expiry of his contract in December 2028. Romano also added the telling line that Messi’s future in MLS will stretch until 2028 for “at least” another two years, with the prospect of an extension to his existing terms “to be evaluated later on.”
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

It’s unclear what the future will hold for Lionel Messi. / Rich Storry/Getty ImagesIf it were up to David Beckham and Inter Miami (and MLS at large), Messi would be given a lifetime contract. The legendary World Cup winner is the ultimate marketing tool for a division which he is continuing to dominate.

Even at this advanced stage of his career, Messi remains the most destructive attacking force in MLS. The 39-year-old leads the league for goals, xG, shots and shots on target, while also creating the most clear cut chances across the league.

“There will be a before and after Messi,” Inter Miami co-owner Jorge Mas said after striking the biggest deal in the history of U.S. soccer three years ago. He simply doesn’t want the “after Messi” bit to begin just yet.

Inter Miami’s valuation has more than doubled to $1.3 billion since Messi’s arrival, while interest in fixtures across the league have enjoyed an unprecedented boom with the ability to market the shy and retiring Argentine.
While there is a swollen glut of invested individuals hellbent on extending Messi’s Floridian swansong, the man himself hasn’t shown too much of an appetite for an endless playing career.

When Messi tearfully announced his international retirement after the draining experience of playing through the 2026 World Cup while his father Jorge was dying, he hinted at an imminent exit from the global stage altogether. “All I ever did was play soccer,” he wrote in an open letter to his late dad in August, “and now I’m really not sure if I’ll keep doing it for much longer.”

Steps have already been taken for Messi to make a smooth transition into a post-playing career, with an ever-expanding portfolio of clubs coming under his ownership. “I am just starting out,” Messi said of his budding business empire. The same can no longer be said for his days on the field.

ftbpro_01m66n45fsxx.title: ‘I Can Confirm’—Robert Lewandowski Reveals Why He Rejected Arsenal Move
ftbpro_01m66n45fsxx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray5:30 PM EDTRobert Lewandowski has poked fun at the Gunners. / Harry Figiel/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesRobert Lewandowski has joked that his desire to win silverware was the reason he never decided to join Arsenal during his illustrious career.

The 38-year-old headed to Major League Soccer last summer to join Chicago Fire, bringing the curtain down on an astonishing spell at Europe’s top table with Borussia Dortmund, Bayern Munich and, most recently, Barcelona. He scored 567 times for the three European giants, but his career could have worked out very differently.

Lewandowski was regularly linked with a move to Arsenal over the years, with the striker revealing that the club’s former goalkeeper and his international teammate Wojciech Szczęsny tried to convince him to move to north London.

“I can confirm that Wojciech tried to convince me to join Arsenal,” Lewandowski revealed in 2014. “We had several talks about this. It was him who did most of the talking, how the club looks inside, what Arsène Wenger thinks of me.”
Lewandowski was never tempted by the prospect of joining the Gunners, however, and a viral clip circulating on social media has now revealed exactly why.
The sharpshooter was asked why he snubbed Arsenal, to which he jokingly replied: “I wanted to win some titles.”
When quickly reminded that Arsenal finally won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years last season, Lewandowski responded: “Maybe you don’t have to wait so long if I joined Arsenal.”

Arsenal wanted Lewandowski before he left Borussia Dortmund. / Team 2 Sportphoto/ullstein bild/Getty ImagesIt was not only Szczęsny who wanted Lewandowski at the Emirates Stadium. Wenger was keen on signing him before he traded Dortmund for their Klassiker rivals Bayern Munich.

“Yes we looked into Lewandowski, but honestly he signed for Bayern one-and-a-half years ago, everyone knows that,” Wenger confessed in January 2014, shortly after Lewandowski’s move to Bayern was confirmed.

The former Arsenal manager added: “We are like everyone, we look out there and see what is happening. If an opportunity turns up, you know as well that all the big players are at big clubs at the moment and they go for important targets.”
So, what would have happened if Lewandowski had joined Arsenal instead of Bayern?

Well, Arsenal would have entered the 2014–15 season, during which they finished third and won the FA Cup, with one of Europe’s leading strikers in their ranks. Lewandowski scored 25 times in his debut season with Bayern, goals which would have proven very useful for the Gunners.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Lewandowski won everything on offer at Bayern. / Michael Regan/UEFA/Getty ImagesArsenal were reliant on Alexis Sánchez, who scored the same number as Lewandowski that term, and Olivier Giroud for the majority of their goals, but perhaps the addition of the Poland international’s relentless output would have thrust them to greater things.

Lewandowski proceeded to score 41+ goals in each of his remaining seven seasons with Bayern. There’s no doubt he would have vastly improved Wenger’s forward line, perhaps even helping end the club’s agonizing wait for Premier League or Champions League glory.

Unfortunately for Arsenal, the titles Lewandowski craved were always likely to be far more forthcoming at Bayern, where he eventually tallied 19 titles—including eight Bundesliga trophies and one Champions League crown.
Catalonia proved similarly fruitful for Lewandowski, who won seven more major trophies with Barcelona following his move in 2022.

ftbpro_01m66pqjmsph.title: Man City Predicted Lineup vs. Brighton: Haaland Returns to Lead Fearsome Forwards
ftbpro_01m66pqjmsph.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray3:00 PM EDTErling Haaland is the Premier League’s top scorer. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesThe second part of Manchester City’s double bill with Brighton & Hove Albion offers the Premier League leaders the chance to solidify their place at the summit.

The Cityzens, who conquered Brighton on penalties in the Carabao Cup midweek, can clinch their eighth win of the league season at the Etihad Stadium this Saturday, which would almost certainly guarantee them top spot for at least another week.

Victory is particularly important considering last weekend’s disappointing defeat at Aston Villa, which extinguished City’s perfect record in the Premier League. Nicolas Jackson’s brace punished an error-strewn performance, with major improvements required for Brighton’s visit.
Here’s the side Enzo Maresca could select.

GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—Despite Gerónimo Rulli’s heroics midweek and Donnarumma’s glaring error at Villa Park, Maresca has confirmed the Italian as the undisputed first-choice between the posts.

RB: Abdukodir Khusanov—Matheus Nunes should return to the matchday squad after missing the last three games, but Maresca could persist with Khusanov at right back until the Portugal international regains full match sharpness.

CB: Rúben Dias—Dias secured a well-earned rest in the cup, leaving him fresh for the visit of the division’s top scorers. Brighton have managed 23 goals in eight outings, with three of those scored against Arsenal last month.

CB: Marc Guéhi—The Englishman’s costly error at Villa Park saw him sacrificed at halftime, and he conceded another two goals as one of few retained starters on Wednesday evening. It’s not been the best spell for Guéhi.

LB: Joško Gvardiol—Nico O’Reilly continues to push the 24-year-old at left back, but the England international played the entirety of the first match with Brighton, leaving the door open for Gvardiol’s return.

CM: Elliot Anderson—Anderson has made an outstanding start to his City career, instantly filling the shoes of Rodri in admirable fashion. After Erling Haaland, the midfielder is the next guaranteed name on the teamsheet.

CM: Enzo Fernández—It’s been a steady introduction for Fernández, who is yet to reach the peak of his powers in a light blue jersey. He could use a statement performance against Brighton having been overshadowed by Anderson to date.

RW: Iliman Ndiaye—During an off-day at Villa Park, it was Ndiaye who looked most likely to spark City into life. The summer recruit nabbed an assist and consistently wreaked havoc down the right wing.

AM: Rayan Cherki—Maresca will be wary of overloading Cherki, who has already played 13 times this season, but City find it difficult to replace his creativity in attacking zones. He’s already delivered six goals and three assists.

LW: Jérémy Doku—City’s turbo-charged winger will likely return to the starting lineup. They need consistent performances from him moving forward given Antoine Semenyo will be missing until after the November international break.

ST: Erling Haaland—Haaland leads the Premier League for goals scored this season with an impressive haul of nine. He’s also netted seven times in as many matches with Brighton previously, only blanking once against them.

ftbpro_01m66q5tf1yb.title: ‘How Champions Respond’—Hansi Flick Reveals How Lamine Yamal Reacted to Ballon d’Or Snub
ftbpro_01m66q5tf1yb.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas2:30 PM EDTHansi Flick (right) recently said that Lamine Yamal deserved to win the Ballon d’Or. / Alex Caparros/Getty ImagesBarcelona manager Hansi Flick believes Lamine Yamal has reacted impressively to coming up short in the 2026 Ballon d’Or voting, stating he’s responded like a “champion” to the disappointing result.

For the second year in a row, Yamal had to sit and clap as another player took home soccer’s most prestigious individual honor. A year after coming second to Ousmane Dembélé, the teenager finished on the Ballon d’Or podium again, this time behind Kylian Mbappé and winner Harry Kane.

Although you could see the disappointment on Yamal’s face after missing out once again, he congratulated Kane and declared his time “will come.” Yamal stated his focus is now back to helping Barcelona achieve success, and on the eve of their weekend clash against Alavés, Flick praised the way his star player handled the Ballon d’Or snub.

“I’m very proud of Lamine,” Flick said. “Because he reacted very good, in my opinion. And what I see also in the training, he’s very focused and this is the way how champions respond. He’s doing a very good job at the moment and I’m very happy that he’s on this way. His mentality is also very good for the team.”
Captains armband. 19-years-old. pic.twitter.com/5pLwvuvtNj

Yamal didn’t return from the gala in London empty-handed, winning the Kopa Trophy as the best young talent in the world for the third year in a row. Still, Yamal confessed he wished the honor had gone to Barcelona teammate Pau Cubarsí, which is something Flick also appreciated.

“I said this to him and also to the team,” Flick added. “The words he said after the trophy he got, about  Pau Cubarsí, it was great for me. Pau normally deserved to win this trophy. Because Lamine, the last two seasons he won it also.
“For me it’s the best time to give Pau Cubarsí this trophy, because he played an unbelievable last season and also he played an excellent World Cup.”

Lamine Yamal is having a fantastic start of the season.  / Ibrahim Ezzat/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFlick has shown little interest in Ballon d’Or scrutiny during each of the last two years in which Yamal has been a serious contender, even looking slightly annoyed when he revealed a couple of his players were traveling to London for Monday’s ceremony 24 hours after losing to Real Madrid in El Clásico.

Still, Yamal clearly cares about adding a Ballon d’Or to his résumé, evidenced by the lengthy public campaign he went on to make his winning case. Although Flick wasn’t overly impressed by Yamal’s tactics, he also said he’d support his claim.

“I would not prefer this,” Flick said about Yamal’s campaigning. “But he is doing it, and has the self-confidence, he wants to win the Ballon d’Or. This is normal as a player, this is an important thing, and important trophy. I will support him.”
Earlier in the season, Flick insisted that Yamal “deserves to win the Ballon d’Or,” and after Barcelona’s recent victory against Real Betis, he anointed him as the world’s best.

“This is, for me, at the moment, the best player in the world,” said the Barça boss. “I’m very happy with his performance and this is what I want to see. And of course he has a lot of pressure, he’s 19 and he played in the past almost every game, also with the national team.
“But he’s 100% focused and committed with everything and this is really good. It’s amazing, his performance and his attitude and this is how big, big players are.”

Barcelona have lost consecutive games for the first time since February.  / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesFor Yamal to get over the hump and finally collect the Ballon d’Or next year, steering Barcelona to the summit of Spanish and European soccer is a must.

Both him and Barça started the season with a dream 11-game unbeaten run, but the shine has somewhat disappeared after losses against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in the past week. The defeats were two significant blows and Yamal was largely anonymous in both games, but Flick is confident his team can correct course with the season still in its infancy.

“It’s a long, long way to the end of the season where you can win the title,” Flick said on Friday. “Now is a good moment, nothing happened really bad. Of course we lost against Real Madrid, no one here loves it, the players don’t, I don’t, the fans don’t, the club don’t.
“But at the end we have to manage it, and how I said before, I think it was possible to win this game. But we have to accept this defeat and we’ll do it, and we’ll learn from it.”

Yamal is the first player in Europe’s top-five leagues to register double-digit goals and assists this term. After a couple of subpar showings in two defeats, and fueled by the heartbreak of another Ballon d‘Or snub, the teenager will be eager to help Barça return to winning ways against Alavés on Saturday.

ftbpro_01m66qg4rjcq.title: Christian Pulisic Puts Definitive End to AC Milan Future Speculation
ftbpro_01m66qg4rjcq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom1:05 PM EDTChristian Pulisic will be in Milan for the long term. / Tiziano Ballabio/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesChristian Pulisic has officially signed a new contract with Italian giants AC Milan through the summer of 2031, ensuring that he will still be in Serie A by the time the next World Cup kicks off.

The star U.S. forward has spent the previous three years at San Siro after leaving Chelsea in a deal worth around €21 million ($23.4 million at current exchange rates). The most prolific years of his European career have come in Milan’s red and black, although he endured a dip in form last term before embarking upon an intriguing new chapter under Ruben Amorim this season.
While Pulisic may have been in and out of the former Manchester United boss’s immediate plans, Milan have made it clear that the Pennsylvania product has a long future at the club.

A brief statement released on Friday announced that Pulisic had signed new terms until June 30, 2031. “Captain America’s Rossonero mission continues,” the club’s social media account wrote above a quote from the player himself: “Milan has given me everything. It feels like home and I’m in love with the club.”
That affection is mutual, but it remains to be seen whether the ramifications of Pulisic’s decision are quite as positive.

It’s never been a faultless relationship between Mauricio Pochettino (left) and Christian Pulisic. / Bob Kupbens/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesU.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino has endured a spiky relationship with Pulisic. The seeds of doubt were sewn when the Milan forward requested to skip the 2025 Gold Cup after a draining European campaign in Italy. Pulisic, however, was willing to grace the USMNT with his presence for the two pre-tournament friendlies. Pochettino promptly left him off the roster entirely.

Even more than a year on from that indiscretion, that attitude still rankled with the Argentine manager. Without explicitly naming Pulisic, Pochettino fumed in September: “You say, ‘If I play, I have not holidays. I cannot arrive fresh for the World Cup.’ ... You know now that is bull----.”

Pulisic would be welcomed back into the fold ahead of the World Cup—which may as well have only lasted 45 minutes for him—before landing on the naughty step once more. Pochettino left Pulisic off his roster for the last set of fall internationals without providing any substantial explanation.

It remains to be seen if the versatile forward will be back in contention for November’s fixtures but even if he is, Pochettino has already made it abundantly clear that there is a new culture with a new set of players ahead of the 2030 World Cup. By sticking with Milan, Pulisic has not given his international manager any new information to consider. He remains the same streaky goalscorer worn down by the same European schedule for the same fallen giant enduring the same season of highs and lows.

Pochettino’s willingness to put his faith in MLS talent shows that the status of a player’s club now longer carries the same weight it once did for USMNT managers. If Pulisic is to work his way back into the World Cup plans, he will have to prove it on the pitch rather than with his portfolio of elite European clubs.

Christian Pulisic has never played a league game in the U.S. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesFor all Pulisic’s World Cup heartbreak, there was a sense of union between the USMNT’s great hope and his distant public. The winger’s name was at least 10 times the size of the font above ‘USA’ on Fox Sports’ World Cup graphics while the level of support each player received from the crowds was similarly weighted in Pulisic’s favor.

Outside Levi’s Stadium before the round of 32 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina, vendors could scarcely meet the demand for “authentic Pulisic tattoo sleeves.” That fans had these pieces of unofficial memorabilia immediately confiscated by stadium workers just 10 yards around the corner of the entrance didn’t seem to dilute their fervor.

If not quite commensurate, that affection was reciprocated by Pulisic. After reveling in the raucous reception of the USMNT’s World Cup opener against Paraguay on home soil, the most talented member of his nation’s generation gushed: “Being in America, having this crowd around us, seeing the red, white and blue, all our red and white striped shirts in the crowd, it’s awesome.”

In the immediate aftermath of the USMNT’s exit, reports claimed that Pulisic may not be leaving American soil just yet. New York City FC were linked with a sensational move for the 28-year-old, with the club’s chief executive Brad Sims stressing that every MLS club would be keen on such a deal.
“If you ask any of my 29 counterparts across the league if they would be interested in having Christian Pulisic on their team, I’m pretty sure you’d get 29 yeses,” Sims claimed.

However, the NYCFC CEO also made it clear that his franchise—if not every other in North America—would be unable to pry Pulisic away from the riches of Milan unless the Italian giants are willing sellers. As this contract has proven, they are not.

ftbpro_01m66s3tvfkd.title: ‘Toxic Reaction’—Man Utd’s Pursuit of Carrick Replacement Already at Risk
ftbpro_01m66s3tvfkd.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:35 PM EDTMichael Carrick (left) could be replaced by Eddie Howe at Manchester United. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesEddie Howe, one of the leading contenders to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, could be dissuaded from even considering the position thanks to the “toxic reaction” of the fanbase at the suggestion of his arrival.

Michael Carrick remains at the helm of Manchester United for now, but his position at the club is precarious, to say the least. The Red Devils have embarked on an all-too-familiar cycle in 2026, with initial optimism and a distinct upturn in results making way for a much bleaker picture in short order.

The mood at the Theatre of Dreams has soured rapidly at the start of the new season after Carrick was given the job full-time. Not enough was done in the summer to ensure the manager had a roster capable of coping with the increased demands this campaign would bring, and Carrick himself has struggled to balance his side tactically, which wasn’t an issue down the stretch last season.

Players have decried Carrick and the hierarchy publicly, and there‘s an overwhelming sense that the club are mired in crisis once more. Carrick remains resolute, but he seems to be on the brink. Successors are being considered, and one of the potential candidates, Howe, risks being scared off.

Howe is aware of fan sentiment. / David Davies/PA Images/Getty ImagesThere’s reportedly a divide in the Man Utd hierarchy regarding preferred candidates. Former Newcastle United manager Howe is supposedly sporting director Jason Wilcox’s choice, but support isn’t unanimous.

The Telegraph understands that while Howe would accept the job if offered to him, he hasn’t got the impression that Man Utd are in hot pursuit. Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have received backing from elsewhere, while some also want the club to aggressively pursue either Aston Villa’s Unai Emery or Como’s Cesc Fàbregas.

Man Utd supporters are after an exotic appointment, with plenty perhaps erroneously believing that Howe doesn’t move the needle. The aforementioned Telegraph report suggests that Howe would be well aware of the negative fan sentiment surrounding his potential arrival, with prominent online figure and Man Utd fan Mark Goldbridge among those leading the charge against Howe.
Such visceral animosity and the lack of alignment pervading over the club would be enough to deter the ex-Newcastle boss, who worked wonders on Tyneside and at Bournemouth before that.

Jason Tindall was Howe’s assistant on Tyneside.  / Richard Sellers/PA Images/Getty ImagesAs dysfunctional as the past 15 years have been at the Theatre of Dreams, Man Utd remain a seismic institution capable of attracting any player or manager (within reason).

Howe has enough of an ego to back himself to restore the Red Devils to their past glories, but he’d need assurances if Wilcox gets his way after Carrick is fired, which could be this weekend if they’re beaten at Chelsea.

The 48-year-old was influential in recruitment at his previous two jobs, and his track record suggests Man Utd would be wise to appease Howe in the market. While aided by Saudi cash, he was able to morph his Newcastle team into one that nobody in the Premier League wanted to face. They twice qualified for the Champions League under him, and ended their 56-year wait for a major trophy by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025.

Given how poorly Man Utd have recruited in recent years, they’d be wise to hand the keys to Howe, who clearly has an eye for talent and knows exactly who he wants to fulfill specific roles in his system.
Moreover, it’s hard to envisage a world where Howe doesn’t have right-hand man Jason Tindall by his side.

ftbpro_01m66x29ykhx.title: Four La Masia Talents That Could Help Barcelona Navigate Defensive Injury Crisis
ftbpro_01m66x29ykhx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas7:20 PM EDTIt could be a matter of time before Brian Fariñas makes his senior Barcelona debut.  / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesBarcelona are dealing with a major defensive injury crisis that Hansi Flick recognized will force the club to promote young La Masia talents that could feature for the senior team in upcoming games.

The Catalans saw their perfect start of the season come crashing down last week, suffering consecutive defeats for the first time since February in their first significant tests of the campaign against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

To make matters worse, Barcelona lost three defenders to injury in a matter of eight days. Eric García, Jules Koundé and Xavi Espart are all out of action for some time, joining injured center back Andreas Christensen in the treatment room.
As a result, Flick has just four defenders with first team experience at his disposal in João Cancelo, Gerard Martín, Alejandro Balde and Pau Cubarsí.

The Catalans were in a similar position back in the spring when fullback injuries saw Flick grant Espart his senior debut. The German boss hasn’t been afraid to turn to inexperienced La Masia talents during his tenure, and with the January transfer window still months away, Flick will be forced to do it again.
Simply put, Barcelona need options in defense, and there are four La Masia talents that could potentially help solve the Blaugrana injury crisis.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Hafiz Gariba joined La Masia in 2025.  / FC BarcelonaHafiz Gariba might be a completely unknown name in the soccer world, but Barcelona believe they found a diamond in the rough in the 19-year-old Ghanaian.

Barcelona beat Real Madrid in the race to sign the center back at the start of 2025 after initially getting scouted by a Spanish development academy in a trial held in Ghana. He has since progressed through La Masia’s ranks and is now an untouchable at the heart of defense for Barça Atlétic, helping the B team currently top the standings of Spain’s fourth division.

Gariba is known for his impressive speed, which allows him to thrive defending open space and make corrections once other defenders have been left behind—essential traits to succeed in Flick’s defensive system.

The teenager trained under Flick at the start of preseason, but an illness prevented him from joining Barcelona’s preseason tour in the United Kingdom. He’s since returned to full form, and although he’s not registered to play in the Champions League, Gariba could be an option for La Liga matches.
Guillem Víctor has spent a decade at La Masia / Pedro Salado/Getty ImagesIf Flick wants to find another Espart, then promoting fellow versatile fullback Guillem Víctor is the most obvious answer.

The 19-year-old could become the second member of the Víctor family to debut for Barcelona under Flick, following in the footsteps of his brother Pau, who featured during the German’s debut term and is currently playing for Braga in Portugal.

Víctor has been at La Masia for a decade and was part of the U-19 side that won an unprecedented treble in 2024–25, conquering the league, the Copa del Rey and Barça’s third Youth League title. Now, he has started all but one game at right back for Barça Atlétic this season.

Like many La Masia talents, Víctor is known for his versatility, having played almost every position on the pitch during his academy days. He has the traits of a trademark Barcelona player, and the club’s style of play is engrained in his brain.

Like Espart, Cubarsí, Marc Bernal and Lamine Yamal, Víctor is part of Barcelona’s renowned 2007 generation of talents. After training with the first team during the week, it wouldn’t be surprising if he makes the matchday squad against Alavés on Saturday.

Álex Campos has been on the bench for Barcelona’s two most recent games.  / Pedro Salado/Getty ImagesÁlex Campos is the commander of Barça Atlétic’s backline and has been flirting with making his senior debut over the last week, featuring on the bench against PSG and Real Madrid.

Campos was born in 2008 and skipped an age group to join Barça Atlétic at only 16. Two seasons later, the towering defender has formed a brilliant partnership with Gariba and Juliano Belletti’s side has conceded just four goals through eight games this season. The only game Barça Atlétic have lost came at the weekend when Campos was with the first team for El Clásico.

After joining La Masia in 2021, Campos signed a contract extension this summer to stay at Barcelona until 2029. Like most Barça academy defenders, his quality on the ball is one of his best traits, as is his ability in the air. Comparisons are futile, but according to AS, many at Barcelona view him as “Cubarsí’s clone.”
Campos has split time this season training under Flick, and after being included a couple of times in the first team’s squad, a senior debut could be very close for the exciting 18-year-old.

ftbpro_01m671ggaqjc.title: Phil Parkinson Under Pressure, But Wrexham's Record Spending Must Also Be Questioned
ftbpro_01m671ggaqjc.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay6:16 PM EDTWrexham have lost four of their last seven matches in the Championship. / Getty ImagesWrexham need to improve significantly after losing 1–0 to Sheffield United on Friday, a result that puts even more scrutiny on manager Phil Parkinson, but also on the club’s record summer spending.

The Red Dragons entered the match in Championship purgatory, sitting 17th in the table but still six points from both the playoff positions and the relegation zone. That precarious balance meant their trip to Bramall Lane was always likely to influence the mood heading into a crucial run of fixtures.

By the end of the weekend, Wrexham could find themselves closer to League One than the Premier League after another poor performance. Parkinson will face even greater pressure if his side fails to show signs of improvement against Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers next week. However, questions should also be asked of the squad and the club’s summer recruitment.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Wrexham have managed just one shot on target in each of their last two matches. / George Wood/Getty ImagesWrexham won both league meetings with the Blades last season and spent $48 million on seven new signings over the summer. It seems ironic, then, to blame their poor start on recruitment when Sheffield United did not spend a penny on transfer fees during the same window.

Yet even after a club-record outlay, which included breaking the transfer record to sign goalkeeper Anthony Patterson, this Wrexham side is clearly still lacking quality at both ends of the pitch, an issue amplified by injuries to Josh Windass and, to a lesser extent, Nathan Broadhead.

Having struggled on the road for much of the season, Wrexham found themselves on the back foot from the outset at Bramall Lane. Romelle Donovan terrorized Issa Kaboré down the flank, while Jordan Ayew caused major problems with his movement against a defense low on confidence.

Wrexham were forced to sit back, absorb pressure and hope they could capitalize on the few chances that came their way. Sheffield United gifted them possession when Japhet Tanganga attempted to play out from the back, but Lewis O’Brien could only muster a wayward effort that was blocked inside the box.

It was little surprise when the home side eventually took the lead. A better pass from Tanganga carved open the Wrexham defense, allowing Ayew to turn Dom Hyam with ease and fire a low shot toward goal. Patterson could only parry the ball into the path of Ben Brereton Díaz, who finished from close range.
We fall to defeat in Sheffield.🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/gvUjkNKFIF
The goal meant Wrexham have now conceded in each of their last eight matches and kept just two clean sheets all season.

For the second consecutive week, Wrexham went into halftime trailing by a goal without registering a shot on target. Parkinson responded by introducing striker Sam Smith and defender Max Cleworth in an attempt to address the problems at both ends of the pitch. Club captain Hyam was among those withdrawn, with Wrexham short on defensive reinforcement after Dan Scarr and Lewis Brunt were both allowed to leave.

Smith added energy and enterprise to the attack, but it was Kieffer Moore who had the best opportunity to equalize, sending a poor effort over the crossbar. Parkinson’s side certainly carried more of a threat after the break, although they remained vulnerable at the other end.

Sheffield United almost doubled their lead when Ayew latched onto an excellent pass from goalkeeper Michael Cooper, only to be denied by a superb recovery challenge from Ben Sheaf. That moment of hard work and determination embodied the Parkinson teams of the past that have been missing for much of the new season. It was also a rare highlight in an otherwise sloppy performance, with Wrexham repeatedly guilty of giving the ball away cheaply and rarely looking capable of making anything happen in possession.

Having conceded a soft goal and offering little in attack, the harsh reality is difficult to ignore. Wrexham have now won just three matches this season and are without a victory in their last five away games, scoring only once during that run.

It also marks the first time Parkinson’s side has lost consecutive league matches this calendar year. Only Watford (two) have scored fewer away goals than Wrexham (five) in the Championship this season.

Whether those problems are the responsibility of the manager, the players or those in charge of recruitment is for the owners to decide. What remains clear is that while there is still time to turn things around, every defeat makes that task more difficult.

ftbpro_01m672qwjbnp.title: FIFA Won’t Give Equal Pay at the 2027 Women’s World Cup—Here’s Why USWNT Wins Anyway
ftbpro_01m672qwjbnp.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:40 PM EDTEmma Hayes’s squad has an increased prize pot to play for. / Ronald Smits/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesAs if the U.S. women’s national team wasn’t already gunning for global glory next summer, the stakes just got even higher.

The four-time women’s World Cup champions (1991, 1999, 2015, 2019) were utterly humiliated three years ago on an international stage that they have notoriously commanded for decades. The USWNT crashed out in the round of 16 of the 2023 World Cup, losing on penalty kicks to Sweden to mark the team’s earliest-ever exit from the tournament.

The squad may have won the Olympic Games the following summer under newly appointed manager Emma Hayes; however, reclaiming the podium of soccer’s most prestigious competition has remained top of mind.

The Stars and Stripes won’t mind the considerable increase in pay either. FIFA is reportedly planning to drastically increase the prize money for the 2027 Women’s World Cup, per Sky Sports News. Performance-based prizes will amount to $220 million for the 32 teams competing in Brazil, pending approval by the FIFA Council in December. It is a sum that doubles the $110 million doled out at the 2023 Australia and New Zealand tournament and is over seven times the $30 million divided up in 2019 France.
dark. Next. Are USWNT Capable of Winning World Cup? Not Like This. Are USWNT Capable of Winning World Cup? Not Like This

It marks a significant win for the women’s game, but it still does not match the prize money handed out at the 2026 men’s tournament across North America this summer, an ambition FIFA president Gianni Infantino had initially expressed back in 2023.

“Our ambition would, of course, to be able to have equality in payments for the 2026 men's and 2027 Women’s World Cup,” Infantino said before the tournament kicked off. “This is the objective we set to ourselves. FIFA is stepping up with actions not just with words ... but unfortunately this is not the case with everyone across the industry. Broadcasters and sponsors, dear friends, have to do more in this respect.”

The 2026 World Cup—which reportedly generated a record-breaking $15 billion in revenue due to unprecedented ticket resale prices, highly scrutinized commercial sponsorships and broadcast deals—had a record-smashing performance-based prize pot of $655 million to be distributed among the 48 competing nations. If the prize pools were equal for the men’s and women’s tournaments, then 2027 Brazil would see a performance-based prize pot of at least $436 million, which accounts for the 16 less teams competing.
Yet, even despite this giant pay gap, the USWNT players are actually in a unique position of gain.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Trinity Rodman is expected to lead the USWNT to great success next summer. /  Ronald Smits/SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesThe U.S. Soccer Federation agreed to landmark collective bargaining agreements with the men’s and women’s national teams back in 2022, equalizing compensation for the very first time. The CBAs, which run through 2028, made USSF the first national governing body to promise both sexes matching money, and this includes the dollars from the 2026 men’s tournament and the 2027 women’s tournament.

The U.S. Soccer players’ unions agreed to pool World Cup prize money from the men’s and women’s editions of the tournament (2026 and 2027). 20% of that money goes to the the federation itself, while the 52 players—26 men and 26 women—split the other 80% equally.

The U.S. men’s national team earned $16 million in performance-based prize money from FIFA for advancing to the round of 16 this summer, which results in $12.8 million for the 52 players and $3.2 million for the federation. Therefore, each player—the 26 players rostered to the USMNT this summer and the 26 rostered to the USWNT next summer—walked away with around $246,153 in their pockets, excluding any added payments they may have received out of the $12.5 million FIFA initially doled out to each nation in guaranteed compensation.

The same practice will apply next summer, with the USWNT players sharing their prize money with the USMNT players. If the winners of 2027 Brazil earn around 7.6% of the total performance-based prize pot—like the champions Spain did this summer (earning $50 million of the $655 million pot)—then U.S. Soccer can expect to have a payday of $16.72 million for the USWNT winning, excluding any guaranteed compensation for simply competing in the tournament. That would mean around $257,230 for each USMNT and USWNT player.

2026 runners-up Argentina earned $33 million in performance-based prizes this summer, around 5% of the prize pot. Should the USWNT lose in the final next summer, each U.S. Soccer player will pocket around $169,230. If the USWNT crash out of the round of 16 again, each player will earn around $82,584.
