ftbpro_01m674dp8bmm.title: ‘Not in Disneyland’—Mikel Arteta’s Max Dowman Warning After Costly Red Card
ftbpro_01m674dp8bmm.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:00 PM EDTMikel Arteta (right) looked far from pleased after Max Dowman got a red card against Fleetwod Town. / Carl Recine/Getty Images Days after Mikel Arteta was visibly enraged at Max Dowman after the teenager got sent off for the first time in his Arsenal career, the manager has defended his reaction and warned the prodigious winger that “we are not in Disneyland.”

One of the most notable moments of Arsenal’s humiliating midweek Carabao Cup round four elimination at the hands of League Two side Fleetwood Town was the straight red card Dowman received for launching a knee at an opponent following a dangerous tackle that went unpunished.

Perhaps even more noteworthy was Arteta’s reaction. Instead of offering some encouragement to the 16-year-old, the cross-armed Spaniard looked furious when he said a few words to Dowman as the young player left the pitch and headed into the locker room.

Arteta later explained that his words had something to do with what he told Dowman and the rest of the team prior to the match, something that the teenager clearly didn’t keep in mind when he lost his head.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

Mikel Arteta didn’t mince words when talking about Max Dowman’s red card.  / Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty ImagesMany were critical of Arteta’s treatment of Dowman following his red card; however, the Spanish boss was quick to double down.

“I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction,” Arteta confessed ahead of Arsenal’s marquee weekend clash with Liverpool. “Whether that’s positive or negative. I understand, but you need to understand the context, the relationship I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

“If you see the reaction of my mother and father with me sometimes, you’d say ‘I don’t like that reaction,’ but for me it was the best reaction ever, to be able to be who I am. But you want, obviously, the best and most beautiful one. You want to see the reaction of his teammates when they have to play with 10 men?

“That’s the reaction, that’s the level,” Arteta added. “Whether it’s right or wrong, that’s the reaction. And the reaction when I don’t win, you know what it is? I’m p----d off, big time. We need to be ready, this is the environment and the reality.

“Otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level, and we look after him so much, like you cannot imagine. But at the same time, we are going to demand him like anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise, the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair, that’s all.”

Max Dowman will mis Arsenal’s next three domestic matches.  / Nick Potts/PA Images/Getty ImagesAlthough Arteta was furious at Dowman, he also recognized the red card incident was judged harshly and voiced his frustration after Arsenal’s appeal to reduce his three-match suspension was rejected by the English Football Association.

“Very disappointed to be fair,” Arteta said on the FA’s decision. “Especially with the reckless tackles that he received but then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action. And yeah, disappointed it’s not being overturned.

“It is what it is,” the Spaniard boss added. “We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Not only the action, obviously, that is so evident when you look it back in slow motion, [but also] the previous action and Max’s action. It’s clear obviously we have a different opinion. And on top of that I think you need to read the context of the player, the age and what happened previously.”

Dowman was lucky to avoid getting seriously injured following the harsh tackle from Harrison Neal that prompted his angry, red card-inducing reaction, with Arteta recognizing “it could’ve been really bad.”
Max Dowman. Youngest in charge. pic.twitter.com/ToBV5rK3XF

Still, Arteta reiterated that Dowman must learn how to keep his composure, because his electrifying style of play will continue to be tested by opponents, as was the case when he got sent off a month ago while on international duty with England U-19’s side.

“We need to be able to tell each other the things as they are,” Arteta said. “Because he’s 16 and we have to be very protective of him, but at the same time very straight with him, with what to expect from him towards the team, the individuals and the club.”

Finally, Arteta confirmed there’s no issue between him and Dowman following Tuesday’s red card incident. With the teenager sidelined for the next three Premier League matches, the Champions League bout against Slavia Prague on Nov. 4 is the only game Dowman could potentially feature in before the November international break.

fuvk7p3c6b561s66ow0vu2529.title: Dallas have a 'championship mentality', says Quill
fuvk7p3c6b561s66ow0vu2529.subtitle: FC Dallas and the San Jose Earthquakes are playoff-bound, and they both want home advantage in the postseason.
paragraphs: Eric Quill lauded FC Dallas' "championship mentality" as they prepare to continue their fine MLS form against the San Jose Earthquakes on Saturday.
Dallas are flying high in the Western Conference, having secured their playoff place already, as they sit third, just four points behind leader Vancouver Whitecaps.

They have lost just one of their last nine league games (W5 D3) and come into this match on the back of a dramatic 2-2 draw with the Houston Dynamo, in which Dallas equalised in the 11th minute of second-half stoppage time.
It was a vital point that keeps them in control of securing a top-four place, which would mean home advantage in the playoffs, and Quill was thrilled with the fight they showed.
"I'm proud of my guys for fighting back. I thought we were the brighter team and created the bigger chances," he said after the draw with Houston.
"We kept scrapping and fighting to get the goal, even with four minutes left in stoppage time, when it could have been deflating.
"We don't lose our fight. That's our mentality. We have a championship mentality, and we're going to keep fighting."
San Jose, meanwhile, secured their playoff berth last time out with a 1-1 draw against MLS leaders Nashville SC.
They are now unbeaten in their last nine matches, drawing each of the last three, and they sit one place and three points below Dallas in the West.
"We're guaranteed at least ninth place, so hopefully we can do well over the next four games and position ourselves to have a couple of games at home," Arena said after securing their playoff spot.
"We're tired, but we can rebound [from the draw with Nashville], and we're ready to play Dallas."
FC Dallas – Petar Musa
With a goal against Houston, Petar Musa became the first Dallas player to reach 20 goals in a single regular season.
Dallas are the 21st different MLS team to have a 20-goal scorer, while Musa is the 32nd player in MLS history to have at least one season with 20 or more regular-season goals.
San Jose Earthquakes – Preston Judd
With 16 goals in 2026, Preston Judd is the fourth San Jose player (Chris Wondolowski – five times, Jeremy Ebobisse, Ronald Cerritos) with at least 15 goals in a single regular season.
Only Wondolowski (27 in 2012 and 18 in 2010) and Ebobisse (17 in 2022) have had more goals in a regular season than Judd.
MATCH PREDICTION: FC DALLAS WIN
Dallas have scored multiple goals in five straight meetings with San Jose, including a 3-2 road win in May.
Dallas' longest streak of multi-goal games in MLS play against any opponent is six straight against Colorado Rapids (2001-03) and the New York Red Bulls (2000-2002).
San Jose do have seven road wins in the 2026 regular season, though, surpassing their six away wins from 2025 and marking their most in a season since recording nine in 2012.
Their 13 road wins over the past two seasons are one more than their 12 MLS road wins from 2020-24 combined.

Dallas have not allowed a goal in any of their last three home matches, though they have only scored two goals (W2 D1). Their longest run of home regular-season shutouts is four straight matches, done two different times in the 2011 season.
San Jose Earthquakes – 23.9%

fzhafkysws3g1ux8fnmoe3180.title: De la Fuente promises 'the best is yet to come' for Spain
fzhafkysws3g1ux8fnmoe3180.subtitle: Luis de la Fuente has penned a long-term contract extension to stay in charge of Spain, and he promised the best is still to come.
paragraphs: Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has vowed "the best is yet to come" from the reigning world and European champions.
De la Fuente has agreed a contract extension to stay in charge of Spain through to the end of Euro 2032.
Since De la Fuente replaced Luis Enrique in 2022, Spain have been dominant.
La Roja won Euro 2024 and then repeated the trick at this year's World Cup.
Spain are on a 38-game unbeaten run in competitive matches, which is a record for a European or South American team.
But De la Fuente insists Spain are not done yet.
"I only think about time and how fragile we are. Life has taught me to be very short-sighted," he said.

"My goal is to arrive in good shape for [Euro 2028]. But of course, I'm especially excited about reaching the 2030 World Cup, but also, now, the 2032 European Championship. We're going to try, with all our strength.
"The best is yet to come. The third star [World Cup crown] would be like something out of a movie."
Spain face England on Saturday before taking on Croatia and Czechia, in their opening Nations League games.

g6qeo1k6ex7o118w0iszxgs6s.title: Bayern made a statement with emphatic win over Leipzig – Kane
g6qeo1k6ex7o118w0iszxgs6s.subtitle: Bayern Munich hit RB Leipzig for six on Saturday, and Harry Kane felt a statement victory was needed for the Bundesliga champions.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich's 6-1 thrashing of RB Leipzig provided a much-needed statement win for the Bundesliga champions.
That is the view of Harry Kane, who set up two goals and scored one of his own on Saturday.
Bayern have become the first team in Bundesliga history to score 18 goals in their opening three home matches of a season, surpassing their own previous record of 17 set in the 2020-21 campaign.
They had 17 shots on target, their highest tally in a Bundesliga match since August 2022, when they managed 20 against Borussia Monchengladbach.
This triumph came on the back of unconvincing displays in draws against Augsburg and Viking, and Kane feels Bayern needed this level of performance.

"After the last two results, I think it was important to make a statement, and we did that from the first minute," said Kane, who scored his 102nd goal in his 100th Bundesliga appearance, more than any other player in their first 100 games in the competition.

"I think we had enough chances in the last two games to score goals and win, but we didn't get the results we wanted. There was more talk than usual, so it was important to keep cool heads and avoid mistakes.
"And we did that from start to finish, from front to back. It was excellent. When you score six goals against an opponent like that, you can be really proud."

Luis Diaz scored his second Bundesliga hat-trick, having previously done so in a 5-1 win against Hoffenheim in February, and was directly involved in four goals in a single Bundesliga match for the first time (three goals, one assist).
"That was really impressive. We were focused and all over them from the start," said Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl.
"We'd caused ourselves issues at times in the last two games. We really wanted to avoid that today. We put Leipzig under so much pressure that they were forced into mistakes.
"At times you can't blame the opposition because we were just so good. The size of the score is also deserved. It was a very good performance.

"We need this stability in the weeks ahead. We had almost 50 shots in the last two games, but there were also moments where we weren't alert enough. We showed what we can do. When the guys see that what we plan to do works, then you also see that joy on the pitch."
Bayern's focus now turns to a Champions League meeting with Arsenal.

g93sxl53vrbt17cur8xphbyb5.title: Roma 4-2 Cagliari: Mora inspires victory as hosts leave it late again
g93sxl53vrbt17cur8xphbyb5.subtitle: Despite being pegged back late on, Roma managed to overcome Cagliari to take all three points at Stadio Olimpico.
paragraphs: Roma extended their unbeaten start in Serie A with a 4-2 victory over Cagliari at Stadio Olimpico.

Gian Piero Gasperini's side found themselves heading for a draw after Daniel Maldini's 81st-minute equaliser, but substitutes Rodrigo Mora and Donyell Malen ensured Roma would stay third in the league.
Cagliari were awarded a penalty after Niccolo Pisilli blocked Michel Adopo's header with his arm, and after a VAR check, M'Bala Nzola coolly slotted into the bottom-right corner in the 10th minute.

However, Roma were ahead by the 21st minute. Emanuele Lulli restored parity with a towering header at the back post from Nahuel Molina's cross, and his whipped cross five minutes later was side-footed in by Pisilli.

Matias Soule almost caught Elia Caprile when his free-kick from the right wing threatened at the near post, while Adopo failed to get enough power on a first-time finish to trouble Pierluigi Gollini at the other end.
Malen and Mora were introduced in the second half, but Cagliari still provided plenty of threat as Alieu Fadera forced a reflex save from Gollini on the hour.

And their persistence paid off as Maldini fired in after impressive work from Adam Obert on the left wing, only for Mora to head in from Daniele Ghilardi's cross five minutes later to restore Roma's lead.

Mora was also at the heart of Roma's fourth, which came 110 seconds after their third, as he drove to the byline before cutting back for Malen, who saw his initial attempt blocked before scoring on the rebound.
Como, meanwhile, completed a late turnaround to defeat Torino 3-1, as Jacobo Ramon, Nico Paz and Martin Baturina all scored after the 81st minute to move Cesc Fabregas' team into the top four.
Gasperini's super subs get Roma over the line

After scoring an 89th-minute equaliser to snatch a point against Napoli last time out, Roma left it late again, albeit they will feel they were worthy of at least a point, having accumulated 3.02 expected goals (xG) on this occasion to Cagliari's 2.4.

Mora made the all-important impact off the bench, creating a joint-high three chances (level with Molina and Soule), while Malen recorded the most shots (four) and touches in the opposition box (seven).
It was also an impressive performance from 19-year-old Lulli, who created two chances, won three of his five duels and recorded two interceptions before being substituted off in the 76th minute.

With his goal and assist, Lulli is now one of the two defenders born from 2007 onwards to have recorded at least three direct goal contributions in the top five European leagues this season, along with Barcelona's Xavi Espart.
Roma remain four points behind leaders Lazio, who thrashed Sassuolo earlier on Tuesday, with an away trip to Cagliari up next for Gasperini's side.

gewkk0ufoqe31p0p0jwxq7m6q.title: Inter 2-1 Fiorentina: Zielinski completes stunning late turnaround
gewkk0ufoqe31p0p0jwxq7m6q.subtitle: Inter looked set to suffer a shock loss to Fiorentina, but turned things around late on to win and leapfrog Lazio to the Serie A summit.
paragraphs: Piotr Zielinski scored a 97th-minute penalty to complete a brilliant late turnaround from Inter and secure a 2-1 win over Fiorentina to go top of Serie A.

It looked like Fiorentina were set to earn a shock victory after Alex Jimenez's goal, with David de Gea frustrating the hosts at the other end, but Marcus Thuram found the equaliser before winning the penalty that ultimately secured all three points.

Inter struggled to make inroads early on, but turned up the heat after the half-hour mark, with De Gea keeping out Thuram with an outstretched leg before clawing a Francesco Pio Esposito header off the line a minute later.
Thuram kept pushing for a breakthrough before half-time, but was again thwarted by De Gea, who got down sharply to push his low strike away.
Marin Pongracic made an impressive block to deny Thuram early in the second half, while De Gea was well-placed to reflexively parry the Frenchman's volley shortly after.

However, Fiorentina broke the deadlock against the run of play in the 65th minute as Nicolo Fagioli intercepted a clearance and teed up Jimenez, who arrowed a stunning long-range effort into the top-right corner.
Carlos Augusto struck the crossbar twice in just over a minute; his glancing header skimmed the top before he got in front of his marker on a corner to flick it behind him and off the frame again.
De Gea once again leapt into action to deny Petar Sucic, but Thuram's persistence finally paid off in the 91st minute as his low shot trickled past the Spaniard and into the bottom-right corner.

Thuram continued to be a nuisance and was dragged down by Valde, with the referee pointing straight to the spot. Zielinski made no mistake when he stepped up, emphatically firing into the roof of the net, giving De Gea no chance.
Thuram spares Inter's blushes

It would have been a huge win – and confidence boost – for struggling Fiorentina against the reigning champions, but Cristian Chivu's side showed their determination to make sure they did not walk away empty-handed.
Despite a slow start, Inter kept the pressure on Fiorentina throughout, and for the most part, the visitors were indebted to their goalkeeper, as De Gea made eight saves.

But Inter showed off exactly what makes them champions and did not give up until the final whistle, with Thuram getting his reward for an electric performance that had looked fruitless until stoppage time.

The Frenchman had nine of Inter's 33 shots, and also topped the charts for attempts on target (four) and touches in the opposition box (13), eventually using the crowded penalty area to his advantage to unsight De Gea.
He is now the third Inter player to score in at least seven consecutive Serie A home matches in the three-points-per-win era, after Romelu Lukaku in 2021 and Christian Vieri in 2003 (11 straight).

Inter were deserving of the victory, racking up 3.4 expected goals (xG) to Fiorentina's 0.24 from seven attempts, but Paolo Vanoli will feel hard done by, especially after his side had the chance to double their lead, only for Ivan Provedel to keep out Wilfried Gnonto's curler.

gj4ejay9b4dt1ftfabc1saz21.title: Bournemouth boss Rose not rushing Kroupi's return from injury
gj4ejay9b4dt1ftfabc1saz21.subtitle: Junior Kroupi has made two substitute appearances since returning from injury, but Marco Rose remained cautious about the Bournemouth star.
paragraphs: Marco Rose revealed Bournemouth "still need to build up" Junior Kroupi to full match sharpness before he can be considered for a place back in the starting line-up.
Kroupi missed the first three months of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a foot injury he sustained in pre-season, having enjoyed a sensational debut campaign for the Cherries.
The now 20-year-old registered 13 goals across 35 appearances in all competitions, helping Bournemouth qualify for their maiden season in European competition.

Kroupi (13) also broke the record for the most Premier League goals scored by a teenager in their debut season, surpassing Robbie Fowler in 1993-94 and Robbie Keane in 1999-00 (both 12), which saw a number of clubs register their interest over the summer.
Arsenal, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona were all linked with a move for the Frenchman, but his injury setback scuppered any chance of securing a move away.
He has slowly made his return to the fold, coming off the bench in Bournemouth's 3-0 win over Manchester United and Wednesday's win over Aston Villa in the EFL Cup.
Ahead of Saturday's visit to Leeds United on Saturday, Rose told reporters: "We still need to build up his game time.
"I'm really happy to have him back, to have his quality, but he knows that he has to be patient in this situation to not get in a difficult situation with another injury.
"We need to get him fit, in a good spot with more and more match time in between good sessions of training."
Bournemouth are also without midfielder Alex Scott, but he is set to return shortly after sustaining a thigh injury while on international duty with England.
However, even with Kroupi and Scott unavailable, Bournemouth have been in sensational form, winning their last five matches across all competitions with clean sheets.
The Cherries last won three Premier League games in a row between August and September last season, but they have never done so without conceding in the competition.
"Even in pre-season I felt we are in a good way and in a good direction," Rose said of Bournemouth's recent run of results.
"The first games were good, but we just missed some situations and made some individual mistakes to concede easy goals and that is why we didn't get results.
"These days, most games are going in our direction, but it's hard work, and we have to continue this hard work."

gjn3gk8sxcnl1qexld1ciwb3s.title: Everton 0-2 Chelsea: Neto shines to end Moyes' unbeaten start
gjn3gk8sxcnl1qexld1ciwb3s.subtitle: Chelsea dominated after the break against Everton, with Pedro Neto bookending the second half with two goals to secure the victory.
paragraphs: Pedro Neto's second-half brace secured Chelsea a 2-0 win over Everton, whose unbeaten start to the Premier League season came to an end.
An entertaining first half did not result in any goals, though Moises Caicedo hit the woodwork, and Neto was the star in a dominant Chelsea showing after the break.
He scored within the first minute of the second half and then secured all three points in the 90th minute, profiting from some poor Everton defending.
The hosts started well, with Emiliano Martinez holding onto Merlin Rohl's drilled effort, before getting fully behind Thierno Barry's glancing header on the set-piece.
Jack Grealish's bouncing volley then needed to be tipped over the bar before Vitalii Mykolenko skilfully opened up space to tee up Barry, who could only poke at Martinez on the turn.
After a couple of flashpoints, Chelsea finished the first half on top, with Caicedo smacking a powerful strike against the crossbar while unmarked during a corner.
And Maxence Lacroix got in front of his marker on another set-piece just before half-time, but his flicked header was cleared off the line by Harrison Armstrong.

Chelsea made a fast start after the break, though, with Morgan Rogers – who may have counted himself lucky to be still on the pitch after a crunching 50-50 tackle with James Garner while he was already on a booking – linking up well with Jorrel Hato on the left, and the deflected cross was turned home by Neto.
Rogers continued to cause problems, with his first-time effort blocked by Rohl before Palmer attempted to catch Pickford out from the edge of the box, but the ball ended up in the stands.

Martinez was stretchered off in the 75th minute with a head injury, and though Everton tried to apply late pressure to Mike Penders, they were instead caught out at the other end as Pickford made himself big to deny Joao Pedro following a Palmer-led counter-attack.

Chelsea eventually breached Everton's defence again ahead of a lengthy 11 minutes of stoppage time. Jordan Henderson's free-kick hit the wall, but the Toffees did not clear their lines, and Neto reacted quickest to slot into the bottom-left corner.
Neto finds his groove on Merseyside

Chelsea have not had a lot of joy on their recent travels to Everton, winning just one of their previous nine such Premier League games (D2 L6) prior to this one, and they lost their first match at Hill Dickinson Stadium 3-0 last season.

However, Xabi Alonso's side made it back-to-back league wins, scoring as many goals on Saturday as they did in their last nine visits, though they had to ride their luck at times, especially in the first half.

Having netted twice in the opening three minutes against Bournemouth last time out, it was a slow start by Chelsea's standards, with this being the second-longest they have had to wait for a goal in the Premier League this season.

Tensions were high in the first half, with five yellow cards, though things settled down after the break, helped by Neto's goal. He has now scored more Premier League goals (12) for Chelsea (76 appearances) than he did for Wolves (111 apps).
This also marked the first time Neto has scored twice in a game in his 187th Premier League appearance.

But while the goals – and ultimately the win – will please Alonso, it is their defensive work that will bring him the most joy as they kept their first Premier League clean sheet in 23 games, ending their long wait for a Premier League shutout.

go94193jbak516w0vulmmmceo.title: Wiegman: Toone's impressive attitude earned England call-up
go94193jbak516w0vulmmmceo.subtitle: England face Greece in a Women's World Cup qualifier first leg on Friday, with Sarina Wiegman calling up Ella Toone to her squad late on.
paragraphs: Ella Toone's impressive response to being left out of England's squad was the reasoning behind her late call up to the Lionesses' fold, says Sarina Wiegman.
Toone, along with Arsenal's Chloe Kelly, were omitted from the initial squad after Wiegman said the pair had failed to live up to expectations for their clubs in recent weeks.
However, Lucy Bronze was ruled out with a minor injury ahead of their Women's World Cup qualifier first leg away to Greece, prompting Wiegman to make a swift replacement.
And she decided to call up Toone, who has netted 24 goals in 69 England outings, as well as winning two European Championships during her time with the Lionesses.

The 27-year-old has failed to score or assist in her first four Women's Super League games with Manchester United this season, and after learning she had missed out on the latest England squad, she revealed her frustration.
"It's about me now, I've got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to keep getting better," Toone said post-match after the Liverpool game.
"I'll use the international break to reset, get my mind focused, and then we'll go again."
And that answer, and her form, impressed Wiegman, who said: "I think when I gave her the call, of course, it was a hard call, and she was very disappointed.
"But the first thing she said was, 'Okay, I'm going to get back, how are we going to do that?' She has support around her too.
"That answer [after the game] and the way she spoke, I thought that was really good."
England are preparing to take on Greece at Pankritio Stadio on Friday, having finished second in their World Cup qualifying group behind Spain.
This will be the first ever meeting between Greece and England, with the Lionesses unbeaten in their last 41 fixtures when facing an opponent for the very first time (W34 D7).

England are also unbeaten in each of their last 15 matches when facing a European nation for the first time in a competitive fixture (W13 D2), scoring 87 goals and conceding just three times. Their last defeat in such a game came in a Women's World Cup qualifying play-off match against France in October 2002.

In League A of the World Cup qualification groups, only Germany (16) won more points than England (15). Likewise, only Spain (21) and Germany (18) scored more goals than the Lionesses (13), with potentially two more play-off matches to come.

The winners face either Slovakia or Ukraine on 26 November and 5 December in another two-leg play-off to decide which team progresses to next year's World Cup, which is being held in Brazil from 24 June to 25 July.
And Wiegman wants her team to put in a comprehensive performance ahead of the second leg in Leicester next Tuesday.
"Of course, that's the main goal," Wiegman added. "We're fully focused on how we want to play tomorrow. What do we expect from Greece?
"We've never played them before. They've done well in that campaign too.
"So we have our game plan ready, being the best we can be, and then we absolutely want to dominate that game tomorrow and win it, of course."

gpbyudt8p0ix1enx8mf2nfplp.title: Columbus boss Courtois emphasises importance of recovery during run-in
gpbyudt8p0ix1enx8mf2nfplp.subtitle: The Columbus Crew have improved their form in recent weeks but are still seven points off the playoff spots ahead of hosting Charlotte FC.
paragraphs: The Columbus Crew's interim head coach Laurent Courtois is confident after his side's recent performances, but he has urged them to recover well ahead of the run-in.
After wins over CF Montreal and Inter Miami, the Crew fell to a late defeat against Orlando City last time out, in their first game after the international break.
Columbus slumped to a 3-2 loss in Florida, despite equalising twice through Taha Habroune and Brais Mendez.
The Crew are now seven points off the playoff places with six regular-season games remaining, while they will also face St. Louis City in the U.S. Open Cup final later this month.
With an important run of fixtures ahead, Courtois believes his players must rest well in between matches.
"We have important games coming out pretty fast," Courtois said.
"We recover, we make sure that we are aware of everything that we want to keep, and modify a couple of things, especially against different opponents.
"We're confident that the group is in a good spot.

"It sucks because coming into that environment [in Orlando] and producing what they've produced and getting out with zero points is really tough. I'm really proud of the way that they performed on and off the ball.
"In terms of performance, it's in the continuity of what they've done the last few weeks, if not months. Yeah, we look forward to the next game, but first, let's recover."
Charlotte, meanwhile, are fifth in the Eastern Conference and just three points behind second-place Inter Miami ahead of their trip to Ohio.
Dean Smith's side pulled off a remarkable comeback last time out, recovering from a 2-0 deficit to defeat FC Dallas 3-2 at home.
Columbus Crew – Taha Habroune
Habroune scored and assisted against Orlando at the weekend and perhaps deserved to finish on the winning side.
Only Orlando's Antoine Griezmann (eight) created more chances than Habroune (six), while the latter also won six of his 11 duels.
Charlotte FC – Idan Toklomati
Only Pep Biel (12) has scored more MLS goals for Charlotte than Toklomati (11) this season, with the latter starring in their turnaround win over Dallas.
Toklomati scored two goals, including the 92nd-minute winner, and assisted the other, while he also created four chances (the second-most).
MATCH PREDICTION – DRAW
Despite losing against Orlando, Columbus have won three of their last four games across all competitions, after winning just one of their previous eight (L7).
However, one of those previous defeats came against Charlotte back in August; Smith's side won 3-1 at home.
Charlotte have lost just one of their last five MLS meetings with Columbus (W3 D1), though Columbus are unbeaten (W1 D1) in both home games during that run.
Nevertheless, only Miami (27), Nashville (23) and the Chicago Fire (20) have won more points on the road in the Eastern Conference than Charlotte this year (18).
Columbus Crew – 41.2%

gqvvjw28apmq1knr0kwh7vxo0.title: Eullaffroy demands Montreal manage emotional 'fear' against Atlanta
gqvvjw28apmq1knr0kwh7vxo0.subtitle: Both Montreal and Atlanta United will be desperate for a win to boost their MLS play-off hopes in the Eastern Conference.
paragraphs: Philippe Eullaffroy will hope CF Montreal can better manage their fearful emotions when they host Atlanta United in Thursday's MLS clash at Stade Saputo.
Eullaffroy warned his side that they must deal with situations better after two late concessions saw them lose 2-1 to rivals Toronto FC last time out in the division.

Montreal conceded in the 93rd and 95th minutes, losing for just the second time in the club's MLS history after heading into second-half stoppage time leading (also 4-3 to Chicago Fire in March 2024).
"We lost the match due to our emotional management during stoppage time," said interim coach Eullaffroy.
"Between the fear of losing the match, and perhaps even the fear of winning it, we made poor decisions during those tense moments."
The defeat left Montreal bottom of the Eastern Conference table and 12 points adrift of play-off contention.
Atlanta are just a place and three points above their next hosts after a 3-1 loss to FC Cincinnati that boosted their play-off aspirations and damaged Gerardo Martino's same hopes.
That marked only Atlanta's second loss in six MLS games, but four draws in that span leave Martino's side with a mountain to climb to make the postseason.
"Cincinnati is the game so far where I would say it was very important [for] playoff implications," Martino said. "An opportunity that we let slip away."
Martino did feel aggrieved with some officiating decisions, though he conceded his team were once again punished for not taking their chances.
"What's happened is that we created chances, but most of the season it's been difficult to convert them," he added.
CF Montreal – Daniel Rios
Either Daniel Rios (four goals) or Prince Owusu (six goals) has scored 10 of Montreal's last 12 regular-season goals, dating back to early August.
Rios will expect to continue his hot run of form here, too. He has scored three times in his last five MLS matches, nearing a record for his personal best.
Indeed, Rios is just one goal away from matching his career high of seven goals in a single season, a feat he achieved in 2022 with Charlotte FC and in 2024 with Atlanta.
Atlanta United – Miguel Almiron
Miguel Almiron looked lively on his return from international duty, scoring Atlanta's only goal in the defeat to Cincinnati.
In fact, he has been involved in a team-high eight goals (five goals, three assists) since returning from the World Cup break.
The former Newcastle United forward has also recorded three shots and as many chances created in six different matches during that period, the most of any MLS player.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Although the Opta supercomputer's predictions suggested Montreal are the narrow favourites based on its data-backed simulations, the draw seems like a real possibility.
Montreal are on a two-game winless streak, while Atlanta's three-match unbeaten run came to an end last time out.
However, Atlanta are unbeaten in four straight regular-season away matches (W2 D2), keeping clean sheets in the last two.
The Five Stripes have only had one longer unbeaten run on the road in club history, a seven-match stretch in 2018 when they won the MLS Cup that campaign.
They also enjoy this fixture. Atlanta have failed to score in only one of their 18 regular-season meetings with Montreal.

Atlanta have averaged 1.8 goals per match (33 in 18) against Montreal, their highest average against any Eastern Conference opponent, but the Canadian side will hope home advantage gives them a chance of at least a point here.
CF Montreal win – 42.4%
Atlanta United – 33.5%

gr5g8mb1c63a159vk164iryzi.title: Arena predicts 'hectic' month ahead for playoff-chasing San Jose
gr5g8mb1c63a159vk164iryzi.subtitle: The San Jose Earthquakes are in the mix to reach the playoffs this season, and their next outing sees them visit the Colorado Rapids.
paragraphs: Bruce Arena says the San Jose Earthquakes' goal this season was always to reach the playoffs, but he knows his team must overcome a "hectic" October to reach their target.
The Earthquakes signed off for the international break with a 3-1 win against the Portland Timbers at PayPal Park, with Preston Judd and Eduard Lowen both on target.
It was a result that extended their unbeaten run in the MLS to six games (W3 D3), leaving them fourth in the Western Conference and one point ahead of the Houston Dynamo.
San Jose take on the Colorado Rapids this weekend, which is the first of seven games to end their regular season, six of which come between now and October 31.
Their standout fixtures include clashes against Nashville SC and FC Dallas, and Arena believes the Earthquakes' next few games will decide the outcome of their season.
"There are a lot of difficult games ahead. So hopefully we can win a few more and position ourselves to be in the playoffs," Arena said.
"Our goal this year is to qualify for the playoffs. We're not there yet. It's not going to be easy. It's going to be a hectic month.
"Our goal all along was to be better and get better every year. We improved from 2024 to 2025. We're making progress this year, and we're continuing to grow."
Colorado, meanwhile, saw their three-game unbeaten run in the league come to an end before the international break, as they went down 3-2 against the Los Angeles Galaxy.
Donavan Phillip and Paxten Aaronson had given the Rapids a two-goal cushion heading into half-time, but Reggie Cannon's own goal got the Galaxy back into it after the break.
From there, Colorado were unable to compete with their opponents, with two goals in eight minutes from Joao Klauss and Justin Haak completing the second-half turnaround.
Colorado boss Matt Wells conceded he had seen this script play out before, citing the goals his team conceded at Dignity Health Sports Park as "terrible".
"This is probably the feeling right now," Wells conceded. "It's not the same movie, but it's one of the most difficult movies. I thought we were very good during the first half.
"We had a lot of players missing, so I had to change things up a bit tactically, but on the whole I think it worked quite well. I really liked the personality we played with.

"It was our typical intensity, and we could have had a bigger lead at half-time. There is the temptation now when you lose 3-2 from 2-0 up at half-time to make the second half a bigger deal and a wider problem than it is, but we just gave three terrible goals away."
Colorado Rapids – Paxten Aaronson
Aaronson (23) and Phillips (21) both scored in Colorado's defeat to the LA Galaxy last time out.
Among the 36 goals scored by the Rapids this term, 28 of those have been scored by players aged 25 or younger (at time of game), and 19 of those by players 23 or younger.
SJ Earthquakes – Preston Judd
Judd recorded his third multi-goal game of the season in San Jose's win over the Timbers.
The only players in Earthquakes' history with more multi-goal matches in a single MLS regular season are Chris Wondolowski (six in 2012) and Jeremy Ebobisse (four in 2022).
MATCH PREDICTION: COLORADO RAPIDS WIN

In each of the last four regular-season matches between Colorado and San Jose, the road team has won. Prior to that, the visiting team had won just one of the previous 20 regular season meetings (D7) in the fixture.

The Rapids have six clean sheets in their last seven home matches after recording just one in their first six regular-season games at home in 2026. Colorado's seven shutouts at home this season are one shy of matching the team’s total across the previous two seasons combined.

San Jose's win over Portland before the international break was their ninth game this season with three or more goals, tied for the second-most games in a single regular season with 2019. The Earthquakes' only regular season with more three-goal games was 2012 (11).
Colorado Rapids – 41.3%
SJ Earthquakes – 32.1%

gri8oerjzzia14g3mxa0nic1r.title: Croatia must 'take special care' of Modric, says Bilic
gri8oerjzzia14g3mxa0nic1r.subtitle: Croatia host England in the Nations League on Saturday, and Slaven Bilic will hope Luka Modric can inspire victory against the Three Lions.
paragraphs: Slaven Bilic believes Croatia must "take special care" of Luka Modric as they prepare to face England in the Nations League.
Croatia started their Nations League campaign with a 2-1 win over Czechia before losing 4-1 to Spain last time out.
Modric opened the scoring in their win over Czechia, which was also the first goal of Bilic's second tenure with the national team.
The 41-year-old was used as a late substitute against Spain, with the world champions comfortably leading at the time of his introduction.
Bilic insisted they will monitor Modric's minutes, but is confident the AC Milan midfielder can make an impact for Croatia.
"Of course, as with many other players, we have to be mindful of his workload, which is why we take special care of him," said Bilic.
"He is simply unique. The old saying is that age is just a number, but with him, it really seems that way and he proves it.
"He simply keeps going because he is unique and because he means so much to the team.
"He is more than a player, more than a captain. He is an icon. His importance can be seen everywhere, at the table, at dinner, in meetings.
"But above all, he is here because he still gives so much on the pitch and makes a difference."
Croatia have won eight of their last nine competitive home matches (D1) since a 1-0 loss to Turkiye in an October 2023 European Championship qualifier.
However, despite losing only four of their last 41 home competitive internationals, three have been in the Nations League (v France and Portugal in 2020 and Austria in 2022).

Bilic's side will play mostly behind closed doors due to crowd disturbances involving Croatia fans during a Nations League match against France in March 2025. There is an exception for schoolchildren, plus 100 travelling England supporters.
Since beating England in the 2018 World Cup semi-final, Croatia are winless in all four games against the Three Lions (D1 L3).

gru5i8m9b6au1402fn21i4rtc.title: Maresca: Ipswich game the perfect chance for Man City to bounce back
gru5i8m9b6au1402fn21i4rtc.subtitle: Manchester City were beaten by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, with Ipswich Town up next in the Premier League.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca believes Saturday's home game against Ipswich Town presents Manchester City with the ideal opportunity to respond to their 4-2 defeat against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.
Maresca watched on as his City team were outclassed by the European champions, with three goals in the opening 32 minutes giving them too great a mountain to climb.
City conceded three goals in the first half of a home game for the first time since November 2015 against Liverpool in the Premier League, but they did respond after the break.

Erling Haaland’s second-half double came either side of Maghnes Akliouche being gifted a goal by Gianluigi Donnarumma's error, but Maresca instantly turned his attention to their upcoming Premier League assignment.
City have won all six of their Premier League games so far this season, and Maresca intends to keep that run going, telling City TV: "It's a chance for us [to bounce back].
"It's going to be tough because they have all week to recover their energy. We need to manage some players, but again, we need to continue our run and try to win on Saturday.”
Maresca did, however, believe his team deserved a lot more against Luis Enrique's side, with defender Marc Guehi saying positives could be taken from their defeat to PSG.
"First half, we needed to do a lot better, me included, for the first two goals," Guehi added. "Second half, I think, it was the complete opposite; we were a lot more aggressive.
"I think every single person knew that if we kept fighting, there was something there. It's only the start of the competition. We can learn from this for future games."
Ipswich go to the Etihad Stadium off the back of a stunning late comeback against Fulham, with Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea scoring in a 2-1 win at Portman Road.

Gary O’Neil's only previous league trip to Man City as a manager saw his Wolves side lose 5-1 in May 2024, while his only game against Maresca was also a four-goal defeat (Wolves 2-6 Chelsea in August 2024).
But Ipswich defender O'Shea wants his team to continue to build on their great start, though he knows a trip to City will be the sternest test of their campaign so far.
"We pride ourselves on having good characters in the group and being fit, strong lads. We work really, really hard, and it's important," O'Shea said.
"It's a great start. Obviously, last time in the Premier League [in 2024-25] we found it difficult and probably got on the wrong end of results, and were unlucky too at times.
"To be where we are after these games is good, but it's got to push us on even more. We can't be happy."
Manchester City – Erling Haaland
Haaland has four goals in two Premier League games against Ipswich, while he's scored 20 goals in 21 appearances against newly promoted sides.

Of players with 10+ games against promoted teams, only Alexander Isak (one every 69 minutes) and Thierry Henry (one every 74 minutes) have a better minutes-per-goal ratio than Haaland (one every 82 minutes).
Ipswich Town – Abdul Ouattara
Ouattara scored his first Premier League goal on what was his sixth appearance last time out, becoming the first Ivorian player to net for Ipswich in the competition.
He also won possession back three times in the final third against Fulham, more than any other Ipswich player, though he may find that difficult to do against Maresca's side.
MATCH PREDICTION: MANCHESTER CITY WIN
City most recently faced Ipswich in the 2024-25 Premier League season, winning both games by an aggregate score of 10-1 (4-1 at the Etihad, 6-0 at Portman Road).

The Citizens are unbeaten in 31 Premier League games against promoted sides (W28 D3) since losing 2-1 to Leeds United in April 2021. They've kept a clean sheet in 10 of their last 12 such matches, while at the Etihad Stadium, they've won all 16 games since that defeat to Leeds, scoring 53 goals in the process.

Maresca's men have also won each of their six Premier League games so far this season – only Chelsea in 2005-06 (first nine) and Liverpool in 2019-20 (first eight) have won their first seven from the start of a campaign, and Maresca could become the first manager to ever win his opening seven in charge of a club in the competition.
Ipswich, meanwhile, have won three of their six Premier League games so far this season (L3), just one fewer than they did in the whole of 2024-25 (W4 D10 L24).
All three of Ipswich's Premier League wins this season have come via 90th minute goals – it's as many 90th minute winners as they scored in their first six campaigns in the competition combined.

However, the Tractor Boys have played 33 away games against City in all competitions and have kept just one clean sheet, with goalkeeper Paul Cooper recording a shutout in a 1-0 win at Maine Road in March 1983.
Manchester City – 73%

gvzf41muug8g1etzes1hbf96q.title: Centurion White wants MLS Cup glory
gvzf41muug8g1etzes1hbf96q.subtitle: Brian White has now netted 100 MLS goals, but his sights are set on leading the Vancouver Whitecaps to a title, not individual records.
paragraphs: Brian White is focused wholly on leading the Vancouver Whitecaps to MLS Cup glory.
White scored his 18th league goal of the season last time out, as the Whitecaps beat San Diego FC 4-1.
The Whitecaps are closing in on clinching the number one seed in the Western Conference, which would give them home advantage all the way through the playoffs.
White's goal was his 100th in MLS, with the 30-year-old having netted double the number of goals this season as any other Whitecaps player (Thomas Muller ranks second with nine goals).
But he is not concerned with individual records.
"Something I've always wanted to get to and had my eyes on, if I'm being honest, to get to 100 goals," said White.
"But at the end of the day, you want to win championships with the team. To see those things are nice, but you want to win MLS Cup.
"I would win MLS Cup, and that's first and foremost on my mind."
Vancouver have scored 67 league goals in 2026, already setting a new club record.
They lost to Inter Miami in last year's MLS Cup showdown.
Their last two regular-season games see them face the Seattle Sounders and CF Montreal.
"We are ready to attack the last two games," said coach Jesper Sorensen. "And hopefully that will be enough also to win the Western Conference regular season."
Vancouver Whitecaps - Brian White
White took the headlines with his milestone MLS goal, but ten different Whitecaps players were involved in one of their four goals in the win over San Diego, the most in a match in club history.
They are the first team since Orlando City against D.C. United in July 2024 to have 10 different players involved in at least one goal in a match.
Seattle Sounders - Dejan Joveljic
The Sounders were shut out by the Houston Dynamo in a 1-0 defeat in midweek, and Seattle might need a big performance from Joveljic.
He has netted only three goals since the end of August.
MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN

The Sounders had 70.5% possession in their loss to Houston on Wednesday. It was the fourth time since Opta began detailed data collection of MLS in 2010 that Seattle held at least 70% of the ball in a regular-season match, but they managed to win only one of those (D1 L2).
The Whitecaps have lost only two of their last 10 regular-season meetings with Seattle (W5 D3), including posting a 2–0 road victory on August 16.
Vancouver last defeated Seattle twice in a single regular season in 2014 when they won two of three meetings (D1).
Seattle have managed just one win in their last 13 away matches in all competitions dating back to early April (D5 L7), a 3-0 victory over the New England Revolution on October 10.
The Sounders have not won an away match against a Western Conference team since a 1-0 win at Houston on April 4.
Vancouver Whitecaps - 49.7%
Seattle Sounders - 24.9%

h19admpk1hzh18lj9dbi5g4ia.title: Romero hails 'incredible' former Spurs team-mate Van de Ven
h19admpk1hzh18lj9dbi5g4ia.subtitle: Cristian Romero and Micky van de Ven started 73 games together for Tottenham and helped them end a 17-year trophy drought.
paragraphs: Cristian Romero has called former Tottenham team-mate Micky van de Ven "incredible" and a player who "has everything".
The two centre-backs spent three seasons together at Spurs before Romero's departure to Atletico Madrid this summer.
Spurs won 34 of the 73 games in which Romero and Van de Ven both started (46.6% – D14 L25), while their win rate dropped to 37.5% when at least one of the two players was absent (P80 W30 D15 L35).
They also scored more goals per game (1.8 to 1.6) and conceded fewer (1.4 to 1.6) when both players started, with their most significant moment coming in the 2024-25 Europa League final.
Spurs defeated Manchester United 1-0 in the showpiece to end a 17-year trophy drought, with Van de Ven denying the Red Devils with an acrobatic clearance off the line.
Romero's time at Spurs ended on a sour note as they survived relegation by the skin of their teeth last season, but the Argentine had plenty of praise for his former team-mate.
"At the club level, at Tottenham, I got to share a lot with Micky van de Ven, and I feel that it was impressive," Romero told Argentinian journalist Gaston Edul.
"He is an incredible player, and he has everything.
"I think obviously it will depend on him, because he is young, where and what he wants to do for his career, because he has it all.
"He has speed, he plays the ball, he is fast, he defends well, defends high, plays well with his feet, is technical.

"Truthfully, at club level, I feel he has been a team-mate that understood me very well from day one and who elevated me. I elevated him, and I also have a very good relationship [with him]. He's a very good centre-back."

h1miee5ch2cj1jwm7oaixs318.title: The Numbers Game: Inter look to overturn miserable derby record versus Milan
h1miee5ch2cj1jwm7oaixs318.subtitle: Inter have a dismal recent record against Milan, but with the Rossoneri enduring an injury crisis, they are favourites for Sunday's derby.
paragraphs: One of the biggest rivalries in European football returns on Saturday, as AC Milan face Inter at San Siro in Serie A.

And the stakes are already high, a mere nine games into the season. Inter's tremendous start has seen them surge eight points clear of Milan, and a victory on Saturday could all but knock their rivals out of the Scudetto picture already.
Ruben Amorim only suffered his first Serie A defeat on Wednesday, but with injuries starting to bite at his Milan squad, the Rossoneri look to be up against it.
But who will emerge with the bragging rights? Here, we delve into the best Opta insights to provide a data-powered match preview.
The Opta supercomputer is siding with Inter ahead of this one, with their win probability standing at 46.9%.
Milan triumphed in 28.2% of the model's pre-match simulations, with the remaining 24.9% finishing level.

Cristian Chivu's side are also strongly favoured to retain their title in our 2026-27 season predictions, doing so in 54.4% of simulations. Milan's Scudetto hopes are only estimated at 3.3%, with Roma (15.6%), Como (12.8%) and Lazio (11.8%) viewed as more likely challengers.

However, despite Inter's superiority in Serie A – they have finished above their rivals in eight of the last nine seasons, the only exception being the Rossoneri's Scudetto triumph in 2021-22 – their recent derby record leaves plenty to be desired.
Indeed, Inter have failed to win any of the last seven competitive meetings between the teams (D2 L5, excluding a 1-1 pre-season friendly draw in August).
It is their worst run against their rivals since going 10 without a victory across all competitions between November 2002 and April 2005.

In addition to three defeats in the teams' last four Serie A clashes (D1), Inter's dire streak includes a Supercoppa Italiana final loss in January 2025 and an aggregate defeat in the Coppa Italia semi-finals during the same season.
Prior to this seven-match winless run, Inter had won five straight derbies, all of which took place in 2023, including both legs of a Champions League semi-final tie.

Milan triumphed 1-0 in both league meetings between the clubs in 2025-26, making Chivu just the third Inter coach to lose his first two games against Milan in all competitions, after Giuseppe Meazza in 1947 and Giuseppe Chiappella between 1975 and 1976.

Following a sterling first campaign at the helm in 2026-27, it feels like the absence of a derby victory might be the one thing that is missing for Chivu, who will be highly motivated ahead of this game.
Injuries leave Milan in tricky spot
Milan and Inter went into Serie A's midweek slate as two of the four teams yet to taste defeat in the division this season.

But while Lazio, Roma and Inter all picked up three points, albeit in unconvincing fashion in the Nerazzurri's case, Milan slumped to their first league loss under Amorim, going down 4-2 at home to Bologna.

Samuel Mbangula's hat-trick condemned the Rossoneri to defeat, as he became just the second player to score an away Serie A treble against Milan, after Gabriel Batistuta for Fiorentina in September 1998.
It was the first instance of Milan conceding four goals in a home Serie A match since January 2023, when they went down 5-2 to Sassuolo.

Amorim said afterwards that his team "looked tired from the first minute", with a series of injuries – particularly in midfield – restricting his options. And Milan had better find some energy from somewhere before Saturday.

Wednesday's defeat was Milan's fifth in home Serie A games since the start of 2026, only the fifth time in the last 50 years that they have hit that figure in a single calendar year, after 1997 (five), 2012 (six), 2017 (seven) and 2021 (seven).
Of course, both teams will be playing on their own turf at San Siro this weekend, but the Rossoneri are the designated 'home' side.

Reports suggest Milan are hoping to recover Mario Gila and Diego Moreira from their respective injuries ahead of the derby, and though Adrien Rabiot, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia and Alexis Saelemaekers are all deemed unlikely to return, Amorim said on Wednesday that he may have to "take a risk" with some players.
Inter look to Thuram to fill Martinez's boots
Inter needed late own goals from Venezia duo Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal to claim a 2-0 victory at the Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on Wednesday.
And Chivu was far from impressed with his team's display, saying afterwards that he wished he could have substituted everyone.
Nevertheless, Inter's 25 points after nine matches are a new club record at this stage of a season in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95).
Even when considering three points per win all-time, this is the joint-best start to a Serie A campaign in their history, alongside 1966-67 and 1988-89.

And unlike their rivals, Chivu's side should be reasonably well-rested after he made five changes to his starting lineup in Venice, with Hakan Calhanoglu, Manuel Akanji, Nicolo Barella, Francesco Pio Esposito, and Henrikh Mkhitaryan all dropping to the bench.

The Nerazzurri's one major fitness issue concerns their captain and attacking talisman Lautaro Martinez, who is likely to be absent once again after sustaining a hamstring issue during a recent Champions League defeat to Club Brugge.

The Argentine has scored nine goals in 21 Derby della Madonnina appearances overall, in addition to providing three assists. He has faced Milan more often than any other club as an Inter player, while he has only provided more goal involvements versus Cagliari (13 – 12 goals, one assist).
His absence is clearly a major blow for the Nerazzurri, but they do have another attacker in tremendous form.

Marcus Thuram has provided at least one goal involvement in 12 of his last 14 Serie A games dating back to a 5-2 victory over Roma on April 5 (11 goals and five assists in total), with only Roma star Donyell Malen (14 goals and three assists) registering more goal contributions since this run began.
PLAYERS TO WATCH
AC Milan – Alphadjo Cisse
With their ranks depleted, Milan will be keen for Cisse to maintain his strong form, after he netted a first-half brace against Bologna.

At the age of 20 years and six days, his double – which took him to four Serie A goals for the season – made him the third-youngest Rossoneri player to net more than twice in the competition during the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95).
Only Alexandre Pato (18 years and 147 days on January 27, 2008) and Stephan El Shaarawy (19 years and 332 days on September 23, 2012) did so at a younger age.
Inter – Piotr Zielinski

Zielinski (two goals, two assists) is one of five midfielders to have scored more than one goal and provided more than one assist in Serie A this season, alongside Rabiot, Nico Paz, Romano Schmid and Mattia Zaccagni.
Among these players, only Rabiot (486) has played fewer minutes in the competition this season than the Pole (533).

h7xm4yhya9qp1bvfflwf0ykr5.title: Malen injury 'not too bad', assures Xavi after Netherlands withdrawal
h7xm4yhya9qp1bvfflwf0ykr5.subtitle: Donyell Malen's withdrawal from the Netherlands squad may have concerned Roma supporters, but Xavi is confident he only has a minor injury.
paragraphs: The injury that caused Donyell Malen to withdraw from the Netherlands' squad is "not too bad", head coach Xavi said in a positive update on the Roma forward.
Malen has been in sensational form since swapping Aston Villa for the Italian capital in January.

Since making his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances in the competition, at least twice as many as any other player in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
He has helped the Giallorossi make a flying start to the new campaign under Gian Piero Gasperini, as they sit top of the table on goal difference heading into the international break.

Like Scudetto holders Inter, they opened 2026-27 with four straight victories, though they did let a 2-0 lead slip in Saturday's head-to-head clash between the top two, a game that saw Malen play the full 90 minutes.
Roma's supporters face a nervous wait regarding Malen's condition after he pulled out of Xavi's first Oranje squad, with reports suggesting it is a knee issue.
But Xavi does not believe it is a serious injury, having discussed the withdrawals of Malen and Justin Kluivert at a press conference on Monday.
"It's a pity, because Donyell is in splendid form, but it happened at the last moment, the same as Kluivert," Xavi said. "That's football, you have to adapt.
"I believe Donyell is okay, that it is not too bad. I don't know how long it will take for him to recover."
Malen has already scored six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, while over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player in the division and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes-per-goal rate in the Italian top flight.
Malen will sit out the Netherlands' Nations League meetings with Germany, Serbia (twice) and Greece, with Xavi's Oranje debut on Thursday pitting him against new Nationalelf boss Jurgen Klopp.

hbjr7uly86ec1owb7dd7qv1uu.title: France 1-1 Italy: Rabiot error denies Zidane victory on home debut
hbjr7uly86ec1owb7dd7qv1uu.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane failed to win his first home match as France boss after Italy held Les Bleus to a draw at the Stade de France.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane was denied victory on his home debut as France boss after Italy fought back for a 1-1 draw at the Stade de France.

Michael Olise's stunning strike looked set to secure France a third consecutive 1-0 win in the Nations League, but Alessandro Bastoni pounced on an error from Adrien Rabiot to rescue a point for Italy, before Dayot Upamecano also saw red.

Although France dominated possession in the early stages, Italy squandered a huge chance to take the lead after Moise Kean shot straight at Mike Maignan from close range following a brilliant low cross from Michael Kayode.

The hosts hit the crossbar when Doue's deflected centre landed on Gianluigi Donnarumma's crossbar, but it was Italy who wasted another big chance before the break as Davide Frattesi's eventual shot from Kayode's long throw was deflected wide of the left post.
France then made Italy pay for their wastefulness 10 minutes into the second half. Rayan Cherki won a free-kick on the edge of the box, and he rolled the ball for Olise to smash in off the crossbar.

However, the Azzurri levelled against the run of play in the 68th minute as Rabiot played Lucas da Cunha into trouble, and Bastoni took full advantage as he won possession and expertly finished past Maignan.

France's hopes of finding a winner took a blow five minutes from time after Upamecano was shown a second yellow card for bringing down Kean, and the visitors managed to hold on for an important point on the road.
France miss Mbappe's magic

Zidane's side prevailed last time out against Belgium without star striker Kylian Mbappe, with Olise providing the goods on that occasion, but the Bayern Munich winger's contribution on this occasion was not enough for France.

Although Olise, Doue and Ousmane Dembele combined for 12 shots, with the latter responsible for six of those attempts, it was only an unstoppable effort from Olise which managed to get the better of Donnarumma, who made seven saves for Roberto Mancini's side.

Overall, Mancini will certainly be the happier of the two coaches. Italy won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.46 to 1.21 despite recording fewer shots (14 to 18) and far fewer touches in the opposition box (18 to 49).
France conceded eight shots before the break, their highest total at half-time of a home match since July 2016 in the European Championship semi-final against Germany (11).

While France remain top of Group A1 in the Nations League, Zidane will know his side must click in attack to give their defenders more to work with; France have scored once in each of their three games.

hi1iq0f80sjm1jy4maebp511y.title: Wales 0-1 Denmark: Hojlund penalty condemns Bellamy's side to third Nations League defeat
hi1iq0f80sjm1jy4maebp511y.subtitle: Rasmus Hojlund's 75th-minute penalty ensured Denmark overcame Wales in Group A4 of the Nations League.
paragraphs: Rasmus Hojlund's penalty was the difference as Denmark overcame a stubborn Wales 1-0 in the Nations League at Cardiff City Stadium.
After Danny Ward pulled off a couple of brilliant stops to deny the visitors, the Wrexham goalkeeper made an error in judgement by bringing down Gustav Isaksen inside the box.
That allowed Hojlund to convert his penalty, with Denmark now sitting in second place in Group A4, six points behind leaders Portugal.

Wales almost found the back of the net in the early exchanges, but Brennan Johnson fired wide from a tight angle before Denmark captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg was substituted after sustaining an early injury.
Morten Hjulmand headed wide of the upright, while Sorba Thomas failed to test Mads Hermansen with a free-kick at the other end.
The visitors should have taken the lead before half-time, but Isaksen was unable to convert his chances, first heading over from close range, and then blazing a wild attempt into the stands.

Ward had to be alert to keep out Hojlund’s close-range strike in the opening five minutes of the second half before making a stunning stop moments later, tipping Isaksen's header onto the left-hand post.
Johnson was presented with a good opportunity, but the Everton attacker could only fire over the woodwork, following an explosive run from Thomas down the left flank.

However, Ward went from hero to villain for Wales after bringing down Isaksen in the penalty area, with Hojlund stepping up to coolly convert the spot-kick into the bottom-left corner in the 75th minute.
Craig Bellamy's side struggled to muster a response afterwards, with Wales now sitting third in Group A4, with one win and three defeats.
Ward goes from hero to zero for Wales
Coming into this game, Wales knew they had to win if they were to have any chance of progressing to the quarter-finals of the competition.
They were indebted to Ward, who made a string of fine saves to keep Denmark at bay. The goalkeeper made three saves, with the one against Isaksen in the second half being the best of the bunch.

However, Ward showed a lack of concentration as he felled Isaksen in the 18-yard box, after conceding possession, presenting Denmark with the opportunity to seal all three points, which Hojlund duly took.
Hojlund has now scored eight goals in his last 10 competitive internationals for Denmark, who have won five consecutive meetings with Wales in all competitions, conceding just one goal.

The visitors deserved this victory, having recorded 13 shots with four attempts on target, reflected by an expected goals (xG) of 2.20. Conversely, Wales' six shots and 0.37 xG were both their lowest in a home fixture in the competition.

hiutuw90pahrz4rldalzpec6.title: 'It's now or never' – Janssen urges Portland to keep pressure on playoff spots
hiutuw90pahrz4rldalzpec6.subtitle: The Portland Timbers are just outside the playoff spots in the Western Conference and want to get back to winning ways against Sporting KC.
paragraphs: Portland Timbers forward Vincent Janssen noted that they are running out of time to clinch an MLS playoff berth and urged his team to continue the push against Sporting Kansas City.
The Timbers are 10th in the Western Conference, but on 32 points, which is only four behind the LA Galaxy in the race for the final wildcard spot with seven games to play.

However, they went into the international break after a slump in form, going winless in four straight matches, and losing each of the last three, including a 3-1 defeat to the San Jose Earthquakes last time out.

Janssen still believes Portland have what it takes to make it through to the postseason, with the Timbers wanting to make up for the difficult position they have put themselves in after recent results.
"It's now or never for the next couple of games," he said. "That's the situation we've put ourselves in, and that's the situation we're trying to get ourselves out of, too.
"I've heard these guys say whenever you get into these playoffs, everything is possible. So, I think that's our goal.
"Get in there, and we'll figure it out from there. But I think we do have the quality and the ability to get there."
As for Sporting KC, they prop up the West with 21 points, but two wins in their last four games have given them some hope.
It looks too late for them to make a playoff push, given the 15-point gap to the Galaxy and a last-gasp 2-1 loss to the Seattle Sounders last time out, but head coach Raphael Wicky remains positive.
"It's a game which hurts because I think we've deserved way more than losing the game in the last minute," he said when asked about the Seattle result.
"But the team have responded really well to that because they feel they performed well.
"The way they have played for the last two months has been interesting and is going in a very good direction, and it gives them more confidence."
Sporting Kansas City – Andre Luiz
Andre Luiz has scored a goal in four straight league games, the first player to do so for Sporting KC since Dejan Joveljic in May-June 2025.
The last longer streak by a Sporting player was Johnny Russell's eight straight games in September-October 2021.
Portland Timbers – James Pantemis

hl8g2s953m0u16yblg5azdqsv.title: Canada 'can beat just about anybody', says Marsch ahead of USA test
hl8g2s953m0u16yblg5azdqsv.subtitle: After Jacob Shaffelburg scored twice in Canada's 2-0 win over Peru, Jesse Marsch said the result proved his team can compete with anyone.
paragraphs: Jesse Marsch believes Canada's 2-0 victory over Peru proved they can beat "just about anybody" and views their upcoming clash with the United States as a yardstick to measure their progress.
A first-half brace from Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg sealed a deserved victory for the hosts in Montreal, maintaining their 100% record in this international break.

Canada, who also defeated Chile 1-0 in their previous game, fired off 17 shots to Peru's four and won the expected goals (xG) battle by 1.94 to 0.23, creating four Opta-defined big chances, compared to their opponent's zero.
Marsch will now go up against his home country, as Canada prepare to face the USA in their final friendly of this international break, in Minnesota on Tuesday.
And he feels that game will be a valuable test, telling reporters after full-time: "I thought we dictated the pace and the way the game was played from the beginning.
"We feel like we could have come away with even more goals.

"We'll keep working on things, we'll keep trying to capitalise on moments and now, when we go to play the U.S. down there, we know we'll face an opponent that has a lot of quality, that is athletic, with a good coach and a good way of playing.

"It'll be a big challenge for us, but we feel confident against any opponent that we play, and if we dictate the terms of the match and control the game the way we like to control it, we feel we can beat just about anybody."
Marsch also highlighted Peru's recent results – including a 1-1 draw with Mexico earlier this week – as further evidence of the quality of Canada's latest performance.
Peru were also competitive against eventual World Cup winners Spain in a pre-tournament friendly in June, losing 3-1, though they went down 4-1 to the USA at the start of this international break.
"It's a credit to the team and a credit to what we're establishing here that we can manage that, because that's a team that gave Mexico a very good match," Marsch said.
"Even if you go back to when they played Spain over the summer, they gave Spain a really good match.
"We made them look worse than they are, because of how we performed."

hlxzeey3f16s1j8aj5m0bnezh.title: Glasner aiming to turn Forest's positive signs into points on Palace return
hlxzeey3f16s1j8aj5m0bnezh.subtitle: Oliver Glasner returns to Selhurst Park for the first time since leaving Crystal Palace, this time in charge of Nottingham Forest.
paragraphs: Oliver Glasner believes there are plenty of positives to take from his early Nottingham Forest tenure, but he acknowledged his team are not where they want to be in the table.
Glasner is preparing to return to Crystal Palace this Sunday for the first time since leaving the Eagles this summer, following a trophy-laden two-year spell at Selhurst Park.
During his time at the club, Glasner won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League before deciding to seek a new challenge following the expiration of his contract.
That has taken him to Forest, where he has overseen an indifferent start to the season. They are 13th in the Premier League with five points from their first five league matches.
Forest entered the extended international break on the back of a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Coventry City, and Glasner wants a response from his players on the road.
"There are many positive signals from the stats; we're very consistent in defence, and we've had the third-most shots," Glasner said.
"But we could have done better. We need to improve the quality of the shots, where we are shooting from and the number of big chances we're creating.
"This is the potential we have in these encouraging signals, but it is our responsibility to get the results from this.
"It's a Premier League game we want to win. We've shown very good away form this year, and this is what we want to show again."
Pierre Sage has also endured a difficult start to life in the Selhurst Park hot seat, with Palace signing off for the international break with a 0-0 draw away to in-form Leeds United.
The Eagles are just one point and two places below Forest in the Premier League, with this the first of three huge straight grudge matches for Palace in all competitions.

Forest replaced Palace in last year's Europa League when the Eagles were expelled due to a breach of multi-club ownership rules involving John Textor, who was an investor in both Palace and Ligue 1 giants Lyon.
Now back in the Europa League, Palace face Lyon after the Forest game, before visiting old rivals Brighton on October 18.

"The two teams are close in the table, close in how they are playing. There is a former manager and player [Daniel Munoz] coming back, which is why [the atmosphere] will be more than normal," Sage said.
"That's why details are important, and the atmosphere is one of those details to deal with in a good way. I hope and expect all the fans will be with us. I know they will be.
"If they can give us 1% more, it will be better for us. But everybody must remind themselves what happened with this manager.
"They won three titles here for the first time for the club. I have big respect for him, as I have for Daniel Munoz, who also left this summer."
Crystal Palace – Anan Khalaili
Khalaili has made 21 tackles in the Premier League this season, more than any other player.
It's the most in a player's first five appearances in the competition since Florentino in October 2025 (21), while the last with more was Joao Palhinha in August 2022 (26).
Nottingham Forest – Morgan Gibbs-White
Gibbs-White has scored (six goals) or assisted (four assists) in each of Forest's last eight Premier League away games.

Only Andy Cole (Aug-Dec 1993), Robin van Persie (Jan-May 2011), and Erling Haaland (Feb-Sep 2023) have ever registered a goal involvement in nine consecutive away appearances in the competition's history.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Palace have never won in 12 Premier League meetings with Forest (D8 L4) – both the most the Eagles have faced a side without winning and most the Tricky Trees have played an opponent without losing in the competition.
Forest have also lost just one of their last 17 league matches against Palace (W7 D9), and are unbeaten in 11 (W3 D8) since a 1-0 Championship defeat all the way back in December 2011.

The Tricky Trees have won all four of their away Premier League matches against London clubs in 2026. Only two non-London teams have ever won 5+ successive Premier League games in the capital: Liverpool (Mar 2019-Jan 2020) and Manchester City (3 times, most recently six from Feb-Aug 2024).

Palace, meanwhile, have won just one of their last 12 Premier League games (D4 L7), beating Fulham 3-2 in September. Since the first match in this period (April 20th), they have earned the fewest points of any ever-present Premier League club (seven), despite playing the most games.

Sage's side have also lost both of their Premier League games at Selhurst Park this season. Only in 1997-98, 2004-05, and 2017-18 have they ever lost their opening three home matches of a league campaign.
Crystal Palace – 36.3%
Nottingham Forest – 34.9%

hmr70hruydzg1mytol6xilo6i.title: Man City great Silva comes out of retirement to play in Hong Kong
hmr70hruydzg1mytol6xilo6i.subtitle: Three years on from his retirement, four-time Premier League champion David Silva will represent Sha Tin in Hong Kong.
paragraphs: Manchester City legend David Silva has reversed his retirement from football to join Hong Kong Premier League club Sha Tin, at the age of 40.
Silva made 309 Premier League appearances for City between 2010 and 2020 – the most by any player for the club.
He scored 60 goals and provided 93 assists in the Premier League – the second-most by any City player behind Kevin De Bruyne's 118 – and won the title four times.

He also lifted the FA Cup twice, the EFL Cup five times and the Community Shield twice during his time at the Etihad Stadium, as well as winning two European Championships and the World Cup with Spain.

Silva retired in 2023 following three seasons with Real Sociedad, having suffered a serious knee injury, but he will now represent a team who sit eighth in the Hong Kong Premier League after four matches, having only won promotion to the top flight last season.
"I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong," Silva said in a video posted to Instagram.
Prior to joining City, Silva started his career with Valencia, providing 46 goal involvements (21 goals, 25 assists) in 119 appearances in LaLiga.
