hqajl9dq1rieztkd8vqjsxcu.title: Kaptein relieved to overcome 'difficult' Women's Champions League tie
hqajl9dq1rieztkd8vqjsxcu.subtitle: Chelsea survived a scare in their Women's Champions League opener, with Wieke Kaptein's goal enough to see off debutants Austria Wien.
paragraphs: Wieke Kaptein expressed her relief at beginning Chelsea's Women's Champions League campaign with a win after battling their way past Austria Wien on Wednesday.
Kaptein's stunning 11th-minute goal proved to be the difference as Chelsea claimed a 1-0 victory, but tournament debutants Wien had several chances to at least earn a point.
After Alyssa Thompson shot wide shortly after Kaptein's fine finish, Wien looked the more likely to alter the scoreline, bringing some good saves out of Livia Peng throughout.
Virginia Kirchberger turned over from close range before Louise Schoffel's effort whistled past the bottom-left corner as the visitors started to dominate at the end of the first half.
Peng had to be on her toes to deny Valentina Potzl and Modesta Uka, with the latter also curling a shot onto the left post in Wien's best chance of earning a deserved draw.
Sonia Bompastor's side were only able to muster an expected goals (xG) total of 1.4 from their 13 shots, while Wien registered a tally of 0.9 xG from two more attempts.
Kaptein acknowledged the difficulties her side faced against Wien, suggesting that her team should have capitalised on their early dominance by scoring more.
"It was a tough game. They put pressure on us and made it a little bit more difficult," Kaptein told Disney+.
"We could have scored more goals, and we needed to punish them more. Overall, we won, it's good, and now we need to focus on the next game.
"For sure [relief]. In the last 10 minutes, we were fighting. We stuck together as a team, but we could have kept the ball a bit better.

"They are a good team, and they are not in the Champions League for nothing. They were really dangerous in our half. But we need to look at ourselves as we could have punished them a little bit more."
Chelsea's victory followed an unconvincing 2-0 triumph against Birmingham City in the Women's Super League last weekend, which continued their unbeaten start in the league.
After beginning their campaign with a frustrating 1-1 draw with Aston Villa, the Blues thumped Manchester United 5-0 but have been far from their best in their last two matches.
They face their sternest test this Sunday against Arsenal, who are two points behind them in the WSL after taking five points from their opening three games.
However, Thompson believes their hard-fought victory against Wien is something Chelsea can build on ahead of their return to domestic action.
"The team came together in the end, and we fought as much as we could. It's a good test for us, for our first game to have a physical battle," Thompson said.
"We are going to play so many different teams and styles during the Champions League, so every test is great for us, and we came out with the three points, so it was a good win.
"The level dropped a little bit, and we were losing tackles, but we got back into the game and were ready for the physical fight.
"At that point, it turned into that, and we knew what game we had to play. We're strong, and we know we can play different styles, so in the end we just had to fight it out."

hvmev0vtnpd51lyyud6cbhf2g.title: Sassuolo 2-6 Lazio: Gattuso's men run riot to go top of Serie A
hvmev0vtnpd51lyyud6cbhf2g.subtitle: After eight goals, two missed penalties and a red card, Lazio left MAPEI Stadium with all three points to go top of Serie A.
paragraphs: Lazio moved back to the top of Serie A after thrashing 10-man Sassuolo 6-2 at MAPEI Stadium.

Despite seeing two penalties saved in the second half, Gennaro Gattuso's side remain unbeaten in the league this season, but could drop down to second when reigning champions Inter face Venezia on Wednesday,
It was a breathless start, with Kenneth Taylor scoring after just two minutes before Kristian Thorstvedt levelled for the hosts, beating Christos Mandas after a pinpoint pass from Josh Doig.

The goals continued to flow, but it was high-flying Lazio who started to take control as Gustav Isaksen's finish from a tight angle was followed up by a clinical strike from Romano Floriani Mussolini in the 16th minute.

Sassuolo were then dealt a huge blow just after the half-hour mark as Thorstvedt was shown a straight red card for a late challenge on Mattia Zaccagni, and though Sebastiano Esposito pulled a goal back for Albero Aquilani's side, Zaccagni restored Lazio's two-goal lead on the stroke of half-time.
The second half followed suit with plenty of goalmouth action, though it all came in Sassuolo's box.
Lazio were awarded a penalty after Simone Cinquegrano blocked Zaccagni's curler with his arm, but the Lazio captain saw his weak penalty saved by Stefano Turati.

The Sassuolo goalkeeper could do nothing in the 55th minute when Tijjani Noslin bent into the bottom-right corner from range, but Turati did manage to save another spot-kick, this time denying Davide Frattesi after Isaksen was hacked down by Duje Caleta-Car.
Nevertheless, Lazio continued to pile on the pressure and Noslin got his second 10 minutes after his first, this time rifling into the top-right corner from distance, leaving Turati with no chance.

Matteo Cancellieri squandered two golden opportunities late on, first heading wide while completely unmarked at the back post before seeing a low drive blocked in the six-yard box, as Lazio could not improve their goal difference any further.
Good omen for Lazio?

Before this encounter, the last Serie A match in which as many as four goals had been scored in the first 16 minutes of play had been Atalanta v Bologna in April 2019, with neither side wasting any time on this occasion.
However, it was Lazio who finished far happier, accumulating 3.39 expected goals (xG), albeit a total boosted by their two penalties, as they made the most of their numerical advantage on the road.

Despite missing a penalty, captain Zaccagni was particularly impressive; along with his goal and two assists, he created the most chances of any player (four), completed the most dribbles (3/4), won the joint-most duels (7/9) and recorded as many as five shots in a Serie A match since December 2023.
Lazio are now unbeaten in their first nine games of the season, achieving this feat for the fifth time overall and the first since 1999-2000, when they last won the Scudetto.
There is still a long way to go for Lazio, but with no European football this season, they may well fancy their chances of challenging Inter for Serie A glory.

Lazio were awarded a penalty after Simone Cinquegrano blocked Zaccagni's curler with his arm, but the Lazio captain saw his weak penalty saved by Stefano Turati.

The Sassuolo goalkeeper could do nothing in the 55th minute when Tijjani Noslin bent into the bottom-right corner from range, but Turati did manage to save another spot-kick, this time denying Davide Frattesi after Isaksen was hacked down by Duje Caleta-Car.

Nevertheless, Lazio continued to pile on the pressure and Noslin got his second 10 minutes after his first, this time rifling into the top-right corner from distance, leaving Turati with no chance.

Matteo Cancellieri squandered two golden opportunities late on, first heading wide while completely unmarked at the back post before seeing a low drive blocked in the six-yard box, as Lazio could not improve their goal difference any further.

Good omen for Lazio?

Before this encounter, the last Serie A match in which as many as four goals had been scored in the first 16 minutes of play had been Atalanta v Bologna in April 2019, with neither side wasting any time on this occasion.

However, it was Lazio who finished far happier, accumulating 3.39 expected goals (xG), albeit a total boosted by their two penalties, as they made the most of their numerical advantage on the road.

Despite missing a penalty, captain Zaccagni was particularly impressive; along with his goal and two assists, he created the most chances of any player (four), completed the most dribbles (3/4), won the joint-most duels (7/9) and recorded as many as five shots in a Serie A match since December 2023.

Lazio are now unbeaten in their first nine games of the season, achieving this feat for the fifth time overall and the first since 1999-2000, when they last won the Scudetto.

There is still a long way to go for Lazio, but with no European football this season, they may well fancy their chances of challenging Inter for Serie A glory.

i19e037wx0lw15bn8hvvtpqdz.title: London City 'building something special' after going second in WSL
i19e037wx0lw15bn8hvvtpqdz.subtitle: Alexia Putellas scored her first Women's Super League goal for London City Lionesses, helping them to a third win of the season.
paragraphs: Alexia Putellas says London City Lionesses want to "build something special" after a 2-0 win over Brighton moved them up to second in the Women's Super League.
Putellas scored her first league goal since joining the Lionesses to help them to the victory that sees them move within three points of leaders Manchester City.

London City dominated throughout and got their reward for their bright start in the 29th minute, with Putellas picking out the bottom corner from the edge of the area after some sloppy Brighton defending.
The Seagulls almost equalised shortly after, with Emily Murphy's looping header hitting the crossbar, and Kiko Seike could only fire wide on the rebound.

Freya Godfrey also hit the woodwork for London City in the second half, but Lucia Corrales made sure of all three points in the 92nd minute by turning in Delphine Cascarino's cross following a counter-attack.
Putellas has been vocal about her hopes of big achievements with London City this season, and she is thrilled to be off the mark for her new club.
"I'm so happy, I'm so proud. The most important thing is we got three points here," she told Sky Sports.
"We are trying to be unpredictable. We can score through possession and counter-attacks; we can do both. I think we achieved that.
"It's a new challenge for everyone; we want to build something special here, and we have to keep pushing and showing up for each other. We want to give our best this season.
"It's the beginning; we just have begun. There's a lot of points yet. We have to improve the same details; we'll be there [around the top of the table] for sure."
London City only just edged the shot count (11 to 10) but had three shots on target compared to Brighton's one.
The visitors also accumulated a higher expected goals total, racking up 1.6 xG, while the Lionesses accumulated 1.3.

London City could drop back down the table by the end of the weekend, with five WSL matches being played on Sunday, but head coach Eder Maestre is confident they can continue to cause problems for the top teams.
"We have the underdog mentality; we're humble but have the target to reach those limits," she told Sky Sports.
"It's temporary, but we're dreaming big, so hopefully we can be in that position later in the competition."

i1fvwn6qnzce1g7k6h5ixx2rz.title: Merino would be 'more valued' in another country, says De la Fuente
i1fvwn6qnzce1g7k6h5ixx2rz.subtitle: Mikel Merino produced another impressive substitute display, scoring two goals off the bench, to help Spain recover to beat 10-man Croatia.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente heaped praise on Spain match-winner Mikel Merino after his double off the bench booked La Roja's spot in the quarter-finals of the Nations League.
Spain came from behind to beat 10-man Croatia 2-1 on Tuesday at Stadion Poljud, ensuring they made it four wins from four to begin their Group A3 campaign.
Ivan Perisic gave Croatia a deserved 13th-minute lead, with the hosts almost doubling their tally soon after, but Unai Simon atoned for an earlier error to deny Igor Matanovic.
De la Fuente turned to his bench at the break and brought on Merino for Alex Baena, and the Arsenal midfielder hauled Spain level with a fine finish just after the hour.

Croatia then had goalscorer Perisic sent off in the 79th minute for a second bookable offence, after a foul on Marc Cucurella, and Spain made their man advantage count two minutes from time when Merino thumped home the winner with his left foot.
Merino has established a reputation as being a key player off the bench for Spain, and he has now scored six goals in 16 substitute appearances for La Roja since the start of 2025.

No player has netted more as a substitute for a European national team in that time, while under De la Fuente, he has scored seven times off the bench, more than any other Spain player during his tenure.
"It's an honour to coach a player like that," De la Fuente said of Merino. "In another country he would be more valued.
"I hope more will be done. Merino is one of the best in the world in his position.
"He has the class to play in any team and can always play, obviously. He knows how to understand these moments of the match.
"He has that gift that is the sense of the goal, for important goals, too."
The result extended Spain's unbeaten run to 43 matches in all competitions (W33 D10), though there were some concerns for De la Fuente.
Spain have now conceded at least one goal in their last four matches (five goals in total), their worst run of consecutive games without a clean sheet since June 2025 (six).

The five goals La Roja have conceded in their last four matches is the same number as in their previous 18, while Croatia were able to edge the expected goals (xG) battle with a total of 1.17 from their 10 shots, compared to Spain's 1.08 from the same number of attempts.
De la Fuente, however, had no doubts that his team would come back to earn the win, describing his side as "ambitious footballers" who always strive to be the best.
"I am proud for many reasons," De la Fuente added. "But it was a game that we knew would go like that, where the opponent would have that attitude.
"We knew how to understand it. In the first half we suffered. It was hard, but in the second we wore down the opponent, we created chances and Merino appeared once again.
"We saw a team that did not give up. This was achieved by very ambitious footballers. They are insatiable. They want more and more.
"They are not satisfied with anything other than winning. If you do everything you have to do to win, you're closer to doing it.
"We are not satisfied with being world champions. There is room to improve. We have to grow as a team."

i2t4lgiizda51ai6125dalujy.title: Mbappe suffered knee hyperextension with France
i2t4lgiizda51ai6125dalujy.subtitle: France will be without Kylian Mbappe for the rest of the international break, with Real Madrid confirming the diagnosis of the injury.
paragraphs: Real Madrid have confirmed that Kylian Mbappe has been diagnosed with hyperextension in his left knee.
Mbappe scored the winner for France in a narrow 1-0 victory over Turkiye, securing Zinedine Zidane a victory in his first match in charge.

However, he pulled up immediately after scoring and was taken off five minutes later, with France confirming that he had withdrawn from the squad to return to Madrid for treatment following the match.
France initially revealed their captain had suffered a tendon injury following the game, with Zidane saying "it's not going well" when asked about it.
While Madrid have not revealed how long he will be sidelined for, Spanish media are reporting he is only set for around two weeks on the sidelines.
Mbappe has already netted six goals in LaLiga this season, making him the first player to score that many goals in Madrid's opening five league matches since Karim Benzema in 2021-22 (also six).
It remains to be seen if he will be available for their first match after the international break against Villarreal on October 10.
Madrid then face Roma in the Champions League four days later before welcoming Sevilla to the Bernabeu the following weekend.

i5mnw08oz72q186guw1m53vs7.title: Zidane lauds Da Cunha displays in France midfield
i5mnw08oz72q186guw1m53vs7.subtitle: Lucas Da Cunha has impressed for France in the Nations League, and Zinedine Zidane spoke highly about the Como midfielder.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane praised the impact Lucas Da Cunha has had in France's midfield during this international break.
Da Cunha started against both Belgium and Italy in the Nations League, with Les Bleus winning the first match 1-0 before drawing 1-1 with the Azzurri on Friday.
Against Belgium, Da Cunha won possession more often than any other France player (six times), while also recording the second-most touches (97) and successful passes (83).
He then created the most chances of any player at the Stade de France on Friday (four), also completing 82 of his 85 passes (96.5%).
However, Da Cunha was involved in the mistake which led to Italy's equaliser, as Alessandro Bastoni pounced on a mix-up between the Como midfielder and Adrien Rabiot.
Nevertheless, Zidane defended the 25-year-old and focused on the positives from his two performances during this break.
"Football is about trying to make as few mistakes as possible. I'm not going to get into the question of whose fault it is. When there's a mistake, it's everyone's fault," said Zidane.
"What do I expect from a midfielder? What he has done, what he is doing and what he is doing.
"He deserves to be here with us, he deserves to have played, like all the others. I really like this player, he has a lot of personality.
"He's not afraid to play. He filters the passes. It's everything I love, he can make those 40-yard switches. He's quite an interesting player."
France are top of Group A1 in the Nations League after three games, and they face second-place Belgium in their final match of the extended break.

i89d3zf9rdegzelk5hbqmer1.title: Hallgrimsson impressed by energy on show in victory over Israel
i89d3zf9rdegzelk5hbqmer1.subtitle: The Republic of Ireland claimed their first Nations League win against Israel on Sunday, with three first-half goals doing the damage.
paragraphs: Heimir Hallgrimsson said he was impressed with the energy of his Republic of Ireland team during their 3-0 victory against Israel in the Nations League.
The Republic of Ireland swept aside Israel at Nagyerdei Stadion, with three goals in the space of 12 minutes from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealing the win.
Parrott opened the scoring in the 13th minute when his shot squirmed under Daniel Peretz after James Abankwah cut the ball back for the in-form striker to finish into the net.
It got even better for Hallgrimsson's side three minutes later when Idah tucked home, with Moylan's fine run ending with a shot that found the bottom corner in the 25th minute.

The Republic of Ireland scored three goals in the first 25 minutes of a match for the first time since October 2014 against Gibraltar (18th min), and only the second time in their history away from home, after August 1996 against Liechtenstein (four in 19th min).
They also enjoyed their joint-biggest win in the Nations League, and outright biggest away from home, alongside a 3-0 victory over Scotland in June 2022.

Hallgrimsson's side had three different goalscorers (excluding own goals) in a single game for the first time since October 2023 against Gibraltar (four), and the Republic of Ireland boss was thrilled with his team's display.
"I must say, I did not expect so much energy for 90 minutes," Halgrimsson said. "There were a lot of empty tanks at the end of the game.
"Given all the circumstances, with the emotions, the bad preparation and all of those things, to have this energy and power for such a long time really impressed me.
"The character was there. In tough times, you find your leaders, they will emerge. These guys showed how much they loved their country. The performance showed that."
The Republic of Ireland finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.57 from their nine attempts to Israel's 0.31 from their eight shots at Caoimhin Kelleher's net.

Israel have now conceded 3+ goals in 11 matches since the start of 2024 in all competitions, the joint-most of any UEFA nation in this time (level with Liechtenstein), with the Republic of Ireland's forwards impressing.

Up to and including the Republic of Ireland's first goal, each of the nation's last seven goals in competitive internationals (excluding own goals) had been scored by Parrott, the longest run by any player for the side.
Moylan, meanwhile, became the first player to score and assist a goal in the same match for the Republic of Ireland since Robbie Brady against Finland, also in the Nations League, in October 2024.

He now has six goal involvements (four goals, two assists) in four senior international appearances for his country, and he will be hoping to add to that tally in the Republic of Ireland's next game against Austria this Thursday.

ic1l0swye6up1788ghbuhiltm.title: Esposito brothers want to 'share the field more often' for Italy
ic1l0swye6up1788ghbuhiltm.subtitle: Francesco Pio Esposito and Sebastiano Esposito both featured for Italy in their Nations League win over Turkiye on Monday.
paragraphs: Francesco Pio Esposito hopes to "share the field more often" with brother Sebastiano for Italy after they both featured against Turkiye on Monday.
Italy ran out 4-1 winners in the Nations League, marking Roberto Mancini's first win since returning to the helm.
Francesco Pio Esposito scored and assisted in the victory, while his older brother Sebastiano Esposito recorded the most shots (three) of any Italy player.

They are the fourth pair of brothers to play in the same match for Italy, after Filippo and Simone Inzaghi (twice in 2000), Aldo and Luigi Cevenini (once in 1915), and Giuseppe and Felice Milano (three times between 1912 and 1913).

Francesco Pio Esposito, meanwhile, surpassed the five-goal mark with the Azzurri at 21 years and 92 days; only two players have achieved this at a younger age: Giuseppe Meazza (19 years and 261 days) and Gianni Rivera (21 years and 78 days).
"I thoroughly enjoyed playing with Seba. It was his first time, so I tried not to overwhelm him with emotions. We had fun, and I'm happy for his debut," Francesco Pio Esposito told Vivo Azzurro.
"Hopefully, we can share the field more often. There was a lot of desire and enthusiasm, which is what you always need when wearing this shirt."
Sebastiano Esposito added: "Mancini told us to enjoy it... Although it's not easy because of the emotions you feel.
"If you're playing for Azzurri with your brother, it's even more complicated. Mancini explained how we should position ourselves and move. It was beautiful."
Italy won an away match with a 3+ goal margin for the first time since November 2019 (3-0 v Bosnia-Herzegovina).
Indeed, the Azzurri have returned to winning with Mancini as head coach after 1,198 days since the last time (3-2 v Netherlands, June 2023).

idsknt1eils211okld1u2o6kh.title: Gyokeres 'extremely happy' at Arsenal despite exit rumours
idsknt1eils211okld1u2o6kh.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres' future at Arsenal was in doubt during the summer window, but the striker is focused on proving his worth in north London.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres insists he is "extremely happy" at Arsenal and wants to fight for his place under Mikel Arteta.
The 28-year-old joined Arsenal last summer and scored 21 goals across 55 appearances as the Gunners won the Premier League and reached the finals of the Champions League and the EFL Cup.
However, the Sweden international has struggled for minutes in 2026-27, starting on just two of his five appearances across all competitions and failing to register a direct goal contribution so far.
Kai Havertz has been Arteta's preferred option so far this term, and he scored three goals across seven games before suffering an injury while representing Germany.
Gyokeres was linked with a move away from Arsenal in the summer, with reports suggesting the Gunners were willing to include him in a swap deal for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.
Despite the rumours, Gyokeres is fully focused on earning more minutes and scoring more goals with Arsenal.
"Of course, there was a lot of speculation," said Gyokeres. "But I had a full pre-season, and it felt good.
"I was fully focused on Arsenal. For me, staying was a given. I'm extremely happy at the club.
"It's clear that I want to play football as much as possible. Hopefully that will come, too. You always want to be on the field as a football player.
"Of course, you expect more playing time, but we have an extremely good squad with a lot of good players and have been doing well here at the start.
"I obviously need to do better and I'm willing to do it, so it's no problem. It's good [the dialogue with the coach]. I just try to do well when I get the chance and score goals."
Gyokeres is on international duty with Sweden, for whom he has scored twice in as many Nations League matches.
He is set to feature against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Romania in the same competition before Arsenal face Leeds United on October 10.

Viktor Gyokeres insists he is "extremely happy" at Arsenal and wants to fight for his place under Mikel Arteta.

The 28-year-old joined Arsenal last summer and scored 21 goals across 55 appearances as the Gunners won the Premier League and reached the finals of the Champions League and the EFL Cup.

However, the Sweden international has struggled for minutes in 2026-27, starting on just two of his five appearances across all competitions and failing to register a direct goal contribution so far.

Kai Havertz has been Arteta's preferred option so far this term, and he scored three goals across seven games before suffering an injury while representing Germany.

Gyokeres was linked with a move away from Arsenal in the summer, with reports suggesting the Gunners were willing to include him in a swap deal for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.

Despite the rumours, Gyokeres is fully focused on earning more minutes and scoring more goals with Arsenal.

"Of course, there was a lot of speculation," said Gyokeres. "But I had a full pre-season, and it felt good.

"I was fully focused on Arsenal. For me, staying was a given. I'm extremely happy at the club.

"It's clear that I want to play football as much as possible. Hopefully that will come, too. You always want to be on the field as a football player.

"Of course, you expect more playing time, but we have an extremely good squad with a lot of good players and have been doing well here at the start.

"I obviously need to do better and I'm willing to do it, so it's no problem. It's good [the dialogue with the coach]. I just try to do well when I get the chance and score goals."

Gyokeres is on international duty with Sweden, for whom he has scored twice in as many Nations League matches.

He is set to feature against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Romania in the same competition before Arsenal face Leeds United on October 10.

igf1gaosvt0k1spb27po4j153.title: Bayern not expected to revive Wirtz interest as Rummenigge surprised by Liverpool struggles
igf1gaosvt0k1spb27po4j153.subtitle: Florian Wirtz has struggled at Liverpool, but Bayern Munich – who were potential suitors last year – are unlikely to move for him.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge does not expect the club to revive their interest in Florian Wirtz in the near future, despite the Germany international's struggles at Liverpool.
Wirtz was coveted by Bayern after helping Bayer Leverkusen win an unbeaten Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double in 2023-24, before he made a €137m (£116m) move to Anfield last year.
But the 23-year-old creator is yet to hit top form under either Arne Slot or Andoni Iraola, only registering seven goals and nine assists in 55 outings in all competitions.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool this season, registering just one assist despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
Wirtz's struggles have prompted speculation that Bayern could look to bring him back to Germany, but Rummenigge pointed out the strong options already available to Vincent Kompany in his position.
"First of all, that's not my job," Rummenigge told AZ when asked about a possible move for Wirtz.
"You mustn't forget that Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry play in that position, and there are other options such as Ismael Saibari.
"There's no need to buy a fourth player for the amount of money Wirtz would probably cost. Whether something else could still be possible at some point? I don't know.
"The question is whether Wirtz is happy at Liverpool. I can't judge that.
"Uli [Hoeness] and I were in contact with his father and mother for a while. Then they made a different decision, and we respected that."
Asked if he was surprised to see Wirtz struggle in the Premier League, Rummenigge replied: "Honestly: yes.
"We were given the impression that he was going to Liverpool because the manager at the time, Arne Slot, had promised him the number 10 position, which he had also played at Leverkusen.
"That was an important factor in his decision to choose Liverpool. Financially, there were no dramatic differences. He made his decision, and we accepted it.
"That's why I say that every step a player takes is something he has to think through carefully beforehand."
Wirtz is currently on international duty with Germany, who have four points from their first two Nations League games under Jurgen Klopp, ahead of Thursday's clash with Serbia.

ih7cimc7ax3i11rr61zpumv62.title: Flick unfazed by PSG and Madrid losses, says season is a 'very long road'
ih7cimc7ax3i11rr61zpumv62.subtitle: Barcelona are looking to bounce back after two straight defeats, and Hansi Flick remains calm ahead of facing Alaves in LaLiga.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick is not fazed by Barcelona's back-to-back defeats, insisting it is "a very long road" ahead of their LaLiga clash with Alaves.

Barcelona had made a perfect start to the season, winning each of their first 11 games in all competitions, but last week, they were beaten 4-2 by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League before going down 2-1 to rivals Real Madrid in a LaLiga Clasico.
Flick's side remain top of LaLiga despite Kylian Mbappe's late goal condemning them to a first league defeat of the campaign, but they now sit just two points ahead of second-place Atletico Madrid.
Injuries have also played their part in those two defeats, and Flick remains calm about their recent results, with all his focus on getting three points against Alaves.
"It's what I've always said: this is a very long road," Flick said in his press conference.
"Nothing is irreversible. We lost against Real Madrid, and nobody likes that, but we have to manage it, and as I said before, I think it was possible to win that game, and we had chances.
"But we have to accept the defeat and learn from it. We have Jules [Kounde] out, Xavi Espart, Dani Olmo, Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen… It's not easy to manage this, and we have to find solutions.
"For [Saturday], we're clear: the most important thing is the three points."
Alaves made a strong start to LaLiga, helping them to sit seventh after 10 games, but they are winless in their last six matches (D2 L4).
However, they have not gone seven or more games without a victory in the competition since January 2025 (P7 D4 L3).
While Barcelona are big scorers this season, netting 40 goals in total, Alaves may feel they have a chance, with the reigning champions also conceding in six of their games so far.
"Ultimately, defending isn't just the defenders' job; even the striker defends," Flick said when asked about their defensive fragility.
"Everyone is involved. To begin with, we can't lose the ball easily. We lost possession a few times against Real Madrid, which isn't good.

"It's something that happens to us often, and we need to play more intelligently, more focused. When we're defending in our own area, it's also important to mark our opponents well, and we didn't do that either.
"We have to improve in these situations. We train it, we take it into account, and we talk about it with the players."
Barcelona – Lamine Yamal
Lamine Yamal has scored 38 goals in 111 LaLiga appearances.
Only Mbappe (41 in 79 games) has netted more goals before turning 20 in Europe's big-five leagues in the 21st century.
Lucas Boye is Alaves' top scorer in the 2026-27 LaLiga season with five goals but has played eight games in the competition against Barcelona without scoring.
Only against Celta Vigo and Sevilla (both 10) has he played more top-flight matches without netting a goal.
MATCH PREDICTION: BARCELONA WIN
Barcelona's 1-0 defeat in May of this year ended their longest unbeaten run against Alavés in LaLiga (16 games – W14 D2).
They have only lost consecutive games against them in the competition on one previous occasion (two defeats between 1999 and 2000).

However, Barcelona are overwhelming favourites to triumph on Saturday and have scored in each of their last 36 home games in LaLiga (108 goals), their longest scoring run at home in the competition since 2014 (56 games, 193 goals).
And Alaves are on their longest winless run away from home against Barcelona in LaLiga (P8 D1 L7), since a 2-1 victory in September 2016.

Barcelona have been trailing for the fewest minutes in LaLiga this season (43) and are one of five teams, alongside Levante, Athletic Club, Real Sociedad and Madrid, who have not dropped a single point from a winning position.

ijepls8n0ygb1ow0k0z4jkxcq.title: Confident Brighton enjoying the moment after fine start
ijepls8n0ygb1ow0k0z4jkxcq.subtitle: Brighton and Crystal Palace were both in European action on Thursday, and the rivals clash at the Amex Stadium on Sunday.
paragraphs: Georginio Rutter says Brighton's squad are revelling in the moment after their fantastic start to the campaign.
Brighton thrashed Kauno Zalgiris 4-0 on Thursday in their first Conference League match.
Rutter scored twice and provided an assist as Fabian Hurzeler's team continued their fine form.
Brighton sit third in the Premier League, having won four of their six games, including beating Arsenal 3-0 before the international break.
The Seagulls are the league's highest scorers (18 goals), and also lead the way for expected goals (12.9).
"It's not every time one player [who scores]," said Rutter.
"We are a good team, everybody scores, and everybody assists, so I think the atmosphere of the team at the moment is very good, so we are confident and in good shape."
Next up for Brighton is a home clash with rivals Crystal Palace.
Like Brighton, Palace were in European action on Thursday. They lost 3-2 to Lyon in the Europa League.
Pierre Sage, who was Lyon's former coach, bemoaned a poor first-half display from Palace.
He told UEFA: "It's a very disappointing return because we lost. I can't take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn't there.
"The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.
"We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.
"I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half."
Brighton – Pascal Gross
Gross has been involved in seven goals in his last five Premier League appearances for Brighton (three goals, four assists), assisting in each of his last three games.
The 35-year-old could become the oldest player with an assist in four games in a row since Gianfranco Zola in December 2002, who was 36 during a five-game streak for Chelsea.
Crystal Palace – Daichi Kamada
Kamada has been involved in four goals in his last four Premier League appearances (one goal, three assists).
The Japan international did not score or assist in any of his first 64 games in the competition for Palace.
MATCH PREDICTION: BRIGHTON WIN

Brighton are the Opta supercomputer's favourites, but they have lost their last two home Premier League games against Palace – they have not lost three in a row at home against their rivals in their league history.
Palace have won three of their last four Premier League games against Brighton (D1), as many as they managed in their first 14 against the Seagulls (D7 L4).

For the fourth time in their last six Premier League seasons, Brighton have won as many as 13 points in their first six games (13 in 2021-22, 13 in 2022-23, 15 in 2023-24, 13 in 2026-27). Only Arsenal and Manchester City (five each) have achieved that tally in more seasons in that timeframe.
Palace have failed to score in four of their last six away Premier League matches, as many as in their previous 26 games on the road.

Brighton are the first side to score as many as 18 goals in their first six Premier League games in a season since Brighton themselves in 2023-24 (18). The Seagulls went on to finish 11th that season, the only time in Premier League history a team had started a season with 18+ goals in their first six games and not finished in the top six.
Brighton – 60.2%
Crystal Palace – 18.9%

j3333qh4ryty1vb7sl2pc56j4.title: World Cup defeat to Argentina most painful moment of England career, says Kane
j3333qh4ryty1vb7sl2pc56j4.subtitle: England were beaten in the semi-finals of this summer's World Cup by Argentina, a defeat Harry Kane said still plays on his mind.
paragraphs: Harry Kane described England's semi-final defeat to Argentina at this summer's World Cup as the most painful moment of his career with the Three Lions.
England were on the cusp of reaching the World Cup final for the first time since 1966 when Anthony Gordon turned in Morgan Rogers's cross in the 55th minute.
However, two late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez completed the turnaround, with Lionel Messi bagging both assists at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Argentina were trailing until the 85th minute against England, the latest a team has been behind but gone on to win in normal time in a World Cup semi-final, making the defeat all the more difficult for Kane.
Thomas Tuchel came under fire for his tactical approach to the match, electing to replace both Gordon and Declan Rice for more defensive options to try and see the win out.

England have now been eliminated in each of their last three matches at this stage of a World Cup (1990, 2018, 2026), while Kane has also been involved in the Three Lions' defeats in the European Championship finals against both Italy and Spain.
However, England's latest setback hurt him the most, with Kane saying: "I'm so passionate about England, especially because I have been on this journey now.
"I have been to the finals, to semi-finals and been so close. Each one hurts in a different way. This one hurt, for sure. More than any other one.
"I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar [in the quarter-final against France] just in the way that it happened.
"It just felt like it wasn't us as a team. It wasn't the team that we wanted to be and said we'd be.

"I sometimes think when you maybe go against your beliefs, and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing in a way where, if we lose doing it our way, you accept it, take it on the chin and move on.
"It's tough and it will still be tough. You have to move on."
The result overshadowed a landmark occasion for Kane, who made his 121st appearance in all competitions for England, the outright most of any outfield player for the nation.
England were, however, able to end the tournament on a high, claiming third place after beating France 6-4 in an enthralling clash at Hard Rock Stadium three days later.
Tuchel's side are preparing for their first match since that victory this Saturday, with World Cup champions Spain their opponents in the Nations League at Wembley Stadium.

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
And Kane said while the pain from such disappointments "stays with you", England must use it as fuel as they aim to reach the next level on the international stage.
"It's something that we haven't quite been able to do in the latter stages of tournaments against the bigger nations and the better nations," Kane added.
"And it may be a mixture of things. It may be personalities, it may be mentality, it may be just the direction and how we want to play in those games.

"I think it's conversations that we need to have as a group and team. Not just sit down but as we gradually go through these next games, through this next period of the Nations League, which we want to try and win.
"We want to try and take that next step because I think that'll be an important step for us as a team.

"I know there's a perception that the Nations League may not be as important, but when you haven't won for so long, I think just the feeling of winning a trophy with England could then catapult us to head into the Euros in a couple of years."

j49lyuo2wnib157sf60kt2alp.title: Ancelotti to maintain new Brazil approach after thrashing India
j49lyuo2wnib157sf60kt2alp.subtitle: Brazil ran out 4-0 winners in their first-ever meeting with India, and Carlo Ancelotti will continue to give his younger players a chance.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti insisted he will continue to give young players a chance after Brazil's comfortable win over India on Friday.
Samuel Lino scored twice in a 4-0 victory, with Estevao and Pedro also scoring in Kolkata, in what was the first-ever meeting between the two countries.
The likes of Arthur Dias (19), Gabriel Bontempo (21) and Andrey Santos (22) all started for the Selecao, while 22-year-old goalkeeper Pedro Morisco also made his debut.
Brazil accumulated 1.2 expected goals (xG) to India's 0.29, with the hosts, expectedly, not offering much threat in the attacking third.
Nevertheless, Ancelotti was pleased to see how his younger players performed, and he plans to name a similar squad for next month's international break.
"We are doing very well in these aspects, we have to give them opportunities," said Ancelotti after the win.
"These are players who have more difficulties, players who don't get playing time at their clubs have more difficulty playing a competitive game, as might be the case with Estevao and Endrick.

"Getting to know these players better, I think Jair Cunha played very well. Bontempo better in the first game than in the second game. Breno [Bidon] came on showing his qualities. Artur Dias was very good, the goalkeepers too."
Brazil have gone unbeaten during this extended international break, drawing and winning against Australia before their victory over India.
Ancelotti's side will return to Asia next month to take on Japan and Singapore in friendly matches.

"Getting to know these players better, I think Jair Cunha played very well. Bontempo better in the first game than in the second game. Breno [Bidon] came on showing his qualities. Artur Dias was very good, the goalkeepers too."

Brazil have gone unbeaten during this extended international break, drawing and winning against Australia before their victory over India.

Ancelotti's side will return to Asia next month to take on Japan and Singapore in friendly matches.

j9y5vgxkjdax1hyiy7x5gf36m.title: Bonucci targets Juventus head coach role in the future
j9y5vgxkjdax1hyiy7x5gf36m.subtitle: Juventus travel to Lecce on Sunday, with the Bianconeri hoping to reduce the pressure on Luciano Spalletti with a win in Serie A.
paragraphs: Former Juventus defender Leonardo Bonucci revealed his dream role is to become head coach of either Italy or the Bianconeri.
Bonucci made 502 appearances for Juve across two spells, which were split by a brief one-season stint with rivals AC Milan.
The centre-back won eight Serie A titles with Juve and four Coppa Italia titles, while also helping them reach the Champions League final twice, losing on both occasions.
Bonucci is currently a part of Roberto Mancini's staff at the Italy national team, though he made clear his intentions to become a head coach himself.
And Juve, who face Lecce on Sunday, would be Bonucci's dream role at club level.
"It is a project that began almost ten years ago. At 30, I had an idea of when my playing career would end and how much time I would need to earn my coaching badges," said Bonucci at an event.
"I am 39 now, and I had promised myself I would become a head coach at 40. Next year, I will complete the final qualification I need to coach at every level.

"But now I am on this journey with the national team, which is enjoyable, exciting and stressful. Perhaps I will put it off for a few years, but the goal is to try to become a head coach, because making it is far from guaranteed.
"Juventus [is the goal] above all. But I think there is a professional side to you that pushes you to accept challenges even when they go against your personal preferences.
"The desire to become a coach pushes you even further. But the dream is Juventus or the national team."
Following Juve's poor start under Luciano Spalletti, who is very much under pressure, they are just two points ahead of their upcoming opponents Lecce.
Lecce head into this contest with plenty of confidence after thrashing Udinese 3-0 last time out.
Lecce – Tiago Gabriel
Tiago Gabriel has scored four goals in Serie A since the start of last season, the most by any defender born in 2004 or later.
Among these players, he also leads in appearances (43), interceptions (54), clearances (274), and aerial duels won (138) in the competition over the same period.
Juventus – Randal Kolo Muani
Six of Randal Kolo Muani's nine Serie A goals for Juventus have been scored away from home (67%).

Among players who have netted at least as many goals for the club in the competition, only Sergio Brio (75%) has a higher percentage of away goals (Federico Chiesa, Michele Padovano and Riccardo Carapellese also have 67%).
MATCH PREDICTION: JUVENTUS WIN
This is the first time in Serie A history Lecce and Juve have faced each other from MD8 onwards with fewer than three points separating them.
Prior to this season, the smallest gap between the two sides after seven games was on MD17 of the 1989-90 campaign (four points in favour of Juve).
Only Inter (13) have won more Serie A away games against Lecce than Juve (12, level with Roma), while there have been five draws and three wins for Lecce.
Lecce have won just one of their 20 Serie A matches against Juve since the 2004-05 season (D5 L14): a 2-0 victory on 20th February 2011, with goals from Djamel Mesbah and Andrea Bertolacci.

Juventus have picked up 11 points so far in this Serie A season (W3 D2 L2); should they fail to win against Lecce, they would have fewer than 14 points after their first eight games in two consecutive seasons for the first time in the three-points-for-a-win era.

jasja5a88gdg12kq75hokms6r.title: Musah aiming to repay faith shown in him by Milan boss Amorim
jasja5a88gdg12kq75hokms6r.subtitle: Yunus Musah has played a big part in AC Milan's strong start to the 2026-27 campaign, forming a strong relationship with Ruben Amorim.
paragraphs: Yunus Musah is hoping to make the most of his second chance at AC Milan after being given a new lease of life under Ruben Amorim.
Musah has become an integral part of Amorim's plans this season after falling out of favour under Massimiliano Allegri and spending the 2025-26 season out on loan.
The 23-year-old joined Atalanta but failed to make an impact, starting six games across all competitions and scoring just two goals.
However, since Amorim's arrival at San Siro, Musah has racked up 419 minutes of action for Milan in his six outings, four of which have been from the start.

And though he is yet to register a goal involvement, his performances have certainly caught the eye. Within the Rossoneri's ranks, only Samuel Chukwueze (11) and Christian Pulisic (five) have completed more dribbles than Musah's four (level with Diego Moreira).
Musah's displays have seen him return to the United States national team after missing out on their World Cup squad, and he has put his resurgence down to Amorim's impact.
"I thought maybe [he was] just saying this like other managers just to keep you there at the club," Musah said.
"But as pre-season was going on, I saw that I was playing a lot, he was talking to me a lot, and it was true. And I started the season, played a lot of minutes, a lot of starts.
"And then now coming to the national team as well, being back here. So it's been a great start to the season, having managers believe in me again.
"As a player, that's what you want really, managers believing in you and letting you play."
Milan signed off for the extended international break with a 3-0 win over Lecce, with Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Moreira all on target in a dominant home win.
The result continued Milan's strong start under Amorim, with the club sitting fifth in Serie A and just two points behind early table-toppers Roma and Inter.
Amorim is only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to remain unbeaten in each of his first five league games, and the first to do so since Massimo Giacomini in 1979-80.
Milan are also unbeaten in their first five Serie A matches for the first time since 2022-23, and they will be hoping to continue that run against Sassuolo this Sunday.

jfiqg8afxo45122d6ogsbdpet.title: Palmer misses too many opportunities to represent England, says Tuchel
jfiqg8afxo45122d6ogsbdpet.subtitle: Cole Palmer was one of five players to drop out of England's Nations League squad, something Thomas Tuchel thinks he will regret.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel believes Cole Palmer has wasted yet another opportunity to play for England after the Chelsea star withdrew from the Three Lions' Nations League squad.
Palmer was a surprise omission from Tuchel's World Cup squad this summer, with an injury-hit 2025-26 campaign impacting his form and resulting in him being left out.
However, Palmer has started the new season with the bit between his teeth, scoring two goals as well as providing two assists in five Premier League games for Chelsea.
But the 24-year-old, along with Declan Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo have all dropped out, with Palmer's reasoning due to a niggling injury.

Palmer has only played three times for England since Tuchel replaced Gareth Southgate, and the Three Lions boss said his latest withdrawal could hinder his chances of future call-ups with the European Championships on the horizon.

"For sure, it's a missed opportunity," said Tuchel in a press conference ahead of their Nations League opener against Spain at Wembley Stadium. "It's another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities.
"I don't blame him for it, it's just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team.

"For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp, there is the next level of impression that you cannot achieve, because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity."
Tuchel said he was not worried players may put their clubs above playing for their country.
"We are not managing the load. When I was in club football, I used the term 'international break' and, when you hear it from the other side, it is a totally different picture," he added.
"It is a competitive environment, but it is also an environment that the players love to be a part of.
"That is what togetherness and brotherhood look like, and that is what we have created since last September in qualifying. We will never compromise on that.
"We will never let it creep in that we have a feeling players do not want to come. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England."
England are preparing for their first match since finishing third at the World Cup, when they beat France 6-4 following their semi-final defeat to Argentina.
And they take on Luis de la Fuente's world champions, who are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation.

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

jn6bt9bizaff1nq2ukzc84ehq.title: De Zerbi sees 'right spirit and character' in Tottenham's draw at Man Utd
jn6bt9bizaff1nq2ukzc84ehq.subtitle: Tottenham's wait for a first Premier League win of the season continued at Manchester United, but Roberto De Zerbi left a happy man.
paragraphs: Roberto De Zerbi is confident Tottenham's first Premier League win of the season is around the corner after seeing "the right spirit and character" against Manchester United.
De Zerbi watched on as Spurs played out a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford on Saturday, despite going behind to Bryan Mbeumo's goal and seeing Rodrigo Bentancur sent off.
The visitors had dominated for much of the encounter without reward, and they were hit with a sucker punch in the 73rd minute when Mbeumo finished past Antonin Kinsky.
It went from bad to worse for Spurs five minutes later when Bentancur was sent for an early bath, after he headbutted Luke Shaw following a coming together between the pair.
However, in the second of eight additional minutes, Dominic Solanke got the better of Lisandro Martinez and glanced Sandro Tonali's teasing cross into the bottom-right corner.

Spurs have now failed to win each of their opening six games of a league season for just the fourth time in their history, after 2008-09, 1955-56 and 1912-13, but De Zerbi said there were plenty of positives for his team to take from their performance.
"I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four," De Zerbi told Sky Sports.
"The second half, it is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.
"We suffered in the game but in every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat.
"We have to react in all the ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kissed Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.
"We win the game if we play as a team. We didn't win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games."

The quality of Spurs' chances were backed up by the metrics, with De Zerbi's side finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.56 from their 12 shots, compared to United's 0.77 from the same number of attempts.
And it looked as though they would come away with nothing until Solanke, who was captaining Spurs for the first time, popped up with a confidence-boosting leveller.
Solanke has netted four Premier League goals against the Red Devils, his joint-most against an opponent (also four vs Aston Villa, Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest).

Meanwhile, the City Ground (four) is the only away venue he has scored more often at than Old Trafford (three) in the competition, and De Zerbi is hoping this latest goal will be the foundation Solanke needs to build on for the rest of the season.
"He is a good player for Tottenham," De Zerbi said of Solanke. "There are not too many strikers better than Solanke.
"Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially at that moment because he suffered because Tottenham didn't score or win any games.
"He is a great guy, a great player and we are behind him. We have to believe in ourselves and this football way.
"If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don't play as a team, it is impossible."

jrgwp331bn481g51kmup6mypt.title: Liverpool 2-2 London City Lionesses: Fernandez's last-gasp own goal denies Putellas and Co
jrgwp331bn481g51kmup6mypt.subtitle: London City Lionesses lost ground in the Women's Super League title race as a late own goal saw them draw with Liverpool on Sunday.
paragraphs: Jana Fernandez scored a 92nd-minute own goal as Liverpool salvaged a 2-2 draw against London City Lionesses at St Helens Stadium on Sunday.
London City appeared set for a fifth Women's Super League victory in a row after Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani struck, following Beata Olsson's penalty for the Reds.
But Liverpool, who dominated the second half, got their rewards in the closing stages, with the unfortunate Fernandez turning Cornelia Kapocs' cross into her own net.
The Reds opened the scoring in the 19th minute when Jenna Clark was brought down inside the area by Mapi Leon, with Olsson ruthlessly dispatching from 12 yards out.
However, London City hit back three minutes later. Khiara Keating was caught dawdling on the ball by Godfrey, who pinched possession and rolled into the empty net.
The visitors completed the turnaround just before half-time through Diani, with the London City striker pouncing on another mistake, this time from Alejandra Bernabe, to score.
Liverpool piled on the pressure after the break, with Elene Lete denying Natalia Ramos' curling attempt before Kapocs clipped the crossbar with a deep delivery into the box.
Gareth Taylor's side got the goal their performance merited in stoppage time, but Liverpool's winless run in the WSL stretched to three matches as they stay down in 10th.
Earlier in the day, Chelsea came from a goal down to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 and temporarily go top of the table, ahead of the Manchester derby later on Sunday.
Molly Bartrip had put Palace into a 20th-minute lead, but a moment of individual quality from Melvine Malard hauled the Blues level as she picked out the top-right corner.
Chelsea and Malard doubled their respective tallies in the 75th minute, with Sandy Baltimore coming off the bench to score a penalty on the stroke of full-time to seal the win.
Aston Villa's resurgence under interim head coach Brian Sorensen also continued, with the Villans coming out on top in a five-goal thriller with Everton, winning 3-2.
London City lose ground as Malard keeps Chelsea unbeaten

After spending big during the summer, London City have made a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign, though they were outfought in the second half against Liverpool and were perhaps fortunate to even come away with a point.
London City registered an expected goals (xG) total of 2.09 from their 10 attempts in the first half, but they were restricted to a tally of 0.08 from the two shots they managed after the break.

However, Liverpool were unable to convert that improved second-half display into three points. The Reds remain winless in each of their last six league games against London City (D4 L2), since a 1-0 away triumph in December 2020 in the WSL2.

But for Chelsea, they can enjoy being top of the WSL for a couple of hours before Manchester City and Manchester United lock horns, with Malard taking her goal tally in the league to four. Only Victoria Pelova (five), Oceane Hurtre (six) and Khadija Shaw (seven) have netted more this season.

In the WSL era, Chelsea have now won each of their eight matches against Palace in all competitions by an aggregate score of 28-1, while they are unbeaten in each of their last 39 WSL games across September, October and November (W34 D5), since a 2-1 loss away to Liverpool in September 2022.

In the WSL era, Chelsea have now won each of their eight matches against Palace in all competitions by an aggregate score of 28-1, while they are unbeaten in each of their last 39 WSL games across September, October and November (W34 D5), since a 2-1 loss away to Liverpool in September 2022.

jtzgzz7rb2t21jtcvhiomcwek.title: De Zerbi hopes Marbella trip creates team mentality for struggling Spurs
jtzgzz7rb2t21jtcvhiomcwek.subtitle: Tottenham will hope to finally get their first win of the Premier League season on Monday, having spent some time training in Marbella.
paragraphs: Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players "need to feel like a team" and hopes their recent trip to Marbella has fostered a positive feeling ahead of hosting Coventry City.
Spurs are still yet to win in the Premier League this season, sitting bottom of the table with a mere three points on the board after six matches.
They showed great fight to recover from a goal down to draw with Manchester United last time out, however, even after Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for headbutting Luke Shaw.

De Zerbi's squad then jetted out to Marbella for a warm-weather training camp ahead of Coventry visiting the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Monday, and the Italian feels that trip has served as a positive bonding experience.
"It's more about the players being with each other, because okay, I'm a coach, I take responsibility, but the responsibility is on everybody, from the boss down to the players," he said.
"They have to feel that they are a team. I think in Manchester, especially in the toughest moment after the red card, we showed we have character.
"So, we have to show character from the beginning at home with our fans, because if we want to, we can change the history of this season – and last season as well."

Coventry looked set for a tough campaign when they lost their opening four games following promotion from the Championship, but they have responded superbly with wins over Nottingham Forest (1-0) and Newcastle United (4-1).
Although Frank Lampard acknowledges Spurs will have high expectations on home soil, he believes Coventry can cause an upset if they maintain their recent levels.
"When I look at them play, they have a lot of quality with a very good coach," Lampard said of Spurs.
"We worry about ourselves and from the start we had on paper, to where we've got to with these two wins, that makes us feel good, so it's not the time for comparisons.
"As we're a promoted side, I'm sure they'll have a feeling of confidence against us. That's fine.
"We have to believe in ourselves and go there with our own confidence and play with the same purpose we did against Newcastle."
Tottenham – Dominic Solanke

Solanke's late equaliser at Old Trafford earned Tottenham a point against United last time out. However, Solanke has now won none of the last eight Premier League games in which he has scored (D2 L6).
Only three players have ever had a longer such run – Steven Fletcher (10 games, Dec 2011 – Sept 2012), Abdoulaye Doucoure (nine, Sept 2017 – March 2019) and Zian Flemming (nine in 2025-26).
Coventry City – Sidiki Cherif
Cherif scored in his first Premier League start for Coventry against Newcastle.
The only three Sky Blues players to score in their first two Premier League starts are John Williams (August 1992), Mick Quinn (November 1992) and Dion Dublin (September 1994).
MATCH PREDICTION – TOTTENHAM WIN
Coventry lost their first four Premier League matches this season, but since then, they have won their last two.
In English top-flight history, only three teams have lost their opening four matches of a campaign then won three in a row – Derby County in 1899-00, Arsenal in 1923-24 and Aston Villa in 1997-98.
The Sky Blues are on their longest winning run in the top flight since January and February 1998, when they posted five straight victories under Gordon Strachan.
However, this game represents a golden opportunity for Spurs to get their campaign up and running.
Only three teams have had more touches in the opposition box in the Premier League this season than Spurs (182) and only two sides have completed more passes in the final third (770).

They rank bottom for shot conversion rate (3.6%) and have underperformed their expected goals (xG) figures by 3.6 goals (three goals from 6.6 xG), but Roberto De Zerbi will hope this is the match where their luck turns.
Coventry City – 23.9%

jwyq4zlrxv61dgyugo49v88g.title: Spalletti unlikely to start Woltemade and Kolo Muani together for Juve
jwyq4zlrxv61dgyugo49v88g.subtitle: Juventus face a tough task to get their Serie A campaign back on track, as they host high-flying Lazio on Sunday.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti has hinted at not starting Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani together when Juventus take on Lazio in Serie A.
Both Woltemade and Kolo Muani scored in Juve's Europa League win over Celta Vigo on Thursday, with the Newcastle United loanee volleying in an equaliser before the latter's stoppage-time winner.

Meanwhile in Serie A, Juve have picked up 11 points from their first six matches this season (W3 D2 L1); in the last 10 campaigns, they have only failed to surpass this points tally after their first seven games in the competition on two occasions: 11 in 2021-22 and 10 in 2022-23.
After their Europa League win, Woltemade stated he wanted to play alongside Kolo Muani, but Spalletti seems to have other plans for Sunday's game.
"We need to expand the range of starters and divide up the time on the field," said the Juve boss.
"Woltemade did well against Celta and, unlike with Cagliari, he managed to put the ball in the net.
"This ability to be ready when opportunity knocks is crucial and rewards those who are most determined.
"Lazio have two physical centre-backs, so it will be difficult to get through them unless we have bodies in the box."
Lazio are still unbeaten in Serie A this season, with five wins and one draw.

The Biancocelesti have avoided defeat in each of their first seven matches of a Serie A campaign on only six previous occasions in their history, but they have never registered six wins (W5 D2 in both 1972-73 and 1999-2000, the season of their last Scudetto).
Ahead of their trip to Allianz Stadium, Gennaro Gattuso has urged his Lazio side to play without any fear.
"We have to go to Turin aware that we are facing a great team that has reaped less than it has sown," said Gattuso.
"What interests me is courage. We have to play a game of mentality, without fear. They are stronger than us, but I want to see a team that takes them on and trades blow for blow.
"Being afraid gets us nothing. We are on a journey and we have to improve game by game.
"We are doing a lot of good things, but I want to see further improvement. No fear, no fright."
Juventus – Randal Kolo Muani

Kolo Muani has been involved in two goals in his last three league games (one goal, one assist); as many goal involvements as he registered in his previous 33 matches across Europe's top five leagues.

Following his goal against Cagliari last time out, the Frenchman could score in consecutive matches in these competitions for the first time since January and February 2025, during his first three appearances for Juventus.
Lazio – Tijjani Noslin

Noslin's first Serie A goal was against Juventus in February 2024 for Hellas Verona (2-2). The Dutchman, who has two goals and two assists in his last three matches, is enjoying his best season in Europe's top 10 leagues in terms of minutes per goal involvement, with a goal or assist every 65 minutes.

In the current Italian top flight campaign, only Edon Zhegrova (one goal/assist every 39 minutes) and Marcus Thuram (one goal/assist every 58 minutes) have a better rate (minimum three goal involvements).
MATCH PREDICTION: JUVENTUS WIN
For the first time in Serie A history, Juve (11 points) will face Lazio (16) during the first half of a season with at least five fewer points than the Biancocelesti.

The last nine Serie A matches between Juve and Lazio have seen a perfectly even record, with three wins apiece and three draws; this follows Juve winning 12 of their previous 15 league games against Lazio (D1 L2).
Juve have beaten Lazio more times than any other side in Serie A (W87 D40 L37) and have scored more goals against them than any other club in the competition, too (290).
The Bianconeri have scored in 13 consecutive home Serie A matches against Lazio (30 goals in total, 2.3 per game on average), though Lazio boss Gattuso is hoping to make some history on Sunday.

Gattuso (W5 D1) could become the first manager in Serie A history to win six of his first seven games in charge of Lazio in the competition; Igor Tudor, Tommaso Maestrelli and Vladimir Petkovic all won five of their first seven.

k0vumt2dvmsh1dkqgfb114h2j.title: Carrick insists Man Utd have 'moved on' after Martinez statement
k0vumt2dvmsh1dkqgfb114h2j.subtitle: Manchester United's preparation for Leeds United has been overshadowed by Lisandro Martinez's post-match Champions League interview.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United have "moved on" after Lisandro Martinez's explosive statement in midweek, and he is confident they can get a result against Leeds United.

Following United's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League – a result which stretched their winless run to five games – Martinez suggested there had not been sufficient investment in the squad.
He also singled out technical director Jason Wilcox, saying "we expect more from the top".
Later in the week, Martinez issued an apology, saying he had spoken to the club and that the issue is resolved internally, though his interview got a lot of fans and pundits talking.
However, Carrick insists the situation has been dealt with, and the squad are unified as they look to earn a win against their rivals in the Premier League.
"I think it's just come out and acknowledged the situation, and, as a group, we've moved on," Carrick said. "It's really not drama for us as a group.
"There's a lot of people who say a lot of things – ex-pros or not ex-pros – it doesn't necessarily mean they understand what is going on here.

"The players totally believe me. Just because people talk on the outside doesn't mean that is the truth. I am telling you the truth. The squad was in a fantastic place [in training on Friday], better than I have seen it for a while. That is it, plain and simple. We are living it every day and know what it feels like.

"We are emotional and care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe you shouldn't say at that certain time, but it doesn't distract us from what we are creating here and the environment and spirit within the group.
"It [the squad] is not affected, I am telling you. We are in a good place, and I am really happy with the boys. I think there was a good reaction."
Asked whether Martinez is available for Sunday, Carrick added: "He is part of the squad."
United are unbeaten in their last seven away games against Leeds in all competitions (W5 D2) since losing 1-0 in the Premier League in September 2002.
But United have just six points in six top-flight games in 2026-27 (W1 D3 L2), their lowest after six league games since 1986-87 under Ron Atkinson (four).
For a second consecutive season, the Red Devils have no clean sheets in their first six games, the first time they have done so in back-to-back campaigns since 1930-31 and 1931-32.
They are also without a win in their last four Premier League games, but while the pressure is rising on Carrick, he noted a victory would be important for more than just him.
"I don't need results. We all need results. It is not about me," he said.
"Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player and anyone else who works at this club.
"It is not about me. I don't go into work every day thinking about this situation thinking about me. It is not about me and not about any individual players; it is about the football club.

"What we stand for and what we live for and the history and things we need to live up to – that is what drives us. Whatever is best for the club and the team on Sunday is the most important thing; it is not about me."

k26118i798ru19zg60owop19m.title: Norway 1-2 Portugal: Ramos punishes Nyland error to seal Nations League victory
k26118i798ru19zg60owop19m.subtitle: Jorge Jesus' strong start to his Portugal tenure continued with a win over Norway, though his team were helped by Orjan Nyland's mistake.
paragraphs: Orjan Nyland's second-half error proved costly as Goncalo Ramos helped Portugal to back-to-back victories in the Nations League after a 2-1 triumph against Norway.
Nyland gifted possession to Ramos, who lofted in the winning goal, with that error coming just three minutes after Erling Haaland had hauled Stale Solbakken's side level.
Joao Felix laid the foundations for the visitors' win in the first half, with Jorge Jesus' strong start to his Portugal tenure seeing his team go top of the Group A4 table.
Both sides started brightly at Ullevaal Stadion, with Joao Neves heading over before Haaland's first-time effort was brilliantly kept out by Diogo Costa at his near post.

However, it was Jorge Jesus' side who took the lead in the 17th minute through Joao Felix, who placed a fine finish from the edge of the penalty area past the dive of Nyland and into the bottom-left corner following Pedro Neto's cutback.

Norway cranked up the pressure at the end of the first half, with Haaland's towering header thwarted by Costa once again, with the Manchester City forward then nodding into the grateful arms of the Portugal goalkeeper in first-half stoppage time.

Haaland, however, was not to be denied his customary goal. Martin Odegaard's free-kick was spilled by Costa, with Patrick Berg nodding the rebound across the six-yard box for the Norway number nine to tuck home the leveller six minutes after the restart.

But no sooner had they got themselves level, Norway fell behind again. A calamitous error from Nyland saw his pass picked off by Ramos, who took a touch before lofting the ball over the retreating goalkeeper and into the net.
Rafael Leao nearly made an instant impact off the bench, but his shot deflected off Fredrik Aursnes and onto the crossbar, before VAR saved Nyland from further embarrassment.
A long ball forward from Costa caught Norway napping and Ramos was able to steal in front of Nyland before finishing, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against him.

The hosts controlled the final 15 minutes, with Andreas Schjelderup forcing Costa into action, but Portugal's defence held firm to make it two wins from two to begin their Nations League title defence.
No Ronaldo? No problem for Portugal

Jesus elected to make four changes to the side that battled their way past Wales on his Portugal bow, with Cristiano Ronaldo, whose seven shots without scoring against Craig Bellamy's side was his most in a game for his country since October 2025, one of those alterations.

But despite a change in personnel, it was one of the starters against Wales in Joao Felix who shone once more. He has now scored six goals across his last 11 starts for Portugal, with his former Al-Nassr boss Jesus getting the best out of him.

The defending Nations League champions were put through their paces by Norway, who were led by Haaland once again. The in-form striker has now scored in 11 of his last 14 competitive games for Norway and City combined (17 goals in total), and in each of his last six (10 goals).

However, a lapse in concentration from Nyland proved costly, with Norway pushing for an equaliser in the closing stages but unable to find a way past Costa, who made five important saves to preserve his team's victory.

Solbakken will feel his team had done enough to take at least a point from the contest. Norway finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.72 from their 22 shots, with 1.69 of that tally coming from Haaland, while Portugal mustered an xG of 1.03 from their 12 attempts.

k5j1x0og8hth1akcd69a5lwq4.title: Lecce 0-2 Juventus: Luiz stars to clinch much-needed win for Spalletti
k5j1x0og8hth1akcd69a5lwq4.subtitle: Juventus scored twice in 12 minutes in the first half to see off Lecce and get back to winning ways in Serie A.
paragraphs: Douglas Luiz got a goal and an assist to lead Juventus to a 2-0 win over Lecce, who finished with 10 men at Stadio Ettore Giardiniero.
Luciano Spalletti has come under pressure after a topsy-turvy start to the season, but Luiz set up Weston McKennie before bagging a goal himself to get Juve back to winning ways in Serie A.
Lecce were almost in front after just 27 seconds as Konan N'Dri stuck out a leg to block Guglielmo Vicario's clearance on the edge of the six-yard box, but it flew just wide.
The hosts continued to show the greater threat in front of goal, but without testing Vicario, as Amar Fatah curled high and wide of the top-right corner.

But Juve opened the scoring with their first shot after Luiz won a central free-kick, which he clipped over Lecce's defence to pick out McKennie, who guided a scuffed first-time finish over Wladimiro Falcone after 29 minutes.

That sparked Juve into life, and Randal Kolo Muani fired wide before Luiz doubled their lead four minutes before the break, sweeping a long-range shot past Falcone, despite the goalkeeper getting a touch on it.
Lecce were on the front foot again at the start of the second half, with Oumar Ngom and Kialonda Gaspar both seeing efforts comfortably saved by Vicario.
Vicario also kept out Paco Esteban and N'Dri on either side of Nick Woltemade blazing over while one-on-one at close range, with Juventus holding out for a win.
With only seconds remaining, Lecce were dealt a blow for their next match against Frosinone, as Gaspar was shown a second yellow card – this one for dissent.
Luiz helps cover over some of the cracks
A 3-0 loss to high-flying Lazio last time out in Serie A ramped up the pressure on Juventus, who had won just one of their last four games in all competitions before facing Lecce (D2 L1).

Three points on the board will provide a big boost to Juve, who now sit seventh in the table, but there will still be questions asked as they struggled to put much pressure on Lecce for large swathes of the contest.

Juventus were clinical – scoring with both of their shots on target – but they only managed eight attempts worth 1.07 expected goals, compared to 16 shots from Lecce, though their chances only amounted to 0.94 xG as they failed to find their golden touch.
Luiz pulled the strings before the break, though, scoring and providing an assist in the same match for the first time in his career in the top five European leagues (261st match).

He was the only player to create more than one chance (two) for Juventus, while he also had the most touches (94), accurate passes (64/78) and passes in the final third (28) of anyone else on the team.
It should come as no surprise, though, given no team has won more Serie A away matches against Lecce than Juve (13, level with Inter).
