k7w5zq6s68fm1xh6odhr5uuv9.title: Mbappe reveals his mother wanted him to join Liverpool in 2017
k7w5zq6s68fm1xh6odhr5uuv9.subtitle: Real Madrid and France superstar Kylian Mbappe could have joined Liverpool nine years ago, if his mother had her way.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has revealed he was "close" to joining Liverpool in 2017, after his mother and agent, Fayza Lamari, "fell in love" with the club during negotiations with Jurgen Klopp.

Nine years ago, Mbappe was one of the hottest properties in world football after bursting onto the scene with Monaco, having registered 40 goal involvements in just 60 appearances for the club (27 goals, 13 assists).
Mbappe ultimately joined PSG in a loan deal that became permanent the following year, plundering 256 goals in 308 outings for the Parisiens and winning 15 trophies, including six Ligue 1 titles.
He then, of course, moved to Real Madrid in 2024, and though he has scored 94 goals in just 111 games for the Spanish giants, he is yet to win the Champions League, LaLiga, or the Copa del Rey.

While working as a German television pundit at this year's World Cup, at which Mbappe became the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 22 goals, Klopp reflected on Liverpool's pursuit of the then-teenage sensation.
Klopp disclosed he accompanied several Liverpool officials on a private plane from Blackpool to Nice, where they met with Mbappe and his mother to discuss a potential transfer.
And on Tuesday, in an interview with The Athletic, Mbappe revealed just how close he came to moving to Anfield.
"It was while I was playing in Monaco. I had to take a decision," Mbappe said. "And yes, I was close to Liverpool.
"My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.
"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, in Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone.
"But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool, you're going to be there, playing at Anfield, it's going to be insane for you.' I was like, 'Okay!'

"She went there for the first step of negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, 'It's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club.'
"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

"All the time, we were talking. She'd say, 'For me, you have to go to Liverpool'. I said, 'Okay, okay, okay', because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him."

Reflecting on Klopp's attempts to explain Liverpool's project, Mbappe added: "I said, 'You don't need to convince me. You're Jurgen Klopp, it's Liverpool, a great club, so if I'm here, I have some interest. But I have other things, other projects, that are also good.'
"I said to him, 'Whatever decision I take is going to be a good decision, because we are talking about some of the biggest clubs in the world.'
"It's a funny story. But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my hometown."
Mbappe will be in action for France during the international break, with Les Bleus' first game under Zinedine Zidane pitting them against Turkiye on Friday, in the Nations League.

k7wthojov8zp1i7359kb6yg36.title: 'Maybe I shouldn't even be on the touchline' – Allegri enraged by red card
k7wthojov8zp1i7359kb6yg36.subtitle: Massimiliano did not finish Napoli's thrilling draw on the touchline due to his complaints, and he was not happy with the red card.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri was enraged by his late red card in the draw with Roma, claiming he "shouldn't even be on the touchline", but believes Napoli have what it takes to move up the table.
Napoli twice gave up a lead against Roma in a thrilling draw – they had led 2-0 in the 48th minute after goals on either side of half-time from Frank Anguissa and Scott McTominay.
Matias Soule and Leonardo Balerdi then levelled the score with two goals in five minutes before McTominay's second of the match put Napoli back in front in the 83rd minute.

However, Napoli failed to hold on until the end, with Balerdi equalising for the second time, and Allegri was sent off in the aftermath for dissent as he felt the Argentinian had committed a foul on Sam Beukema in the build-up.
"The fourth official called the referee and got me sent off, but I said absolutely nothing," Allegri told DAZN Italia.

"Next time I will have to sit on the bench and not move, because every time I move, I get sent off. I had to pay €80,000 in fines last season, so maybe I shouldn't even be on the touchline from now on.
"I see others who practically run onto the pitch, and nobody says anything; when I move, I'm punished."
"I thank the fourth official, and for the rest, I can only congratulate the lads for their performance," he added sarcastically.

A win over Roma would have massively helped Napoli make moves up the table, but despite winning the expected goals (xG) battle 2.4 to 1.9, they could not turn it into three points and instead sit 10th.

Allegri remains under scrutiny at Napoli, with their leaky defence causing them problems – they have conceded six goals this week across two games in all competitions (also a 4-3 win over Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League).
"I think the team played well, also defensively, against a strong side," Allegri added.
"We had the chance to go 3-0 up; we then had the lead at 3-2 but conceded again. If we play with this spirit, we will climb the table.
"I changed my way of playing now; it is all on the attack. Since the start of the season, I even try to use four strikers if I can.
"Unfortunately, we've dropped a lot of points along the way. I'm still angry at the way the game ended, so I'm perhaps lacking sharpness in evaluating how the match went."

kepifo523mu11a2g7dhkeee15.title: Seattle youngster Gomez has 'unlimited potential' - Schmetzer
kepifo523mu11a2g7dhkeee15.subtitle: Sebastian Gomez has scored in two straight matches, and Brian Schmetzer feels the Seattle Sounders youngster has "unlimited potential".
paragraphs: Seattle Sounders coach Brian Schmetzer believes Sebastian Gomez has "unlimited potential" amid the youngster's fine run of form.
Gomez came off the bench to score for Seattle for the second straight match on Saturday, in a 2-2 draw with San Diego FC.
He became the fourth Sounders player to come off the bench and score in two straight regular-season MLS matches, joining Fredy Montero, Obafemi Martins and Sammy Ochoa.
And Schmetzer feels the sky is the limit for the 20-year-old.
"The kid has a really, really, really bright future as long as he stays at this club," Schmetzer said.
"He's that good. I love smart players. Some of the things he did were veteran-like moves.
"The kid's got unlimited potential. We're lucky to have him. He's making my life difficult."
Seattle take on the Houston Dynamo on Wednesday.
The Sounders sit seventh in the Western Conference, two places and four points behind the Dynamo.
Seattle led 2-0 against San Diego, only to throw their lead away, in what was a huge blow for Schmetzer.
"It feels like a loss," Schmetzer said. "We were much better than them. We should have closed that game out.
"Those guys put every piece of themselves into that game and we should have come out with three points."
Seattle Sounders - Albert Rusnak
Rusnak led Seattle for shots (three) and chances created (three) against San Diego, though he did not manage to score or assist.
He has 11 assists and four goals in MLS this year.
Houston Dynamo - Guilherme
Guilherme has 10 assists and 16 goals for the Dynamo this term.
He is the first Houston player to record 15+ goals and 10+ assists in a single regular-season campaign.
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
The Dynamo have won one of their last 11 regular-season matches (D7 L3), including going seven straight without a win (D5 L2).
This run came immediately after a stretch of five straight wins from late June through mid-August.
Seattle have won only four of their last 20 MLS matches (D7 L9) dating back to mid-May, with all four wins coming consecutively in September and October.
However, Seattle have suffered just one defeat in their last 12 matches (W4 D7), including drawing the last two.
The Sounders are unbeaten in 19 all-time home matches against Houston in all competitions (W14 D5), though the Dynamo have earned draws in their last two visits to Lumen Field.
Houston have scored five goals in those 19 matches, never scoring more than once in any match.
Seattle Sounders - 51.2%

kf0cqx4figyu1qhx0cer6fhet.title: O'Neil pushes Ipswich 'to keep going' after battling draw with Forest
kf0cqx4figyu1qhx0cer6fhet.subtitle: Ipswich Town fought hard for a point against Nottingham Forest, and Gary O'Neil was proud of his side's resilience at home.
paragraphs: Gary O'Neil has pushed his Ipswich Town side "to keep going" after a hard-earned draw with Nottingham Forest on Friday.
Ipswich came from behind to draw 1-1 at Portman Road, with Julio Enciso cancelling out Neco Williams' opener.
The Tractor Boys were on the back foot for the majority of the contest, with Forest accumulating 2.31 expected goals (xG) from 17 shots to the home side's 0.46 from seven attempts.
In fact, Ipswich only had one shot in the second half, which came from Jack Clarke in the 92nd minute.

Nevertheless, Ipswich have 10 points in eight Premier League games this season (W3 D1 L4); only in 1993-94 have they ever hit double figures in fewer matches from the start of any of their six previous campaigns in the competition (fifth game).

They have also gained more points from losing positions in the Premier League this season than any other side (seven) – they only gained four in the entirety of their last season in the competition (2024-25).
Exequiel Palacios was particularly impressive in midfield, leading Ipswich in chances created (two), touches (99) and accurate passes (77).

He also won possession 14 times in this game, the most by any player in a single Premier League match this season, with the last to do so as often being Curtis Jones for Liverpool v Everton in April of last term (16).
"We had to hang on and fight, that's what we needed. Tough game in tough conditions," O'Neil told Sky Sports.
"We were never good enough with the ball and it ended up being Forest direct balls that took control. We had to try and match that but the conditions were tough.

"They are a good side but to go 1-0 down and fight back, there are lots of ways to be successful in football matches and we rolled our sleeves up and dug in. Massive second half to get a point and keep a clean sheet in the second half.
"This league will test you. Really proud of the players but we have to keep going. We have some time before facing Hull [City]. Proud of the players."

kfpdqeeqq5b61s167hfxol4ih.title: Ronaldo benched for tactical reasons, says Jesus
kfpdqeeqq5b61s167hfxol4ih.subtitle: Portugal won 2-1 against Norway in the Nations League, with Cristiano Ronaldo an unused substitute for Jorge Jesus' side on Sunday.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus insisted it was a "tactical choice" to leave Cristiano Ronaldo on the bench during Portugal's Nations League victory over Norway.
Portugal won 2-1 on Sunday at Ullevaal Stadion after goals from Joao Felix and Goncalo Ramos, which came either side of a strike from Erling Haaland.
Joao Felix has now scored six goals in his last 11 games as a starter for Portugal as he continues to thrive under Jesus, whom he also worked under at Al-Nassr.
Jesus' side struggled for much of the contest, accumulating just 1.04 expected goals (xG) after being restricted to just 38% of possession, while Norway registered 2.52 xG from 22 shots.
Nevertheless, Portugal continued their perfect start to their Nations League title defence, even with Ronaldo unable to get minutes off the bench.
"It wasn't the right moment to bring Ronaldo into the game; it was a tactical choice," said Jesus on the matter.
"I needed a player with different characteristics, but that doesn't mean he's out of the options. Perhaps he'll play against Denmark."
Haaland posed the biggest threat to Portugal's win; the Manchester City striker led the match in shots (eight) and was responsible for 1.5 of Norway's xG tally.
Although Haaland managed to score, Jesus was satisfied with the way his side defended against Norway.
"It was an excellent victory because we played against one of the best teams in Europe right now. They are in the top five, like Portugal," added Jesus.
"They have a striker who can score at any moment. It’s incredible.

"Our back line, and especially the two centre-backs, with the help of Joao Palhinha and Ruben Neves when they moved into the defensive phase, were very strong in the central corridor. Even so, Haaland had seven shots inside the box and scored once.
"We were once again organised defensively and more creative offensively, also with the introduction of new players.
"Offensively, we still lack ideas, there isn't yet a collective effort. It's normal: I haven't had time for that."

klp9qw2wgkxo1h22snaj4t0hq.title: Udinese 0-2 AC Milan: Pulisic and Hutchinson extend Amorim's unbeaten Serie A start
klp9qw2wgkxo1h22snaj4t0hq.subtitle: AC Milan provided the perfect response to their Europa League defeat to Bournemouth by beating Udinese comfortably on Sunday.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim's unbeaten start to life in Serie A continued as goals in either half from Christian Pulisic and Omari Hutchinson earned AC Milan a 2-0 win over Udinese.
Milan remain within four points of leaders Inter after eight games of their season, as they delivered the perfect response to their Europa League thrashing by Bournemouth.

The Rossoneri needed just six minutes to get ahead after some quick thinking from Luka Modric, whose free-kick caught the Udinese defence napping, with Pulisic plucking the ball out the sky before finishing coolly beyond Maduka Okoye.
Davide Bartesaghi should have doubled Milan's lead five minutes later after he was slipped in by Pulisic, but as he closed in on goal, he lashed his left-footed effort over the bar.
Bartesaghi and Pulisic then somehow failed to turn Fikayo Tomori's cross home, with some last-ditch defending from James Abankwah then denying Strahinja Pavlovic a shot at goal just before the break.
Milan upped the pressure on the hour mark, with Pulisic thwarted at the near post by Okoye, with Goncalo Ramos then curling over from outside the area moments later.
But the visitors' dominance was rewarded in the 65th minute through Hutchinson. Ardon Jashari's strike was only parried into the path of the on-loan attacker, who was the quickest to react.

A wonderful piece of goalkeeping denied Milan a third soon after. Pulisic's goal-bound effort deflected off Christian Kabasele and into the path of Ramos, but his first-time shot was superbly tipped onto the crossbar by Okoye.
Mike Maignan, sent off in midweek against Bournemouth, preserved his clean sheet late on after thwarting Keinan Davis from point-blank range, as Milan comfortably held on.
Timeless Modric rolls back the years as Milan keep up the pressure

After enduring a difficult return to England on Thursday as Milan were thumped 3-0 by Bournemouth in the Europa League, Amorim had a point to prove, and his strong start in Serie A extended to eight matches.

It is the third time in the last 20 top-flight seasons that Milan have gone this long without defeat, after 2020-21 and 2021-22, and it was a moment of class and quality that got them up and running at Bluenergy Stadium.

Modric's delicate ball over the top saw him become the player who has provided the most assists after turning 40 since Serie A returned to 20 teams (from 2004-05), with this his fourth, which saw him surpass Zlatan Ibrahimovic (three).

Milan have made it four straight Serie A away wins against Udinese, doing so with an aggregate scoreline of 12-2, matching their best record against the same opposition in the competition between 1999 and 2001, and they could have won by a more handsome scoreline here.
Amorim's side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 3.12 from their 19 shots, seven of which were on target, compared to Udinese's total of 0.42 from their 12 attempts.

kqlgyhi2hciz1o73ornof6ij0.title: Slegers relieved as Arsenal take 'step in the direction' with derby win at Spurs
kqlgyhi2hciz1o73ornof6ij0.subtitle: Arsenal ended a five-game winless run in the Women's Super League with a victory over rivals Tottenham on Saturday.
paragraphs: Arsenal boss Renee Slegers believes her side's victory over rival Tottenham "was a step in the right direction".
After a run of five games without a win in the Women's Super League (D3 L2), the Gunners came from behind to defeat Spurs 2-1 on Saturday.
Spurs took the lead in the 13th minute through Cathinka Tandberg, but Georgia Stanway restored parity at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium just four minutes later.
Alessia Russo, who assisted Stanway's equaliser, then scored the winner from the penalty spot just before the hour mark after Ella Morris handled the ball in the box.
Arsenal have now won 11 of their 14 North London derbies in the WSL (D2 L1), with this victory moving the Gunners up to sixth, one point and two places behind Spurs.
Slegers told BBC Sport: "Happiness mainly. I see the fans and what it means for them.

"I'm happy for the players, who stuck in, in a really difficult period for us. There were good moments from us. It was a step in the right direction. Very happy with the win but we have to back it up.

"Things in different phases were good. We were brave in our press. We did well playing around them and dominating the ball. We created fewer shots than last week but we weren't expecting to. The opportunities created were good."
Arsenal won the expected goals (xG) battle 2.24 to 0.3, restricting Spurs to just one shot on target, which was their goal.
Russo was responsible for the majority of Arsenal's xG (1.21), while she also created the most chances in the match (three) and won seven of her 12 duels.
"I've worked on it [the penalty] in training, first and foremost," said Russo, who has scored more WSL goals against Spurs (nine) than any other opponent.

"I think we knew some of us were going to have to step up today in different moments. It's been tough for us, there's no denying. Whether it was Foordy stepping up, Misa making saves, me on the pen – everyone stepped up.

"We've got injuries right now as well. I'm happy to play where I'm needed. I'm a nine but if I'm needed deeper, that's what I'll do. We have different players that can play in different places. I'll give all I can to this team."

ktrfhh9h465d1pb339g4qt7bh.title: Noonan wants to build on Cincinnati's 'deciding moment' against Houston
ktrfhh9h465d1pb339g4qt7bh.subtitle: FC Cincinnati are right in the mix for a playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, and they face a struggling CF Montreal side next.
paragraphs: Pat Noonan believes FC Cincinnati's last-gasp draw against the Houston Dynamo could be a "deciding moment" in their quest to reach the playoffs this season.
Cincinnati found themselves 2-0 down after 51 minutes at Shell Energy Stadium thanks to goals from Guilherme and Mateusz Bogusz, the latter scoring from the penalty spot.
Bryan Ramirez halved the deficit in the 73rd minute before Kevin Denkey scored a spot-kick in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to seal a share of the spoils.
It was a result that kept Cincinnati ninth in the Eastern Conference, but the likes of New York City FC, D.C. United and Toronto FC are all chasing Noonan's side.
Cincinnati make the trip to Stade Saputo this weekend to face struggling CF Montreal, and Noonan believes his team's latest stalemate could be a solid foundation to build on.
"I think it could be a deciding moment in this stretch run," Noonan said. "We have nine games left in the season, and every game is going to be so important to pick up points.
"And that's because of the position that we're in, where we're fighting for a playoff spot. This isn't about everything being pretty now, or style.
"We were able to get an important point, and so, for the psyche of the group and how to be on the road, like I said, against a strong opponent and push the game like that.
"How do we get more of that urgency, but not recklessness?"
Montreal, meanwhile, will just want the 2026 season to come to an end after they were beaten 2-0 by the Columbus Crew in their last league match.
Only Sporting Kansas City (17) have lost more MLS matches this season than Montreal (15), who find themselves rooted to the bottom of the East on 21 points from 26 games.
It's also been a disappointing start to Alexis Sanchez's Montreal career, as he has failed to register a single goal contribution in his seven matches for the club.
During their defeat to Columbus, Sanchez's frustrations were evident as his team struggled to create any opportunities whenever they got the chance to go forward.
Interim boss Philippe Eullaffroy understood the Chilean's concerns about the team, but he said Sanchez remained committed to the cause and was just showing his passion.
"Alexis would like the team to play faster forward and use more space behind the defenders. I agree, and I ask for it, but it is not happening," Eullaffroy conceded.
"After the game, he was upset and tense about the development of the second half, as were several of his team-mates."
Montreal – Prince Owusu
In a season of frustration for Montreal, Owusu has been the only shining light, scoring 13 goals in 24 league appearances so far this season.
Owusu also has a good record against Montreal. He has scored three goals in six MLS outings against them, only managing to find the back of the net more against D.C. (four).
Cincinnati – Kevin Denkey
With Denkey unavailable after being selected to represent Togo during the international break, Evander will be the man Cincinnati will turn to in the final third.
Only Inter Miami's Lionel Messi (33) has more goal involvements in the MLS this season than Evander's 25 (13 goals, 12 assists).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Cincinnati earned a draw when trailing by two goals for the eighth time in the club's MLS era (since 2019) against Houston last time out. Three of those occurrences have happened this season and in all three of those occurrences in 2026, they had trailed by two goals in the second half.
But they will be hoping for a better result here. They have a good record against Montreal, winning their last four MLS meetings against them.
And Noonan's side will be desperate for a win. They are without a victory in their last five league matches (D3 L2) since a 2-1 triumph over NYCFC on August 19.

Montreal, meanwhile, will be out to end their poor run at Stade Saputo. Only Minnesota United (two) have fewer home wins in the MLS this season than Montreal (three), who last won in front of their home crowd on May 9 against Orlando City.

kupgoltp1j3i1wxwy2inc3azm.title: Kompany may miss 'weeks' after training ground collapse, says Bayern director Eberl
kupgoltp1j3i1wxwy2inc3azm.subtitle: Vincent Kompany collapsed during a Bayern Munich training session on Friday and will not be on the sidelines at Freiburg this weekend.
paragraphs: Bayern Munich will not have Vincent Kompany on the sidelines for several weeks after he collapsed on the training ground, though sporting director Max Eberl says the head coach will be with the squad in spirit.
On Friday, as Bayern stepped up their preparations for Sunday's Bundesliga trip to Freiburg, Kompany collapsed during a training session.
It was subsequently confirmed that the former Manchester City and Belgium centre-back was stable and undergoing tests in hospital, with his assistant Aaron Danks set to take the reins this weekend.
And Eberl, who decided against asking for Sunday's game to be postponed, says Kompany will be given as long as it takes to make a full recovery.
"The good news is he's stable, and we've spoken," Eberl said. "It wasn't a pleasant moment for any of us.
"He's in the hospital and will stay for a few days until everything has been checked out. This just goes to show that health is the most important thing in life—not football.
"We at Bayern Munich are all in this together. The most important thing is finding the cause. He shouldn't come back until he's fit – we have to protect him. He is in the best hands.
"Vinnie will be given all the time he needs; we're not setting any timeframes. We need to figure out what it is. Then we can calmly consider what the recovery time means.
"We're not talking about days, but weeks – everyone should be clear about that.
"The coaching staff isn't considering changing anything. They all have Vinnie's spirit with them. That's how we’ll approach the next few weeks."
Bayern, who drew 2-2 with Arsenal in the Champions League in midweek, have 14 points on the board after six Bundesliga games and entered matchday seven top of the table.
Hosts Freiburg are third, just one point worse off, after losing 2-1 to Bayer Leverkusen last weekend. They then went down 3-0 to Monaco in the Europa League on Thursday.
Freiburg – Yuito Suzuki
Suzuki, who is Freiburg's leading Bundesliga scorer this season with four goals, is available again after serving a red card suspension.
Among all players with at least four Bundesliga goals this term, he has the best shot conversion rate (50%), while Bayern's Harry Kane has the lowest among that group (14%).
Bayern Munich – Harry Kane
Kane – who will discover on Monday whether he has won the Ballon d'Or – is the joint-leading assist provider in the Bundesliga this campaign with five, level with Werder Bremen's Marco Grull.

That means he has already equalled his total from the entire previous Bundesliga season (in 31 games), and, for the first time, Kane has provided multiple assists in two consecutive Bundesliga games (two each against Augsburg and RB Leipzig).
MATCH PREDICTION – BAYERN MUNICH WIN
Freiburg have only won one of their last 21 matches in all competitions against Bayern (W1 D4 L16), managing a 2-1 victory in the DFB-Pokal quarter-finals in April 2023.
In the Bundesliga, Freiburg are winless in their last 20 meetings with Bayern (D4 L16), with their last victory being a 2-1 home success in May 2015.
Freiburg have also lost their last eight Bundesliga games against teams who started the matchday top of the Bundesliga table – the longest ongoing losing streak of any club.

Freiburg have won their first three home games of a Bundesliga season for only the second time after 2016-17, when they won their first four, so they should not be expected to roll over without a fight.

Bayern's five points from three away Bundesliga games this term are their fewest at this stage of a season since 2014-15 (also five), but they should still have too much quality for their hosts, with the Opta supercomputer making them clear favourites.
OPTA WIN PROBABILITY
Bayern Munich – 66.2%

kysd4qby7bie14m8w76y4tcyy.title: Flamengo 0-0 Estudiantes (2-3 pens): Muslera's penalty heroics seal spot in Copa Libertadores final
kysd4qby7bie14m8w76y4tcyy.subtitle: After two goalless draws across both legs of the semi-final, Fernando Muslera came up trumps for Estudiantes in the Copa Libertadores.
paragraphs: Fernando Muslera saved three penalties to help Estudiantes overcome a second-half red card and beat defending champions Flamengo to reach the Copa Libertadores final.
After goalless draws across both legs of the semi-final, Muslera brilliantly saved Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta and Bruno Henrique's attempts to seal a 3-2 triumph in the shoot-out.
Estudiantes, who saw Baltasar Rodriguez sent off in the 50th minute for a second yellow card, will now face Palmeiras in the final at the Centenario Stadium on November 28.
Both teams started brightly in their quest to take an early lead, with Estudiantes defenders Santiago Nunez and Marcos Rojo forcing Agustin Rossi into making two smart stops.
The first half petered out, but it burst into life five minutes after the restart when Rodriguez was sent off for a second bookable offence for a needless challenge on Jorginho.
His dismissal allowed Flamengo to control from there, but efforts from Paqueta were comfortably held by Muslera, with penalties deciding who would reach the showpiece match.
Giorgian de Arrascaeta and Jose Sosa got their sides off to the perfect start in the shoot-out, with Jorginho the first to blink as his stuttering run-up failed to fool Muslera.
Edwuin Cetre could not make Estudiantes' advantage count, but Paqueta was also denied from 12 yards out, with Muslera diving to his right to deny the Brazilian.

Eros Mancuso, Leo Pereira and Tiago Palacios all scored to keep the shootout going, but Muslera proved to be the hero as he dived to the same side and thwarted Henrique's effort, sparking wild scenes among the Estudiantes supporters at the Maracana.
Magic Muslera puts woeful World Cup behind him

At this summer's World Cup, Muslera came out of retirement to represent Uruguay in the finals, but it proved to be a tournament to forget. He became the first goalkeeper on record since 1966 to commit three errors leading to goals in a single edition of FIFA's flagship competition.

In Uruguay's final group match, a 1-0 defeat to Spain, Alex Baena's shot squirmed through his grasp and Muslera was replaced by Sergio Rochet at half-time as the nation made a goalkeeper substitution in a World Cup match for the first time since substitutions were introduced at the tournament in 1970.

Muslera subsequently announced his second retirement from international football, but that will be a distant memory after his performance here, as he ensured Estudiantes' spot in the Copa Libertadores final for the first time since 2009.

Estudiantes will now aim to break a seven-year streak of consecutive tournament victories by Brazilian teams in South America's premier club competition, with the last non-Brazilian club to lift the trophy being Argentina's River Plate in 2018.

But even after having a man sent off, Estudiantes were only just edged out in the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 0.79 from their eight attempts to Flamengo's 0.86 from their 13 attempts, with both teams having three shots on target.

The first half petered out, but it burst into life five minutes after the restart when Rodriguez was sent off for a second bookable offence for a needless challenge on Jorginho. 

His dismissal allowed Flamengo to control from there, but efforts from Paqueta were comfortably held by Muslera, with penalties deciding who would reach the showpiece match.

Giorgian de Arrascaeta and Jose Sosa got their sides off to the perfect start in the shoot-out, with Jorginho the first to blink as his stuttering run-up failed to fool Muslera. 

Edwuin Cetre could not make Estudiantes' advantage count, but Paqueta was also denied from 12 yards out, with Muslera diving to his right to deny the Brazilian. 

Eros Mancuso, Leo Pereira and Tiago Palacios all scored to keep the shootout going, but Muslera proved to be the hero as he dived to the same side and thwarted Henrique's effort, sparking wild scenes among the Estudiantes supporters at the Maracana. 

Magic Muslera puts woeful World Cup behind him

At this summer's World Cup, Muslera came out of retirement to represent Uruguay in the finals, but it proved to be a tournament to forget. He became the first goalkeeper on record since 1966 to commit three errors leading to goals in a single edition of FIFA's flagship competition.

In Uruguay's final group match, a 1-0 defeat to Spain, Alex Baena's shot squirmed through his grasp and Muslera was replaced by Sergio Rochet at half-time as the nation made a goalkeeper substitution in a World Cup match for the first time since substitutions were introduced at the tournament in 1970. 

Muslera subsequently announced his second retirement from international football, but that will be a distant memory after his performance here, as he ensured Estudiantes' spot in the Copa Libertadores final for the first time since 2009. 

Estudiantes will now aim to break a seven-year streak of consecutive tournament victories by Brazilian teams in South America's premier club competition, with the last non-Brazilian club to lift the trophy being Argentina's River Plate in 2018.

But even after having a man sent off, Estudiantes were only just edged out in the expected goals (xG) battle, registering a total of 0.79 from their eight attempts to Flamengo's 0.86 from their 13 attempts, with both teams having three shots on target.

l19ef15wtq3j18exn3r706lgc.title: Portugal shelve Ronaldo controversy as Jesus demands full focus on Norway
l19ef15wtq3j18exn3r706lgc.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's exit from the Portugal squad has hogged the headlines in recent days, but Jorge Jesus' team have another game to play.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says Portugal's focus is purely on Sunday's clash with Norway, with the fallout from Cristiano Ronaldo's departure being shelved until after that game.
Ronaldo's glittering international career may be over after he stormed out of Portugal's camp earlier this week, amid reports of a rift with new head coach Jesus.
Jesus – who worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr – left the 41-year-old on the bench throughout a 2-1 Nations League win over Erling Haaland and company in Oslo last week.

Ronaldo then trained away from his team-mates before leaving the camp on the eve of the Selecao's entertaining 4-2 win over Denmark on Thursday, which saw Joao Cancelo, Goncalo Ramos, Vitinha and Joao Felix get on the scoresheet.

Ronaldo took to social media to say he will "tell the truth" about his exit from the camp in due course, while Jesus has refused to go into detail about the incident, only saying he would never allow any player to dictate his decisions as a coach.

Portugal will play their first home game since Ronaldo's departure on Sunday, knowing another victory over Norway at Porto's Estadio do Dragao would all but guarantee qualification for the last eight next March.
And that is the only thing on Jesus' mind, as he told reporters: "The focus has to be on the national team, and on Norway in this case, on what we have to do well.
"It's not about us ignoring Cris, he is a symbol of the national team and of Portugal. After the game, there will be plenty of time to talk about it."

Asked if Ronaldo could at least return in an ambassadorial role before the 2030 World Cup, which Portugal will co-host alongside Spain and Morocco, Jesus said: "You are already looking ahead to 2030. It's four years. Football is day by day, it's not even month by month.
"Tomorrow [Sunday], the game is the most important thing. It will be very intense, and that's what I want to talk about. I don't want to change the subject.
"I'm going to focus on what I talked about – the team and our opponent. Norway is a team, in my opinion, who are in the top five in Europe, with great players.
"Then, we will have time to analyse what happens here."
Jesus was then asked what sort of reception he expected from Portugal's home fans, given the perception of a rift between himself and the country's greatest-ever player.
"The affection that I seek is nothing more than what the national team should get," he said. "The affection should be for the team, for the players.
"I am part of a team, I am the commander of a team. Before, I was also a staunch, crazy fan of the national team, and I didn't look at the coach or the players, I looked at the flag.
"I don't want to be part of anything except the national team."

Since the start of 2025, Portugal have won 80% of their matches when Ronaldo has not appeared (P5 W4 D1), compared to just 59% when he has featured (P17 W10 D4 L3), also averaging almost twice as many goals per game without Ronaldo (3.4) than with him (1.9).

l31su4tqxt5513puj1xs5xhs7.title: Iraola hails Wirtz after under-fire playmaker turns in creative masterclass
l31su4tqxt5513puj1xs5xhs7.subtitle: Florian Wirtz created nine chances, including laying on an assist, as Liverpool beat Brentford 2-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola hailed Florian Wirtz's creative influence after the Germany international helped Liverpool come from behind to beat Brentford.

After a chaotic finish to the first half of Saturday's game, which saw Keane Lewis-Potter put Brentford in front before Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off, Wirtz helped Liverpool complete a second-half fightback.
He assisted Victor Munoz's equaliser, before Alexander Isak fired home on his return from injury to put the Reds 2-1 up.

Despite a few nervy moments late on, Iraola's side held on, with Brentford being reduced to nine men in stoppage time as Vitaly Janelt felled Rio Ngumoha from behind, having already been booked for dissent.
Wirtz's assist was his second in the Premier League this season, both of which have been for Munoz, after the duo also combined for a goal against Nottingham Forest in August.

Having come under fire for his performances since arriving from Bayer Leverkusen, Wirtz created nine chances from open play on Saturday, becoming the first player to achieve that feat in a single Premier League game since January 2021.

On that occasion, it was Sadio Mane who teed up nine opportunities from open play, also for Liverpool against Burnley. The previous player to do so for an away team, meanwhile, was Samir Nasri for Manchester City against Tottenham in August 2011 (10).
Asked about Wirtz's influence after Brentford received their first red card, Iraola said: "I think, especially in the second half, it's the situation where if you need a player there, you need Flo.

"It's like when you're going with Rio, it's very similar. There are very few spaces, small pockets, no time on the ball... there are some delicate things you have to find because Brentford are a team that defend their box really, really well.
"I think you need players like Flo, like Rio, like Victor, who was lovely when attacking against the full-back and who can make the difference."
While Iraola was pleased with large aspects of Liverpool's performance, he acknowledged they should have managed the situation better after going 2-1 up.
"I think we played really well in the minutes up until we scored to make it 2-1 against 10 players. We were being patient and finding good positions and were in control," he said.
"I was probably more disappointed after we scored, because after you score to make it 2-1, then you feel like you have something to lose.
"We missed clear counters to finish the game and it put us back overall. But I think the situation against 10 players, we dealt with that quite well."

Brentford's first red card was widely debated in the aftermath of the game, with Yarmoliuk appearing to thrust his head into Jeremy Jacquet while the players were jostling before a corner, although the Liverpool centre-back went down theatrically.
Iraola would not be drawn on that debate, saying: "I think it's a hard one. I have to say that. I've seen it on the screen, but I still don't know. I'm not sure."
But Keith Andrews had a clear view on it, saying: "I do think they [Liverpool] were cute and clever, but Yarmo needs to do better, so I can understand why it was a red.
"If you look at where Jacquet is walking, he's not looking at the ball, is he? He's walking into Yarmo."

lbec2iriu4t51vc4ef8ufu623.title: Fleetwood Town 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens): Premier League champions stunned in EFL Cup giant-killing
lbec2iriu4t51vc4ef8ufu623.subtitle: Fleetwood Town are into the quarter-finals of the EFL Cup after they stunned Arsenal on a remarkable night at Highbury Stadium.
paragraphs: Fleetwood Town pulled off a giant-killing for the ages as they beat Premier League champions Arsenal 5-3 on penalties in the EFL Cup.
Arsenal's first game at a ground called Highbury Stadium in 20 years ended in a humbling as Max Dowman was sent off late on in a 1-1 draw, with Bruno Guimaraes missing the decisive penalty.
Goalkeeper Jay Lynch was a Fleetwood hero as he kept out Guimaraes' spot-kick, paving the way for Conor Haughey to seal the most famous win in the club's history.

Play was paused early on due to a drone flying over the stadium. But when play resumed, Arsenal could not get into gear, and their slack start was punished in the 21st minute, with Aaron Loupalo-Bi getting the better of Marli Salmon and finishing neatly beyond Illan Meslier.
Jurrien Timber headed off target towards the end of the first half, but Mikel Arteta wasted no time in making alterations at the break.
Timber was replaced by Ben White, while Martin Odegaard came on for Salmon.
Those changes paid dividends as the Gunners drew level in the 50th minute, with Viktor Gyokeres bundling home a scrappy equaliser after Fleetwood failed to deal with a left-wing centre.
Kai Havertz seemed all set to put Arsenal ahead when Lynch spiled Dowman's strike, but Rhys Bennett made a stunning block.
Havertz slammed wide after latching onto Odegaard's throughball soon after, but Arsenal's flurry soon died off.

And their task was made more difficult in the 85th minute, with Dowman sent off for violent conduct after he kicked out at Andy Cannon following a robust but fair challenge from the Fleetwood attacker.
Lynch made a spectacular stop to deny White what seemed set to be a certain winner, and he was at it again in the shoot-out, lunging to his left to thwart Guimaraes.
Haughey then made no mistake, as Fleetwood – 18th in League Two – dumped out last season's runners-up.
The FA Cup is the English competition usually associated with giant-killings, but this result is arguably the biggest shock in the history of the EFL Cup.
There are 84 places between Fleetwood and Arsenal in the English football pyramid, but Matt Lawlor's team played with the endeavour, effort and quality needed to go up against the best.

Fleetwood, who had not won any of their previous five meetings with Premier League opponents, only had three shots across the 90 minutes. They got two of them on target. They created chances worth just 0.26 expected goals to Arsenal's 2.21 xG.

But it mattered little, for they were simply up for the battle, and Arsenal could not match them. The Gunners were, of course, slicker in possession, but there was a distinct lack of craft, Odegaard aside. He created three chances, which led the visitors along with Piero Hincapie, Ceadach O’Neill and Eberechi Eze.
As expected in such a win, the underdogs relied on their goalkeeper, and Lynch delivered with five saves. The most important one of all was the one in the shoot-out, though.

This is a victory that will go down in Fleetwood folklore, the greatest night in their history, and the quarter-finals await. Arsenal, meanwhile, must lick their wounds ahead of a trip to Anfield on Sunday.

lch8oscyb3r011xedse39jmpj.title: Slegers accepts pressure amid poor Arsenal form
lch8oscyb3r011xedse39jmpj.subtitle: Arsenal's poor start to the season could get worse when they face Manchester City on Sunday, and Renee Slegers knows results must improve.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers acknowledged she has "to find the solutions" to Arsenal's poor form ahead of their huge Women's Super League clash with Manchester City this weekend.
Arsenal are winless in each of their last three league games (D2 L1) and could equal their worst runs without victory in the competition, set in May 2014 and October 2023.
The Gunners are only the third team in WSL history to score two or fewer goals and concede two or fewer goals across their opening four matches, along with Liverpool in 2014 and Chelsea in 2018-19.
Failure to win this game will see Arsenal record their second-worst start after five games in the division, behind only 2014 (four).
"I have to find the solutions, I have to be calm. I have to get direction," said Slegers.
"I have to lead now but at the same time, what I also feel is gratitude for how everyone is responding and how together we are, the session on the pitch was today. It was really, really good."
Slegers also explained the reason for missing her post-match interview after Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Paris FC in the Women's Champions League, during which the WSL side squandered a two-goal lead.
"After the game, there was emotion from my end but to control that point quickly I made the decision to be with the team instead," said the Gunners boss.
"So I spent time with the players straight after the game. I thought that was important and that was a decision I made in the moment in my leadership and I decided to be with the team."
City have won their home game against Arsenal in six of the last nine WSL seasons (D1 L2), with those matches averaging 3.9 goals (21 for City, 14 for the Gunners).
Arsenal versus City is one of only two WSL fixtures to see both teams win 10+ times, with the Gunners leading the head-to-head 12-11 (2 draws).

lfdikrk6b86aze9k16jkzmbr.title: Coventry City 0-1 Fulham: Bobb opens account to seal consecutive wins for Arbeloa's side
lfdikrk6b86aze9k16jkzmbr.subtitle: Oscar Bobb propelled Fulham to a 1-0 victory over Coventry City with his first Premier League goal for the club.
paragraphs: Oscar Bobb's first Premier League goal for Fulham sealed a 1-0 win over Coventry City on Saturday.
Chances were few and far between at CBS Arena, with Josh King striking the post in the first half before Bobb's decisive strike in the 80th minute.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side started on the front foot, with Bobb and Gonzalo Garcia combining neatly before the latter saw his shot blocked. Moments later, Carl Rushworth was called into action to deny Shay Charles' sprayed shot.

Fulham went even closer in the 18th minute when Bobb picked out King inside the box, who controlled nicely before drilling a powerful effort high against Rushworth's right-hand post, with Alex Iwobi unable to turn home the rebound.
Coventry struggled to create many chances of note, though Jay Dasilva's inswinging cross was nodded over the bar by Brandon Thomas-Asante.
Thomas-Asante then squandered a promising opening on the half-hour mark after pouncing on a misplaced pass from Antonee Robinson, but his effort was comfortably saved by Bernd Leno.

Coventry endured another nervous moment just before the break as Robinson sent a bouncing cross into the box for Garcia, with Milan van Ewijk sliding across to intercept, his attempted clearance sending the ball skidding past his own near post and into the side netting.

Charles could not believe he did not break the deadlock in the 69th minute, when Timothy Castagne's knock-on from Bobb's cross found him unmarked at the back post, though he failed to guide the ball home.
With the contest seemingly heading towards a stalemate, Bobb finally produced a moment of magic.

The Norwegian showcased some brilliant footwork to dance past Dasilva and Jack Rudoni before bending a sublime effort into the far corner, leaving Rushworth rooted to the spot and sealing Fulham's second win of the season.
Bobb helps fuel Fulham's turnaround
After failing to win any of their opening six Premier League matches of the season, many of the Fulham persuasion might have felt it was time to hit the panic button.
But Arbeloa's side have kick-started a turnaround, following up their first victory of the campaign against Hull City last time out with another here to climb to 12th in the table.
In doing so, Fulham ended a run of eight away games without a win, having alternated between a draw (four) and a loss (four) each time.

Indeed, Fulham have now won consecutive Premier League games for the first time since March, when they beat Sunderland and Tottenham, while they last recorded back-to-back victories without conceding in December 2025.
And Bobb proved decisive in extending that run, scoring the winner despite registering an individual expected goals (xG) total of just 0.07, which shows the high quality of his finish.
He also ended a run of 29 Premier League appearances without a goal involvement, having last registered an assist for Manchester City against Wolves in August 2025.
It was also only his second goal in the league, with his first coming for Man City against Newcastle United in January 2024.
Meanwhile, Coventry boss Frank Lampard has now won just three of his last 25 Premier League matches (D4 L18).
He is also winless in his last 11 meetings with Spanish managers (D1 L10), having last beaten one when his Chelsea side defeated Pep Guardiola's Manchester City 2-1 in June 2020.

And Bobb proved decisive in extending that run, scoring the winner despite registering an individual expected goals (xG) total of just 0.07, which shows the high quality of his finish.

He also ended a run of 29 Premier League appearances without a goal involvement, having last registered an assist for Manchester City against Wolves in August 2025.

It was also only his second goal in the league, with his first coming for Man City against Newcastle United in January 2024. 

Meanwhile, Coventry boss Frank Lampard has now won just three of his last 25 Premier League matches (D4 L18). 

He is also winless in his last 11 meetings with Spanish managers (D1 L10), having last beaten one when his Chelsea side defeated Pep Guardiola's Manchester City 2-1 in June 2020.

lhamzf4q2c8s18bytkx0sf7qz.title: Spain 4-1 Croatia: Yamal nets brace as unbeaten run reaches 40 games
lhamzf4q2c8s18bytkx0sf7qz.subtitle: In their first home match since winning the World Cup, Spain defeated Croatia at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal scored twice and got an assist for Spain as the world champions defeated Croatia 4-1 in the Nations League.

Marc Pubill and Nico Williams were also on the scoresheet for La Roja at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan, where Rodri showcased the World Cup before kick-off in Spain's first home game since winning the competition in the summer.

Just as he did against England in their Nations League opener, Yamal opened the scoring inside the first two minutes as he curled Alex Baena's cut-back into the bottom-left corner with a first-time finish.

Spain pushed for a second, with Pau Cubarsi shooting narrowly wide from distance, but Croatia scored against the run of play just before the half-hour mark as Dion Beljo headed in from Ivan Perisic's pinpoint cross.
However, the hosts were back ahead just three minutes later as Yamal played a corner short before eventually sending in a cross, which was headed in by an unmarked Pubill in the six-yard box.

Mikel Oyarzabal saw a goal ruled out for offside and Fermin Lopez struck the woodwork before half-time, but Spain eventually got their third in the 63rd minute as Yamal powered in at the near post following Pedri's level reverse pass.

Pedri saw a long-range strike pushed away by Dominik Livakovic shortly after Franjo Ivanovic curled wide at the other end, though Williams wrapped up a comfortable victory with a clinical finish in the 89th minute.
Yamal becoming inevitable for club and country

Through Yamal, Spain have scored in the first two minutes of play in consecutive matches for the first time in any competition since at least 2004, and it was just the start of another stellar performance from the teenager.

To go along with his two goals and assist, Yamal also created the joint-most chances for his side (two), attempted the most passes in the final third (24) and the most dribbles (nine), while also winning both of his tackles.
Despite conceding, Luis de la Fuente's side were in control throughout, accumulating 1.77 expected goals (xG) from 16 attempts while restricting Croatia to just 0.44 xG from five shots.
La Roja are now unbeaten in their last 40 matches across all competitions (W31 D9), the best such record by a European nation.

Indeed, Spain have won each of their last nine matches in all competitions, equalling their best winning streak with De la Fuente as head coach (W9 between June and July 2024), and it means they remain in control of Group A3 in the Nations League after winning six points from their opening two games.

ljv8ouvw66d41e9owff5erinc.title: Saletros to take learnings from recent Chicago losses into playoffs
ljv8ouvw66d41e9owff5erinc.subtitle: The Chicago Fire have lost their last two in MLS, but Anton Saletros remains optimistic ahead of their visit to Atlanta United.
paragraphs: Chicago Fire midfielder Anton Saletros believes the club must take lessons from their recent MLS defeats into the playoffs.
The Fire are fourth in the Eastern Conference with four games to go, the first of which is a trip to Atlanta United, but they have faltered in recent games.
After stringing together a three-game winning run, Chicago have lost back-to-back matches over the last week.
They followed up a 3-1 defeat to the Philadelphia Union with a 1-0 loss to the New England Revolution.
Despite dropping six points, Saletros believes Chicago can take positives from their recent form.
"I think we develop, and we learn every week," said Saletros, who wore the armband against New England.
"I think these games where we played decently but didn't win, it's going to be important to experience that, especially in the playoffs, when sometimes the game can be decided in one moment.
"So it's a great experience for us, as a group, to have been through that.
"We obviously want to win the game, we want to win every game we play. It's a mixed feeling, but also after a loss, you're not very happy."
Atlanta are 14th in the East, but are just six points off the postseason places ahead of hosting Chicago.
In their most recent MLS outing, the Five Stripes lost 3-1 to Inter Miami after a brace from Lionel Messi.
Atlanta United – Fafa Picault
Picault scored Atlanta's lone goal against Inter Miami with an 89th-minute penalty.
Since the beginning of the 2018 season, Picault has scored 15 regular-season goals in the 85th minute or later, with only Carles Gil (16) also having at least that many in that time.
Chicago Fire – Maren Haile-Selassie
Haile-Selassie has scored Chicago's last two goals against Atlanta, with the lone goal in May's 1-0 win and Chicago's final goal in a 2-2 draw last July.
No MLS player has a longer active streak of league matches with a goal against Atlanta, while the last longer streak was a three-match run by Lucho Acosta in 2023–24.
MATCH PREDICTION: CHICAGO FIRE WIN

Chicago allowed just five shots in their loss to New England. It was the third time this season that Chicago had faced five or fewer shots in an MLS match, after the team had one such game in each of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 seasons.

Atlanta attempted 14 more shots than Miami (21–7) in the Five Stripes' 3-1 home loss. It was the fourth time this season that Atlanta had 14 or more shots than their opponent in an MLS match, their most such games in a single season in club history.
Atlanta have won seven of eight regular-season home matches against Chicago (D1) for an average of 2.75 points per match.

The only MLS team with a higher points-per-match average in home games against another team (min. eight games) in the post-shootout era (since 2000) is Los Angeles FC against the Seattle Sounders (2.80).
Atlanta United – 32.4%

lk70bbzpvx2910hrv2orwnf4b.title: Gakpo withdraws from Netherlands squad with ankle injury
lk70bbzpvx2910hrv2orwnf4b.subtitle: Liverpool have been dealt another injury blow during the international break, with Cody Gakpo the latest to return to Merseyside.
paragraphs: Cody Gakpo has returned to Liverpool and is unavailable for the Netherlands' last two Nations League games after suffering an ankle injury.
The forward sustained the issue in the Netherlands' 2-1 win over Serbia on Sunday and was substituted after just 17 minutes following a hard tackle.
Following the game, Xavi said he did not think the injury was serious, but after tests on Monday, Gakpo has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad.
Nobody has been called up to replace him for the remaining two games of the international break.
Liverpool confirmed Gakpo would undergo further assessment at their training centre but did not say how long he was expected to be sidelined.
It is a blow for the Dutchman, who has made a strong start to the season after being linked with a transfer away from Anfield to Tottenham and Manchester City this summer.
He has already racked up six goal involvements in all competitions – two goals and four assists – more than any other player for the club.
His 13 chances created, meanwhile, are second only to Dominik Szoboszlai.
Liverpool return to action against City on October 11.

lr9hp1yjc6vz19tl4yru8mrde.title: Barkley hopes Fenerbahce win can turn Villa's league fortunes around
lr9hp1yjc6vz19tl4yru8mrde.subtitle: Aston Villa thumped Fenerbahce in the Champions League, and they will be hoping to build on that against Newcastle United this Saturday.
paragraphs: Ross Barkley believes a confidence-boosting win over Fenerbahce in the Champions League could be the result Aston Villa needed to kickstart their Premier League season.
Villa recorded their biggest ever win in major European competition on Wednesday with a 6-0 win at Villa Park, with Barkley scoring twice during the second half.
Johan Manzambi marked his debut in the Champions League with a goal, while two strikes from the in-form Nicolas Jackson had Unai Emery's side cruising going into the break.
Barkley then tucked away a 68th-minute penalty before bringing up his brace soon after, with Tammy Abraham's close-range finish adding further gloss to the scoreline late on.
However, the Villans' attention now turns to the Premier League, with a trip to St. James' Park to face Newcastle United up next as they aim to secure their second league victory of the season.
Villa are 16th in the league ahead of matchday seven, though Barkley is confident their form will start to improve.
"It was a great performance overall by the team, and we needed this result," Barkley said.
"We're still gelling, we've got loads of new players, we're all getting on the same page on the training pitch, and we worked well.
"We've got loads of top players in the squad, new additions, and it was nice to play in the game and chip in with a couple of goals to build some confidence within the team.
"Maybe it surprises teams here, with the atmosphere. It's intense. The fans get behind us if we win our duels, and that's why John McGinn is so key for us.
"He wins duels, gets us going, he's passionate, and he lifts the fans and the team. We were fantastic today, and hopefully we can keep building on that."
While Villa are riding the crest of a wave, Newcastle come into the clash off the back of a disappointing 4-1 defeat to newly-promoted Coventry City earlier this week.
Jack Rudoni and Sidiki Cherif had Coventry two goals in front early in the second half before a thunderbolt from Sven Botman threatened a comeback for the Magpies.
However, two goals in five minutes from Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni sealed the win for the Sky Blues, with Matthias Jaissle's side missing the chance to go fourth in the table.

The result saw Newcastle concede 4+ goals in back-to-back Premier League away games for the first time since December 2012 (4-3 loss to Man Utd, 7-3 loss to Arsenal), though Nico Gonzalez believed the scoreline flattered Coventry.
"We had clear chances to draw. We improved on many things, but there are things we have to work on,” Nico told Sky Sports.
"I think it's normal in this league that there are always goals in the last minute. Everyone goes forward, and it's hard to keep defending as well as the first minutes.
"The result is not what happened in the game. I've seen so many games where it's 2-1 and you draw. I don't feel concerned. We've done many things right.
"It's clear what we have to improve. It's easy to work on because we know the things we need to do better. If we improve them, I'm sure we'll have a great season."
Newcastle United – Harvey Barnes
Barnes has been involved in 10 goals in 13 Premier League games against Villa (six goals, four assists), his joint-most against an opponent, along with West Ham.
He only has more Premier League goals against Leeds United (seven), and you feel his influence will be key in Newcastle's attempts to get back to winning ways.
Aston Villa – Nicolas Jackson

Jackson is a player full of confidence after his brace against Fenerbahce saw him become the first player to score in as many as four of his first five Champions League starts since Sebastien Haller in December 2021 (all five).
The Senegal international has also scored in his last two Premier League games, only netting in three in a row once in the competition (May 2024 for Chelsea).
MATCH PREDICTION: NEWCASTLE UNITED WIN

Despite being favoured by the Opta supercomputer, Newcastle are winless in their last three Premier League games against Villa (D1 L2), losing 2-0 in their most recent game. They haven't lost consecutive games against them since losing both games in 2004-05.

Newcastle have also gone 12 consecutive Premier League games without a clean sheet at St James' Park, last having a longer run without a shutout between December 1998 and August 1999 under Ruud Gullit (13 games).

The Magpies have conceded 13 Premier League goals this season, their third-most after six matches after 1999-00 (18) and 2021-22 (14), going on to finish 11th in both seasons. Only Chelsea (36) have faced more shots on target this season than Newcastle (34).
Villa won 2-0 in their last away Premier League game against Newcastle. They haven't won consecutive league visits to St James' since a run of three between 1955-56 and 1957-58.

But Villa's defence has also been an issue. They have conceded 11 goals in six Premier League games this season, their most at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87 (16), when they eventually finished bottom.

It could also be a landmark day for Villa boss Emery. He has won 99 of his 196 Premier League games (D44 L53). Victory here would make him the joint-ninth fastest manager to 100 wins in the competition.
Newcastle United – 41.5%

ls2q804htidq1aoa8gilyaj7s.title: Manchester City 3-2 Brighton: Shaw scores twice to maintain perfect start
ls2q804htidq1aoa8gilyaj7s.subtitle: Manchester City survived a scare to beat Brighton in the Women's Super League, while there were also wins for Chelsea and Manchester United.
paragraphs: Manchester City's perfect start to their Women's Super League title defence continued on Sunday as Khadija Shaw scored twice in an entertaining 3-2 win over Brighton.
All five of the game's goals came in a frantic first half, with Lauren Hemp twice teeing up Shaw before Niamh Charles pulled the Citizens three clear by the 17th minute.
But Brighton, who picked up their first league win of the season against Charlton Athletic last week, hit back with two goals in six minutes from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes.
However, Andree Jeglertz's side were able to hold on for their sixth consecutive league win, ensuring they remained two points clear of Chelsea in the early-season table.
The Citizens needed just five minutes to open the scoring through Shaw, who poked in from close range after getting ahead of Chiamaka Nnadozie and reaching Hemp's cross.

It looked as though the defending WSL champions would run away with the win after two quickfire goals, with Shaw holding off Hayes and Gabby George to head another Hemp delivery into the net, before Charles picked out the bottom-left corner.
Shaw, Hemp and Grace Clinton all came close to adding to their tally before the half an hour mark, but City took their foot off the gas and allowed Brighton to settle.
Garcia tucked home Fran Kirby's cross in the 31st minute before Hayes was left unmarked from a corner and saw her header beat Ayaka Yamashita from inside the box.
In what was a scrappy second half, Shaw's low effort represented City's best chance of scoring a fourth, with the league leaders holding on for another big win on home soil.
In-form Shaw helps City reach seventh heaven

Though it was far from their most convincing display this season, City once again found a way to get the job done, and their strong start to their WSL campaign owes to the goal-scoring exploits of Shaw, who is in a rich vein of form.

Shaw has now scored in each of her last six WSL starts, equalling her longest run of consecutive starts with a goal in the competition (six, February to April 2024). Overall, the Jamaican has 89 goals in 85 English top-flight starts.

And City needed their striker to be at her best to ensure they remained top of the table, with Chelsea thumping London rivals Tottenham 6-2 at Stamford Bridge. Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter both scored twice, with Sjoeke Nusken and Maika Hamano also on target off the bench.

It was a dominant display on a landmark day for Sonia Bompastor, who marked her 50th WSL game with a win. She has now earned 125 points in her first 50 matches in the competition, overtaking Joe Montemurro (123) for the most points won by any manager across their first 50 games in the WSL.

Manchester United also secured their third consecutive league win with a 3-1 victory over Charlton Athletic. Ella Toone and Andrea Medina had put the Red Devils in a good position before Leah Davidson pulled one back, but Julia Zigiotti Olme sealed the win in the 31st minute.

London City Lionesses kept up their strong start to the season as first-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and Freya Godfrey were enough to see off Everton 2-1, despite Hannah Cain's 71st-minute strike threatening a tense finish.

lsdmjjhgt8o41hzudgy94ekbb.title: Besiktas 2-2 Crystal Palace: Super-sub Olaitan adds to Sage's woes
lsdmjjhgt8o41hzudgy94ekbb.subtitle: Crystal Palace came from behind to lead against Besiktas, but could not hold onto all three points, even as the hosts finished with 10 men.
paragraphs: Junior Olaitan came off the bench to help Besiktas come from behind to earn a 2-2 draw against Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

Wilfred Ndidi had given Besiktas the lead on the stroke of half-time before quickfire goals from Yeremy Pino and Jean-Philippe Mateta after the break flipped the script, but Olaitan had the final say, even as the hosts finished the game with 10 men.

With Pierre Sage under increasing pressure, Palace thought they had made a dream start when Mateta picked out the bottom-left corner after six minutes. He latched onto a loose cross, but he had strayed narrowly offside.
Chris Richards' looping header landed on the roof of the net shortly after, before Mateta tamely scuffed a volley into Alexander Nubel's gloves from a corner on the half-hour mark.
Besiktas scored with their first effort on target in the first minute of first-half stoppage time. Ndidi plucked a long ball out of the air and drilled his low shot past Walter Benitez.

However, Palace made a bright start to the second half, and this one was rewarded. They faced a long wait after Pino was flagged offside after he slid in to meet Anan Khalaili's right-sided cross and poke it beyond Nubel, but the 51st-minute equaliser was given following a VAR review.
And Mateta put Palace in front just four minutes later, pouncing on a loose back pass from Tiago Djalo to rifle an emphatic effort into the back of the net for his first goal of the season.

Sage's team failed to add to their advantage, though, and Olaitan punished them for it as he intercepted a loose Khalaili clearance and skipped past two defenders before sending a skidding shot beyond Benitez in the 73rd minute.

Besiktas set up a nervy ending for themselves four minutes later as Umit Akdag lunged in with a two-footed tackle on Jorgen Strand Larsen, resulting in a straight red card, but the hosts held out for a point.
Sage's worries grow as Palace lack bite

Reports earlier this week suggested Sage's position is looking precarious after Palace were thrashed 5-0 by rivals Brighton in the Premier League, meaning they would have wanted to come away with three points from Tupras Stadyumu.
Mateta's disallowed goal was only marginally offside, but Palace were unable to build momentum afterwards and looked like they had been dealt a hammer blow late in the first half.
But they responded well, with only 259 seconds separating their two goals, which were of quality given Palace only accumulated 0.4 expected goals (xG) overall from their eight attempts.
Their problems this term have been in defence, though, as they have kept just one clean sheet in their last 16 games on the road in all competitions, shipping a total of 33 goals in that time.

Mateta's first goal of the season is one weight off their shoulders; he has now scored 63 goals in all competitions for Palace, 26 more than any other player since his debut in February 2021 (Eberechi Eze next on 37).

But Besiktas were never going down without a fight as they extended their unbeaten start in the Europa League (W2 D1), while also making it five games without defeat on home soil in Europe (W4 D1 including qualifiers).

ltgew7fj584c1scxtmoa5sdjy.title: Kovac: Sabah clash offers Dortmund perfect chance to end scoring struggles
ltgew7fj584c1scxtmoa5sdjy.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund are without a goal in their last two matches in all competitions, and they face Champions League debutants Sabah next.
paragraphs: Borussia Dortmund's Champions League fixture against Sabah could be the perfect opportunity to reignite their recently misfiring attack, so says Niko Kovac.
Dortmund return to Champions League action on Tuesday when they make the trip to Baki Olimpiya Stadionu to face the Azerbaijani minnows, who made history last time out.
In what was just their second game in major European competition, Sabah recorded their first win on the European stage when they beat Slavia Praha 2-0 on home soil.
And they may fancy their chances against a Dortmund side that have struggled since returning from the international break, with their problems coming in the final third.

They have scored just two goals in their last three matches across all competitions, while they have failed to find the back of the net in back-to-back games for the first time since February 2025, after losing 1-0 to Bodo/Glimt and playing out a goalless draw with Union Berlin last week.
Kovac's side registered an expected goals (xG) total of just 1.09 from their 10 shots against Union, and only two of those forced Frederik Ronnow into making a save.

Dortmund have also had fewer than 10 shots in five of their last six Champions League matches (83%). In their first 12 games in the competition under Kovac, they had fewer than 10 shots on just two occasions (17%), averaging 14.1 attempts per game.
"We need to play much more accurately, much more precisely, and much more automatically in the final third," Kovac told reporters of his team's attack.
"Union defended well, but we also didn’t play the way I would have liked, because it would have been possible to attack behind the opponent's defence to ultimately break through their line.
"We need to get back to doing that quickly, because you can only win games by scoring goals."

This will be just the second European Cup or Champions League game between teams from Azerbaijan and Germany, following Qarabag's 3-2 win over Eintracht Frankfurt in January earlier this year, though Dortmund have a good record against teams from that part of the world.

BVB have won all four of their matches against Azerbaijani opponents in European competitions (including qualifiers), beating Qarabag twice in Europa League qualifying in 2010-11 and Qabala twice in the Europa League group stage in 2015-16.
They have, however, lost four of their last six Champions League matches (W2), as many defeats as they had in their previous 17 matches in the competition combined (four).

And after going without a win in their last three games in all competitions, Dortmund's Sporting Director Lars Ricken said things must improve quickly if they are to maintain the standards they set during the early parts of the campaign.
"We can see that we're going through a somewhat difficult phase right now. Going three games in a row without a win isn't normal for Borussia Dortmund," Ricken conceded.
"But we have to remind ourselves that we established an excellent position for ourselves early in the season, in the Bundesliga, the DFB-Pokal and the Champions League.
"That's still the case. Now it's about showing our willingness to fight and, in the truest sense of the word, to defend that position.

"But of course, we also want to take the initiative more often on offence again, to be aggressive and determined, create scoring chances, score goals, and regain that hunger to win games at all costs.
"When you have a challenge like this in the Champions League, you can fly to Baku with enthusiasm and anticipation. That should be our mindset now."

m2km546gaa8e10unl6wphjtoa.title: Colombia must give Suarez more support, says head coach Lorenzo
m2km546gaa8e10unl6wphjtoa.subtitle: Colombia lost 1-0 to Paraguay in a friendly on Friday, with star striker Luis Suarez unable to make an impact at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
paragraphs: Colombia head coach Nestor Lorenzo believes his side "should have supported Luis Suarez a bit more" in their defeat to Paraguay on Friday.
Paraguay won 1-0 at Sports Illustrated Stadium thanks to Hugo Benitez's winner in the 56th minute.
Although Colombia recorded almost three times as many shots as Paraguay (14 to five), the latter accumulated more expected goals (0.95 to 0.89) and hit the target just as often (two).
Colombia struggled to get Suarez into the game; the striker was responsible for just one of their 14 shots and recorded the fewest touches of any starting player in the team (14).
Suarez had scored in each of his previous seven games for club and country, netting eight times in that run, and Lorenzo acknowledged Colombia must create more chances for their talisman.
"I think we should have supported Luis Suarez a bit more," said Lorenzo.
"We needed more width from the full-backs. And when we did get forward, perhaps we didn't deliver enough crosses, and we faced an opponent that defends very well deep in their own half.

"The problem is that we struggled to get our build-up play right, we let ourselves get pressed, we made a lot of mistakes in that area, and we played against a team that had just come from a very well-prepared World Cup, which made things difficult for us.
"There were times when we made very simple, very childish mistakes, I'd say, in the final play; either we didn't cross the ball, or we went back and lost possession.
"We're still building, and we'll draw conclusions as time goes on. I think there are some positive things to highlight, even though I acknowledge the team didn't play well."
Colombia face Peru in the final game of the international break on October 6.

mb6zakc8ytax1tip7i9m9dlsx.title: Alonso insists 'Premier League is the main focus' after EFL Cup exit
mb6zakc8ytax1tip7i9m9dlsx.subtitle: Chelsea were knocked out on penalties by Liverpool in the EFL Cup last 16, but Xabi Alonso's priorities lie elsewhere.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso insisted "the Premier League is the main focus" for Chelsea after their EFL Cup exit against Liverpool.
The Blues were knocked out on penalties at Anfield, with the Reds winning 6-5 in the shoot-out after Wesley Fofana missed the decisive spot-kick.
The tie finished 1-1 after 90 minutes as Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo scored penalties for their respective sides in the first half.
Chelsea had the opportunity to win the shoot-out, but debutant Emmanuel Emegha saw his effort saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili.
Despite a chance at early silverware now gone for ex-Liverpool star Alonso, the Spaniard quickly turned his focus to Chelsea's Premier League clash with Manchester United on Saturday.
"Every time you reach the penalties, someone will feel it is harsh to go out of the competition. It was really close from both sides. Penalties mean it is open to anything," Alonso told Sky Sports.
"They have performed at a good enough level to compete at Anfield. We conceded the penalty and it was even. The game was really close for both sides.
"This is football. It is part of our job. We were showing a good level and this is what it takes to come to these stadiums. The Premier League is the main focus.
"We don't have much time to recover because the game is Saturday, early kick-off so we need to change the mindset quite quickly."
In the absence of the injured Joao Pedro and suspended Cole Palmer, Rogers took on more responsibility in Chelsea's attack.
He led his side in shots (six), touches in the box (nine) and successful dribbles (3/5) to go along with his goal.
"It is probably the worst way to lose a game," Rogers told ITV Sport.
"It was an even game and at times we had the better of it. I had half chances that I'd have liked to have put away.
"It was one of those that can go either way and you have to accept it."
