Leeds, meanwhile, lost a Premier League game in which they opened the scoring in the second half for the first time since October 1992 (1-2 vs Queens Park Rangers).

"Gutted for my lads because they showed an excellent performance. I'm heartbroken that we didn't take anything away. But also proud because we played excellent in the first half," Daniel Farke told BBC Sport.

"I said at half-time, if we have more clarity and belief in our situations, then we can win this game. We went for it, even to score the second goal, we had the momentum on our side, but Arsenal are the reigning champions. One of the best teams, if not the best team in Europe – this means one of the best teams in the world.

"Even with little details they are able to capitalise. All credit goes to them, they found a way to turn this game."

os8l375x88913mhtxody0l71.title: Alvarez's first Atletico goal of 2026-27 delights Simeone
os8l375x88913mhtxody0l71.subtitle: Julian Alvarez grabbed his first goal of the season, but Atletico Madrid could not overcome Stuttgart in the Champions League.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone was delighted for Julian Alvarez after the Atletico Madrid striker broke his goalscoring duck for the season.
Alvarez, who wanted to leave Atletico in the summer transfer window, netted his first goal of the campaign in a 1-1 Champions League draw with Stuttgart on Tuesday.

Jamie Leweling opened the scoring at MHPArena, but Alvarez restored parity early in the second half, brilliantly scooping a left-footed finish into the top corner after meeting Ademola Lookman's centre.

Alvarez now has 26 Champions League goals, which is the outright fourth most by an Argentinian player, behind Lionel Messi (129), Sergio Aguero (41) and Lautaro Martinez (27).Morten Hjulmand's 64th-minute red card made matters more difficult for Atletico, but Simeone was thrilled for Alvarez, who was jeered by the club's fans earlier this season.
"He scored a fantastic goal, I'm really happy for him," Simeone said of Alvarez.
"We need him to get to where we want to be."
Atletico have kept just one clean sheet in their last 12 away Champions League games, shipping a total of 23 goals in those matches.
However, Simeone felt that, after a sluggish start, his team showed their mettle, especially after Hjulmand's dismissal.

"I think what we saw at the end of the first half and during the second, both with 11 and 10 players, is who we are: competitive, hardworking, humble, with many players who make great efforts," he said.
"We're trying to build towards the goals the club wants.

"With the [Stuttgart] goal, the team improved. That's normal, it made us react. The team started to show signs of being in the game. We knew the goal was coming, and with the sending-off, we had to readjust."
Atletico have taken four points from their first three Champions League outings this term. They host Bayern Munich in their next fixture.

ovzps9q8n3ql1rb5rd8eezqn8.title: Bournemouth 3-0 Sturm Graz: Evanilson nets stunner in historic home victory
ovzps9q8n3ql1rb5rd8eezqn8.subtitle: Bournemouth ensured a historic European encounter at Vitality Stadium ended in victory, with Sturm Graz no match for Marco Rose's side.
paragraphs: Bournemouth marked their first home game in European competition with a victory as they swept aside Sturm Graz 3-0 to seal back-to-back wins in the Europa League.
Evanilson's superb 43rd-minute header put Bournemouth ahead, with Rayan making an instant impact off the bench by scoring the Cherries' second from close range.
Alvaro Rodriguez sealed the deal with a late penalty, with Marco Rose's side welcoming Serie A and European giants AC Milan to the Vitality Stadium next Thursday.
Marcus Tavernier squandered a huge chance to give Bournemouth a 12th-minute lead, but after he was found by Adam Smith's glorious cross, he failed to test Daniil Khudyakov.

Bournemouth thought they had taken the lead when Tavernier's teasing corner was flicked on by Evanilson, with the loose ball turned in on the line by Bafode Diakite, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against the Frenchman in the goalmouth scramble.

Tavernier then thundered a curling effort against the left post before the Cherries survived a scare at the other end when Belmin Beganovic went down under Smith's challenge, but the Sturm Graz attacker was booked for simulation, though the replays showed there was contact.
And the hosts made the most of their luck two minutes before half-time through Evanilson, who looped a stunning header from Smith's cross over Khudyakov and into the net.

But Sturm Graz came out firing after the break and should have drawn level just after the hour. Simon Seidl's delivery to the back post ended with Jurgen Heil rattling the woodwork, with Djordje Petrovic on hand to repel Jacob Hodl on the rebound.

However, the hosts doubled their advantage in the 76th minute. Lewis Cook's corner was only punched as far as Rayan, who sent a right-footed shot towards goal on the swivel that squirmed through the grasp of Khudyakov.

Bournemouth were keen to add to their tally late on, with Justin Kluivert stinging the palms of Khudyakov, and they would add further gloss to the scoreline when James Hill was chopped down inside the area by Jon Gorenc Stankovic, with Rodriguez sending the resulting penalty down the middle.
Evanilson a head above the rest in statement Bournemouth win

Ahead of kick-off, Rose described Bournemouth's 5-1 defeat to Chelsea in the Premier League last weekend as a "real slap" in the face. The Cherries boss urged his players to deliver a response, and they certainly did that here.

The Cherries' win was laid on the foundations of Evanilson's quite wonderful opening goal. At 16.3 metres, the Brazilian scored the furthest-distance headed goal in a major European competition this season, while it was his second goal of 2026-27 in his eighth outing in all competitions.

In what was a historic match for the Bournemouth home faithful, they watched their team become the first English side to win their first two matches in major European competition since Bolton Wanderers in the 2005-06 UEFA Cup.
Rayan, meanwhile, is the youngest player (aged 20) to score in an English club's first two major European matches since an 18-year-old Jimmy Greaves scored in Chelsea's first two in 1958.

English clubs are unbeaten in their last 35 matches in major European competition against Austrian sides (W28 D7) since Arsenal lost 1-0 to Austria Wien in October 1991 in the European Cup, and Bournemouth were deserving winners.

Rose's side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.68 from their 24 shots to Sturm Graz's 0.36 from their six attempts, with Bournemouth now hoping this win can be used to turn their Premier League fortunes around. They face Sunderland, who also won in the Europa League earlier on Thursday, this weekend.

owv3frz9a51szoys3zgrvbi3.title: Tuchel laments England's mistakes and missed chances
owv3frz9a51szoys3zgrvbi3.subtitle: England created a lot of their own problems against Spain, and could not turn their half-time lead into a victory over the world champions.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel was left to rue England's mistakes and missed chances as they were beaten 3-2 by Spain in the opening match of their Nations League campaign.
England had threatened to give Spain a scare after coming from behind – after a Marc Guehi mistake gifted Lamine Yamal a second-minute opener – through Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane before half-time.
However after the break, Kane then missed a penalty, rattling the crossbar after his standing leg slipped, and Spain mounted a comeback of their own.

Nico O'Reilly gifted the ball to Spain deep in England's half, with Alex Baena ultimately profiting before Mikel Oyarzabal netted the winner in the 74th minute, coming back to haunt England after scoring the winning goal at Euro 2024.
England have conceded 3+ goals in consecutive matches for the first time since June 1995 (3-3 v Sweden, 1-3 v Brazil on that occasion).
The Three Lions have also conceded 13 goals in their last six matches in all competitions, almost double the total they had shipped in their first 17 under Tuchel (seven).
This is the first time England have made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive match since June 2019 against the Netherlands, also in the Nations League.
"Terrible start, the worst start possible," Tuchel told ITV Sport.
"It makes it so, so difficult to be behind against this type of team. After 10-12 minutes, I think we were the better team. We dominated in the opponent's half.

"We created and scored two goals, our best 15 minutes after the whistle. We couldn't convert the penalty – I think then maybe Spain would have believed that their long run of unbeaten games ends here.

"Another big, big mistake for 2-2. The third goal was the only goal they really scored. Just is what it is. We have to keep going and learn from it. Take what is positive and take the points back to the Czech Republic."
Spain are now unbeaten in their last 39 games (in 90 minutes), extending the longest such streak by a European nation (W30 D9).
And it meant they piled more worry on England, who have won just six of their last 16 matches against nations ranked in FIFA's top 10.
"I was not in charge for all of these 16 matches, for sure not, and I think we did everything to beat Spain," said Tuchel.

"Details matter on this kind of level. Like I said, the amount of clear-cut mistakes was too high on our side, unfortunately, and in the last 20 metres they were more composed and more clinical to convert our ball-losses into clear-cut chances.
"We will keep on pushing this team.
"We proved it at the World Cup that we are capable to do it in tournaments. We cannot prove it in the result [against Spain], but I think the way we played was enough to beat them."

ozwkzownn6f81vxfq1struemf.title: Smith impressed with Charlotte's consistency ahead of Orlando clash
ozwkzownn6f81vxfq1struemf.subtitle: Charlotte FC have secured their playoff berth, but could still rise up the Eastern Conference as they prepare to host Orlando City.
paragraphs: Dean Smith praised his Charlotte FC side for their consistency ahead of welcoming Orlando City SC to Bank of America Stadium.
Charlotte booked their place in the playoffs with a 4-0 victory over CF Montreal on Wednesday, with Liel Abada scoring a hat-trick for The Crown.
Idan Toklomati also got on the scoresheet, with Charlotte now guaranteed a top-six finish in the Eastern Conference.
Charlotte have also reached the 50-point mark for the third consecutive season, joining Inter Miami as the only clubs to do so in the 2024, 2025 and 2026 campaigns.
The Crown could still finish further up the table, but Smith took the time to praise his side for their consistency over the last three seasons.
"To be honest, my job first of all was to go and win a game, to qualify for the playoffs and then see how far we can go," said Smith.
"How many points we can get, what position we can end up in and still two games in the regular season to go and do that, then we'll start thinking about how we approach the playoffs.
"Consistency is about winning football games and getting points and we've managed to get more than 50 points in the three years I've been here.
"I'm really pleased with the consistency that the players have shown. We've won some away games, but the majority of our wins always come here, so it's good to be back with our fans behind us."
Orlando City are seventh in the East after a 2-2 draw with the Chicago Fire last time out, and are yet to confirm their place in the postseason.
Victory against Charlotte would see Orlando secure a top-nine finish, though their battle to finish above the wildcard places would go down to the final day.
Charlotte FC – Idan Toklomati
Toklomati recorded a goal and an assist in Charlotte's win over Montreal, while also winning the joint-most duels (6/11).
He has scored in each of his last five MLS games, the longest such run in Charlotte's history.
Orlando City – Antoine Griezmann
After scoring against Chicago, Antoine Griezmann became just the fourth player in MLS history to record a goal or assist in at least 12 consecutive matches in a single regular season.
MATCH PREDICTION: CHARLOTTE FC WIN
Charlotte have won 31 points in 16 home games this season; only Nashville SC (44) and the New England Revolution (35) have won more such points in 2026 among Eastern Conference teams.
However, Orlando have got the better of Charlotte of late, unbeaten in the last four MLS matches between the two teams (W2 D2).
A win for Charlotte would be their first against Orlando in the league since November 2024. The Lions during that period have outscored Charlotte 10-5, following a 4-1 win back in April.
Orlando are unbeaten in their last four MLS outings, but three of those have been draws, including each of the last two.

p29ae257wecj1fgvb494s1xyu.title: Arteta delighted with Arsenal's 'great attacking flow'
p29ae257wecj1fgvb494s1xyu.subtitle: Arsenal looked back to their best against Lille in the Champions League, and Mikel Arteta is pleased with his forward line.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta believes his Arsenal side are "showing great attacking flow" ahead of a crucial test against Nottingham Forest.
The Gunners have come back strong after the international break, defeating Leeds United 2-1 in the Premier League and Lille 3-0 in the Champions League.

Arsenal have won 14 of their last 17 Premier League games (L3), with nine of those wins coming via a one-goal margin. In the last two seasons, the Gunners have won 17 games by a single goal, the most of any side in Europe's big-five leagues.
However, the last two Premier League meetings between Forest and Arsenal at the City Ground have ended goalless, with 40 shots attempted without success.
Arteta is hoping to change their fortunes around at the City Ground, and is not bothered about how the goals come about.
When asked about Arsenal scoring more goals from open play this season, Arteta responded: "We are getting criticised for scoring goals!
"Regardless of the manner that we score them, the team is showing a great attacking flow. We’ve scored some beautiful goals, but the value is exactly the same.
"I think we have to be a team that is able to score in many, many ways and that will make it harder for the opponent.
"We're going to try really hard to score goals and to prevent goals as well. It's going to be a really tough match; they're an extremely well-coached team.
"We know that, we already have experience with Oliver [Glasner] in the past, and they're a team that, at home, can create a really special momentum, so we are ready for it."
Forest have won one of their last 11 Premier League games against Arsenal (D2 L8), a 1-0 home win in May 2023. The Tricky Trees have failed to score in each of their last four.

Glasner has just five wins in 29 games (D9 L15) since a 2-1 win at Fulham put his Crystal Palace side fourth in the league on December 7 last year, and he acknowledged the size of the task ahead against Arsenal.
"It's huge credit to Mikel Arteta and Arsenal. It's now a team that has been built over years and always at the beginning finding a core and then always adding the right pieces," said Glasner.

"It's not just the quality, it's also the mentality in how they play. I think in every game this season they were outrunning the opposition. It's incredible. The effort, the mindset Mikel created there is incredible.
"They have so many world-class players they can react from the bench. It was now in the second consecutive game where the players who came on had a huge impact, and this shows the quality they have.
"This is what we are facing, and I think the structure of how they are playing, everybody knows and analyses, but the way they execute it makes it so difficult."

p4zhh0xydyf31mp7yed27rdfg.title: Arteta laments Arsenal's profligacy after shock EFL Cup exit
p4zhh0xydyf31mp7yed27rdfg.subtitle: Arsenal were dumped out of the EFL Cup by fourth-tier Fleetwood Town, in one of the biggest upsets in the competition's history.
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta had no issues with Arsenal's effort or attitude in their shock EFL Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town.
Arsenal, last year's runners-up, crashed out of the competition on Tuesday as fourth-tier Fleetwood pulled off an incredible cup upset.
Fleetwood prevailed 5-3 on penalties following a 1-1 draw at Highbury Stadium.
Aaron Loupalo-Bi put Fleetwood into the lead in the 21st minute, and though Viktor Gyokeres levelled in scruffy fashion early in the second half, Fleetwood held firm to take the game to penalties.

Max Dowman saw red for the Gunners late on, too, and Arsenal's night reached its low point when Conor Haughey slammed home the winning penalty after Bruno Guimaraes had been denied by the superb Jay Lynch.
Arteta, though, insisted his team did not lack a desire to win.

"First of all, congratulate Fleetwood for what they have done, for winning the match and going through to the next round, for the way they have done it and for the atmosphere they have created," he told Sky Sports.
"A really sad day for us. I cannot fault the attitude of the players, I have not seen anybody not doing what is required at this level.
"We had so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots – if you want the margin to be bigger than penalties you have to capitalise on that, and we didn't.

"We gave them momentum, but then they created nothing through the whole game but we didn’t capitalise on that, then the margins become so small. That's football, that's the beauty of this competition and especially in this country. It's a very sad day.

"Attitude-wise, I have zero [issues], otherwise I would be absolutely fuming. We are sad, we are all sad, we have a responsibility. It was nothing to do with effort or application or wanting to go and win it, but we lacked other things, and that has been shown in the scoreline."
Arsenal had 26 shots, hitting the target seven times, and created chances worth 2.21 expected goals.

p9cahx7vraeq120v39txebcgk.title: Vitinha wants Ronaldo return after 'turbulent' international break
p9cahx7vraeq120v39txebcgk.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's immediate Portugal future is in doubt, but compatriot Vitinha hopes to see their record scorer return to the squad.
paragraphs: Vitinha revealed he hopes "everything gets resolved" between Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal boss Jorge Jesus after a "turbulent" international break.
Ronaldo left Portugal's squad during the extended break after being an unused substitute during their 2-1 win over Norway.
The 41-year-old released a statement apologising to his team-mates, but accused head coach Jesus of "breaking his word" after leaving him on the bench.
Ronaldo also said he would accept whatever punishment Portugal's Football Federation (FPF) impose, with the FPF provisionally suspending their captain.
When asked about the situation after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League win over Manchester City, Vitinha expressed his desire to see Ronaldo return for the November break.
"It was a turbulent international break – full of high emotions," Vitinha told TNT Sports.
"For my part, I just hope everything gets resolved for the best. I hope he [Ronaldo] returns and that everything turns out fine.
"The truth is, that's what we all want. I hope he comes back and everything is sorted out."
Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 appearances for Portugal, netting more often than any other player for his country.
Portugal have already qualified for the quarter-finals of the Nations League after winning all four of their matches during the previous break.
In November, Jesus' side will face Denmark and Wales as they look to clinch top spot in Group A4.

pbavn0mactaa17l67uej7am8z.title: Leeds 'were the dominant side' against Man Utd, says Farke
pbavn0mactaa17l67uej7am8z.subtitle: Leeds United were the better side for long periods against Manchester United, with Daniel Farke feeling they could have earned three points.
paragraphs: Daniel Farke believes Leeds United were "dominant" for long stretches against Manchester United, noting his players were slightly disappointed to settle for a draw on Sunday.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's opener as the old rivals drew 1-1 at Elland Road, though it was Leeds who had the better chances to win the contest in the second half.

Leeds are now unbeaten in their last three Premier League matches against Man Utd (W1 D2), their joint-longest unbeaten run against the Red Devils in the competition, along with another run of three between September 1994 and December 1995.

They tallied 12 shots to their visitors' 13, but their chances were of a higher quality as they amassed 1.44 expected goals (xG) to Man Utd's 0.91 – 1.18 of Leeds' tally came from set-pieces as they dominated on a physical level.
And speaking to Sky Sports afterwards, Farke was left to rue missed second-half chances from the likes of Ao Tanaka, Noah Okafor and Anton Stach.
"We were the dominant side today, but sadly we could not fully capitalise on it because we lacked quality around the opponents' box," Farke said.
Harry Maguire said in his post-match interview that Man Utd had attempted to match Leeds' 3-4-3 system.
When asked about that tweak from Michael Carrick, Farke said: "It says a lot about how much respect we've earned, but it is no coincidence.
"We're unbeaten at home and haven't suffered too many losses over the last three years.
"It says a lot about how far we've come that we are slightly disappointed it was just a point against Manchester United.
"Overall, it was not necessary to be in a losing position at half-time, but it is still Manchester United – they have unbelievable individual quality up front. "

Calvert-Lewin's goal was his 12th for Leeds in the Premier League at Elland Road, with only Erling Haaland (19) and Igor Thiago (14) scoring more home goals in the competition since his first home match for the club.
Many pundits, and indeed, the Opta supercomputer, tagged Leeds as pre-match favourites against an out-of-form Man Utd side, but Calvert-Lewin said the hosts had done well to shut out that noise.
"It was important that we didn't read too much into it. They are still a good team with a lot of quality. It is just general football stuff, isn't it?," he said.
"You have Sky Sports News on; you hear what's going on in the football world, but we are so used to it as players that it is important you pay no mind to it and focus on the game."

pegatjantgti1vobgwd9y86p2.title: 'We try and win every game' – Colorado determined to stick to identity to earn playoff spot
pegatjantgti1vobgwd9y86p2.subtitle: Colorado Rapids and the LA Galaxy both want to make sure they are in the postseason, but they still have work to do to make it happen.
paragraphs: Matt Wells wants the Colorado Rapids to stick to their identity as they continue their push to secure an MLS playoff spot against the LA Galaxy.
Colorado currently sit seventh in the Western Conference on 36 points, and they come into this game unbeaten in their last three matches (W1 D2).
However, they threw away a 3-1 lead against the Seattle Sounders last time out, conceding twice in the last 15 minutes, including a stoppage-time equaliser from Caden Clark.

And on the road, the Rapids have had their struggles, failing to win any of their last five away games in the competition, with their last such win coming against Minnesota United before the World Cup break in May.
But Wells is not changing his approach despite the end of the regular season approaching, as he remains confident Colorado have what it takes to clinch their playoff berth.
"No special messages [about the playoff push]," he said. "We try and win every game.

"So, for me, our process here is that we're always immersed in the game preparation. It's like if we want to look any further ahead than the Galaxy, then we'll go to the Galaxy and get a total of zero points.
"We have to be fully focused on our next opponent. We're trying to guess the dynamic of the team they'll put out, both personnel and tactically.
"We're in a good spot. It's about us going out in all of these games now. It's about us going out and playing to our identity, playing our style and executing the game plan that we've put into place.
"We know as a group, whenever we've done that, we've been successful."
The Galaxy are also pushing to make it to the postseason, and they sit three points behind the Rapids in eighth.
Greg Vanney's side have lost just one of their last four league games (W2 D1) and come into this match on the back of a 3-2 comeback win over Minnesota last weekend.
LA Galaxy – Marco Reus
Marco Reus scored the 13th regular-season goal of his MLS career on Saturday, but it was only his second league goal on the road for LA Galaxy.
Reus' three goals this month are tied for his most in a single calendar month for the Galaxy, also netting three earlier this season in April.
Colorado Rapids – Morgan Whittaker
On Saturday, Morgan Whittaker tallied a brace for Colorado in his first career start for the club, becoming the second Rapids player to do that this season (Kosi Thompson – April 12).
Prior to this season, the last Rapids player to have multiple goals in his first regular-season start for the club was Raul Diaz Arce in 2001.
MATCH PREDICTION: LA GALAXY WIN
LA Galaxy have earned 41 all-time regular-season wins against the Rapids (incl. shootout wins), tied for their most wins against a single MLS opponent (also the San Jose Earthquakes).
The only MLS team to have more wins against a single team in regular-season play is Columbus against the New England Revolution (42).

Trailing 2-1 in the 75th minute, the Galaxy scored twice to earn a 3-2 comeback win against Minnesota United last weekend. It was the second time over the last eight seasons that the Galaxy rallied to win after trailing in the 75th minute or later, also doing so in March 2024 at Sporting Kansas City.
But the Rapids earned a 3-3 draw Saturday against Seattle, their first time scoring three or more goals since a 6-2 win against the Houston Dynamo in April.
Colorado scored at least three goals in three of their first seven matches in 2026 across all competitions but have done so in just one of their last 23 games.
Colorado Rapids – 27.8%

pfd0u7cfq7vm16u81hvck88xz.title: Alaves 1-2 Atletico Madrid: Romero wins it late after Perez red card
pfd0u7cfq7vm16u81hvck88xz.subtitle: Atletico Madrid left it late, but ultimately Cristian Romero proved the matchwinner in a 2-1 LaLiga victory over Alaves.
paragraphs: Cristian Romero's late header earned Atletico Madrid a 2-1 win over 10-player Alaves at Estadio de Mendizorroza on Saturday.
Alejandro Grimaldo fired Diego Simeone's side ahead but Alaves levelled shortly before the break thanks to Lucas Boye's penalty.
However, the hosts were up against it when Angel Perez saw red just after the hour, and Romero scored the winner thanks to a sublime cross from Alex Baena.
Jonathan David was unlucky to see a 14th-minute effort headed for the right corner well saved by Alaves goalkeeper Antonio Sivera.
Ademola Lookman also went close twice before Atleti took the lead just after the half hour, with Grimaldo drilling into the bottom-right corner after being slipped in by David.

But Quintero Gonzalez awarded Alaves a penalty on the stroke of half-time when Robin Le Normand was judged to have hauled down Toni Martinez in the penalty area, and Boye dispatched his spot-kick past Jan Oblak.
Alaves were facing an uphill task just after the hour when Perez was sent off for an ugly lunge on Julian Alvarez, with Gonzalez upgrading from a yellow card after a VAR intervention.

Alvarez then saw a free-kick clip the left-hand post, but Atleti did find the winner with three minutes to go, Baena's stupendous outside-of-the-boot cross headed home at the back post by former Tottenham man Romero.
Atleti break Alaves' resolve
It may have taken longer than they would have liked, but Atleti were good value for the three points in this one.
Simeone's side had 22 shots to Alaves eight, with seven of those on target to the hosts' three.
Indeed, Alaves' open-play xG registered at just 0.29, with their first-half penalty lifting that to 1.09, compared to Atleti's 2.12.
David has been a big contributor for Atleti, who climb to second with this victory, with the Canadian scoring three and assisting two in his past four LaLiga outings.
Veteran Koke showed his enduring talent, attempting 122 passes for Atleti in this game, the most of any player in LaLiga this season.
Atleti now turn their attentions to Tuesday's Champions League contest at home to Manchester United.

phzjzor1ct0714pn2bxzrdw5a.title: 'I give up' – Klopp exasperated by debate over Kimmich's Germany role
phzjzor1ct0714pn2bxzrdw5a.subtitle: Continued questions over Joshua Kimmich's Germany future have left Jurgen Klopp frustrated, with the ex-Liverpool boss lashing out.
paragraphs: An exasperated Jurgen Klopp said he has given up on answering questions about Joshua Kimmich's Germany future, amid continued speculation regarding his place in the team.

Following a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a surprise 1-0 defeat to Greece, Klopp avoided becoming the first Germany boss to fail to win his first three games in charge on Thursday, as Tom Bischof and Florian Wirtz scored in a 2-0 win over Serbia.
That victory came without captain Kimmich, as Aleksandar Pavlovic played alongside the two goalscorers in the centre of Germany's midfield.
Ahead of Sunday's trip to Greece, Klopp allowed several players – including Bayern Munich stalwart Kimmich – to return to their clubs.
That only fuelled speculation in the German media that the 31-year-old, whose 116 caps are the seventh-most in Die Nationalelf's history, may not be part of Klopp's long-term plans.
But when that prospect was put to Klopp again at Saturday's pre-match press conference, his frustration was clear.
"You can tell that it's extremely difficult for me to say anything about that, because you want to make a story out of it. We played a good game. Our midfield was top class," Klopp said.
"But can you imagine how s***** it would be if Germany had three, and only three, top-class midfielders?
"Why make it about one player when it's about the fact that we need several good players? We need all sorts of players. We need leaders. We need runners. We need everything.
"It was a loaded question. I understand that it's a logical and normal question, but I think it’s coming too soon.
"I'm very satisfied with all the lads. I'm looking forward to the future, and I hope we have a large pool.
"I just don't stand a chance with that question, without you guys making something out of it. I give up. Seriously. Officially.
"With respect to that topic, I give up. Do what you want with it. I'm happy with the last game, and I'm happy that Joshua Kimmich is a leading player for Germany."
Germany are third in Group A2 ahead of their fourth game, with Greece leading the way on seven points.
The Netherlands are second with five, while Serbia are yet to earn a point.

pj4nruo91hfx1jig9z6eq7kd4.title: Strasbourg 1-3 Paris Saint-Germain: Dembele stars in comeback triumph
pj4nruo91hfx1jig9z6eq7kd4.subtitle: Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty, got an assist and scored a goal as Paris Saint-Germain came from behind to beat Strasbourg on Saturday.
paragraphs: Paris Saint-Germain left it late to go top of Ligue 1 as Ousmane Dembele came off the bench to lead Luis Enrique's side to a 3-1 comeback win away to Strasbourg.
Giovanni Reyna had given Strasbourg a deserved lead in the first half, with the likes of Dembele, Achraf Hakimi, Desire Doue and Vitinha all watching on from the sidelines.
After coming on, Dembele missed a penalty in the 72nd minute, but he crossed for Illia Zabarnyi to level things up before getting himself on the scoresheet soon after.
Doue added further gloss to the scoreline in second-half stoppage time, with PSG now level on points at the summit with Monaco, who play Lorient on Sunday.
PSG started brightly and only the fingertips of Filip Jorgensen stopped Ferran Torres' header, but the visitors' dominance was without reward and they fell behind moments later.

After heading just wide, Reyna was on the money in the 17th minute. The American collected Gessime Yassine's pass before squeezing the ball in at Matvey Safonov's near post, with his shot taking a nick off Lucas Hernandez on its way in.

The hosts continued to push for a second, with Safonov producing a stunning save low to his left to keep out Conrad Harder's glancing header, with Luis Enrique making a triple change before also introducing Dembele and Hakimi just after the hour mark.
But it was Strasbourg who continued to threaten, with Harder again forcing Safonov into action at his near post before the PSG goalkeeper got down to thwart Karim Coulibaly.
However, following that flurry of goalmouth action, PSG were awarded a penalty when Doue's shot towards goal was handled by Pape Diop, only for Dembele to send the spot-kick past Jorgensen's post.
Dembele atoned for his error six minutes later when his teasing delivery to the back post was turned in by Zabarnyi, and PSG went ahead five minutes from time.

Coulibaly could only clear Hakimi's cross as far as Dembele, who shifted the ball onto his left foot before squeezing his effort under the grasp of Jorgensen, with the Ligue 1 champions rubber-stamping the win in the 93rd minute when Doue swept into an empty net after being teed up by Ferran.
Super subs make the difference for PSG

After PSG put on a superb display during their 4-2 win over Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday, Luis Enrique elected to rest some of his big-hitters, a decision that saw his team fail to fire in a disjointed opening period.

But once some of his first-team regulars entered the fray, there only looked like being one winner. Dembele did not let his head drop after his penalty miss, and he went on to finish with team-high totals for shots (four) and touches in the opposition box (eight).
Doue also impressed off the bench. His two shots on target were more than any other PSG player, while Vitinha also showed his class by creating a team-leading three chances.

The result saw PSG score in their 14th consecutive away game in Ligue 1. Only between January and September 2021 (15) have they managed to do so in more consecutive road matches, while they also won after trailing at half-time away from home in the top flight for the first time since January 2025, against Lens.

Luis Enrique's side were deserving victors too, finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.61 from their 18 attempts, to Strasbourg's 0.97 from 16 shots, though the PSG boss will want to see more improvement when they welcome Barcelona to the Parc des Princes in the Champions League next week.

Giovanni Reyna had given Strasbourg a deserved lead in the first half, with the likes of Dembele, Achraf Hakimi, Desire Doue and Vitinha all watching on from the sidelines. 

After coming on, Dembele missed a penalty in the 72nd minute, but he crossed for Illia Zabarnyi to level things up before getting himself on the scoresheet soon after. 

Doue added further gloss to the scoreline in second-half stoppage time, with PSG now level on points at the summit with Monaco, who play Lorient on Sunday. 

PSG started brightly and only the fingertips of Filip Jorgensen stopped Ferran Torres' header, but the visitors' dominance was without reward and they fell behind moments later.

After heading just wide, Reyna was on the money in the 17th minute. The American collected Gessime Yassine's pass before squeezing the ball in at Matvey Safonov's near post, with his shot taking a nick off Lucas Hernandez on its way in.

The hosts continued to push for a second, with Safonov producing a stunning save low to his left to keep out Conrad Harder's glancing header, with Luis Enrique making a triple change before also introducing Dembele and Hakimi just after the hour mark. 

But it was Strasbourg who continued to threaten, with Harder again forcing Safonov into action at his near post before the PSG goalkeeper got down to thwart Karim Coulibaly. 

However, following that flurry of goalmouth action, PSG were awarded a penalty when Doue's shot towards goal was handled by Pape Diop, only for Dembele to send the spot-kick past Jorgensen's post.

Dembele atoned for his error six minutes later when his teasing delivery to the back post was turned in by Zabarnyi, and PSG went ahead five minutes from time.

pl2reuu4fnuc1c3qcbr5cdn3j.title: Carrick confirms 'fully committed' Fernandes will remain Man Utd captain
pl2reuu4fnuc1c3qcbr5cdn3j.subtitle: Bruno Fernandes did not play a part in Manchester United's defeat to Bournemouth, but he looks set to return against Chelsea on Saturday.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick insisted Bruno Fernandes remains "committed" to the cause at Manchester United and will continue as the club's captain against Chelsea this weekend.
Fernandes was named on the bench for a Premier League game for United for only the sixth time last Sunday, with the Red Devils going down 3-0 at home to Bournemouth.
It was the first time he had not started a match under Carrick, while it was the second time he was an unused substitute while at United, along with May 2025 against Brentford.
The 32-year-old was dropped from United's starting line-up after questioning the tactics deployed by Carrick during a 4-1 defeat to Champions League debutants Como.
United are without a win in their last eight matches across all competitions (D3 L5), last having a longer winless run between October and November 1988 (nine).
Carrick will remain in charge of United's trip to Stamford Bridge to face Chelsea, with Fernandes set to return to the starting line-up having held talks with the Red Devils boss during the week.
"It was a decision about what we felt about the game, that's it. Bruno's fully committed to this football club, absolutely no issues with that," Carrick told reporters.
"We move forward, we make decisions as we go, and we're looking forward to the game on Saturday now."
After their defeat to Bournemouth, Carrick was applauded off by the United fans, who quickly turned to jeers aimed towards the players and the club's hierarchy at full-time.
Reports have suggested that Carrick has been given time to try and turn things around, though Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe have been linked with replacing him.
"I don't need any assurances from anyone. I totally get the position," Carrick added on his position.
"I understand the job, I understand the responsibilities, I understand what comes with that, so I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard."
When questioned about how he is dealing with the noise around his team, Carrick continued: "I don't see it, really. I see the things that I need to see.

"I don't look for it. It doesn't really help in any way. I've said before, I don't see it, really. I've said before, I care about what the supporters think, what it feels like in the stadium, them travelling to come and see us and support us.
"I care about what we give them and what they see. I genuinely don't take notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do to be better.
"I don't need anyone else to tell me. I care about what it feels like in the stadium, them travelling to games for us, to come and see us and support us.

"I care about what we give them, what we offer them and what they see. I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don't need anyone else to tell me anything else."

pwjko6izw2901mqrmt3btupes.title: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton: Isak on target again as Iraola ends wait for home league win
pwjko6izw2901mqrmt3btupes.subtitle: Brighton went to Anfield on the back of a superb run, but Fabian Hurzeler's team fell short in a 2-0 defeat to Liverpool.
paragraphs: Alexander Isak scored for the third Premier League game running as Liverpool snapped Brighton's brilliant form with a 2-0 win at Anfield.
Brighton went into Sunday's contest flying high in third place after a run of four straight league wins, which came by an aggregate score of 15-0.
Yet the Seagulls had their wings clipped as Liverpool raced into a 2-0 lead by the 21st minute.
Matters might have been much different had Yasin Ayari put away an early chance for the visitors, but the Sweden international sliced over a gaping goal.
Brighton were swiftly punished, with Florian Wirtz's wayward effort diverting in off the unfortunate Pascal Gross.

Isak then continued his fine form as he nudged in from Bradley Barcola's cross. The former Newcastle United striker has netted in three straight league games for the first time since January 2025, when he went on a run of eight matches with a goal.
Ayari struck the woodwork following a bad error from Alisson Becker, but Brighton's attack was blunted after the break.
Maxim De Cuyper had their best chance, but found his path to goal blocked by substitute Trey Nyoni, who had just replaced the injured Wirtz.

Liverpool's day almost got better when Luka Vuskovic thumped an overhit backpass towards his own goal, but Bart Verbruggen was on hand to spare his blushes and minimise the damage for Fabian Hurzeler's team.
Setback for the Seagulls as Iraola gets up and running at home
Brighton have arguably been the standout team so far this season in the Premier League, but despite their four straight clean sheets, they had been giving up chances.
Indeed, their 5.16 overperformance of goals conceded compared to their expected goals against figure prior to this weekend's matches was the biggest in the division.
So, something perhaps had to give sooner rather than later, and Liverpool had the attacking talent to take advantage.

Liverpool had nine shots in the first half, but got four of them on target, and their work paid off to put them in a commanding position, even if they did get fortunate that Ayari did not have his shooting boots on.

The Reds are unbeaten in all 127 of their Premier League home games when leading by 2+ goals at half-time (W124 D3), and in truth they never looked likely to let this lead slip, albeit Nyoni's vital challenge on De Cuyper helped Liverpool stave off the nerves.

This was Iraola's first league win at Anfield as Liverpool boss, and it ensured the Reds did not fail to win each of their opening four home matches of a league campaign for only the fourth time, after 1894-95, 1911-12, and 2012-13.

pzj343hohn5w1gvonrgporm00.title: Spalletti sees Rennes matchup as 'maturity test' for Juventus
pzj343hohn5w1gvonrgporm00.subtitle: Despite their poor form in Serie A, Juventus are looking to maintain their perfect start in the Europa League when they host Rennes.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti believes Juventus' Europa League matchup with Rennes will be a "maturity test" for his side.
Juve are top of the league phase table after two matchdays following a 5-0 win over NEC and 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo, but their Serie A form has suffered.
The Bianconeri are eighth in Serie A after seven games following a 3-0 home defeat to Lazio, who are eight points ahead of Juve in second – level on points with leaders Inter.
Juve have lost two of their last five Serie A home games (W2 D1), as many defeats as they recorded in their previous 44 top-flight matches at the Allianz Stadium (W24 D18).
Nevertheless, they have won their last four home major European matches, scoring 12 goals and conceding two, and Spalletti desires a professional performance against Rennes.

When asked why Juve's results have differed in Serie A and the Europa League, Spalletti said: "There's no specific reason. Every match has its own history, and you have to react to what the opposition brings each time.
"You need to understand the consequences of their approach and know when to press and when to stick back. We have to be more decisive when we make a choice.
"Rennes is strong on the open field and physically.

"They have fast attackers and the [Ligue 1] top scorer, Lepaul. They are having a good season; they are sixth, but one point below the top spot, so they have enthusiasm, and for us it is a maturity test.
"We must be good at determining things with our attitude."
Juve and Rennes met in the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final, with the Italian side winning 4-2 on aggregate (2-0 home, 2-2 away).
In all European competition, Rennes have lost all four of their away matches in Italy, losing to a different team each time (Juve, Udinese, Lazio, AC Milan).

q6b5vmfgkz9611l1o52dueykq.title: Conte wants next club to be one that 'somewhat lost sight of their history'
q6b5vmfgkz9611l1o52dueykq.subtitle: Antonio Conte has been out of work since May, but he already has an idea of what kind of club he would like to join next.
paragraphs: Antonio Conte says he would like his next job to be at a club that has "somewhat lost sight of their history" and does not mind the pressure that would come with it.
Conte has been out of management since the end of the 2025-26 campaign, when he left Napoli after leading them to a second-place finish behind Inter.
During his two-year stint in Naples, Conte won the Scudetto and a Supercoppa Italiana.
Since then, he has been linked with the Italy job – which eventually went to Roberto Mancini – as well as Manchester United and Juventus, amid pressure on both Michael Carrick and Luciano Spalletti.
Conte has said he would like to return to the Premier League, having previously managed Chelsea, whom he led to the Premier League title in 2016-17, and Tottenham.

"If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself – a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories – you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back – if it isn't there today – to fight for those goals," Conte said when asked about his future.

"I know full well that only one team can win every year, but I must carry in my heart – and instil in the hearts of the fans, my players and my directors – that spark, that hope that makes you say, 'F***, we can win'.
"Even that 1% – but it must be a 1% that can become 70, 80 or even 100%. It depends on how you convey it.
"The manager is important because he conveys that message, day in, day out.

"He has daily interactions with everyone: with his staff, the masseur, the kit man, the physiotherapist, the groundsman – all people who need to be involved and feel part of the drive to make history, and you only make history by winning.
"There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more.
"Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete."

qch5619dbk9u1uymw7xa8r1ec.title: Spain winger Munoz learning from competition with Yamal
qch5619dbk9u1uymw7xa8r1ec.subtitle: Victor Munoz is serving as back-up to Lamine Yamal in the Spain squad, but the Liverpool winger is using the opportunity to grow his game.
paragraphs: Spain winger Victor Munoz called it "a privilege" to learn from Lamine Yamal as they compete for the same position in Luis De la Fuente's lineup.
Both players were a part of Spain's World Cup-winning squad in the summer, though Munoz did not feature due to injury as La Roja lifted the trophy for a second time in their history.
While Yamal also failed to have his desired impact at the tournament, he has helped Spain make a strong start to their Nations League campaign during this international break.
The teenager has scored three goals and provided one assist in wins over England and Croatia, with Munoz also featuring against the latter.
Yamal is currently one of the favourites to win the Ballon d'Or this month, and Munoz is making the most of training with the Barcelona superstar.
"I try to learn a lot from him; he’s a good friend of mine and we spend a lot of time together," said Munoz.
"It’s a privilege for me and he helps me a lot in my day-to-day life.
"[De la Fuente tells me to] just be myself. Try to help the team in attack and defence, try to be direct and try one-on-one. Those are what I think are my strengths."
Munoz completed a reported £35m (€40m) move to Liverpool in the summer, scoring once in six games so far, three of which were starts.
His only goal was an equaliser against Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, with Andoni Iraola's side still unbeaten across all competitions in 2026-27 (W4 D3).
"I do notice a difference between LaLiga and the Premier League," added the 23-year-old.
"LaLiga is more tactical, the Premier League is more physical. The intensity of the training sessions there is very high and it's helping me grow."

qew05q90l5xy1da8x4jev3pqz.title: Amorim: Milan improving despite second-half struggle against Atalanta
qew05q90l5xy1da8x4jev3pqz.subtitle: AC Milan extended their unbeaten start in Serie A to seven matches after beating Atalanta, but Ruben Amorim said improvements were needed.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim said AC Milan's struggles in the second half of Sunday's 3-2 win over Atalanta does not change the fact he is seeing improvements across all areas of his team.
Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A extended to seven matches at San Siro, but the Rossoneri survived a scare in the closing stages as Atalanta threatened an epic comeback.
Goncalo Ramos' 24th-minute penalty had given Milan the lead, with the in-form Adrien Rabiot doubling the hosts' tally just before the break to put Amorim's side in control.
Milan pulled further clear through Mario Gila, who headed in from a corner which came after Marco Carnesecchi had done brilliantly to keep out Ramos' second penalty.
Gianluca Gaetano came off the bench and scored seven minutes after his arrival, with Nikola Krstovic setting up a grandstand finish when he tucked home in the 81st minute.
However, Milan were able to hold on and claim an important three points, avoiding defeat in their first seven Serie A matches for the first time since 2021-22 (W6 D1).

Milan also ended a six-game winless run against Atalanta in the top flight, and though Amorim conceded the second-half display from his team was far from ideal, he believes that his players are slowly getting to grips with his tactics.
"Of course, the result is the most important thing, but we also have to analyse the performance," Amorim told DAZN Italia and Sky Sport Italia.
"I said against Sassuolo we were improving as a team, the final minutes don't change that, they just give us a clear idea that we have a lot of work to do.

"The momentum changed completely, as before the Atalanta goal, we were controlling the game and closer to a fourth goal than conceding a first, but some bad decisions, especially in the build-up, gave them opportunities, and we have to improve that."

The result also saw Amorim (W4 D3) become only the third Milan manager in Serie A history to remain unbeaten in each of his first seven games in charge, after Hector Puricelli in 1955 (W3 D4) and Luis Carniglia in 1963 (W4 D3).

Rabiot has been key to Milan's strong start, and he has now been involved in at least one goal in four consecutive matches for the first time in his career while playing across Europe's top five leagues.
The last midfielder to achieve this for Milan in Serie A was Hakan Calhanoglu in December 2020 (one assist per game against Parma, Genoa and Sassuolo, one goal and two assists against Lazio).
However, when speaking to Sky Sport Italia, Rabiot said he was angry with the way Milan performed in the second half, adding he wanted more from the substitutes.
"Rabiot is a really important player," Amorim said of Rabiot's comments. "I felt that after half-time we spoke to him.
"This is a guy who is experienced, he knows he cannot stop every play when he has a yellow.
"He was too important today to change him, but if I felt one more foul would lead to a card, I'd change him. I didn't feel that today."

Ruben Amorim said AC Milan's struggles in the second half of Sunday's 3-2 win over Atalanta does not change the fact he is seeing improvements across all areas of his team. 

Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A extended to seven matches at San Siro, but the Rossoneri survived a scare in the closing stages as Atalanta threatened an epic comeback. 

Goncalo Ramos' 24th-minute penalty had given Milan the lead, with the in-form Adrien Rabiot doubling the hosts' tally just before the break to put Amorim's side in control. 

Milan pulled further clear through Mario Gila, who headed in from a corner which came after Marco Carnesecchi had done brilliantly to keep out Ramos' second penalty. 

Gianluca Gaetano came off the bench and scored seven minutes after his arrival, with Nikola Krstovic setting up a grandstand finish when he tucked home in the 81st minute. 

However, Milan were able to hold on and claim an important three points, avoiding defeat in their first seven Serie A matches for the first time since 2021-22 (W6 D1). 

Milan also ended a six-game winless run against Atalanta in the top flight, and though Amorim conceded the second-half display from his team was far from ideal, he believes that his players are slowly getting to grips with his tactics. 

"Of course, the result is the most important thing, but we also have to analyse the performance," Amorim told DAZN Italia and Sky Sport Italia.

"I said against Sassuolo we were improving as a team, the final minutes don't change that, they just give us a clear idea that we have a lot of work to do.

"The momentum changed completely, as before the Atalanta goal, we were controlling the game and closer to a fourth goal than conceding a first, but some bad decisions, especially in the build-up, gave them opportunities, and we have to improve that."

The result also saw Amorim (W4 D3) become only the third Milan manager in Serie A history to remain unbeaten in each of his first seven games in charge, after Hector Puricelli in 1955 (W3 D4) and Luis Carniglia in 1963 (W4 D3).

Rabiot has been key to Milan's strong start, and he has now been involved in at least one goal in four consecutive matches for the first time in his career while playing across Europe's top five leagues. 

The last midfielder to achieve this for Milan in Serie A was Hakan Calhanoglu in December 2020 (one assist per game against Parma, Genoa and Sassuolo, one goal and two assists against Lazio).

However, when speaking to Sky Sport Italia, Rabiot said he was angry with the way Milan performed in the second half, adding he wanted more from the substitutes. 

"Rabiot is a really important player," Amorim said of Rabiot's comments. "I felt that after half-time we spoke to him.

"This is a guy who is experienced, he knows he cannot stop every play when he has a yellow.

"He was too important today to change him, but if I felt one more foul would lead to a card, I'd change him. I didn't feel that today."

qf8ewf9pfu3azgslf7swe3ah.title: Sage hails Palace fight after snatch-and-grab EFL Cup win at Fulham
qf8ewf9pfu3azgslf7swe3ah.subtitle: Crystal Palace earned a much-needed victory to ease the pressure on Pierre Sage and reach the last eight of the EFL Cup.
paragraphs: Pierre Sage believes Crystal Palace "fought better than we played" after grinding out a 1-0 win over Fulham to reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals.
Sage was under pressure after a run of poor Premier League results with Palace, but some of that weight has eased after Eddie Nketiah's goal helped them to the win over Fulham.
Alvaro Arbeloa's side had dominated the first half, with Kenny Tete, Rodrigo Muniz, Antonee Robinson and Joachim Andersen all missing chances in the first 21 minutes.
And Nketiah scored with Palace's first shot in the 37th minute, deftly turning Oscar Mingueza's cross past Benjamin Lecomte to give them the lead against the run of play.
Fulham continued to dominate in the second half, with Dean Henderson keeping Alex Iwobi out at point-blank range before also pushing away Gonzalo Garcia's stoppage-time header.

Palace have won each of their last five away games against Fulham in all competitions, and have reached the quarter-final of the EFL Cup in back-to-back seasons for the first time since 1999-00 and 2000-01.

While Sage was thrilled to pick up a much-needed win – and set up a meeting with Sunderland in the next round – he noted how important it is to make sure this performance transfers to the Premier League.
"We fought better than we played because we didn't have the ball too much, but sometimes we have to do it like this," Sage told Sky Sports.
"But we have to keep that up in the Premier League because we did not pick up three points [against Fulham].
"Our first final is against Tottenham on Saturday. We are really focused on this. We need points in the Premier League, and we need to be concentrated on this."
Palace had just four shots against Fulham worth 0.6 expected goals (xG), while the Cottagers underperformed their 1.5 xG from 14 attempts.
Sage's side also had just 25.6% possession, only attempted 280 passes, and had six touches in the opposition box, while Fulham had 29 and four Opta-defined 'big' chances.

This is the second time this season Fulham have lost to Palace at home, going down 3-2 in the Premier League thanks to a last-minute winner on that occasion, and Arbeloa rued his side's missed chances this time around.
"I'm disappointed. It was a similar game to the one we played some weeks ago [against Palace in the league]," he said.
"We controlled the game, had the chances and, in the end, they took their chance. One shot, one goal, and they were defending all the time.

"It didn't work. We need to do better against a team like this that defends in a low block. We need to move the ball quicker, look for the wide areas, put in more crosses and do better with the final pass.
"It's another day and the same story, so we need to improve. They were not jumping and pressing us. They were defending the space.
"You have to do it for 90 minutes, one time and another time. You need to be patient but aggressive at the same time. We have to do better."

qhsho3pm0as61xs0e18vg4pe7.title: Van Dijk: Utter nonsense I influenced Netherlands World Cup tactics
qhsho3pm0as61xs0e18vg4pe7.subtitle: Virgil van Dijk is not impressed by claims he influenced a tactical change at the World Cup, hitting back during a press conference.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk slammed the suggestion that he had forced Ronald Koeman into changing his Netherlands tactics at the World Cup as "utter nonsense".
The Netherlands were knocked out of the World Cup in the round of 32 on penalties by Morocco – after a 1-1 draw – having gone unbeaten throughout their group stage.
Van Dijk served as Koeman's captain throughout the tournament, with the 63-year-old leaving his position following their early exit.
In a press conference ahead of the Netherlands' Nations League clash with Germany, Van Dijk clashed with reporters after it was insinuated that he was involved in tactical shifts.
Koeman had played a back four throughout the group stage, where they won two of their games and drew the other, before switching to a back five for their clash with Morocco.
"One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. That is utter nonsense," Van Dijk told one reporter.
"The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup. Those are the hard facts.
"We didn't play a good World Cup. It's not about me. You perform together; you're a team. Your claim that I destroyed Dutch football after the World Cup – that sort of thing is completely baseless.
"The plan is devised by the staff. Nonsense is being spread so that I look even worse. That happens far too often.
"I was told that it was my fault we played with five, that Ronald Koeman and I have destroyed Dutch football.
"The plan worked for 89 minutes, even though it was a bad match. We almost broke through. The idea that I destroyed Dutch football makes absolutely no sense. I didn't decide that."
Van Dijk will continue to captain the Netherlands under new head coach Xavi and could win his 100th cap in this extended international break if he plays in all four of their Nations League matches.
The first of which comes at home against Germany on Thursday.

qilthhwpuk491mqo788h4wi1n.title: Argentina 7-0 Burkina Faso: Martinez gets three goal involvements as makeshift visitors thrashed
qilthhwpuk491mqo788h4wi1n.subtitle: Lionel Scaloni put out a strong Argentina lineup against Burkina Faso on Saturday, and he was rewarded with a dominant seven-goal win.
paragraphs: Lautaro Martinez scored one goal and assisted two as Argentina thrashed an understrength Burkina Faso side 7-0 in a friendly marred by travel disruption.

The visitors only arrived in Buenos Aires six hours before kick-off due to their original flight from Morocco being cancelled, and with several first-team players opting not to travel due to fatigue, head coach Amir Abdou fielded a youthful team.
Unsurprisingly, they were no match for the World Cup runners-up, who stormed into a five-goal lead before half-time.

The opening goal came just four minutes in, after Monmouni Diallo scythed down Agustin Giay near the byline on the right-hand side. Martinez's resulting penalty was saved by Razack Guira, but the Inter man was alive to the rebound to finish left-footed.

Argentina's second goal was a comedy of errors from Burkina Faso's point of view, as Julian Alvarez's cross was turned into his own net by Diallo, and Gianluca Prestianni made it 3-0 after just 12 minutes, having exchanged passes with Martinez.

The fourth and fifth goals arrived within 86 seconds of each other later in the first half. Nico Paz brought down Alexis Mac Allister's lofted pass and tucked home, then a cheap giveaway from Hasamadou Ouedraogo was punished in slick fashion by the Albiceleste, with Prestianni centring for an Alvarez tap-in.
Mercifully for Burkina Faso, the goals dried up somewhat in the second half, though Argentina still added two more.

The first of those came from Franco Mastantuono, who finished left-footed after being found by Martinez on the counter, and the Real Madrid winger was also involved in the build-up to the stoppage-time seventh. He found Valentin Barco on the left side of the area, and a lofted delivery from the Chelsea man was headed in by Giuliano Simeone.
Martinez maintains Argentina hot streak
With Lionel Messi set to make a farewell Argentina appearance against Benin on Tuesday, there was a danger of their preceding games being overlooked.

But Lionel Scaloni has certainly taken them seriously, and this victory – which came off the back of a 4-0 thrashing of Bolivia – saw several young players state their case for a central role in Argentina's new era.
Four of the hosts' six goalscorers were aged 23 or younger, though there was still room for two members of their 2022 World Cup-winning squad – Martinez and Alvarez – to contribute.
Martinez now has a hugely impressive 42 goals in 86 senior caps for Argentina, and half of those (21) have come since the start of 2024, having made his international debut way back in 2017.

Argentina's margin of victory was the joint sixth largest in their history and their joint-biggest since 1975, having also won 7-0 against Curacao (in 2023), Bolivia (in 2015) and Hong Kong (in 2014) in that time.

qopf73okp1491ws9iw17uiqju.title: Van Bommel relishing clash against 'special' Zidane and France
qopf73okp1491ws9iw17uiqju.subtitle: Mark van Bommel made a winning start to life in charge of Belgium, but a difficult test against Zinedine Zidane and France awaits.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel is relishing the chance to do battle with Zinedine Zidane and France as he prepares to build on Belgium's strong start to their Nations League campaign.
Belgium began life under Van Bommel with a 2-0 win at the Stadio Olimpico against Italy, with Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio scoring in either half for the Red Devils.
The result saw Italy lose a home match while conceding two goals without scoring for only the second time in the last 40 years, following a defeat to Croatia in August 2006.
It was the perfect start for Van Bommel, who replaced Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, but his early tenure is set to face its sternest test at the Stade Roi Baudouin.
France, also under new management with Zidane, made a winning start to their Nations League campaign with a 1-0 victory over Turkiye, with Kylian Mbappe on target.
Mbappe has since been ruled out of the clash with Belgium after being diagnosed with hyperextension in his left knee, something Van Bommel was disappointed to hear.
"It is special to coach against someone ​like that," Van Bommel said. "He was an exceptional footballer and I played against him once, with ​Barcelona against Real Madrid.
"If a dribbling move is named after you, then you must have done pretty well. ‌As ⁠a coach too, of course. He is a good coach, that's clear.
"I think it's a shame that Mbappe isn't there, because you always want to have the best footballers playing against you.
"I don't know exactly what injury he has, but I would have liked him to be there."
Belgium were deserving of their win against Italy, finishing with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.76 from their 19 shots to the Azzurri's 1.7 from their 21 attempts.
And Van Bommel wants to see his Belgium team maintain the attacking approach they showed against Roberto Mancini's side.
"I started [my ​coaching tenure] last Monday by emphasising intensity and willingness to work," Van Bommel added.
"The idea has to remain the same. Of course, you ⁠have to take the quality of the opponent into account, but that does not change our ​style of play.
"If you are beaten in a situation, that's not a problem. As long as ​everyone knows what they have to do."
Following their clash with France, Belgium face Turkiye at home before concluding the international break against Zidane's side again at the Stade de France on October 5.

qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.title: Kolo Muani not facing spell out after hand surgery
qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.subtitle: Randal Kolo Muani has undergone surgery on a fractured finger on his right hand, but he will not miss any time for Juventus.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Randal Kolo Muani will remain available for selection after undergoing surgery on a fractured finger.
Kolo Muani played 89 minutes on Saturday as the Bianconeri returned to winning ways in Serie A, beating Atalanta 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium.
He played on despite sustaining an injury to his right hand, and though the issue required surgery, reports in Italy said he would return to training with Juve within a couple of days.
A statement released on Juve's website said: "During the first half of Sunday's match against Atalanta, Randal Kolo Muani sustained an injury to the fifth finger of his right hand.
"Tests carried out after the match revealed a fracture of the proximal phalanx, making osteosynthesis surgery necessary.
"The operation, performed this afternoon by Dr Loris Pegoli, was completely successful and the player will remain available for selection."
Kolo Muani has appeared in all six of the Bianconeri's matches in all competitions this season, starting five of those and recording one goal and two assists in 468 minutes.

He was not selected in Zinedine Zidane's first France squad ahead of their Nations League fixtures against Turkiye, Belgium and Italy, so will continue training with his club ahead of Juve facing Cagliari on October 11.

qqqbqf6zgtez1j0u2gpraflg2.title: Alonso keen for Chelsea to manage emotions of rivalry against Spurs
qqqbqf6zgtez1j0u2gpraflg2.subtitle: Chelsea and Tottenham face off in a London derby on Saturday, with the Blues looking to continue their excellent form against their rivals.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso has urged Chelsea to have "good emotional control" when they host Tottenham in the Premier League, to not let the occasion get away from them.
After a shaky run of form before the international break, Chelsea have steadied the ship since returning to action earlier this month, winning both of their games.
Chelsea sit fourth in the Premier League table and are looking to win three consecutive top-flight games for the first time since a run of four in January/February.

Recent form against Spurs suggests that will be possible, as the Blues have won each of their last six league games against the north London side, their joint-longest-ever winning league run against them (also six between January 2000 and March 2002).
Spurs have only won one of their last 36 league visits to Stamford Bridge (D11 L24) but have picked up only two points since that 3-1 win in 2017-18 (D2 L6).
And Alonso is looking forward to his first taste of the rivalry.
"Every derby is special; you feel the energy and excitement from the stands," he said.
"We need to use that energy on the pitch because we need to connect well. We need to have good emotional control as well because there is a lot of passion and commitment from both sides.
"Playing football with heart is what we want.

"I knew about [the six-match winning streak], but it is another game. We need to prove again that we can continue that run, and knowing it is a special game, so we need to play with heart, head and intelligence."
Last time out against Everton, Chelsea kept their first Premier League clean sheet in 23 games, but they have not recorded back-to-back shutouts since December last season.
It will be Mike Penders starting in goal against Spurs, with Emiliano Martinez sidelined through injury after being stretchered off in their last match.
"He is ready," Alonso said when asked about Penders. "He has been training well, played a couple of cup games where he has showed he has a good level.
"In a few minutes against Everton, he showed his personality and qualities. That's why we have a squad for these situations, and we are fully convinced Mike can play very well.

"We wanted to have the best possible options, so we moved for Emi [in the summer transfer window]. Mike is a keeper for now and for the future, learning with an experienced keeper like Emi. We are happy with Mike; he is prepared."

qr8rcroalm411grfttpoih1vm.title: Manchester City 1-1 Paris Saint-Germain: Elimbi Gilbert keeps hosts winless in Champions League
qr8rcroalm411grfttpoih1vm.subtitle: Manchester City looked set to earn their first win in the 2026-27 Women's Champions League, but a late PSG equaliser denied them.
paragraphs: A late equaliser from Tara Elimbi Gilbert kept Manchester City winless after three matchdays in the Women's Champions League, as they drew 1-1 with Paris Saint-Germain.

It looked as though the Women's Super League champions would record their first victory in Europe this term when Khadija Shaw converted an 85th-minute penalty, but they were unable to hold on as Elimbi Gilbert struck after coming off the bench.

The best chance created by either team during a low-key first half saw Shaw fire wide following a lovely outside-of-the-boot pass from Lauren Hemp, with PSG starting tentatively but working their way into the contest by the interval.

City came on strong again in the second half, with Aoba Fujino firing over the crossbar from a tight angle before Oliwia Szperkowska got down brilliantly to thwart the unmarked Shaw from their best chance yet.

The Jamaica forward prodded over in another opening before going down under Griedge Mbock's challenge to win a late spot-kick, which she fired into the bottom-left corner even with Szperkowska diving the right way.

But Mbock was involved in PSG's equaliser three minutes later, playing in Elimbi Gilbert for a composed finish through the legs of Ayaka Yamashita, lifting PSG to five points and leaving City on three.
City's European struggles continue

While City's WSL title defence has started strongly, with Andree Jeglertz's side taking 19 points from seven games to sit level with Chelsea at the top of the table, their domestic form has not translated to Europe.
Dating back to last season, City are winless in four Champions League games (D3 L1), their joint-longest run in the competition, alongside another four-match streak in 2018.

City had 15 shots to PSG's nine, though their expected goals (xG) figure of 2.01 was greatly boosted by Shaw's penalty. PSG only managed 0.78 xG, with 0.34 of that tally coming from Elimbi Gilbert's goal.
PSG are now unbeaten in their opening three games of this season's league phase (W1 D2), marking their best such start in the competition since winning all six group-stage matches in 2021-22.
In Thursday's other games, there were big away wins for Barcelona, who have nine points on the board after three games, and Juventus.
The reigning champions thumped Danish outfit Koge 8-0 with Claudia Pina helping herself to a brace and six other players on target, while Juve triumphed 4-1 at Austria Wien.

qs3d3nk4ujjt136z7tvntuyfl.title: Al-Hilal 3-2 Al-Ittihad: Summerville's stunner settles five-goal thriller
qs3d3nk4ujjt136z7tvntuyfl.subtitle: Al-Hilal moved back to the top of the Saudi Pro League table after edging past Al-Ittihad, whose unbeaten start came to an end.
paragraphs: Crysencio Summerville's stunning strike proved to be the difference as Al-Hilal earned a thrilling 3-2 win over Al-Ittihad in the Saudi Pro League.
Gabriel Martinelli and Ollie Watkins scored on either side of Youssef En-Nesyri's equaliser, but Summerville's curler was enough to secure three points after Steven Bergwijn's late spot-kick.
Watkins, Martinelli and Saimon Bouabre all saw shots saved in the opening six minutes before the Brazilian got the breakthrough 11 minutes in.
Al-Hilal moved it well down the right, and Watkins pulled it back from the byline, with Martinelli adjusting his run quickly to turn it past Predrag Rajkovic first time.

En-Nesyri pulled Al-Ittihad level just 11 minutes later, finishing off a fast break by latching onto Marwan Al Sahafi's throughball without having to break stride to curl a fine effort past Yassine Bounou.
Watkins restored Al-Hilal's lead on the half-hour mark; he put pressure on Danilo while he tried to make a routine clearance and volleyed in the loose ball.

The striker was denied a second goal on the stroke of half-time as he was adjudged to have turned it over the line using his arm, while Faris Abdi was given a reprieve after scoring an own goal as Kalidou Koulibaly was offside when he knocked the ball down.
But Summerville added a third for Al-Hilal in the 64th minute after a lovely jinking run down the left before he cut inside and bent a lovely strike into the bottom-right corner.

Al-Ittihad set up a nervy ending, though, with Ruben Neves' late tackle on Jan-Carlo Simic in the box awarded as a penalty, which Bergwijn emphatically fired in after 89 minutes, but the visitors could not find an equaliser.
Summerville scored the winner, but Watkins ran the show
Summerville's goal turned out to be the winner in a fiery match that finished with Al-Ittihad furiously surrounding the referee, but Watkins will take the plaudits.
He has impressed since his move from Aston Villa over the summer, netting his fifth goal of the campaign and taking his tally of assists up to six after setting up the other two goals on Saturday.
Watkins had a joint-team-high three shots (level with Martinelli) and topped the charts for chances created (four) and touches in the opposition box (11), despite having just 30 touches overall.

Al-Hilal continued their early-season momentum, having now recorded seven wins in the Saudi Pro League, leaving them top of the table, while also dealing Al-Ittihad their first defeat of the campaign.
The visitors certainly had their chances, though, getting five of their eight shots on target, but they just could not muster another late chance to potentially force a draw.

qwz67owk5jjrzkuopdxojeqb.title: Emery sees room for improvement despite Villa's big Champions League win
qwz67owk5jjrzkuopdxojeqb.subtitle: Aston Villa recorded their biggest win in European competition by thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0, but Unai Emery is seeking perfection.
paragraphs: Unai Emery believes "there are still things to improve" after his Aston Villa side thrashed Fenerbahce 6-0 in the Champions League.
Villa have recorded their biggest ever win in major European competition, and their biggest victory under Emery across all competitions.
Johan Manzambi opened the scoring before Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both netted braces and Tammy Abraham sealed the win in the 90th minute.
Villa have won 18 of their last 20 home games in major European competition (D1 L1), and are on the joint-longest active winning streak at home in such competitions (11 – level with Freiburg).

Emery's side are one of two teams to score three first-half goals in both of their opening two games of a Champions League campaign, alongside Paris Saint-Germain this season, but the Spaniard still sees room for improvement.
"Overall it was a very good match. There are still things to improve," Emery told TNT Sports.
"It was a strong result for us. Maybe Fenerbahce didn't deserve [to concede] those six goals.
"[We must] keep going forward. [It helps] confidence for us. We did some changes to get other players confidence and minutes.
"What we did today was fantastic. The Champions League is very difficult."
Manzambi, who turned 21 on Wednesday, became the second player to score on his Champions League debut on his birthday, alongside Spartak Moscow's Romulo v Barcelona in September 2012 (22 years old).
Emery was Spartak Moscow's coach for that game.
Jackson praised the performance of the Switzerland international, as well as his compatriot Ibrahim Mbaye, who assisted Barkley's second goal.
"He [Manzambi] is a top player. I'm really happy we're playing together. I hope we score many more goals together," Jackson told TNT Sports.
"He [Mbaye] is an amazing player. We're in the [Senegal] national team together. Hopefully he'll get more time to play. He's very fast. It's good to have him."
Jackson is the first player to score in as many as four of his first five Champions League starts since Sebastien Haller in December 2021 (all five).
He could have taken home the match ball, but Barkley took the penalty instead of the former Chelsea striker.
"Yeah, I wanted to take it but the most important thing is we win. Hopefully next time I'll get the hat-trick," Jackson added.
