qxfq9pg149jr1632xee1ruunj.title: Serbia 1-2 Netherlands: Meerdink double earns Xavi first victory
qxfq9pg149jr1632xee1ruunj.subtitle: Xavi got himself up and running with the Netherlands as goals in either half from Mexx Meerdink were enough to get past Serbia on Sunday.
paragraphs: Mexx Meerdink scored twice as the Netherlands earned their first victory under new boss Xavi after they beat Serbia 2-1 at Stadion Rajko Mitic in the Nations League.
The Netherlands needed a stoppage-time equaliser from Cody Gakpo on Xavi's debut against Germany, but they overcame a stern test on Sunday to seal all three points.

Dejan Joveljic brought the first save out of Bart Verbruggen in the 17th minute before Meerdink stung the palms of Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, with his shot coming after Gakpo was forced off due to an injury.

But the Netherlands made the breakthrough in the 30th minute when Crysencio Summerville was fouled inside the penalty area by Aleksa Terzic, with Meerdink stepping up and wrapping his effort into the bottom-right corner.
Denzel Dumfries should have doubled the visitors' lead after he was brilliantly slipped in by Meerdink, but Milinkovic-Savic was on hand to repel his attempt from a tight angle.

However, Serbia needed just 54 seconds after the break to draw level. Verbruggen made two excellent stops to deny Luka Jovic and Andrija Zivkovic, but Sasa Lukic's scuffed shot made its way back to Jovic, who finished first time from close range.

Ruben van Bommel, who replaced Gakpo in the first half, saw his bouncing effort hit the post before Ryan Gravenberch's long-range shot was comfortably held by Milinkovic-Savic as the Netherlands laid siege to Serbia's goal.
And their persistence was rewarded in the 69th minute through the lively Meerdink, who, on the slide, found the bottom-right corner after being teed up by substitute Guus Til.

Serbia almost pegged back the Netherlands soon after, but Jovic's header from a Dusan Tadic corner just evaded the far post, with Xavi's side holding on to go top of Group A2 ahead of Germany's clash with Greece later in the day.
Meerdink making the most of his chance

After being initially left out of Xavi's first Netherlands squad, Meerdink, along with Til, were called up as late replacements for the injured Justin Kluivert and Donyell Malen, and the AZ striker has impressed in his first two Nations League games this season.

Only Finland's Joel Pohjanpalo (three) has scored more goals in the 2026-27 Nations League than Meerdink (two, level with three other players), while he also finished with a team-high total for shots on target (three), while only Van Bommel (seven) had more touches in the opposition box than his six.

Following their 1-1 draw with Germany, Xavi said his team delivered a "superior" second-half display, though it was more of a complete performance from his team here, despite allowing Jovic to score an equaliser so soon into the second half.
The Netherlands finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.75 from their 25 shots, eight of which were on target, compared to Serbia's total of 1.41 from their 11 attempts.
Xavi's side are on their travels again, with a clash against Greece to come this Thursday before they end the international break with a home game against Serbia on October 4.

qxwdv55f3zd1iowhzzs6djy1.title: Mihailovic says Toronto must harness home support in MLS play-off chase
qxwdv55f3zd1iowhzzs6djy1.subtitle: Toronto FC beat their Canadian rivals CF Montreal last time out, but can they keep their momentum going against Orlando City?
paragraphs: Djordje Mihailovic says Toronto FC must make the most of their vocal home support, as they look to build further momentum after Saturday's Canadian Classique win over CF Montreal.
Playing against his former club, Mihailovic capped an incredible stoppage time comeback from Robin Fraser's team, who were 1-0 down entering the 93rd minute at BMO Field.
Lewis Morgan scored their equaliser before Mihailovic popped up at the far post with a 95th-minute winner, sparking wild scenes among the home fans.
That victory lifted Toronto to 11th in the Eastern Conference, although they are still four points adrift of the play-off picture with just six regular-season games to play.
The first of those is at home to Orlando City on Wednesday, and Mihailovic knows they cannot afford to slip up on their own turf.
"We know how much the fans give us when we play here. You can see, all season long, that we're never quitting until the final whistle," Mihailovic said.
"They give us so much energy and we need them in the final stretch.
"We're slowly trying to creep up into that last playoff spot. There are two more games at home, and we need them."
Orlando are seventh in the East, five points clear of Toronto, after beating the Columbus Crew 3-2 last time out.

Ivan Angulo scored the all-important goal in the 89th minute, and goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau knew it was vital for Martin Perelman's side to end their three-game losing run coming out of the international break.
"We know how crucial the points are from now until the end of the year," the Canada international said.

"It's going to be super important to continue putting in strong performances. Coming back from the break, it was important to get out strong and find a response toward the end of the game, so we're very happy with it."
Toronto FC – Josh Sargent
Sargent's seven goals in MLS this term are the joint-most of any Toronto player, alongside Daniel Salloi.

That is despite the United States international only playing 1,618 minutes, compared to Salloi's 2,353. Sargent also leads all of his team-mates for expected goals, performing about in line with his 7.14 xG.
Orlando City – Antoine Griezmann
Griezmann is seen as one of the favourites for the 2026 MLS Newcomer of the Year award, having provided another goal and assist against Columbus last time out.
The former World Cup winner has nine goals in MLS, and Orlando are unbeaten across the eight games in which he has scored in all competitions (W7 D1).
MATCH PREDICTION – DRAW
Toronto have only lost two of their 15 MLS games at home this year, tallying five wins and eight draws on their own turf.
The Reds have lost three of their last six league games, however (W2 D1), whereas Orlando have four victories in their last six (L2).
Orlando won the most recent MLS meeting between the teams, 3-0 on home soil in September with Griezmann joining Angulo and Harvey Sarajian on the scoresheet.
Orlando have only won three of their 14 away games in MLS this year (D2 L9), so it would be little surprise to see the spoils shared.

r0fh5g2o5qvm1mtkqlukr4syh.title: Lyon 3-2 Crystal Palace: Sage condemned to defeat on homecoming
r0fh5g2o5qvm1mtkqlukr4syh.subtitle: Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage was hoping for a happy return to Lyon, but his former side took all three points in the Europa League.
paragraphs: Lyon's perfect start to their Europa League campaign continued on Thursday as they beat Crystal Palace 3-2 and spoilt Pierre Sage's return to the Groupama Stadium.
Former Lyon boss Sage saw his Palace side fall 2-0 down before the break after goals from Corentin Tolisso and Ernest Nuamah put the Ligue 1 giants in control.
Yeremy Pino and Daichi Kamada responded for the Eagles in an entertaining second half, but substitute Pavel Sulc's 76th-minute strike proved to be the winning goal.
The hosts were ahead after just eight minutes as Palace failed to clear Nuamah's in-swinging corner, allowing Tolisso to fire in at Walter Benitez's near post for the opener.

Ismaila Sarr saw a header drift wide after the half-hour mark, and the Eagles were dealt a blow in first-half stoppage time when Keito Nakamura sprinted into the box before squaring to Nuamah for a simple finish.

However, Palace halved the deficit just five minutes into the second half when Adam Wharton played Pino into the Lyon penalty area with a brilliant first-time pass, and the Spaniard beat Dominik Greif with an emphatic finish.
Jorgen Strand Larsen missed a huge chance to equalise moments later, heading over from Wharton's corner, while Sarr's driven cross into the six-yard box was expertly pushed away by Greif.

Lyon then regained control and restored their two-goal cushion in the 76th minute as Nakamura's mishit effort was flicked in by Sulc, though Kamada teed up a nervy ending after reacting quickest to a loose ball in the box five minutes later.

Chris Richards went mightily close to an equaliser in the final minute of normal time as he connected well with Wharton's corner, but Greif managed to get enough behind his save to keep out the defender's header.
Lyon's wide men trouble Palace
The contest was fought evenly, with Lyon edging the expected goals (xG) battle 1.71 to 1.58 after both sides recorded four shots on target and created four Opta-defined big chances each.

The difference-makers, however, were Lyon's wingers. Nuamah played a crucial role in Lyon's first goal before scoring a timely second before the break, while Nakamura recorded two assists, even if the second was unintentional.
Nuamah and Nakamura both recorded the joint-most touches in the box among Lyon players (five), while the latter created a team-high four chances and completed 100% of his dribbles (2/2).

While Lyon have ended a four-game winless run against English teams in the Europa League, there will be plenty of positives to take for Sage's Palace side, who went toe-to-toe against the fourth-place team in Ligue 1.
Wharton impressed as ever, creating four chances as Palace looked to mount a comeback, but Strand Larsen's failure to hit the target with any of his four shots (team-high) proved costly.

Former Lyon boss Sage saw his Palace side fall 2-0 down before the break after goals from Corentin Tolisso and Ernest Nuamah put the Ligue 1 giants in control. 

Yeremy Pino and Daichi Kamada responded for the Eagles in an entertaining second half, but substitute Pavel Sulc's 76th-minute strike proved to be the winning goal.

The hosts were ahead after just eight minutes as Palace failed to clear Nuamah's in-swinging corner, allowing Tolisso to fire in at Walter Benitez's near post for the opener. 

Ismaila Sarr saw a header drift wide after the half-hour mark, and the Eagles were dealt a blow in first-half stoppage time when Keito Nakamura sprinted into the box before squaring to Nuamah for a simple finish.

However, Palace halved the deficit just five minutes into the second half when Adam Wharton played Pino into the Lyon penalty area with a brilliant first-time pass, and the Spaniard beat Dominik Greif with an emphatic finish. 

Jorgen Strand Larsen missed a huge chance to equalise moments later, heading over from Wharton's corner, while Sarr's driven cross into the six-yard box was expertly pushed away by Greif.

Lyon then regained control and restored their two-goal cushion in the 76th minute as Nakamura's mishit effort was flicked in by Sulc, though Kamada teed up a nervy ending after reacting quickest to a loose ball in the box five minutes later. 

Chris Richards went mightily close to an equaliser in the final minute of normal time as he connected well with Wharton's corner, but Greif managed to get enough behind his save to keep out the defender's header.

Lyon's wide men trouble Palace

The contest was fought evenly, with Lyon edging the expected goals (xG) battle 1.71 to 1.58 after both sides recorded four shots on target and created four Opta-defined big chances each.

The difference-makers, however, were Lyon's wingers. Nuamah played a crucial role in Lyon's first goal before scoring a timely second before the break, while Nakamura recorded two assists, even if the second was unintentional.

Nuamah and Nakamura both recorded the joint-most touches in the box among Lyon players (five), while the latter created a team-high four chances and completed 100% of his dribbles (2/2).

While Lyon have ended a four-game winless run against English teams in the Europa League, there will be plenty of positives to take for Sage's Palace side, who went toe-to-toe against the fourth-place team in Ligue 1.

Wharton impressed as ever, creating four chances as Palace looked to mount a comeback, but Strand Larsen's failure to hit the target with any of his four shots (team-high) proved costly.

r3wyrp46e4jk1slc1q2zcot5r.title: Burnley sack Hayen after dismal Championship start
r3wyrp46e4jk1slc1q2zcot5r.subtitle: Nicky Hayen's Burnley reign did not last long, with the Belgian being dismissed following a chastening 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City.
paragraphs: Burnley have sacked head coach Nicky Hayen after just 12 Championship games, with the Clarets marooned inside the relegation zone.
Hayen took charge at Turf Moor following last season's relegation from the Premier League, after Scott Parker was dismissed in April.

The former Club Brugge and Genk boss was tasked with leading Burnley back to the top flight at the first attempt, but after only winning one game all campaign, they could face a fight to avoid a second straight drop.
Having lost 4-1 to Lincoln City on Saturday, Burnley have the joint-worst defensive record in the Championship alongside Preston North End, conceding 25 goals in just 12 games.

Only Derby County (69), Bolton Wanderers (67) and Cardiff City (65) have faced more shots on target than Burnley's 64, while their expected goals against (xGA) figure of 20.01 is the fifth worst in the division.
Hayen's exit was confirmed just a couple of hours after the Lincoln defeat, with a short club statement reading: "Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect.
"The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season."
Burnley's next game is at home to Portsmouth on October 31, when a failure to pick up three points would see the Clarets make unwanted history.
They have not won a home league game since beating Leeds United in the top flight on October 18, 2025.
The record winless run at home in England's top four divisions, in terms of days, is Sheffield Wednesday's 376-day streak between April 2025 and May 2026, which Burnley could surpass next week.

r6h4gnskrr3l1orxnnc4ifskk.title: Roma 2-0 Genoa: Incredible Castro goal helps Gasperini's men overcome Malen absence
r6h4gnskrr3l1orxnnc4ifskk.subtitle: Despite Donyell Malen's ban, Roma moved back to within two points of Inter by beating Genoa 2-0, helped by an incredible opening goal.
paragraphs: Santiago Castro and Emanuele Lulli both scored their first goals for Roma, the former with a sensational lob, as they beat Genoa 2-0 to move back within two points of the Serie A summit.

Having seen Inter defeat Bologna 3-1 to pull clear at the top of the table earlier on Saturday, Roma saw off a stern challenge from Genoa – managed by Giallorossi icon Daniele De Rossi – to keep pace with the Nerazzurri.
Chances were at a premium for much of the first half, though the crossbar was rattled at both ends within the space of three minutes.

For Roma, defender Leonardo Balerdi met Niccolo Pisilli's corner with a header that bounced clear off the woodwork, then Genoa's Stephan El Shaarawy – who played 348 games for the Giallorossi across two spells at the club – left the frame of the goal shaking with a thunderous 20-yard volley.
But Roma only needed five minutes at the start of the second half to make the breakthrough, and Castro's first goal for the club was certainly one to remember.

Matias Soule's inswinging corner from the right side was glanced on by Castro but ricocheted back into his path, with white shirts surrounding him. In a tight space, he spun away from two markers before scooping an incredible effort into the far corner with the outside of his right boot.
While Roma's first goal was all about the finish, it was the build-up that made their 68th-minute second special.

Soule had two defenders for company when he received the ball up against the touchline inside his own half, but some lovely footwork allowed him to escape down the right flank, and after dribbling inside and exchanging passes with Lorenzo Pellegrini, he crossed to give teenager Lulli a tap-in.

Pierluigi Gollini had to stay alert to parry a stinging drive from Milutin Osmajic, but that was as much danger as Gian Piero Gasperini's side faced as they cruised to their fifth win in seven Serie A matches this term.
Castro and Soule strut their stuff

With Donyell Malen – who has scored a remarkable 23 goals in 28 games for the club since his January arrival – suspended following his red card against Como, Roma needed to find alternative sources of goals on Saturday.
And Castro, a €35m acquisition from Bologna, stepped up in a big way, having failed to score from seven shots in his first four outings for Roma, all of which came from the bench.
When the ball fell to the Argentine near the right corner of the six-yard box, there were nine white shirts – plus goalkeeper Justin Bijlow – between him and the Genoa net.

It would not have occurred to 99% of players to try a dinked finish into the far top corner, with seemingly no space for the ball to fit into, but Castro produced a magical moment to break the deadlock.

Like Castro, Lulli had never previously found the net for Roma, but his finish was a far simpler one that owed much to Soule's daring run. No player on the pitch created more chances than Soule's three, while he also led the charts for passes into the final third (30) plus dribbles attempted (five) and completed (three).
Roma now have 17 points on the board after seven games (W5 D2), marking the first time they have hit that tally by this stage of a Serie A season since 2014-15 (18 in that case).

r7tuvsm5z29e1mmru95hzyb6p.title: MLS commissioner: Kane interest 'the fulfilment of a dream' after Beckham, Messi moves
r7tuvsm5z29e1mmru95hzyb6p.subtitle: Harry Kane recently said he would like to play in MLS one day, and the league's commissioner, Don Garber, would welcome him with open arms.
paragraphs: Harry Kane's interest in moving to MLS is the "fulfilment of a dream" for the league's commissioner Don Garber, who says David Beckham and Lionel Messi should be thanked for keeping the competition relevant.

Kane, who scored six goals in four appearances for England during the international break and matched Peter Shilton's team record of 125 caps, is close to reaching an agreement to extend his contract with Bayern Munich.

Reports suggest the Three Lions' captain will commit his future to the German giants until 2029, having scored 73 goals for club and country in 2025-26 to mark himself out as one of the favourites to win the Ballon d'Or.

But beyond that, the striker recently suggested he would be open to playing in MLS in the twilight of his career, with his ambition to become a kicker in the NFL being another attraction of a move stateside.
And for Garber, who has been in charge of MLS since 1999, that statement alone shows just how far the league has come.
"I would love for him to do that," Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation.
"That sounds colloquial, but we actually have that written down.
"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world saying, 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.'

"I think Messi proved that. That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barcelona, a dynamic that would not have him wanting to play in Saudi Arabia.
"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye from his international career."

Messi's move to Inter Miami in 2023 has been an immeasurable success for MLS, with the forward winning his eighth Ballon d'Or and leading Argentina to a second straight World Cup final while playing his club football in the United States.
But it was David Beckham's decision to join the LA Galaxy in 2007 that initially put the league on the map.
"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said, when asked to compare Beckham and Messi's respective impacts on MLS.
"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.
"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.
"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David, there's probably no Major League Soccer.
"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

r8f5i4efubdb12fo2wigegrus.title: Gasperini pokes at Mourinho's spending as Roma prepare for Madrid
r8f5i4efubdb12fo2wigegrus.subtitle: Jose Mourinho will return to former club Roma when Real Madrid make the trip to Italy for Wednesday's Champions League clash.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini joked he is in awe of Jose Mourinho's ability to convince his clubs to "spend large sums of money" before the pair meet in the Champions League.
Mourinho returns to former club Roma on Wednesday as Real Madrid prepare for their second game of this season's top European competition.
Gasperini insisted Mourinho will "deserve all the recognition he'll receive" from Roma supporters, but still aimed a slight jibe at Madrid's spending habits.
"Results speak for Jose. He’s one of the most successful coaches," Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia.
"If I had to take one thing, it would be his ability to persuade clubs to buy extraordinary players and spend large sums of money; that is extraordinary."
"He's very good for the rest too, and his results. But that remains a great ability."
Mourinho's record in this competition also speaks for itself. Madrid have only lost one of their 19 group/league phase matches in the Champions League under him (W15 D3).

Meanwhile, Roma have lost each of their last four games in the competition against Madrid without scoring a goal – their joint-longest losing streak against an opponent in the European Cup/Champions League.
"It's a bit difficult to have Real Madrid as a benchmark. In what they represent globally, they are the club with the most titles and the most fans worldwide," Gasperini added.

"So, this isn't the comparison we should focus on; it's what happens on the pitch. We recently played Inter and Como, two of Italy's best teams, and now we face one of the best in Europe and the world.
"Our target is to measure ourselves against them to understand how competitive we can be."
Mourinho guided Roma to Europa Conference League success in the 2021-22 season, winning the club's first trophy since 2008 and marking their maiden triumph in Europe.
But the Portuguese boss is not interested in sentiment as Madrid look to build on their 2-1 victory over Inter in their Champions League opener this campaign.

"It will be just another game. If I can forget who I'm playing against, and I'm doing that and will do it during the game, then it's just another game," Mourinho said in Tuesday's pre-match press conference.
"As I said before, we're not yet feeling the real pressure of the Champions League. Looking at what's still to come, I think Real Madrid and Roma will both qualify.
"Maybe before or after the game I'll put my hand on my heart, but during the game there will be no doubt. Roma want to win, and so do I. At that moment, love is forgotten."

rc5wgx1akovy1nyomau4artl1.title: Arteta praises Arsenal's patience after narrow win against Forest
rc5wgx1akovy1nyomau4artl1.subtitle: Arsenal condemned Nottingham Forest to a third-straight defeat with a 1-0 win at the City Ground on Sunday, much to Mikel Arteta's delight.
paragraphs: Despite a largely flat performance, Mikel Arteta hailed his Arsenal side's patience and will after their narrow 1-0 victory at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
Noni Madueke scored the winner in the 80th minute at the City Ground, with his far-corner strike deflecting in off Jair Cunha after Gabriel Magalhaes and Declan Rice both sent efforts over the bar.
Forest defended admirably and posed a strong challenge to the reigning Premier League champions in the closing stages, with Chris Wood and Murillo spurning promising chances.
The result marked a third straight defeat for Oliver Glasner's side, while it boosted the Gunners back up to second in the table.
"We knew the margins would be really small," Arteta told Sky Sports. "They are extremely well coached and organised.
"The longer the game goes on, they gain more belief. We had to be so patient. And clinical when we got the chance.
"The way they were defending, they were more comfortable. But we have players with different qualities and can adapt to what the game is delivering.
"We have another three big chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating chances, they will come.
"Today, let's enjoy the win, because it was a very tough one."

Arsenal have made narrow victories something of a habit under Arteta, with the Gunners recording the joint-highest number of 1-0 wins in the Premier League of any side since the Spaniard took charge (32, level with Everton).

Arteta's side have also followed up their title-winning campaign strongly, having now won as many as six of their opening seven games of a Premier League season for the fourth time – after also winning six in 2004-05, 2007-08, and 2022-23.
Forest, meanwhile, will have to wait for their first home win of the season.
Along with Schalke, the Tricky Trees are also one of just two sides without a home league goal in Europe's top five leagues this season.

They are also just the fifth side in English top-flight history to fail to score in their first four home matches of a campaign, after West Brom in 1921-22, Everton in 1998-99, Crystal Palace in 2018-19, and Huddersfield Town in 2018-19.
Despite the defeat, Glasner opted to look at the positives, praising his side's performance and urging patience.
"Very tough to take, bit of deja vu," the Forest boss told BBC Match of the Day.

"Many things here we feel the result is unfair but it’s what stands and it's zero points at home. Very good performance against the champions. We caused many problems, didn't give them a lot and at the end we have zero points.
"Feels a bit weird to have a third defeat in a row but I see progress in every game and today the effort was amazing – it was just the result we can't be pleased with.
"Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.
"And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good."

rdtewxxxoxyl1t0f3d1jxunw8.title: Bronze excited for Chelsea to 'prove ourselves' against Lyon
rdtewxxxoxyl1t0f3d1jxunw8.subtitle: Chelsea head to Lyon looking to make it two wins from two in the Women's Champions League, but Lucy Bronze is expecting a tough test.
paragraphs: Lucy Bronze is relishing the chance for Chelsea to "prove ourselves" against Lyon in the Women's Champions League.
Chelsea began their European campaign with a narrow 1-0 victory over Austria Wien last time out and are one of six teams with three points on the board so far.
Lyon were another that won their opener, but they sit top of the early standings after thrashing Servette 8-0 last time out.

In the Champions League, Lyon have won two of their four games against Chelsea (D1 L1); among sides they have faced more than twice, only against Juventus (43%) and Umea IK (25%) do they possess a lower win rate in the competition than against the Blues (50%).
And Bronze, a former Lyon player, is looking forward to the clash against her former side, seeing it as a good marker for where Chelsea are up to in the season.
"It's so exciting," Bronze said, as quoted on Chelsea's website. "My time at Lyon was amazing.
"All the girls, Ellie [Carpenter], Keish [Kadeisha Buchanan] and Melvine [Malard] had a great time at Lyon, and we all actually played there together as well.
"We're excited to go there, to be focused on the Champions League, and we know what pedigree Lyon have in the Champions League.
"To go toe to toe with another team who's one of the best in the world and test ourselves and prove ourselves is going to be exciting."
Chelsea have lost three of their last six away games in the Champions League (W2 D1), though all three defeats came in the knockout stages.
The Blues have lost just one of their 15 group/league-stage away matches in the competition (W11 D3).
Lyon are heavy favourites according to the Opta supercomputer, with a 65.2% win probability to Chelsea's 15.9%, but Bronze is not shying away from the test ahead of them.

rhejui4ma6m613sn0vtwie157.title: Hearts thrashing not 'seismic' for Celtic's season, Maloney insists
rhejui4ma6m613sn0vtwie157.subtitle: Celtic thumped Hearts 7-1 ahead of Thursday's Europa League clash with Celta Vigo, a result Shaun Maloney said was not on his mind.
paragraphs: Shaun Maloney pushed back the suggestion that Celtic's 7-1 victory over Scottish Premiership rivals Hearts was a "seismic" moment in their season.
Celtic moved four points clear at the top of the league table with a stunning performance at Parkhead, with Callum Osmand, Benjamin Nygren and Camilo Duran all impressing.
But Martin O'Neill's side now turn their attention to Europe as they welcome Celta Vigo to Glasgow on Thursday, hoping to get their Europa League campaign up and running.
The Scottish champions are yet to win in Europe this season, losing to Ferencvaros before being thumped by Benfica 4-1 on MD2.

Celtic have lost their last three European matches, conceding 3+ goals in all three games (12 in total). They have only lost four in a row within a single season once before, doing so in the 2017-18 Champions League.
The two teams previously met in the 2002-03 UEFA Cup, with Celtic progressing on away goals after a 2-2 aggregate draw (1-0 home, 1-2 away defeat).
Maloney, taking over media duties while O'Neill took care of a personal matter, was asked if Sunday's win was a turning point, but he replied: "No, it didn't feel that seismic, Hearts.
"I know it was a really good performance. Some of the attacking stuff was really good, but it doesn't feel like sort of big moment."
Celta have lost both of their away European matches in Scotland, losing 1-0 both times at Aberdeen in 1971 and Celtic in 2002.
Claudio Giraldez's side have also started their Europa League campaign with back-to-back defeats, the latest of which saw them squander a lead and lose 2-1 to Juventus.

The LaLiga side have lost their last two away Europa League matches, though they have not lost three in a row in major European competition since losing four between March 2001 and October 2002 in the UEFA Cup.
"It's going to be a very different game. I think it sounds really simple, but some of the basics that we did – we had to outrun Hearts in certain areas, and we did," Maloney added.

"The 50-50s came out on our side in that game. There are some fundamental things about a game of football that we got right in that game, we got right in the second half of Benfica, and those sorts of things are probably the challenges we've had since the start of the season.
"With the ball, we can be really creative. We just need to have the same level without the ball consistently, and against Hearts we did. We'll definitely need that [against Celta].
"I think if we can get a really committed team with and without the ball, then we can definitely win this game.
"Celta are a good side, and they can definitely hurt you. So we need both sides, and I just want to see us continue on from the last seven to 10 days on that."

ri1h1rkhmw761xfz05jlw3g17.title: Kane: This is my best chance of winning the Ballon d'Or
ri1h1rkhmw761xfz05jlw3g17.subtitle: Harry Kane is among the favourites to win the Ballon d'Or this year, and the Bayern Munich striker said he could not have done any more.
paragraphs: Harry Kane believes this is the best chance of his career to win the Ballon d'Or after a sensational season with Bayern Munich and England.
Kane is among the top contenders to lift the prestigious individual accolade next month, with Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe also in contention.
The England captain plundered 65 across all competitions for Bayern before scoring six more to help Thomas Tuchel's side finish third at this summer's World Cup.
No other player from Europe's top five leagues scored more than 50 goals in all competitions last term, with Mbappe his closest challenger with a half-century for Madrid.

Kane is hoping to become the fifth English player to win the Ballon d'Or and the first since Michael Owen in 2001. Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) had previously claimed the award.
And ahead of England's clash with Spain in their Nations League opener, Kane insisted he could have done nothing more in his attempt to try and lift the Ballon d'Or.
"Best chance right now, yeah, whether that's in the future as well. We'll have to wait and see, but I think yes, so far in my career, it is the best chance without a doubt," Kane said.
"I think I spoke quite openly last season from a personal point of view.
"It was my best year without a doubt, but also, from a team point of you was my best in terms of trophies and performances. It's something that would be amazing to win.
"I know there's been a lot of talk about it, and I'm sure it will be over the next month until it's announced and that's part and parcel of it.
"I'd be extremely proud to win it. I think I've done a lot of great things that I'm proud of last year for sure.
"But like I keep saying, ultimately, it's down to other people now and their opinion on it. The players and their opinion on last season, so we'll have to wait and see what happens.
"I know it won't be the last time I talk about it, but yeah, there's still another month or so to go. My focus is on trying to help this team get a good win against Spain."

Kane will be hoping to improve his Ballon d'Or chances against a Spain side that are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation following their World Cup success.

The Three Lions have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2). Those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

Jude Bellingham will also be keen to make an impact. The Real Madrid star has scored seven goals in 10 appearances for England in 2026. The last midfielder with more goals in a calendar year for the Three Lions was David Platt in 1993 (eight).

And his performances were recognised as he scooped the England Men's Player of the Year award for the second year running. Only Wayne Rooney (four) has won the award more times than Bellingham (two, level with Kane, Bukayo Saka, Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard).

riwf612il9031764r8onxt90y.title: Flick sees no need for Barca to rest Yamal ahead of PSG, Madrid tests
riwf612il9031764r8onxt90y.subtitle: Lamine Yamal provided two assists, including one for Anthony Gordon that followed a sensational piece of skill, against Galatasaray.
paragraphs: Hansi Flick is content that Lamine Yamal does not need to have his minutes managed ahead of a testing period for Barcelona, who will face Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in the next 11 days.
The Blaugrana made it two wins from their opening two games in the Champions League on Tuesday, as they came from behind to beat Galatasaray 4-1 in Istanbul.
Joao Cancelo, Fermin Lopez, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi got Barca's goals, but Ballon d'Or contender Yamal was the real star of the show.
He laid on two assists, with the second coming from a sensational fake rabona on the right side of the area, and was also involved in the build-up to Adeyemi's clinching goal.
In the process, Yamal became the first teenager (19 years, 92 days old) to record 25 goal involvements in the Champions League (12 goals, 13 assists in 35 appearances).
Despite Barca establishing their three-goal lead by the 65th minute, Flick opted to leave Yamal on for the full game, as he was confident the winger did not need a rest.
"Lamine didn't score today, but he provided the final pass for two of the goals and he was excellent," Flick told Movistar after the game.
"He's an incredible player and very important for us."
Asked if he considered taking Yamal off in the second half, Flick said: "No, I didn't consider it. We're managing the workload of other players, too.
"Lamine is very good physically, he's ready for everything and, as we saw in the second half, it's very important to have a player like him on the field."

Having made a perfect start in LaLiga with eight wins from eight matches, Barca visit Real Betis on Saturday, then go to the Parc des Princes to face two-time defending European champions PSG next Tuesday.

They will then welcome Real Madrid to Camp Nou for the first edition of El Clasico in 2026-27, on October 25. Further tests against Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid also await them before the November international break.
Barca's big win took them top of the early Champions League table, having scored nine goals in their opening two games, but Flick still feels there is room for improvement.
"I think in the Champions League, even when we're playing well, there are situations where we don't make the right decisions in the final third," Flick said.
"That's something we have to improve. In this stadium, with this atmosphere, it wasn't easy, but I'm very happy."

rjx4wkmhfs981hz5g8z4tkgyk.title: Turkiye 1-4 Italy: First-half blitz gets Mancini's second stint up and running
rjx4wkmhfs981hz5g8z4tkgyk.subtitle: Italy claimed their first win in the Nations League as three goals inside the first 27 minutes proved to be enough to battle past Turkiye.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini claimed his first victory since returning to take charge of Italy as three-first half goals helped down Turkiye 4-1 in the Nations League on Monday.
Alessandro Bastoni, Davide Frattesi and Michael Kayode had Italy cruising by the 27th minute, though Baris Alper Yilmaz threatened a comeback early in the second half.
However, Francesco Pio Esposito's 50th-minute header proved to be decisive for Italy, who moved onto three points in Group A1 after their first two matches.

Bastoni handed Italy the ideal start in the ninth minute. A flat corner from the left was not dealt with by Zeki Celik, with the Inter defender winning his battle against Salih Ozcan and turning the ball into the roof of the net on the slide.

It got even better for the Azzurri soon after. A free-flowing move on the edge of the Turkiye area ended with Kayode's shot being saved by Altay Bayindir, but Frattesi was the quickest on the scene to tuck home the rebound in the 22nd minute.

And just five minutes later, Italy had their third. Another great piece of play between Giacomo Raspadori and Francesco Pio Esposito saw the latter shift the ball on to Kayode, who made no mistake from inside the box to mark his international debut with a goal.
Raspadori and Sebastiano Esposito then fired off target to cap a dominant opening 45 minutes for Mancini's side as the Turkiye players exited the pitch to a chorus of jeers.

However, Turkiye gave their fans something to cheer within 76 seconds of the restart when Yilmaz turned Oguz Aydin's teasing delivery past Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was out of position after coming out to try and claim a long ball over the top.

But no sooner had they got themselves back in the game, Bayindir gifted Italy their fourth goal. His loose pass was picked off and resulted in Sandro Tonali striking an effort against the right post, with Francesco Pio Esposito on hand to nod in the rebound.

The blistering start to the second half continued when Yilmaz's shot hit the woodwork on its way in, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against Arda Guler, with Aydin then failing to trouble Donnarumma from a tight angle.
Kerem Akturkoglu then blazed over a glorious chance before Eren Elmali failed to get a touch on Ismail Yuksek's cross, with Italy able to hold on to claim a deserved triumph.
Azzurri find their groove to rubbish Montella's pre-match prediction

Before kick-off, Turkiye boss Vincenzo Montella vowed that his team would emerge victorious against Italy, but his pre-match hopes of a morale-boosting win were all but over before half an hour had elapsed in Bursaspor.

Italy scored three goals inside the first 30 minutes of play for the first time since a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania in September 2021, with Moise Kean, an Edgaras Utkus own goal and Raspadori on target in that game.

This was also the first time the Azzurri had scored four goals in the Nations League since a 4-1 win against Israel in October 2024, and their dominance was backed up by the metrics in what was an entertaining encounter.

Mancini's side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.39 from their 14 shots compared to Turkiye's 1.86 xG from one more attempt, though the hosts did win the xG battle in the second half (1.77 to 0.76).

There was also a special moment for Francesco Pio and Sebastiano Esposito, who became the fourth pair of brothers to contest the same match with Italy, after Filippo and Simone Inzaghi (twice in 2000), Aldo and Luigi Cevenini (once in 1915), and Giuseppe and Felice Milano (three times between 1912 and 1913).

rp2c9mrz8yca1j2dier76rljt.title: 'Not ideal' for Arsenal to drop points after late mix-up, says Russo
rp2c9mrz8yca1j2dier76rljt.subtitle: Leah Williamson was penalised for a handball in the box after a defensive mix-up as Arsenal gifted Paris FC a late equaliser from the spot.
paragraphs: Alessia Russo conceded it was "not ideal" for Arsenal to drop points in a 2-2 draw with Paris FC in the Women's Champions League, but hopes the goals keep flowing.
Arsenal had led 2-0 against Paris, but a freakish late mix-up ultimately gifted the hosts a late equaliser after they had pulled themselves back into the game.
Russo netted her first goal of the season just before the break, playing a neat one-two with Georgia Stanway before picking out the bottom corner.

Shortly after, Evelyne Viens hit the bar for Paris, who had created the better chances in the early exchanges, but Arsenal doubled their advantage five minutes into the second half with Stanway's first goal for the Gunners.
Paris continued to prove a threat on the counter-attack, though, and halved the deficit in the 71st minute, with Clara Mateo rounding Misa to slot in.

But with five minutes left, Leah Williamson secured the ball with her hand to take a goal-kick, but the referee deemed that Misa had already taken it when passing it to her, thus awarding a penalty for handball, which Maeline Mendy converted in the 87th minute.
"I mean, not ideal," Russo told Arsenal's media channels about the dropped points.
"I think we lost control of the second half a little way before [the penalty] anyway.
"So, it's about managing the game a little bit better. I also think the first half, and throughout the game, we had some really, really good spells, so now it's about using that to push forward."
Arsenal have now failed to win from 2+ goals up in the Champions League twice since the start of last season, having never thrown away that kind of lead between 2001-02 and 2024-25.
But despite the disappointing finish, one positive for the Gunners was Russo's first goal of the season after she drew a blank in her first five outings this season.
"I always want to try and score and create, and yeah, it was about finding the half the yard to get a shot off, so I'm happy to do that," she said.
"I think maybe [it's] an area we've been not confident in the last few games, but I see it every day in training, the quality that we have.

"I didn't think it was going to take us long. I think that it was nice to see that, but also just credit to all of us, the staff. We've been working really hard behind the scenes, really pushing, and we'll continue to do that."
While Arsenal failed to hold onto their lead, there were big wins elsewhere in the Champions League, with reigning champions putting six past Roma.
Caroline Graham Hansen netted a brace, as did Claudia Pina, with Ewa Pajor also on target, while a Shukurat Oladipo own goal completed their scoring in the 6-0 rout.
And Juventus ran out 3-0 winners over Hacken thanks to three second-half goals.

But with five minutes left, Leah Williamson secured the ball with her hand to take a goal-kick, but the referee deemed that Misa had already taken it when passing it to her, thus awarding a penalty for handball, which Maeline Mendy converted in the 87th minute.

"I mean, not ideal," Russo told Arsenal's media channels about the dropped points.

"I think we lost control of the second half a little way before [the penalty] anyway.

"So, it's about managing the game a little bit better. I also think the first half, and throughout the game, we had some really, really good spells, so now it's about using that to push forward."

Arsenal have now failed to win from 2+ goals up in the Champions League twice since the start of last season, having never thrown away that kind of lead between 2001-02 and 2024-25.

But despite the disappointing finish, one positive for the Gunners was Russo's first goal of the season after she drew a blank in her first five outings this season.

"I always want to try and score and create, and yeah, it was about finding the half the yard to get a shot off, so I'm happy to do that," she said.

"I think maybe [it's] an area we've been not confident in the last few games, but I see it every day in training, the quality that we have.

"I didn't think it was going to take us long. I think that it was nice to see that, but also just credit to all of us, the staff. We've been working really hard behind the scenes, really pushing, and we'll continue to do that."

While Arsenal failed to hold onto their lead, there were big wins elsewhere in the Champions League, with reigning champions putting six past Roma.

Caroline Graham Hansen netted a brace, as did Claudia Pina, with Ewa Pajor also on target, while a Shukurat Oladipo own goal completed their scoring in the 6-0 rout.

And Juventus ran out 3-0 winners over Hacken thanks to three second-half goals.

rra6xhird1g1lzfw8kg58xs0.title: 'Hats off to Cristiano!' – Zidane salutes Ronaldo's career amid Portugal rift
rra6xhird1g1lzfw8kg58xs0.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo caused a stir when he left Portugal's Nations League camp but Zinedine Zidane still has high praise for his former player.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane believes Cristiano Ronaldo's "great career" should be saluted amid reports of tensions between the 41-year-old and Portugal.
Ronaldo made headlines last week when he announced he had left Portugal's Nations League camp following their second game – a 2-1 win over Norway in which he was an unused substitute.
Reports prior to his exit suggested there was a disagreement between Ronaldo and Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus over his game time.
The Portugal captain said he would tell his side of the story in due course.
While Jesus has left the door open for Ronaldo to link up with the squad again in November, it remains unclear what is set to happen next month.
But Zidane, who managed Ronaldo at Real Madrid between 2016 and 2018, winning three Champions League titles and LaLiga among their honours, came to the defence of his former player.
"He made me win incredible things," Zidane said when asked about Ronaldo's current situation.
"I think we have to salute his great career; what he has done is exceptional.
"I was lucky enough to have him with me. Hats off to Cristiano!
"I still have a lot of respect in general for all the players, but even more so for those with whom I spent time, and especially Cristiano, who still made us win a lot of things."

rrsw0lbtj8yh1b4ivbpwvxruq.title: Mancini: Winning start to Nations League the only medicine to cure Italy
rrsw0lbtj8yh1b4ivbpwvxruq.subtitle: Roberto Mancini begins his second stint in charge of Italy against Belgium in the Nations League, and he wants to get fans back onside.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes a winning start to Italy's Nations League campaign will be the perfect medicine after the Azzurri missed out on the World Cup this summer.
Italy welcome Belgium to the Stadio Olimpico on Friday, for what will be Mancini's first match back in charge after replacing Gennaro Gattuso.
Mancini previously led the Azzurri from 2018 to 2023, guiding them to the European Championship title five years ago by beating England on penalties.
During his first spell, Mancini led Italy on a 37-match unbeaten streak, a European record that has since been surpassed by Spain following their victory over Argentina in the World Cup final.

The 61-year-old won 38 of his 58 games during his first stint (D12 L8) before resigning in August 2023 after a failed qualification bid for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, before having a short-lived spell in charge of Saudi Arabia.
Italy have been placed in Group A1 alongside Belgium, France and Turkiye, and they will play all three nations during this extended international break.

The Azzurri have finished third in the Nations League twice, doing so in 2020-21 and 2022-23, and Mancini believes a good start will go some way to repairing the damaged relationship between the supporters and their team.
"To play well from the start, which won't be easy considering we've had just two days to prepare for this game," Mancini told reporters about his aims for the Nations League.
"This is what international football is like. We have to get things done quickly and get results. That is the only medicine for what ails us.
"We hope to reach the final four of the Nations League. It's a strong group and so it won't be easy, but we'll try. I can't wait to hear the national anthem playing.
"Many of these players are experienced, and naturally there is pressure, but it's positive pressure because playing football is their passion, and they need to enjoy it."

Mancini's last game in charge of Italy saw the Azzurri beat the Netherlands 3-2 to seal third place in the Nations League three years ago, but the end of his tenure was overshadowed by his failure to secure a spot at the Qatar World Cup.
After Luciano Spalletti's tenure, Gattuso also failed to lead Italy to the tournament, with Italy losing 4-1 on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina as they missed out on a third consecutive edition.
"Unfortunately, this is football, you can lose games sometimes in absurd fashion," Mancini added.
"But the good thing about the sport is that it gives you an opportunity to make up for it immediately. We must keep it in mind, but then focus on the future."
Gianluigi Donnarumma was in between the sticks for Italy during those near misses, and he too echoed the disappointment of Mancini.
Donnarumma has played for Italy since he was 17 years old, and following his nation's latest setback, he may not play at his first World Cup until he is 31.
"It's been very tough," Donnarumma told Sky Sport Italia. "I struggle to even explain it. This has been a very long and difficult summer, but we must start again.
"It's a new era, tomorrow we have a big game and the fans like us are disappointed, so it's up to us to fire them up and get them to fall back in love with the Azzurri jersey."

rtpfqwg2ox3h1se8jv58r9u3n.title: Netherlands boss Xavi relishing 'great challenge' against Klopp's Germany
rtpfqwg2ox3h1se8jv58r9u3n.subtitle: Xavi begins his tenure with the Netherlands against Germany in the Nations League, and he is looking forward to the challenge ahead.
paragraphs: Xavi described his first game in charge of the Netherlands as a "great challenge" as they prepare to welcome Germany and Jurgen Klopp to the Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday.
It is a meeting of two coaches making their debuts for the respective nations, with Xavi having replaced Ronald Koeman after another early exit at this summer's World Cup.
The Netherlands were eliminated from the World Cup in the round of 32 on penalties by Morocco, the first time they had failed to reach the last 16 at the tournament.
Xavi had been out of management since leaving Barcelona in 2024, having won LaLiga in 2022-23 and the Supercopa de Espana in the same season.
He compiled 90 wins, 23 draws and 29 defeats in 142 games in charge of the Blaugrana across all competitions, giving him a win percentage of 62.7%.
Xavi is the first foreign coach of the Netherlands since Ernst Happel in 1977-1978, and he is looking forward to going head-to-head with former Liverpool boss Klopp.
"We have to play our best football tomorrow because Germany are a great team," Xavi told reporters.
"I can feel this rivalry. Everyone in our team is really looking forward to the game, and it is a great way for us to start this journey.
"He [Klopp] has been one of the best coaches in the world in recent years. It will be a great challenge for the whole team and for me personally.
"It is always the goal to win, but it is even more important to leave a good impression with the execution. I want the team to show passion, ambition, desire and our philosophy."
When he was unveiled, Xavi described himself as a "winner" and he was confident that his success as a player could be translated to the Netherlands' dugout.
Xavi also believes the quality within the Netherlands' ranks can deliver what he intends to achieve.
"They have the capacity to carry out what we ask of them. I have clearly seen that in the training sessions," Xavi added.
"They are hard workers and are open to listening. I am very happy with that. And I was impressed by the physical aspect, among other things."
The Netherlands also face back-to-back away games versus Serbia and Greece, and a home clash with Serbia on October 4 after they take on Germany.
Memphis Depay, Wout Weghorst, Marten de Roon, Guus Til and injured midfielder Mats Wieffer are missing from Xavi's first Netherlands squad.

Ruben van Bommel and Gjivai Zechiel have been handed senior call-ups, while Jurrien Timber is also expected to feature throughout their four matches having struggled with a groin injury at the start of the campaign.
"We are now focused on tomorrow, not on the rest of the matches. We are ready," Xavi said.
"We have to be a bit careful with Jurrien Timber, who was injured for a long time. But he is available, that goes for everyone."

rysdaimgmck4126owuwtb2lf3.title: Davis excited to see Sporting KC's response to heavy Nashville loss
rysdaimgmck4126owuwtb2lf3.subtitle: Sporting Kansas City's playoff hopes are over after losing to Nashville SC, but Jake Davis still wants to see positivity against RSL.
paragraphs: Sporting Kansas City midfielder Jake Davis expects to see a strong reaction from his team when they host struggling Real Salt Lake in MLS on Saturday.
Sporting KC continue to prop up the Western Conference table with five games to play, and their 4-0 loss to Nashville SC ended their slim hopes of reaching the playoffs.
They are winless in their last three outings (D1 L2), while they have also failed to win their last two matches on home soil, with their last such victory coming on September 12.
But Sporting are determined to finish the season on a high, and Davis is looking forward to seeing the team’s reaction on the pitch.
"Right now, I'm thinking about beating Salt Lake," he said. "I think we need to focus on everything we can give this weekend.
"I sit here, and I see the quality the group has had in the last couple weeks, and I'm excited for Saturday.
"I think we're going to go out, be strong, bring our quality and put on a good performance for our fans and beat Salt Lake."
Unlike their opponents, RSL are still chasing a place in the postseason, as they sit 11th in the West, just five points behind ninth-place Colorado Rapids.
However, they have won just one of their last 16 games (D5 L10), with that victory coming on home soil – they have only registered one road victory in 2026, against Atlanta United in March.

They conceded a stoppage-time equaliser in a 1-1 draw with the San Jose Earthquakes last time out, but were dealt an injury blow as goal scorer Luc De Fougerolles went off injured shortly after hitting the back of the net.
"We don't know the extent of De Fougerolles' injury," head coach Pablo Mastroeni said after that game.
"It doesn't look good... I don't want to overreact to this moment, but he needed help getting to the locker room.
"What he's brought to this team in just a short time has been transformational. Fingers crossed he recovers quick, and it's just a cramp, but we'll see."
Sporting Kansas City – Stefan Cleveland
Sporting KC's 4-0 defeat to Nashville was the 14th time this season that they have allowed three or more goals in a match, the most in a single season in MLS history.
Sporting and Stefan Cleveland have allowed three or more goals in five of their last eight league matches, a run he will be desperate to turn around.
Real Salt Lake – Luc De Fougerolles
De Fougerolles scored Real Salt Lake's lone goal in their draw with San Jose, though he was substituted off injured shortly after, meaning it remains to be seen if he will feature on Saturday.
It was just the second goal scored by an RSL defender in this year's regular season after Lukas Engel scored against Los Angeles FC on July 22.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Real Salt Lake are unbeaten in five straight meetings with Sporting KC (W4 D1), including winning each of the last two meetings.
Dating back to the start of the 2015 season, RSL have 15 wins in 26 regular-season meetings with Sporting (D6 L5).

Sporting KC suffered their fourth four-goal defeat of the season on Wednesday when they lost to league-leading Nashville. Prior to this season, Sporting had just four losses by four or more goals in regular-season play over the previous six seasons dating back to 2020.
RSL, meanwhile, conceded in the fourth minute of stoppage time in their draw with San Jose, the 12th time they have failed to win in their last 13 matches in all competitions (D3 L9).
They have managed one clean sheet over the 13 matches, doing so in their only win (3-0 vs. New England Revolution).
Sporting Kansas City – 35.5%
Real Salt Lake – 38.5%

rzk3tikbpi3j11qi14wfhf8nz.title: Berg Johnsen urges Sporting KC team-mates to be 'on the same wavelength'
rzk3tikbpi3j11qi14wfhf8nz.subtitle: Sporting Kansas City's hopes of reaching the MLS play-offs are slowly fading ahead of their trip to the Houston Dynamo on Saturday.
paragraphs: Sporting Kansas City captain Lasse Berg Johnson has urged his team-mates to "make sure we are on the same wavelength" as they prepare to take on the Houston Dynamo.
Sporting KC are currently bottom of the Western Conference, and their misery was compounded last weekend following a 4-3 defeat against the Philadelphia Union.
Despite leading 3-0 after 16 minutes, SKC conceded four goals in nine second-half minutes to fall further away from the play-off places.
Berg Johnsen believes his side must communicate better on the pitch if they are to turn their season around.

"We need to talk to each other and look at each other and agree on if we are going to press them for the next minutes or are we going to keep playing or are we going to go longer and go for the second balls," said the SKC captain.
"As a team, I don't think we have managed it well enough in those situations.

"We need to look at it and see how can we solve it better on the pitch, because in those moments, what usually happens is we players can be silent, so we need to talk to each other to make sure we are on the same wavelength.
"If we either go longer or if we try to play or if we press them or if we sit, we have not managed that good enough."
Houston, on the other hand, are second in the West and just five points behind leaders Vancouver Whitecaps.
However, after losing 1-0 to the San Jose Earthquakes, the Dynamo drew 2-2 with FC Cincinnati last time out; Houston have won just once in their last six MLS games (D3 L2).
Houston Dynamo – Guilherme
Guilherme scored his team-leading 14th goal of the season on Saturday, tied for the second-most goals in a single regular season by a Dynamo player, with Erick Torres in 2017.
The only player with more regular-season goals in a season for Houston was Mauro Manotas in 2018 (19).
Sporting Kansas City – Andre Luiz
Andre Luiz recorded his first MLS brace on Saturday and has scored three goals in his first four games with Sporting KC.
Sporting are averaging 2.25 goals per game in MLS matches in which Luiz has played, compared to 0.95 this season without Luiz playing.
MATCH PREDICTION: HOUSTON DYNAMO WIN

Houston extended their home unbeaten streak to nine games (W6 D3) with a draw with Cincinnati. The Dynamo have recorded five home unbeaten streaks of 10 or more games in their history, with the last one coming in 2019 (10 games).

The Dynamo earned a win on the road against SKC in August and are looking to sweep the season series for the first time. Houston have just two wins in their last 11 regular-season matches against Sporting KC and have not won at home since May 2021.
Sporting KC have scored three or more goals in three straight regular-season matches after scoring three goals just once in their first 22 league matches of 2026.
It is their first time scoring three or more goals in three straight league games since August 2022, and the club have never done so in four straight.
Houston Dynamo – 63.5%
Sporting Kansas City – 17.1%

s3uqbh4cps281qbh7l4ny0022.title: England 5-0 Greece (8-1 agg): Wiegman's side march on in World Cup qualifying play-offs
s3uqbh4cps281qbh7l4ny0022.subtitle: England booked their place in the next round of Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs with a resounding five-star win in Leicester.
paragraphs: England stormed into the next round of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs after a 5-0 second-leg victory at King Power Stadium, which secured an 8-1 aggregate win.
Lauren James starred with two goals and an assist, with Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway also on the scoresheet as they set up a meeting with Ukraine in the next round.

It took just over two minutes for Russo to break the deadlock; James profited from a midfield mix-up and teed up the Arsenal striker, who skipped away from Eleni Markou's challenge to coolly slot past Styliani Katergiannaki.

Moments later, Hannah Hampton was alert to keep out Ioanna Papatheodorou at the other end before James doubled England's lead 16 minutes in, rifling a stunning strike into the top-right corner after meeting Maya Le Tissier's lay-off.
Le Tissier then blazed over from two yards out under pressure in the 29th minute, but it mattered little as England got two more goals in the following five minutes.
Stanway got in front of her defender to glance in Lauren Hemp's cross in the 30th minute before James ghosted in behind Greece's defence to meet Hemp's low delivery shortly after.

Lexi Potter thought she had marked her England debut with a goal on the stroke of half-time, as her drilled strike nestled into the bottom-right corner, but Stanway was penalised for a foul in the build-up.

Stanway continued to prove a threat, though, and had a goal disallowed herself after the break. She leapt to bring down Alex Greenwood's long pass before volleying past Katergiannaki, but she had just strayed marginally offside.

Stanway and Beth Mead both had chances to add to England's tally, but it was Russo who added some more gloss to the scoreline as Greece's defence were drawn to the ball, and she fired the fifth into an empty net.
Freya Godfrey also came close to a debut goal, with her low curler pushed away by Katergiannaki, and despite England piling on the pressure late on, they could not find a sixth.
England find their clinical edge
Despite scoring three goals in the first leg, one thing Sarina Wiegman highlighted as an area of improvement for the Lionesses was their finishing, having had 26 shots in Crete.
The first half proved England still have the golden touch in front of goal with four first-half goals, and they could have had more with two more disallowed on either side of the break.

James only played the first 45 minutes, but impressed, having three shots worth 0.66 expected goals (xG), scoring with both of her efforts on target, as well as getting an assist with the one chance she created.
But Stanway's fine form in World Cup qualifying continued as she is now England's top scorer under Wiegman with 33 goals, edging away from Mead (32).
Stanway is also just the second player to reach 50+ goal involvements (also 17 assists) under the Dutch manager, after Mead (58 – 32 goals, 26 assists).

Greece offered little going the other way, accumulating just 0.07 xG to England's 4.75, and it means the Lionesses have now won their last seven home matches in all competitions without conceding (24-0 on aggregate) for the first time in their history.

England will now face Ukraine for the second time in World Cup qualifying, having been in their group originally; they won both of those meetings by an aggregate 9-1, and they will be hoping for something similar with a place in the tournament on the line.

s7b8t49nltsw1ptr5r75k92c2.title: Belgium 0-1 France: Olise keeps Zidane perfect with last-gasp winner
s7b8t49nltsw1ptr5r75k92c2.subtitle: France's wastefulness looked set to earn them a draw with Belgium, but Michael Olise came off the bench to ensure they left with a win.
paragraphs: Michael Olise came off the bench to snatch France a late 1-0 victory over Belgium in the Nations League to continue their 100% start.

It looked like Zinedine Zidane's side were set to be frustrated in the injured Kylian Mbappe's absence, but Olise took just 11 minutes after his introduction to score the winner at Stade Roi Baudouin.
France started brightly, and Desire Doue almost scored a stunning opener just 12 minutes in; he twisted away from his marker and slalomed into the box before firing his shot against the crossbar.
Doue almost turned provider shortly after as he whipped a delightful cross in from the right, and though Esteban Lepaul quickly adjusted his feet, his first-time effort was straight at Senne Lammens.
Maghnes Akliouche's free-kick was then spilled by Lammens, who jumped straight back up to smother Lepaul's follow-up. But Romeo Lavia was then needed on the line to deny Pierre Kalulu.
Doue continued to provide the sparkle for France and bent a whipped effort narrowly wide seven minutes after the break.
Two minutes later, Lucas da Cunha came close to a debut goal with his fizzed effort through the crowded box, but it struck the foot of the right post.
Belgium grew into the game the longer it went on, with substitute Dodi Lukebakio surging forward in the 73rd minute to poke a shot on goal, which Mike Maignan smothered.
Lukebakio stung Maignan's palms shortly after with a powerful low effort, and though the goalkeeper failed to hold it on the first attempt, no Belgian player was following in.

France's quality eventually told, however, as Olise latched onto fellow substitute Rayan Cherki's pass and strode forward from the halfway line before curling a lovely finish into the bottom right corner in the 88th minute.
France get over the line after a stuttering attacking display

France's wealth of attacking talent is clear for all to see, but Mbappe is the lynchpin, having also scored the winner against Turkiye last time out when Les Bleus had struggled to break their opponents down.
Zidane shuffled his pack, leaving an obvious replacement in Ousmane Dembele – who entered the fray in the second half – on the bench.
Three players made their debuts as starters in France's team (Andy Diouf, Jeremy Jacquet and Da Cunha), a first since August 2010, when there were six debutants in the line-up.
France certainly had plenty of chances to put the game to bed, racking up 18 shots with seven of those on target, with their attempts amounting to 1.15 expected goals (xG).

Doue was their best outlet, having five shots himself, with two of those testing Lammens and another hitting the woodwork. He had a game-high 16 touches in the opposition box, and also created four chances for his team-mates.
But it was Olise who turned the tide, pulling out a high-quality goal to spare France's blushes and ensure Zidane made it two wins from two.

Belgium will feel the game was theirs for the taking, having held off France for so long, but their first shot on target did not come until the 73rd minute, and when Matias Fernandez-Pardo had a golden opportunity to snatch a draw at the end, he went down too easily as he fired wide, with no penalty forthcoming.

sao5hfjffdkl1i8gntjydzncn.title: Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig: Mbappe on target to extend perfect Champions League start
sao5hfjffdkl1i8gntjydzncn.subtitle: After a dramatic victory over Roma last time out in the Champions League, Real Madrid recorded a routine win over RB Leipzig on Wednesday.
paragraphs: Real Madrid maintained their perfect start in the Champions League this season with a 4-1 win over RB Leipzig.

Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande were on the scoresheet for Jose Mourinho's side at the Estadio Bernabeu as Los Blancos made it three wins from three to begin their European campaign in 2026-27.

After a slow start, the first chance fell the way of Romulo, who saw his volley on the swivel parried behind by Thibaut Courtois, while Vinicius Junior was denied at the other end by Maarten Vandevoordt in the next attack.

Christopher Nkunku then squandered a huge chance for Leipzig, shooting straight at Courtois, and he rued the miss almost immediately as Silva was on hand to score on the rebound after Guler's first-time strike squirmed through the legs of Vandevoordt.
Vinicius' long-range strike was saved on the stroke of half-time, while Federico Valverde tested the Leipzig goalkeeper soon after the restart as Madrid made a fast start to the second half.

And their efforts were rewarded in the 52nd minute as Guler doubled Madrid's lead. Jude Bellingham picked out Mbappe at the back post and the Frenchman's goal-bound header was prodded over the line by Guler.
Mbappe made sure of all three points in the 83rd minute as he curled into the top-right corner, but Leipzig did net a consolation two minutes later as Tidiam Gomis side-footed past Courtois.
However, Madrid still had the last laugh, as former Leipzig winger Diomande volleyed past Vandevoordt in sensational fashion with three minutes to play.
Madrid's stars on show on Champions League night
Mourinho complained about his side's overall performance in their dramatic win over Roma, but the Portuguese will have no such complaints after a dominant showing at home.
Los Blancos won the expected goals (xG) battle 2.91 to 1.44 as they recorded 18 shots to Leipzig's 11, having obtained 64.3% of possession.

Mbappe led the way in the final third, registering the most shots for his side (four) and touches in the opposition box (10), while also creating two chances for his team-mates to go along with his goal and assist.

He has also scored and assisted in the same Champions League match for the first time in his Madrid career (28 appearances). The last time he managed it was with Paris Saint-Germain against Juventus in November 2022.

Guler, who hit the target with all three of his shots and completed 100% of his dribbles (3/3), has scored in two consecutive matches for Madrid in all competitions for the third time in his career, while Diomande also recorded a goal and assist off the bench to place more pressure on Vinicius.

Vinicius has not attempted a single dribble in his last two matches across all competitions, the first time he has strung together two consecutive starts without attempting a dribble in his career with Los Blancos.

Diomande, meanwhile, at 19 years and 341 days, has become the youngest Madrid substitute to score and assist in a Champions League match, giving Mourinho plenty of attacking options amid Vinicius' LaLiga suspension for this Sunday's Clasico.

sfulzbmntwbh1d0cmwqifixhy.title: Zidane ready to make changes ahead of crucial Belgium clash
sfulzbmntwbh1d0cmwqifixhy.subtitle: Zinedine Zidane will make "smart changes" as his France side prepare to meet Belgium in Group A1 of the Nations League.
paragraphs: France head coach Zinedine Zidane has stressed he will make changes to his side ahead of a crucial Nations League meeting with Belgium on Monday.
After three matchdays, Les Bleus occupy top spot in Group A1, sitting one point ahead of second-placed Belgium.
However, it has been a far from ideal campaign for the two-time World Cup winners, with Zidane having lost Kylian Mbappe and Dayot Upamecano to injury and suspension, respectively.
That has forced Zidane to utilise his squad depth, but the former Real Madrid coach is happy with the options he has at his disposal.
"There will be changes, that's for sure. It is our fourth match, and we can't just do anything," Zidane told reporters.
"We will make smart changes, and above all, we will do it to be competitive."
The 1998 world champion is determined to rotate his squad, with the hope that this brings togetherness as well as keeping everyone sharp for the games ahead.
"It is to show that we are all involved and that all the players are committed to this team, to demonstrate that there is a lot of competition within the French national team," Zidane said.
After overcoming Belgium 1–0 thanks to a late strike from Michael Olise in the reverse fixture, Zidane expects a stern test against Mark van Bommel's side at the Stade de France.
"They played very well in the first match against us and caused us tactical difficulties," said Zidane.
"They are capable of many things. Against Turkiye, they posed problems for the opposition, so they are strong both collectively and individually," added the France boss.
However, Zidane is relishing the challenge and "tension" of managing France, having replaced long-term coach Didier Deschamps after the 2026 World Cup.
Zidane said: "I have always felt it, and I like it. I like feeling that tension, I enjoy it.
"But what I love most of all is what I do – being with the players, with this group, that is what I enjoy.
"The demands are the same, but the difference is that the work with the national team differs from that at club level."

shmnnfdqci5r1fg5b4ffob2ss.title: Alonso: Chelsea must be self-critical and take responsibility after Spurs loss
shmnnfdqci5r1fg5b4ffob2ss.subtitle: Chelsea lost at home to Tottenham in the Premier League for the first time since 2018, with Cole Palmer also sent off for the Blues.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso believes his Chelsea side "have to be self-critical and take responsibility" for their defeat to Tottenham.
The Blues lost to Spurs in the Premier League for the first time since April 2018 after a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge.
Goalkeeper Mike Penders scored an own goal before Mathys Tel doubled their lead with a sublime solo effort, which came after Cole Palmer was sent off.
Chelsea failed to score at home in a Premier League London derby for just the second time in their last 17 such games, after a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace on MD1 last season.
The Blues had just seven attempts against Spurs, their fewest in a league game this season and their fewest at home in the competition since January against Brentford (six).
"I think that there were many different moments in the game. First half I wanted more intensity. We wanted high pressing but we were not strong enough in duels," Alonso told BBC Match of the Day.

"We had some kind of chances in the first half and in the second half, we talked and we started a bit better. We had a good chance with Pedro [Neto]. We had spoken about how important the first goal would be and when they scored I felt 'ah, this is not what we wanted'.
"Straightaway almost, came the red card. Disappointed with the result and we have to be honest with the performance, we could have played better.
"It would be so easy to talk about the players we're missing but with the squad that we have, we believe we can do better with the team that we have.
"We have to be self-critical and take responsibility."
Penders became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to score an own goal in a Premier League match, after Petr Cech against Everton in December 2009.
He (21y 85d) is also the second-youngest goalkeeper to score an own goal in the Premier League, after Illan Meslier (20y 354d) for Leeds against Wolves in February 2021.
"This is football," said Alonso when asked about Penders' mistake.
"It is about doing great things and dealing with difficult moments. We will support Mike. We come together from these moments."

spg5pl0s04xv14ffyt4svtu51.title: Bellamy concedes Wales had to 'suffer a lot' against Portugal
spg5pl0s04xv14ffyt4svtu51.subtitle: Wales were narrowly beaten by Portugal to start their Nations League campaign, with Craig Bellamy's side put under pressure in Lisbon.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy admitted Wales had to "suffer a lot" against Portugal but hailed his injury-hit side's resilience in their Nations League opener.
Wales began their Nations League campaign with a narrow 1-0 defeat to Portugal, with Joao Felix's deflected first-half strike proving the difference.
Cristiano Ronaldo also had a goal ruled out for offside after the break, while Wales finished the contest on top, hitting the woodwork late on through Brennan Johnson.

Despite that, Wales are without a win in their last five matches in all competitions (D3 L2), while they have lost five of their last 10 matches (W2 D3), one more than in their previous 25 outings (W11 D10 L4).
The 23 shots Wales faced against Portugal is their most in a single game since a Nations League match against Turkiye in November 2024 (25).
But Bellamy was impressed with how his team played despite being under pressure for long spells in the game.
"It was a difficult game for us. We had to suffer a lot," said Bellamy.
"I think that's the longest we've been in a game without the ball.
"We could have done more with the ball, but I'm beyond proud as well.
"We have a lot of players who weren't here. That's OK; we can handle it.

"A lot of players who don't play week in, week out. So, for them to use the energy they were able to, we've got to have a big heart to be able to do that. They've always shown that, and they showed that again."
The loss leaves Wales bottom of Group A4 after the first matchday, with Norway and Denmark also drawn alongside them.
Wales are missing the likes of Harry Wilson, Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor and Nathan Broadhead through injury, and face a quick turnaround before facing Denmark away on Sunday.
Bellamy is determined to see an improved performance when they step out in Copenhagen.
"There's more for us, so that's something we always look at as a positive," he added.
"How can we improve? How can we get better?"
