The loss leaves Wales bottom of Group A4 after the first matchday, with Norway and Denmark also drawn alongside them.

Wales are missing the likes of Harry Wilson, Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor and Nathan Broadhead through injury, and face a quick turnaround before facing Denmark away on Sunday.

Bellamy is determined to see an improved performance when they step out in Copenhagen.

"There's more for us, so that's something we always look at as a positive," he added.

"How can we improve? How can we get better?"

ssaan07uq4u11kvyh91wp2o2m.title: Fraser lauds Salloi impact ahead of Toronto's crucial run-in
ssaan07uq4u11kvyh91wp2o2m.subtitle: Toronto FC could make a huge step towards clinching a play-off spot when they travel to the Columbus Crew this weekend.
paragraphs: Toronto FC head coach Robin Fraser has lauded the impact of forward Daniel Salloi this season, ahead of a crucial clash with the Columbus Crew.
The Reds are 10th in the Eastern Conference, level on points with ninth-place New York Red Bulls, who currently occupy the final postseason spot and are just one point ahead of Columbus.
Toronto took a huge step towards qualifying for the play-offs with a 2-0 victory over the Red Bulls last time out, with Salloi scoring their second goal to secure all three points.
In his first season with the Reds, Salloi has scored eight goals and provided seven assists, directly contributing to more goals than any of his team-mates.
Fraser praised his forward for leading the charge, especially after the injuries Toronto suffered earlier in the season.
"Daniel's been great for us all year," said Fraser.
"I think early in the year when we were going through this rash of injuries, Daniel was scoring a number of goals for us and really keeping us in games and winning games for us.
"He's been tremendous all year long, and whatever role, whether it’s on the bench or from the start, he's contributed greatly to us, and we're certainly excited to have him."
Columbus' improving MLS form continued last time out as they defeated FC Cincinnati 2-0 on the road.
However, their momentum suffered a blow as they lost on penalties in the US Open Cup final against St. Louis City on Wednesday.
Columbus Crew – Gonzalo Tapia
Tapia both scored and assisted in the Crew's victory over Cincinnati, marking his second such MLS match since joining the club in the summer.
He scored with his only shot against Cincinnati, while also leading his team-mates for touches in the opposition box (four) and possessions won (four).
Toronto FC – Jonathan Osorio
Osorio assisted Salloi's strike for Toronto in their win over the Red Bulls.
The midfielder also led Toronto in chances created (two), touches (49), completed passes (26), possessions won (eight) and interceptions (four).
MATCH PREDICTION: COLUMBUS CREW WIN
Columbus have won four of their last five league games; only Nashville SC and the Philadelphia Union (both 13) have picked up more points over the last five games.
Toronto are also in good form, with the Reds unbeaten in their last three MLS games (W2 D1) during this play-off push.
Hosts Columbus have seven wins, two draws, and six losses this season in 15 MLS contests at home. Toronto have three wins, three draws, and eight losses on the road this season in league matches.
Toronto did win the most recent meeting between these two sides, picking up a 2-1 victory back in March on home soil.
Columbus Crew – 54.2%

stqwkx31cso81els99iixu4ll.title: Juventus boss Spalletti bemused by VAR's decision to rule out late winner
stqwkx31cso81els99iixu4ll.subtitle: Juventus thought they had snatched a late win in the Europa League against Rennes, but Jhon Lucumi's joy was cut short by VAR.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti was left scratching his head at VAR after it intervened to rule out Jhon Lucumi's late goal in Juventus' 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League.
Zeki Celik had given Juventus a fifth-minute lead at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday before Mousa Al Tamari's clever flick beat Guglielmo Vicario soon after to level things up.
Rennes took the lead just before half-time through Boulaye Dia's penalty, but the hosts hit back with a spot-kick of their own, with Nick Woltemade converting from 12 yards out.
And with the spoils looking set to be shared, Juventus thought they had snatched all three points when Lucumi saw his shot deflect off Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal and into the net.
However, the goal was ruled out after a VAR review, with Lucumi deemed to have been in an offside position when Teun Koopmeiners flicked on Douglas Luiz's free-kick.
"I didn't understand it, and I'm going to look into it," Spalletti said of the incident. "When I saw it in the dressing room, I was surprised and disappointed.
"The Rennes player could have cleared that ball and Lucumi didn't impede him. I thought I knew this rule, but after the game I have a lot of doubts.
"The referee was very good, but a little less good on this incident."
The result saw Juventus drop points for the first time in the Europa League this season, though they still sit seventh in the 36-team standings heading into MD4.
Spalletti elected to start Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani for the first time this season, with the on-loan Newcastle United striker impressing.

Woltemade also teed up Celik for the Bianconeri's opening goal, while his strike saw him become only the third player to have scored in each of his first three appearances with Juventus in the major European competitions, after Darko Kovacevic in 1999 and Roberto Baggio in 1990.
Kolo Muani, meanwhile, had a less impactful display. He only fired off one shot while having just 24 touches, the fewest of any starting outfield Juventus player.
The Frenchman was replaced in the 80th minute by Jeremie Boga, and Spalletti said he expected more from Kolo Muani and Woltemade despite the latter's performance.
"They did well, but I think I can expect more from both of them, because their qualities are greater than the performance they gave," Spalletti added.
"What the two of them produce isn't just the sum of their individual qualities. They can coexist, and when they work together, they can become three, not two."

t1v2e3jvr5vy1kmvcz1w3ggmb.title: Ronaldo 'let the team down' by training poorly at Man Utd, claims Ten Hag
t1v2e3jvr5vy1kmvcz1w3ggmb.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo was a bad influence on his team-mates during his second spell at Manchester United, Erik ten Hag has alleged.
paragraphs: Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of being a poor trainer when the duo worked together at Manchester United, saying the forward "let the team down."
Ronaldo and Ten Hag spent a brief few months together at Old Trafford in the early stages of 2022-23, with their spectacular falling-out marring the first half of United's campaign.
Ronaldo reportedly wanted to leave the club in the summer of 2022, and amid tensions with new boss Ten Hag, his contract was terminated in November.

In an explosive interview with Piers Morgan, Ronaldo said he felt "betrayed" by Ten Hag and did not respect the Dutchman, who had dropped the five-time Ballon d'Or winner from his starting lineup on several occasions.
And now, speaking to The Athletic, Ten Hag has alleged Ronaldo was a bad influence on many of his team-mates, even urging them to tone down their efforts in training.
"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag said. "I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for, before I came to United.
"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire.
"Many times I would say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you, to bring you in the right positions, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score.'
"He was not capable of doing this. It's the wrong idea to put this to me, that I expected him to do the pressing. He was exhausted. He couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession.
"The reason was because he didn't prepare himself. Every top team has to embrace the top players, but the top players must work for the team.

"He was telling the players, 'Save your legs at training'. I understand it when you are fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first, you have to train yourself to get to the right fitness levels."
Ronaldo has been in the headlines again recently, over another public row with a head coach.

Having been left on the bench by Jorge Jesus during Portugal's 2-1 Nations League win over Norway last month, Ronaldo abruptly left the Selecao's camp and accused his former Al-Nassr boss of breaching his trust.

Though his international career remains in doubt, key figures in the Portuguese Football Federation have opened the door for the 41-year-old to return, and he was only handed a 30-day suspension from the Portugal setup following an investigation into the incident.

t2o7kaxn3igb1bcbn8dpsl64m.title: Turkiye name Yalcin as Montella's successor
t2o7kaxn3igb1bcbn8dpsl64m.subtitle: Turkiye will be led by Sergen Yalcin in their final two Nations League matches in November after he succeeded Vincenzo Montella.
paragraphs: Turkiye have appointed Sergen Yalcin as Vincenzo Montella's successor.
Montella was sacked following a disappointing few months, in which Turkiye were knocked out in the group stage of the World Cup and made a dismal start to their Nations League campaign.
Turkiye lost all four of their Nations League matches, going down to France, Italy (twice) and Belgium.
Montella won 21 of his 40 matches in charge of Turkiye (52.5%), suffering 14 defeats.
And former Besiktas coach Yalcin will now take over, ahead of their final two Nations League games against Belgium and France in November.
The Turkish Football Association (TFF) confirmed his appointment on Tuesday in a statement, while Yalcin spoke of his pride after taking over the national team role.
"This duty is a very important one," Yalcin said during a programme on Kafa Sports, as quoted by Turkiye Today.
"The crescent and star are above everything. It is a position every coach wants to reach. Being the people's coach is a wonderful feeling.
"It is a source of pride and happiness for me, too. Hopefully, with everyone's support, a successful journey awaits us with the national team."
Yalcin has spent his managerial career working in the Turkish Super Lig, most recently leaving his second spell at Besiktas in May.
He has won 121 of his 276 games in all competitions as a manager (D67 L88), with an average win percentage of 43.8%.

t4d0bd3ewwd01gny6mbzs3t3q.title: Kane: England did what we had to do against Czechia
t4d0bd3ewwd01gny6mbzs3t3q.subtitle: England were under slight pressure to get a win against Czechia after their loss to Spain, and Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane secured it.
paragraphs: Harry Kane said England "did what we had to do" after beating 10-man Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League.
England suffered a disappointing defeat to Spain last time out, but they got their first win of this season's edition at Fortuna Arena.

Pavel Sulc was sent off after 25 minutes for a late tackle on Elliot Anderson, and the Three Lions made their numerical advantage count in the second half, with Anthony Gordon and Kane both on target for the second game running.
Kane has netted four goals in six Nations League appearances since the start of the 2024-25 edition.
The pressure was on England – despite Thomas Tuchel saying before the match that this was not a “must-win” fixture – and Kane was thrilled the team came out on top.
"Job done, it was a professional performance," he told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"It wasn't the most exciting game of football, but we did what we had to. Won the game, good clean sheet, and we take it into the next one.
"When a team who likes to defend get a man sent off, it becomes even tougher. You have to be patient. Against 10 you have to move it quickly, and as they tire, the spaces will open up."
Gordon was a key figure for England again with his opening goal; he now has four goals and four assists across his last nine international appearances.
He is also the second Barcelona player to score in consecutive appearances for England, after Gary Lineker in 1989.
"He's showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England," Kane said of Gordon, who had a team-high four shots and created four chances.

"His performances in the last couple of games have been some of his best that he has played in an England shirt, and I think he is just relishing putting the shirt on and being one of the main men in the team.
"He is an important player for us, and he showed that during the World Cup."
England had conceded 13 goals in their previous six appearances prior to this match, meaning a clean sheet would have been high on their priority list.

Next in Group A3, England travel to Croatia, who are also on three points after following up their win with a 4-1 defeat to Spain on Tuesday, but Tuchel was hesitant to give away any plans for the next match.
"I cannot tell you," he told BBC Radio 5 Live when asked about potential changes. "We have three days, which is a big difference to two games.
"We decided not to travel back to England but to stay in Prague one more night, get some good rest, and then travel to Croatia and have two training sessions there.
"We will push everyone to be available, even Nico O'Reilly and Ezri Konsa, hopefully and then we know more. The next match is important for us against a direct opponent, and we want to win."
On the game itself, Tuchel added: "We played a professional second half.
"We stepped up in urgency, bit of quicker play and better ball speed. We deserved to win the second half.

"With the red card, we became heavy, heavy favourites. A clean sheet is always important; it gives everyone a good feeling. Always things to improve, but overall a serious performance and a deserved win."

tafeaa7zwemq1wkj09tgzehu3.title: 'This time we will win' – Montella promisies Turkiye victory against Italy
tafeaa7zwemq1wkj09tgzehu3.subtitle: Turkiye began their Nations League campaign with a defeat to France, but Vincenzo Montella was confident of beating Italy on home soil.
paragraphs: Vincenzo Montella has vowed he will lead Turkiye to victory against Italy in the Nations League following their narrow 1-0 defeat to France on Friday.
Kylian Mbappe's 54th-minute strike was enough to earn Zinedine Zidane a victory in his first game in charge at Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadyumu.
Ugurcan Cakir was shown a late red card for a handball outside of the box, but Montella was thrilled with the way his team played against France's star-studded squad.
Turkiye finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.21 from their 12 shots, compared to France's tally of 1.17 from the same number of attempts.

And Montella's side come up against an Italy team who began their second stint under Roberto Mancini with a 2-0 defeat at home against Belgium, with Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio scoring in either half to hand Mark van Bommel a winning debut.
It is the first meeting between the two nations since a 0-0 draw in an international friendly in June 2024, but Italy have a good record in this fixture.
The Azzurri have never lost to Turkiye in their previous 14 matches against them (W10 D4).
However, Montella believes his team's performance against France is a solid foundation to build on, and he was confident of getting the better of Italy on Monday.
"You all played very well and showed your fighting spirit," Montella told his squad.
"We conceded a goal due to a momentary lapse in concentration, but we could have won this match.
"Now we will immediately gather our energy and focus on the Italy match. This time we will win, as long as we play with the same discipline and passion."
Turkiye find themselves third in Group A1 after the opening round of fixtures, with clashes against Belgium and Italy to come before the end of the international break.

tel52ebpc26g10vq0gdny0cw3.title: In-form Gyokeres full of confidence after another Nations League goal
tel52ebpc26g10vq0gdny0cw3.subtitle: Viktor Gyokeres believes he is back to his best after scoring for the seventh Nations League game in a row against Romania with Sweden.
paragraphs: Viktor Gyokeres revelled in his sensational scoring streak in the Nations League after his goal helped Sweden beat Romania 1-0 at Arena Nationala on Monday.
Gyokeres netted the only goal in the 13th minute, tucking in from close range after Sebastian Nanasi had turned a cross to the back post against the woodwork.
The in-form Arsenal striker has now scored in his last seven consecutive Nations League matches, while this was his fourth successive goal in this year's campaign.
Gyokeres' four goals are the joint-most in this year's competition, level with Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, Leo Walta, Michael Olise and Troy Parrott.
His contributions to Graham Potter's side have been crucial after Alexander Isak withdrew from the squad with an injury, but Sweden have remained unbeaten in his absence.
Sweden are top of Group B4 after four matches, winning three of those, putting themselves in a commanding position to return to the top table of the Nations League.

Gyokeres' form comes at a crucial time ahead of the return of the Premier League, as Kai Havertz sustained an injury while playing for Germany, with the Swede the likely replacement for Mikel Arteta's side when they face Leeds United this Saturday.

The 28-year-old has failed to score in his first five appearances in all competitions for the Gunners in 2026-27, with just two of those being starts, but Gyokeres feels his strong run during the international break has put him back at the top of his game.
"It feels good. It feels like you get good chances, and then you score," Gyokeres told Viaplay, as quoted by Fotbolldirekt.
"But we could have done more in the first half and killed the game.
"We let them play and didn't get up in the press well enough in the second half, so we made it difficult for ourselves."

tgxhg0n4g4tu1c8dj8nl0qj0f.title: Coventry City 4-1 Newcastle United: Lampard's men out of relegation zone after back-to-back wins
tgxhg0n4g4tu1c8dj8nl0qj0f.subtitle: Coventry City stormed to a 4-1 Premier League win over a porous Newcastle United side at the Coventry Building Society Arena on Monday.
paragraphs: Coventry City thrashed Newcastle United 4-1 to make it back-to-back Premier League wins and climb out of the relegation zone.

Having got their campaign up and running with a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest before the international break, Frank Lampard's side produced another clinical counter-attacking performance at the Coventry Building Society Arena on Monday.

Goals from Jack Rudoni and Sidiki Cherif put them 2-0 up, and though Sven Botman's piledriver gave Newcastle hope of a comeback, substitutes Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni struck late on to put the game beyond Matthias Jaissle's side.

A lacklustre start saw Newcastle fall behind six minutes in, with Rudoni keeping his cool from the penalty spot after Lukas Hornicek spilled what should have been a routine ball to collect and exacerbated the issue by tripping Cherif.

The Magpies soon grew into the encounter, but Coventry were saved by two heroic clearances from Bobby Thomas, one in front of an unguarded net after Jacob Murphy knocked Harvey Barnes' cross back into the danger zone, then another to deny Matias Fernandez-Pardo what seemed a certain goal after he rounded Carl Rushworth.

But Coventry continued to carry a threat on the break throughout the first half, with Cherif shooting straight at Hornicek when he could have played in a team-mate, and the hosts doubled their advantage three minutes into the second period.
When Newcastle could not fully clear the lines from a long throw, Cherif took a touch near the D, then swivelled and drilled a wonderful finish into the bottom-right corner.

Cherif should have had his brace soon afterwards, only to slice badly wide following a botched Botman clearance, but after Joe Willock fired over, the Dutchman thundered a 20-yard shot into the near corner to give Rushworth no chance.

Newcastle then started to look menacing again, but when Joelinton conceded possession cheaply on the edge of his own area in the 81st minute, Simms saw his shot deflect off Malick Thiaw and skip past Hornicek.
And Coventry would add further gloss to the scoreline through Manchester City loanee Mfuni, who blasted a brilliant effort in off the far post, four minutes from time.
There's a new Cherif in town

Monday's result lifts Coventry to 14th in the early-season standings, level on points with Manchester United and only two behind Newcastle, and Lampard had his substitutes to thank for killing the contest.

Simms had only been on the pitch for three minutes and 15 seconds when he scored to make it 3-1, while Mfuni's impact was also rapid, as he made it 4-1 three minutes and 31 seconds after his introduction.
But before then, Cherif had been the star of the show, winning a penalty and scoring with a great finish on the swivel on his first Premier League start.

He is the first Coventry player to achieve both feats in a single Premier League game since Lee Carsley against Everton in January 2001, while his goal was the Sky Blues' first from outside the box in the competition since David Thompson stuck in that same month, also against Newcastle.

Despite having 10 shots more than their hosts could manage (19 to nine), Newcastle had the same amount of shots on target as Coventry (six) and only narrowly edged the expected goals battle by 1.81 xG to 1.43 – 0.99 of the hosts' tally came from set-pieces, with their long throws causing the Magpies constant issues.

No team has conceded more goals in the Premier League this season than Newcastle (13, level with Chelsea and Bournemouth), and they host Aston Villa next time out, while Coventry visit winless Tottenham.

thfihuws9x1xz59k2dq115ly.title: Isak leaves Sweden camp with 'minor injury'
thfihuws9x1xz59k2dq115ly.subtitle: After a brilliant start to the 2026-27 season for Alexander Isak, he now has an injury concern after leaving Sweden's camp after one game.
paragraphs: Alexander Isak has left Sweden's camp and is returning to Liverpool after suffering "a minor injury" while on international duty.
Isak played the whole 90 minutes against Romania on Friday and was on the scoresheet in their 2-1 win, extending his hot streak to start the season.
The striker has five goals in eight matches for club and country so far this term.
Isak had gone down and looked in some discomfort during the match against Romania but had initially said it was just a "heavy stamp" that led to his blood-stained sock.
Liverpool did not confirm the full extent of the injury in their statement, simply saying: "Isak is to return to Liverpool from international duty due to a minor injury.
"The striker will not be involved in Sweden's three remaining fixtures in the current international break and will now be assessed by club medical staff at the AXA Training Centre."
Isak endured an injury-hit first campaign at Anfield, suffering a leg fracture that ruled him out for months, having also missed five games between October and November last year with a groin issue.
However, Liverpool will hope he will be available for their first match after the international break, when they host Manchester City on October 11.

tljp0o9eug051uwv4x3v30zwr.title: 'I don't care about Dallas' – Sorensen only focused on Vancouver in fight for top spot
tljp0o9eug051uwv4x3v30zwr.subtitle: Vancouver Whitecaps host San Diego FC on Wednesday as they look to hold on to top spot in the Western Conference.
paragraphs: Vancouver Whitecaps boss Jesper Sorensen insisted he does not care about FC Dallas in the battle for first place in the Western Conference.
The Whitecaps are top of the West, but only by a point after losing 1-0 to the Colorado Rapids last time out.
In fact, Vancouver have only won one of their last six league matches (D3 L2), allowing Dallas to close the gap to just one point with three games to go.
The Whitecaps host San Diego FC next on Wednesday, which will be followed by a home clash with the Seattle Sounders and a trip to rivals CF Montreal.
Despite the mounting pressure on Dallas, Sorensen insisted his full focus is on his Vancouver side.
"I don't care about Dallas. I care about us," said Sorensen. "I care about us getting the right feeling of how we play.
"I think we have been talking and last year we did not talk much about first place. We just attacked things.
"I think now we have been talking about maybe defending first place because we have had it for a while. I don't think that's the right thing or the right way to see it.
"I don't go into where we end up. We end up where we end up. I don't care. What I care about is how we play."
San Diego are 12th in the West after a 2-2 draw with the Sounders on the weekend, marking their third consecutive draw and fifth in six matches (L6).
They will be eliminated from play-off contention if they lose at Vancouver, or if they draw and Real Salt Lake win at Austin FC.
Vancouver Whitecaps – Brian White
White has scored four goals in three career matches against San Diego, including playoffs, tied with Petar Musa for the most goals scored against San Diego.
He scored multiple goals in each of his last two against them, including two goals and two assists at San Diego in May.
San Diego FC – Cedric Bakambu
Bakambu scored both of San Diego's goals in their draw with Seattle on Saturday, including a match-tying penalty in the sixth minute of second-half stoppage time.
The former Villarreal forward is the eighth different San Diego player to score multiple goals in an MLS match.
MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN
Vancouver's defeat at Colorado was their 11th loss in their last 44 regular-season matches dating back to July 2025.
The Whitecaps have not suffered consecutive league defeats in that time, posting a record of W7 D3 L0 in the matches following the previous 10 losses.
San Diego's winless run extended to nine matches (D5 L4) with their draw against the Sounders, equalling the longest regular-season streak in club history, set earlier this year.
They have not won a match outside of California since a 1-0 win at Sporting Kansas City on March 7.
Vancouver have won two straight over San Diego, both on the road, including the 2025 Western Conference Final.
The home side has never won this matchup, though, as San Diego recorded a 5-3 win at BC Place in their only previous road match against the Whitecaps in March 2025.
Vancouver Whitecaps – 54.7%

tnvql0suiluo1i4f4f40maljz.title: FC Cincinnati 0-2 Columbus Crew: Smash-and-grab win boosts visitors' playoff hopes
tnvql0suiluo1i4f4f40maljz.subtitle: Gonzalo Tapia and Taha Habroune scored as the Columbus Crew overcame their rivals FC Cincinnati in MLS, moving within reach of the playoffs.
paragraphs: The Columbus Crew breathed fresh life into their MLS Cup Playoff hopes with a 2-0 victory over rivals FC Cincinnati at TQL Stadium on Sunday.

Gonzalo Tapia and Taha Habroune were on target in a win that lifted Laurent Courtois' team to within two places and one point of Cincinnati, who occupy the final wild-card place in the Eastern Conference.

The result came despite Cincinnati dominating for long periods, with Teenage Hadebe and David Doudera both going close before Tapia opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, heading Brais Mendez's deep corner home after being left unmarked at the back post.

Cincinnati continued to push after falling behind, with Patrick Schulte called into action by Tom Barlow and Evander, the latter via a deflected free-kick, but the Crew struck again nine minutes into the second half.
Tapia was released down the right-flank by Santiago Rodriguez, and when the Chilean cut the ball back for Habroune, the 20-year-old stroked first-time into the bottom-left corner.

Columbus captain Sean Zawadzki hit his own post and Kevin Denkey turned wide from close range, but that was as close as Cincinnati came to forcing a grandstand finish, as their own postseason ambitions took a major blow.
Columbus take their chances
A look at the underlying stats might have people questioning just how the Crew won this game.

They only managed three shots in total, with both of their attempts on target finding the net, and put up a mere 0.3 expected goals (xG). By comparison, Cincinnati had 23 shots (seven on target) and amassed 1.91 xG.
The Crew have now won five of their last six matches in all competitions (L1) after losing seven of their previous eight, going into Wednesday's U.S. Open Cup final versus St. Louis City.

Cincinnati, meanwhile, were found wanting defensively yet again. During this regular season, the Orange and Blue have seen a total of 130 goals scored in their games (68 for, 62 against), just six off the record of 136 set by Inter Miami in 2025 (81 for, 55 against in that instance), with four games left to play.

tsxqbmujnuvw1heo35oydfyem.title: Manchester United 1-1 Manchester City: Terland equaliser ends WSL champions' perfect start
tsxqbmujnuvw1heo35oydfyem.subtitle: Manchester City were so close to extending their 100% start to seven Women's Super League games, but Elisabeth Terland had other ideas.
paragraphs: Elisabeth Terland halted Manchester City's 100% start to the Women's Super League season after helping Manchester United come back to earn a 1-1 draw.

United had dominated large spells of the Manchester derby at Progress with Unity Stadium before Khadija Shaw broke the deadlock, but Terland ensured Eva Olid's side claimed a point to stop City going back to the top of the table.
Aoba Fujino flashed a powerful shot wide on the turn early on before United took control, with Ella Toone and Jess Park both testing Ayaka Yamashita.
The second half started with United on top, but they piled pressure on City without any reward, as Terland saw a close-range shot smothered by Yamashita after a mistake from Alex Greenwood.
Park then smacked the crossbar after being gifted too much space on the edge of the box, but the game opened up around the hour, with Phallon Tullis-Joyce getting down sharply to deny Shaw.

And the Jamaican got the opener in the 66th minute despite having Dominique Janssen tight to her. Shaw held off her marker and opened up the smallest pocket of space to pick out the bottom-right corner on her 100th WSL appearance.
Julia Zigiotti Olme blazed over the crossbar after a lovely flowing move down the left, but as United committed bodies forward, City almost caught them out on the counter.
Tullis-Joyce was sharp to deny Fujino before Grace Clinton saw an effort cleared off the line by Maya Le Tissier.
But the pressure eventually told for the hosts, with Le Tissier's cross only half-cleared by Shaw, and Terland met it first time to drill past Yamashita in the 89th minute.
Terland puts a dampener on Shaw's century
Shaw likes a big moment, and she was at the centre of both goals, as she made history by giving City the lead, before her clearing header inadvertently teed up Terland.
Her century of WSL appearances has resulted in Shaw scoring 91 goals, already more than any other player has managed in their first 100 appearances in the competition.

It is her fifth goal in eight appearances against United, and it also means she is the first player to score in their first six starts of a WSL season, despite not having her best game in a City shirt.

United were on the brink of suffering three straight defeats to their rivals, but instead, they are the first team to take points off City in the league this term, stopping them from equalling their best start to a WSL season (2017-18, when they won their first seven games).

While City had more shots (17 to 11) and more expected goals (1.61 xG to 1.01), on the balance of the game, United will feel a point is the least they deserved after having Andree Jeglertz's side on the ropes.

And while their three-game winning streak has come to an end, United are now unbeaten in their last five league games, and their resurgence has seen them move up to fourth, while City sit second behind Chelsea on goal difference.

u645o0y3pdje1kgjaef516kku.title: 'The boys gave absolutely everything' – Chivu hails Inter's thrilling comeback
u645o0y3pdje1kgjaef516kku.subtitle: Inter scored two stoppage time goals to come from behind and seal a thrilling win over Fiorentina on Sunday, delighting Cristian Chivu.
paragraphs: Cristian Chivu could not help but praise his Inter side after they scored twice in stoppage time to seal a superb comeback win over Fiorentina on Sunday.
Inter looked set for a shock defeat after Alex Jimenez arrowed a brilliant 30-yard strike into the top corner in the 65th minute.
But Inter fought back late on and secured victory through Marcus Thuram and Piotr Zielinski.
After being frustrated by David De Gea for much of the match, Thuram finally slid one past the Spaniard, bundling home a low shot in the 91st minute.
Thuram was felled by Valde deep in stoppage time, and Zielinski made no mistake from the spot, drilling into the roof of the net to lift Inter back to the Serie A summit.
"We'd played a really good, disciplined game and found ourselves behind to a shot from 30 yards out," Chivu reflected.
"We got our reward for the quality we'd shown. We stayed calm, kept our heads and did what we needed to do in a game like this.
"The boys gave absolutely everything right until the end to achieve what we'd set out to do, which was to win.
"These games are never easy. I was hoping Zielinski would score, but it's never straightforward.
"Even if the result had gone the other way, I'd have said exactly the same things. The boys deserve nothing but praise for their performance today."

u6iq7jq2zooo1imquzotci5gr.title: Carrick insists 'big picture' at Man Utd is still positive as pressure mounts
u6iq7jq2zooo1imquzotci5gr.subtitle: Michael Carrick's future is increasingly in doubt amid a dire run of form for Manchester United, but he is trying to remain upbeat.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick feels the negativity surrounding Manchester United's Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid does not reflect "the big picture" at the club, though he knows they must turn their results around quickly amid mounting criticism.
Carrick's future came under further scrutiny on Wednesday as United were handily beaten by LaLiga giants Atletico at the Estadio Metropolitano.

Pablo Barrios' 47-second opener set the tone for another dismal evening for United, who had Leny Yoro sent off for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity and ultimately lost 2-0, with Ademola Lookman scoring the clinching goal in the 79th minute.
Having also drawn 1-1 with 10-man Tottenham on Saturday, United are winless in five matches in all competitions (D2 L3), their worst run since a six-game streak in January 2025 (D2 L4).
And this season, Ipswich Town (5-2 in the Premier League) and Sabah (4-0 in the Champions League) are the only sides United have beaten overall (PL9 W2 D2 L5).

But in his post-match press conference, Carrick insisted there were still positives the Red Devils could take from a game that saw them create four Opta-defined big chances – their most without scoring in a Champions League match since September 2012 against Galatasaray (also four).
"We need to find a way, for sure. Tonight is a one-off game, which is very different – it's the Champions League, it's a tough place to come," Carrick said.
"In that sense, the bigger picture is a different story. We need to improve certain things, and we're doing certain things okay. But we need to win games, for sure."

Asked if he felt his players' confidence had deserted them amid United's dreadful run, Carrick was dismissive of those suggestions and pinpointed Sunday's trip to Leeds United as an ideal fixture to bounce back:
"I don't see confidence as an issue," he said. "I think to come here and respond and take the ball like we did, and control spells and create chances... it shows the confidence is there.
"There's the big disappointment of not winning, of course, but what a great game we have on Sunday to prepare for.
"It's a fantastic game for us, for the club, with the history for the supporters. Everything to do with the game is a great game, so we'll be ready for that."
In the aftermath of Tuesday's game, centre-back Lisandro Martinez made headlines for criticising United's hierarchy in an explosive interview with Amazon Prime.

While the Argentine defended Carrick, he said everyone at Old Trafford "expected more from the top" and directly criticised the club's technical director Jason Wilcox, saying there was not sufficient investment in the squad this summer.
Asked about Martinez's pointed words, Carrick said:  "I haven't seen it.
"You come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional. I have not seen it, so I don't think it is the right time [to respond].
"We all care and show that in different ways, but now is the time to be together and work through it."

u9ficnk1p1l81c7nns8fodend.title: Mourinho: If I was Vinicius, I would have left Madrid
u9ficnk1p1l81c7nns8fodend.subtitle: Vinicius Junior's four-game ban in LaLiga starts this week, and Jose Mourinho feels the Real Madrid forward has been mistreated in Spain.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho has hailed Vinicius Junior's resilience as he starts a four-game ban in LaLiga, saying he would have left Real Madrid long ago if he was the Brazilian.
Madrid welcome Sevilla to the Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday, having taken 18 points from their first eight league games at the start of Mourinho's second stint in charge.

But they will be without Vinicius for that game – and each of the next three, which includes the first Clasico of the season against Barcelona – after he received a red card for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up to a disallowed goal late on against Villarreal.

The length of Vinicius' suspension was announced around two hours before Madrid's chaotic 4-3 win over Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, which Mourinho suggested was done intentionally to damage his team.
Mourinho has been outspoken in his belief that Vinicius is treated differently to other players in Spain, and he is amazed the forward has not been driven out of the country.
"He's a spectacular kid who it's easy to have a good relationship with," Mourinho told reporters.
"He's a fantastic boy. Tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile...
"If it were me in his place, I probably wouldn't be here.
"In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league in another country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him."

Asked why Vinicius had committed his long-term future to the club by signing a new contract this summer, Mourinho said: "Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, for believing that things can always improve, he renewed and he keeps on smiling.
"Nobody can... well, they can influence him negatively, because he's human... but they can't take away his joy of living and working and being with his team-mates. No one can do that."
Sevilla have enjoyed a positive start to their first full campaign under Luis Garcia, having been tipped as possible relegation candidates in pre-season.
They go into matchday nine with 14 points on the board and sit fifth in the table, only four points adrift of Madrid.
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Real Madrid – Kylian Mbappe

With Vinicius out, even more of the attacking burden will fall on Mbappe. He has been involved in four goals in four LaLiga games against Sevilla (three goals and one assist), scoring in three different matches against them.
He has only found the net in more separate matches in the competition against Real Sociedad (four, also three against three other teams).
Sevilla – Robbie Ure

Ure attempted five shots in Sevilla's last LaLiga match against Levante, equalling the record for a Sevilla player in an away game in the competition since the start of last season (also five by Akor Adams against Elche in January 2026).
His chances will surely be more limited at the Bernabeu, but might he be able to make one count?
MATCH PREDICTION – REAL MADRID WIN
Real Madrid are unbeaten in their last 15 LaLiga matches against Sevilla (W13 D2) and could now record their longest-ever unbeaten run against them in the competition.
If Los Blancos score, they will also set their longest scoring streak against Sevilla in the league's history (currently 15 games, 29 goals).

Sevilla have also lost on 16 of their last 17 trips to the Bernabeu in LaLiga (D1), failing to win there since a 3-4 victory in December 2008; this is their worst winless away run against Real Madrid in the competition.
Sunday's hosts are also enjoying an excellent run on their own turf, winning each of their last seven home games in LaLiga.
They have only once recorded a longer winning run at home in the competition since the 2020-21 season, winning 10 straight between April and November 2025.

While Mourinho's men are clear favourites, Sevilla should not be expected to simply roll over, having gone unbeaten through their first four away games of 2026-27. That is their longest such run from the start of a campaign since 2011-12 (first six, W1 D5).

ubm4jgod0jmm17n6rn01njn10.title: Tchouameni backs Mbappe, Olise or Dembele for Ballon d'Or glory
ubm4jgod0jmm17n6rn01njn10.subtitle: The winner of the Ballon d'Or will be announced later this month, and Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni has picked his top three candidates.
paragraphs: Aurelien Tchouameni believes the winner of this year's Ballon d'Or should be a player from France, with Kylian Mbappe, Michael Olise and Ousmane Dembele his favourites.
The winner of the prestigious individual award will be announced on October 26, with Bayern Munich's Harry Kane and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal among the top contenders.
Mbappe has also been predicted to challenge for his first Ballon d'Or crown, despite failing to win any silverware with Real Madrid during the 2025-26 campaign.
Mbappe registered 43 goals in 47 appearances in all competitions for Los Blancos last season, then carried his stellar form into a record-breaking World Cup this summer.

He made history by becoming the competition's all-time top scorer with 22 goals, while Mbappe's 14 goal involvements (10 goals, four assists) were also the most at a single edition of the World Cup on record (since 1966), though France could only finish fourth.

Olise, meanwhile, ended the Bundesliga season with 34 goal involvements (15 goals, 19 assists), a new record for a winger since Opta data collection began in the German top flight in 2004-05, as Bayern Munich won the league title and the DFB-Pokal.
He, too, had an impressive World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, becoming the first player on record (since 1966) to register seven assists at a single edition.

Ballon d'Or holder Dembele saw his 2025-26 season disrupted by injuries, but he still managed to record 34 goal involvements (22 goals, 12 assists) in all competitions as Paris Saint-Germain retained their Champions League crown and won Ligue 1.
Lionel Messi was the last player to win back-to-back Ballon d'Or awards in 2019 and 2021, though Tchouameni expects a French player to scoop the title this time around.
"The Ballon d'Or must go to a French player, obviously," Tchouameni stated during an interview with France24.
"Kylian had an exceptional season, Ousmane too, by winning the Champions League with PSG, and, of course, Michael Olise."
France have five players in contention for the Ballon d'Or, with Bayern's Dayot Upamecano and Arsenal's William Saliba also nominated after fine individual campaigns.
Spain are the best represented nation after winning the World Cup, with Yamal, Pau Cubarsi, Marc Cucurella, Rodri, Fabian Ruiz and Ferran Torres making the 30-man shortlist.
PSG have 10 players all up for nomination, with Fabian the only player to win both the Champions League and World Cup, putting him in with an outside shot of an unlikely win.
Kane, however, is tipped to become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after a sensational season with Bayern.

He plundered 65 goals across all competitions for Vincent Kompany's side, before hitting six more to help England finish third at the World Cup, the final tournament to fall in the 2026 Ballon d'Or eligibility period.
No other player from Europe's top five leagues scored more than 50 goals in all competitions last term, with Mbappe netting a half-century for LaLiga giants Madrid.

Yamal won LaLiga with Barcelona and scored 16 goals in the league, the joint-fourth highest tally in the division. His 225 completed dribbles were also more than any other player across Europe's top five leagues.

At 19 years and six days, Yamal also became the third-youngest player to play in a World Cup final, after Pele in 1958 (17y 249d) and Giuseppe Bergomi in 1982 (18y 201d), going on to help Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 at MetLife Stadium.

ue7w46xevg80zzepwfku4k0y.title: 'We are under expectation' – Emery urges Villa to keep pushing after City win
ue7w46xevg80zzepwfku4k0y.subtitle: Aston Villa continued their trend of troubling Manchester City in the Premier League, picking up a 2-1 win on Saturday.
paragraphs: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has tempered expectations after his side's win over Manchester City, saying they are "progressing but still under our own expectations."
Emery's side sealed a 2-1 victory at Villa Park on Saturday, with Nicolas Jackson netting in either half.
For both of his goals, Jackson was helped by some calamitous defending from City, with John McGinn teeing the Senegalese up to punish Marc Guehi's error for his opener inside six minutes.

Erling Haaland levelled the scores briefly at the start of the second half, but Villa duly made the most of another City error, with Jackson hitting a shot straight at Gianluigi Donnarumma that the Italian somehow let slip through his grasp.
"We are progressing but we are under our expectations from the beginning of the season because we started so poorly," Emery told BBC Match of the Day.

"Now we are progressing, improving. We analysed the match against Arsenal at home. We competed well but it wasn’t enough. We analysed the match against Forest at home. We lost and our performance was so, so bad. We improved so many things against Brentford at home. We were better but it was not enough.
"Today, with everything we worked on to try to set our standards high, it was a step forward. In the league, we are progressing but still under expectation."
Indeed, Villa are the first side to win three consecutive Premier League games against City since Liverpool's fourth straight win over them in December 2016.

And since Emery took charge of the club in November 2022, the Villans have won five of their eight league meetings with Man City (L3) – at least two more victories than any other side has managed against them in that period.
"We planned this match, trying to keep the same consistency and demands," Emery continued. "This is the level we want to achieve and keep. High demands. Today was a really good test.
"I was so excited about this test, how we were facing them. After the match, progressively, it's about getting better.
"Eventually, the players will have a good impact when we need them. Today is one step forward. That is our clear, clear understanding.”

ui0djsawhs771h6var9jos2gk.title: Burnley 1-2 Wolves: Super-sub Chirewa completes comeback win
ui0djsawhs771h6var9jos2gk.subtitle: Burnley's long, long wait for a home league win goes on after Wolves came from behind to get back to winning ways in the Championship.
paragraphs: Tawanda Chirewa made an immediate impact off the bench to complete Wolves' 2-1 comeback win over Burnley in the Championship.
Burnley started well at Turf Moor as Jamie Vardy scored his first goal for the club, but the Clarets gifted goals to Fer Lopez and Chirewa as Wolves piled more misery on Nicky Hayen.
After Jean-Ricner Bellegarde fired off-target in the second minute, it was all Burnley with Vardy forcing Jose Sa into a sharp, low save following a pacy counter-attack shortly after.

Vardy gave Wolves another warning before he then broke the deadlock 20 minutes in; Burnley worked it well down the left, with Jacob Bruun Larsen spinning to tee up the 39-year-old, who ghosted between the centre-backs to fire past Sa.
Largie Ramazani and Bruun Larsen both had chances to add to their tally, but only the latter hit the target, with Sa making a comfortable save to deny him.

Wolves rode out the pressure over the first half an hour before flipping momentum in their favour. Kyle Walker gave the ball away cheaply, and Sean Neave picked out Lopez, whose shot snuck in off the foot of the near post.
Bruun Larsen cleared the crossbar after the break, with Gregoire Coudert then pushing away a Lopez free-kick before making a double save to keep out Said and Jackson Tchatchoua.

uiu7tetpefut1340eqpkbt6n5.title: Portugal 2-1 Norway: Ramos scores again as 10 men hold on
uiu7tetpefut1340eqpkbt6n5.subtitle: In Cristiano Ronaldo's absence, Goncalo Ramos once again took his chance to shine as he netted the winner for Portugal against Norway.
paragraphs: Goncalo Ramos grabbed Portugal's winner as Jorge Jesus' team survived Francisco Conceicao's late dismissal to see off Norway 2-1 in the Nations League.
Ramos has taken his chance to shine for Portugal in the wake of Cristiano Ronaldo's departure from their squad.
And the forward took his tally for this international break to three goals as Portugal maintained their 100% start to their Nations League Group A4 campaign.
They had to do it the hard way at Estadio Do Dragao, where 36th-minute Kristoffer Ajer's stunner put Norway ahead.
Ajer sublimely curled an exquisite finish into the top-right corner, but the defender's effort was matched in quality by Joao Cancelo just two minutes later.
Cancelo met Nuno Mendes' throw-in and, from the edge of the box, arrowed a first-time strike beyond Egil Selvik.
The full-back went close to a second early in the second half, before Erling Haaland dragged wide from his first, and only, opportunity.
Haaland was taken off shortly after in a surprise move, though he did not appear to be moving entirely freely, and Portugal almost took the lead when Ruben Neves sliced over from point-blank range.
Yet Portugal finally got their second goal in the 79th minute, with Joao Felix teeing up Ramos to finish deftly.

There was time for drama when a member of Norway's bench seemed to see red before Conceicao then received two bookings in swift succession for dissent, but Portugal held onto the points, despite their numerical disadvantage.
Ramos the main man as Portugal prove there is life after Ronaldo
Ronaldo's departure has overshadowed what has been a superb first four games in charge for Jesus, who has already guided defending champions Portugal into the Nations League knockout stages.

They have beaten Norway twice, and Jesus will be particularly pleased with how tightly under wraps his defence kept Haaland, who did have three shots but only had the one real chance, which he scuffed.
Ramos got the crucial goal, and both of the shots he had were on target, and if Ronaldo really is to retire, then Portugal do have their natural front man lined up.
It was a mixed day for Conceicao, who was Portugal's most creative player (four chances created), yet then showed a real lack of composure and professionalism to get himself sent off.
Ultimately, though, it is a case of job done for Portugal, who can rest easy heading into the November fixtures, knowing their place in the next round is secure.

ujh51dkqxtog1r51runmdcod2.title: Real Betis 2-5 Barcelona: Yamal takes centre stage in heated LaLiga clash
ujh51dkqxtog1r51runmdcod2.subtitle: Barcelona came out on top against Real Betis in a match which featured seven goals, one disallowed strike, and one red card for a headbutt.
paragraphs: Barcelona thrashed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 in a fiery LaLiga clash at Estadio La Cartuja de Sevilla.

Lamine Yamal was at the heart of things, scoring a wonderful opener and assisting Gabriel Jesus later on, while the teenager was also headbutted by Facundo Bernal, which resulted in the Betis player being sent off.

The action started in the 10th minute as Yamal cut inside with brilliant skill before curling into the top-left corner, but Betis were level before the half-hour mark as Valentin Gomez headed in from Pablo Fornals' cross.
Hector Bellerin squandered a great chance, shooting straight at Joan Garcia from Fornals' cut-back, and he immediately rued that miss as Rodri headed in from Fermin Lopez's corner in the 41st minute.

Betis thought they equalised before the break when Giovani Lo Celso scored a sensational volley from distance, only for it to be disallowed for a handball against Cucho Hernandez in the build-up, and Barca piled on the misery as Yamal squared for Gabriel Jesus to make it 3-1 six minutes after the restart.

Abde Ezzalzouli halved Barca's lead two minutes later, but his goal was overshadowed by a flashpoint as Yamal and Bernal came together seconds after the goal was scored, with the latter twice headbutting the Barcelona winger.

Betis struggled with their numerical disadvantage, and Hansi Flick's side restored their two-goal lead when Eric Garcia tapped in after a brave header back across the box from Pau Cubarsi, who also teed up Dani Olmo for a stunning finish in the 81st minute to round off the win.
Yamal thrives in the heat of the battle

Yamal rattled the Betis fans early on with his goal, and the winger was booed with every touch he took, even more so after Bernal's sending-off, but the 19-year-old proved why he is a Ballon d'Or contender.
He completed six of his eight dribbles, as many as the whole Betis team combined, while also leading his side in shots (four) to go along with his goal and assist.

Yamal is the first player from Europe's top-five leagues to reach 10 assists this season across all competitions, and also the player who has been involved in the most goals this season across all competitions (nine goals and 10 assists).
He has scored eight goals in LaLiga this term, the highest tally by a Spanish player after the first nine matches of his club in a season of the competition since Diego Costa in 2013-14 (eight).
But Flick has reason to be delighted with his whole team, who accumulated 3.04 expected goals (xG) to Betis' 0.98.
Barca are the second team to win their first nine matches of a season in the entire history of LaLiga, after Real Madrid in 1968-69.
Additionally, they have scored 39 goals, the second-highest goal-scoring record for a team after their first nine matches of a competition season, after Sevilla in 1940-41 (42).

uz78au0dt47e1wsg3dj0q41pd.title: Buffon backs Spalletti to stay and succeed at Juventus
uz78au0dt47e1wsg3dj0q41pd.subtitle: Luciano Spalletti is starting to come under pressure due to Juventus winning just one of their last five Serie A matches.
paragraphs: Former Juventus goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon believes Luciano Spalletti is still the right person to lead the club, saying: "The problem can't just be the coach if you fire five of them in four years".
Spalletti is under pressure after a disappointing start to the season by Juventus, who suffered a damaging 3-0 loss to Lazio in Serie A at the weekend.
That defeat leaves them eighth in the league table on 11 points, already eight behind Inter and Lazio, who are level on points at the summit.
Juventus have lost two of their last five Serie A home games (W2 D1), as many defeats as they recorded in their previous 44 top-flight matches at Allianz Stadium (W24 D18).

Spalletti has overseen back-to-back wins to start their Europa League campaign, but there are already murmurs of discontent around his position, though Buffon believes it would be a mistake to let him go.
"If I have one hope, it is to see Spalletti continue his work until the end," he told La Gazzetta dello Sport.
"The problem can't just be the coach if you fire five of them in four years.

"It might not be the strongest Juve we've ever seen, but taking away [Kenan] Yildiz, [Manuel] Locatelli, [Marcus] Thuram, [Jeff] Ekhator, [Arkadiusz] Milik and [Kamil] Grabara would be like taking [Fabio] Cannavaro, Buffon, [Francesco] Totti, [Alessandro] Nesta and [Andrea] Pirlo away from Italy.

"They have to rebuild, and instead they're lacking. Luciano never looks for any excuses, but he also played three days after Celta Vigo and a long journey after getting back home at five in the morning."

Juventus have accumulated just 11 points from their first seven Serie A games, failing to surpass that mark after the first seven games for the third time in the last 11 seasons, after 2021-22 (11 points) and 2022-23 (10).
At this stage, reports suggest Juventus will continue to back Spalletti, while defender Bremer is said to have apologised for his post-match outburst after Lazio.
He accused some of his team-mates of getting "scared" and "hiding", but Buffon also understood the defender's frustration.
"I did that as well, and it was always instinctively," Buffon added.
"I never planned a speech; I always thought it was right to speak in the moment. I knew that I had to say certain things at certain points.
"I understand Bremer's outburst. However, when you talk, you always have to be in the position where you're the one who is giving the most and can afford to make certain jabs.
"But you have to question yourself first. Sometimes I needed to be told off as well."

v3q0sbpul8glz2gon2zetbjr.title: De Bruyne 'even better' in a deeper midfield role for Napoli, insists Allegri
v3q0sbpul8glz2gon2zetbjr.subtitle: Kevin De Bruyne scored twice after starting in the central midfield pairing, and Massimiliano Allegri believes he can be successful there.
paragraphs: Massimiliano Allegri is trying to convince Kevin De Bruyne to take on a new role for Napoli, but the Belgian is not keen on playing deeper in midfield.
Napoli got back to winning ways in Serie A as they cruised to a 3-0 victory over Frosinone, with De Bruyne scoring twice on either side of Noa Lang's goal.

He scored his first from the penalty spot – dispatching the re-take after Rasmus Hojlund's initial effort was saved but pulled back for encroachment – and rounded off the scoring with the last kick of the game.

De Bruyne has notched his first Serie A brace and his 12th multi-goal performance in the top five European leagues – it is the first time he has done so since April 2024 against Crystal Palace for Manchester City in the Premier League.
Due to the injuries in his squad, Allegri opted to change to 3-4-3 formation, with De Bruyne lining up alongside Stanislav Lobotka in the centre of midfield.
"He is an extraordinary player, and in my view, if he's working as a playmaker in that midfield pairing, he's even better," Allegri told Sky Sport Italia about De Bruyne.
"I told him he can extend his career by another couple of years if he plays in that position.
"He doesn't like it very much, as he enjoys himself more in an advanced role, but he did really well.

"Let's not forget, he was out injured for a long time last year; [Andre-Frank Zambo] Anguissa and [Billy] Gilmour were injured too, so it takes a little time and patience to get everyone in good shape.
"The most important thing is to be more solid and protect the defence; we still allowed too many opportunities."
Napoli moved up to eighth in Serie A with their third win of the season and are now unbeaten in their last three league games after back-to-back losses.
The Partenopei were particularly dominant in the first half, having 13 of their 19 shots before the break, and Allegri is keen to replicate that performance going forward.
"The best thing was the aggression and hunger we showed at the start of the game," Allegri added.
"If we want to analyse it technically, there were six or seven situations where we got into good positions and didn't even manage to get a shot on goal.
"Frosinone are a team who can go on the counter if you don't finish that move; it turns into a ping-pong match and forces you to use up a lot of energy.
"In the second half, we were a little more defensive, as there were many players back from a long time out and they were getting tired.
"We did well to control the situation, then had the chances that we simply cannot get wrong; we needed to make the right passes when two-on-one or three-on-two."

v5nls8gpxetf155mesmu9bd9j.title: Arena: Regular-season run-in 'critically important' for San Jose
v5nls8gpxetf155mesmu9bd9j.subtitle: The San Jose Earthquakes have only won one of their last six MLS games, and they are not yet sure of their playoff place.
paragraphs: Bruce Arena knows the San Jose Earthquakes face a "critically important" regular-season run-in.
With three games remaining in the regular season, the Earthquakes sit fourth in MLS' Western Conference.
While they are sure of a postseason spot, they have not yet qualified for the playoffs, as they could still finish in the wildcard slots.
That is due to a run of just one win in six games, while they lost 3-0 to FC Dallas last time out.

All three goals San Jose Earthquakes conceded in their loss to Dallas were scored after the 80th minute. It was the first time in club history that they have lost a match by three or more goals despite not allowing a goal before the 75th minute.
San Jose host the Colorado Rapids on Wednesday, before taking on Real Salt Lake on home turf and then rounding out the regular season with a trip to Minnesota United.
And Arena knows how vital the next two games at home are as his team aim to rediscover a winning touch.
"Yes, those are two important home games," he said.
"We'll take the first one and try to get three points, but certainly they're critically important."
San Jose had their chances against Dallas, but they lacked a clinical touch in front of his goal.
"Both teams had chances. That's all part of the exercise," Arena said.
"You know, you got to finish your chances, and we knew it was going to be a tight game, and it turned out to be that. So not being able to convert a quality chance makes a difference in the game."
The Rapids sit eighth in the West, and are not yet sure of their place in the playoffs.
San Jose Earthquakes - Preston Judd
Judd has 16 MLS goals to his name this year.
He has had 65 shots in the league, which is 31 more than any other Rapids player this season.
Colorado Rapids - Morgan Whitaker
Whitaker scored the lone goal in Colorado's win over the Vancouver Whitecaps on Saturday, his third goal since debuting for the club in September.
Three players have combined to score nine of the Rapids' 11 goals since the start of September, with Whitaker, Paxten Aaronson and Donavan Philip with three apiece.
MATCH PREDICTION: SAN JOSE WIN
The Rapids have lost only one of their last eight matches (W2 D5).
Colorado have kept a clean sheet in each of their last eight wins, last winning a match in which they conceded a goal on April 11 against the Houston Dynamo (6-2).
The Earthquakes won nine of their first 10 matches this season (L1) through the end of April but have managed four wins in 21 regular-season matches since (D9 L8).
In fact, the Earthquakes had four more points through the end of April (27) than they have managed from May through now (21).
Plus, the Rapids have won their last two away matches against San Jose after winning only two of their previous 21 road matches against them (D8 L11).
However, Opta's model is backing San Jose to take the points..
San Jose Earthquakes - 47.2%
Colorado Rapids - 26.5%

San Jose Earthquakes - Preston Judd

v5pye2h7azd41b3b8yt2e6jz4.title: Sassuolo 1-1 AC Milan: Amorim's side hold on to protect unbeaten start
v5pye2h7azd41b3b8yt2e6jz4.subtitle: AC Milan are one of just four teams still yet to lose in Serie A this season, though Sassuolo certainly put that record under pressure.
paragraphs: AC Milan remain unbeaten across their first six games in Serie A this season, but had to hold onto a point in a 1-1 draw with Sassuolo at MAPEI Stadium.
Adrien Rabiot put Ruben Amorim's side in front just after the hour with a brilliant strike, but Cas Odenthal swiftly cancelled it out to share the spoils.
The game took some time to spark into life, with Darryl Bakola blazing a long-range effort over early on before Vasilije Adzic and Armand Lauriente also failed to hit the target for Sassuolo.
Rabiot glanced a header clear of the crossbar after the half-hour mark, but Milan turned up the pressure during the nine minutes of first-half stoppage time.
Diego Moreira improvised a volley under pressure, which Arijanet Muric pushed away, and the goalkeeper also smothered Strahinja Pavlovic's far-post header.
Milan saw a penalty shout waved away after Duje Caleta-Car appeared to drag down Goncalo Ramos, who then curled a speculative effort wide from the left.

However, it was Luka Modric's half-time introduction that helped turn the tide as he linked up a lovely Milan move before threading it into Rabiot, who rifled in a tight-angled effort from the left of the box in the 63rd minute.
Sassuolo responded well, with Mike Maignan making a double save to keep out Kieron Bowie and Kristian Thorstvedt, who will feel he should have done better with his backheel flick.
But Odenthal restored parity five minutes later, squeezing his poked shot through the crowded box from a corner.
Sassuolo then thought they had found an 88th-minute winner when Thorstvedt fired in from close range, but the referee's whistle had already gone after Ramos went down under a challenge from Bowie.
Milan force to dig deep to take point
While the first half was a slow burn, the second finished with a high tempo, with Maignan having to be at full stretch to deny Thorstvedt and ensure Milan left with a point.

The first shot on target did not come until the 43rd minute, courtesy of Ramos, but both sides eventually finished with 11 shots apiece, while Sassuolo only just narrowly edged the expected goals (xG) battle 1.2 to 1.17.

Rabiot is now Milan's joint-top scorer this season with three goals. Only Roma's Donyell Malen (six) has registered more goal involvements than the Frenchman (five – three goals, two assists) in Serie A this season.

But Milan were never safe when Alberto Aquilani turned to his bench. Sassuolo have now scored five goals via substitutes, while Milan have conceded three goals from players that have entered the fray off the bench.
While Amorim would have wanted to walk away with a win, the point keeps Milan in the mix at the top with 12 points, though they have now drawn three of their last four league games.

vaiivu6dxrt017dro52fse4l0.title: Manchester City 2-2 Brighton (4-3 pens): Rulli's shoot-out heroics sends EFL Cup holders through
vaiivu6dxrt017dro52fse4l0.subtitle: Manchester City's EFL Cup title defence was put at risk by Brighton, but back-up goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli starred in a penalty shoot-out.
paragraphs: Geronimo Rulli's saved two penalties as Manchester City reached the quarter-finals of the EFL Cup after a 4-3 shoot-out win with Brighton following a 1-1 draw in normal time.
Mateo Kovacic cancelled out Malick Yalcouye's opener before City came back from behind again after Georginio Rutter had put the Seagulls back in front at the Etihad Stadium.
Vitor Reis ensured the tie would go to penalties, and Rulli proved to be City's hero in the shoot-out, saving spot-kicks from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to ensure the holders' progression.
Rayan Cherki was at the heart of City's early pressure, first testing Steele in the seventh minute before seeing his shot deflect off Yalcouye and over the Brighton crossbar.
But Fabian Hurzeler's side grew into the contest, with Rutter forcing stops out of Rulli, and there was nothing the City goalkeeper could do for the visitors' opener.
Slick play down the right-hand side saw Jack Hinshelwood collect possession inside the City box before finding Rutter, whose goal-bound effort was turned in from close range by Yalcouye.

However, City drew level five minutes before half-time through Kovacic. After appeals for a handball against Jaouen Hadjam were waved away, Phil Foden laid the ball off for the Croatian to bend a superb effort in off the left post.
Brighton did not let their heads drop, though, and retook the lead within 77 seconds of the restart when Hadjam's cutback was swept into the bottom-right corner by Rutter.

Rutter should have put Brighton further clear just before the hour. First, his curling strike was tipped onto the crossbar by Rulli, with the Frenchman then rounding City's goalkeeper moments later, but his shot from a tight angle rippled the side-netting.

And Brighton were made to pay in the 72nd minute by Reis, who inadvertently turned Cherki's powerful free-kick past the sprawling dive of Steele, with Mats Wieffer coming closest to a winner late on, only to strike the woodwork.
Both sides stayed perfect for their first three penalties until Kovacic was denied by Steele, but Ayari failed to make Brighton's advantage count as Rulli dived to his left to make the save.
Cherki stepped up and coolly slotted from 12 yards out, but Dunk could not repeat the trick to force sudden death, with Rulli guessing right to send City through.
Cherki shines among Maresca's many changes
Enzo Maresca elected to make nine changes to the City side that was beaten by Aston Villa last weekend, with Marc Guehi and Cherki the only ones to keep their places.

And City were not at their free-flowing best in attack, only managing to muster an expected goals (xG) total of 0.87 from their 13 shots, three of which were on target, compared to Brighton's tally of 2.06 from their 17 attempts.

Nevertheless, Maresca's side were able to get the job done on spot-kicks. They have now won or progressed from their last eight EFL Cup matches, their joint-best ever winning run in the competition, becoming one of only seven teams to have done so.
It was no surprise to see Cherki pull the strings. He finished with team-high totals for shots (six), chances created (four) and passes in the final third (23), further proving why he is so pivotal.
Cherki will surely be set to feature again when Brighton head back to the Etihad Stadium in the Premier League this weekend.

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vdueugzzdr8v1u9dow76lhnu1.title: Maestre says 6-1 rout of Spurs could be a 'game-changer' for London City
vdueugzzdr8v1u9dow76lhnu1.subtitle: Alexia Putellas and Kadidiatou Diani inspired London City Lionesses to a 6-1 win over Tottenham on Sunday, taking them third in the WSL.
paragraphs: After London City Lionesses trounced Tottenham 6-1 in the Women's Super League, head coach Eder Maestre said the result could be a "game-changer" for his team.

Captain Alexia Putellas and France international Kadidiatou Diani scored two goals apiece as London City ran riot at Brisbane Road, with Danielle van de Donk and Delphine Cascarino also on target for the visitors.
Maestre's team were 3-0 up by half-time, with Putellas getting her goals in the third and 34th minutes, building on her first WSL strike in a 2-0 victory over Brighton last week.
Putellas now has 49 goal involvements in her last 50 starts at club and international level, scoring 28 times and providing 21 assists for London City, Barcelona and Spain.
London City have 12 points on the board after five WSL matches, and Maestre believes the dominant nature of their latest win will provide everyone at the club with a major boost.
"The three points are the same as you can have in every game, but this kind of win can be a game-changer, in terms of showing everyone that we are pushing hard," said Maestre.
"But, at the same time, we need to be humble as well. The teams that are used to being there and occupying these places [at the top] are still there.
"I'm so happy we're hitting our targets. When you have these kinds of players it is about trying to find chemistry and it takes time.
"It's a process, and we're in the process of building something strong."
Spurs had not lost any of their first four games of 2026-27, taking 10 points, but Martin Ho said they could have no excuses for the way their performance levels dropped.
"Really poor, not acceptable from us as a group. Defensively, we didn't win the first ball or the second ball. In duels, we were poor. We have to move on," Ho said.
"The team collectively needs to own that and we will, and that starts with me, I take responsibility for it.
"We were just not at it, but that can't be the level. Everyone will be disappointed – that was not the level we expect. We conceded six goals and you don't want to be doing that."
In Sunday's other early games, there were also one-sided victories for Brighton, who thumped pointless Charlton Athletic 5-1, and Chelsea.

Sonia Bompastor's Blues eased to a 3-0 win over London rivals West Ham, with Melvine Malard opening the scoring in the 38th minute, before late goals from Kiera Walsh and Maika Hamano made the points safe.
Everton also beat Birmingham City 2-1, while Aston Villa played out a 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace.

veep3y452f5c154sn474jn56t.title: Simeone delighted Barrios opened his goalscoring account for the season
veep3y452f5c154sn474jn56t.subtitle: Atletico Madrid earned a 2-0 Champions League win over Manchester United, a victory that was built on Pablo Barrios' first-minute goal.
paragraphs: Diego Simeone was thrilled that Pablo Barrios got the goal he needed to boost his confidence as Atletico Madrid beat 10-man Manchester United in the Champions League.
Having lost their opening match in the competition 2-1 to Liverpool, Atletico got their first win on the board this campaign.
Barrios broke the deadlock with his first goal of the season after just 47 seconds, netting Atletico's second-earliest Champions League goal, to get them off to a dream start.
Atletico then hit the woodwork on either side of half-time and Johnny Cardoso's disallowed effort due to a handball by Marcos Llorente in the build-up.
But after Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Jonathan David a goalscoring opportunity, it took Ademola Lookman just five more minutes to add Atletico's second and effectively secure all three points.
"A good transition in attack," Simeone told Movistar when asked about the first goal.
"Barrios needed a goal to connect with what he needs to continue growing, which is to find the back of the net. We're happy about it."
He then added about Lookman: "He's a very important player; he has very good stats, he scores goals, he's good in one-on-one situations…
"He's not at that point where that comes through, but he's rediscovered his scoring touch; he had the instinct to follow up the play, and the rebound went his way. We got a win we needed."
Since the start of 2023-24, only Arsenal and Bayern Munich (both 16) have won more home games in the Champions League than Atletico (P19 – W15 D1 L3).
But they had to play this one without captain Koke, who missed the clash following the death of his mother on Tuesday.
Barrios dedicated his goal to Koke, saying he wanted to make sure the team showed their support on a difficult day.
"First and foremost, besides the team, it was very important for Koke and his whole family; it's a very tough day for them. This victory is for them," he said.
"It has been very hard news for everyone, and I said that if I scored, I would do that, and it just came out naturally.
"The early goal helped us control the game. We're very happy with the win."
