vhqlv9tok3j41oau25bwifhad.title: Luis Enrique trying to 'manage the noise' around superstar Doue
vhqlv9tok3j41oau25bwifhad.subtitle: Desire Doue has had a sensational start to the season, and Luis Enrique says the only difficult thing is managing the "noise" around him.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique claimed the only difficulty when it comes to managing Desire Doue is keeping a lid on the hype around the Paris Saint-Germain star.

Doue has made a sensational start to the season. He starred against Barcelona and Manchester City in the Champions League, and has contributed to eight goals in total (four goals, four assists) in all competitions.
With Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia out injured, the onus is on Doue to keep performing for PSG, who top Ligue 1 ahead of facing Le Havre on Friday.
But when asked about managing such a talent, Luis Enrique said: "For a player of his technical ability and age, the most difficult thing is managing the noise around him.
"It's the most difficult for me because I know Desire Doue perfectly. He's a player with an incredible work ethic and a constant desire to help the team.

vluu9nphhblq1iizrybh49rh9.title: Neuer takes responsibility for 'silly mistake' in Bayern draw
vluu9nphhblq1iizrybh49rh9.subtitle: Bayern Munich were held to a 2-2 draw by Augsburg on Saturday, with Manuel Neuer making a huge mistake inside the opening 10 seconds.
paragraphs: Manuel Neuer called his early error in Bayern Munich's 2-2 draw with Augsburg a "silly mistake".
Bayern twice came from behind at WWK Arena to salvage a point as Ismael Saibari and Nathaniel Brown cancelled out goals from Robin Fellhauer and Rodrigo Ribeiro.
Fellhauer scored after just 8.37 seconds as he dispossessed Neuer and dispatched into an unguarded net, recording the fastest goal in Bundesliga history.
Bayern have started the Bundesliga season with 11 points from their first five matches – the last time they had fewer points at this stage was in 2010-11 (eight).

Nevertheless, Bayern are unbeaten in their last 29 Bundesliga games (W21 D8) – they have only had a longer unbeaten run away from home once before, with 33 consecutive unbeaten matches between 2012 and 2014.
"It was a silly mistake by me," said Neuer, who, at 40 years and 197 days old, has overtaken Jens Lehmann to become the seventh-oldest player in Bundesliga history.
"I had to bring the ball onto my left foot because two players were closing me down from the right. I should simply have made a different decision.
"I first had to reflect, take a deep breath and, of course, I still hoped we could turn the game around.
"I think we had the chances to do so, but unfortunately, we failed to take them."
Bayern failed to move level on points with early Bundesliga leaders Borussia Dortmund, who drew 2-2 with Werder Bremen on Friday.
Despite the costly mistake from Neuer, Vincent Kompany has backed his goalkeeper to bounce back quickly.
"Of course, we wished for a better start. I've played enough football to know that this happens, and you can't change it," said the Bayern boss.
"He [Neuer] knows how to deal with the situation, and we stand together as a team."

Everton have lost their last two Premier League games, though, last losing three straight with David Moyes at the helm way back in October 2011.

With 46.7% of simulations going their way, Newcastle are favourites, with Everton claiming all three points in 26.8% of scenarios and earning a draw in 26.5%.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No. 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player; I don't.
"I think going forward, Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.
"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home; for me, he can't be in the team."
Wirtz has been called up in Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the upcoming Nations League.
Klopp – the former Liverpool manager – has named two squads, with Wirtz getting a rest before being in contention for their final two games of the international break against Serbia and Greece.
"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," Carragher added.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany; that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world; we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game; he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.
"I would love that to happen. I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."
Liverpool, who sit sixth in the Premier League table on nine points after an unbeaten start, return to action on October 11 against leaders Manchester City.

vx2gfa0wnl8a1dz4zx74zmxy2.title: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham: Spurs pounce on Palmer and Penders horror shows
vx2gfa0wnl8a1dz4zx74zmxy2.subtitle: Mike Penders' calamitous own goal and a late strike from Mathys Tel saw Tottenham beat 10-man Chelsea 2-0.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer saw red as Tottenham claimed a deserved 2-0 victory over a dismal Chelsea side at Stamford Bridge.
Spurs had only won on one of their last 36 league visits to Chelsea prior to Saturday's contest, with that triumph coming in 2017-18.

But Roberto De Zerbi's team improved on that record, and claimed their second Premier League win of the campaign, thanks to a calamitous own goal from Mike Penders and Mathys Tel's sumptuous late strike.
Palmer's dismissal, which came between Spurs' goals, compounded a miserable day for Xabi Alonso, who suffered his first home defeat as Chelsea boss.
Spurs were dominant from the off, though it was not until the 29th minute that they created a clear opening, with Omar Marmoush firing at Penders from Andy Robertson's cutback.
Penders had to smother Tel's attempt soon after, but Jordan Henderson forced Antonin Kinsky into a save at the other end.
Pedro Neto also forced Kinsky into action before the break, and Spurs were dealt a blow early in the second half as James Maddison went off injured.
Former Chelsea man Conor Gallagher came on in his place and would go on to play a pivotal role, though only after Neto had drawn another stop out of Kinsky following Mateus Fernandes' error.

But Spurs' deserved goal arrived in the 77th minute. Penders, who featured in the absence of Emiliano Martinez, came out to punch Fernandes' corner, but got it all wrong and instead flapped his attempted clearance back over his own line, with Maxence Lacroix unable to hook it clear.
Chelsea's misery was compounded when Palmer, nine minutes after he was booked for lashing out at Fernandes, received his second yellow card following a stamp on Gallagher.
Tel then capped off a superb Spurs win, charging through midfield and sending a low, crisp strike into the bottom-left corner from range.
Alonso's dismal day at the office

While De Zerbi will feel it is finally clicking for his Spurs team, this was a bad, bad day for Alonso, and it showed the work he has to do to get this Chelsea side back to where the club's fans feel they should be.

Chelsea had just seven attempts, their fewest in a Premier League game this season and their fewest at home in the competition since January against Brentford (six). Spurs had 15 shots and created chances worth 0.74 expected goals (xG) to the Blues' 0.43.
They failed to score at home in a Premier League London derby for just the second time in their last 17 such games, after a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace on MD1 last season.
This also marks the first time Chelsea have been beaten by Spurs while also failing to score at Stamford Bridge since December 1986 (2-0).
Their performance was summed up by Palmer's petulance. The playmaker led Chelsea for chances created (two) but was far from his best, and his loss of temper proved costly.

Palmer's dismissal was the 100th red card Chelsea have been shown in the Premier League (excluding rescinded cards), with the Blues becoming the third team to reach this milestone, after Everton (113) and Arsenal (110).

Penders, meanwhile, had a full Premier League debut to forget, as he became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to score an own goal in the competition, after Petr Cech against Everton in December 2009.

w2bsx12fply21ob3lk2dnadul.subtitle: Mike Penders' full Premier League debut went badly on Saturday, as his calamitous fumble led to Tottenham beating Chelsea.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso and Maxence Lacroix rallied around Mike Penders following the goalkeeper's error in Chelsea's loss to Tottenham.
Chelsea went down 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, where Cole Palmer saw red.

Palmer's dismissal came just after Penders, who was making his first Premier League start due to Emiliano Martinez's absence, scored a calamitous own goal when he punched a corner back over his own line.
Lacroix tried to stop it getting over the line, but could not do so, and Chelsea's defeat was rounded off when Mathys Tel scored late on.
Penders became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to score an own goal in a Premier League match, after Petr Cech against Everton in December 2009.

At the age of 21 years and 85 days, the Belgian became the second-youngest goalkeeper to net a Premier League own goal, after Illan Meslier (20 years and 354 days) for Leeds United against Wolves in February 2021.
Alonso has backed Penders to regain his confidence, though. The Chelsea boss said: "It's part of the business; you need to deal with mistakes and we keep confidence in Mike.
14 - Since the start of March, Chelsea have lost more games in all competitions than any other side in Europe's big-five leagues (14).
"We win and we lose together and it's part of the job to deal with mistakes, myself as well as everyone.
"We support Mike and Geo [Quenda] as well, the guys starting their first [Premier League] games. He will want to prove he can do better, and we also have to show that."
Lacroix added: "He is a young goalkeeper and he has a lot of talent. He will learn from this. This can happen in football careers and in life.
"Everyone makes mistakes, and we have to be with him and we are going to be with him. We are behind him. He will help us this season and now we have to help him."
Penders is set to start again when Chelsea face Liverpool in the EFL Cup on Wednesday.

w4om5zym0avj1j3r66l0j1x0l.title: Neto dedicates Chelsea win to injured Martinez
w4om5zym0avj1j3r66l0j1x0l.subtitle: Pedro Neto's brace saw Chelsea defeat Everton, but the Blues saw goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez stretchered off at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
paragraphs: Pedro Neto dedicated Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton to injured goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.
The Blues won 2-0 at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday, with Neto scoring twice in the second half to seal all three points.
Chelsea have won nine of the last 10 Premier League games when Neto has scored (L1), with the Portuguese player netting his first ever brace in the competition (187th appearance).
This was also Chelsea’s first clean sheet in 23 Premier League matches, since a 2-0 home win against Brentford in January, though they had to endure a goalkeeper change in the second half.
Martinez was stretchered off in the 75th minute after sustaining a head injury following a collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite.
"We are really pleased. Shame for Emi [Martinez] but we wish you all the best. This win is for him," Neto told TNT Sports.
"We needed a clean sheet to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike [Penders] did as well.
"It's really important. We know it's tough to play away, even at home there are no easy games.
"We came here with personality, with good intentions to win the match and really happy with the result."
Everton had just six shots against Chelsea, their fewest in a Premier League game since last December against Arsenal (five).
The Toffees failed to score in a Premier League home game for the first time since February (1-0 against Manchester United).
Everton conceded in the opening minute of the second half before some poor defending led to Neto's second in the 90th minute.
"We knew the way they were going to get wide and pull the ball back a lot. In the first half, we dealt with that well," Everton defender James Tarkowski told Evertontv.
"We didn't manage to do that [for the first goal]. We didn't manage to get numbers back in the box – and we got punished for it.
"The second goal, it feels a bit flukey at the time – to defend a free-kick so well initially, and then to fall at their lad's foot.
"We got punished, and it's a shame because I didn't think there was a lot in the game."

w4tlhtfp5huo11h5lb72ixdxq.title: Wiegman not focused on expiring England contract
w4tlhtfp5huo11h5lb72ixdxq.subtitle: Sarina Wiegman's contract as England boss expires after next year's Women's World Cup, but her focus is on qualifying for the tournament.
paragraphs: England boss Sarina Wiegman insisted her focus is on qualifying for next year's Women's World Cup and not on her expiring contract.
The Lionesses face Greece in a two-legged play-off semi-final, with the winner facing either Slovakia or Ukraine for a spot in next summer's competition.
Wiegman has led England to back-to-back European Championship titles so far during her tenure, while also reaching the World Cup final in 2023.

She is the first-ever men's or women's manager to reach five consecutive major international tournament finals, after also reaching the showpiece in both competitions during her time with the Netherlands.
Despite her contract with the Lionesses ending after the World Cup, Wiegman's full focus is on qualifying for the tournament.
"We had conversations before," said Wiegman when asked if talks had taken place about a possible extension.
"We have regular conversations together, and we talk about the future, but at this point I'm just really focusing on Greece, and we want to get through and qualify for the World Cup.
"I talk to Mark [Bullingham, FA CEO] every two weeks, and we speak about what's happening now, what's in the future, but there's no news now.
"I'm just focusing on Greece and hopefully the World Cup."
England were forced into the play-off rounds after finishing second in their qualifying group, which also featured Spain, Iceland and Ukraine.
The Lionesses finished level on 15 points with Spain, the reigning world champions, but missed out on top spot due to head-to-head after losing 4-0 to their rivals.

w6gh3flamwa117m0ohtrqzngo.title: The Numbers Game: Can Tuchel shore up England's defence against Czechia?
w6gh3flamwa117m0ohtrqzngo.subtitle: After opening their Nations League campaigns, Czechia and England are looking to pick up their first three points of 2026-27 on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Both Czechia and England stumbled at the first Nations League hurdle, losing their games to Croatia and Spain, respectively.
England played out a five-goal thriller with Spain but ended up on the wrong side of the result after throwing away a lead to eventually lose 3-2.
As for Czechia, they were undone by Luka Modric, who rolled back the years to help Croatia to a 2-1 victory.
That leaves both nations on zero points in Group A3, but neither will want to still be empty-handed with a third of their group games gone.
So, who will come out on top at Fortuna Arena? Here, using Opta data, we look at the key talking points ahead of Tuesday's clash.
Both teams will already feel this is a must-win fixture given the thick-and-fast nature of the Nations League campaign, and it is England who are expected to come out on top.
England have lost just one of their last nine meetings with Czechia in all competitions (W6 D2).
However, that loss came on their last visit to the nation back in October 2019 (2-1).
They are given a 68.8% chance of victory when they head to Prague, with a further 18.7% chance of a draw.
Only three teams have won consecutive home matches against England this century: Spain (a run of three), France and Sweden (both two).
Czechia will be looking to add their names to that list, but they are given just a 12.4% chance of coming away with all three points.
Will Tuchel fix defensive frailties?

England went through a rollercoaster of emotions at Wembley; a Marc Guehi error inside two minutes gave Lamine Yamal the opener, but Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both scored to give the Three Lions a half-time lead.
Momentum then swung on a missed Kane penalty, with Alex Baena – profiting from Nico O'Reilly's slack pass – and Mikel Oyarzabal coming off the bench to secure all three points for Spain.
A lot has been made about England's identity over this international break and how they can bring the best out of their players, especially defensively.
And it is at the back that Thomas Tuchel will be keen to shore things up, and soon.
That match was the first time England have made two errors leading to a goal in a competitive game since June 2019 against the Netherlands, also in the Nations League.
England have conceded 13 goals in their last six games, almost double the amount they had in their first 17 under Tuchel (seven).
In fact, they have conceded at least three goals in their last two outings, having also beaten France 6-4 to secure third place at the World Cup, last doing so in three in a row in February 1927.
It is a stark contrast to early in Tuchel's reign when England went through qualifying for the summer's tournament without conceding a single goal.

Their recent run means that England have lost two of their last three matches in all competitions – also the heartbreaking 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final – as many as in their previous 23 combined.

wav3ntlc08wp1cze3r7eqqlqe.title: Gasperini thrilled with 'clarity and order' from 10-man Roma
wav3ntlc08wp1cze3r7eqqlqe.subtitle: Roma were forced to defend hard to secure a point against Como on Sunday, after Donyell Malen was sent off in the second half.
paragraphs: Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini praised the "clarity and order" his side showed in defence after being reduced to 10 men in Sunday's 0-0 draw with Como.
Roma missed the chance to reclaim top spot in Serie A after Donyell Malen was sent off in the 53rd minute for a late challenge on Kaiki, though Como could not make the most of their advantage.
Malen had earlier struck the side netting while attempting to round Jean Butez, while Paulo Dybala saw a tame first-time effort saved by the Como goalkeeper.

Lorenzo Pellegrini also struck the post with a superb curling effort before the break, while Como pushed hard for a winner in the second, with Pierluigi Gollini denying a strong Nico Paz snap-shot before Jesus Rodriguez fired wide of the target.
"This is our disappointment, because I clearly don't know how the match would have ended, but it seemed to me like we were pretty confident we had a good chance," Gasperini told reporters.
"So we were forced to defend, and we did so with great clarity and order. It's clear that when you play 30 minutes with ten men, you come away with a draw, and that's fine too.
"Unfortunately, I have to say that in the first half we had some excellent scoring opportunities.
"Como even had a couple of important ones, but I think we gave the impression we could take the lead.
"It's clear that if you play 30 minutes of 90 minutes with ten men, it means you've played two-thirds of the game against a strong team like Como with an even number of men."
Indeed, Roma's attack was certainly blunted on this occasion, with the Giallorossi managing just nine shots – their lowest in a Serie A match this season.

But Gasperini will take encouragement from another resolute defensive display, with Roma recording their fourth clean sheet of the campaign – more than any other Serie A side. In fact, the Giallorossi have not conceded a first-half goal in any of their last 11 league matches.

Como, meanwhile, have equalled their best-ever start to a Serie A campaign, adjusted for three points per win. Cesc Fabregas' side have collected 11 points from their opening six matches, matching their tally from 1950-51.
"We didn't make the most of the extra man, including with our possession, as we should’ve had more patience and moved the ball around faster," Fabregas conceded.
"This team is young, but still managed to avoid conceding any counter-attack situations, so in that sense it is positive."

wc2cwyh036qi111cc9o3y3hdj.title: Turkiye 0-1 France: Mbappe secures win on Zidane's debut
wc2cwyh036qi111cc9o3y3hdj.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe continued his scoring run for France, but it remains to be seen if he will be available next time out after going off injured.
paragraphs: Zinedine Zidane got off to a winning start as France coach, with Kylian Mbappe securing him a 1-0 win over Turkiye in their Nations League opener.

Mbappe found the breakthrough in the 54th minute but went off injured shortly after, and France could not add to his goal despite Turkiye goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir being shown an 87th-minute red card for a handball outside his box.

Turkiye almost stunned France just four minutes in as Baris Alper Yilmaz latched onto a long ball, only to be denied by Mike Maignan, who also sprang back up to deny Can Uzun before a belated offside flag went up.
Mbappe then scuffed an effort wide at the other end, while Rayan Cherki saw a low shot blocked by Merih Demiral as France struggled to break through Turkiye's defence.
Michael Olise forced a stretching save out of Cakir in France's best chance of the first half, and Adrien Rabiot then blazed over from the resulting corner.

Les Bleus made a sluggish start to the second half, though, and could have been behind in the 50th minute, but Maignan reacted brilliantly to push the unmarked Ismail Yuksek's diving header over the crossbar.

And just four minutes later, Mbappe broke the deadlock. Turkiye lost possession deep in their own half, and Olise immediately switched it to the France captain, who drilled past Cakir from the left of the box.
However, he hurt himself in the process, immediately pulling up, and he lasted just five more minutes before he was substituted off.
Mbappe's replacement, Desire Doue, saw a long-range curler pushed away while Jules Kounde hit the foot of the left post after sitting Uzun down in the box.

Turkiye kept pushing for an equaliser, with Maignan standing tall at his near post to keep out Guler, but France finished with all the momentum after Cakir was sent off when he rushed out of his box to smother Bradley Barcola's run and the ball hit his outstretched arm.
Mbappe matches his own record but gives Zidane a worry

The last thing France – and Real Madrid fans – wanted to see was Mbappe exiting the pitch after receiving medical attention. While it may have been precautionary, the France captain looked uncomfortable.
He made his mark before he had to go off though, netting the first goal of the Zidane era and getting France off to a perfect start in the competition.
Mbappe scored his 12th goal for France in 2026, equalling the highest total for a Les Bleus player in a single calendar year in the 21st century, matching his own record from 2022.

France were far from their free-flowing best despite having a lot of their big hitters on the pitch as they accumulated 1.21 expected goals (xG) from 12 attempts, only slightly more than Turkiye's 1.14 xG from 12 shots.

Guler tried to work some magic for Turkiye, who are set to come up against it with Italy and Belgium also in their group, having three shots – a game high – while also creating three chances and having 88 touches, more than any of his team-mates.

wcgdtzwvo9ki1ug2m77dsxo9z.title: New York Red Bulls 2-0 Inter Miami: Messi unable to spark comeback after Casemiro own goal
wcgdtzwvo9ki1ug2m77dsxo9z.subtitle: Inter Miami's three-game winning run in MLS came to an end after a lacklustre performance against the New York Red Bulls.
paragraphs: Casemiro scored an own goal as Inter Miami fell to a 2-0 defeat against the New York Red Bulls in MLS.

Lionel Messi was unable to make an impact off the bench after Casemiro's early mistake, while Emil Forsberg secured all three points for the hosts late on as the Herons saw their three-game winning run snapped.

Julian Hall should have opened the scoring with the first shot of the game, turning Cade Cowell's cut-back past the left post, but it mattered little as another low cross from Cowell in the seventh minute was turned into his own net by Casemiro.

Hall missed another great opportunity in the 18th minute as he headed over from inside the six-yard box, despite having an unguarded goal in front of him, while Jorge Ruvalcaba missed a carbon copy of Hall's first chance on the stroke of half-time.
Messi was introduced off the bench after a quiet start to the second half, but NYRB's dominance, and wastefulness, continued as Ruvalcaba was twice denied while one-on-one with Dayne St. Clair.
Miami's best chances came in the 84th minute, but Santiago Morales was kept out by Ethan Horvath after an inch-perfect pass from Messi, while Telasco Segovia's rebound cannoned back off the crossbar.

An experienced presence in Forsberg then wrapped things up in the 91st minute, scoring a simple tap-in after Cameron Harper intercepted a poor pass from St. Clair and squared it to the Swedish midfielder.
Worrying signs for Miami
Despite the Red Bulls eventually scoring a second, the scoreline is still a flattering one for Miami, who were second-best from minute one to 90 at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
NYRB accumulated 3.31 expected goals (xG) from 19 shots, five of which were Opta-defined big chances, while restricting Miami to just 0.81 from their 12 attempts.
Both Hall and Ruvalcaba will be wondering how they did not get on the scoresheet, with the pair responsible for 1.92 of the Red Bulls' xG and four of their five big chances.

Ruvalcaba led NYRB in xG (1.34), shots (six), touches in the box (seven) and big chances (three), and Michael Bradley will acknowledge his side could have been punished on another day by the likes of Messi and Luis Suarez.

However, on this occasion, Suarez registered two shots worth just 0.09 xG, while Messi recorded one shot and created two chances off the bench, with Miami now turning their attention to a home clash with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday.

wffvfp0b1hzw1gh7ni93aiv2a.title: Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea (6-5 pens): Fofana miss costs Alonso on Anfield return
wffvfp0b1hzw1gh7ni93aiv2a.subtitle: It was Liverpool who emerged victorious from a dramatic penalty shoot-out against Chelsea, booking their spot in the EFL Cup quarter-finals.
paragraphs: Wesley Fofana missed the decisive penalty as Liverpool defeated Chelsea 6-5 in a dramatic EFL Cup shoot-out, following a 1-1 draw in Wednesday's fourth-round tie.
Spot-kicks were central throughout the contest, with Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo both scoring from 12 yards within the space of three first-half minutes.

After an end-to-end second half, the drama continued into the shoot-out with Kostas Tsimikas and Emmanuel Emegha both missing chances to win it for their respective teams, the latter on his Chelsea debut.

And after a rocket of a kick from Joe Gomez found the top-right corner, Fofana sent his effort spiralling into the Kop, dropping Xabi Alonso to defeat on his first return to Anfield since taking the Chelsea job.

Rogers saw an early penalty appeal fall on deaf ears, but referee Darren England did point to the spot in the 38th minute, when Moises Caicedo got goal-side of Ryan Gravenberch and was clattered from behind by the Dutchman.

With Cole Palmer suspended following his red card against Tottenham on Saturday, it was Rogers who converted into the right side of the goal, after a brief moment in which it appeared former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson might take the kick.
But the Reds had a penalty of their own shortly after Rogers' goal, with Gakpo finding the bottom-left corner after Fofana inexplicably handled from a corner.

Mike Penders made two excellent saves as Liverpool dialled up the pressure after half-time, keeping out a bullet header from Ronald Araujo and tipping a strike from Bradley Barcola around the post, moments after the Frenchman came on alongside Florian Wirtz.

Chelsea continued to carry a threat, with Giorgi Mamardashvili getting down brilliantly to thwart Marco Palestra following a powerful run from Rogers, though they may not have made it to the shoot-out, if not for Levi Colwill making a heroic block in front of Wirtz.

After seven perfect kicks, Valentin Barco's effort bounced off the inside of the post but Tsimikas – who scored the decisive spot-kick when the teams met in the 2022 FA Cup final – blazed wildly over when presented with the chance to win the tie for Liverpool.
After Henderson made light of the Kop's boos to send it to sudden death, Emegha failed to punish Gravenberch for his saved kick, and it was Fofana who made the all-important error for Chelsea.
Penalties galore at Anfield

The fact that Wednesday's game was decided from the spot should have come as a surprise to nobody – five of the last 10 meetings between Liverpool and Chelsea, across all competitions, have finished level (three Liverpool wins, two Chelsea wins).

In regulation time, two players who relish playing in the EFL Cup kept their composure from 12 yards. Rogers now has 11 goal involvements in the EFL Cup overall (six goals, five assists) – he is the only player with at least five goals and five assists in the competition since 2023-24.

Gakpo's 11 goals in the EFL Cup, meanwhile, are the most of any player since the start of 2023-24. His successful spot-kick maintained his 100% scoring record when appearing in the competition at Anfield – he has netted in all seven such games (eight goals in total).

Both of those players were also on target in the shoot-out, but the same could not be said of Barco, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Emegha and Fofana as Liverpool – just as they did in both domestic cup finals in 2021-22 – inflicted penalty woe on the Blues.

wh34n2kgjnf011d7yilj0rt8y.title: Klopp insists Germany's defeat to Greece is 'part of the process'
wh34n2kgjnf011d7yilj0rt8y.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's first home match as Germany boss ended in a 1-0 defeat to Greece, though he believes there is no reason to panic.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp insisted Germany's defeat to Greece in the Nations League is "part of the process", as he took responsibility for the team selection.
Germany lost 1-0 at WWK Arena after substitute Dimitrios Kourbelis' deflected strike in the 74th minute was enough to see the visitors maintain their perfect start to Group A2.

Klopp's side won the expected goals (xG) battle 1.27 to 0.72, dominated possession (75.8%) and recorded twice as many shots as Greece (16 to eight), though could not find their way past Konstantinos Tzolakis, who made five saves.
Germany's new-look front four featured Younes Ebnoutalib, Bambase Conte and Kevin Scahde, though it was a familiar face in Karim Adeyemi who led the way in shots (three) and chances created (four).
After a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands in their campaign opener, Klopp is still waiting for his first win since succeeding Julian Nagelsmann, though the former Liverpool boss is far from concerned.
"It's part of the process. Absolutely," said Klopp after the defeat.
"The lineup, the composition, the substitutions: that's all one hundred percent my responsibility.
"It was clear that we wouldn't completely dismantle a deep-lying Greek opponent, especially in key moments where we perhaps lacked a bit of luck or their outstanding goalkeeper was there.
"I could have lived with not winning the game by a large margin, or even not winning at all, but you can't afford to lose it.
"We've only been together for a week, we're facing a deep-lying opponent, we're a newly assembled team, and then we need to have our systems in place.
"I'm sorry that the euphoria has somehow subsided... For me, that's not a problem; I just know that football needs training, football needs routines."
Germany face Serbia next on Thursday before their return fixture against Greece on October 4.

whxh6uzvhg7k1rgrx525fdhvq.title: Fernandes criticises Man Utd's pressing tactics in heavy Como loss
whxh6uzvhg7k1rgrx525fdhvq.subtitle: Bruno Fernandes was frustrated with Manchester United's pressing versus Como, while Michael Carrick said the performance was "unacceptable".
paragraphs: Bruno Fernandes was critical of Manchester United's tactics after they slumped to a disappointing 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.
Nico Paz was the star of the show for Como as he got two goals and an assist, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon also hitting the back of the net in a stellar performance.

Joshua Zirkzee scored a stoppage-time consolation, but it was too late to stop United from stretching their winless streak to seven games in all competitions (D3 L4) for the first time since a run of eight between November and December 2015.
United struggled to match Como's intensity, especially after conceding in the second minute for the second consecutive Champions League match.
And Fernandes, who was substituted off in the 67th minute for Zirkzee, seemingly hit out at Michael Carrick's tactics following the loss.

When asked by TNT Sports about a lack of cohesion in the team's pressing, Fernandes replied: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball.

"But sometimes, when you give too much [of] the ball to these teams, they get confident; they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then, obviously, when you recover the ball, [with] the legs and the brain [it is] much more difficult to make it work."
Pressed on whether the wrong tactical decision was made, Fernandes added: "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it; it's not on me.
"I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable – as they did to us.
"The centre-back was coming to mark me all the way into my own half. Sometimes we had to do that as a team, and we were not really able to do it.

"A team that likes to play through the middle and likes these small connections. If you give them too much time on the ball to think, and to rotate on the middle of the pitch, they create a big space on the outside; that's what they did. The goal – the first one – comes from that."
The comments were then posed to Carrick in his post-match press conference.
"We actually were half-pressed man-to-man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that," Carrick said.
"And whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."
United have failed to win any of their first six away games of a campaign (D3 L3) for the first time since 2014-15, when Carrick played in the sixth game against Manchester City (0-1).
The Red Devils have only won two games in 2026-27, with their last victory coming on MD1 of the Champions League against Sabah on September 10.
"It was more than disappointing," Carrick, who was seen apologising to supporters at the full-time whistle, told TNT Sports. "I think everybody has got to take responsibility for that.
"I 100% take responsibility for the overall team and the performance – that's where it stops. It stops with me, and I'm absolutely fine with that.
"I accept that totally. But as a supporter of this football club for so long, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say.

"It was nowhere near good enough in so many ways. We didn't deserve to get anything from the game. I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters. They are the heartbeat of this football club, and they always will be.
"For them to travel, I had to apologise for the performance. To have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them.
"There are no excuses at all. It is not acceptable. It's not about me. It's about digesting the game and how it went. That is the most important thing right now."

wj6ite446b0b1ieip0ymjflzu.title: Ngumoha becoming a more 'complete player' for Liverpool, says Iraola
wj6ite446b0b1ieip0ymjflzu.subtitle: Liverpool maintained their perfect start in the Champions League with a comeback win over Villarreal, with Rio Ngumoha starring at Anfield.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola believes Rio Ngumoha is becoming a more "complete player" for Liverpool after starring in their 4-3 win over Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday.
Ngumoha produced a stunning display with assists for Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister in either half, but Liverpool had things far from their own way at Anfield.
Villarreal capitalised on some poor Liverpool defending to go two goals up by the 29th minute, with Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona ruthlessly punishing those errors.
But the Reds hauled themselves level before the break, with Mac Allister heading in Kostas Tsimikas' corner before Araujo charged in at the back post to nod home the equaliser.
An outrageous touch and cross from Ngumoha teed up Mac Allister's second in the 65th minute, with substitute Florian Wirtz netting his first goal of the season soon after.
Tani Oluwaseyi's 87th-minute finish threatened a nervy finish, but Liverpool were able to hold on and make it three wins from three to start their Champions League campaign.

But the standout performance came from Ngumoha, who at 18 years and 52 days old, became the third-youngest player to provide multiple assists in a Champions League game behind Warren Zaire-Emery against AC Milan in 2023 (17y 231d) and Theo Walcott against Hamburg in 2006 (17y 250d).

On record since 2003-04, Ngumoha is also just the fourth player to complete 7+ dribbles in multiple Champions League games as a teenager (two), along with Lamine Yamal (four), Cristiano Ronaldo (three) and Arjen Robben (two), with Iraola lauding the talented teenager.
"I am really happy with Rio. He is trying to improve everything that we try to correct," he told Amazon Prime. "He is playing a lot more on the right and he has adapted really well.
"He's going more inside. He struggled defensively in the first half. The second half was much better. He's becoming a more complete player. He's still only 18.
"In the first half, they were overloading the middle. We decided to put Ryan [Gravenberch] at right-back and be more of a threat working with Rio. I value Ryan a lot.
"We decided to try a bit more one-sided, help more on the left. From there, we finished the first half well and started the second half really well."

Ngumoha's display also saw him become the youngest player on record since 2008-09 to complete 5+ dribbles (seven), have 10+ touches in the opposition box (12) and register an assist (two) in a Champions League match, but he was quick to praise Liverpool's spirit in their comeback.

All four times Liverpool have been two goals down at home in major European competition inside the opening 29 minutes, they have gone on the win the game, while they won a match in the competition in which they were two goals down for the second time, previously doing so against Villarreal in the semi-finals in May 2022.

The Reds have now avoided defeat in five of their six games in all competitions this season in which they have conceded the opening goal (W3 D2 L1), already more than across the entirety of 2025-26 (W2 D2 L18) under Arne Slot.
Liverpool are only one of two teams with nine points from three games in this year's league phase along with holders Paris Saint-Germain, who beat Barcelona 4-2 on MD3.
Ngumoha is yet to score for Liverpool this season, but he said his performance against Villarreal has provided the perfect platform to be more ruthless in front of goal.
"It was a top performance from the boys. We were two goals down but the mentality was always there. We knew we were going to win," Ngumoha added.
"It's up there with one of the best I've played. I enjoyed myself and the team helped me a lot.
"Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one v one or two v one, I believe in myself. I'll just keep going and be ruthless.

wm2lyh9f5k8c1e855n74q2xo2.title: Celta Vigo 1-2 Juventus: Kolo Muani heads in stoppage-time winner
wm2lyh9f5k8c1e855n74q2xo2.subtitle: Despite struggling to create many clear-cut chances against Celta Vigo, Juventus won their Europa League encounter in stoppage time.
paragraphs: Juventus left it late to remain top of the Europa League table after Randal Kolo Muani scored a 92nd-minute winner in the Bianconeri's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo.
The Serie A giants found themselves 1-0 down heading into the break after Hugo Alvarez's opener, but Nick Woltemade volleyed Luciano Spalletti's side level in the second half.
And in the dying moments, Andrea Cambiaso's cross into the box was headed home by Kolo Muani in the dying minutes to snatch all three points at Estadio Abanca-Balaidos.
Celta scored with just their second shot as they worked the ball across the box before Williot Swedberg teed up Alvarez for an easy finish from close range in the 18th minute.

Woltemade squandered a good chance to equalise before half-time, blazing over from close range, but he restored parity just before the hour mark with a fine volley into the bottom-right corner after Marcos Alonso inexplicably tried to control a cross on his chest but instead set up the striker.

Javi Rueda fired into the side-netting soon after, despite his team-mates pleading for a cut-back in the box, while Nico Gonzalez curled agonisingly wide of the left post at the other end in the 88th minute.
However, Spalletti's side conjured up one more chance, with Kolo Muani sending Cambiaso's cross through the legs of Ionut Radu to break the hearts of the home fans.
Struggling strikers ease pressure on Spalletti

Juve fans have been calling for Antonio Conte to be reappointed in recent weeks after a poor start to the season under Spalletti, but summer signings Woltemade and Kolo Muani, who have come under plenty of criticism themselves, stepped up for their head coach.

Woltemade scored his second Europa League goal for the Bianconeri, which helped inspire a comeback from the visitors, while Kolo Muani has now scored two in two across all competitions as both strikers found their scoring touch at an important time.

Juve (1.7) accumulated more expected goals (xG) than Celta (1.02), which comes as no surprise after they recorded 22 shots to the Spanish side's nine and had over twice as many touches in the opposition box (46 to 17).
Spalletti will hope this serves as a confidence booster for his side, who won after trailing for the first time since November 2025 in a home match against Cagliari in Serie A.
The Bianconeri remain perfect in the Europa League this season nonetheless, sitting in top spot after two matchdays – ahead of Bayer Leverkusen on goals scored.

wm5894nwfatt1edlf69baichy.title: Le Bris embracing Europa League challenge after comeback win over Torreense
wm5894nwfatt1edlf69baichy.subtitle: Sunderland left it late to maintain their perfect start to their Europa League campaign, with Noah Sadiki's goal seeing off Torreense.
paragraphs: Regis Le Bris insisted he was enjoying every single second of Sunderland's Europa League campaign after they left it late to beat Torreense at Estadio Dr. Magalhaes Pessoa.
Sunderland made it two wins from two in Europe on Thursday as Noah Sadiki's 93rd-minute winner ensured the Black Cats survived a scare against their second-tier opponents.
Torreense had taken the lead just before half-time through a stunning strike from Volnei Feltes, with the defender ending his driving run with a curling finish past Robin Roefs.
However, the Premier League side hit back in the 67th minute when Jules Ahoka headed into the bottom-right corner after being teed up by substitute Nordi Mukiele's delivery.
And just as though the spoils looked set to be shared, Granit Xhaka's lay-off was thumped in at Lucas Paes' near post by Sadiki, sending the travelling fans into ecstasy.

Sunderland became the first English team to score a 90th-minute winning goal in the Europa League since Manchester United against Rangers in January 2025, and first away from home since Wolves at Besiktas in October 2019.
And despite their struggles in the Premier League, with Sunderland 17th with four points from their first six matches, Le Bris is embracing the challenge of European competition.
"We're back in Europe 53 years later and winning this game right at the end is very special. It is a symbol, and important, I think, for many reasons," Le Bris said.
"The first one is for our club and our fans. They were fantastic once again.
"Also, we are growing up, and we need these experiences, and I think the team showed this belief until the very end. It is important for us to show this mindset.
"We like it. We are looking forward to the next game, and I think we earned this opportunity [European football] last season.
"I'm enjoying every single second. It's going to be challenging and demanding but exciting as well. We want to embrace the challenge."

The first half saw just four shots attempted by both sides combined (one for Torreense, three for Sunderland), the fewest in the first half of a Europa League game involving an English team since Arsenal vs Qarabag in December 2018 (four).

But Sunderland found their groove in the second half, with seven of the Black Cats' eight goals in major European competition scored in the second half, including all three in this season's Europa League.

At 20 years and 160 days, Ahoka became the third African player under the age of 21 to score for an English club in the Europa League, along with Ademola Lookman for Everton (20 years, 48 days in December 2017) and Amad Diallo for Man United in March 2021 (18 years, 243 days).
Sadiki, meanwhile, picked the perfect time to score his first Sunderland goal, though he acknowledged the difficulties his team had to face against Torreense.
"I'm really happy for the team because we showed great mentality today. We were down but we came back," Sadiki told UEFA.com
"That's what we needed to do, and now we focus on the next game. Granit Xhaka told me to shoot. I didn't think twice. I was waiting for it. I'm really happy.

"But they made it really difficult for us, even though people considered us favourites before the game. I'm really happy for them because they showed what it means to play in the Europa League, even though they're in the second division.
"You don't have to be scared of the big teams. So they played really well, but unfortunately for them, we won."

At 20 years and 160 days, Ahoka became the third African player under the age of 21 to score for an English club in the Europa League, along with Ademola Lookman for Everton (20 years, 48 days in December 2017) and Amad Diallo for Man United in March 2021 (18 years, 243 days).

Sadiki, meanwhile, picked the perfect time to score his first Sunderland goal, though he acknowledged the difficulties his team had to face against Torreense. 

"I'm really happy for the team because we showed great mentality today. We were down but we came back," Sadiki told UEFA.com

"That's what we needed to do, and now we focus on the next game. Granit Xhaka told me to shoot. I didn't think twice. I was waiting for it. I'm really happy.

"But they made it really difficult for us, even though people considered us favourites before the game. I'm really happy for them because they showed what it means to play in the Europa League, even though they're in the second division.

"You don't have to be scared of the big teams. So they played really well, but unfortunately for them, we won."

wngeyza7njkl1f8bnmelp2i13.title: Hinshelwood delighted to score on injury return for Brighton
wngeyza7njkl1f8bnmelp2i13.subtitle: Brighton began their Conference League campaign with a big win over Kauno Zalgiris, with Jack Hinshelwood getting on the scoresheet.
paragraphs: Jack Hinshelwood expressed his delight after returning from injury to score in Brighton's Conference League win over Kauno Zalgiris.
Participating in European competition for just the second time, Brighton started their Conference League campaign with a 4-0 win at the Amex Stadium.
Georginio Rutter broke the deadlock in the 41st minute before also assisting Hinshelwood before half-time, and the Frenchman scored again after the break before Matt O'Riley wrapped up the win.

It was as dominant a performance as Fabian Hurzeler could have hoped for, with the Seagulls producing 4.02 expected goals (xG) from 35 shots while restricting their opponents to just 0.04 from four attempts.
In-form midfielder Pascal Gross created nine chances, the most by a player for a Premier League side since Martin Odegaard created 10 for Arsenal against Man Utd in January 2025.

Only Barcelona (43) and Bayern Munich (30) have scored more goals in all competitions this season than Brighton (29) among clubs in Europe's big-five leagues, and Hinshelwood was glad to return after an ankle injury.
"It's nice to just be back with the boys," he told TNT Sports.
"They have been on such a good run, and I have really missed it out there, so to be back out there tonight, fighting for this badge which I love doing is the main thing tonight.
"Fair play to Kauno Zalgiris, they came and made it difficult for us. We had to stay patient and I think we did that well.
"Georginio with a great goal and then to set me up as well he done really well. I think it was a really professional performance, we had to work for it, but it was a job well done."
Brighton's fourth goal was assisted by 18-year-old debutant Younes Ibrahim, who earned high praise from Hinshelwood.
"Shout out to Younes for coming on for his debut," added Hinshelwood.
"He has been training really well and he deserved it. He has a good attitude and is a good lad."

wr6gl8v1zsss1qwbwzekpnd0a.title: Zirkzee replaces injured Brobbey in Netherlands' Nations League squad
wr6gl8v1zsss1qwbwzekpnd0a.subtitle: Brian Brobbey's injury against Germany has seen him withdraw from the Netherlands squad, with Joshua Zirkzee called up to replace him.
paragraphs: The Netherlands have confirmed Joshua Zirkzee will link up with Xavi's squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures following an injury to Brian Brobbey.
Brobbey was replaced in the 35th minute by Mexx Meerdink during Thursday's 1-1 draw with Germany, an incident which led to Felix Nmecha opening the scoring.
Cody Gakpo was able to salvage a point with a stoppage-time leveller at Johan Cruijff Arena, but Xavi has been forced into making an early change to his squad.
The in-form Sunderland striker looked in visible discomfort as he left the pitch, clutching his hamstring, though the Netherlands did not disclose the severity of the injury.
It offers the chance for Zirkzee to impress new Netherlands boss Xavi, with the Manchester United forward set to make his first appearance for his nation since November 2024.
Zirkzee has accumulated six caps for the Netherlands since making his debut against Turkiye in July two years ago.
The Netherlands sit third in Group A2 following the first round of fixtures, with Greece at the top of the table following their 2-1 victory against Serbia away from home.
Serbia are the Netherlands' next opponents this Sunday, before the Oranje travel to Greece and welcome Serbia to Philips Stadion on October 4.

wwsxwpitejpr1pe68fx5hxdni.title: Corbeanu rallies Toronto, insisting 'season's not over'
wwsxwpitejpr1pe68fx5hxdni.subtitle: Both Toronto FC and D.C. United are sitting outside the playoff places, with their fates out of their own hands with three games left.
paragraphs: Toronto FC forward Theo Corbeanu insists their season is not over as they prepare to host D.C. United, with their MLS playoff hopes hanging in the balance.
With three games of the regular season remaining, Toronto sit 11th, three points behind ninth-place New York Red Bulls, with their fate seemingly out of their own hands.
Having lost three straight games in September, the Reds have lost just one of their four matches since (W2 D1), though it was a damaging 4-2 loss to the Columbus Crew last time out.
That defeat could prove to be costly in the playoff race, but Corbeanu is not ready to give up the fight just yet.
"There's three games, so our season's not over," he said.
"Although [the Columbus game] was obviously an extremely important game, and we didn't get the job done, there's three games.

"I think if we can play our best football in these three games and finish off on a high, continue our belief and fight until the end and replicate some of the good things that we were able to display [against the Crew], I'm pretty sure we can put ourselves in a respectable position.
"Whatever that is, I don't know, but we have another game against D.C. on Wednesday; that's the only focus right now."
D.C. are also sitting outside the playoff positions, though they sit three points further back from Toronto, leaving them in an even more precarious position.
Back-to-back defeats in a double-header to FC Cincinnati have stretched D.C.'s losing streak to three games, and they have won just one of their last eight in MLS.
Rene Weiler has injuries to contend with, which is making it hard for him to rotate in a hectic schedule, and he acknowledged they have a tough task ahead of them.
"Of course, we're going to find a solution, but the squad is really tight right now," he said.
"I think it's almost impossible to qualify for the playoffs, but we will find a solution."
Toronto FC – Daniel Salloi
Daniel Salloi is Toronto's leading scorer with nine goals, three of which have been the tone-setting first of the match.
He also leads the way for assists (seven) among his team-mates and has had a hand in three goals across his last three MLS matches (two goals, one assist).
D.C. United – Brandon Servania
D.C. have failed to score in 10 of their 31 MLS games this season, including last time out against FC Cincinnati, but it was not for lack of trying.
Brandon Servania had a game-high five shots in that match, though he only managed to get one on target, as his search for a first league goal of the season went on.
MATCH PREDICTION: TORONTO FC WIN
Toronto have won just two of their last MLS clashes with D.C. (D3 L3), though both of their victories came on home soil.
And Robin Fraser will be hoping his side's home form carries them through again, as they have lost just two of their 16 matches at BMO Field in 2026 (W5 D9).
In fact, they are looking to extend their unbeaten streak on home soil to eight games.
By contrast, D.C., who did beat Toronto 2-1 in the reverse fixture in July, have struggled for form on the road, earning just two away wins all season (D7 L6).

wz74yrwefqx51qjd8me0jg35b.title: Maresca: Man City 'have to be more lucky' after Villa defeat
wz74yrwefqx51qjd8me0jg35b.subtitle: Man City boss Enzo Maresca believes his side deserved more from their 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca believes Manchester City were unfortunate not to win against Aston Villa on Saturday, believing his side "sometimes have to be more lucky."
City were handed their first defeat of the Premier League season, ending their perfect start, as Nicolas Jackson's brace condemned them to a 2-1 loss at Villa Park.

Jackson smartly capitalised on some very sloppy Man City defending in both of his goals, first making the most of Marc Guehi's cheap turnover in the sixth minute, before then seeing his reared shot squeeze past Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Erling Haaland sparked the possibility of a comeback as he levelled the scoreline in the 52nd minute, while Josko Gvardiol saw a good effort parried onto the crossbar as City looked to keep their strong start going.
“When we scored, I had the feeling the entire game we were in control," Maresca told BBC Match of the Day.
"We created many chances but sometimes we have to be more lucky. We considered just one transition the entire second half and unfortunately, they score.
"We struggled the first probably 10-15 minutes and we expected them in one way and they were in a different way. We adjusted and controlled the game.
“Even for us it was a good game, performance. Unfortunately, we lost but overall we did enough to deserve something more. We’ll learn from it and move on."

City were largely architects of their own downfall, though. Since the start of last season, only Jan Paul van Hecke (four) has made more errors leading to goals among Premier League outfield players than Guehi's three.

Donnarumma, meanwhile, has made three errors directly leading to goals in the competition since joining City last season, with only Bart Verbruggen (five) and Robin Roefs (four) committing more in that time among goalkeepers.
Moreover, having conceded just eight goals in their opening nine matches of the season across competitions, Maresca's side have now shipped nine in their last four outings.

In all, Saturday's defeat means three of City's last five Premier League losses have come at the hands of Villa, while they have lost four consecutive away league games against the same opponent for the first time since February 2023 against Tottenham.

wz7w239njetd1whvtv7no8ku1.title: Maguire: Man Utd players must look at themselves, not blame Carrick
wz7w239njetd1whvtv7no8ku1.subtitle: Jamie Carragher feels Manchester United must sack Michael Carrick, but Harry Maguire says it is time for the players to stand up.
paragraphs: Harry Maguire says Manchester United's players must look in the mirror and take responsibility for their dire results, admitting "something needs to change" at Old Trafford.
United's dreadful 2026-27 campaign hit a new low on Sunday as they were thumped 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford, following an error-strewn performance.

Rayan popped up totally unmarked to score Bournemouth's opening goal, Leny Yoro's slip led to Marcus Tavernier tapping home for 2-0, then Senne Lammens raced well off his line and was beaten by Evanilson for the Cherries' second-half clincher.
United have now gone eight games without a victory in all competitions (D3 L5) for the first time since December 2015.
Having not suffered back-to-back defeats at any stage of the 2025-26 season, the Red Devils have lost consecutive games twice during this run.
And, since the start of 2023-24, no Premier League team has lost more home games by a margin of at least three goals, across all competitions, than United (seven).

Their latest embarrassing result – which came with captain Bruno Fernandes watching on from the bench, following his public criticism of Michael Carrick's tactics – will only intensify the pressure on the United boss, but Maguire says the players are responsible.
"It wasn't good enough. We're disappointed to give a goal away so early – from another set-play – as conceding first in the Premier League makes it difficult," Maguire told Sky Sports.
"A mistake for the second goal makes it hard for ourselves. We didn't perform well enough as individuals or as a team and we didn't deserve anything from the game.
"It's not clicking at the moment. Results are not good enough and performances in the last week have not been good enough.

"It's still early in the season. You've got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror – that's the most important thing – and think what more you can contribute to the team. If we do that, we'll get somewhere."
Asked if he and his team-mates would hold talks about the situation, Maguire said: "If those conversations happen, they will remain private.
"We want to do more, to be better and get better results. At the moment, it's nowhere near good enough and something needs to change.
"Of course, you have to look after your own performances and take responsibility.
"This is a huge club and every day you have to prove why you're wearing this badge. At the moment, we're not doing enough as players.
"Michael turned our season on its head last year and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven't performed well enough as individuals."

With seven points on the board after eight games, United have made their worst start to a league season since 1986-87 (four points from seven matches), and former Liverpool centre-back Jamie Carragher believes Carrick's time is up.
Speaking in his role as a Sky Sports pundit, Carragher said: "Manchester United need to make that change tonight, they need to make that decision.
"The fans have taken the side of Michael Carrick and it's not about him being the manager, it's about him being a huge figure in United's history.
"Those players have done nothing compared to teams of the past, so Michael Carrick is always going to win that fight with Bruno Fernandes, and rightly so, no matter how talented a player he is.
"But also, Manchester United as a football club, one of the biggest in the world, are 16th in the Premier League right now and that can't continue.
"Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight – not just for the good of Manchester United, but also for the good of Michael Carrick.
"It's not nice watching him walking around the stadium at the end, he's really hurting and what's happening right now is not good for United and not good for Carrick."

x0mzan5qt69u1ll8ybllckjp9.title: Manchester United 2-1 West Ham: Terland and Medina hand Olid first WSL victory
x0mzan5qt69u1ll8ybllckjp9.subtitle: Eva Olid finally claimed her first Women's Super League victory as Manchester United survived a nervy ending to beat West Ham on Sunday.
paragraphs: Manchester United got their Women's Super League campaign up and running as goals from Elisabeth Terland and Andrea Medina clinched a 2-1 win over West Ham.
After failing to win their first three league fixtures, it proved to be the fourth time lucky for Eva Olid, with the Red Devils deserving of their first WSL triumph in 2026-27.
Terland needed just nine minutes at the Progress with Unity Stadium to give United the lead, with the Norwegian rising highest to head in Anna Sandberg's inviting corner.
Viviane Asseyi then squandered two chances to get West Ham level, with Ella Toone's strike from distance comfortably held by Constance Picaud-Inconnu at the other end.
Picaud-Inconnu then produced a stunning stop to tip Hanna Lundkvist's header over the crossbar, before Medina thundered against the woodwork early in the second half.

Terland then saw an attempt brilliantly saved down low by Picaud-Inconnu, but United's pressure eventually told in the 72nd minute when Medina picked out the top-right corner after seeing her initial effort blocked by Saki Kumagai.

But after United failed in their attempts to add further gloss to the scoreline, Asseyi was tripped inside the area by Sandberg, with the West Ham forward stepping up to send Phallon Tullis-Joyce the wrong way from 12 yards, though the Red Devils held on for the win.
Terland a head above the rest

United arrived into Sunday's clash with the threat of becoming only the second of the WSL's 'big four' teams to fail to win their first four games of the season, but they delivered a dominant display from start to finish, despite a late lapse in concentration.

They are now unbeaten in their last 13 league games against West Ham (W9 D4), with Terland's opener setting them on their way. Since her WSL debut in September 2022, only Khadija Shaw (31) has scored more headed goals in the competition than Terland (10).

United had attempted just 10 shots in the WSL this season ahead of facing the Hammers, and they bettered that in just one game here. They fired off 15 attempts, worth an expected goals (xG) value of 1.67, compared to West Ham's tally of 1.13 from their nine efforts.

Medina was the particular standout for the Red Devils, scoring her first goal for the club. She also finished with team-high totals for chances created (four), crosses (six), touches in the opposition box (11), and duels won (eight).

Medina was the particular standout for the Red Devils, scoring her first goal for the club. She also finished with team-high totals for chances created (four), crosses (six), touches in the opposition box (11), and duels won (eight).

x0x0bwhb5vw41xotvivelt5y4.title: PSG must stop Yamal if they want to beat Barcelona, says Luis Enrique
x0x0bwhb5vw41xotvivelt5y4.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona square off in the Champions League on Tuesday, with Lamine Yamal the player to watch for Luis Enrique.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique believes keeping the ball away from Lamine Yamal will prove crucial if Paris Saint-Germain are to get anything out of their blockbuster clash with Barcelona.
In what has been dubbed as the standout tie of the league phase of this year's Champions League, PSG and Barcelona lock horns at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday.
Both teams have enjoyed strong starts to their respective campaigns, with Hansi Flick's side winning all nine of their opening LaLiga fixtures to sit five points clear at the top.

They are the first team to do so since Real Madrid in 1968-69, while their 39 goals are the second-most by a team after their first nine matches in LaLiga, after the Sevilla team of 1940-41 plundered 42 goals.
And key to their early-season form has been Yamal, who has been tipped to challenge Bayern Munich's Harry Kane and Madrid's Kylian Mbappe for the Ballon d'Or this year.

Yamal grabbed a goal and an assist during Barcelona's 5-2 win away at Real Betis on Saturday, taking his tally to 19 goal involvements (nine goals, 10 assists) across all competitions in 2026-27, more than any other player from Europe's top five leagues.
The 19-year-old has already been involved in five goals in two Champions League appearances in 2026-27 (one goal, four assists), assisting two goals in each game.

He's the youngest player to assist 2+ goals in consecutive appearances (19 years, 92 days), while Raul in 2002 is the only player in Champions League history to assist 2+ goals in three games in a row.
And in his pre-match press conference, Luis Enrique acknowledged the threat Yamal will pose to his PSG team.
"The best way to stop Lamine Yamal is to keep the ball away from Barcelona," Luis Enrique told reporters.
"If he cannot get the ball, everything is calm. That would be ideal, but we know it won't be the case because it is difficult to play against Barcelona and Lamine Yamal.
"The way to defend a team with their quality is to be wary and approach it as a team. But it's not just Lamine. There's Raphinha, Pedri. There are a lot of top players."
The PSG boss did, however, push back on comparisons between Yamal and Lionel Messi, which have been a frequent occurrence since he made his debut for Barca in 2023.
"I think Lamine wants to be Lamine, and he is doing very well," Luis Enrique added.
"He is improving in every aspect of his game, but if you compare him with the best player ever, there will only be one winner.
"Maybe we can speak in the future about that, but right now, it is best not to compare him with Messi."

This will be the 17th time that PSG have faced Barcelona (W6 D4 L6), which will be the joint-most games they have played against an opponent in major European competitions (also 17 v Bayern Munich – W7 D1 L9), and Tuesday's clash could be one to remember.

Of all fixtures played 10+ times in European Cup or Champions League history, only Ajax versus Bayern (3.9) has a higher goals-per-game ratio than PSG versus Barcelona (3.8 – 57 goals in 15 meetings).

Flick's side have scored 4+ goals in four consecutive games in the league or group phase of this competition, the longest-ever run by a team in the European Cup or Champions League, while PSG are unbeaten in their last 12 games in the tournament (W8 D4).

"I'm focusing on their quality. I've played for and managed Barca, and I have a very close relationship with Catalonia," Luis Enrique said of Barcelona, who he managed between 2014 and 2017 and won the Champions League with in 2014-15.
"I'm very attached to Barca, but I'm PSG's manager. Initially, I struggled to play against Barca, but I've got used to it. They have top-quality players and a team with values.
"Despite that, I want to win tomorrow. It's a huge source of motivation for me to face the club that has mattered the most to me in my career."

The Spaniard was also asked whether the eagerly-anticipated clash was like the final had come early, to which he responded: "No, because this competition gives us the chance to play this kind of game [in the league phase].
"When we think about the rest of the competition, we're among the favourites, but there are several teams that can win it."

x6xbpdb7h4dk12hy7o2h904y9.title: Italy 'below expectations' against Belgium, laments Mancini
x6xbpdb7h4dk12hy7o2h904y9.subtitle: Roberto Mancini's first match back as Italy boss ended in a 2-0 defeat to Belgium, with the Azzurri jeered off at Stadio Olimpico.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes Italy's first-half performance against Belgium was "below expectations" and proved costly in their Nations League clash.
In their first match since Mancini's return to the helm, Italy lost 2-0 to Belgium at Stadio Olimpico after goals from Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio either side of half-time.
Italy have lost a home match while conceding at least two goals without scoring any for only the second time in the last 40 years, after a 2-0 defeat in a friendly against Croatia in August 2006.
The Azzurri ended the match with 1.5 expected goals (xG), though only 0.3 of their tally came in the first half, while Belgium accumulated 2.5 of their 2.7 xG before the break.
Gianluigi Donnarumma made six saves to try and inspire a comeback for Italy, but Senne Lammens also made six saves at the other end to keep Belgium in front.
While Mancini acknowledged Italy's improvements after the break, he admitted their first 45 minutes were not good enough.
"Belgium played better in the first half, we took the initiative in the second and could've equalised, but we conceded on a counter-attack with our error. This is football," Mancini told RAI Sport.
"The first half was below expectations, as Belgium played better, but not the second half.
"The team did really well until that second goal. We had four or five chances to equalise, we pinned them back, but Belgium are a strong side."
Italy, who have failed to qualify for each of the last three World Cups, were jeered off the pitch at full-time in Rome.
Riccardo Calafiori was "hurt" by the reaction of the fans and has urged his team-mates to focus on the positives from the defeat.

"They hurt, because at times I felt the passion of the crowd. We've got to do better, we all know that, starting from the next match," said Calafiori, who won possession eight times and created three chances.

"I saw a good team in fits and starts. We've just started working with a new coach, but other areas I didn't like, we left gaps and conceded two avoidable goals. We must try to look at the positive aspects.
"There is a lot of work to do, we've just started with a new coach, so we'll see."

xa2ituxo2nuf1np6uvcrllagz.title: Kompany insists Bayern 'not far off our best version'
xa2ituxo2nuf1np6uvcrllagz.subtitle: Bayern Munich have been off the pace so far in the Bundesliga, and Vincent Kompany's side face a tough test in RB Leipzig on Saturday.
paragraphs: Vincent Kompany believes Bayern Munich are "not far off our best version" ahead of their Bundesliga clash with RB Leipzig.
Kompany's words come despite a poor start to the season by Bayern's standards, which includes a 3-3 draw against Viking in the Champions League.
Bayern are enduring their worst start to a Bundesliga campaign in four years after taking just 11 points from their opening five games.
They have already dropped four points this season (W3 D2), as many as they gave up in the entire first half of the previous campaign (W15 D2).
Kompany's side are third in the early standings, two points and two places ahead of upcoming opponents Leipzig, who are brimming with confidence.
Leipzig have won three of their last four games across all competitions (L1), including a 6-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt and 5-0 victory over Hamburg in the league.
Kompany is wary of the threat posed by Leipzig, but he has complete faith in his Bayern side.
"We want to attack. We're playing at home. We're hungry," said the Belgian head coach.
"We know about Leipzig's strengths. You can see they've made a few changes. It's helped the team. They're coming here with confidence.
"We've had 50 shots on goal over the last two games. We've been doing lots of collective things well. If we do a few things better, then we're not far off our best version. We know we can do it.
"These games often come down to the quality on the pitch. They've got quick wide players and strong attackers. We also have that.
"They have defenders who also get involved in attack and a goalkeeper who's good on the ball. We also have that as well.
"They're games with a lot of creativity. If things start to go one way, then they can really go that way. Let's see what happens."
Bayern Munich – Harry Kane
Harry Kane is set to make his 100th Bundesliga appearance; his 101 goals are already a record for a player in their first 100 games in the competition.
He has provided three assists in his last three Bundesliga matches, including two against Augsburg, as many as he managed in his previous 31 appearances.
RB Leipzig – Christopher Nkunku
Christopher Nkunku scored his first Bundesliga hat-trick in his 124th appearance, which was also the first perfect hat-trick by a Leipzig player in the competition.
He has already scored three Bundesliga goals away to Bayern; only Dodi Lukebakio and Markus Rosenberg (four each) have scored more Bundesliga goals at the Allianz Arena as a visiting player.
MATCH PREDICTION: BAYERN MUNICH WIN
Bayern have the best attack in the Bundesliga this season, having scored 16 goals, while Leipzig have the second-best with 15 – a new club record for Leipzig after five games of a Bundesliga season.
Kompany's side have scored 12 goals in their first two home games of this Bundesliga season; only Frankfurt in 1976-77 (13) have ever scored more in their opening two home matches of a campaign.

Bayern have won each of their last three matches against Leipzig in all competitions, including the DFB-Pokal quarter-final in February this year; they last won four consecutive meetings between April 2021 and July 2022.
Leipzig have lost each of their last four Bundesliga away games, a run only bottom-placed Borussia Monchengladbach currently match in the league.
Leipzig boss Martin Demichelis made 259 appearances for Bayern between 2003 and 2010, winning the domestic double four times.

In the last 13 Bundesliga seasons, only two managers have won their first away game against Bayern at the Allianz Arena: Alfred Schreuder with Hoffenheim and Peter Bosz with Bayer Leverkusen, both in autumn 2019.
Bayern Munich – 73.9%
