xblzh5ci0yf31uqbnvsccynoz.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal's Nations League camp amid reports of rift
xblzh5ci0yf31uqbnvsccynoz.subtitle: Media reports suggested there was some tension in Portugal's camp between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo, who has now left the squad.
paragraphs: Cristiano Ronaldo announced he has left Portugal's Nations League squad ahead of their match against Denmark on Thursday.
Ronaldo started for Portugal in their 1-0 win over Wales in their opening game before being taken off in the 67th minute, but was an unused substitute in the 2-1 victory against Norway.
Following that game, there have been reports of a rift between Ronaldo and head coach Jorge Jesus, who had stated before the game that he planned to use the 41-year-old at some stage.
In Wednesday's press conference, Jesus said he had already spoken to Ronaldo about his role this international break, saying he would also not play against Denmark.

The Portugal captain trained away from his team-mates on Monday and Tuesday, with media reports suggesting there was a "crisis" meeting being held between Ronaldo, Jesus and Portugal Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca to clear the air.

"After the press conference of the national team, and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have made the decision to leave the national team training camp," Ronaldo posted on Instagram.
"In due course, I will tell all the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led me to leave the national team, to which I always dedicated myself.
"Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my team-mates good luck, without exception."
Ronaldo is the all-time leading scorer in men's international football (146 goals) and is pursuing the milestone of 1,000 career goals.
Portugal will be without Ronaldo for their clash with Denmark, as well as the return fixture against Norway on October 4.
The Selecao currently sit top of Group A4 with six points from six, with Jesus making a perfect start to his tenure.

xcevc6fjm5o7142oc5wiao3vx.title: Plenty of positives for Pocognoli as Scotland debut ends in goalless draw
xcevc6fjm5o7142oc5wiao3vx.subtitle: Sebastien Pocognoli's Scotland tenure began with a goalless draw against Slovenia, though he felt his side were worthy of all three points.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli said there were plenty of positives from his first match in charge of Scotland as they began their Nations League campaign with a 0-0 draw against Slovenia.
Pocognoli, sitting in the Scotland dugout for the first time since replacing Steve Clarke, watched on as his side overcame a tepid first-half display to claim a point away from home.
Andraz Sporar thought he had given Slovenia an eighth-minute lead when he crashed an effort in off the post, but the goal was ruled out for an offside against Danijel Sturm.
The Slovenia number nine then diverted an attempt just wide of the right post, with debutant Robbie Ure seeing his left-footed strike hit the post just before the break.
From there, the visitors dominated, and they should have gone in front when Oli McBurnie burst into the area, but he was unable to take the ball around Jan Oblak.
Aaron Hickey flicked a header from a corner just wide before substitute Kieron Bowie saw his shot from a tight angle smothered by Oblak as Scotland continued to probe.
McBurnie's header from point-blank range was repelled by the goalkeeper, but the best chance fell to Bowie late on. However, he scuffed his shot wide of the right post from close range.
Scotland had 17 shots against Slovenia, their most attempts in a match without scoring since June 2021 (19 shots against Czechia), but Pocognoli remained upbeat.
"I think we had two games in the same game, but you can analyse it in a positive way," Pocognoli said. "The first half was not what we expected in terms of structure.
"We were in between for the press. We were a bit surprised about the formation of Slovenia, but at half-time we fixed this, and you can see that the second half was much better.
"We produced what we wanted to show every minute, but in the first half we learned to stick together, to defend the box, to be resilient and to be patient to change the game.
"We were also challenged about set-pieces. After five minutes, we had many set-pieces to defend on, so that's the positive way to look at the first half.
"It was not always positive, but in the second half we had a game on the ball against a low block.

"So we had a lot of good movement through the side, through the lines, and we should have scored, to be honest, but the counter-press was good, the high [line] of the defence was good, just because the position of the players was better.
"Clean sheet, that's also positive, but we want to win, but I think we can take this positively."
Scotland are also now unbeaten in three consecutive away games in the Nations League for the first time (W2 D1), though they may feel they were deserving of all three points.
They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.9, with five of their 17 attempts on target, compared to Slovenia's tally of 0.5 from four shots.
However, Scotland failed to score in three competitive matches in a row for the first time since October 2004, something Billy Gilmour said must improve moving forward.

"Yeah, the two halves were totally different," Gilmour said. "I think in the first half we were still getting to grips with the situations off the ball and on the ball, but the second half was a good performance.

"Obviously, you need to score. We've had great chances. We never took them, but it's definitely something to build on. I mean, we're walking off gutted that we never scored, but in the second half it was really good.
"We came out in the second half, we were right at it, we stayed up there, we were putting pressure on them, creating chances, and the final part just never came.
"Of course, we're disappointed. We created enough chances to maybe take the game, but yeah, we came off having given it all."

"Clean sheet, that's also positive, but we want to win, but I think we can take this positively."

Scotland are also now unbeaten in three consecutive away games in the Nations League for the first time (W2 D1), though they may feel they were deserving of all three points. 

They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.9, with five of their 17 attempts on target, compared to Slovenia's tally of 0.5 from four shots. 

However, Scotland failed to score in three competitive matches in a row for the first time since October 2004, something Billy Gilmour said must improve moving forward. 

"Yeah, the two halves were totally different," Gilmour said. "I think in the first half we were still getting to grips with the situations off the ball and on the ball, but the second half was a good performance.

"Obviously, you need to score. We've had great chances. We never took them, but it's definitely something to build on. I mean, we're walking off gutted that we never scored, but in the second half it was really good.

"We came out in the second half, we were right at it, we stayed up there, we were putting pressure on them, creating chances, and the final part just never came.

"Of course, we're disappointed. We created enough chances to maybe take the game, but yeah, we came off having given it all."

xf931mi8g5j61ko5pel33bxtf.title: Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Mbappe at the double as Mourinho gets Clasico win
xf931mi8g5j61ko5pel33bxtf.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe, who is aiming to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday, decided Sunday's Clasico as Real Madrid defeated Barcelona.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe scored twice, grabbing an 87th-minute winner, as Real Madrid claimed a 2-1 away victory over Barcelona in El Clasico.
Barca were hoping to become the first team on record to start a season in one of Europe's top five leagues with 10 straight victories, having already built a six-point buffer to Madrid.

But Hansi Flick's side were up against it when Gerard Martin's attempted clearance ricocheted in off Mbappe in the 41st minute, although Raphinha's 13th goal of the LaLiga season drew them level shortly after the hour mark.
However, a wonderful, late counter from Madrid resulted in Mbappe slotting home to silence Camp Nou, with Jose Mourinho celebrating with a knee slide on the sidelines.
Madrid quickly got on the front foot as they looked to quiet the crowd, but no white shirts were lurking for a tap-in when Joan Garcia could only parry Arda Guler's drive.

Raphinha had three efforts at the other end, the second of which was the most threatening as his first-time strike whistled over the crossbar following some industrious work from Pedri, while Andrii Lunin – standing in for Thibaut Courtois, who was suffering from flu – denied Anthony Gordon.

Yan Diomande was one of Madrid's bright sparks in attack, and their opening goal came from him being slipped into the area by Marc Cucurella. The Ivorian's centre was far from his best, but Martin blasted it straight off Mbappe and in.
Barca should have had a quickfire equaliser when Lamine Yamal scuffed an uncharacteristically poor finish wide, but Flick's team were cut open on two more occasions before the interval.
Mbappe rifled against the inside of the post, only for the offside flag to go up against him, but Diomande was onside when he broke in behind and hit the side-netting moments later.
Madrid spurned another excellent counter-attacking chance early in the second half, with Jude Bellingham failing to get his pass off when Mbappe was supporting him against an isolated Martin.
And Barca made those reprieves count when Raphinha's shot proved too hot for Lunin to handle, after the Brazilian was cleverly found by Pedri on the right side of the area.
Lunin made a one-handed save to keep out Martin's header, though he was lucky to see one Yamal effort drift narrowly wide and another smack Dean Huijsen in the face.

However, there was a twist to come at the other end as, after more superb work from the outstanding Bellingham, substitute Eduardo Camavinga burst into the area and centred for Mbappe, who simply could not miss.
Mbappe outduels Yamal ahead of Ballon d'Or ceremony
Just 24 hours before the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony takes place in London, Sunday's Clasico featured two of the main contenders for the prize – Yamal and Mbappe.
And though the voting has long since been finalised, it was Mbappe who provided one final reminder of his credentials to be crowned the best player in the world.

There may have been a huge slice of fortune about Mbappe's opener, but his brace took him to five goals in two visits to Barca as a Madrid player. That is the most by any Blancos player since the start of 2013-14, surpassing Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema (four each).

Yamal, meanwhile, missed a glaring chance to equalise in the first half and was unable to hit the net with any of his five shots, which were worth a team-high 0.51 expected goals (xG). He also failed to create a single chance and only completed 76.6% of his passes (47/76).
And, on a night where Barca could have opened up a huge nine-point gap to Madrid and made LaLiga history in the process, it was Mourinho who earned the bragging rights.

His unbeaten run in Clasico matches – which dates back to his previous spell in charge of Madrid – now stands at six games (W4 D2). He is just the third Blancos coach to enjoy such a run, after Miguel Munoz (1962 to 1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001 to 2003) both had seven-match streaks.

Flick, meanwhile, also continues his wait for his 100th Barca win, having seen his team now lose back-to-back games in the space of five days, following the midweek Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

xh91ucfsayx71aru40tk0eod8.title: Eullafroy to give Montreal youngsters a chance in remaining games
xh91ucfsayx71aru40tk0eod8.subtitle: CF Montreal cannot qualify for the playoffs, and head coach Philippe Eullaffroy is set to play more youngsters against Charlotte FC.
paragraphs: CF Montreal head coach Philippe Eullaffroy plans to use their remaining MLS regular season games to give more minutes to younger players.
Montreal are bottom of the Eastern Conference and unable to reach the postseason with just three games to play.
Eullaffroy has already displayed his intention to give his younger players a chance in their 2-0 defeat to Supporters' Shield winners Nashville SC.
Seventeen-year-old Samsy Keita started in goal, while there were also outings for Olger Escobar and Hennadii Synchuk (both 20).
Montreal face Charlotte on Wednesday, and Keita could be in line for another start at Bank of America Stadium.
"We have to optimise the last three games that we have left of the regular season to develop [younger players]," said Eullaffroy.
"To improve the performance that they will be able to give us in the near future. And when I say near future, I mean already projecting ourselves into next season.
"So, Samsy is one of the players in the squad with the greatest potential. He got his first minutes at 17 years old, which not many goalkeepers get to experience at this level.
"We sensed he was ready for a while now; we threw him in at the deep end and he didn’t disappoint.
"He justified starting against the MLS Supporters' Shield champions. He was calm, safe."

Charlotte have already qualified for the playoffs, but they missed the chance to close the gap to Inter Miami and the New England Revolution further up the East after a loss to the Portland Timbers last time out.
Dean Smith's side lost 3-2 in Portland after conceding a 96th-minute winner on the road.
Charlotte FC – Idan Toklomati
Toklomati scored the second of Charlotte's two goals against Portland on Saturday, his fourth straight regular-season match with a goal.
Toklomati is the first player in Charlotte's MLS history to score in four straight regular-season matches.
CF Montreal – Samsy Keita
The two goals Montreal conceded in their loss to Nashville took them to 62 goals allowed this season, the second most in a single season in club history (64 in 2024).
However, teenager Keita impressed on his debut, saving three of the five shots on target he faced.
MATCH PREDICTION: CHARLOTTE FC WIN

Charlotte have collected 68 points at home since the start of last season (W21 D5 L6), second-most in MLS behind only Nashville (79) in that time. Charlotte's 21 home wins over the last two seasons are also second only to Nashville (25).
Montreal, meanwhile, have won two of their last 20 regular-season matches (D7 L11) dating back to mid-May. Their 13 points over that time are the fewest in MLS.
Charlotte have won three of their last four meetings with Montreal (L1), including recording a 2–1 road win on September 9.
Montreal had gone unbeaten in the first five meetings between the sides (W4 D1) prior to Charlotte winning three of the last four.

xj8xneulbxt13zk7nw3wcuxl.title: United States 4-2 Chile: Teenagers Hall and Albert break records in friendly win
xj8xneulbxt13zk7nw3wcuxl.subtitle: Records were broken by both Julian Hall and Mathis Albert as the United States made it back-to-back wins, beating Chile 4-2.
paragraphs: Teenagers Julian Hall and Mathis Albert were among the goalscorers as a new-look United States team beat Chile 4-2 in an entertaining friendly on Tuesday.

Mauricio Pochettino made 10 changes from the side that thrashed Peru 4-1 on Saturday, but the USA claimed another four-goal victory at Energizer Park, where Middlesbrough's Sebastian Berhalter played a starring role and was supported by some of the team's newcomers.

The St. Louis crowd were treated to an open start as Lawrence Vigouroux got down well to repel Miles Robinson's header, before Ben Brereton Diaz and Dario Osorio both struck the woodwork in the space of two minutes for Chile.

The USA went in front in the 37th minute as Hall cleverly dummied Sergino Dest's pass through to Berhalter, who applied a calm finish, though some weak goalkeeping from Chris Brady allowed Diego Ulloa to prod the equaliser over the line in first-half stoppage time.

Chile then went in front through a rasping strike from Maximiliano Gutierrez four minutes into the second half, but the USA were only behind for a couple of minutes as Hall's glancing header diverted Gio Reyna's inswinging cross home.
The USA led again when Chris Richards powered Berhalter's corner past Vigouroux with 72 minutes gone, and they got a clinching goal in added time.
Auston Trusty headed Antonee Robinson's free-kick back across goal, and on the stretch, Albert diverted the ball off the underside of the crossbar and in.
Both Hall and Albert made history for the USA on Tuesday, as their promising form continued ahead of a showdown with old rivals Mexico on Saturday.
Hall's goal – coming off the back of his debut strike against Peru – made the 18-year-old the youngest player to score on his first two outings for the USMNT.
And Albert's late effort made the Borussia Dortmund man the youngest scorer in the team's modern history, at the age of 17 years and 131 days (since at least 1988).
He surpassed Christian Pulisic, who had set the mark at the age of 17 years and 253 days old when he was also with Dortmund, against Bolivia in May 2016.

The USA only narrowly had more shots (18 to 17) and shots on target (nine to eight) than Chile, but their chances were of a far greater quality as they won the expected goals (xG) battle by 2.55 to 1.23.

xk9d48m2npsc17n7ynf5ybhvf.title: 'Someone has got to make a play', says Mastroeni amid Real Salt Lake woes
xk9d48m2npsc17n7ynf5ybhvf.subtitle: Real Salt Lake still have not won in MLS since the World Cup, ahead of Sunday's clash with the high-flying New England Revolution.
paragraphs: Pablo Mastroeni feels Real Salt Lake's shortcomings have been in both boxes, saying "someone's got to make a play" if they are to end their 13-game winless streak.
RSL have not won since beating the Colorado Rapids on May 16, drawing four matches and losing nine in that stretch, with each of their last four being losses.
It is the longest single-season winless run in their MLS history, with their only longer sequence spanning being an 18-match skid between August 2005 and May 2006.
They travelled to Lumen Field to face the Seattle Sounders – who were themselves on a 13-game winless run – on Wednesday, only to lose 2-0 to goals from Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnak.

Now sitting three points adrift of the playoff picture, they host the New England Revolution on Saturday, when Mastroeni believes it will come down to the big moments, rather than his team's tactical approach.
Mastroeni told KSL Sports after the Seattle game: "Did we compete the right way? This is what I asked the guys in the locker room. Every one of them said yes.
"Did you work extremely hard for the guy next to you when he made a mistake? Absolutely. Tactically between the boxes, did we execute the gameplan? Yes.
"And that just leaves the boxes again. Someone's got to step up and make a play. I think that's the biggest difference. [Against Seattle], the two shots, their guys executed.
"You can't tactic your way into the goal. You can't structure your way into the goal. You've got to make plays to get in the goal. That's just the name of the game.

"If you're doing everything you can, and it's still not enough, we're either not good enough at the moment or we're unlucky. Either way, there's only one way forward, and that's put your head down and keep grinding."
The Revs, meanwhile, are second in the Eastern Conference but 11 points behind Supporters' Shield frontrunners Nashville SC.

They overcame Orlando City SC 4-2 in a thriller last time out, with Peyton Miller and Carles Gil both finding the net in second-half stoppage time, after New England had conceded an 88th-minute equaliser.
"We're never satisfied. We never give up. I think this is a special group, just how we're able to fight through adversity," said United States midfielder Brooklyn Raines.
"This group is really special, and it's just something that we continue to strive for – that we're never satisfied with anything."
Real Salt Lake – Morgan Guilavogui
Guilavogui will stay with RSL throughout the international break, having declined a call-up from Guinea, and his ball-carrying ability makes him a real threat.

His 130 progressive carries this season – in just 1,381 MLS minutes – are the third-most of any RSL player, after Noel Caliskan (175) and Juan Manuel Sanabria (131). Those players have played 2,197 and 1,746 minutes, respectively.
New England Revolution – Carles Gil
Gil's 12 goals in MLS this season are five more than any other player has scored for New England (Dor Turgeman and Peyton Miller have seven apiece).
His 29 shots on target are also more than any of his team-mates have had this season, and with 71 chances teed up for team-mates, he is the league's top creator in 2026.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW
Real Salt Lake have got the better of New England of late, going unbeaten in the last four MLS matches between the two clubs.
A win for New England would be their first against Salt Lake in the league since May 2017, and during that period, RSL have outscored the Revs by nine goals to three.
The Opta supercomputer struggles to split the teams, however, which is perhaps understandable given RSL have home advantage but are in terrible form.
While RSL have 23 points from 13 outings on home soil this term (W7 D2 L4), the Revs have earned 17 from 13 road trips (W5 D2 L6).
New England Revolution – 36.7%

xl3mmyn1sj4g13pd84ahxehab.title: Varas insists San Diego are not 'hiding' amid winless run
xl3mmyn1sj4g13pd84ahxehab.subtitle: San Diego FC are without a win in almost two months in MLS, with their playoff hopes slipping away ahead of hosting the Seattle Sounders.
paragraphs: Mikey Varas insists San Diego FC are not hiding from their troubles as they look to end their eight-game winless streak in MLS against the Seattle Sounders.
With only four games left to play, San Diego sit 12th in the Western Conference on 34 points, just five behind the Colorado Rapids in the final wildcard spot.
San Diego started well after returning from the World Cup break, but they have not tasted victory in MLS since August 30, drawing four and losing four of their games since.

They twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with the LA Galaxy last time out to keep their playoff hopes alive, though Varas is aware that they need to turn their form around soon if they want to make it to the postseason.
"[Against the Galaxy] we created 2.6 xG, and the opponent created 0.6; the math makes sense that you win the game, and we're not winning the game," Varas said after the draw.
"So that's why I say for me, it's a good performance, but it's not enough, and we all know that we're definitely not hiding from that and not saying that everything is OK.
"We know we need wins, and we need wins fast. And I think that we're on our way to making the right steps."
As for Seattle, they sit seventh in the West after a stunning turnaround in form following the World Cup hiatus, though they are winless in their last two.
A 1-0 loss to FC Dallas was followed by a 1-1 draw with CF Montreal, though they still have a six-point cushion over Real Salt Lake in 10th.
Captain Cristian Roldan does not want the team to rest on their laurels, and he believes they have what it takes to put up a strong fight.
"This is our season right here, the next four games," he said. "We're right at the cusp of making the playoffs and not making the playoffs.
"With four games left against four tough teams, this is our season here. So if we're not ready for these games, if we don't come prepared for these games, we're going to get eaten alive.
"We have to play like it's the playoffs, and we're going to see what this team is capable of in tough environments."
San Diego FC – Anders Dreyer
Anders Dreyer's goal against LA Galaxy marked his 19th MLS match with at least one goal contribution this season, tied for the third-most in MLS.
His 41 matches with a goal contribution since the start of last season rank second to only Lionel Messi's 44 games.
Seattle Sounders – Sebastian Gomez
Sebastian Gomez scored his second goal of the season on Saturday, becoming the fourth Sounders player under 21 to record a multi-goal season.

xmblg77wt2sf1dia65u132jv6.title: Jesus has 'zero' fear of Norway despite Fernandes injury issue
xmblg77wt2sf1dia65u132jv6.subtitle: Portugal have three points on the board in the Nations League and face high-flying Norway next, but Jorge Jesus is relishing the clash.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus says he is "not afraid of Norway" as Portugal prepare to build on their winning start to the Nations League.
Jesus' debut ended in a narrow 1-0 win over Wales on Thursday, with Joao Felix's deflected shot securing all three points.
However, Portugal now travel to Norway, who sit top of the group after a 3-2 win over Denmark, with Erling Haaland scoring a brace.

Norway have not lost at home since March 2024, and are high scorers in all competitions, having netted 37 goals in World Cup qualifying during a perfect campaign, and then scoring 13 goals in the tournament proper.
Jesus acknowledged the quality of the team they are facing but believes the quality in his own squad will shine through.
"[It's going to be a] difficult game because of the quality the team has; they demonstrated it at the World Cup," Jesus said of Norway.
"They have a forward duo that is perhaps the best in Europe right now, and besides that, they have other players we know from the Portuguese league.

"They have their strengths and their quality, but so do we. Despite having little time to work with me, we will have quality. I'm not afraid of Norway at all, zero. I look more at the team defensively than offensively."
Jesus will be without Bruno Fernandes for the trip to Oslo, though, with the Manchester United captain suffering from an injury.
He has played in all seven of United's matches this season, starting six of those, and featured from the start against Wales before being withdrawn in the 90th minute.
"Against Wales, we went in with practically everyone physically available and came out with a complicated problem with Bruno Fernandes; we'll see what happens," Jesus said.
"He's coming off an injury at United, and he told me he's been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.
"It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales. I've already spoken to him, and I prefer not to risk it in this game, so he's fully fit for the Denmark match."
Cristiano Ronaldo is in the running to get a starting place, though, having had a goal disallowed against Wales last time out.
"Let's start with his performance against Wales. We had 15 shots inside the box, and of those 15, Ronaldo was involved in seven, and two of those were on target," Jesus said.
"That was a lot. His performance can be better, obviously; he came close to scoring, but I've already spoken to him.

"He played 65 minutes [against Wales]. I'll see how he is, whether I start him or come off the bench, because whether we like it or not, Cristiano isn't Joao Neves, who is 20 years old and can play two games in a row every three days.
"We have to look at it from that perspective, but he's one of the players about whom training will tell us something."

xmjx49de6f3c14ij3ypdhalr5.title: Andrews 'torn' as Brentford keep Premier League unbeaten run intact
xmjx49de6f3c14ij3ypdhalr5.subtitle: Keith Andrews was left "torn" after his Brentford side continued their unbeaten Premier League run with a 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.
paragraphs: Brentford boss Keith Andrews was left "torn" after seeing his side salvage a point against Aston Villa in a 2-2 draw at Villa Park.
In an enthralling Premier League encounter, Yehor Yarmoliuk gave the visitors the lead in the 10th minute before Nicolas Jackson netted an equaliser 88 seconds later.
John McGinn scored Villa's second 13 minutes from time, as his effort took a massive deflection off Kristoffer Ajer, who redeemed himself moments later, slotting home from close range.
The result sees Brentford sit fourth in the Premier League table, and continuing their unbeaten run in the competition.
The Bees are also undefeated in their last eight games in the Premier League, but have lost eight points from winning position in the process, with only Bournemouth (nine) having lost more.
However, it was mixed emotions for Andrews, whose side mustered an expected goals (xG) of 1.25 from 14 shots.

"[I am] Torn to be honest. I liked a lot today - spirit, grit, determination. There was evidence of rustiness, which is understandable, but I don't like to use that as an excuse, but the boys have been away for three weeks so it's trying to find the balance," said Andrews.
"Then we had Kevin's [Shade] injury, Jannik [Schuster] wasn't right and came off at half time, so we got tested today.
“But we're also up against a team who I thought were just starting to click before the international break.
“But the fact that we're disappointed coming away from home to a Champions League team who spend big money tells you a lot."

Meanwhile, Unai Emery considered the result to be fair, even though Aston Villa have now failed to win any of their opening three home games in a league campaign for the first time since 2015-16, when they were without a win in their first nine league matches at Villa Park (D3 L6).

Reflecting on the game, Emery said, “To draw at home is not a good result. I think we played a match with a lot of things improved from our last home match against [Nottingham] Forest. We created chances but conceded more chances than I expected.
“Maybe the result is fair, but analysing how we are improving things, competing better, I can't tell nothing to the players about the match.
“We'll try to analyse again how we can improve even more. A better match than against Forest. Keep going forward.
"We tried, we pushed, we had chances but so did they. At the end we could've won, but also we could've lost."
Emery will be hoping for different fortunes come Tuesday, as his side host Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.

xtdn5nw2pn271ume666t790mf.title: Iraola aiming to rediscover home comforts with Liverpool
xtdn5nw2pn271ume666t790mf.subtitle: Liverpool are yet to win a home Premier League game this season, though their form at Anfield in other competitions has been better.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola knows it is important for Liverpool to build a winning feeling at Anfield, as they prepare to welcome Villarreal to Merseyside in the Champions League.
A 2-1 win over nine-man Brentford on Saturday lifted Liverpool to fifth in the Premier League table, but they are yet to win a home league game under Iraola (D2 L1).

Having lost 3-0 to Manchester City last time out at Anfield, the Reds have only triumphed on their own turf this season in the Champions League (2-1 against Atletico Madrid) and the EFL Cup (3-1 against Tottenham).
Liverpool have won 15 of their last 16 home games in the group or league stage of the Champions League, however, with the only exception being a 4-1 loss to PSV under Arne Slot last November.
And Iraola hopes getting a morale-boosting victory on Tuesday could act as a springboard for them to start performing at Anfield on the domestic level.
"It is true that we have had better results away than at home, but it is just the beginning," he said. "We had very good games, Atletico was a good game, Spurs was a very good game.
"If you ask me, I always prefer to play at home. I would 100% prefer to be playing at home. It is true that the demands of each game are different. We take it one by one.

"For me, now it is Villarreal, that's it. It finishes there. Prepare and focus on that one. It is going to be demanding tomorrow, I know them very well and we need a performance like we had against Atletico."

Iraola was then asked about the form of Florian Wirtz, who was in excellent form against Brentford as he created nine chances from open play – the most by any player in a Premier League game since Sadio Mane teed up nine against Burnley in January 2021, also for Liverpool.
Wirtz has also assisted on back-to-back appearances for the Reds for the first time, having also laid on a goal against LASK in Europe a week ago.

"I think he is coming from two very good games, he played really well against LASK and the other day [against Brentford], I think he helped the team a lot, in possession and out of possession," Iraola said of the Germany international.
"I hope we can keep him there. We analyse and scrutinise everything, but he has done well, it is fair to say that."
Liverpool have suffered a pair of injury blows, though, with Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai both hobbling off against Brentford.
While Szoboszlai has only mildly reaggravated an existing issue and will not be out for long, Iraola does not expect Frimpong to return until after the November international break.
"I think they are different circumstances, Jeremie Frimpong has a new muscle injury. It happened, I think in the second or third minute that he was playing," Iraola said.
"It's difficult to predict. We will have to wait until he recovers but it is going to be difficult to have him back before the break.

"Dominik Szoboszlai is different, it is not a new injury. It hasn't worsened, the injury, but we probably have to be a bit patient until he recovers fully. It is not like he has to wait a long time to come back, it is more or less the same situation he was in this past week.

"We need more patience with him, but I appreciate what he did the other day, to be available, want to contribute in a very difficult game that you know is going to be very physical. To put himself there and want to play, that speaks very well."

xuogoga7dy6518sd68iw7giga.subtitle: Vancouver Whitecaps are looking to get back on track in their first for top spot in the Western Conference against Los Angeles FC.
paragraphs: Jesper Sorensen believes Vancouver Whitecaps' strength will be put to the test as they prepare to face Los Angeles FC in MLS without Thomas Muller.

Muller suffered a hamstring injury during the Whitecaps' 3-1 loss to the Chicago Fire on Tuesday, though Sorensen did not reveal the severity of the issue or how long it will keep the German sidelined.
It comes at a bad time for Vancouver, who sit top of the Western Conference with only a three-point cushion to St. Louis City SC and FC Dallas in second and third, respectively.
Vancouver have won just two of their last six MLS games (D1 L3), and are winless in their last two, having also drawn 3-3 with D.C. United before their loss to Chicago.
But Sorensen expects his team to overcome their recent issues without Muller and is confident they have the squad depth to do so.
"That's why we have more than just 11 players," said Sorensen.
"And you know what? This is also a situation where things are not just going our way, and that's also a good challenge.
"That's what you have to grow from. You cannot always have it your way and then believe you will get stronger."

As for LAFC, they have seen a lot of change over the international break, with head coach Marc Dos Santos sacked following a run of one win in 10 regular-season matches (D5 L4) dating back to the start of August.
That run has seen them drop down to sixth in the West, and they are nine points behind Saturday's opponents after a run of three without a victory.
Xavi Tamarit has been appointed as Dos Santos' successor on an interim basis, and he has high hopes for what they can do in their last six games of the regular season.
"First of all, I'm really happy to have this opportunity," Tamarit told reporters. "I appreciate the club trusted [in] me and the players.
"What we want to improve is to give very simple but clear concepts in the tactical aspects and give clear roles for each player on the pitch to have a really clear idea and a really clear identity."
Los Angeles FC – Denis Bouanga
Denis Bouanga has 16 career goal contributions in 15 matches in all competitions against the Whitecaps (nine goals, seven assists), his most against any MLS club.
Vancouver have limited Bouanga to just one goal and one assist over the last six meetings in all competitions dating back to November 2024.
Vancouver Whitecaps – Mathias Laborda
Mathias Laborda scored Vancouver's lone goal in their defeat to Chicago on Tuesday, his 12th regular-season MLS goal.
The only defender to score more in league play since Laborda made his MLS debut in 2023 is Anthony Markanich with 18 goals.
MATCH PREDICTION: LOS ANGELES FC WIN
Vancouver are unbeaten in four straight meetings with LAFC in all competitions (W1 D3), with the lone win coming in the only match played at BMO Stadium in that time.
That win, a 1-0 victory in June 2025, is one of two Whitecaps wins in 14 all-time away matches against LAFC (D4 L8).

And the Whitecaps have won seven of their last 18 regular-season matches (D5 L6) after opening the season with eight wins in nine (L1). They have not lost consecutive league matches in over a year, since losing against the LA Galaxy and Colorado Rapids in July 2025.

LAFC's eight points over the last 10 regular-season matches equal their fewest in any 10-match span in club history (June-September 2023), but given their home advantage, the Opta supercomputer is backing them for a much-needed victory.
Los Angeles FC – 44.8%
Vancouver Whitecaps – 28.3%

xxws0ur5l19n15c1lbv98nvmb.title: 'It won't happen next time', say Leverkusen after Boniface storms down tunnel
xxws0ur5l19n15c1lbv98nvmb.subtitle: Victor Boniface was an unused substitute once again for Bayer Leverkusen once again on Saturday, as they edged out Mainz.
paragraphs: Bayer Leverkusen boss Carles Martinez says he will "speak to" Victor Boniface after the striker appeared to storm down the tunnel following an unused substitute appearance during the win over Mainz.
Leverkusen moved fourth in the Bundesliga table after holding on for a narrow 4-3 victory during a seven-goal thriller at MEWA Arena.
However, Boniface was once again restricted to a spectator role.
The Nigeria international hit double figures for goals across all competitions in his first two seasons with Leverkusen, but has only played five minutes this term.
When Martinez made his final two substitutions in the 84th minute against Mainz, Boniface headed straight down the tunnel rather than return to the bench.
"I didn't notice it during the game," the Leverkusen boss told Kolner Stadt-Anzeiger. "I don't know anything about it. If that's what happened, we'll speak to him.
"I can understand that every player wants to help the team. At the same time, these decisions are part of football. At that moment, I decided to make those substitutions."
"I don't know, maybe he needed to go to the toilet," added sporting managing director Simon Rolfes. "Perhaps he went into the dressing room a little too early. It won't happen next time."
After starting the season with a shock 3-2 loss to promoted Elversberg, Leverkusen are now unbeaten in their last four Bundesliga games (W3 D1).

Leverkusen have also scored two or more goals in all seven of their competitive matches under Martinez.

Bayer Leverkusen boss Carles Martinez says he will "speak to" Victor Boniface after the striker appeared to storm down the tunnel following an unused substitute appearance during the win over Mainz.

Leverkusen moved fourth in the Bundesliga table after holding on for a narrow 4-3 victory during a seven-goal thriller at MEWA Arena.

However, Boniface was once again restricted to a spectator role.

The Nigeria international hit double figures for goals across all competitions in his first two seasons with Leverkusen, but has only played five minutes this term.

When Martinez made his final two substitutions in the 84th minute against Mainz, Boniface headed straight down the tunnel rather than return to the bench.

"I didn't notice it during the game," the Leverkusen boss told Kolner Stadt-Anzeiger. "I don't know anything about it. If that's what happened, we'll speak to him.

"I can understand that every player wants to help the team. At the same time, these decisions are part of football. At that moment, I decided to make those substitutions."

"I don't know, maybe he needed to go to the toilet," added sporting managing director Simon Rolfes. "Perhaps he went into the dressing room a little too early. It won't happen next time."

After starting the season with a shock 3-2 loss to promoted Elversberg, Leverkusen are now unbeaten in their last four Bundesliga games (W3 D1).

Their 10 points at this stage of the season are two more than they had after five games in 2025-26. The last time they had more points at this stage was in their title-winning campaign (13 in 2023-24).

Leverkusen have also scored two or more goals in all seven of their competitive matches under Martinez.

y0udvedwlbly1dcdxuekeh198.title: Kovac: Dortmund must push to the limit to defeat Union Berlin
y0udvedwlbly1dcdxuekeh198.subtitle: Borussia Dortmund travel to Union Berlin on Saturday in the hopes of reclaiming top spot in the Bundesliga.
paragraphs: Niko Kovac has urged his Borussia Dortmund side to "push ourselves to the limit" in order to defeat Union Berlin.
Dortmund are second in the Bundesliga, behind Freiburg on goal difference, but saw their perfect start come to an end last time out against Werder Bremen.
Despite leading 2-0 as late as the 87th minute, Dortmund collapsed to a 2-2 draw at Signal Iduna Park.
Their momentum also stalled during the week after they lost 1-0 to Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League.
Nevertheless, Dortmund have 13 points from their opening five matches, the exact same tally they had at this stage of the 2025-26 Bundesliga season, which was Kovac's first full campaign in charge.
Prior to Kovac's appointment, Dortmund had started a Bundesliga season with at least 13 points from five games only three times, and no other manager has achieved such a start twice.
Despite their strong start to the season, Kovac is wary of the threat posed by upcoming opponents Union.
"We want to take three points there. But we know how difficult it is there," said Kovac.
"Last season we won 3-0, but it was still a tough battle right up to the last second. I expect the same.
"In their last game against Elversberg, they returned to the level of intensity and aggressiveness they've shown in recent years. It's going to be intense!
"We'll have to push ourselves to the limit and win the battles they force upon us. If you think you can just go there and coast through the game, it’ll be tough.
"Many teams have already learned that the hard way."
Union are 16th after five games, but got their first win of the season on the board last time out against Elversberg (1-0).
Union Berlin – Livan Burcu
Livan Burcu has recorded the most total take-ons (14) and successful take-ons (nine) for the club in the Bundesliga this season, despite playing less than half (215) of the 450 possible minutes.
Against Elversberg, he scored the winner in just 32 minutes of play and registered a joint-team-high three shots, level with Andras Schafer.
Borussia Dortmund – Nico Schlotterbeck
Nico Schlotterbeck has scored six Bundesliga goals since the start of last season, more than any other current centre-back in the competition in that period.
Schlotterbeck also scored in the last meeting between Union and Dortmund in January 2026.
MATCH PREDICTION: BORUSSIA DORTMUND WIN

Dortmund have won their first two away matches of this Bundesliga season; only twice have they started a campaign with a longer winning streak on the road: 2000-01 (first three) and 2010-11 (first eight).
Going back to last season, Dortmund have won three consecutive Bundesliga away games for the first time under Kovac.

Union have lost each of their last three Bundesliga matches against Dortmund by an aggregate score of 12-0; this is the first time the club have suffered three consecutive top-flight defeats against a single opponent without scoring.
However, Union have earned all four of their points in the 2026-27 Bundesliga season in home matches.

They have scored four of their five Bundesliga goals from set-pieces, the highest proportion in the league (80%). Dortmund have scored only one of their 11 league goals from a set-piece (9%), with only RB Leipzig having a lower share (7%).
Borussia Dortmund – 57.1%

y399gjst1a2r164dk0wu85d1e.title: Fabregas dismisses suggestions he could replace Carrick at Man Utd
y399gjst1a2r164dk0wu85d1e.subtitle: Cesc Fabregas and Michael Carrick will go head to head in the Champions League, though the Spaniard has been linked with his opponent's job.
paragraphs: Cesc Fabregas shrugged off suggestions that he could be a replacement for Michael Carrick at Manchester United, saying such questions are disrespectful.

Fabregas and Carrick will face each other as opposition managers, 17 years after playing on opposing sides in both legs of the 2008-09 Champions League semi-finals, between Arsenal and United (won 4-1 on aggregate by the Red Devils).
Carrick is coming under scrutiny after a tough start to life as United's permanent head coach, after earning just one win in seven Premier League games so far in 2026-27.
It is their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87 – also one victory after seven games.
They are also on a run of six matches without a victory, with their last win coming on MD1 of the Champions League against Sabah (4-0).
Meanwhile, Como have gone from strength to strength during their time under Fabregas, first earning promotion to Serie A before qualifying for the Champions League for the first time.

The Spaniard has been linked with the likes of Chelsea and Barcelona in the last year, with United the latest to be put forward as a potential future destination, but Fabregas gave his support to Carrick.
"I won't answer that question because I think that's not a very nice question," Fabregas said on Tuesday.
"I don't think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side."

This will be the first meeting between Como and United – since the start of last season, the six matches between Italian and English sides in the Champions League have been won by the Premier League outfit on five occasions (L1 – Atalanta 2-1 Chelsea the exception).

But United have just one win in their last 10 away Champions League matches (D3 L6) and have only kept one clean sheet in their last 15 on the road. Both the win and clean sheet were in a 2-0 victory over Villarreal in November 2021.
"Manchester United is a historical club I know very, very well," Fabregas added.
"We have so much respect for who they are, for what they do, because they have incredible players.
"I know Steve Holland very well because I worked with him for years at Chelsea, and I know Michael has done really well in previous clubs as well.
"Last year he did really well, bringing Manchester United back to where they belong, which is the Champions League, for the first time in many years, so it's not all bad.
"It's an honour to host them for the first time in our history."

y3u6ulpbp7zw1o7xr32uwb8wl.title: Freiburg 1-3 Bayern Munich: Upamecano scores stunner as Gnabry brings up Bundesliga century
y3u6ulpbp7zw1o7xr32uwb8wl.subtitle: Bayern Munich moved back above Borussia Dortmund on goal difference, ahead of the rivals' huge Bundesliga meeting next Saturday.
paragraphs: Dayot Upamecano's brilliant solo goal and Serge Gnabry's 100th Bundesliga strike helped Bayern Munich to a 3-1 win at Freiburg, as they returned to the top of the table.

Having been overhauled at the summit by Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, as a result of Maximilian Beier's late winner against Eintracht Frankfurt, Bayern were under the tutelage of assistant coach Aaron Danks, after Vincent Kompany collapsed at training on Friday.

However, Kompany – who was taken to hospital for tests and is in a stable condition – will be able to celebrate three points, with Michael Olise getting Bayern's clinching goal after Tom Bischof put through his own net to tee up a nervy finish.

Less than two minutes had gone when the game was paused due to red smoke billowing out from a pyrotechnic and drifting across the pitch, and that interruption seemed to stop either team from building any momentum.

But Bayern broke the deadlock through an unlikely source in the 16th minute. Upamecano turned defence into attack in an instant when he blocked Niklas Beste's shot, skipped between two challenges and found Harry Kane.
The Ballon d'Or candidate quickly moved the ball onto Olise, who played Upamecano clean through on goal, and he finished like a striker through the legs of Mio Backhaus.

Backhaus made a good stop to thwart Nathaniel Brown as Bayern hunted a second goal, but he had to pick the ball out of his net again in the 42nd minute, with Gnabry following Upamecano's lead by slotting through the goalkeeper's legs.

Backhaus kept Freiburg in the contest for much of the second half, making two saves to thwart substitute Ismael Saibari and one to keep out Kane, and Bayern's position was under threat when Bischof scored an own goal in the 82nd minute.
Freiburg's one clear chance to equalise fell the way of substitute Cyriaque Irie, but Jonas Urbig came up with the save.

And, after the offside flag denied Sacha Boey, Olise profited from Backhaus missing two attempts to clear outside his area, sliding his finish into an empty net to make the points safe in stoppage time.
Gnabry brings up century, Upamecano channels inner Kane

Until Kompany's health scare, much of the focus ahead of this game was on Kane, who will discover on Monday whether he has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001.
But the Bavarian giants have plenty of other sources of goals – not least Gnabry. The winger's goal was his 100th in the Bundesliga, on his 267th appearance in the competition.
He is only the third player still active in the league to reach that mark, after Hoffenheim's Andrej Kramaric (141) and Gnabry's team-mate Kane (102).

But Upamecano stole the headlines with what was his 11th Bundesliga goal in 245 appearances, and surely the first that saw him start a move inside his own area, run the length of the pitch, then finish one-v-one with an opposing goalkeeper.

Bayern, who had 17 shots and 2.94 expected goals, compared to Freiburg's 0.99 xG from 17 attempts of their own, are back at the summit on goal difference ahead of facing Dortmund in the first Klassiker of the season next week.

y7u57ezd7pdm1d43tzruinwms.title: ​Philadelphia boss Richter plays down expectations of Sullivan stardom
y7u57ezd7pdm1d43tzruinwms.subtitle: Cavan Sullivan made history for the United States during the international break, and he will be back in MLS action this weekend.
paragraphs: Philadelphia Union boss Ryan Richter has played down the burgeoning expectations surrounding United States history-maker Cavan Sullivan, encouraging the breakout star to continue working hard ahead of the MLS run-in.
During the international break, Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in the history of the USMNT when he found the net in their 3-0 victory over Mexico.
At the age of 17 years and five days, Sullivan surpassed Mathis Albert, who found the net against Chile only four days earlier at the age of 17 years and 131 days.
On Saturday, he will be back in MLS action as Philadelphia host Real Salt Lake, and the Union's interim boss Richter says it is unfair to expect him to rise to stardom instantly.
"You can't put on those kinds of expectations. I know he'll continue to work in that way, and our job is to help him as much as we possibly can to reach those goals," Richter said.
"He has got an amazing support system around him, a great family; his older brother is also a national team player – they keep his feet on the ground more than anyone.
"We've known him for a long time, so to me, he's still the eight-year-old kid running around like crazy, pulling off something incredible on the field. That's still the kid I see.

"He is so driven to be an amazing player one day, and he keeps his feet on the ground and stays focused on that. He understands you just don't get to that level; it takes hard work, and nothing's guaranteed for an athlete."
The Union went into the international break on a 12-game unbeaten run (W10 D2), the longest regular-season streak in their history.

They have also won their last six matches, which is the longest winning run in their MLS history, and Richter says that even with some players heading off on international duty, they have maintained their intensity in training.
"Credit to the guys that were here – we didn't drop the focus or the intensity at all. That was pretty cool," Richter told reporters.
"Not having a game at the weekend, you don't have an end goal at the end of the training week, but they did a great job to push the intensity and focus.
"We train every day to try to get better and keep building in the way we want to play, building in our individual things that we need to get better at."

While Philadelphia are sixth in the Eastern Conference, Real Salt Lake are 11th in the West and four points outside the playoff picture, having endured a long winless run before beating the New England Revolution 3-0 prior to the break.
Philadelphia Union – Milan Iloski
Iloski scored a hat-trick in Philadelphia's win against Orlando City SC before the international break.
That made him the only player to score multiple hat-tricks in MLS this season, having previously netted a treble against Inter Miami.
Real Salt Lake – Sergi Solans
Solans scored a brace in Real Salt Lake's win over New England before the international break.

That double saw him pull further clear as his team's leading goalscorer this season, with 11. He is their only player to hit double figures (Zavier Gozo is second with six) and the only player on the team with multiple braces this year.
MATCH PREDICTION: PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN
The Philadelphia Union have only managed to defeat Real Salt Lake once in 13 regular-season matches between the sides, a 4-1 victory on May 19, 2018.
Overall, Real Salt Lake lead the series with six wins and six draws, to just one loss. This game will be the second meeting between the two sides since 2019 (also facing off in 2024).
While the Union are in tremendous form, Real Salt Lake only snapped their 13-game winless streak in their final game before the international break, beating New England 3-0.
That was the longest single-season winless streak in the club's MLS history, and even if they are back in the win column, Philadelphia are clear favourites on home soil.
OPTA WIN PROBABILITY
Philadelphia Union – 59.9%
Real Salt Lake – 19.1%

yaxpi5gfiki010zpfrdyaknu1.title: Hoffenheim 3-0 Bayer Leverkusen: Kramaric stars in eventful win as Martinez's men falter
yaxpi5gfiki010zpfrdyaknu1.subtitle: Bayer Leverkusen slumped to a 3-0 defeat to Hoffenheim as Carles Martinez's side drew a blank at the SNP Arena.
paragraphs: Bayer Leverkusen missed a chance to close the gap at the top of the Bundesliga table, as they fell to a 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim on Sunday.
Andrej Kramaric starred at SNP Arena with a goal and an assist, and Alexander Prass and Max Moerstedt also got on the scoresheet, though Prass was sent off in the dying minutes.
Patrik Schick nodded wide just five minutes in, following Aleix Garcia's corner, while Nathan Tella failed to guide the Czech striker's headed pass on target moments later.

Hoffenheim's first opportunity arrived in the 12th minute, when Fisnik Asslani saw two right-footed drives parried by a diving Mark Flekken, while Schick continued to spurn chances at the other end, firing high off Ibrahim Maza's set-up.

There was little to separate the two sides until the 76th minute, when Leverkusen captain Edmond Tapsoba dragged down Asslani inside the box, with Kramaric making no mistake from 12 yards out, firing down the middle to beat Flekken.

Robert Andrich saw a powerful strike parried by Oliver Baumann as Carles Martinez's side pushed for a response, ultimately to no avail as a frenetic final few minutes saw Hoffenheim add some gloss to the scoreline.

Prass combined with Kramaric to drill in a superb high strike from 18 yards out in the 89th minute, leaving Flekken with no chance, though the Austrian was soon given his marching orders after being shown a second yellow card for his excessive celebration.

The one-man disadvantage did not deter the hosts, who added a third in the sixth minute of stoppage time after Kramaric's shot was parried onto the crossbar, with Moerstedt poking home to cap off a fast break in the following move.
Kramaric brings up Hoffenheim's 1,000th

Christian Ilzer will have plenty to be pleased about following Sunday's emphatic victory, which saw Hoffenheim record three consecutive wins across all competitions for just the second time under the Austrian. Their only longer winning run during his tenure came in January, when they secured five wins on the spin.

It was also Hoffenheim's biggest Bundesliga victory since beating Freiburg 3-0 in February, with their only bigger league success under Ilzer coming in a 5-1 thrashing of Borussia Monchengladbach in January.
Kramaric was at the heart of the triumph, scoring Hoffenheim's 1,000th Bundesliga goal while also reaching a significant individual milestone.

The veteran Croatian now boasts 201 direct goal involvements in the competition (141 goals, 60 assists). Since 2004-05, only Robert Lewandowski (367), Thomas Muller (323) and Marco Reus (251) have registered more, with Mario Gomez also on 201.

Kramaric also extended his remarkable record from the spot, converting his 18th consecutive Bundesliga penalty. Only Bayern's Harry Kane has enjoyed a longer such streak in the competition, having scored 24 successive penalties for Bayern Munich between 2023 and 2026.
In all, the hosts were no match for Leverkusen, producing 3.46 expected goals (xG) to the Werkself's meagre 0.62 xG.
yaxpi5gfiki010zpfrdyaknu1.html:
Bayer Leverkusen missed a chance to close the gap at the top of the Bundesliga table, as they fell to a 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim on Sunday. 

Andrej Kramaric starred at SNP Arena with a goal and an assist, and Alexander Prass and Max Moerstedt also got on the scoresheet, though Prass was sent off in the dying minutes. 

Patrik Schick nodded wide just five minutes in, following Aleix Garcia's corner, while Nathan Tella failed to guide the Czech striker's headed pass on target moments later. 

Hoffenheim's first opportunity arrived in the 12th minute, when Fisnik Asslani saw two right-footed drives parried by a diving Mark Flekken, while Schick continued to spurn chances at the other end, firing high off Ibrahim Maza's set-up. 

There was little to separate the two sides until the 76th minute, when Leverkusen captain Edmond Tapsoba dragged down Asslani inside the box, with Kramaric making no mistake from 12 yards out, firing down the middle to beat Flekken. 

Robert Andrich saw a powerful strike parried by Oliver Baumann as Carles Martinez's side pushed for a response, ultimately to no avail as a frenetic final few minutes saw Hoffenheim add some gloss to the scoreline. 

Prass combined with Kramaric to drill in a superb high strike from 18 yards out in the 89th minute, leaving Flekken with no chance, though the Austrian was soon given his marching orders after being shown a second yellow card for his excessive celebration. 

The one-man disadvantage did not deter the hosts, who added a third in the sixth minute of stoppage time after Kramaric's shot was parried onto the crossbar, with Moerstedt poking home to cap off a fast break in the following move. 

Kramaric brings up Hoffenheim's 1,000th 

Christian Ilzer will have plenty to be pleased about following Sunday's emphatic victory, which saw Hoffenheim record three consecutive wins across all competitions for just the second time under the Austrian. Their only longer winning run during his tenure came in January, when they secured five wins on the spin. 

It was also Hoffenheim's biggest Bundesliga victory since beating Freiburg 3-0 in February, with their only bigger league success under Ilzer coming in a 5-1 thrashing of Borussia Monchengladbach in January. 

Kramaric was at the heart of the triumph, scoring Hoffenheim's 1,000th Bundesliga goal while also reaching a significant individual milestone. 

The veteran Croatian now boasts 201 direct goal involvements in the competition (141 goals, 60 assists). Since 2004-05, only Robert Lewandowski (367), Thomas Muller (323) and Marco Reus (251) have registered more, with Mario Gomez also on 201. 

Kramaric also extended his remarkable record from the spot, converting his 18th consecutive Bundesliga penalty. Only Bayern's Harry Kane has enjoyed a longer such streak in the competition, having scored 24 successive penalties for Bayern Munich between 2023 and 2026. 

In all, the hosts were no match for Leverkusen, producing 3.46 expected goals (xG) to the Werkself's meagre 0.62 xG.

ycibu60ctvzf1bvfu5mmnmg5r.title: The Numbers Game: Spain take record unbeaten run to Wembley as Tuchel looks to rebuild trust
ycibu60ctvzf1bvfu5mmnmg5r.subtitle: England are still dealing with the scars of their World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, ahead of their Nations League clash with Spain.
paragraphs: Just over two months on from their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals, England are back in action at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.

And their opening game in the 2026-27 Nations League pits them against the team they would have faced in the World Cup final, had Thomas Tuchel's side not retreated into their own penalty area after Anthony Gordon's goal and conceded two late goals to Argentina.

Spain travel to London off the back of their second World Cup win, having held Lionel Messi and company to zero shots through 90 minutes of the final – the first time that has ever occurred – before claiming the trophy through Ferran Torres' extra-time goal.
The top two teams in Group A3 will progress to the quarter-finals next March, but with Croatia and Czechia also lurking, the Three Lions and La Roja will have to be switched on.
Who will get off to a positive start? Here, we preview the game using Opta insights.
What's expected?
Saturday's match looks almost too close to call on paper, and the Opta supercomputer is also struggling.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the predictive model, England were victorious in 33.6% of scenarios.
Spain have the slight edge, with a win probability of 40.2%, with the remaining 26.2% of simulations being drawn.
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently triumphing 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.
Their last away game against the Three Lions also ended in a 2-1 victory, at Wembley in the first edition of the Nations League, in September 2018.
Gareth Southgate's England did manage a memorable victory in the reverse fixture of that group, however, with a Raheem Sterling brace and a Marcus Rashford goal sealing a 3-2 triumph in Seville.
But England have only won two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine of those matches (D2).
One of those victories was a 1-0 triumph at home to Spain in November 2011, though, with the other being a 3-2 success in Germany in March 2016.
Tuchel aims to rebuild trust after semi-final collapse
It is now 60 years of hurt for England at major tournaments, with their next shot at silverware coming on home soil at Euro 2028.
And after this year's World Cup, perhaps more than any other edition in recent history, there was a real feeling of what could have been.
England were in a commanding position when Gordon applied the finishing touch to Morgan Rogers' cross 55 minutes into their tense semi-final clash with the Albiceleste in Atlanta.
They then immediately retreated into their shells, not helped by Tuchel introducing defenders Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O'Reilly with his first three substitutions.

Between opening the scoring and conceding an 85th-minute equaliser to Enzo Fernandez, the Three Lions had just 11.9% possession, the lowest share ever recorded by a leading team in a World Cup match over a period of at least 10 minutes (since 1966) by a team who were leading. Their leading passer in that period was centre-back Marc Guehi, with six.
Defeat felt inevitable from the moment Argentina levelled, and now Tuchel – who faced stern criticism from supporters and the media – has bridges to build.

A win over the World champions would be a fine place to start, and it should be noted that Tuchel has the best win rate of any England manager to ever lead the team for at least 10 matches, at 77% (P22 W17 D2 L3), while the Three Lions have only averaged more goals per game under Walter Winterbottom (2.8) than Tuchel (2.3).

England have also won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their most recent five without conceding. Only once in their history have they previously won six in a row to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
But after the meek surrender that ended their World Cup dream, fans will want to see intensity and creativity.

The withdrawals of Declan Rice and Cole Palmer – who scored against Spain in the Euro 2024 final before being overlooked by Tuchel for the World Cup – do not help matters, though Morgan Gibbs-White could now have a chance to impress. His 13 goals in the Premier League this calendar year are the joint-most of any player, alongside Erling Haaland.
Spain out to extend record-breaking run
The mood in Spain's camp could hardly be more positive coming into this fixture, having followed up their World Cup triumph by handing head coach Luis de la Fuente a six-year contract extension.
They are also defending a 38-match unbeaten run in all competitions, winning 29 games and drawing nine in that time.
It is the longest-ever streak by a European or South American nation, dating back to a 1-0 defeat to Colombia in March 2024, which took place on English soil, at West Ham's London Stadium.

La Roja's last competitive defeat, which came all the way back in March 2023, also occurred in Britain, as they lost 2-0 to Scotland in a qualifier for Euro 2024. England will hope that is a positive omen.

But this is a truly special Roja side, led by Ballon d'Or contender Lamine Yamal but also boasting plenty of other talent across the board – including World Cup Golden Ball winner Rodri and Young Player of the Tournament Pau Cubarsi.
Aided by Yamal's brilliance, Spain also reached the final of the 2024-25 Nations League, eventually going down to Portugal on penalties following a 2-2 draw in the final.

Spain's last five Nations League matches have seen them both score multiple goals and concede multiple goals, which is the longest run by any nation – in any tier – since the tournament's inception in 2018.

La Roja have reached three of the last four Nations League finals, also losing to France in 2020-21 and beating Croatia on penalties in 2022-23. Excluding spot-kicks, they have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).
And during the last edition of the Nations League, only Cristiano Ronaldo (eight goals) outscored Mikel Oyarzabal (four).

The Real Sociedad forward has 26 goals involvements across his last 25 international appearances (19 goals, seven assists), a run that started with him scoring the winner against England in the Euro 2024 final.
England – Jude Bellingham
While England's attack is spearheaded by one of Yamal's Ballon d'Or rivals in Harry Kane, Bellingham has been the Three Lions talisman this year, netting seven goals in 10 appearances for England.
David Platt was the last midfielder to find the net more often for them in a single calendar year, back in 1993 (eight).
Barcelona have scored 31 goals in their first seven games in LaLiga this season, with only Sevilla in 1940-41 (40) ever bettering their tally at this stage.

And Yamal has been a key part of their sensational attacking start, with only team-mate Raphinha (12) bettering his seven goals in the competition and only Kylian Mbappe (41) having more shots than his 38.

ygh90t5xvllp1ijr0nqxvxboo.title: Ancelotti encourages Brazil 'to play with joy' during difficult period
ygh90t5xvllp1ijr0nqxvxboo.subtitle: Brazil are undergoing a reset after their disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, and Carlo Ancelotti believes they must enjoy the process.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti has encouraged his Brazil players to "play with joy" during a "difficult period" for the national team.
Brazil were knocked out in the round of 16 at the World Cup this summer, prompting Ancelotti to overhaul the squad in preparation for the 2028 Copa America and 2030 World Cup.
While record-scorer Neymar retired after the tournament, the likes of Casemiro and Fabinho were left out by Ancelotti, who has given more minutes to younger players during this international break.
Brazil faced Australia twice in September, drawing 1-1 in Townsville before winning 4-2 in Brisbane, though Raphinha did suffer an injury in the victory.
Ancelotti's side take on India for the first time on Saturday, and he wants his players to play without pressure in Kolkata.
"The joy of playing football is important to Brazilians," said Ancelotti.
"Happiness is a very important quality that Brazilians have as part of their culture. So, I would like the players to play with joy, with happiness.
"Because sometimes, with the pressure of the game, you forget what football is, that it's a sport, that it's entertainment. And you have to play with joy.
"The truth is that these are tests. We're going to do another test [against India].

"I spoke with all the young players who are going to play or played in the first game and told them that for them it's not a test, it's an opportunity to show the quality they can have. So they need to take all of this calmly because it's not a test for them.
"It's true, the last few years for the Brazilian national team haven't been very good. Since 2002, Brazil hasn't managed to win the World Cup.
"All these defeats, this whole difficult period, serve as motivation for us to be a new generation of players who can compete with the best in the coming years."

yiidc45bzl8619509wbafcn63.title: Gasperini resolved to pick up where Roma left off in Serie A
yiidc45bzl8619509wbafcn63.subtitle: Roma sit top of the Serie A table ahead of the return to action this weekend, and Gian Piero Gasperini does not want their level to drop.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini is determined to see Roma "start where we left off" in Serie A when they return from the international break.
Roma made a stunning start to the 2026-27 campaign and sit top of the table, above reigning champions Inter due to their superior goal difference.
It is the first time since 2014-15 (when they recorded five wins) that Roma have remained unbeaten across their opening five league matches of the season.
Gasperini has so far been hesitant to say that Roma are in the Serie A title race, but they were rampant before the international break.
They are the second-highest scorers (14 goals, behind Inter's 15), and have the joint-second-best defensive record, conceding just three times (Cagliari have let in two).

"We had a pretty small number of players and couldn't play any friendlies, so we went for continuity with the work that we did in the first week and then took a few days off," Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia.
"[Monday] is the last day of holiday, and after that, we will get back into the league mentality, which we left during a great period of results and performances. We want to start where we left off.
"There have been lots of small factors, starting with the fact that I inherited a group that gave me their availability from the very first training session.
"The team had had a good end to the previous season, but the players immediately showed a willingness to explore different paths and different types of football.

"I also had the trust from the club. I've been appreciated by a club that initially brought me in as an opponent and rival. There was even a bit of scepticism. Gaining the appreciation of the Roma supporters has been a great success for me; I'm truly grateful."
Gasperini (299) is close to winning his 300th match as a manager in Serie A.
Only four managers have reached this milestone so far in the competition: Giovanni Trapattoni (352), Massimiliano Allegri (324), Luciano Spalletti (305) and Nereo Rocco (302).
He could reach that landmark against Como when his team returns to action on October 11, with Cesc Fabregas' side also in good form, having lost just one of their five league games so far (W3 D1).
"Anyone who watches football appreciates the evolution of their team, the quality of players they have and the quality of the games they play," Gasperini said about Como.
"Inter are still the strongest in terms of their squad and results, but Como can fight up there along with the rest of them.
"I've seen Fabregas say he uses Subbuteo to explain how to attack with depth. I have to use it to figure out how to stop him."
Gasperini is also preparing for the return of Roma's former boss Jose Mourinho, who will bring Real Madrid to Stadio Olimpico in the Champions League next week.
Mourinho led Roma to win the inaugural edition of the Conference League in May 2022, beating Feyenoord 1-0 in the final.
"Jose is, rightly, a special one, and he manages to find success on and off the pitch," Gasperini said of Mourinho.

"He won the Conference League and reached a Europa League final with Roma. He might have done a bit less in the league, but most of the fans still appreciate him. That means he has something special."

ykmt3bgt5dcn1rwmw6vsayuo3.title: Sorensen urges Whitecaps to keep performing at extremely high level
ykmt3bgt5dcn1rwmw6vsayuo3.subtitle: The Vancouver Whitecaps are looking to strengthen their grip on top spot in the Western Conference as they host playoff-chasing D.C. United.
paragraphs: Jesper Sorensen is thrilled with the level of Vancouver Whitecaps' performances this term and is determined to finish the MLS regular season strongly, starting with D.C. United.
Vancouver sit top of the Western Conference standings on 49 points, and they could clinch their playoff spot this weekend, though they would need to win and hope a few other results go their way.
They have alternated between a loss and a win in their last four league games, most recently brushing aside Real Salt Lake 3-0.
With not long left of the regular season, Sorensen revealed he is not changing his approach to games as he wants to maintain the Whitecaps' consistency ahead of a busy period.
"If we don't perform well enough, we can still win a game, but we'll not win consistently if we're not performing well on a consistent basis," Sorensen said. "For me, it's about how you play.
"I think over the course of the season, we have been performing extremely well, and that's what we have to keep up. You can lose a game even as the better team; that's how football works.
"But if you don't consistently perform and push the players towards good performances, it's difficult to improve."

D.C. are looking to try and make a late push for the playoffs; they sit 11th in the East but are only four points behind ninth-place FC Cincinnati despite winning just one of their last eight games (D4 L3).
They lost 2-1 to Charlotte FC last time out, and although the pressure is starting to mount on head coach Rene Weiler, he is focusing on the journey his players are going on.
"We are in the process of building something more sustainable, more consistent," he said. "We did the first step together.
"We cleaned up, and now we have to try to stabilise the team and then make a third step to winning more games.
"To overtake one or two teams [in the playoff race] is a big step, but I see a team much better than last season."
Vancouver Whitecaps – Yohei Takaoka
Yohei Takaoka has registered 11 clean sheets this season, recording 10+ shutouts in consecutive seasons.
The only other goalkeeper in club history to have 10 or more shutouts in any MLS season was David Ousted, who also did it in consecutive seasons (2014 and 2015).
D.C. United – Lucas Bartlett
Lucas Bartlett scored his third goal of the season for D.C. on Saturday, which ranks as the third-most among the team this season.
He is the first defender to score at least three goals in a single regular season for the club since Donovan Pines in 2023.
MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN
Vancouver and D.C. are meeting for the 12th time and the first time since a 2-2 draw in Canada in September 2023.
That was the only match in the fixture's history in which both teams scored multiple goals, as the series has averaged 1.4 combined goals per match.

The Whitecaps earned a 3-0 win against RSL last time out, making it the club's ninth shutout win by multiple goals in the 2026 regular season. The MLS record for such games in a single campaign is 10, set by Chivas USA in 2007, Atlanta United in 2019 and Philadelphia Union in 2022.
As for D.C., they have played out a draw in five of their last seven road matches and six of their 11 games away from home this season.
The six away draws are United's most in a single regular season, since having seven in 2018, while it is two more than they had in 2025 (four).
Vancouver Whitecaps – 73.4%
