They lost 2-1 to Charlotte FC last time out, and although the pressure is starting to mount on head coach Rene Weiler, he is focusing on the journey his players are going on.

"We are in the process of building something more sustainable, more consistent," he said. "We did the first step together.

"We cleaned up, and now we have to try to stabilise the team and then make a third step to winning more games.

"To overtake one or two teams [in the playoff race] is a big step, but I see a team much better than last season."

PLAYERS TO WATCH

Vancouver Whitecaps – Yohei Takaoka

Yohei Takaoka has registered 11 clean sheets this season, recording 10+ shutouts in consecutive seasons.

The only other goalkeeper in club history to have 10 or more shutouts in any MLS season was David Ousted, who also did it in consecutive seasons (2014 and 2015).

D.C. United – Lucas Bartlett

Lucas Bartlett scored his third goal of the season for D.C. on Saturday, which ranks as the third-most among the team this season.

He is the first defender to score at least three goals in a single regular season for the club since Donovan Pines in 2023.

MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN

Vancouver and D.C. are meeting for the 12th time and the first time since a 2-2 draw in Canada in September 2023.

That was the only match in the fixture's history in which both teams scored multiple goals, as the series has averaged 1.4 combined goals per match.

The Whitecaps earned a 3-0 win against RSL last time out, making it the club's ninth shutout win by multiple goals in the 2026 regular season. The MLS record for such games in a single campaign is 10, set by Chivas USA in 2007, Atlanta United in 2019 and Philadelphia Union in 2022.

As for D.C., they have played out a draw in five of their last seven road matches and six of their 11 games away from home this season.

The six away draws are United's most in a single regular season, since having seven in 2018, while it is two more than they had in 2025 (four).

OPTA WIN PROBABILITY

Vancouver Whitecaps – 73.4%

Draw – 16%

D.C. United – 10.6%

ym2xb51gsj51mi4qx7qffxho.title: Iraola sees 'every competition as an opportunity' ahead of EFL Cup clash with Chelsea
ym2xb51gsj51mi4qx7qffxho.subtitle: Andoni Iraola may be in his first season with Liverpool, but he knows there is pressure on for the Reds to lift trophies.
paragraphs: Andoni Iraola says Liverpool must treat every competition as a chance to lift silverware, as they prepare to face Chelsea in an EFL Cup round-of-16 showdown.
A quarter-final place will be on the line at Anfield as two Premier League heavyweights do battle, with Liverpool having already overcome Tottenham in the third round.
Liverpool were eliminated in the fourth round last season, going down 3-0 at home to Crystal Palace.
They have not gone out before the quarter-final stage in consecutive seasons since 2017-18 (third round) and 2018-19 (third round), the latter of which was a home defeat to Chelsea.
Liverpool's two previous EFL Cup meetings with Chelsea were in the final of the competition, with the Reds lifting the trophy in both 2021-22 (0-0, won on penalties) and 2023-24 (1-0).
And though Iraola acknowledges Liverpool were unfortunate to draw Xabi Alonso's side so early in the competition, he knows he will always be under pressure to deliver silverware to Merseyside.
"We want to be in the next round. We've been unlucky in the draw; we are playing Chelsea. They have been unlucky also," Iraola told reporters.
"But we want to earn the right to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win.
"Every competition is an opportunity, especially when you are the coach of Liverpool. You have to take it like this.
"I would love to win tomorrow and have the chance to go further in the competition, but I know we will have to play well and beat a very good team."
Iraola was upbeat about Florian Wirtz's chances of being involved, after the Germany international was substituted during Sunday's 2-0 win over Brighton with an apparent ankle injury.

The Reds boss also acknowledged there was a need for squad rotation, with Liverpool playing three more games – against Arsenal and Crystal Palace in the Premier League and Fenerbahce in the Champions League – prior to the November international break.
"Florian was fine, I'm quite optimistic that he will be available," Iraola said.
"There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game, we want to be competitive. We need to see how the legs are.
"Not just in the League Cup, but also in the Champions League, we are trying to make some changes from game to game, because I think it's almost mandatory."

ypxlhrxhp6ib1jcblh7i2tdft.title: Juventus strikers Kolo Muani and Woltemade to start together against Rennes
ypxlhrxhp6ib1jcblh7i2tdft.subtitle: After they both scored in Juventus' Europa League win over Celta Vigo, Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade will both start against Rennes.
paragraphs: Randal Kolo Muani insisted he is "very comfortable playing with any team-mate" as he prepares to start alongside Nick Woltemade for Juventus against Rennes.
Both strikers joined the Bianconeri this summer, with Kolo Muani securing a permanent move from Paris Saint-Germain, while Woltemade joined on a season-long loan from Newcastle United.
Kolo Muani has scored three times this season to Woltemade's two goals, though they both netted in a 2-1 win over Celta Vigo last time out in the Europa League.

Woltemade has scored in both games for Juventus in the Europa League this season; only two players have netted in their first three appearances for the club in major European competition: Darko Kovacevic in 1999 and Roberto Baggio in 1990.
After the win over Celta, Woltemade stated his desire to start alongside Kolo Muani, which did not happen in their 3-0 defeat to Lazio on the weekend.
However, ahead of their Europa League match-up with Rennes, Spalletti confirmed both strikers will start on Thursday.
"In football, it's important that the coach trusts you. The coach gives me valuable advice to keep going beyond my limits," said Kolo Muani.

"I'm very comfortable playing with any team-mate. In training, we work on what the coach asks us to do, but we know it's then up to us to put it into practice, and we also have the freedom to take responsibility."
Juve have won their last four home matches in major European competition, scoring 12 goals and conceding two. They last had a longer home winning run between November 2020 and December 2021 (six).
The Bianconeri and Rennes previously met in the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final, with the Italian side winning 4-2 on aggregate (2-0 home, 2-2 away).
"Rennes will come here looking to win," added Kolo Muani.
"We won our first two matches, and we'll try to win the third as well. Of course, I hope that performing well here will also help me return to the national team."

yre5cfl6j0zb1jkokmfeged8y.title: Sunderland 0-2 Brighton: Three in a row for Hurzeler's men despite Struijk red
yre5cfl6j0zb1jkokmfeged8y.subtitle: Pascal Struijk saw red but Brighton were still too good in a 2-0 Premier League triumph over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.
paragraphs: Brighton earned a third straight Premier League victory as Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam were on target in a 2-0 win at Sunderland despite Pascal Struijk's red card.
De Cuyper opened the scoring after 53 minutes at the Stadium of Light, sliding past Robin Roefs after great work by Pascal Gross.

Struijk was shown a straight red for bringing down Wilson Isidor shortly after, but Hadjam made sure of the points in second-half injury time as Brighton backed up wins over Coventry City and Arsenal.
Brighton had the better openings in a dismal first half, with Diego Gomez denied by one-on-one by Roefs in just the eighth minute after an error from Kevin Danso.
Nordi Mukiele's 30-yard effort was saved low to the left by Bart Verbruggen in Sunderland's only shot on target of the first half.
Struijk's guided header from Gross' free-kick came back off the left post on the stroke of half-time, but the visitors went ahead after 53 minutes.
Gomez's flicked header was picked up by Gross, who slipped in De Cuyper to coolly roll past Roefs into the bottom-left corner.
Just four minutes later, Brighton were down to 10 as Struijk was sent off when referee Thomas Bramall judged his haul on Isidor was a denial of a goalscoring opportunity.
Gross nearly made it 2-0 with an audacious effort from inside his own half after picking Granit Xhaka's pocket, but Roefs was relieved to see it go past the right-hand post.
Brighton did make sure of the win, though, as Georginio Rutter rolled the ball into the path of Hadjam, who drilled his shot past Roefs and into the bottom-right corner.
Gross contributes again as Brighton roll on
There was little to split the teams in a first half that produced little in terms of quality, with just one shot on target from either side – albeit Struijk also hit the post for Brighton.
The Seagulls, fresh off a wonderful 3-0 win over champions Arsenal prior to the international break, will feel they edged proceedings and you could not really argue when they hit the front.
Gross was influential again for Brighton, and he now has four Premier League assists – the most in the division – and has contributed two goals and four assists in his past three top-flight outings.
Brighton, who are just two points off top spot in third, have now won on back-to-back visits to the Stadium of Light having failed to win on any of their previous nine league visits (D2, L7).
The visitors were good value for the win, and finished the game with an xG of 1.12 to Sunderland's 0.64 despite playing much of the second half a man down.
Fabian Hurzeler's side now have three straight wins without conceding, with Brighton having achieved such a feat just once in the Premier League back in 2018.

yrh4sxzw546m13380fknosd85.title: Fluminense 1-2 Palmeiras: Wesley inspires Copa Libertadores hope in semi-final first leg
yrh4sxzw546m13380fknosd85.subtitle: Palmeiras have a 2-1 lead to defend in the second leg of their Copa Libertadores semi-final tie next week, though it could have been more.
paragraphs: Wesley Nata's stoppage-time goal inspired hope for Fluminense in their bid to reach the Copa Libertadores final, but they still have it all to do following a 2-1 first-leg semi-final loss to Palmeiras.

It was three-time champions and 2025 runners-up Palmeiras who took control at the Maracana, with Flaco Lopez and Marlon Freitas striking to put them 2-0 up before Wesley cut their lead to one goal late on.

Neither team threatened with regularity during a tense first half, though Carlos Miguel stood tall to deny Fluminense forward Hulk shortly before the scoring was opened at the other end, in stoppage time.

Joaquin Piquerez crossed first-time from the left after making an underlapping run in support of Andreas Pereira, and though Lopez's shot on the slide was straight at Fluminense goalkeeper Fabio, he could not keep it out.
Fabio was forced into a sharp save by Piquerez at the start of the second half, while a glancing header from Agustin Canobbio drifted wide at the other end.

Fabio then made himself big to smother Felipe Anderson's shot, but when he parried Ramon Sosa's attempt in the 85th minute, Fluminense failed to clear their lines and Freitas drove a half-volley into the bottom-left corner.

Though Fluminense's performance was largely flat, they will only need to overturn a one-goal deficit in Sao Paulo, after Wesley headed Guga's floated cross over the stranded Carlos Miguel three minutes into added time.
Fluminense's home record ends after meek display

Fluminense were participating in their third Copa Libertadores semi-final tie, having never previously lost a match at this stage (W2 D2), scoring at least two goals in every one of those games and progressing to the final on both occasions (2008 and 2023).
In addition, they had never previously lost a home match in the knockout stages of the Copa Libertadores, with 15 wins and five draws in 20 attempts.
After seeing those records swept away, they will have to do things the hard way if they are to reach South America's showpiece match for a third time.
They may feel fortunate to have received a lifeline from Wesley late on, having only generated 0.48 expected goals (xG) from 11 shots, compared to Palmeiras' 1.18 from seven.

After scoring the opener, Lopez leads all Palmeiras players for both goals and assists (four of each) in this year's Libertadores, and the Alviverde have not avoided defeat in seven of their last 10 away Libertadores games against fellow Brazilian teams (W4 D3 L3).

yx2r1tpe17lw1omm77kg9e5yz.title: 'If there were five Monumentals, they would be full' – Scaloni braced for emotional Messi farewell
yx2r1tpe17lw1omm77kg9e5yz.subtitle: Lionel Messi will play his 208th and final game for Argentina on Tuesday, and Lionel Scaloni knows there will not be a dry eye in the house.
paragraphs: Lionel Scaloni feels Argentina's supporters could fill the Estadio Monumental five times over for Lionel Messi's farewell outing, which he is sure will be an emotional occasion.
The World Cup runners-up trounced Burkina Faso 7-0 on Saturday, following up their 4-0 win over Bolivia to remain perfect during this international break.
Argentina's next match will be their most eagerly anticipated of all, as Messi returns to the fold for one final time, for a farewell match against Benin on Tuesday.

Messi announced his decision to retire from international football in the aftermath of July's extra-time defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, and he will end his Argentina career with 208 senior caps – the most of any player in the team's history.
Messi also has more goals for Argentina than any other player (125) and more goal involvements at the World Cup than anyone else in history (33 – 21 goals, 12 assists).
The 39-year-old is the only player to start three World Cup finals, leading Argentina to glory in Qatar four years ago, and Scaloni expects a reception befitting an all-time great.
"I imagine Tuesday's match to be very emotional for everyone, including Leo. It will be an unforgettable day," Scaloni said.
"It will be his day and that of his team-mates, who also gave him his greatest footballing joy. I am grateful to be able to enjoy it, and I am going to be a mere spectator.

"I imagine that if there were five Monumentals, they would be full. I want people to understand what he transmits on the pitch, to his team-mates, to opponents, for people on the outside. That is what we are going to miss the most."

While Argentina are entering the post-Messi era, with a host of young players – including Nico Paz and Franco Mastantuono – impressing in recent games, they do at least look to have continuity in the dugout.

Scaloni is expected to renew his contract to at least run through the 2028 Copa America and potentially the 2030 World Cup, and midfielder Enzo Fernandez knows how important that would be for the Albiceleste.
"It would be very important for us that he continues, he put this together. We have to continue competing at the highest level," Fernandez said.
"Now we have to process the issue of Leo leaving and continue with the same line along which we came."
Asked how he retains his passion for a role he has held for eight years, Scaloni said: "I always try to live it.
"I understand what this position implies, but I believe that you can do both things and not lock yourself up only in a football office. Being able to enjoy yourself is important."

yyc48whrkuhm14mv9ti4qg6wu.title: Smith says focus remains on Charlotte after recording 50th victory
yyc48whrkuhm14mv9ti4qg6wu.subtitle: Dean Smith enjoyed his 50th win in charge of Charlotte FC last weekend, and he will be hoping to add another against the Chicago Fire.
paragraphs: Dean Smith intends to continue winning at Charlotte FC after claiming his 50th victory in charge of the Crown in all competitions, last time out against D.C. United.
Smith replaced Christian Lattanzio at Charlotte in December 2023 and has gone on to manage 112 matches for the club, with their results improving year-on-year under him.
Charlotte have finished fifth and then fourth in the Eastern Conference with Smith at the helm, while they find themselves fourth in the division so far this season.
However, they have failed to go beyond the first round of the playoffs while Smith has been at the club, something they will be hoping to rectify by the end of the 2026 campaign.
Ashley Westwood and Allan Saint-Maximin were on target in Smith's 50th win with Charlotte, with their goals sealing a 2-1 victory over D.C. at Bank of America Stadium.
Charlotte meet the Chicago Fire this weekend, and while Smith was thrilled with his personal achievement, he said that his main focus remains on the team's aspirations.
"[I'm] just pleased," Smith said. "I mean, it's 50 wins in 112 games. It's a good record, but we just want to keep winning them.
"It's not about my records, it's about the club. Every win, you probably don't enjoy them as much as you should because you're always thinking about the next game.
"So, hopefully we can get to the end of the season, and I'm enjoying the win for a special reason. I think we're getting there. The building blocks have been there.
"The ideology, everybody knows what is expected of them, so I think that's the easy part. The hardest part is always recruiting good people and good players."
Chicago are just four points behind Charlotte heading into this weekend's meeting, and they will be seeking a return to winning ways following a 3-0 defeat to Nashville SC.
Sam Surridge's 33rd-minute opener was followed up by second-half strikes from Cristian Espinoza and Hany Mukhtar to seal a comfortable triumph for the Eastern leaders.

The Fire were only able to register an expected goals (xG) total of 0.91 from their nine shots, only one of which was on target, with Gregg Berhalter conceding after the match that his team were simply beaten by stronger opposition.
"I don't look at it as if the result was unfortunate for us. We just lost to a better team. It's really simple," Berhalter said.
"I think the most important lesson from this evening is that Nashville are a benchmark for us. This is a team that we want to reach and with which we want to be able to compete.
"At the beginning, we were a little too conservative. We held on, then we lost a goal. We got back into the game, but then we lost another one.
"For us, the conclusion is that as a team, we have to improve."

The Fire's task against Charlotte will be made even more difficult, with Noah Allen, Chris Brady, Anzor Mekvabishvili, Puso Dithejane, Robert Lewandowski and Robin Lod all joining up with their respective national teams for the extended international break.
Charlotte FC – Allan Saint-Maximin
Since making his debut for Charlotte, only Cavan Sullivan (30), Kristoffer Velde (25) and Guilherme (23) have completed more dribbles in the MLS than Saint-Maximin's 22.
The former Newcastle United star also has five assists and one goal for Charlotte in that time, and he will be hoping to make his mark once again for Smith's side.
Chicago Fire – Maren Haile-Selassie
Haile-Selassie has scored eight goals this season for Chicago, the most among players currently on the Fire's roster.
Five of those goals have come in road matches this season, including four goals in his last four road matches.
MATCH PREDICTION: CHARLOTTE FC WIN

Chicago earned a 2-1 win over Charlotte in the first meeting between the two teams this season back in August. It was the third straight win in the series for the Fire, after they had lost five straight in the fixture entering last season.
The Fire were shut out for just the second time this regular season in their road loss to Nashville, tied for the fewest games being held scoreless this season with Inter Miami.
That ended a 21-game run with a goal in league play, as it was the first time Chicago had failed to score since March 7, against the Columbus Crew.

Dean Smith intends to continue winning at Charlotte FC after claiming his 50th victory in charge of the Crown in all competitions, last time out against D.C. United. 

Smith replaced Christian Lattanzio at Charlotte in December 2023 and has gone on to manage 112 matches for the club, with their results improving year-on-year under him.

Charlotte have finished fifth and then fourth in the Eastern Conference with Smith at the helm, while they find themselves fourth in the division so far this season. 

However, they have failed to go beyond the first round of the playoffs while Smith has been at the club, something they will be hoping to rectify by the end of the 2026 campaign. 

Ashley Westwood and Allan Saint-Maximin were on target in Smith's 50th win with Charlotte, with their goals sealing a 2-1 victory over D.C. at Bank of America Stadium.

yyjyzcfg4gz1v1lygu5o6dxf.title: Klopp not promising silverware ahead of Germany debut
yyjyzcfg4gz1v1lygu5o6dxf.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp is preparing to take charge of Germany for the first time on Thursday, though he was quick to temper expectations of his team.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp refused to make any promises of delivering silverware for Germany ahead of his debut against the Netherlands in the Nations League.
Klopp is preparing for his first game in charge at the Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday after replacing Julian Nagelsmann following Germany's disappointing World Cup campaign.
Germany were knocked out in the round of 32 at the World Cup after losing on penalties to Paraguay, a defeat which led to Nagelsmann's departure after three years in charge.
The former Liverpool boss has signed a four-year deal, which will see him guide the team at the European Championship in 2028 and the World Cup two years later.
Nagelsmann had said following Germany's Euro 2024 quarter-final defeat that he was sad he ​would have to wait two years to lift the World Cup, something that did not come true.
Klopp was also asked about his remark at the ​start of his Liverpool tenure that he would probably have won a title if ​he was still in the job four years later.
"I ​don't want to promise anything," Klopp told a press conference. "What I can say ​is we will try and that's what it is about now. That's where we are at ‌the ⁠moment.
"We have had a little debate, rightly or wrongly, I think, about the impression that we have a lower quality than in other countries.
"This has become the main issue. We need to train better, train differently. But I firmly believe that it is always possible to improve training.
"This not only applies to football, but also to many other areas."
Germany have failed to go beyond the round of 32 in each of the last three editions of the World Cup, going out in the group stage in 2018 and 2022 before this summer's exit.
They last lifted silverware on the international stage in 2014, when they won the World Cup in Brazil.
Klopp made the decision to name two separate squads ahead of their Nations League fixtures against the Netherlands, Serbia and Greece, who they play home and away.
He named 16 uncapped players, with 44 players selected in total.
"I am in charge of the senior team and my task is ​to take the football there so that we are in ​with a ⁠chance to win every game we play," Klopp added.
"It won't work every day, but we are working at it. I hope we can see some things already tomorrow. We ⁠need to ​take steps and the boys are ready for ​that."
This will be the first meeting between the two nations since October 2024, with Jamie Leweling's 64th-minute strike enough to earn a 1-0 win for Germany.
Germany are unbeaten in their last three matches against the Netherlands (W2 D1) since a 4-2 defeat in a European Championship qualifier in September 2019.
"That doesn't mean anything to me, because I've never felt that rivalry," Klopp said of the rivalry between Germany and the Netherlands.
"It would be better to ask Rudi Voller, as someone who has actually experienced it firsthand.

"I know what this game means, and ideally, the atmosphere tomorrow night will be heated. It will be a difficult game for the players because the opposition is really good, with tremendous talent and some excellent footballers.
"It's crazy how many top players the Dutch national team has. If we want to have any chance at all, we have to approach it as a real 'derby'.
"For us, it's the beginning of something. We want to get off to a good start. Everything surrounding the game only plays a minor role."

yz317m1a7zkw1cjih001h8tcf.title: 'Don't betray me' – Mourinho highlights need for trust with Real Madrid players
yz317m1a7zkw1cjih001h8tcf.subtitle: Jose Mourinho has returned to Real Madrid, but he still has certain rules that help him get the best out of his players.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho insists that trust between player and manager is key to getting the best out of a team as he looks to get Real Madrid back to the top of their game.
Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu after a 13-year absence and has made a strong start so far, losing just two of his eight matches in charge (W6).
Despite that, Madrid sit six points behind runaway leaders Barcelona, who have a 100% record so far, and went into the break on the back of a controversial 2-1 loss to derby rivals Atletico Madrid.
Mourinho is tasked with bringing some silverware back to Los Blancos, after they failed to get their hands on a single trophy last season and also struggled domestically in 2024-25.
"Don't betray me," Mourinho told the Bet It Drives Show when asked about trust and management.
"When I say don't betray me, of course, I'm speaking about football. Don't betray me, and I'll always be there for you.
"There are rules that are not negotiable. If you report at 9 a.m., it's 9 a.m. for everybody. If you arrive at 9.15, even if you're a superstar, you just can't. I don't accept it.
"But another thing is giving them freedom to express themselves."
Madrid started last season with Xabi Alonso at the helm, but he was sacked in January and replaced by Alvaro Arbeloa.
He then left his post at the end of 2025-26, with Madrid opting to turn to a more familiar figure to try and stop Barcelona's dominance.
During his first spell between 2010 and 2013, he won one LaLiga title, a Copa del Rey and the Supercopa de Espana.
"After two seasons where the biggest club in the world didn't have the best results and a little 'divorce' with the fans, the club contacted me," he said.
"They told me 'We know you. You know us. You know the club, you know the culture.
"We need you. We need you to rebuild. We need you to start again an amazing decade that the club had. We need a person with your profile'."

z50mt167hwpu1rb7p32bypwc9.title: Denmark 2-4 Portugal: No Ronaldo, no problem for Jesus in six-goal thriller
z50mt167hwpu1rb7p32bypwc9.subtitle: Cristiano Ronaldo's sensational departure from the Portugal camp did not affect Jorge Jesus' side against Denmark, as they earned a 4-2 win.
paragraphs: Portugal made light of Cristiano Ronaldo's absence as they earned a thrilling 4-2 away win over Denmark in the Nations League on Thursday.

The defending champions were playing their first game since Ronaldo abruptly left their camp on Wednesday, saying he would "tell the truth" about his reported row with head coach Jorge Jesus "in due time".
But Portugal did not miss the five-time Ballon d'Or winner in Copenhagen, with Joao Cancelo, Goncalo Ramos, Vitinha and Joao Felix scoring to keep them perfect after three games in Group A4.

After Rasmus Hojlund failed to get a touch on Adam Daghim's ball across the face of the Portugal goal, the visitors started to take control of the game, with Ramos turning Cancelo's scuffed cross-shot against the left post.

But the Selecao did have the lead just nine seconds after that near miss. Daghim's attempt to kickstart a Denmark counter-attack was cut out by Cancelo, who exchanged passes with Ramos before clipping a cute finish over Mads Hermansen.

Wearing the iconic number seven shirt following Ronaldo's departure, Rafael Leao forced Hermansen into action before Denmark struck back in stunning fashion, Mikkel Damsgaard curling a glorious effort into the far corner from the left of the box in the 23rd minute.

But the hosts were not level for long, as Ramos finished off another lovely Portugal move two minutes later. He backheeled skilfully to Fernandes before darting in behind, racing onto the Portugal captain's return pass and prodding into the near corner.

Hermansen denied Ramos and Fernandes either side of half-time, with the first of those saves coming after he cheaply conceded possession himself, but Hojlund got Denmark level eight minutes after the restart. He lobbed Diogo Costa following Damsgaard's defence-splitting pass, then taunted Portugal by copying Ronaldo's iconic "siuuu" celebration.

Portugal refused to go away, though, and after Ramos' acrobatic effort whistled over the crossbar, Vitinha ghosted onto Fernandes' cross and nodded past Hermansen at his near post with 67 minutes on the clock.
And there was still time for Ronaldo's Al-Nassr team-mate Joao Felix to add a fourth goal, sweeping a cutback from fellow substitute Diogo Dalot home three minutes from time.
Portugal attack thrives without Ronaldo
As is so often the case with Portugal, all the headlines in the build-up to Thursday's game were dominated by one man.

Ronaldo may be the all-time leading scorer in men's internationals, finding the net 146 times in 234 outings for Portugal, but Jesus responded firmly when asked about the forward's shock departure, saying: "It will never be any player that will change my ideas as coach. Never. Not him, not anyone in football."
And, at least on this evidence, perhaps Portugal are better off without Ronaldo in their lineup.

The combinations for their first two goals – both of which involved Ramos, the man leading the line in Ronaldo's absence – were slick, and they generated 19 shots and 2.74 expected goals (xG) throughout the game, compared to Denmark's 12 shots and 0.67 xG.

Hojlund celebrated mischievously after making it 2-2, but of all the goals, Vitinha's looked the most like something out of the Ronaldo playbook. Despite his stature as one of the shortest players on the pitch, the Paris Saint-Germain star scored his first senior international goal – on his 46th cap – with a perfect downward header.

z5fkq30i4m7613zir6le3jn3o.title: 'I'd love to play there' – Arsenal's Raya open to future LaLiga move
z5fkq30i4m7613zir6le3jn3o.subtitle: David Raya has played his entire career in England since leaving Spain in 2012, but he said a return to his homeland could be a possibility.
paragraphs: David Raya revealed he "would love" to play in LaLiga during his professional career, but the Arsenal goalkeeper insisted he was happy with the Premier League champions.
Raya, who joined Arsenal from Brentford in 2024 after spending the previous season on loan with the Gunners, has become a crucial part of Mikel Arteta's side since his arrival.
He has made 157 appearances across all competitions for Arsenal, keeping 74 clean sheets, at least 31 more than any other Premier League goalkeeper (Jordan Pickford – 43).
It's also 11 more shutouts than any other goalkeeper across Europe's top five leagues (Yann Sommer – 66) in that time, as well as winning three Premier League Golden Gloves.
The Spaniard has played his entire career in England, turning out for the likes of Blackburn Rovers, Southport, Brentford and now Arsenal.
But when asked about the possibility of returning to Spain, where he left in 2012 at the age of 16 to join Blackburn, Raya told Marca: "Yes, I would love to.
"I would love to try out LaLiga. For now, I'm very happy here [at Arsenal], but I would certainly like to experience the Spanish league.
"I think it's a very competitive league. Perhaps, in the future, I could play for a Spanish club. I'm Spanish, and I'd love to play there – that's for sure."
Raya has carried on his fine form in the Premier League this season, with only Brighton's Bart Verbruggen (five) keeping more clean sheets than the Arsenal shot-stopper's four.
The 31-year-old was crucial in ending Arsenal's wait for the top-flight title last season, while also helping them reach the final of the Champions League and EFL Cup.
He was also part of Luis de la Fuente's Spain side that lifted their second World Cup this summer, though Raya did not play a single minute, with Unai Simon preferred in net.
"I believe I've had a perfect year," Raya added. "Perhaps the only thing missing was playing in the World Cup.
"Every year since I arrived at Arsenal, I've continued to improve and hopefully that will keep happening.

"But I truly believe this year, by winning the Premier League and playing a decisive role in the league, the Champions League, and the Community Shield. It has been my best season as a professional, being impactful and lifting trophies."
Arsenal face Bayern Munich in a mouth-watering Champions League tie on Wednesday, and Raya has his eyes firmly set on adding more silverware to his trophy cabinet.
"I want to win it all," he said. "We want to establish ourselves as favourites, and that is our goal.
"Hopefully, this year we can improve upon last season by winning the Champions League, but there is still a long way to go before that happens."

z7v2ve94jedb1krprocjmls3o.title: Galatasaray 1-4 Barcelona: Yamal inspires Flick's side to comeback win
z7v2ve94jedb1krprocjmls3o.subtitle: Barcelona swept aside another Champions League opponent as Galatasaray proved no match for Lamine Yamal on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal delivered a creative masterclass in the Champions League as Barcelona came from behind to win 4-1 away at Galatasaray.
Aleksey Batrakov's 28th-minute opener had Barca on the ropes on Tuesday, before Baris Alper Yilmaz saw a headed finish ruled out after a VAR check.

But Hansi Flick's side roared back with Joao Cancelo's first-half leveller, before Yamal teed up both Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon after the interval to make it two wins in as many European games for Barca.

Gordon had earlier seen a great opening go amiss after Ugurcan Cakir denied him from Pedri's lofted throughball, while Dani Olmo wasted a free header from Yamal's cross as Barca dominated the opening stages.
Those misses came back to haunt Barcelona when Rafael Leao cut back for Batrakov, whose right-footed drive from the edge of the box beat Joan Garcia with a slight deflection off Cancelo.

Galatasaray thought they had doubled their lead six minutes later. Yilmaz headed home from Victor Osimhen's flick after Batrakov's left-sided corner, only for the full-back to be found offside after a VAR review.
That reprieve paid dividends for Barca just before half-time when Olmo stole possession from Davinson Sanchez and teed up Cancelo to curl his leveller into the far corner.
Gordon should have put Barcelona ahead early into the second half, but somehow steered off target after Yamal laid on a glorious chance for his fellow winger.
But they did not have to wait too long to take the lead as Fermin stooped to head into the bottom-right corner from Yamal's dinked delivery in the 50th minute.
Yamal claimed another assist three minutes later, displaying silky feet down the right before offloading for Gordon to thrash in low at Cakir's near post.
The Spain winger was heavily involved in Barca's fourth, too. Gabriel Jesus' heavy touch from Yamal's throughball rolled through for Karim Adeyemi, who hammered past Cakir's left hand.
Yamal blazed over another late chance, while Adeyemi fired into the side netting as Barca eased to yet another victory.
Defensive frailty no problem for free-scoring Barca
Barcelona have thrashed any opponent that has come into their sight so far this season, scoring a ridiculous 34 goals to stay perfect after eight LaLiga games.
Flick's side also crushed Feyenoord 5-1 in their opener in this competition, but the first half on Tuesday marked arguably their toughest test yet.

Galatasaray gleefully exploited a leaky Barca defence early on. They failed to keep a clean sheet in last season's entire Champions League campaign, and are yet to record a shutout in this season as well (14 games in total).
But down the other end, Barcelona excelled once again, despite missing talisman Raphinha. The Blaugrana have now scored 84 in 28 Champions League games under Flick.

zdxx6q2tuzjk13wsgn38keor8.title: Luis Enrique lauds PSG's mentality after comeback win
zdxx6q2tuzjk13wsgn38keor8.subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain fell behind to Strasbourg, but Luis Enrique was delighted with the mentality demonstrated by his team in a 3-1 win.
paragraphs: Paris Saint-Germain proved their mentality in their 3-1 comeback win over Strasbourg, so says Luis Enrique.
Two-time European champions PSG fell behind to Giovanni Reyna's effort in the 17th minute at Stade de la Meinau.

However, a late turnaround secured a dramatic victory, with Illia Zabarnyi's 77th-minute leveller paving the way for substitutes Ousmane Dembele, who had earlier missed a penalty, and Desire Doue to clinch the three points.

PSG have now won their last six games in all competitions. Only Barcelona, who Luis Enrique's team face in the Champions League on Tuesday, have a longer current winning streak among teams from the top five European leagues.
And Luis Enrique was thrilled with his team's mentality.
"The teams playing against us have extra motivation, and that is what is difficult to manage when you are a player for a team like PSG," he said.
"But I'm happy. We expected to have difficulties, but we started the match positively. We needed that first goal to feel comfortable in the game.

zg8akpz6tfsq1pbm1tum4atjb.title: 'I would have liked to stay' – Kimmich reluctant to leave Germany camp
zg8akpz6tfsq1pbm1tum4atjb.subtitle: Joshua Kimmich is heading back to Bayern Munich after only being named in the first of Jurgen Klopp's two Germany squads.
paragraphs: Joshua Kimmich admitted he "would have liked to stay" with Germany for the entirety of the international break but understands why Jurgen Klopp called up two squads.
For Klopp's first matches in charge, he opted to call up 44 players across two squads to see as many players as possible in the extended break.
He remains winless after his first two matches in charge, though, having conceded a late equaliser to the Netherlands in a 1-1 draw before suffering a shock 1-0 loss to Greece on Sunday.
Six of the players from Klopp's first squad will stay on with the second: Finn Dahmen, Nico Schlotterbeck, Philipp Treu, Yannik Engelhardt, Bambase Conte and Serge Gnabry.
Florian Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt were originally called up for the second squad but arrived earlier to replace the injured Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala.
Despite being the team captain, Kimmich is not one of those remaining in the squad for their last two games against Serbia and Greece.
"I would have liked to stay, but I also understand that the coach wants to get to know some other players," Kimmich said after the loss to Greece.
"That was the plan from the beginning: that we would rotate the squads.
"Accordingly, I'll be cheering the team on from home."
Klopp is the third German head coach to go winless in his first two international matches (D1 L1).
Previously, this had only happened to Sepp Herberger and Helmut Schon; the two later World Cup-winning coaches then won their third international match.
Germany's next match is at home to Serbia on Thursday before they round off this block of fixtures with a trip to Greece on October 4.

zhklqh0zv4m41kotvtsa2ypuv.title: The Numbers Game: Rampant England aim to finish strong
zhklqh0zv4m41kotvtsa2ypuv.subtitle: Harry Kane is set to make a landmark appearance as England aim to round off the extended international window in style against Czechia.
paragraphs: England round off the first international break of the season, aiming to make it three straight wins in the Nations League.
After starting their campaign with a 3-2 loss to world champions Spain at Wembley, England beat Czechia 2-0 and then thrashed Croatia 7-0.
Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice each, while Jude Bellingham was also on target and laid on three assists. Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also scored in the emphatic victory.
Thomas Tuchel has seen his team plunder 11 goals in the three games across this extended international window so far, and there is one more match to come, as Czechia visit Wembley on Tuesday.
This fixture comes just a week on from a routine win in Prague, where the Three Lions were helped out by Pavel Sulc's red card midway through the first half.
Here, we preview England v Czechia, calling on Opta's key insights.
The Opta supercomputer is making England the clear favourites, with a 79.8% win probability.
Czechia come out on top in just 7.9% of the model's 10,000 data-led simulations, while there is a 12.3% chance of a draw.
And given the head-to-head record between these teams, it is hardly surprising to see England so well fancied.
Czechia have lost six of their eight competitive meetings with England (W2), though they have always responded to back-to-back losses with a win – they have lost their last two.
England are also unbeaten in all eight of their games against Czechia at Wembley (W6 D2), the most recent of which saw the Three Lions finish their Euro 2020 group-stage campaign with a 1-0 win.
The Three Lions have not lost back-to-back competitive home matches between November 1999 (v Scotland) and October 2000 (v Germany).
Tuchel's team showing their teeth

There was so much frustration among England's fanbase in the wake of Tuchel's pragmatic, perhaps pessimistic, approach during the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina, as there was a real feeling that this Three Lions squad has the attacking talent to cut through most other teams.
That attacking quality has been on show over the past fortnight, and Tuchel will be eyeing up a strong finish to this extended stint with his squad.

Across their last four games in all competitions, England have won 6-4 against France and 7-0 against Croatia. It is the first time they have scored 6+ goals in two different games in a calendar year since 2019, while they last did so in three different games in 1908.

And while Kane remains England's talisman up top, there is a plethora of talent behind the Bayern Munich captain who are proving the Three Lions should always be out to stamp their authority on matches.
Gordon has scored in each of his last four appearances for England. The last player other than Kane to score in five in a row for the team was Wayne Rooney between October 2014 and March 2015.
The Barcelona winger has actually netted two headed goals in his last two England appearances – across 248 total club appearances, he has not scored a single header.
Other than Kane, Gordon is the only player to be directly involved in a goal in five consecutive England appearances across the last 10 years (four goals, two assists).
Against Croatia, Saka scored two right-footed goals in a match for the first time in his senior career for club and country.

Bellingham, meanwhile, was directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time. He is the first player to record three assists in a game for the Three Lions since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.
England have lost Alex Scott, who faces up to two months on the sidelines, and Ezri Konsa due to injury, with Rico Lewis called up, but their attack is fit and firing.
Czechia's dismal start
They sit bottom of the group after losing their opening three games, going down 3-1 to Spain and 2-1 to Croatia, either side of that defeat to England.
Santi Denia has lost all three of his games in charge of Czechia and could be the second manager to lose their first four matches with the nation after Vaclav Jezek in 1973, then as Czechoslovakia.
In fact, Czechia have lost five of their last six games in all competitions (D1), including each of the last four in a row. They last lost five consecutively between July 1972 and March 1973.

Across all of the teams competing in the 2026-27 Nations League, Czechia's 1.73 expected goals is the sixth-lowest. They have had just 16 shots, with only Gibraltar (14) and Liechtenstein (nine) having fewer attempts in the competition.
Only six teams, meanwhile, have conceded more goals than Czechia (seven) so far.
Czechia have already faced 56 shots – an average of 18.7 per game – with 22 of those hitting the target.
This is a team that are not clinical going forward and are open at the back. England, at home, should not be having any trouble.
England – Harry Kane
If Kane features in this match, he will make his 125th England appearance, which would see him equal Peter Shilton as the all-time most capped player in the Three Lions' history.
With his double last time out, Kane became the first player to score 10+ goals in three different calendar years for England: 11 in 2026, 16 in 2021 and 12 in 2019.

Kane has netted 89 goals across his 124 caps to date, and a flurry here could well set him on the way to really close in on a century before 2026 is up. At the very least, he should be targeting making this calendar year his best for a goal return on the international stage.
Czechia – Adam Hlozek
Given their drab form, Czechia hardly have many players who are shining in an attacking sense.
But Hlozek has been one of their better performers.
He leads the way in their squad in the past three games for goal involvements (two assists), shots (four) and chances created (four).
England's defence should not have too much to worry about, but Hlozek could pose them a few problems if given the chance.

zit5l0y7gd31b35ffiml4rcf.title: Hurzeler wants 'dirty atmosphere' at Brighton ahead of Conference League opener
zit5l0y7gd31b35ffiml4rcf.subtitle: Brighton take on Kauno Zalgiris in the first game of their Conference League campaign, and Fabian Hurzeler wants a fortress-feel at home.
paragraphs: Fabian Hurzeler revealed he does not want Brighton to be a "nice" club and has called on the fans to create a "dirty atmosphere" in their Conference League opener on Thursday.
Brighton host Kauno Zalgiris, hoping to carry their momentum from an excellent start in the Premier League, where they are third after six games, into their European campaign.

The Seagulls are participating in a major European competition for just the second time in their history after reaching the last 16 of the 2023-24 Europa League, where they were knocked out by Roma (4-1 on aggregate).
Brighton have kept a clean sheet in each of their previous five wins in major European competitions, with each of their last three such victories coming via 1-0 scorelines.
The club previously stated their ambition to win silverware this season, and Hurzeler believes that can only be done if they become "ruthless".
"I use this word, this dirty club or this dirty atmosphere – that's a little bit of what I meant by this phrase," said Hurzeler.
"It's like, keep building this fortress at home.
"Like, together with the fans, creating a loud, energetic atmosphere where they are our 12th player, and I think that's just an example for being not nice.
"Of course, we are known for being a well-structured club or having one of the best recruitments in the world, but these kinds of things don't help you to win anything.
"I think we need to have this mindset of, 'Focus on us, believe in our quality, believe that we can compete with every team, but with 'nice', you win nothing'.
"We are also not nice in personal duels. We want to be ruthless in personal duels. We want to create this energetic atmosphere, where it makes it so hard to come to this place.
"I think we made great progress, the last months. Great progress, the last year, and we have to keep building this together with our fans to be not the nice football club anymore."

zk4ch04xqb631ilkwlth87cs6.title: Gasperini worried by Pellegrini's injury after Roma's big win over Slovan Bratislava
zk4ch04xqb631ilkwlth87cs6.subtitle: Roma claimed their first Champions League win of the season by thrashing Slovan Bratislava, but Lorenzo Pellegrini's injury is a worry.
paragraphs: Gian Piero Gasperini was concerned about the extent of Lorenzo Pellegrini's injury after Roma's 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava.
Roma failed to win their opening two Champions League fixtures, drawing with Fenerbahce before losing in dramatic fashion to Real Madrid.
However, they swatted aside Slovan in style on Tuesday to get up and running.
Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina, Niccolo Pisilli and Donyell Malen were on target, but captain Pellegrini was forced off with a muscular issue early in the second half.
As quoted by Football Italia, Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia: "I saw very important responses from the squad, because the fixture list is packed and I need everyone to be up to the task.

"This allows us to go forward with confidence and expand the list of potential starters in this team. My only worry is that now we've got Bryan Cristante back on the bench, we risk losing Pellegrini for a while."
Gasperini subsequently confirmed Pellegrini faces around three weeks out.
"I don't think it's serious. Even though it's a minor injury, when it's a muscle injury it takes 20 days," he said.
"I think it's of that magnitude. Now this week we have an extra day before Napoli, then we have a series of games every three days.

"The attacking line is crucial now, in terms of substitutions, quality, and numbers. So we're facing a series of games where, if we don't get [Paulo] Dybala back quickly, we'll definitely be short-handed."
Roma dominated from the off, with Slovan managing just a single shot, which was worth a meagre 0.02 expected goals.
Gasperini's team ended a run of five games without a win in major European competitions (D3 L2), with this their first victory since beating Stuttgart 2-0 in the Europa League in January.
This was Roma's first win in the Champions League since February 2019, when they beat Porto 2-1.

Hermoso put them ahead in the 21st minute. With Daniele Ghilardi providing the assist, it marked the first time two defenders have combined for a Champions League goal for Roma since September 2015, when Lucas Digne assisted Vasilis Torosidis against BATE Borisov.
Molina doubled Roma's lead before the break, with Pisilli and Malen then completing the rout in the second half.
Malen is the first player to be involved in a goal in each of Roma's first three matches of a Champions League campaign, with the Dutchman scoring three goals and providing two assists so far.
"It was important for us to have the right approach from the start, both because we needed three points," Gasperini said. "There are no easy games in the Champions League. I liked the way we played."
Slovan have now lost all 11 of their Champions League matches, extending their record of the most games played by a team in the competition to have lost 100% of them.
Tougher tests are to come for Roma next month, with away games against Manchester United and holders Paris Saint-Germain next up.
"They are incredible tests and give us the opportunity to grow even more," added Gasperini. "This is the spirit with which we will approach those games."

Tougher tests are to come for Roma next month, with away games against Manchester United and holders Paris Saint-Germain next up.

"They are incredible tests and give us the opportunity to grow even more," added Gasperini. "This is the spirit with which we will approach those games."

zl3oigiwpg8k126yfx6zhwffd.title: Maresca: No doubt over Donnarumma's spot as Man City's number one
zl3oigiwpg8k126yfx6zhwffd.subtitle: Geronimo Rulli's saves sent Manchester City into the EFL Cup quarter-finals, but Gianluigi Donnarumma's place is under no threat.
paragraphs: Enzo Maresca was thrilled with Geronimo Rulli's match-winning display against Brighton, but he has "no doubt" about Gianluigi Donnarumma as Manchester City's number one goalkeeper.
Donnarumma was handed a rest by Maresca for Wednesday's EFL Cup fourth-round clash at the Etihad Stadium, where Rulli ultimately proved to be City's hero in a 4-3 shoot-out win following a 2-2 draw.
Brighton led twice, through Malick Yalcouye and Georginio Rutter, but City fought back, with Mateo Kovacic and Vitor Reis on target to force penalties.
Kovacic blinked first in the shoot-out, as he saw his spot-kick kept out by Jason Steele.
Rulli, though, stepped up to spare Kovacic's blushes, denying Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk, either side of Rayan Cherki converting his penalty, to seal the holders' place in the quarter-finals.

Donnarumma has not been at his best this season, and was at fault for Aston Villa's winner in City's first Premier League loss of the campaign last weekend. In fact, the Italian has already made two errors leading to goals this term, and three leading to shots.
Yet Maresca was blunt in his response when asked if Rulli could now usurp Donnarumma as first-choice.
"No, absolutely not from my point of view," Maresca said.
"He's working well, but he knows exactly his role and there is not any doubt about that. Absolutely no doubt.
"I think overall he was good, especially in the build-up. It was not easy because they are a team that goes man to man, aggressive.
"He made, also, one good save during the game and he was good."
City were fortunate, given Brighton created by far the better chances, registering 2.03 expected goals to the hosts' 0.76.
Maresca made wholesale changes, with Erling Haaland, Josko Gvardiol, Ruben Dias and Elliot Anderson sitting out altogether, while Jeremy Doku and Enzo Fernandez came on as substitutes.
However, the City boss did not regret that decision, saying: "I was happy with the way we planned the game, with the rotation, especially I was very, very happy with the ones on the pitch."
Maresca's men will face third-tier Bradford City at home in the last eight.

zo8jy0jqd0ly1p62n3y28loix.title: Colorado taking 'baby steps' towards playoffs, says Wells
zo8jy0jqd0ly1p62n3y28loix.subtitle: The Colorado Rapids have yet to secure their playoff spot with two regular-season matches remaining, with the Chicago Fire up next.
paragraphs: Matt Wells believes the Colorado Rapids' hopes of reaching the playoffs are "in our hands" as they prepare to take on the Chicago Fire at Dick's Sporting Goods Park.
Colorado are seventh in the Western Conference heading into the penultimate fixture of their regular season campaign, but plenty of teams around them are in with a chance.
Just three points separate 11th-place Portland Timbers from the Rapids, with LA Galaxy, Real Salt Lake and the Seattle Sounders all aiming to secure a spot in the postseason.
The Rapids were held to a 2-2 draw against the San Jose Earthquakes in midweek, despite leading in the 73rd minute and having a man advantage over their opponents.
However, just two minutes after going ahead, Kosi Thompson was sent off to even things up, with Jack Jasinski scoring an 83rd-minute equaliser for Bruce Arena's side.

"There was a temptation, given the order of the scoring, there is an element of frustration in the group, especially given the fact we were in a position with 15 minutes to go with three points in our hands and our opponent down to 10 men," Wells said.
"Obviously, that didn't last long. We ended up evening the sides but sometimes there is that chaos in these types of games, and we have experienced it a couple of times.
"But, for me, I chose to take the positives. I have been critical all season about our ability to come from behind. I thought the response was excellent to turn the game around.

"It's baby steps. Of course, we would have loved all three points, but we left with a very valuable point. We have two games to go, we're sat in seventh position. We're five games unbeaten in the MLS and that is very difficult to do.
"There are only a couple of teams in that same vein of form. We have loads to play for. We're in an excellent spot, but it's in our hands, and we have two very tough games to go."
Chicago, meanwhile, are already assured of their spot in the playoffs, but they will want to pick up their recent form after drawing 2-2 with Orlando City SC in midweek.
Gregg Berhalter's side have just won one of their last four matches in the MLS (D2 L1), leaving them at risk of dropping out of the top four in the Eastern Conference.
They did, however, show grit and determination against Orlando, coming from two goals down in the second half to take a point, with Jonathan Bamba starring off the bench.
Chicago take on the Columbus Crew in their final regular-season encounter of the season, before their attention swiftly returns to improving on last season's playoff run.
Colorado Rapids – Darren Yapi
Yapi came off the bench to score Colorado's second goal against San Jose on Wednesday.
Over the last three seasons, Yapi has scored five goals as a substitute in MLS play, and no other Rapids player has scored more than one goal off the bench in that time.
Chicago Fire – Robert Lewandowski
Lewandowski failed to score for the eighth straight match on Wednesday despite attempting seven shots, a run he will want to end here.
He has had just one longer scoreless run in league play over his time in the Bundesliga and LaLiga, going nine in a row without scoring for Borussia Dortmund from December 2010 to February 2011.
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

This will be the first meeting between Colorado and Chicago since a 4-1 Fire win on April 20, 2019. This is Chicago’s first visit to Dick's Sporting Goods Park in over eight years, since a 2-2 draw in June 2018.

Colorado are on a 10-match unbeaten run at home in MLS play (W7 D3), keeping clean sheets in each of the seven victories. It's the second time in team history they have posted seven clean-sheet wins over 10 home regular-season matches (also August 2007 – May 2008).

The Fire, meanwhile, came from 2-0 down to earn a 2-2 draw with Orlando on Wednesday. They had lost the last 19 regular-season matches in which they trailed by multiple goals at any point dating back to August 2024.
Colorado Rapids – 37.2%

zsa2ubvyobgz1wnufs92e6jek.title: 'The goals and the points will come' – Slegers optimistic despite Arsenal's slow start
zsa2ubvyobgz1wnufs92e6jek.subtitle: Arsenal were dealt their first defeat of the Women's Super League season against Chelsea, but Renee Slegers remained calm about her team.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers remains confident her Arsenal team can achieve great things this season despite slipping to their first Women's Super League defeat of the campaign.
Arsenal were beaten 1-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, with Alyssa Thompson pouncing on some sloppy defending to score the only goal just before the break.
The Gunners improved after the interval, having also seen Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey hit the woodwork in the first half, but they were unable to find an equaliser.
Arsenal's attacking troubles have been a topic of conversation as they have scored just two goals this campaign, with only Charlton Athletic (one) netting fewer in the WSL so far.
Slegers' side had 18 shots, but only two of those forced Hannah Hampton into making a save, with those efforts generating an expected goals (xG) total of just 1.04.
The result also saw Arsenal's 20-game unbeaten run in the WSL come to an end, leaving them seventh in the table and already seven points behind leaders Manchester City.

And while Slegers expressed her disappointment with the defeat, she backed her players to hit their stride sooner rather than later, with a Women's Champions League clash against Paris FC coming up this Wednesday.
"Very disappointed. We know it's a tough game Chelsea away. I think we did well in the first half in the physical battle and dominated until their goal," Slegers told Sky Sports.
"We found it hard in the second half and it cost us more energy. It's a cocktail of things. It's everything. Technical and psychological. We're looking at it.
"I believe in these players. The goals and the points will come. I believe in them."
For Chelsea, however, they ensured their own unbeaten run in the WSL continued. They are now 12 games without defeat in the league.

The Blues are also now unbeaten across their opening four games of a WSL campaign for the fourth successive season, while Arsenal only have five points to their name at this stage for the second time in the last three seasons (also 2024-25).
Keira Walsh has been key to Chelsea's strong start to the season, and she once again played a starring role in the middle of midfield against Arsenal.
She finished with team-high totals for chances created (three), accurate passes (62) and possession won (10), while only Lucy Bronze (107) had more touches for Chelsea than Walsh's 92.
The England international acknowledged the difficulties Chelsea came up against as Arsenal searched for an equaliser, but she was thrilled to help get her team over the line.
"It's hard, Arsenal were chasing a goal and changed formation a bit," Walsh said. "It was important that we kept a clean sheet and stayed in the game.
"Ellie [Carpenter] took us up the pitch a bit at the end and it really helped."
Walsh was also not reading too much into Chelsea's unbeaten league run, adding: "I don't really think we think about it.
"We've got both sides to our game and we showed that in spells. Everyone was fighting for each other. Every first and second ball was ours."

zu6iq4of8orb14xs100thrkvr.title: St. Louis City SC 6-2 LA Galaxy: Holse hat-trick leads the way in record-equalling win
zu6iq4of8orb14xs100thrkvr.subtitle: Carlo Holse hit a hat-trick as St. Louis City SC cruised to a 6-2 victory over the LA Galaxy, taking a slice of history in the process.
paragraphs: St. Louis City SC stretched their unbeaten run in all competitions to a record-equalling 20 games as they thrashed the LA Galaxy 6-2.
Carlo Holse starred with a hat-trick inside 21 minutes at Energizer Park, where the hosts led 5-1 by half-time.
Holse got the ball rolling in the second minute, sliding in to turn home from Rafael Navarro's tee-up.
He doubled up five minutes later, lashing a left-footed drive beyond JT Marcinkowski.
Holse capped off his hat-trick in sublime fashion, taking in a long ball on his chest before tucking a finish in at the right-hand post.
Robert Taylor's stunner dragged the Galaxy back into it, but Navarro's penalty restored St. Louis' three-goal cushion.
Lukas MacNaughton's brilliant header put the hosts four to the good before the interval, and Navarro's fine, low strike made it 6-1 shortly after the restart.
Joao Klauss grabbed another consolation for the Galaxy, as St. Louis surged to 50 points, just one behind the Western Conference-leading Vancouver Whitecaps.
Hose and Navarro star as St. Louis close in on history
Holse's hat-trick was the second-fastest in MLS history from the start of a game.
He also became the fifth player in the competition to net a hat-trick inside the opening 30 minutes of a match.
Navarro continued his flying start to life at St. Louis. He is now on 17 goals this season, with seven of those coming for his new team, and 10 for the Colorado Rapids.

It was St. Louis' brutally clinical first-half display that saw them race clear. They have scored 29 first-half goals in 28 MLS games this term. Only Inter Miami (33) and the Whitecaps (33) have netted more times in the opening period.
St. Louis are unbeaten since May in all competitions, with this run matching the record for an MLS team, previously set by the New York Red Bulls in 2016.

They are unbeaten in 18 straight MLS matches, which means they have tied with the Columbus Crew's class of 2004 in second place in the league's record books. Only FC Dallas (19 games unbeaten in 2010) have gone more fixtures without a defeat in the competition.

zxbr4oyrendb1lf2mtm67u34g.title: Women's Super League predictions: Man City's perfect record expected to continue against Brighton
zxbr4oyrendb1lf2mtm67u34g.subtitle: Manchester City are backed to make it six wins from six in the Women's Super League, but Chelsea and London City Lionesses are lurking.
paragraphs: The Women's Super League gets back underway this weekend following the international break, with plenty of intriguing fixtures at both ends of the table.
Manchester City are out on their own at the top of the pile, with their perfect record on the line against Brighton, with the chasing pack looking to capitalise if they suffer a surprise defeat.
Sonia Bompastor will be hoping to mark her 50th WSL game in charge of Chelsea with a win against Tottenham, while London City Lionesses square off against Everton.
Aston Villa, Birmingham City and Charlton Athletic are all without a league win so far this term, while Arsenal will be aiming to kick their stuttering season back into life.
Manchester United and Eva Olid will also be looking to continue their recent revival, with West Ham and Crystal Palace locking horns in their quest to pull clear of the bottom.
But who will be the winners and losers on MD6 in the WSL? We consulted the Opta supercomputer to find out.
ARSENAL V BIRMINGHAM CITY
The weekend's action begins at the Emirates Stadium as Arsenal take on Birmingham City, in what is the only fixture taking place on Saturday.
Both Arsenal and Birmingham signed off for the international break with defeats, with Renee Slegers' side losing to Manchester City while the Blues were beaten at Everton.
This will be the first WSL campaign that Arsenal and Birmingham have met in since 2021-22, and the Opta supercomputer has backed the Gunners to return to winning ways.

Across 10,000 data-led simulations, Arsenal are assigned an 81.5% win probability, the highest of any team on MD6. Birmingham's hopes of a first league win of the season are 7.1%, while the likelihood of a draw is 11.4%.

The Gunners' position as overwhelming favourites perhaps owes to their impressive record against newly promoted sides. Arsenal are unbeaten in each of their last 30 WSL games against such opposition (W26 D4), since a 1-0 loss at home to Man City in May 2014.

But with five points from five games, this is Arsenal's second-worst start to a WSL campaign, better only than their beginning to the 2014 season (four points), while they could go winless in five consecutive top-flight matches for the very first time.

However, they come up against a Birmingham side that have lost each of their last six WSL away games against Arsenal, while also being the only team to concede more than once in all five of their league games so far this season.
CRYSTAL PALACE V WEST HAM
Sunday's action starts with a London derby at The 360 Engage Stadium, with Crystal Palace and West Ham squaring off as they aim to spark their seasons into life.

Palace have drawn their last two games against Aston Villa and Birmingham, respectively, despite conceding first in both. The Eagles had previously only avoided defeat in two of 19 WSL matches when falling behind (D2 L17), showing they are an improved outfit.

They are just three points above West Ham, who, in their 3-0 loss to Chelsea last time out, failed to take a single shot in a game in the competition for the first time, in their 171st outing in the WSL.

Palace have lost each of their last three games against West Ham in all competitions, with the Hammers winning 5-2 at home and 7-1 away in their previous two WSL meetings with Palace, with the latter their biggest-ever win in the competition.

But the Opta supercomputer has backed Palace to take all three points, assigning them a 45.8% chance of victory. West Ham are predicted to win in 27.5% of simulations, with a draw rated slightly lower at 26.7%.
Another rivalry in the capital also takes centre-stage during Sunday's early slate, as Chelsea look to keep pace at the top of the standings when they face Tottenham.

Chelsea have won their last four league matches and could win five in a row in the WSL for the first time since the start of last season, but they face a Spurs side aiming to bounce back from a 6-1 hammering by London City Lionesses.

The Blues have had the better of their rivals, winning all 13 of their WSL meetings with Spurs, the only team to face an opponent more than 10 times in the competition and still boast a 100% win rate, and that is expected to continue here.
Chelsea are the favourites with a win probability of 78.4%, in a match that will see Bompastor oversee her 50th match in the WSL.
She has earned 122 points in her first 49 matches (W38 D8 L3) and could overtake Joe Montemurro (123) for the most points won by any manager across their first 50 matches in the competition.

Spurs will be out to spoil the party, though they are winless in each of their last 20 WSL games against 'big-four' opposition (D4 L16), since a 1-0 win over Arsenal in December 2023. In comparison, they have won 14 of their last 20 league matches against non-'big-four' opponents (D2 L4).
A win could see Spurs go above Chelsea in the table, with the Opta supercomputer rating their chances of an upset at 8.6%, while a draw was predicted in 13% of simulations.
LONDON CITY LIONESSES V EVERTON
The big-spending London City Lionesses have enjoyed a strong start to their WSL campaign, and they will be hoping that can continue against Everton.

London City have won each of their last three WSL matches, their longest winning run in the competition. They could win four consecutive league games for the first time since doing so between March and April 2025 in the WSL2.

And key to their fast start has been Alexia Putellas, who has four goal involvements in the WSL this term (three goals, one assist). Across the last five seasons, she has only registered more goal contributions in her opening five league appearances once: six for Barcelona in 2024-25 (four goals, two assists).

Everton have, however, won three of their opening five WSL games this season (L2), taking nine points, their joint-second highest tally at this stage of a campaign in the competition. Only in 2020-21 have the Toffees collected more from their first five matches (13).

London City's first ever win in the WSL came against Everton last September, and they are the favourites to get one over the Toffees again here. Eder Maestre's side assigned a 57.9% win probability, while the visitors won just 20.2% of our simulations, a slightly lower chance than the match ending in a draw (21.9%).
CHARLTON ATHLETIC V MANCHESTER UNITED
It's been a difficult return to the WSL for Charlton Athletic, with the Addicks the only team without a point so far this season, and things do not get any easier this weekend.
Manchester United are the visitors to The Valley, with the Red Devils hoping to put together back-to-back league wins without conceding for the first time since March 2025.

This will be the first meeting between Charlton and United since the 2018-19 WSL2 season, when the Red Devils won 3-0 at home and 2-1 away, and the Opta supercomputer predicts a similar outcome on Sunday.
United are predicted to emerge victorious in 62.4% of the 10,000 pre-match simulations, while Charlton's chances of a first league win are rated at 17.8%.

The Red Devils are the only team to face newly promoted teams more than once in the WSL and still boast a 100% win rate, winning all 14 of their matches by an aggregate score of 40-4, while Charlton have lost each of their first five WSL games.
Only Yeovil Town in the 2017 Spring Series (first seven) and Leicester City in 2021-22 (first nine) have ever endured a longer losing run to begin their history in the competition.
ASTON VILLA V LIVERPOOL

Another team aiming to secure their first league win of the season is Aston Villa, who are without a victory in their last nine WSL matches (D3 L6), since a 2-1 triumph at Leicester City in March 2026, with Liverpool their next opponents.

However, the Opta supercomputer has predicted a similar result at the Broadfield Stadium. Brighton are assigned a 54.7% chance of getting one over their rivals, while Palace's hopes are rated at just 22%, with a draw slightly higher at 23.3%.

Palace are winless in their last four games against Brighton in all competitions (D1 L3), a run that started with a 5-1 away loss in December 2018, while they are also without a win in their last six WSL matches (D3 L3), losing their last two.

Brighton, meanwhile, have won two of their last three WSL games (L1), having gone winless in their previous seven (D4 L3). Following their 3-0 victory over West Ham on MD7, the Seagulls are looking to win consecutive league matches without conceding for the first time since November 2021.

And this weekend's hosts will be looking to build on their good home form. They have won their last two home games in the WSL, as many victories as in their last 10 combined (W2 D3 L5), though Palace are the first newly promoted side to remain unbeaten in their opening three away games of a WSL season, drawing all three this term.
BIRMINGHAM CITY V TOTTENHAM

After beating Charlton last time out, Birmingham will be hoping to pull further clear of the bottom of the table when they take on Tottenham, who are out for revenge after their defeat in the north London derby.

However, against no side have Birmingham played more games without winning in the WSL than Tottenham, failing in all four attempts (D1 L3). They also have their worst goals-per-game rate in the competition against Spurs (0.25 – 1 in 4).

But Spurs are in need of a victory, having lost each of their last three WSL games. They could lose more in a row for the first time since a run of five defeats between February and March 2025 under Robert Vilahamn.

Tottenham will have confidence coming into this fixture, though, given they have won each of their last four games against Birmingham in all competitions without conceding – they have never won five in a row against an opponent as a WSL side.

And the Opta supercomputer has backed Spurs to return to winning ways at St. Andrew's, handing them a 40% win probability. Birmingham's hopes of a second league win of the season are rated at 34.2%, while a draw is backed to happen in 25.8% of the pre-match simulations.

One thing from this fixture you can expect is goals. Spurs' nine WSL away games in 2026 have seen 49 total goals scored (25F, 24A) at an average of 5.4 per game, the highest rate of any team on the road in a calendar year.
CHARLTON ATHLETIC V CHELSEA
Chelsea are riding high after following up their 3-1 win over Crystal Palace last time out with a 2-0 triumph over Roma to stay perfect in their Champions League campaign.

They make the trip to The Valley this Sunday to face a Charlton side that have lost each of their four WSL home games by an aggregate score of 12-2. The only team to lose their first five home matches in the competition are Yeovil Town (first 11 between 2017 and 2018).

This will be only the third meeting between Charlton and Chelsea in the WSL era, with the Addicks losing 4-0 in the FA Cup both times, in January 2020 (at home) and January 2025 (away), and this weekend's hosts may be fearing the worst.

Chelsea have scored 98 goals in 32 games against newly promoted sides in the WSL, averaging three goals per match, while they sit top of the league table for the first time since the end of MD7 last season, and they will want to remain there.
The Blues are unbeaten in their last 22 league games when starting the day as the WSL leaders (W17 D5), since a 1-0 loss to Man City in February 2024, and that stretch is expected to continue.
Sonia Bompastor's side are handed a huge 80.5% win probability, higher than any other team on MD8. Charlton's hopes are rated at just 8.5% for a win, with a draw deemed slightly more likely at 10.9%.
