However, against no side have Birmingham played more games without winning in the WSL than Tottenham, failing in all four attempts (D1 L3). They also have their worst goals-per-game rate in the competition against Spurs (0.25 – 1 in 4).

But Spurs are in need of a victory, having lost each of their last three WSL games. They could lose more in a row for the first time since a run of five defeats between February and March 2025 under Robert Vilahamn. 

Tottenham will have confidence coming into this fixture, though, given they have won each of their last four games against Birmingham in all competitions without conceding – they have never won five in a row against an opponent as a WSL side.

And the Opta supercomputer has backed Spurs to return to winning ways at St. Andrew's, handing them a 40% win probability. Birmingham's hopes of a second league win of the season are rated at 34.2%, while a draw is backed to happen in 25.8% of the pre-match simulations. 

One thing from this fixture you can expect is goals. Spurs' nine WSL away games in 2026 have seen 49 total goals scored (25F, 24A) at an average of 5.4 per game, the highest rate of any team on the road in a calendar year. 

CHARLTON ATHLETIC V CHELSEA

Chelsea are riding high after following up their 3-1 win over Crystal Palace last time out with a 2-0 triumph over Roma to stay perfect in their Champions League campaign.

They make the trip to The Valley this Sunday to face a Charlton side that have lost each of their four WSL home games by an aggregate score of 12-2. The only team to lose their first five home matches in the competition are Yeovil Town (first 11 between 2017 and 2018).

This will be only the third meeting between Charlton and Chelsea in the WSL era, with the Addicks losing 4-0 in the FA Cup both times, in January 2020 (at home) and January 2025 (away), and this weekend's hosts may be fearing the worst. 

Chelsea have scored 98 goals in 32 games against newly promoted sides in the WSL, averaging three goals per match, while they sit top of the league table for the first time since the end of MD7 last season, and they will want to remain there. 

The Blues are unbeaten in their last 22 league games when starting the day as the WSL leaders (W17 D5), since a 1-0 loss to Man City in February 2024, and that stretch is expected to continue.

Sonia Bompastor's side are handed a huge 80.5% win probability, higher than any other team on MD8. Charlton's hopes are rated at just 8.5% for a win, with a draw deemed slightly more likely at 10.9%.

zz73wu9lqi7fzdybm64lhkbm.title: Borussia Dortmund 3-2 Werder Bremen: Sabitzer strikes late to seal DFB-Pokal progress
zz73wu9lqi7fzdybm64lhkbm.subtitle: Niclas Fullkrug scored twice against his old club, but Borussia Dortmund managed to get the job done in a tight DFB-Pokal tie.
paragraphs: Marcel Sabitzer's stoppage-time free-kick saw Borussia Dortmund fend off Werder Bremen 3-2 in the DFB-Pokal.
Werder had come from 2-0 down to restore parity thanks to a quickfire double from former Dortmund striker Niclas Fullkrug.
But Sabitzer cropped up with a winner in the 93rd minute, sending Niko Kovac's team into the last 16.
Kick-off was delayed at Signa Iduna Park, where Serhou Guirassy put Dortmund ahead inside six minutes once play got under way.
Julian Ryerson set up Guirassy at the end of a slick move, and the striker duly converted from close range.
Maximilian Beier had a goal disallowed for offside, but Carney Chukwuemeka netted a second for BVB in the 17th minute, finishing from Jobe Bellingham's knockdown.
Yet Werder flipped the script after the break thanks to substitute Fullkrug.
He had only been on the pitch six minutes when he converted from the penalty spot after Mick Schmetgens had been fouled.
Fullkrug doubled up three minutes later, brilliantly nutmegging Waldemar Anton before slamming in an equaliser.
There was to be one last twist, though, as Sabitzer bent in a free-kick from the edge of the box to seal BVB's progress.
Fullkrug surpasses Bayern stars as Sabitzer snaps Dortmund's free-kick drought
Against his old club, Fullkrug was on fire.
He has now netted 11 goals in all competitions this season, which makes him the highest-scoring Bundesliga player in 2026-27, overtaking Michael Olise and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane (10 each).
Fullkrug has now netted in seven successive matches, equalling the Werder record in the Bundesliga era (Rudi Voller between November 1982 and March 1983).
This was only Fullkrug's second brace in a DFB-Pokal tie. His first came way back in August 2017, for Hannover against Bonner SC.
However, Sabitzer had the final say.
The winner was his first goal since he netted against Werder in January, but it also marked BVB's first direct free-kick goal since November 2024, when Julian Brandt scored against Freiburg.
While Dortmund can celebrate their dramatic win, Kovac will be far from happy with how his team controlled the game when 2-0 up.
Perhaps it was a case of too much, too soon: This was the earliest BVB had taken a two-goal lead in a cup match since February 2021.
